It acts very similar to the mining software
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: this is solely multiplayer as i only bought this game to play with friends, did not play this single player nor do i believe i will, At this point due to the disconnects will only what i can and when disconnected will watch my friends through dc, cuz i wont make everyone re-run a dungeon due to poor/none re-connection system.But here are my pointsPros: -game is fun time flies by, - For multiplayer  as long as 1 of your friends have anything unlocked is shared amongst the whole party this is a great con in my view (when u have faulty multiplayer)Cons: -No reconnect attempts if your WiFi or connection just twitches for 1 ms, it disconnects you and if you are in the dungeon then gg (lost ch 2 and 3 final dungeon cuz of this)-Some classes feels boring and nonsensical (Shepard,Scholar,friar..)-No real description how stats help you and how to balance them besides B-lining to your main stat-Game bugs way too much to list (only naming the bugs that bother me the most)-Lack of real variety in play style the most "flexible" are the mages with various staff,grimore,wands with various elements and such, -Whats the point of dropping the most money,rare weapons,rare consumables at the last dungeon for? Like there is no real way to "reap your rewards" you just end the screen looking nice.-Personal opinion just to round back up to my first con, why not let us join mid journey? like what if one of us has to go to the toilet, eat,shower,LIFE happens then what? lets meet up tomorrow?  I do not see why make this restriction.Overall game is fun would like to give them a better rating, willing to change it aswell, but again as i do believe we have gone too deep in the rabbit hole of "is ok for game developers to launch super buggy and kinda unplayble gamemodes(mulitplayer) Day 1"Like i still believe we can go back to the good old times where day 1 should be a whole product with small thingies here and there dont work as intended fine, but when everyone says multiplayer is unplayable then we have a problem. I feel unless you label your game "early access" then you owe me a fully developed game with a fully functional multiplayer. Note bought this on sale (10% not bad for a newly launched game) which was enough to "convince me" and my friends got it already but honestly if i had read the comments and reviews about the multiplayer i would not have.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Not for everyone, but pretty good overall.  Even on the easiest difficulty settings, I find the level bosses too hard with TPK resulting.  I think it is more the RNG of reward items than any lack of skill.IF you intend to play co-op online, be warned that there is significant amounts of down-time waiting on other players to make a move, and for a game this simple, that can be a bit painful IMO
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Wait a few months before buying if you want a good overall experience. Pros: - The combat uses a grid now so the combat is actually a lot more thoughtful and strategic - There is plenty of content - Most aspects from the mechanical and technical side of the game work properlyCons: - UI is a complete mess and none of the resizing options actually make it feel good. - None of the weapons have sound effects - There is no way to filter or sort shops by price - Performance can be kind of weird when loading dungeons - Camera in combat is kind of bad, I think you should be able to rotate it 360 degrees.Honestly its a good game but it just wasn't ready to be released yet, definitely needed some more polish.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: For The King 2 truly shines is in its multiplayer experience. Collaborating with friends adds an extra layer of enjoyment to the game, as you strategize, plan, and face challenges together. The cooperative nature of the game fosters camaraderie, and the shared victories (or defeats) create memorable moments that will have you coming back for more. The ability to play both locally and online ensures that you can connect with your friends regardless of physical distance.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of FTK 1, and I do really like all the updates made in FTK 2! While I've experienced some minor bugs since launch (characters or screens getting stuck), the new graphics & lore store updates are exciting! Very exciting upping to 4 players. Anyway, I do recommend this game for folks that like turn-based, kinda-goofy, dnd-esque adventuring!
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: For the king! Good game to play with friends so you're not stuck controlling all 4 characters. Still has some things to fix but doesn't hamper gameplay other then slowing it down. (My main thing being the UI options for what to do with items in your inventory/equipped. Sometimes that UI box ending up appearing in the top right corner and makes me unable to select the top few options.)
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Great sequel to the first game, though it's just as challenging (and frustrating at times with that RNG)! Game is fun in single player mode but definitely shines when you have some friends all playing together. It did start off a bit glitchy but the devs have been pretty on top of things with patches/fixes and I haven't encountered more than a couple of bugs in my time playing the game.Really looking forward to the rest of the story and what is in store in the future in terms of additional campaigns, updates, etc
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

Maybe it was a controller issue but holy Zeus...Hint to the devs: The "B" button on a controller typically takes you out of the currently open menu. _childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: A very clever way of making the equivalent of a board game as a videogame. It's charming, it has a lot of content and it's challenging.Honestly don't read too much into the people complaining that the game is too hard. The game might not teach you enough about how to be good at the game, perhaps (haven't done the tutorial as I'm used to the gameplay of the first game which is basically the same) but the balancing is pretty solid. You can quite easily steamroll opponents if you play your cards right and the RNG is a lot less problematic than in the first game. For instance things like acid and thieves are a lot easier to prevent/counter while in general gear is more rare but way way way stronger than in the first game. You basically slowly become a powerhouse whereas in the previous game you would quickly pile a lot of trash and hope to make the best out of it (I exaggerate a bit but close to it).It's just a great game, but you have to have the patience to carefully think before clicking and it's not for everyone (not a critic, sometimes I just want to mash buttons too).
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: so far so good! i am enjoying this one a lot more than the first so far. loooove the new secondary mechanics and combat grid! only gripe i have right now is that some combat still feels a *little* unfair towards players, for example, the queen's guard fights in scenario 1. combat is either not balanced for 3 players or maybe it is just too strong in general but i'm sure it will be worked on :) overall positive and i would recommend this game!!
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game, with serious potential to become much better than the 1st game. There are still some issues to be adressed, mostly regarding game stability and random crashes that you can only overcome with completely restarting the game. Thankfully the auto-save feature is working well so there are no rollbacks when you alt+f4, but please work on those issues since they can become really frustrating and end up ruining the whole game experience.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Honest Review:Loved the first game. Beat every mode and map on master. Unlocked everything in lore store had a massive blast. First game on PlayStation I actually got the platinum trophy on.This game is a massive upgrade. The world, the graphics, the textures, everything is so much more beautiful. Granted it’s still cartoony but much more HD. No idea where the multiplayer bugs are coming from. Three friends and I loaded flawlessly. No lag, no stuttering, no disconnects or freezes.UI is a little confusing at first and certain times when using the Focus feature it doesn’t work, but other than that it is a wonderful upgrade. Confusing at first sure, but once figured out is a breeze. Controller support is terrible though. Buddy was constantly unable to play from his couch so sat back down on his desk and had a blast. Overall ignore the people crying about they can’t recommend this blah blah blah. It’s $20. Money is money and should be respected when spent but for $20 I got my moneys worth and respect the first game hugely. Day one in any game there’s bound to be glitches or bugs. They’ll get fixed.Now shut up and smoke your pipes.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: While it seems other players are still encountering play problems, my party and I have been steadily playing this game weekly for months and have great enjoyment of the storyline, the art, and the mechanics (next week we begin Chapter 5 so we'll see how it ends!). A lot more complex than the first game, but the storylines do finish a bit abruptly for each chapter, and we have to restart each adventure from scratch instead of carrying anything over. The devs are pushing active improvements, so we rarely encounter any bugs the way we did when we first started playing around launch. Would recommend to anyone who loved the first one that wants to continue a storyline, but is willing to learn a more complex battle system.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Several thousand review with 58% (at the moment of writing) tell us 2 things basically.A) Game was not released in a satisfactory condition and should have been either postponed or released as Early Access before ironing out most flawsB) Game itself is very popular since so many people bought it within week of release. Probably due to FTK1 successMy 2 cents. Game seems to run just fine without any crashes/bugs for me (!) so I have no issue leaving a positive review as I think this will be a great game once patched. Several new mechanics (tactical map, etc.) are working fine and will provide more depth to gameplay. UI needs some work, but that should be done with pretty soon with all the (justified) negative feedback.I hope IronOak will learn their lesson and I also hope they won't be too disheartened by the negativity. I think the game will ultimately make them proud and fans happy.And yes, I'm a bit of a fanboy as I loved FTK1 solo and coop. Can't wait to jump into this one with friends.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with saying I never played 'For The King I' and I have only played 'For The King II' solo. Perhaps this game is more enjoyable when playing with friends.I'm aware that there were a lot of bugs and issues on launch and that the developers have been rolling out hotfixes daily. I ran into a few bugs but not enough to put me off (It did annoy me a bit that every hotfix rolled out was 2.5GB for a 7GB game).Issues I had with the game:1. The UI was unintuitive and lacked tool tips. Whilst they do have the encyclopedia, it was annoying to have to go into it to find symbols to see what they meant. Some symbols I couldn't even find. Overall it just felt a bit clunky.2. Lack of variety in gameplay. All combat felt the same and all classes felt more or less the same with the only difference being either melee damage or magic range damage. It also feels like you just go until you run out of healing resources and then you die. There is an in-game 'Lore Store' at the main menu where you spend currency earned through completing quests during the game (Note: This is not a microtransaction system, at least not so far as I can tell at time of writing). I'm not sure if the idea is to unlock extra loadout items to help you progress in the game but most of the items are hidden and locked and it's not clear what you need to do to make them available to purchase. I don't feel any excitement taking my Lore Store dollars to the Lore Store because there is never anything new for sale.I wouldn't say it's a terrible game but it's the first game I've ever considered refunding due to lack of enjoyment and after deciding to give it the benefit of the doubt and put some more time into it, I kind of regret not following through with the refund.It's entirely possible that there are elements of the game I've completely overlooked but I would put that back on the games general lack of clarity.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from FTK, I definitely echo the sentiment that the general look and feel of the UI may have degraded from the original title, however that's where I stop agreeing with most negative reviews.Difficulty is similar between both games, which means progressing through the game and grabbing loot feel familiar. Personally, I'd appreciate more mystery tiles and perhaps a chance in Act 1 to encounter a potential character unlock (though I may just have not seen it yet).No crashes yet, and my only major bug was that I could not purchase from goblin merchants in dungeons, preventing me from buying better gear as well as getting a key to unlock the door at the end.Overall, 7/10. Could use some polish. Nicely toasted on the outside, but a little raw in the middle.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and easily replayable rouge-lite. Fun to play solo and with friends. Each run varies wildly from run to run which makes it all the more fun in my opinion. The game has an element of chance that brings a very rewarding challenge. The only problem I personally have with the game is the character pool to choose from. They each hold a lot of interesting characteristics but I feel that a few stand out to be the most viable and useful. I hope that more characters are implemented in the future or some changes are made to the existing pool.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: I did not know how this game was going to be handled compared to the first game. I can honestly say I love the upgrade from 3 to 4 people and the front and back row mechanics. I loved For the King. I love this game even more, especially after the devs absolute insane response time to patching issues from day one. Bravo hats off to IronOak Games.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say this is a great game. Loved FTK1, was hesitant looking at reviews but decided to give it a try. So far I've been having a ton of fun, quite similar to FTK1 with just a bunch of improvements or new fun things added. They've pretty well just taken FTK1 and improved everything that was good about it and added a good amount of new stuff for new and returning players to enjoy. They've changed the combat system and for the better. It's not crazy complex or anything, but much more interesting and tactic based than just "ok which enemy to aim at?" and therefore is much more fun. My only real issue was at release there was not enough tooltips, returning players could figure out the old stuff of course but there was a decent amount of new stuff you just had to guess what it did (and poor new players). However, one of the many updates they've already released for bugfixing/balancing/etc. has added the missing tooltips. Great to see a developer listen to their community and their criticisms and not just dump a game and forget it and leave it a buggy mess and I'm sure it will continue to improve with their planned updates in the future. If you're a fan of turn based fantasy combat or D&D adjacent table-top games I 10/10 recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: How is this a sequel to the first game is beyond me. Only differences/improvements are that you start with a loadout, you can play with 4 players, and the introduction of frontline/backrow into combat. Having a starting loadout is cool but doesn't really add much to the experience by itself alone. Being able to play up to 4 players now instead of 3 players is also cool and allows for more interesting party compositions, but it's not a huge improvement and could be done in first game. Introduction of frontline-backrow to combat is cool on paper, but doesn't add the strategic depth it is supposed to add because enemies somehow always hit your backline even when you are protecting them anyway. There is still no skill tree for classes, even something that would give passive bonuses would be good enough. There is no explanation to class skills and most of them have very low impact on how you play the game. Very annoying mechanics like evasive are still there. I had to fight agains 5 evasive imps with my blacksmith once. They were doing 0 damage to me because of my armor and I miss all my attacks because of evasive. That simple fight took half an hour to finish. There is no innovation in inventory and character sheet, no improvement in how quests and dungeons are played, and I can keep going. This is just a reskin of first game with some small changes that wouldn't justify it being called a new game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have some mixed feelings. Let’s start with the biggest issue: you’re constantly in the dark about so many things. The game barely conveys any meaningful information – everything from the status of your characters, what the symbols and position effects are (very few hover tooltips provided), or even simple things like tracking waves of enemies (looking at you, 3 waves of imps!). It feels like you’re always playing catch-up, which would be fine if it felt intentional, but it’s mostly just frustrating.And don’t even get me started on the leveling. The moment you fall behind even by a single level, you’re basically done for. The difficulty scaling is brutal if you’re off the pace by even a little. It becomes a downward spiral, making it hard to regain ground once you’ve lost it.Then there’s the randomness. I get that roguelikes rely on luck to some extent, but For the King 2 takes it a bit too far. One lucky treasure chest early on can make or break your run. If you get something good, great! But if you’re unlucky, you’ll be grinding and scraping by, watching as the game punishes you for not getting that golden start.Overall, it has a lot of potential, and there’s fun to be had if you can roll with the punches. But the lack of clear information and the reliance on luck can make it feel like an uphill battle, where even the smallest mistakes or unlucky breaks cost you the whole run.

_childDocuments_.review: For the King II is a buggy mess that makes you wonder how the developers have made such simple mistakes in the game's construction.Before we go on, I should let you know that I signed up and was accepted to join the closed beta of this game. I reported a few bugs- such as various UI bugs and menu errors in the settings menu including your settings not saving when you do something as simple as relaunching the game, and those bugs (to this very day) have not been fixed.Now, I'm not here entirely to rag on For the King II, nor it's Developer- In fact they have removed some serious game breaking bugs after all, and the game is, for the most part, playable.However, I was genuinely afraid to buy this game after my experience with the beta, and reading the reviews- Mostly because a lot of the reviews were severely mixed, a lot of the negatives mentioned bugs I had run into and reported, and most importantly, a lot of the negative reviews don't seem to agree with the changes from For the King.However, I spent a day or two reading the positive reviews, and I found myself deciding to give it a try, and give it a benefit of the doubt. And here's my overview of For the King 2- A whole 5 hours worth of experience:1. From launching the game, it never saves any of your settings upon relaunching. Any time you set it to any particular window type or size, or change any graphical setting, it will always launch in it's default setting. I have no idea what causes this, but it seems to like launching itself in "Medium Graphics" and "Full Screen Mode". 2. If the refusing to save settings was not already annoying enough, if you are playing in Borderless Window Mode or Fullscreen, the game will crash at random intervals. For no reason at all, this will not happen if you swap to regular windowed mode. Alt-Tabbing also has a tendency to cause the game to obliterate, sometimes even crashing modern graphics drivers, even if they're up to date- this latter part will only happen if you're using Borderless Windowed mode.3. Lore Books that you obtain do not update appropriately to reflect how many you have correctly, this is one of the few number errors I noticed, but there's a few other here and there in the game, this is just the more obvious ones.Those are just the bugs I've encountered like. Within the first chapter of the game, which, mind you, I'm going out of my way to explore as much of the chapter on my first play through as I possibly can, as I enjoy For the King, and my friend and I want to see what there is to the game.But that's not the only issue.There's a lot of game problems- Like. Questions. That don't make sense about the game, both aesthetically and mechanically.For example:1. Exactly how character abilities function or what their percent chance to actually activate remains unclear. For example, the hunter has a chance to gain an extra movement point in the overworld. But what IS that extra movement point? And is this SUPPOSED to be able to activate more than once? If it is, sure, but whats the chance of that happening? And if it's not, then why was I able to move an extra 4-5 spaces due to it activating 4-5 times in a row? Why is finding Herbs so rare? If their skill is useless and rare, why do they get less abilities than Hunter which is absolutely meta?2. Why change how pipes work? They worked mechanically fine in the previous game. I get you might have wanted to make it so upgrades were more important or swapping them was better, or you wanted to diversify playstyles. But doesn't this just further nerf how the Herbalist is supposed to be used into the ground without giving them ways to make up for it?3. Why do enemies get massive tile attacks that players literally cannot avoid because of how little they can move and how cramped space is? Why is this something that can happen super early on in the game? While we're on that, why can some enemies get instant death abilities early in the game?4. Why completely overhaul the system and restrict players to a time limit instead of sticking to the "It gets harder the longer you remain in the game but you can keep playing" system? It feels strange to limit people to an arbitrary 50 round limit.Anyways, those are my main observations.

_childDocuments_.review: (Update)When I played it on the first day it came out, the loot drop was not good and there was a number of other things; like minor bugs. Playing it today Jan 2024 the loot drop seems better and with the number of fixes they have done to the game is overall is better.The ProsI like the special effects, like fire, ice and lightning animations of the weapons effects. They look pretty good! And the ground area can catch fire or be frozen ect, which is neat. There were a number of bugs with multiplayer that was addressed and fixed. Now it plays more stable. If you can play with another friend online and the game experience is pretty fun. I recommend it.I like the traits tab in the Lore Store, where you can select a special ability to add to your characters. This helps when it come to game play with characters. Also you can buy items for your characters like powerful candys and Godsbeards to start with; which really helps when you first start out.The town merchants reset pretty often. Seems like every 7 days or after a quest completion. So if you have played "For the King I" and liked it, you will like this one too. Although there is some changes in this one. For one the grid based combat is interesting, but is a pain at the same time moving around and the Lore store is different compared to the old version. You can unlock new sanctums and stuff in the game like the old version. I just did a complete play through of all the chapters and the ending is really over the top! But looking at the Lore store I didn't get many unlocks at the last chapter? So I looked it up on wiki and found out you need to devote to more sanctums to unlock the better version of them. 10 devotes each. Which will take a while to get them.And then there is random events in the chapters that can spawn. So if your wondering why you don't have many cosmetics unlocked, you have too look at wiki and its usually a random event quest in some chapter you need to complete to get it. So just play more and it will happen.The ConsThe Lore store new weapons and armor is only for starter characters. In the loadout tab you can buy items at the start of your game for your characters; but the items are all low level. I get why this is, they don't want you to start with a over powered weapon. But there isn't a long list of stuff to unlock later to buy or find a golden sword, armor or staffs and bows? Instead I'm guessing it is already in there, but was more fun the other way around. Once you get to chapter 5 in the game and you kill all the scourges; which is like 5 or six of them. You will need to disable the chaos refiners and then you can mostly sail through the game not worrying about the chaos building up. I like grinding or farming for the best gear and this chapter is the only chapter that lets you relax and grind equipment. ALL of the other chapters is a race against time!! The problem is the weapons and armor just isn't powerful enough if you grind end game stuff. I feel like its too under powered and its missing something.Then there is the scaling of the loot; depending on what level you are. The stuff that does drop after farming strongholds, most of the time isn't that good. I'm not sure how the loot drop works and compares to your level? Maybe it only scales up after you level up two more times with all your characters? Because a lot of them time you get the same loot you have already seen before hand.Also the difficulty level at the start of the chapter does not scale up to the Lore gained? So in For the King 1, you could increase the difficulty level to get MORE Lore in dungeons and stuff. And this is the way I liked to play it! But this version does not do that? You can make it harder; but it will be for nothing? Set the chapter to easy and then complete a dungeon, you will get 6 Lore. Now start again and set the chapter to hard and complete the same dungeon, you get 6 Lore? See? I don't know why?Lastly, I have only one more issue with the combat. I want an option in menu to speed up combat. Combat attacks and counter attacks are WAY to slow. In the beginning I didn't mind it. But later when I'm trying to get it over with, its just takes too long, you know? (Update) there is a setting in the menu to speed up combat. Omg. I didn't see it. Its in there...Overall the game is still pretty fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Gamers are so annoying. This game released in a non-perfect state with some annoying bugs, but 99% of them were fixed by day 3. So many unedited reviews leave this excellent sequel at "mixed" when the only lingering issues are a UI that leaves a little to be desired and a couple minor bugs. Otherwise, this is a direct upgrade to For The King, and the combat improvements shine. Even the story, which is not the draw for these games, is more appealing. There's actually a compelling reason to get behind what you're doing other than "go hit the bad stuff because pls help." Characters are great, traits are rewarding, tiled combat adds an extra layer to encounters, and the game looks beautiful for its simplistic style. The developers have said they're working on a QoL update, which will include UI changes. For The King 2 deserves to have those rushed negative reviews changed to positive at this point, but people today love bashing something and finding the next thing to overreact about. I don't review games typically, but I'm hoping this can help push it to "positive" instead of "mixed," which it so clearly does not deserve.

_childDocuments_.review: An important caveat - I am primarily a solo player in FtK. That being said, I  think a lot of the hate this game is getting is unwarranted. For those who played the first game, FtK2 feels like an upgrade in every sense of the word. The combat is almost wholly reconfigured, with a drastic improvement to turn economy as well as a deeper tactical element when it comes to tile repositioning, AoE damage planning, and a whole host of new items and weapons that bring in exciting different strategies. To add, there are new characters, events, and surprises around every corner. If you had any semblance of enjoyment in the first game, I highly recommend checking this out.All this being said, the game is not without its bugs and flaws. These feel primarily on display in online multiplayer sessions with more than 2 players in the party. We’ve seen issues with network connections, bugs that stop combat music, bugs where the save state seems to be out of sync with the board causing new hex tile events to stop spawning until a quest obj is started, bugs that soft lock certain dungeons from progressing, etc.. What I have also seen though, is a very motivated and dedicated development team doing the most they can to reconcile these bugs and remain openly transparent with the community. If you’re on the fence about 2 at all, I advise you to pick up the first game and get a feel for the mechanics and playstyle to see if it’s for you. If you played and enjoyed the first game? This is a no-brainer pickup in my opinion. And much like the first, I suspect IronOak is hard at work on DLC for the near future.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to do this, I do, but as much as I love FTK1, this isn't there yet.  First, there is a much more noticeable delay between getting in to fights and loading back to the world map.  It's so much it really does distract from the game after a while.  Second, the evasion rate seems to have been severely buffed for enemies this game.  You can still win, but it is much more annoying to fight an evasive group.  The game, in my opinion, only allows a certain party comp to be successful.  Some of the classes just aren't good enough to even bother with or have horrible passives to against the basic enemies you will constantly encounter.     Finally, my biggest gripe is that it launched without some kind of longer mode.  The campaign is a bunch of small different acts where you have to create a new party each act and nothing carries over.  I'm not against something like this, but add in something that makes it feel like there is a reason to replay the previous acts.  For example, you can carry on an item.  Or some gold, or a random passive gets added to a new hero.  FTK1 made it seem like your characters could actually level a while and you became actual heroes.  Games seem to last days, if not weeks.  Here, the act is over in literal hours. My max level was 7 in any act, and you just start again.  It's not fun in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I think so far (5.4 hours in), this is a good game. The core gameplay feels similar enough to the first one that it isn't a departure, but feels like a good successor (like it should).Let me address some of the issues from other reviews based on my experience (not discounting, just offering a different perspective). 1. Multiplayer - Of the 5.4 hours played, 100% of it was in multiplayer. The first server we spun up, my friend was able to join instantly. We had no problems setting up the game and no major desync issues. We saw some similar desync that the first game had with arrows not being in the same position, but nothing game-breaking. After a couple of hours, we took a short break, a hotfix was pushed during that time and we both updated our games. Unfortunately, it broke the join functionality if a password was on the server. We removed the password and unlisted the server, and had no problems joining up. 2. Bugs - As far as bugs go, didn't encounter anything game-breaking or frustrating. There was a funny bug where two enemies would occupy the same tile in a fight, but that never caused the fight to not end properly or for us to feel overwhelmed. 3. UI/UX - is the UI basic? Yeah. Could it do with some type of theme to match the game? Yes. Is it horrible? No. It functions extremely well, it's extremely responsive, and easy to navigate IMO.4. Encyclopedia - I thought the search functionality worked exactly like I would've expected it to in a Wiki/Encyclopedia and when looking up things, I found them pretty quickly. Zero complaints.What I liked QoL:1. End screen on party wipe - seeing stats of each character was awesome2. Expansion of herb types and effects3. UI and navigation of UI feels more responsive than in the first game4. Hotbar on screen for itemsOverall: I think this is a great game. I'm enjoying it, and will continue to play it in the near future. I'm excited to see what the roadmap holds for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that the disconnection issues have been sorted for my buddy and I in the latest patch I can finally give this game a thumbs up. Although, there is still a bit of black screen flickering which only happens in this game for me so it has to be an FTK2 problem. I am sure there are some bugs here and there in the game but it seems to be generally stable, finally. FTK 2 is pretty much like FTK 1 except instead of having a grand adventure you have a bunch of different smaller ones which are the different acts of the game. We beat the first act being level 8 (14 is the max) and now we have to start act 2 with new characters. I know the devs have promised more items in future updates but I really feel like this is more of a an expansion to FTK rather than a completely new game. No matter the shortcomings, this is more FTK so I am really glad it is here and the co-op is an absolute blast. I am looking forward to finishing the game with my buddy and hopefully to future game updates that expand the content. I really also hope they add some grand adventure mode so we can get our characters to max level before the act is over. Sure, it was a super rocky beginning but you can tell the devs care about their game and are working hard on improving it. I can definitely recommend this game now. If you like turn based games then this should be right up your alley.Update: Well, I've played a lot more since the original review and have one major grievance - the choice to make the otherwise grand adventure split into smaller chapters where your characters do not persist from one chapter to the next, despite the story continuing even referencing your past deeds, makes almost no sense to me. The only reason I can think of deciding to do this is to get people trying out more classes than they would have if the characters were used until they die. The problem is that this makes it so right when you get great gear and really find a party synergy it is all ripped away from you and you have to start it all over again. This makes the progression feel extremely stunted an I think is a major detractor to FTK2. Despite the many improvements in FTK2 over the original I believe that the original is the superior game simply because the character progression actually feels meaningful where FTK2 just cuts you off right when your character is really coming together. I think the non-persistent characters and chapter story structure are what makes this game worse than the original. They were so close to making a game that completely eclipses the original but then decided to knee cap themselves in a very strange and frustrating manner. So, yes it is fun and I am happy I bought it and am playing it but I don't get the satisfaction out of FTK2 that I did out of FTK2. I really hope they decide to remedy this and add in grand adventures with higher level caps as an unpaid update as that should have been in the base game.

They added more and more unnecessary things to the game like hyperinflation, random movement slowed by nearly everything in game, your class may be nearly useless because you never get a weapon drop, and breakable items that can be stolen.  Yes we need adversity but stacking it again and again just takes joy out of the game.  Buy something else.Just for the game makers:  hyperinflation is just foolish.  You never have enough money anyway.  In FTK 3, if it is made, simply have a coin drop for level one and then as things get harder add the character levels to the drop rate.  If level 1 is 10 coins level 4 is 14 coins - see no need for inflation at all.  Breakable items is okay but in one fight I broke 4 weapons in one battle on my scholar. _childDocuments_.review: I'm updating my review because the devs have reached out and actually listened to their base by removing the FOMO scourge from this game. I applaud them and thank them for this. However, I still can't recommend FtK2 just yet.The new grid system, and the floor traps that go along with it, have added nothing to the flow of the battle, and have just made me rage quit several times. It's a misery. The RNG is already punishing enough without adding this random element of chaos, and it feels cheap. I have no suggestion to make it better - it needs to be removed from the game completely IMO.I need to be able to move the camera in battle. Seeing what's going on is also an infuriating struggle, and too many times I lost turns by attacking the wrong enemy or moved to the wrong grid square just from the bad camera. The UI, in general, is still an unintuitive mess. The classes now have preset faces and headgear which infuse a personality into characters and removes the player from the role playing aspect which made the first game such a joy. If I want to play as an alchemist, unfortunately that means playing as a hag. I can't vibe with this decision.FtK remains a unique experience that makes time with friends an absolute riot, but right now, FtK2 is simply not fun due to so many half-baked new additions that have bogged down the flow of the game and the sense of reward. If you spend time reading these reviews, you will see that FtK has a very passionate fan base becaue FtK is so great, so if Iron Oak continues to iron out all these problems, and continues to maintain a good relationship with their base, their first free weekend is going to be a monumental turn around for Ftk2 and the studio.

_childDocuments_.review: Tricky to truly recommend primarily because it’s virtually identical to For The King 1 (FTK1). If you liked the first game and want more then go for it, but if you haven’t played the first then it might be better to just get that as it’s a bit cheaper and has a bunch of content already. On the flipside, FTK2 already has a good amount of content, and it seems there'll be plenty more free content on its way too.Nice elements include that FTK2 now supports four heroes instead of FTK1’s three. Three was always a little tricky if you were playing with two people as you'd either have to share the third character, or one of you only plays one. With four characters then a 2-2 split is obviously nicer, and, of course, opens up opportunities for four-player friend groups.The introduction of the battle grid, with its positioning mechanics, adds a little extra depth to combat. I didn’t feel that the original game really lacked for combat depth considering what it was trying to do, but the additional depth in FTK2 doesn’t hurt it. Something else nice is that there seems to be a good range of weapon and armour options that also add to the combat considerations. Plus the secondary action system lets you switch weapons in combat (which previously took a whole turn to do in FTK1), so you get you more options to adapt to enemy line ups.On difficulty, a lot of people talk about FTK2 being punishing, but – and this could just be my experience with the series and optimisation board games in general talking – I genuinely believe FTK2's more lenient than its predecessor, at least for the first two scenarios. FTK1 did  mess about, for instance, if you didn’t have some upgraded weapons by the first dungeon then your run was dead in the water. However, I’ve found I’ve been able to get by in FTK2 with worse equipment for longer than I would’ve been able to in FTK1, and I feel I can recover from hard fights easier. I can’t deny that my experience with both games has helped me: knowing when and which fights to take, when to use focus, when to takes chances, and numerous other little efficiencies make a big difference. If you like optimising then the FTK series practically begs you to do so because you can struggle if you don’t. However, like I said, I think FTK2 is a little gentler overall. If you’re new to the series then you might not feel that on your first few outings, but I assure you that, with a little knowledge and a keen eye on efficiency, you’ll find yourself finishing ‘easy’ difficulty scenarios without too much stress.There’re a few things I like less. The new, higher battle camera angle doesn’t let you feel as involved in the action as the first game, even though I suspect it’s a necessary element to help players manage the new battle grid. This is particularly confusing because a lot of the game’s store page screenshots indicate that the side-on battle camera is still very much in use, which clearly isn’t the case unless I’ve missed a setting. To remedy this, I’ve found you can switch the camera dynamism setting to high and it’ll zoom around a bit more, but it’s not quite the same. Also, despite the higher angle, the larger combats still manage to get a bit cluttered if there’re a lot of enemies. Enemy health bars and statuses can be hard to read compared to FTK1, and, while you can select enemies to get a box in the corner with their information, sometimes even selecting enemies for this purpose (or for attacks) can be fiddly too.Other negatives include the UI, which was a mess in FTK1 and apparently hasn’t changed in this one either. For instance, swapping equipment between characters is a hassle. I get that they want characters to be next to one another to swap stuff, but at least let me view multiple characters’ inventories at once so I can drag stuff between adjacent characters and compare things quicker. Instead, I have to look at one character’s equipment then swap to another to look at theirs, then select something to unequip it, then click it again to send it over, then another press to equip it there, then possibly send back the now unequipped piece. Just horrid. Particularly bad in a game where you can optimise things like accessory swapping outside of combat to help with whatever each character is doing in the overworld as part of the min-maxing the game's difficulty is begging you to do.Overall though, it’s a decent romp, particularly if you liked the original, but developers, IronOak Games, by and large have just made the same game, even keeping special abilities and attacks from previous classes and weapons. I don’t dislike the game at all, but I don’t know if the changes (good and bad) really make it value for money over just playing the original. Ultimately, it’s up to you. Both are decent games, and I’m sure FTK2 will continue to receive support for years to come, but if you already have the original and haven’t done everything in it then you won’t be getting a significantly different experience by coming over here instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Launch day bugs were a mess even after the closed Beta. Would have benefited from another open Beta. I wanted to love this game, I really did. This game kicks you when you are down and reminds you of your place in Fahrul.The first game is fantastic. I take issue with the accuracy of what a 95% chance to hit really means, but I got over that. This game: The 5 chapters have zero character continuity. You restart your progress over and over and......over. This is rough because levels 1-3 are brutal. The rogue-lite mechanics don't ever seem to swing into your favor. 9/10, the Lucky scourge will be the first to conquer and not only do you lose out on valuable loot at the beginning of each run, the scourge doesn't spawn close. Early game companions are clutch such as the Wolf and Eagle. Late game companions are trash such as Sunderbone. Not everyone is going to complete each adventure on their first try. There are multiple secret items in the game and no context on how to find/stumble upon them without diving into the discord community(super helpful). There is a large amount of information that is not explained in the moment, both game mechanics and objective details. When I finished all 5 chapters, it was a relief that I didn't have to keep going, not a sensation of joy and accomplishment. As a product to play, this game is nearly mechanically sound. It works just as the devs designed. I just can't admit that I had "fun"I thank the entire team at IronOakGmaing for their incredibly hard work in crafting this world and opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: Might have just gotten lucky compared to some of the other people reviewing, but was able to play 4player multiplayer for ~3 hrs last night with no issue for anyone.  We weren't all off work and able to start until the first hotfix patch was already deployed, so that may have had something to do with it.  But it kind of kills me to see nearly 50% mixed reviews on this wonderful game at launch.Of course, there are some features that you may have enjoyed from FTK1 that are not present on launch.  But personally, I am enjoying the clean and updated graphics, as well all the new features that were added which I've experienced so far.  Playing as a new class (stable-boy) with some new weapons on a new campaign with a new battle system and the same old friends (except now my wife is also playing b/c we can have four in a party now!?)...it's a great time.Sure, I have a wishlist for things that could be improved - hover-tooltips for expanded info without having to open Encyclopedia, more salient pings, more vibrant colors for some map icons, etc. - but the core of the game is still FTK, and that core is great.  I feel that the game still has soul & charm just like the first.  We're having a blast.Everyone is entitled to their own opinion, but some of the doom & gloom posts over this launch are over the top IMO.  That being said, if you truly don't to deal with any bumps or want a 1000% polished experience, maybe give it...a week?  A month?  Idk.  They've been super responsive and working hard to patch things in the first day, so I don't think anything broken will stay that way for long.All that being said - I would recommend this game in good faith.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I'll join the minority and take the side of an unpopular opinion.Yes, the devs did an oopsie because the UI is absolutely horrible in every way, shape and form.Yes, they had enough time to address all of the issues.Yes, it looks like the game hasn't been play tested at all.Yes, it WAS unbalanced in terms of "chaos."No, the game is not unplayable, so stop exaggerating with all the negative reviews.Honestly, just looks like the devs have improved in what the first game didn't have, but on the other side, they worsened everything else the first game did right.Though the improvements outweigh the setbacks so I personally don't mind. The combat is much more interactive as you're forced to move around with your character and talk to your fellow adventurers even more about what to do next.Finally playing as 2 players gives 2 playable characters to each of you and you no longer leave that one friend behind just because the first game was for 3 players only.Items are finally more unique than ever, with some random stats (not always) added each time you find them so each character can technically use all of them at this point.The lore store looks better than in the first game, my favorite part is being able to buy more items for your "loadout" phase, where you select what to bring with you at the beginning and also the traits, oh yes.Despite everything, the devs are tirelessly working on throwing patch after patch (even though it's not the patch we're all waiting for, it's coming in December), so give credit where credit is due.I still recommend this game despite it's noticeable flaws, it feels like playing the first game for the first time again. Stop crying.7/10 - For now.EDIT (1st of August 2024):- Also made first half of my (old) review slightly better to read. To each their own.After many bug fixing and QoL, the devs have listened and fixed most, if not all the issues that have arisen on launch.You see, if the first game was great, why couldn't be the second? I keep my positive review.I find it insanely hard to believe from all the negative reviews that the game is bad, even as a FTK1 veteran (you won't find the game on my profile since I own it on a different platform) that there are any bugs.I can count on both my hands the amount we've had a connection issue as a 4-player party across all my 100 hours as of the time of this review, and no, we had no game-breaking bugs nor any other reasons to dislike playing the second game. (Apart from the campaign being chapter-based, but that doesn't make the game bad.)For people who leave a negative review due to difficulty and other related things, skill issue. Our group finished the game multiple times even before the devs have started fixing things. (Normal mode was fairly easy for us, so I don't grasp the reality of people complaining about easy mode being dififcult... Nowadays, the game scales enemies based on the amount of party members.)Today I would give it a solid 10/10 - Single-chapter campaign when?

_childDocuments_.review: I think the reviews emphasizing the bugs are a little over-dramatic. There were a few very major bugs at launch, but there were also 2 Hotfixes rolled out in the first 24 hours to address some of the most serious problems. I respect IronOak's urgency and dedication to making sure the game is fun and functional for their most passionate customers. Overall, the game is a step up from For The King 1 in terms of overall quality of life and presentation, and I also like that the story is a continuation with some cute references here and there to the events and characters of the first game. POSITIVES:+ More players in multiplayer!+ Difficulty feels pretty darn challenging, but manageable for experienced players or those who put in time+ Enemies on higher difficulties aren't just damage sponges, they have improved AI and decision making skills+ The games each feel very lengthy and in-depth+ Some new classes to shake up the formula+ Soundtrack is still as impressive and whimsical as always+ Overall polish of the game sans the few serious day 1 bugs is solid+ Lore points shop is a great encouragement to explore everything and achievement hunt+ Transferring games between single and multiplayer is a really cool feature+ Story is still fun and doesn't take itself too seriously (Looking at you, Boner)+ Combat animations range from super cool to hilarious, and it's always fun to watch enemies ragdoll when you kill themNEGATIVES:- The UI can feel a little clunky at times, especially in multiplayer where someone else taking an action makes you not able to interact with the UI during that time- Why can I see the enemies' debuffs on their health bars but I have to look in the bottom right corner of the screen for the ones on my characters?- Multiplayer can be a little laggy- A few lingering bugs, annoying but not even close to a dealbreaker- I think the early game could've done with a little more variety compared to the first game- Despite loving the length of the game, I think there needs to be alternatives to just sitting down and playing a whole campaign- Mercenaries are a great addition overall (I love the Spider pet!), but they feel just a little half baked and under-explored. Being able to find permanent party members or taking on a hard challenge to get a rare permanent teammate would've been nice, and not being able to control them is frustrating sometimes.I think the game could benefit from some ironing out of simple problems and some more depth of content, but if you were a fan of the first game you'll most certainly find something to enjoy here. Two thumbs up for RPG lovers, DnD players and fans of the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:  If you liked the FTK1 then you'll probably like this game.  It brings back a lot of the fun (and anguish) of playing with the RNG Gods.  (Gotta love those 89% misses!!!)You can have up to 4 players in a party.  FTK1 only had up to 3.  The expanded battle zone keeps things interesting.The loot drop rate seems a lot more generous compared with FTK1 (although some of what drops feels like incremental upgrades).The Bad:  A few mechanics are a bit worse compared to FTK1.  My friends and I don't recall there being load times before and after each battle and noticed them immediately in FTK2.In FTK1, each player was always able to simultaneously view special vendors (such as night markets) on the campaign map.  In FTK2, the only the active player can view the shop's inventory.  They have to leave the shop before it becomes viewable to everyone.  I'm not sure if that's intended or a bug.The balance between some classes seems a bit off.  The farmer seems far superior to the blacksmith due to the proc rate of their passives.  I recently finished Chapter 2 with an alchemist and only ever crafted 1 potion the entire run.There are also some minor bugs such as some goblins not losing their immunity even though they had the wet condition.  Overall, it's a fun game to play with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, an improvement on For the King.There's a lot of problems I've noticed for the interface though. As an example, there are a lot of instances where it would be nice to be able to check your character's inventory, but you just can't. Or there's no way within the game to check what a tile's status effect is or does. There's no way, even within the in-game encyclopedia, to find out how a weapon being breakable actually, you know, worksAnd the info expansion system, of hovering over a word to find out what it does, works pretty well, when it works..Sometimes it just kinda doesn't, or there's no way to access what you'd need toI hope, in time, they polish the game more, and iron out a lot of these quality of life problems. But it does say something that the game has been out for over a year, and there's still countless UI problemsAlso, one thing I noticed on my first play-through. The way the game's story is told, it really encourages you to rush, and finish objectivesBut that's not reflected in the actual gameplay. You aren't rewarded for example, saving resistance members as quickly as you can. You're rewarded for taking as much time as you can lollygagging until the last second, because you get loot and xp from combat encounters and other events, not progressing the story. And progressing the story faster than you need to doesn't give you what you would have gotten from grindingJust, a little bit annoying for a new player. You try and play the game at face value, and inevitably loose because you're underleveled. So you have to then break immersion and play it in the grindy way so you actually have a chance

_childDocuments_.review: a fun and fulfilling improvement to the original. _childDocuments_.review: For the King 2 is an old-fashioned sequel. It takes everything fun and fantastic about the first game, and just builds on it. New regions to explore, a really rewarding loadout system, combat is engaging and challenging. A lot of folk are complaining about how hard it is. It's a roguelite game, it's meant to be challenging but honestly, it's really not once you understand what the threats are. It has some minor launch woes. Matchmaking and multiplayer is a bit buggy to start but in the game itself, very few issues.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: A definite upgrade from the first game.  The graphics are an improvement IMO.  And everything feels a little cleaner and sharper.  The gameplay loop is very similar to the original.  I think many of the complainers have forgotten that dying is part of the game when you start off.  That said its not impossible though with some skilled gameplay.  A few annoyances ought to be addressed.  Namely:- The camera angle on fights is a bit wonky.  A few options here would be appreciated.- There are some bugs on the map with locations disappearing and then reappearing. - Im not too keen on the fog of war as it makes seeing which biome is where a little difficult.Nothing that a few patches will sort out though.  And the devs seem to be listening and responsive.  So im pretty confident this will live up to its predecessor.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Too easy, too many major changes that I personally dislike (combat turn/speed system, boat system, taunt, starting items, classes all play basically the same way as each other, no real chance for long build up of gear and levels because every campaign section/chapter is so short) and overall, if I wanted to play an rpg like this, I'd just play the original, that one was actually challenging (this one, with 2 friends we've already blown through about half the game in around a day or two, less in terms of actual playtime and so far our "strategy" has been "big number funni", admittedly only on apprentice, but compared to the original? where even on the easiest difficulty if you didnt take things seriously (at least just starting out) you would lose? has a disappointing lack of "game over" and actually difficult combats. Hardest part is the boredom and tedious fights.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: : Loved the first For the King game, but the sequel is a mess. The other reviews claiming they have fixed the bugs are wrong, there are still a lot of game ending bugs. But we can forgive the buggy launch as they are taking steps to fix it & we're shell-shocked gamers jaded by the industry already. This game would be funner if we didn't have the first one to compare it to. They've changed enough to make the game feel fresh, but they haven't improved it enough to renew the sense of adventure. It feels like less of a indie work of passion and more of a soulless sequel launched too early.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the first FTK, and this is definitely an improvement. It's fun, and has a lot of new features over the first FTK, but the bugs are glaring. (I only play multiplayer, I've heard its not as bad in single player but I have no clue)-You can't pass traps to people who have the right stats for disarming the trap, the menu acts like it gets passed but it goes right back to the first person who had it.-Rarely, you may fail a stat check, or trap disarm, but other players will see it as passed and continue adventuring, meaning the run is now separated into two different instances, forcing a restart. If you had to restart after a trap disarm, you are now forced to clear the dungeon while controlling your friends characters due to there being no party management inside dungeons.-Disconnecting or crashing in certain spots can cause issues, massive ones. We crashed right after a fight as it was going back to the map, causing a run ending bug to occur. Every menu popped up at once, with filler text, and no menu would close, no buttons were intractable, and no keyboard buttons would function, causing an ALT+F4. Reloading the save file wouldn't work.We still managed to complete chapter one after 15 hours, and 3 restarts (In which no restart was due to a party wipe, just bugs). I love this game still, and the developers do seem to be working on the bugs, but as it is right now I can't recommend buying it for multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: Literally unplayable.Loved FTK, want to love FTK2. I was putting up with all the jank and the new ui and liking the new mechanics and reworked classes, but now the game won't even launch. I'm stuck at a black screen no matter what fixes I've trawled from the internet to try, and nothing works. I keep uninstalling and reinstalling, and when I verify my game files through steam it always says there's one file that's a problem and that it's fixed, but I launch the game to a black screen again. We just finished the trudge through chapter 3 but now I can't play at all to see if it gets better or not. I've anticipated this game for a literal year and it's so crushing to have to fight through all the bugs just to finally be denied the ability to play at all.Edit: Less than 24hrs after I posted this the devs pushed an update that fixed the black screen issue and I was able to play again. _childDocuments_.review: My friends and I (3 people) absolutely loved the first one and played it again and again and even bought the dlc. We looked forward to this sequel an we weren't disappointed. _childDocuments_.review: While what's there from FTK 1 is good and expanded upon, the game is released as a buggy mess. Minor bugs such as a textbox with "X has joined the adventure!" not disappearing, the game not telling you you're in a invisible submenu and as such not allowing you to do overworld travel, to major bugs not allowing anything to be done in a dungeon leading to us all having to quit the game, to actual desyncs where combat goes different for each person playing the same session. The devs did not playtest or have enough QA for this one, and it shows. Very sad as my friends and I were looking forward to enjoying this game. Hope it gets patched to not be this horrible over time, but games should not be released in such a mediocre unfinished state. I don't recommend this at all.Edit: Most of the bugs are fixed at this point, but that doesn't excuse the horrible state of the game at launch, a large portion of those (gamebreaking) bugs could've been found if they simply playtested their own game for multiplayer, which it advertises as an option to play the game. The ever growing practice of releasing games in unfinished states (which was very clearly the case here, an extra week of polish would've solved all the issues) has to stop somewhere, so I'm leaving the negative review up. I don't recommend supporting this kind of game development.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game because it is fun and you will have a good time playing with friends, but not because it is good.Sadly, with FTK2 the devs missed the mark so far. I'm saying so far, because it's still getting lots of stuff added and fixed. But some stuff seems to be intentional and some of that is really bad.First off, the UI design and control just got a much worse from the first game. I don't know why they decided to remove easy access to the inventory from fights or why they made it so much harder to identify which buffs or debuffs a character has, but it must have been a concious choice by someone that someone else apprpoved of.The Design of the adventures feels lazy. Sure they are way more packed than in the first game and overall a little more exciting, but tbesides some new purely annoying mechanics they don't bring anything great to the table. The level distribution of enemies on the map feels random at times. Sometimes you will be heavily overleveled, sometimes 2 levels behind. All by just following the main questline.The classes feel mostly underwhelming. The special traits feel much less impactful than in the first game and the stats in combination with the weapon choices just make every run a "we play whatever we find and it works anyway" instead of a "I want to specialize on this and play my character my way". I like some randomness, but I'd also like to play a whacky strat that I came up with, not one the game force onto me. I think the class selection should be more impactful and so should be the type of weapon you play.Ontop of that, there are just a lot of time-filler in the game that is just there to stretch out gametime. Like every quest will need you to walk way across the map, then it will rain 90% of the time and oh also there will be swamps which gut your movement entirely. On a ship you can encounter the kraken which is not just a an incredibly difficult boss, but also has no loot or even reward xp if you manage to kill it.Bards, which were an iconic class in the first game and beloved by the community are still missing. I really hope they will at some point add mod support via steam workshop to keep the game interesting and fun - but they will probably make the same bad decision as with the first one (where the feature got cancelled).Overall, the game is fun because the concept is fun. Everything else is lacking though. I would also probably not recommend it for solo players.

_childDocuments_.review: So I see the reviews are "Mixed".I wasn't on release but it seems a lot of the hate comes from the period of time, anyway....For those who are curious to how good this game is?It is good, very enjoyable.It has great mechanics which were added, fixed, developed from the previous one, I will list some below:* Actual tanks, you can taunt as a bonus action which is huge in my book.* armor/magic resistance feels good and rewarding.* online works well for us, no issues.* shopping, questing, traveling seems to have more to them.a down side is that it feels "built" for 4 players... I don't know if there is a scaling factor or not but playing duos is very hard.. the second campaign had us dead for about 10 times but the first 4 characters (2 players) we ran was a hit.some conclusionsif you enjoyed For the king 1, I cannot see how you will not enjoy the second one. :)

_childDocuments_.review: So far enjoying the game although there are a few concerns over some of the UI based issues which are echoed throughout the comments and arguably a few balancing issues (some fights seem a little over the top, could be due to balancing a party of 4 rather than 3 in FTK1) but otherwise a decent game albeit it does seem a larger expansion in many ways rather than a sequel (I may not be far enough to see any massive changes outside of some of the combat changes).BreakdownFew QoL things that could be handy - Appreciate the fixed camera style, however if this moves occasionally for an action cam perhaps a little freedom of movement would go far to appease some of the "cannot see model X Y Z" Alternatively a way to phase out units could be useful? either as a group or individually.More UI tool tips, as someone who hasnt played FTK for a long time I completely forgot what tool tip was what and what abilities characters have. A mouse over tool tip or quick explanation upon seeing an icon or ability the first time would be super helpful to those who may not be aware of the encyclopedia or be daunted by a wall of text.Better stat accuracy/transparency, without knowing what you roll and being given either a success or a fail it does feel like you're being cheated at times. A numerical value of what's needed for a success would be wonderful but may make things a bit too busy!Quick Restart button - Going through all the menus when you utterly fail your run if a little crushing at times.Minor bug bares - Needs more Events, doesn't feel like there are that many left in the game to discoverEnemy balancing, some of the enemies feel veeeeery strong early game (which isn't always a bad thing) but when you're ambushed on turn one by something you have no hope of defeating with a full party it feels a little mean spirited. Perhaps a drip feed in difficulty to be ambushed from level 1 onward may be a fairer mechanic or after X item amount.Duplicated abilities/characters, the abilities of both the farmer and the shepherd feel a little under thought.Either combine both or remove one and insert X class here alternatively add a different ability as it's not needed twice effectively.Differing abilities could be focused more on healing with the class via food items/godsbeard for example.However, the wolf on the shepherd RNG is pretty fun when it pops. (The farmer feels like the worse of the two classes).Still enjoying this alot however and will continue to do so, looking forward to the infinite dungeon mode!Thanks Devs!

_childDocuments_.review: In the week since launch I have thoroughly enjoyed this game just as much, if not a little more, than the first. The new combat system adds a lot to what the first game had. Having 4 party members as opposed to 3 changes the ideal party composition, and makes splitting the party less of a death sentence now that you can travel in pairs. Separating the combat turn into primary and secondary actions has also been a cool change to see. Swapping weapons during combat in now a viable option to cater to the threat at hand. Now you can use your secondary action to switch out to a different weapon and still be able to attack on that same turn. I am still trying to figure out the best strategies with the new grid based layout, but so far it has been much more interesting and dynamic than the straight up 3 on 3. If you enjoy turn based RPGs, I would definitely recommend.

Really seems like they balanced all the big fights where each person would have a mercenary with them as well as a ludicrous amount of healing.Pro tip for anyone who wants to beat the game without thinking, evasion is king.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time tabletop, role-play game fan, For The King II presses all the right buttons for me. Pushing my luck leads to rewards or wallowing in sorrow, but there’s always one more turn waiting for me. Runs great on my rig, fast load times, unobtrusive tool tips, and enough UI customization for comfort. Incredibly high resolution assets look great when zoomed in on the map, and the colours really pop. The Royal Tutor never feels in the way while stepping you through the initial run through the game, making it feel like a trusted advisor rather than a tutorial. A well polished package, a worthy successor to For The King - and I’m certain hours and hours of fun ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I came back to re-review the game after playing it for some time. I've beaten the full campaign, played it through solo and with friends, and my review of the game is still NEGATIVE. My complaints down below have not changed whatsoever, For the King 2 is still a buggy mess even after over a month of launch + updates. There's more bugs than before, more softlocks than before, and the past few updates have been trying to address these only. The most recent patch is the first to address any QOL changes, but the bugs / mess are still there.  This game hasn't changed, even with the 1.1 Update. The developers will need --> A LOT <-- of time to fix this game and get it to to a polished feel. It's beyond absurd that the first game they created feels incredible to play, then you play the second one and it's an awful, buggy mess. The developers deserve all the blame they getGenuinely disappointed by this release. So many bugs and glitches on launch, some were just clowny (not being able to move in overworld randomly). name: Company of Heroes 3
detailed_description: Digital Premium Edition For the true strategy game enthusiast. The Digital Premium Edition is the definitive way to experience Company of Heroes 3. Included content: Company Of Heroes 3 Devil’s Brigade DLC Pack Premium DLC Pack Expansion #1 [Coming 2023] Premium US HQ Cosmetic [Legendary] Premium Victory Point Cosmetic [Legendary] Premium US M4 Sherman Cosmetic [Legendary] Join our Discord Server
about_the_game: Company of Heroes 3 brings the series' acclaimed authentic and tactical gameplay to a stunning new setting. Immerse yourself in two epic campaigns, four unique multiplayer & co-op factions, and a breathtaking new theatre spanning from the sweeping deserts of North Africa to the rolling hills of Italy. Join the Fight with new features such as Full Tactical Pause and our Dynamic Campaign Map, which enable you to take complete control of the battlefield. The legendary strategy franchise is back! Company of Heroes 3 is the ultimate package of action, tactics and strategy. Take charge in the heat of real-time battle, then command as a General guiding the overall campaign where every decision matters. Overwhelm your opponents with four unique factions and all-new international Battlegroups. Command ground, air and naval forces and build supply lines to crush enemy advances on the new Dynamic Campaign Map - no two playthroughs are ever alike! Play at your own pace across campaign and skirmish modes before diving into blistering multiplayer action. Discover the untold stories of a stunning Mediterranean theatre featuring next-generation destructible environments, all powered by Relic's proprietary Essence Engine. Company of Heroes 3 delivers the next generation of acclaimed tactical gameplay. Beloved combat mechanics collide with authentic new gameplay features, making for the deepest tactical experience to date. ​ Make use of daring flanking moves to expose enemy side armor, experience all new infantry breaching mechanics allowing you to flush enemy units from their garrisons, and master elevation to enhance your line of sight and gain the upper hand. Welcome to the Mediterranean - a breathtaking new theatre filled with untold stories of war. Engage ferocious enemy forces across Italian mountain passes, breathtaking coastal vistas and the sweeping deserts of N Africa. Stunning visuals deliver authentic and highly diverse environments designed to keep you on your toes. ​ Mountainous maps will require uniquely different strategies from coastal towns, with verticality now greatly affecting units’ line of sight (True Sight). Desert plains will call for careful reconnaissance and daring armored maneuvers. On this new frontline, intelligence trumps speed and clever use of local terrain will let you bewilder your opponents and rout them from the field. Experience the biggest single-player campaign in franchise history. The new Dynamic Campaign Map delivers full ‘sandbox-style’ gameplay, allowing players to command the overall war effort and experience an unprecedented level of strategic choice. ​ Establish vital supply lines before deploying rear guard defenses to secure your advance. Launch air and naval strikes to weaken and scatter enemy forces or liberate a nearby town to develop a Partisan spy network. Choose your forces and upgrade your veteran companies to match your playstyle. Meanwhile, the optional Full Tactical Pause feature allows players total control over the pacing of single-player action. Plan your attacks, then effortlessly queue up lethal precision plays that will give you the edge in battle. Company of Heroes 3 promises to delight even the most ardent WW2 enthusiasts thanks to the largest number of launch factions in the series to date. ​ New army customization mechanics will allow you to call in the help of a varied cast of specialist units. Take up the fight with new elite squads including the American-Canadian Special Service Forces, the revered Gurkhas from the Commonwealth and many more. ​ From devastating tank destroyers to clandestine recon vehicles, Company of Heroes 3 features the largest roster in the series to date. The super-light Weasel, the armor-sniping Nashorn, and the Chaffee Light Tank are just a few of the units making their debut. Also, let's not forget revamped classics like the M3 Recovery Vehicle Halftrack, which can now be used to repair and steal abandoned enemy vehicles! Feel the blistering impact of every mortar shell and naval bombardment with Relic's state-of-the-art Essence Engine. In Company of Heroes 3, every location becomes a fully destructible sandbox, opening up limitless tactical gameplay options for you or your enemy to exploit. ​ Bring fortified buildings crashing down onto enemy squads, then witness enhanced destruction mechanics at play as soldiers exploit fresh ruins as dynamic cover. Stunning new rendering and particle FX technology depicts fire, sand and smoke like never before. Brilliant new soldier animations combine with enhanced AI, delivering realistic squad reactions to the battlefield. Optimized for DirectX 12 and multi-core CPUs, Relic's new engine technology will deliver cinematic action to rival any Hollywood blockbuster.

_childDocuments_.review: Would not recommend this game right now. I could go on and on.... the graphics, severe downgrade from COH2. The only upgrade are the animations for vehicle destruction being really nice. My units don't retreat when I say retreat. Instead, they stand there and get shot at and die despite having the retreat symbol above their head. I've got alot of experience of the COH games on both 1 and 2. Current smooth brain meta: German medical car. Use medical car literally anywhere in the first 5 minutes of the game, and you'll win. On some match, my 6 man US rifle squad chased down a 2 man assault gren squad. The 2 men run for like.. 300 meters ALL THE WAY back to the medical car without taking any losses, fully reinforce, turn around and attack my guys. I had to retreat. Apparently I have a better chance at winning the lottery than my 6 man squad not killing the remaining 2 in an assault gren squad despite them being shot in the back. Simple solution and I don't have to be a game dev to figure it out: if the medical car or the SQUAD is in combat, it cannot reinforce squads. Only halftracks should be able to reinforce in combat, that at least gives players more time before that halftrack gets out onto the field. Currently, frontline presence is way to strong with a medical car in the back just reinforcing everything, including blobsOther complaints:When I tell my vehicles to face forward, they do a couple of U turns before finally facing forward.Bersaglieri are now overpoweredEverything is way too bright Height advantage and cover are extremely inconsistent. My squads will be behind concrete and still not have green cover.Pressing R to reverse move vehicles is inconsistent, most of the time I have to micro the vehicles reverse retreat path alot just to ensure that the juicy fat ass rear armor doesn't get presented to the enemyBlobbing is still a problemAny unit paradropping anywhere on the map at the start of the game is terrible, this needs to be fixedFinal thoughts:Literally wait till this game is on sale for 5 dollars, don't spend 60 dollars on it. _childDocuments_.review: Time to ignore the old reviews!
