_childDocuments_.review: Company of Heroes 3 is a game that has not progressed beyond multiple beta tests packed with player input, and squandered a 4-month delay.Is it fun? A little. But it has a complete and utter lack of polish, attention to detail, or love. If you want to skip the details, go to the bottom two paragraphs.For starters, on Day One, tons of people apparently just couldn't start the game. Whilst I can't remember specifically who and why, and whilst bugs are expected on launch, something that bad and as a large of an issue as it was on the COH3 Discord is a very poor sight.The gameplay is competent, and has multiple additions which I was happy to see- For instance, tank riders. The tactical pause during campaign is also very nice. Cover is more useful than it previously has been. However, there are also additions, and lack of things that have been in previous COH games, that can dampen the experience. When giving a soldier a move order, you no longer see their exact route, just a straight line to where they're going, which can be a potential pain when planning. Repair times are horribly long. Your soldiers automatically vault over waist-high cover on route to an objective, and whilst to some this removes an inconveniences, I have a personal distaste for it.Audio is weak- I've been told it's to be "realistic", and "unHollywoodish". An explosion sounding weaker than a book dropping onto the floor (I actually dropped a hardback book on my floor to confirm if this simile was true) is realistic, apparently. Rifles sounded like me flicking myself with my finger at times. Voicelines for captured enemy vehicles keep the enemy voicelines. I captured an Opel Blitz when playing as the US, and the voicelines were still German-accented. At times, vehicles did not have engine sounds.Graphics are at a tier I consider on par with COH2. I don't really care for them- Not in the "I dislike them" way, but in the "they don't matter" way. However, there are details here and there left out. For instance, an Opel Blitz I used had wheels that just didn't move.Art is decent, but lined with faults. Various vehicles and weapons have icons reused from previous Company of Heroes games- Where they do not even belong. The M3 Lee's icon is an M4 Sherman from Company of Heroes 2, for instance. The title menu art has American soldiers wielding what look more like M14s than M1 Garands, rifles that weren't used until the Vietnam War.For Preordering the Deluxe edition, yes, shame on me for preordering a game in what was the year of our lord, 2022 (the year COH3 was originally going to come out), I received multiple skins for both Preordering and getting the Deluxe. They're... Meh. The infantry skins are especially low-tier meh. Armored vehicles, base, and vic point skins were decent enough.Speaking of skins, those are the only ones available as of right now. There is no leveling up system as of now as there was in COH2- Complete a match get 1500 points, win get an additional 500, and when you get 6000 total you level up and get goodies, for those who aren't familiar. However, there is a greyed out store option, which makes me nervous. I hope to God that they don't make most, if not all, cosmetics paid-for and add a leveling up system.NOT HAVING TO DO WITH GAME ITSELF: There has been a large amount of negativity towards COH3 from people who've played it, and at the same time many people love it. Some who love it are incredibly angry towards people with any negativity towards COH3- I have heard multiple times in the official COH3 Discord the idea that the reason this game's reviews are mixed is because of trolls and hate spam. Furthermore, saying anything even remotely negative has gotten some (including myself) insulted and berated. People who have said they don't like COH3 who also happened to play COH2 have been said to have invalid opinions for just liking COH2, for instance (though it might've been just a joke). Whilst this is a minority of the community, it is still definitely to note, as it is a relatively vocal one. I am actually allowing comments on this review so this vocal minority can provide me with some giggles.Overall, the game is competent but lacks anything that will make me truly enjoy it. It feels like a beta, filled with placeholders and concepts. And as previously mentioned: There was a four month delay! I couldn't even tell a difference between a beta version of a mission and its launch counterpart, which was before the delay.COH3 is missed potential. Check back in a few months.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:If you like the following:- Eating broken glass- taking your ex wife's mother out for dinner.- take comfort in dissapointment.Then I highly recommend buying this game.Long version:I would have to preface this by saying I have well over 3000+ hours in the COH series. I really enjoyed them. But this release has so many issues and so many deep rooted problems it is an insult to the series. 1.) GraphicsThe graphics are "passable" I regret the choices they made in regards to fully destructible enviroments. But the game was released with many problems in regards to its graphics. Issues that should have been cought in alpha testing.- Airplanes were metal silver cigars- the animations that some of the planes were doing were outright wrong or just downright comedic. A stuka bomb dropping down felt like a pinata coming down. There was no oomph at all.- The infantry units sometimes hold weapons to their feet all these things are graphical in nature but overall the atmosphere this game breathes is honestly cartoonish and not gritty. I prefer COH2 graphics over this one. I dare to say COH2 might look just better because it has a more gritty approach to things. Now it just feels like American GI on mediteranian cruise. - GameplayThe gameplay has a LOT of potential but sadly it is mired in many issuess that again show a depressing theme for this game's release. Its absolute lack of polish or beta testing.  From pathfinding being horrendous, to simple bugs making entire game plans useless. To list them:- Tanks cannot drive well at all they are slow and even after 3 patches it is still a crime to try and use medium tanks. - throwing satchels in specific ways on infantry means the bag will get glued to the unit and outright kill them. - Line of sight barely works as intended. There are situations where someone is standing 2 pixels higher than my infantry gaining the advantage of height and seeing my units get slammed.For lack of a better word the german faction just outright sucks. The units they get are all early war and mid war. While the allies get Easy eights, black princes and a wide variety of tanks. The current meta is swamped with Light tank spam and the germans have no viable counter to it.Marders barely work due to the way the turning and aiming works. The developers.My biggest issue is with the development team the outright disconnect between what they are doing and projecting to what are genuine concerns is painful. I miss the old relic with bugoo and where it felt like we were listened to. When 1.2 was released they buffed the air strafe and when I told the developers how this would ruin the multiplayer I was told that they had faith in the development team ad i had to wait 3 weeks to see how things pan out.After 2 days of having as streak of losses a hotfix was released to address an issue that was flagged even BEFORE the buff. On top of that all we read is how great the team is working. But the balance in the game is nowhere to be found. It isn't fun playing germans and we are locked into one commander. I sincerly hope relic can right the ship but at this point with the developers being scaled down i worry that we might end up with this being the lat product relic releases and I find that very disturbing.Maybe in a year with 2 expansions the game will be better but honerstly for me this game is a HARD no for anyone interested in new games.------------------------------------------------I have played an additional 103 hours and witnessed the updates and the revision is as follows:- The game has been improved in some ways normally I would laud it but 70% of what they fixed should have been there on release. There is no excuse. - Pathfinding is still broken period. this after 3 patches to "improve it" - The balance in this game is honestly offensive. Relic is NOT testing a single thing they release. The latest expansion basically added a massive desynch bug. Which can happen. But to see the artillery the germans get plaster the allies into liquid tommy isn't funny and it is a blatant oversight.In the end the game is Company of heroes 0.4. IF relic continues with patches and listens more closer to the community there is a game to be found. Sadly however a year later almost and so many things that feel not finished. I don't know what else to say. I only play this game with a friend but the inbalance isn't fun for axis or allies.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of CoH1 and CoH2 - however with all the hype around this game and subsequent flopped launch, I stayed away for quite a long time until recently. TLDR; I recommend this game - it is fun for me as a casual PVP player.I've seen a lot of bad reviews for this game for failing to live up to the standards of prior games, complaints about faction balance, etc. And yeah, admittedly there are a few rough points here and there. I don't think these criticisms are fair to say "this game if awful because I don't like x, y, and z". Instead, I'd balance it with pros and cons. In my opinion:Pros:-Well-paced multiplayer matches with a variety of strategies and units to choose from-Devs that seem to care about multiplayer balance and are frequently releasing patches-Great weapon / explosion sound design - feels gritty and chaotic-Clear visual graphics - easy to differentiate units/see what is happening on the field-Fun casual multiplayer experience (advise playing with friends as the community is a weird mix of super friendly and super toxic)-Factions do not have parity - that is every faction plays a bit different!Cons:-AI kinda sucks. The skirmish and coop vs. AI experience is not amazing. I think this has always been a problem with CoH though - I recall AI in CoH1&2 constantly running troops just to cap points and map hacking to avoid MGs. This hasn't changed.-The grand campaign is disappointing. Its a great idea - not executed well. The missions are awesome, the campaign skirmishes feel like lazy filler.-The unit responses and banter can be overwhelming. In big fights, your units talk so much with "fluff" it is easy to miss the important sound queues like a unit coming under fire or being destroyed.-Weird microtransaction garbage. I'm fine with skins - but the level of paywall to lock commander choices is disheartening. I've played 113 hours generally giving a decent amount of effort on earning the weekly and daily points and still haven't unlocked my first commander.Overall, I have had a lot of fun playing the game. If you've been skeptical to get it, but enjoy playing PVP - I highly suggest you give it a try once it goes on sale again.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited my review to change my negative review to a positive one, but with some remaining criticisms. The gameplay is amazing. This is the first strategy game in a long time to capture a similar feel to the golden era of strategy (Dawn of War, company of Heroes 1, etc.). The strategic and tactical elements of gameplay makes the combat feel extremely immersive and satisfying.My only complaint is the daily challenges are very tedious to complete (i.e., destroy 2 Sherman tanks with Wehrmacht infantry). Not only is it annoyingly specific, which forces you to adopt certain play styles just to earn valor, but the cost of cosmetics which can be purchased with valor is astronomically high.You will have to play dozens of matches to get a single skin for a single unit. But if you're willing to dish out cash, you can buy the same cosmetic for the equivalent of $1 or $2. Fingers crossed they fix this. As of now, I give the game an 8/10. If they address the challenges and microtransactions, it's an easy 10/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - After 100 hours game time, I can say that there are bugs, yes there are imbalance issues, but there are new additions to the franchise's game play that I love and overall, I'm not dissatisfied. 4 out of 5 stars.The bad:- Balance issues are present. I find the German artillery to be overpowered in comparison to that of the US and UK forces.- It's more of a minor issue, but I was hoping for a heavy armour anti tank option for the US. Though considering such options were not available en mass at this stage in WWII, it is acceptable from a historical accuracy perspective. - In the Italian campaign overview mode, I just don't see the point in having supply emplacements, the unit population cost is prohibitively high, and with the amount of airfields dotted about the map, why opt for spending a lot of resources on an aircraft carrier?- Command points in battles seem to have little to no use- The variety of game types (capture the flag, annihilation, attrition) cannot be selected and if, like me, you don't like the attrition or capture the flag styles, this can be annoying. I like long running battles, damn it!The grey area:- Yes, you can purchase aesthetic skins in game, though that's not really my thing. I like the standard skins that come with the base game. But that's no different to COH 2 and not detrimental from my perspective, so I don't know why there are so many reviews trying to incite lynch mobs to take up arms over it.- You have no ability to select or purchase different battlegroups (in COH 2 these would be 'commanders') in skirmish/online games. Though there does seem to be the footwork put in place for later content releases, but why not implement these at release? But there is enough variety currently to keep me entertained, so this neither a + or a -.The good:- The Italian campaign brings in a 'Total War' style of game play with an overview of the area of operations, which I massively approve of. - I don't know if it is just me, but the survivability of the US Sherman tanks in the campaign modes have been improved versus COH 2.- My PC is fitted with an 11400F CPU, a 4080 OC GPU, and I use a 60hz monitor with FPS limited to 60 accordingly. COH 2 barely ran above 35 FPS when set to max settings on 4k. With the same settings on COH 3, there is no issue hitting the FPS limit no matter how many units are on the field.- Speaking of graphics, it is a beautiful game!- Firing from an elevated position, this puts your troops in a position where they take less damage, and those they are attacking take more. I'm sure there are points I'm missing, but these are the main ones, and as I said, no I'm not dissatisfied with the game. Yes, it is rough around the edges and maybe it should have had more time being spent on the finishing touches before release, but the same was said about COH 2 before it, and I have racked up 1000 hours on that and still love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend the game, but with some reservations and in Retrospect I should have waited a few weeks for the bug fixes to get rolled out.  Note I am only playing single player, so my review doesn't comment on multi-player.Pros:1. Its COH, having played COH1 & 2, all the C&C games and Starcraft/Warcraft RTS of course I'm going to play it.2. Some of the Campaign maps seem realistic on the Italian Campaign and have villages, hilly terrain, etc.3. I like some of the new units that I don't recall being in previous COH games.4. It is fun, I already played this game way more than I thought I would since it released.5. Tactical Pause is great when sometimes you need a breather to think about things and come up with a strategy or assign engineers to setup defenses. 6. It has its exciting moments, like in the Italian campaign sometimes I ran into units I didn't expect like Brummbar or Panthers that were hull down.Cons:1.  I have a 2070 RTX which does ok, but seems to struggle more with COH3 than the other games.  So I only have most of my settings medium and don't feel like I'm getting the full graphics experience.2.  Additional point on graphics - on the Italian campaign main map view, the GPU gets around 70-80% and the fans spin up, I don't have this issue with Civ 6 for instance.  Seems like something is not optimal.3.  There are little annoying bugs, they don't break the game, but seems like some could get fixed.  For instance I have experienced when you faction  picks up an enemy's weapon - their voices change to the other teams!  Like Afrikacorps picking up Vickers or 2 pounder AT gun, they will get UK accents.4.  Italian campaign seems like its needs to adjustment - there is never enough Pop-Cap on the main map to have more than a few planes/ships with your companies and building defenses takes Pop-Cap so I only managed to build one defense on the map.  Axis team though seems to have a bunch of recon planes they are flying around.5.  AI in the campaign is sometimes buggy, on one map for instance it kept attacking me on the left side of the map and I just setup some defenses and units and wiping them out and the AI never took a run at my base or right flank.6.  Path logic for vehicles has some bugs - I started laughing a few times when I sent Greyhounds to a place on the map and set their facing and they get there and drive around in a circle a couple times before facing the right direction I told them too. LOL3-19-2023 updateI finished both the DAK and Italian campaigns.  I still keep my thumbs up for the game being fun in playing, but the Italian campaign was a bit of a let down on the cutscenes and the story, its essentially the 2 generals and the Partisans leader popping up and either agreeing or arguing.  Some of the missions have characters, but its just "pop-ups" of the portrait and them talking.  There were some other screens popping up with stuff to read like letters, but none of the good content I remember from COH1 or COH2 that had a story and real characters.  After finishing the last mission in the Italian campaign I was very underwhelmed by the cartoonist movie cutscenes.  All I could think was after all these years since COH2 waiting on COH 3 and all the time I spent playing the Italian campaign, this is all I get?  This is my reward for completing a bunch of missions and skirmishes and 60 bucks for the game??  Some leaders bickering and falling in love with each other and a cartoon at the end?  What a letdown.My other huge complaint is after finally upgrading my companies enough to call in the good stuff, like the Churchhill Black Prince or Easy 8, I barely got to use them.  Pop cap restrictions are also ridiculous on some missions and units.  So for a Sherman Easy 8 and rifleman call in takes 20 and then you are on a mission and only 50 or 75 Pop cap and then by the time you have enough command points to call one of the good units in, there's no pop-cap room left unless you "sacrifice" you existing units.  What happened to the ability to recall and take units from the field?  I'm pretty sure the COH2 Soviet mission let you do this.  Another major grip, what happened to reinforce?  So team weapon is down to 1 or 2 units, why can't I take a rifileman group and reinforce them?  Instead I have to get a Medical truck and drive it over there.

_childDocuments_.review: Did a bit of playing for this during the Free weekend.Despite my low hours it was very buggy, considering this has been out for over a year now it seems.It is still another COH game, so veterans or returning playing might like it just with how it is.... But that is a bit far from it.- The writing at least for the first couple of hours just feels so bad, like a college student's combination of a sitcom with WW2 history. They pit your commanders against each other is some middle school playground arguments. - Choices ultimately do not seem to matter much aside from prioritizing taking over certain portions of the map earlier than others, with little consequence of prioritizing one over another.- The controls are pretty off and very different from COH2 or COH. This could just be me needing to spend more time to learn or go over the options.- There are a ton of bugs, between Campaign breaking issues or AI, or Pathing for units.-- Had multiple instances of overworld emplacements suddenly re-appearing after a skirmish or mission when I had just destroyed them in the same turn.-- Instances of destroyed emplacements still mowing down companies -- AI will sometimes just move squads in or through heavily fortified locations, not even attack moving or moving to proper cover at times-- Had more than a few dozen instances of squads getting stuck with pathing to a location.--- Getting stuck in an endless mantle loop--- Getting stuck on stationary vehicles--- Getting stuck on destroyed vehicles--- Occasionally retreating to HQ despite a field Hospital set as an active rally/retreat flag-- Tutorial bugs of going to quick, getting locked out after building a unit too quick, making the objective not clear since it was not built after the OBJ was put on screenNote I have not tried multiplayer, but I personally enjoyed the COH series for its single-player campaigns and the coop missions. Really wished this was even worth the 30$ with it being on 50% sale, but I feel like I'd be more frustrated with the constant bugs and the subpar narrative/story.

_childDocuments_.review: I am in no way a long time COH franchise fan, though I played a good bit of COH2 online.  I'm a long time, top 100 Warcraft III competitive player, and master league SC2.  I have had the itch for an RTS for a long time now, especially with how bad reforged was/is.This ain't it.  I regret putting more than 2 hours into it, since they denied my refund @ 4 hours.  I'll keep this short - it just isn't fun.  Forget the glitches/graphics/audio/gui/etc.  The "core" gameplay is what everyone that is reviewing this game positively is focusing on.  Meh.  It's ok.  It has no grand scale feeling like a WWII game should.  It's boring.  It's a few guys with guns and then tanks and then the game is over.  Rinse and repeat.  Even at its best, which I have faith this game will be really good in say 3 years (when it's $20 or less on humble bundle) it still won't be that much fun.  It's impossible to not compare a modern RTS with SC2.  I get it, SC2 was like 3 major expansions and a ton of content patches and overhauls - but this game simply isn't even the same ballpark.  It can't hang.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a lot of fun with CoH3 so far. Yes, the single player is underwhelming, and yes, a release with lackluster social features and placeholder images in the loadout section is not something to be proud of. However: the multiplayer feels amazingly vibrant compared to the last installments. Factions are diverse, teching feels like an impactful choice, and a lot of counters are much more fun to micro. The battlegroups are also an absolute improvement over CoH2's commanders. With the frequent patches we have seen so far, I think CoH3 has a bright future ahead of it.Edit:CoH3 went through a long rough patch, and I hated the lack of progress. However, recent patches and the addition of new battlegroups have brought the game into a state that we can all be satisfied with. If the game would've released like this, it would have been received well. With more regular patching the future looks bright. Balancing is also getting better and better. Give it a try and have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Still a lot of work to be done on Company of Heroes 3 for it to measure up to the amazing Company of Heroes 2 but some good early signs and good enough elements...maybe not to buy it at full price but definetly when it gets discounted down to the $60-$70 range.  The positives are in single player in particular, the Italian campaign is really good in terms of being able to fight on tactical battlegrounds but also move units strategically through the Italian theater and complete different challenges and tasks.  North Africa leaves a bit to be desired, it's a shorter campaign where you fight as the Germans in a very straightforward manner reminiscent of the original Company of Heroes but it feels like a bit of a let down...comparisons will always be made with the Italian campaign and it seems backward and substandard compared with the multi-aspect control and more engaging game play you have throughout the Italian campaign.Multiplayer isn't too bad...but certain elements need SERIOUS, SERIOUS work.  Only one or two maps for 4v4 and three or four (I think?) for 3v3 is pretty disappointing, those maps get old QUICK. New ones have been promised in upcoming updates and they can't be added to multiplayer soon enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:-Four factions with new units/designs-Two campaigns including a very ambitious grand strategy campaign-Workshop support-Much faster load timesNegatives:-Bugs-No observer mode-There is in-game currency-The graphics are dated-Campaign 'tone' is completely off and the Italian Campaign seems unfinished towards the end.Relic are well known for patching and improving their games (look at COH2 at launch), but not putting 'Early Access' on the store page seems to have been their biggest mistake, and now most people will be scared off. Relic should have released this at half price, with only one campaign and two factions, under Early Access. Then raise the price as content is added. My guess is that they were concerned it would not look good in comparison to COH2 in terms of content, so they opted to get 4 factions and 2 campaigns ready, and fell short with polish, particles and map quantity. Since launch, most of these things have been improved, but I am still noticing the low detail of some models and animations.The mixed review score this currently has is disappointing. What makes it worse is that we have people posting joke reviews during the free weekend. One review had only played for 15 minutes (not enough for 1 match, so they didn't play at all) and listed complaints people had shortly after launch, all of which have been addressed. They just don't know what they are talking about! Combine that with people posting negative reviews to complain that one factions is more powerful than another (all factions are overpowered if you were to believe them all) and you get a very skewed idea of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: After 300+ hours my overall opinion is the development team at Relic took this game and broke it into many little pieces and gave us 20% at launch. It feels disingenuous, and that's before you get to the story of the game. COH and COH2 had some of the best WW2 stories in video games. COH3 is written by an MBA-brained drone who does not care at all about the NA campaign, the people, the tactics or the effect this titanic conflict had on our world. They shoehorn in a story that uses the people Bengasi as wallpaper. The narrator of the story compares the British to Nazis and implies that the fighting with them really doesn't matter, Then we get a story of what the writer really cared about, a young activist girl....The Italian campaign writing is just as poor but without the woke BS, while the voice acting is pretty stereotypical. The American sounds like a cowboy, the Brit sounds like a teacher, the Italian partisan woman is fiery, Oh My! I am glad Relic is an indy studio again, it means meritocracy will return to their firm and we will get better games, content and respect for WW2 and the people portrayed in the conflict. Overall you shouldn't pay more than $20 for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A sad decline for the series.  Going by the screenshots you would think it is business as usual but now in the North African and Italian theatres.  Unfortunately the game has really gone South with a bland and uninteresting attempt at making a Total War style campaign map that is rife with bugs and imbalances to the point that you just quit and move to comp stomping or PVP.  Comp Stomp is tragically awful with AI opponents that barely challenge you and currently in Co-op Vs. AI you can't choose difficulty which makes the matches even more tedious.Visually it looks fine but doesn't look that far removed from COH 2 in some areas and given this title was released on consoles as well (thanks SEGA) a lot of mechanics are downgraded to be playable on controllers.  Battle groups are bland and uninteresting and some are weirdly anachronistic.  The Black prince in Italy?  I mean it shouldn't be in any theatre of war since it never saw action.  Matilda II's rolling around Italian towns?  DAK units in desert gear fighting in Monte Cassino?  Sure, why not.  I know the series isn't hardcore realistic but Relic used to at least keep the units looking appropriate for the time and theatre of conflict.  Italy doesn't even get to be it's own faction in this game.  Sadly it just hangs on like a floater in the DAK battlegroup options rather than becoming its own faction to give you something genuinely new for the series.  It's not like Italy didn't have enough equipment to make its own faction from and given relic don't care too much about sticking to historical fact for some units they could easily have made battlegroups around adding vehicles like the P40, Celere Sahariano amongst some lend lease and captured equipment to make other groups from.  Relic have tried to improve the game since launch last year but none of the animal themed updates have really given the game the improvements it so badly needs.  At the time of writing this review they only recently added in the ability to customise your profile, but you better believe the cosmetic store was up and running week 1 with zero issues.  Want to have your infantry running around in some interesting unit specific uniforms or camo schemes?  Well screw you buddy, have brown instead.  The store features zero actual camo schemes or unit uniforms and just gives you the most generic "World War" alike schemes they could spaff out in a single afternoon now give them money on top of the money they already got off you for this tripe.I can say that on the positive side the voice work is decent in the English language version at least for the allied side, the German side had to have their voice lines reworked because it hurt the ears of German players so much.  Weapons sound ok but they lack the punch from previous games and the big boom artillery pieces don't smack audibly anywhere near as much as they used to.  Hell they don't even deform the terrain as much as they used to.  People being set on fire by flamethrowers looks cartoonish now with this odd flame effect that looks like it's attached to the character rather than actually looking like he is burning to death.  I recommend you pick up COH 2 if you haven't already since that game offers far more diversity of troops, units and maps alongside a healthy online community and a hell of a lot more mods.  COH 3 still has units from the campaign locked from online or co-op (Sherman II for instance) meaning these will be sold off in DLC chunks in the future to keep this zombie of a franchise still lurching forward.  I hope Relic have either a Dawn of War 1 remaster in the works or some new killer project because now they are independent they are going to struggle making any profit with this lacklustre effort.

Instead they decided to implement some stupid custom unit skins nobody cares about lol. We dont even have the time to look at them while playing the game, properly, at high level.Very few maps at launch (just stupid, should have at least 10 or more)* Some examples of missing UX features that CoH2 had and were essential:- Double pressing F1 no longer focuses on the base- Player colors are wrong- Can't see player names- Icons too small, no option to change size- Spacebar doesn't focus or cycle through last events- Events list on top of screen is too big and no option to change size, it just clutters the whole screen- When unit in group is selected through tab, the minimap highlights the whole group instead of the single unit that is selected (this was shown in coh2)- A bug in which player armies are wrong when game is on loading screen- Shift doesn't deselect units from group like in CoH2 (why the ♥♥♥♥ change this? why not keep backwards compatibility with your previous very polished very good game, specially knowing most of your CoH3 players will come from CoH2 and not from outside of it)- Attack ground makes tank stop and it doesn't fire immediately (unlike coh2 in which the tank kept moving and it would fire where you tell it to fire)Conclusion: overall just a downgrade from CoH2. _childDocuments_.review: I've got a ton of hours in coh2.Major disappointment. They ♥♥♥♥♥♥ this one up. Went for the micro transaction angle and launched an unfinished game with less soul and polish than their previous installments. Feels like they were preying on the shortage of high quality RTS games, hoping people were desperate enough to eat a plateful of dog turds. If this was relics first foray into the genre, I'd at least applaud their ambition, but from a studio with almost 20 years of experience putting out the third installment of their premier game, it's an absolute tragedy.·Graphics are not 2023 level -- probably about 2016 level (this series **was** known for it's visual fidelity.)·Games all feel the same. ·Animation detail is way lower quality than 10 year old predecessor. ·Unique faction mechanics have been flattened. No more russian zerg or british defensive playstyles. Everyone can generally do the same thing.·Vehicles are 'slidey' and have poor pathing. Planes flying in look like the invisible hand of a child is controlling them.·There are barely any multiplayer maps (some categories have 3.) ·Gamepace is too fast (you can play a game on all 3 of the 2v2 maps within an hour.) ·Main menu art looks like a high school wall mural.·UI both in and out of game looks like some weird free chinese game.·Massively reduced audio quality.        -10 year old Coh2 main menu would change it's scene and music (without missing a beat,) when selecting a new army.      -Gunshots, explosions, and voice acting have become much less intense. Particularly the voice acting. ·First pushed out "major" patch was... them rolling out the in game cosmetic store -- exorbitantly priced of course.Previous games were masterclasses. Incredible, unique pieces of work that pushed both graphics and the genre. This here is a soulless version of those classics. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. _childDocuments_.review: I've played COH1 solo and multi, skipped COH2 and gave COH3 a go so my opinion comes from comparison to COH1 mostly. I've only completed 2 campaigns and I'm not even touching the multi.In short: the game feels very nice and I enjoyed it but it's just damn too expensive for what it is, compared to COH1. Feels like a DLC for COH1 rather than a new game. EDIT: I'm changing my review to positive to show appreciation for Relic going independent. Game keeps getting updated and we've even got new  free battlegroups.The good:- Voice acting - awesome job on that front, great vibes like previous titles- German Campaign - in general it's fun to play, sometimes enemy units will spawn in questionable places but it's decent.- Total-War-style Campaign - cool idea, quite fun at the start but after a while it's a bit too repetitive though. Most missions are the same skirmish on the same map with the same company. The custom missions within that campaign and turn-based map features are fun nontheless.- Sound design - it feels well done but unfortunately we don't get any bangers like we had in COH1- Maps and enviorment design - multi level towns, curvy roads, variety of architecture and consistent aesthetics. The destruction of the enviorment feels great as well and the flow of each scenario feels intact with the maps.- No artillery spam - indirect fire weapons are no longer the only way to win a match- Nice variety of units, skills and vehicles, some of them are on the border of historical accuracy but it's not too much over the top.The bad:- EXPENSIVE - the game is WAAAAY too expensive for the ammount of gameplay it provides. This is the main reason I'm giving the negative review.- Short - I've finished both campaigns in 24 hours, quite disappointing.- Bugged - units often get stuck on each other, grenades/repair/artillery fails to work when ordered, units constantly fire at an obstacle instead of the target and other similar issues. There isn't a lot of it but it's noticeable.- Questionable AI - the tanks love turning their backs on every AT gun in sight, very often the reason why I'm winning is because the AI just fails so badly at commanding the tanks (infantry is much better though).- The story - An american corproal commanding a company of brits, Polish tanks capturing Monte Casino by riding behind the enemy lines, rescuing some lost unit in almost every mission, some random bloke from Benghazi reminding you after every mission that Germans are the bad guys in the campaign where you play as the Germans, some bloke writing unrelated letters about whatever to his family, brits driving through the same ambush like 10 times and so on... There is just so many things that are either unrelated, unhistorical, wrong or just dumb that it takes a lot of the immersion from the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game deserves a honest review by someone who has played CoH since 2009 (so 14 years) after all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. First, let us start from the disappointing things:1. Some icons are placeholders from CoH2, and this happens for a lot of units. For instance the DAK recon vehicle has the icon of the .50cal jeep from CoH2, one Marder III model (I think the M variant from Wehrmacht) has the icon of SU-85, and several others. This is simply sloppy. How long does it take to make a unit icon? 2 hours maybe? Come on Relic...2. Several basic features from previous games were or still are missing. For instance, at release, you couldn't queue orders in the tacmap, or capture points. Then they added it a few weeks later. You cannot see player names on units in multiplayer,  some tooltips are missing, and few other small things that make the game feel unfinished.3. After all the negative feedback, the devs did not change their road map and they still went for the in-game shop before prioritizing other vital things. This is simply a stupid move, most likely pushed by an idiot project manager/leader who should be replaced.4. No ranked multiplayer after 3 months from release. I can understand that you don't want to release it immediately to have time to balance the game, but now... What's the excuse?5. Poor map variety and they are mostly bad. Have the community build maps for you in an internal beta release.6. VPs bleeding is way to fast. Put back the old CoH2 system.And now for the positive things:1. New game mechanics, very well though: Elevation mechanics is great, basically if your soldiers are above the enemy, the elevation will negate cover. Towable guns are a great addition. Auto-vault is great. Really. Well done, we needed it! And tank riders, that is so cool and useful to move infantry around.2. Animations are way better than CoH2, in CoH2 every unit seems to move in slow motion, even when they aim, here they are more responsive, you see them slide into cover and duck. Tanks suspensions feel real.3. First CoH ever to release with 4 factions, and they weren't even that horribly balanced (still at release DAK and UK were OP but not in a critical way, except the Tiger reserve that got nerfed the day after they released the game).4. Finally after two games you can remap the keyboard.5. Nice SP campaigns for those who are interested.6. Old point system from CoH1, that is way better than CoH2. At least every game is not down to "cut the only enemy fuel point".7. Tank armour is way better, now StuGs are not made of cardboard and a Tiger feels like a Tiger and doesn't get denied by long-range cheap tank destroyers like in CoH2 (I hated that mechanic so much, why should a SU-85 outrange a Tiger or a Panther no one knows).8. No pay2win commanders, now we have 3 commander trees like in CoH1, way better to balance, but with more variety since some ability are exclusive and you have to choose which one you want. Way easier to balance. Probably they will release more in future, I hope not too many, otherwise it ends up like CoH2.8. Mortars and indirect fire weapons are really dangerous. If you get barraged by a mortar and you try to stick around you get wiped. MGs area of suppression is great and denies blobbers excellently (and maybe this is why there are a lot of people saying "CoH 2 is better", because the real problem with CoH2 is the total absence of blob denial cheap units. Yes you have MGs but they are not nearly as effective, and all heavy anti-blob is relegated to a high tier for a high fuel cost.Now let's discuss all the haters. Unfortunately, every time a CoH game/expansion is released, it is always the same story: Coh X was better than Coh X + 1. I have heard this with CoH2, it came out and everyone was "CoH 1 is way better!". There are still people saying that. CoH2 had its issues, but the improvements over CoH1 were many, first of all the sniper mechanics (the snipers with the predator suit were such ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I would never go back to that) and the true sight. Moreover these people do not consider a simple thing: CoH2 is a TEN years old game, and it was basically garbage until 2017. It took 4 years to bring the game to a balanced multiplayer state. FOUR YEARS. And CoH 1 is no less, everyone forgets that in competitive multiplayer basically every match is Wehrmacht vs USA because the other factions are STILL, after 16 years, broken beyond remedy. Maybe these people started playing CoH1 or CoH2 4 or 5 years ago, so they never saw the dark days of those games, or they forgot, but let me remind you:- Do you remember when Tales of Valor came out and the Kangaroo transport costed the same as a Panzer Elite 250, it had the health of a Sherman tank and you could basically load a bren section and a RE with PIAT and base rape the opponent unless he spent all the munitions in the world to mine every possible meter of the battlefield? And the 250 AT halftrack with the thread breaking shots that HALVES the health of any tank? And the awesome British LT that denies suppression? And what about CoH2? Have you played the game when there was coldtech, no tac map? Or when they released the Case Blue addon with the Elite Troops Doctrine and the Tiger Ace that took 20 minutes to destroy (yes you had no income anymore, but you could basically win the match with one unit)? Or when they released the Soviet Industry Commander that allowed you to roll out 3 T-34's at min 10? Or when they released the Western Front Armies, do you remember the OPKW? And the UKF, with the Bofourious that in one burst wiped out an entire squad, the Mortar (aka Mordor) Pit that coudl cover half of the map and one shot any squad? The Churchill that had (and still has) more health than a King Tiger? The 2016 patch that made the Stuart and AEC on the same level of T-70''s, while being cheaper and coming out 3 or 4 minutes early? And the "click on the map to remove German units" artillery cover ability that basically deleted everything on screen? And Tulip rockets that could brin a KT to 20% of its health with one salvo and also stun it at the same time? Do you remember that year  the automatch was stuck between 70 and 90% allied search, no one wanted to play Axis anymore, at the only competitive tournament of that year (I think it was the War Paint Championship), the only person who managed to win with Axis was DevM? And what about all the broken (still broken) commanders that no one managed to fix and for which every competitive tournament runs with the "commander terminator" mode, so that you cannot keep spamming ostturppen vs usa mechanized every single game?Am I annoyed that the game was released in this state? Yes, and some things really show sloppiness.Is it better than CoH2? Yes and no. It has way better potential and several gameplay mechanics are better. But the game feels unifinished, and CoH2 simply has some features missing from this game that should have been there in the first place.Does it deserve a negative review? No, definitely not. _childDocuments_.review: The RTS component of the game is honestly excellent. The cover system works, pretty much everything is destructible, using explosives feels incredible, carefully positioning mortar and machine gun crews and microing infantry and tanks and is an absolutely delightful experience, and when all the pieces click together you really do feel like batma- Captain Winters, directing a company sized unit.Which is a shame, cause the campaign is hilariously unfinished. It was awful at launch, got a rework since that made the map layer a little more tolerable and tried to make minor abilities like detachments less useless, and yet it still feels like youre beta testing an amateur 4x game. Companies have a progression system but the campaign isnt long enough to really specialize any of them, and most wont even reach the very cool upgrades. Unlocking the cool "instantly deploy two sherman tanks" ability feels like garbage when you get to use it once in the 20 hour campaign, on the turn before its abrupt, albeit historically accurate ending. Playing the scripted missions in the campaign is great, they play like small urban combat puzzles that the game give you some tools to solve and you have to figure out, but most of the campaign will be generic skirmishes. The campaign characters could have been interesting, in a world where their stories led anywhere and they were given time to develop. Overall the single player Italy campaign feels incredibly rushed out, with some very fun story missions that were clearly meant to have a better, more coherent connective tissue woven between them that just isnt there. Don't buy this game at full price, but once it goes on sale, the RTS battles and mechanics are polished to hell and theres nothing else like them.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't buy this game for the campaign.  I haven't tried it and will probably never play it.  I primarily played coh2 pvp multiplayer and same goes for coh3.The skirmish / multiplayer feels good in the current state and is in my opinion worth buying the game for if you want to play multiplayer.+ It runs well (better than coh2 ever did)+ There are plenty of quality of life improvements over the predecessors (optional auto reinforce, key rebinds, etc.)+ There is already enough faction, unit and battle group diversity to keep it interesting for some time.  The game has, on release, (excluding the vast quantity of commanders coh2 accumulated over many years) almost as much match diversity as coh2 does 10 years on.  I expect this will continue to get better.+ Balance seems reasonable enough.  Hard to say when people are still figuring out how to play the factions, but nothing seems grossly unbalanced and this will constantly evolve (there has already been a balance patch).+ There are enough maps to keep matches diverse (14 total).  There are five 1v1 maps, and one less for each increase in match size (2v2->4, 3v3->3, 4v4->2).+ I have not encountered ANY noticeable bugs that affected gameplay, but I think the post-game scoreboards aren't working properly and I believe there are some veterancy descriptions missing.+ The bots seem decent enough, but as is expected in a fair match it won't really pose a challenge to a remotely skilled player even on the highest difficulty+ There is workshop support on release, which is probably good for comp-stomp players to keep it more interesting.If you liked coh2 skirmish / multiplayer you will probably like coh3 skirmish / multiplayer.  There is probably enough here to keep you entertained for a fair while in multiplayer and obviously more maps, battle groups and probably factions, will come.

_childDocuments_.review: What a game. It would be truly great if it wasn't so crippled by incessant crashes. Like many others, I pre-purchased this game back in August of 2022. When Relic said they were postponing the launch, I expected them to release an almost flawless game. What a shame upon release. In the time I have invested so far, I have literally experienced at least fifty(50) crashes. That is completely unacceptable for a game that had so much time in Alpha and a delayed launch. The strategic map view and tactics of the Italian campaign is about the most fun I've had in an RTS game. The graphics are great and the overall smoothness of play is phenomenal. It's a shame that I really like this game since I can't attentively play it without wanting to smash my screen every time it crashes mid game (especially multiplayer with friends). But it's not solely crashes that plagues this game. I've even beat a campaign mission, twice, just to sit there and the ending screen never comes. You can't prompt the mission to finish either. You just have to swallow the hate and reload a previous save and deliberately avoid that mission. Again, this is completely unacceptable given how long the release was delayed. I know Relic is working to resolve these issues and they are usually great at addressing community feedback/criticism. I just hope they address it quick enough before too many people say "F*** it" and dropkick the game out of their minds forever. For all these reasons, I cannot recommend this game in its current state. It's just pathetic.**Update as of May 2024**The software patches have fixed all the quality of life issues with the game. I have played numerous hours of both multiplayer coop and the single player campaign with no issues. It is also nice to see new battle groups finally be added. I do hope a lot more are on the way. The game plays great and is very exciting to play competitively. I feel comfortable saying the game has reached the status it should have been upon initial release, but I digress. If you like a good RTS and military history, this is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a shame to see the series in this state while nostalgic over the first COH as my favourite & Acknowledge COH2 experimentation that can be enjoyable monetisation aside, COH 3 feel like an early access game that shifted its focus into monetization too early then providing an enjoyable & endearing experience to play again & again.    It is understandable that while I haven't gone through the whole game through the free weekend, I have no desire to waste time with little return to continue.I'll list my concerns:A) I get a unremarkable cutscene that gets boring & should have instead be used for the Italy Campaign.   B) Menu that looks like I'm playing a mobile game.C) When trying the Campaign, it never prompted to try tutorial which would have helped avoid mistake & features for new playersD) In the North Africa Campaign played half a dozen mission was bored & felt the narrative wasn't focused on the Germans that you play as would prefer the narrative stick with the faction you play as it feels disjointed, I couldn't seem able to play set missions unlike almost every other campaign. E) The Italy Campaign intro mission of the invasion of Sicily was a worse version of COH 1 Invasion into Normandy how did you mess that up. F) Bugs in the Italy Campaign such as during enemy turns you don't see enemies move & act without the camera moving on occasion, request a company that doesn't spawn in but reminds you I need to move it every turn, orders on the Campaign Map feels laggy & doesn't like you giving orders to multiple units in quick succession with long lag time to wait for the animation to go ahead, being that it's been years since release it's unlikely they'll fix it.G) Italy Campaign idea is interesting but the result is subpar too many skirmishes, & the characters weren't inspiring but felt they were charactures then living beings, a direction like COH2 Ardennes Assault was better feeling repayable & interesting to play, would prefer they recreate that type or more better curated missions.   H) Price tag absurd even with the sale, either pay to play the older COH games & DLC or pay any other strategy game would be better spent then on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Company of Heroes 3

_childDocuments_.review: The campaign is engaging — a whole new strategy map for the Italian campaign similar to the Total War series. The multiplayer is fun as always, but features are still barebones since there is no ranked automatch or a progression system. But I would still buy it since, at its core, it is the best Company of Heroes game with updated gameplay and graphics.Edit. The latest update, Coral Viper, adds a ton of free content ... Makes it so much challenging, fun in multiplayer matches. This game is not the same as it was at launch. It's amazing now, and there are a ton of great new maps too! My favorite new map is the 4v4 Oasis Desert. Huge map, tons of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Go play CoH 2 instead, game looks and feels really off, tanks and mortars have no impact, they sound like duds. Health bars like WoT exist making it feel even more arcadey. Same performance issues as CoH 2 exist. Some of the battlegroup designs are interesting but they are overshadowed by poor arcadey looking gameplay. Doesnt even look that better visually from a 10 year old game and the UI elements look really unpolished. There are also bad pathing issues and units will wobble in place next to a tank or a structure etc. I was hoping it would be worth it a year after launch but there is 0 reason to buy this when CoH 2 exists and is just better in almost every wave.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Company of Heroes 2 for 750 Hours and why? Because it has a wide variety of units and generals with their own abilities and special units, many maps, a perk system with little improvements for some units and a meta rank/level system in which you can prestige 3 times over. At release these aspects are missing or less advanced in Company of Heroes 3. For me COH is all about the Multiplayer, not even against other human players but with my friends against the hardest AI's or a few steps down just to try new units and tactics. Also the grind was fun and gain a lootcrate every 3 matches in which you could get a perk for a unit, 500 gold (10000 -15000 for a non-real-money-pay general), or immediately a new general, or a new frame-skin for the lobby, or a new victory animation at the end of a battle. Now it's just a short video with the short text "Victory" or "Defeat". Why not introducing a new experience-loot system where you get xp based on difficulty of the AI you defeat, how many and which units you neutralized, how many hardpoints  got captured and how long etc. There is so much opportunity with that and a little extra dopamin at the end of the match for a player. I don't really care about the singleplayer or if it's missing completely as long as the skirmish matches with friends are every time an epic experience full of soldier, tank and artillery battles. I'm not sure if the developers are planning to release DLC's to extend the variety of units, abilities and even factions like soviets or if they are planning to implement a meta level or xp system.But now it feels like a demo version of a full game for half the price. Even little things like when I'm in am mach with 2 friends and I cant see which units are from which player and can't warn them of an imminent attack. Or bugs like I mount an howitzer and the truck + Howitzer is unmovable and completely stuck and unusable until I use a tank to teamdamage it out of the buggy existence. And the voiceacting for me as a german is horrible because it's english voice actors that try to sound german but it's a rubbish mishmash and is not actual german .... why?For the good part. It is really pretty and a graphical improvement. Tank models and animations, also explosions and buildings collapsing are really detailed and nice to watch. The addition of sidearmor is also a tactical improvement and salvage tanks aree a great idea.But as long as it lacks units, abilities like the Eisenbahngeschütz,, tanks like the King Tiger, Elefant, Pershing and other cool variants of the previous game it doesn't really feel like a successor of the series and is not recommended in my opinion. And it might has to do with that I just played 10 Hours and I'm missing something, but I think I played every faction and tried out almost all specilization trees and it's not satisfying....yet...

_childDocuments_.review: So far, between the launch and mp test, I've put 18 hours of gameplay into COH3. It's been fun. Nothing groundbreaking; just a seemingly solid title in a classic franchise and in a genre of games lacking in major releases. If you liked any other COH game you'll probably like this one. Gameplay feels a bit slow at times with how tanky infantry can be while in cover, but proper use of combined arms will always see you come out on top. Game has ran well for me and I've only had a few crashes during loading screens. Only real complaint is that the sound design could really use some work. A lot of weapon and cannon fire sounds pretty a like to each other. If you're looking at that mixed status and are feeling on the fence then I recommend simply trying the game out yourself and refund it if you really don't like what you see. A lot of the discussions have been childish and entitled. You'll see most negative reviews with only a half hour played and complaints about art style choices. Everyone is free to not like the direction Relic took with the visuals. I personally don't care for the direction either. However, the reaction to that decision and some other issues that ultimately boil down to nitpicks has been ridiculous. I've seen some people compare this game to Anthem or BF 2042. COH3 may not be your cup of tea and it certainly has flaws, but let's not compare it to games that are fundamentally broken from a game design standpoint. You know a lot of this reminds me of when COH2 launched. Sure, now it's apparently the height of the franchise, but when it came out people hated it. I completely stayed away from it for years based on those reactions despite loving COH1 and still playing that game to this day. Looking back on those negative reviews they seem just as dumb as the ones for this game. People unironically complained about the EASTERN FRONT being portrayed in a negative light. "It's called Company of Heros not Company of Warcrimes!!!" Ugh. I wonder how many potential fans will be turned away by all this? I missed the boat on COH2; I don't intend to miss this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's what Claude Opus thinks of this game:Company of Heroes 3 is a triumphant return for Relic's acclaimed RTS series. While it may play it safe in some areas, sticking to the tried-and-true CoH formula, the game delivers where it counts with fantastic real-time tactical gameplay, impressive graphics, and a wealth of content.The core gameplay remains as satisfying as ever, with the signature cover system and emphasis on positioning and flanking making for tense, dynamic battles 1. Relic has made some nice refinements, like better modeling of vehicle armor and the ability to tow anti-tank guns, that enhance the tactical depth without overcomplicating things 1. The destructible environments and weighty combat effects make the battlefields feel visceral and immersive 4.The two singleplayer campaigns offer very different but equally engaging experiences. The North African operation is a superb showcase of classic, linear RTS mission design 4, while the Italian dynamic campaign, despite some rough edges, provides a welcome dose of strategic decision-making with its light Total War-style overworld 45. The ability to customize your Companies with unique upgrades and abilities is a great addition 4.Multiplayer is where the game stumbles a bit, with some early balance issues and a limited unit roster hampering the experience 4. But the strong core gameplay still shines through, and Relic has a good track record of long-term support and improvement as seen with CoH2 1. With some patches and expansions, CoH3's multiplayer could really shine.Visually, CoH3 is a treat, with detailed units, great destruction effects, and a gritty WW2 aesthetic. The sound design is also excellent, though the voice mixing could use some work 1. Overall, it's a technically impressive package.In the end, Company of Heroes 3 succeeds by sticking to its roots and delivering more of the series' signature tactical action and memorable WW2 spectacle 5. What it lacks in big innovations, it makes up for in polish, variety, and sheer fun factor. Relic has delivered a robust and refined RTS experience that both long-time fans and newcomers can enjoy. If you love WW2 strategy gaming, Company of Heroes 3 is an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played +1,500 hours on COH1, and +2,000 hours on COH2. This game at best is at a level of early access, but really is at a state open-beta. I think most people who have good reviews have their nostalgia blinders on, and are ignoring a lot of issues with the game. Overall a lot of the issues are minor, this game is playable; HOWEVER, all of the issues add up to a hot mess of a game. We've waited over 10 years, and its sad the game has been released at this state.I HAVE ONLY PLAYED MULTIPLAYER PROS:- 4 playable factions - Reassigning hotkeys - No bugsplats/crashes - Faster loading screens compared to COH2  - Auto-reinforce at baseOverall gameplay is similar to COH2 & COH1. They have implemented most of the mechanics from COH2, including vaulting, reversing vehicles, etc. This is the first COH game that has been released with more than two factions. I haven't experienced any bugsplats or crashes when playing, and overall load-in times are greater than COH2. CONS:- UI, UI, UI, UI- Artwork- Audio - Lack of Commanders - Graphics/Visuals are comparable to COH2- No in-game leaderboard/rankingUI:The interface is absolutely atrocious, from the starting menu to icons. The starting menu is a homage to COH1, yet somehow looks way worse. The menu/settings/font are a far cry from any game released in the last decade.In-game is just as bad. While in-game you cannot view the name of teammates by clicking on their base or units. Even if you have unique-colors it still doesn't show any player names. To access the playerlist and see what doctrines are picked by teammates, you have to pull up the menu which covers the entire screen. Compared to COH2, where you can pull up the player list in the upper left corner. Icons like the repair icon on vehicles is minuscule. There is no build icon at all. Mousing over engineer builds has nothing. Hotkeys are reassignable but don't translate well with COH2 hotkeys. Commander choices/abilities in-game are on the far right of the screen; you tend to even forget about them  or even notice they are there. These issues may be minuscule, but a decent UI is very important in RTS games. Artwork:Abysmal. COH2 had great artwork from all of the commander icons and doctrine selection icons. COH3 doctrine/commander icons are trash. Look at COH1 doctrine selection screen. It pulls up a well-made menu with artwork and you can easily discern abilities. COH3 doctrine selection menu and icons are bland and small. Even the faceplates are terrible: one of the faceplates looks like a 2000's game artwork. This has no reflection of the gameplay, but if I only cared about gameplay, I'd go play CS-GO.Audio:Has no life to it, doesn't really wow you.Doctrines/Commanders:More doctrines and commanders would be great, but this game did just release with 4 playable factions. So this isn't really a knock on the game, but something to consider.Graphics/Visuals: This game was released about a decade later after COH2, and really doesn't improve much. This also just might be a bias because I'm already disliking many of the other issues of game. However, compared to COH2 a lot of explosions, gunfire, and effects are completely lackluster. Infantry or tanks taking damage doesn't have that great of an impact.SummaryCOH3 is a horrid successor to COH2. It barely improves on much other than different factions. The gameplay mechanics are similar but COH3 just has worse UI. This really just amounts to a Italian/Afrika corp DLC. I can't really ♥♥♥♥ on the developers. This seems like a cash-grab from Sega/Relic executives releasing this game way too early. If any triple-A game released a game at this state, people would be in uproar (I.E No Man's Sky). Yet, the COH community has an intense love for this game, because it ends up being the only game we play. Probably why there's so many mixed opinions.I expect in a year or so this game will definitely be much improved, but for now I'm pissed I bought this game for $60.TDLR; COH3 is just a bad COH2 DLC where you can RP as the Afrika Corps and Erwin Rommel.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to even begin..First off don't mind the low playtime as I've played tons of hours on Alpha and Beta sessions and I've been a loyal and die-hard fan of CoH series since first game and i really wanted to see the next installment to succeed, sadly i have lost hope,dedication and any trust i had for Relic.In multiplayer beta tests a lot of testers (including me) have been reporting that the UI needs a thorough rework, otherwise people will complain as it is possibly the worst UI design i have ever seen in my life - totally unintuitive, way too big, simply bad.Relic assured us they're listening to the feedback and appropriate measures were taken to address such issues, boy how wrong we were.. Relic did absolutely NOTHING to address this and tons of other issues that were reported even since Alpha tests. So don't be even slightly surprised that some people are review bombing this game simply because they were lied to.Some people even took it as far as to warn potential buyers on their forums and got banned for that.. simply unbelievable how greedy Relic have become.First day of launch I've created a fast skirmish game to see how much has actually changed since last the multiplayer beta test, and you know what? literally nothing has changed.. it is still the same beta we've been playing a few months back.. (despite Relic claiming that that beta was at least a few builds old and final game would be way more polished and we've believed them.. sadly, yet another lie)I even had to quit the game early because of that UI my eyes actually started to hurt a same notion that i've experienced in Beta.Let me list a few other issues:- Main menu, exactly the same as in beta: Simple,basic and uninteresting.(Clearly they tried their own spin on CoH 1 design, but failed miserably)-No MP progression whatsoever, no levels, no drops, nothing. (MP will get boring very quickly without any sense of progression)-Inventory system is as simple as it could be (not a bad thing).. minus the fact that you can't even view/edit your profile stats, change your banner and title (wtf?)-Questionable design choices, they've been listening and creating this game based on feedback mainly from competitive players. Clearly they've forgotten that vast majority of players are playing this game casually / for fun not competitively. And that is why this game's tempo feels faster than it was in CoH 2 and we have YOLO infantry zerg spam for example.-They seem to be proud of the fact that during the launch this game's got 4 playable factions, but every single faction seem.. unfinished and unpolished, some even to degree of having reused unit icons from previous games (does this feel like a finished game to you? bear in mind that this is NOT early access, this is a full version of the game and they dare to charge full AAA price for that.)-No new maps since MP Beta - very few of them overall-AI is so bad it still needs at least a few months to develop properly-No national voice acting, every nation speaks plain english.which feels unimmersive, yes, Germans too lol.-Personally i haven't played the campaign since Alpha but from what people seem to report it's mediocre at best, definitely not nearly as immersive and engaging as in first and second game.-Camera is way too close, makes your head spin sometimes.-Personally not a fan of new ,,Doctrines" instead of commanders we've got in CoH2. The doctrines seem lackluster and confusing compared to the commanders - personal preference i guess.-Addition of Store I know we had one back in CoH2 but it worked quite well and you could buy nearly anything with the points that you've got by completing battles. But with CoH3 is it really necessary to implement microtransactions so early knowing that the game is basically still unpolished beta they've charged you full price for? Not by a long shot.-No after match map viewing or ,,fatalities" we've got in CoH2 - that was a nice touch instead of ending the game so abruptly in this game.-No player indicator on units - You don't know which player controls which unit.-Vehicle navigation is atrocious lost so many vehicles because of that it's insane.-Knowing how faster-paced this game is, artillery is next to useless and they've even greatly reduced the range on arty-units-Minor bugs i won't even bother to list here cause' they can and will easily be ironed out.To sum it all up:Relic refused to listen to the community, they kept lying and giving false hope, kept riding on the fame of first and second game and now they're getting review bombed by people they screwed over and lied to, fitting. Hope their competitive community they've catered this game to will be enough to pay their bills..Game is nowhere near completed - bland beta stage at best, lacks quality,content, any progression and overall polish.Definitely not worth the full price, maybe one year later from now on and definitely on discount, maybe then Relic will learn not to release half-baked, unfinished and overpriced products on launch (RIP DoW).

Do you like your vehicles to go 360 degree turns when you have them move only a few feet away, especially you very venerable units like trucks? How about a bland art style? After DOW 3 failness, then there was AOE4 that looked like mobile game until the community revolted and it still has less effort than AOE3 which came out 15 years ago, now RELIC’s new masterpiece, this garbage. Nothing really new to see here. A boring campaign that you can play in other WW2 RTS games. A weapon two system that has been in games like Men of War and even Blitzkrieg for decades, yet somehow done even more poorly here. I know that devs often have to come to a compromise with investors and publishers who want to push out products for quarterly earnings margins, but this is just sadness. Avoid until many patches and sales.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: If you have even a slight suspicion you may like the game, even as a new player, get it. It's a seriously good and unique strategy title, which on its own is a rare beast in our days.Full review:As a new player to the series, I find CoH 3 a challenging but very pleasant game that I keep coming back to every day. It scratches a certain itch few games do with its well-designed unit system, intense real-time combat, and pace that keeps you on your toes throughout the whole game.Campaign:I found the new Italian campaign helpful to learn the basics of the game, but also quite engaging with its total war-esque map view that allows you to build several companies and use them in different areas of the map as you battle your way to liberate Italy. Now, the difficulty of this campaign is rarely challenging, and I get that it's a gateway for multiplayer, but when I finished the campaign in just a few days I kept craving for more, and I see potential in a fully-fledged CoH title that is focused heavily around this type of campaign. I wish it was longer, but regardless, it was a great experience. The only thing I really didn't like was needing to control two armies in the later missions and switch between them when advancing.Multiplayer:As a new player, I was genuinely scared going into MP given how old the series is and how many veteran players it has, and it certainly did not go very well the first couple of games, but thanks to YouTube and guides, I'm able to improve bit by bit, even though I'm always seemingly playing the Allies. So far, the MP is difficult, micro-management is really challenging, there's no pause option, you have to keep going throughout the whole game, but what it offers in exchange is a thrilling experience with mass battles, encirclements, tank engagements, which are all extremely fun despite natural frustrations of being a competitive game. Although I've spent thousands of hours in MOBAs and other RTSs over the years, I enter every CoH3 MP game nervous but excited, and I feel amazing when something works well and a few of my squads manage to push the enemy, force the retreat, and claim the flag. There isn't a better feeling than setting up your defence properly, placing the machine gun to cover the central area of the flag, having a few riflemen guarding the flanks, and then seeing the enemy tank blow up on a mine I've carefully placed with engineers to prevent a breakthrough. Only to be flanked by two enemy flamethrower tanks that burn my infantry in an instant. This game is seriously rewarding and punishing at the same time.I've not yet found the community particularly helpful, people in the chat seem to enjoy insulting each other, but I warn them in advance I'm a new player and usually it ends amicably. Performance:I'm having zero issues running the game on my old system with 1080 and 4790k. It runs on the highest settings and does not struggle in large engagements. The graphics are very nice.There's some clunkiness around pathfinding, but honestly, as a new player there isn't anything that is really annoying or preventing me from enjoying the game. A lot of things come down to your knowledge, skill and reactions, and I'm expecting to keep getting better. I think I'm going to be playing this game for years.Other:I'm just a huge fan of WW2 games and strategies in general, so for me, CoH3 fills a perfect place between the grand strategy of HOI4 and first-person shooters such as Hell Let Loose. Few games offer company-level combat where every soldier matters and decisions can cost you the game.All-in-all, I'm super happy with my purchase, I have zero complaints that players of previous titles may have. My only sorrow is that somehow I completely missed the earlier entries in the series. Well done, devs!

_childDocuments_.review: People being divided on the game is 100% justified. I received the game free from AMD so from a monetary stand point, I'm into the game for nothing. Everything you see about past CoH games compared to this one in terms of CoH3's shortcomings are accurate. The game is none the less fun. I'm 12h into the Italy campaign and loving it. CoH3 does feel more like Total War had a baby with Sins of Solar Empire in my personal opinion, which is fine for me for now. The cut scene's are garbage, loading screens look like they're straight out of Red Baron 2 circa 1997 (aging myself here.) The war map feels cheesy and is easily described as frustrating. The skirmish game play is the redeeming feature here. My advice, if you have friends that want to play, get the game for the co-op vs AI modes and play the campaign in-between. That's where your fun is going to be here.For those of us old enough to have spent hundreds of hours in Combat Mission: Beyond Overlord, CoH3 will absolutely remind you of that gem and you'll love the hell out of it. CoH3 feels a lot like a modern version of CM:BO.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved company of heroes 2 a ton and was really looking forward to CoH3. I read that a lot of reviews were negative and that the game was unfinished along with many other complaints made by the community. I bought the game either way because relic did such a good job with CoH2 that I figured they would put serious effort into making CoH3 just as great. A lot of complaints made are valid so I suggest reading some of the negatives for perspective. The game needs a lot more work and a lot more content such as units, command abilities, maps, etc. That right there is basically the game itself and its missing a lot. However I was able to overlook that since I still could find enjoyment in what is currently there. The HUGE problem here is that the developers are adding in cosmetic items and as relic says "only some" can be earned for free. This means they are focusing on making paid cosmetics for an unfinished game, effectively turning this game into a cash cow. To me it seems like they are trying to sucker people like me into buying the game while piggybacking off of the previous installment's reputation. Then they do paid cosmetics on an unfinished game immediately after they received a bunch of backlash and negative feedback. Whoever is making these decisions is going to kill the game and lose their community. I would love to get a refund for this because of all of these horrible choices they keep making, however I already exceeded the 2 week and 2 hrs refund policy. RIP 60$ for an unfinished game thats already being monetized by secondary means. If you want to play Company of Heroes, wait for things to go on sale and buy CoH2, its infinitely better and is pretty cheap when on sale. Otherwise, find a different game commander, this soldier is leaving the battlefield.  o7

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the Company of Heroes franchise for years, and have played multiple RTS games competitively (SC2, AoE, etc) and I have to say that Company of Heroes 3 has really outdone itself in the multiplayer department. The game's multiplayer is incredibly engaging and compelling, and I've found myself sinking hours into it without even realizing it.What really sets Company of Heroes 3's multiplayer apart is the tactical game play. This is a game where you have to think on your feet, adapt to your opponent's tactics, and make quick decisions that can make or break your chances of victory. The longer time to kill in CoH3 allows for a much more cerebral feel to the strategy involved over it's predecessors. It's intense, it's challenging, and it's incredibly rewarding when you finally emerge victorious.The game's graphics and sound design feel somewhat washed out, but it is hardly noticeable in the when focusing multiplayer matches. Overall, I highly recommend Company of Heroes 3 to anyone who loves strategy games and is looking for a multiplayer experience that will keep them coming back for more.
