_childDocuments_.review: These are my first impressions of CoH 3. The game came out literally 2 days ago and I have yet to reach 2 hours of gameplay yet, so a lot of this can change, but anyway, here we go. PS: I might be comparing this game to CoH 1 and 2, because I love both of those and I feel like any new installment in a series should be at least equal to the previous one.The first thing that caught my eye, and kept catching my eye, was the graphics. Jezus, the graphics are bad. CoH 2 had way better graphics, and I feel like this and CoH 1 are sort of competing for second place in terms of graphics. Considering CoH 1 came out in October 2006, a full 16 years ago, that is not a good thing. If you really like or value graphics, I would tell you not to get this game based on that alone. Personally, I don't care too much, but it's still not fun to look at.The very next thing that took my attention was the mandatory tutorial at the beginning. I don't like games that force you to go through a tutorial first, especially when the game is very similar to other popular games that already exist, like CoH 1 and 2. It's not too big a deal, but still something that irks me.Then I jumped into a few skirmish matches and noticed a few more things. First, the unit list is now in the middle of the bottom of your screen instead of the top right corner where it used to be, which feels counterintuitive and wrong for someone who's played CoH 1 and 2 extensively. Maybe it's less bad for people new to the franchise, but personally I kept losing track of where the unit list was and had no idea how my units were doing half the time. Most of the hud is nice I guess, it's not what I'm used to but I wouldn't say that it's bad, but the unit list being in the "wrong" place really irks me.The sound design is also kind of weird, sometimes you can still hear the sounds of a fight you panned the camera away from while not hearing the sounds of a fight you panned your camera to. I noticed this when I moved my camera away from my panzers bullying a stuart to my MG42 getting swarmed by infantry, and despite that I was still hearing the cannonfire from the tanks instead of the mg fire from the MG42.These are all things I don't like, but what I do like is that despite these flaws, the game still managed to capture that CoH feel I know and love. For now I'd still say CoH 2 is vastly superior (despite the fact that 3 out of 5 factions have to be bought seperately, that's something 3 does better: all the factions are included with the base game here) but personally I'm gonna be keeping 3 in the hopes they fix the graphics and sound and maybe also give us the option to put the unit list back where it belongs.For people who don't have it yet, I'd say wait for a sale for now, and hope it improves.Edit: After I wrote this, I revisited CoH 2 since I actually hadn't played it in a month or so, and jeez, the differences between 3 and 2 are even bigger than I thought. This is honestly kinda sad, that the newest installment in this beautiful series is so unbelievably terrible compared to the precious ones.

_childDocuments_.review: With the negative sentiment surrounding Company of Heroes 3 since before it's launch you might think it was a terrible game. You might think Relic had repeated their awful blunder with Dawn of War 3 where they tried to attract the MOBA audience, younger players, and completely alienated the existing fanbase. In reality? The game is basically just the third Company of Heroes game. It doesn't do anything special. The only big problem with it is that Company of Heroes 2 came out 10 years ago. So expectations are higher but the game really feels like a sequel that should have come out only a few years after 2. The improvements it adds are all fairly minor things like Tanks having weak points on their sides or small quality of life improvements. It just doesn't feel like a sequel made 10 years later.It's most significant new addition is a single player campaign that features a turn based world map. It's interesting, and adds a lot more playtime. But also doesn't feel like anything revolutionary. The multiplayer is pretty much the exact same besides the factions having their tech trees shuffled around some. So with that I would pretty much give the game a 7 out of 10. Good but not amazing after a 10 year wait. But there is a little more to it. The game feels like it was rushed to market as most games these days. It's functional but rough around the edges in some places. But Relic was fairly quick to address most of the biggest gripes by fans like overly bright colors or weak audio. Not that it's helped their review scores. The COH community may be one of the whiniest bunch of negative Nancies I have ever seen on Steam. The game simply isn't that bad. Mediocre for now until it's polished more, and gets more multiplayer maps. But the COH2 launch was WAY worse back in the day.

_childDocuments_.review: Comparison is the Thief of JoyIf I had not been playing the Company of Heroes franchise since its inception, I would see a mountain of negative release reviews and move on.I forget which graphics card I bought, that the original CoH was bundled with, but I remember holding the paper CD cover. Looking through the clear plastic and seeing three G.I.’s looking back at me. For a teenager low on money, playing Counter-Strike 1.6 scout sniper maps and the Battlefield 2142 multiplayer beta. These three strong men offered something new; the chance to master a battlefield and lead a platoon to victory. Not having yet seen Saving Private Ryan, and who’s only media experience of WWII was Call of Duty: II. It felt like an isometric masterpiece, a symphony of strategy. At least, until I dipped my toes into 1v1 competitive multiplayer.The combination of hormones and an undying competitive streak, saw me put a hole through a rotting wooden floorboard next to my computer. The game that I will never forget. My opponent; probably a much older Wehrmacht player, exclusively playing veteran upgraded pioneer flamers and snipers. I had no counter and got a whooping, this was too much for my teenage rifle spamming brain to handle. I swore off 1v1s for a long time and wandered in and out of regular play. Playing every iteration of the franchise, including the pay to win Company of Heroes: Online.The reason I tell you this, is because for me and I suspect a large number of Company of Heroes veterans. The rose tinted goggles are strapped on tight. Nostalgia and experience are difficult things to tease out when you’re trying to give a comprehensive and impartial review.Did Company of Heroes 3, suck on launch? Yes.I want to tell you a little bit about neurochemistry. When your brain sends a signal to your nerves it does so with gates. There is a period of time just after the message has been sent, where it is harder to send a subsequent message. This is called the refractory period. Nostalgia I believe is a long term refractory period, where nothing ever hits as good as the original. Addicts experience this with their chosen substance, the feeling becoming weaker with time and repetition.Playing the Company of Heroes 3 dynamic campaign — a decent adaption of a Total War campaign. You control Corporal Conti’s squad, scaling the cliffs of Normandy, dodging hot lead spat by a Machinengewehr Zwei und Vierßig. All seems lost until Conti underhands the perfect pineapple, setting off a series of secondary explosions that craters all three Flak 88s. The mission continues with Easy Eight Shermans saving the day and rolling over the coastal defenders.It is pure Cinema. Was it as good as the first time I played this mission in Company of Heroes 1? No, but how could you compare something so steeped in nostalgia, that the experience has become removed from reality of 2006.The reality of 2006 was a considerably different landscape for the gaming industry. THQ had not yet gone into administration which would lead to a corporate takeover by Sega. Patches would have to be downloaded from the official site and installed in release order. Social media wasn’t really a thing, neither was the 24 hour media cycle and the need to dominate it. The world felt like it moved slower, and it did.Over time, like with all things, the gaming industry has been taken over by the money men. Profits first and quality somewhere after corporate bonuses. Perhaps this drove the need to release a game with four factions, two separate and different styled campaigns, simultaneous console and PC versions. All firsts, in the franchise's history. Did Sega bite off more than the development team could swallow? Almost certainly.It’s hard to see a release state that would have delighted every part of the player base that enjoys this game. It would have been more palatable in open beta, but profits would not allow a second missed deadline. This combination saw the game monumentally review-bombed.It’s been a tumultuous year with the end result being a Sega-less Relic and a very competitive and playable Company of Heroes 3. With Relic solely at the helm, despite harsh staffing cuts, the game is better than ever. Updates are now coming monthly to the game, feedback is sought on all socials and implemented quickly. The in-game store is about to undergo a major revision, and the next update will nearly halve the responsiveness of the game. The community managers are active and prolific with memes. The slow behemoth of decision by committee has ostensibly been removed.The Graphics are the best you’ll find in a modern RTS with Dx12 and AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution, which means it runs great on my limited gaming laptop. The colour palette and creative vibe mirror the Italian Mediterranean. With the dreary browns and greys only dominating the game, at the end of a long match, with lots of artillery cratered moonscaping. The audio is still the game's Achilles heel, but a great base of voice-lines is slowly growing on the community. Etching out their own nostalgic feel already. I haven’t had a crash during normal play for at least 6 months.The TL;DR is: The only thing that kept me playing Company of Heroes 3 was nostalgia and hope. It’s finally paid off. As a long time player, it’s refreshing to have monthly updates that add new content to nearly every patch. It’s exciting to see what an independent Relic will do with a small team and how they’re going to grow the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow they have managed to make COH3 worse than COH2 even though the games are 10 years apart. This is an incredibly disappointing release. Not only it feels extremely unpolished but also unfinished. I don't know if developers these days just don't care about their products or if the quality control is just so lacking. Graphically the game is obviously running a newer engine but the overall result looks worse than COH2. Attention to detail is not there at all and the game lacks basic features that its predecessor had. Probably the absolute worst is the sound design. I don't even understand how WW2 sounds can be screwed up this hard. There is promise in this game but I suggest waiting at least a year from now before buying.Pros:- New features and theater that show a lot of promise if patched extensively- Game is more fluid than COH2- Two SP campaignsCons:- Visually ugly - primarily explosions and artillery effects- Horrible sound design (across the board but impacts and engines are almost impossible to hear and guns sound like airsoft guns)- Lack of basic features (proper team colouring, key binding, tooltip on dropped weapons, crushing etc.)- Horrible animations (wheels on some vehicles dont move, reload animations are worse than coh2, tanks drive through tents without destroying them)- Campaign narration is uninteresting and really cringey- UI and artwork- The game is clearly not finished (enemies spawning right in your view in Afrikakorps campaign, not possible to view replays and lots more)5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, one of the most significant issues with Company of Heroes 3 is the lack of innovation. The game fails to introduce any new game mechanics or features, instead relying heavily on the same gameplay elements that were present in the previous games. As a result, the game feels repetitive and stale, with nothing new to offer long-time fans of the series.Secondly, the game's graphics and visual design are also disappointing. Despite the advancements in technology, Company of Heroes 3's graphics look outdated and unimpressive. The environments lack detail, and the textures are muddy, making the game feel like it was released a decade ago.Another issue is the game's performance. Company of Heroes 3 is plagued with bugs and glitches, which hinder the gameplay experience. The AI is also lacking, often making illogical decisions, and the game's interface is clunky and unintuitive.Lastly, the game's campaign mode is lackluster, with a forgettable story and uninteresting characters. The missions lack variety and fail to provide any real challenge, leaving players feeling like they are going through the motions rather than experiencing an engaging narrative.Overall, Company of Heroes 3 fails to live up to its predecessors, offering nothing new or innovative, and falling short in several key areas. Fans of the series may find themselves disappointed by the game's lack of evolution, while newcomers may find it difficult to justify the price tag for a game that feels outdated and uninspired.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid core gameplay loop.2 Campaigns:Africa Campaign is a series of scripted missions, all very well made with varied objectives and gameplay. Unfortunately plays up the Clean Wehrmacht/Clean Rommel myth a bit and portrays any war crimes done by the Nazi government as solely by the SS.Italian Campaign is a meta-map campaign on the Southern Italian peninsular up to Rome where you move pieces about the map, non-scripted skirmish battles interspersed with scripted battles. Skirmish encounters between forces can get samey due to lack of AI aggression, but objectives still vary in skirmish encounters so it's still somewhat fun. Scripted battles are all very well done however. Where the Italian campaign is a let down are the metamap mechanics and emplacements. You can safely bypass/charge through most emplacements but cutting them off from their supply lines does not cause them to bleed hp; this can get annoying but does not hurt you as you blitz up the peninsular. There's some fun to be had with the Special forces and the Paratroopers, being able to daisy chain their paradrop/strategic airlifts means you can conquer flanks and then rapidly redeployment past the front. (I was able to defeat Bari, at the southern edge of the meta-map, pretty late with 1 paratrooper coy and then rapidly redeploy it all the way to the northern edge of the meta-map in 2 turns)Often it feels that you overpower the AI very rapidly and don't really ever get to use the "big name" units in battles, I never did use a Whizzbang in the Italian Campaign due to how fast I overcame the enemy.WRT to Multiplayer, there's some weird stuff that's missing from the previous game, Parties being disbanded weirdly, scoreboards some times closing when you're not done looking, etc. Mostly thing I'd expect to be fixed over time.

_childDocuments_.review: Im not a veteran of all COH titles. I played 400 hrs of COH2 and thats it. I didnt see the launch of COH2 & how bad it was. I dont have any special position for Relic, where I somehow accept them releasing incomplete games. I did play all the alpha tests for COH3 and I can see what has been done and what hasnt been done after them.To keep this simple: COH3 is unfinished. -Its poorly optimized-the sounds are horrible and you cant follow the battle based on sounds anymore, like in COH2-the animations are extremely lacking and worse than in previous titles-there is less troop & cp variety than in COH2-theres very few maps and basically no new ones after the alphas-the game has been downgraded in many ways from alphas, the most striking example being the destruction (why is the performance ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ even with the downgrades?)-multiplayer lacks basic features like ranked, punishing players who quit immediately, reconnecting to matches, replays (MY BIGGEST PROBLEM IS THE UNFINISHED STATE OF MP)-I dont really care that much about the graphics, but if you compare the graphical fidelity to the performance, it doesnt add up (destruction has been downgraded?)EDIT 280223:-Horrible pathing-bugs that will get your squad killed, for example models getting stuck on terrain while retreating-input lag-the balancing is horrible and things that were discussed after latest MP alpha are completely ignored by Relic (off-maps, flame throwers etc)-CANT DRIVE OVER SOLDIERS WITH VEHICLES-lots of placeholder UI thats just inacceptable in this price range game, also completely wrong icons in many places that create confusion-unique colors are completely whack, I can be allied with the same red color as the enemy territory is displayed withEDIT 09032023:Played through most of the Italian campaign with the hardest difficulty. The turn based mode is completely lack-luster. The AI is stupid and doesnt pose a challenge, doesnt utilize the tools it has (0 bombing runs, 0 arty used outside of Anzio Annie with its few strikes, 0 naval bombardment). There is VERY little variety in the missions, mostly just a few different modifiers on the same few MP maps there are, its extremely repetitive. Out of the +50 missions/skirmishes Ive done, 3 have been interesting. There are no cutscenes, there is no connection to whats happening, whos doing what and no real story playing out. The turn-based map has crashed on me about every 4-5hrs. One has to have very low standards to consider this a good campaign. Just another unfinished thing in this game.EDIT 13032023:Finished the Italy campaign, it never got any better. The final mission is extremely easy and lackluster. The battles for Winter Line are not represented in a way that does them justice. The game ends abruptly, which is to be expected from something that is, in reality, an Early Access title. There isnt even an achievement for completing the campaign on the hardest difficulty, or without retreating once. There couldve been so much more done with Monte Cassino or Winter Line, but wasnt. The places couldve demanded multiple attacks with different modifiers to actually capture the places, but this wasnt the case. The game is worse in my eyes after I have now seen the most it has to offer. AT MAX WORTH 15E!An AAA title, sold with a premium price and after several delays in release, the game has a core to it that can turn in to a recommendable game, but right now its just lacking in so many ways that it cant be recommended.The biggest problem I have is the lack of any respect for MP players. The game still doesnt have a system in place to punish players who quit all the time. COH2 was ruined by chinese internet cafe players who left if they lost the first engagement. The same will happen here as well, if such a system isnt implemented soon. But will it be implemented soon? I find it highly unlikely, as there is no ranked mode, no replay system, no reconnecting to matches etc. This is 2023 and COH3 is not released in Early Access. It shouldve been, for 15e. The game is nowhere near worth 50e or more. DONT BUY IT AT FULL PRICE! Theres already ways of getting it for much cheaper.COH3 has fishy Denuvo anti-tamper software included, which is proven to slow down the performance of the game. Just another proof of Relic wanting money more than customer satisfaction. Regarding that, the game will clearly have a crazy monetization scheme with individual skins per troop or vehicle, so more things to sell. Great!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a nice blend of both COH 1 and COH 2, which seems to upset every fanboy of either one (compromise always does). The balance changes to buildings, tanks, and infantry make the games feel much more real world in the combat and its consequences. Needing a well balanced and layered line not dependent on buildings that can be easily taken out with artillery and air support. Being early war, the late war heavy tanks cant unrealistically carry you to victory. Creating a much more dynamic combat experience than the COH 2 heavy tank rush, and while there are more heavy fortifications and gun emplacements like COH 1, they are much better balanced and harder to pull off perfectly. Rockets and A.T. units have been much better balanced so you cant just storm around the field blobbing panzerfusiliers with rockets or A.T. conscript squads. And while i haven't fully experimented with them, the snipers seems to be returning as a viable unit. A fun and worthwhile comeback. The factions are very well balanced, more so than any other COH launch. Some balance issues i had day 1 were fixed by day 2, and i hope the trend of constant review and revision is consistent. The explosions, ricochets, and battlefield damage effects are dramatically improved and more fun to play with, most people judging the game based on the graphics seem to just prefer the dark aesthetic that the Eastern front provided or cling to a few easily fixable bugs. (Or just hate change). Of course Italy will be more colorful, not something i saw as a downside. The campaign, though i have not played it as much as skirmishes, tells of the lesser known theatre of WWII that was of huge importance to the allied victory over the axis. While im not a huge fan of RTS campaigns in general im playing this one mostly for the historical perspective. They did a really good job of illuminating the political, logistic, and combat maneuvers used. If you're willing to pay attention. While i haven't tried the Afrikakorps Campaign, im thrilled to be able to experience Rommel's legendary fighters that terrorized the deserts for years. All stories often overlooked by every other WWII game. I now have my hopes up for more and can only hope and pray they add the Japanese and some pacific maps at some point.

Wehr - Fallschrim pios and sniper into T4. add a sniper or the overtuned AA gun team for good measure.Have fun trying to beat any of these strats if you arent running a meta strat of your own. It all becomes incredibly stale incredibly fast, and even if you do find ways to beat the cheese? Theres no endgame for being the best cheeseball. You just win and or ruin the game, by spamming the same strat over again like some sort of psychopath, again for no gain since:The game doesnt have an esports scene. Relic/sega DO NOT support competitive play.You arent rewarded for being a 'meta' player. Theres no reason to tough it out, other than mental insanity. Theres no ranked rewards. You dont get a unique title or perk. Theres no status that you get. You dont get special skins or anything. And if you do, the game didnt launch with any of this. Why would you continue queueing as a new player to COH if all youre gonna play is the same strategy on the same limited map pool for no reward??? What the hell for??You will never find any creativity, or any variance or deviation; because it is NOT rewarded. Whats rewarded is practicing the meta of the month due to the consistent malpractice that the balance team puts out year after year, patch after patch in COH. Play COH1s campaign and then play COH3's. Youll want to vomit. The modding community will carry the comp - stomp/single player content. _childDocuments_.review: Hello,I purchased this game on release earlier this year. I have previously played Company of Heroes 2, and other Relic titles. This game released with two campaigns and multiplayer from the beginning. The two campaigns were a total war-like invasion of Italy campaign, and a sequenced campaign based on Rommel in North Africa. Two great scenes for what should have been great campaigns. The total war-like campaign was incomplete. Mission triggers would lock up making it unable to progress the campaign in nearly all the mandatory missions. There was a wide option to choose how to advance your forces (should i use bombers to soften the Germans before advancing my armored division, or use my newly created battleships to shore bombard?) but practically they did nothing to make the campaign easier, even on harder difficulties. The AI was incapable of defending settlements to the point you could run multiple divisions through a gauntlet of fire and attrition on the campaign map, take the required settlement, delete the depleted division and just recruit a new one. This has not been improved since launch. Multiplayer: On release an absolutely heavy German bias. For whatever reason on launch Relic decided giving the German-Italian faction a unit that could throw its own smoke at zero munitions cost, move faster when running out of smoke, and attack ground with a flamethrower (and the unit had 2 of them). This unit at vet 1 also got a heatseeking AT satchel for light-medium anti armor. There were several units like this, and after a few months they were patched all the way down into uselessness. This is a trend that has continued the entire time this game has been out. Paradrop planes being shot down by AA? Relic didn't buff their health, they just made paradrop planes invincible. From Launch to present Relic has prioritized cosmetic sales. Before any unit buffs or nerfs, long before any attempts at fixing the campaign ai, Relic unveiled their cosmetic store. The player pop has dropped from 19,397 peak to 2,620 peak in under a year. Now in order to get additional sales they are releasing an expansion for 17 dollars that includes a couple multiplayer maps, battle-groups that are more likely than not broken and won't see patches until well into the new year (if their track record is anything to show for it), and more cosmetics. Do not buy this game. Don't buy it for 60 dollars, don't buy it for 48 dollars, don't buy it for 20 dollars. You will be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: After the perennial classic COH1, I distinctly recall how intensely disappointed I was with COH2 at launch, even today years later. Greedy micro-transactions, lazy and shortsighted design, and the most unbalanced game I had ever seen launched, ever. Fortunately it appears COH3 has avoided its predecessor's myriad pitfalls. One-dimensional sliced-and-diced microtransaction commanders are now a smaller number of much more tightly designed doctrines with many ways to approach each one. Ubiquitous damage sponge tanks have given way to infantry and lighter vehicles earlier in the game. Used well they are monsters, used poorly they die immediately. Even heavy tanks having weak side and rear armor means positional play can deal with a heavy front plate on a tank, as it should always have been. I remain optimistic that they will incorporate the other major weaknesses of tanks as well, such as mobility kills, and of course artillery and air power as the reasons the heavy tank as a concept never worked in real life. Tanks are important but far from indestructible with AT weaponry; tanks die QUICKLY when flanked, the central tactical problem is to flank and also not be yourself flanked. My only critique is that the side/rear armor detection seems glitchy; sometimes tanks will be hit in the front and it will say "side" or "rear" incorrectly, and sometimes you will hit them in the rear and it may say "side" or its silence indicates a front armor hit incorrectly. Also, I feel tanks could have less vision range and more attack range than they do, meaning you should accompany them with infantry for their better sight range, meaning a tank with infantry will effectively see even further compared to a tank without infantry assistance.COH3's factions and commanders are variable, replayable, and well-designed. I only wish there were... more? In the midgame you will routinely exhaust all your picks from your doctrines and have command points piling up that you of course will never be able to spend. I notice some patterns where a faction is missing something non-doctrinally and that type of thing is tacked onto multiple of its commanders, and perhaps a non-doctrinal addition is warranted to allow the doctrines to diversify into their respective specializations even further. I also feel a few of the doctrines have some weird inclusions and some useless picks, but overall a very solid starting point from which significant improvements are not far away. I like COH3. Far more than I ever liked COH2 and I have only played this new installment a handful of times, and even with so little content compared to its predecessor it is nevertheless a vastly superior strategy game. With the same extent of improvements, refinements, and additions over the coming years as COH2, COH3 will likely be the best and definitive Company of Heroes for the next ten years.

However I see the crashing issue being fixed by patches quickly, and the AI issue should be able to be tweaked with the mod support. Even with those I've still had a blast with the game, which is what we're paying money for.The animations and general fluidity of the game are top notch. The campaign map (while there are some things I may have done differently) is great and you have a lot of flexibility in how you play / tools at your disposal. _childDocuments_.review: Company of Heroes 3 is great and unique game, that will make happy CoH series veterans, and still will be great gateway for new players. Is the game perfect? No. Is the game in "Full release state" Also no. Is so many negative reviews deserved? Definitely no.The game have some annoying bugs, there are some missings assets, and some overall rough edges, but when I am reading all those negative reviews, i am starting to think if those players played the same game as i did. Gameplay In this time, there is only few RTS games, with such depth and competitive potential. No matter if you are wanna be pro player, want to play competitive and climb the community ladder, or just casual player, enjoying two campaigns or just casual matches with friends. You will have a lot of fun in both cases. Gameplay is sometimes criticized by CoH2 veterans, for being "slower" and more spongey. But honestly? As someone who loved CoH1 and didn´t really enjoyed CoH2 for being too fast and TOO MUCH competitive, i feel CoH3 to be in perfect spot between arcadish CoH1 and not forgiving CoH2. There is still a lot of space for improving, and overcoming your opponent thanks to your skill, but if you make mistake, forget babysit your units for 5 seconds, they still have chance of surviving, and your game isn´t lost because one lost vehicle. Compared to similar games in the genre, Iron Harvest for example, Company of Heroes 3 is in my eyes best game gameplaywise.Graphics, Audio and visuals  The game looks really good, if someone is telling you, that CoH2 or even CoH1 looked better, they didn´t played the game for looong time. Game si colourfull, fire, explosions and other effects looks great, and whole stylization looks decent. Yeah, CoH3 isn´t the most visually stunning game there is, But this is RTS strategy, There is no need for stunning grapthics with RTX. For it´s genre there is not much games that would look much better. Weapons and vehicles sounds better and more realistic, and even tho there definitlly are war games that sounds better, if you aren´t total WWII nerd, you will have no problem with it. Only complain i have with Audio in CoH3 are voicelines and music. they aren´t bad, but I must agree here with some dissapointed players, that CoH1 had both music and voicelines better. State of Game  A lot of people are complaing about the state of the game. Here, i must agree that whole game feels unpolished. some assets are missing (pictures of units) sometime unit model starts asserting dominance with T-pose (this still happens in CoH1 and CoH2 tho) and sometimes vehicle pathfinding is so broken, that your tank do a full circle before starts going in straight line. Yeah. that is annoying, and you will lost more then few tanks because of it. But devs are working on fixing it, balancing the units, communicating with community, and i believe, all will get better really soon. When CoH2 was released, the backslash was even bigger then now. And look at this now. at least 2/3 of not recommending reviews, are saying how much CoH2 is better, and how it always was such a gem. No. It. Was. Not. CoH3 will be polished, bugs will be fixed, and CoH3 will surpass its precedecors even more then already did. So is the game in "Full release state"? No. In my opinion, they really should release only "Early access", or take at least 4-5 months more to finish the game, But it is still really good game, and there were now awesome games released in much worse states before... (looking at you CP) Final thoughts If you made it this far, and are you still wandering, if to buy, not buy, or wait some time before buying. In my opinion you should buy right away. Yeah the game needs some polishing, but it is still one of the best games in it´s genre, and if you want future for good RTS games, it is needed to support the devs, even thought they might done something better. Game is great, Multiplayer is fun, Singleplayer will take few hours to finish, and looking back at CoH2, in matter of weeks or few months the game will be perfect. By buying it now, you will support the devs, and game will be polished sooner. If you are scared by all those negative reviews, just read them once again. 2/3 of them are just rants from CoH2 players, who don´t remember the state of CoH2 when released. 1/3 complains are maybe partially valid, but as i said before, Nothing is so bad that it should earn such hate.

_childDocuments_.review: I have close to thirty-five hours, roughly 8 hours in the campaigns, the rest in auto-match.I do not typically review games but the controversy of this release, my feelings about the RTS genre as a whole, and my desire for the community and developer to refine COH3 all combined push me to say a few things.The Campaign is underwhelming, it was released with numerous glitches and poorly layered triggers that made it possible to completely stall the progression of the campaign at Salerno. The very first Campaign mission area had three separate ways for me to break the game, and require a complete restart of the campaign each time. I threw in the towel on enjoying the dynamic over-map system vs real time battles, because clearly it wasn't ready yet.New patches have fixed some of the issues I experienced, which is why overall I feel I can recommend the game as an experience, but I refuse to recommend it without explaining that the state of the game today is frankly embarrassing.The Automatch is released without any clear ranking system within the game, has no Map Pool Veto, creates a replay file but lacks any proper replay saving or analysis in game, and perhaps most egregious of all there is no live in-game observer mode.Both Axis and Allies have powerful and nearly game-breaking abilities from my personal experience, in general though I feel that players of similar skill level are able to play out an intense, dogged, and absolutely lethal maneuvers. Tanks in general feel responsive and lighter vehicles feel appropriate nimble by comparison. Infantry has fewer ways to cripple a vehicle, but rifle fire is marginally effective against most light vehicles. Squads move through the terrain with more intelligence than in COH2. The command choices and point trees are a refreshing level of flexibility coming from COH2. The tech upgrades provide timings for attacks with new improvements to throw off prepared enemy defenses and counters, and I never had a game where I felt like I was incapable of producing a force that could provide some counter to even the toughest enemy composition.There are numerous active abilities that are covered or removed from units after upgrades or veteran levels, which is a baffling and incredibly costly situation. Imagine not being able to deploy smoke launchers or use a special ability on a Panzer as DAK because you decide you also wanted vehicles who could cap. (The cap passive ability icon replaces active ability icons on several DAK units, I have found through painful trials.) Instances like the former show a game with potential to balance, refine, and polish each of the four factions into an even more enjoyable state. The fun of the game is let down by seeing the obvious points where lack of care or time led to a complete destruction of the quality control.Despite all the issues I have encountered, over 20 hours of solo automatch games, I have had three epic hour long knock-down drag out games that I came out of feeling like I had just experience the real vision of the developers, despite the complete lack of polish the game suffers.In conclusion, if you are the kind of person who can suffer the failures of others and see through to the quality RTS they've created underneath, buy this. If you aren't, wait for the community to fix everything ourselves, and buy the game for 5 dollars in three years when the developer abandon it entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried and tried probably more than 20 times now to get into this game. I bought it day one after waiting forever in anticipation. The game launched as a buggy POS mess and remains in the current state. As soon as you get to the main menu you will wonder if you just bought a $50 title or a $5 indie game. The more I play the more I realize how much time and work you need to put in to this to even be able to lose gracefully in online skirmishes. The more I play the more I realize that I would rather be at my actual job getting paid than trying to learn how to play this game and have a somewhat decent time online. The single player is extremely boring and repetitive. The only thing that changes is the enemy AI's difficulty. I think it took me less than a week to beat the game in single player? And at no point did I learn anything new or helpful for online skirmishes, and at no point did I find myself having fun. Over 50 hours spent trying to learn online game play, watching guides, playing and practicing. It's truly NEVER a good experience for me as a new player. Maybe 1 out of 20 games you play against someone else who hasn't been playing the series competitively for a very long time. The rest of the time you're just going to be getting canned. The multiplayer is just a complete sandbox for experienced players to absolutely f*** on new players and then j*** each other off in their tournaments of 60 players. These 60 players are really the only people that enjoy the multiplayer side of this game. To add to this mess, the game just FEELS incomplete and rushed, the experienced players seem to say that the game is not enjoyable, and the balances of factions even at competition level are a complete joke. There's no actual tier system that works. You could be Bronze 3 with 10% win rate after 50 games and still be playing against extremely experienced players regularly. The only redeemable quality about this game is that THERE IS NO PENALTY FOR LEAVING/QUITTING GAMES EARLY. YOU CAN JUST LEAVE AT ANY POINT AND START UP A NEW GAME! WHAT A NIFTY TRICK! I just ended up just leaving every time the game stopped becoming fun because why not? You're going to lose anyways. Your opponent is always FAR better than you. How it took so many years and work to release this pile of hot garbage is beyond me. If you enjoy learning by losing constantly to better players, winning to players even worse than you or just not having a good time while you play video games, this game might be for you. But if you aren't interested in wasting your money and free time, I would stay away from this title. It's unfortunate that there aren't any good WW2 RTS multiplayer games anymore. After many many MANY attempts to enjoy this game in ANY capacity, I will be removing this from my library and forgetting about it. I suggest you save yourself the money unless you find this game years from now on sale for like $5 or something. That's truly all that the current content is worth. Just look at the content of the OVERWHELMINGLY terrible reviews and look at the content of the very few and far between good ones. I regret ever trying to get into Company of Heroes. I think I would rather go through learning League of Legends all over again before getting CoH 2 and 3. Look elsewhere funseekers, as you will find non here.

name: In Stars And Time
detailed_description: What would you do if you were forced to relive your failures over and over again? In Stars and Time tells the story of Siffrin and their adventurer friends—a found family bound together by fate in order to end the tyrannical reign of an evil king. But as victory is just within the party’s grasp, a tragedy occurs, the clock resets, and they have to do it all again . As Siffrin’s the only one who notices this loop, each new start wears away at his cheerful veneer, yet he keeps going in hopes he can end this temporal tragedy once and for all. In Stars and Time is a time-looping RPG adventure . With each loop, Siffrin gains a new perspective on the world around them, opening up new solutions to puzzles and allowing them to make better choices in conversation. Equip memories as armor, pray to the Change God to improve your team’s capabilities each loop, and challenge deadly foes to Rock, Paper, Scissors as Siffrin seeks the truth. ✦ Our Adventurers Siffrin (he/they): Stressed, depressed, and under duress. (Don’t worry about it. They’re doing fine.) The punmaster protagonist of our neverending tale. Mirabelle (she/her): A caring and nervous housemaiden mysteriously blessed by the god she so ardently follows. Isabeau (he/him): Defender with a heart of gold. Cares dearly for his people and his friends. Odile (she/her): The mature and nonsensical researcher studying…something. (No, she will not tell you what it is.) Bonnie (they/them): Wait a minute, who brought this kid along??? ✦ Features Save the world through the power of Rock, Paper, Scissors in strategic turn-based RPG combat encounters. Ignore the limits of time and space to fix your past mistakes by repeating the same two days over and over again. Equip the memories you have of your friends to make your party stronger in combat. Watch the fate of this world unfold as you escape the twists and turns of this endless(???) loop. Eat samossas with your friends! Get heckled by a cheeky ethereal being of infinite starlight . Pray to a god for good luck in your travels. You’re gonna need it. If any of this interests you, you might also want to play the game’s initial prototype, START AGAIN START AGAIN START AGAIN: A Prologue . While you don’t need to play it to understand In Stars and Time, it’s fun to see the game’s roots!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, straight to the point. I wholeheartedly recommend this game, it's a fantastic experience through and through, and has given me a lot to mull over in my mind. This is with a caveat though, mainly that the first and second acts are really intent on setting things up, as it were, to the point of pretty much entirely railroading you aside from some simple side stuff. I have never really been a person to be bothered by extended set-ups in games, regardless of whether it makes things a slog, but (especially with reading some of the other reviews while stewing a bit on my thoughts) I do think it is pertinent to mention that. The game does open up MUCH more past act 2, so if you can get through that, you should be fine, unless the overall game-loop (yes, I hear your mental snickering) is not to your taste.Ok, basic "recommend or not?" stuff is over, I'm going to try and delve into my personal thoughts from here. This will be more than guaranteed to contain spoilers, so if you prefer to not be spoiled, don't read the rest.So, this game was really something, and being someone who has both played a LOT of games and loves to read stories, whether on the internet or with a physical book, my genuine thoughts as of writing this are that the game has really impressed me. I've been around the bend at this point in terms of interacting with media and video games, played stuff like Legend of the dragoon, and the original Artonelico, and I've read plenty of different genre's of fiction (stuff like Fablehaven, or the nausicaa manga), and watched plenty of shows. Now, I say this because of all the things I've read or watched or played over the years, In stars and time has actually managed to make me feel something no other game has, to my memory. It has actually managed to sicken me with pure, raw, dread. I mean like, actually made me feel ill when i was going through a certain part of the game. I've felt all sorts of things from interacting with stories, I've felt terror, I've teared up and on occasion cried when a story has actually touched me, I've even genuinely just simply felt satisfied with a story's conclusion very rarely. But never has a game actually made me tense up mentally from dread of what I know is going to happen so well that it's gotten such a visceral reaction out of me, and even sustained it, at that.For me personally, even if the only good part of the game was that section, I would still think VERY highly of the game and it's developer for managing to do that to me, as that is a fantastic experience and will probably be something I remember for a while. however, this was just a single section of the entire game, and this was just the most standout emotion and moment for me (I would ramble on about other particular parts for hours. Alas, word limit.)! To be honest, i'll have to wait a year or two to see if it really sticks, but for now, I would say that this is one of the best games I've ever played!P.S. insertdisc5, if your reading this, the king is my favorite character, it was a treat reading his entire speech at the Nostalgie achievement part, and even more of a treat when he completely turned around and called Siffrin out for having the audacity to try and "just talk things through" to a man who is literally freezing an entire country in time in order to fulfill his wish. The actual epitome of "YOU THOUGHT!". (his "death" was really beautiful too!)

_childDocuments_.review: In Stars and Time is a game that I think has made it's way into one of my top 10. It's not without it's flaws but I really feel like, specifically from a gameplay and story standpoint, this game really improves upon on the first game and makes it a much more enjoyable experience. I will say that I personally really enjoyed the game at first but found myself getting a little bored/frustrated during subsequent loops, it wasn't until I hit my 20th loop that I started having fun with the game again. I specifically liked how there was a lot of intrigue and expansion of the universe that I hadn't thought of but was well addressed. With that said, I am going to be going over some spoilers in the section below, so skip to the non blacked out part of this review if you haven't finished the game yet. While this game is kinda slow in places, I often felt that if I was messing up or missing something later in the game, that was on me. This game really knows how to communicate a lot and not waste your time if you don't let it. It's one of the rare pieces of timeloop media I felt a genuine interest and passion towards. It has something to say and says it well. All of the characters are great and the mechanics are really good. I would recommend getting this game first and then playing the prologue personally because that way the game will be more fun, but the first game did give me PTSD when it came to certain areas so there's that. Definitely a worthwhile game that has dreamy art, a cool story, a nice soundtrack, endearing characters, fun gameplay, and a lot of routes if you look for them. Don't skip this one, it's worth a playthrough!

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute gem of a game. It's one of those games that is an extremely slow burn initially and if you aren't invested in the story then it won't be for you. At first it was annoying for Siffrin to not be able to ask the questions I wanted to ask, or to look into what I wanted to look into until something clicked and I realised that Siffrin is a character with their own wants, needs and way of thinking. I wasn't supposed to be moulding Siffrin into some caricature of myself to puppeteer and make the decisions I would make like other RPGs, but rather I was meant to see through their perspective. Maybe it's a weird distinction to make and this only applies to me, but that initial frustration I felt came from this misunderstanding of what the game was presenting to me.I love the writing. A few things felt preachy here and there but when the sheer QUALITY of the story is this good then a few bumps are barely worth mentioning. Characters are lively and easily differentiated from one-another, the world itself feels so well-crafted as if there is more than the box we're put in. I can't sing this game's praises high enough.The black & white aesthetic of everything is great, the music is retro and enjoyable, I love it. This game has lived rent-free in my head for days, and it's one of the very few experiences I wish I hadn't reached the end of. Ironic, I know.

The cute characters, the development, the amount of unique dialogue, how well everything is tied back together, all the different optional stuff, etc etc etc. The game loop can get tiring at times, but I understand it's necessary for the story line and what not, and if you put some background noise in the back it's not too bad. Plus, if you wanted to be all artsy, technically it helps you understand how the main character's feeling. I also like the dark spin on the whole time loop idea. It feels like such a obvious opportunity, but I don't feel like I've seen it that much; but this was a great interpretation on it. I have to say I almost cried an embarrassing amount during this game, and then did actually cry as well. The emotional beats are really well crafted and never feel out of place. The ire of the game loop is maybe the only problem I had with this game the entire run. Everything else was very engaging. All day when I couldn't play the game I was just hoping to get back to it and thinking over what I thought could be happening. Easily moving up as one of my favorite story-based games ever. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: objectively one of the best games i've ever played in my life, and personally my favorite of all time. isat is utterly filled with life and passion and emotion, crafted with the kind of meticulous care that shows in every little pixel and piece of dialogue. the ost is absolutely beautiful- i regularly get goosebumps listening to it, or just start crying, or both if i'm actually playing the game. the art style is absolutely adorable, which makes both the sweeter moments in the game and the more horrific ones hit that much harder than they already do. the perfect balance of silly goofy, deeply emotional, and absolutely horrific. i didnt think it would go nearly as far as it did exploring certain aspects of time loops and their effect on mental health but i am so, SO glad that it did. i have never had this much fun playing a game in my life. my 5+ year streak of not staying up too late and getting normal sleep, shattered by the 38 hours i spent awake mostly playing, but sometimes talking or thinking about or writing isat. the story, the gameplay itself, the music, the emotion, the WORLDBUILDING dear god the worldbuilding. my chest actually physically aches whenever i think about any aspect of the game beyond surface level. i have never in my life felt the motivation to Create as strongly as i do when i think about this game. if you're hesitant, if you're tempted, even if you're only vaguely curious: please, PLEASE give this game a go. you will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for 45 hours (plus an additonal 35 on another platform), spanning two full playthroughs, and getting every single achievement (Getting all 43 in one run for that matter, since my second playthrough was from scratch on steam) I think I've spent more than enough time to leave a well informed review.Upon re-reading this I honestly can't say this is the most objective thing but uh.... well too late?Big rambling ahead. You have been warned.tldr: very good. good vibeo gaem. also contains The Horrors/Trauma. beware of the gut punches. Also may feel a bit slow at times.Let me preface this review with one more thing even if it isn't important: I have not played OMORI, or other RPGmaker games and the sort, so take this from the perspective of someone who is not familiarized with this type of game. This is effectively a whole new genre for me.This game KICKS ASS. It also will kick you in the stomach. Several times. Play the game. Do it. Don't spoil yourself, though, because that removes half the intrigue. The game's writing is REALLY good, and that's actually surprising to me. The characters themselves actually feel like they could be real people, at least in some way. Also, the OST is just a banger. There are a lot of really good tracks. Don't expect the gameplay and combat to blow you away, since it is still a turn-based RPG type game, but I found the way combat was designed and how a lot plays into each other to be pretty fun. For what it is, it's pretty solid but rarely difficult. Don't be surprised if gameplay feels a bit repetitive/frustrating later on; it's basically that way by design and is somehow used to the story's advantage. But, keep in mind there is actually a fair amount of QOL features to prevent the game from becoming entirely unfun and tedious.Just know that once you start, you'll probably get sucked into the loop yourself. It was surprisingly hard to put down for me. Now GO PLAY THE GAME. Or play the demo. Or read the rest and  play the game. Or don't at all! I don't really care.As I was saying, again this game is REALLY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. Like, it's an art piece in more than just the art/visuals. The game takes advantage of the fact that yes, this is in fact a video game, and lets you immerse yourself in the perspective of what I can best describe is the "literally me" protagonist who's got some Problems™, Siffrin, who got put in a time loop. I'll spare the details because I don't want to give spoilers, but you really get to experience firsthand what the time loop does to him over the course of the game. (Spoiler alert: Nothing Good)There's a lot of really good moments and plenty of The Horrors™ to go around as the game goes on. Also, the side content/quests are great and you shouldn't ignore them. This game practically begs you to go for that 100% completion (I rarely try to 100% my games. This was an exception).Once again, I also have to say. The OST is amazing. The story is something you don't want to be spoiled on. It's got some real gut punches sprinkled through, but also some really touching or funny moments to even things out. There's some real personality to the writing. The game somehow manages to make a child character not annoying and actually likeable, it's unbelievable I know. Oh, one last thing. The completely unapologetic integration of LGBTQ+ rep is unfathomably based, it's done very well and presented in a realistic and relatable way. Also yeah, there's the acknowledgement and inclusion of pronouns. Cry about it. ♥♥♥♥♥ and whine about it, even. It's a thing that exists, get over it. It's not the end of the world. It doesn't really matter anyways. I wanted to mention that part for the sole purpose of humoring myself knowing there's people that get butthurt at the mention of them.If I had to give it a number rating, this would be a 9/10 from me.I could definitely go on and on about this game if this wasn't a review, but that's what I'll leave it at. This is just my take. GO PLAY THE GAME AND SEE FOR YOURSELF!!! YOU (probably) WON'T REGRET IT! Form your own opinion about this!! Don't just take my word for it! On the fence? Again, there's a FREE DEMO sitting there, just waiting for you. What's the worst that could happen???

_childDocuments_.review: In Stars And Time has managed to make me cry at least fifteen times throughout its entirety. Yes, the game-play is repetitive - as is expected of a game that revolves primarily around time loops - but if you look beyond this, you'll find a story that is wonderfully addicting and treacherous in the best way possible. You'll start looking forward to the changes the new timeline will bring and learn to cherish the smallest of conversations - just like the protagonist does. You get to know the five complex saviors, their hopes, dreams, fears, and realize that you have become irrevocably attached to them. Siffrin is so real, so tangible in their responses to the situations that you cannot help but feel every sliver of hope and downfall, every bit of pain and laugh. Grab-the-tissues out of 10, would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, this game is a masterpiece. In my opinion, it is the best time loop game to date, and is on par with if not better than Omori and Undertale.REVIEWThis game felt very simple at first, and it was quite clear how time loops would play into the basic grand quest story we've come to love in RPGs. Until (hehe),  In case you didn't read that (good on you for staying spoiler free), I'm basically saying that there was a lot more depth to this than I had realised. There was so much lore, and I could really feel how this whole ordeal was affecting the character, and how that in turn impacted those around them. I was in awe.Here's a little blessing! You can skip through conversations you've already heard. And it doesn't feel like it was just added at the end to make everything faster, it feels so integrated and clear. You basically zone in and out of conversation!This game knows that playing through the same series of events over and over can get boring. It actually uses this to help you identify even more with our main character! Your feelings translate to the game, and the game as well as its characters actually seem to react to this feeling! Because of this, every single loop feels like its own new adventure.SUMMARYGraphics: 4/5 - I really like the art style! I think it really compliments the mood of the game, and I really appreciated how certain stylistic choices were actually addressed in the game's lore.Gameplay: 4/5 - Great gameplay overall! Interactions feel satisfying, and the simple yet engaging combat mechanics compliment the game's design. Soundtrack: 4/5 - Basic but nostalgic. It is used very well to make me feel anxious at times haha.Plot: 5/5 - I'm in love. I cried a lot, but that might just be who I am. It would appeal to those who liked titles such as Omori and Undertale, though it does feel quite different.Characters: 5/5 - I immediately connected with the little heroes of this game, and they all felt so unique and real. I adore how they interact with you as the game progresses.RECOMMENDATIONUm, hello? TRY THIS GAME???I'd recommend this game to you if you appreciate:- Undertale/Omori- Queer rep- Simple but meaningful world exploration with lots of backtracking- A deep or long story with lots of loreFINAL NOTEI'm editing this review months after I first played it and I just need to say that this replayability is incredible. I really adore this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Excels at gameplay/story integration and emotive writing, in a way that will probably turn a lot of people off.A great portion of ISAT isn't very fun. Although combat is novel, it gradually reveals itself to be fairly shallow as you use the same abilities over and over, getting lazier on strategy as it becomes no longer needed. It is fun to explore the detailed environments, but after a while they start feeling very samey and you're largely digging through things you've seen before. The character dialogue is excellent, but after you've read it a dozen times, you start wishing people weren't so long-winded. ISAT becomes a game you learn to speedrun with minor variations. Do all of this again but read this one book, pick up this one item, talk to this one person. You constantly are retreading your footsteps and teetering on the edge of a feeling of satisfaction which then gets pulled away from you as you realize you have to again backtrack to something you've seen before.All of this is by design. ISAT is very intent on putting you in Siffrin's shoes, and they are going through an experience that slowly wears its novelty and their mental state into dust. The game gets very dark and unpleasant, and even fellow schadenfreude enjoyers may find it begin to bum them out. You should probably consider doing what Siffrin can't, which is to take breaks to recover.Recommended, but specifically for the kind of person who enjoys wringing every last drop of enjoyment out of something and then reveling in the ashes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was incredibly charming! The story & the characters all felt so lovingly crafted, and the entire game was so charming from start to finish. I haven't gotten all the achievements yet, but I'm planning on going back and trying to get them, so maybe my (very small) grievances will be addressed there, but I do want to mention 2 things I felt were a bit lacking:- There's a moment at the climax of the story that I feel didn't give me enough catharsis; I felt there was a tonal transition missing between 2 very good moments, that would've made them both hit a lot harder. They're both back to back, and I found they were both really important an heartfelt moments, but I feel it would've went over better if there had been some sort of transition between the two.- There's a character that I wish I could've talked to at the end of the game. Maybe I missed something during my playthrough, so I may just have to keep playing, but with that said I do feel that there were certain small plot threads that I wish we could've known more about. Worldbuilding things that I thought would come back were left a bit in the air, but again maybe I just need to play more and/or we may get more stories related to them! Who knows!Even with those 2 small things though, I really do recommend this game. I very much enjoyed my time with it, I really care about the characters a lot, and I relate to Siffrin so much. If you're the type of person who goes back to their favorite stories because they miss the characters, I think this game will make you feel seen. The thematics around journeys (and their inevitable ends), wishes, promises, found family and love are all incredibly heartfelt, and feel very meta in that I, as the player, really felt seen in how stories matter to me.Another aspect I haven't touched upon is that this game is MUCH longer and has a lot more content than I was expecting. I love RPGMaker projects, and I never take how short a game is as a negative, but In Stars And Time kept surprising me with how it kept going, which I suppose is also very appropriate for the story and its thematics. I would say you are definitely getting a bang for your buck with this!Finally, my final argument: Isabeau is THE babygirl ever. I love him.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy games like Undertale, Detlarune, Oneshot, and other emotional character driven indie RPG games then this game is absolutely for you. The entire time I was playing this game I was making sure to search everywhere in the hopes of finding new dialogue options, new lore, and new character details. I didn't even find everything! I still have so so many questions about this games lore and I NEED it to become popular enough for people to make hour long videos that explain the games lore. Now in terms of game play I do think parts of the game are very tedious, which was probably by design. Going through the house over and over and over gets draining, but I feel like it helps put you in the mind space of Sif. Also after Sif gets past lvl 60ish all the sadnesses become more of minor annoyances. Combat was very.. basic rpg. When I first started playing I found the "rock paper scissors" mechanics a little... on the nose, but I didn't really care and by my 10th loop didn't even think about it. A part of me wished that fight mechanics could have been more than just "hit it with the craft its weak with until it dies" but the simple mechanics makes going through the same sadnesses over and over again more bearable. Last note: I like how the game displayed certain themes. Going through constant loops Sif was bound to have a mental break eventually. I felt uncomfortable and worried when it happened but in a good way. If someone is sensitive to certain topics and want to play the game I do recommend looking at the potential triggers so that you can makes the best decision for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: I could kiss this game. I could marry this game. In Stars and Time is so heartwrenchingly good that I actually finished it two days after it came out last November, but I've been trying to figure out what I should even say in my review ever since. I love it! I think about it every single day! I have nothing but good things to say about this game, and I really want people to play it. This review does not technically contain spoilers, but I do talk a lot about the intro and the way the game handles its emotional highs, so if you want to go in completely blind, look away.The premise is so clever and so brilliantly executed. I love that it drops you into the very end of a fantasy RPG and encourages you to fill in the blanks. You are on a quest to save the country alongside the Chosen One. You are, essentially, the party’s rogue. You are not the main character. You are quiet and reserved, and you don’t join in on group hugs or talk about your feelings or your mysterious past, and all this is why you are simultaneously the best and worst possible candidate for a time loop. Siffrin was created in a lab to be bad at mindfulness. Siffrin absolutely refuses to let their party know that anything is wrong. You think to yourself, “Wow. It’s almost like this guy would actually rather die than ask for help.” AND THEN HE DOES! MULTIPLE TIMES!!! Oh, Siffrin. My dear friend Siffrin. You are like a little dog that I carry around in my purse. Very small. Very cute. Very good at going straight for the jugular. More than anything, I want to see you thrive. But the schadenfreude is truly exquisite. Anyway, you should buy this game if you want to watch a theatre kid descend into madness.A bit about the worldbuilding: The setting is fun and fresh and charming. Dormont has all the trappings of a cozy little starting (ending) village, and the game even riffs on things like the expectation that you’ll be allowed to waltz in and out of the villagers’ houses whenever you please. It starts off strong, and it only gets stronger as you go! And the magic system is rock paper scissors. This means that combat is super easy to get the hang of with minimal explanation. It also means that everyone gets to do cool poses when they kill a monster, which is awesome. Like, are you kidding me? Siffrin gets to wear a wizard hat AND do a peace sign? On a daily basis? I would be completely insufferable.Next, I have to mention the characters, because I adore them. ISAT’s character dynamics are so, so well-balanced. Their dialogue is so much fun no matter how many times you loop back, and their absolutely stellar chemistry makes every conversation a treat. The character writing is perhaps the biggest highlight of the game. It is genuinely phenomenal the whole way down, and it often hits much closer to home than you might expect from the silly writing style. No notes.ISAT also takes full advantage of its core concept, exploring the emotional repercussions of a time loop in a way that feels both fulfilling and deliciously evil. Remember what I said about the schadenfreude? Have you ever seen a character get thrown into a blender and left to puree so long that they start to completely lose their grip on reality? Would You Like To? If you enjoy time loops as a vehicle for tragedy, you will love ISAT. If you often find yourself wishing that other time loop stories would Go There, I can assure you that ISAT does. Things can be so much worse for Siffrin than you ever anticipated. You CAN and WILL make them worse. Life could be dream.Closing thoughts AKA unsolicited advice that you can skip over if you’d like:There are things in this game that are very easy to miss. If you’re big on lore (like me), I would recommend inspecting and experimenting as much as possible, and also keeping a few different save files for different points in the game. Ultimately, it is up to you whether or not you want to stop and smell the flowers, but you will always be rewarded for doing so. And finally–sometimes, yes, this game is tedious on purpose. This is not necessarily a bad thing. It has to be at least a little bit tedious, because it’s a story about being stuck in a time loop and reliving the same two days over and over again. You will have to backtrack, search an area, find nothing, loop back, realize Siffrin missed something, and go all the way back to search it again. For me, it wasn’t a problem, but for you, it might be. Personally, I barely noticed because I was so excited to see what happened next, but, y’know. Your mileage may vary. I’ve seen a lot of people complaining about this, so I felt like it was worth touching on. But I would also like to mention that you really can tell the developer paid a lot of attention to quality of life. ISAT isn’t really a roguelike, and you can skip around if you need to. It’s a very thoughtful game. It wants you to be frustrated sometimes, but its obstacles never feel spiteful. At the end of the day, it wants you to succeed. And I want it to succeed right back! I love it a lot. It was such a fun ride. If you’re even a little bit interested, you should definitely give it a try. I think you’ll be pleasantly surprised! I certainly was. If you made it this far, thanks for reading. Hope this was helpful, or at least entertaining. Have a good day.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the nebulous "Indie RPG" subgenre, check it out!Comparisons to heavyweights like Omori and Undertale are inevitable, so i think it's more fruitful to talk about what's different from those.Siffrin, your main character, is experiencing a time loop that nobody else is aware of. It's like if you played Majora's Mask and Link had a party of friends with him. Those friends would be completely unaware. Wouldn't they find it... Kind of weird you know where all the keys are, all the boss weaknesses, and solve all the traps? Wouldn't he have some weight on his psyche from watching his friends die over and over and they don't even know? Would he find a way to communicate to them, or simply shoulder it all?If that kind of drama interests you, this game is great.-If you interacts with everything in an RPG to read the flavor text, this is for you.  One town and One dungeon never told me more about a game's world and setting so quickly.-Indie RPG's live and die on their music, and this doesn't slouch. Lots of small touches like music seamlessly changing from indoors to outdoors. Combat music is imposing and matches the suprising difficulty.-Cute characters with lots of energy and very animated poses. This is an already experienced RPG party that has reached their final dungeon, and you're simply joining in at the end, learning about their already established backstories.-Combat is on the face similar to OMORI, but is more difficult (Yes, actual difficulty! Death is a game mechanic!) and fast paced. There are ATB bars, cooldowns, necessary buffs, and swapping turns to open up minmaxing opportunities. Even the Jackpot, similar to Omori's "Release Energy", is more subdued and requires setup.-Never too difficult. you can always run to a savepoint to heal, or purposefully loop to grab extra healing items. You're never without options, and this is encouraged.If you're worried timelooping in an RPG would lead to repeating plot over and over and over, you can choose which savepoint you load from, and skipping dialog you've read before is an actual ability your character gains. It's explained awkwardly, but is a very funny way to solve it.tl;dr siffrin is cute

_childDocuments_.review: In Stars and Time was a game I had to obsessively finish - I could not, for the life of me, put it down. I was charmed by the initial demo, which spotlighted the game's combat system and charming art style. I wasn't even really intending to buy it at full price until I saw how fantastic and beautiful the fanart was, and I figured "There has to be something special about this game."And special it was.The experience of playing through this game has you mirroring a lot of the emotions held within it: the feelings of isolation, depression, and madness. Beyond that, using time loops as a mechanism to tell the story is ingenious, especially when you start to play more for efficiency than for experience. I chalk a lot of this up to the writer being incredibly experienced, but also due to the characters of ISAT being around for a long time. Their dialogue feels real, and I find myself feeling seen playing this game in a way that no one else has seen me. Not even my therapists, friends, or family understand me truly as well as I have felt this game has in multiple ways.This game is going to become a comforting new favorite of mine. I cannot begin to express the joy and relief I felt at reaching its ending. It felt almost like a personal journey just for me, like it reached out and touched me in just the right way. I can only hope other people who need this game find the same relief I did watching Siffrin and their friends. Please play it. Know that everything is going to be okay.

_childDocuments_.review: "In Stars and Time" is a very well written time loop story with turn based combat. The way the game uses the time loop mechanics to force the player to experience the same emotions the main character is experiencing is very clever. When the main character felt dread about repeating the same day over again, I felt dread, when the main character felt excited about a breakthrough, I felt excited as well. I will say though, the time loop nature of the story leads to some not fun parts, where you have to repeat roughly the same things over and over before the story really progresses (which I think is on purpose). This is slightly mitigated by how lovable and entertaining the characters and their interactions with each other are though, and it never truly felt like a chore to read the same scenes multiple times, especially when they often change based on what happens in the loop. But if you really want, there's a convenient skip button to fast forward through conversations you've already read. This is also one of the rare games that have made me cry real tears. Overall, I highly recommend to anyone who can be patient with the parts of the game that cause friction (like the battle system) and are prepared for an emotional narrative driven experience. (read the content warnings and take them seriously)

_childDocuments_.review: A time-loop story that begins at the end. Or so it seems. As Siffrin, you're tasked to enter the House of Change to defeat the King, in an apparently fairly standard JRPG affair, with quirky characters and a literal rock-paper-scissors based battle systems. Things go according to plan. Honed player reflexes kick in. And then, you die.From the top.The story is a thrilling mystery. It stars a small town, a decent size dungeon, and a fairly large cast of well defined characters. As you loop several times on your way to defeat the King, you uncover bits of intriguing backstory. The battle system gets more intricate as you meet stronger foes, learn their tells and your team gains more abilities. The character dialog is endearing, if a bit too energetic. You get into a confortable groove. And then, you die.From the top, again.The more you play, the more depth you uncover. The seemingly cheerful story lingers on the more psychologically scarring elements of the time prison. Siffrin progressively reveals hidden layers and trauma, as his frustration grows mirroring your own. The House holds few secrets now. Or does it? Check it again, from top to bottom, and back again. Every interaction could yield precious new information. Maybe you've seen this bit of dialog before. Maybe you haven't? Will you skip it, on the off chance it's changed? You both pay more attention and progressively lose focus. And so, you die.From the top, again.After enough loops, the systems grow frustrating. The looping structure is utterly merciless, forcing you to go over every excruciating moments you've already exhausted all possible outcomes of. New options become sparse. The battle system, too simplistic. Thankfully, Siffrin retains the experience they earn through each loop, making them progressively unstoppable. You can skip most of what you've been through before. Why bother to check every spot *again*? What interaction are you missing to progress this *specific* narrative thread? It's grating, infuriating. And then you uncover a critical piece of information, and everything becomes new again. Time to review all you've found so far. You know what you have to do.From the top, again.Ultimately, the game excels at its character interactions, with heartfelt and sincere moments of bonding. More than its psychological horror coating, more than its overarching lore puzzle, the game explores themes of found family, agency, consent and forgiveness, with moving (if a little didactic) ace/aro, trans, masc gay romance representation, and more. The pacing gets frantic, with back-loaded twists, culminating in emotional catharsis that may feel like it's going a bit everywhere at once - though still managing to land on its feet. After finishing the game, you're left with the sense you've experienced something precious, an individual voice echoing through the craft, a vision that shines through and overpowers the systemic warts, the questionable pacing, the dreary repetition. And once you must say goodbye to these people, you're left with a void to fill. Only one thing left to do.From the top, again!
