Unmask the true killers in this sprawling narrative and discover their devious motives. Observe closely and reconstruct each scene of death. Your skills of deduction can identify each suspect, motive and murder weapon. Reveal the true nature of the mysterious Golden Idol and those who covet it. Follow the journey of a cursed aristocratic family as you untangle a web of deceit and villainy in your hunt for the truth behind this dark conspiracy.
short_description: A new kind of detective game that allows you to think and investigate freely. Discover clues surrounding 12 strange and gruesome deaths and build your own theory. Pick your suspect, deduce the motive, unmask the awful truth.

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches that Obra Dinn itch, and a much better detective game than, well, most detective games on Steam. It's shorter and easier than Obra Dinn, finished it in a few hours with no hints needed, but that's not necessarily a bad thing: it's a succession of clever, interesting, easily digested chapters that link into a good story which doesn't outstay its welcome. And it didn't force me to spend an entire hour sorting out dead seamen by staring at their pixelated shoes, so there's that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem of a game whose style might not be everyone's cup of tea, but to those it is, it is impossible not to love it.Mechanically it is extremely simple, the game can be played only with a mouse, doesn't require reflexes, and doesn't have fail conditions (i.e. the player losing). And yet, it more than compensates for it narratively. Actually, days later I'm still amazed how they squeezed out such a strong narrative out of such a simple premise.I don't want to say anything else out of fear of spoiling other's experience because this is a game that absolutely deserves to be enjoyed to its fullest by everyone. But let me just say that it starts deceptively simple and then goes on a crescendo culminating in a last level which literally made my jaw drop.10/10 absolutely recommend it to anyone who is into a slower, story-driven-puzzles, investigation game. The only downside is that you'll be sad it ends so soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game because I read a review comparing it to . If you find yourself in the same position, know that this game is, I think, a midpoint between your average on-rails mystery-solving game (think,  or ) and . It unfortunately isn't quite as good, and I think tempering your expectations to that level will help your enjoyment.In general, I found that the fill-in-the-prompt solving mechanic was just less elegant than I was hoping it'd be.  gives the player a standardized format and simply asks them to find the information needed to fill in those standardized info-boxes, and allows the question of "What happened?" to primarily exist outside of the progression mechanics; on the other hand,  gives the player prompts that goads them into explicitly answering detailed questions about what happens in order to progress. All in all, it feels a little more like an on-rails experience.Now, if you haven't played  but have played other mystery games and want something a little more engaging, then look no further! This game is a compilation of a few short vignettes where each mystery ties in to make one greater story emerge. DLC and all, I finished in about 9 hours, and found the experience engaging enough to binge in one sitting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on a decent sale (I think I paid like $10), and I'm satisfied with my experience. It's similar to the Return of the Obra Dinn mechanically, but less frustration-inducing. You investigate for clues, and then 'fill in the blank' to figure out whodunnit and why. Solving the cases is satisfying and the story/characters are good.If I had bought the game at full price I think I might be a little unhappy that $18 only got me 6 hours of gameplay, but either way it was a pleasant six hours. Worth playing especially if you like point and click and/or mystery games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The story is entertaining and the deductive design is very well done. They’ve done a good job of making the more advanced vignettes feel challenging without being overwhelming. The Thinking screen is usually designed in a way that subtly lets you test and verify your theories without actually having to have it all solved at once. Tons of fun, keep it coming!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The definition of a hidden gem. The Case of the Golden Idol is a clever deduction game that does the unthinkable these days: it treats its players with respect. For a very affordable price you are presented with high quality point-and-click mysteries that for once actually expect you to do the mental heavy lifting yourself. Pure atmospheric fun through challenging puzzles without the game holding your hand every single step of the way. Accompanied by a fantastic soundtrack, you’ll have to work for your reward each scenario: the immensely satisfying gratification of having solved something without accessing the hints. Golden Idol is a genuinely enjoyable set of thought exercises that reward patience and creativity. The experience might not be for everyone, but this is exactly the type of game that deserves and needs to be showered in praise so that more polished products such as this one can come into existence. Highly recommended for a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Not only is it incredibly satisfying to connect the dots in each scenario, it's also satisfying to piece together the overall story from these vignettes that initially don't seem as interwoven as they actually are. I'd love to see a sequel to this game, or a brand new game from this same developer that's similar to this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic but very short game detective game. The first game I've ever played that, in my opinion, had a good story. The game clues you in on deductions in a wide variety of ways, keeping gameplay remarkably fresh. The twelve cases all tie together really nicely, and there's lots of clues hidden in earlier cases that give tons of insight later on. Very well designed; definitely pick up if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly one of the best detective/puzzle games I've played. The way that this game functions is unlike any other I've played. I loved every minute of it. I was able to feel that rush of excitement upon figuring out little clues that were in the background. 10/10 can't wait to buy the expansions!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best mystery/detective games I've ever played. Right up there with Obra Dinn, The Case of the Golden Idol lets you solve mysteries in a way that feels way more organic than most games other in the genre.  I love it. I want more. I want a sequel, I want copycats, I want this to become a whole genre of games. On the negative side, it's pretty short (6 hours) and I can't see much replay value.  Even if you forget the details, certain "big picture" elements to the story will probably stick out in your mind and make it easy to solve the mysteries even years down the line.  So if you don't have a lot of money for games and that kind of value proposition doesn't seem "worth it" for you, I can understand waiting for a sale. Personally I'm glad I bought it, it's that kind of experience for me, but I won't judge people for being hesitant. Oh, the game has a demo? Play the demo, see if it looks like something you'd like. HOWEVER, if you, like me, loved loved LOVED Return of the Obra Dinn, You pretty much have to buy this game because its the only thing that's come out since that approaches that in terms of quality.Alright thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A truly remarkable way to tell a story that I don't think could exist in any other medium. It's a fairly short, buttoned up experience and I'd recommend playing it through in just a few sittings so you can keep all the little details straight. Did you like Return of the Obra Dinn? If so, you'll like this too I bet.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really great. It is an excellent puzzle game with stylised pixel graphics. You must take shreds of evidence and pick out key words and phrases from what you find to piece together what happened in each scene. The story is beautifully interwoven with every scene being an important part of the overall story and it wasn't until the very end that I was able to piece everything together in a very satisfying way.The game took me approximately 6 hours to finish and there is no replayability, but that's not a problem at all because it is a very well crafted experience that I can easily recommend. I personally would also recommend turning off highlights against the game's recommendation. For me turning off highlights made discoveries more exciting and it is easy enough to turn them back on if you are really struggling to find pieces of evidence to use.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't done a review in a while. Haven't really used Steam or played a PC game in a while for that matter.Was positively glued to this one. If you enjoyed Return of the Obra Dinn, and wanted more like that. I think this is your jam. -Difficulty:Like RotOD, I would recommend using no hints whatsoever. Not even one. I did use item highlighting though. I didn't feel like the game was necessarily meant to be played without that.At times solutions feel just out of your grasp, and then you get it, and it's a rewarding feeling.Use pen and paper for anything the game's UI notes don't help you track. You won't need it much, as the game does a fair amount of this for you.Sometimes there's a passive attempt to swerve you as the acting sleuth, but I found this to be enjoyable.-Negative:Not really anything. Maybe a knock against it is that in a couple rare instances (like maybe 5% of the game) I felt like I got lucky, but it kept things moving. I think RotOD hintless did not allow much of that but it has been a while since I beat that.Like RotOD its one of those games where I'd entertain a memory wipe just to re-experience it.-Story/Engagement:I felt the story to be better than RotOD and actually be pertinent. I won't say more than that.The style choices of the game felt very charming and unique. It all gets you attached to what is going on.Can also recommend all the DLC. I can't wait for the 2024 'sequel'.Good luck, and enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is an immensely enjoyable game of puzzle solving / murder mysterying. The difficulty is just right, with the multiple submission sections for answers helping to build you towards the final solution. Each tableau is amusingly presented and manages to tell an interesting story that builds well towards the final chapter. I'm so excited to get started on the DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 This is a great game.I am amazed how well the difficulty curve was balanced and how seemingly unrelated scenes later on start to give away the big picture.Storytelling on the macro level and micro level is very well thought out and the twists you can't foresee,It's a very refreshing take on detective games and everybody  who likes logical puzzles should definitely try this. If you like any classical English literature you also will get a lot out of the setting and If your team makes another project, also think about working on a slightly more refined artstyle. I think many people might be pushed away by the first visual impression of the game. I myself got only really excited about it, after trying the demo.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, it's a great detective game that does minimal hand holding. It was genuinely hard at times!! _childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol is a phenomenal and engaging point and click mystery/puzzle/investigation game. Each chapter drops you in media res into a crime scene, from which point you explore the scene(s), collect evidence, and ultimately compile everything into a coherent explanation of events. The storyline is captivating, and feeds you just enough to keep you engaged and guessing until the last chapter. The main storyline is supplemented by the two DLC, which act as prequels to the main game and really tie up the story nicely (I recommend that the DLC are played after the main story). The story itself is bizarre in the best way possible, and I enjoyed the satirical take on British imperialism, politics, and greed. The artstyle is an absolute feast for the eyes and lends itself nicely to the strong storyline, lore, and gameplay. Don't let yourself be offput by the artstyle--when you're playing the game, it just works. Coupled with the OST, which features unique tracks for each chapter of the main story and DLCs, the presentation of this game is high-quality and refreshingly unique. The puzzles are observation, reason, and deduction based, and provide just enough difficulty to keep your mind working and occupied without being so hard as to render the game frustrating or unplayable. They drive the story forward and make you feel like an active participant in the game as opposed to a passive viewer.While it's reminiscent of Return of the Obra Dinn, The Case of the Golden Idol is incredibly unique and one of the few games that I wish I could wipe my memory of and replay again for the first time. It holds a special place in my heart and I know will be one of the games I recommend to anybody who will listen, and which I will think about often. Highly, highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The Case of the Golden Idol is a point and click detective game, with simple but brilliant gameplay. Get a moment frozen in time, poke around it looking for clues, and then deduce whatever sequence of events immediately led up to that moment. What's really great is the way the gameplay escalates. You'll start with two people figuring out why one pushed the other off a cliff, and by the end you'll be deducing the identities of elaborate sets of characters, their personalities, loyalties, and motivations. It also keeps those deductions fresh, one moment you'll be deciphering sets of runes and another you'll be figuring out who sat where at a dinner table. The music is great, the writing is fun, and the process of solving each mystery is unique and delightful.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

The puzzles were the perfect level of difficulty (This is of course subjective, for me I like a challenge without feeling hopelessly frustrated).You always knew all parts of the puzzle could be found, you might just not have fund the relevant clue for the given question yet.I wish there were 1000 games like this. _childDocuments_.review: How much did I like this game? Well, let me tell you.On the second to last puzzle, I had an "Aha!" moment when I realized that I was misinterpreting a piece of evidence. This allowed me to rethink the entire situation and figure out the solution. Unfortunately for me, I bumped my computer at the exact same time and it shut off.I booted up my computer, restarted the game, and discovered that my save file had been corrupted. The developers had foreseen this happening and provided a way to import save game files to reach the spot where the corruption occurred. I couldn't figure out how to do it properly (I'm sure more tech savvy people could do it but I am not one of them so I was stuck with a corrupted save file).Instead of simply giving up and not finishing the game (since I was so far into it) I decided to start over and I may or may not have used a guide to quickly fill out the solutions to the first ten cases again. Though, to be honest, I remembered most of the solutions anyways.Long story short I have essentially finished the game twice. The game itself is a series of murder mysteries (with an overarching story) where you have to investigate and fill in word puzzles. It's a good time if you couldn't tell from what I've written here.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic thinking game! You must gather key words by exploring (and clicking on) people, desks, books, corpses, and more. _childDocuments_.review: Fun little puzzle game! This is a story puzzler, so understanding what happened and why is more important than any sort of individual logic. _childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing is as it appears, but everything can be made to make sense in the best mystery game I've played since  Return of the Obra Dinn. Golden Idol makes you think in similar ways (and about similar things -- identity, death, and crime) but using a point and click interface to investigate and explore. If you let yourself get into the scenarios, take notes, and put the pieces together yourself, the experience is fun and rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: There is one big flaw with the game:  There are actual points in the game where you are forced to guess based off of the given evidence.There is a flow that the game sets up early on that logical deduction and proper evaluation of the evidence will tell you the answer.  This rule is broken by the time you reach, arguably, the mermaid bar.  At that point you have to begin to guess on the most likely, not the obvious.  After that there are just some straight up shot in the dark guesses to make that may or may not work which makes the game a drag.  I've been obsessing over some of the later levels because of the drawn conclusions to the point where I mathematically proved to myself that the evidence simply does not exist to construct the narration given the established mechanics of the game.  That, in my honest opinion, is a cheap shot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a truly spectacular detective game with some very clever puzzle mechanics.  The core gameplay loop is extremely satisfying.  You examine semi-animated (gorgeous) tableaus to obtain a set of visual clues that you order and combine into slots to solve each chapter's mystery.  The game also does a great job of slowly ramping up complexity and introducing variations to the gameplay loop.My only gripe has to do with a revelation that occurs quite late in the game.  I won't spoil anything, but to me the thing that was revealed was not adequately supported by the preceding plot and gameplay experience.  Am I simply a dumbass that didn't catch numerous references left by the developers hinting at this revelation?  Possibly.  But if I didn't figure it out, or at least suspect it, plenty of others didn't.  There is a concept in storytelling referred to as "suprevitable" where a culminating revelation at the end of the story is found to be both surprising but inevitable based on what came before it.  This is accomplished by what is referred to as a "clue path" that guides the player or viewer towards the inevitable conclusion.  I would say that this game's clue path just needed a little bit of fixing.However, this did not keep me from enjoying the game or buying the DLC at full price in a heartbeat and enjoying the hell out of that as well.  Really great stuff, hope to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Return of the Obra Dinn 2, as the game could have been named, if it had been by the same author.A mystery packed game, where you have to resolve what happened and what the story really is. And oh boy, this game delivers if you like puzzle/mystery games.Best of this kind of games, which are, sadly, quite few.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol probably has one of my most favourite mystery game mechanics I’ve ever encountered (second to the Ace Attorney series) where it directly ties in with actually figuring out the details of the individual cases making up the overarching plot to progress through the story along with barely any hand-holding which made it satisfyingly challenging in the best way.You’re only presented with a single scene each chapter and are required to collect keywords from any clickable item/person available on the scene whether it be from an article, a piece of dialogue, maps, etc. You’re then tasked to figure out what is going on in that 1 scene you’re presented with using the keywords you’ve collected to fill in some blanks of some statement presented to you by the game. You’ll be switching between going to the “Exploring” board where you search the scene to go through the clues available and the “Thinking” board where you sum up your findings to figure out what is actually happening at the scene with the keywords you have available. The interface was so simple and convenient that I had no trouble getting used to the game mechanic in no time. Though the game mechanic seems simple enough, Color Gray Games managed to make the game more difficult as you progress through each chapter where you’ll be presented with larger locations, loads more clues, and even red herrings that made it more challenging to deduce what was actually going on in each scene. You’re even provided with a hint system though I wouldn’t suggest making use of it since it makes for such a satisfying experience if you actually manage to solve the case only with the clues available, and there were a few times when we had to test out a few hypotheses before we got to the actual answer which made for a satisfying reveal when we actually managed to solve it. If we got stuck, it would usually be because of something we overlooked and that’s how clever the developers were at picking what clues to be made available.All in all, I loved the game for its unique mystery solving mechanic with cleverly sprinkled clues and a compelling story with a few unexpected twists that kept me adequately absorbed. However, I would have preferred for the characters to be more fleshed out where they have even more backstory about their motivations and an even crazier, and thought-provoking plot though the lack of depth might be a stylistic choice especially with its cartoonish visual presentation. With these things considered, I highly recommend this game to any mystery adventure game fanatic out there!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! At least one of them I had to sit on overnight, and several I had to break out some paper to write notes. I never had to use any hints which made me feel accomplished. I do wish the game was a little bit longer because I enjoyed it and wanted to keep going. I'd suggest waiting for a sale if you are tight on money only because it feels a touch short for the price. I'd love to see some DLC or a sequel, or a totally new story using the same mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great deduction game where you hunt around for clues and fill in gaps in order to figure out what happened.  It took me 5.6 hours to finish all 11 episodes plus the epilogue, with no hints used.  I probably should have waited for this game to be discounted more before I bought it but I certainly don't regret buying it.  I can easily see myself replaying this game again in a few years.  Hopefully the developers will add more content or make a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game on Steam.  A really inventive spin on the point and click mystery genre.  I'm giving this a negative review, however, due to the horrible Switch port, which is so bad that the developers deserve to be called out on other platforms. I loved this game and recommended it to my Wife.  She wanted to play on Switch rather than PC so she purchased the Switch version.  She completed the game and was starting the additional cases DLC, when, upon closing the game and reentering, the game deleted her entire save file, erasing all her progress.  We did some research and it turns out this has been a known issue for the better part of a year, that happens to every player whenever the game is closed and reopened.  Whenever the game is closed, for any reason, progress is deleted.  They've known about this for months and not bothered to fix it.  They've continued to knowingly sell the game in a broken state, even going so far as releasing additional DLC content, but haven't bothered to fix a save deleting glitch that effects every player.  Totally unacceptable!  I was planning on buying the sequel, but I'm now removing from my wishlist and will not consider purchasing for any reason.Again, all this refers to the Switch port of the game, but I feel this is such egregious behavior by the developer, criticism deserves to bleed over to other platforms.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A real curio of a game which requires you to study a scene and determine what on earth happened. Featuring an interesting and often macabre story with a series of dastardly characters and unfortunate events. Not entirely without frustration on occasion but hugely compelling and ultimately satisfying. The DLC, although just 3 scenes, is happily more of the same and worth it for fans like me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: So... I would not not recommend this. It's not a bad game. But, to be honest, it feels extremely easy. It took me about 3-4hrs to finish all main episodes, and this includes at least one hour spent with one eye on the game and one on a Chinese drama with subtitles I need to actually read. I would highly recommend it to anyone who has never played detective-type games, but if you played Return of Obra Dinn and found it just perfect difficulty-wise, The Case of Golden Idol might be a bit dissapointing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

Needs another grammar/type pass and there are one or two very small bugs, but overall it's remarkably impressive storytelling from such a simple, short, lo-fi puzzle game. A truly innovative mechanic that easily could have kept me engrossed for another 10 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like point and click games, but I always feel lost in the huge environments and options they give to solve mysteries. Also I'm not a huge reader. The Case of the Golden Idol caught my attention from the first chapter since it was a one-screen scenario where you could guess what happened without going around for hours asking all the people about their daily lives. Moving onto the next chapters you can find up to 4 screens and things might become a little difficult, but not overwhelming. _childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. The puzzles are really intricate and unique, and you'll be finding yourself using really subtle clues to figure out how something happened. The main issue, the game is short. It took me 7.5 hours to beat the entire game, including DLC. I've heard a lot of comparison to Return of the Obra Dinn, which is fairly similar in the ways that they conduct the puzzles, meaning that you can't just randomly quess and check, but it will let you know when you're right. The differences start there though. The game takes place across decades, compared to the Obra Dinn which took place across one day, so you'll be matching the same faces to the same names for returning characters, compared to the Obra Dinn where there was just one page to match a name to a face. Similarly, there is a lot more reading documents in this one to collect words related to the case, rather than the Obra Dinn which was almost entirely clues from the environment. The Obra Dinn was almost entirely focused on what happened to the members of the crew, and who they specifically were, while this game wants you to focus on the actual events that happened to lead up to the moment you are witnessing. They take different approaches to the same broad concept, and while I do remember the Return of the Obra Dinn being longer than this game, both felt like they were cut off too soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Less a review and more a story-spoiler reflection (no mysteries spoiled, though!) about the arc of the game and its relationship to historical context, and why I love it so much:A truly wild, unexpected, and incredibly clever setting for a detective game: There are two types of puzzles here at the end of most missions:  and .  take advantage of the scene compositions, the details, the rules that are given in a scene.  ask you to report what happened by installing color-coded parts of speech - names, verbs, prepositions, objects - into slots.I'll explain with a non-game example that's typical of the deductive puzzles you'll find here: You see someone in the middle of cooking a meal. You are given access to the recipe book and a cupboard with ingredients, each with a symbol label that corresponds to its contents but doesn't directly illustrate its contents (say, a diamond-shape for celery, a star for salt). The recipe book tells you some of the ingredients that go into the pot and in what order, some ingredients that absolutely do not go into the pot, and the rest of the ingredient list is torn off. In this game, you would first complete a logic puzzle, figuring out which label goes to what ingredient using the clues. Then, you would complete a descriptive puzzle, by looking the cupboard, see perhaps what has been used and what hasn't, what's missing entirely. The logic puzzles were absolutely my favorite part and were the most satisfying to solve. I loved putting together all of the different pieces and filling in the details of every scene. The fill-in-the-blank descriptive puzzles were difficult for me and took a lot of grimacing and muttering to myself to figure out. It's a consequence of the format of the game: as you progress to the more difficult puzzles, the number of blanks in the fill-in-the-blank descriptive puzzles get overwhelming and, for me, confusing. And, of course, there are clues you collect that are ultimately noise and don't actually fit into the final puzzle solution. If you have trouble with language-based puzzles, this one might be tough for you - though I think it's certainly still worth buying and trying out for the logic puzzles, even if you have to stumble through the description puzzles. What I found interesting about the mechanics of this game is that you are always visiting a scene when it is in motion. You are not so much the detective as you are an omniscient observer who pauses time to peer into a decades-long drama as it unfolds. You are the only entity in this universe who can know the whole story through your observations - each other player in this drama is short-sighted and blinded by self-interest. Sure, there are dastardly machinations, but they are constantly and consistently derailed. So are the best plans of mice and men.Overall: Great game, great setting. Very memorable, and exactly what I'm looking for in a game: something that 1) doesn't break the bank; 2) gets innovative with game formats in a way that doesn't require a high-dollar computer; 3) depends more on mental skill than motor skill (by which I mean, playing it makes you feel smarter); 4) makes bold choices about story, setting, and design; and 5) puts in the effort required to make it all work. If you're into any of the top Steam tags for this game, you can't miss it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and pleasantly challenging deduction-based adventure. Sort of a less grand and less smooth Obra Dinn’s younger brother that is still entertaining and can hold its own at the family reunion. Also, Obra Dinn got the looks in the family. Golden Idol, though, got “interesting features” (or whatever it is they say about ugly children), so it makes up for it with abundant charm and charisma.This game is a series of vignettes, post-crime, where you get to look at the aftermath and untangle a surprisingly complex, soap opera-like ball of yarn where siblings backstab, secret societies lurk and power-hungry villains scheme, all of which frequently culminates in bizarre murder scenes with lots of bodies, but really – when thigs are this fun – who’s counting? The plot is overarching and covers all the vignettes (11 of them plus epilogue) with a recurring cast of characters that establishes itself by mid-game. There’s no narration to speak of besides notes/letters/cards hidden in people’s pockets and a summary of the crime you’ll get after solving it, which adds additional details to the scene you had to work with.  And yet, the story is twisted and layered and doesn’t shy away from crossing into “over-the-top” territory on more than one occasion (which speaks loads about the talent behind this game) but also adds a few complexities to the gameplay because of that.First, gameplay itself – in the “exploring” mode you look at the scene of the crime and collect clues (can be highlighted or not, depending on your preference) that are, in this case, words. After that, you will switch into “thinking” mode, where various tricky questions about what just happened will be presented as scrolls with blank spaces. Your goal is to fill these scrolls with correct words using deduction and logic, extracting info from all the clues you have seen. In its basic form – this is a very fun and rather challenging gameplay, not unlike Obra Dinn at its heart. However, going back to few complexities mentioned above, it isn’t without a few drawbacks. One of them is that the complex plot makes it a difficult game to pick up even after a break of a few days. The game relies heavily on the previous cases to understand the next one, and number of characters and details that you need to keep in mind is pretty high – there can be people who were wearing disguise a few cases back or a specific pocket item that suddenly pops up again – all those small, numerous details escape you after a few days off, making it unnecessarily difficult to get back into it or, alternatively, miss a myriad of references that could help solve the case.Another drawback that could bring an occasional frustration is “fit the right word into a slot” busywork, where you spend more time finding what this game wants you to put in the scroll, even after getting a good idea of what happened, because several words can fit the bill, but the game will only allow that precise one it wants, of course. With all that being said, this is still a highly entertaining game that will make you put your thinking cap on, and if you’re a fan of logic and observation-based puzzles, this will fill the void left in our hearts by Return of the Obra Dinn’s completion and unexplainably low number of purely deduction-focused games.Graphics… Well… This element grows on you. While I have found it to be unique and full of understated indie charm and great use of lighting, many people I have spoken with about this game found the visuals plainly unappealing. I get that, so if you’re looking at the screenshots and thinking “what the hell”, you’re in good company. I, however, think that unpolished, a bit jarring look with a dash of caricature in it can win you over if not right away, then at least as you progress through the game and find yourself enjoying it.  While this component is very subjective, points for originality can safely be added to Golden Idol’s arsenal of points – this is no copy-cat of trendy styles, and the artists blazed their own way, which will always be a plus in my book.The ominous instrumental music is neither all that memorable nor too mundane (besides the DLC- there’s an exotic notable track there that was really cool). It serves as a decent background to lots of thinking you’ll be doing without distracting too much. It can get a bit repetitive eventually, but this is a solid work that aims to support, not to outshine. No voiceover here which is just fine, as we have only a few sentences to read in each case. Add occasional sound effects for ambience, and you’ll get rather minimal but well-implemented soundscape that won’t get you to “ooh and ah” but will get you through the game with no complaints. This indie adventure managed to get an impressive number of reviews (overwhelmingly positive, by the way) which is quite the feat for a small, unique game like this and, at least in this particular case, a good indicator that there’s lots of entertainment value of brain-teasing variety to be found. Golden Idol is, by no means, perfect, but if you’re even remotely into the core gameplay of deduction/logic - this is certainly a game not to miss. Also maybe, just maybe, the amount of praise and positive feedback games like Obra Dinn and Golden Idol are getting shows an overall lack of them in the adventure gaming space, and that people jump on the opportunity to work that gray matter the second it presents itself. With the market being oversaturated with mediocre titles of “pick your favorite trope” variety, I remain hopeful that we’ll get more interesting, engaging games like this.Now I’m off to take in yet another scene with 5 dead people and various sharp objects sticking out of them - a typical day in the Golden Idol universe, where murder is a natural way of getting things you want.  I mean… it works, right?

_childDocuments_.review: Gem of a game. The Case of the Golden Idol is a detective/deduction game which takes place in high class society in a setting kind of like 1700s or 1800s Europe, and revolves around the eponymous Golden Idol. I hate puzzle games. But what makes The Golden Idol different for me is that, when in many puzzle games intricate puzzles get put before you, it breaks my illusion of the game world being realistic because there's often little reason for there to be crazy puzzles just to get in a door or something like that. Puzzles feel like obstacles I have to do before I get to play the real game. But with a good detective game like this, people have motives and it is reasonable that they'd want to cover their tracks. Piecing apart the scenes you see in The Golden Idol teaches you about the characters and is fundamentally what progresses the story. In The Case of the Golden Idol, you load into a scenario. There will probably be a few rooms or areas for your to look around and examine stuff in, and you have a panel where you have to describe what's happened by filling in blanks with words you saw from examining stuff. Probably sounds pretty simple, but of course the scenarios get complicated. The scenes you have to analyze are really well done too. They get fairly difficult (for an anti-puzzle-gamer like me), but I love the attention to detail where you might learn something from a note, pretty standard. But you could have to remember something from a previous scenario to solve the current one, or simply observe something in the background art that isn't interact-able, but when you see it everything makes sense.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've ever played.I've enjoyed point and clicks before, but despite how easy it is to get immersed in them at first, they often get too difficult and therefore boring for me. Right away, this game offered a feature to highlight the important objects so I wouldn't have to pixel hunt, immediately making it more accessible for me. Sure, there are some things that might have been cool to find on my own, but the game really is difficult enough as it is if you take it seriously.And this game wants you to take it seriously.Everything is significant in the most charming of ways. If you're ever stuck, the answer is always to look a little closer (something that just feels painful and redundant in similar titles), and the game is built on that. The simple structure of every level is that if you understand the scene, you can solve it. Even the hint system reflects this, as it requires essentially a flash-card drill to access each hint. This is because in of itself, being more familiar with the objects and characters at play will help you succeed! Also, it keeps the player from cheating themself out of the full experience by digging for hints before putting in the effort of observing the whole scene.On top of excellent mechanics, I love the artfully creepy graphics and the (albeit dark) sense of humor the game has. It has familiar elements and yet feels like an entirely new presentation from any story like this one that I know.As for shortcomings: I do wish it was longer. Once I started to really understand how the game works, I blazed through it and it was over. I just bought the DLC and I hope the quality matches the base game.It would also be nice if I had more control over the music, or if it changed a little more often. The game features many great looping tracks, but a few got old for me.If you can buy this game on sale, it's a steal. If you buy it full price, I believe it's still worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely entertaining and engaging mystery detective puzzle game that involves the player deducing what happened in a certain scene depending on various contextual clues provided within said scene. The prior description may give the game a simple impression, but the execution and brilliance of the developer team turned into what may have been a dull puzzle game to play on the side into an experience unlike any other. If you enjoy doing detective work and juggling your brain around, I think you'll enjoy the game; I certainly have.Also, a quick note: if you're going to play this game, play it in the classic mode (non-Redux). I initially was under the impression that since the Redux version is the newer one, it would provide the player with a better experience. To my misfortune, the main reason Redux was created was to modify the UI to be more suitable for small screen devices like the Nintendo Switch and Steam Deck. Consequentially, this reduces the usability of the UI (or rather makes it very inconvenient) on more conventional and larger screens players may use on desktop setups. This game is also quite fun to play with friends. While lacking in traditional co-op features and functionality, solving the stages with my buddies was a highly enjoyable experience.

In the end the game is a bit short and most cases are quite easy, a harder challenge would have been welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute gem if you liked The return of the Obra Dinn.  Not to easy, Not to hard, but really satisfying resolution vibe. This game, in addition to have an interesting underlying study is really easy to handle to focus on murder resolution. I just finished it and I AM JEALOUS of you who are about to start it !
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best detective game I have ever played. The story is simple but intricate and told in a really fun patch-work kinda way that you can piece together and figure out all by yourself. There are even a lot of story details that are unnecessary to complete the game but can further enhance the plot. I highly encourage not using any hints because this game is not very solvable if you just revisit each clue multiple times (you can also use process of elimination if you're few prompts short). My favorite part of the game is a spolier so read further below if you don't care.......I was hard stuck on the last chapter, I finished all the prompts except the one for lazarus visiting the manor because I couldn't for the life of me figure out his motivation for coming here. That was until I re-read keen's letter about laz's past, and I got to thinking about his origins, at first I went back to look at the criminals from a previous chapter and none fit the bill. So, I started thinking what if someone used the idol to make themselves younger? So I went back to look at each character and their past, one character that disappeared from the story suddenly and was never mentioned again until the very end was edmund cloudsley, so after I finally figured out lazarus (ironic name) is a younger edmund, it made so much sense why he went to the manor and I solved the final case just like that!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game if you like puzzle solving and detective like games, you can see if you like the art style from the images (I personally like this kinda of art style) and the story is pretty simple, but well thought of. What really made the story good for me was the fact that they don't really tell you any of it. You have to figure everything out basically! Not too hard if you're not that good at puzzles, but also not too easy if you're looking for a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Works perfectly on steam deck. The game is going to be compared a lot to Obra Dinn, and it's definitely a similar idea. But if Obra Dinn seemed a little overwhelming for you, having this broken down into distinct cases definitely makes it more digestible.The cases ramp up in complexity in a really good, satisfying way. The story, art, and music are all very good. Took me about five hours for full completion. Definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I liked a lot about this game. The investigation mechanics are satisfying, the environmental narrative is very interesting to unfold and the overarching plot is quite captivating. While not a massive fan of the art style it gives the game extra visual personality. A bit pricey, perhaps. Money well spent if you're into the genre, though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic relatively short puzzle game that tells an interesting story in a very unique way. Each individual puzzle leaves you overwhelmed with info but then as you put it all together the the whole system seamlessly reveals story elements in a very satisfying way. My favourite part is that many of the twists in the story are discovered through deductive reasoning rather than outwardly told.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, but I wish I had my expectations tempered a bit. While similar to Obra Dinn, the puzzles just aren't on the same level; they range from way too straightforward to far too ambiguous. I didn't have too many of those satisfying "aha" moments when figuring things out.Still, it's a clever game with an interesting-enough story, so I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome investigation game. It has a lot in common with Return of the Obra-Dinn. It's however faster to play (as in more focused on investigating than moving around) and somewhat more guided. The story is compeling and got me surprised up to the very end, the art is weird in a good sense. It scratches an itch that is rarely scratched, I wish there was more like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: While the comparisons to Obra Dinn are well-founded (investigating snapshots in time to solve a murder) this game is far more than a 2D imitation. This game's innovation is introducing unique rules and customs in each murder that you must learn to understand the case. They're like logic puzzles that unravel themselves as you draw connections between pieces of evidence, with new ideas presented with every chapter. An absolute joy to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking to scratch that Obra Dinn itch this is the closest you can get. It's broken up into chapters with an overarching story so it's great for if you like to play in short bursts. I can't say much more without spoiling anything so if a detective game is what you're looking for you can't do much better than this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: As most other reviews have mentioned, this game absolutely scratches the Obra Dinn itch and it's wonderful! That said, there are enough differences that this game stands far above and beyond its itch-scratching role: The story moves linearly by chapters so the growing narrative investment isn't only "what happened?," there's a great element of "what's going to happen?" Because of this, there's a great feeling of solving mysteries that aren't included in the drag and drop boxes. You begin to notice patterns, recognize faces, belongings, etc. & to note different plots unfolding. Seriously, the joy of realizing "Oh that's actually _____" is so well done and feels so organic.The best way I could summarize this game is that it's an S-tier point-and-click where the point-and-click objects and combinations are words instead of objects. Instead of creating some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ balloon-pin combo (looking at you, Grim Fandango), you uncover a narrative.I can only hope these two games offer a metric to define a new genre & we'll find ourselves with many more similar games soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. Intuitive puzzler with a lot of "Aha!" moments and being thrilled by picking up a key clue - kind of like a series of mini escape rooms where you have to piece together what has happened. Like others have mentioned, you often begin being fairly overwhelmed by all the names and characters, but the game is very good at sorting your clues for you and subtly helping you along without holding your hand. Also thankful the game doesn't do a lot to "trick" you with names that are similar, tons of red herrings and so on - while some clues are of course misleading, they are well-integrated into the small narratives. I will say that the price point of 18 euro is fairly high - each case is unlikely to take more than 20-40 minutes depending on reading speed and how much you get stuck, with the later cases being harder than the earlier cases, so I assume most players will find between 4-8 hours of content here. Which is fine, but I would consider getting it on sale for the same reason.No regrets from me though - absolutely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: What a great little game. Clever and thoughtful, with a puzzle structure that relies on observation and deduction. It reminded me a bit of RETURN OF THE OBRA DINN, which is one of my favourite games. Some of the later scenarios have a confusing sentence structure that makes it hard to grasp what the puzzle is asking for, but other than that, I loved the game, the setting that was developed, and the narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really well made game. If you played Return of the Obra Dinn, you will absolutely loves this game. It has a similiar concept. In this game you have to solve 11 cases. They often revolve around somebody's death and you have to figure out the names of the people participating in the scene, what happened and sometimes some extra information.At first you will think "there is no way I can solve this" but in the end you will always have that AHA moment where it clicks together. The story is complex. There are a lot of names to remember but after several chapters, you will start to recognise some of the characters and some of the later chapters will allow you to quickly jump to previous chapter to review them. So you don't really have to worry about forgetting something. At first, the individual cases may seem disconnected, but there are couple of plot twist that change your perspection.When you finish the game and revisit those earlier chapters, you will see all the clues that were carefully placed there that back then meant nothing, but now show the whole story. And that's perfect storytelling.10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Overall decent.  Great puzzles, storyline, interface, art, music.I was startled but ultimately liked that you're immediately dropped into playing the game, and then it slowly ramps up in complexity.I liked the way that details are implied without having to use exposition.  And the deduction puzzles step you through the logic of how events connect, further developing the story. (The finished level summaries felt a little obsolete to me, but were reassuring to neatly confirm after the fact)Really enjoyed the overarching story line and slow realisations.The word mechanic was hit and miss.  I tried a screen or two without indicators, but ultimately played the rest with indicators and it kind of just became a "collect 'em all" chore.  Once I realised you can move the stored words around it became easier to organise.  Mildly disappointed with a couple of redundancies in the logic puzzles, especially the DLCs.  Also spots where relevant names were in items but not underlined which was annoying.otherwise the interface was pretty decent.I didn't end up using any hints, but I did have to brute force a couple of word spots.art style great, nostalgic, although the constant jiggling animations were a little annoying at first.music setting the mood was great but sometimes discordant and grating on repeat.Very neat little game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great detective game with clever scenarios and an overarching narrative that keeps twisting and turning. The tone is wonderfully tongue-in-cheek, and the art, albeit low-res, works incredibly well. In most cases, I deduced my way up to near-solution, then applied some trial & error to carry me to the finish line. There are some moments that might frustrate the impatient player but take a step back and the solution will surely present itself. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Relatively short game. Novel premise, similar to Obra Dinn, I enjoyed Obra Dinn better but still had a good time with this game.Writing isn't great but there aren't any typos or anything like that so it's fine. Each scenario makes you think and slowly piece the scene together. If you like detective games, I highly recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Good attempt, but ultimately not clever. Like many similar games, it suffers from errors in framing its logic and deduction (sometimes what you are supposed to logically deduce is probably not what an intelligent person would logically deduce, or final solutions include steps of deduction that would be omitted/unnecessary). It's very hard for developers of this game to put themselves in the player's shoes, but I'm tired of half-attempts. If a game like this doesn't feel clever, it's a glorified drag and drop simulator. That's what I got out of this. I felt the gameplay was dragging words around, not figuring things out.Recommended only to fans of the genre who want to fund indie projects. For those who compare it to Obra Dinn and Outer Wilds: No, those games are clever and have excellent presentation. This isn't on the same level at all. Wary buyers heed this review well and buy those other games first if you haven't experienced them!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: What to say, amazing game, it's like a sort of return to the obra dinn light. It was recommended by the developer of obra dinn no less.Some puzzles are really hard, some are too easy. I bought the game in sale so paid  15 euro for 10 hours of game time which could be less if you really really pay attention. I really recommend it, the attention to detail is awesome, some puzzles might have been made more difficult, but the story in itself was great fun. I d buy a sequel in a heartbeat. We need more games like this. But it is a lot of money for only 10 hours of gametime so be sure to buy int in a sale or when the price goes down.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Obra Dinn a lot, so when people said this was a similarly compelling mystery of course I dug in. It's not really your traditional murder mystery, you're deducing what happened from context clues - most of the time the "deaths" aren't even really the focus, I would even say this is more of an "archaeologist" game than a "detective" game.Short and sweet, and I really enjoyed the story being told. Go into it blind and you probably won't regret the time you spent playing this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol is a short narrative-detective kind of game. The gameplay is very similar to Return of the Obra Dinn (which I loved).You are shown a series of vignettes -- moments frozen in time. Your goals in each vignette are to identify the characters in the scene, and describe the events transpiring. Use observation and deduction to fill in the blanks to solve the puzzle. This mechanicis very fun and satisfying to solve!The Case of the Golden Idol has a delightful story, with twists, surprises, and humor along the way. It was refreshingly short, taking me only 7 hours to solve the whole story. I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys engaging stories and detective gameplay!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol is creative, smart and rewarding, everything I was looking for. What a way to tell a story!The only criticism I have towards this game is the sudden spike in difficulty. Scenes 1 and 2 are really easy, almost trivial, then scene 3 has a LOT going on. Also, scene 5 was the hardest one in the whole game for me. There's just too much information in that one! And it's odd that the hardest scene happens so early.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, look its not for everyone. HOWEVER I do think it is an excellent little puzzle game which streamlined the ideas in Obra Dinn to make them more generally accessible and easy to use as well as having a more interesting story. Both are good games but if I had a choice I'd probably say this one is better. Great purchase for anyone looking to enjoy some great background story telling and some really interesting puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of soul. I really enjoyed the investigative work you do in the game. You have to wear your detective hat here, but it never feels tedious or like busy work. Delving into the narrative while unraveling the ugly underbelly of its dark mysteries is incredibly rewarding, especially once you solve some of the trickier scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game and played it with my husband based on the overwhelmingly positive reviews. My initial impression before playing the game was that the art is hideous. The characters look awful and the settings lack essence. And that's not because of the 16-bit nature of the art style, plenty of games choose 16-bit art as their medium and still create rich characters and environments to help the player feel immersed in the game. The art makes it difficult to become emotionally invested in what goes on. The other reason why I didn't like it is because as a player, I don't have any involvement in the story. It doesn't matter if I figure things out, it holds no baring on the story. So I'm just an observer. And I felt the story itself wasn't really all that impressive or original, especially the anti-climactic ending. I'd probably only recommend buying this if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Did not make me feel smarter. But! Logical reasoning problems are at an appropriately challenging level, well arranged in a cohesive fashion, and even weaved with some humor. Very good for shot holidays. I don't want to make any enemies but this is more enjoyable than Aviary Attorney, honestly, because this achieves more with much less bells and whistles. And that is what a good game should do.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The story is fine, the game play is fine. Its very much like a light version of the Return of the Obra Dinn. There's some very poor musical choices, while there's a couple of great songs. However, the length of the game doesn't justify the $18 price. Took me five hours which is probably about average, and there's honestly no replayability to this game. I appreciate the artistic implementation(except for those really weird songs) and the story telling, but I don't think there's enough here for the price, I'd recommend picking it up for under $10( I know that's not what the dev/publisher want to hear).
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: So much fun to piece together all the details of the scene and figure out what might have happened. The puzzles are so well designed, largely self-contained but they reward you paying attention to how the events are unfolding. I also like how strongly it discourages you from accessing hints - I ended up solving the whole game without any which is just miles more satisfying than letting impatience get the better of you. Lots of comparisons to the Return of the Obra Dinn. I would say this game feels less difficult, but a lot of this is because it has slicker gameplay and is less frustrating from a UI point of view, so it's easier to switch between clues and make the links at the same speed your brain is whirring. Highly recommend for fans of escape rooms who are bored of the same old room escape format - this needs you to make connections in a similar way, but the puzzle mechanics are different enough ti feel fresh and new. I don't think I've enjoyed a puzzler this much since Chants of Sennaar and am super excited for the new golden idol game coming soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: + Fun caricature-esque visual style+ Nice music+ Runs smoothly (no glitches or slowdown, one random crash, no progress lost)+ Engaging gameplay and intriguing, open-ended puzzles+ Interesting story (if a bit anticlimactic in my opinion)- Very short. I'm no Poirot but still 100%'d this game in one evening.- The graphics are a bit misleading sometimes (no spoilers - Some characters appear in multiple scenes and their skin tones appear to change significantly, making ID'ing them much harder)- There are hundreds of clues in the game and every one can be spotted in plain sight, except for two that rely on timing a click on an object moving in the background. This isn't challenging at all, but obfuscating hints like this is a really weird design choice in a puzzle game and led to a lot of frustration for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, worth the spend. Gameplay was interesting and compelling enough that I was happy to see it all the way through and was satisfied it ended when it did. Can be a little easy at times, but there are enough generally compelling red herrings that get it through. Haven't played Obra Din, but this was great, buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited to play this game because I am a huge fan of Return of the Obra Dinn. After finishing it, I would say I was not disappointed. However, I want to point out that this game is shorter and its gameplay is less engaging than that of Return of the Obra Dinn. Though I'd say the deduction is more straightforward and nothing will really confuse and frustrate you as some of the deductions in Obra Dinn did **cough Chinese Topmen cough. The storytelling using the environments and details throughout the different chapters is superb. If you are fan of this genre, or somebody who's looking to scratch that Obra Dinn itch, I'd recommend getting it now at full price; I'd still recommend all other players to try this game when it's on sale. And please, for anyone that hasn't played the masterpieces that are Outer Wilds and Return of the Obra Dinn: please go play them without reading any review or spoilers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Solid fun with minimum fuss, distilling the detective game genre into the bare essentials, by having you examine scenes as they are happening instead of laboriously interviewing after the fact.Very reminiscent of Return of Obra Dinn, in a good way. If you liked that, you're probably going to like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect game for a lazy Sunday. The artwork is unusual but suits the tone of the game. The score, which can verge on repetitive depending on how long you take to solve a case, is also pleasantly unusual.I'd love to see more games in the vein of this and Obra Dinn. 'Sherlockalikes' maybe?The only drawback was that Case 10 bugged out for me and now I can't complete the game unless I wipe my save and start from scratch, which sucks!8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Loved taking the time to piece all the well-laid clues together, and took some pride in trying not using the hints system.  In contrast Return of the Obra Dinn (while still a quality title) was just a touch long and honestly very depressing, whereas this was similar in body count but the music and wavery pixel animations provide enough 'life' to make it more of an adventure.  Featuring backstory and lore that stretches over several (in-game) decades creates a sense of compulsion to continue gnawing these puzzles to the marrow.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches the Obra Dinn itch while feeling completely like its own game. It’s so unique, creative, and unsettling. Very fun for anyone who likes point-and-click games or puzzle games in general.Side note, I downloaded and played the demo for the sequel and I have no idea what happened but the devs switched up the UI and art style and I can’t for the life of me decide why they would do that. Sequel feels like a mobile game. It’s also a lot easier due to some UI changes. It kind of hurt to play because of how much I loved the original.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to the Cloudsley family. They are part of the criminal underworld belonging to a secret society. Pure logic, this game operates on pure logic. Everything you need to solve the whodunit and why they did it in each of the eleven chapters is there, but you will need to have an eye for detail and need to persevere a bit.Each chapter builds on itself, gradually increasing in difficulty in:The number of items you obtain.The number of words that are highlighted.The number of people involved. You can look back in solved chapters to identify people if you need a reminder. If you don’t want to do that take pictures of the panels after you solve them.There are directions for gameplay in the game that include how to access a hint.The mouse wheel scrolls larger so you can zoom in.It does support controllers.You drag and drop the words, a right click removes them. You might need another instance of a name or item, just drag it from the panels you have it on. If you can't drag from one panel without it disappearing try another.If you prefer, you can toggle between the Thinking and Exploring panels by tapping the spacebar.I played with highlights turned on, as the game suggested. It will be a pixel hunt for some items if you do not.Click all red  or underlined wordsFocus on characters and how they fit in.Are they a friend or foe? Are they an employee?Identify all the people who are in the scenes with their first and last names. Pay attention to what is being said and what the characters look like in that moment. Are they afraid, in pain, bleeding?Sometimes the process of elimination worked well for me. If you have two or fewer errors the text will be yellow and the panel heading will say that as well.The game will try to trick you as you go along by adding evidence or characters that have no bearing on the current chapter.Thumbs up for me, good luck to you all!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game that provides the rare eureka moments that only a select few games are capable of. Most similar to games like Return of the Obra Dinn and Duck Detective mechanically, but also has some likeness to the narrative exploration of Outer Wilds. The way in which each subsequent case builds upon the previous gets you invested in the characters and gives some solid stepping stones into each new puzzle. The cases build in difficulty progressively, but mostly in a fair manner that grows alongside your skills and familiarity with the characters, motives, and mechanics. My only gripe is that the final case makes some pretty large leaps and references to past events which aren't entirely clear until same major plot points are revealed in the epilogue. Maybe I didn't pick up on some subtle hints from previous missions, but the difficulty spiked a lot in the final case. The base game and both DLC are well worth playing, and a new game "The Rise of the Golden Idol" will be coming later in the year.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I feel kinda mixed about the game overall.Gameplay-wise, this game is great. You look around a crime scene, gather a bunch of clues and keywords, then piece them together to reveal what happened. Although there is a little bit of guidance in the form of having to fill the blanks on a paper, the game mostly leaves you to figure things out. The puzzles feels logical and the clues are well-laid out with some very creative ones mixed in. On the gameplay front I don't really have anything to complain about.However, this game is a mystery game. Because of that I greatly value the writing, the story, and the feeling of mystery in the narrative. Unfortunately this is where the game kinda falls a bit flat for me.The characters are pretty flat and one dimensional. You're not a detective or anyone that can actually interact with the characters. So everyone is basically just a clue dispenser.The individual murders you're solving are not very interesting, narratively. Some light SPOILERS in this paragraph. Almost all the murders methods are completely mundane. He was shot, he was stabbed, he was poisoned. And almost all the motives are either: he was killed in an accident or he was killed because the cult ordered it. Not very interesting.And the overall narrative is not very impressive either. You can probably figure out the nature of the conspiracy pretty quickly because it's pretty shallow. And after you figure it out, there isn't any mystery anymore. You just watch the conspiracy play out exactly as you expect it would.Again, I'd like to reiterate that gameplay-wise, I had a great time. The puzzles are fun, I felt like I was genuinely putting it together myself. It's just that the mystery isn't very mysterious and the overall narrative is nothing noteworthy.Still recommend, but be aware the plot is not going to wow you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The gameplay is what you can see in the trailers. It's just inspecting crime scenes to collect names, verbs and nouns, and then arranging them to make sentences. It sounds simple, but what makes it great is how logical and accessible the puzzles are, while still offering a satisfying level of challenge. It's absolutely a must play for any fans of investigation games.My only complaint is how short it is. Discounting the amount of time I spent with the game idling while I had to do other things, it probably took me about 4h to beat it without hints. Still, as far as faults go, there not being more of it barely counts as one. I just hope that the devs can make more of it soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle-solving gameplay with an incredible narrative that manages to change up the formula each level. The DLCs are also equally amazing, expanding the world even more than the base game already did. The music is also great, especially for the DLCS, and the art style is very charming.I will say, some of the puzzles require a bit too much interpolation of information gathered. (Specifally the 9th case of base game and the 2nd case of the 2nd DLC)Even still, 9/10 puzzle game would easily recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap; very addictive, cleverly written indie. Loved it. Since having Covid-19 three times, long-term effects include my brain not functioning properly anymore, and it really worries me. It did take me far longer to suss out the nuances, admittedly, but I was able to finally finish the damned thing, and I couldn't be more pleased. Worth it. :-)
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I saw it at Game Maker's Toolkit video about detective games and wanted to try it myself.Very similar to return of the obra dinn with viewing static scenes and deducting what happend. It is easy at first and gets more and more challenging and last 2 levels were quite tough and required some 200 iq deduction skills.Overall it was a great experience and I can reccomend to anyone who wants to play some fantastic investigation game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing. It eventually gets repetitive, and too many of the puzzles can only be solved by trial and error. It also suggests that fascism tries to promote individual virtue, where actually it only promotes group virtues. Maybe because the game designers don't like being virtuous, so they made the bad guys order virtue.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle makers is back with another absolute banger. The only issue I had with this game was finishing it and having no more to play. Just hard enough to make you stare at the same screen for over an hour, while being intuitive enough to keep you from looking up a guide. Oh how close I came, how thrilling it was when I solved it anyways! No one makes games like this and man do I wish he made some more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A very thoughtful and well-designed deduction style puzzle game with a similar vibe to Return of the Obra Dinn. The visual style is distinct yet charming, and overall the presentation makes looking at the meticulously crafted scenes that make up the game a constant pleasure. The setting is also quite interesting, though I will let it speak for itself as you play the game. I highly recommend this game for those who enjoy exploring unique game worlds with puzzle mechanics like the aforementioned Obra Dinn or Outer Wilds where a lot of the "game" takes place in your mind as you suss out clues and attempt to string them all together in a satisfying moment of realization.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let this game fool you: the first scene is simple, without anything behind the curtains. That will quickly stop being true. An excellent little narrative that asks you to figure out what's happening in a scene. But remember: there's more happening in these lives than purely what the game asks for...During the last major level, while trying to put the right people in the right places, the big 'twist' finally hit me, and everything went from disjointed events to a full story. I could have played this game forever, and was so sad as I saw the finish line approach. Big recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - if you are on the fence about this I would wait for a sale because its going to be a one and done. Not long for some people or the frustration might turn your opinion in the last 2-3 cases from positive to negative.I played without hints and without obvious sparkles to give clues on what you had to click. _childDocuments_.review: I was directed to this game by friends. I am not usually playing detective puzzle stories so this was a new experience for me. My first impression was from art and initially it felt like it is not my kind of cup. But I gave the game a shot and played it. The moment I got into the story the art together with music made so much sense to me. No other style would have worked for me. The atmosphere I felt because of this combination was spot on. If I try to describe the atmosphere I got from this, it felt like reading Dickens' story sitting next to the window in a warm room during a cold dark winter evening. You yourself feel safe and cozy, but there is suspense below the surface and you are aware of danger and darkness around you. And if at the beginning I was skeptical about this choice, at the end of the game I loved it. Story itself pulled me in immediately. I was living through story lines of characters like I was reading a good book or watching amazing TV series. I became very invested in some of the characters' lives and wanted to see more and more of them. Even though you do not know biographies of characters in this story, the creators of the game made them very real to me. I felt like I knew the people in this story. I could spot and fantasize that there are both friendship and romantic links between people and was so happy to see some of my theories confirmed or denied at the end. If I would be a streamer my watchers would have listened to me ranting about who is dating who, and who should be dating who, and why. This game was a big discovery for me and I think I might play similar things in future.
