Please do, I'm craving more games like that (and yes, I played DLCs already, they were also fantastic, except the stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moon orientation)
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good, it gets a bit too complicated at the end and it can be challenging on people with my dyslexia when these empty boxes come up more and you almost have to piece together the *entire* thing and the words start to blend but that's moreso a me thing. Just a solid heads up to anyone else with mid/severe dyslexia.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great detective, mystery game.  This game has the pleasure of making you have to think about both the individual case you are trying to solve, but understand the bigger picture.  It is not the most groundbreaking story or anything, but I loved the mysteries of finding out about each death.  Also, the graphics were wonderful.  9/10, highly recommend it if you like point and click detective games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: is one of the most addictive mystery games I have ever seen. You follow the tragedies and schemes of those pursuing the Golden Idol, a mysterious artifact with fabled abilities. You are shown frozen moments, most often when there is a murder involved, and have to examine every inch of the scene to decipher what happened. You get to look inside people's coats, examine paintings and rulebooks, and pick up clues from delightfully clever riddles. Backstabbing and betrayal, secret societies and strange rituals, and so much more! I highly recommend for fans of  and for any gumshoe who enjoys a story-rich narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: As hundreds of others have said already... If you liked obra dinn, you'll love this game. Very unique art style, immersive story and makes you feel like a brainiac when you manage to piece all the clues together! My only frustration is that now I've finished it, I'm craving more and there's isn't much in the way of replay value!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: There aren't many investigation games that really make you think, and then actually make sense when you figure everything out. It's challenging without ever feeling unfair.You can kinda cheat when you've got most of a scene solved, by using process of elimination to figure out the last couple of details. I'll admit I did this a few times when I was stumped, but then I always went back and figured out how I was SUPPOSED to get that answer. The clues were always there in plain sight, I just missed them until I had a better idea of what I was looking for. Honestly, outstanding puzzle design.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better point-and-click mystery games I've played.  Fun story and a good level of challenge once you get past the first few cases.  It felt a bit short, I think the main story took about 5 1/2 hours to finish without any hints, but I enjoyed my time.  I do think the price is fair with the DLC and I do hope they make another.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: How can I phrase this nicely: you probably won't like this game. If you're a puzzle diehard, then this will/should have been on your radar, and this review mostly doesn't concern you.But if you only occasionally play puzzle games, this will leave you wanting. The base game is pretty good -- a fairly smooth, deduction-based puzzle game that tells stories in quite interesting ways. The only downside -- almost certainly whined about relentlessly in the devs' Discord -- is that the base game is somewhat easy. For you, the non-puzzle player, that's a good thing: "somewhat easy" will still be 7-9hrs (among 11 scenarios) of piecing together a twisting, turning story.And then there's the DLCs. Induction-based, primarily. "Harder", with ___ more ___ and even more ____, not just ____ but also _____, leading ____ to _____. (Phrases: "red herrings", "significantly", "waste", "dollar", "money", "phrases", "time", .......) You get the picture: completing scenarios/panels becomes more about eliminating useless possibilities and testing out "theory groupings". You also have to metagame like an absolute madman if you want to get the DLC done semi-quickly.Do not waste money on the DLC unless you just like completing hard things for the sake of it. This is not a very popular game, so there's no one to impress.Base game: 8/10 (accounting for difficulty, 7.5/10)DLC 1 (Spider of Lanka): 5/10 -- very disappointing, contains the worst kind of puzzle errors: errors that are extremely obvious and yet the developers are adamant that they're intentionalDLC 2 (Lemurian Vampire): 6/10. If you enjoy Friday/Saturday NYT crosswords, this is clearly a 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Gave this a shot after seeing it in a "best of 2022" article - easy to pickup and very rewarding. Was hooked right from the get go. By the end of it, was not just the puzzle solving that I was enjoying but the evolution of the story itself From seeing the other reviews, it appears Obra Dinn will be next on my list!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best things I've played in a while. I'm always itching for a 'pure' deduction game, and this one's good enough that I'll buy whatever Color Gray Games makes next. Seriously.The gameplay mechanic is brilliantly intuitive, and the mysteries are challenging without ever resorting to gimmicks. Also SO satisfying when the story starts to come together. Brb going to go recommend this to everyone I know lmao
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a game like this but boy was it fun! Interesting story and I enjoyed the UI for piecing clues together. Art was different and a bit reminiscent of old Lucas Arts games. For me it was quite challenging sometimes but I realized later that I needed to slow down and pay close attention to everything. Definitely would recommend to a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A unique spin on the detective genre. It took me a while to get used to the art, but I did eventually. The game is so clever, and I loved figuring stuff out beneath the surface (even if I needed to call in my sister for help so our collective 2 braincells could figure it out). Give it a go if you enjoy puzzles!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Just the fact that there is a counter of how many clues you have and need to collect is beautiful. It creates a free space to just think and work with all you have. Really fun art style, clever story and storytelling. Probably the only two negatives would be: slightly repetitive soundtrack and the senteces that you need to complete are sometimes just oddly put together in the first place. Still, one of the best point & clicks I have ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fantastic, and i loved almost all of it, please giveth more of this kind of game.I managed to solve 10 of 11 cases without any help or hints. The difficulty went up with every case which is one thing i am not completely happy about, because i am not sure if the higher difficulty in later cases is the result of more complex questions to answer or worse case...design? I prefered the first 8 cases over the last 3 because it felt to me as if it was getting more complicated just for the sake of it.Now, the last case confuses me - i figured most if it out but could not put it together - so i used a hint... and then the other three because all four of them did not answer any of my questions and basically told me what i already knew. Then i looked up the solution in a guide and honestly ...im still confused. Nontheless, 8/11
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This was exactly what I wanted from a deductive detective game. Go in as blind as possible, as the fun is literally piecing together the story, Instead of being a character in the game, you are an outside observer trying to piece together the who, what, where, and how of each murder. The game is generous in letting you know when you -almost- have the answers to a given section and separates out different  questions so you don't have to solve everything at once. I solved the game +DLC in about 8 hours without hints and was genuinely surprised at a some of the developments. If you like logic puzzles and mysteries without having to slog though a visual novel (nothing against visual novels but I have things to do), then this is absolutely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is objectively the best detective game I've ever played. I wish I could re experience it again. The main story is incredible, and the DLCs are pretty good and nice. The puzzles are fantastic and unravelling each level is so satisfying. It basically takes the best parts of Dangonronpa, and combines it with this incredible plot that unfolds more and more in every level. I genuinely cannot recommend this game enough. also, very based Godot devs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: At a length of around 8 hours, this may be the best detective style game I've played. So many design choices were masterfully done.The game tells an excellent story that weaves in cleanly with the mysteries you're tasked with solving. Nothing feels like clutter, and those who pay attention to the underlying story will have an easier time interpreting the events of some subsequent chapters.On top of that, the interface for solving the chapters is done in an incremental fashion that allows you to test your assumptions (e.g. what is the name of person x) while attempting to solve the overall case (person x did thing y because of situation z). This game offers a fantastic experience for anyone who enjoys this genre..
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect game for me, it's really fun. Gather clues from the scene, identify people involved, piece together events all from rather vague contextual clues. It genuinely put your skill in reasoning, deduction, and logic to tests. Makes you feels super smart after solving a case, lol. A solid 10/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Uniquely detailed pixel-art, well-placed music, and overall a well made detective game. The story didn't intrigue me at first but grew on me the more I played.The logic puzzles have a good balance of difficulty. Some are very easy while a couple of them are difficult enough to stop you in your tracks but not make you want to bang your head against the wall in frustration. I'll definitely be getting the DLC in the near future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, what can I say. When Lucas Pope recommends you a detective game you know it will be a good one :)I'd prefer if it would be slightly more difficult and I regret that it's not more intertwined between murders like Obra Dinn was but nevertheless it's a great fun and I enjoyed the story greatly.If you're on the fence just download the demo to see if estetics and form of solving mystery is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting and clever fill-in-the-blanks investigation. I was looking for something similar to Return of The Obra Dinn, and this partly scratched that itch while adding its own ideas+ Satisfyingly challenging, with a reasonable difficulty curve. Loads of 'aha!' moments, and the quirky art style/soundtrack grew on me. Loved joining the dots between the various puzzles- Very very occasionally possible to spoil the solutions
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: After all the great reviews and "this year's 'Return of the Obra Dinn'" comments I expected more from this game. It's pleasant enough to play (dropping words into boxes is always fun) but the logic is often very obscure and the pixelly graphics get to be more annoying than anything else. By the end you're supposed to be able to reconstruct a chain of events, but tbh I just didn't care enough to think about it any more. And completing it in six hours made it fairly pricey per hour played. Some of the music is good though!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: ✅🔳 Recommended - buy it on sale🔳 Avoid Time to finish – 8 hours with no hintsWorth revisiting? Will be fun to revisit in a year or so when I've forgotten some of the solutions✅Best PartThe chosen art style, music and overall presentation are, at first, very strange. However, as you progress further into the game and get to know the characters and their individual, often dark motives, the presentation complements the story, creating an unnerving, unique experience.❌Worst PartFor some reason launching and closing the game breaks my HDR, forcing me to restart it.OverallThe Case of the Golden Idol is a fantastic detective/puzzle game hybrid, with a unique look, intriguing story hooks and satisfying puzzles with solutions which can be deduced entirely from clues found within the game. If you're a fan of other genre contemporaries, such as Return of the Obra Dinn, The Case of the Golden Idol is highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible one of a kind puzzle narrative game that often tests your critical thinking, invites amusement, dark reflection, and intrigue into a world similar too, but not necessarily our own. Overall, an incredible story filled with ancient artefacts, cults, political intrigue, the history of a giant conspiracy, who-dunnit murders and snapshot world-building. Cannot wait for The Rise of the Golden Idol.Base game - 9.5/10The Spider of Lanka - 9/10The Lemurian Vampire - 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is a truly unique game in terms of puzzle gameplay and art style, both of which I adore. I enjoyed piecing together the clues from each scenario, all of which were logical and made sense. I also loved the unfolding of the excellent story chapter by chapter. It's not a particularly long game but one which is definitely memorable and well worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Really good logic deduction game where you are tasked with finding the answers to a number of questions relating to an incident which consists of one or more (nearly) freeze frame scenes.Most of the time this consists of three categories of questions:1) The full names of all characters in the scenes2) Some specific questions about scene specific elements, for example who sat where at the table. 3) A textual overview of the whole case and what happened.The main goal is to solve 3) and you can use 1) and 2) to assist with this task. You can get keywords by investigating the scenes like a point and click game, these can be used to answer the questions in each category. Each category is also verified if you have all correct and there is some aid like Obra Dinn if you are almost correct. This is the story of a number of incidents surrounding a golden idol, in the end, through deduction you can piece together the full story of the events and the characters. Highly recommended for people who enjoyed Return of the Obra Dinn or logical deduction/murder mystery games. It is basically a novel new take on Obra Dinn's systems. I quite liked the music as well.My only gripe is that it is sometimes too easy to trial and error solutions like in Obra Dinn, I feel there was one in particular where I had two answers that could be correct and I couldn't find the clue that would lead you to the right solution. But since there was 50% chance to be correct it's really easy to just test the other possibility rather than finding it out for yourself.6 hours to beat, used no hints. Hope the developers will add more cases and/or create a similar style game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: FabulousI enjoyed every second of this. It's smart and makes you think you're smart when you link things together because of it's fantastic writing.Admittedly there were points I had to somewhat guess the answer to because I was a little confused, but when I actually solved certain cases it all made sense and I berated myself for not seeing the clues.This is especially true of the last case, of which when I answered it and understood why the answer was correct, an actual lightning bolt struck me and tied the whole thing together and it was just such a fantastic revelation that ended the game perfectly.What I wouldn't do for more content like this.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: One of the finest detective games I've ever played. Well paced and so engaging that once I started playing I never wanted to stop until I got the end. If I have any criticisms, they aren't popping up in my head as I write this review. Absolutely sublime from start to finish. Can't wait to see what Color Gray Games does next!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a cool detective game. I was engaged while playing it most of the time. Some puzzles are fuzzy and lean more into moonlogic but most are fun to decipher. Many of the clues are found in texts, that got tedious after a while. I had wished the scenes and objects themselves to be my main way of finding truth. Nice game, no where near as good as Obra Dinn though, keep your hype level moderate.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Terrific. Loved every minute of it. Anyone can tell that this looks very similar to Obra Dinn, but The Case of the Golden Idol benefits from having 12 different self-contained mysteries to solve and an overarching narrative that is fun and engaging to piece together as the game goes along. Each mystery contains unique puzzles to solve that lead to many satisfying "a-ha!" moments. One of the best games I've played this year, and that's a phenomenal feat from an indie debut, considering this is the same year that Elden Ring came out.Edit: Check out the two DLCs too. Worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice game if you liked The return of Obra Dinn or similar detective games. It contains a lot of nice deduction puzzle chapters that together creates a story.I really recommend that you avoid reading anything more about the game and that you try to avoid the hints as much as possible to increase the experience; because it feels great when you deduct every piece in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic from start to finish. Finally someone has followed up Obra Dinn with another "Detective" game, or maybe a "Dinn-alike", with a boatload of style, gravitas, horror and mystery which befits the genre.The game is definitely easier than Obra Dinn, but it's very clever in how it makes it easier: you are given two kinds of clues - word clues, like a first name or a verb (usually "murdered" or something equally sinister), and observation clues in the environment. Like Obra Dinn the game can also be brute-forced if you feel you're close to an answer, but like Obra Dinn it's very good at making sure its observational requirement for each of its 14 puzzles are fair enough that you'll get them most of the time.I will say that clue-hunting with indicators turned off doesn't work well. There's often a situation where a clue ends up being a word pulled off a note or letter, or someone saying something, and it's sometimes very mean-spirited (the word "here" is required at one point). Fortunately the game strongly recommends you keep the clue indicators on, which really aids game pace. In short, much like Return Of The Obra Dinn, this game is a fantastic game for one or two players to puzzle over on an October evening whilst it's raining outside. And much like that game, I'm now very desperate for a sequel or a followup!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of puzzle games or logic puzzles, this game is an absolute must play.The game succeeds in making the characters recognizable and memorable so that you can follow the through-line through the entirety of the story. By the end everything is revealed and you are rewarded with If the developers choose to make another game like this, I will definitely be sure to try it, even if its more of the same with a new story and some new twists and turns.Wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: If you love 'Whodunnits' you're going to adore this. The graphics are grimy and pixelated, the music is like an 18th Century opera composer met a sound-experimentalist and had too much booze; The result is just an overall ambience that is really great, funny and sardonic garnished with a little bit of creepy pasta. The fictional story elements pack a punch, too - a dizzying brew of politics, subversion, 18th Century virtues and a nod to history with a satirical hat.The developers have been clever enough to present you with - what seems like - simple puzzles but you actually spend a good hour or so on each one. You're presented with loads of different bits of information so you find yourself hypothesising loads of different possibilities and having to spend the time eliminating each one against the clues available. It's a slow and in-depth process due to the amount of information to sift through and it's an incredibly well-designed mechanism. For gamers like me, who are mature and looking for games that stretch your brain-chains so gloriously that you feel you're temporarily a part of something really clever and really great, this is for you.My only criticism is that I'd like some more of it. Recommended, absolutely! I'm now considering changing my career to become the reincarnated Sherlock Holmes. Well done, devs. Keep my money. KEEP IT
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful investigation gem! A satiric costume drama infused with the esoteric. How it throws you in right after the moment of death, where you need to entangle bits and people into words that has to be filled in like little puzzles (resembling a mechanic in Return of the Obra Dinn). It is simply great fun!I would think fans of the Black Adder-esque, the Professor Layton-series and Return of the Obra Dinn would enjoy this very much indeed. It does end up feeling very much like its own take on the investigation-genre.My only criticism would be that the last two scenarios are too big in scope, or unnecessarily complicated, and keeping track of numbers and times during a day was a bit tedious and had been done much better in a previous scenario.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly brilliant. The overarching plot kept me hooked the whole time, and it really put my brain to the test. I had a actual conspiracy theorist boards (red string and all) going for multiple scenarios, and I immediately bought the DLCs after finishing the base game (and ended up enjoying those more!).Top buy for those who like detective games that don't hold your hand. Can't wait for the sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who hasn't played Obra Dinn, I can only say I'm so excited to try that game after I finish this one because this has scratched an itch for me that I didn't even realize I could get scratched. I can't get enough of how truly fun and engaging this style of deduction is. I feel like my input and interpretation are actually being engaged, and I will miss that feeling when the game is over.The art is also so charming and the music is always atmospheric without annoying me, and I get annoyed easily by repetition so I mean that to mean a lot. I've been playing with a friend and I think it's honestly my ideal way to experience it, as there's lots of little bits of charm in between all the great escalation of difficulty and intensity, and I think seeing it all play out in front of it is even better than just writing or talking about it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game is obviously inspired by The Return of the Obra Dinn - both in gameplay, and style of narrative.But The Case of the Golden Idol is still very good, on its own!Improvements to interface, solid puzzle variety. Everything was logical, as it should be.It was very enjoyable, and had 6-8 hours of content to it, including the levels from the demo. Yeah, the demo is also solid and gives a taste of the game!Definitely recommended if you are into detective/deduction games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't heard enough people talking about this game. It's very good! When I do hear it described, it's compared to Return of the Obra Dinn. While the visuals are completely different, I believe the comparison is appropriate. However, I much prefer the way this game separates the game into discreet chapters. This made it much easier to keep track of all of the clues and know when I was supposed to apply each of them. It kept the puzzles from being overwhelming and let me play the game in 20-40 minute chunks without losing track of what was happening.I'd buy a sequel day one. No notes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Score : 9/10 This game is everything you could hope for and then more. It builds an amazing atmosphere with its stylistic visuals and aa gripping story through its 11 cases. Both of these highs are complemented by an amazing soundtrack.One thing does have to be said for all the people that are coming to the game expecting a "detective" game. I wouldnt really call it a detective game rather a "puzzle mystery" game. You do not influence  outcomes and verdicts and thus this game shouldnt be classified as a detective game. You do however review evidence and through deduction attempt solving the presented cases.You wont regret this purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game. From an interesting and consistent art style to a unique story that gets more fascinating the more you examine it, to some atmospheric tracks. It is great.I played through the base game and DLC, and had a blast. The puzzles are challenging and engaging. And I'm sad that I'm done now. Well worth a geez if you're eager for a puzzle and mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: If you like using your brain, puzzles and solving cases, this game is the closest thing to feeling like a detective. Search for clues to find out who is who, who killed who and the events that happened.More accessible maybe than Obra Dinn due to the colors, the easier navigation and the cartoonish look of gruesome murders, I highely recommend this game that I "binge-played". I can't wait for more of the same type. Length and difficulty is perfect. It can be done without using any hints but is difficult enough to make you wreck your brain. The story is complex, and funny, with twists and turns. A really really good find!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most innovative and addicting puzzle adventure games I've ever played. Solving each case in Golden Idol is incredibly fun and everything is logically deducible without guessing. I just wish it was a bit longer, and the final case is a bit disappointing compared to some of the earlier ones.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fun but definitely on the slightly too easy side for me. There isn't much to compare The case of the Golden Idol to other than Obra Dinn so if you haven't played that I'd recommend The case of the Golden Idol first as a warm up and then Obra Dinn since it's more difficult and requires significantly more deduction. If you play this after Obra Dinn it's going to be a relatively easy jaunt. Still enjoyable and worth picking up on a sale since there are very few games in this genre for those of us who enjoy them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game!The story was interesting and the game trusts you to put two and two together, and while it can be a little challenging at time, it's definitely worth it!I didn't use any hints so I cannot make a comment on how helpful they are if you are stuck, but as most of these other reviews state, if you are a fan of Return of the Obra Dinn, this is a great find highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept for a game. The puzzles and clues are interesting (some a bit involved) but not impossible to figure out. There's a counter at each level to let you know if you've found everything. There is also an "easier" mode that shows clues; it can be toggled on and off as needed.  It's a cool storyline to follow the family and the idol across the years and how things develop.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game in the vein of Obra Dinn and it's a promising take on the adventure/investigation genre.What is interesting here is that you're not playing any particular role, you're not the detective or anything, and even Obra Dinn - a similar game - tried to give you motivation. Here you are a spectator, a reader, and you have to make an effort to understand what happens. You are presented with a scene that initially looks confusing. There is a number of clues to click on. There's kind of a questionnaire you have to fill out to "complete" every "level" but it's a helpful tool to understand the events more than a challenge. The fun comes from getting from what the hell is even happening here part to a complete understanding of the series of events that led to a moment you witness now.Again, you're not here to accuse anyone or to influence the events, you're just here to understand them. This feels like a bold and distinctly videogame-ish way to tell the story. The closest analogy in the traditional media might be a heist movie where you're presented with some sequence and then the explanations are thrown at you, but here you're supposed to be much more active.It's not too hard and there are hints available. I highly recommend it even if you don't like the art style, I sure don't. The DLC (The Spider of Lanka) is more of the same and is totally worth it too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun, pretty short point and click detective, "figure-it-out-yourself" kinda game. A lot of people compare it to Return of the Obra Dinn, and there are a fair few similarities, but it didn't really scratch the same itch in quite  the way other people talk about it. The mystery wraps up really well, and I found the ending to be surprisingly good, since I hadn't really expected much. All in all, it's probably better to think of this as a more traditional puzzle game about figuring out crimes rather than looking at it as if it could be more Obra Dinn.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. Only needed one hint the entire time, and that's because I was too hyperfocused on the one plot element - funny enough, the pre-hint suggestions warn you against doing exactly that. Overall, it could've done to be longer for the price it's at, but it was sweet and enjoyable. The story was the right amount of convoluted to be interesting and unique without being bloated or pretentious.The art style is hilarious moreso than horrifying (eg: the Pear brothers case) but it's great for the atmosphere and theme of some locations. The music is gorgeous, honestly. Superbly well-done and it repeats on each screen without getting too grating. Every level has its own motif, too - at least from what I could tell. Honestly, I hope this dev team makes more like this, with other interesting stories they can come up with.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol is a perfect game to play together with your significant other. Writing down clues, solving the scenes together, high-fiving after those incredible "AH-HAH" moments. It's pure bliss and I can't recommend it enough.Sure, it's probably just as fun played solo, but there's just something so special about playing detective with a partner, that I think everyone should try it at least once.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece following the footsteps of Obra Dinn.Much simpler in mechanics but still leaps ahead of the usual detective point & click games. They have refined the work of a madman (Lucas Pope in Obra Dinn) into a more normal experience, but you still have to think as hard and look for details as in the other game.I can only hope that more games like this one get released. Obra Dinn was a very difficult game to reexecute, but we certainly want more games with ambitious deduction game mechanics like this one.It also reminds me a little of the Sherlock Holmes Tabletop games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of doing books of brain teasers in bed when I was sick as a kid. A lot of tough scenarios that have you guessing. I strongly recommend playing without hints/markers, but they help a lot if you get stuck.Good introduction to mechanics and I liked the variety from episode to episode. I often had a feeling of "Oh god" when everything was getting set up, and got sort of overwhelmed. But taking everything one clue at a time makes it much more manageable.Did feel like some later scenes served more as story exposition over challenging puzzles, which was disappointing. The overall story was well-written and had me oohing and aahing. The artstyle is both creepy and charming.DLC: Spider of Lanka trades width for depth, with some real headscratchers that require you consolidate a lot of information from different places while being contained in only 3 scenes. Continued the exciting scenarios from the base game and I wish there had been more.On the flip side, The Lemurian Vampire I felt was too complex to follow logically, but maybe my brain was just fried from the earlier mysteries. The overall story was also intriguing, and I wish there had been more, but I didn't gather the story beats well from the vague clues like I could with the base game and Spider of Lanka. A lot of guesswork (though pretty simple to fill in the blanks using context clues) once I got all the clues. I completed the DLC but still don't know how I was supposed to gather a lot of the details from the minimal interactions I could access. Tough but not particularly fun.8/10 I haven't played a logic game that encaptured me like this since Obra Dinn, and Golden Idol is different enough that OD fans will immediately enjoy it. I look forward to anything this team puts out next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game was certainly an interesting experience! At first, I had my doubts because I honestly thought its particular pixelated style was a bit off-putting. But I got used to it quickly, and now I think it goes very well with the absurdism present in the game. I loved the plot  . The soundtrack is also good. Sometimes it was frustrating because my deduction was correct, but perhaps I failed in the placement of a word, and that made it take me much longer to solve some cases. Even so, I finished it in about 9 hours. That is why I recommend it, but only if you buy it on sale. The original price seems quite high to me, but I think it's worth playing  if you can get it for less. I would love to play the DLCs and the sequel in the future, so it's a yes from me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: really cool game - each chapter leads to a series of increasingly complicated logic puzzles that can seem daunting at first, but the game does a great job at sectioning off pieces of each mystery so no matter how stuck you start to feel you can bite off a small part that will snowball into solving the rest of the puzzle. obviously if you enjoyed Obra Dinn you will get a kick out of this game, I definitely felt similar levels of satisfaction solving each case.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great detective game where you gather clues to deduce a series of events that lead up to a murder. It's split into 4 chapters, usually comprised of 3 cases, each increasing in complexity as you go along. The progression here feels really solid, offering a good challenge that never felt illogical or unfair. The main game takes around 6 hours to complete and for the quality of the experience it really feels worth it. Definitely give it a go if you're looking for a fun mystery to get stuck into.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Golden Idol is quite a unique game that does a pretty good job at scratching the detective itch you might feel if you've played games like Return of the Obra Dinn before, with its own charming visuals distinct from others. The game is not long, probably about 4-5 hours if you haven't played the demo, across 11.5 levels (12th is an epilogue of sorts), but packs a fun story delivered very uniquely, since you are merely discovering it instead of taking part. My only hesitation with recommending this game is that its actual mysteries aren't very difficult to solve, mostly due to a lack of red herrings. So I'd recommend Golden Idol. If you want a game that leaves you scratching your head for hours debating possible solutions you'll want to look elsewhere, but if you're just in it for a fun time and a unique game, definitely check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Masterfully crafted puzzle game with great use of logic puzzles, mystery and red herrings. You really have to pay attention to detail and use information given in interesting ways to solve the scenes. You may also have to think outside the box or use a bit of guesswork when the game withholds info. My sister and I beat every chapter 100% without hints and it was fantastic. We shared so many epiphanies where everything clicked at once and resulted in us solving a bunch of narratives or puzzles at once. You really feel like a detective playing this game, I highly recommend it if you're a logical/analytical person looking for a fun puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptional detective-y deductive puzzle game. It gives you just enough terms to work with and variables to fill that it's hard to brute-force or cheese the blanks, but without being overwhelming or unreasonable to figure out. It pairs this with a unique and compelling story which takes some unexpected turns along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to anyone who can read in English and likes "detective" games. The story is very intriguing that makes me really wanna play the next episode. (It also helped me improved my English name memory “impairment” as I always find it hard to remember a bunch of English names as a Chinese)The only thing I could complain is that the game is too short! I want more!!!!!!!!! But, the story is condensed and makes me really satisfied. Probably this game would be the best indie game of 2022 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer : Bought the game with my own money.The case of the golden idol is a point and click puzzle/mystery adventure. You will have to investigate a series of mysterious deaths inexplicably related to a strange artefact.    My review :Graphics : 2 points : Very charming 2D pixel art.Gameplay : 1 points : A simple point and click, that works perfectly.Sound : 0,5 point : The soundtrack is nice, but not unforgettable.Replay value : 0 points : Once you have done 1 playthrough, you dont need to come back to it. Entertainment value : 2 points : TL.DR : 5,5/10A very nice and cool mystery game. Very well writen, it has some head scratching moments.If you liked "Return of the Obra Dinn" you will like "the case of the golden idol".
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A deduction who dunnit? adventure game. I (and you) know exactly what kind of game you can expect just by looking at the screenshots (trailer not so much), it attracted to me, yet i put off playing it, until i gave it a chance.You can choose to go pixel hunting and gather all the clues or choose to go the easy route and have them handed to you but that really spoils the fun (and you won't get an achievement), although it can also be tedious to find that last missing clue.It starts of easy offcourse with a few suspects, a few items, up until the end where you get almost a whole essay with 3 murders each with their own victim/murderer/location etc etc, and there in the last 3-4 cases it kinda gets too difficult, and i honestly looked up the guide for some tips.Also i found the ending a bit disappointing, it was just 1 story page (while there were 3 murders), even so i really hope on a sequel as i played this from the beginning to the end in 1 sitting, and i barely do that anymore these days.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This scratched the mystery itch I've had since playing Return of the Obra Dinn!  I was in my Hercule Poirot bag! The puzzles are great and compact.  The art style is a little jarring, but some of it reminds me of Hotline Miami, and once I got used to it, I appreciated the detail of the pixel art.  It's short, but I think it's well worth a try if you like a brain teaser!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I at first posted a negative review, citing how aggravating some of these mysteries in this game were and how, in my opinion, unsatisfying some of the answers to the puzzles where. However, as days went by, the storyline that had developed over the 12 chapters of this game never left my mind and I couldn't deny the Case of the Golden Idol's beauty. The art style and the soundtrack are divine. And the mysteries are so complex and crafted stunningly. I think I was just frustrated that I was not clever enough to solve some of them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much intricacy, narrative intelligence and attention to detail in this game, it's hard to describe without spoiling it. Suffice to say over the course of several days it took me to solve everything, I had sooo many "eurêka" moments while doing something else. It is very satisfying when two little details from separate episodes of this game suddenly click together in my brain and make me understand some subtle causality link.The really masterful thing the creators of this game managed to do is to slowly, seamlessly switch from independent puzzles you solve one by one, to more complex ones where backtracking may be useful to really be sure you understand everything, and by the last episode when the interface gives you shortcuts to backtrack quickly, it's already a habit you took without the game ever telling you to.(not that the game ever tells you anything - in this game, it is the player who tells the game how things work, and somehow it doesn't feel weird at all)
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches the same itch as Return of the Obrah Dinn, but in a bite-sized way.The murder mysteries are broken up into individual dioramas, which makes it easy to pick up and play in smaller chunks.The logical deduction feels fair and satisfying 99% of the time, and the gameplay interaction of "solving" the mysteries leaves enough room for error, and requires enough lateral thinking, that it doesn't feel like a multiple-choice.Very good murder mystery game, I highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: It's an investigation game where you have to identify events based on still images and various bits of information like letters, books and whatever a character is thinking or saying. From these bits of text you obtain words that you'll use to fill blanks in several separated texts on your report.The game tells a story divided into chapters.I found it relatively easy up to the ninth over eleven chapters. The epilogue was pretty much straightforward and no effort at all.From chapter nine, finding out what happened wasn't much more difficult. However there are so many blanks to I've often struggled to guess what part of what I found out was to be reported where and then using what words.Beside that little detail, I've enjoyed finding out what was happening and discovering the story chapter by chapter.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty short (~7 hours for the main story), but this is one of those games whose experience can't be measured in dollars per hour. In the style of Obra Dinn, the player must sift through frozen moments in time and piece together whodunnit. Gameplay-wise, the puzzles start simple and become much more complex with large amounts of information to consider. The difficulty is enough to make the solution satisfying and intuitive without being frustrating. The game also helps you by adding secondary goals within each case (e.g. identify each character) to organize your thoughts and break down the larger investigation into manageable parts. If you're really stuck, there's also a hint button, but it's probably worth it to keep thinking for a bit longer to make that next breakthrough. Admittedly, I couldn't help but take advantage of the "two or fewer slots are incorrect" indicator to cheese some of the case solutions.Golden Idol's storytelling has definitely earned its acclaim. In the process of poring through all the details of each case, the player is gradually exposed to an overarching narrative with lots of moving parts. Each solved case contributes a small piece of the story, but many aspects of the plot remain obscure until you solve later cases. Similarly, the player builds a profile of each of the characters in broken-up pieces: their motives, their affiliations, their secrets, etc. As a result, although the game is relatively short, the dense delivery of the story makes each hour of gameplay very satisfying.Before playing the game, I thought the art style looked a little crusty on the Steam store page, but I grew to really like it. It ends up being a part of Golden Idol's sense of humor and generally gritty aesthetic. The rough-around-the-edges styling of many of the characters also physically reflects their inner character traits. (Side note: I'm noticing in the trailer for the sequel a lot of weird deepfake animation for the characters' facial movements and I really hope that's just a placeholder.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: How else do I put it but...FUN! It was so fun. And satisfying. One of those puzzle/whodunit games where the "I don't get it" to "OHHH! DUH!" is so satisfying. Emphasis on satisfying. The story itself is interesting; it's wacky enough that the investigation can take you to places you didn't consider, but grounded enough that it never feels like cheating. Highly recommend if you like whodunits.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a cool detective/mystery game. It really encourages you to take notes to entangle the meta plot between the single murder cases, which becomes necessary for the last scenes. I really enjoyed the structure of the whole game and like a mad man writing notes and ideas and drawing character relationship graphs. In the end every single question gets answered and the game makes you feel like you are the smart-ass detective that solved it all with your own wits while in reality leading you very smart.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome and it kinda came out of nowhere. It's a mystery game where you have a scene set and you have to piece what happened exactly. It is very similar to Obra Dinn only a little bit easier. For example in obra dinn you would be left to wonder what you missed in the memories to complete everything, meanwhile in the golden idol it tells you when you found everything you need to complete the case. And even if you missed something there is an easy highlight toggle that allows you to see what you missed incase you dont feel like pixel hunting. There is also a hint system, that i didnt use personally, for people that feel stuck.Overall if someone enjoyed obra dinn they will enjoy this one. The story i would say is pretty similar, when it comes to theme that is, i feel like its told somewhat better here tho maybe because its a series of events that  have almost the same cast of character so you can follow it easier instead of 60 people like Dinn. Personaly it took my around 6-6.5 hours to finish the game which i think is fair for the asking price and the enjoyment it brought me. But i have to say that i wish it was longer, even if it was a bunch of different stories and had like 70 scenarios i would still play them all. So i do hope they decide to either create a few more stories and release them as free updates or even as dlc. But i have to say that a major factor that i find this game this good is that the scenarios were connected and not individual murder cases. It made you want to see what would be the end. Awesome work.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: In many detective games you can get spoiled due to there being a limited number of dialog options, or there being some other way in which your character makes a deduction before you as the player; not here! Having to fill in individual words to piece together my deductions made every solution feel earned. The overarching story was also super interesting and seeing how the vignettes for each case fit together was very satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Briefly Put, it's like... a 2d version of The Return of the Obra-dinn.If, like me, you enjoyed that game, you'll enjoy this one as well.I've 3 hours so far, and only about a third of the way through. It's starts off simple, but quickly gets more... not complicated, exactly... but there is a more rooms, places to investigate, items to look at, clues and words to find.Once you have completed a level, you start to understand. I've finished a level or two with a hint and things I hadn't considered suddenly slot into place and make sense. I've found that tid-bits from previous levels can help you in later ones. Which is a good thing, everything seems to nicely tie together so far.Funny, I was eager to play a beta under NDA... then I discovered and got lost in this instead. Well worth it so far, however, like Obra-dinn. I fear I won't get to replay it after once I finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked The Return of Obra Dinn, you'll probably like this one. This game offers 12 murder cases with frozen-in-time vignettes, and it's your job to try and explain what happened.The investigation happens in two screens: exploration screen allows moving between scenes where murder takes place, and thinking screen which has certain key questions that must be answered. The actual solving happens by finding clues in the exploration screen, which then show up as words in the thinking screen. These words can then be dragged into their (hopefully) correctly induced spots .Cases grow in complexity quite rapidly as does the story, and you really have to pay attention not only to the immediate pieces of evidence in the thinking screen, but to different documents, diaries and statements scattered about. And you also have to think about  you found the evidence, and what sequence of events would explain the evidence. I'd advice having an outside documentation method for quick cross-referencing, especially in the last case.I recommend this to people who are into murder mysteries, and who are not afraid of a tough challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Obra Dinn, you might find this one way more merciful with your deductions. Overall, I highly recommend this game, but please take your time with it, lest you feel it pale in comparison to longer, more complicated titles.

There are 15(?) puzzles total. By the 8th, I had become overwhelmed with how many characters and events there were to remember. The art style is very unique and is part of what pulled me in initially.The music is very memorable and subtle at the same time, especially the Inn tracks.If you want a detective journey to get lost in and enjoy the mental process of "pinning clues to a board", then this title is definitely for you.I enjoyed my time overall, but I likely will not return to this for subsequent playthroughs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game.The game had me at the first chapter. The puzzles are perfectly balanced, making you work for that true detective feeling, whilst not making the story or clues too tenuous.The game managed to get the right level of difficulty throughout, without being too easy at the start, nor too hard at the end. _childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I've always wanted to see more mystery games that require actual deduction and notetaking and The Case of the Golden Idol delivers. While most mystery games lead you along piece-by-piece to the right answer, Golden Idol dumps you into a chaotic scene frozen in time and expects you to figure it all out in one go. Not all the sections are built the same, when this game gets good it gets REALLY good. The game somehow creates strong build-up and revelations to mysteries despite showing you everything all at once.I must also praise the storytelling in this game for how well it's hidden. Every scene has large implications for an ongoing narrative, but you don't really discover most of it until the end of the game. Going back and piecing together how every moment ties into each other was the debatably the best part of this game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzles, fantastic visuals and audio design. A great passion for point-and-click games is brimming throughout the whole experience. UI is a bit clunky and less music than I'd prefer (making the long sections where I'm thinking things through grating). Though I came close, I never took any hints and I'm glad I didn't.What a heck of a trip this game is. I found myself cheering at the end! Why? Play to find out for yourself ;)9/10 - "These sure are fine coats."
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Although I had to get used to the retro pixel-art graphics in the beginning, I really enjoyed this game. The scenes look deceptively simple at first and quickly increase in complexity. As you read, analyze and reassess all the clues (often over and over again, until things suddenly start clicking in place), a complete story slowly emerges. You will not only find the necessary clues to complete the text puzzles and find out who is who, but also a rich background story to the characters. Who was secretly in love with whom? Who tried to blackmail one of the characters? The static pictures become alive. If you get stuck, it may help to take some notes to assemble the clues from different rooms, letters, books etc. Sometimes it also helps to go back to an earlier chapter to remind yourself of an important detail about a character.Finally solving the puzzles after going over the scene again and suddenly finding the clue you missed feels very rewarding on its own. Completing the whole story feels even better, because all the cases are connected and some things will only really make sense when you look back, knowing the whole story.

_childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol is a point and click puzzle game. You don’t play as any particular character, but rather from the perspective of an omniscient spectator, interested only in understanding the narrative and the drama within it. The game tells the story of the titular golden idol, a magical artefact which, when given different commands, has a variety of effects on the world, from starting fires to draining and giving life. It is exactly the sort of artefact that could do unspeakable evil in the wrong hands, and which - spoiler alert - does exactly that. Mechanically, the Case of the Golden Idol is a point and click puzzle game, but less in the Botanicula sense, and more in the ABC Murders sense. The game consists of a set of tableaus depicting an event - usually a murder - with the player being tasked with understanding the tableau. Clicking serves as a way to gather clues and review evidence, and the game even has a helpful option to highlight all the various clues to avoid pixel hunting. The puzzle element is not within the world itself, but rather, the act of understanding the narrative and making sense of all the clues laid out on the table. This is a logic game. While the tableaus may seem overwhelming when first loaded, it is immensely satisfying to piece together the clues and create a coherent narrative. The clues themselves are expertly crafted, both to create dynamism within the tableau, and to still provide the information needed to solve the scene. It’s a tricky combination, and the Case of the Golden Idol pulls it off perfectly, providing just enough information to solve the mystery, while letting the natural pace of the action do the necessary work to withhold information. The player serves only as a witness to the story in the Case of the Golden Idol. Whether the player successfully solves the mystery of a particular tableau or not has no real bearing on the story, beyond our ability to move forward within it. This creates an interesting dynamic, where the story itself propels the player forward without ever saying anything on its own. Weirdly, the Case of the Golden Idol feels like the player telling themselves a story, crafted from the various threads around them, but one they sort out for themselves nonetheless. This lack of external pressure or any type of character also creates an environment where the player can examine a scene clinically and carefully. By freezing moments and engaging with them piecemeal, the game perfectly captures the sense of logic-based omniscience embodied in the like of Hercule Poirot or Sherlock Holmes. When given the time and space, any of us can take disparate clues and figure out how they all fit together and what their narrative is. Any of us can be a master detective.And it is oh so very satisfying to be that detective.It’s that combination of the lack of external pressure with puzzles that give just enough information to be solvable, but not enough to be simple that make this game nearly perfect. It triggers that deep desire within all of us to understand something. The feeling of taking an empty board and filling it is immensely satisfying, even if the only reason we do it is for our own understanding. No one is counting on us to solve this. There are no stakes. All that matters is our own desire, but the Case of the Golden Idol is compelling enough that, rather than being a flaw, that works in its favour. This is one of the best games I have played, and definitely one of my favourites. After beating the main game, I immediately bought the expansions and devoured those as well. It’s a mechanically simple game, but one that trusts the player to figure it all out. It is magnificent, and I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game. Reminded me of The Return of the Obra Dinn, where you also gradually dissect the events and use knowledge gained to help you progress. Soundtrack also neat. Rooted in reality enough not to feel like occurrences are randomly thrown at you from off-stage because of some highfalutin ghost hullabaloo, but rather figured out through logic and exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game looking for more Obra Dinn deduction puzzles and Golden Idol delivered. Calling this game "more Obra Dinn" is obviously reductive, but Golden Idol strongly holds up to its inspirations.The highlight for me was the straightforward clue hunting, murder mystery approach of the first half of the game. Even in the more simple form, you feel like a genius slowly piecing together solutions. The "fill in the blanks until you lock in the right answer" mechanic is one of my favs in any puzzle game. Golden Idol is also an aesthetic departure from Obra Dinn, with a cozy color palette and soft pixel, point-and-click style presentation. Later scenarios get a bit bogged down by dense rule sets and information dumps, with reliance on a more traditional pen-and-paper logic puzzle word problem approach. This ramping complexity might be enticing for others, but I found it pretty exhausting to even get started on some of the last scenarios. I had to rely on hints for some of these, but the in-game hint system has a great balance of pointing you in the right direction without spoiling the gratification of solving.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Someone once said the quickest way to kill something special is to compare it to something else, but if I may be permitted such a transgression I will invite the comparison with Obra DinnIn Obra Dinn, there were one or two moments where everything clicked, I snapped my fingers and went, "aha!" - it's an incredibly satisfying feeling.The Case of the Golden Idol is FILLED with "aha" moments. It's beautiful. It's a natural evolution/further refinement of the detective/puzzle/logic game Obra Dinn really started, and CotGI is a joy to play from start to finishIt's so clever, it's so intricate, it's so well made and well polished.It's a game I actively wanted to keep on playing, and there's not been a game like that for me for years.You know when people say "oh I want to forget that game so I could play it from scratch!" This is genuinely the first game I've had that experience with.The story isn't perfect, but it's far more that satisfactory and sufficient for a type of game like this.I must confess the artstyle was mildly offputting for me at first, but like, not an hour in I got used to it and since I've really grown to love it - there's little else like it and it's extremely charming in a odd wayIf you liked Obra Dinn, go play thisIf you've not played Obra Dinn, go try this
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely brilliant puzzle game with a very engaging story, I have played games like Tales of the Obra Dinn and others in the past, but I always found it hard to come back to as there were usually many things I would forget after having to stop playing to go about daily life, this game captures the same feeling but in chunks so that you could complete any given chapter in a few hours, you could come back to it and you would only have to catch up as far as you were in any given case, which allowed me, a college student, to fit it into my busy schedule. Definitely worth the money and it hooks you in really fast.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is a terrific puzzle game in the Return of the Obra Dinn mold. Like in Obra Dinn, you're presented with baffling scenes and need to determine what happened with a small number of details found in the scene. These clues take the form of words which you slot into a paragraphs to complete the (truly insane) story. Like Obra Dinn, every time you solve a puzzle, you discover something new about the story. But it's a little more of a detective story, as all of these tableaus are traditional murder mysteries, albeit strung into a surprisingly dramatic storyline. It's also incredibly varied, with at least one new mechanic added in every single puzzle. There are relatively few chapters, but the puzzles grow increasingly elaborate and challenging; the last one probably took me as long as the first three combined. The story here is very elaborate and goes some crazy places; it's filled with colourful characters and has some great twists. But it's short and has massive gaps in time; I would have liked some more details filled in, or at least a slightly longer denouement. The ending is a bit anticlimactic. But regardless, I thought this was delightful.

_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Very soft yes. The aesthetic is on point, and the story it's telling is interesting. I quibble with a lot of the mysteries. These aren't necessarily mysteries in a whodunnit sense as much as they are delving into the specifics of what happened, and that didn't really work for me. There's another case, meanwhile, where the evidence requires a massive leap, and I got stuck for a fair few minutes trying to piece together a lack of information.I dunno. It's good, but maybe temper your expectations a little bit.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the better story driven indie games I've played. The alchemical story of a mysterious golden idol weaves together across ~12 episodes where lust, envy, greed, and betrayal cause motion for power. It has conspiracy, new world order, deception and more. It's odd, but in intriguing ways which make clues fun to discover and piece together. Some of the later cases can be a bit difficult, but the game provides just enough detail - and precise detail at that - to make all assumptions decipherable. Definitely support this game if you want a different, more Sherlock Holmes investigative like approach, to story telling and puzzle solving. It's a lot of fun to stream to friends as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The case of the Golden Idol is another fine entry to a sub-genre I would categorize as 'scenario deduction'.  In comparison to other pioneers like Return of the Obra Dinn, Unheard, and CaseCracker, this game's story is a bit on the simpler side. However, it compensates for this with a captivating premise and a tightly-woven plot, masterfully conveyed through the design of the 14 cases.What this game does share with those other titles, is their cold, clinical presentation of the story, accentuated with a shocking and often chilling twist hidden underneath a vast amount of clues. This is, in my opinion, the defining trait of this genre, which I absolutely appreciate.

_childDocuments_.review: is one of the best puzzle games I've ever played. It's similar to games like , but quite a bit more player friendly when it comes to backtracking. You're essentially a detective, in each scene you're able to pick up evidence in the form of words; names, locations, actions, and more. These words are all added to a bank that you use to fill in the blanks and spell out exactly what happened in the scene in front of you. Solving puzzles in  is very rewarding, and it has a great difficulty curve as later scenes require you to pay increased attention to environmental details and recall information from previous scenes. _childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol is a renewal of the indie-game pact of excellence in narrative.- Lore: arguably the most intelligent part of the game. It is a parody of 18th century Britain and everything that revolves around it: imperialism, trading, parliamentary politics, aristocracy and ideology. The writers' take on this parody sets the stage and context in which the story occurs - in a fictional England, revolving around its colonies and overseas subjects. - Art: its pixellated nature was inspired by the good games of decades past. It invites you to relive this experience in a brand new environment, through unprecedented criminal cases.- Music: Kyle Misko immerses you and the characters at every stage of the game. For each chapter, there is a different score. If the lore is its most intelligent aspect, then the soundtrack is its greatest victory.- Gameplay: point-and-click detective game. Your job is to identify each clue present in every chapter and use this information to solve the mystery. You fill in the blanks of a few paragraphs of the story until the correct assessment of the event is completed. It may take some time and a thorough analysis to solve each chapter.- Story: the chapters of The Case of the Golden Idol are interconnected by past events. Along the way, you will meet new characters and encounter old ones. It begins with a return from an exploration trip overseas, which introduces the golden idol artifact and then follows its tracks till the end. As it is with every item that requires huge responsibility, each case follows characters that have their destiny linked to this valuable artifact. The DLCs will then explore the events that lead up to the main story.From chapter to chapter, history will make turns, from an oddity to a miracle; from secrecy to full-blown oppression. You will experience first-hand the effects of those wielding the power of the idol.89/100

_childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol is a fun and addictive murder mystery game heavily inspired by the Return of the Obra Dinn's formula, but topped with a more narrative-focused twist.The game is split into acts, which are further split into separate scenes/murder cases that you have to solve. Each case usually comprises finding all clues in the level, identifying all actors in the scene, and then reconstructing the events that transpired. This is where the Obra Dinn inspirations shine the brightest, as the latter is done by filling in the blanks of the half-written story. In contrast to Obra Dinn, where the set of available words is the same throughout the whole game, The Case of the Golden Idol makes you construct the set of possible words and names by finding clues and exploring the scene, which is a clever way of making the game feel more like a murder mystery and less than a gamified puzzle.All cases are part of an overarching story with the same characters, so they are not always analyzed in isolation only. The story is simplistic, but it lends itself well to this type of game and is interesting enough to make the player push forward. The ending will be a tad underwhelming to some, but I'd argue it's completely passable.The visual presentation is quite interesting. While I felt it was bit "rough" at first, I really started to appreciate it the more I looked at it. Hats off to the developers for embracing such a unique visual style and making it work so splendidly.All in all, The Case of the Golden Idol deserves my recommendation. Although a bit on the easier side, it had me hooked for the entire 7 hours it took me to complete it. A great concept, great visuals, and an interesting setting make this a really appealing package that would be a shame to miss, especially for the fans of murder mysteries.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding detective game with a surprisingly complex and intriguing narrative. Its fill-in-the-blanks mystery gameplay is highly reminiscent of that of Return of the Obra Dinn, but the exact structure and complexity of Golden Idol's challenges, and how those challenges are implemented into the overarching story, results in a unique and appealing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good and very challenging, and while I agree with the comparison to Return of the Obra Dinn that a lot of other reviews have made, I don't think it paints the correct picture. This game has a heavy focus on painting an exact picture of what happened and requires the same attention to detail that Obra Dinn had, but while Obra Dinn focused solely on who was killed and how, and the rest of ther story was just kind of for you to put together in your head, this game more so is painting you a story and the murders that are the vehicle for the story to progress really take a back seat in the second half. If you are anything like me at about the halfway point the game gets more and more convoluted and by the 2nd to last case you aren't really even investigating murders anymore. So don't go in thinking this is just purely a murder investigation story. Also heads up after case 4 the difficulty scales up Dramatically! I absolutely love the art style of this game and wow is the gameplay gripping. You will be staring at the same pictures going back and fourth for 20 minutes wondering what small little detail you are missing, to the point the later game investigations will have you pushing your grey cells to their absolute limits. On the other side of this I got such a wonderful feeling of reward for solving each case I verbally shouted after finishing a particularly difficult section (case 7 made me feel like I was trying to go through a hedge maze blindfolded lol I had no idea what was going on) overall if you enjoy puzzle games or point and click HO games this will prove an extraordinarily difficult but extremely fun challenge that I highly recommend. (8/10 I didnt care for the final 3 cases but overall really good.)

_childDocuments_.review: Comics are art, okay?And now as we established that, we can talk about The Case of the Golden Idol. On the surface it's a point-and-click adventure a-la Obra Dinn in 2D, where you have to deduct who's the killer by some spoken, unspoken, shown and not shown clues. And that you will get, too! I had a great time scratching my detective itch. But if it was , I'd probably was not as excited to recommend this game.While puzzles are not so hard and given time can be solved by any person with reading comprehension skills, where the game actually thrives is it's narrative. I must remind you, that we're talking about a game that basically consists of 12 static scenes scattered around several decades and several places in an imaginary kingdom. But much like comic books tell a story between frames, this game manages to tell a tale between those static point and click scenes. The story is incredibly solid and matches the detective gameplay perfectly. With a twist that is hinted very early on, but still not blatantly telegraphed, so you will be either satisfied with you deduction or pleasantly surprised with your a-ha moment closer to the last chapter.Game's unique artstyle helps to build on the intriguing and eerie plot A LOT. When I've looked at screenshots before buying the game, I was not so happy with it, but after I've spent a couple of hours inside game's universe, it all makes sense and I can't imagine the art done any other way. On the side note, I also don't like scary games and was a bit worried about the game's tone before buying. It felt horrory-dark. But if you have the same problems as me, fear not, the game lacks spooky sounds and sudden movements, so unpleasant pictures won't bother and scare you that much.The other great thing is the game's soundtrack. You're GOING TO sit on one scene for several dozens minutes, thinking about your case. It is crucial for music to not distract you from thinking while also being entertaining. And this game knows when to start a new beautiful song and when to shut up and succumb to the ambiance. Great game, with that low of a price certainly worth a try. Playtime of about 4 hours without DLC of pure detective joy and fun.
