_childDocuments_.review: Long lost in the ether following Westwood having literally misplaced the original source code, it seemed that Westwood's Blade Runner would forever be a forgotten gem. But, reverse engineering of the game had a different fate in mind, while sadly delivering results that would be met with less than warm appraisal. Yes, Nightdive's reverse engineer of the Westwood classic is deeply flawed; the visual presentation has suffered, audio cues are missing, the shooting gallery is inoperative, substantial chunks of dialogue are muted, and the shooting mechanic is extremely mixed when it comes to its responsiveness. But, it would be wrong to think of this re-issue as a failure. The game can be completed from start to finish, and the bare mechanics for the game to operate are in working order. But, for what was meant to be a labour of love, Nightdive have certainly under delivered. Thankfully, the game is also bundled with both the original CD-ROM version of the game with the fan restored content. So, while Nightdive's "enhancement" is something of a disappointment, the original game has been bundled with this release. Blade Runner, for newcomers, is a point and click adventure game based on the Ridley Scott cult classic. The protagonist, Ray McCoy, is the Deckard of the story, a Blade Runner. The game features a variety of settings and modes which allow for maximum replayability. For starters, players can opt as to the personality type of Ray McCoy, while also having the option to manually select dialogue options which they feel are relevant to their investigation. Each interaction, every kill (all in real time) creates the opportunity to access unique story paths, and endings. Blade Runner, in terms of its cyberpunk narrative branching and control of the story, is very much Deus Ex before Deus Ex but in a point and click adventure format (with some real time action sequences). As a piece of interactive story telling and gameplay, the game has aged gracefully in its simple but effective mechanics. Sadly, the visuals have dated poorly but this is to do with the fact that Blade Runner's rendering, upon release, was software based. Blade Runner was never developed with dedicated 3D accelerators for the time. But, what the game may lack in its visual clarify is more than made up for with superb voice acting (featuring Blade Runner alumni including Sean Young, James Hong, and the late Joe Turkel) and overall atmosphere with its iconic Vengelis soundtrack. Overall, Blade Runner is absolutely recommended for those who either do not already own a copy, or have a copy that they are unable to operate on a modern operating system. For those who already are able to play the original classic, the Enhanced Edition has nothing to offer, and is best avoided. Two scores:Original/Restored Version - 5 out of 5Nightdive's Enhanced edition - 1 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sad to say it's bad. Blade Runner was one of my favorite games growing up and it's the reason Blade Runner is my favorite film now. But this port is basically kind of a mess. It feels like it's an emulator wrapped around the game and up-scaled with a blurry filter. Whether that  makes the pre-rendered screens look better is a matter of preference, but there's a lot of problems otherwise.Basically the two good things are: The KIA interface looks better and you can scroll with the mouse wheel. The other thing is the subtitles (except they take up too much screen space, and I don't think all of them are correct, probably because the original script is long gone).The bad is everything else. From the first scene I was disappointed. Clicking on the ground did not make McCoy walk. Though that problem only existed in the first scene, other scenes seemed to be okay. The fact that the 3D models weren't enhanced in any way kind of makes you question the "enhancement" at all. They are still the same low-res voxel technology that always stood out like a sore thumb against the pre-rendered backgrounds. To it's credit, the game was playable from start to finish without any show-stopping bugs, but there were cosmetic bugs throughout. Some of the cosmetic bugs were in the original version of the game, but may have been less noticeable due to the lower resolution, but some are definitely new to this port, for example a lot of objects showing through the background etc. There were audio bugs as well, I encountered one where the love theme for Lucy started playing and wouldn't stop long after that interaction was over, and even saving the game, quitting to the desktop, and loading the game again still kept the incorrect music playing. You also can't change McCoy's behavior after you start the game (or at least I couldn't figure out how to, and even though I chose Erratic it seemed to be User Choice anyway.)I think just looking at the main menu is kind of an indicator that this is a dud. It's these ugly square boxes slapped on some weird concept art with a McCoy that doesn't even look like the guy from the original game.There is a version on  which is the ScummVM version. That version is much more faithful to the original and overall feels better.I supposes Nightdive realized this was sub-par which is why it's on 10 bucks in the US. I didn't even know about this version of the game until the day before it came out, so it doesn't seem like they were too keen on advertising it. Realistically if you're already a fan you might as well get this one just to see what it's about, just don't expect your mind to be blown.Realistically the only good remaster of this game would be to recreate it will all new graphics assets in a 3D Engine like Unreal or something. Probably the only thing to keep from the original game would be the audio and voices. But doing something like that would probably cost more than it would ever make back (if it was made with any kind of quality).

I can not understand in what plane of existence that Nightdive thought this was ok to release in this state, they go through all the trouble with getting the IP and hyping it up only to put out the worst hack job of a mess I have ever seen. Audio issues galore, broken sounds, broken music that likes to break up and sound like I am listening to the game on a 2001 nextel phone, you remember that stupid toothbrush they sold called tooth tunes, that played like a 1 bit version of popular annoying pop songs? Then you got  FRAME RATE STUT-STU-STU-STUTTERING on these supposed "remastered" cut-scenes that they hyped up like it was gonna bring about world peace and change the course of human history. I could drag my balls across broken glass at 60 FPS and tell you its amazing, but its still me dragging my balls across broken glass at 60 FPS. Nightdive put an AWFUL blurry mess of a filter over the cut-scenes with this god awful smoothing effect over it that I had to go check WebMD to make sure I wasn't experiencing symptoms of glaucoma or I wasn't drinking paint thinner again. This game looks WORSE than it ever did, its like that cute girl in high school you had a crush on, but never talked to so one night after downing copious amounts of cheap gas station malt liquor you decide to look her up on social media and now she is 35, with 5 kids and is doing head only above the shoulder face selfies trying to hide the fact she let herself go while her friends comment and tell her shes so pretty but we all really know she's hit the wall, but if you ask her friends they will tell you she has a shining personality. Also, someone please explain to me why I can't point and click for free movement in a POINT AND CLICK game. Was the devs freebasing ambien over at Nightdive studios? Were they drinking the left over cough syrup they had laying around? _childDocuments_.review: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition: A Classic Retro-Adventure Reborn in Neon LightsBlade Runner: Enhanced Edition offers a profound nostalgia trip back to the golden era of adventure games. Originally developed by the iconic Westwood Studios—creators of classics like "The Legend of Kyrandia" and "Lands of Lore"—this game is a testament to the studio's legacy in pioneering rich narrative experiences.As a Blade Runner, you are equipped with investigative skills and tools essential for navigating a world that feels alive. The game showcases revolutionary lighting and visual effects that breathe life into its environment, making it one of the most immersive settings ever crafted in video game history. While the Enhanced Edition aims to modernize the visual experience, it somewhat misses the mark. The enhancements often overshadow finer details, potentially detracting from the original aesthetic. However, playing the game without these enhancements brings back the cherished nostalgic vibe that many fans appreciate.The storyline is exceptional, rivaling the narrative depth and complexity of the original "Blade Runner" film. Players will find themselves weaving through storylines that intersect with familiar characters and iconic locations from the movie. The gameplay is challenging, with a dynamic narrative that shifts based on your decisions and actions, ensuring a unique experience for every player.Final Verdict:"Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition" is a remarkable journey back in time. Despite some flaws in the visual updates, the game’s core experience remains untouched, offering a blend of nostalgia and deep, adaptive gameplay that stands the test of time. After 31 years, it continues to be a captivating adventure worth exploring.Score: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: [Second Patch Edit - the purchase now comes bundled with a "classic edition", aka ScummVM version, and a toggle to use the old graphics on Enhanced Edition. While the recent patch did improve some stuff, overall there are still a bunch of rough visuals spots, so while I do consider this game worth playing, I encourage buying it for ScummVM's version, or use the classic toggle on Enhanced Edition. Original review below.]It’s too bad it doesn't live up.I get that the source code was lost, I get preserving this game by reversing it wasn't a small feat, I get the game is a bizarre technical nightmare on how it uses the voxels or whatever hell they are.I was still expecting better from NightDive. I sincerely cannot imagine anyone there looking at this and thinking it was acceptable.Let me be perfectly clear- Blade Runner is one of the best PC games you can play of the era, but just please do yourself a favor and go enjoy it on ScummVM. It's not just the small changes to movement, UI, interactables, ugly font and alike that bother me the most, it's how the visuals have been absolutely butchered due to changes in the way environmental elements (like fog) works, how the models are rendered and the hard contrast between the two- it's incredibly distracting and off-putting. It genuinely would have been better to keep everything rather compressed or compensate with similar visual tricks to mask at that point.The original Blade Runner and it's sequel are by far some of the most gorgeous visual feasts in cinema, a triumph of craftsmanship, atmosphere and design, the eternally resonant monologue by Roy in particular is easily one of the most beautiful scenes in any movie ever made- and this gem of a game lovingly captured all of that. Something this title lost in its enhancement to the point of insult.I don't know if something got messy in the end, and I hope to God almighty this can be saved or at least compensated a bit, because more people should play this game.And hell, if you don't care about any of this, fine, the game still works and is easily accessible- I am sadly incapable of recommending it if you even care a little about the actual experience.

_childDocuments_.review: "I'm walking through the desert when I see this developer lying on its back, belly baking in the hot sun -- kicking their legs, trying to turn themselves over, but they can't -- and I'm not helping....I kick some sand into their eyes for good measure."CAVEAT EMPTOR...If you are running an outdated GPU (such as ATI 5870 or 6970) the Enhanced Edition will not function properly -- even though you are within minimum specs.This is due to an error in "Shader Model 4" that Nightdive Studios is unwilling/unable to fix.(  )OTHERWISE...They have patched this title since its very poor launch -- and both the Enhanced & Standard Editions will work for everyone(else).  You can buy this title with confidence!  You take the role of Ray McCoy -- Blade Runner rookie.Uncover the identities of a rogue band of Replicants, in a narrative that takes place alongside that of the original film from 1982.  Several actors reprise their roles, here, and while gameplay can get repetitive due to limited scene structure, your choices matters and will lead to a variety of outcomes...This newly 'Enhance Edition' offers Steam Achievements, a modern overlay, and a smoothed-out/upscaled GFX renderer that reduces the original art to some smudging -- but 'Classic Mode' for the original graphics experience is thankfully just a keystroke ('Q') away.Controls are of a simple mouseclick/pixel-hunting variety-- so your off-hand is free to enjoy a tumbler of whiskey, or two, by saxophone.There is also a "Classic Edition' included with the Steam purchase, which is a basic ScummVM port.Both editions include an option to experience extra content, but bugs may be introduced that way.This is a great game, and well-worth your money & time!. . .It isn't called murder -- it's called retirement.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the "enhanced" option. This is an old-school point-n-click adventure. The art, voices, music, and story are very good. But, the graphics are extremely dated. The "enhancement" is simply a blur filter which removes detail from scenes. I do prefer it blurred since it cleans up rough pixelation, but there are times when the blur effect will make a cityscape look like a cave (you can toggle the effect on/off at any time). I would never have completed the game without a walk-thru. There is no quest journal or guide in the game. I ran around aimlessly until it triggered some progress. There are many actors from the 1982 Blade Runner movie and the scenes stay very true to the source. I generally can't recommend this, but hardcore Blade Runner fans will appreciate it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: The enhanced edition gets a lot of hate but I didn't have any of the problems that people have reported. My understanding is that the bugs were fixed. This also includes the two other versions that you can play, but only the Enhanced Version allows you to obtain achievements. Over all this is a fun experience and if you're a fan of Blade Runner then you'll like the story. There are multiple endings and every play through allows for a new experience.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: This review was originally negative but the comments were really helpful, I gave the game another try and starting to understand how this style of game works. It's a very well made game. Thank you to everyone who left a comment. Original review:Believe it or not, , not the remaster. I'm playing the original ScummVM version that got added after the remaster turned out so awful. (btw, thank you to whoever added subtitles to the original version.)I like Blade Runner, I like detective games, I've played point-and-click detective games before, but I just can't get into this one. The game gives you ZERO direction on what to do, where to go, what to pick up, if you missed something, what order to do things in, I looked up several walkthroughs and they all say to do different things, I don't get it. No hints, nothing. I'm not saying the game needs to spell it out for me, but some of this evidence is so minute and easy to miss that I flat out missed it and didn't know it was there. Like the shell casings on the floor, I never would've thought to check there or if there was a gun in the first place (there wasn't one in the opening cutscene). The walkthroughs said there was also a candy bar, I couldn't find it anywhere. And the photo enhancers, how the hell would I have known the girl had an ankle bracelet? I can't read the game's mind! At least when looking around environments for clues, the cursor turns green when hovering over something you can click on. And then I got flat-out stuck on the part where you confront the sushi chef and chase him, just leads me to a locked door and dead end. The walkthroughs say he's supposed to jump down from the ceiling and attack me, but nothing. Just a locked door. I'm NOT saying the game is bad, especially considering that it's considered a great game and cult classic. It got (poorly) remastered for a reason, after all. The game looks great for its time with its Resident Evil-style pre-rendered environments, and absolutely nails the overall Blade Runner vibe, right down to the slow pacing. I think it's cool that they even brought back the "artificial animals" subplot from the original novel (Philip K ♥♥♥♥'s , which was the basis for Blade Runner). I just shouldn't feel frustrated playing this game. I was looking forward to it, only to end up putting it down almost immediately. Maybe I'll come back to it, most likely not. Maybe point-and-click games just aren't my thing, I dunno. TL;DR game does a piss-poor job of telling you where to go, what to do, if you missed any clues, etc. I was completely lost and ended up getting stuck with no idea how to fix it.

_childDocuments_.review: I own both the GoG and this version.  I ran both at 720x480 (side by side) and here's my quick analysis.Visuals: GoG > Steam (only slightly and even at 5120x1440)Sound: GoG = SteamKIA menu = GoG < Steam (steam has a high res menu)Movement = GoG = Steam (I don't know what people are talking about not being able to walk freely.  I can walk to the same places on the GoG version)Compatibility: GoG < Steam (My GoG version doesn't close properly most times and requires me to end GoG.  I have no such issues with the Steam version.  Plus it works with the Steam deck.Notes:Steam desk... for mouse clicks you have to configure a mouse button since the touchscreen is not calibrated.Personally, I don't think there's anything wrong with this version.  The graphical different is so minor because of how dated they look anyway.  Anyway, I loved the game back in the 90's and will enjoy it again.  And, I can even play it on the go.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I have all versions, both my son And I own the original disc based game.This is my most favorite PC game in all PC gaming history, the game is a masterpiece from start to finish, an amazing recreation of the film world and is so alive with all the sounds and music that feels so apart of it. and I applaud Nightdive for it's Labor of love on this, it was no easy task considering the source material  is MIA in a Westwood studio move years ago and now we get a version that can play on modern PC hardware as well as video game consoles giving Blade runner the extra life that the replicants so desperately sought.The nasty neg reviews on this enhanced edition are not warranted and reactions are quite frankly childish IMO.The devs have plans to patch the new enhanced edition and have already  gave us the original as well as the extra content edition. _childDocuments_.review: Read a detailed review here: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition has managed to ruin the unique aesthetic and feel of the original largely thanks to an inaccurate AI-upscaling method and some questionable design choices. To be honest, the only ‘upgrade’ in the remaster over the original is the addition of cutscenes and controller support. The decision to de-list the original from GOG was also a crappy move. But, as an apology, Nightdive is giving away the original, titled Blade Runner Classic when you purchase the Enhanced Edition on Steam. But, if the only selling point of your remaster is the ability to play the unaltered version, then what’s the point of remastering it in the first place? That being said, Nightdive has a good record of patching their remasters until they’re in an acceptable state (reference: Blood: Fresh Supply). If you’re desperately itching to revisit the classic, you can buy it for a reasonable $9.99 and play the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: So, first thing's first. It pays to remember that the original game honestly hasn't aged well.The writing is *abysmal* – a wellspring of second-hand embarrassment that just doesn't let up, teetering between critically failed attempts at appearing cool and successful attempts at emulating the Ford narration track of the film's original theatrical cut. That's… not a good look.The state-of-the-art-of-1997 interactive movie shell is juddery and janky and compressed all to hell, badly showing its age. Even the intro text crawl can't move in a smooth pace! Whenever pure primary colours appear in the FMV, it's soft and flickery with artifacting. Everybody in my room burst laughing and had to leave upon seeing the antagonist stride on the screen, looking like The Gap incarnate, in the opening scene.That all said, the restauration work seems merely OK. It's glitchier than the original and the bright, sharp UI clashes completely with the muddy CGI art direction. Nightdive also regrettably omitted subtitling the FMV cutscenes for some reason, a disservice since the audio is compressed, noise filtered and compressed again and the spoken lines are often…  nolaned in delivery.The best way to think of the original game is that it's a CGI kusoge along the lines of Kenji Eno's WARP output except now there's a license. A bad piece of fanfic, dripping second-hand embarrassment and nostalgic music cues (ersatz Vangelis). And the minefield puppy. Not sure what's up with this restauration, though, because it feels… off. Think I might refund a game for once.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Don’t play the Enhanced Edition. Play through the original version with a ScummVM CRT shader such as crt-mattias or crt-lottes-fast to relive the glory days. Even in 2024, Blade Runner is still an exceptional point-and-click adventure that is oozing with awesome sci-fi atmosphere. A must play for every Blade Runner and cyberpunk fan.Edit: playing the original version via Steam doesn’t count your hours played and there are no achievements. You’ll have to play it for the sheer enjoyment of it, just like the good ol’ days!

_childDocuments_.review: First time playing. Playing the classic w/ restored content. Briefly tried the enhanced edition and the "updated" graphics were like plastic and destroyed so much character and detail. You can toggle it, but I preferred to use the cut content for a complete experience. It comes with an older ScummVM, but you can obviously use a newer one and point it at the data files if you want.Considering this game was made in the mid-90's, it's amazing how much of an achievement it must have been at the time. It's a point and click adventure game that really makes you feel like a detective, and the chase/shooting sequences help make it feel deadly and need to stay on your toes.Basically, if you are looking for a game that's like Blade Runner, this is obviously the one to get as they absolutely nailed it.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the enhanced edition and everything worked (contrary to some other reviews). It's a lovely game with lots of attention to detail. I recommend you save the game every 5min towards the end, because there are some unexpected situations where you may suddenly die. Recommend playing this for the story, and also the nice visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: A true masterpiece of the point and click genre. The player is a colleague of Rick Deckard humorously named Ray McCoy. McCoy is the protagonist of the sort of sequel to the Blade Runner movie. Actors from the movie appear in the same roles, most notably Sean Young as Rachael. The story is pretty good and follows the lore of the movie accurately. The gameplay is fun if not slightly frustrating due to there being a fair amount of guess work having to be done by the player to progress proceedings. I completed the game relatively easily on the hardest difficulty, and as a huge fan of the movie I felt satisfied.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Play the original. It's an option. The re-make, or re-master, or whatever was simply a bump up of original content to 60 FPS, a blur filter that covers up all the original detail, and a glitch'y marriage between original and "updated" features. They kept the original textures for the physical items you find, but when they pop up while using the "enhanced edition" they don't flow and rotate around the screen. They disappear in an instant. Not a fan of this one. But, at least, they can make money off of the original. Thank god they kept that option.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: While the game's slow pace and 'outdated' visuals and design may put off newcomers, Blade Runner proves to be an excellent point and click adventure with a truly branching narrative that kept me on my toes throughout. There are so many choices you won't even realize you're making that change the outcome, and on top of that, the game has a very innovative series of randomized elements that ensure no two playthroughs will be the same.If you enjoy a good sci-fi mystery that honors the narrative and style of the original film, you can't do much better than this. I would love to see a full remake one day that would allow this unique experience to reach more players.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game. The graphics and artistic vision hold up despite being a game made for Windows 95. The game mechanics leave much to be desired however. Be expected to run around the same district for 20 minutes only to then think there's nothing else to do there only to then find out there's a person that only happens to appear randomly that you need to talk to. I still highly recommend this game but don't jump into this game expecting things to be quick and straightforward.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Only a first impression: I don't know if the game had have the original spoken german language, but now it has and as soon as i was in the game, i got that pleasant feeling of playing a really good adventure again. The dialogues are great with a lot of humor and the well-known German speakers of the good old 1980s and 90s of the last century seems also to be remastered and bring back pleasant memories. The game controls with mouse + keyboard work flawless and the reworked visuals look a lot nicer in my opinion. The game progress can be saved by manual saving at any time from the game menu. Fantastic work....Thank you, Nightdive Studios for bringing us back these amazing title, even better than once.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: There are no "mixed" feelings about this game - it's a must have. I think recently the new updates allowed for a lot of flexibility, you can play the original Blade Runner in its original form too, so there is no need to dislike the remastered version anymore. In any case the game is getting updates so if you're on the fence then don't worry.The game is a visual masterpiece. There are multiple endings and slightly different ways to play the game. I remember when I first played this, I was 6 years old and we went to a computer store. The game had several CDs it cost about $100. Back then computers were very expensive and this was a visual masterpiece. The graphics have dated over time, but not to any point where it deters from the feeling or atmosphere. The Blade Runner universe is almost perfectly captured in this game, the art and aesthetic, the story, the lonely nature, the persistent rain - just beautiful. Westwood studios was the original creator of this title, the same company that did Command and Conquer, back then they released incredible titles, this is one of them.Overall, a must buy for any Point Click Adventure enthusiast or a person who wants a really good Blade Runner story.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

It was kicking.- Characters. Even though they portray existing characters from Blade Runner (which happens simultaneously) and other popular media (Matilda from "Leon").- Locations, the city and the atmosphere. Similar is made in The Longest Journey.- Music. Perfect re-imagining of Vangelis's tracks. Also, nice Klepacki styled samples and tracks.Cons.:- The remake is quite poor - it could have added a lot to the interface of the clues. Also, to the graphics. Instead - more graphical issues.- Glitches.

Love Blade runner, i wonder if it will retain its unique perfection, in a future it helped to weave. Thank you for this!!
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good. I liked the first half more than the second. I thought it was fun  trying to sniff out the reps, trying to solve a murder. 2nd half was more like an action game so to speak. Never played the original, but I completed it without trouble. I just wish there was a few more cases before we got to the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: With the recently released update the game is now running properly, at least in the first few scenes, I haven't had the time to check out the rest of the game yet. But I have to admit I'm not a fan of the 'enhanced' graphics. Yes, they are smoother, but they have also lost a lot of detail. Luckily you can switch to the original graphics by pressing Q, which looks better in my opinion. And if you don't like the new GUI of the enhanced version you can also install the original version and run it using SCUMMVM. So there is currently no reason not to pick up this version. The only question is whether to install and play the enhanced version or the original version.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Although this game is technically a movie tie-in, it's absolutely , a  in its own right.Blade runner makes the modern "cinematic experience" type game look silly, and I can't help but feel a bit sad, knowing that video games will never be this good  again.If you haven't played this gem yet, I can't recommend it enough. For the time being it seems the classic edition is still the best way to experience this game. The enhanced edition has some problems, and the menu and interface are quite bare-bones. It doesn't fit the game.

name: Forspoken
detailed_description: In Tanta We Trust After bringing peace to Athia, Frey’s journey continues as she searches for a way to permanently rid the land from the effects of the Break. Amid her search, she follows a mysterious voice that leads her into the past. When she emerges, Frey finds herself surrounded by chaos and destruction. Injured and draped in blood-soaked clothing, she discovers a grim truth about her fate. The recently thriving Athia is at war, but why and with whom? Accompanied by Tanta Cinta, and a new set of magic, Frey must uncover the answers and save Athia once more – and attempt to save herself. Digital Deluxe Edition The Digital Deluxe Edition on PC includes: Forspoken PC Full Game Download Forspoken Mini Artbook (Digital Download) Forspoken Mini Soundtrack (Digital Download) Prequel Story DLC ‘Forspoken: In Tanta We Trust’ (Summer 2023) Prequel Story DLC Early Access Ultra Settings OS Version: Windows® 10 64-bit (After November 2019 Update) or Windows® 11 64-bit Processor: AMD Ryzen™5 5800X (3.8 GHz or better) / Intel® Core™ i7-12700 Memory: 32GB Graphics: AMD Radeon™ RX 6800 XT 16GB / NVIDIA® GeForce® RTX 4080 16 GB VRAM DirectX Version: 12 Disk Space: NVMe SSD 150GB or more Additional Notes: 2160p 60fps About the Game Mysteriously transported from New York City, Frey Holland finds herself trapped in the breathtaking land of Athia. A magical, sentient bracelet is inexplicably wrapped around her arm, and Frey discovers the ability to cast powerful spells and use magic to traverse the sprawling landscapes of Athia. Frey nicknames her new golden companion “Cuff” and sets off to find a way home. Frey soon learns this beautiful land once flourished under the reign of benevolent matriarchs, called Tantas, until a devastating blight relentlessly corrupted everything it touched. The Break  transformed animals into beasts, men into monsters, and rich landscapes into four dangerous realms. At the center of their shattered domains, the Tantas now rule as maddened and evil sorceresses. Unaffected by the Break and desperate for answers, Frey reluctantly agrees to help the last remaining citizens of Athia who see her as their only hope. Frey’s journey through this strange and treacherous land will take her deep into the heart of corruption where she must battle monstrous  creatures, confront the powerful Tantas, and uncover secrets that awaken something much more from within. KEY FEATURES: The Odyssey of a Reluctant Hero Lead Frey on an unforgettable journey in her search for a way home after being mysteriously transported to a breathtaking, fantastical land. Unravel the mysteries of Athia as Frey travels through the calamitous Break and discovers how to wield an immense power. A Beautiful and Cruel Open-World - Explore the sprawling realms of Athia, a striking land of remarkable vistas and otherworldly creatures brought to life through stunning graphics and cutting-edge technology. Venture deep into corrupted territories where a mysterious darkness defiles everything it touches. Customizable Arsenal of Spells - Take on twisted monsters in magical combat with a wide range of powerful abilities catering to a variety of playstyles – from fast-paced and exhilarating to strategic and methodical. Intuitive, Magic-Enhanced Parkour - Scale walls, vault across canyons, leap from dizzying heights, and dash through vast landscapes. Frey's unique abilities allow her to fluidly traverse the open world with ease.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to all Robocop fans. It has some issues, of course - but nothing that undermines the experience. It is pure nostalgia. Robocop is my favorite movie of all time, and being able to play a game that was really made by people that, if not fans themselves, researched about the history of the character and created a game that really makes the player feel like he's in Alex Murphy's shoes (or should I say armour?). So many cutscenes and small details - such as the exact place where he was killed being showed to us, even with the chalk draw made by the police, makes me recommend this game to anyone who is a Robocop fan.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of decent things about this game, but it has too many problems. Ignoring those, it's not a terribly ambitious game, but achieves what I assume to be the goal of being a decently fun, brainless shooter that is pretty faithful to the first movie. But the game suffers from bugs and poor optimization. I've lost progress multiple times due to bugs. And the framerate tanks on some sections to what I'd estimate to be sub-20 FPS on an NVIDIA 3090 and an AMD 5900. I might forgive this if it were less frequent and the game were a visual masterpiece, but the graphics feel like they're about 10 years old and the slowdowns are persistent throughout certain areas of the game. If they fix these issues, it might be worth it on sale or once the price drops. As it stands now, I'd stay away regardless of the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Paul Verhoeven’s RoboCop is one of the quintessential action movies of the 1980s. It pushed the envelope with over-the-top violence, killer one-liners, and fantastic special effects, mixed with a biting anti-corporate social commentary under the surface that resonated with audiences. As for me, original Robocop (1987) is one of my favorite childhood films. Is a perfect cyberpunk dystopia. Mega-corporations with divisions affecting nearly every level of consumer need, society, and government want to control everything around them. One such mega-corporation, based on the storyline of the movie, is Omni Consumer Products (OCP) are the main antagonists of the RoboCop franchise. OCP  wants is to overthrow the current government in Detroit, which they consider to be corrupt, and assume total control over the city. After this, they plan to demolish the entire city so as to construct Delta City in it's place, their «ideal city» with fully privatized services; in fact, OCP would control every single aspect of the city. A modernist future where everything is glass-towers, rounded and smooth designs. A future that has no soul and is completely sterile, coming closer and closer...The appeal to nostalgia is strong, and that can have a significant impact on how much mileage you get out of this. As a pure shooter, Rogue City isn’t overly ambitious, but it’s a lot of fun to play even if you don’t know anything about the series. However, if you grew up with RoboCop or recently watched the movies then it is chock-full of references and nods that add a lot to the experience. I found myself laughing out loud the first time I saw someone driving a 6000 SUX or I found «Nukem» Board Game, you can't play «Nukem», but it's still an excellent detail that proves the developers are fans of the series. - "Get Them Before They Get You.". Probably exploding the groin of a baddie is a silly, but it’s so much more entertaining if you know that it’s pulled directly from the film. RoboCop: Rogue City is a pitch-perfect throwback to the action movies of the ‘80s. It’s over-the-top violence with charm, largely well put together but rough on the edges. Most importantly, it's a fun way to spend time in a beloved fictional universe that doesn’t overstay its welcome. Blasting at goons as an unstoppable walking machine remains as extremely entertaining as it seemed on the big screen, thanks in part to an impressive commitment to capturing the look and feel of the original film. Mixing in elements like routine police work and side quests does a great job changing the pace, too. Even if it’s not the best example of visual fidelity, and prone to some bugs along the way, that love of RoboCop shines through. I respect the developers, and I respect their decisions for the most part. This is a game made by people with the same type of love I have for RoboCop. I felt that. I felt it throughout the whole game.If you have seen the films, Rogue City is a triumphant return to the streets of Old Detroit. Murphy’s partnerships, weapons, voice, soundtrack and action combat will pull players back into the gritty world of OCP’s 2024 Detroit city. The gore, visuals and cast all strike the right chords and while objectives mostly follow similar lines, the action is what really makes it pop.

_childDocuments_.review: After creating the surprisingly good Terminator Resistance, Teyon returns by making an excellent Robocop game. Rogue City takes place between the second and third film and does a great job blending the satirical dark humor of the first movie with the corny camp of the second. Alex Murphy is still trying to reconcile if he is man or machine while OCP is once again causing mayhem across the city to try and make a quick buck out of it. The game does a great job recreating the dystopian Detroit portrayed in the movies and the police precinct looks exactly the way it does in the film. As with Terminator Resistance, Rogue City is a AA experience and looks like a remaster of a game that came out 10 years ago. Peter Weller comes back to voice act Robocop and really helps to sell the cheesy robotic dialogue that enhances the experience. The gameplay is pretty decent, Robocop is a walking tank so there is little to no cover to take advantage of, just the slow walk towards gangs of enemies as you tear them to pieces, the actual combat never wore out its welcome in the 15 hours it took me to complete it. The game has RPG mechanics that like with Terminator Resistance are kind of mediocre but do not hamper the experience. There is a mechanic in the game where you can use hardware pickups to upgrade Robocops ability to use his iconic Auto 9 handgun, it is a bizarre upgrade system that is hard to explain and pretty clunky, but with enough tinkering you become overpowered. By the end of the game my Auto 9 was full auto, had no recoil, and had unlimited ammo with no need to reload. I was able to fire so fast that my screen would tear occasionally when too much was going on on screen. There are a few set pieces in the game but mainly you are dropped into a hub spot in down town Detroit during various ours of the day while you do various quests and sidequests. It is kind of repetitive going through the same area several times but since you can actively talk with the citizens of the city you can see how Robocops action do effect the area overtime. There are various moments where Robocop has bouts of PTSD that cause the gameplay to glitch intentionally. While thematically it works and makes sense, from a gameplay perspective it can get annoying and was a slog to get through. TLDR, Robocop is a fantastic continuation of the Robocop series and a great sequel to the second film. It is really cool to see a developer have such a huge passion for a property and make a well thought out game like this on a small budget that honors the source material and not cost the consumer $70. I will be excited to see what other potential 80s or 90s property Teyon might tackle next, be it Judge Dredd, They Live, or even something out of left field like Bucakroo Banzai since they already convinced Peter Weller to work on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A Gloriously Violent Love Letter to the Robocop FilmsRobocop Rogue City is a true masterpiece and a love letter to the classic Robocop films that fans of the series are sure to adore. This game is by far one of the best film to game adaptions, standing tall alongside other greats such as Terminator Resistance and Alien Colonial Marines.As someone who grew up watching the Robocop films and other ultra-violent action films of the 80s, I was immediately drawn into the world of Robocop Rogue City. From the sound of my mechanical footsteps to carrying Robocop's iconic Modified M23R handgun, the game makes you feel like the cybernetic law enforcement officer himself, and it's nothing short of badass.One aspect of the game that truly stands out is its gloriously bloody and gory presentation. The level of violence is reminiscent of the films and adds an extra layer of intensity to the gameplay. The way enemies are displayed and dispatched had me feeling strong Fallout vibes, and I mean this in the best way possible.The leveling system in Robocop Rogue City adds an engaging role-playing game (RPG) element to the experience. This, combined with the visceral combat and a richly detailed world, makes for an incredibly immersive and enjoyable game.Overall, Robocop Rogue City is a masterpiece that pays homage to the classic films while still managing to stand on its own as a fantastic gaming experience. Whether you're a longtime fan of the series or just a fan of action-packed games, this title is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is an amazing shooter. The gunplay feels nice, the mechanics are great, and the game uses the environment well. Even though the animations- especially for the weapons that aren't your primary weapon- are very lacking, it's impossible to look over how well the game functions overall. The worst aspect of RoboCop isn't the game mechanics, but the character models and voice acting. Robocop himself feels like his usual self, clunky and awkward, which is good. The other character models however are as awkward as Robocop. If they do move, it's stiff, and weird to look at. The characters are restrained to a 2x2 foot area, and every time the models even try to so much as walk in a direction, the game fades to black, and fades back in with the models in the right place with no real time passage. The voice acting is fairly bad, and you can almost imagine the script they're reading off of. Cutscenes would be an absolute drag if it weren't for the story.I haven't played through the entire game, but so far, it's good, but not $50. Wait for a sale unless you have extra cash.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I won't lie: This game has a fair amount of jank, its satire never reaches the heights of its cinematic predecessor and it has production values that makes you ask "Was this financed with change found between couch cushions?". Also, its pacing borders on "catastro♥♥♥♥".But its strengths are there and their impact is huge. Like Terminator: Resistance (made by the same studio), it's clearly a love letter to its franchise, made by fans who understood the assignment and filled its playtime (about 15 hours) with fun, gory gunplay, some good laughs and a heap of fanservice. Full price may be a bit much for people who are not gigantic RoboCop-Fans, but for those who are or are willing to wait for a sale, this is a great little game. _childDocuments_.review: Part immersive sim, part FPS, all cop. An extremely fun and satisfying romp through the world of Robocop. Combat strikes a good balance between making you feel slow and powerful while not feeling overly clunky or frustrating. Upgrade system lets you tweak Robocop's main handgun to suit each encounter and while the skill system isn't super in-depth, I felt it had just the right amount of impact on the gameplay to not feel too oppressive. Graphics aren't the most top of the line, but the environmental destructibility is top notch and not only serves to make the combat more intense and fun, but also gives you tactical options like throwing explosive canisters and TVs at enemies, or even just flat out grabbing and throwing them out of windows. Story is a bit clumsy and oddly paced at times, but it's overall fun, and hearing Peter Weller as Robocop is the cherry on top. The game also features some investigative sections to split up the combat encounters, and while some of these can drag on a bit long at times, they are on the whole really fun and do a great job at fleshing out the Robocop world more. What really sells the game for me though is the dedication the devs showed in reproducing the world from the movie. Rather than trying to "modernize" the setting to reflect the modern day, the game sticks to its "near future according to the 1980s" presentation, where a police station with a spacious computer server room and an entire maintenance bay for its cyborg cop still has its officers using typewriters and reviewing security footage shot on grainy VHS tapes. And aside from a few clunky lines, the references to the films are generally used to good effect to maintain continuity.So overall, while the game can be a bit rough and clunky at times, the combat is overall visceral and satisfying and the presentation is filled to the brim with references to the movies and fun environments to shoot apart. Well worth it for fans of Robocop or anyone looking for a fun single player FPS campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: A thoroughly enjoyable mix of modern FPS elements with character progression and fun police-procedural side missions. The dev team has an understanding of the license -- violent, but satirical -- and the game delivers tons of fan service with Easter eggs and callbacks a plenty. It's great to hear Peter Weller back in the role, and the sci-fi story and various side plots make sense in that action-game-based-on-an-action-movie way. It's a skillful, respectful use of the license and a heck of a lot of fun throughout.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Robocop game, it's nearly PERFECT.  Yes, because it's THE Robocop.  He doesn't sprint with speed of sound or shoot flashy magics.  He's just a sturdy clunky robot with big guns, and yeah it just works so well in that regard.  If you're looking for a Robocop game, there is none better.But if you're looking for something else this might not be for you.  It's just mediocre by the industry standard.  The graphics are leaning towards great, with some weird wonky animations here and there.  Other things are pretty standard, very first-person shooter basics, with some little tricks to get us engaged in combat.  Btw, I get dizzy at times playing this game.  Not sure if it's just me or there's something with how the game's visuals work.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the original RoboCop movie and first person shooters you'll definitely like this game! Teyon have done a fantastic job of bringing the world of the first two movies into video game form. It's obvious that a lot of love for the source material was poured into the making of this game, with many of the places and people from the movies carried over with great care. The game play is a blend of shooting and world building side quests. The combat mechanics do a great job of selling the fantasy of being RoboCop and, along with skill progression in the game, make every fire fight a treat. The exploration and narrative side quests, while good for rounding out Robo as a character, did create to big a gap in the action sometimes. I do appreciate that the game isn't all shooting but I think the pacing between shooting and exposition could have done with the bit of adjustment. That really is the only very minor grip I have against what is otherwise a fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been quite a few years since I found it difficult to stop thinking about a game but Robocop changed that. while I experience trouble with FPS and the occasional crash (infuriatingly) during important cut-scenes, the overall experience was phenomenal. It's the Robocop sequel we all hoped for and finally have.

_childDocuments_.review: What seems to be a direct sequel to the 1990 film Robocop 2, Rogue City drops you into the titanium shoes of the half man, half machine, Robocop. This review is written, taking into account that the game comes from a relatively small developer and no doubt, by other games standard, a small budget.The game does an excellent job of capturing the feel of the movies, it would seem the developers have not only watched the movies but also respect them (quite rare for todays licensed materials). Enough faces from the film pop up to make it feel familiar and there are locations that im not sure how accurate they are, but you know where you are straight away. I was half expecting a button bashing shooter with little else, what you actually get is a game that feels a mix between alien isolation and la noire, whith some shooting in between.Yes there are some issues, some technical which can be patched out, but also design. Theres quite a few sections of backtracking, with little to do. The voice acting is iffy in places, although mostly on point and ive had 2, maybe 3 crashes. I think the shooting sections could be quite cool in 3rd person as well.8/10 easily, i hope they do a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic gameplay and story that is true to the original movies. Feeling like a walking tank with the various skills you unlock enabling you to serve the public trust, protect the innocent and uphold the law!Voice acting is great though facial animations are rather stiff.Story wise it felt like something that I would consider on par with the first movie which I believe is fantasticLevel design is great with the police station looking exactly like it does in the movies, though keep in mind you are a big cyborg who isn't known for his speed with certain areas being fairly large.Game length is roughly 10-16 hours depending on how thorough you are in exploration (which I recommend as it directly ties to how much EXP you can get)Actions have consequences and you can either lean more into RoboCop than Alex Murphy or choose to be both part man part machine as your actions affect the world around you, which is more important to you upholding the law or serving the public trust?Customisation and skills are key to how you will play the game as there is a level cap and currently no new game+ (which I am looking forward to) As I chose to be a fast moving tank with a heart of gold able to deflect bullets with my own body, dash into groups of enemies and throw them into lower atmosphere.Highly recommend Solid 9/10 unfortunately some bugs occurred such as weapons disappearing mid boss fight, getting stuck in objects when talking to npcs at awkward angles, with the only fix being to restart from a checkpoint. Hope anyone who decides to purchase enjoys their time with this fantastic game!

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: This is a frantic high action first person shooter with some mild exploration and RPG elements mixed in. The violence is humorously extreme. Unlike most modern first person shooters, you feel like a walking tank rather than a super fast and jumpy maniac. There are semi-open hubs and levels, but it is not truly open world in that sense. I genuinely enjoyed every moment.Graphics and Sound: This game features current gen (as of the beginning of 2024) graphics and sound design. It looks extremely nice and fits the source material well. Sound is generally solid, but the voice acting stands out as particularly good.Production and Feel: The developers obviously paid attention to the source material. They did an excellent job of making you feel like Robocop in the 1980's future. It is surprisingly well done.Stability: At the time of this writing, the game has some stability and crashing issues for many players. But to be fair, the developers are still patching it and updating. Still, I wish it launched in a better state.Overall Opinion: This game is excellent and feels like a love letter to the franchise that it's based on. The action is eye-poppingly violent and there are cool down periods of light exploration and dialog. The game would be nearly perfect if it was a little more stable. Rating: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Great homage to the 1987 cult classic film.  Fans of that will like this a lot.  They even got the original actor (Peter Weller) to do RoboCop's voice, which I really appreciated.  As far as game-play goes:  solid FPS shooting mechanics, makes you really feel like a death dealing machine.  Great graphics, good sound, light RPG elements for upgrading your skills and some dialogue options which lead to different endings.  Not too difficult, as I finished it on Hard in 16h and never died (from gunshots).  My only gripe is that the pacing of the story sometimes feels disjointed, but other than that, a good game. 8/10 (Might be slightly skewed as I was a huge fan of the original movie).
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Rogue city with very low expectations. Movie based videogames are notoriously bad. And yes, it isn't a AAA game, it has rough edges and early PS4 graphics, but oh boy is it a great game. If you haven't watched the original robocop trilogy lately, the first one was great, the second one, in spite of (or because of) Frank Miller's scrip was barely watchable, and the less is said about part 3 and the soulless remake the better. (Can't comment on the TV show and animated series, haven't watched them yet.) Rogue city is the real sequel to Robocop part 1 and 2 where I'm concerned. You can tell that everyone involved loves the source material and did everything their tight budget allowed to make this the best possible Robocop game. (ok, that's not saying much, given the competition) Heck, Peter Weller voices robo, and a few other original cast members also reprise their roles. They nailed the feel and humor of the originals. Stepping into Murphys clunky shoes feels great, right away you get the "Walking Tank" feeling. Sure robocop isn't very agile or fast, but he's a bullet sponge that can tear through street scum like wet toilet paper. Aside from racking up a body count, you also do regular police work, like passing out parking tickets, responding to calls, and even saving a cat or two. (Sounds dull, but leads to some hilarious and even heartwarming scenes). Rogue city is just a blast to play. To get the full unstoppable one-cyborg-army feel, start new game plus and max out your gun's 6.2 pcb. You'll make Ed-209 looks like a roomba in comparison. Even with new game + I rarely like a game enough to play it again, but I just started my third playthrough, that ought to tell you something. In short, If you like robocop, and don't need to have the newest ray traced polish in a good game, you need to play Robocop: Rogue city.Just be sure to get it on sale, instead of the 55 Dollars it normally costs.Oh, also if you are an achievement hound, they are very doable.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game very much.Voice actors are great!The sound level of voices changes a lot, some are quite low (Antonowsky) some are very loud (Becker) which is a bit annoying.Sounds are very good in my opinion. There was nothing that sounded wrong, cheap or misplaced.Graphics are great. Only some elements are only ok, which is some smoke, dust and mist look a bit cheap when they are moving around. Also, sometimes objects like cars or NPCs missing shadows underneath and stand out because of that.But overall there is a lot love to details.And, I have to mention this, I adore the gore...really.And these two elements, what you see and what you hear, generates a certain atmosphere that I enjoyed greatly. The debris, scrap, rubbish and dirt covers the rundown cityscape perfectly. What stopped me so that I take my time to look closer was the scenery, the items and things standing around. It looked so real for coming out of the 80/90s. I found my old Epson 9-needle printer sitting on some desks in the game, quite unreal for me.What surprised me was also the detailed walls and floors. As an example, the partly wet linoleum floor in the hospital as it was just cleaned some minutes before. The light reflection of wet and not wet parts looked amazingly real. And even better the linoleum had scratches as in reality.Gameplay is solid, skill tree is straight forward. The additional Auto-9 circuit board and chips was not bad but seemed unnecessary to me. A circuit system were you had to add circuits and chips to enlarge the skill tree would have been better in my view.The actual skill tree and this boost-bonus-construction-kit is to separate from each other.Story is decent, though not an eye opener and no real twists, but otherwise this might not have been right with the settings for a Robocop tale. The last battle felt too short and was over too suddenly. Overall the game felt a bit short, 1/3 longer would have been better.Although then it would be longer in story-telling than the movies of that time. And that might be the decision behind that.Yeah, this does not destroy my impression of the game.Initially I had a lot of problems with crashes and BSOD, where I wanted to refund the game. Steam denied as it was more than two weeks in my library, although I had only 20 minutes of “playtime”, but these were only trials to get the game running. And I was in contact with the game support that two weeks. Which was cumbersome as it seemed no one read my description, because I got always the same advice what I should do, which did not work. Eventually I received decent advice and could finally run the game.

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is nothing short of an incredible time and modern video games could learn a thing for 20 from it;   Harking back to the 5th and 6th generation of gaming, RoboCop puts gameplay and content first, though that's not to say the visuals are impacted, because they aren't..  the game looks stunning from start to finish!I cannot stress enough just how accurate this game is,  how much time and love was put into this project from the developers, it's truly a letter of love.   From blasting scum and blowing the limbs of slimeballs with propane tanks, to roaming the streets, chatting around the town and leaving parking tickets,  RoboCop remains fun, thorough and engaging.There's plenty of side quests to take part in along the main story,  each rewarding you with XP so that you can further upgrade RoboCop's abilities;    Your actions and choices in Detroit also change the outcome of the game and impacts characters as you go along.Did I mention this game is accurate?   Not just to the source materials but also the time period, it captures the feel as if it were an official movie,  y'know, before RoboCop 3 that totally doesn't exist. --  As a bonus,  the game features zero leftist influence / mental illness flags and political correctness,  everything is just as it was back in the good ole' days.Rock solid titles that leaves me rock hard.      My old grips are the spongy bosses and no new game +.

_childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered this game, and downloaded on day one. I love Robocop as a concept and character, especially being a child of the 80s. I had what I thought were reasonable expectations, and the early buzz was great.However, the game is a disappointment. The shooting is boring, the upgrade paths don't really inspire experimentation, and the story is a snoozefest. All of the witty satire of the original movie is largely devoid from this game. In fact, it would've been AWESOME if this had just been a videogame version of the original movie storyline, complete with Botticker and ♥♥♥♥ Jones as the villains.On top of all that, the non-shooter segments are the very worst of walking simulator BS that's present in modern games. Detroit isn't dying, it's dead. A game like this is a relic in the age of engaging movement shooters like Doom Eternal.Murphy himself looks incredible, and it's pretty neat that they got Weller to do the voice, but this a definite "wait for a Steam Sale", as I feel I got burned paying full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Cops and Robbers was always a trope that perforated the 80s and 90s with the like of Hard Boiled, HEAT, Die Hard, Lethal Weapon, etc. Essentially there was no shortage of the boys in blue on the American Silver Screen, however in 1987 Paul Verhoeven released the ultimate display in Street Justice, RoboCop. There's no denying the legacy that this series holds, despite later endeavors sullying the incredible first entry (the second films ok imo), however Teyon again does something incredible by making Rogue City feel like a solid continuation of the overarching plot established in the original film and further emphasized in the subsequent second installment which is great since this game takes place between the second and third film something that is a saving grace for this game, because lets be real here, RC3 and after is largely forgettable.But even with all that table dressing how does the game hold up? I can say with certainty that this is probably the closest we will ever get to a RoboCop power fantasy, the games gory, RoboCop chugs along slowly, and Peter Weller keeps that monotone chrome voice as flat as ever, you really do feel like RoboCop, and I went as far as playing "Red Rain" by Peter Gabriel to get that cocaine lab effect that Peter Weller got, but the usual RoboCop theme works just as well, really selling the idea of you being a near unstoppable force, but outside of all the guns and glamor rests the themes of corporate greed, politics, and the loss of identity that is central to RoboCop as a character which was beautifully done, almost feeling like a horror game at points and these small breaks from the usual protecting and serving are not just welcoming but sobering for people that are already familiar with the story, and the emphasis on it really helps you connect to the your leading man. As I did briefly state gun-play is great all around, and getting to play with guns other than Robo's trusty Auto-9  does help mix things up even if it's only slightly, but the real meat and potato's comes from the upgrading system that effects both Robo individually and his sidearm. You can freely upgrade your Auto-9 to be a fully automatic shotgun pistol that amplifies the gore and *sometimes* causes explosions and yeah that does sound dumb but hey it's suppose to be an action movie so why not go a little nuts?However my biggest grip about this game has to probably be the lack of a New Game+ mode. By the time I finished the game I was barely even close to leveling all of Robo's abilities, along with maxing out the Auto-9 to my preferences. I think after 10-15 hours of play I think players would like to go back fully maxed out to really revel in the mayhem that I enjoyed, or at least go back for secrets, because circuits for the pistol can be merged but it's kinda of just this is what you get and that's that, if you were an idiot like me and merged all your circuits together hoping to get just the right piece to max your stats.And I get it, Teyon is relatively small but for all we know they might add additional content later on down the road since they did that with their previous entries, even their first foray, that being Rambo. But all in all I think the game is good mindless fun you can grind out in a good 10-15hrs but once the credits roll I feel like that's just all folks.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a thumbs up because it's Robocop, however it could be a lot better. The story/missions feel clunky and patched together without flowing smoothly. It does improve as it goes along but the first few levels are a bit hard to follow. The gameplay is a standard 1st person shooter affair which again initially seems disjointed and overly complicated until you unlock the special upgrades for your gun (ie the auto-reload) which then makes you feel like Robocop. There's plenty of Easter Eggs for fans of the original films and nice subtle touches like Alex Murphy's portrait in the Lost in Line Of Duty wall display (and the database). There's also some 'comedy' missions like getting a card signed by everyone and fetching a towel for one of your colleagues who was taking a shower and forget to take a towel with him.There are elements of free-roam whilst around the town and police station parts but the game would have been much better as a full open world free roam where you could choose to go wherever you wanted to stop crime as you see fit, rather than having to strictly follow the story.Worth playing if you're a fan.

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is a phenomenal game. It is everything I could ever possibly want out of such a title, and then some. Since hearing about Rogue City for the first time after it was announced, it's been on my wishlist since then. I had the great pleasure of playing the Rogue City demo during Steam's latest Next Fest. Typically, I will NEVER pre-order anything, but the demo absolutely blew me away, and I was sold on it. So much in fact that I pre-ordered the Alex Murphy edition at my earliest convenience. Based on how the developers reacted to feedback from the demo, they immediately got to work fixing the bugs and further polishing the game before release, which speaks volumes to how much they care about their game's success.I can say having played the game 48 hours early due to pre-ordering it that you don't need to worry about the OCP shotgun - while fun to use, it's not pay-to-win since most weapons you can pick up are better options anyway. The OCP shotgun basically just occupies your picked up weapon slot, and once you run out of ammo, you're going to throw it away and grab something else instead. As far as I can tell, it performs identically to the sawed-off pump shotgun that you can pick up from some enemies. Aside from that, the cosmetic skins are cool but not necessary.At any rate, I have almost nothing but good things to say about Rogue City, and oh man, you're going to hear them.First, I'd like to start off by saying that this game is a love letter to the RoboCop original trilogy. I am a big fan of RoboCop 1, and having watched it, there are several aspects of Rogue City that immediately stand out as references and call backs to the movies. If you have not at least seen RoboCop 1 before playing this, you owe it to yourself - it will give you a greater appreciation for the game. However, if you have not seen any of the RoboCop movies, Rogue City is still a great place to start. Admittedly, I have not seen RoboCop 2 or 3 yet, but I will definitely be going back to watch them. Rogue City takes place between RoboCop 2 and 3 chronologically, making it a sequel to 2 and a prequel to 3. Some of the plot elements either come from or tie in to the original trilogy, adding context to Rogue City.So much of Rogue City's attention to detail and polish give it a great deal of charm. Everything, from the familiar cast of characters, to RoboCop's aloof one-liners, to the subtle dark comedy and dry wit, to small details as homage to the movies like the police cars doing a burnout out of the precinct's parking garage and the sparks when the back of the car scrapes the pavement going up the ramp, and even cracks in your visor that are consistent both in first-person as well as in cutscenes, all just adds to the experience. The city environment, fashion sense of characters, and CRT televisons and computer monitors all lends itself to that gritty, yet glamorized retro-futuristic feel of the 80's and Old Detroit. The movement, your HUD, and many interactions makes you feel like Alex Murphy, the clinically dead remains of someone trapped inside a machine. The musical score is on point, and takes me back to the movies. Rogue City is to the RoboCop Trilogy what Batman: Arkham Asylum is to The Dark Knight Trilogy - just as the Batman games make you feel like Batman, Rogue City makes you feel like RoboCop. The immersion is incredibly solid.Set pieces are absolutely beautiful. On max graphics settings, environments are almost photo-realistic. Lighting during daytime is gorgeous and casts realistic shadows over the environment. Liquid surfaces reflect the world, lighting, entities, and all that jazz. I'm personally not a fan of Nvidia DLSS, which is why I have it turned off. Even with DLSS turned off, on max settings, I'm getting a solid 40-50 FPS on my 2-generation-old RTX 2080 in most areas. I've had frame drops to the high 20's in some scenarios, but those are few and far between, and so far have only happened to me in cutscenes and dialogue where reaction time is not important. All I can say is that they've outdone themselves on how beautiful this game is.Rogue City's actual gameplay is extremely fun. Combat is anywhere between satisfying and exhilarating in any given engagement - the game will throw different flavors of goons at you, and it will be your job to mow them down; sometimes one-by-one with your trusty Auto 9, other times by throwing objects into them, shooting propane tanks to wipe out entire crowds, and grabbing punks by the neck before throwing them into each other, up into the air, or out of the plate glass window of a sky rise. Huge blood stains will show up on walls behind gunshot victims, blooming outward and dripping down the wall. Pools of reflective blood will spread under dead bodies. It's intense and action-packed, and the violence is over the top, just like in the movies.Depending on where you aim, the kill shot will have different effects: a headshot will explode an enemy's head, sending giblets flying everywhere. Arm shots will blow the arm off, sending the character screaming into a unique death animation and dialogue. Leg shots will blow the leg off, instantly dropping the attacker to the ground. Kill shots to the center of mass will simply blow enemies backwards off their feet, instantly knocking them down and clearing your line of fire - even if they are already in a death animation, meaning you can blow a hole in their chest as a quick and satisfying coup-de-grace. You even get a special achievement for shooting enemies in the crotch, and are treated to a very funny death animation where they double over clutching their obliterated manhood. I can definitely say that it hasn't gotten old for me yet.During the quiet points of the game, you largely get to explore beautifully crafted environments in Old Detroit, immersing yourself in the lore of the RoboCop series. Rogue City plays almost like an action-RPG. You can interact with civilians, listen in on conversations, do detective work, scan for clues, solve mysteries, and pick up side quests. Every little thing you do gives you a bit of XP. Leveling up gives you a skill point that you can spend increasing your stats and unlocking special abilities. Each character that you are able to interact with gives you several dialogue options, some of which will change the outcome of the conversation, or even the quest that you're doing.As Alex Murphy, you are not only the master of your own destiny, but also hold the fate of Detroit in your hands. You feel the weight of the decisions you make, and the consequences they entail. The action and combat is insanely fun and varied, and the story is compelling. It is your decision how to pursue your Prime Directives, and serve whichever directive you believe is the greater good.Rogue City is a traditional return to the actually good triple-A titles of 10 to 15 years ago which are relegated to rare gems today, that were innovative, solid, and fun. It is an homage to the RoboCop franchise. Buy the game. You will not regret it.10/10 - "I'd buy THAT for a dollar!"EDIT: Having beaten the game, I am a bit disappointed at what I believe is a lack of replayability. It would also be nice to have achievements based on which difficulty you completed the game on since I beat the game on the hardest difficulty, which all things considered wasn't that tough. Still, it's a superhero game, and more of a power fantasy than a balanced shooter, so that is not a problem.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a big Robocop fan, then this game is a must have. It does a great job capturing the spirit of the movies. If you aren't a Robo fan, you can probably afford to skip it. The gameplay and design are very last gen. There is no cover system, no quick-time events, and no bells and whistles. There is a very basic leveling system that can unlock abilities for Robo to use. One of the best things the game does is, it keeps the Auto-9 (Robocop's starting weapon) relevant by making it upgradable via motherboards and chips the player can find throughout the game. The motherboards also make the weapon highly customizable, so you can have a full auto weapon or a high powered, single shot, hand cannon. It's great because the Auto-9 is iconic and it should never feel useless. Bad stuff.I would not recommend getting the Alex Murphy edition unless you really want to support the developers. It only gets you one skin for Robo, and one skin for this gun. There is no way to manually save the game and there is no easy way to know when the auto-save feature kicked in. If you are done playing, you have to just keep checking the "load game" menu and read the time stamp to see when the last save was. The only other bad thing I will say is, there are a lot of moments in the game that feel like maybe they budget was stretched thin, or maybe they were running out of time. In a apartment building? Look at the corkboard in the lobby.... weird, its the same one from the police station. Shoot a machine gun.... The shells are coming out backwards. Shooting a bunch of gang members.... its the same model used for all 3 gang members.  You like seeing the city? Can't wait to see the rest of the city?  Too bad, it's the same city block recycled 4 or 5 times. Overall, the game has some problems and it feels a little old fashioned, but if you love Robocop and want a experience that feels loyal to the films, then this kicks ass and is a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game and a fantastic love letter to the old school Robocop fans. Just like Terminator Resistance was a fantastic love letter to all T1 & T2 fans. The only thing where you can see some downfalls is in the animation esp. character facial animations but I can give it a pass because those guys are not AAA studio for start (I definitely wouldn't let it slide if it was CDPR doing it). Sound design is also very good, although the Auto 9 doesn't exactly sound like the one from the film which may be just a copyright issue or something because I don't think those guys would mess this up (actually used the movie auto 9 mod and it sounds so great). _childDocuments_.review: At first, Robocop: Rogue City might seem to be just a shooter with a bit of loot on the side. But soon it becomes clear that the game is much more than that: You do not just shoot people as Robocop, you ARE Robocop. There is a good main story with lots of sidequests, crime solving, and exploration. Your dialogue choices often have consequences, not just for how others treat you, but sometimes for yourself as well. Talk to citizens, roam around the city looking for occurences worth investigating, and should you find someone comitting a crime, it is your choice how to deal with them. The game also features a large skill system which is rather straightforward, but can also change how you can approach certain missions, such as attempting to fix broken technology or analyzing incriminating evidence.As for the atmosphere and story, it is highly recommended to watch the movies Robocop 1 and 2 before playing this. It helps a lot with understanding the world presented here and also explains many details that newcomers would otherwise not understand. Additionally, the writers perfectly understood the source material they were working with: You will find exactly the same types of conflicts depicted in the movies, as well as the same brilliant biting satire that will make most of you raise an eyebrow a few times.Two negative points though: One: the main pistol is too overpowered, and makes using any other weapon pretty much obsolete. While the weapon is actually one of Robocop's trademarks, it would be good from a gameplay perspective to encourage players to use a little more variety.Second: The game's performance is not ideal. Many players complain about having low FPS even on lower settings, and there is a bunch of mods out there modifying the engine to run faster (and making it look extremely bland and ugly in the process).To me, this is one of those "one in a million" games where everything just fits: the story, the atmosphere, the gameplay, it is just pure fun. I highly recommend this for any fan of the movies, and also for those who enjoy shooters with RPG elements in general.
