_childDocuments_.review: It would be a lot better game if it did not have the same aiming glitch as Rock* games. Try to aim left, the gun drags right and you miss every shot, and vise versa. Makes the big fights almost impossible cause you cant hit sxit your aiming at. Game needs a whole revamp of the controls and physics.I have always loved Robocop and was looking forward to this game for awhile. Another disappointing(ehhh, maybe not that bad) purchase from Steam. I FXXXXXG hate steam, so there's that.Q.C. in video games has died. Do more testing before release. Update per developer response:Since you responded, Ill go a little deeper into the bugs I found.First, In an early mission, Who killed Casey Caramel, when you talk to the guy next to the dumpster that believes in aliens, if you move wrong you can get stuck in the corner between the dumpster and that little pole. I have also found other aiming bugs.If you are aiming and shooting at a target, and another target near by moves, it draggs you aim towards the moving target. Makes you miss every shot.Also, the squares that are used for ricocheting shots, it also drags the auto aim and tries to follow the target, instead of leaving the aim on the square, again missing all the shots. I cant stand a game that tries to play for me.  Im hitting nothing but the fire button, why is the game moving my aim for me? Im not hitting that input, the gun should not move.Also, the hard load into fights. If you die or fail, there's several spot where you hard load into an immediate fight. 20 enemy open instantly and there no cover.The ground clutter is also horrible. Trying to move into cover in a fight is aggravating cause there always ground clutter that stops you from moving, and you cant see it cause its at your feet. This makes fights frustrating, not fun.I played thru this game on the hardest difficulty and managed to beat the game and find all these bugs in less than 2 days. I am one of several pro-gamers out there offering our services to test these games before release. These problems are preventable.This is what us pro-gamers call a 90% game. It looks like you tried real hard to make a good game, and it is, there a lot of good game here. But it feels like at about the 90% point of having the game done, it gets rushed thru the last 10% and the game falls short of what it could of been had just a little more work been done.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------1-30-2024 update:I would give this a more neutral review if steam offer it. Only having the choice of good or bad limits us. I picked thumbs down cause this game should not of been released in this state.After several play thru's, I am giving a more in depth review. First, I am very critical of games. I have seen prices going up, as game quality goes down. Because of this I have decided to be very stern in how I review games. I think this game was released too soon and needed more work, that being said, this game is a lot of fun.First, the bad, I went over the aiming bugs, but a little more on the ground clutter...I can pick up a dumpster, throw it across the street and crush 3 bad guys to death, but a empty cardboard box stops a 800 Lb cyborg in its tracks. There is so many destroy-able environments in the levels, but invincible cardboard boxes? A design oversight I guess. The movement is slow a clunky, but I think this was on purpose to adhere to authenticy. Robocop wasent know for his agility, so I wont criticize hard for this, unlike the invincible cardboard boxes.... those are so aggravating!!!The other aggravating bug is, throwing bad guys and having them disappear and clip thru walls. Not a serious game breaking bug, but it dose impact the immersion.The game is a resource hog. I kinda feel like my supergamingcomputer should of handles this game better. I had to put my setting closer to mid to stop my GPU fans from screaming. This is the first game Ive played in a long time that couldent eaisly handle ultra setting. Maybe it needed more optimization? For the record, I am not getting the crashing bugs other people are reporting. Mostly visual bugs, that while they get annoying, they really dont affect gameplay.The unskippable cut scenes...Some are fully skippable by pressing X (on controller), other you have to keep pumping X. Kinda annoying, and makes speed running a little more tiresome. A option to hard skip cut sceens and get back to gameplay would be a nice QOL improvement.Now for the good...They worked real hard to make the game authentic to the franchise. It seems to take place between Robocop 2 and 3, as the old man and officer Ann Lewis are still alive.Its a straight forward FPS slow tanky shooter. If you like shooters, but ones that are not fast paced, this is a very enjoyable game. The replay is very high, I played thru 5 times in 4 days and still am not bored. I grabbed it on sale the other day, despite its bugs, for the price i got it, not bad at all. If your a Robocop fan like me, definitely worth a try. It is bloody and gory, just like Robocop should be. The levels range from OK to very good. For a single player offline game, it could of been a little better, but with Robocops slow movement and no driving sections too big of maps may of dragged on the gameplay. Im undecided if having no driving at all added or subtracted to this game. So on that opinion Ill stay neutral and you can decide.So, it you consider Nacom a AAA company, I give it a mid rating, if you consider it a B company, Id give it a good rating. Over all Id feel like this is a 7.5 out of 10.I wont spoil it here, but the ending, and the final boss fight, they got that about perfect. So while I gave it a negative review as there is no neutral option, it was because of the release state, and the problems seem easily fixable to me. I do think this overall it is a good game and worth playing. I would be interested in a sequel, and maybe adding some driving...Or just remaking Robocop 1 and 2 with this engine...Adding a bonus level where you get to pilot the Robocop 2 chassis? MMO with a whole city of cyborg cops and renegade machines going at it to decide the future of old Detroit....????

_childDocuments_.review: Allow me to preface this by saying that Robocop is one of my favorite movies of all time, and that may have something to do with the low score I've given it. Being Robocop and walking through Old Detroit massacring criminals is fun, the weapon selection is decent and it feels great punching people with the force of 3 semi trucks. The Auto 9 customization is also interesting, putting chips in a motherboard to give the gun new and fun abilities is great for me, a person who loves scrolling menus. Unfortunately though, that is where my praise for this game ends, as the writing, voiced dialogue and other gameplay present is quite abysmal. True to Robocop form, there are satirical advertisements that play on radios and some news segments that appear as cutscenes and whoever wrote them is NOT Paul Verhoeven, they wouldn't know subtlety if it shot their hand off with a shotgun and then blasted them to death in an old factory. In the movies, Robocop is a bloodthirsty machine who's mission is to get out in the street and blast criminals, but he never outright says he's bloodthirsty, and in this game he does. Peter Weller does a decent job returning as Robocop, but the rest of the cast is downright terrible, to the point that I'm convinced 99% of the budget went to the IP. A lot of the gameplay, other than filling Old Detroit with bodies, is just regular police work, giving tickets, apprehending vandals, etc. which on it's own doesn't bother me, I love to see Robocop doing actual police work, but all of the NPC's sound like the people voicing them don't really want to be there, or they just don't care, or both. Maybe the bad VA is intentional, like it's trying to be a schlocky 80's movie, but it doesn't feel like dialogue from Robocop. A lot of the dialogue is goofy too, which is not something I consider when I think Robocop, not in the way it's written here at least. Robocop had some ridiculous stuff going on in it, sure, but it took itself seriously enough that it didn't feel goofy, unlike in this game where there is a character who loves doing laundry(????????) and willingly goes to prison because he gets to live there for free and do laundry all day. Also, it gives the illusion that the game is open world, but if you leave an area, it instantly fails all side quests in that area? This is really confusing to me, and seems like something an early open world game from the PS2 era would do. Not to mention that higher difficulty only changes gameplay by making enemies bullet sponge and turns your armor to paper.Perhaps I am jaded, but I cannot recommend this game to anyone who likes Robocop, to me it's a tasteless cash grab, and for $50 you could buy many many better games. Maybe if I finish the game my opinion will change, but for now, it is a stain on one of my favorite films of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus this game has soul. There's so much detail in the environments and the gunplay feels pretty fun so far. But there's so much soul put into this, you can tell the developers are passionate about this. If there's a weaker point I'd say the non-combat drags a bit, but the dialogue is pretty enjoyable. Some friends and I lost our minds over some particularly well-educated drug dealers discussing economics in a tense fight, only for Robocop to cut the discussion short. I can't speak on the length of the game just yet but this is a fun experience thus far.The biggest issue I will note however is that there is no manual saving. It doesn't sound too bad but the auto-saves aren't especially generous. If you encounter a bug or crash you could stand to lose some progress, though not too awfully much.Lastly, the skills you can upgrade and weapon upgrades you can unlock are super fun and I desperately hope the devs add New Game+ in the future, going for another run through the game with an even more obscenely-powerful Robocop just sounds fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: I watched the first two Robocop movies in anticipation for this movie, after I experienced the delightful adaptation that Teyon did with Terminator: Resistance. Like Resistance, Rogue City proves to be another passionate love letter to an 80s action IP, with even better gameplay and a pretty engaging story.Don't get me wrong, it's not gonna blow your socks off - but it's oozing with love for the franchise at every possible turn. Quests frequently make callbacks to moments from the films, characters are rendered to a quality degree (aside from the stiff animations and lip syncing which coincidentally look good for Robocop himself), but the environments are the star of the show. I've never been so consistently impressed with the level of detail and the beautiful lighting that the artists managed to achieve with this game. UE5 has been given to some very talented individuals.Gameplay is pretty solid. Levelling didn't feel very impactful and the game can be completed with just your default pistol and no abilities, but at its best it's very satisfying to pop heads, limbs and men's pickles with a surprisingly vast arsenal. It's like a slow DOOM, and I mean that as a compliment.It's really worth supporting the AA gaming scene that isn't dominated by microtransactions, user-retention metrics, and cocaine-snorting suits. Give this game a go.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is disrespectful to the player!I was quite excited to play this game as it would take me back to my own RoboCop experiences as a youth. Like a retro story in a modern game? Awesome! But I'm feeling bored after playing less than 10 hours. The graphics are somewhat of a let down - I expected more. Gameplay is clunky at best with many of the opponents seemingly stuck in their place, not responding to my presence. I can't seem to get smooth mouse movements going, but either that's user settings not right on my part (had a quick look in mouse settings but couldn't improve it) or it's meant to be this way given that RoboCop is perhaps a robot and less smooth compared to a human?? Then again, I was expecting him to be able to be super precise (when he's not malfunctioning) - he's optimized machine, afterall.The story is meh and too linear. Often long monologues that aren't edited well - long pauses between conversations, repeated, tiring dialogs. The side objectives are a pain, making your run around for no apparent good reason. You can't explore anything outside of a few rooms here and there but why not let me roam around in the RoboCop world to discover new things or shoot up some random bad guys. Like you've given me a killing machine and I can't put it to use! Very frustrating. There is no figuring anything out - like the story was written for dumb-ass players. You know exactly where to go, which door to open, which button to push, which bad guy to kill. Also, let me kill the target, even if it means I fail the mission and start again. Don't baby me as a player - it's disrespectful.Look, my gaming time is limited in a given week, so I can't afford to waste it on mediocre experiences. I think I'm going to have to write this one off and move on.Also, why did I buy this game? The reviews!! They seemed mostly positive but maybe it was wishful thinking on my part?

_childDocuments_.review: The game is faithful to the original movies, right down to the characters appearing and the design of the police station.  I’ve seen the CEO of OCP, Max Becker, Officer Lewis and Sergeant Warren for starters.  If you loved the movies or the old school Terminator FPS games (very similar feel), this one is for you.Beyond that, it's a standard first-person shooter game with above average but not cutting-edge graphics.  I should qualify that by saying it does run on the Unreal engine, and my card is a 3060 Super which puts my rig just a hair below recommended specs.  Game play is smooth with a controller or keyboard and mouse.  Likewise, all the weapons have unique firing characteristics.  Robo doesn't truly run (just a light jog without any level ups), so making use of the environment and the tons of destructible objects in it is important.  Good shooting is important too.  Bad guys seem to be able to take 4 or 5 hits to the torso, but head and crotch shots are instant kills, and fairly gorey.  The devs know what makes FPS gamers tick though.  There’s an achievement for shooting somebody in the groin, and another for shooting the gas tank of a bad guy’s moving motorcycle. Med kits are reasonably plentiful and Robo's armor offsets the lack of true run and gun play at lower levels.  I'm not too far into the game but the story thus far seems decent as well.  So, again, if you're a fan of the franchise, it's definitely worth a pick up.  If you're looking for the next hot replacement for Call of Duty, this ain't quite it.  Overall, a very good game IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this review by saying I got the game on sale at 30% off.Is the game an accurate adaptation of the titular movie ? YESIs the gameplay fun? Yes, albeit a bit repetitive towards the end. Good thing it takes 10-15 hours to complete.Am I pissed because of a couple game breaking bugs I encountered? YES.Redoing entire mission because save checkpoints are not frequent and because you can’t save manually is a bit of pain. After the last boss battle, the game bugged and I didn’t see the ending. So I was also disappointed.It’s a good game and definitely shows the love for the movie, but I cannot in good faith recommend a game that would require me to do the final mission 3+ times to achieve the outcome I wanted because of bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: You’re a walking tank spouting cheesey one liners whilst shooting bad guys in the d*ck. Solid 10/10.Ah yes, the ultimate power fantasy:delivering parking citations!Finally! You can play as the bad guy.A little disappointed that I could not freely commit police brutality like in real life though.This will be a helpful review, Citizen.One of the greatest redemption arcs in gaming history. From Rambo to Terminator to now Robocop. Maybe the company that made Gollum, Kong & that Walking Dead game will have a redemption moment too, although they've got a lot more to make up for...These devs have mastered a niche yet strangely lucrative business model of making first person shooter game based off of 80s movies and it's refreshing to see them be so successful. You can really tell the people who made it love Robocop, the game has a soul and care to it that alot of other games seem to lack. I played it not remembering much about Robocop too and came away loving it, then rewatched the films and rediscovered my love for the franchise. It’s a really great little game and I hope they do more.This game is a fantastic power fantasy that does a pretty good job of making you feel like Robocop, even down to the sound he makes when he walks. It's so fun, it had me giggling like a schoolgirl the way Robocop just slowly stomps down corridors into enemies and starts blasting them. The world is nicely crafted and truthful to the source material, which makes exploring and doing quests nice. It's an amazing homage and fun arcade shooter. It's kind of refreshing to not having to find chest high walls for cover, stealth or other things. I just walk like a fridge on wheels into a room and start blasting.Everything just felt so authentic. From the slowness of Robocop, to having to do actual police work, to even having to go around the precinct and have people sign a card. The behavior of the other cops when everything was going from bad to worse. Some were crying, others were looking for other jobs. There was so much going on that made it feel that it just wasn't about blowing up bad guys. Also, yeeting dumpsters at bikers and land mines was way more fun that I ever anticipated.The authenticity of the police station was surreal. Robo had been my favorite movie when I was 6 years old. To walk around that police station so accurately portrayed and full of life was such an experience. The mundane nature of a lot of the tasks you do, just like real police work was also so much fun. The part where you stand at the podium in the police station had me going. Whenever I see people say they hated that part, I know that person hates absurdity and fun. I just appreciated that not every quest involved shooting. I think my favorite was Robo and Pickles hanging out talking movies like a couple of bros at the video store, that was hilarious. But now that I think of it, it ended with a big shootout too, so Bonus!The story. The world building. It's all so well done and satisfying but on a much smaller scale than most games these days. Shows how games don't need to be so massively open world and a billion boring repeatative missions. The story turned out surprisingly well, enough so that it feels like it could be a genuine Robocop movie. There’s so much nuance in the way the game does some incredible continuation of its over-the-top world, and yet manages to weave in contemporary concerns about police brutality, wealth inequality, and other issues that have increased relevance. Plus the attention to detail, actually enforcing the prime directives through game play (you can't just run around guns blazing and shooting everyone), the Auto 9 always being the best gun (especially if you upgrade it). Even Robo's slow walk felt good and didn't make the game a slog.The combat is fun, the world is so lovingly crafted to the first two films, and there is a certain charm about it that reminds me of old school semi-open first person shooters like Deus ex.I loved interacting with the fellow cast back at the police station, I loved wandering around that little Detroit block and getting into shenanigans with side characters solving side plot threads that can either feel pretty major or can be something as ridiculous as Robocop finding lost cats. And I absolutely loved going through so many of those recreated locations from the first two films to have firefights where just everything is reactive. There isn't a piece of the environment that doesn't scatter with debris when you shoot it and it's awesome. I also really wasn’t expecting a lot of the depth of some of the side characters. I liked that there were 4 characters whose outcomes were determined by your interactions with them. Adds a ton of depth to the story, and gives the game a ton of replay value. Seeing how your actions affect these characters in different ways is just really cool and makes me want to go back and play again to see the possible changes. Also some of the side quests were surprisingly good. As a movie collector/fan, the quest in the video store with Pickles was really charming. Brought that heavy 80’s VHS vibe that Robocop has always had.Definitely more depth than I would have expected and really shows that the satire of the period and original film was not lost on the developers. I also loved that the political choices/path was so gray. Like, both options had major pitfalls and it frankly made me personally want to remain A-political as a roleplay of Robo. They really nailed the sense of responsibility you’re supposed to feel as Robocop. Neither side sees you as a human, and they both have their own agenda. But Robo is a genuine hero, so he’s going to do what he thinks is right, despite no one really caring for him. Because he’s the only one willing to accept the responsibility.It’s a game I actually look forward to playing. The animations are janky as all hell in dialogue and cutscenes... but the game has a certain double A charm to it for me as a late 80s millennial who grew up with RoboCop. Even if I hadn't, I think I would definitely still enjoy it for what it is. Basically parts of this game just really remind you that it's a budget title, but none of it outweighs the amount of love and care that goes into this game that ultimately pulls you into it and immerses you in it even if there are things that are distracting. I had a ton of fun. It’s MUCH better than I expected and would recommend. It’s not perfectly polished but I didn’t have any horrible issues and it’s to 100%. Who would’ve thought that a 15-20 hour Robocop game would be the best RPG/FPS of the year. The 7/10 licensed video game is back and I couldn’t be happier!As a fan that was reminded of his love for this world thanks to this game though, it’s a 10/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of the first two Robocop movies, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. While the game is not perfect and has a few graphic anomalies (mesh vertex stretching on actor lips), a few bugs (which can be overcome by work around suggestions provided by the Steam community), it is by far the best Robocop game we're going to get. I can live with it - happily!I have never been a fan of paid professional gaming reviews written by folks who rushed the game over a weekend off to meet deadlines. It really feels to me like I played a completely different game than they did.One of the biggest gripes always seems to be "Its not worth how much I spent on it, blah, blah, blah, etc." Boo hoo! I'm not rich but dropping $50 on a game in a world where the value of a dollar has shrunk for decades isn't absurd. I have no problem paying what I paid for what I received because the game was freakin' fun! I have spent far more and got far less. A single meal at a fast food joint hovers around $20 in most states. Spare us all the righteous indignation for having to spend a little hard earned scratch on a hobby like video gaming. I could buy a Bayliner boat with all the money I've spent on video games, DLCs and in game content over all the years I've played.  If you can't afford to pay for a game to support a developer who poured the heart and soul into such a passion project, perhaps you should find a different hobby. All in all, I can say that Robocop Rogue City was a joy to experience, chalk full of nostalgia and was a beautiful ultra-violent gib-fest in all its campy 80's era action movie glory. If you're even the slightest fan of the Robocop silver screen saga, stop reading this and get the game. You'll love it far more than hate, I can promise you that. Also, look at the steam community reviews. Very positive!  If the game sucked as bad as all these paid knucklehead reviewers said it did, it wouldn't be doing this good. That's a fact. If anything I wrote here inspires you to give this game a try, then I feel I've done my part to give this a fair shake. If not, oh well. Sounds like a 'you' problem.

_childDocuments_.review: The same developers  of this game also made Terminator : Resistance.Robocop Rouge City...Terminator Resistance...Robocop...VSTerminator..You see what i'm thinking! A perfect sequel to this! I sure hope they will develop that one!This game is really good so far. for a Robocop fan it's the best game ever!So you can see where I'm coming from, my dad first showed me Robocop the movie when I was 6 years old, left it on the TV thinking it'd be fine and then left the room to talk to family in the other room.The trauma and nightmares from ED 209 and the melting man took many years to get over so Robocop, for me, always had this edge to it over everything else. It was hard hitting, ultra cool and iconic. The Terminator was great, but Robocop wasn't trying to be a Terminator movie, it was it's own thing entirely and hard to replicate - especially in a videogame.Robocop is so cool to me that I am very picky when it comes to representing the first movie.Back then technology was limited so my first Robocop game I played was on the Amstrad CPC 464. the title theme music and stage music is such a nostalgia hit every time (go and listen for yourself!) and the game tried to be as Robocop as possible (these things being shooting bad guys and having certain things like sections where you target an enemy in first person using your sights and so on.As the years went by, Robocop movies got worse. they made a CARTOON out of it, they made action figures and toys that fired real caps! (I actually loved these).There have been MANY Robocop videogames across many platforms, including in the arcades! Robocop vs Terminator on the megadrive was excellent but absolutely rock solid to complete, most Robocop games are notorious for being difficult.Back in 2003 they released a Robocop 1st person game.. it wasn't good at all, and his walking sound will make you feel like you have overdosed on nuke.It seems that Robocop was destined to be on this downhill slope where the bar was raised so high with the first movie - the only way was down.That was until Teyon took hold of the controls and decided to make a Robocop game themselves, with the look and feel of the original first movie. I had serious doubts when this was revealed however and so I went into this with expectations so low, it came as no surprise to me to be greeted with a black screen for 5 minutes upon launching the game..(it doesnt take that long after that initial load now)They made a bold move developing this game, this sacred IP, especially with a low budget, but there is a real attention to detail and passion put into this game that would have been replaced with stuff that isn't welcome in a Robocop game so it would sell more copies to the average gamer if made by someone else. So IMO this developer was the best choice for this, and the higher the budget can only mean more fingers in the pie of this game. Constant DLC, stripped down content and so on.The low budget works for the fans, but for your average games it lacks a certain quality that gamers have been spoiled with over the years. If you like Shenmue then you will feel right at home with the cut scenes in this game XDThe design and style of the game just suits the original film so well, the sound of robocop walking around, some of the data you see when you scan, PETER WELLERS VOICE!!!! It's all spot on. Some of the details are so good, it's a bit jarring then when the animations tend to stick out - they needed more work and a bigger budget to get these right.The city looks fantastic as well, similar graphics to Resident Evil 7.Gameplay wise it reminds me of a game called L.A NOIRE, where you can interact with a crime scene, discover evidence, talk to people to find answers to the case. Often it will end with a rewarding shootout or some story closure. Some cut scenes and animations are hit and miss, some of the characters are excellent - really good voice acting and detail to them and interesting dialogue. Then there are others that seem very cheesy and basic, many of the enemies and "Punks" I think are just annoying and remind me of Keith flints style from the prodigy, in the firestarter video only with very bad acting instead.This game is not your usual FPS game where you go from a to b shooting your way through, there are side objectives to complete which help draw you in to the world and for the most part it does a great job, at least so far.Some of the shooting mechanics are a bit basic and I do wish that the movement of the gun felt a bit looser, with the gun fixed to just off centre of the screen you feel a bit rigid and a bit stiff walking around and aiming, no gun spinning or putting your gun back in your leg (lol) just misses some opportunities there to make you feel like you are Robocop, but the sounds he makes whilst walking and talking as well they have nailed that, and his look.His rigid and slow movement helps make you feel like a machine, but you lose that cool precision you would expect from BEING Robocop when it comes to gunplay.I think if they released this game with a VR mode , even charge extra for that, that would be a superb match for this game where the gun movement would feel more natural to your own movements, spinning the gun around and using your spike hand and that sort of thing.Whilst playing this game it makes you wonder about other IPs that deserve this kind of care and attention and some come to mind such as Judge Dredd and Die Hard! They would be excellent sources of material for this developer to get their teeth into and get out there.It's about time there was a decent Robocop game out there that respects and UNDERSTANDS why people love Robocop. I've only scratched the surface of this game but I can see how some things can be repetitive and the gameplay can feel a bit sluggish, but the story and dialogue so far is well written and engaging with plenty of variety of things to get you going from a to b. I would have lost interest if this was just purely an FPS shooter so I am thankful of the story and characters within it that make it feel like you are in a down and out, dangerous drug filled futuristic detroit (with retro arcade machines!) Performance wise its fine, especially for the first week! Expect bugs with any game on launch these days but it runs fine on my system with no lag at all or crashes but we shall see.Is this game worth full price though? I hear its got about a 17 hour campaign, so for me that is worth it. BUT if you love Robocop and are on the fence about paying full price - remember that the higher the price, the more the devs will get for this and are more likely to do more updates and fixes or more titles featuring other cool IPs they can make a decent game out of. I would have had to have waited for this to be on sale as my budget is low for games at the moment.Casual games should probably pay between £25 and £30 imoThis is definitely the best Robocop game out there, and I am enjoying it a lot so far. Just remember though that it didn't have a massive budget so it lacks a certain polish that is expected of big budget or big name games but it does all of the other things really well. Having Peter Weller voice Robocop just blows my mind every time, if they had a voice actor imitate the voice it just wouldnt feel right, and would lack that authenticity to really draw you in.I look at this game like I look at the original Resident Evil game, the acting isn't always very convincing but the overall gameplay and presentation is enough to make you look past those flaws and just enjoy the experience at hand and what you have at hand is a lengthy game, decent dialogue and character building moments, good graphics and easy to get into shooting mechanics and a levelling up system to give it a little depth and RPG style to it. It isn't going to win any game of the year awards, but fans will see passed the flaws and enjoy this very much.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it. It's good. REALLY good.An absolute gem. Greatly satisfying shooting mechanics with punchy sounds, 90' style cinema over-the-top gore, that'll scratch that power fantasy itch (though on Hard difficulty you do need to have some tactical sense, prioritise targets and sometimes make use of cover).The game features RPG elements in the form of skills and abilities (anything from more healing charges, a damage absorbing shield, ricocheting bullets off walls like in the movie, hacking various devices etc.) and customising the iconic Auto-9 - RoboCop's gun - which is a cool little "puzzle" to solve in order to build the most optimal setup. This gun gets absolutely ridiculous later in the game, and I love it.The pace of the game is good. It introduces new enemy types, hazards and weapons at a steady pace, always sprinkling in something new, as well as NOT recycling mission structure much. It's NOT a "checklist simulator" like many recent open world games that have about 10 activities for the player to engage with, and repeat them ad nauseum across a bloated world. Nope. RoboCop: Rogue City is a narrative-driven game that does its absolute best to always present the player with something new to do.Anything that approaches "reusing" content is, in my opinion, executed well - first, the game teaches the player about a new mechanic, and some time later it comes up again, but this time the stakes are more dire, and the player has to rely on their previous experience with a similar mechanic. This is nothing but good design, and have game progression should look like.I find the story to be captivating, and the characters well written. Sure, it's not at the level of meticulous quality that some AAA titles reach, and the characters' tone and/or animations don't always match the mood of the situation, but that's a decisive minory - vast majority of the story was a pleasure to partake in.And "partake" isn't a random word - the narrative isn't just a story you passively watch unfold, as this game does present the player with choices that impact the outcome, not only for RoboCop himself, but also a cast of the few closest characters, as well as (without going into specifics) the political situation and the city of Detroit at large.The importance of choice outweighs something that I find to be a small, but noticeable shortcoming of the narrative - the quests don't really offer much in terms of a "failure state". Despite there being a fair amount of detective work and investigation, I haven't encountered a situation where RoboCop could end up drawing the wrong conclusions and arresting someone innocent.The only "failure states" are when RoboCop dies (but that just leads to reloading a checkpoint, so it doesn't really count), and on occasion failing to save hostages etc. (which impacts your mission evaluation score, and thus gained EXP points).Does the game have minor glitches and bugs? Yes.Do they hinder gameplay? Only once in the entire playthrough I've encountered a progress bug that required me to restart a mission - that's a bit sour, but the gameplay is more than fun enough, so replaying the section wasn't unpleasant. But if you dread having to replay a mission, you should probably wait a few weeks until the most pressing issues are patched.The support is responding to bug report emails very promptly, and assures that the dev team is working on rolling out patches. Given the sheer love put into this game (which shows in the little details) I'm very much inclined to believe.

_childDocuments_.review: After many many MANY game and PC crashes an trying different possible solutions for it, i can finally change my review to positive, but with a warning:If you like Robocop, this game is a real must have! BE AWARE for the possibility for severe game and PC crashes which some people experience. If you have (Windows) Mirrored Volumes like me, a PC crash forces a many hours lasting resync of them (not to mention possible loss of (other) data and Windows causing extra problems because of the crashes!) ============================================I finally found the solution after trying many other things I had to lookup in steam Discussions: LOWERING GPU POWER LIMIT IN MSI AFTERBURNER (From 100% to 90% in my case) Played a 2 and 4 hours session without crash after this change :DNOTE: Lowering the GPU Power Limit was the last thing i tried for solving the crashing problems, it's very possible other changes I've made are also responsible for the final effect of not crashing!============================================I hope the devs can make an update for the game which prevents these crashes from happening. This terrible path to the solution is something no gamer should go trough.Anyway, now I finally can play without crashing: I LOVE IT! I'm not gonna spoil anything, just try it! Playing the game without knowing anything of what's to come is the best way to experience it :DPC Specs & Extra info about the crashes: Since lowering the GPU Power Limit solved the problem for me, I can't ignore the possibility of faulty hardware like a power supply that doesn't deliver enough power under heavy loads. I haven't looked into this any further, but as i also play (and sometimes record at the same time) VR games (which are a HUGE load for CPU and GPU) without ANY crashes, I'd be surprised my Corsair RM750X has problems (Should deliver more then ever required by all hardware under heavy load)I can be wrong, who knows, all hardware dies eventually.Ryzen 7 3700XRTX207032GB RAMCorsair RM750X PSU Windows 10 Pro

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Robocop is a a classic cyberpunk/superhero 80s movie about a rookie cop named Alex Murphy who got gunned down on his first day on the job, then reviving as the titular metallic avenger killing folks and taking names. Rogue City is a game adaption taking place after the first two movies. Robocop, now established, is trying to keep the city under control as all the gangs of Detroit want the notorious “new guy” to notice them uWu. In addition to sparse but notable malfunctions Robocop has his work cut out for him to keep the city under control. Bringing B movie charm, camp (and production value) Rogue City is treats the source material with love and respect and also is a pretty decent game on top of it all. Visceral shooting as well as numerous side quest to flesh out the world and other characters introduce in the game. Definitely wait for a sale (especially if you’ve never seen Robocop. Get on that though)  but I think the money was well spent. Spoiler Free In-Depth ReviewRobocop is a pretty popular media phenomenon released in the good ole 80s (Well, as good as a decade can be with the Crack Epidemic and the Cold War, I guess. But POP CULTURE!) that had it all. Action, drama, philosophy, and almost out of place visceral gore. If you haven’t seen the movie yet, then shame on you, and I don’t know why you’d play this game if that’s the case but the game gives you a bit of hints here and there to catch you up to speed....wait...you want me to get you up to speed? Well, fine, but I’ll put emphasis on SPEED.Robocop tells the tale of Alex Murphy, a rookie cop who tries to make a name for himself in old Detroit, a hive of scum and villainy even at the best of times. But quite abruptly during his first day on the job, one could say he did make a name for himself, penciled right on a concrete tombstone,as he’s mercilessly gunned down by a group of armed thugs. Miraculously enough, he survived (more or less). Brought back to life with the help of OCP-Omni Consumer Products (if Umbrella focused more on tech and cyborgs rather than “health” products), he becomes a mix of man and machine, and with new found abilities and prowess due to his high tech augments, he seeks to bring back justice to the streets of Detroit, while trying to make sure he keeps what shreds of humanity remains.Rogue City takes place after the first 2 films. At that point, Robocop is firmly established and his reputation for killing dudes precedes him. A “new guy” in town who has taken over the remnants of the Nuke drug trade from Robocop 2 has all the local gangs chopping at the bits to be recognized. During a routine hostage situation caused by these maniacs (Routine should tell you all that needs to be said), Murphy begins malfunctioning and the footage of it was streamed all across the news of the city. To top it all off, Max Becker, an OCP executive, has been assigned to abrasively “assist” Murphy due to his meltdown on live tv. Can Robocop keep it together, as well as keep the city safe from this “new guy?”Rogue City isn’t really a looker, and in many ways the design can come across cheap. Robocop himself looks great, and they even managed to get the original actor Peter Weller to reprise the role as a voice actor. But many of the models in the game would fit in about 8-10 years ago, which honestly I’m fine with. The voice acting on some of the other characters are hit or miss though, with many of the thugs you come across basically being the same high pitched guy. But part of that ads to the camp B movie charm that even the original movie had at points.As this is a first person shooter though, the primary thing we care about is the bullet flinging. And Rogue City is very enjoyable on that front. Shooting is visceral and unsurprisingly brutal (Might say it doesn’t fit the tone if you hadn’t seen anything Robocop, but Murphy got ripped the shreds in the original). You have Robocop’s iconic Auto 9 to gun down gang bangers with, as well as a host of other rifles, shotguns, and pistols that you can pillage from your foes' cold, dead, and...uh....eviscerated hands. The Auto 9 can be further enhanced with various OCP motherboards that you find across the game to further enhance the carnage and gore (LITERALLY! There is literally an upgrade to increase the gore). Beyond shooting, Robocop has a mean left hook, being able to punch out thugs as well as fling almost anything at the opposition. Sofas, Computer monitors, desk, chairs, even the thugs themselves. Narcon spared no expense in putting the hurt on those that would try to sabotage the peace of Old Detroit. Rogue City isn’t really open world, rather the city of Detroit acts as a somewhat spacious hub that you explore, get leads, and then pursue your adversaries in their own dedicated levels. There are also a host of side  quest that you can undergo to enhance the public perception of Robocop, but also assist other characters in the main story in their own story arcs like Pickles, a junkie turned informant who is trying to go straight, and Ulysseus, a young techy cop who the others mistrust as an OCP informant, but perhaps within in a young man trying to better himself as well as his community. There is cheese, so much so that I might have to break out the nachos, but it’s treated with so much sincerity and love and respect for the source material that it elevated my enjoyment of the game.Somewhat early-mid game, I began to regret my purchase. Shooting was REALLY samey and the same gun toting junkie was so monotonous, but the game does spice it up a bit further in and as it went on I started to enjoy it more and more and even went out of my ways to get all the achievements (They are pretty easy to get though so if you are an achievement hunter know that) and due all the side quest (Not getting all the collectibles though, let’s not get crazy).Perhaps wait for a sale (I paid $30 and I thought it was worth that), but definitely a good game even for a player without. A Robocop background (Although you really should prior to playing as there are LOOOADS of references and callbacks, and some things might not make full sense without it).

I have begun a NG+ game (There will be trouble difficulty) and I feel like a ROBOGOD and still having fun. Why do I not recommend the game?I did not have this issue during my first play through. However, the game has been crashing. First during the first mission. The second was at start up showing the Intel Arc card. The third was during the chop shop side quest. I updated my card and Windows. Many people are having this issue with the game being unstable. This is not an issue with hardware.  And I have not encountered this issue with other games. It is clearly an issue with the game since being updated.I cannot recommend the game no matter how much I loved playing through my first game until this issue is fixed. The game is broken at this time. When the game is fixed and stable I will change my review. However, buy at your own risk. This issue is due to game commands failing which causes a fatal error. Then the game takes a few minutes to close. It will not let me close it or open my task manager to kill it. I have to wait.No matter how fun or how good a game is, broken is broken. It needs to be fixed. Remember this game does not let you save. It has save points. So a good deal of play during a quest can be lost and require you to start over. _childDocuments_.review: My early impression of the game is that If you're already a fan of RoboCop you'll like this. If not, then go watch the movies. It's not a AAA game but it's close enough. That doesn't mean that the devs didn't put a lot of love into this. While the facial animations may be lacking and the NPC voice lines may sound a little phoned-in at times it still goes far in capturing the feel of the movies with everything else. That said Peter Weller's performance is still the voice of RoboCop many of us grew up with and is fantastic. The game-play and atmosphere are where this game shines. I thought I'd be just blasting my way through the missions but instead I'm playing a beat cop investigating thefts and giving out parking tickets. The blasting is still there (and it's fun) but the variation in missions was a welcomed surprise.I'll update how I feel about the story once I've cleared it but the game is so far good enough that I want to see where it's going.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good graphics, but annoying that there's pretty much no way to disable upscaling... wtf, devs, do you think everyone has a PC that sucks?Anyway, this will not be a game for everyone. It's a game you'll enjoy if you specifically ever wanted to be in RoboCop's "shoes" as a kid... and you never quite got your fix (pun intended) on the 8-bit consoles.It can be enjoyable if you don't expect much more form it than what it is: Take control of Robocop in a movie and wander around in a small neighborhood, shooting every single bad guy either in the head... or in the d*ck, whichever you prefer. There will be plenty of them to shoot. I recommend the highest difficulty, it made the game less boring for me since I actually sometimes did struggle to stay alive, so something else  to do besides pointing my gun at people's d... faces - but it isn't really a challenge if you know what you're doing.Sadly, it doesn't have much replay value. Might have been able to make some use of a New Game Plus mode, at least being able to keep one of the skills you desire, so you can start the game again by using other means than your previous playthrough, but no such thing exists. You finish the game and... that's it.I wish there was a neutral recommendation button. I kinda liked the game. I'm the type of guy who likes games that tend to get boring. So, really, I recommend playing it only if you're really a fan, otherwise don't bother. You will get bored in about 2 hours, and then you'll never play it again, let alone finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this game but I couldn't enjoy it. I first heard about it from a streamer saying it's "a hidden jewel, underrated game" so I was really excited to add it in my playlist. I don't know exactly what went wrong, my expectations were either unrealistic or I spoiled myself playing other games that I consider to be a lot better than RoboCop: Rogue City. I highly believe that if this game was released 10-15 years ago I would be impressed, but by my today's standards, this wasn't a good experience for me.To kick off some things, I never watched the movies (I might do it in the future) so I'm out of context with the story. I read that the developers did a great job of keeping the source material, so good job to them. This never stopped me to enjoy a game and I judge most of the titles I play by the gameplay they provide. The combat of RoboCop is very basic and below your average FPS game, it feels like a cheap version of Cyberpunk 2077 but without any of the cool features, you walk and popup heads which is fun, but it gets boring really quick. After completing some of the story you'll find new types of enemies that don't die that easily, but here comes the issue near the end: they become too tanky and you literally have to use 30 magazines with full upgrades in order to kill an ED 209 for example. It also doesn't help when the AI is so bad that most encounters feel the same, while having only a non-directional dash and some additional active skills. There are no real options for weapons, the classic pistol outclasses most of the guns that have really low ammo count for some reason; it feels like there is no sense of progression, most of the skill upgrades didn't have any impact; the PCB upgrades were really confusing and they felt like a slug rather than an engaging system; the HUD is so retro, it gives me some vibes from the past, I wish it was a little bit more modern without breaking the immersion; the night vision almost killed my retina. There are also many side quests that I tried to do as much as possible, but they felt like a chore rather than a fun time.Were there any good parts that I enjoyed? Yes, but too little to make me want to change my mind. I really liked the "glitches" with the memories from the past, those were my favorite segments from the campaign. Being able to highlight enemies from distance while tapping their heads was a good practice for my aim, same as the training range. I am also a huge fan of the idea of player's choices having consequences and having the option to side with different characters. But there is where the positive points stop, the game is too short to be worth the full price. I am really sorry, but I can't recommend it, maybe it's worth for the fans of the movies.

_childDocuments_.review: A Nostalgic Fan Service with Technical WoesRoboCop, the iconic cybernetic law enforcement officer, returns to the gaming world in this much-anticipated release that blends nostalgic fan service with a frustratingly poor technical performance. While the game successfully immerses players in the dystopian world of Old Detroit and delivers a hefty dose of RoboCop lore, it is plagued by a slew of technical issues that hamper the overall experience.Pros:Nostalgic Fan Service: RoboCop aficionados will undoubtedly appreciate the game's commitment to staying true to the source material. The atmosphere, character designs, and overall tone of the game effectively capture the essence of the original films and comics.Iconic Weapons and Gadgets: Players can wield an array of iconic weapons and gadgets that RoboCop fans will instantly recognize, from the Auto-9 pistol to the ED-209. The authenticity of these tools adds to the game's appeal.Storytelling: The game's narrative weaves a compelling storyline that immerses players in the gritty world of Old Detroit. It delves into RoboCop's internal struggles and explores moral dilemmas, enhancing the overall storytelling experience.Cons:Technical Nightmares: Unfortunately, RoboCop is riddled with technical issues that severely hinder the gaming experience. Frequent crashes, frame rate drops, and long loading times make the game frustrating to play.Game-breaking Bugs: Some players have reported encountering game-breaking bugs, such as quests that cannot be completed due to soft locks or broken scripts. These issues disrupt the otherwise engaging narrative.Lackluster Graphics: While the game's art style is reminiscent of the '80s, the overall graphics and animations appear outdated. This, combined with the technical problems, makes for a visually underwhelming experience.Missed Potential: RoboCop could have been a true gem for fans, but the technical issues overshadow its potential. A lack of polish and optimization significantly detracts from the enjoyment of the game.In conclusion, RoboCop offers a hefty dose of nostalgia and fan service for devotees of the franchise. However, the game's numerous technical problems severely limit its overall enjoyment. If you're a die-hard RoboCop fan willing to overlook these issues, you may find some enjoyment in revisiting Old Detroit with the iconic cyborg. But for those seeking a polished and seamless gaming experience, it's advisable to wait for patches and updates to address the game's glaring shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: Good character design, voice acting and sound effects. Nice graphics.  Good story and characters: a lot of your favourites will be here if you're a fan of the first two films. Good variety of enemies and attacks: their AI is also quite impressive. If you're into a bit of the old ultraviolence in an over the top style reminiscent of the films and certain comic books, you should be set. Popping heads and shooting grenades did not get old.This ran well (albeit with medium DLSS/FSR) on my 32GB RAM 5800x/3080 10GB vRAM Windows VM under Linux host at 3440x1440 VRR. 16GB system RAM should also be fine: total usage on my VM was under 50%. 10bpp colour (HDR) works OK with ini file tweaks: I did not try ultrawide tweaks on my first playthough. It was fine without either, so don't think you have to tweak or mod this unless you have very specific requirements.The world is a little bit thin in places, but that's to be expected from a smaller studio and a small development budget. Exploration is usually rewarded via experience points. Music variety is also lacking, but wasn't particularly noticeable to me until 75% complete. Well worth ~£1/hour of gameplay: ~100% first playthough was about 24 hours on "Hard" mode. It might be worth skimming a skills guide if you're not sure where to spend you points. I went with the humanity/detective skills to A) roleplay as the human side and B) max XP on my first run. I'm looking forward to messing about a bit more in New Game Plus mode: all my skills were reset to zero, but i retained the points, so could re-spec.I thoroughly enjoyed this game, and completed it in a few evenings (and a couple of late nights!) Gunplay was good: I mostly stuck to the iconic Auto-9, and you probably will too, as you can essentially re-spec it at any time to handle a variety of situations and enemy types. I mainly used the other weapons early game, and for a very few specific situations. The Auto-9 gets a good amount of variety through weapon mods: add in melee kills and the extra skills (dash, armour and slow-motion, did not try shockwave this time through) really help you feel like the big metal man himself.

_childDocuments_.review: This one would be a 9/10 for me. I did not think I would actually be giving GOTY to ROBOCOP Rouge City, but its honestly the best Robocop ANYTHING we have had since the first to movies.If you enjoyed the 80's style of the RoboCop movie then you will like the feel of this game as they mostly stayed true to that aesthetic. Peter Weller, the same actor from the movies, was used for this creation so they definitely put in the effort for this game.The sound effects are minimal but I did enjoy the score, would have benefited from an actual orchestra but it all fits in. The music style in combat really does have a late 80's/early 90's vibe to it. The graphics as far as environments go are at times quite impressive as you would expect for an Unreal 5 based game, though there is a weird contrast in some area. You'll definitely want a more powerful GPU for the Unreal 5, and 4K with 60fps just looks spectacular! Characters also take on a somewhat last gen quality to them when you enter into dialogue, which is in some ways isn't charming but with how far we have come shouldn't be to hard to sync up dialogue or basic human interactions. Speaking of the characters, this is where the negatives start. The main missions are generally action packed enough to keep it interesting but many of the side missions are painfully tedious. (((SPOILER))) One example is a side mission that has you fetching a towel for a guy who is in the shower... no joke. Stuff like this has me scratching my head seeing there was nothing like this at all in any Robocop universe. There is a LOT of dialogue to get through here and while some love that in RPG games, I have to admit I start to get bored at times and want something more challenging than finding some idiots towel.If you like to 100% games and do everything as I try to, this one may prove tedious to you as it was to me. I was also frustrated that early on there were things like safes you cant open unless you have a certain level of upgrades but at that early stage of the game it is what it is. Replay value at its finest. Overall I think they did a pretty good job here and if you want an old school style combat based RPG, or you loved the RoboCop or Robocop 2 movies, this should win your heart over.

_childDocuments_.review: Set in the gritty, dystopian landscape of Old Detroit, "RoboCop: Rogue City" captures the essence of the 1987 classic with stunning accuracy. As RoboCop, players will engage in intense gun battles, using the iconic Auto-9 pistol to uphold the law. The story is ok, with numerous references to the film that will satisfy veteran fans. The return of Peter Weller's voice adds to the authenticity of the game, creating an experience that feels like a direct continuation of the cinematic saga.The gameplay is a mix of combat and investigative skills, reflecting RoboCop's dual nature as a law enforcer and detective. Primarily a first-person shooter, the game immerses players in the action from RoboCop's perspective. Controlling RoboCop feels like manoeuvring a tank, with his heavy, deliberate movements and powerful weaponry. Investigative segments break the action, requiring players to analyse crime scenes and make choices that influence the narrative. Visually, "RoboCop: Rogue City" captures the dark, industrial aesthetic of its cinematic counterpart, despite some dated character models and animations. The sound design is exceptional, with the iconic RoboCop theme and authentic sound effects adding to the immersive experience."RoboCop: Rogue City" is a fitting tribute to the original film series, offering fans the chance to once again step into the metallic boots of their favourite cyborg lawman. RoboCop would approve. I completed the game in slightly less than 20 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game, purely playing for nostalgia sake. At point blank range, you'd expect 3 bullets right in center mass would end anyone without armour, yet the NPCs will still run around waiting for that final 4th bullet to end them. Yes you can modify the damage output with chips however still not as effective as it should be.Graphics: 3 out of 5- Lots of artifacting on models- Gore is pretty cool to see, NPC heads do explode when you land a 3-burst shot onto their heads, yet when target limbs and empty 12 bullets into it nothing happens. But if a grenade explodes near them they get dismembered. - Cannot see player's (RoboCop's) legs when looking straight down.- No player reflection on mirror surfaces

If you're going to pick this up, just know that it's not constant action - there is a good amount of exploring and NPC interaction, but it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is a very fun FPS! Took me about 16 hours to complete.I won't claim to be the biggest RoboCop fan, as I have only seen the first movie a handful of times and I have only seen RoboCop 2 once. But even with that said, this game feels like the perfect RoboCop experience. Gun play feels phenomenal, Story is as campy and fun as the films, returning characters (even the actors voices) from the films are in here, the list goes on of praises I can give this game.One negative I can give though is that RoboCop: Rogue City has no manual saving. Game is auto save only and only saves at the beginning of a mission and every time you use a door to enter a new area. This wouldn't be so bad if the open area segments have you go for upwards to an hour without it saving a single time. An update that adds manual saves would be amazing.TLDR RoboCop: Rogue City is a solid 8/10 FPS. If anything, maybe wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, Im going to update my review after finishing the game. According to the achievement stats I am in the 12% of people who have actually completed the last mission so I think I'm more or less qualified to give my opinions.I initially gave this a thumbs down as I hated the mundane police duties and forced side quests as I found them extremely boring and tedious. But, I must say I did really enjoy the combat and story and it sort of had me hooked all of the way through. So don't be fooled by the latter as there is still a great game here under the surface. There Isn't much to do upon completing your first play through an option to start a new game with all of your upgrades carried over would have been nice. But for the price you get a 14 hour campaign which was mostly enjoyable when the action was on screen.It would have been better if they kept the main story a bit more linear and focused. Then they could have had a serve and protect game mode where you go around the city doing all the mundane police ♥♥♥♥, like saving cats from burning buildings (yes this is actually one of the side quests...) This would have added some extra value and given players something to do after completing the game.All in all id say its worth a play through if your a Robocop fan or a Nostalgia chaser. 7/10Teyon did a great job and Im looking forward to seeing what their next project will be. Would love to see them do a blade runner game next :D Pretty please!
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: As a lifelong Robocop fan, I am very satisfied with this long overdue sequel game to a film series that is as classic as the terminator (The first two robocop movies anyways). The environments capture the films perfectly. And the Characters are pretty good too. If you're a fan, This will absolutely scratch that robocop itch. As a newcomer, its a very fun game. Side quests help break up the pace. combat is a much more engaging than the trailer made it look. Controlling robocop and watching someone else control robocop are two very different things. I was skeptical. Now I'm convinced. Solid outing. The true Robocop 3.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not stress enough the importance of keeping bad ass franchises like this alive. It's something that most companies tend to use as a cash grab. But thanks to the amazing people at Teyon, we get (in my opinion) one of the best video game adaptations of a movie. Sure, it has some minor glitches, but for all it's worth, it's a truly amazing experience. The dialogue is spot on, the characters are intriguing, and the story is damn near perfect. To anyone who's thinking about picking this up, and is a huge robocop fan, this is a MUST.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by no means the absolute end-all of ultimate FPS experiences, but it is *THE* ultimate RoboCop experience. _childDocuments_.review: This is another surprisingly good, movie-inspired game. What I appreciated most about this game was how the campaign stayed true to the movies. Everything felt very reminiscent of the 1987 original. I've always been a big fan of the Robocop movies, and overall this game did the movies justice. The only negatives for me were the dated graphics and very poorly optimized game engine. I have a GeForce 3090 Ti and I had to turn all the graphics settings down to minimum just to play with tolerable slow downs and occasional sluggishness. Virtually every other AAA game I can easily play on near max settings. To be honest, I came very close to uninstalling and abandoning the game altogether in the first couple of hours of gameplay, but I'm glad I decided to give the game a chance after turning the graphics down. I'm usually a stickler for top-notch graphics in my video games, but the game was definitely worth the price despite this draw back. I do recommend it for anyone who's a fan of the Robocop franchise or anyone who enjoys a good shooter game and has a tolerance for dated graphics. I'd give it a 7/10, and I truly hope there will be a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop: Rogue City remains exceptionally faithful to its source material, immersing players in an artistic atmosphere and aesthetic perfectly reminiscent of the retro-cyberpunk Paul Verhoeven classic. Set in the dystopian American landscape of Detroit, the game faithfully captures the essence of its origins. The iconic soundtrack makes a triumphant return, further enhancing the experience, while the inclusion of Peter Weller's voice adds an extra layer of authenticity to the portrayal of Robocop.As one of the first titles to utilize the UE5 engine, Robocop: Rogue City boasts breathtaking visuals. From the stunning Lumen lighting to the lifelike nanite detailing and real-time reflections, the game achieves a level of visual fidelity that is truly impressive. The gameplay seamlessly translates the essence of Robocop, allowing players to navigate environments with precision and power, leaving destruction in their wake. The combat is exhilarating, with levels often resembling intense shooting galleries as players face off against a variety of enemy types. The game doesn't shy away from its ultraviolent sensibilities, with limbs and heads flying as Robocop unleashes devastation. Additionally, the inclusion of an open-world area adds depth to the experience, allowing players to explore, interact with NPCs, and solve crimes. Robocop: Rogue City incorporates RPG elements, allowing players to level up Robocop's skills and unlock new abilities. The pseudo loot system adds a layer of customization, particularly with the iconic auto-9 gun, allowing players to tailor their experience to their playstyle.While the game excels in many aspects, there are a couple of downsides to note. The tone of the game occasionally feels too PG and light-hearted, missing some of the biting satire and darkness that made the original series iconic. Additionally, the facial animations and lip sync could be improved for a more immersive experience.Despite these flaws, Robocop: Rogue City is a hidden gem that deserves recognition. The dedication of the development team shines through, delivering an authentic Robocop experience that will delight fans of the franchise. It's a testament to what can be achieved by a smaller team relative to larger AAA titles, and I thoroughly enjoyed my time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game FEELS like Robocop, right down to the Janky 80's style movement to your character in game, with no crouch, no dodge, lean or jump buttons... in short, exactly what a Robocop game SHOULD be like.There's shortcomings, like a lack of a quick save meaning you have to reach a checkpoint before being able to leave the mission (too bad if kids wake up) and I encountered a game stopping bug in a sidequest where an NPC fell through the floor while blocking a doorway, requiring the entire mission to be restarted (goodbye hour of gameplay progress and quite a few good "chip" RNG rolls that I didn't luck out on a second time) But overall, the game is fun. Although perhaps not full-priced value. I'd recommend saving it for a christmas sale where it goes 50% off, and then definitely grab it.

_childDocuments_.review: 50/50 If you are a robocop fan, game can be enjoyable if you get past the shallow and repetitive gameplay. Game is plagued by a series of graphical issues and performance bugs. In only 17 hours of gameplay, I have had a fatal crash atleast a dozen times. Some npc's have been caught in a T pose, light stuttering, frame drops (not often, but they do happen)the Good: Robocop! Fun shooter elements and gore. Basic gameplay, don't expect anything like Doom.The Bad: While the graphical bugs aren't gamebreaking, they can get quite annoying such as stuttering, light flickering on npc's that make it look like they have christmas lights attached to them (not an exaggeration)The biggest peeve I have so far is the constant crashing.And I do mean constant, at seemingly random and extremely inconvenient times. Such as in the middle of a huge battle.Completely resetting your checkpoint and making it harder to recover since you are not given any chance to recover before you are immediately fired upon. ( I play on hard, so this is an issue)Game is still fun, but the gameplay, story, etc. are shallow and cliche, but that may be the running theme of this game. It is based entirely off of an 80's action movie.For what it is, it is a great homage to a great movie.This game is definitely fan service, and I have enjoyed it thus far, but that enjoyment is impeded upon though by the performance issues.**EDIT** After another 10 hours of play, I absolutely would not recommend this game in its current state. The crashes are even worse now, and I can not even finish my game. Crashes as soon as I try loading a save.I have a 4080, so the performance and crashing is not on my end.Even after updating my drivers, and trying to revalidate the game files. Nothing is working. So 30 hrs of gameplay probably just got ruined ,and there is not much replay value here to make me motivated to want to restart at this time.I would wait until game goes on sale, or is patched a few more times to make it worth paying for/playing in its current state.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Set right after the only robocop movies that can be considered good (admittedly they've all aged like milk by 2023 standards) Rogue City is a decent entry in an IP that has basically been dead for decades. If you want to follow the story completely though, you will need to watch those movies, the game doesn't try to explain the backstory at all.Overall it's a decent FPS game with some light RPG elements. It's not all that complex and it's pretty linear. It nails the aesthetic it was going for, although unfortunately it's held back by UE5's issue, namely stutters in some specific situations,  nanite causing pop-in (easily noticeable by just looking at the ground) and lumen (GI and reflections) being run at low resolutions which causes a lot of graphical noise and shimmering in some areas. These issues are pretty noticeable and  happen even with the relevant settings set to "Epic".If you liked RoboCop, you'll see this as a decent homage to the original movies. Otherwise this game might be a hit or miss.

_childDocuments_.review: You get to be Robocop - a slow walking, man-sized tank with a burst fire 9mm, shooting bad guys while the epic music plays. You also get to issue parking tickets and rescue cats from buildings. Don't expect a AAA experience from this game - the lack of budget shows in the form of dialogue mostly performed by characters in a standard idle pose, there's the occasional crash, there's poorly optimized scenes, there's the occasional bit of Polish text, brass ejecting the wrong way, etc.However, when the action kicks in, it's VERY good and you will forget the shortcomings.It's the game the Robocop movie fans were asking for, and it was developed by a team who are also clearly fans of the movies. Besides, they got Peter Weller to voice Robocop again - which explains the 50€ price tag. This game is worth buying.Hopefully they'll make an expansion for this.

_childDocuments_.review: Review - Score 8.5/10For a fan of the IP, this is just a fantastic game. It's not perfect (unlike the source material), but it has a lot of the spirit of the first two movies; it serves nostalgia in consistent fashion, and finds it's own brand of 80's inspired "cheese".This is not exactly a "boomer-shooter", but is definitely more akin to something like DOOM than a tactical or "modern" shooter e.g., CoD, Battlefield, etc. You're basically a walking tank, which is what RoboCop was always intended to be. The gunplay is fun, has weight, and is overall satisfying. The combat, and largely the game, gives off the impression of how your mind would imagine it would be like to "be" RoboCop.It's great that they secured Peter for RC's voice. Those are little details that go a long way for the target audience. Additionally, while all arms are serviceable, they (the devs) made sure nothing was quite as fun to shoot as the iconic auto-DE from the films.My overall criticisms can be summarized with "occasional jank and cheesiness, with some missions being much more interesting than others."If you like the IP, you'll love the game. It's a great tribute to the RC universe.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I never would've believed a RoboCop game can end up so great, but having it play like Deus Ex: Human Revolution (without stealth, crouch or jumping) + Mass Effect 1's simple skill tree (10 points per skill with specializations at 2-6-10), was a very inspired choice.Shooting feels great, there's dismemberment (with extra gore with a mod for the Auto-9) and the headshots are explosive.Exploration in a semi-open world is rewarded with bonus experience and every side quest is fun and interesting to do, especially the choices between justice and serving the public trust.There's a massive attention to detail with total fidelity to the movies, beautifully rendered in Unreal Engine 5 with all the bells & whistles (DLSS 3.5, FSR 2.2, Intel XeSS) and even areas which wouldn't make sense from a level design perspective, are there fully detailed because it just makes sense.It has a simple, yet intriguing story which helps provide either a wholesome experience or a bad Robo one, giving you a choice when it matters and whose effect can be seen in later missions.Sound design is good and on point, although it could use a little more precision on certain surfaces (like the watery ones due to Robo's stomping, there should be splashes of different sizes).Getting Peter Weller to reprise his role as the face and voice actor of RoboCop is a big bonus.RoboCop: Rogue City was an awesome experience with a good solid story, attention to detail in a semi-open world, a simple but effective skill system and Auto-9 modifications, beautiful graphics with plenty performance choices, good sound design, boosted by showing respect to the source material and Peter Weller as the original Alex Murphy/RoboCop.Sometimes simple is better and this game proves it.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: solid game that pays homage to the films. great story and nice gunplay, with only a few flawspros * gunplay and the skill tree systems are great. if youre doing everything, you can easily get around 40-50 skillpoints first playthrough.* story is great, the main characters are well made and their storylines feel fleshed out.* character development is also nice to see, especially for Murphy.cons* optimization was a little rough for me. i have a decent system and until i found a workaround to get decent dps, i had some major frame drops, especially during fights with several enemies (could have just been a me problem tbf).* the voice acting could have used a little work. you can clearly tell that they reused the same few voice actors for the majority of the game* the facial animations are pretty underwhelming for a game so recent. lip syncing can be atrocious at times and a lot of the character models are reusedstill, the game is pretty good and worth the price imo. the good things about this game outweigh the bad, and it was a fun experience overall.SCORE: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is a fantastic blast from the past, seamlessly blending the gritty charm of the classic 80s movie with modern gameplay and stunning visuals. Fans of the original RoboCop will appreciate the detailed homage to the iconic film, with a faithfully recreated Detroit that feels both nostalgic and immersive. The game captures the essence of being RoboCop—walking the line between man and machine, dishing out justice in thrilling first-person combat, and interacting with a city that feels alive and dangerous.The developers have done an impressive job of honoring the legacy of RoboCop, even with the challenge of lost cast members from the original trilogy. The voice acting, atmosphere, and soundtrack all evoke that retro-futuristic 80s vibe, paying respect to the film’s tone and characters while still delivering something fresh for modern players. Whether it’s the gritty storytelling, intense gunplay, or the sense of stepping right into one of the most memorable sci-fi franchises of the past, RoboCop: Rogue City is a love letter to fans and a rewarding experience for newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: as people are saying, the atmosphere is great and it is a very faithful extension of the robocop universe. The dialogue is funny and the satire is there in good form. The problem is just that the gunplay is very meh. I get that you move slowly as robocop, so that's not really an issue for immersion, however every fight you get into just ends up being a maze in a warehouse or an industrial basement. Robocop's gun, while having unlimited ammo, is quite impotent, taking about three bursts to the chest for your average baddy. The ragdolls and damage modelling are ok to subpar. It's 2024 and we still get these cartoonishly weightless ragdolling where someone flying backwards looks like a dead beetle with his arms knotting up in front of his chest while his legs do the same. You just feel like a slow protagonist from any fps in the early 2000s. It's severely boring unfortunately and it seems clear to me that most people rate it so well for how it handles the source material (also pretty standard gunfights in that, so it's pretty on-brand, I guess).
