I'm primarily and MMO and Souls-likes gamer nowadays and I couldn't put this down. The story works and fits with the world. It's a way better follow-up to RoboCop 2 than we actually got and it feels like it was made by people who care. Everything you want to see and experience is there. Yeah ED-209 is a giant bullet sponge but he always was :PHonestly struggling to think of a better love letter to fans of a particular property since the War/Fall of Cybertron Transformers games and aside from a Souls-Like Highlander ever being made, I can't ask for more. This is a game made for people like me to fangasm and it does its job.One weak spot for me was I struggled with any need to diversify my weapon usage aside from weapons actually used in the movies that I wanted to use. _childDocuments_.review: Between RoboCop Rogue City and Terminator Resistance, Teyon has shown a level of caring and adherence to the original stories as these two movies-turned-games have.  This game takes place shortly after the events of the second RoboCop movie, and for anyone that is a fan of them you're going to have a lot of nostalgia points throughout your playthrough.Now, this game isn't breaking any new ground in the FPS genre.  The actual game elements are fairly generic with a skill tree for both Robo and his Auto-9, AI that doesn't adapt, and no high speed antics like you find in most modern games.  What you get instead of a chance to really feel like you are Alex Murphy in a way no other game to day has even come close to.  Also, it's kind of fun to be a slow plodding tank with many guns and other fun ways to lower the population of Detroit.  I haven't found the game to be terribly difficult, but what you have here is a game that is a better RoboCop 3 than the movie could have been.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I loved Rouge City despite it's flaws and certain lack of polish in areas. Seeing Robocop getting some refreshed attention was fantastic.Game length is decent enough, though after the credits I was left wanting more story simply for how much I had enjoyed to game up to that point. Gameplay is pretty easily broken down into 3 parts: walking your beat, investigation, and combat. It's a simple recipe that works very well together while helping to break up the pacing a bit. Even if some sequences were awkwardly too short in the middle of combat. There is a lot of map recycling however, which can feel like padding to some extent, but given the small dev team I doubt they had the resources to make more unique maps than just the same Downtown area at different times of the day.Walking the beat can help to even the pacing a bit but it can get sloooow. I get that Robocop is a literal walking tank of a cyborg, and I don't have any issues with moving around Downtown Detroit on foot patrol or any other level for that matter... just wish there was an "auto walk" button. Robo can't run, more like a brisk jog, but he doesn't run out of stamina doing so, at least not that I noticed.Investigation sequences are dead easy, given how Robo can just scan his environment and find highlighted clues.Combat is also pretty simple. Shoot at the perp until he goes down. Some enemies do have weakspots, but not many. Robocop can use an array of weaponry that can be found in a level, although you will need to keep them stocked with ammunition. It's only towards the end of the game where Robo will have access to weapons besides the odd shotgun and assault rifle. However, the default Auto-9, which can be modified/upgraded through the course of the game, is more than sufficient for 90% of the combat encounters you'll have. Also helps you get infinite ammo for it as well, significantly reducing the consequences of missing. Enemies will occasionally try to take cover, but often don't and just stand there. Many can be bullet sponges, but Rouge City does allow the player to really feel like a walking tank as most small arm fire does negligible damage (at least on normal difficulty). Only when Robo gets surrounded or overwhelmed by a horde of baddies will your HP take a hit. OCP recovery charges act as med-kits and you can also heal from circuit breakers, I only found myself a bit short on HP in a couple sequences, and those were in the end-game sections.Robocop has a full skill tree that can enhance his capabilities. Simply performing your duties as a police officer by seizing drugs to issuing parking tickets will award you XP. Making sure to do everything in each area will also result in a higher analysis score back at DPD HQ and will award more upgrade points. I found investing in armor, vitality, engineering, deduction, and (possibly) psychology to be the most beneficial. These skills can also help in moments of dialogue.Overall the game from a structural standpoint is great, no real complaints at all. But Rouge City does stumble in a few other departments.The visuals are a mixed bag, on one hand the environments look fantastic, but the NPC models are somewhat lifeless. The stilted and jerky animations work fine for Robocop, whose own model is superb, but everyone else doesn't meet the same level of polish. The poor animations in dialogue sequences break immersion pretty badly.Voice acting is also mixed, Peter Weller returns to voice Robocop again, and he does a stand-out job doing so. Same thing with most of the other central NPCs. But the enemies and some of the secondary characters don't feel as well done, and it's also pretty immersion breaking when every single enemy of each faction sounds the same. Every Torchhead for example sounds like they've been done by one person and it's impossible to ignore it. The other sounds I don't have any issues with, although I really was hoping the Auto-9 would have sounded like it did in the films.I really did like how Rouge City put a background internal struggle with Alex Murphy reliving his past as a bit of extra "flavor" to the story. Though quite a bit of the time these devolved into classic Horror Game level manipulation tropes that I've seen done to death. Still, it was a nice change of pace and another layer of detail and storytelling which is always welcome.Rouge City is the epitome of a "Middle Shelf Game" and it's not trying to pretend it's anything else. Just another bit of proof that you don't need an overpaid CEO, several hundred devs and a massive budget with shareholder meetings promising to ship 10 million copies to make a good game. Now just need to see that same treatment to Judge Dredd... (preferably the Karl Urban portrayal).

_childDocuments_.review: BOTTOM LINE: This is definitely not a Triple A title but it's still pretty fun. Worth $20, but no more.THE GOOD: Developers did a GREAT job capturing the look and feel of the Robocop Movies. The city is dirty, the people are hopeless, the cops are worn out, the criminals are over the top. The story is well written and would make a decent movie on its own. Like the movies, it compares the humanity of Alex Murphy who is supposed to be the cold, unfeeling machine with the inhumanity of the OCP who treat him like an asset and refer to him as "it."IN BETWEEN: Had to put this as a middle ground because its a mixed bag. This is a really good Robocop simulator. When you walk around, you are heavy and ponderous, just like Robocop. Sprinting isn't very fast because he isn't very fast. On the other hand, you don't have to worry about stamina because he never gets tired. THE BAD: Gunplay is kinda boring. As mentioned before, you're Robocop. You think some tweaked out street toughs are going to take you down? Well, they can sadly. You're like a squishy tank. Can't jump, can't crouch. You can take cover by standing behind things and you can sidestep to be a harder target. It'll take a lot of shots for you to have to worry about health and most battles are over before you run out of healing items. I've only come across a handful of guns and none of them are real improvements over your stock gun.Graphics are...okay. It feels like playing Vampire The Masquerade: Bloodlines, only in a much better engine. The world looks good, lots of shadows and reflections and lens flares. But the animation on characters is right out of 2005. Lots of bad lip sync, everyone moves their head and hands too much when they talk. ALL OF THE BADGUYS SOUND THE SAME. Every single one of them all talk like mohawk leather-jacket characters from a 90's cartoon; that high pitched frantic screaming voice. The "investigations" are kind of neat and add something to break up gameplay but there's no real depth there. Arkham games did it way better. Overall it's a very linear open world game. You can go where you want and do missions in whatever order you want, but everything is in a straight line.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend RoboCop: Rogue City. Take my words with a grain of salt, though. The game consists of levels you get to explore, that are also recycled throughout the campaign. Biggest example here being Downtown Detroit. I imagined the game to be open world, but it's basically just diet open world. Biggest highlight has to be the story, combat and investigation. The shooting is extremely good and when you aim it has the lock-on effect just like in the films. There have been moments where the lock-on didn't happen and I wasn't sure if it was a bug or an intended feature through damage taken. The ingame models for everyone except for RoboCop look pretty bland and are recycled for any non-story related characters. Performance can be an issue with some bugs/glitches that can and probably will impede progression. There are ingame fixes for them, but usually result in you having to reload a chapter in the story costing time and progress. Until then we can only hope the devs get on it and don't make this game into an abandonware. Investigation is pretty fun, where you scan certain objects to get very interesting details about chemicals and some cool effects to help solve a case. It can be very annoying sometimes as there are certain moments where you have to look for where you can scan and the only way to find the scan locations is to have the mouse hover over the spot exactly. Over some time of playing, you'll get experience points to put into RoboCop. They give bonuses to certain aspects plus, if you put enough into one column you'll unlock an ability/passive which can be very fun to mess around with. If you are a big fan of RoboCop, I'm sure you'll still enjoy it quite alot despite all of the flaws present in the game. If you aren't a fanatic, just wait for the game to go on discount, Because: "I'll buy that for a dollar!"7/10 I will have it a 9 or 10/10 depending on if the game gets some patches it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop: Rogue City --- Most PlayRobocop: Rogue City is more than just a game; it's a riveting journey back into a nostalgic yet futuristic Detroit, where technology and justice entwine in a battle against crime. From the moment you don the iconic steel armor of Robocop, you're thrust into a narrative that is as engaging as it is reminiscent of the original films, especially with Peter Weller reprising his role, lending an authentic touch that fans will appreciate.The game is a visual spectacle with its cyberpunk aesthetics, bringing Old Detroit to life in a way that's both fresh and familiar. The bustling cityscape, filled with neon lights and towering skyscrapers, sets a perfect stage for the high-octane action that unfolds.At the heart of Robocop: Rogue City is its gameplay, which is an exhilarating blend of combat, investigation, and moral choices. The ability to navigate through different scenarios either with a stern hand or a voice of reason adds a layer of depth, making every encounter feel consequential. The inclusion of various side quests and the impact of your choices on the overall narrative creates a rich, immersive experience.The arsenal at your disposal, led by the classic Auto 9 gun, makes combat satisfying and robust. The upgradeable abilities add a layer of strategy, allowing for a tailored approach to different challenges. Every shootout is a thrilling dance of bullets, strategy, and justice.The storyline is compelling, filled with twists that keep you invested. The characters, both new and returning, are well fleshed out, adding to the emotional weight of the narrative. The plot unfolds at a pace that keeps you hooked, with enough suspense to keep you guessing and enough action to keep your adrenaline pumping.Robocop: Rogue City doesn't just rest on the laurels of its storied franchise; it builds upon it, creating a modern-day cyberpunk saga that is both a tribute to the past and a bold step into the future. This game is not just a trip down memory lane, but a well-crafted narrative adventure that stands tall on its own merits.In conclusion, Robocop: Rogue City is a masterful blend of action, narrative, and nostalgia. It's a game that respects its roots while offering a modern, engaging, and satisfying gaming experience. Whether you're a long-time fan of Robocop or new to the franchise, Robocop: Rogue City is a captivating adventure that is well worth your time.

Objectively speaking, the game is hardly difficult, with harder difficulties only allowing for more enemy damage, aggression and health. It's mildly repetitive and enemy variation is minimal, but the writing and story make it fairly easy to ignore, assuming you really like the RoboCop movie's style. The only thing I found a bit unsatisfying was how the antagonists are dealt with, spoiler: TL;DR: It's a perfect and loyal RoboCop game, but only a somewhat decent action-shooter otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: For context when discussing performance:R7 5800X3D | 32GB 3600MHz | RTX 3080 | 2560*1440Performance & Technical:Unreal 5 goes hard - both in visuals and in its technical demands. The game was ran at Epic details, high quality Lumen reflections and DLSS quality. Robocop is using Nanite and Lumen, the latter part is using software lumen for reflections layered on SSR which actually looks good for the most part. Nanite geo is also really impressive, there are shots in this AA game that knock AAA games on their ass. It’s also, at the same time, clear to see the lower budget assets of the game like the character animations and models as well as animation work in general. Performance wise, it’s running fair I’d say considering the tech at use. There are no stutters to speak of as I believe the game is using the UE5 JIT compiler as well as a pre-compilation step, which is not visible when you first boot the game. It just stutters a while in the menu and the CPU usage shoots up a bit while the shaders are compiled. Actual frame rates could be better but it seems to be fair and you can also disable Lumen for a pretty sizeable gain in performance. There are a couple of rough spots where frame rates tank a little bit bellow 60, furthermore, as all UE5 games run noticeably better with upscaling due to the nature of Nanite and due to the fact that Lumen is on, I’d hoped for a little better DLSS implementation. As it stands, most of the time DLSS looks great and runs a lot better than native but has clear issues with ghosting and SSR resolve. Now, this seems to be more of an NVIDIA AA issue as DLAA also has similar issues but upscaling exacerbates the issues somewhat. Overall, an at times, amazing looking game with some clear issues with IQ and some rather heavy yet fair requirements.Gameplay & Narrative:Yeah so it all boils down to shooting dudes in the face. The game has some skill trees which can introduce some fun new abilities in combat like dashing into people or deflecting bullets of certain surfaces which adds a bit of spice to the slaughter. The main pistol can also be upgraded to change its characteristics ranging from clear changes like full auto modes to boring stuff like faster reloads. There are some interactive environmental elements in combat but it’s fairly simple. It’s point and shoot but it does feel very satisfying due to a combination of good audible and visual feedback. Melons pop, blood flies, the guns sound meaty and it looks really nice for the most part. The game also introduces some side activity content ranging from goofy satire that series is known for like taking complaints to solving goofy yet gnarly murders. I will say, most of the side content thus far isn’t all too impressive but it gets the job done. It’s the main missions that keep you going. Ultimately though, there isn’t much here that you probably haven’t experienced elsewhere but what is here is of, mostly, good quality and the world of Robocop is very well realized. I’ve got no real nostalgia for the movies and so I’m sort of seeing it for what it is and I have to say I like what Teyon has accomplished here. Even if it is very par for the course and at times sluggish due to some lackluster side activities.TLDR:Robocop serves some, at times, amazing looking visuals coupled with some not so great AA quality animation & facial work while running fair with upscaling. There’s a lot of fun to be had even for non Robocop fans looking for some mindless, bloody shooting - driven by a mostly enjoyable story.I recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: It's impressive how much Teyon has improved since their attempt at a Rambo video game, which had to be among the worst video games of that decade. They showed a lot of improvement with their Terminator adaptation and have become even better now with this version of RoboCop, which pays a lot of homage to fans of the franchise and, surprisingly, actually stays accurate to the source material. And I bought this video game solely because it seemed to stay true to the roots of RoboCop. Yes, RoboCop is actually unapologetically white male as he should be. There's none of those blatant woke tropes that we often see in modern productions these days where people have to virtue signal every time you walk around a corner or load into a new cutscene. As they like to say, it feels good to be represented for once.The game is just pure fun and carnage as video games should be. Minor destructible environments such as being able to chip away at pillars, lots of gore which is reminiscent to the bloody mess that was the F.E.A.R franchise, and even a morality system where prominent NPCs will actually remember actions that you make or dialogue that you choose in response. There's a lot of content which surprised me, as I thought this was going to be a very short video game and that it might be too overpriced at $50 USD. It is still kind of short, though, so for a lot of people, $50 USD full price might seem too steep of a price tag for a singleplayer video game. But somewhere around 50 quests, split somewhat evenly between main missions and side missions? A fun RPG system that allows you to invest points into a character build as well as being able to upgrade your pistol efficiency? And a semi-open world where you have a lot of opportunity for exploration and easter egg hunting? That's pretty good for a AA video game title.You don't need to spend the extra $12 USD or so on the current DLC as these are just cosmetic packs, but I'd recommend doing so just to support these developers in their journey to AAA status, as Robocop is a step in the right direction and I am holding onto hope that they can only continue to go up ever since their Rambo video game. On a sale? It's worth the buy even more so, especially for shooter game fans and Robocop fans in general. Maybe a Judge Dredd video game can be next.Things to dislike:-While I love the gunplay and the gore, the ragdolls need massive improvement. It is not at all realistic to the degree that you'd find from games like Red Dead Redemption and Grand Theft Auto. Corpses are constantly contorted in an unrealistic way. I love ragdoll physics but the physics here are immersion breaking.-The psychology path in the skill tree needs reworking. It is fundamentally useless and a waste of points currently. Unless it was just bugged for me. I almost always focus on maximizing the skills that allows me access to more dialogue choices such as with Fallout, but with this game, you don't actually need to do anything but put two points into it to access ALL special dialogue choices, which are very minimal. I think I did every quest and talked to as many NPCs as I could find and I only remember seeing around three or so special "psychology" dialogue choices. It sounds important when you are researching the skills tab, but it truly isn't. As of now, I don't think there's any way to reset skills points, either. Which also needs to be added as it's become the norm in modern gaming for players to be given the freedom to explore different builds without needing to restart from the very beginning.-There needs to be a "new game+" mode so that people can re-experience the video game with the skills that they've unlocked. Otherwise, XP needs to be given in greater values so that you level up more before the conclusion of the video game. There simply isn't enough to do in this game to maximize all of your character's skills. Crime evidence is littered throughout the maps, for example, and gives you a point value for collecting it but for many areas of the game, these points are redundant unless you have the quest for collecting a certain amount of crime evidence items, and this side quest doesn't exist in every map. I'd suggest converting the arbitrary points value of these items into XP points instead. It'd encourage players to find more of the secrets as well, because those stashes are otherwise pointless to look for since you are not actually being rewarded for it. -The music isn't all that great, especially during some of the more action packed sequences of the game. You'd expect something way better than what they used. Something to get you pumped as a robotic cop dispensing deathly justice to all of the criminals and thugs. The music here seemed more like something you'd hear from a Spider-Man game as you are swinging around the city or something. It's more peaceful, relaxing music rather than something that you'd expect to play during a major boss battle.-The game needs a manual save feature or better auto-saving. I had to quit playing at some point and when I came back to it, I was like 10+ minutes behind from where I signed out. I can only imagine how far back you can go if you actually die. -Difficulty is a bit too easy, but that's just a personal gripe. Even on expert mode, I only died twice. And both instances were not even to the bosses, but because I was distracted by something else going on around me and looked away from my HP bar momentarily. Other than that, I really did enjoy the 14 or so hours I put into the game. I got all of the achievements in that time frame, and playing it on an easier difficulty probably means that you can beat it even faster so take that as you will for its price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: It's jank. It's got awkward voice acting. It has performance problems.And it's the most fun game I played all yearFor those unfamiliar with Teyon, they're a AA studio previously known for Nintendo DS shoverlware and Rambo The Video Game, an on rails shooter that was one of the worst games of 2014. Years later they released Terminator Resistance, a Terminator FPS that gained a cult like following. But this, this is their biggest, and in my opinion, best game yet. This is a game made with passion, with respect for the license it's based off of, and a game that is just plain old fun. Hell they even got Peter Weller to reprise his role as Robocop.It is a Robocop FPS, so naturally, you move slow. But that doesn't matter, since while you are slow, you are strong and powerful, combined with the fact YOU HAVE ZERO RECOIL. Who needs to hide behind cover? Just walk out into the open and shoot the dirtbags. Or better idea, pick something up and throw it at them. Or hell, JUST PICK THE CRIMINAL UP AND THROW THEM! It's so good and every gun packs a punch and is satisfying to use. Enemies are balanced around the fact that you're Robocop, so they'll have certain parts protected or will be armed with different tools to counter you. For example: Some enemies will wear helmets that make them immune to headshots...but not immune to nutshots (There's even an achievement for killing someone with a nutshot.)Even the writing of the game is top notch. It's clearly AA quality but they make the most out of what they're capable of doing, and despite the jankness in conversations you're still invested in the story. In fact your choices actually matter throughout the entire game and actually change the course of the story.Buy it. It's honestly one of the top 10 games of the year. Teyon outdid themselves and went above and beyond to create a FPS where you are fully immersed as Robocop. I hope we can get some updates to fix the performance issues, New Game+ and a chapter select, and maybe a Mac port down the road and Steam Deck verification. Can't wait to see what license Teyon works with next.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics wise, its rather amazingly done. Gameplay is fun, story is...interesting for sure. Really like the open world parts in between missions, and being able to make somewhat impactful choices. All in all, as a fan of the franchise, this takes place in the span of time between RoboCop 2 and 3, with a lot of mentions littered throughout of it, especially 3 right at the end parts. As an entry to the RoboCop universe, would say this is a great one. As a game, sure its solid but I have a few primary gripes with no manual saving and human enemies being insanely tanky, taking even 50 cal shots to the chest with no problem. The Mercs are especially terrible with this, especially the 'Specialist' units. For those, its easier to channel your inner Terminator and just blow out their kneecaps.With those, it does lean heavily on skills and upgrading your Auto-9's PCB to have a few for each use, be they clearing mobs or going for boss fights where you need a lot of punch. Still does realistically give you the Auto-9 staying very much useful through the entire thing. All in all, story is alright. Not great, but still fairly solid. Are a lot of parts that are just bothersome, like bomb defusal where if you mess up then be prepared to load the last autosave and hopefully was just before you started.Does have its issues, but its still fairly well rounded imo. And having a wide variety of weapons, including the friggin Cobra Cannon is a big nostalgic grin.

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rouge City is an excellent game. Not perfect but excellent. It does the source material justice and adapts it neatly to an Ego-Shooter with story and “crime solving” elements. The Story combines elements of the movies RoboCop 1 and 2, alters them and reuses them but without adapting them too much and thereby disfiguring them. You play in the future as envisioned in 1980s, what means the future tech also looks that way.  I found the atmosphere they created by this nearly perfect.  The pacing is good, the shooting sequences are interrupted with other tasks and the story is told in a great way.However, as stated in the beginning, the game has its flaws: A minor one is the fact, that they reused some NPC models to often. This is fine with the enemies but some NPC especially guards in the prison and others should have more variation. Another minor one is that your main weapon, RoboCops legendary Auto-9 is too powerful once its gets the Update that makes it unnecessary to reload. Its funny but it is imbalanced since it takes away a lot of the remaining dangers that come with reloading (you are a walking tank anyway). Personally, my biggest issue was the fact that the world does not feel lived in, especially in Down Town in Old Detroit and at the police station. The developers did a great job creating scenes and atmosphere, but once you walked by, listened to the dialog, walked on and then return a little while later  and everyone remains as they were for all the time, it simply seems artificial. For example, there is a guy at the gas station at one at your visits to town, that kneels before it and checks something. Neat little detail… until you notice that he is doing this for eternity. Here more alteration and maybe also some “random” crime to stop would have been nice.But these are minor things that hinder the emersions at certain moments. Otherwise, it is a great game with great atmosphere. So, grab it when it is on sale, load the Auto-9 (as long as you have to) and slowly walk your way to justice. *And do not forget: “Dead or alive, you are coming with me…”*Seriously though, Robo is a slow-moving machine.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: Short and sweet game that really does a stellar job of putting you in the role of Alex Murphy and adds a surprising level of depth when looking into the psychology and trauma of just how it could be when one becomes a Robocop. Gunplay is arcady but fun. Easy game overall, but is loyal to the power fantasy. Good fan service. Disappointing boss fight and underused soundtrack. 8.5/10In detail: I was cautious when starting out with this one. I was worried it would be lame, but actually I grew to love it very quickly. The shooting felt simplistic at first but it gets better. I really like how you roleplay as a cop, albeit a robotic one. Giving tickets, fines, taking evidence, confiscating drugs, letting people off with a warning (or not) helping out your fellow colleagues and patrolling your streets. It was great, and because of this it means you explore a lot of the areas you play in. The fan service is on point! If you watched the classic films then you will not be disappointed. Positives:It's more than a dumb shooter. At time when going into the trauma and PTSD of Murphy it becomes a bit like FEAR with a bit of Max Payne (the nightmare scenes). this was great as it really makes you see the suffering Robocop goes through. Power fantasy! once you get the hang of the controls you really start to smash and shoot people in ways that never get old. Paul Weller! OG voice actor is back to reprise his role! Great with immersion.Dialogue options: Not sure how much they really effect the ending but it was an appreciated feature.Areas: The game doesn't have many, but I loved the police station, lots of attention to detail given and it was nice taking a break between missions and checking out the posters on the wall, missing people, wanted posters, pics of old detroit etc.Negatives:Boss battles are not designed well. You basically have to cheese them as if you fight properly you will die.Voice acting and character assets: They put a lot of attention into Robocop and got Paul Weller, but the other main side characters did not get the same treatment and it shows, both when you hear them and see them. The other NPCs are also quite samey. It's a double AA studio so ok, but still it's a noticeable thing.Soundtrack: Robocop has an iconic soundtrack and it's a shame how criminally underutilised this is. There are moments where the sound cuts out and you just have silence. Not good.Arenas: There are about a half dozen one off areas you go to, but for most part the downtown detroit hub gets overused, granted there is a lot to explore and see in it, but it gets overused. Again, AA studio I know, but it's noticeable!

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop has always been my ultimate passion and the main reason I entered robotics. Loved the films even the 3rd one and of course hated the 2014 one (it never existed). I have played all the good old games from the arcade game to the Robocop vs Terminator and now Rogue City.The story is typically a 80's action story, it is made to please that generation and it does a great job.The Robocop personality although the act is done by Peter Weller but it is mostly closer to Robocop The Future of Law Enforcement TV series than the 1987 movie. I personally did not like the 2nd movie much but this story is between 2nd and right before 3rd movie (I highly suggest watch all the films again before playing).Robocop in the TV series had more objectives like helping a cat + finding a thief and stuff like that so if you are a fan of the TV series this game actually puts you in the shoes of that Robocop not the 1987 Robocop. There are so many cheesy objectives which is very relevant to the TV series than the movies.I finished the game on maximum difficulty and it took around 14 hours, I managed to max out 3 skills completely. So if you are worried about the length of game not allowing you to max out your skills then there is nothing to worry about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop Rouge City is the game incarnation of the movie. You are Robo, it's light hearted but lots of action. It's easy, and short, not really any boss fight to remember. But the game is still good, a feel good game. Very arcady. Once you know this you are an extreme killing machine, even on the hardest difficulty. The upgrade mechanism for your gun is fun and can be used for different play styles. To make it harder I played on hardest difficulty and rolled a dice which skill to pick when leveling. It made the game somewhat harder, but was still easy compared to many other games. About the only real con is the fetch quests which are few but it just breaks the action.Buy if you want to be Robocop for 8 hours, do not buy if you want a deep 50 hour game.

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop Rouge City is a game that is not to be slept on. As basic as the gameplay looks, there is an RPG element to it. You have the freedom to build Robocop how you like, very tanky, extreme precision, super detective or all of the above. The choice is yours. The story takes place after Robocop 2 so it is a perfect setup for a Robocop game. There is a ton of nostalgia in this game. From characters to locations to one liners from the movies. I was really surprised by the length of the game as well. Everytime I thought the game was about to end there was a new level to tackle. The game looks stunning! I have a pretty decent setup but this was the only game I really had to  tweak settings for it to hold a stable 60fps. Some open world elements where you can do side objectives and there are instances as well that are linear. I played on the hardest difficulty available when you started the game and didn't find it too much of a challenge once I upgraded the Auto-9.The talk about this game is accurate, it is fun, entertaining and a real nod to the movies and the lore. I waited for a sale but you will get your $$$ worth for sure, especially if you are a Robocop fan. "Dead or Alive you're coming with me"

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good!The shooting in the game is SO MUCH FUN. Blowing away enemies is so satisfying that I would say that alone is worth the price I paid for the game. I found a bug that honestly made the game even more fun to play. I upgraded my auto-9 using a PCB with full auto, then did so again with a different PCB that had no reloads and it was like having a minigun. It seriously was so amazing to do and I PRAY they never patch it because I might drop in every now and again just to shoot up bad guys lol. The game isn't extremely long, it took me 16 hours to 100% the game with achievements. Be wary that it is NOT open world free roam in the way most would interpret it. You will play in one location at a time and do things within the area, divided by different segments. Me not realizing this was completely my fault and made me surprised when I played the game initially but I think it's still good regardless and accomplishes what it sets out to do. It's very much story driven and gives you the ability to make choices which may affect some aspects of the game, but I can't personally speak to what those choices truly change. The game does have a new game + which maybe I'll try eventually, but I feel for the most part I got what I wanted out of the game. I'm definitely dropping in again to shoot bad guys though. 10/10 S tier.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say that they did an awesome job on this game.   Playing as Robocop  was such much fun and the details in the environments definitely nailed the 80's look.   They made each area full of clutter and items that made the game look real and the music really made the mood when taking out the bad guys.   While playing you will upgrade skills which was hard to decide on and you upgrade your gun.   The gun upgrade was rather unique in that you have computer boards with chips on it.   You have to find the right chips to get a board upgraded without hitting the negative trees.   One board you get later gives constant firing and one gives no reload, so you have to choose which board works best for your gameplay.  Your auto cannon is the best weapon of the game due to unlimited ammo and upgrades, but there are some guns with limited ammo that do more damage like assault rifles, rocket launchers, grenade launches, and sniper rifles.   They did come in handy in many situations.   Most importantly the game has many choices that can affect the ending and you see how Robocop struggles with being human and machine.   I truly hope they make a sequel, because I want to play more :-)

_childDocuments_.review: It starts out really strong but quickly fades into repetitive boredom. The game designer was able to nail the motif and feel of the movie; however, everything from gameplay to animation, mechanics, voice acting are all lacking. Once you play the opening sequence, that's pretty much the rest of the game. There's no variety. The side mission is a disgrace to side mission; more like gap fillers from getting signatures to going up to the car and press a button to issue a ticket. I couldn't sit through the rest of the game play after what it seemed like a never ending grind. The graphics is great. But this feels more like an awesome demo than a full game. I commend the indie devs who was able to nail the motif and feel of the game that brought back a lot of nostalgia from the past. However, this is a game that just seem very unpolished and desperately need more talent and funding. I would recommend picking this up for $10 just for kicks during the holidays.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is better than it has any right to be.I've seen the Robocop films, but not a superfan, don't remember any of the characters aside from the main character, and I didn't mind the reboot. That's what you're dealing with here.That said, there are a couple of key things that really stood out to me here:*I'm just down for a solid single-player FPS game with strong story and some RPG elements. Deus Ex et al and Prey 2017 are amongst my favourite games of all time. This kinda ticks that box (albeit with a much stronger emphasis on just shooting stuff than either of those - this is NOT an immersive sim, although it adopts some ideas from that genre).*The RPG elements mean there appears to be some scope for replayability, and for me to let the nerd brain kick in and work out how to min/max. Turbo nerd yo.*This thing oozes love for the source material. I'm sure there are a million references passing me by, but I can tell they're there. This feels like a game that loves winking and nodding at people in the know, and while I'm not one of them, I also just kinda enjoy playing a title that has some love put into it.I'm coming to this well after release, it seems super solid tech wise. I've had no crashes, smooth frame rate although it started to chug after an extended session so I restarted the game in case of a memory leak. Playing on Hard which seems to have a level of challenge but I also fear (now that I'm several hours in) that I'm probably not too far off feeling OP, which, in a Robocop game, is kind of the point. A textbook example for all existing IP games to look to, especially when they don't have a AAA budget. Really well executed.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it took me about 15 hours to complete this game. I enjoyed it - short, but sweet. For fans of the original movies, I agree with most reviewers that this is a must-buy, especially if on offer. The dialogue by Peter Weller is worth the purchase alone - it really feels like the original Robocop.Pros+ Its Robocop+ It is authentic in nearly every way from OCP to voice acting by original stars+ The shooting is sufficiently satisfying+ Graphics improved after update and you can now use DLSS+ It feels like a final movie that we never hadCons- You have to kill ED 209 three times in total- Some of the pickup weapons are awful, such as the early assault rifle- The perks/skills system doesn't feel like it truly impacts a playthrough- Levels/new areas cause loading screens- Your Detroit patrol area is used multiple times (same map) as is OCP HQ twiceIdeally, the team would add some form of 'Instant Action' to give you something to do after completing the campaign. Some might also want multiplayer but for me it would just be another excuse to be Robocop.

_childDocuments_.review: I am pretty fond of 80s scifi movies and RoboCop is one of my favorites.This game does a beautiful job of capturing the spirit of the movie and allowing you to explore it as the player.As for gameplay, it can get a little repetitive at times. The game bounces back and forth between what I'd call "Story Zones" and "Combat Zones."In "Story Zones," you're free to wander the map, discover hidden items and bonuses, pick up side quests, and interact with NPCs through fully-voiced dialog options.In "Combat Zones," the maps are much more linear and you move down hallways from one room to the next. In these maps, the game feels reminiscent of arcade shooters. You're RoboCop; you're big and slow. You'll come around the corner into a new room where all the bad guys are posted behind cover. You have to either post up and shoot as they pop out; or get strategic and maneuver around their cover, using throwable items or your plethora of unlockable abilities.The game is generous with their skill points, allowing you to upgrade your systems pretty well. But the Auto-9 upgrade system is much more dynamic than I expected from this little game. You can swap out motherboards, each with different possibilities. You then collect chips by exploring the world and can use them to unlock or enhance the board's stats. It pays to take the time to look into it and periodically swap out chips or boards for better ones. I also found myself swapping motherboards mid-mission based on what challenge I was facing.The story was fun and kept my interest. Your choices do have impact, but some are completely nonconsequential. Some characters' stories change based on how you treated them or handled their questline.The biggest gripe I had with the game was the lack of manual saving. The game only saves when you enter a new zone or complete a quest. This means once you sit down, you're committed to playing for a while. There were definitely a couple nights where I wasn't sure I'd have time to complete a mission, so I'd have to just skip RoboCop that day.At the end of the day, this is definitely a game for RoboCop fans. As a game on its own, I'm not sure there's quite enough there to warrant picking it up without that interest. But if you like the original movies, it's a must have.I've beaten it, and I find myself wanting to play more, but there's not much replayability without just starting over. I'd love to see more added, but time will tell.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I came for the 80's/90's action hero antics, and i stayed to collect signatures on a get-well card for a fellow officer.It's not quite Yakuza-levels of subversion of expectations, but i do love how quirky this game can be.There's far more world-and-character-building than i was expecting, which admittedly slows down the pace quite a bit at times, but i do like how immersive it gets.Oh, those cool 80's/90's action hero antics are also there. Looks absolutely gorgeous, too. And they have the proper theme. And Peter Weller himself does Murphy's voice. And there's tons of throwbacks to the movies. Yeah, get this. Not buying this game would be a crime, citizen. :p
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: In this era, where so-called 'writers' massacre the existing lore to introduce their own agendas, it is a breath of fresh air to see a studio go the extra mile to stay consistent with the canon lore. The overall setting is an amazing reconstruction of the late 80s-90s.Playing as Robocop feels exactly as you'd expect - the character is slow and steady, and has the firepower and durability to match. You can also customize Robocop, upgrading his stats and unlocking more skills along the way. His default weapon, the Auto-9, can also be further upgraded - eventually becoming pretty much your go-to weapon for almost all situations.There are a number of side characters with interesting questlines of their own, with fairly rewarding conclusions if you make the right choices.The music is just great - pretty much faithful to the original movie soundtracks.The graphics aren't all that amazing for a modern game, but everything else more than makes up for it.If you liked the Robocop series, or just want to play a shooter featuring someone other than the usual fast+frail characters, then this is a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: By the end, Robocop: Rogue City felt like the product of Ewe Boll deciding to try something new and turn a movie into a computer game.Terribly boring by the end. You see everything the game has to offer in the first hour.They say this is an old-school shooter? Well, the AI functions like it's from the 90's so in that sense it is.The characters and plot are some of the worst I've seen in a game. They try to be self aware by poking fun at the tropes they rely on, but it's clear they were just incredibly lazy.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful and fun game made by fans and for fans of Robocop. 9 hours of an intense main campaign and 20 if you intend to do all the secondary ones, which include police investigation and endearing moments based the lore of the franchise. Really faithful to the spirit and the movie of the 80s. Teyon has really outdone himself since they made Terminator Resistance, which wasn't half bad at all either. Firing the Auto-9 on evil criminals scum is a real pleasure.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: In the first 5 minutes I shot a guy's arm off as he was throwing a grenade so the grenade fell at his feet, next to his severed arm, and he blew up.Then later I snatched a guy off of a motorcycle and threw him into another guy on a motorcycle and then picked up that first guy's motorcycle and threw it at the two dudes so they blew up.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Just a great, old school first person shooter. Turn your brain off and have fun shooting baddies. Never watched the movies until recently but I was happy on how close the developers stuck to the source material, Pure fan service! You really feel like an unstoppable force,  Graphics are amazing, high amounts of detail indoors and outside.Patrolling the streets of old Detroit at night feels immersive and really sets the mood of a gritty, crime ridden, run down city. No micro transactions, season passes, or woke nonsense.Only con i had was the price was a little steep so wait for a sale.10/10 would throw a CRT monitor at criminals again!
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR You have spent more money on worse games that will disappoint you. This one will not. It's not the best ever, but it's worth more than one, even two, playthroughs. If you like hyperviolence and action movies, this is "action movie: the game."You can critique a few things about this game. Graphics are a touch dated looking at times, problems with dialogue tracking for the character models at times, relatively "straightforward" gameplay (I am a walking tank, what could you possibly do to me?) You can find things to complain about, certainly.But the trade-off is I can upgrade my Auto-9 to operate like a CIWS with a limitless supply of ammunition while upgrading Robocop/Murphy's software to become an ancient Mesopotamian death god that separates bullets into explosive flechettes on contact. I can pick a guy up by the neck and throw him into his buddies. I can perform actual community policing like a beat cop, giving a warning to a kid praying graffiti or a ticket to a punk smoking at the gas pump. I can save all the supporting characters, or focus on the arch-criminal solely and let them all die. It has a schlockky B-Movie plot that somehow surprises you and tugs at the right heart strings occasionally.Robocop : Rogue City is a love letter to 80's and 90's action movies that went over the top on the violence and their messaging, and keeps faith to the original themes of its inspirational work.Also I can make my gun into a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ weapon of mass destruction in a puzzle mini-game, which is the only minigame I ever wanted to play.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I have beat the game on console in addition to playing it on PC. It is an excellent rendition of the classic Robocop in a video game. I would definitely recommend this to anyone fond of the original Robocop movies, i.e., Robocop 1 and 2. This games story serves as a better Robocop 3 than the original Robocop movie did. I am hopeful that they will release dlc or something else for the game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I love everything about this game. The environment sounds, ambient music, the iconic clunk-clunk-clunk of Robo's walking, down to Peter Weller's voice... it's just perfect. Combined with the graphics, HUD, and environment detail, it feels like I'm in the 1987 movie. From the flyers/ads on walls, to the neon, smoky vibe of an arcade, to products in a rundown convenience store, everything was thought out and feels authentic to the world and movies.I never knew how much I'd love exploring the rundown, decaying Old Detroit. From finding easter eggs in the nooks and crannies of Metro South Precinct, to walking around the streets and interacting with citizens, choosing how to dispense justice, uphold the law, and serve the public trust mercifully or by the book, this game is incredibly enjoyable and satisfying as a RoboCop fan.Teyon worked their asses off to make it as authentic an experience as possible, and it shows.In addition to the technical and immersion sides of the game, the gameplay itself is also good. The shooting gives me Soldier of Fortune vibes – visceral, gory, with several heads blown off each encounter – and the fully destructible environments that get chipped away and crumble while you’re in a firefight is awesome. I especially like how Robo can just walk up to someone in a firefight, pick them up, and throw them across the room into 2 other bad guys. It really makes you feel like a walking tank and force of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nature.Also, I was pleasantly surprised to see how customizable Robo's skills are. Each trait/skill line makes sense and I look forward to playing through the game multiple times and see the different ways of completing objectives with different skills. For example, there are times when I could’ve used my “Deduction” trait line to deduce evidence of a crime I was investigating, but since I didn’t invest down that line, I had to find another way of completing my objective. This is the type of stuff I’ve always wanted from a RoboCop game.If I had to mention a complaint,  and maybe a more open world. Regardless, I hope there’s more of this game in the future (DLC, sequel, whatever, just give us more of this!)Edit: They just added NG+ like we all asked. Best game best dev who listens <3
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

This is how you honour an iconic character and the world they are in. THANK YOU DEVS. They did a great job with Teminator, They f*&king smashed this IP out of the park. I cannot wait for what they do next. DLC for this, hell Id love to see them have a go at Judge Dredd, or Aliens.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as I entered it was amazing, it was taking some of the best elements of the resident evil franchise and throwing them into this masterpiece.  The feels really hit when I heard the OG theme, and this seems to so far stay true to the original movies (not 3 ofc because we don't talk about R3 or the USA network version). This game is beautiful and should have been out in the 80s!
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Positives: The Game has amazing Graphics and Gameplay. It´s fun and does a great job at giving you that classic "Robo Cop" feeling. It feels realistic and the gore just adds to it. The Map is very detailed and filled with just the right amount of loot. There are many Sidequests and a logical Perk/LevlingsystemNegatives: There are a lot of loading-screens when ever you leave or enter certent rooms. Also the dialogues are ruining the emersion because of the very primitive and somewhat floppy Faceanimations. Another reason the dialogue Cutsceens feel unemersive is that the Camera angels are limeted to the shoulder of the person who isn´t talking at that time. One last point is that the game puts a lot of straint on your GPU, especially in Cutsceens.Conclusion: It´s overall still a good game. It´s very fun and if you´re not so much a Story-Gamer and you dont care about sidequests and dialogues than you will enjoy it even more.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the original three RoboCop movies, then you'll love this game. The music is there, the story is similar to the movies, and the voice acting isn't too bad and especially from Peter Weller, who returned to voice RoboCop once again! As for game-play, it's a decent shooter that gives you plenty to do for a single player game. If you rush the story, you can probably beat it in less than 10 hours. But if you take your time to do everything the game has to offer, it will easily take twice that much time to complete. In the end, this game was a lot of fun and more than worth the price of purchase. I'm also really hopeful that some additional content DLC is announced. I'll be buying it for sure when they do.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. It's a fun NPC shooter. The gory upgrades and new weapons you gain while progressing make it worth while. The head shots i cannot get enough of. The graphics are on point. I have no issues running it 2k on a 4070 super. At times, the voice acting is pretty mediocre, as if the game developer only had enough budget for 4 voice actors. The villains all have the same voice, which is something i would not expect (considering the game has amazing graphics). This is where it feels cheapo. However, the gameplay and fun is comparable to any other NPC fps AAA title. I do have to take a break from the  cutscenes. The game has a great story, but the game is flooded with cutscenes. I found myself spending more time watching sentences than shooting at times. It was driving me crazy. lol. Id buy this at a discount, but not full price. If you can get it at $30 or <, it's a steal.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I pretty much never do game reviews not really my thing. That being said in the time i've been alive? RoboCo: Rogue City swallowed my time with ease. I hopped on to try out the game, and instead I was up until 6am when last i'd looked it'd been noon the day before.I bought the game in advance so I could satiate my curiosity and I was not disappointed. You require reasonable suspicion when investigating private property. You are allowed to conduct regular police duties from parking tickets to murder investigations!The combat feels good and honest to the original RoboCops clunky and armored form. The Pistol is your only permanent weapon through the game, yet its a blast to use with upgrades allowing you to modify its performance for a variety of profiles.In short: Between dedication to the source material, the spirit of robocop, and an entertaining experience that absorbed every moment of my attention? I Completed the game yesterday and have no regrets with my purchase. I will likely be doing further playthroughs, hopeful the devs make some dlc for this if they have a good concept, or that they work on other properties of my childhood.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast from the past, a nostalgia trip for those in the late 80's/Early 90's who loved the Robocop movies. The game sticks to the core elements that made the show popular: * Gore* Cheesy and awkward TV ads and news reports* Your friendly neighborhood badass and polite android* A cool depiction of Detroit city.As old school goes, also expect the same treatment as a first person shooter, very Wolfenstein and Doom like. Basic but works well! Graphics are awesome, with fluid game play and pretty good performance. Ultrawide compatibility however, no HDR support left a sour taste in my mouth. A small gripe is that they made Louis dialogs weak and somewhat cringe when interacting with Robocop. Very minor and it didn't deter me to play this hidden gem. I'd say for a small studio, Teyon nailed it better than nowadays mediocre Triple AAA RPG shooters.This game gets a thumbs up! Hopefully, you'll get to enjoy it as much as I am!
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Teyon continues to become one of the most interesting devs to watch. These guys *got* Terminator, and that was on a shoestring budget. Robocop: Rogue City is a smoother ride in general. There's still some poor optimization but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, you feel like Robocop for every second of this experience. You will serve the public trust, protect the innocent, and uphold the law at all times. You will shoot dudes in the nuts, throw guys into exploding barrels, and remind everyone that Peter Weller can still kill it with the voice. Hell, it even has branching storylines, and while they work to varied effectiveness, it's more than you can get outta Bioware these days. So do you want to feel like Robocop or not? That should be all you need to ask yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to sum it up, I'd say that Robocop: Rogue City has alot of heart, but little imagination. It's one hell of a passion project in regards the old films, but fails to have any identity outside of "Robocop 2.5". It ties up loose ends, threads them into a third film I passed on watching, all with one of the most uncharismatic villains I can remember. If you can get past that though...then damn, does it scratch an itch. Patrolling Detroit, solving crimes, and issuing parking tickets is a dream come true. The combat may be too easy (even on the hardest difficulty), but they give you enough fun toys that the novelty lasts through the run time. Peter Weller nails the dialogue and proves why he's the GOAT, selling alot of emotional nuance through the cracks of Robo's monotone. I wish Rogue City had more ambition, teeth, budget, and some better political chops to do credit to Verhoevan's original (it does get a little *too* pro-cop), but it's still utterly sincere. Like I said, it's got heart, and that's rare enough in the gaming market.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City feels like the RoboCop films.The action is bloody, the quips are dry, the capitalism is evil, the goons are filthy, the movement is literally clunky, and the comedy of RoboCop doing chores and basic police work doesn't get old - possibly because they never highlight it.A proper save system (or an autosave on log-out) would have been welcome. As would New Game +.Strongly recommended for all fans of RoboCop. A solid 10 to 20-hour story.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a cop, but get this, he’s also a robot.  This game captures the essence of the source material.  Once again, from the same devs as Terminator: Resistance, we get a solid licensed product.  Play as RoboCop through an engaging story, with interesting characters along the way, RPG mechanics, and a dynamic ending.  Best of all, they managed to make a walking tank of a character fun to play.  The game’s difficulty is well balanced between feeling like a proper killing machine, but not being invulnerable.  There’s absolutely some rough edges, but they’re overshadowed.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Having cleared this game, Its one of the best we got this year. the only real complaints I'd have are that there is no NG+ and some sections of the game just lock you in an arena with little to no cover that are very trial and error, but this really only happened twice. I'd love to see some story DLC come out for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Concept is great, you got to play as Robocop, can't get better than that.  Literal chills when the Robocop theme comes on.  The story itself ain't bad, it's linear but explore more aspect of Murphy's past + his emotional ride after being put in a metal frame.The main issue I have is the game play + the play-ability.  The combat is super repetitive and gets boring after a while.  The other weapons are not very good comparing to the upgraded Auto-9 (only fun thing is the shotgun).  Now here is why I do not recommend this game.  This game crashes ALL the time.  I get it sometime games crash here and there, but when I can't complete a scenario without crashing 5-10 times it gets annoying, as this game using an auto save system.I would have recommend this game just because of Ed-209 and Robocop alone, however the crash is just too much and imo its not worth the 60 dollars.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent action title that, in my opinion, does good service to the IP. While there was a fair amount of area re-use that led to the open-ended "out on the beat" segments feeling same-y, they weren't long enough to be a major drag.If you liked plodding around in power armor in Fallout 4 / 76, you'll probably enjoy this - you are slow, you are big, and you basically don't afraid of anything. The penultimate set piece of fighting through a construction site and listening to the goons radio while you just carve through everything they do to stop you was probably peak action movie content and very memorable.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this. It's basically Operation Wolf interspersed with bouts of Outer Worlds-style light RPG exploration and choice driven mini stories in a small but perfectly formed hub. The character models (except Murphy and a few others) look like they are from a 10 year old PS3 game but the locations are absolutely top notch and really take advantage of Nanite and Lumen lighting when maxed out graphically - squint your eyes in some of these locations and they could be real. I paid just over £20 for this and it felt about right.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true Ode to RoboCop fans from all generations, it stays true to the source and that is to be commended. And thank you for a very fun game in a very sarcastic and apathetic world!

_childDocuments_.review: Paul Verhoeven's heavy handed satire of capitalism and the militarization of police is back, and it's pretty dang good. RoboCop: Rogue City puts you right in the heavy, metal shoes of the title character, stomping around Detroit, blasting Nuke dealers. The game looks great, and runs pretty well too. The gameplay just feels good, and really makes you feel like you are RoboCop. Slowly marching towards enemies, bullets bouncing off your armor as you unload your Auto-9. The story leaves a little to be desired, but is serviceable enough that it doesn't get in the way of enjoying this game. If you've been waiting for a good RoboCop game, you'll definitely want to pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Deserves every praise it is being given.Some technical issues aside, Robocop: Rogue City is a fantastic game.Some good/bad points in no specific order:- It is free of Mtx.- Cosmetics B/S is minor and limited to pre-order and Deluxe edition crap, still annoying but minor. - On the subject of Deluxe Edition B/S. The 'Alex Murphy' edition does include a shotgun that could be argued to provide a game-play advantage, which is kind of a stupid choice and does lower my opinion of the game a bit.- There are also some bugs, which thankfully tend to fall into the "funny & stupid" side of things as opposed to the "annoying & game breaking" that some AAA studios are famous for.- It should also be noted that Teyon is NOT a AAA studio and is AA (at best). This is reflected in the price tag, with the game being priced somewhat lower that today's typical AAA offerings.- The Shooter elements really capture what it means to be the walking apocalypse that is Robocop. You start powerful and gain strength from there. - These shooting elements are supported by a good story, some fairly decent character development (Both RPG elements and story-wise).While there are many other points I could make, like how the voice acting and facial animation is hit & miss or that the soundtrack is somewhat simple, I will instead jump to the main point that I believe makes this game a insta-buy (assuming you are a fan of Robocop). This game is faithful to the movies, and respects the IP it is based on. Teyon had the humility and good sense to make a  'Robocop' with the 'Robocop' IP. You pay for 'Robocop' and you get exactly that 'Robocop'. Which is surprisingly refreshing in the modern gaming landscape.

Plus with the rpg elements flushes the game out nicely so its not all run and gun. dialog options worked well. Mine story was really good thorough  enjoyed it, but the side quest not so much but thy are worth doing for the xp and the gear you can acquire. Graphics: not the best, But not trash. the  gore is done perfectly especially when you take limbs and heads off. In all i really did enjoy this game. it did bring back memory when i first watch robocop so for me a lot of nostalgia there. Give this game a go if you want a good fps RPG
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: This was an incredibly satisfying game to play these days. Just a tight story, a refreshing variety of tones, incredibly satisfying combat with detailed reactions from the enemies and environment. While you can sometimes tell it's not the highest budget game, the environments and lighting really put more expensive games to shame. And then you just buy it and play it and get to a highly satisfying conclusion and you're done. Like all good games used to be!
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Unironically game of the year material. The attention to detail is amazing, it's an absolute love letter to RoboCop in both content and theme, and it is simply fun to play.There are a few gameplay choices I may not agree with, but that's personal preference and slowing down with age. The physics also breaks down at low frame rates, and they do have some bugs to hammer out.But at the end of the day, this is the most fun I've had with a video game in years.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: They do a great job of making it feel like living in a RoboCop movie, and the attention to detail is stunning.The faces and lipsyncing look like they are from the early 2000s, and some of the writing is downright cringeworthy. But you get to play as RobCop, which makes up for a lot of it.All told, I would recommend this game with a warning to approach the writing and dialog in the same way you might approach an MST3000 movie's writing.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: First the negatives: ED-209 fights were... grindy and easily cheesed, I was disappointed. Animations are a bit stiff (specially facial animations), but otherwise it's like actually being RoboCop at some scene from the first movie. A surprisingly good story with all the enemies from the first two movies and some cool additions. 4.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Not the deepest FPS you'll ever find (so far, at least), but if you're a Robocop fan then you'll likely gloss over that and thoroughly enjoy it. The settings, the gun, the stompy walk, the characters, the targeting system blip.....feels as close as you're likely to get to being in the movie. Well worth the wait. Can we have a VR version please? (actually scrap that, my pants wouldn't take the excitement)
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely outstanding game. Incredibly fun gameplay, interesting progression system, brilliant atmosphere and plenty of fan service. Being able to explore some of the most prominent (and less so) areas from the movies was a real nostalgia trip and all the nods to the films were tremendously done, I can't think of one that felt shoehorned in. I thoroughly enjoyed hearing Peter Weller step back into the role and I'd be remiss if I didn't mention the voice actor for Lewis did a great job as the character.If you're a fan of Robocop this is the best game that's ever been made out of the franchise, if you aren't then it's still an enjoyable gameplay experience with over-the-top violence and dark humour.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Back when I was a kid in the early 1990s, I watched first Robocop, Robocop 2, and 3 for countless times. I collect Robocop toys, and also, I used to play Robocop for the NES and arcade cabinet!Three decades later,  this game was released, and when as soon as the title screen showed up, the music hit me hard with nostalgia. It also reminds me of the long way since the Robocop NES release. The story takes after Robocop 2 and prequel to Robocop 3. Rather it canon or not, but the story is so good! There are a lot of Robocop movie references and Easter eggs in the game! The best part is that the original Robocop actor Peter Weller is back and voice Robocop!This game is FPS, and you get to feel like being in Robocop movie! It ain't fast FPS like Call of duty, Counter strike,  and any other modern FPS games. The graphic is outstanding! During gameplay, you sometimes notice the same characters' models face with different names, hair, and clothes, but hey, the gameplay and story are all the matter.I can't speak for people who have never seen the Robocop movie but highly recommand to watch all three Robocop movies before playing this game. if you're a huge fan of Robocop, this is a must play. Also, I feel bad for people who are huge fans of Robocop, who are not gamers, and never get to play this game. And hey, Robocop fans, you must buy this game now, and you can not skip this game. It's worth a full price, but if you wait for this game to finally hit the discount, you must say:  I'd buy that for a dollar!
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's a good game, and worth buying if you're on the fence.On the negative side:- The voice acting is a triple threat; bad delivery, bad direction, and bad script. It's probably the biggest thing that makes the game feel "AA". Mark Holden's VO for the Old Man stands out as exceptionally bad, Peter Weller's for Robocop stands out as exceptionally good (perhaps to be expected).- The game's audio cues aren't quite right - some voice lines get cut off on occasion, and I had one instance where I managed to walk through an audio trigger twice, triggering a line repeat.- The autosave system isn't great; it's not super clear when the game has saved and I opened up the game to discover I'd lost progress more than once. This was never crippling, but it was certainly annoying.- The "Hub" environments feel a little small, mainly due to overuse. Bigger hubs would be unwelcome because Robocop (appropriately) moves slow and trudging around for too long would be eminently un-fun. Still you visit downtown at least 4 times and the police station many more; by the time the game is over they'll start to feel small just due to how much has been fit into those spaces.And that's. . .basically it, everything else is somewhere between serviceable to great.For starters, the game  absolutely gorgeous, maybe the best I've personally ever seen. Especially when character models aren't on-screen (aside Robocop himself, who's also pretty perfect) it absolutely punches above its weight class in terms of the textures, effects, and visual variety. If graphics are a big draw for you, it's totally worth picking up just for that reason.While the hub areas are re-used a little too much, the environments themselves have really nice variety and the interactive destruction adds a lot of verisimilitude (cans spilling out of vending machines, spray paint exploding in puffs of color, walls getting holes blown in them, etc.).The gunplay is satisfying enough. The game isn't particularly difficult; I steamrolled the game on hard, and I think I died to mines more than enemies. Your starting pistol very quickly overpowers any other weapon you find - by the end I had an infinite ammo machine gun with pinpoint accuracy that one-shot most enemies - but the other weapons you find are more opportunistic (e.g. the sniper rifle lets me engage from further away) rather than a core part of your loadout. Since you lack mobility or cover options, combat is more about damage management and efficiency than it is "can I shoot them before me". Definitely a power fantasy, but they make the resource management aspects of it fun. I was never enthralled by the combat mechanics, but I finished the game without getting bored of it so there's that.All in all, if you're interested you should pick it up. At full price I think it lacks some polish, but if you care more about graphics than VO work, or you find it on a light sale, it's very worth it. I think I picked it up for something like $30 and I'm quite pleased with what I got for that price.

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is a pitch-perfect throwback to the action movies of the ‘80s. It’s over-the-top violence with charm, largely well put together but rough on the edges. Most importantly, it's a fun way to spend time in a beloved fictional universe that doesn’t overstay its welcome. Blasting at goons as an unstoppable walking machine remains as extremely entertaining as it seemed on the big screen, thanks in part to an impressive commitment to capturing the look and feel of the original film. Mixing in elements like routine police work and side quests does a great job changing the pace, too.

_childDocuments_.review: Always nice to see a licensed game that was obviously made by people with a passion for the source material! Teyon faced a unique challenge with this one; making a FPS/RPG with a character who, canonically, has the speed and mobility of a tank (ironically, this would have worked better as a rail shooter than their unfortunate Rambo game). But they rose to the occasion, making a title where the action focuses around utilizing the hero's insane tankiness and superior gunplay to win as opposed to diving for cover or jumping around. Combined with a slo-mo feature and RoboCop's canon targeting abilities, it makes for a very engaging combat system despite explicitly being designed around being tougher than just about any enemy you face.The RPG elements are light, but fun and do a good job of making you feel like your actions have an impact on the characters and the city as a whole. The skill trees are simple, but they do their job and you do have meaningful choices in what you prioritize with your build.Most important here is the story and tone; Rogue City feels very much like a natural extension of what Verhoeven and company set forth in the original movie, with biting satire coupled with over-the-top violence and thrilling action. There are all the cool setpieces you'd expect from a RoboCop story, plenty of cheeky and fun references to the films, great new gags, plenty of returning characters (including some surprising ones that only die-hard fans are likely to get), and the sort of iconic fights that are must-haves, including rematches with ED-209 and a new RoboCop 2. The story is clever, with an excellent new villain and a great exploration of Murphy's existential struggle. And the voice acting is, by and large, excellent. Peter Weller knocks it out of the park in his return to the role, and the soundalikes they got for other recurring characters (notably Lewis) do a solid job as well.The only real drawbacks are that this is a mid-budget title from a competent but not expansive studio. As a result, there are visual hiccups here and there, and a lot of the non-key character models get reused and reskinned as varying NPCs. Apart from those and a few minor bugs (I had two freezes/crashes in total during my entire playthrough) and the confounding lack of a manual save function, it's nevertheless a very solid title.I thoroughly enjoyed my time with Rogue City, and definitely plan to take a run through New Game Plus soon to try a few different story paths and see if I can 100% everything this time around. If you're a RoboCop fan, this is a must-play.
