_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I like this game. As a person born in the early 80s, it brought me back many, many memories from my chilhood, specially from action-hero movies of the era and the 80s culture in general. Robocop was (and still is) one of my favorite heroes of my childhood, alongside others like the T-800 from Terminator 2.As for playability, I know this may not be an AAA game, but nonetheless, it's a good FPS, with a lot of gore and very loyal to the Robocop movies. It's not as fast paced as the classic FPSs I'm used to, like Doom, Quake and more specifically Unreal Tournament, but the gaming experience is pretty good.On the technical side, this game is one of the very first that uses Unreal Engine 5, which looks AMAZING with its very detailed environments: both the Police Station and the executive floor of the OCP building are very loyal to its movie counterparts. The characters are very loyal to the movies too: not only because Peter Weller provides his voice and likeness to the Robocop character, but also because most of the main characters look very similar to the actual actors that starred the Robocop movies, specially Reed, Lewis, the Old Man, and even some secondary characters like Officer Estevez, to name a few. I also have to mention that the main villain, Wendell Antonowsky, looks very similar to Alan Rickman's character Hans Gruber from Die Hard. Another character that caught my attention is Samantha Ortiz, which also looks similar to another movie character of the era: Melina from Total Recall. Overall, all characters look 80s-styled, which of course it's the way it is supossed to be. It's amazing what can be done with Unreal Engine 5.On the other hand, I must say that this game seems to be targeted at an audience that, like me, was born in the 80s and 90s, and it may not be appealing to younger players that are in their late teens and early 20s.There are also some bugs, glitches and minor issues that should be solved with a patch. I wrote a list ordered by importance, from the most important to the least important:- Sometimes the game freezes after playing for several hours, and either ends crashing to the desktop or I have to press Ctrl + Alt + Del and reboot the OS. This however could be a problem with the Unreal Engine itself, rather than the game, since I have another game made with Unreal Engine 4 that has the same issue. This is top priority and should be fixed ASAP.- The game seems to have performance issues when running in borderless window. I set it to Fullscreen (as I do with every game), and also activated Nvidia DLSS and the problem is gone: it runs perfect now at 1080p, with no FPS limit and full detail. This may not be an issue at all, but should be cheked.- There is an annoying glitch with the auto-targeting system: when I pick up certain weapons and aim down the sights, the auto-targeting system gets disabled and no longer works until I leave the area I'm on (by entering or exiting a building, for example), or load previously saved game. This is very, very annoying, because the enemies are no longer highlighted on the HUD and this makes things a little difficult, specially when shooting in low-visibility conditions, such as shooting trough a smoke screen. This happens with both the .50 cal and Cobra sniper rifles as well as the mercenaries' assault rifle. This is another glitch that should be fixed ASAP.- There are some other minor HUD glitches, such as the health and weapon indicators showing up when not in combat (gun holstered) or sometimes the ammo counter showing 20 | 320 on Robocop's pistol, which is supposed to have unlimited magazines.- There are also some inconsistencies that the devs did miss probably because they are an European team. For example, the dates written in the evidence boxes found on the Police Station are written in dd/mm/yyyy format, but the Americans use the mm/dd/yyyy format. Also, Americans begin the week on sundays: I'm not sure but I think the calendars shown on many places in the game begin the week on mondays. Another thing that I found out is that it seems that Robocop's Police Car is front-wheel drive, which is inconsistent with the real-life Ford Crown Victoria Police Interceptor that is based on, which is rear-wheel drive (like most American cars):  I noticed this when Robo gets into his car and leaves the station: the cinematic shows the car spinning its front wheels and doing a burnout, which would not be possible on a rear-wheel drive car.Anyways the game is good and worth playing. I hope you devs release a patch addressing the issues mentioned above.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot of fun to play, and brought back a lot of fun memories of watching the movies as a child. It definitely felt like I was reliving those experiences, and continuing them. To those who made this, thank you for all the effort you put in to making it feel like a proper Robocop story. I am -really- hoping that there will be a sequel, or some DLC regarding that teaser at the end.On to specifics about the gameplay: Robocop is an unstoppable, slow, clunky tank that destroys just about anything he targets that isn't an even bigger war machine. Just as he's supposed to be. Even so, the skill points and customization of his Auto-9 pistol give some room for strategy and making the combat flow as it feels right to the player. There's also some fights where you definitely will need a bit of that strategy. My only complaint might be that while some of the levels and arenas feel very fun to run around in and having a moving battle with lots of weapon-swaps, it ended up not going that way for me. I pretty much just used the Auto-9 for most fights, and generally found a bit of cover to duck in and out of while I picked enemies off. It seemed like the game would actually punish you for exploring those bigger arenas for fighting in, since Robocop is absolutely terrible at dodging, or taking cover (again, as he should be.) There's things you can do to get around that a little, like using skills for shields or dashing, but that never really felt quite right to me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is based on the first 4-5 hours of the game that I already played, will likely Update as I get further along in the full version.Story and level design felt good, RoboCop felt like controlling a tank in combat. Weapons felt very good with lots of stopping power.Gibs like being able to shoot enemies hands off or making their heads explode and "painting the environment" with them in combat sections was a nice touch. Can grab enemies and use them as shields or throw them through glass panes and punch em too. And there's destructible environment like pillars, panes of glass, couches, vending machines etc. Made me nostalgic for some older Shooters like Soldier of Fortune.Almost hard to believe this got made today in various (good) ways, since it feels very authentic and respectful of the movies it is based on from the 80s. Cops are (mostly) the good guys and you get to play as one and hunt down criminal "Scumbags". It's also refreshing that they didn't try to make RoboCop PC like OCP tried to do in RoboCop 2. Criminals, cops and prostitutes mostly behave, talk and look like you'd expect and I didn't have to sit through some neologist lecture about "sex workers" or something. Characters are largely believable and interesting even if some are over the top.The Semi Open-World Quest Hub with side objectives and secrets reminded me of a mix between Deus Ex: Human Revolution and Vampire: Bloodlines.If the rest of the game can live up to the content of the early game with the Intro, police station and the first Hub it'll be great. It also made me Rewatch the movies after a long time, and yes even afterwards it still feels largely authentic. You can recognize various elements you've seen in the game watching the movies.Main complaints would be no straightforward way to just disable Upscaling/DLSS (I switched to TAA with 100% Res scale), Robo sprinting too slow in the main Quest Hubs, it's fine during combat but I can see walking around slowly in Hubs while doing side-quests and exploring getting old (I didn't try the Engineering 2 Sprint yet) and some of the combat sections might end up too easy in parts (TV tower had way too many healing items, I didn't know what to do with all of them and was sometimes healing at 80-90% HP, I'll probably restart on a harder difficulty).I didn't really have major technical issues, since I'm not expecting to play brand-new Unreal Engine 5 games on 10 year old hardware and it ran fine on my GTX 4090. They could probably benefit from a "Building Shaders" screen at the beginning though, so people don't think the temporary stutter when starting it up for the first time is a hardware issue, and the Main menu Screen still looks a bit cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic movie game from the developers that brought you Terminator: Resistance, which is also a fantastic movie game. Seriously this developer needs more attention. RoboCop: Rogue City is graphically pretty, violent as hell in the spirit of the movie, has a good story, and by some miracle they even got Peter Weller himself to voice the titular character. Not only is it a great shooter but the game is of decent length and has lots of cool side missions where you help solve crimes and do detective work. Just overall, this game is a great experience. It contains all kind of content and references from the movies, takes place shortly after the events of RoboCop 2, and feels like the proper RoboCop 3 we deserved.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: This game nails the feel of the movies, while giving you a fun shooter with skill upgrades and a great weapon modification system. The writing is great, and I can look past the voice acting on minor npc's not being super well done because the writing is good. The main characters all have good to great voice acting and they really nail their parts. I thought the story was going to stop much earlier than it actually did, which was a fun surprise. The fact that I can issue parking tickets as a side objective while trying to solve crimes is so funny and on brand for the character of Robo Cop. This is a game to play once or twice, get all the achievements and have a good time doing it. I'd love it if there was a NG+, but only to help a second play through go a little quicker.If you want to play a game for a couple days that feels solid and is a good, movie-like experience, I suggest this one.

_childDocuments_.review: There are good and bad aspects to this game but overall, it just feels unfinished. SLIGHT SPOILER ALERT! Starting with the bad: - If you disable the repetitive and constant music, you will hear almost nothing. They added barely any background sound effects. - Everything about this game is extremely basic. - Too many "missions" that are just tedious tasks like getting people to sign a get well soon card, fetching a towel from a locker for someone in the shower, giving a ticket, etc. Basically all side quests just feel like cheap filler quests to make the game look like it has more playable hours. In total, the game has 15 playable hours IF you do ALL side quests and spend some time just looking around at textures, bad animations, etc. like I did. There's really only a few levels and it's over before you know it. - Animations are very janky and even broken at times (like being able to see the characters eyes through their eyelids when they blink. - Some of the upgrade-able perks/skills don't actually work in the game. - You start off with infinite ammo and with one of the most powerful guns in the game (especially once upgraded). It's fine it just kind of feels a little OP. - The game feels chunky and underdeveloped. You get pretty much 3 or 4 main areas that you play in and those areas just repeat with slightly different missions and bad guys. - Barely any combat variety. You're pretty much just doing the same thing over and over again. Bad guys are all pretty much exactly the same. There is no variety to them or their actions (for instance none of them surrender, none of them run away, etc. It's like arcade-level "AI". - Unnatural cut-scenes, speech, movements/animations, etc. of the characters. Again, feels very unfinished. - You cannot manually save in this game and while you can "revert to last save checkpoint". you have no idea when that checkpoint was - it doesn't tell you. It can send you back several missions and an hours worth of game-play, which can be extremely frustrating. - The menu's are the most basic menus I have seen since I was a kid playing some indie PlayStation games. Again, feels unfinished. - Inconsistent graphics. It often feels like each level, parts of levels, characters, etc. were all designed by a different studio and it can be a bit distracting. Robocop himself (when viewed in cut scenes) looks great but then some of the other characters... well... let's just say they need a lot of work. The good: - They stuck with the original characters. In 2023 - a time when they replace characters left and right for "political correctness" or whatever their reason is - it's nice to see a dev team stick to the original material. I think that this aspect alone is what actually made this game popular. I mean it's the main reason I downloaded it. - Decent graphics for the most part. I mean it's no path tracing and it has tons of bugs in graphic fidelity but I think it's a good, early showcase/demo for Unreal Engine 5's Lumen engine. ... I sat here and really tried but those are the best things I could think of for this game. Overall it was just "okay" but mostly felt more like a demo for a game that is going to be released a couple of years from now... as in, it feels like they needed a couple more years to make this a fully fleshed-out game. It's lacking in almost every way possible. The most I would pay for this game (now, seeing what it is) is maybe $10. I would wait till it goes on DEEP sale if you are considering trying it. I really should have watched a playthrough video before purchasing this one. I actually, for the first time in my life, tried to return a game (this game) but unfortunately I had already passed the acceptable amount of play time for a return (by just a few minutes). Otherwise I would have stopped playing and just returned it. Since I couldn't return it through, I decided to just play it all the way through to see how it was... was not worth it. Why this game has such raving reviews is beyond me. I really do think it's just because they were faithful to the franchise and that's it. o other game studios should take note: What the fans want is for you to be faithful to the franchise and not change all the characters, the story, etc. with your forceful political views. 3/10 is the rating I give for this one though.

_childDocuments_.review: This game pays a beautiful homage to the source material, it's easy to tell how much the devs love it. The immersion works so well thanks to the heavy steps sound with clunky movements, the Auto 9 shooting mechanics with the scanning system, the fact that it is possible to go out in the streets and uphold the law doing stuff like issue parking tickets (LOL) and the dialogue options, all of this together with Peter Weller's voice acting conveys the feeling that you really are RoboCop himself and for me this is  the best thing about this game because I just love this character.If you like the original movies and also did like Teyon's previous game Terminator: Resistance then you can't go wrong here, just pick it up and show these guys some support because they deserve it.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the movie. That's one of the reasons that made me want to buy the game, and it's probably this nostalgic factor alone that drives the sales. There really isn't anything else that scratches that, for lack of a better word, Verhoevian-itch: fans haven't seen or played anything remotely this tongue-in-cheek fascist since Helldivers 2. Hell, we probably won't ever see another Paul Verhoeven (film) in our lifetime. So, if none of this is clicking with you right now, chances are Rogue City isn't for you.The closest game-equivalent I would compare it to is DOOM, although DOOM satisfyingly embraces the FPS aesthetic that something like Rogue City teeters across. And although I wouldn't go so far as to compare this with something like LA: Noir, or even Dishonored, Rogue City does have elements of investigation and exploration to it that remind me of both games. Honestly, besides the gritty eighties dystopic backdrop that comes straight from the movie/s, if you're going into the franchise blind, the game doesn't introduce what's going on all that well. It's properly in medias res, for better or worse.Lastly, I'll round off this recommendation by saying that this is the first real game that's pushed the boundaries of my old, faithful 1080 Ti - nearly 10 years chugging along. My boy has really been feeling it these past 10 hours, so much so, that I've had to shelve Rogue City for an entirely different rig: putting up the graphics makes everything laggy and choppy (although gloriously, gloriously in fine detail), so aiming is really difficult, let alone playing enjoyably on higher difficulties.TL:DR: If you never watched the movie, watch the movie. If you didn't like the movie, what're you wasting your time reading this review for? If you loved the movie, I think this will scratch that Verhoevian-itch. I'd love to see this studio take on either The Running Man, or perhaps Total Recall. Now, move along, citizen! Robocop has a new rig to build...

_childDocuments_.review: This game did a great job at capturing the feel of the movies and putting it into an immersive game. The skill system made sense, the "mini game" of upgrading PCBs for the Auto-9 was a nice break (and one particular PCB, I think it was during my first visit to the CEO floor of OCP, turned the Auto-9 into such a beast, I barely ever picked up secondary weapons). The story was good, they are clear in the start that it takes place between the 2nd and 3rd movie, which helps with the immersion (if you know the movies). I was thrilled they convinced Peter Weller to do the voice acting, and he nailed it. The writers did a great job at coming up with dialogue that fit for him. I was surprised they didn't/couldn't get Nancy Allen to voice Anne Lewis, that would have sealed the deal. Also, seemed there were some small and amusing easter eggs referencing CyberPunk 2077 and the later Deus Ex games - so keep your eyes peeled for those!I was disappointed that the game used only a checkpoint system for saving. It was tough to know when a checkpoint was reached, so I had to make sure I had enough time to finish a level - a few of the larger levels can easily take an hour if you are looking for all the "goodies" to maximize your XP or do secondary objectives. Sometimes combat was tricky when using a controller. There were a few "Range challenges" and I had to switch to using the mouse so I could aim fast enough (accurately) to complete them. Because of the (mostly) true-to-movie way that RoboCop moves, you can't truly 'run-and-gun', you have to be strategic and play to where you put your skill points. I was frustrated that when you returned to places, things would sometimes change and you wouldn't be able to open safes you saw the first time. Or in one level, I found the combination, but when I tried to go into the only unexplored room, I couldn't enter it yet as I didn't have the Warrant yet. I didn't have a chance to explore after the mission objectives were finished, so another missed safe. From a Roleplay standpoint, the writers did a fine job given this isn't an RPG focused game. The handful of characters you have repeated interactions with do have conversation trees that can impact the game and their personal outcomes. Seeing the final outcome of those choices in the last interactive scene and the final "Mediabreak" before credits was rewarding. I will definitely be playing this again.

_childDocuments_.review: The famous movie hero is back in the video games. And his comeback is glorious!The game is based on the original movies from 1987 and 1990. According to the timeline the game events take place between 2nd and 3rd films. It has many references to the original franchise. You will meet all old characters including Anne Lewis, Sergeant Warren Reed, OCP CEO and so on.Every character has been recreated to match their look from the original movie, so you got the feeling you are watching the sequel.By the gameplay it is a “Shooter” and a rather basic one. Robocop can not hide in cover, can not jump over obstacles, can not crouch and so on. But this suits the character quite well actually. During the game you can feel yourself as a “walking tank”: heavy armor and gun-power but limited mobility. That is exactly how the original Robocop behaved in the movies. Still the game is quite difficult: despite most of the enemies are not being able to do you much damage, you can easily end up dead if you are not careful. Also you can learn some special abilities, which diversify the shooting activity. You can use slow motion, shield and shockwave to get the extra edge against the bandits.There is also another gameplay aspect besides the shooting - a mundane policeman activity. When being sent on the mission we are going through the streets, where secondary quests (objectives) can be found.We can issue tickets for minor crimes like parking violations, drinking in public and so on. There are quests for murder case solving, searching for a stolen car and so on.The game creates a remarkable feeling of day-to-day policeman work.During the game we will rescue hostages, break through the walls, search for evidence - pretty much everything you may expect from the Robocop game.The little disappointment is the detective aspect: mostly it ends up scanning crime scene, searching for the clues, like it is done in “Batman” series. There is a feeling it could be implemented in a more sophisticated manner. Also there are not many cases where we act as a detective.The world is relatively small: we have the exact same town district to patrol over and over again. It changes as the story goes, revealing the new areas, but it is the same streets.Still most of the main story missions take place at the dedicated locations such as abandoned quarry, bank during a robbery, the prison during a riot and others.The story itself is unremarkable. It mostly repeats the patterns from the original movies, including Robocop’s memory flashes from his human past, OCP planning for citizen eviction and so on. Still the story is solid enough.The game provides numerous choices within dialogues, which allows character development towards a soulless machine or a compassionate human. In reality these are almost pointless and have no significant impact on the story or gameplay. Still they create an affinity with the character, so you can feel the story as your own.Graphics left a mixed impression. It is in high detail with modern rendering of particulates, lights, shadows and so on. But the characters could be rendered better. Animation is quite basic, especially notable for idle ones. There is almost no gesticulation in dialogues, so characters do not appear to be alive. The game uses some kind of special technique for the hair rendering, which creates unrealistic views most of the time.But the most disturbing issue is that the game does not render smoothly. It often jitters during the camera movement. Despite disabling some graphic options, I was unable to get rid of the problem completely.Overall optimization could also be better. Despite the game locations being relatively small I often encounter a swap/lag during movement, when extra area is loaded on-the-fly. In scan mode, when AR highlights the enemies and special objects there are also lags, which is very annoying.But the worst part is numerous errors and glitches. During the walkthrough the game crashed several times, making me restart from the checkpoint.Music is unremarkable. The game mostly reuses the soundtracks from the original movies. Still it is actually a good solution. You do not need any new original soundtrack for the game like this.Overall it is 7/10. If you are a Robocop fan you are going to love this game, but if you are not - you will find nothing special here. The gamedesign is almost perfect here, but the technical implementation could be much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Recently finished & loved Terminator Resistance by Teyon, & I loved Robocop as well.BUT, it has some nasty performance/stability issues.I kind of hate Unreal Engine 5? Lumen & Nanite seem overhyped, I've played fan mods hacking path tracing into older games like Half-Life & Quake where the picture quality is more stable & less epilepsy-inducing-- Not to mention UE4 games with more standard raytracing methods, that have looked better in many ways.Sure, if you have some of the most powerful hardware around & can max out at Epic 4k with 60+fps then you might have stable smooth picture quality & less crashing, & you should just stop reading right now & assess if you like linear story-driven single player games & enjoyed Teyon's Terminator, then this is more or less an obvious choice, BUY IT (be warned: I experimented with highest r.lumen values based on defaultScalability & even those didn't 100% fix noise & ghosting)-- BUT, ANYTHING below highest specs, where you need to start compromising settings to maintain smooth framerate, you will both have crashing issues & stuttering as well as the image quality breaking apart because Lumen is really wonky, some levels will be awful to play on lower settings where the indirect lighting bouncing around will become downright epileptic & ghosty & reflections will be insanely flickery with strange artifacts.I imagine in 10 years, assuming I haven't dropped dead yet & I have some future PC that's not even been built yet, then reinstalling this will feel really nostalgic & I'll again end up spending dozens of hours in it just like I've done with Crysis in the last few years or FEAR, Max Payne 2 (throwing those deliberately as references also for some minor gameplay similarities), I remember still playing Crysis in 2007 with 15-40fps, still was a mindblowing game I liked even then-- This of course isn't mindblowing, but it is fun with a surprisingly decent story & that lite-RPG immersive experience where you just get to be in the world & talk with funny NPCs with some story consequences to your words & actions while having comically overblown violence & gore in action setpieces.Structurally Robocop is split into sections where you visit the police station talking & doing minor side quests, visit the Downtown area of Old Detroit to patrol & do good old fashioned police work, interacting with NPCs, discovering side quests (not all are marked on the map or signposted), & then the plot investigations & developments take you to visit other areas like an abandoned Mall, a Bank, a Steel Mill, a Prison, slaughterhouse & more-- usually the places outside of the Precinct & Downtown area are more combat focused, by the end though there's a really cool section in Downtown Detroit where you save civilians from burning buildings, rescue shop owners & other people calling for help, retaking the city from chaos-- It's a very well paced balanced adventure, with some relatively complex characters, good twists & turns to the plot & a good heart to the main core, Robocop/Alex Murphy dealing with his humanity, his past, some fun hallucination/nightmare sequence stuff-- I've been replaying Max Payne 2 recently & they feel very similar in ways, in themes and plot developments, the world in Max Payne 2 is similarly satirical.Gameplay maybe leans a bit easy (on normal difficulty), not complaining, but worth mentioning, though it's harder if you don't focus on maxing Vitality & Armor stats-- Some really heavy hitting enemies later in the game & health pickups can be at places more stingy (some fun RPG stuff with skill checks/conversation checks, could have used more of that).I liked the pistol motherboard modding thing, finding new motherboards hidden around with a unique mix of strengths & weaknesses and swapping those on the fly to suit the situations-- RPG stuff is similar to Terminator, nothing groundbreaking, there for flavouring, the NPC relationship stuff is maybe a tiny bit more in-depth compared to Terminator, your actions & words have consequences, winning/losing public trust, upholding the law, political intrigue, it's all handled pretty great in my opinion. It's no Baldur's Gate 3 or even Mass Effect, but it's definitely appropriate to the subject matter & done as well as it needed for the game as a whole.The Robocop signature ridiculous violence is fantastic, sure there are games out these days with good gore & dismemberment (Resident Evil 2 remake, Dead Space remake, Dying Light & more) but when you unload a burst from your Auto-9 into a squishy gangster at point blank range with your slomo on, the fountain of blood that pours out in a pseudo 3D manner, & the smoke/dust clouds that all feel like they dynamically react to the environment in again a pseudo 3D manner, is some of the best looking impact effects in a game like this I've seen in a while, blowing off limbs & throwing creeps out windows or tossing explosives into a crowd is your main gameplay loop from start to end that just doesn't get old (would probably get old if you cut out the downtime when you do the police work stuff exploring, investigating, talking, but it's paced well-- same goes for a lot of FPS games, if they didn't have more, even FEAR or Max Payne would get old without graphic novels, some spooky jump scary segments etc to break up the action)Tech/performance is one of the weakest aspects of Robocop, visually in ways it feels almost like a downgrade from Terminator & it has all to do with Epic's beta software-- Here's the thing, if you disable Lumen-- you add some cvar into Engine ini -- Then the game will run as well as any UE4 game, with minimal crashing & more typical UE stuttering, but this game has no fallback rasterized solutions for ambient indirect lighting/shadowing, and only minor fallback reflective/shiny material stuff. In UE4 devs would bake some ambient indirect lighting & shadowing into areas or use some UE4 jank to dynamically simulate it but it looked fine enough & ran well enough in UE4, Terminator Resistance looks & runs great.Robocop Resistance was built from the ground up with UE5 tech, levels, areas, were built & tested with Lumen & nothing else. If you disable Lumen, Robocop looks borderline broken, there's nothing cohesive & natural looking to the game without the lights/shadows/shaders on, it just looks flat & broken, like a dev test map.If you enable Lumen but run sub Epic-- Lower internal resolution, downscaled lumen effects, upscaling etc-- Well get ready to discover if you have epilepsy my friend, Lumen breaks down, doesn't know what to do in many situations, constant noise & swirly effects, ghosting, artifacting, bizarre flickering black splotches in the reflections (even with higher settings).When it works it looks great, & if you have a great PC it no doubt looks & runs great most of the time, but for the rest of us plebs, be warned, it'll feel like a downgrade from UE4 games even, & those have their own fair share of issues as well visually & stuttering-wise.I'll add, there's a "dlssg-to-fsr3" tool on Nexusmods that you can use if you have a 2000-3000RTX series card to convert DLSS3 Framegen into FSR3 framegen & use those to improve performance, I had mostly 60fps 90% of the time with that with most settings at mixture high-low without disabling stuff, just bad stuttering & the tool does increase crashing by A LOT.(laptop, i5-11400H, 3050RTX 4GBVRAM, 16GBRAM, Win11)Game is wonderful though, if you put aside AA jank in optimization, character animations & lipsyncing, the overall package is just a great return to that 2000-2010 game philosophy I've missed so much in my FPS games, where they do have some extra fluff, flavour, but not overblown bloated all-in-one monstrosities. Surprisingly good writing, fun realized world, great shooting, Robocop has some hilarious oneliners--& play it on your future machines or if you have your fancy 4090s with i9-15000K whatever.

_childDocuments_.review: For refrence my entire playthrough was on steam deckI haven't watched any of the original robo cop movies but im very enticed to now. I think the game captures very well what the character is and does a good job setting up not only its story but the characters involved as well. The problem is that the setup also is what bogs the game down. Adding in unnecessary dialogue choices doesn't make sense when robo cop has a clearly defined personality and motives for what he does so being able to choose to alter that doesn't make sense especially since its very claer what robocop would actually say/do and choosing the opposite just wouldn't make sense for his character let alone the player leading to a false sense of choice that your never encouraged to take because its clearly not good choice. On a technical level the game works on steam deck. Emphasis on works, It holds 30 fps relatively easily but anytime you change from gameplay to cutscene the game comes to an absolute halt as it tries to transition. Speaking of loading times arent terrible but you got about a 10-15 second wait time. Thankfully the game only crashed once on me. I don't recommend putting the steam deck on sleep mode when playing. Just reach a checkpoint and exit because once i did that and the audio got completely warped until i went into a new area/cutscene which allowed the game to reload its assets. The game has its moments for sure with sudden freezing and drops in fps. Usually doesn't take more then 5-10 seconds for it to figure itself out but with a game like this its expected. I really never had issues gameplay wise besides that and it mostly happened outside of gun fights when the game is attempting to load the area in which your in. Pop ups on occasion but mostly texture loading taking its time but nothing game breaking. Again the fact this even runs as smoothly as it does for 88% of the time i wont really knock it for that especially seeing as other games that have been coming out are down right unplayable. So something to expect but again nothing you cant get past. I mostly played docked to a 4k tv which definitely helped visually but when i did play in handheld mode on occasion the game looked fine just ofc lower picture quality but by in large i played in docked mode about 95% of the time at home.Humanizing robo cop isnt bad but the player gets to "choose" how to do so it just sorta interrupts the gameplay and comes off as shallow and pedantic. Which is made worse when you have a whole skill tree dedicated to dialogue related choices that feels useless. The only real difference is what happens with the characters at the end of the game but its very obvious what choices will either help or hurt them. Well expect for one.That aside the other characters come off as genuine. Well as much as they can anyways because the face animations in the ultra static dialogue cut scenes are very bland at best. Robo and becker are really the only 2 who did a good job voice acting wise meanwhile everyone else got so few lines that trying to fit any emotion in them would've been hard enough but the script was just bland overall.Gameplay wise playing as robo makes you feel like a walking tank but of course youre not immune to damage. Upgrading has its own set of problems referring to the auto 9 specifically but when in actual use it does the job well and it does it right. Unfortunately while you're able to use other guns that bad guys drop you never really care to as the recoil is crazy high, damage is to low or with shotguns the spread is so small that you might as well never use them unless in tight corridors and even then if youre not right on top of your target youre missing everytime and thats just lame.The level design is solid but repeating the same area 3 times is not cool. The unique areas you visit on one off missions are cool and they feel great to play in like the bank but they end so quickly that you feel like youre not allowed to much fun or they come off as short lived. I sorta just wanted to be robocop and let loose on criminals for longer stretches but was always restricted by how the devs set up the gun fights as they always came off as short. The gun fights themselves are fun and the enemies AI is smart enough to move around and give robo some trouble with flanking him and all so they atleast got that rightReally what it comes down to is. Are you a fan of robo cop? or the idea as playing as him like i was? then you'll have fun. Because i had fun and im glad i bought this game. I would like a sequel so they could capitalize on what they started here, but the game is flawed in nearly every aspect. So if you're okay with dealing with the elements of the game bogging it down you can get to the fun of shooting bad guys and giving tickets to all those thugs who are illegally parked

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I'd see the day that we have a good Robocop game. I can remember back playing Robocop 2 and a few others on just about every platform. They were all bad and never did the character justice. Robocop: Rogue City really turns that around. This is about as good a game I could have imagine for the Robocop series.Robocop: Rogue City is about what you'd expect from a Robocop story. There's corporate espionage, attempts to de-fund or get rid of the Detroit police force, emotional problems for Alex Murphy and the bad guys behind it all taking full advantage of the situation. There's lots of good character moments for Murphy. He has a good on screen relationship with many characters, a lot of which return from the films.The game play is basic and very satisfying. It is of course a shooting game. You spend a lot of time walking slowly through hallways blowing holes in gang members. This is a lot of fun, especially when you acquire of the upgrades late game. The majority of the levels are pulled together and are situated in a hub level. This part I really enjoy. It gives you a chance to walk around parts of old Detroit and help the common man in their struggles with life and crime. You also get to deal justice to those breaking the law and even distribute parking tickets. It's good fun and surprisingly quite varied in terms of plot. The presentation for the most part is very good. All the characters we know from the movies have been very well recreated. So has the surroundings, including all the rooms of the police department and the old abandoned steel works. The UI and sound design is also on point. It's not very futuristic and maintains that late 80s vibe that made the film special. A lot of the music from the movies also return, which is very welcome. It wasn't all great. The game's performance was a little all over the place. The majority of game time for me was at a steady 60fps but there were certain scenes that would drive my GPU to the point where it sounded like it was going to take a flight. These were usually in game cutscenes and mundane scenes where nothing was happened. After it did this, the game would stutter all over the place. I suspected it was my (aging) computer but after a game reset, it tended to behave itself for a couple of hours. Until it did it again and I repeated the process. Despite the issue, it was never bad enough that I had to stop playing. I finished the game over three days. If you're a fan of Robocop, this game is well worth buying. There's a lot of great call backs to the films, but that doesn't mean that it's all about the nostalgia. The story was genuinely good and I had a lot of fun breaking it all down, trying to find out who the culprit was. Well worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it as a hardcore fan of RoboCop since I saw the first movie (RoboCop 1987) as a kid. But even if I'm a fan I'll give you a honest review. It's nice, you are a walking tank shooting down criminal scum along the path. The Game progress as if you were watching a TV Series, has it's part as a open map but can't exactly return back to previous point (so if you have some unfinished business do it now while you have the chance). It has a nice texture once it load up its renders ascetic are good all around, character model well some are fine but pretty much are re-use model except for key point character. Of course, RoboCop look perfect.: Pretty much you can get all the achievement in one goal but they are a bit tedious to obtain them. Music has it's old nostalgia theme from the old movie from RoboCop 1 & 2. Instead of a 50$ game is fell more as a 40$ to 35$, if you are a hardcore fan, then maybe spending 50$ isn't so bad. If you don't want to spend 50$ then wait for a special sale to happen. But one have to admit that it's a great game to pass time and good to relieve a childhood memories for the fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! This is the game I didn't know I needed in my life.I am a massive fan of the Peter Weller Robocop movies and I had no idea there was this game coming up.Instant buy and I am not disappointed after 3 hours in.It is not just shooting, you also have to solve crimes as side quests. Shooting is a bit stiff from the hip, but Robocop is not known as Dark Souls roly poly hero. He is a tank, which fits my clumsy playstyle.You can upgrade his abilities and his OCP pistol step by step, which makes it a little RPG. I get Fallout 4 vibes sometimes.Best feature - you can give out parking tickets when you are in town.I only just scratched the surface of the game yet. I am cautious what is coming up next.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Good nostalgic peace. Game is somewhat slow phase story about RoboCop. If you liked the old movies, this is your game. Lots of shooting separated by finding wallets, clues and storytelling. I did laugh at loud when I realized you can daddy choke thugs and throw them ass first. Grab a first guy by his neck, throw him at the second guy killing the first guy and knocking down the second. Grab the second guy by his neck and repeat until there are no guys. You can also use other surfaces or throw upwards and use your slow time ability to savour the moment.This is from the point of players: to buy or not to buy. Yes, to buy, with full price only if you really liked the “old” RoboCop 1 and 2 movies (not 3rd, we don’t speak about it, there is only 1st and 2nd). If buying is done without that touch of nostalgia on your shoulders you might end up regretting buying it at full price. full price would be in order if game was more polished and had more overall rounded edges. At its current state the game definitely delivers good story and good combat. Puns, game deliver puns. Really. As a standalone piece "as if not knowing RoboCop" would be 6.5/10. However, adding up all the nostalgia and immersion from the RoboCop movies, storytelling and overall "vibe" it is about 8.5 and with couple of beers (whiskey) it goes easily to 9/10. I really liked to play the game.Game is a bit short; Detroit city area could be bigger and have more ambient life. After playthrough I was left with a feeling that this game could have been made longer and it would have been in a sense “better”. If speaking of that in game Detroit city section, you can only add so much happening there before player start to wonder what kind of hellhole this is and why everything happens “just here”. Still, it could be like 3 areas where you could drive your patrol car and spot criminalities or help citizens by your own choice. Now it’s a bit weird that RoboCop by his lawful righteousness outright “knows” that there are 3 things he needs to rectify and player needs to find them. IMO would be better to let player “spot” criminalities that he understands to be ones  and reward xp when he has done like 3 of them. But again, this is semantics and personal preference. I played this game on "hard" and it took 21 hours to finish, it felt quick but story did unveil and came to finish. In the end there even was some hint of sequel with Japanese buyers (No please, there is no RoboCop 3, please) Also a part from time to time "I will run to hit RoboCop with my sledgehammer just after he rammed thru wall and throw motorcycle killing my 3 gang members" there is close to none of that overwhelming power to brute force enemies in to submission. One or two "NO YOU" scenarios where thug flies thru second floor window and obtains quick serenity of realization to surrender before landing agony, would be cool addition.Overall, yes, I like the game, yes you should buy it, now or later but play it. Yes, I will play it thought again and try to make more reasonable choices with perks this time.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Played the last mission for new years, and I gotta say it's one of the best shooters I've played, with a keen detail of gore and the power exuded from every gun as you clean up the streets of Old Detroit, along with the many, many callbacks to the films. A must play for Robocop fans and highly recommended for those who want a break from the current style of shooters to focus on a slower shooter without the hyper tactical gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is so far, so good.With Peter Weller back in the iconic role and the city looking like a 1980s future hellscape, RoboCop: Rogue City is really neat AA title and a ton of fun to play. They REALLY nailed the look of the original movie so far, and I'm actually amazed. _childDocuments_.review: The Game Seemed Like An Arcade Shooter After The Trailers But Still Peeked My Interest.It Is Much More Than That.A Full Fledged RPG Thankfully With Not Too Much Talking Choices But Still The Choices Matter.It Is Action Packed And Fun, And If You Are Interested In The Other Outcomes You Can Play It Multiple Times Easily.I Love The Skill Tree As Well, Not Just The Usual Armor, Combat, Etc. _childDocuments_.review: I want to get the biggest part out of the way. If you are looking for a run and gun style game that is full on action all the time, this game might not be for you. While I was streaming Robocop: Rogue City, I constantly explained the game more as a walking sim with shooting galley sections thrown in. Part Walking Sim - The reason I say this is more of a walking sim style game with shooting gallery sections would be based on the fact that you spend quite a bit of time walking around looking for Nuke, Fake Money, and Incriminating Documents for extra experience (if you choose to). Same thing for side quests and other collectibles (chip boards). Robocop's walking speed is what you would expect from Robocop. It's slow, it's menacing, and determined to serve some justice. Traversing around the semi open areas at this pace might deter people from exploring the areas or just be a turn off all together. It didn't bother me because it felt very true to what I thought being Robocop would feel like and enjoy a good walking sim. Each area has its fair share of world building elements as well. Turning on a radio to get a little snippet of news, reading a piece of junk mail, seeing a police taped off area just adds another layer to the game. You can sense and feel the crime, grime, and no good that is going on in game. Interacting with people in the game does seem to influence the story a little bit. I won't touch too much on this because of spoilers. There are a hand full of NPC's you get to interact with over the course of you playthrough that can change how people feel and interact about you. After playthrough 1, I went full good guy and felt like I got a heroes ending. Curious to see if I make some different choices if that changes or not.Side quests - Most side quests in Robocop really do slow the pace of the game down if all you are looking for is action. If helping someone find a cat, solving a crime on a commercial set, or issuing parking tickets sounds like something you can get behind, then you will enjoy the side content quite a bit. I can't state just how much I enjoyed doing all the small things that Robocop has to do from time to time but it definitely won't be for everyone. Combat - When you do get into a bit of action, the game is a blast. I haven't laughed so much during a gun fight in my life. Dashing in (one of you unlockables you can unlock), grabbing a baddie by their neck and throwing him back at his buddies was some of the most fun I have had. Grabbing the motorcycle riders off their bike when they are coming at you was a must. Blowing up the motorcycles as they were trying to get away makes for some real explosive moments. The guns all handle well and all serve their purpose and I don't have a whole lot to say here. Some of the upgrades also help with keeping the combat fun and fresh. The shockwave ability to stun enemies (or flat out kill them when fully upgraded) or adding extra armor (which also gives you some damage reduction) lets you feel like the relentless doom engine of justice you are. Add the ability to have a chance to ricochet bullets off walls (while using the VATS style Robocop view) made for some fun fights as well. I just wish there would have been more combat sections. After you beat the game, credits roll and that's it. No new game plus, no leader boards (not a big deal for me), no level or section select. If you want to replay the game on a higher difficulty you can and make some different choice that (might) impact the story. The story itself feels good and is the true Robocop 4 we never got. This will be a contender for my Game of the Year. Amazing game with a little bit of nostalgia thrown in.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: It's an OK game. If it wasn't RoboCop, then I think it would probably be a bad game. I'm not eager to complete it, or ever really have the urge to play it but it's fun and simple to play when I want to chill out on a single player game (much like Terminator Resistance). The story is decent and the level design is very good, in keeping with the films. The voice acting is bad, animations are pretty poor and the graphics are... OK? I say that because no matter what I do, it's constantly screen tearing, washy and generally unpleasant. There always seems to be a noticeable amount of input lag too, which can become quite tiresome to deal with. I've never had issues with graphics in games, and this isn't exactly a demanding game so maybe I just have that weird set up that this game doesn't like, but I can't seem to find a fix for any of these issues. Will I keep playing it? Yes, I like RoboCop and it's a simple game to play. Would I recommend it? No, it's just not a good game. Any other IP and this game would have flopped. If you like RoboCop and get it on sale at half price or more, then go for it. Otherwise, buy something else or save your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually just watched robocop last night, so I am not a super fan or nostalgic since owning this game. After playing the demo on Next-fest, I went ahead and picked it up and it seems solid for people who enjoy the robocop world. I do think they should fix some UE 5 crashing from a simple alt+tab and I do have a very high-end PC, so I assume others might be unhappy with the engine's implementation.- Frame gen seems to work well as of now (I get people hate on it. I just love super high frames on my eyes and the latency is like 15 milliseconds, so please don't pass it if you have the 40XX) - There is some pop-in and my SSD and DDR 5 is pretty quick, so I believe this needs to be fixedOverall the game is a good time and head shots feel great. Mouse sensitivity required a bit of work on my part too. Summary: Game is good for its cheap price for those looking for a casual 80s throwback. You can tell it was made with love and it's probably the main selling point. It has issues, so if you are on dated mid tier hardware... your experience mighjt suffer. The texture pop in and crashing that occur from tabbing around is pretty annoying and while I'm not IGN or equivalent, I do recommend you try and refund if you dislike it. This is a very 7-8 out of 10 vibe and if you're already a fan it's probably a full 9 or 10. This an Alan Wake 2 are a steal for current content and pricing. Please feel free to comment about your GPU performance as I have a spare 1070, 1080, RX 580, 6600, 4060ti 16 gig and 4080. Sadly skipped the 30 - series for 40, but I figure there is no point in a review if I don't offer any further help :)

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best Robocop game ever made.This game captures the tone and atmosphere of the films in a way fans will love and the gameplay is great as well. _childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolutely massive homage to RoboCop to such an extent that at times it feels like it's trying to right the wrongs of RoboCop 3 and make an open apology to Fans. I'm going to mix things up and start with The BAD first, since there's not much of it. * Facial animations are really lacking, so NPC's have a case of BethesdaFace, not a lot going on there. * Some voice acting can be a bit iffy at times, but it's pretty rare. * Some voice lines from enemies can get repetitive* If you don't explore a LOT you can miss out on missions that will pop up as failed objectives in your reviews. There's nothing telling you that these will happen while out and about. you NEED to explore. * Some iconic sounds from the film are missing such as the Auto-9, some of Robo's movement audio, ED-209's sounds, etc. The re-creations are a good attempt, but the originals are probably missing for a good reason. (Likely legal) Yeah. That's literally all i'm seeing for anything 'bad' from this game. Now the good. * Facial captures of characters from the films are uncannily real and look absolutely fantastic. * RoboCop looks stunningly good and Peter Weller reprises his role as Murphy so accurately as a voice actor you wouldn't even know a day has passed since the first film. * Getting to do day-to-day things as RoboCop actually makes him feel more real somehow and finally adds that extra depth to his character that I know Weller has been wanting to see. * Your actions and conversation choices matter heavily when dealing with characters, most NPC's have a sort of outcome in the game and based on your choices those can be pretty varied endings. * The plot takes some fantastic twists and turns in ways that may very well catch you off guard. * Gameplay is broken up into Investigations , Combat, Character Interactions and Exploration so you're always on the lookout for something cool. * Varied skill tree actually makes you feel significantly more powerful as you level up your various skills. EXP is aquired from finding loot, taking down hostiles and a huge boost at the end during your debrief based on what objectives you completed. * Detroit looks film accurate and amazingly grungy, yet still somehow not as horrible as current Real Detroit, which really says something about the state of the world today. * You are a huge chonker in combat and FEEL powerful, enemy reactions to being taken out can also be pretty hilarious. (Aim for the groin at least once, you'll thank me later.) * So much reverence for Robocop 1 and 2 that you will really feel like you're just playing what the third movie should've been. * About 9 -10 hours if you only do the story , 17 - 20 hours if you go for finding everything. Some of this is, admittedly, because Robocop can't sprint like he's in a zoomer shooter. He's a chonker. A fantastic purchase if you're just a casual shooter fan , an absolute MUST BUY if you're a fan of RoboCop.Bonus :  RoboCop can do the Robot dance for a kid at one point.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit, I wasn't a massive Robocop fan before this game- I knew a bunch of trivia and thought the first movie was amazing, but I wouldn't call myself a Robocop nerd, or a diehard fan. This game has changed that.For full clarity, a lot of the negatives you hear about this game are ~99% accurate- the dialogue and voice acting are generally sub-par, the facial animations are a meme, and there are some larger issues with the game's replayability and certain parts being tedius (The streets are repetitive and annoying, and for some reason there's no new game plus mode). Also, the game runs like ass on my PC, but I may just have outdated hardware.And yet this game, despite all of that, is still easily one of the most fun FPS games I've ever played, both from a gameplay standpoint and from an IP standpoint. Every review telling you that this game is pure Robocop nerd Ecstasy is 100% accurate, from the different subtle animations and model details, to direct movie setpieces, to references to every single movie (Even a tinge of 3, but the game never acknowledges 3 happened), even down to motifs and story beats. If you want to enjoy Robocop and 80's action hero fun, this is the place.I'll also touch on the combat a bit since folks tend to get wrapped up in the nostalgia and forget this is more than just a playable Robocop 2.5: you truly feel like an unstoppable death machine, at all times. Even by the end missions, when you have a bunch of abilities and upgrades and fighting tough enemies, you still feel like you can just slowly walk into an arena, hold right click, and delete bad guys. Obviously, once you get abilities and know how to use the environment (You can throw people lmao), you'll learn cover and sightlines do help, but the game never forces you to play like its call of duty- You're Robocop, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ being in a firefight as Robocop is an experience.In short, if you're fine dealing with some odd and end problems because the game wasn't made by a massive studio, this game is a must have even if you're only slightly interested in Robocop- hell, even if you're just looking for a unique FPS title with a different spin besides "Use cover aim good", you don't need to watch the movies to understand it, aside from a few easily missable references- if you're cool spending the money, its absolutely worth it. And remember: Dead or alive, they're coming with you.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this quite a bit. It's a fun, self contained, uncomplicated, singleplayer experience that retains its identity true to the source material. It feels like you're playing in the movies. They did a swell job. These are some of my favorite games, when I can have a well put together experience and never have to pick it up again. It sounds strange, but it leaves me with better memories for longer than most games with "tons of replayability," like coop shooters, for example, or any multiplayer game that has "season passes." Alex Murphy Edition is worthless though, unless you want to support the devs. Which, frankly, for the job they did... They deserve. :PIn the words of britta perry and abed nadir;"Like Robocop?""JUST like Rowboat Cop... She's a bad rowboat. Sink her!"

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game for any RoboCop fans, it sticks to the story line and feels like a movie. The gameplay is lovely, I do feel there are not as many side-quests as there should be, but the main plot line is good. There are a few issues which I feel need to be addressed:1. The game will randomly crash in some parts (for me the courthouse it kept crashing over and over) with no explanation why. Could be that my computer is lacking but I have fairly good FPS with the in-game optimization settings.2. Lack of cloud saving, cannot transfer progress from device to device.Overall the game is solid, just a bit rough around the edges, I think some more DLC could be added (2014 robocop skin/animations?) and some extra storyline con tent, but the game is really good.

_childDocuments_.review: Teyon has done it again - Robocop: Rogue City is a great and faithful recreation of a Robocop world. _childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Playing RoboCop: Rogue City was an incredible experience for me. From the moment I started playing, I was utterly immersed in the game's world. The first-person perspective and the realistic-looking environments of old Detroit made me feel like I was there, patrolling the streets as Robocop. The character itself felt incredibly powerful, moving like a tank as one faced off against wave after wave of thugs and cybernetic humanoid robots in various arenas around and inside buildings in the city.The objectives in the game were thrilling and kept me on the edge of my seat, always chasing after action and suspense. I loved feeling in control of Robocop and quickly taking down enemies. Even though the game was a bit expensive and some of the voice narrations could have been better, it stayed within the overall experience.If you're a fan of action-packed games with immersive environments and exciting gameplay, I highly recommend giving RoboCop: Rogue City a play-through. Despite a few minor downsides, it's worth the investment.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: A licensed title that actually respects the source material, and brings some interesting ideas like being a slow moving tank to the FPS genre. The story is engaging, the RPG choices feel like they matter, and the music is very nostalgic.Some drawbacks include unnecessary talents, overly tanky ED 209s without mechanics to defeat them easier, and the occasional bug. The game's still great despite these shortcomings.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, but janky. Love that they stayed so true to the source material and didn't arbitrarily race/gender swap anyone, and Robocop felt like the walking tank he is. Only issue was some bugs, especially crashing in the final cutscenes. The game reloaded to before the final boss and I did not have another 20 minutes of that in me. Please allow manual saves.

At the beginning, I took it as being close to the movies, but after so long playing, I just couldn't stomach it any more. You might like what the game has to offer, but I couldn't finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of Robocop you'll love this game. it's a nice faithful recreation of the Robocop universe.The graphics are pretty decent, and using the new UE5 engine.There's nothing quite like playing as Robocop, the pacing in places can be a bit slow, and some of the side quests do become a little repetitive, and likewise the slow plodding pace of Robocop might not be to everyone's taste. If you put those aside you do get left with a decent game, that's worth the time to play. All of the achievements can be got in a single play through with no need to play on stupidly hard levels in order to unlock, I would recommend playing on hard for a slightly harder challenge, the boss battles can be a little annoying on hard, but they're still doable, although if you find it challenging you can always knock the difficulty down without penalty.My biggest gripe is with the saves, there are no manual saves and you're reliant on the autosaves, which aren't that obvious when they're happening, so you have to quickly check the savers to see the timestamp before you log off, otherwise you can find yourself having to redo bits again.The gun play is good, some weapons are better than others, and with the right PCB the only gun you'll end up using is the Auto-9. The game could do a little better explaining how the chips work on the PCB's and also about the chip merging, once you get the hang of it, it's quote easy to update. One thing to note the Weapon Spray is the only one you want to keep a low % modifier on.It's worth picking up outside of a sale, but if it's in a sale then it should be an instant buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually amazing! _childDocuments_.review: An incredibly, satisfying, and challenging RoboCop game that any true fan has always wanted. _childDocuments_.review: If you factor in nostalgia Robocop Rogue City will be almost a pleasure for the fans, however, take that away, and you only have a decent shooter with some unfinished ideas. 👍 +Combat is satisfactory+Great nostalgia bait 👎-A lot of ideas/game mechanics that were half-baked-Outside of its main combat song, the game's soundtrack is abysmal/nonexistentThe game is set somewhere after Robocop 2 so if you never watched the movies, I would highly recommend you do so before playing the game for two main reasons, one it wouldn't make much sense if you didn't, and two, it may help with the enjoyment of the game. If you did watch the movies and didn't like them, now or in the past, then I would highly advise against playing the game. The story relies heavily on your nostalgia and has a lot of callbacks to its original movies and as a somewhat decent fan of the first two movies, it did put a smile on my face. It won't blow your mind, the villains aren't that interesting, but seeing familiar faces and enemies was quite enjoyable. To be fair the first two movies were never groundbreaking stories either, they always felt, even when I was a kid, a bit janky, low budget, but back then who cared? You had a walking robot putting holes into bad guys, what else could you ask for, the game is pretty much the same. Robocop Rogue City does have a few side stories as well which were quite ok to be honest, but I'll talk more about it in the gameplay aspect. Story rating: 7/10Let's get the best parts out of the way, the combat. You're a walking, almost invincible, tank, and you shoot bad guys in the face with, 90% of the time, just your cool handgun for 13 hours or so. It's nothing exciting, it's certainly not even close to being a great shooter, but just like the story, it works by using nostalgia as its main attraction. You can tell by most reviewers "ah who cares you're Robocop and that's awesome".  Personally, I could not play this game for more than an hour or so per day. Outside of shooting waves of uninteresting bad guys, the game had some interesting ideas that just did not come to fruition, either due to lack of time, skill, or budget. They implemented these ideas and just kinda dropped the ball. What I'm talking about is the immersive-sim aspects. As you reach the city the first time, you'll notice you can explore freely, and discover some side-quests and some hidden areas. They're all extremely basic and unrewarding, but as I played, it reminded me of Deus Ex HR and I could easily tell they tried to have something similar, but just couldn't nail it. Even the side quests make you investigate stuff, but it's extremely on rails and boring as hell. And it's not the only aspect immersive-sim aspect they tried to implement as the game also has a leveling system which again was quite bad. Gameplay rating: 7/10The voice acting is cringey, no doubt about it, but it works so well for this game that I just couldn't hate it at all. On the other hand, the music was a massive fail and it's baffling how so many developers can't grasp the fact that the music can make a game from good to awesome, take Hotline Miami for example. Robocop Rogue City has like one cool combat theme that is a remix of the original theme and that's about it. Exploration which is like half the game is dead silent. Combat fights have one garbage repetitive song and that's it. As for the sound effects, they're all okay, and I suppose lore-accurate. Not much else to add. Audio rating: 6/10Surprisingly considering its engine, the game runs smoothly without hiccups or stutters. Its visuals are clean and quite gorgeous, and the game uses some nicely pre-baked lighting effects that complement the nostalgic atmosphere. It's a shame that most of the time, the game just feels empty as you explore it, very budgety. The level design of most missions is average at best, but you really can't expect much from such a game. As I've mentioned in the gameplay part, they tried to make Robocop an immersive sim, but just couldn't do it, and you can easily tell when you start exploring the city. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score: 7.5/10Honestly, I wasn't going to recommend it, but considering there's not really anything bad with it, I changed my mind about it, but with a huge caveat. If you've seen the movies and liked them, buy it on a sale. If you didn't like the movies, stay away from it.

_childDocuments_.review: For what it lacks in polish it more than makes up for in authenticity and a sincere love for it's source. At the end of the day, it's a very "middle AA" game. But, what's focused on is so good that it's hard not to love it. The clomping, lumbering, Monster truck that walks like a man power you feel just moving through a firefight is so perfectly RoboCop that it's only one upped by the sound design of his weight, the crushing of debris (and people) and the iconic brutal chatter of the Auto 9. It's short comings, Imo, only add to the charm of it's budget and execution. It feels B list, because it IS B list.  They focused on the action, feedback and feel first and foremost and much like the films, it's so over the top that when things pop off, you can't help but be shocked and wowed every time. However, and speaking strictly objectively, it does have faults in the form of animations and some pacing here and there. Again, I find them charming and ultimately non offensive, but they are worth mentioning. But if you can look past these things and if you're anything like me, may find they add to the punching weight and enjoyment of the game overall. Like a good Reb Brown flick, the problems are worth it for when he stands on a truck with a Machine gun screaming~ It's not the best game. It's not a great game. But it's a damn fun, brutal, funny and plucky one. If you give a care about RoboCop, you'll adore this. If you don't, you may find faults, but the second you pull the trigger on the Auto 9, you'll forget them all instantly.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay isn't actually as slow as the trailers made out - that was one thing putting me off. It's simple, but... fun. It's hard to put a word to or describe it, but it just... works. It's not complex, it's not bloated with customiseable features. It's just... go get em. Dead or alive they're coming with you. No bs.But the thing that really surprised me is the effort that's gone in to other areas of the game.I just walked past a cat pushing a bucket off a bit of scaffolding. That didn't need to be there. But it was. The attention to detail in environments really isn't something people are mentioning but it's great.The humanising elements of Robocop, and him remembering he's Murphy, are done very well indeed. It's hard to do it justice in quick words.And it has an overall vibe and charm from all of that that just makes it... great. You can tell this is made by those who loved the franchise/concept.It seems to be well optimised for me too - running it on quite high settings on a 1080, which I did not expect from AA jank.But, on the jank, a few things to note. The lip sync is a bit off, the voice acting is good but occasionally terrible, and for instance the very first guy you see has his arm clipping through an AUG. If you've played through the 360 era you've seen worse. I've had a crash or two too, and there's no manual save feature to be sure you're good. But otherwise? Genuinely a fantastic and surprisingly good game. It's one of those games where it's greater than the sum of its parts. It just all... works.Maybe wait for it on sale, and see if you can buy it for a dollar. It's sure worth a lot more.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic, no-nonsense game that doesn't burden you with complex and unnecessary upgrades. It offers a straightforward, action-packed story that harks back to the nostalgic days of catchy one-liners and intense drama. In between the main missions, there are also cool and touching moments that provide depth to your character's backstory. Despite some minor drawbacks like occasional awkward camera angles and dialogue that falls flat, the game manages to deliver a compelling narrative and keep you engaged consistently. If you're in the market for a no-frills experience where you can pick up a weapon and mow down bad guys like an unstoppable force, this game is a must-have.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun Robocop game. I personally enjoyed the cop missions, and the talking quests. The world is beautifully realized, and it really feels like you're playing a part in a Robocop TV show. I feel that if it was shooting 100% of the time, the feel of the game would be totally different. It's those in between moments that really let you feel the city. This is similar to Warhammer Space Marine in that it really gives you that RoboCop experience, and doesn't feel like a generic action game with a thin coat of paint.* Great graphics and graphical design* Fun destructible environments * Weapons have a hit, and the flying debris and body parts really make the battles feel dynamic * Both RoboCop responses you can select and dialog that you can not are well written, and again fits the theme of the cop show. Lots of snarky Robocop remarks to have fun with. Really hope there's a meaty DLC/RoboCop 2, with more 80's action movie adult fun, and even more destruction.

_childDocuments_.review: This could've been an awesome game. Social Media marketing presented it as being a traditional, pure-action FPS based on the classic RoboCop movies, and instead what I got was an FPS that tried way too hard to be an RPG and only managed to do a less than mediocre job at it. I will make this very short: if you are expecting (like I was) just an action-packed shooting game you will be quite disappointed. Too much dialogue, too much (unsatisfying) role-playing, too much "open world" wandering around the cities with almost nothing to do except waste your time as you get from point A to Point B. The homage to RoboCop itself was great though, and when there was FINALLY some shooting, it was awesome. So, they should've just made a plain-old shooter, that would've worked more than fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Plays like a FPS from 10 years ago but in a way that works with the overall retro charm. If you aren't a fan of the original Verhoeven film then some of that charm might be lost on you, but it does a good job of getting that grimy 80s action movie aesthetic without ever taking it seriously.The FPS action is a little dated but I found the clunky tank movement and heavy armor was a nice change of pace after getting used to games like Deathloop, Doom, Cyberpunk 2077 etc where you have insane amounts of movement.Game UX could have some improvements, particularly how there's too long between autosaves, but overall a decent mid-range throwback FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: A gift from the heavens for the children of the 80s.One of the best 80s action movies made into a modern game and they even brought back Peter Weller, THE Robocop.Storywise set after the second movie the game has you investigate a new player on the field of crime who is getting the gangs of Detroit working for him. Nuke's back, ED-209 is back and grimy crime-ridden streets of the city are back.While, afaik, they only got Peter Weller back to voice Robo, they have the likenesses of other characters from the movie, which, thankfully, includes Nancy Allen as Anne Lewis, Robo's faithful partner and Robert DoQui as Sgt. Reed and Dan O'Herlihy as The Old Man. Would have been perfect if they got them to voice their characters, but sadly Dan and Robert passed away and Nancy seems to have retired. Which brings me to the rest of the graphics, they are damn fine, everything looks faithful to the movies, I really like the lighting system. Now don't expect the latest AAA graphics, this is not call of duty, but this is damn fine for a AA game.Music is fine, it seems they couldn't use the original soundtrack, which is a shame, but the music fits and does its job.Gameplay wise, it's an FPS, though it feels more like playing a tank, since you are slow moving and cover is not really an option. You always have your Auto-9 as main gun (which is also upgradeable, so you can basically use it the whole game...which you should) and you can pick up dropped weapons from your enemies (1 at a time). You also have a point based upgrade system for your different systems (like engineering which allows you to hack stuff).It's not revolutionizing the FPS genre, but what is there is enough for the scope of the game and to have fun.Took me like 16 hours to 100% the game and if you are a fan of the movies this is really a must buy (similar to the Terminator game from a couple years ago), if you don't know the movies I'd still recommend it as it is a solid AA FPS that is not too expensive and surely will be discounted in the coming winter sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll start by talking about what this game isn’t - it’s not a “bold reinterpretation” or “revised for modern audiences”. It doesn’t hate itself, it doesn’t feel morally superior to its audience, and it doesn’t lecture and wag its finger at you like a schoolmarm for being problematic because you want something to stay the way you fondly remember it. What a beautiful rarity in this foul age to come across something made with love and affection for both an IP and its fans. It makes you dream of chaining those responsible to their desks and not releasing them until they have made an adaptation of every 80s/90s franchise you ever loved.So what is it? To me it feels like a hyper-condensed version of the newer Deus Ex games sprinkled liberally with 80s cheese and satisfying UE5 combat. There’s a basic skill system, and a very nice little gun customization element where you can turn your pistol into anything from an autoshotgun to a marksman weapon. These mechanics fade into the background and leave you free to enjoy exploring the dystopian urban environments and blasting their various miscreants into bloody chunks. As a heavily armored tinman, you aren’t fast and agile (no bunnyhopping or twitchy leaning); this lends itself to a uniquely slow-paced combat style that gives you time to appreciate the excellent gore and environmental destruction as furniture and masonry explodes and paper flies everywhere. Hurl CRT monitors at people! Throw punks into the air and blast them into wet pieces! Shoot biker gas tanks and watch them explode in glorious slow motion! Listen to the satisfying plink-plink of pistol rounds bouncing off your upgraded armour! It looks and sounds great, there’s a good ratio of dialogue and action, and it even spends time reflecting on what makes a man vs a machine and the possible conflicts between law and ethics. It has that oddly optimistic 80s warmth that stands at odds with the nightmarish urban decay. What an unexpectedly great game.
