_childDocuments_.review: Let's admit it,  fans, we all dreamed of this since the moment we saw the original movie for the first time. I mean, it's not like we didn't have  games before. There were quite a lot of those and some were actually good. A lot of people, most likely, remember  and  versions of  game based on comic of the same name (canceled  version was pretty solid too), there was a couple of  arcades and I'm sure all of us can name some personal favorites. Like I always loved the  version of . The thing is, though, it was never about a good game. When it's about , what we all really wanted is an FPS. With 's signature vision, targeting and stuff like that. All that played such a huge role in a movie that it was impossible not to want that in a form of a video game.Naturally, there were some attempts. The first one came out in 1992 for ,  and . , who always had a thing for simulators, brought us their own take on . Heavily different from all the others. It was a very daring attempt, since despite all the limitations, the game not only provided us with 3D graphics, it also allowed us to experience everything we wanted. Driving the car, saving the hostages, shooting the baddies from first-person view and even flying. Since it's  we talking about. Some people actually liked the game. Just because of its mind-blowing presentation. Was it a good game, though? Nope. Thanks to the limitations I've mentioned, the whole thing felt like a clunky mess. Especially the flying level, which I just hate. But enough about that. Let's talk about our next game.The next first-person game didn't happen until 2003. Remember ? Dudes behind  series? Well, they've made their own  game. Many consider it to be the worst  game ever, but it's not true. Especially since it had a lot of the right ideas. It didn't have a car, but the rest of the stuff was there. It was a first-person shooter, in which we were walking around, completing various objectives (both main and optional) and doing some other... ... stuff. It didn't feel good at all (especially on  thanks to its C stick), but for a fan? It was still fun to just walk around, aiming, saying things like “Your move, creep!” in 's voice... But yeah, it was a bad game. And people hated it.More time passed. And guess what? We've got an announcement that some guys decided to finally give us what we wanted. Press was excited, audience was excited... I wasn't. Why? Because I knew the guys. 's previous game was  and... I can't stand it. It wasn't completely unplayable, but the whole thing was a lot like a series of tunnel-like maps and clunky mechanics. It was also cheap, cheesy and very cringeworthy. Sure, it offered a lot of nostalgia, but it wasn't a good game. Far from it. Naturally, I expected the same from . And unfortunately, I was right.Can't say what we've got here is exactly the same game, but yes, in many ways  feels like  re-skin. We've got the same “important” choices, we've got the same kind of skill tree with some really stupid options, etc. But of course, we're only part human now. While another part of us is a machine. Pretty heavy one too. And that's, I must say, is the best part of this game.  actually did manage to capture the feeling. While playing this game, you will feel like a heavy cyborg. It was hard to balance things out for a game, in which player can't jump or move fast, but somehow they managed. Things do feel natural. And, of course, everything you may think of when you hear “” is here.All the right SFX, all the juicy one-liners, ' , , , ... It's all here.  knows nostalgia. And they know how to sell it. Not like it needs any special treatment, since nostalgia pretty much sells by itself, but still. Unfortunately, when I look at  without nostalgia glasses? All I see is a bad game. Very, very bad game.Where should I start? You know what, the irony is – it feels a lot like a sequel to that 2003 game. Except missions in ' game started with  sitting in his chair, while in 's game those end with that. The actual formula, though, is pretty much the same. Despite  trying to hide it by giving its maps some sort of an open world feeling, it's still that. A series of small maps with baddies to shoot and objectives to finish. Sometimes it's ridiculous just how similar these two games are. That's just one of the things about . It feels ancient. And not in a good way. You may expect driving the car around, listening to your radio and responding to threats, but no. You'll just slowly walk through maps (non-shooting parts actually feel pretty terrible), doing things.And that's another problem. See, the writing in this game is laughably dumb. Remember when in second movie  messed with 's programming and made him act like a clown? That's exactly what we've got here. I'm not exaggerating. Here's an example. One of the objectives wants you to find a towel for a dude in a shower. Because he can't just use any towel, he needs the one of the right color. And no, it's not just one stupid objective. Most of them are like that. We'll collect signatures for a get well card, we'll carry the drunk people around, we'll lecture people for resting their feet in a fountain... Should I say that it feels cringeworthy? Even that old Korean commercial, in which  stole the fridge full of chicken didn't feel  painful.The game's quite buggy too. It may crash now and then, while one time after cutscene I spawned in the middle of the shelf with no way to get out. What can I say? The game feels cheap. And I'm not talking about how it looks. Even though yes, it looks like a bloody PS3 title. I actually compared it with 2008 game called  and they look shockingly similar. The real problem, though, is that the most important things, like balance and AI are done in “nah, why bother” way. Some parts are so terribly made that, most likely, will lead to some cheap deaths, while enemies are so dumb that very often end up killing each other. I remember some PS2 games with much smarter baddies. Wow, . Just wow.Don't expect much from the story either. I already mentioned that writing here is terrible, so... yeah. The main development is forced and stupid, the game doesn't really fit in a canon lore properly, after hearing that certain one-liner about trouble for a million time I wanted to scream and, the worst of all, most of the time it's just cheesy empty talks. Aside from a couple of moments during the final part, this game is ridiculously anticlimactic and not spectacular at all. Seriously, even 2003 game had more satisfying intro. Da heck?!So... yeah. Like I said, nostalgia sells. And it sells well. How much would you like  depends solely on how strong your nostalgia glasses are. Because honestly, without them this game is terrible and pretty much everything on today's market is better than it. Even those cheap Chinese FPS'. With those glasses on, though, there's a big chance for you to enjoy this. Except you won't see the actual game. All you'll see is that little kid who just watched a good movie on VHS. The one he wasn't supposed to see due to age restrictions. You know what I'm talking 'bout. But the dream? The dream is still a dream. Unfortunately. Dixi.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game is WAY better than it has any right to be! The combat feels really good, and I enjoyed the side quests, branching story, and dialogue/decision choices that allow you to be more empathetic, though you can play it more like a bastard pig if you like. I feel it captures the spirit and themes of the film quite well, and the humour feels on-point too.The biggest weakness for me is the uneven performance, which can vary quite drastically based on what's happening on screen. In some areas I'm comfortably over 120 fps, but in other areas, particularly during heavy combat, the frame rate can drop as low as 30-40. It doesn't usually last for too long however, so it didn't affect my enjoyment too badly. I was playing on basically the highest settings though, and the game does look great, so the lower performance is somewhat justified. The Steel Mill level had a nasty bug where the framerate drops down to like 15-20 fps and stays there until you enter another area, but this was the only occasion this happened. The facial animation and voice acting could be better too, but this can be forgiven as the budget is obviously nowhere near what a AAA game would have and I feel the developers here allocated their budget, time, and effort where it counts.Overall, Robocop: Rogue City is a great game that I recommend particularly to fans of the original movie.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure how people are so positive about this game. Even though I haven't played it much (yet a bit more than Steam says), from the first minutes it was not just smelling but stinking with low budget. This is clearly a B grade game, not AAA and neither AA. The animations, especially in dialogue (of which there is plenty here) are very stale and unimpressive, some look too genuine, as if they were downloaded for free on a preset animations marketplace. Dialogue, so far, was also feeling quite cheap - most of the jokes here aren't funny at all and there are a lot of them. Some dialogues feel empty and strange, as if the writers didn't know how people actually think and talk. The graphics are quite nice, even though strange animations and sometimes empty / inadequate level design ruin it all for me. I personally also have some strange bluriness in the picture - as if I am playing without my glasses. I can see things but I can't see the details due to blurred out edges and colors that just slightly mix with each other. I tried configuring DLSS, gamma and graphics settings, but the game remains weirdly soapy for me - though I am not sure that it should be the case for everyone. The gameplay may be the strongest part here, since the weapons feel nice, the combat and movement are quite responsive and an overall feeling of a human shaped tank is there. The only problem I have is weird reload and aiming animations for some of the weapons. The ragdoll system could also use some polish, since all the enemies drop down like the haven't got a single bone in their body.All in all, I am not sure how to judge this game. I have only played 1.5 hours, so I don't really know if it gets better later on or not - but from what I've seen up to now, I am very unsatisfied. A lot of people say that it feels like a '80s film - I say that these people don't know how neither cheap games, nor '80s films feel like, so they mistakenly confuse these two things.I really wish I liked this game but I have to make a refund.

_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: "Play the game citizen or there will be... trouble"As you play Rogue City, you decide what kind of cop you'll be. It's a brilliant combination of investigation, action and moral dilemmas, weirdly it's what I've always wanted from a Batman game.One key aspect of Rogue City is Murphy working through his own thoughts on whether he is more man or metal.And this is what I thought worked so well, the existential thoughts, the debate on whether Robocop should have human rights like the ability to vote? the politicians true to life in that neither are appealing options but a decision must be made nonetheless.And the battle of justice or serving the public trust. It just works so well and gave it a level of depth and heart it feels exactly like an important part of the Robocop series and a true entry.This isn't just an action game. Your choices have consequences, how you interact with characters will affect them later, you have to consider what you are and what you want Detroit to be. I loved this game. Just so much. It's so classicly 80's, it's voice acted to perfection, it looks grungey and grim as it should do and the one liners are great.I can't rave about it enough really.The game play is fantastic and I'm not super into shooters so I was surprised at how much I enjoyed that aspect, there's so much you can do with the PCB boards and the different effects they have. I particularly enjoyed investigating, gathering evidence and the interactions with perpetrators.* Is there any voice so iconic as Peter wellers? Reprising his role as Robocop as any good citizen should! * Sidenote, I wanted to play this on my Steam Deck but the cloud saves don't seem to work properly which is a little disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey Robocop fans outta there! Even though I would like to say a few words about this game here, you should know that this is (once again) not a real review. Thanks for your understanding. 😉So what's the best way to start? The game is a terrific adaptation of the popular RoboCop movies with - admittedly - a few unpleasant things that don't get a thumbs down in my recommendation for this review. The atmosphere in this game was too ingenious, captivating me by the second. The story with the main missions and side missions were mostly captivating and great - some were actually boring or just strange. The stories and the background of the protagonists and some of the sourpusses were wonderfully funny, but also profound - especially when it came to Alex Murphy. The ability to influence the story largely through your own decisions really appealed to me and I'm glad how the story turned out in the end.The feature that you can improve your character with many skills was logical and well implemented. I also tried to make RoboCop as "human as possible". And everyone has to find out for themselves how this is possible. 😊Now you probably want to list some negative points, right? Ok, of course they're part of it. But it's still important to know that Teyon is a small development company that somehow managed to win the rights for Terminator and RoboCop. And rightly so, in my opinion. Well, now to the negative:As I briefly mentioned above, there were some quests that were either just boring or even illogical and not really "appropriate" as far as RoboCop is concerned. But as long as I got my XPs for it, that was bearable. I also have to say that the gunplay was extremely negative. If you were involved in a shootout with several enemies, you had to struggle more to aim properly. I know what the developers were thinking, but aiming is an absolute cramp that you can't otherwise imagine. So slow and inaccurate. You had to sleep with the "bad aiming" to get to grips with it, especially in the later stages. But what I like to emphasize again and again: Just try to always aim upside down, it'll go faster 😉 Another thing I didn't like was RoboCop's very slow movement. And before the hardcore RoboCop fans jump on me. Yes, I know that RoboCop is a robot that generally moves slowly and inaccurately. But in the game I found the movements really "exhausting" at times. But you can cope with that too. And yes, there were also some in-game bugs that made you wonder why you hadn't seen them before. For example, I once saw a police officer in the station whose face was suddenly twisted 180 degrees (*) and I felt a bit sick at the sight of it. Or that I saw a "flying" cigarette at the petrol station. Or spurting blood that was just "hanging" in the air. Yes, there were bugs like this in this game, but also in many other games. That's why there's definitely no thumbs down for me in the review.(*) To summarize, I can say that the 23 Euros I paid for the game were very much worth it. Just as was the case with Terminator: Resistance. Teyon knows all too well how to "integrate" 80s/90s flair from movies into good games. I really hope that more movies will make it into games in the future from the hand of Teyon!Rating:80/100

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid and after seeing Verhoeven's RoboCop, we played it on the school yard almost every day. I -figuratively- always shot my buddies in the nuts, never thought that I can do it -literally- in a video game in 2024 (2023)! Also, one of the cops during a side mission looks like Ron Jeremy, 10/10!Funny memories aside, that's a pleasant surprise from Teyon. I mean their Terminator game was super atmospheric and the graphics was amazing and spit image of the T1-T2 movies, but the writing was bad (especially the DLC was insult to the human mind). Also, as a game, it was... lackluster from all pespective. Gameplay, gunplay, whatever.Anyhow, they (Teyon devs) really got their ♥♥♥♥ together, because this game is pure gold. Very faithful and respectful to the original movies, gameplay is great, writing is cool and the graphics/atmosphere is superb. My only grief is stability/performance. During ~3.5 hours of game I had a crash and for some reason cutscenes are lagging and stuttering like hell. I frequently experience 5-15 FPS during cutscenes, while during the game it rarely drops below 60.EDIT: Finished the game, and I would like to add some considerations to my review. As the game progressed, got my opinion about the game more ambivalent. I still recommend it, but definitely not at full price. Shortcomings are too abundant for me, both technical and design ones.Technical ones are carryover from Terminator: Resistance, guess they use the same engine (to me it seems they used some graphical assets too). Checkpoints are too infrequent, sometimes there are 10-15 minutes between them, so if you die at the wrong moment, then tough luck, you have to go through the same drill. Also, roughly after my original review, I started to get a crash every hour or so. Seemingly triggered randomly. Graphical slowdown also affected significant part of the gameplay for me, it was especially visible during the steel mill map. Going to the end of the map, all was fine and dandy. Going back to the starting point, 5-15 FPS.Now segwaying to the design issues. I guess Teyon was on a short(ish) budget, because the gameplay is arbitrarily extended. You have to cross most of the maps twice, but the pinnacle is downtown Detroit. Same map, playing it four times. Yes, weather, conditions and such chances, but still the same map four (!) times. Either way, game is still thumbs up from me, but definitely not such a major development from Terminator: Resistance as it seemed first.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: This game bucks every single trend in modern franchises. It stays true to the source material, doesn't tear down beloved characters, doesn't change its tone to suit modern audiences, doesn't emulate other successful shooters, it's functional and complete, and it's actually fun to play. I'm shocked that this game can exist at all in 2023, but I love that it does!
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Is it a mindblowing FPS? Nope. Is it an excellent Robocop game?...Absolutely.So I will say this, for all of the flaws Teyon games usually have, they always nail a feeling of authenticity that you rarely, if ever, see nowadays. Playing this game legit feels like your playing through one of the movies, from the style of the police station, the environments, the enemies, the weapons, even Peter Weller himself returns to voice Robocop. Canonically, the game takes place between Robocop 2 & 3, so like the Terminator game in a way, it ignores that BAD entries to the series.Even the games flaws work to it's advantage at times. You move SOOO damn slow, but I didn't care once, because Robocop is supposed to be slow. He's a damn Tank, and as a result the game is designed with this in mind. You have access to quite a few weapons, but I rarely found any reason to not use my main pistol...but thats ok, cause thats largely the main weapon he uses, and it feels like the devs knew some people would prefer that, so you can even upgrade/modify your main gun. The game is LOADED with easter eggs/references to the movies.Now, I mentioned the game has some flaws, and while most are either no big deal, don't interfere with gameplay, or even lend to the experience, there are a couple that are pretty glaring. The biggest one is the game has a TON of graphical problems on PCs that aren't brand new, even though the graphics, too be fair, aren't the games strong point to begin with, and while most don't interfere with gameplay, they can be VERY distracting, and some areas of the game tanked my framerate pretty hard. Grabbing enemies and throwing them always seems to have them go through walls or the ground. And one that was kind of a personal gripe for me, they barely give you any opportunities to use the Cobra Assault cannon, which is an inconic weapon from the movies.To put it simply, if youre a die hard Robocop fan, this game is a MUST HAVE. It's far from perfect, but it is more than worthy of the title. It's fun and it makes you feel like Robocop, and given there attention to detail and authenticity when it comes to games based on movies from the 80s-early 90s, I'm actually really curious to see which one Teyon attempts next.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: For me, Robocop felt like a college kid's computer science project that got an A+, along with extra credit. The graphics aren't great, the facial animations are seriously lacking, the dialog is often ridiculous, and the plot is rather predictable, but DAMN, is it a lot of fun.Seems like one of those games where the devs really cared about the subject matter and wanted to make a great game, but just didn't have the resources to make a triple-A title.It kinda reminds me of Aliens: Dark Descent and Terminator: Resistance, in that both of those were amazingly fun games that could have benefitted from a much bigger budget, although I'd rank Robocop just a touch lower than those other two.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:* No manual saving - game uses automatic save checkpoints. * Game isn't auto-detecting my monitor's base refresh rate of 120hz - has options to use 30fps and 60fps framerate locks but not 120hz. * Game doesn't do a very good job of presenting side missions in some circumstances - I have had multiple levels where I completed them and didn't even know there were certain side missions / tasks available until afterward as they were never presented in any noticeable way so I wouldn't find out until my after-action report and find out several side opportunities were completely missed. * Likely due to a lower-budget game, there isn't a lot of music in the game; some good music during roaming & combat can add quite a bit to the experience. There's a little bit of it toward the end which was good, but I think the right roaming and combat music in the right situations adds a lot of feeling to the game. * I did not enjoy the bomb disarm mini-game at all - thankfully it's only used in the game a couple of times. Pros:* Excellent graphics. I was pleasantly surprised by just how good they are in a AA title like this with a limited budget. Devs did a good job with this. * Controls are very simple and straight-forward for the shooting / combat aspect of the game. Very easy to get into the game. * Good solid narrative story and side quests that were fun to follow throughout the game. * Good environmental opportunities for throwing explodable objects at the enemies. * Game runs pretty well in terms of performance - I've seen quite a few mentions of hitching by other people but I have seen none of that, myself; game runs pretty darn smooth the majority of the time in 4K @ 60fps (this is on an RTX 3090 and 11900K). Game is pretty demanding, so just be reasonable with your graphics & framerates selections and the game should run fairly well for you. I'm running the game on a standard SATA drive (not an NVME drive) and no issues at all with stuttering or hitching. * Many different types of enemies during the combat so things stay interesting and not boring or too repetitive as you have to deal with the enemy types differently.  * I've seen some folks in the forums talk about stability issues with the game and a lot of crashes, but I had exactly zero crashes in ~16 hours of playing it. * Game has good, enjoyable mechanics in terms of the combat - good upgrade system so you can tailor RoboCop's abilities and enhancements to your play-style. RoboCop has some special abilities that you can unlock with them - for example he has a shield mode and a slow-mo mode that remind me of armor mode in Crysis & Slow-Mo from Fear / Trepang2 that are fun to use. * Zero wokeness in the game which was incredibly welcome. * No Epic Online Services.* No Denuvo.* No extra DRM or additional launchers needed. Game Length: ~16-17 hours. Final Rating: 8/10. With the AAA games industry in such shambles today with the ESG / DEI / Woke-Mind-Virus seeming to infect almost everything at the AAA level, it's A and AA games like this one that are having their time to shine and gaining support from gamers. I find myself buying more of these types of games than I ever have and I strongly recommend this game to others. I love supporting studios that make good content that gamers want without any of the nonsense.

_childDocuments_.review: This product presents an initial allure with its visually enrapturing esthetics. However, upon closer examination, a plethora of technical deficiencies emerge, including memory leaks, buffering issues, and scripting errors; such flaws manifest in soft crashes and soft locking. Furthermore, the animation quality falls short of expectations, marked by occasional aberrations in cutscenes, particularly in facial expressions.Compounding these technical inadequacies are optional quests within the game that offer little substantive value. Players find themselves engaging in menial tasks as RoboCop, yielding minimal experience points and inconsequential oscillations in reputation with both the public and characters of interest.In defiance of its brevity and linearity, the game's narrative structure fails to provide meaningful feedback on player choices throughout the storyline. Thus, the semblance of agency offered to players appears illusory.In sum, "RoboCop: Rogue City" fails to meet consumer expectations. Its technical defects, bred with a lustreless narrative execution, undermine its capacity to do justice to the iconic character of RoboCop and the rich universe he inhabits.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best Robocop videogame we've had and, probably, the best game we are going to get. However, like many others have pointed out, this game is for the Robocop movie fans, so if you are expecting a modern FPS with all the modern features - you will not find them here. This game is about details, atmosphere, and, like Terminator: Resistance, it's been made by fans for fans.Story.As good as any action movie from the 80s - 90s. Big and strong good guy loved and surrounded by women kicks bad guys' butts, punishes the evil and protects the innocent. No superpowers, only technologies and skills. A perfect example (for both kids and adults) of what a man should look like, without all that wokeness about crying men and strong women or non-binary deer-helicopters.Gameplay.This is Robocop, he is a walking turret, which means that he is slow, so forget about covers, sliding, etc. You either accept this or not, and if not, then why are you even here? But, he can do a little bit of sprinting and dashing.Shooting, which you will be doing most of the time, is fun. I know that Robocop should use only the Auto 9 but I was so happy to see the famous Uzi and Tec-9 which almost any old action movie had, I cannot remember any other FPS where I would get to shoot those SMGs.Upgrading your skills isn't necessary, even on Extreme difficulty, except, maybe, Engineering and Vitality, which may prove useful, if you want to first-try the bosses. Upgrading the Auto 9 by installing new motherboards is essential because it's the only weapon that is always with you.Graphics.It's decent. I wish I could tell the same about optimisation.Women.I like to see beautiful people on the screen, both women and men. It's something I pay money for, not for ugly orcs approved by modern standards. In this game, all women are attractive, there're prostitutes, strippers and women who need to be saved by a strong man. Can you imagine that? Almost like in real life. Who would have thought that games can be like this.A few words about the cons.In my opinion, the game takes too long, it took me 18 hours, so I would think twice next time I decided to play it again. On the other hand, no one forces you to go through the side quests. There are some crashes, frame drops and graphical issues.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to be able to recommend this game. Really, I do. But there's a lot of little things wrong about it that kind of make me unable to recommend it.1. The voice acting. Peter Weller does a good enough job, and they've got the guy that voices Sarge in the Battlefield Bad Company series, though he's terribly underutilized (Wasted an opportunity to use him as Sargent Reed). The voice acting is lackluster. Like they spent their entire budget on securing Peter Weller and nobody else.2. There's a bunch of bugs. Sometimes people won't move when they're supposed to. Sometimes you teleport somewhere else during a conversation. Sometimes, you're talking movies with Pickles and you glitch under the video store and fall four-thousand meters under it.This game could be so much better, but it's like they neglected certain aspects of the game. The game looks decent enough, minus the same face syndrome a lot of characters have, and the Oblivion-esque number of voice actors they have.I know the devs could turn this around if they wanted to.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. Robocop Rogue City overdelivers on its promises and shows that Teyon really cares about the games they're putting out. Their previous game, Terminator Resistance, was also made with a lot of the same care and passion. If you like indulgent and gory first-person shooting, small explorable hubs with optional side content that's more involving and fleshed out than it has any right to be, and choices that determine the fate of the characters, pick this one up. Yeah, I'm surprised how much they packed in this Robocop game. Best part is all of it is fun.

name: Ultra Age
detailed_description: Slash your way through a futuristic Earth overrun with ruthless mutants and powerful robots as Age, a young soldier sent on a mission to prevent the destruction of humankind. Now including ‘Rebirth Project,’ the all-new rogue-lite side mission that can be accessed from the main menu! (DLC installation is required.) Far in the future, the resources of Earth have become insufficient, its ecosystem long ago changed irrevocably by a passing meteor. Humankind has divided into two: the people who have escaped Earth and relocated to the space colony, 'Orbital Arc,' and those who have remained on Earth in a facility called ‘The Shelter.’ Humanity vanished from earth after civilians from The Shelter failed on the experiment that was meant to be the last hope for humanity, while people from the Orbital Arc sent expeditions to earth in search for resources . Failing to find any signs of life, A young sword-wielding warrior named Age falls down from orbit to Earth. Accompanied by his floating android, Helvis, he must find the indispensable key to the survival of humankind... Slash through foes with a variety of blades in high-speed, stylish action! Change blades on the fly into powerful moves to create linkage and run combos. Different attributes and varied actions call for strategy against different types of foes. Launch the wire skill to pull smaller enemies toward you, or Quantum Warp to get instant access to larger foes! Use the wire to strategically overcome crowds, traverse gaps on land and quickly grab items. Gather elements to enhance your blades, expand your skills, and learn new combos. Install modules and power gear to level up Age and increase your arsenal of blades to take down the toughest of enemies. Use Helvis to burst into Critical Rage, cast Healing Pocket to recover, or Time Shift to loot more items. Follow Age on his journey in the year 3174. Experience cutscenes that tell the story of Age’s mission across futuristic mecha, forests and deserts developed with Unreal Engine. Encounter mysterious characters and overcome menacing bosses to uncover the story behind the fate of humankind. Fight through a series of hexagonal zones spanning 30 Floors as a reincarnate construct of Age. Consisting of battle zones with increasing difficulty and rewards, new monsters and bosses not seen in the main game, an enhanced upgrade system, and new blade affinities, ‘Rebirth Project’ adds a completely separate game experience providing hours and hours of gameplay to Ultra Age.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Finished the game on Normal within 6 hours.Game is quite good, it was developed by 6-9 people, you can definitely feel it, but it is still great Indie level of game. Story is quite interesting, gameplay is fun, game ends before you get bored. Try the demo and if you like that you will like the full game. Some elements in game felt bit unfinished (see below).Combat is good and swift, dodge mechanic feels very natural it does use some DMC/Bayonetta elements, and sometimes camera is clunky and every time your enemy goes off screen you lose lock on, but so far it was minor inconvinience, You can chain combos, switch weapon on the run to do combos. If you like the demo, you would like final game.If you want to know how does combat/gameplay feel:Take speed of nier combatSword switch similar to DMC, + Nero armAnd now put these 2 elements in X-Men origins wolverine quality of game. Thats what you can expect, nice mechanics but not polished to the level of DMC5/Bayonetta.Game is sort of a crossover between Nier and DMC/Bayonetta.Pros:+each boss is unique, there is a lot of them+weaponswitch for impressive combos+story+dodge mechanism+interesting enemies+no need to grind, you can find plenty of crystals by fighting and if you want to get more crystals you can press time capsule and all enemies will respawn - Ideally in the "maze" sections.Cons:-no new game plus/post game content (like arenas with bosses or replay a level)-You cannot max out "parts" as I was expecting or I must have missed 10 cores-for some reason when you max healing you can store up to 200 energy, but container still replenish only 100 points (not 100%). Kinda sucks when you die at boss and can only recover 50% of health recovery nearby or backtrack to other energy box.-from mid game you end up using only 2 weapons out of all 6 (to be fair 2 basically are upgraded version of original swords-parry mechanic on Claymore is somehow late and clumsy, hard to time properly on regular mobs.-camera is to close for my liking most of the time, sometimes its super annoying as you canot see ♥♥♥♥, specially against balls throwing offscreen beams at youo-lock-on enemies is lost if the enemy goes offscreen (minor annoyance),-forwarding time is not utilized in the game or required for progress. I never had to forward time to replenish swords. The lowest I got was to 8 Claymore charges, when fighing only robotic enemies with it. So there is no need to save on time capsules. Basically it is better to use Time manipulation to get new respawns when you are in the maze sections or when you cleared multiple spawns and need to return back.  You can get better drops and grind crystals.-I have died like 5 times in this game; 3 times because of camera, 2 times because I was rushing boss.Still fun game and worth the 30% of AAA game pricetag.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend Ultra Age overall, but it does have some significant flaws with it. On a fair numerical scale, where the line for an average game is 5 instead of 7, I would rate this game 6.5/10. It's a fair effort for the first game from a new studio, and I hope that they learn from the experience and their next game will be even better.Speaking of the positives of the game, the combat overall feels good. All the attacks feel fluid and the dodge is responsive. Attack animations are done well for the most parts and the hit effects and light trails from the weapon attacks look good without becoming overly flashy and distracting. There is a hookshot that either lets you drag small enemies towards you or teleport towards the target, which smooths out the friction of running towards enemies in a big arena and keeps the action moving. There is a cool weapon-swapping attack gives you i-frames and a weapon-specific attack, like a launcher, a dash attack or a counter, which encourages you to swap weapons mid-combo. All these things are cool and important for the hard to pin down "feel" of the game, and it's encouraging for a new studio to be able to nail down these intangibles in their first game.However, there are also a fair few problems with the game, both in the combat system and just in general. Starting with the non-combat issues, the story and music are pretty lackluster, which dampen the overall mood of the game. There is a weapon durability mechanic where you can unleash a super-attack when your weapon is about to break, which is cool in the heat of combat but leads to you having to keep on the lookout for crystal vein pickups which turn into weapons in between combat encounters to ensure that you don't run out of the weapons that you need. There is also a weird time advancing mechanic that will speed up the regeneration of crystal veins, which is basically an overly-complicated way of letting you mine more crystals. It's baffling that in a character action game with a time manipulation mechanic, that mechanic manifests itself in farming loot and not in slowing down time after a perfect dodge like you see in Bayonetta or Nier Automata.Now for my gripes with the combat mechanics, which hurt more for me to say. Firstly, although there are 6 weapons for you to collect in total, all of them are just different variations of swords. You basically have short swords and heavy swords, with some minor moveset differences between them. They don't really play very differently. On top of that, two of the weapons deal bonus damage against certain enemy types: the katana against biological monsters, and the claymore against robots, which are the only 2 types of enemies in the game. This leads to a situation when you play on hard difficulty where enemies become so bullet-spongy that it's not worth using anything else besides the katana and claymore. Furthermore, if you're at a boss that is robot type for example and you're stuck and need many attempts, you will eventually run out of claymores and need to backtrack through the level to farm more of them, which drags the pace of the game to a halt.Finally, we come to my biggest gripe with the game, which is an obvious padding of game length through scarce checkpoints. Basically, your level progress is only saved at checkpoints and you will be sent all the way back to the last checkpoint when you die. This wouldn't be too bad on its own, except that just before most bosses there is a random maze section. You have to go through a set of corridors and rooms arranged in a random configuration and fight groups of enemies before you even get into the boss arena. There is no checkpoint at the end of the maze just before the boss, so every time you die to the boss you get sent all the way back to the beginning and have to do the whole maze again. The maze is randomised each time so you can't memorise the quickest way to get to the boss, which means that essentially the maze becomes a randomised resource tax for your heals and weapons before every boss attempt. The game autosaves when you use your heals and when your weapons break so you can't even save scum to conserve your resources. There is no good reason to have this except to artificially pad out the playtime, and I hope that the developers don't repeat this again with their future games.Overall, even with all that criticism, I want to reiterate that I like the game overall and I want to see the developer improve with their next game. Fans of character action games know that a lot of bad game design elements can and will be forgiven as long as the combat itself feels good. Just look at Bayonetta with its many instakill QTEs, and the forced Space Harrier minigame section just before one of its most fun and challenging boss fights that you have to play over and over again every time you die to that boss. I will criticise those game elements to the day I die, but Bayonetta is still one of my favourite character action games. Likewise, Ultra Age is still a fun, compact game with stylish combat that you should give a proper chance to.

_childDocuments_.review: SHADES OF TAN, THE GAME!Is it 2005 again?Ah yes, Ultra Age, the poor mans version of DMC.After playing the game, the best way I can describe this game is that it has the resource management aspects and checkpoint system of Dark Souls, with the combat and style of something like DMC5 or Nier Automata, and a progression system that takes cues from both styles of game while also being it's own thing. Which is to say that the game is very good!Ultra Age I still think is more of a rough gem for action game freaks and I absolutely loved it. I’m on my 3rd play though and it has gotten better each time through. The combat is fun and feels really well weighted. There is good sense of progression in the game in terms of unlocking new blades/ abilities and upgrading them that makes it really fun to play again and again. You never feel too weak or too overpowered.The combat is the bread and butter of this game.  It is not a very original system by any means and could probably use another mechanic or 2 but it is still fun and satisfying.  The game is so fluid in its combat and  like I said every move feels weighty and satisfying to pull off. It's honestly such a great experience and the last time I had this much fun with an action RPG was NieR Automata. Not only that but the performance on the Steam Deck is great.But it’s the voice acting that’s down right terrible. Somehow the main character sounds more robotic than his actual robot companion. It's actually down right embarrassing, but it's such a fun experience due to the solid gameplay. Honestly, the only thing is that you can never take the story (which handles some pretty intense themes) seriously because the voice actor seems like they used the bot from google translate to voice all of his lines. It's NakeyJakey bad voice acting level tier. Although I guess FF7 Remake had some of the worst conversation interactions of the modern era too and I survived that, so if you did as well I'm sure you’ll be able to handle Ultra Age.Despite having the worst voice acting l've ever heard in a modern video game, the gameplay is fun. It's just a mindless tear down of enemies. A good game to play when you just wanna kill stuff with a big sword. The game looks good and the fact it was made by 4 friends just sells it for me. I love buying and supporting these kind of passion projects.If you are a fan of action games then this is a hidden gem that should be added to your collection. It is nothing crazy special, but nevertheless it is a requisite purchase if some of your favorite games are Darksiders, Devil May Cry and Ninja Gaiden, just to name a few, and if you would consider anything that fits into the same league as those games in any way shape or form to be a must buy.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game sacrificed everything to make up for a great hack n slash game. Turned out the gameplay mechanics are rather dated. Enemy AI behavior can be weird. Basically, the entire game wants you to wield particular blades for enemies. For example, the katana is vulnerable for bio-organic/living things while the Claymore does massive chunk of damage to humanoids and robots. Although you are allowed to change between 4 blades, having to play with enemy vulnerabilities in mind limits creativity. This is especially during boss fights. Its a slug fest and takes forever to defeat bosses if you don't use certain blades. Also durability is tied to your blades which forces you to go out for a rage move every time your time your blade is on the point of breaking. Even air time isn't safe. Mashing the right trigger is what the game demands when you are horded by enemies. The creativity for combos is there but these restrictions put you to play without creativity. Furthermore, some robots aren't balanced and can be, at times, tougher than bosses.For a game which sacrificed visual fidelity, voice acting, poor animation, the only redeeming aspect was the gameplay. But alas! Gameplay felt sub-par. The developers have surely run out of ideas when they put the same 2 bossess at the latter part of the game. And what was the night and day cycle even for? Barren wasteland, empty forests as far as much eyes can stretch but once you venture, there is nothing there. Not even a power core cleverly stacked somewhere. Every thing is in plain sight. I gave this game an overall rating of 5/10 cuz I finished it. Played 5 mins of the DLC Project Rebirth but couldn't tolerate it anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: 6 hours straight in and the game STILL gets me invested to a degree. This is the kinda game that you would play as a kid and then become a part of your childhood games like GTA, Splinter Cell, Wolverine Origins etc. By all means I'm not saying the game is a masterpiece or anything, but this game's the kind of game that belongs in the old era of games when everyone created something original and was trying to see what works, all the while taking a close look at their peers and taking notes of what was done right.The story is engaging, and the way the game tells it just proves again the quality of linear styled games when done right. While the characters aren't really memorable, they're not dislikable. The only problem is the game doesn't really tell you much about who these people are. But the interaction between these characters do show that they're not one-dimensional, and the voice acting in this is very decent.The combat took what was done right from games like DMC 3/5, MGR, and made them more easier pick up, as in a lot more easier to get used to without losing much of what makes it feel good. For example combos are a lot more easier to remember and it takes only a bit of time to get used to them until you seamlessly transition between weapons; also weapon switching. Each weapon swap is an attack, a movement, and a block; the attack also differs depending on if you're in the air or on the ground.The level design is perfect for a linear game like this, there's never a moment where you feel lost but also never a moment where you feel underwhelmed or lose the feeling of exploration. It's ALMOST half as comparable to DMC 1's with how it takes you from place to place but still make the old levels accessible. Aesthetic-wise it looks gorgeous, the animations are really good for an indie game and the sound design is well-done. While the music is up to standard it does leave a little bit to be desired; nonetheless, it has it moments in where it matters like the boss fights (which are pretty good also) and ambiance.Overall, this tickles my monkey brain, me me like and happy.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game looking for a lightweight action title to tide me over until some other large releases came down the pipeline. Fortunately, that's exactly what this product is. This title clearly takes inspiration from some of the action combat genre's heavy hitters like the Bayonetta and Devil May Cry franchises, and while it adds some unique elements, its rough edges are noticeable enough that it tarnishes the experience.The game performs well, with no crashes or major bugs to speak of. There are some frame drops in certain areas, which may also be an intentional, dramatic slowdown by the developers, but they never got in the way of the combat. Surprisingly, the combat felt good. Weapons have weight behind them, and the game gives you several options when it comes to combo routes. Furthermore, there are mechanics that are inspired by other games, like the grappling hook, which emulates the warp function from Final Fantasy XV. Because of this, there is a lot of player freedom, but that's about where the positives end.There are some design choices that feel a little undercooked. The enemies look and feel like asset rips from the Unity store, in the sense that they don't feel unique, and much of the animation work and fight design make the enemies tedious to challenge. Health bars are often very large, and even when I had maxed out every single option on the skill tree, fights still felt like they dragged on well past their welcome. Half the time, if you take damage, it's because an attack is poorly telegraphed, or because the hitbox lasts too long, or because an enemy hit you from off screen and there was no way you could react. Some enemies just baffle me; their entire kit is unfun to play against, and I wonder how some of them made it in to the final game. Despite these problems though, the developers give you a broken tool in claymore weapons, which have a defensive counter ability which makes you completely invincible from all sides. The window for this counter is extremely long, and completely trivialises most fights if you have a general inkling of when enemies may attack. You can also equip two of these claymores, so while a weapon durability mechanic does exist, the game never punishes you for using the most broken weapons in the game. Not that this durability mechanic is anything to write home about regardless, because both this and the 'time passing' mechanic don't impact the game in any meaningful way. Couple this with a camera that often is too close to the player, and you've got a recipe for a lazy way to finish the game. I feel like this game could have been more unique. With enemies and locales that felt generic, an extremely generic player character model, and no distinct types of weapons or mechanics, at times Ultra Age feels like a combination of assets that the developers twisted into a functional product. Sure, the combat is good, but I'd really only recommend this title if you've played all the other big hitters and are just looking for something to tide you over until something bigger and more polished comes along.

_childDocuments_.review: A MUST HAVE for any action game fan.In short: -the gameplay is the star of the show here, it's the reason to buy the game. It is a very well done mix of Devilmaycry and Nier, with simple combos for all the swords that can be used in different situations (aoe, focus attack, leaps etc). Also all the swords are good against certain enemy types and have a switch attack (for instance the greatsword has a block mechanic for it's switch attack) that makes it so you always want to use everything in your arsenal. The enemies are pretty brutal at times and you must use your dodge/block and your attacks to keep on the pressure, or you can get killed very fast when surrounded, even on normal difficulty. You also have a pseudo-graplinghook that adds a lot of mobility in fights.-honestly it's pointless to go over anything else the game offers since every other aspect (sound, exploration, story, graphics, lvl up mechanics) are all just...decent, nothing to write home about. But I really think the gameplay carries the game on it's back.-one other note is that even tho you can't rebind keys, the default setup is actually really good for mouse&keyboard; it's rare to find a game where I don't want to tweak any keybindings.-I've also found no bugs of any nature in my time with it and the game runs really smooth.Highly recommended for some good old DMC fun, aka comboing enemies to death. Hope to see more from these devs, they did really well IMO with this game, especially for the price. So many garbage games out there for 30 40 bucks and this one (on sale right now for 12 euro!!??) just offers SO much enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good, the fact that when you press a button the move immediatly comes out, it's impressive for an indie. The new dub REALLY change the feeling of the game, I tried the original version on switch (old dub, low graphics), and the pc version is aeons better than that. The "color coating" mechanic is a bit strange as a game design choice (for example, red enemies receive more damage from red weapons and less from other colors), extremely limiting the combo variety and  their structure, but it is just a minor gripe because the game is still very fun to play even with just one weapon.For 20 bucks day one, the game is a steal, worth every dollar. You can clearly see that the devs loves tight action games, and they succeded in making their personal entry in the genre, a solid one too. Good job!Mind that, at the actual moment, this game has NO new game +, no chapter select and no multiple save data, it's a one way trip 'til the end, but the devs already said in their last interview that endgame contents are coming in summer, sooo you have two options: buy the game now, support those 8-10 indie developers and wait for the update, or buy it later when the game will feel more "complete". I still recommend the former tho ;)EDIT: free DLC is out, it's cool

_childDocuments_.review: Ultra Age is a action game that unfortunately falls short in several areas. _childDocuments_.review: I beat Ultra Age on Hard mode. On an indie level this game is decent at best, but it is not great by any means of a character action game. Nonetheless, I appreciate the effort and hope to see these devs try hard to refine their craft more, create more games of this type, and do better in aspects I believe that Ultra Age did not do so good at. Details will be farther below with what I think they could do instead in the particular aspects. In short this game is a painfully mid Nier Automata + MGRR combination that has ideas and questionable design decisions alongside a lackluster story and soundtrack that make the experience fall flat compared to what it is attempting to be.Details as to what I think sucks about Ultra Age and how to change them:-There is no system that provides an incentive for the player to use multiple weapons and to be stylish in combat. Instead, make me have to use all of my weapons so I get bonus currency or specifics unlocks for long-term good performance in combat encounters. -The damage types system pushes the player not to experiment with any possible depth to the combat. Instead this leads to players wanting to spam only 1 weapon that does the best damage to the enemy type they are fighting, the only two types being robotic or organic enemies. It is because of this damage type system that only 2 weapons in the game (the Claymore, and the Katana) are worth upgrading while the others (the Steel Blade, Lightning Blade, Gunblade, and Charge Claymore) suck in comparison because they do not deal full damage or are as effective at killing your enemies as the best two weapons are. Get rid of the damage types, get rid of the irrelevant environmental battling from the Charge Claymore, and make all weapons do full damage to enemies and each weapon is just a different moveset with its own benefits that all perform well in combat so that the player will want to use and experiment with each weapon in the game at some point aside from the ones that fit their particular playstyle.-The modules system and Power Gears is a neat idea that is held back by the irregularity at which the module types are dropped from enemies, not being able to equip more than one module of each singular type, and different gear upgrades just being plain better than others (Critical and Blade Modules outperform the Boosters and Wire by a landslide after the first level). There is no customization with the modules, it is only a system that "upgrades" the player by checking off boxes rather than being something to customize your character's effectiveness in combat as you see fit if there were any flexibility in the effectiveness of combat to begin with. Get rid of the lack of customization in the modules system, and instead of Power Gears just allow the player to upgrade by spending crystals and any other basic currency from combat to upgrade their character.-Time Shift and numbered weapon uses, useless mechanics that do nothing but attempt to trick the player to make more mistakes and waste time in a terrible way. Instead of these gameplay methods, I recommend that Time Shift instead becomes an ability that allows the player to switch the level they are in to either day or night in order to fight optional bosses and find upgrades or collectibles that they would not be able to find without using this ability, and also this could be neat as it would allow the devs to make each single level be as if you are playing 2 levels in one. Get rid of the weapon uses and instead provide a meter that fills up as you use each of the weapon to then overcharge the weapon like you do with a break attack, this will allow that system to exist without having to make the player be punished with not possibly being able to use a weapon mid-combat because of something having too much health or the weapon they needed didn't drop another use in multiple previous combat encounters.-A lot of the levels have big open hallways and spaces that exist for no reason, and the train level in particular has a questionable design decision to move the train to get to a stairway that was clearly accessible by just jumping down from the railing above it the entire time. Make each level have true obstacles in the level that aren't just keycards, and make each level a hallway that has the player making use of your jumping, dashing, and wire system to acquire collectibles or find secrets to then go to open combat rooms with maybe some neat environmental objects or interactable things in them that allow the player and enemies to use their surroundings to their own advantages.-The story had me rolling my eyes and uninterested the entire time as Age, Helvis, Medea, Deucalion, and Atlas were nowhere near interesting of characters to make a good gateway to the attempts of depth to the setting that is as bare bones as can be, the humor is dry and boring, and any lore is just non-existent or dumped on you in dialogue out of nowhere. Make the basics of the story as good as possible, make the lore optional to the player, make your characters have a presence to the player even when they aren't on screen, make your protagonist, their allies, and enemies more captivating and likeable through giving them each a unique style of some sort and allowing them to shine in different, and exciting ways.-The roguelike delving idea is pretty neat but this needs some work, we need more level and room variations in it. More enemies and mixing of them to vary it up. More modifiers on the enemies and give some to the player to make things interesting for them as well. Optional bosses, collectibles, or bonuses of some sort that can in these.-Don't re-use bosses if you aren't going to give them new attacks, new movesets, or anything at all different about them. Also, make the arenas for bosses just as epic and interesting as the bosses themselves.-The soundtrack needs a lot more excitement in it to fit with the high-speed, tons of action mood that combat is meant to have. Use more rock and metal style instrumentals to kick things up a notch in combat, and make your non-combat tracks as grand as possible depending on the mood of the situation more often.I do not believe I am truly unfair with what I have stated here. I only pose these with the intent that improvement can be done. With these changes that I believe the devs are quite capable of doing, they'd have an action-indie gold mine to release to players that love action games, and character action games like myself and many others.

_childDocuments_.review: They say imitation is the highest form of flattery, and while the character action game genre in general were an inspiration for Ultra Age, the similarities to Nier Automata border on plagiarism. To be fair though, it is one of my favorite game of all time, so not the worst game to copy homework from.It's an indie creation from the land of worse sushi called kimbab and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ kpop culture, despite being indie the presentation is surprisingly decent. Visuals are a big potential draw, but somehow the game remained very niche at the time of writing this review. The optimization, particle effects and animations are surprisingly top notch, what is pretty apparent however is the unimaginative environment design, I'm not even talking about drawing similarities from environments and camera shifts of automata, more so how dull a lot of the corridors and arenas are (especially in the bloody palace mode HOLY F***), the more you look around the more the cracks start to show, the feeling that it's a rushjob of copy pasted assets and clutter, plastered around a unity map, never quite goes away. The enemy visual design is not too exciting, the robots share very similar visuals, and biological enemies are a few repeated crystal animals, then some variants are just recolors. All in all, it's a very competent looking game at first glance, with low budget starting to show only once you start playing it.However we all know the visuals are not the most important, and gameplay wise it's a decent game, they have neat mechanics of their own, and some borrowed from the genre classics. Different timed combos, several weapon types, light air juggling, invincibility dodge, enhanced combos through leveling, enemy weaknesses to certain weapon types, Nero grapple, "devil trigger", and most uniquely weapon durability, with special attacks when you break them. There is not a style meter to keep you switching the weapons around, but both enemy weakness and durability heavily incentivize it regardless. You'd think that with the weapon amount there is going to be huge overlap in weakness exploiting, when enemy types are only 2 - biological and mechanical, but some weapons have special effects of their own that are handy to keep around, most notably gun sword to apply bleed, and lightning sword to apply shock. I'd say the enemy encounters are somewhat hit or miss, at times it feels like there is not enough time to ever do a combo without getting hit, so you might resort to safe attacks like parry-riposte, or invincibility triggering weapon breaks, at times there is also too many projectiles around, and unlike Automata - your little pod (yes, I'm not joking, you get a pod in this game too) cannot shoot these projectiles down.There are also some weirder mechanics, like a time of day skip, changing the day-night cycle, as well as refreshing enemies and loot pickups (those are of course the weapons and healing charges), or upgrades so dumb they feel borderline useless - like the looting with your grapple, when you still need to be somewhat close to loot anyway, so that's several upgrade points wasted, for a potential 1-2 seconds save sometimes, said upgrade also doesn't work on loot crates that contain "modules", which are just randomize stat upgrades.Story is surprisingly, not a 1 to 1 copy of automata, though it does borrow a bit from it, I didn't pay a lot of attention to it as writing was extremely unengaging, I recall the main character being a clone that wants a power of immortaility, which is probably gathered through unethical means, and you discover some ruins of ancient civilization with rogue AI around, as well as those crystal corruptions spread around the place. Your pod is also a mcguffin of some sort, I'd guess it makes immortality gathering process more efficient and even more unethical and genocidal, there is like 3-4 characters in the whole game, so it's not like there is much to work with.Lastly the audio, combat audio is nice, some action sequence music is decent rock stuff, volume mixing is not AS f***ed as I'd expect from a small indie project, that said, I do wish some attacks would have better audio tells before you get hit, some of them feel unsynced, some get drowned out etc., and with how many enemies they like to throw in the arena, surrounding you from all sides at times, it makes it a rough time, with how much camera turning you need to do, it might unironically be one of the few char action games that are easier to play on KB+M instead of a pad.Overall, it's a decent 6 hour action game, I didn't like it as much as Assault Spy, but I don't regret buying and playing it, you can probably pick it up at decent sales too. And there is a free dlc included now, that's just a bloody palace with some rogue-lite elements, it's a tad unbalanced, and feels like some HP upgrades have been cut from the mode, but it's not "unbeatable" or anything, just takes a tad to practice. Still, don't let the runtime fool you, I had the game running idle, I'd say I've played main game for like 6 hours and bloody palace for probably 10-12, so if you don't vibe with second mode, you get 1/3rd of total potential playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game in all honesty.To get the story out of the way first..... well, it could be better but it's mostly passable. It has some standard anime tropes and bits you can see coming from a mile away.I played the game with Japanese voice acting and that was fine! There is a few minor moments where the voice acting doesn't quite deliver but i'd say it's a 99% positive experience. Good job on the Japanese voice actors!But what we really play these games for is the combat and I can say that the combat although a little bit basic is really really solid. It feels smooth, responsive, swapping between weapons is easy and has that same smooth feeling. If I had to give it 1 gripe is that it doesn't reward you enough to swap weapons around. Match the weapon with what the enemy is weak to and you basically have the winning combo.An example of this is the claymore vs the katana, the katana is strong vs biological enemies but weak vs mechanical, this makes it so the katana basically does like 10% of the dmg the claymore would do vs the mechanical enemies. So you just spam the same attack with the claymore to win easily. And this is another small issue, or big depending how you look at it, the movesets across all weapons are basically the same. Atk > heavy, Atk atk > heavy, etc etc. So it makes every weapon feel a bit samey. But because the combat feel so smooth and responsive this isn't too much of an issue but your mileage may vary.This issue of the weapon damage penalty is resolved in the free roguelite mode DLC a bit cause the extreme penalty is removed. You just get 100% of base dmg and a strong weapon get's the damage bonus (Example: Katana does 100 dmg vs a mechanical enemy but the claymore does 130, in the story mode this was more like the katana does 10 dmg the claymore does 200). This makes it so it isn't a heavy punishment to swap weapons around and it feels good putting your blades on almost breaking and just swapping between them dishing out multiple break blade attacks which do a lot of damage.But generally the combat just feels really really good. Could I recommend it for $21? No. The story is way too short for that at only ~5 hours including watching all cutscenes and the roguelite mode can be cleared in about another 3-5 hours and doesn't really require any of that typical roguelite grinding. But on a sale? Most definitely! If this dev team had some more budget and maybe time for an ultra age 2 or another game, adding more weapons, a broader moveset they would have an absolute winner on their hands. As it sits right now if I had to give the game a grade I would say a solid 7/10 leaning towards a 7.5 simply because the combat system feels so smooth and responsive.

_childDocuments_.review: I played an indie spectacle fighter, Assault Spy, and really enjoyed it. Ever since then, I've tried various indie games that LOOK like spectacle fighters, hoping that I'll find the same enjoyment. Unfortunately, most of those games play more like God of War 3 (or worse), and I end up disappointed.Enter Ultra Age. It LOOKS like it should play like Devil May Cry. You can switch between 4 weapons on the fly, you can cancel your attacks to do combos, it looks really cool, etc… However, because of fundamental design flaws, it doesn't play like Devil May Cry at all. Let's take for example combos. In Ultra Age, you can do various pre-determined combos (e.g. light attack + heavy attack will do one combo, light attack + light attack + heavy attack will do a different combo, etc…). However, you're not incentivized to do any combos that take too long since the enemy will start attacking you before you can complete it. Furthermore, you can straight up do more damage by doing 2 small combos (i.e. light attack + heavy attack) instead of doing 1 long combo (e.g. light attack + light attack + light attack + heavy attack). This means that instead of playing the game by trying out various different combos as you progress through the game, you quickly learn the optimal combos for each weapon:	• Katana: Heavy attack + change blade attack, heavy attack + change blade attack, repeat…	• Claymore: Light attack + heavy attack, light attack + heavy attack, repeat…	• Lightning Blade:  Light attack + heavy attack + heavy attack, light attack + heavy attack + heavy attack, repeat…Doing the same combos over and over again isn't fun. While you can choose to try other attacks, there's little incentive and you're going to quickly get bored since despite the game having 6 different weapons, they fundamentally play the exact same as each other (hell, two of them are basically copies with one being the "Claymore" and another being the "Charge Claymore"). They're all swords, and a lot of their attacks do the exact same thing (e.g. Light attack + light attack + light attack + heavy attack is the same for all of the weapons). So there's no incentive to create crazy combos, combining different weapons since the weapons are so similar to each other. Instead of creating crazy combos, the game allows you to press one button to do a cool looking attack that does a lot of damage AND you're invincible for the entire attack animation. This is balanced by the fact that you can only do this when the durability of your weapons gets low (weapons can break in this game, but it's not a big deal since you can equip like 15 of each weapon). However, while this LOOKS cool, it doesn't provide any sense of achievement since all you did is press a button to use the attack.Even if you felt like trying to use different weapons in your combos, the game discourages you from doing so. This is because different weapons are effective against different types of enemies. The Katana is effective against biological enemies whereas the claymore and lightning blade are effective against mechanical enemies. When I say "effective" I mean doing like…… 75% more damage than a weapon that is "ineffective". This means that you will always be using the same weapons over and over again.It also doesn't help that there's very limited enemy variety, and that you'll be facing the same enemies over and over again. There are like 2 biological enemies (a bird and a jaguar) and like 4 mechanical enemies (a robot, a ranged robot, a flying ranged robot, and a "heavy" robot). In regards to your defensive options, while the game is competent, it's nothing special. You have a dodge and a parry (in the form of the change blade attack on your claymore). It's pretty easy to both dodge and parry enemy attacks (both have pretty generous windows). You also have an energy bar that fills up as you defeat enemies. You can use 25% of your energy to basically recover 25% of your health. So you're typically not that afraid of dying.One good thing about the game are the bosses. They look really cool and are pretty decent to fight. I just wish they were more challenging, since I beat most bosses on the first try. At max it took me like 3 tries to beat a boss.The progression system is very…..strange. You have a classic skill tree where you can get passive benefits such as increased damage, new moves, etc… However, there's also a "module" system in that you can equip up to 6 modules to get various stat benefits (i.e. higher health, damage, critical rate, critical damage, armor, and a "master" module that increases all stats). What's weird about this system is that it's very restrictive, in that you can't equip more than 1 "type" of module at the same time (i.e. you can't have 2 damage modules, only one). What this means is that after getting a good type of the module (e.g. a rare damage module), you'll never be excited to find another damage module again. For like 90% of the modules that dropped from enemies or that I encountered out in the wild, I never cared about them since my current modules were better.There's a story, but it's pretty barebones. There's absolutely no world/lore building done and you're simply thrown into the world with little to no explanation. There's the main characters, Age and Helvis, who are apparently really good friends. There's Medea, who's apparently supposed to be some badass that you should be scared of. There's Deucalion, who's some super smart leader or something. But just because the game SAYS these things, doesn't mean I accept it/understand the significance of it. For example, in like the tutorial level Helvis "dies" and Age is really upset about this and swears revenge. Welp, just because the character is really upset by it doesn't mean the audience is since I only spent like 20 minutes with Helvis so who cares if he "died". ♥♥♥♥ like that happens a lot where something happens and the characters seem to care a lot, but I simply didn't since the game does a very poor job of making me invested in the world.Overall, Ultra Age was pretty repetitive. While the game looks great, the fundamental gameplay is pretty flawed.

_childDocuments_.review: t's the year 3XXX, and humanity isn't doing too good. The planet that appears to be Earth is inhabited by robots, mutated animals and colour-coded crystals. The remaining humanity seems to exist as part of [ORBIT], while the last people on Earth were part of [FRONTIER]. The story is pretty cryptic, and the game could've used a Codex. You play as Age, a member of [ORBIT]'s Exploration Division, tasked with recovering a piece of technology referred to as [FRONTIER] relic. Along with your companion AI, Helvis you collect the relic, which makes you a target of the [ORBIT] Combat Division. What ensues is a journey for Age and Helvis to find a ship and get back to [ORBIT], killing loads of things in the process The game is mostly linear hack and slash action-adventure. The game's main mechanic revolves around Age's nano-blade, which can take different forms, based on the kinds of crystals he picks up. Different blades are effective against different enemy types, and each blade has a durability limit. Once the weapon gets close to breaking, you have the option to shatter it, dealing increased damage, before re-fashioning the blade (as long as you have enough crystals to do so). Each blade has its own skill tree, but I found that towards the end of the game I had excessive currency to upgrade everything I wanted—although the game features the “enemies respawn whenever you do” mechanic, there's no penalty on death and no corpse runs, so currency stacks infinitely. Each weapon has same basic combos from chaining light and heavy attacks, with additional effects being available via the skill tree. One weapon does bonus damage to animals, and another to robots, so you'll constantly have those 2 in your 4 weapon slots, most likely. There's 2 basic enemy types- animals and robots. Robots have different attack patterns, but they tended to blend together. There's no parrying so dash-dodge is critical. In some areas, it's possible to get caught in a corner, where the camera goes haywire, and a few enemies finish you off “off-screen”. However, I didn't find this particularly annoying, and that's something that can happen in any 3rd person hack'n'slash. Oh, there's also a grappling hook, so you can pull weak enemies towards yourself, or propel yourself towards the bigger foes. The game's highlight are the bosses. There's a fair amount of variety here (although a few get reused at one point). Still, considering the game only has 4 main levels (plus intro and final boss arena), I was pleasantly surprised. Getting to credits took about 11 hours- and there's a roguelike tower maze DLC that lets you fight different enemy combos, which I haven't tried. The game's levels are linear, but occasionally you have to go into randomly generated mazes to fight in a bunch of arenas until you find a miniboss that drops a key item so you can move on with the main game. Overall, a fairly simple game, with some memorable boss fights.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat feels good and really fun.
