_childDocuments_.review: BUYER BEWARE, This is NOT a game, this is just another VR Techdemo that was put together in a haste and then abandoned. The developer promised Multiplayer and it never happened, the trailer is misleading because you think it has Multiplayer but it's just some disembodied Kayaks that follow a path trough some goals and they call this "racing". It only has like 4-5 maps and except one, they're all an open area for you to paddle around. I'm really disappointed this is not a Game, I was expecting paddling down a river rapids and maybe getting some Multiplayer, but this is not it.Note: This is why VR failed, there's a few gems worth playing but most of the "Games" are just abandoned concepts and tech demos that go nowhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I waited long for the decision; to refund or not. I'd like to support the dev, especially because they're Dutch :-). But, unfortunately, I have to agree with the negative comments. I refunded. It just isn't enough. The dessert map is very short, the other maps have square km's (or at least they seem to have), but not much content either. Imagine a 2D game that has very few maps, even less content and a pricetag of 20 euro's... it would probably have no more than 20% positive reviews. Apparently you can get away with that on VR, but for me it isn't enough. Maybe I'll try again in a few years from now, after many content upgrades.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: For the 20 minutes it worked, it looked pretty good, but the kayaking controls felt weird and there's not a lot to do.After first boot the game lags out or just crashes completely (WMR hp reverb g2)Would probably work on an oculus headset, so it's probably a fault of the reverb, but it was annoying as hell.impressive as a showcase but barely a game, really.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:  Turned out tit was my Valve Index Tether cable causing a lot of issues! I replaced the tether cable and now it runs smooth!  With as side effect,severe muscle pain ! Thank you for that! I clearly need the training! :)  Looks amazing, but my PC  clearly can not handle it. Very laggy and I get very motion sick in a very short time. (with rtl 2080 super +  3700x + Valve Index)This one will  be collecting dust  in my library until I get a hardware upgrade.  Still a vote up based on my first impression.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Visually outstanding game, that has a variety of maps that look incredibly different from one another and will all leave you in awe. The developers are all wonderful people and communicate with the players so well. If you enjoy a step down from the real world and want to look around beautiful landscapes this game allows that. And if you want to race through tight courses and try and get your best time this game also allows that! I highly recommend this game to anyone with even slight interest
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not gonna give it a like or a dislike button. This game is the exact middle.Graphically, this is one of the best looking games on VR, Obviously they went for the "Whoa" factor when creating this.BUT for a normal VR user who is not into kayaking or sports...that's it. You see these beautiful areas and then it gets repetative afterwards. The other problem is that while the areas are BEAUTIFUL, they are pretty small and you can go around them in less 10 minutes. For now this a pretty small, pretty cool experience for VR, but nothing more than that. I would say pick it up when I'ts on sale, MAYBE they add more levels in the future ? but for those 4-5 levels the game containing, I'ts not worth full price in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: While the graphics seem nice at first you start to realize that it's all just high quality assets that don't really fit together. There is no artstyle and no design, the maps seem strangely lifeless. There is no gameplay except the paddling which is interesting and fun for about 1 or 2 hours. But there is no actual game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This is the prettiest VR game I've EVER seen.The gameplay is simple, relaxing and satisfying.The sound design is perfect, with a solid sense of depth and brilliant music direction.The controls are intuitive and immersiveThe physics feel satisfying - the water looks great.The game performs excellently at 90hz and with some tweaking it can really maximize your GPUs potential.This game has the looks of Chris Hemsworth, but the soft velvety touch of Hugh Jackman
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: What I like the most is doing a smooth and efficient run. It's (not that) easy to learn, but hard to master. So I expect to spend quite some time on each track.The kayaking sensation is great and quite a workout for the upper body, as far as it's possible in VR. And of course the environments quality is a huge cherry on the top.I played the demo for a couple of hours (on one track) and the complete game is what I hoped for, more content and varied conditions.Didn't explore it fully yet, had to refrain my perfectionist side to have a taste of everything. So far it's great, I'll confirm it after having played for 10 hours or so.It's funny to see ghosts struggling wildly in the rocks and stuff like that. Though when I was the one in the rocks, I had to restart as soon as I passed the finish line to overwrite the evidence :D Then sometimes admiring my own ghost messing-up, but hopefully I'm in front.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game! Ive played the demo for this game in the last two steam next fests, and I was ecstatic to see it release. It is probably the most graphically impressive vr game out right now, even beating half life alyx. (we'll see if hubris will beat it out or not.) It is absolutely stunning. I thoroughly enjoyed playing the 3 new maps. They have cool and unique things to explore. I look forward to chasing after achievements and doing races which I have not touched at all yet. Can definitely see myself playing this for hours on end in the coming months. Well worth the price!extra note: I dont know if there are plans to add more maps, but if so, I cant wait to see what the team will come up with.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: If you're thinking of getting this to have a relaxing time slowly coasting through beautiful environments, this game isn't it because there is stuttering when the kayak turns and this causes motion sickness for me. This stuttering only happens when the kayak turns. If you turn your head when the kayak is not turning, there is no stuttering. If the kayak is moving straight, there is no stuttering. But when the kayak turns, oh boy, the stuttering starts and the motion sickness starts soon after.There is a smoothing option in the game and it reduces the stuttering but there is still too much stuttering even when this setting is maxed out. I lowered the graphics settings to the lowest and there is no effect at all on the stuttering. ASW doesn't help either. GPU can be at less than 50% utilization and yup, still stutters when the kayak turns. My rig: PIco 4 with Pico Connect, AMD 7600X with 64Gb RAM, running Windows 11 (Resizable BAR is on, HAGS is off) off an NVME SSD and RTX 4070. It's not the hardware: there is something not working correctly with the game when the kayak is turning.On the forums you get people who claim the game is "well optimized" and runs perfectly smooth. Well, I can run DCS and IL2 smoothly, and those games are not known to be "well optimized" so no, this game is far from being "well optimized". Yes, there are posts on the forum about this stuttering that only shows up when the kayak is turning, but you get a bunch of white knights minimizing the problem that these people faced. I now realize this sort of toxic behaviour is actually a sign that I"m going to regret a purchase: there's a chance I'm going to face the exact problem, and then what will I do?If you do decide to take a chance on this game (and who can blame you because the game does look gorgeous ... as long as the kayak doesn't turn), be prepared to return the game if you do notice the stuttering that only happens when the kayak turns. Don't do what I did and try to tweak the game and then realize the 2hr window to return the game ran out.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't had a VR experience stimulate me like this since theBlu from 2016.  Absolutely stunning!  The visual polish will blow you away and drown out all awareness of the real world.  You'll be transported to the most beautiful parts of our planet Earth and never want to leave. Costa Rica is my favorite, with the Canyon and the Arctic not to far behind.  Norway still looks incredible but just doesn't have enough to explore in my opinion.  The music selection is also right on point and I haven't felt the need to mute it even though I would in any other "experience nature" type game.  It just accompanies each scene perfectly. This is a complete experience as is and all their planned updates are just extra gravy.  I would love to see more set piece type additions like the crumbling ice in the arctic, or other small things to bring life to each scene.  There is a waterfall in another app called Grand Canyon VR that was executed perfectly in both its animation and the sound design of passing though it, and I would love to see something similar here.  A quiet trolling motor would be a great addition for people like me that are probably never going to touch the racing.  Maybe a couple landing spots on shore where you can just sit and take it in like their Meditation VR app could be nice.This team clearly knows how to make eye catching scenery and I don't want to tell them how to do their jobs better, but there are a couple things I think could be improved if they're open to input.  The main one being night time scenes.  The lighting just doesn't look as good as it could.  Maybe its better on OLED headsets but on my LCD Index, its a smidge to dark and doesn't add any magic to the scene.  Maybe they're going for realism but I think they should make night time scenes look more mystical and fantastic.  Give me a larger then life moon and make everything well lit and blue. I noticed there is an option to turn off water ripples, but they don't bother me at all and actually do add to the immersion for me. However, the splashes caused by the paddle don't look very good to me and I'd prefer an option to turn those off.The distant water in the Arctic doesn't look as good as the distant water in the Costa Rica or Norway for some reason.  I can see the tiling and some weirdness with the reflections that don't show up at all in any of the other scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: It's really a great beautiful game to , (Played the Beta)The handling is great and you can put your controllers on a stick and a fan for even greater immersion.When racing but not trying to get world records I average at 10 kcal/min. (Top is 14.7 kcal/min)After 30 hours in it, searched for all the achievements, I will still play it :)I had to try canoe IRL because of the game, both are great
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Paddled about a bit. Looked about, realised I was extremely bored in a sterile VR world with nothing to do, the graphics are nice and the water looks great but not like "oh my god it's so real" levels like some people say. I think it would appeal to some people that like boat stuff but me personally? Nah.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves kayaking (I just got back from a week-long trip), this game is almost a dream come true! The environments look absolutely stunning and although the physics are not perfect, they come pretty close to reality. There is room for improvement of course. For example, the kayak often seems to drift to the left - even when I'm only paddling on the left side. The ambient sounds could also be improved, and the music seemed a bit bland - I turned it off almost immediately. But those are just minor criticisms. So far I'm really enjoying the game, and it seems like a pretty good workout, too! I hope there will be new environments to explore in the future.Edit: I listened to the music a bit more and some if it is actually pretty nice and relaxing. But turning the music is off more immersive of course. Speaking of immersive: kayaking right next to a giant whale is an awesome experience which actually made me feel a litte bit queasy.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: The Oar needs to rotate when you rotate your hands together.  It just moves like you have hooks on your hands and 2 pivot points.  You can't reposition your hands on the oar, nor see your hands which is disappointing.  For a game where you're just sat in place holding an oar, not much attention was paid to the immersion of holding an oar which other than the movement of the kayak and the scenery is all there is.  The paddling is also a bit odd.  Sometimes pushing off rocks doesn't push the kayak the correct direction which is also odd.Also, real kayaks feature a neoprene apron around the pilot but not this one.  Why not?  It would cover the immersion breaking "person-less" inside of the kayak and could also offer some sound design when you rock or move around.  Missed opportunity.I was prepared to really like the scenery when I loaded up the first area and the feeling was decent but the graphics were meh.  Everything was set to Epic and default as the game loaded.  Is there an auto -detect script running to see the hardware the game is running on or does it just parse the DirextX info?  Dynamic shadows where off, does this have a GI implementation?   I have a 3080ti and I would expect all options to be on to begin with.  Set everything from Epic to Cinematic, turned on dynamic shadows (not sure that even changed much?), and turned the resolution scale up to 150% and THEN the detail in the scenery pOpped.  Still no frame drops and this way the scenery did in fact look very realistic.Its just odd that it didn't look that way on Epic, a bit odd.Other than those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, a great shoulder workout and cool areas to relax or paddle around in.I'd guess you need some beef in your PC to actually get the most out of this but if you do, its quite interesting.Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this experience is decently fun to spend an hour or two in; however, unless they add live multiplayer or other engaging single player content, the game-play just simply isn't fun enough on its own. You can only wonder in awe at the beauty of their maps for so long. Don't expect to be finding boatloads of fun here. Just gorgeous scenery.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, clearly some good stuff to explore and so far a very relaxing experience… my kids were very happy to discover the penguins!I would like to see some river runs, and one thing that would absolutely seal the deal is if the developer can add telemetry out so I can use my motion platform - this game would be absolutely perfect for bobbing up and down on a motion rig! Look forward to playing this more and keep fingers crossed for some DLC for rivers! Great job.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Just wow. I am really surprised how awesome it looks with all the little details in VR. The performance is very good and you can fine tune it with a lot of graphics settings (it even supports Nvidia DLSS).I just wanted to have a quick look at it and stayed for almost two hours on my first session. And I wasn't even on a single race - I just enjoyed the view on the four big locations and I'm very sure I haven't seen it all.Definitely recommended, the price is also fair.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap! Finally something with impressive fidelity on a 3090, played with a friend (its not multiplayer) but we streamed our screens in vr with discord, was a really relaxing way to meetup in VR. Taped my controllers to a 5 foot PVC pipe I had laying around and it was a massive deltoid / tricep workout!!! 2 hours in and a lot more to explore, only looked at two of the 4 worlds. Cant wait to show this to family and play more!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Its an overall nice experience even for someone who never had anything to do with this sport.The game runs good for the well made graphics but dont expect the best looking game ever - specialy on something like the quest 2 you will have the usual distance pixelation and it needs alot of tweaking to get a decent result - specialy for someone like me who wants clean graphics.It can also be fairly demanding on the body depending on how you play it and how you are sitting and it can be a good workout for the upper body.Some negative points:- Some areas can be too dark to see anything . even during daytime.- Graphic settings dont allow enough customization of certain effects etc.- DLSS implementation is really bad! Something is totaly wrong here!- Physics can sometimes be a bit frustrating - picking up speed can be difficult.- Performance on the new DLC Map is noticeable worse and very inconsistent (low fps near Waterdrops)If you are into kayaking then this is a solid recomendation - specialy on sale and with the new dlc despite its issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Even on my aging 2080 this game looks mind-boggingly phenomenal. For the slow exploration part of the game, ASW/SSW/motion smooting is very acceptable which allows for stunningly high resolutions. But even without pushing the GPU past the reprojection level the game looks better than anything I have seen to date. How did you guys pull this off?Besides the graphics, controlling the kayak is very well done too. It took me a bit to really figure it out but after chasing kingjets ghost through a glacier I got the hang of it. Contentwise there is not a staggering amount, but between the exploration and the handful of races each map has this is definitely worth the money, even if it's only to see how well it looks everytime you upgrade your PC.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of the old immersive experiences back when VR first came out.  It's a great way to show off VR to guests, just sit down and go.  The DLC is a must have, my favorite of any of the locations, I hope they have more rapids coming soon.  I highly recommend this!  My only con is the bird animations.   Work on that and it's perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Not a ton here to enjoy, but the replayability is great. The kayaking is a middle-point between unbelievably realistic and easy to master. There's not a ton of ways to get it wrong- if your paddle goes in you'll get forward momentum without having to think about the angle of the fin. The locations are a mix of relaxing Australian canyons and scary, thunderous fjords of Norway. I'd give it an 7.5/10. Great for stress relief but I would argue against using it for exercise, as you're basically just flailing your arms for race time. Once there are more maps and bundles, I would bump it up to an 8.5.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy kayaking outdoors and in the winter time this is a nice way to fulfil my desire to go kayaking when it's too cold outside.  The kayaking physics feel pretty good, and +there is an arcade and simulation mode.  The environments are beautiful and the water looks pretty good except it could be a bit better where the water meets the land.  There are no currents so it always feels like you are in perfectly calm water.  That is one thing I wish it had as it feels strange not having to make adjustments for mild currents and the wind blowing you around a bit.  Overall I think it is great for what it is and I am glad I bought it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. Can't wait to play it with a next gen headset in the future. Hopefully they keep adding depth to the game. More intersting areas in each map and more maps. I love the immersion when  playing with 1lb wrist weights, going to try 2lb wrist weights when they arrive. Hopefully they'll have at least 1v1 coop and/or racing with friends someday. Looks great maxed out on my aging pimax 5k vision and my 7900x/4090, I just need a higher rez headset now.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some serious potential, wish it had live multiplayer and more things to do. It's sad for me because I have never been so immersed and meditative inside a VR title.If you are into kayaking, rafting, or any kind of paddling you will dig this game more than any other on VR almost guaranteed. There is nothing like this anywhere else in gaming and I can't wait for the devs to build on this fantastic skeleton.I recommend the Prosaber by ProtubeVR for a paddle because i found it to be the perfect size and form for a realistic experience without taping your controllers to a broomstick.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: More than just pretty graphics!Stunning experience, great to show off to family and friends. If you have fun exploring the different maps in free mode, there is actually a lot to discover (check the achievements).The races are short and fun. They can be challenging if you are going for the gold medal.Very excited for future updates and more content!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best experiences I've had in VR. A very nice realistic graphic. Very good physics. Good sound. Here you can see how VR can be. Definitely a buy recommendation if you want to chill or do some sport, as there is also an opponent mode. I hope there will be more DLC in the future to see more places. Four at the moment.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game play with fantastic lighting and scenery.  The controls are so simple that anyone can just jump into and play, but also includes many additional options for more customized and 'sim-like' experience.On top of that, the Kayak interaction and controls seem very dead-on to what it feels like the Kayak, which I've personally had a decent bit of experience with. The motions and the reactions to those motions were exactly what I had been used to; It was amazing.You can choose between racing others or simply explore areas at your own pace.I never thought I'd enjoy the non-racing mode as much as I did... but it can be very relaxing and makes for a nice break between racing to let your arms cool down. It's an incredibly peaceful experience in that mode.Keep up the great work; Can't wait to see what comes next from the team!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Feels fantastic and I like the added feature of being able to stick your head underwater to see the fish and turtles.  But PLEASE add some loading screens.  It takes over a minute for the worlds to load and there is just a black screen the entire loading time.  I stopped the program five or six times before I realized I should try and wait it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: (NEUTRAL) Beautiful graphics with nice mechanics however as others have stated, this is merely an experience and not particularly a game. There isnt really much to do after you've had a look around 4 areas give or take. Race mode is against what I assume ghosts of players or bots and not multiplayer.  Seems just like a demo which makes the price a little unjustifiable for now. The game does seem like it can be built upon so maybe there will be updates in the future. It will be a great game if it gets further developed.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible! Been exploring the ice caves and got borked at in a storm! The light reflecting off the rocks from the lightning was fantastic! Really chill game with some competitive racing I doubt I'll bother with much, might be wrong but not really my thing, I'll probably set one or two times though just to try it. Can't access the store yet so can't comment on what that's about but hopefully new locations to explore, will update this when it's out. Well worth the money, good work devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing VR experience.  Graphics are outstanding, and the water physics are realistic.  Kayaking through the various locales is super relaxing, and I've enjoyed exploring the maps over and over.  The racing is fun too.  I hope the developer adds content because I would love to see other locations.  Highly recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: By far visually best looking game to date! Yes, even better than Half-Life: Alyx. I was stunned, when I first started in Costa-Rica. With Varjo VR-3 and RTX 3080Ti its almost like true life. So many details and surprises along the trip. It feels totally alive. Water effects are the best I have seen in VR. Surpassed my expectations and they were high. I would pay even 40 EUROS for such quality content. Would be nice to have more places to go in the future. Areas are pretty big to discover. You could easily hang around in one area an hour, looking these amazing alive surroundings. Definately suggest to grab this game whatever is the price!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: If you actually kayak then you are in for a bad time. The game wants you to use tiny little arm movements because if you use a proper paddle stroke it will have you turning left when paddling forward on the left hand side, I presume the engine thinks you are paddling backwards at this point... Back paddling worked fine though.....
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very much into VR experiences that arent necessarily games, but realistic relaxing places to destress, like Google Earth VR, Ocean Rift Mixed Reality Mode, etc. This app fits the bill. Its beautiful, its realistic, though I do think it ztilñ needs more. I wish it could take us to places like the Venice Canals, etc to experience those places in VR. I also wish they would bring this natively to the Quest 3. Regardless, kudos to the devs for a well put together experience and hopefully they make progress with their roadmap.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Best looking game/experience atm. 8 euro for 1 DLC map is a bit much but it's extra long, has fast parts with a waterfall drop and the trees look amazing. Besides, this is a niche HQ-experience in the niche PCVR market basically excluding anyone without a high end graphics card. I'm just glad they're still putting effort into this.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute to sit in a kayak and the feeling pushing yourself off a solid object is nice... so is witnessing the stormy weather - and while the graphics are better than most VR titles, they are not good enough to impress. I know, the screenshots talk big game, but the VR experience really isn't that. If you want visuals in VR just play Alyx or the Lab.I found myself drawn to paddle to places that turned out to be outside the map boundaries causing you to get reset (the maps are freaking tiny!).The experience looses it's appeal rapidly, and then there's no game to be had beyond a poor racing gamelet which is purely about cheesing how the paddles move, making it not even fun.On sale for the experience, maybe, but I was expecting so much more for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Looked very promising and the swiming pool test level performed flawlessly, but as soon as I tried a real level, the framerate immediately dropped to nauseating levels - setting the graphics to the lowest possible settings did not help. A Ryzen 3700X, 32G RAM and RTX 2060 was insufficient even though it ought to at least match the minium requirements.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This is certainly worth the money.The game has stunning graphics and amazing physics with the kayak, making paddling even at higher speeds feel smooth as you glide across the water.Being able to interact with things, push yourself off walls or rocks when you get too close is an amazing feature that this game absolutely nailed.I love the smaller achievements that this game has to offer, making it fun to go around and help animals and find hidden areas.The game feels as good as it looks, this is a must try, and for the price you're really getting a discounted price.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning environments and immersion. A level above the other VR environments I've experienced to date. Quite a workout too!Initially, I was a bit disorientated by the bobbing of the kayak, but adjusted to it fairly quickly.Works REALLY well on my Quest 2 via optical USB link cable. Have a decent Ryzen PC with an RTX3070 - but only after a reboot as the other software I run seems to leak memory!Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something else. When combining 120 hz refresh rate, controllers on the stick and with these stunning graphics on 2.0 resoliution scale i actualy feel that i am there, in a virtual world that just looks, feels and sounds like real life.I fell in love with this game. I recommend this to everyone. I would love to see more content for this game (new maps, boats, etc...).
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not even sure where to begin with this review.Kayak VR: Mirage is simply mesmerizing and beautiful and well worth the money just for the experience of paddling around and taking in the scenery. It's gorgeous and I feel I still have so much to explore in the environments.Some of the criticism is that the content is lacking, and I can see that. If you're not hugely into racing or want to play this often, the content that is currently there can get stale fast. I was worried about that myself, but I think what's important to consider is this game's future.The promises of future development are what convinced me to buy it, because I want to support the huge potential of KVR:M moving forward. This is obviously a passion project, and I have faith in the devs to bring it to the next level. Free roam and racing real-time multiplayer is going to contribute immensely here, as are new environments, more weather, more game modes and more wildlife.Even if you find the content lacking at this stage, I still think it's worth the purchase as an investment in the game's future. I will continue to enjoy this for a while to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing stuff.  My shoulders are burning and so is my PC in this 36 degree heat but its worth it.  Looks fantastic (Some serious witchcraft going on there!), plays great and is one hell of a shoulder workout, even without resistance.10/10 Would get a family member to occasionally spray water in my face again.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Whether you like Kayaking or not this is still an essential VR purchase, instead of trying to be a jack of all trades Kayak VR Mirage has a laser focus on being a master of one and it absolutely nails it. The feeling of paddling through these gorgeous locations with their beautiful soundscapes is unlike any other PC VR game in recent memory. It's great to see a title pushing the power of PC VR again, I'm already excited at the prospect of future locations and I wish this dev team all the very best! Genuinely brilliant work!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This sure is a really relaxing experience, if that's what you're after.It can also be an intense and sweaty experience if you do some of the races.I'm liking that it has some things to interact with in the water, like inflatables that has small quests for you and other things like driftwood and trash (plastic bottles etc).There's also alot of animals to see, both in water and air.Graphics are superb, even with my 1080ti.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. The feel of the kayak on the water is so great. The translucent look in the shallow water is sublime. The rock textures are fantastic. Some areas are larger than others, but all are unique. Free exploration is perfect. Still haven't done so well at the racing. The main thing is the need for more. Venice Canals. The Chicago River. Autumn Splendor. Haunted Hills. Winter Retreat. More...Even Larger areas. Day/Night cycle if wanted. Rock On!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing game for VR. The ability to deeply immerse yourself in such beautiful maps with not only stunning visual graphics, but killer audio design is so good while also getting a killer workout. AND THEY JUST ADDED MULTIPLAYER!!!!!The game offers great multiplayer with the full ability to see your friend's avatar and boat in real time. I couldn't be more pleased with Kayak VR and i hope people will give this game a try because its so worth it
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write a lot of reviews, but I feel compelled to add mine to what I see as watermark vr experience/game. I was especially motivated by a negative review here that said that the graphics for this are "meh". They're not. Obviously. And it's hard to imagine anything more immersive than rowing this kayak.  I read a comment somewhere that said the devs hope to add fishing as a feature. That would be amazing! Imagine a big fish dragging the kayak along as it tries to run......yes please!!Update; the new DLC? Wow. Just wow. I remember seeing whitewater on the road map, but I really thought that would be something much further down the road. Amazing job by the devs, and all running just fine on my GTX 1070. I wish some of the newer vr games were optimized so well. I don't meet the minimum specs for an awful lot of the new games coming out, but I can still run titles like this and HL:Alyx? C'mon!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: It does not take more than one hour to like this "game", it is super relaxing and having done a fair bit of kayak and canoeing the physics are spot on, worth mentioning that the dev was quite forward thinking having a whole array of settings if you place the controller on a pole (will do, already playing on a small bin bag sitting like on a kayak it is super immersive). As some have said the locations are currently few, however I can see these released partially as addon and DLC, I would not mind paying for even more detailed macro-locations to explore.I would find cool if there was a way to play own songs directly in game, however easily done on PC by simply lowering in game music and opening whatever player.Playable no issue on cinamatic on a 1080ti with 8700k - there is Fidelity FX which is the first time I ever used and actually add that bit of FPS to make it better, graphics here are photo-realistic and water is stunning.I do a fair bit of Flight Simulation, which in VR is really stunning, and I have to say that this is just right next to it for me. More, bigger, locations and mechanics and this would be a top VR game of all time!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome and the graphics beautifuls but we absolutly need more maps to explored et really more big ,it would be cool if we could do a slowly long exploration ride in the jungle or anywhere and add a option for ride with friends in local and online like 2-4 players togethers. It work great with i7 10700F and GTX 1660 ,default settings ,just put msaa and it's not the perfection but look great and good performance on my Quest 2 with airlink ,no steam vr.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't tried the multiplayer race mode, but I love the "free roam" aspect of the game. While some of the maps are limited, the Antarctica and Costa Rica environments have a fair amount of content to explore. This is a must-have title for anyone who enjoys realistic and breathtaking virtual scenery. The world-building is top-notch. Everything looks amazing on my Reverb G2. I was very impressed with the thunderstorm effects in the Norway map and the lush jungle river in Costa Rica. As for the kayaking part, the water physics and paddle mechanics are reasonably believable and straightforward to learn. It's easy to work up a sweat by paddling quickly, but I still consider it to be a casual experience. It probably won't appeal to you if you only like games with "frenetic" and "rogue-like" in the description. If you're a fan of walking simulators and meditation apps, this is perfect for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are very nice, I have most settings on cinematic and 1.6 render scale with a 3080 and it runs at 80 fps.  The game is fun, sights are beautiful, racing is fun but very hard.  Its a good workout too.  This is a great game to relax in, or work up a sweat.  VR controls are great too, there is almost no jank at all.It needs more maps, but its still great for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I've really put more time into this game and ...TL/DR - Thank you for this game, for me it is a life changing experience!I recently found this game two days ago.I watched a few YouTube reviews, checked the steam reviews, bought the game ... LOVED IT and then used my 3d printer to make attachments for a wooden rod so now I have an oar ... this took the game to a whole new level!I love VR, I really love getting into and learning new and complex processes.I am also a Combat Veteran with tours in Iraq, East Timor and Afghanistan and deal with the subsequent PTSD.I also work in a hospital, no pressure with that one ... lol (I am actually on-call for the week as I write this).This game / application is so much more to me than a game.It gives me a chance to relax like I've not had in my home beforeI can really, truly immerse myself in it, I can explore at my own pace, with no external pressures.I can't express how grateful I am, truly grateful.It's hard to decompress and when I am on-call (it goes for 7 days, 24 hours a day in that week), the stress and lack of sleep builds up quickly.so, from the bottom of my heart, thank you!Thank you so very much.Also, I live in the USA now, but am an Australian.I love the Australian environment (feels like the Kimberly) ... it's just wonderfulThank you to all involved, best money ever spent on a game!Thank you. -----Original review:I've played for a bit over 30 minutes and this just blew me away!It is fun, relaxing and a workout on your shoulders too!Great graphics, love the physics.  The locations are great, I cant wait to get into it more.Just incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I've been in all kinds of VR games, and worlds in social platforms that I thought nothing could beat.... and this beats them all. _childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: this isnt just a gimmick VR experience, the gameplay from the races are super competitive and actually lend to a gameplay loop that you want to repeat, to shave off a couple secs on the leaderboards or just get some more 'sea miles' for new kayak colours and stuff. theres so many different modes like night or day or raining and they all have theyre own weather  conditions and leaderboards, i can see myself trying to top each one. plus really good exercise, you'll want to keep playing past your limits because its just so fun :Dand it's sooooooooooo pretty like ridiculously compared to most VR titles currently
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cool! Haven't enjoyed the "WOW" effect of a new VR game in a long time, this game made me feel it all! Yes, at the beginning it seems that there is not enough direction where to swim, people are used to the game directing you, but here you yourself just have to explore everything and this is where the fun begins, because then you realize that you don’t need signs, you yourself are free to swim wherever you want. I enjoyed it a lot!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful realistic graphics and special effects.  Exciting having a swam of great whites below me.  Would love to see more updates, such as waterfalls, white rapids, and more marine life.  The stingrays and turtles were a nice addition. If the developers added new places as expansion packs, such as a Jurrastic park or maybe Lockness, I would definitely buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: A bit disappointed, I was expecting more, Graphically amazing and great to show off VR to friends also if you want to meditate but the races are not great and the physics are annoying, quite realistic if you attach controllers to an actual stick but all in all there are a few more levels from the demo that are actually better than that level but there is really nothing to do in the game apart from a few races and explore, I was expecting rapids levels with faster pace, it looked like that in the trailer but you just have to row super fast to get that speed which is achievable but overall it is a very slow paced tech demo. If you like the meditation aspect check out Deep State, its similar except you walk around very realistic settings and mediate with audio and visuals thrown at you. Overall I will give it a thumbs up but it could be half the price and it would be worth it. I'll play a bit more and might change my mind
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I don't care much for kayaking, but this is definitely the best looking VR game currently in the market. The free roam mode is super relaxing. The sound effects and music are almost as good as the visuals.Pretty well optimized too – kudos to the dev for adding DLSS, Fidelity FX, resolution scaling, sharpening sliders and lots of other genuinely useful graphics settings.Worth the full price, even if just to take in the scenery for a couple hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: The immersion is really good, the mechanics are very realistic. Good variety of scenes and different stages within the scenes. LOVE the different weather and times of day, and hope we see even more such options (e.g. would like the storm conditions on every scene). It is a very taxing game graphically, the highest resolution settings make a huge difference in gameplay and smoothness of experience, but you'll need an elite rig to go that high. My only complaint is that I wish there were more interesting things to see, and when we do get them (animals like penguins for example), the movement and graphics are so unrealistic as to be a negative to immersion. It's already nearly a 5-star game for me, but just a few tweaks away from perfection
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Was sinking my oars into the mesmerizingly gorgeous water in the Norwegian night when the message appeared: "achievement unlocked: WW2 plane". Bang, there's an aircraft possibly just underneath my boat and it's in the middle of the night, can't see it! Wait, there it is, a silhouette! Splash, splash, splaaash, squeesh: yeah, it's a fighter. My wife already wants to buy a real little inflatable boat and hit the sea next weekend. I guess I'll not talk her out of it. Fantastic piece of art Kayak VR is!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: It's boring.  Graphics are gorgeous but unfortunately it doesn't save Kayak VR. Thumbs up for trying something new and different, it's just not the kind of experience I'm interested. What is wrong with Kayak VR? It's not my idea of fun. Swinging arms and enjoying beautiful view, that is it.  I didn't experience any VR sickness in the game, changing direction on Vr games can be particularly nausiating for newcomers. I can have a full lunch while playing VR in full immersive mode for two hours straight. Be wary when VR YouTube channels rave about a game, probably because the selection of games are so limited. VR Youtube channels raved about Sniper Elite VR, it was buggy mess (read my review), they raved about Song in The Smoke (bush crafting survival). None of the games was fun. The problem with VR is that 19/20 games are a mix of wave or arena shooters. HL Alyx set the bar. Fallout 4 still suffers from old time VR mechanics.   I've only "played" eighteen minutes, and writing this before requesting refund. This is not a game this is an VR "experience". I'm still thimbing this up because it's so cheap here in South Africa local price is about ZAR130 (US $7). I am not taking a swipe at the developers who worked hard on this, the visuals are photo realistic  VR needs something huge like an Assasins Creed Oddesy, Far Cry, Elden Ring, Horizon Zero Dawn with HL Alyx standard controls, no wall clipping etc. I'm going back to HL Alyx again for the 5th time! My PC is also not up to the task of running, I'm on Ryzen Gen 3 CPU, Geforce 1660Ti, 48GB Ram and nVMe drive but still not capable of smooth framerate. The problem with Kayak VR is that it is boring. I'm requesting a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! What beautiful landscapes, coupled with truly realistic water textures and wave movements. The waves kicked up by the "storm" setting in Norway are fantastically convincing, with some water periodically flying off the paddle right in front of your face. That storm is great fun to paddle into! Handling your paddle is just right, including the ability to "push off" from nearby rocks, or even shove the paddle down into a shallow sandy bottom just beneath you. Some other reviewers state you need to tape your controllers to the ends of a stick, but you do NOT. You simply make the same motions as you would in a real kayak. You need those controllers in your hands to feel the haptic feedback while stroking through water.Birds in the air, penguins waddling about, and crabs on the shore all add to the sense that "you are there." Playing the game gives you a bit of exercise too, though there is no actual water resistance, so that is about the only thing that doesn't feel real. However, the controllers "buzz" in your hands when pushing against water, simulating resistance, which helps quite a bit.There are only four locations so far, but each has more choices as regards time of day and weather conditions. You can either free roam or race. A tremendous achievement; buy this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: The first half hour of this game was really fun, considering I have never done anything close to kayaking in my life. However, because I have never kayaked, this game was really boring after a bit. The only thing going for it was the scenery, but it all looked the same after a bit, there wasnt much to do other than move your arms in the same motion. And I'm not very good at it, so I didn't want to race just to have my ass beat into the ground by some pro. Anyway, if you aren't into kayaking, I wouldn't recommend it. If you are, then I guess it might be okay, it just wasn't very fun for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are very impressive and the physics feel good. I like the choice of free roam or racing mode, although I suck at racing. You can get achievements for finding hidden things in the levels.Overall it's a great looking VR game and definitely worth it to support the developers, although I don't know how much replayability it has.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: If there were an experience that was the forerunner of Holodecks this game would be it! Once I put on my headset I was transported. From paddling along Kings Canyon to navigating Icebergs in Antarctica or the stormy seas at night around an island with a light house, were awesome memories beyond words!I hope these DEVs make more experiences like this,it would be a game changer for all other VR benchmarks.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Stunningly beautiful environments, serene soundscapes and perfect physics all come together to form the closest thing to being there possible. Each area is unique and has something special to offer, I very much look forward to completely exploring them all. The racing is pretty intense, definitely works a few muscles that have atrophied over the last couple years of sitting on my ass. It'll take a bit of work to become competitive but it's more than fun enough to be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Giving this a thumbs up with a caveatThe gameplay is great. The environments are very detailed and the actual movement using the paddle feels as natural as I could expect a VR kayaking game to be. Multiplayer was also flawless. The caveat is that this is one of the only VR games I've played that has given me serious motion sickness. I regularly fly fighter jets and drift cars in VR for extended periods of time and I couldn't actually kayak for more than 15 minutes without feeling like I was going to vomit. Which is pretty disappointing, given that the multiplayer works flawlessly and how beautiful the game actually is.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of kayaking IRL, you'll enjoy this.I bought this game on sale, expecting to maybe enjoy it for a second and then show it off to a friend or two eventually. The first person I showed it to sighed and relaxed multiple times until he chilled out so hard that I had to try it too. This one goes on the Steam Favorites List.Best water graphics I've seen in a game in a long time, especially for interactive water physics.Best graphics in general that I've seen in VR. The realism is almost as high as I am.At the time of this review I've only had the game open for 54 minutes but I already feel safe giving it a positive review. I'll be spending a good amount of time just floating around, probably with a YouTube video projected into my virtual lap and a cat in my irl lap.DISCLAIMER: my new computer is monstrously powerful and i don't know how it performs on average hardware(though even on a 3080ti i can tell this game is very well-optimized relative to its graphical load, compared to other graphics-heavy vr games i've played.)
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: It was alright, for for the price I can't justify having it. YouTubers are going nuts over the graphics, but for me, it was in the uncanny valley. _childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: i'm going to give my constructive criticisms as a seasoned VR gamer.I bought this game and so far I enjoyed some of what I've played so far. I will keep in mind that this is their first drop and I hope the devs wont abandon because there is serious potential but it needs loads more content and improvements, but in this $20 (on sale) game I, i'm looking at this as an investment for what this could potentially end up being.Playing on: Valve Index Full Set (bought last month)Nv GeForce 380 RTXAMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Initial review, thoughts, and comments:The graphics are not as "photo-realistic" as people are claiming. I have them set to cinematic with 1.7 res boost but things in the distance look blurry. Maybe a rendering draw distance option can be added? Still pretty though.The index controllers work decently so far but need to be fine tuned (occasional spinning of oars, etc)down the line, adding a body and hands models would help with the immersion and let you know where your hand is on the oar easier. Finger tracking always a bonus for immersion.I read all these comments hyping up the water but its nothing close to what I was expecting.I was hoping to see a more detailed fluid simulation and more detailed splash effects, they look like place holders. The ripples if you hit the water look like a trail of circular raindrops instead of cutting through the water realistically. That's an intense thing to achieve and run well, but would add more of a visual presence of you interaction with water with the oar.We need more intricate and interesting water routes on these maps!  only 1 has an ice slide which is I liked a lot.imagine kayaking down a giant mud slick down a mountain in Hawaii? maybe passing by erupting volcano that sends small bits of matter around the player (embers, splashes from rocks seen and heard by player, paddling close to glowing flowing lava trails for prettiness purposes) or a adding scratches and mud/water/dirt to your player model would help make things look more professional and immersion as well. Maps done on casual should be given the option for a "levelution" free roam mode where these events occur (like the volcano, storm, falling trees, lightning on certain objects near player that makes them explode for excitement). Its cool when things start out normal and then you see highly detailed storm clouds coming in and the waves start to change and the tension starts to build as rain and wind fly by your ear, or a volcano in the distance you can reach that's slowly erupting.MORE NARROW INTENSE DOWNHILL PASSAGE WAYS PLEASE! These were the most exhilarating. Co-op casual mode down the line. Add side missions like spear fishing, normal fishing, penguin knockout challenge haha). Or research picture taking of animals, tripes, pretty scenes).Maybe way down the line add the ability to fight or befriend island natives 9 (fight if they shoot first kinda deal). You could have a bow and arrow, knife, or speargun as weapons plus other things (oar). Add the option to extend the oar distance, my arms are too long for the fixed distance.Animal models and animations need more fidelity and life given to them, and some activity animations or more interaction with the player.decent work out on the races. But we need way more race options. You guys got this, with time this will be what I think it could be. also, need more rocking on water boat sounds when idling on the water (after you add in dynamic waves :P)good stuff. 2.5/5 Right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, BUT...Its definitely one of the prettiest VR titles i've played! Great sense of actually being in a kayak and paddling around different environments. The water is 1st class and the best VR crabs i've seen so far!BUT once you have slapped your last inflatable and lay on the floor to get a peek underwater and drown yourself, there really isn't much to do! it gets a bit depressing TBH.They ruined it with the racing nonsense and should of had actual kayak courses like the Olympics in rapids and tight turns going back on yourself against the current! And co-op missions or something. its just too dull.I love that this game is a thing though because its the direction VR should be going and really good to see- Buy on sale for cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start, I've been following this game since one of the first few pre-release announcements via Reddit, and I was already infatuated with the idea. I've never been kayaking, never thought about it before, and the only similar experience I had with it was a canoe trip I had taken as a kid, yet this game stirred something within me and wanted to try a new experience.As for the game, it's rough on hardware. My 3080 was sweating trying to make everything look good at the Epic setting. Looks amazing with the Index, though. I've only spent a few minutes in game, but I was already immersed in the arid heat of Australia in the summer, thanks to the PC that struggled to run it. And, even better, I can open my window here in Winter and get even more immersed in the freezing tundra that is Antarctica. Not quite the same since my space heater is a few feet away, but jokes aside, get the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: The environments are breathtakingly beautiful and immersive (3080 ti).  The new guided tour feature is a game-changer for me, giving me the much needed motivation to get back on my rowing machine (controllers are not needed).  I can see myself putting in a lot more hours in this game in the near future. _childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, the game is very beautiful and seems to be very good, I enter the game and go to the pool where the game runs very well but when I try to enter a map I get 5-10 fps even though I have all the requirements that the game asks.This isn't really an analysis, it's more of a request for help to find out if it happened to anyone else.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really beautiful. And at the same time, incredibly boring. There is plenty of beautiful maps, however the game comes with only 3 modes, of which none are engaging:- Race, in which you need to go as fast as possible. However rowing with your controllers feels bad for the purpose: making tiny adjustments with the wrists makes you go faster than realistic full body swings.- Free roam, where you will explore a map by rowing yourself. While the maps are very beautiful, the kayaking itself is a bit dull. It's not like there are rapids or such.- exploring, where you can only sit and look around you.Don't get me wrong, this can be a fun game if  doing nothing and just looking around floats your boat, but I can not imagine me playing this for more than 2 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kind of a mixed bag. On the one hand, the game looks very pretty, the physics are good and the controls work perfectly. But on the other, there's just nothing to really... do. There's an initial 'wow' factor for the first 20 minutes, but other than that there's not really any interesting content to the game. You kinda just kayak and that's it. You can race others but that doesn't really add anything and also gets boring quickly. It's a great tech demo, but I personally wouldn't recommend buying it. If something like this was incorporated into an actual game, with a story, objectives, and just anything else that would make you want to boot it up more than once, it would be a great buy. But this is literally just kayaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: As mentioned by other reviewers the game crashes regularly when using WMR headset, in my case the HP Reverb G2 in combination with RTX 3070 graphics card. Crashes seem to occur when switching from scenery but also randomly during gameplay.Pitty because the experience is nice, bar some animals like the turtle and orca which are a bit robot-like.Physics are OK but a bit fidgety; forward strokes are sometimes interpreted as backward strokes which is a bit frustrating.Due to the the crashes I refunded.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Read a couple of reviews for this. The best review was really accurate. An amazing VR experience let down by the fact that it is unbelievably buggy. At the start in the tutorial, if you don't get moving it just corrupts the screen and locks up. The most I've managed to stay paddling for is about five minutes... then locks up with distorted graphics. Each time I have to take VR headset off and task manager cancel the program. Really spoils it. A disappointing experience that could have been amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Kayak is at this point an experience than a full-fledged game. It is enough to swim for a while to understand that it is only a technology demo. We have not much, because four to the truth beautiful and picturesque maps, but unfortunately boring and poor in things to do on them. On each we get two/three routes to sail in an average of up to five minutes, which in total will take an hour and a half and that's it. All this, the creators wanted to hide - in the map selection menu we have only three items displayed to get to the fourth board we have to scroll with the list to the right, giving the illusion that there are more than there actually are. I wonder why they just didn't display all four ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°). Free swim mode is a pleasure like photo mode in cyberpunk - cool cool cool to show mom. Supposedly we have achivments to find a hidden finder on each of these boards, but it's already such a lazy clogging. On the forums, people are asking for modes in the genre of collecting trash that floats in the water, or even the ability to fish, but that's an abstract I'm not even counting on. Developers will nod, of course, but we will know them by their deeds. Since such trivial features aren't there at launch I don't expect them to appear in the future. I have the impression that the maps are so small that there is no chance to develop them with new routes or activities in possible updates. They make a sensational first impression, but you quickly notice that it's a pleasure for a few moments. They are closed, linear and form one whole rather than an open space that can be edited. In the end we get a niche production that gives us a unique experience, unfortunately short and highly disposable - which is why in such situations it is a blessing to be able to return at times without demos. Just in time to play, experience, acquire, reflect and possibly return. Therefore, do not read my opinion as negative. I'm more interested in getting your attention and giving a different opinion than just drooling over the graphics.  ps. Resetting the position of the canoe is broken, doing it during the race unbelievable things happen, from flying into space to exploring worlds on the other side of the textures.

_childDocuments_.review: Warning to HP Reverb G2 / WMR Users! (Solved! - see comments)Many, many crashes, but when it worked, it was jaw-dropping! I spent about an hour with it and about 30 minutes of that was spent restarting Mirage, SteamVR, WMR, and my computer. I'm on an Alienware with an RTX 3070, so no lack of horsepower. I regularly run BeatSaber, which is highly-optimized, and Dirt Rally 2.0, which is poorly-optimized, but I've found settings that work well for both. Unfortunately, no combination of settings I've tried so far has kept Mirage from crashing about 8 out of 10 times. That said, I'll keep using it because it provided exactly the workout I was looking for and did so beautifully! Hopefully it can do so more consistently as the devs have more time for testing on various hardware. Great job!!! Please, please, please address the crashes with WMR! And please comment here if you've found a fix. I've tried with and without most graphics settings at this point. Mirage hangs, the view freezes in the HMD, and SteamVR sometimes suggests a restart. That's all I have to go on so far ...
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice!I ran into 2 issues. #1: after the tutorial I picked "tour" thinking that was the "do whatever I want mode". When it started I had no paddle. Turns out "tour" mode the kayak is self driving but that was clear at all. I had to search on the net to find out what I'd done wrong.#2: I've only played the Costa Rica level so far and it's gorgeous. But, when I went into the "Jungle" the waves didn't appear to change. There should be no or almost no waves once you're off the coast. This as someone that's actually kind of kayaked in similar areas. The water should be pretty close to still back there and it took away from the immersion. You can google videos of "Kayaking at Ao Thalane" and the first hit you'll see the ocean level of choppy waves is much less once they enter a canyon so it's missing that relaxing feeling in the canyons.  Not a huge issue, mostly just surprised given how much work they put into this. Maybe an update will calm the waters inside.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

I have to ask for help here since google is useless and cant find any support. Basically game runs only in the pool and its smooth, but whatever map i pick there is just black screen and eveually crashes and freezes, ive run vr games way more demanding than this..
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game but to be honest, for $22.99, there are better games to spend your time on. There's no real objective other than paddle around and enjoy the scenery. If there were races or other little fun objectives, this game would be even better but there's really no other point other than a time waster. The controls were fine, contrary to what other people seem to say in reviews, even though there is nowhere to rest the paddles, it's fine. The game feels nice, has the best performance out there to be honest, I had everything on cinematic and didn't notice a single bit of lag or stutter. If you like Kayaking, just the general idea of it and having a way to do it without leaving home, this is definitely the game for you, to be honest, I'd rather Kayak for real lol I recommend the game because it definitely looks like there has been some work done on it and it isn't all that bad of an experience, but I personally would not keep the game as I only found it fun for the first 15 minutes.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games where a thumbs sideways would be appreciated. It's very good looking, it ran way better on my PC than some older VR games I have (which I'd expect to be less graphically intense). But it's more of a demo of what VR could be than a full fledged experience. In the time I played, about an hour and a half, I finished the Australian and Costa Rican runs, I got out of bound in Alaska and that only leaves Norwegia it would seem. That's really too short for 23 euro in my mind. Also, it's too much like real kayaking (I'm guessing) in that it's too physically intense to get anywhere. I mean, the developer is literally called "Better Than Life". So why wouldn't they make the actual kayaking better than life? I'm refunding this for now, but maybe if it's on sale sometime I'll change my mind. Or if they improve the aspects I've mentioned.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing. Developers are finally realizing that bad graphics and VR do not need to go hand in hand. With a Geforce RTX 3090 the game runs butter smooth on cinematic and looks great. There is lots of fauna to gawk at (say hi to the turtle!) and you can even stick your head underwater. The motions are good and the kayak moves realistically... sort of. Flipping isn't supported, or maybe I wasn't able to do it.There are some cons. Splashes look really ugly, and since you see them so much it is immersion breaking. Some textures are too low quality, especially the ground textures right under the boat. These don't detract too much once you get going and shouldn't put you off buying this.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review:Kayak VR is exactly what you'd expect, a kayaking simulator with a heavy emphasis on the visuals and it is beautiful. There were times where I felt truly immersed and forgot I'm actually just some fool with plastic on his head. I felt I was there, sailing through caves with water dripping on my head, cruising around the beach and being scared to death by the that dog. The game has a pool you start in and can practice around, then jump into one of four maps with a couple weather settings, free roam around and take in the scenery or test your skills with one of the race modes. There's two or three different courses per map so not a great deal of content overall and I do wonder about the longevity this game will have. While you're exploring little events will happen; the dog appearing, a penguin diving into water or the iceberg breaking off and while they're great little additions that make the game feel alive, the fact they happen in the same way every time will, I think, get boring when you replay them. There's a roadmap for features to be added, but I cant see much in the way of free DLC maps so far. Then again, although this does cost £16.99 which is pretty steep, in comparison to a lot of VR games its not terrible. The online race functionality and customisable parts you buy with your sea miles is what people will come back for. You can see other players as you paddle in the time trials and there's of course a leader board system. I'm seriously terrible with it personally, but it's still pretty invigorating. This isn't a terrible workout game honestly, when you go for those deep strokes at speed you can get a real sweat on. The kayak physics seem to be pretty much spot on, as they should be. You can't twist the paddle is the only thing I can think of, though I suppose twisting two controllers independently would cause some serious physics screw ups so its fair enough. If you have enough space you could tape them to a boom handle or an actual paddle and have a pretty sweet time. Some maniac suggested added support for a rowing machine on the roadmap forum, great idea though, one of the best things about VR is turning workouts into something you can actually enjoy.An area I feel could use some improvement is the audio, which is no means bad, but I think greater detail there would aid the sense of immersion. Little sounds for the paddle hitting the boat especially would be good. Some more ocean noises too, things are a little too quiet out there..Good game overall though, not a vast amount of content but visually pretty stunning with solid graphics options. I like the arctic caves especially and the storm on the Norway map. Definitely tests your VR seasickness legs though, be warned.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Bought in the sale as looked interesting, but just feels like a glorified tech demo. Once you've paddled about a bit it gets old pretty quickly, there's only 4 locations and not much else to see. Graphics are nice, and I don't suffer the performance issues others are mentioning. I'm running an 8 year old i7-4930k, MSI GTX 1080 Ti, 32Gb DDR3 RAM, Win10 Pro with everything on maximum and super sampling at 1.5 and it runs faultlessly via AirLink on Quest 2 (v42), no stutter, lag, frame drops or anything negative. I am running direct via the Oculus runtime, so maybe running via SteamVR is the issue here. Ultimately, it looks pretty and is a good advert for what VR can bring and I give kudos to the developers to what they've set out to achieve, but it just doesn't hold my attention. The old adage, "graphics don't make a game" springs to mind. Even with racing there's really not that much of a game here and it's pretty limited unless they intend to add more locations. As technically good as it is, it really needs more content for any chance of longevity.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: My experience is that the game mechanics are screwed up. For instance, if I paddle on the right, it should push the nose left. Sometimes it does, but usually it pushed the nose right! Once it starts swinging either right or left, the only way to stop it is to back paddle. Not reasonably usable. Great visuals though.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Glitchy and laggy at times, not really optimized at the moment. But the graphics and scenes detailing are really nice. _childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I can recommend this game at this time. It is very limited in content. I believe I have played demos that have more content than the game currently does. There seem to be only four maps, and they are small. I thought that the kayak races would have you go through long routes in these worlds, but instead they have you doing little loops and turns in a small area. I think the arctic level for instance, was about the size of Halo 3's The Pit map. I assumed this game was early access and I'm shocked to find out its not. I was going to not write a review but when I saw it wasn't in early access I decided to write this. It just simply isn't enough content to justify being a released game @ $22 or whatever it was I paid at. I know they have a roadmap and it is listed that new levels would come in it, but it also contains a disclaimer that says basically "We can just simply not follow this roadmap at any time if we feel that is best to do"edit: Tried the game again after a few months, it just crashes Unreal Engine now and I can't even play it. Yeah, hard pass

_childDocuments_.review: Kayak Mirage is a bit the Vision Pro of PCVR. It shows a vertical slice of what VR could be. The graphics and the controls are spot on. The four levels included boast beautifully designed environments and also lush sea life. I dream of the day we'll have an open world kayak exploration game that looks like this. Also, there is a pretty active discord community that shares tips and tricks for the physics-based paddling which is well implemented. A must-buy for PCVR-lovers. I sit down on a little bench for playing and strap wrist weights 6lb to each hand which makes a great workout.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning game! Sometimes runs bad when on higher settings but runs fine on lower settings which seems about right. Still being developed so thats cool! _childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: You sit in a kayak without getting wet. The scenery is gorgeous. The controls are great. You can use your paddle to bump off obstacles. In the tutorial you get to play with pool toys. Apart from paddling through air this feels very real.  You don't get smashed against the cliffs and drown. The water that enters your kaya because it has not been secured does not sink you. It is chill af.Ther eare quite a few areas to paddle in. Tropic beeches and rivers. Fjords. Night and day. Rough waves. If you put on an audio book you will get your daily hour of workout. Aboslutely worth it the asking price.Edit: If you play this more than an hour a day you are much fitter than I.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Sitting in a kayak and watching the fishes swim past or watch the Southern Polar lights. This is really a match made in heaven for VR. This made me smile and going ooh and ah.Wonderful environments with lovingly crafted details. And even on a moderate rig with a 6600XT outstanding performance and free room to oversample which really sharpens up the images. The interface is also very simple and intuitive.Small gripe, the advanced rowing options seem unworkable with two controllers that I tried.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing this game for the beautiful visuals, and it was incredibly fun to paddle around even in the pool at the beginning. The physics felt correct and somewhat satisfying to push things around with.There are some environments that felt incredibly dark at night (which... I mean it IS night time) that even on my monitor it was difficult to parse what I was looking at besides darkness. People who were watching me play mirrored my thoughts it was quite dark and hard to tell what was happening. It's odd going to a completely different location at night and feeling like there's not much setting them apart from each other, but I understand they are going for realism.That being said, this game unfortunately taught me how severe motion sickness can get in VR, especially if you play for too long. If you don't usually have an issue with motion sickness it may not be a problem for you, but if you do pace out your time in these VR waters and you should have a pleasant time (even if it's just going on the guided tour). The racing seems like it could be fun, but it also just made me feel a bit ill.I would still recommend this game to people with a VR headset if they are looking for a slightly more intensive experience since it is quite beautiful (and somewhat exhausting if you wanna paddle fast, but isn't that part of the fun?), but be aware if you have issues with motion sickness.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This is great for getting some exercise in VR, and if you attach your controllers to a real pole, possibly the best PC VR demo that exists.Super intuitive controls that everyone already understands, and no buttons to learn!  I wish there were more locations, but the 4 they do have are stunning.  It's like really kayaking through Antarctica, but you only have to spend $20!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: wonderful visuals, great overall paddling simulation, I didn't have problems EXCEPT for the fact that I am just much too used to the physical feedback from an actual kayak.
