It's also a great way to dive into Polish history and understand how people lived under the oppression of Russian Empire.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: A striking re-envision of the 1900 Poland powered by alluring visuals does make for a solid premise for an RPG. But while The Thaumaturge delivers some quality written bits and a certain atmosphere, it does fail to lay the bricks for its world and the action that takes place in it. There is an obvious disparity in the level of writing quality when it comes to the flavorous texts related to the protagonist's powers and the storytelling at large. The former is deliciously inquisitive, providing you the means to let your mind’s eye get to work. On the other hand, the latter is often blunt with artificial exchanges of dialogues that drive a system of choices which leads to less than credible consequences. It doesn’t help that your actions as a thaumaturge are not properly explained and you are acting the way you do just because the game’s journal tells you to do it. Traces of today’s social political influences are also notable at every corner to the detriment of one's immersion.The gameplay doesn’t fare much better than its storytelling counterpart. The stylized combat system looks interesting at start, but its mechanics fail to evolve into something that can justify the countless battles ahead. It’s rather easy to find the winning combo and repeat it from start to (probably) finish while wondering why you are constantly forced to do this.Having the powers to read other’s emotions does give you an edge in solving mysteries. But the detective work quickly devolves into a routine of pixel hunting for objects by spamming the perception button and coming to automatic conclusions which open new dialogue options. It’s a rather lazy system that tries to masquerade as interactive gameplay while in reality is just following the guide line from point A to point B.The Thaumaturge presents itself as a nice-looking package which once opened will most likely lead to the disappointment of anyone in search for something meaningful. I really wish this was an RPG driven by a good story involving mystical detective work. But I didn't find what I was looking for here and now I'm worried about the way Fool's Theory will handle The Witcher's remake.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. I'm generally happy with my time I've spent with the game. The story, the atmosphere, most of the characters, were top notch, I think, much stronger than your average western game.  Graphics wise, the environments were really well done, the main characters  kinda looked OK, but the facial animations had left a lot be desired, mainly due to budget reasons, I guess. The general gameplay loop was somewhat uninteresting for the most part, some would say, as something  marketed as an RPG, should have had more interactive activities, and not just collecting nice pictures and clues - which by the was kinda cool, but it got old after 20+ hours of gameplay. But for me, the most important and interesting part of the game were the salutors, and their importance in the story, as they are really interesting, from mechanical perspective and look extremely cool and gave the game a very unique feeling. I wish the combat was more balanced though, sometimes fights were really easy even on hard, but there were once or twice in the game when I screamed at my monitor. I think my main problem with the combat comes with the lack of variety of enemies and lack of player interaction - for most of the time, I used the same abilities, because it was too easy (apart for the two cases where It did not really mattered what abilities I mixed, I still lost, skill issue, I know, had to lower the difficulty), I was not really forced to use anything new. Music was also something of a mixed bag. I liked what was there, there were just way too few tracks used in the game, and repeated over and over - guess due to budget reasons.But please, don't take me wrong. This game is special. I want the developers not to abandon the game, and make a sequel and spice up the gameplay and combat, and they will have something of a masterpiece on their hand! Please buy the game and support the developers, they really deserve it! Thank you for this little flawed gem, Fool's Theory!

A Polish sense of humour and Polish culture!CONS: NOTHING SIGNIFICANT - English subtitles sometimes incorrect compared to voices. _childDocuments_.review: The game’s set in a Warsaw that’s got more shadows than a candlelit room, and you’re there to stir the pot with spells while dealing with family drama that’s stickier than overcooked pasta. And let’s not forget the political mess that’s more tangled than your earphones after being in your pocket for exactly two seconds.But it’s not all doom and gloom. The game’s got a sense of humor that’s as dry as a martini, with characters that are as eccentric as they are endearing. Sure, the pacing might sometimes have the urgency of a sloth on a leisurely stroll, but that’s all part of the charm.In short, “The Thaumaturge” is like that one friend who’s a little odd, a little brilliant, and always has a story to tell that’s too bizarre to be made up. So, if you’re ready for a historical RPG that doesn’t take itself too seriously, give it a whirl. Just remember, in the world of “The Thaumaturge,” expect the unexpected – and maybe keep an eye out for any stray spells.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game... but only to a handful of people. The biggest selling point is the story and the characters. The combat is simple but has an enjoyable enough loop, especially whilst you unlock the first three salutors. But by the half-way mark in the game, you'll probably be tired of it. _childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game. If you enjoy story-driven games, The Thaumaturge is not to be missed. Player takes control Wiktor, a young thaumaturge who has been exiled from his home. Wiktor possesses the ability to read people’s thoughts simply by touching objects that are tied to them. The narrative unfolds in early 20th-century Warsaw, during a tumultuous period where real historical events are woven into the storyline. A central element of the game involves the choice of whether to align with or resist Russian authority, which adds layers of tension and moral ambiguity. I’ve always found it fascinating to make decisions based on real historical events in video games, and this game offers a variety of potential endings that stem from the player's choices. You don't need to worry about making a decision too early in the game - these choices come much later, and each ending is carefully developed, offering a satisfying conclusion. What’s more, the developer never judges the player’s decisions, which allows for a more personal, experience.As for the gameplay, much of it revolves around detective work, where the player clicks on items and receives thoughts, eventually piecing together clues to understand what’s going on in a particular situation. This aspect of the game is a highlight for me. Besides, the dialogues are literary, sharp, humorous, witty like those in Disco Elysium. The voice acting is superb, and the characters feel vibrant and full of life. Each NPC has a distinct personality, contributing to the rich content and thought provoking discussions that Wiktor engages in, and that scene about inscribing words in onion and fork is brilliant and funny.Combat is another significant aspect of the game, but it’s not always necessary. You can often avoid conflict by carefully picking answers or deciding to bear insults with dialogue. Most of the fights aren’t difficult, except for the one arises when you decide to join the  at the end of the game. A unique feature of the game is the assistance you receive from demons born from "flaws". Starting with "Pride" flaw, along the way Wiktor can acquire more demons and I ended up having all 8 of them, who fight along with me but surprisingly, I regretted taking some after seeing how losing flaws altered other character’s personalities. Eventually, not all flaws are inherently negative, some are more like virtues that define a person’s identity.The game’s atmosphere is well crafted, every character feels fully realized. There were many moments when I had to pause and reflect deeply on my choices, especially when asked whether being a Thaumaturge is a gift or a curse, or whether I should remove a flaw from another character. The stakes of each feel significant, and some choices will limit the future options, making the game constantly evolving based on your actions. The relationships and the freedom of choice are other aspects I truly appreciated. The game doesn’t shy away from presenting moral dilemmas. For instance, it is not too difficult to understand the pressure behind Wiktor’s father’s decision, but whether you agree with him is entirely up to you. Player also have the ability to decide whether to kill or spare certain enemies, just keep in mind your decisions can directly impact the storyline, offering different outcomes.In conclusion, The Thaumaturge is absolutely a gem, and I highly recommend it. I would love to see a DLC expansion or a sequel in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Fascinating RPG set in 19th Century Eastern Europe. You are Wiktor Szulski, a Polish Thaumaturge. Gameplay consists of wandering around, talking to people - making dialogue-based decisions influenced by the RPG mechanics, your previous choices, and any evidence/secrets you've uncovered via your thaumatalurgical powers - and turn-based combat. As you go around catching demons, and upgrading your stats, combat becomes more and more tactical. Can you uncover and solve the many mysteries that plague Warsaw - from the criminal underworld to the Tsar's court. If you're a fan of decision-based/dialogue-driven action-RPG games, then I'd definitely recommend checking this one out!

It's totally my kind of game, but if you like action games and don't like reading and watching long dialogue scenes, don't play it.

_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like isometric RPGs and are alright with a darkish fantasy in historical setting? If either applies, that's a resounding yes.We play as Wiktor Szulski, a thaumatruge from Warsaw, at the time when Poland has officially not been a country for about a century. This sets the stage for the plot of the game, which makes a decent effort at depicting a highly volatile, tense society with many factions and where people routinely "disappear" - only with added thaumaturgy.Some people say the world is shallow, but I actualy quite liked how understated thaumatrugy is, because the magic itself from the view of outsider is sutble enough that a good amount of people just thinks thaumaturgy is some sort of a scam, and even the well informed have no idea what you can do. In general, what you can do is: feel thoughts and feelings of people when touching objects they used, allowing you to essentially pick up people's scerets whethere they want to or not and you can very much manipulate people with your powers if you know enough about them. The only way to get these powers is to be lucky enough to be born with them and form a contract with a salutor who from that point will be your constant companion - an immaterial being, mostly folklore inspired, invisible to anyone but other thaumaturges. For you, that is Upyr - and I quite liked Upyr, actually - he's very much a silent companion with limited expression, but the game has Wiktor have full on dialogue with him, implying it's us who can't understand. I genuinely liked the idea for it far much then I expected and I'd absolutely play more games/read books that would explore it from different angles (especially the Flaw system, which I won't get into here).Gameplay wise - it's a dialogue driven rpg with investigations - so expect a lot of walking and clicking on clues. That is in the game description. Now, it is not really a detective story, which I was half-expecting - most of the time the investigations are just you being too curious for your own good (which is understandable - who wouldn't be when you can untangle people's scerets from merely wandering around and touching their things). Works really well at what it intends. You spend a lot of the time exploring the environemtn, finding clues in the form of things and papers people left, giving you a small glimpse into the life of the city.The dialogue is mostly written well, the voice acting is good as well - some uneven performances here and there, but mostly great, and as a bonus most of the major voice actors are Polish so they do, in fact, pronounce the names of everything correctly which was fun to hear. It is a "this character will remember this" type game in a classical sense, your choices in dialogue do matter - either long or short term.Combat was alright. Can't say too much about it, I'm here for the plot, but it is fairly classic, has a few different builds you can experiment with - though it gets a bit borning toward the end when you've gottten a good grasp on it.Plot wise I'm pretty happy with how it develops too (and I was worried what they'll do with Rasputin since he appears in game - but think the story handles him quite nicely). There is a variety of endings that all fit within the setting fairly well. The major NPCs you interact with feel realistic, have sensible backgrounds and generally feel fairly fleshed out. It can be tricky to do the "you return after 15 years" trope - here it works well. There are people Wiktor knew and reconnects with, but this can go both well and not - they're not the same people anymore.Overall I think it's a really good game. It does what it says - it's a good isometric rpg, it has a darker tone, the setting is done justice, the dialogue is written nicely and the plot I personally liked as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying this game. It is different in a good way. It reminds me of Vampyr with a Slavic twist and a little bit of Persona mixed in. I saw bad reviews about the graphics but they work with the dark, downtrodden atmosphere. I find myself trying to explore everywhere to see all the graphical details. _childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: "The Thaumaturge" is a reverent nod to the bygone era of 20th-century Europe, braiding historical authenticity with the ethereal threads of magic and demonology, drawn from the rich tapestry of eastern European lore. My experience with this story-driven marvel has been nothing short of immersive, charging each story choice and turn-based battle with meaningful consequences that resonate through the unfolding narrative.I could not help but be pulled into the mystical world of "The Thaumaturge" where just the right amount of choice carries weight and the ripple effect of your decisions alters the story's course. This is a game that respects the player's agency while presenting a plot that doubles as a covert lesson in eastern European history and mythology. It educates while it entertains, embedding authentic cultural references within its enigmatic mystery.From a design standpoint, "The Thaumaturge" excels with graphics so crisp that the smallest details stand in sharp relief. Sweat beads on a character's brow, the gentle melting of snow upon warm skin—it's a visual banquet that takes full advantage of current-generation game graphics. The polished aesthetic complements the narrative's depth, conjuring atmospheres that feel tangible, almost as if one could stretch out a hand and touch the vintage surfaces of a bygone time.Fans of classic turn-based strategy will find comfort in the familiarity of "The Thaumaturge's" combat system. Echoes of influence from "Final Fantasy" are unmistakable yet beautifully interwoven with innovative elements that breathe new life into this time-honored mechanic.The combat strategy is nuanced and layered, allowing players to engage with its intricacies to emerge victorious against the demons that lurk within. The combat takes place both in the physical and metaphysical realms. It challenges gamers to rethink their approach to conflict resolution within the game, never leaning too far into territory that could be labeled derivative."The Thaumaturge," with its historical underpinnings and a spellbound world rife with supernatural intrigue, is an unmissable indulgence for RPG aficionados. It's a portal to another era where I found myself immersed, an experience enriched with lessons from the past, and brimming with mystery and the thrill of a time period adventure.Gamer history buffs, a lover of lore, or a seeker of gaming experiences where choices have significance, "The Thaumaturge" will not disappoint. It's a testament to the power of video games as vehicles for storytelling and a shining example of the heights that game development can reach.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Not Exactly What I Expected, But Still A Enjoyable Experience.I was intrigued by this game when I played the demo during last year's Steam Next Fest. The dark fantasy settings and the subtle writing really caught my attention. The story and what's in store later down the line interest me greatly. I imagine the story being similar to that of Jim Butcher's Dresden Files but in Central Europe. Well, what I experience in the full game is not exactly what I anticipated it would be. The story centers more around human struggles and less supernatural stuff, and the gameplay also has some confusing designs. Yet, I still find the The Thaumaturge an interesting ride.Thing I Like About The Thaumaturge:Compliments→The story isn't what I expected, but it's still interesting to see how a thaumaturge manages his way into society.→I enjoy the writing of this game.→ I love how the game recreates some of the well-known folklore creatures in its style, eerie but wonderful.→I actually learned a lot about Polish history.Things I Like And Dislike About The Thaumaturge:Combat and BuildsLike→Builds: Even though you only have four abilities throughout the game, the options to buff those abilities are quite rich. From simple upgrades like more damage and additional debuff, to interesting ones like granting your salutor faster moves or breaking enemies down faster for finishers. It is important to customize each ability to fit the salutor of your playstyle.→Salutors: Probably the most interesting part of the combat. Salutors have their own abilities, though they are not upgradable. You can freely choose which one to use during battles. Each of them specializes in different aspects of combat: some are great debuffer/finisher, some focus on reducing Focus points, and some are hybrids. It is interesting to note that salutors synergize quite well with each other. With the right combination and your buffed abilities, it is not uncommon to instantly turn the tide in harder battles.Dislike→Confusing Design: What I don't like about combat is that you have to use your basic abilities first before you can use your upgraded ones. I genuinely don't know what the logic behind this design is. Not only does this design make the fights, even the easier ones, take longer than they should, but it also takes up space, which could potentially introduce new alternative abilities for true build variety.→Encounters: I am disappointed to see how little variety the enemy roster contains, and there are no thaumaturge or actual salutor fights either. Enemies only hit you, make you bleed with different knives, and shoot you. That's it. There is no debuffer, no buffer, and no other class. Traits could increase the difficulty of the fight, except we can easily break them with one move from the right salutor.Things I Dislike About The Thaumaturge:1. The Whole "Detective" ThingThe other part of the game is to run around the map, spamming your perception button, to see if any red particles concentrate on one spot. This is how you "detect" clues. Once Wiktor collects all the clues, he will automatically conclude the solutions or ideas himself. This design may appeal to those who just want to get through the story as fast as possible, but to me, it makes the whole situation less interactive on the player's part. There is no secret component on items for you to interact with and discover, and there is certainly no need for you to actually piece the clues together.2. Other complaints→ I wish the whole "feed your Flaw" system could have more impact than dialogue choices. Other than Wiktor's downfall, Upyr could also benefit from the evolving Flaw and become stronger in combat. The same deal goes with all the other salutors.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting to like this game so much. It has an immersive story with lots of dialogues and cutscenes without fall into boredom. _childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: So I only just started the second of the three acts so take my review with a grain of salt I suppose. This is like if Disco Elysium and the JoJo anime had a polish baby. You have basically spirits called 'salutors' which each represent a different trait that serve as your Disco Elysium inner monologue voices when you investigate items and have conversations. It's an RPG set in 1905 Warsaw with some detective-like elements and stat-based conversation choices. The game is top-down style when navigating the world and then in normal third-person style during the turn based combat.Unfortunately the product is less than the sum of its parts. I don't like leaving negative reviews and I would say the game is still worth getting at a discount (probably substantial) but here are my issues with it:1. The items to find through investigating are very easy as there is a giant red glow around everything when you ping your 'detective sense' button and they're generally in the immediate quest area 2. The combat is super easy and thus super boring. It tries to be a complicated and strategic system where you match the right salutor to the right enemy traits and theres also skill modifiers to unlock with exp which is supposed to offer some play style variety but you basically can just power through every fight by equipping damage boosting skill modifiers and just relying on your strongest attack. 3. The voice acting is super hit or miss. First off, the game only has an english audiotrack despite being set in Warsaw and involving a storyline which heavily features Rasputin and the Russian royalty. That aside, some of the voice actors don't even bother attempting an accent and you end up with someone who looks like a sixty year old polish police officer but sounds like a monotone american thirty year old.4. A lot of the 'sidequests' just involve you randomly running around town spamming your 'detective-sense' button to find thrown around items that trigger you to have to go to a location and press a button to get a postcard of an activity or event. For example, you find a bunch of stuff on the ground in one of the town districts and then get told to go to a story teller in another district and when you get there and press the button to interact with him you just get a drawing of him telling you a story. There is nothing to actually do.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. It's well set up for a sequel. If you like detective games that requires some reading and carefully making dialogue choices you will probably like this. Combat could be better, I enjoy turn based combat systems but this is not for everyone, and even for those who like turn based it still needs some refinement. Main quests and the meaningful side quests were really engaging and i never found myself not invested in what was going on.The only real gripe I had with the game is there are a ton of "quests" (not main quests, or side quests, but like optional exploration quests) which are almost necessary to have enough experience going into the final act to pass a non insignificant number of skill checks. If you're going to structure your game like this, the content has to be more engaging in my opinion. I did all of them and what it amounts to is find 3 clues, go to place, screen turns black, you get a sketch on your screen, and the quest is complete. I think it's cool to have small stuff like this in a game which encourages exploration and can add context to the world but maybe have the reward be something other than (almost necessary) experience. The Salutor feature was really cool, honestly I loved it. I really felt like a thaumaturge. To me it sets this game apart as a unique experience and the roleplay element of it is fantastic which has a lot of potential for more.7/10. Did enough that I would buy the sequel and am hopeful the next game will be more refined. I am the target demographic though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge is the best game I've discovered this year. After finishing it, I felt a void and couldn't stick with any other title for a while.Have you tried our Polish game? We play as Wiktor Szulski The Thaumaturge is a game made with a lot of love and hard work by Fool's Theory. That much is apparent within the first couple of hours and grows more obvious the longer a user plays. Its lack of a way to make searching for clues interesting may lead some players astray, but they will miss out on a demon-fueled magical adventure. It stumbles in other places, but it more than makes up for it with its monster designs and terrific storytelling. The Thaumaturge's mixture of 20th-century technology and magic should prove too fun to pass up, and players looking for a detective mystery with some intrigue and nightmares might have found something they can't find anywhere else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: The thaumaturge combines a superbly told story of a man struggling with his pride and inner demons with the vivid history of Warsaw in 1905, plus a mystical component in the form of the Salutors, which takes up Eastern European folklore. The turn-based battles are fun and each new Salutor not only adds new combat options, but also makes the player feel more and more like a powerful Thaumaturge controlling powerful spirits. In addition to the well-told story, the highlight of the game is the superbly designed Salutors. There is also a great soundtrack that rounds off the dense atmosphere. However, the major design flaw in the game are the long distances you have to walk in the otherwise beautiful game world. In a sequel, I would also like to see more opportunities to interact with the Salutors you find - I also really wished that they could speak.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely recommend this game to anyone who likes an interesting plot, because the story is the most important thing in this game and I have to admit that it is breathtaking.The game itself is more of an adventure game with a lot of RPG elements. Exploring the world and solving puzzles is more about finding the right information in locations - it is not a detective game. The combat system is turn-based (you can choose the difficulty level and it may be a challenge for the player), but don't expect something like XCOM or Jagged Alliance - it is more like a card game, although the videos showing the effects of our choices are very satisfying.A solid 8/10 in my opinion, mainly because of the plot. If Wiktor's investigation also consisted in solving logical puzzles and the fight took place on a map, then I would give it 10/10 and the game would be a sure candidate for the title of game of the year.To sum up, it is a very successful production, Thaumaturge 2 (if it is ever created) may be an outstanding game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: A generally excellent game! Amazing story and characters, interesting combat, a beautiful world- It's all you can ask for from an RPG really!Only two very minor complaints; one is that I wish your demons had more interaction with the story than their respective arcs! Of course I wouldn't expect them to have more interaction with Wiktor than Upyr does, but i did wish they had some story relevance more than once to endear you to them (especially considering the special mechanism of the end boss). That being said, the cast of characters was colourful enough that it does well without it.Second one is that this game absolutely eats up computers. I can't recommend this game to most of my friends because it would cause their computers to implode! I keep having to go 'DUDE YOU SHOULD PLAY THE THAUMATURGE... once you get a better rig tho', which sucks cuz I want more people to play this game!!!!But yes, as with above, 100% recommend this game if you computer can take it. It was just a fantastic experience all around.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Capturing demons to bolster your occult skills, solving murders with thaumaturgy, getting into fist fights with random sailors, finding out everyone's secrets in the early 20th century Warsaw. What's not to like?The Thaumaturge is not a polished AAA game, but if you don't mind a few rough edges here and there, it makes for an ambitious indie game with nice visuals and detailed world building. The game world is beautiful, voice acting is alright. Choices matter. Combat is turn based and fairly easy to learn. I thought it was a bit challenging at times, but if you just want to immerse yourself in the story, you can make the combat easier any time.For me the best part in the game was encountering and capturing various salutor demons and utilizing their skills and synergies in combat. A very satisfactory RPG experience and definitely worth checking out if you find the setting intriguing.  However, if you're not into the whole historical setting and goth aesthetic, maybe wait until a discount. The game involves a lot of running around, picking up stuff and picking sides, but it's not very complex. The main selling point is the general concept of thaumaturgy. And getting to hang around with cool guy Rasputin.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge is a great turn-based rpg that respects your time. A wonderful story, fun characters, and beautiful graphics/artwork all come together in a great gem of a game. The music is also top notch and well worth the price for the soundtrack. I would highly recommend for anyone looking for a slower pace but still fun, engaging and exciting game. The combat is unique and challenging without being overly complicated. Plays like a great novel and easily one of my top games of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

So far the game is quite easy but i don't mind because the story is cool! --Here is the first 30 min:  I know to soon to gie a positive review! But i will update as i go.Things to notice:- A bit of euro jank with the movement and the some stutter- You get at least the idea early on that you can make an impact on the story- The characters seem to have some real dept they are not very one note- Focus on eastern europeaan conflicts- Very very story focus! _childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: don't be confused by the turn based combat and the complex story with multiple sidequests: this is not your run-of-the-mill RPG. If anything, this game is something like a Sherlock Holmes game with a few combats sprinkled here and there. Something like if one of the Vampire The Masquerade visual novels had a child with Pokemon (I'm afraid you'll only get this last part if you play the game).That does not mean, in any way, that the game is bad. On the contrary, this is one of the best games I've played lately, but if you come here expecting to skip every dialogue and jump right into the action, you are going to be very, very disappointed. If anything, the game has TOO MUCH combat for my taste. I often find myself trying to do the fights as fast as possible so I can go back to the mystery solving.You will also be extremely disappointed if you expect to play with a character that speaks and acts like you: you will make many decisions and get to very different outcomes than other players, but the main character, Wiktor Szulski (yes, I had to google the name) has his own personality, and you will have to go through that.On the technical aspect, I've had a few fps drops here and there, but still nothing too important, and I definitely didn't find any gamebreaking bugs. Many so called triple A's could learn a thing or two.In summary, if you are looking for a game with a strong story component and some greatly captivating lore, this is for you. On the other hand, if you are looking for a Baldur's Gate type of RPG, you better find something else. But if you do, be advised: you are missing on a product with an amazing story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: great game if you love shen megami tensei, the designs of the demons are neat, and after collecting them all i would say that i end up using all of them so none of them feel useless. Most combats are similiar with boss fights requiring the most strategy, though Ive enjoyed the easier fights to use some of my more favorite helpers. The only compliant id really have is that the game is limited by its budget, which inst to say that cut scenes are bad in the game, its just that the game could use a bit more polish. 8.5/10 game for me would like to have a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Interesting concept of emotion magic-Underused setting-Enjoyable alternate history angleCons:-Bland/slow turn based combat that lacks depth-Walking/Running simulator, you'll be spamming right lick and following the quest trail for 80% of the game-Terribly written dialogue, in particular for the gang leader-Bad voice acting, the playable character is as stiff as a board, it's so dreary that I wish it was just a text based game-Needlessly confusing dialogue, for the first 4 hours I kept leaving a conversation wondering "what the hell did any of that mean?", like they expect you to read their very own magic system encyclopedia before playing-Surface level progression, it's quite literally 4 straight lines of "better dialogue options" & new cards for the combat system-Lots of time wasting, I don't mind reading in games in the slightest, but having a fully voiced cast, it's very jarring to swap from a 1 minute conversation, to 10 minutes of reading about the tiny details of someones home. This is of course part of the investigation part of the game, but it's so padded out that for every 1 needed investigation, there will be at least 3-4 it forces you to do.I'm honestly super disappointed by this one, if you don't find yourself enjoying it in the first 2 hours, don't expect it to get better.Buy on big sale & judge by the first few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, I'm playing combat on story mode but enjoying everything else tremendously. It's one of those where you'll especially enjoy it if you like reading and are willing to immerse yourself in someone else's world-building. And as a fan of alternative history and well-thought-out supernatural worlds within the real world, the team did a great job lovingly creating this world, its characters and their conflicts. It's all fully voiced as well, even if the English voice acting is often a bit bored-sounding or even uncanny.This is also a beautiful game. Some very talented folk at Fool's Theory. Kudos.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Very atmospheric, they really nailed the tone and the ost was exceptional and I've learned some very interesting things during the time period. The story was pretty good and I really enjoyed the gameplay. Not too sure if my choices and actions really mattered that much but it did shape Viktor's personality. Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of story, characters and overall atmosphere. I think there is great potential for a sequel with the characters of this game making a return . To me, the main protagonist can stand well alongside other iconic gaming characters – I think he has a very strong presentation here.However, if the mentioned positives do not interest you, then there might not be much for you here. I felt the game was overall quite repetitive, though the combat sometimes has its exciting moments where you manage to queue up your attacks in just the right way to destroy everything in a way that could almost be considered elegant. The game is great and I recommend it despite its flaws, but how highly depends on personal taste, because not everyone will enjoy this or not get annoyed enough by the repetition to see the end. But my perception of that may have been a bit diluted by the fact that I wanted to find almost every single tiny detail that there was to find in the world and have read every single text presented in the game. When I think about that, going from start to finish might be achieved 2-3x faster compared to my initial review hours.Often times I cannot be bothered to write a review for games I play, but this game is less known and I think it deserves to be better known. I would love to see more of it in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This is very boring thank you very much. Dialogues, the whole city. Everything has an empty, empty feeling. The amount of notes scattered around... _childDocuments_.review: So far I have completed the game only once, but will be back for sure for the second run. Great atmosphere, nice Warsaw, emotional and engaging story with nicely written characters - these are the strongest points.I regret the game does not have Polish dubbing (but fortunately it's something 11 bit is working on). Sometimes the gameplay is a bit boring, because in the course of the game no new mechanics are introduced - this is probably the biggest flaw, but still it is a very engaging game that gave me a lot of fun. Also it is relatively easy - the fights are mostly very easy and repeatable, I hope it will get improved over time. If you like story-rich games with great atmosphere and interesting characters - it's a game for you. If you prefer action-packed games with challanges - probably it's not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid effort by the devs, decent story, the isometric genre looks pretty good in this day in age. That being said, it did play pretty loose with the history of the region, lumping some of which was adjusted to meet the sentiments of modern audiences.  There are enough small nods to general geekdom, and Easter eggs to other series and books that are fun to find.  You'll get a solid 22-23 hours out of the experience, not sure it is worth playing through again for a slightly different ending cut-scene. Performance wise, this game is surprisingly heavy, and has pretty drastic swings in performance needs between transitions of environments. Seems to also have a slight memory leak where by the end of a 3-4 hour period, textures stop appearing (on a card with 16GB of VRAM), and cause some jarring visual bugs such as the skin missing between a neck and torso. Other oddities include the game remaining fully rendered and asking for all resources in pause menus and when it is no longer in focus. Better to save and quit when you need to step away for any length of time otherwise you’ll be sucking the full power of your rig from the wall that whole time. TLDR; good effort, decent story, pretty visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me of another game.Disco ElysiumYou get a lot of text to read, can solve conversations with different aproaches, level your skills and your descisions matter.The Story is unique to me, the theme of this people (Thaumaturges) who can read Messages imprinted into common items. You have your "Salutor" and can aquire other Salutors. A guy named "Rasputin" helps you with this task. You can manipulate others and force them to do as you wish (kinda Jedi Mind tricks).The game takes place most of the time in Warsaw 1905, a time of change. You get the chance to experiance a little bit of the folklore, the working conditions of those ppl, religious believes and russias secret police (Ochrada).Things I liked- the storytelling- new Setting with the Thaumaturges- Consequences of your choices- the game has DLSS and works fine with it. I can't remember any crashes im my playthrough- different ways of winning the fights (reduce focus, brute force, dots doing the job)- up to 8 Salutors helping you in the fights- a flaw "system". Some characters on your journeys will have flaws. You can make them yours and recieve another buff with every flaw you collect. Your MC has the flaw: "pride"- there were 2 or 3 moments that caught me off guard. I didn't expect the change of events and I remember it positive. Games don't often can do this kind of things, especially when it's not at the end of the game. If I remember correct at the end of an Act something pretty weired happened and i didn't expect it at all!- pretty stories to relax more while playing with the Landmarks and other Eventy you can acompany while playingThings I didn't like- kinda repetetive fights with your enemys, on hard difficulty only the last enemy was challenging- Ghosting appeared around the MC with DLSS from time to time for a short period of time when you move around with MC- It's impossible to unlock all Skills in 1 Playthrough (maybe because it's not supposed to be like that). The game throws Skillpoints at you in the beginning. In the later Stages of your Playthrough the same excercises don't give you the same amount of exp and you rarely gain another skillpoint (diminishing return or a new Skillpoint needs more exp. The game never shows you Numbers, only a progression on a plank until you recieve another Skillpoint)- the game tells you, that you have only "limited time" to complete side Missions but in the end i think thats not true. You could change the time of the day as often as you wanted, the time was still indicated with the same remaining slice of a watch. There is a Point of no return, but until then you can do all the side quests as you please- walking around and using the "snap" with your char reminded me of "Hogwards Legacy" and casting "Revelio" everywhere you walk around. The good thing is this maps are smaller than those in Hogwards Legacy- the "Pride" flaw will take your free will away in the later stages of the game, if you used it a lot of times. (there is a Achievement to use it often)In my Opinion this game is pretty worth it if you like to read a lot, explore the areas you were given and take your time with relaxing while playing. The fighting System is round based, you are not in a hurry to decide what you like to do. You get used to the mechanic of the battles. The game gives you time to gather clues and when you found all of them it gives you a conclusion to this connected hints. The resume about it is used in conversations. The game can have value in replaying it since it's up to you how you influence your surrounding. You can end up with up to 8 Salutors or with less. People can survive or die to your path because of your descisions.I played the game without the DLC content, which was at my time the Soundtrack and the 3D image for a 3D printer and the clothes pack. So I didn't miss any ingame storys.I would not comprehend this game with "Disco Elysium" too much since the Settings are different. You had your fights in a conversation in Disco Elysium, you had your random rolls, could study things with ingame time and so on.In "The Thaumaturge" you have only random Numbers on your dmg rolls and the chance of interrupting your enemy. You have less variety on developing your character. It's more straight forward. If you foung a Clue, it can have a fixed Number that you must beat to get the Info. You can check the same Item later in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like point&click adventures? Do you enjoy turn-based combat? Do you find the historical setting with a magical spin on it enticing? Do you enjoy reading and exploring a lot?If you answered yes, this game is for you. The setting and world building is fantastic. The combat isn't incredibly deep but it's very fun regardless. And the story was interesting. I managed to reach 2 main endings and my decisions have clearly impacted the story. Very nice. The characters are well done IMO. The salutors are quite different gameplay-wise. Pure damage, control-focused, condition-based, there are multiple ways to fight with them and I certainly appreciate the available choices. Morana FTW, control was my favorite.Sure, the game may seem very simple to some people, I'd say it depends on one's preferences. Basically if you dislike anything I have listed in the first paragraph, you might not enjoy it. Or you still may.I hope that there will be a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: great storytelling, characters and atmosphere, mediocre and boring gameplayThe story is fantastic, and the characters are fleshed out and interesting. There are multiple approaches to some situations and there are consequences for doing things a certain way.However in many cases the consequences are strange or unclear, and the whole gameplay loop is immensely boring.The combat is repetitive and easy, the exploration is dull and doesn't motivate you to explore. _childDocuments_.review: All around a solid AA game.The combat was far and away the highlight for me.  Everything is based on rounds and time based attacks, but what's interesting is you can (usually) see what your opponent is going to do in their rounds so you adjust according to that.  Then there's an entire system of traits that give abilities to enemies (Won't take negative effects, Heals X every turn) that can only be disabled by attacking with certain salutors (demons) that you own.  Demon attacks are also time based and have a variety of abilities that can also be set - damage over time, time bombs, etc.  Felt just challenging enough on "hard" difficulty.The story was OK.  1905 Warsaw was interesting to poke around in, and there are lots of "fluff" pieces to read and explore.  I found most of the characters to be pretty boring outside of a few side characters who were more interestingly written.  But mostly I found myself speeding through the dialogue in the latter quarter of the game, especially when things started being more on rails.  There seems like there was a relatively decent amount of divergence in story options, if that's your sort of thing.  And you get a nice little epilogue summing up all of your choices.The most disappointing aspect was the "detective" work.  This involves running around the map constantly pressing right click to scan the area for clues which show up as a red mist, and then become more apparent as you get closer to them.  In a few of the quests and side quests you could have divergent paths based on if you bothered finding all of the clues or not, but mostly it felt like an exercise in time gating having to hunt down objects on the map.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Gameplay Walkthrough - The Thaumaturge is a thought-provoking and haunting RPG that expertly combines gameplay and narrative, leading to one of the most unique RPG experiences . Its stunning setting and choice-driven narrative will undoubtedly stick with me for a long time as I reflect on the tough decisions I made with Wiktor as he comes to terms with this dark, fantasy-filled version of Warsaw. The combat arguably takes too long to reveal its riches, but once that initial barrier is overcome, it offers the same level of depth and choice present in other aspects of The Thaumaturge.The supernatural powers at protagonist Wiktor Szulski’s disposal pave the way to a satisfying battle system that carves out its own identity, despite looking like something out of Shin Megami Tensei or Persona upon first glance. There are technical rough edges here and there, but I firmly believe that RPG fans should definitely check outThe Thaumaturge whenever they find time in this busy year of RPGs in 2024.Rating - 8/10 ( GO FOR IT )

_childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge, despite its shortcomings at times is a beautifully realized game with world building and writing that is rarely seen in games nowadays, While I enjoyed its simple yet fun combat system, its main attraction was its well told story and a chance to explore a beautifully designed semi open world the team crafted. Shout-out to the art direction team leading this game, they really earned their paycheck with this one. If you are a fan of story led games, with well crafted characters and narrative concepts that are explored from diverse points of view, Then the Thaumaturge is a definitive recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: A fresh and interesting CRPG with a unique setting and story. Taking place in 1905 Warsaw, you solve mysteries as a wizard detective along with your best buddy Gregori Rasputin. You are a Thaumaturge, a magician gifted with the ability to discern and extract people's "flaws" and win the aid of demons called salutors that are attracted to them. Sounds a bit like Persona right? That's not an accident I'm sure, this is very much a grim, eastern european, turn of the century take on Persona. The world, writing characters and voice acting are all top notch. The combat, however, is a resounding meh. I'm not sure why I found the combat in this game so tedious at 18 hours when Persona 5 has extremely similar combat and was over a 100 hours long without me getting bored, but it's missing SOMETHING that causes it to get old real fast. There's a level of polish missing from the game, no pun intended, but that's to be expected from a relatively low budget indie release. If it were up to me, I would have cut all the "Urban Mysteries" side quests, which amounted to very little more than map clutter. I get that they are supposed to make Warsaw feel like a living breathing city, and I appreciate the pains taken to lovingly portray the city of 1905 in such fidelity, but they just felt like a chore, nothing more.That being said, I can heartily recommend this for fans of CRPGs, Urban Fantasy and Historical Fiction. This is a setting and story you so rarely see in games, and it feels fresh and novel.

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing out of my mouth was "You can pet the dog!" This game was a lot of fun, if a bit tedious at times with the amount of running back and forth you have to do for all the urban secrets and tailor inspirations but I found the story very good. I'm curious to see what the other end of some of the choices I made look like, so it probably won't be long before I'm doing another play through. Voice acting is a bit hit or miss, some of the accents are pretty inconsistent, and sometimes the audio doesn't match the subtitles, but even when the voice acting is a bit wonky it didn't spoil my enjoyment of the game. In fact it was pretty nice to be able to laugh over a slightly silly line delivery when the story is so grim and dark all the time. Honestly if you like RPG's, history and gothic fantasy then I'd recommend checking it out.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not what I expected from trailer, but it's not bad. I loved many things about it. The writing is decent, and the characters are nice and likeable  their own way). I enjoyed exploration and world-building in general, the game offers plenty of details, landmarks and historical bits to discover. Not sure that fixed isometric camera was the right choice for such activities.Combat was my least favourite part. It was repetitive and somewhat annoying. The system is clunky, and overcomplicated in general, but JRPG lovers might enjoy it. Non-combat scenarios are rare, and in most cases you can't avoid a fight. I did all the side-content I could get (missed few collectibles and couple of costumes), but I barely had enough exp to reach the 3rd combos. Early in game, you get showered with those points, and game encourages you to spend them, and develop all of your aspects to do the quests, but by the moment you get to the higher skills, the exp practically stops.  Could still win final boss fight with a second attempt. People had mentioned poor resource optimization, and I can confirm it. Game eats GPU like it's a Cyberpunk-grade AAA product, and not a small isometric RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed my time with The Thaumaturge. It's clear that the developers poured a lot of love into creating this game. Although I encountered a few minor frustrations during my playthrough, they were nothing too serious. And I didn’t encounter any bugs; the game is stable.The combat mechanics are quite original, but they quickly become repetitive and lack challenge after a while. The investigation segments are interesting, but sometimes the guidance is a bit too heavy-handed. I also found that the protagonist sometimes jumps to conclusions too quickly, while at other times, it felt like the opposite.The graphics and artistic direction are fairly standard. It’s not a particularly beautiful game, but it’s not unattractive either. The soundtrack effectively immerses you in a Slavic universe, though it remains simple. The story is intriguing and kept me interested until the end. However, the pacing speeds up too much towards the finale, and some endings feel more rushed than others. This is a common issue in many games, unfortunately. I also regret that some side quests, particularly those involving political choices, do not significantly influence the ending.I would recommend The Thaumaturge to players who enjoy isometric RPGs and prioritize story over combat.

_childDocuments_.review: As an RPG, The Thaumaturge is bog standard: you do side quests and main quests, you level up to improve your magic, you overcome enemies, you finish the game. But there are three aspects that really stand out. First, I liked the combat mechanics: it's a turn-based card game where you attack both by yourself and by your creatures (salutors), exploiting enemy vulnerabilities and rushing to kill them before they deal enough damage to you. Doesn't sound exciting, I know, but it kept me engaged throughout, although the fights were quite easy.Second, the plot and setting. The Thaumaturge is set is early XX century Poland, which means that you rebel against the Russian empire (or not), mingle in a society where you can notice signs of the impending doom, meet Tsar Nicolas himself, and one of your best friends in the game is, of course, Grigori Rasputin. Combines with the premise of magic actually existing in this world, it all sounds like a lot of balderdash, but actually the world is very cleverly put together and believable. I really enjoyed all the little stories and lore pieces that you find here, and although I'm no expert I think the authors really tried to be faithful at least to the spirit of real historical Poland of the time.Which brings me to the third point: the writing. Everything you do in the game is accompanied by a very well written description, and although you will certainly skim through most rather than wallow in every note and every clue you pick up, it also adds a lot to the atmosphere. I enjoyed the reading that The Thaumaturge makes you do, it's maybe not at the level of Disco Elysium but it does the job very nicely. Overall, great game, not too long, the story moves along briskly, and quite a few of my 22 hours were spent chasing collectibles. Wholeheartedly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the story, I immersed in Wiktor's life and followed different branches based on his decisions. And decisions do matter, which is a good thing in my books. So, I recommend this game, at least first run was absolutely enjoyable.What I did not like is the obscurity of consequences to your actions. Sometimes game tells you "this dialog option is not available due to your previous decisions" and you have no clue what decisions it has in mind. What is worse, sometimes dialog options and even entire side quests disappear without a trace and pretty often there is no way to know how did this happen. Internet search does not help either - apparently not too many people play it.

_childDocuments_.review: **SPOILER FREE**The Thaumaturge is a pseudo historical game taking place in the early 20th century. In the almost three hours I've spent in game as of writing this review, I've been to multiple locales and gotten a taste of beginning and intermediate combat.The game is what it is - you play a character who can see certain things in the world that most people cannot. You can gain a companion spirit called a Salutor - and that's as in depth as I'm going to go with it.There are historical figures in the game, and very real situations that actually happened in real places. If you're curious how accurately the eastern European countryside is displayed in this game, it is accurate for the time period. Matters for some, not so much for others. I'm ambivalent.The price of the game is extremely fair considering I've played 3 hours and don't feel like I'm even a quarter of the way through yet. You can also get the deluxe which has some nice goodies in it, such as a soundtrack which is actually decent to listen to on its own.At the end of the day, there are worse games you could spend your money on, and I am enjoying myself a great deal in the limited sample I've played.One last thing: combat is turn based and "card" based. You could probably steamroll through on story mode, but I picked the middle of the road option, and you have to be thoughtful with your combat once you get past the tutorial.Good luck, have fun, eat the slice of cake because we could all get hit by a comet in our sleep and no longer exist tomorrow. Life's too short.

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't bring myself to finish the game, even though I found it quite interesting. The reason is simple: most quests are marked as "time-sensitive" and will become unavailable after a certain point.The problem is, the game doesn't tell you what these time restrictions are!  To make matters worse, many quests require you to manually wait for a specific time of day. Every time I'm forced to do this, I get stressed out, wondering if I'm going to accidentally fail other quests I've already started.It's incredibly frustrating because I really want to experience everything the game world has to offer. But I don't want to have to play through the entire game multiple times just to see everything!

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased the game on a whim and absolutely loved it. What a breath of fresh air in an otherwise stagnant and soulless industry. Aside from a few minor technical flaws, the game is nearly perfect. Great care was clearly taken when crafting the mythology, the setting, the atmosphere, the narrative, and so on. The focus of The Thaumaturge is story and you'll spend a lot of time exploring, reading notes, and engaging in dialog. This creates a wonderfully immersive experience that few modern titles achieve. The combat system is good enough for this type of game, but that's a secondary priority. If action is your desire, you have a million other games to choose; this one is offering something different. It's a unique bright spot in the world of modern interactive media.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy............ I really really really wanted to like this game but I have mixed feelings... I would not recommend, but still there are good aspects. _childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge is a Turn-Based RPG mixed with a heavy emphasis on detective work and a bit of collectathon (collectibles give a lot of XP and are everywhere, but obtaining them all isn't necessary)You'll be playing as Wiktor Szulski a Thaumaturge (demon hunter / detective guy) in Poland in 1905, basically just before the revolution of the kingdom of Poland against the Russian Empire, and if I mention it, it is because it is central in the plot of the game.In all of this Wiktor our friendly Thaumaturge will come back to Warsaw a city that he despise after having been banished by his father years ago, it is due to his death that he will eventually come back to help emotionally his sister that is now alone.Multiple events will make that Wiktor will stay longer than he intended and solve crimes and different mysteries in the city of Warsaw.While the prologue is played in Georgia, the remainder of the game is completely played in Warsaw, a city where the Russian Empire and the Socialists tend to not have only friendly encounters, I have to say that the game being played mostly in one city wasn't my favorite thing about the game and that the prologue is probably what I've liked the most, but overall the world design of the game is really well done and polished, it is probably where the game shine the most to be frank.As for the story, I believe it is relatively good for a AA but it has some pacing problems especially if you tend to take your time, you'll have tense moments and then really long times without anything going on, you should also expect to read a lot because while the game is fully voiced as far as characters are concerned, it isn't the case for the collectibles.Now gameplay wise, it is turn-based, Wiktor will almost always be alone with one demon that he can change whenever he wants, each demons in the game have its specificity, such as doing more damage to full health enemies or another one that is the opposite and is good at finishing kill, there is also one based on luck, and finally one or two based on being completely broken too.Because while the game is really well balanced early on it start to fall apart really quickly once you unlock a certain demon, that I won't name here, but we'll call it "M".M, alongside a few others completely destroy the game and even make for some fights where the enemies simply cannot damage you at all, so is it that bad after all ? Well in my opinion it isn't because you're not forced to use M and can simply restrict yourself to more balanced demons.Difficulty wise, as I mentioned before M is broken, and I've played in challenge mode, which is the hardest difficulty, but the biggest problem of the game in my opinion lie in it's story difficulty (the lowest) where you simply take almost no damage, but the enemies aren't more squishy either, which make for some long and uninteresting fights while I'm sure some people just want to experience the story, it needs to be fixed ASAP, that difficulty should allow for much faster fights to allow people to enjoy the game without them.Because well, while I like the fighting system, outside of the challenge mode it is boring and repetitive. Toward the end I have to say that it was becoming a bit too stale but it was maybe due to me abusing M to get rid of the fights, but I think overall it is simply because outside of the demons the fighting system doesn't evolve much during the game and while early on there is only a few fights which is perfect, later on they tend to put much more of them.Luckily for us "M" happen to be quite good for the eyes.I've taken 35 hours to complete the game by being slow and taking my time, overall the game is pleasant, I would not say it is the best game I've ever played but it is definitely a good surprise.Also, I've played a press build for the game, but when I've played the game it was full of technical problems such as loading screens, freeze, slowdowns etc... (more toward the end of the game as the prologue was really smooth) so be careful about that even though no review seem to mention that problem, so it was probably fixed for the release.Here is a link to a voiced review if you prefer listening to me with a french accent or want something more complete:

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about The Thaumaturge, but translation issues, spotty storytelling, and poorly developed mechanics prevent it from being something that I highly recommend. The writing in the game is usually serviceable. There are some very good moments between the main character and his sister and some interesting interactions with the history of Poland. Most of the issues with the dialogue appear to be caused be with translation problems. I was able to overlook most of this, but there were multiple times where characters talking to each other did not appear to be having the same conversation or I just plain didn't understand what they were talking about. More problematic is the voice acting. It is generally quite mediocre, with much of it being quite poor. Accents are all over the place with some of the cast seeming to be doing bad American accents for Polish or Russian characters. Most of the acting was not enjoyably bad, instead just making the characters harder to invest in. While I'm unsure if it would entirely fix the issue, I would greatly prefer if characters just spoke in their native languages with subtitles. The overarching story is largely enjoyable, albeit with a somewhat rushed and limp ending. It's really the main appeal to the game, along with the excellent designs for the salutors (spirits or demons). You interact with several historical figures during the game, primarily Grigori Rasputin. From what I understand, it portrays him semi-realistically, though personally I didn't care for his character much in the game (his voice acting is among the strongest in the game however). On a final note, there are several instances of bizarre anachronistic pop culture references in the game. They're minor overall, but jarring and just a very odd inclusion. Quests in the game are another issue. Most of the game is played by clicking on every icon in your environment, then talking to a character to resolve the quest, frequently with a choice of outcome. There's essentially no deduction required on the part of the player, you simply need to find the right places to click. This was fine during the more fleshed out quests, however the game also features dozens of tiny miniquests that have very little value to completing other than a small amount of experience points as rewards. These could be ignored if preferred, however there are a few of these that turn into larger side quests that can result in completing your collection of skills. It would be better if these were clearly marked, but best of all if the quests were trimmed to a smaller amount of more worthwhile encounters. Experience points and skills felt underdeveloped as well. For the first part of the game, I received more skill points than I could use, and assumed that this pace would continue. This left me frustrated at the end of the game when leveling slowed to the point where I actually didn't have enough points to increase skills to complete some of the final checks in the game. If I had a better idea going in of what to expect, I would have made different decisions. The game does not communicate what to expect however. Finally, combat. Combat is turn-based and was somewhat interesting, however it feels like it needed more development to turn into something really worthwhile. As is, the majority of combat encounters on the standard difficulty are trivially easy, with sudden spikes in difficulty during bosses. This is mostly a problem because of the sheer number of combat encounters during the game. Essentially every quest results in someone attacking you, frequently for very silly reasons. A final frustration for me with the game was the inability to make decisions that I preferred. Sometimes this is because the game does not fully explain the consequences of your actions and sometimes you simply will not be able to choose what your character does at all. Every choice-based RPG will have the latter to some extent, but it felt particularly frustrating to me here. I found myself giving the game more chances than I would normally due to its premise, some of its strong presentation, and the indie game studio behind it. I found it overall unfulfilling, but I still remain interested in what the team does next. I hope they learn from the weaknesses of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Achievements bugged out. Almost finished second act. Caught all Salutors. Did every quest I could.Game suffers from overabundance of ambition and lack of execution. It might try to convince you that there is a fun demonic combat to be had and adventure-like, detective type work to do. Neither is true.Combat is your typical one-action-per-round turn based combat with very slight variation. All in all, because of how incredibly easy the combat is, it doesnt amount to much. Becomes very repetitive very fast.There is no detective work to be done. You dont even have to read most of the text from the clues you keep picking up- the main character will outright tell you what happened when you collect all the clues in the set. Just pulse your batman vision like madman and collect all clues until the game gives you a solution. Well done detective!The setting might be interesting if you are a Pole, like Polish history or like the year 1905. Otherwise it amounts to taking place in a random European city of the era, but with more alcohol consumption.Audio and visuals are a mess. The voice actors try to affect some sort of Polish/Russian English accent early on, but most give up as the game goes on and just use plain English. The artists knew how to make cool looking Salutors, but apparently their artistic passion doesnt extend to pleasing human facial features. At least Wiktor and Ligia look ok.Lastly, the game has a terminal lack of systems. Its billed as an RPG, but you have no real inventory, equipment, money and so on. The amount of actual quests (not errands that are all the same) is fairly small.Hate to be so negative, as I liked the premise and the main character, but there are better ways of spending your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Original and intriguing. This game draws you in mainly through the narrative, the world it has, the characters, and, above all, the relationships between them. Wiktor Szulski is not a classic game protagonist; he does not exist artificially alienated from the NPCs, but he lives in a web of relationships. The dialogues sparkle, there's a sense of over-the-top, eastern European humor (i.e., the magical space between wanting to commit suicide and enjoying another day). The quests are good; I'm really looking forward to what happens next with the "Fisherman," the painter and the murders! And the lore is impressive, especially since it's created from scratch. The motif of the Salutors dovetails perfectly with the themes of facing one's own and others' demons, as well as shouldering some sort of legacy, which are so heavily emphasized in the story itself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, if you've watched a couple of videos, read the synopsis, and thought, 'yes, this game is right up my alley', you're most likely correct. I was all set to buy this game on release, then some of the reviews caused me to hesitate. I finally went for it and was very glad I did; I thoroughly enjoyed this game from start to finish.I found the game to be very compelling. Wiktor's a fascinating protagonist and, although you can influence his trajectory and choose his dialogue responses, he is a strongly defined character with a set history, so if you're looking for a game with a player character you can mold, Wiktor isn't it. I enjoyed getting to know him and to see his story unfold, and this game was constantly on my mind when I was unable to play it. The game-play is very simple, particularly outside of combat. It's largely point and click and there is no deductive reasoning to be done; as long as you find all the clues, WIktor draws his own conclusions with no input from the player. The combat operates a little like a deck builder. It wasn't always my favourite part of the game (and Wiktor manages to get into more fights than seemed realistic), but the battles are typically brief and do provide variety, so I didn't hate them, either. I did find very little difference between the easy mode and the normal mode; if you really begin to struggle, your only real recourse is to switch up your tactics. I did appreciate that I could pause the game at any point. This is a game you can easily pause, put down, walk away, and pick up at a later point. The characters, dialogue, and voice acting were all enjoyable. The voice acting wasn't always amazing but then this is hardly a big budget game. I think the game is perfectly priced for what you can expect. Around 35 hours is what it took for me to complete all side missions and collect all collectibles.Now for the two parts I really enjoyed:The atmosphere is wonderful. The music, time period, the characters' appearances, and Warsaw itself are in complete harmony. I was completely absorbed into Wiktor's world. The design of the salutors is fantastic. I appreciated that the game didn't shy away from making the characters look very ugly at times.The endings are varied and several of the choices you make do have direct consequences. I felt that I didn't get the best ending, but it was clear which choices I had made had influenced that, and I have only myself to blame! I have a couple of saves I'm likely to reload so I can try for a different ending. If you're wanting to do the same, I recommend putting off the main story in Act 2 until you've done all the side quests and collectibles you want to.

And the games basically is telling the player where to go and what to do, so where is the mystery in exploring?The bad:-Side quests are boring, and it feels more like grinding to increase your level.-Game play is dull and predictable. _childDocuments_.review: - The game is set in 1905 Warsaw, and really digs into the turbulent politics and social tensions of the city, as well as the day-to-day life of its citizens with stylish sketches of everyday scenes. A lot of effort has gone into realising the setting and making it believable.- Likewise, the more magical aspects of the plot are grounded in folklore and their own internal logic, treated more like a mystic science. The 'salutors', demonic spirits that enable your magical abilities, are all taken from mythical creatures and beautifully modelled, with some quite brutal combat animations.- There are a lot of significant choices to be made in how you resolve quests and respond to characters, and most of these have meaningful consequences for the story and how others respond to you. Some quests even have unmarked steps, where going to speak to a relevant character or explore a relevant location will open up further options, which feel very rewarding.- Taking up to 40 hours for a thorough playthrough and with six major endings and dozens of minor variations, there's definitely good value for money here without it overstaying its welcome.- The voice acting varies quite drastically in quality - most of it is good and some is excellent, but there are also one or two characters with quite bizarre delivery, and certain minor characters have inexplicable American, Irish or English accents despite being Polish or Russian.- The turn-based combat has some interesting ideas, but certain abilities and tactics are far more effective than others. Battles are rarely challenging even on hard difficulty, although the 'final boss' did take a few tries, and fights are sometimes a bit too frequent.- Skill points are very easy to earn in the early game but seem to hit a wall around the midpoint, which is also the point where skills begin to cost two or three points to unlock. This combination just feels very unsatisfying, and means that even a completionist will only get around half of the final tier skills.- The plot feels a bit rushed towards the end, with certain major characters and ideas being introduced without much lead-in. This pacing issue may be, in part, because events accelerate as the stakes rise, but I do think these concepts could have been seeded a bit earlier.All in all, the biggest reason I'd recommend The Thaumaturge is that it's trying something different and doing a pretty decent job at it - it's no Disco Elysium, but the setting, characters and 'lore' are well-realised and I always felt like my choices had meaningful consequences.
