_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is great, but it's not BLOOD. I'm sorry but I have to make the comparison because playing Cultic and facing my own expectations made me realise one aspect that made Blood so unique.This isn't as much criticism towards Cultic per se, but just some thoughts I had , when I wanted to vocalise what it is that made Blood my favourite FPS ever - and what it makes it different to modern games. Please don't misinterpret this comment as me dissing Cultic, as I said, I think it's great but I have a really special place in my gaming history for Blood and hence I just wanted to write this.And yes- I will be talking more about Blood in this review than I will talk about Cultic. I don't need to say anything about Cultic because you already know it's a great game so just buy it - I'm here to talk about how I'm really hard to please because I love Blood and I don't think I'll ever get an FPS  that would be as special for me and playing Cultic helped me to understand the difference with old build engine games and modern ones-  but especially Blood. So this is my recommendation to buy not only Cultic but DEFINITELY also Blood: Fresh Supply! Just do it.What Blood gets right is that it's not afraid of being more goofy, more old school game where unrealistic physics aren't a problem.Well, it is OLD. But what I mean is that Blood has insanely fun dynamite -lobbing and rag doll mechanics. I feel that this is something many reviewer's and critics seem to miss about Blood. Point being, Blood was the most fun Build engine game thanks to the fact that it didn't try to hide the fact that it's a video game and concentrated on the fun game play loop. Modern games seem to miss this. I don't understand why game maker's don't try to replicate more of the completely outrageous physics of Blood. It's unrealistic to make a zombie or cultist to fly across the screen with gore chunks with crazy speed, but that is FUN. I like Cultic but it's not fast, floaty and outrageous like that.I admit that Cultic has the unenviable position to be compared to Blood, mostly due to the references it wears on it's sleeve itself. Blood was fun, probably the most fun I've had with an old school FPS. It's more tongue in cheek but not only that - the physics are much more floaty and comical. But that makes the dynamite lobbing and destruction also more entertaining. This is one thing that Resident Evil 4 also understood - it's a game that it isn't afraid of being a "video game". Many modern games seem to fall into this trap that they try to bit too much go for some level of higher so-called "realism" but sometimes the old school games captured something special just because they seemed to have more justification of being a GAME. Goofy, unrealistic and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a great little game. Very nice and atmospheric, some good solid gameplay, nice and fast paced but also with some flexibility in how to approach fights if you want. Lots of little hidden secrets like an old school game, and while the art feels kind of like them it's done with much more modern back end methods that make it it all, thanks to good skill on the creators part, feel old school, yet still play smooth and with many of the more modern polishes and conveniences of modern engines.Pros-Gameplay, biggest pro.-Story/world, nice and interesting and largely handled through environmental stuff.-music and auidio, all great to listen to while playing, everything sounds good when fighting, and music is nice and energizing.-Art, very nicely done old pseudo pixel/old 3d style art and environments.-Pacing, nice variety of things and levels to keep it feeling different and fresh as you play,Cons-Length, it's quite short, just 5 or 6 hours even if you spend a lot of time exploring in the main story, a very enjoyable few hours those were mind you, but still short. And this is after the added interlude story update, only 4-5 without it. There is also survival mode that's decent, though definitely not for everybody. Given the price I'd say it's a great game still, but for those short on money wanting something to last awhile... depending on how much you like replaying stuff or working for high scores, this may or may not be for you. Hopefully new updates might add to this, but again even as is I'd say it's worth it.-Performance, a very minor con. It still ran good solid frame rate at all times but I got a higher/mid end system, but cranked my graphics card a lot more than I'd expect, even in menu/paused to go do other things. So it's more taxing than you might think, and have hoped if you have a really simple computer. So double check the requirements, sadly not much in the zone of graphical options or fps capping in case it was trying to render more fps than needed, but oh well. Still did at least play ok for me.Though on that note of the requirements, the current 3gb it says is inaccurate, it's closer to 6gb now with updates, not a huge deal just something they might want to change, and you be aware of if that matters till they do.

_childDocuments_.review: A promising start.Cultic chapter one is a great foundation for, when finished, probably one of the best feeling retro inspired shooters out there. And even though it is clearly inspired by blood with the cultist and some of weaponry it has a feel entirely of it's own. There are some points that can be improved upon however and im hoping we can see that in chapter two and hopefulfy three.Things that I think can be improved upon:- More assets. Sure the maps felt immersive but seeing only 1 type of tree and 1 type of shrubbery that were just sized differently for the entire game made some areas feel very samey. The trees are just an example but also the trucks, cabins and some other stuff is repeated just enough that it made me think "oh hey it's that same asset again"- Enemy AI. Enemies get stuck on terrain quite often, they also have a habit of killing eachother when they are bunched up trying to shoot you. A bit lame when that happens.- More varied environments. I feel like the game had a bit too many cramped areas like the crypt, mines, caves etc that all played very similar because of the nature of such environments. Areas like the mining town, and the asylum outskirts stood out more because they were bigger and forced you to think about how to aproach the area or what building to explore first.- Better bosses. The boss fights were pretty underwhelming, both were stationary targets and both pretty annoying to fight because of the way you had to deal with both the boss and the spawning of cultists.- More set pieces. Seeing the sky lighting up and the asylum being set on fire were unique moments that stood out, Those were great.Those are just a few things I could think of but even currently just chapter one is well worth it. I've had great fun and I will jump back in a few more times to find all the remaining secrets and achievements.Well done to Jason Smith for delivering such an exceptional game, can't wait to see where it goes next.

Now filled with anger, he plans on taking revenge by killing the cult and all of its members. _childDocuments_.review: An all-around excellent FPS game. CULTIC has the distinction of being one of the few games that has perfectly predicted me as a player.For context, when I started this game, I did so while streaming, so a friend could watch. During our discussion, I would note things like, "The level design here is excellent" or "hey, this is a cool area." Within moments, CULTIC would have me swearing in panic as I realized I'd been pulled into yet another trap, my friend all the while doubled over with glee. The music is incredible. The visuals are haunting, sinister, and detailed in a way that only games with a low-res sensibility can be without alienating modern-day players. The weapons are punchy and fun to use, the sound design is excellent, killing people with dining room furniture is satisfying, and the level design is  good. Insanely good. I can't express to you enough how intuitive and well thought-out the levels are in terms of design. I've spent an awful lot of time crawling around several of these levels and still managed to not see or find everything.I heavily recommend this game if you're into DOOM-esque shooters, action-horror shooters like Blood, or just plain challenging shooter games with a retro aesthetic. This is A-level indie dev work, which is especially surprising given the size of the developer team: one guy.Do yourself a favor and give at least the demo a shot. You'll very likely want to come back for the whole thing.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing shooters for almost three decades, and this is one of my favorites in recent memory.  First of all, let me address the game's look and feel, probably its most salient aspect.The art style is unique, weirdly beautiful, and fits the game's tone perfectly.  I have never seen a game that looks like this before, and I can only guess how much effort went into getting it to have this look without making everything an ugly, pixelated mess.  Yes, you really can see an enemy across even the game's largest maps well enough to no-scope headshot them, and you'll be doing a lot of that if you want to stay alive.  That brings me to combat:This game does long range combat remarkably well, something I have rarely seen done with any real level of effectiveness in a "boomer shooter."  You can fight an enemy hundreds of meters away, and both you and that enemy will pose a serious threat to one another, requiring use of cover and quick aiming to come out on top.  However, the game gives you the precision to do this very effectively with a little practice, mostly by means of the lever action rifle or scoped FG 42.  That's not to say long range combat is the only way to handle things.  Close range combat is just as good, with a very cool retro weapon set that offers up a Mauser C96, double barrel shotgun, and a Sten MkIV, among other weapons that can be highly effective up close.  There are literally no bad weapons in this game.  I have played through it several times now, upgrading different weapons in different ways, and I can't find a way to break my build.  Upgrades will definitely affect how you play, but they never govern it entirely.Explosives and incendiaries are plentiful, and hilariously fun, as they should be.Enemy variety is much better than middling for the genre, with a good selection of baddies on tap to blast.  No complaints in that regard.Controls are simple, old-school WASD, but done right, with good responsiveness.The level design really feels like a natural progression of old Build Engine games.  Environments range from claustrophobic to enormous, and present a wide variety of combat challenges.  Environments manage to feel fairly real and immersive despite the graphical style, and I think that owes much to the developer embracing the limitations of the low-polygon, sprite-based retro shooter by way of the game's artistic rendering.As far as negatives go, the game is fairly short.  With only 26 hours, I'm almost through my third run, this time on Extreme, having beaten Hard and Very Hard.  That said, this game was essentially made by one individual, so there's only so much  length and content to be reasonably expected.  Another issue is that there is some platforming (mostly to get to secrets) that doesn't feel quite right in a few places.  There are also some combat scenarios that at first feel grossly unfair -- like "Blood" unfair.  However, I've always managed to find a way through them with some work.  Really, none of that is unusual for the genre, and it never really feels in any way crippling.Simply put: if you like retro shooters, you'll probably like this game.  Highly Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Got bored one day, bought this game, booted it up...INSTANT 10/10Dear lord this game is amazing AND IT IS DONE BY ONE GUY?! WHAAAAAAAAA?So what are you expecting from this game?It's a Retro FPS, you boot it up, start a new game, pick up the weapon in front of you and shoot your way through enemies...simple as that.- There is a story, simple but effective: it's the 1960, you're a detective investigating on a case of people dissapearing, for one reason or another you're taken off the case but that ain't enough to stop you so you picked up a gun and your car to put the word end to the case...turns out it's cultist and they ain't happy to see ya. The lore is told through files; but of course the real star of the show is the gameplay.- The gameplay rocks: The arsenal is perfect and each gun feels chunky, meaty, powerful; Headshots are satisfying and play a big role much like explosions and fire, most of the environment is interactive and there's stuff to YEET at the enemies, the movement is perfect, quick enough to feel like you're in an action movie, the dodge, the kick boosting and the slide compliment the movement; much like a pizza with a good beer.- The enemies are varied: Cultist armed with various weapons, Armored, Zombies, ABOMINATIONS FROM ANOTHER DIMENTIONS... they have a simple AI (Find player, kill player, HOOGA BOOGA) and yet they can surprise you, also they all hurt like hell.- The OST surprised me, i was expecting creepy tunes and chanting ( I got that), i wasn't expecting an action movie OST, it's good.- The atmosphere of this game is another highlight, it can go from: Feeling like Ash Williams, killing cultist, spouting one liners ( Yourself of course, the character is silent) and then all of a sudden it's: "Why is the music gone? Why is everything gone quiet? Why do i have a bad fee...AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA"- The game has 10 levels but they're well designed and long just the right amount of time.If you're a fan of FUN FPS games then...BUY THIS GAME! Even at full price it's worth every cent!

_childDocuments_.review: A retro-style FPS that honestly surprised me of how good it is. I started gaming a bit late, so I didn't have any fond memory of retro FPS games with this style. At first I was skeptical that I'd enjoy this the way other people do. But damn, from the very first level, it hooked me in. The gunplay and combat sandbox especially sold this game for me. Despite using 2D sprites for enemies and your weapons, the animation and weapon recoil make the combat weighty, punchy and satisfying. Nailing a headshot with the repeater feels so good in this game.The enemies are also well done. Each of them serves a purpose in pressuring the player to use the right tool and keep them on their toes. As the game progresses, you get to upgrade your weapons and become stronger, but more supernatural enemies join the fight to keep up the pace. It's the mix of challenge and power fantasy all the way through.Each map has well crafted layouts with decently paced combat, exploration, cool set pieces and atmospheric horror. Experiencing this blind (not literally, just not looking up walkthroughs) with my headphones on was one of the few games that made me sit and finish the game from start to finish.But it's not really finished since this only has the first chapter. And honestly, the first chapter being 4 hours long, brimming with content, secrets, and variety of each level, is already more than worthy of the price. I'm eagerly looking forward to see what comes next.

_childDocuments_.review: CULTIC is one of those games that hits all the right notes with me. From the atmosphere and tone to the gameplay it all feels just right. The dark/horror aesthetics are incredible and feel like a mix of Resident Evil meets BLOOD, but takes itself a bit more seriously which isn't a fault by any means.The guns are some of the most fun I've used in an FPS recently, they're incredibly weighty and pack a big punch while also staying relevant in the player's arsenal throughout the campaign. It helps that the cultists are quite reactive too. Popping heads hasn't felt so good in a game in a long time. The gibbing is great too, enemies can burst into a pool of viscera, blood will stick to the walls and ceilings and slowly drip. Direct impact dynamite kills on groups are probably some of the most satisfying ways to take out enemies in this game.Player movement feels great, there's weight to it without being unwieldy or floaty. It gets especially fun once you start incorporating momentum kicks in for much faster movement.The game certainly lends itself to playing more tactically than other retry throwbacks, so running and gunning might not always be the best choice. Other times you're free to let loose and unleash hell.If I had to make a criticism; there are a lot of fights that you can take on mostly safely from a distance, that due in part to many of the levels being quite open. This doesn't mean they aren't fun by any means, you're just generally a lot more safe when at a distance as the cultists attacks become much easier to avoid.Some of the best encounters are the ones where you're in a tight spot or indoors. There is one level towards the end that is entirely indoors and it's probably my favorite or second favorite level of the game.TLDR: Guns feel great, gibbing is fantastic, movement is fun and the atmosphere is spot on. I put 20 hours into the demo and I'm probably gonna put at least a hundred into Chapter One alone. Super stoked to see where Chapter Two will take us!Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: What a game. I caught wind of the title via Civvie11 and Skillup in some of their demo roundup videos. I played the demo about 5 times before the drop of the main game. With one playthrough complete I'll go ahead and drop my recommendation. For a price tag of 9.99USD and a single playthrough runtime of 4 hours for myself (on Hard with most secrets found in each level. About half all secrets found) it's a pretty solid bundle of fun. If you are intimate with shooters then I would recommend Hard as the difficulty to attempt your first playthrough on. If you are intimate with retro shooters specifically then perhaps a bump up might help. I don't play many and only found myself dying a few times over the entire 4 hours. Though I was on the brink a good handful of times after a fight. With that out of the way I'll try to simplify the into of my biggest points into a more readable pro's and con's moving forward.PROS-Wonderful level design. Secrets galore and some must be pretty well hidden since I scanned over things pretty hard. The flow and chance to tackle a lot of encounters in at least a couple different ways was welcome too. -Retro Look. Despite the simple looking style the game has it rocks it super well. A great balance of old school looks with more modern touches like the lighting really gives the game a great feel and ambiance. It also maintains fairly good clarity in hectic combat. Though the shields later enemies get can hide their robe color and make it harder to identify them until they let you know what kind of weapon they have via using it on you.-Tight gameplay. Headshots and they feel good. The game doesn't reward you with health or anything crazy for them but the pleasure of popping cultists grapes and how much more effective it is takes care of that for you. You naturally learn very quickly how much easier encounters can go by making it a focus to land shots accurately. The armament of weapons feel great, sound good, and maintain the style the game is after.CONS-Ledges seem...Rounded? This one  is a bit hard to explain. Overall the movement is great for about 95% of the stuff you are doing. However there's a few times you are having to balance on small ledges or are trying to make a difficult jump for a secret you can see and it just feels..Off. When you feel like you should be just on the edge of what is under you it can be easy to just sort of slide off until you are completely off and fall. It's a strange bit of wonkyness but of my four hours this maybe only accounted for 10 minutes or so of playtime total between 3-4 different situations. -You'll have to wait for more. This isn't really any fault of the Dev. (One? Crazy, I know.) Despite the wonderful package this game is I just can't wait until I get to dive into the next chapter. I thought the wait for a few months after the demo was hard.... Time for playthrough #2Overall 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: DUSK meets BLOOD in this indie extravaganza.What would have other-wise been an impressive project for a small team, and which feels expertly crafted by multiple people firing on all cylinders, seems to be 99% the work of a single guy. That alone is worthy of praise and commendation. But aside from the impressive level of craftsmanship we have here, the game itself is tight, well-thought-out (for the most part), and has some decidedly poignant features that keep it from being just another run-of-the-mill retro shooter.The gameplay plays like a mix between BLOOD and DUSK as I stated, with a slide feature when running and crouching simultaneously. This allows the wide open parts to actually feel a lot smaller than they look, which is both good and bad, since you can spam the slide as much as you want, but more than that, it allows you to easily dodge thrown objects and gunfire if you time it right. This becomes the bread-and-butter way of dealing with long-range enemies towards the last quarter of the game, where rifle ammunition is low and valuable, as you can slide around to get up close with the shotgun. A lot of the secrets are exceptionally well hidden, though I did get most of them on a few levels, some levels I didn't get any, although from what I experienced, I seemed to have stumbled upon secrets I didn't even know were secrets. I will also say, I found the weapon progression system in need of a few tweaks. The Incinerator, Grenade Launcher, and FG-42 weren't acquired till the last third of the game, and you basically get them almost all at once. Having the grenade launcher earlier in the game would have been more helpful, especially during the zombie horde sections, and would have been a much better way to introduce it than the Sten, which you could have acquired earlier since it uses the same ammo as the pistol and isn't too much of an upgrade.The level design overall is enjoyable. There is a lot of thought put into the atmosphere and dressings of each level, making many of them stand out, especially the Shipyard which was uniquely fun, swimming round the docks, going from ship to ship. The Asylum was also exceptionally memorable with its spooky atmosphere and tight quarters. The rest of the levels were all well done too, and I cannot think of one that I did not enjoy playing through. It shifts from sprawling levels that are wide and open, to close-knit tunnels and corridors, to catwalks and slight platforming segments. It varies its approach in just the right way that you like to see, keeping you entertained in your progression almost as much as it entertains you with its gameplay. A few of the pop culture nods such as the shed with the "DEAD OPEN INSIDE DONT" were neat little easter eggs that gave me a chuckle. The bosses, of which there are 3 minibosses, I believe, which then become standard enemies afterwards, with one final boss, all feel properly introduced and adequately intimidating the first time around. The chainsaw miniboss had a particularly unnerving introduction and had me feeling anxious all the way up until finally meeting him. The final boss himself wasn't too much of a problem, I only died once on Hard difficulty fighting him, as he is very easy to exploit with the Incinerator.The music accompanying you is quite exceptional and he must have some sort of background in musical education, or as a side hobby since the crafting of moods and the progression of various instrumentation into crescendos and lulls is expertly done. It can go from creating a sense of dread to instilling a thrilling sense of adrenaline as the music becomes more frenetic and action-focused. Which is something this game does extraordinarily well too, from its art design, to its level design, to its music and gameplay, it manages to switch from being fast paced and action-heavy to slower paced and more atmospheric quickly, and almost effortlessly.This is definitely a game that was crafted by someone who knew exactly what they wanted to make, how they wanted to make it, and the execution illustrates all of that.Extremely RecommendedHigh

_childDocuments_.review: A really well made, and well realised old school shooter. The levels aren't too big, but they're dense and challenging, with increasingly tough combat scenarios and tonnes of secrets to find in the story mode. The levels and the game overall doesn't overstay its welcome, but there is a survival horde mode if you're wanting more. You could also go for the higher difficulty modes in the story as well, of course (normal is challenging enough for me).The graphics and art style is creepy, and will make you jump especially early on when you're less familiar with the game. The tougher mini-boss enemies in particular will put you on edge when they relentlessly charge you down and can kill you in only a few hits.The gunplay is exceptionally tight, and each gun from the starting pistol and hatchet to the late game weapons is completely unique from every other weapon, with them all having a purpose (while still being able to be used exclusively, if you just wanted to use a pistol or shotgun).If you're craving an older style of shooter, absolutely buy this one!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to take a bite out of this game like its a giant cartoon haunch of meat.The presentation is amazing, it looks good, it feels good, it plays good. Visually, it has a pleasing palette, and a great artstyle, while keeping everything readable. The areas have a continuity and clear progression to them that I like a lot, and I think it’s really neat that you get to return to the area shown in the main menu and opening cutscene.Levels are pretty long, but you can save and come back at any point without issue. There's a mix between more open areas and tighter corridors, and sometimes multiple routes you can take. Exploration is rewarding, there's plenty of secrets, and you'll never be short on ammo as long as you don't rush through everything. When going at my own pace and trying to be mostly thorough I found about half of the secrets.You can approach combat in a more methodical way, or much faster if you know what you're doing. Either way, you can't play like an idiot and expect to get away with it for long. Situational awareness is vital. Take stock of your enemies, use what’s available to you, and aim for the head. Headshots in this game are some of the meatiest, most gratifying ones out there. It's got some fun movement tech as well, but I think it’s better to get the hang of things first before looking that up.The weapons are all really fun and satisfying to use. They're upgradeable, and you'll find the weapon parts necessary for that in the normal environment and secrets. None of the weapons become obsolete later on, your pistol will be as reliable a tool as everything else, no need for it to waste inventory space like some other games. The hatchet in particular is one of my favorite melee options in an fps, not only because it can be thrown (and you can hold 10 at a time), but because you can use it to headshot close enemies if you charge a strike and aim just a bit up. This is a beautiful thing and I’m angry that more games don’t do things like this. I'm a hatchet fan until the day I die.Sometimes the enemy AI can be a bit dumb, especially around doors. Also, molotovs can feel like they can end fights too easily, but they do come with the very real risk of setting your own self on fire if you aren't careful and/or you’re in a tight space, so I wouldn’t call it a free win by any means.The threat from the two bossfights mainly comes from normal enemies spawning in the arena, while you try to manage both them and the bosses themselves. I don't think they're done poorly, but mechanics wise they don't stand out much from the rest of the fps genre. They do have good buildup leading from the preceding levels, and fun presentation.None of the negatives are significant enough to really hamper my experience, and the positives come together in a way that makes this an incredibly solid game. One of the best of the recent retro fps revival, in my opinion. There's a demo to try if you're on the fence, it's what pushed me over the edge to buy it. I got about 3 ½ hours on my first playthrough, and 14 after spending time in the endless mode and achievement hunting. Considering the quality of the game, I think it's well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: For $9.99 Cultic has been one of the best values and overall gaming experiences I've had this year. We've seen some pretty great games like the new God of War, but something about Jason Smith's solo project lovingly recreating the best parts of a 1990s FPS minus all the bad parts was just amazing. I don't think I have the words to describe how much I enjoyed this game.I first heard of Cultic watching a review from youtuber Civvie 11 and while this isn't the kind of game I normally played the free demo had me hooked. It really is impressive how well the game flows. I thought enemies would be hard to spot with the retro graphics, but I found it pretty easy to spot the cultists at a distance. The guns feels impactful and the weapons feel like they're doing damage.Spent just shy of 6 hours clearing this game on standard difficulty. I'm sure veterans of these games will do it faster. It is worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not just one of the best retro shooters. It's one of the best games i've ever played in recent times.wow oh wow i was pleasantly suprised how great of a game this turned out to be, when i initially bought it and played it. At first glance it seemed like your typical 90's shooter that wanted to capture the nostalgia feel of that era but boy was i wrong, it does way more than it's aesthetic style, the game is a well rounded fps game in general, the gunplay is amazing, enemies are fun to fight and the variety is well done to keep the game fresh, all the weapons feel punchy and powerful, there isn't one single gun in the game that feels useless or gets redundant later on unlike most fps games, even the hatchet axe is useful for it's one shot charged meele attack against the basic common enemies. The level design is unique and atmospheric, the general pacing of the game never drags on or gets stale which contributes the game's replayability, i've had the game for a week and i've already completed it 5 times, which is rare for me to do because i usually replay a game for once or twice and than move on to the next one.Overall this is easily one of the best fps games i've played, do me a favour, stop reading the reviews and get this game asap, no excuses not to get it with it's awfully generous cheap price, you get more enjoyment out of this game than a modern day triple-AAA-budget slop

_childDocuments_.review: Properly enjoyed this thanks to fast and fluid movement, satisfying gunplay (with great slow-mo gore explosions), and an unexpected amount of flexibility and creativity when you add in weapon modifications and a decent amount of environmental interaction. The presentation is doubly impressive as it's both "authentic" but still modernised without breaking the illusion.Running battles against mobs of cultists and mutants are the obvious highlight but there are also a ton of secrets to find, impactful weapon upgrades, and even a few super-effective creepy sequences. If you're looking for narrative context, it's more fleshed out than you might expect in the genre with a ton of notes and environmental storytelling elements. My negatives would be the lack of any unique gameplay mechanics (it's more a super polished version of what's come before), two major boss battles that feel simplistic and underwhelming, and perhaps the need for a little more colour.I put my thoughts together more comprehensively in a written and video review:

_childDocuments_.review: One solo developer has created one of the best first-person shooters ever made.Whether screwing around and enjoying the atmosphere and acrobatic flow of combat, playing with the many fun toys in your arsenal at a low difficulty, or sprinting, leaping and crawling from desperate moment to moment at the highest difficulty, 'Extreme', in which each enemy is a potentially lethal threat... It simply has a sense of flow and good balance and sheer *fun* I haven't seen achieved so well since FEAR, while evoking rich atmosphere, tension and excitement with low-detail but beautifully lit environments as well as anything has since the original Unreal.Cultic feels as much a Survival Horror as Resident Evil 1 and as much of a horror adventure as Resident Evil 4.The levels are varied in mood and core gameplay while retaining a perfectly consistent aesthetic and atmosphere throughout, all the more remarkable for choosing a bizarre fusion of true 3d gaming, 2.5d style sprites, and voxel-sculpted environmental props. The balance of action and horror, tension and catharsis was excellent. The freedom granted by the level design to sneak, ambush, lure enemies, rain down explosives from afar, leap in for melee, and mix up all of the above as you struggle through each battle was so much fun!If I were to criticise any quality of the game it would be the use of low-detail sprites for the enemies, with a weak rotation and a lack of rotated views - hitting enemies, reading the damage you're achieving, and recognising their animations for imminent attack can be slightly unclear for someone used to the richer sprite animations of Project Brutality/Brutal Doom, or for someone not used to sprite-based enemies in 3D/2.5d shooters at all.This is all I can find, the only criticism I can muster. The game was smooth, 99% bug-free, completely stable. It didn't annoy me, ever - it didn't bore me, ever. I was eager to go back each day for a few levels at a time until I finished it, something I experience a few times in a decade due to mental health struggles that make concentration and commitment to a game, book or series exceptionally difficult.You should buy this at a high price. Don't wait for a sale, get it now.

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is an old school FPS that can easily be mistaken for a 1997 release, unlike many "boomer shooters", a term which has been used way too liberally recently in my opinion, the game echoes many aspects that made the FPS classics stick out in our memory. At its core, it is a traditional FPS game, you start out with a simple melee weapon and progress to pick up an expanding arsenal that checks every box, trusty shotgun, explosives launcher, sniper rifle, automatic gun with high rate of fire etc. The level progression is linear, just like in the classics of the genre, you move through levels, picking up  keys and learning about the story through optional journals. The enemies also vary from simple grunts, to high HP powerhouses, as well as ones with magical abilities and long range attacks. Every staple of the classic FPS is here, as if someone was checking off a list.What makes Cultic work so well, as opposed to many contemporaries, is the atmosphere. From the very first moment in the game, you are dropped into a world of horror, the game maintains a grimy, dirty and dark tone throughout the entire playthrough. The setting is very similar to one of my favorites classic shooters, Blood, which was the main reason I picked it up. The influences of Blood are very clear, cultists, darkness, dynamite...If I had to pick a single developer to make an actual sequel to Blood, the developer of Cultic would be my first choice. The only negatives I can report is that the game is pretty short and I am not a fan of the upgrade mechanic, although it is well done and not absolutely necessary for progression, I've barely used it in my playthrough. If you are a fan of classics like Blood, Heretic, etc, I would highly advise picking Cultic up at it's extremely modest $9.99 price tag. You're going to have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Took a while to get into it, but it was definitely worth persevering past the first couple levels. I love all of the weapons, especially the lever gun, and there are a lot of unique enemy designs too. Think Blood mixed with Quake and Resident Evil 4. My biggest complaints are the ugly voxels and the repetitive visuals, but it's still a very good game and one of the best solo projects on steam in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: My potential issue with retro FPS games is that I hate to be lost with no direction, searching for color-coded keys just on the edge of falling asleep out of boredom. Hey, I was around when these types of games were new, so I'm getting older. Cultic is retro in the best types of ways, and modern in the best, too. I haven't been wandering around, bored to tears, about to quit. The levels aren't entirely linear, but they're like wide-linear, and it does push you toward a logical conclusion to each level. Tight action, interesting lore you find in each level, and the music is actually REALLY good in a synthwave, Carpenter-esque way! As a dude who knows I'm broken and doesn't really care much for music in anything, really, I love this music. Highly recommending this game! And if you're older, less-skilled, or just have a low tolerance for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and want to enjoy a game, this game doesn't have to be ultra-hard. I'm just vibin', killin' cultists and wandering horrors. It's a good time, and that's the highest praise I can ever give.

_childDocuments_.review: Legitimately one of the best shooters I've had the pleasure of playing.Fantastic atmosphere, well designed levels with themes that make them stand out from each other, great enemy designs that make them easy to quickly read while still being a danger to the player, and a pretty good story. The weapons are the best part of the game for me. All of them are punchy, incredibly satisfying to use, have great sound and visual design and maintain relevancy through the entire campaign. Both of the shotguns in the game are some of the most satisfying I've ever used, with the double barrel rivalling even Blood's sawn-off in terms of the cultist carnage it brings. Buy this game. It worth all your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I was utterly captivated by CULTIC, a retro-inspired horror-themed FPS that shines brightly in the recent resurgence of the genre. Drawing inspiration from classic games like RE4 and DOOM '93, as well as other shooters of that era, CULTIC may not be as lengthy or complex as a modern full-budget title, but it throws its punches where it matters.The exceptional sound design truly elevates the experience. Each weapon boasts a distinct sound, and the auditory feedback from headshots, exploding cultists, and environmental events masterfully informs the player without the need for visual cues. The mechanical clatter of weapons and the visceral, guttural sounds of enemies disintegrating into gibs make the entire experience intensel satisfying.CULTIC's level design is superb and engaging, offering a consistent variety of level types that create unique arenas for gunplay. The atmospheric, sprawling environments encourage exploration, while the smaller, more compact areas are intricately detailed and immersive. Although the sprite-based visuals can occasionally make it difficult to spot distant enemies, this minor issue doesn't detract from the overall quality. Each level is distinct and inventive while maintaining the game's cohesive theme.The movement mechanics are swift yet versatile, allowing for fast-paced action or more strategic, measured gameplay.Your arsenal functions as a versatile toolbox, with specific weapons and equipment tailored for different situations. The real fun is in adapting your tactics and weapon choice to each encounter. I dont want to spoil any specific details, but I will say that CULTIC offers a unique and interesting loadout.The story is simple yet intriguing. A game like this doesnt need a good story but its a pleasant surprise to find one. I'm not typically one to read every note and letter in games, but CULTIC held my attention with its environmental storytelling and supplementary notes. I couldnt wait to discover every bit of exposition and world-building the game had to offer.The visuals pay homage to the sprite era of FPS games while incorporating modern, stylized flair that sets CULTIC apart from the rest.It may seem odd to say, but CULTIC doesn't necessarily break new ground in gameplay. Instead, it builds upon a tried-and-true formula, what it takes from its inspirations it executes flawlessly. I was surprised when the credits rolled and I learned that this game was made by one guy. You can tell that this is a passion project with a ton of talent behind it and I can't wait for the next chapter.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I've really been enjoying this title. There are lot of positives here to go through so let's get started. The developer has done a great job of catching nostalgia. This doesn't only feel like playing blood or other old school boomer shooters. it really captures the ambience of 90s horror movies as well. That being said it's just innovative enough to still feel like a boomer shooter without being stale. There are a lot of ways to approach a situation (within the confines of kill ♥♥♥♥ before ♥♥♥♥ kills you) from throwing axes and molotovs, kicking enemies out the way to run and gunning things.The controls are just innovative enough to feel fresh without taking away from running around killing enemies. You load up axe throws, throw grenades, slide on the floor and headshots deals extra damage. All departures from the original formula this game was based on. I enjoy the limited ammo requiring you to at least occasionally approach situations out of your comfort zone, which brings me to my next point.There aren't that many weapons, but it feels good. Each weapon has it's own ammo and they all fill a niche you want from this sort of game. I particularly love the shotgun "straight out of doom(2)", with the option of firing one barrel at a time. The enemies again, not that varied and not that many of them, but they all fill a role, there is one design in particular that I love but I don't want to give any spoilersI don't really have any negatives to say about this game it does what it says on the tin but I have a few 'neutral' points. While the level design really has some highlights, there a few areas that leave a few things to be desired, which leads me to my next point. In theory I like the idea of upgrading weapons but I've never been a completionist. It's nice stumbling on secrets but because upgrade parts are limited I feel like I'm gimping my run if I miss any. I recently discovered a secret that gives you a new gun but it was tedious preforming the action to acquire it, I worked it out many minutes before I actually unlocked it.With all that out the way I give this game a very solid 9/10. I'm basing my rating on price point, what's offered on the store page and what's delivered in the product. If you're not into old school shooters, obviously this game wouldn't be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished the game a few minutes ago and what I can say is that this game honestly and literally brought tears to my eyes - in the good way. I really hope the devs are reading this... not many games manage to have this effect. Please make more!I really don't know how to describe this game... It is a true mid to late 90s shooter... 30 years later. That's something I've been waiting for far too long. The game isn't too long, unfortunately, but maybe that's for the best, not overstaying its welcome. For the length of it, however, every second felt like I'm kid again, and the gamer in me finally awoken one more time.With the look and feel of the game, its style reminds me a lot of Blood and Return to Castle Wolfenstein, the latter in part because of the weapons you use, but also because of evil cult story, the zombies, etc... Yes, it does have a story, and it even has quite a surprising amount of lore.The game ran flawlessly on Windows, and although I've had a crash under Proton in Linux, I can forgive that, because the native Linux client doesn't exist, or not yet anyway.For the fans of 90s FPS games, this game is a must have!

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly one of the spiritual successors (Besides Dusk) of one of the masterpiece-defining genre FPS of all time, namely Blood, Cultic is.... welp, spectacular? without flaw? I mean, besides the new trinity of boomer shooter (Ion fury, Dusk and Amid Evil) is, like, THE only safe purchase of modern boomer shooter... or simply FPS.... you can do. Doesn't matter what you like, this is the game. Gameplay wise, it's basically Blood (actually, this is what Blood 2 should have been) but modernized: similar story (I mean, not that much if you think about it, but the VIBE is right there), similar tones, plus a sophisticated gameplay's mechanics. Such as, some new possibility of movement, conjoined with a level and enemy design that is capable of valorising such decision in gameplay design, weapons that fits both thematically and gameplay wise. Noteworthy is even the soundtrack: every single piece is memorable, with a particular rhythm but the game KNOWS when to... drop the beat ( ;) ).... I won't ever bother writing 'Worth buying?', if you don't get the answer, you probably don't enjoy playing FPS... or videogames in general, that is. P.S. _childDocuments_.review: If you're into retro shooters of any kind, like Blood, Duke Nukem, Classic Doom or the more recent games like DUSK, Cultic fits right in with the best of them.Here's some gameplay if you wanna skip in, but the DEMO should sell you on it There are some levels that stand out as my favorites, and some that are almost too accurate to the classic games Cultic is trying to replicate (some levels are like a maze), but I never found myself fully lost which is a testament to the level design.Gameplay is solid with gun sound effects really adding some weight to the gunplay, but for me the star of the show is the OST.. this soundtrack SLAPS.Some levels have sections that adopt a sort of horror element, which was surprisingly refreshing, but most of the gameplay is just shooting dudes across the map.Overall, I recommend Cultic. I was able to beat it in 2 hours with each level averaging 10 to 20 minutes (granted I wasn't going for secrets). For $10 this game is a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, the game play is top notch, great atmosphere and plenty of scope for imaginative strategies.Graphics are really effective despite the very rough pixel style.I'm playing on easy and it is still quite challenging in places, so plenty of scope for more seasoned players.AI is a little daft at time, but that adds to the fun when they blow themselves up or do something silly.Maps are good and not frustrating on purpose, some jumping and crouching can be a little tricky, but nothing that is too annoying.  Game tells you when you need something to do something and a bit of logic works out how to get to places you cant see an obvious path to.Game also doesn't make you go around in circles for the sake of it.Highly recommended at this price and has good replay with the secrets/difficulties/achievements
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Have you played Blood (1997)? No? Then play it because CULTIC is just a Blood 2.0, everything CULTIC did was a blast of awesomeness and I deeply loved that feeling of being a kid playing Blood again, that nostalgia that went beyond a great experience.CULTIC is a retro-shooter that will test your skills and patience when it comes to deal with masses of cultists and abominations. Admittedly one of the reasons I also wanted to do this review was when I threw a dynamite bundle at a bunch of cultists and one of them ran right toward the bundle and kicked it back at me, that precious moment of "Oh F***" made me laugh so much because it was new, it was something I wasn't expecting, the AI will do some crazy things to test you, so yes you can expect some nasty stuff when it comes to the combat, either cultists throwing axes at you or opening a door and getting you off-guard (Yes, really, keep your guns loaded).The weapons feel unique and you'll learn what each one of them do at a particular case-scenario, you can blast away a group of cultists with a dynamite bundle or throw a molotov at them, fire damage works wonders against flesh. You can keep your shotgun ready to blast some enemies in half or just snipe them down at a distance with the FG-42, you can use your lever action rifle to explode some heads or use the Sten to mown down the opposition, really there is an weapon for what you need, even your pistol is useful, just don't try to take down the big ones with it only. And if you are wondering if bullets explodes dynamites sticks/bundles, yes, it does, throw a bundle near someone and then shoot it down when many more go toward you, the best "improvised landmine" you'll make.There is secrets, there is a story behind, there is an upcoming episode as well, yes this is the first episode only so be aware that the next episode will also be paid (from what I got, if I'm wrong about that then I'll edit this review). If you want a game that plays really well and give you that "old-school" feeling then CULTIC is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW FOR CHAPTER ONE (16/10/2022)SHORT REVIEWCULTIC is a first-person shooter. You play as a detective who travels to the wilderness after numerous people and an investigator go missing. The detective themselves get jumped and murdered, before waking up in a pile of bodies with renewed energy. If you ever played a Build game then you'll be right at home. Plenty of weapons, tons of enemies, locations are big and wide and the difficulty spike is smooth.LONG REVIEWSTORYIn 1963 several people have gone missing in the New Grandwell wilderness, and when an Investigator has gone missing a Detective is sent out to find out what is happening. But the moment the Detective arrives, they are ambushed by Cultists and murdered, thrown into a pile of dead bodies. Miraculously, the Detective is brought back to life and sets off to stop these cultists with renewed energy.Each level has notes and readables that provide little bits of world building information specific to each level, as well as notes left by the missing Investigator who explains what had been happening.GAMEPLAYWEAPONSCULTIC has plenty of weapons the Detective can use against the Cultists. You have the traditional Pistols, Double Barrel and Rifles along with some unique ones like the Lever-Action and Grenade Launcher to name a few. These weapons can be upgraded at Workbenches to increase certain stats and provide new features to use.ENEMIESAs the Detective moves further into the wilderness more and more enemies begin to appear. At first it'll be just Cultists wielding firearms but slowly more and more horrific, undead creatures begin to take stage. Each enemy has a unique style and a weapon to counter them.LEVEL LAYOUTOne spot that CULTIC shines (for me at least) is the level designs. The majority of levels are vast and open, with plenty of spaces to explore as well as small linear sections to help guide you on the right track.OVERALLIf you're a fan of boomer shooters and want to add some horror to your usual run-and-gun fun then I highly recommend CULTIC.

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant addition to the renaissance of oldschool shooters. The genre is going through a second youth, with talented developers going back to the games of old, and doing them again, but better. Cultic is a throwback to the gritty Build engine games, first of all Blood, but also Shadow Warrior, Redneck Rampage, and Rise of the Triad. Most of your enemies are humans, current or former: cultists in obligatory robes, undead, or some gory abominations. The locations are huge, but realistic, built to resemble actual real world places like a mining town or an abandoned hospital, peppered with secrets, and frequently giving you a lot of space for non-linear approach. The plot is minimalistic — it's the 60s, and you are a disgraced detective fighting an evil cult — but comes with a bunch of notes and letters that details to flesh out the otherwise simple story. The gunplay is fast and brutal, but leaves a room for errors — enemies won't just gun you down with perfect precision before you know what hit you, like they used to back in the day. Probably the only downside is the game's length: it's just 10 levels, each about a hour long. Can't wait to see chapter 2!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game because of the Blood vibes from it (probably my favorite old school shooter), and while it delivers that in spades it is also so much more. The shooting is great, every weapon feels powerful and punchy and all are useful in various situations. The music is great as well. Only negative thing I can say is that it sucks that we have to wait for the second chapter, but you can bet your ass I am picking it up as soon as it comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing the old Build games like Duke Nukem or Shadow Warrior. But Blood always felt like the most exciting of them all with its dark cultic themes and viciously aggressive gameplay.Cultic as a love letter to the BUILD shooters of those times is very successful. It is inspired by them, but not replicating them. The action, the atmosphere the level design is varied, visceral and offers interesting shifts from level to level.I really like it and out of the recent boomer shooters, I've enjoyed playing it the most.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through once on normal difficulty and had an absolute blast with this game.  The combat is so masterfully executed with fantastic movement options. Each weapon has a very specific use and feels great to use.  Exploring the world and seeing where a potential secret could be and then succesfully hunting it down is immensely satisfying.  Weapon sounds are chunky and satisfying and give you exactly the feedback you'd want them to in order to keep the violence moving without stopping to think too long about how things are interacting.All in all this was absolutely a fantastic piece and I'm excited to go through on harder difficulties and mess around with the unique survival mode. _childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent single player action/horror game. Although at first glance it may seem like one of those "new retro shooters" (it is to some extent, it shares some similarities with games like Blood), Cultic is actually closer to survival horror action games like Resident Evil 4 or Evil Within.Cultic has great atmosphere and level design. The weapons feel great and are very different from each other. Also, you can upgrade them using a specific item that you can find in the environments, so trying to find the secrets inside the levels is recommended, luckily their locations are not very cryptic.Unaware enemies are weaker, and although the game doesn't have an explicit stealth mecanic, you should try to make a silent approach every time you see an enemy or group of them that have not detected you yet. You can throw them axes of TNT bundles.There are different difficulty levels, and the way you play this game changes a lot between them. The gameplay that the low/medium difficulties allow is very different from the way you will have to play on the higher ones. So even though the game isn't very long, you'll definitely want to play it again to see those changes.My only complaints are the music, which is great but in my opinion it doesn't fit very well with the tone of the game, maybe a more atmospheric soundscape would work better I think.... My other complaint is the enemy AI, which is a bit inconsistent: sometimes enemies exhibit interesting behaviors like kicking TNT bundles you throw at them or successfully flanking you even in the larger and complex areas, but other times they get stuck in the level without a reason or fall off ledges even when you are not near of them...Anyway, this is just the first chapter and maybe these issues will be fixed in future episodes. This one is excelent and you should give it a change.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start by saying what this isn't - because I think people are getting the wrong idea:THIS IS NOT A SPIRITUAL SEQUEL TO BLOOD.It doesn't really play much like it despite having cultists, dynamite and enemies that can wreck you in seconds. This doesn't stop Cultic from being one of the best retro inspired FPS games currently available, but if you got into Cultic expecting a real BLOOD 2, then you might be disappointed. There is certainly Blood in its veins (heh) but there's far more to it than that.What Cultic is, is a really fun mixture of some of the best bits of the late 90s and early 2000s shooters. It combines the hallway shooting of classic Doom and Build Engine games with the expanded "open corridor" approach to combat encounters found in the first Far Cry game. Most encounters are completely open to however you want to approach them, giving the player a freedom of play style not found in many of it's old school inspired contemporaries Weapons are punchy and fun and enemies are relatively varied even if both are a little stock. It is another game with a pistol, shotgun, smg weapon set and various colours of robed cultists carrying the same. The feel of the guns and the fun to be had taking out these bad guys though more than makes up for these nitpicks, however, because nitpicks they are.I've just finished my first play through on hard and that took me about 5/6 hours without finding all the secrets. Will be looking to get that extreme difficulty play through achievement at some point soon. Would highly recommend Cultic.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal execution of the "Boomer Shooter" formula. Everything feels and plays like a labor of love, it's downright impressive this was ENTIRELY made by a single guy. The atmosphere, gameplay, fun factor and even the immersion are off the charts. All the characteristcs of a well made game come together to make this unique and unforgettable. While I recommend anyone to try it out, beware of the difficulty, as is common with this genre the game will rightfully kick your a-s-s (and even then, it's not one bit unfair, talk about balance). Do keep in mind, however, this is only chapter one. A tiny tad of controversy sparks out of chapter-based games, and while I usually am against the format, I do stand for this particular example. As mentioned before, this is the work of a single artist. Sound effects, music, sprite\model work, level design, etc. are all done by just him. Not only it shall take time, it will also cost dosh, so he deserves it. All in all 10\10 Thought this was from the guys from New Blood at first lmao
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this since the first demo, and I really have to say that it is incredible value for money. The passion that has gone into this very clear, and I definitely would like to highlight the most special achievement this game has pulled off: inspiration/homage without being stale or reductive.The game is very clearly influenced by the 90s FPS Blood (with hints of Return To Castle Wolfenstein in the weapon selection and level design), but has managed to be open with these inspirations while carving out its own identity. It is familiar without being a rip off.One of the ways in which the game achieves this is through its unique colour palette. While I was initially turned off by the strange filtering and off-putting colours, over time I grew to appreciate the strength of the design. The deep earth and rust tones, combined with the chunky (for lack of a better word) art style, made the world seem quite grim and oppressive, especially when combined with some of the more gross and sinister character designs (though there is one monster which is meant to be scary but just comes off as goofy due to its animation and behaviours).The combat is visceral and satisfying, with gory headshots and explosions occasionally causing you to go into slo-mo, which really helps you savour the moment. Objects in the world can be used as makeshift weapons and traps, which can really make you feel like an Indiana Jones-esque combat pragmatist at times.The level design is dense and full of exploration opportunities. There is linearity but there are so many rewards for finding secrets that you dont feel too confined to the main path. The highlight for me was probably the path leading to the Asylum level, as there was a good mixture between open arenas and tight encounters.Story-wise, things are pretty threadbare. There are documents scattered around the levels which provide some background lore, but I didn't find them particularly compelling. Luckily, it is not a plot-focused game, so the documents are there mainly to provide flavour as  opposed to deepening the plot.My only real critique is that the music does not match the tone of the game; the grim body horror and evil cult plot elements do not mesh with the melancholic, mournful nature of the music. I would also say that the final boss wasn't a particularly interesting fight, but some of the encounters preceding it were fantastic.Performance wise, my piece of ♥♥♥♥ laptop struggled with the higher settings, but things were fine when i turned stuff down. No real loss as it is a retro-inspired game without a huge level of graphical fidelity. I didn't seem to experience any bugs, but I suppose things could have been better optimised.Overall, I absolutely recommend this. Extremely satisfied with my day 1 purchase, and I am hyped for chapter 2.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: A modern (retro throwback) classic! This game has everything; bullet time, TNT, a kick-ass shotgun, action sliding, mother ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TNT+molotov combos. I love the art style and it's awesome the game supports ultra-wide resolutions. As for gameplay, it's not quite run and gun and there is usually more than one way to tackle an encounter. Don't be afraid to use your TNT and the environment to your advantage. If you stick to just using your weapons, you'll have a bad time. Blow ♥♥♥♥ up. Good enemy variety. Weapon feedback is good. I'm really enjoying the game so far. My only gripe is that while the music is good, sometimes it just loops too much and gets repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: The first time you see some CULTIC screenshots or videos you might think that we are talking about a game that was based in Doom or Build engine games such as Blood and Shadow Warrior, but  this game is Visually, this game is outstanding and everything from the color pallete to how the voxel-built models look gorgeous and complements the environment, the mix of 2D and 3D utilized makes CULTIC extremely unique among other FPS games out there, this thing kinda has it's own soul. We also have some beautiful spritework done for the "player model" because believe it when I say that you  in here, but the great work is also extended to the enemies and their animations and the weapons... OOOH, THE GUNS! They all sound amazing and look incredible and feel amazing to use, with each one of them having a situation they excel in so you don't be overly dependent on a single one to carry you through the game.Think that's all that we have? Oh but it isn't, because the way levels are designed make it for an incredible easy experience to go through them, find key items and where to progress, everything feels incredibly organic and in no moment I felt lost while playing CULTIC, and I even found a bunch of secrets withoug using a guide, just because all of them were hidden in places where you could simply find them through exploration, not button mashing or attacking random walls.This one is definitely on my list of favorite FPS games ever.

_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: CULTIC is excellent! It's kind of a mashup between Blood and Resident Evil 4, wrapped up in a 'retro-shooter' package. The combat is great, with weapons feeling satisfying to use and enough enemy variety to keep encounters interesting and dynamic. The level design is good, with secrets and interconnections, and the art is tasteful too; lo-fi but without feeling cheap or tacky or lacking in detail. _childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: MAJOR SPOILERS BELOWRelevant Insights to my Cultic Exp: - Played on Hard Difficulty- Did not try to find every secret but found most of them- Already have a sense for these kind of games- Used most weapons, but the STEN was used the least. Focused upgrades: Pistol, Lever Action, Double Barrel, Grenade Launcher, Sniper.- Biggest surprise: can get through most of beginning of the game with charged-up Axe melee with no problem, and also witnessing enemies kick away my TNT. That interaction was cool. Set piece setups are great, and no limitations to how far you can engage the enemies were a great breath of fresh air (and you CAN stealth things if you are able to, believe or not). Deciding whether or not to use a molotov/flamethrower/lantern vs dynamite/barrel changed up certain parts dramatically.I like this game a lot. I think the dynamics of the game play are cool, the level designs are great albeit I am not sure why spiral stairs are such a headache for me in this game, the atmosphere is awesome especially the first time boxes thrown at you in the ship at you don't know why it's happening, music is spooky and sound design is great, the interlude is awesome and I wish there was some more of that, the puzzles are interesting, etc...; In regards to the stairs, I think it's an FOV distortion problem that I have but not sure if other players have. The graphics are great and the color palette is very unique if you take it all in. I love that each level is a giant sandbox with double-backing and looping that is on purpose! Great callback for me personally to games like Quake, Duke, and Doom.It's definitely a 3D Realms game (which is good!) with the level exploration, traversal, and non-hindered use of the entire accessible environment pieces. The AI is definitely your typical AI with some of them being particularly fun to deal with whether it's the snipers laying down in some cases (although I didn't see it that much after the first official encounter with them), the Ghost Cultist throwing things at you and the panic that settles in when it starts like crushing your head or something with it's telekinetic powers, the shield cultists actually using the shield and being a nuisance, the chainsaw cultists second stage of rage, and just the overall aggressiveness of each AI works great for the levels that range from claustrophobic hallways to arena churches. I really appreciated that the monsters and undead were not part of this larger enemy spectrum - they were an opposing force to the cultists and you find them many times either at odds or separated with the cultists fortifying their locations to "defend" their selves from the undead onslaught. Nice touch. I love finding the notes and reading up on stuff. The fact I can pick up stuff to throw barrels and lanterns is great, and hands down one of THE most satisfying things was throwing an explosive barrel and timing shooting it right and watching it work. I just got a few gripes: the interlude was VERY interesting and a great intro, and sometimes I feel that level of contrast isn't met by the end of the game. The sheer "♥♥♥♥ you" of cultists pretending to be officers was so good. I am glad the creepy factor stayed throughout and wasn't just blown on the intro. Something else that bothered me is the Sten is clearly better in the enemy's hands than mine. The church hold-out fight with the Cultists and Tank was very interesting and cool, until I realized the tank wasn't a real threat as long as I had the dynamite and grenade launcher handy which is only underwhelming in retrospect. However that boss fight was DOO DOO. The only reason I had to restart a few times was because of the cultists! That boss needs to hit the gym or something... or perhaps we'll see in Part 2 what's really the big bad? That's probably where the epicenter and culmination of this goes. After all, isn't the entire fight sequence of the game getting us ready for the finale anyway? Like Rocky training for the big night.Closing: Great Game. I can't say I am used to needing to pay for a part 2 of this, but I think a part 1 with interlude on Hard Difficulty or more is where you're going to get the best experience out of this. I got 7.5 hours out of this which is longer than some other "boomer shooters" so it's still a good value. I think paying for a Part 2 is not bad especially if you want to support the efforts of 3D Realms; clearly there's a lot of love put into this game! If you're chasing times, achievements, and secrets then that's where your replay-ability is going to be along with the survival modes. I love that this feels like a voxel spiritual homage to Blood. I loved blowing things up and killing enemies in funny ways, and there's definitely a lot of Easter eggs in this game that you'll find. Yes, I did spend at least 30 minutes of my total play time scouring bathrooms to find the pissing cultist and I found him. Appropriately, I threw TNT at him.

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever wanted a sequel to Blood or a game that captures horror with the balance of a boomer shooter, then you need to get Cultic. Cultic is great as despite your arsenal and capabilities, it still feels like a horror game. You become immersed with storytelling from the map and enemy placements of the story of this world and how certain enemies are introduced they'll catch you in a surprise or for sacrifice if you're not careful. It's gunplay is great each weapon is unique despite some that may seem to overlap with the right upgrades. The difficulty is great as their reaction and damages are fair and the different types compliment each to force you to deal with certain ones before the engagement or impromptu in a surprise. The color of this game is great as it's a unique look that I can only say Blood was able to capture of a creepy color texture for a boomer shooter game. _childDocuments_.review: Its a boomer shooter made by a guy who knows exactly what makes a boomer shooter great. Cultic takes lessons from the past 20 years of shooters and perfects the recipe. Levels are not confusing, the movement and combat are very fluid, the atmosphere is very rich and immersive, the voxel environment and interactables are a contrast to the sprites so nothing blends together even though the color palate is just several different shades of brown on most maps in act 1. Cultic's story is good! Telling it through the environment with notepads left behind by another detective was a good call. I've never seen such a fun variety of weapons in a BS before either. Every weapon has its place and the upgrades available make every weapon useable. I never found myself using  just one weapon as a crutch for missions in a row. Each gun has its own clear purpose, but are also versatile enough to not need to hotswap weapons constantly. The TNT bundle with a molotov attached was an amazing twist on a throwable I havent seen before and loved it. Played and beat on hard difficulty and got the perfect balance of difficulty and progress. Hard but not too hard.Really enjoyed act 1, waiting eagerly for act 2 and the rest of the game.I hope Jasozz Games doesn't ever compromise the amazing content for money or time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is well worth your time if you like horror and boomshoots, especially if you feel that most modern games just don't give you enough explosives. At times I've had nearly 50 sticks of TNT in my pocket in this game and I've had a wonderful time using them. Maintaining a spooky atmosphere is difficult when you're carrying such a huge and effective arsenal, but Cultic somehow pulls it off: the sudden appearance of a ghost or harvester can invoke genuine panic as you frantically backpedal and fumble with your weapons. Combat is pretty deadly - just standing out in the open will get you cut to pieces quickly - but a well-placed headshot will put most foes down immediately, so there's a good balance of lethality between player and enemy. Unusually for this genre there's actually a good variety of ranges to combat, from mazelike hallways to big open areas, so weapon choice is key to success. It's fortunate, then, that your toolkit is wide, interesting, and upgradeable, with each gun suited to different situations. All of them feel great to fire too - enemies gib into bloody chunks, heads explode, burning cultists scream and run around the room, and there's a little bit of bullet time at moments of peak carnage so you can enjoy the spectacle fully. You can even hurl furniture at enemies if you get desperate! I'd advise not to forget to play through the Interlude when you finish the story: it adds a new level, a new perspective, and some new guns, and hints at what's to come. Completing the package is a fun and customizable Survival mode, so once you find all the secrets in the main game there's still plenty to keep you occupied. I was shocked to discover after playing that this was the work of a solo dev - congratulations to him for such an achievement. At only £8.50 it's a steal; I'll look forward to the next chapter.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome retro-shooter, which draws a lot of inspiration from Blood, but with a bigger focus on horror segments.The weapon arsenal mixes your run-of-the-mill double-barrel shotgun with unorthodox and much rarer things like an FG42 rifle or China Lake pump-action grenade launcher. The gunplay feels quite nice and is fairly detailed for a game of this sub-genre.This game is a steal for the price, you should definitely try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Fantastic retro FPS, worthy to sit next to The Greats. Didn't run across any bugs during my play time, smooth frame rate. Guns were punchy and found myself switching weapons for certain enemies like it was Doom Eternal. Not a requirement but doing so was more effective. Graphic/Art style really make it stand out on its own and the music matches perfectly encouraging me to keep playing. _childDocuments_.review: This game captures the best of Blood in terms of lo-fi sprites, palette, and, of course, bad-monks-with-guns thing, but has its' own unique, more Lovecraftian, and more serious, atmosphere. Author tried to make diverse types of levels, and almost succeeded (but sometimes there's still a slight feel of repetition). There are many different ways to fight, from sniping enemies at the distance, to rushing with two-barrel shotgun or throwing TNTs around the corners. Every weapon can be very deadly, and the pistol remained my go-to choice to the very end. The enemies are scary. The music is good. (If you hear it, the big fight is coming). Recommended if you liked Blood, or if you want to experience entertaining and rewarding, but not too demanding, old-school FPS combat. P.S. Lack of underwater enemies was a bit disappointing, I hope chapter II will have them.
