_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Cultic is a *phenomenal* game from one-man developer Jason Smith. Don't be fooled by its retro, OG Doom-like graphics; the gunplay here is as tight and satisfying as any modern shooter. Every aspect of Cultic succeeds: The atmosphere, the visual design, the lore, and most importantly, the gameplay. Cultic is a Doom-like in the sense that you go through the levels and shoot the enemies. The objectives generally never get more complicated than "find the locked door, find the key, go back to the locked door." Each of these steps involves getting past waves of enemies, usually robed cultists bearing everything from hatchets to machine guns, and a few more surprises that I wouldn't dream of spoiling.The guns, enemies, and environments are so tightly designed that I found myself grinning as I picked up a key and heard the grumbles of cultists flooding the room above me. I never got tired of nailing a fast headshot with the level-action rifle, using the slow motion that sometimes triggers on kills to swing my aim and pop another head, and then pull out my shotgun to blast away the enemies rounding a corner to try and surround me. 10/10. If you have ever enjoyed a shooter, you owe it to yourself to play Cultic.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great homage to Blood with it's own original flair, but it has some problems. First off, the game struggles to maintain 60 FPS at 2560x1440 even with shadows turned down to minimum on my i9 3080, but your mileage may vary and I'm not gonna hold that against the game. My main complaints are the sounds, which have been bitcrushed to match the voxel and pixel aesthetics. While it may seem novel at first, the bitcrushing gets old VERY fast, and makes guns and such sound way less impactful. It also ruins a lot of the music, as it cuts a lot of the bass out of these droning ambient tracks that could otherwise be very good. I just don't understand the decision to make the sounds so crispy. Blood and other Build Engine games had low-res audio, sure- but it all sounded clean and had a great range. Caleb's voice was deep, the shotgun felt heavy to fire, and the cultist screams were clear and crisp. Other than my gripes with the audio, the game is great. While it may appear as "Blood 2", Cultic has its own unique gameplay with a bit slower, slightly stiffer movement when compared to Blood, but a greater focus on accurate gunplay with reloads and headshots unify the movement and level design and it all comes together perfectly. All I could ask for in the gameplay department. The lever action rifle is especially great, and probably the best feeling and functioning repeater I've used in an FPS. Here's hoping we get voice acting for the protagonist eventually. It would be cool to have an actual character to stand alongside Caleb and the likes.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best boomer shooters I have seen in ages. Enemies are obliterated by the bite of your bullets, and heads roll upon the taste of your blade. This game gives you a lot of room to approach enemies and kill them in your own ways, and I like the kinds of games that do that. The ones that allow you to be creative.Excellent with a capital E.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I will add my voice to the choir on this one. For a single person to have created this is an accomplishment in and of itself let alone that it is such a fun game. It is a breath of fresh air in an age where everything relies on gimmicks and social politics for there to be such a raw and unabashed commitment to the core of old-school gameplay. There are so many little flourishes and touches that add to the atmosphere of this game and somehow despite being fairly simple the combat is positively gripping I think largely because you feel as though you have an agency in the world. When you kill someone they are most unequivocably dead. That is obvious due to the fountains of blood and the excess of core which of course is just magnificent and long missed in games these days. Killing in modern video games is given such emotional gravitas that we forget that there was once a time when you could blow imps into jibs and giggle like a mad fool doing it. This brings that back in spades. It is Blood on steroids.Of course the AI is a little weak. Enemies get stuck on things etc. but that's not what this game is about anyway. This game is about shooting endless hordes of cultists and having fun doing it and boy did I. Highly recommended. Can't wait for chapter 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic - Half the game for half the priceLook at that: an indie Blood inspired FPS which takes inspiration from every 2.5D era shooters! We haven't seen that before, have we?I'll be honest - Blood is one of my all time favourites. Duke Nukem is mindless; just run and shoot. There is nothing else to it. By episode 2 you will see everything the game has to offer. The most fun I can have with it is by breaking level progression with the jetpack. With modern extravaganza of action games we have today, Duke simply doesn't hold up. Hell, most people who know the character haven't even played the game. Over the top character and good voice actor is what keeps the game from falling into the depths of obscurity… And accessibility for normalfags; Blood does everything Duke tried to better despite not having nearly as much fame and I'm still mad about that.***Rant of a mad man about BloodAs mentioned above, main problem of 2.5D shooters is their simplicity. This's a problem for Shadow Warrior, Douk, even Doom. Blood managed to avoid what will be longstanding problem of mindless shooting with its punishing gameplay: sticking to cover rather than strafing is imperative to not get shredded; using dynamite to quickly kill a group of cultists; checking every corner assuming there is an enemy behind(because there is). To stay alive, player needs to kill enemies quickly; to kill quickly, player needs to use the most appropriate weapon for the situation. Survival through the pure effectiveness is the concept that I wish were utilized more in videogames. The only modern game having that, which I can name from top of my head, is Ultrakill.This's awesome, right? A game with great atmosphere, a good charismatic protagonist, which wasn't written by someone with the sense of humour of 14 years old, a handful of dark jokes and references, and gameplay, that rewards both player's abilities and strategic thinking - the golden nugget waiting to be discovered; ideal time for Blood appreciators to receive a fan created spiritual successor they have been waiting for for 24 years…too bad :)***Sweet little liesDeveloper doesn't explicitly call Cultic Blood's spiritual successor, even if main inspiration with middle 20th century United States setting and a cult as a main antagonist is clear; what truly baffles me are players that claim Cultic to be it. There is no specific game that Cultic can be a spiritual successor of, rather like the majority of modern retro shooters, it's a compilation of existing ideas glued together. Overall gameplay is similar to Ion Fury with its pseudo 2.5D look and fast paced gameplay, prioritizing fast movement over tactics. Enemies are inspired by Blood's and Dusk's rosters. Mandatory Stunt Move™, because Ultrakill did it, and now every other game should have at least one.Cultic is a good game like any modern sedan is a good car. It won't give you troubles, it's nice to drive and is convenient if you have a family, but every time you stop at traffic light, you share the road with similar looking sedans with no personality. You have seen this retro shooter before. No new ideas to be seen. Why fix what's not broken? Audience is fine with how the matter is now.All bullets are projectiles that can be dodged by strafing, encouraging frantic behaviour rather than punishing it. On top of that the game showers the player in healing items. Every enemy encounter can be entered with full health; there is so much health lying around, on top of the 15HP pickups being dropped by every other foe.On the bright side, atmosphere and level design are good. These are what developer made the best. Levels aren't overly complicated, there are memorable moments now and then, and secret hunting to be done if that's your thing. This makes the fact even more clear: - developer doesn't know what made Blood so special beyond its appearance.To sum everything up: enjoyable game, but too casual. Game will cost you 10 quid and Chapter 1 with 10 maps will take you 3-5 hours to complete… Also Chapter 2 will be sold as DLC for 10 more pounds some day. What retro shooter this will be without a “Coming soon” label?

_childDocuments_.review: My first review went over Steam's anemic character limit, so I had to rewrite it to condense my points.This game is absolutely baller, everything about it is punching way above its weight, especially for a solo dev project. If you are even a little bit interested in this game, stop reading reviews and just play it! Huge props to 3D Realms for funding this absolutely insane man. I'll put everything in bullet points because Steam's text limit is really stingy.1. Movement.The building blocks of any good shooter, the movement in this game feels fantastic. It's hard to describe in detail, but it's super fluid, and the jumping has a sort of bouncy/spongey feeling that's just hard to put into words. It feels great, man. There are a lot of fun little tricks you can do to bypass sections of levels, bruteforce your way into secrets that were intended to be accessed another way, and just go really bloody fast. 2. Gunplay/WeaponsGunplay feels great. The handgun is awesome out of the box, has a very chunky, metallic, authoritative sound. The lever-action is damn near perfection, sounds excellent, hits like a truck, served as my workhorse in the later stages of the game, popping heads with ease. I didn't "get" the shotgun at first, you do have to be really in the enemy's face, but you can upgrade it and it becomes a powerhouse. Getting the extended choke (improved pellet spread) makes it feel like a totally different weapon in the best way possible. SMG is pretty good, standard boomer shooter machine gun. Sounds good, hits pretty hard, has enough ammo to clear more than one room without reloading. Only complaint here is that the game can sometimes be a little too generous with ammo, especially in the latter half of the game, SPOILER: 3. Enemies.Enemies are good. Their AI could stand to be touched up in any followups but the level design does a lot of the heavy lifting in that regard, which I'll get into next. Variety is excellent, lots of different enemy types to deal with, many of which are genuinely frightening the first time you encounter them. There are also some reskins thrown in during some sections to spice things up on top of the already wide rogues gallery. Everything is balanced and feels fun to fight, just perfection. 4. Environment and level design.Level design is top notch. Everywhere you go feels like it could be a real place, every arena you fight in feels meticulously planned out. You feel like you're genuinely fighting through ambushes and patrols that real people would set up. They're cleverly laid out so that most of the time, you can get eyes on a few of the threats, but never all of them. Sometimes the game will pull the rug out from under you and drop you into an ambush. The game likes to  play tricks on you like spawning a closed container by a locked exit that you have to walk past to find the switch that opens it, but when you come back, there are shotgunners waiting for you in the now very open container, all while you're getting pressured from an enemy up on a hill.  The levels have an atmosphere so thick you could cut it with an axe. There were a lot of levels that made me un-glue my finger from the sprint key just so I could slow down and absorb the ambience, or because I was genuinely uneasy. It goes from shooter to survival horror seamlessly, then transitions back like it's nothing. I would genuinely adore seeing a survival horror title come from this developer, especially if it had guns and melee that felt as satisfying as these.You also have a lot of fun things to interact with in the environment. The secrets are super intuitively placed, and I was able to find a majority of them just by being vigilant and poking around. As far as I can tell there's nothing super abstract or frustrating to find, they're all perfectly placed, give you a fair reward for the effort put in to finding them, and really spice up the game's already superb levels. You can pick up lanterns and use them as bootleg molotov cocktails, which is especially useful before you get your hands on a real one, you can pick up objects and use them as shields or throw them at enemies, you get lots of fun little notes and blurbs to read when interacting with some objects. You can pick up shields from enemies you kill that hold them, so long as you don't smash it, which restricts use of 2-handed weapons and your alt-fire, but lets you tank bullets so that you can get your bearings and get to cover if need be, or just allow you to push through some sections where you're getting shot at from afar unscathed.5. StoryStory's good, not much to say since there isn't a ton and it's not completed. The notes I did find were well written and engaging, feel pretty authentic, and I did get invested in the story of one unnamed reporter you find the field journals of laying around. Conceptually, the setting, the way the shield cultists look and behave, and some of the locations make me think that the story and setting took some inspiration from Resident Evil 4, but it definitely took a lot of inspiration from BLOOD.. It's tough to really rank this one without the full picture from the potential following chapters, but so far I really dig it. I want to know more, and that's rare for a shooter to pull off!6. DifficultyI don't know what changes between difficulty levels, honestly. I went in on Very Hard, and boy howdy does this game hold up its end of the bargain. I spent the 60% of the game constantly sitting at 25 HP (the HP you regen to automatically when you get knocked below it). Once you get the hang of the weapons, enemy timings, movement, and how the game expects you to use tools like dynamite, it gets a lot easier, but it was kinda rough for me at the start. At the beginning of one level I loaded a save probably 20 times or more. If you're not super well versed in boomer shooters that don't mind shafting you, I'd say go for Hard or Normal difficulties, I'm just a masochist and force myself to play on hard difficulties.Overall, I'd say the game is hard but plenty fair. Never at any point did I feel like I was thrown into an impossible or excessively difficult situation, even at 25HP it was just harder but doable. I imagine on lower difficulty settings it's way more forgiving. In general, the cultists don't mess around.7. Misc/closing thoughts.Game runs great for me. Never once had a technical hitch or any kind of stuttering. I hear that some people have issues with native fullscreen not running well on 4k monitors, though I wouldn't know as I don't have one. As I said, my only 3 nitpicks are that ammo drops are a little too generous at times, though it seems most of the challenge comes from the encounters rather than the need to conserve ammo. Sometimes enemies can blend in with the background, and the pixelated artstyle, while very charming and I wouldn't dream of changing it, can facilitate that. Maybe some kind of slight outline shine to make them stand out and make it a little more readable could help, but honestly I don't think anything necessarily needs to change. Viewing enemies from above can be problematic since everything is 2D sprites, but you'll never run into a situation where you just can't see them, only where it's a little hard to hit them because of the angle you're looking at the enemy from. Last nitpick is that a couple sections are confusing, or don't really make it clear what the game wants you to do to progress. This was a very small minority of my playtime, so I don't think it's really worth docking points for.9/10, awesome game

_childDocuments_.review: This is a true tour-de-force of the new Boomer-Shooter subgenre. I was not expecting to get this level of quality for what I paid.PROS:Engaging gameplay! The guns feel great, the movement speed and controls are just right, and I found it very difficult to not know where I was supposed to go apart from getting stuck for a while in a couple of spots. You can also choose your own playstyle just thru how you engage in combat. You can pick off from afar or barge right in, and the game will not strongly suggest one or the other to you; In fact it seems to accomodate both. Enemies are fairly dumb (which can be forgiven for zombie-type enemies I guess), but not so dumb that it's not a challenge. Excellent sound design!! The game has a very unique collection of SFX that have just the right amount of bitcrushing on them to give them that beloved "crunchy" tone. The gun SFX are especially outstanding in my opinion, they all have just the right amount of weight and it adds a lot to the experience.No ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cutscenes!! If I want a movie, I'll go watch one. I'm always chuffed when a developer knows you don't need cutscenes in this kind of FPS. The story is kept nicely out of the way via notes you pick up a la Resident Evil 4, one of two influences this game wears on its sleeve (the other being Blood, as Civvie before me has pointed out).Not unlike DUSK, you can set the graphics to whatever era's style you're into, with plenty of interchangeable retro or modern options in the video settings. If you want just a tad spiky-looking, you can do that. If you want it to look full-on 1996 VGA quality, you can do that too (you sick bastard).CONS:Fairly short experience, though part 2 is in the works (can't wait!)Harder difficulties are devastatingly BRUTAL in this game. But maybe you're into that...The graphics are a bit overly mottled-brown, which isn't something I miss about shooters from the eras this game takes influence from, and I think it could've been left in the past. Really struggling to come up with any more!! Maybe a bit more enemy variety would have been nice.Other than that, I can't think of the last time I was this satisfied by a game I bought. Bigass thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: A sincere and heartfelt love letter to Blood. Doesn't play exactly like other Build games as there a few extra mechanics thrown in, but I've found these features to be pretty enjoyable and well polished, and they don't alter the overall dynamic of the game. Like Blood, this is very much a 'hard' boomer-shooter; the enemies aren't carrying nerf-guns, don't have minivan-size hit-boxes, and will ruin your day very quickly if you don't proceed with caution or are reckless in your engagements. Better variety of enemies than I was expecting. Fantastic level designs, beats the snot out of most AAA shooters in that regard. Special commendation for the art and aesthetic choices made; I understand the rough textures and coarse palette aren't everyone's cup of tea, but to me it all fit the game perfectly. The gritty, slightly posterized visuals make it feel like you're hopping right into the world of a pulp horror comic book, precisely reflecting the setting/tone the game is going for. Pretty amazing it was mostly done by one guy. I agree it's on the short side (roughly 10hrs), relative to other shooters on the market, but the exceptional quality more than makes up for this. Will happily throw money at the screen for follow up episodes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best damn games I've ever played. I'm actually not that into pure FPS games, for the most part but, this game really does it for me. I love the weapons, especially the feel of them. Between the sound, the feedback, the visuals and the use, the guns are some of the best done in any game I've played. Very little is as satisfying as blowing off cultist heads with the double barrel. Speaking of cultists, they make fantastic enemies. Each of them is different, posing a different kind of threat that keeps you on your toes. You don't get overwhelmed by the many types either. They're introduced incrementally, giving you just enough time to get used to the ones presented before another joins the menagerie. Each type is fun and interesting and provides a decent challenge on their own. The level design is just as excellent. They're sprawling affairs that wind and loop back on themselves at times, but never so much that you can't get a handle on the layouts. They're also interesting, aesthetically. They look great, feel great (not to mention menacing and atmospheric) and each are memorable for their own reasons. The hidden secrets in each level are damn satisfying to find too. Some are fairly obvious and others are much more challenging to find. I, most certainly, have not found all. I spent time in each level hunting them down but, those secrets are tucked away nicely. It'll be fun to go through and search again. The story is told largely by notes you find and environmental storytelling. Really nice stuff. It doesn't shove exposition down your throat. It's just around for you to see, if you pay attention. I really can't get over how damn good this game is. As far as replayability goes. It has it. No secret endings, different choices, or rpg elements. Nothing like that. It's just so damn fun you'll want to do it again. Now that's replayability. Get this game. You will not regret it. _childDocuments_.review: Move around fast, shoot cultists in the face. This is a fine example of first person shooting done right.PROS:-All the weapons are satisfying to use and don't become obsolete -Moving around feels good, and you can reach high speeds by air kicking-"Bullet time" slow down is very fun and happens just often enough-Large variety of weapons to use and enemies to fight-Enemies can die in different ways, burning, headshots ect.-Secrets make sense and have indicators on where they are-Pays homage to Blood but still has its own identity and style-Chapter One has a pretty good number of maps. Took me about 3 hours to completeCONS:-The game doesn't display your keys (at least not that I could find) and this makes it kind of confusing when you're trying to remember what key you picked up or if you picked up a key at allThis game can be pretty punishing at times: but normal never gets anywhere near the levels of hair-pulling frustration that Blood was capable of. Enemies will plink you from any distance very accurately once you've alerted them and multiple enemies can absolutely shred you to pieces in seconds even on normal. This is offset by enemies sometimes dropping small health pickups. The higher difficulties of this game are absolutely UNFORGIVING though and almost reach Blood levels, so beware.Conclusion: this game is an absolute steal at 10 dollars and I can't wait to see what the madman behind it comes up with next for the rest of the chapters. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually too big on retro FPS but Cultic blew me away and stands on its own amidst the comparisons to Blood. It facilitates slower, strategic play, and really encourages switching through weapons to play to their strengths. The level design is top notch and never overstays its welcome. After warming up to the mechanics, you can continue playing slow and deliberate, or you have the freedom to go full Doom Eternal, strafing through the levels to a gorgeous soundtrack while being encouraged to flip through  your diverse arsenal, all while accompanied by the screams of burning robed cultists left behind in your wake. The controls are tight, and enemy targeting isn't hitscan, which really encourages you to take advantage of the fluid movement baked into the game. It really is whatever you want to make of it, but it's always at the very least badass and great to look at.

_childDocuments_.review: I've talked about in the past how the Boomer Shooter market is full of Quantity over Quality products, with many of them having poor difficulty balance, lack of ammo, bad level design, guns that feel like plastic toys and overall a huge lack of originality throughout the genre. CULTIC however, is not one of them. It's a one man team who has seen many of the best Boomer Shooters and knows what he's doing. I will admit though, CULTIC does start out rough and without any knowledge of how to survive in the first few levels, it can be annoying.My biggest complaint at first was how easy it was to burn through your ammo. You only get three guns at this point in the game so you'll have to switch between a Luger, a Rifle and a Shotgun. But once you realise that your hatchet is your best friend, you'll be saving ammo constantly by using it. It's a beast in the beginning of the game and once you use it for the majority of the first three/four levels, you'll have tons of ammo to get you through the game. Thankfully, this rewards you later as in further levels throughout, the game gives you tons of ammo at the beginning of some missions with a lot of ballistic armour. Another problem I had initially as well was the graphics. They look(ed) extremely ugly for a Boomer Shooter and it was giving me an eye sore. Thankfully, you can make them better by turning off most of the fancy graphics options in video menu. Now the game actually looked great! The game has some really interesting levels and that's where my praises of the game start to coming in. First off, the level design is great! I always love a shooter that dares to be adventurous with it's level design. If you feel like you're on an epic journey, that makes it all the more better and CULTIC has some awesome levels, from a Chapel, to a Mining Town, to the Cult's main base, it's all excellent and makes for some great fun to explore.CULTIC also has some fantastic gunplay once you get into the swing of things. The game has a great variety of weapons that are all effective and sound awesome. Weapon management throughout felt great and I continued to use different weapons in different situations and for some difficult enemies. The game also felt challenging enough while mostly not being annoying. Despite some grievances I have with a couple of annoying enemies, once you get who they are down, you'll be smooth sailing on defeating them quickly.Another great aspect of this game is the music. There are some really great tunes here throughout the game and they really get you excited during many of the gunfights throughout the game. The final moment during the ending got me so pumped up for more, which leads me to probably my biggest praise of the entire game. CULTIC feels complete. If this was just the entire game, I would be sold immediately. But considering there is more episodes coming, I'm excited to see what the developer brings to the table. I can already imagine how good the next few episodes are going to be. But it's amazing how fully fleshed this game is. I beat the game around 2.5/3 Hours, but I cannot wait to play more and come back to this again and again!Overall, CULTIC is a pretty sweet Boomer Shooter that doesn't fall into the Quantity over Quality syndrome this genre has had since DUSK blew up in popularity. Jason Smith, the developer of the game gets what makes this genre work and I am excited to see what comes next for CULTIC. I cannot recommend this game enough. I became enthralled once I nearly reached the halfway point and I feel fans of the genre, who love games like DUSK, AMID EVIL, Ion Fury and Prodeus will love this. A very promising, very awesome game.

_childDocuments_.review: What an exceptional title!The amount of bang for your buck on display here - literally - is well ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ worth it if you're even remotely interested in Boomer Shooters, most especially if you have penchant for id Software and 3D Realms titles of old; I was particularly reminded of the best parts of Doom and Blood.Unlike other run-and-gun Boomer Shooters, though, here you need to apply more strategy and be more cautious, especially on higher difficulty levels: players who bring good habits from Doom Eternal - i.e. dodging and fast weapon switching - will fare well here.Finally, the fact that this is very much the work of a solo developer is in its own right astounding: the amount of creativity on display, not to mention tonal consistency and sparse (which is perfect for the genre) yet intriguing narrative, make this a must-play for genre aficionados. _childDocuments_.review: A retro-style FPS done right. CULTIC draws heavily from Blood for its weapons, enemies and environments, thought it does so without outright ripping the 1997 classic off. Granted, you'll spend the majority of the game blasting your way through hooded cultists, zombies and other monstrosities with shotguns, submachine guns and dynamite, but in between firefights the game likes to focus on the horror angle, serving quiet moments of palpable tension, usually leading up to the introduction of a brand new type of abominable adversary. The tone of the game is generally more subdued as well, with more down-to-earth creepy locales (don't expect a carnival or a mad scientist's lab) and a silent hero.  The weapon selection is fairly standard, focusing on practicality rather than uniqueness, which is fine by me. The workhorse weapons of Blood are still there, and I never really liked the flare gun or life leech anyway. The guns all feel and perform very well, and their functionality can additionally be upgraded with weapon parts hidden throughout the level which serve as a good incentive for secret hunting. What else can I say, it's insanely impressive that one guy made this game all by himself, and for the price it's at it should be a no brainer for any retro FPS fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into cultic with a lot of expectations and not only did the developer meet my expectations he FAR EXCEEDED THEM. Great level design, Great art style (Old School low poly aesthetic), Satisfying weapons with visceral feedback, Ambient sound design and music is also top notch and last but not least the game is BUG FREE which these days usually isn't the case. You can feel the developer put everything he had in this game and the end result is nothing short of perfect.Now to address the things most people assume about Cultic before playing. Is it like Blood? Not at all it has more inspiration from Resident Evil than blood. In Blood you're a one man army but in cultic you'll be hammered real good if you're not careful. You'll have to use tactics and switch weapons carefully to attack every foe because there are lots of unique enemy npcs in this game with their own weaknesses, But don't worry Cultic has a weapon wheel selection mechanic which means you can switch weapons very easily. _childDocuments_.review: I'd say that, overall, this is a good game. I don't really know if it deserves 98% of positive reviews, but since Steam has a binary approach to reviews, it's understandable.I had a problem with the game though. The dev wrote, in an answer to one of the Steam reviews, that he made the game to encourage the player to approach the levels as they want. Yet, I feel like you’re not properly rewarded for being aggressive. Take Doom 2016 or Doom Eternal for example (I know they are AAA but bear with me), you have all the tools you need to feel powerful and efficient while being aggressive. You can switch weapon extremely quickly, and use that to cancel the cooldown of the heavier weapons, you run by default and, most of the time, it's enough to avoid attacks (as long as you keep moving), you can (in Doom Eternal) dash to stay longer in the air or to go to high and/or advantageous areas faster, you have various grenades, chainsaw and glory kills that briefly grant you with invulnerability, different ways of regaining health, shield and ammos, even while blasting at Mach 20 through wave of enemies.In Cultic, I felt way too powerless. You can't switch weapons fast, you don't run by default, your resources are all limited (at least on hard) and it's a bad idea to pick them during fights unless you take cover. Combined with levels in which you either don't have enough space to doge attacks (narrow corridors and labyrinths, small rooms...) or levels that are so wide that it becomes hard to see where the (many) enemies are, I was annoyed by the aggressive approach most of the time. The few times I kind of had to be aggressive, I ended up spamming the dodge button because I couldn't see all the enemies that were attacking me.It pains me to write this because I really like fast paced/aggressive shooters. Maybe it's because the ones that I like the most are recent and "modern" and not old school like Cultic. I also haven't played Blood, which is said to be the biggest inspiration for this game, so the fact that Cultic doesn't scratch that Blood itch in me might be the reason why I'm skeptical.There are still issues that don't depend solely on my tastes : the enemy A.I. is bad and the pathfinding is atrocious; the visuals (low poly + pixel art + color palette) are not suited for long distance kills, it literally hurt my eyes to try to see the enemies from far away, which is a problem since the game is supposed to let you play as you want; and the bosses are pretty underwhelming, you can easily abuse their A.I. flaws, and there are simultaneous waves of enemies to make it artificially harder.Other than that, the game has great visuals and artistic direction, a great soundtrack, a great atmosphere, a cool gunfeel and a good level design when you approach it carefully. It's a good game but I feel like the 98% of positive reviews can be misleading. That's why I thought that some people might want to know these details before buying the game. If you're ok with the aspects I mentioned, it's worth giving Cultic a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt, one of the best if not THE BEST "retro" shooters you can buy right now. Everything about this game is top notch and it stands head and shoulders and eyeballs above the rest in a crowded field. Let's check why:- Graphics are a perfect mix of 2D and 3D/voxels that threads the needle perfectly as far as style goes allowing the game to keep a retro vibe while enjoying all the benefits that modern advancements can provide without turning it into a pixel pastiche or Unreal/Unity asset nightmare- Art style is a gritty, washed out style that again, perfectly threads the needle of old-school and new. Blood meets Redneck Rampage meets Chasm meets Quake. The weapon sprites and animations are gorgeous. If there was a single negative I could conjure, it's that because everything is so brown and grey, sometimes it's easy to miss things if you're not looking a little more carefully. Luckily items all have a nice golden glow to them.- Sound design is nearly perfect. Weapons are loud and punchy, enemies scream at you and splatter into lovely gibs with blood dripping around you. Dynamite and Molotovs explode satisfyingly. The shotgun was done by right and when you double barrel you can almost hear Caleb's maniacal approving laughter. Holding down the trigger on the machine gun is next to godliness. The music switches between spooky ambient and pulsing tracks (sometimes slightly jarringly) appropriate to the situation, and is a great mix of tracks that wouldn't be out of place in an 80's horror flick scored by Carpenter.- Level design is very very good. Some early spots can feel a bit too open and loose but as the maps go on you can tell that the designers are getting a better handle on it and tightening their grip. Locations are build engine style recreations of real life areas and places that lack some of the detail that made those games so popular but makes up for in atmosphere and its own form of verisimilitude. I would love to see a level editor or mod support.- Gameplay is tremendous. Fast. Bloody. Deadly(ish). You can go as fast as you like or take your time. The game rewards twitchy trigger fingers just as much as it does creeping around and headshotting cultists from across the map with your rifle. Lovely variety of enemies ranging in difficulty and threat keep you on your toes. Only criticism here is that some of the cultists don't stand out as much as they could with regard to their robe colour (I have been shot in a variety of horrible ways by cultists in grey that I swore were simply packing pistols). Health and ammunition are plentiful but not enough that you feel like you're doing too well. Game is a bit easy in this regard and I'm playing on Hard. Maybe extreme is closer to Blood levels of pain that I'm accustomed to. Also, thanks to a fun little physics engine you can pick up, drop, and toss most objects you'd expect to be able to allowing... immersive-sim elements of environment manipulation! Feel free to chuck those red barrels around and set up traps. Throw that lamp in the window down into that crowed room. Build a ladder out of barrels to get somewhere you shouldn't go normally. Awesome. ALSO, there is a weapon upgrade system that lets you find weapon parts (XP, cyber modules WHATEVER) around and use them to give yourself powerful permanent boosts to your favourite firearms. Most of these parts are found in the various secrets hidden across the levels, secrets that are going to make you work a bit to find. There are some in the first map that broke my brain trying to find.What are you waiting for? This game is way too cheap for what you're getting. It's wildly underpriced and hurts me that the designer doesn't feel more confident in what he's created to sell it higher. His loss should be YOUR GAIN. And I haven't even touched the survival mode. Try the demo if you're not convinced but come on, just look at it and the price and do the right thing.tl;dr - Blood meets Redneck Rampage meets Warlock meets Resident Evil 4. Best shooter to come out in a long, long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Coolest shooter I've played since Titanfall 2. A love letter to all shooters, integrating elements from Doom, Deus Ex, and Call of Duty, to Silent Hill, Resident Evil 4, and the Last of Us. It's rad af and I'm so glad there's a dev out there innovating on shooters in general, rather than acting like a reactionary vanguard of the old. There's so much fun to be had pick n mixing across gaming history. Fun little hatchets one hitting enemies like in Black Ops. Crouch and slide speed glitching like in Warframe. Shield enemies from Resident Evil 4, which you can then equip like the riot shields from Modern Warfare. Silent Hill and Stalker-esque grotesque and supernatural enemies. Deux Ex and Duke Nukem 3D sandboxes with secret areas that are contextualised as part of the world. Doom-style taunting, where you can get enemies to attack each other. Dark Messiah environmental hazards, combined with kicking and throwing. Heck, even Last of Us style weapon upgrades, built from parts you scavenge from the environment. None of it feels gimmicky. It's all integrated so well. Thanks Jasozz!

_childDocuments_.review: Review as of 5/18/2023 (chapter 1 only)Cultic is absurdly fun. Cultic is also difficult, but fair.I'm going to avoid mentioning Monolith Studios game "Blood" outside of this section, because this game deserves to stand on it's own merit. The developer has clearly played and took inspiration. Here's where they're similar.1. Both have some similar weapons.2. In both of these games, you'll be killing cultists.3. They're both incredible.The tone, mechanics, difficulty, story, and most other things are much different.I picked up Cultic after enjoying the demo looking for a break from my usual routine. The demo was fun, but didn't blow me away. So I played the first level. Then I played the first level again. And again. There was so much to see, do, and so many options that I couldn't move forward until I felt I bled it dry, even trying different difficulties. The combat, secrets, movement quirks, and surprising amount of interactivity are all incredibly satisfying to play. Then I beat the game. Every level was better than the last, all ten of them.Then I did an achievement run. Then I hit the leaderboard in hoard mode. Now I'm trying to beat it on extreme difficulty. I'm somehow more captivated than I have been by a game in a long time. The amount of care and passion put into this, by one person, is insane. Even if the second half is somehow a massive downgrade, I'd gladly be satisfied with what I have already, but my hopes are high.The only complaint I have is that I can't imagine 20ish levels being enough for how good the core of this game is. I hope the developer is either wanting, able, or willing to open up mod support. I say that as a person who has only ever played Doom mods. I can't think of a higher compliment than that.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game has a lot of bang for its buck. Going in blind and taking your time, you could spend 5 hours on the campaign. Then, put in 5 hours on the wave-based survival mode. Any achievement hunters should easily be able to push past 15 hours, and survival mode offers a decent challenge for its rather simplistic approach.     Also, whether through "scene selection" (keeping another save file's loadouts) or starting a new game, the campaign has a decent level of replayability, with difficulty increases not only improving enemy damage, but spawn placement, enemy type, AND number (something too many games refuse to mess with). There's also another layer with "Custom" difficulty settings, but I cannot vouch for how it would feel to make every enemy a champion, and then multiply the projectiles by 10x.     What isn't noted on this review is that I have another 8 hours logged on the demo, which only has 1 level and 1 survival map, likely due to said survival map. If you like Half-Life and Doom, you'll love the campaign. If you love Doom (2016), then you'll enjoy the survival maps. I believe most people should feel satisfied with the combat, powerful headshots, secret hunting, and even finding perfect points or ledges to snipe or launch an ambush from.     Also, the difficulty and pacing is perfect for any player. Make a save every five feet, peer around corners, and pick off your enemies with a lever action rifle. Or alternatively, use your axe to bypass any shield in your way, shotgun anyone you can't axe, and kick jump your way across the map to see how fast you can beat a level. ().     If you find yourself on the fence with the game, try the demo, as what you see there is what you get (minus a few enemy variations). Also, I find myself shocked (and rather glad) that enemies don't feel bullet spongy, even on the later difficulties (if you have the right damage upgrades on the right weapons, I always upgrade the shotgun first, then the Stetson).      Lastly, the game was a nominee for Steam's "Labor of Love" award (though not the winner), as evident by the developer releasing an extra map, an extra level teasing Cultic Chapter 2, and the insane work and bugfixes that have gone into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Blood..Lives..Again..First impression is pretty damn solid, good secrets that reward exploration, Enemy variety in the early levels is a bit meh with it just being different colours of cultist, but it tells you what the enemies are about at a glance so no points lost. _childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the philistines parroting each other in the reviews with "LOL Blood 2". CULTIC is Like blood on a very surface level, that being: both games have cultists as enemies and dynamite as a weapon. The game, while has certain callbacks to it, plays nothing like Blood. However, it is a VERY good old school shooter and you should definetely play it. Because everyone have already fellated it enough in the reviews, I'll add some nitpicky complaints to the mix. Firstly. I didn't like the redisigned first map compared to the early demo; it feels very flat now, that can be said about most of the maps in CULTIC that have big open spaces, actually. The game is way too generous with ammo for my tastes as well, ironically, at times it feels a lot like cryptic passage add-on for Blood. So maybe in this sense CULTIC is like Blood 2, lol. Secondly. The game has kind of a weird weapon balancing. Lever action rifle is just straight up better than sniper rifle for sniping purposes most of the time. Fully upgraded handgun is a beast of a weapon that's better than shotgun and machine gun in most cases where these two weapons would be useful. Incinerator, that you'll get in the last 4 levels , is ridiculously overpowered, it's primary fire pumps out what feels like Satan's own ♥♥♥, that one shots most enemies including some of the mini bosses, the range of this thing is terrific, it shoots in an arc, so it can go over the cover, the ammo is aplenty and as a cherry on top it doesn't need to be reloaded, needless to say, the last boss doesn't have a chance against it. The only bad weapon in the game is the grenade launcher, it'is a joke even with all the upgrades, it's splash radius is pathetic, and it's damage output is not that good for how little ammo for it the game gives you.And finally. For some strange reason the item "blast armor" gives you health, which is probably a bug.Highly recommended. Go play it.

_childDocuments_.review: The , which blossomed in the wake of David Szymanski's 2018 breakout hit , has now been well underway for nearly half a decade. Currently, the genre appears to be teetering between receding back into the pixelated fog of 90's nostalgia, or remaining, as a niche, but well supported haven for wonky doors, questionably balanced weaponry and edgy Satanism.Jason Smith's  manages to make a strong case for the longevity of the , without reinventing the wheel – like, at all. Hell, you begin the game by crawling out of a shallow grave, ala the opening moments of Monolith Productions's 1997 classic . Devotee's of  will immediately recognize the brown robes of the hatchet-wielding Cultist's you encounter only moments later, after entering the . Said devotees are likely to go from bemused to ecstatic, after being reunited with a very dear old friend:  I paid $11.49 for my copy of . The TNT in this game was easily worth $5 of that entry price. It's just, so good. The ability to independently light, drop and/or throw the TNT, while initially a little cumbersome, enables a tremendous amount of problem solving mid-combat. Sense an ambush waiting around the next corner? Huck a stick of TNT, and if your hunch was correct, then prepare for a shower of bloody gibblets to come bouncing around that corner. Being chased by a chainsaw maniac? Drop a lit stick between your feet, as you frantically sprint away, likely while bunny-hopping over several bear-traps in the process.I could go on about how tactile each weapon from ’s diverse arsenal feels to use at great length – especially that bolt-action rifle, which gave me flashbacks to using the  from  – but, I’ll refrain. I will, however, take a moment to note the role ’s exquisite weapon design plays in the moment-to-moment gameplay loop, which often has you charging at the enemy, closing in the distance, then dealing damage and immediately collecting a small amount of health as your reward, before retreating, reloading and finding a new cluster of targets. It feels like a balanced mix of ’s , made famous by Bungie’s Jaime Griesemer, and 2016’s , which incentivized risky behaviour (in this case, melee combat) by rewarding it with health.In addition to designing a fantastic game, Jason Smith has also crafted a rather gorgeous one. ’s distinct palette provides a back-alley miasma of colour: filthy browns, the tainted pinks and purples of a week-old gasoline shimmer, all with the occasional highlight of a piss yellow. It’s an aesthetic that could only be described as a gamble – doubly so, given the addition of voxels, which blend rather seamlessly with the flat, Build Engine-esque sprites. Yet somehow,  manages to make its ugliness compelling, creating an atmosphere that’s far greater than the mere sum of its parts. Oh, and the sky-boxes are genuinely striking at times, which is a Hell of a thing to say about a .This relentless sense of style elevates the traditional, but imaginatively designed levels, giving them a powerful sense of place, the kind that would usually come at the cost of playability. In , however, the arenas are just as engaging to explore after the carnage as they were to strafe around in circles, spewing hot lead and being showered with gibs. I don’t think secret-hunting in a  has ever felt this organic to me, in large part due to that consistency of the level-design, which is maintained through-out, despite each room feeling unique and bespoke.The sole exception to this level-design excellence comes at the early-to-middle-point of the game, when you'll find yourself hopelessly lost in these pitch-black woods, exploring an atrociously recursive space. Maybe my brightness settings are just too low, but searching for those three pieces of that bloody bridge mechanism was beyond frustrating. Funny enough, the sequence much later on, when the player is  trapped in a  maze, was shockingly fun in contrast. It's hard to believe that the same designer who managed to make navigating a honest-to-God hedge-maze interesting also made... . The sequence in the woods reminded me of 's two worst levels, combined:  and ". Thankfully, it doesn't last for very long. And that sequence does end with a very memorable ambush, which almost made the preceding frustration worth it.I eagerly await  of . I'm sure I'll have more to say then.

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is centered around very grounded classical gameplay and features, but the presentation and design are overwhelmingly unique, straying from the established norms for shooters, with more bold and risky decisions. It offers more. It has hooks beyond the gameplay. The art direction, setting, atmosphere, palette, setpieces and interplay of horror elements are stunning. The developer's keen understanding of outdoor spaces should also be mentioned, harking back to Half-Life's 'Surface Tension' chapter, and arguably surpassing the experience. You rarely feel boxed in unless the developer wants you to. Cultic eschews 'corridor gameplay' for very immersive well-designed theater. It's an incredible package, looks beautiful. A must-play, revives and expands upon the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is the best Retro FPS I've ever played. I played the original demo, and it was amazing back then. It's even better now.Something I never expected when I first played the demo was how much upgrading your character would be a factor. Not only can you upgrade your guns at workbenches using weapon parts, but you can permanently increase your maximum health by finding "imbued remains" throughout the game.If you don't care for the upgrades and want to rely only on your mechanical skill, you can just ignore them. Don't pick up any imbued remains, don't use workbenches. It's not like they're remotely required, each piece of imbued remains only increases your max HP by 5. On my first playthrough on the Hard difficulty, I only found 3 to bump by health to 115.Cultic's guns are masterfully crafted, each one remains useful throughout the entire game (and not just because of the upgrades).The hatchet is good for low-level cultists, especially opposing hatchet-wielders.The handgun can be used to effectively take out enemies from long range AND deal decent damage at close range.The lever-action rifle acts as the game's revolver, having a much slower firing speed than the handgun but with much more power and perfect accuracy, though also with scarcer ammo.The shotgun is absolutely insane at close range, and can reduce an enemy to a fountain of blood if you discharge both barrels at once.The STEN has less accuracy than the handgun, but much higher DPS, making it a better use of your ammo when it comes to crowds.The grenade launcher is probably the least useful gun, but only because you already have more than enough explosive power with the TNT and molotov cocktails.The FG42 is like the lever-action rifle, but with a scope and a different ammo type. If you are low on ammo for one, you can rely on the other.The incinerator is a flamethrower, and Jesus Christ is it powerful. It can immediately dispatch a low-level cultist using a single point of ammo (of which you can hold several hundred). Even the toughest enemies can go down in 5-10 points of ammo. The alt-fire is powerful too, but the the primary fire can get infinitely more use out of the same amount of ammo the alt-fire consumes.Each gun gets 4 upgrades (except the incinerator because it's already powerful enough). The first one always costs 4 weapon parts, and in every case it's a simple damage boost (except with the Grenade Launcher, where it's an increase in explosion size). The second one always costs 2 parts and in every case is a higher magazine/clip/tube/whatever capacity (except with the Shotgun where it's a faster reload). The third and fourth are weapon-specific and are usually 2 weapon parts, but are occasionally 1, 3, or 4. Some examples are better accuracy for the Handgun and STEN, tighter spread for the Shotgun, and a full-auto mode for the FG42.(I actually have a nitpick with one upgrade, the Lever-Action's "Deadeye." I think it's practically useless, especially for 3 weapon parts, which could be spend on something infinitely better like a faster fire rate for the STEN or a burst-fire mode for the Handgun. Deadeye just grants a small amount of slow-motion on a successful headshot with the lever-action's alt-fire, which barely helps, and also there's already a chance of it happening on a kill. I have two ideas: 1. reduce the weapon part cost to one, or 2. remove the Lever-Action's alt-fire by default, and have the upgrade actually be what allows you to use it, along with the slow-mo thing.)

_childDocuments_.review: I want to write a review for this so bad, but I have to first get over my physical and mental trauma I got from playing the game, maybe I´ll force myself to finish the review this year...Edit 07.01.2023: Working on a video review about the game now, I don´t think I can put all this in textOk, so I recently played the game a bit more and I can now confidently explain my problems: -The biggest issue is that the game takes inspiration from games like Blood or Dusk but fails to execute what these games did, both of those games manage to get the spooky atmosphere down better than cultic and also have more enjoyable gameplay-I think the game plays too slow. It is trying to go for that spooky atmosphere by being a slower shooter but both Blood and Dusk got a good atmosphere despite being more fast paced-Combat doesn´t feel good. Ok, let me elaborate my problems here: First of all you are basically forced to headshot or you wont deal any damage, I tested it and on Very hard you need about 9 shots from your pistol to the body to kill an enemy and 4 to the head... This is just way too much in my opinion. Enemys are way too tanky making combat boring, because you are very squishy. If you run out of armor you are basically dead in 3 or 4 hits. Enemys also seem to have unlimed precision even at the greatest of ranges making long range fights undesirable. Secondly enemys should be easily recognised, just like in blood they wear different coloured robes so they can be distinguished. Or so you would think... The grey robed cultists either hold a relatively harmless pistol or an absolutely devastating Sten submaschinegun that will annihilate you as soon as you are in their line of sight. And then the brown robed guys. They are either comepletly harmless and just throw hatches at you or they  are armed with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ grenade launcher that almost kills you with the first shot. And lastly I think the enemy roster is too small, but not in the way that it needs more enemys but rather there is a specific type of enemy missing. So in the game you either have enmys that are killed in like 5 bullets or less or you have enemys that were boss encounters and take like 90 bullets. That is just really annoying as there are no enemys in between, so you either fight bullet sponges or cannonfodder. -Headshot mechanic: I really like the headshots in the game, they feel good. It´s a bit boring you are forced to do them to deal serious damage to your enemys but it´s ok. But now to my problem: sometimes randomly when you gib an enemy or their head, a slowmo will play. This is either annoying, when the enemy is far away and you can´t really see the head exploding or when the enemy is the last one standing after a big fight and you just want to move on. Sometimes this also gives you time to react to a situation but that´s the exception in my experience. It just feels weird to have this feature just randomly implemented, I don´t see a reason to have it, especially since explosions also sometimes trigger this and it´s just even weirder when you can´t even see the viscera of the exploded enemy but still there is a slowmo. I would´ve really liked it, if this was a feature of the game that you sort of get this slowmotion bonus for every headshot and it plays similar to superhot, with the difference that you don´t have to stand still but play well and headshot cultists.So TL;DR: The game tries to be a spiritual successor to games like Blood or Dusk, but can´t hold up to those games and has very boring combat due to enemys either dying too quick or taking way too long to kill and then there is the sometimes annoying headshot mechanic that just gets in the way of the player and is only sometimes cool. I can see the good game, it just has too many flaws for me. Feel free to disagree and state your own opinion in the comments, maybe I will update the list in case there is something else I want to get off my chest. I will be checking out chapter 2 to see if the game improved.

short (barely 4 hours with me searching for extra ammo/weapons/unlocks)- game loads very very long, it looks like its crashed when it does that as experienced by me and reported by other players- cultist with a pistol hits me from the other side of the map in first shot - suuuure- you can't swim down under water just by moving mouse down, you have to press crouch - wtf?- world doesn't seem believable with some cultists just standing around waiting for player like manekins- I can drag barrels through walls- easy to miss where to go on shipyard map- still contains bug from demo when you tab back to game it fires your main weapon- weird difficulty spikes- didn't like the crypt that much- having finished the game I have to say the map design is not great for me, I feel like there is too much going from intense to boring traversal and looking for the way- its actually expensive compared to amount of content - _childDocuments_.review: This review is a checklist of what might be a deal breaker for you, so if none of these things bother you then you should consider trying the game out:The enemies are okay, and a decent challenge. But after I realized I couldn't play this game in a survival horror fashion because it wasn't paced well, I rethought my strategy and felt that maybe this game was way more fun on the lower difficulty. So I switched from the Mouse & Keyboard to a controller and put it on Casual. I was still wrong. I now allowed the game to goof off, and here I was sliding around infinitely in between enemies, and I still felt like I couldn't progress. The enemies were surprisingly still dangerous on Casual, but even after you get rid of them, you still don't know where to go. I thought it would be more fun to increase the enemy count, turn on infinite ammo, and just enjoy a killfest, but you can't do that either.I upped the movement speed and ran around at mach 10, and was reminded constantly that the fall damage was unfair. I just got so tired of trying to figure this game out. If the game doesn't know what it wants to be, then neither would I.Also the dynamite bundles suck. I think the game is supposed to be atmospheric, but it's more colorful on the store page then when you finally load it.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely tremendous accomplishment. Cultic is a singular game that does everything phenomenally well. Lets start with gunplay: clean and every weapon feels excellent. Not a tremendous amount of variety in terms of weapons; however, this isn't a bad thing at all. In fact I think it's a good thing. The guns feel purposeful, designed with intent. And they are a joy to use, landing headshots with the long rifle is as satisfying the 1st time as it is the 51st. I rarely find myself getting excited with retroshooters, like I'm talking about edge of my chair excitment, but with Cultic I got excited. Probably the third map is where I really started to vibe with the game, everything opens up and it's unbelievable how massive these maps are. I'm actually pretty shocked with the maps in general, these feel like the best map design I've seen in a very significant amount of time. They're complex and detailed, but still expertly designed. I feel like the game has an amazing scope. I'm thinking of it in comparison to DOOM Eternal right, a modern AAA title with massive teams behind it, and even still Cultic feels like its a larger game. I don't really know how it accomplishes this? Maybe its because of the incredible variety in maps? It really feels like a world that's lived in, things lead into eachother in believable ways, whereas DE is sort of fractured in its map design and never really expands beyond increasing enemies, interactive movement items and corridors (not that this is bad at all, I am of the opinion that DE is THE shooter to beat for any modern fps, and Cultic honstely proves itself as a worthy game because it outdoes DE in a lot of significant ways). It's unbelievable that this is just made by one dude, the skill and passion in Clutic is clear and it BEGS for a replay. Can't wait for Cultic 2!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: It would universally seem that any game developed and/or published by 3D Realms always has the same problem: combat is not fun. Cultic sets the initial expectation of a slow-paced atmospheric game with stealth elements (i.e. the ability to crouch, walk slow, sneak up on enemies, utilize traps). But then very quickly the game introduces a myriad of standard enemies all with the ability to spot you from a mile away and immediately attack with hit-scan shots fired from an aimbot. This combat system feels so out of place with what should be a slow-paced experience. You'll be presented with scenarios such as: there's an enemy encampent on the other side of a bridge, with cultists standing around a bonfire. And look, there's an exploding barrel conveniently placed at the bridge entrance for you to carry and then throw, with the obvious intention of blowing them all up. But then halfway across the bridge, all enemies spot you and fire immediately with no delay. Then your barrel explodes, and you're left wondering why the F the devs even bothered to place that barrel.After these unfun encounters occur more than a few times, you'll realize this game is actually meant to be played more like Doom. But it doesn't make sense to incorporate so many elements that encourage slow-paced gameplay and atmospheric enjoyment. It would be comparable to playing Resident Evil as if it were Doom. Why bother with great atmosphere and tension, only to waste it all with a combat system clearly designed around bunny hopping and flick-shots?If you know this going in, and play it as such, then perhaps you'll enjoy it. But if you thought you were going into a slower more atmospheric game, you'll hate it.I just don't understand why anyone would think this is fun. It's not.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This game is FANTASTIC and you should absolutely play it (or at least try the demo). I can't wait for the upcoming DLC and will buy it instantly the day it's released.I saw this game in discovery queue and it immediately got my attention due to very interestic graphic style. I downloaded the demo and fell in love with it, bought the full game after like 30 minutes of playing the demo version.Game has great atmosphere, the story itself although simple, is interesting - I really like the way that it's presented to the user. I don't want to spoil anything because it's really worth discovering on your own.As I said, gunplay is absolutely fantastic, the are multiple weapons and they are all useful in their own way. I was playing on Extreme difficulty (I strongly advise you to do the same, the game isn't that hard) and it was pure joy to plan out encounters with enemies - where to hide, which weapons to use etc.There are 10 levels and each one is unique and introduces something that wasn't included in previous ones. Sometimes there are even horror-like elements, where you are alone in a dark cave with your lighter as the only source of light, lost in dark woods or inside mental asylum - there were a couple of times where I really got scared and jumped on my chair.The only thing that I think could be better are boss fights - they are quite easy and honestly a bit boring - just hide behind a wall and spam dynamite towards the enemy. _childDocuments_.review: Where do i even beginThis game is fantastic.(TL;DR at the bottom)I started out unsure of how i felt about it.  basic movement and combat felt clunky right off the bat.  i finished the first level with mixed feelings, but by the time i finished the second i was slaughtering cultists with a huge grin on my face. Level design is top notch.  the world feels natural and well put together.  secrets are easy to come by and i never felt like any of the secrets would be impossible to find if i didnt just stumble upon it. the secrets are like, "oh this door won't budge and the windows are barricaded but if i could get on the roof i bet i could enter through the chimney."  there is a large variety of levels as well, even various designs in a single level so youre always mixing up your playstyle.  some levels are vast with a focus on slow movement and precise sniping.  some are close quarters where youre flicking your crosshair left and right while your shotty disposes of enemies by the hundreds.  some are slow and eerie, letting you get immersed into the world before the combat starts to ramp up. 10/10The weapon variety is killer, pun intended.  i found myself using the axe you start the game with in every level of the game.  no gun serves every purpose, you WILL be switching between your entire arsenal but not like you would be in doom eternal since the gameplay is a bit slower than that.  even weapons that are supposed to be direct upgrades are often relegated to specific situations.  nothing took the show and ran with it and nothing was left in the dust either, everything fit its place very well. 10/10The story is, while simple, still engaging and worth paying attention to.  the story is told to you through notes and typewriters you discover throughout the world.  some even being written by the same person so you learn their story as you progress, i even found myself looking forward to the next note so i could learn more about whats going on.  my one and only gripe with the story is the climax of the lore (for lack of a better term) happens right at the very end.  i was so excited to see where the story went next but all i got were the credits.  this is however just chapter 1 with chapter 2 coming down the road at some point (fingers crossed).  9/10The soundtrack is very hit or miss.  it often just doesn't feel right and the queues for when music plays or doesnt play is very cut and dry. so you will be wondering an area looking for supplies with very energetic music playing in the background until you exit that given area. i wished the music was toned down a bit and instead had a focus on the ambience and atmosphere since this game is very immersive but the music does take you out of the world a bit. 7/10TL;DR all in all i give CULTIC a 9/10.  It does everything you would ask a retro FPS to do very well.  Great level design, weapon choice, an amazing story that you can choose to engage with, well executed enemy variants, and my only issue with the game being the soundtrack.  the music isn't bad, it just doesn't fit the game that well and is sometimes playing in the background a lot more than you'd want it to.  CULTIC is well worth the $10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. Buy it now. If you are at all a fan of retro shooters, this is a must-buy.However, I have multiple minor points of criticism that are aimed at helping the dev while this game is still in early access. If you have not played the game yet, do not read further. Just buy the damn game, you won't regret it.1. The model of the lever action. This isn't necessarily a *flaw*, but more so a grievance. The barrel is WAY too short when you're holding the gun, it looks ridiculous. If I'm not mistaken, this is by design, as the lever action appears to be a Mare's Leg, which is an actual, real life gun. However, that doesn't stop it from looking ludicrous. The barrel of the sprite is so small that it looks like a pistol, and it throws off the whole look. What makes this worse is that I love Lever Action rifles! And more specifically, the lever action is my favorite weapon! I want to feel like a Cowboy, and the ugly midget barrel takes me out of my Clit Eastwood RP. Please devs, add in an option to increase the barrel length of the lever action. I know this is a small grievance, but it legitimately upset me while playing. (And if you're reading this devs, please also add an option to play The Good, Bad, and the Ugly theme whenever I start popping heads with the alt fire, I will pay more weapon parts for this feature.)Speaking on weapon parts (fastest segue in the west), they feel a little mishandled. Simply put, most of them are boring. Although objectively helpful, increasing the magazine size is so generic and underwhelming that I literally didn't do it a single time. The only gun that would be useful on, the Shotgun, doesn't have it. But perhaps the worst part is that none of the upgrades are actually interesting. The only ones that is genuinely interesting (imo) is the Lever Action upgrade that gives you slow motion with every alt-fire headshot, and the Grenade Launcher upgrade that gives you fragmentation. They're great! More like those please. But almost every upgrade is some generic improvement on a slightly pertinent stat. Here's a good rule of thumb; If your weapon upgrade boils down to the same function as a weapon attachment from Call of Duty, it's probably not very good.For example, the pistol is totally and completely outclassed by the Sten, so why not give it the option to convert it into a revolver? Or even better yet, to stick with the makeshift, old-timey weapon aesthetic, why not have the switch from the Luger to a Revolver be a homemade, makeshift conversion to a higher caliber round? It dynamically shows that the protagonist has to scrounge around for anything he can use, and be crafty. It would also just look super cool to see a revolver cartridge stuffed into the body of a Luger, held together with duct tape and steadfast prayer. Or how about going crazy with this idea? The protagonist gets carried away with his DIY gun improvements, and turns the double barrel shotgun into this 8-barreled monstrosity that takes can hold 3 rounds in each barrel and takes 10 full seconds to reload, but possesses enough firepower to blow away a house. Adding onto the theme of sacrificing reliability for raw power, you could make the shotgun occasionally fire two barrels with one trigger pull, wasting a little bit of ammo. To subvert expectations a little bit, instead of having the alt-fire unleash all chambers at once, throw in a curve ball. Once you press alt-fire, the barrels start spinning like a chain gun, and you hear the protagonist's maniacal laughter as he unleashes a storm of buckshot into Hell's spawn.Especially since it appears like we're going to hell in the next chapter, wacky ideas like this are both appropriate to the setting and add to the charm of the game. I could keep coming up with ideas for Gun modifications and upgrades all day (I'm available for hire, just saying. Ah, who am I kidding, I do this ♥♥♥♥ for free), but I think we've gotten a little off track in my gun-related fantasies. Point of the story is; the weapon upgrade system is underwhelming. A flat damage increase and extra mag size is undoubtedly useful, but they're so uninteresting and yawn-inducing that you feel cheated, despite their objective utility. Please, in whatever way you see fit, spice up the weapon upgrade system. It's promising, but needs some... spizzaz... to reach it's full potential. (This is kind of a tangent aimed almost solely at the dev, so sorry about that, but I have to get it off my chest.)Speaking broader, WW2 weapons are perfectly serviceable, but I feel like it could be so much more interesting. Sure, it's more accurate to real life for the weapon upgrades to be a shoulder sling, or a better lever, or a higher capacity magazine. Yet those are all BORING. Not only are they conceptually uninteresting, they are mechanically pointless. All they do is allow the gun to be slightly better at what it already does. With or without higher damage rounds, the Sten performs exactly the same function, the only alteration is how long it takes to perform the function. Weapon upgrades or modifications don't have to be nearly as crazy as the two that I've suggested so far, it could be something the Sten stacking damage of the next mag based on how many enemies were killed in the previous 50 rounds, or the shotgun stacking overkill damage to your next shot, leading to you exponentially building up damage until you miss or unload all that built up damage into a single enemy. Those upgrades wouldn't change the primary role of the weapon, but they would change how you use them. They reward you for skillful, efficient play with those weapons by scaling your effectiveness directly with your competence in using them. It adds a level of depth that gives the game longevity that many other great FPS games simply lack. That's why Overkill is so beloved. To close up my senile, tedious ramblings, don't feel afraid to experiment. We don't just want Blood 2: For Real This Time, we want Cultic. Also, feel free to shamelessly steal any of my ideas if you feel so inclined, I doubt they're worth a damn, but you never know. (Except that Cowboy option, that's an invaluable suggestion right there.)

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic horror take on the doomlike genre that's full of surprises, at least on hard. Idk about easier difficulties. It liberally borrows from other FPS subgenres, with headshots being crucial to the gameplay, but not to the point that it leaves the doomlike tradition behind. I love the 60s vibe that it has going, which is quite refreshing after playing some more generic and/or crappy shooters. Ammo is not given to you on a plate - you absolutely *need* to manage your resources. The gunplay is wonderful, with the opportunity to upgrade most of your weapons via a very simple system of finding parts (usually in secrets) to use at workbenches that you will find throughout the game. Ace music. The level design can *occasionally* be a bit confusing, however, this should be an instant buy for anyone after a doomlike that leans more into horror rather than straight up action. That being said, the action is definitely still there.Performance is a little bit questionable when one considers how it looks and plays. It definitely needs some optimisation. It recommends a friggin' GTX 1070. Why? If I didn't know better, I'd be asking if it's running a crypto miner in the background lol. This isn't really a problem for me at 1440p with a Ryzen 5800x and a 2070 Super, mostly staying above 120fps, (edit: locked 120 with my 4080 16GB) but there's millions of computers out there that should be able to run this properly but can't.There's a story, if you give a ****. Entirely skippable, as it's mainly told through notes that you find.Also, voxels. 9/10, one of the best shooters of 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Oozing with atmosphere and excellent level design / gun play. Definitely worth the asking price.I really have to say, CULTIC has completely blown away my expectations. I'm usually pretty critical of nu-boomer-shooters, lots of them really just lack any soul. This game does not have this problem. I sat down and played through the entire campaign without any breaks or pauses. It was genuinely gripping, and a masterclass in environmental storytelling (with notes to make things more clear). The level design was incredibly well done, pushing the player in one direction clearly while also enabling more open exploration on some levels, I didn't get lost once.You can tell that a lot of care went into making each encounter. You're always given just enough enemies to make a given fight a challenge but never unfairly so. Any point where I got stuck in the game really came down to approaching a problem from a different angle. There's about 4 enemies in the game that I think are somewhat tanky, but it's not just for the sake of making a sponge, it always serves a purpose. Even then, 2 of the 4 have an explicit weakness that makes fighting them way more manageable. The only section I struggled with was in a mid-game map, and that was because I failed to use my resources effectively and ran out of ammo. In a sea of very same-y boomer shooters I really think CULTIC stands out, and deserves recognition for its application of the formula.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I usually don't get my money's worth on games under 10$, where to start...- Intricate level design with full-featured set pieces, linear maps broken up by expansive hubs to explore- STUFFED. WITH. SECRETS.- Diversity of enemy design, hitscanners, ghouls, and others balanced out with eldritch horrors. You will usually always know if an encounter is oncoming if you're careful- Full Arsenal of weapons each of which can be upgraded for differing play styles run-by-run; moreso you can just main one or two weapons (short and a long range, or even the hatchet and TNT if you like)- The shotgun is good (at close range)- The jump is REALLY good (vastly underappreciated)My only cons? They're not cons they're actually pros I just hate horror:- Heavily atmospheric, the dev really knew what he was doing going for the dithering style and combining in a lot of well-paced BGM and haunting sounds backed up with environmental cues and lore that makes the setting cause the hairs to stand up on the back of your neck- Occasional jumpscares that will make you lose your ♥♥♥♥ the first playthrough, these are easily remedied with explosives and FIRE FIRE FIRE on the next ones- two or three enemy types that are completely, pissantly annoying but you'll get good at peering through the darkness and atomizing them with time and experience.Either way if this was 40$ I'd suggest waiting for a sale, solid buy at 25$, but this is an ABSOLUTE BUY for 10$.
