_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most satisfying and fun shooter I've played in years. Among the legions of new retro throwback shooters coming onto the market Cultic stands tall. Striking visuals, extremely good gunplay, the best headshots you've ever seen, levels that have clearly seen a frankly insane amount of attention to detail, and the cultists are just so cute when they run around on fire.Criticisms: I did not enjoy the crypt level very much, and I think this game probably needs a little bit more tutorial. I found out that I had a kick ability roughly 80% of the way through. That may be more an indictment of me as a smoothbrained idiot who doesn't pay attention than on the dev.My trivial issues aside, Episode 2 can't come soon enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Mr. Jasozz,Thank you for making such a great game. I was in a slump with games, playing the same doldrum game and thinking to myself that I needed something new; something to get me in the spirit of the season. I may have been looking for something else, but believe me when I say that what I ended up finding was much better than what I was looking for.  The artwork is AMAZING for a "retro-style" game like this. I've played more than a few "retro-style" games, and they end up being not nearly as detailed as this. For you speed-runners out there, shame on you. If there's one type of gamer that I utterly cannot stand, it's most certainly a speed-runner. They beat the game in less than an hour then complain that they didn't see anything and that the game was too quick. If you look at my times on each level, you'll notice that I spent more time looking around at stuff than I ever did just going through the game. That's what I always want out of a game, and you delivered. That being said, I didn't want a "museum tour". I'm not going to bash it too much because I didn't end up buying it, but when I read the gameplay reviews of Scorn, I didn't end up buying it out of disappointment. I was looking for more action in a game. This is no "museum tour". You have to plan your advancement and make sure you shoot fast and shoot straight. That being said, this was the perfect combination of atmosphere and action. Not too much of one, not too much of the other.There are only two gripes about the game, but don't think because I'm griping that I hate this game. Numbuh Won: Platforming is slightly annoying. I'll be the first to say I suck at First Person Platforming. There's no way you could be worse than me at First Person Platforming. It's impossible. I think it's the combination of the camera and the slipperiness of the movement in this game, but again, don't take this one too hard. I was able to finally get through the platforming parts, and  Again, I suck at platforming, so take this with a grain of salt. Numbuh Tew: I think there should be more explanation on the keybindings. I didn't even know there was a Kick command until half-way through the game. And I'm still not really sure what the point of kicking is. Also, there's a dodge command, too. I messed around with it a bit, but honestly never used it much. They are interesting features, but only the most avid of gamers are going to utilize them to their full extent. I may have missed any explanations about them while I was going through the first map, but again, I didn't really see a reason to use either of them.OH! While we're on the subject, has anyone figured out what the red bar next to the heart is supposed to mean? At one point I was automatically healing while under a certain amount of health, but I had no idea what affected such an outcome. And the bar next to the heart went up and down, but there was never an explanation about what that did or why I should care. I mostly relied on healing drops and using the aid kit that you carry around. Finally, there's no breathing bar either. While underwater elements are not all that common, I would like to see how much time I have to breath. At first I thought I had unlimited breath, but then I started taking massive damage at increments, which I immediately deduced must be some sort of breathing mechanic. But again, that wasn't really explained and there is no bar or notification on the HUD for such a mechanic.But both of those are trivial complaints. There aren't enough underwater moments to care too much about breath. And the Heart bar I did wonder about, but I never really needed any further explanation in regards to how I played the game. Other than that, there were no game-breaking bugs. There were no hair-pulling moments. I had fun and it's perfect for this time of the year.  I don't mean for the price. You can't beat the price for the amount of gameplay you get. I mean I'm hooked.  For now, I guess I have to wait. But you have made a satisfied customer out of me. Please, do not stop your work on this game. I've seen it too many times that developers end up never finishing their games. As is, based on how the first chapter ended, it's perfectly fine to end it here, if that's your intent. But honestly, it would be a greatly missed opportunity. I look forward to your future work, and I wish you the best of luck and whatever you decide to do.Sincerely,A Satisfied Customer

_childDocuments_.review: tl:dr: Action FPS where the player fights an evil cult with some of the most visceral feeling weapons I've ever experienced.Amazing game heavily inspired by Blood. I also see elements of RE4 and some things that remind me of Return to castle wolfenstein. The player fights their way through an evil cult using a variety of awesome weapons. Literally every weapon is good and feels amazing to use, this game even gives games like dusk a run for their money in terms of game feel. The TNT is peak content, delivering that rare satisfaction of gibbing groups of cultists not felt since Blood itself. The shotgun is literally Blood's shotgun back and better than ever, decapitating any poor SoB that gets your way. Surprise, surprise, a good flamethrower in this game as well.There are many other weapons I will leave unnamed for you to experience yourself.The Graphics are in a strange place for me, some of the areas seem uninspired with reused assets, but the game overall is very nice looking with an excellent style. I know this is an indie game in its purest form so it deserves some slack with some of the arenas feeling samey. For every area that looks similar there is another that is awesome though, there are some amazing set pieces here and there. I get the feeling that this game will get much more impressive visually as the dev gains more experience and begins to really go wild.The music is top tier, the sound design is excellent. The popping of cultist heads never stops being satisfying, the weapons sound as meaty as they should.Honestly the biggest downside at the moment, is the lack of content, the game clocked in about 3 hours for me to complete the first and only chapter. If you want an amazing top tier 3 hour experience and want to help support the dev, buy it now. This is a game to keep an eye on, I think it will be an instant classic similar to Dusk.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the game Blood 2 wishes it was.The game from start to finish is a spooky, action-packed thrill ride filled with blasting possessed cultists and creepy eldritch abominations for added bonus as you progress deeper into its macabre story. Unlike what you'd expect, the game doesn't have just one pace. It's interesting how often you'll be stuck in quiet, eerie scenes rather than action-oriented set pieces, which you wouldn't normally expect from an FPS game like this, but boy can this game get downright scary. There are some atmospheric set pieces that really instill terror and dread, which is kind of like Dusk's later levels. I'd keep your boom stick close in those moments if I were you.The music was my favorite part of this game, as well as the overall sound design. Both are absolutely top-notch and better than they have a right to be, honestly. Right out of the gate in the first level, I was head bopping along to the very well done soundtrack that's both adrenaline pumping and fear inducing sometimes. E1M1 and E1M3's combat music are just some of my personal favorites and good examples of this game's awesome soundtrack. Combined with really cool graphical (giblets and blood decals are hilariously gruesome) and lighting effects that set a dark, unnerving tone that in my opinion, manages to fill the void the original Blood left behind while also bringing some of its own creativity and ideas to the FPS genre. I cannot emphasize enough how well-made and fun this game was for such a small (basically one-man team) developer.Episode one is 10 levels with episode 2 coming out at a later date (for 10 more bucks I assume) so the story doesn't end after the climatic boss fight. Definitely worth the asking price if you're craving a really solid, fun retro throwback shooter that oozes atmosphere and creative charm.Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good inspired old-school shooter somewhat weighed down by the fact it is an inspired old-school shooter. The palette/shading is certainly evocative and moody but all that brown and blue and rust are sort of an... 1 + 1 + 1 = 1 situation. The environments of the 10 maps are indeed rather varied even though there's a thick blanket of that old school palette. No fault to the game though because  and it executes it well.The weapons and damage profile is the highlight here for me; everything feels beefy and full of impact (except perhaps the STEN SMG which feels... pretty meh all around). The bosses  were mostly (all?) damage sponges which... eh, fine, whatever. That's old-school, right?There's a story that's played through with sparse notes you can optionally read. I found them fine, even somewhat comical, but you aren't really here for a story, right?Some really nice set pieces in here, too! Some might classify a few as jump scares - I don't feel they were that "cheap" as most were highly telegraphed/foreshadowed. Some of the mob rushes got me and I lost a bit of progress due to not quicksaving (minor new-school complaint: I feel like auto checkpoints could've been a bit more generous, but "that's a skill issue" I suppose).Sound was good, music was... fine? Maybe a bit out of its element here and there; I did appreciate the . I encountered no bugs or slowdowns; you can probably finish this in 4 hours or less if you play more fast paced like a boomer shooter. If anyone wanted to argue I'd say this is not a boomer shooter as the way I played felt like I was being rewarded for being somewhat strategic in nature. There's a sniper rifle, might as well use it, right?Pick this up if you want a sepia-rust-toned shooter to work through in a day or across a few nights. You'll have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying that I really like this game, however I would like to clarify one point for potential buyers.A lot of reviews are calling this game very similar to titles like Blood and Dusk, and while that's true to a certain extent when it comes to aspects like the eerie atmosphere, the color palette, the setting and the simple, visceral excitement of holding a stick of dynamite and a lighter. However, for me Cultic doesn't feel that similar to the aforementioned titles when it comes to the actual gameplay loop. With a much greater emphasis on headshots and methodical approaches, Cultic feels like the more modern game here. And I don't mean the term "modern" as "better", but that there's simply a different flow to the core gameplay loop. I love both Dusk and Cultic equally, but they're fundamentally different games when it come to the actual gameplay.Or maybe I'm just playing it wrong. And if I am, I don't care, because I'm having a blast (pun intended).

_childDocuments_.review: Easily my favourite of the classic shooter revivals. It goes way beyond just paying tribute and really brings a fresh feeling to the genre through stellar art direction, modern controls and maybe the best level design I've seen in a modern fps. It is a linear classic shooter, but you can really feel elements of survival horror and immersive sim in here too which make it just so much more grabbing and atmospheric.It is a testament to what a one-man development team can achieve. There's a kind of consistent vision that makes this game incredibly magical. From the music to the gameplay, from the lore to the level design, everything just works so well together. The gunplay is unmatched. So crisp, so clean and with such a good arsenal of guns and movements, all of which really have their role. The gameplay feels very modern, and you really feel like it is a step up from the games that inspired it. The most magical part of this game though, is the level design. It is ridiculously good, with locations that feel real and grounded. Moving along is so intuitive, and figuring out which way to go is never a case of just walking till you're shot at. Instead, the game is full of environmental storytelling, blending together found notes and details in the environment to direct you. Every stage naturally connects to each other and yet feels varied. It's so good that it causes a sort of immersive state, where everything about the world feels real, and the (seemingly simple) story nevertheless grabs you. It took me about 6 hours (runtime 3:52 but had some restarts) to beat Chapter 1 and Interlude on Very Hard, and I just can't wait to see what's next. The recently added interlude really doubles down on the environmental storytelling, providing enough clues about the surrounding world to make you feel like Chapter 2 might very well take the storytelling and immersive elements to the next level.

_childDocuments_.review: Written from a perspective of a fellow FPS gamedev.short version: It is an absolute must playThe game was recommended to me by a friend, and at first glance, I was reluctant to pick it up because of sprite weapons and enemies. I'm biased toward full 3d games of the bygone era: Quake, Unreal, Half-Life, Return to Castle Wolfenstein, Soldier of Fortune, etc.However after giving it a fair fighting chance I fell in love with it, and totally forgot about my initial reservations. This game takes cues from all the great FPS-es of yesteryear, mixes it up and builds upon the industrial knowledge with immaculate taste and restraint. Playing through the game, I couldn't help, but to get reminded of all the games I played back then, plus many more, seeing their design spirit and philosophies implemented once more.This game is one of the best solo-dev games I had a pleasure of playing. All of the technical and design elements keep a rock steady, high quality bar, and I haven't encounter even one element, that would stuck out from this excellence.The storyline is a classic throwback to the occult themes of games like blood, doom, quake, or wolfenstein. The lovecraftian deep dive from harmless cultists through possessed metal patients, finishing up on demonic beasts from horror worlds. I just keeps getting more and more twisted and hellish.Wrapping up, I want to give a big hearty thanks for including my all time favorite: the FG42 (which I fell in love with long ago by playing Return To Castle Wolfenstein), and making it such a satisfyingly powerful battle implement.From one dev to another: Hats off. Games like these is why I wanted to work in this industry in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: A 2D stylized boom shooter following the styles of DOOM, Quake, and other such run-n-gun style titles. Players take control of a nameless cop who wakes up in a mass grave, as a conspiracy involving an ominous demonic cult begins to take control of the surrounding woodland. You can dash, slide, kick, explode, and headshot streak your way through each level in a variety of ways. Guns are varied and there is one for each niche of playstyle, intended to complement player movement and aligned targets (rifles, shotguns, pistols, explosives, etc). I particularly enjoy the art style, which is a grimy pixel nightmare filled with grotesque monsters and creepy cultists. The level layouts are fun and exciting, prompting players to find secret areas filled with helpful boons along the way. As the game currently is, its well worth the price, having some extra replayability for those looking to stretch their speed running and parkour skills.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely excellent ride!If you've always had a bit of a thing for 90s first-person shooters from a graphical point of view but shied away from their just-as-dated user experience: Cultic is your fix. It presents itself like a modern recreation of spoopy Doom-era retro shooters, but does so much more that I'm having issues putting retro anywhere near it. What I'd call it is an evolution of lofi aesthetics in every possibly way, crossed with the briskness of old shooters, modern sensibilities and just as many amenities to give you the best time possible.But let's break this down a little: Visually it gives you low poly, voxel, low-resolution sprites and tons of low-color palette / dithering shaders all at the same time. Put in motion, it's easily the most intensive expression of lofi aesthetics that I've come across in recent years. While not perfectly consistent all the time, you just can't help but love all the work that went into these details and spatial lofiness resulting from it. This is mostly for the sound as well: effects, ambience and music form a coherent whole and you'll immediately notice how everything in it has a distinct, well-designed sonic character. Gameplay wise, it feels and flows very much like a modern shooting game: smooth controls and UI, weapon customization, destructable and interactable props, flashlights, varied long and short range distance combat... you name it, it's somehow somewhere in there. Add a couple environmental puzzles, complex level structures, horror/suspense sequences, plenty of situational variation and you may get why I often felt more as if I'm playing a sort of Half-Life 2 or even Stalker demake.Overall, I really really enjoyed this game and I hope there'll be more to come in the next episodes/DLCs. Highly recommended unless you can't stand the whole occultism-yay-blood-everywhere kind of thing.

_childDocuments_.review: While CULTIC draws inspiration from Blood, it falters in key areas, notably the dynamite mechanic. Unlike Blood, the dynamite in CULTIC feels awkward and poorly executed. It lacks what made the mechanic shine in Blood.The shotgun, meant to be a staple, disappoints with an inexplicable lack of satisfaction in its usage. The upgrade system seems hastily implemented, failing to add depth or enhance the overall experience.However, the most glaring misstep is undoubtedly the mishandling of the dynamite. Its design is clunky and unsatisfying, a sentiment echoed throughout the Steam forums. It's disheartening to see such a pivotal gameplay element fall short of expectations.CULTIC attempts to pay homage to Blood but stumbles at nearly every turn. The effort to capture the essence of its predecessor is evident, yet it ultimately misses the mark. There's potential here, but it's overshadowed by the glaring issues, particularly the mishandled dynamite mechanic. Keep refining, developers; you're close, but this attempt falls short of the mark set by Blood.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This game is a SOLO project.  Keep that in mind.CULTIC is a masterpiece of which many of us were not aware or expecting: its legacy will be that of a solo project which, seemingly out of nowhere, took the "boomer shooter" market by storm, and will henceforth serve as the standard to which new retro FPS titles are compared. It is undeniably the best retro-styled FPS I have ever played, which inevitably rules it as one of the best FPS I have ever played, which is all the more impressive that it was created by one man.  Whether it's the soundtrack, atmosphere, story-telling, or gameplay, I must say that CULTIC has been even more of an enjoyable experience than the original Doom or Quake games, and surpasses even Amid Evil, Dusk, Nightmare Reaper, and Prodeus.  Priced at only $9.99 and with a run time of 4.5 hours (and don't let that playtime fool you: it's packed with action), this game is a must-buy, discounted or not.It's difficult to say exactly what the narrative is behind the protagonist, but you play as a man who finds himself delving deeper and deeper into a Lovecraftian cult hidden in the dark crevices of somewhere in northern North America.  The story is simple, and is presented to the player through journal entries which can be found scattered across the maps.  The further you progress, the more you will learn of how regular men became entangled in a cult promising them wealth and power, and what ultimately The Will is.CULTIC is a retro-style FPS.  This means that while it appears like a proper retro-FPS, it contains modern FPS features which set it apart.  There are crosshairs, headshots, charged melee attacks, throw-able objects, and weapon upgrades, as well as dodging, sliding, kicking, and reloading.  Many of the weapons have alt-fire modes, which allow for flexible gameplay.  At your side you can keep a backup medical kit to restore any health lost, and the pack can be refilled with smaller medical kits if your health is already full.  You can pick off distant enemies with your FG42 or lever-action rifle, slide in with your double-barreled shotgun, incinerate hordes with your flamethrower, or lead cultists into a dynamite trap.  It sounds rather simple but try out the demo and you'll see how well-paced and addicting the gameplay is.  Oh, and there's slow-motion following gory final kills.  Yes please.Enemies range from your generic cultists armed with pistols and hatchets to zombies, poltergeists, and even greater monstrosities that I won't spoil.  They are fairly accurate and will try to pick you off from a distance if they spot you, or blow you out of cover with explosives, but the game still feels like the most fair FPS I've played.  I died a few times, but never did I feel even slightly cheated like in Quake or any other game with those "gotcha" moments with demons appearing out of nowhere once I picked up a key: the enemies are in set locations, and for those few that ambush you, your gut will be expecting it anyway (those of you who faced those bony and "Medieval" foes already know what I mean).The maps, like most retro FPS games, are generally open-ended, with objectives being locked behind doors; other maps are more linear and progression is dictated by finding levers to activate lifts or destroy rubble blockages.  Games are saved through checkpoints and manual saves, with no limit on the latter with the exception that the game will not save during combat.  For a retro-styled FPS, this game looks amazing, but this is not due to its graphical fidelity (as in Amid Evil or the redone Quake), but its style.  My first impression from the screenshots was that this game looked rusty.  I wasn't entirely wrong, but once you play the game the rendering will put the screenshots to shame, and you will learn that this rusty, incandescent color scheme is perfectly fitting for the atmosphere and setting.  This game has its own visual appeal that many will find similar to Blood, and that includes the glorious gibs.  I would say the only shortcoming of the visuals is that the sprites of fallen enemies turn with the player, which can look rather goofy, unlike in, say, Prodeus, where there are several angles for enemy sprites.For those who have played the game already, many will agree that they instantly fell in love with the game's atmosphere when they fell down the pit in the first mission, and it's this consistent atmosphere in CULTIC that is rarely paralleled in most FPS games.  There's something about CULTIC's Lovecraftian themes which aren't forced or over-done like in most games of the same persuasion.  There's no otherworldly dimensions or over-the-top and extravagant, abstract atmospheres; rather, this game takes a laconic approach and makes familiar sights home to horror.  This game is honest about what it presents, which makes it all the more authentic, believable, and confident.Whether it's the crunching of boots in the forest, the splashing of brains from a lever-action headshot, the unintelligible invocations of cultists, the explosion of dynamite, the chopping of wooden crates with a hatchet, or the boom of your shotgun, the sound effects are brilliant, especially considering this was one man who made the game.  Better yet is the soundtrack, which ranges from creepy, pulsating dark ambient (I'm looking at you, flesh pit in mission 1) to memorable synth tracks (the best track in the game is arguably when the player first beholds the demonic rift in the sky).  The developer didn't need Andrew Hulshult for this retro FPS game: he alone made a soundtrack that fits perfectly with his game's atmosphere, and is easily one of the best soundtracks in an FPS game ever made.Like most retro-styled FPS games, the controls are simple.  You can remap all keys, which is basically a necessity.  You can access weapons through shortcuts or a weapon wheel which slows time down.  There are also separate keys for sliding and crouching, which some will find refreshing given how many games will tie these two commands to the same key.  Running an Intel Core i7 10th Gen and NVIDIA RTX2070 Super, the game ran smoothly for me at max settings, and I have a hard time imagining it would run poorly on most systems.  The only glitch I experienced was having my character get stuck in a wall during the mission with the tank boss (until getting nudged out by an enemy).  I experienced no crashes or freezes.  The game is stable.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey you… you like first-person shooters? Can’t get past the glory days of the janky 90’s? Oh boy, do 3D Realms and Jason Smith have a treat for you.Cultic is a classic shooter to the core that leans so heavily into its Blood influences I’m shocked Tchurnabog wasn’t the final boss. I can’t remember the last time I was as impressed with a shooter as I was with this one. But I love Blood, so maybe I’m being biased.GAMEPLAY & MECHANICSYou need to be a bit strategic, this game punishes mistakes, but in a way that always seems fair.It is responsive as hell, and when things die there is this really satisfying feeling you get from the shear gore, mixed with the sound that just makes it feel impactful.Enemies are nicely designed, heavily old-school horror film inspired, and make for a pretty good challenge. They can be a little dumb sometimes, but those moments often feel like you got lucky.Level design is impressive, even if some of the levels feel long-winded, and there seem to be entirely too many mines in this game (like goldmines, not explosive ones... but there are bear traps, so watch out for those).The weapons are what you’d expect from a shooter like this, pistol, fast-firing assault rifle, a precision rifle for some accuracy, lots of dynamite, so much dynamite, use the dynamite.Aside from the fairly lengthy 1 chapter campaign, there is also an endlessly enjoyable hoard mode.The environments are very interactable, its impressive how creatively you can make your way through levels.There are tons of secrets to find, and they always feel worth it.PRESENTATIONThe graphics are suitably chunky, meaty, but it works well with the setting, the art style is gloomy, tense, and filled with a sense of mystery and dread.The gore and blood are extremely satisfying. When you kill something, you don’t need to check, you know.Sound design is excellent. It’s not only really good at informing you about what’s happening around you, but it is oppressive, makes the gunfights satisfying, and works to polish off the 90’s shooter feel.The music is also quite good, the perfect addition to the scenes these tracks set.It's just so damn focused, nothing is out of place. Generally when a game is developed by a single person it takes some of the quality out of the game; but not with this one. It gives you a single, honed-in, tightly optimised and balanced little masterpiece. Good show Jason Smith, thank you for this one.

From the hatchet to the Sten gun, it's an utter joy to go through the levels murdering cultists. And the dynamite...good lord the Dynamite. Caleb's shedding a blood soaked tear it's that good. The music too is fantastic. Fits the tone perfectly well and does its jobNow i can't fully speak for the level design since  i've only gotten past the first two levels however from what i've seen so far it's great. Going from the garage to the wilderness to the cave in the first level was seamless and the progression and escalation was flawless. The easiest thumbs up i've ever given on this site bar none
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Blood?Do you like Build-engine FPS?Do you like challenging but rewarding gameplay?Exploration!Atmosphere!An amazing soundtrack!Amazing sound design!The first level took around an hour to complete!It's like a spiritual sequel to Blood, feels like the Build engine ramped up to 11, with an absolutely amazing dynamic style soundtrack, that evokes the feeling of a horror movie that will creep you out during a lot of the darker sections. Slow and careful over run and gun will be rewarded and mastering movement will save you a lot of the time. Warning: Addictive 'just a few more minutes' game play.Recommend good stereo headphones for the best audio experience. Brown pants moment [fave part]: Opening of "The Mine Town". Absolute pants filler.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: If you like retro shooters you'll be pleased with this, nothing ground breaking but good solid gameplay, What really sets it apart for me is the beautiful level design and the MUSIC. The music is a jam, I loved it. I don't think a game being a one man project makes it more or less recommendable but the dev did a great job, kudos man.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still early in the game, but I can already tell you this game is excellent. Great level design, fantastic and visceral combat, great horror atmosphere etc, this game has it all. I only wish the colour palette were not quite so brown. There is a lot of brown, so I hope you really like brown. Still, the gameplay is bloody fantastic and you should definitely play this if you like any shooters from the 90s.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game! I don't think I have ever been this excited to share a review of a game and I rarely ever do. From a lifelong gamer and a person spoiled with many options to play whatever game or platform I choose, this game really resonated with me and has landed a special place in my heart. I don't know if it is cause I am older now or because maybe I am over saturated with too many games that sometimes the joy of gaming gets diminished. How is it that I can play an Indie game made by one person and enjoy so much easier than some triple A title like gta or assassins creed? I don't know what it was about the retro style and the music (childhood, 80-90's nostalgia?) that drew me into it? Usually I would be looking for something with more modern graphics and realism.  It was so easy and enjoyable to just pick up this game and play for a session and get into this flow state. Thanks Jason for making this masterpiece! I think is a great example of how an individuals creativity and inspiration can make something so genuine and atmospheric. Opposed to something that already has this cookie cutter mold that corporations endlessly pump out.  Best $10 on gaming I have ever spent.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: CULTIC is a fantastic throwback FPS with heavy influence from Blood and similar pulp horror.The Good:+I'm not a fan of the color filter, but it can be turned off in the menus, making those gorgeous pixels shine.+Despite being mostly WW-era weapons, the guns feel punchy and brutal.+Buttery smooth combat enhanced by great sound effects.+Lots of game modes for different types of play.The Bad:-Currently only 1 chapter.-A few too many cultist-type enemies. I'd like to see some more horror creatures.-The movement is very smooth during combat, but becomes slippery during mandatory platforming.-Not a fan of the "mandatory" upgrade system.Bottom Line:I cannot recommend CULTIC enough, it is a fantastic FPS game that scratches a bloody itch. Moreover, at the full price it is still and absolute steal. And, if you still aren't sure. There's a great demo!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: The movement and gun-play felt great. Hit-detection on the enemies was forgiving for me, nailing head-shots and feeling stylish the whole way through.The antiquated design of the weapons and the achromatic color palette were enjoyable to me. I like the look of this game. Reminds me of something like  or , aesthetically. Fall-time, remote location, robed figures. Rust and rundown buildings. There's something comfy about it.Audio is great. The guns sound chunky. Most of the music were head-rocking, good jams. Some tracks, though, felt out of place for me. Could be due in part to them playing during some of the more circuitous, disorienting levels. Ones where I'd find myself combing the map, after having killed everyone, needing to find some switch in order to progress. But such moments were uncommon enough that it doesn't hinder my opinion of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: A great FPS with nice long levels that have great pacing. The game also has a killer soundtrack that suits the mood perfectly. The weapons are pretty standard but satisfying. Many of them have alternate firing and the game also has a simple upgrade system to give your weapons more of a kick. I beat the game on Hard in about 6 hours. I was looking around quite a bit and exploring for secrets so keep that in mind. Obviously the length of the game is going to be longer if you put the difficulty up higher. I'm guessing a standard full playthrough would range between 3-5 hours if playing on normal/hard. Definitely worth the money. I would have gladly paid 15-20 bucks for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. The gunplay feels superb, the level design is first class with very nice secrets and variety and throwing TNT into hoards of enemies until they are only mush never gets old.Combine all of this with the fact that this was developed by only one guy really says something. Not only about the skills from this developer, but also how damn bad today "Triple A" games with millions of budget are in comparison.I haven't finished the game yet, but others have said it is fairly short. Maybe, but for the price of 10 bucks this is really nothing to complain about. I'm really looking forward to the next chapters.If you enjoy singleplayer FPS games do yourself a favor and get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Good.For the price asked, its a solid FPS in retro style.You get a few hours of campaign plus an arena mode.The latter isnt to my liking, i prefer modes that alternate the main campaign, like ironman mode, New Game Plus, Randomizers or Mutators.Sadly, the game is void of any of that as of now.It offers a few difficulty levels though.Gunplay is good, visuals as well.Its a bit creepy and def. atmospheric.Going through it is fun.Yet ultimatively, while good, its not outstanding. Overall its a stylized version of Dusk, if we are frank.Hooded guys, Sawman dude, some supernatural thingies, a few zombies here and there.The setpieces arent original as well.Woods, Mines, Lakes. The way we have seen plenty of before. Thats basically it.It could be a mod for Dusk or any other 90s inspired shooter out there.I wished some aspects of the gameplay came with more of a twist and the gameplay itself had some more depth to it.Like upgrading your weapons the way "Forgive me father" does it, by branching off and coming with downsides.The lack of replayability through a lack of modes comes on top.So what is left if you scrap the nice visual presentation?Not a lot. Actually nothing any other shooter out there hasnt done far better.Yet, its a recommendation.Its good enough to stand its ground even though its "generic".But is it a masterpiece like the rating suggests?Not at all.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: The games a fantastic buy for 10$ especially for those who are into retro shooters. The game is tough like old school shooters that it totes to be music is pretty good too! All of the weapons feel like they have love put into them and ammo feels pretty scarce on higher difficulties. highly recommend the buy!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is a masterfully crafted retro-shooter, with a striking atmosphere and visuals. The gameplay is tightly executed, and blowing up cultists and making headshots never felt better. The Winchester Rifle is one of the most satisfactory video-game's gun to date. For its price, I wholeheartedly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is no Blood 2..Blood, Duke Nukem 3d, Shadow Warrior & Redneck Rampage are among my favourite classic games.I just found this boring.. stretched out levels with not much soul. gun play was dull, gfx style is also dull & music sucks.But I would say give it a shot.. you can always get a refund... I did.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best feeling and most lovingly crafted boomer-shooters out there right now. Levels are huge and highly-explorable, beautiful sprite design and chunky sound for weapons and enemies, and a pretty interesting detective narrative that takes a turn toward a more "Indiana Jones" type of vibe at a certain point. Very much captures the spirit of Blood and other classic shooters while still maintaining its own modern spin. Hopefully future episodes are just as good or even better than what we've already got. TLDR; Jason Smith absolutely deserves your money.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a big old-school FPS player, but Cultic has made a convert of me. It controls beautifully, the weapons all feel really satisfying (my personal favourite is the lever-action rifle) and have impact to them, combat can be hectic but not overwhelming, level design is solid, the soundtrack is excellent, and the art style is great. There are secrets dotted around most levels to find, and there are notes and journals that fill in some interesting backstory.And when you finish the main story, there's a survival mode to tackle as well.Definitely worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: The art style and atmosphere are top notch, as is the sound track. The levels feel like real places, with a lot of detail and weird nooks and crannies with hidden secrets. The environments are impeccably designed to complement the combat encounters - there are usually multiple ways to approach each scenario. There's a lot of long-range combat - the enemies' aim is very accurate, but so is yours. And the "sniping combat" is top notch. Close range is fun too, with the shotgun. The flamethrower deserves special mention - it may be my favorite flamethrower in any FPS I've played. It just feels really good to use - it has a long enough range to be effective without putting you in danger and there's enough ammo for it so that you can have fun.The AI can be a little weird at times, with bigger enemies getting stuck on things - but they'll also do stuff like kick your dynamite away from them.The hard difficulty felt perfectly balanced and fun for someone who enjoys FPS games regularly. There were a few parts where I was scraping by for ammo, but those situations forced me to regroup and try another approach with different weapons.Highly recommended. A must play for FPS fans.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: It's Blood meets RE4 and I'm so down for it.Music is thumping, weapons have punch and simply feel good to fire, enemy variety isn't bad, and the settings/set pieces are well thought out  and exciting. The horde mode is a nice addition for quick sessions after you've beaten the first chapter. Looking forward to the next chapters! Keep em coming!Hatchets make cultists go gibby-goo!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great and the developer knows what he's doing; he's cool ♥♥♥♥.The levels are varied and there's a lot of environmental storytelling; there's notes, cool vistas, and a sense of progression that permeates the entirety of the experience.The shooting is exceptionally well done, with headshots being brutal and weapons varied, they all have a ton of feedback and the game is pretty gory; there's even a cool effect that slows down the screen randomly when shooting at enemies heads, you can disable this if you want, but I personally find it really cool.There's also a ton of modifiers to customise your experience, from difficulty settings, to even the ability to fine tune the values of enemies health, aggression, speed, etc. It's really good.The developer is also quite attentive and answers questions in the forum regularly, he tries to help people whenever he can -which is quite often-, thankfully.The game is a bit short for now, but it's longer than your average COD campaign, with a heck of a lot more quality in its design and, it even has a ton replayability, I'm talking about some form of NG+ at the end, where you can play through the game again whilst keeping your equipment and weapon upgrades from the end of the game; stuff like this is really nice.I recommend getting the game whether it's on sale, or at a regular price; I think for what it is, the game is fairly priced, and the fact its made a singular guy seals the deal for me.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This is like if Blood and Resident Evil 4 had a baby. Its a glorious thing to behold.Crunchy voxels, abject pixel violence, killer soundtrack, amazing set pieces and level design, and a weapons roster that hits all four corners of the classic FPS formula. The only thing I ask for is more. A perfect blend of Survival Horror and Classic FPS elements. A high recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty much Resident Evil in the build engine. Really satisfying gunplay, pretty good enemy variety and fun levels. You can upgrade your guns which helps feel like you're making progression in addition to permanent health upgrades that are hidden in levels.I really liked how the secrets are all logical secrets. In a lot of build engine and retro shooters, many secrets are invisible walls or things similar to that. All secrets in Cultic you could for the most part, easily catch by eye or general curiosity.The game is priced well for the time spent in the campaign, it's clearly repayable, and there is a horde based survival mode.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic knows what it's doing, and knows it well. It distinguishes its well versed ideology in the topic of boomer shooters to the point that its clarity of vision isn't muddied by its earlier inspirations. It's elevated by them while offering something completely fresh. The combat is grungy, crunchy, and completely satisfying. Something that hasn't been experienced in this type of shooter for quiet some time.

_childDocuments_.review: very good Blood 2022 simulator.A excellent send up to a old classic and retro shooter fair in general though some veterans may find it easier than they may want.Weapon selection is top notch, alot of vintage classics (given that its taking place in what seems like the 70s it makes sense) and yet all of them are more obscure choices which is refreshing.Enemy variety is somewhat sparse but placed well enough where it doesn't become boring.level designs are top notch and while expansive don't get frustrating.The music is a real treat, with intimidating and menacing scores to go with some areas.I'm personally not a huge fan of the art design but it doesn't ever get in the way of gameplay and of course am already looking forward to episode 2 whenever that drops.All in all a great game and well worth its asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Great retro style shooter in the vein (no pun intended) of Blood. It also has a lot of neat little nods to other games and genres like survival horror. I got vibes from Resident Evil, Silent Hill, Blood, Doom etc. in some of the levels and enemies. Every level is well designed, the action is great fun. The guns...man they're so crunchy. That shotgun when you get a headshot and their head pops like a grape and you get that slowdown...just bliss. Highly recommended for shooter fans and retro gamers, and I can't wait for future updates from the developer.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best retro styled FPS games I have ever played. Cultic brings a great combination of gameplay, atmosphere, and story to the table. Visually it limits itself because of its retro style, yet these are some of the most beautiful visuals in a retro styled game I've ever played. While the game starts out slow, with the game giving you the most boring weapons first, a few levels in and you will love it! The combat is as smooth as slicing through butter or eating a very juicy peach. It's very fast-paced and feels perfect with the combat. There are (SEVERAL) really smooth and perfect combat sections throughout the game that feel so smooth, so fun, and the music makes it even more badass. And I'm talking even more badass than doomguy, because that's how well designed the combat is of this game. You are gifted a useful arsenal where every weapon can be useful in many scenarios, (even in late-game.) The story is more in depth than a lot of other games. You can read notes that inform you about many story related topics and also some filler. These notes are a little useful to the gameplay, (or at least in one scenario) where you have to read or skim a note to help you find a key. The main story is quite interesting and while it's not one of the main things that keeps you playing, it does add one to the fun and the theme. (I think story might be a lot more important in the next chapter, judging by how there's more story in the Interlude.) The game is one of few, that actually has the environments tell a story by themselves. In many other games, the environment gives a basic idea, but in Cultic the environments have every single detail in every single note.The music is great and makes a lot of moments, (like combat) so much more enjoyable and kick-ass. But it also does a GREAT job at adding onto the atmosphere of an area. Seriously, the music in Clutic is severely underrated!I would say the game is around 95% good, and the other 5% for a few smaller issues, but again, these are really small issues. In the ship level, I must've wasted over 30 minutes trying to find where to get a key, and they hid it in a hard to find spot. But if you run into the same problem, pay attention to the floor ;), but everything else is fine, if not awesome!Cultic is an awesome game inspired by retro graphics and older games, (like Blood, Doom, etc.) Cultic doesn't try to hide its inspirations, but Cultic itself is too good and too unique to call it a copy or anything like that. Cultic is an awesome game, and It's quite cheap! Seriously, if you have the money, go ahead and play it!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing shooter with homages to games like Blood, yet still being unique in it's own way.I could come up with all sorts of long drawn out points on its positives and take up a paragraphs describing the different things that make it so good but its best to try it yourself, it is outstanding and well worth it. A crime to miss out on this if you enjoy this style of game

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game yesterday on hard difficult, and it's a boner of a game damn very good combat, and after you get a taste for the controls and how to play properly on very hard is even better, the tight combat and the close calls you do and how you can react to certain encounters is always incredible I would 1000% recommend to any fan of boomer shooters, all the weapons are insanely cool and good to use, not even once I thought some weapon were underpowered or clunky/janky very good response on controls the level design is so good to play and most and damn this game have a lot of details and a unique visual, the music is also very good and fits everytime and everytime the music stops is always a good scare, I didn't read the story yet don't know much my superficial understand is that you have a cult trying to summon something and I need to kill them, also there are some references in this game that I really like and are very cleaver, a game that is created for fans of boomer shooters indeed 10/10.Just as an update I finished the game on very hard and yeah it still kick in so just buy it already
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is a rollercoaster of action and horror set pieces that interwine and change constantly in order to deliver a dirty, thrilling and bombastic journey in this god forsaken place.The art direction, while at first it may look just plain ugly (Specially in static screenshots) works extremely well in conveying the atmosphere and the tone of the game. In addition, it's surprisingly easier to spot far away threats, allowing the player to snipe from afar before getting in the fray of the combat.The soundtrack is amazing, goes from somber tones, dread tracks, upbeating sounds that push the player foward and some sections that are just pure ambience sound (Silence).The gameplay is meaty, the weapons pack a punch and the impact of the weapons is specially notable when popping heads, exploding enemies into chunks or burning everything into ashes while they scream. While the arsenal is certainly highly lethal and volatile, the enemies are not set too far behind in terms of power, they will shoot, throw explosives, throw back the explosives you throw at them... pounce at you and tear you apart in melee-range.The only two complaints I have are:-The swimming controls are weird, specially when I try to swim in the surface but the game just allows to dive while in the water.-The stairs feel slippery to walk/run through.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is an example that good games don't need to come from a big company to be amazing, the developer really has great potential.This game has everything, it's frenetic and spooky when needs to be, retro styled graphics like the 90's and a simple gameplay with some mechanic additions, the OST also is simply amazing.Can't wait to see the next chapters.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hyped from the moment I played the first demo of this game.  Blood by Monolith is one of my all-time favorite FPS games (mainly due to its level design and the majestic immortal voice of Stephan Weyte) and although I was late to the Blood party, it quickly rose to my upper echelon of FPS titles.  I wish there was a proper sequel done.  People said there was a Blood II, but I don't believe them, just like how I don't believe it when people say there was a POSTAL III.  Much like Dusk before it, CULTIC is the product of one developer, Jason Smith.  However, Jason takes it a bit further by not just designing and programming the weapons, art, levels, characters, and gameplay, but by composing the music as well.  It is clear that a lot of inspiration came from Blood, such as the hooded cultist enemies whose robe color indicates what weapon they are using, impactful weaponry that includes a powerful double-barrel shotgun, different armor types that protect against specific damage sources, and even the beginnings of their first levels, which involve the protagonists rising from their graves.  CULTIC differs from Blood in many other respects.  CULTIC has a stylistic limited color palette that may initially seem off-putting, but given the setting and theme, fits the game very well and Jason is to be commended for it.  Along with the palette is a low-fi and "crispy" assortment of sound effects that are satisfying to me, especially when running through grassy and gravel-paved areas.  CULTIC has headshots, and they are some of the most satisfying headshots I have ever seen in a videogame.  The dopamine rush from popping a line of zombie heads with a single well-placed Lever-Action Rifle shot rivals that of mowing down a group of Zombiemen in classic DOOM with a Super Shotgun blast.  Getting a headshot or explosive kill has a chance to trigger a short period of slow-motion like in Killing Floor.  I think this is helpful in heavy combat and for punctuating a big kill with a well-thrown bundle of TNT, but I can see how this could be a negative to other players.  The levels are excellently crafted and are aesthetically pleasing. Jason has designed expansive areas such as the Shipyard in level 2, the Asylum Grounds, and the Mining Town.  The game also has many creepy and unsettling areas, such as the beginning of the Mining Town level, the Crypts, and the interior of the Asylum (to me, asylums are perfect settings for horror media).  Most of the levels are fairly linear, but are designed in such a way to encourage and reward exploration through secrets and to just admire the scenery.CULTIC's weapons can be upgraded with Weapon Parts that are scattered around the levels.  Most upgrades are standard, such as increased damage, better accuracy, and increased fire rate, but there are a few unconventional upgrades, such as guaranteed slow motion for headshots with the Lever-Action Rifle's alt-fire and increased knockback with the Shotgun that can boost the player while jumping.  I think an alt-fire for the Grenade Launcher that shoots electric grenades that don't do as much damage as primary fire but stun enemies would have been a neat addition.  The traditional nature of most of the upgrades is not a major complaint, however.Besides the robed cultists, the game's enemy roster includes eldritch monsters like a fast, brutish behemoth and what can be best described as a fat gray creature with a vertical mouth that takes up its entire torso and long, sharp teeth that devastates your health if it gets too close.  To me, the most annoying enemy is the Ghost, a flying cultist covered in a white sheet with two eye holes who attacks by tekekinetically throwing objects at you, even if the Ghost is out of sight.  However, if the Ghost looks at you, it turns your screen red, shakes your view, and greatly slows you down while doing damage over time until you break line of sight or kill them.  The Ghost is not annoying in a bad way in that it serves as an effective horror enemy in cramped interior locations and as a dangerous support unit in large battles.  Just like in Blood, each enemy has a burning death animation in which they flail about screaming.  The screams the cultists make are not as iconic as Blood's "IT BURNS IT BURNS AGHAHAGHHAGH" but fire kills are still fun to execute.As if the main campaign, which spans 10 huge levels, is not enough, CULTIC offers a Survival Mode that is best described as single player Killing Floor done better.  You fight waves of enemies that increase in number with each wave.  Each kill earns the player money that can be spent on weapons, ammo, and other supplies at a shop between waves.  Survival Mode pushes the player's skills to their limits and rewards ammo efficiency and movement techniques.  Much like Dusk and Ultrakill, CULTIC has its own movement tech that greatly increases the player's movement speed through jump kicking.  I have put as much, if not more, time into Survival Mode as the main campaign.  Special mention has to go to how the game approaches its difficulty settings.  Jason has done an excellent job designing the skill levels, much like how id Software crafted the Ultra-Violence difficulty in classic DOOM.  Not only does enemy damage increase at higher difficulties, but enemy counts do as well.  This leads to a high-risk/high-reward approach to the game on higher difficulty settings, such as greater counts of enemies wielding shotguns, who hit very hard but have a chance of dropping shotgun ammo on death.  Another special mention goes toward the better-balanced cultists of CULTIC.  Although I like Blood, one aspect I think is BS is how its cultists, the most common enemy type in the game, have instant reaction times and can mow you down in seconds if you don't deal with them ASAP.  CULTIC's cultists (heh) attacks can be baited by darting in and out of cover and dodged in open levels by bunny hopping and sliding.  I cannot forget the soundtrack either.  It's very well done with heavy combat-appropriate rock songs, atmospheric pieces that go well with exploration, and creepy ambient songs that can fit right in a Halloween or Friday the 13th style horror movie.As if all the positives already mentioned are not good enough, CULTIC has a low price tag of $10 USD.  Jason could have charged twice as much and I would have no problem with it.  This ranks it among the best deals in gaming along with Vampire Survivors and The Orange Box.  This is only chapter 1, also.  If Chapter 2 turns out to be a separate purchase, I would have no problem with it as well.  Chalk up another excellent title in the retro FPS renaissance.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good though extremely short. "Chapter 1" should have been a dead giveaway. satisfying gameplay, good to nice level design, and one of the most useful flamethrowers I've ever seen in a game. But overall just good. Finished Ion Fury recently and I still recommend that for your first person shooter fix.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, but the level design could be a little bit better. The worst level I have ever played in the game is definitely the Crypts, unnecessary CQB (which is quite fine) and confusing areas as to where to go next especially the water areas in the map are atrocious. Last I checked water levels are the worst in most FPS, some do it great but Cultic kinda messed it up in the Crypts level. I do recommend Cultic, but I would only recommend playing Fallen Aces and Dusk before getting this game. Those games are a lot better in my opinion especially the open environment factor for Fallen Aces.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY enjoyed CULTIC. The atmosphere that this game creates is incredible and each level didn't feel repetitive. I played CULTIC on the hardest difficulty and If you buy this game I recommend you do too, It didn't feel overly difficult and added a level of challenge that was super rewarding and satisfying. I highly recommend you check this game out if you are a fan of boomer shooters or are just looking for a chill game to play in your spare time.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: very, very fun. with a lot of boomer shooters, something kinda feels off at the beginning. dusk, quake, half life, none of them are super fun to begin with. they kinda escalate as you get more weapons and understand the game better. not this game. this game starts at its peak, then stays there. it's a very headshot-heavy game. you can kill most common enemies with a single swing of your axe, as long as you aim at their neck to cut off their head. i feel like i didn't use the latter end of the weapons a whole lot, though. i kinda found myself struggling to use 45 dynamite, 29 molotovs, 15 grenades, and 150 flamethrower ammo when most enemies go down in one or two shotgun shots and i've still got 90 of those left.
