_childDocuments_.review: Unusual shooter. Not a straight remake of a 90's shooter, but clearly taking inspiration from earlier generations. A unique and enjoyable vision of mechanics and atmosphere.I'm going to do my own newgame+ where I increase the difficulty, but use cheats to give me all the weapons and upgrades in L1.Hopeful that chapter 2 will release soon, but I still need to try the free intermission level.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Very well done old-style FPS, with good modern mechanics thrown in. Very easily a recommend. The shooting is satisfying, the challenge is well done but not frustrating (I'm playing on Very Hard at the moment). People are commonly comparing this to Blood, and while there are some definite similarities/connections, I agree with the dev's stance that this game stands on its own. Mechanics such as occasional slow-motion with headshots, modern FPS movement, and even a weapon upgrade system help differentiate it as its own game. Just an FYI, according to recent discussion posts on the matter, you are buying Chapter 1 in its entirety, which the dev's estimated to be 4-5 hours of game time (not including the survival mode). There is a Chapter 2 planned, but that is currently being planned as a separate, episodic release that you will have to pay for in addition to this. That's the model they are going with. I, personally, do not have an issue with that. They've priced this just right for what it is, and I am happy to do the same when the next chapter comes out. But, some might take issue with that, and I feel it should be worth making that information available so people can make a more informed purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: (My friend got this for me as a gift, but I was going to buy after my next paycheck. Thanks bud!)One of the best "classic shooter" throwbacks I've played in a long time!I hesitate to call it a "Boomer Shooter", you are not this speedy indestructible force, you won't be tripping over ammo (until the last 3/4's mark) this game is challenging, you will die frequently in the beginning; you need to be precise with your shots if you want to survive.I almost want to compare it to Resident Evil 4, but you move a bit more deftly than Leon does and the game plays like "classic shooter" of the golden age of 90's FPS's.Oh yeah I almost forgot; the music slaps!The first chapter took me 3sh hours on my first go.This game is not to be missed!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: A sweet but short game, Cultic is a boomer shooter that pays good homage to games that came before it such as Blood and Doom, taking inspiration from the more recent trends within these sorts of shooters by making the gameplay brutal and smooth. The art direction and sound are great, and the music is good, which lends well to the almost horror feel of the game especially when you enter locations that are dark and hear the music stop.Overall I don't have much negative to say about the game other than that it is short. I beat the game after 4 and a half hours on hard difficulty, but it was an enjoyable experience all the way through.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Im only one hour in and i can already tell its a blast. Once you get used to bindings and movement of this game, its so smooth. Also secrets (at least 1st map) didnt feel like i had to go out of my way to find every single one, not the type of go to this wall press e kind of thing. The headshots in this game are prob my fav feature so crisp and clean. Im def satisfied with what i got for this little money.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: There's one minor detail that speaks about the design philosophy behind this game; the doors.If you hit the use key on a door it opens slowly, giving you time to peer in and snipe anyone you see inside. Alternatively, you can kick the door open instantly and go full aggression mode, if you're lacking in patience.This reinforces the core idea of "play your way", with both slower and methodical play and fast-paced blitzkrieg action being entirely viable, as long as you have the ammo for it.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Any game with hauntings is good in my opinion.Okay, but seriously, this game is really well put together. I like a lot of the levels; the atmosphere is great. Every weapon is useful in some capacity. Only really ran out of ammo for everything once. Hoping there's more to come. I really appreciate the feature to turn off the color filtering and dithering.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This game was extremely enjoyable, the fact it was made by mostly one man. There is more substance here then games with full studios with million dollar budgets. The best way i can describe it is almost like medal honor or return to castle wolfenstien mixed with blood. Very Gnarly. Very cool. great sound and art. Just a fun game, probably worth more then the asking price. Will be waiting for chapter 2
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review just after finishing the game, and I must say that it's quality it's mind blowing considering how cheap it is. I played this game because after playing Ashes Dead Man Walking and Afterglow, I needed a little bit more of the retro genre in my life. Games like these not only show how important art direction is, but also they set an example of what a one person project is capable of achieving. I played the game in hard, and I am very happy with its learning curve and the difficulty of the game. The gunplay is pure satisfaction, though I think the game could've benefited from having a revolver available on its arsenal. Still, this is only because I am biased towards them, the guns available to you are nothing short of fun to use, and during my walkthrough I found myself using all of them.The story is interesting enough to give you a reason to read the not-so-many notes scattered around the map, and requires attention and imagination from the player in order to grasp how truly horrofying the situation you are in really is. Still, it's more of an action FPS than a horror game, and it manages to find a good balance between those 2 to make the world you're find yourself in makes sense.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Blood was my first game ever, so Cultic got my interest right away, obviously. And I think it does a great job of capturing that Blood atmosphere, gameplay, explosions, fear, cool weapons and interesting level design. It's mindblowing that Cultic is being made by one guy only - Jason, you da MVP! Cultic is also the first game in my Steam library that I bothered getting all achievements for - that's how much I enjoyed it. I can't wait for next chapters - I hope they will change the scenery a bit. Maybe something snowy or more city-like? Only Jason knows for now.I do wish the Survival mode got some tweaks here and there, though. I didn't like the timer in between the waves. It serves no real purpose other than stress the player and not give him an opportunity to really brace himself for the next challenge. And this mode is REALLY tough, too! Partly because it's so rare for enemies to drop some real cash... I didn't enjoy it as much as normal campaign, although I like the idea of it. Upgrading weapons, looking for old school secrets, popping enemies' heads and just taking in the unsettling vibe of the game - that's Cultic for ya! Grab it and play the hell out of it, you won't regret any second of the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: While short (3-5 hours), Cultic brings sleek, fast gameplay for you to enjoy, plenty of secrets for you to explore, and an incredible soundtrack that helps to draw you in.Through the aesthetic presented and the simplicity of gameplay, Cultic is a fantastic experience and wonderful homage to a bygone era of PC gaming. Many compare it to "Blood" from decades ago.  I had never experienced "Blood", so for me this has been more reminiscent gameplay wise of Duke Nukem 3d (though Cultic is much more refined).  A decent selection of weapons is at your disposal, though they don't have a ton of variety (axes, dynamite, pistol, lever action rifle, shotgun, etc). There is a weapon upgrade system available to add some variety as you play and gather weapon parts (which you can often find in secret areas).Beyond the core story gameplay, there is a survival mode available to help with the replayability aspect of the game.  There are also several difficultly modes available to choose from, so Cultic can be an enjoyable experience or challenge for whoever wishes to give it a go.At times surprising in how creepy the game can get, Cultic maintains an overall dark tone with little humor, but oozing with atmosphere.   I will be updating this as I play more, but from the time spent before release and now, Cultic is a surprise hit this year. Do yourself a favor and pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: CULTIC joins the pantheon of the Boomer Shooter renaissance.It may look like BLOOD at a quick glance but it has more to offer than that.CULTIC is a really well polished, and extremely satisfying shooter.The atmosphere is oozing with personality.Think BLOOD with a pinch of Resident Evil 4, a dash of DUSK, and a hint of other Horror Shooter aromas. If you are in anyway a fan of the FPS genre you should definitely grab this.Well done Jason you knocked it out of the park. Looking forward to the rest whenever it comes out.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: So I beat this game the same night I bought it. I never really played Retro FPS games but this game was super dope. The movement is fluid and the weapons are pretty fun to use. My favorite is head shots with the lever action. Im strictly FPS and Battle Royale games. I play the occasional story mode game. I recommend this game to anyone looking for something different!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome retro shooter, not much to complain about, good length, has even some stuff to do after beating the game, lots of secrets and the usual stuff. I guess I miss some of the things that made Blood an awesome game such as weird weapons and the enemies, that's the one thing I'd definitely think about if there's more content or a second part one day, a bit more variety when it comes to enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic game of exceptional value. remarkably developed by a single man?crisp and fluid combat controls, generous weapon and enemy assortment, distinctly varied environments, crunchy sound design with wonderful backing tracks and deeply caramelized visuals. surprisingly lengthy in its run.if that isn't sufficient there are plenty of difficulty settings, hidden secrets and an alternative game-mode to keep replayability high.easily the most straightforward purchase on steam at the moment
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Gib someone, pick up their eyeballs, yeet said eyeballs at another enemy, get an achievement10/10Played the demo awhile back and liked what was on offer, that was the tiniest of tastes for what was in store. It's a boomer shooter with an excellent horror atmosphere a-la Blood that feels fresh and punchy. If any of those words mean anything to you, you've probably already bought it. For anyone else, you should also buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Very immersive and fun boomer shooter, guns feel good to use, graphics/art style is lovely and fits the theme quite well, it's very immersive in the sense that there's legitimate moments of creepiness within the game, nothing overwhelming, but it did  make my heart race a bit on medium settings. Overall I clocked in about 9 hours and some odd minutes casually strolling through the game, dying a bit, and exploring. I also wanted to mention that while this isn't a HUGE focus there is a story, a lot like DOOM 2016 where you can either skip it and ignore it but honestly finding the little notes about what was going on overall and the events unfolding through the perspective of other characters who were there before me along side the environmental storytelling did A LOT to immerse me in the game.  It's interesting reading someone slowly finding themselves over their head through notes, only to see a skeleton or mutilated body as the result of the end of their journey.  Can't believe this was all (mostly) made by one dude, most def one of my favorite games of this year.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: What a literal phenomenal experience! Thank you so much Jason! You really recreated the magic of the classics and I felt like a kid again. Would love to hand you millions and get a sequel. Looking forward to anything you do moving forward. If you need a voice actor for the next one let me know!  So much detail into everything - everything felt so satisfying. I can't believe this is just you who did this. It is a tour de force!PS If you click fps and then click show highest rated... Scroll down and you will see that Cultic is RIGHT UNDERNEATH BLOOD!!! Congrats!!!!I swallow your soul!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic: Chapter One is an impressive game and even more so when you realize it was all done by a solo developer. It is a fun shooter with most importantly shooting that feels good. As you progress through the story you get more weapons that helps keep the combat fresh. The visual style is great unique and a throwback to older shooters on PC. The music pairs well with the aesthetic. The game took me about 5-6 hours to complete and I am very much looking forward to chapter 2 whenever that comes out.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is getting a ton of credit as a kind of spiritual successor to Blood, and it really earns that comparison, but that isn't all that the game does. I felt the DNA of the past thirty years of shooters wrapped up into this thing, taking something and learning from every major leap that the FPS has gone through to create a real love letter to the genre. It's got Doom and Blood and Unreal and Half Life all over its level design, but also the whip fast speed of a more modern shooter and the intensity and rhythm of the 2016 Doom and Eternal. I even found myself regularly thinking about Alexander Brandon's work on the original Deus Ex while bouncing my head along to the excellent score. I almost can't believe that this whole game came from one dude, and I can't wait to see where Jason Smith goes next. An absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast. Hugely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a rock solid game. Great graphics, interesting story, awesome sound design, good soundtrack, an awesome atmosphere, and the gameplay OH THE GAMEPLAY. SO great, can't recommend enough. Plus it's TEN DOLLARS, seriously a few hours of great retro shooting that soulfully recreates old school build engine, but adds on in small ways that makes the game so fluid and amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: What a lot of "Boomer shooters" and old-school shooters get wrong, this game does right. Between the beautiful art (music and pixel work) and solid mechanics and maps, this game has a lot to offer in it's first chapter alone. I can not wait to see what else these guys cook up.P.S. You can kill enemies with eyeballs.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Incredible SP campaign that takes a lot of ideas from modern fast-paced shooters, and incorporates them into the sort of level design that makes Build shooters like Duke and Blood a classic. The Survival mode seems like it gives it infinite play value, although it would be nice to see a daily feature. One note: Hard seems a lot more like Medium in other games, and I've heard Medium is pretty easy. Huge recommend if you like the modern Doom games, DUSK, or classic Build games.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: when i found and threw soap at someone to instantly kill them like dusk is when i realized i would love this game. it was much more than i was expecting it to be both content and length wise, and yet it never dragged on, only for the end to eventually come and then learn that there will be another episode in the future. the music is such a great part of the experience and the freedom in encounters is very fun, being able to snipe from a distance, engage in close quarters, just blindly throwing hatchets, molotovs and dynamite everywhere, or going the route of just punching everything in the face so hard it explodes. will absolutely be going back to try and beat the game on extreme difficulty, and later when there's a new episode to play through.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished a play through of the MONOLITH classic BLOOD, a friend recommended I check this game out. I have not been disappointed! The levels are impressively designed, typically taking me ~45 minutes per map to destroy most enemies. The custom difficulty is great, allowing players to really fine tune their play through. Make it as simple or brutal as you want to. This game doesn't hold your hand - it expects you to explore, follow the trail of your dead, and try to survive to get through to the next map. While I wish there were some nice-to-haves like a minimap or 3rd person view, I don't mind that they're not around. Survival mode is cool. I hope that they give us some more options to tweak that a bit. This is a fantastic game that is definitely worth your time if you love old school FPS with horror & occult themes.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: The easiest and best way to describe this game as a 37 year old fps player is a really tight, really solid, really smooth, enjoyable experience.Cultic is a single chapter game, but is priced accordingly, which as a start is massively refreshing in a gaming world of early access.  The game really does feel like a labour of love for the dev and this transfers subsequently for us players, playing the game.I highly recommend this game, it is right up there with Amid Evil, Dusk, Ion Fury & Prodeus as the benchmarkers in this new wave of boomer shooters.10/10 - Buy it
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: A *must play*. I grew up playing Apogee/3D Realms games, and Cultic somehow managed to hit all my nostalgia buttons while also delivering a superior evolution to all core elements of the retro boomer shooter.Things that stood out:-The excellent level design, which tells an ever deepening story via the atmosphere and design itself-The head shots-The impressive use of voxels-Secrets galore-Abundant use of dynamite-Head shots!-Impressive boss battles (for this engine especially)-Meaty, satisfying weapons-The fact that this whole game was made by one person!-HEAD. SHOTS.As many have said, this is a true spiritual successor to 1997's Blood. My kid self is happy, my grown up self is happy. Win win. Can't wait for episode 2.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. If you're looking at it, you're most likely a fan of the genre -- this scratches every boomer shooter itch I've had. Coming from Duke Nukem, Blood, Shadow Warrior, and Ion Fury this game stands shoulder to shoulder with giants for me.I love the mechanics, they're all very fun and clever. The gameplay is fast-paced and fluid. The graphics are incredible. I love what the dev did with the palette, and it's dripping with style.All in all, I'm barely an hour in and I love this so far. I completed the first level, and took my time to take everything in and look for the secrets, which there were several! I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid mix of a modern retro shooter with survival horror elements.Cultic excels in atmosphere and the pace of its combat and exploration. All levels in the game have an excellent length and a more open level design compared to their peers, exploring and searching for secrets is excellent, shooting has satisfying feedback and has some degree of depth which mastery is essential for playing on higher difficulties (And at the same time, it's not so fast and demanding that it sends you into the realm of tendonitis), the balance of ammo and resources is sharp, and the horror narrative is efficiently integrated, elevating the experience to something beyond just another shooter trying to copy games from 20 years ago.The lowfi/modern aesthetic evoking games from the DOS/PS1 era (While it doesn't look like anything that existed in those days) is also interesting, giving a grungy and rustic texture to the game while conserving the legibility of the scenarios and enhancing the silhouette of enemies. It's not exactly a beautiful game, but it has a lot of nostalgic charm and there's no visual clutter. It is efficient and well produced. And the soundtrack does not appeal to the current clichés of generic heavy metal riffs, opting for more ambient and dark moody tones (Which is not to say that things do not get intense). I was quite surprised.Anyway, Cultic it's simply a very well put together game and a satisfying experience. It's a game you'll want to come back to again and again simply because it feels so good to play.  It's everything you'd expect from a game like this and a bit more. Enough to justify the purchase.A must-have addition for anyone who enjoys the genre. Just play the demo, i'm sure you'll be convinced.PS: Everything works fine, although I have had occasional framerate issues for some obscure reason. If that bothers you, maybe some research is in order.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: It is a lot of fun. The fast pace and high tension is incredibly engaging, the horror elements massively compliment the atmosphere, and the gameplay is incredibly satisfying. Though chapter 1 isn't amazingly long, it's replay value is driven by how fantastically entertaining each level is. Thanks for making this game
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Of all the ' boomer' shooters I've played so far I enjoy Nightmare Reaper and Cultic the most (still waiting on systemshock and serlaco). Cool environments and nice explorable maps, great movement (if a little bit slow if you want true retro fps style) and cool punchy guns. (go for the headshots, it'll make your life alot easier)It has the retro vibe down to a tee wile still having its own style. Difficulty is good on hard and haven't found any bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This game was excellent. I'm not someone who usually plays shooters, but this game's artstyle and gameplay in the demo really piqued my interest. Now that the full game is out, I can't recommend it enough. The levels are really varied, especially the last couple. The secrets are quite good too. As a newbie to shooters I was able to make it through comfortably on the Standard difficulty, may have to give it another go on a harder difficulty soon enough. I think the best bit is the atmosphere though, you can tell a ridiculous amount of work was put into the small details, like when you get up to the enemy camps on top of one of the levels and there are mattresses for them to sleep, and one even has a teddy bear. All from a solo dev too, kudos to ya!I give it a: Copious Amount of Hatchets / 10
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Had mixed feelings about the game.Performance wise most of the time it worked well, but it would drop down to 50-70 at times on certain levels, and the game felt more sluggish at those times. I have a 6700 xt, so should be able to run this game with no issues.Maps were also a mixed bag, sometimes were confusing on where to go. The general atmosphere was pretty nice. Graphical wise, it was an interesting art style, but the color grading was hard to look at at times, especially in the darker areas. I've played plenty of actual older games and homages to them, so it wasn't that.The weapons were fun to use, very nice flamethrower for instance. Some of the enemies were fun to fight, but with the amount of damage you take, them being all around you with almost perfect aim didn't help staying alive. Some enemies like the chainsaw guy were quite annoying as if you got too close, you couldn't dodge or get out of the way, so if he caught you, you were dead unless you managed to do enough damage. Having basically every enemy have a ranged attack made it so there wasn't really much variety. Having a combination of melee and ranged would have been more interesting, as even the melee ones always had some ranged abilities, so there wasn't much point in getting close to the enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Another fantastic addition to the boomer shooter genreControls are really tight, gunplay is fun and rewarding and the map design is *chefs kiss* with it both looking believable and lived in while also giving you great places to maneuver in both combat and in map progression. Only one map gave me a sense of "I have no idea where I'm going" but I feel that was the purpose of the design. A little on the easy side for veteran boomer shooter players, but still definitely something to experience with the environmental story telling being interesting enough to have me reading diary logs.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this for a while, and while other indie games have let me down this one definitely did not.Some of the best level design I've seen in a while, notably Mine Town, Shipyard and Asylum but every level had something unique to offer.Really smooth movement and satisfying gunplay.  The environments and art are also really cohesive.  The game is drippy with style.  I especially enjoyed how you can interact with a bunch of little things in the world.Only complaints are sometimes the music gets a bit repetitive and doesn't quite fit the mood (in some of the intense action areas)  And fire (from lamps/molotovs/flamethrower) makes almost all big non-boss enemies irrelevant, but when using a gun they are bullet sponges and take forever to kill.  The handgun also becomes a sniper rifle with the damage/accuracy upgrades, I feel like there should be some damage falloff at long range.  Some of these balance issues could definitely be because I played on standard difficulty, they might be less of an issue on higher difficulties.9/10, one of the most enjoyable games I've played this year, REALLY excited for Chapter 2 in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Retro FPS with heavy influence from classics like BLOOD and Doom but with modern movement mechanics (sliding, dodging, etc), Absolutely killer atmosphere that effortlessly switches between fast paced shooter and slow paced horror, great enemy design and sound effects, good story, great visuals, and an awesome final boss.An unbelievable steal for only $9.99.9.5/10 - Can't wait for chapter 2.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: On the higher difficulties, this game is an awesome combination of boomer shooter design with action-horror design. The influence from RE4 and Blood are very clear, yet on higher difficulties, this feels like a game with an identity all its own. I recommend it, having played it a lot pirated before buying it. It's a gem that manages to satisfy both my boomer shooter desires and action-horror itches.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Wow what a great game this was. The atmosphere, music and level design are all top notch and the weapons all feel great to use (this was the first FPS game where the Pistol is actually my favorite weapon). For a game made by one person the quality is insane and it is a great tribute to Blood. I hope the dev adds some kind of New Game+ mode to keep upgrading weapons :) highly recommend and super hype for Chapter Two!!!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Rough around the edges, its main strength is mostly having some incredibly well designed visuals and audio direction that makes everything feel fun to fire and kill. The game isn't very difficult, mostly relying on cheap traps for a cheap death. Ammo for certain weapons felt a little bit sparse, TNT feels powerful but the throw feels weak and hard to gauge, movement is a bit weird but can be adapted to, weapon upgrading feels like a frivolous addition that doesn't warrant appearing, secrets feel satisfying to find.Not the greatest FPS ever released as anticipations would have suggested, but a completely solid FPS with a few hang ups here and there.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another boomer shooter? Yeah, but at the same time, nope. Cultic isn't a simple Doom clone, it's an amazing experience that takes a good amount of inspiration from Blood, but adds so much more that it becomes its own twisted thing. Visceral FPS combat, punchy weapons, exceedingly well designed levels, enemies that are fun to fight, the list goes on. This is the real deal, pure raw first person shooting fun of the highest caliber.Still here? Run to the store and buy it, you fool!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game that will remind you of 'Blood' back in the good old days of classic 90s fps.PROS: NostalgiaNice visualsGreat soundCONS:Some very poorly design platforming partsControls could be better, make use of the space bar to dodge instead of double tapping which often occur in unwanted moves.7.2/10
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This is simply an amazing game. Feels old but modern at the same time, shooting is precise, and there are tons of secrets to discover at each level. Map design is pretty good too, you never feel too lost but you can always explore different areas of the map. I didn't like the color palette at first but it grew on me as I played the game.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game's early access release, or full release forever. it is now one of my favorite FPS shooters of all time. There is absolutely a lot of stuff in this game that makes me feel like I'm playing a newer remade BLOOD, and that's a good thing. If you have been around playing boomer shooters since Wolf3d, or just got into boomer shooters, this one is the king. I put it up there with Dusk, Amid Evil, and Iron Fury. GET IT NOW!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent boomer shooter revival here. The secrets are not cryptic or boring and keep up with the pace of the game. The game tells you the story as fast as possible and its optional to even read it! No stupid lore ruining the momentum of the game. It even has a survival mode and the upgrade mechanics of the game's weapons fit perfectly into both modes. Secrets are very rewarding. The game's movement feels modernized which may be good for people that are new to the old style. Please turn off the double tap to dodge it will get you killed. I finished the game on the second to the last difficulty. It's also not too long of a game as well which is great because you can improve your times if you are interested so it does have some replay value. It is priced very fair for how much it offers. This game continues in the tradition of "game play before lore" which is part of why boomer shooters are great, the game also has some great creepy atmosphere going for it. Love the ambient music when I heard it but I didn't hear enough. If you change your controls you can abuse the slide mechanic for some fast level clears. If you are still looking for more reviews to help you decide allow me to help. If you see "game too hard" "ran out of ammo" "bad story" "game is too short"simply move on to the next review.Again I played on the second to last difficulty my 1st play-through and only ran out of certain ammo near the end. It might not have happened if I used more explosives in the right places. It took me a little over 6 hours and I looked up about 4 secrets because the pace of the game was fast and fun, I found the rest on my own!If you don't like a feature there is probably a check box to turn it off! I disabled the slow mo kills, I am not a fan of newer game mechanics in my boomer shooters. Excellent features for controller as well for even more old school feel. Final boss is lame af, (but very fast killable). The game designer must think bed of chaos is good game design... (its not). Also the music goes silent a lot when you are not in battle so it makes looking for that last secret very quiet. I was expecting more enemies but I haven't tried the final difficulty. A job well done, congraturation!!! This story is hapy end!!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Very, very good. I went on a kick of trying a ton of retro shooter demos, and I found a wealth of incredible games. Of those, I was sad to see only one was available for purchase immediately, but if I had been made to choose, it would have been CULTIC anyway. There's so much inherited here from legacy titles, especially Blood, but in my opinion CULTIC blows the old measure of games away--it truly is a modern successor, with a new engine, and some of the best controls and shooting on the market.I was under the misconception that the demo of the game covered most of Chapter One, that my $10 purchase (at full price mind you) was going to go towards maybe the first and second levels. It should tell you everything you need to know when that was still a good deal to me.But there's more; a wealth of levels, enemies, and weapons, with a tense horror atmosphere and fun, balanced gameplay the entire way through.I cannot recommend this game highly enough, and have myself joined the legions of people waiting on the next chapter. If you are reading this, I can only assume you have even the slightest interest in this game, and I can safely say that if you've been drawn in by the look and feel and need any further word to dive in, then do it. You will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: A good game with a high level Bitcrush aesthetic. All the gameplay aspects are really top notch aside from enemy AI. While enemies are smart enough to walk down staircases, they otherwise just go towards you, get stuck in water, and have really good aim (maybe the good aim is a "hard" mode thing). You eventually learn how to game it but it feels like a cheap solution. The story does pull you in, but the direction after Chapter One is extremely disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best retro-revival shooter I've played to date. It nails everything that was great about classic FPS games, while managing to work in modern touches that never feel out of place. Weapon upgrades as a reward for finding secrets is a smart and very welcome touch.There's little humor, which works just fine in this setting. Though the atmosphere is dark, I think it walks the line between heavy-handed and campy pretty well. The story is serviceable, doled out in "logs" scattered throughout the world. It's so minimal that even seasoned FPS-lore-ignorers will probably find themselves reading them. Besides that, everything that's not central to the story of you, John Cultman, killing cultists, is stripped away.Visuals are excellent. The voxel art is interesting, the use of shaders underneath all that retro filter jank is impressive, and the spritework is very good.CULTIC's gameplay is the star of the show. Movement is fast and not over-complicated. Enemies are fun and challenging, without ever being unfair. Only one enemy is "hitscan", and their attack has a timer before it damages you. The gunplay is intensely satisfying. All the weapons feel powerful, sound great, and fulfill unique needs perfectly. I found myself switching between most of the weapons very often.My only nitpick is that movement has a weird "weight" to it that caused me to walk off a lot of staircases and walkways. Like, alarmingly often. Not too bad given everything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this one blew me away. I played the Demo for CULTIC before release and thoroughly enjoyed my time with the first stage. The full release (at least, chapter one) does not disappoint. The level design here is fantastic. You'll want to take your time to uncover all the secrets, which are sometimes tricky to locate but never frustratingly so. Gunplay and movement is suitably responsive, chunky, impactful, and just plain satisfying. But by far the best part of CULTIC is its aesthetics and inspirations. Cultists wield strangely familiar shields, (like the castle ganados in RE4), areas are appropriately gloomy and atmospheric, and the storyline conveyed by notes and journals is simple but full of campy fun. I also feel that the upgrade mechanics provide a bit of replayability (apart from replaying stages) providing for specialization in different weapons. My only serious con is that by the end of chapter one some of the surroundings begin to feel a bit samey: similar color palates of earthy browns, green, and grey muddle things a bit. But it isn't so bad as to kill my enjoyment of the stellar gameplay and environment. If you enjoy games like DUSK, DOOM, and, of course, Blood, you will enjoy CULTIC. You might also see shades of Bioshock here with the mixture of linear and open level design, weapon handling, and a sense of being in an otherworldly place. The price point is just right--what are you waiting for.

_childDocuments_.review: I went in expecting Blood, but this is so much better due to the lack of hit-scanners. Level design is very open with long range options available, making it extremely satisfying to slowly pick off enemies. The Re4 influences, surprisingly effective horror segments, satisfying/varied weapons, incredible headshot pop, fun to use dynamite/explosives, all contributed to me wanting to keep playing. Nothing beats Doom Eternal, but this is up there with the kings of the boomer shooter genre like Dusk & Ultrakill. I eagerly await Chapter 2.

I won't even get into the excellent execution of aesthetic combining sign-posted sprites with voxels and 3d environments. All of this amazing game in a low $10 package from a solo dev. _childDocuments_.review: A very pleasant surprise, this boomer shooter inspired by Blood (and Resident Evil 4 to an extent) and developed by one person manages to impress quite a bit. First off, the art-style is extremely effective and helps create an eerie, immersive atmosphere, worthy of the occult. Joining the visuals is a really good soundtrack that keeps you engaged while fighting and wary while exploring the abandoned asylums and ruins. Subtle and creepy sound effects also accentuate the horror, but rarely, so that, when it happens, it's extremely memorable and impactful.The level design is also great, the levels fit together logically giving a surprising sense of place to the environments you're exploring. The secrets are well hidden and fun to find and the locations' design helps keep you moving while you mow down cultists. Said cultists are not that varied and are only joined by a handful of supernatural entities, two of them which are just brutes, but considering the one-man team, I'd say it's not that big of a complaint. Hopefully chapter two brings more variety here.The weapons are pretty typical, but feel good to use. Shotguns maybe lack some punch, but the sniper is super fun to use and compensates for that. There are also some pretty useful movement mechanics to help you along the way. You can slide, dash and roll after a fall from height and it all feels snappy and fun to use. You can also kick enemies and throw objects at them, which is also good fun and can get you out of some tricky situations. Mechanics are topped of with an upgrade crafting system for weapons which incentivizes you to explore for secrets even more and it all mixes really well to create a must-play for boomer shooter fans.

_childDocuments_.review: CULTIC. It's CULTIC, what more can I say?CULTIC is a single developer Retro FPS game by Jason Smith that absolutely stands out as one of the finest FPS experience in recent memory. Taking control of a retired detective, you'll fight your way through a vast cultist menace, use a variety of solid and satisfying weapons, and throw absolutely everything not nailed to the ground and MORE. CULTIC, much like earlier Retro Throwbacks like DUSK, knows that people who plays these kinds of games most likely understand the basic structure of a Retro FPS title and proceed to subvert expectations by adding things never before added to create a absolutely fantastic experience. Gameplay of CULTIC takes a lot of similar beats to Build Engine Styled Games, with it's focus on real-ish environments constructed with the style of blocky 2.5D aesthetics. But also features similar aspects to the Half Life games, specifically Half Life 2's use of physics and having areas with goodies stashed everywhere encouraging exploration. The Weapons are some of the finest I've ever had the pleasure of using. From rifles that use magnum ammo, to pump action grenade launcher, to all the Dynamite cataloged in the course of human history. It is such a fine selection of weapons that all have their use in one way or another. You can even find upgrade parts to upgrade your weapons even further, which is always such a fun feature to include in games like this. With that come the enemies, and like a certain Bloody game, the cultists are a variety of pain and punishment with the upside being absolutely joyful to dismantle into pieces. Further with the other non-cultist enemies taking advantages of certain aspects in the game such as tight arenas or physics objects. Despite having ten full levels in this first chapter, they are absolutely packed full with detail and overflowing to the brim with atmosphere and more importantly secrets! I think the best thing about this gameplay is that once I beat the chapter, I immediately wanted more. Which there is a arena mode if that's your cup of tea.Style wise, CULTIC instantly hits it out of the park with one of the most unique visual styles in a Retro FPS game. And whats even more impressive is that it does not make the game difficult to read during combat, making it even more outstanding. It gives off a murky and washed out vibe in mixture with the pixel art and is further assisted with the voxel models and enemy sprites. The sound design is also fantastic with everything you do sounding oh so chunky and impactful, especially those headshots. It's also good to point out that CULTIC manages to create a such a rich horror environment without using any cheap jumpscares or whatnot. Just coming from the enemies wandering in, extremely quiet details, or the sheer atmosphere of some of the maps, something I give mad respect for.Overall, CULTIC is just a masterclass of a Retro FPS title and show how much you can do with the Retro FPS sub-genre if you are able to branch out, adding aspects to the formula and make it work. It doesn't just copy what has been done before, it mimics and proceeds with flying colors into something truly unique. And this is all in the first chapter, and for ten dollars, TEN DOLLARS. With my only negative points being that it ended and the case of difficultly centered achievements, I can easily say that I am a huge fan of this game and am eagerly waiting for the second part of this game to drop! (Footnote: since Chapter 2 is going to be a DLC rather than being a Early Access, I can technically review CULTIC now!)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm fairly indifferent to retro-style visuals, but I end up playing a lot of games that look like that because of the side benefit: it's very freeing for the developer. When you're not worried about high-fidelity photo-realistic graphics it frees up a lot of time to polish things like the gameplay loop, the feel of the tools at the players disposal, and fun level design.And Cultic has a ton of all of this. Lots of environmental storytelling, interesting problems around every turn, and an expanding arsenal that always feels satisfying. I don't even particularly like the Blood series, but this game made me love the dynamite mechanic. For roughly the cost of a movie you can get hours or pure shooter entertainment, where it truly feels like you're laying siege to an entire cult. Well worth the time I spent with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game, even with zero considerations, but when you factor in that every texture, model, script and song was made by one guy it's really an incredible testament to what can be accomplished when someone that is highly skilled executes on a creative vision. I really enjoyed the pacing of Chapter 1, starting off with a strong Resident Evil 4 vibe with slow and methodical combat encounters that becomes more fast paced and traditionally boomer-shooter-esque as the player's arsenal expands enabling them to rip and tear through enemies that were previously threats that needed to be approached carefully. I played through the game on the "Very Hard" difficulty and I found it appropriately challenging, often having to savescum through some harder encounters, but rarely to the point of frustration. The only thing I do not like about this game is the stylized color palette and sparse lighting can make identifying your enemies very difficult sometimes. This creative decision occasionally puts you in the scenario where you walk into a new dark area, and the enemies get the opportunity to attack you before you can even know they're there, as they're only visible by their muzzle flashes. This forces you to resort to blindly returning fire into the darkness hoping to hit your attacker. The sharpshooter enemies that hitscan from very far and do a large chunk of damage (24 points on very hard if Im not mistaken, making it narrowly NOT an instakill from the regenerating health threshold, which I think is a great design decision) are particularly annoying because of this. Keep in mind that is my one real nitpick with this game. Otherwise it's excellent. There's really a totally different game-feel from the archetypal boomer shooter and I would have a hard time even putting the "boomer shooter" label on it since it's influences are clearly drawn from genres other than classic FPS. It has horror encounters that I think work much better than they do in Dusk and Hrot since you really have to learn how to deal with new enemies as you encounter them for the first time. It's never as simple as pull out your shotgun and start blasting. Okay, sometimes it is. But sometimes getting up close to an enemy is a death with, and you need to use fire. Other times, they're totally immune to fire. There's a lot of tactical variation keeping you on your toes.  Highly recommended to anyone who enjoys a good FPS single player experience.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Not that often I get to play a game that I finish (Chapter One) and then instantly start playing again at the hardest difficulty. Cultic is a game that gets almost everything right from the first second. The inspiration from Blood is clear but it doesn't stay on just the atmosphere and visuals. Gunplay is as satisfying if not more than the Monolith classic, exploding cultists using dynamite or lighting them on fire using oil lamps or molotov cocktails as sadistically fun as it was back in 1997. The horror elements elevate the experience even more. The game really starts as a survival horror where you have to carefully manage your equipment and actively seek secret stashes of ammo to actually survive. Slowly but surely you extend your arsenal, you upgrade your weapons and find enough ammo to conquer a small country. But that doesn't really make the game easier. The challenge slowly escalates and depending on the difficulty you picked you will find yourself struggling to survive on each new area you enter. I don't think it ever reaches the sadistic nature of original Blood, but still playing it on Extreme really is extremely challenging especially if you opt yourself to avoid using quick saves. I was sceptical about the visuals at first but soon I realized how fitting they are to the atmosphere of the game. It really is the equivalent of old exploitation movies of yesteryear, a bit like if the movie Mandy was released on a bootleg VHS. The music is also for the most part amazing and extremely fitting except maybe the second to last level where I found it was a bit too bombastic and got a bit tiring after a few loops. But everything else, top tier stuff. Do I have anything negative to say about Cutltic? Maybe the enemies are too accurate making some areas extremely annoying at times. Sometimes they spot you from a mile away and they never miss a shot even if they are just throwing axes by hand. If their weapons followed the same rules your do (pistol being kind of inaccurate from long distances, shotguns not doing much damage from a distance and also having a wide spread, etc) I think it would bit a bit smoother. Also them knowing your location to the pixel and shooting you the moment you take a corner also feels a bit cheap. A fraction of a second to react to them would be much appreciated instead of just hoping I can tank their first attack before dodging the rest. Still, I love every single second in the game. A true Blood sequel and a pure boomer shooter without unnecessary gimmicks (no multipliers, no combos, no weird attacks and weapons, no shooting to the beat) that nails absolutely everything. Can't wait for the next episodes.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely good fun. The music runs risk of dimming this effect at times, by remaining very dramatic for extended periods rather than keeping low-key and moody, but I didn't dislike it either. What I didn't quite expect was how much I would be reminded of Resident Evil 4, especially later on but actually, throughout, this game owes as much to RE4 as it does to Blood.The first chapter I bombed through in just shy of 4 hours, in one day. _childDocuments_.review: I can't express how good this game is. This guy knocked it out of the park and this is, for my money, the best boomer shooter made yet. Yes, better than Dusk or Amid Evil.It's partly my taste, of course, because I just love chunky pixelated graphics. You can do such satisfying, high-contrast damage modeling. But beyond that, Cultic just seems to nail everything that someone who has been playing these games and is *smart* would know to focus on: fast, fluid movement, very powerful sounding weapons (that are also *very* powerful), exceedingly few bullet sponges, sections that build up tension (and then release), nice set pieces, thumping music, good lighting, *satisfying* secrets that are not overly numerous, difficult, or tedious to find (looking at you Ion Fury)...The list just goes on, and all of it is paired to modern level design that never once feels like a maze (even when the level is intentionally designed like a maze). This is huge, because the Build Engine games Cultic is so inspired by often were quite terrible about leading the player through the level, and you'd just get plain stuck because you missed a detail somewhere.The attention to genre convention and careful design even goes down to some really little details that long-time FPS players will appreciate, like soaring out of the water when you surface instead of the tepid bobble most games have (you know, where you want to get out of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥' water and can't despite ground level being roughly a foot high).I mean, I'm just rambling now. Cultic is very good, you should go play it.Fans of Blood will get that added layer of satisfaction in recognizing a series of gameplay elements and motifs, but this is not an attempt to just replicate Blood and, indeed, this may be the only old-style shooter that I think competes with OG Blood...especially if he is able to produce two more episodes of this quality.That said, I don't think the attention to detail in the level design is there as compared to Blood, especially if one were to compare Cultic to Death Wish (which is just...*mwuah,* pinchy fingers), but creating art assets is hard, and with more time, I'm sure he will be able to incorporate more themes (it's also the case that Cultic's art design doesn't lend itself as easily to certain levels of detail you got in Blood's environments, which is no doubt intentional and cut down on the work he had to do...remember one guy made this).This isn't to say Cultic doesn't have visually fantastic and atmospheric moments, because it does, and like Blood, Cultic feels like a game I can play over and over just because its *fun* (you know, how most games used to be). As compared to any *one* episode of OG Blood, I think Episode 1 can stand next to any of them when taken as a whole because it is a more consistent experience (OG Blood had moments of soaring, incredible quality and design which would then later be contrasted with frustrating design choices, usually due to crushing difficulty spikes). Constructive criticism: enemies indeed get stuck on geometry too often. The tank section was a bit more frustrating than fun (second hardest difficulty, though). Not really much else to complain about.It's a tall order, but even if we never get an Episode 2, Episode 1 is one of the best shooters ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically Resident Evil 4(there are so many direct callbacks to Resident Evil 4 that if you told me this was meant to be an RE 4 fan remake as a boomer shooter I'd probably believe you) meets Halo but with Blood graphics.A pretty good survival horror game is buried beneath the retro shooter look and to my surprise the horror element of this game is legitimately creepy at certain points even if part of me is kind of laughing because like "Gee willickers what mega popular game have I obviously seen this guy in before? lol" I played on Hard difficulty which is what is recommended if you know your way around a shooter and for the most part it wasn't very difficult but there are some spikes(this is why I said Halo earlier...if you're a fan of Halo 2 there are points where you're going to remember Jackal snipers) It's short but if this really is just episode 1 and we're getting more I will be excited about and buy the next episode(s) that come later. _childDocuments_.review: Cultic is another retro-throwback FPS, most reminiscent of the similarly-excellent DUSK, with a bit of Resident Evil 4 thrown in the mix.You play as a rogue detective investigating a mysterious cult. And by "investigate" I mean "completely annihilate with an assortment of ballistic, explosive and flammable tools of destruction".You blast your way through a series of creepy rural locations, all of which are deceptively huge and detailed, considering the game's pixelly aesthetic. While the game my look old-school, the scope and interactivity is very modern.Every weapon feels unique and good to use, and each has its own set of strategic uses, as well as four optional upgrades, that you can unlock by finding the classic FPS secret areas. Enemies are also memorable and distinctive. Every encounter feels pretty unique. Cultic is all killer, no filler. While the game itself is quite short ( I beat it in about 6 hours), it has a ton of replay value in the form of extra difficulty options, secrets to find and different upgrades to choose. I'll definitely replay it at least once.All the bloodshed and action is scored with a genuinely very good soundtrack that reliably gets the heart pounding.I am not a huge fan of the FPS genre (as evidenced by the fact that I played this with a controller. It works great by the way), but Cultic can join DUSK and Half-Life 2 as games that really won me over. It's crazy good!

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent retro-inspired shooter for the modern age.Combat is fun, with many encounters perfectly riding the line between "no sweat" and "oh sh**!" when playing on hard or higher difficulties. Weapons feel and sound hefty, with the somewhat lo-fi sound adding even more satisfying crunch. Levels are surprisingly large and varied, and full of secrets, some of which are hard to find without feeling unfairly hidden.Performance can occasionally be lower than expected, and can occasionally vary substantially in scenes with long draw distances. This can happen even when rendering at low resolutions, perhaps indicating that the bottleneck is not the GPU, but elsewhere. That said most of the game still runs flat out, and the overall experience is one of a snappy, responsive shooter.Stylistically, the game makes use of a "dithering" post-processing filter that may or may not appeal to everyone. It can be easily turned off in-game however, and looks just fine without it.The game looks great on an ultrawide monitor,  however the default FOV setting is ludicrously fish-eyed at such aspect ratios. This too is easily adjustable, but perhaps the game would benefit from a way of automatically setting the FOV based on aspect ratio.In-game menu help is present—barely—but would benefit from a more detailed indication of performance impact (for applicable settings). The help text for the "doodad count" setting also appears to be incorrect, showing instead help for the screen shake option.The ability to toggle display of in-game FPS is a nice option in theory, but in practice is totally unusable. There doesn't appear to be any averaging, reducing the displayed FPS value to a flickering blur that seems to update on every rendered frame. It'd be nice to see this fixed.For the most part, the games few issues are non-intrusive, and don't meaningfully detract from the experience. The big exception to this is the game's highly variable performance, with frame rate drops being especially jarring given the overall simpler, retro aesthetic. Jumping from 120+ FPS to below 60 FPS does hurt the presentation of scenes with long draw distances, and as it doesn't seem to be a function of GPU horsepower, changing the game's few settings helps little. All that said the drop are infrequent, likely due to the design of most levels, and are likely even less visible when running the game at a lower overall refresh rate (as the drop in frame rate is relatively much smaller).This is a great game, and absolutely recommended for those who enjoy a meaty throwback shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Blood's cooler younger brother.CULTIC is a magnificent solo project where you play as a detective investigating a mining community in the mountains to discover it has been taken over by a mad cult devoted to a force known only as "The Will". The cultist swell their ranks with devoted robed lunatics, combat specialists equipped with special weapons, as well as hulking monsters and other shambling things. Very large enemy variety that you don't really see until a few levels in. Speaking of, the levels are surprisingly large and varied, with towns, rocky forests, mines, crypts, even one that takes place on a cargo ship. The game is pretty linear, though with side paths and secret areas to reward explorers. They're well designed, with several memorable set pieces and little moments that will incorporate key hunts (though not as tedious as the retro games that inspired it), switch pressing, or light puzzle elements (usually just putting a thing in another thing).Weapons are a selection of retro designes from the Mauser (obv inspired by RE4's Red9), a mare's leg, sawn-off shotgun, Sten smg, FG42 paratrooper rifle, & China Lake. All are satisfying and upgradeable (though the shotgun seems a bit weak starting off). My only non-complaint about this entire fantastic game is that the first person sprites don't change with certain upgrades that you'd think would make them look different, like the pistol stock or smg increased magazine.If you're a fan of retro shooters or are looking for a game with a unique "spooky" tone, don't miss CULTIC.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give a neutral review I would, but I liked it more than I didn't and the price point is fair, so I'll give it a positive. It's also impressive that this is a one-person endeavor. TL;DR; It's a good Unity-Engine FPS shooter, but it still feels like every other Unity-Engine FPS shooter.The game is fun, and it really has the heart of a 90s shooter. If you liked Blood back in the day, you will be happy about a lot of this game.Most of the maps are well designed, though (like many games in this genre) the later maps are smaller, feel rushed, and are not as thought out as the earlier maps. The first maps take 20-40 minutes to beat, while the later maps take around 10-15. Weapons are fun, not a lot of them, but the ones it gives you work well. Though I'm not really sure why they decided to feature Nazi weapons without context, but whatever. The sound design is great. The music is decent though some of the tracks are a little grating. So my main complaint about the game is by halfway through the first level you realize, "Oh I'm playing another 'retro-FPS' game made in Unity". While this is definitely a solid iteration, there is nothing that really makes the game-play unique, and almost ironically (as this was a common complaint about later games made in the BUILD engine) it feels like more of the same.  Even the slow-down mechanic (which has been done to death) feels tacked on and doesn't really add anything to the game. The game is also very short and ends abruptly, I was able to beat it in 2 and a half hours when usually games like this I expect to spend 9-12 hours, but, for 10 bucks, it's fine.Overall, if you like these types of games as I do, it will be a satisfying experience. Just don't expect anything groundbreaking here. I'd give it a 6/10 closer to a 5 than a 7.

There isn't a cooldown, so you can shift around the world quickly.-The guns feel great with a shotgun that is the perfect medium range, single punch that all these games need. -Meaty headshots-The hatchet is fun to throw at the enemies, with a chunky single hit aswell.-Level design is smart and tight.Cons;-I'm not crazy about the color palette. It is a bit too samey through out.-Kind of wish there were more variety of enemies, more so visually.-levels can lack a bit of variety as well, though that could be due to the very specific color choice.Boomer shooters are probably my favourite FPS' and this is a legit, top tier one. For some reason the price and the fact that is called "chapter 1", I think pushed me off from getting it sooner, thinking it was a smaller 2-3 hour chunk of a bigger series of games...however, there is a lot of content, care, and thoughtfulness put into this game.It is extremely confident in its play and never felt out of place with the big boys of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes yes yes yes yes I can fully recommend this game wholeheartedly. If you liked DUSK and if you liked Blood: Fresh Supply, you might like this.I should talk about presentation first. It does wear it's inspirations on it's sleeves but farther beyond that, it had a few great scary moments towards the start of the game that made me jump, the first level's underground segment and second level's ship basement come to mind. More than I'd been scared before even in other games of it's ilk, and that should be saying something.Once you get into the proper flow of the game, every new level has amazing setpieces that sell the world you're exploring and fighting through. The scope is big and only gets bigger.The music's also wonderful too.Gameplay. I played on Hard mode difficulty. I found every secret 98% by myself on Episode 1 and needed a guide only one time. I've yet to scour the Interlude level for all it's secrets but I'm liking what I see.Most enemies are humanoid and have the obvious weakspot, but they can be pretty tanky if you have a hard time with aiming.How you deal with the situation might depend on your approach, whether you're a lobber who hides behind walls or around corners, or you're a boomer shooter veteran who runs to the side of every pistol shot thrown their way, or maybe you like taking the stealth option for as long as you can get away with it and take on the cultists from the shadows, there's something for everyone here. As a more cautious person myself, I've taken a mixture of all three approaches wherever it suited me best.Early-game I'd say my favorite between the first three guns would be the Shotgun. If you can close the distance it's damage output is super good against most weaker enemies.Alas, you only get the more fun weapons late into Ep 1. Once I got ahold of the game's best sniper weapon, it was lights out for all remaining enemies that were out in the open field. Though that's not to say it trivialized the rest of the game, there were many enclosed spaces you couldn't do that from with and plenty of enemy types needed the extra firepower that you couldn't do from far away anyways. But it certainly made using it a lot more fun. Don't be afraid to use every tool you have, it's there for a reason.Secrets and other stuff. If you're a secret hunter, this game is broadly not bad in that regard. A good chunk of the earlier levels will have you in the think tank trying to figure out where to look, but everything that you can find that's marked as a secret has a logical through-line that you can follow. Some are in air ducts or destructible terrain, others are underwater or tucked in odd corners, nooks, crannies, and even on ledges over the sides of walls in some cases.If you can't find the last one, think to yourself, "Where could I get to if I was a cat?" The kind of cat that can platform and crawl their way to places that are pretty far out-of-the-way for a human to reach. The amount of times this will help you might be surprising.tl;dr, a must-play for people who like FPS games with good singleplayer campaigns.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so here's the deal:You're gonna fork over $10 for this gem.I want you to think about what $10 dollars means to you. Is it a dumbass fast-food meal that you're gonna eat and then "git rid" of later? Is it gas money? A gram? Look...the thing is...I don't want to hear it, and I know damned well that Jason Smith, the SOLO developer for this masterpiece, doesn't want to hear it either. He busted his ass to deliver the best boomer-shooter I've ever played; and I've played them all. Those $10 give you access to a Blood-inspired, cultist slaying, romp through the most open-ended levels I've ever seen in a boomer-shooter. The attention to detail is great too. He really nails the whole vibe of every level in the game. The way that levels loop back onto themselves is really awesome too. I was always amazed when I'd note a locked door early on in the level, and then end up using that door as an exit after obtaining the key needed for it. The first level alone kept me occupied for about 40 minutes on very hard difficulty. The sheer amount of interactability and complexity in the levels astounded me. It's just nothing that games that inspired it ever achieved. The soundtrack is really good too. It also helps nail the atmosphere that Jason was going for. Always fast when the action is good, and always quiet and eerie when it need to set a more sp00ky tone. I could say more but I won't. That's it. You'll get paid again. If you are a kid, and don't have a job, then do what you gotta do for that $10. You're welcome. Personal rating: 9.5/10Difficulty: 4.5/10 (very hard)

_childDocuments_.review: Right away, to those of you who just need to decide what difficulty to pick and quickly dive in, go for Extreme if you feel ballsy. It won't be too insane of you. Other than a couple of spikes that made me curse my arrogance, and one of them has been fixed by this point,  it's surprisingly manageable. The resulting hassle is a tactical feast rather than a frustrating mess. CULTIC borrows many things from Blood, yet leaves most of its relentless bullsh*t in the past. I'm saying it lovingly, of course (). For one, hitscan cultists here give you plenty of time to react to their presence, that being a saving grace when making higher difficulties viable. Now, for those in need of convincing.CULTIC celebrates its roots. I love the playfully macabre vibes it excretes, invoking memories of RE4, Blood, and Splatterhouse. Speaking of references, the game allows itself just the right amount of relevant nods while not offsetting the grimness of its world with some current out-of-character gags to please the crowd. Many things you'll find in it are hilarious and there's a ton of camp smeared about, although, for the majority of the time, the tone is appropriately morbid and the humour is pitch-dark, which I find extremely immersive. This game is going to age gracefully in every aspect of its presentation.If I remember correctly, the overlay filter used to be more aggressive before the release. Or maybe it only seemed that way? Somehow, CULTIC looks significantly better in action than on screenshots or in trailers. The visuals have been beaten into a pulp, coated in all shades of a bruise, and tastefully so. I can't get enough of these classy colours, they're extremely effective at painting the overall mood and tone. The skybox is beyond gorgeous and, even just by looking at the main menu, one can tell the artistry is pure grunge. Not to mention the stellar HUD, boasting fancy yet perfectly readable fonts. I'm a sucker for those.Local highly-detailed scenery is complemented with voxels for pickups and props. They're on the money, and not just visually, adding to the environmental interactivity. You can shatter a toilet or grab a chair and break someone's back with it. Oil lamps spill, furniture crumbles, barrels explode, and the explosions are fierily massive, facilitating gorgeous fire effects. Ah, screaming people running around on fire! It takes me home. The gore parade gets magnified by the dynamic and manually placed lighting, which gets reflected on your guns and enemy sprites. Also, I adore it when I can see my character's feet in a shooter. Not a kink, I swear.Map design is one, though. While CULTIC's isn't as intricate or varied as that of Blood, there are plenty of expansive maps for one chapter. I'm a slow player, so you can probably subtract several hours from my playtime, but these 10 appropriately grimy places are a bang for your buck either way. You get your caves and mines, docks, canyons, asylum, village, crypt, mansion, caves and mines again... maybe slightly too many of the latter for my taste. There's nothing you haven't seen before, yet every classic location is done competently. They neatly loop around and facilitate amazing encounter design that makes you expect death around every corner and use your booby-trapped surroundings to dispose of enemy hordes effectively.When stuffing said surroundings with secrets, CULTIC comes the closest to Blood by making you pay attention to environmental cues like cracks in the walls, vents, hidden buttons, or platforming opportunities. Besides, finding at least a few nooks per level is almost necessary because of the stern ammo distribution and the fact no one likes to miss out on upgrades, permanent health buffs, sometimes whole new weapons. The maps are interesting structurally rather than visually. Still, these tight haunted corridors, stuffy cellars, or your good old bodies piling in the middle of a room possess a strong atmosphere, drenched in rich ambience and pleasant music. Sometimes interspersed with moments of eerie silence.However brief. I’m not sure if “shooting shouting cultists with a Mauser” was the intended predominant impression to take away from the experience, but it felt better than it sounds. RE4 designs are evidently the strongest influence in this field. You'll see cultists wielding everything from axes and shields to grenade launchers, and they'll constitute the majority of your kills. Despite that theoretical monotony, they were fun to deal with. I had to seize advantageous positions to ambush them, hide for a breather, crouch and scamper like a rat, use everything in my arsenal, which was highly satisfying. Said monotony simply didn't get the chance to set in.To boot, every so often, you'll encounter monsters like ghosts, instakill chainsaw maniacs, savage long-jumping zombies, gargantuan skull-headed feral brutes, skeletons, and something my Steam friend accurately described as a "p*ssy monster from Michigan: Report from Hell". I particularly appreciated the tightly-tailored encounters where you, for example, get to fight a chainsaw maniac while manoeuvring around bear traps or when two of them chase you in a narrow hedge maze. That was exciting! Most of this game's encounters are extremely well-designed, it's full of such Panic Horror surprises. As a matter of fact, however, the real horror is you.These cultists messed with the wrong person who has the means to take them to school. Starting with all the ways to get out of trouble like fluid movement, including slides, dodges, and double-jumping. Local gunplay is smooth and snappy, with guns ringing, clicking, and clacking as they should. Shrilling gunshots lead to delightful headsplosions, making splurts of blood spray around the place. Punctuating the weight behind random moments of badassery, slow motion triggers sparingly on headshots and multikills. The overall game feel is enhanced by the combat awareness provided. Since finetuned feedback lets you know when you hit, kill or receive damage, violence here feels impactful and visceral.Harvesting it to the fullest is your arsenal. An insanely potent Mauser, a double-barrel that gets passable after a few upgrades, an enjoyable lever-action rifle capable of popping multiple heads when the cultists are lined up, a grenade launcher that is vital for your survival, and a surprisingly great flamethrower for a genre that loves to f*ck them up. There are 10 or so pieces altogether, but these are the ones I typically had ammo for. CULTIC is stingy like that, making up for it with tons of dynamite and Molotovs for all occasions. And don't forget you have a secondary fire for every gun and a cathartic tertiary fire for the explosives. It would be obscene to ask for more... but I'd love to see a working chainsaw in the next chapter, please.This review is glowing for a reason. At this point, it should be evident that CULTIC has class. The developer approached it with all seriousness and it could be seen long before the job was finished. Now, looking at how fast the game gets fixed and updated, how much people love it, I'm just glad to see the result corresponding to the efforts invested. To top it off, the polish is superb. I only had one random crash that I consider acceptable. All in all, between the timeless style, killer gunplay, and 10 saturated levels, even the worst of which never drag thanks to the great encounter design, CULTIC is a riveting joyride. Don't wait for a discount, it's a steal at full price.My curator

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: 10/10 Chunky 90's pixels that give me the same dopamine hit Doom, Wolfenstein 3D, and Duke Nukem 3D did. I prefer playing without the dithering and the simpler color palate, but that's a subjective personal preference. Music: 8/10 Moody, ambient, depressing, the Jelly to the game's Peanut Butter. Almost 10/10, but needs more reverb. This is subjective. Game Play: 20/10 The game's Boom Boom's feel nice and boomy. Weapons sound chunky when fired, and give good feedback visually and audio wise. Taking damage also gives you clear feedback visually and audio wise. If you've played Doom, Duke Nukem, or Quake, you will easily take to controlling the game and moving through it's environments. New players are given space to learn the mechanics of the game in a straightforward manner. Being a true 3D game, you get to experience some very well thought out pieces of vertical game play. This game's world both looks and feels big. Bottom line, this game feels unreasonably good to play.Story: 7/10 It's a tale as old as time. A person is sent to investigate something that other people deemed more important than them, have interest in. In the case of Cultic, you're investigating what seems to be a high-profile missing person's case. After a series of incredibly unfortunate events, you wake up in the ground after being left for dead. Seeking answers and armed with only a Zippo lighter, a hatchet past it's prime, and a pistol that's clearly been dug out of the ground only days ago, you move forward. Only fear and the instinctual need for self preservation allow you to move forward. Long story short, angry dead guy uses boom booms to find out why dead.Presentation: 10/10 Cultic succeeds in what it set out to do as a piece of art. Environments are moody and tense. During the game you can find notes in typewriters and in the environment that give you a sense of what's happening in the world around you. Beyond using text for world building, Cultic also uses it's environment to tell a story. You can find dead bodies made out of voxels scattered around the world, often with a weapon laying next to them. You can find bodies wrapped in burlap, hanging from ceilings in a cave. You can find tables lit with candles, occupied by skulls and piles of viscera. The artistic limitations of the game allow your imagination to fill in the blanks the game deliberately puts in front of you. Overall Score: 9/10 Games these days are rarely perfect, but Cultic comes damn close. It succeeds in hitting those check boxes and delivering precious hits of dopamine that the shooters of yesteryear gave me. Past that, it builds upon and does more than they ever could. Cultic is the sequel to Blood that I always wanted, but never got. Play this game.
