_childDocuments_.review: In the ever-evolving landscape of video games, certain titles stand out as exceptional pieces of art, combining gripping narratives, innovative gameplay mechanics, and stunning visuals to create an immersive experience. Among these, Persona 5 Royal unquestionably claims its spot as one of the best video games of all time. Released as an enhanced version of the critically acclaimed Persona 5, this game transcends its genre and captivates players with its compelling story, intricate characters, and refined gameplay mechanics.At the core of Persona 5 Royal's excellence lies its narrative brilliance. The game takes players on a rollercoaster ride through the vibrant streets of Tokyo, intertwining the supernatural with the mundane aspects of daily life. The protagonist, a high school student codenamed Joker, becomes entangled in a web of corruption and conspiracy as he and his group of Persona users, the Phantom Thieves, strive to reform society by 'stealing the hearts' of the corrupt evildoers in the world. The story unfolds in a series of meticulously crafted arcs, each delving into the lives of the main characters and exposing the dark secrets that bind them.One of the standout features of Persona 5 Royal (and the Persona franchise in general) is its ability to address complex and relevant social issues. The game fearlessly tackles topics such as societal expectations and pressure, corruption, the impact of technology on personal relationships/the world around us, and even heavier themes such as mental health issues, sexual assault, suicide, and more. This narrative depth elevates Persona 5 Royal beyond a mere gaming experience, turning it into a thought-provoking exploration of contemporary societal challenges and social commentary.Persona 5 Royal boasts a cast of very memorable characters, each with their own unique personalities, backgrounds, and struggles. The game successfully establishes a deep connection between players and the characters, as their growth and development are intricately woven into the overarching narrative. The 'Confidant system' (a.k.a The Social Link system), a mechanic that popuralized the Persona franchise and that has been everpresent since Persona 3, allows players to build relationships with these characters; providing emotional depth, personal memories with said characters, and tangible gameplay benefits, up to a maximum "Confidant Rank' of 10. It also happens to be the case that 10 different unique Romance paths can be unlocked and explored, even simultaneously (although this can get messy, and I would not recommend it, especially so to the faint of heart and those with a good conscience).Another selling point for this game is that the characters and cast feel very believable and 'alive', making for a that much more immersive experience. The top shelf, high quality, and realistic voice acting (both available in Japanese or English, although I recommend playing with English dub to any non-native-level-Japanese speaking player) sells these characters so extremely well and really makes you forget that you are playing a game or even looking at a piece of fiction in the first place. Because of this you're *right there* with these characters in the present moment, and you unavoidably grow fond of them the more personally you get to know them; and the more endeavours you undertake and overcome together.The enhanced Royal version of Persona 5 also brings with it the inclusion of new characters, such as Kasumi Yoshizawa and Takuto Maruki, who add further layers to the narrative, introducing fresh perspectives and dynamics to the already established cast of characters, and besides this other characters were given additional screentime in this version of the game as well. The well-crafted character arcs, the humor that every character brings in their own way, and the emotional impact of their personal stories contribute significantly to the game's universal acclaim.Persona 5 Royal is a visual feast that combines a distinct art style with a vibrant color palette. The game's unique blend of Anime, cel-shaded graphics and stylish character designs creates a visually stunning world that sets it apart from other videogame titles. The attention to detail in the level design; which is based on real-life locations in Japan that have been recreated in-game in an almost 1:1 fashion, the beautiful and lively Anime cutscenes, the designs of the Personas -  the manifestation of characters' inner selves - are also a treat to the eyes, and above all the imaginative settings of the 'Palaces' that you and your crew have to traverse through all contribute to the game's aesthetic appeal.Moreover, the game is accompanied by a phenomenal soundtrack composed by the fantastic composer and music artist Shoji Meguro. The game's music and Original Soundtrack do not only enhance the atmosphere, but also becomes an integral part of the overall experience. The jazzy tunes and energetic beats, and above all the lead singer Lyn's super unique and smooth voice perfectly complement the game's stylish aesthetic; creating a synergy that further immerses players in the captivating world of this unforgettable masterpiece.The addition of new personas, confidants, game(play) mechanics, and locations expands the game's scope; providing players with even more content to explore than ever before. The revamped dungeons, known as Palaces, offer improved mechanics and challenges, keeping the gameplay engaging and dynamic for returning players and newcomers alike.The inclusion of the Thieves' Den, a customizable hub for players to showcase their achievements and interact with the game's lore, adds a layer of personalization to the experience. These enhancements demonstrate the developers' commitment to delivering a polished and well-rounded fresh gaming experience for both returning players and new players alike.Most of all, the game simply has an astounding amount of (gameplay) mechanics. When you're not saving the world, you can do things like read a book, hit a few homeruns in baseball, study, go out on a date, do fitness, go shopping, fishing, go to the arcade, watch a movie with someone, etc. But in the palaces, you're busy with stealth, planning, item management, and strategic turn-based combat. You feel like you're truly transported into the game's world because of the sheer amount of things you can do in it.I absolutely recommend this game to anybody who can appreciate a videogame that has a fantastic memorable cast of characters, doesn't mind tons of dialogue to read/listen through, loves snappy, stylish and strategic turn-based combat, can really appreciate a good original soundtrack to listen to for days on end, loves an emphasis on a truly marvelously stylish artstyle, likes Anime, and can tolerate a game with extremely hype moments that are offset and juxtaposed with many moments of slow burn/some grinding here and there.Persona 5 Royal stands as a testament to the potential of video games as an art form. Its narrative depth, well-developed characters, stunning design, and extensive gameplay mechanics collectively contribute to its status as one of the best video games of all time. The game's ability to tackle relevant social issues while providing an immersive and enjoyable experience cements its place in the pantheon of gaming masterpieces. Persona 5 Royal is not merely a game; it is a work of art that transcends the boundaries of its medium, leaving a truly indelible mark on the hearts of players worldwide. P.S Thanks for reading my review.-lustY

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people give this game a solid 10 out of 10, but I would go a step further and say this game is genre-defining. The level of insane detail and painstaking effort put into this game make it arguably the greatest JRPG ever created. Although legitimate criticisms of the game exist, like the lack of player direction at the beginning, they pale in contrast to the unfathomable amount of work put into it. Atlus expertly captures the subtleties of daily life and the realism of its story sequences while perfectly weaving them into the life of a phantom thief. The game presents a very intriguing villain while also maintaining the fantasy element by featuring bosses that are incredibly interesting and fun to fight. In my opinion, a modern JRPG would be an enormous hit if it could even accomplish half of what Persona 5 Royal has. I genuinely believe that the game is ahead of its time and is one of, if not THE best JRPG ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal has captivated my imagination from the very outset, leaving an enduring impression. The game seamlessly weaves profound psychological intricacies into its captivating narrative, but what truly distinguishes it is its .One of the most remarkable aspects of Persona 5 Royal is its awesome ability to foster a profound connection with each character. Meeting, interacting with, and sharing their joys and sorrows made them feel like lifelong companions. The characters' emotional depth is astonishing, evoking a genuine empathy as if they were cherished friends. I became  in their lives.The game's narrative is nothing short of a ! Every chapter and plot twist is spellbinding, compelling players to contemplate moral dilemmas and choices alongside the characters. It's a tale of justice and freedom, brimming with inner conflicts and authentic emotions. Playing Persona 5 Royal feels less like gaming and more like inhabiting the lives of these characters.The game's presentation, encompassing visual aesthetics and user interface, impeccably integrates turn-based combat with real-life simulation. The meticulous attention to detail is evident not only in the menus but also in the stylish character designs and the intricacies of the Metaverse. This level of artistry and craftsmanship is a rare gem in the gaming world.From uncovering the mysteries of the Palace of Cognitions to nurturing relationships with the characters and fighting for the hearts of the people, Persona 5 Royal challenges players emotionally and morally, imparting values of friendship, loyalty, and the pursuit of one's beliefs.In conclusion, . It distinguishes itself as one of the greatest games ever created, leaving an indelible impression on players through its impassioned storytelling, captivating adventures, and the exceptional artistry of its game design.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal does not deviate from the Persona formula: a mix of JRPG and visual novel. It surpasses its predecessor Persona 4 on its main weak points.Let's be honest Persona 5 is an excellent but niche title. It's extremely "Japanese" and visual novel oriented, so if you're reluctant to either of these aspects I wouldn't recommend it.What I liked:- An incredible ost- A meticulous art direction, which goes into micro-detail, I have rarely seen that.- Appearance of level design in the dungeons which makes their progress more enjoyable- The persona formula: time management between real life and secret life that still works.- Endearing characters- The narration of the persona is still very pleasant- A pleasant scenario, with some more mature messages. Be careful, it remains at the level of a "shonen". Some messages are very pragmatic but terribly true, I could relate to some stories/passages of the game.- Improved fights- A colossal game durationWhat I regret:- The interesting fights are still too rare. The special challenges should be in the game not optional!- Poor quality content that acts as filler: the "requests" and the "mementos". On a game of this length, it seems difficult to have interesting content all the way through.- The grind of the confidants: We are more interested in the right answers than in the dialogue, which goes against the concept of the confidants.- The concept of infiltration as extensive and important as Sekiro's: useless and just a pretext.I dream of a Persona with the density of a Disco Elysium with hardcore combat/donjons, it's not that far from it...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolute perfection. I'd never played a Persona game prior to this one and I have to say that I'm already a big fan. The all-out attacks and Showtimes are definitely my favorite parts of it. Each character having their own special moves and scenes makes it feel so alive as well.  The characters are perfect. I totally thought that some of the non-party confidants were gonna end up being kinda generic but I'm extremely happy that I was wrong. Each and every one of them have such bright and unique personalities, none of them feel forced or shallow. Never thought I'd end up liking a politician, even in a video game. Yoshida gets my vote!  The romance scenes with the female characters are really sweet. True to life, it's advised that you don't go and tell each one that you love them in a single playthrough or there WILL be hell to pay. I ultimately chose Haru because she's damn precious and I was hoping maybe she'd stop murdering me at Tycoon.   As for the music, this sh𝗶t is Pokémon levels of banger. That being said, the Starlight battle theme "Groovy" along with "Gentle Madman", "Price (Another Version)" and "A Woman (Another Version)" have to be my favorites.  It's not really my place to say this but if you're interested in trying out the Persona series, I'd say that this one is a phantastic place to start.   Really excited to see how Persona 6 turns out!

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about Scamsona 5: Actually “Finished” Edition?It is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Persona game in the series, however newcomers to the series, normies who enjoyed Swiper from Dora the Explorer, and mask fetishists alike will agree it’s the best simply because they haven’t played the older games, or played them after this ♥♥♥♥-show.It's a game about people, getting to know them, day 1 bugs like ♥♥♥♥ resolution, FPS issues, grainy textures and resolution – even though this edition is now two years old and is being —you know Microsoft, that company that doesn’t know what a computer is or how to put games on them?It's also a game about cut content from previous games that nobody liked being recycled into this one for no real reason – but hey, ♥♥♥♥ unique enemy design, right?A game about cut content from the original release being added to the game—and then having the gall to ask for full price!Everything in the game looks pixelated and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ unless you move things up to 4k, so might as well buy on Switch or be prepared for the inevitable sudden stops in gameplay because Sega apparently doesn’t know how to port games to PC unless it is a Yakuza series.This isn’t a me issue either, my game ran at 120+fps with and without the lock, so it’s definitely the game.If you boycotted Shin Megami Tensei III: Nocturne Remaster but bought this game I’d like for you to find the nearest noose you absolute clown.Breaking the tradition of copying and improving the previous “Grand” entry title (which would have been Persona 4 Golden) Persona 5 was a half-finished game that released for $60, and now these idiotic rabid fans are going to tell you it’s worth another $60.Do yourself a favor: become a phantom thief and obtain a “Russian Demo Copy” of this game, or ask your friend on Discord to gift you that Xbox Game Pass that’s expiring in a few days. This game and its developers are not worth funding.The characters are more one-dimensional, pedantic, and boring in this game than any other Persona series. You’ll find yourself seeing previous characters poorly aped in this edition, along with the worst voice acting I have ever witnessed in a Sega series – Sonic games were considered as I wrote this. When I played the original game replaying it became much more feasible when I switched back to Japanese. So for those of you who don’t like to read: your ears and memories will thank me later, switch to anything but English for spoken language. The story is good…at the beginning.  Endgame spoiler:  A WHOLE IN-GAME MONTH SUDDENLY APPEARS IN THIS EDITION ALONG WITH A NEW CHARACTER AND YOU ALL DON’T FIND IT ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FISHY THAT FFVII REMAKE HAD AN UPGRADE OPTION BUT THIS DIDN’T?Soon as you’re done with the first boss it kind of rolls off, if you ever played a previous Persona game this feels like a title meant for normies, similar to how World of Warcraft’s DLC simplifies the game with each release, or how Dungeons and Dragons is getting more and more casual. The opening and first dungeon make you think each place will be unique, feature interesting exploration and problem-solving, but it doesn’t. Each level after the first two are just normal dungeons with what appears to be unique enemies that quickly turn into the same 3D models we’ve seen since 2011. There’s DLC from previous games included in all versions, however due to the developers making a Fallout 4 VR Release Day error with resolution the game still looks better on switch, and all lines look jagged as hell in any resolution below 4K, making anyone who rates this a 5/5 or call it a "masterpiece now that it's on PC" look idiotic.After making it through the first dungeon the second one has no luster or upgrade. A hook line here, some seeds there, this game is a silly re-hash with absolutely zero focus or love on improving it. I'm fourteen hours into my playthrough and hoping I'm wrong, because I'll change my review if so.[update: 40hrs in and no change. Persona 3 FES & Persona 4 Golden are still leagues better than this trash heap, even with the cut content restored in this version.]Speaking of stupid people, since I know the fans are as rabid as DCS World and Chrono Trigger fans, enjoy having comments disabled. [edit: also thank you for proving my point, wow y'all are salty someone has a real opinion. 50+ downvotes, more than either of the previous fanbases combined.]You ever been so pissed about someone being right in a review you gave their review a jester, boosting its visibility higher because any vote (down, up, and funny) and any award react helps visibility regardless?Me neither.Persona 1/5 – Steal your money; steal from them before they get you.

_childDocuments_.review: The sign is a subtle joke. The shop is called "Sneed's Feed & Seed", where feed and seed both end in the sound "-eed", thus rhyming with the name of the owner, Sneed. The sign says that the shop was "Formerly Chuck's", implying that the two words beginning with "F" and "S" would have ended with "-uck", rhyming with "Chuck". So, when Chuck owned the shop, it would have been called "Chuck's Feed and Seed".

_childDocuments_.review: Great combat, story, and soundtrack. Improves upon Persona 4 by fixing the only glaring issue: dungeon design. There are still some randomly generated areas but the main dungeons are each hand-made, thematic and more interactive than the predecessors. My only complaint is the cast all have extremely over-the-top backstories that can be a bit distracting at times. Where P3/4 have you interacting with students that have normal "student problems", everyone in P5 has some loved one who's been murdered and they feel the need to avenge or some other crazy trauma. The characters are still great but they don't feel as real as the P4 cast. There's an astounding amount of content at over 100 hours yet it somehow never gets too repetitive. The "new" Royal content is also totally worth replaying the game for but maybe wait for a sale if that's all you're interested in. Either way, you'll still be playing through the whole game to get to the Royal content at the end. Highly recommend to JRPG fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to discuss Persona 5 Royal. Instead, I will discuss its impact on me as a person:This game carried me through 4 consecutive months of escapism I put myself through in order to spice up my weekly routine of Work, Gym, Martial Arts, and coming home alone to my parents and sister. Being a 24 year old can be tough, but being a single 24 year old introvert with no relationship prospects is brutal.Funnily enough, Persona 5 Royal taught me to face reality head on rather than make excuses and use games to cope. I want to work hard to better myself while maintaining hope for a better future no matter what curve balls life throws at me. While I'm no social butterfly, I'm now starting to develop the confidence to talk to a pretty woman or try new things that are outside my rigid routine. At the end of the day, life goes on irregardless of my circumstances. It's up to me to decide if I am going to sink into the mud and whine about how life isn't fair and the odds are stacked against me or if I'm going to make the most of the hand I've been dealt and take advantage of the opportunities around me.Finally, I fully intend for Persona 5 Royal to be the last game I play for a long time. Gone are the days of coming home from work or the gym and locking myself away in my office while I mindlessly grind away. I want to rediscover my passions and find fulfillment in the things and people around me. I call on you to do the same.Once you finish Persona 5 Royal of course. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Legendary game. P4G is my favourite persona game hands down, but I will fully admit that P5R has the best style, presentation, and gameplay in the entire series (have not played P3R yet, I expect that game to match or top this, on top of supposedly having the best story in the series). The confidant social links in this game are really, really well done. Persona 4 golden still has the best characters, and the most engaging social links due to the more intimate nature of them. The theme of your friendships outside of the phantom thieves being more so mutual contracts as opposed to friendships (hence confidants instead of social links) is both a pro and a con imo. However by the end, they are all so heartwarming and enjoyable they overcome the initial coldness some of them may exhume. And the writing is very well done. The individual writing for characters in P4G feels more grounded and real to me, hence my preference for them, but really it's like saying 5 pounds of gold is better than 4 and a half pounds of gold, they're both amazing.The story is wonderful, again, persona 4's story resonated with me a little more personally than this one, but the suspense, writing, and of course the presentation are unmatched. Persona 5 is THE place to start the series for anyone on the fence, or anyone who dislikes JRPG's or this type of game. It transcends genres thanks to the quality of life improvements and increase engagement in battles over P4G or the original P3 releases, and the action filled story is very easy to get into. Persona 4 as an example takes more to get into if the setting isn't one that resonates with you off the bat, and if you dislike more traditional JRPG dungeon crawlers you may find the RPG side of P4 and the especially the original P3 releases is too much of a road block to enjoy the rest of the game (I personally love them, but I also love JRPG's so it's not surprise. The average consumer will for sure find this much more palatable, and long time vets can enjoy the depth the combat system has). Persona 5 just oozes creativity and style. From the heights of the jazz funk and pop inspired OST to the charm of exploring Tokyo in such detail, this games presentation hits off at a 10/10. Persona has never been this stylish, and this series is KNOWN for being stylish! My only con with the game is the story, if persona 4's story is a 10/10 for me, this one sits closer to an 8.5/10. There's a few low parts that most people won't care about or even notice, but if you're coming off of persona 4 or persona 3, the former I can attest has no low spots in it's narrative (imo ofc) at all (I've heard p3 is considered to be even better, makes me all the more excited to experience it), you'll probably notice. But it's worth it, the transition into the third act is worth any burn out you may feel in the end of the second act. I already know when I play this game again that damned space station section is gonna annoy me, mainly because I disliked the narrative that led up to it. In this part of the story Ryuji really pissed me off. People love to ♥♥♥♥ on Yusuke from P4 but Ryuji is Yusuke with none of his positive traits, and an annoying attitude. His selfish nature makes it hard for me to like him as the "bro" character for this game, and I never found myself agreeing with him until he finally nears the end of his character arc, which is just, well mid. Yusuke is my bro, Ryuji is the annoying dumb guy who can get out of my party LOL He feels like the worst aspects of Yusuke and Kanji mixed together, with none of their respective unique perspectives that made their flaws work so well in P4. He does finally find his footing though, but he really feels the weakest out of the entire cast, and his impact on the story is almost nothing outside of being an instigator for internal conflict. I could nitpick a few more characters if I wanted to as well, but I'll begin to sound a bit too p4 fan boyish since most of my complains are coming from comparisons of characters from said game. My opinion doesn't seem to be the minority though. But, to re-iterate, i'm saying the 4 pounds of gold is not quite as good as the 5 pounds of gold, no one outside of people who love the other persona games would find this to be an issue at all, the writing is superb as it is in any persona game, and the localisation team did an excellent job. The writing feels both modern and timeless once again.Long story short, you need to play this game if you have not. My personal recommendation is to play persona 4 golden first, then persona 5R, then persona 3 reload as you'll be able to climb the ladder of quality of life changes. Some people may find it impossible to, for a lack of a better word, play something more primitive in comparison, and they'd be loosing out on some amazing entires. However, for some, this game was the starting point for them to explore the series and find the one they love the most! This game is a 9.5/10 and I do mean that literally, a good game is a 6/10, this one, like all the persona games, is a once in a life time experience you need to try. I'll also add any bias in my review does carry some "first persona game syndrom" vibes. Persona 4 golden was my first, that ontop of the games story premise and characters resonating with me more personally than I expected (and more personally than persona 5) creates a bias you'll find through the fandom, so take my complaints about the narrative with a grain of salt.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the definitive version of Persona 5. It adds an extra 100 hours of content through new confidants, increasing the size of the already existing palaces, adding new palaces, new story, and adding new post-game / side content. The PC version of course is the best performing and best looking of the versions of the game as well. Persona 5's story is fantastic as well; covering a lot of themes that have never really been touched on before in a video game, and not being afraid of getting into some pretty dark and mature subject matter. This is a really dark and depressing game, but at the same time balances it with moments of hope. The story doesn't want to punch the player or the characters while they are down, but puts them into terrible situations that feel true to real life and therefore are believable. Life is extremely messy and a lot of evil people get in the way of it, and that is what Persona 5 is exploring. I don't think any other game developer would have the backbone to commit to such a storyline.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10After moving to Tokyo, the protagonist finds the way to rebel against society by stealing the hearts of evil people. Alongside a cast of similar-minded rebels they attempt to break the chains holding back society. While not required, a lot of the themes and scenes have more of an impact if you are familiar with Japanese society and culture. 6.5/10The battle tracks are perhaps the most memorable aspect of the game and they initially work great, however, after a while they become stale, repetitive and even boring. I can hear them on my own, but god help me if I need to hear the same tracks in battle every single time I decide to get some experience.  7.5/10It looks good and has some really nice-looking effects. However, it’s nothing out of the world and more games make them look even better and add more variety to the character’s expressions and dynamics. 7/10A dungeon crawler combined with a school life sim. Basically, you have two options. You battle through different areas, gaining experience, evolving your personas and obtaining items or; you focus on building your relationships. This works most of the time except that battles can become stale and the same soundtrack repeats again and again during the fighting. Regarding the school life, it’s definitely interesting meeting your confidants, getting to know them better, help them grow (though some are better than others by a large margin), and eventually gaining new abilities based on how they help you.While this last part can work well on its own, it has a major disadvantage that I will discuss further down. 7.5/10The story starts really strong with the situations you are faced and then, it seems the “villains” of each arc are just cut-and-paste characters from other games. They basically have one negative trait and that’s taken to an extreme and makes their whole personality.One of the biggest gripes I have with this game is that throughout it, the decisions, the characters seem to follow a certain logic but, for a plot twist to work they must suddenly change and become smarter, more careful (and all is explained via flashbacks). Also, the traitor in your group is painfully obvious.It’s still enjoyable and, the last semester added in Royal is the best one yet. It solves a lot of the issues other villains had and it does include an interesting twist.Regarding the characters itself, most are enjoyable and well done, with different personalities. However, the MC is the weakest character of all, since they have practically no voice lines, they don’t seem to react to the world. Everything they say seems scripted or forced, and they are treated as the leader of the group just because. The character barely participates in group conversations, gives meaningful insight or doesn’t look like they should be leading.Having more voices lines would have certainly aided, especially in intense or important scenes.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely mind-blowingly amazing game.The characters, the story, the music, the UI, absolutely everything about this game is amazing and dripping with style. If I wanted to sit here and talk about how much I loved this game I would have to spend an hour writing down every little thing. I'll spare everyone from that though. All you need to know is that Persona 5 is a long journey, you'll probably put at least 100 hours into the game from beginning to end... but you'll love every minute. It is worth the journey, and I recommend you start that journey ASAP.You're sure to fall in love with the cast of oddball characters you befriend through out the story. The combat is fantastic and constantly evolving through the entire runtime of the game. I had things happen for the first time in the final 5 hours of the game even. If you like turn-based combat you're gonna adore the battle system of this game. There's a lot to do outside of combat too. There is a social sim portion of the game too, which at first sounds like a bore, but it was one of my favorite things to sit down and play through. There are endless options for things to do, from building relationships with your friends to burger eating contests. It's very well done and sure to please. I won't go into the story, it should be experienced first-hand. But it was phenomenal. It'll stick its claws in you and not let go all the way to the end. (and they stick the landing too, it's fantastic)So I can keep going on and on, but you should probably just pick this game up and start your epic journey while jamming out to the sick soundtrack of this game. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: It just feels like P5R improved every superficial element that was subpar in P4G (mainly in the presentation department) at the cost of elements that made P4G special. Yes, the dungeons are hand crafted set pieces now instead of P4G's corridor marathon, but they're still the same repetitive game-play loop of ambushing shadows and opening doors. The trivial puzzles that are occasionally sprinkled in hardly breakup the monotony. And in any case, P4G's corridors make a return in Mementos, only now longer and more monotonous than before. Yes, the combat and interfaces look flashier but the game is even more shy about presenting any kind of challenge than P4G. Yes, your new gang has some interesting moments but there are much less special events with them than in P4G, and there are so many monotonous dialogues about the rotten adults in charge that would surprise even the Kids Next Door. It doesn't help that most boss fights consist of equally monotonous monologues about how rotten they are. There's more problematic elements I could gripe on & on about: Yusuke's creepiness ("Pose nude for me or I'm calling the cops"), Haru coming in too late in the plot, Makoto & Futaba dominating the party too much, the fortune teller that predicts what your friends want to hear in exchange for money, etc. etc. Finally, P5R adds a third semester & while the main story of this extra leg is fairly compelling, there is almost nothing new to do here. It's "Go to the Gym or Jazz Club until the timer runs out" semester, because none of the other daily activities are worth doing at this point. Overall, it just feels like I spent 150 hours on an experience that would have been better if it lasted 40 hours. I don't doubt the skill & commitment dedicated to make this game, I'm just skeptical that the end result is still slight downgrade from Persona 4.

They all have fun personalities while also having emotional and sympathetic stories that truly make you feel for them- U get to say ♥♥♥♥ the police for this gamecons:- Some of the puzzles in levels are downright confusing or even frustrating to the point where I have gone from excited to play to closing the game within the same hour because I had to take a break from pure frustration even with a walkthrough. - Navigation is downright awful. _childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt one of the best games I have played this year, it is the second time I have finished it, and because of the love I have for it I decided to platinum it (which I ended up doing after a few hours). Persona 5 Royal is more than a game, it makes me very happy to listen to its wonderful songs or remember good moments with the characters that you meet in the story.Speaking of the story, it can sometimes be weak or a little boring, as well as excite you and make you want to play for hours and hours without feeling tired.  When I saw the true ending for the first time I couldn't believe that I had finished playing a tremendous work of art, quite a few hours are spent in front of the screen playing this game, my first game reaching 111 hours and my second game reaching only 60 hours.  I will never get tired of playing Persona 5 Royal again.I recommend it?Well, it is more than obvious, if it is true that the first hours of play are a bit boring and that sometimes the long hours of play overwhelm the player, but it is quite worth devoting many hours to this game.  Comparing it with other people, this game has pros and cons (like all games in the world).  Its story seems meh to some, but it must be recognized that it improves many aspects of previous games, becoming more comfortable, such as its great outstanding combat.  The great style and musical section of the game makes you fall in love even with the fragrance.Would I recommend starting with this game to enter the persona saga?No and yes, there are many aspects that make it good, but comparing it with the great story that Persona 3 Reload has, I would recommend starting with 3 Reload solely for the story, in terms of social links, Persona 3 Reload is a little behind .  While Persona 5 Royal has a bit more lively social links, I could tell you, instead of spending time with one social link, you can invite others to spend time with them at the same time.Whether you start with whoever it is, 3 Reload, 4 Golden or 5 Royal.  They all have that something that makes them special and that beautiful message that you learn as you play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Persona 4 Golden a couple of years ago, my expectations for Persona 5 Royal were sky high. In just about a couple hours of playing, those expectations were shattered as I quickly realized how just about every aspect of the game was a step up from just about every comparable non-Persona JRPG that I have played. What sets P5R apart can be found in the game's unique and stylish presentation, profound and complex story, and of course, fantastic and incredible soundtrack. Similar to the other entries in the franchise, the core gameplay mechanics revolve around turn-based combat and daily life simulation, both of which are done expertly. Lastly, the characters are well-written, well-developed, and relatable, making it easy to get invested in each of their stories. Through the characters and the story, P5R addresses issues on mental health and shared societal anxieties by presenting them in a manner that is easy to relate to and understand. Persona 5 Royal is an iconic game that ranks at the peak of its genre due to its beautiful presentation, masterful storytelling, and an unforgettable soundtrack.

I was not dissapointedGameplay - 7/10The mix between infiltrating the palaces and visual novel story segments, although tedious at times was really fun. Costume DLC's also give you the possibility to change the battle music. I highly recommend the Gekkoukan High one.Characters - 9/10Characters are what got me into this game in the first place. _childDocuments_.review: Makes light of your free time by slapping you in the face and making you lose HOURS of progress for no reason.Basically it allows you to enter a palace with -2 days left, AFTER the deadline for completing it. This means that you get to waste hours of gameplay inside the palace, thinking that you're making progress, just to be slapped in the face when surprise surprise, it tells you that you need another day to send a calling card. And then another day to get back in the palace again.So if you start after this completely unintuitive deadline, you FAIL 100% of the time. Pretty confusing right?After you fail you either have the option to get sent back a week (so lose even more hours of your progress) or load a savefile to an earlier day, IF you have one.Do the dev think they're smart? Are they making a statement against procastination? Or is it just blatant incompetence and malice?  Playing the game until the first palace is also plenty enough time to make your refund window expire. Pretty smart right?The first dungeon is basically a perpetual cesspoll of enemies, so have fun fighting the same guys AGAIN from scratch for another 5 hours.This has to be one of the WORST intentional design choices I've ever seen. Anyone in QA, the dev side or the production side that allowed this to stay in the game (and even in the "new" royale version) needs to get a reality check on how valuable people's time is.The first arc is basically an insane info-dump of many interwined mechanics, so I don't think I'm responsible at all for missing the treasure room deadline hidden in the calendar. And even if I did, the game should've given me a game over BEFORE I wasted 5 hours. After the game over, it should've sent me back a day or two, not A WHOLE WEEK. Obviously if you decide to read or watch the "5 things I wish I knew before starting Persona 5" you would know this, but the fact that you HAVE to read articles like that is already an indication of how badly designed this game is. Something so egregious shouldn't be in the game at all.I don't know if I'll be continuing with the game, because it definetely doesn't feel worth the time now

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think Persona 5 is a bad game overall, but personally I was extremely disappointed by the narrative. As someone who's played an unhealthy amount of RPGs, I have huge issues with this game's story and characters. The plot starts off with some bold themes of society reform and rebellion, only for them to fall completely flat after the first 10 hours of gameplay, mainly due to the terrible way party members, and especially the villains, are handled through the rest of the game. Basically, if you are going into Persona 5 looking for a groundbreaking story tackling social issues, then you'll be quite let down.However, my biggest problem with this game is its lenght. The story, which as I said ends up falling flat on its face pretty early, stretches over for an outrageous 120 average hours of play time, filled to the brim with superficial dialogues and self-centered morals. The only reason I pulled through was because I was already 40 hours into the game by the time I realized it was going nowhere with its themes.All in all, I'd only recommend Persona 5 to very, very new RPG players, or those with a lot of free time on their hands. If you are interested in the Persona franchise, then I heavily suggest trying Persona 4 Golden instead, which is also available on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely oozes with style. The early game is a bit of a slog but it never get's outright boring. 16hr in I wish dialogue was a little less cheesy but it's true to the vibe it's going for.----------------------------------------------------TLDR: The style, music, and combat(ish) continued to be the only standout aspects of the game for me. Having weak character writing, clunky (out of combat) gameplay, and really bad story pacing by design. All these initially passable things only souring as the game went on far longer than it needed too. I did not end it on a very good note. However, despite the complaining I still recommend giving it a shot as a lot of my complaints are very subjective. There are huge gaps between any main story events happening by design. This makes everything feel disconnected by hours of daily life shenanigans making what deceptively little story it has suffer in pacing meaning it has to speed run every time important stuff  start happening. This  be palatable if the character writing in-between palaces was strong enough but see the next section for why it isn't.Plot twists also sorta just happen only explaining why it happened after the fact when whichever relevant character goes  and suddenly remembers every minute detail that lead to it happening instead of building up to it organically. Joker is a self insert. 70% of his actions and thoughts are relayed through Morgana, sometimes feeling like Morgana's puppet rather than a character. Self Inserts are fine, but feeling like your every move is being ratatouille'd by the cat in your sack can feel asinine.The characters are fun with striking personalities. However, the confidant events make them feel like cardboard cutouts that that stop existing when not observed. None of them being capable of thinking for each other or themselves, the only character progression with them happening when Joker is available to tell them every step of their lives. Grab a glass and take a shot every time a Confidant says "Because of you." Fun and stylish but with unusual choices that makes it feels like it's constantly trying to stretch for time. -Spamming you with social stat pop-ups long after you've maxed them.-A few "puzzles" that boil down to walking back and forth over and over.-Weird palace objectives that feel like they were added just to pad the length. Example: *Phantom Thief* intercepts a transmission with a shadow that so happens to have what we need to open a door that is locked but we have to go all away around to get him. We go all the way around a 20min detour get to him then he teleports to where we already were because other dude bro said "maybe you shouldn't have that key card while up there where you aren't supposed to be" then we use the grappling hook the game conveniently forgets about to just go back where we started.Despite all this complaining (playing it this long has really made me bitter) I still recommend giving the game a shot even if I stopped enjoying it by the end. These things are mainly personal peeves and are very subjective and the core gameplay is still fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't decide if I should give it a thumbs up or down...I'm a Persona believer, I played 2 (well, half of 2) back on PS1 and was blown away by 3 and the social link system and of course the refinements we got in 4.I enjoyed 5R a lot but honestly I feel like they overdid the length of dialog and interactions. The ceaseless instant messaging interruptions (Oh, we are worried. Please don't worry. Bye.), the reiterative and pointless exchanges where they call you on the phone every time to rehash what you just did in person, and the horribly padded social link events for each confidant, did we really need 10 of them when barely anything happens in each? Add to that that some key combat related abilities are locked behind said events, which you won't know on your first playthrough. That can make the experience way less enjoyable for you for the simple fact of not leveling that s-link quicker.It also seems that by around half of the game they completely changed gears on the dungeon design and they decided to just make them huge and more grindy. Add that awful UFO boss fight and the fact that for the last quarter of the game they seemed to have ran out of boss ideas and they kept throwing at you the old no-weakness no-strategy variety. Just hit it for 10 minutes until it dies, heal as needed.I just had to kill four instances of the same mini-boss, with a 2 minutes walk between them, they are not called the same but they are fought the same way. It's not one of those endurance and resource management gauntlets either. You are given chance to heal and use items and even have to confirm before starting the fights. Someone literally thought it was a good idea to make you do the same lackluster fight 4 times in a row. Speak volumes of the design approach they took with P5.So I'm at around 100 hours into the game but in the last 25 I've been falling out of love with it. Sure it's absolutely the best and most refined Persona experience ever but also it feels like every single activity should have been trimmed by 25% to prevent the game from overstaying its welcome. It's actually pretty sad to spoil such a grand experience with needless filler....I wrote the above before finishing the game but since then I've finally beat it, both the standard final boss and the extra one. By that time I was so bored that I just switched the game to super-easy difficulty. The game just burned me out for weeks with pointless stuff to the point that I didn't care anymore to bother with the demanding final boss encounters.The game has great reviews but a completion rate (on steam at least) of less than 25% despite having a very-easy difficulty option. I hope ATLUS can read into that and fix those distorted desires.

_childDocuments_.review: I should open this up by saying that there are a great number of good things about this game. Aesthetically and thematically it's just up my street, and the combat and creature capturing elements are wicked. I should also say, I was a huge Persona 3 fan, and played that through to the end years back - but there's just a couple issues that make this game frustrating to the point of it being unplayable for me personally.1: The dialogue is too on-the-nose. Broadly speaking, it's well written - but details are repeated constantly. Obvious plotpoints are treated as new information, by multiple characters reitterating the same points throughout. Which would also be passable, if there wasn't just so much of it. You spend half of your time rehashing stuff, to the point where it's boring and irritating.2: The game is on rails. As in, I don't feel like any choices I make actually change the plot. The dialogue choices are, more often than not, just re-wordings of the same sentiments, and when they arn't - it feels inconsequential. Otherwise, it feels arbitary when I can/cannot do certain tasks, like heading out to town of an evening or not. Usually, Morgana will stop you from doing whatever that is, saying you should sleep - and there is no clear reason why, that night, above others, is treated differently. And also, no clear reason, why I should let a cat stop me from doing my damned laundry.3: Morgana's inane battle commentary. Every single attack is punctuated with cocky, high-pitched catchphrases. It adds absolutely nothing to the game, and I would probably not feel the need to even write this review if there was a simple option to turn it off. I don't need to hear "It's scary how good I am!" 4 times in a row, every single battle. There is literally 1 single line attached to each action out of a very small pool of outcomes - and it wears thin very quickly. The only option to stop it is to change to Japanese, or to turn the dialogue off entirely - and that's way too invasive a fix.Truth be told, if Atlus simply put in an option to remove the battle commentary from Morgana (and later apparently Futaba) I would happily change this review to a positive one and carry on playing - it effects the playability of the game for me that dramatically. And I know I'm not alone, there are multiple threads online about this specific topic. It's such an easy fix - please implement it.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 is definitely one of the games of all time. I remember hearing about it all the time back in 2016 but I never really cared enough to play it until now, that I got into the series as a whole.After being absolutely blown away and in love with Persona 3 FES and Persona 4 Golden, I was really excited to finally boot up Persona 5 Royal. Did it meet all of my expectations and blow me away even more to the point where I'd call it the best game in the series, as many others claimed all these years?I'll start with the overwhelming positives. The game looks fantastic, the music (as usual) is stellar and the world truly feels more alive than ever, considering P5 has more places to go to than 3 and 4 combined. The utilization of newer generation consoles and their power really helped push this series in a direction that has rendered its aesthetics and looks to be absolutely stunning. The story too was incredible but I can't say it was perfect. The words "Phantom Thieves" really start living in your head rent free after playing this game. The characters in this game are ones to remember; I can easily say that I enjoyed mostly everyone that joins the party, as well as the misc. social links. Wait, my bad, confidants. The changes to how your confidants give you abilities that influence the gameplay is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GOOD of a feature. And speaking of gameplay, the game is overloaded with quality of life options compared to its predecessors, which might make it too easy at times, but in all honesty helps take Persona turn based combat to a new level.. For example, while I do believe the story of P5 is awesome, there are some really low lows for all the really high highs. The beginning of the game grabs you by the balls and drags you through the best pieces of narrative seen in gaming history, only to later get a little annoying and obnoxious in the middle and occasionally drop some f-you bombs towards anyone who dislikes cringy clichès to finally become reach an incredible climax right at the end.I used to think that Persona 5 had a bad habbit of never ending and feeling EXTREMELY padded. Royal did not do this gripe of mine any favors and if anything, it only reinforced the feeling that the game overstayed it's welcome. Now it wasn't my first rhodeo as I had played Persona 4 Golden prior and done the extra content in that game, but it just felt a lot more naturally done than the way P5 went about it. Now having played the game a second time, I'm more open to it and and have come to terms with most things but it still doesn't really get as good as it did in 4.Now for my last, biggest complaint of all.There is nothing new to be said here. Morgana is an extremely divisive character and it's extremely easy to hate him. Personally, I really hate him. I cannot stand his head-over-heels attitude for Ann and the fact he has to come explain every minute detail about your daily/upcoming activities like the exposition horse that he is. Having now played the game for longer, I still can't get over just how much annoyance he adds to the game's social sim elements. Even though I know it will never happen, now seeing that even Metaphor will have a mascot-esque character, I sincerely hope Atlus does away with these annoying characters. (future me's edit: gallica is an amazing character and I love her) They add nothing to the game even if their Japanese audience tries to say otherwise.So to summarize, I definitely don't think that Persona 5 is overhyped or overrated or anything of the sort. It definitely met most of my expectations and I'm very glad I played it. This is a humongous game and it's truly hard to express every feeling without forgetting details and it's a game that everyone has to go through. I really hope that if one day we see a Persona 6, it takes the scale and improvements made in 5 and really puts them to good use.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember wanting to quit the game at hour 5-10. however progression-systems do begin to unlock overtime keeping you somewhat hopeful and interested. The story, combat, side-activities however, just isn't interesting enough to keep you entertained for the full 90ish hours you'll need to complete the game.- The story gets monotonous at times. It leans heavily on suicide to get us to care about the characters, which is just poor story telling. The leading character trait of most characters is their sense of justice, which gets old very quickly when all story dialogue is pretty much this.- The dating-sim aspect of getting to know other characters is less of a side-quest/side-story and more of a bland. uninteresting conversation, again centered around justice.- The combat. Stealth is a joke. Combat gets VERY grindy. It's a repeated cycle of aiming for weaknesses, going into an all-out-attack to finish the battle. Couple this with that fact that palaces are LONG (3-5 hours each) and your basically praying to get to boss battle at the end.- You'll spend ALOT of time outside of palaces doing side activities to improve social stats. These get boring quickly after you've played them once or twice. You'll spend 20-30 days (around 40-60 activities) between palaces, doing the same 3-5 activities again and again, its so boring.In general, almost every aspect of the game gets repetitive and no single aspect is worth the 90 hour time sink. Towards the end I played on mute listening to music and even then couldn't finish the game.

It took you at least 100+ hours of play to cover all the content;+ Very bright and elaborate characters that you will remember for a lifetime and an abundance of dialogues with them through which you will form bonds with the characters you need.+ Good combat system, in jrpg style, but with some nuances...I especially remember the system for creating new personas;+ You will have to remember your school program to pass exams at school, and perhaps you will learn something new. :)+ The possibility of romance with the theme of who you like and the system is worked out extremely well. :)+ Quite adequate system requirements and excellent optimization in the game.There are also mnuses, but there are not many of them:- Sometimes extremely lengthy dialogues between the main events, where I simply can’t save normally in order to continue later;- Sometimes the balance in battles and some final bosses raises some questions;- I don’t understand why they impose Kasumi like that if she is introduced only at the end of the game;- Some menu items are not very convenient. I don't regret the time spent. I highly recommend this amazing game to everyone.Score 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good that I paid $120 for it: I bought the original Persona 5 on PS4 and I bought Persona 5 Royal for Steam. This is a game so fun that I literally have myself and three other people playing it in our Discord server to exchange ideas. The characters, setting, art design, graphics, and controls all function perfectly, but it's the story, gameplay mechanics, combat, and of course, music, that sets P5R apart from any other JRPG I've ever played. It's just too much fun to put down, the story really sucks you in and in my honest opinion, these elements coming together so cohesively makes this one of the greatest JRPGs of all time and the best game in the entire Shin Megami Tensei lineup. That speaks volumes, because its predecessors - Persona 4 (Golden) and Persona 3 (F.E.S.) are also two of the greatest JRPGs of all time (VERY highly recommended if you like this one), so this game had gigantic shoes to fill - and somehow reinvented them in the process.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 136 hours to beat this game and I don't regret a single second. As someone new to the Persona franchise the best way I would describe this is a JRPG as well as its story smashed together with StardewValley in terms of feel. Every day cycle has you figuring out how to max your stats or do activities before diving into combat and gameplay.I highly recommend you play this game AS BLIND AS POSSIBLE (story is H U G E)! The only thing you need to know is get the person named Maruki to confidant rank 9 by mid Nov. to unlock the extra content. Other than that just start playing and enjoy the ride at your own pace. The music, characters (oh god the characters), and story are phenomenal and will leave you feeling like you got your money's worth in the first 20 hours which isn't even 1/3rd of the game. If you're interested in the slightest please check it out!

_childDocuments_.review: You experience the majority of the story through the eyes of the protagonist, who, after being falsely accused of assault, is sent from his hometown to the bustling city of Tokyo, where he is supposed to lay low and live an honest life during his year-long probation. Under the watchful eye of his probation officer, the cynical bachelor and café owner named Sojiro, the protagonist begins enrollment at Shujin Academy, where fateful encounters begin to set a thrilling and unforgettable story in motion. After discovering the existence of the Metaverse, as well as his unique talents that allow him to steal the hearts of the most evil individuals society has to offer, the protagonist, while being sponsored by a divine being named Igor and his Velvet room attendants, becomes the leader of the Phantom Thieves, a suave group of vigilantes and outcasts dedicated to reforming society.  Surviving the ups and downs of school life, choosing your daily actitivies wisely, strengthening the bonds with your confidants, finding new Persona users, working out at the gym, keeping the interest of your divine collaborators, planning and carrying out your infiltrations while staying hidden - P5R is a game that has you realize the importance of proper time management, to the point where you end up feeling motivated to implement a thing or two into your own life experience. As a Persona veteran who has played the P5 vanilla version, P5R on the PS4 console, and who could not resist the pull of a Steam release, I can assure newcomers to the series that you will not regret spending your money (OR TIME lol) on this masterpiece of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal sits on a backbone of a Calendar RPG, where you can do only two things a day: Go through dungeon crawling and turn based combat in either Palaces or Mementos, spent time with confidants, or pass these time periods in any other way this game gives you. Palaces change about once every month, and Mementos has randomized map layouts, but has it's depth limited to the amount of Palaces you've cleared. On the other hand, confidants provide a visual novel element to the game where your responses dictate how quickly you level them up. There's simply too many mechanics this game has for me to fit into one review in good faith, but rest assured they all blended together well, and is why I have the playtime I do. The story is good, too. Sometimes it drags on a bit, but it ain't too bad. The soundtrack is great. My two biggest complaints are that new game plus is nowhere near as enjoyable, with all the story segments, forced tutorials, and confidant ranks being skipped through and boring, AND that PC key configuration isn't the best. There has to be a button for everything a button is assigned to on the keyboard section of the controls. If I switch a button in the keyboard section to a button on my mouse, that mouse button being assigned to a button on my keyboard to make it work, that button I have assigned to my mouse might be used for another in-game action this game has that button assigned to it, making me have to find where it is, assign that action to something random, and only THEN can I leave the key configuration screen. Why can't certain game actions just NOT need a button assigned to them? Certain buttons seemingly can't be rerouted, either. The buttons this game uses for my Xbox Controller were perfectly fine thankfully, so I never had an issue. Other than those two, the game is amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal is a brilliant game that’s just way too ****ing long.The game at first is incredible. Your friends are well-written, fun characters. Your enemies are cruel, compelling antagonists. You’ll play through both intense conflicts and light-hearted breaks, creating an enjoyable story that feels fantastical yet somewhat relatable. The gameplay is also great. The turn-based combat is generally enjoyable, constantly adding new mechanics to keep things fresh, and the palaces (dungeons) each feel distinct from one another and throw mostly interesting challenges at you.However, the game really starts to drag after the first few arcs. The writing becomes wildly inconsistent, with a couple of the new party members feeling relatively lacklustre, and most of the villains incredibly generic. The gameplay also becomes stale, with palaces becoming repetitive and some mid/late game bosses being really poorly designed. It’s never necessary awful, but when each tenth of a game is longer than most full ones, a couple dull sections can really damage your enjoyment. It’s a shame because most of the game’s final arcs are really quite good but I found myself kind of just wanting to be done with it. The Royal content, for example, is incredible. It captures what made the early sections of the game so good and goes beyond them, featuring the game’s best antagonist, the most interesting party member, and a fascinating moral dilemma. But I definitely didn’t enjoy it as much as I could have due to it having gone on for too long by that point.I really did enjoy the game overall – it sits comfortably at a light 8/10. But I simply cannot recommend it. Its best content is really quite incredible but it’s not worth it in the end. Play Persona 4 Golden instead, a game that’s long but doesn’t feel like it’s often actively disrespecting your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the play time as this is play through number 5. I've completed Persona 5 and Persona 5 Royal twice each on PlayStation.It is absolutely not hyperbole when I say this game saved my life.I had never played a Persona game before so when this released in 2017 (in the UK) it completely passed me by, but in January 2019 my sister passed away completely unexpectedly and needless to say my whole world ended. I was struggling to cope and couldn't see any light at the end of the tunnel. I needed something to take my mind off of everything, I needed to escape and that's when I saw Persona 5 on sale on PSN. I had a quick read up on it and being a fan of things like Final Fantasy and some other JRPG's I decided to give it a go, as I was willing to try anything.For the next 2 weeks I became completely engrossed in this world and the characters and relationships that lie within brought me back from the brink, literally. I needed an outlet and escape from reality and this game so fully delivered that at least for a few hours a day, I could disappear into another world and fully forget all the pain and misery that was going on in the real world. I honestly do not know what would have happened if I hadn't have had Persona 5 arrive in my life at that precise moment.Having played the original and Royal through multiple times now I am also now fully aware that it isn't just nostalgia or me having heightened feelings for the game, it truly is a masterpiece and if you like JRPG's at all then you owe it to yourself to play this game.Thank you to Atlus for the gift of this game, it's for the reasons I've stated here that I will buy every version of this they ever release and I look forward to the inevitable Persona 6!

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal is in my opinion the perfection of turn based combat as well as an excellent social sim. It has a huge cast of unforgettable and well realized characters (and the SIU director), some incredible dungeon designs (visually and gameplay wise), the best video game soundtrack of all time, and a story that even with its 100+ hour runtime leaves you wanting to do it all over again. You will laugh, you will cry, you will probably cringe at some point (just being honest). Most importantly though, the game will assuredly leave an impression on you if you reach either the game's original ending or the "new" Royal ending. The story of Persona 5 is expertly crafted. The game starts in medias res, showing our protagonist, Joker, escaping from a casino while guided by his teammates. Joker is captured while escaping, and brought to an interrogation with prosecutor Sae Niijima. She proceeds to ask him questions that we as players don’t know the answers to yet, but those questions peak the player’s interest. She talks of stealing hearts and another world as though we should be aware of the meaning behind her words. Then we are thrust back in time to April of the same year. What then follows is 100 hours of riveting story arcs, with incredible party members, interesting supporting characters, and immoral villains. You discover another world called the Metaverse and learn that you have the power to change society by infiltrating palaces (a.k.a. RPG dungeons) and stealing the treasure of the ruler. Without spoilers I will just say that the game just gets better and better as it goes, culminating in a final act that is my favorite ending to any game. You will know all of these characters as people by the end of the story, and you will feel both extreme satisfaction and a bitter hollowness knowing that your time with them is at an end. Combat in Persona 5 is a very fluid affair. Rather than navigate menus and sub menus constantly. Most basic actions are just bound to single keys or face buttons on a controller. This makes the pace of battle incredibly quick, as by the end of the first palace you will likely have a handle on which button does what and never need to think about it again. Grinding is not really required at all, it is possible to beat the game without doing any (I know, I've done it). However, there is an instakill ability unlocked by progressing through the game that makes you instantly win battles with enemies far below your level and you still gain the experience and money from the fight. This makes leveling incredibly quick in the late game so no need for hours upon hours of mashing the attack button on stuff that poses no threat to you.The major mechanic that differentiates the combat from other JRPGs is the "one more" system. Hitting enemy weaknesses causes them to be knocked down and triggers a "one more" allowing you to take a second turn or hand that turn off to another member of the party for increased damage. These can be chained together through your entire four person party, culminating in your final party member doing massive damage for 0 cost. These mechanics and controls culminate in the best feeling turn based battle system I have ever used. Nothing I have played before or since has felt as good as this system has to control. Whether against common enemies roaming the palaces or the corrupted rulers of those spaces the game feels fun to play from beginning to end, which is incredibly important in a game of this length.An important aspect to mention when talking about how the game plays is the dungeon design. In game the dungeons are referred to as palaces, and without spoiling things I will say that they are all ruled by the villain of their respective story arcs. These are not randomly generated hallways and rooms that you will see repeated ad nauseum. Each palace is hand crafted and they are all visually distinct from one another. You’ll solve puzzles, sneak around, and do some minor platforming between the various bits of combat. No two palaces feel the same, which is impressive considering that they are at minimum around 4-5 hours to complete each on a first playthrough, with some being considerably longer. The combat isn’t the only gameplay however. Many of the ingame days have Joker just living out his life as a high school student. You do various activities like work out, study, eat, read, watch movies, etc. These activities raise Joker’s social stats, which in turn allows him to do more activities. Talking with your confidants (major NPCs that Joker has a meaningful connection to) will level them up, unlocking new abilities for Joker and his party to use while in the game’s palaces. Some have more use than others, but in the Royal version of the game, rarely is there an ability that is not useful in some way. Some of these confidants are locked behind social stat requirements. Making raising them important to making sure that you are as powerful as you can be.Throughout the game you unlock more and more places to explore outside of the palaces. These new places in turn open up new opportunities to raise social stats, provide new vendors for items, or serve as hangout spots for Joker and his confidants. The last thing to talk about regarding the game itself is the presentation. Everybody on the internet has heard people talk to death about how good Persona 5 looks. Unfortunately for everybody, I’m about to jump on that bandwagon as well. The art style on display here ensures that the game will never age. I’m not an art or graphic design major by any means so I don’t properly have the words to describe it, but just seeing the game in motion will convince anybody that art style is more important than raw graphical power.Likewise I’m not a music major either, so I can’t dive into the technical reasons behind why the music is so good. The soundtrack runs the gamut from slow somber tracks for the nights spent exploring Yongen-Jaya, to intense boss themes, and jazzy battle tunes. There are some true standouts that still hit me hard to this day after hearing them in their original context. I can listen to almost any song off this soundtrack anytime and never get bored of it. Everything stated above is just my opinion. I know over the years it has become trendy to hate Persona 5 and the Royal version for various reasons. However for me, this game hit at just the right time in my life and it hit me hard. I flat out hated JRPGs and Anime before playing this game, I thought of them as just “weeb ♥♥♥♥” and said that they “weren’t for me”. I only tried Persona because I had friends tell me that they loved it and that I would probably love it too. I went in with lower than zero expectations and came away not only willing to play more JRPGs, but also to watch anime that I had never given the chance before. For all the reasons that I have tried to list in this review, I was left completely floored by an experience I thought I was going to hate. I ended up loving the characters, the world, the gameplay, the music, the art, everything about it. It was the best possible experience to have as an introduction to the genre. _childDocuments_.review: I have my problems with Persona 5's bloated story, its cheesy and weak writing, the fact that the game peaks with the first palace narrative wise, the game's themes and messages being frequently contradicted to tell an unfunny joke or a strangely inappropriate sexual one, and the characters being done kind of dirty in the narrative many times. I don't think this game is a masterpiece as I once did back in 2018. However, Persona 5 does more than enough to almost make you forget about its failings. Its got an absolute BANGER of a soundtrack, its style is unmatched, the characters are a joy to experience thanks to their great voice actors and good enough character writing, and the big one, the gameplay is MY JAM. What ultimately ends up saving P5 for me is the gameplay loop of thief by day, highschool student by night. While not all palaces hit the same high quality, it's still awesome to experience them. It's great to see what kind of narrative storytelling is done through these palaces to bolster their palace rulers, even if most are one dimensional baddies. I love the act of combat and recruiting demons to fight on my side. I love fusing personas and seeing what kind I need for the fights ahead. I love recruiting new party members because not only is it a new homie, but it's someone new that I can experiment with. I love planning my schedule to maximize my dungeon adventures and my time hanging out with some legitimately compelling characters. Both the social sim and dungeon crawling aspects of the game blend and complement each other beautifully.Persona 5 gets a lot of stuff wrong, but it gets more than enough right to make this adventure still worth experiencing. Plus, this is the Royal edition, which makes some incredible QOL improvements and adds, and I'm not kidding here, the best section of the entire game. Even if it is at the end and extends this already bloated game.Also! This PC port is great! Bit miffed about no ultrawide, and the 120fps cap is a bit annoying, but in the amount of time I've had with this version, it runs great on my gaming PC and on my Steam Deck.This'll be my 4th time playing this game, so even though I sounded a bit negative, I still ultimately very much recommend this game!
