_childDocuments_.review: So for full disclosure I've played this game to completion at least three times by this point. First with the original on PS4, and then the first launch of the Royal Edition on PS4, and now finally once again on PC (Steam).As such it would be very fair to say that this game is one of my utmost favorites. Like all JRPG's this game is very long, especially if you are a first time player in the genre, and especially for this entry in the series. However, this entry is also the easiest to get into out of the rest in the entire series. It has quite a number of quality of life updates compared to Persona 3 and Persona 4 and it takes a bit more time explaining the concept of the game longer as well so it's not as confusing to get into. However, this Version of Persona 5 Royal also comes with a bunch of DLC that does dramatically lower the difficulty in the game if you decide to use it. The upside is that if you decide you want to use the DLC the game does come with harder difficulty settings that you can chose at the start that will balance things out. Though for folks coming through again or are already familiar with the Persona Series as a whole, that may still not be enough to keep the challenge. But that's not too much of an issue in my opinion.I feel that where this game shines the most is the story and presentation of the story. It starts off pretty low-stakes and takes plenty of time to introduce the player to the setting and the various party members they meet, and many of the side-characters get their time to shine in the narrative as well, though on a more symbolic and meta-level. For the most part Persona 5 Royal does follow the standard RPG tropes when it comes to story telling, but that's not a bad thing at all. It handles them very well and can become really engrossing to see how the story takes those tropes and uses them to weave it's own story. Helping the story of the game is the absolutely killer soundtrack that just keeps going strong song after song; scene after scene. It really helps set the mood and tone, further enhancing the game's atmosphere. I highly recommend buying the OST if you can.All in all, without spoiling anything I heartily recommend giving this game a fair chance. It will require some time investment and ability to overlook some standard RPG conventions these days, but I feel that it is worth it for the absolute treasure of a story it presents. Especially if themes of Rebellion against Corruption, Dealing the with the Pain and Sorrow of Loss and Life, and Being Trapped in the Past are your cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: So, didn't want to leave a review until I entirely finished the game and if im being completely honest, this is the best game I've ever played.(Ill try to avoid spoilers)Difficulty.I love turn based games and this has a really cool system for it, but some things can make the game really easy because of a mechanic that allows you to switch to your party members with buffs after landing a weak hit without wasting any of there turns after its over. This gives you an incentive to actually level them up instead of just the ones you like and leaving the ones you don't like.Metaverse.This is the fictional world of this game and I believe it does it well, this is where the main action happens and other then a few kinks it needs to work out its fun, the main one is save points which can get REALLY annoying if you just want to go to bed but you cant get to a save point, other then that the main premise is fighting shadows and make your way to the top to fight the main boss of the place.Length.This game is ridiculously long and at the time of review I have played it for 120 hours or so and that's just for the base story including dlc (the main games story takes about 100 hours), some of those where afk due to not wanting to lose progress but wanting to take a break but most of it is actually playing it. _childDocuments_.review: It's really a weird combination of Digimon, visual novel, time-management/life sim, and JRPG somehow works really well without getting too bogged down by anything other than time-management anxieties.Most of your game will be chunks of ~21 or so days where you're managing school/social life while diving into a "Palace" (dungeon) before a deadline can give you a game-over (You will be warned MANY times about needing to get certain steps done so that doesn't happen)The "Palaces" (Dungeons) are mostly headache free, with the exception of the boss of the 5th Palace and I did get lost in the 6th palace for a bit. You'll have ~21 days to find a path to the "treasure", send a calling card, and then steal the "treasure", which makes up most of the game loop, with ~9 palaces (depending on how you count them, and if you meet a certain ending's path conditions) and a decent chunk of downtime between each palace.On normal difficulty, I didn't see any need to grind so long as I didn't skip too many enemies AND was good at using the combat system (Hitting thing's weaknesses to knock them down, triggering "One-More", or a "Hold-up" if it was the last one needed to be knocked down).Story: 3.5/5Characters: 4/5Combat: 4/5Music: 5/5Overall: 4/5For me, it's been a really long time since I last wanted to crack open a turn-based RPG, with both Octopath Traveler and Bravely Default not succeeding in saving a genre I had grown tired of... But Persona 5 Royal changed that for me.Also, absolutely need to RESPECT the 'M' ESRB rating, there are some dark scenes in many characters story.

_childDocuments_.review: The consensus I see in the reviews of this game is that it positively affects your life outside of the game as well, and I wholeheartedly agree. Somehow, a game like this has given me motivation that I have never experienced elsewhere. One of the big ways it does this is with the use of time. The most free time you can get allows you to do two things per day, and early on the game warns you to make good use of your time. At the end of my first play through, I hadn't yet managed to max out my friendship with all the people you can meet, I only barely maxed out my social stats, it left me with so much more to see. But even if I couldn't do everything I wanted to with the time they gave me, I wouldn't have done nearly as much as if I slept through the free time in the evenings.Not only does this game visually demonstrate why you should use your time, but many of the songs heavily encourage you to chase something. Follow your dreams, you can make an effect on others' lives, don't give up. A large message of this game is that the goal is to "Help people in need," and it feels almost as if players are the ones in need, even if they don't realise it.And honestly, I'm not gonna tell you to get this game, get it if you think you might like it. But even if you don't get it, or maybe can't get it, I think listening to the OST is also an experience in itself. During quarantine on an average day of online schooling, I decided to start the P5 OST in its entirety, including the P5R songs, and I was crying by the end, despite not knowing a damn thing about how the story goes. This game truly does feel life changing. It absorbs you until you finish it, and leaves you with a fresh new perspective on life. I started it early January, and only finished it early July. In this time it has become my favorite game, and I will be playing others in the series shortly. I hope you can get as much out of this game as I did :)

_childDocuments_.review: I have now purchased this game four times (PS4 Digital, PS4 Physical, PS4 P5R Phantom Thieves Edition and now Steam) since 2017, and still believe it's the best contemporary JRPG available to purchase and the gold standard for the genre. I don't have anywhere close to the right words to describe how excellent this game is. This is a masterclass of storytelling, character development and turn-based combat. The PC port runs well, but this is a game made in the PS3 era, and isn't too demanding on hardware. This is a 90+ hour story (unless you skip all the dialogue) that delivers every step of the way, but does rely heavily on its artstyle, music and characters to deliver on its potential. Royal is P5 + Qol update, with the main additional content feeling like a bulky £20 DLC. If you haven't already played P5, this is the best place to start. If you have, it's difficult to tell you if Royal's additional content is worth paying full retail for again.

While the Phantom Thieves could have been written much better, this game has some of the most interesting side characters in the franchise imo. Characters like Iwai, Sojiro, Kawakami, and Maruki honestly carry the game. The soundtrack slaps, the UI and art style is beautiful, voice acting is perfect, and the gameplay is objectively the best in the franchise. Palaces are a massive improvement over P4 dungeons, and there are way more side activities you can do than in any other Persona game. Not only is this my favourite Persona game, it is my favourite game of all time. Even though it's flawed, I'm sure you'll still have a very good time with it on your first playthrough. If you would want to replay it numerous times, I recommend you do so with mods, at least the ones that completely rework the difficulty. Either way, if you're at least a tiny bit interested in P5R, then go for it and buy the game now. I 100% recommend it and honestly, most of the problems this game has are only really noticeable if you are mentally deranged just like me and put over 1K hours into this damn singleplayer game lol.tl;dr game so good I haven't touched grass in months 👍

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, and it's one of the best JRPGs I've played. It's strongest selling point is the aesthetic of the game, with great visual design and audio throughout the game both in its base form and in this, the Royal version. The combat is very solid, the different levels are all unique and interesting with various puzzles to mix it up between bits of combat, and the "social link" character stories are almost all good in some way or another. That said, the game isn't perfect. I had some technical issues running the game, with some sluggish framerates here and there especially in Royal specific sections, an odd recurring issue where the game would randomly tab out (not crash or anything, just force me to look at a different window I had running on my PC), and another issue that would cause the game to no longer recognize my controller until I pressed a button, so all the button prompts would switch to the PC's controls and the mouse cursor to appear though this was the most minor problem of all the technical stuff. Also, if you've played the base game before and want to see the Royal additions, it isn't a whole lot that makes it worth it over the base game. If you're new to Persona 5, I definitely recommend Royal, but if you have a copy that isn't Royal, you're not missing much. The "True Ending" characters are among the worse ones of the game in my personal opinion, and ultimately didn't feel like it added much to the ending of the story, instead just being a simple bonus of content. Doing that is fine, but to me calling this content part of a "True Ending" makes it feel like it should substantially change the outcome or do more than just add a 30 second cutscene tacked onto the end. All that to basically say, without spoilers, that I like most of the writing but I have problems with what was added with Royal. I've probably played close to 250 hours total between my time on PC with Royal and on PS4 a few years ago with the base game, and it's fun the whole time. It's gotten me interested in the other Persona games and I hope to enjoy them as much as I like this game. Highly recommend trying this one out if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR.  If you like JRPGs or just RPGs with rich characters and solid stories, then you will like this game.  Its a Rpg with platforming mechanics, and deep social sim mechanics.  If that sounds interesting, then this is a game that you should be playing. I loved Persona 4 golden when I played it on the Vita years ago.  It was my first experience with the Persona Series.  While that game oozed substance and had great characters, there were a few things that could have been improved which have been taken care of in Person 5.  For one, combat has become much more involved;  Instead of just using your personas to attack and beat monsters, you have melee attacks, ranged weapons, different attack types, and many other mechanics which add a ton of variety to a type of combat that can certainly get repetitive. The team behind this game also went to great lengths building a new engine specifically for person 5 and it shows in every aspect of the game.  Everything from the flourishes when you beat a monster to the way that characters can interact with the world via the platforming sections and even the stealth mechanics.  All of these things further add to the formula that made Person 4 so great in the first place. Persona 4 while being a great game, also lacked some things in the way that it was presented overall.  The social aspects of the game almost felt a bit too much like padding in places, but because the characters were so fun to interact with, it didn't matter.  Persona 5 does follow this to some extent but it adds more to justify the social aspects of the game than the former title.  Many of the characters you interact with are not characters you are going to be bringing into combat but they are interesting non-the-less.  And following this idea, the characters in Persona 5 are much more proactive.  Rather than waiting for the next thing to happen, they go out in the world and take the initiative; this really makes you feel like you are a phantom thief.  As for the story, well I can't comment on the full story since I've only scratched the surface but thus far I am really enjoying the deeper adult themes of this game.  Persona 4's themes were more centered around things that you'd expect to see in a high school drama while Person 5 explores themes of criminality, psychology, victimhood, and villainy (as well as many other things).  The antagonists feel like scumbags but they are not one note scumbags; for the most part you can understand how they got to where they are now. The victims also react like real victims; when someone is abused they rarely will try to get revenge or turn on their abuser and instead attempt to rationalize why they were abused,   This port is just really damned good.  Its solid in many ways and it runs extremely well on the steam deck.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 is another of those games that are treated as a masterpiece but once you play it yourself... It's rather disappointing. You really can't trust weebs and should always keep your expectations low every time they start praising a work to this level.For a game that focuses on story, it sure does not do a good job at it. It wants to send a message but not even the writers believed in that message themselves, a basic example is that it'll tell you about how it's not good to be reducing girls to sex, only for later on reduce those same girls to... sex, not just through their outfits but because they thought that it would be a good idea to try and turn it into a relationship simulator mixed with the usual JRPG style almost 2 decades ago and it only got worse from there.It didn't change much from the previous 2 games, always having that one character whose only function is to be preying after girls even if that completely destroys their personality and really for me the thing I disliked the most was Yusuke's mistreatment, he is one of the few good characters and after his arc is over he gets reduced to nothing but a target of jokes.Yusuke, I liked him a lot while playing. The game treats him like he's a pervert and make that a frequent joke, none of the other characters want to accept that he is being honest when he says that he has no interest in the sexuality of the body and that was never funny. He's starving and none of the characters ever consider helping him, he's a joke for them — Yes it was funny when he said「先日公園で、うまそうなキノコを発見してな…」but the reason for him to be saying that is not. Why do I have to watch him suffer when the protagonist makes so much money he could help his friend eat? Does anyone find that funny?Something similar happened to Ryuji where he went from being a friend that's a little dumb, but with a good heart, to a friend that only thinks about sex. The writers have done this twice before and somehow still think that it's funny, same with the homophobia that came out of nowhere with certain 2 characters that kept going after Ryuji... Not to mention they turned him into a punching bag when he used to get beaten by his father.The game wants you to see the main cast as good guys but they can't even treat their own friends well.Persona 5's story as a whole is bad. Near the end of the base game there's a sudden change in tone that came out of nowhere, absolutely no building up, no indication that it would ever take that route — They couldn't even bother to make it a gradual process, but that's what happens when you think that it's a good idea to introduce multiple characters and never really develop any of them, so why would they be able to develop the world itself? When there's barely any time for the relevant individuals to grow?Maybe it could have worked out if they had limited the number of characters and focused more on developing their relationship without any of that romancing aspect. Maybe if they had kept the same direction the game seemed to be going towards at the start, one of touching on more serious themes and respecting their weight and its impact on the characters that go through those things it could have worked out. Instead, we get a teenager mess where none really act like they've been through things. They don't even allow tragedy to happen, everything needs to be GOOD and nothing BAD can happen, there has to be a good end for the good guys and a bad end for the bad guys!Older teens, which seem to be the target audience of this game, aren't stupid and they can handle negative feelings and they don't need someone to hold their hand and tell them explicitly that someone is bad, it's good for them to be thinking about that on their own so they learn how to interpret media.It's quite ironic how they want to talk about injustice but can't not include homophobic (that was going to step into transphobia territory at some point during development) jokes, that unlike Persona 4 you can't excuse it with it being normalized at the time of its release, and can't respect their female characters and the male characters who were victims of violence.Why does Ann always need to be used as a weapon of seduction? Why is Ryuji nothing more than a "funny guy" character when he had a rough childhood, much like Yusuke and Akechi?Why can't Yusuke be treated well without everyone acting like he's an Alien? Wasn't the point that some people are treated like trash the moment they lose the one thing that gave them value and society throws them away, and this time it could have been different?It could have been more serious about how the power adults, parents in special, hold over kids destroys them and how power as a whole is used to shut down those who dare to oppose big figures that benefit from that structure, but they wasted it on making it about killing a single bald guy and a divine being.I hate Morgana.I need Morgana to get mauled.I hate Morgana. I need him euthanized.The girls only exist for you to romance them, much like the other characters, they're shallow and basic, archetypes. Hifumi is nice, but like Yusuke she doesn't get enough screentime and, in my opinion, they could have had great interactions if she hadn't been replaced with Makoto.The art isn't all that great either, it's decent but when you compare it to Persona 2's it's clear that something went wrong, the heads are all weird and the expressions oddly stiff. Just look at the distance between each eye and try to imagine what the cranium looks like, or really just the top part of the head, it's ENORMOUS. Everyone loves that UI but if you have weak eyes like mine it can hurt after a while because of how red it is and sometimes I don't want to see all that moving around, it gets tiring.Yes, the design for the characters is good when it comes to their casual clothing — again because of how what the girls, other than Haru, wear as their phantom thief outfit, whatever it's called in English — but the sprites aren't and many look bad after you look at them for long enough.Honestly, not even the models for the humans are that good.Can the game be enjoyable?Yeah, it can. I had lots of fun despite those things, I almost stopped playing after Yusuke's arc because of how boring it got and he was The reason for me to play, but if one enjoys easy grinding and a simple fighting system it can be fun for a while — Unless what you want is an enjoyable and good story, then no, you won't be enjoying it that much and should play any other SMT game if it needs to be from the franchise.There's really nothing much special about it as a whole. You'll play it once, have fun, and then not really touch it again once you remember how bad the story is even if you crave some easy leveling up game or miss a character you liked.It's only slightly better than Persona 4, but enough for me to finish what comes after the "final boss".Also, I hate Morgana.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is mid at best, if I'm being entirely honest.That being said, TL;DR, if you enjoy anime stuff and have enjoyed previous installments of the series or just like mechanically basic JRPG's, you'll probably enjoy this game.Now to get into the bulk of my issues with this game:There are some frustrating aspects of the main story line and some of the side quests, particularly the dark themes combined with the annoyingly naive disposition of the main cast. Some villainous characters in the game also never get their just dues. Minor spoiler: the fact that we couldn't send the couple making essentially CP to jail is a travesty.Also, I seriously doubt the general public would give a ♥♥♥♥ if some unethical rich dude died of a heart attack. I, in fact, think that a huge chunk of the population would enjoy it and most of the rest couldn't care less.Some anime tropes that are insufferable and unfunny are also squished into this game and I find that to be pretty annoying, like casual sexual harassment from the main male cast. An anime staple, I know, but come on, that stuffs never been funny. However, Persona's strong points are still strong in this game. Most of the social links and side story development are satisfactory, this is also probably most of the reason why people play these games. I know that's why I kept playing it.The bulk of the non-combat gameplay is basically a hold over from the previous games, which is fine, cause there wasn't anything really wrong with the daily activities your character did between dungeons. This is also where a bulk of the side character developments happen and therefor, are the best parts of the game.The dungeon crawling and exploration is also largely a hold over from the previous games, which is a shame cause that was always Persona's weak point. They added some minor problem solving and platforming/exploration aspects to the game, but they're so easy that they're a minor distraction at best. Dungeon design varies from bland to extremely poor, with no outstanding levels that are fun to play, with the later dungeons being full of back tracking, looping rooms and basic puzzle solving in same-y looking corridors and rooms full of the same enemies.Combat is also mostly similar to the previous games except they've added a bunch of mechanics to make it even easier like the sneaking mechanic which makes ambushes trivial. This only gets easier the further the story progresses. They did add a few new elements and status effects along with tech skills and such to spice it up but the mid-late game will still revolve around your OP MC one shotting mobs and nuking bosses as quickly as possible using overpowered Persona's and builds. This of course is only applicable if you know how to use the fusion system, but that's not difficult to learn and fusion guides are plentiful on the internet if, like me, you just want to smash through the dungeon segments as quickly as possible so you can do more side character development. The art direction of this game, like the other games in the series, is stellar and in fact might be the best yet. I'm also certain this is a huge chunk of the reason why the game scores so highly despite is numerous flaws.Anyways. that's all I can think to say about this game. By no means is it perfect in my opinion, and I did find a big chunk of it to be pretty frustrating, but I did enjoy my time with the rest of it that didn't annoy me and I don't regret purchasing or playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: There are games that you adore purely out of enjoyment. Baldur's Gate 3 and Hades come to mind for games like that. There are also games that you love because of the message it gives, the story it tells. These games really make you think about what you just played, and they stay with you for months, even years. Games like Omori and Outer Wilds are peak examples of this. And yet, Persona 5 Royal managed to accomplish both of these feats at the same time.I'm sure it's clear by that first paragraph, but Persona 5 is possibly the best game I've ever played. I've been on the fence crowning games "the best." For so long, Omori held that title for me. However, Persona 5 is the very first game that has me doubting that fact. Like, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game is incredible. I was honestly a bit hesitant to approach this game. JRPGs combat has never really hooked me in, and seeing the daunting 100 hour playtime associated with P5R didn't ease my doubts. However, I've always been a gamer who puts story and the characters above all else, and so many people online raved about those aspects in Persona 5. So when the game went on sale, of course I had to buy it.And thank god I did. I remember seeing the opening towards the game and being shocked that it was fully animated like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ anime. My expectations shot straight up after that, and Persona 5 met me there. There's one thing I appreciate with Persona 5 and it's the lack of hesitance or sugarcoating for serious topics. There is some dark stuff that is covered in this game, yet it's all dark stuff that exists all across our world. Take the first palace for example. Kamoshida, the first main antagonist, is truly an awful piece of ♥♥♥♥. And the game isn't afraid of telling you the horrendous stuff he's done. Physical and sexual abuse, death threats, pushing someone to suicide, all under the guise of a school's most acclaimed teacher. It truly is horrifying the crimes he's done, yet I think Persona 5 does really well in telling it. The entire point of the game is pointing out corruption in our world today and how we should stand up against it. Not everyone has magical powers like the characters in Persona 5 do, but we all have some power to stand up to injustice. Of course, I don't want to undermine anyone who's going through hard times. Hell, Persona was my escape from the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ things I was going through in my life. I just want to say that in the end, everything will inevitably get better. It could take a day, a week, months, or even years, yet it's important we don't forget that. I think deep down I knew this lesson, but it truly was Persona that revealed the full extent of the truth. If you're wondering, the story remains amazing throughout the entire game. There are close to 10 palaces (don't want to spoil the true amount), that each tackle heavy themes, and I loved all of them. Though of course, a story is only as good as its characters, and like I've said already multiple times, Persona's characters are abso-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-lutely amazing. In fact, I'll go through each of the main cast individually. Morgana: Whether he's a cat, a human, a car, or a helicopter, this little fella has grown on me so much. I'm not going to lie, I really didn't like Morgana originally. He was always a bit stuck up and quite honestly annoying. The story however does him such a good justice. He's an intensely insecure and flawed character, yet grows on the Phantom Thieves around him, just like how he'll likely grow on you when you play. Wish he was better in combat though...Ryuji: I probably embody Ryuji the most out of any character. A lovable, sorta air-headed goofball who wants the best for the people he loves. Ryuji's character arc is by far the best in this game, and it really isn't close. I don't want to spoil too much, but his character growth is just so, so heartwarming to see. I couldn't help but have a beaming smile whenever he appeared on screen. He's also a runner who had a really bad knee injury just like me. How could we not be bros?Ann: Probably a lot of people's "waifu," if you can really have one in a game of teenagers...It's pretty clear the Persona markets Ann as the sultry, seducing type of character, but I personally think that it actually benefits Ann's character a lot. She goes from a girl who lacks any self-confidence or love for herself to someone who practically oozes confidence wherever she goes. Her positivity is frankly infectious, and her interactions with the rest of the cast always makes me laugh. You know, Morgana simps over Ann, even though he's a cat...Yusuke: If Yusuke didn't exist, Ryuji would be best boy. Unfortunately, Yusuke does exist, so sucks to be Ryuji. I love that Yusuke is so unabashedly himself. He's not afraid to express his weird artist brain nor speak whatever is on his mind. I constantly think of random scenes or quotes from Yusuke that never fail to make me laugh. He brings good-natured humor into the game that somehow doesn't feel forced or unnatural, even in the most serious of moments.Makoto: I said earlier that I embodied Ryuji, but Makoto is the one I relate to the most. Her dealing with the expectations of being the "perfect child" at school is something that I relate with. Having such intense pressure being placed on you that you feel like you can't do anything sucks, and is something that Makoto slowly learns to grow out of. She learns to find what she truly wants to do, not what others want her to do, and that's a lesson that I learned recently as well. Her strict yet kind personality really made her be a welcoming presence in the game, especially to counteract all those goofballs I listed above. Plus, her dating dialogue is really cute. Such a dork.Futaba: Similar to Yusuke though while he's an artist, Futaba is a gamer. I lied when I said Ryuji's character arc was the best by a country mile. Futaba is honestly right on par with him. She practically becomes a whole other person by the end of the game, yet the growth she went through makes it seem so natural for Futaba as a character. Her interactions with the cast are hilarious, as she uses the internet slang that the rest of the group never really seem to catch onto. Futaba also has some of the most emotional scenes in the entire game.Haru: I really wish Haru was in this game longer. She has the disadvantage of being the last main cast character introduced, which really limits her screen time compared to the other characters. Despite that, Haru was such an amazing character to watch and grow. Similar to Makoto, Haru is able to really find her footing in life and pursue what she wants. She starts out as someone who'd so easily bend to others, yet ends up as one of the most strong-willed characters in the game. She's also by far the kindest character in the game, always going out to make sure the others are alright. Though I swear to go she has a violent other side...Those are all the main cast, but there are 15 or so other characters that you can build relationships with. Some of my favorites are Sojiro, the father figure in the game, and Yoshia, who's simply the GOAT. While the main cast is amazing, it's these alternate characters that really make this game stand out from the rest. Every single character in this game is amazing and memorable, and I will be remembering all of them for a very, very long time.Overall, Persona 5 Royal is one of the best games I've ever played. Either the best or the 2nd best, still not sure right now. From it's excellent story and themes to its characters and even the above average JRPG combat (it's honestly great, but I physically don't have enough words to talk about it in this review), this game is amazing from top to bottom. It's a long ride, but oh boy is it worth it for the absolutely cathartic ending. I've never cried so much because of a game in my entire life. Hell, maybe even in general. 12/10 game, please do yourself a service and play.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this up I couldn't think of any major cons for this game. It was my first persona game so I didn't know what to expect. The characters are mostly the highlight here, Ryuji, Ann, Yusuke and everyone else are pretty well written and I love how most characters are very unique. No two characters feel the same. They all serve their own specific roles and they do it well. One big plus for this game is definitely the whole noir/jazzy/classy style. Something about it just tickles my brain in the right spot. A massive personal complaint that comes to mind however is the final palace. It is very long and it feels very undercooked. The boss at the end was a visual treat and it finished the game off with a bang but any and all interest left out the window when the palace was artificially extended with pointless puzzles and for lack of a better term exposition dumps. Overall the game was an incredible experience and I recommend it wholeheartedly.

The Social sim part of the game is also pretty good although it's not exactly the focus of the game you can take part of many activities during your day be it along or with confidants. The BadWell I don't think the game has any glaring issue, the only thing I did not like was the AA the game has, no matter what you do you get visible jaggies and shimmering on some objects, not even taking the resolution slider to 2x my native resolution helped that much. _childDocuments_.review: Completed today, 100% achievements.I've played many SMT games, and I'd overall rate it 8/10.  I enjoyed Persona 4 Golden better as many do, but I hate saying that as a way to devalue just how much this game offers.Better graphics.  Bigger world.  Great detail in palaces over random hallway simulator (despite still being fairly linear).  Incredible music.  It is so much for what you'd want as a sequel.Two things that really dig at me, causing the 8/10:1) The plot pacing is just... weird.  Staying spoiler free, I didn't feel quite as driven to a major narrative as I did in the other persona games (i.e. climbing Tartarus & discovering the origins of the dark hour, or slowly uncovering the mystery of the "TV world" and the murders).  You kind of take an objective immediately in front of you, with subtle HINTS of a bigger scheme... but you never really feel invested in it until the very end. There is a particular 'payoff' moment the story starts to really zoom VERY late and it's all great then... but the getting there can feel really strained. That said, the Royal story really brought me into that SMT-esque 'morality is a gray area' that I hoped to get more during the game too.2) The pacing of that story really got me too.  To maximize time, you complete palaces in one game day.  This puts the time between action sometimes REALLY long, and the daily life stuff can become tedious.  Coming off of other SMT games like SMTV, or Strange Journey Redux, where action and narrative interlock a bit more, this felt like peaks and valleys much more often.  It took me about 120 hours to do it all in one playthrough, but I feel like at least 20-30 of those hours could have been streamlined or sped up to minimize the valleys.That said, by the end, I was emotionally invested, and loved the game.  Small adjustments in pacing and story delivery would be all I could have asked for.  Everything else was on par with the high quality I expect from persona.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most overrated pieces of media I've ever experienced.TL;DR: It's not , but I wouldn't recommend it to just anyone. Only to those who are avid fans of really long JRPGs (or Persona) and that can tolerate a cast rich in characters with little depth (there are exceptions). . There are a lot of content locked behind those social links: ). Rush through the first one, interact with it as much as you can or you will not have access to the entirety of the Royal Post game. Besides giving you a warning that this social link is time limited, the game doesn't give you any clues of the content locked behind it. IMO: The game could be shorter-Joker is a silent protagonist whose only fixed personality traits I could recognize are his perseverance and ability to believe in others. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Best game of all time 10/10 just buy it. They somehow made the perfect game even better. Do NOT skip any dialogue on your first play through. It is insanely worth the price at around 100 hours per play through.Probably one of my favorite games of all time. I only have 57 hours on steam and have probably around 400 more on PS4. I try-harded and got all of the achievements on my first go. The royal edition adds so much to the game and I would definitely recommend this version to all new-comers. I would however also warn people who want to play the rest of the persona series to start with different games as none of them will feel as clean as this one. Story: The story of this game is set in Japan and is so fantastic that I wont even say a thing about it. Just do not skip any dialogue, look at youtube videos about it or spoil yourself. You will hate it. The character development for most characters is really nice to see and is usually very natural. Gameplay: The game is an RPG where you take control of personas which are basically like pokemon. You go through a story dungeon experience some story and go through the next story dungeon. Each of the dungeons are extremely memorable and do not overstay their welcome. There are some changes the royal version made that made previously very boring and unfun dungeons extremely cool. At the end of each dungeon there is a boss which in the royal edition also get a new phase when compared to the original persona 5. There are a bunch of elements which different personas can be weak to and the point of combat is to buff yourself up, hit weaknesses and either befriend or defeat the enemies. Since it is a JRPG there is a twist to the game. The twist being that the other half of the game is a social simulator where you forge bonds with your friends and teammates and others in the real world to assist your escapades in the dungeons. You also have to manage social stats which allow you to progress the social bonds with characters and do things in the world. The game starts off kind of slow. The tutorial ends on the 2nd of may where the first dungeon is used as a tutorial for everything. I PROMISE IT GETS GOOD.Music: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Atlas sound team is just crazy. I would highly recommend the soundtrack on spotify as you can kind of get the vibe of the game. I have nothing more to say than that some of the tracks are really upbeat, moving and some just out of this world. The music is used very well in game too and it never feels like your are forced to listen to the same song over and over and over again. I think 3 of my 100 hours on my first play through were just listening to the music in the background. Design: The game is stylish as hell. Every single menu, piece of UI, character, attack, area, city, dungeon and persona is designed extremely well. Each of the dungeons are visually different and explore really unique themes. There are a couple of completly animated cut scenes and attack moves which are really cool. Negatives: When you finish the game, depending on how invested you get, it will really be OVER.To conclude, get it. Do yourself a favor and get this game. It was the sort of experience where after the credits I thought, "Wow, its over.... Now what?" I will probably never forget this game and some of the soundtracks still give me goosebumps when I hear them. 10/10 TO GET TO THE TRUE ENDING YOU HAVE TO Even after 500 hours I still cant find the Ginza line ;-;

_childDocuments_.review: I've never been so emotionally attached to a game. One of the best RPGs to ever play period. There is A LOT of it and almost never-ending, but within it, is a super rich story, akin to a whole couple of seasons worth of an anime with multiple major plot developments throughout, an overarching storyline and fantastic character development. To some this might be the best part, and it certainly doesn't ever let you down. But if you don't like spending time running around, living a live talking to people and exploring the city, then you might get annoyed. But for everything else related to combat, progression and gameplay, would make even the most uncertain people drool due to the flavour and mechanics that the game throws at you at a steady and easy to understand pace.This game is great all around and you're guaranteed to have the playtime that will quickly surpass whatever price you pay for this. This is how true games are made within their respective genres.There are few games that mark me as much as this one, a masterpiece through and through.If you are into RPGs this is one of those games that you NEED to play and experience, it's on a whole other level. 10/10 - You'll never see it coming.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first run. The high playtime is mostly attributed to time spent AFK, or in the My Palace mode, actually getting through the game took closer to 150 hours and I attribute that to my generally slow reading pace in social portions of the game combined with grinding in dungeons and mementos.This game has tons and tons of story, with over a dozen of characters to build relationships and interact with. The amount of those story sections that are voice acted is less than half, but there's still enough voiced content to where it makes Persona 5 seem like a season or two of an anime, take that as you will.I mentioned that it took me a while to read this but that's owing to my switching all of the language options to Japanese to familiarize myself more with the kanji and kana. The kanji doesn't have furigana, but that isn't too surprising considering how uncommon it is to see in Japanese media that isn't directly aimed at children. As for the more gameplay focused aspects of the game; the build of your party becomes more diverse as you make it through the story, so it's going to be a couple dozen hours before you have a full party of 4 characters and longer still before you can start swapping them out. In addition to leveling up your party through combat, finding/buying new equipment for them, the social aspects outside of dungeons can unlock confidant bonuses that can grant new abilities be they buffs/resistances, attacks, or Persona transformations. Completely maxing out your relationships with party members and side characters widens the pool of Personas you're able to create in The Velvet Room.The Velvet Room is a hub that can be accessed at the entrances of dungeons and in several areas of the overworld. From there you can access combat challenges, but the main reason to visit is to fuse two or more Personas into stronger Personas. You can also drop off Personas to boost their stats in the Velvet Room. Unfortunately, it's possible to get incredibly powerful Personas for free very early on since this is a complete version of Persona 5 that includes unlocked DLC as part of the new game, so it may be difficult to ignore a free high-level Persona if you want to trivialize a majority of the game. The plot of Persona 5 is divided fairly well into arcs that cover themes of power harassment, sexual harassment/assault, suicidal depression, an over-arcing theme of free will, and quite a bit more, but the juxtaposition between those heavy topics with the fantastic ideas of changing someone's will by going through a literal mind palace and defeating their dark shadow keeps the tone from becoming too heavy. The core gameplay mechanics of using Personas is also fairly whimsical. The Personas themselves are all anime  personifications of deities, monsters, and figures from folklore or ancient religions so the idea of collecting them like Pokemon and using them to ultimately change the minds of awful people is one of the great appealing factors of the Persona games in general. If you're interested in achievement hunting, this is one of the easier games for that. It's lengthy, but much easier to unlock all of the achievements for this game than Persona 4 Golden. If you're interested in playing this game as a learner of the Japanese language, there are multiple voiced scenes that can be unlocked and replayed as you go through the game. Again, there's no furigana, but since a lot of terms are repeated, it's not terribly difficult to familiarize yourself with which words correspond to which kanji. Even in voiced scenes that can't necessarily or easily be replayed, there is a log function. It's restricted to giving you a log of that scene and that scene alone, but you can use it to repeat lines as long as you don't advance too far. I played through this game a couple of times on the Playstation 4 before it was available on Steam, and I can see myself playing it again in time. It's a really engaging game, the characters are really likable, and the presentation is fantastic. I picked this up for full price on Steam and was highly satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; good game, crap port. Maybe consider forcing FXAA in the Nvidia drivers rather than in-game to anti-alias the entire presentation including the aliased fonts (unless for some reason you consider this part of the intended presentation— I'm sure there's someone out there thinking this)I've played through this game twice previously. Partially on PS3, mostly on PS4 and a brief look at the PS4 version on PS5. If you want to play a Persona game you'll like this, but I'll admit that I prefer Persona 4— the extremely lengthy dungeons of P5, the crap story, inferior cast and even more glacial pacing detract a little. And really, I just prefer the small town vibe of P4. But I can't pretend that I don't like this game when I've played it for a couple hundred hours, yeah?The PC version is not great. This is essentially a PS3 game that was ported to PS4 and then had an expanded version exclusively released on PS4, which this is based on; as such, the game looks like a PS3 game with a nice art style more than a PS4 game. Performance is good, as you would expect given technological advances, but it could be better. An RTX 3080 10GB graphics card can put out 4K@120FPS, but it's very much on the edge. On the lower-end of things, a GTX 1650 Max-Q (40W) laptop graphics card can't max out the 2880x1800 resolution of my laptop screen, requiring 75% to avoid dropping frames at 60Hz in the opening scene and likely therefore 50% to avoid dropping frames throughout the game. It looks pretty rough at such a low resolution. Other games that look visually similar can run at the full resolution and refresh using this hardware.The game also doesn't support any anti-aliasing more advanced than spacial post-processing filters. TAA would be nice, DLSS/FSR 2 would be nicer. This is a game that has a very shimmery appearance and a lot of low-resolution aliased assets including, unforgivably, the fonts! Unless your resolution is very low, I'd suggest forcing FXAA in the Nvidia drivers to anti-alias the entire presentation rather than using the in-game option that only works selectively.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start off by saying that this game is simply amazing, and I could go on about every single thing good about this game for hours, like the art style. the combat system, and mind-blowing soundtrack, that still remains to have one of if not  the best soundtracks I have ever heard in a video game. This game is the literal definition of choosing a powerful theme and sticking with it until you have made a masterpiece. And yet, I still cannot say what exactly what this games theme is, unlike the previous two Persona games that made it obvious what the theme was. But I would say that the theme for Persona 5 would be about the true meaning of justice and freedom. Throughout the game we are constantly seeing people who are suffering from others distorted and twisted desires. It could be as small as a high school stalker, to plagiarism, to people in power who think they can do anything they want.It's honestly one of the best stories I've seen, but even after all that, there is one thing about this game that really does effect the enjoyment of the game for me. The confidants.If you're like me, you got this game because you loved playing through Persona 4 Golden. I liked how lovable each and every character was, and even the "villains" were really well thought out. A huge reason why these characters were so lovable was because of the social links the game had. Now, I knew Persona 5 Royal would be a whole different experience, but just wow. This is just tiring. I am not the type of gamer to skip any dialogue in video games, as I always like to hear what a character has to say, but this was the first game that has ever made me even consider skipping dialogue because there is just SO MUCH FILLER that it actually gets on my nerves. It doesn't help that most of the filler does not have voice lines and are just mumbles. Now i get that there's a thing called budget, but I think a lot of it could have been handled so much better. The only characters that I feel actually have proper character development with the perfect amount of filler in their confidants were Ryuji and Makoto, unlike previous Persona games like 3 and 4 which actually made every single social link feel fresh, with just the perfect amount of filler that really made you, the player, feel like you got to know the character better with every level you get a social link to. However, I understand that that is just my personal opinion about the game and I'm sure there are many people who disagree with me about the social link/confidant system the game has. So I'd say the only way to figure out if you like it or not, is to try the game out for yourself, so while I do still recommend this game, just wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me get this bit out of the way before I go heavily into detail for a TLDR: Do I think the game is worth playing?  especially if you find it on sale during a Sega or Atlus promotion. It's well worth the time investment if you're a fan of SMT games or turn-based RPGs. That being said... Do I think it's the greatest thing since sliced bread? Absolutely not. It's good, but caught on it's own leash. There will be spoilers, but they'll be marked.The game starts off at a pretty high note all things considered. It's a LOT faster to get into the gameplay than Persona 4 did, thank goodness. There's a number of improvements to the core gameplay that helps bridge elements from across the series together. I absolutely LOVE that the classic SMT demons are the Shadows now, just like they used to be back in Persona 1/2 and SMT if. It helps significantly to aid in memory and recognition rather than just color-swapped masked blobs and objects from 3/4, which I thought was a pretty significant downside to those games. The fact that you actually have to negotiate with the Shadows to recruit them like they are really demons, plus the commentary by them in battle, and the fact that they are no longer purely random in said negotiations are huge benefits to help bridge the gap between series. The Baton Pass mechanic further incentivizes identifying weaknesses by offering additional moves and decisions. Do you pass the baton to someone else, or double-dip for setup? The UI presentation is also very much improved upon and gives the game a unique style. A number of smaller quality-of-life improvements such as being able to save the game nearly anywhere in the real world and plenty of Safe Rooms helps you be able to pick up and play if you only want to burn a little bit of time for preparations, and is far better than having to go chase a bloody blue butterfly every day. The palaces offer actual constructed dungeons in a Persona game again rather than simply procedural-generated grids in voids, but Mementos does carry that side... Persona 5 Royal seems to hate the idea of letting the player off the leash entirely. Significant chunks of the game will basically have you railroaded by plot devices or a certain unlikable cat and deny you the opportunity to pursue Social Links or dungeon exploration. The Battle UI actually doesn't go far enough with showing who goes next unless you press on the D-Pad, and we're still in that weird Persona slant where buffs and debuffs are three-turn and single-target only unless you got 'Ma' versions. There's two new elements in Nuke and Psychic, but in practice, there's nothing interesting with them beyond just needing a unique element to tie to party members. This wouldn't bother me except that they already split Light and Dark into both offense/instakill at the same time so Nuke/Psychic just feel like pure filler as a result. In terms of balance, the game likes to 'try' to be difficult (especially if you play on Hard, did two playthroughs on Normal/Hard to compare) but also keeps fudging it's rolls for the player. Showtime moves, your Support interjecting, multiple fully-automatic Social Links and the Royal content all seem to act more like a helicopter parent yanking you away from scraping your knee up and learning your lesson through a bit of trial and error. It doesn't help that while you can ignore the Showtime button, a bunch of other things are basically automatically triggered without your inputs. Oh, and speaking of the Royal content....This is where we get kind of finnicky, and this entire section is probably going to be marked with spoilers to the point of impersonating some top-secret documents through this stint.In conclusion, it's well worth it if you find this game on sale, and perhaps even at full price if you're a real sucker for RPGs or the Atlus brand. But just be aware that this game is not the pure and perfect game that people often rave it is. It's got some problems that set me off in particular, but I still enjoyed it nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; An amazing masterpiece of a JRPG that has earned and exceeds it's laurels, even if the spinoff content will never live up to it. Persona 5 Royal has earned the hype. Anyone who has played a Megaten game can enjoy P5R thoroughly. There is very little that can be out and out *bad* about the game. I personally prefer Nocturne and SMT 1, however if you appreciate mainline for it's combat, you could enjoy this. This game isn't hard, at most you have to do basic main line strategy against Okumura. The baton pass system really adds to the one more mechanic, so it doesn't feel like a somewhat watered down iteration of press turn. The fusion system is great and offers a lot of ways to boost up personas so that you can pick and choose favourites. I feel that the absurd power that can be gained from fusion alarm and executions is maybe overkill, but it's great that the option is there just to mess around with. I found that I really loved what SMT 5 did with it's fusion, and I don't think 5R is as in depth but I can get the same feeling of having a big toolbox to work with rather than somewhat stiff fusion demands from older games.The characters are very hit and miss in my opinion. While it's worth doing social links just for the abilities you can get and their fusions, some characters I personally don't care for or actively outright hate in Futaba's case. Some fall to the wayside and you honestly don't lose out for it due to the game's difficulty. I appreciate the freedom that it offers, with very few social links feeling absolutely necessary like Takemi's. For the most part, I find the story and characters within them enjoyable and they feel like a pretty fun friend group. I prefer the investigation team from 4, but the phantom thieves have a very certain charisma to them. Out of everyone, I found Yusuke to be my favourite from the game for being such a fun social link. The balance is absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥, but that's no surprise. 5R's approach to absolute player freedom and making any team viable you can get some absolutely ridiculously powerful stuff. A lot of people deride 5R for this, but getting the higher echelons of power in this game does feel very rewarding and fun to just stomp down on the game. Great art direction and music really makes your absolute rolls feel great. Baton pass lends to it for sure, I think that without it 5's combat would feel much worse. It's not hard to clear dungeons extremely easily and quickly before the deadline, but it wasn't very hard to do in 4 either.The music has earned it's hype, it's great stuff. If you're curious, I personally recommend 'Ideal and the real', it's my favorite track to the game. Don't check the comments however, while most of them contain nothing but well wishes to Maruki's late voice actor, some may try to spoil the social link and it's best left seen for yourself. I can't think of an out and out bad song. Blooming villain is likely the weakest song in game, which is a shame considering it's the boss music. Thankfully this includes DLCS for outfits from older games like If... and 4, so you can always put on something more to your tastes by wearing a different uniform in the dungeons. I personally enjoy If's the most.Free time feels the best to spend in 5, the pseudo open world approach that 5 takes on is great. It's always fun to discover new locations and see what they sell and then keeping a mental note to come and check up on it again sometime for more items that spawn after a dungeon. It really adds to the immersion that 5 works overtime to pull off. It's only a shame Morgana feels the need to comment on absolutely everything.If you're wondering where to jump in with Persona or Megaten in general, start here. If you don't like what you're getting here, you won't like anything else Atlus has produced. 5 is the culmination of Megaten and Persona's time as a franchise and took what works. It drops the ball now and then, but this is as close to perfect as you can get from them. It's not my favourite game from them by a mile, but it would be ridiculous to ignore the absurd amount of love and effort that has clearly went into 5R. If you like JRPGS in general, this game is for you. I don't envy the team working on Persona 6, following up P5R is going to be nothing short of a miracle.

_childDocuments_.review: Starting off by saying I don't typically like these turn based combat games. I'll go as far as to say I actively avoid them. However my good friend Mae (hi you absolute goob) bought it for me so I decided to give it a try and low and behold, here we are.Persona 5 royal was an interesting journey for me, I started out being amazed by just how much dialog there was and how invested the game allows you to become for each of your friends (called Confidants). I found each of them ASIDE FROM MISHIMA, THAT LOSER, LEFT HIM AT 1 STAR WITH NO REGRETS (aside from not being able to get a particular persona, you've been warned), to all be rich in their own stories, personalities, likes and dislikes. Combat, for me, is what kept me coming back. Whether it be the Palaces or mementos, battling with personas is incredibly in-depth with all kinds of room for strategic play and varying playstyles. That is an aspect I found severely lacking in other turn based combat games. Furthermore the creatures you battle with, the personas, are fantastic. They all look awesome in their own ways and there hundreds of them to choose from. It often felt a lot like a pokemon game with a great emphasis on capturing and creating new ones to fight alongside you.There were a couple things I was not a fan of. Although I loved the social simulator aspect of the game, I did feel like it dragged on a bit from time to time. Sometimes there would be a large gap in time between palaces and I'd be like "Come onnnnn I WANT TO FIGHT".Another thing is: mandatory maxing of certain confidants. Not that the game forces you to max them, but it SHOULD and you will miss out if you do not. My advice if you've just picked this up? work on confidant rankings above all else ESPECIALLY Akechi and Maruki. Those 2 are vital to getting the most out of Persona 5 R. Ultimately Persona 5 R got 153 hours out of me to finish my first playthrough and I'm glad I got to experience the game even if it isn't my usual speed. I give it a 9/10. I look forward to an eventual 6th entry.Makoto is best girl btw

_childDocuments_.review: After completing this game... I am in awe.Persona 5 Royal is incredible in so many ways. Stylistically, musically, and narratively, it is top notch. I can't really understate how incredible this game is. Perhaps some people might find the combat lacking, but truthfully the combat is just a part of the gameplay of Persona 5 Royal. The real meat of the game is the time management/visual novel gameplay, which involves maxing out your "social links," which, while they do give you bonuses which help with combat and progression, also allow you to better get to know the characters of the story. I could sit here and talk about all the amazing things in Persona 5: the unique and varied designs of the characters, shadows, and persona; the many different narrative themes of Persona 5's 100 hour long plot; the satisfaction that comes from late game Persona crafting when you have essentially unlimited resources to try and build the best Persona you can. I mean, it says a lot about this game that the biggest criticisms I can come up with are things like: 1. The game arguably has too much content, I 100% it in 150 hours and there are still many challenges for me to complete. 2. There are so many different forms of progression that on normal the game becomes too easy too soon due to lack of balance (advice: if you are enjoying Persona's combat, wait to get Ryuji's social link to Rank 7 and don't grind too much; also, if you are a JRPG vet who wants a legit challenging experience on your first playthrough, I would set the difficulty to Hard as soon as you feel you'e learned the ropes). Around halfway through you pretty much have to actively avoid breaking the game balance. So yeah, absolutely incredible game, 10/10, don't spoil it for yourself. If you love JRPGs, and maybe even if you don't, you're gonna love this.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 was very enjoyable for me, but the ability to enjoy it comes with some hefty asks that most other games don't require for one to enjoy themselves.Two friends of mine tried it and quit within the first two hours for a simple reason: the start. I will be very blunt with you - it's bad, almost comically so. P5 Royal is a game that will take you over a hundred hours on average from start to true ending, and a very large portion of this time (30+ hours) is just a slog of a handholding tutorial with an outright grating narrative. The low points were the lowest i've ever seen in a Persona game by far.However, Persona 5 Royal is also a game where the more time you invest in playing it, the better it gets. As some of the most important twists and plot hooks are built up and revealed, you get a glimpse of the back-loaded greatness P5R has to offer- from the explosive combat to the satisfying life sim, tied in with an ongoing and interesting mystery to solve. It felt like the stakes were continuously rising- along with the highs that came with them. The only reason I can't flat out recommend it to everyone is because of the first thirty or forty hours.The turn based combat is fun and engaging yet streamlined for a JRPG, the soundtrack has some real bangers, and there are plenty of story moments that I enjoyed very much. The life sim aspect of the game was interesting to plan out too, as always. By the end, I had grown attached to the majority of the Phantom Thieves' group, and a number of the side-character confidants as well. The lows are low, but the highs are high.If you are someone who sees "thirty hour slog at the beginning" and has to do some serious thinking about whether or not you should try it, I don't think I can recommend the game for you. The only reason I got past the beginning myself was because I had not only been a fan of the series, but was also streaming it to some of my closest friends every second of the way, and we got to cut up about how bad it got in the beginning, making it much more bearable. If you're looking for a more accessible entry into the persona series, I will heartily recommend Persona 4 Golden instead. But if you're a fan of the persona series, or enjoy long-winded JRPGs with exponential returns on investment ala FF14, I would recommend giving P5 Royal a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Hooooo BooooiAfter over 100 hours of game play and finally finishing the third semester i can actually join the overall discussion around this game, and i gotta say...I love itStarting off with the game play aspect, as someone whose experience with turn based combat is essentially just Persona 4&5 so far, the combat here is pretty good. Animations are fast but flashy enough to not get stale after seeing on repeat for 100 hours, and mapping the controls to each individual button on a controller (or keys if your on MnKB) makes fights faster in comparison to Persona 4's approach on scrolling through them with the D-Pad. The 'one more' mechanic not only helps these encounters feel fast, but encourages the player to use different personas in their arsenal as well as their other party members. Theres also the 'baton pass' mechanic, this is such a fun tool use and fits right in with the Persona franchises love with striking weaknesses that its a surprise that none of the other games had it. While the turn based combat is fun and easy to learn, Persona 5 runs into the same issue I had with Persona 4's combat, in fact its even worse in this case, in that the game is just way too damn easy after the first 2 dungeons. After beating the first 2 dungeons in Persona 5 most of these poor shadows just couldn't even touch me, a big reason for that is partly due to most of the personas that I levelled up and unlocked at the time having abilities that wiped the floor with these losers, and also in part to my boi Ryuji. Its already well known at this point but unlocking Ryujis rank 7 insta kill ability essentially just makes grinding a breeze. Not only do you get to just ram through low levelled shadows, but also get full exp and yen for doing so with no loss. Whilst I appreciated this at first for making grinding manageable, the monkey paw effect of having the difficulty take a nosedive made me question whether the trade off was worth it. Honestly, besides over-levelling issue, there's also the fact that Physical damage is just wayy too good, it practically wipes through shadows that don't have resistances to it and its also the only skill type in the game to have a colossal rank which emphasises just how much more powerful it is compared to the others. The bosses in this are a mixed issue as well, on one hand they have some fun gimmicks and attacks they can throw at you, but they're also far too humble when it comes to dishing out damage numbers (and i played the whole game on Hard). Bosses here fall victim to the ever so powerful physical skills and either needed bigger health pools (not to the extent of P4) or more powerful attacks to really pressure players. As it stands right now they're unfortunately fun but easy to breeze through (with the exception of Okumara). In terms of the social aspect of this game, there's not really much i can add onto that hasn't already been said before. The day to day activities of living as a high school student and bonding with your confidants as well levelling up your social stats is ridiculously addicting and embarrassingly enough I think I spent more time getting stressed out over deciding which which activity i was to spend on each day than each all the bosses combined. Getting into the flow of managing your social schedule and seeing which days you have free to spend on Mementos & Palaces (combat stuff) and which ones to focus on confidants or part time jobs is the best part of the game and makes up for the lack of challenge through the 1st quarter of the game.This game also has the best UI I have ever seen like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ why does it looks so good, seriously more Western devs need to take notes from this game because we need to break out of this 'less is more' mentality with how a lot of their UI's tend to look. The comic book aesthetic combined with the bold red and black colours make opening and looking at menus so satisfying, which is a plus considering menus are most of the combat anyway. It isn't just the UI, the entire game just oozes with style with the way that the characters and world are cell shaded, to the point where at some point I didn't even think this was a JRPG. Overall, this game was an absolute blast to play through, apart from my critiques on the lack of difficulty I would easily replay this game again on NewGame+.(also, whoever at Atlus thought it was a good idea for the extremely OP DLC persona's to be free in the persona compendium needs to be fired, like come on this game is already too easy as it i)

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game a lot but real talk....I'm glad it's over.Persona 5 Royal is a JRPG in a contemporary setting. That's really all I needed to know for it to pop up on my radar. When I jumped into it (having never played a Persona game before) I found a pretty standard set of mechanics with some life sim and time management kinks thrown in. As you grow closer to people in the life sim portion of the game, you actually grow stronger in the JRPG portion. I like this idea. There's just one problem: One of these characters has essential system mechanics gated behind their social story line. No spoilers here, though. However, without this character, it's not impossible for enemies to just wipe you if you're playing on a higher difficulty and they happen to have a type advantage, ESPECIALLY if this advantage is against Joker himself, since if he gets knocked out, the game ends. Apparently, revival drugs work on everyone EXCEPT Joker. Make sure to ambush every monster you can or you risk dying without being able to act. This is on higher difficulties, though. On normal and lower, you can probably tank a round.The game has a great soundtrack and the visual presentation is cool. The only problem I have with the presentation is how aggressively colorful it is. Seriously, if you have epilepsy, maybe turn down the color settings on your monitor before booting this one up. Otherwise, no notes.Honestly, the game is just good. If you like JRPGs, pick it up. It is AGGRESSIVELY anime but don't hold that against it. Persona 5 is a good time. But ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is it long. 80 hours for a play through and a lot of that is reading text. If that's not your thing, you might want to look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterfully crafted and executed RPG.Every moment of it oozes a slick style that few games can match.  The game is quite long, I'm 30 hours in and not halfway done with my first play through.  The story is more fun, better written, and has more memorable characters than most of the recent series on Netflix.I love the dungeon diving gameplay where the amount and quality of your consumables makes a massive difference in how far you can dive and how easily you can achieve success.  Slower, more patient people can grind and stock up, and take their time while the more adventurous can try to blitz to the end of a run while running dry on HP, SP and rez items.The pokemon-style Personas you capture and "craft" via gothic executions and resurrections are all little works of art in their own rite.  The turn based combat is fun for RPG fans with a lot of bells, whistles, and bonuses for the astute.  The baton-toss gimmick is a momentum builder where you gift your extra turn to another player, adding various buffs and perks every time you do it.I'm also grateful for the top-right button that gives you a hint at nearly any stage of the game for those looking for it.  This is nice if you don't want to stress about the mini games or keep referring to a chart to remember what weaknesses are available.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game for people that aren't into RPGs. It catches you with a pretty interesting story and introduces you to the gameplay in a really nice way that is well paced. I don't usually finish RPG games, but I have replayed the original (non "Royal") Persona 5 multiple times, and now gone through this one. In general I would say Persona 5 has been one of my personal favorite experiences with games, and Royal is just a generally enhanced version of the original.This game paces itself by going between the story, daily life and battle portion in chunks. Not only are battles intuitive for new players, it has some unique twists (e.g. "Baton Pass") compared to other RPGs, which make it more fun. The daily life part provides a good break from the main story and battle allowing you to explore the city and improve your stats and relationships to help with battling later. The soundtrack and the general art style of the game is also great.From the point of view of someone coming from the original, I generally like what they added to Royal. The additional content is nice and more time is given to interact with things in daily life. One highlight for me is how Mementos is less boring with its new mechanics. There's a new semester, which provides some interesting additional story. While I was playing it I found it nice, but I have no strong opinions to share here, I may wanna go through it again to better understand how I feel about this part of the game. Either way it's more Persona 5 to play, and I like Persona 5.As far as the PC port is concerned, I have no complaints aside from the existence of Denuvo DRM, which I hope it gets removed as soon as it's cracked just out of principle. That said, I did not observe major performance issues. The ability to play at 120 FPS is good and the game looks pretty sharp after tweaking the settings.With all that out of the way, as much as I like this game, I personally dislike a few things, most of which comes from the original game and is still present on Royal. Some opinions I would highlight are:- The reliance on googling and the network feature to experience the whole game is probably one of its major downsides to me. This was especially an issue on the original game with the laughably low amount of time you actually had to do things, and it's good for new players that Royal actually gives more time to players in daily life and more opportunity for earning 'points'. However it still doesn't solve the root issue, where the dialogue choices you need to make make seemingly no sense most of the time and random trivia questions that you couldn't possibly know most of the time leave important point progression up to chance. I'm very conflicted about this because I do not know what a solution if any would be applicable to this issue.- The writing of this game is both its pro and con. I'll not go into detail as to avoid spoilers, but the characters here start really strong, there's some really heavy plot with emotion, like the stuff going on with Ann for example. But when their major plot is done and they've been fully introduced, these characters go downhill and become a bit of a joke, like their whole story is dismissed. There are really cringe points in this game, like what happens with Morgana well later on in the game. Somehow, the story still works and still has impact, but it's far from perfect.- Fusing personas is an interesting mechanic, but one that you'll either like or hate doing as a beginner. It's something I personally somewhat avoided on my first playthrough, and the thing is that for better or worse, this game is just about easy enough on normal that it won't punish you for not taking advantage of it often. I was hoping for quality of life improvements on Royal like showing all registered personas in the Fuse by Result section, or showing duplicate skills existent in other Personas, but neither of those exist in this game.- Some of the bonus content that was previously DLC in the vanilla game can be way too OP. The bonus Personas for instance, you can already summon a level 90 Persona at the very start of the game, which makes no sense. You'll need to personally avoid using these to not break the game balance further.To end, just some thoughts on the difficulty, or rather the lack thereof I had while progressing through this playthrough as a returning player. On Royal, 'Merciless' is still a messy difficulty that ends up easier than its supposedly easier counterpart 'Hard', so I chose to personally stick to 'Hard' on my playthrough. I think that Royal has added things that benefit the experience of new players, but they have in the process made the game easier for returning players seeking challenge. Some confidant abilities () are especially unbalanced and will help with that. I personally wish there was a proper step above Hard, one where I would not have to add restrictions on my own to make the game more challenging.
