_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely has the makings of a great game, even a masterpiece. But in its core this game is just lacking in most of its aspects. It wouldn't be false to say this game preffers style over substance. Story and Characters - The story is pretty simple but entertaining, some parts I would even say are really good (secret ending). However, this game just has such a difference between its hights and its lows. The lore is pretty fun and interesting, the whole theme of thieves that steal peoples hearts and change people is very interesting at first. Additionally the corrupt gouvernment part which uses the your group for their gain and how their greed makes them kill eachother is also very intriguing. However, some parts of this like all the villains being connected, and the main villain being just plain boring evil when other smaller villains had better motivations (some of them), and if not that at least they weren't evil as in mustache twirling power hungry evil.The characters are a veeeery mixed bag, bordering from likeable and enjoyable, intriguing, to plain annoying, forced and predictable. The main crew especially has "anime tropes" and annoying chatacters problems, with most of them being uninteresting, plain and annyoing. I won't go into much detail (many others have done so), and will just say even though it has its high points, this games story and characters aren't its strong point.Gameplay - If you haven't played a Persona game before and are looking for a more relaxed game then others, this may be the one for you. Gameplay is split into two pars: combat and slice of life. In the slice of life part you essentially do things to boost your stats, chemistry with teammates, social links with people, upgrade gear, make money, be in school, explore side stories etc etc. This part is a very relaxing expierience until you realise that you should have planned what you were going to do with your time more. Essentially your entire game you are on a timer, so don't waste time like me my first run. The combat part is another point of controversy, because it is described by veteran Persona fans as the most easy and forgiving combat system in the franchise. Even though I haven't played other Persona titles, I would agree, because even on hard mode my first run i died less then 20 times. However, it needs to be pointed out that dying to this game sometimes feels so cheap and will frustrate you. It happens all of a sudden, with you just going through the motions, barely paying attention because all the enemies are easy and then you are just dead after entering a fight. The bosses are also a mixed bag, with some being really enjoyable and some just being too hard and annoying (Okumura and his robots). Overall I would say that the whole combat system and mechanics are just good enough to keep you entertained with their high point being really impressive.Vibe - This game is all about vibe. The UI, the menus, the details, the music, the designs... This games strives on these aspect, they define it. These are the things that hook most people on the most, i still listen to some of the songs and watch the intros. The whole thiefs thing in the story is very fun and I found it to be the most enjoyable part of the story. How the story is told also, jumping back and forth between past and present is very nice, but it gets old after a while.Overall I would buy this game on sale, in its lenght it has great value alone, though it is too long. I wouldn't exactly say this game is a masterpiece, or even great, but it can be enjoyable. It's criminally easy even on the highest difficulty, so it's a pretty good game to just relax to. However if you are searching for a better story expierience, or expect a great story or gameplay or anything from this game you might end up dissapointed. This game is competent, it has the potential to achieve greatness yet refuses to take the neccessary risks in story and character writing to do so, it ends up being pretty generic by the end, with of course a few exceptions. This game perfectly encapsulates modern games: mediocre to alright with high potential. I honestly am still waiting to expeirience a modern game which has achieved its full, or close to its full potential.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is simply great. At the very least, I most certainly enjoyed the 100+ hours of gameplay I sunk my teeth into.If I were to write a synopsis for the game's plot...Joker is a wanted criminal that gets caught by the cops. But wait! He's not a criminal, right? That's what he's gotta prove to his prosecutor, as he recalls his memories up to that situation. And his memories involve making friends, having wild adventures, and the fact that this isn't his first time being arrested.As a victim of false accusation, he is chosen by fate to change its course. He will fight against the very society that kicked him down at its corrupt roots, sure, but the situation may be bigger than he thinks. Will Joker answer the call? Or will he let his ruin come to pass?Persona 5 Royal is a turn based JRPG. This means all units on the field take turns attacking, based whoever has the higher Agility (Ag) stat. You can start fights as an ambush, meaning all your party members get a turn before the enemy. However, the opposite is also true; the enemy can ambush you and put you in a surrounded state. How you approach these non-boss fights will determine how difficult you'll make things for yourself.Each party member can use a Persona, the representation of their inner rebellion. Personas give access to skill usage. Everyone will have their own element and role they end up specializing in, but Joker is the most versatile since he can carry multiple Personae. If he dies, the battle instantly ends in a loss. It will be important to keep him alive over the others when necessary. There are multiple attack types in the game, and three different ways to deal bonus damage. If an enemy is weak to an attack, it's a weak hit. Physical hits can land a critical hit. In both instances, you knock the enemy down! You can also inflict status effects and then hit them with certain attacks for technical damage, which may sometimes knock them down too. You have dungeons called Palaces that you must infiltrate and steal the Treasure of in order to progress the story. Mementos is another dungeon that you can visit after completing the first Palace, which constantly expands and has varying floor layouts. Mementos serves as a way to grind and possibly capture Persona you may have missed on previous Palaces.You can also bond with the various characters known as Confidants in the game, which gives you extra gameplay benefits for doing so. Maxing out Confidants can lead to some additional special moments in the story, and some of them are actually key to being able to access the Royal portion of the game.Most notably, your actions in the game are timed. You are given an in-game calendar that will be used to keep track of the game's story progress. Spending time with your Confidants, visiting Mementos, crafting items, and committing to miscellaneous activities during your free time will cause time to pass. There is a limited amount of time that you have to work with, and every Palace has a deadline. Failing to meet this deadline will cause you to fail. Thus, you should plan carefully to have satisfying results.The game's not very hard overall. There are many ways in-game to make things easier for you, without needing changing the difficulty setting. Playing this for the first time? If you want to just enjoy the story, you can go as far as playing on Safe mode. Otherwise, for those who want to seek a challenge, I recommend a blind playthrough on Hard or Merciless (I played on Hard). Do note that certain fights may be easier for you if you play on Merciless, due to the presence of a 3x damage multiplier for Weak/Critical hits. I'll keep this brief because this review is already kinda long. There'll be plenty of twists and turns, and each character (particularly your Confidants) are well done. A big part of enjoying the game and sticking with it is the story. If you're not into a story rich game, you'll find this game to be a drag. If you are interested in a story rich game, then it's almost certain that at , you'll like at least one character. As for aesthetics? You can definitely tell the game has a unique style, which is complemented well by the music. By the way, the OST for the game is outstanding.You like big story? You like RPGS? You like turn based battles? This is worth your purchase. Answered no to any of these? I'd still give it a try. Only time I wouldn't recommend this to someone is if they don't like any of these things.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 is, without a doubt, one of the most unique and impactful games I’ve ever played and easily my number 1 game. From the start, it pulls you into an unforgettable world—a stylish, Tokyo-inspired city where you balance life as a high school student and a "Phantom Thief," fighting against society's corruption. The story is captivating, exploring themes of justice, rebellion, and the power of friendship in a way that feels meaningful without being heavy-handed.One of the most impressive aspects of Persona 5 is its art style. Everything has a bold, high-energy look, from the character designs to the menus, giving the game a vibe that’s entirely its own. The soundtrack is also phenomenal, mixing jazz and rock to create tracks that make everything from battles to exploration feel exciting. Each tune has such personality that it stays with you even after you turn off the game.But what really makes Persona 5 special is its cast of characters. As you play, you build relationships with each member of the Phantom Thieves, along with other “Confidants” who add depth and skills to your journey. These aren’t just side characters—they each have their own struggles, motivations, and growth arcs, which makes them feel genuinely real. By the end, you feel like you know them as well as your own friends, and you want to see each one succeed.The combat system is also fantastic. It's turn-based but with a ton of strategy built in, and every fight feels fast-paced and intense. You can exploit enemy weaknesses, pull off All-Out Attacks, and summon powerful “Personas” that add a whole layer of tactics. It keeps you engaged while rewarding you for thinking strategically, which is rare to find in RPGs of this style.My first playthrough lasted just shy of about 200 hours of gameplay, Persona 5 is a long ride, but every moment feels worthwhile. The combination of a deep story, relatable characters, and a stylish world makes it stand out from any other game out there. If you love games with a great narrative and want something that challenges you to think and feel, Persona 5 is a must-play experience that will leave a lasting impact.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal is one of the best games I've ever played. Here's some backstory.I learned about Persona 5 by chance, it was on one of my dad's friend's Playstation 3's. That was until I got my PC. I got a PS3 emulator and a copy of the game and I beat the game. Then I played again. And again. And again. It became one of my favorite games, if not my favorite. It's powerful characters, messages, aesthetic, music, story and overall feel just hit all the right notes for me. Unfortunately, I was restricted to P5 vanilla until my dad managed to get a PS5 in a raffle. The first game my brother and I bought was Persona 5 Royal. Nearly a year and a half of buildup, waiting to play P5R and when I did, I could not put it down. The additions that Royal added, the characters of Maruki and Sumi, the extensions on Akechi's character, the wonderful new Palace and endings, P5R exceeded my expectations.After beating P5R, I brought out my PS2 and played through Persona 3 FES. I would absolutely recommend going and playing that or Persona 3 Portable, both FES and Portable have an absolutely phenomenal main story, with incredible characters, themes and music, but that's a story for another time. (I'm currently playing Persona 4 Golden and so far, it's fantastic.) Just a few weeks after that, the Persona community received some of the best news we'd received in years. Persona 5 Royal was getting a port/upgrade to PC, Switch and Xbox, Persona 4 Golden was getting a port to modern PS consoles, Xbox and Switch and Persona 3 Portable was getting a remaster and being put on all platforms (not a great remaster, but again, story from another time.)That brings us here. I mainly bought it so I could mod the game, but even if you're not interested in mods, please, please play it. You won't regret it.

Even after completing the main storyline, there will still be plenty of quests, missions, and achievements for you to complete, significantly increasing the playtime and adding replayability.Overall, Persona 5 Royal is an incredibly captivating game with an engaging plot, vibrant graphics, and a plethora of new features that bring a fresh perspective to the game. _childDocuments_.review: First off, let me just say, this game didn't just steal my heart, it snatched my entire circadian rhythm. I'm talking "just-one-more-turn" syndrome but on a whole new level. You think you're just going to play for an hour, and suddenly it's 4 AM and you're emotionally invested in a cat that turns into a bus.Graphics? Gorgeous. It's like someone took the concept of 'stylish' and cranked it up to 11. The characters are so well-designed, I started questioning my own fashion choices. Why can't I look that cool wearing a mask and a trench coat?The story? It's like diving into a bowl of your favorite cereal and finding out each flake leads to another dimension where your high school life is a mix of acing exams and battling grotesque creatures. It's like if Hogwarts met Inception, but with more jazz.Gameplay? You'll juggle between being a model student and a phantom thief. One moment you're answering questions in class about Japanese history, and the next, you're in a supernatural realm stealing hearts and changing minds. It's like living a double life, but without the risk of your parents grounding you.But let's talk about the real MVP here: the soundtrack. It slaps harder than a reality check. You'll find yourself jamming to the tunes even when you're not playing. Grocery shopping? Phantom Thief. Doing laundry? Phantom Thief. In a job interview? Well, you get the idea.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll probably end up writing a lot about this game, so if you want a quick review, here it is: This game was an incredible experience. Although I'm not in the same age group as the characters, I ended up identifying with them. The story is deep, heavy, but at the same time light and full of twists and turns. I was so immersed in the story that I reached a point where I’d wake up early just to play. The characters are extremely charismatic, and the story is impeccable. The game has a mind-blowing plot (especially in the true ending). And about the turn-based combat, which I thought would be a weak point—it was quite the opposite. The system is fluid and became one of the most fun parts of the game.The truth is, the first time I heard about this game, I had no interest in playing it because it was turn-based, a style I don’t usually enjoy. But, after some recommendations from friends, I decided to give it a shot. I downloaded the pirated version, ran it on a PS3 emulator, and immediately hit my first obstacle: the game didn't have a translation in my language. It might seem like a minor detail, but at the time, I had never studied another language, so even English was hard for me.Still, I pressed on, with a dusty dictionary I had at home and a translator on my phone (couldn’t use it on the computer because an alt + tab might crash the emulator), i was determined to understand what made this game so special. At first, it was quite challenging; I can say the first 30 hours were a struggle to understand what was going on in the story, but gradually, I got the hang of it, and my dictionary lookups became less and less frequent. Honestly, that alone made the game worth it for me, as it turned out to be the spark that got me interested in learning a new language, which I think is priceless.Even with poor performance and frequent crashes on the emulator (this was my second obstacle, my PC was like a potato), I played for about 90 hours and got completely immersed in the story. But when the Royal version of the game was announced for PC, I dropped everything I had done in the game so far (I was practically at the last palace) and decided to wait to play an original copy, thinking I owed it to Atlus.I couldn't really afford the game at launch, so I waited for a sale that fit my budget, but it never came. Until a friend decided to gift it to me for my birthday (if you're reading this, thank you so much, you have no idea how happy I was to receive this gift). And from then on, it was pure joy! This time, language was no longer a barrier, and the performance of this PC port was impeccable.In the end, I got all the achievements in the game, explored every detail, and enjoyed everything the game has to offer (for the second time, but now in the Royal version). Honestly, I love Persona 5, and though it’s not a perfect game, it’s definitely one of my favorites.

_childDocuments_.review: Here we go Persona 5 Royal is on PC and it didn't disappoint, one of the best rpg's released in the past few years.So what is this game? It's a unique jRPG with high emphasis on story. It has no relation to other games but shares similar lore (what you see in Final Fantasy games) so it's a great starting point for new players.This is royal version which comes with additional content which adds more hours of gameplay after finishing the main story. It incorporates additional content into the game and story very well so it doesn't feel out of place by any means. It feels like the additional content was there from the beginning.While I prefer the story of Persona 4 Golden (which was more serious in my opinion and even philosophical), I prefer the dungeons or palaces of this game, it's like day and night. Although Royal story makes up for it.You play as Joker, a teenage boy who arrives into a new town and goes to a new school where he meets new friends and discovers the metaverse. Soon Joker meets a talking cat, witnesses some shocking events at the school and the journey begins.Game consists of two different worlds – real world set in Shibuya and metaverse. In the real world you have to go to school, you increase your stats, build relationaships with friends and do other stuff which includes growing plants, fishing, playing games, watching movies, reading books, studying, making coffee and more. Every action cost time, basically you can do two thing per day.Metaverse is where you steal hearts. After you identify the person you can go to their palace to steal their heart which changes that person in real world. Each palace is entirely different both in visuals and gameplay. Exploring palaces takes time, each one of them has its quirks, some have puzzles or additional requirements and each main boss offers a unique experience and forces you to use different tactics.There are several playable characters although you can only take three of them with you into combat besides Joker. You can switch them mid-combat or at the entrance so if you see that you need to change the composition of the party, it's easy to do.Each character has their persona in metaverse and have their own costumes. While Joker can use multiple personas.Velvet room is the place where you can fuse personas to make new ones, rearrange your personas, buy new ones etc. In general it's a place where you manage your personas.While in combat, if you critically injure the monster (except bosses and tough enemies) they speak to you and you can demand three things – joining you which means that monster becomes one of your personas with its own skills, ask for money or ask for an item. You can of course just kill them.There's also mementos, it's like a common palace of all the aociety instead of one person. Mementos has many floors but in general it's just a generic dungeon and place where you go to do side requests and farm.Real world time management can be tricky when you don't know what to do. Increasing social stats is important but also increasing friendship rank with your friends opens up their side-stories and gives you abilities in metaverse. You can meet and interact with non-playable characters so you'll need to manage who to dedicate your time to well.Eventually if you rank up a girl to max rank you can become a couple or decide to friendzone her. You can go into relatioship with multiple girls both your age and older, like your teacher.You get to buy your gear (you can find some), buy/make items which heals of buffs you or debuff/damages the enemies.Combat is turn based and often requires some planning and knowledge of the game to exploit all the weaknesses of the enemies. I played on easy because i wanted story and still managed to die few times. You take turns and you have few choices each turn. Physical attack, guns, persona or item. Each enemy has its weakness to certain attack or element (some have no weakness) and it's up to you to discover them.So in short gameplay consists of real life activities and dialogues and metaverse. Don't forget that you can spend as much time in metaverse once you're there as you like and it will count as one activity.Graphically the game is quite unique. It's Atlus game, the only other similar looking game is Catherine made by the same developers. The graphics look great, amazing art-style which stands out of any other game. Palaces especially look great and it's a great leap from Persona 4 Golden where you only had mazes with identical textures everywhere.Performance isn't the greatest, especially if you turn up rendering scale. But this game is fine even at 30fps.Played on 5800x, rtx 3080/4080, 32gb @3440x1440. I had render scale on 150%, game looked amazing and very crisp although I was getting some fps drops which was weird since the game isn't a technical marvel. There's lack of graphics options.No ultrawide support obviously because there's lots of 2D images. Partially works with flawless widescreen. 2D images are stretched and you can see the void where 2D background boundaries end. Anime cut-scenes are stretched, use reshade and bind a button to quickly change the aspect ratio when cut-scenes play.Sound design is absolutely outstanding. This game deserves the best soundtrack of the year. Really it has one of the best soundtracks in the industry. After playing this you'll either go to youtube or spotify to listen to those songs.Voice acting was good too, each character sounded nice even though it's not always the case with niche japanese games.It's a wonderful game filled with 100+ hours of pure content, worth any price and is close to being a masterpiece. The story could be better and it has some weird minor performance issues but it's a must have for any rpg fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Get it on sale if you are REALLY need to play this rerelease, but in short:— Game is made laughably easy by "balance" changes (you no longer have to ration your SP, they throw items at you, Mementos grinding was made brainless by Jose or whatever the kid's name was, allowing me to get a million yen in the first 1/3'rd of the game (still had 80% SP on my whole team, and I effectively have infinite money, it's just a choice on whether or not I want to waste X hours seeing the number go up)).— Story is still laughably bad, feels like a rough draft more than a finished product; all the story points are seen a mile away unless you're high or just turning your brain off to mindlessly see number go up during lock-down fusions.— Morgana.— Had to fiddle with the graphics to get it to a point where it didn't make my eyes hurt from the blur (had to set it to %200 upscale, which is just laughable on its own), otherwise the graphics look passable to good.— For a game that is carried by its cast, a lot of the actual dialogue choices you make actually don't matter, or they influence how many social points you get towards a Confidant's rank (and some of these perhaps don't translate well, but a number of the Confidant choices feel like they're either awkward or just saying what the other person wants to hear rather than what they want to hear, which isn't exactly what a good friend is or would say; a guide is recommended if you don't want to get shafted by arbitrary "You picked the dialogue option asking for more information instead of the one that just says "Yes!", so you're going to need to waste a timeslot hanging out with them, OR spend money at Chihaya's to increase the Confidant rank that way).— Too few battle songs, you'll hear the new Royal theme constantly, and never the old "You'll never SEE IT COMMMIIIIN~!" — None of the main cast really feel like friends, just beings of (heavily contrived) circumstance that must work together; compare to the gang of the earlier Persona 4, where there was good chemistry there that inspires fanart to this day.— The dub is atrocious and had me switch off it immediately; this is always a constant and goes without saying, but use subs. Though I also feel as if the localisers did their usual butchery (Futaba saying "KEK!" and various slang put here and there that just does not match the tone or vibes, IE the Phantom Website comments that sound like something a CEO would say while drunkenly mimicking what "A little zoomer" would say on the 'net).— Goro.— Morgana.—Okumura's Palace is still a slog to play, and, impressively enough, Fatlus made the boss fight substantially worse than in Vanilla (playtesters too expensive, small family company, plz understand; oh, and buy the $200 Persona 3: Reloaded Special Edition plz :)).— Denuovo.— Can't fast-forward through All-out Attack animations because lol (you're going to be seeing the animation probably a thousand times by the end of the game, as it's a long, long game with quite a bit of padding).— Kasumi, the new character added in Royal, is literally just a poochie. When she's not on screen, and before she has a scene, the characters talk about "Woah, did you hear about that athletic honor student? She's so cute, think I have a shot with her?" and "She's so great!" When she does interact with your character, she's always kissing up to you for literally no reason (she's a very popular student, so shouldn't she be less willing to just be BEST FRIENDS with someone she just met? Much less one with the MC's current reputation upon meeting?).— Morgana.Like, if this is your first JRPG ever, or if you don't play games besides the top 10 on Twitch, then it's pretty great. But if you've played other SMT games, read VNs or novels with proper characterization, or just even browsed Pixiv for pics of cute girls, then there really isn't much here beyond the surface-level flash and style that this game offers, which, admittedly, it does have in spades. Wish I could be more positive about this, as it HAS potential, and it leaves me hungry for a more finished product, but playtesting and hiring a professional storyboard team is too expensive for poor old Fatlus (this game is seven years old and still being sold at full price).

After that I could finally start enjoying the game, but by the time I hit 60+ hours I already wanted it to end. _childDocuments_.review: Forewarning about this game; It showcases some fairly serious topics. If you are not okay with uncomfortable topics such as sexual assault, physical and mental abuse, police brutality, drugs, gambling or other heavy topics in these veins, you may opt to pass on this game. Fantastic game, but it pulls no punches with the topics it wishes to discuss.With that out of the way, this game is a fantastic addition to almost anybody's collection. This game is half JRPG half Social Game, as anybody remotely familiar with Persona probably knows.Your general flow of gameplay is each in-game day you have limited actions you can take ("Time" isn't quite accurate here, as it's not constrained by our physical time, just simply after you commit to something you move on to the next point of time in the day) to either interact and build up relationships with people (Which imparts bonuses either in combat or outside of dungeons), build up stats, or delve into the game's dungeons. Often times these are interlinked with a set deadline to complete the current dungeon in the story. Because of this, you're forced to make decisions on where you want to allocate that time, as dabbling in everything (ESPECIALLY on your first playthrough when social stats are low) is very difficult. I do like this as it means you'll have 2 equally good decisions and because you know you cannot do both you'll simply have to decide. To go a bit more in-depth, building up relationships with people can impart a variety of bonuses. Sometimes it gives new options in combat, sometimes it bolsters them if it's a party member, sometimes it gives you out-of-dungeon bonuses such as more shop items available. Overall, it's a core of the game but it plays into the main point which is the JRPG side.Going to the JRPG side, this is a game that takes what is normally traditional turn-based combat, but puts a bit more skill behind it in the way of strategy. Even though it has a "Pokemon"-like tradeoff with attacks having types and enemies with weaknesses, it goes a step further where hitting enemies with weaknesses gives you extra turns, of which you can pass to others for stat boosts or just capitalize on the momentum with the best equipped character. Buffs, debuffs, and status conditions are an excellent mechanic here as well, as status conditions can make enemies have weaknesses they may not otherwise have. However, this also both goes AGAINST the player (as enemies can do this too), but also makes enemies have a higher difficulty than you might expect for JRPGs. Even "Mook" enemies can potentially 2 shot you if you're not careful, meaning you're consistently trying to make use of your kit. This really reinforces the "Thieves" theme though, as you hit hard and hit fast without letting the enemy retaliate.That theme extends to the "Palaces" (This game's version of Dungeons in other JRPGs), where you get a plethora of stealth tools to try and get ambushes on enemies. Not being seen makes combat easier too as the less your detection level the less enemies you have to fight. The palaces themselves are gorgeous; Between the inherently surreal feel most of them give, to the very 3-Dimensional exploration that really makes it feel you're moving around an intricate environment, finding routes that might not otherwise exist, it is a joy to explore every single one.As for story, the story is top notch. The game uses the very magical side where you have special powers (the Personas) plus the whimsical side of the Palaces to directly mirror the very grounded and real-world topics it talks about. The first Palace really showcases this well; You're off to fight the King of the literal Castle. The King views everybody as little more than their slaves. Which is just a showcase of somebody who due to their position is able to get what they want, and everybody will turn a blind eye to what's actually going on due to their accolades. It's a great way to use what should be a fantasy type theme, and use it to visually showcase your story.I don't need to say much about the Music. You've probably heard it already, but in case you haven't, even the "Generic Enemy" music is an absolute banger of a song. It's not often you get a lyrical song for regular enemies, and that should tell you everything about the entire soundtrack. It's catchy, it's fun, it's amazing. I want them to put it as DLC so I can download it.So for complaints;The game has a lot of, shall we call them "Noob Traps". The game will put very steep "Social Stat" requirements early on, but neglect to tell you that certain Social Links will provide those stats if you just progress on those. As such you may waste time doing things that don't accomplish much in the grand scheme and only find out halfway through the game (at which point it may be too late to go back).The game's higher difficulty is definitely a bit harsh, especially early on since you may not know enemy weaknesses despite the game demanding you do. As such early enemies sometimes will literally 1-shot you if you fail to kill them fast enough. I don't mind harder games but that feels a BIT steep.Similarily there's a couple points in the game that expect you to have specific moves or setups to be able to feasibly do (Everybody who's played fears Palace 5), so it's possible to permanently softlock yourself if you don't use multiple saves.That said, these are mild nitpicks honestly. The game is fantastic, story is amazing, characters are lovable, music is awesome. Strong recommend for anybody looking for a great overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Prepare for an all-new RPG experience in Persona 5 Royal based in the universe of the award-winning series, Persona! Don the mask of Joker and join the Phantom Thieves of Hearts. Break free from the chains of modern society and stage grand heists to infiltrate the minds of the corrupt and make them change their ways! Persona 5 Royal is packed with new characters, confidants, story depth, new locations to explore, and a new grappling hook mechanic for stealthy access to new areas. With a new semester at Shujin Academy, get ready to strengthen your abilities in the metaverse and in your daily life. Persona 5 Royal presents a unique visual style and award nominated composer Shoji Meguro returns with an all-new soundtrack. Explore Tokyo, unlock new Personas, customize your own personal Thieves Den, discover a never-before-seen story arc, cutscenes, alternate endings, and more! Even for the most seasoned Phantom Thieves among us, Persona 5 Royal is a new challenge to defy conventions, discover the power within, and fight for justice. Wear the mask. Reveal your truth.

name: Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp
detailed_description: DANGANRONPA S: ULTIMATE SUMMER CAMP is now on Steam! Summary Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp is a massively enhanced version of Ultimate Talent Development Plan, the boardgame from Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony. The stage is set at the tropical resort of Jabberwock Island, and players improve their characters via the 'Development (Boardgame),' 'Battle,' and so on. Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp is the dream crossover of Danganronpa characters with over 1,000 event scenes, and offers new swimsuit outfits for all characters. Also, players can now collect collab illustrations drawn for merchandise in the Mono Mono Machine! ・Game features Development (Boardgame) The main part of the game in which players will develop their character over 50 days (50 turns) of summer camp on Jabberwock Island. Roll a die to determine how many spaces to move. An event will be triggered depending on which square the character lands on. Each character has various stats, including level. Character stats improve by leveling up, stopping on a Growth Square, or interacting with other characters on Event Squares. Bosses placed by Monokuma and monster battles triggered by Battle Squares will impede the player's path along the way. Talent Squares grant Talent Fragments, which grant characters new skills. Players will also need to acquire weapons and armor at shops and treasure chests as well as utilize cards featuring useful effects to their advantage. Battle A Battle Mode can be played separately from the Battle Squares found in the boardgame. Develop characters and form a party of up to four members and take on the 200-floor Tower of Despair where Monokuma-type monsters await. In the Tower of Despair, enemies attack in waves, and the player is rewarded with Monokuma Medals upon victory. Players need to increase their characters' levels while learning skills and gearing up their characters in order to emerge victorious. School Store In the School Store, players can spend Monokuma Medals and Monocoins they've obtained in battle to gain new characters and support items using the MonoMono Machine. Each character has different rarities, and the higher the rarity, the faster they will grow in Development mode.

_childDocuments_.review: - $20 for a gacha game with additional microtransactions- Only 5 characters available at the start, unlocking everyone else will take forever unless you pay up- All assets (art, music, short voice clips) are ripped from other Danganronpa games, they didn't even bother recording any new lines- No real story, just short character interactions + some fanservice (swimsuits etc)- Awful PC port, the game starts in a window and you need to sit through a 40 minute prologue to get to the display settings, also it takes 3+ minutes to load every time you launch it even on a decent gaming PC, and a lot longer (up to 30 minutes) on weaker systems according to forum postsOnly for the most die-hard Danganronpa fans, everyone else should steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a conditional recommendation; if you answer NO to any of the questions, DO NOT BUY!Have you played Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc?Have you played Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair?Have you played Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls?Have you played Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony?Have you cleared all of them?Did you go beyond clearing the games to experience character lore (free time events; minigames; etc)?Did you... at least not dislike... the Ultimate Talent Development Plan in V3?Are you willing to play V3's UTDPlan but bigger and better?Are you okay with gacha to collect cards (playable characters AND hundreds of permanent microbuff cards)?Do you love the characters of Danganronpa?Do you wish you could see more free time events between them all?Now this one's important...Is this game on SALE?!Remember, if you answered NO to anything, then absolutely do not buy under any circumstance.Also, a warning. The overarching story of this game doesn't seem to be replayable, and once experienced... it's gone. People have been known to have trouble resetting progress... reset may be intentionally especially difficult since there is a monetised option for collecting the cards... y'know, with real money (please don't actually use that thing, lol, you can get them all for free... eventually).But the lack of replay/review function for the overall story is concerning. It was actually kind'a neat...Basically, this is for hardcore Danganronpa lovers who didn't mind the UTDP in V3 (and maybe even liked it).It's a'ight and I like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Regrettably, I have been a fan of the Danganronpa series since a bunch of my friends got super into it during high school. I’ve played all of the games but never watched the anime series. Needless to say, I like the high points of Danganronpa. It’s got some really bad parts, but I’m mostly able to look over them. Hearing news about another Danganronpa entry had me excited and I half expected it to get ported to Steam eventually despite launching on the Switch initially. Since it was advertised as an expansion for the postgame dungeon crawler/board game found in Danganronpa V3, I knew what to expect going in. But what I didn’t expect was for a complete game to be inferior to what was once a bonus mode. Also spoilers ahead for the whole franchise.As previously mentioned, if you played V3, it’s Ultimate Talent Development Plan. If you need an explanation, the focus of the game is a pseudo-make-your-own RPG party member on a board game where your decisions impact your character’s level, stats, and skills. Some of the board spaces and specific turns show off visual novel-style character interactions with everyone from all 3 entries, but besides that, there’s no gameplay similarity between this and the mainline games. In the original, after making a party of characters you’d enter an RPG dungeon crawler with random encounters, boss fights, and little areas you could explore for loot, you would cycle between the two modes, making stronger characters from your progress in both the dungeon and the board game. Repeat indefinitely until you either see all the character interactions or beat the final boss in the RPG section. It wasn’t much on its own, but as post-game content it was huge. I loved wandering around in an old-school dungeon crawler with characters I liked and the unique dialogue I sometimes got was a cherry on top. I had a fair share of fun because it was a nice bonus for what was already a complete game.So how did Danganronpa S handle making what was originally side-content its own thing? The marketing entirely focused on making it a bigger experience, and it’s precisely that. But bigger doesn’t always mean better. What was once a short 15-minute experience with the board game is now a 40-minute endeavor. The only small addition is that the bosses are now also on the board. Otherwise, the drastic increase in time investment required was a major detriment to my enjoyment of the game. Also unlike V3, the game heavily encourages doing the board game with every character for both story progression and to get better characters for the dungeon. Speaking of the dungeon crawler elements, they’ve been entirely stripped away. What took its place is just a gauntlet of enemy encounters that I had the auto-battle feature plow through for the whole 100 floors. Danganronpa S rips away elements from the V3 version just to elongate the less interesting part of the game. My time with the board game segments was a never-ending grind that I was only able to get through because of how little effort it actually required. I highly doubt that most people who pick this up will want to finish it. I hated the board game so much. I would toggle my brain off frequently until I stopped on an event space that wasn’t something I’ve already seen.That leaves us with the other selling point: interactions between characters across different entries in the series. Again, this is something V3 already did but S brings in Ultra Despair Girls characters. However, I honestly don’t even think these half of these characters are interesting enough to warrant considering their interactions. Except maybe Monaca but that’s because she was a way more interesting and threatening villain than Junko was. Otherwise, I just really don’t care for the kids, bears, or Hiro’s mom. The most compelling events usually involve characters that didn’t get much screen time or some characters catching onto a detail that would be a major plot point naturally. For example, seeing that Tenko actually admires Chihiro despite their gender or seeing Korekiyo catch onto Mikan’s more controlling side. I think my favorite scenes were seeing a bunch of characters cluing into Monaca faking her handicap status. There’s minor stuff like seeing Gonta and Gundham getting along due to their shared love of animals. Besides that, there’s a complete lack of any story. What little remains is cut into tiny segments separated by hours of repeated interactions. It’s a complete tonal shift and expects you to take the plot really seriously in the final hour after playing as every character too.Also, a complaint of mine is that all of the art and music are recycled from past entries! The only new art pieces are 3 full illustrations, the cover art, and swimsuit sprites for everyone. The music is entirely unoriginal though. This is really disheartening since Masafumi Takada’s music was one of the highlights for me. I know that cutting corners by reusing content is a very common practice in game development, but when your game is almost fully composed of it is when it starts to bother me.I want to go over who this game is for in the first place. This game is for the extreme hardcore Danganronpa fans. It’s impossible to enjoy this without any familiarity because of the massive spoilers for every plot point. That’s why this game is monetized with microtransactions! Wanna play with the best possible Celeste character immediately? Fork over 100 yen and you can! It’s not actually on the Steam page, but you can go to a vending machine in-game that wants your money. I personally did not get to play as my favorite characters throughout the battle gauntlet. I never got to play as Himiko or Celeste until the very end. I could definitely see Spike Chunsoft pinching a few pennies off the impatient bunch. The sluggish nature I mentioned is likely entirely intentional in an attempt to push people towards it. Microtransactions in visual novels aren’t something I’m looking forward to seeing replicated.Danganronpa S is ultimately a time waster for the most devoted Danganronpa fans. And as someone who enjoyed all 3 mainline games, it apparently seems like I’m not a part of that group. And even to that crowd, I wouldn’t recommend picking this up. Unless you’re so desperate to see your waifu in any official capacity, you’re better off spending your time elsewhere.  If you’re hoping for more Danganronpa, go look at fan-made content. Honestly I feel as though I’d enjoy actual fanfiction more than what was passed off as official.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most bottom of the barrel, blatant cash grab I've seen in a long time, and I knew this going in, but still left disappointed. Danganronpa S is just the board game crap recycled from V3, with a couple extra scenes and a few new enemies, but the gameplay is just as bare bones and simple as it was before. The new sprites and scenes are incredibly lazy, and feel like they were written by fans, just incredibly basic fan fiction interactions. A lot of the reviews here are like "just google your favs scenes" but honestly I don't think its worth doing that either you can probably write your own version of two characters running into each other and talking for 30 seconds better. I haven't been heavily invested in the series in awhile now but I think even if I was I still wouldn't really give a ♥♥♥♥. If you're gonna make a lazy cash grab with gacha mechanics, at least make it a little entertaining, the gacha is pointless since you can grind infinite free currency with an auto clicker, so spending any more money on in app purchases is even more of a waste than your standard gacha fare, and the new swimsuit characters are weaker than the older highest rarity characters so I don't know why they're even here. _childDocuments_.review: **Before reading this review, please keep in mind that this is MY opinion and shouldn't affect how other people view this game**Alright, so before I begin this review, I would like to say that I am a HUGE Danganronpa Fan. I've seen my boyfriend play the main 3 games and Ultra Despair girls for me. This is the reason I bought this game in the first place. Because I thought "Hey, it's a Danganronpa game and a gacha (which I also happen to enjoy)! It could be fun to see how this turns out." Even through seeing the mixed feelings about this game, I remained optimistic, and decided that I wanted to go through the entire main story before I gave my review. Here is what I thought was good, mixed, and bad with it. Good things:-New interactions with characters: As a fan of Danganronpa, I thought it was nice to see the characters in a new enviroment where they could interact, regardless of what game they were in.-Easy to pull on the gacha: If you do regular runs with the characters and do the occasional tower run, then I believe it is very generous when it comes to the gacha, which is something that not all gacha games give.-Bathing suit skins: Alright alright, of course I can't mention this game without mentioning the fact that one can see the characters in bathing suits, and as somebody who definitely likes the eye candy, I can definitely say that it was a definite plus of the game. Mixed Things:-It can get a bit too easy once you unlock the scrolls: Now I wasn't really sure whether this is good or bad, so I decided to create a mixed category just for this. So once one gets to level 20 (and every 20 tier until 100) one can obtain a scroll which makes the game a bit easier as you don't need to go to every single Mini boss to get said scroll. Now, while I do believe that it is nice so one can actually progress in the runs faster, when you get all of those scrolls, it almost feels a little too easy. Like there were runs I was done before day 20 and then had nothing to do for the rest except interact with friend tiles, and that wasn't nice. Bad Things:-Easily Repetitive: So as somebody who did every single character run in the game, I can say this with certainty. This game becomes SO repetitive after a while. You do the exact same thing just with different character. You beat all the bosses, try to beat the main (secret) boss, and get to lvl 100. You have no idea how many of my characters I got the same skills with since I knew it would work, regardless of their type. And this repetitiveness made the game so tedious to deal with.  -Only one map: This leads to my first point here which is that it is repetitive, but I believe that having one map doesn't help. Like sure, if there were different maps (or at least routes) for every character, then maybe that could help it not be so repetitive, but I feel like it could have helped. But nope. -Predictible story: Sure, maybe the ending of the story was a bit different than what I had imagined, but the overall predictability on what would happen in the story, was just too much of a bad sign for me. -Tedious tower levels: While i will say that some of the tower levels were pretty easy and a good way of getting coins, I feel like some of them just had objectives that were just...so tedious that I didn't even bother completing them. -Limited classes: There are only 3 different classes of characters, and while they do focus on different things, I feel like there should have been more, since again, it lead to a feeling of repetitiveness while playing the game.Overall, would I recommend this game? I am not sure, I don't think I could especially with how I felt towards it in the end. And the price doesn't help. I feel this could have been more of like a free game (as most gachas are), but just the fact that it costs so much for a game that after a while becomes repetitive, no. I wish there was a mixed opinion button, but hey. For now I'll just have to leave my review to help, but I will still say that I don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is simply a longer and slightly more tedious version of V3's Ultimate Talent Development Plan and Despair Dungeon with some minor QoL. Featuring one big board, 50 turns that tend to drag on forever when going for 100% completion (literally just cheat, it makes things so much easier), and a super basic rpg that you can just leave on auto battle and win 98% of the time. This port is fine, I haven't run into any of the issues other people have had. Though I have noticed on numerous occasions dialogue boxes being labelled for the wrong character or voices being swapped. At least 20 hours of my play time is doing other stuff while grinding for materials in the rpg, mashing A every 20-30 seconds to start the battle again. Some of the in game medals are asinine (like beating the board game 200 times, literally just cheat).I do like being able to buy scrolls and higher level gear from the central shop so I don't have to go through all the dungeons again, but that's the only positive I have.If you're really into Danganronpa, buy it on sale for the new character interactions and maybe swimsuits. Otherwise, go play the main games.

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved the Danganronpa series since I first got introduced to the insanity with Trigger Happy Havoc, and since then I've platinumed 1, 2 and V3, while also watching the anime series and OVA. I was happy to hear about another game in the series (I'm aware of Ultimate Despair Girls but never picked it up as it didn't seem to offer enough gameplay or story wise), but the store page made me hesitant - so I checked out some reviews, and one person online mentioned that it was a bit of a love letter to the series. So with that, I decided to pick it up.The game is basically the worst aspect of V3 (Ultimate Development Plan + Monokuma's Test), as the whole gameplay loop. That's the stick, but the carrot is nice and cute cut scenes of characters from all over the series interacting with each other. So essentially, you have your love of the characters and series competing with the grossness of a very grindy and not very fun gameplay loop.Not only that, but there's a shop in the main menu. While the currency for this shop can be obtained within the game, it's in pretty short supply - but never fear! There are microtransactions that allow you to get around this. >.> So that's also gross.So for all this, why am I giving the game a thumbs up? 3 reasons:1. To let Spike Chunsoft know that there's enough love for Danganronpa that we'd appreciate more games. Maybe just a bit more fun next time - more carrot, less stick.2. Even if there's way too much grind for the events you get, seeing all these awesome characters again is nice.3. This is the main reason, and why I feel like this game may be some sort of secret masterpiece. Firstly, following the ending and twist of V3, having this as the next entry - V4 as it were - is just so damn appropriate in the context of the twist. Beyond that, this is a series where despair is one of the main themes. Having our beloved series release a game that's grindy, unfun, is selling a lot of itself on fan service, and has gacha mechanics and microtransactions - is that not just the epitome of despair?

_childDocuments_.review: Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp is a game for fan service and an extension of V3's Talent minigame. This is similar to Animal Crossing Amibo Festival without the toys. With a battle gauntlet RPG design. This mean there's no exploration or dungeon crawling at all in the Battle Tower section. Every Danganronpa cast is here except for the Danganronpa 3 anime. Story is about the Danganronpa cast go in Jabberock Island from the 2nd game for a summer camp trip, but Monokuma wants to spread despair. By doing so, the cast must gather Hope Fragments by completing 50 days (50 turns) on every single character. Thats all to the story. The player must collect character cards by completing tasks from both the Talent Development and Battle Tower. It is very grindy and boring. Luckily the Battle Tower mode does have a auto battle feature. There is an option to buy these cards, but its a greedy tactic for micro-transaction. I don't recommend this game.This game does support the PS4 controller and Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically a fanfiction come to life. "What if everybody lived, and they all went to Summer Camp in the Matrix together? And also Monokuma was there, and summoned wacky digital monsters to have an excuse for combat?" That's the whole premise. Either you like that idea on sight, or you hate it on sight. Playing the game will not change your view either way.Two kinds of people will like this game - If you've seen or played all 3 main games and UDG, and really absorbed the lore and the character dynamics, you'll feel rewarded by various blink-and-you'll-miss-it references to small details in those games. Or, if you WISH you could get into the DR games, but they're too gory for you to handle - you're in luck! This is truly a "everybody lives AU" where characters mention plotting bad things, and past suffering, but it's like one-tenth as traumatizing as UDG, which is, imo, as dark as the series gets in terms of on-screen dark content.A third type of person who loooooves grinding and pixel-retro dungeon-crawling and turn-based combat, and doesn't mind swimsuit models of anime characters, will also find this game worth their money if it's on sale.There's a lot left to be desired in the explanations of stats and skills. If you get impatient with the slow pace of combat progression in the Battle Mode, you'll have to look up online guides on sites other than Steam. The whole shape of this game is based fully on the V3 post-game mode "talent development" so much so that V3's character's stats are directly copied from there. There are a few typos and confusing word choices that seem to stem from the translation choice to hew closer to the JP original text of THIS game, than the English translations of the OTHER games. Unfortunately, they still make Gonta talk like a caveman. He can TOO read! :(The game DOES have a gacha system, but it is 100% possible to unlock everything with in-game battles and grinding, there is NO pay-to-win here. There's no online multiplayer at all, so if you choose to pay any more than the sale-price into the "School Store Vending Machine" you're just choosing to spend money instead of time on unlocking the content of the game. This is a feel-good "power of friendship" visual novel that touches on some dark themes, and has some light Dragon-Quest-ish combat slapped on top. It's not a mystery-solving or combat-focused experience. Uber-fans could justifiably accuse this game of blaspheming against the series' central themes. But if you're able to ignore that part, and just want to learn more about the characters and their alternate-universe friendships, and just have some fun? This might be a good time for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp is a game that almost tries to be good, but, for the most part, isn't. Let's explore the ups and downs of the game (+, +/-, -, ?):+ I love seeing all these Danganronpa characters together! I need more Akane, Aoi, Miu and so forth in my life! For reasons!+ The game board is interesting.* There are many possibilities, many variables to take into account when improving your characters**+ The game looks and sounds nice, as Danganronpa always does.+ The turn-based RPG approach is interesting at first...+/- ... but then it's always the same thing. This game is extremely repetitive.+/- * The board never changes.- Acquiring skills is painful and very limited.- **Once your run is done, it's done. You can't continue leveling up your character after your run is over.- You need to get lucky in order to be strong AND fast enough to win the fights. Oh, and bosses are usually easier to beat than the normal enemies.- Unlocking everything would take forever. So, why would I try when nothing ever changes in the game anyway? If you really want to unlock everything, enjoy the random mono machines! Grinding! Grinding everywhere!- Everything comes and goes so fast, there's barely any time to get anything meaningful out of anything in the game.-- There's no story here, which is very, very fatal. Danganronpa has always been about the story and the characters, both of which are mostly absent. Yes, the characters might interact with each other, but does it matter? No.? I have rarely felt so disappointed with a game in my life. I love Danganronpa, but it's very hard to defend this game.? An absolute hardcore fan MAY love this.? This as a real board game could be damn awesome! Give us that instead of whatever the hell this is...Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp is sadly Danganronpa ASS: Ultimate Summer Grind. The game offers almost nothing to its players. Maybe, if you're the ultimate fan, you might get more out of this than I did. Sadly, I cannot recommend this to any sane person. I suggest you to play any other board game, get loaded, pass out and wake up naked without any money. That's pretty much how this game works anyway. 3/10.

_childDocuments_.review: It's ironic that so many people trash on the game for not being good, while for me it's the only Danganronpa game that feels like a game, rather than a visual novel with mini-games, with decent replay value. But I'm just part of the minority, who love the game as it is, and that's fine.I'll keep it brief. The game is designed to be a grindy fan-service board game rpg gacha. There is no actual plot to speak of, you can expect plenty of character interactions from across all 4 games, including Ultra Despair Girls, although there won't be any character development to take note of. You basically level up your characters individually by playing the development mode, or in other words, the board game where you roll a dice and land on panels, like in Mario Party games. The main goal is to level up your characters as much as you can, so they can be used as a traditional turn-based rpg 4-man party in the Tower Climb Battle Mode, in which your goal is to beat the waves of enemies, so you can advance further in the tower, until you reach the boss of the stage.There are 3 different types of vending machines, like in the previous Danganronpa games, from where you can unlock different characters in the exchange of in-game currency. This is the part which many people trash the game for, because it has an integrated microtransaction system in place, from where you can get X currency at the exchange of real life money. I need to note that unlike Freeware games, you can unlock everything there is to unlock in this game without paying for any microtransactions. There is no content locked behind paywalls. But the grinding can become excessive and tedious for some people.To conclude, I mainly play this game when I want to relax, unwind and turn my brain off, while vibing to music or podcasts. I love the game for what it is and do not regret my purchase at all. I'd only recommend you to get this game if you are looking for a:1. Happy world Danganronpa setting where all characters interact with each other.2. You like, or at the very least won't mind, grinding in video games. 3. You are looking for a simple, colorful game to unwind to.

_childDocuments_.review: It's what it says on the tin. A remake of ultimate talent development plan for $20, bigger gacha system, and microtransactions if you want a specific pull. I got gifted this, so will I play through it anyway? Probably. But you should probably not, since nothing about this is worth $20. Even if the dialogue was worthwhile (which it isn't, because Kodaka didn't write it), a lot of the transcripts for the events are on DRwiki anyway.Strong fangame energy from something that is "official" content in the loosest sense possible. For being such a die hard fan of the series that I am, one would think I'd be more offended, but I really don't care actually. Nothing can un-say or undo what was done in the canon and how we felt about it. That's one of the main points of the story of DR. Despite this tepid attempt to ruin it, I don't think it sustained any meaningful damage.Game shouldn't exist/10

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I played through UTDP in danganronpa v3, beat the entire thing and even grinded for extra couple hours to develop all the characters in the game for a little bonus dialogue. If we don't count the schizo grind in the end, it was ok, the dialogue brought joy, the cross-series interactions were welcome and exciting, even though it's all silly non-canon for-funzies stuff. In this game, I can't really fathom the amount of grind compared to the UTDP mode. You have 68 characters, each one takes 15-20 minutes to develop, there's a high chance you roll garbage even if you have U-cards, so the development doesn't guarantee further tower progression, the amount of pulls you get is minuscule with how many hours you have to put in, I just have massive hoyoverse games Vietnam flashbacks in this one and it's sickening. And the few fun interactions in each 15-20 minute run don't make up for the soul-draining non-stop grind. _childDocuments_.review: (Link to my Youtube play-through at the end of the review for anyone wanting to see a sample of gameplay before buying)Might as well post a review for Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp, since I've currently sunk 9 hours or so into this game and am pleasantly enjoying it for what it is. First thing you need to understand: this is a spin-off AU, and as such it has no relation (as far as I'm aware) to the actual story of the Danganronpa games. It's basically Danganronpa V3's Ultimate Talent Development Plan board game mode, except greatly extended and set on Jabberwock Island (Danganronpa 2's setting).Second thing you need to understand: this is a very grind-y sort of game. In essence, you pick a character from Trigger Happy Havoc, Goodbye Despair, Ultra Despair Girls or V3; you take them into Development Mode (the board game), where you level them up and develop their skills; then you can use your developed characters as party members in the Battle Mode, which is like an old-school turn-based RPG. All throughout this, you earn special Monocoins which can be used to unlock other characters or gain useful items/hype cards (which boost certain characters) from the various different MonoMono gacha Machines available in the Store mode. Rinse and repeat...So far, I've only managed to get to the fourth island in Development Mode and haven't even yet got to floor 10 in Battle Mode, so even after 9 hours of play there's still more for me to get my teeth into. The key point being: if you're not into games that do require you to grind a fair bit, then Danganronpa S may not be to your tastes. In essence, you have to develop your characters, get Monocoins, unlock more characters plus items and hype cards to improve their stats, develop more characters, redo characters you've already developed from scratch in order to make them even better, then push a bit further in Battle Mode, and so on and so forth.Personally, I've been enjoying it. Even if you're not into grind-y games, you might still like Danganronpa S just to do the friendly events in Development Mode, where you can get to see some of your favourite characters interacting with one another.There are only several other minor points worth noting:-If only the Ultra Despair Girls cast line-up for this game had also included Yuta Asahina and Fujisaki's dad, right? On the plus side though, thank god Haiji Towa wasn't included.-Everyone gets swimsuit sprites! Unfortunately, I feel like the designers got a bit bored once they reached V3's cast, as some of the Killing Harmony crew have the blandest swimwear of all time...-Mukuro is still disguised as Junko. She doesn't get sprites of her own self. Feels bad, man.-If only we could also have had some of the Danganronpa 3 anime characters starring in this too, right?But with all that said and done, I do recommend Danganronpa S - particularly if you enjoy the franchise. It's worth a shot, even just to see all your favourite characters having a nice, fun time and not having to worry about them trying to murder one another...

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a recycled version of the Talent Development Program from DRV3. It's not as high quality, but it is definitely easier to get through than DRV3's, so I can at least appreciate that. I guess my disappointment stems from me thinking it would have leaned more VN than the regular bonus mode. (Hell. I would've even been fine if they just did another version of the bonus modes from DR1 or DR2. Actually, why DIDN'T they just make it a huge Love Across the Universe??? That would've been  ). I wasn't a fan of it the first time, and I'm still not. I mean, the reason I love the games so much is because of its original gameplay and story, NOT the bonus mode gameplays (who the hell is raving about that...) The only fun thing about those is the bonus content and/ or the possibility of romancing a couple of your favs.As for the bonus interactions themselves... the writing is so  ... OFF. It's like they got someone who had a general idea of what the character's shtick is and ran with it, so you just get a lot of one-note dialogue. (This is especially true for Tenko). Of course, it's not all bad, but it just makes you wonder why they would release such a half-assed game. In the beginning, I was actually super hyped, even more so when I was seeing new CGs and sprites of the characters, but that was short-lived.A thing it does right that I wish they had done for the DRV3's Talent Development Program was that you could actually go back and look at the interactions you were able to get through development.Now, imagine my disdain when they brought back Monokuma's Dungeon 2.0 😌.. I was not happy to see this again, but I was elated to see it wasn't the same time-consuming BS as DRV3's. The only thing you have to worry about is pulling U versions of the characters and maxing them out. I'm not well-versed in these types of games, as I'm not at all interested in them, so I can't say for certain if I'm just really bad at them, but from what I experienced: It's still quite time-consuming and you have to be extremely lucky in a playthrough to complete each goal within the 50 days. Numerous times, I have played with the intention of maxing out the character and completing the goals, but because of a series of bad rolls and luck, I'm wasting my days on lowly Monobeasts and am hardly getting any progress on my stats, hence barely even reaching the 3rd island by day 45.Dear lord and DON'T get me started on when the Monkubs show up throughout my playthroughs. Tell me, why in the hell they made it so that the Monokubs--who are there to provide support and NOT be evil--are able to  impede on my progress????? Imagine my horror and  when Monosuke and Monokid show up and take a portion of my Monocoins when it's already hard enough to get a good roll to land on a shop or even earn a Shop Card; or, how about when Monodam shows up to forge my equipment and somehow he instead greatly decreases my stats when I just bought an upgrade with my dwindling Monocoins??? Are you kidding me?! I must be missing something, but I would think this game would have put a focus on fun and interactions with characters rather than making that incredibly difficult to do. Speaking of rolls, when I want to focus on landing on friendship squares, jfc I'm left wondering why they didn't separate it like they did in DRV3? 1 for Talent and another for Friendship, at the very least. It would make it so much less of a headache if I was able to land on more Strength or Talent Fragment squares, but of course that would be too easy... and why would it be easy? 🫠 It's not like this was supposed to be a celebration of DR's 10th anniversary and a gift for the fans..... Oh wait.But, at least if it gets too hard collecting all the presents, art, interactions, Ns Rs Ss Us, you can just buy 'em ! 🤪  🤠 Let's make an in-game purchase, shall we? 🤡 (Can you tell this game's made me insane in the membrane?)Overall, because I have an unhealthy obsession with Kokichi and an undying love for Danganronpa, I continue to play the game. However, if you're not the biggest fan and/ or Tobyn Jacobs when it comes to their favorite Danganronpa character, I suggest pretending this game doesn't exist AT ALL. It's an immensely offensive cash-grab to us fans.

Going into it you're going to get basic rpg combat and interactions between characters from all video games in the Danganronpa series (as of release). _childDocuments_.review: This game is based on the Ultimate Talent Development Plan from Danganronpa V3. For the most part, it is about the same game. There are some differences compared to it, however. This game is somewhat like a gacha game. To get all the characters and the new character cards requires a good amount of grinding.Do not play this this game if you are expecting anything significant. The game is mostly travelling around the board and talking to other characters. Play this game if you would like to see cute and funny interactions between characters. Honestly, the RPG battle mechanics are not that fun. It is somewhat basic. This game does not have dungeon crawling unlike Monokuma's test in V3. It is just battles. This game has a storyline but it is not to the level of the main games. I would only consider this game if you are a big fan of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: [Works on Steam Deck]I've seen a lot of complaints about this being a game that revolves around micro-transactions and I'd like to state although there are micro-transactions in the game, you do not necessarily need to buy them (although it is very tempting).This is basically a spin-off of the Danganronpa series, that plays as a board game and offers fan-service here and there. You can collect your favourite characters through cards (Either bought or earned through monomono coins) and you train them up by playing around the board.Honestly, i quite enjoy it as something to do when i don't want to think too much and just want my brain to be empty.6/10 - Not as great as the other entries in the series, but much of what i would expect from a spin-off game.

name: Dead Space
detailed_description: Dead Space Digital Deluxe Edition The Dead Space Digital Deluxe Edition includes the base game and 5 exclusive cosmetics (3 Unique Suits and 2 Suit Textures). It’s everything you need to look your best while surviving the horrors aboard the USG Ishimura. About the Game The sci-fi survival-horror classic Dead Space™ returns, completely rebuilt from the ground up to offer a deeper, more immersive experience. This remake brings jaw-dropping visual fidelity, suspenseful atmospheric audio, and improvements to gameplay while staying faithful to the original game’s thrilling vision. Isaac Clarke is an everyman engineer on a mission to repair a vast mining ship, the USG Ishimura, only to discover something has gone horribly wrong. The ship's crew has been slaughtered and Isaac’s beloved partner, Nicole, is lost somewhere on board. Now alone and armed with only his engineering tools and skills, Isaac races to find Nicole as the nightmarish mystery of what happened aboard the Ishimura unravels around him. Trapped with hostile creatures called Necromorphs, Isaac faces a battle for survival, not only against the escalating terrors of the ship but against his own crumbling sanity. IMMERSE YOURSELF IN NEXT-GEN SCI-FI HORROR A sci-fi horror classic returns fully rebuilt from the ground up with elevated visual fidelity and 3D atmospheric audio. From the frighteningly detailed rooms and workspaces of a slaughtered crew to the eerie atmospheric sounds of a desolate spaceship, you’ll explore a stunning sci-fi setting full of unpredictable and tense moments without interruption. UNRAVEL THE MYSTERY ABOARD THE USG ISHIMURA What starts as a routine repair mission for engineer Isaac Clarke and the crew of the USG Kellion quickly turns into a battle for survival as the truth behind the horrors onboard begins to unravel. Following an expanded narrative experience, uncover the dark secrets behind the events aboard the USG Ishimura through the final logs of the ill-fated crew and your encounters with the few survivors that remain. IMPROVISE TO SURVIVE Confront the nightmare aboard the USG Ishimura with genre-defining strategic gameplay. Repurpose and upgrade Isaac’s engineering tools to creatively defeat enemies with precision.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead space is one of my favourite horror game to this day when they announced the remake i just though it was another cash grab, a carbon copy of the original game with a fancy paint job but then i found out they were bringing Gunner Wright for Issac it grabbed my attention.Playing the remake felt like playing the original, it felt great and i like how they added the weapons into the environment it felt a lot more natural. I love how they changed the environment to be similar to the OG but still different. the side missions were a nice touch bringing a nice bit of options to to but i wish there were more side missions. The enemies are well made and have nice sound design. the armour was nicely remade faithful to the original and they even gave you a legacy rig which was a really nice touch The Dead space remake is a remake done right which is sadly rare, good job Motion Studio you seem very passionate about this remake and i hope that you continue to make some great games

I'm very pleased with this product, but i will say that i got all the bugs imaginable for this game though.  bugs--not being able to run at time-invisible enemy-missing items (key cards/power boxes)-unloaded doors-unloaded rooms that are completely black-fixed (stuck) camera angle-the play is invisible-the title screen is black and unloaded.There are some of the bugs i have encountered with this game, but the game its self is too good and i can look pass all the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a flawless example of what I want from modern-day remakes. The original Dead Space was fantastic but was slightly hindered by its somewhat clunky zero gravity mechanics and unbalanced array of weapons. The remake fixes all of these issues without changing anything meaningful about the aesthetics or level design of the original game. It very literally only upgrades the combat mechanics and the graphics while leaving the spirit of the original game very much intact. I wish that more modern remakes would take a lesson from this game. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who wants to get into more horror games this year, this game feels like a great starting point. Sure, I had to really ♥♥♥♥ around with the settings, but after getting it all down and getting to experience the game, this is great. The devs really nailed the atmosphere, while not particularly "scary" for me, I still get a kick out of, just looking at the blood writings and audio logs. The different weapons feel extremely satisfying to use, and when I eventually run out of ammo, I feel powerless against the Necromorphs, like I should be. Other people have also said that this game is extremely faithful to the original . I never played the original, but I can respect a group of devs that respect the source material.And the best praise of all, this game is actually ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ playable, unlike .Whether this is your first horror game, or you wanna revisit a classic, this is definitely the way to go. Hard recommend.
