_childDocuments_.review: The changes to the original game were a definite improvement. The story is even more intriguing than before. The graphics are a definite boon to the game. Occasional errors with loading were encountered where visually the room hasn't loaded, but physically it is there; as soon as you step into the room the visuals snap in. This happened maybe 5 times over the course of 20 hours of game play. Improved dialogue for the characters. Far more atmospheric than the original. I really liked the addition of the security clearance levels and master level access; Encouraged me to explore more. It made those areas scarier as the random encounters raised the alone vibe. I was glad to see the change to the zero-g. I remember having to jump around and then look around trying to find enemies, who also moved, being a frustrating mechanic from the original; that is now gone. The remake was well done. I pray the makers don't get greedy, rush, and skip, all the effort they put in for remaking the second one.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Space

_childDocuments_.review: Considering EA's track record I was really worried about this game and wasnt expecting much effort to be put into this but after finishing the game I have never been happier to be so wrong. This is easily one of the best remakes I have ever played and I think all companies that are looking to do something like this in the future should use Dead Space as a blueprint for how to remake a game the right way. I have played and beaten Dead Space 1, 2, and even 3 multiple times and I am a big fan of the franchise but I would be lying if I said Dead Space 3 and then the lack of Dead Space games after that didnt have me feeling  like the Dead Space I knew and loved was gone. With the Dead Space remake however, not only was the original games atmosphere and charm beautifully replicated, but it was taken a step further to keep things fresh for veterans of the series like myself. Everything was familiar but at the same time it had all changed enough to keep me on the edge of my seat the whole way through. As a remake this game is honestly up there with Resident Evil 2 for me as one of my absolute favorites. Both games managed to take a beloved game that has been played to death by its many fans, and refurbish it to bring it up to date while still keeping all the things that made us fall in love with the originals. Dead Space exceeded all of my expectations and I highly encourage everyone, new or returning, to give it a shot. Heres hoping that Dead Space 2 gets the same treatment in the near future. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space is my favourite game, I have been playing it since 2009 and at first I was afraid that the remake could be just a copy paste. The developers managed to keep all the things we love, but they also introduced a lot of stuff that really adds depth to the game and new gameplay options, thanks to the new side quests. The new graphics and gameplay are amazing, but there are two things I do not like: The blood effects look bad for a game based around gore and PERSONALLY I don´t like the new face models for Isaac, Hammond and Kyne, they look like different characters. This issues don´t ruin the fun in any way. 10/10 game for long-time fans and new players.

_childDocuments_.review: So, as someone who played the original Dead Space to death, the remake is good. But if you're like me, and you played the original game dozens of times, you might not get that much out of it. Isaac having a voice is cool, and Gunnar Wright is predictably great in the role, but not much else has changed other than visuals. That said if you HAVEN'T played Dead Space and you're interested, this is absolutely the version you should play.The remake irons out some of the annoying parts of the original, but not all. You do still feel like an errand boy sometimes, and the number of times you have to do a different task before you can complete your orginal task, get's super grating. But it's still fun overall. The new visuals are great, the new voice work is mostly solid, (Hammond and Kyne being the only obvious downgrades).Performance wise I can't say much, technically I don't meet minimum requirements (I only have 8 gigs of RAM) so I had to run the game on low, and it had to be the ONLY THING running, but it did run ok in those circumstances.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 6 hours in and its exactly what I'd hoped it would be. I spent countless hours on the original and was concerned on how this would turn out. I am NOT disapointed. Its the same great game as before with some slight reworks to levels (extra loot rooms/key items moved to different spots in room) while staying true to the original game design. Its enough of a redesign to keep you on your toes and slightly confused if you played the original. The sounds will keep you on edge and wondering when an enemy is going to pop out. Combat feels good and graphics are great. Only issue I had happen to me was a room decided to only load 3/4 of the assets inside making it impossible to progress. After reloading twice it worked and have had no further issues.  Overall great game that will be consuming my weekend.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space Remake is a reimagining of the iconic survival horror game that terrified players when it first launched. Set aboard the derelict mining spaceship Ishimura, players once again step into the shoes of engineer Isaac Clarke as he battles grotesque creatures known as Necromorphs while uncovering the dark secrets of the ship. With updated graphics, enhanced gameplay mechanics, and modernized controls, the remake aims to deliver an even more immersive and terrifying experience for both newcomers and fans of the original game.Pros:Updated graphics and visuals that breathe new life into the haunting atmosphere of the Ishimura.Modernized controls and gameplay mechanics that improve the overall experience while retaining the essence of the original.Enhanced audio design and soundtrack that heighten the tension and horror of the game.Faithful recreation of the original storyline with added depth and nuance, including potential new story elements.Potential for additional content and features to surprise both new and veteran players alike.Cons:♥♥♥♥♥♥ Map, these days we are used to fast travel and + a map that you can not add a waypoint to i miss fast travel other than that it's ok, Possibility of technical issues or performance problems, especially on certain platforms or hardware configurations. Necromorphs does not feel as threatning as they did in the original they do not run like crazy at you comes up to you like resident evil zombies in remake can be improvedGraphics:Dead Space Remake boasts updated graphics and visuals, with detailed character models, realistic environments, and improved lighting effects that bring the terrifying world of the Ishimura to life like never before. From the dimly lit corridors to the blood-soaked rooms, the remake aims to capture the eerie atmosphere and chilling aesthetic of the original game while leveraging the power of modern hardware.Gameplay:The gameplay in Dead Space Remake is modernized controls and mechanics, offering a smoother and more intuitive experience for players. From dismembering Necromorphs with strategic limb targeting to solving environmental puzzles and managing resources, every aspect of the gameplay is carefully crafted to balance nostalgia with innovation.Story:the storyline of Dead Space Remake is expected to closely follow the events of the original game,  With updated character models and voice acting, the remake deliver a more immersive and chilling storytelling experience for both new and returning players.Audio:The audio design in Dead Space Remake is enhanced, with atmospheric sound effects and a haunting soundtrack that complement the horror and tension of the gameplay. From the eerie whispers of the Necromorphs to the unsettling creaks and groans of the Ishimura, the remake deliver an immersive audio experience that adds to the overall atmosphere of the game.Replay Value:Dead Space Remake offer significant replay value, with multiple difficulty levels, unlockable content, and potential new features to keep players coming back for more. Whether you're a veteran of the original game or experiencing it for the first time, the remake aims to offer a compelling and terrifying experience that will keep you on the edge of your seat.Final Verdict: the most iconic survival horror games of all time. With updated graphics, enhanced gameplay mechanics, and a faithful recreation of the original experience, the remake satisfy both longtime fans and newcomers alike. EA Motive's dedication to preserving the spirit of Dead Space inspires confidence that Dead Space Remake will deliver a worthy successor to the classic horror title.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'd say this remake is a net improvement. Most of the changes Motive made to the game's formula work out, and the new bits of lore we get here and there are welcome, and expand the already tight story of the first game. I will say, however, that the changes made to zero - G took a lot of the fun out of the zero - G environments, and made some puzzles laughably easy, because they were originally designed with an entirely different zero - G system in mind. I know that might not have been Motive's call, but it's there nonetheless. The game also felt far too easy, even on hard. I'm not saying this needs to be Dark Souls or anything, but some extra challenge would be appreciated.

_childDocuments_.review: What I liked about your game, Motive, was the transparent communication with the players throughout your production period. Not a lot of developers have the guts to show the WIP of their works, but you did, and kept impressing us even more with each video uploaded on YouTube platform.Yeah, this isn't a review anymore, but a love letter. Thank you for putting all the effort to remake this game. While it stays true to the original, it's also different. Dejavu hits sometimes, but you guys have twisted it so good I feel like I'm being gaslighted.Even though you guys were completely transparent with the Sound Design aspect of this game, it still keeps catching me offguard. I really hope it wins the Sound Design award, you guys more than deserve it. Okay, back to review. Sound Design of this game is the second best I've seen (first is Hunt: Showdown). With every step you take in a dark hall, you can hear a Necromorph stalking you, ready to jump on you at any time. And don't let me get started about the whispers you keep hearing. Sounds of monsters are so well done I had to pause the game and scream as a mofo sneaked up on me in the dark.Many of the sounds are from the original, but effects have been added to them that make them completely new. For example, when you use a Health Pack, depending on the severity of your injuries, Isaac breaths a fresh air with various intensities. Also his voice changes depending on his injuries, makes you feel it when you're running around with RED hp.About the music, in an instance, I heard an out of tune plucked string instrument, it was wild af. Also it seems that every type of Necromorph have their own type of "music" attached to them. For example, those mimic-like skin tissue enemies that crawl on you have a very distinct fast and high pitch violin plays in a very chaotic and, again, distinct staccato fashion. It was beautiful, which lead me to quit and write this review.__________It stays true to "cutting off limbs," and honestly, it feels way harder than other Dead Space games. Or maybe I'm getting old. I had no problem aiming at the tail of a Leaper in the past, but here these guys are so agile with their tails, it feels like they hide them behind their bodies. Stasis isn't as op as it used to be.I've been playing on Hard difficulty, and had my ass handed back to me in a few instances. Enemies, however, feel a little bullet spongy. It's not easy to stun theme, and melee attacks are even less effective than the other games. However, it allows you to do a very quick melee attack after aiming, which helps when enemies get unexpectedly close.I love the new "Pick your poison" sections. Sometimes you have to divert power from one of your two options to a new section to progress... which leads to interesting choices. You want to venture in the dark? Or do you want to have the life support cut off from the area and rely on your Oxygen supply to carry you through? Both choices are equally thrilling and fun.Zero Gravity sections have been changed to what Dead Space 2 did: once you disengage your gravity boots, you have to rely on the installed Thrusters of your suit to orient yourself and find your way to the objective.Speaking of objectives, the Objective Finder (known as the Locator) is a bit annoying. Instead of being on-hold, it's now a single time use. If you didn't get it the first time, you have to use it again. Sometimes I have to check 5 times because the signal goes through the ground to show that you have to descend, but it's a bit difficult to follow when you're in a hurry.In addition to the main objective, which progresses the story, there are now optional objectives you can follow. Can't spoil much, but they are intertwined with the main objective. However, how it works and switching between main and optional objectives are a bit annoying. If you complete an optional objective, and it leads to another optional objective, game automatically switches to main objective, which means you have to manually change to the optional objective if you want to follow it.Upgrading your weapons and suit is a bit more complex than before: in addition to Power Nodes, you now require Upgrade Parts to further upgrade your equipment. This disallows you to break the early game balance by putting all your Nodes in, let's say, Plasma Cutter and wreck havoc on your enemies. This was annoying at first, but a welcome change, since it keeps the challenge throughout the entire playthrough.New weapons, instead of bought, are now acquired throughout the game. Also another way of keeping the balance in your fresh playthrough. In the previous games (Especially Dead Space 2) you could just buy a Linegun as soon as possible, and go through 4/5 of the game without much of a hassle. No more of that here.However, on higher difficulty settings, you realize that some weapons are simply outclassed completely by other weapons.__________Isaac now talks, and he's modeled after the voice actor, Gunner Wright! I love this guy's voice and it really brought Isaac to life in Dead Space 2. The voice acting of other characters are decent, but it lacks the depth that the original game had.The characters in the Remake feel like they've already been through this ♥♥♥♥ for some time. Kendra's "I don't know, something's in the room with us!" or Zach Hammond's "THEN REROUTE THE DAMN POWER!" from the original still haunt me to this day. They felt authentic and real. I finished the remake and I barely remember a line that was said.Some parts of the story have been changed to connect this game to the rest of the series, which was a welcome change.__________Graphics have improved a lot. There are godrays that really capture the feel of a foggy full of smoke area. Your flashlight also interacts with the fogs and smokes, which makes it interesting while engaging the enemies. There's also the screenshot on the Store Page, where godrays are going through the fog from behind a hanging tram system. It looks as beautiful in game as it looks there. There are also more stunning visuals like that later on.On the otherhand, for reflections, the game uses Screen Space effects intensively. In some instances, for example the beginning where the big screen is showing the progress of CEC, if you don't look at the screen, there will be no reflections on the ground. Immersion breaking.For enemies, the more you damage a limb, the more damaged the tissue becomes, eventually leaving nothing but bones, which you can shoot to cut. This also indicates how much damage an enemy has received to their limbs. You have to see their limbs after a non-lethal explosion. It looks and feels good.I can't really say much about the character faces. They look good enough :DThere are also small details such as the ignition torch on Flamethrower emitting light on objects.__________Throughout the game, I'm encountering severe stutters. I thought maybe it's because I'm playing on a 12100 and 6700 XT, but people with better systems are also reporting similar issues. This thing really hurts the overall smoothness of the game, and honestly shouldn't be ignored in a review.__________ I highly recommend this game. If you're new to the series, it's a great game. It's thrilling, scary, and puts you on your toes. Good headset is extremely recommended. Don't be like me and play it with earplugs. Get a proper sound system.If you're a veteran, I have to say the game has been in good hands. Definitely give it a try. I highly believe you'll like it.

_childDocuments_.review: + Mostly faithful recreation of the original (if you liked the original you will like this game, no doubt about it)+ Expands areas and concepts from the original in a clever way+ Adds in the improved gameplay from DS2+ Very smooth and enjoyable combat; all the weapons are fun and satisfying to use (even the Pulse Rifle has been balanced to be better now)+ Heavily incentivised to backtrack to unlock new things throughout the game+ Surprisingly long playtime for a single-player horror game (I played 19 hours for my first playthrough)+ Gorgeous visuals with practically no performance issues (unlike some recent space-set survival horror games)+ Thankfully no crafting system - the straight-forward, old-school upgrades are a better system+/- Voice acting is mostly good but some of the actors deliver their lines way too slowly, to an obnoxious degree+/- Lighting is overall great but sometimes they go too far in making areas dark to the point where it's almost impossible to see things+/- The true ending is hidden behind completing New Game Plus- The final boss is laughably easy and underwhelming (true to the original, I know)- Some mild wokeness which is a little bit cringe but not too bad- Nicole is noticeably older than Isaac which is a bit jarring- Isaac looks absolutely nothing like in the originals8.5/10 - A top-tier remake which excels in almost every way and is a text-book example on how to remake a beloved survival-horror classic, though it's not without some (minor) flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently played Dead Space(2008) about a month ago for the first time. With that being said I can see what all has changed without a 15 year gap to forget the little details. This game so far is far better than the original. Giving Isaac dialogue and taking his helmet off a few times makes him feel more human. Also the addition of the Nicole side mission helps the player feel some type of empathy for Isaac. In the 2008 version she was barely mentioned and i didn't even know his wife was on board apparently until i was almost done with the game. I have definitely jumped way more this go round. The sounds and Isaac's heart beat intensifying when his character is scared really gets you going. Graphics are amazing! There are a few optimization issues I've noticed, but cant say im surprised. All the changes I've noticed so far are for the better. The zero G parts are way smoother, the tram station concept i believe is better, the skin tear animation is awesome! Anyway if you played the game before and loved it then this is even better! If you have never played a Dead Space before than this is a great way to dive into the universe. Dead Space 2 aged pretty well so I would give that a go also.

_childDocuments_.review: This is through my own personal experience with this game so please keep in mind that everyone's experience with this game maybe different than mine. Before I really get through this review I just want to say that I am a HUGE Dead Space fan so coming into this game I had high expectations and let me tell you.. this game did not disappoint. I haven't played through the original game in quite sometime so everything to me felt new again. I enjoyed this game personally and I would recommend this game to anyone looking to get into the Dead Space franchise without having to play the original game and having to download patches. Yes, there are performance issues with the game but that did not affect me a whole lot personally. Although there was a glitch cut scene where a couple of scripted characters did not spawn in for me, this required me to go into my documents and delete the game shaders and redownload them, when this didn't work I had to verify the games files integrity, when this didn't work, I had to delete the shaders, verify the games files integrity AND then reload a different save which then fixed this issue. But this wasn't game breaking nor did it sour my experience with this game. Honestly this was really the only REAL issue I ran into throughout my entire play through, yes, I did see bits and pieces of the game loading in levels and assets but it wasn't all too bad. To really sum it up, the game stays true to the original and adds in a fine layer to mix things up just like Capcoms Resident Evil 2 Remake. Keeping the game the same while changing things up just a bit to change it up with fans who are familiar with the game.100% Recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Grandfather Isaac flies to save his grandmother Nicole.Oh yes, along the way you will have to shoot at necromen (necromorph) with glowing eyes. Some are so magical that they continue to walk on their feet without meat - science fiction!But if you don’t nitpick in detail about biology, this is a good shooter (or a good horror game for those who haven’t played Dead Space)!Dead Space 2008 could only be completed with a plasma cutter or pulse rifle, whereas now you have to use the entire arsenal of weapons to survive. There are a lot of weapons here, and a couple of new guns have been added! And the weapon is really “mining” and is used more for mining ore, but it’s also great for dismembering necromorphs!And yes, USG "Ishimura" is completely open, but it's even a little weird and ruins the atmosphere and immersion, in my opinion. After all, in reality, Ishimura is a multi-kilometer mining starship, so why can Isaac run from one end of Ishimura to the other in 5 minutes??? Ahahahah... SCIENCE FICTION!And so, in general, this is the same Dead Space, with improved graphics, combat and a plot more successfully integrated into the lore (one note, in the cartoon Dead Space: Downfall, the marker was really 20 meters high, when here the maximum is 4-5 meters, and the [containment field/dead space/safe zone around the marker] works differently, oh well, the writers, as always, smoked something, ahahaha... This point was corrected in Dead Space 2 2011 and it is still strange that it was not corrected in this remake).Oh, and there wasn’t enough money for the final cut-scene, because the piece of rock that falls on Aegis 7 was drawn in 2D, seriously??? EA, are you still that greedy???Okay, these are my little quibbles, the game is good!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the original Dead Space on PC and that wasnt very easy to play, lots of issues mouse control was terrible. Frame Rate decided how many issues you had.Honest question to the people who bought this, if the game was poor for you and it didn't run that well or you experienced bad issues, why would you give this game a good review? You should be holding the game makers accountable where it matters, bad reviews and review bombing.Honest question to the people who made this, Why bother making a game that you dont intend to make fixes for after the many people who have announced their issues. If you're not going to do a good job on a release, don't bother making the game guys. Its not that hard. If you gave people the choice between playing a stable game or charging them Triple A prices for a unstable game that everyone has already had the opportunity to play for years, I'm pretty sure the answer is at least obvious to the majority of us.I loved the Dead Space series, especially Dead Space 2, given there were less issues on that. There were less issues on Dead Space 3, despite it being on origin and nuked in terms of functionality after EA/Origin stopped caring about it. The very least they could do is get it right this time on PC. But, they didn't. Again, I love Dead Space and think that Dead Space 1 is a great game that is worth playing, it gets a solid 10/10 from me. But, this remake is a solid fail imo. It sounds like not everyone had issues, but the fact there are so many people who have complained about the stability on forums all over the place, a page is dedicated to surfacing many of these issues and discussing solutions in a single place, and yet these guys don't give a damn about it is enough for me to post a review and point this out. 6 hours of game time and at least 2 crashes per hour, and now in the latest area it 100% crashes everytime I enter a specific room? What is going on, I dont remember this many issues in the original on pc.Go buy the first game, It at the very least is more stable if you can get beyond the mouse struggles, maybe even get a cheap console to play it on. So sad, very disappointing.EDIT: I have to adjust my review because it turned out that 14xxx Series Intel processors are plagued with a weird stability issue. My crashes have at least possibly ceased with the latest bios update. It might be worth noting this for others looking for answers. I will say that the stuttering is still there but, without the crashes I can say thats a definitive improvement over the original game in terms of playability. The crashes were really killing it for me before, maybe not so much now.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic and faithful remake that takes some missteps in its execution. It is a great game, but a few things stood out for me that I feel should have been different.The three side quests should've just been integrated into the story.  They provide good backstory and are more or less along the way of the main path anyway.  As is, they're hard to keep track of due to the game's very limited HUD.  This disrupts the otherwise excellent pacing and flow of the game.There is still a limit of four equipped weapons.  Being able to use all weapons easily in battle would’ve been great fun.  It's a cumbersome limitation that didn’t need to exist.The boss fights are awful.  The boss fights were a weak point in the original, but they were not annoying.  Here, they are. _childDocuments_.review: First of all is this a good remake of the old game?      Yes, for sure!     This game instills the same loneliness and horror that the original did with a new coat of paint, excellent new methods of story telling through more conversations that happen as well as audio logs found throughout the Ishimura.  Gun upgrades still feel as rewarding as ever as the player collects power nodes throughout the ship they can upgrade various stats on their tools as well as their suit to improve survivability.  If you like the Resident Evil franchise before they went First Person I can strongly recommend this game.  Maybe not the remake as of yet but if you are interested in checking out the world maybe grab the original, as its still playable and fully complete.      However I will say that within the remake there are a few things that the team did to make the game feel a lot more smooth and less annoying.  The meteor segment that you had to laser focus on in the original title got redone so you don't feel like you have to lean forward and enter gamer stance to accomplish, as well as a few other redesigns that I would rather not spoil.  However a few things to make note, ensure you are installing this game on an SSD not an HDD otherwise some pretty odd things may occur like the following:    When progressing through the initial part of the story one of my favorite weapons in the game was unfortunately missing, The Ripper, a tool that essentially shoots chainsaw blades into your enemies.  Pretty great for dismembering limbs if you ask me, so it was a bummer that it wasn't present where everyone online stated where it would be.  No big deal though I moved on and just decided to use some of the other tools I usually don't use in my playthroughs I have used in the past.       Another thing that came up was that there was supposed to be a big cutscene where the villain, Mercer, explains his evil plans and why he thinks they aren't so evil to Isaac while they are face to face through a panel of glass.  When I ran into this scene it was just Isaac standing there talking to himself.  At the end of the scene an invisible monster broke through the glass and lucky enough since I was using the flamethrower as one of my weapons it wasn't too big of a problem.       Now for the big issue and the primary reason I am even writing this and why I can't justify anyone buying this or maybe I am extremely unlucky... I just got into Chapter 12, the last mission, and I was tasked to put 3 power cells back into a generator to essentially get the main story moving again.  I slowly descend into a pit where they're supposed to be located and to my surprise I could not find them.  Reloaded the game, went back down, no power cells.   Closed the game, checked file integrity through Steam, reopened it, descended into madness and still no power cells.  Now I am stuck waiting for EA to get back to me on a possible fix for this which could be who knows how long.  Further proving that games should NOT be purchased at launch, which is unfortunate because this is one of my favorite franchises.    TL;DR:                   Would I buy it now?  Yes, but only if you are a die hard fan of the franchise or something to scratch that Resident Evil itch.Edit:For some reason when I created another file and ran to the point where the Ripper spawns it was there.  I closed the game, and checked my other file to see if the power cells were there.  The only thing I changed was the game from being on an HDD to a SSD if this is really what caused the issue that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Game is still great but that's an awful bug.

_childDocuments_.review: Great remake, giving Dead Space a fresh coat of paint. And yes, the Plasma Cutter is still the best weapon.What's different? Visuals. This isn't a remaster; every visual was redone from the ground up, bringing this horror classic into the modern era. From textures and detail, to lighting and shadow, everything looks fantastic. The original game already had a foreboding atmosphere, which is made all the more striking now. This does lead to some heavy resource usage however and may result in needing to turn down the settings if your hardware is a little behind. When trying to keep most settings on ultra/high, my frames became almost non-existent. The game still looks and feels great on medium-high settings, but be warned.Beyond the visual clarity, some areas and quests, including small sections of the story, have been altered. They aren't changed drastically, so the remake still keeps much of the same feel while throwing a few new surprises to veterans. Sound design is still as top-notch as it was over a decade ago and I believe many of the original sound cues are the same. Notably, Isaac actually speaks this time (with the same VA). The game plays much more fluidly, at least from how I remember it. They have mixed in some of the QOL features from DS2/3, from the way Isaac moves, to Zero-G sections. It feels much less clunky (similar to DS2) while still restraining itself from the action romp of the third game. All weapons and tools make a return without any significant change in how they function. Loading screens are essentially gone, or at least extremely well hidden; this makes travel across the Ishimura incredibly smooth during long backtracking sessions for the few new side-quests that have been added.I did encounter a few technical bugs here and there, none of which were thankfully game-breaking (and most of which will probably be patched out). Otherwise, the game performs pretty solidly assuming your PC can handle it. If you love Dead Space and haven't played in a while, I definitely recommend giving this one a try, as it remains largely faithful to the original while still providing what feels like a new experience.

I don't care how "cheap" they are; I have not needed one yet for any MULTITUDE of things, and I'm not dropping another $80-$100 on a new peripheral just to play ONE game (now and in the foreseeable future.) 5 or so years from now when HDD are all but phased out? Call me then.That said, I did install this game to my HDD, just to see, and it DID run - and as far as I could tell run well - for the half hour or so I played it. I still refunded it because I didn't feel like getting half way through the game only for an impassable "error" to be thrown up because "LOL NO SSD." So I dunno. They should have been more detailed as to what they meant by errors, because if it was just longer loading times, I could have lived with those. And yet.Update: after a couple weeks or so of other people testing this game off of high-speed HDDs, apparently you can play it just fine from start to finish, so I bought it again. The only issues I ran into on my playthrough were a few times (I can count on one hand) where a spawned necromorph was invisible for a few seconds before it fully loaded in. There was some stuttering between some areas, but evidently that happens no matter what your game is loaded on. All that said it's one of the best, most faithful remakes of a game I have ever played...might even be THE most faithful ones ever.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't stop thinking about the way Isaac looks at where I point camera at. I know, bog standard third person video game features, seemingly every game has it these days. But, something about his high-tech welder mask that emits horizontal cold light dangles on the line between appearing human and alien. Or, maybe it's the robotic, heavy steps with dirty metal slabs on his shoulders reflecting the light bleeding in motion. It's easy to forget that Isaac Clarke - our avatar - is a human, until he grunts, cuss and stomp the pain away.(this is the part where I must clarify that while I did play the original Dead Space, I ultimately left half way through feeling somewhat unfulfilled, a very technically advanced experience and tremendous atmosphere that never managed to make me feel like I was in grave danger).-----------------------------------------------------------------------Playing Dead Space 2023 made me realize that AAA gaming hasn't progressed as much as I expected in the last 15 years. The whole "cutting limbs off" shebang remains Dead Space's most talked subject which over a decade later, only got iterated further instead of being pushed forward. At the same time, the idea of a remake that keeps "just enough" from the original is worth a debate point. After all, if we are all whole then what's the point of remaking us whole?The changes are visually visceral, the improvements are on paper, spectacular and clever. Weapons' alternative fire modes are more fun and balanced and useful. The metroidvania-lite structure introduces thrilling risk to the core loop. The changes to structure and level design make things flow better and give the Ishimura a more concrete identity gameplay-wise. The AI director is introduced to keep you on edge, create excitement through unpredictability. Enemies are tweaked and reworked to better complement the intensity and combat pacing. The "pick your poison" element built into specific rooms gives player more agency. On paper, Dead Space 2023 is a "perfect game".But that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, there's no such things as "perfect" games. You can nitpick that the base necromorphs move slower and the final boss fight is trite and easy, but got'cha like those never take away from complete packages. I don't think Dead Space is a perfect game, and it doesn't need to be so.But the thing about the game that cemented my love for it, is the contrast between Isaac in a soulless engineering suit, moving at the pace of a bulldozer, violently mowing down gratuitous creatures with coldness in his "eyes", while muttering "♥♥♥♥ this ship". This is a controversial change, giving Isaac Clarke a voice that is, from the same actor in the sequels no less. It's arguable that the lack of voice for Isaac Clarke added to the sinister beckoning atmosphere of Ishimura's stranded status, as "in space, nobody can hear you tearing apart flesh" remains constrained within these corporate backed space stations. What dirty job happened in the Ishimura stays in Ishimura. "Capitalism is a ♥♥♥♥♥", Dead Space broadly announces through various wall graffiti and text logs, even more so through Isaac's gestures of violence, which, towards the end, get even more exhausting.I think horror, at their most fullest, showcases human killing off their own self, both literally and figuratively. Like the slow descend to madness of Dani from Midsommar, the audience might not need to impose judgment onto character to feel their pain from dying, or actually, killing themselves from the inside. While Isaac used to be interpreted by his expressive movement and action, that Isaac before was a cog in the machine and just like puzzle design in an average Uncharted game, cogs are often conveniently thrown away in a corner so the machinist can come later and put it where it belongs. The new Isaac is the architect of death, one that has full agency of his action, the air that keeps the machine cooled and uninterrupted. The horror comes when this architect - us, realising his human part is slowly decaying. Are we more used to Isaac's real lavishly animated eyes full of humanity and hope, or the back of his head and his "health bar" visualized by his backbone which lights him up like a beacon in every single corner on this ship? The cruelty of futuristic industrialism renders us wholly alienated, where the only human trait left is the vaguely oval-shaped head animating above the vaguely backbone-shaped body clumsily twist and turn, mimicking real human movement. Human's worth as much as their head and body, until the voice comes up, blood drips down, and then the pain makes us whole.I strongly believe that remakes don't hold the duty to keep the spirit of the original alive. Souls can be reborn but never replicated. If anything, for me Dead Space did above and beyond what it was meant to be, to give an aging soul a new voice. This might not have been an original piece created entirely through new ideas, but it dares to speak up, loud and clearly, through fierce tone and end in powerful silence.

Here's a few differences between DS(2023) and DS(2008):-Modernized Zero-G navigation that makes the movement more akin to the sequels. _childDocuments_.review: So, I just finished my first play through, and I am definitely going back in for the new game+ later. This game is absolutely an improvement on the original Dead Space, and that is a very, very difficult thing to accomplish. The atmosphere has been pretty much better all around. There were a few things from the original game that I wish were in this one, but that pretty much adds up to maybe 4 to 6 specific sound effects that I prefer the original versions of. Other than that, the sound design was all around just better, and the graphical enhancements (particularly lighting improvements) just kicked the atmosphere into the next gear pretty consistently. This game looks and sounds amazing, and it is somehow significantly more immersive than the original. However, the atmosphere is the smallest improvement that was made in this humble gamer's opinion.The most significant improvements come in the gameplay. This game is just ridiculously fun to play. The guns have been drastically improved from the original. Most of the alternate fire modes were change and made infinitely more useful. So I found myself running a loadout that I would not have been caught dead with in the original game. The damage system on enemies and corpses is just objectively better, with the pealing system being used to deliver even more diagetic combat information to the player like which limbs are the weakest on the player's target. The progression system was also improved. There are a lot more upgrades for the guns and no empty nodes. the only barrier to weapon progression is finding upgrades in the game that expand the gun's upgrade tree.The story has also been greatly improved. While I think it comes at the cost of one of the character's personality, the overall narrative along with the writing for each other character is just a lot more cohesive and enjoyable than the original. There are even some characters that you kinda only saw through longs in the original that have their own stories sort of brought to life in this one. I definitely hold this version of the game as my personal head cannon for the series, and I enjoyed the changes to the story so much that I want Motive Studios to make a DS2 and 3 that follow their version of the story instead of the original. Because Motive revitalizes some sub plot threads that came from my favorite logs in the original game, and Motive has opened the door for those threads to be further explored and fulfilled where the original trilogy just kinda forgot those parts of the Dead Space universe. Obviously won't say what any of these things entail. I don't want to spoil this.Last but not least is the Ishimura itself. Along with the stellar atmosphere that both improves and respects the legacy of the original, the completely seamless experience of the Ishimura pushes the entire game an extra mile. There's no loading screens. The tram system is (as far as I could tell) an actual functioning tram system, and exploring the bowls of the massive industry defining planet cracker is as intuitive and terrifying as it ever has been. Seriously, play this game. Then, play the new game+. Then, play it again, and for Pete's sake buy the 70 dollar version. We need to show EA that projects like this are worth the funding. It's been a long time since I played a newly released feature complete single player game that was anywhere near this good. We really need more of these, and we need EA to fund more Motive Studio Dead Space projects.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space is a must-play for fans of survival horror games. The game's combat system is both intense and satisfying, as players must strategically dismember enemies to defeat them. The unique approach to combat adds a layer of strategy that is not often seen in other horror games, making it a thrilling and exciting experience.The atmosphere of Dead Space is truly frightening, with a foreboding soundtrack, dimly lit environments, and grotesque enemies that will have players constantly on edge. The game does an excellent job of creating a sense of isolation, as players are stranded on a spaceship with no hope of escape. The graphics and sound design work together to create a haunting and immersive experience.In addition to its thrilling combat and spine-chilling atmosphere, Dead Space also features a well-written and engaging storyline that will keep players invested from start to finish. The game's "Impossible" difficulty mode offers a great challenge for players looking to test their skills and push themselves to their limits. Overall, Dead Space is a true masterpiece of the survival horror genre and is not to be missed.

In game design, the player should *never* be frustrated. I completely gave up just 30 minutes after the Steam refund window and this will anger me whenever I think about this game. I wrongfully assumed that they'd fix this broken mess in the remake but all these glaring flaws of the original have been carefully preserved for this remake. I wasted $60 on this trash and I hope I can save you from sharing this same fate.

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal upgrade to a beloved classic, this remake takes what made the original good and elevates it on every level. Let's look at some of the changes. First, utilizing the zero-G controls of the later games made zero-G sections in this game far more fun than flinging yourself wall-to-wall with no control once you make the jump. It also makes sections like the basketball court a lot more fun. Opening the map up to be fully explored at any point in the game is another masterful choice, especially with the addition of security doors that encourage backtracking to get better gear and more loot. Speaking of gear, how they retooled upgrading makes it so much better than the original as well. Rather than waste nodes on empty slots, every node slot upgrades your weapon in some way. Not to mention the addition of unique weapon upgrades that add more firepower to each weapon, like damage over time for the plasma cutter. Back to the map itself, while many key areas play out the same, there are many changes in how you go from area to area, and certain areas are fully retooled to be unique from the original (thank you no more turret section). And also, the overall look and design of the game is beautiful. Like, when I'm not getting chased down by man-made horrors beyond my comprehension, I can stare out the windows of the bridge to Aegis-VII and get such a breathtaking view. The game looks just as good as it plays. Overall, if you love the original, this will blow your mind, and is a must-buy at any price. I sincerely hope EA plans to put out more Dead Space content, because Titan Station deserves to be given the same remake treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I left this review not long after launch and hoped it would be fixed. Changed to negative now as almost a year later and they have still not fixed the vast majority of issues this port has. Awesome remake stifled by an abysmal  PC port.ORIGINAL REVIEW:It's an excellent remake so far! Stays faithful to the original while taking some upgrades from the 2nd one and adding some extras to keep long time fans on their toes. Overall the visual presentation is outstanding! There are some muddy textures when seen up close in the light, but most of the game is dark and looks really stunning. Audio work is some of the best that has ever been done! Positional audio reminds me of the old Thief games but with the added benefit of modern acoustics/reverb. Everything sounds crisp and weighty. For the most part it plays great too for me. Shaders are pre-compiled (hopefully this is redone if drivers are updated too). There are definitely a fair few stutters around still tho. Nothing too bad for me yet, especially after I disabled dynamic res. But this seems to be an issue for most people so hopefully it can be resolved in a future patch.Frustrating to find out Denuvo is in this game too and not listed on the store page. I wouldn't have bought the game until that was removed if I was aware before. There's a good chance that is the cause of the stutters and the sooner they get rid of it the better.Edit: Anyone else noticing the muddy textures should disable DLSS and FSR and just go for TAA. Apparently something to do with variable rate shading is causing the textures to look worse since it's  sampling from the lower upscaled res. Roughness maps look crisp on TAA and I hope they can fix that too.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to believe, but Dead Space runs flawlessly. (i7 13700k, RTX4090 FE)Even without DLSS, i can play with TAA with the very best optics in 4k at an average of 95 fps. (TAA looks better than DLSS Quality and i locked it at 95hz)All on Ultra of course and raytraced ambient occlusion.It's possible! They can optimize!It's just EA. You may think what you want of this company, but if something can't go wrong, especially if you don't want to lose against the Callisto Trashocol disaster, they just pump in as much mo until it runs decent. Seems unfair, but here we finally have a perfect example of good optimization.Okay, in large rooms the framerate can drop to 75 fps. But it still remains smooth in these moments, "jerk-free" and doesn't disturb the flow of the game. You don't really notice the drops.Not much needs to be said about the game itself. It's a masterpiece, it's as fun as ever and now it just looks amazing.Thumbs up.Edit: Thumbs down....Happy too soon.After about 4 hours of happy playing time, I suddenly had a one-second black screen. After that, the game had a slight stuttering problem and looked a bit blurry. Ok, I thought to myself, somehow crashed, it can happen.So restarted and everything worked again.BUT! Since the black screen, the system suddenly runs at full throttle and the CPU suddenly gets way too hot. Over 100 degrees! and of course the PC gets way too loud. In addition, the graphics card is suddenly more busy and also gets hotter.I can't figure it out and have tried several things. The game is suddenly broken. As soon as you start it, the first loading screen doesn't even come, directly 100° and everything is full steam ahead and loud.What happened!?Everything was fine before this black screen.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be talking about the game in very broad strokes so don't worry about spoilers. I'm bananas about the Dead Space series. The experience of playing the original in 2009 or so left a massive impression on me and I think this is overall a pretty fantastic update. I've played the original  duology to death on every system, listened to stuff, looked at stuff, everything. So as someone who has Nicole's monologue burnt into the back of my eyelids, I was pretty sceptical Motive would be able to win me over with Dead Space 23. I was very pleasantly surprised, though. It's clear a lot of love and care went into refining Dead Space for the remake and in many ways I find these refinements make the setting, characters, and mysteries all a lot more compelling. On the lead up to release there was an IGN series of short interviews with developers, artists, writers, etc working on the remake. It was really fascinating hearing about how they were approaching different aspects of the project, there's a lot of interesting insights about the aesthetic and thematic goals of the game in there that get me really craving a Dead Space 23 art book. If you're sceptical about Dead Space 23, I think they're worth a watch. It's really striking how thoughtful they've been in creating their take on Dead Space and I don't think their efforts deserve to go so easily overlooked. If you're really interested in the artistry of the series I'd also highly recommend The Art of Dead Space, it's a great book and an amazing collection of art that really lays bare the core identity of the series. It's been a great companion piece to Dead Space 23.  I think a lot of people have been comparing the choices and artistic aims of the original team and the new devs in bad faith, I really can't see anything but reverence for the source material here. I'd also say that the differences that are there are interesting and well worth exploring!I'm also glad Dead Space has room to breathe again, EA really pushed the extended universe the first time around and I'm glad to see that mistake hasn't been repeated. I'm not someone who's super into lore, I like finding extra information that re-contextualises things in cool ways but this extended universe stuff can get pretty silly. There were animated movies, books, tie-in games, a Wii rail shooter (which I enjoyed) and most of it just served to undermine the setting and the horror for me. That isn't to say the remake shies away from its roots because it absolutely doesn't, there's an entire New Game+ path that I think incorporates a direct reference to one of the extended universe novels. If you're a lorehead you'll definitely recognise familiar names in text logs, even very forgettable characters get some mentions in. I really love this about the remake, it reincorporates a lot of this disparate stuff into more of a coherent whole. I think my favourite addition is the AI director that manages encounters and atmospheric effects. Dead Space is a game that invokes hypervigilance, I think that's part of what makes the series so compelling. You're always alert, always listening and watching, always looking over your shoulder. It has an intensity that I feel is absolutely unmatched. With the AI director in the mix that feeling is sharper than ever. You can't rely on memory alone to get you through now. Yeah, you can still memorise spawns and there are still an abundance of scripted encounters but you can never safely bet you know what's coming and when. Sometimes the lights will flicker and steam will hiss from the pipes- nothing. But sometimes a pregnant and most of a divider will be waiting for you right by the shop. You can truly never assume you're safe, that feeling is no longer illusory as it was in Dead Space 2008. I think that's great. I also found that the director would spawn interesting combinations of enemy types which is cool, it went a long way to making the threat more unpredictable. I never really experienced any of the performance issues everyone else is talking about so I think my main issue with the game is very petty. I flat out do not like the redesign of the Soldier rig. They look like those guys who're really into Mandalorian themed tactical gear and Punisher stuff. So, yeah, not sure if that's an intentional update to reflect reality but, aesthetically speaking, I found it very jarring. I think this is a very solid foundation to build on to bring back the Dead Space series. I hope in the future there might be more challenge modes, higher difficulties, more unlockable suits. Most of all though I hope Motive, like their predecessors, take some pointers from the Resident Evil games. I'm a big fan of the records system in the recent Resident Evil titles. It contributes enormously to replayability and it's neat getting to examine all the models, animations, concept art, all the good stuff. As someone who likes crafts and fan projects, something like that would be indispensable. it's all work that very much deserves to be admired, too. Some of the detail on the necromorphs is ludicrous. A records system would also be a great excuse to do wild runs like beating the game without healing or opening the shop. Just give me a reason, Motive.There are thousands of things about this remake that I could just keep gushing about. Maybe I'll update this review over time and do just that (I have). But I hope for now this review has gone some way to convincing you to try out Dead Space. Tanya Clarke killed it as Nicole, too.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be the first to admit. I expected this game to crash and burn. To make fun of people that bought what I assumed would be another EA dumpster fire. I was salty over what happened to visceral games and what they did to the series at the very end. When I heard that the original game was being remastered, one of my favorite games ever made that spawned a spectacular sequel , some fun and interesting spinoffs and books, and a deeply disappointing  final mainline entry. I fully expected it to devolve into a ♥♥♥♥ show that I wanted no part of. Eventually game play came out and while I thought it looked clunky and soulless with a new coat of paint. Eventually I could see the old game I deeply adored buried deep in there and it started to bring me hope for the game that truly brought me into my love of horror games. As of writing I have completed the game and I am about to start my NG+ playthrough. I couldn't have been happier with this game. In my opinion it is a remake in the same vein as the Resident Evil 2 remake. Everything old is new again. The Necromorphs look amazingly detailed and grizzly looking and the peeling system they added that originally thought would be unnoticeable in the heat of combat was a fantastic feature and helped me track which enemies were battle damaged in the thick of combat so I could prioritize better ammo on healthy enemies in order to save ammo and be efficient. Its incredible to watch the clothing, armor and even skin get scorched, severed and even blasted off by the weapons in game. For instant gratification, use the force gun on them. The new "open world" layout for the Ishimura is also a feature that I was skeptical of at first, but as the ship opened up more and more , the more I came to appreciate it. Gone is the old system of locked power node rooms and having to always keep a spare node in your inventory to open the rooms when you came to them. Instead these locked areas are opened up with the new security rating mechanic which greatly improved the feeling of progression for me personally as I would excitedly back track to these areas when ever my clearance increased and I felt the contents of these rooms was almost always worth the trek, more so I would imagine on hard or impossible compared to the lower difficulty where you are just showered in health and ammo. My one gripe with it is why is the Captain's clearance only level one. I guess it could be justified in some way in lore given how things go down but it still seemed weird.Weapons, my god the weapons. Every thing sounds fantastic and really show you how dangerous these engineering tools can be in the hands of an untrained person swinging them around or a engineer hell bent on finding his girlfriend thanks to the peeling mechanic again on the Necromorphs. Everything sounds like it packs a punch and it shows on their corpses after the fight ends. One thing that bothered me at first was some of weapons had their alternate fire modes changed. For example, the Line gun used to have a timed mine that would demolish anything that was near it after its small timer was up. Now its more of a trip laser that does continuous high damage along its path once placed on any surface, perfect for setting up a kill zone when you knew Necromorphs would start spawning in. I ended up loving the new alternate fire modes in the remake and had a blast trying to figure out how to best use them in each scenario, really made the game play feel that much deeper. Hands down, they are all better than the original game's version.The new story is also really good, they made several changes to audio and text logs to really flesh out the lore of the setting. Answering some questions and setting up a few more. I didn't like how somethings were completely spelled out for the player, but its probably for the best as before some of them are only answered in the sequels and kinda messily too. The game also has side objectives Isaac can do on the ship now as well that further flesh out some characters and their motivations. All the characters in my opinion were changed for the better and in some instances much more sympathetic and relatable instead of being just one note bad guys.All in all, playing the game was an amazing experience and it took me a little more than fourteen hours to beat the game and it's side missions and I still feel like I accidentally missed out on a few things at the end, some thing I am quickly going to correct on NG+.It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥ what EA did and what happened to Visceral Games, but that wasn't Motives fault. I sincerely hope that doesn't stop people form giving the game a chance. If it helps, then just pretend a different publisher funded it, but in an age where gaming seems to have devolved into terrible copy and paste game design, mediocre combat and truly awful writing. Its honestly refreshing to see a remaster that was more than just a cash grab and it honestly felt like every step of its development was filled with actual passion from some very talented people. As you could tell from my long winded review, I highly recommend fans of the original 08 release to give this game a try and for newer players to try out easily the best 3rd person shooter/horror game on the market. In my opinion nothing even comes remotely close for what the game is trying to do,

_childDocuments_.review: This game is another survival horror classic that has improved in almost every way, much like the Resident Evil remakes and hopefully the Silent Hill 2 remake.I never beat the original game, and I didn't play it long before playing the remake. So I was coming in without nostalgia but a pretty good idea of what to expect. From someone who didn't necessarily have an attachment to the original, I can safely say that this is a pretty great remake, and an excellent standalone game.Dead Space puts you in the shoes of Isaac Clarke, an engineer investigating a massive abandoned "planet cracker" ship. When he and his crew are attacked by endless hordes of flesh monsters -- Necromorphs -- it becomes a desperate struggle to escape the ship instead. Personally, I feel the story has been massively improved from the first. With Isaac talking now, conversations are much smoother and Isaac feels like he has more initiative. Kendra is a much more likable character and feels more natural. Hammond... might be a slight downgrade, with the new voice actor sounding a bit dull. But generally, a lot of the story beats have been touched up and tends to be more exciting. Plus the new side quests give more reason to back track, and the new intensity director makes going back just as exciting as going forward. I also hear there's an alternate ending, though I've yet to see it.The combat is incredibly engaging. A wide variety of enemy types and good placement, even by the intensity director, mixes things up. The weapons have been massively upgraded, and all of them feel very satisfying to use. My personal favorites are probably the flamethrower, contact beam, and force gun. But all of the weapons are great, especially with the improved upgrade system making it far more interesting to use power nodes.The best part about combat is the kinesis module -- tearing their limbs off and jamming it back into them and watching them fly is so satisfying. It gives skill expression to combat beyond "shoot them in the head", or in this case, "cut their limbs off". You can also kill enemies using a wheelchair.Anyways, this game is pretty great all and all. If you're a survival horror fan, this is a must play. Plus my name is also Isaac, so I'm basically in the game. This makes it the best game released since The Binding of Isaac.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR if you want to skip my yapping. The game is amazing as the reviews already show. Play it. SimpleThe Original Dead Space is easily my favorite horror game that I’ve ever played through. Despite some of it’s aged level design and few gameplay mechanics like the zero gravity sections for example, the direction that was taken making the dark, creepy, and desolate atmosphere of the Ishimura with gameplay blended so perfectly well into visual itself while offering graphic and horrific, sometimes stress inducing, is what made the game standout the most in my opinion. The game does a fantastic job of making sure you feel the horrific and hopeless situation you’re in while playing as Isaac and it does so much to make sure you don’t feel like you’re escaping that scenario. When I first heard that this beloved game was getting a remake after so long of no hope that EA would touch this series after Dead Space 3 not making the numbers they wanted, I was excited but scared. Despite all the games having their moments of horror and scares, the original Dead Space had a level of dread in its setting and direction that the other games were not able to match. I was even more worried with Callisto Protocol…being Callisto Protocol. And let’s be for real, this is EA, not the best track record.To see that EA and the developers not only made sure to keep the spirit of what made the original game alive and refreshing, but in some ways make it even better than the original! (I do have my icks on a few changes but I would be petty to have that be a drag to what they managed to accomplish.) It comes to full surprise that they’ve managed to do so well.The graphics are perfect, not too little to argue if it is an upgrade and not too to where you feel like it’s not Dead Space anymore. The gameplay is better than I could have imagined. From reworks to the arsenal of the original. Thanks to the interaction and secondary fire changes, every weapon feels strong and unique. In the original I honestly constantly ran with 3 weapons with my 4th option being a filler incase of low ammo. In the remake every weapon is worth using now. A weapon like the Flamethrower was absolute garbage in the original, but on here it’s unbelievable how fun and good it is now. For a good 2 hours on one of my play sessions, I was In disbelief I haven’t used the Plasma cutter for so long when in the original I wouldn’t dare myself to take it off. The new Zero Gravity sections are a much needed change and all of them don’t feel annoying and a chore to do. Being able to explore more parts of the Ishimura is a great and terrifying experience with the new director making sure you don’t have a moment of peace and silence in your horrific journey. The game does even more to make sure you don’t escape the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you’re in with the new director and no loading screens essentially anywhere. The detail of Necromorphs being torn apart as you damage them is endless fun with how the weapons perform now. With all the changes to how the game plays, it manages to go beyond of what the original managed accomplish in a lot of ways.There are some things that I can’t say are perfect. I won’t get into the story too much as I don’t want this review to involve spoilers, but the change of Isaac not being voiceless is a bit of a mixed change. While I do love how they make Isaac be more empathetic and interactive in the story, having him be voiceless allowed characters to be more attachable to the player. Some of the changes to the characters are still a bit jarring, like Hammond for example, but I’m not gonna trash it like it’s downright bad. It’s something I think can be a debate for some people. And some particular story moments, like the ending for example can also be debated if the original was done better.But I digress. This remake of Dead Space is a great and welcomed surprise from EA. Motive were able to do a fantastic job of bringing Dead Space back, making it feel like a new experience while also keeping the original intact. In its entirety, it’s still the original. But playing it makes it feel like it’s a brand new game all over again. This is by far one of the best remakes I’ve ever played and I can’t recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Dead Space so I was pretty excited to see this game come out. I was not disappointed at all when I started playing. The game was done perfectly and should be a model for any remake out there. It did so much to encapsulate the true feeling of horror that you feel when you played the original. You get the same feeling from the original game, but they added and changed so much content that it made me feel like I was playing a completely new game. The storyline is still essentially the same, but it does everything right when it comes to building more around the existing story.The addition of side quests and the ability to truly explore the Ishimura with the new systems in place to make sure that you never have the same experience twice are phenomenal. If you enjoyed the first dead space game, then you're going to love this one 1000x more.All of that being said...there are some game breaking bugs that you will experience. For instance, I saved my game and went to fight Leviathan and my audio logs started to bug out to the point where I couldn't hear or see anyone talking. Then, when it was time to progress to the next area, my chat with Hammond completely stopped working and the doors were stuck on standby so I had to alt-f4 (reloading the game didn't fix anything). I've also been yeeted out of the map by a few zombies when I try to run past them. Tbh I haven't played a game recently that hasn't had bugs like this so it's hard for me to dock the team for having these issues, but they really need to get fixed because it can be something that completely breaks the game. If you're willing to fight past some of those bugs, which are few and far between, then it's definitely worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to turn the spooky bois into a lovely garlic butter steak and potatoes skillet, follow the steps below:INGREDIENTS LIST FOR THE STEAK AND POTATOES1 1/2 lb (650g) flank steak, sliced against grain (if you squish the scary bois you can take some chunks from them. You can use organs as well, but they have a weird squishy taste to them)1 1/2 lb (650g) baby yellow potatoes, quartered1 tablespoon olive oil3 tablespoons butter, divided5 garlic cloves, minced1 teaspoon fresh thyme, chopped1 teaspoon fresh rosemary, chopped1 teaspoon fresh oregano, choppedSalt and fresh cracked pepperCrushed red chili pepper flakes, optionalThe marinade1/3 cup soy sauce (or coconut amino for paleo and gluten-free)1 tablespoon olive oil1 tablespoon hot sauce (we used Sriracha)Fresh cracked pepperDIRECTIONS1. To prepare the garlic butter steak recipe with potatoes wedges: In a large bowl, combine the steak (spooky boi chunks) with soy sauce, olive oil, pepper, and hot sauce. Set aside and allow steak (spooky boi chunks) to marinate while you cook potatoes. (be warned that other spooky bois may try to eat this while marinating)2. In a large skillet over medium-high heat (you can go into the engine maintenance room, very big fire above you), mix 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter. When butter is melted, add potatoes wedges. Cook for about 4 minutes, stir and cook an additional 4-5 minutes until potatoes wedges are golden and fork-tender. Transfer sauteed potatoes to a plate and set aside. (be careful for the babies, they will attempt to yoink the potatoes)3. Keep the same skillet over medium heat and add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter, garlic, red chili pepper flakes, and fresh herbs. Lay the steak (spooky boi chunks) in one layer in the skillet, keeping the drained steak marinade for later. Cook the steak (spooky boi chunks) on each side for 1 minute each, until nicely browned – adjust timing depending on how you like your steak.4. Right before the Garlic Butter steak (cooked spooky boi chunks) is done, you can stir in the reserved marinade if you like, and cook for one minute. Add the potatoes wedges back to the garlic butter steak pan and heat through. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if necessary.5. Remove from heat and serve immediately your steak (cooked spooky boi chunks) and potatoes, garnished with more crushed chili pepper, fresh herbs, and a sprinkle of parmesan cheese over the potatoes if you like. Enjoy!I am not liable for any death or injuries as a result of one attempting this recipe.

_childDocuments_.review: This is unexpectedly an amazingly good game. I've never been a fan of the Dead Space franchise (didn't play the first three games), so this marks my entry into the whole shabang and what an entry it is!This game shows polish, it has a lot of complex gameplay systems and mechanics that greatly help with feeling immersed. Things that other games *coughcough*Starcitizen*cough* promise for years - that when you open a door to open space, all other open nearby rooms and corridors vent their atmosphere - are implemented here. Among a long list of other sensible, functional systems. Sound design is very high quality and the difficulty also seems fair. Also can we talk about just how properly 2023 this game looks? REALLY good. Awesome volumetric light effects, very crisp tonemapping and bloom and the various holo UI screens are also nicely made. _childDocuments_.review: A great remake of the original sci-horror epic, Dead Space is a 3rd person survival-horror type game.Not just a simple improvement on graphics (which are amazing), but addition of entire new map areas, different boss fights, secrets, alternate endings, and removal of annoyances (such as power-node doors). Isaac can run now too, huge plus. Platform stability is good, rarely crashes. Lighting and sound changes deserve a special shout-out, definitely amps up the horror immersion, even for experienced players (much darker areas, no more 'loud' vent crashing).Isaac is a lot 'clunkier'; melee feels more awkward, and the stasis in PARTICULAR is rather infuriating; no longer an instant spell cast for safety, its additional animation treats it more of a fireball projectile rather than an area of effect space-breather. These changes could be a pro for immersion or con for gameplay. Watch for high temperatures on your computer! Immersion improvement comes at a price.   Some character models in cut-scenes completely disappear upon certain play-throughs, especially fast ones. Major flaw. The good thing is that the game will continue to progress normally.Not perfect, but I appreciate any inroads in the Dead Space series. Worth every penny spent in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Space

_childDocuments_.review: Like Resident Evil 2: Remake, the devs knew the do's and don'ts of what they were working with, a flawless remake that manages to keep the spirit of the original game and only adds enough new content here and there, the Dead Space gameplay feels fresh as ever with this new coat of paint, with the only new aspect of the gameplay being the gore being layered (skin>muscle>bone> then the limb gets cut)Some new dialogue here and there, ficts perfectly since its just more context to the Unitology that veterans of the series are gonna enjoy and newcomers will understand the whole religious theme, Isaac speaks too, with Gunner Wright returning as Isaac, the same VA for DS2 and DS3, solid dialogue that fits the character, nothing overblown, Isaac still is the good ol' mechanic that its fighting for his life here, Nicole VA, Tanya Clarke came back for her character and same as Isaac, nice dialogues, solid stuff, good acting.On the technical deparment the game runs flawless, no stuttering, no crashes, solid framerates even at Ultra settings on 2560x1440p resolution, granted my machine is overkill (5800x3D, 3090ti, 32gb RAM at 3600mhz) but with DLSS 2 and 3 being and option it has great perfomance for almost all configurations.Very happy with this remake, I'm an avid fan and I was kinda worried, but its solid, manages to perfectly capture the spirit of the original and doesn't have unnecesary changes, great for veterans of the series and newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a faithful remake of the original with upgrades in all the right places - I think they nailed it.- Issac got a personality module inserted- The sound effects 👌. _childDocuments_.review: Playing the Dead Space remaster was the first time I played the game, aside from a few minutes watching friends play it on Xbox.Dead Space brings a unique approach to the singleplayer shooter genre. Rather than just "shooting to kill", you're forced to think outside of the box in order to kill immortal enemies, while conserving resources (not uncommon for survival games). My only gripe is that I wish there was more.Lots of points in the game, you're given different weapons and tools, but the different ways you can use them isn't always 100% clear. I went through most of the game frustrated, trying to conserve my ammo. It wouldn't be until the end of the game, where out of shear desperation, I'd find super-easy ways to cheese some enemies. Up until those times, it was easier just to fork over the cash for your ammo of choice.If you love mindless shooters, this is the game for you. I loved exploring the cool environments, but honestly the enemies made it hard to appreciate. I'm a PC guy playing w/ controller, so it's definitely a skill issue, but the random onslaught of enemies often had me reloading because I didn't have the proper weapons equipped. It made it harder to enjoy the world and story.That being said, near the end, I started to find the combat cycle monotonous and I just wish I could plow through to the end. The "zero gravity spaces" especially really ground my gears, with the broken nav system, and random enemies showing up from every which way. Maybe that's just me.The story was my favorite part of the game. I would've loved to go back and collect all the logs, listen to all the audio, and stay up until 3am watching lore videos. I honestly wish I could've gotten more. The ending is fine, but the story along the way really sets you up for something special.It shouldn't come as a surprise nowadays; the game runs poorly. Hardware requirements are above, but honestly it's not an amazing experience. For a game that's  dark, the render pipeline is packed full of temporal AA and generative upscaling.On Steam Deck, there were no issues with the game itself, but playing w/ default settings is unplayable. The frame-rate is "ok", but the visuals look like murky soup from all the upscaling, so the game is virtually unplayable. After toning down all the settings, the game is "clearer", but performance is inconsistent. Mostly you get 30-40fps, but there are obvious "un-optimized" areas where it drops to slideshow-tier.This makes me really sad, because it reminds me of games like Alien: Isolation, whose graphics look better (at a smaller resolution, granted), run 2-3x better, and is over .I don't think I am going to 100% this game. I really wanted to, but lots of last achievements look difficult, which I don't think I'm going to be able to do, unless I commit my weekends to playing on desktop. This makes me kind of sad, but I still would recommend you try the game if you're already thinking about it.
