_childDocuments_.review: This Dead Space remake is, in my opinion, the epitome of what a remake should be: Honoring the original vision of the game while improving upon what was there to begin with. In other words, if the original team of Dead Space created this game today, I imagine it may not be far off from what we have received with this game. There are many positives to have with this remake with few negatives, so let's go through it quickly.Improvements:- Isaac Clarke is no longer a silent protagonist- Graphics and lighting- Greater Exploration- Interesting Side Stories- Necromorph dismemberment- AI Director which makes exploration more tense- Added Dead Space 2 Zero GPositives:- Story is interesting and compelling- Gameplay is intense and very fun- No HUD which gives a more immersive horror experience- Foam HandDrawbacks:- Replaying the game can be annoying due to security clearance not carrying over and unskippable in-game cutscenes (luckily cutscenes are not common and generally short)- Impossible mode does not increase difficulty, or at least very little, and instead turns the game game into a 'Die and Restart' mode which I am not the biggest fan of- Stuttering when entering areas that require a new load in- One feature that I wish got a little more love is the "Limited Power System." Essentially, when some system needs power in order to advance, sometimes you may need to turn off power to the lights or even life support. I wish there were more areas that required you to make a decision between these options or even add more to the mix like Zero G and maybe even something like "Ventilation" which would cause more necromorphs to spawn.Overall, it's not a perfect game of course, but it is an especially fun game that does way more right than wrong that it gets a 10/10 score from me and a definite recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Yo, fellow gamers and furry enthusiasts! It's Kiba Snowpaw here, your alpha male Ice Wolf from the ice world of HowlStrom. I've got some chilling insights on the epic return of the sci-fi horror classic, . I remember when I first got my paws on the original Dead Space back in 2008 and followed the spine-tingling franchise ever since. Now, let's dive deep into the icy depths of this masterful remake.In the 2023 remake of , we once again step into the boots of Isaac Clarke, an engineer thrust into a nightmare aboard the USG Ishimura. This colossal mining ship is overrun by Necromorphs, monstrous reanimated corpses that turn the ship into a blood-soaked labyrinth. Isaac's mission is to find his beloved partner, Nicole, while unraveling the sinister mystery behind the Marker, a relic that drives people mad and resurrects the dead.The original  was a game-changer, combining survival horror with a rich sci-fi narrative. This remake stays true to its roots while introducing visual and gameplay enhancements that make it feel fresh and terrifyingly immersive. It's a thrilling blend of nostalgia and innovation, capturing the essence of the original while pushing the boundaries of modern gaming.Motive Studio, the pack behind this epic remake, is part of the Electronic Arts family. These guys have resurrected  with such dedication, it's like they were born on HowlStrom with a natural talent for crafting icy horror masterpieces. The use of the Frostbite Engine showcases their prowess, delivering stunning visuals and seamless gameplay.Let's break down the key elements of this game: The graphics are jaw-dropping. From the eerie corridors to the grotesque Necromorphs, every detail is meticulously crafted. The dynamic lighting and volumetric fog create an oppressive atmosphere that keeps you on edge. The sound design is a symphony of terror. The creaks of the Ishimura, the distant screams, and the whispering voices create an immersive audio experience. Wearing headphones? You'll feel like you're actually aboard the doomed ship. The remake introduces improvements like thrusters for zero-gravity movement and a revamped combat system. Isaac is no longer a silent protagonist; his voice adds depth to his character and interactions. Isaac Clarke is our everyman hero, an engineer turned survivor. His journey is both physical and psychological as he battles Necromorphs and his own sanity. The crew of the USG Kellion and Ishimura come alive with enhanced voice acting and more fleshed-out backstories. Characters like Kendra Daniels and Zach Hammond add layers to the narrative. Isaac's transformation from a desperate engineer to a hardened survivor is compelling. His hallucinations and memories of Nicole provide emotional weight to the horror.The game is structured around the exploration of the Ishimura, divided into distinct sections like Medical, Engineering, and Hydroponics. Each area presents unique challenges and enemies, keeping the gameplay varied and engaging. The seamless transitions and lack of loading screens enhance the immersive experience.The impact of  on the survival horror genre cannot be overstated. This remake reaffirms its status as a genre-defining title. It influences new players and veterans alike, showing how a remake should be done.The hook of  lies in its perfect blend of sci-fi horror and survival gameplay. The thesis? To survive, you must confront your fears head-on, whether they're Necromorphs or the ghosts of your past. As a long-time fan and FPS gamer, this remake was a howl of a time. It brought back memories of my first terrifying playthrough while introducing new thrills. (2023) is a masterclass in how to remake a beloved game. It respects the source material while enhancing it for a modern audience. The balance of horror, narrative, and gameplay is near perfect.In conclusion,  (2023) is a chilling triumph. Whether you're a long-time fan like me or a newcomer to the series, this game is a must-play. It's a testament to the power of a well-crafted remake and a shining example of what survival horror should be. So, gear up, fellow furries and gamers, and prepare for a journey into the heart of darkness aboard the USG Ishimura. This Ice Wolf gives it a frosty thumbs-up!

_childDocuments_.review: Surpasses all expectations. Better than the original in nearly every conceivable way. This is the way you do remakes. NO cut content, only enhancing what existed before and adding additional content on top of it. The graphics are fantastic, the game-play loop feels fun and engaging, much more similar to Dead Space 2 in that everything feels more fluid and smooth, kinesis is much more effective with ripping off limbs and pinning enemies to walls, just like DS2. The story feels way more fleshed out with a lot of additional dialogue and exposition surrounding the lore, about what the marker is doing to people, unitology, etc. The story just feels more complete and immersive than in the original game. It's more up front and center, versus just in the background. The new inter-connectivity of the Ishimura makes the ship feel tangible and massive in size and scope. There's more incentive to backtrack and revisit previously explored areas now due to the security clearance system(sort of similar to how the Power Node doors worked in the old games). I just can't stop glowing about this game.It DOES have some performance issues right now, but I expect these to be patched sooner rather than later. There is some stuttering, and it's my belief this is due to shader loading but I could be wrong. The game pre-loads shaders, but I don't think it's preloading ALL of them. The game also utilizes inherent Variable Rate Shading, and there's no way to turn it off. This is causing some issues with aliasing and muddier than usual textures when utilizing DLSS. It becomes more obvious the lower the internal res gets. There's also some weird "ghosting" like effect on Issac's character model with DLSS on. It's more obvious in brighter lit environments, but when strafing back and forth with Issac, you notice a trailing/ghosting effect on the model. If you turn DLSS off, it solves this about 90% of the way I'd say. The problem is, turning DLSS off is a major performance hit, and depending on your hardware, it may not be worth it to you to do so. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Remakes are probably one of the most controversial takes on media as they become all more and more common as technology progresses.  Movies, shows and games alike all receive the treatment, redone for modern sensibilities or new takes or more commonly to attempt to breathe new life into something that has shown its age as the graphical and technological landscape changes.A lot of the time remakes get immediately eschewed by many for being void of artistic merit, simply copying what is already there and often times losing the "soul" that gives something its artistic life to begin with.  An easy attempt at a sure cash in, banking on nostalgia and cobbling together something to get a guaranteed buy from some old fans and hopefully capture a younger audience.However, every once in awhile, a remake gets "it".  A studio understands what made the game special in the first place, artistically, critically and is able to capture that essence and bring it into the modern age, and all that comes with it.  I think the gold standard for remakes when it comes to video games that most serious gamers will regard is the 2002 Resident Evil remake of the 1996 game.  Despite only an 8 year difference.  REmake (as it's affectionately called) improves in every aspect of the original (except for maybe some of the unintentional camp...to which is still pays homage).  Graphically, narratively,and artistically.  It adds to what is there in only meaningful ways while staying truly faithful to it's source.  And while the Resident Evil 2 remake is exceptionally good (less so it's sister sequel) it falls nearly into the realm of a total re-imagining.  Of the highest quality but drastically different from its source material.Dead Space 2023, manages, despite all my expectations.  To be an improvement, in every way over the 2008 original, one of my most beloved games of all time.   Initially heavily skeptical and assuming The Callisto Protocol to be my new love and the DS remake to be a meandering attempt at recapturing the feel of the original.  But truly, Motive Studio has done a truly remarkable job at understanding what made Dead Space excellent.  From it's beautiful graphics and lighting and excellent sound design and the tightened up gameplay.  Dead Space truly only sought to add and improve upon what was there, while still feeling entirely its own.  With a more expansive take on the games narrative and structure, you're offered more freedom to move and stretch your legs around the Ishimura's horrifying halls, while also always being pushed directly ahead for those who wish to pursue at the pace they feel most comfortable...or uncomfortable in this case.I think the most remarkable thing is that for the most part, the gameplay functions almost entirely the same and the only improvements are to the general tightness of aiming, Dead Space despite being a game from 5 years ago, still plays so well with only simple tweaking.  And while the original Dead Space manages to look quite decent for its age thanks to some excellent lightning, I would be hard pressed to give any reason now to choose the original over the remake if not for personal nostalgia.  As the remake in my opinion, improves over everything that was there before, expanding on the story, adding some simple sidequests and offering some more insight into Isaac Clarke and as well the horrifying necromorphs themselves.If I had any critique over the remake it would be that perhaps it doesnt add enough to the original to shake things up.  But its a truly delicate balance and adding in new bosses, enemy types or areas and you may spoiling what was already there or separating yourself further from the initial source material.Ultimately, the Dead Space remake is a truly faithful, fun, horrifying and deeply engaging game that should leave any fans of Dead Space deeply pleased while hopefully bringing in many new fans to the series.  Here's hoping we get 2 afterwards!

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space (2008) was a sleeper hit that no one saw coming. It still stands as one of the best gaming experiences out there, and though not perfect, it can't get but a glowing review.And this remake, actually takes the core concepts of the original game, redesigns them, adds upon them, and... just mechanically speaking, creates a product that... is probably what Dead Space would be if it came out today using today's technology. Put it simply, Dead Space remake is a woke mess that poisons the original story. And in a story driven horror game, that is kind of important. Characters are made gay... disproportionately to reality, gender bathrooms are added... and of course. THE MESSAGE is everywhere. The problem with redesigning the characters to fit a certain political mold, is that they don't fit the original story. For example, in the original game Hammond is a no nonsense military type. He's takes charge of the situation, but you can't really trust him because of his military affiliation. The game shows a competent, military career man, and when doubt is placed on his actions, it's that very competency that gives credence to the doubt. IT WORKS. Yes he's competent, but he's military. Can we really trust him? pam pam paaam......Here he just cries about his dead boyfriend for the entirety of the game. Since Isaac is now a voiced protagonist, a lot of Hammond's decisions are given to Isaac. This sort of makes Isaac more competent, but it castrates Hammond. So when doubt is cast upon Hammond's intention... it's like: "Who? The whinny little crabby who hasn't done anything except moan about his boyfriend?" Which of course makes the person throwing shade Hammond's way IMMEDIATELY the bad guy. Which of course, that person is. Now i CAN go into every single character and how the remake just does them dirty. But that's not the point. The point is, that the story is just not as good as the original. It's the same beats, sure, but it fails miserably in the details, breaking the flow and the immersion. And this is why I don't recommend this. Play the original. Yes, it requires fixes to run on modern machines. Yes the remake is FAR superior mechanically. To the point, that i HATE how well it's done. (Well except the enemy AI) But you'll come out of the original understanding why it's a horror classic. You'll get out of the remake going "man that's a lot of woke ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but neat mechanics though. Wish they were in a better told story"Edit: I figured it out! this is a Live action Disney remake. Technically superior in every way. But soulless corporate fluff that ruins the original story by making you wonder if it was ever good in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of Dead Space's continued relevancy can be owed to its moody, atmospheric approach to horror that's full of little immersive details not seen in many other horror titles. The most innovative of these details has got to be the way gameplay and HUD elements are seamlessly woven together. Health and stasis charges are shown on the back of the protagonist Isaac's armor, and floating holograms for ammo, maps and inventory slots adhere Dead Space's gameplay systems perfectly to its in-game world. In addition, all the gameplay and cutscenes are woven together in a single unbroken camera shot, adding to this cohesive flow that fully immerses the player in the dark, brooding wreckage of the USG Ishimura.Sadly, the majority of the overall story arc isn't on par with the ingame atmosphere. Most of the characters feel generic, the dialogue is forgettable, and the main and side objectives all blend together into a soup of story-driven chores. Luckily, though, Dead Space is smart enough to tell most of its story through moment-to-moment gameplay rather than through cutscenes. It establishes its thick horror atmosphere by simply letting the player explore and find the bloody aftermath of the horrifying Necromorphs lurking in the shadows, with detailed visuals and clever sound design adding to the ominous mood. And what few cutscenes there are rarely take the player out of the driver's seat - as Isaac can still be controlled while watching his video-call hologram or witnessing a major event ingame, and I usually just tuned out the audio calls and logs that pop up from time to time.The combat is... absolutely brutal. Dead Space's unique combat system encourages the player to shoot or cut off Necromorphs' limbs to conserve ammo, giving the TPS combat a hack-and-slash-y feel with a variety of unique weapons that all feel specifically designed to rip these disgusting monsters apart. Also, time slowdown and telekinesis abilities play off the game's goofy physics and zero-gravity areas, and these features are also woven into simple but effective puzzles that add some variety to the combat/exploration loop.This remake is by no means a masterpiece, though, and most of the issues I have with it can be summed up in one word: uniformity. Even though Dead Space's core gameplay loop is fun, briskly paced and super immersive, the environments (and even characters) feel kinda... recycled. The metroidvania-esque map design is great in concept, but is unintuitive to navigate with all of the homogeneous metal hallways and darkly lit control rooms. They look great, fit the industrial theme well and are full of lots of little details that make exploration fun, but these areas are really hard to distinguish from each other after a while. There's even a "Locator" feature where you can press a button to show a line pointing you to the next objective, and I ended up pressing this constantly because I kept forgetting where I was. And like I said before, the characters (with a couple exceptions like Dr. Mercer) all blend together due to very predictable writing - and while there were some major plot twists that caught my attention near the end, the first two-thirds of this game's story felt very formulaic. I can only take so many dark metal hallways, flesh monsters, and generic scientists before my brain starts hurting from a lack of variety.Despite these issues, I still enjoyed Dead Space. There are a lot of amazing ideas here - such as the hack-and-slash-y shooting mechanics, the cohesive sense of immersion, the detailed visuals and sound design, and the space setting combined with zero-gravity physics. But there isn't enough variety in environments and story beats to keep Dead Space's gameplay loop from getting a little repetitive, and it would probably make for a more consistently exciting experience if the 12 hours of gameplay were whittled down to a 7-8 hour long title. As it is, though, Dead Space is still a really solid horror-shooter that's worth the time of anyone who's in the mood for slice-and-dicing some Necromorphs. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: The real horror of this game doesn't come from the monsters themselves, it comes from the looming threat they pose--they can show up out of nowhere at any time. It doesn't feel like a scary game at first, but once you have two monsters on you, you're low on health, and you're out of ammo, that's when the real horror kicks in. By limiting your resources, the game forces you to be very deliberate with how you go about killing each monster--a shot to the head is a shot wasted, you have to go for the limbs. I'm not a big fan of horror games that just make you go from one place to another, doing one task after another purely for the sake of it, and Dead Space is guilty of this, but it makes up for it with its eerie and beautifully designed environment. Some parts of the environment and weapons are a bit generic-scifi-ish, but that's very easily overlooked when everything is such eye candy. The best way I can describe this game is that it's kind of like Doom, but in Doom the monsters fear you, and in Dead Space you fear the monsters. That said, the game design of Dead Space doesn't inspire much more fear beyond the looming threat the monsters pose (at least so far, I haven't played through the whole game yet but I'm leaving this review because I've enjoyed what I've played so far), and even this threat is very easily overcome-able if you know what you're doing, for the most part. It's very rare to come by a part of this game that uses the medium of videogames to inspire horror in a way that something like a show or movie couldn't. The last thing I should mention is that if you're playing this on Linux with proton experimental, you'll experience some minor lag spikes throughout the game. It's still entirely playable, but you may freeze up once every twenty minutes or so. I recommend this game if you like scifi horror that's scary but not too scary.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I'd just like to say I haven't actually encountered any framerate or stuttering issues with this game. I don't want to say that because I didn't experience any, they don't exist, but that's just something to keep in mind.Anyways, after a medium playthrough and an Impossible + One Gun hybrid run, I can safely say this game rules. Dead Space 1 was already a beloved masterpiece, but this game takes that and makes an overall net improvement to the game. When the worst thing people have to say about the game is that Isaac looks like Adam Sandler now, that means there's not a lot bad about it!The gameplay and gunplay is great, the weapon balance is a lot better, node doors have been replaced with security clearance you level up over the course of the game, which I think just makes the overall game flow way better, and Isaac actually talking now RULES. He's such a cool character, and they still kept him restrained so he only ever talks during cutscenes/RIG videos or big moments in the gameplay. And when he does talk? He's just super cool, and has some genuinely badass one-liners. The fact that it's also  identifying issues, coming up with plans and strategies and being a character who's active and taking the initiative when it comes to repairing the ship makes a LOT more sense than being an emotionless, silent robot that's just following orders.The weapon rebalances are super nice, with every weapon now having very clear strengths and weaknesses but actually being worth using, my favorite being the Flamethrower due to its surprisingly high damage and effectiveness, and its unique weapon ability being able to create so much safe space for you. Really, I would like to talk a lot, but I feel I don't need to. This game is definitely a strong 9/10-10/10 range game for me, and I'd heavily recommend it to people looking to get into the series and those that have played the OG a lot. Here's hoping the 2 remake is just as good, and they just scrap everything about 3 and make an entirely different 3 narratively and tone-wise so we can have a properly strong trilogy this time!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: If they can/have fixed all the tech issues from release, it's BRILLIANTI have a very special place for this game in my heart as my number 1 favourite horror game to date, so it means a lot to me that it got a remake especially since the base steam version in perma-bugged. This is hands down the game that has restored my faith for horror games coming this year, it has flaws but they're not really with the gameplay or the design of the campaign or the graphics, it's more technical stuff that unfortunately comes with a lot of releases in recent years, that granted can be fixed. The cons immediately i'd say is the performance, on release it had a LOT of bugs, a mix of stuff that ruins the atmosphere, and stuff that can stop your game in it's tracks by softlocking you. My game never crashed but it may as well have done, it would occaisionally go to black screen, 'load shaders' then throw me back in somewhere that i can't get out, i got thrown into the abyss with one white tile beneath me when as i walked into the leviathan room lmao. When trying to NG+ sometimes it wouldn't load anything and it would just go silent and i thought it was corrupted. There was one part in chapter 12 that nearly caused me to start the entire game again because the battery boxes wouldn't load in the room past the 2 guardians, fortunately i had a save, and there was a way to do it that meant touching absolutely no pickups and walking all the way there instead of running, which was dumb. apart from that it's just little things that don't break the game but ruin atmosphere in a game that HEAVILY relies on atmosphere, enemies that just pop into reality or spawn invisible and attack you then become visible, doors and rooms that still need to load as you approach them, just little things like that could be improved so that it feels like a smooth, immersive horror experience.THE PROS ARE SO COOL, the rework on weapons bar the pulse rifle are so good, new guns have different functions and secondary fires now that have new uses, the graphics help MASSIVELY with atmosphere since they did a brilliant job with lighting, the quality and look of people and surfaces is beautiful, the rework of stasis and kinesis in this game is perfect, it just overall feels smoother and more fun. The exploration is better and the world is one place now instead of individual levels and it has some replay value, not much but it's there and the fact that they've made enemies random as you work your way back keeps the tension high. Live gameplay animations was a nice touch, makes it feel like the world is still moving around you and your'e still part of it, doesn't take you out of it with cutscenes like most other games. Weapon upgrades need to be found now so you can unlock more of the node slots on your guns to stop you from becoming OP early, keeping the game interesting and forcing you to think carefully about your resources and options, and the fact that node doors have been removed from the world is great for this and means you don't have to hold onto them, keep upgrading whenever you can.This is a really well done and faithful remake to the best Dead Space game in the franchise and i'd happily put it at 8/10, if they fix the tech issues completely in the future to the point where they are barely noticable it would be a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Dead Space again after so many years feels so damn good. This is a proper remake, not one of those scams that simply brush the textures a little bit and call it a "remaster". This game is a completely redone Dead Space 1. It keeps the core aspect of the game intact but enhances the game in multiple ways.The story is mostly the same, you are Isaac Clarke, an engineer on his way to the Ishimura, a giant mining ship which suddenly went completely silent. You and your team are tasked to find out what happened and repair any potential damage. It is assumed that the comms system broke down but when you arrive you find out that there is something much more sinister at play. The crew of the ship is mostly dead and the corpses are turned into undead mutants, called Necromorphs. The only way to deal with those creatures is to tear them apart since even a badly damaged necromorph will hunt you down.The gameplay is almost the same as the original game, you walk around the ship and can have different weapons, starting with the plasma cutter. Weapons can deal damage to different body parts and eventually tear the limbs off, which does massive damage to the main HP of the enemy. Necromorphs are designed in a way that they have multiple limbs and depending on what you destroy, you might take their ability to attack, to walk or other stuff. Taking enough limbs from an enemy will kill it faster than just doing damage normally, so you have to aim carefully if you don't want to waste ammo. Killed enemies can be further destroyed by stomping on them, which will release additional loot but will also make sure that they don't just pretend to be dead (which they can do). New here is that the enemies are now designed in layers, you can peel skin, tissue, muscle and finally bone from them untl the limb finally snaps. This gives the already detailed amputation system much more depth and makes the game even more eerie to look at. This can happen to you too if you die, making death scenes quite disturbing. Weapons have been rebalanced, I found myself rarely using any other weapon than the standard Plasma Cutter, your starting weapon. The cutter was already so powerful and perfect to cut off limbs, other weapons felt so weak in comparison. In the remake they have buffed the weapons, so now everything feels more viable, they also limited the amount of upgrades that you can put into a weapon at the beginning. You now need schematics to unlock more of the upgrade grid for a weapon so you won't max the Plasma Cutter before anything else.  You also don't have to buy the other weapons anymore int he shop, this time you get them while you progress through the game which encourages you even more to use them.They changed a bit of the story, overall it still is the same but Isaac is not silent anymore and takes part in conversations, comments on events that happen in the game and you have the feeling he is more part of the overall story instead of just being a silent stand-in for the player. This is more reminiscent of DS2 and 3 than the first one but it's not a bad change to be honest. Isaac was never a "Gordon Freeman" and that's okay. The game menu, as usual, is the RIG system, which is an immersive Ui that is a direct part of the game world itself. When opening the menu, ISaac simply activates a holographic display and browses his inventory or checks the map. You can also, just like before, place a hologrpahic line that helps you to find your next objective in the ship. This is a really helpful tool and I still cannot believe that no other game tried to recreate this concept. Whzile you can just follow straight the objective, you can and you should check other paths and rooms because they can contain additional loot, even if you have a high risk in finding more enemies.The combat is very solid, gunplay feels great. Each weapon has a primary and secondary firing mode and you can have 4 weapons equipped and switch between them on the go. Additionally you have stasis and kinesis, two extra modules that are similiar to "spells" in fantasy games. Stasis slows enemies down to a crawl, which makes it easy to hit them or to evade an attack, kinesis allows you to pick up objects or even dead bodies and throw them around. This can be used to solve puzzles but also to jurt enemies. Kinesis is much stronger than it was in the original game, which makes this a welcome change.And of course, the atmosphere of the game is fantastic. Seeing the game in modern graphics adds much more to the scare factor. The lighting is briliant, the new sound system makes you much more paranoid. There is nothing more unnerving like walking down a dark hallway with nothing but the shine of your flashlight while you hear some sounds int he distance. And suddenly a necromorph jumps out right behind you. The game does know how it can get you and I love it.If you are looking for a great survival horror game, look no furthe, this is as good as it can get. And since Dead Space got a remake, there is now a good chance that we can get one for DS 2 and 3 as well, we might even finally get DS4 if we are lucky. I'm glad they decided to revive the series and I'm even more happy that this isn't the usual cash grab that you normally see in this business, especially since EA is the publisher.

_childDocuments_.review: EA takes a leaf out of Capcom's book with the remake of , because not only is this is a remake done right, it's a hugely enjoyable experience from start to finish that enhances the property in all the right areas. This 2023 remake honours the source game in all aspects, even ironing out the original games rough edges and expanding nicely upon the games lore so purists of the original should fret not.  now looks and sounds terrific by modern day gaming standards (just listening to the ship creak and groan is enough to induce pant-soiling in those first few hours without the demonic howls of the creatures on board that will eventually pummel towards you), but they have taken core concepts and game mechanics from the original and modernised them for the better making playing this version of the game far more enjoyable to play.  Now not only do a handful of the mining weapons you encounter offer actual usefulness to the player, each and every tool is useful in this remake and if upgraded correctly can provide a devastating attack that works to the players advantage. I also like how they have integrated the weapons into the game now having the player find them dotted around the ship rather than purchasing them from a store. It's a small change but it adds to the immersion factor greatly.Lore has also been expanded upon,  with new side quests and characters that delve into the motivations of key characters in the game giving it a lot more depth than the original. Many of the big boss fights, while still similar in nature to the original, have been tweaked and changed for the better making the grotesque encounters with them even more terrifying.One major change is the way the game handles zero gravity, which to be honest was a bit messy in the original game. I don’t think the technology was quite there for it when the original made its debut as I generally found these sections in the original frustrating to move through. With this remake they are exhilarating sections to navigate through (one can quickly lose their bearings if not paying attention which will often have fatal consequences for the player) and I regularly found myself drawing deep breaths just like Isaac himself while moving through these sections. I can't stress enough how good they are now. These sections are like chalk and cheese when comparing them to the original.  Another major change is that the main protagonist now also has a voice, but thankfully he only speaks when spoken too so unlike other third person adventures you don't have to listen to the character natter away to themselves constantly (aka Nathan Drake or Aloy) which is an annoying feature in most modern games today. My only gripes is that the game can't sustain the tension of the first few hours due to its lengthy running time so the scares and frights eventually give way to some slight annoyance, especially since the game likes to continuously throw you into rooms with increasing number of Necromorphs. Also enemy variety is a bit limited.  From around the four/five hours mark the player would have encountered almost all varieties of enemies the game throws at you so the surprise factor diminishes somewhat, especially given that the player becomes more of a force to be reckoned with as  the game progresses and you upgrade your weapons.Performance is good for the most part but there are traversal stutters (movement between two different areas) that slightly hamper the game performance. In my eyes these are small gripes though because when eveything is said and done, Motive have provided gamer's with an outstanding single player experience from top to bottom that I can't recommend enough. I am comfortable EA hand over the license to Motive now because they have proven they clearly understand the assignment.Bring on the remake of the second game!

_childDocuments_.review: Played on:AMD Ryzen 9 5900XSapphire Toxic 6900XTX Extreme Edition (driver 22.11.2)32 GB 3600 MHz RAMWindows 10 Pro (v. 22H2, build 19045.2546)A very solid remake. It looks and plays great for the most part. I played w/ all graphics settings set as high as they would go at 1440p w/ AMD FSR 2.0 set to Quality and RTAO enabled. I got 100+ FPS for the majority of the experience. The frame rate was pegged at my monitor's max refresh rate of 165 until I enabled RTAO. It took me a little over 20 hours to complete my first run. I am the sort to do all side quests and explore every nook and cranny, so the game could certainly be completed quicker. There is a NG+ that contains new monsters and secrets and an alternate ending.The only technical issues I encountered were a couple instances in which button prompts would stay on the screen even after I had completed them. The game also hung on close a couple times. All I had to do was alt+tab out and close it from Steam. Nothing major. One knock I have against the gameplay is the backtracking. There is a fair amount of backtracking. This can be a bit tedious, but it isn't too bad. You get a good amount of loot out of it, so it's worth it. The issue I really have with the backtracking is how difficult it can be to find your way. The map isn't always helpful and areas can be laid out in a confusing manner. A way point system would have been nice. Overall, a very good game. I am pleased with my purchase, and I look forward to continuing on w/ NG+.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very, very and very good remake. I actually can't believe EA published it, a solid 10 point to this remake from me.Edit: This is not a remake, this is an art.Here's optimal graphic settings and fix for stutter;VRS - OFFAA - TAA (FSR is not recommended unless you have a very weak computer that can't reach 60 FPS)AA QUALITY - HIGHGRAPHICS QUALITY - CUSTOM LIGHT QUALITY - ULTRA (doesn't effect FPS)SHADOW QUALITY - HIGH (to gain extra FPS you can set it to medium but not recommended)REFLECTION QUALITY - MEDIUM (to avoid bad reflection quality use this setting at medium)VOLUMETRIC RESOLUTION - MEDIUM AMBIANT OCCLUSION - RTAO (to gain 15-20 FPS you can make this setting SSAO but not recommended)DEPTH OF FIELD QUALITY - HIGH (if you are experiencing too much FPS drop during cutscenes make this setting low)So after you set the graphic settings just close the game and go to your documents folder on your computer. Find "Dead Space (2023)" folder and open it, after that delete the cache folder inside. If you are using AMD card like me don't forget to clear the shader cache from adrenaline software too, that's all about it folks now just launch the game and enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok I will start by saying this is a great remake, and its not just a remake like how we have had something like Resident Evil remakes, no this is on a scale where it is a true no changes just updated fixed and improved with some added stuff remake.  I have to say this is great, I'm loving this.However, there is the matter that my computer can run loads of games at the best if not the highest graphics along with no lag and more.  Yet from the start it takes forever to get from the loading and agreement to the stutter and lag of the start menu where even I'm setting the options to the best I can where it should run fine.  But it still gets lag a bit and when I try to stream on discord to show friends or even when I exit yes exit the game, it will freeze and I have to close the game then stop it running on steam.  That seems a bit off and makes me wonder if this was something that was missed or excused.  Really hope if anything this gets fixed.So pros and cons?PROSGraphics: They are great!  Love them and how detailed it got, you can see a clear difference from the original to this.Controls: Nothing different but easy mapping for what you want and how you want to play.Sound: Ok I will admit, I am not listening to the music in the game.  I have that all the way off but the other sounds they are maxed so I get the best feelings of dread and more.  To me music is great and I will probably turn it back on once I do new game plus but till then, this makes the game truly terrifying.Story: This is a great story and I will state all of them are.  Best chance you get watch the anime, read the books (I think there are books), and if you can play the other games even the rail shooter one.  This adds to the stories and bridges them.Bonus Content: Ok at first I was worried that the extra armor I got was not going to be something I can wear and upgrade since at first when I looked it up there was no info.  But I will just say this, if you get bonus armor its just skin over your current on.  Which means your armor still can be upgraded so when you due get new armor at the in game store, and I'm talking about the ones you buy to upgrade nothing like skins or such, it will shift back to normal armor but just reset it to the armor you want and your great.CONSGeneral Game issues starting and exiting: Said this before but it seems to be something I may not be the only one having problems with.  I did do the verify and even uninstall and reinstall but nothing changed.  I think this needs to get looked at asap or this may cause some to feel its not worth going through all that just to play and end a game.Info about weapons and how everything works: Ok I wish there was a stat set up some place to help you figure out the best weapons and options but there is none and that means whatever you throw into a weapon to upgrade your stuck with so get used to that and hope for the best.  It is not really a con just, you better do your research.And thats it!  Really I do not see any problems with the game other then do your homework on how the game is played and if your on the fence do yourself a favor and watch other people playing it.  Note this is rated M for a reason so be ready for blood, gore, and just all around styles of Event Horizon game play.  Really this game is out there and one of the best, I already know next to RE4 remake when it comes out the next VGAs will have this one and that one fighting on which game did the better remake if not horror.All in all take your time, do not rush this, and remember to read and listen to the files.  There are so much plot points in everything to help you.  Take your time and remember to back track to get everything.  Otherwise new game plus is where you will start our journey at getting things you need that you missed.Also, if your wondering if the bonus dlc for deluxe is worth it, um I have to say no.  It is just fun stuff to have but does not make the game any different unless you want fun armor styles.  Thats it, have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space Remake is a masterful reimagining of the 2008 classic, taking everything that made the original great and enhancing it for modern audiences. The atmospheric tension is palpable, with the haunting corridors of the USG Ishimura brought to life with stunning visuals and a deeply immersive sound design. The upgraded graphics, along with detailed textures and lighting effects, make every shadow and grotesque necromorph even more terrifying. The gameplay has been refined, maintaining the perfect blend of action and survival horror, while the improved mechanics and voice acting breathe new life into the story. The game captures the essence of isolation and dread, making every encounter feel intense and unpredictable. Dead Space Remake is a must-play for both newcomers and fans of the original, delivering a terrifying, unforgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A very well polished remade. Though it is not flawless, but still excellent. 9.5/10-The story now has more depth to it. Also Issac finally has a voice, and that can be both pro and con. It's nice to know the protag has a voice, but he sounded too confident, like he has no fear, which took away some of the scariness. -Mechanic wise it's definitely a clear improvement from the OG, like going from DS1 to DS2.-The gore in this remake feels great. In the OG, the limbs snapped like twigs. Now they feel there is actual meat and blood on the enemies.-The atmosphere of the game is still as great as DS always been, but took it up to another notch to fit in with the modern gaming standard. The lightings, the sounds were done so well.-I played hard mode and I barely feel scared. Sure they do more damage, but if they don't run or jump at me like in the OG, then that isn't really matter.-More guns is a nice thing. Though I see them almost pointless or a distraction. I barely use some of them because spreading power nodes among them all would be a waste. And also there are only 4 slots for guns, so can't carry all the guns with me.-Final boss is probably the easiest one I ever encountered, like... boring.Saying all that, it is still an excellent game, because it has always been excellent.Remake DS2 & DS3 pls. MAKE US WHOLE.Edit:After completing Impossible mode, I have extra notes about the game as a wholeThe puzzles are just right, and blended well with the action and story. No need for ridiculous amount of backtracking, or puzzles that are out of place.Focusing only on 4 weapons made the game much more enjoyable. It's nice to have guns fully upgraded by the end of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game in general doesn't run the best but when it's working it is an acceptable framerate, turning DLSS on however addresses the performance issues and makes the game run smooth though that shouldn't be an excuse to be lazy with optimisation. Traversal stutters however are another issue, they're baked into the game and there is no way around them, your mileage may vary but I cannot stress enough that you need an SSD to play this game, the developers weren't kidding with the minimum/recommended specs, with a HDD you're likely to experience severe traversal stutter.The game itself is as you'd expect, it's Dead Space, it's very faithful to the original with improvements that you would expect to see from the advancement in tech, the game design is still pretty old school like obvious enemy spawns, but if you were wanting to get into Dead Space or play it again, this is the definitive way to play.Also worth mentioning that the menus don't have mouse input, you need to use the keyboard to navigate the menus, who's the genius that thought this would be a good idea? It's not hard to navigate with the arrow keys by any means but it's a bit silly using the mouse isn't an option.If you do have any issues with the game don't expect patches however, there have been two small patches and the game is abandoned.

_childDocuments_.review: [EDIT --- 22nd December of 2023]I decided on giving the game another try now that it is included with EA play. The remake is kind of an in-between DS1 and DS2, which is in my opinion, after some careful thinking, completely passable.When I first played it, I felt like it strayed too far from the original, but that isn't all bad. Personally I wasn't a fan of DS2 as it was too fast paced and linear for me. It didn't have that same "hub" feeling as the Ishimura gave me in the 2008 original.I still think it could've done some things better. The pacing could be slower. I think the original built tension by letting sounds and atmosphere freak out the player more so than just the necromorphs lunging at you. That being said, the remake does plenty of things right that I simply couldn't see in the less than two hours of my first run of the game.I always want to know that my money isn't being just flushed down the drain - so when I buy a game for a high price I want to make sure I experience it in its entirety before I ask for a refund, or decide to keep it.2 hours is simply too little time to give a thorough review of something.I do however  think that some of the politically charged dialogues between characters and in text logs is completely unnecessary and it brings me to experience negative thoughts regarding the game. It simply didn't need these changes. Nor does any game for that matter, but I suppose it's the way of the world. We cannot change those who strive for progressiveness, since being progressive is now the trend. All we can do is accept and adapt, even if it doesn't sit quite right with me. Bottom-line: I do recommend this game now, although I still think the remake lacks some things that the original executed flawlessly and vice versa. Nevertheless, the original game was in dire need of some gameplay adjustments if a reboot would ever see the light of day. I think Motive managed quite well, although I have yet to play the entire thing, so I cannot say for sure. If you're still uncertain, or just really cheap like me, buy a month of EA play for $4 and play the game to its completion that way. No reason to spend more than the bare minimum if it's an option - even IF the game is a hit. Either way, I'm happy to announce that another attempt at playing this game definitely made me whole. ORIGINAL REVIEW:Most of the negative reviews on here is people complaining that the game runs bad, but they admit to in fact still liking the game when they CAN play it like they're supposed to be able to. I'm here to sell you on why the game is bad. Terrible, in fact. And why you'd be better off skipping this miserable excuse for a remake and simply going back and playing another run of the 2008 version.This is the take of a true Dead Space fan.                                                                           ******The animations in the remake are a joke. In the original game, Isaac's animations felt like he was an engineer who didn't know what he was doing while meleeing enemies for example. His amateurish close combat skills fit the character. The remake makes this melee much faster as if he's no longer in as much of a desperate situation as the game wants you to believe. He looks like he's been trained in close quarters combat which he hasn't.You could sense the weight of his engineering suit in the original as he was walking around, almost waddling from side to side - yes the controls were clunky - but this only increased the immersion. In the remake, Isaac moves faster. This is better for realism to some extent because realistically, if you were put in his shoes - you would also be running away from these monsters as fast as you could - but now the pacing of the game is ruined. If I can run away from my enemies every time, where has the horror gone? The desperation? On top of this the suit feels light. Almost like a plastic shell that Isaac only wears for the looks. He skips around from left to right without anything to slow him down. It feels bland and it feels like a massive downgrade.Sound and atmosphere are comparably much worse than the original DESPITE the multiple videos of Motive describing their carefully detailed sound re-design. (More on this can be heard and compared if you click on the link at the bottom of this review where I urge you to check out a rant by another disappointed player). Fake hype train lies to make people pre-order the game. And it seemed to have worked as well! Firing sounds are plain and non impactful. The plasma cutter sounds not unlike a leaf blower modified with a suppressor. It's real bad. People here are saying Motive improved Visceral Games' characters. I disagree; and not because I'm conservative scum who doesn't advocate for inclusion; characters are emotionless and void of character, which is very ironic. A relationship between two important characters has been replaced with empty vacuum because the voice actors fail to deliver believable dialogue. Adding a voice for Isaac might've seemed like a good choice for realism, but it adds nothing to the game whatsoever. His minor grunting and heavy breathing was oftentimes enough in the original - if not a better choice, because you felt more in tune with the protagonist since his muted voice lines left you feeling more immersed; as if you and Isaac were in fact the same person.The enemies are apparently terribly scripted and have no uniqueness to them. They all look the same, and the crawling animations for some of them are bugged into oblivion. Their screeching voice lines are also a downgrade and sound generic zombie-like.On the topic of Hud: picking up items are "laggy", almost as if in 20fps and it really puts me off. This might be considered nitpicking - but to me, even minute details count towards my judgement of the game. I simply can't get past the poorly implemented combat and the new animations that a lot of people seem to be praising. I played too little of the remake to get into the "layering" concept, but to me, the original's combat was standing fine on its own - it didn't need a do-over.There are numerous more things to mention, but I'm hoping this will be enough to make you at least consider not buying the game and instead going for the cheaper and superior original. (Or just have the patience to wait for a crack).I cannot see myself playing this because despite all the praises that this game is getting, it is far inferior to that of the original. Either the general consumers and fans of the genre have bought into the idea that improved graphics and progressiveness is the only thing that's needed in order to make a game great, or I just have too high of a standard when it comes to Dead Space. The original Dead Space, despite being a clone of Resident Evil 4, is an absolute masterpiece in the horror genre of games. It certainly did not need a remake this bad.                                                                   ******I have just one thing to say to the gaming industry: Why don't you just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ die already? Just give up and die.Need more persuasion? Take a look for yourself and decide afterwards:

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think that the original Dead Space needed to be remade. I thought it was perfectly fine, an amazing product of its time and also still amazing still to this day. My mind has not changed on that matter upon finishing this remake since I still think the original stands perfectly on its own and didn't need to be remade. However I cannot lie and say that the remake isn't a great game. In fact, it's actually insanely good, incredibly well made and polished.There isn't much that has changed from the original, but where changes were made, it was mostly for the better. The graphics, sound, enemy design, environmental design, the zero-G segments, the combat - basicly everything feels like it's state of the art, up to date and the game simply is a pleasure to play. HOWEVER. That's not to say that some changes weren't for the worse. Even though all of the voice acting has been re-recorded and Isaac has been given a voice like in Dead Space 2 and 3, all of the characters feel completely lifeless, emotionless, muted and overall just utterly fake when compared to the original's equivalents. Sure, I appreciated the way Hammond's story was handled and the way it ended was in my opinion even better than the original, but it doesn't feel nearly as impactful as in the original just because all the conversations felt fake.The combat had also undergone a huge change but here, the result was clearly for the better in every way. The original's combat feels like a point and click adventure in comparison to the new mechanics introduced in the remake. No longer do you just shoot at the limbs, now you have to take into consideration the individual layers necromorphs are made of. The creators describe it as a peeling system of sorts where you first have to expose the deeper layers of the necromorphs body/limb to then eventualy dismember it and it is so good, you wont believe me unless you try it for yourself. Thanks to this addition some previously garbage weapons were made incredibly useful such as the flamehrower,  however for some reason the plasma cutter still remains to be the most powerful and reliable weapon in the game. Also the upgrade system got remade for the better. No longer do you have to put power nodes into empty slots that do nothing, every upgrade feels like it makes you more powerful.As with any other remake or remaster it's quite hard to simply reccomend the game, even though it's clearly a more pleasant and up to date experience than the original (though admittedly worse in some aspects). The truth is, if you've played the original, aside from the secret ending, which doesn't really change anything all that much, there is nothing new that awaits you in this game. If you've never played the original I think it's a great way to get introduced to the Dead Space series and in that case it's an easy recommend. For some, experiencing dead space again in a fresh new coat of paint could be exactly what they want if they are big fans and want to reexperience their favourite game. In that case a recommendation is also warranted. But for most that have already played the original, I don't really think it's a great investment. Dead Space is a horror game and most of its appeal is lost upon finishing its first playthrough. You already know every section and the horror is simply no longer effective. If you don't mind, sure go ahead and buy it but don't be surprised when you'll feel like it's not nearly as scary or fun as the original. The truth is, you've most likely already had fun and there is only a little more to be had. Climbing the same hill can be fun even on repeat trips, it just tends to be nearly not as fun as or as impactful as it was the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: Too stingy on ammo:    After getting more guns, the game keeps giving me ammo for guns I don't use, like I've got tons of ammo for gravity gun and flamethrower but no ammo for plasma cutter and pulse rifle.     Poor autosave system:     I ran out of ammo after killing the hunter. Right after that I was dragged by a tentacle and I needed to shoot but I have no ammo, had no choice but to rewind to lose 15 minutes of progress.    In the room with nuclear warhead and two exploding necromorphs, I thought I must not kill necromorphs but slow them down with stasis. It happens I ran out of stasis so I flew back to ishimura and bought one pack then returned then died. When I got revived and went inside again, I discovered I had no stasis. If it wasn't for I found out you can kill exploding necromorphs without them exploding, I would fly back to ishimura again. REALLY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FRUSTRATING.     ♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss fight:    No idea how to dodge attack of the hive mind so I just kept running randomly. dying many times because I don't have more health packs.     Leviathan fight was equally ♥♥♥♥♥♥.    Didn't make the fact that you need to kill hunter with something else. In the second encounter it says "kill the hunter", so I thought I need to spend all my bullets on it but it turns out I need to kill it with engine fire? what?    Control:    When you are low on health and spam F key, it doesn't all register, annoying. When you want to freeze enemy with C while shooting, it usually doesn't work and I misused quite a few stasis packs due to this. I was spamming C key and then I let go of mouse2.    Looting is so bad. The animation is slow. You need to press two even three times to loot a box. And it usually misses for some reason. You just can't pick it up. There are many rooms in the game with 5 to 10 boxes to loot. It is so annoying that I just spam E key nonstop.   Puzzle:   The puzzle generally lacks hints. I can remember several times where there is a battery missing and I can't find one anywhere near.   The one where you reroute power in zero-g is horrible. I lose my bearing in zero-g and I need to get close to "the thing" to move it into place. Just horrible experience.   Pathfinding:   Press X to show where to go is great since I get lost all the time. The path it shows is mostly good but sometimes confusing. This is not good experience. I hate open world games that reveal path with a keypress. It ruins the game, you only look at the line, not the world. In a linear experience, it is not that bad but I still prefer figuring out the way myself.    Performance Issue:     I am running this game on a Ryzen 5600 + RTX 4070ti rig at 2k ultra quality with dlss quality. Getting about 110fps on average. Not very optimized compared to re4 which I am getting 170fps almost all the time without dlss. In the last few chapters, my CPU refuse to boost higher and the framerate dips to about 80fps. Not too low but makes me sick because there is A LOT OF STUTTER, whose severity is between minor and gamebreaking. Luckily, it doens't stutter when I am shooting but almost exclusively when I am moving to another room, which you do all the time in the game.    Conclusion:    First few chapters are enjoyable and sometimes spooky but it drags on. At the end I just want to finish this game asap so much that I turned down difficulty for the hive mind boss fight. It is not easy for me to finish a game but not every game finish is good. I have a mixed feeling about this game. It is certainly not bad, but not as good as games I really like, for example, darks souls 3, elden ring and metro exodus either. Maybe I am just really picky and really bad at solving puzzles. I would reluctantly recommend this game since games I can finish is already rare.

_childDocuments_.review: First, a word of caution:If you do not have an SSD and instead use an HDD like I still do, you're going to encounter some weird bugs. None of them ruined my enjoyment of the game, and I was able to recognize that it wasn't really the game's fault, it was my hardware. You can absolutely still play from a hard drive and enjoy yourself, but be aware that you may encounter some problems.With that said, though, this is probably the single best remake of a game out there. It's not about what the game changes, but rather about what it doesn't. Most (I do mean most, some are a bit questionable) of the changes made were objectively correct, such as lifting the zero-g segments from future installments and giving Isaac speaking lines. Otherwise, the game is extremely faithful to the original, so much so that I felt like I was playing it again for the first time.The new definitive way to play Dead Space going forward, and a new gold standard for what a game remake should be. I didn't even intend to play New Game+ going in initially, but I had such a fantastic time playing through the first time that I genuinely want to keep going.

_childDocuments_.review: As you may have noticed, there are occasional negative reviews on this game citing bad performance, and I am one of those people. My current specs are as follows:Ryzen 5 5600XRX 6800 XT (16gb of VRAM)32gb of 3600mhz low latency RAM1TB NVME SSD Running at 1080pSo as you can see, I am meeting and sometimes exceeding the recommended requirements of this game, I've tried adjusting settings accordingly, and don't have any other programs open, made sure the drivers are installed correctly, etc you know the drill. Yet, I am getting persistent frame drops, and freezes, making it really frustrating to play since this is, ya know, a survival horror game where things jump out at you, and when the game freezes when a new sudden thing happens on screen it makes it difficult to react. I made the mistake of holding onto this game beyond the 2 week period that you are able to refund the game, which I get is a me problem, but I had hoped it was some sort of bug that they would eventually fix. Nearly 5 months later, I can't say I'm holding my breath anymore as the game still has these issues. I don't always buy games brand new, I'm not exactly a pre-order collectors edition type of guy, but I was excited for this and wanted to join in with everyone else in the community who were experiencing the game. While I'm glad everyone else enjoyed playing this game when it first came out with no issues, and I am able to see its a smaller group of people that has had these performance issues, however I so painfully wish that I didn't spend the money on this.I can't say everyone is going to have the same issues as I did, but I wouldn't take the risk if I were you.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Jason,I must admit, my dear slasher counterpart, that Dead Space has crawled its way into my cold, dark heart. As the embodiment of nightmares, I am no stranger to the macabre and the horrifying, but this interactive horror masterpiece has left me positively gleeful with sadistic delight.Dead Space is a testament to the sinister creativity that lurks within the darkest recesses of the human mind. From the moment I stepped foot onto the doomed USG Ishimura, I felt an electric surge of anticipation, relishing in the claustrophobic atmosphere and the palpable sense of impending doom. The game's expertly crafted narrative ensnares players in a web of cosmic horror, each step leading them closer to the brink of insanity.The attention to detail in Dead Space is exquisite, my dear Jason. The grotesque and visceral creature designs, with their twisted limbs and gnashing teeth, are a sight to behold. The meticulous dismemberment mechanics, allowing players to strategically sever limbs from these abominations, is a stroke of genius, catering to our shared penchant for bloody carnage. The haunting sound design further amplifies the sense of dread, every creak and whisper conspiring to send shivers down one's spine.Ah, the gameplay, my dear silent friend, is a symphony of terror. The strategic dissection of necromorphs with the Plasma Cutter, the harrowing encounters in zero-gravity environments, and the heart-pounding moments of desperate survival against overwhelming odds all weave together to create a chillingly addictive experience. The scarcity of resources adds an extra layer of tension, as each decision must be calculated and every shot fired counts.But it is the psychological horror that truly sets Dead Space apart, my hockey-masked comrade. The relentless whispers of madness, the hallucinations that taunt the protagonist's fragile sanity, and the eerie silence broken only by the distant scuttling of necromorphs serve to burrow deep into the player's subconscious. The game expertly manipulates fears and phobias, leaving players in a perpetual state of anxiety and unease.my dear Jason, Dead Space is a morbid masterpiece, a sinister symphony that dances upon the jagged edges of terror and madness. It indulges our shared appetite for horror and offers a chilling reminder of the boundless possibilities of interactive nightmares. I implore you, my hockey-masked friend, to embrace the horrors of Dead Space, for it embodies the very essence of our eternal existence—feeding on fear, reveling in darkness, and etching nightmares into the hearts of all who dare to play.With wicked glee,Freddy Krueger

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space ReviewIntroduction:Dead Space is a landmark survival horror game that plunges players into the eerie and hostile environment of a derelict spaceship. Originally released in 2008, it remains a classic in the genre due to its gripping narrative, intense gameplay, and exceptional atmosphere.Gameplay:Dead Space excels in delivering a balanced mix of combat, exploration, and puzzle-solving. The game's structure masterfully alternates between periods of intense, dark, and scary encounters and moments of strategic exploration. Players are constantly on edge, scavenging for resources and utilizing their abilities to survive. The introduction of zero-gravity areas, where players can use a jet pack, adds a refreshing twist to the gameplay mechanics, keeping the experience dynamic and engaging.Story:The narrative continues to push players in the direction of discovery, unraveling the mysteries of the main ship. The plot thickens as we uncover details about the experiments taking place, adding layers of intrigue and unfinished business right from the start. This sense of ongoing discovery keeps players invested in the storyline and eager to uncover the ship's dark secrets.Graphics and Audio:While the graphics remain beautiful, the initial visual awe has somewhat diminished over time. However, the game's sound design and music continue to impress, particularly when playing with headphones. The audio experience is exceptional, with realistic sounds of outer space and a haunting score that amplifies the tension and immersion. Atmosphere and Immersion:Dead Space excels in world-building, creating an atmosphere that is both terrifying and immersive. The use of sound and visual elements effectively enhances the sense of dread and tension. Playing with headphones significantly heightens the immersion, making every creak and whisper feel real and immediate. The game keeps players on the edge of their seats, delivering a truly engrossing experience.Conclusion:After 19 hours of gameplay, Dead Space stands out as a masterpiece of the survival horror genre. The game's pace, combining puzzles and shooting parts, is expertly balanced, keeping players engaged throughout. The end game lived up to expectations, providing a satisfying and thrilling conclusion to the harrowing journey. Despite the graphics losing some of their initial impact, the exceptional sound design and immersive atmosphere make up for it. Overall, Dead Space is a must-play for fans of horror games, delivering a memorable and spine-chilling adventure. I would rate this game a solid 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: +  A perfectly captured version of Dead Space that does nothing but improve upon the original. The addition of lore from the sequels and comics, the carefully selected changes in story - any and all changes from the original Dead Space feels purposeful and fitting. The atmosphere of the Ishimura is still very much intact, with new scares and unexpected changes here or there to keep you on your toes.+  No overly complicated 'melee system', no bizarre animation canceling combo system. Dead Space's combat is just as smooth and purposeful as it was years ago - stomping and melee, responsive guns with alternate fire modes, a focus on gunplay that makes you feel competent but vulnerable. +  I recall the gore system in the original being some of the best gore in the industry at the time. This was a quality that the remake took seriously, and it SHOWS: the force gun shredding all skin off of a Necromorph, leaving a shambling mess of muscle and blood. Shots actually revealing bone and sinew underneath each hole. It's incredibly detailed in a way befitting a cosmic horror game where parasite aliens repurpose your body into abominations.+  I didn't even know that the original Dead Space had lackluster no gravity content, until I played this game's take on these segments. Full body control in zero-g with access to all of your weapons turns all of the segments from the first game, which were annoying and predictable by comparison, into stand out sections of the game that add to the horror.+  Best weapon change ever, a significant upgrade from the past game. The SOUND on this thing is so strong.+  My first playthrough, which involved me attempting to go for everything and anything I can, earned me a 12 H runtime. The game features harder difficulties and a NG+ mode with additional enemy types and unique rewards and weapons, meaning that anyone seriously addicted to the Dead Space formula could easily get far more runtime out of the game.+  Far more fleshed out as a character with his own voice lines! Personally, I think it's a positive change, since it never made sense to me that Isaac didn't want to talk at least a little bit, and it fits into the story of Dead Space 2.+  Several of the unique upgrades do crazy changes to the guns - for example, the plasma cutter 'knockdown' blades. They feel fantastic to use!+  Replaced with a far superior clearance level system, giving you much more comfort in upgrading your weapons and armor.-  I had one or two crashes that set me back some time on progress, where the game jumped to the Ishimura's loading screen and I didn't have an autosave nearby.-  The only thing I can think of that was significantly worse in the remake. Just felt... lame.I honestly don't have much to say bad about this remake. It is perfect - it takes the flawless atmosphere and gameplay of the original Dead Space and dials up the graphical fidelity and meat of the experience up to 11. It carefully improves where it can while leaving alone what was already perfect. And, in the face of lackluster spiritual successors that have come out recently, it shows exactly what made the original so timeless.If you loved Dead Space 1, buy this - it is basically the best way to play it.If you like Survival Horror, buy this - Dead Space has, I think, the most intense atmosphere out of any game in the genre I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I have to preface this by saying: I never played the first Dead Space, or any of the sequels. Likewise, I don't usually play horror games, though I have enjoyed games with horror elements (such as the Half Life series, or Halo's flood levels). Because I wasn't sure if I'd be able to handle it alone, I streamed this game to my friends while playing it, so we could all be spooked collectively.With that said... This is one of the best games I've ever played. I thoroughly enjoyed every second of it, and wish I could scrub my brain of the experience just so I could play it again with fresh eyes.The thing that initially drew me to this franchise was the combat; I had seen short clips of people playing this game, as well as the original several years ago, and always found the concept of the rotating plasma cutter and dismemberment really fun. And after playing through the game, I can confirm that the combat is  fun. The atmosphere and story are both wonderful, but the combat really completes the whole package in a way that solidifies this game's unique identity. The controls are clunky at first, which helps increase tension and fear early on, but by the end of the game you'll feel like a master of Isaac's numerous weaponized power tools. And the combination of dismemberment, enemy variety, and weapon selection keeps each encounter feeling fresh and fun without getting repetitive.The atmosphere is also phenomenal, as is the storytelling. Again, I've never played the original, but supposedly Isaac is a silent protagonist in the OG Dead Space. With that in mind, I have to say that the Isaac we see in this game is a  improvement. Isaac's characterization was one of the driving forces that kept me committed to the journey, as his realistic and relatable responses (varying from frightened, to pissed off, and eventually to exhausted) made him feel notably more human than the necromorphs he's forced to face. This goes a long way in making the story really hit home when it comes at you with its biggest twists, which it certainly is waiting to shock you with even if you think otherwise.Additionally, the game is absolutely beautiful, in both wonderful and horrifying ways. The lighting and setpieces do fantastic work to really sell the entire experience of being stuck on a massive derelict ghost ship, and the designs of the various locations on the ship actually offer unique and recognizable differences, so each chapter of the game is able to have its own identity.The game is certainly scary, though not horrifically so. If you're brand new to horror themes altogether, or have a strong sensitivity to gore, this game will definitely scare you more than it scared me, but overall it's more concerned with putting you in tense situations than it is with outright terrifying you. I don't mind this, as the experience overall was just the right amount of scary, tense, and fun, but it might fall short for veterans of the horror genre who are looking specifically for intense scares.My only complaints are that the bosses are underwhelming both in terms of fear and difficulty, and that there is one cutscene about three quarters of the way through the game that suffered a major, almost game-breaking bug that ruined an otherwise serious story moment. Essentially, only Isaac appeared in the cutscene, with none of the other actors or sounds showing up, and the monsters spawned post-cutscene were also missing. If you encounter this issue, there are several fixes on the forums to try out: the one that worked for me was deleting the game's shader cache to force it to rebuild them, and also going up on the elevator before going down.But apart from those two complaints, this was a phenomenal game, and I absolutely recommend you pick it up if you're looking for a fun, spooky game.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Dead Space was one of my favorite games of all time, and even though this remake wasn't entirely necessary, it's the new definitive way to experience this game, for fans and newcomers of the series alike. The story is generally the same, but with an extra emphasis on character development and dialogue. It takes nothing away from the story, instead making it even more cinematic. In my opinion it fits in with the trilogy even better because of this. Levels are very similar, but with some tweaked gameplay, especially with the zero gravity, the game feels better than ever. On top of that, enemy encounters are different as well. I played the original so many times that I remembered certain encounters and scares. For that to be changed in this remake kept me on my toes and honestly nervous and scared at times. This was the new experience I was looking for in this remake. And of course the visuals are phenomenal, though I did experience a lot of stuttering, especially during the cutscene transitions. So if anyone has any fixes feel free to hit me up. Otherwise I'll do some research on my own. But really, Dead Space is back on top of the survival horror charts. Hopefully this leads to a potential sequel, or a Dead Space 2 remake! 9/10
