_childDocuments_.review: Or Dead Space is a remake of the classic Dead Space from 2008. Dead Space is a third person shooter.You play as Isaac Clarke. Your girlfriend is a doctor aboard the USG Ishimura, a position you advised her to take. You are an engineer and are headed out to repair the Ishimura. When you arrive on station the damage is much worse than you thought. On your way in the auto docking system crashes your ship.The graphics are greatly improved, but the controls seem worse that the original. I last played the original about three years ago, but don't recall so much accidental resource use. I believe this is in part because Dead Space 2023 is also playable on a console. Some items require you to be aiming, others require that you not be aiming. This also happens when you are in Zero G, space. You need to collect oxygen using the E key, the same key that is used to rotate you.You can't jump. I could make a reason why you can jump, like your boots hold you on the deck. But, when you're running in the dark you frequently get stuck because of something on the ground that you can't see because you're either busy running or gunning to stay alive.Saves are at save stations. There are also auto saves, normally before a fight where you are very likely to die a few times until you figure out what you need to do in the fight.There are a lot of jump scares, initially causing you to waste ammo. Ammo and healing are very limited. I tended to use a specific weapon until I ran low on ammo and then switched to one with plenty of ammo, rinse and repeat. Some mobs are best dealt with a specific weapon. You'll notice when you enter an area that you tend to keep getting ammo for a specific weapon, that's your clue that is probably the weapon you want to be using. There are a variety of weapons and you can upgrade them. You can select up to four weapons to fit your combat style. Most of the weapons have a secondary fire function that is a more powerful attack and uses more ammo.The story is very dark, mental health issues, suicide, murder, hallucinations, and much more. This isn't a story for the faint of heart.I had a few times where the game wouldn't close out when I exited and one crash when I was trying to load a saved game. Most of these occurred after hours of game play.A graphically improved version of Dead Space, but the controls seem a little clunkier than the original. There are some fights where you will die multiple times until you figure out what you need to do.CPU: AMD Ryzen™ 9 7950X3DMotherboard: Gigabyte X670E AORUS EXTREME (rev. 1x)RAM: G.SKILL Trident Z5 Neo Series (AMD Expo) DDR5 RAM 64GB (2x32GB)Video: ASUS TUF Gaming GeForce RTX 4080Or

_childDocuments_.review: While they mostly took care to make sure their changes were relatively consistent with the overall franchise, I was extremely disappointed with many of them. Isaac didn't need more lines- he's experiencing the shock and stress of encountering alien life; that alien life wears the flayed corpses of humans, and  he's not a combatant. The dude was rightfully in shock, and you felt that as the player in the original. The way Hammond went out in the remake was super lame and made the brutes feel like 'just another' murderous necromorph. In the original, I had emotional investment in killing the brutes after he died. The ambiguity of how Isaac progressed in the original wasn't a 'plot hole' in the strictest sense. It had many potential explanations ranging from Nicole being a Necromorph the marker used to help Isaac progress, to telekenesis manipulation. It provided mystery and theory crafting opportunity; the remake expects me to believe that highly trained personnel brought a mentally and emotionally compromised engineer to a rescue operation while perpetually omitting the stone cold fact that Nicole was dead, rolling the dice that he continuously wouldn't watch the rest of the video at any point. And I'll absolutely be that guy- Nicole looks too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ old. Yes yes, shallow gamer and whatever other nonsense. I'm not the one dating her and I don't care about her resume, she's a visual eye sore. You know it, I know it, everybody knows it. So is Isaac, but at least he wears a helmet most of the time. They don't look like they're within a decade of each other. It astounds me the mental gymnastics so many people are performing to justify this. We can headcanon the idea that all that stress literally added 25 years to her face and  not Isaac's, but we can't headcanon how Isaac got through a two-person path without having to retcon and fully change the ending?I fell in love with the original for everything it was, not what it wasn't or what it could be. Visually the game is stunning, but frankly I expect nothing less for a game like this under the EA budget.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of Dead Space, and specially the first Dead Space, i'm extremely happy to say that this is a very good remake! In short, it's the version you should play, if you are new to the series or think about it. As someone who spent way too many hours on the original, i have some issues, but they are really just nitpicks. The ship is a great haunted house and the biggest fear i had was that the game was going to be too dark. Not because it's scary, but because its annoying. I can't see and it makes me angry and miss a lot! But the lightning is pretty much spot on, not too dark, but enough for the atmosphere. The whole game looks amazing, which is another thing why i would hate if it was black dark. There's some areas that are extra dark, but that's fine. The lightning effects, fire, shadows and smoke/gas/fog look really good, and i didn't run into many issues. Once Isaac got stuck on the floor, and couldn't even turn. When i aimed, his hand just went through his chest. Small potatoes. Compared to the original, this game has a lot of talking. But not so much that it would be disturbing. Sometimes i was wishing that everyone would shut the heck up, while i was trying to shoot things, but it was only like once. After a bit of a shock and after learning that Isaac's face is the voice actors, who is the same guy who voiced him in Dead Space 2 and 3, i was okay with it. Both him speaking and having a new face. Same with Nicole and all of the cast. I'm okay with the story changes too. With Isaac now speaking, the dialogue has been altered slightly, same with some specific lines. Important stuff is there, a lot of the dialogue is word for word and new stuff fits the story. The sounds are good, just the volume is weirdly low and some sound effects seem to be missing that final oomph. Same with music, a lot of it is straight from the original, and it works.Isaac's new Engineering Suit looks very good, on all levels! At first, i thought it looked a bit too bulky and weird, which is funny to say considering what it is. But after getting level 2 suit, i was turned around. I love it, the lightning makes it look very nice and i'm not tired of looking at it even after 20+ hours. The game overall looks very nice and runs well too. The game ran fine, except for the last boss where the FPS dropped to 20-30 (From my usual 80-90). At least on intel and nvidia hardware, the game runs well!One of the only nitpicks i have is the weapons and the map. The weapons feel a bit off, like the original had way more punch and power in them. I need to take a lot more shots, even with upgraded cutter, and assault rifle has the same issue. But the new contact beam is great! The weapon effects also are either really good (Contact Beam) or really bad (Plasma Cutter, Assault Rifle) but firing the Force Gun from close distance is always a treat! Another issue is balance, at least for me. I didn't get enough ammo and had to spend credits to buy plasma and assault ammo, and still use contact beam and force gun a lot. Maybe i was playing the game wrong, but i feel like i got boat load of 100 credit item drops from enemies, lockers and chests. Those should be patched completely out and replaced with ammo. And then there's the map, my kinda biggest small complaint. The map is good and works, don't get me wrong. But i was expecting to get a Dead Space style 3D map. Kinda like in Dead Space. But heck, maybe we get that in the sequel. At least we have a map, backtracking, side quests and lot of surprises for a veteran like me.  The new open Ishimura is not like coming home, but more like someone built your home out of photographs, but did a real good job. It's close to the original, almost every area is there and then some. But it's a bit different. Again, that's just a nitpick, that's all i have, because in the end, i love this game too. I can't sit here and say i didn't enjoy every minute and i'm going to be playing it again and again. I'm so happy this remake turned out this good!

_childDocuments_.review: Constantly spawning enemies right behind the player to keep them surrounded is BAD GAME DESIGN.  If an enemy can only be beaten with a certain weapon(s), then force that weapon(s) into the player's hands when they fight it, otherwise a player will have to go into their inventory and equip it manually-- which is not possible in every encounter.That said... This was a damn good game. I am happy to say they not only kept the base plot intact, but actually cleared up a couple plot holes and REALLY improved the characters. The atmosphere is tense, and survival is the main goal, not killing everything. This is a very well-done Survival Horror game.I was tremendously disappointed with the original game's sequels. I hope that if these new devs try to remake them as well, they will redesign them from the ground up (Seriously, Dead Space 2 wasn't scary and 3 was a travesty).And remember: Good horror stories MUST have happy endings, if not bittersweet ones. Otherwise the story isn't a suspenseful ride, its a slow buildup to disappointment. No one will want to see a sequel to a story that doesn't have a good ending; they already know how it will end.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure, my playtime is inflated because I left the game idling for like a day on accident. That being said, I will probably eventually actually reach 56 hours of playtime, because I think this is one of the finest survival horror games out there. More in the vein of the 2002 Resident Evil remake than the recent RE2-4 remakes, this takes everything great about the original, fixes some of the issues the original had, and layers on great new stuff on top to make a game I think newcomers and veterans will be exceptionally pleased with. The newly expanded and interconnected Ishimura feels more like a real place than ever, and the Intensity Director does a great job of making every step you take through its corridors tense, even when backtracking. Every weapon has been refined to feel powerful and satisfying, both on their own and because of the new necromorph gore system, which not only makes combat much more visceral but also really helps weapons like the Force Gun and Flamethrower shine. I have few, if any, complaints with the game, such as some minor visual glitches and the large boss sequences having framerate issues (though this may be a problem specific to my rig), none of which I think should deter you from playing this game. It's on the same level as the aforementioned Resident Evil 1 remake, taking what was already golden material and refining and expanding it to allow it to be its best self. Don't miss out on this.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Dead Space by Visceral set a very high bar for what is to be achieved in the framework of whats possible. Dead Space 1 was a masterpiece (ofc only my subjective opinion) and I admit, I was quite sceptical but also hopeful when I heard of the "reboot" announcement.After now some 6 hours and halfway into the game I think I can somewhat judge what I saw so far and what is to come. If anything changes in the later chapters I will ofc edit my review if I see necessary.1. the atmosphere of the first Dead Space has been kept and in some ways even enhanced. The addition of mechanics like the intensity director gives the game a whole new environmental feel. Nailed it.2. The graphics from 2008 look quite dated by now and I am happy to see that the remake has been very faithful to the overall texture design and enhanced it as well to look more modern but also more worn. The new graphics are very neat most times and stunning in some point. 3. Gameplay has been already rather exceptional with the birth of the Dead Space series due to the strategic dismemberment. The Remake improved with the peel system/mechanic an already quite solid system. It also balanced out weapon power quite well because ngl the og Plasma Cutter with full upgrades almost one shots every necromorph. Now I at least need 2. Also the new upgrade paths gate you a bit from over-investing into one weapon/system head on which adds so more interesting progression and also again balances things out a little.4. The story of Dead Space was never exceptional. Fun concept of weirdo artefact go brrrr and cause zombie apocalypse. With the addition of more voice actors and Gunner Wright now completely voicing Isaac the whole game feels more alive (and dead) however sometimes I referred the more silent sections. Also there were some minor changes to story progression which are no problem imo because they tie more into how the characters would act, instead of Isaac being the mindless "Yes Sir, I will do that" guy.For me personally this is a worthy successor to the original and in some ways it is even better (e.g. gameplay). If you liked the OG Dead Space 1, well you will probably like this one. Play on Hard for a nice challenge tho.If you are new: Strap in and fasten your seat belts because you are in for a ride.Always keep in mind what I am saying is in the end only the babbling of a guy who wished to see this game succeed and is happy to go back to one of the adventures of his childhood. Thank you for reading :)EDIT: I had some minor performance issues which I so far could not trace to any hardware component. Likely there are some things that are not optimised perfectly but overall the performance is fine. I had one sever frame drop which fixed itself on the fly.My System:CPU: Ryzen 7 2700XGPU: Asus TUF RTX 3070ti 8GBRAM: 16 GB Corsair Vengeance 3200MHzSSD: Samsung Evo 970 Plus 1TBMB: Asus ROG B450 F V2EDIT 2: When terrain loads in (like after opening a door or elevator) there are some more stutters later on in the game. Nothing to write home about but a lil nuisance none the less. Hope there will be a fix for that. Original evaluation does not change, still a blast to play.Final Edit: *Disclaimer* this includes spoilers:Overall I loved it. The graphical fidelity and the atmospheric pressure on the player are phenomenal. I encountered more performance issues like lag spikes to the end which did not coincide with any of my hardware spiking so I assume it is still a software related issue or rather optimising issue. The end was mostly like I remember it although I must say the bait and switch at the end got me off guard. I stick to what I said at the start: Highly recommend it.As for the performance issues, I hope they will be addressed in future updates and I also hope a better protection software than Denuvo (although I do not know if that is rumors or not) will be used.Anyways I love the original dead space! There is no doubt about it. I have very fond memories of DS1 when I played it as a 15 year old boy. the remake gave me this feeling back. Exploring the known unknown. It gives me back the difficulty of the first playthrough. The remake is how I remember the original to be. Not better nor worse but the same game in a new age. With more nuances and improved gameplay which made me feel like that 15 year old boy again. And for this experience im truely thankful to Motive Studios for giving us this absolute gem.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remake of the 2008 original game of the same name. This review will assume you've either played the original or are unbothered by minor mechanical and story spoilers. - Improved visuals - Issac now has a voice, the character did not speak at all in the first game. Dead Space 2 was when he got a voice.- The limb system is improved, flesh will tear off the bone before more force is required to maim a necromorph.- Upgrades are slightly different, arguably improved- Some of the puzzles are different, for instance that horrible sequence where the ADS cannons are offline in the original is dramatically improved.On the following specs I was able to run the game at the high preset at 1440p around 50-90FPS. However, I ended up enabling V-sync to lock it at 60 because the fluctuation became too much.Ryzen 5 5600XRTX307032GB DDR4 @ 3600MhzIn addition to the visuals, the game does a much better job at conveying what is actually going on while still being vaguely mysterious. Of course this is difficult to achieve having played the other two games numerous times.The one improvement I wished was in the remake is the ability to alter what the locator is looking for. Such that you're able to find benches, stores or save stations easier.There are other differences as well such as needing security clearance to open certain lockers or storage units. You won't miss them, it's part of the story. Previously, you would have needed to use a power node to open [optional] doors. A resource used otherwise to upgrade weapons or your suit. Kind of like using a shiv in the Last of Us to open doors.This is a great remake, if it doesn't inspire Dead Space 2 and 3 to also get remade I hope at the very least in reignites interest in the franchise and Dead Space 4 gets made.There are many people that describe this series as “Survival Horror”. And they also say that Dead Space 3 specifically strays from this path becoming an “action” game. Well, I've got news for those people, Dead Space was always an action game — just set with a horror aesthetic and theme. What I believe people intend on conveying when they say “survival horror” is that there is resource scarcity that requires management that makes combat more difficult. Which is not untrue of Dead Space, but on the medium difficulty there's nearly no place where you won't have health packs or ammo. In my understanding, the term “survival” — at least in regards to genre tags — implies there is something akin to tending to needs like hunger, thirst, sleep, etc. But for whatever reason, the survival part of “survival horror” seems to only be used in the more traditional sense. The sense where you are trying to not die. Which can be applied to a considerably large number of games. In any case, I consider the Dead Space series, or games like Resident Evil 4 and older to be action games set in a horror theme. The original 3 Resident Evil games, not the remakes, are what I truly think of when the term Survival Horror is used — 'tank' controls, inability to aim precisely and fixed cameras. But that's just my two cents.

I loved the selection of guns and the upgrade system for them, although I'm glad I played Dead Space on easy mode because I found the combat challenging. At points I had very little ammo. The anti gravity puzzles were fun, whilst providing a decent amount of challenge and variety to gameplay. The story is alright, it's not super original but it's decent enough, and a lot more background is told through text logs and audio logs for those interested in details.I absolutely recommended for sci-fi horror fans, especially if you didn't get to play the original like me! _childDocuments_.review: I'd say this game falls under the gold standard of what a remake should do: feels very much like the original but with gameplay tweaks that improve quality of life, refined story where needed, some familiar puzzles with new ones added in, new gameplay elements that expand on the original, and of course graphical improvements. Although a few gripes: On rare occasions a plain necromorph will ambush you but not be drawn until it hits you or takes damage itself (incredibly annoying when it does happen, but again it is a seldom bug that quickly fixes itself and never resulted in a death for me). Also baffling is that the complex cutscenes worked perfectly well... but one particular cutscene safely behind glass had two NPC's chatting with each other and only one loaded in somehow and never corrected in future playthroughs for me. Very happily platinumed this game in ~40 hours and loved what they did with it.

_childDocuments_.review: After the initial "performance fixes" I've beaten this game multiple times. Had around a 50-80 fps experience with no crashes. It's a great game that stays very faithful to the original game while also still managing to be fresh and keep you on your toes. Problem is, those "performance fixes" only partially fixed the problem. The game still suffers from immense stuttering, fps drops, horrible screen tears if you have v-sync off, and now with the newest driver updates, CONSTANT crashes. The solutions I've seen from the community have temporary fixes such as deleting your cache in the game files, and although it does help, it doesn't fix the issue (at least not for me). After around 30 min of game time it still hard crashes. One crash made me restart my whole computer. The fact that the devs and EA haven't offered an update or comment to address these issues yet is honestly baffling and quite frankly worrying if they want this game to stand the test of time like the original did. If it weren't for the performance issues this would be a damn near perfect game. However, as long as these issues persist, I can't in good conscience recommend this game to ANYONE with a Mid-Tier PC build or lower. I'm on an RTX 4080 with 32GB and I still get stuttering and frame drops when going to a new area of the map. Until then, it'll just stay as yet another reminder as to why EA and anything affiliated with them is terrible in one form or another.Update : the Driver Latest updates have apparently fixed the crashing for most players. However, there are still players in the community who still have issues with regular crashes or fps drops. Until EA/ Motive themselves come up with an update or fix, I will still keep my negative review for this game due to the horrible communication or lack thereof from the people who made the game. They took their money and ran, and until they themselves update it, my points in my review still stand. Don't get me wrong, it's a great game but the stability really needs to be worked on.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space was a masterpiece when it was released in 2008, and somehow feels even more so remade in 2023, when engrossing singleplayer horror story games are so rare. It threads the needle by doing something original, meaningful, and memorable, while giving appropriate nods to the properties that inspired it. Sixteen years later, much of that quality still shines though, though the inevitability of progress has ground some of the luster off of this title and made the offering feel more limited than it once did....an incredible journey back to the golden age of survival horror. Though limited and not entirely ageless, it presents something that holds up despite the time that has passed, and is absolutely a sojourn worth taking for fans of the genre. The greatest tragedy of this remake is that it didn’t sell enough to justify a remake of its sequel, which is largely regarded as the strongest entry of the trilogy. Even knowing the story ends here, I highly recommend picking up a copy and taking this wild trip to the infested halls of the Ishimura whether it’s your first time or not.Full review:

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely faithful and imaginative remake that adapts every part of the 2008 classic. This is great news for a majority of sections of the game, and only rarely did I wish they chose to cut a piece out instead of bringing it back. Overall, the game has been improved in every way possible.-The Environments of the Ishimura look fantastic with all of the new graphical power we have in 2023-The story is greatly enhanced, and now that Isaac has his voice(Gunner Wright is great as in DS 2 and DS3) all of the characters and interactions are way more fleshed out. The story is much easier to follow, with a lot of the niche details in the original becoming key story points in this remake, it was a joy to re-experience, and it feels fresh enough to keep even returning players very interested.-Side content and exploration is a welcome expansion to the previously linear Ishimura. Instead of the trams functioning as gates between chapters, they are now a fast-travel system to connect the now fully explorable . This is important, as new Side Missions and Upgradable clearance levels make this backtracking rewarding, with resources, upgrades, and juicy story details. I won't spoil the missions in full detail, but one of them is a line of missions that follow Nicole during the outbreak on the Ishimura, and another has you craft a special access keycard to open locked rooms. There's even a secret side mission only accessible in NG+ which leads to a new secret ending.-Gameplay has been enhanced as well, with a lot of gameplay improvements from later in the franchise making their way back to the remake and fit right in. Things like flying around in zero-g, and instakill kinesis objects feel like they were there all along, and slight changes like making the weapon and rig upgrades not have any filler nodes, every weapon having special upgrades that must be found in the world, and weapons being found organically instead of being bought increases weapon diversity a ton, and it just plays so naturally, and is such a great progression from the original.Overall, its a fantastic package, that is definitely worth repeat playthoughs and achievement hunting. This, in my opinion, is the definitive way to experince Isaac Clarkes journey into the USG Ishimura, and I cannot give it enough praise. Dead Space is back!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a spectacular remake of an already good game.  The best features include atmospheric touches that make you feel like you're on board a dilapidated space station where there's danger around every turn, and terrific pacing that makes you feel like you need to play for another 30 minutes just to see what's going to happen next.The pacing, in fact, is the best feature since it ties in so well to the story.  It always feels like there is a big reveal coming up (and there usually is), and that there is an imminent danger that has to be overcome (and there always is).  You never feel like you're slogging through anything no matter how many hordes of undead you have to wade through to get to the next destination.Combat feels good as the game emphasizes taking your enemies apart literally limb from limb.  The game gives you a ton of very different weapons and provides strong incentives for you to use them and not get stuck using just one weapon.Finally, although the game is categorized as "space horror", and it is creepy and atmospheric, it's not outright terrifying.  More importantly, it doesn't (usually) rely on jump scares or other cheap tricks to keep the player scared.  Instead, it uses background sounds, lighting effects, and story hooks to immerse you and keep you feeling uneasy every step of the way.Negatives:  By about the sixth chapter you've seen all the enemies that there are to see, so the combat does get a little repetitive, especially toward the end of the game when it feels like you're just having more enemies thrown at you instead of having different types of encounters.  Relatedly, although the game does a pretty good job of autosaving, there were a few times that I was frustrated by having to play too much content over again after a death.  Oh, and one of the achievements gives away a plot point.  That was frustrating.Finally, I experienced a few minor bugs related to opening and closing the game, but I saw very few issues while playing.  I think the game is in a very stable place for an initial release.I typically don't like FPS games, and I don't like horror games, but this one was done with such expertise that I can't help but be very impressed with it.  It gets particularly high marks for its atmosphere and pacing, though almost all its features are executed well.  This was a 92/100 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Scary, fun, action-packed and damn well-made -- Dead Space (2023) is everything you wanted from a Dead Space remake... and more! This review will focus on the additions Motive have added to the original experience... and spoiler-alert: They're awesome.1. Side MissionsThe addition of side missions adds a whole new dimension to the USG Ishimura. Whereas before you had to watch animated films like Downfall, or read licensed comics / wiki pages... Now you can get a window into the side of the story you DON'T see. The side missions don't detract from the main game, and notably, they don't decanonize or mess with the story of the original, they ADD rather than take away.2. Awesome SkinsThe addition of extra suits is cool. 'Nuff said. They're cool looking and let you experience some of the scariest moments of the 2008 original with a nice new coat of paint over Isaac. Or, deer antlers... if that's what you're into...3. The SECRET EndingThe best part about this secret ending, added in by the Team Motive, is the fact that it blatantly sets up a remake of the sequel, arguably one of the best horror games of its era... if you've ever played Dead Space 2, this fact alone should be enough for you to purchase the game and support the developersClosing thoughts;Dead Space (2023) is a painstakingly faithful remake of the 2008 original, and if there's any development team I trust with the future of the Dead Space franchise... it's MOTIVE. From side missions, to secret endings, and cool-looking suits, MOTIVE have shown their ability in adding to the original experience, and also somehow keeping the integrity and horror of the masterful original intact.BUY THIS GAME.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dead Space remake is the biggest surprise of 2023. Seriously, who expected a project of this level from EA? And they suddenly got a beautiful Sci-Fi horror. Dead Space in its kind back in 2008 was unique. Sci-Fi horrors don't come out often. And here is a remake that is not only made on a par with the original, but also surpasses it in many points. Dead Space is a wonderful horror, excellent technical condition and optimization. One of the best examples of the use of modern technologies of volumetric light and fog in games. Good optimization. An additional ending that is more logically suitable for the game for the plot connection with the sequel. Not long duration, open seamless location of the entire ship. As an independent game, Dead Space does not reach 10/10. But as a remake, before and what a miracle came out of EA - 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: UpdateSo after around 25 hours of play time, I've finished the remake. Excellent, excellent re-imagining of a game that I adored as a teenager. I really can't overstate how pleased I am with how Motive handled this project. I mentioned in my original review that the opening moments of the game showed a deep understanding and appreciation for the OG Dead Space. Having played through the entire game and sought out every collectible, I can confidently say that that opinion stands. This game has a level of care and attention to detail that just makes me happy. The updates and ways Motive expanded on the core experience (side missions, additional weapon upgrades paths, reworked enemy encounters and bosses) really made the game feel fresh again, but did not feel contrived or tacked on. I especially want to praise the visual overhaul, the game looks magnificent. On that same note, the sound design is phenomenal. The people who worked on the environmental sound are real cheeky bastards. Hissing steam, grinding engines, malfunctioning doors, shattering vents, all of it sounds so visceral and angry. You will have heart attacks while just walking around, even in the absence of combat. It's evil, but works so well to keep the experience tense and unnerving. Great stuff!Overall a magnificent game. I'm a winning streak recently, went from the great indie gems Hidden Deep and Subnautica to this. I think I need to play something happier now though, I am very tired.Original thoughts are posted below for posterity:Dead Space was the first game I can remember beating again and again and again immediately after my first playthrough. I was still in high school when that trailer dropped, and picked the game up on release. I LOVE that title. I'm only an hour in so far and it's apparent that the team who worked on this remake also loved DS1. The attention to detail, dialogue and scenario parity, and world building are excellent. _childDocuments_.review: Dead Space:2023 or "My face is tired" editionEverything about this game, is like watching someone defile a corpse while staring you straight in the face while they do it. We're not talking just a mild stare down, no, this is eye contact held for the entire duration until every hole has been thoroughly ruined and a few new holes have been made when those wore out. This is a flat downgrade in every way that matters.The weapons are objectively worse across the board.Animations are so bad that the Swarmers just didn't receive any. Evidently just porting over perfectly functional (and superior) animations weren't in the budget. All of it was spent mo-capping a slasher transformation. it definitely didn't go into the faces. Thousand yard stares for everyone!The sound design is so terrible that many sounds (especially important ones like enemy call outs) get drowned out by music, and environmental sound effects.The atmosphere is all but gone, replaced with a kind of amateur hour haunted house aesthetic. Which gets even stranger that the game is almost afraid to show any real gore or viscera. It's hidden in the darkness, both the Necromorphs and the environment are hidden in a nice obscuring fog and a sheet of oily blackness so we don't offend the censors with anything too shocking.Lighting? What lighting, we're going full Doom 3 levels of darkness because that's what scary is right? Bumping into things in the dark is what's hip with all the streamer kiddies these days.I hope you like credits, because that's what 70% of all drops are going to be. The game will even be generous and tip you the lowest amount possible, 100, as often as possible.And the story? Well the invalids at Motive have decided that in order to really understand just what is going on in this "introductory" experience into the series, you've read some novels, watched a few animated movies oh and have already played the games before. That's not even getting into the clearly mandatory diversity inclusions that have been oh so subtly sprinkled into everything.If there were any positives I could grant the game it's few and far between. Sure, the game now has improved graphical fidelity. Everything sure does look pretty, when I can actually SEE it. A 15 year old graphical bug on the PC port has now been fixed, huzzah. Anything the developers could imagine getting some visual effect has, some of them are even passable. The 3D map has been removed in favor of a 2D map that is only marginally less useless. They brought back the breadcrumbs system from Dead Space 2, then managed to make it worse, but hey points for effort I suppose. Gunner Wright is back, and also his back must surely be in pain after carrying the entire performance by himself.The short and narrow of it is this: this game is an objectively inferior recreation of a game that came out almost 15 years ago despite having a larger team working on it. A larger budget to produce it, an worst of all, the ground work had already been done by another, more competent team in the past.Sometimes, dead is better.

_childDocuments_.review: A superb game I for once enjoyed playing again for a bit because usually I'm not very attracted by remakes unless they could provide a decent new content.Callisto Protocol comparison for people who want honest point of view is quite simple:- Visuals & textures are incomparable. Callisto feels like a generic UE game while it's all the opposite for Dead Space. The textures are well-chosen, they are even organic like the ones you could have seen in the "Event Horizon" movie.- The game was not stuttering with RT that much compared to Callisto. In Callisto I had to tweak the UE settings on RT properly to get rid of the stutters. And it's not tied to AMD at all.- User interface is THE one in Dead Space. OK, I will be straight to the point here: it's an iconic one. Callisto tried to mimic it but failed badly, you can't even move around with it.- Progression is good in Dead Space and you are granted much-much more tools, armors, and weapons than in Callisto.- Each and any weapon in Dead Space is giving you a full tree to unlock and use it the way you want - and it's an enjoyment to progress through it.- Map design in Dead Space is much better and encourages exploration with a bit of new goals introduced by the remake.- Dead Space combat system is providing you a lot of ways to deal with enemies compared to Callisto BUT to be honest here, Callisto does offer something in the ways of melee combat and it's the ONLY good feature in "devenir" to me. A very good one at its base, it's something to scratch and it's probably the first iteration of a system that needs to be developed further for future games. The evade move is just what we need in nowadays games instead of that decades old roll.- Traversal system is way better in Dead Space with the ZERO-G suit jetpack. Callisto is about tunnel crawling with no interactions at all and that EVER OVERUSED sliding inside a tiny space in between two walls.- Callisto Protocol has pretty good animations, vaulting over crates, climbing down stairs and so on. Dead Space could maybe benefit on new ones not going away, however, from proper armor weight.- General content which seems to be several times longer than Callisto (to me it's like at least x2 times).To conclude: Dead Space is far superior to Callisto Protocol.The only drawback of Dead Space 2023? The price. Not corresponding at all to what it is (refunded for that reason). It should have been halved. And I do hope they will also do a remake of the second episode and above all a remake of the third one in CO-OP taking that into account.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an overall solid remake. If you liked the original, can just about guarantee you'll enjoy this. Just about everything you loved about the original is here, if not improved, especially the sound design, which was one of my favorite aspects of the original. Even if you know an enemy has spawned and is closing in, the startling music doesnt play until you are physically facing them. It still gets me multiple times and I love that they kept that feature. In addition to giving it a nice spitshine to bring it up to modern graphical standards, they actually did add a few new things as well. The dismemberment itself even seems more detailed in just how much each shot blasts away, the force gun actually straight up blasts their skin off. There were some minor changes to the story and characters, as well as the pacing of the story, but nothing glaring or that takes away from the game. They also let you respec your weapon upgrades. I can't remember for sure, but I don't recall being able to do that in the original. Weapons have all been re-tuned so they can all be useful. Yes the flamethrower actually isn't terrible anymore. Also the gave Issac actual dialogue in this version, where as the original he was almost completely silent. There were only two issues I had really. One is that while the game retains a lot of good features from the original, it actually inherited some of its graphical problems too. Ive noticed the same glitches with enemy limbs clipping through the floor and walls like the could in the original. You think they would have fixed that. The second one, and this is the big one for me, is that imo, remakes should never be full priced releases. Its a good remake, its well done, it looks beautiful. It is still however a remake of a near 15 year old game, and they want $60 for it? It's good, but it's not THAT good. I personally wouldn't recommend buying at full price, but if youre a diehard you'll likely still be happy with it. If you see it on sale, then it should be an instabuy.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's a really great remake that's faithful to the original but marred by a couple frankly unacceptable issues. The game does work out of the box for 21:9 wide screen, which is nice to see (looking at you, Elden Ring.)--First off, the frame rate is VERY inconsistent on my PC. I'm playing on an RTX 3070Ti, Ryzen 5 3600, and 16GB of 3600MHz RAM, with an SSD as storage, and while it usually hovers around 85-95 fps with settings at high and DLSS on Balanced, it very frequently dips into the 40s range. Twice in my playthrough, it has dropped to about 15-20 fps and stays there for a few minutes for no apparent reason. Changing settings even causes the frame rate to remain lowered for extended periods of time, so I'd put money on it being some kind of caching/memory issue that will likely be fixed up in the near future. (Anyone who knows more about these types of issues, I'd love to hear your thoughts, as I'm still a CS student myself and am curious what causes this exactly).--The UI did not consider PC AT ALL, despite the game being sold on Steam. That is, the UI for the inventory and workbench, among others, utilize the arrow keys to navigate, ENTER to accept, and ESC to go back, rather than simply using the mouse. I mean, it's 2023 and this frankly should be illegal on PC releases at this point.As for the gameplay itself, it's an otherwise fully modernized Dead Space 1 in all its glory, with some really nice tweaks and changes that clearly came from people with respect for the original. I'm an avid fan of the original and am usually a purist when it comes to remakes/remasters, and there's nothing so far that I wouldn't have changed. If the two issues above were to be fixed, I'd have no hesitation touting this as another example of a gold standard for remakes. If you haven't played the original, do yourself a favor and check it out now if you're curious. If you have, this is a great way to re-experience a classic.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely breathtaking remake of its predecessor, Dead Space 2023 once again follows the nightmarish events of an unknowing Maintenance Team responding to the distress call sent by the space fairing mining vessel U.S.G. Ishimura and the coinciding outbreak caused by their discovery of a monolith known as the Marker. Building off of the original iteration, Dead Space 2023 offers an all new experience and revised story, giving a voice and agency to the once silent protagonist Isaac Clarke and greatly developing many of its characters while offering a Metroidvania approach towards opening up and re-exploring the Ishimura with the usage of Security Clearance Levels and Side Missions that offer unique loot and all new areas to discover. The environments and graphical overhaul of the remake improve upon what was already absolute perfection 15 years prior, redefining the terror of the cold, dark and cramped steel corridors of the Ishimura crawling with strange and horrific monsters waiting to tear you apart when your guard is lowered. While Dead Space 2023 dramatically improved upon the many of the originals own shortcomings, there are still glaring issues that hampered the horror into near comedy. There were several points in the game which enemies and events failed to load in time, leading to invisible enemies rushing me, T-posing NPCs failing to load their death animation and cutscenes that fail to load any NPCs, leading to awkward one sided exchanges with Isaac talking to himself. I thoroughly enjoyed Dead Space 2023 and all of its replay value, and the amount of variety the remake brought to keep me guessing and on my toes. If you're looking for a genuinely terrifying game or need a nostalgia trip, I'd HIGHLY recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: You are sent as a rescue team to help a troubled mining ship, like it's another monday morning. But after setting foot on the USG Ishimura itself, you will soon realize that you too, will wish for a rescue.A classic survival-horror game that still hold up 15 years later. The Remake is definitely one of those modern remakes that don't smell the quickly done work; Graphics are cranked up to modern standard, but some entire areas have been remade. In both cases, old and new rooms will feel just like what you remembered, but in 2023. Isaac is much more relatable as he is talking now, a few dialogues have been updated following this upgrade.The instinctive and original gameplay has been preserved, with a small update given to the weapon upgrade systems, to match the more recent Dead Space 2.Thanks to modern computers, the Ishimura itself is now one giant level that you will explore, sometimes with back-track to precedent areas; some of them will be altered and every room you enter, wheter it is for the first or seventh time, will never feel safe.Necromorphs are an almost constant threat that will keep you on the edge of insanity.Sometimes it feels like a tabletop rpg where you can immerse yourself in the horror of the ship, exploring it the way you want, fighting the way you prefer with the monsters that roam the ship.9/10, superbe atmosphere to look at and play in, good gameplay and instant-classic narrative inspired by movies like Alien and The Thing.I removed one point because 60€ is a bit much for a game you've already played 15 years ago, even tho the amount of work put in it simply transpires.Better than Callisto Protocol

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 remakeThis remake has everything I remember from the original but better. Graphics are beautiful, especially space scenes. Isaac is a bit dramatic though... his noises are extra. I'm happy to see they brought back the store and bench. It has replay value; I would definitely play this again. _childDocuments_.review: This positive review makes me sad for my  review I wrote. On one hand, I really enjoyed revisiting the Dead Space universe with Isaac. It’s well polished (outside of some performance hiccups (which I am acknowledging but not condemning). Gun play is great as a reskinned  clone. On the other hand, I am praising a game that I absolutely sprinted through the first half- because I knew exactly what was going to happen and where it would happen, because of . The conundrum becomes, we as consumers are praising a remake, and voting with our wallet, we would rather play a retelling of a story we already know, than to acknowledge the hard work it takes to create an entirely new IP, doing new and DIFFERENT things in the genre. I really hope developers are not discouraged for trying new things with survival horror. Remaking a , with virtually the same look at and feel almost feels too soon. I’m sure people will be quick to point out the praise and success of the , however, there was much more time in between both games (21 years) which allowed for the vast difference in technology and console generations, and the remake radically changed the gameplay into a more modern feel. Dead Space (2008) and this game are virtually identical with the story beats.I gave a negative review, primarily because of some of the gameplay decisions, BUT, I was much more interested and invested in exploring the story of , then any slight deviation or side mission in Dead Space.  universe appeals to me a tad more, creatively. That being said, I loved Isaac Clark in the original trilogy, I was invested in where the story was going to go after the Awakening DLC, and I HOPE, EA uses this opportunity to use this game as a launching pad, to propel the story in a different direction. Pretend Dead Space 2 and 3 do not exist, and let’s see where you can take this character moving forward. But if you’ve played the first game, and recall the series of events even vaguely, you likely won’t be surprised by anything in the remake outside of some nice eye candy. (BTW, Callisto Protocol is a much better looking game for what it’s worth)

_childDocuments_.review: Why does this get a thumbs down from me?Well, I am a long time player of the House of the Dead series, it is literally a childhood classic for me, so when I saw this remake of the first game, I was excited about it. However, instead of bringing me joy, the game turned around and stuck a middle finger in my face and was horrible compared to the original. Sure, its got nicer graphics, but thats about all I am willing to say about this game that is good. Everything feels too beefy, especially on easy and normal mode, along with incredibly tight frames where enemies can just hit you and ruin your no-hit runs because they simply just got close to you out of camera frame which makes it impossible to shoot them until they just get a free hit off of you. Sometimes, an enemy will also hit you, even if you kill them before they finish their attack animation, which feels wrong. Somehow the original arcade cabinet wasnt *THAT* bad, y'know for being made in 1996. This game was made in 2022 using not only UNITY but a better coding engine, yet it has more bugs and flaws than a 1996 game. _childDocuments_.review: What the original does better:-fairness of mechanics. Even though the arcade version still has a bit of jank like getting jumped quickly, most of the enemies are actually pretty easy to kill as long as you understand how they work: shoot the weaker zombies in the head to kill them fast, shoot the stronger enemies in the arms to buy yourself time and expose the head. Some of the really tough and annoying enemies can be dealt with easily if you know how they work. The remake sort of does that, but it's less consistent in that sometimes you'll decapitate a zombie and they'll still be charging at you for one of your hitpoints.-An absolute banger of a soundtrack. The remake doesn't have the original soundtrack, let alone a remastered version of it, probably for copyright reasons. That's understandable and respectable, but if you've ever listened to Chapter 2's "revenge" for the original arcade version, you can understand why I don't want to settle for less.-Bullets actually do real damage. With the remake, it feels like you have to shoot incredibly fast at everything and  you won't get hit. This is especially apparent with certain moments where you can't start dealing damage to certain enemies until an animation is completed, and is even more so obvious with the last two bosses. A full playthrough in the remake is liable to make your trigger finger sore, if the arcade version didn't do that badly enough.-There will never be a situation where an enemy offscreen deals damage to you. This isn't the case with the remake, especially in horde mode. The remake also likes to center the camera to whatever monster you/the game wants to target, making aiming a little difficult at times. To my knowledge, the original doesn't have that.What the remake does better than the original:-you don't have to spend 500 hours learning about PC emulators and sacrifice your firstborn child to get the original House of the Dead running on your computer.

_childDocuments_.review: Me, in 2007: "Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles is pretty great, and probably the closest thing to a House of the Dead 1 remake we'll ever get."Me, in 2022: "The House of the Dead: Remake is pretty great, and probably the closest thing to a Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles remake we'll ever get."Life is wild sometimes. The House of the Dead was one of my favorite arcade games as a kid, one that also provided amusement in college when Typing of the Dead was one of the few games I had on my laptop. As of this writing, having beaten the game to see how faithful it is, I can safely say that it is  faithful, having closely recreated the original level design, enemy placement and event branching while updating the visuals with a modern polish that nevertheless adheres to the original art direction and atmosphere. Similar to the justly well regarded Resident Evil 2 remake, it gave me a sensation like I was seeing on-screen today what my adolescent imagination parsed from the blocky polygons of the late 90s. It also adds a lot of tasteful extra touches, like dramatic lighting in areas that were very flatly lit in the original, unique designs for all scientists that you save, enemies ragdoll on death in a satisfying way and can still be shot post-post-mortem, and so on. The visuals combine reverence for the source material with smart use of modern tech to make for a way better visual experience than I ever figured we'd see in an update for this game. Sound design is also pretty good, and the new voice acting even somehow manages to capture the same weird energy as the original without coming across as tongue-in-cheek or self-aware. I felt very satisfied with the presentation overall. The one minor nitpick that stood out was the use of 30fps video clips for things like the tutorial attract demo and the menu background, which originally confused and alarmed me on start up.As for gameplay, every zombie, scientist, item and branching path flag is exactly where it was in the original game, at least from what I could tell from my first playthrough. This degree of faithfulness did lend itself to feeling a bit easy on the default difficulty, so if you are a veteran of the original you might want to consider bumping it up if you want to break a sweat. I have yet to dive into the game's original modes, but seeing as my primary motivation for buying this was the hope for a faithful and good looking remake, and that's what I got, I felt comfortable making the recommendation even without having thoroughly weighed every hour of game time available. One minor change that I've seen lamented in a review or two is that the game dropped the original's "backtrack through the game" sequence during the credits, but I suspect that might be a technical thing as the remade levels might be too large and detailed to be easily snipped together in real-time, and I do not feel consternation about the developer's decision to spare us more 30fps recorded video in place of live gameplay.If you're a fan of the OG HOTD games, a fan of arcade rail shooters in general, or even someone who just likes zombies and/or spooky houses, I'd say you can definitely find $20 worth of entertainment here. If you desire a more modern style of game, maybe it's not for you, but the clearly advertised fact that it's a remake of a 90s arcade game should have informed your decision even before you reached the review section. If nothing else, buy this so we can get a House of the Dead 2 remake in a similar fashion and then I think I'm that much closer to checking off every item on my list of dream remakes of games from my childhood. I'd appreciate it.

_childDocuments_.review: The House of the Dead: Remake is a remake of the game of the same name, first released in 1996. It's a light gun, rail shooter game, the type you usually find at arcades. You cannot move the character besides shooting and reloading. You play as agents Thomas Rogan and/or his partner G, as they try to rescue fellow agent Sophie from the mansion of mad scientist Dr. Curien. The mansion is overrun with monstrous creatures, with different shapes and sizes. Some are weak and some others powerful, they serve as bosses.As a remake, this game is near-identical to the original. It's almost a 1:1 remake with better graphics. The original game is known for its corny lines, and this remake still retains that. At least the voice acting and quality is a bit better. The enemy placement and alternate pathways seem to be identical as well, or even if it’s not the change is minor. There are no new story moments, new levels, or anything. If you played with the original game, you will be very familiar with the levels and enemy placement.There are, however, some new features. Like you can play the campaign in Horde Mode, where a lot more zombies appear. But the most welcome change for me is the ability to switch weapons anytime. To unlock this, first you must complete the game saving all scientists, and its not that hard. Then secret chests with alternate weapons will start appearing in your next run. Some weapons are like a powerful crossbow for example, great for killing bosses. Or an assault rifle, for peppering whatever's in front of you with bullets. You don't have to keep using the basic pistol.Length-wise, this game is like what you'll expect, very short. You can finish it like under an hour. But if that's your only purpose, then I don't recommend buying this game, watch a playthrough instead. To fully enjoy it, I recommend trying out different weapons and pathways, as well as hunting for the achievements. Or when you're bored one evening and just want to shoot some zombies. Its not a multiple-hour-long zombie horror adventure like Resident Evil.There is a problem for this game at my end, where it would either blackscreen, freeze, or just downright crashes my computer at a load screen. Even a fresh reinstall didn't fix it. I managed to get it fixed by deleting all files named MegaPixel Studio SA at C: -> Users -> (your name) -> AppData -> LocalLow and verifying the game files. Then start the game and use the Exclusive Fullscreen mode at Options. It works perfectly for now, and I don't want to tamper with it anymore in fear of breaking it again. If you can analyze more, I'd love to hear about it.As someone who played the original game since I was a kid up until a few months ago, I'd definitely recommend The House of the Dead: Remake. Some people say it's nostalgia bait, as its almost the same game just with better graphics and some new features. And while that might be true, it's still worth a try, especially if you love achievement hunting. Go play the original games, and I do hope we get the others released for PC, and maybe some remade as well. Fans of zombie shooter games will definitely love the HotD franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a child, there were three games that pretty much any other kid you met was guaranteed to have played: Tekken 3, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, and The House of the Dead. While the latter did not have the staying power of the other two, particularly after the rail shooter genre died out, HOTD was very impactful in its time. Alongside Resident Evil, it revived zombies in the public imagination - going so far as to inspire the likes of George A. Romero. So when I heard the news that one of my most beloved childhood games was getting a remake, I was ecstatic.Until I watched some gameplay footage, anyway. But I believe watching a game and playing it are often two very different experiences, so here we are: I've finally played through House of the Dead Remake.It's a pile of crap. This has to be one of the worst remakes I've ever played. Given Sega's lack of interest in reanimating this old zombie, I feel like developer MegaPixel and publisher Forever Entertainment's main interests lay in wresting some nostalgia dollars from people who grew up playing the original, because this is clearly not an attempt to introduce a classic to a new generation of fans. There simply isn't enough effort put in. Gone are the iconic character designs, the vibrant and striking colour palette, the campy fun, the well-animated violence, the punchy sound effects and the incredible soundtrack.Instead, what we've got here is a washed-out blob of mediocrity. Everything is functional, and nothing more. The art design is hideous, with only the Hermit boss looking decent, and it's hard to even tell things apart. The fluid effects - blood, slime, water, lava - are distractingly bad and feel like they come from a pre-alpha version of the game. The guns sound like toys. They feel weak too, because the ragdoll physics are so limp compared to the hand-animated reactions of enemies in the 1996 game. I could go on and on.The original House of the Dead had a distinct corny charm born from its lack of self-awareness. House of the Dead Remake feels like it's trying to border on parody, but it doesn't even accomplish that. For whatever odd reason, the serious parts have been made more serious and the comic parts more comic, and the end result doesn't mesh well.The most heinous crime of all is the soundtrack. The original House of the Dead boasts some of the best arcade music in history. House of the Dead Remake's OST sounds like a YouTube musician making HOTD-inspired music, and you know how YouTube musicians are. Everything has been douched up with excessive synths and shred-metal wankery. No sense of proportion. I know, I know, Forever Entertainment didn't license the original's soundtrack and the composer's Twinkies were too soggy and bla bla bla. I also don't give a ♥♥♥♥; I have my own problems. This soundtrack isn't bad just compared to the original, it's bad by itself. It sounds like circus music, and strengthens my feeling that no one making this remake was interested in the cohesive whole as much as their own contribution.This is a very harsh assessment, but I feel MegaPixel's dev team were simply too immature. Talented people who are probably big fans of the original game, but have neither honed their craft nor learned about subtlety enough to have a project like this outsourced to them. The emojis in the loading screens contributed to this conclusion. [¬º-°]¬Playing House of the Dead Remake is like drinking a soda after it's gone flat. It wears the skin of the original, but lacks the heart. 'Soul vs soulless remake' is a bit of a meme, but I feel it really applies here. The original game managed to do more with technology 25 years in the past. Go play that.

_childDocuments_.review: I desperately want to recommend this game, I really do. I WANT to love it. I build arcades and my own light guns, so this game seemed like it was made for me, but I'm gobsmacked that it was released without a shred of light gun support. Even now, well over a year and a half after it's release, playing it on my arcade with my light gun (where it should really shine) is damn near impossible. Even after spending time trying to fine tune the mouse speed to be reasonably close to 1:1 with my gun movements, the game insists on moving my crosshair around for me every time I hit reload or continue. Every time it jumps, my gun's aim is now offset by a random amount. One moment my cursor will be slightly off my gun aim to the left, then it'll be 5 inches to the right, then it'll be stuck to the side of the screen. Please, just give me an option to use absolute mouse coordinates! There's also no multimouse support, so anybody with 2 guns like me is SOL. Honestly, I really wanted to like this game. It does so many things right, but it's impossible to play on proper hardware.

_childDocuments_.review: This remake does capture the feel of the OG pretty well. The game play is fun, rewarding quick reflexes and accuracy.Their are branching paths, different weapons to find, shootable items, secrets and in-game achievements. Would like to emphasise the game is good fun to play.( I have been a bit critical in some of my review) Graphics are good in 4k and run smoothly which is important. Using GSYNC and borderless window mode works a treat. This game does seem to push the PC pretty hard. Reading the comments that some are having crashes. I haven't had any stability issues which makes me think for those with stability issues overclocking may be the issue. This is the type of game that will push a system so if hardware isn't dialed in it may be a potential cause. Sound and music is ok. The audio quality is average. Nothing to write home about but serviceable.I do kinda feel that the audio lets the experience down a bit. The game has branching paths to find and three endings.  As the campaign is short, maybe 15-20 minutes give or take the replay ability comes from getting the unlockables, earning achievements, seeing the different endings etc. I think the campaign could be a bit bigger even with the branching paths. Either that or more game modes, maybe a survival game mode for example. As it is the content is limited.Something I think could be done better is how the combat feels and the general feedback when you shoot something. The combat is ok but I don't quite get the sense of holding a powerful firearm and doing serious damage with it. I'm not sure exactly what it is that feels a bit underwhelming. Also shootable items need to give more feedback when destroyed visually or with better sound effects or be more obvious or something I'm not sure. Shooting bonus items is a big part of the OG as is the branching paths. Making this feel rewarding is important.Overall the game comes recommended if you understand that it's designed for multiple play throughs to see all the endings, unlock all the weapons, earn all achievements etc. The shortness of the campaign, the lack of varied game modes as well as the 'not quite as satisfying combat as it could be' hold it back a little but it's still a good game and worth a recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: is a reimagining of the classic game with the same name from 1996. While we will never get a PC release of the original game due to  losing the code, this is possibly the best way for everyone to experience the game. Unless you emulate it, are lucky enough for your arcade to have it, or you can spend thousands of dollars to get a cabinet to go and play the game.I myself have never played the original but there was a cabinet that was at the arcade where I live. To this day, it’s one of the biggest regrets in my life for not experiencing the classic - I did watch a few lets plays on the game, however. One thing I should note is that while I do like some of the changes present in the remake, I do have a few issues with them that I will explain later on in the review.Also, this is the only  title in the mainline games to actually take place in a house rather than a city. has gone into insanity in his pursuit of life and death and unleashes biologically engineered creatures on his staff at the . Two days later, after getting a distress call from ,  decides to go to the creature-infested mansion. The story is rather simple and straightforward, nothing has changed from the 1996 version, and everything remains the same. There is nothing to really talk about in terms of story as it’s quite short, fitting for an arcade release. The cheesy voice acting is there, although while they are still good I am a bit more used to  and  voices from the original. is an on-rail shooter, you follow a straight path where you will have to shoot zombies and save scientists. Saving scientists will reward you with points and sometimes a health kit, be careful however, if shot, your health will go down by one tick. Your score will determine the ending you get after a run, with a total of three endings to get. At the end of each level, you will fight a boss, each having a weak point that the game will show you, with the exception of the final boss won't show you its weak point.There are a ton of collectibles for you to find throughout the levels that will help increase your score. If you save all of the scientists in a level, you can unlock a different weapon to use, however, you must find these weapons in the levels, which require you to replay the game. Although in my opinion, I go the classic route and only use the pistol to fight my way through the mansion.There is also a  mode that you can play which will increase the number of enemies that you will encounter. There are a few different difficulty options you can choose, such as playing the game on the original arcade difficulty.There are multiple paths that you can take throughout the game, these will have different enemies for you to face and different scientists for you to save. The story does not change when taking these different routes, but they have their own interesting ways of going through it all.The original  had one of the best soundtracks that I have heard in gaming history, and I was hoping to get something that was just as good and updated. However, that was not the case here. We got entirely new music for the levels that do make nods to the original in a few ways. Although I can’t fault the devs on this one with the little research I did, it turns out the reason the original soundtrack was not included appears to be unknown but I assume it was due to legal issues.My overall thoughts on the whole soundtrack are that it’s ok for the most part. It will never beat the original and I do wish that it was included but oh well.The  has a very beautiful aesthetic capturing the gothic horror theme very well. Although I should note that the game had a much better graphical feel in the arcade version than what we get here. This also applies to some of the enemy models that simply had better designs. With this said, the designs provided here do have charm and still look good. The game ran fine for me, but I did hear of some performance issues that others have experienced. I may have come across something when I recorded my video on it but I have yet to confirm this.I am not going to lie here, I had low exceptions on this remake, as the original did a great job at what it accomplished. However, I am glad that I am wrong, somewhat. While I do have a few issues with this remake, it’s not entirely the game's fault or even the dev team's. I do recommend buying this game but maybe wait for a sale. While the nostalgia factor is there, you only get about 30 mins of gameplay out of this title. To me, that’s not worth the asking price of 29.99 CDN, a 50% off sale would be perfect for the game to go and pick it up though.I have heard that the sequel The  will also be remastered as well and by the time of my writing, it’s apparently halfway done. I’ll definitely try that game out when it releases.If you want to see a look into how the game is played, then check out the video I made, note that there may be some performance issues from the game in my video.

_childDocuments_.review: The House of the Death: Remake is, as the name implies, a remake of Sega's classic on rails shooter.The graphics and gameplay have been overhauled.The game also features two-player local co-op, multiple endings, and a photo mode.Watch a snippet of gameplay here: In addition to improved graphics and performance, House of the Dead: Remake features new audio, updated controls, a horde mode, leaderboards, a photo mode, achievements, and a gallery.In addition, the remake can be started with 2 players via the local cooperative multiplayer as mentioned earlier.While there are four levels in total, each instance has several routes that in turn put other threats in the way, as long as you are aware of the various criteria. Some paths require shooting a specific element in a room, while another path only opens after you fail to eliminate an exact opponent. Walking these paths is not just for fun or variety, as route A, for example, contains a chance to score a higher number of points, while route B can offer something helpful such as a hidden medkit in a destructible barrel or crateThe game also works great on the Steam Deck: The enemies blow apart nicely and it really matters where you shoot.If you shoot at a hand or arm, you can really see it flying off in pieces, if you shoot in his stomach, you can really see the ribcage.Shoot him in the leg and he'll fall over. Those small details are nicely done and as a fan of the original game I can appreciate this.The story is a little bit different and the level bosses have also been given a new look.Unfortunately, some bosses have received a little less attention than the others, so you sometimes have a whole new enemy and sometimes recognize him one on one from the original, but I don't see anything wrong with that.

_childDocuments_.review: IMPORTANT NOTE: other users in the reviews have reported that this wouldn't load past the main menu. This also happened to me at first on its initial launch as well; after selecting my mode, only the audio was working; shutting it down via CTRL-ALT-DEL and re-starting the game fixed it. This is NOT the first time that's happened with a Steam game on its inaugural start-up, so I won't hold that against it and neither should you. In fact, having used Steam since 2004 (Half-Life 2's digital launch) across 3 very different systems, I recommend that for most games you should get your options configured, then exit-and-restart it, then actually begin playing. OK, on to why this gets the recommendation!I had this in my wishlist for a while but never bothered because the reviews were mixed and my rig is a decade old at this point and has a GPU that doesn't meet the minimum requirements. My system:CPU : Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4770 CPU @ 3.40GHzNVIDIA GeForce GTX 760 w/ VRAM of 1024 MBRAM: 16267 MbWindows 10 (64 bit)But today I got it in a Humble bundle, so why not fire it up instead of waiting for my next build? Well, I'm impressed  I'm giving it a thumbs-up for a few reasons:1) It's giving you exactly what it says it will. I played the original arcade HOTD to completion a few times back when it was a staple of the waning years of arcades, and even a quick amount of time with this revealed that it hits the beats like a good cover should. And since the original source code for HOTD is still lost at this point - as is the code for the original PC port it got from Sega in the late '90s - this remade version is the next best thing.2) It ran just fine after lowering the resolution from 1080 to 720, with all the graphic options turned to maximum. This old workhorse can't do 4k at 30 fps unless it's a sprite-based game, but after the initial launch hiccup this ran without issues. I didn't notice any frame-rate drops either until various parts of Stage 3, and even then it was perfectly playable. Can't ask for more than that. 3) The classic replay options get complimented with your modern trimmings: monster gallery, horde mode, credits system, achievements, stats, unlockables, controller vibration, positional surround sound (nothing like hearing an off-screen chainsaw rev up or a monster moan in your rear speakers!) and so on. HOTD was well-regarded for being an arcade rail shooter, a genre as linear as it gets, to also feature with branching paths and multiple endings, encouraging you even in single-player to spend more tokens on extra replays. This keeps it up.  4) Solid implementation of the controller option. I was born in late '82 and anyone who played light-gun games on an NES controller without the Zapper knows that always hindered the fun. The SNES and Genesis controllers weren't much better. D-pads and face buttons were just the way it was, and ports of coin-op games were...well, the only way to experience Operation Wolf and Terminator 2 etc. outside of an arcade. Thumbsticks, triggers, and sensitivity adjustments go a long way in improving things, and barring a VR port or mod, this is it. (I own the Wii and PS3 ports of HOTD 3&4 and Overkill, along with PS Move and a Sharp Shooter. I assure you, the controls here are fine and beat not having this game at all.) 5) IT'S FUN. Really, I spent enough time with the original cabinet to assure you that this is worthy and worthwhile in and of itself. For those who crave nostalgia and want the exact same low-poly experience from close to 30 years ago (!), nothing else will satisfy. For everybody else, this is just fine and worth the time.As for value? Well, whether or not you buy this at its regular price, you'll get better value for your money than you would have from loading however many tokens you put into the cabinet for a play-through! ;)

House of The Dead: Remake plays as a regular Shoot'em Up Arcade game, but has its own twists and turns.Play as the cringeworthy cringelord, Rogan, who's tasked with saving scientists from hordes of zombies... At first, not taking a hit for an entire campaign sounds quite harsh but then you unlock the Invincible Cheat Code and suddenly it becomes a walk in the park. You can also play alone, or tag along with your toxic friends that will inevitably break your heart. In Co-op mode, you can play competitively or cooperatively, the difference is that in the former, each player has a seperate score and in the latter, you've both got the same score... Competitive Co-Op mode is the best; it kind of familiarizes you with the heartbreak that's coming, without a doubt lolAll in all, it's an  4 hours tops to 100%, like every run of the campaign is 20 minutes long... It's short and sweet and really makes your phone calls that you conduct with one hand with your "toxic friends that you've got nothing in common with" less boring.
