_childDocuments_.review: It's best to set the record straight from the outset over the matter of who this game is NOT for: If are the kind of person that has never played or understood the appeal of traditional coin-op arcade machines and the gameplay associated with them, or if you are the kind of person that wants a game to keep you busy for very long before you reach the end, The House of the Dead: Remake is absolutely not for you. As the remake of an on rails shooter originally released for arcade machines, this is an incredibly short (around 30 minutes from start to finish), very difficult game, where part of the appeal and longevity is pushing yourself harder and harder on repeat playthroughs for better scores and cleaner runs. If you're a younger person or just never cared for arcades before, it's very likely this is the very first time you've heard of the concept of a game like this. If you're used to today's cinematic 60-hour epics, this is a far cry from that and thus might not appeal to you and that is perfectly fine. This aspect of arcade-y game design is mostly extinct, these days, save from niche circles.The Retro videogame craze does not seem to have ever truly felt the need to include the On-Rails Light Gun shooter genre. In spite all the buzz around 80s nostalgia got in the latter half of the 00s, 90s nostalgia throughout the 2010s and the 2000s nostalgia wave brewing up today, we have gotten less than a dozen new games in the genre in the last decade and a half, even less so that ever got officially ported to home platforms. The House of the Dead: Remake is one of the few brave games that dares venturing into this long forgotten genre of gaming's yesteryear in modern times, promising to revitalise one of the most important games released in the 90s.Exactly like the 1996 original, the only real control you have is aiming, shooting and reloading. Your character automatically moves from scene to scene as you clear the area of enemies. The game has a huge interconnected web of branching paths, where defeating certain enemies, rescuing (or failing to rescue) certain civilians, shooting certain parts of the scenery or getting pushed off ledges will send you back and forth between many different routes around the setting of the game. Enemies will always appear in the exact same spots and behave the exact same way every time, encouraging memorisation and anticipation of the enemies that await you. The creatures are surprisingly accurate to their positioning and tactics in the original game, so thankfully, your skills should mostly transfer over just fine. It's absoluytely not an exact match as the pace of the game is much faster than the original and the enemies spongier on average, but it did not personally take me very long to adapt. There are many ways to play the game, then, whether your focus is to explore the entire mansion and uncover all the paths to the end or trying to find your favourite route, either the easiest or the one that rewards you the most points.You are given a limited number of lives and credits to get to the end of the game. Health pickups are few and far between, hidden behind scenery props or awarded by some rescued civilians. If you run out of everything, the game still allows you to continue by sacrificing a big chunk of your score as long as you have any to spare. This is mostly there if your goal is just to casually get to the end.All of this effectively means gameplay is essentially intact when compared to the original game. Have you ever played House of the Dead 1 or 2 on PC in any capacity? Then this will pretty much feel identical to that. If you liked those games for the gameplay, I do not see why you would not enjoy this one too. If you really insist that the game must be played with a light gun, then there are many solutions for that nowadays, such as Wii Remotes + Dolphinbars, 4 point sensor guns or Sinden. One of the few real new additions are unlockable weapons and Horde mode. After your first playthrough, you unlock an Armoury and 4 guns will be hidden across the game's 4 Chapters. Find them and you unlock them for use right up. All 4 are comically overpowered in their own silly little way. The Crossbow is kind of weak against most enemies, but it can shred bosses in seconds, The Pitter is an incredibly goofy harpoon that mostly OHKO's enemies and sends them flying to the nearest wall, the Grenade Launcher blows up everything in its path and the Assault Rifle shreds through regular enemies with no aiming ability required. These weapons trivialise the game, but go hand in hand with Horde mode, where the enemies are multiplied tenfold and you will need every bit of firepower available so you don't take damage every 5 seconds. Horde mode is just goofy fun. It's really not a mode to be taken seriously at all, but if you like over the top action, you'll probably love playing Multiplayer in this mode.At least between the intervals where the game isn't chugging. There's frankly not much wrong with the actual gameplay of the game itself. It's a faithful recreation of the original game, but performance is all sorts of screwed up an easily the biggest dampener on the fun. Despite the Recommended Specs implying this is a GPU heavy game, I was far more CPU throttled throughout my time here, but this game will still drop out of 60FPS often. Depending your hardware and graphics settings, at least it will not go below 30 too often, but still, performance is floaty. Similarly bad are the loading times: If you do not install this game on an SSD, you WILL regret it. On first load, the game often takes damn near two minutes to start on a mechanical drive. The game stuttering or outright freezing for a second or two as it loads new areas mid-stage is also not uncommon. Perforomance wise, the game is thankfully not the horror show I hear the Switch version is, but this still could've been optimised a whole lot better. Thankfully, the game does have very good Ultrawide support and turning the graphics settings all the way down doesn't hurt the looks of it too badly while skyrocketing the consistency of performance. If anything, I find the excessive bloom of the game very ugly, so turn that off for a big performance increase.Speaking of graphics, the game looks solid, but, the art style and vibe of the game are completely different from the original. If you were a fan of the moody and somewhat sincere atmosphere and execution of the original, this has mostly been replaced by somewhat standard horror vibes, as the game is mostly trying to appeal to the "unintentional cheesyness" side of the original. For lack of better words, the parts people made fun of the original for and not the parts they celebrated. Due to licensing issues, not even the melodies of the original's soundtrack remain, which is certainly one of the most disappointing aspects of the remake. The new soundtrack isn't bad, but it really doesn't hold a candle to the iconic tunes of the original.I do overall recommend the game, though this is mostly me expecting the awful performance gets patched later and acknowledging that missing the original soundtrack is very disappointing. For the sake of transparency, it must be said that I have been credited in the game under "Special Thanks". Despite my best efforts to write an honest, critical review where I highlight what I liked and didn't like about the game and why I feel it would or wouldn't fit you, whether you believe that impacts my ability to reach a truly impartial conclusion is entirely up to you.

It's fun but I have problems regarding the PC port:Having played HoTD 3 and 4 along with Vampire Night on the PS2, it's safe to say I have had some time within this specific type of rail-shooters - overall this remake is enjoyable overall and I feel it's faithful enough to the previous games in the series I played. I cannot speak how it compares to the original as that is far before my time. The main issue I have is how iffy the hitboxes are. Compared to the Switch version that I also own, the PC port feels like it either doesn't register who I'm shooting, or in one case - it did the polar opposite and registeed me hitting 2 zombies when my cursor was no where near their bodies.Graphically speaking it's very good, with a decent amount of settings you can modify, however I got occasional dips that threw me off on numerous occasions, and it just freezing also happened once or twice during my last session. I heard from when I was streaming that a watcher with considerably more powerful hardware then I also suffered performance problems, which I personally find problematic.Audio is also good, and still keeps the iconic cheesy factor they're known for, and I like the music too as it had an upbeat tune to it. But once again I found that it would just freeze, particularly loading and it makes an ear-splitting noise! I realise that it can happen while loading, but other games just don't have sound when loading and freezes in past experience, which is an overall pleasant experience.I also want to note in a unrelated manor that this game is PLAGUED with typos and spelling errors - even the Achievements of all things have typos in them!So in conclusion, the HoTD remake is a fun game, but the aforementioned problems really mess with overall experience. The lack of Quality Control in the PC port makes it a tough to recommend at an asking price of £23 or your regional equivalent! _childDocuments_.review: STEAMDECK. Works perfectly fine on Steamdeck, right out of the box no tinkering, online functional. Runs at max settings.House of the Dead Remake is an odd game to figure out how to review and recommend to anyone who isn't already a fan of the genre. It's a remake of a game within a genre that's super niche, that doesn't do anything new with the genre and instead goes for 1:1 faithful remake of the OG.So i'll keep it simple and review it as follows.Are you a fan of the original House of the Dead? If yes than this game is definitely worth the purchase. Its the same exact game except with brand new graphics and audio. There is some new stuff like new difficulties(there's a new mode but really its just a difficulty increase) and weapons(that need to be unlocked first). The music has been replaced, the music isn't bad or good, just not as good as the original. If you're not planning to do multiple playthroughs, trying to rescue all the npcs and beat all the difficulties than at a cost of 24.99 I would say the game isn't worth it, buy it on sale most definitely. You can beat the game in under 2 hours on default settings. More so if you don't have a light gun to use, than you're not even playing it as best intended. But if you got the light gun and plan on milking every corner of the game, its def worth the full price as its both cheaper than the OG version by a long mile but also has more content.Not knowledgeable of House of the Dead but a fan of old school light gun on-rail shooters? Than this game is a easy and definite recommend, its one of the God fathers of on-rail light gun shooters. I'm not an enthusiast of the genre, so idk with what this game has to offer if its up to par with what you may expect from modern on-rail light gun shooters. So at its full price im not sure it is worth it for you or not, but I will say I am happy with the purchase but I also did buy it on a dirt cheap sale(80% off).Now not familiar with on-rail light gun shooters at all? I would say this is the type of game you buy to strictly enjoy with a friend, especially if you have the light guns or motion controls. Its a fast paced fun time, just shooting things ala Contra/Sunset Riders style albeit just from a first person perspective and where the game autoscrolls. As mentioned you can beat it quick, in under two hours. It's just a game to own to bust out along with Mario Party, Just Dance etc during get togethers, parties or game nights. But anyone who isn't a fan of the genre looking for a genuine solo experience isn't gonna find it here or worth it. Looking for a great coop experience? Also not worth it at full price due to length and content.There you go

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who had the unfortunate luck of playing the Switch port first, I can confidently say that this PC version is the definitive way to play. The game is a near 1:1 recreation of the original arcade game from Sega AM1 in 1996 - something I'm tremendously happy with. However, my gripes surrounding the game most notably includes the new soundtrack. You have likely already heard that it lacks the punch of the original game, or more specifically, the FEEL the original musicians were trying to convey. People have already put videos online of what the game would be like with the original soundtrack, and it's MUCH better. My other issue has to do with the pacing of the bosses, which feels ever so slightly off from the original (especially Hermit and Magician.) Other than that, this game is well worth the asking price if you're aware that as an arcade title, one play-through should last you about thirty minutes. It's also worth bringing up that a few people have asked me about how to unlock the other weapons in the game. It's a convoluted process, but if you remember how to unlock the Armory in the original, then you're half-way there. I feel that once you get the four other weapons, the gameplay widens significantly, but it's unfortunately too much effort to get for most players (especially those who are new to the game.) All and all, as a House of the Dead die-hard fan, I think that while this product could have been better in several regards, I'm ultimately happy with the product we got (But I REALLY hope that mods fill in the blanks.)

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll start this one off by saying that I have very little knowledge of the original Sega Saturn / arcade version of this game. The most experience I have with his series is blasting away zombies in  for my late, beloved Dreamcast. So, I can’t say what this remake gets right or wrong in comparison to the original.What I can tell you is that, to someone going into this one with no expectations whatsoever, it feels like they did a lot of things right. I had so much fun rampaging through the mansion that the few nitpicky things I could say about it almost didn’t register for me.In fact, since I played this about a month ago, I’m having a hard time thinking of anything that really rubbed me the wrong way. Umm… It’s super short? The bosses still feel like they’re meant to eat quarters, even though nobody even has quarters anymore? Controlling the game kinda sucks if you’re using a controller, so it might be worth busting out a mouse and keyboard instead? Of course, all these things can be dismissed if you remember that this is a remake of a port of an arcade light-gun game.If that short list of half-hearted complaints completely turns you off, I get it. This game probably won’t have much appeal for folks who never saw the nineties. But, if you’re willing to go along for the ride, you’ll likely find this to be a fun, frantic race through a wonderfully goofy, gory haunted house – one that oozes nineties cheesiness but has been given a fresh coat of paint that will appeal to players with modern sensibilities.Keep in mind, though: this game is  short – it may be worth waiting for a sale to pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fan of the original, I've played the Arcade on the big light gun machine and the lesser known PC port that was released for Windows 95/98. I was excited to have learned of and seen what this remake would propose. But upon playing it, I have mixed feelings.So far with what I liked was that yeah the visuals did indeed get an update here. Things are a little more atmospheric, the zombies are more grotesque, the bosses got amazing redesigns and vice versa. It all looks fantastic.The cheesy acting is also still intact, if anyone remembers how the arcade went with how deadpan the voice acting was in it. It was unintentionally hilarious more than the intended effect the game was aiming for. What was even more off-putting was the music choice in the game, which with this remake, I welcome the change of tunes.As far as handling the game itself, I've cut through this game in less than hour. That's probably because of experience, like knowing where the zombies are, knowing everything that there was to expect. The gameplay was well-retained here.But then we get to the problems of the game itself. I can tell the developers focused more on prettying the visuals up more than making a tightly coded and fluidly running game. I didn't have problems running the game itself but I've seen some aspects where assets would be floating in mid-air, like those robots with the claws. I would shoot their claws away and there was a couple points where I've seen them floating for no reason.The biggest problem was when I got to the typewriter to input my name for the score. I had more problems dealing with that than the entire game itself! XD I tried all that I could, but nothing worked. I typed my name over and over, ESC to use keyboard and back to using cursor. Tried to use Enter but nothing. What was that all about?This all brings me to an opinion I have when it comes to remakes/remasters and how everyone desires their favorite games to be brought to modern standards, have a makeover .etc;It really matters who's the one doing either a remaster or remake. This game is a prime example. You'll have your incredibly fantastic remakes in the Crash Trilogy, Spyro Trilogy and Tony Hawk 1+2. But then you'll have your crash and burn attempts in Warcraft III Reforged, Tony Hawk HD and others.There will be a House of the Dead 2 remake sometime in the future, but it doesn't give me much hope. I wanted to love this remake but it's really just a new paint job with the same guts shoved out. Don't get me wrong, I do want remakes too, but I want GOOD remakes more than BAD remakes.This one is a bad remake, just cheap nostalgic grab.

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my VR gameplay here: Yes, you can technically play The House of the Dead Remake in VR using the UUVR mod by Raicuparta. Playing with a gamepad and UUVR, somehow makes the game use gaze-based aiming combo with the joysticks. You basically do your best to center your camera on the target and shoot. You can't always center the camera on the target though. Also, for some unknown reason, doing this also makes you invulnerable. I have no idea how. Maybe the poor frame rates cause this. I don't know.Anyways, with all the above issues, I would only recommend using UUVR if you are a passionate VR gamer and already own this game. _childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a missed opportunity for a good remake. For starters, it took me about 5 minutes to get into the main screen, and I’ve got a high end computer. It seems poorly optimized and given little polish. My main problem with the game though, is its butchering of the original soundtrack. They copied most of everything from the original game, down to enemy placement and power-up locations, but for some reason decided to remake the OST. All they had to do was remaster the classic songs, but instead what we got is some boring elevator music that very superficially resembles the original. It might seem unimportant, but the music is what really set the tone for the game and gave us an extra boost of adrenaline. Without it, the game just feels bland and boring.I’m very glad that the remake was completely faithful to the original in its level design, but they still could have added some more features. For starters, I was hoping for a casual game mode, much like the one implemented in the House of Dead 2. In this mode you are able to collect power ups throughout the game which allow you to replay it selecting more ammo, higher damage or just goofs such as shooting bait instead of bullets. There are no minigames, no replay of boss fights to unlock extras, or anything worthwhile besides the arcade mode.Without any new game modes, the experience is only about 15 minutes long, and that isn’t worth paying full price. To be fair, there is a horde mode, but all it does is add more zombies. The game itself doesn’t give you any good reasons to play it more than once.Sure, the graphics and effects are pretty decent, but that is to be expected. Enemies clipping on each other and objects after dying is still present. The game is also way darker, which you might think would add to a more horrorish feel, but to me it just makes it feel more boring. Overall, this game feels like just another cash grab using nostalgia to bait players. They have been somewhat true to the original material, but not enough to interest old school players. It’s also not good enough on its own to interest any new players, so there’s no reason for it to exist.

_childDocuments_.review: As of this review, I have 100% achievements.The House of the Dead is my favorite arcade game series. I was very eager to play this remake when it was announced in 2019, alongside The House of the Dead 2: Remake. However, I do have some genuine issues with the remake, as well as some genuine praise.The remake is beautiful, no doubt about it. The environments are full of detail and the lighting does it justice, especially when using the in-game Photo Mode. I also liked the in-game models, although I didn’t like them much when I first saw them, as I felt it took away too much of the art style from the 1996 original, but have since grown on me.The developers made great use of the Unity engine, but I think that the developers could not (or did not) fix some issues before release. When opening the game for the first time, I was loaded into an infinite black screen, the main menu music started playing, then Unity crashed. As of this review, I have nearly 10 hours put into the game and have crashed only 3 times. Others have had issues as well.Another problem regarding the remake’s graphics are major rendering failures. This occurs every time without fail in certain sections of Chapter 4: “The house of the dead”. These sections are right after the Chariot fight when heading to the cave to fight Hanged Man, right after the Hanged Man fight when heading into the room with electricity beams, and during the cutscene when entering the BioReactor room to fight Magician. The rooms are empty voids for about 2 seconds before the assets load in.I think this is a Unity engine issue, or maybe how the game was developed. Maybe the developers have too much loaded at once that it starts to cause issues during gameplay? Please feel free to educate me in the comments if I'm wrong.However, it would explain the constant framerate drops, as well as the atrocious loading times. I have the recommended specs for the remake, yet on average I get 40-50 FPS, just below 60 at times (and 40-45 FPS in co-op), and the long loading times when starting a campaign or transitioning through levels kills the flow of the game, I find myself on my phone waiting for levels to load. While the game does play fairly normally when in-game, I feel it is poorly optimized.This is a nitpick, but there is no “classic” or “retro” mode option, essentially making the remake look and feel like the 1996 original, old polygon models and all. While I admit that I may be asking too much, it would have made for a great additional feature.I also take issue with the blood splash effects when killing zombies/creatures. While some may say this is a nitpick, I think it’s a problem to a degree. It’s very out of place and doesn’t look good, especially when fighting Hanged Man/Magician, it just looks terrible. An option to disable it would be nice.The sound design in the remake is honestly good. The soundtrack, while good, isn’t on the same level as the 1996 original as I don’t feel it’s as recognizable, but is by no means terrible. However, I will say that an option to choose between the original or remake soundtrack would have been a welcome feature. I will point out that members of the community already have mods in place to swap the remake’s soundtrack for the 1996 original’s.The sound design is pure bliss. Shooting zombies and turning them into gore sounds meaty, the zombies/creatures sound haunting, and other ambiance/environmental noise are spot on. I genuinely cannot complain about the sounds in the game.The voice acting in the game is also great. The original had some cheesy dialogue (although not as cheesy as THotD2), and the remake captures that perfectly in these new voices.The remake is almost 1-to-1 with the original, with modern touches. Using a mouse or controller to aim and shoot felt very nice after tweaking the settings. After playing through the game with each, it’s safe to say I would prefer using a mouse. Official light-gun functionality would have been a great addition. But while there is no official support, the community has already provided fixes to do just that using PC compatible light-guns and Wii remotes.I have genuine praise for the addition of skippable cutscenes. I do love what they did with the remade cutscenes, but it’s nice to be able to skip them when playing the game multiple times.Another thing I have genuine praise for is Horde Mode, it was chaotic but very fun. On harder difficulties, it raises the challenge to survive to its maximum. Although it did make framerate drops more frequent than in a normal playthrough, I still had fun.Hunting for secrets was fun and rewarding, I had a blast (pun intended) playing with the hidden/unlockable weapons found throughout the campaign. My favorite ones are the Grenade Launcher and Assault Rifle.While I do have a problem with the remake’s blood splash effects, they didn't feel out of place was when I was shooting zombies into gibs, which was really satisfying, props to the sound design. Seeing the zombies/creatures ragdoll after death was also funny, even if a bit out of place.On the topic of zombie and creature death, I do have one big criticism of the gameplay: shooting the head off a zombie/creature doesn't equal instant death, in most cases. 8 times out of 10 when I shoot a zombie’s head clean off, it’s body would still attack me and take my health. This can be infuriating sometimes, especially if playing on harder difficulties or in Horde Mode. Killing the brain should equate to instant death, just like the 1996 original. I can only hope this gets patched.The remake has plenty of customizable settings such as automatic reload/reload speed, reticle shadows/border opacity/thickness, and video/audio/controller settings. The House of the Dead: Remake is probably the most customizable game in the series with how many settings it has.However, there are settings from previous games that are missing here. Of which being the option to change the blood color. The remake tries to have it all by having most enemies bleed red, others bleeding green. Having the option to change blood color has been seen in most home releases of House of the Dead games, like in THotD2 & 3 Return.Another setting that is not in this remake is the setting to change the player’s reticle shape. While every gun in the game has its own reticle, having the option to change it would have been nice, again like in THotD2 & 3 Return.I detailed many problems that The House of the Dead: Remake has, including poor optimization, rendering problems, framerate drops, long loading times, and missing feature/settings. While I take issue with these problems, I believe they can, and will, be fixed by developers. The developers of the game do respond to concerns and criticisms of players in the Steam Forums. I made a post talking about some grammatical and spelling errors in the game’s in-game text and achievements, and a developer responded that it will be patched after a proofreading.This leads me to believe that the developers are working to fix most of the issues mentioned, I hope these are patched sooner rather than later. I will be sure to update this review in the case a patch comes.Despite its flaws, I can still say I had a fun experience playing and experiencing The House of the Dead: Remake. I was taken back to when I played The House of the Dead for the first time, and ended the game with a smile on my face. I hope the developers learn from this experience to polish the game, and to have a good launch for The House of the Dead 2: Remake.Overall, I recommend buying and playing The House of the Dead: Remake. I believe that the game will be updated/patched. I admit that it’s still a fun game, and a good remake of an old arcade classic. I think it’s worth your $25, but I don't blame you if you wait until the game is patched or goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Can you smell that? That musty smell, the kind of smelly smell that smells... smelly. You remember it, carpet and popcorn is a smell you will never forget. It's been 25 years, you're all grown up, your body stench is gone, the arcades are closed. You are old, crusty, paying bills. However the only hope you have... that we have... is that more and more companies are reinventing games from our youth bringing back our most cherished memories and our adventures around the arcades looking for next thrill.What's changed from a new face lift and bringing one of the most popular rail shooters to PC? Well, from the face lift, not much. The developers have taken great care to clone the original staying faithful to the original material, bad voice acting included. Included in a fresh repackage is a new hoard mode that multiplies the enemies, a new score system, various difficulties and an armory. Outside of that, nothing has been changed, bringing back non stop blasting fun.If this is your first visit, welcome. If you've waited 25 years to come back, welcome back. Load up, grab a friend, and get that popcorn ready. Take a seat, picture "Silent Scope" on your left and "Maximum Force/Area 51 Combo" on your right. Still have those old tokens you never used? Perfect. Welcome back to childhood.

It just looks cheap, and somehow worse than the original, which is hilarious because the original game is from 1996.The second worst part is the music. This remake, however, has a very lazy sounding rendition of the original's soundtrack.This is clearly a game remade with no love. It's not the worst of course: it's functional, it's playable, and it's decent enough. But it lacks the heart and soul that made the original special. As a game, it's decent enough. _childDocuments_.review: Overall a very great remake that proves Rail Shooters are still fun in 2022. If you're a fan of the series you don't want to miss out on this or the upcoming Remake of HOTD2.RETAINED from the Original:-Enemy placement is identical to the original-The visual style is borrowed from the newer games in the series, but adapted to HOTD 1's environments-Every single room from the original has been recreated with brand new details to provide better context to your surroundings-All the cutscenes and voice lines are back, re-recorded with new voice actors.-Just like the original, gameplay involves spamming pistol shots at groups of 1-4 zombies (The Horde shooting of HOTD4 and Scarlet Dawn is given it's own mode) -2-player Co-op is here, but you can now also do a 2-player versus mode where you try to out-score your opponent. Multiplayer can be done with a friend couch-coop style or through steam remote play. (Just make sure your friend isn't using an Auto-Clicker to ruin the game.)-Blood color options are back (After an update) Although Zombies' exposed wounds and blood stains on their weapons appear green, and their insides will always appear as red, you can now choose from 20 different colors for the blood itself, ranging from different shades of Blue, Navy, Green, Yellow as well as Purple, Pink, Orange, White, Black and of course Red. There's also a really neat randomize option which will change the blood color for every single shot that lands on a zombie. Personally, I suggest going with a Dark Green or Yellow as they look the best besides Red.What's NEW:-New forms of aiming. Because this is a PC/Console game and not an Arcade game, there are new ways to control your aim, including Gyro Aiming to try and mimic Lightgun gameplay (Playstation or Switch Pro Controller required), Mouse aiming for those who struggle with precision aiming, and of course Analog Stick or Keyboard aiming if it's your only option.-New Horde mode, which puts up to 15 times the amount of Zombies in each level. (This is for the fans of HOTD4 and Scarlet Dawn)-2 Options for scoring. Classic scoring, which rewards getting headshots and taking less damage, and Modern scoring, which rewards killing enemies as quickly as possible, dismembering corpses as much as you can, and destroying as much of the environment as physically possible.-A gallery for viewing all the enemy models-4 New unlockable weapons, Including What's MISSING:-Good lightgun support. I don't have a lightgun, so i'd recommend checking the game's steam forum page for updates on this.-The original music. The game uses brand new music that's directly based off of the original soundtrack. That's not a problem though because the new soundtrack is great and there are mods to replace it with the original one. (You can also just play the original music on YouTube in the background)

_childDocuments_.review: Sad to see people have technical issues with this game. I played for a couple of hours today, beat it 3-4 times and honestly had a genuine blast.The remake is mostly well made and all the mechanics work fine. Maybe with the modern graphics some things are a bit harder to spot, but increasing the gamma/brightness helped a bit.It looks good and plays exactly how I remembered it in arcade mode with the classic point system, but I have to say that I enjoy it way more with the modern point system.The only issue I noticed was playing the new "horde mode", which increases the amount of zombies in most encounters, and sometimes may cause issues like getting hit from a position you can't shoot... but the game is really forgiving with i-frames after getting hit + amount of credits.It's just great, dumb funPS: After unlocking a certain weapon I did in fact have some performance issues and audio stuttering
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: Does this remake do a few things right? Absolutely. Do mods fix some of the games audio disappointments? Yup. Is there potential for this version to grow and become the definitive version of House of the Dead 1? Heck yes. Is this game worth $30 and will it ever realise ANY of that potential?No.PS: The game WILL run like trash on lesser GPU's because every texture in the game is ridiculously big, and you can't change the quality settings.
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: The remake is well done. PC graphics and physics are on top. The game has almost no flaws. Perhaps the only thing that upset was the lack of an original soundtrack. P.S: In any case, I am very grateful to the developers for re-experiencing childhood emotions. Thank you for taking me back to 1998, to an arcade club not far from my house. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: You know what you are getting. Basically a hi octane on rails mouse shooter with great updated graphics which takes about 30 mins to play through. It's house of the dead for mouse looking pretty. No more no less. Does it's job and delivers. Not really my thing but I got this as part of a bundle and enjoyed it for what it was. _childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine when it works. Blowing away zombies with physics is a great touch. Would be a good enough game when it goes on sale. But I don't recommend it because it doesn't work on many PCs, especially with AMD GPUs, though some players with Nvidia GPUs are affected as well. For over a year now, several people have reported issues with blank screens and crashes, yet the developers remain silent. Other players complain about performance issues, yet the developers remain silent.It's kinda sad because games built in Unity generally just work, but the devs must have botched something to make this game so unstable.tl;dr - blank screens, crashes, poor performance on many PCs. Not recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: This would have felt a lot more fuller of an experience if they had a remake of House of the Dead 2 included in the package. I mean 25€ is rather steep for something most people are gonna beat in 30 minutes or less and spend and average time of 2-3 hours on. This remake feels cheap and sloppy in many areas. There's a good deal of glitches, unnecessary (or in certain instances just bad) changes from the original game and, in all honesty, the original 1996 title looks better. Visual information is much clearer in the original title. Here the gloss, bloom, environmental damage and overdone gore effects muddle up visual clarity.And no light gun support?! Are we gonna get remakes of point & click adventure games with no mouse support next?I'm gonna have to give this game a big fat pass.
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an epic fail! How such an iconic game gets remade and released without proper lightgun support is mind blowing. I have been chatting with the devs and they said they didn't test lightguns. Absolute positioning was implemented in the menus but not in-game. I'm hoping this is easy to patch but considering that the Switch release was a mess and the PS4 version launched without Move support, I'm not too hopeful.
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful remake of the original arcade classic released in 1996.Wonderful graphics which still fit the gothic horror and even expand on the design of the original, detailed and expressive character and enemy models, and high octane gameplay very much akin to the arcade release.This PC port of THOTD: Remake is the best one graphically and performance-wise compared to the PS4 and Switch ports which the comparisons made are night and day.A fantastic job a recreating such an iconic staple in modern horror and arcade game history. Really hope to see a remake of THOTD 2 soon!
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: While I like the original House of the Dead game, the remake was a bit of a let down. The graphics are cool, sound design is cool. And the replayability? High. Story? Well, not so much, but the original wasn't an award winning story either.So then? Why I don't recommend the game? The lousy technical issues which make it a disaster on the other hand. Patchable, but at least if there would be any patch for these performance issues.1) Alt+Tab freezes and crashes it.2) Arenas doesn't really like to load in. During the later game part it becomes frequent. You can see the characters floating in the air, while no meshes and textures seen. 3) In windowed mode it likes to slow down or freeze/stalls for some seconds, then jump to a point where it should actually be.4) Sometimes you watch the loading screen more than you actually play on a level.
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: This remake was such a disappointment.From the fact that the soundtrack is different (you can mod the original soundtrack back in), to the fact that the enemies feels more like bullet sponges than actual enemies.They got almost everything about the game wrong. I'm surprised you can sell this for this price considering how short it is. And how much less replayable this game is to the original.The bosses are a joke. I have more trouble with the instahit zombies on Arcade Difficulties than I do the actul bosses. The only time I got hit was because I let them.They did The Magician so dirty. Not only replacing his theme with a god awful recreation, but also nerfing his speed and making his ultimate attack a basic attack. That's not to mention how much easier this game is since you have all of your weapons in your arsenal once you've unlocked them.I have to give props for the graphics and gunplay though, that felt solid. And the fact you added in cheat codes is a nice touch, wish we still had those for most games.But overall, unless you can get this game for EXTREMELY CHEAP. Don't buy it, stay away. The original is still much better.
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: I know quite a few people might want to hear this. This being from someone who is one of the most predominant speed runners of this game.Its alright.Yeah that may surprise you, and yes I own this on all platforms. With over 200 hours across all systems, you'd think id have more to say then "alright" but no. The game itself is awesome, if not being compared to what its working off. No, the original code wasn't lost, this was just a team, that being Megapixel that was tasked to hire out a bunch of people to make a game for Forever Entertainment.This being the same studio that are known to dump quite a few of their projects if they don’t work out. As someone who reads quite a few investor reports by them, the stats show that this game was just sitting there, "finished" for a bit, before it was the best time $$ to release it. Ever hear about the new Fear Effect game? No? oh it was just a write off you won’t see much about. And yes, I’ll give them crud, for as much as I know they should be able to take it. Anyways, onto the actual review. On the note that this is a true finished game, well that is just a huge lie. Not only is it incomplete but it’s also not going to be fixed, does it work though? Kinda... I mean besides from A LOT of technical issues, mostly on the PC release. The game itself runs, and I guess that's what matters. I mean if you count that the game broke during a large event I was invited to, that’s a good look, isn’t it? It’s fun, I mean it also looks amazing besides the fact that it seems like it was optimised with a NASA computer in mind. And at the end of the day, you can point and click, yeah a $40 point and click game, I’m guessing you might be seeing where I’m going with this.  I mean being honest they did well with the “fun” aspect. It’s a fun game.It’s just, how much “fun”. I mean 15 minutes of fun for $40aud is a total waste of money. SURE, you can replay the game you say. But dam is it just not fun after an hour or two. I mean I speedrun the game and love the series, so I don’t mind. But to the average consumer, wow you’d must have a large monetary deficit to rationalise buying this game.  But what’s good you say? Well, the voice actors are amazing. I mean that’s about it, other then several cases of stealing and not crediting the wiki made by a group who only has the best intentions with providing people content.No but its fine that they credited them way after release, isn’t it? You may think, well this dudes talking mad crud about a game he plays a lot. Well yeah. If you look really far past the series previous releases, the game isn’t bad. I mean I’d say a solid 6/10. The models made for the game look amazing, and for me it’s a lot better than the source material. Does it serve as a in all honesty a true “remake” of the original. I’m not sure. What do you call a game that simply does nothing new and just remakes all the assets? A remake? Or just a cheap cash grab?I know I’m hard on this game, but I think forever could have done a lot more, that being guiding megapixel into making a better experience. It also sucks that they released several different versions of the same game on different systems, all with their own issues since they don’t care much about compatibility. Just go out and search the wide web for the other games in the series. For those who know, The lanterns are all out for how much soul was actually put into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game in a bundle and am going to give it a recommend, with caveats.  The game is what it says it is, a remake of The House of the Dead arcade game for the PC.  It is just the arcade game and a horde mode.  There are a few extras, like a gallery mode to view enemies, but it is pretty bare bones as far as features.In the game you are trying to stop some guy named Curien who has created an army of the dead in his house.  He has a really big house with lots of different routes to get to him and his three boss monsters.  You can unlock different paths, but all that really does is give you slightly different scenery while you are destroying the same undead.  There is not much variety in the enemies, and the voice acting is horrible, though I think that is on purpose.  I think they were going for a bad B-movie quality to the voice overs.  They either told the voice actors to do a bad job, or just hired poor voice actors.The gun play translates to mouse very well and the game is fun.  It takes maybe 10-20 minutes to beat the game, so understand that the game is not really worth the asking price of $30.  I got this game in a bundle and am recommending it because if you are a fan of the series, and understand that you are literally just getting the arcade game with a few extras, and are happy with that, then you will be satisfied with the game.Otherwise wait for it to go on sale, or go to an arcade, you can beat the game with less money than the game costs, as this game is good, just not worth $30.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful and nostalgic experience.Originally a game made by SEGA in 1996 (arcades) on Model 2C hardware. Two conversions: Sega Saturn and PC with poor graphics but 120% of playability (even with mouse on PC). Now, we are getting pure fun (kinda short) with awesome graphics and challenging achievements.There is hardly any story behind the game: you must kill the horde of zombies (and bosses) in mystery mansion and save the world from evil.This remake is solidly made - modern and detailed graphics with an old school feeling. Nothing sophisticated: take the gun and shoot. Shoot a lot. Shoot different parts of the body and the guts will fly around you.If you take into account how detailed this game is made, you wouldn't complain about price. Sure, it is short, but I bet, you toss the coin (or ten) into arcade machine, if you meet it somewhere. Just for flying zombie guts, fun and play.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's good, the gameplay, the graphics, the BGM, even the voice acting is still terrible as it should be, which is perfect, but kinda disappointed on the final boss Magician that it becomes much slower and easier than the original HOTD. However, it still worth your money to have a chance to experience such huge nostalgic feeling and it definitely will bring back your childhood memories.

_childDocuments_.review: I dunno if it would actually work as a light gun shooter because (at least on arcade difficulty) despite being the remake of one, because it feels like the game expects you to be a perfect shot and to shoot the enemies in a very precise order to avoid getting hit -- the game will feel different to anyone who played the original just because of this. The enemies attack much faster and don't seem to be easily stunned like they can be in the arcade, but they also seem to attack in order of proximity to you as well, which makes it often feel like you're supposed to 100% finish enemies one at a time, rather than hitting all the zombies, reloading, then finishing the ones that you stun. It's kinda weird feeling.Obviously this is a remake, so there are certain things like rebalancing of the bosses that have taken place (Chariot is a bit more dangerous than before, and his 2nd phase isn't (100%) a freebie like it is in the arcade) .I think they kinda fumbled on Magician a bit -- he's too tanky to balance out the fact you're much more accurate with a M&K versus a lightgun, and his fireballs seem to get cancelled whenever you hit him enough, which is very strange.This is a pretty entertaining aim trainer of sorts, and a nice little trip down nostalgia lane if you grew up with the original house of the dead. I'd get it on sale if you're looking for a nostalgia trip.
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: Runs way better than the switch and looks alot nicer too! _childDocuments_.review: For all my childhood, One game that still stick around in my memory and holds a special place in my heart is The house of the dead.I remember when my dad and I wanted to go have some fun and encourage me to play shooting games at the local arcade with him, and it was the House of the Dead. This game is my very first arcade game and this game stuck to my memory. Since then, every time I had a chances, I would always go back to the arcade and tried play every iteration, every episode from every platforms of the house of the dead when the opportunity arrives. I even managed to find every secret of the House of the Dead 4 by myself, by watching other player playing at the arcade who tries to goes for a high score. I could say that this series are a part of my life.Sorry for the long rant, here’s a game review.I honestly enjoy this Remake of the HOTD. Everything in this game could be describe simply as “done right”. Every sequences, hidden route, enemy spawn, even the cheesiness of the voice actor. Everything here is just perfectly recreated without skipping a beat. Kudos to the developer of this remake.However, one thing that is still in the way of making this game perfect, is the soundtrack. This remake has “ZERO” original soundtrack and it’s the only thing that In the way of giving this game a perfect score. Overall, for the HOTD fans out there, it is a magical moment just to play the games that is a part of my childhood, this game would just hit right for you.

For me it's much easier to aim using the mouse instead of an actual light gun. Please "remake" the rest of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest weaknesses of House of the Dead Remake was being announced and showed up as a switch game, don't get me wrong, the switch is good portable device, but I feel like the art-style they were aiming for, wasn’t really designed for hardware like switch, and pc version of HotDR really shows it, the game looks significantly improved visually, and runs at much more stable framerateWhat you are looking at, it’s a 1:1 conversion of the original on-rail shooter House of the Dead, being the biggest change on the visuals department, but for most of the part it’s the same game, there’s some small addictions like the horde mode and some new secrets added, but that’s about it.Keep in mind this is an arcade game and as a result it’s a really short experience and might not offer the “value” that most are looking for, but I still had my fun with it.My only gripes with it it’s the absence of the original soundtrack and no online multiplayer, this game would be totally a blast If I could co-op with a friend online, but as it is right now, no such option.I’m a big sucker for on-rail shooters in general, and I really enjoyed this game , but if you want my unbiased opinion, I would suggest wait for sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all of the classics to be remade, this was on my "Top 5" list. PRO's:-Amazing gameplay with plenty of gore-Nostalgic game that is being reintroduced to a new generation-Short campaign to allow players the chance of restarting a run without the hassle of spending hours to restart for a high score-Beautiful graphics and lighting-New players don't have to jump right into a coin eating machine (Like I did back in the day)-Challenging gameplay that keeps you on edge and keeps you hungry for the next run of zombie stomping mayhemCON's:-Players have experience stutters occasionally-Some achievements seem bugged-Enemies appear to have randomized HP values but only the adder enemies-Game becomes trivial after unlocking the armoryThe pro's of this game easily outweigh the cons, of course, this is opinionated. I do see where the enemy HP values seem randomized and it's a little problem out of the big picture of the game. Which is the fact that this game is a complete rework of the original and there's obviously going to need to be some updates to improve these aspects. I am also seeing some people having performance issues and as unfortunate as this is, I personally cannot agree with the complaints. I have experienced maybe two frame drops and that was due to my recording software. Otherwise, it runs smother than your colon after a hot cup of joe. Some people have claimed that this game lost it's charm with the updated graphics, sound, etc. I cannot agree with this, either. The original game was a light-gun rail shooter with cheesy graphics and terrible voice acting due to the constraints of technology. This is a brand new imagination of the concept of The House of The Dead. Look at the most recent games, from The House of The Dead II to Overkill, the games have been dingy and had a subtle hint of "Grindhouse" aspects. Except for Overkill. That was all Grindhouse. They brought back the "horror" to a dark tale.All in all, an uncut diamond waiting to be a finished masterpiece and I am so happy to be a part of the process.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, there's pros and cons to it though:Cons: -Short Campaign-Some minor frame drops, though these are really minor (except when I spammed a a specific unlockable on one of the bosses)-Story is also short being mostly a scenic run and gun with dialogue in cutscenespros:-Steam version is simply beautiful compared to Switch-Voices are cheesy like the original-Similar music to the original (one of them was so good I kept humming it)-Lots of extra content for replayability this almost nullifies the shortness issues. You have many different extra side areas to go through, a secret area full of goodies that unlocks new weapons to find, new weapons to find, multiple endings, you can in the new mode switch your character to G, Rogan's partner who does get his own actual story dialogues too as well as co-op (yes including home local co-op)-There's extra modes like Original or Modern which changes how the game plays, for example a different point system, you can play as G, and some differences in enemies. There's also Horde mode which is a flood of zombies to kill (and yes it is co-op and you can use unlocked weapons if you desire)-There's a gallery of enemies to unlock by going different routes which will unlock their 3D models to look at, hear and yes it even contains their names, notable information and this includes even weaknesses.-Mouse works perfectly here as well.All in all I think this game is great, a real throw back and a different kind of game than is typically out there nowadays. Cheap and has lots of fun features. I seen some say well I beat it in 30 minutes, while you can do that by just shooting all guns ablazing I think this doesn't tell you the full picture of the replayability and details one missed out on in that play through that really changes up the experience and are fun to find, use or explore and more.

_childDocuments_.review: == Short Review - No Spoilers ==The House of the Ded: Remake is - imagine that - a remake of the original Arcade game "House of the Dead" (by Sega) from the mid 1990s. As the original, it is a typical "Rail Shooter", meaning that the player has the ability to aim with the mouse at various incoming enemies (aka "Zombies"), while the character automatically moves through the different levels of the game.Truth be told, I won't dignify this game with a fully-fledged review. Let's start with the facts, though:- game features very similar content as the original game from the 90s- graphics have been slightly reworked- online play is availableHere is what I didn't like about this game (switching to my subjective views):1) The game is utterly unstable. It crashed repeatedly to desktop at various stages. I couldn't even get it to work once at WQHD resolution and the problem is definitely not with my hardware. Obviously, crashes can also be provoked when clicking the main menu / the loading screen before loading is finished.2) The remake has obviously been done with the intention to be close to the original (which is not a bad thing as such), but if I compare this remake with e.g. the one of Resident Evil 2 (or 1 for that matter), it is easy to see that the devs didn't invest that much time in making this a breathtaking game when it comes to the graphics (quite the opposite).3) Following up on that, there are just about zero improvements to the game play as such which could have been done with much less effort, but greater impact. You can finish the game as is in ~40 minutes on normal difficulty without ever breaking to sweat. After that there is almost zero replay value. This weighs even more heavily when considering the price tag the put on the game...4) When looking at the mediocre graphics, the performance of the game is simply pathetic. I had to switch off almost all details and effects and the game was still laggy as hell. This may or may not be due to the use of the Unity Engine, but I frankly don't care. I can run modern, up to date first person shooters fluently on my machine which have much better graphics and this performance is just not tolerable. 0/10 points.All in all, there is truly nothing I can recommend about this game. If you like the genre, give "The Typing of the Dead: Overkill / The House of the Dead: Overkill" a try which puts this one to shame in each and every single aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw that this game was coming out, I knew that I had to buy it. The original arcade House of the Dead was one of my favorite games growing up. A bowling alley near my cousin's house had a machine there, and we would spend more time at the game than we would actually bowling, feeding quarter after quarter into it. The remake does not disappoint for me in any way. The core of the game is still there, in all of its cheesy, late 90s glory. The voice acting is better, but still goofy as hell, and the game still delivers that arcade-level difficulty. For me this feels like the best kind of nostalgia comfort food, and I can't wait to sink hours into this game trying for all of the achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a lot of fun.  I used to love arcade on-rails shooters growing up so this was a short but sweet nostalgia blast from the past. Nostalgia is definitely not worth full price.  I had fun and feel the 8,49€ is worth it, but wouldn't have been happy paying much more.What's there to say that isn't clear from the trailer? A bit of care comes in as there's scientists running about that you should avoid killing, as they reward you with additional health if you don't kill them.I feel a bit put out by the 'unlockable weapons' claim in the description because I saw no weapon collection points at all, and that was with two playthroughs. _childDocuments_.review: The original House of the Dead with updated graphics and a few new features added. Saving all the scientists allows you to unlock four different weapons you can switch to during normal gameplay. A crossbow that does high damage and is good against bosses, a gun that fires large wooden spikes that does high damage and can pin enemies to walls and launch them around, a grenade launcher mostly included for another new mode, and an automatic rifle that does less damage than the gun but fires quickly and holds 30 shots. There is a new horde mode that significantly increases the number of enemies, it doesn't add new areas but does have you attacked from some additional angles. A new scoring mode was added along with some difficulty options that can increase the amount of damage enemies take and there are some options for changing blood color, change reticle color, to set auto reloads, for aim assist, mouse sensitivity. I wouldn't want to try playing this with a controller and it's not going to be as fun unless you buy one of those newer $150-$400 rumble light-guns that work on HD TVs and monitors but it works reasonable well with the mouse.The real problem is the fairly high price asked for the game and the first House of the Dead is a short game with only a few side paths in the first three stages and nothing that interesting mechanically other than saving the scientists. The new guns can be fun to use, especially the spike shooting gun and the horse mode puts more action in the game but the best ports of these games are things like Time Crisis 3's PS2 port that added a large number of challenge maps and an entire second campaign with a side character of the main game or Vampire Night's PS2 release that added a lot of side quest and unlockables.It's a fun but fairly bare bones offering that would need you to buy an expensive HD supporting light-gun (Sinden/Gun4IR) for it to reach its full potential.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: Very good remake. Something something game critics never get it. I think some critics never played a lightgun game in their lives. It runs well despite some initial load times when first starting it up for me. Only complaints from me are:Lack of any kind of weapon pick ups. I know this wasn't a thing in the original but come on. You can make a change like that. Having shotgun or machine gun pickups like in the later HOTD games would have changed things up. * Edit: okay, there ARE weapon pick ups but they're hidden? Why? Why make them hidden? I'm glad they're in the game but maybe make it a little obvious that (1) they exist and (2) how to unlock them? There's no auto-fire option. That's when you hold down the fire key and it keeps firing. You have to keep hitting the button every single time. So if you're using a mouse you will kill your wrist. Thankfully, you can hit Spacebar to fire and still aim with the mouse but it's still a wrist work out. Luckily you can disable the "Reload" voice and set the reload time to be nonexistant so you can just keep firing. One nitpick: when you enter your name to confirm your name you have to hit Tab and not Enter like the screen prompts tell you. Also, no curse words which is bizarre for a game like this but I guess that's a remnant from a Nintendo mandate because this launched as a Switch exclusive for about 2 weeks.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I don't personally think its worth the full price, but it depends on how much you enjoy light gun shooters and house of the dead. Now on to the rest of my thoughts.Considering this is pretty much a faithful recreation of the Sega Saturn House of the dead game with some extra stuff tacked on and graphics revamped, its pretty good. The acting is still pretty cheesy as either the audio or the script is the same, not as cheese filled as other House of the Dead games, but still something to laugh at when they speak. Gameplay is your standard light gun shebang shoot bad guys still they stop moving, don't shoot civilians (scientists), with the house of the dead bonus of branching paths to add replayability and bosses. However, and this is the reason I say this game isn't worth it's current price, if you decent at light gun games you can beat this game with no cheats and just the pistol in 30 minutes or less. At the time of writing this, which according to steam is about 4 hours of playtime,  I have about 32 of the games 41 current achievements with the remaining ones being easily missable, secret, or grindy. Of course ignoring completing the game, this is still fun with or without friends, but your mileage will most certainly vary.3 more hours of playtime later, I've gotten all the achievements under 8 hours of gameplay (maybe even less as I left the game idling more than once). About 7 hours of gameplay till completetion for a 25 dollar game. As I said earlier, if you ignore completion and just play this game to have fun, as I will from time to time, this game is probably worth it at its current price or a small sale, but If you play games maybe once or twice or to completion, you may not find the game worth $25.

_childDocuments_.review: I consider the original hotd as one of my fav games of all time and one of my fondest gaming memories was being able to beat the arcade game without getting hit once. Now with the announcement of a remake I was really excited and was able to try it first on the nintendo switch. Well... It was horrible. So I waited for the pc version hoping it will be better and all the issues ironed out. Unfortunately not really much has change between the pc and the switch versions. My pros and cons about this game.Pros+ Game is dirt cheap if you can get it on sale. + The nostalgia factor is there and it even has the terrible voice acting to make the game as close to the original game as possible.+ It's cool they add a horde mode and difficulty sliders which gave the game more replayability.+ Few issues aside the game is still fun. The game can be beaten in 20 to 30 mins but discovering and going new paths and finding secrets will always keep you coming back for more.+ Achievements and photomode.Cons- Mediocre remake and pretty inferior to the original game.- No lightgun support.- Buggy and riddled with a lot of issues. I remember being far into the game and my character just decides to stop moving entirely which in turn softlocked me. Lol! - Shots doesn't register sometimes.- Some areas stutters and drops your fps.- Graphics isn't really that good and looks like a ps3/360 game. Some zombies looks terrible, blood looks like paint, gore is bad, and everyone looks like they were drenched in oil or something. Even older hotd games like 4 and scarlet dawn looks and runs better than this game.-Game's physics is terrible and zombies drop like string puppets instead of dying in a more realistic manner.- Sounds isn't as good and doesn't have that same impact as the original. Also the sounds is buggy in this game and randomly drops while playing.- Bosses are terrible in the remake compared to the original game. It feels like they were remade to be more cheaper and they also shorten the leeway to counter their attacks making fighting them frustrating at times. Also why is the final boss such a bullet sponge?- Mouse movement in this game is sluggish and at time it feels like you're fighting with the crosshairs more rather than the zombies themselves. It's also really hard to enjoy Horde mode where every second counts because of the sluggish mouse movement and delay.To end my review I would say that this was a welcome attempt to remake hotd but it's marred with more issues that aren't even present in the original game. Still I would give this a thumbs up because I got the game really cheap on sale and it's even bundled with panzer dragon. This is a 5/10 game for me but a must have if you just want casual fun and a game that you can beat in half an hour.

_childDocuments_.review: What I write for this review is the experience I had with the game, everybody will experience things differently. This is my honest review if you don't like it well tough. Also no game is safe from a review whether its early access or full release, now onto the review.I remember this game back in my childhood when you had to go to an arcade store to play games, the arcade stores where you get quarters to put in the machine to play the game. This was one of my favorite arcade games to play & was my first zombie game. House Of The Dead: Remake was just fantastic remade as it was back in 1996. At the time of games in 1996 it was a masterpiece & was really good for an arcade game. The graphics are definitely better now than it was in 1996 & I didn't really see anything out of place or anything in the remake.The sound was okay, I think the gun sound could have been remade & the reloading sound as well. The zombies sounds were about standard.The acting was okay for its time & I for one kind of miss the acting of videos back in the 1990-2000 era. There is shared/split screen co-op just like it was back in 1996, both looking at the same screen & coordinate with each other. Arcade games did campaign co-op so much better than today's standards games. The House Of The Dead: Remake was just as fun as it was when I was a child. I wish MegaPixal Studio could reboot the series with today's graphics but keep the arcade style. So with that The House Of The Dead: Remake gets a 8/10 score for me & I definitely recommend picking this game up if you are hardcore fan of the arcade games being brought back to life.That's the Pony review for The House Of The Dead: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: It's actually a really bad remake. I loved the original. Played it so much as a kid at arcades. Recently got to play it again at magfest after over a decade and it was very nostalgic. Could go through the whole game without having to continue I played it so much. This "remake" is just a mess. Sound/music is really bad. It sounds like it skips constantly and the tone doesn't fit the atmosphere. Not sure if it's bugged but a lot of moments of instant hits you have no chance of preventing. I lost count the amount of times a door was opened and was instantly hit. At moments some enemies that would die in one shot to the face would then take 3-6+ shots to die at other moments they are encountered. It seemed to be random. (yes I avoided shooting the metal attachments on some of the enemies) Boss's health I can't tell if are inflated heavily and/or are given moments of invincibility. Invincibility for damage was absolutely noticeable on the third and final bosses. Overall this trampled on my childhood memories of the original game that made it so fun and enjoyable. You're better off finding the original on PC if you can than wasting money on this mess. It's more like they turned it into a typical modern arcade shooter that forces hits on you to make you spend money to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Who is this game for? The cynical part of me says for the kind of people drunk in a barcade going "cool, House of the Dead! I remember that!" and then credit feeding through. Except it's not in an arcade, and no mouse, controller, or motion controls effectively moving a cursor around on the screen is the same as a point and shoot light gun for speed and accuracy.Letting go that this isn't arcade House of the Dead, this is a Remake, it's an okay game. Some of the enemy timing has been changed, sometimes things hit you faster than they would in the original, most of the bosses were nerfed into the ground, sometimes the range at which a zombie can hit you is inconsistent from other points in the game, and sometimes a zombie is still alive even without a head. It's a pretty game, the ragdolling is humorous and inline with HotD, and the layouts are faithful, but it's the finer details being what alienates me from feeling like this is a true upgraded experience from the original game... that has never had an arcade accurate port.  HotD 2,3,4 all got ports to XBox, Wii, PS3/4, even Switch, but no love for the original, arcade HotD.And finally, the music lacks compared to the original.tl;dr This would be a better game in the arcade than House of the Dead Scarlet Dawn, but the home experience is lacking for anything more than just a throwaway afternoon experience. Even 12 year old me could finish the arcade game in less quarters than this game costs

_childDocuments_.review: The House of The Dead, a game which haunted us in our childhood, a game with absolute terrible story and plot. BUT! It was perfect. (I'm talking about the classic, 1997 version)This legendary game just got remastered, and remade. I was crying coz it was supposed to be a Nintendo only remake but Sega, megapixel didn't disappoint us. Yes ladies and gentlemen, it's here for PC and I've spent around 3-4 hours (considering its term final week and the game takes 30~ ish minutes to finish.. considering you can finish the game without dying) and I think I have a good idea how the game was.First things first. Megapixel nailed it with the setting and when it comes to keeping the original stuff original. Definitely we didn't ask for a horde mode but any game developer remastering legendary titles would love to mess around with a thing or two (Rockstar I'm looking at you). But the graphics, gore, gameplay was just as I wanted it to be. Personally speaking, playing on easy mode is simply not fair as every zombie will die to a bullet on their fingertips. But the classic one certainly was the difficult one (I mean, 99% of the OG games were difficult for anyone). But the elephant of the room is, it had hype for the OG players and it delivered.Now to the sides I didn't like. I mean, how much effort would it take to keep the original soundtracks? I can't remember Michael Jackson singing in House of Dead (RIP GTA VC) that SEGA or Megapixel would have a hard time restoring / recreating those (meh, I'll just mod it) but it is what it is.Another thing I'm not a fan of is the hardware hunger. I mean, the optimization is just fine, unless you're playing on Horde mode where you can face some lags. But yes, cranking the gfx down is also an option but no matter how much we complain graphics won't be downgraded no matter what. The only reason I'm saying this is because 99% of the players who will be playing this game in the first place will be those who want to revisit their childhood or past. Yes, I do expect new fans of the title to arise but as I expect some senior citizens to dive in this game, maybe something a bit more *optimized* would work. But hey I ain't complaining.Final score 9.8/10 (just coz I miss the old soundtracks)

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty underwhelming remake of a game that wasn't all too exciting to begin with (for me at least). The new character and zombie models are well-done, and it's cool to see the 1996 original be brought to 2022 graphics standards, but the facial animations look clumsy and straight out of The Sims; the remixed songs aren't nearly as memorable as the originals; even the basic pistol can rip through zombies with relative ease, making the game much easier than before; and the replay value can be exhausted before you reach the 5 hours of play time mark.To be fair, something that could be coloring my opinion is that I've played through the arcade original numerous times, so I've had my fill of it. But even then, once you've beaten this game a few times, whether it's the remake or (especially) the original, you'll have done pretty much everything there is to do in it: play through it once with the classic pistol on one route, play through it while saving all the scientists on another route, play through it while collecting all the hidden weapons on another route, and play through it with some of the new guns on another route. It's all very repetitive. $25 is too much for this game. Considering how short it is, and the amount of extra content isn't much more than the Sega Saturn/Windows 98 version, I say you wait until it's on sale to get it (maybe for like $10 or $15). For $10 or $15, it's a fun little quickie, but for $25, it's just an empty experience.

_childDocuments_.review: REPLAYABILITY WARNING: Currently, dying means nothing. You can keep respawning over and over till you get to the final boss. This means not much replayability. I think it's essential that the devs put a limit on respawns. Having the risk of dying and having to start from the start of the level was its charm and that rogue-like mechanic made sure you got every shot on point so you don't die. You can finish the game in 50 minutes or less on your first try. Big mistake, infinite lives should only be in a new/casual difficulty mode.Otherwise, I recommend this game if nothing except for the mindblowing phenomenal character art and level art. An absolutely astounding and faithful modernized remake of the original game that filled in the empty and drab environment and gave all of it exactly what the original creators would have imagined it to be. So uncannily faithful that I got a lot of overlapping flashbacks while playing through the familiar areas. So much so that I can really deceive myself into thinking this is what it actually looked like back in the day (you know, the weird nostalgic graphical upgrades you have when you try to imagine how an old favorite game of yours looked like, until you play through it again and realize how bad it was). Clearly a lot of thought and resources went into this remake and it really shows. The graphics are nuts. Great job by those teams.But, stupidly horrible music choice and design ruins the atmosphere and leaves it feeling like a cheap arcade game. Fortunately, you can mute the Music and the UI Effects in the menu to solve that issue so all is well.
