_childDocuments_.review: Bought it at 50% sale, and played it for only an hour and a half. I COULD refund it should I want to, but I decided against it since I think the developers earned my money fair and square (besides, you're expected to spend that much at an arcade cabinet anyways.)The classic mode was a good trip down the memory lane. A new coat of graphics and gameplay tweaks made me re-live my childhood years all over in the most vivid and satisfying way. (I have a habit of pushing my tongue against the back of my teeth when I'm tense. Suffice to say my tongue rn is very numb, just as it was when I was a kid.) I had a blast, and I proceeded replay it the second time to moment my first playthrough was over.The horde mode, though, is an odd beast. It spawns a lot of enemies -- well of course. that's in the name. but really, a lot. to the point it makes you think THIS MUCH is what you should be gunning down if you were really charging in into an undead infested mansion. It's plays completely different to the original and, that's of course a good thing seeing as how short the original game is. More good contents to enjoy is always welcomed. It plays a bit like HotD 4 or Scarlet Dawn with how many enemies you're overwhelmed with constantly, but it is to my chagrin when I say that this remake sadly lacks the polish of those entries and you'll take a lotta cheap hits from the enemies off-screen. But I can say with confidence that I'd rather have it than not.That being said, the devs knew exactly what buttons they needed to push when it comes to visual feedbacks. You might remember that HotD 1 WAS the most gore-heavy of the series. The original HotD series got less and less bloody gory as far as on-screen violence went. That is not the case here, and the grimey gothic horror atmosphere of the origial first game is well and truly represented. The "gibs" and the ragdolls takes the proverbial cake, and I found immense amount of joy watching the enemy corpses being turned into mush, or, seeing my well-timed shots leading to the enemy corpses flying across the room (like it's the ealry 2000's and the ragdoll physics -- you know, those bouncy, overly dramatic, weightless kind -- just become a thing).The only problem I have with this game is the same as the one I had with the original game - THE FRICKIN' MAGICIAN. This overdressed, overhyped, and overrated clown of a final boss is too much of a bullet sponge that I have no shame in admitting that I resorted to autoclicker whenever I had to dispatch him. Sorry not sorry, but I've my index finger's health and my mouse's longevity to think of.All in all, I can see myself re-installing this game 3 times or so every year just to play for an hour to blast off some steam. It was a worthwhile purchase, and I can only hope the rest of the series, as well as other classic on-rail shooters potentially getting the similar kind of face-lifts.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard refund, and i never refund games, ever.But you have to draw a line somewhere.And I can also explain why that is so.First of all, I'm a huge HOTD fan. At the age of 21, I played the 1 arcade machine ad nauseam. Then onto Sega Saturn. And over time every part. So you can tell I mean it when I say HOTD is my favorite arcade machine of all time. And I think even the Sega Saturn port is better than this remake.I could overlook the laughable performance if the rest of the game was good, but it isn't. And by that I certainly don't mean the optics. The developers have put a lot of effort into this. But it's also the only one. I'm talking about gameplay here. And that's king in a game like this.Here's a list of things that are absolutely unforgivable after playing through the campaign four times.1- The zombies no longer have a dismemberment system. They disintegrate, but what has always distinguished House of the Dead games is that you can strategically sever body parts. It's not just a gimmick, it's really important in a game like this. In this remake, the zombies disintegrate after enough fire. Even if you just shoot the arm to disarm the ax thrower, it just vaporizes and doesn't lose the arm. Unless, of course, you are "lucky" that the animation randomly resolves this part of the body first.2- Which directly affects the difficulty level. In the original you can even see if someone is playing easy or hard. On easy you only have to shoot one or even no body part. On hard you have to disassemble the zombie into its individual parts so that it finally gives peace. I didn't notice the slightest difference between easy and arcade (the supposedly highest) level of difficulty.3- The hit detection is so bad that the bats usually need two hits. an opponent who appears in masses and who you should reliably kill with one hit, who swallows two hits at once is not a fun opponent. I really don't understand why you didn't just increase the amount.4- The enemies with the iron ball are now the real boss because you can no longer shoot the balls in flight. I tried, didn't shoot the zombie and just focused on the ball. Even after 4 tries I couldn't get the thing out of the air.5- The horde mode is a bad joke. Only the default zombies increase in number. Sometimes you get a hit from a zombie who isn't even in the picture. By that I mean no zombies other than the normal increases in number. No bats, no worms and most other zombies like the slimy green one or the zombies at the beginning under the bridge. That's the definition of laziness in development.6- As already mentioned, the performance is really bad. For example, I can play Borderlands 3 smoothly on my system in 1440p on high without frame drops. And BL3 is poorly optimized. In this mobile game my frames drop in inexplicable moments to 40 frames which immediately wipes out the playability.I could go on forever but I value my time more. Of course, at first I thought I was dramatizing, so I played the arcade machine. Two times in a row. It was fun and I'm sticking with this version now. All the other "little things" that are missing or made differently kill all the fun for me in this Remake.After the really crappy Panzer Dragoon Remake, the developers now have another classic Sega ip on their conscience. I never want to buy another game from them again. Because it's just not enough. Yes, the visuals are nice, but Sega games have always excelled primarily in gameplay, but that's apparently only the last priority in these remakes.I can only advise everyone to save the money. The price would be justified if it worked like a "26" year old game. But what was delivered here is just a soulless cash grab. Get the AM2 emulator and HOTD rom. You will have more fun with it.But what annoys me the most is that new generations are fobbed off with this version and think sega can't do good gameplay. If I had played House of the Dead for the first time with this remake, I would never play a Sega lightgun shooter again.And that's the real drama of this remake. It erases good games that were milestones in game development.

_childDocuments_.review: Stylistically it looks good, not much unlike later HOTD sequels (after 3 at least), but the overall visuals somehow make the dismemberment and holes on enemies less hard hitting and the ragdoll deaths grow boring too. Technically it's nothing to write home about, there are all kinds of low quality aspects yet it requires a pretty good PC to run well all the same (I have a 1080 and the game often hovers around 40fps when maxed out at 1440p, it really doesn't justify this visually). The menus don't really have a good arrangement or style to them either but that could be forgiven if the rest was ace.Gameplay wise it's a completely pointless release without a lightgun (cheap inferior Wii & Move/Aim style methods to ape one were neat 15 years ago but don't really cut it either and the same goes for potential gyro based controls on all platforms it's on like the Deck, since they still just move the crosshair rather than an FPS camera or similar).Idk what they were thinking choosing to remake this of all the Sega games they could have potentially asked for. Sure it’s technically a 3D on rails shooter like their Panzer Dragoon remake, but that was always gamepad based like Starfox or Sin & Punishment (incidentally the sequel had separate difficulty and leaderboards if you were playing it with a classic controller and analog sticks or the Wii remote, you just can't have all in one mode), you at least guide a character around like a 3D shoot 'em up and have to dodge enemy fire and obstacles and rotate the camera, not just drag some crosshair around compared to actually having to aim and shoot, without crosshair, fast and accurately as was the point of the original releases and their home ports that only a poor player 2 would play with a standard gamepad instead of a lightgun.It supports mouse controls but you can't turn the crosshair off so even if you do have a Sinden lightgun or similar device there's no optimal way to play it, plus the way enemies pop up/stall is clearly tuned to the console gamepad controls (and there are no separate leaderboards between that and mouse controls so you can tell who's gonna dominate those).They should have worked with the Sinden creator or made their own gun to bundle with the game and promise many more lightgun games to justify the accessory's up front cost (and also detect the device properly and give it its own leaderboards rather than lump them with the mouse/everyone). VR compatibility would be great too, with a digital recreation of a great arcade cabinet, of course only on PC (or Quest if it can be ported down to that level) and the coming PSVR2 as the current PSVR has the same problems I mentioned for Wii/Move and doesn't really cut it for lightgun precision & fun emulation.I really don't understand what gameplay value people find in twiddling their thumbs to move some crosshair around a screen (or do the same with their mouse, it's just point and click), it doesn't at all resemble the arcade experience it was made to be. There's no entertainment, there's no fun, there's nothing to see here. They need some sense slapped into them or something because they're increasing the ratings of something even they'll tire of in a couple more hours, guaranteed, because there's nothing to work with, you don't improve your reflexes or faux-real gun aiming skills or anything to make you keep going and trying to get better, advance further or finish it without the free play continues crutch, and so on like the original and every other self and player respecting lightgun shooter.Mind this is just the fundamentals, because there are also plenty more underlying gameplay issues, where in place of the finely tuned enemy encounters they've added randomized, invisible to the eye before they occur, elements, like varied speed and health on enemies so you can't properly prioritize threats and how you handle them because one enemy you'd normally down before they get to you is now going to be in your face in a split second or not go down with the amount of shots it should, so even under ideal circumstances, it's only by luck rather than skill and know how that you will be able to advance further or finish it on one credit, when everyone knows any arcade game should be first of all fair rather than feel like a coin muncher, even when said coins are free in a home version like this one. This is a disaster.Edit: so, you can disable crosshair but there's all kinds of other issues for the mouse-hijacking PC lightguns as shown in videos like this (plus what I said earlier about leaderboards etc. stands, but of course without a mass produced cheaper lightgun folks who even own a Sinden or Gun4IR are few and far between so that's what they should have remedied with a new Sega gun before attempting to offer such a game twisting it for gamepads/mouse):

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I want to thank the devs for remastering this masterpiece. I heard good things about the original The House Of The Dead but didn't get a chance to play it. Now that I experienced it, I can say that it is awesome. The game is a on-rails shooter. Zombies pop up from left and right and you have to kill them. This simple premise is what makes The House Of The Dead so enjoyable. In levels, you can save scientists. If you save them all, you unlock an armory. After that you can collect extra weapons like a grenade launcher and assault rifle. With extra weapons game becomes more enjoyable. It has two game modes, Original and Horde mode. The original is the classic experience. You play 4 levels on your desired difficulty and finish the game. In horde mode, the game becomes harder. Nearly every enemy encounter is doubled. You really need those extra weapons if you plan to survive in horde mode. Overall, it is really a great game. The level design, enemies, guns, soundtrack, every part of the game is excellent. I'm glad that I played it and now I can't wait for The House Of The Dead 2

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through this game twice on PC I have some mixed feelings on it. The optimization while better than on other platforms still isn't quite as good as it should be. For some users it crashes on AMD graphics, though I haven't experienced this myself on the 7900 XTX. Also while you can get native light gun support to, that's only available with a mod such as Argonlefou's Arcade Mod Plugin, and then you still need to run the game in borderless mode in order to allow the border to appear for the Sinden Light Gun(if you have that). It's definitely fast paced and fun to play, but there are points where the cheapest qualities of the arcade version still show. For example, the window to save civilians and NPCs is incredibly tight. It often requires perfect accuracy and timing. There's times where I still felt like enemies were getting cheap hits in on me. Also the majority of bosses have extremely tiny weak points which are hard to hit. The graphics and lighting are excellent, and the performance has been excellent on both PCs I've played it on, one with an RTX 3080 Ti and the other with an RX 7900 XTX. Again with the Sinden Light Gun, it's still a blast, for as cheap as the game can be at times(skill issue). I still love it, but get it on sale and if you have a light gun, get Argonlefou's Arcade Mod Plugin as well.

_childDocuments_.review: All things considered, this one turned out to be surprisingly decent.After seeing the Switch based premiere of the game I was afraid of the general graphical fidelity of it's eventual versions, but those doubts were quickly laid to rest after I finally tried the game by myself. The graphics are obviously not of AAA quality, but I was never expecting them to be. The game gets the job done in that department save for one aspect: the HUD. OH MY GOD IT'S SO FHOKKIN UGLY IT LOOKS LIKE WORDART IN BABY'S FIRST POWERPOINT PRESENTATION HOW CAN YOU PUT THIS MUCH EFFORT INTO RECREATING THE 3D WORLD OF A CLASSIC AND YET SOMEHOW SHIP THE GAME WITH THIS FECALLIC EXCUSE OF A HUD? POOP! Okay, moving on. The gameplay is a slightly different story. For a person who has played HotD 2 for a probably unhealthy amount of times back in the days and even nowadays occasionally, I found the gunplay to be too...floaty(?) and slow if that makes sense. You see, there's a maximum firing rate defined by the game and no matter how fast you give it inputs, your rate will never exceed the predefined limit. As a proud man who ghengrhaped Tower, Hierophant and Strength in both HotD 2's original story and it's Boss Mode more times than I could ever count just by spamming the primary fire as fast as I could I found that to be quite distracting. By floaty I mean both the weapon sound effects, the PS3/360-era almost Gmod-eque ragdoll physics and the slightly wonky player camera that always keeps focusing on the mutilated corpses of defeated enemies 2-3 seconds longer than it should. That last particular point kinda slows down the game's originally more frantic pace unnecessarily. Ah, pace killing that reminds me! Magician is absolutely crap in this version, a pathetic joke compared to it's original form, I should never be able to STUNLOCK MAGICIAN with medium effort of all things. Alright, a few positives: the voice acting is amazing and by amazing I mean that it's exactly the way it should be; needlessly overacted, campy and cheesy as ♥♥♥, just the way I like it. Be advised that the soundtrack of this game is not the same as the original as the devs couldn't get the rights to use it, instead they've decided to compose their own pieces that try to emulate the feel of the experience as much as possible. You could say that these tracks are more Daytona than HotD, they are definitely more goofy, melodious and less intense than they originally were, but I for one was not bothered by this change. They are absolutely not better than the originals, but they're, again surprisingly decent for something composed as a substitute. I particularly liked the basic "boss theme" that mixes instruments associated with retro gaming with more common instruments. It sounds like it came straight out of Shantae: Half Genie Hero and that's definitely not criticism.If they fix up the meh gunplay and the sluggish camera movement a little then I'm sure that the HotD 2 remake will be nothing short of amazing or at the very least considerably enjoyable, even if it won't have the original soundtrack.Now please, finish it up already, this edging is getting quite ridiculous! I want to suffer like G did!

_childDocuments_.review: ***This will be a quick review without my usual pros and cons list. This is one of two games I wish I owned the actual arcade (the other being Time Crisis). I loved it! _childDocuments_.review: I played the original a lot on Sega Saturn and in the arcade and this is a great remake! The pacing is snappy and perfectly tuned so that you're never bored nor overwhelmed.  The graphics really set the mood -- They may not be as slick as the Resident Evil 4 Remake, but this is still the best-looking lightgun game of all time (and I've played HotD5). Yes, the game is short (30 mins to complete) but there are a lot of branching paths, cheevos, and challenges to discover.  BUT nevermind that OCD completionist busywork: The reason why this game is worth getting is because they've made it damn fun to shoot and destroy monsters over and over.  Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake is a pretty good action, on rails shooter and a pretty nice remake of a classic arcade game. Now I've never really played the original game, except maybe when I was younger at the arcade and what I saw from youtube walkthroughs so I will still compare the remake to the original. So what is the story.In 1998 the AMS was involved in an incident involving the DBR Corporation and it's head researcher Dr Curien, two agents agent G and Thomas Rogan are sent to Dr Curien’s mansion after receiving a call of people being killed, they arrive to discover horror and carnage. Zombies and other bioengineered monsters roaming the area and there is only one man to blame Dr Curien, soon it's up to the two agents to stop Dr Curien and his mad ambitions.Okay then the likes, the gameplay is pretty good it's your simple on rails shooter fast-paced with monsters around every corner, but there's also a little expiration involved where you can pick a certain path that can change how you proceed to the boss. The graphics are really good with plenty of great detail, nice use of color and some very interesting set pieces with a lot of improvements on the original game. The levels are very good, it's almost a shot by shot remake of the original game, but a bunch more detail and little touches with scenery that just makes the place feel more alive and some parts just make you want to stop and stare at it.The enemies and bosses are really good; the remake does a great job in improving on the original designs of the creatures designs making them much more terrifying and gruesome. The story is pretty good and simple you basically shoot the monster until you get to the final boss, but compared to the original game, this one feels a bit more cinematic like in the opening level where Rogan opens the first door he shoots it and gives a little gun twirl, it's these little touches that just make it feel more cinematic.The music is good there are some nice soundtracks and the game gives you an option to play the original soundtrack or the new one which was good. The voice acting is good in the original it was pretty cheesy but this game well it still has some cheesiness in it, but it feels better acted, I especially like The Magicians voice.I also like that after beating the game there are little bios on the different creatures that you've encountered, I also like that there was a save system so if you messed up on getting some achievements you can just quit the game and play it where you left off which helped on getting certain achievements.Okay then the dislikes, the game can be very short if you're not going after any of the achievements. The price for the game is also too high I mean $25 for such a short game, maybe 10 bucks or 15 at best. I mean I could see it 20 if they included like the original game and maybe one of the spin-offs to it. Some of the achievements were such a pain to get the worst being invincible and no ammo wasted, Invincible completing the whole game without getting hurt was pretty hard due to the fact that enemies can be pretty cheap with their attacks if you're not really careful.The no ammo wasted where you're supposed to use all the ammo in the clip before reloading is really a pain because if you get hurt or if you are in a cutscene and you haven't reloaded your gun the game will automatically reload it for you which stops you from getting the achievement.Now then THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake is a pretty good action, on rails shooter and a pretty nice remake of a classic arcade game, so with pretty good gameplay, really good enemies and bosses and pretty good and simple story, I do recommend this game, but I also recommend getting it on sale so you can save some money like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: The House of the Dead's Remake is a lot of fun. They kept the goofy, oldschool horror aesthetic of the original and made it work really well, alongside keeping the fast and frenzied gunplay the original series is known for. It's extremely faithful to the original and added a lot of miscellaneous touches to make the game that much more endearing. It falls short in some areas and makes up for it in others. Slight spoiler warning if you care about that stuff.The gameplay is my favourite part of the game as enemies are suitably tanky, fast and will explode into various bits and pieces when destroyed. Though this time, instead of having distinctive death animations corresponding to how they were died, zombies just ragdoll. I can see why people would think it's lazy but unloading the assault rifle into a zombie and watching it fly 50 feet is so endearing to me. There are also new modes in the game such as Horde Mode. House of the Dead with more Dead™. I found this mode to be a stupid amount of fun after playing the series for decades, though it is pretty unbalanced. You will get hit by offscreen enemies constantly.  Alongside that, there is the Modern™ scoring system which rewards killing quickly and upholding a short-term combo that acts as a multiplier. I've had so much fun absolutely wailing on a corpse to bridge the gap between enemy spawns so I can earn more points. It's a great touch. However, some enemies in the remake are just unfun and some of the original enemy placements do not work here. For example, the half-metal zombie Robert sucks wherever he's placed. For some reason they made him way too fast for his bulk so you're almost destined to take a hit. In the same vein, the bosses are not as fun as they used to be. However Hangedman is one million times better than he used to be. Mostly due to the game's updated graphics. The graphics in this game are phenomenal with, not only a massive level of care to make every area exciting and unique, but numerous minute details to make Curien's Mansion look far more ravaged. The game's lighting also deserves a mention as it makes every area visually lively, something the original couldn't do with its hardware. Moreover, the original House of the Dead games give each enemy type its own character through its distinguished artstyle, which this remake does beautifully. Even in the bloody piles they collapse into. However, the remake isn't without its drawbacks.Every game in the original series has strong sound design to tie the games together, suiting the general vibe of each game perfectly. The remake has some of the worst mixing in a video game. First off, the music. I could barely tell what the tracks were because, with default settings, the tracks get completely buried under the sheer volume of sound effects, alongside sounding really thin and flat. Some sounds absolutely scream at the player for no discernible reason and heavily detract from the experience. The guns sound awful too. They do the damage they're supposed to but sound like toy guns you would buy on holiday for a fiver. I cannot truly believe a gun that sounds that small would be able to completely rip apart a mutated human being. On the other hand, the zombies sound pretty good. I can't complain about that. The voice acting is as cheesy as I wanted to be too, though decently better than the original. I can't complain about that either.- The scientists are now their own people and not reused character models, and killed scientists have their faces crossed out in the chapter end screen. Good stuff. - You can view the different zombie types in a gallery, where each of them have animations and sounds unique to the gallery. Bosses too. - The gallery can also be used to view acquired guns and achievements. Putting the achievements in a medal box makes me feel like I've actually done something with my day by collecting them.- - The zombies now have facial expressions and not flat textures. I love killing something that looks annoyed at me. - Unlocking the armoury causes weapon cases to spawn on repeat playthroughs, adding a lot of replay value beyond the branching paths the series is known for. - There is now a level select screen. I don't have to play through the entire game to replay a single chapter.  The Remake does a lot of things right. I love the gameplay and the art style, I love the voice acting and character models, and the UI is really easy to use and navigate. Unfortunately the sound design really falls short, and there is some gameplay jank. On the whole, it's a lot of fun and stays true to the original series.

_childDocuments_.review: My play time is 75% trying to get this running with my Sinden light gun properly - I'm glad I waited for the sale (50% off) but honestly that is too much to pay.First off the game is playable with a mouse but if you want to play with a light gun it'll require fan fixes to get it going - why are these not supported! Secondly the game is incredibly short <30mins to complete - that said there are alternative/hidden routes depending on player choices and if you can save the scientists to provide keycards etc but players might also get joy from going back and beating their previous scores but that is it.I completed the game but only got one of the achievements - despite there being standard ones for beating bosses, finishing the game etc - possibly due to having to use the fan fixes? Also there is a typo in the achievement description for: "Reinforcements!: Let Player 2 join the game while in a middle of a campaing."Anyway regarding gameplay - as others have stated it is janky - enemies spawn in places and attack you before you can take a shot, sometimes they just stand and wait to get shot or will already be dead before they appear on screen.Some enemies will take varying damage depending on when you fight them on one 'screen' an enemy might require require two shots to kill or for their head to be blown off but on the next screen that exact same enemy type will require four or five shots before being killed even if you take their head off first and the final boss literally throws attacks at you that are the same colour as the skybox behind it (depending on where it maneuvers) so they are incredibly difficult to hit. The code/project files for the original game were lost in time therefore the developers had to remake this from the ground up - they really could have improved the experience and revamped this series. The developers are actively working on remaking the sequel at the moment (honestly after this I'd prefer a straight port of the Wii version of HotD 2 & 3 instead of a full remake) but hopefully they are able to take player feedback into consideration and develop it to a much higher standard and then come back and polish up this game. I will likely return to it as a party game when having friends round - hence having a light gun but that said House of the Dead Overkill is far far far superior to this game in every way.If you are interested in playing House of the Dead, I'd suggest getting an abandonware version/emulating it rather than suffering with this remake OR if you just have to try this version wait for a 75/80% off sale unless the developers really make an effort to patch this game.

But low and behold they were smart and decided to release it for everything else, of course what i looked forward to most was the PC, meaning that modding could take place, which also mean't that you could potentially play with the Classic Sounds and Music... and thankfully that mod was made it is known as "HOTD1 Classic Sounds and Music Mod" which you can get off of Nexus and it's as simple as extracting the file into the main file where the HOTD exe is. _childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent remake! I originally thought with Forever Entertainment using the Unity engine to make this game that it wasn't going to look or run very good, but I was wrong. A lot of the graphical updates are perfect modern reimaginings, while keeping the pacing and level design exactly the same as the Arcade original.The only things I found really weird and out of place (odd considering it's HotD) was the complete lack of the original music! The new music is just new stuff that VAGUELY sounds HotD-ish. I thought SEGA had all the rights to their in-house music? Also, NO NATIVE LIGHTGUN SUPPORT?! NO NATIVE RAW MOUSE INPUT SUPPORT for a LIGHTGUN game?!I understand no one makes lightguns for consoles or PC these days, but with the fairly recent release of both Sinden Lightgun and Gun4IR, you'd think Forever Entertainment would try to contact them to let them implement their Lightgun controllers natively into HotD: R. Maybe in a future patch?Until then, the modding community has come through again with Mystery's Single Lightgun and Multiplayer Lightgun patches for HotD: R. You can find links to his patches in the community guides.Overall, as a huge fan of HotD, and lightgun games in general, I give this a 8/10. FE should've tried harder to implement modern lightguns out of the box, since they were remaking a lightgun game, but it is what it is. If you loved the Arcade original, I can't recommend this game enough! If you never had any experience with arcades or lightgun games, this 30-minute game may not interest you at all, but like most games, it's definitely better playing multiplayer with a friend! It's just a shame they didn't implement ONLINE!

_childDocuments_.review: So right off the bat, just got to say this game is a mixed bag of both good and bad for me. In terms of classic House of The Dead they certainly have done a good job re-creating everything to be 1:1 so far. The biggest con in my eyes is the length of the game. It's not bad, just feels like it needs more if its going to be priced at 25$. I know that may sound petty, but these kinds of games even on the market for Wii was only worth 10$ 1&2 separately. So for that price they could have done House of The Dead 1&2 together and maybe brought the price up to 30$ (15$ each) since they put effort into keeping it true to the original. I remember back on House of The Dead 2 you had to fight your way through the Town, Coliseum, Canals, and then finally make it all the way to Goldman's tower. Now I know that this is the Remake of 1, though it feels more of a remaster. It feels super short no matter what difficulty you are on. I never really got to play the original and with rail arcade shooters they are not meant to be overly long. But I think they should really tie in 2 be it a DLC/Update or a separate game. I would say it would be best to tie in as a DLC so I can justify keeping it. I totally recommend getting it to play. Since it will roughly take 1 hour or less to beat. And if you don't feel satisfied you can refund it no problem. It only took me 48 minutes because I restarted the story a few times trying to get co-op to work (still can't but I will figure it out eventually). Sometimes there is an audio glitch or two. The intro bugged out and I couldn't hear anything until the game started. Other than that the amount of time you will put in will most likely be trying to get the 3 endings. All of which are based on your score and actions. Long-term replay-ability might or it might not last, even though horde mode does exist. Overall a cult-classic that I am happy to have come back to life. Wish I had a Gun-Con for this, though I don't know if there even is one that is made for modern tech (I am a bit out of time in this aspect because I still have the original Gun-Con that requires old-school box TV's). I look forward to seeing more Classic Rail shooters make a return (Time crisis and etc.). But overall was fun for a quick moment.
_childDocuments_.name: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD: Remake

_childDocuments_.review: This is the same game I used to play when I was 12 during the hot summer nights spent at the arcade by the seaside. What a time to be alive, truly joyful memories. Many people have moved on since then and arcades have closed down so this is all that remains of an era that may very well never come back anymore. So any little tidbit of nostalgia is a treasure, whnever its actually being crafted with love and care.All in all I think this remake is not only faithful to the original but also not too fancy so it strikes a good balance between what is being expected by fans and a relatively "new" product for newcomers to enjoy.Having "aim assist" and "auto reload" is kind of insulting but I understand gamers nowadays have been spoonfed by devs all their life and their brains are slower than us kids back then, so I'll try not to puke, nor laugh (too loudly).In any event, the game has some bugs. I could not unlock 2 achievements despite meeting the requirements and the game refused to recognize my keyboard while typing the agent's name at the end of the game, both of which were pretty annoying but not gamebreaking by any means.It feels strange that the framerate is sometimes a bit floaty considering I'm using a RTX3070 to run a Switch game, but alas that's what we got.I wont lie, playing this just made me wish even more for a comeback of the arcades.

_childDocuments_.review: you can really tell this was the first HOTD game.- It's short, 4 levels in total. My fastest run so far is about 30-40 minutes on the hardest difficulty, which you'll notice is half my current play time. I've beaten it twice in just over an hour, there's 3 endings based on your score and overall performance.- there are minimal paths in each level, and when they do deviate it's really not by much, ultimately it ends up being a longer route vs a shortcut. Good for speedrunners maybe if that's a thing for this game?- something just feels, off... about the hit registration. definitely feels different to the old arcade cabinets and not just because there's no physical gun.- the harder the difficulty you play on, the more unavoidable attacks seem to happen. really feels like being back at an arcade playing a game designed to yoink as much coinage from your pocket as possible lmao- some of the subtitles have spelling mistakes currently. It's mildly hilarious to me.- the audio has a hardcoded dynamic volume effect. firing off a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of shots will dramatically lower the volume of everything else completely. the zombie sounds disappear so you might miss important audio cues and the music is vanishes. it kind of sucks, i dont know why this is a thing. games haven't had limited sound channels since the early 90's so i don't see the reason to basically limit the amount of sounds that can be heard, because if you shoot fast enough all you'll hear is your gun and bullet ricochets. maybe that's just "realistic" though idk lolanyway, onto the good things:- boy howdy is this a nostalgia trip. i love it. Even if you never played the original, this is still a great on-rails shooter.- there's an autoreload option if you want that for whatever reason- the games visual update is pretty nice, the animations stay mostly faithful to the janky feel of the late 90's and all the iconic zombie types are still recognisable.- the bad script writing is still cheesy as hell.- horde mode is ridiculously more fun than the normal campaign.- a decent range of achievements from easy to achieve to seemingly impossible- good old fashioned in-game cheats are unlocked based on how many achievements you have. Alternatively, there are codes you can use to instantly unlock them, like infinite ammo etc- as much as i've missed the RELOAD RELOAD RELOAD RELOAD RELOAD shouts... i'm glad the option to turn it off is in the base game and didn't have to be patched in. that's good thinking- The sound track is as i remember. hits me right in the memories, though i will say, HOTD2 had the better OST in every way, especially the Magician fight- The game actually has support for ultrawide resolutions... how does this game have it but certain triple A titles don't. ♥♥♥♥♥♥ whatTL:DR: Overall, still an amazing game, but a bit pricey considering how short it is. This was a relatively long game back when it first released, nowadays, not so much. Please HOTD 2 + 3 next, and Vampire Night

_childDocuments_.review: Without SEGA AM1 (WOW Entertainment / R&D #1), the game seems like a bit off. The animations are not as smooth as the original, but this is acceptable. In the horde mode, the camera can be swayed and point in opposition to attacking zombies. Thus, you cannot shoot those attacking zombie. "Reload" warning voices are so toxic to my ears.Weapons in the game are very limit compared to the original mode in the House of the Dead 2. Most short hair female scientists are having the same face; this is a lack of creativity. Were you guy lazy? I realized that their faces look like characters from Telltale Games; especially their eyes.Sadly, when a player shot a scientist, there is no 'MISSED SHOT' in a red X symbol as the classic, plus an unlucky guy body blends in a pile of zombie corpses. So, you won't notice your sin easily. Ragdoll physics makes the game becomes more realistic, but a bouncing dead zombie can block a bullet traveling. There was a case study in Time Crisis 5; the same problem.The most disappointment is the Magician; he is not as fast as the 1996, especially the close attacking movement. However, this game is not expensive for trying, but it is not very compatible with a light gun compared to emulated HOD: Scarlett Dawn with Jconfig in PC. Using a mouse will be a better choice (or use a cat if you like).In conclusion, it isn't bad. Just buy and try it by youself.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time experiencing The house of the Dead and I can testify that it is an awesome rail shooter.While the campaign is initially short, multiple pathways lead to a decent amount of variety on subsequent playthroughs. There are two scoring systems that also change how you approach the game : The classical scoring system rewarding more points for headshots, scientist saves and not getting hit.The modern scoring system rewarding more points for quick eliminations of the enemies and removing any way of loosing points (except if you find yourself in a situation where you need to pay points to buy a continue coin).In addition to that there is also a marketed Horde Mode which basically just adds in a bunch more enemies on screen on certain moments of the game. Meanwhile it initially can be fun to mow down a horde I found out that the mode doesn't really add that much to the game and even partially ruins the experience. Sometimes less is simply more.Speaking of less I believe that the biggest flaw of the game is it's price. I hope that most nostalgia seeking people or simply fans of the genre can cope with the initial entry price but I believe that at face value The house of the Dead remake is still a bit too steeply priced.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, this is not perfect. But for what it is, it is worth it.I'd gladly blame nostalgia for my love for the remake, but this is different looking, sounding, and even playing, really, that I can honestly say it stands on it's own.I don't use lightguns, i'd love to, but those are expensive. I play my railshooters with my mouse, and the game works perfectly for it, just like the pc port of the original.The only real downside, imo, is the soundtrack. It had a lot of care put into it, but it's competing with one of the best soundtracks I have ever heard, especially for a zombie game. It sounds game-ier and like a halloween attraction. It's just not as good, while not being bad, it was competing with something too powerful.There's some slowdown, namely in the factory floor path, but it's rare, and it shouldn't get in your way. Some graphic stuff is weird, it all has modder's sheen, some models aren't that great, some lighting is EH.But the gameplay is exactly what it should be, and it's so fun.If you're a fan, I do recommend it. If you're a real strickler for lightgun compat, wait until they fix it, if they can.

name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance
detailed_description: A NEW LEGACY BEGINS... Experience the massively popular world of Baldur's Gate as never before. Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance thrusts you into an epic Dungeons & Dragons adventure filled with intense action, intricate puzzles and sinister intrigue, where your mastery of cold steel and devastating spells is the only thing between you and ultimate evil. • A ground-breaking adventure, featuring the 3rd Edition Dungeons & Dragons® rule set. • Explosive spell effects and incredibly detailed creatures and environments deliver a more realistic gaming experience. • Three customizable characters, each with distinctive powers, appearances and abilities that develop throughout the game. • Battle alone or join a friend in two-player cooperative mode. • Explore Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance all over again, experiencing newfound adventures with a different customized character or replaying in Extreme mode for ten times the difficulty and fun. • Dolby Surround sound, real-time sound effect mixing, Hollywood voice talent and an original soundtrack by acclaimed composer Jeremy Soule.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to work at a EB Games store over 10 years ago. My boss was working behind the counter, handling some trade ins for a customer that had a stack of old PS2 and original Xbox games from his closed down video store. He went through them all until he got to a certain game which popped up with the trade in value of nothing. He told the customer it was worthless and the customer told him to keep it for free.The boss looked at it for a while then saw him throw it into the bin out the back as he couldn't do anything with it.It was this game. I was glad I pulled it out and saved it.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite old Hack n' Slash titles from the PS2 era with an amazing soundtrack by Jeremy Soule. If you wanted to play couch co-op Diablo with a friend, this was it. The port seems serviceable, though not a lot has been enhanced or improved since the 2001 release. This unfortunately means that while a bunch of new resolution options are available to you, you're still going to see blurry UI elements and a few low bitrate FMV cutscenes that were compressed to fit on a PS2 disc. It's no big deal, but with such a barebones re-release being done to a game that could frankly use some enhancement, there isn't a ton of incentive to choose this over an ISO. Give us some achievements or something. While I loved this game, it was outclassed by Snowblind's next ARPG Champions of Norrath, which improved on this title in every way. Let's hope we get a Steam release of that next. Recommending because I want more Snowblind Studios games on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me point out that this negative rating isn't for the game. The game is great! It's perfect. It's like a D&D campaign, but just for you. It's a very non-offensive game that can run on any PC, doesn't take much space, and is also coop. Supposedly. If both parties involved have controllers. My only criticisms lie with the game's original issues and a singular crash, so far. HOWEVER, that aside, it isn't worth thirty dollars.This game is as of the moment, quite literally, TWO DECADES OLD. This game should be half the price. It's also an abysmal port. The UI looks like it's been glazed over with Vaseline and character selection screen looks like a 240p Youtube video. It's embarrassing and lazy. This is not a remaster, but it definitely should be, as that would at least justify the price over this blatant nostalgia cash grab. As I stated earlier the original issues this game had still function here, though these are mostly balancing issues. The game was beatable back in the day and still is now. They could have at the very least included "quality of life" improvements, like take for example, the map. I think being able to summon a map on screen is great, but why not add a full blown map to the in-game menu for the areas you've explored? That way you can see the entire landscape instead of just a fraction of it when you move around. Also, I feel it's worth mentioning this game has Remote Play, which is nice, but much like the old PS2 title, both players are locked into a certain radius of each other. If one stops moving the camera locks off the other player. This can get your partner or you trapped and then killed. On ye' olden PS2 this made sense and while annoying it didn't feel wrong; you guys were right next to each other in real life looking at the same screen. Remote Play, to be fair, is effectively emulating being next to someone while playing with them, but you're still staring at two different screens AWAY from each other. It's weird. This last bit isn't a criticism, just something I wish could be altered, but I assume this is more a limitation of Remote Play than it is fault not considered by the developer's of this game. I would naturally conclude this by saying "Wait for it to go on sale," but sadly if this game is anything like the early access game that is Baldur's Gate 3 it probably won't ever actually see a drop in price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games from my childhood but for anyone having an issue with the game playing faster than normal all you need to do is limit the frame rate to 60fps in nvidia control panel. Go into NVIDIA Control Panel > Manage 3D Settings > Program Settings. Select the Dark Alliance Executable. Look for Max Frame Rate option. Set to 60 FPS.Hopefully this helps someone. :)

_childDocuments_.review: It's the same Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance from the PS2 and Xbox era. It's a good game. But the PC port is lazy and I would say terrible. From what I saw it runs ok. But there are no graphics options, not even a resolution option. I don't even know what resolution it's running at. The HUD is all blurry. This has to be one of the laziest PC ports I have ever seen. I was looking forward to this port. I was pretty excited for it actually. This game, the sequel and the two Champions games on the PS2 were my favorite ARPG's on the PS2 and they were the only good Western themed ARPG's on the system. If you wanted good ARPG's you had no choice. Otherwise it was just weeb JRPG's. Yes I paid $30 for this game. But I refunded it. I already have it on the Switch and with the Switch's smaller screen it looks better on there. I can't recommend this port especially at this price. It's far too lazy to justify the $30 price tag. As PC gamers we expect to at least seem some graphics options. At least a resolution setting. Do no buy this port for the current price. If you just have to buy it then at least wait for sale. It's extremely lazy. You have been warned.  It's more like a $10-$15 game than $30.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a straight port of a 20 year old B-tier console game. Not a remake or a remaster. They got it running on modern hardware, included some VERY minimal tweaks to the graphics to account for the fact that nobody is playing on a square CRT anymore and released it. So for the people who've been commenting on the dated graphics, yes: it is, indeed, graphically inferior to whichever triple-A titles that released a decade or more later you wish to compare it to.As ports go, it's been a pretty good one. I've encountered no bugs or stuttering or anything of the like and I'm at the final boss right now (taking a break from getting stomped). Other people tell a different tale but I can only speak to my own experience. If you're looking for a true RPG experience (Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, etc) then this isn't really it. This is very much a hack & slash kind of game with some light RPG elements. And a somewhat simple one, at that. It's fun, though. And challenging.Just... good god.  I  it wasn't this hard back in the day.  I'm  of it...Oh, and I should probably mention that it's a bit short.  I'm at the final boss 11.3 hours in and I spent about an hour, collectively, grinding.

_childDocuments_.review: FIRST IMPRESSIONS:This is a fascinating, unexpected release. These are some of my FAVORITE PS2 games, and I love to see them getting more love. Especially with Mac and Linux support, too. But there are a ton of quirks.The Xbox models are used here, which means you have some very mid-2000s "HD" looking character models with very NOT HD looking environments, etc. stands out very weirdly. Emphasizes the boob physics, too.You have ZERO video options. You can alt-enter to go windowed, but you get what it gives you. It DOES support ultrawide, which is incredible, but the character select menu gets cropped off.Sound is super compressed and crunchy. The sound quality is one of the defining features of this engine for me - I play it regularly on PS2 with surround sound and it sounds great - this copy does not. This could be due to the Dolby encoding not playing back properly natively on my PC.Mouse and keyboard controls are surprisingly intuitive.This appears to be using OpenGL - which means you may have a hard time hooking it for capture.I am very suspicious that some emulation trickery is happening here. I'm not mad about it, just hope it's above-board. I would LOVE for them to release the second one like this with save porting, and then move on to Champions of Norrath and Champions Return to Arms. I have always said I would still buy new games today using this engine - the soundscapes are incredible, the visuals are wonderful with realistic water effects, awesome particles, and glowy lighting. I'd love to see a return of this era.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.Simple plot, simple characters, simple controls. Just good, old fashioned hack n slash dungeon crawling fun.Before I go further it's important to note that Baldur's Gate is a city in the Forgotten Realms setting of Dungeons & Dragons. The Dark Alliance games have NOTHING to do with the Baldur's Gate series of games made by Bioware/Larian other than the name of the city the 2 series of games take place in.Plays mostly like an ARPG but for some reason doesn't really feel exactly like one. Partially because of the controls. You can WASD your character for a start. You can customize keyboard controls which I did for a few controls that seemed a little inconvenient to press while using WASD. I also switched things that I've used as a standard for years like changing jump to space bar. *default: z (so this one falls into both categories.)So far I've only really played Kromlech.Leveling sometimes gives you a point in one of your core stats and each level you get points to spend on passive and active abilities. (As well as additional health/mana) Each one has improved benefits per tier and costs more points each tier. You also don't get piles of gear thrown at you like most ARPGs. Each act has a hub and each hub has a vendor. The vendor usually sells about 3 sets of armor and a decent variety of weapons. The first vendor only sells a few magic weapons. You won't be upgrading constantly, but steadily and usually in small increments. In Act one I was mostly saving up for the set of Scale armor. (And the flaming long sword that I got as a reward at the end of Act I anyway.) I will mention there's no manual and there's more than a few things you'll probably be scratching your head about. 'of disruption' I believe will give a chance to completely disintegrate an undead opponent if you get a critical hit. A weapon that's "keen" gives a higher chance to score a critical hit.Voice acting is decent enough, as is the music. Nothing spectacular, nothing too terrible. I think some of its biggest strengths lie in its relative simplicity and decent design choices. Since you'll be doing a lot of selling of items you find, you're given a staircase back to the hub/city every couple of levels which are fairly small, fairly linear, and easy to navigate. You'll also start to get recall potions which allow you to instantly teleport back to your hub (changes per act) where your vendor and quest givers are. When you're done, simply hit recall again and you'll be teleported back to the spot you left from. So you won't find an amazing, heart wrenching story or characters you'd give your life to save here, but what you will find is a pretty fun hack n slash game, now remastered and free from consoles. Highly recommend if you're into that sort of thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance has been one of my all-time favorite games since I was very young and it was a wonderful surprise to find out that it was being ported to PC. I've always wanted my fiance to have the experience of playing this game as well, so imagine my thrill on finding that it's Remote Play compatible, according to the store page! Unfortunately, when we started the game, the Two Player button was inactive and no matter what we did to try to activate it, nothing worked. Initially, I was fine with the fact that the game is $30 because unlike other gamers, I CAN be lured by nostalgia to pay even up to full price for a game that I absolutely love. But after being misled by the store page, I began to feel disappointed by other aspects, too - namely the fact that you're being asked to pay 30 bucks for what you can do with a free emulator - nothing has been polished, nothing has been updated, and the tutorial is clunky and over-informative. (As an aside: if you're playing with headphones the Black Isle Studios screen knife-f***s your ears each and every time you start the game because it sounds just... so awful.) I love this game and put many hours into it as a geeky lil preteen, and would no doubt put many more hours into it now on PC, but until they can make this version of the game more enticing than the GameCube version that I still have, I won't be coming back to it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, redundant, and ridiculous. Usually when an older game has dated game play mechanics you chalk it up to it being an older game, but a lot of the stuff that makes Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance irritating was irritating when the game first came out.As a kid I couldn't figure out why this game was difficult, but as an adult I actually see specific things that make the game overly hard and redundant. You start by picking from one of three characters, your generic archer, sorceress and warrior. This was originally a GameCube game, so the first thing you notice is that the graphics are great, with very rounded textures and shaders making it feel incredibly polished. The game still looks really good when you consider the fact that it came out decades ago. As for the story... there really isn't one. Baldur's Gate is just the name of the town you start in, it's like if a Legend of Zelda game was titled "Hyrule." But even though the stream-of-consciousness narrative takes some weird turns I could only understand why the game was titled "Dark Alliance" by reading a plot synopsis on Wikipedia, and at that point I cracked up because it made the whole game feel like one big joke. With that said, the game is very faithful to D&D-style lore. It's your basic hack and slash, though you'll only level about fifteen times before you complete the game. Not only is leveling difficult, but the skills cost so many skill points that often you have to skip adding skill points for one level so you can get double for the next to buy the ability you prefer. This makes the game feel redundant, since you only end up getting two or three total abilities by the end of the game. The warrior is by far the strongest and best character. There is an exploit in both Dark Alliance games wherein attacking the enemies from the side is actually more effective than blocking. The enemies are programmed to turn like automobiles for some reason, so if you can attack them as they're turning to attack you you can dispatch them easily. You also get a jump button, and this is something that was highly innovative at the time, believe it or not. What's not innovative is the backtracking and terrible camera. Enemies will often one-shot kill the player by attacking from off screen with a thrown weapon. In some areas, the camera is fixed, other times it's pointed in precisely the wrong direction. Also, you don't get town portal warps like in games like Diablo, so you have to walk all the way back to the towns to sell your gear. This is the reason the archer character is the worst character to play as. Arrows are heavy, so you have to back track to the town every few minutes to replenish them. At the end of the game I didn't have enough arrows to complete the first floor of the final dungeon (You can't go back to the town at this point) so the only way I could beat it by running past all the enemies.And the final boss can only be defeated with a melee weapon anyway, so it makes most of the levelling and skill building you've done up to that point seem pointless. All that really matters is how many health potions and how much armor you have stocked up since the class types are fixed. The sorceress is probably the most fun to play as, but you don't get access to more than one or two skills to play around with until the end of the game. She gets a little sword that auto-attacks enemies like a pet while you use other magic attacks to dispatch foes, plus she has ranged and area of effect attacks. Once you beat the game you can attempt "the gauntlet", which has you playing as Drizzt from D&D lore to clear ten rooms in fifteen minutes. Then you unlock extreme mode, which lets you continue leveling your character to see what the higher level skills look like. Actually, if you become skilled at running past the weak foes, you can beat the bosses with little effort since most of them have avoidable attacks. So really you could complete much of this game without levelling and instead just rushing through the dungeons to face the bosses. With that said, there's a decent amount of content here and the game is polished enough to recommend playing, but you can expect to get frustrated because the game is designed to frustrate you, and you'll probably be somewhat disappointed that you have to play through the game two or three times to really experience the full effect of the robust skill options the game offers.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing on PS2. It was even better with graphical enhancements via PCSX2 emulation but took some performance hits to do so. The port to PC blows them away! It is impressive how good the original game assets look without the limitations of the original PS2 GPU. This game is a timeless classic.  It has great replay value; at least once for each character class. It takes more than one play-through to really understand how to best leverage the different skills of each character. I can only hope that Dark Alliance II will also be ported to PC.

_childDocuments_.review: - Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance is an absolute classic! I remember battling through dungeons with my brother for hours on end with this masterpiece. Our playstation 2 ran so hot because we'd leave the game running 24/7 until we finally beat it. They don't make games like this anymore, not even in the same series. The sequel was also a great game but they have long since stepped away from their classic d&d roots when they made Dark Alliance 3. - This game is the perfect hack and slash for both casual and hardcore players. The soundtrack and having full voice acting is amazing! Despite its age, the graphics hold up in my opinion for this genre of game. We used to play on a small tv with a low resolution so honestly, it looks much better these days than it ever did. This port in my experience has been flawless except for one thing that I will get to shortly. - The game runs smooth and the controls feel natural on mouse and keyboard. I was surprised by how well it played with keyboard/mouse, but I bet it would be more enjoyable using a controller. This leads to the one thing I dislike about this PC version of Dark Alliance; as of the time of this post, you need a controller in order to play co-op someone. I purchased this game initially to play with a friend only to find out that we can't play co-op with keyboard/mouse. I hope they add in that support, I don't really understand why hasn't been implemented when playing single player has worked perfectly.- If you haven't played this before and aren't for its nostalgia surge, I highly recommend giving this gem a try! If you are a fan of any of the Forgotten Realms games like Neverwinter Nights and Baldur's Gate 1&2 or other hack and slashers like Diablo, you will more than likely fall in love with this game. You may even yourself crossing your fingers like me for a port of Dark Alliance 2! In addition to the sequel, I look forward to a port of Champions of Norath. That game is another absolute RPG masterpiece.- There is a fair amount of replayability with Dark Alliance, playing on Hard difficulty on a new character can be very challenging but also rewarding with better loot!- "Transferring" characters from one game to another is possible (i.e. if you decide you want to keep your character and their gear and play again on Hard after you've beaten the game.)- When you finish the game on Hard difficulty there is a secret that is unlocked. I will not spoil it and I'd advise you to not spoil it for yourself either. Let's just say that fans of D&D will love it and will want to play the game again because of it.- Note my played hours would probably be well over 100 hours, we played it quite a bit when it first came out. My playtime will double if they add in co-op support for keyboard mouse users. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot, but I have a lot of nostalgia for it from my childhood. While I personally enjoy it and will continue to play it, I don't know if I can recommend it to strangers on Steam. Not for $30. I think $15 would be a much more reasonable price for a port of a game from 2001. The current devs seem to have done some bugfixes, and I haven't experienced any noticeable bugs in my first playthrough. But outside of some improved textures, there don't seem to be any major changes or improvements to this 20+ year-old game; this is a port, not a remaster, so temper your expectations accordingly. As for the game itself, I enjoy it, but there are certainly better ARPGs, and much better introductions to the Forgotten Realms (e.g. this is a Baldur's Gate game in name only). The story is paper-thin (lore is practically nonexistent), the gameplay is simplistic, and the difficulty can be punishing without exploits. It's good for mindless hack'n'slash gameplay, but aside from sparse opportunities to lead enemies into traps, your only options are a) basic attack, b) special attack until you run out of mana, or c) run away. Since the weakest mobs can kill you in a couple hits, you'll want to grind levels or cheese the enemy AI to gain a decent footing. And by grind, I mean play as far as you can before you hit a difficulty wall, then import that character to a new save and start the whole damn game over - rinse and repeat until the game is comfortable. You will be constantly chugging potions, or if you're stingy like me, waiting to slowly regenerate health and mana. I took those opportunities to take a ♥♥♥♥ or do some push-ups or check my phone, but the fact is, there's a lot of waiting. Looting and leveling is fun, but leveling is slow, and once you have the best equipment in your zone, gold has no purpose and quickly piles up. Would be nice if you could buy "XP Potions" or if weapons had durability, some kind of goldsink. I don't want to bag on this game too much, but it's pretty bare-bones. If you played it when it came out, or you're a big fan of Diablo-clones or Forgotten Realms, maybe pick it up on sale. Just don't expect complex game design or modern polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Baldur's gate Dark Alliance is a classic from the sixth generation consoles. If you enjoyed it back then or want to pick it up for nostalgia sake or don't want to mess with setting up an emulator, this is an easy recommendation.But what if you're new to this game? what does a 20 year old game have to offer someone who has never seen or even heard of Dark Alliance? While I wouldn't consider myself an expert, I have played the Dark Alliance (and Champions of Norrath) games every year for over 10 years now. So what is Dark Alliance? Unlike it's PC predecessors, Dark Alliance is a hack n slash Arpg with local co-op support for 2 players. Don't let the Baldur's gate comparison scare you away though, Dark Alliance takes the setting of the famous city and little else from the PC titles apart from some sprinkles of lore for those who are familiar with the forgotten realms. On its own its a solid if not short game, a complete playthrough should take you about 8-10 hours. It has some replay value in the form of a secret unlockable character and the extreme difficulty that comes with them.Dark Alliance looked amazing when it was released back in 2001 and it looks great now on pc, however technical sacrifices had to be made to put it on the consoles it released on. Because of this modern Arpg players might find Dark Alliance a bit slow. The original game couldn't render a ton of fast paced enemies and effects all at once so its a much more methodical experience. If you're used to mowing down hordes of enemies in PoE or Diablo just keep that in mind.In closing: if you're a fan of the forgetten realms and don't mind a slower placed Arpg and/or you have a friend to kill some time with this game is worth a play.

Some great game physics for a game that came out in the early  2000. There are a few players that might call this game a health potion simulator because you will have to use a lot of health potions if you want to beat this game. On another note the Developer's clearly stated this game was a rerelease, not a remaster, not a remake. So don't expect anything major beside upscaled resolution and uncapped framerate. The price for this game is quite expensive for a game that came out 20 years ago but i'm just glad that it got a port.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Version:This is a good, reliable port of a classic Hack and Slash game from the PS2 era. It's a fully 3d,  top-down, looter RPG with an adjustable rotating camera which smoothly slides to first person when you talk to NPCs who are fully voice-acted. The game just works. I didn't adjust anything or change any settings; I just turned it on and it worked! (Remember when games used to be like that?)If you have played Champions of Norrath, this game is basically the same as of one of those minus the character creator, having been produced at about the same time by the same people. Rather than the world of Everquest however, this game is set in the D&D universe. You get three characters to choose from, Dwarf, Elf or Ranger. You get a cutscene which doesn't go well for your character...after which you get a simple series of hack and slash tasks from talking to the innkeeper that begins to unravel a conspiracy. This is simple, old-school loot RPG; NOT Mass Effect.The game is fairly straightforward and doesn't waste your time with a lot of tutorials. Complexity-wise, it's closer to Borderlands than Mass Effect. Having played several ARPGs including Grim Dawn, The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing, Victor Vran, etc. I can say that this one is pretty well-done. It lacks the dodge-rolls and souls-like elements of some newer ARPGs but it holds up very well and is easy to get into. This game has a very 90s fantasy aesthetic in how the female characters are designed. This doesn't bother me but if you are bothered by it, fair warning. There isn't any sex or nudity in it so don't avoid it (or buy it) for that.Usually when I turn on a game, I take for granted that I am going to have to tinker with it and adjust some things before I start playing. For this game though, I just turn it on and it works. I don't adjust anything. In that sense, it really captures the feeling of playing a PS2 game at the turn of the century before patches, DLC downloads, and unfinished, unreliable piece of **** games. It's a port of a console game from the turn of the century. Why would you play it on a keyboard? I use keyboard and mouse for most games but it never occurred to me to do that with this one. ARPGs are for controllers in my experience. I've never had a good time playing an ARPG with a keyboard and mouse.It plays fine with a controller. How is it with keyboard and mouse? I don't know because I never use that control setup with this type of game.Yeah it's more than I paid for it when I bought the "Greatest Hits"  version for PS2 as a kid. I bought it because I want to support game preservation and because I want the devs to port the sequel and Champions of Norrath to Steam as well.If you don't want to pay this much for an old game, just wishlist it and wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic cooperative isometric hack n' slash, or mage 'em up if you choose.This game was a game that brought me and my girl together, so I have nostalgia glasses for it. be warned, this will be a positive review.Sound, graphics, and controls are all just as good as I remember. The graphical enhancements in this game are the fact that we can play it on a modern TV in HD without too much aliasing and dithering. (This game released when CRT and Tubes were king, complete with chonky pixels.)The audio isn't mixed very well, so vocals are very quiet, while effects are extremely loud and distracting. However, the sound in general is great. The stereo effect is tied to the center of the display, not the characters left/right sides. So, if you are an audiophile of any sort that uses positional cues to figure out where attacks are coming from and stuff, that will throw you off for a bit.So far, it runs great and has yet to crash. I have only encountered one issue, which is a truly bizarre issue. During our first cooperative session, our Xbox controllers swapped from player 1 to player 2, which made me a mage and her a dwarf. We have different generation 1st party Microsoft Xbox controllers, She has a Xbox One S white controller that was bundled with the console, with micro usb or usb OTG. I have a Xbox Series controller that has type c. Really, it doesn't matter because it made it a little interesting mixing up the characters like that.The ONLY drawback to this port is the lack of PC options to take advantage of, both graphically and in the audio menu. I really don't like how I don't have control over the options, such as bloom, motion blur, dialog volume, ambient music/sound volume, vsync, and any filtering of the textures. None of those options are present, and I would have loved to see all of that be a thing in this PC version.A big drawback to the game is that you cannot use the same character as player 2. Only one person can be the mage/fighter/archer/drizzt at any time. Now, that was true back on the PlayStation 2 when I first played the game, so its not a fault of the PC port. But, I would have loved to see this change made to the game because running around as a pair of hot mages blowing up the thieves and undead would have been quite a bit of fun.The ending was trash. I was hoping for a jump through a final gate to be heralded as a hero of Baldur's Gate, but alas that was not the case. We never got to see Aylth and her uh...very large and exquisite  ever again...I don't know if this a port of a specific console version, but what I can tell you is that it is fun and looks pretty good. I can't wait for Dark Alliance 2 to hit Steam.8/10 because THIS ISN'T THE PLACE FOR THAT!
