_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a bit of reminiscence about BaldursGate and/or Diablo 1 then this is it. You get to choose from archer, warrior, wizard. And there is a co-op too. You see some random fantasy story start and there you begin. Here is your rusty knife and help with cellar rat problem while finding secret way to thief hideout. It’s nice, you get nothing wrong with that and that is just that. Solid game, nothing more or less. The major distinction between the two games is that you are using movement to position yourself to gain advantage, not only clicking on enemy to engage it in most direct way, slash/slash, gulp potion. I played on hard as the start seemed too easy. Boy was I wrong. The game has (as I read a lot about it) wrongly done armor calculation. So even with full plate +5 at end, every creep in the level was able to land a high dmg blow that took more then half of my health. Fight against a group. As awarrior should. Sure thing. It just take a bit of luck for them to land that 2 crits or what is it and sniffing flowers from the ground you go. But it takes you on whole other plane of existence. You start to learn patterns and use smarts to conquer. You soon learn that enemies that present bigger object (even bigger humanoids) are bulkier and game engine must move them more then smaller in order to turn them. Because they can attack only in certain angle. So you just position yourself behind them and start the carousel of joy. I learned for first time with wolves that you just let one chase you, as you run you start turning with him in tail to create a circle, then you start tightening it down to get behind and start to bite him to his surprise. Rinse and repeat. You will use it a lot, because if you don’t then it is only a matter of dice how many hits or seconds till they land that hard hit for more then half health. I played only dwarf, so not sure about spells. I can only say that as dwarf you should get the continuous block with twohanded skill. It will make you life a lot easier. You will use from time to time whirlwind, but oh boy, that skill is terrible. I have never seen it executed this bad, even animation sucks. You turn in small static circle with centrum in midlle of your axe and body. So your body and axe both circle around middle of your handle. Hillarious. Landing two blows to those near. Can be used only with twohanded axes or hammers. The next skill he has is even worse. Some hammer slam – with hammers only. 40 dmg when your weapons do 100. That is an insult. And you even pay with mana for it. BTW you need to click right after the animation of your swing ends to get the fastest next swing, otherwise you need to wait for like half a sec to swing again. Unless you get hold of that you limit your dps to 2/3 only. Twohanded swords are the fastest and have longest reach. That way they are also the best to employ carousel technique that is required on hard. This way you can focus your skill points on more useful skills. From start it was hard to get good weapons, you could only buy them. So I was saving on health potions and using regeneration. This way I was able to master multitasking at home and put even my wife to shame. Muhahaha. Now that is something money can’t buy. I had a lot of fun with this game. I liked the zombies the most I think and hated Yeties the most (strong fast and far reaching). The random way zombies dismantled upon hitting was keeping it exiting the whole time. Which was lucky for me as they were used often. I liked the story, it was good that at end they told you all and it clicked nicely. Even the starting tavern elven song was giving more sense, which was nice. I liked that the priest of Ilmatter was there in the catacombs to give you healing, exactly at that moment it was needed. It was very nice touch. Thumbs up for that. The place where I received my above intermediate degree in this game was Karne the thief boss. There I learned to cut corners to gain that extra window when they turn to land few free hits. Because imagine that you need to hit him like 50 times and he needs to hit you 2-3 times – on hard on one load. I was always saving all money to buy the best weapon in new act. It was well worth it. When you finally had a lot of money it didn’t matter as there was no shop. The last location you are inside of a tower with no use of potion of return. But you get all potions you need from containers and mobs. BTW there is no townportal, or teleport, but there is potion of return, you activate it from menu as to prevent accidents. In last location with few loads before opening chests you can get nice equip. This way I learned that scaling up regen is really not worth it. Enemies are nice and variable. Wisps were refreshing, they were creating a small pack, when their static levels filled they went out of the cluster to attack you and as their static levels lowered they were returning. Doing high lightning dps to area around them. The key for fighter was to keep him entertained to move a bit further and just as the levels were going down you engaged it, till other from cluster didn’t start to go against you. Really more like playing with adhesive/repelent materials. So all in all good that I played it on hard as it was keeping me more at my toes and made the game more interesting and deep. Oh and the enemies can be really stupid. Some bosses you can completely shoot with arrows right as they splutter with anger at your face. Like that Lizzardman boss that got stuck on one end of battering ram, while I was standing on the other and loosed arrow after arrow until he dropped. Hilarious, I cleansed the genofond. This was a nice game. I would say not for you if you don’t like fantasy or Forgotten Realms and don’t want to play anything like Diablo.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: It's simple yet very fun imo. I can't quite put my finger on it, but this game has something that new AAA games lack. It's not quite like most ARPG's out there, I would say it feels kind of souls like, due to the fact that you can't always go in guns blazing. Mobs can and will own you if you don't pay attention (I'm on normal difficulty, maybe I just suck).
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Don't pay any attention to the naysayers. This is as fantastic as it was on the PS2 (which I still own) and has aged quite well. I have encountered exactly *ONE* glitch and it was the ice dragon partially going inside a wall of the ice cave. It wasn't game-breaking in the slightest as all I had to do was maneuver myself to get him to fly up and away from it. Other than that I have experienced *zero* bugs, UI issues of any kind, or graphical problems. It's a fantastic game from a fantastic era for gaming and I highly recommend it. A sale would be nice but I personally have found it to be worth the $30.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Can't really see myself playing this till they release some sort of patch to lock the games frame rate. Right now I get over 100 frames and my character basically sprints everywhere. I loved these games on my Xbox back in the day, it's a shame no one caught this before release.I can't currently recommend this because it lacks this very basic function.***EDIT***I was able to fix this problem, I opened my Nvidia Control Panel, and was able to tell it to have VSync on this game specifically. Now I get a solid 60 Frames, and the game runs as it should. Still pretty lazy to leave this setting out of the Menu. So I'm not changing to recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: +1 A pleasant surprise to play this again after so many years.  Time hasn't been overly kind to it, but many models seem to generally have been updated to higher-detail (unless it was ahead of its time?).  The terrain is rather bland and low-poly, though there are patches later in the game that are better.  For it's price and half-hearted upgrade, I give it a 5.  It's OK, though there are many amazing games in the same price bracket that probably should get your money first.  But if you played it in your youth and want to experience it again, I doubt you'd regret it.... Just make sure you're wearing your +5 rose-tinted glasses first!
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: I've encountered repeated crashes when changing zones. Restarted the game from the beginning 2 times already to see if I can get past Act 1 but I give up. Maybe it's because I'm running at 4K but without the ability to alter graphics options I can't test this. Really disappointed because I loved this game as a kid.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to recommend this game since it's a PC port of one of my favorite games from my childhood; however, you should beware of these three things.1. Controller support for local multiplayer isn't working. 2. Unlike Dark Alliance II, this port doesn't include Steam Achievements. (Which is strange since achievements were added on other platforms.)3. There doesn't seem to be any active dev support for this title. Bugs sit reported and ignored in the community forums, and there doesn't seem to be a way to reach any developers.4. The global pricing seems to be off. Based on the forum comments, it appears that this price is wildly inconsistent across geos. As it stands in my region, it is 30 USD for a game from the Gamecube / PS2 era. I would stay it's a steep price, but probably would still be worth it if not for the issues above.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in > 12 hours on Easy. Its fun, very much your standard ARPG with hack and slash, loot drops after bosses and the like. After you beat the game you get to play as Drizzt Do'Urden in a timed dungeon speedrun. Kinda cool I guess? But that's it. Base game, no extras (really interesting/helpful ones, for that matter) and thats it. I would recommend this because I am a big Champions of Norrath fan, but for the price, campaign time and progression, character customization which there is none, I cannot. On a $10-$15 discount? Sure. But not for this. Hell, I think Champions of Norrath had a longer questline and better character customization than this game if my memory serves me right. But I digress. For the price you pay for the limitations this game has, Don't waste your time.TL;DRDon't buy unless you really want too, wait for a discount (which has never happened), and remaster Champions of Norrath.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: A childhood favorite of mine. Didn't know this was coming to PC but it was a pleasant surprise nonetheless! Hoping they add BG:DA2 as well! I know many people, including myself, would be interested in a netplay patch, so here's hoping! So far it's running great for me but the one bug I've encountered is rather surprising and I didn't see any discussion threads about it. As of the current version I'm on, there seems to be an issue when overwriting saved data. The saved data gets overwritten, saves successfully but then generates another save on a separate slot. This separate save is a corrupted save and therefore cannot be loaded. After 64 files, I was unable to save and needed to go in and manually delete the generated corrupted saves. Doing so almost lost me my progress but thankfully it's easy enough to restore saves should you make a backup before working around this bug. Tested the classic cheat codes, which appear to be intact, but the level warp menu is bugged out. Despite it being a little rough around the edges, I'm thoroughly enjoying my time with it. I'd definitely pick it up if you were a diehard BG:DA back in the day or have a newfound/budding interest in the BG series.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite(aside from Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance 2) of all the games on PS2.I'm so glad this game got ported on steam so I can enjoy the remote play feature that allows me to play on the same screen with some friends without being physically there.I really hope they port the 2nd game which is my favorite of the two.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: My first experience with ARPG games back on the PS2, so this was a heavy nostalgia trip for me.Really simple and straightforward, but I feel like the loot & progression is very rewarding.  The price is a little steep, but if you played this and enjoyed previously, you'll still probably enjoy it.  Would recommend playing with a friend via Remote Play Together.Please re-release the 2nd game.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Baldur's Gate was the first RPG that I played so I love coming back to it.  I play more on my PC now and was able to link my PS4 controller to it . Makes game play easier for me since I am not a strong keyboard player.Silly as it is, the smooth effect of the water makes me just want to run circles in it for fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: I played the hell out of Champions of Norrath and Champions: Return to Arms as a kid but never got the chance to delve into this gem or the sequel to it. Now that I've had my fun with this installment, I'm craving Dark Alliance 2 as well as the rest of my childhood. When are we going to see them all on steam!? I gotta have them! I've had a taste and i need more!
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: I played this with my Brother and Father back when it came out. Good times. If you are new to the game I would say you could easily enjoy it. Only advice I have is if you are playing solo start on easy unless you want to drag around 100 lbs of hp pots. The price is a bit high however I am hoping they add the other games as a package deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: I completely, absolutely, positively, 150%-ly recommend this game to others. Purely because this is my favorite game ever and I have grown up on it since I was probably eight or nine years old (or younger.) Thoroughly scarred me as a kid because of the blood and gore. Not the existence of it but the fact that the enemies corpses remain there for the entirety of the game. That you could really hear the guts being ripped from their body or their legs being yanked off by a spiked club and fully immerse in the fact you brought death to every corridor you crossed, and was reminded of it as you back tracked among the dead. Great eerie music, fantastic graphics for its time and still impresses me today. Pretty good voice acting, inspite of there not being too much talking in this game. Hoardes upon hoardes of monsters, and it becomes addictive every time you kill something. Bosses die a slow death, beholders will bleed out and have their eyes roll to the back of their head... it's all just, mwah. 150000% recommend this game.Oh, and there's big tits in this game too. Big bouncy ones! I see people complaining the price of this game is too high, but I think $30 dollars is absolutely fair to me! This game has hours of gameplay on it to me, as I love 100% this game over and over again!! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: It still holds up after so many years. Played this on the deck and it ran flawlessly. This game is very challenging to play solo which I liked. They did a good job porting it to PC. While the graphics is not good as it's an older game, it has it's charms. There's enemy variety as well which was nice. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Very stable port with instant load times. If you enjoyed this game as a kid you will most likely enjoy it again. I keep seeing people complain about the price, but I can spend $30 on a meal and I don't get to enjoy that meal for 24 hours of fun (with more to come). The value added in this release is really the resolution. Using an emulator hurt my eyes after a while and it's not perfectly stable like this version is.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: feel the need to part with your gold? You've come to the right place, traveler! One of my all-time favorite video games finally came to steam. This got a remaster earlier this year for ps4 / xbox and i bought it on ps4. I bought it here to show full support for the devs so they can hopefully do the same for BGDA 2 or champions of norrath. This is a phenomenal game, runs great (granted there are no graphics options, which will undoubtedly upset a few people) and is exactly how you remember it. I recommend playing this with a controller. $30 may be a little steep for some, but I didn't think twice about buying this instantly. No regretti
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent port. Even comes with the "can't turn down background noise, just music and sound effects" bug that plagued the first. Jokes aside, it's an excellent dungeon crawler/beat'em up. Tells a fun story set on the Sword Coast, and ends with a cool boss fight, and a great closing cut scene. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing even beyond the nostalgia factor. It has easily withstood the test of time in terms of replayability and is only limited by its linear storyline. There are few games like it, and I am super appreciative that Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance I & II are on steam. I really hope that Champions of Norrath comes to PC as well in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: First let me address the "do not recommend" rating; Simply put, this game did not age well. For its time, it was a great hack'n'slash RPG, and I made a lot of memories playing this when I was a kid. But it's over 20 years old, the difficulty is all over the place, a lot of recurring hitbox issues (at least when I played with mouse+keyboard) and overall the gameplay loop isn't that rewarding (long level up times, and you're still better off just spamming melee attacks).Having played it a long time ago, it was worth the buy so I could have it in my library, but I don't imagine a new player would be fully satisfied with their purchase especially when compared to modern titles available for the same price.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: I never played this and Dark Alliance 2 when they came out long ago on the PS2, but I did play the last two games in the series, Champions of Norrath and Champions Return to Arms. While the latter are much better in every way, BG:DA is a really fun time, even if it can be a hard at times since equipment drops are purely RNG. Its that old-school goodness that frustrates you yet reminds you of simpler, more straight forward times in gaming. Baldur's Gate is not without its bugs and glitches in this PC port, but they are minimal and thus far not game-breaking. However, the nonexistent graphics and resolutions options are a major let down in what is a pretty decent, if bare-minimum, port. Overall, BG:DA is fun to play but the bare-minimum port with little updates sees BG:DA earning a 7/10 for the PC port of this title. I really cannot wait for more of these old-school games to come to PC, especially the Champions games! Pick up on sale for hours of entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Never played this game when it came out but always wanted.Was not disappointed, played from start to finish on normal with my girlfriend and the game was hard but enjoyable. (locked at 60fps cause higher than that and it seems mobs where hitting harder).Played with 2 xbox one gamepad via bluetooth and it worked flawlessly.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Its not much of an actual DnD game as it is an arcade hack n' slash with a coat of DnD paint.Its a good arcade hack n' slash but if you are looking to play DnD I suggest Neverwinter Nights or Solasta Crown of the magister.Exactly as I remember it flaws and all. Given all of that I would suggest waiting for it to go on sale for 5-10$.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Great action RPG, and good story to go with it.  I would advise waiting for a sale as I think it is overpriced at $30.  The game is not very long, but it is fun, you can start over with the same character to play through again at a higher difficulty level and continue to level your character making them stronger.  There is also a hidden Extreme difficulty, which provides new challenges and better gear to find and purchase from vendors.  This game also has a bit of a cliff hanger ending that leads right into Dark Alliance II, so it is advised to play this game before part 2 if you can.  Even with the high price, I still think it is a classic Action RPG that was ahead of its time when it came out originally on the PS2.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic ARPG, now give us the Champions remaster please.  30 smackaroos is kinda pricey though.  Oh also make a DnD Heroes port to PC.  Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance,  DnD Heroes, and Champions Return to Norath have been the games I've always used as my gold standards.  Something about this era of ARPGs always had a certain charm to them, they've always had a high replay value for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: This game came out during the Great Holiday Flood of 2001, when the PS2 at the end of it's first year, was getting literally two must have games per week.It was one of the best games that released during that time, and like most of the old classics is still a blast now while being more enjoyable than most modern releases.Come for the amazing breast and water physics. Stay for the company over a pint of ale.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: It's like coming home. One of my favorite games ever. First played on a friend's Nintendo GameCube, I was able to pick it up later on the PlayStation 2, and beat it many, many times. Getting to dive back into it on PC at a beautiful 1080p and at 60fps is a wonderful experience. Best played with a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: I really regret buying this game. The controls on PC are not that great. Clearly was meant for consoles and PC was an afterthought that was not well executed. To top it off once you get to the second level of the thieves guild you cant get any farther due to a. extremely difficult falling stone puzzle that cant seem to get past.  The time frame to react and jump to the next stone is way to short. Plus its random every time so you cant even memorize a pattern. Way too infuriating I do not recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Just like I remember it, I love it. And getting to play it with a friend who had never played it before because he never owned a PS2 is making it that much better. It sucks it has to be done through Steam Remote Play which means you need 2 controllers but I'm not mad, they'd have to basically reinvent the game to shove multiplayer into it so I get it. People are upset about the price tag but I'm sure a lot of work went into getting a PC port going & I think their thought process is that the game won't get a ton of sales so they needed to have a higher price to pay for the cost of the port. $30 at the end of the day isn't really that much so idk. I'm hoping they lower the price after they've made back the cost of the port as I'd like to see more people experience this masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: The core game looks amazing and runs at 4k. This game is a port and not a remaster so the menu images are still running the 480p resolution they were on the PS2 but the actual game graphics look amazing. Running on an ssd there is only a 1 second load time. The game runs much better on PC than it ever did on PS2 and look so good on a huge 4k tv. 30$ is steep. If this came with BGDA2 as well I would be much happier with the price but I love this game so I ponied up the money and cant say I regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a hardcore fan and want to play this game regardless of how badly it translates to PC (like me), then you should get it.  But, just know the camera angles and controls are horrible on PC.  Extremely frustratingly bad.  I understand why they left the game alone and just made it compatible for today's PC hardware, but I think they should have made a few small modifications to upgrade it some.  If you have a controller it might be fun, but I don't and it's only nostalgia that I'll play it for.  Oh, and I'm just getting to the crypts and the game has crashed 3 times already.EDIT: I found that remapping the keys makes a huge difference.  Once you figure out a key mapping that works for you and get use to it, it's very playable with some patience.  Also, I figured out the crashing was happening primarily when transitioning maps while walking/running or clicking.  If I just stop moving and clicking and just click the select button to transition I don't get crashes.  Changed vote from not recommended to recommended.  If you liked the original game you'll like this once you get passed these issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best ARPG's of all time and my personal favorite. I grew up playing this game on the PS2 , and played it mainly couch CO-OP with my brother. I have waited for it forever to be brought to PC so seeing this pop up on the steam store page I was just soo excited to play it again. That being said though the game really is just a straight port. They did not add any graphical options other than a resolution scale button and some kind of smoothing filter setting. I assume the game just runs at whatever you have your monitors resolution at. Pros+ One of the greatest ARPG's Ever has finally been brought to PC+ Game looks clear and crisp since it can be played in HD on modern hardware+ Runs at a smooth 60fps with no lag whatsoever+ Online CO-OP works great using remote play which allows both players to play on one PC ( Both players have to have controllers plugged into their PC's for this to work properly , does not work with mouse and keyboard. ) + Hearing the Elf Song Tavern song never gets old!+ combat is just as fun as everCons:- No real settings other than like a resolution scale bar and a smoothing filter option- game is a direct port with nothing new added ( if you like the game on ps2, xbox, or gamecube you will like it though)- for some reason the level warp cheat menu is messed up and does not scroll up and down like its supposed to- does not have online co-op other than using remote play ( no servers on their end )- They did not redo the HUD so its low resolution compared to the rest of the game.here is a video i made on getting online remote play CO-OP working :
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: There is something wrong with saving when playing on the Steam Deck. Playing will randomly crash the game. I think it's the game saves because when I stream from PC but it accesses game saves on the deck it will also crash.I'm very nostalgic for these games but the game-breaking crashes on Steam Deck and total lie about cloud save functionality makes this a disappointing cash grab and poor PC port. Very disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game when I was younger on the Gamecube and had been looking for it on the PC for a few years now. I decided to search for it on Steam once again and was happy to see that they had finally released it. After just a few hours of playing it, I am extremely pleased with how much fun it is to play. It places above many modern games in my books. It's just one of those games that feels like the developers put their heart into, if that makes any sense. Anyway, I don't typically leave reviews, but I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the greatest games of the arc where they tried to adapt RPGs to faster styles of play. Oozing with detail, charisma, amazing character design and voice acting, and truly ahead of its time - I really had a blast playing this when I was a kid on the PS2, and now again with the PC port. Get it next time it's on sale for sure, 110%!
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: This is awesome having this game on PC without having to use an emulator, and to be able to play with remoteplaytogether is a huge bonus. The higher resolution capabilities of today make this game look quite a bit better. I am curious if the hit points and damage has been altered because I'm getting 1 or 2 shot killed by standard units on normal, even wolves and bats and even with the best armor you can buy. It's like that throughout the game as well. I never remember having to block very much playing on ps2 but you can barely scrape by even with blocking on normal difficulty, it is kind of annoying, especially when you are fighting a boss and you can't get hit even one time or it's over. I mean I expect that on hard but not normal.I bought at this way too high a price to hopefully encourage the other game to come to steam as well. It makes sense for all parties to put these old games on steam!
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nostalgic. Albeit, I don't remember it being this difficult to beat. Wearing paper plate armor gives you no benefits so do yourself a favor for the first playthrough and boost your constitution and fortitude if you want some survivability. Playing Vahn was the best option for me as he has a very balanced playstyle. Range and melee. Bows are also very reliable until you pick up the onyx sword or a two-handed adamantine weapon late game. If you start on normal you'll pick things up quickly but find that enemies carve through paper plate armor like in the movies. So the range game is the ultimately the best option.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun reminder of older Sword Coast games. It is a hack and slash adventure with enough plot to keep you looking for the next part of the quest, and wishing that you could get to a safe area to sell all the loot you have accumulated while traversing the dungeons. Graphics, although old are still enjoyable, especially if you feel the urge to watch a dwarf in a diaper jump around in the fountain at the center of town as your coop players sort their inventory.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: The smell of the sewers has taking a liking to you...I have played the dark alliance games on PS2 for nearly 20 years now and I can say this is the best version. The game looks really sharp in 1440p at 60 fps and uses barely any power. If they port Dark Alliance 2 i'll throw my money at that one too without hesitation. 10/10 Would smash every box and jar in my path again.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Not a perfect launch by any means , but they managed to fix most of the problems with small updates . 30eu is a bit pricey ,but im willing to pay the price for one of my favorite games of all time . Hopefully they will do the same for BGDA 2 , Champions of Norrath and even Fallout BOS . Small heads up , if you played BGDA2 , they haven't included some quality of life improvements , like using shift button for spells , so you have to manually scroll through your spell list to find the one you want to use ,as well some other stuff , like camera zoom , but im just happy i can play this on a PC without emulators . All in all , I recommend this game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: i don't even own this game only because i feel it's a little over priced. I think 25$ would be a good price for it. But my friend got it and we are doing a play through on remote play. And i can say it's a wonderful game we are having a blast playing it together. And we plan on doing multiple play through's with each other and i can't wait. If you see the game for 25$ get it you wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Man, 20 years or so later and I still love this game. It was the first Dungeon crawler / RPG type game I ever played.So of course I had to buy it again, after this I graduated to Morrowind. I think it holds up very well, graphics are dated yes, however the story is both classic and entertaining. If you have a trend of playing these types of games and happened to miss this one or was born way after... it's worth the gameplay, For $30? debatable it 100% cashed in on my nostalgia, and likely anyone else who gave this a glowing review too. Maybe if enough people buy this we can finally get a proper ending to the series. Ironic how Dark Alliance was my first Action RPG / Dungeon Crawler AND the first of many canceled-after-a-major-cliff-hanger-ending game. The unresolved plot after the sequel STILL bothers me.. I know I'm not the only one with this 20 year long Osiris Killing blue balls.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: This is very much Nostalgia for me that's pushing me to recommend this game I love the old timey hack and slash and I love the enemies, based on D&D I am currently trying to go full runs on each character including extreme in order to make sure I get my full money's worth out of the game,  my advice if you want to play this game try waiting for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: I am fortunate enough to own and still play the PS2 version of this game.  This is a decent port with a small upscale to it.  I haven't noticed any major problems, but I also have not yet played it a lot.  I will abuse this as much as the PS2 copy I have been playing for years and I will update my review if I find things.The difficulty does seem a tad harder on the PC when comparing Normal to Normal, but I think it is just a scaling error and I think I actually prefer it as it is now.  I'd say the price is worth it, the physical Greatest Hits copies (remember the $20 re-releases) sell for at least $40 on the secondary market.  Grab it on sale if price is really of concern.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad port, they seem to have patched most issues ive seen people have (crashes, resolution) and ive had a pretty good (very nostalgic) time playing through easy/medium/extreme with no issues. No groundbreaking graphics updates or anything, just a 1080p update it seems, but if you miss this childhood gem i definitely recommend:)
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: It's kind of crap, but it's that good kind of crap that gets you a few giggles with zero brainpower involved and gives you a headache by the time you're done with it. Looting feels chaotic and weird. Hard to tell when you're dying until you're actually dead. Shameless Diablo/Gauntlet style game. Enjoyable with a friend (Remote play runs buttery smooth). A product of its time, really.Also it's apparently made by the folks who developed the original Fallout games so there's that.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game when it first released and played Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance 2 so nostalgia is a factor in recommending this game however I feel as though this game appeals to people who like ARPGs, D&D, or classic rpgs. Solo is great coop is even better if you can find a friend. Well worth the purchase for amount of hours it provides in content and experience. Updating after a while more playing. Still recommend purchasing but have some suggestions for developers I'd say better multiplayer access for online, more achievements to unlock, and maybe some sound remaster if possible. Other than that hope to see Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance 2 and then 3 finally one day.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance

_childDocuments_.review: I would be very skeptical of anyone reviewing this game solely out of nostalgia because this game is not good 20+ years after its' release, especially at the price $30 price point. Now, mind you, I played this game solo so maybe it's a better with a friend. As a solo player, it is a  that you play this game on easy. At first, I tried to play this game on normal but found the enemies to practically be one shotting me while they were practically damage sponges. _childDocuments_.review: The steam playtime cannot convey the amount of time i have spent in this game. that being said it has a lot of good and a lot of hangups. the combat is fun, the weapons, armor, and the art design is good if a product of its time (almost every female model in the game, the sorceress PC included, has a chest like two watermelons barely covered by the clothes,) you fight a variety of enemies in various environments so the game never really gets stale, and the puzzles, dungeons, and enemies you fight are always super interesting. that being said there is also just, a lot of things that kind of objectively suck about that game. even back on the XBOX (cant speak for the play station version) the game was riddles with bugs, glitches, and slowdown, which this port inherited. the difficulty system suck so if you're playing anything other than easy by the mid game the enemies just melt your health bar, and even playing solo up to that point is a challenge because of the lack of a second player to split the damage. the ranged damage system sucks and is super clunky and sensitive, and is hard to aim even if you get the level upgrade that is explicitly supposed to help you aim. and the "return to town system" work really weirdly. since this is a dungeon crawler you'll want to be constantly returning to town since you cant carry any more loot once your bag is full, so you will want to sell stuff at the shop and buy yourself better items, but you can only do so using "recall potions" which you can either buy at a hefty price, or use when the game gives you one (and it usually gives you one at the end of a strip of dungeon when it REALLY wants you to go back to town) and walking back to where you were, or buying a bunch from the store to teleport back and forth between the town and where you were, but suffer from having a bunch of heavy potions in your bag. in the end while yes i'm probably blinded by nostalgia, if you can look past the hangups and play on easy (especially if you're playing alone) its a great and super fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an absolute classic and the cornerstone of couch co-op at the time. The gameplay is excellent if simple, the music and effects are really nice, although the story is not as grandiose as a more contemporary RPG. The controls are as well excellent. It would be hard to find ways to improve the base experience of the game, it was crafted very well when it first released.The game took me about 12 hours to complete on normal difficulty, but your mileage may vary because I did beat this at least ten times when it first came out. Besides normal, there's three other difficulties, and while I played with the archer, there's two other classes to play as, too. This lends very well to replaying the game because each character plays very differently. There are also unlockable modes and characters which just adds more and more: you get a lot of content for the price.I think most people will be buying this for nostalgia sake because while the game is excellent, it is CAD$38 for a 20 year old port. If you really want to play it, it's not a bad route to go, but if you have a PS2 or Gamecube laying around, this PC release might not add enough to warrant a rebuy. It was worth it to me because I get to play it on my platform of choice, but your priorities may lie elsewhere.Dark Alliance translates well enough to PC. M+KB controls do work, although I would still advise a controller. It is, however, just a port, with not much beyond the basics added for a 20yr old game such as support for higher resolutions. Unfortunately achievements are not here despite being on the Playstation and Xbox ports.Textures have not been improved, nor have character models. You notice this harshly for UI elements. That said, it was a really good looking game in 2001 and it's still pretty nice to look at, just rough around the edges. There is one PC related peculiarity and that is the framerate is tied to physics, so you will need to lock to 60fps to remain playable.Game runs without issues, controls also work great. At maximum details, the Steam Deck maintains 60fps and it's a smooth experience throughout the entire game. The 16:10 aspect is also supported and works well. Text is legible.Ultrawide is supported out of the gate and works well. UI elements do not stretch. I don't think ultrawide necessarily improves the experience, however, because while it lets you look ahead to a degree, most of the time the areas of the screen which ultrawide resolutions reveal over 16:9 is nothing of much import. You usually see outside the bounds of levels.It's not a demanding game, and it's a slightly updated port of a 20 year old game. It goes without saying my 5600X and RTX3080 can max the game out, especially with the 60fps cap. Chances are any PC within the last decade could play it well.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been over 20 years since I had given any thoughts about Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance (%$&#...). I genuinely liked the game (wasn't anything quite like it on console), but I only ever completed the first act (messed up a dupe attempt; lost my gear and my will to continue gimped out).It's 2024; I've finally closed this chapter of my life and here's what I think about Dark Alliance.It was extremely okay.I'll elaborate. The story was pretty straight forward; an unknown enemy plots to destroy the titular city and you the intrepid hero must thwart their plans. Or whatever. This isn't a story heavy game and I honestly couldn't name a character who stood out (apart from an elven bar maiden...)The meat of the game is hacking and slashing. You will do plenty of hacking and slashing. Is it revolutionary? No. Is it at least fun? Eh, it kills time. Every enemy feels the same... and dealing with them is pretty much the same. I played as the dwarf fighter and my whole strategy summed up to: "attack, attack, block... repeat".If combat is the meat then items are the potatoes and lemme tell you this... not a lot of variety. There's enough for the game length (10-12 hours), but nothing is gonna really wow you. You'll find a great weapon off a random mob and find the same exact weapon off a rack.The music is there. Can't say I had any favorite tracks or really anything I can remember. It fits the visuals. And speaking of. Well, it's a 20 year old game. It's not awful looking, but it's certainly not gonna amaze you and stylistically it's pretty straightforward--a goblin looks like a goblin, a rat looks like a rat, etc.There's also a new game plus(which you unlock after beating a timed gauntlet using Drizzt Do'Urden) named EXTREME MODE. Wherein you load up a previous character without any of gear. EXTREME.Also a co-op mode which isn't online so you'll have to either do couch co-op or remote play (I tried it out using a deck and my laptop and it ran fine, but I didn't play long).Would I recommend it? If you're feeling nostalgic then sure why not? Pick it up on sale and be a little underwhelmed. Otherwise I can't imagine wasting time or money when there's just so many better options.

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence to recommend this but as of writing this I simply feel it's the worst way to currently play Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance. First off, It is an extremely barebones port of the Xbox version of the game, understandably so but it brings with it all of the Xbox's unique graphical quirks. Most notably there are jarring clipping issues characters seem to have during conversations that simply don't exist in the PS2 and Gamecube ports.As well, most people are passing it off as "old games were harder" but the damage enemies deal is beyond ♥♥♥♥♥♥ in this port. Just comparing gameplay of "The Gauntlet" between this PC port and my Gamecube and PS2 copies shows that enemies like spiders go from the simple fodder they should be to 2-shotting monsters that WILL end your run if you aggro more than like 3. Granted I haven't fired up my Xbox copy since I acquired it so that may just be another quirk of the Xbox port that has simply never been addressed due to the games age and general "obscurity", but it is definitely an issue when even a longtime fan and player was getting frustrated getting randomly 1-shotted multiple times in a session during a normal difficulty playthrough.I really hope I can return to this review in the future and change my opinion to a solid recommendation because I love this game, its sequel and the spiritual successors they had, but until then you can definitely pass on this at full price, and if you're a longtime fan maybe wait until a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ atrocious. I know it came out on ps2 but damn did this age like milk. I gave up on this game around the second chapter of the game. It was clear the gameplay wasn't going to get better at all, with it actually getting worse. Everything is incredibly spongy and you have to do nothing but chug health potions when fighting or else you will die. The weapon variety is piss poor, despite there being tons of different kinds. The reason for this is that almost all of them have the same animation, with the speed of it barely feeling different. The enemies are the same, there are tons of them but they all act the same for the most part. By the time I left the first chapter, enemies were getting near impossible to deal with without chugging dozens of potions, but then in chapter 2, I couldn't keep enough on me without running out and dying. Because there is little depth to this game's combat, I have to either tank everything with potions or take a trillion years on each encounter, diving in and out hitting the crowd once or twice, only for them to two shot me. I know this is a re-release of an old ps2 game, but idk if they updated it or anything. I can't really tell if the graphics are different or if something else was updated. It is possible this was re-released without changing anything, which would be fine, but this  game hasn't aged well at all. A remaster or remake that does more than a face lift would have done this game well. I tried to refund this game, but since I played for 5 hours, waiting for the gameplay to get better, I can't get one. Thankfully I only put 50 minutes into the second one so I got a refund for that one. Which I also don't recommend because it is a literal carbon copy of the first. Sad that this is bad cause I remember it being really fun as a child. Do not recommend, just go play diablo.

_childDocuments_.review: Baldur's Gate's Dark Alliance  (Overall Gameplay)The game play of Baldur's Gate is reminiscent of the classic PS1 era. I fondly remember playing this game 20 years ago, always choosing the elf character. I wanted to try something different this time and went with the Archer. While the game remains the same, selecting other characters can lead to unique experiences. I particularly enjoyed the challenge of playing as the Archer. The storyline is straightforward, making it a great adventure/role-playing game. Your preferred style of play will determine which character is best suited for you. If you enjoy magic, stick with the elf. But if you're up for a challenge, the Archer may be the wild card you need in this game.(Recommendation)If you're a fan of D&D or the slash genre, I highly recommend this game. Depending on your chosen difficulty level, it has a PS1 feel and can be consuming. Hard mode can be challenging, as you can be killed with just one hit. However, if you're looking to prepare for Baldur Gates 3, this game is great. Overall, I rate it 8 out of 10. It falls short of a 10 out of 10 games because it lacks diversity. The archer/fighter/magician combination can be a little bland, so I appreciate the second version for its differences.*Rating*8/10

_childDocuments_.review: A little pricey but a fun adventure nonetheless! It's a bit slower and more tactical than your average ARPG. There's little details too, like how zombies will lose their limbs as you hit them and even continue to crawl to attack you.There are annoyances like the difficulty which I fits more in the frustrating end than a fun challenge. Most bosses involve running around and getting a few hits in or risk being killed in a few hits. It can feel a bit gimmicky and annoying but that is par for the course with the genre.I played as the sorceress who is definitely the hardest class at the beginning but once you get some good spells and put points into them it was worth it. If you're curious and enjoy older style rpgs give it a try (though maybe on sale). Can't wait to try out the sequel which I hear is much better.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game when it came out on the PS2 pretty much constantly.  In fact, I still have my original copy.  I was curious how this port would fare, and I'm happy to say it plays identically to the PS2 version, with the one difference being that it loads faster on PC.  Sure, the graphics are dated, and the gameplay is pretty simplistic, but that's not always a bad thing.  It's a straightforward ARPG set in the Forgotten Realms.  It says it's on D&D 3rd Edition ruleset, but it definitely doesn't feel like it.  There's just some familiar spell and feat names, that's all. As far as gameplay goes, it plays well.  It's hack and slash, and you use the D-Pad to select your active spell or feat from a scroll wheel.  It's fairly unwieldy if you have two spells that aren't particularly close together, but it IS still pretty convenient and innovative for spell selection.  You can also switch between a ranged weapon and melee weapon, but unless you're playing a character with high strength, you may want to forego keeping both on you, as inventory/weight management is a constant struggle.  Or, you know, just let the bad loot go.  But I've never been able to do that.I've only played solo on PC, and I'm finding it fairly easy, because of the sheer amount of potions that drop.  If potions were more scarce, it would be a little more difficult.  If the co-op experience is anything like it was on PS2, then that's where this game will shine.  It's a fun experience to play with a friend, and can make things go much more quickly, and can keep it from being as much of a slog as it can sometimes be.The major drawback, to me, is the price.  $29.99 is too much for a game this old that has no updates or new features or improved graphics or anything.  I love this game, so I paid the price, but if you're not familiar or haven't played it, it will probably be better to wait for it to go on sale (if it ever does).  Also, a little tip: play the Sorceress.  She's awesome, and her ball lightning spell wrecks literally everything.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, this game is pretty hard, but the real challenge is justifying spending thirty dollars on a bare bones port over twenty years old.Personal grievances aside, it is a blast from the past that does hold up really well and it looks pretty solid in 4k resolution. There is local co-op, but no online. Though, it never had it.Honestly, its age aside, the content does merit the price tag. They’re not as in-depth as other Baldur’s titles since the gameplay is streamlined for a more fast paced experience to be enjoyed with friends, but the RPG mechanics are there, and they are satisfying for the type of game.There are three characters/classes to choose from that each feel different and come with different perks to acquire as you level up and scavenge more powerful loot. That’s about it, but it’s incredibly meaty for the type of dungeon crawler it is. You should perhaps take into account that this was the first Baldur’s title to be developed exclusively for consoles, and it contains all the strengths and weaknesses of that decision.My personal recommendation: If you have someone to play through it with, then don’t worry about the price tag too much. The content and experience is worth it. Though, I may point you to other titles if you desire a more single-player experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first review of any game Ive purchased on Steam ever. But the game does support remote control mode and I fully intend on buying a remote specifically for this game). The music, the sound effects everything brings me back to playing this game back in the day. All nostalgia aside there are some flaws that are just unavoidable when porting a game like this over to PC. The keyboard controls "out of the box" make the game almost tedious to play and if I hadnt any experience with the game from the past i would have asked for a refund right away. With some simple control tweaking it fixed everything. I want to recommend changing the "use potion"  buttons around. Playing the fighter I switched the health potion button to the space bar because that made more sense. I also changed the camera controls (camera left to the "Q" key and camera right to the "E" key made more sense to me). i also changed the jump button to "Left Shift". Other than keyboard controls this game is just a perfect and fun as it was when i was a kid and I plan on logging many many hours on it. Now if only we can get Champions of Norrath here on steam!!

name: FixFox
detailed_description: Buzz 'As a peaceful walk-enjoyer in real life, it's nice to see you can do the same in FixFox. Nice strolls through meadows and mountains are encouraged, as is chilling by a campfire afterwards. It's just all-round nice. I am here for it.' - Rock Paper Shotgun About the Game FixFox is a wholesome sci-fi adventure game. Play as Vix, an unlucky space mechanic, who crashlands on a mysterious planet where tools are forbidden. Accompanied by her trusty toolbox Tin, Vix travels across the planet Karamel discovering hidden stashes left by pirates, repairing friendly household appliances, and sampling tasty local delicacies. Traverse the planet on a peppy scooter, clear pathways with a hefty power loader, or simply go on a peaceful journey by foot to uncover all the landmarks on Karamel. Hum along to catchy chiptunes while discovering secret locations, testing your noggin on whimsical puzzles, and finally settling down for the night next to a toasty campfire looking up at the starry sky. Repair machines with uplifting personalities such as a passionate lawn mower using unconventional tools like coins, bandages, glowy bananas… anything really. Live out a space mechanic’s dream by constructing and operating giant mechs to help out the local robots with their peculiar problems. Fixing things can be tough but ending the day with cozy food always makes it better. Enjoy delicious meals the planet dwellers have to offer such as homey soups, warm rice bowls, and totally-not-expired pudding. Making a friend over a meal with hospitable robots may just reveal a vital clue to solving your next quest. Starting with an unassuming beacon repair job Vix quickly finds herself mixed up in more than her own tale. An estranged brother looking for his long lost sibling, specialized artificial intelligences working through past traumas, and an ongoing feud between two planet factions are just a few of the tangled mysteries that need to be taken apart and fixed. In order to survive the global catastrophe of Earth’s cold atmosphere post climate change, mankind has genetically modified themselves to take on animal traits. The fur acquired from the genetic splicing helps humanity cope with the freezing weather and the ability to hibernate allows humans to sleep through long interstellar flights. This furry future is where the story of FixFox takes place. In the early 90s, my parents brought home our very first computer - the Polish knockoff of the Atari 8-bit. Using an old handbook, I learned how to code in Basic. From that moment, I wanted to dedicate my life to making games. Fast forward to 2012, after visiting the Peace Memorial in Hiroshima and witnessing the consequences of violence and hatred, I made a personal vow to never play or make violent games. Instead, I focus on making games that promote kindness and friendship. With experience from game jams and heartwarming support from my friends and family, the dream of making this game has become a reality. Fueled by my passion for wholesome stories, sci-fi, and adventure games, FixFox was designed, written, drawn, and programmed by me - Jaroslav Meloun. The music was composed and produced by the exceptionally talented Aleix Ramon. The key art of Vix was created by the amazingly talented Jana Kilianová. My wish is for YOUR dream to come true, just like mine!

_childDocuments_.review: 12.2h (100% achievement, finished the game) No. Yes (~5 achievements). No. is an adventure game where you have to explore several regions, solve puzzles, and fix mechanical appliances with unconventional tools. Note that you can't apply the fixing method used in the game in real life.- Unique gameplay about fixing items- Guided arrows help to figure out the next objective, especially in the vast region- Simple puzzles that can be tricky if you don't remember the newly introduced mechanics- All areas in the region will be reshuffled after you progress the game- It's hard to find items if you have too many items in your toolboxIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 was displayed in a top-down, pixelated view. Regions have a certain pattern in them with the difference in theme and obstacle type, although the game tries to mix things up by displaying a lot of different areas living in each region: a farm region will have farm-related areas, a snowy region will have snowy-related areas, and so on. I was impressed with the details that are put in the food and broken mechanicals though. The food looks delicious while the mechanicals look informative enough to fix.The indoors look weird because of the perspective. Despite displaying interiors in top-down views, the game still tries to show the walls' sides. Objects that are mounted on the sides will appear skewed, and the corners look weird since the separator was displayed horizontally instead of diagonally.The story is a lighthearted one. You are Vix, a SPACR engineer that is tasked to fix a broken beacon on planet Karamel. The story will develop from there, allowing you to meet new characters and help their problems. You won't discover much at first - everything will be revealed little by little as you finish more objectives. To be honest, the main plot is pretty much empty, although I enjoyed the conversations and the characters' backgrounds, whether it's the main character or the AIs.As I said before,  is a game about exploration, puzzles, and fixing items. You will have to explore the whole region to find habitable areas and follow the objectives until you are tasked to find four machine parts. Each machine part will be hidden beneath a simple puzzle, which will vary based on the upgrades that you have. Broken machinery will sometimes also be put in between, allowing you to fix them to progress the game. The game will then loop the same process again, introducing you to 3 more regions with a different theme. The gameplay might feel repetitive after a while, although the game will still try to spice things up near the end.Puzzles are easy but can be tricky to solve if you are not attentive enough. They will revolve around your "upgrades", and the game never says which one to use explicitly. It might take a while before you understand what the game means, especially if you need to use the newly-introduced "upgrades" that you weren't used to. Luckily, you can always try to use all "upgrades" that you have if it doesn't work out. On the good side, the "upgrades" will be more obvious once you know which details to look for, so you don't have to spend as much time as you were in the middle half of the game. Fixing items are fun. To be honest, this is the part of the gameplay that I enjoyed the most. Objects with certain characteristics will be required to do this - flat tools like spatulas and coins can be used to unscrew a bolt, tape tools like bandages and postage stamps can be used to fix a broken wire, and so on. Some mechanics might look similar to what we know in real life, although other unrealistic ones such as brushing a machine's teeth will also be available later on. Although it can feel repetitive after a while, I still liked the simplicity. Heck, I even took a lot of optional quests just because I liked fixing items.You can't filter tools in your toolbox. Since you need to use some tools to fix items, hoarding tools are necessary. However, doing so might bury some tools at the very bottom of the toolbox, making them hard to find. The game might allow you to move tools to different spaces, but it's going to take time to sort them all manually.As a game that focuses on exploration, the game knows how to make it not frustrating. You can either look at a sign or ask people in the area for a general direction, and a guided arrow will be shown to give you the general direction and distance. The maps are also informative enough, showing everything available in that location to make it easier to plan your next route.Exploring the region can be tedious after a while though. You can only do exploration with your scooter at first, and it runs very slow compared to the vast area. Although it works when you explore the region for the first time, you'll get bored quickly once you have to move between areas several times. Luckily, the game will introduce a teleporter service later on, cutting my exploration time.I finished the game in 12.2h. The game isn't hard to finish as long as you know what to do. Despite having 2 endings, there isn't much difference between them. Moreover, the game will advise you to save before you make the choice, so you can always experience both endings in one save. Speaking of saving, the autosave does a really good job with it. It always saves right after I got a new objective, and the game will create a new save slot for each chapter. I hardly need to do a manual save because of that.I hate that areas are always reshuffled and maps are reset after I progress the game. has a lot of features combined into the game, and it did it brilliantly. That heartwarming feeling when you talk to people as you eat, that satisfaction when you fixed an object - everything was balanced perfectly. Moreover, it also has a lot of QoL features that are usually ignored in most games, which made the game more enjoyable. If you like games where you have to tinker around with unconventional tools and solve easy puzzles, make sure to try this one.

_childDocuments_.review: My heart.(spoilers ahead, I don't know how to write this without spoiling anything)---I played this game while in recovery from COVID19, stuck at home for days on end because even though the worst of the virus is gone, the fatigue and lethargy and brain fog remain for who knows how long. A body that was already breaking even before the pandemic, already pushed close to the limit before this latest shove. Now I have to recalibrate how much I can still do what makes life worth living without pushing myself too hard to the point of not having said life to live.I've also felt for a very long time that the closest I have to a spirituality is the profound connection of information, data, bits and bytes across space and time, connecting any brain anywhere just through electrified rocks.The endgame hit me like a ton of bricks. Vix's disintegrating body, pushed to its limit after pursuing long-held dreams despite a body so similarly broken, despite every warning and concern. The mission to "rest your body" hit especially, especially close. And then the beautiful afterlife (purgatory?) of data, just so much data, bits and bytes. free floating information...the picture of my soul.But what especially hit me hard, what's left me in tears writing this, was Tin. I too have a best friend who I adore with every bit of my being, a friend who I've butted heads with over concerns of safety, a friend who looks out for me as I do him, two salty sassbuckets joined at the hip. When Tin re-emerged with Vix and EM made a comment about two souls so intertwined that they reemerge together...I thought of him. When Vix tells Tin in the epilogue that they love being stuck in the same room together, I thought of how he kept me company while I recover from COVID, or from whatever random health malady I happen to be dealing with that week, how if I was destined to be stuck in a room forever, at lesat I'd want him around. And then the decision to pick either the medbay or toss it for a life together with Tin. Usually in these stories the "ideal besties" route would involve sacrificing the possibility of better health to keep the relationship, and I was tempted. But I thought about how I wished I could get a cartridge to fix my broken body. How I don't want to be stuck in a room forever. I looked at Tin and I thought, surely I could bring you with me?And when I made the choice to use the medical cartridge, and Tin frowned for a second before wishing us "good luck", I remembered my best friend, and how he'd want me to be better more than anything.And now I'm sitting here crying, writing possibly the most personal and vulnerable video game review ever. I don't even write that many reviews. Maybe it's my weird knack of picking exactly the kind of "escapist" media that ends up reflecting the very thing I'm trying to escape from. Maybe it's a lot of things. But this game...this game will hit you where you least expect it, and it will be worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it a masterpiece? No, but it isn't bad either. You play a (not overly successful) repairman in a future where humans have spliced with animals and conquered space because they can now hibernate for many years. All household or other appliances talk with you, and when they are defective you have to select the right tool(s) and use it at the right place(s) to make them working again. Your last job brought you to a far away planet full of ancient tech with the assignment to repair the communications beacon. Your ship crashlands, you have no communications with the rest of the universe and you have lost the contents of your toolbox (hammer, screwdriver and duct - who needs more?). You will meet strange appliances, an even stranger cult worshipping "the creator" and having outlawed all tools, and have to find a way to repair the beacon before you can get off the planet. Run around and find stuff, use it to repair more and more complicated things. Talk with your best (and only) friend - your toolbox - and with all the appliances you meet. Eat various meals while you listen to the locals.  Supports kb+mouse or gamepad.Charming and (mostly) peaceful adventure, cute and quite polished for an indie production.

_childDocuments_.review: My disappointment with this game is pretty profound, to be honest.FixFox is a game that is *almost* good. It has a very interesting core concept for its gameplay, a story that makes it clear its author has thoughts they'd like to share and themes they want to explore, and a world that they spent some amount of time thinking about and detailing for you to explore. It has a fun art style, a cozy world, good music, and colorful characters.Then, it thoroughly kneecaps itself by being absolutely terrified that the player might get lost. Despite being called a puzzle game, the game has almost no puzzles in it because it is almost always *telling* you the solutions, whether it's in basic gameplay, or giving you objective markers to lead you from place to place by the nose. The game is so afraid that you'll get stuck on a puzzle or won't figure out where to go next that it gives you almost no agency except to push the buttons that make the plot progress. It feels like a tutorial without a real game attached to it.Not only that, but what puzzles and exploration exist get easier rather than harder, because as you go on the game starts giving you tools to skip them that can be used indefinitely. It speaks volumes of your opinion of your game's basic gameplay loop if skipping it is considered to be a *reward*.Unfortunately, this line of thinking applies to its actual plot as well. Characters in the plot aren't just telling you what to do, they're also telling you what the plot *means* and what its messages are at almost every juncture, as literally as possible. Characters will have arcs and then essentially tell you to your face what they've learned and how they think they can be better. They will tell you about what happened and what about it was right or wrong, and why, in about the most literal terms possible. The game isn't just afraid of the audience not getting to continue the story, it's also afraid of the audience not *understanding* the story, so instead of letting you think about what it's showing you and why, the game just tells you what to think. Even if in general I don't disagree with what the game says, being constantly told what to think about the game's events leaves a sour taste in my mouth.And then, the piece de resistance, the ending. I'll be frank, this ending made any goodwill that I had for this game shrivel up and die. I genuinely don't even understand why any of it was necessary, that part could've been cut out and replaced with *literally nothing* and the end product would've been improved. The entire last act of the story already felt like budget or time were running out and actual gameplay content was getting thin on the ground (the entire last chapter basically gives up and becomes a full-on walking simulator), but the ending feels like the part where the bottom just falls out of the whole thing.TL;DR, a game with interesting ideas and good worldbuilding absolutely hamstringed by poor execution and a dogged aversion to giving players agency. Wish I could recommend, but at the end of the day I can't.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game. You have to select 'yes' or 'no' on whether you recommend something before Steam lets you post a review, and I struggled with the decision. Ultimately, I picked 'no' because I found my experience of the game became too frustrating to continue my playthrough, but potentially other people's mileage may vary.There were elements that I found genuinely very engaging: the larger plotline with robots and AIs (which I'll keep vague due to spoilers), the NPCs who actually contributed to the story, the themes of recorded and corrupted memories, and some of the more one-off puzzles. I quite liked shuffling around a few detachable cargo bays full of storage units in order to get the forklift-type vehicle where I needed it to go, for example.There were some aspects that I didn't really feel strongly about: the entire concept of spliced organic lifeforms (I didn't think it added much to what I saw of the story, but it didn't really detract much either), the mini-game of matching objects to elements of a device that needs fixing, the need to gather materials because they break after a few uses.Then there were the things that frustrated me: the resettable limits on how many fixes/gathers you could do in a row (seemed like a needless inconvenience just to add tension of a looming threat, but you can avoid it perfectly so really it's hardly tense, just grating!), the re-randomising maps, the army of bland robot NPCs who only served to give directions to locations on said re-randomising maps, and the times when the way to progress the story became so unclear as to impede enjoyment. The maps re-scrambling themselves seemed only to cause more delays in story by forcing prolonged 'exploration' in the form of dull travel between largely similar settlements. My experience would definitely have been improved if this hadn't been a feature, or if there were an option to toggle it off.I gave up after making a repeated effort to find the next things that would let me get on with the story, only to be foiled by  a mechanical issue - the item meant to point you to the next target location only directed me to two areas I did not yet have the resource to access, and didn't update to point me to the things I needed to create that resource. This led to maybe an hour of frustratedly trundling around the map just to see if I could stumble across something useful. I didn't. There was no walkthrough or guide in the community hub on Steam so I tried looking up online guides but only found one 'full game walkthrough' let's play video without helpful sub-sections. I didn't really fancy spending even longer trying to sift through it to find the point I was stuck at, especially since all the terrain of each map is so similar as to make it nearly impossible to pick out specific areas or points in the narrative via thumbnails. At this point, I decided to stop trying to give it the benefit of the doubt and forcing myself to keep going so I could assess the full experience (which I really try to do for indie games I get through Curator Connect) and just post my review.I feel a little sad about this because there was definitely potential for me to have enjoyed this game more, but I will almost certainly never finish it because some of the design choices (especially when combined with a few points where the lack of a written walkthrough was a major nuisance) ended up hampering my enjoyment to the point where I had to quit. I am very relieved to finally strike it off my 'to review' list. Maybe someday I'll come back to that giant let's play video just so I can read the rest of the story and find out what happens without having to slog through actually playing the game any more.With all that said, I really did appreciate all the heart and creative work that clearly went into developing Fixfox and I'm impressed that the dev made the whole thing almost single-handed (save for the music and the key art of Vix). I hope Jaroslav Meloun will find plenty to learn from and build upon from the reception of Fixfox, and I hope they will keep making games. I'd definitely be willing to give their next title a go based on all the potential this one has.You can follow my Steam Curator page at !

_childDocuments_.review: I actually had this game on my wishlist and was planning to check it out at some point when I've got more time. Now that I got a review copy, I thought I'd provide a bit of that important early feedback. It seems like a solid game with original repair puzzles, 2D exploration, various quirky AI NPCs and a good bit of lore. Apparently most people find it very relaxing, though personally I wish there was an option to tone down all the blinky and jumpy stuff in addition to turning off text shake. It also seems like there might be quick-time events upcoming, with two different groups out to get you. I really hope I'm wrong and all that talk about "dangers" and stuff is just fluff, but it doesn't strike me as the kind of game where you can fail badly in any case. I also hope that sentient door will stop making those weirdly sexual-undertoned comments about me touching them (probably so harmless/subtle that kids won't get it, but cringey imo). Other than those issues, I found this game quite refreshing. To be updated later - I've certainly liked it enough to come back to it. UPDATE 1 (3h): Finished some , found a bunch of loot, did cool sci-fi stuff, started discovering old mysteries. Still mildly disoriented, there's a lot going on. _childDocuments_.review: Oof, it's tough giving this a thumbs down.  It has a lot of heart and sincerity - I want more folks to try it, I want those inclined to fall in love with it to find it and do so.  At the same time, the play of the game is shallow, and the story, while I'm okay with the conclusion, needed to decide at the outset which of its stories to tell and focus on telling that story well and consistently.  There's a bit of whiplash between the 80% that would make for a *terrific* children's book and the 20% that's just... no, dude.  Too dark, or too conveniently tragic, or too exculpatory.  I don't feel like I can recommend it, much as I might wish I could.The core gameplay relies a lot on procedural generation, meaning anything outside of the critical path feel samey and pointless.  The loop is supposed to go , but these steps in practice only add pointless busywork to advancing the story in much the same way random battles in JRPGs do.  Also note that it's not a game of finding clever solutions using improvised tools - it is not a point and click adventure game where you're seeing if you can fix X using Y, it's a game that tells you that Y will fix X every time (e.g., items with the "tape" trait will fix anything where that trait is applicable) and thus the only issue is staying stocked on Ys.  Add in that it seems eager to short-circuit its own mechanics (e.g., there's one form of fast travel that's almost instantly obsoleted by a second, better form of fast-travel), up to and including discarding chunks of core gameplay (e.g., the first of the two fast travel options initially needing you to fix 'em to use 'em, but later deciding nah, from here on any new ones you find won't need fixing, just activating).  It would almost be perfect for a younger age group who wouldn't notice or much mind its shortcomings.Story-wise, the game doesn't seem able to decide which of its ideas it wants to be about, or to have any sort of hierarchy regarding which elements should be focused on or treated as more or less important than others.  There's a plot hook very early on regarding two factions that is set up as though it's going to be core to the game, but the very few scenes where it comes up again only serves to directly undermine both itself and the other, unrelated efforts you're engaging in, until a point at the very end where it gets deus-ex-machina'd into an instantly-tidy resolution.  I wouldn't want any of it to be left out, but it's in dire need of better structure, pacing, and just a little less clumsiness in how the game tells you its stories.  (The particular way its ending is executed didn't subtract anything for me, though I don't disagree with the criticism I've seen some other folks give.)This is, I have to stress, only just on the side of negative rather than neutral - if you think it's for you despite all this, by all means try it.  It's not a bad game, just a flawed one.
