_childDocuments_.review: I have watched FixFox from its humble beginnings quite a few years ago (under its original name, Spacer) and I knew it will be the heart project, put together with the sheer will of a one-man army by a person, whose skills are matched only by his incredible dilligence. And yet, I was surprised by the result: By the scope of the landscape created, by the distinct flair of individual locations accompanied with perfectly matched music score, by the many things you can do in the game, which are not actually needed, but were put there just for fun of it (I'm looking at you, zipline!). Every now and then, you notice some detail that had to be immensely laborious yet it is not "necessary" per se: Shadows that change throughout the day. Slowly moving clockworks at the background of the underground base. Different music tunes, that played together compound themselves into yet another tune in a manner, that would leave J.S. Bach proud. These little details show that the person behind the game did not care about the effort needed, nor for the RoI KPIs, nor for the focus groups feedback. No, the only valid measure was the vision of the final product. It does not scream "look at me, I am beautiful" as some other games do, but if you listen closely, you will notice it is.And yet, this is not the best thing about this game. Nor are the quirky puzzles: If you come solely for the puzzles, you will probably leave a little bit disappointed. The fix jobs get repetitive rather quickly and while they still manage to stay strangely entertraining (I blame my borderline OCD for that), they do not force you into any serious thinking. There are some more creative puzzles woven throughout the game, but it's nothing you'd be required to put your serious thinking cap on. But that's OK, as these are not the point of the game. The point of the game - and its best feature by far - is its storyline.I dare to say that anybody who reviews FixFox before the final credits roll is doing the game the disservice. Because many things that can be seen and experienced throughout the game will fall into place only after its story is over. During the playthrough I sometimes felt that the dialogues were a wee bit too cheesy, or the tasks a little bit too quirky, or the story a little bit ... paper-y; and it seemed that even the characters in the game acknowledge that from time to time. Well, my fellow gamer, there is a reason for that. And my calloused cynical self was surprised and moved when I got to it. Or maybe I got soft with the age, I don't know. Go there. See for yourself. It's worth the time.Is this a "masterpiece"? Maybe; who am I to tell. But what I am sure of that this is the purest soul work I've seen in a long long time. Maybe ever.You did good, author. You. Did. Good.

_childDocuments_.review: SUMMARY: A chill, charming game of puzzle-solving via crafting and open world exploration with an extremely strong aesthetic and a surprising plot.  Crashland on a distant world, fix stuff with random junk, build robots, and eventually unravel a mystery!  Very much It's Own Thing, but if you like the whole collect-puzzle-storyline thing you'll probably enjoy it.FixFox is a game that screams "I have an idea and I am going to implement it!"  It's a game where a genetically engineered human with fox traits lands on a planet of robots, fixes things with band-aids and spatulas, and unravels a centuries old mystery.  With 16 bit style.You're Vix, a human in a time where everyone is genetically spliced (fur is great for survival, and hypernation allows hypersleep).  As part of the future run by benevolent AIs you're dispatched to a distant world despite your dodgy record to start up a navigtion beacon.  Thats when things go wrong - you loose your tools, the planet is run by very human robots, and battling factions keep the planet stagnant.So it's up to you to figure out what happened, help the inhabitants, and find your place in this wacky world.  Here's what it involves.FIXING: The name is FixFox?  You'll repair various devices with junk lying around.  This is fun (if not overly challenging if you're a hoarder) because you have to undo items, push switches, replace parts, and so on.COLLECT: You'll need that junk to fix things by stealing pirate hordes, doing jobs, trading, and using vending machines.  Everything has a purpose, and the mysterious Oraclebots can help you.TRAVEL: There's a big world with multiple zones you'll need to explore.  Fortunately you unlock more methods of transport over time (honestly, it feels like an embarassment of options, but they have their own points).PUZZLE: There's all sorts of puzzles you'll solve.  Most are pretty simple, but engaging enough to make you think.  Nothing is too hard, but you'll want to pay attention to dialogue.EAT: When you get food it reveals secrets.  Really, everyone who serves you gives you a clue.FOLLOW THE STORY: It's NOT simple, and in many cases is surprising, touching, or horrific.  There's a backstory to this game, far beyond "junk-obsessed fox person fixes stuff."All of this is done with 16-bit-ish graphics, a strong aesthetic, good sound, AND a very visceral, tactile game design.  Many elements like fixing and eating feel real because you pick items up, dust stuff off, move a spoon to your mouth, etc.  It draws you into the game.Is the game good?  I'd say yes because it's very clearly a tight, consistent vision that is well-realized.  FixFox is an experience as much as a game - it just depends if it's your kind of game.So if you like a light puzzler, wandering around, collecting things and getting resources, and want something with an interesting plot, give it a try.  FixFox scratches multiple itches.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cute game with beautiful colors, design, and music. The characters are lovable and you get attached to them easily once you start playing. As a person who does not play too many games and prefers the relaxing, go-at-your-own-pace type games, this is a winner for me! I like that it stops where you left off and gives you clues along the way to help you out (love you, Tin). I love solving puzzles and this one allows you to explore their vast world while doing so. You get big quests, little wild quests, and random things along the way that catch your attention. I appreciate the ability to go off and explore, and the availability of quests if I want to complete them. Overall very enjoyable game!

_childDocuments_.review: Super chill game with fitting good music. And I think it looks pretty good, definitely got a cohesive design.The puzzles aren't hard, but they do require some thinking, which I think is fitting for the overall tone of the game. The fixing gameplay was the reason this game caught my eye and while I do think it could have been expanded a bit more, it is thankfully NOT a game that relies on its "primary" feature as the sole feature, it has some variety among its mechanics making the majority of the game feel constantly fresh. _childDocuments_.review: Nice game! It is fun to get a resource hoarder/puzzler game with absolutely no combat. _childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly charming game. I especially love the idea of a game that manages to encapsulate some of that old school point-and-click "which object do I use on which thing" but without having strict 1:1 choices or frustrating dead ends. They made a clever choice to expose the properties of objects as a way to help you figure out which tools are needed to solve a puzzle, rather than just having to get into the mind of the game designer who thought "oh, use the rubber hose on the puddle to drain the water" or whatever. It's got a really unique set of challenges and mechanics. Also soup and pudding. Plus I'm a sucker for chunky pixels. The end.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! It has an amazingly pleasant combination of relaxed game play with exploration, humor, and visual beauty. For how relaxing it is, though, it is deep and complex - you can tell this game was made with much love because every detail feels handmade and deliberate. The exploration is very fun - it's really cool to learn of this world's history, the different natural environments, and the various forms of problem solving. As for the humor, Tin is such a great companion to have - funny, caring, and introspective. In many ways, Tin is the real human in this game.And the graphics are just gorgeous - neat visual solutions with color palettes that are just delicious to look at. Also, the animation of motion, events, and space itself are just absolutely phenomenal.$13 is a real steal for this game!Highly recommend for anyone looking for an honestly good time and a game that is overflowing with joy and beauty.

_childDocuments_.review:
FixFox is a wholesome sci-fi adventure game. Play as Vix, an unlucky space mechanic, who crashlands on a mysterious planet where tools are forbidden. Accompanied by her trusty toolbox Tin, Vix travels across the planet Karamel discovering hidden stashes left by pirates, repairing friendly household appliances, and sampling tasty local delicacies.

Traverse the planet on a peppy scooter, clear pathways with a hefty power loader, or simply go on a peaceful journey by foot to uncover all the landmarks on Karamel.

Hum along to catchy chiptunes while discovering secret locations, testing your noggin on whimsical puzzles, and finally settling down for the night next to a toasty campfire looking up at the starry sky.

name: Teslagrad 2
detailed_description: Discover another tower In the Magnetic North! Lumina, a young Teslamancer, finds herself stranded after her airship crashes in Wyrmheim, a remote and treacherous land to the North. Embark on a dangerous adventure, exploring a gigantic, abandoned tower looming over a fjordside valley, on a quest to get Lumina home and back to her family. Use electromagnetic powers to survive the dangers of a wild and untamed land. Defend yourself against Viking raiders, face gruesome beasts inspired by Nordic mythology, and triumph against epic bosses! As your journey progresses, you’ll discover new skills and equipment needed to uncover the secrets of the land and delve into the dark past of Lumina’s ancestors. Teslagrad 2 is the follow-up to the hugely popular physics-based game where electromagnetic powers are at the heart of survival. With improved visuals, a bigger world, and new puzzle-solving tools, Teslagrad 2 delivers a fresh and immersive puzzle-platform experience! Key Features Scandinavia Meets Metroidvania . The world’s first ‘Scandivania’ – a grandiose Steampunk-meets-Norse adventure accompanied by an orchestral soundtrack inspired by Nordic folk tones and electronic tracks. Magnetic Gameplay . Test your logic skills with perplexing puzzles based on real electromagnetic physics and enjoy a new twist with curved magnets! Master Fluid Motion . Perfect new and returning skills and use them to move quickly and skillfully through the world, combining Lumina’s abilities such as blinking, sliding, and magnetizing to build extra momentum. Epic Boss Battles . Use your skills to overcome boss fights which unlock new abilities and additional areas to explore. Visual Storytelling . Teslagrad 2 unfolds through what you see, with no text, voiceover or loading screens to interrupt gameplay. Explore an Abundant World . Discover rich and beautiful 2D hand-painted environments set in a wild and ravaged world full of hidden collectibles, secrets, and lore.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? It is a very good looking metroidvania, but without the typical combat. Actually, it is a quite unusual metroidvania. We play a little girl named Luminia (who first appeared in the game World to The West), who is hunted by humans and gets eaten alive by most animals or plants she encounters. She runs away as fast as she can from most foes, only sometimes she uses the environment to get a little revenge and kill an enemy. Lumina was flying along in her little zeppelin, when she got attacked and her blimp shot down in an abandoned region. The aim of the game is to return home. She is a Teslamancer, which means she controls electricity. She may not have an attack, but she starts the game with the ability to dash. Very soon she finds a dress with magical properties, which allow her to use magnetic force and polarities. At least I think that it is a magnetic force that allows her to run along walls or fly up in (magnetic?) currents. There is no speech in the game. There is also no text in the game. So some things might be a bit hard to understand - visual storytelling may be an art, but can't easily explain everything.During the game, Lumina learns new abilities by obtaining new equipment, which allow her to access areas that have been so far unreachable. A typical metroidvania game element - but the abilities are not typical. No walljump or double jump, but fast swimming or a block-breaking slide. Even the fast travel is different than in most metroidvanias. There are no teleporting portals, but there is a central hub and cables that Lumina can move on using her electromagnetic powers. So she can reach the various regions in the game, like the castle, a snowy mountain or the flooded caves.In the course of the game, you shouldn't expect direct confrontations with the enemies, especially at the beginning of the game. Lumina has no attacks and has to use her dash ability to move quickly and avoid certain death. She is attracted or repelled by certain platforms, and the main gameplay challenge is how to reach the next room while at the same time not getting killed by various deadly things (spikes, electricity fields...) or enemies. She often has to run while being chased by something deadly. While you learn to fight to survive in most metroidvanias, here you need to learn how to move fast, using your various abilities. There are some challenging, frustrating moments due to complex puzzle-platforming elements. Boss fights are also special, you have to think of ways to damage bosses without having an attack. If you die, you reappear at one of the many checkpoints. This is more like Limbo, there is no real punishment for dying, apart from being very annoying and having to go again through some places you already managed to survive.Gamepad is of course supported. To return home doesn't take too long, but there are 81 cards are hidden in the game for completionists. Also other stuff is hidden and not necessary to finish the main story, like extra abilities. The visuals and animations are amazing, the game is really a little beauty.A refreshing but short metroidvania where you don't kill (most of) your enemies, but simply outrun (-swim, -climb, -jump, -fly) them. Actually, it is more of a physics-based puzzle platformer than a classic metroidvania.

_childDocuments_.review: I am so disappointed in this game after completing it and the secret boss (for collecting all scrolls?), especially after I played and enjoyed the first Teslagrad. So much of the ride is good but not great, but the ending sours the whole experience, and left me feeling extremely angry with the game's failure to live up to expectations or even just function properly. I'll get into it after a few important nitpicks, just a heads up for mild spoilers, as Steam is incorrectly saying I've played for 5 minutes.The first minor issue I ran into is that the controls are quite janky. The physics-first approach means that you'll often glitch out (sometimes into walls when carrying boxes, which required a hard reset). Many times I would only jump, barely glance off of a wall or a slightly slanted floor, and end up flinging in a random direction completely off the map. This also ends up working against the way a tight metroidvania should work, because I could glitch myself into flying upwards or through walls into secret areas, way before I got the powerups I needed to get in the right way. Sort of fun in its own way, but it made the gameplay feel very amateurish.Second, guidance is not great. The map has blurry shadows for areas you haven't discovered yet, but unlike most metroidvanias it *still* has blurry shadows even when you've explored everywhere the game has to offer. You'll end up wasting hours in the wrong places trying to find a way in that doesn't exist, because every other blurry area nearby DID have a way in. Through glitch tactics I also got into a few secret areas that don't appear to be part of the game: the camera just gave up and stayed in the previous room, so I was walking around blind inside these rooms until they killed me or spat me back out. But most importantly, while the main path sort of tells you where to go next, there are so many activatable shortcuts and winding paths that it's anyone's guess what direction you should be heading. Many of the puzzles to advance in the main path also required obscure powerup combinations that are not taught to the player in any way (axe + magnet, for instance), which means you'll default to backtracking and then realize later that you could have kept going.Third, navigation sucks. There are no warp rooms, so if you fall off one of the many towers then enjoy replaying the last ten minutes of rooms again. When you're seeking out the scrolls you will be manually navigating from one corner of the map to the others, and many of them are hidden in little alcoves you will have to fall off of a cliff to get into, with the same issue of having to do it all over again if you mess up. Heads up that quitting the game will sometimes reset your checkpoint to the top if you miss, which will save you a ton of time if you don't want to solve the same puzzles over and over again. But in general I backtracked about five times as much as I wanted to, even for a metroidvania.Here's the real problem with this game though: the boss battles are just NOT fun. I think the developers even recognized this, because they put in some infinitely refreshing extra hit orbs at all of them, so you don't just die in one hit at every new untelegraphed attack pattern. Bosses are constantly doing unpredictable nonsense immediately, the hitboxes do not match their attack animations, and since any mistake restarts the whole fight, everything becomes trial and error to figure out what to do after you die to it the first few times. Most unfortunately, bosses are SLOOOOOW, and usually have a minimum of 3 phases with no checkpoints. If you mess up at the end when things get more difficult, you'll have a very long wait to even see the new attacks and learn how to dodge them.This is what turned my experience from "it's an okay game" to "fix your janky garbage!" The final 2 bosses take everything bad about boss fights and make it ten times worse. The first boss has two unskippable cutscenes that I ended up watching some 15-25 times, and an easy first phase that you have to do every time you mess up in the second phase. At this point you're loaded with abilities and only one of them can damage him in each of his two phases, so you have to fail a half-dozen times before you even figure out what to do, while his attacks immediately target you and instantly send you back to the beginning. But, for reasons I can only assume are an attempt at adding "difficulty", this time there are no extra hit orbs, no checkpoints, and a forced restart time of about 30 seconds waiting to try again, every single time you die. It turned "not fun" into infuriating, and I genuinely almost ragequit forever, which is something that never happens to me. The fight was designed by the developers to suck an hour away from you in the most hostile way possible, where half of the time you aren't even playing at all, and the other half of the time you're replaying the easy first phase, because there's no checkpoint at the halfway mark.The secret final boss was more of the same. Untelegraphed instant kills (including a third phase start-up that's a guaranteed kill until you see it), bad hitboxes that don't match the animations and even go outside of the (finally!) telegraphed attack areas, and a bad overall design involving spheres that makes the janky player physics your main enemy. Thankfully there is a checkpoint at the beginning and I got through this one quickly, but most of the time you will die because the physics didn't launch you high enough or your jump input was completely ignored. After this, the game ends so suddenly that I felt completely unsatisfied, and asking myself how much better it would have been if we had a boss where you used the magnet powers to dodge waves of colored red and blue balls, or slid on curves that caught fire, or moved through water streams to magnetically pull lasers towards the enemy. None of what made the exploration gameplay fun was ever showcased in the bosses, you just had to bash your head against a brick wall of unfair deaths and boring repetition until the stars of jank aligned.So, is Teslagrad 2 a good game? Unfortunately, no. It has all of the elements of a great metroidvania, but none of the heart of one. At its best there are moments of real inspiration, cool abilities, and fun puzzles. But the game plays it safe with all of these things, barely explores what you can do with them, feels unfinished and janky, and royally botches the ending. The relentless focus on combat was very silly considering none of your abilities are really combat focused, and directly contradicts what makes the game fun. It needed a tighter design more focused on puzzles, and less obsessed with trying (and failing) to be everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like here, but there's a few major flaws here that mean I must recommend against purchasing the game.  The first is a design issue - two actions (slide and ground slam) are mapped to the same button, and sometimes it seems they can activate on positive OR negative edge. So you can start a slide, jump, release slide, and slam yourself into a trap or deadly pit if you're lucky. If you're not lucky, you wind up losing a half an hour of gameplay and have to redo the last zone you're in.   The second one is that it is bizarrely easy to get softlocked - stuck in an area that the devs clearly didn't seem to think you'd return to at that point. Given the above issues with slamming unexpectedly, and the game's structure, this has happened to me twice in my just under 3 hours with the game. I like the game, but I'm not redoing the opening a third time.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: is a surprisingly fantastic platformer that has a brilliant movement system (once you unlock the initial abilities), great atmosphere with detailed background, and an enticing story said without words. The initial adventure in this game is short (3-4 hrs) but your adventure does not have to end since there are so much more to do after defeating the main boss. The second half of the game features 4 secret abilities unlocked behind simple time trial races, free roam to collect all the cards including one card hidden within an additional boss (golem) and discovering the "true ending" with a final boss that is very challenging. Exploring the map with this games movement system (specifically the slide momentum and upgraded electrical current dash) is a blast and reminds me of the fun continuous flow of movement seen in the  games. Would recommend this hidden gem to anyone that enjoys a solid platformer with great movement and puzzle mechanics. [10/10]
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, Teslagrad delivers a beautiful and artistic story though an enjoyable experience. Teslagrad 2 is a worthy successor to the predecessor. I still have much to unlock and explore, and thankful to have more so than the the first release. This map is larger and with more secrets and enjoyable powers to utilize in that exploration. However, I have completed the story. The story is enjoyable and family friendly, with cute and touching moments. The music is well done and is something that I could just enjoy listening to while working on my YouTube channel. I get moments where the music reminds me of The Witcher, another soundtrack that I thoroughly enjoy. The bosses this time are easier and harder. While in the first Teslagrad, I could time things a little more manually and handle the fights with practice. I felt that some of the fights in Teslagrad 2 were more chaotic in timing and lining up skills, while having less going on in the fight, as was sometimes the challenge in the first release.In short, Teslagrad 2 is highly recommended, as is the Teslagrad. These games are a worry free experience and family friendly. The boss fights can get stressful, but do not let that deter you from the overall experience. If this old man can do it, I know you can too.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you aren't playing Teslagrad you are missing out.The movement is so fluid and fun to play around with. The boss fights are so unique and epic. The music, backgrounds and general atmosphere are all top notch metroidvania without trying to be anything but itself.This is everything I could have ever wanted in a sequel and more. Absolutely worth it at full price
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Surprised by some of these negative reviews since to me it was better than Teslagrad (which I played directly beforehand - it drove me to buy this immediately) in every way. Beautiful painted sprites, great visual storytelling and compelling level design.Yes, it's pretty short, but it's all killer, no filler. The platforming feels better than the original and the art direction is amazing. The real final boss/true ending requires collecting all 81 optional cards, and unusually for one of these games I think that's actually worthwhile -- it's not too hard and optional areas are a *significant* percentage of the content. It's so gorgeous that running around is a treat.The only quibbles for me are that a) I wish it were longer, b) I got stuck twice and could've used some hints about mechanisms like repelling from thrown axes (I genuinely thought I was soft-locked), and c) seriously couldn't the checkpoint have been *after* his little animation with the painting? Unusually for a Metroidvania-type game there are no fewer than four optional/secret traversal powers that I'm not totally sure about, since they do effectively let you bypass certain puzzles/platforming sections. But I guess I shouldn't complain because I could not have beaten the final boss without them!
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: The art looks nice, but that's the highest point for this game. I struggle to recommend it. The physics are incredibly janky, I often found myself clipping through the floor and becoming softlocked. In a game where you die in one or two hits, bosses should not have unskippable cutscenes you have to endure each time, two of them for the penultimate boss even. The movement felt inconsistent and weird. Your slide, which is a key ability to move around with and should feel amazing, becomes crippled a while after you get it when they bind the ground slam to the same key, causing you to frequently slam into the ground while platforming. While the art is nice, the animations were also frequently bad, skipping frames and giving a jagged appearance in all sorts of places. Falling in particular looks very low effort. Overall, the game lacks polish and just has a thousand little things that prevent it from being great. I'd skip this one, even if you liked the first Teslagrad. The shift to action platformer is not to its credit.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: I love the first Teslagrad; it was short but lovely and a very original mix of a puzzle game (with a bit of platforming) and metroidvania. Teslagrad 2 changes the original formula more toward a platformer with puzzle elements and metroidvania; the magnetism powers are now more focused on movement. Unfortunately, the physics is not reliable enough to support this new direction for gameplay and often behaves unpredictably and randomly, making the game feel unpolished and frustrating during the fights with bosses (Teslagrad's idea for boss fights is that you need to repeat the sequence of moves a few times in the row without a mistake as you die after one hit and random physics gets in a way during these fights). It definitely has its own charm; the visuals and music improved a lot. I recommend Teslagard 2, but play the first one first; it's the better game.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Nice graphics, music and puzzles, similar to the original Teslagrad but less gloomy and more fun, reminds me of Ori and the blind forest.Edit : the game can be completed within 5 hours but there are many more complex puzzle to do to unlock everything. Currently 9h in and still not killed the final boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Annoying under every single aspect except visually and musically.Navigation is tedious both when going forward AND when backtracking (there are shortcuts but they either save little time or are far from the next one, making moving orizontally almost as annoying and repetitive as doing it vertically)Even if backtracking isn't your cup of tea you will still need to re-do some points, mostly because you died (sometime because of a skill issue, others because even the "parkour puzzles" are annoying, much more so if you have to get past them to get to an already visited area so backtrack at your own peril).The combat system probably gets more complex judging from Options>Controls but bosses have been, up until now at least, just damage phase (aka dodge dodge dodge) > do the thing (aka use one (1) singular ability in a specific way) 3 times to win, only exceptions being a golem which I could not damage and a snake that varied the fight with... having 2 damage phases between your "do the thing" phase. Your enjoyment of the bosses will most likely vary around how many times you get killed/have to redo a phase because of some goofy ahh hitbox or attack.Game looks good and music is kinda nice, lore is boring but the cards are very nicely made... other than that personally I can't find a single aspect of the gameplay enjoyable, and I got the game for like 20 cents through the profits from cleaning my Steam inventory, can't really recommend it :/
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Was pretty decent up till the final boss, which soured me on the whole experience.The first phase is alright, but then on the second phase the boss hits you with an attack which is impossible to avoid, unless you already know what to expect. On top of that the game takes away your second health point before the second phase, for no good reason. This leads you to get instantly killed. You then have to keep replaying the first phase, and watch both the unskippable cutscenes, till you figure out what to do in the second phase. Don't understand how this got past QA.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like Teslagrad 2.The first Teslagrad was an innovative puzzle platformer that was charming and pleasant. It was a little rough around the edges, but it's theming and puzzles were fun and delightful. Being able to accumulate different polaric powers was so exciting and memorable!This game fails to capture those feelings from the first game.First of all, the game is very short. I was able to complete the main story in less than 2 hours, which is terrible. Even the original game, while also short, was at least 6-8 hours long.Secondly, the powers can feel a bit awkward to maneuver with. Early on, you get lots of mobility powers but they feel extremely clunky and unsatisfying to use at times. I especially disliked the feeling of repelling myself away from magnets. For some reason, the physics were uncomfortable and it was hard to make it work.There's a power very late in the game that I thought was extremely innovative and clever, but since it's the last one you get, there's not a lot of time spent exploring the mechanic. Overall, this game was a huge letdown. I was looking forward to the sequel of the original Teslagrad having more powers, puzzles, and adventures to explore. Instead, it was an insultingly short adventure that was SHOCKINGLY lackluster.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the first Teslagrad and wanted to support the developer by buying their second game. Unfortunately, it wasn't nearly as good or polished as the first.The controls are loose and they often bug out. For a platformer, this is a cardinal sin.The bosses are also boring and obnoxious. Not fun at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Quite simply, Teslagrad 2 takes all of the elements that made Teslagrad 1 great, and cranks them into overdrive.The Story: Preserving the same methods of silent storytelling as the original, T2 links T1 and World to the West together to make a seamless cohesive storyline. Seemingly innocuous background art from T1 is given massive significance in T2, and new story elements introduced in T2 are deliberately left a bit vague so they can be expanded in future games. Characters have complex motives which gives them a lot of depth.The Music: Jørn Lavoll outdoes himself. Fire up the game and listen to the title screen music. Just listen, let it develop. It didn't have to be that good since most people will just spam a button to get to the menus, but what an intro. Many more musical styles are explored here, ranging from heavy metal to jungle to whimsical, with plenty of callbacks to music from T1.The Gameplay: Movement is much more fluid and rewarding. Blinking, a core ability from T1, is given to you from the very start of T2. Sliding was an ability cut from T1 but brought back in T2, and the levels embrace it in plenty of places, with slopes everywhere to launch from. Simple platforming and very mild puzzles lead up to the first boss, but then the puzzle platforming begins to show its true robustness, with new puzzle elements supported by the new item collectibles. Lots more variety in terrain, and some very-appreciated "fast-travel checkpoint" options to get around the much larger map. The boss fights start easy and ramp up to very hard if you're going for all achievements.This game is a masterpiece. If you liked Teslagrad 1 in any capacity, this is a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not even five hours of playtime to beat the game, worst designed final boss design I've seen in many years. First phase is very annoying and second phase one shots you in just a couple of seconds. With no hints or idea what to do about it, there is no autosave which makes the boss repetative, annoying and unfun. Overall the whole game is filled with incredibly bad design choices. For one thing there are collectibles, as if it was a metroidvania (this is not a metroidvania) its a railroad game where you can backtrack to find collectibles. The problem is backtracking is VERY slow and there are no teleports in this game, meaning if you fall down in the wrong place, time to redo all the platforming you just spent several minutes to get through. The game is designed to traverse long distances fast, but sadly the game is very zoomed in so there are many times you don't have time to see deadly obstacles before you are killed by them. Its like many different people designed different parts of the game without talking about how they would work together. Since you can't see things in time most of the platforming is done throwing your face into the unknown, get flamed/crushed/speared and then redoing it when you know what to expect.The difficulty is very uneven, the final boss is very hard and there is one or two other bosses that is quite challenging but the rest of the game is a breeze. The platforming is very easy while bosses are not, overall it doesn't feel cohesive. The storytelling is also very poorly done, it doesn't make sense in the world and is just pushed in your face, in the form of nonsensical small videos in weird places. In the first place, I don't know who I am, where I am or what I am doing. Why am I supposed to care about some small video of vikings fighting eachother? Very low immersion for me.Some music tracks were good and that's probably the most positive I can say about the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: A well-made game that is a lot of fun. Exploring the world is a very entertaining experience and the magnetism abilities play quite smoothly. The game can easily be played through in a few hours, but for all the achievements you have to collect all the cards hidden on the map. This, on the other hand, takes much longer but is still a lot of fun. The puzzles in the game are all relatively easy to solve. The only negative thing about the game are the boss fights. Each fight is very short and can usually be solved immediately by repeating the same move. Nevertheless, it is a very enjoyable game that is definitely worth buying. You don't necessarily need to have played the first part to understand the story, which you learn along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: This has the buttery smooth performance of rayman legends and none of the buttery smooth controls of rayman legends. Indeed, it is extremely obvious the devs never played any rayman games before as they would have designed the controls so much better if they had. It is also literally impossible to keep track of ability gates in this game so you are forced to enjoy it as a puzzle game rather than a metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, I'm 2 hours in and I'm enjoying it.   Here's the issue I'm having; I'm playing it on the steamdeck and it crashes.  It doesn't crash during the areas where I am playing the game, it crashes during the cut scenes.  I've restarted it and it skips the cut scene and I can play the game.  I am at area right now where the cut scene is large and I cannot proceed any farther it just stops, can't go any further.My current recommendation is to play this on your pc. If you are playing it on the steamdeck, wait until it's verified.  I'll change my recommendation once it's verified for the steamdeck and I can play it with little to no issues..
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first one, and love almost everything about this one, but the controls are a bit off with this one, there are a lot of out of bounds bugs that render your save file useless, unless you go into the save and manually edit your spawn point. And for some reason it stutters and freezes sometimes. If I could give a mixed option, I would chose that one. I am 50/50 about this game. Oh and the game is ridiculously short too.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Teslagrad 2 is a decent game and a good sequel.It is shorter than the prequel but more polished.Made by Norwegian indie devs, this time they tried to merge the Teslapunk genre with Scandinavian culture and lore.Nordic inspired music plays in the viking village, electronic music plays inside the technologically advanced towers.The art is beautiful and the style is more polished.The skill based agility puzzles are a bit difficult but not that hard.The level design is intuitive and the harpoon checkpoints allow for easy fast travel.The Teslamancer abilities are cool and fluid to use, very enjoyable.The boss fights are easy once figured out, but learning the patterns is hard when you die in 1 hit.I know that's just how the Metroidvania genre is, but is really annoying.Especially the final boss fight. They didn't learn and repeated the same as in the prequel, a multi-phase fight where if you die at any stage, you have to restart from the very beginning, travel to the boss room and watch the unskippable cinematic.(now you remember that you die in 1 hit and you'll understand how this becomes frustrating..)To get the True Ending, you must collect 4 secret abilities. Doing so also unlocks the secret map that reveals all 81 collectible scrolls.Most achievements are tied to the collectibles as they reveal the lore and story. Teslagrad 2 uses visual storytelling but the made-up Norwegian writings on the walls do not have English translation or subtitles (how are we to figure them out if not look up on the internet).Hopefully we see our protagonists Nikola and Lumina again.Fascinating world, waiting for Telsagrad 3 !
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: its mid, the returning mechanics are good but the new ones are meh plus it only took me 2.4 hours and i didnt play too fast. To explain further there is multiple upgrades but its kind of pointless since the only point for the last one is a few doors and to hit the final boss 3 mins after you get it. alot of the weakpoints for the bosses are not very communicated and the art and story is very bad at points (the scene you get the last upgrade as example) to conclude i'd say get it on discount if you need a teslagrad fix.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice, short & sweet Metroidvania. I dont think I've played anything like it before. It's truly a breath of fresh air. It's not trying to be a soulslike (or Hollow Knight). It has its own unique flavor. Can't believe it has flown under the radar! Highlights:+ Beautiful art+ Great music soundtrack & vocals+ The main character has great movement right at the beginning of the game!+ Amazing traversal powers: Teleport, Moving around upside down, etc. Just a joy to control.+ Wonderful physics+ No corpse runs or any other "Dark Souls" mechanics that will waste your time Cons- Story might not be terribly clear since it's all communicated to you visually- The short length will prob scare away a few - No replay options beyond side quests after you finishI really loved this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: I had played Teslagrad a while ago and really wasn't expecting a followup to that first opus; so I was pretty glad seeing a second one was being released, and quite curious about it,My fist impressions are that, it doesn't disappoint: the graphical art is a bit similar in some points to the first one, while being a tad more colorful, and I was surprised to see that some elements, as well visual as musical, were reminiscent of Ori and the Blind Forest (the visual resemblance at some point, concerning some nature elements, such as trees, waterfalls as well as some foes, is rather staggering). The music is very beautiful too imo, and corresponds well to the sceneries of a slavic / nordic folklore. So artistically, it's a continuation of the first which doesn't break off too much from it, while presenting a certain evolution.As for the gameplay, simply said, the controls are easy to learn while hard to master, given the situations you will be put into - I died a lot for the time I started to play the game, but the automatic save points were placed in a *very* fair way, made apparently to not frustrate the player - otherwise, there are many passages and sections that are rather tricky, and if you fail it's only a chance to do it again, to better handle the lightning based character's actions.....I need to play more of this, have just started it but felt compelled to write a review anyway - it's with no doubt a game which quality stays faithful to the first one's,and once again glad this game came out. Just a tiny bit puzzled this game doesn't have more reviews - but it might be logical, as another metroidvania of the same sort (Rusted Moss) was released just one week before, and Teslagrad 2's release might have been a bit overshadowed by Rusted Moss' one; I hope in any case that Teslagrad 2 meets some good success because it would be frankly deserved. A followup worthy of praise, beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome little game, it's a lot of fun to play. The art style and music are amazing. The one fault I have is with the super frustrating map. It shows openings where there are none, walls where there are openings, and generally is useless. I can't count how many times I planned a path, only to have to turn around because of a dead end which isn't shown on the map. Otherwise, great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: I played both Teslagrad 1 and Teslagrad 2 back-to-back and I can just honestly say: Teslagrad 2 is not only a much, MUCH better game, it might also one of my favorite games of the year.Instead of relying on the magnet-based abilities from the first game, Teslagrad 2 instead gives you the short-range teleport from the start and just expands from there. Both it and the later traversal abilities make it a joy to get around the game world, and the devs know it too, giving you plenty of opportunities to do slick movement through it. The world itself also looks a lot nicer, since it's no longer confined to a single tower and can actually show off different biomes and also now features a fast travel option to get easily back to previous areas which is very much appreciated since there's also a lot more optional areas to explore (including some secret powerups and even bosses)Speaking of bosses, they are also not only better designed, but also give you an extra hit before each fight, reducing a lot of the trial and error that plagued the first game's boss fights.Overall, Teslagrad 2 is just a huge step up from the prequel. My only real gripe is that the map, while more useful, does not let you set markers yourself to keep track of stuff you might want to check out later. But that is really just a minor annoyance more than anything.As mentioned above, I played Teslagrad 1 & 2 back-to-back. I couldn't wait to be done with Teslagrad 1, but when I finished Teslagrad 2, I hopped right back in there to explore the world just a little bit more. So yeah, Teslagrad 2 is highly recommended, if you are a fan of Metroidvanias, do NOT sleep on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Way less janky than the first one and actually a pretty fun moveset, it's pretty short and there's secrets to find after finishing it but while I found the platforming fun, the game didn't manage to keep me interested enough (the map is pretty lackluster, and no annotation doesn't help to remember some places you would like to recheck)
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty huge downgrade from the first game. The second instalment feels like an early access or beta rather than a finished product. The gameplay is not responsive enough, the bosses are quite boring, the exploration is not fun and even though certain sections are padded (having to jump down and then redo a platforming section because the flower that gives you levitation is only on the lowest level as opposed to there being another one halfway through) the game is only 3h long. I wouldn't have minded the length if the end product felt polished, with an engaging gameplay mechanic. Instead we have bland powers which feel awkward to use and frustrating rather than engaging bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic sequel that improves upon its predecessor in almost every way. Beautiful hand drawn art and animation, fantastic soundtrack.While in the first game you were stuck in a tower trying to climb it by solving puzzles. here you get to explore the world of Wyrmheim and see a variety of open world locations.There's plenty of additions and new abilities you can use that makes traversing the world quick and exciting. it's especially good for end game if you decide to find all the cards (which I would recommend as you get to solve extra puzzles, and earn new abilities!) Works great on Deck, but using the default proton settings you cannot open the map. After selecting proton experimental I was able to open the map and complete the entire game without issues.Good power draw, 8-10 Watts, so you can play for about 5 hours on a full charge.If you love puzzle platformers, metroidvanias or good games in general you gotta try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game, it took me ~10 hours to 100% it, and i felt like it derserves more positive reviews, than it currently has. Being a successor to Teslagrad, it's a puzzle platformer with metroidvania elements, but this one is more refined than the first part. Visuals are great, controls became better, bosses are somewhat creative and it genuinely felt good to play
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: okay, after being disappointed by all the unpolished mechanics of the game and writing this review, I somehow returned to it and cleared it again last time. And second time was mostly fun! You really can get used to all these quirks.Previous version of review is here (and remember, it was negative one). All these points still apply (game being short and some mechanics being unreasonably underdone), so be careful if those are dealbreakers for you.1. 3 hours to kill final boss and get first ending, 6 hours for completionist run.2. Game tries to be precise platformer from time to time, while having awfully inertial physics and really clumsy controls. Final boss and true final boss are especially guilty of this. Moreover, one of your optional upgrades could make final boss harder and you can't disable it :)If you love Teslagrad 1 and want to experience its style all over again, buy it; otherwise save your money for something better.  This game really is 6 hours, out of which 4 are okayish metroidvania and 2 are frustration over your character not sticking to magnetic platforms/spheres and flying outside of screen instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Solid animation and music, but somehow the gameplay and exploration leave a little to be desired.It is quite different than the first one. More than puzzles it's more about platforming. It gives the game a quick feel to it. However, even though it seems like one big map and you are finding new abilities, there really isn't any required backtracking so it feels like a strange not really metroidvania.  It feels a bit like fast past high end action game for smartphones.On PC it feels like it is lacking something, but is still probably a good buy on sale for people who like the animation.  It's very short, but....  also with the current game design it would probably wear out it's welcome if it was much longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: !!!!!!!PLEASE READ BEFORE BUYING.!!!!!!!Aw sh*t, here we go again...Jokes aside, I played the first instalment in the teslagrad series and I'm here to tell you that, as a whole, I enjoyed this game more than the first and the developers from Rain Games fixed most of the issues plaguing the first game... sorta. It's kinda like they took five steps forward, but one back. Lemme explain...UPGRADES OVER THE FIRST: Art and environments are even better than the first. These guys have an eye for beautiful environments and they know how to blend 2d and 3d assets well with beautiful parallax backgrounds too.The world feels a bit more open and backtracking doesn't suck. It's actually quite fun to zip around and find all the cards littered across the game world.Soundtrack is still awesome as always. Please, give the composers a raise!!! And that lady humming in the background when you're in the central village can take my money and empty my account... The music is THAT GOOD!Story is still pretty awesome. I had a bit more trouble understanding this one, but the world building is still very much on point!Gameplay is fun as hell, especially sliding and jumping and using magnetism with your axe and the puzzles and the bosses (for the most part) are more enjoyable for me here. The physics system is even more impressive and DAMN IT'S SO GOOD! But seriously, I could slide around the village all day. My gosh, it's so much fun... Until when it isn't.SHORTCOMINGS: Unfortunately, this is mostly in gameplay dept. While the physics system is very intricate and fun, it also creates avenues for the game to just go off the rails and for the the physics to react in the way it's not supposed to. The physics based movement is pretty realistic, but sometimes that's not fun as in some stressfull scenarios, that really gets annoying cuz your movement may feel funky. It's a little hard to explain, but if you play against the FINAL boss, you'll know what i mean. Sometimes, it just breaks and it can become frustrating. Sometimes the realism means you only have a small window to make the right move or you're deep in doodoo.Another area where the gameplay falls a bit short is the diffiiculty. It's smooth sailing for the most part and compared to the TREMENDOUSLY FRUSTRATING FIRST GAME, this is a lot tamer and it's better for it. The only down side is that the two last bosses are on a whole different level from everything else in the entire game. SHEESH! It got too difficult too quick. It was so bad that I only beat the second final boss due to a bug that caused her to stop attacking me completely. THAT IS NOT FUN AT ALL, ESPECIALLY SINCE THIS IS SUPPOSED TO BE THE CLIMACTIC END TO AN HONESTLY GREAT JOURNEY!Overall, I still think this game is very much worth your time and money. It's paced well, gorgeous and very fun, save for a few annoying moments and a disappointingly hard and somewhat unfair final stage.THANKS FOR READING THIS VERY LONG REVIEW AND I WISH YOU ALL THE VERY BEST! HAVE A WONDERFUL DAY!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game does many things very well. Compared to the original game, it does some things better, and a few things worse. On the plus side, the powers have gotten more fun - in particular, once you are kitted out, movement is incredibly fun with your powers. You zip along on water and land, zap through wires, engage with a lot of twisty ramps and paths straight out of 2d sonic - all kinds of good stuff. The puzzles take advantage of this in a good way, most of the time, and the "extra" puzzles are engaging. The final boss is a brilliant use of the blink ability as an action puzzle tool, and the Final Final boss is an excellent use of the polarity cloak. On the "neither good nor bad" side of things, the art style for our MC is a little less substantive, though very well animated, and the art direction is a tad more polished but a little less cohesive? For example, the snow peaks just cut in, without transition.  on the negative side, the bosses, with the exception of the final one (and the final final one), are sort of dull. Teslagrad 1 had "simple" bosses, too, but they were a lot more imaginative and felt better to fight with. For example, in the first game, you had to teleport into one boss to get them to be struck by lightning, dodged wind sweeps and bomb enemies, and the arena fell apart. Second boss. This second boss, you...dodge through it, dodge through it's minions, and dodged through it's lightning attack. It's only slightly faster paced, but given the cooldown on your dodge, this meant the battle had more cheap deaths, and was more frustrating, while also being easier and more boring. The only two bosses that remotely feel great use...your first ability (plus the axe to attack), and the the polarity cloak - your second upgrade (plus it's enhanced version). The boss for sliding is incredibly easy and boring, the down slam boss is simplistic in the extreme, and the first two bosses are so simplistic you can almost sleep through them. I don't know who was on enemy design, but I just went back to Teslagrad 1 - the bosses were almost all superior, versus the equivalents here, mechanically. The deplorable - the basic movement is janky. And not just slightly. there are jitters and glitches in the basic run and fall animation, and the game loses track of your location regularly, to a slight degree. For example, early on you run from a monster girl - you'll know her when you see her - Well, initially I was fairly close to her. and then the game glitched the movement, and I was 2 body-lengths ahead. In most areas, these occasional but pretty regular issues weren't too much of a problem, but they can play absolutely merry hob with any sort of complicated or precise platforming. It is very clear the devs polished the power systems well, and skipped some QA work on the really early, basic systems instead. Which is a great shame,

_childDocuments_.review: Freakin Nailed it again.Rain Games has Released another gem among their catalog of games.For those of you playing a Rain game for the 1st time, Don't worry about missing out on lore.  The game does a fantastic job of guiding you thru the lore even if you haven't played Teslagrad or World to The West via collectibles and on scream prompters.If you'd REALLY like to know the story, I recommend playing Teslagrad 1 and WttW.  Mesmer as well for the additional world building but it's not essential.BACK TO THE GAME!Oh boy! You're in for a puzzle Metroidvania Collectible and it's an electrifying time!  This game takes place Alongside Mesmer, RIGHT after World to the West.You've crash landed from being pursued and must make your way. TO THE TOWER!!!You'll puzzle solve, use sweet fluid magnetic controls, platform, have boss fights, EPIC BANGER MUSIC SLAYIN IT, and collectibles with lore pieces scattered thru out the world map. The game doesn't hold your hand BUT, it is VERY intuitive. The game clocks at about 3-6 hours depending on how skilled you are at platforming metroidvanias. It is an absolute spark of a gem and well worth the 20$ dollars + some if you play the original Teslagrad.The artwork and 3d models is fantastic, the BGMS slay again, and the.... in game nordic language? all bow wrap this present with a resounding boom and thunderous delivery.10/10 I hope more people see how wonderful these Game Devs are and give their other games a shot!Mad Respect for a Norwegian Game Studio! You will ALWAYS have the tools to get out of an area you are in that you can currently access.as a reminder,  once you have the axe, you can repel yourself against it + jump for a SUPER MEGA JUMP.You should be able to get out of ANY area if you do this right.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kinda... schyzophrenic?The main path to the normal ending plays like a linear puzzle platformer where you occasionally get new traversal abilities. It's very short (2-3 hours depending on whether you get stuck on puzzles and challenges), often frustrating and not fun.Then, there's the optional stuff. You need to get four (very well hidden) additional abilities to unlock the true last boss and true ending, plus you can find 81 card, most of which require little platforming challenges to get. This is where I started to have fun but for bad reasons. You see, I didn't have fun because it was more interesting than the main path but because the new abilities gave me more control on my aerial movement.Speking of which, one of the huge issues with this game is aerial movement, due to the fact that the physics engine (and most platforming challenges) uses momentum and positioning to the extreme. Meaning that if you don't do exactly what the game wants you to do, you will fail. Most often, you will try something again and again until one of two things hapen:- you give up and try something else which doesn't work, and something else, and something else again until you realize that your first choice was good but you didn't perform correctly- you eventally succeed but you don't know what you did differently from you 1000 previous attempsThe second huge issue is that the game does a very bad job at explaining how to use your abilities. Sometimes, it doesn't even explain them at all. There's at least one move that is required to progress but the game NEVER tells you that you can do it.The third huge flaw are the enemies: you have 1 HP and most enemies are placed in trap positions. The bosses are even worse: they are either boring because you need to dodge their attacks for a long time until they become vulnerable or they are frustrating because their actions (and those of the enemies they summon) are random so victory is only a matter of luck.Some more flaws.- The camera is too close to the character so, often, you will die from traps that you just couldn't know were there.- No fast travel; there are shortcuts but it's not nearly enough.- By default, the map only shows the layout of the explored areas (which isn't even alway accurate), your position and the position where you got abilities. You can't even put markers to remind you of places that you can't access yet. When you have all four bonus abilities, you can get an upgrade that shows where the cards are but it's too much and too late.There are some good things in the game, such as the art style and the fact that every main ability has several uses but it's not nearly enough to counterbalance all the bad things.TL;DR: Bad game, don't buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: What happens when you mix Teslagrad 1 with Celeste? This beauty.This game is just incredible. It takes everything that was fun in the first Teslagrad, and turbo-charged it. The movement options are incredible and can really be pushed very, very far, but the game is balanced for more casual players, making it a game that is easy to learn, but hard to master. Some bossfights will make you cry, though, but keep going =p.Visually, the game is beautiful. There are so many details hidden in the environment that you could stop anywhere in the game and look in the background to find something interesting. The animations are incredible, and the attention to detail is off the charts. Lumina bends when on a slope, each new item changes her appearance, and she even put on her hood when she's in a wet area, only to remove it when she's in an interior. Some background animations lack a bit of frames and stutter a bit, yeah, but these are rare occurences. The music is just WOW. The music in Teslagrad 1 was good, but it was mainly ambiant music that blended into the game. For the sequel, Jorn Lavoll completely became mad with power. With multiple singers and across multiple music styles, the OST is absolutely amazing. Ambiant, metal, orchestral, "viking", the soundtrack is so diverse and huge that you WILL find a music that suits you. Probably one of the best soundtrack I've heard since NieR: Automata.The story is built upon everything that was setup in the first game and in World to the West. You don't *need* to play these two games to enjoy the story, but knowing what they are about greatly helps. As usual, the story is not shown to you clearly and you could do the whole game without even noticing there is one. If you want to understand everything, you will have to look for details, analyze the scrolls that the game gives you and even translate old norse written in a custom alphabet. But it is worth, because the story is really great. When you play the game again after understanding the story, the cutscenes really hits different.Obviously, the game is not perfect, there are some little bugs and improvements to do here and there, but Rain-Games is known to support their games and update everything that needs to be updated, so don't let a couple of oddities fool you. This is an absolute banger and you must play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Teslagrad 2 oozes with Norwegian spirit, the environment, the characters, the music.Sequel features more combat and moving around quickly, with dozens of secret rooms. But it also requires a lot less thinking, the puzzles are more about execution and precision.The main story is nearly same length as the first game, so don't expect the game to be long (out of my hours 2-3 were the game running on background). If you will only play the main story the game might even feel lacking, so I highly recommend finding the secrets. The optional rooms also have the most challenging rooms in the game while the main story is easier this time (but just like before, the final boss is not a total pushover which I appreciated).The controls were mostly fine, but they could've still been more refined. Same with the magnetic physics, now and then completely unexpected bounces happen (which might or might not benefit you). And obtaining certain powers can cause problems when you would not want to use them (The ground pound move in general happened accidentally a lot, and the blink axe power against the final boss where enemies are often behind wires made it harder to hit them.)The magnetic axe is a great idea. a double jump exists in the game, but using the axe to help launch yourself in the air lets you do very high jumps. Without the magnetism it would've been just a God of War's Leviathan Axe ripoff. I also enjoyed how fast you can slide.I was disappointed that there is still no method to warp between areas, especially now that the map is larger than before. It makes returning to places more cumbersome when you have to claw yourself back out from wherever you go. And think twice before dropping down, I had to repeat entire areas more than once because I fell down and the game autosaved the moment I landed. So my tip is, if you're falling big time without meaning to, quickly exit the game before the autosave makes you swear.Playing the game on release, there weren't many guides out there, but I was able to fully complete the game thanks to a map you can find that lets you see where the collectables are. It did take me a lot of digging around to find it though.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is seriously amazing. The movement system, more specifically the slide momentum, carries this game. The art style is impeccable and the soundtrack is astonishing. Also, the secrets are some of the most fun parts of the game, including getting all collectables, they are where the game truly shines the most. Leaving a lot to get at the end makes the game have a bit of an open world experience at the last stretch, which feels incredibly fun to do.The only major complain I have is that it's really, REALLY short. Being able to beat the main story of a game this amazing in UNDER 2 HOURS kinda casually is just insane (I played it in another platform and kinda speedran it, that's why the 2.2 hours)Still, it doesn't make it bad, somehow I still feel like it was worth the price, considering how stupidly happy I was playing it!

_childDocuments_.review: A game never learn from their mistakes a decade ago...The good side first: great art, lovely character, intrigue world-building, and speechless storytelling!But that's not what make (any) game become a good game. No. Games need "gameplay" in order to make it memorable/enjoyable!And that's what lack from this title.Admittedly, the core idea of the game that explore "electromagnetic" mechanic is charming. Build a platforming world with north/south magnetic field here and there, while let the player to switch on/off their character became a psudo-magnetic object in order to solve the puzzle. Sound fun and challenging and have a lot of potential interesting levels. Implementing it right and the game might join the greatest puzzles of all time club (notable members: Fez, Portal, Baba is You, Patrick's Parabox, etc).However, this game ruin the opportunity. Even with the second chance.The magnetic mechanic itself is so clunky! Yes, the physics was implemented realistically, e.g., jumping is projectile. But does the game  need that realistic aspect, like putting realistic first and player intention later (not to mention that the control is not tight at all)? Combined with the continuously coordination and curved platforming everywhere, now each jump is crucial since a slightly different initial angle/position result in huge different outcome momentum. Which the game take a sadistic path that require you to make perfect jump and maintain correct momentum multiple times in a row.Furthermore, a room in this game is too large with too less checkpoints. A misjump at the last part of the platforming section will cost you a minute, because now you need to redo everything from start of the room, again.The annoying platforming is one thing. But boss fights take the frustration to another level.Basically, you have 1 HP.Really? In 2023??? When other games in the industry concern about accessibility and have option to subdued these frustrations, let player enjoy the game the way they like. (And, maybe, after they beat the game once, they might comeback for the intentional experience later!)Duck, even Dark Souls allows mistakes!!!Bosses also have no HP-bar (we all know that each boss have 3 HP in this game). The only indicator is embedded in the visual representation of the boss (like, there are 3 locks on the boss character, dealing a damage removes a lock). This design might looked immersion, however in this game it's only bring frustration. That is you will never be sure if you have dealt the damage successfully onto the boss. So good luck with the moose boss, which is only the second one in the game.Honestly, whose the target audience of this amazing world-building but punishing gameplay?I don't understand why the developer  develop a game this  (in a bad way). I don't wanna even use the word "hard" or "challenging", because the game is unforgivably difficult to the point that it is not fair to play the game anymore.So, if you enjoy torturing yourself, like playing Getting Over It (by yourself, not just watching YouTuber screaming in pain). Then this game might be perfect for you.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent metroid-like with a wonderful visual style, stunning animation and very satisfying controls and movement. The first game was charming, but proved quite frustrating to play because of how floaty the platforming could feel despite how demanding the game got. Teslagrad 2 thankfully has none of that. It can still be a challenging game, but moving around, jumping, climbing, zipping, all feels and looks fantastic. It also does a thing I love, but not enough metroid-likes do correctly: you get new abilities, but they are not just to open an arbitrary door and then nothing else. All the moves you acquire add to your movement and attack options, making navigating the environment quicker and more enjoyable each time. It's wonderful stuff, and I had a great time zooming around back and forth, finding everything on my own. It's not a very long game, I would imagine a normal playthrough will take you about 3-4 hours, and then a few more depending on if you try to find all the scrolls and secrets. I recommend it, as there is a ton of world building and environmental storytelling to discover through this. It took me 8 hours in total and I thoroughly enjoyed my time.The 100% secret final boss is REALLY tough, but it was very satisfying completing the game. Gorgeous artstyle and wonderful animation, fantastic soundtrack, great world building and wordless narrative. I'm excited to see what the developers will do next in this world, as this is stellar work and an excellent metroid-like well worth playing.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to put a natural stance on this as while a really nicely made game it has some really big problems that the developers need to improve in.The main  for me is the wonderful music, worldbuilding and enviromental storytelling (my favourite!). It is genuenly fun playing through  sections. Really good placement for secrets. I'm sure there is more that doesn't come off from the top of my head.The main . The two main problems for me are: room/checkpoint design and controls (I played on a controller, can't say for keyboard). Get it with at least 25% or so off (it's a 3-6 hour game tops), and after you beat the moose boss decide if it was frustrating for you or not. You should probably still be in the first 2 hours and be able to refund if it is too bad for your taste, perfectly reasonable. I think the final boss is way more problematic than the moose was, I will probably never truly finish the game because of it sadly, however up until that I did have a great time.

_childDocuments_.review: (Review edited after 100%ing the game)The main storyline feels a bit short and initially a bit confusing, with too many seemingly one-off characters. This is later compensated with the scrolls and visual storytelling elements. In other words, the story is broad, not long, and leads to an exploration-based gameplay (I feel this is the reason for some players not liking the game -- they just go for the main story, and that's okay). There is no better thing to do than explore the expansive, unique, diverse world.And how better to explore a world this beautiful than with the amazing movement system. It comes at an expense to some variety in puzzles though; some mechanics feel like they have unused potential. The game does introduce quite a few of them, with many underused or one-offs too, like the initial barrage from the airship. A few player abilities feel like they trivialize too many puzzles and some features probably should have a bit more polish, for example the map fog-of-war.Additionally, there are several quality-of-life improvements over the original, like additional map markers, "fast-travel", adding an extra hit point for boss fights, and the secret map. These are really really good.The visuals are better that the original, and that one was S-tier. The only downside is perhaps a tiny bit of inconsistency between the hand-drawn parts and some animations. And the music is unrivaled. Absolutely mesmerizing, beautiful and full of wonders. Wow!Conclusion: this game is burdened by massive expectations from it's predecessors, but I honestly think it lives up to them. It isn't just a continuation of the story though; it is something new too. There are some things that could, and should, be improved though. Finally: the game gets better, the latter you are in the story. It's great all along and epic at the 81-scroll finale. 9.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun to play and has a great atmosphere that feels very rich while barely bogging down the pace with long exposition or cut-scenes. Compared to Teslagrad 1, this is what I would want from a sequel. Spiritually the same while functionally  being very different. While I loved the first game, this makes the original feel rather slow, small, and clunky; especially in its movement and precision. This makes the platforming and puzzling a fair bit more forgiving (and I'd say the puzzles themselves are probably a bit easier) but personally I'd say the fact you can solve some levels in multiple ways (depending on your progression and how much secrets you've unlocked) is an improvement.If you like head-scratching puzzles over puzzles that test your motor skills you'll probably end up still liking Teslagrad 1 more; but I doubt you'll end up disappointed with its sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I played through Teslagrad Remastered and Teslagrad 2 back to back, 100%ing both. The real second half the game is collecting all of the cards. Once you do this there is an additional challenge, and collecting them all is really fun once you unlock all abilities. The game is worth the price, but look out for deals if you aren't sure. Pros:Art styleMusicNumber of abilitiesLevel/Puzzle DesignCons: Lack of a real fast travel systemMagnetic mechanics don't perform well around cornersGame does not tell you the additional ways to use the abilities (with axe, hold blue cloak, throw axe and hit jump at same time to launch very high)

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could say this game is worth your time and money but the controls are super floaty and the exploration is not particularly interesting, I didn't finish the game because the final boss is complete bs and has multiple phases and will one shot you (you get one free hit at every boss but due to the floaty controls it's really easy to lose that freebie so after dying immediately on the 2nd phase and being put back to before the first phase I quit it's not worth my time and I don't really think it would be worth anyone else's.it has some interesting ideas but the boring world, story, and floaty controls leave me wishing I was playing a better game.it kinda feels like someone wanted to make their own version of Ori and the Will of the Wisps and used Teslagrad as a setting but didn't really know what they were doing.
