_childDocuments_.review: I've played the first game out of pure curiosity, since it was free at the time thanks to my PS Plus subscription. I wasn't a big fan of the metroidvania genre yet, and I had no expectations. Even tho the game didn't blew my mind, I really enjoyed it, for many reasons : its watercolor style, its unique magnet mechanics, the mystery surrounding the story, the great score, and even the bossfights, as painful as they were !I tried to convince some of my friends to play it, even gifted it to someone, but I felt like not many shared my viewpoint. I discovered later, actually while searching for answers playing the second title, that a lot of people didn't apreciate it as much as I did.Anyway, when I saw the announcement for the second game, I was very much hyped. It made its way to the top of my wishlist instantly, and I waited for the right time to buy it. Christmas was the best oppurtiny, so I gifted it to myself, and let's say that I was a bit apprehensive at first launch. I'm not a big fan of the 3D style in this game, it didn't felt as coherent and immersive as Rayman Legends did, for example. I guess I'm too much attached to the old one that I can't understand the change, but the animation feels too janky and unpolished to me to be unnoticed.Then came the technical problems, which is the thing that bothers me the most here. It's always funny to find some bugs that aren't an obstacle to the experience, like here, the speed boost you get from full hoping + slide. However, I had difficulties running it on my Steam Deck, so I had to try dfferent versions of Proton to simply open my map. Again, I get it, it wasn't made compatible for the Steam Deck, but that's just a minor issue. I got softlocked in the Halvtann fight because the boss glitched and killed both me and himself at the same time, causing the cracked ice to stay solid and not let me continue the rest of the game. This was a killer for me, I wasn't motivated to continue after that, but I wanted to be done with it, so I created a new save file, and completed it entirely. Also, it is pretty easy to get out of bounds and the game tends to lag every now and them, so this can be annoying.Gameplay-wise, I would say that it doesn't quite live up to its expectations :- The puzzles are okay, but not as thoughtful as the first game.- The magnetic hood is split into two parts and you only get the red part at the end of the game. That's a questionnable choice of game-design for me, since it is the core of Teslagrad's fun.- Having the slide and the hammer on the same button makes movement a bit frustrating.- The physics are too janky to feel satisfying. I was a very big fan of the hood mechanic in the first game, but here it feels like having to fight the game all the way through. However, sliding in this game feels great.- I didn't like the boss fights, except for Eleanor, which was balanced and made good use of the newly obtained abilities. But the others would feel either too easy (like Halvtann, Fafnir and Huldr) or too difficult (like Galvann because of the axe being hard to aim, and The First Draug which was especially painful to beat)- The map is too big for what it is used for. It feels like it was thought like a metroidvania map, where you would go back and forth a lot of times (the grapples are a testimony of this), but there's not enough upgrades or interesting secrets to justify this size, like Hollow Knight or Metroid Dread would have done. This is particularly visible in the case of the giant room below the first tower, which exists only for a cryptic collectible, whereas it could have been an epic bossfight room.Story-wise, I find it cool to have the player unravel the story by himself using little illustrations hidden throughout the game. That doesn't mean I understood it tho lol!As for the "small viewing stations", I think I preffered the puppet shows of the first game, it was easier to understand while being its own thing.And personnally, I don't think that the fact that this game is short makes it bad, on the contrary.So yeah, in the end I'd say : neither great nor bad for a game very few asked for.I'm no journalist, so consider this my honest impression of the game and nothing else, go try it for yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: Teslagrad 2 is a lovely little puzzle platformer affair that lets the player play with some surprisingly deep movement mechanics in a nice quality package that doesn't overstay its welcome.  I hesitate to call it a "metroidvania" per se because you never actually need to backtrack through the environments at all to beat the game.  That being said, it does metroidvania things of featuring a steadily expanding toolkit of powers that makes the player feel pretty cool by the end and having an open, interconnected world with collectibles in old areas reachable by said powers (though vanishingly few collectibles actually affect gameplay), so maybe that's enough for some people.  The story is entirely wordless, which can be nice for brevity, but feel as if I had trouble understanding some of the backstory as a result.  That doesn't really affect what I feel this game's strongest suit is, though, which is the movement.  Lumina's powerups are largely traversal focused, with combat functionality coming second; this results in some very satisfying movement options once you get going.  Once you get the slide dash, you can start zipping through the map at high speed, and the powerups only keep the momentum going.  The fast travel system that the map has isn't exactly comprehensive, but the game encourages you to use your traversal skills to get around; this enforced (for the completionist types out there) by the few bonus powerups strewn across the map.  In order to unlock bonus powerups, you need to complete a small trial in which you must get from one point of the map to another within some restrictive time limit.  Completing these trials requires and rewards having a grasp on how the game's movement system.On the topic of completion, I got about 75% through the game's collectibles and beat the final boss in about 5 hours.  Most collectibles are cards that contain illustrations of various scene's from the game's world and backstory.  If you're into the completion aspect, then I suspect it wouldn't take too many more hours than where I got to, but I found the story's final boss to be a satisfying enough conclusion (at least as satisfying as could be when I didn't feel I had a good grasp on the story).Anyway, Teslagrad 2 is a fantastic little romp, regardless of how much time you want to put into it.  I definitely recommend at least giving it a look.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but satisfying game, and a great sequel! The physics gameplay mechanics are easy to use and are great when you learn to master them. Wish there were challenge levels like with the remastered version of Teslagrad, but I enjoyed it all the way through (with some unanswered questions that can lead to another sequel).I recommend this game for anyone that played the first game, and even if you didn't, the sequel does a great job of being a good starting point (should still play the first one first, of course lol)

_childDocuments_.review: I really dig the short, more guided approach to Metroidvania in this game. If you stick to the main quest, and you'll complete it in about 3 hours. But it's totally worth it to explore because the additional content is great (hidden abilities, secret bosses)On the artistic side, I think they nailed it. The visuals tell the story which I like (even though the story is pretty basic) . The music is spot on, especially when you enter certain areas. It pulls you in and makes the whole experience pretty immersive. Plus, the Nordic/Scandinavian setting is a nice set up.Movement is really well done. You start off feeling weak and slow, then gradually power up and zoom around the map. The puzzles are cool too – nice balance of these two elements.The bosses are kinda underwhelming, especially for a Metroidvania/platformer. I was hoping for epic, tougher fights.The game trolls you sometimes. Like, you're zooming around with your powers, then bam, you hit a puzzle at full speed and just die lmao.I love the physic of this game (electricity, magnets). I thinks it's cool and orginal, but it makes some move inconsistent ? I can't really describe it, but some moments I went like “come on, I can’t make this easy jump. Really ?”Overall, I liked it! I'd recommend it to anyone new to Metroidvania games. It's not too hard, fairly short, and you won't get stuck since it guides you along.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely HATED the original teslagrad game so i'm honestly very pleasantly suprised with Teslagrad 2 because i went in fully convinced that i wouldn't like it. Why pick it up then you ask? Well it was on sale and i liked the art, also despite a long list of grievances i have with the original game, the core mechanic of magnetism has potential. Potential that is fully realised in teslagrad 2 and then some. This game is superior to its predecessor in every way conceivable, from art to level design and from music to load times. But the biggest improvement are the controls. Gone are the overly sensitive and janky controls that wanted you to do precision jumps, instead they are replaced with some of the smoothest and most fun movement abilities i've seen. The slide especially is just godlike, as it keeps momentum when you jump sorta like in the messenger. So if you're skilled enough you can absolutely zoom across the longer flat stretches of terrain inbetween the more condensed areas.Speaking of the areas the level design in teslagrad 2 makes full use of this new movement system, offering room after room of unique and fun challenges to overcome. I don't think there was any room that made me rage, unlike the original game where it happened every other room. It was so good in fact that i went out of my way to collect all extra optional collectibles in this game, contrary to the original where i only collected about half before dropping it altogether. This added about 2 and a half hours of extra content on top of the 3 or so it took me to do the main quest. In terms of value for money then this game scores pretty low with such a short runtime, especially if you only do the main quest. But the movement is so smooth that i'd say it's almost worth it at full price and definately worth it on a discount. It goes pretty deep quite often so keep it on your wishlist just in case!If you do pick it up you'll be treated to some absolutely gorgeous vistas accompanied with beautiful norse music as you jump, slide and dash through the levels. These levels have far fewer enemies to bother you than the previous instalment, which is a great thing as combat was never teslagrads' strongsuit. Like the first game, teslagrad 2 has few bosses to test your skills but unlike said game these are actually fun rather than rage inducing. The tighter controls as well as more fun mechanics make for bosses that were challenging in the right way this time around. They're also a lot easier in this game which is a good thing in my opinion as that means you can return faster to the amazing puzzle/parkour challenges. Defeating a boss also has some lore shortly therafter but once more these are delivered without words. It's up to you to piece everything together but not required to beat or enjoy the game. I picked up some of the story but honestly my main enjoyment was the fun movement and creative level design, both of which give me reason enough to recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game and watching an amazing lore video by MetalFox Dioxymore on youtube (Go watch it, it's a trully wonderful video) I'm changing my analyzis and recommendation.The three main points I had signaled in my previous analyzes were the non presentation of the main character, what's the reason for her to go in that adventure and her lack of agency, now I have an answer for both of them.Lumina's reason is going back home, because this game is a direct continuation of World to the West (Another Rain Studio's game) and she's presented in that game. Her lack of agency comes from this game only being a epilogue for her previous adventure but it is actually the VILLAIN story (That started before Teslagrad 1). I don't agree with the studio's decision to have those answers in outside materials but, after watching MetalFox's video, and have all the pieces coming together I got to appreciate the game for what it is. Now I'm going to play World to the West and can't wait for the next entry in the Teslaverse!

_childDocuments_.review: A metroidvania platformer with great movement. It's as enjoyable as the first, IIRC.The movement in this game is probably the most satisfying part. You get a lot of ways to move quickly through the environment and it's satisfying. And as you unlock more and more, it all works together really nicely. I was flying around the map going back for secrets and unlocks like it was nothing. This is something that is missing from a lot of big Metroidvania's with back tracking. Fast travel is nice, but this was more fun. By the end, would have liked to have both lol.The story seems like it's intriguing, but it's hard to discern what is going on. I kinda get it, but not quite. I wish it was a bit clearer. The game has very low challenge until the very end. Last two bosses are a huge difficulty spike IMO.One flaw, may be in the "secret" powers. I found a few moves early on that made it so I could bypass some puzzle mechanics. I don't think I did anything beyond what is intended to get these secret moves, and I believe doing what I did is probably common. It may also be intended by the dev, not sure.Some issues:1. The throw mechanic is not used often, so little I forgot about it until some random point I needed it.2. If you can use the right joystick to pan camera, it doesn't work on my Elite Wireless 2. If this isn't in the game, it should be.3. Second to last boss is challenging, but the biggest challenge was having to watch the cinematic each time.4. There are some areas on the map that exist that I don't believe you can get to. I have the game 100% and all scrolls and there is no way that I can see to get to these areas.All in all, this is a good game and worth playing. I believe I left the game on for a few hours, so probably 10 hours to 100% the game. Finding everything was easy enough. Price tag is probably worth it if you liked the first, but I'd wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Teslagrad 2 is a very pretty game and has fun powers and traversal, but it has some of the same flaws as the first one: the bosses are frustrating and not fun to get through. You have at max one extra hit you can take, what you need to do to damage the bosses is not always clear, and they have gigantic attacks that fill the screen and are hard to dodge. Worst of all there are often unskippable cutscenes you will have to watch again and again after you are returned to the checkpoint.There are a ton of collectibles but as far as I've seen no in game tools to help you find them. You'll either have to search for a long time or use a guide. If you aren't willing to do that, which I wasn't, this is a very short game. I finished in 3 hours and as you can tell from my review I'm not even particularly good at it.Nothing wrong with a shorter game, just something you should be aware of if you are looking for something longer.If you don't mind a few frustrating boss fights it is definitely worth playing. I just hope if there's a Teslagrad 3 they add things like health upgrades, or collectible sensors, or give the collectibles some reward element so you feel like you've gotten a benefit from collecting them rather than are checking off a box.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game greatly.  The visuals and music are fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: Teslagrad 2 is a tricky game to recommend. Proof of it is that I'm on the verge of not recommending it even when I enjoyed it and fully completed it. When the game is, let's say, working as intended, it's a wonder. It's a gorgeous game with an incredible soundtrack, the game never fails to deliver on that, but it's the relationship between the power-ups and the level design what's hit or miss.See, all these electromagnetic power-ups are super cool to use and make you gain a lot of speed many times. The thing is, if the power-ups of your game make you gain lots of speed with little control over it most of the time, why are there segments of the map plagued with tiny platforms or narrow gaps between hazards? It's like the game had no playtesting, worse even it's that, since this game has a metroidvania component, you are going to go over these segments several times while looking for the collectibles.I enjoyed the game, I like how it handles being both a linear experience and a map full of secrets at the same time, and it's a pleasure to go zooming from one side of the map to the other thanks to the ludicrous speed you can get. That, and the fact that I can't stress enough how gorgeous the game is, is why I recommend it. But know before entering that you are going to be frustrated at times by a level design worthy of the Sonic franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous metroidvania but also kind of fustrating at times. Let's get the positive things out first, the artstyle and sound design are stellar. One of the prettiest games I have seen in a long time. It's also a good game overall, it's fun, the various powers are fun to use, the bosses (even if there where only a handfulhad great design and where not that hard to figure out (last phase of the "final" boss is kind of bs tho, especially since you have to redoo phase 1 if you fail, it's defintly not clear what you are suposed to do).The controls however can be a bit fiddly and the physics engine is a bit jank at times, for example when you propell yourself with the various magnetic abilities, sometimes it work, sometimes it doesn't even if im sure I do exactly the same thing.  It's a fairly short game, if you just count the main storyline, but there are a ton of collectables and a true ending/secret boss (I found like 20% at most, didn't go out of my way to find them so they are definitly hidden outside the main path). I'm not going to go back and find them right away, but might do it at a later time.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun metroidvania with a focus on platforming and physics based movement. There aren't really puzzles so much as obstacles this time around, and the bosses are still frustrating the first play through, but if you liked Teslagrad 1 or metroidvanias are your thing, you'll probably like this.The world feels gigantic, and there's a lot of lore that's told through the environment and collectibles. Movement is just plain fun, though at first it can feel a little inconsistent. With every new ability you'll feel like new parts of the world are open to explore and the old parts just got more nuanced and interesting.I've played it through a few dozen times now and am trying my hand at speedrunning it. _childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: Really loved the first Teslagrad (one of my favourite indie games) and was looking forward to the sequel big time. It doesn't disappoint - this is a magnificent Metroidvania. It's better than the original, which still sets a very high bar, with ambitious gameplay mechanics that see you hurtling all over the place. It's very cool.The graphics are fantastic and, even better, that soundtrack is just outstanding. Downsides? As with the original, the difficulty can be extreme. This is at its worst during some of the boss fights. It can get incredibly frustrating as it creates a roadblock to progress. Persevere and you'll beat them, but it's not enjoyable grinding until you master the exact routine. However, some of them are cool - the snake boss is an awesome concept, for example, but just go into this game expecting a challenge.Overall? Massively impressed by Teslagrad 2. This should go down as one of the top indie games of the year. A must for any Metroidvania buff, too!

_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: After finally beating the story, I can say I'm very happy I purchased this.  Lets go through the main points.Graphics: 9/10The graphics are updated from the original game Teslagrad, and they did an amazing job here.  Animations, Vivid scenery, lots of little areas to explore, and a  more useful map.  Even the UI had an overhaul, and I rather enjoy it.  The magnetism polarity was a great touch, and it looks even cooler than the first game.Sound: 9/10The sounds, ambiance, and music all add up to another amazing journey.  Everything sounds like you're actually there, and with the right headphones, you could even practically close your eyes and still know where everything is.Gameplay: 7/10One of the few times I have to say 2 steps forward, one step back.  On one hand, the new moves are great, and only add to the multitude of ways to get around the map.  Its fun to do just about every move in the game, with a single caveat.  Sliding and ground-pound are the same button.  This means you really have to think about where you slide, and make sure you don't press the button again when jumping over a pit.Some new moves are just simple upgrades, like the lightning dash ability can work in other places, and the direction you go when dashing is entirely dependent on what direction you are facing if you are using magnetism, which i think is a great touch.  Other moves are entirely new like sliding, which is a cool move i never knew i needed.There are also a few other secret moves that you can unlock by exploring the map more and solving challenges.  However, the buttons these moves are set to cannot be changed (in the in-game menus (as of the time of this review))Story: 9.5/10The story is told in the same way as the previous game.  with videos, pictures, and actions.  No words, though the characters do make various noises, like grunts, or affirmative sounds.  This game also has a  more of the interesting Rune writing that's meant to be able to be deciphered; especially in or near any secret rooms.Overall: 8/10I definitely enjoyed my time playing this.  I'm going to go back to the original game and finish collecting all the hidden collectibles, then come back and collect all of them from this game too.  It's so fun to move around, even with the minor setbacks, and although i had to get used to the magnetism of this game, after getting the hang of it, I like it better than the first one.  It seems more realistic, which is a huge plus for a game where that's one of the core mechanics.I recommend this game whether or not you've played the original, but there are absolutely points in the story that are made so much better if you've played it.  In any case, though, you're in for a fun time!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a recommendation with a few caveats.The first thing I need to mention is the length; the critical path from beginning to end can easily be completed in around 4 hours. You could probably add another 3-4 hours if you want to 100% it and get the "real" ending. Not inherently a bad thing but if you're looking for a lengthy experience you should look elsewhere.Some other reviews refer to this as a metroidvania (a nebulous term at the best of times) and the devs refer to it as a Scandivania thus implying it should belong to this sub-genre. While technically you could argue the case, if you go into Teslagrad 2 expecting a metroidvania I think you will be disappointed. What you have here is a physics based puzzle platformer with some beautiful visuals and music. Yes the map is "open" but unless you want to find all the collectables (non-functional items that unlock something if all are found) you won't need to backtrack much and won't notice any real ability gating. The optional collectables are where the metroidvania aspects come in; if you ignore them it won't feel like one.Gameplay wise, it plays well enough, the character movement feels weighty and deliberate and the abilities are enjoyable enough to use. Combat is mostly indirect though some other options emerge later on. There's less physics jank in this one than the original and the platforming sections were mostly quite fluid.The initially cryptic narrative is wordless and is very much inspired by Nordic folklore, it does enough to push you through the short run time.There's two things I want to mention to the devs; please allow players to skip the currently un-skippable cutscenes that play before and in between phases of the games hardest boss. This was by far the most frustrating thing I encountered in the game. Secondly, mapping slide/ground smash to the same button isn't optimal and can lead to some unintended actions.In conclusion, I enjoyed my time with Teslagrad 2. It looks and sounds great, and plays well enough. If you're looking for a short but sweet puzzle platformer then give this one a shot, otherwise wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited for this game since I finished the first Teslagrad and this worth worth the wait.I had trouble finishing it because I'm not very good at platformers so I ended up on a bittersweet note.But it doesn't spoil the pleasure of the rest of the game, the music of Jorn Lavoll is so good, I really love it ! The overall Art Direction, the backgrounds, the sound design, the story, everything is really beautiful.You should definitely get it !
_childDocuments_.name: Teslagrad 2

_childDocuments_.review:
Lumina, a young Teslamancer, finds herself stranded after her airship crashes in Wyrmheim, a remote and treacherous land to the North.

Embark on a dangerous adventure, exploring a gigantic, abandoned tower looming over a fjordside valley, on a quest to get Lumina home and back to her family.

Use electromagnetic powers to survive the dangers of a wild and untamed land. Defend yourself against Viking raiders, face gruesome beasts inspired by Nordic mythology, and triumph against epic bosses! As your journey progresses, you'll discover new skills and equipment needed to uncover the secrets of the land and delve into the dark past of Lumina's ancestors.

name: Afterimage
detailed_description: Deluxe Edition The Deluxe Edition includes the full game, digital artbook, and digital soundtrack DISCORD About the Game A great deity created the world named Engardin, leaving four goliaths before her departure. The Goliaths abided by their different divine callings and upheld the order and flow of this world. Hence, the lives in Engardin reincarnated and multiplied. Humans were the last creation, and their ever-expanding ambitions led to a protracted war against the Goliaths. Engardin was engulfed in flames, until a huge explosion known as 'The Razing' devastated the Holy Grounds of mankind and brought a swift end to the conflict. But the divine order was broken, and lives withered away. The age of mankind came to an end. The survivors of the conflict scattered across Engardin. Severed from the Well of Mankind and unable to reincarnate, they banded together to form settlements. Years have passed since this great cataclysm, and the remaining human settlements have been suddenly assaulted by mystic forces. Renee, a young amnesiac girl and student of Aros, was the lone survivor of the attack on her village. Determined to recover her forgotten memories and locate her lost mentor, she bids farewell to her destroyed village to embark on a journey that will inexplicably set into motion a series of events that will determine the fate of this new world. Experience a gorgeous hand-drawn world Engardin is not only filled with sublime beauty but also plagued by crises. The ruins of Engardin are home to many treasures and secrets, but the Corrupted are waiting for their next prey and ancient deadly traps are ready to kill the careless. Fight Fierce Enemies With humanity in retreat, nature and the creatures that inhabit it have reclaimed Engardin as their own. Battle through over 170 varieties of enemies and 30 tough boss encounters that stand between you and your goal. Bountiful rewards await those who can weather these brutal combat trials. Diversified Character Builds Harness and channel the power of defeated enemies to unlock powerful skills and upgrade a diverse arsenal of weaponry. Become the master of your own fighting style with over 200 different equipment to collect and choose from including 6 classes of main weapon, sub weapon, armor, and accessories. Explore a non-linear world - unearth the secrets buried deep within the ruins of the vast interconnected world of Engardin. Interact with over 50 different NPCs, each with their own story and purpose. Learn more about their role in Engardin through side quests! Fight over 170 varieties of enemies, including 30 tough boss encounters. Deep RPG mechanics allow for diverse character builds – over 200 different equipment to collect and choose from including 6 classes of main weapon, sub weapon, armor and accessories. Invest talent points into a variety of stat upgrades and unique weapon skills for each class of weapon. Determine the fate of the world – discover multiple endings depending on Renee’s actions that will shape the future of Engardin. Stunning 2D art style with animations hand-drawn frame-by-frame. Discover new abilities and new Afterimages that grant unique benefits in your exploration and combat. Use these skills to access new areas, shortcuts, and master these in combat to defeat more difficult enemy encounters! Over 40 original orchestral tracks composed by the Aurogon Sound Team and fully recorded by International Master Philharmonic Orchestra and other various musicians.

short_description: Afterimage is a hand-drawn 2D action adventure that emphasizes fast-paced combat with diversified character builds, non-linear levels, and a gripping story set in the ruins of a fantasy world.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful artwork and unexpectedly massive map, where I'm always finding a new zone. I think there is an optimal way to play, but since the world is pretty open, you can go to zones in an un-optimal sequence, which causes the reactions of npcs to become a little disjointed. But its a pretty minor complaint, and I like that I can find the zones in the order I like.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty good metroidvania game. The best parts are the action and the fights, plus the unique RPG elements, not to mention the map is HUGE. Unfortunately, it's hampered by a nonsensical story. I think if there were more of a story, or even if the existing story made sense, it would have taken the game from good to great. Still fun to play though!
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage feels like a "best-of Metroidvanias". I pretty much like everything about it. The style, the graphics,  the combat, the animations, the bosses, the level design, even the story and characters somewhat even if they definitely had to grow on me and not everything always made sense (which I in part chalk up to the nature of the genre with all the sequence breaking and what not). It's also unusually long for a game of this kind without feeling repetitive or grindy.But if there's one thing to criticize, it's the lack the original ideas. Everything just seems so familiar. While there are a handful of more or less direct references to other Metroidvanias, everything else from the abilities, weapons and skills and character movement to enemies and their attacks also just feels like I've seen it before. Again, all very polished. But a bit of a Déjà vu experience for me nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: It truly frustrates me to give this a negative review because you were "THIS CLOSE" to creating a masterpiece, but stumbled at the goalpost so often that it became tediously mediocre instead.*Absolutly horrible translation that ruins any and all immersion and interest in the already convoluted plot *The plot almost being phenomenal but is constantly ruined by inconsistencies, needless mystique, plain bad writing and lack of dedication to themes and direction.*So many awesome equipment pieces, but you're stuck with the exact same character apperance from start to end since none of your armor pieces visibly change how you look...-Aka. No outfits only reskins. Enjoy looking at the EXACT SAME MODEL for 20+ hours.*Health + mana pots are consumables, fast travel items are consumables, mana regen depends on consumables...  I hate consumables.*So open worlded that you spend 95% of the game dashing around, trying to figure out where the heck you need to go.*5-10 min walks from checkpoint to bosses just to get instakilled, fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: On the whole Afterimage is a Good Metroidvania. Not a Great Metroidvania and nothing that's going to revolutionize the genre, but it's fun! Platforming generally feels good and never gets toooo ridiculous, enemy and boss variety is pretty good, the game is HUGE so there's tons to explore, and exploration rewards generally feel worth it - even the potions you tend to get pretty good use out of. Combat is fast and fluid - or at least, me and my dualblades and absolutely nothing else made it that way, oop, but there's six weapon options that all feel like they have their uses to me!I do think the plot is... pointless, honestly. The characters aren't very engaging, there isn't much drama, the world itself doesn't feel cohesive - just a bunch of Cool Zones To Explore that are only vaguely contextualized by four elements, sometimes - and a lot of basic UI stuff is out of wack - really big stat text in the equip screen meaning you have to scroll, no way to, like, view your overall stats or food buff timers, way, way too many columns in the menu screen and no fast way to switch through them, a "return to last save" mechanic on savequitreload that takes an annoyingly long time bcuz of how long it takes everything to load in that could've been simplified by just having a free "return to last save" button... it's a lot of polish that could easily be fixed and just, isn't.I also think the difficulty is out of wack - everything is level-based but if you get to a zone at its appropriate level You Will Destroy Everything And It Will Be Easy And Unsatisfying, this includes most bosses. This includes Advanced difficulty too honestly. I started on normal, switched to advanced pretty early, switched back to normal when i hit a wall then got bored again and switched back to advanced until the final boss, which is WAY overtuned - way harder than the true final boss, too, and you have to fight this boss two more times in the weird semi-NG+ thing the game has going on that feels pointless, but, whateverrrr.I did have a lot of fun exploring and tearing through enemies and I come away from the game mostly satisfied, but I'm also painfully aware that there's absolutely nothing fresh or novel in this game and I'm probably gonna forget about it in a year's time. Was fun while I was playing it, though, so!
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I tried with this game, but it just never clicked (ignore my playtime, half of it was spent looking at my phone at more interesting stuff).  From the start the story never grabbed me or made me care what I was getting into, but my biggest gripe with this game is that it wasn't fun.  Not everyone is gonna enjoy every game; but if you play a metroidvania, and like metroidvanias, you should be able to pick out a few things to appreciate while you play.  This game is pretty.  That's the only thing I can say that I can appreciate about it because the combat didn't flow, the platforming was uninspired, and the story was as exciting for me as shopping for toilet paper.  I REALLY wish I could push on farther to see if it opens up and actually gets better, but after 4 hours of being bored and waiting for something   to happen, I just can't force myself to care if it ever does.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid Metroidvania title. I'm not sure why all the hate at all. I have about 100 Metroidvania titles in my library and I'd say this is in the top 15%. Challenging bosses. Exploration is fun. Sure, the progress style is like Hollow Knight where you have to find a save point to update the map, but the speed of progression is great. If I'm being honest, a few cons (if you can even call them that) are 1) Exploration isn't the most guided if you are skipping the NPC conversations, 2) It's a big map so traversing can get daunting at times without a true fast travel, 3) There's not much in the defense department. Movement feels nice, but there's not a block or parry and I seem to constantly get hit from walking into enemies. However, you can deflect projectiles and it's rewarding to learn combat with different weapons. I'm a little over 4 hours and just getting to the second boss. He wiped me, but if it's anything like the first boss, once I learn all of the attacks, I'm sure he'll be manageable. The first boss was destroying me at first. About 10 attempts in against the first boss I learned all of the attacks. Even though I lost all of my potions in the meantime I was still able to handedly get through him on 1 life bar.Sure there are things that would make the game more familiar or easy, but that's not what this game is. It's a challenging combat Metroidvania with beautiful aesthetics with a stress on combat mechanics and exploration that rewards the player for investing in the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, although a little strange, the artstyle is good but there is a weird mixture of styles going on, idk what's that about but it's a minor thing, the story also seems needlesly convoluted but you can follow the main idea  pretty okay since it's still pretty simple.The gameplay loop feels great, the combat flows mostly good, exploration is just standard metroidvania stuff but it feels good, maps are complex and there are lot of secrets all over the place, as well as backtracking with you new traversal skills.I'm honestly just writing this to counter the strange chinese review-bombing, idk what's that about but screw those guys, the game is good.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I have 35h on another platform, almost 100%'d the gameBest metroidvania I've ever playedgreat storygreat worldbuilding / loregreat area designgreat explorationgreat charactersgreat enemy varietygreat artgreat voice acting (JP)great combatgreat game lengthtons of multiple endingsoverall huge amount of content9/10 very funThe only negative is late game game balance, I guess. if you explore too much before story content, halfway through the game, you'd just steamroll everything, late game bosses pose no challenge at all. you can just face tank them with all the stats and survivibility items/skills you've unlocked by then.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a fantastic game that is inspired by castlevania games. The controls feel good especially after you unlock your first couple movement abilities. The combat is enjoyable and smooth and the exploration aspect of the game is fun because there are secret nooks and crannies with loot everywhere. The game features a lot of different weapons, equipment, a level up system, potions and cooking and in the skill-tree you unlock new moves for your weapons and they feel good to use.The game world is huge, I often thought the game would end soon only for them to reveal another 2 areas I could explore at the end there are over 20 areas and some extra stuff that doesn’t even appear on the map.One of the best things about the game is the amount of freedom they give the player. The first couple of hours are guided and after that the game lets you go wherever you want. If you want to be dumb and enter an area where every single enemy is higher level than you are (indicated by a skull above their head) you can. Often it is possible to get into areas you aren’t supposed to and once you are in they don’t stop you, it is generally a bad idea to be there but they rarely lock you out.Another thing I really like is that you can do everything in a single savefile and in any order none of the achievements are missable. The game has 10 different endings and if you already have the requirements for a good ending you can still do the bad ones.One of the downsides of all the freedom they give you is that I kept getting lost for a couple hours here and there. However because you can still explore and make progress wherever you are it didn’t feel that bad. Another issue is that it is easy to end up being too strong for a boss and a lot of fights ended up being trivial.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so much, the combat is so engaging and the level design are well made, the platforming sections in this game isn't too hard to get by if you are familiar with platforming. The weapons are all fun you have at least 5 different types of them to play around with their own unique attack animations and skills some weapons you pick up along the way changes or add new skills it keeps things feeling fresh. There isn’t I-frames when starting out you get that as a skill in mid to late game it was pretty hard to get use to since most games, I played had I-frames but I adjusted and found it quite fun learning dodging and positioning your character. There's also a skill tree which you can upgrade by leveling up or by finding/purchasing points for them in the game, some skills are locked and can only be unlocked by scrolls found throughout your journey and they can really make your character feel stronger depending on how you use them. You get to have 2 main hand weapons and 1 sub weapon which is for magic some a cool but I don't use it as much. Besides weapons you also can obtain armour and accessories to aid you in combat, they don’t change how your character look but there’s a slot where you can equip outfits that can change your character’s look and also give bonus stats.The game has many challenging levels and enemies you will encounter you will find yourself dying a couple of times or you can always out heal the damages with potions but they are precious and you can find yourself grinding for minutes or hours trying to restock them. The game has many secrets and secret bosses which you can stumble upon early or needing a skill to traverse to said areas. There’s a couple of NPCS in the game which have side quest. Some quests are long and can leave you clueless where to go next but the map now shows them so you will know where they are to further proceed with the questline, they do give good rewards upon completing and a bit of lore. The main story is straightforward you will know where to go next upon listening or reading the dialogue.The game has an amazing art concept it looks beautiful to play in which appealed to me when I came across it on steam. The music is rememberable and makes you feel immerse by the surrounding environment of the game. The game is fully voiced there’s language options available I personally played in English and the actors did a great job voicing the characters in game A+ levels of voice acting.You also get a free DLC which you can battle all the previous bosses and also 2 new challenging bosses which isn’t in the main story, completing the gives you outfits for your character that changes the looks of your character.Overall, the game is good and well worth the money it isn’t a short game you can get hours of game time from this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Love it.I got about 20h in game and just unlocked the wall jump.I'll start with the cons because there are few imho and some of them can be viewed as pros :- the protagonist, story, and world is... standard chinese anime fare. You will like it or not, personally I don't really care about stories in MVs, I play them for the gameplay.- the world is huge and there's no real quest indicator on where to go or what to do so keeping track of them can be very confusing.- the fast travel is tied to a pretty rare potion (apparently since the update you can buy them for 150 coins at the potions master in Resting Town though).That said :- the world is huge and you get A LOT of content for the price.- the combat is fluid, tight and reminiscent of Aria of Sorrow or SotN (ie : you get a main and a secondary weapon, both can be switched whenever you want depending on your playstyle + a spell button for long range attacks). 6 weapon subclasses (swords, katanas, dual blades, whips, great sword and scythe). I like that it keeps it simple and traditional but a lot of weapon skills can be unlocked in the tree and really fit different playstyles (for instance I really dig the back-and-forth whip slash with jump + attack, great for clearing annoying flying homing fodder).- tight and responsive movement which gives you a dash almost from the get go, double jump after three biomes and wall jump about 5-6h in.- the platforming is precise but quite forgiving as you respawn on the nearest platform if you fall on spikes.- respawn points /save locations are far and away but you move fast and as I said above, the difficulty is pretty generous for an MV (I really dislike the soulslike hardcore direction the genre has taken the last five years. For instance while I loved Aeterna Noctis, it gets absurdly difficult once you start playing with the teleport arrow in the Cosmos). From what I can see yet, there's nothing of that here. It's hard, but you wouldn't play an MV if you didn't like hard games, yet it's fair. If you cleared early Castlevanias or Bloodstained you will clear this.Probably the first MV since Hollow Knight I really can't let down, and the best one since at least Bloodstained (if you exclude Aeterna Noctis, HAAK and Islets, which are imho not completely traditional MVs). This is tradition at its best, so you know what you're getting into. Personally I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing an early review just to counter some of the undeserved poor feedback.  At about 6 hours in, Afterimage has been a thoroughly enjoyable Metroidvania experience so far that's very reminiscent of the Metroid Castlevania games like Symphony of the Night.  I play a *lot* of Metroidvania games and 2d action platformers so I think I have a pretty good perspective on this game type, so here are a few long-winded highlights of the game that might help anyone who's on the fence about getting this game:
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: never have I wavered between recommendation and condemnation of a game so much. There's a good amount of fun to be had playing the game itself, so I guess I'll pop a recommendation on it, but the writing and many aspects of the game design seem absolutely terrible.The writing is completely tell-don't-show:I literally laughed out loud when a special boss killed me in a cutscene, I revived immediately at my last checkpoint (without needing to watch the loading screen cutscene that usually accompanies death), and the characters are freaking out about how the way the boss killed me nearly made it so that I couldn't revive and it took me a long time to come back; as a reminder, my revival in that instance was FASTER than a normal death. One character talks about how he's glad he pushed me to find certain key items throughout the course of the game, but he had literally never mentioned them before now and never made a comment when I picked one of them up. It's kind of frustrating when a big deal is made about the MC's missing memories, but when I literally find the main pair's names written down on inscriptions or in journals, the two of them just brush it off if they even acknowledge it at all. The writers wanted tropes and certain plot progression, but usually failed to properly set any of it up. The things that cause dialogue to happen were so random that I literally forgot the entire reason we were doing anything about halfway through the game. The background worldbuilding almost never amounts to anything: First, let me vent a little about one particular instance (light spoilers that don't mean anything in the grand scheme of things): There were times where I thought the game was trying to imply something clever, but no, it was all coincidence because the "worldbuilding" is just thrown haphazardly throughout the world with no rhyme or reason. There are random messages from what I can only assume are crowdfunding backers littered throughout the world, and their nonsense often seems about as relevant as most of the actual lore monologues in the game. If you ever want to learn anything more than "This biome/area is called X. It's called that because the gods did Y and made it this way" then you're out of luckTHE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ONE WAY WALLS!This entire game is riddled with random trunks, barricades, and crumbling piles of stone that for some unknown reason can only be destroyed if you attack them from one side. I can understand having some of those in your game to help unlock shortcuts or prevent people from accidentally getting the reward at the exit of the occasional jumping puzzle early, but these things are EVERYWHERE. Enforcing linear area discovery despite movement abilities doing that just fine, arbitrarily gating off random sections of the map until you find an entrance to that place on the other side of the world, and even some locations where the wall is blocking off an area that contains nothing of value and is accessed by an open passageway no more than 10 feet away. I would constantly see a massive unexplored section of the map, use one of my consumable fast travel items to get near it, and discover that one room into the unexplored area was a one-way wall that meant there was no way to get into the rest of the unexplored area. The game starts out by teaching you lessons that will become harmful to you later on down the line: I learned early on that exploration is useless because 90% of the time, it's just more potions that I only occasionally use in boss fights, and when it isn't potions, it is probably a path to a one-way wall. The intended progression path through each area is essentially linear for the majority of the game, so I learned that I might as well just go to the next area and get a reward that actually matters. Except if you do stop exploring side paths, you will miss the fact that items REQUIRED for any decent ending are hidden away in random corners of the world. And I don't mean "you gotta find the hidden boss or complete the secret side quests" I mean literally dumped in a completely random corner of the map that you might never find if you're not careful about marking parts of the map that you don't have the powers to access yet. They're not even in thematic locations either, entirely forgettable areas that I'm 100% sure I will not remember if I start a new game. So you not only need to check every unexplored nook and cranny on the map, you need to check every *already-explored* nook and cranny too just to make sure you didn't accidentally miss something. On a similar note, why on earth was one of the main items required to unlock a very pivotal ability locked behind getting a random drop from an entirely forgettable enemy that nobody mentioned? They just said "we need to get a this wind related thing" and it is up to you to decide which of like 4 areas that could be referring to and then instead of exploring them, you're expected to realize you need to grind a certain enemy?Let me reiterate that I did have a good amount of fun with the game. The boss difficulty curve was kind of all over the place, but I still had fun taking them down whether they were tough or not. Finding a clever way to get pieces of treasure using fancy jump techniques or noticing hidden passageways (later in the game where exploration and treasure was actually worth it) was incredibly satisfying. And the game makes sure to constantly provide you with challenges that ensure you can keep regular use of all the movement tricks you've learned thus far. But once I play a little more to get the rest of the endings I haven't quite unlocked, I will likely put the game down, never think of it again, and forget pretty much everything about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I would rate this game around 7.5/10 The art style is really good and the music is great. The map is massive with a lot of variety between areas. Bosses are somewhat challenging but could be annoying sometime. The story is good, and there are multiple endings (and a lot of secrets). There are multiple weapons to use. Each one has there own skill set you can upgrade once you level up. Some items/weapon will also have unique effect which add another layer to the combat. There are also spells in this game. you also can mix and match accessories to optimize you build as well.However, I do have some problems with this game.First is during the early game. Because of how the map and enemy placement is, avoiding damage is almost impossible. I don't claim to be a pro at this type of games. But I play enough to say that this will be difficult. But not in a good way. It basically more annoying than challenging.Then, once you get enough skills, the game get fairly fun and you realized it is at almost the end of the game where you start doing side quests so you can unlock more endings/skills/items. You will start to feel somewhat annoyed again because the game does not labels locations for you. The NPC can tell you to go to town A. But you won't remember where that is because the map is so big. So, unless you spend literally hours running around, you will need to google how to proceed. Then, the game also does not labels where those NPC are either. So imagine speding 2 hours running around and then also have to try to find the NPC who gave the quest. And I forgot to mention that you can't warp to any save points for free. you need to have/buy an item for that. So, if you warp around so much figuring out how to proceed. You will run out of money which you can use to buy others useful things. This also hurt the story as well. To experience the whole story, you will need to do these side quests. And this will just break the flow of the story because the running around create so big of a gap between story points later in the game.The other point that annoyed me is contact damage. you can say that this is part of the design. But because of some bosses' size and how they attack, this just become very annoying. To be honest, the most fun I had was fighting a boss that does not have contact damage (won't name due to spoiler). Also, this game contact damage HURT. Like, a lot.Anyway, I think this game is good. It is not exceptionally good, but good. I would really love seeing some quality of life update.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a beautifully crafted indie title that immerses players in a stunning, hand-drawn world filled with mystery and adventure. As someone with mixed feelings about the game, I found that it offers both captivating moments and areas that could use improvement. The narrative follows Renee, on a quest to find her lost memories in the enchanting yet perilous realm of Engardin. Accompanied by Ifree, your sidekick spirit, their journey is steeped in themes of identity, friendship, and resilience. The bond between Renee and Ifree is a highlight, offering heartfelt moments that resonate throughout their adventure. However, while the premise is intriguing, the story sometimes feels disjointed, with certain plot points lacking depth and clarity. Players may find themselves wanting a more cohesive narrative to fully engage with the emotional stakes. Visually, Afterimage is a standout. The hand-painted backgrounds and character designs are nothing short of breathtaking, creating an immersive atmosphere that beckons exploration. Each area is distinct and beautifully rendered, making it a joy to traverse. The attention to detail is commendable, though some areas can feel overly busy, occasionally detracting from the gameplay.The soundtrack complements the visuals well, with ethereal melodies that enhance the emotional weight of key moments. While some tracks are memorable and elevate the experience, others may fade into the background, which can break the immersive flow. Gameplay in Afterimage offers a blend of platforming and combat, with a Metroidvania-style progression system. The controls are generally responsive, allowing for smooth navigation through the intricately designed environments. However, the combat mechanics can be hit or miss; while some encounters are thrilling and require strategic thinking, others may feel repetitive and unbalanced, leading to frustration.The game's pacing also fluctuates, with some segments feeling dragged out while others rush through important content. This inconsistency can make it challenging to maintain engagement throughout the entirety of the adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it, 100%ed it, but can only recommend it with a number of caveats.- incomprehensible story, writing feels machine-translated despite the voice acting;- item pickups vanish into your inventory without an explanation, good luck finding what you just picked up;- very directionless, even for the standards of the genre;- the NPC quests actively suck, they're similar to Dark Souls in that NPCs just teleport all over the place and you're supposed to accidentally run into them... I just looked them up, no patience for this;- overall jank, both in programming and in art direction (some sprites clash a lot).That said: The movement and moment-to-moment gameplay is so much fun. If you're experienced with Metroidvanias, are somewhat tolerant towards jank, and are looking for another big one to sink your teeth into, this one's not a bad choice!
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a beautifully crafted metroidvania that excels in both art and gameplay. The hand-drawn environments are stunning, filled with vibrant colors and intricate details that make exploration a joy. The combat is fluid and challenging, with a variety of weapons and abilities to master. The story, while somewhat mysterious and cryptic, adds a layer of intrigue that keeps you engaged as you uncover the world’s secrets. If you're a fan of the genre, Afterimage is a must-play that will captivate you from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Most of my problems with the game are personal pet peeves (AKA my incompetence) but this game is worth every penny. But if I may make a suggestion, keep a guide handy just in case. This game won't tell you where to go in particular but it's never unclear as to where you must go next, as there's always something new in every nook and cranny. _childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I generally don't enjoy Metroidvania games -- I enjoy exploration but really hate platforming combat -- but I found this one less unenjoyable than most.  But the fast travel system in this game really drags it down a lot.  The travel points are incredibly far apart and they use an item that only drops finitely.  I ended up really, really not having fun backtracking.  It was like the walking simulator of platforming games.  I got stuck on a boss, and up to this point that had meant that there was somewhere else I could go more scaled to my level, but I just couldn't summon the willpower to go look for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very beautiful to look at. But other than that, the game plays fine.However, my only caveat right now as I'm 2.5 hours is that going across the map is restricted by drinking special potions that allow you to do so. I don't know why you can't do that at the very checkpoints you need to go. And unlike its contemporaries like Ori, movement doesn't feel that great to be honest. Plus, you gotta really be careful with your heals since you're also restricted on that too. Just note, I did help Kickstart this game and completely forgotten about it. It's not bad, but I think you can do better elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a beautiful metroidvania with nice musics.You have equipment : various slots for armor, two for weapons and one for a spellbook and fight your way in a huge world.What I love the most is the exploration. The world is absolutely huge. The first three hours felt like the blink of an eye ... and the the rest of the day too. (I need help.)Apparently the game lasts at least 30 hours for a run.In the beginning I didn't like the combat too much because you can only dodge.  After a few hours there are many weapons and I got used to not being hit by avoiding damage. (By opposition to blocking mechanics.)I'm having so much fun.  I'll explore another area and I'll stop ... promise ... (And then we are the next day ...)Recommended to any metroidvania lover.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Good metroidvania with large maps. Lots of backtracking (even for this genre), but if you make use of placeable markers on map, it´s not that bad.Combat and movement are fine. Contact damage was no problem for me.If you don´t mind playing a game where you don´t really make sense of story because it´s really confusing and badly written, I can recommend Afterimage.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: It's got its problems as a lot of the other reviews have pointed out... But for all the things I could complain about, I still have fun playing it. Sure, some weapons are under tuned... but they controls well and once you start digging into the mastery system the combat loop becomes a real joy to mess around with.Sure, the map design is a bit bland and fast travel isn't as accessible as it maybe should be... But the environments look great are still a blast to explore.Is the story a bit obtuse? Yeah, but its held up with just enough interesting ideas and cool art to keep me invested.Weapons and Items feel oddly sparse? 100% agree, and yet I've not once felt like an area wasn't properly tuned to my character so long as I was relative to the area in level. Overall, It's a good game with a lot of questionable decisions. You can feel the passion the devs put into the project. If you're a big fan of the metroidvania subgenre, this game will scratch the itch. It just probably won't be one you'll remember alongside the greats.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic, if a bit too big, SoulsVania that has a pretty neat story. It's hampered by long stretches of "Where do I go?!" moments which require you to either backtrack to an NPC or wander around randomly until you uncover the pathway or the one spot not filled with insta-kill enemies. I will say though, when you figure out where to go it feels AMAZING and keeps you going for just a bit longer when you originally planned to stop for now.If wandering around banging your head against every pathway frustrates you, i'd still suggest giving this game a try anyway if you can get it on a decent sale. If you're the type of person who presses the spacebar on every wall in an FPS because that's just how you're wired then get the game in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing metroidvania that has all the qualities required to challenge Aeterna Noctis and Hollow Knight for the title of "best metroidvania of all time". Beautiful graphics, immersive atmosphere, enormous world with diverse biomes, varied bestiary, challenging and memorable boss fights, many options for customization, intuitive and responsive controls, etc. The only downsides of the game are the at times confusing story and the early / middle game being slightly too easy.Can't wait for the DLCs and to finish the game at 100%, a contender for game of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Actually a pretty good game, I was skeptical because of the pastel girly colors and kind of generic style but the platforming and combat are actually really tight and enjoyable. It's not so much a 'soulslike' in the sense that you dodge through attacks, but more a castlevanialike where you use the backstep to dodge and avoid. There's all kinds of good stuff and secret passages hidden away in the corners and that makes the maps a lot more interesting than just basic one-place-to-another. I can tell I'm going to enjoy spending a lot of time on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright the game is awesome. i would give this a 4/5 for the only because of the transport animal not giving me the option to travel to other islands properly and making me waste an entire day stuck going back and forth. the game has limited move set. great story even if you're gonna skim through the dialog certain parts of the story will catch your attention. you cant miss anything in this game like quest, endings, the only thing you can lose out on are limited items. when you beat the game instead of putting you into ng+ it places you back to the nearest save points and lets you continues your story so you can get all the ending in one go.

_childDocuments_.review: 游戏我很喜欢，手残如我开头两张地图一直在受苦，后面熟悉了操作后也慢慢流畅起来了，能够玩得很快乐。看现在这个评价这游戏估计没法回本了，给个好评，希望制作者心里能够好受一点。这里附上我很喜欢的诗句：埋心不死留春色，且忍罡风十夜霜。I've seen many people confused by the negative reviews of Chinese players on this game,and perhaps I can explain the reasons: Firstly, the game development company's previous works were not of this type,and many players have not played the Gal*Gunvolt game before. They gave negative reviews because they were not used to the dodge and sprint settings of this type of game. Secondly,there are many people who dislike the game development company and take advantage of Steam's two-hour free refund mechanism to play the game for only one or two hours before leaving negative reviews to lower the game's score. Some even gave negative reviews because there was no discount for the game in the first week.Of course, what disappoints meis that not only many players gave low scores, but also many game bloggers with numerous fans on video websites have irresponsibly commented that"this game is trash,"causing other bloggers who spoke highly of the game to be ridiculed by those who had never played the game and accused them of receiving money.I know that the developers may not be able to recover their costs under these circumstances, but at least the game deserves a fair evaluation. It's a great game and I hope you can come and try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DRgame is mid, devs looked at what was popular in the genre and smashed all the parts together to make a franken-game that shambles along and collapses at the finish line, buy this on a big sale if you truly are interested in playingIf I didn't have to struggle to finish this with a guide I could have 100% beaten this casually in under 20 hoursread below for my thoughts on the gameStory:there is barely anything here, it tries to do the environmental/character based story telling of hollow knight, but makes it so mysterious even with paying attention to everything going on I had no clue what anything meant and none of the games 10 ENDINGS make anything clearer with them all being small short video animatics/motion images of scenes with no dialogue or clear indications of what is being portrayed.art design:this is a mixed bag, whilst the environmental and enemy designs are uniform and fitting for each area, they are often too busy and involved making them look like nothing more than vaguely shaped themed colours, that's besides the fact that edge and wall textures are often overlapping incorrectly, or just have holes in the artwork making me believe there is a hidden passage where there isn't, and some enemy animations either don't look right clipping through their own models or have outlines around the borders of the imagegeneral combat:this feels cheap, enemies are often placed in confined spaces with large attacks that are unable to be dodged or are placed with other enemies with fixed position attacks that you have to avoid specific sections of the level to avoid, flying enemies can clip through all barriers, shortcuts and breakable sections to attack you whilst you are stuck behind them, all enemies will agro to you within a certain circle of you instead of line of sight meaning most enemies get the drop on you until you know their spawn locations, by the half way through the game i had enough health and defence i could just tank most enemies and only ever dodged if their attacks would send me flying/ moved the enemy awaybosses:there is a large variety of very unique bosses to fight, some bosses felt very well thought out and planned with other enemies in the area using minor versions of their attacks meaning you could tell what attacks were coming and make some plans towards them, this does culminate with two areas showcasing the bosses attacks for their area and one of the final bosses using stronger versions of those attacks from the 2 bosses, though unfortunately all bosses suffer from the same thing, this game is a stats bases metroidvania and none of the bosses will give you any tension if you are geared up enough, and this still doesn't excuse some bosses with some of them having no tells for their attacks and with the damage from their attacks being in such a large area you can't really avoid it, a tell should let you know what attacks are coming up without even knowing what it is, the regular enemies do this aplenty but the bosses don't, if I see a backstep whilst holding the hilt of their sword I expect a lunging/dashing sword attack that goes across the screen but when the boss does that it means a fixed area attack I have to avoid instead that isn't a tell its punishment, if I press the green button in the green room and get rewarded the red button in the red room and get rewarded and the blue button in the blue room and get punished it isn't a tell, it's bad game designexploration:barely suffices, most of the areas in the game can be accessed without any upgrades, I beat the 'final' area of the game whilst severely underleveled without even realising it was the final area which trivialised the rest of the game as with end game gear I never even looked at anything else. most areas in the game aren't locked behind specific upgrades or specific bosses which require you to have specific upgrades for, but more boss A dropped Key item B for door C which was never told to you, a specific area in the game called Albedo towers needs you to have wall climbing to access, with specific movement of flying enemies I managed to get the entire way through the area without needing the power-up, there are only 2 power ups i felt were actually needed to progress were the slide dash and swimming, everything else is basically just for convenience, the ripoff hollow knight shade cloak allows you to dash through crimson barriers and phase through attacks with an identical cool down mechanic, you get this item at the very end of the section with the crimson barriers, the only thing it does is make travel through this one area more convenient as all other areas of the game where it the barriers show up are just for items, not story progression,Sound:I don't remember any of it, except the obnoxious water sound for the loading screen,completion:arguably one of the most important aspects of a metroidvania is 100% completion, this sucks, you WILL require a guide to beat this game as even with the end game item that shows you how many collectables are in each area, how many you collected and chimes when you are near a collectable, isn't enough as some items are in such lengthy hidden areas that unless you already know where they are you won't find them, many of the achievements in the game are fairly standard like do all of this, collect all of that, but some are for other random things like specifically damaging an enemy for 666 damage in an RNG numbers system, even following a guide and tweaking that a little it still took me 30 minutes just for this achievement,Overall:I feel like this game had too many chefs in the kitchen as it has the leveling and gear system from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night/Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night, with the skill tree of pointless small numbers of many other games (i'm looking at you Vigil: The Longest Night and The Vagrant), the badge system and indirect story telling of Hollow Knight, the incredibly obnoxious hidden walls mechanic from the Ori games and all of its upgrades (double jump, triple jump, super jump, enemy bouncing, swimming, wall climbing, ripoff shade cloak, slide dashing and swimming) seem unoriginal and boring all of this adds up to make a large but empty world with an identity crisis, underneath the surface there does lie a good game unfortunately it is buried by the Dev's choice to take great aspects from other very successful metroidvanias and ruin them by mashing them together without understanding what made those mechanics work.

_childDocuments_.review: I got Afterimage from HumbleBundle and have really enjoyed it. I'm not certain how much the game costs, but at around 20 hours in, I have thoroughly enjoyed what I've played. Classic metroidvania with little direction, but the game doesn't really punish you for going to far in the wrong direction. There are a ton of mini-bosses and items to find and VAST world doesn't feel empty at all.Overall, I'd recommend putting a few hours in at the right price, if you enjoy the genre. _childDocuments_.review: (The following reviews the content before the patch on 28.04.2023)I have waited for this game now probably since the steam page is up and for now I can say that it was worth it.The visuals are astonishing and the music is perfectly chosen for each scenery.The gameplay is nice and the movement feels very smooth and quick.The open world element can be quite confusing if you're not used to it. If you say now, "but isn't there a quick travel system" and yes there is one.The quick Travel option is quite unique. Many games make it free or with a smol cost. Afterimage on the other hand limits you in the use of it. There is an Item for infinit use but it takes a while until you get it.The Skill tree is a fun system to get more weapon skills and make the game a bit easier.The difficulty is quite balanced and increases in a manageable way even if you dont explore much. It also warns you of the recommended level when you enter a new area.The quest system could be a bit more revealing what the next objective is but every thing else is fine with it.The Characters have good designs but the story is mostly fine, its definitely missing something.All in all it's a very good game, its visually beautiful and more fun to explore the further you get. The Sounds are beautifully composed and it feels natural in addition to the ambient.I would recommend it everyone who likes to explore an astonishing and a bit challenging world.To be fair, this is my personal opinion.Not everyone will feel like I do and will instantly love the game. At the moment I'm probably only 30% done with the game and I'm surprised how much content there is for the Price. Its definitely more then worth the low cost of 25€.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a little slow but most metrovania games are I suppose. Great artwork, combat becomes really fun once you unlock some abilities and get some good gear. _childDocuments_.review: Besides nice art, which you can generate yourself using the midjourney AI the games bring nothing new or challenging into the metroidvania genre. A mediocre stuff to kill your time with easy to kill mobs, dumb dialoges (if you bring them, make sure they are interesting to read) and basic story, no parrying (in 2023) and paid fast travel.Buy Ori, Hollow Knight or Blaphemous
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Worth every penny. The only negatives I have to say that irked me are:The resting potions can be tedious for fast traveling, but you'll almost always have enough currency to buy more.Once an enemy dies, their attacks can STILL kill you and you'll lose the fight. It happened to me a few times during boss fights.It would be nice if you could use the gamepad for more precise movement and map the item hotbar to the joystick.I don't see why they removed the area level from the zone names.The menu for items can be very confusing, since items that you cannot put on the hotbar still give the option to put them there. Also, some of the item's wording can lead to confusion, like weapon arts reading "You can read this to learn this art," but the art actually becomes available instantly after picking it up. There's also no explanation as to what certain stats do, like LUX damage/resistance, final damage, soul resistance, etc. It would also be nice to be able to unequip gear so you can easily see the item's attributes without all the information of what you'll also lose by swapping equipment out. A full stat summary would be great as well to see your total crit rate, crit damage, damage reduction, etc.Map markers are completely absent, with the exception of save points. I used a map created by demajen (@  about halfway through the game, and without it, I probably would have given up. There are certain points in the game that are absolutely and utterly frustrating to figure out where to go next. The quest logs are vague and don't provide any intuitive direction of what to do next.The story tries it's best to create a world of interesting and enchanting mystery, however I think a bit of it was lost in translation. There are many typos scattered throughout the dialogues. Some dialogue isn't voice acted in the middle of a voice acted cutscene (I'm nitpicking here.) Speaking of voice acting, it's fantastic. The actors did a phenomenal job in this game!Those things aside, it was a very enjoyable and a fun experience! I hope to see more content and patches come in the future! Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a game that suffers from it's own ambition. While there are some great ideas, the good is weighed down by several poor design decisions that make the game feel like a slog. The world you can explore is so large that it begins to feel empty, and the combat is stiff, slow, and too easy. There are tons of areas to explore and bosses to fight, but after the first few hours I was constantly wishing that the game would do something, anything, to be more interesting. For a more in depth review check out my video below!
