_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful to look at and runs great on deck.The map is massive but tight combat with a variety of skills/weapons/loot got me hooked all the way. Lots of secrets and skins as well.My only nitpicks are that the sidequests and endings are a bit cryptic, and story/characters are uninteresting.Gameplay itself is pure bliss!
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun.Afterimage is a game with beautiful hand-drawn art that will captivate you as you play through the game. While you may feel the story lacking at times, it is definitely worth it to play til the end. The controls are pretty responsive and compliment the many combat styles offered in the game.The Fast Travel system could be improved, but it is a polished game other than that.I would say give the game a try. You may like it more than you would think.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a massive metroidvania and one of the longest and biggest ones out there. It's full of beautiful maps, very free exploration, and a large number of items and upgrades to find. The movement and combat are similar to the Castlevania games, and I found them quite enjoyable.There are two problems holding this back from being as good as it could've been, though. The first is that the music is rather lacklustre; most of the game's music is completely forgettable, and the Field of Hydro is one of the most surprising and striking areas of the game precisely because it actually has a strong BGM supporting it, so it's a shame the rest of the game doesn't match up.The other, bigger problem is the translation. It's an obvious ESL job full of grammatical mistakes and awkward phrasing all throughout the game, which is frankly bizarre when they went to the trouble of giving it an English dub. The game's story is extremely convoluted, told in many piecemeal fragments spread throughout the game before culminating in large plot dumps towards the end, but because of how the story is told in combination with the rough translation, it's extremely difficult to follow and understand any more than the bare basics of what's going on in the story.I can very much recommend Afterimage for the great aesthetics, the exploration, and the combat all being solid, so it's just a shame that a few elements hold it back from being a true masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Base gameplay is decent, I enjoy it.But... the story is incoherent mess that you can easily encounter out of order and barely any direction on what the expected progression is. I mean, I found several abilities that the difficulty of surrounding challenges suggested I was supposed to find early on after like ~20 hours of play, not that this stopped anything, but it was clear sign I was supposed to have them far sooner.Also, a lot of the map icons you can place are useless for what you might want to mark the map with, which makes marking places you can't go into yet really poorly documented. This results in a lot of wasted backtracking if you forget what kind of obstacle you meant with the stump or the weird glyph.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap this is a great Metroidvania title.  I was not expecting a game this girthy but I am so glad I decided to dig in.  Beautiful hand-drawn art, huge map to explore, great enemy variation, fun combat and talent system for progression.  At 25 dollars US this is an insane steal of a game!  9 out of 10 game IMO that only falls short of the greats like Hollow Knight due to some very small story gripes and hard to follow quest lines.  Everything else is 10/10 quality.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very average all around.A boring snoozefest. I'm 10 hours in and nothing has been a challenge. If you play the game normally you will overpower all the bosses and can just facetank kill them easily.In order to get any semblance of challenge you need to sequence break, but then you run into more problems where the game's combat is poorly designed.The worst offender is the games talent tree. Just looking at it you get the sense it was tacked on last minute. A lot of the bonuses are tiny. For example one of the talents increases money gain(crystal dew), but the values are 2% and 3%. The most money I've ever seen an enemy drop is $8 so 5% more of that is worthless. A similar case can be found for basically every perk.Overall it has decent art, but to me everything was just so basic and boring I couldn't bring myself to continue playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the Biggest Metroidvania game I've ever played, has a lot of charm, and feels pretty good. _childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is nice, and fits well to a metroidvania. That's not the part I have a problem with.I bought this game hoping to find a sweet metroidvania, to chill after a hard day of work.Don't be mistaken, this is an excellent metroidvania, and huge. Really huge.But bosses are too hard for me. They are designed to be at least 1 hour of trial and miserable fail before having a glimpse of hope defeating them. It's too hardcore for me.I play to have fun, and a bit of a challenge. But that's not challenge to me, it's torture.So no, cannot recommend because of this.But that's not the only problem about the game.The fact that at some point every part of the world is reachable, but nothing tells you "next story area is here" completely lost me.I visited at least 4 complete areas (and giving up because stuck like "you miss a skill to go further") before discovering I missed a small thing 10 hours ago that gives me this skill that will grant me new story progress.So yeah ok, you can go nearly everywhere, but guidance is missing. Story progress is far too slow. That is probably because I spent too much time being lost but still...TL;DR: if you like challenge, and are good at remembering where to go, this game will give you fantastic time. Otherwise you will at best get annoyed, at worse discouraged by boss difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I don't understand this game not getting a higher rating. I have played plenty of metroidvanias and this is one is really good.The game is beautiful, the enemy and biome variety is great. Even regular enemies have several attacks, which is a lot of work. The world design is fantastic, you can traverse most of it in the order you please, so getting mobility skills actually feels rewarding (instead of a necessity). Enemies will be too strong if you venture too early, but you won't normally find physical barriers, like needing a specific skill to go on that path. It's a rich game in content, full of exploration rewards and with a good combat variety (and combos). Even the New game + surprised me in the format they chose. They literally added content there relevant to your gameplay, not your typical "Start over against a stronger world" (I won't go into details to avoid spoilers).I'll point the negative aspects that I believe to be the reason for the mild score. I didn't experience any bugs (although some people did). 1- Length. It's a long metroidvania, and people can get tired more easily, specially if you go for completionist or get stuck somewhere.2- Waifus? But seriously, this story driven narrative can be heavier than other games.3- Backtracking. People didn't really want to use the teleport items to move around, I guess. I used around 30% of my total funds in the game to buy those and spent them quite freely. My advice is don't be shy on buying and using those, money comes easily while exploring and there aren't that many things you really want to buy. I understand it can feel bothersome if you want to traverse the whole map for completion... so just don't get frustrated on trying to 100% all maps.4- Personal opinion: Too easy with potions. They should have some usage time, cooldown or at least be a rarity, not a cheap item that can be instantly used at any moment. It's hard to balance a game where you have 3 different progressions (equipment, skills and level). But I was playing in the higher difficulty setting, and still could facetank most of the bosses. It feels wrong that you can just ignore boss mechanics and go ape on exchanging damage and he dies before you do (while underleveled and without a specific build for it).Overall, I strongly recommend this game, specially if you have already played the gods of the genre (I'll assume you know which ones I mean). I hope you find this review helpful, if you have any doubt, you can ask in comments! ^^

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a very pretty art-style, there's a decent sense of art direction and good variety to enemies, environments and weapons. Combat is slightly worse, mostly due to odd hit-boxes and some attacks going through terrain, which can be exploited by both the enemies and the player. The weakest element for me was the story, which I found rather confusing due to poor translation. _childDocuments_.review: All the trimmings of a great metroidvania are here but the execution is extremely poor. Every quest, key item description and NPC gives next to zero useful information for you to gauge where you need to traverse to next. Instead of the exciting eureka moments where you realize you can now reach a previously inaccessible area; you'll find yourself plagued with uncertainty and exclaiming, "Where the heck am I supposed to go now?", more often than not. Some mandatory items don't even give enough information to go off of for you to realize important details such as the boss that insta-killed you hours ago because... "story reasons?", can now be fought normally.The endgame is rife with spongy, high damage enemies; many of which explode for ungodly chunks off your health bar;  that are placed at every ledge and gap to constantly hassle you with guaranteed hits while you're attempting to make progress and even the early game ones will gleefully send you to the ground, subsequently taking high damage on spikes and other hazards, while you're navigating a jumping puzzle.Even the thrill of looting is spoiled by the fact that many items you can find via new mobility options are sorely outclassed by others that you already found by the time you get around to exploring a corner you missed ages ago.The story is the same bland JRPG, "God messed up and now you have to fix everything", schlock so don't count on a compelling narrative to drive you to keep playing.All in all the game has so much promise at the beginning but it will slowly grind you down to the point you don't even care about finishing the story. That is, if you can even find out how through all the arbitrary key items and complete lack of indication on how to do so without having to frequently check guides.

_childDocuments_.review: Since I'm about to complete all the achievements I'm going to edit my review. First of all I played this game mostly vanilla and so all the quality of life improvements I didn't get until I was nearing the end of everything.This game is massive. This game is one of the best metroidvanias out there. It starts a little slow and confusing but once you get the double jump and wall jump, the game basically opens up entirely. The map is really big and there's so much stuff to collect. The enemy variety is great and so are all the bosses. There's very few re-skinned enemies and bosses and they usually are changed up enough to feel like a different fight. The visuals are great and the controls are very responsive. The combat is fluid and every weapon type is unique with strengths and weaknesses. Because there is contact damage, the longer ranged weapons can be nice but they are slower.The skill tree adds new moves to weapons that really makes using them a lot different. There is a parry tied to the great sword and you get an i-frame dash later in the game as well. The combat is very fluid and even though there is a level up system, your strength mostly comes from gear. This means you can access high level areas and get better gear. I never felt like I had to grind levels. The most difficult part of the game is the npc quest lines. This would probably be my only con. It's hard to keep track of them and knowing where they move to is very challenging. Reminded me of vanilla Elden Ring or some old school games. Sometimes there are little to no clues. You will do a lot of back tracking recovering treasures as you unlock new movement options so I ran into a lot of them that way. All in all this is an extremely fun game and well worth the money. There are many different endings and a NG+ but its more of like an epilogue with chapters that allows you to unlock the true ending of the main game. You are never locked out of content and once you unlock an ending you can load up your save file and keep exploring or try another ending.

Not to mention you have to go hours into the game to find a power-up or ability to return to previous areas to get 1 useless thing you need to progress. Unless you got A LOT OF F-ing time and patience to spend then it's not worth t. I wasted a weekend on this and I wish I didn't.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give a more in depth list of my thoughts than usual because I kickstarted this game and it's only fair I give more feedback.Pros:-Movement is really fun. The variety of air stalls from weapons and the enemy bounce give you a lot of air mobility that can be used in inventive ways for traversal and combat. This makes navigating the map looking for items in the endgame less of a chore.-Combat is fun. Weapon variety is good, and the skills are a lot of fun to play around with. This gives you a lot of ways to approach bosses and combat encounters.-Very non-linear, probably owing to influences from Hollow Knight. Pretty much anything past the early game you can approach in any order provided you have the levels, skill and items.-Game looks gorgeous, which goes without saying. Animation is fluid and areas are visually distinct.-Good length, the variety of endings means you can be satisfied without needing to do literally everything and there's a bunch of side quests and hidden bosses to dig your teeth into.-Phenomenal soundtrack. Like, genuinely, every single song in this game is a banger, I was not expecting it to be this good.Cons:-Story is incomprehensible. It reminds me of Final Fantasy 13: it feels like there's a simple and enjoyable story buried there, but it's hidden under layers of proper nouns. The general lack of a glossary or any lore in the bestiary makes it way worse here than FF13, though.-The game has a linear leveling system. This doesn't combine well with the non-linearity this game takes from other metroidvanias. Some bosses you utterly steamroll and others will beat you to a pulp. This is not helped by the EXP drop on death spawning in the boss arena most of the time, sometimes locking you into a fight you likely can't win unless you pause warp out.-Can sometimes be a bit directionless and confusing. This is bound to happen in metroidvanias, but this can be a problem with how non-linear this game is. This is also especially true with sidequests, with the quest log only giving you vague hints about where to go.-Magic's a bit up and down. Some of them are game breaking but others are weak and most of the buffs I just could not figure out what they did.Overall, the core elements of this game are really fun, but slightly let down by the overall package. Definitely a game worth checking out, and I'm looking forward to more.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Afterimage for about 5 hours, I have to say it didn’t quite hit the mark for me. If you’re a hardcore fan of Metroidvanias, it might be worth a try, but I personally wouldn’t recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: To recommend or not is hard for this game I got it of part of the humble bumble and enjoyed it. You have zero direction of knowing where to go. You have to constantly open the map to check where you are and I got lost so often I stopped counting after 30 times. The enemies are interesting and have unique attack patterns and the bosses are just hardcore sometimes. A lot of their attack/hitboxes are bigger than you would expect which hurts you a lot because contact with an enemy hurts you. 90% of the game I was fighting bosses that were acording to a guide atleast 20 levels above me if not more because I didnt know where I had to go. _childDocuments_.review: Fast travel is patched, merchants also sell the consumable. Biggest problem is gone. One little thing wish for improvement: some platform challenge's difficult and reward doesn't match. Often find something after a lengthly platform to be.....potions?=======================================================================In response to devs:1) by the time player has fast travel unlock pre patched, I would already acquire a couple new abilities, which is double jump, dash, and the crouch dash thing. Every time player gains a new ability, it is very natural for ppl like me, to go back and explore (while I still remember). With fast travel locked with an ultra rare potion, this became almost impossible. I don't have that many potions to go back and forth. This change is needed and I appreciate you guys patched it.2) Checkpoints distance are not a huge deal for me if fast travel wasn't locked. 3) to perform a downward kick movement(下踢), it's left stick down + A button on controller. In my experience, left stick will need to be down before you press the A button. I don't know if this is just something with my controller or a common issue.4) With my progress right now I have 3 heals, and I die total of probably 5 times except platform challenges, so the amount of heal is not really a problem for me, but I do think it's a bad design. And also if I recall correctly I had to collect some items to make it happen. So exploration is required, but fast travel is locked? seems bit conflicted to me.5) I do know you can cancel attacks, but from my experience dex weapons are just the superior ones even on damage output.6) Let's say there are 60, and let's say I cut my playtime to 6 hours because I spent total of 1+ hour total on some platform challenges and also legged my way back to some starting area for exploration. So 6 hours I get a total of 3 charm (I also see some hour review mentioned this), which is only 5% of total charms. Unless you tell me this game is going to be 120 hours, then the resource placement is not justified. 7) I am fine with no iframe, I am not fine with enemy glued on my landing point forever on a platform. I can't land on a platform unless they die. All in all, my biggest problem is with the fast travel, like I said everything else is just small things being aggravated by fast travel lock, which seems to be patched. I'll update my review once verified later.======================================================================Original REVIEW:Some very noticeable problem of the game at current stage: 1) Fast travel. Who TF thought it's a good idea to require consumables which you CAN'T buy, and is even rarer than upgrade materials, armors, weapons etc. I beat more bosses than the amount of consumables I hold. So you basically can't fast travel because every time you want to go somewhere else you need to have at least 2 consumables, 1 for going there, 1 for coming back. I already cleared around 6-7 maps and I just don't see free fast travel unlocked. So whoever is playing the game, likely in their first 10 hours will have no fast travel ability. 2) The problem with fast travel further aggravate the issue with checkpoint placement. The amount of bone fire is pathetic. To put hollow knight comparison, just imagine the entire crystal peak area has 2 benches total.  This basically how the checkpoints are placed in this game. Now with the fact you can't fast travel... I don't understand why anyone play tested the game would think this is a good idea.3) The downward kick movement, the control says stick down + A button, but when you actually play it, simultaneously hold your stick down and press A doesn't work. Stick down needs to happen first. Again, why?  4) Resources early game. With my progress now I am sufficient with healing & resources, but the first maybe 5-6 hours? You will only have ONE healing. Yes, you will be clearing 3-4 big regions with only 1 heal available, beating bosses with one 1 heal. And the fact that you can't fast travel, and the fact that there are only like 2 checkpoints for one entire region...5) Merchants are mostly useless. I don't understand, devs placed so many npcs as merchants, but they are mostly useless. They don't sell upgrade materials, they don't sell fast travel consumables, some merchants will have 1-2 legit useful items but that's it. Blacksmith sells weapons that are worth that the ones you can acquire in game, the cooking girl is only useful once, after you bought all her meals she is useless. I've encountered 4-5 merchants so far, and they just feel useless. Unlike hollow knight, you can buy pins and charms and notch, blacksmith does your upgrade, but in this game, these stuff you need to find by exploring, and you can upgrade weapon in the menu yourself. Just feel like defeats the purpose of having these NPCs.6) Weapon imbalance. Usually I go for greatswords, but as far as I can tell, it's so much worse than scythe/whip/dual swords. The problem with greatswords is you can't interrupt enemies. Just can't. And it's slow. The time you do a single attack dex weapons already did at least 2, so dex weapon actually deals more damage. And scythe/whip wins the war with long reach, especially whip has special jump attack which is a f***ing AOE that clears out the flying enemies with ease. Not to mention bosses's attack interval is smaller than greatsword's attack speed, using greatsword in boss battles is basically suicide. Weapon class needs to be balanced.7) Charms. 8 hours in the game I collected total of 3 charms. Judging by the charm slots there should be around 30 charms if not more. The resource placement again is weird. I understand devs don't want players to be OP, but not giving anything in early game is not the way to go.8) enemy placement. This is the problem with collision and enemy AI. So you have no invincibility when dash (at least I haven't got it yet), meaning collision damage. BUT, once an enemy spots you, they will STAY at the platform edge. See the problem here? You just can't jump to that platform without taking damage unless you somehow figure out a way to kill them, normal enemies are fine, but often you will have ranged enemies throwing firebombs at the platform edge, meaning you can't kill them/jump on the platform without tanking the damage. If i-frame is too much, just don't let enemies glued on the edge. I don't recall hollow knight has this problem ever, enemies will no occupy player's landing point forever.I actually like the game, but these problems are very frustrating especially fast travel. Everything else is just minor frustration which can be dealt with, but fast travel mechanism is a major issue here.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to love about this game. The artstyle is beyond amazing, the world is huge (like the biggest I've ever seen in a metroidvania huge) with great variety in locales, and the 2 weapon combat system makes for some fun combos and playstyle variety. However, the execution of it all is very sloppy. The game feels like it took the worst parts of souls like and metroidvania. There's way too many dead ends even for a metroidvania, and you are lost on what to do many times (not in a good way like other titles in the genre). The weapon use doesn't feel smooth at all, which is fine by itself for a casual game, but it doesn't play well into the fact that this game is anything but that. Some bosses are quite hard and require skill expression, which is hard with the subpar handling of weapons and shoddy movement. In the end, you are often incentivized to chicken out and grind to outscale the boss. I really dislike this modern obsession that games have of imitating Souls in it's difficulty without having the necessary tools or framework to do so.Let's switch gears and talk about the world. Although the areas are beautiful, they lack soul in terms of worldbuilding, which makes navigating through such a huge map tedious. Often you end up just mindlessly going through an area just to find the boss and kill it, without any interesting NPCs or lore to support it. While we're on the topic, the story is a hot pile of steaming garbage, except that you can usually make sense of what's inside a pile of garbage. It's really astounding how you could make a story so generic yet so convoluted and ultimately senseless.Side note about the world: apparently the situation was even worse earlier, as teleport potions used to be a limited resource and you couldn't buy them. I'm also generally not a fan of the teleport concept as I feel it's a crutch in lieu of actual good map design (for example Dark Souls 1, Hollow Knight).TL;DR This game tries too hard to be a metroidvania, a soulslike and a story rich game while not capturing the je ne sais quoi in those genres that makes them great. In my opinion game is carried by the phenomenal artstyle and boss design. Buy it for the artstyle and casual engagement, but don't beat yourself if you aren't willing to invest the 30+ hours required to beat this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. If you're into the anime aesthetic and metroidvania then this is definitely right up your alley. Positives:-overall game play feels great, everything from movement to combat mechanics-beautiful and aesthetically pleasing world to explore with minimal loading screens ( mostly teleporting)-hud/ui, tabs look crisp and clean and is very straight forward -music is very pleasing and well suited for each place you go to-lots to do and definitely above average replay value-you can completely  utilize every piece of equipment in the game. This game really defines modifying builds to suit your play style. There isn't one weapon that's super OP that you just use for the whole game because it does a lot of damage.  Each weapon is unique and will have a stats you prioritize more than the other-some fights could be difficult for some, but easy to manage ( getting stronger somewhere else first) Negatives:-will likely have to pull up a guide to get through parts, more often than not -levelling up is a double edged sword since it is very quick and noticeable. You can really shred in areas you're suppose to  anticipate as "difficult" if you're someone who likes to grind out an area before moving to the next ( might take the fun and excitement away for some) -I found a lot of typos in the eng dialogue-voice over could probably use some work. Don't hate it but some characters did seem a little over the top as well as I often found that I was reading the dialogue much faster than the character who was speaking.Overall as I mentioned before,  this game is amazing. I definitely recommend it. I really had to dig deep for the negatives just so it wasn't bias haha. Current price is fine, on discount would be a score for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is one of the best Metroidvanias I’ve ever played. Visuals are stunning, exploration is rewarding, and combat is fast-paced and precise.The map is enormous, probably one of the biggest in the genre, but progression through the world is fast, so it stays exciting. My playtime of 50h is for 100% completion, with backtracking after every new traversal ability, and all endings (incl. NG+).Combat starts simple, but progressively gets more interesting as you unlock new abilities and weapon skills. Make sure you get comfortable with each new combat mechanic, or you’ll hit a skill ceiling in mid-late game and start getting stuck on bosses. For example, at the start, your only method of damage mitigation is to get out of the way. However, throughout the game, you’ll unlock 3 different mechanisms for parrying, several attacks that have built-in i-frames, and a teleporting dodge.Quick note on NG+, it’s not what you think and is necessary to fully understand the story (only takes an extra ~1hr).

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wanted to like it. I've played for about 4 hours and it just doesn't click with me. The combat is kinda meh, you just stagger most enemies and they can't do anything, the dash is not a dodge and gives no i-frames, the talents are just here's a mediocre ability for this specific weapon or +1 or +3 more damage, the weapon variety is decent, but it just doesn't feel like each weapon is distinct enough to have a different feel than another. _childDocuments_.review: A game with great value if you enjoy metroidvanias and this particular one's gameplay. Boss fights are well done and if you take the time to learn them, they can all be done hitless. The design of each areas are varied, and the soundtrack is also pretty up there too. There's five different weapons (sword, GS, whip, dagger, scythe), and all of them are fun to use, however I feel that a few types are significantly better than the others.I've played two other metroidvanias, Ender Lilies and Bloodstain. I feel that Afterimage is SIGNIFICANTLY harder than both of them if played as expected. However, there are a few tricks, most likely unintended, that can boost your damage to obscene level, just in case you get stuck or frustrated. If you are trying to get 100% achievement I highly recommend googling Afterimage map because unlike some other games, if you miss an item in a region, you're probably not going to find it without combing the area for 30 minutes. There's a little scuff here and there which I think is bad game design (for example, being forced to do a super jump into a hole, and touching the hazards on the sides will send you all the way back down. However, an enemy mob can get stuck in the hole, and your super jump speed is FAST. If you get hit, you get knocked to the side and get telepored all the way back down. Your only solution is like .5s reaction time to stop your jump right before hitting the enemy once or twice, and then fall back down. Then repeat until the enemy dies). I also felt map progression could use a little bit more handholding. There are some areas that are blocked off and require new mobility skills you get from progression. However, some paths to different areas are hidden or like four areas back and you've completely forgotten about, which makes you miss three other areas that it's connected to and game/level/character progression gets really wonky. There's a few more complaints I have, but they are minor in the large scheme of things. However, this is an indie company and the base price of the game is low enough that these issues can be overlooked (after malding for a few minutes). Overall, well designed game. Graphics and soundtrack are top-notch and the combat and enemies are varied. The quality of the game is much higher than what I would have expected from the base price.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: C+Afterimage is a massive metroidvania with immense scope and ambition. Even after the first several hours, the map keeps expanding outward. The game’s breadth is impressive, if nothing else. Yet, it’s that same ambition which holds the game back. Especially for the game’s length, small annoyances compound over the course of a playthrough. Equipment is a good first start. There are six different classes of weapons which all have different controls, pros, and cons. Especially in the early game, you will be frequently switching weapons to find what suits your preferences. But at that point, all of the weapons are incomplete. Every weapon class has several unlockable moves which improve game feel generally, but range in usefulness from niche to ‘might as well not exist.’ Comorbid with these problems is the menu. Navigating it seems to take just slightly too long and suffers from the Ocarina of Time problem of having the menu always begin in the same spot—the almost useless items tab. Enemy drops have virtually no use outside of money but there isn’t much to buy with your funds. Some shops are unlockable and by the time you finish their quests, any gear they offer is far outclassed by your own.  Unusual to the genera, Afterimage has a skill tree. The increases are always miniscule so each upgrade feels weightless, except for the aforementioned weapon skills. The game, in general, seems scared of letting the player grow too strong. New gear and upgrades only provide a small numerical boost which can only be felt after a playthrough’s worth of increases. Sorry, I just can’t get excited over a +0.5% hydro damage buff. I’ll talk to my doctor.  The bosses seem equally tired as while they look different aesthetically, just taking the hits to deal damage is usually more than enough. Healing is generous and the bosses give plenty of time for it.  To break up the negativity, the game is quite beautiful with a soundtrack to match. Immense effort was put into presentation and the game won’t let you forget that. …Mostly because the foreground has a nasty habit of obscuring the play space, especially near the edges of rooms. Even when the game is great, it still provides annoyances.  Lastly, let’s circle back to the breadth. The game’s map is huge but not dense. The game resists any typical guidance techniques seen in other metroidvanias. For example, in Super Metroid, once players enter lower Norfair, they won’t be able to leave without knowledge of advanced movement mechanics or the ice beam. The game traps players in an area until they have gotten the needed upgrade to progress. This is fairly typical for the genera where the game does a lot to guide players along the critical path. Afterimage, in contrast, does no such thing. Since the map opens up so quickly there are always many places to check for the critical path. The game cannot lock you to an area because of a consumable, fast-travel item. As the player does progress, they will need to double check an ever-increasing map for the next chain in the critical path. Because of the game’s scope, keeping up with everything in your head becomes difficult. I hope you were making good use of map markers. Occasionally, it felt like I made progress on accident and stumbled my way into the next upgrade. The time between upgrades, meanwhile, can be several hours, especially in the late game. All this to say, little design decisions snowballed into larger issues when viewed as a whole. That consumable fast-travel item is very limited until the late game where you can buy more. As the map’s size increases the backtrack distance becomes larger and more tedious. While the game has fast-travel, you can only teleport from certain save points to certain other points. Even with teleportation, there will be backtracking. This review has been harsh which might make you question the game’s C+. At the end of the day, the game isn’t offensive, just tripped in the finer details. Broadly, it provided an enjoyable experience for the metroidvania faithful (I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone merely dabbling in the genre). The studio has talent. I just hope on their next outing, they scale back the ambition and make a tighter product.

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a beautiful game, with fantastic bosses, fluid combat, engaging platforming and an exquisite soundtrack. So where exactly does the game go wrong? The level and world design. Those two things are the most important aspects of a metroidvania, and yet this game fails to provide with either. The levels are colossal and take ages to walk through, the world design is a confusing mess and you'll often accidentally go the wrong way and get stuck in levels you're incredibly underleveled for. The game overall is just way too long, I frequently caught myself thinking things along the lines of "The game should've been done 8 hours ago, why is it still going?". The story also sucks, but I've never been one to care about story in games. The game's level design is horrendous, but barring in mind all the other positive aspects of the game, I'd still consider this game to be a 5/10 experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to wait until I was a few hours deep in the game to review it--generally, AFTERIMAGE is a pretty solid Metroidvania, and I have been enjoying it a lot. The skill system is very customizable and the world is surprisingly expansive, and it's an easy pick-up-and-play sort of game, for the most part.There are a few bits that aren't as tight as they could be--there's a lot of precision jumping puzzles that need precise jump timing and they can feel a bit mushy at the wrong time, and occasionally the beautiful art gets in the way of discovering the next objective. Also, the story is a bit of a jumble, but that's expected with a plot like this. So far, the pros outweigh the cons and I've been enjoying it, and I'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; A great game for people who likes exploration, collectibles and nice graphicsIts really weird to me seeing all the negative reviews (altough I do understand their points and they might be valued as well). However, at least for me this is one of the most engaging and exciting games in the metroidvania genre. It's really naive to compare this to HK as they are very distinct pots of tea, and when talking of the metroidvania genre, there's definitely a pot of tea for everyone: some are driven by combat, or exploration, collectibles, plot, well, I may be missing other stuff but you got the point. And although HK became a whole (and well deserved) new standard for the genre, we can't miss that this is ; And even within Metroid and Castlevania franchises there are plenty of different gameplay styles on both canon and spin-off titles, though it's well known that, respectively, exploration and combat are the main points of each one. That said, think of Afterlife more on the Metroid side of metroidvania. If exploration is your pot of tea you might find the same appreciation as myself. Otherwise, it should be a love-it-or-hate-it game you may consider to pass or put down in your queue if you were to invest money on a new game. Pros: - Beautiful graphics- Steam Deck friendly (very smooth with very low TDP and 30/40fps, ~4h batt)- With a map so huge, having almost none loading transitions is something to praise- Unlike some people say, there's a well-rounded plot going on to unveil- Level design is really well done- Nice character building, several routes to take on equips/reminiscences (on the leveling system see below)Up to decide: (for me these are pros anw)- Nice leveling system, it can help less experienced players with some quality of life buffs; It can be totally ignored for experienced/hardcore players to no harm- For me, having a huge world to explore is really amazing, but it could be bothersome to others- Non-linearity is a debatable thing, although I find it very linear for the main route actually - Advanced mode is indeed challenging enough, before 1.0.6 it was the default and when I played it on Switch first time the feeling was no different from when I played HK first time- There are lots of skill tracks for people who likes it, however if you're used to those they can become meaningless as there's nothing too daring like HK's Path of Pain or Indivisible's secret path/DLC- Having evade through enemies only mid to late game may add to the challenge, or just become a QOL annoyance, though this is also debatableCons:- I see people talking about backtracking being a hassle, and that's true; If by any chance you just deviate from the main route or if you just come back to places after every new ability this might become an endless walking simulator for some. This definitely lowers the bar for replay value the most- Mid to late game combat becomes predictable- After the default was changed to Normal instead of Advanced the game became too easy for experienced players (might be just ok for beginners, also it's just something you can easily change)-  Plot is really good but we can all agree that, for a game this huge, it certainly could be further developed

_childDocuments_.review: It starts to get interesting after about 15 hours. Neutral not being an option, I don't think it's fair to recommend a game where half the players who got the first achievement stuck around long enough to get the second one.In isolation, a lot of the individual elements are done well enough. The combat is OK, the voice acting is pretty good, the scenery is usually quite decent. The first problem is that the map is absolutely humongous and it takes a very long time for things to start coming together. It feels like a preview of the future where we'll have AI generate endless level designs. The levels are very open from the start and you can explore in a lot of different directions without moving the story along. The game is conservative and inconsistent in giving you a map indicator to follow. You're given 500 map markers to place though, and I'm not sure if it's meant to be a threat.The second problem is coming from difficulty pacing. A typical metroidvania is largely skill based and upgrades are carefully curated. This game lets you level up rapidly and starts by showering you with gear upgrades every couple of minutes. Combined with huge levels and limited direction, this leads to you getting severely overpowered for the early game content. It's really hard to appreciate boss design and move sets when most of the time you don't need to bother dodging and can just stand there punching them into the ground.The skill tree is another thing that creates the impression of nobody really caring. All but a few skills hidden towards the ends of the branches are just blunt "+2 Armor", "+1 Main Wapon attack", "+5HP". About 15 hours into the game, things starts getting more enjoyable. The rapid levelling slows down, the gear scaling starts levelling off and the areas you explore start becoming an actual challenge. By then you'll also unlock some of the advanced traversal skills, so you won't feel like you're missing out on a lot of exploration.The story itself is alright, but the delivery is poorly paced. The main game consists of rare cryptic encounters, loose plot points and abstract lore. Once you complete the main game, you unlock NG+, which is actually nothing of the sort. It lets you play ten short story sections that give context to everything you saw in the main game. They just left 70% of the plot for after you're "done" with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Would really like a middle ground option here. The main game is pretty good, although it has some issues. One, there's just waaaay too much stuff. They could cut like a third of the game and the length would be about right. The translation and the story are pretty mid. Combat is fun, except for the complete lack of defensive options. You have a dash/backdash, but it has no invicibility frames until you get an ability about 80% of the way through the game, and even then it doesn't have enough of them, so dodging through attacks and enemies fails over half the time. The game could really benefit from having i-frames from the start, having a guard/parry, or even both. The way it stands, most boss fights just turn into battles of attrition, which makes them kind of dull.The reason I want a "sort of recommend" option, though, is the endgame. First, the structure is kinda weird. There's seven endings available initially, one of which is a joke ending, and one of which is the ending you need to actually progress the game. Then you go into what they call NG+, but is really a sidestory that fills in huge chunks of the lore all at once, which is... not the best way to go about that sort of thing. Then once you beat NG+, you can go back to the main game and get the true ending. NG+ is broken up into 10 chapters, most of which are pretty boring, just a short romp through a previously visited area and a mediocre boss fight. Each chapter generally takes less than 5 minutes.I did not get through NG+. The problems start with the final boss of the initial game portion. It's pretty awful, with constant dodging (and their dodge of course gets all the i-frames) and a decent bit of tankiness, so getting damage off on them is a pain. But I beat it, got the ending, and went to NG+. Where you play as a completely different character who plays much, much worse than Renee. Her attacks are painfully slow, and while her damage is good, her fights are just a slog because of the slow attack speed. Additionally, that terrible final boss? Congrats, you get to fight them a couple more times on the way.My breaking point, however, was chapter 9 of NG+. You have a long slog through a harder version of an endgame area, followed by a boss fight. I died to the boss, which sucked, but hey, can always re-fight, yeah? Except it kicked me out to the chapter select, and when I went back in, I was back at the beginning of the stupid chapter, with an absurdly long and annoying runback ahead of me. My immediate reaction was to quit the game and uninstall. To hell with that nonsense. The story is fine, but not good enough to deal with that sort of BS.So, TL;DR, main game is good but not great, play it, beat the final boss of the main game, then skip NG+ and the true ending. Watch the rest of the endings on Youtube. You'll end the game with a much better experience that way.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's massive map transforms what would be an otherwise decent game into an ordeal. Mechanics in this do not work like other established games in the genre, leading to muscle memory and gameplay decisions that will get you killed. I hope you like the need to grind. -=-=-=-=-Review-=-=-=-=-After 26 hours I feel I've gotten enough experience with Afterimage for a good confirmation on my feelings about it.Afterimage is a Metroidvania with a MUCH heavier focus on the Castlevania part of the genre. Yes, you do unlock new powers and abilities to help you navigate, but it is much more focused on RPG mechanics such as leveling up, finding new gear, and traversing zones appropriate to your level. Beyond the significant need for moments where you simply have to grind in order to level up enough to actually survive various areas, Afterimage has one other thing going for it. The map is absolutely, and utterly, too big. It's so massive compared to contemporaries that it well exceeds any reasonable size. Even after 26 hours, I don't feel like I'm anywhere near filling out the entire map. It's entertaining at first when you encounter a new biome, but it wears thin after more and more areas keep opening up and your destination, when you know where you *should* be going, is still so very far away. Also, teleportation between locations requires a consumable item. So the size of the map just weighs down on the experience when travel becomes an ordeal only alleviated with a disposable item. While the art style is gorgeous and the animations are well done, it feels like it's a hybrid of various other games that have come out previously and have done things, honestly, better. Ender Lilies, Ghost Song, and of course Hollow Knight come to mind. Furthermore, I'm not too particularly bothered by the voice acting, although it's clear that the script is a translation and the various word choices for character roles is just odd. Conjurers = Chefs, "Master Mage" instead of "Archmage" etc, etc, etc. There are some baffling design decisions that have been constantly frustrating me over the course of this 26 or so hour journey. Mostly the fact that your evasive options is not a viable means to avoid damage, only insofar as avoiding the attack entirely. You cannot use it to phase through enemies, like in Hollow Knight, Ender Lilies, and other 2D Melee based Metroidvanias. This has tripped me up enough to make combat feel like a chore. Contact damage involving enemies above your level, and especially bosses, will three shot you. Making the attacks that enemies do pale in comparison to the damage they can do to you just by touching them. So games that have taught you that your dash is an effective way to avoid damage is a guaranteed way to get yourself wounded or outright killed. I was not put off by the placement of various enemies unlike other reviews, and the platforming restart locations (when you inevitably fall into or move into spikes) isn't as atrocious as other reviews have commented on, but it can still be annoying in some spots. So the update did fix that problem at least. The need to grind is another issue. You can only earn currency from enemies that reward experience. So only enemies above your level may drop Dews. As a result, I had a constant problem keeping a decent supply of Potions, buying anything of value from merchant(s) and conjurers. -=-=-=-=-Conclusion-=-=-=-=-All in all, I can only recommend Afterimage if you're not put off by the size of the map and the need to grind levels and currency to keep yourself topped off. It's not a bad game, and not the worst game I've played in this genre, this year, it's just marred by some questionable design decisions. I don't know if I'll put any additional time into this or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is an exploration and combat focused Metroidvania (MV) in which you take control of Renee, a mage from the fictional world of Engardin, and set out to unravel her interpersonal mysteries relating to the razing and decaying of her homeland. You’ll do this by traversing an impressively large and open-ended MV map, using a variety of different weapons and spells to defeat foes that stand in your way. You’ll hunt down standard MV navigation and traversal tools as well as fight a myriad of bosses in numerous biomes, befriending and aiding side characters along the way.Movement and traversal are fluid, frictionless and satisfying throughout the entire experience, with precise platforming to boot. Good thing, too, because the map is massive, and you’re going to be spending a lot of time moving through it. Thankfully, the map is equally excellent as it is enormous. It’s accurate and helpful and makes use of a robust marker system perfect for a MV this large with this many blocked paths. From a very early stage, the map opens up to you, and you will spend 10-15 hours during the middle of your playthrough with minimal narrative or quest-driven direction, and only your curiosity to drive you forward. This lack of narrative drive is a criticism of the game, but again, the movement, environments, exploration, platforming and combat are all so satisfying that it mitigates the problem. If you enjoy those, you won’t mind  wtf you’re doing or why you’re doing it. But you will wonder about it and yearn for more.It must be said that the game doesn’t rely too heavily on its platforming, saving most of it for mini-challenge sections in each biome. What the game does lean into is its combat, which feels amazing thanks to a variety of weapons, of which you can equip two at each time for interesting combos and playstyles, and all of which have unique movesets. Interestingly, the combat can also feel frustrating, with damage-on-contact, limited dodge options in the early stages, and a slow response time on some weapons. Regardless, the weapon swings all feel good – they’re properly weighty and come with their own unique playstyles, giving you a lot of variety.The game’s lore is largely inspired by FromSoftware’s brand of storytelling – even going so far as to place a massive Elden Ring reference in one of its later areas. What’s strange is how the game doesn’t really reveal its souls-storytelling inspiration until you’re about 20 hours in. It’s then that item descriptions, environments, and inferences from dialogues allow you to see the world more clearly. You will spend the first 60% of the game wondering why you’re in such a gorgeous and well-realized world with its own history and baggage if the game isn’t going to do anything with it. When the game  do something with it, I would cynically say it retreads ground that FromSoftware already has – exploring human hubris in ascension, natural order and one-ness of the universe, as well as a human vs gods conflict. That doesn’t mean it’s bad, however. Afterimage’s reskin of these themes and bread-crumb trails leading to your realizations are actually quite interesting and satisfying, even if they do feel just a little trite at times. In a weird way, this is one of the game’s strong points for me – Engardin feels real and alive, and though your understanding of it may always remain muddy (more on that in a moment), the interesting worldbuilding and mythos of the universe adds a layer of intrigue, meaning, justification and satisfaction to all of your exploration.The game is a stunner. Hand-drawn environments are beautiful, saturated and diverse in theme, color and assets. It’s incredibly refreshing to play a game like this when so many modern games are mired in grim, grotesque and dark, moody tones and settings.Audibly, the music is so on point, I couldn’t ask for much more. Soft piano riffs flow along with the trees and add ambiance to your exploration. Whimsical and bouncy tunes dip, dance and hop with the bountiful colors and vertical movement of each region. Some of the more overt scores, like the high-intensity or haunting ones – feel like low-budget children’s music, but they’re the exception, rather than the rule. There was definitely the odd one out, but overall, the music enhanced the feeling of the game’s fantastical world, narrative and traversal.The voice acting – aside from one or two characters – is equally impressive for a title like this. The audio-visual design of Afterimage is a  and its excellence enhances every moment of sharp gameplay to a greater degree.Strangely, the game struggles to communicate well. Afterimage suffers greatly from a poor, inexplicably low-effort translation and localization. I can’t stress enough how much of a sad, careless job was done to recreate this game’s text into English and how disappointing it is when you realize this story and lore is robust and meaningful. Typos and mistranslations are common, though thankfully, rarely harmful to your ability to play the game and progress the plot. It’s not just issues with text, however, it’s also a  of said text. The game does a poor job of telling the player how to use certain items, labeling menu sections, how to upgrade weapons, info on equipping and activating Afterimages, or even telling you how the idea of an Afterimage fits into the world. None of it is even close to game-breaking, thankfully, and can be described as more of an inconvenience.Despite its large swathes of aimlessness and the game’s struggle to communicate, Afterimage is still a complete joy to play and will go down as one of the better MVs of the last decade or more. Stunning visuals, extremely well-crafted levels with satisfying exploration, a robust world and slick traversal and combat make this an absolute  for any MV fan. Furthermore, unraveling its sidequest secrets, multiple endings and NG+ will leave you staggered at the depth of this game that seemed so shallow in its opening 10 hours. I highly recommend it. Take the leap and get lost in this world.

_childDocuments_.review: After unlocking all achievements, I can say for sure that this is a good game, kinda. However, there are a couple of things that I found annoying/bad while completing the game. The story is almost non-existent. It is scattered around the maps, and even after collecting all the available pieces on the map that's still less than 10% of the main story. After completing multiple endings NG+ is unlocked. Despite how it's named, NG+ is actually just the rest of the main story. So 90% of the story can be found here. I think I reached this point after 30 hours of game play or more. It can definitely be done sooner though. Now the quality of the story is questionable. It's not terrible territory, but it is not far from that either.The bosses are not really a threat at any point, especially if you upgrade your gear or search the map for hidden items. Traversing the maps was more challenging most of the time. Some exceptions apply depending in what order you unlocked your special abilities. Some of them make bossing much easier. For example, the dash upgrade allows you to phase through enemies and attacks. Without it it's extremely hard to dodge some attacks, unless you predict them or react fast enough to get out of range. Sometimes that's not possible without the right abilities.  Now, that's still highly irrelevant because for some reason they added HP potions in this game. So, you have you natural healing ability that requires timing to be used effectively against bosses, and you also have potions which can be activated at any time and they are instant making it possible to face tank everything if needed. They can also be bought from the shop. The game doesn't really do anything to help the player find the right direction. It's a guessing game most of the time which would be fine if the map wasn't so big. Verifying if a guess is right can take a lot of time, especially in the early game when it's expensive to move around. The fast travel is done through a consumable which can be found on the map or bought from an NPC. Not many are available in the beginning, so yeah, it's tedious to backtrack every time you think you figured something out. It is possible to fast travel between the regions without the consumable, but the points where you can go are fixed, so you'll still have to walk around. A lot of hours will be spent walking around the map searching the next location that might help you advance the story. Honestly, using a guide might be better than just doing it blindly. With that being said, the combat is smooth and fun. You have plenty of weapon combinations to choose from. Each type of weapon comes whit its own special abilities and you can even use magic attacks. The game also offers the possibility to build for normal attacks, special attacks or magic attacks. Also, you can build for drop rate or experience gain. So you can optimize your run as you see fit at any point. The music is decent, and the exploration can be quite fun. After you unlock more stuff you'll be zooming around the map. Overall I would rate the game a 6.5 out of 10. I recommend to buy this game at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stellar. I haven't gone for all achievements in a game in years, but I did in Afterimage, within a few days of buying it. (took 38 hours according to the save file, for anyone concerned). The biggest thing to get used to is that your dodge doesn't have iframes. Once you realize that and work past the muscle memory of "dodge through the enemy", it's butter smooth and the combat feels great. The weapons have various skills and many of them chain well or can even animation cancel into each other, which gives a fluid feel to much of it. I spent 99% of my playtime with the greatsword (oneshots most little enemies and is great for hit and runs on mobile bosses) and dual daggers (ridiculous consistent DPS, great for static bosses).The world is massive, it surprised me several times with its size. It's packed with varied enemies and treasures galore - from a million little currency geodes, to a thousand healing potion chests, and a couple hundred actually important pickups (equipment, skill points, etc.). I started using a map about ~halfway through, which was the only reason it was even vaguely possible for me to get all achievements. Still, searching for that last leaf, not sure which ones on the map I had picked up or not, was infuriating. (Also, I did not bother going for 100% map completion or treasure completion - I got all achievements, which includes all major treasures, and I'm happy with that.)\The story is nearly incomprehensible. I felt like I started to understand it right before the ending, and actually started really liking it! Then in NG+ they add some details which make it so much weaker of a narrative. (NG+ isn't really NG+, it's a post-game series of mini-stories). Overall, I heavily recommend Afterimage - so long as you're not looking for a story that makes sense, and only if you can retrain your brain to stop dashing directly into enemies expecting to have iframes.

I get the gist but it's not all that coherent.o Difficulty options leave a little to be desired. "Advanced" is mostly fun without being excessive but environmental damage on the platforming sections is brutal later in the game. "Normal" is more of an easy mode with even bosses not being that much of a threat and environmental damage is turned off entirely (though you still get reset). o Lots of backtracking to find new things in areas past. Personally, I like this, but I'm dropping it in the neutral because fast travel is a little sparse (without items) and a lot of people don't like this aspect.- Enemies always damage on contact (only a problem because of the next one)- Dodge can be awkward. There are no iframes until late game so dodging forward means you usually take damage. Pressing dodge without a direction goes backwards which feels odd.- Attacks can feel a little clunky (sometimes slow and the hit area can feel a bit too focused). I find some of the more interesting weapons (dual blades, whip) difficult to use because of this.Some things can be improved but I'm still giving this a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for March 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before April 2nd, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A beautiful Metroidvania.Afterimage has a large world with multiple different paths that tantalize players with its secrets.   There are tight controls along with a combat system with multiple different weapons. I’ve already found 5 weapons, including a normal sword, a greatsword, a scythe, and a whip, and also enjoyed using all four of those weapons.  Each weapon feels well balanced as well, the slower weapons doing twice the damage of the quicker ones. Afterimage does a poor job with its signposts telling players which direction is the path to the next area.  The story also is a little harder to follow with many characters referring to things players won’t know about.  The English voice acting was ok but some viewers of the stream preferred the Japanese, and it is a better version.  There’s an Experience level-based system, but try as I might, I have no clue where those values are shown to the player.   While the controls are good, they did take a bit to get used to. Pick this up if you like Metroidvanias.  Though this is on the easy side so far it is a great example of the Metroidvania experience, especially building out a map and then backtracking to open up new areas.  There’s a number of large open areas too that just make the player feel like there’s a ton of different directions they want to go at the same time.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing action game. Classic metroidvania style exploration and combat. The length is also nothing to gloss over. For its cost this was one of the best pickups this year for me. There are multiple endings, some which extend the play time by a large amount (and unlocks an additional route which fleshes out more story).The difficulty can feel a bit high initially - compared to similar games, this one does have collision damage and the initial dash/dodge has no i-frames. It is more similar to classic games of this style where you will need to get some boss upgrades to enjoy i-frames and more jumps, etc etc.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I do recommend this game, though by the end of it I was ready for it to be over.Afterimage is a Metroidvania to the core, where you traverse large expanses fighting enemies, finding areas you can't access yet that you'll need to come back to later with new movement abilities, and a map that literally cannot fit on my widescreen monitor at even 10% of actual size. It also dabbles a bit in the Soulsy stuff with bonfires, losing accumulated EXP on death (though you can't lose levels), and various builds you can play with depending on weapons, subweapon, and up to three accessories. It does this all reasonably well.The story is...less coherent than the gameplay design. Like Souls stuff it really wants you to gather pieces of the story and put it together to get an idea of what happened to the world and things you can do to maybe fix things. Unfortunately even after collecting all the lore the story is still kind of incomplete in some details. I've been told some stuff may need programming knowledge to fully grasp but no idea how much of that is the actual case. Regardless, the main story is mostly complete enough to know what's what and that's good enough, even if the postgame decides to throw a curveball into it.Overall I would recommend this game to anyone who wants a solid Metroidvania like I did. My main quibbles are mostly with the story and I know that's not everyone's primary concern, if it's even one at all.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I think I've cracked it! I know why Silksong has been delayed this long. If released now, it will struggle to shine above the rest that are currently in the melting pot of great 2D Metroidvania's and that pot is now getting very full.Afterimage is absolutely in that pot. Its a very VERY good game.Now, I'm probably going to sound a little harsh, but AI doesn't do anything particularity different from the next guy. Like its competition, its large, challenging, looks great and has tight controls, has great platforming sections, loads of bosses and tones of stuff to find and explore, but imho, that's no bad thing.In terms of size and scope, its a huge game, on par with something like Aeterna Noctis. If your trying to 100% it then expect a playthrough to keep you busy for well over 40hrs. I'm about 20hrs in and still have loads to do.Where this game does find is niche would be in its difficulty level. Like others in this class, it is a challenging game but like Aeterna Noctis, it has some forgiving mechanics that won't have crying to mummy when you die or fall on a spike. For newcomers to the genre or anyone who has avoided the harder games like Hollow Knight, AI is a far better balanced game in terms of difficulty especially with the boss fights. They are difficult but not bonkers hard and since everything is level-rated, you can quickly google and check whether an upcoming boss is going to be a walkover, hard but doable or a total nightmare bsed on your own level rating. FYI, don't shy away from trying a boss 10 or even 15 levels above you. I'm currently at level 65 and have managed a few level 72 encounters and to be clear, I count myself as someone who doesn't fair well in boss fights. I finished HK but my god I died a million times!Healing is another mechanic that makes like a little easier, especially in boss encounters. You can equip stuff that will allow a little re-gen over time, swallow a potion that instantly heals or use a valuable glyph to top up your health although the last method will leave you vulnerable for a few seconds.The only major gripe I have with AI, is the story. Its pretty bad and isn't helped with poor translation to English. For me, this isn't too much of an issue as I tend to zone out of a games story pretty quickly if the meat and potatoes are good enough. I had the same thing with AE but the amazing platforming kept me engaged. The same goes for AI.All-in-all, AI is a must addition to anyone's 2D MV Platformer collection.Fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: So after just getting all endings (there is a bunch), I can say, I enjoyed this about as much as Hollow Knight. The Map is enormous. Honestly I was surprised that whenever I got slightly lost, I just ended up finding yet another zone to explore. Like some have mentioned the first real boss () really gave me a thorough beating. After that the game goes easy on you for a bit and then spikes in difficulty in the mid-game. I assume it is because some of these bosses might be designed with the thought in mind, that you might have gotten certain upgrades, that help you beat them. The combat was super fun and satisfying. You can choose a main-weapon, a subweapon and like a magic focus (so a staff, book...). That, plus the accessoiries that add different effects, the armor with different sub-stats and the vast talent tree give you a lot of agency over how you want to play. I saw some people say stuff about how the game doesn't really take you at the hand telling you where to go and while that is true, I feel like that is super fun in metroidvanias. Much like in Hollow Knight, I ran circles a lot before I eventually found an upgrade that opened up even more areas of the map to me. The story is a bit convoluted I would say. I liked it a lot, but it does feel to me like you are never gonna grasp the entirety of what is going on. However, similar games do it in a similar way, so I don't mind. It invites you to make theories yourself. Another thing is the Art. The game is absolutely gorgeous. Be it the effects, characters or backgrounds, everything felt like it was crafted with immense care. Another thing I wanna mention is the voice acting. I played it with Japanese VO and recognized a bunch of voices from anime or jrpgs (Ifree for example has the same VA as Morgana from Persona 5 in Japanese and the MC is voiced by the same VA as Violet from Violet Evergarden). For me that was definitivly a big plus. TL;DR:Art: GreatVoice Acting (played on Japanese): GreatStory: Not on the nose, invites making theories thoughExploration: Map is gigantic, lots of places to explore, sometimes got lost searching for an upgrade to proceed, just to find more areas.Combat: Satisfying and lots of personalization

_childDocuments_.review: I remember watching the preview trailer for this game and being cautiously optimistic. Cool weapon combos and a snappy dash mechanic? Hell yeah. But I missed the chance to play the demo, so I just kept checking every month or so to see if it was finally released.I'm happy to say that the game has exceeded my expectations. The world is massive, there's tons of gear to find, and tons of tech to unlock. I was also really surprised by just how good the audio and visuals were. But most importantly for a metroidvania game: the combat, physics, and difficulty all feel excellent. Exploration becomes an absolute blast once you get the double jump and wall stick -- and I still have 5 more core mechanics to unlock.Based on the earliest patch notes, the devs truly seem to be listening to feedback and making the game even better.This is one of those hidden gems that actually deserve your support.

_childDocuments_.review: OK an update since I've played a good chunk of the game and can provide a more accurate review.Good things first. The game is a fantastic Metroidvania and most fun I've had playing in awhile. It tick everything a MV and SotN fan could ask for such as excellent and rewarding exploration, fun combat, great boss fights that are balanced and challenging but not too frustrating and this is easily most massive map full of secrets I've seen. Extremely strong contender for MV of the year. It even have some fun Easter eggs from SotN. It's evident that the devs are huge fans. The game is not perfect though and there are few issues but I'll say the good generally far outweigh the bad. -Localization is not good. It is quite difficult to make sense of the story and dialogue. -Status screen doesn't provide enough details and spells do not explain what they do exactly. There are several spells that aren't as obvious in their functions.-Refillable flasks doesn't scale up properly with your HP and by the endgame you have to chug like 4 to heal fully. -Visual clarity can be bad in some areas naming it difficult to see enemies. Adding a contrast setting that adjust the backgrounds would definitely help. -Sidequests are difficult to figure out how to complete, this is mostly due to poor localization issue. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty long souls-like type of metroidvania, my review says "I recommend" this game but I don't recommend it because it has a souls-like aspect, no I recommend it because it is a good metroidvania.If you want to play it do not play it for it souls-like part but for its exploration part because it is really good on that field and the map is really huge.The game is beautiful, levels, music (if you like calm music in a metroidvania...) and so on... It is just a matter of personal tastes after all ^^Concerning the exploration it reserves you some difficult and tight sequences and it is a very good thing. There is a "return to a checkpoint" mechanic when you fall in an harmful zone, it is a bit weird but not a problem at all just be prepared sometimes to come back far away of where you fail...The real and major problem is the combat part of the game, as a souls-like game it is easy but extremely punitive I would even say that it is pointlessly extremely punitive, everything deals a ton of damages in this game. To balance things the bosses' patterns are really simplistic, to the point of when you have seen all what a boss can "offer" you know you will beat it no matter what... but take a hit and you lose 1/3 of your life and a lot of tries... You will say: "for example, if you have 100 tries on a specific boss it is a difficult fight", but if the hundredth try is the one where you take no hit and the other ones are those where the boss one-shotted while you learn the patterns, is it still considered difficult or is it artificially difficult easiness? Afterimage falls in the second one...Finally like I said at the beginning it is a good exploration metroidvania but with a "souls-like" aspect which represent the only crippling defect this game has, unfortunately...Knowing that give a chance to this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Two important notes: As of Christmas 2023, the devs are still patching and adding content. Note that many complaints in older reviews (minus contact damage) have been addressed at this point. Also, I strongly recommend downloading demajen's Google Drive map if you get stuck.On that note, the game is ginormous, and will take a completionist, or anyone who wants to see proper endings, around 60 hours or so. Despite some lack of direction and difficulty spikes (the latter of which can be solved by over-leveling and some potions), I loved it. Don't expect much of the story though: the translation isn't the best and some details are only clarified in the very final areas of the game.Since I frequently see questions about being Souls-like, let me clarify a few things. First, as a casual player, I got through the game just fine - even on the Advanced difficulty (there was no Normal when I started). I've no interest in Souls difficulty or banging my head against bosses. Otherwise, similarities are Estus Flask equivalent healing, enemies respawning at save points, dropping recoverable XP on death, reading death markers, items with vague descriptions, lots of unlockable shortcuts, and a few bosses that will roflstomp you, regenerate their health, or spaz out when they're about to die.+Proper Metroidvania. Very open world as game progresses.+Devs keep releasing content+Gorgeous+Lots of detailed enemy types and almost no reskins+Relaxing music+Detailed animations+Lots of weapon variety+Higher level enemies have a mark over their head+Some minor puzzle platforming+Two difficulties (Advanced is default)+Boss rush mode with two additional playable characters+Shortcuts unlocked as you progress+Map pretty detailed and tracks area completion %'s+Map allows 500 markers with many icons to choose from+Save areas indicated by sight and sound from distance+Voice acting isn't too bad for a non-English dev+Secrets everywhere, and almost always hinted at+Item available to help find missing treasure+Can respec with a consumable+Bestiary with drop listings unlocked early on+Can go elsewhere and level up if you meet a tough enemy+No squeaky anime girl shouting on every action+Ability to play two saves at once near end game is neat+You can find all ten endings in a single playthrough+I'd guess 25-70 hours, depending on completionism and guide use~Story makes very little sense until you after finish 6/10 endings~Endings are all underwhelming, however~Characters don't have much personality~Game can have some spikes in difficulty~Enemies telegraph almost all moves, but some give next to no time to react~Boss levels sometimes much higher than zone they're in~Some precise platforming, though none were rage-inducing~Boss rooms not marked, but can usually be predicted by architecture~Death penalty is pretty light~Game's huge. Like, really big.~Could have used a target dummy in town~Most endings are underwhelming, at best~You'll need a guide to see everything-Seven unskippable splash screens-Contact damage and no iframes on normal dodge ability-Few iframes after damage and zero if touching spikes-Iframe dodge not earned til late game-Enemy attacks frequently unavoidable due to AoE or cramped quarters-Hard to tell what talents are available at a glance-Translation and typos need work-Quest objectives can be very vague or even misleading-Often no way to repeat questgiver dialog-Contact damage and no iframes on normal dodge ability-Large number of mechanics etc that aren't explained-No way to track duration of food buffs-Most fast travel requires a consumable-Can use (i.e., waste) potions when full on HP/MP-Final area of game not worth exploring-Have I mentioned contact damage? With things like books or rabbits?Played on:i7-14700, RTX3060, 32GB DDR5-6000 @ 1920x1080Using PowerA Enhanced Wired Controller for Xbox Series X|SAdvanced difficulty

The art style is so good, none of it it really repetitive and the bestiary is interesting too, barely any reused sprites.One big plus for me is that every dialogue in the game has voices, and the voice acting is really good (played with JP voices idk about the rest).The only downsides I noticed during my playthrough are, the endings, while I really loved finding all of them, it felt a bit lacking, and the exploration, since it's a metroidvania, back tracking is to be expected, so having a TP system is nice but, while it didn't bother me much, having to use an item to fast travel and purchasing it every 30 mins to find all the secret and finish exploring might be annoying for some players.Overall, really nice game, a true hidden gem that deserves a lot more visibility that I would recommend to anyone I meet on the street.10/10 just imrpove your endings in the next one-
