_childDocuments_.review: ::EDIT:: Added a section after finishing the game.Finally, a proper metroidvania. After 9 Years of Shadows and The Last Case of Benedict Fox turned out kinda unfinished/meh, I was not expecting Afterimage to deliver so hard.- it is very Igavania inspired, so expect a lot of abilities, weapons, attacks, and mild RPG elements like collecting gear and leveling up- the world is HUGE, and it is quite easy to get lost and/or stuck. Seriously, it is perhaps the biggest metroidvania world I've ever seen- there are some difficult platforming sections, thankfully most of them are optional- expect progression gated behind bosses that drop items and/or abilities- it has "soulslike" elements? When you die, you drop your current XP needed for next level- supposedly it is pretty long, in 30h-50h range, far more than typical metroidvania- story is kinda messy. It has problems with pacing, and it drops so many names, terms that it quickly becomes irrelevant noise- Art style is incoherent at times. Character portraits feel like they were all drawn by different people, and it feels jarring at times. For example, we have our main character is drawn really well, but then her companion spirit looks it was hastily sketched in Blender- UI is kinda messy, unintuitive at times- you have to add map markers manually, and it quickly becomes a choreUpdate after finishing:- Afterimage is HUGE to the point that it almost becomes its flaw. Quantity over quality- there is contact damage when touching enemies, and it eats a sizable chunk of your health every time- The story was all over the place and I could not follow what was going onwhatsoever- quests dont seem very clear on what you need to do AND you will often get lost trying to figure out where next story bit is supposed to happen- there are few frustrating platforming sections- bosses are either gigantic pushovers (early) or hyper agressive damage sponges that can kill you in 3 hits (mid-to-lategame)- music is kinda just there, in the background- difficulty ramps up to absurd levels later on.Overall I found this game to be a mixed bag. It has slick combat system, huge world and gorgeous presentation but I feel that it GREATLY overstayed its welcome and its flaws really drag it down. 6/10Reccomended, but on sale

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a great game, let's start off with that. It has fluid combat mechanics, meaningful weapon choices, and a ton of secrets and items to discover. However, you shouldn't bother with this game if you value your time, because this game loves to waste your time. Two big flaws that ultimately means I cannot in good conscience recommend this to anybody:1) the level design is horrendous. It's literally Dead-ends: The Game. It's like the devs see one of the pillars of metroidvanias is backtracking, and thought this meant putting in as many dead ends as possible to force players to backtrack, because that's somehow fun. Out of the 30 hours of play time, I would say at least 20 hours is devoted to hitting a dead end and having to backtrack to explore a different area of a biome. Heck, this is how a biome works: you get dropped into the center with 5 branching paths out of the nexus. You explore one path until inevitably you reach a point where you can't go on anymore because you lack an ability. Then you turn around and walk back to the nexus to visit the next path. This is incredibly infuriating a few biomes in because it's almost as if the devs though this is what backtracking should be. Good metroidvanias handle backtracking organically, where it doesn't feel like you're doing so, but in this game, it's foced upon you. 2) The story. Oh my god the story. It's not even a translation issue. The devs just don't know how to present a fantastical world at all. The story is confusing because you're expected to learn a few hundred new nouns, and even metaphysical and cosmic concepts like how the world works, how the god works etc (which is never presented in a straightforward way, because devs are trying to ape the Dark Souls style of storytelling without actually knowing how to do it right), before you can even grasp the basics of the main plot. Not to mention the devs absolutely suck at writing dialogue, which means none of the characters are memorable or meaningful. Worse, most of the worldbuilding hinges upon you understanding very technical concepts such as redundancy checks, code merging/splitting, and network concepts. Sigh. What an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mess. This is one of the worst and convoluted story I've ever seen in gaming, and I've been playing games for close to 3 decades now.Conclusion: play the game if you have a lot of time to waste, or enjoy just firing up a game and wandering aimlessly. This game will fulfill that need. But if you want a game to mean something, or deliver a memorable experience, well, skip this one, you're not missing anything.

_childDocuments_.review: The 80% positive rate on this is almost criminal - no this game isn't perfect, but it's still  much better than review scores suggest. Starting with the good side of things, the Gameplay is really solid all around. Especially once you get a few abilities, the movement is crisp, and the builds actually felt pretty impactful and were fun to play around with! (Seriously, this is one of the few games I tried out basically every new weapon I picked up to see how its unique skill worked). Also, the world is . Like seriously I don't remember the last time I played a Metroidvania and just kept wandering and wandering for that long with just an endless pouring in of fresh content. And what's really remarkable is that despite this game's size, the enemies never felt like basic reskins of earlier foes. Honestly, in this genre, for that alone Afterimage should be more positively reviewed :PBut seriously, this world is massive and absolutely gorgeous. I never got sick of the backtracking parts because the world was always just a treat to look at and wander through. Really solid Metroidvania stage design all around imo.That said, there's absolutely room for criticism and improvement here, and I  think I understand people's complaints. For one, the first couple areas are kinda mediocre. I get they wanted to keep it simple to introduce the game, but having played a ton of other Metroidvanias, I found the opening areas here to be really lacking. It's almost like around the midpoint of the game, the designers finally were given freedom to make what they wanted to, and it stays pretty much an absolute banger of a game after that. It's also worth noting in many aspects, this game  re-tread old ground in terms of gameplay - pretty sure every movement upgrade could be found in some other games that I've played just within the past 6 months. However, the execution is still clean - it's fun just to move around the world by the end of it! Also, a lot of the bosses hit me with new and interesting patterns - especially getting into the mid and late game.Definitely the biggest things holding this game back are the writing and soundtrack. Most of the songs are admittedly kinda mediocre, although there are some absolutely phenomenal ones hidden among them. Also, the translation wasn't done all that well for the English version, and I suspect quite a bit was lost along the way. I was still able to piece together the story by the end of the game - and I actually ended up enjoying the story aspect by the end - but  is it hard to follow for most of the game. But in spite of all of that, this game is still a  solid recommended from me, especially for people who've played a couple other Metroidvanias before. Sure, Hollow Knight and so on are "better" games overall, but once you've exhausted the ones everyone knows already, this is seriously one to not sleep on. Give it a go!(Also, NG+ is a complete misnaming. You're not replaying the whole map at all - it's literally just a continuation of the story. Unlocking NG+ is  the end of the game. I can totally see how people would feel left with a sour taste in their mouth if they missed this.)

Like Castlevania SOTN, you can outlevel the enemies in an area and tip the scales in your favor. Don't expect to find a crissagrim to carry you, though.A few minor gripes I have:Overall, I enjoyed it and found it well worth my time and money, despite the little irritations that could be an easy fix.

_childDocuments_.review: 20 hours into the game and honestly, I'm in love with it.for now I'm seeing several negative reviews about the game and some even constructive criticism but let's analyze them briefly and talk about the good and bad things about the game---- TOP NEGATIVE REVIEWS POINTS:FAST TRAVELThe game starts giving us potions as the only fast travel option, these potions are very rare and no NPC sells them at the beginning of the game. But I don't see how this could be negative for the game, I understand who says that the lack of fast travel is a show of ego on the part of developers who trust too much on their map and believe that players will like to go from one side to side without teleporting, but honestly I don't see how the lack of FT can become a problem, given the amount of path that the game offers and forces you as a player to better manage the things you are going to buy or ways that youre going(i know that keep walking in a vast world where you doesn't know where you're suppose to go kind look strange, but for me is something exiting, remember me when i was playing dark souls 1)I only used two potions before reaching the part where you get infinite fast travel in the bigtree(and it was for go to the first zone again, I wanted to see if there was anything to do there)COMBATI would like to start by saying that the devs did a great job in the weapons section, the game has several weapons and each one of them will have a different function and gameplay while you level up the skilltree.The huge amount of weapon variation and their skills opens up a huge skill celling for those who like experimentationthe first point about combat in negative reviews is the contact damage, which I and many other metroidvania players really find interesting and adds to the game, you have to think carefully about where to place your character, when to jump, where to fall, etc.The game's combat is extremely responsive, in my opinion better than the hollow knight itself, with aerial skills, weapon switching, parrys, and many other things.I've seen people (mainly Chinese reviews) complain about the game not having incencibility or initial parry.with respect to i-frame dash, the game doesn't really need i-frame for the whole beginning, the vast majority of bosses are easily dodgeable just by moving a little or jumpingand about the parry being anti-responsive, I don't know, for me in my gameplay the parry of just hitting the projectile and the greatsword parry work very well BOSSESabout the bosses i saw several opinions, mine is that they are fantastic (i just wish that they had more unique ost), the great majority of the bosses are ''easy'' depending on your level, given that it's an open world game and you can get underleveled or overleveled easily, in addition to being able to pick up very strong weapons or armor easily (I myself picked up a weapon 4x better than the one I was using previously, just for being curious in the exploration and climbing a wall)in terms of patterns, the ''mini bosses'' tend to have simpler and easier patterns as usual, but even so, they are still an interesting fight depending on your level.But holy god the main bosses are great, incredible, it's cool to see that the game already has good bosses at the beginning of the game, which makes learn and react quickly to the patterns become something very funART I know some people have commented about the game dimentions or setting that there are times when you look lost or can't see things straight, I just didn't want to comment because it's ''personal'' as I can clearly see the characters and what happens on the screen, but it is undeniable that there are some parts that are a bit complicated, I can remember 2 places off the top of my head, but in general it is not as big problem as people sayAnd about the designs, they are very functional and beautiful, the only thing I could say about the art of the game is that the sprite of the main character being drawn in anime style (style that the game doesn't use) made me uncomfortable for a good while time, but overall you get used to it------------------------ I believe that these were most of the criticisms from the negative reviews,  now I will go into other points that I would like to talk about------------------------MAPThe map is huge. it's gigantic, and above all it's an amazing place to explore, if you go to my profile you'll see that I have hundreds of screenshots... because the world made in this game is just fun to explore.the parkours to obtain items are challenging enough to make me smile when I manage to pass them, and almost always comes a reward in line with the difficulty of the given challengeSOUND DESIGN  OST     I was walking on the meadow when I entered the cave and     begins one of the best ost I've ever heard in games,     honestly what the compositors did in this game is from another     world, ALL zones have a good memorable music   DUB (mostly english)      I played the game in English, and I can say that really, the dubbing is not the best, I forced myself to switch to Japanese      because I couldn't really get the feeling in the characters (Japanese also has some small problems but it's already much      better)  SOUNDS     one thing that bothered me at first was the character's attack screams and the sounds of the hits, her screams feel      inconsistent and out of place, for example using dualblade the character is screaming as if she is lifting something very      heavy.     there is little variation in attack sounds, however the ones that already have are functional, I might want some sounds for the      crit or air strikes. NARRATIVEI'm not going to get into the game's lore, but the narrative, the way the story is conveyed is good enough to be interested in a not-so-creative plot like (go looking for a girl who will probably be my future friend )the characters feel alive, each person you meet on the journey is interesting and someone memorable, I remember when rosalia said she was leaving town and I was desperate traveling the entire map to find out where she would beoverall the narrative is functional and fun to follow------------------------------------------------TLDR: the beginning of the review was me saying my opinion about the general criticism that the game is getting but a summary could be that: it's fun, it has a good world and good soundtrack.if you are looking for a game to get lost in a world where you have to know how to organize things, have exciting fights and spend a lot of time exploring a vast world that seems to have no end and you always will get new things to see, this game will meet your needs!

And if a boss is really mopping the floor with you, you can most likely just divert your course elsewhere and focus on a different area, returning later when you feel powerful enough. It's not linear at all, I felt like I had at least a couple of options on where to go next for most of the game. Plus a bunch of different endings, not to mention a NG+ with even more exclusive content, though I haven't even started on that. It's packed with lore around a weird anime-type story that I only halfway attempted to follow and I still spent 80hrs on my first playthrough. Yeah, this is right up there with Hollow Knight imo. _childDocuments_.review: After getting three different endings and then knowing there is more but with a different character for some obscure fourth ending, I just quit. It was getting tedious and boring. The lore is totally obscure. The story line vague and uninteresting. When I hit the 10 chapter (New Game+) mode, which felt tacked on, I knew I had enough. I really had no idea what the plot was anyway. The game becomes a chore around level 60 to grind. Several of the collectibles seem to have no purpose. I had no idea what to sell and what to keep.  I also hated the collision damage mechanic.I did have an issue with HP regeneration for a bit but that seemed to get cleared up in a patch. But HP regeneration is extremely slow even with the right items and talents. The "subweapon" (stupid naming), which is your magic, is underpowered and MP is very slow to regenerate so I ended up hardly ever using it.  The fast travel mechanic is poorly implemented which requires you to use potions if you really want to get where you need to me. There is fast travel between main hub points but other "resting" points require a potion. I saved using them until the very end when I was trying to get required items for the quests.The quests can be difficult to understand what is required and where exactly to go. I ended up using a quest help guide and a downloaded map to assist with questing. I highly recommend that if you do pick this game up to go get the map online. It helps out a lot as the overall map is quite large and complex. In the end, I felt there is just too much wrong with the game to outright recommend. I can't even say that updates can fix the issues as most of them are with the core gaming aspect itself but maybe?

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is not bad. It looks nice, runs well, is decently fun and is actually fully voiced. However combat feels weird and very linear, skill tree is stupid and pointless, quest book just kinda exists (either make it useful or don't add it at all) and some areas are very annoying to move around (yes I'm talking about the one where you barely see yourself, not even talking about enemies or walls). As for the boss fights, they weren't bad, but there was so few of them in the first 5h. Most of the gameplay was walking around and 2shotting trash mobs. For Metroidvania subgenre fans who have already beaten all the good ones like Hollow Knight, Ori or Blasphemous I would say give Afterimage a try, but for everyone else my opinion is "don't bother".

_childDocuments_.review: It’s an ok game. I’d give it 7/10. The game mechanics are nice, the controller is really good, the many many items and weapons feel unique and well though out, the map,is huge (a bit too much for the good of the game), the music is rather forgettable and the characters feel hollow. The main problem is with the story: it makes zero sense. I had 2 endings that made no.sense.whatsoever. that featured characters I had never seen and made me feel nothing. If a game’s ending is emotionally void I consider that a huge videogame sin. I guess the developers felt like dropping in a bunch of characters (95% of them forgettable and useless) with “fantasy names” would make for a cool story… it does not. The story problem leaks into the gameplay, very often you will have no clue about what to do next. It’s like the characters assume that you, the player, know and care about the world before the game. Overall it’s a nice game. Sadly it feels like it could have been a great game. I had fun but no way in hell am I going to go chasing other several endings that will make me feel absolutely nothing for the world or the characters that inhabit it.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow what an incredible game this was, I was following it for awhile before it came out and was confused why it was getting such bad reviews, I guess they might have patched something out? Cause i didn't experience any issues at all and i had the time of my life. This is also definitely worth every penny this game is HUGE!I will start of rambling about everything i loved and then in the end list the criticism i have, so here we go:I LOVED THE ART DIRECTION, this is such a gorgeous game to look at, it's one of those i have to stop my gameplay and take screenshots of the backgrounds kind of games.This definitely feels like the dev team Really really likes Hollow Knight which i mean it's my fav game so please let me have all the inspiration and homage. It's very much an anime hollow knight with a bit more focus on rpg elements like choosing your weapons & armor and putting on buffs with cooking.It even has actual reference in the game to hollow knight so don't come and pretend it's not inspired by it.Gameplay was fun and easy to understand, the different weapon types was all enjoyable to play around with, and the parkour was fluid and mostly good (we will get to that)Story was pretty well written, there is quite a lot of characters and stuff moving around and the quests were fun to complete. I kind of naturally 100% things because i'm very thorough in my exploration, so i didn't miss much and also could get all achievements at the end pretty easily without much grinding.This game is very easy to 100%, you can get all endings in 1 playthrough and if you just play the game and do all the things by the end you will probably be close anyway. It is very late in giving out achivements and you will not see the majority before you reach late game (probably will get 3-4 in the start/middle) so don't be discouraged by that, they all come at the end lolI also chose to play the game with japanese audio cause i didn't like the english, so the voice acting was great for the japanese!Great music & sound design. It was definitely a bit generic in places, but it was overall very good. Will add some of the pieces to my video game ost list.Small positives:- The bouncing around enemies do when you kill them amused me to no end throughout the entire game- The hitting back projectiles sound is just really satisfying and i loved doing it.- Cute weird npcs like a mushroom we use as a jump pat and a fweet fweet manty ray we ride on- suprises all around. This game kept me suprises about what it was gonna come up with next. Top down map of ocean where i control a manta ray? Never expected that :3- OwlNow it's time for my criticism, and despite these i still immensively enjoyed myself and 100% finished the game.- The hitboxes for the objects you parkour over is sometimes really unclear and the respawn zones are just??? I don't get them sometimes they send you back into the closest spot where your character can stand and sometimes they fling you across the entire room and into a enemy. One of them even had me in a perpetual loop of respawning and despawning. Was a bit annoying but it was thankfully not that big of a deal because the parkour was pretty easy.- The entire NG+ section with 42 was lame and uninteresting, i didn't like the sudden change in playstyle after 45 hours, and i just skipped through it to get back to Renee, i like the character and the storytelling but i didn't care for the gameplay, it was way to easy and way to clunky, there is no reason to fight anything because you don't get gear or xp so i just ran through the sometimes confusing zones it chose without telling me where i needed to go. It's just a copy paste of the map with a new character that has worse movement and combat... Not a fan- This game has like... 10 endings and you have to sit through the credits in like 7 of them... Why? Why not just let us skip the credits after we have seen it once. I love you guys and it's great you want to give credit to everyone but i don't need to see it 7 times in a row when i'm getting all the endings back to back.- Majority of the bosses was quite forgettable to me especially all the early/mid game ones, I don't rememeber a single one of their names or appearances.- While the story was good and enjoyable to experience it was sometimes a bit of a word salad with too much lore and naming things taking up too much of the dialogue instead of focusing on the emotional beats that is more universal. They did put in a lot of thought into the world building so cudos to them for that.Despite those things PLAY THIS GAME if you like metroidvania/light rpg stuff. It's a great game despite what people say, and it has LOTS of content, i kept being suprised by how big the game was, every single time. Definitely worth the price and more.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great metroidvania, and probably the biggest one available today (seriously, it's a lot bigger than Souldiers and probably some 3 to 4 times the entire size of SoTN). Its biggest problem is the story, way to convoluted to grasp your interest. When you want to tell a story that has secrets, you usually keep just a few main things hidden, plainly explaining all the rest of the lore to give players a basis to keep them interested, wanting to know more. I this game, though, they just filled the dialogues with huge texts containing way too many unknown elements thrown at you right of the bat. Too many  to form any consistent lore basis or even to keep track of until very far into the game. When they finally reveal something, you're just tired and already lost interest a long time ago.Pros:- beautiful art.- solid gameplay.- good weapon variety.- some very fun special attacks for each weapon class.- good enemy variety.- movement abilities available early in the game (one of the most important things for any good metroidvania).- huge map (equivalent to several SoTN castles) with interesting enviroments.Cons:- story is too convoluted and has a horrible narrative.- some of the special attacks are not really useful of even fun to use.- magic is basically useless (too costly, easily depleting your mana, and does insignificant damage compared to weapons).- too few teleport points, making some travels a chore (in a game this huge, all savepoints should be teleports).- many quests and items you'll never even know about without guides, because there are no clues (again, in a huge game).- bosses are too easy.Overall, metroidvanias are more focused on exploration and platforming gameplay, so I still totally recommend Afterimage. Very fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: Good metroidvania. So far on the easy side but I have a feeling it will ramp up to something more normal. Since it doesn't have a difficulty slider I expect the game to be somewhat casual with some additional bonus expert elements.The controls and movement feel extremely stiff compared to other games. The game supports 120Hz but the handling definitely feels like 60Hz. Very similar to "Ori" in the visuals and environment. It's made in Unreal which is good.The game features the most beautiful UI I have ever experienced in this type of game, it is kind of overwhelming. It does come at a cost however, every action from flipping a page to opening the menu has some small lag.It is a bit overpriced at 30$ CAD, get it 50% off from that (like I believe I did).This is a translated game and it will not hold you by the hand. You will be expodumped immediately and no one will explain talent points, weapons and such on your arrival. It's both good and bad. I enjoy discovering and having stuff to experiment, but not clearly labeling the skill tree by weapons is confusing for example.

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a fun game. There are something which can be polished or ironed out. _childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful Metroidvania, probably the best I've played in the last couple years. Sound and graphics are great, motion is fluid, character models are crisp and the effects & music's perfect.The good:Extremely tight controls, satisfying combat & movement compared to a lot of other recent games in this genre which is required because this is an enormous game-- I don't think I've ever played a bigger game of this type and it makes Hollow Knight look small! Good job they give you a dash immediately because you will be using it constantly. The map and fast travel system is also good.Lots of in game options and my PS4 controller worked flawlessly without any tinkering even though it doesn't show as formally supported.There's a pile of different weapons so you'll likely find something or several somethings to suit your play style and the difficulty is fairly forgiving at least early on so you'll have time to experiment and learn the ropes and again if you want to play more defensively you can use a few particular weapons to either get access to alternate movement styles or parry rather than using the dodge.For combat, you are really encouraged to dodge attacks rather than parry but there are a few weapons that can let you do that as well. The timing will take a lot of practice to do reliably but once you have it mastered it's quite satisfying to parry & then punish.Bosses can be tough and do big damage but thankfully they aren't artificially tanky or drawn out if you're level & gear appropriate which made for a pleasant change from boring, quarter million HP  10-minute long boss battles that seem to be currently in style (Looking at you, The Last Faith).You'll likely be sinking 25-30 hours into a play-through if you move very quickly and don't care about exploration much, but if you want to do see and do everything you're looking at more like 40 hours for all endings which is pretty amazing these days. You can also sequence break with clever jumping / movement / weapon movesets  so get a little bit of versatility for replays which is a plus. The bad:Honestly, the only negative thing I can say about the game is the difficulty might be a little on the lower side since it's combat-heavy rather than strategy, puzzles or dodging and you can sometimes just brute force fights that look like they were clearly designed to be finessed but that's a minor gripe. You are also not hand-held at all beyond the first area so if you are expecting to be told where to go... you're going to be disappointed because you are expected to just use the abilities you have and explore (or re-explore) to progress.This brings us to an actual flaw of this game: the story is utterly nonsensical and reads much more like a first draft rather than final version which is a real shame and does undermine the overall feel of an otherwise masterfully crafted game. The English voice actors try their best with a barely connected plot but it all sort of falls flat and by the time you make it to the end you probably won't really have a good feel for what you accomplished. This is a Taiwanese-based dev so entirely possible we've lost something in translation?If you liked Hollow Knight, Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night or Vigil: the Longest Night you'll really enjoy this game. It also looks and plays very similarly to Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth while being much, much longer.If it weren't for the story being a letdown I'd give this a 10/10 because it was an otherwise thoroughly enjoyable experience & really scratches that SoTN-style Igavania itch.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: First the good, then the bad, you know the drill.The game looks beautiful, from background to character, weapons, magic, enemies, NPCs, everything is quite nice to look at which helps to lessen the frustration of all the bullpoop that is thrown your way but more of that later. It has all the hallmarks a proper metroidvania should have. Vast areas, exploration of said vast areas, abilites that increase your mobility that open up different parts or entirely new areas, leveling system including a Talenttree with skills that have levels too!, a good variety of weapons and magic and gear that sometimes comes with effects like bleed and poison debuffs or dmg changes like "this weapon deals fire dmg", main and sidequests, interesting story and so on and so forth. If you think of something a metroidvania should have, you probably will find it in Afterimage in one shape or another.And that is also the crux about this game, it has everything, but it alway feels half-assed. Talenttree with skills that have sublevels ? Yes, but the increments are so small that you wouldn't notice them unless you put multiple points in the same talent at once. The Talenttree also includes attacks for your various weapons which sounds nice but mostly are attacks that should be a given. Things like being able to hit upwarts or downwards for example. The idea is nice, but the execution mostly leaves you asking yourself whether it was really necessary to do it this way. One would think it's a normal thing to be able to strike upwards while standing or downwards while midair, no ?This leads to the next problem, the combat. Aside from having difficulties to hit aerial enemies because of the aforementioned restrictions in striking directions, the enemy placement itself is in a lot of cases rather irritating. There are a lot of platforming sections in this game, as should be in a metroidvania, but more often than not you're greeted by a flying enemy right in the path of the last small platform to either hit your without being able to dodge or simply bump into you so that you fall all the way down just to do the whole segment again. I understand that games need a certain level of difficulty to be interesting but man, nobody wants that level of buttholery for every damn platforming section.Another problem with the fighting is the telegraphing and dodging. You can dash back and forth but every enemy has contactdmg followed by a healthy knockback. Combined with the lack of telegraphing attacks from basically every enemy and you'll find yourself in a weird overly precautious fighting style of barely getting a hit in and then dashing away twice to see what happens next. This als extends to the bossfights. Big monsters with even bigger hitboxes, no telegraphed attacks with no visible ways to dodge in very small rooms. You'll always just tank whatever attack comes next, heal through it and try to dmg race the foe to death. It's very unsatisfying. Pair that with the fact that after most of those fights you don't get any loot of any significance and you'll very quickly lose any interest fighting or beating any boss unless it's absolutely necessary.The variety of weaons is nice, several close and mid range combat weapons are available early on in the game. Some are slower, some are faster with the usual pros and cons and through the talenttree you'll also get ideas for possible pairings of weapons (you're allowed to equip 2 weapons and 1 spell) for further increase your dmg output. However, it does feel as if weaponupgrades are quite sparse so you'll end up feeling constantly weaker than everybody else so that it's always n uphill battle, some might like that but i would find an even playing field more enjoyable.The third point I want to mention in more detail is the size of the map. It is truly humongous, which on first glance is great. You can run around for hours simply exploring the areas and you'll have plenty to find and look it. However, you'll also get lost, often. You do have a map but other than Area names and a couple markers you can set yourself that thing only shows you rooms and that's about it. Telporters and resting points are shown as well but nothing else. No npcs, no cities, no doors, no elevators (although those are mostly selfexplained but massive "tubes on the map but still) no nothing. With maps as massive as in this game a couple markers (even if it was only names for subterritories in a given area) would greatly help.There's a bunch of other things noteworthy, some of them are:-you pick up money but have nothing truly interesting to spend it on-the mainquest you get in the beginning is so far out in the map that it's kind of hilarious that the devs bothered in the first place to even show you where to go :D-the movement abilities you can get are scattered so far from each other that you can easily look for multiple hours and not find anything which is quite demotivating-resting points are sometimes weirdly positioned so that corpse runs are quite tedious-there's sidequests but doing them feels more like happenstance than an actual part of the gameThe basic construct for a great game is there, it just needs more full-assing of all the half-assed stuff the devs alrdy put in. I hope for a lot of changes in the future because I'd like to finish the game sooner or later.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 Great metroidvania. It draws on well-known predecessors and adds own touches. The game is very well done although it didn't quite knock my socks of.The movement and attacks are reminiscent of SOTN where your overall fluidity develops as the game progresses, with your move set and player skill level. Visually, it's a lot like Ori with its own twists and Chinese-influenced art style. The Afterimage mechanic is like Hollowknight's charms, although your build also relies on your choice of equipment and talent.The map is huge. It's a long game.Afterimage is great, but it's not stellar. There are a few reasons why I didn't give the game a higher score. Some are design choices and others are lack of refinement.- No minimap. Maybe I'm just tired after work but I find myself constantly opening and closing the map.- Bosses feel repetitive. Compare to games like Ori, Hollowknight, or even Knight Witch, where bosses are quite distinct in terms of visual presentation and the flow of the fight. When bosses have a similar feel, it should be intentional, like one is a powered up version of another. - Foreground objects like pillars block the view. Then you get hit just because you can't see anything. When you take damage or die, it should be on you, the player. Fortunately, there are only a few isolated places where this happens.- The flat bodies on sloped surfaces mock the otherwise beautiful scenery.- They could do a lot more with the story/lore. I'm into that kind of thing and I think there's a lot of potential there.- The English voice acting is bad. The Chinese seemed best, although (and maybe because) I don't know the language, so I stuck with that.- The UX could use some refinement. I'd sometimes use something without intending to or pick something up and have no clue what or where it is.- It's not clear what to do with some items. What is it? What is it for? Can I sell it without regret?- I understand that swimming is difficult to implement but the underwater mechanics feel very low-effort.

_childDocuments_.review: Got a long way to go so going to withhold any grand claims until I'm done, but loving the game so far. Only prior Metroidvania experience is Hollow Knight, which I finished but didn't 100% or do the expansion content with the circus.If you are someone who liked Hollow Knight, you'll almost certainly like this. I'd describe it as Hollow Knight meets traditional RPG, given my background. The combat feels very similarly smooth and satisfying, but there are enough differences to make it still worth a shot even if you don't want "a second hollow knight". But let's be honest, enough people are stoked for silksong that a second hollow knight probably sounds pretty good.The key difference I'm noticing so far: swapping weapons in my loadout to balance access to range, speed, and the talent effects. Runes in Hollow Knight are fun, don't get me wrong, but they don't feel quite like this and they don't feel like it nearly as early.Edit after 20+ hours:Now that I've hit the 1 satisfied hour / $1 ratio that I usually hope for from steam games, I'm pretty confident that this game was worth the money even if the rest somehow turned out to be awful. Which I'm definitely not expecting at this point.There are some cons I'll list first:- Typos on items (like "mysitc", the example I've probably read most). Doesn't significantly detract from anything, but there are enough to be noticeable. Still, small blemish that shouldn't mean much, so just getting that out of the way first.- Some quests will show the dialogue like you're ready when you aren't - specifically thinking of the recipe fetch quests where they ask for a specific item, but then you might not have the other item from some other region you may not have even been to yet. It would be really cool if the dialogue option would acknowledge this at all, and even better if it gave some sort of guidance toward that item's source.- Lack of description for item-based abilities. In particular, subweapons suffer from this the most (the game also doesn't explicitly define subweapon anywhere I remember - it's the 3rd slot for a book / scroll / staff that uses mana). Some of them only do their effects with enemies or when you've taken damage, but aren't necessarily obvious from the name or by comparing them to other similar things. It's fun to test new skills and items imo, but I should still have something better to work with than just a name.- Some weapon skills feel clunkier than others. There's a weapon that gives a cool teleporting strike skill, which made me feel like a cool ninja when I first used it, but you don't control what direction you teleport from (seems random to me) and you don't get i-frames during it. It can sometimes even just kinda miss and run you right into the enemy. This doesn't ruin combat for me, as there are plenty of skills that feel just fine (and this one is still very fun to use regardless), but I can't speak to all the weapon skills I haven't used. YMMV.But all that said, I want to immediately praise the boss design. As frustrated as I got getting whomped by bosses as I binged this game hard over the past few days, it was incredibly rewarding to master all the patterns and get better at dodging things. There was only one attack where I think I needed a specific upgrade to dodge that I still haven't found yet and the rest just took some elbow grease. I was still able to beat that boss, just by surviving those attacks I couldn't dodge and getting much better at dodging the rest.I also want to praise the feeling of rewarding exploration. Aside from a few enemy types that seemed copied and pasted with different elements across regions, most feel unique and fresh when you see them for the first time. It's also pretty rewarding to be missing an ingredient for a recipe, then backtrack and stumble upon a totally new region where that ingredient happens to come from. Ultimately, I think it lacks just a bit of polish and is at a higher price than Hollow Knight so it'd be hard to recommend this over that game, but I see it as totally worth getting both.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a pretty strong recommend.I'll prefaece by saying many of the complaints I've seen are outright invalid, or at least no longer apply. Translations are now pretty good, some of the voices are still very voice actor ish rather than authentic, but it's still perfectly understandable and conveys the idea of the characters and emotion just fine.Some complained about multiple skills using the same inputs, that person never actually used them or different weapons though, as while yes you can have the same up and attack command trigger six different skills, that's based on the given equipped weapon, with only one of any input for each weapon you're using.Pros:- The world is big, very big, you'll keep finding new places hidden here or there or things to explore further as you play the game, well beyond the main storyline. So good amount of content, excellent two thumbs up here.- Graphics and Art, overall it it's a pretty nice looking game, some great art here and there in it, though it's not all perfect, most of the time it makes places feel interesting to be, and there's a good bit of variety in locations and the visual styles.- Gameplay, takes a bit of unlocking of skills and finding of interesting weapons and spellbooks or staffs or equipment to really come into it's own, but there's a pretty good flow of combat and gameplay here. At it's core, it's pretty good, and most of the time you'll find the basic act of moving or fighting to be enjoyable and interesting, and there's some nice depth to it as well.- Plenty of secrets and things to find.- Bosses are good and challenging, mostly at the end or for optional ones, start easy end hard. Some nice fights to pit yourself against here. Most of them are well designed, though a few have some issues her or there.- Variety in magics/skills. There's some pretty varied and interesting magics or stuff, that aren't just straight up attacks. It's nice that they have some creative things they can do, less nice is how most of these don't tell you what they do or how to use them, so you might not experiment and find the fun they can offer when they seem to do nothing upon your first test or such.- Great lore and interesting story, the lore is extensive and quite interesting, and also somewhat grounded, now while the world has it's own rules/physics, that are different from ours, they follow them. So things won't feel to mysterious or nebulous once you play for a few hours and understand the flow of things like how some say Souls games are super open to interpretation and odd in how things happen or work there.Most of the oddities here are from the god when they first made everything, minor spoilers ahead example. Instead of an actual sun the god made a bird that would fly through the sky carrying an orb of fire and dew to rain down life upon the land, when it lands at the edge of the land it will die, and return to the river of souls and be reborn back to do it again another day. This is interesting lore you find if you read and care about such stuff, tons on lots of weapons or some books, but then you find said bird, yes, it's actually a thing. But no one else by shear willpower or something or crap is able to do the same or turn into wacky stories or things like that, no, it's that type of interesting special, because the god made it that way and assigned it that role. So normal people have to work hard to do anything not normal for them, with serious and understandable methods and effort, yourself included. Overall more aproachable for most people than Souls style lore I'd say, but still plenty of depth and quite interesting, I personally liked it a lot. A very unique and interesting setting and story, not overly shoved into you're face, but with lots there if you want to look at it yourself.The cons:- The world is big, and a few areas lack pacing. The waterworks tunnels area among other are just too big and boring to move through, so while lots of places I love going to and exploring, some I also just don't like going back to much. The level of polish/refinement in every area is not always up to par.- The bosses, while mostly good, have some issues. One has sword slashes, the problem is the entire area the sword would slash instantly deals damage even before it reacches the end of the slash, forget the name anoying fire boss with teleporting and and phantom swords, he was probably the worst of all. A few others have some issues like their moves being orange... and the background being orange.. or other art decisions that make seeing or reading what's going on sometimes rather hard. Outside of that one boss, these are mostly nitpicks, but the point is they aren't all perfectly polished, there are some edges here and there, still overall pretty good.- The wall climbing. While I mostly like the moving and stuff in this game, the wall climbing is... really bad when it requires accuracy, it feels bad, and is hard to get detailed precise movement. When you touch a wall you just stick to it instantly sometimes, no full animation or stuff even needed before it counts you on the wall sometimes. Other times I press against one and it won't stick right. You slide down at a decent rate, and when you want to jump back up, you're jump height varies by how long you hold jump, even from the wall climb. Rapidly tapping makes you flit about on the wall as you jump and instantly stick back to the wall, no real animation or delay times here make it really non readable and feel like there's no logic or sense of what your characters doing. Hold to jump more and you'll go a bit higher... or might just latch onto the wall you're climbing up stopping you, jumping up walls even long unobstructed ones just doesn't feel good. But when climbing on walls to get past spikes and pit falls for some platforming, it's pretty bad feeling and can in some places get extremely frustrating. Possibly my biggest negative in the game... it still works ok enough in most places, even if it doesn't feel satisfying, but when they use it for challenges it just isn't that fun most of the time.- Bugs, there are more than a few. Like dashing, doesn't make you invicinible so you hit an attack you'll still take damage. But not always... sometimes you can phase right through enemies even without taking touch damage when dashing, but it's random and not common. Later on you unlock the ability to dash through stuff without harm/touching it. Now, on occasion even with this you will still take hits or get stuck on enemies. Sometimes enemies get stuck on ledges, kill themselves on thorns right after spawning, overall a few issues here and there. Most of them aren't that big of a deal, but a few of them do stand out a bit more, the dodge/dash ones being the most important for actual gameplay I'd say.Overal, I've had some solid enjoyment for many hours, 35 or so hours in now and while I probably explored 95% of the game on my first playthrough, not the most efficiently mind you, I haven't actually finished the final boss (on the proper ending, did get a bad ending when I chose to fight them early), so that's speeks for content and length. And I've liked much of this time, though some did feel a bit grindy trying to explore or figure things out, as some parts get a bit repetitive. You can fast travel, but only between major points, so there's a lot of going back and forth if you want to explore or do side things over the same places again and again. It's not as good as hollow knight, but much closer to that level than I expected it to ever be. So in the end, it's got problems, but still very good metroidvania, and two thumbs up with a good bit of feeling behind them.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm probably not the first one to tell you this but Afterimage is quite literally the single biggest metroidvania in existence and it's not even close. The map is utterly gigantic and feels like it never ends. You could consider this a bad thing but if you're a metroidvania addict like me then you will be hooked on this game from start to finish despite some of its flaws. You see, a big map is only worth so much if the gameplay isn't fun. Here afterimage knocks it out of the park with silky smooth controls and addictive combat. The game is also an absolute treat on the eyes and ears. About the only negatives i can mention are some inbalance in regards to difficulty, the story which is nigh impossible to keep track off as well as the occasional fps drops. Other than that the game is pretty much flawless and therefore a MUST play for any metroidvania fan. If you're not as big of a fan of the genre though this game can be very overwhelming due to the enormous map and lack of guidance.So about the map, as said it's absolutely gigantic but is it a good metroidvania map? I'm very happy to say that it absolutely is! There's TONS of side routes, one way doors, secrets, challenges and collectibles. If you love the exploration part of a metroidvania afterimage has you covered. While it starts moderately linear for the opening act, which is already several hours long and bigger than many metroidvania's, it really opens up around midgame. You have options a plenty where to go next, and while some areas may be too high level for you and thus woop your ass, you still have a few choices at any time! The zones are plentiful and varied and almost all of them are connected to at least two other zones. The whole map is brilliantly interconnected on a macro scale but even within a zone the level design is full of winding and twisting paths that loop back on themselves. I really cannot stress how good the level design is.Exploring all of it is, as usual with metroidvania's, not possible from the getgo. You'll need some movement upgrades that are scattered around the map. There's no real guidance towards these so you can easily miss them and explore new zones without it. Most zones don't make too much use of them as they are more for collectibles that are out of reach. Although there's ofcourse zones that are ability gated. Keeping track of what you need where is fully up to you as the game only marks NPC's and save points. You get the option of placing down up to 500 (!) markers on the map to keep collectibles that you couldn't reach yet tracked. I actually don't mind this system, as long as you're consistent and keep up with marking everything you won't get lost. A good memory will ofcourse also serve you well to remember exactly what you marked down but MV veterans are quite good at this generally.Other than the lack of guidance this game is pretty casual for the most part. The platforming isn't hard but still really fun. The controls are tight and responsive and the whole game feels snappy. This is also true for combat as you can animation cancel pretty much every attack so you'll never be locked into an animation. There's 6 different weapon classes each with their own skilltree which unlocks new attacks that you can seamlessly weave together. You can equip two different weapons at once to further open up your arsenal of combo's. This makes combat diverse, engaging and addicting which is needed though because there's lots of things to kill or avoid spread acros the map. You won't go two screens without something to fight which is also a big plus as it makes the big map feel lived in. Regular enemies are a blast to fight, with a mindblowing variety & amount of critters to fight. All of these have well telegraphed attacks and are both fair and fun to fight. The bosses in my opinion however not so much. They are fun and there's dozens of them but their attacks have very short windups so you will often get hit. The bosses are very understatted though and many of the earlier ones you can brute force. Later ones on the other hand get VERY hard and i had to lower my difficulty for the final ones. It's a shame that i couldn't finish the whole game on advanced difficulty because of this. Had the windups been a bit more clear and telegraphed the bosses could've been statted more fairly and been more fun as a result. Their designs and mechanics are super cool though, no two bosses feel alike and they are a visual spectacle.In fact the whole game is a visual spectacle, the visuals in this one are probably the closest you can get to the perfection that is Ori. It's not quite that perfect but it still blows everything else out of the water. The colours are vibrant, the areas are diverse and the setpieces memorable. In fact this game is so pretty that i took over 1000 screenshots... Woops! Anyways the aesthetic of this game is simple wonderful, there's not a single area that i didn't like and many of them are screensaver worthy! What's also beautiful is the game's orchestral score. There's so many standout tracks and great pieces. I'll gladly listen to this OST for years to come so i suggest you pick it up alongside the game. If you look at the amount of content and the quality on offer, the deluxe edition of this game may gave you more money's worth than most other MV's.So level design, combat, movement, visuals and sound are all great. Unfortunately the same can't be said for the story. Now don't get me wrong, the setting and the backstory is very cool. I picked up some of it and am busy watching a 2 & a half hour lore video as i write this review. There's so many things going on and much of it is intrigueing to say the least. But the way it's told, spread acros this HUGE map with crytpic writing makes it nigh impossible to fully understand what's going on. And the games' 10 different endings all lacked impact because of this. In fact the difficulty spikes, busywork for quests and backtracking as well as unrewarding story payoff made the ending a bit weaker than the rest of the game. It's still really good overal though, and fun enough to fully 100% complete the game. Just beware that this will take you a long time. I explored the whole map without any guide and once i had al areas (almost) fully explored i looked up what to do for the endings. Even with the help at the end i took 46 hours to fully do everything the game has to offer. (Well not really, there's an extra boss rush mode but i'm moving onto other games for now.) What's even more impressive is that during these 46 hours, i had 0 crashes or major bugs. In fact the only rough parts of the game are the slighly longer initial load time (only about one minute total so no biggy) and the occasional FPS drops. Oddly enough pausing my game often fixed this lag. It never lasted for more than a few seconds and barely hampered my enjoyment. The game as it stands now is impressively well made and a MUST play for any metroidvania fan that has some experience with the genre. For first timers maybe give Ori, islets or haiku the robot a try first and then come play this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Heres the thing. I love a metroidvania, and the art style is great. A+ even. The lush backrounds and 2.5d movement is on par with some of the best in this genre. However, in games of this style, two things make the game great. Combat and exploration. As many other reviews mention, a lack of mini-map seriously hinders this. Especially since quick travel to areas you've already explored requires items that as to the writing of this review I have not found to be renewable. Overall the platforming is relatively smooth, and abilities you unlock make it much more fluid as you go along. The problem becomes that the game gives little to no direction or guiding to explain what path is going to dead end in a one way gate (which I'm going to explain in a second) or is a viable progression path.Combat here really suffers. The enemy types are varied enough, but your options for combat aren't. Attacks all seem flavored towards melee, with a supporting magic that I found really underwhelming. The only true raged option is a whip which immediately becomes short range in the air, and on the ground is one of the slowest start up weapons you have. You do get staves and magic books, but the magic system is very very resource dependant, and 2-3 casts of your spells and you are tapped and either have to chug a potion to get back pretty abysmal damage or wait for it to regen over time which takes too long in a boss fight to be viable.Here is where the real meat of the problem with this game lies. The map is insanely big, like far bigger than other map sizes in its genre. The developers decided to use a combo of skill gates, which require items you find throughout the game to pass, and one way gates, which require you to find the other side of it to unlock it, most of the time as a short cut back to an area you've already visited. THERE ARE SO MANY ONE WAY GATES.  Far far too many, and with a lack of mini-map, you end up bouncing between the overmap, and back to the game to path find a way to the gate. Most of the time, the one way gate is a short cut unlocked by a skill gate check but because there is no mini map, the game wants you to go to the over map, mark a location with its sticker system, and then come back with the required skill. ALL OF THAT COULD HAVE BEEN SOLVED WITH AN AUTO-MARK SYSTEM. It would have taken very little time and a small amount of effort to auto mark an impassible gate with a little icon so you know where it is and what skill is needed to progress through it. One way gates get an arrow indicating the direction of the needed bypass. Skill gates get an icon matching that skill. Very simple QOL solution. On top of that, the map system at times is very cluttered and your personal location icon is huge. It actively blocks part of the screen ahead when you are at say a door or pathway so that you can;t see if what is in front of you leads to a path or a wall. They made the map zoom able meaning you can zoom in and out, and then didn;t adjust the player icon to minimize as well. Lastly, I will say some of the puzzle/timing platforming is really cheap. The whole water pulse platforming section where if your foot even brushes the water you warp back to some arbitrary point at the beginning of the puzzle is really lame. I haven't beaten the game, and as it stands right now I more than likely won't. There wasn't enough hook in the combat to get me excited for bosses and combat challenges, the map is so overwhelming that the exploration is tedious and time consuming. The story...well...the story isn't aimed at a western audience, and the dialog is written in such a way as to be very flat and lifeless. I'm sure its more compelling in its original language, and thats on the localization team who converted the written text to spoken word for the voice actors. Overall, I would say this is a labor of love game for die hard MV fans, but most people will be off put by a whole slew of issues that keep it firmly in the "had potential" category.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: - Gameplay feels very good (and is clearly inspired by Hollow Knight). Addicting especially for completionists, I couldn't help but spend all my free time on it til I finished it. The map was fun to explore and was much bigger than I expected.- The environments and the music are both beautiful.- Story and worldbuilding are full of really interesting concepts, but suffer from frankly terrible writing full of typos, rushed incoherence, unnatural phrasing, and lack of necessary explanations. Not sure how much of it is the translation.- Voice acting was hit or miss, I generally liked it but several of the voices were way too obnoxiously "anime" sounding. Overall it was better than not having it at all though.- Difficulty was easy, but you can play on a harder difficulty than I did if you want. I ended up semi-accidentally settling into an HP-regen-focused setup that made me practically invincible even to the final bosses, so it's hard for me to say how hard the bosses are if you play normally. Environmental hazards generally teleport you back a bit instead of hurting or killing you, which makes the platforming challenges much less tedious.Definitely worth playing if you like metroidvania-type games, 9/10 from me. With much better writing and overall story execution it'd be 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: (Note: Playtime may be inflated due to leaving the game idled on pause) Have you ever found yourself playing a metroidvania, reaching the end, and thinking "is that all?"Afterimage has a *massive* map, multiple interwoven story threads, multiple endings, beautiful and visually distinct scenery (such that you can tell the location of any screenshot at a glance), encounters, and animations, fully voice acted, and lovely music.Mechanically, it's the relatively standard blend of "stock" exploration abilities (double jump, break special walls, etc.), and is most distinguished by the ability to simultaneously use two primary weapons and one secondary. Difficulty is somewhat on the easy end, but the "Boss Rush" challenge mode presents everything you'd care to have in that regard.Overall, very worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Review is written with a 100% Save file and all achievements. Main Positives:-The combat skills were very fun to use although I only used a -Scythe for 90% of the run, but Scythe combat is just extremely good. I briefly dabbled in the greatsword and had whip as my side weapon for flying enemies in the early game but each of them were really nice. Most of the boss fights were really good although some felt pretty unfair at some point, however this could also be a product of me accidentally doing a bunch of late game bosses extremely early. Some of the end game bosses are especially interesting with their mechanics.-The art was fantastic and the actual world was very beautiful. The sprite work on the NPCs was cute.-There is a ton of build diveristy available. Although I mostly used the same equipment towards the end, on the way there I was encouraged to experiment a lot as the weapons don't just have stat buffs but special techniques individually as well. Accessories only compounded on this with some having extremely unique effects.-You can explore almost the entire map once you get the double jump. I always welcome metroidvanias that allow you go anywhere you want, although this does lead to a major con I will highlight later.Cons:-The story is a bit of a mess. There's 3 narratives going on concurrently and they're only really told in two methods. Notes you can find on the ground and walls of exposition in conversation. There were times in which I had absolutely no clue what was going on, especially in the beginning. The stories all seem to be half told as well, leaving out any clarifying details that would be be of assistance. There's maybe three real cutscenes in the middle of an extremely long game and would have loved to see more. Even after completing everything I'm still not really sure I understand what happened. -There's not enough guidance towards early/mid game key items. I spent my first 25 hours in the game completely lost in where to go, traipsing through areas where enemies would annihilate me in on hit constantly running into road blocks. The most essential ability for completing the game is the wall jump which is tucked away in a very hard to find dungeon that can be easily missed. I wish at the very least there was an indication for that ability specifically because it was way too easy to miss it entirely despite being essential to unlock all the other abilities. -The B side missions waste a lot of time. There's a side story where you run to the end of a level then get a bunch of exposition. This definitely could have been structured better.Overall. 7.5/12
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Very calm and relaxing exploration with beautiful OST and unique graphics then it becomes a bit more demanding in term of skills but is still very enjoyable.Story as bit of a mess sometimes especially if you did not follow the "classic path" but the endgame content weirdly serves as a good reminder of the storyline which is pretty cool.The main things is you need to know you will NEVER be helped during your progression. Its total exploration with very few other clue to where to go next except the "Go the that area which seems to be at other end of the map". For me its ok, I like the exploration more than the rest but for some it might be too much.I read somewhere it was a soulsvania but to be honest, I am awful souls player and a not super skilled player yet I managed to beat the all game (true ending included) so, I don't think its THAT hard but yeah you will have some challenges along the way :)Overall, very recommended for the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: The artwork and comabat are pretty cool but otherwise this game is all over the place.The story is impossible to piece together, the pieces you find make no sense and they aren't positioned very well so it's easy to miss bits or find them way out of order.The utility gating isn't used very effectively. It mostly felt like it was just locking weapons away (to be fair this was done pretty well, I really felt like I was excited to find weapons because they always made the game a little easier). My main issue with the utility gating is that it wasn't used to direct you through the areas the way Hollow Knight managed to do.The talent point system is so clunky and difficult to use, I never really felt like a given build was special. It was either usable or useless. Also the UI was so frustrating!Overall I really feel like they poured way too much time into the art and rushed the story and gameplay.
