_childDocuments_.review: I can see why this has such polarizing opinions, as theres some to like in this game, and a lot to hate, depending on the person. Lets start with the good. The game is long (if you prefer that), theres a lot of weapons and bosses. Theres mutiple weapons that play a little different with different attacks, and the game is beautiful, even though the running animation is choppy and weird looking. Theres a lot of enemy variety and different zones that mix things up, even if some enemies are just reskins. The platforming is also very good and tight. Then the bad, and oh boy is there a lot. The worst sin this game commits is that it doesn't value your time. It's by an Asian studio which makes sense as how repetitive and grindy it is. First off, as people have said, the game is way too big and maps are super huge but this isn't a good thing. This isnt a good thing as its just a lot of extra running around the same map fighting the same guys and it feels like filler. You will do all this exploring to get boring vendor trash, cooking mats, or fast travel pots. The maps also are constantly full of blocked ways, not by skill gated things but by these stupid walls you can only destroy from one side, more than any game I've ever played. This causes extra backtracking, which combined with the horrible map doesn't help. The map gives you no info on quest markets, NPC names, blocked ways, etc. You spend so much of the game wandering around lost, and using random reddit pages since theres no good walkthrough. The game lets you self pin things but why would you waste all your time doing what they should be doing. Then theres the brainless game decisions. You get no i-frames from dodging, but then can unlock it 90% into the  If its there just include it originally. Same with fast traveling. You can fast travel ONLY from large checkpoints, but you can also from small checkpoints but only with a consumable you have to waste money on for some reason. Why not just allow it from any checkpoint since they literally give you that ability, but this way you have to grind for money because "chinese gacha game". Then theres healing items. You can only carry a random number of all types of potions, and any other are stored away in storage for some reason. If you run out, it doesnt auto restock, you have to go to a save point and rest to restock, which makes no sense. Theres a self heal ability but even as you get more charges your health gets bigger and it barely restores like 20% even when buffed meaning you need to use a lot at once and its slow and during a boss fight is useless because you can't move and many can just attack you. This means you need to rely on pots but for some dumb reason you can only carry 2 or 5 or 3. Then theres the skill tree. I've never been less excited to level up. You literally only get things like "+4 sword attack" "+2% healing" or my favorite "+2% dash distance". Most of these are useless and provide such minimal effect its a slap in the face, and even with multiple you will not notice any difference. You'll only get stronger with new gear but you still have to level since so much of the game is level gated. Why you need to gain 70 levels speaks more to the asian MMO "numbers go up" obssession. You can carry a main and sub weapon, but since the main is going to be best and theres no ranged sub weapons, its kind of pointless since you'll mostly just use the main. Theres a few different attack skills but most are pointless so you'll just spam attack which gets old. Other problems: hitboxes are inconsistent and wonky at times, some bosses vary wildly in difficulty and will suddenly ramp up even though they aren't over leveled from you, doing tons of damage and having massive health. Also areas not having names until you discover it from a random area of text or NPC to talk to is another pointless annoyance. Also many bosses will have attacks that aren't signposted and with having so many different attacks, many of which are tracking or fill up the screen, combined with the bad healing system it becomes super frustrating at times and sometimes you'll just tank damage to beat a boss because dashing is useless without I-frames. The quest journal is so pointless, I had no many quests not finished when i finished the game but had no idea if I had an item for a quest, who I needed to talk to, or what was required. By the end of the game I got 1 ending and there were multiple other things I had not done but after already feeling this game had wasted so much of my time I just couldn't be bothered if it couldn't be asked to provide basic MV systems. It's another case of chinese/korean game being style over substance and quantity over quality. Asking you to waste time grinding, backtracking, and wandering around with baffling obtuse systems, some of which seem specifically designed to be annoying and counter intuitive to the genre. 5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a good but not great Metroidvania for fans of the genre who want something that's not leaning on the Souls formulas.  It's bright, it's colorful, it's generally cheery.  The soundtrack isn't amazing but has a few extreme high points.  The map is huge and full of secrets and items to find, and Afterimage isn't afraid to give you all of your favorite Metroidvania tools - double and triple jumps, wall clinging gloves, aquatic traversal, dashes, teleports between zones, and even a vertical super jump in the lategame.  Combat too follows a mostly straightforward paradigm, with six main weapon categories, a few special attacks for each, and the ability to use two weapons at a time.  There's also various forms of magic as a supplement, though they're not a primary tool by any means.  Afterimage is just a whole lot of game, and running around exploring and fighting is a treat.It's certainly not perfect, though.  It's maybe a bit too much game; you keep finding new areas and they're all expansive but the game wouldn't hurt to be about 20% or so smaller.  There's a lot of hidden items, but many are just generic potions or uninspired rewards that don't feel particularly good to hunt down.  Combat difficulty on the normal setting is mostly trivial with a few difficulty spikes in the late-game or if you're pushing into a harder zone than you're ready for.  There's an extensive talent tree but most of the nodes are minor stat bonuses that aren't especially interesting.  Progression is often extremely hands off and it can be difficult in the later game to determine where to go unless you're being obsessive about map coverage. Lastly and probably most problematic, the localization.  Afterimage really wants to be a story driven game, and the localization is not up to the task; it almost feels like a game that's in a licensed setting and assumes you already know the important points, because it doesn't really tell you what's going on but instead just namedrops a bunch of items, concepts and people and hopes you can keep up.  By the end you have a general sense of what's going on, but it doesn't actually coalesce into an interesting whole.  There's also a lot of uncertainty about the items and skills you're unlocking; it's sometimes unclear what's important, what's not, and what can be safely ignored or disposed of.If you're a fan of the genre, Afterimage is worth a look, but know going into it that the pacing and localization isn't great and set your expectations accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing 16 hours of the metroidvania game Afterimage the last couple of days, but now have to take a break for work.Despite putting all that time in, I seem to be nowhere close to the end of the game. I don't think any game since Hollow Knight has delivered a metroidvania map of this size. That could have been a wasted effort if exploration and traversal were badly thought out, but the world if full of fun secrets and platforming challenges. Like Hollow Knight, the game makes you work hard for traversal ability unlocks, making you appreciate them even more when you have fought through huge difficult map sections that are now trivial to traverse.The story and setting are not as good as in the best games in the genre like Hollow Knight or Ori, but pretty decent. The graphics for enemies and levels are really varied, so there is at least an obvious progression in those areas.The game is more open ended than most other metroidvania games, which works really well with its massive size. The character development subsystems are quite intricate for the genre as well. It is very possible, quite tense and a lot of fun to infiltrate high level areas before most people were meant to.The combat is good. The early game is too easy, but later bosses and enemies can be challenging. No phasing/dashing through enemies or bosses will probably be divisive, and means that you will be jumping a lot in combat situations.The game works great on Steam deck on high graphics settings, but the detailed graphics kind of call for playing the game on a larger display. I have mostly been playing on my OLED ultrawide. The game natively supports ultrawide resolutions.I see a lot of negative reviews on the Steam store that I do not really understand. The game is a massive, great looking, fun to play metoidvania game that most people who enjoy the genre would enjoy to play.

_childDocuments_.review: After 51 hours of playtime and getting all 10 endings I can definitely say this is one of my new favorite games of all time. I'm seriously blown away by it.  When I first got it, I was expecting a typical 10-15 hour long metroidvania. But this game straight up pulled a Hollow Knight on me and blew me away with a 51 hour long adventure.Now, it is true what people say about the story. It is very hard to follow and, while I think I managed to understand it a bit by the end, I still think the localization team could've done a better job at translating some things. I noticed a lot of bad sentence structure that made things hard to read, and the game throws a lot of names and concepts at you that aren't explained until much later in the game, and by that time you've either forgotten, or you probably missed the explanation entirely. I know these modern "soulslike" metroidvanias are trying to do the Dark Souls thing (Hollow Knight did it too), but this one does kinda miss the mark.But as for everything else, it's basically perfect. The combat and exploration, visuals, music, voice acting, character designs... they're all 10/10. Some people have criticized the platforming, but I personally thought it was fine. Sure it's a bit basic like Ender Lillies, but there was nothing bad about it, and there's plenty of platforming puzzles and challenge sections hidden throughout the world.Another aspect people have criticized is the teleportation mechanic. While I understand why people don't like this, I personally felt like this added some strategy to my exploration, that I normally don't do. Having a limited resource for teleportation makes it feel like a big deal, and definitely makes you think about when it's good to use it and when it's not.Another thing I really enjoyed early on was how the map didn't automatically unlock as you explored, you actually had to rest at a confluence in order for the map to unlock the areas you had explored. I really liked  this because it added a lot more strategy to exploration. It made the world feel more intimidating, and made the confluences even more rewarding when I found them. Sadly, this mechanic was patched early on, and now the map just unlocks as you explore like normal. I don't know why they decided to change this, but I really wish they hadn't, it made this game feel more unique compared to the usual metroidvania standard.Overall, this game is a 10/10 for me. Despite the issues with the storytelling, I still greatly enjoyed my experience. This personally has been the biggest gaming surprise in a long time. In a time when the biggest AAA games almost all feel like disappointments(*cough* Jedi Survivor *cough*), it feels so good when an indie game like this can still make me feel excited for gaming.10/10 Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has mixed reviews, but it's in my library, so I decided to take a crack at it. My main guess why it has mixed reviews. It has enormous map and doesn't tell you where to go. Your every move is ball busted by some skill or feature and you are not directed where to go. Eventually I got the hang of exploring and figured out where to go next. But the game is massive. Which is a good thing, however, with limited ability to fast travel it makes exploration more of a chore than it needs to be. Fast travel becomes easier later on, as you have plenty of resources to buy an unlimited amount of an item that lets you travel.The controls are tight and feel good. The combat is interesting. Something feels a little off, but it's fine. Most enemies are easy to kill, and bosses can mostly be steamrolled so long as you have a good weapon and know what weapon arts work with your play style. You can mostly avoid mechanics, which is a shame.The graphics are quite nice. Character models look good. The world building is good, lots of layers and moving parts in the backgrounds. The game can be quite pretty at times. There are a lot of shiny elements.The game has a ton of content. Map is huge, lots of quests, tons of bosses, and a short campaign (NG+) when you are done that leads you towards the true ending. I did all 10 endings. I definitely got my money's worth out of this game.Some issues:1. Items disappear fairly quickly. I fell down and had to go 10 seconds away to get up a ledge and come back, came back, items were gone.2. It's weird to play a game like this without mantle.3. Talent tree could be done way better. It's cumbersome to view and figure out which way to go. It was also not clear which upgrades affected katanas.4. This game busts your balls with fast travel. You can only travel between the major save points. And you have to get a consumable to travel back from anywhere else. I really don't care for it when games do this. Especially metroidvanias. Especially one this big.5. It's really weird to be unable to dash through enemies. Makes boss fights strange.6. It's really complicated to know where to go next. Some map makers for major places to go for upgrades would be super helpful. I mean, the map is huge. It's so challenging to know where to go next, and with the ball busting fast travel it's even more complicated. The game sorta tries to lead you in the right direction, but there are so many ways to go at every turn that it's hard to know which is the right one.7. Quest info is not super helpful as to what to do next. You primarily have to look for map markers, but that doesn't always work, and one time the NPCs marker wasn't there, even though I was able to progress his quest. One quest was bugged and would not complete, though I did do all steps.Overall, this game is worth playing. I think I left it on overnight at one point, but if I had to guess, I got 50+ hours out of this game at 65% achievements with all 10 endings. At the price tag, it's fair for what you get. But if it's on sale, it's worth picking up if you are looking for a decent metroidvania.

I am not big on lore, so the lack of cohesiveness in the story that others mention means absolutely nothing to me.  The combat is great.  The bosses were fun and rewarding without being too painful. _childDocuments_.review: TL,DR: Probably the best metroidvania following Hollow Knight, in ambition and thought but not as tight of a package.Pros:-Long game. A blind run if you are experienced in the genre will take around 20 hours. Lots of exploration awaits.-Decent combat. It's an evolution of the SOTN formula, at first is quite dry but you progress and unlock abilities for the 5 main weapon types and learn wich combination of primary and secondar you feel comfortable with. Weapons equipped also will make certain abilities to change, so maybe a lower damage weapon is what you prefer because you like the ability. The control is quick and responsive.-No magic or range cheese. Magic is good for exploring but won't carry a boss.-The most non linear metroidvania. You will get lost and probably end the game without exploring entire zones. Maybe a zone level will make you look for another route, but maybe you think you can soldier the higher level zone, then you go through higher level zones you are not supposed to do at that point and reach the easier ones later. It's probably the thing I enjoyed the most, the vast majority of lower brow metroidvanias are too linear, this one isn't at all. I'm still trying to figure how to reach certain places and I'm reaching the 30 hour mark.-It's beautiful. Everything is very charming, the art is superb, maps and backgrounds are super detailed and immersive, has a ton of different enemies and the recycled ones have different twists on what they do. Music is not as good as the art, is quite atmospheric but is not an epic style of OST like Hollow Knight that you will automatically buy it apart because it's so good.-Difficulty scales very well. Early to mid game is a walk in the park, later is quite hard. Still, the game gives you certain items with mechanics that make things easier later on, but you can forget those and go full Gamer Mode if that's how you roll. And it has a hard difficulty.Cons:-It's a VERY long game. If you don't want to sink hours and hours, there are smaller metroidvanias. Also sometimes it can feel very samey in the process of exploration because you are doing this for way too long compared to other games. It's a similar situation with the Switch Zeldas, if you know what I mean. The core is really good, but repetition in a game this long makes it duller as time passes.-Classic Castlevania combat. No hit bounce or weapon clash mechanics, responsive control but not as good as Hollow Knight. If you prefer parry style games you won't like this one.-Magic. It's situational. You can try to do a magic build but it's more for times you can't get in range or as a buff but you can't cheese bosses with it if that's how you roll. I think it's the best approach because long range cheese can ruin games like this, but also there aren't exciting spells.-Camera is too far away. I got used to it but I would prefer it closer. I think the game is harder because of that, you can get lost in the screen or get hit from things you normally wouldn't.???:-Quests are ok. They give enough flavour to the game, there are quite a number of side characters. Fortunately it's not levels of Timespinners of walltext.-Ifree. It's always there behind you. At first I think it was a nuisance, but I forgot he was there after a while. He does the I'm a big boy but in a small bean body schtick. He's cute.-Magic cats. There are cats, they are magical, they look like the sad cat from the video that meows very sadly. It's not Zote but, you know you will slay gods for them. But you can't pet them because they are afraid of humans for being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that attacked them. Damn humans.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a generally good and extremely ambitious game.  I had fun with it, but I wanted to like it more than I actually did.My main impression of it is of a game so huge and sprawling that it, maybe more than any other one I've ever played, deserves the title of "an open-world Metroidvania".  You're cut loose on an absolutely ginormous map with very little context (at least in the bewildering English translation), no guidance, no waypoints, no nothing, just a massive and gorgeous world to explore.  Sure, it uses all the traditional skills to gate your progress -- although from the beginning you can sequence-break fairly effectively once you realize that there are a few weapons which allow you to hover for a second with a midair attack -- but it was very rare that I even kept track of what quests I had active; just uncovering the map was the game in itself.  And so you wander around for 20-40 hours until you beat one of the end bosses for one of the eight or so endings.  Then there's New Game+, which is really just an alternate game mode where you play through about an hour of story with a secondary character to get slightly more context for the game's plot, which unlocks a few more endings (and the true one).The open world nature of the game works both for it -- it keeps unfolding LONG after you think it has run out of steam -- and against it, because it's often frustratingly implemented.  The total lack of hand-holding often means you get stuck just because the map is so huge it's not always clear where the logical progression path is.  It's very easy to wander into areas with overleveled enemies (it does mark them as dangerous, but doesn't suggest where to go instead) or to overlook that turn you didn't take three areas ago which is actually the single way into the areas you should now be exploring.  The map allows you to mark it up, but offers NO INDICATION that that's the case, meaning by the time I read a guide telling me to make liberal use of the map I'd already given up on labeling a lot of the secrets I knew I would need to come back to, and forgotten about them because there's just so much content here.  And then there are a lot of details which are clumsy in the interpretation.  For instance, when you're in end-game trying to 100% everything, it turns out that Resting Town and Resting Path share a zone despite looking like two different locations, so you can't 100% one zone without also clearing the other.  Most of the collection achievements are locked behind obscure bosses or areas which literally don't even show up on the map.  This is a game which *requires* a guide if you are at all a completionist, or for most people, just to get past the chokepoints that get sprung on you without warning.More frustratingly, there's absolutely no sense of balance.  Magic is useless: your MP bar recharges like 1% at a time and spells take like 33% of your bar, for attacks that can't be launched in midair, take forever to cast, and do approximately the same damage as your weapon.  Elements are basically an afterthought; if there's a rock-paper-scissors aspect to them, it's never explained and doesn't seem significant.  Critical hits are rare and do something like +25% damage by default.  Equipment and skill bonuses are so marginal that there's no effective strategy aside from "rush late-game equipment as quickly as you can and pick the biggest number on the weapon class you like the most".  (Seriously, you can spend multiple talent points on a buff that gives you +0.5% damage to special weapon skills, and that's *average* for an upgrade.)  So basically there's an entire universe of options presented to you, none of which are as effective as stabbing enemies to death.  Weapon skill unlocks, at least, are solid boosts; for the later ones you have to find their skill scrolls via exploration, which is nice incentive to poke into the map's corners.These sorts of flaws -- there are others, too -- would be the kiss of death in a lesser game.  Here, though, the fundamental gameplay loop at least is solid (though if you're using a controller you may be aggravated by the game's inconsistent detection of pressing down on the analog stick, which is often significant due to ducking, sliding, and ledge-dropping being frequent moves).  So, ultimately, it's still worthwhile to explore a huge, gorgeous, smoothly animated world, and it sucks you in enough to startle you with just how long you've been playing it, how much you've gotten accomplished and how few drops those are in a very big bucket.  Recommended for players looking to sink their teeth into a longer, larger Metroidvania and willing to put up with its idiosyncracies.

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a hidden gem of a Metroidvania type of game. I have no idea how this game is just flying underneath people's radar, but for Ifree's sake, this game is fun. I have spent more time just chilling in a place, admiring the background and music that goes along with it. The soundtrack is gorgeous, sceneary is stunning, combat is not too hard (even with Advanced mode), puzzles and platforming were fun and fair. Although the story is rather simple, it can be a tad bit confusing to follow for all things considered.  (Most of the answers are revealed towards the end of the playthrough and there is a handy lore video to watch if you are interested!) Is it worth the full price? Considering this was done by only a handful of folks from Shang-Hai and complete with proper localized voice acting and very, very minor trnaslation/text mistakes, I say its worth it. But if you can get it on a sale of any kind, then this makes the game even more worthwhile. 8/10 for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give this a thumbs up.  It's a very solid Metroidvania with a huge map and plenty of things to find and even multiple endings.  That said do listen to some criticisms I have on it  before you decide if you'd want to buy this full price or wait for a steam sale.The story of this game is kinda all over the place IMHO, so I'd be wary if you're hoping for a cohesive story to drive you forward in the game.Difficulty is very spikey in a number of points and definitely at the end-game point which can be frustrating.There are souls-like elements, and honestly I don't think they needed them.  It's real aggrivating to feel locked into a boss fight because you were near a level and now you have to keep beating your head on a wall because your XP drops by the boss.  (but you can always grab your XP then enter the menu and go back to the title so that you have your XP back and aren't in the boss room anymore)
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game about the hubris of human greed and the desire to be led/loved by a higher power. Pretty solid Metroidvania from start to finish but some of it's story may or may not get lost in translation and the game world might be a bit TOO big for some. Regardless of these small flaws I had a really good time with it. The music is lovely, the world is vibrant and full of lore to discover, combat is difficult but rewarding. 25$ is more than reasonable for a game with this much love and passion put into it.

My biggest surprise was thinking I was maybe more than a quarter of the way done with this game and then the world got 3X bigger. At about 14 hours in I only have two achievements... out of 46. Crazy.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily my favorite metroidvania (second favorite if you count Metroid Prime, I guess). Extremely beautiful graphics with cohesive art direction for every area, world that actually feels massive, great movement, a lot of bosses; has some really good QoL stuff, including an end-game feature to help with 100% item completion. Story takes effort to piece together, but IMO is pretty enjoyable overall, even if its delivery could be a bit better at times.Originally got it on launch for Switch, 100%ed there, then got the Steam version for a better look at graphics/smoother experience and 100%ed here again, enjoying every last moment of it - and higher resolution indeed takes graphics to a whole new level. The only problem that stands out is subpar localization, although it's not particularly terrible either and is generally limited to what should have been caught by proofreading (typos, missing punctuation, slightly broken English, etc.).
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Top quality MV. Gives me the vibes of Hollow Knight, Ori, SoTN, and a few others. You can feel and see the inspiration from many other MVs and I love it. This game is a metroidvania for metroidvania fans. I started it and didn't want to stop playing it. The biomes are excellent and varied. Music is so good I got the deluxe edition and have the music on my phone. NPCs have unique looks, personality, and dialogue. Voice acting in this game is very well done. Story in this game is philisophically deep, though the subjects have been explored many times. Combat can take some getting used to, but is smooth and tight. This MV is not trying too many new things and that is okay. Like I said it is a metroidvania for metroidvania fans (to quote MV Guru). Even if you're new to the MV genre, I would still grab this. It is a very well done game and worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a vast and engaging game, great game-play and atmosphere, variety of enemies and kinda interesting lore. The map is huge and has many interesting locations-territories. After 20 hours in and I think I am still in the middle. Although the plot most of the times gives you no hint at all as to how to progress to the map. You are completely at the mercy of exploring and you must search every corner in order to find keys/abilities/artifacts that will eventually help you explore more and maybe find the way. Also it lacks mechanics explanation. Beside the abovementioned setbacks I would totally recommend the game!

The stunning graphics and intricate gameplay kept me on the edge of my seat throughout the entire experience. I was constantly challenged by the puzzles and captivated by the storyline. The game mechanics were smooth and intuitive, making it easy to navigate through the virtual world. Overall, I highly recommend Afterimage to any gamer looking for a thrilling and visually stunning adventure. It truly exceeded all of my expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Whoooo..okay then. I don't know if I've written any reviews for games before, but here goes.  Afterimage stumbled into my heart pretty quickly after I first booted it up, and I've been loving it ever since.  It's a gorgeous game with very engaging gameplay and a story that's...confusing, so far.  Let me get my minor nitpicks out of the way and then I'll gush a bit about the game.  SPOILERS BELOW!!!!!1. Balancing seems to be a bit of an issue in my opinion.  I mean this only in that some of the weapons (mainly subweapons) seem to be on the weaker side, not that the monsters are too strong or anything like that.  I think the enemy balancing is pretty good overall, and I found that if I was getting demolished by non-boss enemies I was probably in the wrong place.  My issue here is with the fact that there are a *ton* of accessories and armor sets that are focused around buffing subweapons and mana regen, and yet if you equip all of them, most magic still feels weak in comparison to the main weapons of the game.  Damage is kind of on the low side, but honestly my biggest gripe about it is that you can generally only use magic when you're on the ground, and a few of the more interesting spells even have noticeable difficulty even hitting enemies that are airborne even when you are grounded.  See the 'Wand of Owl' for an excellent example of this-the spell is really cool and unique, but it's tracking issues and the fact that it simply doesn't cast sometimes make it much less usable than it could be. In addition to this, even in the endgame it feels as if you can't really get your mana regenerating fast enough to use spells very frequently at all-and as a result you've kind of gimped yourself by accessorizing mainly for subweapon attack.  (this is almost entirely a complaint in relation to boss fights-operating in the overworld with magic is generally fine given the amount of mana regen on kill, etc that is available.) I know this seems like a lot, but compared to the rest of the game this is a pretty minor point. 2. The english localization is a little rough, and gets rougher the later into the game you get.  There are more than a few noticeable misspellings/grammar issues and it's particularly egregious in New Game +. At best, the team working on this was rushed-and at worst the translation was done by an AI in the later stages of the game.  This should be an easy fix though! 3. The sections in which you are riding a stingray looks bafflingly awful, especially in comparison to how stunning the art of the rest of the game looks.  I can only imagine this section was rushed in order to get the game out as well.  Hard to say what to do here but honestly I'd prefer a list of places I could go over having this segment at all, similarly to the boatman at the end of the Field of Pyro. 4. The audio balancing for the music seems to be a bit wonky-I have to turn it down further than the other sliders in order to make the character voices audible in some situations.  Specifically in the opening cutscene, the music drowns out the voiceover pretty severely. Okay!! It's much harder to talk about the positives of something over talking about the negatives honestly, because like...10/10 no notes for the rest of the game??? The art is beautiful, as is obvious-almost everything in this game is just gorgeous.  The environments, the creatures, the bosses, the characters, etc etc. I love the artstyle and really just everything about this game visually.  The sound design is pretty darn good and while I'm not blown away by the music, it's quite good in some places and serves its purpose in others.  I would...perhaps give the english voice acting a pass.  It's pretty much a cavalcade of very similar iffy anime dub voice actors and I found Ifree's VA in particular to be a bit annoying.  Changed the audio type to Japanese very early in the game and I've never looked back. I think where this game really, really shines is in the combat, the enemy variety, and the area design.  All of the areas are beautiful, and none of them are the same-the game manages to make 3 *very* different fire levels, all with distinct enemies and no overlap.  The enemy variations are, I think, never just reskins (with the exception of one area in the very late game), and all have their own unique movesets, which I think is amazing. The amount of work and love put into the enemy designs is obvious, and just really fleshes the game world out incredibly well. The combat is fun, fluid, and dynamic, and constantly changes as you slowly upgrade your character.  i love the variety in the weapons, the fact that you can use two of them completely together, and the way the talent trees work.  I will say I'd love to have more options on the talent tree, primarily because it looks as though if I grind myself up to lvl 99 I'll be able to fill out the *entire* talent tree.  There is definitely a benefit to this, being able to be extremely versatile in the endgame, but also I feel like it takes away from the ability to truly ~specialize~ in anything in particular.  The weapons themselves are also super cool! There are so many interesting ones with fascinating new moves, unique benefits and drawbacks, and a bunch of options for builds centering around different styles of playing.  I really enjoy that you can make yourself into a glass cannon, essentially, a crit machine that melts bosses but instantly dies if you're hit by a stray gust of wind.  I like that there's an option to buff up your normal attack speed insanely high (though I'm still trying to figure out how to make that one really sing) and I enjoy that you can build yourself as a tanky bruiser who can take a bunch of hits and dish them right back out.  I think the bosses are all extremely varied and well designed-no two feel alike and I really appreciate that.  All of their fights were engaging, and entertaining, and even though at one point I felt that I hit a roadblock with a boss that spent hours wiping the floor with me, I finally beat her and rejoiced only to find that I had missed an entire area-no two areas, no three areas, that probably would have prepared me to fight her better.  This game is very open and does, in fact, allow you to make dumb choices if you really want to.The story is confusing, and full of anime tropes, but I've come to enjoy it quite a bit-especially the multiple endings and the fact that the characters even reference that multiple endings have occurred in the past.  I'll be brief about this as I'm still one ending away from having fully run the gamut but I really like the way that new Game + was implemented into the game.  I think it was interesting-though not particularly deep-but it definitely gave a lot of perspective into the story of the game.  I feel like everything is kind of drip fed to you in a souls-like way and I think that's pretty neat.    In any case, I'm sure I'll come up with more thoughts on the game later, but for now I suggest that if you like metroidvanias, buy this game! It's absolutely worth it and I have had a blast-I plan to 100% it and then maybe even play it a second time.  if I were to give it a rating I'd say it's a 9/10 (9.5 for me because I ignore some of its flaws, 8.5 for someone who is being a bit harsher and we take the average of the two). I hope you enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game, but I just can't. The art style is wonderful, and some of the enemies are absolutely adorable to the point where you feel bad beating them up, but the game has some very big flaws that make it hard to keep playing through the game. The issues I struggled with the most were: 1) the absurd amount of backtracking required (coupled with a horrible collectable map), 2) the weapon skill system, 3) the leveling system that feels extremely lackluster, and 4) the limited fast travel system in such a massive map.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: If you are up for an adventure, then this is the game for you. Not too difficult for the most part except for a couple of end game / relevant bosses. The map is terribly cumbersome to navigate especially late game when you want to go to X but not necessarily via the confluence if you happen to be far away from one and it might have been better to have each area on a single page so one could scroll through one by one (think Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin).The graphics are quite beautiful although they can sometimes hide chests, enemies, etc a little too well so you do really need to open your eyes. There are some inconsistencies with character avatars like the end of Ethan's side quest when he is clearly out of his wheelchair but his avatar is depicted as still being in his wheelchair.I have found a couple of instances where you can soft lock and be forced to either use a resting potion or quit out of the game in order to get out (I was two thirds through the boss fight with Agus and he just teleported out of the arena and never came back).Weapon system is quite interesting and caters to a variety of play styles depending on what works for you. Finally, I feel like some of the achievements are a little too grindy. Get all the things and reach max level seems a bit overkill, especially when you have to guess if missing items are a creature drop or a chest that could be anywhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: WowI seriously got goosebumps immediately on play, the presentation and music is something else. the opening montage is cryptic by design, but it's clear enough in broad strokes.So far:I love the voice over! It adds so much life to the story and is done pretty competently so farThe mood is somber but not dark (kind of like death's gambit)The environment is great, nice verticality, already many metroidvania-style inaccessible paths which surely will be revisitedThey pile on unknown terms in the story / dialogue. I try to keep an open mind and assume it will all be explained in timeThe music is like Death's Gambit but more emotive, and the somber pianos remind me of hollow knightThe overall movement is quick but weighty. I love that we get the dash right awayThe battle feels great, the impact of each slash is felt and our main slash staggers some enemies, which is always niceThe menu reminds me of aeterna noctisIt feels stat based (the numbers on each slash connect) but we'll see how it progressesThis game looks like it is made by a larger team. I love that it automatically starts at very low quality setting on my GPU-less laptop, but I switched to medium and it works fine. On very low, foreground and background elements are blurred, but mid-ground (the plane where the gameplay is) is crisp. On Medium all planes are clear.Overall very good first impression. Currently finishing Lone Fungus (a different but also excellent metroidvania), and will move on to this after
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem. Not only is the game aesthetically pleasing in both visuals and musical score, it's quite possibly THE largest Metroidvania I've ever seen. 33 hours in, I'm STILL discovering new areas.EDITED: 50-ish hours in and I'm almost done with the main story (although I gather there is more work to get the True Ending). It does begin to drag towards the end, not least because some of the bosses have insanely spongey health pools. Still one of the better MV's I've played, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't for me...but its also not a terrible game.  I'll focus on the negatives to explain why...there are positives but just check out other reviewers for that part.I'm overwhelmed by the choices in the map here.  There's no meaningful direction and I have like 5 zones I can backtrack through with tons of paths that I haven't reached a point of a dead end yet.  I can see a lot of people loving this...I haven't played a metroidvania quite like it in decades and its not my preferred way.  This game is too open. To add to this problem is another big one...the weapon upgrades and means of executing them.  I started getting things like tap forward - forward attack but this can only be done on the thumb stick.  These kinds of controls are awkward and inconsistent to pull off in the heat of combat.  It takes one of the more fun parts of this upgrade tree and sucks the fun out of it.  I would try something as simple as a backdash slash with a sword which sounds super helpful on paper and struggled to reliable pull off the move as you have it pictured in your mind. The boss fights were not satisfying to me.  I think this game might struggle with telegraphing attacks nicely.  I didn't get a sense of back and fourth and pattern memorization.  At this point in the game it was largely just going with the flow and overcoming the boss.  None of the 4 or so bosses I faced felt memorable or fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is at least 90% New York style cheesecake, at least that much, yum, but then there's the remaining whatever percent which is spoiled milk, after shovelling it for a few hours I had to put down the spoon.The massive maps are watered down by the samey level design, combat's fine but seems unbalanced on standard difficulty - i quickly got to the point where normal enemies and bosses posed no danger whatsoever. The biggest no-no is the way the game frequently blocks your progress with obstacles which must be destroyed from the other side, with no hint of how to get there, this is something it does constantly and becomes old very quickly.A great shame, but I can't and won't funnel time into games with deeply flawed mechanics and this is one of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing metroidvania game, has elements of Hollow Knight but still manages to break in it's own identity as Afterimage. Overall a solid 8 out of 10 rating.TL:DR:Combat is great because of weapon type combinations and all the weapon combos you can do,Story is disjointed but will make sense eventually.Exploration you will get lost but at least have fun doing it.Combat is great but at the same time its simple to use; when gotten used to it, weapon combos and different type of weapon combinations makes the game feel fresh and unique; this is how it Afterimage makes itself different from others of it's genre.Story is disjointed due to the fact there is only a rough guideline to what you need to do, you will feel lost and sometimes part of the story sequence will be messed up because you went to a different place first and triggered a key point of the story while another part will reference something you don't even know about. Just continue playing and eventually the story will make sense.Exploration is fun as well but you will 100% get lost and will be frustrated by certain exploration mechanics that block you from accessing certain chests or getting to new parts of an area. But at the endgame where you have unlocked all the exploration mechanics, it is a truly wonderful experience to just run through the game and collecting all the missed/blocked chests.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Solid enough Metroidvania that will scratch an itch. As someone that has played basically every game in this genre and scours the internet for up and coming new games with at least 50 yet to be released on my wishlist, I can say that I personally didn't find this one very interesting. I will not give it a thumbs down though because it isn't bad, I just didn't find it very good either. Exploration is there, plenty of new weapons that make enemies take one less hit, but that's just it... I found myself running up to enemies and slashing 3-8 times (which often breaks their attack animation) and moving on. With as many enemies blocking my path forward as there are, I found it tedious and just wanting to move around them rather than through them. I would prefer to see enemies that are more difficult to target that take a hit or two, with the occasional enemy that takes multiple hits and an ability to parry or dash through. In this game I basically run up and hit multiple times or run up and hit once or twice, back dash, and run up and hit once or twice more. Kinda basic and slows down the pace of such a large game.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Dont listen to the haters of this game. This game is a masterfully crafted true Metroidvania with beatiful art and sounddesign with breathtaking graphics. Dont be a sheep and judge the game for yourself. 10/10 Thanks to the devs. of this game \m/ Im thrilled whats in stock in the hole game. Im "just" a few hours in.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: This game shared a lot of similarities with hollow knight and extends its gameplay to a whole new level. Aside from dash, jump, climbing, and double jump, you have triple jump, pogo, spell, weapon switching, and an ENTIRE SKILL TREE. Henceforth, the combat experience can range from basic hit-dodge strategy to utilize skillset to evade enemy and boss fight.Map design of this game is a double-edge sword. If your first game is a "short" metrovania game like hollow knight, the map of this game is unexpectedly and spectacularly huge. Yet, there's nothing repetitive between each map. Adding to this, this game does require you to do a lot of backtracking to advance the story. After acquiring each skill, you can and sometimes need to go back to old area to find a way to new content, which may reward you with new skills that advance your story experience. Boss fight in this game is very clean. It has a lot of bosses with similarity to hollow knight and a lot of unique bosses. And this game balance boss's difficulties pretty well. Bosses are hard but it boils down to your reaction and experience between each time that the boss defeated you. Each boss is unique in their own playstyle and requires players to carefully learn their fighting style while enjoying the boss fights.All in all, I highly recommended this game in the time where we all wait for silksong :D

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous metroidvania with smooth gameplay, oodles of player freedom, and an interesting tale told in a non-linear way.First and foremost, the game has very few exposition dumps and instead spreads out much of its story and lore through "diary" snippets scattered throughout the world and item descriptions. A chunk of the story explanation is also behind some chapters where you play as a different MC during the same timeline as the main game (which the game calls NG+ since you need to complete the main game's endings first to unlock them). That latter aspect in particular really reminded me of NieR for anyone that has played those games.Due to the minimal enforcement the game provides about where to go or what order to do things, it leaves it up to the player to piece together the details and order of events. Someone created an over two hour youtube video covering the game's lore and story before and during the game's timeline in chronological order to give a sense of how much info there is. I would say I picked up a good 85%+ of everything that happened from my own playthrough by the end, but there were definitely a few reveals and connections that I overlooked because of how indirect the game is about presenting its story at times.All in all, I loved the story once I had the full picture, but I can definitely see its presentation being unappealing to someone who wants more direct storytelling. There are 10 endings and you're going to have many information gaps until you've completed all of them, especially the final true ending.The English translation, while mostly fine, had some quirky word choices at times. The Japanese dub was fantastic (with some big VA names involved), and I found the dialogue in the Japanese translation to be clearer and more expressive than the English translation. The English dialogue was perfectly comprehensible; it simply felt stiffer or less natural some of the time.I would suggest anyone used to playing metroidvanias to play on the Advanced difficulty rather than Normal. I played on Normal because the game suggested it, but in hindsight I ended up dying to a boss only once and barely at that despite an over 20 level gap (I unknowingly walked into the boss room while exploring the area which was lower level). The game is generous with healing items and spells (glyphs/prayers), so it's easy to make it through a boss battle on Normal even with lots of mistakes from not knowing the boss' patterns. I imagine on Advanced you might get the more standard metroidvania experience of not being able to tank a ton of mistakes on the first try, properly learning enemies' movesets, and retrying.The combat and movement felt fluid and responsive throughout the game.The core skills (afterimages) are a fairly standard metroidvania set including things like double/triple/super jump, invincibility dash, wall climb, and so on. The talent tree design is a little weird in that they decided to stack multiple levels of upgrade per node instead of simply spreading out the nodes. For example, one node might have a weapon attack boost locked until level X then a second weapon attack boost locked until level Y. It's not a huge deal, but it does make it hard to tell at a glance what nodes are available for upgrade or not as you level up and potentially unblock new layers on nodes.There is a decent amount of melee weapon variety with different ranges, attack speeds, and weapon skills (katanas, swords, scythes, whips, etc.) as well a magic system with spells tied to specific subweapons (staffs, spellbooks, and scrolls). You can have two different types of melee weapons and one magic weapon equipped at once.The game's map is gigantic. On top of that you are given little guidance on where to go. I personally loved the freedom of simply roaming around until I found a way to another area because there are secrets hidden everywhere. The game marks only NPCs on the map for you, so it's entirely up to you to mark things on the map as you go if there are secrets or paths you can't currently access and want to remember.As an added benefit of this free-roam approach, you will level up naturally if you fight enemies you encounter along the way. The only time I did any level grinding was at the very end of the game when I was aiming for the level 99 achievement. I had already reached the mid 80s by that point from simply exploring the map and killing anything I came across.Fast travel to many destinations requires a consumable item which I found annoying at first glance. However, I realized I was running around areas to fully explore them and find secrets anyways, so I barely fast-traveled early-mid game. By late game, I had plenty of currency to buy as many of those consumables as I wanted, so it became a moot point. I would still have preferred it if no fast travel was gated by a consumable, but it was at least much less of an annoyance than I expected at first.The art from start to finish is magnificent. Everything from the character designs to the backgrounds looks amazing.I enjoyed the music throughout, although I can't recall any specific tracks that stood out. It was more of a matter of the music generally fitting the vibe of what was happening and never taking me out of the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game is alright but there are few things you would want to consider.Combat is a bit unusual. Dashing in this game has no invincible frame (not until very very late into the game, like half way through the second last zone) and there is no blocking or parry either. The main way to mitigate damages is to jump over the enemies, which has its own problem because some of the enemies are very tall or hovering in the air.On top of not having an iframe dash is that there is collision damage which is a big nuisance. It was the main source of damage I took during my playthrough because the range of some of the weapon I used is very short so I ended up dashing into enemies, collided and took the damage instead of landing right next to them.These are things that you have to get comfortable with. Otherwise, just don't buy it.There are some really hard platformings which I thoroughly enjoyed. One was the area with one of the end game boss I stumbled upon where I was not supposed to be in because 1. my level was way too low 2. I didn't have the ability to reach there yet in an intended way. So I came up with an overly convoluted way to try and get there and then died to the boss. It was fun though, figuring out the way to make the best use of my limited abilities and squeeze them dry. Other than that are just hard-to-execute jumping.All in all, I give this game thumb up because I like it, thoroughly enjoyed. Do I recommend it? Nah, you wouldn't like it. 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: Well, after 30 hours I just can't fully recommend this game due to several gameplay/mechanical issues:1: The tech tree feels quite useless.You have several incremental upgrades to your characters stats and you can learn some new moves.The incremental stats are what you expect, +3 Hp here, +2 Deff there and some +3 Crit rate, nothing really amazing.  As for the moves, you have quite a lot of them, every weapon has at least 2-3 moves that you can unlock at the end of a tech tree branch. The only issue here is, that for some reason these moves end up using the same input as others, which may result in you doing the wrong move at the wrong time. It can be a little frustrating when you're trying to do a move, but because you held your thumbstick a little to the right, you end up doing another move that gets you killed.2: You can also obtain a variety of spells via magic tomes which is nice, but I forget about them due to the high mana cost. You can't perform more than 2-3 spells before you run out of mana. What's the point in having magic if you can't use it often ? 3: There's an upgrade system for your weapons and tomes. Which is nice, but I don't understand why we didn't get the full package? Like this upgrade system would've benefited more if it worked on armors and offer you a certain ability when you upgrade an item to max level. All you get from these upgrades is just a stat boost and nothing more. 4: Enemies are varied in the beginning but after awhile, you will encounter enemies that look different but they have the same abilities as the ones you saw in the beginning. Because of this, i found some of them feel kinda empty and recycled.5: The Boss fights, is where this game dropped the ball big time.After awhile you gonna end up fighting bosses that just do ridiculous amount of damage. At first i thought, ok maybe I'm just under-leveled, let me go and explore more and find better gear. Well I did that, and yes it did helped, but only by a little, instead of getting killed in 2 hits i was getting killed in 3. Also the weapon upgrades didn't feel to substantial either, i was doing maybe 10-15 dmg more than before. Well, if you're ok with some of the "shortcomings" from above than I say the game is worth it  for the rest of it. (If not full price at least at a discount)And that rest is:The art style and the graphics are amazing, Ori and the blind forest amazing.Sound design is quite good from the sound of the wind to the hard and crunchy noise of your sword hitting the enemy.Music is pretty good and fits well with the aesthetic of the game.Story is also fine, not great but not terrible either. The game has several endings, that add to the replayability of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: "When I first came to the islands I was awed by the birds with their colorful plumage,the beautiful flora,and the unspoiled vast expanses of forests,plains,and jungles. Something about the place had triggered my childhood nostalgia and put me in an optimistic mood! Yet as the weeks rolled on both I and the research team felt increasingly uneasy. We heard strange wails and moans carried by the winds. A colleague's pet german shepherd went missing. Many began having vivid nightmares about monstrous titans,cruel experiments,human sacrifices,tormented spirits,strange alien technologies,what I can only describe as the usage of "real magic",and prolonged battles between unknown civilizations that left devastation behind. Here there were secrets. Dark secrets."~Anon's travel-log before losing contact with the National Guard and the U.S.S. Defiant   After-Image pulled me in immediately. Love everything about it though supposedly this is one of those Metroidvanias that split people down the middle when it comes to liking it or disliking it. I'll try to analyze it in a way that's helpful to any potential future customers..... 1. Main ProtagonistAmnesiac white haired girl with a cute floating wise cracking familiar. Renee normally is not my type. Ironically I care about her and have become invested in her story! I typically prefer female protagonists that are more mature and have more sex appeal but Renee is so likable I was able to connect with her despite my personal bias. While being a somewhat over-used trope,Renee pulls off the "reborn-heroine-with-a-forgotten-past" role in a dignified satisfactory way. She's not too whiny or "edgy" and has just enough agency to push things along!2. Setting/Lore"Mages" are wise sages helping others survive in the new harsh frontier after a calamity left the world broken. Also acting as spiritual guides,they purify the bones of the fallen so souls go through the process of rebirth instead of becoming restless aggressive undead known as "wanderers".In spite of the serious undertones the game is garishly bright and colorful with its' various biomes being lush forests,vast jungles,and flower covered wide open fields. However, there are darker more ominous locales that often allude to malicious intentions,sacrificial rituals,inhumane experimentation,natural disasters,supernatural/paranormal activity,and bloody battles.3. ExplorationThere is "a lot" of platforming in After-Image requiring precision timing and the right skills acquired to open up additional routes. Luckily Renee is very graceful in her movements so I've been able to complete even some of the tougher gauntlets. Renee sits somewhere between Ryu Hayabusa from Ninja Gaiden and Scrooge McDuck from Capcom's fun Duck tales adaptation. She can high jump,air-dash,slide,climb,and bounce off critters to aid her in achieving higher altitudes! If you're are not into high intensity platforming sections I sympathize but for what it is worth, After Image is still much more forgiving than the many thumb blisterers old codgers such as myself played on the original Nintendo! Merchants and other supporting characters offer you advice or give you quests in small towns or sanctuaries interspersed across this vast world. Yes, I do mean "vast". Many claim this is one of the largest Metroidvanias of all time requiring quite the commitment and amount of spare time. Aka,this isn't a game you can beat in just 8-10 hours. Strap in Buckaroo,you are in for an adventure of a life time! Hope your schedule is cleared up because After Image is gonna demand you to put in the work!By the way,telaporting between mystic trees is ever an option with the item required to do so more freely always in stock. This eases up on the burden of back-tracking exponentially.4 CombatFast,fluid,and responsive. Engaging with enemies is satisfying. Not much blood or gore but you still feel like a one-woman-destruction-derby as you fire off spells,effortlessly switch between weapons,dodge incoming attacks like a parkour performing roller-skating kunoichi,and gradually become that much stronger!5. Leveling upThe constellation looking skill-grid seems as if it could be right out of Skyrim or a Final Fantasy yet it's not too difficult to figure out. All you are doing is spending points to allocate into buffs,resistances,more health,more magic,the occasional new weapon technique,or your luck which can lead to better item drops. Personally I relished having the choice to evolve Renee as I saw fit but I know other appreciators of this genre sometimes prefer a more simple and streamlined progression system. 6. Is there cooking,crafting,and gear enhancement opportunities?Yes! You can collect components or other oddities then use them to cook up new recipes or enhance your gear. 7. BossesBosses tend to be tough but fair. As expected certain fearsome foes will evolve or add new moves to their repertoires after a certain point. However, there are also more simplistic "mid bosses" that fall into the one trick pony category. It is a nice variety blending more complex encounters with enjoyable yet brief duels that don't overstay their welcome.8. Enemy designSmack around a grape covered plant dinosaur! Dodge the exploding grenades of what can only be described as Bubsy's evil neko-clones! Find Stitch's "messed up extended family" in the catacombs! After that fight some truly unsettling spectres,multiple-armed spider monkeys,squawking aggressive big birds,small dragons,floating water elemental sharks,and rampaging glowing mushroom people that are not gonna take it anymore! The sheer scope of the creatures and creepy crawlers in this game is impressive! Safe to say whomever came up with this bombastic bestiary at least had some reverence for the 80's,90's, and early 2000s. It is as if a mad scientist in a genetics laboratory creating new life-forms was inspired by Saturday morning cartoons,Japanese anime,Lisa Frank's artwork gracing the covers of countless school notebooks,Disney's animated classics,and video-games that were popular among generation X-ers growing up.While this may all seem too slap-dash,whimsical,outlandish,random,and over the top rest assured you will fight more horrific,intimidating,and unsettling adversaries later on. Apparently the aforementioned mad scientist also had VHS tapes of horror films such as The Thing,Reanimator,and Poltergeist tucked away in his collection too!  After Image lulls you into a nostalgic whimsical comforting fugue of fluttering butterflies right before it pulls the carpet out from underneath you as it finally turns pleasant childhood day-dreams into sheer nightmare fuel! 9. SoundVoice acting,sound effects,and musical scores all hit the perfect pitch with me. Impressive considering just how big this game is and how rapidly it shifts in both mood and tone.  OverallA great Metroidvania with the caveat being it may be too big for certain folks already on a tight schedule or demand a bit too much of those not so fond of overly convoluted rpg mechanics or the somewhat punishing action platformers of the old days. For me personally it has been refreshing and exactly what I needed.....

_childDocuments_.review: _Afterimage_8/10. Perfect Fit. This game is long. It’s really long. But the game has fast travel unlocked from the start (after the first patch) and traversing areas is satisfying. You have map pins available at the very start and I would recommend using them heavily. I think the game is very pretty although I wouldn’t go so far as “beautiful”. The music is appropriate albeit sometimes a bit generic sounding. None of the tracks ever really stood out to me but they were by no means bad. I think the biggest detractor here is the story. It isn’t bad but it isn’t particularly interesting and sometimes people talk a bit too long. Also, I definitely think the writing suffers from translation quality at times. The good:Finding weapons is exciting. There are five main weapon types plus sub-weapons which are your magic slot. Weapons can have unique skills and/or damage types which can make for fun weapon sets. Side quests, while largely either fetch quests or find-the-npc-again-in-a-different-area add to the game’s pacing, help build out the world, and usually end in “good stuff” and/or cute little stories. They rarely, if ever feel time-waste-y. Exploration is satisfying and rewarding. Platforming segments tend to lead to new gear rather than currency caches.Enemy design is quite varied. There are a few pallet-swap types but even then they will have unique (enough) attacks.I never felt the need to grind for money or xp but also never felt too over powered or underpowered in whatever area felt like progress. The acceptable:The buildcraft in this game is close to being really fun. Each weapon type has unique attacks and unlockable skills through skill trees. You can have two main weapons equipped at a time plus one sub-weapon. Experimenting with different weapons and abilities and combo-ing in and out of skills can be really satisfying. My main issue here is how the game handles stats. Increases are largely through gear and usually in small numbers or percentages that stack. It works, and you _can_ min-max to a degree. But if you want to try out, say a poison whip build, you’re going to scroll through every piece of gear for each slot.Boss fights are fine. I beat most bosses on my first or second try with some exception to end game bosses. My biggest issue here is bosses tend to have a fairly limited attack roster to rotate through. Bosses, largely, felt fairly distinct from one another and some were even pretty cool to fight. There are few boss fights that go on, what I would consider, too long. But I could see this being a downside for some. There is not a “traditional” NG+, 100% the game is intended (and required) to complete in a single save slot. The meh:As far as progression blocking through abilities, it’s pretty straightforward. You’ll see something and either very quickly figure out a way to get to it or know exactly the ability you’ll need to progress. Some abilities really only come up once.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun metroidvania with a pretty solid foundation. I enjoyed the art direction a lot and the map is nice to look at. Each area is it's own thing visually so there isn't any same-y type areas. The only real issue concerning areas and map is how big the game is. It's easily the biggest metroidvania I've ever played and I'm pretty sure it contends to be the biggest, period. There might be a point where you just want the game to end and that's valid.Combat is good, nothing really bad to comment. There's a large variety of weapons and spells to pick from with a decent upgrade curve for your weapon selection based on where you are in the game. In typical souls-like fashion, you can upgrade your weapons' level as well. I'll admit, it's been a while since I played so I don't remember if the upgrades actually make that much of a difference but whatever. What really makes combat stand out to me is the abilities for each weapon, and even some abilities that can be used with two different weapon types equipped. There's some clear winners in what's actually "meta" but you can beat the game with any weapons, they're all viable.Some boss fights are good, some not so good and some outright miserable. You'll hit a few that are like bashing your head against a wall until you finally bust through. The redeeming thing here is that you can leave for another area until you've leveled properly if that suits your play-style.Quests in the game are alright and keeping in the spirit of metroidvanias, there's going to be a lot of quest based backtracking. Some of the quests felt cryptic to me and needed a guide for but that's not worth knocking points off for in my opinion. There's also plenty of ability based backtracking to earlier points of the game, but that's to be expected and I think is handled exceptionally well in Afterimage.For the endings and just getting the platinum in general, there's a bit of a grind and I absolutely guarantee you're going to need a guide. This was the most tedious part of the game for me and had me rubbing the top of my head in annoyance. Overall, good stuff. Not the best game I've ever played but I can't complain. It'll definitely occupy some of your time

_childDocuments_.review: I've never felt more mixed about a Metroidvania before. The art style, the boss design, the music, the amount of weapons, the giant skill tree with extensive weapon move sets; it should all make for a fantastic metroidvania. And in its own right is is, it does a lot right. It's lore is interesting, albeit scattered, its got a ton of bosses and each of them were relatively fun fights, and its huge map with tons of areas to explore can be a huge appeal to some. Yet, I found so many aspects of the game to feel lacking. The combat has such potential to be great, but the decision to include contact damage takes away from it so much. Each weapon has a fair amount of skills you can learn, but I found myself not using about 80% of them because doing so would put you at too high of a risk of taking contact damage. The katana's jump attack is what I ended up using to fight mobs and bosses alike nearly the whole game, and without contact damage I feel as if I could've had more fun by stringing together combos more seamlessly. If they made enemies move-sets more dangerous and removed contact damage, I think my overall opinion of this game would've been much better. I also think the map was oversized, and the limited number of locations to where you can fast travel made it so I did not want to collect everything and finish all the achievements, which is a rarity for me when it comes to metroidvanias. I also wish the weapons/magic were scaled differently. It is a linear progression scaling, so if you found a weapon with a cool move set around level 50, it will be borderline useless by the time you reach level 80. I found this particularly bothersome with the magic attacks. I would've liked to experiment more with different staffs and elements but due to the scaling it was not practical to do so. I think Afterimage has great bones, and was a fun enough experience to keep me invested for 40 hours, which is a feat for a metroidvania. Regardless, I think there are a handful of design philosophies implemented that could be improved, and by the end of the game I was fatigued and ready to be done, well before reaching 100% completion.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid metroidvania that does a lot right but with some annoying aspects.  The map is huge with tons to see, do, and find.  This is a double edged sword because it provides a lot of content but can get a bit tedious at times.  Despite the size, I don't think I ever got lost, and generally there's multiple areas accessible to the player at any given time (a huge pro for me).  For the most part the opening up of the map feels organic.  This game is good about opening up areas through movement based power-ups instead of lock-and-key checks (though there are some of the latter).  There's fast travel nodes that you can travel between for free, and then there's consumable items that let you fast travel at will to any checkpoint.  I think making this consumable was a bad idea, but it's not too difficult to stock up on the item.The combat and platforming are the bread and butter of the game, and both are very good.  There's a large variety of enemies with different visual designs and attack patterns.  There's a lot of bosses, and they're diverse and fun to fight.  The platforming doesn't have anything particularly innovative, but there's tons of little platforming challenges sprinkled throughout the game that are mostly engaging.  There's a typical complement of power-ups that given you more movement and exploration options, but again, nothing innovative.The story is passable.  I didn't love it or hate it, though I found myself caring less and less as the game went on.  There's a good amount of lore, it's somewhat convoluted but interesting.  The game has a bunch of different endings locked behind various conditions and bosses.  They're mostly intuitive and fun, though some are duds.  I didn't get the true ending because there's a required item that you can't get until you level up to a certain point.  I killed every boss and explored most of every area, and still wasn't a high enough level.  I would've needed to tediously grind exp (which I did not care to do).  Overall I liked it.  The true ending situation leaves a bad taste in my mouth, but I still enjoyed my time spent.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a souls like platformer, and requires a high degree of skill and repetition. I lead with that because those are the things I don't like about the game, and even though it's a good game if you like those a characteristics, I can't really recommend it except to very specific people.   I do wish it had a different mode or skill level which would allow me to play it like more of an exploratory RPG, even if only in a platformer form. I like to play games in more of an exploratory mode, and with this one I just have to continually remember and be on guard for the creeps instead, which is sort of a dealbreaker for me on a game which is this beautiful and which has such a nice production values. I would prefer just to explore, talk to NPCs fulfill some quests, and so on. I don't mind having to obtain new skills for a game and learn the patterns of creeps and so forth, but having to  execute on those things over and over again in the maps at the same locations every time you visit is a bit more tedium than I like to see in the games I play.  So this is a solid thumbs up if that's what you like! :-)

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game overall.Very nice art style and aesthetics.Controls pretty good.
