_childDocuments_.review: My impression of Afterimage after 79 minutes into it, is that someone played a few really good games, like Ori and maybe Path of Exile or Grim Dawn, and then  those games to a software developer who wasn't all that familiar with video games, who then did the best they could to make a clone from vague descriptions alone.The story, such that it is, is very "tell, not show" oriented, only what exposition there is, isn't very easy to follow, giving the impression that they're intentionally dropping the player into the middle of a story without any real idea what the lore is, except clearly it's meant to be a lore-heavy game.The progression is just as strange. As an example of both progression and narration strangeness, early in the game, you fight a boss, a giant wolf whose defeat is also the first in-game achievement. It's laughably easy! My annoying little floaty companion did the first "helpful" thing ever and launched a fireball at it, only to complain that it was immune to it? I wouldn't know. I killed it too quickly for its effectiveness or ineffectiveness to make any difference. (I'm on the harder difficulty, mind...)The wolf then comes back to life and one-shot ganks you with no chance of victory. After you die, instead of respawning like in a normal Metroidvania, you... talk to your Madame? In... future tense? About things that seem to have happened in the past, which seem to be the events of the game you just played in your present. And then you respawn, and notice a person who looks similarly to you (I think; the dialog box covered her up almost entirely the entire time), who babbles nonsense. Your floating companion (totally not a ripoff of Sein) then, in a horribly irritating and crass voice, complains that the stranger had been babbling nonsense, and says we don't have time. We have to get back to the village. Um... what village?This is the kind of experience I'm having so far.The controls are imprecise at best. The weapon only attacks directly forward so far, but most enemies come from above or below, and there just isn't any good way to attack them, or even to defend against them, other than dodging.But wait! I got a new weapon! An upgrade from my  fantasy sword that is... a stick. It's useless. Shorter range, much slower. It does damage twice, and a bit more of it (somehow), but since it has half the attack speed, it's pretty much meh. It's also vastly more interruptible, and if an enemy so much as breathes at me I freeze up and cancel my attack.Another new weapon, hooray! A... wooden... sickle? Which is actually a scythe, except not (which is good, because scythes aren't weapons, they're tools). Its swing arc animation is much bigger, and covers further out in front, a fair ways above, and even about half its front attack arc behind me! Finally, I thought; I can attack above me and even behind a bit!Nope. It just attacks straight out front. Just like the first weapon. So the animation literally just  to you.The graphics lie, too. Some platforms you can drop through with down+jump like any Metroidvania. Other platforms, you can't. They are identical. Some walls look like they're very clearly hinting at being hidden passages, but aren't. Other walls look like perfectly normal walls, but are, in fact, secret passages. Lots of things in the background sparkle just like loot drops, clearly signaling in the language of video game graphics, that they are interactable. They're not. Some enemies are in the very closest background layer, walking around and looking like they might attack... but they're not interactable, just background features. Other enemies look like they're in the background, and then attack you.The mechanics are a confused mess as well... Obviously there's an HP bar, and a... mana bar, I guess? I have mana potions. I haven't ever used any mana, though. They're framed near an XP bubble, Ori/HK style. Okay, fine, fairly straightforward except... sometimes from battle I get these crystal bubbles. When I collect them, they fill up what seems to be an XP globe, all well and good. But then, I also get "+X Experience Gained" popping up when I defeat other enemies. Still others drop what appears to be loot of some kind (all loot is supiciously just a single glowy starlight sprite...), but that doesn't appear in my inventory or anywhere else, and I  it's also adding to my XP bubble? Maybe? Not sure. It's pretty hard to tell.The level-up system is ripped directly out of constellation/maze systems like Path of Exile or Grim Dawn, only most of the nodes only do one thing: increase primary weapon attack. The nodes are also at odd angles from one another, but with controller, even with a thumbstick, you can only navigate orthogonally, and it often misinterprets my intention. A lot of systems in the game are much more intuitive with a mouse, except in the splash screen it says "Controller strongly recommended" with a picture of an XBox controller, so I used that, but it's awful.So... I'm leveling up (why are abilities grind-based instead of progression-based? This is a Metroidvania, is it not???) and... aha! A node that adds an upward attack! How thrilling! Maybe I can flesh out what should be part of the absolute base standard move set, at long last!It's bound to Up+Attack, and it "waves the greatsword at an upward angle to attack enemies above you." Since the game is absolutely full of localization/translation errors and typos, I figured that "greatsword" was another of those, and it just meant "primary weapon" even if that was currently a wooden stick tied to another wooden stick (a vast upgrade from my gorgeous fantasy longsword/greatsword, somehow...). But no... I can't use the new ability. Maybe it really meant that it has to be a sword, specifically? So I re-equip the sword. Nope, not that either. And yeah... turns out they really did mean "greatsword"? What greatsword? I have absolutely no idea. Haven't seen one. *appends "Great Job!" Van Damme meme sarcastically*So yeah... I'd avoid this one. If you have a high tolerance for confusion, bad narrative, and very preachy religious overtones, and don't mind just wandering around swinging your nonsensical weapons around with their outright lies of attack animations, uh... go for it?Personally I'd get pretty much any other Metroidvania that's ever been made, and have a far, far better time.Hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pleasantly surprised by this and ended up binging this in less than a week. I got all 3 of the main endings and plan on getting the secret ones later.I'll be separating this review into 4 parts.  and  Despite the bad, I still wholeheartedly recommend the game. It's fantastic.Honestly, the best thing about this game is its unique art style for the genre of souls-like metroidvania, and I don't mean this as a backhanded compliment. It has this beautiful and colorful world that is varied throughout. You can immediately tell which zone you're in by the theme and backdrop of the location, or even just the colors that are used. Despite this, the game still manages to convey the oppressive feeling of a world in ruins.It's quite refreshing honestly, as this genre is oversaturated with art styles that fall back on using dull on somber colors, games like Salt and Sanctuary, Ender Lilies and to a certain extent, Hollow Knight, or using "dark blobs" like Ori and the Blind Forest. As such, (almost) every area in Afterimage is memorable and unique, which is honestly quite a feat.It's pretty good and quite varied. You have 6 class of weapons : sword, greatsword, twin daggers, scythe, whips and of course  katana. Each has its own unique quirks, upsides and downsides, but all 6 are viable and allow you to vary up your playstyle should you chose to. You can equip 2 weapon at all time + 1 spell and each spell has its own unique effect. With those weapons, you also have skills for each which can be unlocked from the skill tree. And just when you get the hang of those moves and get comfortable with the build you prefer, the game starts introducing weapons with unique moveset to spice things up. Enemies are varied with there's not really any reskin/recolor of different enemies, ie. same move but looks different (there were a couple, but it's only in the single digits) which makes every zone have its own combat challenge to learn and overcome. While some enemy moves can be a bit cheap, they were never unfair. Bosses were also nicely varied, though not all of them deserve praise. Some were a bundle of fun to fight, while others were a pretty big slog to have to fight. Though there was no boss that made me want to give up on the game, so there's nothing I would call atrocious.There's also contact damage, which, while annoying, is not that big of a problem. It's just something you have to adapt to.It's pretty nice to see a game of this genre embracing voice acting as others would often be silent have weird blabber noise. Every character has a voice and all of them are good/great with nothing standing out as off or bad. Pretty standard for the genre. Good exploration is pretty much a must have. As usual, you get new traversal abilities as you progress which you use to explore more. But with the game's art style, you'll at least get a nice visual treat and it's hard to get confused of where is where. Also, the game has a pretty detailed in-game map, which makes exploring and revisiting areas a lot less tedious.The quests are... they're there, I guess? A lot of them are fetch quest or "hide and seek" wherein you have to find out the NPC would be next. Some of the are straightforward enough, others have the NPC in a corner of the map you're likely to miss. While you have a journal with your quest logs, they never tell you much, just recaps what happened but doesn't give you a whole lot of useful info.The writing is not that good. It might be a translation problem, or it might be the writing. It's a bit weird when the characters are all beautifully voiced, but then the dialogue itself is just...off. Characters would often use a mix of archaic and modern English. It's not that big of a problem though as you can still understand what's being said, though it'll just sound odd and not quite right.Admittedly I couldn't follow the story, so I can't judge its narrative. What I can judge however was how it was presented.I started with pen and paper, taking notes and everything, but I kind of gave up due to how much jargon there was. I feel like it tries to be too complicated. It throws around big Word with capital W, but doesn't go into what they mean. It also likes being really vague, so I don't really know what is being talked about most of the time.If the game just explained some of the stuff, not even in dialogue, but just in a couple of text documents, it would've been fine. I don't know if I just missed them, but there were certainly not in my playthrough.While I praised both earlier, the combat doesn't work well with the amazing art. Since the world they created is vibrant with color, it can sometimes be hard to actually see what's happening during combat. An example of this is against a lava boss. You fight him in a room that is bright red in color. But then he starts casting fire attacks, which are also bright orange/yellow. It's quite hard to see and keep track of his attacks during the chaos and panic. There are also some areas where the foreground obstructs your view, so you don't see what's happening while you fight. Though this only happened with a few bosses/enemies, in only some areas it's still bad enough that it's worth mentioningWhile this wasn't a deal breaker for me, I understand that it might be for others, especially when some bosses become frustrating to fight because of this.This was probably the biggest questionable decision of the game, and is probably why this game didn't receive the good reception it should've on release. To fast travel, you need to be at the big save points. There's only 1 per zone, and the zones are big, so if you're doing a lot back tracking, it can be really frustrating to do unnecessary commuting.To fast travel between the smaller save points, you need to use a consumable. It used to be a rare limited consumable you have to find, but you can now buy it from a merchant. It's still annoying because you need to do a lot of backtracking in the late game and the item cost enough to be pricey when buying in bulk, meanwhile there's potions or upgrade materials you could be purchasing insteadEDIT: One last late addendum, but there's no actual NG+The game tells you there's a NG+, but it's really a side (linear) story you play with a different character that unlocks a hidden map in the main game that gets you to the true ending. There is no replaying the game with your upgrades/weapons/skills, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is certainly no Hollow Knight. It's no Bloodstained, either. I'm sorry to say it's not even on the level of Ender Lilies, a game that itself was deeply flawed. While I ended up liking Ender Lilies enough to 100% it, I can't bring myself to want to keep going in Afterimage despite being nowhere near the end.So, compliments out of the way: The game's really pretty. The art style is consistently great and every area is beautiful and visually distinct, even if the biome placement makes the world as a whole feel like generic fantasy setting #1701520 with arbitrary metroidvania obstacle courses every so often. The music's serviceable - none of it's memorable, but none of it's really bad either, with the sole exception of the miniboss music being the wrong kind of silly.You'll notice I couldn't really mention anything good about this game without bringing up a flaw. That's going to be a theme here.Afterimage's cardinal sin is its combat. Let's get the good out of the way - there's no stamina bar to deal with. Yep, that's it. As for the bad: Compare to Ender Lilies: that game had plenty of its own problems with combat to be sure, but the enemies were generally slower and easier to read despite (or perhaps because of) also dealing contact damage, your weapons and subweapons were more reliable, and you started the game with iframes on your dash. Hollow Knight had fast enemies dealing contact damage but their fast attacks all had obvious tells while your own attacks had knockback and no windup.The combat isn't the only part Afterimage doesn't get right, though.Again, compare to Ender Lilies: the controls were generally solid, the world was way less padded and felt like it could plausibly exist, the one time I got stuck with no idea how to progress ended up being my fault for setting the gamma too low, there weren't any wasted systems, and the translation and writing were both solid.It's disappointing because under all the jank I can see a lot of potential in Afterimage. But potential is all it is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing Metroidvania game. It is fun, difficult and very challenging.Let me stress the most important points I noticed so far:- Visually the game is incredible. It is very polished and it shows that the graphic and art section put a lot of work into every single sprite and area.- The map is MASSIVE. This is good because it encourages to keep exploring and backtracking once you get some new skill to try to access areas and spots you couldn't reach the first time you arrived to some zones.On the other hand, the magnitude of the map can be overwhelming and even somewhat frustrating at times because the areas are huge and when you think you have found the right path, you come across a fork that takes you in 3 other different directions, so you can easily get lost.- As is the style of any Metrodivania game, it is clear that you require skills and power ups to be able to continue exploring the map, but the game doesn't really tell you anything or is very vague as to where you should go. It isn't until several areas after that you acquire the double jump and climb abilities which are the most useful for accessing various points on the map that are unreachable at the start.- The combat. At first sight it seems simple, but the fact that you can use a sword, greatsword, twin blades,a scythe and a katana, along a whip makes it very dyanmic, even more so because you can unlock special attacks and movements for each.The game encourages you to switch weapons based on the enemies you're up against, but it's kind of cumbersome to have to pause the game and make the change in the menu. Had this been possible with a shortcut in the controller/keyboard and even being able to do combos by actively combining and changing different weapons during combat it would have been much better.On the other hand, although the majority of the weapons only change their appearance and color palette slightly, there are several with unique effects and with clear references to games of the genre (there is a certain sword that an enemy in the shape of a magic book drops just like in SotN), which encourages you to experiment with whatever you come across (what is the deal wiht the doll accesory that throws SD heads of Renee? lol)- My last point is the bosses. Even though the mechanics consist of learning their patterns, damn, I suddenly feel like I'm in a game like Dark Souls/Bloodborne/some other FromSoftware ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ because in some cases the difficulty escalates to an extremely high level and you get BTFO very easily (already I'm level 70 with the skill tree quite developed and I just can't deal with a knight boss after the library and a mutant butterfly that petrifies you in a forest). The difficulty curve is very exaggerated for some bosses.Overall I think it is a great game and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly an amazing game that rivals Hollow Knight in terms of metroidvanias. The art design is beautiful and immaculate, enemy designs are varied and unique and the atmosphere feels captivating as well with the beautiful orchestral soundtrack that give me studio ghibli vibes.Gameplay wise the game plays smooth as butter, controls are tight and responsive and for as long as I have been playing I haven't noticed any hit box detection issues or glitches. The game is a good challenge too, with engaging boss fights and a plethora of monsters to hack your way through. The game is also forgiving in that you can pause the game to use health potions in the middle of battle. Equipment is varied and versatile, I don't know how balanced the game is however since I've only played through with a scythe, which seems to be overpowered possibly.Overall this game is an incredible accomplishment well worth the 20 bucks. I await to see what this developer comes out with next.

_childDocuments_.review: (Got it as a gift from a friend, not the devs.)A fantastic metroidvania. Not quite another Hollow Knight, but still fantastic.Pros:1. The controls are tight.2. The world is extremely big.3. Good story, just wish it was told a bit better.4. Lots of weapons to vary your playstyle as you go.5. Bosses were fun without being Souls-hard.6. Bunch of upgrades to your movement tech to help spice things up.7. All the environments were beautiful and each was unique.8. Tons of enemy types.9. A nice little indicator will tell you when you have strayed into an area you shouldn't be in yet. Trust me: when the indicator is there, you probably don't want to be.10. Tons of bosses and all were fun. I did have some issue with Brandr as his teleport would put him right inside of me with no way to stop the damage, but that was the only one that felt cheap.Cons:1. The side-quests points could be found out of order, leading to some jumbled story-telling and confusion. It felt bad in Breath of the Wild (and Tears of the Kingdom) and it felt bad here.2. The main story feels like a lot happened that wasn't told to the player. I got the World Flower ending and I still don't know exactly what was happening and why there were multiple Renees. More clear story-telling would have been nice. Ifree's and 42's stories were told clearly, but Renee's definitely was not.3. I would have liked some more hints as to how to get each ending. I had to use a guide. The world is HUGE and providing vague hints does nothing to help the player.4. Most of the talents costing two points resulted in less impactful level-ups as a lot of them were "Oh, well, I only got one point and I need two to buy anything so this level-up means nothing."5. Mana was used up far too fast. I found it impractical and just didn't use it, even with an equipment load-out meant for it.6. Some of the weapon skills didn't work, and most of them felt kinda useless. They seemed to do less damage than me just spamming the normal attack, even the final hidden ones.7. Hitting A to advance the dialogue sometimes skipped scenes where the characters actually did something, leading to missed story.8. It would have been nice if the slower weapons like the 2-handers did more damage to the veins and the 1-sided gates. I kept my dual-blades in my off-hand just for this purpose, but it felt weird that my tiny little daggers did the same amount of damage as my big 2-hander to a gate.9. The quest log was completely pointless as the text in there for each quest tells you absolutely nothing about what is going on with the quest and where to go to advance it.10. For the collection quests, were we supposed to just scroll through the massive Beastiary in hopes of finding the right item?I mean, no game is perfect, but this game is an utter blast and I suggest any fans of Hollow Knight to give this game a shot. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are fan of games like Hollow Knight or Ori chances are you will enjoy this game!  The art work is pretty, the music is great, and while I don't fully understand the story yet I am enjoying it and trying to piece it all together.  The mechanics work smoothly for the most part, there is a little frustration sometimes.  My biggest complaint is the lack of directions, there is not a lot of guidance which leads to just random exploring and often finding yourself in an area that you can't fully access yet or with too high level of monsters. _childDocuments_.review: Not that good, but not that bad. It's just another 'OK' game.Pros:The game is not as hard as those of the same type (obviously designed for kids), so it is a good place to start for those who are not used to Metroidvania. Additionally, the arts and music are well-composed. These are all the good things I can think about.Cons:1). Poor direction. It is "inevitable" for you to spend 85-90% of your time dashing around. It would be exciting for you for the first 5-10 hours as you could explore a lot but then the word 'exploring' would suddenly change to 'boring'.2). Stupid weapons' abilities or character's skills. There are various skills and weapons in this game but they are all useless. You could easily beat the game with just a simple hit. Using skills will only lead you to the wrong moves and, afterwards, get hit for free.3). Dodge, in this game, is a dash. So, when you think you do the dodge, you basically do the dash and will get hit if you dash into your enemies. There is no iframe during the animation. The developers do not understand the differences between the two words.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Absolutely gorgeous environments with decent music and a lot of variety- Responsive movement and fun exploration (if you dont mind backtracking and/or adding markers to your map)- Engaging combat with a lot of different options to chose fromCons:Overall experience lacks polish, e.g. - You can break the order of the (already confusing) story by reaching certain areas before others. - You can make some boss fights almost trivial if you reach a late game area early and find a weapon with very high atk stats. - Sometimes secrets are well hidden and require keen observation, and other times what looks like a secret leads you to an almost out of bounds section of the map where no treasure awaits you and the art gets all wonky.- Some weapons and particularly magic items will grant you abilities but there is no way to know what these abilities do besides guessing based on the name and using them. In general the UI lacks clarity, for example you can't compare an item with the one currently equipped, you can't easily tell which talents are available to level, maxxed or not yet available, etc.-----Despite these shortcomings, I still had a great time with this game. The most important things which is the visual aspect and the action are well done and enjoyable and they provide a strong foundation that makes the weaker parts a lot more palatable. The story is very confusing but still somewhat engaging, especially towards the end. The game is fully voice acted in English and of a decent quality which is commendable. There's a big anime inspiration aesthetically, especially for characters, but it doesn't fall into the tropes of oversexualized characters or over-the-top reactions, which I appreciated.If you're itching for a cool metroidvania that will take about 20-30 hours to complete (and more if you're aiming for full completion, achievements and a certain endgame thing), I can definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Metroidvanias like Castlevania and Blood of the Moon, I love this game. I enjoyed the satisfaction of discovering secrets, especially with the aid of a particular ability that acts somewhat like a treasure detector without being too obvious. The many weapons and accessories are also fun as there are various combinations for different situations like treasure hunting for rare enemy drops or boss survival.One thing I don't like about the game, however, is the lack of a minimap, especially for a Metroidvania, which meant that I had to open up the map every few seconds just to keep track of where I'm headed. It would be better if the devs can implement a toggleable minimap overlay with zoom, especially when the areas are quite extensive, and there are so many areas to cover.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: To get the bad out of the way first...- The story is disjointed and hard to follow. There are multiple endings, but it's intended that you get all the main story endings. - There's very little direction on where you should go and when. This is a double-edged sword in the sense that you're free to explore at your leisure, but I encountered several story bits from what I can assume was the wrong side of the screen.- The translation's fairly rough, characters tend to talk in a way that feels too formal or rigid. And yer wan who says "I shall guide your way once you have taken the oath" is lying. There's no oath to take. Don't be like me and constantly going back to Misty Waters after getting a new ending to see if she says anything different, hah!- The bosses can feel downright unfair at times when you're not prepared.- The touch damage in this game drives me absolutely bloody crazy because your dash doesn't have i-frames. I don't mind not having i-frames (without beating a certain boss, that is) but it makes repositioning when you're cornered a nightmare. And enemies all have varied attacks with good telegraphs, but the touch damage renders some of that pointless sometimes.-Sometimes enemies can be obscured by the foreground, resulting in cheap hits.- Ifree doesn't like seafood and he thinks everyone who does isn't normal.He's a poopyhead.But honestly, so far, this is my game of 2023. So it's time for the positives!- The controls feel sublime. Dashing, jumping, swinging your weapon all feel responsive and fluid.- Combat is fast-paced but not too fast (for the most part), and all weapons feel nice and crunchy (which is SUPER important for me), with great sound design, hitstop, and screen shake when needed. This is backed up by plenty of different enemies to fight.- The game boasts a bounty of bosses, and a lot of them are quite difficult and overwhelming at first, but fun and fair once you get the patterns down. Just remember that you don't have i-frames until you beat a certain boss, so it's all about positioning!- All the weapons feel great and have fun moves to unlock.- There's a wealth of different accessories that help diversify your build, and curious minds will find no shortage of skill points. So it's not really restrictive in how you allocate your points.- The presentation is drop-dead gorgeous, from the stunning visuals to the lovely ambient tracks for each area in the game.- The map being so huge is a double-edged sword, but I found it a joy to explore and get lost in....Yeah I absolutely love this game. When I finished playing it for a day, I kept thinking about wanting to play more. It just feels so good to play.It's got plenty of issues, but if you can come to grips with them you'll be in for a treat.If you read the whole review, thanks for reading what's basically a hyperfixation infodump.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: It's ironic that such a pretty game needs more polish. The designer strikes me as a chef with all the same high quality ingredients the best restaurants in town use, but has only the basic ability to cook. The result is the worst game I've played this year.Combat is there but feels clunky, repetitive, slow, and uninspired. The game opts for quantity of weapons over quality of combat interactions resulting in lengthy back and forth's with basic enemies that immediately feel like a chore and only get more dull as enemies become able to tank hits and repeat their one attack pattern. There's a lot of weapons but none of them feel particularly thought out as to why they should be there. The designer knows that weapon size roughly informs the speed and damage, but doesn't really understand why there are different weapons in a game so combat doesn't take any of that into account.You're given a lot of mobility from the start with dashing, a sustainable jump, and the ability to extend the jump slightly by doing an attack for some reason, though this is wasted when you realise you can dash after jumping from the start of the game also to both sustain height and go further. There's a delay between hitting the ground and being able to jump again that undermines the actual mobility, and dashing has a low enough cooldown that you can feel the dev got bored of play testing with slower movement. After all - why undervalue the beautiful scenery by letting players speed run past it?There's also crafting and cooking (crafting 2), because it's 2023 and all games just have to put this padding in, I'm guessing it's some kind of insecurity thing. But even the menus find a way to be disappointing since for some reason the game remembers where you were last in the sub-menu, but always launches the menu to the items page even if you were last on inventory so expect to be constantly switching just to try out weapons or look at what you picked up turning even that into a chore.This game also commits the sin of giving you too few skill tree points to buy anything with them when the system is first introduced, but seeing how large the tree is and how measly the upgrades are, it looks like they didn't spend enough time in excel balancing everything out.The game also has some very intense lore going on but it's not about to waste it's time actually telling you what any of the nonsense is. God is dead or gone or something but also you're the chosen by god but also you're an anime character because that's popular. Your save points allude to the fruit of knowledge, the world was ruined by a flood... I quite like new takes on Christian mythology and I like the idea of playing a kind of anime soul shepherd, but this game is too busy enjoying the smell of its own farts so it's entirely there to justify the aesthetic, not to actually inform the gameplay or game mechanics - after all this is just a Hollow Knight clone, it's not here to do anything revolutionary (it has crafting after all).This game's visual give it such a head start that it's a shame it kills it's audience with a death by a thousand cuts - mainly to the project manger's budget and the release schedule by the feel of things.The end result is much like my 2nd girlfriend - pretty, pretentious, and surprisingly shallow.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a seemingly simple game that transforms into an expansive and complex game. There are several moments where this game opens up and you're like wow this is big. There are more than a hundred weapons to choose from that each change the flow of combat. There are a large variety of enemy types and environments that never make this game stale. All of this together makes this game hard to put down. Traveling throughout the map is very seamless and easy to do. Hidden walls and pathways are plentiful and actually feel rewarding when found. The skill tree is large and there is some weight to the progression.However, there are several features that I wish were in the game from the start though. From the start, there is no dodge on roll. I think this limits the fluidity of this game.  I think the game could use a more direct questing system. A lot of times I was wondering, especially at the beginning, what my goal was. A lot of the bosses are easy with the exception of a handful later on, which are actually very fun and complex fights. These drawbacks are noticeable but they don't really takeaway from the all of the resounding positives that bring this game up.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't beaten this game yet after 24 hours of gameplay, which is great! It's such an interesting world, and huge too. It's easy to just pick a direction and start walking, getting sidetracked from whatever you intended to do, because there's just so much to look for and so many hiding spots to crawl into and discover.Something that I don't recall seeing in other similar games is the little hover mechanic, where if you swing a weapon mid-air you float a little longer. It opens up a lot of interesting possibilities for exploring if you can get a feel for it, but as it's kind of non-standard, lack of practice with this one specific skill doesn't hinder progress overall. Controls are really good, though some boss fights can feel a bit frustrating and unfair at times, and picking up items off the ground doesn't work well all the time.I see reviews and discussions regarding the voice acting for the game, specifically the English track, and in my opinion there isn't anything wrong with the acting. The writing, on the other hand, leaves a LOT to be desired. The translation is sorely lacking, and while I can't comment on accuracy, I can say that the wording is extremely awkward in parts, and complete gibberish in others. I have no idea how someone translated it, someone else read over it, and someone else read it out loud and not a single one of them stopped to ask, "Why does this say this and how on earth am I supposed to deliver this?" The actors are a 7/10, good and inoffensive; whoever was responsible for the final written version should probably look into a career change.Overall it's a super fun game and I highly recommend it. Just press some buttons, jump around a lot, and don't think about any of it too hard.

Of course there are some minor issues with its design or mechanics but overall its really good, 8.5/10.Warning! Dont play on normall if you want a challenge, in reallity its easy mode. _childDocuments_.review: This game makes me feel like a kid in a candy store. There's so much content! As of this writing, I've played for nine hours and have barely scratched the surface of what this game has to offer. The map is gigantic and well made, there are secrets in every corner and the graphics are beautiful. The only downsides so far are the nonsensical story and low difficult. _childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is an incredibly well made Metroidvania that is truly massive in all good ways. It has a few flaws, notably translation... while decent, I noticed quite a few spelling mistakes. Bosses are pretty weird, they're either top tier or just... below average. Same with music too, tho it's mostly bangers. Enemies also have insane tracking for no reason at all. Difficulty-wise it's pretty alright, tho most reviews that talk about it don't mention one detail. See, at all times you have a lot of freedom on where to go, which is good. Tho starting like 1/3 into the game, you may wander into areas that are like +40 lvls away from yours in terms of damage, so you will get 2-3 shotted in no time. If you happen to choose the "correct" path, difficulty won't jump much. So if you're getting pummeled in 3 hits, well, maybe consider going somewhere else. Or just don't get hit, I'm not your dad. Totally didn't suffer on a boss for 40 minutes getting 2-shotted cause I was stubborn, no, that didn't happen.Speaking of freedom, there is a lot of variety on how to play. You get 6 weapon types with learnable skills (and sometimes unique bonuses that includes moveset additions) and spells. You can equip 2 weapons + spell at a time, allowing for quite a lot of combinations. World is BIG and fun to explore, there's a lot of secrets and fair share of side-quests. Overall, I liked this game a lot. It's really up there in my top of metroidvanias, if you like this genre - this is a must play. As for newcomers, I feel like this could be a good entry point.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: So, there is  a major rift in Metroidvanias as of late (really the last 10 years or so). The vast majority of "Metroidvanias" have little to no relation to Metroid or Castlevania and are instead 2d Dark Souls that pride themselves on minimalist combat, barren lands with next to nothing to discover, minimalist to no spells that inspire any creativity, little to no RPG, little to no actual backtracking AKA exploring and finding hidden goodies that make you giggle, little to no relevant platforming and little to no power fantasy as the basis of these games relies on hard boss fights, which means the devs need you to remain fairly stagnant so they can balance properly. Most of your time in these games will be using IFrames and swinging a weapon. In fact, I would say these games leave out everything that makes a Metroidvania what it is, beyond it being 2d and having a map.Then, there games that actually deserve the name Metroidvania, like this one. If you loved Castlevania SotN, AoS, Bloodstained, then this game is for you. Its the real deal. Finally we have a game that scratches every itch ive longed for. Amazing platforming, hundreds of secrets all around, tons of upgrade paths and quests at every turn, every hour of this game has you thinking on what to do next in pure excitement as your options are plentiful. It does justice to the genre and is the perfect step in the right direction for someone like me, who has wondered why every other game misses the mark. Power fantasy is out of control, you can become a complete monster as you upgrade weapon skills and get unique weapon arts, as well as new abilities. By the end you will feel like a God taking on the world.The story it seems people couldn't understand, but I really feel like that shows the quality of the reviewers. Its not a hard grasp. A girl has Amnesia, she wakes up with a companion that helps her and joins a village. The village is razed and you learn someone has taken the village leaders Soul essentially, you learn about the stream of consciousness (which people couldn't understand?). When people die they enter a stream of consciousness where they can be brought back because of an artificial Well linking to the stream of consciousness. The Holy Lands used this Well to bring people back infinitely to fight wars for them, before something terrible happened and the land was destroyed. Your goal is to find out how the Land Fell, who the girl is who "killed"? your Village leader and took her soul, what she wants to do with the soul, and also finding out why you can't remember your past (Amnesia is a symptom when a soul is brought back from death, its not that complicated). Outside of that most of the stories are self contained and very easy to follow. If you can't understand any of this idk how people feed themselves tbh. Maybe that's why I can't fathom people liking these dumbed down, plain 2d Souls concepts where dodge and swing is considered the height of combat evolution. Not to mention the amount of memory it takes to complete a game this size to remember every obstacle and find all its goodies with each new ability you get probably puts some.... other people off. Long term memory issues I guess. Anyways, a bit of salt there at the end. The game is amazing, im more upset we don't get more games like this because 90% of the genre has been hijacked with 2d Souls that are the antithesis of a Metroidvania but strangely share the same name.Edit: I should follow this up by stating I was playing on "Normal" difficulty, I had no idea I had done this. I will say though.... I prefer it after trying Advanced, which was the old Standard mode. On Normal you don't take damage from platforming obstacles, so you aren't limited in attempts. This makes platforming very fun and not frustrating. The mobs are the same, but do about 30% less damage, which makes exploring the levels far more fun, especially with contact damage. You can go through all your potions easily on Advanced. Bosses seemed similar, maybe 15% easier or something? Not super noticeable. I think Normal is the best difficulty if you value a highly fun platforming, adventure, exploration, power fantasy concept. It cuts out a lot of frustration and feels much more in line with how Castlevania SotN was balanced or Metroid. Sometimes difficulty just makes it harder to enjoy the games other amazing aspects. I don't really want to have to heal everytime I see a single enemy and some of the platforming aspects would have you giving up considering it takes like 20% of your hp everytime you fail, that means you blow all your healing trying to do one puzzle and now have to go all the way back to a tree and heal. Dark Souls was not good for these genres, we don't need frustration in EVERY game. Keep it chill, just like Castlevania and Metroid did.

_childDocuments_.review: Maps are too big and you can only teleport to major respawn points from another respawn point, otherwise, it costs a consumable. Not sure why exploration is punished with manual/limited backtracking this way. Combat is decent. I like the idea of different weapons with gradually unlocked move sets that you can combine on the fly, except that it doesn't feel very smooth. You are also often forced/encouraged to switch your weapon type and move set when you get a new weapon that has better stats. Difficulty has been low in my 9 hours of playtime. Has contact damage, which I'm not a fan of. Equipment system doesn't seem well designed. With the all of incrementally stronger weapons to find, didn't see the point of upgrading weapons.Boring story and quests that are slow to progress.

_childDocuments_.review: The way this game animates, with your character jerking around when she runs, clashes horribly with the smooth tracking of the foreground and background. The jerking camera combined with the off-tempo movement of the fore/background gave me a huge headache in about 5 minutes, like motion blur on steroids. Combined with totally mediocre combat and schizophrenic design, along with an incomprehensible story and bloated size make this a hard pass for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Well I'm giving this game the thumbs up, I actually don't recommend it. I think it is a good game. But if anyone asked if they should play it I would recommend a dozen games first and Afterimage does rather a lot wrong that drives me insane.Firstly the art: While the game is beautiful and there are scenes that just look fantastic it has that problem of telling a brand new designer to make a box and then slapping their hand when they put way to much effort into it because its just a box. It doesn't need to be that complicated. There were a number of times where I couldn't tell the foreground for the background. Also a side note because I don't know where else to say this: When you have a thing to make it hard to see don't make it eye bleeding purple! Seriously my eyes were hurting after looking at it and I shouldn't ever need to say that about an obscuring texture.Level design: This is probably where the game loses the most points. Being a metrovania I'm sure the thought process was "They should be able to go anywhere right off the bat" well this lead me to having an extremely disjointed play through with often getting lost and confused and having to look up a walkthrough in order to figure out where I was supposed to be going. I somehow sequence broke the game several times. Also at one point the only way to progress was to get an enemy to follow you so you could bounce on its head, this is not obvious in any way.And lastly the story... I couldn't follow any of this. Maybe I'm just getting old and having a harder time following anime-esk plots but I had literally no idea what was going on. ♥♥♥♥ was happening and they were throwing proper nouns at me and I was just baffled. Maybe this was because I did parts out of order, maybe because I wasn't reading the journals, but either way the ending came around and there was a second Renee and then a third one and I don't know how we got there. Also at one point I found a boss and Renee went "You burned down the village didn't you?" to which I honestly didn't know which ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ village she was talking about. After some time I finally realized she meant the village in the tutorial, this was 16 hours after the tutorial, I had no idea we were still trying to figure that out.But my biggest issue with this game is that there is talent and promise in this game and the people who were making it were clearly passionate about it. But the problem is all of that is spread way to thin. The game is twice as large as it really needs to be and that wore out my good will and I was just ready for the game to end before I fought the final boss
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: This game has quickly become one of my favorite Metroidvanias, up there with Ender Lilies and F.I.S.T.. It's not quite on the level of Bloodstained of SOTN, but it's comfortably in the top 10 greats of the genre. I've completed this game once before on Playstation, where it took me about 60 hours to reach 100%. I enjoyed it so much that I also picked it up on Steam and started playing a few days ago, intending to just to kill a little time while I waited for another game I pre-ordered to go live. It's a testament to this game's quality that I ended up getting thoroughly hooked yet again and had to perfect complete it a second time before putting it down.Just two bits of information for anyone who wants to get the most out of this game. After starting a new game, it gives you a choice of difficulty between normal and advanced mode. Advanced is the difficulty the game originally launched with and is the one I would recommend. Normal is basically easy mode and gives you way too much leeway to face tank damage rather than properly evading it, as well eliminating damage from most environmental traps. This game is definitely a lesser experience without it's challenge, so I highly recommend the Advanced difficulty. My second bit of info is that this game seems to lack any kind of baked in dead zones for analogue sticks. I noticed this on the Playstation version as well, and it seems that even the slightest imperfection in your sticks will cause the main character to frequently turn around during the middle of combos. There are options on Steam to manually force dead zones as well as an option in-game to play with the digital pad instead, so go with whichever works best for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a hard game to review. It's in a spot of being very close to greatness, but at the same its issues make it so it feels like a 7/10 game.On the positive side, the map is massive, environement and enemy diversity is pretty nice, as well as pretty nice player expression with a few different weapons with several special moves each. Overall, it plays pretty nice, combat is fluid, platforming is very satisfying and has many interesting challenges for extra items.Unfortunately, there's issues that makes the progression feel kind of annoying, there's a lot of moments where you need to do one thing to be able to progress and it can be annoying to find out what it is. The game has a quest log that can help sometimes, but on a lot of quests it doesn't even remind you where the dialog line told you to go. Speaking of dialog, maybe it's the cultural divide, but the story felt quite confusing and poorly told. After achieving the true ending of the game, I still have no idea of the role some of the characters played in the story.The map also abuses one way gates way too much, and the main path is easily confused with the myriad of side paths (the fact that there's so many is a positive in my book), which considering you need a healthy economy to even be able to teleport to the save points is a questionable decision. I do not understand what compelled them to lock the save point to save point teleport to only one per area, but it really doesn't work well on such a massive map.Bosses are one of the most dissapointing areas of the game, most bosses were a first try for me without even using consumables, a decision I made early on to increase the challenge for myself.Afterimage is a game I recommend, but with caution, this is something you should only play if you've already gone through every great metroidvania in existance. If it did a lot of things a bit better it could be amazing, but alas, it falls in the "just ok" category.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a game I recommend with a few caveats. The gameplay is quite good, and the art is fantastic. The RPG elements really make a difference, and I enjoyed building a min maxed crit build. Those things carried the game for me. That being said, the story is virtually nonsensical. I've played my fair share of translated games, but Afterimage by far has the worst translations/plot of anything I have played. It is akin to From's take on storytelling but somehow even more vague. The map is LARGE. Large almost to the point of being annoying. Thank god for resting potions (lets you travel betweens confluences).The boss fights are hit and miss. They have some really cool designs but some of them are borderline bad with their execution. If you're looking for the tight back and forth of a souls game or bosses designed with the ability to no hit them, you may want to look elsewhere. The majority of the bosses I simply overpowered through optimization of gear/talents (plus air sword/smash down combo is op). With all the negatives out of the way, I still recommend the game. It's a solid metroidvania that has a ton of heart put into it and loads of content.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I like a metroidvania, but not this one. After only one hour I'm giving up on it - the maps are huge, and mostly empty, so it's just really *boring* to navigate. The visuals are often confusing (some lines look like platforms and are not, other very similar looking lines are slopes you can jump onto and walk up). The combat so far is essentially just "duck near a monster and hit attack repeatedly" except for one monster that killed me from full health with only appearing to hit me one time (it's possible that its "teleport" action was an attack too, but if so there was no visual indication of this and I didn't notice taking damage).At no point in finding all these things to complain about did I feel like I was having fun.Other reviewers seem to be into the visuals, but I prefer clear visuals over pretty.An hour in I didn't really have any sense of story or goals at all; I got some sort of side quest where the description was like "take a thing to the right place for it" with no indication of what that right place would be or how I would find or or how I would complete the quest if I got there. I found various "badges" that seem to think they are story but they're more just kind of jumbled messes of words.

It looks pretty enough, and you can tell that's where they focused the bulk of the design immediately upon playing it. Under the hood, it's barely held together. You can stumble over easy to replicate glitches that benefit you by  man, it's sad.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Deserves to stand at the top of its genre, right below HK, Ori, and the classics. The visuals are wonderful; screenshots do not do the animated background justice. The controls and combat are absolutely BRILLIANT, especially when you master cancelling attacks into movement and vice versa. The world is ENORMOUS, with many areas being completely optional but not without substance. It gets away with this by having several endings that all require exploring different areas to collect different key items and abilities. For genre enthusiasts, the abilities themselves are not terribly original, but they are probably the best versions of familiar powers (especially the foot dive). The end kinda drags because of how involved getting all the endings is, but it is ultimately satisfying and doesn't detract from the thrill of the early and mid-game. Being Chinese in origin, there are some translation issues, but it's not too bad. The English voice-acting helps keep it engaging.It's a truly great game that I put in my list of top 10 metroidvanias of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvania available, the maps are huge, graphics looks great, game play is also really solid, there are some annoying mechanics, like some enemies have like higher contact damage than their actual attack or that thing that turns you to a bubble when you hit an environmental hazard, then spawns you into very annoying situations, but overall i would gladly recommend it to people that enjoy this type of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: The good things about this game first: It looks beautiful.Unfortunately, the good things end there. The game has almost no narrative structure. Half the time you don't know where you have to go next. Your character and that annoying sidekick always pretend to know the dude you are looking for or at least know where he/she/it is but still don't mark it on your map. The story being a complete cluster♥♥♥♥ doesn't help.The game world is huge. That's theoretically a good thing but the amount of backtracking you have to do here is from another world. You can only port between certain locations for free while the other available options cost a consumable item. That combined with constantly feeling lost turned it into an unenjoyable experience.The so called talent system feels like it's not doing anything. The weapon skills are either completely obnoxious to use in a fight or simply do not have any additional effect worth mentioning. You can just spam attack all game anyway. Oh and dodge not having an immunity frame was probably the dumbest decision I've seen in a while.So before wasting your time here, I recommend getting Bloodstained or Sundered.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: It's an awesome metroidvania with a lot of content and variety of enemies, combat is very fun too, art style and music are both great and it has pretty decent replayability with the Trial of Soul content.Not everything is perfect, some enemies could have been more fun to fight (including some bosses) but the good definitely outweighs the bad
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game. With a bad map system and a giant map you end up running circles frequently. When you end up fighting a boss the respawn point is mostly 5minutes away from the boss itself so dying requires you running all the way back. All the weapons feel the same with just a difference in range/speed. The ability tree isn't that interesting. Most of them either give % bonus. (Like % physical damage reduction) or you get an additional attack which doesn't add much. (Like a dash attack for only the scythe. But you're just as good to simply run up to the enemy and do a normal attack.)Get the game on sale if you really want it.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely fun metroidvania, there are a few rough parts, but once you get the hang of it it's one of the best, if not the best, "new" games I've played this year. Especially for the price point. It has a massive world, and while you may get lost once or twice, it flows and directs you fairly well. Combat is completely serviceable and I never felt annoyed by it, extremely boilerplate but at the same time, that's sorta what I want. It doesn't try to reinvent the wheel, it just refines what's there. Extremely good art, and the soundtrack has some very good standout tracks, others are a bit plain.The only minor complaint I have is once you get to the end of the game, you sorta hit this power peak and you still have a few hours left to go where you already have the best equipment so you just go through the motions of "okay now where do I go to access X".  Sometimes the translation has a few typos, and the world itself is more interesting than the main plot at times. Overall I enjoyed my time with it immensely, and I basically belted it out over the course of a week, looking forward to playing it when I left for work. I recommend it thoroughly to anyone who's a fan of metriodvanias and can look past a little bit of jank starting out until you adapt to some of the controls. Fun game
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: At the time I write this review, I've only played 3.5 hours.I like the game so far, the gameplay feels good, but it has been so easy, that is worrisome that the whole game will be a breeze.The soundtrack is so boring, that I can't feel attached to the game. Is not bad (as music is very subjective), but is so lackluster, that is a bit hard to play the game, even while the gameplay itself is fun for me.This game is obviously so inspired on Castlevania, that is surprising that the developers thought on taking on of the strongest aspect of the series and throw it into the trash can, like if that would make the game better.I plan on finishing the game, but I can already tell is not going to be a memorable experience.One last note: Paid fast travel? REALLY??

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better metroidvania out there. The visual is beautiful, the music is great, and the combat is fun where you can use 2 out of 6 types of weapons available. The inputs are interesting since there are a few "weapon skills" that needed directional input to use it. The map is quite big but is not that bad to travel around since you can easily spam horizontal dash, and super dash and dive for vertical movements. Its not perfect thoThe main thing that bothers me immediately is the "Normal" difficulty is pretty much "Easy" mode since the damage you take is very very low. If you want any kind of challenge, play it in "Advance" difficulty. But even then the game is pretty generous with the healing.The game progression is confusing. The map is pretty open, you can easily go to areas where you're not supposed to be yet with enemies much higher level than you. So it doesn't only block you with unlockable skills like other metroidvanias, it will also do a stats check with those enemies.The last thing is this game has elemental damage stuff, but they dont really explain to you the basics like if they do extra damage or what. I was just brute forcing my way through the game with raw damages.But still, its a solid metroidvania

_childDocuments_.review: The lack of minimap combined with one way gates and having to pay to teleport (You can technically teleport for free from main nodes, but when you are 60 seconds away from any teleport point, much less the main node...)While you can technically buy the teleport item, it is not cost efficient. Combine the lack of a minimap with the difficulty of moving the camera around (you can only move the camera in some locations and really only up/down) and the kill points that are sometimes a bit too large... it can make some of the platforming extra annoying. Especially when you are basically locked out of future areas if you can't make a rather precise jump over some spikes.Oh, and while it is nice that you don't just instantly die (you only take damage under specific situations), the teleport to location can be weird. Sometimes I'll teleport just a few steps away from the trap. Sometimes I am teleported all the way to the start. Even weirder is the one time I was teleported to the end of the puzzle?  Oh, and being teleported will trigger every mechanism in your path (breaking platforms, moving walls, etc.)Oh, and as extra salt on the wound, some areas don't have maps at all and will basically choose a somewhat random (random as in no discernible reason) part of the map as your location.The marking system is also really annoying on controller. No wrap around, so if you want the last item, you can be clicking for a while. No way to control with the joysticks/d-pads that I found (since that will move the cursor instead).There are some other oddities with controller where the controller might click under/through a menu or click everything on the screen.You also have platforms that honestly aren't that intuitive since if you are slightly off, you can't go through and it isn't always obvious unless you really scour the map.Also, why is the collectible scanner basically one of the last items you get?

_childDocuments_.review: Frustrating Exploration and Unclear Direction in AfterimageAfterimage had a lot of potential. The hand-drawn art style is gorgeous, and the combat feels decent once you get the hang of it. However, several issues drag the experience down.Lost in the Labyrinth: Missing Minimap is a Major Miss: Forget the convenience of a minimap. Afterimage expects you to decipher its labyrinthine world with only a basic map that offers little to no guidance. Prepare to spend a lot of time wandering in circles, retracing your steps, and desperately wishing for a hint of where to go next.Confusing Level Design: The environments are beautiful, but they often lack clear signposting for progression. I spent a lot of time wandering around, unsure where to go next. Backtracking is a core part of Metroidvanias, but Afterimage makes it feel like a chore without better direction.Cryptic Storytelling: The story throws references and lore at you without much context. If you haven't played other games in the series (if there are any), you'll be left confused about what's happening and who these characters are. Other Issues:Quest System Is More Obnoxious Than Helpful: The quest system, if you can call it that, throws cryptic objectives your way without any context. Good luck figuring out what exactly you need to do or where to find that next elusive upgrade.Hidden UI Elements: The XP bar is particularly sneaky and took me way too long to find.Final Verdict: 4.5/10If you're a patient explorer who loves piecing together cryptic narratives, Afterimage might hold some charm. But for those who prefer a more focused and user-friendly experience, this one might leave you feeling lost and frustrated.Consider this review helpful if:You value clear level design and intuitive exploration.You prefer stories that are easy to follow without needing prior knowledge.I would recommend checking out some gameplay videos or reviews before diving into Afterimage. It's not a bad game by any means, but be prepared for some significant roadblocks along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic and very large, running me about 27 hours without really doing 100% stuff, Metroidvania that lives pretty much entirely on its own merits, with references being VERY sparse (though the Hollow Knight bench and lamp will always make me smile). The story is incredibly intriguing if a little clumsy at times, the translation has almost no issues outside of backer reward messages sometimes being incomprehensible which is a genuinely grand feat, the voice direction is absolutely stellar in English and presumably Japanese and Chinese as well, the 6 different weapon types and countless different ways to do combat are all interesting and only become better and better as you get unique passives into the late game, the art direction is fan-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-tastic and the music direction is pretty nice too. I think the absolute worst thing you could say about this game is that the post-game is called NG+ and in minor mechanic spoilers  but there's other mechanics like the Afterimage system that mostly brush up on that, being the games Badges or Charms or what have you. There's also some spells that straight up don't tell you what they do and just give you a name, but I only encountered one (Phantom) that really made me scratch my head on what it actually did. But when those are the worst things you can say about the game, that's at most 0.5 off a score if you'd wanna be mean about it.The talent tree is also swinging for 50/50 as on one hand the unique skills you can unlock through it all give each weapon significantly both more personality and utility, especially in the case of the Whip which has probably one of the most simple but fun Mastery bonuses... but there's also a lot of upgrades that are just fodder like "+1% resistance/damage with an element" mixed in right before really good ♥♥♥♥ like "gives you +5 MP when an end-game total is like 50-60" or crit-chance. I get why the devs did it, I ended up using a relatively midgame Spell for pretty much the entire game once I got it as it just blew everything else out of the water damage-wise, but man it was a weird feeling.For what little it's worth since I'm not Metroidvania Review member or known streamer or really anyone, overall if I had to give the game a score it'd very easily be a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Treat this as a neutral score.Have fun finding yourself in this humongous world without any idea what to do next. The game excels at NOT holding your hand, even with the basics of just progressing with the main story. I was under the impression that metroidvanias reward the player for curiosity and backtracking when it comes to the exploration, resulting in boosting stats and finding better items, but apparently with Afterimage you’ll have to be traversing this vast world and explore every nook and cranny just to find each small step allowing you to progress. This is undoubtedly the worst aspect of this game, because the pacing issues can easily restrain you from continuing playing, as it is so easy to get filled with frustration and start bashing your head against the wall – multiple guides and Reddit posts are your best friend here.If you have the patience though, you’ll be rewarded for your efforts, because apart from the aforementioned issue it’s a glorious game – the world and atmosphere are gorgeous, the player has vast options for character development that fits their playstyle best and the mechanics allow for very tight and satisfying gameplay. The game is also surprisingly rich with content, lasting about 30h if you know what to do and where to go.Overall, it’s good, but horrendously confusing – just don’t expect to always know what the hell’s going on.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a solid metroidvania. So far what I can say is the combat is fun, the bosses are great, and the map is HUGE. Lots of optional stuff as well. The game does a great job rewarding you for exploring, and while there is a bit of item bloat, its not like castlevania SOTN where every item is worse than the one you already have. There is a ton of backtracking, multiple different paths to take (although some of the early ones are really high level so you get one shot lol).Its not all that challenging, I have run into 1 boss that took multiple attempts, but so far all the enemies are designed fairly so cant complain.It doesn't do anything really unique or groundbreaking, but its just a really solid entry, The art and visuals are some of the best we have seen in the genre in the past year, soundtrack is good but not amazing.For full price I would say go ahead and buy if you are craving a fairly standard metroidvania experience, but if you want something groudbreaking, probably wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a solid game with a great aesthetic that shows more of what an action adventure metroidvania can be. The game feels more punishing more than it does difficult. If you like exploring, stretching your platforming skills and recognizing boss tells, patterns and proper responses then give this game a try. Exploring is a delight; One of the smaller aspects that you probably won't notice is that there aren't any loading screens between rooms or areas. I can't recall games that have done this... What they do isn't even revolutionary; just filling the transition area with something like clouds to help with the tileset transition. So when you're running around you can really easily lose track of time.  If you've played other metroidvania games you sort of know what to expect when it comes to exploration powerups. If you're creative with your movement you can get to harder areas sooner than you're supposed to, resulting in quite the adventure. Othertimes, you'll end up coming across paths that you can't access so be sure to open your map and drop a pin. It all really does feel standard fare when it comes to exploration. Combat is enjoyable, each of the 6 weapon types has a set of input actions that you can use for situational attacks; these range from chasers where you dash after them, Anti-air, sweeps and plunging attacks. Then there's really simple magic; equip the spell you want and push a button. It's good for bursting an enemy down but isn't meannt for regular combat. The bosses ramp up in difficulty and you're going to feel like you aren't progressing; but overcoming those roadblocks is what is fun. If you're losing too often, take a step back and learn how they talk. Afterimage has a superbly strong foundation that has room to grow. Exploring the world is fun to explore; each area having a track that sets the mood. If you're creative you can find solutions to reach new heights. Bosses air more on the punishing side but they're all fairly readable if you take the time. You probably noticed I didn't mention story; that's because it is lightly told through items and character dialogue; since it's a kickstarter game a lot of potential lore items are replaced with supporter inserted text. I respect them doing it but it does take away from the world in the slightest way. Though the most important part is in the first hour or so, setting the tone of "You will die, you will come back, and it is you who will decide when you are broken."

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for more than 20 hours. It may seem interesting at first. Beautiful vistas, different environmental. And it is not a bad game. But its flaws overcome its positives.Positives:- Different weapons and different moves for each one of them. Weapons are the core gameplay.- Great variety of settings, enormous map.- Variety of enemies, some of them with interesting attacks. - Gentle learning curve.- Fluidity of movement. Sadly, all these pros became cons in an unfortunate turn of events.Negatives:- Incomprehensible story.- Too many enemies, items and foods, so many that they require in-game study, consulting guides and wikias to understand them, subtracting a lot of immersion. - Many items are not useful too. There are dozens of weapons, but you always tend to use the most powerful ones. So the study required for understanding the inventory system is even less satisfying. - The map is simply gigantic. Expect more that double the amount of backtracking that a standard metroidvania. It’s too much.- In some parts, expecially during some bosses, the difficulties spikes a lot, making them unfair with attacks that cover almost all the screen. That gave me Hollow Knight vibes, not in a good sense. - When you finally acquire some abilities to access previously locked areas, there is often a small corridor with a chest that contains a consumable. What a disappointment. In general, I'm disappointed. I'm sorry because this is a potentially great Metroidvania but the difficulty spikes, the gigantic map, terrible story, the generic enemies’ aesthetics and the grind limit its potential.At the tenth difficulty spike from a boss, I decided to not finish it. I was bored and frustrated.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Metroidvania game overall, not a perfect game, but a solid 8.5/10.Pros - Large world to explore, lot of secrets to find, combat feels responsive, significant variations in weapons and how they work gives you a variety of playstyles to fit your own preference. Despite the huge world, the map is very easy to mark for inaccessible areas locked by clear future skills.Cons - With so many secrets and tiny little areas that are locked by progression abilities, the problem is that a lot of the secrets are basically worthless items or tiny amounts of the currency, its impossible to tell which ones are actually impactful upgrades, so you can waste a LOT of time clearing old marked secrets and not getting anything worthwhile. The biggest con is that the leveling system is very schizophrenic, with upgrades locked arbitrarily behind certain levels and each individual weapon having their own upgrade path means that you'll reach several points where there's nothing to actually spend your level up points on that actually gives you a buff until you hit the next unlock point, and after about level 60, you are 100% fully upgraded as strong as you will be in your chosen playstyle, with all further level ups just filling out other weapon skills that you probably aren't even using.Still, overall, solid game, would be interested in seeing more from this developer.

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially enjoying this one, but after a while the complete aimlessness got to me. There's next to no guidance on where you're supposed to be going next, and the map is huge and riddled with dead ends and skill gates. That's obviously standard for a Metroidvania but this Afterimage takes it to the absolute extreme.Some people will get a kick out of how open-ended progress is in this game, but I just found it a complete slog. Constantly backtracking through huge portions of the map trying to find a new route I can progress down, using a map that's way too light on info, only to still run into dead end after dead end just wasn't fun for me. There's a time when I might have enjoyed that sort of meticulous exploration, but these days I just don't have the time or the patience that this game demands of me.

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus you have no clue where to go, where you  go and what you  actually do. You are lost - at all times. And not in the fun-kinda-way. You are literally 100%ing the game, just to search for what you actually have to do next or how you get anywhere. It's just frustrating.Otherwise it's the most vanilla metroid-vania with being unremarkable in every other aspect and slightly below average combat, since it feels a bit clunky and unfinished. Can't dodge through enemies, can't dodge through attacks and there is "contact damage" on top. Everything together makes for a very stiff feeling combat.edit: After finding that one elevator I missed, which blends into the environment on that freaking huge map, I could finally progress. So, after "finishing" the first of like 10 endings, some of which require ng+ and post game and what not, I still can't recommend it.You just reach other variations of the same bland and uninspired map over and over again.The game is way too huge with way too many dead ends and it's obscure beyond any reasonable degree. You get A LOT of quest items and have no clue why or what they are for. You get a key like 10 hours after finding the door for it, so have fun remembering that. There are barriers all over the world you can't get past. How to unlock those? Well, why would the game want you to know that?The gameplay never evolves. You unlock some skills that are mostly bad or require specific weapon canceling techniques to be useful to avoid the awful animation lock. The biggest gripe is that you have contact damage and no way to void many of the full screen boss attacks since you don't have an invincible dash, requiring you to "tank" those and spam healing potions or out level the boss.There is sadly barely any skill involved due to that. You have such small damage windows, it's not feasible otherwise. The contact damage is so dumb, if you want to attack some bosses with some special moves or daggers, you actually damage yourself in the process.I read somewhere that you do acquire an invincible dash at some point, but apparently not before finishing the game, so what's the point? Just reading up on what you need to do and with who to talk to get more endings is simply asinine. The story is also dull as hell and they tried their hardest to not make it interesting, relying solely on the gimmick of making everything obscure and fill in some (not all) pages in the later endings and story tidbits to provide "answers", but since you couldn't follow anyway, you never had any questions to begin with, so for the majority of the game it's just nonsensical drivel to you.

_childDocuments_.review: A quite enjoyable, and beautifully crafted metroidvania-style game. The areas are each wonderfully designed, giving each their own feel and uniqueness instead of the same scenery over and over. Speaking of levels though, the game is pretty massive. Areas are big, and with save points spread out there can be quite a bit of back-tracking if you die. Items to teleport back to previous areas are also limited at first, so there is a bit of managing when to return and when to keep pressing on. But I never had an issue of running out myself.The gameplay is customizable, with having 2 weapons equipped at all times that you can use to pull off some amazing combos. Your traits also help specialize your character into different weapons, unlocking new skills and the like, though the points for these are fairly easy to get so there is little worry about going one route, only to wish you had trained a different weapon later. As with any metroidvania game, you'll get your skills like double jump and all as you progress, meaning you will have to backtrack through levels sometimes multiple times if you want to get items and equipment to help you push forward.The story, for this style of game, feels pretty well done compared to some others that focus more on gameplay and less on dialogue with NPCs. There are quite a number of people you will meet, offering quests or just speaking with them in different locations, each having their own story to tell.All in all, a great game of the genre, and pretty highly recommended.
