_childDocuments_.review: Alright I beat this game, got all achievements, then beat it again for fun, and I have to say it's really great.Good visuals, good level design, lots of traversal abilities, a lot of areas with a ton of enemy types per area and compared to other Metroidvanias it's at least twice as long with twice as much content.Combat is quick and fluid and you can equip 2 main weapons at a time and a magic weapon as well. All weapon types are useful and each have their own sets of abilities, varieties and uses. Personally I like having either the katana (blade) or a scythe paired with a greatsword. Katana abilities have long reach and scythe abilities have good short range damage and debuff application, while the greatswords allow me to parry and counterattack as well as dish out a big chunk of damage at a time.Level design is great and you'll find yourself coming back to areas whenever you unlock a new traversal ability to find secrets or reach items you couldn't reach before, classic Metroidvania action. Each area looks unique and has its own set of enemies and traversal challenges. Though I do have to say, it may have a little too many forests and fire zones (spoiler alert).Enemies are numerous and diverse and I love that each zone has unique enemies with new attacks that you need to learn... but who the hell thought spider monkeys was a good idea? lolStory may be a bit generic but I do love the several plot twists. I also love how NG+ is a separate game mode and unlocks new levels, characters, bosses and story elements as well as affect/alter the base game map.Art style is good and interesting, and it's a nice change from the usual dark themed metroidvanias. This one is colorful, cheerful and beautiful.Music is superb. Early game music is cheerful and laid back, while late game music is powerful and encouraging. Never got bored or annoyed of the music, and in fact I downloaded some of the OSTs to listen to them in my car.All in all for all Metroidvania fans, this is a must try at least.

If you're like me and you just appreciate running around, finding little secrets and fighting bosses in between, then this game is absolutely for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game with all achievements. Afterimage is a surprising gem of the metroidvania genre with a very large map to explore and traverse, and a diverse combat choice for players. It's an astounding recommend for fans of the genre, but I can imagine many new to the genre would feel a bit overwhelmed by the map size and not-too-stellar story. The game follows rpg system of power progression without boss level scaling so balancing can be weird: early to mid game you can get 2 or 3 shots by a random boss or mob in an unsuspecting area, but by the end game you can face tank most bosses with the stats-stealing dagger. Ofc, that doesn't take away much of my enjoyment with the game, so a recommend regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful visuals & soundtrack, however the game heavily dependent on jumping and dashingI played with a keyboard and mouse and I expected that my character would dash only when I pressed the dash button, but it seems to activates on it's own when jumping left or right direction. Since this game heavily uses the dash option to get to platforms; this dysfunction is makes the game less enjoyable and quite tedious.I think this is a wonderful game, but I think it needs more polishing to make the controls more responsive and easier to use.Pros:+ Beautiful artwork, characters, environment, animation+ Wonderful instrumental soundtrack+ Slow story build+ Relaxed paceCons:- Getting hit freezes your character and knocks her back, which gets to be pretty annoying. You must wait to land before starting to move again (breaks immersion)- Double jump is unlocked far into the game, which requires repeating content to get everything- Unable to zoom in or out of talent tree, difficult to see what options are available- Scroll and panning the talent tree view is a challenge, you bounce from one item to next- The dash button seems to activate whenever you jump on its own, making it much harder to control where your character goes.- No preset keyboard layout for ASWD + Mouse. (Only joy stick or keyboard arrow keys), you can remap keys though- Treasure rewards are given out long before they are usable. I got a scroll that unlocks a talent +20 levels before I can actually use it.

_childDocuments_.review: A metroidvania with a huge map, fun combat controls and very difficult boss fights. Closer to newer Castlevania style gameplay (Symphony of the Night, Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night) in terms of speed.There are 6 different weapon types to play with: sword, great sword, scythe, whip, dual blades, and katana. Each weapon have their own move sets. What makes the combat fun is that you can equip 2 weapons at a time and can use either of them at any point of attack. You can cancel a sword normal string on the ground into a dual blade rising attack into a sword dive attack. You also have a subweapon, which is the magic attack that uses mana and does various things and is relatively straight forward. I do think the bigger appeal is the weapon system.There is a skill tree that lets you increase your stats and learn new moves for weapons.The map in this game is ginormous. They really do want you to explore in this game. I got to a point in the game where I probably explored like 70% of the game before I got another progression tool. You will get lost. You will probably refer to a guide of some sort if you want to try to find everything.The boss fights are very difficult in this game. A lot of pattern recognition and memorization in this game. You will die a lot. Some of the fights might seem unfair due do huge hitboxes and what seems to be undodgeable attacks. They really want you to learn and not be in places you shouldn't put yourself into.There are two difficulties. Normal and Advance. Advance is the default difficult and the intended way to play the game. Normal was added later and significantly lowers the difficult down to the point where you can pretty much face tank all the boss fights. I guess they added Normal just for people that want to enjoy the exploration from how hard the boss fights are.There is a mode where you can fight bosses as much as you want. Good for learn boss patterns and doing challenges such as going for damageless attempts.The music is alright, very setting the tone of the area. Nothing upbeat or high energy/tempo.I'm sure the story is good, I kind of spaced out during the dialogue. I find it a bit difficult to follow a story where there is too huge of a gap from story point to story point from all the exploration.Some cons/nitpicks:-There is no mini-map. I find myself opening the map like 2 or 3 times a minute just to figure out my location.-Besides telling you how many items you acquired out of the total items in the area, there is no way for you to know what items you are missing in the area. Have to check pretty much every point.-I don't recall seeing a status screen so it is a bit difficult to keep track of your stats when trying to do certain armor/accessory combos-This game has contact damage. Doesn't bug me as much but some people are turned off by it-Outside of using teleport save spots, warping is not free in this game. You need a specific item to warp freely, which you can buy.-Money is somewhat finite in this game. There are nodes that will give you a certain amount but outside of that you need to sell materials for money.-Most likely will need a guide for full completion.This game will probably run you somewhere between 20-40 hours depending on what you want to achieve. I had a good time with this game. It is very fun. People that are hardcore into boss fighting will fight a lot of replay-ability from learning and doing damageless attempts.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm always looking for good Metroidvania games, but I think this developer overshot challenging and went straight to punishing. Mostly, I'm annoyed with the "dash/evade" function. Notice it isn't the "dodge" function. I don't know why they went through the trouble of adding depth to the background. If you're going to put everything on the same layer. Touching an enemy that isn't attacking damages. You. Trying to dodge past an enemy damage is you. Making it so that you have to dash away from the enemy instead of past the enemy makes it more frustrating because you have to go back and you only dash a certain distance so trying to make it back in the same way to get a strike in can easily be thrown off so dashing back means that you're likely to be hit by the enemy anyway. This gets particularly bad when you get cornered by low ceilings and a bunch of enemies so you don't have a chance to get out of it. Navigation is another issue as well. No maps or directions. No guidance of any kind that might indicate where you might need to go. You have to feel around in this maze and try to remember where you went , but the whole layout is a jumbled mess.It's a nice start, but it really needs a lot more polishing before I can give this a better rating.

_childDocuments_.review: Way more content than expected. I went in to the game expecting it to be kind of bad. The art looks pretty, but from appearance alone the combat looks boring.  And it started off feeling that way. But the further I progress, the more difficult and faster the bosses and enemies are becoming. While that might not be a plus for some people, there are consumable health potions that make most of the fights really easy, on top of the estus flask style consumable. The characters are cute, and it's all voiced dialog. The story is kind of reminiscent of a JRPG though, which might be good for some people, but personally it makes me feel like skipping the dialog frequently. Yet I am immersed enough in it to read the little lore bits scattered throughout the world. Overall I'd say it's an amazing game, and the only thing really holding it back from being one of my favourites is how long the pacing is slow, and the music. The music isn't bad. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and will definitely replay it in the future. I did 100% it and that took about 47.5 hours (with the help of some guides and the occasional Google search). Some people are talking about the map being too large or the game too long, but I consider both of those to be pluses in my book.If you like Metriodvania games with RPG elements then I wholeheartedly recommend this game. If you don't like Hollow Knight style platforming, then you might want to stay way. By that I mean when you need to pogo off of hazards, do wall climbs while avoiding spikes, or dash/jump through narrow spike-filled openings. I could do without most of it myself, but I didn't find most of the platforming in this to be onerous. No section took more than a couple of minutes worth of retries to get passed. Nothing as rough as the White Palace in general, let alone the Path of Pain, from Hollow Knight.Of the similar games I really enjoy, and often replay, I would order the list from best to worst (well really more like great to good) like this:Bloodstained: Ritual of the NightASTLIBRA RevisionDust: An Elysian TailVigil: The Longest NightHollow KnightAfterimageThe Vagrant8Doors: Arum's Afterlife AdventureMinoriaENDER LILIESBefore list a few pros and cons, let me say that I think some of the cons listed in other reviews have been address or mitigated by the last patch that came out. For example, they added NPC markers to the map that help out quite a bit with quests.I really enjoyed the combat and the abilities available. They are mostly abilities you will have seen in other similar games.The voice acting was good and the story was decent, though confusing early on.Some may consider it a con, but I like how you could access a good portion of the world/map part way into the game. It never forces you into a linear path, though that does leave it up to you to figure out where you need to go sometimes. If you enjoy exploring a whole map, then you will have no trouble finding where you need to go on your own. I don't enjoy pixel graphics, so I really like the art style of games like this. My only complaint is that the main character, Renee, seems to be the most pixel-like of any sprite in the game. It was kind of jarring at times how bad she looked compared to the environment and enemies.There were too many accessories. I didn't use most of them and sorting through them to find what was useful was a bit of a chore.The English translation needs some work. It detracted from what was a decent story.This may be more of a preference, but I didn't care for the mechanic of taking damage from touching enemies. It would have bothered me less if you didn't take damage for touching enemies during weapon skills. It limited the viability of some skills quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great Metroidvania. The maps are huge. Plenty of bosses with a wide variety in design and attacks. There's plenty of challenging platforming if you want to get some items early, but you could get abilities later that make it much easier. Combat allows you to use 2 out of like 6 weapon types at a time so I suggest concentrating on 2 of your favourites. However, the map only shows Save Points so if you come across things you cannot reach yet, you'll have to mark it manually on the map. But eventually it'll become second nature so it doesn't become annoying.My only complaint is that directions for quests are vague so you'll probably stumble onto many of your objectives accidentally. Also, because of that and the fact areas have multiple entrances, you could get story beats out of order and become confused about what is happening.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this. It doesn't really hand-hold, which is a little uncomfortable at first, but IMO adds to the experience as the game progresses. Where to go next is very non-linear and up to the player, with many later areas softly difficulty-gated rather than ability gated and the game really encourages exploration of the huge map. While there isn't often an explicit direction given regarding progression, I never felt it was unfair, and it feels good working out the clues rather than having the answer given on a plate. The way there are almost always multiple possible progression routes up until right near the end of the game make it uncommon to get properly stuck.Towards the end I did look at a guide for one thing progression-wise, but it turned out there was a fairly obvious suggestion by one of the characters in-game which I had forgotten about because it happened quite a bit earlier. This sort of suggestion is a fairly common thing in the game, a character or text will tell about something in passing and then at some point you can to go and have an investigate - I really like it for the most part as it feels like you have a lot more agency than if they had just put a quest marker where you need to go.The game has a lot of lore, and this is presented in a very non-linear manner which along with the fairly extreme oddness of the world can be quite confusing, but the world seems well thought out and coherent which makes it quite fun to figure out. After completing the game I watched a video on the lore, and it's really very interesting.Combat-wise I found the game initially fairly simple - for the most part it's melee only, there are spells but they didn't ever seem that useful. As the skill tree opens up you get a lot more variety in the melee though, with some of the advanced techniques adding ranged attacks. Unfortunately the later techniques are sometimes very different to the initial weapon style, so you need to spec quite a bit into a given tree to properly see what a weapon type is like. For example, the blade (katana-ish) weapon is initially a very short range small hit-box weapon, but one of the later skills is a ranged field of effect attack, which completely transforms the play-style. This means in the early game everything feels very similar just with different ranges, speeds, and damages, but later on everything is quite different and it's a bit of luck whether the things you've initially specced into are good or not - it's possible in the end to spec into everything with points to spare but not really more than two or three in the midgame.I mostly stuck to the dual blades weapon, which are probably the shortest fastest weapon, because they add a lot of mobility and DPS, and was pleased as the later techniques only add to that with spinning attack-double-jumps which do huge damage and seem great against bosses, but I tried some of the others later on and they seem varied and interesting. I think there may be balance issues though as some people have complained of a difficulty spike, which I didn't find at all (and i'm fairly bad at this sort of thing) so I imagine that's probably down to either weapon choice or the soft difficulty-gating of some areas.Overall, I'd recommend this to anyone who likes complex metroidvanias with a more player-driven and non-linear feeling to the progression. I haven't played many games like this but I think this is one of my favourites in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to like this game, i did, i got it from someone as a gift and this game looks amazing, the art is fresh and different and that's about it...The game tries a lot but fail in almost every single aspect:The combat is boring, enemies do contact damage, and if you ever played a 2D game you know how annoying and cheap this is. Most enemies can be stun locked by your basic attacks, and ranged enemies projectiles can be reflected but does chip damage back so it's just not satisfying. The boss battles are just boring, the bosses have super armor and do not react to you at all, they have 3 to 5 attacks and just rotate between them very predictably.The songs and sounds are very basic, i just played the game for almost 4 hours and closed it now to write this and i can't remember them for the life of me, not memorable at all.The controls are ok, very responsive, as expected of a 2D game, i've played it on a 360 controller and its just ok, on K&M tho? you have to remap it to WASD if you have any self respect, the game itself advises you to use a controller because playing on K&M is just straight up bad.You have unlocks to upgrade your movement but nothing groundbreaker, its more of the same from every metroidvania you've seen a thousand times, double jump, dash, etc.It has a skill tree and levels, but the game did NOT need any of it, to be honest, removing the skill tree and levels just doesn't change anything about the game...the skills are not worth it as most are just "+2% attack", "3% crit chance" if even that much. very basic and most you wont even feel in combat...the "weapon skills" are the worst by far, instead of just having these unlocked from the beginning, you only have the basic attack...that's it...want more? a combo? (no combos at all, not even in the skill tree), hitting below or above you? the VERY BASIC of metroidvania? go grind a little to unlock a skill and forget about combos or actual special skills.The game has armour and magic, the magic is so bad i wont even comment on it...the armour tho? SO MUCH detail for the armour portrait on the menu, but NO ARMOUR CHANGE IN-CHARACTER WHATSOEVER! this is atrocious.but now for the main problem and why i stopped playing and came here to write: THE MAP.This game's map is the worst thing to ever happen to a metroidvania, you don't ever know where are you going, for what purpose and if you even are going to reach something!THE AMOUNT OF TIMES I WALKED FOR MINUTES TO BE MET BY A LOCKED DOOR IS JUST ASTOUNDING FOR 4 HOURS OF GAMEPLAY OMG!i have 14 quests on my quest log and i have NO IDEA what im supposed to do in ANY of them! no markers, no descriptions, no bosses, just locked doors and corridors leading to NOTHING!!I've found npcs on the world asking for items and none of them give me at least a tip to where to find the item, the only quest i've completed so far was from a humanoid cat that needed me to kill a boss immediately behind him, and that's IT, i walked and walked and jumped more than i ever jumped in a game ever in my life, but i have no idea where i was or why i was even going. most quest npcs just repeat one really unhelpful line, or just vanish into the ether, the quest log does not help at all and the map is the worst thing to ever happen to a metroidvania.before a vein in my brain explodes im gonna end this review, idk how people are giving this game positive reviews, but to each their own i guess.thanks for the gift by the way, i really tried to like it, i love metroidvanias but that one is just not for me, if it had a better map i could tolerate everything else, but alas, go play Timespinner, its way better than Afterimage in every single way, and also, cheaper.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, I didn't think highly of Afterimage. The talent tree design turned me off. The levels were arranged in such a limited and linear nature. And the voice-acting, no shame to the voice actors though, killed my vibe for the game. Yes, the art style looks great, but at the time it only made me think Afterimage was all about looks and no substance. I am glad I was wrong. Once I unlock the essential abilities, the game becomes way more interesting. Equipment piles up. There are tons of secrets hidden through each level. With just wall-climb and double-jump, you can explore the whole game without hindrance. Exploration feels rewarding not only because of the secret treasures but also because of the great platforming. In other words, this metroidvania requires you to be patient at the start. To be fair, in terms of novelty the gating-abilities in Afterimage doesn't shake the world much. They are the usual trope you can see in most of the metroidvania. It's fine to follow the tradition, but the other parts of the game need to pick up the slack. I am glad that this game does the platforming well. Every level encourages you to use all of your abilities to the fullest. Hidden rooms with subtle hints? Check. Sections of platforming challenges? Check. Levels aren't barricaded with hard locks? Check. Like I said, with just wall-climb and double-jump(and stepping on enemies too which comes with double-jump for some reason), you can access almost every level in the game in whatever order that pleases you. I have a great time jumping on enemies to reach places that are way over my character's level and get immediately one-shot.I wouldn't dedicate a section for this kind of old-school weapon system were it not for that one special feature. When equipping weapons with special passives in the main slot, the sub weapons will inherit that passives should you perform any weapon skills. Since the game hasn't patched it for a whole year after release, I am listing this interaction as a feature. This design opens up a new way to customize your load out. You can equip a weapon which causes bleed in successive hits in the main slot, and a weapon that has multi-hit skills in the sub slot to benefit from that passive. This effect only works with weapon skills and doesn't work in reverse. This is fine because you can still take advantage of other passives in the sub slot with normal attack. Take my load out for example: a poison scythe in main hand and a bleed whip in sub. Both weapons have rather fast and multi-hit attacks, so applying those status effects is a breeze.→Art style is great. The colors are pleasant to the eyes.→Quite several equipment and weapons with special effects.→Meals all have a permanent upgrade for first consumption and temporary buff.→Love that Hollow Knight easter egg.I am not saying it's bad but it certainly doesn't feel good when it comes to talent upgrade, especially at the start. Afterimage puts a rather restricting condition(requiring lv25, etc.) on the simplest upgrades such as minor health boost and defense increase. This design simplifies the branching paths and in a way encourages players to level up. However, the feeling of getting slightly stronger after each level-up is lost. Players either have to hold up to the points until they reach the level or choose some upgrades that are unrelated to their prefer playstyles. For better reference, take a look at Salt and Sanctuary. That game also has a similar skill tree and upgrade currency. It feels way more rewarding to invest in upgrades since you can easily tailor your build with no limitation.→100% map exploration is literal. It doesn't matter if you get all the important items. You really need to clear out all the grey area in a level to be considered 100%.→English translation contains a lot of errors, and weird to read.→Items can get stuck when you kill an enemy in sliding section.→Story to me feels rather incoherent.中文小簡評→內容豐富，但你得先撐過前期有些枯燥的流程。→如果你能撐過去，這款便是個體感不錯、探索有趣、跳台好玩的類銀河系惡魔城。→畫風亮麗，用色舒適。→雖然關鍵技能了無新意，但各個關卡設計能夠讓你充分利用這些技能進行探索。→多數地區並沒有太多硬性障礙物，因此只靠爬牆和二段跳可以去很多地方。→很多裝備和武器有特殊被動及加成。→主武器的被動能套用在副武器的戰技上，這項設計讓配裝上多了點小巧思。→餐點類消耗品有首次食用永久升級及時效性buff。→空洞騎士彩蛋~~→前期技能樹限制太多，玩家不容易感受到升等的快感，要不點些無關緊要的強化，要不存起來等角色達到相對應等級。→100%地圖探索是字面上的意思，就算你撿完所有隱藏寶物，只要該地區還有灰色地帶，就表示你並沒有100%探索完.....→英文譯本有很多文法上的錯誤，讀起來也很奇怪。→故事...不知道怎麼講，很跳tone很亂。

_childDocuments_.review: A Massive metroidvania that's more middling than good.Pros:    - Beautiful Visuals    - No bugsCons:    - It's so easy that you barely have to try against most bosses    - The game is far too open too quickly.      - There's a bunch of story, but none of it is very good and I don't think the translation has been done very well.I'd mark this as more of a mediocre game than good or bad.  I didn't have a bad time with the game, but after completing all the possible endings, I didn't really feel fulfilled.  The endings are all really weird and incomplete as well.  Even when you get the "true" ending, it feels like the story ends before it should and doesn't really wrap up the story events.Also, when it comes to metroid-vania style games, restricting the player in meaningful ways is important.  If the world is too open too soon, the player can get lost and not understand what to do next.  I managed to explore and complete about 60% of the map only about 1/8th of the way into the game and I could not find where to go to get the next skill I needed to move forward.  I've played lots of Metroidvania games and this one let me do a lot more a lot earlier than any other.  This combined with poor lampposting for where to go made the game last a lot longer than I think it should have.On top of that, the majority of the skills you get aren't used in interesting ways.Combine this with combat that requires little more than simply mashing the attack button (because you don't really need to dodge or worry about damage taken) and it makes for more of a tedious game than an engaging one

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never leave reviews, and haven't even fully finished the game, but I feel the need to drop a review purely based on how much I have been loving this game, even with some of it's quirks.This game feels like it's reignited my 100% soul, since secrets and passages are so satisfying to find and feel natural. Honestly, there is a part of this game that reminds me of Dust: An Elysian Tail, that I played the living hell out of when I was younger and probably started some of my collecting tendencies. This game has hooked me so thoroughly that I just can't stop digging, exploring, etc.Combat feels almost perfectly catered to the playstyle I like and keeps me hooked on what I can do and what I could do in the future. Things have the proper weight, platforming is tight and fun, combat has a lot of tiny nuances that don't really mean all that much in the end, but helps you find your "niche" so to speak. My go-to combo has been scythe+greatsword, and honestly, for a game to make me like greatswords in combat is an achievement. They have a satisfying *THUNK* *THUNK* (counter) *THUNK!!!!!!* feel to it without it feeling unwieldy, if that makes any sense lol.One of my favorite things with it is how much you can technically sequence break and absolutely do things slightly out of order. There are very blatant "you don't have the ability needed to progress" moments so common in the genre, but there are many small little moments where it feels blatant that they expect you to be a certain level or have a certain ability, but sometimes if you think "Hmm, I can do that" you actually can. Weapon swings holding you in the air is amazing for these moments. There was absolutely a moment where I did a puzzle without the ability that it was probably designed around, looked back, and thought "Huh, if I didn't have a return potion I would probably be softlocked" lol. Overall vibes and style feel on-point, there are some points where it can feel mildly disjointed, but as other reviews have pointed out, music is good albeit sometimes generic, art is good but sometimes feels slightly disconnected, though not badly, etc. I feel like overall the part I have the harder time with is dialogue and some of the writing, though honestly I feel like it can probably be related to some potential translation issues. I ended up glancing over dialogue and then skipping before the VA finishes mostly because the wording of a lot of stuff felt a bit stilted, though not enough to be incredibly distracting.Also, for some reason I almost feel a bit of Dark Souls charm in some things as well. If you sequence break and go into areas you blatantly aren't leveled/geared for, it almost feels like a completely different game, with one boss that I absolutely treated like a DS boss of "fight against it until you beat it" purely for fun, because it felt super satisfying. Playing this way can sometimes reveal some slightly stilted hitboxes, but overall the entire time I thought "I can beat this" despite defeating them revealing I was 10 levels too low lol.So yeah, anyway, a lot of words for "Game good, some slightly stilted parts, but you should still buy"Edit:I have now finished the game (mostly, haven't 100%'d and haven't completed all the side quests), and I feel like I stand by pretty much everything I said in this review. Very slightly stilted dialogue kinda obscured some of the story, but not enough to ruin it at all, and pieces were definitely coming together by the end. Definitely good, not trying to make it too much of a con, but it did feel like there were parts I just wasn't getting, which could just be me.There's some details with all the different endings you  can get that feels like it requires a guide at some point, and honestly I feel like if you feel like you've reached the extent that raw exploration can take you, guides can be helpful especially for achieving the more niche endings (though I can say that raw exploration was enough for me to make it through most of the steps), but also I am the type of person that does like to play with 100% guides and the fact that I was able to do a lot of it without it and still felt like I was able to achieve most of it on my own is an accomplishment, and honestly it isn't required to use a guide, it's just that some of the niche endings are, well, niche. Combat continued to be mostly satisfying, I stuck to my scythe/greatsword combo through the entire first playthrough, and am now thinking about exploring the other paths for fun, though it's taking some getting used to. There is a point in the game for me where I felt like I got every ability I could, so sequence breaking felt way less common, but with leveling you can still feel like it if you so wanted, and I do feel like difficulty is kept at a relatively constant high. I don't think I ever experienced a spike like when I did that late game area early, but it was still good, and most bosses weren't a breeze other than the "all creatures in the area" bosses. Overall, I would still heavily recommend this game, there is a lot of fun to be had, and secrets aboundEdit:Ok, final edit. I have 100% the game now, gotten everything, killed every boss, etc. The only thing I haven't really finished has been the new Trial of the Soul mode, of which I've beaten all the individual bosses, but I haven't finished the combinations, and I haven't kept my hits below the minimums.All around for this final edit: everything holds true except now it's even higher of a rec. I don't think the "stilted"-ness of some of the dialogue and story are as much of an issue anymore, and I feel partially bad for attempting to chalk it up to a translation issue. I've come to appreciate the combat a lot more. If there were one little thing that's not really a negative, it just happened to be the case for my playthrough, once you have found every item, every collectable, and every dew clump, dew becomes quite hard to come by lol. Ultimately I had to use a cheesy strat to get all I needed for achievements, but I would also imagine that most won't so vigorously collect everything like I did lol.Overall, I just can't stop thinking about this game, and honestly is a game of the year for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a fun, challenging, and visually stunning addition to the Metroidvania genre.To get some of the negatives out of the way (or at least, what were negatives for me while playing):Now, all of that to say, I really enjoyed this game the more I got into it. I definitely suffered from trying to beat bosses that were higher level than I had business fighting, but once my levelling matched that of the enemy's a bit better, the game became a lot smoother (this is really my fault - you aren't typically obligated to beat any one boss at any one time. I'm just stubborn and once I encountered a new boss, I wanted to beat it right then and there even if I was significantly underlevelled at the time). The boss fights are really fun and challenging, and satisfying to complete. The bosses themselves present a wide range of fighting styles and frankly, look super cool. The game is  visually stunning; like, it is just flat-out gorgeous with beautiful environments. I thought (most of) the characters were interesting and well-designed. I got my first ending at ~35 hours in and then had another ~22 hours of content to go through (additional endings, NG+, achievement clean-up, etc). This game is . Like, big big. Do not go in expecting to be done in 15 hours. By that point, you'll have maybe come across ~six areas out of ~25. Marking your map as you explore for treasures you cannot yet access, areas blocked by abilities you don't have yet, etc is the best advice I can give you on this front. All in all, Afterimage is a solid Metroidvania choice you can really sink your teeth into. It shines in its beautifully designed worlds and fun/interesting/challenging boss fights. While it's not without its cons, if you enjoy this genre, aren't put-off by mediocre storytelling, and simply want a fun game to play, this is a solid pick.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful metroidvania game with great music, deep and complex lore, fluid movement, satisfying combat, enormous map, a ton of content, and gives a decent amount of challenge without being too frustrating. This game fits the use case of Steam Deck OLED extremely well, and looks superb on the OLED screen. My Steam play time for this game is bugged but I actually have around 70 hours into this game for 100% completion. I did not refer to any guide until I got my first ending so if you are stuck somewhere just explore a bit more. I highly recommend it to Steam Deck owners.However, I do have some criticisms for the game:1. The rewards for exploration are usually very underwhelming (mostly fast travel consumables). The designer seems to be way too stingy.2. On the topic of fast travel consumables, it is not a very nice design to require some consumable just to fast travel. The free fast travel points are also way too few and far between. In some areas you need to go through some tough enemy placement just to get from respawn to fight the boss again, and that is not enjoyable experience.3. There are very few really good equipment. Almost all equipment that are good in specs give you some debuff. I think you need to provide some OP items and equipment especially in latter part of the game to make the player feel somewhat powerful.4. It is a bit annoying that you are forced to use the analog stick for movement, and there are many challenging platforming sections that require a ton of precision. Specifically, to dive kick you need to hold the stick down and that is annoying. I used an 8bitdo M30 controller and that dpad help me a ton going over those platforming sections.5. Most characters speak in riddles and they are not doing a good job telling the story. There are some messages spread in the world, but the designer should put more to help players understand what is going on. After watching a few Youtube videos explaining the lore I am still confused by the concept of "Resonants" in the lore.6. I would prefer not losing consumables that you used before you died.

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a beautiful game with many ideas and systems, but the main issue is that none of the ideas were thought through. The game looks very beautiful and it's main appeal are the hand drawn graphics. Backgrounds are nice and lively and it is very pleasant to look at. The style can look overdesigned at times. Music is really soothing, atmospheric and strengthens the ambient of their respective zones and moments. And that is where the praise ends.  seems fun at first, and does have some interesting traversing challenges. Afterimage implemented RPG like leveling up system with a somewhat okay skill tree in size, but with +1 damage type passive upgrades. The skill tree is very messy in its design, multiple points can be put in the same node and you can't tell at a glance which upgrade is available. Besides passive bonuses they also grant weapon moves which are disappointing in damage and actual usage. The biggest sin is "diversified character builds" the game is claiming, as you are basically railroaded into having points in every node if you level up enough. The only difference in build is which weapons you use. You don't have invincibility frames on dodge which is very weird choice as you can't react to attacks that are frequently instantaneous. Environment doesn't help either, as you will be restricted in movement. Enemy attacks are often random and with bosses' attacks being mostly impossible to read. Bosses, while mixed bag in mechanics, are almost always simple DPS races. Some of the important gameplay upgrades come waaay too late. is too big to go for what the game designers decided here. As in every metroidvania, there are obstacles and hidden paths that become available after some new items/abilities are acquired. Every region in the game has almost all types of this hidden areas. You will have to backtrack to every area to check if you can traverse any of those paths with currently available skills every single time you unlock something. Another sin is the locked doors which appear 5 hours before you acquire the key. With all the hidden paths good luck at remembering everything (and guessing if the right door for the key). That wouldn't be problem if the exploration isn't meaningless. Rewards for your exploration are often meaningless - some credits, skill point, small upgrades, weapons barely stronger than what you have that will be outclassed in hour or two. If you have any completionistic tendencies this will very quickly turn into chore. The game does give you tools for the map and it actually expects you to use them.Another problem is the lack of minimap. You basically have to look at the map all the time to traverse the area while backtracking. The fast travel is gated behind consumables which can be bought with credits. The fast travel points aren't always places where'd you want them. is in typical Soulslike fashion obscure and almost impossible to follow. It is very contrived, bombarding the player with unnecessary terminology and references to events that player has no way to memorize. The translation doesn't help either. It's also told through key items which the game bombards you with. You end up with so many gems orb and whatnot and until the plot demands, you really have no idea what is their purpose despite the description. The game suffers the disconnect in the tone. All characters and plot points convey the mood of tragedy and sadness but the game is overly vibrant with colour as it tries too hard to seem like an adventure. The tone of the areas mostly overwhelms the story. As scarce as the plot is, it'll be very hard for story to drive you going forward.The menus aren't organized good either as you have to scroll through couple of them to get to the one you need. And most of the time you will need some adjusting through sub menus to get to what you're looking for. There is a weapon upgrade system but is hidden away as the game suffers from many other contrivances and obscurities. In  the game is well made but too ambitious. Most of the features, while complete, were not planned well and their implementations lack practicality. The gameplay isn't good and story isn't strong enough to drive you to the end. It tries to give you playtime for your money but in the end it doesn't respect your time.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Its a "bad" good game. Would recommend to those who have delved into many metroidvanias, but not to someone who has not. At first the game seemed like any other cheaply made <$10 game, but after delving into the fully (finishing all the endings), I stand "partially" corrected. It has a surprising amount of content, but its is hampered down by the "anime" side of the game. The game sacrifices clarity in both visual and story elements for the "anime" tag, but overall, this can be mostly overlooked if you are willing to look up a guide if you do happen to get lost (and skip over the overabundance of chit chat). Combat wise, its a mix of Hollow Knight movement with Castlevania (Bloodstained) rpg elements. At times, it works, at other times, it fails completely. My biggest gripe is the fact that weapon upgrades are not deterministic (you cannot craft them and you cant be like "oh that enemy uses a whip, they will probably drop one if I kill them enough"). You have to happen upon the weapons, which is fine, except that you have to spec into weapon types in your talent tree and if you just happen to miss the hidden "your weapon of choice" in an area, you are just going to be weaker for a while. (Luckily later on the game you can accumulate enough points to  circumvent this problem). With the lack of a real guiding hand in where to go, you often go to areas way above your level, which would be fine in something like Hollow Knight (you can simply "outplay") or Castlevania (you can simply "prepare better"), but this game with its nondeterministic upgrades, leads to some very "unwinnable" situations. That would be fine, except for the fact that when you die, you experience is stranded in the middle of the boss room, where you cannot retrieve it without locking yourself in the boss fight again, so that chunk of EXP is just gone. The other mechanic of Potions staying consumed even after you die, makes it even more punishing to try to push your limits and do content that you are underleveled for. Those problems aside, it has a deep pool of content,  visually pretty good (although lacking some clarity sometimes), and a decently solid gameplay feel, it is plenty worth your time and money. The lack of "polish" really dampens the mood early on into the game, but if you push through that, the game is actually really damn good.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was fun and challenging. Huge map to explore, lots of bosses, side-bosses, quests, and hidden stuff.It has a good variety of enemies(they don't feel repetitive).The inventory is designed a bit weird but nothing too bad.The gameplay is fair. I've heard people complain about not being able to dash through enemies but I don't see the problem with that.The map is huge and sometimes I felt a bit lost due to the lack of direction, but that was primarily because at that time I didn't explore enough.The story was intriguing. Not the most groundbreaking thing out there but it's good. I found that many people didn't understand the story but it seems to be a case of "too lazy to read".Overall I recommend this game.UPDATE: After half a year since release, not all Kickstarter promises have been fulfilled. So that's a bummer.

name: Lunistice
detailed_description: Lunistice is a linear 3D platformer that is heavily inspired by the 32-bit era of yesteryear. Follow Hana the Tanuki on her adventure through her dreams! Explore the different dreamscapes to guide her to her final destination - The Moon - and try to uncover the secrets of 'The Lunistice' along the way! Explore a multitude of different dreamscapes created from Hana's memories! Jump and run through an old shrine, a fancy water park or a world made out of food! Lunistice is designed as a simple and short experience that you can easily play in short bursts! Have fun and enjoy the good vibes! Try to beat your fastest times and highest completion and get an S-Rank on every stage! And if you're looking for some additional variety: play the whole game as a different character with their own skills and gameplay!

_childDocuments_.review: Ironically the best 3D Sonic game that I played, which I know is not a very high bar, but still, I purchased Sonic 06 as a gift for a birthday, and I waited 10+ years for a good rail section.  These sliding levels are so much fun and have so much mid-air escapism, actually so good, and probably the most well-implemented version of this type of gameplay. The first zone is mostly generic platforming, but as soon as you hit the theme park, the game is like a full-on Roller Coaster fetish, and I absolutely love it.Now the game is not just a linear runner, well it kinda is, but the way they designed the levels with the forks, you can pretty much play it as a collection game and explore different parts of the stages, and I am pretty sure it's intentional. It's not difficult, there is a checkpoint almost every 20 seconds, you can take your time and enjoy it the way you want, for me it was just playing the stages and enjoying the level design. I thought the camera movement was not perfect, but it's something that I got over after the first 10 minutes, and you can lower the sensitivity, it's just that sometimes they will fix on certain angles and it will make it hard to judge the distance, that being said, what retro-inspired game would it be if the camera didn't kill a few times. For the most part, I didn't have any big issues with the platforming, it's a relatively forgiving game, you can do a double-jump+air spin so you have a lot of control in the air. The best part of the game, aside from that killer soundtrack, the levels are just so pretty (except maybe for the first zone) so many cool angles when you move around. They introduce a few different stage mechanics here and there, but it's a pretty basic platfomer, nothing too complicated. You can replay the game with different characters that have unique perks, granted I am not sure when I unlocked them (probably after beating it). You should be able to finish the game within 3 hours, but you can get a lot more out of it, depending on your completionist needs.(+) Awesome soundtrack, loved it(+) Solid-level design, like a tasty strawberry cheesecake (+) Lovely sliding sections, enjoyable aesthetic moving around(+) Different characters with unique perks (I think I unlocked them)(+) Decent collection/achievement supportNothing comes to mind. I had maybe 1 glitch and it took me a few minutes to adapt to camera movement, that is about it.It's just a fun and pretty platformer, what can I say. Some of the most fun sliding/rail sections, I really enjoyed just looking at her gliding on the lines, so many cool angles. There is a bunch of collection content, I kinda just played through the levels, but you can get more out of it.

Play the same levels again but with a character that functions slightly different than the original one.-Collectibles can be frustrating at times. _childDocuments_.review: Okay, editing my review now that I've completed everything.For context, I am a 2D maso-core platforming fan (think modded Celeste, Pizza Tower, etc), so while I definitely have experience platforming, the addition of a third dimension required a bit of adjustment for me.This game is fantastic, that's apparent from the beginning. Three things I see a lot of 3D platfromers (of much larger scope and budget than Lunistice) struggle with are ease of movement, collectible placement, and camera movement. This game is great in all those respects, making the game a super tight and satisfying experience right off the bat.As you progress, it becomes extremely clear this game punches way above its weight class, especially for a FIVE DOLLAR(!) price tag. The replayability is great, as with a lot of high quality platformers, and the ranks and guest characters add a neat paradigm shift in gameplay as you go back through the levels.So, my few crtisisms are as follows: dragonbone desert (Toukee's last stage) is a major slosh, despite having a more complex, less linear layout with some fun platforming. Having to collect 900 things while not dying (for S rank) seems very out of place considering the shorter, more linear layouts the other stages have. Also, Toree feels unwieldy, especially with the 1 health and lack of attack. The constant kiting of enemies makes things awkward compared to Hana and Toukee with their attacks. These criticisms, however, do not take away from the sheer quality and value of this game.Oh, and its great for speedrunning!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I feel a bit bad giving Lunistice a negative review, because I really don't bear it any ill will and it has a lot of good things going for it. A chill soundtrack, nice visual design, clearly a good deal of love put into designing it, etc. but... for something that brands itself as a casual and relaxing experience, it makes me have a death grip on my controller. It's like EVERYTHING has ice physics, and every second platform is slanted at an angle that makes movement physics on it act just a bit unfamiliar, and every drop is an instadeath reset-to-checkpoint.I don't feel like every platformer needs super precise physics and controls necessarily, but I feel that if you have controls like Lunistice's, you should also be a bit more generous with platform real estate and maybe have pickups(cranes, really, just the cranes, are there even any other elevant pickups other than the letters and the other letters?) have a slightly greater "magnetism" radius so I don't need to be dead-on to grab them.I found Lunistice to be a stressful platformer to play, personally.

_childDocuments_.review: A very well crafted 3D platformer. I have to be careful with these because a bad camera = motion sickness for me, but this is pretty smooth. I've had a couple of slippery-ness issues jumping onto a few small platforms, but that's probably my terrible reaction time not the game.Great music, great graphics, great options, super cheap price. 100% thumbs up

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is pretty much the perfect short cute indie collectathon.First off, the music is all fantastic, I can’t state that enough. The OST itself is already worth more than the ridiculously low price of this game. You get a free game with this bangin OST! Each area has its own feel, and just like Sonic music, there’s a progression of a musical theme between acts of a stage.The level designs for each stage/act are stellar. Not only do they stand alone as fantastic, mostly linear, ridiculously fun obstacle courses, being able to house many types of collectables and secrets to find, but they all work perfectly for the THREE playable characters all with different movesets. That is a feat and a half. Each stage also has a wildly different and vibrant theme, making each location distinct and memorable, as well as making this fictional world super interesting and somewhere I’d want a future game to revisit.As far as completion systems go, the ranking system is thankfully very sensible and lets you get both S ranks that you need per act on separate attempts, rather than forcing you to get a perfect run each act. In general, finding all the collectables and getting 100% completion isn’t unfairly difficult at all, and you’re able to find everything with some amount of ease as long as you’re looking, which is not just a godsend, but actually fun.Essentially, if you like 3d platformers and speed, you’ll love this criminally underpriced star 💫Objective - 9/10;Subjective - 9/10;
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game has managed to visually capture a special feeling from the low-poly PS1 days, like with games like Jumping Flash. It has tight controls, good FPS, sprawling colors and an amazing soundtrack. S-rank can be achieved by doing the requirements separately and your time to finish the level doesn't affect your ranking so you can take your time exploring. It's just great
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, another platformer with a cute animal mascot. It’s truly the golden age for Furries all over the gaming world!This game is just a treat to play through for the few hours it provides. The platforming collecthathon is smooth and satisfying, the world and story is interesting to go through, and the OST is really darn catchy. It's a perfect $5 game.Lunistice is a linear platformer reminiscent of the ps1 era with 32 bit visuals that has gameplay similar to Mario galaxy and the momentum of sonic the hedgehog, and in my mind it's what 3D Sonic games should be. The game is broken into several themed levels with each level having several hidden paths containing letters, if you collect all the letters you'll unlock reports telling you the game's plot via diary entries, finding about the true nature of the game world.There are 14 levels across 7 worlds, each with four optional hidden bonuses to find, and S ranks to earn in terms of collecting all the coin-like-items and not dying. The movement is tight, fun and satisfying once you get the hang of it, with only a double jump and an extra twirl attack that can be chained together to make for really fun tricks. The game can be very challenging at times but fortunately, checkpoints are common and fairly placed, so you rarely ever find yourself being set back much further than where you died.The game can be beaten in a couple of hours, but it's a very sweet experience for the whole duration, and the best part is that the game is a complete steal at only 4.99! It took me 5 hours to complete the game with the first character, after which the game unlocked two new characters that collectively took me few more hours to complete. And the other two characters control very differently from the main one and each have their own special final level to unlock! After beating everything with them, I then went back and replayed it with the first character a couple more times because it's that much fun once you master the movement. In my eyes, that's a lot of value for $4! What are you waiting for?10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a game I really, REALLY wanted to enjoy. A 32-bit Sonic-inspired 3D Platformer?  It might as well have been made for me specifically, and that's something I really felt playing the demo.  But once I got the full game and got to play the rest of it, that excitement turned to annoyance, then frustration, and then finally apathyOn the surface, Lunistice is a fine enough game. It looks great, runs great, has decent music and controls, and all of that should lead to something great. But for this game, none of that matters once you start peeling back the layers. Something that makes itself readily apparent once you get to the 2nd or 3rd world is that there really isn't a lot to this game. Now, for something that's trying to be "retro" like this, that normally wouldn't be a problem. Hell, one of my all time favorite games is Sonic 2, a game that's pretty damn simple and to the point. But Lunistice takes that a step further by having no boss fights, no story outside of the opening and ending cutscenes (and the optional journal pieces), and hardly any enemy variety. All the game really has is just a bunch of levels. Yeah, those levels can be played and replayed to get higher ranks, faster times (which you aren't rewarded for), and different experiences with different characters.  But there's nothing outside of thatAnd since there's nothing outside of hte levels, you'd think they'd be polished to a fine sheen, but they aren't. In fact, the longer the game goes on, the more just plain unfun mechanics it throws at you. Balloons with wonky physics in the 3rd world, rhythm sections in the 4th world reminiscient of Beep Block Skyways that are overly punishing, grind rails in worlds 5 and 6 with some of the worst hit detection I've ever seen, and disappearing platforms in the final world that disappear FAR too fast.  All of these and more just serve to make later levels far more frustrating than fun, especially if you're going for 100%  Ultimately, it's because of this frustration that I gave up on 100%ing the game, and it's this frustration that killed it for meLike I said, Lunistice is a pretty game with fun controls and fun music, but none of that matters if the only thing the game has to offer, those being the levels, are just unfun.  I wanted to love this game. I wanted to see the fantastic 32-bit platformer that everyone else did, but I just couldn't look past the glaring flaws4/10. It's a notable first effort, but it's too rough around the edges and has too little to really offer

_childDocuments_.review: Guys.G U Y S.ITS SO CHEAP WHO ALLOWED THISThe replay-ability in this game is off the charts for its $5 price tag. _childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a game I've been looking forward to since I found out about it and tried the demo. Now that the full game is out, and having just completed the main adventure. I have to say I'm thoroughly impressed and the final product in some ways surpasses the expectations I had.Lunistice is a very simple 3D platformer, but that is one of its biggest strengths. It takes what works about it and runs with that, no unnecessary fluff or padding. Everything here is super tight, enjoyable, and polished, making it just feel good to play through whether you are looking to just do a casual playthrough or repeats for better and better times. The quality and amount of content you can get from this game for just 5 bucks makes it a no-brainer to me.The main contributor to that is just how incredible the controls are, its very rare to come across a platformer  tight and responsive, not once did I really feel a death was undeserved due to poor controls. Hana, the main playable character, has an extremely simple moveset, but even that has some depth to it that lets you flex your skills and carve out alternate routes. Her attack can be used middair to let yourself elongate your jumps, and even better, if you attack and jump at the same time you get an extra high jump. While this is very simple, this lets you really figure out some fun alternate paths and skips, it makes replaying the levels a lot of fun to get better times, something I did with the demo and am sure to do here as well.And these levels are all incredibly fun to play through thanks to their design, while most are linear, there is little optimizations you can do all over the place to really get a satisfying flow going. The first few levels are very straightforward and basic, but things quickly pick up and provide some fun gimmicks hat don't feel too intrusive and obnoxious and really get their time to get fleshed out despite the fairly short runtime. The railgrinding and speed boosts in particular are both incredibly fun, finding ways to keep your speed off the speed boost as long as possible is very enjoyable, and the railgrinding keeps you engaged by making you balance to stay at top speed, while reacting to any enemies or secrets/alternate paths along the way, which you will be wanting to look for with how well done the collectibles are in this game.A lot of platformers pad out their games by making the necessary collectibles for 100% annoyingly obscure to find. Lunistice entirely avoids this by making the collectibles require you to pay attention to notice little things and/or making you go through fun little segments that play off the stage's gimmicks to get the collectibles necessary. I was easily able to get everything within at most two playthroughs of a level, while it still being challenging and interesting enough to be worth collecting.Top off all the quality levels and gameplay with an incredible soundtrack, gorgeous retro artstyle, basic but interesting story/setting, and even two more characters that are both fun to play and allow for different approaches to the same levels (with some of their own levels, even!)... You have a game that I can easily recommend to any other fans of platformers. Please give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty cool. You jump around and collect stuff across a number of long levels. That's it.The pixelated filter can be disabled thankfully. I didn't own a console to be nostalgic about this subgenre so I played without the pixelation.To obtain all S ranks you need to collect everything and beat each level without dying (which can be achieved in separate runs). The weird part is that not only you there are no time constraints but also the game has three characters and for all achievements you have to get S ranks with each of them. So basically you have to 100% the game three times over (including collectibles). Weird, kind of waste of time, but that's alright.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Really REALLY fun game to play and 100%. it strays from being repetitive thanks to two unique characters you unlock after base game (with different mechanics from the protagonist). art style and aesthetic is nostalgiac and beautiful; gameplay is pretty good, a fast paced 3D platformer with collectibles. A little tip for smoother controls because its a little harder to play with the default settings:- Smooth Turning OFF (when this is on it you cant make sharp turns so when you wanna turn around fast you kinda do an awkward glide which slows you down or kills you- Shadow ON (this helps with precision and landing)- Horizontal camera speed 150-200% (if you're using a controller and having to move to camera around constantly while platforming it helps to have the sensitivity higher so you dont have to stop and turn your camera. just keep dashin through! you can write Lunistice off as a "sonic clone" but it at least is unique enough to stand on its own 2 feet with its unique roster of characters, beautiful artstyle and interesting lore. definitely a game worth your time.-
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: We live in a world that horribly misunderstands what a game is. They think it's bigger, badder, and grander. Spending billions upon billions for the best graphics to wow investors and often forgetting the core of what a game truly is.Lunistice gets it. It understands what a game is more than any triple A blockbuster corporation ever could. It's fun.What a silly concept right? Fun is such a subjective term. I mean a lot of triple A games are decently fun so what makes them fail on a fundamental level compared to Lunistice? Soul. Love. Passion.Indescribable things and yet here they are in Lunistice. Nothing feels hollow or without reason. Mechanics I was skeptical about in later levels stepped up for course 2 and showed me they had reason to belong. Nothing felt like it was put in just because they needed to check off a spreadsheet list. It feels fun. It feels refreshing. It doesn't try to be anything more than what it should be. It knows what it needs to be and who it is.In an industry that tries for all of it's might to crush competition and squeeze out the heart and soul of anything for an extra dime, this game shows that all you need is a good design and love to make something special.It genuinely brings tears to my eyes that I can really still feel the same love I felt when I was a kid today. Thank you A Grumpy Fox for reminding me that there really truly is hope that passion and purpose still exists out there in the industry. I look forward to what you give us next.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem. Well made relaxing 3D platformer, a combination of jumps, climbing, sliding and running but never frustrating, and you can do triple jumps, even 4 jumps when you unlock the birdie character. The devs know how to create levels with challenging yet not too much, all the monsters are one-hit kills, but your character got 3 lives and the checkpoint are not far, so basically this is a mistake-tolerant game.I especially enjoy the cake-candy and crystal world, tbh each world is unique and interesting in its own way. In later levels some jumps can be tricky because the platforms/blocks appear/vanish on a timely basis, player needs to calculate the beats to pass certain areas. If you like to explore you'll always find hidden letters in more challenging paths, but if you only focus on the finish line it's perfectly okay. When the game is beaten for the first time, 2 more characters with unique abilities will be unlocked to offer huge replay value.For me this game is totally worth $4.99, I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Started out cute and funny, but ended up being frustrating.The game has blind jumps and mechanics you can't possibly understand on the first try (i.e. you have to attack something and instantly jump off to catch another platform).When the path split, you don't know which one is the main path. In one level I had a checkpoint pointing to a side path instead of the main path. Before I realized, I was already thrown into a booster which catapulted me into the next checkpoint and I couldn't go back.Sometimes I already see the secret path, but I miss the jump, then I kill myself, but the last checkpoint is so far away.It would be nice if this game learned from every other platformer and have the shadow of the character straight downwards, so if I'm in the air, I can exactly see where I'm landing.In addition to that, it would be nice to be able to rotate the camera more upwards (allow for more pitch), to see more of the ground / shadow. That would be a day & night difference and give me full control of landing.The deceleration of the character might be by design, but it's very annoying when you have to collect 5 cranes that are placed in an X formation. There should be another way to place cranes and still be able to collect them all in one satisfying sweep.Some might argue it's nitpicky and the game is cheap, but I could also just play A Hat in Time. There is not much this game has to offer, except cute graphics right now. However, all these things are very small adjustments that can be fixed. I'm looking forward for the next update, so I can recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute, very fun, very affordable, what more can you ask for? Incredible game especially for the price - You can get the normal ending in one evening, and there is plenty of reasons to replay levels for unlocking hidden things or exploring new paths you hadn't figured out before. There are more characters to unlock and the game is very speedrunning-friendly if that is your kinda thing. If 3D platforming is at all your thing, get this game!

_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Really, the header sums it all up. Lunistice is a game that sets out to do exactly one thing and does that thing very well- be a fun, fast-paced platformer. Every new level mechanic is easy to grasp and flows well into the design, and players can choose to pursue 100% completion, True Ending completion, or just running through all the levels as fast as they can. It's short, sure, but honestly it feels just as long as it needs to be without overstaying its welcome. Overall a very solid game and you really can't go wrong with a $5 price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a solid little 3D platformer. The games levels are unique from each other and generally well made, I completed the game and there was never any level I dreaded replaying. The collectables as well were satisfying to collect and really naturally placed with the flow of the level, which can't be said for every game in this style. Lunistice felt good to control but does have the same problem that most 3D platformers have, that being the camera. The camera controls takes some getting used to and did impede my view during a few moments, luckily the levels are pretty open and allow for the camera to move. The game may be considered short by some but there is a ton of post game things to do which I always enjoy. I definitely recommend Lunistice if you're a fan of the 3D platformers genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice just awakened my love for 3D platformer again. The game is really cute with pixelated 3D background, characters and cute musics. It fits the game style really well I'll say. Other than that Lunistice makes jumping around here and there feels great by having a triple jump mechanic and a really REALLY challenging platforms which need a precise movements and jumps. But there's checkpoint by the way so don't panic yet unless you're going for a full S run like me. After that, the price is obviously cheap. Just grab the game right away, no need to wait for sales anymore. In conclusion, It's a really fun game. That's it. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This Is a MUST BUY GAME!!Overview:Lunistice is one of the most compelling and charming games I have played since Sonic Mania, I was so impressed by its visuals, replayability, OST , smooth controls and THE STORY OML, Lunistice really stands out as its own platformer and I love Hana's design and the Japanese aesthetic! Collectables:So to 100% Lunistice and get the secret ending you need to collect all the letters of Hanas name in act 1 to get the Golden Keys and then get all the letters of Hanas name in act 2 to get the Files, purple platforms will appear at the end of the stage that lead to these items, the keys are just collectables but I would get the Files as they explain more about the story which is quite compelling and I won't spoil it for you! (to get the secret ending you need both the keys and files tho)Gameplay:WOW! This game reminded me of NIGHTS Into Dreams when it came to controls, everything was so smooth and floaty, Hana is a lil ninja always on the go!! The fluidity tied in with the amazing level design opts for a very nice experience which I very much enjoyed!OST-Original Sound Track:This was my favourite part of the game, my personal favourite from the OST was from the level Food-Comfort, a bouncy song that complements the level well! The composing for this game was done so well, and I would buy a CD of it if one was ever made!!Last Note:If the developer sees this by some chance just know, your mom would be so proud bc this game was honestly amazing and you and your team should be so proud of what they have created <3
