_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice commits the cardinal sin of being a platformer with dull level design and physics that make every jump feel more like a leap of faith.Before we get to the gameplay, let's start with Lunistice's most distinct feature: The visuals.The game goes for a SEGA Saturn 32-Bit style, meaning everything is 3D, but it has something very dreamy and charming about it.All worlds look colorful, playful and a bit pixelated, creating this trance feel to it.Add jamming music and it seems like a cheery platformer.The design of the worlds replicate this feeling, they have their familiar themes like beaches, or space, but it simply doesn't feel like it has been done before in that particular way.To the game's detriment, however, the worlds look nicer than they play.The level design is quite simple. There are enemies, wide platforms to jump on, and each world has its own gimmick, while loosing steam midway through, making the gimmicks feel more like the same ones, but with a new coat of paint. The gimmicks especially lack any personality of their own, and are trying to sell you on the idea that simple trampolines, rails, or ground that makes you go slightly faster need their own separate levels.Besides that, there are also forks in the road, where you can do an optional platforming challenge to get additional collectibles if you're looking to 100% the levels, which are alright I guess, just seems odd to divide collectibles from the level. It creates the problem that you might do the optional challenge by accident.Unfortunately, the game doesn't really evolve past that. It's always nothing more than adding a gimmick to the mix. The platforming itself isn't really tight or responsive, you either fight the controls, or simply jump from floating platform A to floating platform B, while having your mind on other things, because it really is dull and has no creative concepts level design-wise, other than pressing the jump button a few times.But, worse than generic level design is undoubtedly a character that doesn't control well.The game's jumps feel more like a leap of faith than anything, you have two jumps, but the first jump is more like a long jump, barely gaining any height, and giving you doubts if you make the jump or not. There's no shadow telling you that information either, so you often end up double jumping just because of unreliability.Additionally, merely turning the character feels absolutely terrible, my closest comparison would be Sonic Lost World levels of turning, where the character slows down dramatically, having more problems doing a 90° turn than a semi-truck. It throws you off completely, therefore you find yourself running more or less in a completely straight line, since whenever the game asks you to turn it isn't satisfying. It doesn't help, either, that doing a 180° turn is notoriously unresponsive, since the character needs a good second to slow down, turn, and then keep going. During tighter platforming sections, I found myself simply sliding off terrain as if my controller had input delay.Another incredibly questionable control choice is to limit the player's control over the y-axis of the camera. So, if you do an optional platforming challenge, and find yourself high up in the sky, you simply cannot look down. The game doesn't let you. Why? This is a deliberate limitation that makes no sense to me, especially with the lack of a shadow when jumping, you can't even use the camera to properly adjust your jumps.What it boiled down to was that I found the rather generic gimmicks that took control away from the player much more enjoyable. I don't need extra tight controls for a fun small platformer to please me, but Lunistice fails to make the simplest movement engaging.I usually even 100% any platformer I get my hands on, but this one made me give up early on.For such a short game, it completely lacks in the simplest departments. Lunistice's movement, nor level design, are endearing. Visually, it has a soul, but the character's controls and physics take my soul. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: So, I really like this game. The music is great, the platforming is tight, the stages are big without being overwhelming. Basically everything about it design-wise worked for me.HOWEVER! I think it probably took me legitimately about an hour to finish the game, but I have three hours on record because the game crashed *at least* a dozen times across my playthrough. I don't know if this is the game being unstable, or if it was caused by something on my end, but the constant crashing really ruined the experience for me. I'd like nothing more than to give Lunistice a big ol' recommendation, but I can't. It's simply too broken.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: It's OK, but just shy of "recommended" territory. Maybe about a 6.5/10. Graphics are fun. Towards the end, the difficulty scales up a bit too much. _childDocuments_.review: Okay, a real review.Game is simple, fun and as someone who has trouble sticking with a game that doesn't evolve mechanics too much, this was approaching the levels of fun I had with "A Hat In Time".Quick and fun levels that never really overstayed their style, a story that you can engage in or ignore, and for a game that lives or dies by the controls, even if they were a little float-y to start with, I could feel the weigh, which meant I was pretty much in control by the end.Silly achievements, the fact that anyone could go back to it and get a newer experience (with a different character) and the fact I could enjoy the music means this game is a jewel that I would have paid more for.But for real, f*ck the cake levels. _childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Good aesthetics. Gameplay isn't too bad except for one thing: if you miss something, there are times you can't go back without restarting the level and losing your cranes. You can't just go back to any prior checkpoint. This has proven very frustrating and unnecessary, and it made me turn off the game. Please do not encourage this type of gameplay behavior.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A nice but short challenging platformer.Once you finish the game you can play with other styles. I dont know if its buggy or i just didnt notice it properly in the first stages but in the later stages the rail grind object changes to something different and shortens the track, once you reach the end of it you just fall down and waste a jump. So you have to jump before you reach the end which is pretty difficult in the last few stages, including the camera having to snap turn.Another odd flaw is the rythm stage suddenly changes the speed of the notes (instead of 2/4 it changes to each beat swapping) which isnt indicated except if you stare at the UI element.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: It gets boring so easily, there isn’t anything that intrusting in level design- both from visual and game play standpoint. Visuals and music are intrusting in theory, but in actual game they come off very forgettable. There’s just nothing very “fun” about this game. Idk, don’t get the overwhelmingly positive rating
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a precision platformer with a character that moves like its on slippery ice, causing a lot of frustrations when trying to complete the game with s rank.Player shadow option is disabled by default, turn it on to have an easier time learning the ropes of the game, by the time i learned about this feature i was already on act 5, unfortunately, with or without player shadows the jumping never stops feeling janky and uncomfortable, you will many times make a precise jump only to slip off of the platforms, had to switch to mouse and keyboards because using a joystick became unbearable.You will rely on moving the player camera to adjust a lot, actively making the character turn around feels like you are draggin them by a rope, its awkward to say the least.There is a button for walking, but you will dread any moment in the gameplay where you are forced to use it, you character will steer  while moving forward, it will never stay still so you can adjust yourself, you have to rely on jumping awkwardly to adjust yourself, in platforms that are so small you can slip off of them, it is a really frustrating combination of unpolished mechanics that can only frustrate the player.Act 4 features the worst gimmick in the game, dissappearing platforms based on a timer.You will die a lot and never get a proper feeling for the rythm because the jumping feels already awkward Devs attempted to correct the awful turning controls by giving you an option to disable smooth turning, this somehow makes the game even more unplayable (maybe because at that time i switched to mouse and keyboard). The character will now instead zoom in the opposite direction, punishing you hard for trying to readjust mid jump.This is not a game for children despite the art style and graphics, its gonna give them more frustration than enjoyment by playing it.The music is good, the art direction is good, the gameplay is at odds with itself, trying to be a fast paced precision platformer, but the speed of the gameplay is too slow and the controls are too slippery for the platforming sections to feel any good.Maybe making the platforms bigger would have helped? maybe not every failed jump be punished with immediate death? or adding more friction when reaching ground?No idea, game has good moments, hope the developer/s learn to capitalize in the strenghts and polish on their weakenesses, game had potential to be really good, it just gets bogged down by some odd design choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Retro 3D-Graphics looks great but the level designs are really generic. Each area has a "gimmick" mechanic which just boils down to "riding a rail" or "moving a little faster" or "jumping higher", etc. These mechanics would probably be fine if your movement wasn't so slow and slippery. There's around 4 or 5 enemies in the game, each only capable of one simple function (flying, moving back and forth, standing still). Combat is relegated to a one button tail swipe. It's not satisfying to use, there's no reason to use it, just skip the enemies entirely.The game markets itself as a simple and casual experience, but that just seems like a cover up for their total lack of creativity. Good art and music isn't enough to make up for a bare bones gameplay experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: + very nice art direction and graphics- one trick pony gameplay- difficulty pacing is inconsistent- level design does little to impress or distinguish itselfLunistice is a third person platformer in a similar vein to some older Sega Saturn and Dreamcast 3D platformers. The main hook, for me at least, were the faithfully created retro graphics which are very reminiscent of the era of PS1/Saturn/N64 early 3D platformers. There is a loose story giving some context to the game but it's not an emphasis.The gameplay is simple with lots of platforming, but it never really does anything meaningful beyond going from A-to-B. People who are interested in beating their scores or comparing scores with others, especially in the context of speedy platforming, might be delighted to play Lunistice, but if that doesn't interest you, there's not a lot to attract the average person.The level design and art direction are quite good, but besides these, I didn't find much substance to the game. There just isn't enough gameplay variety to keep invested. Enemy variety is almost non-existent, and every enemy more or less acts the same way and are dealt with the same way. Enemies pose no real threat and seem to be mostly decoration peppered across levels.While each new world introduces a new mechanic or challenge, like sliding rails or longer chains of jumping between platforms, what most differs between worlds is color scheme and a broad theme (jungle, islands, theme park, etc). The differences are not too dramatic to make exploring a new world interesting: if you took screenshots of each world and made them greyscale, it would be difficult to discern them because everything is so samey.What I'm trying to get at is if you've played ten minutes of Lunistice, nothing of substance really improves or changes going further. It fails to evolve beyond the basic premise of "this is a 3D platformer". While platforming is something the game does well, it's just very monotonous and single-faceted.There is also an issue of difficulty balancing. I found the first few levels quite easy with some minor spikes in difficulty, but near the third world, the platforming becomes so involved, doubly so considering the lack of leeway and unwieldy camera controls. I would assume if you were "close enough" to landing a difficult jump, there might be some lenience and let you have it, but it seems precision is the name of the game here, and that's unfortunate because I was unable to progress further.Lunistice can be fun but I feel its audience is very narrow, and unfortunately I am not in this audience. I do really like the art design and direction, everything looks so fantastic that it was the first thing to draw me to the game, but the actual gameplay is just not that interesting to me. I look forward to seeing what this team can do in the future because it's obvious there is real talent behind the game.Game runs at a locked 60fps irrespective of ingame settings, as well as when max TDP is lowered to as low as 5w. Battery life at lower TDP is greatly expanded, but this is a given considering the simplistic levels and graphics.Controls are fine as stock but I advise fiddling with sensitivities and camera controls because it can be disorienting at times given the nature of the game. Doubly so because of the sometimes frenetic camera work needed to navigate some levels.No issues at all on the Deck, it ran great and looks great. The filesize is also quite small so it could be attractive to those with smaller MicroSD cards or internal storage Decks.

_childDocuments_.review: World 3-2 is not good. The spherical balloon platforms bounce you very inconsistently unless you land in the exact same spot but if you try and slow down to land more precisely you lose the momentum you need to get to the next baloon. It's very difficult to develope muscle memory because your momentum is never consistent from one bounce to the next and they make you navigate 20 of these bounces in a row with no checkpoints. It was not fun just randomly punishing.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a 3D platformer upon floating islands.  The goal is to get to the end of the levels.  I don't have much good to say about it.I tried liking this game, I really did.  I was going for all achievements, but I noticed I was not having fun.  The biggest problem are the paper cranes.  The game makes you feel like you should collect all of them.  This massively slows down the game play as you scour every corner for them.  If you miss one crane in a level, you have to play the entire level all over again if you want to go for all of them.  This can become infuriating after spending all this time looking for every single crane only to be told you have to do it all over again.  There's just so many of them, and how they're placed, it made me so angry while playing.Hana, is not that great to control.  You have to turn on a more visible shadow in the menu.  A shadow, so you can tell where Hana is going to land.  I did not figure this out until the final level.  I can't tell you how many jumps I failed because of this.  There is also smoother turning turned on by default, which makes Hana's turns look better but be less sharp, leading to death.The level design, it's just a bunch of floating islands.  If there is any world building to these levels, I didn't find it.  It's just a set of very linear themed islands.  There are vine grind rails.  You can hold the control stick a certain way to go faster.  But where that indicator was placed, I just found this distracted me from any jumps or enemies I had to hit while doing them.  But there are a few secret paths, and if you miss any of them, have fun collecting all of the cranes again!  While the cranes are mostly on path, the paranoia that I would miss one would not go away.  Just slowing the game down dramatically.There is a story, it is not worth it.  To experience it you have to collect all of the Hana letters, then look out for the new opening.  I didn't really know this the first time playing, leading to me having to play all of the levels again, just to progress the plot.  And the ending, there is all this build up, but it doesn't really pay off.  It ends just before the good part, and it's unsatisfying.There are more characters with their own unique stages.  But in order to play them you have to beat the first 5 levels all over again.  And after I had just replayed the first 5 levels to unlock the story, I was just done.Overall this game left me very angry and frustrated.  I tried to go for the achievements, they seem doable, but the game is too frustrating for me to continue.  Everything in this game is okay, but nothing is done great enough for me to look past my frustration.  I would recommend this game only as a last resort.  There is nothing in this game I feel wasn't done better in other games.  And even the story, it felt too scattered and sparse that it wasn't that appealing, even if you are a fan of the tropes it involves.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't recommend this game. The controls are very floaty and slippy, you could land on a platform and just randomly slip off for no reason. Also it's a bit glitchy as you can just go straight through certain objects like rails next to edges which should stop you from slipping but don't. I think this game was purely made for speed runners only and any one looking for a casual experience should definitely give this one a miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, looks nice and there's cool music, but for a 2022 game it doesn't have a f'ing remapping buttons option?! Nope, thank you.Joysticks these days are made in a way that your hands are naturally placed in a position where your index fingers are on top of L2 and R2. I have a King Kong 2 PRO, btw. The game requires you to press L1 and R1 to attack and jump respectively. This whole game consists of you pressing those buttons several times per minute. I'm neither getting tendinitis over this nor jumping through hoops to connect a DualShock3 (the last actually good controller ever made) to my PC.There's a feature on Steam to remap buttons, but that doesn't work properly. The commands you set to those buttons are stacked on each other. So if I attack on L2, I also recenter the camera. And if I jump on R2, I also jump less than I would because that's the button to walk instead of run.If this silly overlooked mistake is ever fixed, I'll consider buying it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 There are other games worth your attention over this. But if you have played everything else, I guess this can do.The controls are bad but can be made  different kind of bad that is... less bad? if you dont mind over shooting your targets as oppossed to undershooting with the disable smooth turning feature.The game obscures the story and ending behind collectables that are also obscured. We call this a regressive padding trait of games from an outdated time. Bad. Bad design.The game is also very short but the repetitive sound and gameplay design of collecting hundreds of cranes per level is just tiring and annoying after the 3rd time around. It doesnt hold up.It seems like it would be made for completionists but theres nothing to earn for it. Just some worthless p ranks, you unlock everything after beeting the game anyway. and as for the ending? save your self some time and look it up on youtube. Spoiler alert, its not worth it.I can see other people liking this game, but I was just a slog to get through and i blame the collect-a-thon padding for this. If they had removed this, fixed some persective issues with the level design and actually had a story to tell that wasnt obscured, this would have been a 7.5-8. As-is. Just play any other 3d platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: This seems to be purely a speed runner game without variety or creative enemy design and behaviour. _childDocuments_.review: Broken game, running on a RTX 4090 and this thing stutters so much it makes my eyes hurt and miss jumps which is a requirement of the game in order to make it through levels.makes Hogwarts Legacy look like it runs smooth as butter in comparison, even Spyro Enter the dragonfly on ps2 has better frame rate than this pile of crap.Edit: this only seems to happen in fullscreen don't know why this game only runs smoothly in windowed.

_childDocuments_.review: Controls are just slightly too floaty and imprecise.  I never feel secure trying to hit enemies especially those in the air.  The camera needs constant baby sitting and is often too low to be able to see the character shadow to know where I'm landing.  The level design is not clear which route is optional or which is the main path which leads to missing collectibles forcing a replay simply because you couldn't tell which route was which and there's no way to go backwards.Super Lucky's Tale, Mail Mole, both better indie 3D platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun throwback to old school 3d mascot platformers, complete with the difficulty in later levels and the hidden collection challenges. I admit, I got quite frustrated at some of the hidden challenges. (Though to be fair, I unintentionally made the collection challenges harder by thinking they had to be done in a single run. They don't. That's my fault not the games.) As some have said, the actual story of the game is very basic, but I feel its just fine for what this game is trying to be. All in all, a very fun time for both casual players and those who are looking for a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I played this in a state while not being in a super gaming mood.  So take that as a boost to this game's value.This game feels right.  And if I had a few seconds, or just an elevator pitch for the game, it would be that simple phrase.It's a simple 3D platformer mixed with collect-a-thon elements.  It has a cute artstyle and easy on the eyes.  The music is calming too.The level design feels so fined tuned to the physics and I literally struggle to say anything but it just feels right.  You'll sense a theme here.  The collectibles, small and more important, are nearly always on a path where you can get every single one without repeating level geometry.  So while you don't need the collectibles, if you want the S-Ranks, it feels natural.   It's exploration that can involve some searching, but not so hidden that it becomes a huge burden.The resets for ranks are fine.  It's an extremely easy game, but that is perfectly fine.  If you find it stressful, do both ranks separately.I can't add much else for positive without repeating much.  So skipping around and coming back.The negatives.  I came across only two glitches, and was in disbelief both times that it wasn't something else.  This isn't important, but I'm just saying the game feels polished.  The only legitimate complaint I have in this game, ever, was that sometimes platforms can be hard to see, like the cloud/rock things in level 6.  There are also a select few where you might need to backtrack for like a small section of collectibles.  Maybe like 4 times across over 30 important branches.Two illegitimate things I had issues with.  One, there is no momentum things or ways to go faster.  There is vertical momentum conservation which I do appreciate.  I also just feel quite slow in this game.  However, that is literally my issue, as this isn't a momentum-based platformer.  It's not the genre, and I am just a speed addict.My other issue was that the character felt super weighted.  Turning around requires a lot.  So uh... smooth turning being on was the sole cause, it makes it so responsive without it.  However, I think that there may be an in-between that is better for everybody, as not smooth might be too sensitive generally.So to finish this, this game is the epitome of capitalizing on that "flow-state" you achieve when you just hold forward in a 3D platformer and just never stop platforming.  Idunno, I'm awfully rambling and I don't want to spoil things.  The classic music builds as you play level should not be the second level after we heard the theme.   This game is like 5 dollars, it's really good for 3D platforming fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Very small but very fun 3D platformer. Charming art style with charming worlds, solid platforming, and character design. Only level I had qualms with was the rhythm section, but it's manageable and those parts of platfomers tend to be hit or miss for me anyways. Plus there's many collectables, a ranking system, and post-game options that adds lots of replayablity if you find the main experience a little short. Well worth the small price that it tends to go for.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: If you took 3D Sonic, merged it with Katamari Damacy's aesthetic and made it hard as nails, you have Lunistice. Despite being intentionally PS1-themed, the aesthetic is drop-dead gorgeous through the use of amazing texture work, lighting and environments. The music is also absolutely fantastic, and the level design is polished and top-notch, at least mostly.That said, the lack of any sort of overt story or payoff for winning unless you go full sweaty speedrunner mode to unlock the lore bits, is disappointing. Even after beating the game, I had no clue what was happening, and likely never will unless I go for 100%.Yeah, yeah, game is cheap, yadda yadda. But I'd gladly have paid more for even a bit more of a fleshed-out story. As it is, it's a collection of levels but feels a tad unfinished as a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: very short aesthetically flawless sega saturn-esque platformer making good use of Slight weight and momentum (to the point where u have a Slow Down button rather than a run button). very buttery and enveloping, a nice piece of interaction to take in 15-20 minute bites. hana is super cool and id love to see her in a bigger game with a bigger moveset
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game, but there's an option turned on by default that makes it feel 1000x worse to control, can't understand why they decided to do that. But if you turn smooth turning off in the settings, this is an excellent platformer with incredible level design. Like top tier level design for a platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun platformer I've played in a long time. The movement is responsive and precise, stage design varied and well thought out, and the music is excellent. There's even some tidbits of story that I was genuinely interested in and wish we got more. Getting all the achievements for the game was genuinely fun which is something I can't say for 99% of other games out there; there's also some great replay value here. This game is a steal at its asking price, if you're thinking about picking it up just do it!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: What do you look for in a 3D platformer? Precise movement, good level design, a reasonable difficulty curve, and replayability. Lunistice excels at perfecting this formula in its simplicity. It's worth it if you want a short but satisfying experience, while offering a challenge if you want to complete 100% of the game. It's worth its full price, but it's constantly on sale. Just buy it
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! It really brings back some of my childhood memories! I don't have much to say, but try it out! There's a demo, and the game itself is extremely cheap. The only downside is that it's kind of short, with you probably being able to beat it in 3 or 4 hours, but there's lots of replayability. Especially if you try to beat your personal best or (like in my case) actually get a decent time! The levels are pretty short too, so if you have a Steam Deck and a few minutes to spare you can easily do one or two if you're just waiting around.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a gem of a little platformer, well worth the $5 I payed for it.  A mashup of Crash Bandicoot and Sonic Adventure, the game is short, sweet, plays well, sounds great, and has a fun little subversive twist that makes it very memorable.  Honestly a gold standard for indie platformers everywhere, more games should be like Lunistice.

_childDocuments_.review: After switching to the alternate controls (which should definitely be the default controls???) it's a lovely looking, sounding a playing platformer. _childDocuments_.review: Cute and fairly short platformer with a very nice aesthetic artstyle! Movement felt good and level gimmicks were pretty fun. Not much enemy variety and the plot seemed a little out there to me. For the very low price I paid for this it was honestly a steal! For a quick and easy platformer this was worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is such a nice platformer to play! It's one of those humble small games that while doesn't have a whole lot special with it - reminds you of the value in small titles like this.The movement is snappy and easy to control, and the gameplay reminds of Super Mario Galaxy in its basic 3D platforming. The music is good, I find myself enjoying a few world themes quite a lot. Lunistice has a fairly simple but good story, mostly obtained through collecting the letters throughout each level.I honestly have nothing against this game! It's a good yet small platformer, and I'm happy with what it does. It's worth the playthrough if you just want a small 3D platformer to have fun in!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This platformer is an absolute delight and a great example of reduction-based game design.The game features a series of levels with gradually increasing difficulty (though none of them are terribly hard), multiple playable characters, and a deceptively simple character controller that provides a lot of depth to the movement system.Lunistice encourages a speedrunning mindset and measures your time and deaths, and gives you plenty of tools to min-max your time as you gain expertise with its mechanics. There are enemies, but they only really function moving hazards and aren't very threatening. REDUCTION:As I said, this game takes a reductionist philosophy, and it's worth applauding what is NOT in Lunistice:-a combat system (save for a simple spin attack which is largely a movement tool)-overly aggressive enemies-bosses-movement tools or mechanics outside of the player's initial kit-any sort of upgrades-health pickups-high-stress gameplay (i.e. no inclusion of a "lava is constantly rising" level or any such trope)A couple small gripes:-levels feature branching paths that become dead ends and exist to give key or key-like items, however the main path is not always clear -some extreme skill jumps/platforming sections exist with no rewards, just deadends. I suppose the developer thinks making the jumps is its own reward?As such, Lunistice is a fairly unambitious, simple, delightful game. A great way to relax at the end of the day.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me a lot of Mario, honestly.The controls and level design feel like something out of the Galaxy games to be specific.There's even a stage that plays similarly to one level from Galaxy 2 as well.Aside from that, this game is incredibly fun to play even if it's a relatively short game.Instant 10/10 for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely 3D Platformer that is super cute and nostalgic. Simple mechanics. Play fast or slow its up to you. Fun platforming, fun level hazards and mechanics. BANGER and super cozy OST specifically stages 5 and 6, but whole OST slaps. A fun game to pick up anytime and enjoy the beautiful scenery. Great stuff for a low price.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful little platformer with some replay value. I would say that it's primarily inspired by Mario Galaxy's mechanics--in terms of platforming--while maintaining a reasonable amount of speed that would be found from the Sonic franchise.It's wonderfully responsive with mouse and keyboard, and with a controller as well!Sound design and music is the biggest highlight for me! It really reminds me of Nights into Dreams!From the sound of collecting paper cranes, to the catchy soundtrack.I, unfortunately, find the story to be a little lacking. I was very confused with the Kingdom Hearts // Nier: Automata-like ending... I can't seem to piece it together.Nonetheless, a wonderful and reasonably short platformer <3P.S. // Spoilers: The player starts with a fox character lady, and upon beating the game, they'll receive two avian characters. Not a single cat to be found! :(
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Insanely good 3D platformer with the best feeling movement and level flow I've ever played. A pure joy to play and replay with every character and aim for s-ranks and low times. I only wish there were more difficult levels, and that the game would also rank you on time. For a game that plays this fast, it's extremely fun to beat levels as fast as possible, but there is no internal barometer or scoring mechanism for doing so. Would be nice if you were ranked or even given "dev times" ala Mario Kart to compete with. As is you'll have to jump into the game's speedrunning community on discord, which is perhaps not the level of engagement everyone is looking for (myself included).Still, an excellent game and an absolute steal for five bucks. Excited to see what comes next from this dev.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Let me say, this game was 100% an impulse buy. It was cheap, looked good and reviews are amazing and rightfully so. I was a bit on the fence about buying this game because, and I mean this in the nicest way possible, furries. I was afraid it was gonna be something else fro some reason but this game did not disappoint. I've read some reviews about how people are comparing this game to the Sega Saturn games. Oh my god how they were right, this is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love letter to the console. This was such a good time and such an amazing platformer. If you want some nostalgia, a very good platformer ans some challenging jumps. This game will not dissapoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good platformer that falls a little bit on the harder side in comparison to platformers like New Super Lucky's Tale. Although it is (mostly) a fun type of hard.I bought this game mainly because of its artstyle. I know PSX graphics are really popular now but I see them mostly in horror games etc. so seeing a mascot platformer with colorful level was a pleasant surprise. Levels are very well structured. There's the classical approach of having a main path with some harder paths that reward you with extra letters which form a name of protagonists. They’re pretty easy to spot and in the entire game I only missed one secret but that’s on me since I lost my focus. This structure plays well with the character movement that is meant to be fast. By not making any secrets or collectibles obscure the overall flow of blasting through the level is never interrupted. There’s seven worlds with 2 levels each. What’s worth mentioning is that every of those seven worlds has some new mechanic, introduces new gimmicks or focuses more on the ones already introduced. The first level is more of an introduction while the latter one is more robust and fun. It’s a simple yet brilliant way that prevents Lunastice from getting stale. There's also crossover with other indie 3D platformers. When I found out there’s no new levels for them and I could only replay the old ones I was disappointed. I still decided to give it a shot and I’m glad I did. Those new characters completely recontextualize those old levels and it’s best to think of them more as extra challenges. For example Toree is basically “what if you couldn’t attack and had one life” of course there’s more changes such as higher mobility to compensate for the lack of attack move that was also used to jump farther. It’s a great addition for players who enjoyed the base game and want to do something more but just replaying it isn’t appealing for them. There’s also quite satisfying reward for completing those levels but I’ll leave it for others to figure out themselves.So this is when my first complaint is. The achievement that requires the player to destroy every single crystal in the level to me is like “why would you do that”. I know it’s totally optional but why add achievement that promotes playing this game in the least fun way possible? I skipped that of course but it still leaves me confused.I mentioned that this game can be hard but mostly in a fun way. Well, because of few annoyances it isn't always the case. The problem I actually have is how the camera works. It can be janky and sometimes you can’t see anything other than some random wall which can cause one to fall and lose. Also a lot of times I struggled to jump on the platforms correctly and I’m not sure why. It wasn’t like that in other games but it was really hard for me to see depth properly which resulted in me falling down the level because of my misjudgement. I think there has to be something wrong with the shadows because a lot of times it was hard for me to spot my character’s shadow. That was the case especially with those high speed tracks. It turns out that was the case since I learned that there’s drop shadow toggle in the settings. I think it greatly improves overall experience which makes it surprising it wasn’t turned on by default.At the end of the day those complaints are minor inconveniences and didn’t have a huge impact on my enjoyment especially since this game is so brief there’s not enough time to get tired of it before completing it.Definitely worth the price if you look for some nice evening with retro inspired 3D platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Platformer with a pleasant character controller. Each of the levels has time trials, coins to collect, and optional "challenge" items to pick up as well. None of the enemy types seem particularly difficult to overcome with the game's generous healthbar, but the coins and enemies do blend into the environment at times. I prefer the game without the pixel shader, and there are options to modify that and much more. The single cutscene is concise, surprisingly not cliche, AND skippable. Excellently made game, I'm just not one for retrying levels to get a higher letter grade.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Oh this is such a short & sweet game! Pleasant style, music and a cute lil Tanuki too!I love the movement, it feels like there's an input delay but it's adaptable! The levels are short and sweet and the story is short but captivating.. Wish there was more!Part of me wishes time also accounted for ranking, but perhaps that would have been too much combined with crane collecting?For the price, this game is definitely worth picking up!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Completed as of writing this review: All S-Ranks as Hana.A nice, good-looking, indie platformer. To be honest the movement on the controller was a little too sensitive to my liking but I got used to it. The art-style is definitely the highlight, mixing the dated graphics and dream-like aesthetic. The music was good, although the first stages sounded a lil bit repetitive. My only criticism is collecting cranes. If collecting letters is optional, then why do cranes lead to them? I didn't like this idea that I had to go on a linear path due to cranes but partially it's my fault for wanting to collect everything on the first try. I also didn't really understand the main goal in the plot, though it's probably intentional that way. Also adding Toree was a cute touch. The skill ceiling is a little higher than mid, so I'd only suggest you play this if you're ready for precise jumping, which was fine for me but might be tough for anyone else. Summing up, I had a solid time, even if a little stressful due to S-Ranks and it's a good little game!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: lovely and cute, joyful and masterfully designed 3D platformer.reminds me some good things about NiGHTS, Sonic Robo Blast, Super Mario 64...why nobody is talking about it? art, atmosphere, colors, game play, super cool pixel graphics, tunes playing in the background... just WOW,  love it already so much!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay feels great, not so simple as it looks and each new mechanics adds some layers of complexity. I just want to speedrun this game now, the level design is so incredibly well done you want to overcome yourself for each level, going as fast as possible.The decoration for each level is quite simple, but very adequate for a plateformer game and gives each level some sort of uniqueness, along with the music which is also 10/10While the story may not be as important as gameplay and level design, I find it well written and sufficient, it makes you want to explore the world and 100% everything to have more I hope you will continue to make games, but for now thank you for this masterpiece
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A simple, cute, and well designed game that proves that you don't need super advanced graphics or gameplay mechanics to create a beautiful, enjoyable experience in a video game. My amazing friend got this for me as a gift and I could not be happier with the experience I've had so far. Levels simple and well designed, with some challenging elements to make collecting all of the items engaging. While there is a good bit of exploration to be done, most levels are relatively linear and easy to navigate. Not overly complex to the point you'll get lost, but not linear enough to be boring. The graphics are absolutely stunning as well, despite clearly taking inspiration from N64/PS2 games, the devs somehow made everything you encounter look like something magical out of a dream. The music is on point too, reminds me of old Sega Dreamcast games like Monkey Ball and perfectly encapsulates the vibe of running through this world straight out of someone's imagination. This game is a friendly reminder that each individual video game that releases is not just another part of a certain genre, but a work of art within itself. Definitely recommended for those who like 3d platformers as much as I do, this game is a hidden gem and definitely trumps anything Nintendon't or any large game production studio could possibly produce.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly short but awesome 3D platformer with gorgeous visuals, wonderful music and fun but challenging gameplay. It took me a little over 2 hours to go through all stages & finish the game, but i'm way too casual to go for 100% completion. My guess is it takes about 8-10 hours for all side activities and challenges + all achievements. For 5 bucks, it's an absolute steal!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly a pretty solid game, specially considering it was a 30 day project. If it wasn't because I don't find the other characters as fun to play as Hana, I would have actually 100% this game. If you want something short with decent replayability, then I personally think this is a safe purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game nice retro graphics. Levels are cool. The game does get progressively difficult (This applies when playing as other characters). It's not like some of the old retro games it's basically just a jumping platformer so the story is not really there (I think there is one but it was some info at the start which I skipped)
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, it's a fun little romp. The story is simple but unfolds in a satisfying way. The world and characters are all really cute and riff on the ps1 aesthetic quite well.I hated the music sections because I'm bad at music. Otherwise the game was fire.If you aren't me you might get another 4 hours out of the side characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: CAP FPS TO 60 OR THE CAMERA ACTS FUNKY.A great game for 3d platformer lovers and newbies. i'd say if you want to get into them from 2d plats this is perfect because it has a simplistic moveset. Literally aim and jump and you're good. That said, I think it's made for those who want more precision based platforming and to go fast fast fast, almost like Sonic. If you want a game that has a ton of moves then this isn't for you. However, this is also so simple you can pick it up and play whenever you want.  I come back to this one every so often for a palette cleanser just because it's so straightforward.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Insane 3D platformer with tight controls, high replay value, and progressively added stage gimmicks that make the game stay fresh throughout. It's really short, though, as an average playthrough of the game can take about an hour. But the various playable characters unlocked upon beating the game keeps the game from feeling undercooked, so I highly recommend it to any 3D platformer fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Very tight and enjoyable platformer that is a joy to play. Nice progression of levels. Only adjustment I might make is to make landing on rails a little more lenient. The addition of having other characters to try is a great addition to the game's longevity and a testament to the game and level design. Easily worth $5
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a short but sweet experience that I believe deserves the time of day to everyone who loves 3D platformers. Such a simple but effective control scheme made to create a fun experience with a ton of replayability with the rank system, secrets, and the unlockable characters. The levels are well designed, and absolutely beautiful with vibrant colors and that old polygon look of a bygone era. It truly is a happy, dreamlike experience, with some of the best music I've ever heard from an indie project. At such an affordable price, the creator almost sells themself short, but it's such a kind gesture nonetheless. It can be a few hour experience, or up to 10 if you're like me who wanted to 100% all the achievements. If you want something cozy and pleasant to repeatedly come back to, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Played this all summer in 2023 and I can't stop myself from coming back to it! One of the best platformers I've ever played! The entire world is bursting with color, the game play is smooth and fast, and the soundtrack has some fantastic vibes. Highly recommend to anyone looking for an affordably priced platformer!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: BUY. THIS. GAME. It is so immaculate. The platforming feels perfect, the levels are pretty and inventive. Wonderful music and art style. This game is just honestly PERFECT. Such a sweet experience. TRUST ME I’ve played a bunch of 3d platformers throughout my whole life, and this is one of the best of the best. Brimming with creativity and freedom, it deserves to be experienced by everyone. THANK YOU DEVS
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and a good deal for the price. So its hard complain giving the price point but when a game presents a bit story/lore i start hoping for more and it just doesnt deliver on that front. But as long as you dont get your hopes up for something or expect anything substantial as far as a story goes... its a good game even if rather short. Again i only wish the story was more developed because I became interested in the world that was presented.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having a blast, this is one of those super chill 3rd person platformers that are great to just unwind before bed. In fact that's what I've been doing, and if you want to run it on the Steam Deck like me, rest assured it runs flawlessly with every graphic settings and looks really nice. I managed to 'finish' the main game in about 3-4 hours but there's a ton of replay value in the form of extra challenges and other unlockables I'm still chewing through. If you're a completionist, the game is challenging, but not unfair. It controls well and you never really have a death that you feel to yourself, "aw that was cheap". Post game content comments: Honestly, my closing thoughts with indie developers like these, we're living in a golden era for platformer enjoyers like myself. So if you want a quick, chill, easy going game, you can't go wrong with Lunistice.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A great, simple platformer that proves you don't need to have big budgets, fancy graphics or complicated mechanics to have a good time playing games. It's like a piece of the best German or Belgium chocolate, short, sweet and perfection.Protip: map your camera controls to your controller's shoulder buttons, this will allow you to never take your thumbs off both sticks and so you never have to stop to adjust the camera.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Short but highly replayable and polished, Lunistice is everything you could ask for in an extremely affordable package. Many self-billed retro 3D platformers have a tendency to willingly stand in the shadow of their inspirations, so it was a nice breath of fresh air to play one that has a strong gameplay and visual identity of its own rather than just refining and iterating on an existing design.My only major criticism is that the controls are so sensitive yet precise that it takes some getting used to. I played with "smooth turning" turned off, as I felt that the turning radius was very awkward with it on and didn't really address any gripes I might have had with the controls. I feel like a third option between the two extremes might have been a more ideal compromise, but I was otherwise satisfied with the options provided to tweak the controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great and I can absolutely recommend it. The controls are smooth and perfectly designed for the game's platforming mechanic, the music is great, the visual style is so unique; even though we've gotten a veritable deluge of indie 3D platformers in recent memory, this game still stands out from the rest.There are four main collectibles (the letters) in each level. The off roads you need to take to get each letter are usually pretty obvious, which I can't tell you how much I appreciate. I've played enough platformers where the collectibles are too hidden and it ruins the pacing of the game. I can only recall a couple of times that I was scratching my head trying to find a letter.If the game were a few levels longer, it would probably get a bit repetitive without a bit more enemy variety (you don't really encounter any new enemy designs past the third world, I think). But as it stands, this is a very impressive package. Looking forward to this dev's next projects.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game, great difficulty and very amazing aesthetic. It took me about 6 hours to beat, 8 if you count the time I spent playing the demo, but that's just because I try too hard to get things perfect instead of just playing through like you probably will, great game and absolutely amazing for the price!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly well done, simple but challenging speed platformer that feels heavily inspired by 3D Sonic, but does more than enough to stand on its own. The game is visually beautiful, probably one of the best looking examples of the "retro" low-poly look you'll find in a platformer. The music is so well done too. My only complaint is that around Dream 5, difficulty ramps up pretty suddenly (the sweets world made me want to scream) and the engine isn't always quite able to deliver the precision needed to complete jumps every single time. It's doable, but hard. Overall, this is a damn good platformer, and at $5 I'd argue that there are very few games with a better price-to-value than this. Give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A very simple 3D platformer that could be completed much faster than I did it but I enjoy the simplicity behind it. The controls feel tight and it makes for a solid proof of concept. I would love to see a more full game utilizing what is showcased in the game (an average playthrough for one character would be under 3 hours easily)The music is serviceable and compliments the game well but nothing really stuck with me after beating the game.Worth a playthroug
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: i like collectathons. the platforming is pretty mindless for me, i think i would've liked it more when i was a kid. i think it would've been much more up my ally back then because of its extremely simple gameplay - you just jump on stuff and avoid or kill obstacles, and if you collect all the things, theres some lore to read if you want to. its not for people looking for a difficult or highly-precise platforming experience, its much more of a casual experience (which, to be clear, *is* what i was after, personally, because i really suck at platformers lol).
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Tip for anyone going for Toree S-ranks: staying in the green zone on rails allows you to kill enemies on the rails.As for the review, if you're going through the game casually, it's an easy recommend, especially for just $5. There are some pretty cool ideas for levels too, such as the music levels where platforms and obstacles change on the beat, or the level where the music's instruments slowly come in as you collect the 3 tears. Music and art are pretty decent too.However, if you're going for all achievements and/or all S ranks, that's more debatable. Your character seems to maintain their rail momentum until they land, which makes air control much harder, especially if you're trying to land on the same rail again. Most of this criticism doesn't apply once I figured out the trick with Toree as mentioned at the top, but there are still 2 sections that require it, and doing those levels deathless can be frustrating. The hitbox for landing on a rail seems pretty small too, and there were several moments where it felt like I clipped through the rail rather than landing back on it.As for going for S-ranks, the achievements don't require you to get all collectibles and go deathless in the same run, but if you decide to do it for fun, the game can start getting pretty frustrating. When I was doing playthroughs with the other 2 characters, I decided to just do another separate run for a level if I died, rather than trying to go for both in the same run because it started getting annoying.Finally...the final level for Toukie. I really did not like this. 900 collectibles is absolutely ridiculous. Also, the hardest part of the level, where you have to jump onto moving platforms, is at the very end. So trying to do this level deathless, especially since getting to the final part takes 7-10 minutes, gets annoying really quick.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: fun little game, i got about 4 hours of enjoyment out of it and i could see going back for another playthrough at some point. it's got real good PS1 spyro / n64 glover / dreamcast 3D Sonic vibes to it. if you have nostalgia for those games, this is a super focused and polished reflection on those. played excellently on the steam deck, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty solid, cute platformer. I think it's great and you should support the dev.It's just not for me.Don't get me wrong, it's great. I love short indie 3d platformers. I just found myself resetting every level when I made it to the end and realized I'd missed some collectibles. Constantly restarting to try and find them all eventually got frustrating, especially since I don't even know if there's a good reason TO find them. But, I'm NOT gonna refund this game because I think the dev did a pretty good job. And it's cheap.Again, solid game. Buy it. And dev - by all means, make more.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Just 100%'d this game and omg I had a blast. This game is so heckin good and the price-point for it is so beyond worth it! If you are on the fence about this game, don't be. The level design and the gameplay are so CLEAN and I cannot stress this enough. If you are looking for a fast paced platformer this is a must have.To the Devs, you have absolutely inspired me to get into Game design. Keep up the amazing work! I'd love to see more from y'all, especially in this style.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. I absolutely love the 32-bit aesthetic! The game controls well, the movement is fun, and there's a lot of replay value, whether it be mastering the game's movement to get good times, or getting all of the collectibles. The little bits of lore are neat too. There's also cute designs and a fantastic soundtrack to boot! I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A really simple platformer (though that's not a bad thing in this case) with a great art style and good music that has INCREDIBLY smooth controls that flow really well with the levels. Lunistice does suffer from some weird difficulty spikes and is relatively easy to 100% but id still very much recommend it especially with its cheap asking price. Would like to see what else the developers make next, hopefully it controls just as good!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game was honestly a breath of fresh air. I sort of fell off playing platformers mostly when I was younger, but this sorta awoke something in me. I felt like I was a kid again playing my old N64 or GameCube. The game is very polished and the music is amazing. I've played fully priced games with way worse quality than this, this actually feels like it has soul and I only paid 4 dollars for it. Some parts admittedly made me want to tear my hair out from frustration but that was no fault of the game, simply my skill level. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: the art: buoyant and pleasingthe feel: simple and cleanthe vibe: fresh and friendlythe difficulty: well-tuned and balancedthe game: good and cooli *do not* need to play more than this first hour to leave a review. i already know what the heck's good.i *am going* to beat the game, then i am going to s-rank the levels.i *will come back* to hang out in the game, appreciating it's timbre while trying to get good times on each stage.thus i have spoken. thus it is written.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I was DYING for a game with actually good movement and this delivered perfectly. It reminds me of the best aspects of Sonic and Marble Blast Ultra.Pros:* Super fun and fast movement* Forgiving hitboxes* A difficulty curve that is actually smooth* Wonderfully cute aesthetic* Amazing soundtrack* 3 characters adds good variety to the game* By the end of 2 characters S ranks I felt like I'd conquered the game and the third was easier because of my skill increase* S ranks in collectibles and no resets are separate (10/10 dev decision sincerely)* Actually achievable achievements* Perfect length for what it offers* Deepest lore* JerryCons:* Food level platforms kicked my ass
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a short, difficult and awesome game! The difficulty gets harder extremely quickly but I think is generally manageable. I'd like to see more camera options for example, moving the camera closer or further away from the player. I also didn't see options for change refresh rate (the game might handle that automatically?) I would also like to see more checkpoints in some levels.Summed up, would I suggest this game? Absolutely yes!Thank you to those who made this game possible and for those who are reading this! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a really charming platformer. The gameplay and pacing is great, along with a pretty upbeat soundtrack. I love the Nintendo DS artstyle, great callback and an artstyle which is rarely done by a lot of developers. I thoroughly enjoyed my playthrough.  I fully suggest getting this game while on sale - it's a great buy for Steam Deck owners. • The store page might need a little refresh. Especially the cover art - it sadly leaves the impression that game is isn't of quality and kind of undersells your game. I've been past this page before when going through the Steam Discovery Queue and turned my nose due to a couple things on the page. Might be worth a little refresh. • I'm trying to 100% the achievements in this game. However, I'm finding it frustrating when trying to get all the cranes in a single run, and I get to the end and find out I just missed one and cannot go back. It'd be nice if I missed a crane and go past a point of no return, that it simply just gives some indication that you can no longer collect all of the cranes by the end of the level. Maybe just a strike-through on the numbers. I've had it multiple times where I've completed a level and have one missing crane, and sometimes I missed it the start. I think this would make things a little less frustrating having to complete the full level and realise you wasted your time because you didn't get an impromptu.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is the complete package. Easily one of my favourites.The platforming is just so much fun, I can't stress that enough. Each level design is awesome and there are new gimmicks and harder challenges as you make your way through. Going for S-ranks (no deaths and all collectibles) was really satisfying because it never took too long to perfect. The levels are a good length so it wasn't frustrating to have to reset.The art style is gorgeous, and I particularly like the artistic choice for the very last level, especially coupled with the music.The whole soundtrack is incredible and complements the game so well (credits to Knasibas). I've had it on repeat for the past week. For me, music gives an emotional connection to a game, so I really love it when an OST stands out.Everything just fits together perfectly.I got all the achievements as Hana, but I will definitely go back some time to complete the game for the other characters, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: What a great 5th-gen styled 3D platformer! I love the gameplay, physics, level design, music, aesthetics, the overall beautiful simplicity of the game, the intriguing optional story, the loop of acquiring the collectables, and the cool main character. Also, it'll only cost you a few bucks. So, what are you waiting for? I've 100% completed the game both on Switch and on PC, and I had a blast! I can't wait for the DLC! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent 3D platformer. There's this saying that you're closer to perfection when there's less to take away or remove from your game. There's a level of polish to the controls, visuals, and level design that's on the level of recent Mario games when you play as the main character Hana. But, then you have an additional (surprise) playable character that I think puts 3D Sonic to shame. All of this is supported with an charming aesthetic that reminds you of the 32bit console era, but with a modern polish. Lunistice is one of my new favorite 3D platformers!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: What a little belter of a game. Lunistice is a 3D platformer deliberately designed as throwback to the 32/64 bit heyday of the genre. It’s more of a level-based obstacle course design than a collectathon, and plainly owes a lot to Sonic. In fact it feels like the Saturn Sonic game that never was, with 25 years of game design hindsight and hardware that won’t cook itself to death under the strain.3D platformers live or die on the strength of their controls and camera, and both are excellent here. The controls are pitch perfect and feel like they’ve been through a lot of refinement. They’re fast and fluid without ever feeling imprecise and have a wonderful flow to them. Levels are designed with both newcomers and speedrunners in mind, and the difficulty curve is mostly pitched perfectly (with the exception of certain disappearing platforms in 4-2 which can go to hell). There’s a decent number of them too, as well as two extra characters when you finish the game. While it can be completed in 4-5 hours, there’s a lot of replay value here for completionists and speedrunners.The real shocker? They want a fiver for this. Five English pounds. That’s insane value for something that could easily be sold for three times that. They even have a demo, you know, if you’re not sure whether this can compete with a pint. If you have even the slightest interest in retro 3D platformers, just pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite good, but the difficulty is a bit beyond my enjoyment level. However, I do prefer easier games in general, so that's on me. The quality is definitely high, only nitpicks are that it's a bit hard to see where you're landing, and the default settings give you a pretty wide turn radius. The former can be improved slightly by turning off the vertical lock for the camera in the options, letting you put the camera above you when needed, but what would be better would be if your shadow showed up from higher than it does. You have to be fairly close to the ground for the shadow to appear and give you a good feel for your landing spot. The turn radius can be fixed pretty much entirely by turning off smooth turning in the options. Definitely change those settings to have a better time. Recommended if you like decently difficult platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is an absolute gem of a game, one where I genuinely wish I had found it sooner so that I could've played it sooner. It has a single sore spot, but the rest of it is just a lovingly crafted gem.The graphics are very purposefully low quality, though it's more so that they're "Pseudo-Low-Quality". Everything beyond a certain point has a pixellation filter applied, and all objects are very low poly. The textures and lighting, however, are top notch. It makes it feel like a modern remaster of an old 3d platformer rather than a remake, and yet this is an entirely  game. Obviously this is meant to replicate the feeling of old SEGA games, and I think it does a wonderful job in doing so.The audio design is great too. Like, seriously, this game has an extremely underrated OST. The UI sounds are simple but not annoying, same with gameplay sounds. It's a very simple, very tight sound design that works wonders.The gameplay is also simple, but certainly not as easy as it would first appear. It's a 3d platformer, with precision jumping and timings. If you just want to take your time and slowly beat each level, you can do so. Time is unlimited and you don't have lives so you can die as many times as is necessary. The difficulty comes in doing optional objectives or in doing a level fast, like getting an S rank on a stage or finding all of the name blocks. Those in particular require strict timings and precision jumping to complete, especially with S ranks requiring you to beat the stage without dying. The ONE bad thing I will not is that two levels in the game have mandatory rhythm-platforming sections that stretch across the entire level. No, these cannot be skipped, so if you cannot or will not play rhythm games then that section may be a red flag for you.The story is very minimal, but it gives you enough to piece together everything IF you go for optional objectives. If you just play the levels through and never do any side content, you won't have any clue what is happening.Overall though, it's a simple 3D platformer, and that is exactly what it wants to be. I've completed every achievement, S ranked every level with every character, I've done everything. And I can say this: This is good.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a fun, little platformer that I enjoyed playing a lot! Can be finished within 1-2 cozy game sessions. Every level adds fun mechanics and the music is incredibly chill. The story feels a bit disconnected from the gameplay but I guess it makes somewhat sense in the end. It's nice to have story at all! _childDocuments_.review: I have just started playing this game but expect I will play it a lot more.  It's not the most detailed art like you'd expect from a modern AAA game -- more Super Mario 64 caliber art.  But.  And I know this sounds ridiculous.  But this is the first 3-D platformer I've played where the controls are just so smooth that it is, legitimately, just a joy to control.  I've historically been bad at platformers, 2D or 3D.  And the whole time I've been playing this I've been marvelling at how intuitive it feels; the character does exactly what I want her to.  I managed to 100% clear world one, act one, including all cranes and the letters and Mr. Box, on the very first try, without having seen it before or looking anything up, *without dying*.  Obviously the difficulty picks up -- I died 6 times on act two, four of them to the same optional obstacle -- but most platformers I die plenty in the very first area just from controls not working quite how I expected, and moreover, this rate of death from control screwyness never does reach zero.  I haven't once felt ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over by the controls in this game.  And the camera works intuitively too!  I can't even begin to describe how often bad camera angles used to kill me in Sonic Adventure or even Mario Sunshine -- to have full camera control, to not feel like I'm *fighting* the camera the whole way -- is a godsend.

_childDocuments_.review: What a charming little game! Lunistice is short and sweet 3D platformer with a unique visual style. The controls are quite simple, two jumps and and a spin attack that serves a s a third jump when you need it. Everything else comes down to the stage gimmicks to round out levels. From platforming across popping balloons to balancing across rail grinds to gain speed Lunistice always keeps the levels moving at a brisk pace.This game is fairly short, clocking in around 2 hours. _childDocuments_.review: I initially gave this game an absolutely stellar review after finishing my first playthrough, and while I still adore the game and had an absolute blast with my time with it, there's a couple of minor gripes I'd like to outline that keep the game from being a 10/10 in my eyes.I stumbled upon this little game by sheer chance, and what a surprise! Having now finished a 100% playthrough with all 3 characters, and all achievements, I absolutely loved it. I've always had a real soft spot for 3D platformers that are designed for you to go fast - I grew up playing the Sonic series and I can definitely see some of that Sonic Adventure 1 DNA in here.This game does a wonderful job of mixing tight, fast, satisfying 3D platforming with great senses of control, mobility and speed, and you still have those cool set-piece "roller-coaster ride" sections that bounce you all over with dash rings, high-speed runways and grind rails to keep it all fresh, fun and interesting, all the while treating you to some absolutely gorgeous Saturn-style vistas as you grind along. The levels themselves are very fun and varied - much like older Sonic games it's all split into 7 worlds with two levels per world, each with their own gimmick(s) to them, for example one theme park/carnival-themed world will see you sliding around on waterways and bouncing on popping balloons, whereas another world will have you matching your every move to a metronome, as the whole world will shift to the very beat of the stage's BGM. It's also a nice touch that all 3 playable characters, while sharing the first 6 playable worlds, all have a unique world 7.Speaking of the BGM, it's absolutely stellar. Even when you're taking 10-15 minutes on a single stage, the music never gets old. Each and every song in the soundtrack is a pleasure to listen to, and I have to give a special shoutout to the music gimmick present in Melancholy 5-2, although each world's BGM captures the theme and "emotion" each world is centred around lore-wise beautifully. (Although, Food/Comfort's BGM will play in my nightmares after trying to get the resets S rank on 4-2 as Toree). There isn't a great deal of story or lore to be found in the game, which you kind of expect for a game meant to last a few hours, but there's a little bit there which you can piece together by looking at each world's thematics and unlocking special data log entries hidden in each world. Interesting for those who care, but not necessary to appreciate the game, which is a plus in my books.Now, the bad. Overall there isn't too much to complain about here, but I do have some gripes. Firstly, I'd like to have seen a little bit more level variety between the alternate characters in order to really showcase their own characteristics a bit better - something like alternate routes through the levels, or perhaps remixed level layouts. There's very minor tweaks here and there for the alternate characters (e.g. less enemies for Toree as they can't attack, more enemies for Toukie because of their sword and increased jump count), but it would have been nice if, say, there were certain platforming sections core to the level's progression that only Toree had the speed for, or maybe a new enemy type or two unique to Toukie's gameplay, to make it a bit more of a combat-focused experience. Not a huge gripe, but when you're playing the game through back-to-back 3 times in succession you want a bit of variety.Variety, I suppose, is what Toukie's stage 7 was meant to be - and man did I hate it. I wasn't a fan of Toukie at first admittedly - having came fresh off the heels of my Toree playthrough - as they were just slow and the jumps felt pretty useless compared to what I'd grown used to, and with less health than Hana to boot, but by the time Melancholy and Wanderlust came around, I was having a great time - I feel like those stages were purpose-built for Toukie's style of gameplay - with lots of small, narrow platforms, enemies to slice through in the air, it was very satisfying. What I didn't find satisfying, however, was a massive sprawling level that felt less akin to a fast-paced linear platformer, and something more along the lines of Spyro, or Banjo Kazooie. I get that was the intention - but I really feel it just didn't work in this game, not to mention how frustrating it was losing my no-deaths S-rank 3 times in that level right at the end (and that's anywhere from 5 to about 20 minutes down the drain, depending on whether you were going for the bauble S-rank or not in the same run). It's a shame, because I really loved Toree's stage 7 too, and after growing to like Toukie's gameplay during World 6 I was looking forward to what their unique stage would be.So, overall thoughts. Now that I've seen everything the game currently has to offer (an update called Accel Coda is in production, and a sequel to this game is also on the way), I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who enjoys fast-paced 3D platformers. The controls are just tight enough without being awkward, the levels are stunning and are all a joy to play, and best of all it's cheap and short too - definitely something you can play a level or two here and there, or burn through in a single session. If you like these kinds of games, you owe it to yourself to give it a shot. It's not a perfect game, there's still a bit of room for improvement, but it's damn well worth the money and then some.

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a retro styled 3D platformer that takes inspirations from Sonic but rather than heavily focusing on speed, it rewards you for taking your time and collecting objects.This game has a lot to love such as its artstyle, soundtracks and its gameplay but it also comes with some annoyances.First one being the camera. I wish it adjusted accordingly rather than having to control the camera almost continuously. It kills your momentum a lot.Second one is how complicated the levels get in the later levels. First levels are easy to navigate and collecting all the objects is a fun task especially because they take 2 to 3 mins to go through if you miss anything. Later levels have too many collectibles that are hard to find and if you do miss them it feels like a chore to go back since backtracking is not an option and you have to start from the beginning. Which is the reason why i didn't %100 the game.Last one is the controls. This goes hand to hand with the camera and is not a massive issue but it causes some frustrating moments.Apart from the negatives, i think Lunistice is a short, charming and an enjoyable game that you should try. The fact that its so cheap and replayable thanks to its collectibles, secrets and new characters also makes it hard not to recommend it.

The soundtrack is amazing, both atmospheric yet bubbly and energetic. The other characters included feel like good challenge modes. I have to resist myself from playing more because it's so fun. Great work, can't wait to see what this developer does in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremly polished platformer that is just pure joy to play.Let's start with one of the first things you see on this page - the price.
