_childDocuments_.review: I recently picked up Lunistic, and it's an absolute retro inspired steal. It's replicating the look and feel of PSX/Sega Saturn era platformers but brings tight modern controls with well-designed levels, a perfect combo in my book. The controls are a huge deal. I recently played the remastered Crash Bandicoot series and those games brought over then pre-anologe controls, which while faithful, were extremely frustrating. We've had smooth, predictable acceleration for about 2 decades, and there was a reason it was the default starting in the PS2 era. Smooth natural moment in a platformer allows the player to more easily move towards challenging skill and level design based gameplay (the fun stuff) instead of fighting the controls. (Frankly, I don't have the time these days to spend of mastering frustrating controls.)So with the controls out of the way, Lunisitc shines with brilliant, challenging platform levels that immediately made me think “This is what Sonic's 3D transition should have been.” There's just enough speed without being too much. Of course, you wouldn't have Lunistic without the lessons learned with Sonic Adventure, but it's executed so well here it does make me wonder what Sonic Team was thinking back in the day. The difficulty steadily increases with each stage introducing a new platforming mechanic, making each level stand out on their own. I've noticed there's more of these 32bit era 3D homage games showing up lately, and I'm all for it. With Frogun already out and Covert Critter in development, it's nice to see that the retro inspired genre is moving beyond just pixel graphics.Fantastic little game, perfect for the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Good one. Solid design, nice movement fluidity, pleasant music and quite a bit of style variety. Got all collectibles and finished it properly.Only thing i'm not a big fan of is how flat colors in many places are and how little distinct shadows there were, sometimes it was really hard to measure distance to a platform or an obstacle. Shadows and shades are two things that make us perceieve spatial volume, game somewhat lacks em.Lack of ability to look up and down was a bit annoying, levels are often REALLY vertical so it can be hard to scout things.Other than that, it was a pleasant game to play. _childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this little gem of a game. _childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and quick little romp through a handful of colorful levels with banging soundtracks. While the platforming can be a slight bit unforgiving at times because of the preciseness needed to pilot Hana onto some of the smaller platforms, the checkpoint system makes up for this and you'll only ever be set back 30 seconds to a minute or so at any given point.I feel like I have to mention this, even if it's just to be petty: the negative reviews saying the game is too difficult or that stage 4's mechanic is too hard to deal with are all insanely overblown. There is a literal beat counter on screen to help you understand the mechanic and if you have ever played another 3d platformer before you can absolutely beat this game. I know not everyone plays lots of games, but this game really does not deserve any negative reviews for "difficulty". If you have an average amount of patience and a game controller, you can beat the game.Pick it up for 5 dollars, or 4 if you buy it on sale! Absolutely worth a few hours of fun for it's style, sounds, gameplay, just whatever. You'll find 5 dollars worth of value easily.

_childDocuments_.review: This was an impulse buy game, I didn't really expect what I was getting into, but honestly? I'm incredibly happy I did end up impulse buying this game. The art-style is so pretty, each level is so different and beautiful in their own way, and they even give you the option to turn of the pixellation in the settings which pretty much gives you access to a completely different art-style.It's a collectathon at heart, and one of the only ones where I actually didn't look up any guides to find any of the letter pieces. It's been worth it to just re-play the levels and find them myself!You also get access to more characters when you beat the game, and while I haven't beaten the game with them, they're still super fun and unique (even if toree can be a little infuriating at times).For 4 dollars you're getting an incredible hidden gem game, especially if you like platformers like this. _childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat - love this game, and can't wait to play the rest after writing this rq (On Stage 3-1). And I don't know who'll read this but I really want to vent about it somewhere.The Double Jump is tight, has a good arc, and feels good to use. And I  think the game would be better without it. In comparison to the spin, it gives a lot more height and can be used alongside it to save yourself from falls way too easily. It can even be used at the same time as a spin to gain a ridiculous amount of height, which makes some of the platforming way too boring. The spin provides just enough of a height boost to clear gaps just a bit too far for a regular jump, but the double jump makes skipping sections too easy.The most fun I've had so far was running through the first two worlds using just single jumps to clear the gaps and go for S Ranks - which works really well. With Smooth Turning turned off, it's so incredibly fun to rush through stages with some of the best running and jumping in all the 3D platformers I've played, but I always get tripped up by the sections that are designed to require a double jump. If they didn't exist, nor would the double jump, and the game would keep that fun flow of tight jumps and movement.There's an argument to be made of . Firstly, the trend in all games is if something is powerful and limitless, players with use it. A player won't not use a basic attack when they have, like, a free magic spell that defeats everything. Same here - it's too easy to skip through the fun parts of the level with a double jump. Secondly, it's impossible to tell if a gap can be cleared with a single jump or requires two. A lot of my resets were going through sections that could be cleared with single jumps, only to hit the edge of one because the second to last jump had to be a double jump's distance. Every level I've played so far has at least one of these moments.  or crossing some of the floating bridge pieces in some levels are some good examples of this.Just an extra note on the double jump - there's nothing so far that seems to reward using the double jump to explore - for example, the sand arches have nothing on them at the start of 2-1. It seems like such an obvious place to put something to justify having a double jump that lets you scale walls and get to weird places.I genuinely love everything about this game - I've played the first two worlds over a couple of times, just to beat my own time because it's fun to run through. The art style and music are fantastic, and each world theme so far is amazingly represented in its levels and obstacles. The  thing I can't stand is the double jump.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little platformer! Tight and simple controls, a super satisfying sense of flow and momentum, and generally really well-placed collectibles and enemies that allow you to always kinda intuit your next leap before you make it as you zoom through levels. Also just super pretty, with a jammin soundtrack!I WOULD say "i literally just wish there was more of it for me to play", but:1. going back into levels to get the letters/keys/notes you missed is actually really conveniently streamlined and a very worthwhile replay experience (learning to spot optional paths and secrets is really rewarding imo), AND 2. the unlockable characters' different playstyles (and [unique final levels]) are also fun to blast through the game again with, AND 3. there's still more content on the horizon via updates as well! which i am very much looking forward to :)Seriously, if this game cost 3-4 times more, i would still say it's worth it, but for FIVE DOLLARS you literally have no excuse not to give this a shot if you enjoy platformers. No regrets here.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: The game is too cute for the price. But i couldn't play much due to how the camera turns when you turn the left analog. This made me miss a bunch of jumps even with the character shadow on. I wish i could turn it off and have a more precise control. I don't mind the snap camera on specific spots, mostly the small camera turns when turning my character
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Pros and ConsPros:- Charming PSX retro artstyle with actual effort put into it- Fun levels and gimmicks- Moveset feels fluid and fun to use- Level themes are varied and interesting- Moderate to hard difficulty (YMMV)- Base game is fun all the way throughCons:- Some areas feel a bit barren- Postgame content (S ranks) feels lackluster and repetitive- Very limited enemy variety gets tiring quickly- Stages are long and S rank clear conditions are very harsh, often demanding you redo 5-10 minute levels multiple times- Acts 1 and 2 of each world share music, which can get tiring- Bonus characters feel like an afterthought (you just play through the same stages as the base game but with them. They do have special final stages but they aren't very difficult)- Unlocking bonus characters' bonus stages requires you to beat the game from scratch as each of them, which feels unnecessary- they should be given to you at the start- Reward for all S ranks with the main character is a short bonus stage that isn't very hard and an anticlimactic cutscene- Story felt overall unnecessary and had no satisfying conclusionConclusion: A fun little 5 hour game, which for $5 is about right. The post game content is very repetitive so I don't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I would comfortably pay at least double the price for this game. Controls are tight, levels are fun, characters have some interesting variable play styles. Story is interesting, but if you're the kind of person who doesn't enjoy story in platformers then you can easily move along without reading into it. There is a slight issue on some levels where I feel like the color of the collectables blends in a little too well with the color of the environments, but that aside this is just a good fun experience. If you like platformers, you will like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun to play, love the optional use of bumper buttons for jump and attack so my thumb is free to control the camera for better control over the character, also really appreciating that this version of the game lets you fine tune how tight you want to make your turns in the game options (unfortunately lacking from the switch port?) so you can play with as much control as you want and it feels really good.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so close to being a great game, but it just misses the mark to a frustrating degree. The difficulty curve is all over the place, with some mid-game stages being easier than the first level. Often the greatest source of increasing challenge just boils down to landing on thinner and thinner platforms to progress. It's too repetitious as well, which isn't inherently bad, but the level aesthetics rely too much on "floating platform in the void" so the levels kinda blend together, with only a few standout examples. I went to the effort of going for 100% completion, and when I got to the end I felt like I was getting slapped in the face like my effort was for nothing.For it's price it's not bad, it is even quite good in some aspects like accessibility and the frankly amazing gamefeel. To be clear: I hope the developer continues to improve their games in the future, and I DON'T want them to give up!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Been hunting for more low poly games, particularly 3D platformers and this turned out to be another real fun one.  This one has vibes that kinda mix in Nights into Dreams, Sonic, and Crash Bandicoot, having a cute and enjoyable art style and decent challenge to the experience.  I didn't fully beat the game, getting the true ending, but it was a solid hour and a half run for me with what looks like good replayablity due to some bonus characters you unlock and to get the true ending requires you to get all the items and I think not die to get the item required at the end of the stage.  Definitely worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a great throwback game, it looks and feels nostalgic, but plays very well. It's a nice change of pace from many more complex systems that modern games tend to lean into. It's crisp, simple, fun platforming, no broken systems or anything like that, and every stage has a timer so if you're into speedrunning, I could see you getting a lot of playtime out of this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: For the price of a fancy coffee, this is more than worth it. Even if you just do a single playthrough and stop there, I'd argue it's still well worth the price.It scratches all the right nostalgia itches and has a pretty good soundtrack accompanying it every step of the way. Apart from a couple of times where the OST seemed to go silent in a way that leaves you assuming it might be a bug just as much as it might be intentional.The camera can sometimes be a little janky in how it follows you around. Often leaving you facing a completely different direction each time you restart from a checkpoint.It's so cheap. It's so worth it. Just buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game was overall fine, but would recommend only with caveats.-You have to very much into the aesthetic/gameplay style! The 3D platforming is very much aiming to represent a specific time, as the store page indicates. I didn't have a large amount of issues, but landing on tiny platforms which show up a good bit in the endgame (even with shadows added on) seemed very finicky and frustrating at times.-You don't mind re-running stages for collectibles (if you like to get all the do-dads). Stages do get more complex and you are unable to return to earlier areas at certain points, so when you show up to the end missing one item, then you're kinda SOL, hoping to notice what you missed (or using a guide).I did not end up re-running stages after the first few since I wanted to see what all it had to offer, and the platforming does get pretty tight later on, very much in the later levels, but whether it's my issue with depth perception or something else, I missed a few jumps since I thought I was close enough to land, but apparently not. I do appreciate the S rankings only being concerned about cranes/etc. and resets (and you even can get the S rank on individual goal and ignore the other one, which helps if you do want to get the best ranking yourself).I think you could do a lot worse for $5, but also a good bit better. Try out the demo and see if it is up your alley!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very simple platforming game.There is platforming, some momentum-based obstacles, basic enemies, and a little exploration finding some collectibles, but it never gets as difficult or intricate with exploring all these aspects. Getting S rank in all the stages was the only mildly difficult task.However, the game advertises itself as such, and it fulfills its promise of a relaxing platforming experience (Unless you're going for the S Ranks). So I did enjoy my time with it.I also really loved the PS1 aesthetics of the game. I didn't like the pixel resolution, but you can thankfully toggle it off in the options. Very charming game. I loved the environment design and how you can see all the far away stage parts.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game! The main character is simple, but fun to control. The levels are stuffed with fun to grab collectibles, and the layouts are varied and interesting. Each music track is a banger and the lofi visuals are chunky and nice. Impressive effort considering the price and scope of the game, big recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: very fun game, absolutely worth the pricesuper fun platforming, awesome soundtrack, neat visual style, whole nine yardsonly things i would say is that sometimes i can't tell which way i'm meant to go and which way is bonus which is a lil frustrating, and that the levels are very clearly not made for toree, with the exception of the special one
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I find it annoying that I can't recommend this game, but them's the breaks.  What starts as a nice, casual platformer with no gimmicks or frills jumps to nigh Impossible Game levels of difficulty in 4-2.  I couldn't beat it with over half my playtime.  I would say hours, because it certainly felt like exhaustive hours of tortuous failure.  But apparently it wasn't.  That's not great.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute steal for it's price. The main game may be a little short but it is highly engaging, fun and smooth to play. The platforming isn't ludicrously difficult but can be challenging in some areas (I'm looking at you Rhythm levels). The game also scratches that collectathon itch really well and seemlessly integrates it into the speedrunning aspect that appeals to many of those who play platformers. I just finished the main game and there is some extra stuff so it looks pretty replayablethe music is top tier as well. You should buy this game if you are even somewhat of a platformer fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice can be defined by "head empty, no thoughts, just jumping arround", is a cozy 3d platformer that has simple but well executed idea that makes cruising trough this game a pleasant experience, inspired by the likes of Celeste and A hat in time is for sure a good recommendation and a short experience worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This whole game in it of itself is just phenomenal. Not only has it an amazing soundtrack but it also has just such a fluent gameplay its like a little dream. All in all is it a "short" jump n run that was clearly made with love and care.I may not be the most skilled player when it comes to this genre of games, yet did it never felt frustrating to die for the 5,6 or even 12th time. (Mostly because if the amazing music that is playing in the background which keeps you motivated)In my opinion everyone who enjoys well made indie games should give Lunistice a try since it's worth everyones time <3
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A fun 3D platformer with retro visuals, the levels are great and fun to complete. The movement and feels is what I liked most of this game, even tho the movement and jumps can feel a bit floaty, it fit this game and I really enjoyed it. It took me around 6 - 7 hours to 100% the whole game. You start with Hana but you can unlock 2 more characters after finish the campaign for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is INSANELY good you HAVE to play it/try it. It's so cheap and there's also a free demo like come on. The art is amazing, the graphics are amazing, the music is incredibly good so much so that I immediately bought the soundtrack after playing it. The controls are godlike. Everything just feels right and it's all so smooth. There really is no reason to not at least try the demo and see for yourself. This game is just incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute gem and not grabbing it if you have the slightest interest in platformers is a crime considering how unexpensive it is for its quality. The music's awesome, the levels are well designed and it all makes you want to go fast and test the limits of the gameplay. If you've got any hint of doubt, there's even a demo to try it out !
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely fun and well crafted game. Movement feels really good except for a few small nitpicks here and there (it was kind of easy to overshoot some platforms) but there's a lot of gameplay options and tools to help refine your control and make the game easier to handle. It's still a bit challenging towards the end.I do have some feedback for the developer about the beach world and the carnival world specifically. I'd honestly request that water slides give you a free jump at the end of the slide. It just feels like standard gaming convention to get a hop at the end of the slide, without having to worry about the specific timing for myself. That one isn't really necessary though.Additionally, with the jumping balloons in the carnival, I really feel like if I hit the SIDE of the balloon, I should still get jumped. It was just muscle memory for me, jumping to hit the balloons and aiming at the sides rather than precisely on the top hemisphere, and I had a lot of deaths as a result of that muscle memory. Other than that, this was delightful. If you make a sequel I'd love to see more wide open running areas in addition to the precision speed platforming. Running on the wide roads let me enjoy it more before getting back into the focus of the precise sections.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a fast paced and tighty knit 3D platformer that knows what it wants to be and how it wants to make you feel. The game will have you feasting your eyes on gorgeous colourful worlds with catchy up-beat music on each level, combine this with the natural instinct to go fast through each stage and it's an absolute sensory delight. I don't personally like playing games for the sake of nostalgia and to any who are the same, I can confirm that, though the inspiration from 3D games of yesteryear is clear, this is so much more than just a throwback. The only criticism I have, and this is often an issue with 3D platformers, is that the auto movement of the camera can throw off the preciseness of the platforming - especially when moving fast - I'd love an option to disable this. On release, the turning arc of the character also made some precision tricky but since release there has been a patch that addresses this as an option. Definite high recommendation and well worth the money, even for just one playthrough, but for those of you who care about replay value there are 3 characters with different abilities to give the game an extra run or two.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game! Played it fully on the Steam Deck and it was a great fun experience. The art direction is amazing, the throwback level design and features are fun and well thought. If there is only one thing to point is that the levels sometimes ask for a precision level that the controls have not been refined to. Maybe from the Steam Deck controls though, so take it with a grain of salt.Amazing work and such a nostalgic fun consistent, well designed game with a great art direction that is well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful and fun game!!! It took me about 6 hours to 100% the game with Hana. If you're blasting your way through levels you can finish all levels pretty quickly (assuming you're comfortable with 3d platforming) but the joy of it is getting all cranes and S ranks. It's a somewhat short experience for such a good game but all levels are really, really well crafted, with plenty of variability, speedrun shortcuts, hidden secrets, etc. One of the best 3d platformers out there, a must play
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished this game but Lunistice is definitely worth its price tag. I do not play games that have 3d graphics because they make me nauseous. This runs really smoothly on my ok laptop and I have been able to make it to the final world with a mouse and keyboard. The game is easy to learn yet it's levels are challenging. If you're slightly interested please get it! It's only $5
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled across this game while looking for something new to play, and the visuals kinda just jumped out at me. It seemed to be worth checking out. I just started playing this game, and I can already tell I'm gonna love it. The PS1 era graphics are charming, the music is upbeat, the controls are very tight and easy to understand, and it's fairly challenging. The game also has some nice visual settings like a CRT filter and a 20 fps mode to mimic the choppy feel of some early 3D games. I love little details like that. The game also works perfectly on the Steam Deck! I'm really excited to play through the rest of the game. If you like 3D platformers, I'd say this is worth giving a go, especially since it's only 5 bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A perfectly serviceable 3d platformer. No glitches, tight controls, all-in-all nice, and you can get the true ending in a single sitting if you're skilled enough. It's a great game to run through fast and just enjoy a nice lowpoly aesthetic.The platforming never really develops much and the stage-specific mechanics sometimes copy each other. Level 4's rhythm was as advanced as it gets.It mystifies me that the soundtrack costs twice as much as the game but hey.Also, don't go in expecting a story, the story tells you *just* little enough to say that something was happening, but *just* not enough to really matter.A lot of this game is explained when you see the credits and it says the game was only meant to take 30 days to make.I dunked on this game a lot in this review but I do seriously reckon it's worth the money and your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This was an extremely cute little platformer that has a lot of care and love put into it. Fantastic music and a GORGEOUS artstyle, where every level has interesting things about it. The collecting is really nice too, as someone who doesn't like having to one-hundred percent games I definitely want to do it with this game as the levels are setup to minimize backtracking if you're trying to get everything. The music as well needs to be mentioned, as it is amazing and fits every level's unique artstyle perfectly. It is a bit on the shorter side but I'd rather have a game that leaves me wanting more rather than thinking it was too much. I think my biggest complaint is that it is a little too easy. I don't normally play platformers and I found it not that challenging, where I usually messed up jumps because of timing rather than precision and movement. I don't mind games being easy, but I think I would've liked a little more challenge, especially with the enemies. They're all quite simple and are more objects rather than creatures you counter despite their cute designs. I also liked the little story details we get and it really plays well into the 'less is more' concept. Overall a great game and for the price it is a steal!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game that feels like a more polished take on Sonic Adventure/Colors. My only real complaint is in world 4 the primary gimmick are beat-block style platforms. This is usually pretty fun and I may be missing something but unlike most other platformers that attempt the gimmick have the music telegraph when the platforms change state (i.e. beat-block galaxy/skyway from Mario or Rhythm Jump Studio from A Hat in Time) which allow you to focus your eyes on positioning, this level's track doesn't seem to do this.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a long game, but it's a fun experience with a bite-sized but memorable story, and some really enjoyable controls. In a time where the cost of games can vary wildly, and the amount of time you get out can feel disproportionately important, sometimes stuff like this is equally important - a good experience that does what it says on the tin. A great game for anyone who has nostalgia for 3D platformers, or speedrunning-type games.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a great little platformer with good looking retro graphics which I believe worth its asking price (which is quite cheap). Especially recommended for those who like to try and best their high scores. The game is not hard to beat even for casual gamers so you don't have to worry about difficulty even if you are not a veteran in platformers. My only complaint was slightly floaty controls but I was able to adapt to it quickly. Additionally game has 3 characters to choose from so replayability is also here. I would say give it a try if you have any interest in the genre or want to play something without having to think too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and enjoyable game with a really good graphics style! The levels are really fun and while you can beat the game in about 2 hours, to fully beat the game there's tons and tons of collectibles and other characters to unlock! The game controls really well and while the auto camera could use some work it still works well enough and you can always use the right stick. Over all for the price and the content of this game I'd say this game is a 10/10. Hope to see another one soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute little 3D platformer that takes a lot of its DNA from Mario and Sonic games, and if you're a fan of both of those, this is a great choice. The controls aren't nearly as polished as something like Mario Odyssey, and there's perhaps a little too much Sonic-style rail grinding and speed platforming for my tastes, but I don't really care for Sonic games in the first place so maybe it's your cup of tea even if it's not mine. Thankfully I was able to power through those sections, as this game is quite forgiving, forgoing the concept of lives and continues in favor of simply counting how many times you've died at the end when it calculates your score.It's short and sweet, but there's still a lot of content for the price. If you're really on the fence, I'd say just get it. There are worse ways to waste five bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a simple 3D platformer harkening back to the PS1/Sega Saturn era of gaming. Cute mascot, abstract asthatics, and low-poly. I mostly got into it because of the cute Tanuki/Red Panda girl, high reviews, and it's like 5$. For all that it is, it is of exceptional quality. The game has great controls, music, and decent level design. There isn't much narritively going on here outside a "excape from a digital world" kind of thing, to that end, it some what feels incomplete because its so minimal.  I enjoyed probably completing it. I'd recommend it to anyone just hankering for some kind of good platformer.  If you look at a trailer, you probably already know if you want it or not. But I'd say its a solid 8.7/10 all things considered.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a game that's clearly had a lot of love put into it. The controls are super tight, the art style's really well crafted, and the levels are super fun. It reminds me a lot of Toree 3D, another great indie platformer. While the game is short, it can be replayed with different characters that have unique abilities. Lunistice is 100% worth the asking price, especially for how cheap that price is. If you have a couple of hours spare give this game a try! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been playing (and streaming) good amount of PS1/N64 games due to loving the graphical style, this caught my attention when I noticed one of friends was playing it. I gave it a look, and was like "ok I want it" and bought it.What I got was a really good platformer game that doesn't outstay its welcome, the controls feels good, I really like the design of the game and the character design is really excellent.And there's nice extra stuff once you've finished the main game once. Then there's achievements so it added up gameplay for me, I'm really glad to give this a go.If PS1-graphics and platformers are your thing give this a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its miniscule length (according to my Steam Library, it took me 3 hours to get the "good ending") this game was basically released with a price cut. Because, when you consider that quality comes first, Lunistice truly hits the mark in terms of taking inspiration from industry giants such as Super Mario Galaxy, Sonic the Hedgehog and the Donkey Kong Country titles and honouring them while still having an original identity. It feels like a short but sweet love letter to the 3D Platforming genre with 0 filler and only good content. Of course I'm praising the title but it's far from a masterpiece, what I mean is that for only 5 dollars there are literally no excuses to give it at least a chance. To me, the fact that a mere 5 minutes after picking up my controller I was fully aware of the extent of my abilities and that I could precisely calculate how to nail every jump goes a long way in making this such a delightfully fluid and comfortable experience. Play it NOW!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: this game's like a sandwich. it costs about the same as one, it's simple and easy to pick up, and you can finish it in an afternoon. it isn't gonna blow you away or anything, but it's a comfortable delight with some good tunes and a nice art style. there's loads of potential here and i'm eager to see what's in store for the sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth so much more than 5 euros and absolutely deserves its rating.The style, the music and the level construction are great. The individual worlds are unique and each has its own game mechanics. You can play with three different characters once you're through and the characters have their own twist as well.The controls just felt so right that I don't know if I could complain about anything.If you like retro games and platformers, it's almost a must to check out this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: It is £5. For the whole game. It is worth at least thrice that. The controls elegantly ride the fine line between precision and speed, the game mechanics build throughout the whole game and none of them feel redundant or under-utilised (other than the more open level design of 5-2), the secrets are gratifying to discover, and the game doesn't outlive its welcome in the least. Not only does it leave you wanting more, it has a robust post-game with 2 new characters with very interesting differences in their kits. In summary, this is the best platformer to release in years.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun throwback to old collect-a-thon platformers of the 90's and early 2000's. Not to hard if you're just playing the game and not going for S ranks on each level. Going for S-ranks is where you're going to find the difficulty in this game. The unlock-able characters are also nice change of pace in gameplay.A word of warning: S-rank Toree the Duck at you're own risk, this smug duck's fragility and lack of an attack will leave you deeply frustrated and cursing his smug little face.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: When I first tried out SAGE's demo for Lunistice about half a year ago, I was quick to fall in love with its beautifully stylized visuals, simple and fluid controls, and the small set of fun and replayable levels it had in store. It was my favorite game at the event and I was very excited for its release. Now that I have 100%'ed the entire game and experienced everything it has in store, it's safe to say Lunistice is now one of my favorite games. Everything I loved about it beforehand was further expanded in the full release. Not only that, elements such as the lore and the entire soundtrack left a strong impression on me and added even more to the experience. Obviously, it is not without flaw, at times I found frustration when it came to my ability to land on tiny platforms (luckily there is an option for a shadow), and in turn, mastering and S-ranking these stages, forcing me to reset my run, even sometimes very near the end of the level. However, despite that, perfecting these stages feels very satisfying and rewarding, and offering extra collectibles for people who collect all the stage's objects is a good incentive to reach for these rewards. In terms of performance, it's buttery smooth at all times, loading times are quick, and the draw distance is large enough to see most collectibles from far away and plan your route. The whole experience is pretty polished too, it's quite impressive from a $5 indie title. And now, the level design; it's fantastic. Each level is fairly linear with some exceptions (I was not ready for Toukie's last level at all LOL) and is littered with floating platforms, enemies, and collectibles. At different points, there will be an alternate path you can take to usually find a special collectible. The game reaches an addictive flow state compared to games like Sonic, even adapting elements of that series into its own gameplay such as rail surfing, and varied gimmicks that you interact with throughout the level. Luckily, the vast majority of these added interactables are a positive addition to stages, albeit some exceptions such as the 4th stage's main one. For most of your playthrough, you're playing as Hana, the default character, boasting a double jump and a corrective spin attack akin to Mario Galaxy's. After the main story is first completed, you also have access to Toree and Toukie, who have less health and alternate or removed abilities, usually for an added challenge. Speaking of the story, I was very intrigued by the lore the game conveyed through its collectible files. Although they remain cryptic, you slowly figure out what is happening in relation to the game's events, and even learn why you're going through these levels in the first place. Unfortunately though, the game's multiple endings don't really give a satisfying conclusion to the story the game was slowly building up, remaining more cryptic and vague. I was kind of saddened that a game as amazing as this didn't get a more climatic and/or spectacular sendoff. However, I do kind of believe that the true ending is leaving the door open for a potential sequel, so I'll leave it at that. Overall, I really enjoyed the time I had with Lunistice, and I applaud developer AGrumpyFox for creating and persevering in getting this game to the finish line, and they should be very proud of what they've created, and I'm very excited for their next project, whatever it may be. I personally give the game an 8.5/10 and believe that it's a game anyone can easily pick up and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing a bunch of retro styled indie platformers lately, and this is by far my favorite of the bunch! It might even be my favorite game of 2022! If you are looking for a fairly chill, 3D platformer with cute graphics and music, give this one a go. It has good controls and it always feels like it's your fault if you die. My only complaint is how vertically limited the camera is, because I'd like to be able to get a closer look at some of the in game art. Also, there's one section that is rhythm based that was particularly unforgiving, so there is at least one hiccup in this chill game haha!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: the lost sega saturn platformer.for once an indie dev claims retro inspiration for their visuals and understands that it goes farther than a pixelization filter. sure, there are modern sensibilities like high framerates and hella draw distance, but between the saturated color palette and the squared-off level assets and game-feel emulating what it feels to have full 3d movement with only an 8-directional input (i swear that's a compliment to authenticity), this game would have felt right at home on the sega saturn alongside games like croc and sonic 3d blast. this dev has clearly done their homework on retro style choices and i am beyond excited for what they've got next.music slaps, levels have expert pacing and fun themes, and you will  to keep going for those S-ranks. bonus points for .let this be a statement that retro/indie platformers may no longer be bound to purely rareware/nintendo worship.one of the most fun platformers i've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice feels like a game that should exist in a fever dream like some kind of lost media from a bygone time of low-polygons. What i thought was a platforming adventure game turned out to be a challenging and very addicting PRECISION platform-er. Now to be clear that is not my taste at all (I'm really bad at these kinds of games), but something here just hit the spot so much that i ended up 100%ing this game. Who do i recommend this game to? If you like precision-platforming games(or definitely if you're new to them, this is a great place to start), retro vibes, and achievement hunting.How did i play it?Mostly on the Steam Deck, but also on my Desktop and Sony PVM with a Xbox one controller.There really isn't a bad way to play this and the game runs flawlessly. Although after completing all the levels, i found it much easier to get the harder achievements while using the Xbox controllerWhat did i not like?Kinda rare that i have to really think about this one. There are a few spots in the game that the terrain and the camera don't mix well, but as long you move the camera angle before moving your character, its not a big deal.cant think of a single bug or issue. Game-play is simple and straight forward and whenever i died or failed a jump it felt like user error and not the games fault.All in all, Lunistice is an awesome game for its very affordable price and flawless game-play!

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing little platformer for those that love early 3D game consoles (Nintendo 64, Playstation, Dreambox) and decent challenges. Very fun variety across its 7 worlds divided into 15 levels. Great soundtrack! Gameplay is thoughtfully split between two main challenges: (1) collect all items, and (2) survive each level without dying. Levels are graded by each score separately, so you don't have to obsess about doing both at the same time, unless you want to. Find and follow the Lunistice Discord group!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is the best platformer I've played since A Hat In Time, and is possibly the purest and most approachable for a quick burst of pure joy than any other. I love hubworlds, but here it's so wonderful to turn it on knowing I've got 20 minutes before I need to leave, and that I can play three or four levels and have a blast, then put it down keeping all of my progress. It all just works. It looks incredible. I personally chose to keep the graphics chunky and add the CRT filter. The platforming is *very* responsive, every move feels so satisfying and is accompanied by really fun and well-integrated sound effects. The Music inspires excitement and energy to go fast and have fun, while leaving some room to be in awe and just appreciate how awesome everything is.I've died a fair few times, but in all but a couple of instances, it was entirely my fault. The level design is rock solid. Difficulty is managed by choice. There's no lives counter, so you could choose to simply get to the end of each level in your own time. You could also decide to find the hidden letters, which involves some more difficult platforming challenges to the side of the main levels. You could also decide to aim for an S Ranking by collecting everything within a level without dying. There are also two other characters to play who greatly alter how you'll need to approach levels. They each also have a bonus level specific to them at the end of the game. If you're still hungry, take to speed running. The game controls so well that naturally, a speedrunning community is up and running.If you aren't feeling confident at all and what to know if you'll be punished at any time for being new or not particularly dexterous, I really don't think so. The only time you'll be asked to do more than the bare minimum is if you want to unlock the secret last levels, which requires beating the game as harder characters or finding all the letters in each level as Hana- but again, you can die as many times as you need while doing this. If you love platformers or even just have a passing interest, I recommend it, flat-out, no caveats, to all of you.My complaints with the game are very few. I enjoyed the celebration that was the bonus level at the end of Toree's playthrough. Toukie, unfortunately was the last character I played and her last level contains 900 baubles to collect in a massive, open level. I wanted to a true S ranking on everything, which means collecting everything *and* not dying by the end of the level. Finding all 900 wasn't difficult, but it was time consuming, taking about 25 minutes. Then, right at the end of the stage are some very precise and difficult jumps across moving platforms. I failed these twice and had to do the whole thing again. It bothered me because, this game really excels at these levels where you move quickly through varied set pieces and obstacles and can collect everything and finish the level without dying in 3 to 6 minutes. If you die, it doesn't really sting to replay it. But having to crawl around this massive stage again after spending almost half an hour on one run, terrified that I might miss 1 of the 900 baubles and have to scrub the map yet again, sucked. It also made a strange choice to have no music on most of the level, and music from other levels that pop in at different areas of the map. It just doesn't work IMO, which is sad because I really like the assets and the aesthetic of the area! I just wish the level design were very different.If there was a much smaller thing I could ask for though, it would be a tracker for your best combined ranking in each level. You get a ranking for how many collectables you got and a ranking for how many times you died. When you complete a level, it uses both of these to give you an overall ranking - but on the level select screen, you only see your best ranking of these two individually. So theoretically, you could have both S rankings by dying lots while collecting everything, and by skipping all collectables to beat the level without dying. It would be nice to just have an acknowledgement on the level select screen of managing both at once. Nonetheless, I bought a game for less than a fiver, got 17 hours of fun just doing everything there was to do, and only disliked one level. Honestly, that's incredible. I hope the dev and everyone who loves them is proud of their work.

_childDocuments_.review: Great platformer!Lots of energy to the gameplay and catchy soundtrack. It's not too difficult or too easy either, just smooth and tasty platforming goodness. Each chapter does a nice job of introducing something new and standing out stylistically. One small annoyance that I did have is how the commitment to the pleasant retro graphics produces some overly-crispy background/skybox details. Still, Lunistice is a fun, inexpensive, and polished package that communicates the finer points of genre classics within a respectable amount of time. It’s certainly worth picking up, especially if any of its sources of inspiration strike a chord with you.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game transports me to a time when 3D platformers could stand on just the gameplay and level design. I’ve gone through the levels over and over and it hasn’t grown stale; it’s an instant modern classic for me. For five bucks or your regional equivalent, don’t skip Lunistice.

_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: What Tinykin did for N64 era collect a thons, Lunistice does for 32-bit era platformers. A brief delight of a platformer thats well worth the $5 asking price. Great level design, cute asthetic and splendid soundtrack overshadow its brief runtime and puzzling default options like the lag feeling smooth turning.This is retro platforming done right. It gives you the options to play it at 20fps, pixelated with a CRT Filter like the old days or an uncapped FPS, high resolution with a sharp aesthetic. No matter the options, its always fun to play.An easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a fun little plattformer.The gameplay is fast and fun, the flow of the levels is cool, the soundtrack is great and the story and lore are interesting, but a little unsatisfying. (mostly because it doesn't come to much of a conclusion imo)Its price is very low for a game you can sink about 5 hours into with its normal playthrough, and even more with the unlockable characters, that have different gameplay.Buy it, it's good.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I actually bought this one on a whim cause I saw it on Twitter and it looked pretty cool. Probably the best impulse buy ever and that's not even me being nice, it's legit good.Right off the bat, the presentation is excellent all around. The low poly art style is fully realized with nice texture work, models, and creative environments. Music is super catchy and fits the stages pretty well. I wouldn't call the gameplay super fast paced, but it definitely isn't slow. Hana's movement is tight, gameplay has a nice flow, and levels are well-designed. Usually each world throws in a new platforming mechanic to differentiate itself from the last like grind rails or rhythm-timed disappearing platforms. Thankfully it also does so in a way that doesn't feel too under or overused. There's a ranking system encouraging you to perfect each stage along with unlockables like extra characters that get their own bonus stage.It's pretty short, but in a way that still feels fulfilling. 2-3 Hours on average if you're just beating it and up to 10 if you're going for 100%. Which is definitely good for just $5.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Platformers and Jump'n'Runs are normally not my cup of tea - except for Mario/Donkey Kong in my youth - but Lunistices' concept made it super interesting for me. Especially as there hasnt been a lot of (good) games in the same genre recently.The game itself is 100% recommendable for anyone that looks for a quick and fun game inbetween. The level design is absolutely gorgeous, every of the 7 different worlds has its own style in graphics and music and each world has its own gameplay concept - world 4 being my personal favourite.Gameplay itself feels really good, controls and camera are great and every reset I had felt fair to me. There are some sections that require a bit of finesse but overall I would rate it as a rather easy game you can just enjoy.The soundtrack makes every world feel unique, while being not too opressive and letting the gameplay be the main protagonist here.Overall, if you are into platformers and jump n runs, this is a must buy, especially for that price. It has been 2h for me on a casual playthrough, not collecting everything - you still unlock stuff after completion + there are secrets to get.

_childDocuments_.review: It’d be easy to say that this game controls tightly and is excellent value for money (which is true) and call it a day. It’d also be easy to say that this game celebrates the aesthetic and sound of Dreamcast-era mascot platformers (which is also true). If that’s enough to sell you, then this is $5 well spent. This a fun, quick game with enough meat on the bone for challenge seekers and I imagine speedruns will look really cool. As a commercial product this is an incredible deal.I want to shout out some things that this game is not, because I think those also make it special. -It’s not a game from 1999. That draw distance would not have been possible.  This game is what you remember those games feeling like.-It’s not dated. Just as it’s not a game from way back when, it’s not dating itself with any kind of meme or something that makes it feel like a 2022 game either. -It’s not snarky.  It’s entirely earnest in presentation and tone. I think it’d be easy for a game like this to wink at the camera and take potshots at old mascot platformers, but I think it’s better for not stooping to that level.-It’s not difficult. At least not to reach credits. I like challenge but hear me out:  I love Advance Wars. I wish more people did. When Wargroove came out and promised to deliver on that experience I loved it too, but I couldn’t entice many more people to get into those kinds of strategy games.  Wargroove’s difficulty was calibrated for super fans like me, not someone who might be curious but inexperienced.  Lunistice stands alongside older games as a good entry point to its genre.I’ll always be down for platformers in this space, but it’s not hard to hook me. A lot of older games have a special place in my heart, and something that calls back to them will always be welcome. My very favorite thing about this game though is that it’s not catered to me. This isn’t a platformer for people who remember old platformers. This is just a good platformer drawing inspiration from the genre’s history. Ultimately, one day I’ll probably forget about Lunistice. I’ve played a lot of games like Lunistice when I was a lot younger. Those games have deeper hooks in me. Too deep to be unseated. Still, Lunistice is a confident enough game that it doesn’t bog itself down in devotion to the past. This would be a great platformer to be somebody’s first.  Lunistice won’t be an extremely important game to me, but I wouldn’t be at all surprised if it will be to somebody, and it’s definitely earned it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to lie, I saw a video review for this that mostly just showed off the fastest portions of the game in its B-roll footage, and that kind of gave me the wrong idea about what this was going to be.  Nevertheless, this didn't disappoint once I actually got into it. I thoroughly enjoyed the time I spent with this game and I think that for only about five USD, you get more than your money's worth.

Kinda like a small linear Spongebob: Battle for Bikini Bottom with Sonic inspiration. A very enjoyable two hours.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a solid little Platformer. Game lasts around 3ish hours, more if you want to S rank every level. Visually it’s really cute. My only complaints are that the movement is slippery and a bit too fast at times, and that I had a hard time landing on one of the types of rails, where I would just slide off them instead of connecting. Overall I’d recommend it. Excited to see what the devs do next

Solid soundtrack.  Amazing visuals.  Tight, simple controls.   More of a platformer than a collectathon, though I'd play an entire game made like the secret bird character's final stage.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth the £5 spent! The gameplay of this game is so addictive. If the developers take the time to make a fully fleshed out sequel with more levels - and boss fights - I feel they will have a 9/10 indie game on their hands. So far, I can only dish out an 8/10 for this game because the length is a little too short, but overall it is a charming platformer with a lot to love about it. Graphics: 9/10. Those Sega Saturn style pixels in HD are beautiful.Gameplay: 10/10. Addictive, fast paced, and insanely fun. Sound: 7/10. Nothing really stood out, but nothing really feels like a stinker.Length: 7/10. Roughly two hours long on the first playthrough, but the replay value on this game is through the roof; Lots of highscores and rankings to beat.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Simple-but-satisfying platforming. Not terribly difficult, but still has a handful of perilous situations.Story isn't too in-depth, but provides just enough intrigue in a "less is more" sort of way.Only a few hours to complete, and delivers a good amount of solid gameplay without overstaying its welcome & getting too stale.Charming low-poly style that is quite refreshing to see (full game has hi-res option, if the pixelization is bothersome). Delightful music. Good variety of venues to keep things visually fresh.I really appreciate that this game has a demo; more games ought to do it. Definitely worth the $5 for the full game if 3D platformers are of even the slightest bit of interest to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay feel of the Sonic Adventure games mixed with the classic blocky low-res graphic style of the PS1 era. The result is so charming and adorable, it's hard not to have fun with it.You run through colorful stages, collecting items (and some secrets if you explore the side paths), and bashing enemies until you reach the goal. How fast you can do it depends entirely on your skill, since the controls are simple and easy to grasp, and the layout of the levels (save for some of the final ones) is entirely in view, so you always know where you need to move towards.The only complaint I have (if you can call it that) is that sometimes you can slip when landing on the edge of a platform, or when you need to move away from the edge, but give a step towards the edge before moving in the opposite direction. But that's something that happens in most platformers, so it's hard to blame the game.A solid 9/10, must get if you're a platformer enjoyer.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun little game. It controls really well, lots of vibrant locales, and if you go off the beaten path to get everything a level has to offer, you'll start to get the feeling there's something under the surface at work here. Gave me similar vibes to the Toree series, but with stronger graphics and more expansive levels. Took me just under 3 hours to fully complete the main story. Only real gripe here is there's only 3-4 enemy types across all of the levels, they started to get old after a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I just love this how this game perfectly executes what it sets out to do. It's a level-based 3D platformer, with levels designed to be replayed for better time, getting collectibles, and no death (like the Toree games if you've played those). And it just executes this so well! It controls and looks great. Every 2 levels, the game introduces brand new mechanics and a different level theme! The levels generally have set pieces and optional paths for high tier collectibles! It really exceeded my expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game that you can just enjoy and relax. Thanks to the lack of time limits or penalties for deaths. Or you can take a bit more seriously and go for the 'S Ranks' (no deaths + all collectables). Plus the great retro art style, impressively tight controls and fitting soundtrack.If the screenshots and trailer have you wanting the game then their isn't really anything here to dislike.A game that is definitely worth the price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A pure joy to play. While not very long, Lunistice is an excellent example of quality over quantity. Had this game come out in the era it's so inspired by, it would've been a instant and massive success and held onto the same long term fans as Sonic or Mario. If you hold any Nostalgia for early 3D platformers you would be doing yourself a huge disservice by skipping out on this hidden gem. It's only 5$ and feels like the perfect antidote to modern gaming lazy annual releases and battle passes. This game isn't trying to make a ton of money, It's trying to be a great classic game. And it succeeds wonderfully.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

You don't need a story to make a good game or voice acting for that matter. I just feels like alot of elements are missing. I know it was made on short time and it's impressive for whats been done. I think the world 6-1 and 6-2 seam kinda bland It's just a montain with wind mechaics and annoying platforming parts E S P near the end of 6-2. It wasn't hard I just kept messing up the secret path. I was hoping there was a lava world or a snow world with ice physics... but atlas we don't have that. I would only buy this if it was on sale... _childDocuments_.review: a fun, clever game!really well balanced, main routes are not too hard and no penalty for dying means optional challenge sections for collectibles don't feel punishing and terrible like in so many games. plot is nothing to speak of but who cares, it looks great and plays great! love how every stage looks, and each one has fun gimmicks
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: this game pretty much gives you the worth of its price ten-fold just from how good it is in terms of quality and quantity of the content you get, each part of the game doesn't drag out for too long, never lulls, controls well, sounds good. it even has the drop shadow that newer platformers use so you can actually see where you're going to land (this is a weird thing to mention but it is unironically a game changer)game good. buy game. big value
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Earlier tonight I was scrolling through the platformers category for a game to possibly buy. And I saw this game pop up there and it had a cute furry looking character on it's cover. And that made me click on it curious to see what it is. Because yeah I'm a furry so what. So anyways I saw that it had a free demo to download so I downloaded it to try it out. And instantly I was sold on it from the demo alone. So after completing the demo. I was like yeah I'm buying this game. Best $5 you could spend on any game in 2022. The game is fun. I love the platforming. The retro look to it. And how even though it looks like a Sega Saturn game. The gameplay and controls play and feel just like how a game today should be rather than janky 90s stuff. It's amazing and plus you get a lot of game for $5. I highly recommend anyone to give this game a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and the levels have a lot of replay value to them.The three playable characters are great and I enjoyed how each level was built around their different abilities, I also like the use of characters from other indie games in addition to the main character.I think this game is worth the asking price and am excited to see more from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty awesome. And I love that you can replay the game as different characters.The platforming can be really challanging at some points but it's still fun. I love the art style and the characters themself. They all look so beautiful. I only wished the story part could've had a bit more, because I was really interested in the world building. If you like a challenging, beautiful, 3D platformer this might be somthing you wanna play.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥ yeah this game rules. It's not too long and the levels all have unique gimmicks that keep things fresh and fun. There is a ranking system and getting S ranks on every level feels very do-able. There are 3 playable characters that all play slightly differently. Getting 100% requires you to S-rank every level with every character. I had a lot of fun so I might give it a shot.The camera can be less than stellar at points, and player shadow is disabled by default which I think is backwards. There is also a smooth turning setting that should be a little more front facing since I think I prefer it disabled and I played the whole game with it on.Worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really great fun. I have played many platformers and this one is one of the best.That said, I do have one complaint, that the shadow of the player's character is not directly underneath them (as is the case in most 3D platformers) which makes jumping more difficult, but the game is so much fun that this is not so problematic.EDIT: I noticed there is in fact an option to put shadows directly under player.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice feels like the kind of game that some enterprising developer might've released on the Saturn, had they known that there was never going to be a true 3D Sonic game on there. I absolutely adore the low-poly visuals, which almost have a vaporwave quality to them, the soundtrack is exactly what I'm looking for in video game music and if you're willing to go for all S-Ranks, it lasts a remarkably long time for a $5 game. Definitely worth checking out for anyone who enjoys 3D platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a multitude of positive reviews already, so I can only chime in and highlight some of the best things again:- really well done "rail sliding" mechanic- speeding through the levels just feels nice. Better than most recent Sonic games- controls are absolutely on point- impressive feat for a single person developing the game
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This is absolutely without any doubt the best true-to-form platformer I have played in years.   Functionally and aesthetically it is pared back to just what makes the genre fun.  It pulls off the Saturn/PSX era visual styling superbly - really feels like a lost Sega Saturn game.  My family and I sat together passing the the controller back and forth taking turns like old times.  Before we knew it, the game was over and we still wanted more.  Here's to hoping!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: It's such a pretty and charming game that emulates the style of late 90s platformers so well, it's just too bad that I happen to be absolutely terrible at it. I still love this game though, it makes me feel super nostalgic because I used to watch my older sister play games like this when I was a little kid.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really good if you like 3D platformers. The limited graphics make it feel like a DS game, and I really like that. The controls feel really nice, as do the levels. The isn't much I have to say outside of that, aside from me wishing there was bosses/more enemy variety. But outside of that, really solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, challenging platformer that takes elements from the classics. Such as spin attacks like Crash, Rail grinds like Sonic and jumping puzzles like Mario. It's short. But there's decent replay value. There are 3 characters to play with (after beating the game once). Each character changes it up a little to keep it interesting. You can't go wrong for $5. Also, it runs very well on the steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game came up in my daily discovery queue and I am glad it did. It is an excellent game in every way. It is super polished with great movement. Old school creative level design and perfect soundtracks to accompany each level. I would have gladly paid more for this experience as you can tell a lot of effort went into this game. I have nothing bad to say about it and I highly recommend you least try out the demo!Edit: I voted for this game under the award of outstanding visual style!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: The game nails everything it sets out to do. The gameplay is fast paced and rewarding to master. I'm tempted to go back and get faster times per level. The player has a great amount of air control, meaning it's easy to get wherever you want to go. The player always runs, but the addition of a walk button is a great choice; It gives an extra layer of precision toward landing tough jumps. Each of the main "Dream" are fantastic, with my favorite being the fifth. Each has fantastic music, gorgeous aesthetics, and unique level gimmicks. The unique platforming you do from level to level help keep the game fresh and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Short and simple but very polished.  A cute 3D platformer with fairly basic running, jumping, and spin attacking, but everything feels tight and bouncy and satisfying to control.  The solid controls and short length make going for all collectibles a very pleasant time.  Easy recommendation for anyone that likes 3D platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: The best retro 3D platformer I've played in the past decade.It's short, but at $5 it's pretty cheap.  Honestly I would have easily paid $10 or $15 dollars for it.  If I had to describe the gameplay it's like a cross between Sonic and Crash but it controls better than both imo.  The demo does a good job of telling you what you're in for.My time as of this review is 2.7 hours but this was only my first playthrough without getting all of the collectibles or completing levels with a perfect score.  Regarding how much additional content there is: So that's enough to last you maybe 7-11 additional hours if you're a completionist.  Factor in a couple more for achievements.The game is great for replayability and I can't wait to 'jump' back in, 10/10 <3
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Simple and light, is how I would describe this game.Gameplay wise there's nothing overly complex, you go a little fast at times, but it's all fun.One world has a slight difficulty spike due to a certain mechanic but it doesn't hold the rest of the game back.The music is poppy and cheery and meet the aesthetics of the game really well, the sound effects are superb as well, nothing annoying or repetitive that'll grind your gears.Story wise, there is some lore but nothing really concrete; possibly a open end for a sequel or prequel. I found it okay, but nothing worth digging into.Overall, I'd give this game a solid 8/10, Some levels need touch up and the story felt like a plain doughnut.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Right away this felt so nice to control. So much of the game, the platforms and their mechanics, everything, is just satisfying. The levels are the perfect level of iterative where it's not too hand-holdy but doesn't toss a new mechanic into a mix of others without showing you its most basic form first. And shortly after something's introduced, it finds different ways to combine it and make it interesting. Simple to learn, likely a challenge to master (i.e. get S ranks/fully explore a level). There's so many diverging paths to reward you for exploring (and perhaps my only complaint is that in some instances it seems you can't backtrack(?)). There's little touches in there to make the game forgiving if you slip up (like regaining a jump if you collide with an enemy mid-air). The visuals are gorgeous, with or without the filters. The music is great. The game's just so darn fun.It even has controller agnostic UI. More games need this. Please. There are big $80-game studios that still haven't got that figured out yet!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Think Super Mario Galaxy but with Sonic-style rail grinding. Now that's what I call something special. The game controls fantastic and the levels are tons of fun. My only issue is that there isn't more. This gameplay style could only benefit from, and I think should, be expanded upon in a larger game I would gladly pay for.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Fast-paced and fun 3D platformer with adorable retro graphics and no real pressure. Pick it up, give a level or two a go, enjoy the boppin' soundtrack and colourful scenery, then set it down 'til next time.This game sets out to do what it intended to do and succeeds in spades. And in this way, the price point is spot on! No brainer, pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a charming game that says a lot with very little. Simplistic but pure, totally worth the five bucks and then some. The way progression is balanced around how much you want to put in means that if you don't want to 100% the game you're not punished for it, but if you are interested in taking things further you're still rewarded for that. A great little game with great feel-good vibes and a hint of melancholy. My only complaint is that there are only three save files, so I'll have to get creative if I ever want to start fresh.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best 3D platformers I have ever played.To start with the things I liked:Platforming and controls feel great, very fun. I especially like how familiar yet unique each character feels to play.Excellent level design. Every one was very fun and challenging to S rank.Brilliant art design. Every level was nice to look at and stuck in my mind.Fantastic soundtrack.Cute Character designs.A somewhat tough, but very fun and rewarding collectible grind. I 100%'d it and enjoyed every moment of the 10 hour 23 minutes it took me.For things I disliked:S-ranking Toukies last level.Stage 4 as Toree.If I had to give it a number rating (despite all the flaws in that system) I would give it a 9/10. For $4.99, if you have absolutely any interest in the game at all, then it is a MUST BUY.Honestly can't wait to see more from this dev in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: After having followed the development of Lunistice from the start, I am super happy and impressed how it turned out.First of all, the art style and overall aesthetics are consistent and just wonderful to look at. The soundtrack is absolutely amazing and has a lot of energy. The game feels very polished and, although sometimes challenging, the overall difficulty is not frustrating.I really recommend trying this game, especially at such a low price!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: i dig it its a fun little game with some nice graphics some nice tight controls and handling.i love how the rails work being outside the zone slows you down but doesn't knock you off like in other rail grindingi really like the particle effects aswell i had no issues with the game over all outside trying to find some of the secrets on like 1 or 2 of the levelsthis games a gem and its adorableover all good solid stuff!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: First thing I must say is that I played the Next Fest Demo 6 months+ away from launch and the movement with a controller felt bad, you could tell it was made for keyboard first. However, the final release greatly improved the feel of movement, to where precise jumps that felt impossible in the demo were intuitive in the final version. Huge props to the Dev for overhauling the movement.Why would I emphasis movement immediately in this review? Because this is a 3D platformer where you want to both move quickly and precisely though the Mario 3D World and 3D Sonic Style levels this game contains. The game pulls this off well, and you have optional collectables in the form of letters to nab, which gain you a true ending and lore on what the games scenario actually is. I think the presentation of the story is done well, letting you figure out whats happening as you get all the collectables, especially since the demo didn't show any of the narrative. Personally I didn't care for the crane collecting in levels, even as someone who likes getting notes in Banjo Kazooie. They are too numerous to want to keep track of perhaps, at least the first time playing. The level design feels like it flip flops between a more standard platforming style, more mario 3d world esque, and a more sonic adventure style, with mostly boost pads and rails in the level. I slightly preferred the former style but the game's length makes both feel fresh. It is funny to see the sonic elements as they were not present in the demo at all. Speaking of the demo bring back the animal crossing leaf.....Only downsides I can give the game are 1. Weird stutter when turning the camera (YMMV)2. Hitbox on the rails could be bigger, its kinda hard to snap to them.3. Nitpicky, but the alternate characters could have their own lore pickups to add to the narrative of their game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Truly an amazing game.I haven't had a platformer scratch the itch in a very long time, but somehow this $5 gem scratches every single spot for me. The combination of the music and locations is so amazing that I can't help but listen to the OST just doing other stuff now. Legit this is a neat little indie gem that is oozing with personality and love. AAA studios WISH they could make a game I love as much as this.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little game that you can play and beat in around two hours if you just play it with the first character, you unlock two more after that and they both have unique things that make them different, one is more for speedrunning I'd think and the other is for those who like birds, I like this game cool stuff 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start, lemme make something clear real quick: Don´t mind the low play time.
