_childDocuments_.review: After being put off by the abysmal performance issues in the switch release (a great sign for the series' "breath of fresh air" installation), I finally mustered up the willpower to try out the Steam release. I wish I hadn't. I wish I'd stayed blissfully unaware. I love Rune Factory, and I wish this game was better. Every single aspect of this game feels like it was handcrafted to make gameplay as slow, sloppy, and bland as possible. The player character never comes to a clean stop, pitching and sliding across the ground as they switch from, say, running to filling up the watering can. At the same line, the removal of the jump mechanic from previous 3D installations adds a strange heaviness and restriction to movement (want to take a shortcut from one building to another? Well if those two buildings are separated by too steep of a hill, you can ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ forget it!). The game clock has been slowed down for the first time in the series, which I was willing to forgive at first as a concession to the world's grand new scope- expect you're still waiting around for the slow-ass characters to meander to their desks so you can get literally anything done. Hell, even the dash mechanic is slow, moving the player character an almost comical 3 inches forward while frozen a static crouch pose. Not that this mechanic needs to cover much ground anymore, anyway: early game combat is pathetically easy, with monsters that just kinda stand around and look at you until they decide, oh yeah, they're actually supposed to attack.What I've seen of the new mechanic(s) is just... yeesh. The new monster taming system, clearly intended to add more dynamic action or charm to the "brush and dodge" rhythm of the prior installations, is agonizingly boring. Monsters shuffle periodically from side to side until the recharge meter mercifully fills up, and you can fling a beam of light that will net you the failure reaction a few dozen times before the game shows you pity. And yet, the fact that the capture spell need to recharge at all is, I'm sure, another desperate attempt of the developers to prevent you from burning through the bare bones objectives of the early game, lest you realize that all of your work will be done by 2pm every in-game day. Rather than actually enjoying the experience of living in Whatever The Town's Name Was, I frequently found myself bumming around SEED headquarters, plants watered, quests completed, and daily convos exhausted, trying to fight the urge just to accept defeat and skip to the next day."Maybe I'll go fishing or grind some weapon skills to pass the time." 'To pass the time'? I'm playing a video game! This *is* the time waster!!!!The character animations themselves are... just awful. The choreography of the events are so stilted and strange, where models spin and wobble on a dime as they turn about to look maybe not "at" each other, but in the approximate direction of the other party's face. All movement from walking to running is janky and slow, showing a lack of polish that's almost insulting. If someone with the technical knowledge were able to even out the graphical details of two cutscenes from RF5 and, say, Tides of Destiny, and show them to a stranger who had never seen either game before, there is *no* way that person would be able to accurately guess which game released over a decade prior. (And the *walking*. Gah, what the hell is up with the walking? I have never seen such deliberate, high-knee, janky robot steps in a game before. It's awful! We've already figured out walking in 3D games! What happened!!!!)I'm realizing that I haven't even talked about the townspeople themselves... the worst part is that I actually kinda liked them! RF5 has clearly repeated the dating roster quality of 4, with a decent selection of interesting guys and gals for you to get along with (minus one glaring exception for each game). Even before I knew just how much of a slog this experience would be, I was already looking froward to romancing a few different options in separate saves.... ahh well. Fat chance of me getting through this game more than once.And the story itself is downright aggressive in how little it wants to build. With all the preamble of a flash flood, you wake up with amnesia, and save a girl. Now you live in Rune Factory Town! I've never felt less endeared to an entry to this series. I've never felt less interested in learning more. I've said it a million times in this review, but it's just. so. *Sad*.After *checks notes* 9 agonizing hours, I'm throwing in the towel. With wonky controls, a play system that is both insultingly easy and mindnumbingly dull, and a lingering feeling that I was still waiting for the game to start, even after I had long since left the prologue, RF5 simply is not delivering the quality of its predecessors, both direct (with 4), and in spirit (with 3D Oceans/Tides of Destiny). Since I let my hopes blind my common sense, I won't be getting a refund on this particular bad investment. But know this: I continue to slog through this experience with a heavy heart for what could've been... and an open eye on the game's modding community.The absolute best part of Rune Factory 5 is that it gives us a glimmer of hope for RF6. Reviews seem to be high, and other people are having fun. So, even though I stand by my opinion that this is a disappointing mess of wasted potential... maybe it'll do something good for me in the long run.(But even if you disregard this one review, please promise me this: do not buy this game at full price. It is, and the high of it's enjoyment levels, a $20 game at best. Good luck!)

_childDocuments_.review: The game has some serious problems that need to be addressed first. 1) It has difficulties detecting the resolutions available if you have more than one monitors that support different resolutions. In my case I have a 1440p and a 1080p monitor connected. For some reason it will default to my lower spec monitor and will not let me select resolutions that should be available for my main one. I had to resort to some shenanigans to fix that.2) It has problems with many controllers. Personally I use a PS4 controller with only the steam drivers. It gave me some serious trouble to have the game recognize it while every other game I have of the last 5 years have no problems at all with it.3) Many people have reported they have problems with in game menus or cinematics not displaying correctly. Personally I did not face this problem though.4) The game often crashes at loading screens. The game remains responsive during that time, with music playing and you can push buttons and see the tips on screen changing. but it never leaves the loading screen. Your only option is to close the game and restart. This means that if you haven't saved recently you lose all progress. This is a problem that existed in the switch version as well. 5) The game screams from miles away that it is a sloppy mess. I do not expect a triple A game from this company but for 60 euroes I would certainly expect these issues to have been resolved before becoming available for sale.At the moment of my review I have about 11 hours on it. A big chunk of that time was wasted redoing things and reclaiming progress I lost after I had the game crash at a loading screen and this is driving me insane. Unfortunately I am well beyond the 2 hour limit in playing time I had in order to ask for a refund since I was hoping that they would do something about it. Instead there is no feedback at all from the developers. To make the long story short my main complaints have to do with technical problems and the stupidly high price tag it has for what it offers. It might be worth your time if they fix those bugs and make it available at a better price but as it is right now you 'd better stay away.Edit 21/07/2022: It appears that the crashes at loading screen are related to the "Shadows Distance" and "Drawing Distance" settings. In my case I had those set at the "Long" setting. Reverting them back to "Default" fixed the crashes for some reason. Admittedly I did a reinstall of the game so that might also be related. Still given the overall condition and quality of the game I do believe that asking 60€ for it is too much. Hence I will maintain my "Not recommended" stance. Should the price change to something more reasonable though I would probably reconsider it.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface, I recently played RF4 and have played RF2 (don't remember much of that one) and Tide and Frontier. I just recently finished the main story line in RF5. I would recommend if you like story, have some time to kill, and get it on sale. The characters...are fine. The graphics...are fine. The outfits...are fine. And so on, the whole game is fine. Characters:None of the bachelors or bachelorettes stood out to me. The whole town has a weird feel of they're all plot devices instead of real characters. In 4, the whole town felt full of life and intrigue. I loved all the characters. I genuinely felt like I missed out on other bachelors because I loved most of them a lot. The six here, one is a child (standard JRPG stuff, and in other RF games), and they're all just meh. And the females are basically all children except for 2 and one is a crazy sexualized succubus and the other is super straight laced (maybe she opens up?). Which is great if you're into that, but not if you aren't. The guy I married I did eventually grow to really enjoy, but not off the bat. I loved RF4 for the characters. RF5 characters were all just fine for the most part. None were bad, so that's great.Story line:Don't worry, no spoilers. The story I found enjoyable. I'm a sucker for a story, so my bar is set pretty low. The only problem I have is the length. It didn't feel as long as 4. And I just want to say, I don't need a storyline to be super long. The game Stray took me about six hours, and that was me taking my sweet time. I loved that game, and thought the length was great.  The problem I have in RF5 is that I have now finished the main storyline, and there's still a ton left to do. But now the game is just an online job. I've gotten married, and now everyday is just a grind. I'm not sure how they did it with 4, but I think the difficulty climb was such that it took me a long time to get strong enough to finish the storyline, and by then I had done almost everything the game had to offer. I played RF5 on normal, and RF4 on easy, and yet the difficulty in 4 was set that it kept me from progressing super fast. In RF5 I'm at the point where I think I'm done playing it even though there's a ton of requests and things to still do. Mainly because farming is the only thing I have left to do. And I love farming RPGs. I've played so many Harvest Moons and RFs and other similar titles. So it's not like I wasn't prepared and stoked to farm. But only farm? Not really into that. I think if they had balanced difficulty better and made it so you couldn't progress so fast, it'd be way better. My advice would be to meter yourself, so that you don't end up like me. And it really was a balancing issue, and I say this because I'm no amazing gamer. I didn't blow past stuff because of skill.Graphics:Idk exactly what the word graphics encompasses, but I'll be commenting on the overall look of the game. The way that characters and villagers move is honestly appalling. They all look like the have broken legs. You eventually get used to it,  but man is it off putting. When you run with a long sword (maybe some other weapons too) your feet go to the side past your hips so you look like you've just taken over your first biped body and have to figure it out. The female protagonist is super pigeon toed. Idk what it is with JRPGs and making females pigeon toed - maybe they think it's cute? So her power stance is laughable. Her toes point inwards, so she'd fall over instantly. She CAN walk normally, so that was a design choice, not a part of the character. Also the long sword ticks backwards every couple of seconds. Maybe an animation loop? It's just so immersion breaking :(Don't get me STARTED on mounts. Holy cow, your (female at least, I never saw the male) character sits on a little platform that spawns on the animal's back and rides side saddle. The other games weren't side saddle to my memory, so I thought that was weird. The little platform is cute to me, but when the monster runs, you whip around like those crazy balloons outside of car and mattress dealers. Some monsters are better than others. The wolves, the WOLVES man. I just wanna feel cool riding a wolf! But it makes me feel queasy to watch xDIdk anything about engines and video game creation. And I don't have crazy high expectations. I can enjoy a game with clipping issues. My favorite game in the world is Skyrim lol and the characters in that move and walk way better than in RF5. It's legitimately confusing and disappointing that a game released in March 2022 can be so sad to look at. Although I don't recall a single bug in RF5, so that's great.Some people said that RF can't play well in 3D. I disagree, or at least I felt no issue with it. Frontier and Tides of Destiny played well in 3D to my memory, but in hindsight, that was a long time ago, could be rose colored glasses I'm wearing.And it's not like 4/Special had amazing graphics. Its was an older 2.5D game (2012), so my expectations weren't high. But I assumed with how new RF5 is, it would have been better.Combat:I loved the changes in combat. I feel like I can have actual strategies now. Dodging is actually feasible and strategic. 4 had great bosses that kinda sucked because the movement was so limited that dodging and baiting were such a chore if possible at all. They added new bonuses to fighting with villagers as opposed to monsters, which I loved. I created a "child army" with the two children in the game, and it was a blast xD don't hate me, I would never irl lolOverall:I enjoyed the game. Heck I played it almost 60 hours so far :0 apparently. (Steam says 77, and I'd blame that on me leaving the in game menu running) But there are huge disappointments you have to overcome. If you're new to RF, start with 4/Special. I hope RF3 is good and worth playing, I'll give that a shot soon. If you're looking for a well fleshed out, beautiful, deep game, give this one a pass. If you just wanna have some fun, meet some new characters, farm some, etc. game on sale is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Just four months ago I gave up on the Switch version of this game, so I am glad to see it arrive on PC with the main problem (performance) being fixed. If you already know Rune Factory as a series, I probably don't need to explain the gameplay or anything, so I will mostly discuss the port here and might come back to do a full review if I end up finishing the game.The first thing you see when booting up the game is the launcher, one with quite a few options. High resolution support, window options, unlimited framerate, and then others like anti-aliasing, texture resolution, various shadow options, drawing distance, and key config. I tested with both controller and keyboard and mouse and had no issues there - the game actually plays somewhat well on keyboard and mouse and I never felt the need to change the default bindings.Finally in-game, and yes, the complete and utter lack of optimization and performance issues that the Switch version had are suddenly gone. I ran this version at 4k 144 fps with no performance issues to speak of and I cannot emphasize just how much of a changed experience it is. Everything feels smoother, the gameplay is faster, it’s less tedious, there’s just so much gained by actually having the game run properly that even the small things like instantly loading in and out of buildings I had newfound appreciation for.Of course, that’s not to say that it is perfect though. The game still obviously looks like a Switch port and you can easily see this in the low-res textures used across the board and the insane level of asset pop-in present.Unfortunately, this port has only furthered my belief that Rune Factory 5 suffered greatly from its jump to 3D and Switch exclusivity. You can have all the great performance you want, but the game world is still this large, spread-out, and boring thing, the residents just don’t have the same amount of character as those from RF4, and the quality of life could still use some improvements too.It’s not a bad game by any means, but after the exemplary showing that was the Steam version of Rune Factory 4 Special, I am still a bit let down and honestly cannot see myself playing through the rest of this one anytime soon for review. Maybe eventually...Steam Deck performance is definitely not bad and a much better alternative to the 30 fps and below Switch version. Putting the graphics to medium settings and running the game at 720p results in a 60 fps experience with occasional dips to 40-50. Of course, those numbers can be improved with further tweaks to the settings.Would I recommend Rune Factory 5? Ehhhh, kinda. It’s still a fun enough farming sim on its own, but compared to the Rune Factory 4 release that we just got on PC, it is a bit of a disappointment. Would I recommend this version over the Switch version though? Absolutely, and I honestly feel bad for those that already suffered through that release to completion.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the closest you will get to a solid experience with the game.(Had a person ask me to define this line so let me do a quick FYI)----------------------------------Rune Factory 5 released for the japanese market around 2 years ago, and finally released as a Switch Exclusive to the western market around march.There were a lot of us who wanted to love the game, but due to hardware limitations of the switch was the experience extremely sub-par, with Slowdowns and outright freezes mid combat of bosses, and roaming around in town during events would often be single digit framerate.Those issues were all tied to the hardware limitations of the steamdeck and is no longer problem either on the PC or the steamdeck.-----------------------------------RF5 is a new entry in the Rune factory franchise and everything that includes.----------------For those new to the franchise, it's effectively a Farming sim seemlessly merged with an action combat RPG, enjoying the best of both world, the franchise originally started as Spinoff to the Harvest moon games ( now called Story of Seasons ) and have been widely loved.The Purpose of the game is a very seemless loop of tending to your farm / village just like you would in Harvest moon, Stardew vally, Story of Seasons, but what makes it unique is that you can bring the towns people along with you for combat into dungeons / monster filled areas and further use the crops you farmed on your farm as potions / etc to fight monsters that you will then use to upgrade your weapons/ armor / Harvest tools.You can also catch the monsters and by "becoming friendly" with them allow them to help you out with your farming duties, furthermore EVERYTHING in this game have levels, including crops, soil and even the partners you decide to befriend/ romance / or just use as meatshield.Recently the franchise have gotten more traction since they decided to port Rune Factory 4, which originally was a Nintendo DS game to Switch, with such success it ended up being ported to PC and the other consoles as well.With the Success of RF4, RF5 originally targeted Switch exclusivity but in my opinion ended up being a bit too ambitious for the hardware they were targeting.The game itself is solid, there is clear tells this is targeting a handheld, but that's fine, the biggest downside is the camera stutter and jumping that is happening, this is not to be confused with the slowdowns and freezes in the switch version, but simply a 3d camera not properly managed, you can alleviate this a lot by setting the game to exclusive full screen.Which is an unfortunate side effect of this being their first true jump into 3D for the franchise, while RuneFactory 4 does look slightly dated, do I share the sentiment that RF4 is probably the more polished game as by that game have they almost perfected the formula, RF5, is in no way bad, but you can feel that it is relearning certain aspects, and I do hope to see slight patches to Rf5, and that they learn from this iteration for the next franchise entry.Furthermore you can have a flawless 60fps SteamDeck experience, if you set the resolution to 720+ and set quality to "standard".to fix the scuffed video, simply go to properties, and set it to run the newest proton experimental. you're welcome, you now have a portable version of the game running without Switch-itis <3

_childDocuments_.review: Its a fun farming sim combined with a solid ARPG that is difficult to recommend because the clearly superior and perfect game, Rune Factory 4, the prequel to this game exists.Rune Factory 5 is a clearly ambitious title in the series that attempts to take the gameplay of the acclaimed Rune Factory franchise up another level. The problem is, while it does achieve many impressive feats, they always come with downsides that significantly hampers the experience.The town is big and beautiful; but that also means its more time consuming to walk around to talk with characters or to get to where the player wants to go.The map is big and beautiful; which also means that the monster spawns are weird and making farming for material much more annoying than it should be.There's a lot of farms now; and your major, big farms are not connected to one another, so you will have to navigate through menus and endure loading times that adds up every morning if you want to check on all of your farms.The battle is now 3D: great. It looks great, and when it works, it's really good, but when it doesn't the hit box is janky and the movement is weird.And ofcourse the end game dungeon is no Sharence Maze, which significantly cut down on the end game challenges.It is a good game. Great even. But there are better game, with better designs and better gameplay in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: #1 Tip: TURN OFF THE FARM CAMERA! It'll make your game 100% more enjoyable.Also, save yourself some frustration and use a controller, the game really isn't meant to be played with a keyboard and mouse, some of the keys are just really awkward.Anyway, I'm one of those suckers who bought the game on Switch when it came out. We all know how that went performance wise, so here I am, double dipping because I really, really wanted to play the game after waiting years for it.My take is this: I enjoy it for what it is. Although the graphics look like they came from the Gamecube era, they are fine. The game doesn't need super high end graphics anyway, and truthfully, the colors are really pretty and blend really well. I don't like the pop ins, but it's a direct port (not remastered) from the Switch so I understand why they're there, and sometimes they are a bit jarring. I do like how everything is 3D though, it makes it more immersive to me. It has all the standard stuff that every Rune Factory  game has (amnesia, farming, fishing, romance, combat, directives, etc) so there is always plenty to do and they days are long (about 20-30 minutes each in real time) so you never really feel rushed or stressed to get anything done.I haven't experienced any choppiness, lag, or any bugs while playing.If I have to point out something that I don't like it would be how your character constantly screams "WATERING TIME, WATERING TIME, GROW BIG AND STRONG OKAY?, I HOPE IT COMES OUT OKAY!"  (and "LET'S CATCH A BIG ONE!" while fishing)  on every single plot of farmland you water. It's annoying as hell, and the only way to turn it off is by lowering the voice volume in settings... which sucks because then you miss out on hearing the NPC's voices and such during chats and cut scenes.One other thing that really bothers me, but has no effect on game play, is that when you change your character's clothes it doesn't change the look to match while you're talking to people. It will still show you wearing the default SEED gear on the text screen(s) with your character while it's wearing a completely different outfit in the scene in the background. Annoying, but just me being petty.Other than that, I find the game fun and quite relaxing. I look forward to playing it when I can and at ten hours in I haven't even finished the first chapter so I know there is still a lot of content and hours ahead. If you enjoy other Rune Factory games you'll more than likely enjoy this one too, especially if you can look past the muddy visuals and preteen looking bachelor/bachelorettes.

_childDocuments_.review: They actually did it. A port that runs above 10 frames per second.Now I'm sure you're hearing a lot of this in reviews.Some context:Rune Factory 4 came out 12 years ago, shortly thereafter the company behind it, Neverland went bankrupt.As such, Marvelous adopted them after running previous collaborations and they had to build this game... from scratch.All in all, it's a miracle it plays anything at all like 4 while retaining everything else. Especially on a 3D plane. It tells a story about the length of Rune Factory 3 or arc 1-2 of Rune Factory 4. Yes, it *is* shorter in length than 4. But that's partially just because 4 is kind of a colossus in the series.If you have been fed the silver spoon of Rune Factory 4, this game will feel different, it will feel slower in some ways, bigger and emptier in others. Going through empty fields rather than small maps.If this is your first Rune Factory game, it's honestly not a bad place to start. The quality of life such as pointing out event flags, giving you gimmicks in the form of the SEED badge system and other quirks do make the game a bit nifty, if nothing else. Plus the farming in this game is really pleasant.Also semi-hidden bit: Yes, this does still work like the console version, if you own Rune Factory 4, you get the outfits from 4. Not ALL of them, the DLC sure is still DLC, but you get the main outfits of the cast. Dolce, Doug, etc...Also probably the best part of this game that I am hopeful remains a trend going forward. GAY MARRIAGE~Do I recommend this game? Yes. Do I recommend it over Rune Factory 4? ...Nope. 4 is still the magnum opus of the series, even with its flaws. But I do think this game is the start of something beautiful and I am happy to not only see the series return but to also see a port that actually functions as a game rather than a slideshow disguised as one.Edit: After clearing the main scenario a second time after doing the same with the switch port, I stand by what I said. This game also definitely has the quirk where the non-marriage canditates often end up being more engaging/attractive than half the wedding cast. (Hello Simone, Darroch, Terry... ILLUMINATA.)My gripes aside, this game should occupy you for a decent span. A definite grab for a sale, or a purchase now simply to show Marvelous that this game must live on.

_childDocuments_.review: After having played the original Japanese release on the Switch to completion, I figured I would check out the PC port and English localisation to see how it compares.The performance has been improved a lot from the dreadful 20+ second loading times for areas on the Switch.  It's also nice to see that there is dual audio and dual text so we can appreciate just how much fanfiction the localisation is.This game is just terrible. The agonising levels of contrast and bloom cannot hide the Wii-tier graphics, but at least Rune Factory Frontier had a gorgeous aesthetic.  The 3D environment is wasted with lots of pop-in and fade to black for scenes. Stiff animations, unresponsive controls, an overly large empty environment are all bad, but nothing is as damning as how devoid of life the village and characters are.  They will frequently stare lifelessly into the void and take no notice of the people around them, even during a festival. Compare this to how RF4 will have villagers gather, remark to each other and hold items out.  As primitive as those 3DS environments were, they actually had some life to them.On top of that, there are repeat dialogues within the first season for multiple characters.  In RF4, everyone could give you fresh lines for a year and still have room for more.I'm left with the impression that this entry to the series was developed and localised by people who don't like Rune Factory.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ The 3D models of the monsters and characters look really nice. They are vibrant and detailed. However, their animations are as stiff as cardboard.+ Seeing all these rune factory monsters, items and weapons in 3D is really nice. It feels like you're looking at the future of this franchise, and makes you look forward to what they can do with RF6 and Project Dragon. + F u u k a (Steam censors her name if I type it normally because gaben had a stroke)Cons:- Everything about this game feels a LOT slower than RF3 and RF4. The story is slower, the combat is slower, the character events are slower, etc... You have a big world to run around in now so getting from place to place is a bit slower. To compensate for this, the devs made time in this game pass slower compared to previous games so you have the more time to get to places and do the stuff you came to do. However, in practice, this feels terrible, as getting to places is nowhere near as time-consuming as the devs thought it would be, thanks to the new fast travel system. Most of the time, you'll get to places and just have to stand around outside twiddling your thumbs until the shop opens or the event reaches the right time to trigger. This is one of the worst things about the game, as it affects the day-to-day flow of gameplay significantly. - The combat, while serviceable, is a lot slower paced and less responsive than the 2D entries. In RF3 and RF4, your character moves exactly how you tell them to. You press attack, they attack. Hits have immediate feedback, which gives combat this borderline addictive feel. In RF5, all of your animations have some form of start up, so you'll press a button and your character has to take several seconds to process this signal coming his brain before his muscles spring into motion. Rune abilities have also been gimped, and most of them are now borderline useless or indistinguishable from one another. Remember Gust and Rail Strike - two iconic dual blade abilities that make playing dual blade so fun? Well, not only do they have a painfully long start-up and recovery animation in RF5, they barely move your character a few inches forward or backwards. Stiff, slow, and janky is the name of the game here. These may just be the growing pains of moving to 3D, and I hope they iron them out in RF6. - Rune factory stories have never been amazing, but RF5's story was especially barebones. There was not much on offer in the first place, but the slow as ♥♥♥♥ pacing stretched this already thin story even thinner, until you're getting literal microscopic droplets of plot every time you finish a dungeon. RF3 managed to make me care because I had to hide the fact that I'm half-sheep from everyone. RF4 managed to make me care because of the funny dragon. RF5 has... nothing. Why am I doing any of this for this backwater village out in bum♥♥♥♥ nowhere? TLDR: RF5 is a patient of the trademark Rune Factory "First Attempt Syndrome". RF1 and 2 sucked ass so that RF3 and 4 could be two of the best games Marvelous has ever published. My hope is that RF5 needed to suck in order for RF6 and Project Dragon to be genre-defining bangers that blow our socks off in every single way. I love this franchise, and although RF5 was not as good as it could be, the fact that it exists gives me hope that this franchise is still alive, and Yoshifumi will learn from the mistakes this game made so the next games can be just as amazing as RF3 and 4 were.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games in the farming/life sim genre.  I know a lot of people coming from 4S were disappointed in this, but the move to 3D was wonderful and while the graphics are a bit simple, there is a lot of charm here for me. If you want a game where basically everything you do increases the level of some skill, this is for you.  Even eating and sleeping level up and raise your stats.  It's also a crafting lover's dream.  There are lots of different crafting stations to use, and a metric ton of things to make.Farming is involved and engaging. Soil has stats on it that can go up and down and affect what you get in the end.  It's not simply a matter of planting stuff then harvesting, and this system kept me engaged and more hands-on with the whole farm  aspect.The cast is wonderful and varied.  So many hot characters that it's hard to choose lol!The world is pretty big, with outside areas and dungeons.  Lots of combat and loot and treasure chests await you on your journey. If you want a farming game that also has a lot of combat and RPG systems, then this is a highly recommended one, and one of my top ones ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Rune Factory games since the  The only one I haven't played is  because I had too many other things back then. Big Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons fan too, all the way from Back to Nature era. So, now that I had the time, I gave this one a go without checking things like reviews first for old-times' sake.I won't go into the gameplay, graphics, or performance details because frankly I didn't mind them as much. Frontier is still my favorite RF, and this is pretty close graphics-wise to that.Frontier tends to have only a single camera angle so they can pump details on the scene (and Runeys add charm), but of course, it too got its flaws. I'm just that type of player where I just usually adapt regarding those 3 aspects and find ways to get by or around them. Not to mention I've played worse systems, so I'm not the guy to ask about that. The only thing I'd say is making the day longer with no way to pass time quickly makes triggering events really annoying, and, given what I'm gonna say next, is why.  Compared to the aspects above, these are things that I care about the most in Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons/Rune Factory games because they give life to the setting and messing that up makes it just another farming/mining/fishing/crafting game with, in the case of RF, combat. I'm a player who loves these things so I try to extract as much of it as I can, without looking up guides like always to make it exciting, and that means trying to max out everybody's friendship/affection values to see where it leads to.The story overall is alright, at least compared to the RF games I already played. The presentation has a lot of misses though, especially compared to Frontier. Frontier even had anime cutscenes for major fights and the cutscenes to introduce the characters are contextualized to what's happening during the scene; here in 5 they're just presented like a character showcase, and frankly I think that's lazy.Random conversations are pretty weird too: they tend to talk about stuff that's not currently happening unlike, again, the older games in the series. For example, Simone asking if you've seen her son but he's right there beside her; Priscilla asking me to help her with the groceries she's carrying but it's 8 in the morning and she's at home reading a book. Meanwhile you got conversations in old Rune Factories that even change when there's a character present, like how in RF3, some of Marian's dialogue gets quipped on by Sofia if she happens to be present; or in Frontier where Rosetta's dialogue is contextualized to what she's doing, especially when she's just moved in. Danny even interjects when he's present. There are some random dialogues in RF1 to 3 as well but it always fits where they are even if it wasn't animated. Things like these give actual color and character to the townsfolk; makes them feel more alive in a way.This makes it especially jarring for me during character events. For example, one of Priscilla's character events make it apparent that my guy character is pretty reliable strength-wise and is able to carry stuff, yet when a certain event with Cecil happens, I am not asked to help carry stuff at all.The more events I see the more it became apparent to me that these events were written assuming my character was either a girl for the bachelor events, or a guy for the bachelorette events, and they just pasted it regardless if I'm playing a girl or boy. Frankly this is lazy, and as somebody who's even played the Harvest Moon variations, like the Cute/For Girl ones, events actually change. Not all of them, sure, but a lot do.On everyday dialogue at high friendship/affection, the guys flirt with my guy the way guys flirt with girls, and my guy responds like a girl. Then when it's my guy that does it to girls, he then suddenly becomes extra masculine. What's up with this laziness? I know why they're doing it, I just find it lazy how they did it. If they are really concerned about the same-sex thing, they shouldn't be lazy like this and add variations to it. How about a choice at the beginning and not make it just for aesthetic purposes? Copy and pasting, again, feels so lazy and characterization becomes jarring when they act real different all of a sudden. Personality just thrown out of the window and hurts the charm.I haven't played Rune Factory 4, so I don't know how it is there, but the earliest time they had variations like this in Rune Factory for your sex is Tides of Destiny/Oceans. Granted, the options only start to appear post game when Some other things are also weird with the dialogue, which annoyed me when I found out why. Outside of that, the non-bachelor/bachelorettes also got less attention. In previous games (aside from Rune Factory 1 because that's got the least extra stuff dialogue wise), some events were given to them, especially with 3 and Frontier. 3 delivers it through their quest board. Some of them have actual side story dialogues happening, and some can even be an entire branch of side stories. Same with Frontier and Tides of Destiny. Kross (good, good Kross), Brodick, Danny, Bacchus, Gerard, and Jocelyn story stuff come to mind. The few we got here seems like they were part of the cut stuff I mentioned above, like Terry's, Misasagi's, Randolph and Yuki stuff, but usually they're just delegated to extras in bachelor/bachelorette events.So yeah, that's it. If you're like me and you care about these things more than the gameplay itself, then I can't recommend it, but if you do, the latest I can suggest is Rune Factory 3. Other reviews say 4 did everything much, much better though. I should give that one a go someday, too.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mixed on whether to recommend Rune Factory 5 or not. In my opinion, it's not a huge improvement to Rune Factory 4. _childDocuments_.review: Short review;I surprisingly like the game. I would probably like it more if it didn't have so many compatibility issues. I also don't like the romance system. It's pretty dry compared to Rune Factory 4's, and I don't like the idea of random romance events popping up if you prefer to talk to everyone every day! If you absolutely adore Rune Factory 4/Special and are like me, claiming RF4/S as your favorite game of ALL time, then you probably might not like 5 as much, but it wouldn't hurt to give it a chance despite its faults.-Combat is good. Not the best due to some frame drops when too much is going on.. Feels more like Tides of Destiny's with a mix of 4's in some strange way. Can also invite 3 people to your party compared to 2 like in RF4. I also LOVE the link ability! It makes boss fights much more epic and boss runs go by so much smoother. The combat is probably my only favorite part of the game, honestly.-Tandem cooking IS BROKEN. Seriously! Cooking any amount of something (with a high sell price) gives you 2x the amount of items back! Talk about making money fast! Speaking of..-This game is probably the easiest Rune Factory game i've ever played when it comes to making lots of money! Daily tandem cooking+boss run drops+tandem fishing to find the rarest fish= BANK-Story is good. Not as fantastic as Rune Factory 4, but it's decent. The bachelors and bachelorettes are also.. boring, but alright.-Festivals aren't as fun as RF4's, but they definitely have a few good ones that are actually enjoyable to participate in!-Autosaves are a godsend!-Auto Pick-up and being able to load a bunch of items at once into the fetilizer bin, fodder bin, material bin is the most amazing thing this game has over 4!-If you like farming, farming is as basic as it gets. At least this time, your monster friends can help clear out the problematic stones and stumps!Over all, I think the game is worth playing if you like farming sim games with anime elements. The combat is definitely the most fun this game has for me.Full review: I originally got this game for my switch, but I don't play my switch much anymore, so i'm really glad that Marvelous has been releasing their titles on PC now. For people who can't stand the poor performance of the switch, that's definitely a plus. If only the PC versions would release the same time as the switch, or just straight up release them for modern systems so we don't have to deal with performance issues. If only.Now onto the review.At first, I didn't give this game a proper chance. I got it on release day after all, so on release, the performance was extremely poor on my switch. Walking around town, let alone Phoros Woodlands was a nightmare. Considering i'm more of a Rune Factory 4 fan, I decided to drop this game and hope for a fix while sticking to RF4S. Lo and behold, the PC version came and I made sure I had my copy. I mainly just wanted to mod the game due to it having issues besides its poor performance. Compatibility=Not so good..I won't lie. This game is extremely frustrating and annoying to get to work properly. Probably the worst game I have ever had to do so many steps to have work on my PC as of yet. Being the crippling RF fangirl I am, I decided to hurdle through all of the problems to play the game because I wanted to give it a proper chance, even if I would end up not liking it.One important thing to note: If you plan to play with a monitor above 1080p, you're going to run into the annoying issue of your actual resolution not showing up. Then there's the chance not even 1080p will show up.. If you're like me and most people, who have two graphics cards installed into your system, yet another issue pursues. You're forced to play in discrete mode rather than hybrid. The game will not even recognize your full resolution if you don't switch it! The quick "fix" (if you could call it that..) is to disable your integrated graphics card through Device Manager, then go to the RF5 configuration tool to check in your resolution. After that, NEVER OPEN THE CONFIG AGAIN. Just pretend it doesn't exist!I've had so many problems getting my 4k monitor to read through the game, only for it to revert to 720p?? Don't get me started on the lack of ultrawide for the people who have ultrawide displays.. They have to use a mod called RF5fix in order to even play with that resolution.Besides the resolution issue, this game has made my PC crash several times. So often during gameplay that I actually had to reformat my PC. Twice! Just for this game! Yep, I'm that committed to playing because I've given it a proper chance to actually get through the utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ compatibility issues to play. I only hope that Rune Factory 6 will do better and allow higher resolutions for PC gamers. PLEASE, MARVELOUS! Give us higher resolutions by default, without having to switch cards!There's also an issue when it comes to sounds. You really have to tweak your sound settings, especially during the summer season! Luckily there is a setting that allows you to lower the ambient sounds (aka bugs buzzing and birds chirping). I have to keep it at the absolute lowest setting in order for it to not completely drown out the music. Speaking of, there are occasions where the music in game would come to a complete stop! I'm not sure why it does that, but it could be pretty annoying and off-putting.Now onto mods! I recommend playing this game with mods. There are some helpful QoL mods and mods that fix issues with the games. My favorite mod which is definitely worth having is the Better Furniture Placement mod! I cannot stand the default furniture placement in this game. It's got to be the worst ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ placement i've ever had to deal with. The items can't even be placed onto a wall or corner without there being massive gaps separating them!Another useful mod is the mod that allows you to not accidentally hammer your crops! If you're a bit of a masher when it comes to breaking down stones like I am and you're too close to the farm, accidents happen.. then you have to unfortunately restart your day! There's much more useful ones, like the NPC Details mod (Definite must-have!) and more! You can download RF5 mods from NexusMods or . Definitely check them out!I still play this game to this day and have been playing it almost every day alongside my boyfriend. I haven't fully beaten the game yet, but i'm pretty close to the story's completion! I only hope the game doesn't continue to be problematic for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Rune Factory 5

_childDocuments_.review: I'm fairly new to farming games and I found this one to be utterly charming with a very easy to learn tutorial/guide in the form of requests from the villagers explaining and asking for you to complete a certain task which also taught you some of the very many systems along the way.It was all very busy and addictive, so much so I got a very numb bum from sitting absorbed for so many hours at a time. (I recommend some extra padding on your chair for this game)The villagers are very charming and funny and unique, each one with very many different lines of conversation to say each day and as time progresses. I went crazy with the cooking and baking trying to level their affinity and spoil them into liking me more! :D I loved the little outfits you could change into, well I bought the cheap little dlc ones but its well worth while upgrading the town bakery as Yuki the baker is a 'closet' seamstress (get it??) and will sell you outfits too. Great idea!! I always wanted to eat fresh bread when trying on clothes, in rl Id need plenty of bigger sizes for clothes shopping in a bakery however!! Teehee!!You can tame animals and send them back to your little farms and the animals will do some of your farm work for you when you sweeten them up for a while first with pats and treats!! In fact some of them are great fighting buddies too, I found the 'mother of all chickens' at the back of the phobos woodlands and she was amazing!! Like a massive plane on a runway she'd charge at the enemies and mow them all down!! BEST ANIMAL COMPANION IN A GAME EVER!! Funniest thing to watch too! She's  a 'must have' buddy!! She does limit your viewpoint sometimes as she can take up most of the screen shes so huge but shes adorable!! But you cant ride her, at least she wouldnt let me ride her, too many sessions trying on clothes in Yukis bakery eating fresh bread I suspect! :D Cant blame her for that, I wouldnt let me ride me either!There is romance in the game but Im a bit miffed at how thats implemented. You can confess to your chosen lover at almost anytime but you will get rebuffed until certain conditions are met, so at this point, Ive finished the main game and am still in the process of finishing some of the characters little personal stories. Now Im not sure when exactly I get to start dating my 'lucky guy' but I sure hope its soon as Im tired of confessing my love and being laughed at. Bit of a romance killer that.Another small issue for me is how you learn new recipes in this game, you get to buy recipe bread of the infamous yuki, I think shes a bit like the local drug drealer, she has her finger in 'so many pies', hehehehe! Anyway go to Yuki and request the bread you want to learn a skill for, weapon, crafting, cookery, farming or chemistry. She'll sell you the bread and then you eat it to learn new recipes. (No wonder Im having trouble finding a date!!)You eat a lot of bread in this game! But not all of them will teach you a recipe, even if they say they are level 5 and you've leveled that crafting ability up to level 20 for some reason you just cant eat the damn bread, I ended up with tons of uneaten bread in my fridge taking up space and having to go there every couple of levels  to try again with it. Such a time consuming and annoying system for such a lovely game. GrrrAnother little annoyance for neat freaks like myself is every time I would clean and clear all the rocks and stones and sticks and weeds off one of my farms, and this would take ages, the next day it would all be back again, my little farming animals wouldn't bother with the debris so Id be at this every morning for at least a few hours and this gets tedious....so tedious....Id love an animal buddy who'd specialise in forestry and mining for this very purpose.The story is really sweet oh and the combat! The combat is really fun and the dungeons are also really fun, not too long with lots of nice chests and rewards. I always play on easy and I loved how pleasant and fun the combat is in this game, it really is lovely and not stressful at all.Just such a lovely fun game and not expensive at all for the huge amount of activities and content within, well done to the developers, Ill certainly be looking for more of your games to play. Now I'm off to eat some bread, for some reason I've developed a craving....

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Earlier handheld Rune Factory games are much better. If you can stand the grind or you're looking to enjoy a very long, cozy game, then I'm sure you will find some fun in this. I originally said I would not recommend this game, but here I am still playing it.I love Rune Factory and, before it, Harvest Moon. Rune Factory 3 and 4 were fantastic. Rune Factory 5 though is weighed down by needless grinding. It will take you about 50 hours to upgrade shops to get useful items and probably closer to 70 hours to get all the crops. I wouldn't even bash it for the time if it felt like any of it was worth it, but its all for falsely extending game time. I am 40 hours in at the time of this review and have my highest relationship at 5/10. I really want to explore the romance options and get to leverage the new dragon system to grow a massive field of crops or even a giant crop, but honestly I'm getting worn down by the grind. Its sad to see how little effort they put in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Really REALLY vexing for me.I don't know if its because its a port or its just how the game is but it feels really chonky to play, you can get used to it but aiming, farming camera, placing and throwing, all feel terrible, and the options in the settings just feel like a bandage more than an option.Game-wise the story is garbage and has always been garbage because its not the point, the main points are farming, romance, and RPG elements.FARMING: The mechanics are the best of any Harvest moon alikes and has the magnify glass if you want to optimize, I just don't like the Farm Dragons since they feel really out of place, unlike the Stone whale and even against the golem gundam.ROMANCE: Terrible choices, at least for the bachelorettes. Their archetype may be different-ish at best, but theyre all the same young teen minus Lewdmila who is literally the last one you meet!(only best gift is the damn Emery Flower btw) Compared to the male choices who have a wider and better variance! and to make it worse Elsje and Misasagi ARE NOT MARRIAGE CANDIDATES!?!?!? really considering just taking the Venti lookalike at this point.RPG: this is the most vexing part, the combat is terrible but its always been like that and i rather they dont focus more on it because they tried that for ToD and we lost farming. The skill system however is more where its at and at its core its a wonderful system. and the way you can get different results based on an items level and how you upgrade certain things is amazing. It makes it fun to Experiment.TL;DR:  at its core its a great game, fun to play. but it feels rushed, clunky controls, missing alot of things that are still in RF4, and a few of the things they did add in feel uninspired ( ♥♥♥♥ Farm Dragons)

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to the original Switch version this game runs at a whole new night and day level in terms of performance. I am able to run the game at 120fps at 1440p with little issues. The only issues I truly run into is when going to an area for the first time and it slows down a bit, but once its loaded I never have the issue again in my play session. Dungeons themselves run flawlessly though. In terms of the game itself, its Rune Factory 5 through and through, and I still really enjoy this game. I love the characters of Rigbarth a lot of the streamlining the gameplay has done over the previous entry, and just enjoy everything this game tries to do. Sure there are some things that Rune Factory 4 does better such as the depth to a lot of characters, but I feel like there is plenty to enjoy in this adventure. This has me excited for future Rune Factory titles, as I feel like this entry can be a good starting point to base future 3D Rune Factory games off of.

_childDocuments_.review: Never played a RF game before but I have countless of hours in Stardew Valley, Story of Seasons and Harvest Moon games and this just feels..... bland. _childDocuments_.review: Rune Factory 5 is rough around the edges, but I still had a lot of fun with it. Something about the way all the parts work together still draws me to it. Even after completing the main storyline, there's always still plenty to do as there are recipes you haven't unlocked yet, another romantic journey to embark on and plenty of upgrades you can still make in the city. RF 5 has its flaws, but the enchanted loop of constant progression and discovery helps to alleviate many of these annoyances, so they don't sting as much.PROS:✓ Character and enemy models look good✓ Core gameplay loop is addictive and fun✓ Farming and crafting are pretty much perfectly executed✓ Beautiful art style✓ More accessible and inclusive than previous titles✓ Builds on what made previous games fun✓ Variety of activities✓ Massive game length possibility after main story✓ Fully 3D world with complete camera control✓ Huge world to explore that feels alive✓ Extensive skill system✓ Easy to get immersed in for hours✓ Teeming with unique dungeons✓ Cast overflowing with charm✓ Decent combat✓ Same-sex marriage for the first time in the series✓ Involved story✓ Finally the game runs as it should on the pc versionCONS:- Ugly and lifeless environments- Occasionally clunky gameplay- Doesn’t move the series forward much- Important scenes aren't fully voiced- Some of the more interesting story themes only scratch the surface- Inability to press the furniture against the walls and too much distance between them- Lack of jumping ability in 3D game is a misunderstanding
_childDocuments_.name: Rune Factory 5

_childDocuments_.review: I feel really bad that so many wonderfull artists' talent, experience and effort was wasted and not utilized in this rather rushed game. The town and areas look and feel shallow to play in. Which seems to be a trend with a lot of new games; larger areas at the expense of carefully planned and beautifully detailed ones, which was characteristic to the earlier Rune factory games. It feels vast, empty, and soulless. But there was one area i really liked though, it kinda felt like it embraced the vast emptiness and filled it with weird trippy visuals that entranced you sometimes, it was cool and i really liked it. However they all follow the same formula with just squared off spaces and rooms where you fight and then go off to the next squared room. Another thing that took me out of the game is the shameless fetishizing of the characters. The characters in this game have some very good, genuinely interesting stories but with many of them it's overshadowed by the obvious attempts at appealing to as many kinks as possible and to me atleast it ruins the idea of them being actual characters with complex emotions and convincing personalities. They become more like oversexualised pixels trying to appeal to all the kinks out there. Nothing more exemplifies this to me than seeing people who are playing the games referring to the characters as "horse boy" (from RF4) or "the sleepy guy", "dilf", or "furry", What is up with wanting shallow characters that can be boiled down to a single, identifying, aspect of them? I don't think of the "appealing to all" factor applies to the part of everyone being romanceable regardless of gender, the only thing that bugs me about this is that theres not enough dialogue involved to make it convincing; even when married, characters (even those who you are supposed to be just friends with at this point) give of the vibe through dialogue that they have a crush on you, frankly it's weird and uncomfortable to have so many people wanting your ass at all times, there should be limits. so that there were some seperation between love and friendship because the romance is not the only thing that matters in these games, isn't it also about connecting with people and forming friendships? The story is uninspiring and boring, discovering the other characters stories is way more exciting but is undermined by having them only be discovered through romance, which is also a cheap and obvious way of squeezing out more playtime and repetition, rather than making an interesting game people would want to play more of. And although the spring and summer melodies stressed me out, the fall melody actually made me slow down and take a long, slow look at the world around me, this was because it was just such a beautifully composed melody, but it also had the effect of forcing me to realise all its empty and rushed sides which did not at all fit to the beautiful music. Tomoko Morita is a wonderful composer and i hope maybe the future game/games will be worthy of her skill, and this of course applies to all the artists, programmers, writers and others whose skill and effort didn't deserve to be in this empty husk of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town on Gameboy, Rune Factory 1 through 4 on Nintendo DS, this game feels empty.I personally don't understand the need to change to 3D from the old top-down 2.5D, landscape is as barren as an early 2000s free MMO; The graphics feels cheap, nowhere near as visually stunning as the previous Rune Factory games, or maybe it's the shift from a tiny Nintendo DS screen to a 1440p monitor.Game progression is disastrously bad, for a game that branched off Harvest Moon, the Story portion of the game has little to no ties to core elements of the series(farming, relationships, monster rearing  etc..). Played the game on NORMAL, has already finished the main story and all the dungeons(including the endgame dungeon), and it's only midway through Summer of the 1st year. Games like Stardew Valley and My Time at Portia have probably ruined the RF series for me. Don't play this game before those 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Rune Factory 4 is my favorite game of all time. It has been for close to a decade. I am 100% the target audience for this game. So why do I have a combined ~3 hours playtime in this between the switch and PC releases, and why do I recommend you stay FAR away despite my low playtime?I was beyond giddy when RF5 was announced bringing my favorite franchise back from the dead and I bought it on release date, expecting the reviews mentioning performance issues to just be the usual griping from games media. I refunded RF5 less than three hours later, heartbroken. 'Performance issues' does not even begin to describe how unforgivably poorly this game ran on switch. It crawled. It limped. I promise I am genuinely not the type to be put off by the occasional stutter here or there (I have put up with a heavily modded Sims 4 on a low end gaming laptop for reference) but the game looked and felt so bad I literally could not bring myself to keep playing and see more no matter how much I want to. If the game had visuals or gameplay worth the jank then I am absolutely sure I could power through it but it just does not feel good to play. Animations, including attack animations and other actions, feel very weightless and limp. Hair animations look godawful and the little that I interacted with the farming it did not feel good or intuitive. I would say that Rune Factory 4 has a unique art style, or at least that it doesn't come off as generic. Rune Factory 5 abandoned that art style and it just looks like Pokemon Scarlet and Violet with a better shader. There just isn't enough substance there to justify the performance issues.So I closed the game and went to return it and thought that was that. I came out of those three hours jaded about a game I and so many others hoped against hope for for a decade may happen being an unfinished sloppy mess.The PC release fell onto my radar about a week ago so I looked up some reviews and most of them mentioned a real improvement of the performance issues. As if I wasn't fooled by this exact review trick last time, I bought the game on steam, chose some lower end settings to give the game a shot, and booted up. RF5 on PC literally stutters in the pre-rendered 2d animated title cutscene. Multiple times. These are not quick stutters, the game essentially freezes for a second or longer. When I got into the gameplay this continued repeatedly. The game is literally rendering a single forest clearing and one enemy at this point. I'm not playing on a college laptop here, this is  unacceptable. Marvelous should feel completely ashamed of themselves for choosing to release this game TWICE in this state. They SHOULD go bankrupt after this one. And I am the most gullible idiot on the planet for getting my hopes up for this game a second time. Please just play Rune Factory 4 Special instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Review based on previous experience of RF 3, 4 and Frontier.This game is an easy go-to time passer. Rune Factory 5 still carries on its uniqueness of great casts and the game universe. Rune Factory(RF) 5 is superior to its predecessors in: VA casts, reasonable event flags (compared to 4 and Frontier), more warp points, better resource placements, graphics, and probably most requested of all: same sex romance. It still has the same: Story vibes, great casts, varieties of collectibles, monsters and crops, and calming ambiance. Mechanic-wise is the same as RF4, with some changes due to 2D to 3D gameplays. Hats and masks still change according to what you equips, consistent on all outfits i have (in-game unlockables and DLC outfits)But the game is worse than its hand-held game counterparts: especially the walking speed, the rune abilities (which is faster, and animation cancelable in 3 and 4), and exploits which fastens the game (like stacking many full stack of branches besides each other and mash button to hit many of them at once), also less features (vs 4 and maybe 3). Its a lot better than Frontier except maybe the casts? (biased.)The game is good, but can be a lot better, which is evident in almost every aspects of the game; the 3D sprites/animation (especially the dynamic hair/clothing), the cutscenes, the controls, or the interaction between characters. Which have impact on the immersion and the overall smoothness of game-plays.Also, please stop making hot characters and forbade me from dating them.I think this is a good buy. But maybe too expensive for a RPG/Farming/Dating Sim experience, so just wait for a discount.(I bought Digital Deluxe at 10% discount. I think every RF4 outfits are very well ported)

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I saw this game on discount thinking it was a cheap knockoff anime dating simulator of some kind.But let me tell you, this game is an absolute work of art.Farming was the hook, entertaining, fun, profitable. Taming monsters. Loot. Boss fights. You can even drag your chosen weifu into battle to see if she’s actually worthy.All this on the table, the amount of craftable food, armor, clothing, and weapons, this game supports a mind-blowing amount of crafting recipes, all unique and useful in their own way.If you want a cross between FarmVille, Kingdom Hearts, all tied up nicely into a light-hearted harum for your weifu, this game is certainly for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant surprise of a game. I have played most Havest Moon games and others like it. But this is my first foray into the Rune Factory series. At first the fun cycle of farming kept me playing but the addition of a decent story with a fantastic set of characters in the town has meant I now have 80+ hours and am still loving it. The RPG and combat systems are much more in depth when compared to other games in this genre. The world is so beautiful and great to explore. You also still get the staple features such as fishing, festivals and side missions.These might all be expected features of a long term rune factory fan but it feels like the series pushes these types of systems forward in different ways. For example, the plots of soil on your farm have tons of detail attributed to them, you can ignore it if you want to keep it simple but if you want more depth you can monitor your soil and take steps to make your soil better in different ways. I've never seen this type of game do such intricate and interesting changes to well known mechanics like this.It also includes a pokemon style like taming system so you can make allies out of the monsters you fight out in the wild which you can look after, gather their produce or even have them fight by your side. I could keep going through other features that make playing this worthwhile but overall this is a fantastic game. I'm looking forward to future installments and am interested in playing the earlier installments of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore time, I have over 100 on switch.This is the best version of the game to get if you can't decide. There are aspects of this game that are better and worse than RF4. For starters, as an action rpg this one feels a lot better. The combat feels like combat and not just random nonsense like every previous entry does. When you lose it generally feels like your fault. Part of that is more control of movement, but also generally there are less attacks that will ohko you in this one, so you don't have to pay as much attention to specific resistances to get past road blocks. As farming game, I think this one is a little worse. There are some more crops, but the change in perspective makes the farming much messier than it was in RF4. I believe the mechanics themselves are basically identical but the control is less intuitive. That's partially to be expected because the specific farming controls were tweaked over literal decades and have dna from a game that got it right on its very first entry.. It's still tolerable and you only really have to interface with it as much as you feel like. I don't think it's nearly as mechanically nuanced but Harvestella is a pretty polished way to implement behind the back third person farming.  I think this is a good rune factory game. The game still has plenty of content. There isn't, on paper, as much post game as RF4 but a lot of the post game and maze stuff wasn't really that great anyways. I think the characters and substories are great, and there is a lot more meta control over those elements if you don't want to deal with substories while doing your day to day. The days themselves are much longer which is a blessing and a curse. You have to wait longer for shops to open, but after you have your farm and barn established it feels pretty easy to get everything you want to do finished in a day. It's also worth noting that this is the first RF with same sex relationships. you can't really change the main character much (even just hair and skin colour would probably be enough, most story of seasons games allow for this now) but I think it's a cool inclusion for people who want it. I tend to like the female character designs and I like that I can still play as her without sacrificing marrying the insane succubus.This is a sequel to a game franchise that many people were convinced was dead. It's not an earth shattering game and it's got a lot of little flaws but this is sort of a niche series and it's wearing a lot of hats. I would love to see a rune factory 6 and a port of frontier, and I'm looking forward to the remake of 3.

This makes grinding bosses for SEED points super quick.+Triggering events is way less painful and random than it was in previous entries, with bubbles/character icons telling you exactly where you need to go to trigger an event. +Tons of Easter eggs and references to previous RF games to tickle fan nostalgia TL;DRClassic RF story with classic twists and characters. _childDocuments_.review: Rune Factory 5 has a unique way of rewarding players of any skill level for pursuing things they're already interested in. Came for the romance? Congrats, the townspeople like you so much that now you can purchase an upgrade for cool outfit changes. Wanna smash some rocks? Congrats, now combat has become increasingly easy. Wanna go out and clear the main line plot as quick as possible? Your walking skill has gone up and now you can complete the game even quicker. It's definitely a game you can put as much or as little strategy into skill grinding as wanted which I think tends to make it enjoyable for any amount of investment you put in.     Onto the bad bits: It's still a little glitchy. From what I've seen, the graphics are better than the switch version but still tend to lag behind at times. A lot of character interaction still loops over multiple days. Some of the towns member events that occur over a day/night cycle fail to restore stats, and the quest giving dialogue messes up.It's still a great game if you're looking for an RPG to just dive into But I might wait to pay such a high price until some of the bugs have been patched.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll make it brief, since most folk have long-covered the glowing positives of the game and its features: you see the negative comments about how you "should just buy Rune Factory 4 instead"?They fail to mention that RF4S (the 'special' Steam release) is a poor, compressed-mess port of the game, and the sentiment is generally blinded by the admittedly fantastic title..  And yes, I loved 4, but those bashing 5 are doing so without really, critically, looking at what 5 offers on its own.If you liked 4, or the addition of dungeon crawling on top of a farm sim piques your interest, give it a shot. RF5 is personally my favourite in the series, and between the new additions (same-sex marriage and still having kids? based - great waifu/husbando line-up for the most part) and quality of life features, you'll likely stand to have a lovely time toddering about.I will say, if you plan to use keyboard and mouse, you may want to look into RF5 Fix - the BepInEx mod on Github that fixes a mouse-only camera control issue. You  buy these outfits as separate DLC, meaning their only source is buying the Deluxe version. If you really want these outfits, save yourself a future headache and dish the extra 10 dollarydoos (on this sale!). _childDocuments_.review: TLDRIf you've never played a Rune Factory game before and want the best possible introduction to the series, buy Rune Factory 4 Special If you've played and loved Rune Factory 4 ... maybe just get this on sale and go replay RF4 again while you wait. If you've never played a Rune Factory game before and aren't interested in 4 at all, like the look of this, or really like one of the marriage options ... buy Rune Factory 4 anyway If you're being held at gunpoint and forced to buy this game...play it and you'll have a good time ----------------------------------This is absolutely not a bad game, it just has the unfortunate disadvantage of having to follow Rune Factory 4. I am very glad that it exists at all, with the previous developers going bankrupt after RF4, and I'm grateful to Marvellous for not letting the IP did. It's partly why I was happy to buy it both for Switch and Steam, to support one of my favourite series'It's just ... fine. It is good enough to the point where I am able to play it and have fun, as long as I suppress the thought that I could be replaying Rune Factory 4 instead.As silly as it sounds I think the worst thing about RF5 for me is that Rigbarth is just so ugly...the buildings themselves are nice enough, but they're connected by dirt roads and neon green grass with not much to see or interact with in between. I could forgive the dungeons and areas where you fight monsters being ugly, but the main place that you spend 80% of the game in is just not pleasant to look at The marriage options, visually, are all very nice to look at, both in 2D and 3D. There is also gay marriage which makes my bisexual self happy. Unfortunately, with the exception of the last character you unlock who might be one of the best in the entire series, they're just a bit ... bland. A lot of the marriage options in the older Rune Factory games leaned a bit too much on the "gag character" side for me, and RF4 managed to strike a really good balance between quirky and relatable romances...5 has mostly removed the weirdness from their romance options in favour of familiar, safe anime stereotype characters. They're all just fine, I have my favourites, and admittedly I haven't gotten married yet so maybe they're more expressive after that, but they're a bit one note.In the transition to 3D the gameplay has definitely become more clunky, but it's something you begrudgingly get used to. It just doesn't feel as fast or as precise as older games. The models do look lovely, especially the monsters. But everything that I love about Rune Factory is still here, the great intersection of JRPG and Farm Sim, the star raising, the grind, the crazy ways that you can get ridiculously powerful...because it keeps so much of the core series, it IS funI am going to at least play a full in-game year, complete the story, and marry someone to say that I have done it and given the game a fair chance. I am having fun with it, and if I won't force myself to stop playing; but man do I miss my ex (Rune Factory 4 Special)

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited for this game ever since Rune Factory 4 came out. I'm very disappointed in the complete lack of innovation this game has had on the franchise. The combat is pretty much the exact same from the other games. This is a bad thing. The combat in rune factory isn't HORRIBLE, but it's very awkward. It's always been acceptable given that the game is doing farm sim, dating sim, and combat all at the same time. But really, you still have skills that after they're cast, you're frozen in place for a full second. You're extremely punished in combat for being still at all. The best way to fight anything is just to strafe and never use skills or spells unless it's a select few that you get later in the game. I feel that Marvelous has gotten complacent in their farming sims. No longer can you just repeat the same game over and over and expect me to be impressed. The most this game is different from the others is the graphics, nothing else. Rune Factory is a pretty unique franchise, but it's slowly not getting unique anymore. Indie titles are starting to overshadow the big budget farming sims, and Harvestella coming soon is looking to destroy the entire standard that's been set.On the topic of graphics, the graphics for this game are pretty good given how the previous games looked. It's not really what you play this game for anyway One complaint I have are that the textures for the graphics are all compressed, resulting in them being slightly blurry even at highest settings, you can tell by looking at the fine details in the clothing, which bothers me a bit, seems like something that would be a feature for the PC port: uncompressed textures. Now here's the worst part, a part I wasn't bothered by until I realized I would be spending 30% of gameplay talking to these characters:The bachelorette choices are just awful. All but one out of six marriageable female characters are obviously aged 14-16. To be fair, the previous games were like that, but COME ON. First of all, there are three VERY ATTRACTIVE single women in the town that are without a doubt adults, none are candidates. Now all this would be just fine and all, it's Japan, they have an awful sexual culture, I don't care that much about the dating aspect anyway... BUT look at the MALE candidates! ALL BUT LIKE 1 OR 2 LOOK ACCEPTABLY OLD ENOUGH TO MARRY. Not only are the choices awful age wise, character wise they're ♥♥♥♥ too! They're completely forgettable and bland, have nothing interesting to say at all. Except one character, ♥♥♥♥♥, the redheaded furry that looks like she's 12. She only speaks in animal noises and "rawr XD" gibberish. This is by far, the WORST character I have ever encountered in a harvest moon-like game. Every moment that I hear her voice my brain ROTS .
