_childDocuments_.review: After 110 hours of gameplay, I can now review Rune Factory 5 confidently.To get a good idea of what the actual gameplay is like, reviews on YouTube were pretty helpful to me before I bought it.Pros:(1) The game is like a 3D Japanese Stardew Valley to give an idea about it.(2) The game tries to do a lot of things to bring entertainment. It's an RPG adventure, a dating sim (with family building elements), a farming sim, has a simple combat system, monster catching system, and a decent crafting system. It does an okay job of everything and each element comes together into a nicely completed game.(3) It's a casual game with lots to do at the start.(4) The town is nice and the characters are fun.Neutral:(1) Music is only okay.(2) Combat is only okay.(3) The story is okay.Cons (I nitpick a lot of stuff, especially the terrible grinding.):(1) There is a lot of bad/unfun grinding. For example, to fully upgrade the town and farms, about 100,000 wood and 80,000 stone is needed. A player can harvest about 50 wood/stone per real life minute in the most boring way possible. (What idiot would design a game like this?) The game and post-game was completely over before I managed to get many of these upgrades, which were pretty useless at that point. Even if you use a save scum shop exploit, it is only possible to buy 10 wood/stone per real-life second with absolutely no way to automate it. It is so unbelievably unfun. This is a clear mistake in game design.(2) There is a time system in the game. It works via hours. Each morning, the character wakes up at 6am. 2 real-life seconds == 1 minute in-game time. There is absolutely no way to fast-forward through the day, and most events only happen at particular times during the day. Forcibly making the player possibly wait a hundred times for 10-18 real-life minutes is terrible game design. I don't care how the game designers try to justify this. It's ridiculously not fun.(3) The endgame is just grindy. There isn't really any meaningful content besides seducing townsfolk. The endgame dungeon is very short and there isn't much of a reason to replay the dungeon levels other than grinding.(4) The combat system is only barely acceptable. The mechanics are barely acceptable and there isn't enough content for the combat to be very meaningful. The leveling system is totally broken. If my level 400 character defeats several level 2000 monsters, I might gain 1 level. Something isn't right with that ... The combat after a certain point isn't even fun enough to bother leveling up anymore in addition to there being no content.(5) The developers seemed to want to forcibly slow down everything in the game. When I want to plant seeds, about 500 for a few of the in-game farms, I can only plant them 4 at a time. This one task, of many tasks in the game, can take about 10 real-life minutes. After the 50th time, this is not so fun, along with the other tasks that are also just chores. There is some automation for these tasks, but it isn't well designed (It's not the first time something isn't well designed in this game. I could make a very long list, but I'm just pointing out the main things.).(6) The level design is quite bad. The game areas are empty, barren, and boring. It feels like 1 underpaid employee possibly created every area in the game on a tight financial budget with a tight schedule.(7) The rare item drop rate is very bad (1% for many items from bosses), and you will not really understand the crafting system without looking up guides. There are hidden stats (important ones concerning luck and drop rates) that will not display when crafting or on items. The crafting system is good, but it could be so much better if it was more clear.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game, at least not for the current price point. I have a number of reasons why. First, it's important to note that I've never played any of the other Rune Factory games, so I am not biased by the nostalgia. I take this game at face value, without any sort of attachment to the characters or story or world, and when looked at objectively, this game has a LOT of issues for something that costs $50.This game is similar to most farming simulators, in that you can farm, craft items, cook, develop relationships with villagers, get married, and go on adventures. You can also capture animals and enslave them. There is even a plot, though it's not a very good one. Pros: 1. The game is very pretty. Cons: 1. The biggest con for me is the random game crashes that occur FAR too often. I had to actually stop playing the game, because every time I tried to turn in a quest in order to further advance the story, the game crashed, so I literally can't continue. 2. Every day, rocks and tree stumps appear in your farming area. Even if you clear it every single day, they just randomly appear again the next day. I wouldn't have an issue with this, except that they appear ON MY CROPS AND DESTROY THEM.3. (a)You can't place furniture on any sort of grid, you just have to drop them willy nilly and hope for the best. There's no rotating, or lining things up, and while that might be fine for some peope, it drives me insane. Because - (b)you need SO MUCH FURNITURE. For cooking alone, I have about 8 different items that are taking up space in the tiny room I'm given to live in. 4. The controls are a little wonky and it's tough to get used to it. The menus are needlessly complicated. I should be able to just hit I to open my inventory. I think this might be because it's transferred from the switch? Not sure, but it's a small thing because once you get used to it, it's pretty easy to remember. I just think it could be much simpler than it is. 5. Cutscene issues. If you're lucky enough to get a cutscene that doesn't crash your game, you now have to worry about whether or not it's a cutscene that will advance time. Because some of them do that. You can miss entire festivals, all because you started the wrong cutscene at the wrong time. And they're unavoidable, too! If you make the mistake of stepping into the wrong area at the wrong time, you're screwed. This is also a problem because for some of the cutscenes, you can only have one active at a time...and these can take several days to get through before you can start the next one. So, for example, if you want to start the event with character A, but you run into character B first, you now have to complete all the cutscenes with character B before you can even start with character A. 6. Building relationships. Talking to everyone every single day and giving loved gifts should make building relationships with the villagers move along at a pretty good pace. The issue, though, is that giving a loved gift only gives about 5% xp. Loved gifts aren't exactly easy to come by, so raising up the relationships becomes very difficult. Giving a loved gift on a birthday doesn't even double the amount. It's a huge pain in the ass, and honestly makes me not care about any of them. 7. Last but not least, the villagers themselves. Their personalites are random and inconsistent. The little cutscenes you get with them are awkward and most of the time make no sense. This could be a translation issue, but it doesn't change the fact that it's very difficult to really develop any sort of attachment to the characters in the game. Including my own character, honestly, which I didn't even get to customize, and frankly is just a really nosy do-gooder with no personality. Anyway, I could go on, but honestly the short of it is that I do not recommend paying $50 for this game. I paid $25 because I got it on sale, and I still think I paid too much. I feel like the folks who rave about this game are the same ones who played the first four and are just feeling sentimental. There are so many other games out there that are better *and CHEAPER) than this one. Go play one of those instead. Trust me.

_childDocuments_.review: According to my wife’s boyfriend, Rune factory 5 is a hollow, borderline soulless game that lacks any real drive. There is not one aspect of the game that is pulled off in a satisfying way. It’s like the budget went mostly towards the animated cutscenes. Like they started making this on the 3DS and just emulated it when they jumped to console and PC.Yet for me…… RF5 is the most gay-accessible farming-sim game I have played to date. It’s literally the game the gays have been waiting for. Not only can you marry male or female characters regardless of your gender, you can marry furries! I tried replaying RF4S but having to play as a girl after being spoiled with RF5, I just couldn’t get into it (I did play RF4 religiously on the 3DS, back when you just made do with whatever dating mechanics you were given). This alone makes it worth it for me.The Rune Factory franchise itself has a load of jank in it's gameplay that can be both fun and annoying. RF5 is a little more approachable than RF4 for newcomers and can be easy to sink a few hundred hours into. Expect low brow gameplay with charming characters and a long progression system. If that's in your wheelhouse, I'd say you're good to go.The story is a bit short and manages to have many plot holes and loose ends in spite of its brevity, but if I'm being honest I've never been particularly impressed by RF stories. They often follow similar patterns (seriously, enough amnesia, it's just lazy) and are generally bland. It's a fantasy farming/life sim game first and foremost, not a story game. Still a fun game though.There's a solid game underneath the multiple hiccups, its still Rune Factory after all. But it definitely gives the impression of a dish that was rushed out of the oven too soon. Despite its flaws I’ve really enjoyed it but maybe that's just because I love and will play any farming game with romance that I can get my hands on as well as the fact that I can be an unapologetic flamboyant homosexual and marry any of the men I want. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad. That's about it. Not as good as RF4 so if you have to get one get that one instead. This very much feels like the studio's  first 3D game and has a number of accompanying bugs and issues. some crashes, odd loading times, startup lag, and a rather empty world. It does have a certain charm and I can't say I dislike any of the characters but I can't really say that I like them all too much. They feel uninspired, generic. These types of games usually fall on a few tropes but this feels a bit worse. There's also the ghost of cut content wafting around, certain characters feel as though they should be romancable but aren't. There was some buzz around gay marriage this time around but it's handled in a rather hamfisted way. The whole "everyone is bisexual" trope is a little silly. It feels forced or off in moments that really shouldn't be. Some people just ain't gay, and this anyone and everyone approach feels a bit cheap. _childDocuments_.review: this is my favorite game i picked up during summer sale 2023! very underrated. i loved Rune Factory 4 back on my 3ds, and all the mixed reviews had me hesitating on whether or not to get rf5. Ircha Gaming on youtube was obsessed with it and kept praising it, and she's pretty well versed on cozy games/lifesim games. so i decided to take the plunge!i made sure to alter my expectations to "not as good as RF4", and what i found is, my experience is more like "this is like an RF4 remake but in 3D"! just maybe with a bit less content than RF4 had (smaller budget). the gameplay is top notch like it was in rf4, but some small hitches in the presentation and art style betray that this game was made just after the company nearly stopped existing. temper your expectations based on that and you'll be okay!i'm playing it on Steam Deck, and for the game to be good on it, there are a few mods you MUST install for it to be enjoyable. yes it's a hassle, but imho, worth it! these mods are necessary because the devs sadly seem to have abandoned the pc port.. thankfully the mods fix up most problems. the mods are: - controller fix (so you get controller button icons all around the game, instead of keyboard keys which gets really confusing.)- rf5fix (fixes stuff like the aspect ratio). it also lets you set draw distance to way higher, and crank up a bunch of quality settings.. it makes the game feel more alive and less barren!- and you can optionally also add the hd texture mod (on nexus) to make it look prettierthen set refresh rate to 40hz and fps limit to 40fps as wellso after all that modding, how is the game itself?well, i feel like i'm playing RF4, but in 3D! so many of the little things i loved in RF4 are here! like the way you pick stacks of items up, the way you talk to people, the short voice tidbits, the cute sparkly sound effects, the many gameplay systems rf4 had.. i absolutely love it!but if you haven't played any Rune Factory games before, what should you expect? well, have you ever played a Story of Seasons or Harvest Moon game? it's that, plus fantasy and RPG elements added to it. you can sink hundreds of hours into it, especially if you love hanging out in the relaxing, colorful, pretty world of RF5. and if you've ever played Stardew Valley, you'll probably be a bit underwhelmed by the game because Stardew basically mastered the farming game genre and easily beats any Harvest Moon game imho, so while RF5 has more gameplay systems and variety than Harvest Moon, stardew still has more than either of those. but stardew isn't in a cutesy 3d anime art style and isn't part of a well established franchise! so they both have their charm. and i love both. if you're on the fence because of all these reviews: keep in mind most of these are about the Switch version which is very stuttery and runs badly. the steam version runs way better, and is prettier when modded!highly recommended if you're a fan of life sim/farming sim games like Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, My Time At Portia/Sandrock, and the like!❤️

_childDocuments_.review: I put an unreal amount of hours into Rune Factory: Frontier on the Wii back in the day, and it was one of the greatest gaming experiences of my entire life. My brothers and I grew up on the Harvest Moon series (starting with 64) and were always very deep into RPGs. Ratiata Stories, FFX, FFIX, Oblivion, Paper Mario etc. When we heard about a "Fantasy Harvest Moon" we pretended to laugh at it and ignore it. Burying the fact that we'd always felt the urge to battle in one of these farming sims. Rune Factory: Frontier delivered everything we'd ever wanted in a game. So when the series started cutting it's slice of life\farming elements, I kinda dropped off of the series. We picked up RF4 which was great, but not the true successor to Frontier...A top down game could never live up to it no matter how good it was. After 18 hours in Game I can say that I'm getting those Frontier vibes again. And it feels incredible. ...They're even doing the insane Farm voice acting. _childDocuments_.review: I keep seeing comparisons being drawn between Rune Factory 5 and Harvestella. After playing a fair amount of both, Harvestella is a more polished experience, while Rune Factory 5 is the more fleshed-out of the two. If you care about graphics and overall gameplay, get Harvestella. This game looks like a hot mess from 2008. In fact, it looks worse than the Rune Factory titles released on the Wii. Not sure what happened there, but over time I found that it -- weirdly -- added charm to the overall experience, and there was a childlike earnestness to some of the developer's decisions. If you care about romancing characters, a cozy atmosphere, and easy combat, get Rune Factory 5. Regarding combat, it's very, very clunky. Any form of challenge you may encounter is super artificial, only coming from spongy, over-leveled enemies that you have to tank and cross your fingers you won't die before they do. The developers tried to implement some form of strategy by including a dodge-roll mechanic that allows you to parry if you move out of the way just in time, but it's so annoyingly janky that it actively causes me to wipe. Also, the animation lock is ROUGH. If the developers implemented a patch that included animation cancelling, the combat would feel immensely better. It sounds like I hate this game, but I am weirdly addicted to it. There's moments of greatness that are so profound that they're enough to keep me wading through the b.s. I can't say that I recommend this game fully -- only get this if the problems I listed above wouldn't bother you all that much.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good so far, it's the Rune Factory style effectively updated for a mostly behind-the-shoulder 3rd Person View.  The 3rd Person View works pretty well, giving a lot more immersion than the top-down style of Rune Factory 4 (which is the only one of the series I've actually played), though there are a few minor things I've noticed that don't work as well with it, notably that precision tasks like placing furniture can be kind of wonky.  Not enough for me to call the controls an issue, but it is worth pointing out.  Haven't gotten too far into it yet to comment much on the story, but I like the characters so far - they're not quite as colorful or over-the-top personality-wise as some of the characters from the previous game, but they're each still charming in their own ways.Honestly, I was a little worried about this one since I've seen a fair number of reviews effectively calling it an inferior game compared to its predecessor, but as usual it seems like minor gripes being blown way out of proportion.  Outside of the story, which again I haven't played enough to comment on yet, almost every other complaint I've seem seems silly - things like the other fields being far away or the town being too big are non-issues due to a fast travel system to the fields & even a few fast travel points around town (and even if you weren't using those then we're still talking barely a minute of running across town, tops).  The complaints about the grind also seem silly to me, as at least in my mind that's the main point of the game in this genre - you have to build up your skills, money, relationships, etc. slowly over time, just like basically every other simulation-style game out there.tl;dr: If you liked Rune Factory 4 but want new locations & characters instead of just replaying it, you'll like Rune Factory 5.  Probably worth it even at full price if you're a big fan of the style, but if you can wait for a sale then it's absolutely worth it if you like simulation games in general.

_childDocuments_.review: I really would only recommend this game to hardcore Rune Factory fans. It's just possibly the roughest entry in the series. I would say if you want console RF, go play Tides of Destiny instead if you can. I originally had the switch version of this and it was almost unplayable with really bad stuttery lag. The pc version luckily runs way better and I haven't had any issues. Unfortuantely, it's not enough to save the game from it's other issues. It's just kind of all around lacking. It's not "bad" but the characters feel sterilized more and the story is functional but somewhat bland. The game is kind of an eye sore in spots in comparison to RF4/3 and lacks those game's artistic stylisation outside of character portraits. There's a lot of little details that cause the game to die by a thousand cuts. I had to turn off ambient sounds in the summer season for example because they made a god awful cicada noise loop incessantly. Considering how saturated the farming/fantasy life genre currently is this game really should've had more support and not been released in it's current state. Despite all of this, it still just has that RF charm and I find myself enjoying it anyways. Get it at a steep discount if you're a big RF fan and haven't played the others in the series. I almost grabbed this version just to show support for more RF games to be made. At least the current in dev game for the series looks much better.

_childDocuments_.review: The great:More Rune Factory! For many people reading this, that might be all you really wantedThe good in summary:Not bad for a port of a Switch game (most of my playtime is still on that version)Decent variety of activities comparable to other games in the seriesSame depth to crafting/upgrading (though here really it only matters much if you're playing on hard)Combat can be surprisingly funSome good stories and interesting characters mixed in (and some boring/weird ones)The bad in detail:There's an uneven lack of polish on just about everything, from the awkward walk/run animations, to a strange mix of high and low rez UI textures here and there, to animations where one frame has a part of the model pop jarringly out of place repeatedlyThe flow of control while interacting with things is all over the place, there's a lot of "idle" control-locked animation baked into many non-combat actions that's particularly jarring when you're harvesting plants and suchThe inventory system is still worse and harder to navigate than the one in Rune Factory: Frontier and Oceans, which had a perfectly serviceable selection wheel (or two separately customizable ones at that) that has bafflingly never popped up again in the seriesConclusion:It's not a bad game by any means, it runs well enough on my PC, and it hits pretty much all the same high notes as previous RF games for the day to day activities. Hopefully it'll get some post-launch polish to address some of the control and animation quality issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Liked the female character designs.- Combat was fun, especially now that you can add 3 people to your party. Dungeon crawling and boss battles were also fun. These seem to be the few aspects that were not changed much from the other Rune Factory games.- There are a lot of QOL improvements from the other Rune Factory games e.g. you can transfer wood/stone, weeds and fodder to the respective bins in bulk and also fast travel from anywhere.- No RNG required to romance characters like in Rune Factory 4. I personally close to marry Lucy. Cons:- Compared to other Rune Factory games, story was kinda mid and way too predictable.  - Certain quests require you to be at specific locations at specific times yet there is no way to fast-forward in-game time. They also changed the progression of time to 2 second per game minute instead of 1 second per game minute in the other games so time literally passes slower. - They should have never tried to transition from 2D to 3D IMO. I don’t understand why the Devs keep trying to fix what isn’t even broken. 3D graphics look like ♥♥♥♥. Characters in the “3D cut scenes” show almost no emotion and they even have to overlay the 2D models to compensate. Some of the 3D cut scenes don’t even make sense. In the end of Act 2, the main character (MC) rides the Light Dragon literally standing up. Like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ how is he balancing? Were to the Devs too incompetent to animate proper dragon riding animations? Probably. This is in stark contrast to the ending of one of the acts in Rune Factory 4 where the MC rides the Wind Dragon back home and it was a touching scene.   - On that note, the town looks too artificial. Buildings are way too far apart and are placed at awkward angles. Doesn’t feel like a town people actually live in, more like a stage set of a town. - The number of festivals seem to have decreased. I hate how during the festivals, the NPCs just stand around in clusters without interacting with each other. Another thing the other Rune Factory games did better in 2D.- Placing furniture in your house/farm is a nightmare, especially for people with OCD. For some asinine reason, the Devs thought that furniture needed to have a HUGE gap between it and all other structures. This means that you cannot place your furniture against the wall in your house. Not only that, these is no grid etc. to help you place your furniture, meaning it will look disgustingly sloppy with none of the furniture lining up. - ~25% of the steam achievements require marrying each of the bachelors/bachelorettes. IMO, there should have been only one achievement on getting married. The game does not even allow you to marry multiple people. Personally, I have zero interest in marrying any of the dudes so 100%ing the game is already impossible for me.- One of the key mechanics in the game require the MC to talk to NPCs to earn Rune Points to be used for upgrades/unlocks. This is a staple of the genre. However, each of the NPCs seem to have only like 5 lines of dialogue, a stark contrast to the other Rune Factory games where NPCs had 100+ lines. I was already getting repeated lines after the first in-game week, making talking to them a chore.  - The male MC has an extremely annoying voice and can’t seem to shut the ♥♥♥♥ up when doing repeated tasks like farming or mining/logging. I cringe when he goes “Yatta” every other time I auto pick-up items. - NPCs that sell items also cannot shut the ♥♥♥♥ up and let you browse items to buy in peace and instead yap the same line of dialogue EVERY 5 seconds. - Hate that the so-called “cut scenes” for the romance trigger automatically, even the male ones that I have no interest in, and basically freeze romance progress with other characters until it is resolved. Overall, 5/10. RF3 > RF4 > RF5. Kinda sad that the rune factory games are progressively getting worse. Still, Rune Factory 4 was at least an OK game. Rune Factory 5 is basically the Dragon Age 2 of the Rune Factory franchise. A decent farming and life sim that I can’t stop playing but as a Rune Factory game, utter trash. I feel like the Devs were forced to make the game in 3D and phoned it in. I find it funny that this is the cheapest Rune Factory game on steam despite being the latest one, almost as if the Devs themselves had no faith in their product.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, and its like? Did you want the mines in Stardew valley to have a higher emphasis on combat? Did you dream of Dungeon crawling, or having a narrative driven farming game? You may just be the right fit for Rune Factory 5This here game is a RPG first and a Farm Sim/Harvest Moon-like second. You'll be grown crops, wooing townsfolk, and doing a LOT of simple combat. Be prepared to have level-ups galore in a multitude of skills. Every step and move you make will have an associated stat or skill that can be leveled. This is RF5's main draw. If you want a lot of RPG then its here for your pleasureThe farming is nice, simplistic, and feeds easily into other systems of buffing, crafting, and romancing. The gearing is relatively fine, you'll make most of your best stuff, and that has its draws. The combat and dungeon design is just OK, and the bosses are a hilarious mixed bag. Some seem utterly bland, some more inspired, none of them really stand out nor challenge. This is fine, as you'll be grinding those too.Did I say Grind? that's RF5's main Schtick. Grinding for levels, grinding enemies for loot and rare drops, grinding skills to make and do more stuff, grinding days for crops and townsfolk and gifts. Its girnd: the game. Mildly addictive too, if my playtime is anything to go by. If you like this kind of game ~a la~ Disgaea, Phantom brave, etc then you'll like RF5. What you may not like is the HORRIBLE voice acting, the HORRIBLE plot and story, and the pretty awful performance. even on PC! it has an art design....The game look OK at best, and runs pretty sloppy. The narrative, which is a large part of the title, is bland, dull, trite,..its got nothing going on and nothing to talk about. Might have been better left without it, as its very distracting. That said, the title is fine. FINE. 6-7/10. it runs, its fun, its got a lot of time to kill. Its even mildly replayable if you want to run the other gener or date someone new. Its pretty ok, and when its fun its FUN. it just has a lot of other stuff holding it down and tripping it up. I guess wait for a sale, but 40 bones for ~90 hours of game is a bargain.

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly laid back RPG in the vein of Harvest Moon.  The combat isn't terribly difficult and can be annoying with long animations.  There are several ways to break the game and get late game items early on (in a legitimate fashion) which can be fun.The romance part (at least for male characters) is ruined though since you can only romance the kid looking characters and not the big mommy milfs.  The game actually has the poor taste to put a sleepy chef with huge knockers, a sexy fox lady in short shorts, and a sultry pirate nurse in front of you and then doesn't let you romance them.  It would have been awesome if they let you romance Elsje or Misasagi or Simone but nope, the only options are all the kids that look like grade-schoolers.Oh also, the game has very, extremely annoying voice overs that can drive you insane.  Doing actions on the farm and having the character perform a voice line for each one or when you are in a shopping menu and the character has to say "Take your time, OK?" once every ten seconds (no, that's not an exaggeration).  It can get difficult to want to keep playing because it is so annoying.The farming is OK and managing all that can be fun but all the crafting you have to do to level stuff up can be a bit tedious at times.  It's also pretty annoying how they do the cooking tables as each type of cooking has to have it's own table.  It gets a little ridiculous having to remember which of the 7 cooking tables you need to visit to make the thing you want to make.  These could have easily be combined into one table that is upgraded over time to allow for more functionality.Overall I put a good amount of time into it and I enjoy it however If I could go back and do it again I don't think I would pay full price for it.  Waiting for a sale and picking this up at a 39.99~29.99 price point would probably be perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has very deep and complex mechanics for farming, crafting and upgrading, but it never makes any real use out of them. You can spend hours leveling up your crops, learning the tricky and intricate ways to optimally craft and ugprade equipment, decking out your villagers in the best available gear and training your monster companions for greatest efficiency in battle; but none of it really matters because you'll have cleared the main storyline and the supposedly challenging postgame dungeon before you've ever felt a need to craft actual endgame gear.To give you a sense of how shallow the content is, more players have cleared the postgame dungeon down to the last floor than have made it halfway through autumn on year 1. It's really a waste of a great system for a fantasty farming simulator. The core gameplay is satisfying but there is no need or reward for learning and mastering what it has to offer. Even on "Hard" difficulty, the entire thing can be plowed through spamming level 1 spells and abilities.It is with a heavy heart that I say you shouldn't bother with this installment in the Rune Factory series. It had potential but it delivered in what feels like a woefully incomplete state.

_childDocuments_.review: Pay no heed to the play time listed, I copied my save over form the switch version to play this on steam. It was worth it to buy the game twice. This game is super solid, it knows what it wants to be and executes it very well. It makes farming fun, combat fun, gives you a reason to talk to the NPC's regularly. It gives you a well defined progression system that isn't afraid of letting players free style it. You can beat a demon dog to death with a watering can then eat a massive turnip. Games fun, immersive, casual, and heartwarming. I wanna compare this to harvestella, which is the game that encouraged me to start up rune factory 5 in the first place. I had played a bit of rune factory 4 on 3ds when that was still new, and I remember being rather impressed by it compared to harvest moon games I had played previously. But for whatever reason, I put the game down one day and never picked it back up. I was hoping harvestella would be a square themed rune factory I could sink my teeth into. And despite being a competent game, it was a very boring one on top of that. I think thats proof in the pudding of how far Rune factory goes to make itself fun to play. It gives life to something that well funded imitators just can't pull off. It has good writing, fun combat, worthwhile mechanics, ect ect ect. THe game feeds back into itself in many ways, giving you an almost gotcha level feeling of progression. You can always be leveling this, working on that, focusing on this goal, whatever. Now for the complaining bits. Game has some ♥♥♥♥♥ parts too. Decoration just isn't worth doing. They allow you to place stuff all over the world, anywhere you can find a flat piece of land. But you can't have your furniture close to your walls in the building you live in. Everything has to be awkwardly pushed forward, taking up extra space and it looks garish as ♥♥♥. It almost feels like they wan't you to decorate cuz they have a selection of decoration items, but you can't place anything on walls or on desks, and nothing can be close to a wall, so don't bother. Also, there are some enemies who have some instant death projectiles too. Maybe one's a melee attack, All on common enemies that easily get lost in the shuffle of a fight, and more than once blended in with the environment. This sends you straight to the hospitle, where they take a huge fee for passing out (though it gets more manageable the more you focus on farming)  So that's a bit of a ♥♥♥♥♥.Lastly, I wish the dodge wasn't tied to a button release opposed to a button press. Most of the buttons are filled, granted, but I'm sure there was a better way. You press the R button to enter a walk, which also locks your characters direction to the camera for precise aiming (Works on furniture placing too). It also grants you access to your extra rune abilities if and when you unlock those. But if you release it in under a second, you character will do an evasive dash instead, which means unless you got a quick finger, all of your dodges are gonna be delayed. You can't even just hold the button and release when an attack comes out, since it locks out after a little bit. 0Honestly though, I'm really happy to have come across this game. I've just gotten to winter of my first year, started the season married to my bride of choice ♥♥♥♥♥, beat the final secret dungeon the game has to offer, and am eager to go even further. If the game makers read this for whatever reason, I'd love a DLC expansion or two for character interactions and dungeons. Just sayin, at least my moneys on the table

It's not amazing and it's not even good, but it's not bad either... it's just OK.NPCs don't help you much, half the time they just follow and stand there.For some reason you'll have entire boulders or tree stumps just appearing out of thin air in your farming areas and it's so frustrating, you'll be gone for like 30 seconds and it can happen. _childDocuments_.review: While this game isn't terrible, it's still a pretty bad game. At its best, it's barely correct. At its worse, it lacks basic features.- You cannot put more than 9 items in the same group, so you end up with tens of pile of 9 items. Those items are, sometimes, at various level which is a good idea. But you can't separate those easily, so you can't throw / sell only the lower levels.- You cannot access your ressources when crafting. Plus, you cannot separate ressources in different chests. It's very difficult to know how much ressource you have.- About housing, there is no grid nor camera when you move your furniture, so you cannot put them exactly where you want. In addition, you have to let a space between furnitures so the character can go through. As a result, your place looks like a mess and there's nothing you can do about this.- You level up by eating bread. It's not a problem per say, but it's typical of how they approched the game : with no idea how to link the gameplays together. Crafting, combat, exploration and so on are kind of all over the places, never really impacting each other.- Graphics are bad for a 50€ game. Add this to empty backgrounds despite various environment, and the exploration isn't compelling.- Fighting is OK in general with a lot of various way.- Events are empty. Litteraly. There's nothing to do except for going to a place and talk once with people. Which is a shame because I actually liked the characters...I don't think this game is bad : you can still have a good time with some good characters and fun combats. But it lacks too many basic elements of crafting - social sim to be considered as "good". And since it's the 5th entry of a serie, it's unforgivable and DEFINITELY not worth 50 €.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love this game and hold it dear as part of a cherished franchise, it’s undeniably the weakest installment in terms of storytelling. The narrative lacks consistency, giving a rushed impression that undermines what could have been a truly impactful tale. The villain, unfortunately, comes across as a missed opportunity, only making an appearance late in the game before undergoing an abrupt change of heart, an underwhelming payoff that falls short of the franchise’s usual standards.The ending, which centers around the journey of friendship and the beauty of building connections, had so much potential. The concept is solid, but the execution left much to be desired. The resolution felt unsatisfying, lacking the emotional weight that made previous entries memorable.Another disappointment was the quality of the CG graphics. While the early visuals are striking, likely designed for promotional appeal, the quality dips significantly as the game progresses, turning cutscenes in the latter stages into something resembling a low-effort slideshow rather than the vibrant animations the franchise is known for.Despite these shortcomings, I still deeply appreciate the game’s charming townspeople, who were written with care and personality. However, issues like an outdated engine, poor performance, and fragmented storytelling detracted from the experience. I’m hopeful that the next entry in the Rune Factory series will address these issues and restore the franchise’s reputation for immersive storytelling and quality gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a easy game to review and recommend.First stay away from the switch version, I've played both extensively and the PC port is perfect. I enjoyed my time with this on switch, but the lag was indeed very noticeable.On PC? Its like a brand new game, so don't sully you're opinion on this from the switch.Outside my praise for how well done this pc port is, here are my other highlights.The story is actually pretty good, the combat is fun, I love the art direction, it brings back my nostalgia for my first; harvest moon save the homeland, "weird comparison I know", but that's just how it feels for me.I love all the character's in rf5, so much so that I know exactly what answers to give during harvest festivals. Something that I've never been able to quite grasp in previous installments, like my beloved rf4.Now the bad...You're MC talks too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much, example you want to water you're crops one by one right? well you will be plagued with; IT'S WATERING TIME!, GROW UP BIG AND STRONG OK?, HOPE IT COMES OUT OK? Rinse and repeat quite frequently  I can manage it, by making fun of it. but when fishing??? LETS CATCH A BIG ONE, EASY DOES IT, and lastly, HOPE I GET A BITE. Every.... Single.... CAST!!!It throws off my timing, and ruins the relaxation of fishing. I can't fish in this game without thinking of RDR2 fishing for some reason lol.Decorating you're room is terrible as well, Everything you place will be a good 2ft away from the wall, so there is a ugly awkward space between everything and you're wall. On Switch you had to glitch the game to fix it, on PC you can do that or mod it. RF4 had a similar issue, but being top down allowed a little more freedom to aligned everything, not much but still. While on the topic of houses.... You stay in Seed's "you're organization barracks" Top floor. No door between the main hall and you're floor. Yet one of you're potential love interest, gets her own room with a door, as does you're captain, on the main floor. How the hell are you supposed to make baby's like this??? You kinda have to turn off you're brain and pretend, there is some kind of barrier between the twist staircases between yours and the main hall. As a result it never really feels like you're own home, after you finish the main story, you can buy a house, but it only counts as a secondary home, and is not much better. I love Rune factory 5, but this issues keep it far from near perfection. The Goodnews? All are easily fixed in Rune Factory 6.There are some other little bits of good and bad, like the size of the map, how lived in it feels, and the speed of how time goes by, but their more debatable between what people will like or dislike, this were just my in general highlighted thoughts.Should you purchase Rune Factory 5? I'm biased here because I love this series, and I own stock in Tencent. "Their owner"          But yes I think you should, if you like games like Stardew valley, Story Of Seasons ect and want more games like it.Just keep some of this issues in mind since they do keep this game from being the best in the series.My Final score is: 8 out of 10. This was never going to be able to reach 10, but it could and should have made 9, but the Housing / Decorating issue's really hurts this title in a big way. and the repetitive dialog, "especially when fishing". Can really annoy the crap out of you.

_childDocuments_.review: ive played maybe 8 or so hours on the switch version and that was pretty bad (even overclocked) so coming from that feels great here. the game looks more clean and runs much better and getting the uncompressed textures mod from the nexus is a must if u want it to look more like an old sega anime game type pc port lol.its still just rune factory 5 with a stable framerate tho. nothing special going for this port other than performance and mods floating around. if u own the game on switch and stopped playing or find it hard to play due to performance then buy this (like me). if u simply have never played rune factory but want a chil farming sim with real rpg elements unlike stardew then this game is for u. if ur fresh off the rune factory 4 boat u will most likely be disappointed due to the new 3d style (which looks like a polished ps2 game/mobile game).so yeah, pros:-great performance over switch version-semi-kinda-sorta-not really mod support-its rune factory so it can be enjoyed ina very chill enviroment-music is a vibe-can run on almost anything tbh-decent amount of choices for graphic options (for an anime game)-learning curve aint rly a thing. just read tutorialscons:-3d art style is wack asf-game feels like it was released unfinished control wise sometimes-mouse and keyboard controls are japanese pc port quality (nails on a chalkboard)-controller support can get a little quirky sometimes-zero enhancements to texture quality was made out of the box. you will start with the base textures used on switch and will need to download a 100 some mb pack to change that-this is the EASIEST GAME EVER MADE 90% of the timein conclusion: play L4D2 with anime mods instead idk its more fun imo

_childDocuments_.review: Earth-mate for Life! This game get a lot of unnecessary hate from the fans and its sad. Stop riding 4 so hard, it had its own flaws (and i loved that one too) I thought of writing a long review but in short:Loved: The characters (even if some were copy paste traits of 4, Hina is so precious and Ludmidla being such an open perv was fun, they are all great, they deliver the usual cheesy and corny lines I'm here for :) ), the music top tier as always, even if faulty- 3d environment and expansive map to explore was an upgrade.(sure it could have used a little more spruce and glam but it was nice and can't deny its an improvement in the series even to the older 3d tittles) Loved they updated technical things like being able to switch easy between storage,among other newer things;More time in the day! _childDocuments_.review: I'm guessing that going the full 3d route was cheaper to make. Ah well. Having fun so far anyway even if the charm of the handhelds is gone.Fans of 4 will be glad to see the animal issue is still here! Notice how your main patch of farmland doesn't have a monster barn? A clever way to try and cover up the crazy lag you get from animals working on it every morning. Getting up early and going to a farm dragon will show you that the lag issue still exists from animals harvesting. At least it's easier to avoid being near? There is also a fun glitch some have had of their animal just going poof. I have had that happen in 4 once as well though. My poor wooly.Speaking of farm dragons, they way they were introduced and randomly given to you throughout the story feels really weird. Just "Here is dragon." :| I just don't understand why they aren't seasonal fields. The ice dragon isn't a winter field for example. There are no differences at all. Feels like a waste making models for them. Would have been fine letting us have the random little season fields and then one farm dragon that we could expand upon. Maybe he couple keep growing for more crop space. Give the crystals more of a permanent purpose.Targeting feels bad. Doesn't help that they gutted the darkness spell. Used to lock enemies in place now it pushes them away. Hammers have been painful to level on enemies. The range just feels terrible. Good thing to do is just work on taming the first boss and brush/feed it every day. That thing makes me useless. Just farm up 8 bells from the boss, brush it 15 times, then give it bells till she joins. You can even ride her and just command it to spam fire. Sadly I haven't seen a way to skip the boss cutscene. The stupid smoke introduction plays every time. For multiple bosses. Each time you enter. Biggest complaint about the game so far right there.Kinda wish the town was smaller? A mod that adds more teleport points does help a ton with that. If you are working on friendship with someone that lives on the other side of town and are just ending days after gifting then I suggest it.Mods like RF fix and Better Furniture Placement are basically a requirement. The game is very picky about where you can place things. I want my entire kitchen set by my farm darn it. I also recommend Automatic Fishing. Sure, the minigame is just the one from 4. But do you REALLY wanna go through all that again?All in all, it still feels almost exactly like 4 once you get into the groove of things. Same gameplay pattern. 3d just doesn't feel as good.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is even better than Rune Factory 5.Rune Factory 4 had a lot of bugs, and took a long time to fix any of them, and it's still buggy as heck, to the point of being difficult to play. It was hard to embrace.Rune Factory 5 has far fewer bugs, and is perfectly playable in its release state. It is a lot more playable and easier to get used to playing.It also has great gameplay, tons of content, fun and friendly characters, a delightful storyline, cool monsters to cute monsters to fight, befriend, tame, mount, and hang out with.Plus with the loads of highly desirable characters as friends and lovers, RF5 has provided way more options than before, especially considering the diversity they offer.Lastly, might I add that the game offers SO MUCH in the way of unique storylines for each NPC in the game, befriending people unlocks entire side storylines, there is so much to do this game will provide hundreds of hours of gameplay.I think this might be one of my favorite Farm Sims to date. Plus it might be one of my top favorite RPGs too, since I love mastering the wide variety of weapons and magic available and going on adventures in this game. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a keyboard player and the port of this is terrible.  Some things can only be done by using keyboard only, the mouse either doesn't work as it should or doesn't work at all (having the mouse disappear during conversations....), catching fish by only pressing F instead of the same click used to start fishing, etc..  Huge negatives here for gameplay.The change in camera for farming is amazingly terrible.  Getting close to the farm area just to have the camera angle switched, with it's much small field of view is beyond irritating.  At least expand the view to encompass the farm plot and surrounding area.Recipe breads?  ....ugh.  Currently, my toon is rank 21 in cooking has had three to five skill ups and still can't use another recipe bread.  At least let someone know what skill level they need to be to use these things.  The entire game leaves the player guessing at many things that should be simple.Tool usage.  There is no reason to have such a convoluted system to use farm tools.  This is a 2020 title that throws back to 1990 era item usage.  If you approach a rock, auto-equip the necessary tool and use it on the rock by clicking OR simply make repeated left arrows cycle through the various tools.  There is absolutely no need to press Q to do the same things.  Too convoluted and messy.The one thing I can say is the combat is fairly decent.  Other than that, My Time in Sandrock has RF5 beat in every other aspect.As one can see the negatives focus on mechanics.  The story itself was decent, not ground breaking through the end of chapter 1, but decent and enjoyable.  The characters were good and interactions with them were fun.Only did one festival and during festival day the town was empty.  Tried to find the festivities but there were none around.  Never did another since it seemed to be a waste of points.Starting quests/helper board needs a lot of polish.  Timing is the biggest thing.  The farm starts with rocks and tree stumps in the middle of it.  Yet, the quests providing the axe and hammer come days after the player begins the game.  Same with fishing.  Day X, give Beatrice a squid.  Day X+1 Try fishing, here's a pole.  That's just backwards.  Getting the tools needed to do things should be the first quests given.  Not planting, not harvesting, not explore the woods, not deliver item x to person y.  If the player is to be provided the tools via quest then they ABSOLUTELY need to be the first quests given.  Otherwise, there is much wasted money on tools that will be duplicated.  The current system is beyond terrible.TL;DR:  The game has massive room for improvement in gameplay and mechanics and informing the player of them making the game frustrating to play in spite of the decent story and characters.  Can't recommend.  Go play Sandrock.

Controls during farming are extremely clunky, and you are constantly fighting against the camera (which snaps to top-down view in a farming field with the shipping box/fertilizer/fodder which are outside the top-down view zone).The RPG aspect is great. Not innovative, but great. Dungeons and field combat zones feature unique monsters filled with personality and unique attacks/gimmicks. You can befriend monsters, and each has their own unique farming task that you can customize slightly. You can bring friends and husbands/wives to adventure with you. Dungeons also have their own unique puzzles and stage hazards, and the overall layout of each dungeon is different. Weapons, weapon skills, and magic all sport VERY different play styles (different timings and ranges, etc.)If you like RPGs, and don't mind the mess of a farming sim this is, then get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: (I've played this game on Switch. Purchased it again on Steam, so I've spent longer on the game than it shows on the review, about 40 hours or so.)Although this game is a sort of step-down from Rune Factory 4, what people don't seem to understand is that RF4 was made by a seasoned development team that had 6+ years of experience creating a very specific type of game, which were 3D farming/adventure games with 2D backgrounds for handheld consoles. Unfortunately, even with the huge success of RF4's launch on the 3DS, it could not save the developers parent company from going bankrupt. Part of the team and the director was bought out by Marvelous, and, honestly, its a miracle RF5 even exists in the first place, let alone the game itself feeling very much a good fit into the RF series, since it was developed by mostly new developers in a different environment. So when you see people trying to directly compare RF4 to RF5, just know the situations are vastly different and it's rather unfair to compare the two. Although, the game running the way it did on the Switch is inexcusable.With that tidbit out of the way, I can honestly say that this game is great. Stardew Valley always felt dry and boring in almost every way. While not being a bad game in any sense, everything felt like it wasn't enough. Characters felt kind of dull, the art wasn't great (fixed easily with mods), combat was barebones, farming mechanics were effective but standard, and fishing was fun for the first hour. It is the only game farming game I know of that boasts multiplayer so it has that going for it. I felt much of the same about other farming sims like Harvest Moon and Story of Seasons feel into this same category of "not enough stuff to engage with." I was even desperate enough to Kickstart Re: Legend... Which will be the first and last project I ever Kickstart. Harvestella looked like a great alternative at first, but after trying the demo and looking up more information about it, the lacking story, weak combat, and absence of marriage options really drags it down.RF games are different, though. There's always so much to do and so many things to level up. Every usable weapon has a level, running is a level, sleeping is a level, eating is a level, etc. The farming mechanics themselves seem pretty simple, but are extremely deep you honestly probably won't even know how to do 80% of the things you can do in farms without looking it up. You can tame almost every creature in the game, and each one will yield or do something different. The choice of things that can be done and depth of RF games are often dizzying, but the game never really forces you to engage in all of them, not do you really need to. You're always free to take the game on piecemeal or try to cram your day to make it as efficient as possible. Combat is passable in this entry, not all that amazing, but functionally fine and still more engaging than combat in other farming games. The choice of bachelors and bachelorettes are quite nice, as well, and with the introduction of same-sex marriages, your preferences are no longer locked out to your character gender.There is still a ways to go for the current RF team, however. A lot of minor but consistent issues still nag the game, such as chopping and mining hitboxes being janky, the farming camera being wonky, lack of the huge post-game content RF4 had, not being able to place furniture close to each other (fixed with mods) and the game honestly looking like an upscaled PS2 game, just to name a couple. I still think Rune Factory games are the best farming sim games out there, and RF5 is in that top category. It was enough for me to buy the game again on Steam even though I owned the RF5 Special Edition on Switch. I'm really crossing my fingers the team will have enough experience now and has the proper budget for their next Rune Factory game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of Rune Factory since Rune Factory 2 (which is my favorite). That said, I've played all games in the series except Frontier and Tides of Destiny. I delayed getting this game for two years due to bad reviews. 20 hours in, I'm willing to admit it's not that great. It has glaring issues. Sometimes the controls freak out (I play on mouse and keyboard) and I'm unable to attack with my mouse until I open my bag and close it. It *obviously* lacks polish in SO many ways. There are constant, minor graphical issues (even on max settings). The graphics are sometimes slightly worse or on par with GameCube graphics. I don't demand mind blowing graphics in 2024, but there's a certain standard you come to expect. Overall, the game looks visually similar to Legends Arceus, which people criticized upon release for the subpar graphical quality. Then, there's the sound. The music is pretty good overall and the reuse of some tracks like Blessia Island is nostalgic for me. But some of the music (mainly the ambient sounds like cicadas, RAIN, and birds) never seems to turn down. There is only 0 and 100 on the volume scale.I also have some nitpicks - mainly, I don't like how crops can be grown all year, and you can't unlock crops until you complete quests to do so. So you have a very limited selection of seeds until then. I'm used to crops being on a seasonal rotation, where they die out upon reaching the next season. I also am not a huge fan of the half-wolf characters, like Misagi and the pink-haired wolf girl (bleeps her name...). Misagi especially feels like a fetish or a trope character from anime. But at least she is more tolerable to speak to than pink-haired wolf girl, with the childish gnawing sounds. Additionally, I hate the festival directive stuff. What is the point of having festivals we have to unlock? I think it was introduced in possibly RF4 and, if so, I hated it then too. On that note, the festival grounds. It is just a plaza with no decorations or anything to make the location feel significant. I'm sure I will experience more nitpicks and probably come to agree with the fully negative reviews from RF fans as I come to complete the game.All in all, there's no two ways about it: nearly every aspect of this game feels rushed. In all honesty, my main goals are to get married to either Martin or Reinhard and finish the game. I am giving it a thumbs up because I can't leave a "mixed" or "neutral" or "meh" review. For Rune Factory fans like myself, the familiarity IS there. 20 hours in and having completed the first chapter, it hasn't been *so* terrible that I'd straight up not recommend it to Rune Factory fans. You genuinely have to temper your expectations going in. I knew this game had a bad reputation at least graphically and performance wise, but I decided to give it a shot. If anything, it's making me want to revisit all of the DS entries. I really, really hope the developers of the next Rune Factory (Guardians of Azuma) produce a solid entry after such a weak one.

_childDocuments_.review: God I should have listened to all the bad reviews, but I really wanted to place my faith in the good reviews. Tbh this isn't too bad of a game, it's actually pretty decent. But is it worth ~$50 CAD / ~$36 USD (assuming you aren't buying the deluxe version)? The answer is no. At least for me. If anyone buys this game, I would recommend getting it during a sale. Like those seasonal sales Steam has. Like seriously, save your money and get it at a discount. But anyways, let's get into the review.My Score: 6/10Pros:- Another Rune Factory Game to play while we wait for more Rune Factory!- Relaxing, lots of time to do lots of things- Same sex marriage (hooray alice x ludmilla)- Farming cycle is still the same and is very satisfying- Crafting is also the same and is very easy to use- Grinding for skill levels is also very easy and satisfying- Combat is okay, nothing too crazy (tho dodging has actually been made useful)- Mob/Boss farming is much easier now- Monster/Boss taming also feels much easier now- Decently sized open world (not too big, but also not too small)- Lots of save points (and auto saves)- Villagers hand out free stuff (that can be EXTREMELY helpful both early on and in end game)Neutral:- The days are too long. Lots of time is great, but sometimes you are just stuck waiting for certain nighttime events to happen. Other times, you are just done with your stuff for the day and want to go to the next day, but there is still lots of time left so you have to find SOMETHING to do. (Not that this is a bad thing. It gives you time to level up your skills and whatnot, but sometimes you just want to progress)- The difficulty level isn't too bad. I played blind on a hard run and was able to clear it just fine. If anything, I feel as though there were areas which were too easy (especially for a hard mode).- Missions are okay. I'm talking about the ones on the SEED board, and more specifically, the main missions that help you unlock cool things. These are okay. They are your standard missions. Sometimes it is a simple farming mission, and sometimes you are forced to gather 50 monsters and force them into your tiny barn. I do not have the money for this and the insurance I have is very small. Please give me mercy.Cons:- Let's get this out of the way: THE GRAPHICS ARE KINDA BAD. Yes the world looks pretty, and yes the character models look very nice and cool. But when you look more closely at things like the trees, you notice how bad these graphics are. No, I was not expecting Elden Ring graphics. But was I expecting Pokemon levels of bad? NO! I was not expecting the trees to look like those stand trees in theater plays. I was not expecting the large amount of clipping in the world, whether it be normal objects like the bushes sticking inside of nearby rocks to the character models clipping in their own body. - Also, while we're in the subject: THE CHARACTER MODELS ARE ALSO KINDA BAD. Like seriously. The slanted eyes on Simone's model look very weird, and Elsje's face looks too elongated. Also, some character models have eye colors that DON'T EVEN MATCH THEIR CHARACTER ART. Case in point: Ryker. His character art has him with brown eyes, yet his character model clearly has him with blue eyes. Is it the lighting??? Am I colorblind??? Or is this for real??!?!?!- More on design choice: the world is very empty. It feels kinda lonely. The town feels so desolate despite its rather large size. I wish that as we progressed through the game, more people would come and the town would become more populated. But nope. It remains large and empty. Additionally, when exploring the world, monsters only come out when you are near a gate. Which means for almost 75% of the time you are walking around, there is very little monsters (unless you are in a dungeon). Do I want more monsters? Maybe (I may be a masochist). I just want the world to feel a little more full and a little less lonely.- Controls are kinda wonky. They are easy to play with when you get used to them. However, I would not recommend using a controller. Just don't. The camera moves too slowly and the key bindings are a little funny. But once again, with enough time, one can get used to it and there shall be no more complaints.- The story really sucks. Like it seriously sucks. I spent half my time playing just waiting for something to happen (as you usually need to wait at least a day in between after seeing some cutscenes). Only after you get to the end does the game finally pick up the pace. The pacing is so slow that I tend to forget many important plot points. Not that you really need to know them since all that matters is what happens at the end. The characters did not move me, and  Basically, these characters are super boring to me - Town events are littered all over the town. Instead of being randomized, they are simply seen on the map on a certain area. By going to that area, you can activate the town event. At first, this sounds nice since you can choose to do some character events over others. But then, 20 million town events start popping up, and you get locked into very, very, VERY long cutscenes + series of cutscenes. There have been many times where I was just walking around town when suddenly, a cutscene descends on me and locks me in for a good couple of minutes. Like bruh, I just wanted to go buy some bread :(((( And if you complete the event in an area where ANOTHER event takes place, you get EVEN MORE CUTSCENES! Like gyattdamn I just want my bread ;((((((- Furniture placing is annoying. There are huge spaces between the furniture and the wall, and I cannot tell you just how many times I have thrown an item towards my chest, only for it to land in the space between it and the wall.- Combat can be very bad. More specifically, certain bosses are just VERY ANNOYING. They aren't hard and are 100% doable, but they are hella annoying. They will move quickly and will continuously stun lock you. Additionally, combat animations will extremely long and will lock you, so if you are in a bad position, you will DEFINITELY be getting stun locked.- You can't romance the hot charactersIn conclusion, if you don't look too deep into the game, it's pretty decent and actually fun! But if you're like me and just came back from playing Rune Factory 4, lower your expectations. This is no RF4. Sure, it may have some better quality of life aspects, but it doesn't have the characters, story, and soul of RF4. More importantly, you cannot romance the hot characters in this game.RIP Misasagi, I loved you

_childDocuments_.review: A great addition to the series. It's not perfect by any means though (NPC walking animations.... I'm looking at you). I think the hype of this game's release skewed some fans' expectations, as it is a niche market, and the companies who make these kinds of games aren't typically as affluent as other big game companies who make other kinds of games.  They also can't solo it and pour all their time/passion into it like what happened with Stardew Valley (which is a game I also love so no shade there). If you like the old Rune Factory games and/or Harvest moon games, you'll likely like this one. The graphics for this one look a little dated, but because it looks like an old PS2/Gamecube game, I have a soft spot for it, since it looks like some of the games that introduced me to the genre in the first place.I'd give it a 7.5/10 overall. Cool characters, nice vibrant cell-shaded aesthetic, laid-back farming, an okay story to keep you occupied, a variety of monsters to tame, and game performance is great on my PC (with some minor bugs but nothing game-breaking). I'm having a great time with it, so hopefully, this one sells well enough for us to see a Rune Factory 6 one day.

_childDocuments_.review: For those new to the series Rune Factory is a farming sim in the same vein as Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, and Stardew Valley, however what differentiates it is that its a complete RPG as well.  An in-depth crafting system combines these two elements and you wind up with just a tremendous amount of game.  In an era where games frequently feel incomplete and ask you to pay for DLC to get a finished product this game feels like you're getting two or three games for the price of one.It's a great franchise, but they really outdid themselves with this one.  I bought it on Switch and found the story so compelling I rushed through the dungeons pretty quickly without doing a lot of farming.  There were a few times that became a problem, but there's really no need to rush.  The Switch version is fine, but for as many hours as I was putting into it the load screens were slow and this version on PC is noticeably better.I've bought the game twice now and it's been worth every penny.  If you own a Steam Deck I've been playing this on it with no problems.  I highly recommend this game.  It's fun, it's filled with deep, complicated systems to learn, and the different weapon types bring a lot of variety to combat.

It feels like whoever made those characters understood what was attractive and didn't realize they kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ with my interest in other characters. Also, purple wolf man needs less purple or something. Any other color and maybe I would boink.  The fighting feels...Easier? For the most part, most the weapons feel like you are pressing the same button and dashing sometimes from attacks. Another problem is that the game rewards you with far too many health options so even if you got hit, you always can eat a whole cake in one bite and keep walking. I almost want to up the challenge factor at the start and middle ground with more attack patterns and health, because once you've reached the conclusion there is so much roughness it feels like the game woke up in such a strange way. Consistency is all I ask. If it is hard mode, make it feel like I am suffering the whole way through and don't surprise me with monsters that feel like I wasn't prepared to handle to begin with. Managing the field a bit more closely than just plotting land down. There is levels to this and I think that is fun. I wish there was a better way to integrate all three aspects for farming, fighting and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It feels like if you really wanted to, you can wave your hand to it which I think is both bad and good. I think all aspect of the game should be played to extend your gameplay and make the asking price well, worth it.Graphics aren't the best, but Idc about graphics too much as long as the gameplay is fun. Feel like they needed to figure that part out for their next installment because it feels like they didn't add anything to rf5 that rf4 didn't do. And honestly, rf4 is more challenging than rf5 combat wise and scaling when you play on hardmode.I love the gamed despite all this. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, on the scale from 1 to 10, I would rate it a solid 7. Here's why:1. Storyline: I'm really sorry to say this but it's a cringe worthy. I have no problem being the 'good' character or the 'mainstream heroic' plot, but this series is taking too far. It feels like I'm the saint and everyone is waiting for their savior (aka me) while doing nothing. It just doesn't pull your heartstrings like RF 4 does. I still remember how I'm crying over Ventuswill, Volkanon, Leon, Doug, Xiaopai in RF 4 and genuinely eager to know what happens next. But in RF 5 I don't feel anything, even satisfaction when I beat this game.2. The characters' designs are amazing, but their daily dialogues and cutscenes feel awkward to watch. Most of the conversations are repeated dialogues from Day 1, so I personally do not feel any motivation to max out their heart (although most of the villagers are at 8-9 hearts in my game, at some point I just stop trying). I was hoping that I unlock more dialogues by getting closer to them but turns out it doesn't work that way.3. The protagonist (our character) has no character. We don't get to choose our path, mostly it's 'choosing your dialogue' at the first part of the story, but the dialogue's choices are pretty much the same. Lol. The protagonist is too kind to be true, your typical knight in shining armor (although to argue every RF's protagonist feel that way, BUT this protagonist is too much of goody two shoes (especially toward the end of the story). I cringed a little. Sorry.4. The combat SUCKS. Take this from the person who play Persona 4 & RF 4 at easy mode. I played RF5 in hard mode, and I still overpowered the last boss and win it in less then 2 minutes I guess. Even the hard mode is too easy for me who dies in Stardew Valley's mines. There is no reason to forge a new weapon or preparing food before you defeat the boss. 5. The boss fight is really disappointing, sometimes when the boss is charging up attack or doing some pose idk, my attack can't go through it. So I'll just have to wait for the boss to finish their business, then attack. It is very awkward.6. There are too many dungeons, but not one of them is a good one. If I have to rate it, I will probably give it a 5. Hear me out, I love their designs but all of the dungeons pretty much are the same. They're just using the same template and recycling it with more leveled monsters and new bosses.7. The art is good. I'm not a big fan of 3D games but I enjoy this graphic. The only complaint is the world is really big but it doesn't look like it's finished at all. Not a deal breaker for me though.8. Fishing! Love the fishing mechanic, it's simple and relaxing, plus it makes me feel nostalgic to previous RF series.9. Farming/Taming/Quest - Love it, no complaint.I still see myself getting back to the game to do some romance w/ the townsfolk and completing some quests. It's a good game, but with flaws here and there. I still recommend this game to people with some notes to consider.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good solid entrance for rune factory. I only have a few nit picky problems. The story and pacing are garbage. And by the time you get to endgame, you'll get into more high tier crafting but it utterly destorys the balance. My character is about level 200~, and I used the extra directives to increase the levels of the enemies to the point that the end game dungeon has about lvl 800 enemies. They don't do damage to me but now require a decent amount of swings to kill. So it kinda makes the ultimate crafts and ultimate tier upgrading as completely useless. There's no point to it.And then the pacing of the story is far too quick with a rather simple and unforfilling story that doesn't even answer everything. And unless you pace yourself and make the dungeons and story a backburner effort, you will certainly find yourself finishing the game before you can even date someone. I put in about 180 hours according to steam and I havn't gotten to year 2 even. I have finished the game, utterly destroyed the postgame dungeon, maxed out forging, crafting, cooking, and chemistry to 99. And I finally got married after grinding that out. Now, the romantic option I went with was the last one to be introduced so it was going to take longer but I pretty much got everything out of this game to a satisfactory point and I still havn't gotten children yet. So that is my complaint with pacing, in that friendships and romance/marriage is really long to do and I had plowed through everyone thing easily in the meantime.And it really does suck that the game makes your 'home' the second floor bunking area of SEED. You get to expand it and all but you can't move the beds and its just so restricting. The placement of furniture is HORRIBLE. (Thankfully, there are mods on the PC that can fix this for you).But I do recommend this game so let's talk about the good. It's rune factory. The farming is good. It's awesome to figure out cash crops and go out and adventure for items to upgrade your gear with. You will work on leveling up your crops so you can make more money. And then when you get farm dungeons you can use the crystals to get more space to farm and even raise the quality of crops, health of the soil, etc. Capture monsters, befriend them, get their products while they help you water and harvest the crops on the farm. Level them up if you want adventuring buddies.Leveling up your skills rewards you with better gear and better ways to upgrade stuff. If you ever have an issue or a problem with an aspect, you can always upgrade your gear to deal with it. And even cook food that'll give you a buff to deal with it. Chemistry basically superpowers your farm once you learn how to craft chemicals and revitalize and keep your farm and crops healthy.The characters are interesting. Though I feel a good number of the male romance options are boring, imo. (Maybe cause I'm a guy. Eh.) The town and character events are interesting and provide alot of character and depth to most of the characters.It's a good game besides the nitpicky problems with the game's pacing and story, it's a solid entry. and certainly worth the 60$ for the 180 hours I spent on it.
