_childDocuments_.review: RF1 < RF2 < RF3 < RF5 < RF4+++ Romance & FamiliesRF5 seems to have to date the most content when it comes to the post marriage life, even giving you the option to have multiple children. Also the marriage candidates are on par with RF4 if not better, and definitely better than in RF3 (as in for the waifus, I didn't play husbando content). Ludmila is the best girl.+ Monster tamingYou can still tame most monsters, but unlike in RF4, half of the bosses are locked out, which is a bummer.+ Town/Random eventsThese are both better and worse than in RF4. They are better, because they aren't REALLY random, so you don't need to curse the RNG gods for not giving you the required waifu events. They are also worse, as in there are a LOT fewer of them.+ CombatThis has the best combat of any RF game. The enemy variety clearly isn't what it used to be in RF4, since that game had the benefit of reusing all the enemies from previous entries, and the difficulty is a bit too much on the easy side, but that's also because the game is relatively short, so the curve would need to be incredibly steep. I do give props having the ability to both increasing the party size from 2 + player to 3, and still being able to fully equip your party.+ CraftingIt's the same as in RF4, with all the ability to combine 4 item special abilities into 1 item, with all the hidden rarity values and whatnot. What they changed, is that rare cans actually work now when crafted into a weapon.+/- FarmingFarming has been further given options from RF4 to streamline certain aspects, and the farm dragons give more than enough space to grow everything. That being said, there is very little incentive to keep power-farming like in RF4, because the end game does not require any investing in gear, and the Rigbarth Maze is but a pale shadow of the Sharance maze in both RF4 and RF3. Also it's really dumb that the clearly elemental themed dragons, are not even seasonal. The literal fire dragon of molten lava is NOT a summer field, it's just regular, like every other field.+/- "Date festivals"There isn't enough of them, but what is there is good. Also things like new years eve etc. don't get any special treatment unlike in RF4. But at least you can see the fireworks now, since RF5 has an actual skybox.+/- FestivalsHonestly, I've never cared about any of the festival in any of the RF games. At least they aren't as disturbing as in RF1, where every single person is mental about the festival subjects, as if it was N.Korea, and the dear leader forced them to be bonkers about milks or eggs. Anyway they are "fine", as in do them once and win, and then disable them. Except buddy battle, that is the ONLY actually fun and proper festival, and a must to do every time!- Marriage lockYou can't marry until you finish the main quest. I assume this was done to avoid the need to write alternative lines to reflect relationship status in cut scenes and whatever, but still REALLY dumb. I mean heck, RF4 even has child dialogue prompts, for the 1st dungeon (if you have your child/wife/husband with you)!- The WorldIt's... really empty. Like super Mario 64 -empty, as if the switch could not handle all "teh polygons". Though, it could also be, that the game was actually badly optimized, because it does sometimes slow down, at least on switch. It's still bigger than the world of RF3, but it's nowhere near as big as RF4. Also places like the Belpha Ruins, and Calamity's Edge REALLY seemed like there was supposed to so much more to them.- Housing & FurnitureThe housing "options" are bleak, having to live in the attic of the Seed office is really dumb (as in after you get married etc). Also you have enormous amount of empty space, which you can't really do or fill with anything, since the furniture are static, you can't even sit on them, and there is a hard limit how many you can even have. Also you sleep in the entry hallway of your house, like bum. Props for being able to at least change the wallpaper and floors.-- LengthLike RF3, this is relatively short game, but still not as short as RF3. You really are left feeling like there should be more.-- Final Boss--- DeathThey still can't admit that cleaving someone in half, and when they even leave their blood and skull behind, that they were harmed or killed, but just "sent back home". If there is anyone who lives with death as everyday part of their lives, it's farmers.---- Biggest sinYou can't marry Radea.--- Furniture placementIt sucks REALLY bad. You can't put anything next to anything else, or a wall. At least you can use mods on the PC version to fix this, but still, bad work.The game is good, but feels a bit unfinished, like they ran out of time, and had to cut out a LOT of content. What is there is good, but you can't shake the feeling, like there was suppose to be a lot more. What game needed is more content and more polish, and personally, I would have bought content DLCs if the game had any.Looking forward to RF 6 and the "Project Dragon".

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game screamed "baby's first RPG". In the 2 hours I played it felt incredibly elementary in how it handled everything. About the only think I was impressed with, and what made me think the game had quality, was the short animated clips. However, most of those last seconds. The fighting felt clunky, even using a controller. The fighting was also elementary. Just watch the game play trailer and see how easy the enemies are, and how much a none threat they are. It's quite odd in very beginning you are shown how to fight 2 mobs which never touch you, but then afterwards you are so beat up you pass out for story. The fighting is a joke and only there so they can say it is there. The farming and crafting, what little I did in the refund window, also felt elementary and grindy. I wasn't even sure why I would need any of this stuff, as crafting new weapons seemed unimportant as mobs were jokes, even on hard setting. Also I found the furniture placement incredibly annoying as it was very hard to get the items in the position you wanted. So, I didn't think I would make much furniture either. The relationships, which I see many weirdos talk about, are pretty lame. Even in 2 hours, the main 2 "partners" I first met had already gone to 25% of the relationship bar and I hadn't even done anything yet. On top of that, all the characters are clearly young teens 13-15, even for anime style. So the idea that you can marry one is just stupid, and not just because of western ideals of age, but because these kids need to go out and live some life before getting tied down. It is ridiculous so many people put so much emphasis on this part of the game when you can go get plenty of visual novel games if you just want to fantasize about two boys kissing, or better yet just go play Stardew Valley which is actually a good game. In the end, they should have just skipped the relationship stuff and focused on making a better game.So, I wouldn't recommend you buy this game unless you are a very casual gamer who wants no challenge. _childDocuments_.review: Rune Factory has been one of my all time favorites from the geniuses behind the Bokujo Monogatari series. I love the mechanics of farming and the mixture of RPG that makes this titles so emblematic.My favorite out of all of them has always been the second game, but the fifth one might just make me change my favoritism.Although the game lives up to expectations, there are still a few things that could be said it lacks or has issues with, so lets break it down on how I felt the pros and cons from my own perspective.PROS-Cute visuals and nice athmosphere.-Voiced! Even the MCs talk!-Great VAs <3 I was astonished by the number of great seiyus involved in the project.-Battle mechanics are easy to understand and slightly similar to RF4.-World building is excellent, despite having the recurring themes repeat, it still feels fresh.-Story is solid, anyone who has a visual novel and Otome/Dating SIM obsession will enjoy it as well.-The music is beautiful.-Characters feel even more dynamic than in previous installment, probably because of the Voice Acting being more involved.CONS-Has a few bugs (Charcter slides a lot when running and holding onto an object)-Music sometimes randomly stops playing outside buldings.-Event navigation is a bit tricky to traverse, sometimes you might pick up on a event bubble by accident from a character you are not interested in at the moment, and the game locks the event so you can't pick a new one until the active one if finished. So you might want to save before going for one.-For a 3D game, the lack of proper texture redering sometimes really bothers me. There is a moment when the shadows are cast from a specific angle, the characters and monsters get this weird greyed out, kinda similar to manga greytones textures that seem to move on its own even when standing still.---------------------------------And thats about it. The game is still a true master piece tho, I would recommend it to anyone who likes Story of Seasons and RPG games.
_childDocuments_.name: Rune Factory 5

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a very addictive, but very flawed game. Most of the flaws are obvious, the PS3-era graphics, the stuttering that occurs despite having a PC that should be able to wipe the floor with this game. The combat is generally absolutely terrible.Despite that and many other things. The game is very addictive. Leveling up crops, buying recipe bread, putting together ingredients to craft something new. The story is surprisingly decent. The characters are too. Once I got into the game, it was amusing to run into townspeople while I went about my business. You can also get the townspeople to join your battle party. Oh and you can tame most monsters in the game. And you can get them to work on your farm if you get bored of farming. There's a couple of drawbacks to most things like that, such as losing out on statistic bonuses by having monsters harvest for you.Ultimately though the end-game grind is just too grindy for me. Upgrades cost thousands of lumber. Weapon and armor crafting require items that are often found in an area where my existing weapons don't damage the enemies. So there's a chicken and the egg scenario. Also, for some of the other crafting materials that I need, the only way to really know where to get them is to look up a guide online. As one could fight the same enemy numerous times and then realize that there's a 10% chance that you can lock them up with an ability and steal the item.I am very interested in what they do for the sequel to this game. There's a ton of potential in making a 100 hour game that can be replayed (ie the game is more or less 100% completed after 100 hours). I think what we got was a grindy 300+ hour game that gets too grindy for its own good in the end-game. I played the first two acts of Rune Factory 4 Special ( I saw the credits roll ) and I think that this series tends to make the end-game too grindy. But before it gets grindy, it's an incredibly addictive formula.In my opinion, the game should not have so much of a grind as part of the addictive quality is the rapid advancement of getting more money, getting more crops, weapons, armor etc. Once that slows to a crawl the spell that the game had on me is broken. At the end-game it's hard to justify the hours spent to reveal the next very generic looking level of a very generic looking dungeon. The payoff for the grind isn't there. Leveling up crops becomes tedious. Leveling up the fridge to hold your crops becomes tedious. Looking up guides to figure out where the crafting items are that I need to become viable in the next level of the end-game dungeon becomes tedious. The menus get a bit tedious (ie. when trying to grind crafting levels).It was worth it on sale but after the credits roll, feel free to spend about ten more hours then be ready to walk away as the game just will go on forever with a trickle-feed of content. In other words there's no good reason to spend that much time with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rune Factory 5

_childDocuments_.review: As with all rune factory games, there is always a shocking amount of playtime if you really, really want it. For me, it's always worth playing, the cast is endearing, the story is cute, and I don't regret playing it. You really do see some endearing sides to the characters and I've always been satisfied with the farming and crafting aspects of RF. As a fan of the series, this one feels like you hit a wall a lot more suddenly than the previous games in the series. It really slows to a crawl once you beat the story. The RNG can just make things a total drag. It took two weeks in-game to find a certain tree seed. Yeah, maybe you could save scum and reload over and over and over and over and try and brute force it within a few hours-- this is a mentality that comes up a LOT in rune factory games due to certain abysmal RNG chances on a number of things-- but is that really a game at that point lol? Is that a fun and rewarding player experience? Then, that seed takes 50 days to sprout, which is like half an in-game year, and there isn't enough to do in a day to really pass that time honestly. Monster-wise, it took no less than 213 beetles to die to get Dangerous Scissors, even with drop rate boosts, and that just doesn't seem reasonable lmao. I guess what I'm saying is, it's fun for a while, and then it very suddenly is a chore.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having the requirements of a game from late 2016 while barely looking like a product from 2006, i think it is still worth it... AT A DISCOUNT!If you can grab it for 20$ to 25$, go for it, just make sure you surpass the recommended requirements, Japanese PC ports tend to be really bad on average.Outside of the system requirements and the terrible launch it had on Switch (it still is terrible), i don't have many complaints for this game, as a Rune Factory entry at any rate.If you do not know what Rune Factory is, well i can best summarise it as an Action style Sandbox Adventure in a Fantasy setting with RPG and farming elements (refer to games like Stardew Valley for the farming element part).Every game in the series has a Campaign/Main Story that you can do, but you will most likely play it for the game's Sandbox nature, especially since this is not something like Minecraft where you are just placed into a world, given a bunch of tools and are basically told, make your own fun if you can. You have to see it for yourself to understand, which can be done through Youtube or any other video hosting website.For the people familiar with Rune Factory, in simple words, it is a flawed full 3D version of Rune Factory 4, but with different cast of characters and locations, obviously.It has every system 4 did and a few very welcome quality of life improvements such as:1) Being able to access all of your storage containers from 1 place, even from the crafting stations or shipping bin;2) Multiple fast travel points, every farm has a warp point, also every dungeon;3) Easy early tamable Boss Mount that is really fast;4) Being able to have multiple Shipping Bins, so no more harvests ferrying.There might have been more but at the time of writing this, they might  have slipped my mind.For completion sake, i will list a couple of complaints i have with this entry of RF.First, I wish we didn't get forced into every characters's event, without consent mind you. Some people (majority, i know shocker) are straight, and while we, the players, may not take the interactions seriously, having every character be a love interest and being given no choice to to just befriend same sex characters is quite disgusting.Most characters may be just a stereotype with some twists, but not being able to say no to them, while also keeping their relationship high is damaging to whatever personality they may have.I know this system was tacked on just for the west release, but honestly, even if it was built from the ground up with this interaction in mind, it would still not fit well with this kind of game.Second and final complaint, the enemy AI. They seem to have been scaled down quite a bit. They are half as aggressive and as active as they were in 4, some seem to have lost certain moves they used to do or even spam.Some enemy AI can't seem to understand the difference between heights, for instance, if you are inside the south-east cave in Rigbarth Woodlands, the monster above the cave, on the hill, will start swinging/flinging spells at nothing.As a side note for this observation, Ally AI does seem to understand height, after all, they can follow you up and down every flight of stairs just fine so it may have something to do with the limited amount of space enemy AI is allowed to move away from their spawn point, which would limit their pathfinding range which would be the cause that makes them look so dumb when they can't figure out how to reach you.This has been a rather long review, hope it helps some newcomers and long-time fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Rune Factory 5 is much the same as earlier entries in the series but while some things have improved many others seem unfinished or downright overlooked.- Automatic pickups for loot but it doesn't include faster harvesting of crops- Less screen transitions with a larger world but much of it is empty and unused- No seasonal fields even though several of them should have been (located in hot or cold climates)- Longer days so you have time more time to explore or farm but story seem short (easily completed by first summer)- Upgraded tools aren't faster and AoE charging isn't very useful (only improvement I've noticed is better and more numerous drops) but stumps and rocks spawn MUCH faster around your fields.- New catch skill that can be used to get more drops but drop chances seem VERY low (I spent half an hour trying to farm one resource but only got a single drop, feels like it's in the 0.0X% range even with luck upgraded gear)- Shop schedules aren't properly tuned, some services aren't available during open hours while others have many attendants available. Example: only one NPC at the bath but bakery and general store has three.Still gets a positive recommendation from me but it's with many caveats, Rune Factory 5 could have been MUCH better with just a bit more polish but sadly it seems to have been shipped and abandoned before it was finished.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on release for Switch, and stopped playing after 4 hours because the graphical stuttering and lag were so terrible. I decided to wait for it to port over to PC, and then wait further for a sale before trying it out again. Having accomplished that, though... I still feel very lukewarm about the game. It's not  but it's not great.One thing the game has going for it is the gameplay loop; it is still fun and it scratches the itch of farming, animal raising and socialisation. And though it is laughably easy, the combat is something I honestly enjoy; there's lots of variety in weapons, so it's easy to find something to fit your play style. I also like the cast of characters overall, though I would say I preferred the cast of RF4 as an ensemble. They do have a character to fit every trope you'd expect in a game of this genre, but that's not a bad thing; they're honestly all quite endearing in their own way, and there aren't any whom I actively dislike. Speaking of the characters, one thing RF5's leap to 3D has done is provided us with some really nice looking character sprites. Though I've got criticisms about the game's environment and overall performance, the characters themselves look very good. Now, on to criticisms: technically, the game performs  better than it did on the Switch, but I'm still flabbergasted that there are still occasional frame drops and skips in places. These shouldn't be happening on a 3D game that looks like RF5 does, because nothing about what I see on screen indicates any graphical stress. Frankly, RF5 still looks quite barren in the overworld: even with graphical settings turned up to maximum. The splotches of green and brown that make up the distant terrain remind me of a 3D game from the early 2000s, and not something I'd expect to see in a main-line title released in 2022. And if there were any hopes that having the power of a PC would fill in the gaps, unfortunately it doesn't. At maximum draw distance for objects, blades of grass still only 'appear' when your character is within 1 to 2 meters of where they should be.I regularly play much more GPU and CPU-intensive games with zero loss in fidelity, frame skips, etc - but RF5 seems to just randomly struggle. I can only presume this is down to a lack of optimisation in the game itself: perhaps a failing of this being Marvelous's first 3D Rune Factory game, which is such a shame. I would predict that the future RF games will stay 3D, but if they do, graphics optimisation and performance needs to be a point of focus. So, do I like RF5? Overall, I'd say so - but I'd go into it eyes wide open that there are likely other life-sim/farm sim games out there that look and perform much better. It does still give a good Rune Factory experience, but the leap to 3D hasn't been perfect. I'd recommend it, but only if you can get it on a deep discount (50% off or more).

_childDocuments_.review: A conditional recommendation, more like a thumbs in-between than up or down.It is a farming sim with a bunch of anime tropes thrown at the wall to see what sticks.Soundtrack feels like an afterthought. Visuals in the town and farm feel thrown together at the last minute. A lot of the village feels lifeless or tacked on. So much is just flat, lifeless textures.There's nothing unique here, in the town, the actual MEAT of the game that's meant to last. A few lines of dialogue from any of the characters, and you'll immediately clock which anime cloning facility they came out of.The most well-rounded content would be the dungeons. They're fleshed out a lot more, visually, and the soundtrack has some life to it, but they're so easy. By the time you actually have to try in combat, you've already snored your way through half of the story.Half of the story, which you can complete in the first month.I wasn't even rushing. The days are pretty long for a farming sim. Tended the farm, planted my crops, brushed the animals, talked to most of the villagers and it wasn't even the afternoon.I got it on sale for $20. I wouldn't pay a dime more than this, and would only get it if you're starved for farming content. The only reason I'd recommend this is, its nostalgic, it feels like a DS game.Its comfort food, but cheap comfort food. Like the McDonalds of farming sims. Its nothing special, and you've had it before, but it gets the job done.

_childDocuments_.review: I had never played a rune factory game before this one; it seems like the titles are stand-alone, each one having a different story and characters but having similar features to the gameplay. Rune Factory 5 has elements of a farming sim, with the main focus being on developing your town and character. The farming itself is relatively minor, although you can choose to focus on it if you wish. There are a few quality of life features that I have never seen in a farming sim type game before, such as bringing townspeople to adventure with you or taming monsters, and these features along with the enjoyable character interactions have made this one of my favorite casual games to play. There are some features to the controls of the game which may be frustrating, such as having to press a sequence of controls in order to switch between more than 2 weapons, but if the sometimes clunky UI doesn't interfere with your game experience too much I would highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the franchise since RF3 and really enjoyed it, so much that I can't return to Farm / Date Sims without RPG elements (like classic Harvest Moon). But well, let's talk about Rune Factory 5:TL; DR: Good game, shorter than RF4, but worth it if you already finished RF4 5 times (like I already did in 3DS)PROS:- Holding X to gather stuff is a really good quality of life upgrade- Each game day is longer than RF4- Combat progression is more clean (no more need to get 100% critical strike to bypass high defenses)- Combat is less punitive (very few hit kill mechanics)- Cool boss fights- Farming crystals are a really good addition- Fishing now spawns fish constantly- The whole awesome crafting and farming mechanics from RF4 are back here- Town and romance events aren't RNG- You can reset RNG seeds (like shops rotating stock) by reloading your save- You can marry Scarlett, Ludmilla or BeatriceMIXED- Game is more casual (easier enemies, doesn't even need a late game item to reduce all damage to 0, even from post-game dungeon)- Co-op fishing / forging / cooking can only be done 1 time per day, with a chance that no one will join you- Co-op fishing has exclusive fish that you can't find elsewhere- New enemies, but some classic enemies are missing (like turtles, flying birds, and scorpions)- Can't fight most bosses from older games- Weapons balance (dual blades, my favorite, had their ultimate attack nerfed)- The "random item shop' rotating stock" can sell even items you hadn't dropped and shipped yet, like post-game dungeon enemies dropsCONS- Shorter game than RF4- Fewer town and romance events than RF4- No RNG post-game dungeon- Some really hard drop rates (like 0.2% from a boss that you can only kill once a day)- You can't marry Elsje, Simone or Misasagi

_childDocuments_.review: Almost a year I've waited for a sale and I finally bought the deluxe version at 40% off this Spring Sale. At launch this game was more expensive than Elden Ring Deluxe in my region.Anyways, the game runs great on PC. I'm glad that I didn't buy a Switch just for this game. I'm not a die hard Rune Factory fan  and it's been a while since I played RF4 that I mostly forgotten what was missing in the franchise. I'm just satisfied with the upgrade in graphics and added anime cut scenes. Combat is shallow but I treat this as a chillax game so it's a given.Mechanics and new NPCs are slowly being introduced to have a beginner friendly experience. I haven't delved much into the game so I don't have much to comment on.I'm playing this game with audio and language set in Japanese. The text is very readable and it's suitable to intermediate learners. Though, your vocabulary will be tested because some characters will only have their speech written in kana while some really use complicated or very casual words.So far I'm satisfied and I would recommend this game to anyone who's new to the series and those who want to have fun while studying Japanese. It's a rewarding experience to pass the in game licence exam in 100% Japanese! 頑張れ！=============================UPDATE==================================Finally beaten the game at almost 60 hours! Story is JRPG-ish so kinda tropey and not so complex which is fine since I'm also playing the game to expand my Japanese vocabulary. As a game and a study material, this game satisfied both.The weapon crafting system feels overwhelming and convoluted. I've seen some Youtube videos teaching how to game the system and get a higher level crafting skill. There's also an RNG element to crafting so I guess crafting is for those who want to explore the dungeons past the credits roll.Anyways, I have a marriage to look forward to (Ludmila best girl!) and at least I can also improve my gear and take on more difficult dungeons.=============================UPDATE II=================================Finally married best girl. ルドミラ最高!If only I knew that the events for some characters only occur at night, I could've married Ludmila sooner. I kept asking her out but for some reason she can't after three dates. I just wasn't aware that I had to finish Luca's quest by waiting until 7 pm! During my time of ignorance I just afk'ed while having her at my party just to level up her relationship level from 9 to 10 (and that's after showering her gifts). Anyways, lesson learned. Kinda annoying that I cannot play the game without looking up guides.Speaking of guides, some forging combinations are so unintuitive that using guides are unavoidable. Also, I had to mass produce failed high RP products just to level up the forging skill instead of naturally progressing as needed.By the time I've finished the post game dungeon, there's nothing else to look forward to except marriage, kids, and more farming. I wish the story is long enough so that you can marry before finishing it or, marriage progression is fast enough that you can get married in a less grindy pace. Why can I tandem cook, forge, fish with my team mates? If only there was a dating sim element like those from Thousand Arms maybe the dating mechanic would be more interactive and enjoyable. The technology is already in game and is so easy to implement that they only need decent writers to implement such system.Despite the somewhat lacking content, reaching the 100 hour mark and more for a single player game is not bad content wise. There's replayability in marrying the other candidates though I wish some NPC's can be married. It's been awhile since I've married someone in a farming sim game so I attest that to how great their design for Ludmila is (aesthetic, personality, and personal background).It was a nice journey but now I have to move onto my other pending games.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get this part out of the way: 7/10Now let me go over why.Decent game, plenty of fun to be found, not well balanced. If you want Stardew Valley, but with way more anime you might enjoy this. It isn't as good as Stardew, but it isn't bad either. I was able to beat the main story line before the end of summer. I wasn't even rushing it. The biggest complaint I have is with the voice acting. The acting itself is fine, but its inconsistency is the problem. In one story line conversation it is possible to have fully voiced text boxes, unvoiced text boxes, and generic character responses. I would prefer it to be more VO or less, but this strange middle ground means you might skip past a box because you read it faster than the character was talking just to find out they aren't only voicing the first sentence, then you stop to let them say the next box only to have them say only the first of the three sentences. Other VO problems I ran into was at the end (no spoiler, don't worry) the boxes were unvoiced, but the scene had to its course before the next box would display meaning I would be sitting and waiting for 30 seconds while the camera pans and a five word texts box stills their awkwardly.I finished the game in late summer (the second of four seasons) with 3 characters 7/10 or greater in affection and most of the rest at 5 or 6/10. Went to bed at 6 pm nearly every night unless an event asked me to stay up later. I only struggled during Calamity's End, the last dungeon in the game that consists of two maps: a single straight path and the boss arena. Before this point a few "death" or "black" type monster appear with can one shot you out of nowhere. I built up as much dark resistance as I could to help mitigate that, but it didn't help. Checked online to find out the attack that looks like pure darkness that was killing me was considered a "faint" attack and NOT dark. Little tip for those who read this far: the game won't let you take humanoid allies, but you CAN take monster allies. Take them and let them get targeted with the one-shot kill effects.Something I saw as a positive was when even the protagonist called out some of the silly tropes (didn't happen often). One such example happens really early in the game. Your character has amnesia and is welcomed to the town with open arms. Tropey, but fine. Later two of the characters you met after you wake up are trying to figure out who should work where and they ask you because you're there. Your character suggests they aren't the right person to ask since you're new to town and have no idea about who would be the best fit for jobs. Both characters basically say, "doesn't matter what you pick we'll go with it." You pick, the go along with it, and you stand there confused. In short, it's fun. I wouldn't say it is going to change the world but it also never made that claim. If you want Stardew Valley with a silly anime story that is more action-adventure with farming as an after thought then you might like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Rune Factory 5 is the best game of its kind. I initially purchased the game for Nintendo Switch, but was disappointed with the low frame rates of 15-25 fps. However, I was pleased to find that the PC version runs smoothly and provides a more enjoyable experience.Not only does Rune Factory 5 boast impressive performance on PC, but it's also a joy to play. The game's charming storyline and engaging gameplay mechanics keep players coming back for more. The graphics are colorful and beautifully rendered, adding to the overall immersive experience.Beyond its technical and visual features, Rune Factory 5 is also notable for its inclusive relationship options. It's the first game in the franchise to offer same-sex relationships, a progressive step forward in video game representation.One of the standout features of Rune Factory 5 is the ability to form relationships with the various characters in the game. Whether you're courting a potential love interest or bonding with a trusted ally, the interactions feel meaningful and contribute to the overall narrative.Overall, Rune Factory 5 is a must-play game for fans of the series and newcomers alike. The PC version offers smooth performance and a more enjoyable experience than its Nintendo Switch counterpart, and the inclusive relationship options make it a great choice for anyone looking for a fun and immersive gaming experience.

I love a company that will go above and beyond for the fans in that way.I also think the combat is the perfect blend for all players. It is fun and interesting enough for people who like combat, but it's also simple and accessible enough for those who are there for the life aspects of it.There's also a lot of wonderful quality of life stuff in the game to make tasks less tedious but not so automated that it begins to feel pointless. Relationships and skills have a lower cap for accessibility to important unlocks, but then they also have extreme upper levels with rare unlocks and for you to have visual progression (you can get married at like 10 hearts with a person, but I think you can max hearts at like 100?? 10000 I've seen from some people online???? 57 hearts with Martin, and going strong <3). I like knowing that maybe the recipes cap out at 100 cooking skill, but I still can see wow I've reached 175 I've done so much!Overall, it's an amazing game and my favorite farming simulator game since Stardew Valley and the incredibly old Harvest Moon: It's a Wonderful Life (P.S., Rune Factory has some of the original people from the old Harvest Moon team, this is the best successor franchise!)

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, I do recommend RF5 with a couple of asterisks attached. On the one hand, RF4 has a better cast and more content, for 20$ less. On the other hand, I don't have to use mods to marry a girl as a girl. If you're new to the harvest sim genre, you should pick up Stardew Valley first and see if the genre is right for you. If you're new to the Rune Factory series, you should pick up 4 first and see if you like it. If you're a bit of a graphics or challenge snob, maybe check out Serin Fate instead. However, in between Rune Factory 4 and 5, the original publishing company of the Rune Factory series, Neverland, went bankrupt in 2013. I wouldn't be surprised if in the move to XSEED/Marvelous some corners had to be cut in order to get a new game out in time with the new generation. Keeping this in mind, on a decent PC it runs better than on the Switch. If you're thirsting for an all-star voice acting cast with a cliche, but heartfelt story, and some of the best character design seen in a modern JRPG, look no further. There might not be any non-binary option without mods, but if you were turned off by the overly femme models of Harvestella's male-leaning characters, Ares is masc enough to scratch that itch. It's got cute farm dragons, and a wide array of cute monsters to tame and raise on your farm. There's also a werefox bachelor, a literal god bachelor, a werewolf bachelorette, and a succubus bachelorette if you have certain interests. You can also have someone else ride with you on certain monsters, so you can ride a blue-nine tailed fox into the sunset with your favorite villager if you want. Despite its flaws, Rune Factory 5 is a gem of a game, and you should consider checking it out if you've been around the farming sim block a bit and need something familiar, but also new.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game, ruined by far too much bad RNG. Rune factory 5 is the story of game that's fun to play for the base storyline, romance elements, etc. that quickly gets ruined if you try to enjoy the post-game in any meaningful way. With a drop rate of Sub-1% on some items that can't even be obtained outside of limited-time bosses, or worst yet a rather unengaging and extremely boring fishing minigame, the game shines the most when you're enjoying it early on but fails when you want to keep enjoying it after a certain point. Play it once for the story, your chosen romance partner/s, and some fun farming elements. But beyond that, I'd recommend shelfing it in favor of something else. The game heavily encourages SaveScumming as a work around for some real bad RNG elements, such as saving before a boss - reloading - killing the boss again to get your desired drops or; likewise the Heinz exploit is one that is commonly-encouraged in order to try and get end-game crafting items in a reasonable amount of time (Even though that, in and of itself, can take hours-on-end.) Even with a group full of characters with Rare Cans, Clovers, and max-luck accessories, the drop rate on some bosses only goes up to 30% - whcih means you can kill them for in-game weeks+ at a time without ever actually seeing the desired drop. Aside from that, there are some rough crashing issues (I went the entire first year with 0 crashes, then the game just seems to have taken a dip since; bit frustrating but could also be hardware - though I've read I'm not the only one with this issue.) The characters range from interesting, to infuriatingly generic/underdeveloped. The story is pretty nonsensicle but serves well enough to move the plot forward. Really nothing revolutionary, it's your typical JRPG plot and it'll work to get you to the end. The level of character depth is MASSIVE but that's a double edged sword, since as I said... if you REALLY get into it, you will find the hell that is the end-game RNG system buries a lot of your desire to advance your characters/family.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick take - If you're looking for a Harvest Moon + fantasy rpg hybrid, take a closer look at this one. Rune Factory is a solid attempt to create a Farming sim + fantasy adventure hybrid, and in my opinion it does a decent job at it. It doesn't slack on the farming aspect (comparable to HM New Beginnings... I think that was the one I played last) and it brings a passable combat aspect to break up the monotony of farm life. If farming sim is anathema to you, simply walk away from this one as the adventure rpg side is not strong enough to sell itself without the farm side.The Good:PLENTY to do - Between leveling Skills, tending the farms, hunting down materials, and visiting the townsfolk, it's quite easy to find yourself running out of hours in the day.Story - Passable I think. Nothing especially grand, but also doesn't ruin the game.Combat - For a farming sim hybrid, the combat is not bad. You have 6 weapon types (7 if you count Axe/Hammer separately, which the game does not) to choose from, and Magic has 6 elements with 4 spells per element. You also get a Dash/Dodge which has i-frames, so the combat was not a half-baked idea thrown into the mix.The Bad:Character customization - Non-existent almost. There's a male and female avatar, no options to change hairstyle, color, eyes. All you can change later is your outfit and your headgear, and eventually you can swap gender as well.Romance options - This is a negative in my book, but having all the available male and female romance options be completely enthralled with you later regardless of gender is a mistake. I'm not opposed to having same-sex marriage in the game, but the way the courtship and friendship dialogue was handled was done very poorly I think.Crafting - As deep and intricate as the Crafting system is (for example there are 8-9 Cooking craft categories with their own skill level!!!), there are parts of it that are not explained at all. For example, that seemingly trash Rare Can you fished up that pretty much only says it's a vintage piece in the flavour text? Weeeelll, if you just happened to use it to refine your Weapon, now you have better odds at getting rare loot! Whodathunkit? And Accessories are a whole pile of what-the-whats-now.Overall - I first played Rune Factory 4 on the 3DS, and decided to pick up 5 on Steam. I've thoroughly enjoyed both. On a 10 scale I'd say RF5 lands between a 7 an 8 for me. It's a step up from Harvest Moon due to the addition of adventure and fantasy combat, without compromising too much on either side.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for a wholesome game to distract me from the worst summer of my life, and this one was a perfect match. I'm completely new to the genre, but I think this one may become one of my favorites. - The world is beautiful and colorful. Higher settings add reflections and nice details. To me,  the world is just large enough to want to explore. - The main story is divided into chapters. I'm on chapter 2 now, and find myself thinking that I don't want it to end just yet. This is a feeling I don't often get with games. I would describe the story as light, not overly complicated but with a touch of mystery that makes you want to find out more. -  There are lots of weapons and spells to try. My favorite is hand combat where you can slam and spin monsters. The combat itself is basic, but it works for this game. I find myself going through the wilderness often in search of ingredients, and for fishing at various spots. - For a casual player like me, the crafting system is just elaborate enough not to feel too easy. I found myself crafting just about everything, but cooking is my favorite. - There is experimentation and freedom in this game. A tutorial is substantial, but more often than not I choose to experiment and find out things on my own. - Monsters are cute. You can do a lot with them, but I've been keeping mine for farming and resources. - I know I'm in a minority, but I'm very glad that this game has no gender restrictions for romance. It's a much freer gaming experience for me. If it were restricted I would probably not buy it.- There is a choice to have Japanese voice acting. It's just so much better, and the repeating lines don't sound annoying.- I wish dialogue choices for the protagonist had more of an impact, but the main story is linear. An illusion of choice can be a bit annoying. For example, there was one dialogue where I could choose to answer 'yes' or 'no'. I chose 'no', but the protagonist said, "Just kidding... yes." - I wish the protagonist himself and more of the potential partners were older. The design of older characters just wins over the 'kids' in my opinion. All in all, I would definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: So if you're on the fence of getting this version of the game or the Steam version, I'd highly recommend the Steam version of this game and playing with a controller.  This game runs better with much less load times compared to it's Switch counterpart.I'll keep this review short compared to my other reviews:  If you liked Rune Factory 4, you'll like this game.  They basically took the template of Rune Factory 4 and made it's way to 3D with it.  If you played Rune Factory 4, it's extremely easy to get into this game, since it follows the same formula.  The characters are fairly good with maybe a few exceptions, you have a variety of bachelors and bachelorettes to choose from, the game is easy to get into, there's loads of stuff to do outside the main story, there's tons of events and festivals (Some are staple, like cooking and buddy battle, and some are new, like the moo-moo festival), it's pretty easy to sit back and chill playing this game.  Also, same sex marriage, which hasn't been in a RF game till recently.Some cons though:  There's multiple sound bugs I've come across in the game (Music either dying or sound effects getting stuck in a loop, reloading a save fixes this).  For veterans, this game runs on the easy side.  End game quests can be a pain to complete (Especially getting everyone to 10 friendship).  Certain end game mobs have massively high defense in an early part of a dungeon that you'll need to do the 'rosary' trick to avoid them.  Doing a magic build is much harder to do than a melee build.Overall though, I did get enjoyment out of this game, putting over 100 hours on the Switch version and over 40 hours on this version.  Despite the few kinks, I'd definitely recommend this game, but don't go crazy like how I did and min/max everything, take it at your own pace.

_childDocuments_.review: Rune Factory 5 is a great game and it does follow Rune Factory 4 very  well. I think they did a great job with the tutorial section, keeping it short and interesting enough to follow. The characters are like all the other Rune Factory games, very cute and wholesome. The fighting aspect is also pretty easy to pick up and understand being very similar to most MMO type games. It is overall a very cute and fun game to play with very immersive and great story.My Favorite Things:1. The immersive story lines for each character, I love the fact that in all of the Rune Factory games each character has their own story and background that you get to explore as you improve your relationships with them.2. The pets!! The pets you can tame are super cool, and I've always been a huge fan of the fact that they can do most of your farm work for you allowing you to go out and do other things.3. The fishing, cooking, and crafting system is very easy to understand and also pretty fun. It doesn't feel super grind heavy.4. The different weapons you can use is pretty awesome too, you're not stuck with one set way of fighting and you have a lot of freedom on how you want to go about exploration before and after you finish the main story line.Things that could use work:1. The characters seem to be a little lacking from the previous Rune Factory 4 game and it's really sad that you can't date the Rune Factory 4 favorites Doug and Margaret. It's a little difficult to feel any attachment to these new characters as their backstories feel a little weak. Hopefully they expand on some of these character's backstories as we mostly only know very surface level things even after getting to Level 5 relationships or even higher. 2. Open-ended explanations... I don't like that they talk about all of these different things that leave you with a bunch of questions. I don't want to go into too much detail for spoilers but there are certain things about characters that you just don't get to know despite it coming up in conversations multiple times.Overall it's a fun game, but I do really hope they work on some of the things I don't like about it as it is currently. _childDocuments_.review: First things first this is by far the superior version of Rune Factory 5 just for the fact alone that it, you know runs, unlike the  Switch version where getting  like 22 fps is a miracle.If you like any of the Rune Factory games you'll like this BUT there are some things that are negatives the  biggest one  being a growing pain thanks to this being the  first main game entry to be in 3D as well as just badly planned.The biggest is combat. Combat works  mostly the same but in the 3D space they tried to add some vertacality to the basic combos which most enmies won't get hit by espeically when using the fist or hammers which will knockdown an enemy half way through a  combo meaning the second have of it will just whiff. The second part of combat is the kinda, sorta, well flat out ruined most of the  rune abilities that weapons get making them have a long drawn out preparation animation that gives enemies, most of which are faster than you a, just casually waddle away and even if they don't the range is ALWAYS shorter than you think it is.  Same kind of applies to spells too for the most part but the worst thing is that there's sort of a forced push back mechanic which I feel might've  been done to decrease players who knew what they were doing being able to pull off touch of death juggle combos on mini bosses but when most of the weapon abilities or even basic attacks or multihit moves you find yourself getting launched away from an  enemy for trying to beat them down like your supposed to.Outside of that another big problem is pacing in the story which is directly tied to your progression. Even basic tier items will be locked off to you more or less completely. For example fully upgrading your  tools to gold status is ipossible until  at least midway chapter 3 without exploiting some stuff  and flat out getting lucky and randomly finding some gold early on. And Chapter 2 actually  removes one of your main stay abilities which ruins  your ability to get points needed  to  upgrade your house, farm and village thanks to not being able to do a certain type of repetable quest AND also locks you out of gathering a certain type of material   to use farm boosts and this is made even worse by the fact that yo can really only do  only one or two main story events a day before the game makes you wait.With all that said though if you can look past that it's still worth getting, still nice seeing Rune Factory back again and hopefully  the new team can either learn how to make the 3d perspective work in the next entry or go back to what worked before.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to re-write this review now that I've played more than 30 minutes... this is coming from a souls-veteran, a harvest moon lover, and someone who beat RF4. This is an awful, pathetic game for our generation. Now that I've gotten past the atrocious graphics and the blander-than-flour story, I now get to explore the bachelorettes. Some of them have great personalities (and bodies! HUBBA HUBBA) and I'm interested in investing in them. Turns out, those are actually the moms of the bachelorettes and they are not dateable. The ACTUAL bachelorettes look like they are just shy of 13 years old. When I looked this up, I felt genuine disgust. They look and sound like genuine children. I tried swapping the voice acting to Japanese to try and disassociate as I try to romance, but I just can't do it. Ped0ph1lia aside, this game doesn't offer anything new. Combat is incredibly easy, and there isn't really any value for defeating an enemy or a boss. You level up so quickly, and the bonuses are passive, so it doesn't feel like there is any reward for grinding out a skill. The writing is awful. The pacing is awful. I'm disappointed that this game has so many positive reviews. I wonder if these reviewers have played games other than farming sims, or if they are here for the dating of children. If you're looking for a farming sim/dating sim, this is not it. If I hadn't gone AFK for 4 hours, I would refund this game (again). Suggestions for alternatives: Stardew and Dinkum. If you didn't like those, definitely don't get whatever this is.

_childDocuments_.review: After almost a full day of playtime, I think I can relatively fairly judge this game.In some respects it is worse than 4. Storywise, I personally thought it was hilarious how they suddenly made you slave-like royalty in 4, which was super-cute. Being a mercenary in contrast just feels kind of meh. Same obligations, mind you, but it's just a different feel. The explanations of mechanics are sometimes lacking. I'm sure, if this is your entry into the series, you will sometimes feel a bit lost. Sometimes it is very noticable that this is a port. The controls are a bit clunky and if the carrying around and placing of furniture is really the only to do things, they need to fix this ASAP! I cannot place anything against the wall for the life of me. Also, some of the NPCs are plain annoying. Scratch that, one NPC is plain annoying, but that happens.What I love about this game: It is very,, very much like Rune Factory 4. The NPCs are cute, the combat is fun, the farming is there, but quick and easy, there are plenty of cute monsters to tame and the list goes on.I personally think, that a lot of the criticism is so overblown, because people expect a new installment to be better than the previous one and it really seems that they didn't aim for that. They were aiming for as good as. I'm not sure they achieved that, but they got pretty close and that still makes this a marvelous game.If you are new though, start with RF4. :)

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Big leap forward in quality of Town and Relationship events and gameplay, several steps backwards in the writing of the finer details and minor dialogue. If you want a quick and easy score, 7-7.5/10 I cleared the main story a couple of weeks ago. Overall a good Rune Factory game from my perspective. I don't really have any strong feelings to make me want to write essays about game mechanics and stuff, but I want to point out some of the things that stood out to me while playing and grouping them up into positive, meh, and negative experiences.[+] Tons of QoL changes. Can hold down E to stack more of the same item as you walk around, relationship events now pop up as markers when certain conditions are met and aren't RNG, SEED crests that help with a lot of grinding and traveling, etc. Lots of stuff that I wished RF4 had are in here.[+] All the characters have pretty distinct personalities and designs, making (what few) interactions between them and (what few) comments about each other they make interesting and pretty involving.[+] More relationship events and side events, each with a lot more involved writing. I prefer most of the events over RF4's, which were also really good.[+] The 3D action combat is a great improvement. The improved dash mechanics are great and lots of the weapons have been changed to make them feel a lot more distinct from one another. Also you can't get infinitely juggled and dizzy locked by things like Palm Tigers, which is a plus.[+] Link Skills make me actually want to put villagers in my party instead of leaving them on the side and occasionally pick them up so they can act as meat shields for a boss I'm having trouble with. Tandem stuff is also a nice touch.[o] Day length has changed. Every minute is about 3 seconds, which used to be 1 second in RF4. It helps since the maps are much larger but also means every day is longer. It helps when you have lots to do but when you're just sorting through menus, which pause the time, can make days feel like they just don't end.[o] The 3D map is both a blessing and a curse. A blessing in that it helps with immersion, a curse in that its so huge traveling from point A to point B is very long. Exploring field areas and dungeons takes way longer and while mining nodes tend to be within the first few rooms, there are some lengthy trips like going to the Silver nodes in Gadeus Grasslands.[o] The renovation system is ... okay. I preferred how RF4 did it since it was easier to do and didn't require the use of a shop which had opening and closing times and just Orders, but it's not game breaking or anything.[o] Farm dragons are pretty nice mechanically, since you can feed them crystals to gain extra effects, but the fact you need to fast travel between them rather than have them all in one spot like farm expansions in previous games were like is wack.[o] Some relationship events move time forward. It help with immersion but kind of screws with you, especially since maybe a couple of the four or five events that do this are telegraphed and give you the option to quit out before it happens. [-] While relationship and side events are well written, daily dialogue is incredibly underwritten.  I've received certain messages thrice to four times before I even finished the Spring season, and there are times when I've gone up to two characters who were standing next to each other, who I assumed were talking to one another, and never saw a conversation between them. Comparing this to RF4, where the bachelors and bachelorettes had full on conversations you could 'listen' in on by interacting with them when they were in pairs or grouped up together that would change depending on whether they were in the restaurant, in their home, or just fishing next to one another and you see a lot of little details that are missing that made the world feel 'lived in'. It's not super detrimental since the Events are pretty much hard carrying this aspect of the game, but its something I miss sorely.[-] The Ribbitee type enemies have a rare chance to inflict Death (OHKO you) if they deal any damage on you. These are a frequent, reoccurring enemy that appear in most dungeons and fields, including some starting areas. They can also appear in groups, meaning you have to deal with multiple potentially instantly fatal mobs while you have a serviceable lock on system that pushes you into single target combat. I have been insta-killed by these damn things three times already, once when I just ran in and took a random hit I wasn't expecting to take off all my health.  The revival item I can't spell exists in this game, so it kind of helps with that issue somewhat, though I don't know how you obtain it. Basically think SMT Nocturne's random encounters with Mudo/Hama mobs w/o Null Death/Expel Magatama or Tetraja and you've got a basic idea of what it's like to fight these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.[-] The story villain flips sides faster than a Tsundere in a anime that's only interested in seeing her get inside the protag's pants. Makes his  all the more strange.Correction: I'm a big dumb dumb and didn't wait til past 8PM to check if there were and relationship events that occurred then. Apparently that last part is actually a separate smaller relationship mini event that only pops up at around that time.[-] Scythe's first charge is 2x3 plots long. There is no 1x1 plot wide option. Why?And that's it. I'll sand this down more when I got time and more experience, but that's how it's been so far. Still a great experience even with the few flaws it has.

_childDocuments_.review: Isn't exactly as bad as I'd thought, especially in regards to optimizations, mouse+keyboard controls feels pretty good, better than how it was on 4S. Performance is amazing but sadly they don't seem to try to upgrade the textures, however this means that this game can be run on laptop's Integrated Graphics, at least AMD Radeon Vega ones, tried myself on Vega 8 of Ryzen 7 5800H and it's just shy of 100fps usually, can retain more than 60fps at least in town.Storyline wise I'd say it's longer than Rune Factory 3 but shorter than Rune Factory 4 (just 2 story arcs compared to 3 in Rune Factory 4), however I'd criticize so many changes from the previous RF games, notably on how it took like 60% of the story to unlock a damned Flower Shop, like why? Marriage is not tied to the story, unlike RF2 and 3, so if you criticize that aspect like me, this game is safe to play, I can manage to marry someone before the final credits roll.Difficulty wise, this game is too easy, even easier than RF4, just tame the Nine Tailed Fox, make her your party anytime, and even on "Hard" I beat the final boss easily.Interest-wise, to be honest this is like the second most boring to Rune Factory 1 of all the RF games (except Frontier and ToD since I never played them), dialogues are no longer so unique like RF4, so it really took me a while to get the interesting part "kicks in", and the ending is the cheesiest of all RF games.Bachelor/ette-wise, this game has gay marriage if you want it, you can also change your gender but only after finishing the whole story for the first time, but the quality of the potential waifus/husbandos, as a straight asian man I kinda say this game has the least interesting bachelorettes, for bachelors since I never tried dating them idk but I heard the straight women/gay men players do love the bachelors, and I do think they're interesting at the least outside dating. I married Ludmila and she's the only one "as interesting as girls from the previous games" for me on my first impressions, bachelorettes used to be so quirky, and while others do have their quirks, they're like the most "normal" out of all RF games, not to mention all of them are short and "young-looking" except Ludmila and Scarlett, while in RF4 we have Forte, Margaret, and Dolce who are taller and looks older (for an anime standard of course). Map-wise, my experience is like playing GTA III, like I really felt like this is a first attempt of a studio to make a 3D game of a particular series (which, in a way, it kinda is), the buildings are too spread out, moving is slower than previous games, and time also passes way more slowly than in previous games.I only recommend this game if bought under like 50% discount on a sale. I wish there's a "neutral" button on the steam reviews since this is probably that, I can't really recommend it "normally" yet I can't say that I would prevent other people from trying due to how bad it is. Not that bad, yet definitely worse than the Magnum Opus which is RF4.Compared to all mainline series (I never played the spinoff), to sum up, this ties with Rune Factory 2 for me, better than 1 yet worse than 3 and 4 except on the story length where this is longer than RF3 and shorter than 4.FINAL VERDICT : BUY ON HEAVY SALE, BEST EXPERIENCE IS IF YOU NEVER PLAYED RUNE FACTORY 4 BEFORE THIS GAME

_childDocuments_.review: If Tides of Destiny brought you to play 5, You'll be disappointed.Game started with a Persona 5-esque opening, which was awesome, buuut so far it follows the Rune Factory formula without adding anything new. The graphics, the clunky mechanics, the run of the mill jrpg characters. Story/theme is pretty much the same as well. You end up somewhere, you have amnesia, and you'll have to do odd jobs until someone tells you were summoned there . I'm hoping this ones keeps me occupied better than 4........that was garbage.Everyone in this game, including your character, walk like they have a stick up their ass. Not game breaking or anything, but who was the person in production that was like "oh ya, that's how people walk." -_- I recommend turning the shadows to smooth if you're maxing out your graphic settings. If you don't, you'll have these weird, over-sized, pixel shadows that completely pull immersion. Either way, the shadows aren't good, but at least the smooth version doesn't seem to affect characters faces every time you're around light sources. I'm pretty sure the game launcher's default settings are from the Switch because my initial graphics were set to a 720. Maybe even try their settings first an see if its smoother because trying to run it at max you get a lot of stuttering even for a game with ps 2 graphics-20 Hour update- Weird/Sloppy/Lazy, not sure which it is, but they chose that placing your items in your home/farm is not grid based. They also made it so you cant put any items right next to each other, or against any walls.....It irks me to the point that i'm frustrated enough to stop the game and have to type this up because of how stupid it looks. Then I started to notice this game pretty much has absolutely no polish.........If this game was a person, it would be the dude that does his project the night before its due.-48 Hour update-I feel like I wasted my time. Got to the credits way quicker than other Rune Factory installment. Story is really open ended so i'm guessing there is more endgame content, but i've completely lost interest on account i've had better story and dialogue in mediocre games from 1997. The game as a whole just feels empty.........The opening of the game is still the best thing about this one unfortunately.

name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe
detailed_description: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe is a first person exploration game. It is an expanded re-imagining of the critically acclaimed, award winning indie game The Stanley Parable from 2013. When a simple-minded individual named Stanley discovers that the co-workers in his office have mysteriously vanished, he sets off to find answers. You will play as Stanley, and you will not play as Stanley. You will make a choice, and you will have your choices taken from you. The game will end, the game will never end. Contradiction follows contradiction, the rules of how games should work are broken, then broken again. You are not here to win. The Stanley Parable is a game that plays you. What's New? Everything that was in the original Stanley Parable is here, preserved just like it was back in 2013. But The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe also dramatically expands the world of the original game with new content, new choices, and new secrets to uncover. The labyrinth has just gotten bigger. In addition, the game has been visually upgraded to reflect modern technology while faithfully preserving the tone of the original game. Accessibility features have also been added to the game, including localization of in-world text, colorblind options, and content warnings. And just as before, the impeccable voicework of Kevan Brighting will accompany you every step of the way. In The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, everything you remember has been recreated, yet it's different somehow. We've been here before, haven't we? Is Stanley still the same as he was back then? Or is it you who has changed?

_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality.How else to describe The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe?Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time!The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate to all of history of all media ever made.It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone for the stone in which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement.You are not beyond redemption.You may change, and you may become more so much more than you were before.If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, it is this...What a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience.It leaves me hopeful that as a community - as a world there is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we could ever dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.

_childDocuments_.review: The original The Stanley Parable had a fun, semi-unique deconstruction of the state of video games in 2013. Almost a decade worth of indie games later, and the same kind of meta-commentary/do-nothing game just doesn't hold the same appeal. Nothing here is shocking, humorous, or innovative any more; ironically because of the vast multitude of meta-commentary games that The Stanley Parable (2013) helped to create. The majority of the game feels like a stream of consciousness that has no real rhyme, reason, or planning other than "What else needs to be added to justify the £20 price mark?" Spend a morning playing The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, watch The Matrix Resurrections in the evening, and go visit a modern art museum in the afternoon, and by the next morning you'll be yearning for a boring office job in a grey lifeless city to escape the horrors of self-reflection. Also, if you don't find buckets funny then you're out of luck.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: After mulling on them for a while, I think I can articulate my thoughts on Deluxe. Famously, the original was packed with critiques towards narrative design and choice in gaming, stringing the player along their many paths with existentialist musings and witty dialogue. Constantly prodding the imagination and sense of discovery, seamlessly giving its thoroughly planned design a feeling of freedom. Which arguably elevates the purpose of certain endings, if not being the underlying message of the game itself.Before even completing the "Main" ending with the Off button, on the direct path to the control room you can detour into the "Coward", "Window", "430", "Broom Closet", "Button Heaven", "Mariella", "Escape Pod", "Museum", and a final last second choice to hit "On". All before its true ending, not even including all the endings waiting behind the Right door. On my initial replay of this section in Deluxe, I stumbled into two brand new endings entirely on accident. Falling into the pit and pressing elevator buttons repeatedly gave me routes that felt earnestly at home with the original content. A further sarcastic exploration of narrative choice, but with this newfound sense of sincerity behind them. I've even been informed of a new warehouse ending which I haven't seen! While some of the original game's writing is out of date, particularly the ableist "Mariella" ending; I felt more appreciative of the game's messaging and design, and was excited to discover this new content.However, this was the extent of the naturally found content. A new door is placed in a hall before the central left and right choice, baring a very blunt "New Content" sign. The next three endings of the game play out entirely sequentially, leading you along a narrow path which you're unable to alter or interact with. The initial "New Content" route begins with a thin joke of adding a Jump Circle, and the implication of it being the only singular addition. While good criticism and humor is present further into its path, they no longer feel earned. Its spat at you as the Narrator directly reads reviews of the original game. The paths were always predetermined, but there is only one outcome after these strings of sequences. And its to play the original game with the additions of a bucket and collectibles.To their credit however, the Bucket is actually their most brilliant decision. While lacking some of the commentary of the "Major" endings that led to it, it exemplified the writing and design of Stanley better than them. You in essence, do exactly what Deluxe began criticizing. Interacting with this incredibly basic addition to the game, only given value by myself. Yet, this simple addition led to large unexpected changes to the previously existing endings, building something new without explicitly stopping you in your path. You don't even have to pick up the bucket, and do an entirely normal ending if you desire. The Bucket will still be there for you if you decide to. In a game about choice, that felt like one that mattered.As much as the linear path feels in service of the game's opinions of rampant fandom, industry, production, and expansions themselves; They fall into doing the very things they criticize, which does not absolve them from said criticism. The points of its new story make it feel fruitless to have asked more from it. Exploring the office more, been given more genuine choices and routes, be allowed to experiment, maybe we could've even celebrated games as much as there's ample room to be critical about them. Game making is an astronomical effort, even making a third door with a different hallway would've been laborious. But that's exactly what they did, and they made you walk down a straight path with three endings.I do believe ultimately, the game is worth playing, but I can't gloss over these mental hangups; And the slight sourness and pessimism I felt brewing within it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: The Stanley Parable isn't a real game. Let's make that clear right off the bat. It's a commentary on gaming, on narrative tropes, on choice, and perhaps on more... And honestly, that's what made the original so brilliant. So what do you do in order to update the original when it was so flawless? Well, use your added content to make commentary on the nature of added content of course! It's this sort of meta-commentary, including commentary on the nature of reviews itself which makes the Stanley Parable Ultra Deluxe so brilliant. On first boot, I didn't really notice a whole lot of new content. Then second boot, and suddenly a door labeled "new content" is staring me right in the face! I'm not going to spoil all that's in store for players from there, but suffice it to say, once you start discovering new content as it's presented directly to you, you'll want to go back to the original branching paths and see what nuggets of new content you can find, and they are definitely there! Of course, the Broom Closet ending will always be my favorite. hahaSo is it worth the price? Well, given the sheer volume of commentary and new content added, I'd say yes! Don't go in expecting a game you can win. Expect a game that will make you laugh, make you think, make you wonder if maybe the whole point of gaming isn't to win, but to experience the commentary the game makes on the nature of existence itself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: Soooo... it's very hard for me to judge this game, so I will try to take a look from two perspectives:If you're someone who didn't play the original: HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. This is for sure the ultimate version of Stanley Parable, giving you the full experience and more. If you want a meta walking simulator, this game is for you.If you played the original game: BUY ON SALE, unless you're a huge fan. After doing most of the known new content, I get the feeling that it's just a bit more of the same and a lot of the new content was made with existing stuff, just slightly changing it. It's still Stanley, but somehow for me it didn't had the same magic of the first playthrough. If you're a huge fan I'm sure you'll be delighted. If not, it may disappoint you a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Today I was super excited to see the Ultra Deluxe edition of Stanley Parable, so I bought it and installed it on my under-powered laptop. I played the original Stanley Parable with a controller (sad). I didn't have a controller handy, so I tried to default to traditional FPS keyboard/mouse bindings.Why can't I bind R-mouse to "move forward"? Seriously, I'm an old school gamer; WASD is crippling for us old masters :-) Suddenly I find myself totally hamstrung trying to play this game on the PC with keyboard/mouse... and for some reason that feels exactly appropriate for the "Stanley Parable Ultra Deluxe".It's a great game so far. I'd give it 5.1/5 stars if I could use *real* FPS controls, but it gets a 4.91/5 because it's still a good game even though I was forced to use WASD. Worse, I'll probably fall back to a console controller (like the plebes ;-) on my main gaming PC. I have no doubt it will be awesome.Please, Crows Crows Crows, let us bind mouse buttons to movement and actions. :plz: Great game nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: The Stanley Parable is a fun game that I refuse to believe anyone won't likeThe "Ultra Deluxe" Prefix is effectively a a paper hay pretending to be a nice fancy hat. It does not improve the game as much as it should. A lot of fun easter eggs are gone (no more source engine) and the only thing added is the bucket (all it does is reskin all the endings) and adds about 2.5 hours of content. (Most of which is pretty fun) The base game is perfectly fine and this doesn't add much. The main problem is that it didn't add as much as it should, or could have. At that point they should have just made an actual sequel. None was clambering for a addon for the Stanley story.If you have played the Stanley Parable then this game shouldn't be a top priority. If you haven't, then you definitely should play. (Valve needs to add a 5 star rating system lol)

_childDocuments_.review: I was about to write a negative review at first, since I couldn't find any reason for the money spent on this expansion.Then, I've started to dig more and more and I've changed my mind . The ironic part is that the whole game's point is to make fun of its "DLC" nature or "re-imagining". If you're looking for a short answer, then hear me out: . If you've already played the hell out of the original, you'll be pleased to know that I've spent about 6/7 hours with new content. Of course, there are always the "classic" endings.Given the discounted price and the support which Crows Crows Crows definitely deserve, I would say that it's fair deal.For those of you who want to hear more, I have a few more things to add.I'm quite confident that The Stanley Parable could be described as one of the best narrative experiences one could ever imagine in a videogame. Back in 2013, it was a . And I really mean it. I remember being mesmerized while playing through all of the endings, always reinventing themselves and keeping the pace for hours. I could never get tired. In fact, I replayed every ending a couple of years ago in the original version since it always feels refreshing to see after a while.But what's the point of the said things above? Well, it's simple: the new content lives up for it and  if it manages to capture your attention liked it used to do. If you've played The Beginner's Guide and Dr. Langeskov [long title], you'll know that your expectations . I can't put my finger on it, but the writing, the level presentation, the narrator's dialogues are so perfectly made that the new sections blend beautifully into the existing game, adding more layers of depth and more comedic self-awareness. It's a breath of fresh air indeed.All of this is achieved with a simple trick. An object. A . When I first encountered it in the new content area, I simply thought it was one of the various gimmicks made only to entertain you for a few minutes, but the developers really managed to squeeze every ounce of comedic-ness out of it. I just can't imagine. It's terribly genius. Each new line is connected to this object which you'll need to carry around in order to experience new dialogue and "cutscenes". And I know it sounds like madness, but Ultra Deluxe manages to be even stranger and somewhat creepier than it's former edition. I really loved it.This is just a silly side note. I've never managed to get the "Go Outside" achievement on the original Stanley Parable, so it's only natural for me to say that the developers are kind of sadistic with the new achievement related to that one. Good luck to everyone who engages in this new, exciting adventure. : Experience this game.
