_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made. It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone for the stone into which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgment.You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may become more, so much more than you were before. If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, it is this… what a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience. It leaves me hopeful that as a community - as a world, there is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the story of a man named Stanley. Stanley worked for a company in a big building where he was Employee #427. Employee #427's job was simple: he sat at his desk in Room 427 and he pushed buttons on a keyboard.This game, regardless of how you view it, ends with you truly becoming Stanley. all you do is push buttons on a keyboard, maybe do a little mousework if that's what you wish, but, regardless, you are Stanley.11/10

_childDocuments_.review: Well I've been having great fun with the game so far... However, it appears that some endings never really "unlocked" for me.  So there's definitely some glitches that'll prevent you from actually seeing parts of the game. Not to mention that apparently while the previous game prided itself on being able to see any (almost) any given ending at any given point, this new game actually has some semblance of progression, which actually prevents you from seeing previous endings in that progression line again. It's rather peculiar, all things considered. The new content is quite good, I just sincerely hope that they solve some of the current issues.EDIT: I stand corrected. Including the spoiler. Exceptional, no complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just a lazy unity port. I really wish there was a lot more new content in this compared to the original, I still see all of the same assets and the only difference really is maybe better performance and lighting; It's not enough to make this game worth $25 (which is insanely overpriced). The game is very funny still obviously and encourages you to do a multitude of things and all that, but man I wish there was even more endings. I won't give this a negative review since it is still a very good and witty game but I would advise you to wait for a sale.Also I am so tired of the featured reviews for this game being memey and "HAHA FUNNY BUCKET" to get some steam awards.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really exited for this to come out since I loved the original, I was however very worried about how much would be new and how well it would be added to the original content. My worries were for nothing though because it melds well to the original with plenty more exiting and fun new content to explore that is just as clever and unique as the original game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was worried that this game would be more of the same and wouldn't give me the same big stupid grin that the first play through gave me.And I was wrong and right at the same time, Ultra Deluxe IS more of the same but in the BEST way possible.I still had a big stupid grin on my face and it still made me laugh out loud many times over.I think almost every ending has a little twist on it and without spoiling anything the game is easily twice as big as the original.Highly recommend for new and old fans of Stanley alike :)

I dutifully asked the lady in the store room for a long weight, she came back 30 mins later and said "oh, are you still here"  I said "yes, you were getting me the long  ........ wait"Basically this game is that sort of practical joke played on you the player (purchaser) over and over and over again.  Its funny once.The voice acting is very good but the writing is average.  If they had told me they made this game in a week I'd believe them.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the review of a game called The Stanley Parable, and while I'd love to write the whole review as if I were the narrator, I lack the ingenuity and wit to do so, which is why I'll stop now, and proceed with a proper review. So, what is The Stanley Parable, you might be asking? Well, it's a game about choice... Wait a minute, didn't I do this already? Ah, right, this is not the review of The Stanley Parable, as I'm proud to introduce the updated and renovated Ultra Deluxe Review for The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe!And what can I say about such an Ultra Deluxe version? Well, pretty much the same things I said about the original game, so I'll keep some copy-pasted paragraphs, rewrite them here and there, and hope people don't notice it (even though I'm saying what I'm gonna do!).Anyway, what is The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe? The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe is a first person game, and one of the earliest walking simulators. I've been a fan of this game (or is it a franchise now?) since its original mod release, and it's been great seeing it evolve over the years, first with the original Steam release, and now with Ultra Deluxe. The story remains largely unchanged from the previous entries, and it's rather simple, or complex, depending on your choices. The game basically tells the story of Stanley, or Employee 427, who worked in an office. One day, he discovers that all his coworkers have disappeared, and thus decides to explore the office building in search of answers. As he moves through the office, he reaches the game's core: the two doors. A simple concept, choosing left or right, that this game manages to explore in incredible depth. With Ultra Deluxe, even more choices and endings have been added, even endings that affect other endings, and what could be considered a "true" ending.All throughout the game, there's a secondary character, the Narrator. As his name implies, he's the one narrating the story, and thus, guiding Stanley's (and the player's) actions. However, going back to the two doors mentioned above, the player can choose to ignore the Narrator and figuratively wrestle with him for control of the story, the more you progress through the game, the more options that begin to show up, leading to a great deal of replayability as you try to get all the different endings. All this accompanied by the Narrator's hilarious dialogue.The writing is superb, and I can't state this with enough emphasis; while the only speaking character is the Narrator, as mentioned above, almost all his dialogue is hilarious, though there are some somber moments here and there. In Ultra Deluxe, the dialogue has been expanded a whole lot, with even more somber moments and times of reflection; the "true" ending I mentioned above is a particular favourite of mine. Visually speaking, it looks pretty good, and it manages to keep the look of the original despite moving from Source to Unity. There's several new environments to explore, and they all look beautiful. Gameplay wise, it's very simple: you walk and interact with certain objects; as it is a very heavily story-driven game, there's not much else to do, no fancy shooting or parkour sections, but they aren't needed. Finally, the soundtrack, while minimalistic, serves its purpose well.All in all, I can say I definitely recommend this game. Saying too much about it would spoil it, which is why I won't extend this review more than I have to.

_childDocuments_.review: It kind of pains me to not recommend this game but... yeah, I don't. While the new content isn't terrible or anything, it's all kind of built on a single gag, which is that pushing devs to make sequels/expansions to games that don't need it is stupid, and if the dev does it, it's entirely a money grab. Which, paradoxically, this does feel like. I've seen some people recommend new players to this version but... I can't even do that. The original is $10 cheaper and has all of the content you would actually care about.More than anything, I'm just kind of shocked at how long this took to make. I mean, this thing was in development for at least four years, yet from what was added, I truly have no idea how it took that long; there isn't THAT much original content in the game. The Source Engine remake was released just over two years after the original Half-Life 2 mod, so how did this expansion take at least twice as long? Look, I'm not here to complain that the dev isn't working fast enough, but it just seems strange that it spent so long in the oven and came out half-baked.If this were a free expansion or a $5-10 DLC for the original, this would have been much more palletable. But even then, Ultra Deluxe doesn't have nearly as much to say as the original and its message isn't nearly as potent. If you want another Walking Simulator by Davey Wrenden, The Beginner's Guide is a far better choice.I think my overall takeaway is that Wrenden didn't need to spend 4+ years and make an entire $25 game to make the point of "Nothing else needs to be added to this game," he could have just made something else. And should have. He's a very talented guy and it feels like this entire project was a bit of a waste.

_childDocuments_.review: Its nice that the original game was included, and I think this version of the game is the BEST option for people who haven't played The Stanley Parable before, but as someone who thoroughly finished the original 9 years ago, it didn't feel like there was enough content to justify the price. There ended up being about 45 minutes of wholly new areas to go through which was nice (I didn't think the memories area was nearly as clever as the writers thought it was) and new variants of the original endings, plus a couple of new endings as well. However, to see it all means you have to reach each ending again. I get that was probably the point, but the new content just wasn't interesting enough for me not to get tired of running through the same halls and hearing the same grating voice lines ad nauseam (and they get less and less funny each time). If this is someone's first experience with TSP, this is a good buy, but for those who did, I'd recommend waiting for a big sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The nature of this game means I won't be giving any details, but I am glad I got it and have enjoyed/am enjoying it. I would not have thought it would be possible or advisable to attempt something like this with such a great and beloved game, but the dev's creativity clearly outstrips my imagination. They did an excellent job expanding on the humor and things to discover. I am also strangely comforted. 10/10 would set the time again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: This rec comes with the caveat of whether or not you played the original. If you didn't, or maybe it's been so long you forgot everything, then yes, this game is great and you should absolutely buy it. The premise is clever and the games oozes with charm, humor, clever moments. There's a ton of commentary here about video games, choice, and story telling.If you did though, then this is more of a softer recommendation. The new content here is good, and there's plenty of memorable moments, but it's a little lacking. I think $25 is a bit high to ask for what is here. You should catch it on sale, and I would say you should avoid any spoilers or videos until you can actually play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I get the appeal for this game for people, I think. I might be wrong considering people like this game for different reasons. Which is okay.The game's' all about making choices, The game's centered about making choices. but they're mostly making only obvious choices. I thought because this game's centered about choices, it'd feel personal or something. Like the 'little' things you do affect the bigger story, or the concept of butterfly effect or karma would be used in the game, But no, not really. I played this completely blind because I didn't play the OG stanley parable. And when I explored things that doesn't feel obvious to explore, it never really rewards you with anything. And because I played the game completely blind, because I didn't know what the game is all about other than making choices, I didn't know what I was supposed to do. I guess it's because in video games nowdays, there's a lot of choices that you can obey or disobey. People like disobeying things so the game's all centered about that concept. But when I played the game this game, I felt like the "obeying orders and disobeying orders" thing FEELS like obeying orders. Both of them. Because the game is about choices and basically tells you to do BOTH the obeying order and the disobeying order. Making me feel like i had to double disobey it by exploring places around the room or something because I thought there'd be a secret in other play that the game might take notice.Which is why I ended up always trying to interact with objects like turning all pc's off or interacting with this and that and so far the only thing i've ever achieved, and the only thing that has rewarded to me this was the door achievement. It was an achievement I've gotten on my very first run of the game. And even though the achievement itself is meant to be a funny easter egg for people, because I have an unclear way of playing the game, I thought the game would be littered with THAT kind of easter eggs in other places, only to discover the fact that, no, so far, I've only encountered the door (and the keypad if you enter quick enough before the narrator tells you the keypad's number code) as the only really choices that feel invisible or personalized. Meaning I've spent more hours actually just exploring for nothing than the obvious things to do, actually progressing.Anyways, it's just a personal experience of this game. I didn't like it because it was bad, It's just I played it wrong, wasted hours for nothing (and i meant wandering around lots of rooms for a lot of times trying to find something to end up finding nothing, and not how you reset every ending), and now I'm too burnt out and demotivate it to continue it. If you're a blind player, and you have the same mindset of wanting to explore or something, maybe this would helpJust a note for here though. Button path, hands down, favorite path. It's probably the only path that really made me think deeply about life in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: On its own, Ultra Deluxe is a fun, odd time to play, with tons of new surprises to experience. It's a great walking-sim with multiple endings, and dumbfounding moments. Scenarios, in terms of audio work, concepts, and ideas, feel really polished. The game's writing and narrator REALLY shine here. I'd say a half hour is enough to know if this game would be your cup of tea or not. The tea that's there, there's a lot of. I kind of want to make or see a chart of all the possible endings.However, I do feel like someone would get the most out of this game by playing the original first. Which feels weird to say, given that all the og content is here, but there's a ton of Deluxe jokes that would fly over my head, had I not played the original so many years back. This would be a gripe, BUT For newcomers, what's cool is that you can just buy this version, state its your first time playing, and you'll be given a chunk of more time before the Deluxe content starts slipping in. The game is very considerate in that way.

_childDocuments_.review: After having played several hours worth of The Stanley Parable, I could hardly wait to get my hands on The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe. _childDocuments_.review: Skip to the end for less extensive review.The Stanley Parable isn't just a game, it's an experience that redefines what interactive storytelling can achieve. From the moment you step into Stanley's shoes, you're plunged into a world where every choice feels significant, yet delightfully absurd. This game isn't about winning or losing. It's about exploring the myriad paths life can take, and it's executed with such brilliance that it keeps you hooked from start to finish.What makes The Stanley Parable stand out is its uncanny ability to blend humor with deep philosophical insights. As you wander through the empty office, guided by the ever-present narrator, you quickly realize this game is a commentary on choice and free will. The narrator's witty and often sarcastic remarks add a layer of comedy that never detracts from the profound questions the game poses. Instead, it enhances them, making each decision you face feel both hilarious and significant.One of the most striking aspects of The Stanley Parable is its ability to make you reflect on your own life. The game subtly pushes you to question the nature of your choices. Are you really in control? Or are you merely following a predetermined path? It's a question that lingers long after you’ve put down the controller. The game masterfully uses its simple office setting and minimalist design to focus your attention on the narrative and the choices you make, creating an introspective experience that's rare in the world of gaming.The Stanley Parable is a triumph in interactive storytelling. It’s a game that makes you laugh, think, and question everything you know about games and life itself. It's a refreshing reminder that video games can be art, capable of delivering profound messages in ways that are both entertaining and enlightening. For anyone seeking a game that offers more than just an escape, The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe is an absolute must-play. Its not just a game, it's a journey into the heart of choice, consequence, and the human condition.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I just didn't find it that good. I really thought that this would be the sort of game for me, as I always like games with great narratives and commentaries on games/films as a medium and our relationship to the content we consume. I knew the "gist" of the game, that of funny narrator whose ramblings are simple light-hearted humour packed with a meta-commentary on how you play and it having a bunch of different routes, but that's about it. I feel like that's just enough knowledge to still walk in pretty spoilers-free,  but despite only knowing that, I didn't find it that intriguing and I found that it simple doesn't go much beyond its inital premise: there actually isn't that much content, and what little there is doesn't go "deep" enough for it to be that memorable, nor is the humour that amazing. What's worse is when you've seen about 80% of the game, you'll struggle to remember which paths had choices that you should go back to revisit to encounter more content, and which you've fully completed and would simply rail-roaded into watching the same ending you already saw a few sessions before. Do I really want to bother reading wikis and doing a checkmark on every quirky ending I experienced, and seeing which ones I may have missed? ... Well, after seeing what it has to offer, not really. I sort of wish the game bothered to get into a deeper story instead of constantly staying so surface-level with its jokes that it takes often much too far (which is part of the humour, for sure, but it gets boring quick).Oh and for performance on steam deck, it's excellent, didn't run into any issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Whether or not you should buy this game. A choice. A or B. And as with any choice, there are multiple decisions. A, buying the game, on the right, and B, not buying the game, on the left. It's simple logic. Just think in reverse. At the end of every decision, there's a viewport you can use to look back and decide if you made the right choice. Thus, starting from the right, you must ask yourself: Is the right decision the decision that will lead you to your satisfaction?The answer is obviously...Stanley.Stanley, this review seems oddly familiar, have we been here before? Is this yet another shoveled out the door remake or rerelease of a popular game purely to give more money to the developers? It can't be, the developers of the Stanley Parable wouldn't do that. Would they?No, no they wouldn't, I wouldn't let them. This is my story, if I say this remake should have twice the content of the original, then it has twice the content of the original. If I want to replace a game cameo with  TWO new game cameos, if I want to add a bucket, then the Stanley Parable Ultra Deluxe will have all the buckets and collectibles that I want it to have.End of story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: I think what the original Stanley Parable did was break all the game-development rules. The Deluxe Edition expands on it and breaks even more rules, while still staying absolutely true to itself.It's also incredibly touching at times, as it touches upon the pressures developers are faced with while developing sequels or more content for their games.However, when I thought I saw all, the game surprised me with more, and I honestly didn't anticipate that this game would add as much as it did, the marketing and the whole narrative of this game is probably the most well-crafted thing in a very long time.Overall, hate it, too long, can't pet the bucket.

_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made. It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone for the stone into which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement. You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may become more so much more than you were before. If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, It is this: What a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience, it leaves me hopeful that as a community - as a world - there is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you know that the developer of this game was nearly sued for plagiarising "The Stanley Parable (2012)"? Tragically, the lawyers found the plagiarism, and... The jig was up. You would be rather hard-pressed to find another game that took more jigs.That's not all, however. Also in The Stanley Parable’s credits is a writer, Dan Pinchbeck. We can guess that Pinchbeck, presumably not knowing he was plagiarising, signed off the game's credits. Tragically, at least Pinchbeck is is now a much better writer. Perhaps this will inspire him to be the next Brian Fargo (creator of Wasteland 2).Unlike Wasteland 2, however, this game uses the name "The Stanley Parable Ultra Duluxe", a completely unrelated game which was made for a cheap license and a short time frame in 1989 by Interplay, which later sold the rights to Crows Crows Crows and went on to make Wasteland 3.

_childDocuments_.review: ...but they didn't understand that the game was never meant to be funny! It was meant to have a point! It was meant to speak to the human condition! "But where are the jokes? Where are the jokes?" they bemoaned, they screamed. They gnashed their teeth and said "Entertain us!" It wasn't enough. They had to leave a pathetic little thumbs-down review and make all of their pitiful demands.But then, "He's talking too much," they said! First he didn't entertain us, now he won't shut up! It's the inconsistency! It's the lack of accountability! It's the unwillingness to examine with an uncompromising heart the words they are speaking into the world! As though there were no consequences to someone's lack of cohesion in their examination of others! But of course absolutely anyone can leave a review, so here's what we get! We get these demands that seek everything, and are accountable to nothing!We get these demands that say "Ohh, there should be a skip button! You should be able to freeze Stanley in place, while the Narrator sits there forever and ever! We want all of this in the new Stanley Parable! We demand it!" And then, because it was said, because it was spoken, now it simply has to happen! The most immediate desires, every single thing demanded by every person at every moment in time, if someone wants it then it's a crime not to bring it into being!Have we been given to indulging every fleeting whim for no reason other than to do so? Yes! Yes! It seems that this is now the world we live in! It seems that we are a people living in such bleakness and discomfort with ourselves that our entertainment is now our lives! It has come to represent us! It absolutely must speak to who we are as people!Because otherwise, without our entertainment, we have nothing! Without entertainment we would have to face inward toward the cruel bleakness inside of ourselves. We would turn to look at our deeper nature and find a resounding emptiness gazing back with unyielding aggression. And so - so because of this - we require that our amusements and our play things and our flights of fancy be so impossibly captivating that they consume all of our attention, turn our heads completely away from the bleakness! In effect, we have demanded that our entertainment be the collapse of ourselves! What a pitiful reflection of humanity these entertainments are! What a shameful mirror to the human spirit they project!I'm not mad. I'm not mad about any of this. I'm at peace with it. I am the calm center of gravity around which these perversions hurl themselves. I am a waypoint for reasonable and collected discourse. They're the ones that are mad! They're the ones who couldn't stand the idea of me using my game to try to say something! Maybe they were just jealous of me?Yes...yes, of course. They've been jealous of me this whole time! They are mired in fear and insecurity, and cannot help but attempt to tear me down. What a sad state of affairs. When you read these reviews now you can see it. You can taste the bitter resentment. And my, how good does it feel now to speak truth to these words! To finally allow these thoughts out! Contained and managed for so long, neutered and sterilized! At last I am free to truly think, to feel!It must be that they were so discontent with themselves, they couldn't help but leave a negative review on Steam. Perhaps it says far more about them than it ever did about me. Perhaps the state of their psychological being was in such tatters, and my constitution and willpower are so ironclad in comparison, perhaps it was this state that they saw some outlet in which to tear me down!This, you can see, is clearly why they felt the need to expect the game be funny. That it be filled with yuks, and whimsical humor. That it amuse them endlessly from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: A very funny game with multiple great endings/story lines. I dreamt of playing this game for a while now and I must say, it was worth the dreaming. The ironic speeches and the witty banter from the narrator is amazing and made me laugh multiple times. I am sad that other games by these people haven't been seen as much and I am sure that they are great too. (I haven't played them either). This game made me feel like I was in a choose your own adventure book as the decisions you were allowed to make made me feel curious and adventurous. _childDocuments_.review: What do you do with a "meta" game, when the "meta" gets subverted or sublimated by other games (subliminal) trying to shoehorn their way into your 'domain' ? release a gaudy conceptual content patch that tries to be "more" of everything. For that, it's a 7/10 game. The comedy/surreal makes it an 8/10 and its hard to go above that to make it a 9/10 experience yet. Do I recommend a buy ? Not for $30, and $20 seems like a high watermark. It's probably a "3 hour movie" value, whatever you'd pay for a movie you enjoyed once or twice. Yes, you'll get replay value, sort of. But you could also watch other people play too. This game can be easily spoiled, and you will not get the same experience second-hand. Because of the Meta jokes and references, it relies on your mood and choices more than any "on rails" experience can. So if you aren't invested in the "flow" of the game, you can be bored easily. That's the downside of Meta games where you are 'on rails' but asked to pretend you're not, so you can follow the path intended.I can see the thought(s) and in-jokes behind a lot of the work, at some points you literally walk into a 'pretend' game studio making the long awaited sequel, with test posters, merch, pitch documents, people printing song lyrics, font discussions, Font Tests and Position/Size tests, sic. littering the wall(s). Been there, done that. If the joke of Sequels Suck, was the extent of the "New Content" yeah, it wouldn't be justified as a whole new experience. The Steam Reviews section, was endearing. IDK. It also felt like it was making fun of HL2 as well. There's probably a lot of sequel easter-eggs from other game sequels too. There are touches of surrealism and ennui, which the first game has.Sometimes, the joke isn't clever enough, or there's often a sense that they pulled punches with the story to try not to get into too much effort , but then you see the crazy amount of effort with the "new content" versus the old content that does not have a strong "boom", it's a nod, and then it goes back. The details can be missed when you don't push players to explore in one 'new' area, but then require them to explore deeply when it's unexpected. Some things that you'd get an achievement or secret "thumbs up" moment in other comedy/surealism games, aren't rewarded so you don't know if it happened or it's a glitch in the game either. Especially around mini-game sequences that are 'endings' that loop, but have uncertain, consequential changes. And while that's okay, it can feel like you are going through the motions as you revert and redo things, expecting linearity or regression. It's such a strange melancholy to go back to the game and 'sort of remember' how it all fit together as well.

_childDocuments_.review: "we remembered our anniversary, so maybe you can remember to check you left a positive steam review..." I am being bullied and shamed into writing this, how could you, crows crows crows newsletter!FINE, not a review, i am unable to do those, but my experience with the game i guess?And that saying, i didn't experience the game properly at first, but watched videos of other people playing. and i regret it so badly. because now i love everything about this game, and so wish that it was more personal for me. Can't stop myself spiraling into everything related. all of the trailers, little triva, fan content, more random people playthroughs on yt, just to feel the same way as before through them. i even made my mom play it a little (she liked it! she doesn't get this type of media, but she loved the narration at least. Kevan Brighting is a legend).  ..me being stuck like this is kinda ironic.I don't remember the last time i was so invested in anything, i don't know what it is. but hiding behind all the quips and gags (the humor is really good though) there is something special and personal, existential. argh, stupid emotions, i don't know how to do words anymore. and i don't think i can say anything of value here anyway, except that you should really give this game a try, if anything, for the impeccable narration and some good laughs.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully enjoyable expansion of the video game known as The Stanley Parable.While this release does sort of invalidate the previous one, I am still absolutely happy to have purchased and experienced this deeper-dive into the narrator's narrated narration on the narrative that is The Stanley Parable Ultra Deluxe.If you enjoyed the original, it's more of it!If you haven't played the original, watch a trailer or two and see if it might be up your alley. Please try not to spoil yourself if you have any interest at all. It will be worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: I've been reading the negative reviews and I honestly agree with them. From an outsider's perspective, this is a no-brainer. But if you've already played the original game, then I don't think this is worth your time/money.Almost all of the new content just relies on "haha meta" and "haha bucket", which left me pretty underwhelmed, being someone that saw everything the original release had to offer multiple times (and once again today), and considering the delays (which are understandable when this is on a different engine) as well as the hype behind this, since the promotion made it seem like it would unveil a whole new story.As much as I loved the first game and kind of enjoyed <1h of the new content, I still can't say anything positive about this.

_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made.It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone, for the stone into which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted, offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement. You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may become more, so much more than you were before.If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, it is this: What a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience. It leaves me hopeful that as a community - as a world - There is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the "New content" area at the start is only accessible once.No chance to see it again, for shame.Well, I think i have seen everything this "game" has to offer at this point.More dialogue, but not a lot of new "areas" to see. What a shame.For a "game" that calls itself a 2/sequel, i feel like I only got a third to a half as much as the game from 2013.A lot of it feels like repeated jokes of the same jokes in the game that's already there.Was hoping for NEW jokes, but instead of we get retelling of the same jokes.The "blue" ending however did surprise me a little more, expecting MC, getting FW and RL instead did surprise me.The bucket trope wore out 5 minutes into the gag. After that it was just more annoying then funny.The jokes felts forced. And the whole "review & skip" ending felts like it dragged on way to long.I'm happy that the secret escape pod ending got a tiny touch up if you bring the bucket, and the effects of doing that ending.

Crows Crows Crows made an absolutely amazing remake of the original Stanley Parable, and it was well worth the delays.The new choices and endings are great as well. See you in 10 years and thank you for making this awesome game, Crows Crows Crows.

_childDocuments_.review: Just know that this is NOT a joke review, nor will I be providing spoilers of any sort. Everything can be taken seriously and trusted, since I know there is some BS and misinformation going as far as what the "game is really about".First, just to get this out of the way, if you've played the Stanley parable and you want to know how much new stuff is present? Well do you remember how much the original had? This version has a little over double the content if I had to estimate, and thankfully there is a way to skip right to the new stuff.Alright, to everyone else: The Stanley parable is a meta-narrative comedy. I won't go into too much details for fear of spoiler, as the plot and happenings of this game are everything with this game.However, without spoilers I will say this game can get a little creepy, has a few tense moments and such. But let's be clear,  alright? There are no real jumpscares unless you are high (and everything scares you when you are high), nothing worthy of such anyway. One or two things that might creep you out momentarily, but that's it. And its only momentary. The game is supposed to be funny, and for the most part it certainly is.Minor spoiler for those who are getting unnerved when playing or watching the game, still vague but here to reassure you a little:Still a great game, had more than a few laughs, worth getting for sure if you have a good sense of humor, particularly the British kind.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: At first I felt unsure about this new version, but the more I played, the more I was made aware of a mighty bucket's worth of new content for veteran players of the 2013 version. (thanks for the discount to veterans, and reasonable regional pricing, too!)There's quite a lot to search for, if you have the patience to comb through repeating many steps to experiment with the alterations. For new players, it's practically an infinite hole's worth of content.If you never played the 2013 release before, this is even more worth of your time. If you already did, it's a bit repetitive and tiresome in some areas (if you remember most of it, like I did) but still quite enjoyable, witty and thoughtful - just not as intoxicating as the first time (though the bonus item for veterans helps spice up the classic scenes and endings). Would've been welcome to have a bit more new content and more of the cutting room floor content - it's a bit lacking. Writing and narration is still top notch, though. The title doesn't lie, this is indeed an ultra deluxe version of The Stanley Parable. There's quite a few bugs right now (had to lower my resolution and turn v-sync on to engage on the phone ending with the "veteran" item in hand, otherwise no prompts appeared... and a few other problems - I imagine these will be ironed out very soon).If I had to nitpick - I kinda wish there was a skip button to skip some of the narrator's ramblings. Maybe next game?Now, off to get the 10 year achievement legitimately. Forget about that tuesday one, though. You guys are crazy.

_childDocuments_.review: I get the joke about modern remaster and remakes, but i still paid 14 euro for this and for nothing (edit: actually would be better said "not much more"). I think for people that already owned the game it should have been 80% discount. All the new content is fun, but super derivative, not really what stanley parable was. it's more some meta commentary on the game which really don't go anywhere. Moreover they are mostly different endings to the same one in the original, so not even the fun of finding them, i already knew how.I am ok with spending the money, because the devs are great, but i'm at least going to leave a negative review. Don't care that they rebuilt the game in unity, it looks excactly the same, with all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ pixelated textures (like the one over the Chianti bottles). For people that didn't own the original, the price is fair though.Can't wait for this review to be in The Stanley Parable 3

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game to rate. It's a story, most of all. An experience for the player more than the character in the game. It will mess with your head, make you smile, make you concerned and much more.And it's like the original, but better, bigger and more confusing.+ Still looks the same.+ Works on all resolutions/ratios without issue.+ LOTS of extra content compared to the original.+ Has more detail/complexity than you'd think.- The enjoyment will have to end at some point.- Some achievements are REALLY hard.Verdict: Buy it. It's worth it. Also, play the free game, partially by the same maker: Dr. Langeskov, The Tiger, and The Terribly Cursed Emerald: A Whirlwind Heist

_childDocuments_.review: Stanley Parable 12: Stanley's Enormous Didgeridoo is the greatest game since Stanley Parable 11: Stanley Versus Baby. I'm honestly amazed by how this series has been going for 12 games and still going strong with the hilarious commentary on gaming tropes that it has always offered. It never gets old. From the first time I stepped out of the door of Employee 427's office, saw those wonderful "Get Well Someday" balloons, and grabbed my bucket, I knew this would be the perfect gaming experience, and now, on the 12th game in this series, I feel just as enamored.

_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: Has 2 or 3 great sequences on par with the original Stanley Parable and Beginner's guide featuring great environments and gags, but the new content then quickly devolves into you repeating endings from the original game centering around a single joke that gets old fast. Always happy to have more Stanley Parable but I can't see how this took so long or why I'd drop 16 bucks on it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: From the From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe? Such a revolutionary step forward of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made.It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone, for the sins into which Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted, offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgment. You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may become more, so much more than you were before.If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, or is this: What a fortune, a privelage, a joy it is to have had such an experience. It leaves me hopeful as a community - as a world - There is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we could ever dream of in our wildest,  most ambitious visions for a brighter future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: To all those who cheated to get the 10 year achievement - You disgust myself as well as the narrator. You ruined the whole point for this achievement to even be here. We should have just made the description give the cheat so it wouldn't matter in the end, but at that point, why even have the achievement? Congratulations, you can utilize basic computer settings! I hope each of you who has cheated us out of this one glorious and tough achievement to obtain legitimately will always have an uncomfortably warm pillow on both sides forevermore.

Though what even counts as a sequel? Does it count as a sequel if it's got a copy of the original game stuck inside it or does that just make it a huge game sized DLC for the original game? Of course you're wondering if this actually is the Stanley Parable 2 but you know they'd never be so gouache as to actually tell you if this was the Stanley Parable 2.(Hint: it's *probably* the Stanley Parable 2. Just buy it already.)

_childDocuments_.review: I had watched youtubers play this game when the original Stanley Parable was out, I then heard about the ultra deluxe version and patiently waited.  I currently am enjoying this version very much, I love all the gags/jokes and paths that you can follow.  This game is very fun if you have a free day.  My only issue is that I wished that there were more achievements, specifically for each time the game force resets.  It would be nice to be able to keep track of the endings you've completed and not just the ending you get if you listen to the narrator.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: Don't read or watch any spoilers. This game is best experienced for yourself and an absolute blast! Crowns Crowns Crowns, thank you so much for this masterpiece, it deliveres such a grand experience, full of exciting new possibilities. I can feel it right now. Just Stanley and the narrator, exploring the office together!
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: For but a brief moment in time I could experience the joy of jumping. People would ask why I would jump so and I could, finally, after all these years, say that I, (username), were to be jumping for joy! Such a long time I had gone, looking at the joy that was stuck up there, the top shelf that I in my small stature could almost-reach-but-not-quite. Then, for a few moments, I had achieved it. I had joy, and I had jumped for it. The Stanley Parable Ultra Deluxe's new content was worth the wait. I could jump. Would jump again, such amazing content.Wait there's more?
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: The Stanley Parable is one of the classics that you should play. Ultra Deluxe is pretty funny and adds a lot of Meta-Commentary on the first game and other aspects of videogames and the industry in general. The only problem with this is that the game is pretty short. Still, The game is definitely worth but not 20€. So maybe pick it up on sale. To the day of this review the game is on summer sale for 14,73€ which i think its a pretty fair price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE The Stanley Parable. It truly is a frontrunner for my favorite game of all time. I had no reason to buy the game originally because I had seen several people play through it, but when I found out my friend had never experienced it in any capacity, I was thrilled buy Ultra Deluxe, and it has been a wonderful experience getting to watch him experience it for himself for the first time. This game makes me laugh out loud at times, and actually shed tears in others. It's a brilliant game that I cannot recommend enough
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for myself, and giving it another try, I saw that it was much more than I once thought. I had learned to love this version of the game instead of the previous. I also appreciate the fact that they took my review into consideration and put a skip button in. It made the game complete.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to mention that the first version of the Stanley Parable is truly a masterpiece! Now, with the Ultra Deluxe version, this game has been elevated to a new level of excellence. The addition of new content and improved graphics seamlessly integrate with the already captivating gameplay, providing a fresh experience for both fans of the original and newcomers alike. The Ultra Deluxe version is an absolute must-play for anyone who seeks a thought-provoking journey into the nature of free will and choice.

Somehow on a different engine, the visuals still capture the feeling of uncertain isolation with its industrial and office environments. The new content is quite entertaining and expands on the concepts the original entries ever so elegantly put. All I need is an open world structure, co-op, seasonal content, skins, and more collectibles as I won't accept anything but. Never have I been so attached to a bucket.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a story about a man named Stanley. Stanley worked from home, and in his spare time he played games, many, many games. And as he was browsing on YouTube and steam for a new game to play, he found The Stanley Parable. He loved it! The freedom of choice was Stanley's favorite thing in Video Gaming, and this game was perfect at displaying it. The narrator tried to tell him what to do, oh but that didn't last in Stanley's world. And in fact he enjoyed it so much, that after completing everything the game had to offer, every ending and every easter egg and every achievement. he sat down at his desk, and tyoed a review.

_childDocuments_.review: It is the most perfect game to ever exist because there is no need for any other game to ever exist. Stanley Parable is an 11/10 experience that provokes thought and high intellect that can only be found through the eyes of Employee 427. Although "things change", the gameplay is exactly the same every time.It's a novel approach to a game, but get this on sale or not at all.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting update to a solid game. Bonus points for .The "Content Warning" setting is very much appreciated, though I'd argue that it should be updated to add a couple of the new endings as well. (Particularly the  ending)Aside from that, whether you've played the original mod, played the 2013 release, or are brand-new to the game, you're in for a treat. My only advice is to go in as blind as possible, and to strap yourself in.Please note that the new content is hidden for the first few playthroughs, and that 100%-ing the game requires closing and re-opening the game a few times.

_childDocuments_.review: There is less here than I was expecting, but what is here is up to the standards of the original, and the original game sets a very high bar. I know it sounds greedy saying I expected more, especially since they practically rebuilt the entire original game in a new engine. But I'll be honest, the relative lack of "new" endings was a little disappointing. The game is marketed as "expanded reimagining" and thats exactly what you get. Changes to the original content via a clever gimmick along with a new path with some actual new content is what's delivered.However, as previously stated, everything that is here is on point. The Narrator is even better than last time, the humour and absurdity is on point and the commentary about linear narratives is just as good as the original.Totally recommend for new players, but returning players should probably wait until its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely pathetic excuse for a re-release. Nothing more than a pathetic corporate cash grab, with barely any meaningful new content added. Truly a disgrace to the original masterpiece that was The Stanley Parable. Even though I think every game is terrible compared to The Stanley Parable, this one was especially bad. A complete bastardization of what used to be the perfect video game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: If you were in the same boat as me, and were unsure as to whether or not it was worth buying despite playing the game already, let me tell you. It's worth it. While at first it seems like the same game, believe me when i tell you this game is basically a full fledged sequel. So many more endings, and it fits right in with the previous stuff in the game. Could not recommend this enough to both new and old players.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: Their early work was a little too new wave for my tastes, but when Beginners Guide came out in '15, I think they really came into their own, commercial and artistically. The whole game has a clear, crisp narrative, and a new sheen of consimante professionalism that really gives the experience a big boost.Hey Paul!
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever played. This game took me on a roller coaster of emotions and I enjoyed every second of it. I can't believe I've almost explored every path in the game and am dreading it coming to an end but cannot wait to replay it and discover even more secrets and easter eggs. The voice work done by Kevan Brighting was brilliant and moved me to tears multiple times! This game is truly a masterpiece and unlike any other game out there, I am thankful for everyone who worked on this game, it lived far beyond all my expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game. The mechanics of it are fun, the way the lore of it just bundles together like tangled yarn you have to unravel is amazing and I love the narrator! His voice when he's happy is just the best sound ever, I don't understand a lot of his big words but I like to listen to him, Narrators sass and wit make the game funny, and I love narrators reactions, sometimes I load up the game just to listen to him. I can't help but respond even though I know he's not real and he can't hear me. I sorta wish he was real, he'd make a good friend. :)

_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made. It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone for the stone into which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement. You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may become more so much more than you were before. If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, it is this: What a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience, it leaves me hopeful that as a community - as a world - there is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.

_childDocuments_.review: (MM/DD/YY)After replaying, I've decided to change my stance on the Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe. I've grown a lot as a person over the last two years; the game is excellent. The old content is here, which is wonderful, but the new content is something completely different. I wouldn't call this the Deluxe version of the game; it's more of a new game entirely, separate from the original Stanley Parable, that's deeply interwoven with an old one. The marketing of this game primed me for something different than what I was expecting, and that tainted my expectations.With that said, the best way to enjoy the game isn't actually to seek everything; that's what made me get sick on some aspects when I first played it. Not to mention I suffered from Gamer Brain; this game is priced more as a movie than a game.For archival's sake, I'm going to leave my old review up that had a thumbs down. The amount of content in this game is straight up not worth $25. Sure, the writing is fantastic, and that's the main selling point. While it is a fun game, it is not $25 of fun packed into four hours, as it is a $10 game at best. This is an apples to orange comparison, but Undertale is priced at $10 and contains just as amazing writing, not to mention that when you aren't engaged with its writing, it has its own gameplay loop that keeps you invested with its battle system.The original being $15 was already pushing it content-wise, but $25 for this game is honestly outrageous. The new stuff isn't even particularly high-quality, and a lot of the content is ported from the old game with a lot of broken lighting. It isn't a remake by any means, and honestly looks worse in many aspects than the original. If this is the joke of Ultra Deluxe, Crows Crows Crows clearly fails to understand what the developers find funny is not what the consumer finds funny.I also need to mention the control options are god-awful. You cannot set your mouse sensitivity to a precise decimal number, and even if you set it to 0, it still is very, very high,  if you use high DPI on the daily. Also, the game doesn't remember your rebound controls. I had to consistently and repeatedly set Left Shift to crouch on start up every single time, as using left ctrl to do so is awful and uncomfortable for me. It also doesn't allow you to rebind to mouse buttons, as I usually set Mouse5, a side mouse button, to crouch.  My opinions are blatantly in the minority, and I would hate to ruin the enjoyment of the game just because I go against the popular opinion. So stop reading now, unless you're looking for an in-depth look into my hatred of one of the new additions, plus mentions of a few other major things. If you're willing to accidentally read things though, then skip to the  beyond these paragraphs.You still here? Alright, your fault for learning about my hatred of The Bucket, and why The Bucket is a perfect mascot for this game's missed potential. If The Bucket was simply a gag for the New Content areas, fine, it'd be a great joke. Even if it appeared in the main game as just something a bit extra, like a very minor gag every time you pick it up, that'd be fine too. The issue is that The Bucket is a cop-out for writing new and interesting endings, as it just rehashes the old endings with "but you have a bucket now." Sure, many of the endings are  different than their non-bucket counterparts, with one of my personal favorites being one where you kill the bucket, but when you realize that the entire joke is that you have a calming and soothing bucket with you on the normal endings, it gets stale. Too much effort was put into the bucket, and I feel it really hampered the quality of the game. I would've much preferred if The Bucket was cut and put into the museum; the development resources the bucket took could've lead to more interesting areas. Not to mention that some of the bucket endings  to have choice, but in reality, there is no significant difference between the two. There are funny moments with the bucket, and they definitely are funny at first. But I noticed I started to laugh less and less with each Bucket ending I got, as the joke got stale. It isn't a running gag; it is an ordinary gag forcefully put on stage against its will repeatedly, and you can feel its silent plea to be taken off stage more and more every time it goes on. The Bucket is the perfect example of when an idea goes too far and becomes too expansive.To conclude this rant, The Bucket feels like an incredibly lazy way to add new content. Ultra Deluxe had so much potential to expand the original humor of the original, while still being able to modernize it. One of the greatest strengths of this game is how explorable the game is; it always felt like there were more secrets to be discovered. More endings to achieve. More secrets to uncover. Ultra Deluxe only keeps that feeling for people who have never played the original; instead of more content, it is the same content with a different coat of paint, sometimes literally. The game of the Stanley Parable is that of exploration and figuring out where you haven't been; when you take that away, it's just a movie, except you're the one who moves the protagonist in a predetermined path. And the second half of the movie is same as the first half, but with The Bucket. - I'm done ranting now. I tried to make it more coherent; if I failed, oh well. Anyways, the actual conclusion:My thoughts on the game as a whole is that, while I still ended up being a fan of the game, the thing I ranted on and on about is still too big to sway my opinion into the red. I cannot recommend it, as while I enjoyed the game a lot, I didn't enjoy it enough to where it was worth $25. The only reason I didn't feel like I got scammed is because I got the game at a somewhat reasonable $15, as I owned the original. It is yet another mediocre remaster of an old game that looks a bit worse than the original. My final thoughts are is the same as my : Wait for a sale if you really want to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this are the reason why I wish Steam had an option for Mixed reviews, instead of forcing you to pick between either a thumbs up or a thumbs down.Because while I do think TSP Ultra Deluxe has a fair deal of good moments and clearly had a lot of effort put into it, I also think that ultimately, all this new content comes across as pointless and derivative, resulting in a game that feels bloated and unsure of what it's supposed to be doing, compared to the simplicity of the original release. The fact that I can't tell whether this is supposed to be the point or not makes this feeling all the more apparent.TSP Ultra Deluxe is basically the original game, with new content tacked onto it and with some graphical enhancements here and there (mostly better lighting in a few places). I think a major point of disappointment for me is the fact that, while the game does have quite a few new ENDINGS, it has very few new PATHS. I counted I think 4 new paths (one of which I'm not sure if it's bugged or supposed to be so... nonexistent), everything else is reusing the existing paths, all centered around the gag of "the same thing, BUT NOW WITH !!!". This is not at all what I expected when the trailers claimed to have new endings. I expected those new endings to come from new paths cleverly snuck into the existing environment of the game (like the aforementioned four), not... this.Considering the elaborate joke of the "" ending, I can't help but wonder if this is supposed to be intentional. A riff on how all those remakes and remasters lately are very pointless and either add very little or add stuff that dilutes the original experience. But, well, even if that was the intention, TSP Ultra Deluxe still commits that very mistake it's supposedly mocking, it just does so "ironically". If I smash my head with a hammer and say I'm doing it ironically, it doesn't change the fact that I'm smashing my head with a hammer, now does it?This is basically what TSP Ultra Deluxe comes across to me. A supposed parody that doesn't really know what it's trying to do, and feels bloated and unfocused as a result. And while I admit the game gave me a good 6 hours of looking around and curiously checking out the new content, in the end it left me feeling confused and disappointed. And that feeling is why I'm ultimately leaning more towards a thumbs down, since that's probably not a good feeling to have.

_childDocuments_.review: A good idea, but extremely short. After about four hours I had already made every decision I could think of, collected all the stanley figures, and unlocked the "epilogue". I also don't like the whole "New Content" and "The Stanley Parable 2" endings, as the only way to get those is to just play the other endings till a door shows up. On top of that, those endings have absolutely ZERO choice once you go through the door. You just walk and look at the exhibits, the only choice there was is to pick which balloon you like better but no matter what the narrator throws your decision away and picks the opposite balloon. After I had been playing for around four hours, I looked online to make sure I hadn't missed any endings. Some of the endings I read about online were completely far-fetched and without a guide there is no possible way to know that these endings even exist. For instance, there is one ending where you have to click on one of the computers, restart the game, click another computer, restart the game, click another computer, and click on stanley's computer to go to "hevan", where the only thing to do is press buttons and restart the game. Again, my biggest problem is how ridiculously short it is, as you can see I have 5 hours and have already near 100%ed the game. Would probably like it better if it was much cheaper, maybe five bucks, but twenty-five dollars is way to much for this short game. If this is the ultra deluxe version, I can't IMAGINE how short and cruddy the original is.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an incredible addition to the original. Being almost 10 years old, I think it was about time we saw some new additions. The humor and wit of all the new endings is just great. Revisiting the old endings and getting to experience this stupidly funny story is awesome as well. The only gripe I kind of have is it being $25. For basically the same game with 4 hours of new content, I wish it was more like 15-20$ but it's fine honestly. I like supporting them as a company.The new storyline is funny and adds lots of good jokes to laugh at. I like that the bucket lets you redo all of the old endings with a slightly new twist. I also really appreciated them changing the Portal and Minecraft to 2 new games. Some people have been upset about the change, but its been a long time and I like the inclusion of new gags for them.All in all, great game. I recommend it a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the story of a man named Stanley.Stanley worked for a company in a big building where he was Employee #427.Employee #427's job was simple: he sat at his desk in Room 427 and he pushed buttons on a keyboard.Orders came to him through a monitor on his desk telling him what buttons to push, how long to push them, and in what order.This is what Employee #427 did every day of every month of every year, and although others may have considered it soul rending,Stanley relished every moment that the orders came in, as though he had been made exactly for this job.And Stanley was happy.And then one day, something very peculiar happened.Something that would forever change Stanley;Something he would never quite forget.He had been at his desk for nearly an hour when he had realized not one single order had arrived on the monitor for him to follow.No one had shown up to give him instructions, call a meeting, or even say 'hi'. Never in all his years at the company had this happened, this complete isolation.Something was very clearly wrong. Shocked, frozen solid, Stanley found himself unable to move for the longest time.But as he came to his wits and regained his senses, he got up from his desk and stepped out of his office.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game about art and why people create art and consume art. It's a game about games. It's a game about nostalgia. It's a game about modern games with broken features, collectibles, and iterative/gimmicky "new content", which the bucket is a metaphor of. It's a game about cheap re-releases of games. It's a game about greed and the video game industry. It's a game about humans clinging on to the past and wanting sequels of things. It's a game about Stanley.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe The Stanley Parable : Ultra Deluxe? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made. It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone for the stone into which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement. You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may become more so much more than you were before. If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable : Ultra Deluxe, it is this...What a fortune, privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience, it leaves me hopeful that as a community - as a world, there is time for us to become our greater selves, as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: nothing to say but wow. just wow. i played this game a while back, and i did not know anything about the previous game nor about this one. this game made me want to get on my computer every single hour of the day. figure out the puzzles, keep finding new endings, and see what more the game had to offer. it was an extremely fun experience and i'm glad i bought it. 10/10 would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just absolutely perfect, it fit's a sequel in a way that you would never expect a sequel to be I absolutely love and it'll go down as one of my favorite games of all time! I absolutely recommend it to anyone who has or hasn't played the orginal Stanley Parable. Seriously there is no better way to describe why or what the game is about other than to just play it yourself! It absolutely astonishing 10/10!!(SPOILER WARNING, DO NOT READ AHEAD IF YOU HAVE NEVER PLAYED THE GAME, MAJOR SPOILERS AHEAD, YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!!!!)(SERIOUSLY I AM SPOILING THE GAME, DO NOT READ AHEAD IF HAVE NOT PLAYED THE GAME TO IT'S COMPLETION) (fine then have it your way, you have been warned...):I absolutely hate the dumb new bucket!I really utterly despise it, it is just the worst mechanic in the entire game of The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe! It really ruined the game for me, the bucket is not at all funny, he is evil, and even in the expo hall I absolutely hated the bucket that I didn't even grab him (he/her/they whatever this bucket's pronouns are)! I hate them, I hate that she is a crucial part of the sequel I wish that he would simply be erased entirely from the game and have a new expansion be made from the ground up where Stanley actually goes to a bookstore with the narrator, and the narrator buys him a copy of "Office Working for Dummies"! Now that is what I would throw my money at, not just a stupid boring old grey bucket and a bunch of dumb altered endings! (Some endings aren't even different, some are just simple edited versions with a dumb stupid bucket edited into the picture!) Quite honestly, if it wasn't for the fact the narrator is holding me against my control, I wouldn't recommend this at all to anyone! I would not want my friends to go through the same disappointment that is The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe. Seriously I do not recommend this game at all, I hate it; I hate it! Seriously I hate this game. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS GAME AT ALL, IT IS NOT WORTH THE MONEY, PLEASE DON'T BUY IT! I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS GAME. PLEASE HELP I AM BEING FORCED TO RECOMMEND THIS GAME SEND HELP MY IP ADRESS IS 192.-!..Woah what happened there, it must've been those new 5G towers messing with my head once again! Anyways I truly love this game and the bucket. In fact I love the bucket so much I am happily married to the bucket and did not at all despise it ever. Goodbye now, nothing to see here...!

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game is invigorating. It has to be one of my favorite games ever made. The original game had such a big impact on me and my imagination, on what I though possible, when I was a child watching it being played on Youtube. Now, finally having the ability to play it for myself has proved to be even better than I ever imagined. Watching it and playing it are 2 different experiences, both of which I will not forget. Apart from that, The Narrator truly makes the whole game. I absolutely adore him. Sometimes, even though I've found most endings, when I'm having a bad day ill hop on and play The Stanley Parable for a while, simply because although the game-play can be repetitive, the Narrator's voice fills you with nostalgia. And quite frankly I find him hilarious. 10/10 Game. One for the Hall of Fame.

_childDocuments_.review: This game builds on the hilarious narrative in such a fun way. Each new ending and the dialogue that comes with it was always fun to come across, especially once you meet Bucket. Bucket is kind, loving, my best friend, my compatriot, and my other half. I put stickers on its bare bucket body, held a press conference with it, and I fell into a void of space with it. We may drift apart, and Bucket may even be a war criminal with unseen untold amounts of power, but I can never leave the office without it.If you can read this, I love you, Bucket.

Thank you guys for creating such a wonderful experience that was both fun and thought engaging. It was on my bucket list so I am so glad that I got to play it before I kicked the bucket.But honestly guys this game is great and I'd recommend playing it a lot even if you've played the original. Both are fantastic games that have brought much fun to my life. Thank you Crows Crows Crows.

_childDocuments_.review: Is that it?  Surely that's not all the new content.  There has to be something else, right?  I have to say, initial impressions of this game are not positive.  It's just elevators and jumping!  Is this what passes for 'exciting new content'?  If this is new content then I could just read you the whole dictionary - there's 20 hours of new content right there!  Hell, I could count to 30 trillion!  You could put that on the box:  "The Stanley Parable:  Ultra Deluxe, now with over a thousand hours of new content!"You've got to be kidding me!  This is what happens when greedy video game developers with no respect for their fanbase rush a cheap expansion to market for no reason other than to make an easy dollar.  And don't get me started on the level of craftsmanship that's gone into it!  In fact, I'm looking right now at the game's achievements and it's hard to believe one of them actual says "Test Achievement, Please Ignore."  What quality assurance department signed off on this?  I'm infuriated and I'm offended!  I intend to find these people on Twitter and hold them personally accountable.  It's my fault.  I built up too much anticipation around the new content, I'm afraid.  It could never have lived up to such expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: This game is boring.I had not played the original Stanley Parable, however I had watched playthroughs of it on youtube. The writing wasn't clever nor fantastic, but it didn't need to be. The point of the original game was to subvert the various narrative tropes of video games in a funny way. In this, it only needed good writing and to make each of the paths unique in their own way. On the surface, Ultra Deluxe continues down this path, having good writing and subverting more tropes, though this time being more meta about it. However, it fails, and it fails in a rather unexpected way.The game is boring. Seriously boring.Many of the highlights of the original game weren't the clever, subversive writing, nor the amazing creativity. What made the game so popular back then, and gives it most of its popularity, was the incredible charm of the game.  Whenever the game had something to say and a trope to subvert, it always did it in a charming way that stuck with you, long after the game itself was over.This charm is lacking in the new content that's part of Ultra Deluxe. I should note, I've only gone through two paths so far, and both the prologue and these two paths demonstrate this problem. The prologue is a long, subversive joke about professional game reviews contrasted with steam reviews that goes on far, far too long. I would have no problem with the length, but there's no real charm to the sequence. All you had was the narrator talking on and on about reviews and being ironic about one of the review's reccomendations, but the review is only a review. It's not a silly review, it doesn't cause the narrator to respond in an unexpected way, there are no hidden paths to subvert the entire sequence. It's just the narrator talking. And that wouldn't be so bad if the narrator's dialogue was charming, but it isn't. To avoid spoilers, I won't go into details, but it's akin to listening through a boring history lecture, and the joke is that you're sitting through it.Once the prologue is done, you then get into the second prologue, which makes fun of the idea of a Stanley Parable sequel. This part of the game does have some genuine charm to it, but much of it is simply boring or meta. This second prologue shows part of why there isn't much charm to this new content: Many of the jokes aren't funny. They are only references to trends in the game industry or references back to the Stanley Parable. This would be fine, even subversive, but the game makes no attempt to subvert these jokes (or, even worse, they make the subversion the joke itself). It only presents them to you, and gives you no options for how to approach the joke. There are two exceptions, , but the exceptions aren't enough to save the whole.Finally, I tried two of the new content paths. They were reliant on references to the original game, and lacked much of the charm of the original paths. Much of the jokes are simple references the game either doesn't subvert or only subverts by making a reference. Whether or not you are known for subversion, the subversion must have something to make the subversion worth it, and all that was here was nothing. All I was left doing was trundling along, not engaged with the narrative, because I knew the narrative had nothing for me. And I was left feeling bored the whole way through.A lot of other negative reviews talk about how they were disappointed or underwhelmed. They say this as fans of the original Stanley Parable, of which I do not include myself as I have only watched videos of the original game, and had not kept up with the news surrounding Ultra Deluxe. I have no investment in the original and I lack any fond memories of it. It's because of this that I had no expectations of a fantastic, subversive game. All I wanted was a good story with charm. And there is no charm here. only meta jokes about a game it refuses to let go of.I am not frustrated, angry, depressed, or disappointed. I am only bored. This game is just boring. Perhaps that's the worst thing a work of art can be.
