_childDocuments_.review: If you're a mega-fan of the Expanse, you'll get some enjoyment. The setting is beautifully realized, and it is fun walking/flying around interiors that could have been ripped right out of the universe.The characters are just ok. The story has potential but fizzles and doesn't say anything of much importance for the characters or the setting. But most damning, the gameplay is boring, mostly walking around empty ships looking for interactables to get voice lines from. Action scenes are painful quick time events that begged for a simplistic shooting gallery minigame instead. And the choices you make lack the reactivity that make Telltale games worth playing. It is exceptionally short, barely worth a sale price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those times I really wish Steam had a "Thumb sideways" review...Are you a fan of The Expanse and you just want to live in the world for a few more hours? This game is *GREAT* for just sitting and enjoying the atmosphere and story. Two thumbs way up.If that's not you though, then you will probably not enjoy this. It doesn't have much really in the way of gameplay, there was I think exactly 1 interesting/challenging puzzle, and it really expects you to understand the world of The Expanse.So overall: It Depends. *I* enjoyed it. I do wish it had more, you know, game. But as far as walking simulators go it was well done, it played well on my Steam Deck, and as a major Expanse fan I quite enjoyed the story. It took 7.5 hours to get through the entire game + DLC. I'll probably play again later, after I've forgotten some of it, to try and get the last few achievements, but there really isn't a *TON* of game here either, so waiting for the sale isn't a bad plan. But once again, despite my general thumbs-down for most players, if you love The Expanse and you just want the story: Two thumbs way up!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give Telltale a thumbs up and Deck Nine a thumbs down.  Telltale did a wonderful job, per usual.  This was also the best looking Telltale game I've ever seen.  The mechanics of the game were fun - they did a superb job on the maneuvering and magnetic boots.  And as always it was an absolute pleasure to see your choices compared to others.  So why can't I thumb this up?  THE STORY WAS AWFUL.  Full disclosure, I never read the books or saw the actual show, but Good Grief it was BORING and laughable.  It was hard to take anything seriously.  While some of the accents were interesting, there were just certain segments where it was a joke the things that were happening.  The illuminati eye and the pedo-triangle symbol showing up hand in hand put the stamp of idiocy on this, the characters almost entirely being females with throat cancer sounding voices and the ceaseless message of anti-male propaganda was a bore.  The characters, even the ones that seemed interesting, never went beyond a little toe dip in the pool of development.  Instead, the dialogue devoted to quips and sass against men.  I am so sick of these ideologies flooding entertainment when instead we could've had some good story telling.  You can have a bad-a** female character - one who even shows up men - without converting the entire story to nothing more than that shtick.  By the end I sincerely could not care any more who lived or died.  The cast was awful.  Even with great voice acting, the characters were just so..... UGH.  There were segments of the game where you had literally nothing to do for upwards of 5 minutes but sit and listen.  I think in total I might've pressed 20 buttons through all 5 chapters.  I really would love to see Wolf Among Us 2 than this hot garbage story.  Sincerely, my life would've been better not having toiled through this.  This game, the story, the writing, was just too bad to give this a thumbs up.  I will never play this again, or any future expansions beyond Archangel which I bought with it, unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed the game (for the most part) through the first four episodes. Eps 1-3 were great, however the game comes to a screeching halt in episode 4. It's a long, boring slog. I couldn't wait for it to end. Thankfully it appears to pick up again in episode 5. But overall, I like the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it was really good - but really short. If you like the show this is a great game and you'll understand the lore. If you don't know the lore, it's still a fantastic story, and will serve as a wonderful introduction to the series.My problem with this game is that it's $25 for 5 hours of gameplay, seems like a real stretch right now. Maybe get it on sale but I'd BARELY recommend it at this price with the amount of content.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to hit this with the thumbs up, but my review is actually mixed.If I had not already been a huge Expanse nerd, this would have been a down-thumb.  I've read the books, watched the show, so of course I wanted to gobble this up as well.  However, this is a terrible game if you're looking for a one-off.The characters are largely one-dimensional; this is where prior knowledge of the Expanse universe comes into play.  Even the characters that are truly one-dimensional are uplifted by prior experience with the universe.  A Belter isn't just a Belter once you've experienced Belter culture across an entire novel series and a six season show.As for gameplay; it's Telltale.  It's basically a movie, you just have to walk sometimes.  Fun for some folks, horrible for others.  Stacked against classics like The Walking Dead - this measures short.  However, if you're a fan of the Expanse universe, then it's a pretty nice trip down memory lane, some extra info prior to the story that currently exists, and an enjoyable experience.  For context, I just beat the game in 5.4 hours.  It did leave me regretting some decisions and wondering about the outcome of others, so the writing is definitely decent, as expected from Telltale.  All in all this seems like it may have been a junior dev project that got greenlit; there just isn't enough there.Will also caution gamepad users that this game, despite saying it's best enjoyed with a controller (and believe me it really is) is seemingly very hostile towards gamepads.  Mine worked throughout, but I constantly dealt with my glyph prompts having seizures and throwing out keyboard bindings.  The frequency of the stutter was enough that it made it pretty hard to figure out which button I was meant to be pressing sometimes, mainly during QTEs.  I did my due diligence researching this bug and found a couple of promising posts but they were always about a similar-enough-but-different issue, so I never did discover a fix.All in all - 6/10, 10/10 if you're already an Expanse fan.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of The Expanse having read all the books and watching the show and this story holds up as part of the franchise. _childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the story and the characters, which are Telltale's strengths usually. While I do wish there was more time with the crew, they were all pretty fleshed out in the short amount of time they were present. They all had distinct personalities and interesting backstories. The story itself was simple, but it had a lot going on in the background about the universe they live in too. I think the game would have made a good movie; it had good pacing, action, humor, friendship, romance, a good score, and well-written characters. The gameplay was nice too; I liked the zero gravity parts and exploring overall. I've never watched the show, but the atmosphere captured in this game has me interested enough to try watching it. It gives dark sci-fi vibes. I won't spoil it, but the connection the main character makes with another crew member adds stakes to the game and makes it more exciting. There aren't a lot of "big" choices that seem to alter the story much, but a lot of little choices add up to make a significant difference. Overall I enjoyed the game, but I wish it was longer so I could be with these characters more. It's definitely worth a playthrough or two!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I've given up playing this game.  Which I'm sad about, as I love The Expanse.  I've read the books and I'm watching the TV show for the second time.There are 2 main things that are wrong with this game.1) It may be me, but I've consistently lost the saved game when playing the episodes.  I've played through chapter 2 three times, and I played through chapter 3 and half way through chapter 4, but the only saved game listed is in the middle of chapter 3.  Which brings me to:2) Nothing is skippable. Cut scenes, dialog, audio logs - you have to sit through everything, no matter how many times you've already played the episode.The user interface, or rather the user experience, is awful.  I've got 5 saved game slots showing, but I've no idea how to use them.  Nothing I do ever seems to use the other slots, even when they change to indicate they are the 'current slot'.When you start the game, it always has the options 'New Game' or 'Exit', but doesn't include a 'Continue' option until you switch to the 'Saves' tab, and then exit it.  I can't believe that no one involved in the development of the game ever thought "this isn't very intuitive", or "let's make sure that people don't lose where they were in the story, as there's no way to skip anything".Another minor gripe is that there's no native support for ultra-widescreen monitors - I had to find a mod and install it, and it's still not seamless, as some things blank out the centre of the screen, but keep rendering the left and right sides.Overall, there are some things I like about the game, but the (easily fixable) user experience issues have led me to abandon playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: This is all I wanted from a Telltale game. Great license, well written characters, good choices. _childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Well, Telltale games are just as janky as they've always been, so don't expect that to be different if you didn't like how they played before.Unlike their other games though, you get some (still janky) zero G sections. Oh, and there's nigh impossible to find side objectives, but they don't seem to block off key story at least at this point in the plot.But, flaws aside, it's great to get to spend more time with Cara Gee's Camina Drummer. Whilst stylised in typical TT style, the character's fairly true to Cara's TV portrayal. Even certain mannerisms from Cara's Drummer is intact, like the way she almost always stands in a wide "at ease" stance when she's standing still.Shohreh Aghdashloo's Chrisjen Avasarala makes an appearance too (and I look forward to playing her expansion), but apart from that, it looks like most of the voice cast aren't from the series.Glad it's finally on Steam. _childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: The game felt stiff. Not just the characters and their animation, but overall. I mean, in the first 20 minutes (maybe even less) you see multiple characters, but they do not feel distinct at all, and feel like robots, even when they try to joke. What's worse, the story they are trying to follow is just... Boring. I did not get into the original show, because I felt like it had too much politics than anything else, but at least the first episode grabbed my attention for some time.In the game, though... It's just too slow. Don't get me wrong, sometimes it makes sense to have a slow start, nothing wrong with that, but here it feels too tedious. What adds to that is how empty and sterile everything feels. As if there are no real details. Maybe it is because it is space (although the show had much more clutter around), maybe it's because the art is not using cell-shaind that worked great for previous Telltale games, but it just feels too clean, like most modern movies.Even the gameplay feels worse. Seems like you only get 2 choices for everything, and they seem to have even less meaning than in other games. But the the way how character movement feels is extremely outdated. It reminded me of "Dreamfall: The Longest Journey", but that's a game from back in 2006, it was low-budget and still felt much better.I guess I just expected too much. I liked most of the Telltale games, even Jurassic Park one, which a lot of people disliked. I knew they were far from perfect, but the writing was generally good, the story grabbed you and did not let go till the end. They were exciting. But not this one. Or maybe I got spoiled by all "Life is Strange" games.

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings, fellow gamers and enthusiasts! I'm Hiro Blazeheart, a 35-year-old avid gamer with a unique blend of human and wolf-like traits. Today, I'll share my in-depth review of "The Expanse: A Telltale Series". With my best friend Kiba Snowpaw, an Alpha Ice Wolf from the ice world of HowlStrom, we've ventured deep into this game's universe.My journey in "The Expanse" began with anticipation. The game's setting, a rich tapestry of political intrigue and survival in space, immediately struck a chord. As a gamer who has seen countless worlds, the emotional depth and drama in this title were like a siren's call.You play as Camina Drummer, a character who embodies resilience and leadership. Her journey through the Belt is fraught with moral dilemmas and life-or-death decisions, resonating deeply with my own values of loyalty and camaraderie, as reflected in my amber eyes.The zero-gravity exploration is a thrilling experience. Navigating through shipwrecks and making split-second decisions added a layer of realism and urgency. It felt like I was truly part of Drummer's crew, facing the harsh realities of space.Telltale's storytelling prowess shines here. Each character is meticulously crafted, allowing for deep connections and emotional investments. The voice acting, particularly by Cara Gee, adds a layer of authenticity, making every interaction memorable.The choices in "The Expanse" are weighty, often leading to palpable tension. This reflects the unpredictable nature of the Belt, where every decision can lead to unforeseen consequences. It's a testament to the game's ability to immerse you completely in its world.However, no game is without its flaws. Some technical issues and the predictability of the Telltale formula occasionally broke the immersion. Yet, these moments were fleeting, overshadowed by the game's overall excellence.The conclusion of the game left me yearning for more. It was a bittersweet moment, realizing that the journey with Drummer and her crew had come to an end.Personal ReflectionReflecting on my time with "The Expanse", I'm reminded of the cold, starlit skies of HowlStrom. The game, much like the tales of my ice world, weaves a story of survival, loyalty, and the unyielding spirit of adventure.In conclusion, "The Expanse: A Telltale Series" is a remarkable journey that resonates deeply with the heart and soul. As both a gamer and a denizen of HowlStrom, I wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone seeking a profound, emotionally charged experience. Remember, in the depths of space, like in the icy realms of HowlStrom, every choice shapes your destiny.

_childDocuments_.review: A Stellar Interactive Experience for Sci-Fi EnthusiastsThis game is perfect for those who enjoy kicking back and watching an interactive movie unfold. Yes, this is a Telltale game, and while they have a storied history, The Expanse stands out as a stellar addition to their lineup. As a big sci-fi fan, I thoroughly enjoy the series, and now being part of it in an interactive way is pretty rad.Floating around in a desolate ship or even an asteroid is an experience that’s both eerie and exhilarating. The game's atmosphere captures the vast, lonely beauty of space, and the narrative keeps you on the edge of your seat. Telltale has mastered the art of the cliffhanger, and they deploy it to great effect here. Each episode leaves you eagerly anticipating the next, much like a particularly suspenseful binge-worthy series.But beware, this is not just a game; it's an emotional rollercoaster. You'll find yourself making tough decisions, only to second-guess them later. And just when you think you've got things under control, the game throws another curveball your way. In space, no one can hear you scream—except maybe the neighbors if you're really into it. If you're a fan of The Expanse or just love a good sci-fi story, this game is a must-play. Great game, great story, and great fun—just try not to float away.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this a sideways thumbs. It's not a bad game but it is a disappointing - especially if you're a fan of the series. The story itself is a cool prequel to the Expanse story with the exception that if this event took place - it would imply Drummer knew at least the gist of protomolecule before Holden & his crew. That in turn would make you question why she never warned Fred Johnson when ♥♥♥♥ started hitting the fan. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯Sadly I enjoyed the Archangel DLC more than the actual Drummer story.  Game wise - I found it more interesting to make political decisions than floating in a ship graveyard scavenging. Chrisjen Avasarala's sassy no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ attitude and dialogue is entertaining. Most of the characters are underdeveloped storywise or too much of a trope. All the men are portrayed as weak or stupid. Waay too much "strong women" leading and making the decisions:Cox - a pointless character who just wants money. You'd hope by keeping him alive he'd do something more significant at the end but..nope.Rayen - an obnoxious bully who continually emotionally hurts his brother and makes poor decisions  (typical belter) Arlen - Simp. Dude needs to grow some balls.Virgil - I like him - He at least has more of a developed backstory but the muscles on that dude could easily and should have kicked more ass when a gun is pointing at him. Maya is a piss poor example of a Martian - if you've watched the show or read the books - Martian soldiers are considered strong, disciplined, and military oriented. They are also physically fit. Maya unfortunately is an emotional sentimental horn bag of anxiety that anyone could easily snap in half.  They should have taken notes from Bobbie Draper's personality.   Also the forced romance between her and Drummer was exhausting ( I as the player want the ability to choose who I want to romance, not just the choice whether to bang her for one night). I gladly let her die and would do it again. Some of the voice acting were subpar. I enjoyed the personality of Khan but her voice sounded too young for her appearance and the heavy wheezing from smoking 50 packs a day was grating on the ears. Also, I feel bad for Tousaint Zapata. _childDocuments_.review: Picked this up because it looked great. Only realized after an episode or two that it was based on a tv show I have never seen - but that's not why I ultimately have to say no.It's got some decent stuff going for it story and feels wise, and despite not knowing any of the backstory, was engaging enough that I knocked out the 10 hours of "gameplay" pretty quickly, but it's a bit of an oddity.There are a few plot choices along the way, but none of them seem to matter, not really sure because it wasn't really interesting enough to give it a 2nd go. It seems like they may have wanted to do more game-wise, because there are bits that just make no sense. For example, why do you scavenge supplies, when there is never any game use for them, or plot elements that build on them? "We're low on supplies" - yet scavenging supplies changes nothing and the whole conflict never really shows up again. Stuff like that. Seems like a waste of time, maybe these things were just there to stretch out the meager "game time".I imagine it strikes deeper for people who have actually seen the show (and I'll probably go watch it now) but I don't really think it's worth full price unless you're a huge fan. It's a pretty steep price for 10 hours of gameplay that really isn't gameplay (about 6-8 decisions per "episode" and a few arcade moments is about all you get). There is an astonishing amount of area to explore given how little "game" is actually present for any of it. most of your 10 hours will be spent floating through empty corridors. But, I can't really recommend it as a game. If you don't mind paying $5 each for 5 2-hour movies, or you're a big fan of the IP, then this may be right up your alley. Otherwise, I'd probably look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: ***WARNING: THIS REVIEW IS WRITTEN BY AN UNCULTURED ILLITERATE WHO DIDN'T WATCH THE SHOW OR READ THE BOOKS***Excruciatingly traditional plot structure with barely anything attached on. Episode 1. Reveal of the McGuffin. Episode 2. Introduction of the characters. Episode 3. Sudden crisis and panic. Episode 4. Protagonist' struggle and redemption. Episode 5. Victory against all odds. Streamlined storytelling by the book, is almost as interesting as watching some stray plastic bag riding the passing wind.Some may argue that most games' stories can be boiled down to the same number of steps, and while that might be true Telltale's The Expanse barely offers anything to its players in between reveals and progression of core elements of the story. Telltale's games usually feature iconic locations and scenes for each episode, Minecraft, GoT, TWD, Borderlands, most ones I played had them. But in this game you get: Generic prefab ship(comes in different sizes), Generic prefab space station(haunted variant included), main locations are recycled multiple times and seeing the same black abyss gets boring. But credits where it's due. The game technically offers more exploratory freedom compared to their other entities. Most episodes have these filler spacewalk moments which make up the majority of the game's playtime. You see that funny looking debris in the background? You can actually get behind of it. Not only that, inside of ships and stations you can even walk walls in zero G thanks to your trusty mag boots. Exceptional. Mind Boggling even. But worry not even if your mind is boggled to the point of 10 percent efficiency, they dumbed down the puzzles to the point of them being more fitting to the late stage dementia patients and preschool kids under 4yo.Usually games of this kind are used by the IP holder to drag in a new crowd of people and if that was indeed their goal in this case I wonder if they even managed to reach half of their internal expectation numbers. They were smart for taking Mr. Sweeney's Fortnight fund money for this.I still regularly see people from the internet getting surprised that Telltale is back from the grave despite the revival happening almost 6 years ago now. That by itself tells that they failed to reestablish themselves in the market and by looking at The Expanse(which is the result of them being assisted by another studio, Deck Nine), it seems like their future will continue to look grim.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. Telltale Games made some of my favourite games and I was really excited for this new venture. But this is not what I expected, and tbh I struggle calling this a finished experience. So much of the game feels empty. Let me elaborate - this is not the kind of emptiness you want to convey to your audience. Its not to empathize the void of space, it empathizes the emptiness of the game. There are so many mechanics that are just in the game, but have no connection to the overall experience. Sure I could collect the scavenge, but what is the point? As scavangers you would think that it would make a difference, like collecting money did in Tales from the Borderlands. But no, this is just some random collectible that has no influence on how things play out. Furthermore all of this game feels like a pilot to a much bigger game. Most of the episodes can be completed in an hour or two at most. But since almost nothing you do matters, there is no use in exploring the surroundings and getting to know the universe closer.  The character models are most of the time just meh, the voice acting is meh (i really cannot put into words how much the language of the 'belters' annoys me), and the characters themselves are bland.  None of them are memorable, except your love interest, but that is only because the scene with the music player legit made me shed a tear or two. The surroundings are usally quite nice, but if you expected another Telltale Games cartoonish style (that was my expection) you will be let down. The Expanse relies on a more mature look if you ask me, but I just felt like it was out of place.The Expanse is at best a mediocre 7 (more like 5) hour experience that doesn't come close to what Telltale Games used to be. I am deeply saddend by this and cannot in good conscience recommend this game to anyone, unless its in a sale.

The  gets a place in the game but clearly before anyone knows what it is. The game does add context by illustrating the mindset and gamble of people who intend to sell this stuff, especially if you know what happens eventually when it is sold to a private, greedy company. The DLC Archangel takes places around book 3, before the Callisto Incident and before the Free Navy. It contextualizes the actions of Avasarala and how they eventually connected to the Free Navy incident.I enjoyed both story arcs very much, being a die-hard fan of the series. I wish we could have had more of the  and more sci-fi-esque elements of this kind (while the game focuses more on the inner politics of the Belt), but I still loved the commentary it provided on later events of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game mechanics aren’t the most sophisticated or exciting, what really stands out for me is that lingering, warm feeling after finishing a great game—the kind that stays with you for days. The world of The Expanse was beautifully transported into the game and really pulled me in, and I felt like I was right there with the fantastic characters. The protagonist, with her amazing voice and attitude, was a highlight, and she’s surrounded by at least three other characters of the same caliber. For me, these well-developed characters easily outweighed any minor gameplay flaws.I don’t even think you need to have seen the series to fall in love with the world and its characters.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly well-crafted story! As a fan of The Expanse series, this game provided a fascinating look into the world before Season 1, with the rich storytelling that Telltale is known for. The gameplay is classic Telltale—easy to dive into and enjoy. Although hunting down all the hidden data logs was a bit challenging, the story itself was the real focus, which is always what I come to Telltale games for.I would highly recommend this to anyone who enjoyed The Expanse. This game captures the universe perfectly, and I wish there were more Telltale adventures set in this world, as there’s so much potential for new stories—even stories beyond the TV series’ final season.Drummer has always been a favourite character of mine, and the voice acting here truly shines. Her portrayal is brilliant, and getting Shohreh Aghdashloo’s DLC and the wonderful voice acting on top of that was like the cherry on top of an already excellent experience. The cast brings so much depth, making the characters even more relatable and compelling.Overall, this is a fantastic game—immersive, engaging, and a true treat for fans. It was an absolute joy to play! It has made me want to now go back and start from Season 1 again of the TV Series and reread the comics!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say, this game offers a wonderfully indulgent story experience. I’ve played several Telltales Games titles, and while they were enjoyable, none have captivated me quite like The Wolf Among Us. I was really hoping Telltale would release another game that could match or surpass that experience, and I'm still waiting.That said, this game is genuinely fun and engaging, with a compelling narrative that kept me hooked. I highly recommend giving it a try, especially if you appreciate a good story. It's worth experiencing, even if it’s just a taste!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game, love Telltales. Another great game to add to the list of great games they have done. The only thing I have about the game is that it wasn't long enough. Let's hope for more like this and maybe some remasters like TWD ect or maybe more seasons for TWD. (praying) or GOT Batman. I just want more. Great work guys keep it up
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive fan of the TV show of the same name, I Thoroughly enjoyed the game, although it is a tad on the short side. The game brought back the feelings of Telltales the walking dead, while bringing Unique mechanics to suit the universe of The Expanse. I highly Recommend if you are a fan of show or of Telltale games in general.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta admit it kind of hurts to give this a negative review; I'm a huge fan of Camina Drummer and the whole Expanse series and really felt like it was getting a lifeline through Telltale. After a few hits like Telltale Batman (1 & 2) and also Tales from the Borderlands, I had pretty high expectations. However, this is not what I think of as a Telltale game.Rather than refurbing their old engine they switched to UE5, which I suppose I get. However, they changed the gameplay too. There's a lot of walking around in labyrinthine environments, and critical decisions can depend on whether you spotted that *one odd thing* and thought to pick it up... aside from being an unwieldy dynamic it's zero for character development. After a while the whole thing just feels kind of jading, like a tech demo in the worst possible place. I'm pretty sore about it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Seems like a short game, however if you're a fan of The Expanse, you will truly love this epic storytelling experience. There's one particular music track during the game that draws you further into the game's already brilliant ambiance. If you play this with an open mind and with your own choices, you'll absolutely love it. As with all Telltale games, this is yet another masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Camina Drummer was one of my favorite characters on The Expanse, and if you liked her too you ought to consider this. But like most Telltale games, it's not much of a game and choices don't really feel  important. Think of this more like a nice-looking CGI miniseries about Drummer. From that perspective, it's pretty good.I'm two episodes in with three (and the Archangel minisode) to go. I'll update this review if my thoughts change at all - right now the story feels very much like the kind of B-plot Camina Drummer always got on the later seasons of the show.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Telltale's signature narrative-driven style. Set before the events of the series, the game follows Camina Drummer, a fan-favorite character, and explores tough moral decisions amid space conflicts. The gameplay emphasizes player choices, with intense dialogue options and interactive sequences. The game succeeds in capturing the tension and grit of The Expanse universe, though some moments can feel slow. It's a must-play for fans of the show who love story-driven adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Great game so far! Very detailed and immersive even on desktop ( Even better in VR! ). Plays smooth even in VR using UEVR. Loving flying through debris fields searching for gear and exploring. The story is exciting funny and scary... sometimes all at once! I never cared a lot for the show but the game has me hooked so far. I've only played a little into the 2nd episode. Games going to be longer than I thought it would... GOOD! Definitely recommend! SPECS: Ryzen 9, 32gb, 3060ti, ssd, Pico 4-Virtual Desktop-UEVR
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: It was fantastic to hear Cara Gee reprise her role as Camina Drummer. The game, however, is mostly paced slowly, which might not suit everyone’s taste. While it has its strong moments, it falls significantly short in terms of story and choices compared to “Star Trek Resurgence,” which I played just before. On the technical as well as on the QTE side, though, “The Expanse” is far superior. The playtime of not even 5 hours is also quite short. Despite these drawbacks, I still recommend it as a good game, and I look forward to a potential part two. 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I consider myself a fan of The Expanse, and this game feels almost like another season of the TV show, but more than a game it feels like an interactive movie, I don't think it's a bad thing on its own, but the fact that almost no matter what you do you end up getting to almost the same ending seems a bit boring to me. But from what I understand that's how this developer's games work.I still recommend the game for fans like me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: The expanse has good graphics, likeable characters , it has  good exploration for a point and click game and the salvagable items and data logs will give you more context.The story was only good in the first two episodes, episode 3 and 4 felt kind of flat for me and episode 5 was decent.Overall it's a good game of 7 over 10.Grab it with a nice discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the expanse universe, this was a fun and exciting journey a bit short but very enjoyable. The story was interesting but some actions/reactions didnt suite Drummer's character in some cases. Now where this game shines is the beautiful maps that the devs designed where you can explore them in zero G and learn a lot about the expanse lore and the complex politics inside of it.All in all i would rate this experience as an 8/10. Note: game goes very often on big sales. So that is the right time to pick it up
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely wait for this to go on sale.  Has all the right "Expanse" and "Telltale" vibes but it is extremely short.  You can see my hours on record.  And that was it.  The first couple of chapters are decent in length but after that they go very quickly.  Do not pay full price for this. But for less than $10 for the whole set, it's worth it.  (Stop phoning it in Telltale...you're custodians to great IP now show us you're worthy of it.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: It's like an interactive extension of The Expanse series. The game features top-notch acting, atmosphere, sounds, and environment. The narration is great, and while the story is good, it is not particularly remarkable, with a mediocre plot, but seamlessly fitting in The Expanse universe.I don't usually like Telltale games. However, this one, despite having Telltale in its name and being developed by another studio, suited me very well, leaving me wanting more!A must for The Expanse serie fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Basically the prequel to the TV-Series, detailing the journey of Camina Drummer before arriving on Tycho. It's a typical Telltale adventure, so it's more about making decisions which shape the way things play out rather than solving puzzles. To say much more would spoil the fun. The presentation is beautiful, although the locations being mostly space ship interiors are somewhat limiting in terms of graphical splendor. Voices and soundtrack are taken from the series and help immensely to draw you in right from the start.A fantastic game, especially for fans of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Mildly positive, this is too short with too few user interactions to REALLY be worthy of the title "game" - especially the 5th/final "chapter" which is very much of the "blink and you'll miss it" variety. While the graphics - especially space craft - don't dazzle, they are servicable. Which about described the first 4 chapters, now I think of it. For fans of the TV show and comics, at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: This game really requires context to enjoy. In specific because this version of Drummer is a product of the show The Expanse, having context of the show, not the books, is vital. This is most true for the ending which would come off as a dud if you didn't already know what happens next.Otherwise I enjoyed it, felt very close to The Expanse universe. Using a gamepad was much more enjoyable than using KBM for the zero-g sections. Its pretty short, I did the story and dlc in 6 hours. A second run to see the other outcomes would likely get that to 9 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry but NO... I cannot recommend this game. This feels like such a waste of a good theme. I just finished the last episode not even 10 mins ago so i'm still very much processing this. To keep this short Episodes 1-4 i liked but this last episode feels as if all my choices were taken away from me. Before i get into spoilers my final score is a 3/10. I would've given it a 5/10 but this last episode was really that bad in my opinion.    SPOILERS AHEAD!!! Alright the first 4 episode's the game floated from average to good. Episode 1 was the best for me. It had intrigue and tension. Drummer as the main character was performed well through out the episode and the series in general. Some of the other characters though.... was rough. Khan especially.  What the first episode did well it established the stakes of the world. Being a scavenger has its risks and this crew felt very patch worked together. I did not trust any of them. And that tension made every moment interesting. The decisions themselves had stakes cutting off Rayans leg or airlocking Cox both these decisions were great. KINDA WISH I HADN'T KILLED COX THOUGH LOL. He was voice acted beautifully. Now were getting into the MEH episodes 2 and 3. They both felt kind unimportant they could've been squeezed into a single episode. I think that would've made the pacing better. Honestly its hard to even remember what happened those episodes. I think i slept with Maya and that's about it lol. The ending of episode 3 kind redeemed itself just because Drummer was marooned and Maya died but beyond that nothing springs to mind. Episode 4 was much better than the last 2. This episode dives deeper into Drummer and her past. Which was fasinating. And there's this tension because shes on limited oxygen and needs to be saved by getting a signal out. However the ending of the episode kind of loses its footing and introduces characters that you have no real connection too. I had thought i missed something bc i was more confused than anything else. Episode 5 i made a decision , alright I didn't really love these characters. So im just going to be the bad guy and kill everyone i can. Well you cant. Telltale takes away your choice in this episode and pigion holes you into being the good guy.. Now just bc i couldnt choose to make the story go my way isnt why its bad. its bad bc its filled with tropes and logic jumps. It pulls you out of the story. Why the hell did i have to side with the oldcrew that marooned me and left me for dead!? You're  telling me it was just 1 persons fault. The rest of the crew had no choice but to go along with it?? Problem was back in episode 1 the crew defended me and stood up to Cox over the exact same issue. But this time it was ARYAN so that's different... Nah that's just dumb. Again if your going to take my decision way at least make it good. But my final crew after everything WAS JUST Drummer , Virgel , and Julia... OOH by the way WHO THE ♥♥♥♥ IS JULIA!? Yeah we shared a cell together for 10 mins. I guess that means we're Sister's forever now.. I'm sorry but NO THIS LAST EPISODE is just bad. In conclusion I love Scifi Space stuff and narrative driven games. I came in with hopes that maybe this last episode could redeem itself. and i could walk away giving the The Expanse a solid 6 or 7 out of 10. But with 2 episodes that are good with another 2 episodes being MEH , and 1 episode being garbage... This is a 3/10 a bad game. This isn't the telltale i remember. Thx for reading Have a Good Day.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Telltale hit it out of the ballpark with this one. Love the universe of the Expanse and getting to play as the baddest bosmang in the Belt aka Camina is a lot of fun.It's a fun sort of like prequel to the series. Story is interesting and so is the supporting cast. The presentation is great.The Archangel is also pretty damn good. Definitely recommend it for any fans of the series/setting and to Telltale fans. Would love a season 2 of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: It's great to see Telltale with Deck Nine back in game. Amazing story. Finest dialogues, voice acting with super detailed motion capture. You feel very connected with game universe because game lore was written to the smallest details from the history to that strange Belters language. And you don't even feel disconnected even when you stumble on technical side of game: you can easily project same stuff to the real world in near future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm  about half done with it, and as a massive fan of some of Telltale's earlier work, I can say this is their best in years. I find the atmosphere to be right on the money for how i feel a game set in the world of The Expanse should be. The characters are instantly like-able, the choices feel really impactful and definitely make me want to do a second play-through. Overall I'd recommend this game for any fans of The Expanse for a nice 5-8 hour ride in the universe, and any Telltale fan that wants to see a return to form for a great game studio that's had their missteps in the passed few years.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game with one of my favorite characters of the show. Beautiful music, everybody who enjoys the show shouldn't think twice about playing it! I had my reservations because I feared that it could be boring to me knowing the series.. but don't worry, you play a story related to Drummers background which is very interesting to see!The characters in the games are a liiiittle bit flat but that's just because there's one thing that reeeaally bothered me: The game is too short. Yes, I've got about 12 hours gameplay on my steam but that's just because I was disturbed in real life and had to pause the game many times xD Actually you can finish the game in about 6 or 7 hours - and even though there are places you can explore I think the game would be sooo much better if you a) had real shootings instead of cheap quick time actions. with a graphic like that some minor shooter levers would have been greatb) had more conversations with your crew and a few more scenes and options in which you can interact with them. A few more side quests would also be nice - there are almost noticeably few ones and sometimes I had the feeling that I hardly had anything to do in the game because the QTE are very easy. The choices are nice, I like the new look that Telltale chose. But due to its brevity, the game simply doesn't come close to the depth that the series (and the books) offer. So watch the show! Read the novels! And then play the game. Because I love Drummer, she's such a hot badass <3
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved "The Expanse: A Telltale Series." The story is incredibly intriguing, and at the end of each chapter, there's only one thing on my mind: starting the next chapter to find out what happens next. It's a gripping experience that keeps you on the edge of your seat, eager to dive deeper into the unfolding narrative. Now I think that I should explore the books and the TV series of The Expanse universe.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Ten hours of going back to two of The Expanse's most intriguing characters (Camina Drummer and Chrisjen Avasarala), who have as much as baggage to fill up one big space station.The base game as well as the DLC are not action-packed (or rather there's not much else for the player to do but press a few buttons, classic Telltale). Instead the game gives the player time to immerse themselves in the storylines, and learn a bit more about these two fascinating characters through their interactions with others.The game fits in well with what you already know of the characters from the TV series. No surprises here.The only issue I really had was how clumsy/slow the controls were in this game. Not really fun in zero G or even confined spaces.There are many more characters / stories left to explore for another game (and obviously for another TV spin-off). More of Drummer and Avasarala would also be welcome.TL;DR: A story-game for those who want to experience 'The Expanse' vibes through the perspective of two kick-a** women of colour.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: The Expanse: A Telltale Series is a prequel story to the events of the TV show that centers on the character of Camina Drummer as she joins a crew of a scavenger ship hired to find a macguffin. Choices, betrayals and lots of Zero G exploration are involved. Developed by Deck Nine, it follows a similar formula to the established Telltale games genre; heavy story focus, minimal game-play with a few branching plot beats. If you've played any previous Telltale games, you should know what to expect.Pros:- Visually and graphic wise, this may the best game of this genre I've seen. From it's attention to detail and the moody, lonely atmosphere of space, this game does it's visuals well. Character models are equally done well and while there is a bit stylization to the models, I think it works fine.- Overall voice work is done quite well with Cara Gee reprising her role here along with many actors from the show reprising their cameo roles as well. - Much of the exploration in the game is done in it's Zero G environments. While it is disorienting at first (Which it realistically would be), you do get used to it. The control set up for it works surprisingly well and really makes you feel like you're jetting around  in space.- The overall plot, while not the most compelling, is done well enough that it could almost pass for an episode of the show- Choices. Do they matter? Kind of. While not every decision will have an impact, the important ones are highlighted fairly obviously in the game and this will usually lead to alternate versions of scenes. Mainly the lives of the crew are determined by the choices you make as the overall plot progresses.- The game does an excellent job of staying true to the lore of The Expanse and paying attention to particular details of environments, technology and character actions. - QTEs are fairly forgiving so if you're worried about hair trigger reflexes, don't be.- Additionally, the game comes with a good assortment of accessibility options to tailor the QTEs further and provide more tips for playCons:- Game just auto starts on first time run. Not even letting you see the main menu to check your graphic settings. Have to exit the gameplay to the main menu first. I have no idea why they designed it that way, but Devs, don't do that. - Game uses a single playthrough save slot system with auto checkpoints. Not a terrible system with this type of game, but it does mean that if you miss something, you'll have to replay the entire episode. - Post processing graphic options are bundled into a preset. No individual options for DOF, motion blur, chromatic aberration, etc. - No fast forward, skip dialogue options- While the game does offer a stream safe mode (Mute Licensed Music in Audio options), it's doesn't work completely as the The Expanse theme music (which is absolutely copyrighted) will still play on the choices review screen. How this has not been fixed since the game's release is a HUGE oversight. So, streamers and YouTubers beware.- I do hate to admit this, but this may be a game where prior knowledge of the The Expanse universe may be required, either from the shows or the books. The game gives only a cursory overview of the political and social situation in the solar system and those without prior knowledge may not understand the groups and their conflicts as presented.- The inclusion of a certain character in Episode 4 just raises way too many questions and literally acts as a Deus ex machina. It's the only part of the narrative I seriously questioned and feel like I have to ding it for that. Overall, as a fan of The Expanse, I really enjoyed this game and I feel like it's one of the better games of it's genre. If modern Telltale can keep up this quality then the company truly see a revival. As an Expanse fan, I'd it an 8/10.For anyone else, this is more like an 7/10Regardless, I very much recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of narrative story games. This one just falls flat in too many categories for me to recommend. The voice acting is terrible, graphics feel like they're from 2015, and the story just seemed boring. Usually with boring stories, you get great gameplay, but here, the gameplay is about as exciting as the actors sitting in a recording room. I wasn't a fan of the voice accent, and anytime the lead character spoke, I cringed.  Weird facial modelling as well, some characters had mouths that went from one side of their head to the other. For a game from 2023, it's lacking in many technological aspects. No HDR, no DLSS, no RT. It's just a slap-it-together cheap game that wasn't even worth it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing for 4 of the 5 episodes. Absolutely incredible feeling to be playing in a game in the Expanse world; you feel so close to the series and the developers knew what they were doing! I'd say the ending is a bit flat, not enough padding to recognise your choices, however, it definitely makes you want to replay it to see how things can change. They really do need to get going with another season though, doesn't need to be Drummer, could be so many other characters as the lead, make it please!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good. I must say there are some strange decisions with the controls, particularly the way Drummer always faces in the direction of the camera while walking (which was particularly strange considering that Avasarala in Archangel does move freely, maybe something to do with the fact you can walk on walls when in zero g?), and the way the camera phases through walls, but both issues pretty quickly faded into the background after the first episode.One thing that didn't was how certain things like the spacesuit helmet visors didn't quite play along with some of the shaders like the depth of field blur used in many scenes so they stuck out like a sore thumb. It was particularly noticeable in the DLC with all the holograms and transparent surfaces. I suppose I can't really hold it against this game too much since I think it's to do with the Unreal engine? Still, it was pretty distracting.But what you're actually here for, the story, is quite good and worth your time. Most of the characters are fun and compelling and the plot is quite interesting. I don't like to judge these kinds of adventure games on the amount of different endings there are, especially since this is a prequel and Drummer and Avasarala's stories need to go in a particular direction for them to be where they are at the start of the books/show. Instead, I'll say that the choices during the story itself were generally interesting and there were cases where I got to the chapter summary and went "wait, I could've done that?!" I definitely wanna replay this at some point to see the different paths.A lot of criticism I see of this game leans on how you won't get much out of this if you're not already familiar with The Expanse, which I find pretty unfair since that's something you can say about most prequels to large franchises. It is something worth noting, but I wouldn't put it against this game and instead use it as an excuse to recommend you go read/watch the main series first. Otherwise, if you're already an Expanse fan, I'd definitely recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Telltales games, then you should like this one too.Never watched the show but still was fun and interesting. The DLC was kinda weird it didn't really have nothing to do with the main game Performance wise runs good, couldn't get past 120fps. even tho my GPU should so it might be capped Nonetheless  -  7/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: A nice game for less than 10 hours of play.  The story is well written, even it's not a convoluted or complex one, and graphics are captivating. Do not expect a milestone in its genre, however is a decent game,  just be sure to buy it at  discount. Only real doubt is related to the bonus episode: it has nothing to do with the main plot or any possible side story, moreover it is really boring and does not worth any time to spend on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10:A good story with excellent art style and voice performances that near-perfectly pairs with the TV show.This was a treat as an Expanse fan, my only complaints are that there are a couple short plot points weaving into the show that leave a little to be desired, and that the game has me scratching at the arm for a full blown Expanse RPG instead of a limited Telltale title.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Like some many good games, it was over way too soon. I like many others loved the tv show and it was nice getting lots of little easter eggs that tied into the show, such Julie Mao and Fred Johnson (who ever cared for Andersone Daws...). I always had a soft spot for Drummer, so it was nice get to spend more time with the character again. But admitedly I binged played the entire game over a few days, but such is life. I would say to anyone that hasent watched the TV series yet, that should play this game first as you will get some much more out of the TV show after the fact.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If your already a fan of the series then you shouldn't be disappointed with this version of the series made into a game. You don't get the main characters from the show but Drummer and a couple of her crew are the focus and they don't disappoint. The graphics are off the chain and I continuously forgot I was playing a game and not watching a side series or something like that. Great story and acting but as usual it's just not enough, when you make a game this good you got to give a lot of story and substance to keep the entertainment beasts happy. Still great job and I hope there's more to come.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Story is good, so is the music. Especially interesting for fans of the series. A bit overpriced especially considering the graphics quality and additional DLC not included in the price for the base game. About the graphics; it does not look bad, but definitely not as refined as a 2023 game could be. But then again, this makes it playable for fans who are not into pc gaming/building so it's an understandable choice, you can probably play this on a smartphone or laptop without graphics card.It's a short game, the gameplay feels more like an interactive comic, but still it felt immersive. You can get this if you like the Expanse and if there's a discount it may be worth the price.Overall: 7 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Great game 100% recommend only 7 hours long if you get all collectables yes its very short but totally worth it played most telltale/choices matter games definitely worth playing it could of been longer but all in all worth it . there is a DLC extra episode if you want to play more which have not yet but for sure I would play this again
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: The first game from the resurrection of Telltale! I enjoy seeing them back in action! The visuals and story really appeal to me, and it felt like playing a movie. Don't get me wrong, I thoroughly enjoyed the game, but it lacks some character. Old Telltale games gave you four dialogue options and two choices for big decisions. Here, everything is cut down to two choices, meaning the illusion of choice is smaller, and you cannot always choose the path you want to take. I felt a lack of options for replayability. The episodes were also too short. I rushed through the story in one night, whereas in older games, the episodes were at least double the length of these. The only good cliffhangers were in episodes 4 and 5; the others ended on a mediocre note.Still enjoyed it, no bugs, good visuals, mediocre story. Welcome back Telltale!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like a lost episode of the show.  The writing and voice acting bring the world back to life.  And Drummer is one of my favorite characters, so I love that she was chosen as the game's focus.  On the tech side, there are bugs and glitches.  How forgiving you are of these will depend on whether you feel The Expanse has been well represented elsewhere in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: It's OK. Cons: Character writing is terrible. Definitely written for a "modern audience." The voice acting and animation stiffness also doesn't help. Characters are unlikable. Pros: Good soundtrack. Action scenes and quick time events have a decent pace. There is a decent main plot that keeps you invested. Graphics are OK for what it is. The game isn't great but worth the price. If it wasn't leaching off of the Expanse success then I would have given it a negative review. Telltales writing is infected by the mind virus, but so was Amazon's Expanse to a degree.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of the books and early seasons of the show, so this was right up my alley. Despite not REALLY being in the books, thanks to Cara Gee's incredible performance, Drummer is one of the most compelling characters of the TV series and was a perfect choice for the lead part in this game. If you liked the books, the TV series, or the character of Camina Drummer, you should love this experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the books, show, and especially of Drummer, I really enjoyed just getting to inhabit the world a bit more. I can definitely see why folks who aren't already Expanse fans would bounce off this one though, but I appreciate the many little details and worldbuilding this gives to the setting.I also quite enjoyed Archangel if only because I'd watch Shohreh Aghdashloo read the yellow pages. It covered a great bit of backstory that I don't think was covered in other media, which had a great emotional impact at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest merit of this game is that it managed to involve me in the story of never been known universe. I haven't ever heard of "The Expanse" original series, but it was interesting to follow the storyline and watch the characters overcome difficulties.And this is exactly what you expect from Full Motion Video games - to be deeply immersed and involved. Oh, one more thing: the musical accompaniment is outstanding here!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing narrative game giving you more of the story for any fan of The Expanse.I'm a little biased as I loved the show and Camina Drummer was my favorite character. I have not read the books yet but it is on my to read list and will be interested if my opinion changes after that. This is my first foray into the Telltale games though, and it won't be my last.The story is set prior to the events of the show, and shows Drummers rise to a more prominent role in the belt. You're faced with a number of tough choices which shape the narrative (as I've heard all Telltale games do). Your choices feel like they have weight and it is awesome to see things play out. The gameplay was a mix of cutscenes with quick time events, and third person exploration. Being in space and dealing with low/no gravity made the exploration bits pretty enjoyable, and there were enough breaks in the main cutscene/qte content to make it not get boring. I felt it was really balanced all the way through.The DLC with Avasarala was also quite enjoyable. More of a mystery/puzzle narrative, but felt like they really understood her character to it's core.I played this entirely on Steam Deck and it ran flawlessly. 40hz/40fps and didn't feel like it had any issues. Overall the game took me about 6 hours to beat (including the DLC), and I enjoyed it all thoroughly.I highly recommend this for any fan of The Expanse or Telltale games. It's just long enough to get you invested in the story and characters, and makes you feel the weight of your choices.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it.Captured the vibe of the show nicely, I thought. Story is nice enough to care about, but not great, the acting is good. You get to make some tough choices that fit the character. There are some things that feel a bit plot and forced, which the TV show managed to avoid mostly, and there are a few nitpicks about the hard sci-fi physics of it all, which you micht notice if you are a total space nerd like myself, but overall enjoyable, I think.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game BUT... keeping in mind that is Telltale's shortest game I've ever played and that being an avid The Expanse fan as I am I found the story a little underwhelming. For being 8 hours in my run I usally felt that the game was setting up some plotlines that never came into fruition, something that I never experienced before in a Telltale's or The Expanse property. So if you are aware of that but keep craving something new from these worlds go for it. PD: very nice cameos from the actors playing Dawes and Johnson in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I think simply put If you liked the show and/or books you will get enjoyment from this. If you have not seen/read either you will most likely not enjoy it and you can certainly give this one a pass.As a fan of the show I had a blast through this concise but enjoyable experience. It was like watching more good episodes, but with your own interactive input, and with periods where you can explore interesting areas and environments. A worthwhile adventure if you are familiar with The Expanse.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge Expanse fan it pains me give this a thumbs down. The game content is good and makes a compelling story, but there just isn't enough of it. I beat this game in 10 hours, which includes that I played halfway through, before realizing I had made a game play mistake and re-started over from the beginning.  I estimate that a complete play through would take only 6 to 7 hours.  I bought this game on sale, but even for the $30 CDN I paid, I expected more. If you are not an Expanse fan, this game will leave you with buyers remorse.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent! An across the board improvement in my opinion when compared to the old Telltale titles. Same great story and characters, but less pointless scavenger hunting and saying-sim mechanics. The engine is worlds better in presentation, performance, and functionality. Money well spent. If you liked the old titles, you’ll probably like this one too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: My normal games are Generation Zero, and Insurgency Sandstorm so this was a real change of pace and direction for me. I am an Expanse fan and so the title music playing gave me goose bumps. The game is simple maybe a little short, but very pleasurable to play, good dialogue, humorous in places which added an additional layer of enjoyment. I loved it so much so, I got the add on pack to continue. I certainly will go back and repeat it making other choices. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED !
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Just fun and interesting enough to get a quick Expanse fix.  The story is very Telltale with options for how moments will play out without feeling too often like you're being pushed one direction or another.  One or two beautiful moments also make for a compelling story, even if it isn't always the most engaging.  Overall, a good time for a couple of gaming sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Telltale's new series was just as great at their previous games. If you played The Walking Dead , Batman , Guardians of the Galaxy, The Wolf Among Us and Tales from the Borderlands you'll definitely love this series as well. Season two would be great and i hope it happens. I'm itching to watch the expanse TV show now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down, perfect story. Clunky, with minimal graphic quality. Your choices have large impacts on dialog and future choice options. These alternative perspectives & time periods give a new look at the same great Expanse universe we all know- At this time the game is way too short, so I recommend purchasing the Deluxe Edition on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: A great title for fans of The Expanse. The performances are convincing, the story compelling (enough) and the presentation/graphics are of high quality for the genre. As with Telltale games, the story and decision making takes center stage, don't expect a lot of action and exploration. This ran great on a Rog Alky and I had no bugs or crashes
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked The Expanse as much as I did, this game is worth getting, especially on discount.  But I would see the whole show first - it's my favorite of all time.  Amazing cast of heroes and villains, exciting space battles and lots of mystery and intrigue. The game is not nearly as good, and is too short, but I enjoyed it.  I can see why it's short - takes a huge amount of work to create all the graphics and cutscenes.  Would love more games in the Expanse universe.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan on the show or the books then you'll enjoy this in its own right as a short story / prequel, particularly if you're fond of Drummer, the protagonist. I wouldn't expect it stands alone particularly well if you haven't seen or read them however.Visually the game looks really nice with unreal engine 4, and you can edit an ini file to hack an HDR setting on if you're blessed with such a monitor. I'm pretty impressed by the character models and animations and the scenery is generally pretty good.Main complaint is it's quite short. You can expect to get ~8 hours out of a single playthrough, maybe a little more with the DLC. You might get a bit more playtime replaying some episodes to try different choices because whilst they don't change the main storyline they do have an impact on your crew.Hoping we can see more episodes in the future as there's quite a selection of characters in the Expanse that could make for interesting side stories / prequels.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Combining the rich universe of The Expanse with Telltale Games' story-driven gameplay seems the perfect match, and this game delivers with a brilliant story, endearing characters and a pulsating climax.Your decisions matter more than in other Telltale games. Crew members live or die based on the decisions you make. It's easy to develop emotional attachments to the characters, who are brilliantly voiced and impressively expressive.The game is somewhat dragged down by long sequences of hovering through seemingly endless corridors as you explore shipwrecks in your MAG boots. It's sad to think a lot of players probably get so frustrated with these excursions that they rage quit and miss out on what the game has to offer. Thankfully, by about episode 3 these bizarre diversions are over and the story really takes off. Telltale shows they've still got it even after being brought to the verge of bankruptcy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely medicore and extremely short game that is only held up by the merits of the universe it is set in. The story is medicore, only held up by a few good character moments but most feel meaningless because of how short the game is. It took me a little over 4 hours to complete the game. Most other telltale games take ~10 hours for a single season. Not to mention this game is also priced higher than all other telltale games. I would only buy this if it is both on sale and you love the tv show.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Was a bit short. Not as engaging as some of their earlier work (walking dead and borderlands. those were really good). Enjoyable if you're into sci-fi stories. I played through it in 5 hours.I feel like some of the choices didn't have meaningful enough consequences.Hard to recommend, get it when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically it is a very well executed Telltale-style game, although the mouse and keyboard controls were a bit jank.  The zero-g and shipwreck exploration/salvaging segments personally make up for that: they were great and I want them fully fleshed out into their own game.  (Dear Deck Nine, call Blackbird Interactive now.  Team up.  Form the Space Salvaging Game Avengers.)  Voice acting was great and the visuals were the best for a Telltale Game yet.Narratively I quite enjoyed it, although I was annoyed at a key piece of the story just being a callback to the show instead of its own unique thing--it felt both a bit heavy-handed fan service and a missed opportunity.  I liked the characters for their roles and the overall thrust of the story.  Special shout-out for episode three for being really creepy and giving an interesting story of what happened before through logs, documents, and objects.  I will acknowledge some choices offered seemed inconsistent with Drummer, but this is the character years before we encounter her so she could have developed further and, to be blunt, I didn't choose them because they felt wrong so I cannot tell you how they actually come off.Archangel is very different than the rest of the game and it works for what Avaserala is doing at that time.  The narrative was excellent and I looked forward to reading those reports.  Trust me, it will make f-ing sense.Overall I really did enjoy the game and hope Deck Nine does more with The Expanse--or really sci-fi in general.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Ima give this game 2.5 stars out of 5. I really liked the setting, tone, sci-fi elements of the game but the story didn't really make much sense to me. I feel act 3 should have gone in more detail they really missed a cool opportunity with that. As well there is almost no world building in this game, you're thrust straight into the universe and if you're anything like me where you haven't watched or read the expanse series, it was kinda difficult to follow along. The ending felt super rushed. As well some of the motivations of the characters felt strange and unnatural. I admit, I saw sci-fi and Telltale and just immediately bought because I really loved their previous games but this one just didn't do it for me. Hopefully the next one has some better storytelling elements!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best written stories and best looking characters that I have seen in a game in a long time. The story is written well enough to pull strings on my emotions. It has been years since a game had truly made me cry on the inside. I will definitely replay the game's story again, since there are many choices the player makes that can completely alter the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: The game is actually really good and doesn't take this long to actually get through. I am on my second play through. I will say yes the game does run short being as there is only 5 episodes and a 6th episode as DLC.The game takes place prior to the actual series and focuses on the life of Camina Drummer prior to her time on Tycho Station. We also meet Julie Mao before she becomes part of her fathers sick experiment. We also meet some fascinating characters from the Expanse Universe. I believe we do meet Maya in the series briefly but it does give us more time with both Maya and Drummer. I believe everyone does survive in the Expanse lore but you can play the game however you see fit with consequences or rewards for your choices. The MK Core is I believe another Bio Weapon that thankfully was destroyed however it only set back Julie's father not stopping him. We also get to see Europa's Bane which played a big part in season one of "The Expanse".In Episode 6 we get to see some action of our favorite badass Earther handling Earther politics, while avoiding an international crisis, and handling family all while dealing with things going on around her in person.The game feels like it brings me closer to the Expanse Universe and it was fun and entertaining not to mention very informative regarding more history and lore of "The Expanse". However I can really only recommend while it is on sale as for the amount of content for the price I feel doesn't add up. Great game but I literally be the game in 8 hours not including my second playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you like The Expanse (and why would you not), you will like this game (main game as well as the Archangel DLC). Great acting (including the amazing original actors for Drummer and Avaserala). Good story, good choice system. Definitely worth it.What can be improved: First of all: Please give us more episodes. :)Apart from this: While there is good free movement, there's no real free combat (just reaction clicking). I know that's extremely difficult to implement and get right. But you might want to consider this for the next game. And: Next time please release it on Steam right from the start. Makes us happy and you $$$. ;)
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this with a heavy asterisk, im a big fan of the show for context.  This series starts off really strong in the first act, but about 3/4 through theres a very long and tedious walking section that is so boring i almost never finished it.  the finale picks back up and is generally ok, but the game never really gets back to that peak of the first act.  So its good, but it runs out of steam before its over, which is pretty sad because its a short game.  Get it on sale if youre a fan
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I watched the series twice and READ the series 3 times so a game about the earlier days of my favorite character was a no brainer.  It was the basic Telltale handling of the story.  If you like Telltale games and The Expanse you will probably like this.  I liked the main story about Drummer and got the extra DLC, Archangel. Despite Avasarala being my second favorite character, I didn't think she translated well to a game.  All in all, worth my time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Telltale game as you know them, but with massively improved movement freedom. The zero-g atmosphere was executed well and offers a fun movement experience. The characters, beyond the ones we already knew from the show, are well-executed with rounded personalities. The voice-acting, especially Cara's, is amazing! Ultimately, it's still a point-and-click, so don't expect RPG elements or innovative gameplay. You walk around; you click on things and listen to dialogue; and you do some quick-times. If you're into that, you'll be into this one. No knowledge of The Expanse (books or show) is needed, but if you know the universe and (like me) love it, then you'll love this chance to experience it in a different way.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I've never watched the show up to this point, but this game was rather interesting. I have some reservations about the limited choices one could choose from, but besides that, it was a very well put together narrative experience.In the future, I hope that Telltale will shine even more when they get their hands on an IP with limited if no content set in the future so that they can have full or near-full creative direction.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: It's just a string of cliche, badly written character actions and dialogue. There is almost no attention to detail or real thought put into it.
