I love Telltale, and really expected better.At 5 hours long it's also 1/2 to 1/3 the length of any other Telltale game I've played. I guess the character limit in ChatGPT was a problem.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I learned there seems to be a TV series of the same name (never heard of it), but I don't think you need to watch it to find your way into this adventure game. The setting for the game is one of those often heard scenarios found in classic SF from the 1930s like Captain Future: Humanity has colonised part of the solar system, but Earth and it's colonies don't exactly like each other. Add some more or less shady space pirates, and you are there.In this setting, you play a female Han Solo type with the name Camina Drummer. Most of the gameplay consists of walking through gravity free spaceship junkyards. From time to time you have to make decisions that will change the outcome of the story. The secret to success is to make your crew happy and give everybody what he or she needs.This sounds like a waste of time, but doing errands in Zero G is actually fun. And for me, the big advantage of this game is that you can adjust the difficulty exactly to your needs. So you can play it casually or with a bit more adrenalin included. The only thing I might criticise is that chapters 4 and 5 (of five) seem to be a bit rushed. But on the other hand - maybe I just went better at making decisions?I actually like the game and would buy it again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Make sure to watch the TV series first to really understand the setting!I enjoyed the story very much and I think Drummer was portrait spot on. The original voices did a great contribution to that too. This is not a game where you'll get lost along the trip, it's more like being part of a movie where you become part of the tougher choices. I find that very relaxing, yet immersive and introspective. This is a game that primarily wants to tell you a story and about people, not just keep you busy. No long stretches of running around to get from A to B, no farming of XP. I was a bit sad that it ended so soon, but I think the content fits the story. So please don't stretch the story for the sake of time. Rather I'd have loved to go for another adventure. I'd definitely be in for a part II.PS: You don't need to be a Drummer fan to enjoy this. General interest in the characters of the series and what makes them tick will make suffice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: A solid return to form; doesn't reach the heights of Wolf Among Us, Batman or Tales of the Borderlands, but it's a tight, focused tale with some great moments and mature moral choices to make. Noticeable improvement game-play wise have been made; from dead space like movement to less gimmicky action scenes. It took a bit to warm the art style and voice acting, and it could’ve done more to explain its universe to rookies like me, but it's all remarkably solid experience overall.  7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I will never be able to rave about this game enough. The Expanse was already one of the best shows I've ever seen, and I've been dying for more content. The developers perfectly captured the feel of the show in every possible way, while still providing great gameplay. Visually, it's stunning. Great lighting, shadows, animations, models, you name it.Worth every penny and then some!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I know people do not like this game for many reasons but you know you have to give it a shot and in my opinion it was a ok ok game. The company hast to try something new to bring themselves up let just take this game as a warmup part for them they tried may more new things like change in artstyle, choice selection,a littler bit of open world experience, we should wait until they release the big shot and I bet it will worth both our time and money. Peace' Out 🗿👔👖
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the Expanse, particularly the TV series, it's worth a play though. It's over in under 5 hours though so get it in a sale. The Drummer character is based on the TV version so if you're coming from the books it might jar a bit. The story is... fine enough... it was just nice being back in the universe.If you're not a fan of the Expanse I'd pass, I don't think it offers enough to stand up in it's own right.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think it's as bad as people ever make it to be. It's a start from the new Telltale, some parts of the game might be tedious and story might be confusing which I agree but that is true if you never watched The Expanse. I didn't but I did start to enjoy the game later. My suggestion would be for those who are looking to play this, don't have expectations, just see it for yourself. The game isn't good or bad, just something in the middle.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this very much. It helps to know The Expanse TV-Show to comprehend the characters and surroundings. If you loved that show, like I did, chances are you'll love this game. It's not super actiony, it's more like a very immersive prequel season to the TV-Show - one you get to take part in and do stuff and make decisions that matter. The atmosphere is very well conveyed. Particularly loved the zero-G environment - easy to loose orientation at first :-)Loved it! Hope they'll do more episodes soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Weird one. I am fan of the old Telltale games for all their flaws, yet this has got be one of their weaker entries, I got it during a sale, and I stlil feel ripped of for the brevity. The graphics and animation improved a lot. Yet the overall plot was thin and underdeveloped. Due to the "game mechanic" that one explores ruins and space stations, a huge amount of the playing time is spent just walking. The interaction is here and there, yet overall I was completly astounded once the game was over after not even 5 hours. If those 5 hours were mostly an interactive movie, I would be fine. Yet as it stands, the scavenger hunt feels almost intentional to pad play time. A lot of the story beats were rushed and felt out of place. Get it, if you like the Expanse and the Telltale formula, yet wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the series and this is a 'typical' Tell tale game which is just as awesome in it's own right.Being critical, the 4th and 5th chapters feel a bit rushed when compared to the first 3. Still a great addition to the Telltale library and I personally think it's easy to see that The Expanse universe could be integrated into something huge and entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the series I really enjoyed the first episode.Its more of a story than a game I was engaged throughout and really enjoyed the journey.Definitely fun for anyone who is a fan of the tv series. I very much so enjoyed the 6 hours or so of my first play through and will definitely go through it again and see how changing choices determines different outcomes. highly recommended The DLC however i felt was  lacking It was very short and not really engaging or challenging.I guess playing at politics isn't my thing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Good Game imo the story is only about 4 hours but i did enjoy the 4 hours if you like story driven games like the ones telltale do or other similiar developers you will like it either way. at first i was a bit offput by some characters visuals and their voices but i played trough the whole game mainly cause i was constantly curious what would happen next. I urge you to try it and see if you like it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this a sideways thumb I would, there's a lot to like but I feel the game falls short in many areas. The great bits are having more time with Cara Gee as Drummer, and with the DLC getting more Avasarala. But, the game feels way too short, easily beatable in 5 hours, supporting cast is mostly forgettable, and if you want to replay a certain part there's no skipping dialogue or checkpoints to start from. Also character models and specifically their hands are a bit of brain twister they just look wrong sometimes. But to replay, you have to restart from the beginning of an episode and go through everything and the only thing that makes it tolerable is hearing Drummer's dialogue you didn't pick the first time. I also feel that the story shouldn't have been leading up to a hidden blue goo reveal as the thing they were looking for, it feels out of place and wrong. But if you're a fan of The Expanse or this has sparked your interest in the world, watch the show and read the books you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to anyone who's into space and Telltale stuff.It's a PREQUEL to the series so i don´t get what people mean by "don't get it if you haven't seen the series". Only bad thing IMO is that it's a bit short so I really hope they come out with another similar game with maybe the same cast or just another team that's around the same area.I cried at one part that i wont spoil. I told my friend I was streaming for that "if _____  does happen i'm gonna cry". it happened and I cried because I'm a predictable human. 10/10 would play again to play different paths and maybe not have to cry over the same thing. Thinking about buying it for my friend on his b-day since he's a big fan of Telltales TWD and space.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If neutral was an option, I would choose that. Though, I lean towards recommending the game for those who have watched and liked the TV series. The plot device could have been a bit more different from the first few seasons of the The Expanse though. Like most if not all Telltale games, it is mainly a one playthrough game unless you want to get 100% achievements.I recommend for The Expanse fans that have watched the TV series since this is mainly a prequel story for Camina Drummer. It gives her a little bit more of a backstory. The DLC being a day in the life of Avasarala. I recommend for those that have not watched the TV series to watch it first if you are interested in the game. The show is amazing and so are the books.There is two main reasons why I bought the game. It is the Expanse and it revolves around Camina Drummer. Definitely will support The Expanse in anyway I can. However, I feel like they could have gone another route in terms of the plot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the TV series, this game is really a must. Even though one has to get used to the looks, that make it appear more like an animated series (which isn't bad necessarily), the story, the overall setting and the dialogs really match the TV series and are pretty engaging.Especially noteworthy is that the game also uses the same voice actors as the series (at least in English), which allows you to satisfy the need for more, the series has left you with.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: great story and nice little dlc. I hope to see more from the expanse story and id like to see more choices that matter. New mechanics flying around in zero G is a welcomed one although when you mess up in the episode and want to change an option i find you have to redo the entire episode if you want to do it differently, thats my only gripe. It ended a bit on a cliff hanger both with the DLC and the main story, which is good, not complaining here, I just hope to see a continuation. I have never heard of the expanse before, there's a tv series about it i think, i might give it a look since i played the game. The lore is fantastic. I wish there was  more, it should've been longer, also in combat it would be cool if i could actually fight and not just press prompts. I understand this is developed by the telltales company and we all know what there formula is , keep trying new things. i think with the right concept. right ideas and mechanics, the next game will be ever better from them. nice story telling as always, a lot better than their previous titles imo.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: The Expanse game is meh. Its not really a game at all.The story is focused on Drummer between the station massacre and allying with Fred Johnson in the TV series. But the story-line was overused even within the Expanse (SPOILER: ). Most of the choices are largely non-impacting, puzzles are literally kids play, and the actual action scenes are just the "press this controller button within 2 seconds" style of play. No real aiming or skill involved, mostly just wondering around looking for stuff.I recommend waiting for super sale just for the story, IF you like the Expanse TV show. Otherwise skip.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: A brief yet enjoyable interactive story that effectively captures the themes of the novels and TV series. The main character's voice acting is outstanding, but the plot is quite linear. Prior knowledge of the series through the books or TV show is strongly recommended, as the game does not provide backstory.I'd recommend this to any fans of The Expanse, and to sci-fi fans in general who are willing to pick up the books prior to playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Not the strongest addition to telltale's library (action's mid, settings don't vary much, and some of the choices in the later chapters are arbitrary), but if you like the expanse (Camina is now one of my favorite characters), and you like choose your own adventure games, then get this on sale for $15 or less. FYI It's ~ 5 hours long and i don't intend on replaying it (like I said, arbitrary choices which means why try for a different ending)
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: A story, and a good one. Choices are cumulative and the right ones give you a good ending. Characters are believable and invest you in the story. The occasional action scenes are scripted and require you to hit the right button in a limited time. Dying takes you back to the last checkpoint. So if you like a good story this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty good, if you like Telltale games... for book series fans, this game plays like one of the novellas set between the novels. My only real gripe is that they get a lot of physics wrong in episode 2. If they do more of these they need to get a good science advisor & make the writers follow their advice!Without getting too spoilery:You cannot do a "high-G burn" for hours or days & then just suddenly stop for the convenience of the plot. I'll deduct 2 stars for that.  Otherwise, it's aggressively okay!3/5 "flip & burns"
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: This is now, by far, my favorit game ever!!! I've been a fan of the series from the get go and was more than a bit suspicious about the game when it was first announced. I was wrong... SO VERY WRONG. Playing as Camina Drummer is a dream come true. The storyline is amazing, the graphics are breathtaking and the audio is everything you'd hope for. Ten out of ten! I will be playing this game again very soon (and trying to keep a certain character alive this time).
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Short, bit forced flirting with same gender annoyance - Badass Camina Drummer is bi/poly so would have been nice if that was a player choice. My face is so tired from being a straight female gamer. which nothing and noone caters to. Great characters, great animation, great story flow. Very short, and I am sick of episoded games for no reason. But was worth it. Storytelling is Telltales magic, and they are good in this one. Wish it was a full rpg with the Telltale bits in cutscenes. Also I love Camina, Ill buy the next game and also hope they restart the show :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of the Expanse like me then play this game! It will  immerse you into a new story of the Expanse universe, all about the tough Belter Cammina Drummer, slightly before the events the Expanse, tv series. Don't expect this to be an action packed game (go play something else), this game is about story, choices and consequences. I was spectic but the developers nicely cached on the Expanse sphere. Plus having the actressess Cara Gee and Shohreh Agdashloo reprising their rol here is amazing!I hope this studio may produce more Expanse games in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: this is a game that everyone should have, it's a great story some action, and that starfield should get some pointers from this small game  created a perfect balance .... I hope that Bethesda (Tod Howard)  can put his  Ego aside and get back to the basic of great story telling, with a  pinch of evolution.....to be brave  and unafraid  to allow some decent sexual scenes and the feeling of tension and passion on every front  from sex  to cooking a pot of mushroom soup and allowiing some cause and effect.....If you can show fighting scenes you can show sexual scenes that are meaningful and more ,,,,cyberpunk, and mass effect and this game balanced this area very well.....this game has moved me .....making me feel all emotions ,  including having fun.....Thank you Telltale..... and it plays well on my steamdeck......mucho love
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this. I wasn't familiar with the source material, but this didn't matter, I got drawn into the story and atmosphere very quickly anyway. It didn't matter either that some words were unknown to me, if anything, I found that very immersive since language is always evolving, so it's plausible that mankind will use new slang in future.The gameplay might be a bit on the light side, but make no mistake, the story is not, and emotions can hit hard. I had to replay one of the episodes because I was very unhappy with how my decisions played out.Overall, a fine short game, each episode about 1h long. I liked the whole art design, especially of the characters. It will not be everyone's taste but I liked this mix of cartoonish and realistic. It's what caught my attention when seeing the trailer and screenshots, and I'm happy to have played this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Great story that adds a lot of context to some of the characters in the main show. Though not as "grand" as the show, the game itself add some great story elements that do somewhat add to the depth of the show. Especially if you have the Archangel DLC. If you are a fan of The Expanse TV show, playing this will add a lot more meaning some some characters and their backstory. Though, not 100% sure if cannon to the main story, this does fit in a nice place as a prequel so to speak. I would like to see a sequel to this particular story with Drummer, though I do not have very high hopes considering the TV series is currently over. Whether or not there is enough momentum for a sequel remains to be seen as the story itself isn't 100% unique given the characters you play as and what is expected of them in the TV series. Overall, this is a great game, that can be beat in 6-9 hours depending on if you buy the Archangel DLC or not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the series I have not played this game for very long. The main reason is that it is irritatingly flawed: the story does not continue where I had left off and saved games can not be activated. Since I did not feel like starting an hour of playing (why does Steam say "0.4 hours played"?) all over again I have deleted it from my library.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but holds up to the series and books level in terms of writing for the most part.Gameplay is nothing to write home (or anywhere else for that matter) about, so probably get it on sale like I did, then it seems to be worth its money, cause it takes about 7 hours, so it ends up being 3 trips to the cinema.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the EXPANSE TV show on amazon you will enjoy this story game. The music and graphics are very good. Again  l have to caution any one who is not a fan of the TV show. If you have not seen it or like the TV show this is not the game for you to play through. This is for the fans only as you need context to understand what is going on. At the end of this game all it reminded me was how good the lore and books and the TV show was. Recommend to fans only.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend watching "The Expanse" first season before playing this game, since the story occur just before the events of the very first episode.The story and choices are not mind-blowing by themselves, but they are very interesting if you know the show.The Archangel DLC is not action packed, but it's a great way to portray the Undersecretary and the political intrigues she daily faces.The game may feel short too.I just recommend because it's a great complement for the show, and it showcases 2 of my fav characters.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like watching a The Expanse spin-off but you may decide what the character does. Sure it has the old and well known telltale issues of very easy quick action sequences and so on. But if you like a dense and well narrated story that really gets you wanting for more than this is your game. I am just half done, but I already know that I will replay  it at least twice due to the outcome of two of my decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the 'The Expanse' show, this game will feel right like home.And if you didn't saw it, you should.The first time you start it up and hear this gorgous theme song again you know this will be good.And it is. Exactly what you expect from an Expanse story, just the right amount of drama, hope, politics and action.The story itself may be short, but it was very well written. It's set before the events of the show and it tells us more about Drummer's life before we saw her on Tycho Station.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I'm both a fan of telltale games and a bigger fan of The Expanse. And this does a disservice to both franchises. Now, maybe it gets better after chapter 2, but I doubt I'll ever find the motivation to get there. The Episodes are short, and have very little "meat" to them. The characters are thin, the voice acting sporadic in it's quality. Overall, a very disappointing return from telltale. Apparently most of the game was developed by deck 9, but marketed as a telltale series. Hope "The wolf among us 2" is an actual return to form, but after this game, I'll wait till the reviews come in before buying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Episode 5 is like 10 minutes long... this is one of the worst telltale games ive played. Ive played TWD all seasons at least twice, but with the expanse, im 100% sure i will never play the first season ever again. If i had the opportunity to refund, i would. just watch somebody play it on YT, the "critical choices" suck, and theres only like 2 major choices, whereas in TWD there were multiple crucial choices PER EPISODE... THE EXPANSE has ca. 2 crucial choices in the entire season. I do not recommend purchasing. dont let yourself be fooled by the ratings they like to show you firsthand. "Telltale looks its finest it ever has" which is true, graphics are insane, however the game is a 4/10 on a "very good day".
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a joke. 4.4 hours for completion. The walking dead was 3 times that. Chapter 4 had no meaningful decisions. Chapter 5, the big finale, lasted 30 mins. This isn't a good game, if you don't like The Expanse you won't enjoy it. For Expanse fans it will be worth playing, its cool to play as Camina and feel a part of The Expanse universe, but wait till you can get it really cheap. The sad part is they could have made a great game and they have robbed the fans of The Expanse of that experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fellow  fan of "The Expanse" then this is probably a no-brainer. While it doesn't pick up after the "finale" of the show, it lets us look a bit deeper into the life of fan-favorite "Camina Drummer". While it's no classic compared to either the show, or previous "Telltale" efforts like "Wolf Among Us" or "The Walking Dead", it's certainly a solid enough story and for fans, it's just a great opportunity to drop back into the universe of the books and show.  It runs well for me and it looks decent (some odd character models aside). I just wish there was a bit more variety in terms of locations, and yes I know that the locales are mostly true to the show, but that's whats great about games...you don't need to build expensive sets, so you can go a bit crazier. All that said, if you're a fan of the show in particular, definitely pick this one up. If however you're not yet a fan, this is not an appropriate point of entry. Good Job Telltale! Welcome Back!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Wasn't really a fan of this Telltale project. I played this with no knowledge or context of the source material (books and TV series) so I was missing a lot of background which would have done a lot of heavy lifting in understanding the characters and story. TL;DR at the bottom.Since the product description and game itself don't really explain the events in the rest of the Expanse universe, or recommend you to check it out first, or even mention its existence, I suspect a lot of players will wander into this game expecting a mostly coherent and self-contained narrative, fleshed out characters, and meaningful relationships. Unfortunately I don't feel like the writing delivered on those metrics. I struggled to relate to the characters, and moments that I'm clearly meant to feel moved by fell very flat. Like I understood it's a sad moment but I could never fully relate to it.It seems difficult to really appreciate this game and the events in its story if you haven't at least watched the TV series, and given how bored I felt in-game, I'm even less motivated to check out the rest of the Expanse universe than I would have been otherwise.It also doesn't help that the full story is half the length of a standard Telltale game - only 5h instead of the typical ~10h, which makes it difficult to really connect with the characters. Due to this the story feels both too fast  too slow at once, idk how but that's what it felt like.I can contrast this to another Telltale project like Tales from the Borderlands - the characters in that game are original to that project and despite being set in a larger franchise, you can greatly enjoy and appreciate that game with no knowledge of the rest of the Borderlands franchise at all. I say this because I literally had a viewing party with multiple friends who hadn't even heard of Borderlands, and they all thoroughly enjoyed it so much they wanted to check out the games too. When the same friends joined me for this Expanse game, we were all underwhelmed and frankly bored.TL;DR -I found it pretty boring and lackluster. The gameplay is standard Telltale, press X for dialog and press E to interact, but the story may fall very flat if, like me, you haven't experienced the rest of the Expanse universe.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: It's good - but it's short, by telltale standards.  My total playtime (sans DLC) is 5 hours for one playthrough, and I did about one 20-30 minute section twice because I exited the game not realizing the last checkpoint was so far back.Pros:*Standard telltale experience, but with much shorter chapters.*Very forgiving QTEs - which is good 'cause for some reason when a QTE wants you to use a trigger or bumper I practically always whiff it.*Exploration in zero G is cool - you can walk right up walls with your mag boots or just drift and use thrusters to get around.  Easy to get turned around tho.*The characters can be pretty witty sometimes - the flirting between Carmina and the martian lady was priceless.Cons:*It's a prequel and you're playing a key character - none of that tension from some of their other games where you're unsure if the main character will survive.  Literally everybody else feels up for grabs tho.*Short.*There are a few places where the checkpoints are pretty far apart, and no easy way to tell how long its been since the last save AFAICT.*Lacks the attention to detail and accuracy you see in the Expanse show - some stuff might PO some nerds.*I suspect the characters that were in it that were also on the show were chosen because they could get the voice actors, rather than those characters really making sense in that context.  They did ok with though.Things that I liked but others might not have...*There are some optional objectives in the scavenging sections that I totally wiffed (e.g. finding medicine for one of the characters).  I see it as replayability - but some people might not like the scavenger hunt aspect.*It tells you some of the ways the plot could have gone at the end of each chapter.  Kinda entices me to try it again - seems like some major plot points could have gone a totally different way.  But some people might prefer the surprise/hate the spoilers.*Puzzles are straightforwardish - only one had me stuck for any length of time.  If I wanted to play a puzzle game I.... do want to often, but telltale hasn't ever really been all that good at puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely excellent, grateful to be able to spend more time in the universe of The Expanse. One thing that really did annoy me was on my play through, Drummer sneaks behind her enemy and when she tries to shoot them she realizes her gun is empty and squanders her surprise. I hate this. There is no way Drummer would forget to check ammo. There is no way guns in a universe as practical as the Expanse don't clearly indicate to their user that they are empty.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: The Expanse is one of my favourite Sci-fi shows I have seen in a while. When I heard about this, I was all in. With that being said, I didn't know what to expect or if they would be able to capture the magic of the show. I would have to say that they did an amazing job! I had fun with the story, and the small exploration sections were done well. The atmosphere felt very much like you were in the series, and the voice acting was top notch. The experience was also very smooth, with little to no hiccups during the game play or cut scenes. For those who are fans of Telltale or The Expanse, this is worth a play. Yes, it is short, but I prefer a crafted story vs hundred hour open world padded bore fests
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: This is Telltale. The NEW Telltale. Had been releasing games with a lot of meanings, emotions and choices. They didn't disappoint that department, as well expected from Telltale. This game in particural has got a lot of coices that matter to your story and how it plays from the moment of your choice. Such a beautiful prequel to the series "The Expanse". Story 9.5/10, "Choices matters" 10/10, Graphics 10/10 and so on... Definitely would recommend to anyone who likes movies/series/games in space and a type of games that leaves such a powerful positive impact in a lot of ways.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: The, often great, Telltale developers fumbles and crashes with a dull story, excruciatingly boring game play mechanics, grey and dead world, uninteresting characters and a terrible voice actor for the protagonist.First things first. I really like Telltale games and looking forward to the Wolf among us part 2! But this one was clearly for the fans of the television show. I personally haven´t seen The Expanse and when i realised that it was the real lead actor from the show that did the voice acting for the hero (Drummer), i was surprised to say the least. When Cara Gee spoke - it sounded like when you are at the dentist with instruments in your mouth trying to talk at the same time.But, to bring up something positive - the graphic was good! Unfortunately - that was pretty much the only thing good about this game.The premise was solid. You searched shipwreckes for valuables while some of the crew forges dark plans behind your back. But the storytelling consisted mostly about ancient history, things and persons you know nothing about if you haven´t watched the tv show. So the game couldn´t stand on its own in that regard.The game play mechanics were a complete failure. You can compare it with Wolf among us. A game that suceeded to make qte:s pretty fun. Here the qte:s are a disaster. All you do is clicking the left or right mouse button. Thats it. It´s unbelievable lazy and unengaging.The world is dead, grey and dark. It´s hard to feel anyting for the world you enter - let alone to care for.Sure - you can try to care for the characters. But its hard since most of them are a dislikeable bunch of weirdos - talking with an annyoing slang. Maya is alright but not very interesting.And as i´ve already stated once before - the protagonists voice acting was a game breaker. Terrible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: "Yes, but..."If you're a big fan of the expanse, this is great! Telltale games have always been a little weak, but the intro music alone was a hit of dopamine directly into my brain. Some of the action-consequence pairs don't make a lot of sense, which is a bummer. Overall solid story and sequences. Buy it on a heavy sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: What a game. Definitely a huge recommendation. The Base Game is insane, it completely feels like a few episodes of the expanse series. So check it out if you want more story after watching the series. The DLC is very short, so you better get it in sale. But its worth it for the die-hard fans outthere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first Telltale series I've played through. I tried "The Walking Dead" but could not get the hang of the combat. However, having watched the Amazon series of "The Expanse" 3 times, I was very familiar with the characters and story. This made it easy to keep my interest and to complete the series. I finally "got" the combat style. Having completed "The Expanse", I've installed and I'm currently playing "The Wolf Among Us." I love how story rich the Telltale series are.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: IMO, the weakest link with this game is that it rode the wave of hunger for a great space game that Roberts and Todd kicked up with their marketing campaigns over the past chunk of years. The trailers and marketing alludes to a lot of WOW...but it's designed for you to look at it all, get hype, and lie to yourself about what it's gonna be like. By the time you realize what it's actually going to be like you're in deep. Hang on tight.I'm willing to bet a bunch of unsatisfied Starfield players and Space loving gamers in general found a way to this game...paid FULL price...and got let down within 30mins. It's not that this is a horrible title, there is some TELLTALE magic in it here and there. It's just some of the choices come off as unusual filler. What devs did with the art style and sound design feels high tier, but the story and options were mid. What can you really do but stay in the box of a kinda half cooked story? Time and money isn't really respected in gaming right now so it is what it is. Case in point....THE DLC. Huh?? WHAT is it and WHY charge anything at all for that?? Telltale being very Telling with that one.*Buy it full price? HEY'ALL NAW. NO WAY! NOT EVER. Highly DO NOT RECOMMEND.*Buy it on sale for super cheap so you can experience this tilted version of space for yourself? HIGHLY RECOMMEND.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: This game is neither good or bad, it's something entirely different: Content.That's... probably not too good.The game is 'a story' with 'characters' with textures from The Expanse. It's not meaningful, it's not something you will remember, it's just some hours of content.I have a hard time thinking anyone outside The Expanse fandom will think this is a really good game.Now i get it, Drummer is awesome, it's cool to see the ship design close up, but at the end of the day, it's bland content.If your really into The Expanse, the game might be worth it on sale, if not, stay away and watch the series - that's not content, that's art.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I have watched all of the series for the Expanse, I've read the books, and was really looking forward to this game.  I enjoyed it a great bit and it was nice to go through The Expanse universe and make some different decisions as I went through this part of a short Drummer series.  The voice acting is really well done and they do a great job with the environment.  I found it to be pretty good in depth and paid great homage to the whole Expanse universe.If you are a fan of The Expanse, or you're just a sci-fi fan, you'll probably find this fun.  There is a lot of open areas to explore, and while some do eventually lead to a linear end with choices, or just a "fork in the road" of choices, the areas to get there are pretty big and do require exploring, it's not just linear pathing if that makes sense.At some point I'll probably go back and replay it with different decisions to see what happens, and it's also kind of cool to see at the end of a chapter what percentage of other players make similar or different decisions.I think Telltale did a good job with this one.  The Archangel DLC on the other hand? Well that's another story...  But I'd definitely recommend the base game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: A game with my two favorites: Drummer and Avasarala! Amazing. If Bobbie was in this it would be hands down all my favs. I wouldn't recommend playing this if you're not a fan of The Expanse. It's a lot of fun, but I found the game play wonky and dealt with a few major crashes and glitches. Still a blast though. Made me want to go watch the show after I beat it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the books/series, you will probably have some fun with this game, and you will also roll your eyes at the generally bad writing, being clubbed over the head with tie-in material, and so-so game mechanics.If you can look past writing that shrugs and says stuff like "tech" and "scanners" instead of The Expanse's famous dedication to a grounded reality, there IS some good writing, and the performances of Cara Gee, Shohreh Aghdashloo (Archangel DLC) and the rest of the cast are pretty good. The broad strokes of the plot are pretty forgettable (chase the mcguffin, etc.), but there are some great character interactions that work and feel appropriate for this universe.The gameplay elements that aren't conversation... there's stuff there that all works, but none of it is very compelling. You're pretty much just filling time between conversations and decision points, and hunting around for an effectively random location where your current side objective can be satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: It seems to me that the mixed reviews here have all to do with if the player was a fan of the show.  I loved the show and I feel this game does it solid justice.  The maligned voice acting reviews I see must come from people who don't know what the Belter accent is supposed to sound like.  I think everything about this has been as enjoyable as the show.If you like the Expanse and you like gaming, I highly recommend this.If you didn't watch the show, dropping into this universe with no frame of reference is going to make the game feel shallow.  I'd say to check the show out first and see if it sticks for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: i love this game. Great story, i love the zero g gravity and looking around the room for stuff. Having never seen the expanse tv series i did not know the characters or the universe but i now love it and want to watch the tv series i give it 8 out of 10 not so fond of the bonus episode but still great story
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: It's bad. I bought this game because I loved the books, but everything in this Telltale adaptation is terrible.Plot is rehashed and uninspired, gameplay is non-existent, and puzzles are downright insulting (at one point the solution is directly behind you on a wall). Most game time is mired in slow transitions, walking scenes, and long animations. Meanwhile the voice acting is great but limited by stilted dialogue from two raunchy lesbians with zero chemistry.I'm a huge fan of the Expanse but I have no idea how this game is reviewed as Mostly Positive. You'd have a way better time reading the short side stories from James S.A. Corey. This game isn't good, not even for fans of the Expanse.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: So glad Telltale is back. I played this game without having ever watched the series it originated from, but totally got immersed in the story and loved the characters, as usual. As the story progressed you were really invested in keeping your crew alive, and it made me feel that same good anxiety from their Walking Dead years. The story is good, the bonus chapter changes things a bit managing to keep it fresh as well. I really hope more is made into this series. The one negative aspect is that they added this annoying game play element where not everything is decided based on your choices, but you do require at times some obscure items you need to find hidden in the open space ... I don't remember this mechanic in previous games from them and I honestly prefer it didn't exist. But overall I do recommend this to Telltale fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of the expanse show so my opinion is completely bias..but as a fan of the show I'd say playing this game felt like actually getting to participate in episodes of the show we wanted and didn't get.  They said "The Expanse" would "live on" and apparently... it has ^^So For Fans of "The Expanse" I'd say don't hesitate beltalowda!!!If not familiar with the show.. I still think story is worth the journey Great game for a plane trip!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Solid story and choices focused game. Especially for Expanse TV series fans - watching the show builds good background for game plot. In my opinion it is worthy (or even important) to watch show first and then play the game cause many story/character details corresponding to Expanse "uniwersum". As old gaming and sci-fi literature fan (50yo+) I'm highly recommend this title. Have fun :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game if you're a fan of The Expanse. If not I would pass on it until you watch the show, but I would definitely recommend doing so, it's probably one of the best Sci-Fi stories out there. The game is pretty limited in terms of gameplay but you should probably expect this from a telltale game, you don't buy a telltale game for the gameplay, you buy it for the story. And if you like the story of The Expanse this definitely knocks it out of the park. I've only watched the show but it gets the atmosphere just right and really feels accurate and just as good as the show in every way. Honestly my only complaint is that the game is fairly short, I was able to finish it and the DLC in under 6 hours but if you're able to pick it up on sale its definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Remember that this is a TellTale game, so there are a lot of interactive dialogs, response choices, narrative, reading, and QuickTime events, along with a smattering of gameplay. I was able to complete the game and the Archangel DLC in under 8 hours which was perfect for me as I don't have the spare time for massively long games at this stage of my life. 8-12 hours is a sweet spot.I thoroughly enjoyed the story of the main game and was engrossed in the game and the universe. As for the DLC, for the first few minutes, I did not think I would enjoy it as much as the main game. Then it wrapped me in the tendrils of its narrative and setting, and I was hooked. And that’s the case with ‘The Expanse: A Telltale Series’.If you like story rich, RPG where your choice can determinate the outcome you must play this game. Exploring the wrecks and bases, moving in zero gravity, chatting with your companions this is what it makes it so good.Visuals, facial animation, voice acting, performance capture, camera movements, and AWESOME music, are all great.The only issue I have is that it’s so bloody short, however it’s highly replayable. I hope for more chapters.

_childDocuments_.review: A Thrilling Journey Through the Belt with Camina DrummerRating: ★★★★★ (5/5 stars)Camina Drummer takes center stage in this latest Telltale adventure, and let me tell you, it's a ride worth taking! From the moment you step into the boots of this bold, no-nonsense character, you're in for a treat. With all five episodes available at launch, I couldn't help but dive right in, and I'm already hooked.The standout feature of this game, without a doubt, is the exhilarating space walks from derelict ship to ship. The zero-g environments are beautifully rendered, and the attention to detail in capturing the vastness and desolation of space is awe-inspiring. As Camina Drummer, you'll float gracefully through the darkness, navigating through the wreckage of ships long forgotten, and the feeling of weightlessness is nothing short of breathtaking.These space walks are not just a visual spectacle, but they also play a crucial role in the story and gameplay. You'll find yourself scavenging wrecked ships for valuable resources, unearthing hidden secrets, and making life-or-death decisions in the unforgiving vacuum of space. The tension is real, and every choice you make has real consequences, which is classic Telltale (I've played the Wolf Among us and thoroughly enjoyed it, I think Tell Tale as a pretty good formula and they should create more with it). The narrative is gripping, and as a fan of "The Expanse" series, it's a joy to see Camina Drummer's character explored in depth. Her strength, determination, and moral dilemmas are all front and center, and I found myself making difficult choices that ultimately shaped my destiny as the character Drummer and the fate of those around the character Drummer. The game also introduces formidable pirate adversaries who add an extra layer of excitement and danger to the story. The encounters with these ruthless foes are intense and heart-pounding, making for some of the most memorable moments in the game.After playing the first part, I'm eagerly anticipating the subsequent chapters to see how Camina Drummer's journey unfolds. The writing is top-notch, the voice acting is superb and unique, and the production values are stellar, nicely done. In conclusion, I wholeheartedly recommend "Camina Drummer: The Edge of the Belt" to fans of Telltale-style narrative adventures and "The Expanse" series. The space walks alone make it worth the price of admission, and the intriguing story and memorable characters will keep you hooked from start to finish. Don't miss out on this thrilling adventure in the far reaches of the Belt – it's a must-play for any sci-fi enthusiast!
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: Well, basically this is an interactive Expanse! Three years before the TV series, chronologically speaking. Exactly what you think it will be - slow at times, fast when needed, scary from time to time, with a good story and interesting choice. Speaking of which, I suggest you fulfill all secondary objectives before main ones, otherwise you might not have another chance (unless you're planning on re-playing and making other choices)... My only beef is mouse controls - which are un-responsive at times, e.g. you suppose to click RMB or LMB, you do - and nothing happens; or you try to interact with something, but unless you're on a specific pixel - it might not work on a first try. Not a big deal, but few times I got killed because the game refused to register an input. I think it will not be a problem on a game-pad. All in all, thumbs up for buying it for any Expanse fan. You'd be hooked from the first second (the moment the music kicks, you know which one!) :)

_childDocuments_.review: A great game if you just wanna sit back and watch the story unfold, while making your own choices. I'd say you need to have read or seen some of the Expanse in order to fully appreciate this prequel as there are frequent references to characters, events, locations and factions that are not fully explained within this story. It also focuses on Camina Drummer, a pre-existing character and I think it's fun to try and make decisions based on what you would think she'd do. However, while I did enjoy the story, I found the gameplay to be another matter. It's basic. You move through levels and interact with objects scattered throughout. During the more cinematic moments it falls back on QTE's to keep you invested in the action, though these only used 3 different buttons. On the Steam Deck there were some pretty big framerate drops, but those were mostly limited to scenes that had 1 or more ships flying in space. General gameplay did not suffer these drops.
_childDocuments_.name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series

_childDocuments_.review: What a missed opportunity...The story is OK. I was interested for the most part. Unfortunately the majority of characters are boring and undeveloped. Khan has a bit of a story and Virgil was by far the most interesting.You have the typical villain, just babbling but saying nothing. The few interactions between Drummer and the pirates show how simple the 'conflict' between them could be solved: talking. Instead there is a forced fight between the groups that comes across as unnecessary and cheesy.Another terribly forced aspect is the Maya character. Zero development, aside from her basically being angsty cause her background was boo hoo. Suddenly there is a totally forced love connection (? I don't even know wtf or where it came from, apparently Maya just REALLY wants to scissor in space with a stranger). The characters and forced story really were a let down for me. The gameplay is almost non existent but you get to explore and complete a handful of quick time challenges. I'm a fan of the Expanse show and the books so there is some inherent enjoyment to be had here. For anyone who is not, this is a lacklustre walking sim with a really thin story.Lastly, I have not played any other Telltale games but this one has the most idiotic save function. Essentially there is an autosave but it can be anywhere from 30 to 45 minutes between saves. Just let a player save when they want.

_childDocuments_.review: The Expanse definitely starts out slower than I was expecting, and for a while, I felt that the story was boring, the characters were kind of bland, and that the events during the playthrough felt like they were missing context. However, towards the end of the game starting around the end of the third episode and going into the fourth episode, that is when the true game starts in my opinion. For the most part, most of the game is going to be pretty dull, taking place in uninspired and quite frankly overly large empty areas, going in a straight line, to meet dialogue options that for the most part don't really do anything most of the time. There are side objectives but unless if you want to aimlessly wonder around doing nothing for a really long time, they aren't really worth it to do. However, why is this a recommendation? Because of the way that everything within the game evolves towards the end, in addition to it's DLC with the deluxe edition, which in my opinion is 100 percent worth it, and fixes some of the flaws with the missing context from the beginning of the game. This isn't an amazing game by any means, and it is rather short, but I thought that it was an okay experience especially when and if it goes on sale. I am going to give this game a 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I am thrilled to witness the resurgence of Telltale Games, particularly their collaboration with the creators of "Life is Strange," Deck Nine. This game represents a significant evolution in the Telltale/Deck Nine legacy, renowned for titles like "The Walking Dead" and "Life is Strange." While these games have historically centered on compelling storytelling, this latest venture introduces an exhilarating gameplay dimension – zero-gravity exploration. This novel aspect adds a layer of enjoyment I hadn't anticipated, compelling me to delve deeper into the game's world.The character of Drummer stands out as an exceptionally formidable protagonist, adding to the game's allure. As a long-time fan of the television series, my expectations were high, yet this game managed to surpass them. I initially anticipated that my enjoyment would stem solely from the narrative, but I was pleasantly surprised to find the gameplay equally captivating. My fondness for the studios behind this project and the original show may contribute to my bias, but I believe the game's immersive and engaging nature stands on its own merit. I enjoyed the bonus episode as well, especially after having watched the TV show.Looking forward to The Wolf Among Us 2.

name: Fall of Porcupine
detailed_description: Step into the town of Porcupine and take to the well-loved scrubs of Finley, the newest fledgling doctor to join the ranks of St. Ursula's hospital. As the seasons in the small-town change and life starts to stir, you'll soon realize that things aren't always what they seem: Not everyone is honest with themselves and others, the healthcare industry is not as illustrious as it seemed in medical school, and the work/life balance Finley strives toward might be impossible to achieve. Check out the 'Save the World' Edition Explore A Beautiful, Diverse World Not only is there a lot to discover in the old hospital, but also in the small town of Porcupine itself. Take the time to meet the villagers and have a beer with them in the local pub, take a trip to the nearby forest, or spend quality time with your friends. Hardened Professionals, Sweet Friends The blunt head doctor, the selfless nurse, Finley's smart friends, and many other residents populate the small town of Porcupine. Engage in funny, profound, and sometimes serious dialogues, in which you'll be able to choose your answers and influence your relationships. Demonstrate Your Skills and Empathy You don't even have time to look at the clock because your patients are waiting! Investigate what's wrong with them through your conversations and treat them in different minigames that challenge you in logic, speed, and skill. Expose Social Injustice And Structural Problems At first glance, the small town is a warm, friendly place where everyone knows and greets each other. But if you live there for any length of time, you'll suspect that not everyone is as honest as they pretend to be – especially in an unhealthy healthcare-system.

Investigate what's wrong with them through your conversations and treat them in different minigames that challenge you in logic, speed, and skill. Expose Social Injustice And Structural Problems At first glance, the small town is a warm, friendly place where everyone knows and greets each other. But if you live there for any length of time, you'll suspect that not everyone is as honest as they pretend to be – especially in an unhealthy healthcare-system.
short_description: A pidgeon-doctor in a small town. A broken healthcare system. A heartfelt narrative game. Fall of Porcupine tells an emotional story about a young doctor who struggles to find his place. Accompany Finley in a lovingly illustrated world and uncover the darkest secrets of Porcupine.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, it pains me to write a negative review about this game; I wished there was a 'mixed' option for Steam recommendations.All in all, I just can't recommend this game as it has too many flaws that outweigh the few  good things in the game.Fall of Porcupine is a game that draws heavy inspiration from Night in the Woods.Be it the art style, the character interactions, world design; if you've played NITW, you'll immediately find yourself at home.You play as a young doctor that just moved into a small town far away from everything he knows. He has to make new friends, get to know the people in town and manage the stressful shifts working in a hospital with not a lot of experience.---The story itself is great, it gives us a great insight into the life of healthcare workers and what everyone has to deal with.Anxiety. Overworking. Patients that take everything for granted.But also how rewarding this kind of work can be. Helping people, getting to know them, treating them. Nothing bets that feeling that the patients are truly grateful for all the work you are doing.The other great thing are some of the characters you really start to care for over the course of the days. They all have their fears, hopes, worries and happy moments which makes you feel really close to them.The world itself is gorgeous. Everything looks so nice, the character designs are great and you are really drawn into the atmosphere.---Most of them boil down to 'wasting the players time'.The most frustrating thing, especially comparing it to NITW, is, that the town itself is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ empty.Basically every screen is a hallway that's completely empty 95% of the time. There are some very few 'meaningful' interactions sprinkled throughout the days, but most of the town is just a slog to get through. There is an incentive to explore everything on each of the days, but there. just. isn't. anything. there.You are running and running and running and running through each of the screens, hoping to run into a person that you can have an interesting conversation with or just find something like a small secret that helps you connect with the environment, but no, most of this game is empty hallways.This game could be  three hours shorter if it would stop you from going ways where nothing is.On most of the days there are two ways to get to the hospital and you feel like you miss something if you don't go both ways every day. There are some character interactions like an NPC in the basketball court with which you come up with an idea for a comic, but these interactions are few and far between.Even in the hospital you are nudged in the direction that you visit every floor, the cafeteria and the backyard on each day, before and after your shift.Most of the time, you run for 15 seconds to the end of the hallway, just to not be able to progress, having to run back 15 seconds and repeat this ad nauseam.The screens could be 50% shorter (or the character run twice as fast) and it would be way less frustrating in the long term.Next point: the story and its pacing.This one is just wild. The first half of the game is pretty slow as you get to know everything and everyone.The second half picks up on the pace a bit at first, then slowing down again and then completely climaxing during the very end of the game when the game throws everything at you at once and then ending abruptly without you really showing what's happening afterwards with most of the characters.Quite a few NPCs you talk with are interesting at first, but then nothing happens with them. A lot of them feel 'incomplete', like there was so much missing with their story lines. It feels like there had to be more, like with the coffee truck lady or the emo kid near the school.The last big point: the bugs.To be fair: There were no game breaking bugs during my playthrough. Nothing made me restart the game because it was stuck or didn't continue properly.But oh boy, there are  of small bugs that just pull you out of the immersion all the time.* MANY small graphical bugs like objects/characters not being in the correct layer, permanent objects disappearing one day only to reappear the day after (like the paint outline), speech bubbles floating out of the screen so you can't read all the text, NPCs disappearing into walls where no door is and button prompts not vanishing completely, but instead getting stack halfway on the edge of the screen (this happened a lot)* Interaction bugs like people talking about something 'upcoming' that already happened the day before* The notes in your phone seeming to be updated after you talk with a character, only to realize that nothing changed* Minigames not reacting to button inputs at the correct time (especially the stethoscope one)* Achievements being granted for 'hearing every story of an NPC' while there are still a few left in the following daysIt seems there were many things fixed after the release, but seeing that the first patches were frequent and last patch was over two months ago, it doesn't seem that these things will ever get fixed.A few minor complaints:* The phone functions were lackluster; they could have had more text message interactions and more information on the citizens after you talk with them -> immersion!* I played with a controller and the button pressing mini game was impossible with just the two hands, I had to use my nose nearly every time to be able to press every prompt simultaneously---I hate to give this game a thumbs down.There is so much love and passion felt in this game. I wish I could have loved this game for what it strived to be, but in the end, the negatives are just too many.The game just feels unfinished, unpolished and directionless; two halves of different great ideas added together don't always make one good idea.Either the town parts has to be way more interactive, more compact, more NPCs and things to find.Or the hospital part has to be a bigger part of the game.I enjoyed some moments of the game quite a lot, but in the end everything else felt like it was wasting my time too much to recommend this with good conscience.

_childDocuments_.review: Want to preface this with up until the final act I would have given this a thumbs up. I could look past all the shortcomings and praise it as an incredible first effort at a game release. But it just took took a step too far into the red at the end there.:: The good ::Art/VibeFall of Porcupine is a beautifully presented game. The art and atmosphere is incredible. And at times I questioned whether I actually preferred the art-style and atmosphere over that of its spiritual predecessor, and honestly I think I do. They have done a great job at building the world and vibe they set out to. And must make an extra note of the character rigs. They are so bouncey, full of life, and expressive! The game feels great.:: Not a deal-breaker ::MusicThe music itself was very good. However something I noticed while playing is that it is a very quiet game. Occasionally I felt like something was missing and very quickly realised little to no sound was present in the scene at all. I understand this is used intentionally in some cases but too often it just seemed to be missing, and would have otherwise boosted the atmosphere and general feel of the game to another level.:: The not so great ::This game had massive potential and has obviously drawn a lot of comparison between another game involving a town of animals, fall themes, crisp picture-book-esque lineless art direction, dialogue balloons, and sarcastic humor, packed into a narrative based side-scrolling platformer. And it initially looked like it was going to be able to stand on its own two legs against it very very convincingly. However unfortunately it just doesn't quite make it there on a few levels.Bugs/GameplayCertain keyboard keys don't correspond with the UI prompts. Gamepad can be unresponsive at times. Moved back onto PC only to find that some games were literally uncompletable on keyboard. For example, one mini-game requires you to hold down multiple keys (4-5 keys) which seems to stop working after holding two, causing you to immediately bomb multiple unrepeatable parts of the game. Another mini-game seemingly has no instructions on how to play it and despite playing it multiple times through the game, still could not figure out what was required for an "A grade" by the end. NOTE: And on the briefly on subject of grades (because I don't want make a whole other section for it), the grades/mini-games are such a large part of padding out the game time just for them all to seemingly not mean or amount to anything by the end.The game also suffers from some clipping/z-axis issues where parts of characters or props will clip/overlap over one another in passing. I once witnessed this following what should have been a hard hitting scene. Instead I woke up immediately following that scene then proceeded to fly from my bed to the other side of the room while still laying down and asleep, which sort of ruined the mood.NPC movement AI is also quite buggy causing them to be left behind often.WritingFor the most part the writing is solid. At times the humor seems to attempt to emulate that of its spiritual aforementioned predecessor and sometimes meets that mark, and other times doesn't. Otherwise the dialogue is perfectly fine and enjoyable to read.The structure of the narrative on the other hand is not great. Most of the time when it comes to your relationships and learning more about other characters it seems to be a bit of an exposition dump. Instead of building a relationship with the characters throughout the game and the payoff being some personal reveal or hard hitting scene near the end, characters you are hanging out with for the first time seem to abruptly give you their life story by the end of your first hangout and then aren't much further developed upon after that.I was enjoying myself regardless for the first two acts but felt like something was missing that was stopping me from getting fully immersed in the story. It turns out it was because of the seeming lack of one, which was subtly missing from the chit-chat up until that point. The overarching story beyond "slice-of-life pigeon goes to first job and is nervous" doesn't really take shape until the final act and then the game is over. I spent the first two acts wondering what the main plot thread actually was. In retrospect the seeds of the final plot are dotted around the early game but they mean very little until the last act and don't give you a solid enough sense of what the mystery is, or even if there is a mystery in the first place. At best they are hints that there could be a plot, maybe. So by the time it actually comes out that there is indeed an actual overarching something going on to be theorising about, you're already an hour or two away from the credits.The game does a great job at setting the immediate scene (and town in general) and capturing the everyday events taking place presently in-front of Finley, but has a hard time developing on both characters and the story outside of that over the length of the game.The EndingI was writing this review as a recommendation in my head as I was playing as I could look past everything that has been said, enjoy it for everything it does well, and praise it for being a great first release. But the ending just put an unforgettable damper on everything.(Vague spoilers)Edit: days later and I'm still thinking about this review. Wish I could give a neutral rating. On a couple of levels I love this game a lot. But it keeps coming back to the thought of how a third of the story feels missing.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall of Porcupine is a unique narrative adventure focusing on the healthcare system and frontline workers. Despite the anthropomorphic characters, the themes discussed are quite heavy and I would not label this in the “cozy games” category. However, I do have mixed feelings about it. Whilst its shortcomings cannot be ignored, I did enjoy my playthrough and reflective nature of the game, but my recommendation is a borderline one.You play as Finley, the town of Porcupine’s newest arrival and also, their newest resident doctor. After finishing medical school, Finley joins St Ursula’s hospital alongside another new junior doctor. Together they learn the ropes of their new career and navigate the challenges of the hospital. Finley befriends other townsfolk and spends time getting to know everyone in the small village.Despite the cozy synopsis and look of the game, reality starts to set in. Finley first experiences the very real issue of struggling with his work-life balance. After a full day on his feet, his apartment becomes messier, he no longer has the time or energy to do things after his shift finishes and this strain on his mental health becomes the new norm. Without discussing spoilers, there are also much larger societal themes discussed that centre around the healthcare system, with the story ramping up excessively in the concluding moments of the game that is almost unrecognisable in comparison to its modest beginning.Fall of Porcupine is a lengthy game for the genre and gameplay style, at roughly 9-10 hours long, there is a lot of repetition and filler content. In the first Act, I was almost falling asleep with the lack of any real purpose or goal for Finley. Slowly clicking through the text bubbles, walking from A to B felt endless. Many interactions, conversations and tasks could have been at least halved in time. Despite this, in the latter half of the game, it does improve, and most of the dialogue between characters was enjoyable to read. However, the bizarre, repeated dialogue with the vending machine and statues felt out of place for the game.Overall, I am glad that I persisted, as it does get much better than my initial impressions of its first few hours. The fog clears and the focus of the game’s intent becomes finer, and much more interesting. Enough to convert my overall view of it into a positive one.Players follow Finley, a newcomer to the town of Porcupine. The gameplay can be surmised by the following actions: going from Finley’s apartment to the hospital, reading through extensive dialogue, completing minigames at the hospital and then walking back home.  The town is not enormous, however there is no map, and with the amount of walking involved, it feels as if everything is too far away from each other. There are very minimal interactions that can occur on your morning or afternoon walks to and from work, so I do not see any purpose to having them take the time it does. This is my most common gripe with the game, as many of the games non-core decisions seem to have little purpose to it, only extending gametime. As aforementioned, the first Act felt like a slog, and I struggled to continue, however after a few hours, things began improving and I was more drawn into the story. The characters and dialogue are interesting, but it takes too much time to start caring for the story than it should. There are only a handful of decisions to make in the game, but they do lead to different minigames and explores one of the two main characters (Karl & Mia) a bit more. I only wish it were easier to see the other decisions without having to replay the whole game again.Despite my critiques with the game, I did enjoy the banter and relationships between characters. They felt realistic and the dialogue almost always had a purpose (except with the inanimate objects…) Although the introduction to the game displays a warning about its themes, after 8 hours I had swiftly forgotten this and upon its finale, I was in for a shock. Whilst the game is cute and kid-like on the outside, what it discusses is very much for mature audiences, but this is not a complaint, per say, I very much liked this change in direction. Whilst the repetitiveness of the game does take away from the overall impact, the respect, honesty, and vulnerability shown in the portrayal of frontline healthcare workers felt authentic. Furthermore, some of the conversations centred around the general publics opinion of hospitals were extremely thought provoking, prompting players to think from the healthcare workers perspective. This reflective and deep narrative was my favourite element to the game, despite being somewhat overshadowed by its earlier uniformity.Finley is a junior doctor and is closely monitored by more senior staff on his performance. He is tasked to treat a minimum of three patients a day, listening to their health issues and treating or diagnosing as appropriate. This is where the minigames begin. There are only a few different types, but I enjoyed most of them. Ranging from simple rhythm puzzles, deducing a specific set of symbols through trial and error and more. The difficulty felt just right, without being too challenging nor too easy, and was a fun addition.Fall of Porcupine is gorgeous. It reminded me of a similar style seen in  except with a softer, more pastel approach. Each character generally has large, round Disney-like eyes and most backgrounds are bright, cute, and detailed. The art is unanimously gorgeous, and one of the game’s best features.There is no voice acting and I had ample issues with audio (as discussed below). I did experience a hefty number of glitches. Audio commonly cut off and left many scenes in dead silence. Many visual issues with characters during the Winter Festival clipping into the sky, showing up haphazardly. If I used the stairs in the hospital, often I became stuck and could not exit from any door, having to reload the save. During the Festival scene, when trying to leave the area, instead of hitting a wall, I would get stuck off-screen where the camera would not pan, but I could not walk back into view, with the only solution having to reload the save again. Not necessarily a glitch, but there are SO many loading screens between every scene which felt entirely unnecessary.  9-10 hours. YesFall of Porcupine is a unique, narrative-driven adventure that encompasses heavy topics, juxtaposing its cute exterior. Whilst it has a few too many bugs and issues with its pacing, the story, dialogue, and conclusion are memorable and made me enjoy my time in Porcupine. Overall, I recommend waiting for a heavy sale on this one as my recommendation is a borderline.
