_childDocuments_.review: This was, uhhh, rough around the edges, for sure.First off, the art style is beautiful, and the music is fantastic. It gave me big Night in the Woods vibes, who knows, maybe that was a bit of an inspiration, or maybe not. A little thing I also like is how the main menu changes depending on the act you are in, which is cool.The gameplay, for the most part, is pretty good; some of the minigames are nice; there are puzzles here and there; a tad of platforming too; it was neat, but its main focus is certainly the story which is cool.Now the story, the main focus, was pretty decent, I'd say. For the most part, I get what they were going for, and it's pretty good. Some of the writing and dialogue is pretty interesting, with some being funny; it was cool, although as per the description it's also about a broken healthcare system, which, in the gameplay and throughout the game, is not really shown, not that much at least, except maybe a few times does it show or mention/imply something like money and the building not being all that sturdy, which the latter is more on the budget not being done correctly than a broken system, which speaking of budget does get touched upon, so that was cool. But yeah, other than that only if you go out of your way to talk and explore, do you then get a few more mentions of overworking and money and the hospital being understaffed, it could have shown more, which could have helped make the events later in the game come across a bit better or more reasonable (well, as reasonable as an event like that can get), I think. Maybe it's meant to be like that as subtext, and not meant to be obvious or shown all the time, so this might be just me. But for the most part, I liked the story for sure. That ending too was, wow, quite something, and the epilogue plus the music, again, gave me vibes of the NitW game. I don't know why, but I think that's a good thing.Another little thing with dialogue is all the things Finley says, especially the little stories and conversations he has with statues and whatnot. It was cool., wow, this had bugs. Let's start off with the menu itself. At the start of the game, using the mouse to navigate the menu is iffy, so it's better to use the keyboard or, I guess, the controller.Other minor bugs would be many typos throughout the game, some examples being off the bat in the phone messages and with Finley talking to the town square statue; visual bugs with some text bubbles being off screen or halfway off, like with Mia asking you about basketball or with the girl talking about comics; some dialogue doesn't take into account which choice you made of going with Mia or Karl. There were also visual bugs like Mia's chair in the bar being in front of her or Mr. Arndes has his arms and head in the top layer so if you walk to him you'll be under those parts but over his torso.A step ahead of those are: the game not triggering the correct bubble because you decided to talk instead of moving forward; problems using WASD in the notes app in the phone; The main menu changes reset upon closing and re-opening the game; you can trigger an achievement, for example, getting X amount of stories, by simply reloading each time after a story; I guess the achievement triggers on a number instead of each type of story heard.The most egregious bugs, though, would have to be straight up a scene can reset if you decide to talk to someone; for example, in the 'leak' scene, if you talk to Irma, it resets the whole thing, and you have to go through it again. There's also the terrible minigame (in my opinion) of the moving line? It's used when hearing lungs or heartbeats, where you have to press the correct button in the correct line at the correct time. Yeah, that's the worst one to have a bug; half my inputs weren't registering at times, which was not fun, that's for sure. In the minigame tutorials, for the bar one, it gives the tutorial of the basketball one.So yeah, quite a few bugs this had, with at least most not taking away too much from the game. The credits stated a lot of beta testers, but given the amount of bugs still left in the game, I think they should have gone through it one or two more times to get the last few bits ironed out. I swear that minigame one was barely playable sometimes. Another nitpick would be that the grades are still there in the very last bit of the game, which, given the circumstances, I would say isn't needed, so it could have been removed, but that's a small thing., it was a beautiful game with fantastic music and a decent story. Just mind the occasional bug that you'll likely see. At the very least, they don't take much from the game, most of them, at least. It certainly gave me NitW vibes, which, to me, is a good thing.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game.  I was waiting to review this to see about getting a patch.  The developers were really responsive and the glitch I experienced was fixed and the game played fine.    Let’s talk Night in the Woods comparisons.  The art style is similar, as well as the movement.  There is a little bit of jumping required, but it is on the level of Night in the Woods and is very easy.  Your character also has multiple friends, so the player will have to choose who to spend free time with, meaning two play throughs are necessary to have all the experiences, but they are side treks really and playing once gives the whole story.The story is very different.  This game is an ode to health care workers trying their best in a system that is restrictive, underfunded, understaffed, and, in this case, corrupt.  The seriousness of the topic is balanced by many light hearted and tender moments with the members of a small town where everyone knows everyone.  There are a lot of optional interactions.  You can take the bus straight to/from work and get on with it, or you can wander around talking to everyone you can.  I think the more you put into it, the more you will get out of the game.There are mini-games for treating the patients, e.g., a mastermind-like game, prescription balancing, hitting the button at the right time for injections, etc. and other mini-games for some of the outings.  They were very simple, and there is an option to turn them off or at least make them even easier.  Passing or failing any of these doesn’t change the story.  I think they are there to add game play and break up the walking and talking that is the meat of the game.There is only an autosave, which saves pretty frequently.  I wasn’t bothered by it.  I think it was purposeful so you have one game experience and can’t bop back and forth between decisions.  I think the price was fair for both play time and game quality.  I recommend this game for people who enjoy story intensive games.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game day of release, hoping to enjoy it as much as Night in the Woods, which is an obvious inspiration to this game. However I had multiple issues, not including bugs. PROS: - good, likable characters (which honestly? All the characters were so nice, it was somewhat bland)- amazing art style- A trigger warning at the start of the game which I found to be greatly helpfulCONS:- story has no real hook, plot or ending. You're basically just walking around town for half the game. I kept playing, and thinking "when's the plot gonna kick up?" but it never did- The minigames are pretty awful. The entire "game" part of the minigames is things like... playing "Mastermind", pressing buttons quickly enough, etc. Where there's no real fun to be had. I played every minigame, and to be honest they were really boring.- If you suck at the minigames, you get nothing but a bad grade. Aside from ptsd from my school years, it literally affect the plot ZERO times. if you do badly, the evaluator will be like "not your best work" and that's it.- The plot is super slow and sub-par. I kept wondering "how are they going to end this?" and they just... didn't. - Nothing felt like it really mattered. - the "platformer" bits are genuinely so easy I was curious as to how or why they were even in there. _childDocuments_.review: Fall of Porcupine is a charming game with a great concept that will resonate the most with healthcare workers. It shows the struggles of working in a hospital, the responsibilities, the workload, the guilt, and the passion to help people. I often see comparisons of this game with Night in the Woods, but I had trouble connecting with characters from NITW and I thought the main character was irritating. In Porcupine, Finley, his friends, colleagues, and the townspeople are very endearing and likable. The art style of this game is beautiful, with gorgeous light effects and scenery. I felt very emotional at times, and I enjoyed meeting new patients and following them over a few in-game days.However, there are a few negative points I want to talk about. First, the ending of the game. It felt so rushed, unsatisfying, and I really did not expect the game would stop at that point. I was really surprised and frustrated when the credits started rolling. So many things left unresolved:  I really felt disappointed that all these questions would stay without an answer. I have nothing against open endings, but this just felt rushed, like the team could not go further with the story because of time constraints. Another minor thing: While the minigames are fun and diverse, the difficulty is not balanced at all for some of them. The treatment (when you have to press multiple keys/buttons at the same time) is absolutely not ergonomic with a controller (I have only 2 hands!) and the rhythm game is also very difficult (and I am used to playing rhythm games).

_childDocuments_.review: - If you enjoy the art direction of 2017's excellent title Night in the Woods or the more recent Beacon Pines, you're bound to enjoy the look of this game. The characters are all cute little animals in an art style that matches the detail and richness of the environments they reside in- The music is also really good. Most of it is morose sounding piano, string, and vocal arrangements with some percussion thrown in. In the more hectic moments, the percussion ramps up to pair with the introduction of grimy synth- In all, presentation isn't where this game fails. It's most of its other aspects that are disappointing- You play the role of Finley, a fresh out of school M.D. who moves from his big city campus to complete his residency at a hospital in the small dying town of Porcupine. The failures of the town and the paucity of its budget have clearly had an impact on the crumbling, outdated hospital. This has initiated a death spiral of disappointing medical outcomes leading to less funding and poorer reputation and, in turn, worse outcomes again to keep situation circling the drain- It's a sad story, and as a professional in the medical field, I can tell you that it's depressingly common- The story follows the now-rocky relationship between the town and the hospital through Finley's eyes, culminating in a stressful and gut-wrenching event that will change the town forever. Or maybe not. I couldn't tell you, because the game ends incredibly abruptly.- In all, Fall of Porcupine is essentially a 5-act play in 3 acts. By that, I don't mean they crammed a classically-structured play into 60% of the expected runtime. I mean that you see the exposition (Act I), rising action (Act II), and the climax (Act III). Then it just ends. No falling action. No denouement. It's just over and you get nothing to tie up the story other than a paltry post-credits sequence that explains nothing- It's disappointing, because the character development is extremely good. So was the narrative setup. I was so invested in the game up until it ended that the first thought in my head after the shock of seeing the credits roll was: "Why did they do this? To see how well they could tell 3/5 of a story?"- I suppose the devs may be trying to make a statement with the ending choice, but it ultimately just feels like the game is unfinished. Sure, not everything in life or love gets a tidy bow put on it to let you know it's finished. But come on. Life doesn't just end with tragedy. How we pick ourselves up, heal, and move on is just as important as (if not more important than) the precipitating tragedy and its causes. So even if the point being made is some fickle cynical moral regarding life's unsatisfying endings, this game is still unfinished whether whoever wrote it thinks it is or not- I don't even care about the vibes anymore because now I'm mad from thinking about the plot again. Doesn't really matter how the game makes you feel if it just angers you in the end- Fall of Porcupine owes credit to Night in the Woods beyond the artistic references. The perspective and gameplay are less "references" and more "copies"- You have weird dreams every night, then wake up. You go about the town being sure to talk to everyone (maybe even doing a little platforming in order to find secrets), then settle in for a daily routine that changes the time of day. Afterwards, you choose to hang out with one of two friends, but note that your choice of one precludes hanging out with the other for that evening. There's also minigames- See? Same. Except the minigames in Fall of Porcupine are worse and full of bugs (see next section). The Mastermind-clone diagnosis minigame felt especially lazy and and had unnecessarily unforgiving requirements. I had to add backpaddle bindings to comfortably play the procedure minigame despite whatever the specifications say about controller and/or Steam Deck compatibility. The rhythm minigame was so sloppy that it made me feel like I was just suggesting inputs with my controller rather than timing button presses- I wouldn't consider replaying this game unless there were a free update that contained an ending. I certainly wouldn't buy it as DLC with the content-to-dollars ratio of my experience already so weighed against my favor- This game raised my hopes and dashed them expertly- The game didn't even play well owing to all the bugs. I got stuck on geometry. I experienced horrible input lag or poor detection on the rhythm minigames (oh, look, something else Night in the Woods has, and has implemented better). I went through two crashes that erased progress between autosaves. Not sure how much that had to do with playing on the Steam Deck, but other reviews suggest I'm not alone in these complaints- I understand that something being incomplete doesn't make it necessarily bad. Kafka's The Trial and Gogol's Dead Souls were neat books, but they're unfinished because the authors croaked before wrapping them up. If I learn that Fall of Porcupine's writer unfortunately passed away before finishing the story, I'll be happy to change my review, but until then, my opinion is going to remain low- . There's parts of a good game under all the mess, but the incompleteness is baffling and makes Fall of Porcupine impossible to recommend

_childDocuments_.review: There is something about this game, the atmosphere's great, character design is awesome and cute but story-wise this game lacks a lot, some plotlines are just left hanging, they're implied at best never to be brought back again, the "mystery" becomes relevant towards the end of the game. Gameplay Wise it's a really mixed bag, minigames can be RIDDICULOUSLY HARD, but then again failing doesn't translate into anything (also grading system is bonkers I got S mark most of the time, yet stil got ":(" face near the mark). Optimization needs more work, during major event in game devs decided to sprinkle in some particle effects which were so bad, that my game first lost sound, then froze entirely. City feels empty, there's no point in exploring, if you are not supposed to be talking to NPC, they won't be interactive, some token lines of text would do.The game brought up some emotions, interesting plotlines but it feels like there was no point to it all. Pros:- Atmosphere of lovely German town- Cute characters,- Kid friendly,Cons:- Plot feels unfinished,- Bugs- Most of the time I had no idea when the game is saved- Optimization- minigames

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love Fall of Porcupine. It's got a lot going for it, chiefly its fantastic art style, animation, and general vibe, but unfortunately a number of elements come together to frustrate more than delight.First and foremost, it's buggy. I've seen cutscenes play twice, dialogue be cut off by the screen edge, dialogue seemingly completely missing, interaction prompts appear for objects that don't actually lead to an interaction, environments load up seemingly in the wrong state (e.g. bright when the characters are still correctly lit for night time), character clothes appear on the wrong Z-layer, tutorial boxes show keyboard controls when I'm using a controller. This even leads to soft locks - entering the bar after the second day's shift causes the environment to load up with no characters inside, and the door doesn't let you exit, requiring the player to quit out and load back in at a checkpoint to proceed. This bug seems to be locking me out of the "Drinks and Games" achievement too, which just adds to the frustration. During a later sequence an NPC required for a side quest didn't spawn in to the level, meaning I had to spend seven minutes watching a timer tick down before seeing the NPC spawn in mid-air during the next cutscene, and float off the side of the screen never to be seen again.Aside from straight-up bugginess, there are frustrations elsewhere too. Some of the mini-games control in quite a clunky fashion and don't add a whole deal to the experience. In particular, one mini-game that requires holding down multiple buttons or stick directions on the controller at the same time seems like quite an accessibility nightmare. Thankfully the score you get from these games doesn't affect the overall narrative, but it feels very awkward indeed.I'd also say that the environments are simply too large and take too long to navigate. The art assets are really lovely and the screen effects like glowing and reflections help them pop a lot, but nearly all of the areas could have done with being condensed into smaller spaces in an effort to quicken the pace a little. I don't feel a cafeteria in a game should take an entire 20 seconds to cross, for example. This is further exemplified during interactions with a pair of patients where dialogue was bouncing back and forth between all three characters, but due to them being situated in beds on opposite sides of a large room, a lot of the dialogue was merely being shouted at us from off-screen. I wanted to be able to see all the characters at once!And speaking of things taking too long, the pace of the plot really does start out and stay pretty glacial for a while. It eventually picks up quite significantly and then ends very abruptly, with quite a few loose ends and nothing in the way of closure. I think that might be part of the point, but I felt I lost the overall thematic thread of the game somewhere along the way while wishing I could concentrate more on what was going on and worrying less that something would halt my progress entirely.I'll say this though - I really wanted to know what happened. The world and characters that were built up were very compelling and it's almost heartbreaking that they're not being presented in the way that they deserve.I hope that with time and a number of patches that the overall quality of the game could be raised to the point that technical issues wouldn't be such the sour note that they have been for me, but sadly as of right now, that's not the case.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was gearing up to be really enjoyable but ended at the climax of the story. I was just starting to get really invested in the characters when the game just...stops. There were plot points that didn't get tied up, potential character growth that didn't happen, and moving around the large map felt like a chore.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I'd go far enough to say that this is the most important narrative game to come out in a good while, even if I can't recommend it to absolutely everyone. For as gorgeous and picturesque as the town of Porcupine is, Finley and the rest of the St. Ursula's crew go through a lot to say the least. It's both a lovely story about life and death on its own as well as a poignant reflection of society and its attitudes toward the healthcare industry. Despite the culture barrier with the devs being from Germany, I could see so many parallels to healthcare system here in the USA. As long as you can handle the more triggering themes, please give Fall of Porcupine a bit of your attention. This is a story that's going to stick with me for years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I want to like this game – I can see the potential here to be a great game, but it just falls short.The art style and characters are great – and the concept for the story is a good idea, I can see what they were trying to tell here. But ultimately, it is half baked – the game just ends at what I would consider halfway (or maybe ¾) through what is really needed. Which is extremely frustrating and disappointing! The game itself has several bugs present, in a single playthrough there were about 4 times that things just failed to trigger, and I was left meandering around the levels waiting for something to happen, before reloading the game in the hopes that it would fix something. Additionally, autosaves do not happen frequently enough, resulting in having to replay a lot of the game over again. I get why gameplay wise they included puzzles to be ‘doctoring’, but they are convoluted, poorly explained, and buggy. They also do not make any sense as ‘doctor’ activities -- a 5-year-old has a better grasp of what a doctor does then the minigames. But I do see that the game needed something here to make you feel pressured to perform with a ticking clock. But honestly, they are just a source of frustration, because of the lack of polish.In short, it just feels underbaked and released too soon. It has also been 9 months since the last patch - so there is clearly no intent to fix any of the remaining bugs. I would say it is best to avoid, unless you get it really cheap and have nothing better to do with your life.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall of Porcupine This game is about a young doctor named Finley who just started at his first hospital. There he has to deal with patients, new co workers and a boss who has extremely high standards.Besides that he moved to a new city where he doesn't know anyone and is trying to make friends.We're getting an in depth look into how to balance your busy work life and still wanting to have a social life as well.It's a super lovely game that's based on true stories from real people who work in a hospital.The game has fun little mini games in between the stories and dialogue.I absolutely love the artwork! It's super cute and the colors are soothing for the eyes.Due to the game looking so cute, some of the darker parts of the game hit harder. Shouldn't be allowed!Achievement wise this game requires you to replay it (atleast) twice. You keep getting 2 options to choose from so for the second run you need to choose the other option.Having to replay this game is no punishment at all! It gives you more about all the characters and the story. I give this game a 8/10The game is great, the characters are great, the dialogues can be fun and the game makes me feel things!

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: This is not a terrible game. It's fine. I just would not recommend that you spend a whole lot of money to play it. The game feels unfinished, and borrows too heavily from Night in the Woods. Long Story: Fall of Porcupine, according to the devs, was supposed to be a love letter to heath care workers. I didn't come away with that feeling after playing through the game. What I came away with was a rushed and (I am sorry to say) uninspired attempt to replicate the game play experience of Night in the Woods. More precisely, the team borrowed five qualities from NITWs gameplay and story1) The setting: An old declining town past it's prime. The residents have a love/hate relationship with it. The player is encouraged to explore and learn more about the residents.  In NITWs, the player had a lot to do and explore. Lots of optional content, and plenty of other NPCs to learn and get to know. Exploring the city and engaging with the town NPCs was part of the fun. In Fall of Porcupine, there isn't much to do in the city. Sure, you can explore, but there isn't much to find. And there is, as far as I can tell, no serious optional content to take on. The NPCs also do not have anything interesting to say. Really, it's a lot of dead air. The only thing you really do is walk from your house to the hospital. Ugh! 2) The changing of seasons: This sounds silly. But both games begin with the onset of fall and use this as a thematic element. In NITWs, the main character had dropped out of college and was struggling to find a pathway into adulthood. She was transitioning into a new "Season of Life". FOP attempts to portray  this as well, but it feels out of place. Our main character is a med school grad and has a nice job at a hospital. Sure, the hospital is old and declining, but our main character choose to work there. As far as we know, he could have gone anywhere. His boss is a pain in the neck at first, but he is going to have to join the club on that one. 3) Relationship simulation: In addition to the main story, there are junctures where the main character selects one of the side characters to spend time with and learn more about. In NITWs, we get to learn more about these side characters, develop our relationship with them, and these side stories weave their way into the main story. In FOP, we kind of get to learn more about the side characters, but you don't get much in the way of relationship simulation. What you do get to learn about these side characters is not particuraly interesting. Moreover, these side stories do not have much relevance to the main story. (Disclosure: I only played through the "Karl" route). The patient interactions were a missed opportunity. The game treats your relationship with the patients as an afterthought. This could have been some great relationship simulation. The relationship between doctors and patients hasn't been explored much in games. There was potential for some emotional weight here, but the devs were too fixated on using the NITWs template.  4) MinigamesI won't go into comparisons here. As many, many others have pointed out, there isn't much of a point to the minigames in FOP. Some of them are broken, others are impossible on a controller.  5) The art styleThe art style in FOP is quite nice! But again, it is more or less a replica of NITW. It is great that they captured the look and feel of NITWs graphics. But the inherent risk in doing that is that you invite comparisons to a very well-received game. I won't go any further on my gripes with the game (the music, characters, and setting), and I don't want to knock the creators too hard. They do seem like a sweet group of people with good intentions. And this game is not terrible. I think the lesson learned is that you need to make your own game - this game feels like it used NITWs as a template. And if you draw inspiration from other sources, you need to find ways to mix things up and make it your own. There was a lot of potential here.

_childDocuments_.review: [WARNING POSSIBLE GAME SPOILERS]----For the developer's first game, this is very promising! It's a wonderful letter to those working in the medical industry and the game itself is a good experience. It had a bit of a slow start, but after getting to know the characters and the town I found myself invested in even the mundane points in the game play.That being said, unfortunately, I feel very led on by the plot of this 'story rich' game... When the game description says: 'uncover the darkest secrets of Porcupine and it's residents', I expected more going on than just the secrets of St. Ursula's Hospital. I'm aware that the hospital and the characters in it are the focus of the game, however, based on the push back from skeptical/bitter residents, the mold of the fifth floor ward, the mystical ambiance of those passed surrounding the forest's memorials, the questionable hot water being sent through an old fountain to be used for the festival's stew cook off, the missing archive documents, and the townspeople suddenly falling ill thus having hospital reaching max capacity, then the hospital catching on fire and evacuation - I really thought the next part of the game would be about exposing *why* all those people fell ill and the town's hidden history, then leading to the fall of Porcupine? The hospital is only a small part of the entire town.Instead, after all that happens, the game just -- ends? Our characters watch the sun rise as we see the hospital nearly burnt to the ground in the distance. There isn't even a solid confirmation on whether a majority of the town was saved or not after tending to patients in critical condition. Mind you, I know the story was ultimately about the unhealthy healthcare-system, but the reasoning as to why felt shoehorned in so the game could have some form of narrative substance before the end brings you to a halt. I was led to believe that the town's water was contaminated by a mold bacteria which made everyone become gravely ill after eating the stew at the festival's cook off, and thus after helping the townspeople, to then 'uncover the darkest secrets of Porcupine and its residents'. Perhaps it was my fault for reading too deep into the game's story, but based on the information that the game gave me, and the fact this game is tagged *story rich* - mind drew these conclusions and felt quite disappointed by the end of the game having no answers.I understand making games is hard, and that maybe the developers wanted to go harder with the story and characters, but simply ran out of time/ didn't have the budget - it happens. It's just that it happens a little too often with other story rich games. I'm all about drawing my own conclusions in a game, however, the set-up makes it feel like a huge chunk of the narrative is just missing - and I'm sad because I liked this game and wanted more from it's overall message.The game itself is pretty bare bones and not challenging, which is why I depended on the story a bit more. Some of the controls and button inputs can be unresponsive or break sometimes, though, personally it didn't hinder my game play by a lot - it's just annoying to deal with on occasion.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: Initially I was so excited to play this game, it seemed like my perfect game and i was eagerly awaiting its release date. However, after completing the game I am left with an unsatisfied and angry feeling due to how slow the game was initially followed by a sharp build up and no climax. For their first game they have the artwork and music down beautifully, but where it fails is its story. The conversations are long and tedious, you don't really learn anything from them. I didn't enjoy talking to any of the side characters as I felt it was unnecessary. I found only two of the mini games enjoyable, but even if you fail them there's no consequences so there's no real sense of pressure to do them right, you'll pass anyway. A 'C' grade is the same as an 'A' grade, it doesn't affect either short or long term performances. The game has a slow build up, which isn't bad for a more relaxed gameplay, but the story suddenly spikes and claims to have all this tension with no release. There's no explanation for  they just are. The reveal of  . The ending was so abrupt it left me staring at the credits in utter shock because there was no resolution. The story felt cobbled together for the third act, as if they didn't have enough time to develop it and so decided to go with a half-assed rushed idea. I also experienced many typos, which for a story driven game is unacceptable. The dialogue between characters is what makes the story and it really broke your immersion to constantly be seeing typos. The dialogue would also sometimes repeat itself, or just not start so the screen was just frozen. There was a few graphical bugs, such as some of Finley's outfits appearing in the wrong scenario (winter hat and scarf with pyjamas). Also when waking up in bed Finley would sometimes float across his apartment. These bugs were to be expected from me, seeing as the game has only just released and it is their first game, but I hope they get them fixed soon. They've managed to portray some of the struggles health workers go through, but that seems to be the whole game. There isn't an overarching story that makes you want to invest more time exploring the town, and the game has no consequences  for any action you do. In my opinion it's an insult to compare this game to Night In The Woods, whose story is crafted so elegantly.

_childDocuments_.review: The similarities to Night in the woods are undeniable. The game plays slightly differently than the Demo version, with less interactive dialogue while doing things like leaping on the receptionist's desk, which I feel detracts from the game as a whole, making it more linear than it already is. Though I have been enjoying the game thus far, despite all the bugs and typos. Every now and then, after interacting with the world or reloading a save because you wanted to do something different before travelling to a new area or returning to work, the game would hard-lock. So because the game doesn't have a manual save it will reload to your previous save file and potentially disable your phone. Meaning you have to shut off the game completely to fix the issue. It is very annoying as it just comes about at random moments, ruining the time.There are numerous translation mistakes, as I assume this game was originally created in German.Certain mini games during your task will force you into a B or C rating no matter how many times you restart your save file and do the night over again perfectly. Example: The Brothers, you have to inject them with needles and administer their medicine, there is 0 indication on how to do it, but I did it the way I knew I needed to do it, but no matter how many times I tried I could only get the first brother to get a A and no matter how many times I tried his brother (on the left side of the room) is always a B, no matter how perfect I know I have done it. Update: Some of these issues have been fixed, but they still remain for some.No manual saves, which means until you finish a shift you'll start from the very beginning. The game will hard-lock often because it seems like there was no beta testers actually going out of their way to leave the locations they were in and explore the placed at night and go places they shouldn't be interacting with NPCs in previous or future interactions and many other game breaking things. Example: Flower on the window due to the wind, leave the apartment. Hard locked with interactions with the other characters you saw the prior day. If you play for an extended amount of time, the audio becomes distorted and very static which is remedied by restarting the game.If you liked the Night in the Woods story, you'll probably enjoy this one as well. The main character spends a lot of time talking to himself, which is both relaxing and amusing. Adding funny voices to the characters makes it much more endearing, unsure if it will turn into a spooky scary dark twist or anything, but so far it's been fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: This is proving to be a pretty difficult game to review.  On the one hand, I enjoyed myself, and that's enough for a positive review.  The character designs are visually fantastic and consistently-written, the soundtrack is great, and the vibes of the game are nice.  With that said, though, I do have some complaints.First, I encountered some bugs in the game, some merely visual (art assets appearing on the wrong layer), while others affected the gameplay.  It was uncommon, but you should prepare to miss a small number of lines of dialogue, have minigame issues (the heart monitor minigame is especially prone to fail to recognize inputs), and sometimes require a forced game close in the middle of a scene because the controls froze.  Annoying, but you can play past it.  There are additionally issues with the English localization, but more a word repeat/misssing/strange turn of phrase, and those were very rare and not especially distracting.The final issue for me was the writing, and this was a little more of a pervasive issue.  On the one hand, the characters are interesting, believable, and consistent, which is what you'd want in a story like this.  On the other hand, there are severe issues with pacing, made all the worse by large empty areas of the map and frequent path blocking that puts more time between you and your next snippet of dialogue.  Well, I shouldn't say the areas are "empty", there are wonderful art assets everywhere, but I prefer to also have more things to do during my cross-town excursions, and this game doesn't have quite as much to offer in that regard.  On the other hand, there is a very sudden and severe ramp of stakes towards the end of the game, with little in the way of a conclusion for most arcs.  I'm talking like, almost zero falling action or resolution.  Some of the events of the climax could also have used more in the way of foreshadowing, though there were elements scattered here and there for some points.  Was it still good?  Yes, absolutely.  Again, I had fun.  Did it need some editing passes and maybe more time to help the game shine a little brighter?  You betcha.One thing I'll say, regarding a thread of comparison running through many other reviews, is that this is not just Second Night In The Woods.  The tone, plot, characters, and themes are all dramatically different, and one should not base their desire to purchase this game on whether or not they liked that one.  The trailer for the game is a good representation of what you'll find.  If you like what you see, go for it.  Just don't expect all 2D sidescrolling games with animal characters to be the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really like Fall of Porcupine. It's a lot of fun, the characters are nice and interesting, the story and plot that's set up has me engaged, and the world they built is fun to see and feels like a great town. Unfortunately this game is also a buggy mess and it's just not something I can recommend in this state. I hope it gets fixed because what I've seen is a genuinely good story that I do recommend, it's just part of a game that's really unfinished.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Lots of bugs, a very long beginning before the story gets good, and the mechanics of some of the minigames in the hospital lead me to not recommend this game.I finished the whole game wanting to give it a chance and I liked the storyline of the game, but here's why I wouldn't recommend playing: - It has far too many bugs: characters will walk away while in conversation with you and their dialogue will move offscreen to be unreadable, some minigames wouldn't work correctly. It seemed like it needed more time in beta testing for them to work out all of the bugs, they don't make the game unplayable but they are very frustrating. There were also issues with the dialogue itself, there were many missed or misspelled words and some sentences I struggled to make sense of, this impacted the experience and the overall message when you don't know what a character is trying to say. - The main cast of three characters that we see the most of (Finley, Mia, and Karl) feel very one-dimensional. They don't really feel like a friend group all together and I found myself not very attached to Finley as a main character.- The hospital minigames got old very fast and the difficulty scale was not very consistent, at first they were easy, then it seemed the next time they became very difficult, and then the next time were a medium difficulty. I suppose you could justify that as commentary but it was very frustrating for the gameplay.- The play time is very long and the story takes a while to get interesting. It does become an interesting story, but the beginning of the game could have cut down SEVERELY and it would make it much more enjoyable, as it is now I wouldn't recommend getting through the beginning to get to the good parts at the very end of the story. Overall, it has the bones of a game good game, I love the setting and the character design and like I said it has a good story and a good message it just takes too long to get there.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: To be perfectly honest, I wasn't familiar with Fall of Porcupine until very recently. I saw the trailer for the game at one of the summer conferences and was immediately interested in the art style and the premise. A lot of people seem to compare it to Night in The Woods, but I believe this is a little bit disingenuous because, while maybe the devs took some inspiration from NITW, Fall of Porcupine has a lot to offer as its own product.The game was a welcoming surprise that kept me invested from start to finish. The narrative actively explores themes of freedom, loss, sacrifice, and the never ending resilience of the human spirit. You're a young doctor that just moved into a new city and started taking first steps by working in the local hospital. During the daytime, you will be tasked with numerous hospital chores in the form of mini-games and I felt that there was enough variety there to keep you engaged as your progress through the story. The main theme of the game is to show that working in a hospital is not an easy task, and you can't expect to be able to save everyone.In your downtime, you'll be able to socialize with the local crowd, plus you can hang out and explore deeper relationships with your friends. There is a city to explore, but there are not a lot of side activities to be done, there is some roof climbing and the odd tidbit in your apartment with which you can interact, but most of the interactions with the environment are tied to story stuff.In my playthrough, I noticed some bugs. Some of the button prompts didn't work, and the notes app on your phone wasn't showing, until you started the app again. Part of the dialogue was repeating or wasn't showing it all and there were some grammatical errors, but mostly it was nothing that affected my enjoyment of the game.I truly believe that this title deserves more attention, there is a demo you can try so if you like story-driven games with some fun mini-games and interesting characters, give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: Let me tell you a little story.I'm roughly 2/3 through the game, coming off of a very emotional scene where our main character is confronted with the inevitability of death. In the moments immediately afterward, other characters reel from the impact of this death in the community and grieve together. As I go around back of the local bar, I encounter another of the hospital staff, wracked with survivors guilt, and help him come to terms with the fact that there are things we can't control, actions can have unknowable consequences, and we have to move on regardless.Tragically, while entering this part of the game, the main character's torso despawned, meaning that this lovely dialogue was coming out of a raymanesque pile of floating limbs.Fall of Porcupine, frankly, is riddled to the gills with bugs. Some are serious enough to require a restart (talking to a certain NPC after a cutscene disables your movement controls, pressing the wrong button when starting the dancing minigame changed my game language to French, etc.), but even the purely cosmetic ones are a hammerblow to the immersion and atmosphere. This is a 2D talk-'em-up, and is somehow as broken as a modern AAA release.It's a shame, because I really enjoyed most of my time with Fall of Porcupine. The story was quite touching up until it abruptly stopped, and the art design, obviously, is excellent. There's a lovely game in here, but I can't in good conscience recommend it until it's fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game and it pains me to leave a negative review but I honestly just can't recommend it. There are lots of things some big and some small that bring this game down and it could've been such a great experience.I picked up this game mostly because I was interested in the story. I feel like topics around healthcare aren't explored nearly enough so I was extremely interested in how they handle representing underfunded hospitals and overworked staff but I'm really sorry to say I was disappointed at best and I felt kind of insulted at worst. The healthcare system isn't perfect. I feel like everyone has been critical of it at least once whether you complain about high prices or long wait times. These topics are tackled in the story as a passing mention but the people that are most vocal about these issues are portrayed as a couple of angry idiots and the game makes it very clear that you should see them as such. Very disappointing to see a portrayal like that especially because a lot of the criticism for the healthcare system has a lot of nuance to it. I do not need this game to hold a really deep philosophical conversation about healthcare but I was really hoping for a story that's grounded a little more reality especially how I saw it mention that they interviewed healthcare workers when writing the story. The story also feels kind of slow. I get that you'd want to develop the characters before the drama to make the player care about them more, but for how abruptly this game ends, the time spent outside the hospital feels disproportionate. And this feeling is only made worse by the lack of animations, music and weird sound mixing. The characters regardless of situations rarely change their expressions and don't even look at each other while talking. All of them have maybe one idle and one talking animation and this coupled with almost non-existent talking sound effects made the conversations really static and quiet regardless of what was actually being said. The music was very nice when it was there but the majority of the game is spent in complete silence or just ambient sound effects of wind or crickets that are sometimes so loud that they drown out the already quiet music. The game also has some weird tonal shifts kicking off loud and bright minigames in the middle of a quiet and dark moment. There's one pretty serious event in the game that pretty much starts most of the drama of this story and has major consequences later but while you're doing it it's just a funny rpg-like minigame with funny music and goofy attacks! I just couldn't take that moment seriously because of it. Again I wanted to love this game! The art style is cute and nostalgic, the lore that they came up with for the town of Porcupine is cool, and the characters all felt distinct, but the issues I mentioned above dragged it down too much :(

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a happy ending... this isn't the game for you. That being said... if you want a game that gives you insight into the healthcare system? This is a definite. You want to feel things? This game does that.As a healthcare employee the story of this game resonated strongly with what I've experienced over the last decade. It hits hard regardless of where you live (devs are from Germany, I live in the US).I enjoyed the game. The art style is wonderful. I love the little details like when you float as Finley your 'wings' and tail get a bit floofier. Most the characters feel really solid.The things I didn't enjoy... the mini puzzles were meh. They weren't difficult but they also weren't overly exciting. They were such a small part compared to the story that it didn't matter as much to me.  The other thing was the leading and spacing of the text in the speech bubbles in English. Seemed everywhere an 's was used there was a space between the word and the 's. Example: It 's, we 'll, etc. And there were some areas where I think the translating went bad, extra words that made things sound wrong. A few times all the text didn't fit in the speech bubble. But if you are used to reading auto-corrected text to speech from friends and family, you'll figure it out easily enough.But these 'bad' things are things didn't really affect how the game played or the message it was giving. The game overall is rather solid and was enjoyable to play, despite the heaviness of the story. Prepare yourself for an emotional journey and you may want to keep a box of tissues nearby.

_childDocuments_.review: fall of porcupine, a night in the woods like adventure with stunning art, sweet ambient music and incredible characters. the town itself is simply a work of art, the way it changes with the weather is breathtaking and makes the world feel alive, which makes up for the fact that you have to spend a lot of time walking across the town if you want to interact with everything and talk to everyone - i spent a lot of time just walking and praying i wouldn't be locked out of exploring the other part of time before finley's workday starts. the music was an incredible bonus and didn't get on my nerves even after spending at least an hour real time going through the town, which says a lot about how great it is in my opinion.the characters are amazing and it definitely pays off to spend time with them and talk to them as much as you can. finley is a quirky protagonist who admittedly talks a bit too much sometimes, mainly when you interact with objects in the town (mostly the statues.) the other big characters are wondeful and it pays off to play the game twice to see all the hang out options between the two main friends. the story is heavy, real and incredible. i laughed, i cried, i cried some more and then the big shock came and i prayed it wasn't the end only to be hit with the ending titles. the story will leave you feeling vulnerable, shocked, nostalgic, everything and nothing at once. it is raw and bittersweet and so worth it. my only issue is the occasional bug here and there - sometimes when a character follows finley they start sort of flying in the background or get stuck somewhere. my other main issue was with the stethoscope minigame - it felt a bit laggy but admittedly i do suck at it so it might just be me. i also want to quickly highlight the accessibility (that i use every time i have to do the stethoscope minigame and somehow still fail, who knows if it's me at this point.)all in all, i recommend this game - the story, art, characters, music; the emotions you get out of it, all of it is worth a few bugs that i hope will be fixed in an update. i give it 8.5/10 and will definitely play again (i really want that last achievement hehe)

_childDocuments_.review: This one is tough. I played the demo for Fall of Porcupine during the Steam Next Fest and was really looking forward to the full release. I love the premise of what it's like working in a little hospital for a little isolated town, the artwork is great, and I enjoyed talking to and getting to know the characters, but after finally getting the time to sit down with it (about 5-6 hours, some offline), I just felt like I was pushing myself to make any progress. The story wasn't exciting enough to keep me interested, the mini-games offered no challenge, a LOT of time spent walking from A-B, and the constant bugs and visual issues I ran into were frustrating. I think I understand what the writers were going for, but everything felt just a bit too mundane. I think what this game is trying to say could have been accomplished in half the time, or less, with more respect for the player's time. For example, fast-travel exists (kinda) but only for one specific thing and you still need to walk a lot to and from the fast travel location. If you're not going to that same spot per the plot, fast travel was unavailable and you had to spend 5 min walking to a place you've already been to before. Eventually, it just didn't feel worth it to continue playing. Secondly, the bugs. Oh gosh. I played on Steam Deck and I struggle to see how this game is 'verified' on deck. I constantly ran into things like: Text cut off the screen, the aspect ratio incorrect and cut off during conversation/mini games, characters getting stuck on walking paths while following, text overflowing the speech bubbles, text auto-skipping when pressing a button to load the chat bubble but other times it wouldn't skip, audio cutting out oddly, etc. Maybe it was just the platform I played on wasn't tested, but the game felt unpolished and like it wasn't thoroughly play-tested. This feels a little harsh, I know a lot of work went into the game, but when text is cut off or overflowing in a visual novel it's very obvious. This game is lovely, it has a lot of things going for it that it does very well, but as a fully packaged game it just didn't work for me. Additionally, I think the comparisons to Night in the Woods will leave folks disappointed. If I were to recommend this game it would be to someone who really loves visual novels and have some personal connection to the medical industry, but only after it's been patched.

_childDocuments_.review: ---{Gameplay}---☐ Replayability t ☐ Hours upon hours of fun! ☐ Good at parts. ☑ Nothing to remember. ☐ Ping Pong is better. Very simple gameplay, a few mini-games are thrown in, some are fine, others are a bit broken or hard to understand. ---{Story}---☐ It will change your life forever! ☐ You'll stay up all night thinking about it! ☑ Just enough to not skip the cutscene. ☐ Glimpses of good writing. ☐ Monkeys on typewriters could do better. The plot is slice of life until near the end, most of the game you're waiting for something to happen. There are small hints of a bigger thing at play, but they too don't add up enough to get the mystery rolling until the ending happens. The story itself is quite standard, but it has some cute and cozy parts to it. I think if they were to revamp some of the game, they should add more clues to the big surprise. And most importantly add an epilogue!---{Characters}---☐  deep investment into memorable characters! ☐ Well written and have lots of depth! ☑ Enjoyable to watch and interact with! ☐ They do their job well enough. ☐ Unlikable, and not in the good way. Most of the residents of Porcupine have their own charm to them, which is a little sad because they get very little screen-time. Some characters have 4 or 5 conversations through out the game, others have only a few lines of dialogue.'Main' characters have enough screen time to start having a connection with, but they don't really grow. The protagonist Finley doesn't have much of an arc through out the game. Sure, he gets better caring for patients and grows closer to his friends, but that's what most people would do anyway given enough time.One event in the game could be considered a growing moment for him, but it's not like he changes as a character after. He just goes through the moment and the game carries on. Any time for growth at the end is put to the side for the finale. And then the game just ends. I like Finley and the other characters, i'd loved to see a more fulfilling conclusion for them.---{Did I Cry?}---☐ It emotionally scarred me, for better or for worse. ☐ Yes, tears were had... ☐ My eyes got a bit teary. ☑ No crying, but it it still impacted me. ☐ My eyes have never been drier. Despite a lot of problems I did enjoy the story, more than I thought I would. Many of the characters were nice, maybe too many, but they were fun to watch. Sadly though with the ending being quite sudden, not being attached to most of the characters, and the lack of an epilogue, it wasn't enough for even a single tear. This isn't a sad game though, so that's to be expected.---{Graphics}---☐ Beautiful art style, unforgettable. ☑ Uniqe and gorgeous! ☐ Your standard nice looking graphics. ☐ A bit ugly or hard on the eyes. ☐ You call these graphics? The style of the characters are simple yet pleasant, and the art design of the Porcupine is cozy.---{Soundtrack}---☐ One in a billion, a must listen! ☑ They knew what they were doing! ☐ Pretty good! ☐ Eeeeehhh. ☐ Just mute it in options. Most of your time spent is in the hospital or walking around the streets, and the music accompanies that well. It's not stand-out like some other games, but it's still really nice.---{Audio}---☐ More enjoyable than actual music! ☐ Your ears will enjoy it! ☐ Better then most games! ☑ About average. ☐ As bad as nails against a chalk board. Mostly footsteps with a few ambient noises. I did notice some audio levels being louder than others.---{Atmosphere}---☐ It's so dense you could cut it with a knife! ☐ I take a moment to appreciate it every now and then! ☑ Quite likeable! ☐ It works well enough. ☐ Welp... they tried. Porcupine is a pretty big town, a lot of running is needed to get from one end to the other. After a dozen or so trips it can get tedious, but they did a good job making it interesting enough for the first playthrough. The vibe of the town is very connected, it really does feel like everyone you see lives there together, each person knowing the other.---{Bugs}---☐ Not one. Not a single one! ☐ Noticed a few ☑ Can happen often. ☐ Persistent in the game. ☐  The worst part of the game, softlocks, UI bugs, overlapping issues, dialogue repeating or showing up in the wrong place. Over time I hope these are fixed, because this game deserves better.---{Price}---☐ It's free to play!☐ Full price!☑ Wait for a sale.☐ Wait for a  sale.☐ Save your money for anything else.For $20 this is a fine game, if you're looking for another NITW you won't get the same experience. But if you're okay with a simple game with a simple story, this is far from the worst you could choose. Get on sale if you're unsure though. Or try the demo! Apparently it takes place before the start of this game, so it might be a good idea to try it either way.---{Ranking}---☐ G.O.T.Y!☐ 8/10!☑ Better then average!☐ It was OK.☐ Eh, not for me.☐ Don't bother even looking at it.Fall of Porcupine left a soft spot in my heart, it has a nice story with good characters. Honestly most of it's issues could be solved, or at least alleviated, with the addition of an epilogue. I really hope the best for the developers!

_childDocuments_.review: Kaaaaarl!... ahem.Fall of Porcupine leaves me really torn. The story and characters felt great, and while the town could've been more dense, it was at least sufficiently filled with life (given that you technically aren't supposed to spend a lot of your time exploring).But. Bugs! So many of them! (I played this game on Steam Deck, so YMMV on PC, but in any case this is not how "Deck verified" is supposed to look like.)And not just the occasional visual glitch or clunky movement that could be overlooked when it comes to indie titles, but the softlocking sort (e.g. ) that forced me to close and reopen the game a dozen or so times - meaning a return to the most recent one of the way-too-sparse auto-save points, every time.Add to that certain minigames where inputs don't properly register or the timing is significantly off - this sluggishness being blatantly noticeable when activating the minigame accessibility option - and you're in for a frustrating gameplay experience.As such I really can't recommend this game, as much as I want to for its narrative aspects; not in the broken state it's in. Maybe that'll change if the devs should decide to return to releasing patches at some point, instead of leaving this as it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall of Porcupine uses one of the most beautiful art styles and heartfelt, philosophical narratives and dialogue with all the characters (even and especially some around town who you aren't required to talk to like Fauke at the fishing spot in the far left), however, the game could really use some additional polish. While it's nice that the bus stop and elevator can save time, they also cut out much of the potential narratives with residence that are required in order to build a stronger connection to everyone and the story itself. Fall of Porcupine is similar to Night in the Woods (the games are even structured the same where you have to choose between hanging out with either Mia or Karl), but where Night in the Woods spends more time building those solid connections and focusing on how things have changed dynamically between Gregg, Angus, Bea, Mae, and the other residence of Possum Springs as Mae finds herself, this isn't as fleshed out with Mia, Karl, Pina, and Finley and loses a lot of depth and charm as a result. There's so much to work with (at times almost too much where a lot could be stripped away), yet somehow leaves you wanting more simultaneously. That being said, there's charm in the narrative being based around real stories from those who work in healthcare, especially following COVID and is a delight visually. At the hospital there are a number of tasks: shots (one of the most boring of the hospital mini games requiring that you just release the required amount of medication in the red zone), diagnosis (an image based game similar to Wordle or Mastermind), EKG (somewhat similar to your standard Guitar Hero style rhythm game}, pill prescription (a somewhat math based logic puzzle of the fewest pills to prescribe and combine to get the desired result) and changing bedsheets (pressing and releasing buttons under time constraints). Some tasks are genuinely enjoyable while others do get a bit monotonous and tedious (and don't truly have an impact on the story regardless of whether you pass or "fail" (get a C). Overall, it's still a gorgeous narrative driven game that's cozy, especially for the fall season. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Note before reading this review: If there would be an option to give this review a neutral rating, I would have done that. As the story is awesome but the game is unnecessarily long and can feel like a slog to get through. Around the end, the story gets way more interesting and that feeling of it being a slog faded away.  16h? 2/10 2 No, not yet No Yes, many missable achievements No No No No No No you can use the accessibility settings and still unlock the achievements Maybe the one about wirting the comic? Read more around the end of this review for more info.Fall of Porcupine is a story-driven adventure game. You play as Finley, a junior doctor that recently moved to a small town called Porcupine for his new job. You'll meet the people that live in Porcupine, make friends, and work in the hospital. Treating your patients and some of the sidequests requires you to complete some mini-games. Most of them are fine and can be made easier through the accessibility setting in the menu... however, I have no idea how to get a good score in the mini-game for listening to someone's heart/longs. I sucked so so bad at those already at the beginning, let alone later on in the game when it gets harder. The game will warn you at the start of a new game that it deals with heavy subjects. This is very true and if you're sensible about those things, you might want to play this game later or decide it is not for you. As the story is very touching and emotional. It gives a look inside the life of somebody who is working in a hospital, bringing their best A game, but still failing from time to time. Especially around the end of the game, it made me think of healthcare workers during the pandemic. The game had a few bugs while I played through it, nothing really game-breaking but sometimes I could talk to people and then the conversation didn't start. Or was working on a quest but something else was listed at the top as a quest I should be working on. Having objectives at the top of the screen is also an accessibility option, but sometimes it was not accurate of what I should be doing. Another thing that brings the fun of playing Fall of Porcupine down a bit is that a lot of things feel long and slowed down. Rooms are long and most of the time patients lay at the end of the room, streets are long with not much to do in them, which makes them feel long. And since you move a lot through rooms/corridors and streets, it feels like this endless slug that becomes boring very soon. It ramps up the game time while not adding much to the game or the story. The surroundings are beautiful, but not when seeing them for the 5th time. Then the achievements... normally I make sure I can tell you all about them and have unlocked everything myself. However, in this case, I have only unlocked a little over 60%. I haven't unlocked everything as there are key moments in the story where you have to choose between option A and option B and both are tied to achievements, so you have to play at least twice through the game.  There is one achievement about writing a comic with one of the characters but maybe I didn't visit him enough, but randomly in the story he started talking again about wanting to write a story and started the questline from the start, which didn't give me enough time to get through it before the ending, not sure if I would have otherwise. There are also achievements that I have no idea how to unlock, as Emma never talked about a book and I have no clue where I should have heard the mysterious voices. Not having a clue about those 2 achievements and encountering a bug with the comic book storyline made that I didn't play through the game a second time.I did enjoy Fall of Porcupine, and I highly recommend it for the story. As it was so touching and emotional.

_childDocuments_.review: High hopes but no satisfying game.I have played the predecessor Night in the Woods before and I still love it to this day, for anyone reading this and considering this game, go buy Night in the Woods instead, but to anyone still reading I will summarize the goods and the bads in the following section.I will not focus on what the game is or its story for the most part.The good: - The Art stylesFall of Porcupine has a distinct visual art style best resembled by the game "Night in the Woods" and this was the main reason for me to buy it as I hoped for it to be a worthy sequel.-The main storyIt is of a doctor in his residency years. The idea is catchy and not seen often in games before. It is interesting to show the different parts of the medical sector working together. The Bad:- The interactions with the characters:There are not many dialogue choices and later in the game there are even viewers or none.Most of the game is a story that you progress through without shaping the main character’s personality.- The atmosphereThe game does not feel populated by people going on their daily routine and shops to visit and places to see. Most of the time you will travel from on location (most often your home) to another location ( most often the Hospital) but on your way only a hand full of NPC's will have dialogue options and nearly none of them will have you to decide what to say. Thos travel times feel long and take up a good chunk of the game, just walking.  There are only view times where locations are harder to reach that will yield a benefit (having to climb a house to reach a Head or an NPC) but these events are always visible to the player and easy to reach making them nearly impossible to miss. - The ConsequencesNo matter what you do or don't do, the story will progress at one pace and you cannot influence that or your relation to any of the NPC's. No minigame you fail or succeed in will have a lasting effect, not visiting locations daily will have just a bit of an impact on the small progression with the NPCs there.- The BugsI encountered several game breaking bugs: - the fuse box that you had to activate was not interactable, some dialogue did not progress, the phone did not open, NPC'S having the same dialogue or non and several minor visual glitches.- The MusicThe music has a small but not interesting set of pieces, with the title screen music being the most prominent. I would have liked a whider variety of soundtracks.-  The EndThe ending comes to shot and sudden and you are left with a feel of disbelief, you were not able to say goodbye to the characters you have meet and see the locations once again in a different light but a hart cut and a unscippable credit scene makes it really unpleasantThe game felt more like a stretched piece of gum that loses its flavor with each hour you play than the exiting story it could have been. I felt a lot of NPCs were not fully written out like the paramedics with whom you will have only really limited interaction possibilities. I want to make a view comparison of the (NITW) Night in the Woods and explain what is missing in this game.NITW had a lively city with lots of locations that you could visit and a lot of NPC'S at those locations. Each day their dialogue changed in a meaningful way and reflected your actions towards them, there were poems, story’s and friendships to be had, none of those are seen here (FOP). There were special cutsceens that you earn from having interacted often enough with on NPC and there where special events trigged by your action. Often these events were interactive and fun and so different. And don't forget about Deamon Tower.The Soundtrack was amazing, and you can listen to it even when not playing NITW. Fall of porcupine should have been the perfect sequel to NITW as previously you played a collage dropout dealing with the problems of going back to your hometown and in FOP you play a collage graduate who must deal with a bad life as well even though he reaches everything May (NITW min character) did not. All of that is missing in Fall of porcupine and so much more. I am disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: is a poignant story-driven adventure set in the small town of Porcupine. It follows Finley as he begins his career as a junior doctor and slowly uncovers some of the darker secrets of the town and its residents.It is a wonderful game that contrasts casual gameplay with a meaningful and often emotive narrative that provides players with a little insight into the trials and tribulations faced by healthcare professionals. It has delightful visuals with its collage-like art style and seasonal colour palettes which work in tandem with the subtle music and immersive sound design. A few minor bugs crop up but nothing too frustrating, with the overall experience being well-rounded and highly satisfying with its combination of story-focused sections and challenging mini-games. I thoroughly enjoyed Fall fo Porcupine and I’d happily recommend it to anyone looking for a narrative-based adventure game with a good level of interactivity and an important message.My full review of this game where I go into detail about gameplay, narrative and styling is available on .

_childDocuments_.review: First, I want to state this game is very pretty and the first half of the game is very enjoyable. The music is pleasant and fits, but there are issues with some glitches (Some conversations are duplicated, icons appear for conversation but when you interact there's nothing to be stated, One instance Finley entered a room and a patient just slid across the floor). This game is tedious with the amount of running around and backtracking, only to discover there really aren't secrets or payoffs for your exploration. There is a jump button but it isn't really necessary for 99% of the game. The real disappointment is with the story; There are some good moments within, but the 3rd act really loses its way and the ending is just jarring with very little in the way of resolution. This is a game that should have spent a little more time finishing up the story and polishing the presentation, but it is decent for this team's first game. I do not recommend this title because of the disappointing ending, and it appearing unfinished and unpolished. Comparing this to Night in the Woods is not really fair; If you're expecting a tight and emotional experience this game is not that. I truly wished this game was more satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first stumbled upon "Fall of Porcupine," it immediately reminded me of the indie gem "Night in the Woods." Maybe it's the charming autumnal setting or the anthropomorphic animal characters that do the trick. Regardless, this PlayStation 5 adventure has a cozy feel with a unique twist—it delves into the life of a healthcare worker.Welcome to the snug town of Porcupine, where you step into the feathers of Finley, a bird who's now a doctor at the local hospital. Days here are spent juggling hospital shifts and exploring the town's nooks and crannies, engaging with its colorful residents.The game kicks off with Finley facing a patient crisis that leaves him temporarily out of work due to an injury. After his recovery, it's back to the hospital grind, and here's where you'll receive your tasks. Each workday involves caring for three patients, which essentially translates to playing some mini-games. These tasks, like needle injections and stethoscope use, are alright but can be somewhat frustrating and poorly explained. Your performance, whether stellar or subpar, doesn't seem to affect the patient's outcome, making it hard to invest in your minigame scores.However, the heart of this game lies in the interactions with its eclectic characters. The residents of Porcupine are bursting with personality and fascinating stories. Whether chatting with patients in the hospital or bonding with townsfolk, every conversation is a delight. But it's not all sunshine and rainbows. "Fall of Porcupine" tackles real healthcare issues like stress, and there are intriguing mysteries to uncover, both within the hospital and the town's history. While the story is engaging, it does suffer from pacing problems and a rushed conclusion.Visually, the game shines with detailed characters and a palette that exudes relaxation as you explore the town. However, there are performance hiccups and minor bugs, including frame rate drops and characters talking off-screen. The audio, on the other hand, is a perfect match for the small-town atmosphere."Fall of Porcupine" takes players on an emotional journey, shedding light on critical healthcare issues. It's not without its flaws, as the story can get tangled and rushed in places, and technical issues need addressing. Yet, these hitches don't overshadow the joy of living in this world and connecting with its captivating characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this on sale, and I think the sale price is absolutely worth it. Full price, maybe not so much, ONLY for the ending of the game (and some of the "mini-game" mechanics being wonky on a controller).The game had so much character and so much to explore and find. Slightly disappointed in some of the world being unused... (What was up with the weird cult people in the tunnel? Why introduce the mopey fox kid and then suddenly have someone just mention that he moved away?) and the whole third act felt SO rushed. It felt entirely unfinished! One of the characters (your boss) at the ends even says "Hey, come here, I need your help with something quickly!" and you run outside to help her and it's just over, credits roll???I ADORED this game and played it pretty much non stop of two days haha. But the end felt unsatisfying and really, really disappointing...But, if it's on sale, I think it's worth it for the story alone, and getting to know all the cute characters. Talk to EVERYONE. Explore. Explore the playground, the shopping area, the town square, the river--everything you can before you go to the hospital everyday. There are so many stories to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros : + Artstyle - Amazing and fits the theme very well+ Music - Beautifully crafted Calm and relaxing+ Story - Engaging characterization and surprisingly immersive experience of being on the healthcare industry (feel wise of course)Cons :- Bugs - Still quite a lot of them while encountering. Some lead to game locks sadly or some immersion breaking.- Save Functionality - It doesn't have cloud save currently and you can really move it manually as well. Also the game feels like i would benefit with save files.- Story - Both a pro and con, as if the characterization and experience is amazing, the ending does leave a lot of unanswered plot lines.I had a beautiful time playing this game. With its amazing art style and music, the music really makes you care about the world and interested to poke around. First few hours of the game engaged me with unique characters and a quite gripping story. The characters and the patients that you encounter feel real. The mini games are cute as well.But the best part in my opinion of the game is how, at least for me, feels it simulates the experience of being a doctor very well. I do mean this emotionally of course. The way you want to treat and interact with your patients, the way the make you feel attached to some of them, the little annoyances that some patients also have, all makes them feel so real. Not only that but that also helps sets the pressure when the story picks up.--- Spoiler warning ish ----Now sadly the downfall is this game is in my opinion not the bugs, but the story. As much as it does immerse me on the feel of being a doctor, the story and the characters plot progression feels unfinished after the credits roll. Although emotionally it did capture what i thought what the game was trying to potray, it still doesnt really feel accurate to have some plot lines too open ended and up to interpretation. But with all that being said, I still recommend playing the game if you don want to tolerate some of the bugs. I feel the game can give you more empathy and understanding to the message that its trying to convey, even if the story is a bit unsatisfactory.Tl:dr - Game good, makes me feel emphaty, story is a bit lacking in the ending, buy if you can tolerate a lil bit of bugs.
