_childDocuments_.review: IMPORTANT: I haven't finished the game. I left it the halfway point or so. If that changes I'll make sure to update the review.Fall of Porcupine was easily my most waited game for... Ever since it was announced. To the point of checking the Steam page on release to check how many hours were left to be able to play it, get it on release day and so on. But I just... Don't really enjoy it much?Let's get the obvious elephant in the room out of the way first: Night in the woods. FOP wears its NITW inspiration on its sleeve. It's OBVIOUS. And with NITW being one of my favourite games ever, obviously that was one very big reason why I ended up anticipating this game so much. Problem is, seeing it now in hindsight, being so obvious with the inspiration was a bold move that can be equally good and terrible.As I said, one of the good parts is obvious: You're instantly gonna catch the attention of the fanbase of a very very beloved game, and interest will spike almost instantly.But the bad part came when I started playing: This just looks like Night in the woods aesthetically. Nothing is really even close to NITW. And I know I should be judging Fall of Porcupine for being Fall of Porcupine and not Night in the Woods 2, but I feel this reaction is normal precisely because of the very conscious choice of making it look so similar.The first thing that had my alarms ringing was the soundtrack. It's... Charming I guess, but for the most part, it's almost like it isn't even there. It's SO subtle, and simple, that at some points you don't even notice it. There's a lot of parts in the hospital where you're practically in silence. There's this scene with Mia where you're both running to see who makes it first to a basketball court. And I caught myself thinking, in the middle of it, "If this had a good, emotional song in the background, this scene would hit A LOT and would be something people remember". Because, again... That's what NITW would've done. And what made it be so beloved. So it was bold to kinda create some of your game so much after it, making people's expectations go a certain way, and then have them find out it was just the very outer layer that looks similar to it.I loved the demo, because it had what I expected: Main character introduction, then you go to the hospital, the day ends and you hang out with new friends and learn more of their backstories, and then the whole thing ends up with a mystery to hopefully unravel in the back through all the game.But then the full game is just... Very repetitive and samey. You go to the hospital. Have conversations that feel like they go nowhere and feel repetitive and the work consist of sequentally completing a few minigames that go from "Oh, this is entertaining and makes sense contextually" to "I don't know why this is representing doing this thing/I hope I don't have to do many more of these". There's practically no mentions about the mystery, practically no hangouts, practically no mention of anyone's personal lives... It's just "Go to the hospital, do the same three things, go back home, repeat". And sometimes you see Finley making comments and remarks that look like they were actively trying to emulate something that would've come out from NITW... And it just doesn't work. You feel a whiplash. Because it's disconnected. What happened before and what happens later doesn't really fit with that moment. I don't know... I feel like they had the tools to make a GOOD game and a GOOD memorable story, but the choice to work between the margins someone else laid before made some things just not work and feel out of place, disconnected, slow... I can see the love behind it. That's why I'm sad. Because I know they could've made a VERY good game. But I ended up being in a situation of "I really really really want to like this game but I keep getting distracted every 30 minutes because nothing is grabbing my attention". But I'll try and finish it and see if I can end up with a better taste...

_childDocuments_.review: Oof, I am really having a hard time with this game, but I feel ultimately I cannot recommend it.The issue is that I liked the game; I don't mind that it was slow paced and more down to earth, I enjoy smaller stories and seeing the daily life of characters, on a strange way, the game was relaxing for me (Even if I felt pretty stressed trying to impress my boss and get on time to work, not that I had control over either thing.) I did enjoy story, and the characters for the most part.So, if I think all of this, why I can't recommend it?Well...neither of this aspects is strong enough, or good enough, for me to justify the rest.I am not a gamer, and I am not one to talk about the technical aspects of a game, but there were way too many times when the game just, got buggy enough that I needed to take it out and start (the phone not downloading the tasks, my character getting stuck in between places, a characters needed to progress somehow missing from the scene) and this wouldn't be as annoying, if it wasn't because you cannot manually save.The game saves for you, when it does that? You aren't sure, is there any way you can check the last time you saved? Not that I had seen; it was EXTREMELY frustrating for the game to break, and me to re-do everything that I just did. There are other types of bugs; like the HELP option in your phone not working, characters who say you can talk to but then don't, some visual bugs (example, a character has a ribbon, you get in front of said character, and the ribbon is on top of you know) The latter one weren't too distracting or an issue, but worth mentioning. Options in accessibility, like turning off the mini games, were also not working.Perhaps is because I am autistic, so take this with a grain of salt: But the explanation for the mini games multiple times didn't make sense to me, I would read the instruction, have an idea of what I need to do, and then turns out I completely misinterpreted. You can complete the game in around 8 hours, which, for the price I paid, I didn't mind (However, I got the game at half price,) I know technically, I could do other events if I reply the game, but I didn't enjoy this game enough in order to do so.I liked the story and the characters, but not enough to replay it again. Look, a story doesn't have crazy twist and turns in order to be interesting, you can have a simple story and still enjoy to replay, but for that, you need to have strong, charismatic characters, and this game doesn't have them. I enjoy them, and I can't say they were strictly one dimensional, but they weren't anything special either, even when I dedicated my time to one specific character, I didn't felt I got to know him or anything.To top it all off, the story doesn't offer enough variation for me to warrant another replay; the chances to choose where to go and see what someone else is going are few and far between, and wouldn't change the outcome of the story overall. The ending...oh boy; without spoilers, things pick up around the end, where it goes nuts with the amount of escalations, revelations, and such, and while all tied together, it does felt like were on a steady, slow pace, and then suddenly we are going down faster and faster without a stop, and then...is the ending, which is so short, and we see so little, is like you did get that stop, but now is just over. I get, that is suppose to be like a love letter to all those health workers who need to tolerate way too much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, due to a lack of funds, staff, and so forth, and having it end there rather than getting a super sacharine ending or a super depressing one (I really can't see it going on a middle with this one,) makes the experience more realistic, but damn, it still feels abrupt. Even if I enjoyed the game, I can't recommend it because I don't find it enjoyable enough for me to justify all the issues.If I had one recommendation to the devs, is that even if you cannot completely fix the bugs, at least give people the chance to save on their own; I feel it would really alleviate a lot of the issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up Fall of Porcupine during a Steam sale. While I initially enjoyed the game, it slowly got more and more frustrating to actually play the game. The text bubbles had frequent typos, the mini game controls lagged, and there was no way to know when the game had last saved. The only saving grace was that you can turn on a setting to make the mini games easier. If I hadn't used that feature, I wouldn't have finished the game.The story itself is heartfelt and hard hitting. I found myself tearing up several times, but a few tears doesn't make up for the bugs and other frustrations. Sometimes the pacing was so slow it was unbearable. Other times, you felt pressured to move forward that you didn't feel like you had the opportunity to explore the world at all. When the character is concerned about getting to work on time, I am too, but by going straight to work, you can miss parts of the world building.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a hard time deciding whether or not I liked this game enough to recommend it. Overall, I believe it has a lot of potential, but there are a few issues that I had a problem with throughout the story. First, there are definitely some bugs in the game, but it seems that developers are working really hard to fix those issues. There was a point in the game where following a very goofy scene, I wanted to return to my apartment, but was unable to enter. At this point, I was more than halfway through the game and no suggestions fixed the issue. A couple days later, the devs made an update and I was able to continue the story. Secondly, the pacing of the story seems so slow at the beginning, then following an emotional plot point, the game seems to hit you with everything all at once. At the end of the game, there seemed to be all of the major drama and height of the plot, and then the game just... abruptly ends. I didn't believe it was the end. Not only did there seem to be no resolution after building up the story for so long, but I was left with A LOT of questions regarding those hard hitting plot points. Third, while the mini games were enjoyable, there was no direct impact on the story, and there almost felt like there was no point to doing well or doing poorly if you were just going to get the same story regardless. Your patients don't react different, and Dr. K seems to treat you the same regardless of how well you scored.Finally, and I think this might be one of the more important points, is that there were a ton of medical inaccuracies in the game. I streamed this game and had several medical professionals in my chat point out flaws ranging from the medical diagnoses & jargon to the hospital layout/structure. I understand that the game devs likely don't have a medical background, but I think it's really important that if the game is going to feature the medical industry that it be represented in the best, most accurate way possible.Of course, there were several things I liked about the game as well. The soundtrack of this game is so lovely, and definitely deserves a lot more recognition. I'm also a big fan of the art style of this game - I mean, who doesn't love these adorably drawn characters? In addition, while the technical aspects of the healthcare industry were off, the healthcare professionals that watched me play agreed that this game hits the nail on the head in regards to the emotional and mental impact that the industry can have. You'll definitely see the toll that working long hours, getting berated by colleagues and outsiders, and trying to balance a social life outside of work can have on anyone who works in healthcare. All in all, I think Fall of Porcupine is worth a play through. Looking past my dislikes of the game, I think everyone should educate themselves on the trials & hardships that people in the healthcare industry face. This game does a great job showcasing exactly that, and I hope that this game helps spark the conversation of improving the industry as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this game for a while. it's very cute, it follows the Night in the Woods style very well, but it can't quite pull off the same charm and wonder that it's inspiration had. The characters are likable, the setting is quaint (though there's probably a couple too many scenes where 'go to point A' has you run through too many empty screens) The plot is very serviceable up until the final act when all hell breaks loose.The final act isn't bad, but it has -way- too much going on. For one, Finley's accident was supposed to have a mystery attached to it? It's barely mentioned except for people heckling him about the accident but then suddenly it's Important. it leads into an interesting plot reveal, but it feels like it's out of left field. And then there's the riot. And the mysterious plague. And then the fire. I liked the feel of the climax's circumstances, where you're forced to deal with patients in a crisis, but the set up and resolution don't really work. The last scene before the credits roll is nice but.. again it feels unearned and sudden and like there should've been more to the game for some proper resolution. The photographs in the credits offer a tiny bit as does the post credit scene but it... yeah just all feels unearned. Would've liked either expanding the chapter, let it breathe a little more so things can resolve properly, also maybe tease things a bit better (Like, plot reveal -makes sense- with other implications in the game, but it feels like it's underused/underdiscussed, it's just revealed in the middle of a crisis and is revolved during the credits). Just a very messy ending that really does put a crimp on the whole game. If you -really- like Night in the Woods style games and the art style is attractive, it's worth a look, but honestly it's probably more enjoyable as just watching someone else play it on a Let's Play run. I can't say i'll be re-playing it to do the other character scenes (like Night in the woods you have multiple points to pick between 2 characters, however, unlike night in the woods, seeing the storylines to completion by picking the same friend every time doesn't earn you any resolution) Kudos to the team, I'd love to see more from them but with lessons learned from this one. The english dialogue needs another pass, still a lot of errors, and the minigames are still a bit buggy.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall of The Porcupine is an intriguing game that captures attention with its atmospheric setting and impressive art style. The gameplay elements are enjoyable, and the music enhances the overall experience. However, there are a few noticeable drawbacks that prevent it from reaching its full potential. One of the main disappointments is the story. Similar to Firewatch, I had high expectations for the narrative, but I found myself let down when the credits rolled. It feels like the game falls short in delivering a satisfying conclusion. Additionally, there are moments where the pacing becomes monotonous, resulting in a rather boring middle section. While the game showcases creativity in certain sections, it feels rushed overall, which is surprising considering the effort put into other aspects. There are missed opportunities to explore these creative elements more extensively, leaving the impression of unfinished potential. I didn't love the ending, but I enjoyed to journey to get there. On another note this games needs Steam Cloud saves!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to leave a negative review but I had high hopes...Visual styleAtmosphereSound (when it exists)Everything else.This game has a lot of potential, and I've been anticipating it for a long time, but seems... something went wrong. Unfortunately, I can't review the story because I lack the motivation to complete the game. However, regarding the other aspects...The game feels tight and uncomfortable. I play a lot of games, but I've never seen a situation where I couldn't exit the menu by pressing B (on the Xbox controller), and this thing is driving me insane.I can't avoid those pauses during the dialogues that I can't force or skip, those moments when  Finley gets stuck after the loading screen when he is running through the locations.I can't relax while playing it because I keep stumbling over gameplay flaws. It's particularly frustrating that there's no option to "save and quit" the game in the current position or at least provide manual save options. Due to several bugs I've encountered during approximately 3h of gameplay, I've been forced to restart the game, setting me back to a spot I was at 20-30 minutes ago. It's quite annoying.Bugs: Sometimes Finley gets stuck, and sometimes there's no sound at all, not even the sound of 'typing' in dialogues.I'm really disappointed because I expected a lot from Fall of Porcupine. _childDocuments_.review: This story will stick with me for a while.The fact that this was dedicated to healthcare workers makes it even more wonderful and also sad. Sad but true.It is a good story to tell, in a wonderful way.The ending might seem sudden, but I feel it was exactly how it was supposed to be.As a healthcare worker you run around all day, helping everyone and it can feel like a thankless job. And you cannot save or help everyone. Which can be demoralizing and heartbreaking.This game tells that story, in what I feel, was a wonderful way.I played this for 10 hours while streaming, but I could have gone twice that long. I didn't talk to everyone in game, because I read everything out loud on stream and needed to save my voice. If I played this privately I would take more time to explore and get to know every single person.The mini-games were fun (I think I had the easy ones turned on), I liked the characters, the music and the experience as a whole.Do stick around for the credits if you finish the game ;)Thank you devs for the tears and the fun.I loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall of Porcupine is a beautiful story about the state of the healthcare system in general. It delved deep into the dirt, scandals, and manipulation behind it all.. but as well as the little good things such as the doctors and nurses who are passionate about their career and genuinely care for their patients. Some critiques I have for the game:- The stethoscope minigame sometimes doesn't detect when I press the corresponding buttons. Sometimes I have to double tap it for it to register and at best my usual results for that game are a B because of it.- The surgery minigame is difficult for no apparent reason. It's like your fingers are playing twister when you go through this minigame.- When I go off the game to go to the menu then back the sounds except for the background ambiance completely disappear. I have to close the game completely to fix it.- There are times when I don't know I'm still in a cutscene and by instincts I move around then the game stops me and the scene plays out, after the scene finishes I get completely soft-locked because I made the unfortunate decision to move mid-cutscene.Some bugs I noticed:- Finley's body sometimes overlaps with his clothesBut overall I recommend this game for it's beautiful atmosphere, characters, storytelling, and moral lessons that it has in store. _childDocuments_.review: "Fall of Porcupine" by Critical Rabbit is a heartwarming and poignant narrative adventure that delves into the complexities of small-town life and the healthcare system. Set in the picturesque town of Porcupine, players follow Finley, a young doctor, as he navigates the challenges of his new career and builds relationships with the town's residents. Here's a detailed review of the game based on various online sources.Pros:- Engaging Storytelling: The game's narrative is its strongest asset, offering an honest and emotionally resonant depiction of life in the healthcare system. The story tackles heavy themes like stress and mental health with sensitivity and depth, making it a standout in the genre​.- Charming Art Style: The hand-drawn, cartoony visuals are both charming and vibrant, adding a cozy yet melancholic atmosphere to the game. The anthropomorphic characters are full of life and personality, which enhances the overall immersion and emotional connection​​.- Varied Gameplay Mechanics: Fall of Porcupine features a mix of mini-games and puzzles that are well-integrated into the storyline. These range from medical tasks like prescribing medication to leisure activities like basketball and bar brawls. This variety keeps the gameplay engaging and fun​​.Cons:- Lack of Polish in Certain Areas: While the game is generally well-received, some areas feel underdeveloped or rough around the edges. For instance, certain interactions and dialogue sequences can feel slightly off, and some gameplay mechanics could use more refinement to reach their full potential​​.- Underused Features: The messenger function on Finley's phone and other minor features could have been more developed to enhance the interactive experience. This minor shortcoming indicates that there was room for more in-depth interactions​​.- Emotional Weight: While the story is a significant strength, its heavy themes might not appeal to everyone. The game deals with real-life issues that can be emotionally taxing, so players should be prepared for a mix of heartwarming and heart-wrenching moments​​.Conclusion:Fall of Porcupine is a beautifully crafted game that excels in storytelling and character development. Its combination of heartfelt narrative, charming art style, and engaging gameplay makes it a must-play for fans of story-rich games. Despite some lack of polish and underused features, the game's emotional depth and relatable characters make it a memorable experience. Rating: I’d give it a "porcupine-perfect" 9/10 Bird of a feather.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cozy and charming game where you take on the role of a junior doctor in a quaint town. The game features a variety of mini-games that simulate the process of treating patients.The game shares some definite similarities with Night in the Woods, particularly in its narrative style and the way it encourages exploration and interaction. The atmosphere is similarly warm and inviting, making it a perfect choice for fans of that genre.However, there are a few drawbacks worth mentioning. Firstly, there is a significant amount of walking, which can become tedious over time, especially if you're trying to explore every nook and cranny of the town. Additionally, the game has some buggy elements that need addressing, which can occasionally disrupt the otherwise smooth gameplay. Lastly, the German to English translation is incomplete in places, which can lead to some confusion and detract from the overall experience.Despite these issues, the game’s charm and engaging mechanics make it a delightful addition to the cozy game genre.

_childDocuments_.review: After some playtime in game became active bus stops, which allow Finley to go directly to the St. Ursula and move plot forward, skipping travel through the town. My first thought was . Sadly, then come the second one, with understanding that there isn't much to look at. Or anything, besides great artstyle of backgrounds or a little extra minutes of ambient soundtrack.The plot, or, at least, the message of the plot, is fine. Hardships of work of medical stuff is a good base for the story - it's something we all experienced in our lives, can relate to or at least understand. But the thing is - it's stays like that for the good portion of the game, and even "crysis" at the end doesn't changes much. Like a river - a favorite subject of a boar-lady character in game - it's stays calm, then meets a huge step down, and... doesn't even return back, because game has no ending. It just stops at some point. There is so much going on a second ago - a riot, a fraud, fire, plague! And boom - that's all, folks. I believe you have to see some sacral meaning in the "fall" of St. Ursula, and I wish I could, if all the previous narrative wasn't a simple slice of life.Even worse, there is no "slice" in this "life", because it's empty. I've ran to and fro through town whole game, waiting to hit some side activity or event, or start a quest, but never found one, except a brief conversation with some characters, getting a hat back to a hobo, or making up a story with a yak-girl. And it's not a good reward for all the running.Finley have whole phone with contacts of his frineds and family, but can't do anything with that(messages from brother and mom here for... reasons?). There is notes about other characters Finley meets, but it has no purpose - like, why write about fox-kid, if he disappears completely after two days and never comes back?Main hero doesn't changes thought story. He spends time with friends(tho, why are we even friends with Karl? Just because?) and other stuff, but stays the same aguish pigeon like he was from the start. He's insecure, can't stand for himself nor his friends, and at the same time spits out lifes wisdom out of blue for Mia. He has a "mysterious accident" at the start that leads to nothing. A story with a flower that leads to nothing. A funerals tragedy that leads to nothing.Well, maybe his job is entertaining? You go to other floors - most of the time they're closed, except moments when you have to move the plot on them. There is a whole woodpecker-surgeon, and you see him twice for the whole game! TWICE! You go to the cafeteria - and swine boos you away. Basement mole never shows up. Minigames? Broken(thank to bugs) or unfun(because, again, your performance leads to nothing, good or bad).Of course, there is some good parts - brother-rivalry between two retarded deer-twins, whole plotline of Finley first dead patient, memory figurines in the woods, festival. Those small moments framed with great art design and music. And I wish developers the best in their next games because throught those moments I see great potential in their work.But "Fall of Porcupine" is like a rusty bike near Finleys home - it's here from the start of the game, and stays like that to the end. Even Finley doesn't want to take it to himself, as he planned.Also, you can't romance nor Mia, nor Dr Krokowski. Huge L for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game with lovable characters and an important story about the current situation of our health care system. This game is mostly story driven with some minigames here and there. You play as Finley in his first days at St. Ursula Hospital. After a couple shifts you start to realise that your job as a medical assistant is way more difficult than you thought. I loved the combination of funny and emotional dialogues which always keeps in balance. After some hours you start to feel home in Porcupine and you fall in love with its inhabitants. There are some little bugs and glitches but Critial Rabbit is very eager to fix them asap. Thank you very much for this gem of a game. I cried once during my twitch livestream which says a lot about the story. :D

_childDocuments_.review: [small update after finishing the story, please see at the bottom of the text]Like some others have already said, I wanted to like this game sooo bad and it breaks my heart to rate it like that, but with the brutal "recommended, yes or no?" truth Steam is giving me... I have to admit I don't recommend the game :(You are the doctor in the hospital of a small rural village and you face some truths about exhausing work in the medical sector, finding your place, making friends as an adult, and balancing taking care of others and you.The artstyle, the idea, the characters are lovely and got me looking forward to the release very much after playing the demo. But the game has two main issues that can't be overlooked:- Bugs: The obvious one is that the game has been released with several bugs. Mine weren't game breaking fortunately (other players have not been this lucky). Some minigames didn't work well, but that only gives you a bad medical rating and does not affect the story. A few dialogues were mixed up, I couldn't read ingame messages from time to time (only lore), and visuals overlapped or disappear. I see that there have been many bugfixes already tho.- Slow paced, empty world: The sidescrolling town and hospital in the game consist of several screens, but they are so insanely empty of... anything. Why do I have to walk past approx. 10 screens on my way to work if several of them don't have a single dialogue option (don't even get started on real exploring options)? Why is the hospital five stories high if all I need except for floor 3 are like 4 other rooms during the whole game? The beauty of the world does fade after a few hours because there is almost NOTHING to freaking do, except for linearly following the story. And walking... and walking... almost no platforming unfortunately either, despite being a sidescroller.To wrap up, please note that the game isn't a complete failure. Maybe a 3.8 out of 10.I have about 1-2 hours to play left as far as I know and I will finish the story.But I have no intention to running another 8-10 hours in a new game set just to complete the achievements (sometimes you have to choose between activity option A or B).Make a dense story game in a small world - or make a sidescroller with puzzles, platforming and exploring options. But this... is just not it.Sad face :(UPDATE:Unfortunately I have to agree with the critics of the last story arc, because wtf is this? Did the devs run out of money?It seems as if they squished 50% of all plot ideas into the last 2 days, which therefore turn out very clumsyly executed and rushed. This is so unsatisfying (for a game which is 80% about the story and dialogue!) and not fair to the good intentions they had for heath care representation.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, with reservations. This is an imperfect game, and I'm not just talking about the bugs, of which there are many. It's also got some structural and storytelling problems, and the game play can feel samey. The overall message of the game is incredibly unsubtle, though I don't know if that's a problem in and of itself. This game clearly owes a lot to Night in the Woods but isn't as ambitious or strange or touching. Not that it's not touching at all, because it is. But cutesy art and a lot of mini-games aren't what made NITW special. Not those things alone, at least. I wish there'd been more mystery (and mystery solving), more diversity in the mini-games, more characters with unique interactions, just a bit more depth. That said, as someone who worked in a hospital during the first two years of the pandemic, Fall of Porcupine hit in a very particular way that I appreciated very much. The final chapter of the game felt very real, capturing the "it's all falling apart at the seams" feeling that those in healthcare experience all too often, especially when hospitals are having budgets and staff cuts so that executives can line their pockets. And while the game's message is delivered clumsily and maybe too forcefully, it is an important one. I would say that on the whole, I enjoyed this game, imperfections and all, and do have to hand it to the developers for using the medium in a unique way to explore the types of things that aren't typically explored in video games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super promising. Beautiful art, full of character. I love what they're trying to do. But it is not a finished game. As a player that wants to get more or less every challenge correct, being stifled by mini games either being super poorly explained or no back button option, it makes it no fun at all. Also the accessibility settings to have a guiding prompt is only offered in German, which is completely unusable to anyone who doesn't speak German. Once this game has had proper playtesting, I'd love to give it another go because I know for sure it's something I want to properly play. It's just not worth the time right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Similar to Night in the WoodsAmazing soundtrackCompelling story with a juicy twistVisually very lovelyAccessibility for dyslexia and several forms of colourblindnessMap is large and interconnected, so you can always get where you need to goIn-game phone mechanic is so helpfulCons:Short (finished the game in about 8 hrs)Pacing could use some work (Acts 1 and 2 feel very long and Act 3 feels extremely short)Mini-games are hard, even with the "easy mini-games" option selectedSoundtrack is really hard to hear even with in-game volume and computer/headphone audio turned all the way upMap is quite large and it's easy to get lostI love this game. It was different than I expected since you play as a doctor in a hospital as opposed to a college drop-out like in NitW, but I loved it still the same. There are still some bugs that need worked out (ex; Finley sometimes slides across his flat when he gets up in the morning, or text will include /wiggle in the text boxes), but that's to be expected and don't detract from the game. The pacing and the mini-games are my primary complaints. There isn't much time to socialise with other characters, which sometime made it hard to tell who people were in the plot. The first two acts also dragged on a bit, and I think having more days off to socialise would help. Act 3 was extremely short, and the escalation  feels very rushed. My other complaint is that the mini-games are also quite challenging, even on easy mode. Also the catalyst for Act 3 is never resolved.My suggestions:Review mini-game instructions in the phoneAdd a timer to act 3 when Finley is on the ground floor . I feel like that would have added to the player experience.Add hints or make the mini-games easier (especially in the easy mode)Fix the issue with the soundtrack being drowned out/extremely quietAdd a map feature to the phone so players don't get lostLet us visit the Glowmilk Woods on our own. I want to visit Let us find the cause of the illness in Act 3

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Rush job leads to a buggy mess, overuse of the same minigames, and no ending. You need to really have loved Night in the Woods in order to get through what is essentially Night in the Woods 2.I bought the game well aware by other reviewers that the game was riddled with file ending softlocks but waited for patches to come out. After about the 8th pure bugfix patch that came out, I thought the game would be in a state where it could be played through to the end and for the most part it is. The worst thing I ran into was a character disappearing to make getting the good ending to an event impossible, which was fixed by exiting to the main menu and redoing the section.Since this game is pretty blatantly "Night in the Woods 2," complete with Finley's inner monologues and Mia and Karl serving as Gregg and Bea from NitW 1, I'm going to be comparing it to that game.The small town of Porcupine is larger than Possum Springs was but there's also screens that serve no purpose at all. Generally you'll be walking to your job instead of taking the fast travel option because NitW 1 players will be obligated to talk to everyone and check out all of Finley's inner monologues when interacting with inanimate objects. The main issue overall is Porcupine having a fork in the road which both lead to the same destination, and they both have one completely useless screen each so it'll take a while to truly see what the people... And the closed stores and statues have to offer.Story, what's to say, it's about your first days working in a hospital fresh out of medical school. Act 1 is also the only times you'll be seeing the nightmares that plagued NitW 1 while Act 2 does it's job well. Act 3 is supposed to be when the story gets spicy but all of a sudden, it abruptly ends and the credits start rolling. It would be very hard for anyone to see the ending and not go "That's it?"Gameplay is almost exactly the same as NitW 1 but there are far more minigames and you will be doing the same ones over and over again because they just so happen to be how Finley does his job as a medical intern. There is an accessibility option that supposedly simplifies it but all I've noticed it do was slow down the stethoscope game and less shaking on the injection game. Doing Finley's job gets repetitive as you'll be playing each minigame a minimum of about 6 times each.Music is a little more chill so to speak, it lacks a proper ear worm that attaches to you. No real complaints, it does loop properly which is becoming a rarity for indie titles.The elephant in the room with this game is the glitches. If it wasn't obvious by Act 3, this game was a rush job. Waiting for eight bugfix patches to come out wasn't enough as I still constantly had the notes tab of Finley's phone (NitW 1 Mae's Journal) breaking, NPCs getting stuck in walking cycles, and major characters disappearing entirely. If I had played this game without waiting, I surely would have had to start over from a file ending softlock.EDIT: Almost forgot what makes the glitch issue even worse than described. This game has no manual save and file select at all. It is entirely autosaves with long gaps in-between.Final Verdict: If you really, really loved Night in the Woods 1, you'll probably play this anyway. If you either didn't play Night in the Woods or thought it was simply a meh game or worse, avoid this.

_childDocuments_.review: The art and music are lovely, but the quality control on the game is very poor. The messy and incomplete implementation of condition/world state tracking makes what is at times tedious gameplay all the more frustrating when you lose progress or have to repeatedly restart to clear out of a bad state. Fall of Porcupine is incredibly buggy. Whether it is visual bugs such as text overlaying text, random floating UI just visible in the margins of the screen or character and scenery glitches, button inputs that simply don't work, and messy state tracking in the world that either causes you to lose progress if you do things out of a certain order or, worse, have to restart the game to clear your status (and have to redo a bunch of tasks).  I all but gave up when I got to a showstopper bug where an instruction dialog box for dumpster diving with Karl wouldn't clear and I couldn't progress further (and then a combination of opening and closing the pause menu - which was invisible behind this instruction menu - finally got the state unstuck).It's unfortunate, but this game is not worth the frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it, but I'm so glad I bought it at a discount...Overall, I enjoyed the game. The art's beautiful. The characters are good. I can understanding leaving some things hinted at or unanswered, but the plots feels unfinished. I can see what they were aiming for, story-wise, but they didn't give it enough time. _childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the game for hours now, going out of my way to talk with NPCs in search of an actual conflict, but there just doesn't seem to be one. It's rare that I outright drop a game, let alone one I was eagerly wanting to play, but I find the idea of even booting the game again a chore. The game clearly is trying to emulate what made Night in the Woods great while putting its own spin on it, but it doesn't succeed at either. The characters feel dull and listless, the painfully inoffensive protagonist most of all. Finley is unimaginably anodyne as a protagonist. He has no driving force, and from what other reviews say this isn't going to change when the story suddenly happens around him at the last second.The game certainly loves to go for a comedic tone, but this falls flat on its face when a significant chunk of the jokes don't land or go on too long. Rarely do I find myself wanting to skip dialogue this much. The game looks and sounds pretty, but these large vistas work against the game when so much time is spent on slowly walking everywhere. The game's maps are too big and empty to keep me interested.

_childDocuments_.review: Ehh, man, this is a hard one. I really wanted to like this game - especially because of it's german dev team and I am german myself. But this game is just not as good as you might think and way more serious than the artstyle would lead you to expect.Here is my spoiler free review.STORYFirst of all, this game has no story. You experience the daily life of Finley, a newcomer doctor at the local hospital, who is also new in Porcupine. This is it. You get up, take a walk and get ready for work. You have to treat three patients per shift by playing different mini games. Depart of work there is not much to do in this small town. You're friends will ask to hang out with them and you can talk about writing a comic with a school girl, but this "side mission" was completely bugged out in my playthrough, so I couldn't finish it.BUGSThere aren't particularly many bugs, but when some of these bugs occur, you need to restart from the last checkpoint. Smaller bugs are lagging sound, town members bumping against each other and running on spot, repeating dialogue windows and so on. Only during the last section of the game, it really started to lag all along, with massively frame drops and sound just disappearing completely.DETAILSI thought this game would be really made of love, but there aren't as many details as I expeted. Just to name a few:- man is talking about the loss of his hat, but the character model still got it's hat on- Finley always switches clothing from work to private, but other characters are just celebrating with their doctor's coat on- the town is big to run through, but there's nothing to do and only a few objects to click on- if you click on sth and Finley tells you sth about it, the same dialogue can be repeated by switching scenes- sometimes an object seems to be clickable, but nothing happens- some characters may tell you sth, but your character starts asking about the exact same thing you were been told seconds ago, like it never happenedI am sure I have forget about sth, but like this, I sadly cannot recommend Fall of Porcupine.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall of Porcupine:~~~~~~~~~~~~~Finley has just finished his degree in medicine and is eager to put what he learned into practice. He and his fellow graduate, Mia, have been given an opportunity to do so in the small town of Porcupine. Like all small towns, people know each other well, and like a virus, the word spreads quickly when new citizens move in. Finley hasn’t had as much time to socialise with the inhabitants of Porcupine as he would have liked to. And, to make it more difficult, he was involved in a small incident at the hospital which has seen him confined to his home for a few days to recover from a big bang on his noggin. Let’s follow the story of Finley in the Fall of Porcupine.Fall of Porcupine is a story-driven adventure game developed by Critical Rabbit and published by Assemble Entertainment on the 23rd of June 2023, on the Steam platform.I am truly sitting on the fence with this game. There are some very good aspects, and there are some big misses too, probably due to the subject of the game, which is healthcare. The story is rather well-designed, well-told, and has a couple of twists. The presentation of the world, a colourful paper-style artwork, is charming; all the characters that you pass by or speak with are animals. The standout feature for me is the depth of character detail; it’s very good and keeps you wanting to know more about the various personalities. You experience a range of emotions, which you can imagine doctors and patients would go through, and it is well done.  However, the game lacks entertainment value. To be fair, the subject of health is tough. The developer's idea to have tasks in the form of mini-games to complete at the hospital on a daily basis is good, but they are easy and monotonous. I am afraid it is borderline boring! All except for the basketball mini-game that Finley and Mia play after their busy day at the ward, as well as the excursion with Pia in the woods, where you get to experience an easy platformer parkour. The game needs more upbeat moments like this.Finley can walk through the town on his way to his day or night shift. There are two routes that both lead to the Saint Ursula hospital: the scenic route (with a view of the town) and the high street route (where shops are located). Finley will be able to talk to NPCs on the way to the hospital. He has a cell phone which provides information and keeps track of the characters he meets.  There’s also the hospital tasks application, which gives Finley the room, photos of the patients and a treatment icon (telescope, medication etc) for each shift in the form of mini-games. As mentioned, the story is pretty good.  That is, until you arrive at the ending, which is abrupt and left me with a feeling of emptiness. Perhaps this is due to an attempt to elongate the story too much without additional variety.  I’m afraid I didn’t receive my happy pill with this one.   The artwork is colourful and charming, and the music is pleasant throughout the game. I experienced a few bugs, such as Finley disappearing from the screen while moving forward, as well as a few crashes to the desktop which increased the points deduction on my final score.  But I will give it a thumbs up for their effort and choosing a very difficult subject for a game.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Charming Artwork+	Great character persona depth+	Good story +	Trading cards and achievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	Mini games are far too easy-	Has several bugs -	I experienced a few crashes to desktopFall of Porcupine has charming artwork, and the storytelling is rather good. But the game is monotone, and the mini-games are too easy.5/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: Night in the Woods clone: The (mostly) good edition.The game follows a young doctor bird named Finley who deliberately chose to work in a small city with decaying health infrastructure. Guy puts a lot of one man acts talking with statues and objects, like Mae from NITW but without all the mental issues and negativity. You can sense the influence of NITW everywhere, but that's where I felt that most.While its story may feel like a repetitive cycle of everyday routine at the beginning you will feel the crescendo of tensions in later chapters and the game did that just alright to keep me interested along. But. The ending.When a story reaches its seeming climax, you naturally expect the game to give itself a proper closure, but it never comes. it just ends prematurely. Why didn't they write five or six more dialogues to provide more context after all the effort they put together is beyond me, it's almost like they finished the release build on Friday 5PM and minted the gold disc immediately after clocking in next week. This is a major flaw for games such as this, because it's like giving people tasty hotdogs but with one side dipped in ♥♥♥♥. despite the fact that most of the food was tasty and clean all that remains in people's mouths in the end is a taste of ♥♥♥♥. and that's what most of them remember.But as much as the disappointing the ending is, i don't regret spending time in Porcupine. Its outstanding visuals atmospheric music, and its characters and how they're written left enough positive impressions on me to overlook all its weaker points. I, as a person, absolutely hate backtracking, as it's a waste of time. Porcupine has this split over the bridge/under the bridge section meaning you have to endure a fair moment of backtracking every game day in order to talk to all NPCs because you can't freely navigate between two sections of the town because the options such as shortcuts aren't there. some may feel this exhausting because there aren't really that many NPCs in this game you can talk with. Plus alot of the lower-the-bridge sections are empty and just there for the one specific moment in the story to be used. But I didn't care walking around Porcupine for some more. The game perfectly captured this nice little cozy town vibes and it has this effect of warming people's minds. If you like relaxing laidback games or are a fan of NITW it's worth giving it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Someone gifted me Fall of Porcupine and it took me a while before playing it. I'm still grieving and I didn't know how much it'd trigger me. Now that I've finished it, I can say that only one scene triggered me.Though, I nearly gave up after a few seconds because there is no way to see the game's keybinds and as someone not used to this kind of keybinds, I didn't know what key to press to talk and get the talk going with NPCs. (spoiler alert : press E)Fall of Porcupine may be better enjoyed with a controller over KBM. KBM is sometimes scuffed. There are other playability-related issues such as the inability to save manually or to know exactly when your last save occurred.The info on your smartphone about your fellow citizens are giga-scuffed. It will often display info you shouldn't know, be it because you missed a dialogue or because they'll tell you about it later.Mini-games don't always fit the medical action they are supposed to embody.Even if I read that the game is supposed to emphasize the current issues of our medical systems, these stakes only strike during act 3. Before that, working at the hospital feels like a part-time internship.I've had a hard time relating in any possible way with Finley. He is THE goodie two shoes, utmost naive, not very level-headed character, and it's annoying.The end of the game is very abrupt, it clearly lacks an actual epilogue or anything to bring a sense of closure. Plus, the hospital's secret is very... down to earth, nothing to do with the horrific foreshadowing in act 1 and 2.The replayability seems limited. Achievements will ask you to play the game twice.To end on positive notes, the art is very pretty and BGM is good, it fits the mood pretty well. Many characters are truly endearing.Even if you talk to everybody all the time, don't expect more than 8 hours for a full playthrough and less than 6 hours for a straightforward one.EDIT : Play the demo before acquiring the game, demo and game are two different experiences and I really wish I could still have access to it now that I have the full-game. One beautiful sequences, the castle ruins, is only available in the demo (or else, tell me how to get there and when) which is incredibly weird and a true shame since it is clearly advertised on the game's Steam page.I've experienced softlocking bugs during my second playthrough.I wish we could give neutral reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall of Porcupine has fantastic character and environmental art, fantastic music, great animations, and a real honesty to its small town writing that gives the game a lot of heart. It retains a lot of the cozy formula from Night in the Woods (truthfully, most of the games design ideas are copied straight from the former), in which you have regular conversations with regular citizens and get to know them more as the days go by. The game also has much better mini-games than NitW, some of which come as part of your job, and some of which come as surprise activities outside of work. A lot of the side characters are diverse and memorable, doing a good job of leaving you wondering what your next interaction with them may be like. The game also has incentive for a second replay, since certain sequences will require you to choose one of two branching paths to take, which allow you to spend more time with a specific character. And by the end, the climax of the narrative feels well-earned and as dramatic as it should.The game does suffer from some real issues of pacing however- where NitW had issues as well with just how much walking you had to do to get across town each day, it was at least broken up with platforming exploration, finding characters in new places, and meeting new characters high up on the rooftops. So much of your daily routine in FoP however, comes down to holding A or D, and then reading a block of text from one character before moving on to the next. Because of the size of the town, and even the interior of the hospital, this takes a lot of time, going to check on the characters on each side of a screen to see if they've got something interesting to say.The game seems to have a bus mechanic to let you skip a lot of the walking across town, but I never ended up using it as it seemed like it would mean missing conversations with the various townsfolk, which is part of what gives cozy games their heart and charm.Similarly on the characters, whereas the side characters are reasonably memorable, as a consequence of the game being more grounded, the main characters you interact with fall pretty flat, especially for the first half of the game. There's no Gregg here with his wild and unpredictable ADHD antics, no Bea with her understandable frustration with being trapped by the weight of responsibility. For me personally, Karl is probably the only main character I'll remember down the road, as his one on one antics are pretty memorable. A couple of the characters that Finley is supposed to have bonded with, the narrative never really shows you... why. They seem like nice enough folks, but there's nothing particularly unique about them, but the game assumes you'll like them all the same.Similarly with the grounded premise, there's no hook for a very long time into the story- no cutoff hands in the road, no mysterious cults or potential ghosts as its spiritual successor had. The game's attempt to mimic the sense of mystery in that plot is  Needless to say, it takes a long time before something happens with the narrative to get the player invested- I found myself having to break the game up into playing one in-game day per session to keep me going through.And finally, the game fails to have a closure sequence; it simply hits the climax of the plot and then, ends. Which, is a choice. But it leaves you feeling very "...Ok. Now What?"The developer has already patched some of the issues I experience, but hopefully with some more income and some more time they can correct more to make the game a better experience for later players.• The  didn't work for me at all.• Some of the instructions for the mini-games are unclear (the stethoscope one in particular was very confusing for me because I didn't get that you were meant to use both WASD AND the arrow keys).• Every time before a mini-game starts, there's a screen to press E- this is good, but a missed opportunity to have the option to check the instructions for the mini-games again, in case you've forgotten how they work.• There's no text speed option in the game, and it goes a bit too slow for my reading speed. This lead to me double clicking to advance text, which 80% of the time would advance the text, and 20% of the time skip the line entirely. This is mostly an issue because there's also no text log that you can check in case it happens, so you just sort of miss those lines permanently.• Multiple save slots would be a welcome addition.Fall of Porcupine is an artistic wonder. The writing has real heart, although the amount of dull traversal and the slow build-up it takes the narrative to get somewhere can be off-putting. Still, the climax is well done, and there's enough interesting side characters to meet along the way to make it worth the journey.

_childDocuments_.review: Short review for 3 hours in.Holy smoly this game is sleepy. Going into this game, I did not know what to expect. I bought it soon after finding out about it. Figuring from the general setup the game had on showcase, it was something like NITW but its own story and spin on gameplay and it was that in some ways. However the game wants to pace things out extremely far away at times, the town of Porcupine feels like a much much less dense place compare to Possum springs. Felt like I was studying the walking animation more than anything else at times.That being said though the game so far has been enjoyable, story has been pretty alright despite the insistence to pace it out (which I believe is a intentional artist decision). As how its compares to Night in the Woods? Its probably not the "better" of the two games due to pacing preferences but that is fine imo. I am interested in how this game is going to play out and would recommend it so far to anyone who's looking for something inspired a bit by Night in the Woods.Edit after reaching the ending once.A taste of Story Corps, if you do not know what is I urge you to take some time and find out. This game has allot of feeling adjacent to this story telling nonprofit. For those who don't know and want a TLDR, Story Corps is a organization that specialize in recording stories from elderly and publicize them for the public. The stories they told are often of people who are already gone or of people on death's door themselves. In my opinion, this very adjacent relation for Fall of Porcupine is one of the ways it shines the best.However it needs to also be said, Fall of Porcupine feels like a incomplete story. With many loose ends and lack of vague conclusions to derive any closure on anything relating to anyone who wasn't a main character. This void is part of the major contributing factor of why I feel like, after completing the game, I feel that I cannot recommend it.This buggy game which grinds you down with how basic it depiction of its own in-game events are feels like... they've quite literally copy the homework of Night in the Woods in many parts. The game remixes it a little bit but didn't quiet understand why storybeats made that other game feel compelling and in that mimicry, it feels like it failed to land its ending. For whats the game has going for itself, the story is pretty alright, it just wraps up awfully with a bang that feels to soon. Maybe they needed to ship the game out sooner and had to make cuts? I cannot say for them.What I will say though is that I didn't expect to walk out disappointment to this extent and unsure how I feel about a sequel to this game. Since well, you can argue a sequel can wrap up "where are they now" but not sure if it would be worth it if you want to compare to what else can be bought for the same collective sum of income. As nice as Porcupine is, with how it is, I cannot recommend it.I am not sure how I feel replaying this game years latter either.However, I will say, I don't regret playing Fall of Porcupine at the very least.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give it a thumbs up because clearly a lot of love and passion went into it. But, this game has some serious problems, there were several times when it glitched and I couldn't interact with anything and I had to reload. The mini-games get incredibly difficult as time goes on and since there's only a few of them that's not much fun. Maybe making the "work" not fun is part of the theme but I didn't much care for it. It almost seemed like some of them were actually not responding properly to inputs (such as the line graph one). The ending also goes from being a compelling narrative that says a lot without directly saying it to a complete melodrama in the end. I would have given that ending another pass.That said the game does touch on some important issues about healthcare and does make you empathize with the profession. It also creates a very believable anthopromorphized world and the characters are all believable and well written. The art is also perfect in every way, beautiful and expressive.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely character designs and art style. A touching story. Fun minigames.This game is a good 3.5/5 experience that is worth playing through. If you do give it a go then change your settings to make the minigames easier, don’t leave it on default. The experience is let down by some writing issues in parts and some game breaking bugs that persist throughout the game and are easily encountered. Achievements are randomly earned. Interactions can be disjointed if you miss the starting part of it since you can end up either in the middle or the end of a character's dialogue. One minigame in particular does not work properly unless you change the settings. UI elements are visible that shouldn’t be seen (at least for me on Steam Deck). Finally, the story kinda just ends and you’re left with little epilogue and some unanswered questions. It is a shame that this game hasn’t been patched in a while as it could really push this whole experience up to a 4/5. Still, I recommend a play through at least once just because Finley is precious.
