_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful experience! I never played the original Myst or Riven, but bought the bundle as they both looked very interesting. Riven was the better of the two and the more visually appealing remake. Graphics are gorgeous, puzzles are thought provoking and difficult, and exploring the island and story was awesome. As someone who didn't play the original, I think one specific aspect of the puzzles that you're supposed to deduce is perhaps a bit too far fetched (or I'm too dumb, also possible) but otherwise they were the perfect difficulty of note taking and reading through journals. Would highly recommend to puzzle / story / old point-n-click fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game holds up way better than I hoped for. The puzzles feel more grounded and less surreal than many of Myst's puzzles. This new edition looks just how I remembered the original looking though of course now it's fully 3d rendered in much higher resolution. The move to first person shooter controls feels natural and doesn't detract in the slightest. The puzzles themselves felt good for the most part--not too difficult and not to easy. There are some journals in the game that feature a lot of writing but I found the writing to be engaging--the entries were well written enough to easily hold my interest despite being fairly long.The game has a very neat built-in screenshot library, which make 99% of the puzzles solvable without having to take notes. Unfortunately when I played there was some sort of bug which caused screenshots to blur with previously taken ones which made them blurry. One puzzle in particular was annoying when I noticed that a bunch of glyphs I took screenshots of were unreadably blurry. I had to go back and take multiple screenshots of each one until I got a non-blurry result.The fast travel system that you eventually unlock is fairly cumbersome. It's still faster when you're island hopping but there are a lot of slow animations to sit through. It can be frustrating when you want to pop over to one part of the world to check something and then pop back.Still these complaints are rather minor. If you liked Myst or other puzzle games, you'll probably like this one. I sure did!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: In the 90's I was obsessed with the original Myst and Riven. I wanted nothing more than to visit them for real. This is as close as I am going to get to that, and I am very grateful for it.I have now finished the game (without using any hints apart from one accidental minor puzzle spoiler I stumbled upon) so I am updating my review to reflect this.The graphics are incredible and look great on Steam Deck, although I am sure they are the best on a max-spec PC/PCVR rig.I am loving that the game is both such a familiar and nostalgic recreation of one of my favorite games of all time, but also has many bold changes from the original. Some are necessary to adapt the game to realtime 3D/VR, while others I've seen look like they have been made to flesh out the world and the story and provide a sense of wonder, mystery, and discovery for seasoned fans. It's kind of like playing the game for the first time again, which is an incredible gift. I’m sure this was a difficult tightrope to walk, but I think they’ve done an admirable job and managed to stick the landing.I am so happy that they got the original creative leads back together for the remake (Rand Miller, Robyn Miller, and Richard Vander Wende.) I think they have been able to make the new content fit well into the original vision for the game because of this, and the respect that newer Cyantists have for this game as well.The VR controls work well for the most part. I have had a few issues such as a particular puzzle involving sliding tiles being difficult to control, and the hotspots for book pages being a bit difficult to grab, but I managed. I have been playing in both VR (Quest 3 standalone) and flatscreen on deck, so I am assuming the controls for the PCVR version are the same. The flatscreen controls are quite smooth and intuitive and work great on deck also.Also as an aside, the new screenshot and note system they added is quite nice, but to solve the core puzzles in the game I’d still recommend using pen and paper to solve the core puzzles like in the old days, it really is just so much more intuitive. This is why I switched from VR to flatscreen about halfway through the game.I do have a few relatively minor nitpicks. I think the CG humans are much improved over Myst (2021), they still look a bit videogame-y but so far have been good enough. It's a shame, but necessary, to lose the original FMV performances, and I think the new actors and mocap performance matching to original audio has worked pretty well.But these criticisms don’t do much to sully the experience for me. All in all, I loved this game. Thank you so much, Cyan, for making my childhood dream a reality - I've been waiting for this totally immersive experience of Riven for almost 30 years!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I simply HAD to write a quick "review", even though I've just made it to the Jungle Island with the plesiosaurs sunning on the rock (chapter 2 if you're counting). Coming upon these beasts was one of my favorites moment playing the original Riven 27 years ago. Sneaking up on them then watching them lumber away into the water was so fulfilling with the visual remake of Riven I almost yelled.THIS is how you remake a game! Other companies take note:CYAN did this masterfully in all respects. I loved the Myst remakes and of course all the original Myst games, but seeing RIven in all it's visual splendor, even though I haven't even really explored the jungle island area yet? Jaw dropping visuals, beautiful score bringing back such good memories. The satisfaction of solving puzzles is so fulfilling, still, as it was with the original Riven. (Note: I purchased the "Companion" DLC, which I know will help at some point. It's very well-composed and offers small clues, as well as full solutions. I'm so glad it's also in PDF form, so I can copy it from the game's files to my desktop and alt-tab back and forth from the game if and when I need help)Back to the game: as noted, stunning (and I mean STUNNING) visuals, beautiful audio score that touches on so many aural memories of the game, gorgeous animations abound everywhere. Photorealistic water/ocean effects. THe character animations are very well done in 3D (I don't mind the lack of the FMV videos from the original; no way to implement those without degrading the "look" of the game, plus taking up a LOT more install space). Some of the puzzle solving (so far) isn't exactly the same  as in the original but the basics appear to still be there, and I don't mind that. I'm treating this as a new game.Important: the RIVEN re-creation is optimized wonderfully, even on my 5-year old Dell desktop PC that, while still robust, certainly isn't top of the line anymore. And that's with ALL visual settings cranked up to EPIC. Amazing. I mean, I've got a little fan-noise, but not much. If this runs on MY PC, it'll run on yours :-)OK, back to the game. I haven't been as happy to play a computer game in quite a while, and I've played TONS of PC games. Oh, wait....did I mention MULTIPLE SAVE SLOTS (I've used 4 so far, I'd venture there are more than that)? Us older adventure gamers sure appreciate that, Cyan teams. Thank you! Very few games have that feature anymore.For me, so far? 10/10. I can't wait to progress further. Damn, this game is so gorgeous. Glad I'm retired. More time to play Riven :-)Thanks for creating this masterpiece, Cyan. Again.*****NOTE: I am NOT playing the VR version, so I cannot speak to anything VR-related. Just the non-VR version.***********Two notes now that I've been playing for several hours:1) There are 10 manual save slots, which is great.2)Do NOT waste your money on the companion guide, as i did. Many of the "solutions" are obtuse and are in little way actual solutions. There is a good video walkthrough in the "guides" here on Steam and also a decent walkthrough online on one of the gaming sites. The five (I've been counting) times I've needed the "companion guide", it has been an actual help only two of those times. Waste of money.Loving the game, though!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is buggy in some ways—it crashes all the time. The UI is clunky in a lot of ways: going out of bounds (i.e. moving around naturally in VR) leaves you not knowing where to stand for getting back in-bounds, and holding open a book for an extended period of time *really* starts to hurt your wrist, and going into the menu sometimes forces you to use your non-dominant hand until you go back into the game and physically handle an interactable object with your dominant hand. I've had similar problems with Cyan's other VR titles—they really need a UI/UX guy who knows what they're doing.All that said, it's still an amazing experience, and I'd still recommend it for people who have enough technical savvy and cool enough heads to work through the very obvious, actually very bad problems. If I were a professional reviewer, I'd obligate myself with a negative review, but the truth is I personally am really enjoying the game (after an initial period of being very angry with it).

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with the Myst series, and have many fond memories of them.  I have bought the various remastered and improved versions of Myst over the years, and while I enjoyed playing them, I have always considered Riven to be the highlight of the series, and always wondered if they would ever remaster it.  In some ways I didn't care too much, because the original game was great to play and its graphics aged surprisingly well.  But when I saw that this was coming out, I got it as soon as I could, and I was not disappointed.  The improved graphics and ability to freely walk around is certainly nice, but it was the little touches that I appreciated.  For one, they improved the depth of the island, by which I mean they added various things to show how Gehn and the Rivenese lived there.  But they also worked to address potential plot holes from the original game, so that there was a more logical backstory and how some of the puzzles were set-up made more sense.  I won't say more as that might give away some plot points, but if you played the original and remember it well, you will enjoy this game.  And if this is your first time, then I think you will enjoy it as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know how I feel about this game. Its not the original, but is very closely based on it. Its a Remake, not a remaster. To me, the story is weak, and does not really work. They left it and most of the puzzles mostly the same. They did change the world. That I could tell, they didn't do this with Myst. They left it all the same, just linked it in a first person mode. They didn't do that here. If your going to update the game, update the story.The story is weak. Poorly written. Outdated. This is a big deal because you have to read through it to get the answers. This makes playing the game tiresome. Thinks click, but are not always pointed out. I did a lot of guessing and got pretty far. I had to backtrack to try to remember how I would have figured out to get to point. I got really far without an effort. Then I needed to know what it all was that I did to solve a bigger puzzle that used a lot of the information I never picked up on.To be honest, unless you are vested in this game, it doesn't keep me focused in the game. Many of the mechanics are broken in the game. at times the cursor pops up to tell you to interact, and at times it won't. I found Myself going on a click hunt. to see if I could click the right thing. Its not a game for me. I think if they MMO this title. Maybe gave it a chat. Maybe played with others. It might work. _childDocuments_.review: Very accurate recreation of how the original 'felt' to play and explore. Lack of forced perspectives made it easy to get lost in the world again, as much now from taking in the scenery as from missing 'that one item or button', a liveable trade. Main hiccups are mostly technical issues, like lighting and rendering bugs/pop-in at the edges of the screen. Also, the 'internal' screenshot resolutions can frequently render them useless for visual information, *cough* comparing lights to corresponding symbols on a stone wheel *cough*.The 3d renders of characters are often uncanny, but generally understandable alternatives to locking down movement for cutscenes, though the one 'fleeing' character did demonstrate that they were still 'forced' to stop you at least once. Really, the biggest thing that stuck out to me was how neatly trimmed Atrus was, when his journal reads more as a man buried in his work, using your help as a trump card only after months of all-consuming writing and formulating.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to say no to but it’s just not very good in 2024.  I remember playing the original.  Vaguely.  The representation is faithful enough, I think.  But now it’s just a tedious easy puzzle game with a lot of invisible walls as well as endless backtracking with slow unskippable animations (just let me climb a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ladder, why does that have to be on rails?!).  Of course, in the mid-90s, riven was a super impressive game for many reasons.  It looked crazy good.  It was imaginative.  It evoked 3d convincingly enough while actually being a series of stills.  The sound design was amazing.  Myst was more impressive in my opinion but this was a good sequel.  The flip side of the faithful representation in 3D is that while in the 90s there were just no options to go in certain directions depicted convincingly enough by not being able to click on them, recreating it faithfully now means invisible walls.  While in the 90s the animations of stuff moving were impressively blended into the stills (also padded the play time, let's be honest), now, they’re nothing special and take so long that I’ve honestly walked away from switches thinking they did nothing only to then figure out that the animation that you’re now not forced to look at is just very long.  While the vistas and land still lives without people or animals helped not break immersion in the original, now it makes they make the game feel lifeless.  The now version is also much more pixel hunt heavy.  In the original, you’d be face to face with a thing and it’d be clear that it has to do something.  Maybe you don’t have the info or some doodad yet but it was clearly a point of interest.  Now, it’s easy to miss interact-able objects  because they have to be looked at from a relatively narrow range of angles (sometimes... sometimes clicking anywhere within a cubic meter zooms you on an object), the hitboxes are usually tiny, and you’re surrounded by thousands of beautifully rendered objects that do nothing.  While it was fun deciphering the languages, it turned out that I was nowhere near needing to do that and actually I had just missed a rusty valve on a rusty pipe a couple hours previous.  Not failed to see the logic or couldn’t figure out a puzzle, no, missed a brown thing against a brown background, at the edge of the screen.  And don’t get me started on the reading.  So much reading.  Like, worry about oled burn in amount of reading…It's also important to point out that while some of the things that are annoying now were annoying in the 90s, the games in this series were so different than anything else out there, it was worth it.  Now, any recent shooter looks better and has have worlds that feel more alive.This game occupies a weird netherworld for me.  It wasn’t as memorable as Myst so I’m not basking in nostalgia and, while pretty enough, it’s no longer impressive audio-visually and is quite is quite frankly so-so puzzle-wise; I guess the latter was always true but it stood out against its contemporary point and clicks.  I’m inclined to say that if you’d like to experience this piece of video game history, find the original on cd and jump through the no doubt numerous hoops in order to get it to run.Or get this.  Preferably at a deep discount.  But know that you might feel more annoyed than challenged.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really have any hours on record for the game as I played it together with a friend on his setup, however, I have to say, this remake of the 90s classic is absolutely above and beyond what I expected.Everything from the meticulous reproduction of the original environments, the puzzles, either being the same or improved upon, and numerous incredibly smart alterations and additions lead me to say that this is absolutely the definitive version of the game, and a true must-play for fans, players of the original, and newcomers alike.Now while I do praise the game highly, and the experience of stepping into this world all over again was an incredible experience, I will say I find the biggest caveat to both this and the Myst remake is that the characters have been moved to 3D models from FMV. I fully understand and sympathise with the reasons why it has to be this way, and I can't envision anything but the most difficult of ways to attempt to implement a solution that bleeds upscaled or re-shot FMVs of the characters into a fully 3D real-time environment, however, there is a certain magic and immersion I had in the original games due to this marrying of these elements, and the overall experience is lesser for their omission.That is the only possible complaint I can fire at the game though, it stands as a true modern marvel, I would never have expected to experience Riven again in such splendour, and I can't thank the original Starry Expanse team and Cyan for making this happen. Cyan, you were an indelible part of my formative years, and you continue to be a source of joy to this day, keep doing what you're doing ❤️Everyone reading this: Play. This. Game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, this is riven. It's good, and if you haven't played it buy either this one or the original and start exploring. It's one of those rare games where the world itself is the puzzle to be solved. Though there are a few caveats for this release:As a big fan of the original I was at first disappointed to discover quite a few differences as I explored. If you've played the game there's a good chance you'll b-line to the nearest familiar machine only to discover it's mechanics have been changed. I soon discovered that it was changed just enough to give me a new challenge and kept me busy for a good 8 hours. I originally purchased it to explore riven Island again and support the awesome fan team that led the project for 10 years only to discover there's a game there (albeit short) for returning fans as well.Changes come in three categories: 1. Lore fixes, there are a few changes that just make sense lore wise and mostly all harmless. with one major exception that will probably surprise every returning player. 2. Simplifications, there are some changes that seem to have the purpose of making things easier to understand or accessible to vr players, all but one of these are good. 3. New Puzzles, they clearly wanted to give new players a treat and replaced a bunch of puzzle elements, all of it leads to the same place but it has different solutions and even mechanics. I'm of two minds about this, One one hand it was awesome to actually have to play this version of the game and it's the closest i'll ever get to playing it for the first time again, on the other hand Riven relies so heavily on it's world building for puzzles that any change to puzzle elements is also a change to it's world, to put it simply this is not the same Riven... But for the most part it's an equally good Riven with enough meat for new players to keep you busy for a while. Good luck!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who got deeeeeeply engrossed into the Myst universe in the late 90s, Riven was and remains one of my favourite video games of all time, CD-ROM swapping and all. More than just taking Myst and making it bigger/prettier, Riven had a uniquely anthropological element to it's storytelling and puzzle design that has made it stand out not just among the Myst games but within the genre as a whole - there's a wonderful immersive elegance to the idea that a major obstacle to your progress could be solved by a 5-year-old who lives in this world you've been dropped into.  Really my only knock against it was that it's postage stamp-sized resolution has done it's world building and its puzzle design poor justice as monitors have become ever larger and more pixel dense. Suffice to say, I've been dying for a remastered version for decades at this point - this remake was a day-one buy for me and I dived head-first into it. This is a heavy remix of the original's structure - the gorgeous locations all feel highly familiar and the story plays out in a near-identical way, but the puzzle alterations are substantial and will both keep you from speedrunning through based on your memories and completely alter your way of navigating the islands - entering the spinning domes for the first time was an especially big unexpected surprise. One thing I especially appreciate is how the Age of Riven now legitimately feels like it's falling apart - while in the original it's decay always seemed more like it was being told rather than shown, now you get to witness (or cause!) collapsing infrastructure and seismic activity that makes the whole experience feel substantially more precarious.The biggest complaint people have has generally been the CGI actors replacing the FMV. The models are... okay. They're not fantastic, but they're supposedly better than those in the Myst remake (which I've never played) and the complaints some have that they look PS2-quality are hyperbolic. The realities of a freeroaming world and up-to-4k resolutions unfortunately just make FMV impractical. An unfortunate change but the acting scenes in Riven are so infrequent it honestly doesn't bother me too much. Completing the game is also relatively quick, especially if you're familiar with the base structures of the original. Your old notes on Dni numbers and indigenous animals will still be vitally useful here, and while the puzzles are considerably different they're also IMO a bit easier. Altogether I was able to get one achievement short of platinum within about 10 hours. Nevertheless, it's absolutely wonderful to simply revisit this world 25+ years later with the expansive visual perspective the art design truly deserved from the beginning, so much so that the lack of a quick-travel zip mode barely even registers for me. For that alone it was well worth the purchase, and it's enough to make me want to dig up my copes of the extended-universe books again.Riven runs very well on the Deck and is perfectly playable, though it is sometimes a touch slow for textures to fully render in certain visually-dense areas. Some of the video effects for the Linking Book visuals also don't load.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven is one of my top 5 favorite games of all time.  I love Cyan, and have followed the company nearly my entire life - since I first played Myst as a 9 year old kid.  This game originated out of a fan organized remake project called "The Starry Expanse" project - where some intrepid and highly skilled fans slowly and incredibly meticulously were trying to convert the images from the old Riven into high quality 3D maps, and ultimately fully and painstakingly recreate the game in every detail in full 3D.  I anxiously read every development blog update and donated money to the project.  You could tell it was a grueling and difficult endeavor, which went slowly.  Ultimately they made some sort of partnership with Cyan, who hired some of the team, and I think absorbed their work into this.What BLEW MY ABSOLUTE MIND - is that I thought this would be pretty much an inch by inch remake just as the "Starry Expanse" project was doing.  NOPE.  There are some HUGE changes.  No spoilers, but oh my lord.  Also - each time I saw something different early on, my initial fanboy response was disappointment.  Disappointment that it was different from my nostalgia.  But after I thought about the change and the decision behind that change, one by one by one - I agree with every single one of them.  The have truly gone through every tiny part of this game, and made changes that make it feel like a more cohesive, sensible, and story rich world.  The changes they made are incredible.  This is no MACLUNKY!Graphics:  Absolutely stunning.  They are taking advantage of Unreal Engine 5 and oh my GOD the lighting, and the texture / geometry detail is stunning.  I am not sure if they are using nanite and lumen but it looks like they are.  There are some scenes that truly are difficult to distinguish from a photo of a real place.  My only gripe here is the characters.  I do not think they are using metahuman.  The characters are ROUGH.  I really miss the videos of the real live actors.  They previously were so integrated into the CGI world, that it was better matching to the scenery than a lot of blockbuster movies today.  But these characters - the detail is low, the textures are rough, and the lighting is very flat.  Granted I'm on a M2 Max MacBook Pro - but this is with every graphical detail setting set to "Epic."  I wish they could find a way to rotoscope in videos of the actors into a 3D space / VR capable world, but maybe that will become a possibility in the future.Audio:AMAZING as ever.  Robyn Miller's original soundtrack is here, intact, and with all the right gameplay cues.  This is the ONLY video game soundtrack I keep coming back to again and again through the years.  The mood and the atmosphere is unlike any other sound experience.  AND - there is new stuff! That's all I'll say! :-DGameplay:All I can say is there is a MAJOR change in the way the environments and puzzles are laid out.  I love it.  It truly is a whole new game with new things to explore.  If you are upset that it is not an exact match to the "old Riven" then I would just suggest playing the old Riven.  I did leading up to this game and had an absolute blast.  I think they can both stand on their own.Story:I am nowhere close to finishing but I just had to get something down - I will be back here to update later. . . . . Overall rating pending, but this is quickly becoming my game of the year

_childDocuments_.review: The MYST franchise has always held a special place in my heart. I've tried to play modern takes on the formula with Obduction and Quern, but the transition to full 3D environments left me feeling motion-sick after a short time playing. I'm not typically prone to motion sickness in games--It might be a particular combination of Field of View with camera rotation, I'm not sure. Thankfully, I didn't have this problem with Riven. To anyone who hasn't played a game like this; it is not intuitive. You have to immerse yourself in a strange environment and solve your way out using only your perception of that environment and your assumptions of what to do. The game will tell you very little--In that regard, any trouble you get yourself into or out of will be entirely on you. This is not a game you can aimlessly walk around and click on and expect the game to deliver some kind of reward or feel satisfying. Using your wits to understand the path before you and unlocking it IS the game. Getting stuck and looking up the solution will not help--If you're stuck at one part, you're likely going to get stuck at the very next obstacle. Cheating your way through won't leave you with a satisfying experience when the game is over. It's very likely that looking up an answer will have you saying to yourself: "I could have figured that out will a little more time/patience". I've solved many roadblocks by taking a break and returning with a fresh mind, or in some cases, just thinking about the game while I'm not playing will inspire me with ideas to try/explore the next time I log in.The original Riven used full motion video for the characters you encounter in game. With this remake, they have made 3D models of the characters and boy does it not look great. It's an OK solution to the problem at hand but it definitely sticks out. Thankfully, you don't spend too much time with them for it to be such a glaring issue.While I have revisted MYST over the years with its various remakes of higher fidelity graphics, I have stayed away from Riven in the hopes that after enough time, I will have forgotten everything about it and that has been mostly true. I first played Riven on the Playstation in the late 90's or early 2000s and it was a very difficult game because it was my first venture into the genre. I've played all the other games in the Myst series since and returning to Riven has been refreshing as I now feel I can play the game with the experience necessary to succeed. There's definitely a learning curve to 'how' to play these games; the approach, mindset and how to problem solve when you get stuck. Riven can be one of the tougher games of its kind and so I would suggest playing Myst and Myst III: Exile if you think you'd benefit from some practice in an easier (relative term) game.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m giving this a thumbs up but with some big caveats:It’s Riven, so I would guess that the biggest demographic of buyers are people who already experienced this game (people like me). The base flatscreen game is good, it’s mostly on rails with branching paths which may be weird for the younger folks just now getting into it but it should make perfect sense based on the source material and I’m fine with that. This is still Riven; it’s a good game with a really fascinating universe which expands the lore of Myst pretty significantly. I haven’t played either in a while and I never finished Riven before; the visuals and the beauty of the game remain outstanding.The biggest gripe I have is that there are a lot of UI nitpicks: there should be a quick save key, the screenshot notebook should be accessible with a single step: you access the starting journal by bringing up your satchel so this seemed like an obvious move (I might have missed it if it’s there though?). Also, screenshots don’t sync across devices but your cloud saves do, which I suppose is the best outcome if you have to choose but still…The controls really need to be rebindable. I played a little on my Steam Deck and it actually runs pretty well but the preset controller settings are baffling (left bumper for screenshot? What exactly is the right trigger doing?). Currently there’s no changing it in game, so Deck users can fiddle with a custom configuration but I didn’t want to do all that.Ok. That’s the flatscreen situation, I think we’re talking about a C+ or even a B- on execution since the base game is still good and the 3D remake is pretty faithful to the visuals.The VR is at least a solid D, maybe worse. I’m not convince anyone playtested this for more than 15 minutes. The graphics are still good, I’m actually pleasantly surprised it runs on my laptop (beefy legion laptop, but still!). No. This is more about the thoughtlessness of the UI but now the ramifications are infinitely worse.Managing the 3D satchel is pretty cool, but working with the items is a nightmare: the starting journal (or other journals you may find) are atrocious since the programming wants you to turn a page at least 90% before it fully turns which means you keep trying to turn the same page over and over again. This would be easier if you didn’t have to keep your other hand gripping the book and there’s no way to change grips from continual to toggle. Opening doors sometimes works like this too. There’s a lot of accessibility settings which is great but also strange that they didn’t also add the standard VR controller settings as well.Speaking of controllers, I’m also at a loss to explain their approach. Screenshots are able to be taken in the pause menu, the menu itself is accessible (on the Q3) by holding both the X and Y buttons. The Y button brings up the satchel. You interact with grippable stuff with the middle finger grips. You move and look with the joysticks, clicking in to run. So what do the forefinger triggers and the other three buttons do? Mostly nothing? So no screenshot button? Huh?It feels like they had 30 seconds to assign controls and then never went back.So yeah, VR looks cool, it’s why I picked this up. But I’m definitely finishing this in flatscreen.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game, and certainly a contender for best adventure game of the year.Still, I prefer the original, which I played back in 1998, and then again a couple of weeks ago, in anticipation for the remake.Here's why :- In the old game, puzzles felt like they were part of the world. "Solving" them was really about immersing yourself into the world. They were replaced with new puzzles, which, while really good on their own, don't reach that same level of seamless integration. I can only guess as to why the designers made that decision, but the probable reason is that, in the old game, you could literally walk through hints without ever noticing them. This is why people felt the game was hard at the time...possibly too hard?- In the old game, moving around was super fast. You had the zip mode, and could skip any transition with the ESC button. In the remake, and even with the option to skip most transitions, I felt that moving around was more cumbersome. It might not seem much, but when you're stuck, the last thing you want is go through an unskippable animation for the 100th time (I'm thinking about you, domes).- The old game had real actors. While the new 3D models are ok, I don't think the new sections carry the same level of emotional intensity.Overall, my recommendation is to play this game, but if you're not too put off by the graphics, I would highly encourage you to play the old version, first. It's still possibly the best adventure game, ever.

_childDocuments_.review: This is  best remake I've ever played.I expected just a 3D remake of Riven, just like they did with Myst (what, 3 times now? lol). Is it that? Yes... but so much more. If you remember most of the puzzles from the original, you are in for a TREAT! The puzzles all still work the same within the world, but HOW they work have been updated and fits into the world even better than the original, adding another dimension to the puzzles and shaking things up  enough that it feels 100% comfortable but fresh at the same time. The game is gorgeous. As for the people, I'm one of the biggest fans of the original video people, but I was surprisingly 99% okay with the 3D models they used instead: they have the perfect amount of detail, look great, and are true to the original video. Atrus is the only exception for me; they've never really nailed his look with 3D models, but this one was pretty close. I had no problems with the performance, just one little visual glitch with a person in Tay.In short, I  recommend this game! Pro tip: if you find yourself going into your bag over and over for something, check your key bindings for a new key.  :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a "No, but..."  reviewRiven 2024 keeps the content fundamentals - the look, the plot, the iconic puzzle  - but like most abridged editions, loses some of the specific tone and design voice that lived in the less approachable elements and stylistic details.So despite this version's stellar environments and more modern navigation, And those were the chief reasons I loved it when I finally truly played it in 2019; and why it's still worth playing 25+ years after its launch. There are a added touches here and there that feel at home with the original design sensibility  but the changes in flow, puzzles and the new areas take away from how integrated, consistent, justified but incidental everything was in the 1997 version.It sadly feels more inline with what Firmament offered: the new elements are more than often mechanical, repetitive and fairly arbitrary to the point of feeling gamey ... an approach that doesn't live up to the design of Riven '97. But a lot of it is still very good, albeit, in a fragmented, incomplete  way... like in an abridged version.So here's my suggestion:   - using Riven Universal Hint System page where necessary.If, after that, you still  bounce hard off its navigation scheme or low resolution or no hand-holding integrated puzzles, but want to explore more of its world, come here and buy this one to play; you'll have a very decent time. a team seemingly punching above its weight with fascinating new hires; and thus potentially very cool projects on the horizon.And go play Obduction, it's almost as good as Riven 97.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with the original Riven. As far back as I can remember using a computer, I have memories of the game. As a kid I was just exploring, pretending I lived there with a strategy guide at my side to ensure I could see every nook and cranny of the world. As I got older I started to appreciate the aspects of the game I had overlooked as a kid; the incredible world building, puzzle design, sound design, music... I could go on. These things are the reason the game had so greatly captured my imagination as a kid, I just hadn't taken notice of them until I was older. While I have no regrets experiencing the game this way, as it has been hugely influential in my life and my career (I'm a game dev), I have always wished I could experience Riven blind and see if I could solve all of its puzzles myself.This remake has not only allowed me to immerse myself in a world that I've been wanting to visit in VR for a very long time, it also gave me a taste of solving Riven myself without a walkthrough thanks to the changes that have been made. I say "taste" as, even though some puzzles have been changed quite drastically, they still remain very similar in spirit. The changes are all well thought out and tend to make a bit more world building sense than the original's puzzles, though I also think they've been made a tad easier and in so doing, some of the elegant subtlety of the original's puzzles has been lost. It's hard for me to judge the difficulty of the changed puzzles though as, again, being as familiar with the OG as I am I was pretty quickly able to pick up on how the clues were to be applied to the puzzles. There is one major change to how a clue is derived that I really do not like () as the mechanism just doesn't make much world sense to me, but otherwise I am extremely satisfied with how the game design has been tweaked.Aside from puzzle changes, there are also several changes and additions to the world, all of which have clearly been thought through thoroughly. One new area in particular had my jaw drop the first time I entered it. There are also new areas that were previously only teased in the original game, and new details and sequences that wouldn't have been feasible with the pre-rendered nature of the OG, making it feel like these things were always meant to be here and now can be thanks to there being fewer technical limitations. Whether new or old, all the areas and set pieces in the game are wonderful to explore.Of course all these changes and the ability to move freely would be moot if the game didn't look good, but it is as beautiful as ever, if not more-so in some cases. Even in VR, though some graphical fidelity is scaled back, the game looks fantastic. The striking art direction of the OG is all intact. Visually I would say my only complaint is a handful of rather janky animations sprinkled through the game. Some are fantastic - animals in particular seem to have gotten special attention - but there are others that immediately made me remember I was in a video game. Some weird physics moments, a handful of awkward character animations, and unnaturally abrupt elevators were some of the more noticeable ones. This is a pretty minor complaint, but it's one of those areas that the original technically did better.Before moving on from visuals, I'll also say that the character models and animations are quite good all things considered. Some seem to have gotten more care than others but all in all this is Cyan's best attempt at realtime 3D characters.The sound design here is wonderful. I greatly admire the soundscapes created for the original game and was very happy that almost all of the original sounds were reused here where appropriate. While in recent memory Cyan's sound design has been adequate, it's lacked the level of detail in Riven's that conveys mechanisms far more complex or aged than what you'd expect just by looking at them. My only complaint is that there does not seem to be, to my ear, any spatial or binaural audio tech in the game, which is *very* important for creating an immersive VR experience IMHO. Sounds don't quite pan and bounce naturally as a result. I really wish Cyan would invest in this technology in the future, but that aside the sounds themselves truly make Riven feel alive.The original soundtrack was fantastic back when it first released and is still amazing today. It aids greatly in setting the tone and telling the story. My only complaint in regards to the OST is that the handful of new tracks, composed by the original game's composer, do not fit into the existing OST and do not reach the same level of production quality. I'm not sure why but it doesn't seem like any attempt was made to utilize the same synthesizers as the OG OST did and so the new tracks stick out a lot, and not in a good way. The production also seems very dry overall to my ears. I can't complain too much as the original is still here in its entirety, but it would have been great to get new tracks of the same style and quality.Lastly, playing this game in VR was mostly great, thought there are a few things that could be improved. For one, I have been experiencing a nasty crash bug playing in VR, often when the game tries to adjust/unlock my position due to a loading zone or due to some mechanism moving me around. Hoping this can be fixed soon. I also think the screenshot system, while sufficient thanks to the pause menu opening and closing quite quickly, could be improved. Mainly saving the scroll bar position when opening and closing screenshots and adding next/previous buttons when viewing a screenshot would make things a bit more convenient when trying to jump between several different ones. I also wish there was a better way to read journals in VR. I had to hold them at a pretty awkward angle with my Index controllers and ended up just switching to desktop mode to read them as holding them got tiring fast. Overall though the VR interactions seem pretty solid. There are a handful that express weightiness by lagging behind your hand position which I really appreciate. None of the issues I have with the VR implementation outweigh the experience of exploring this world in VR. Anyone with a headset who has been hankering for an amazing world to explore should be getting this game immediately.Conclusion: The original Riven is one of the greatest games ever made, and this remake does it justice. In fact, in some ways, it improves upon the original. While you can't go wrong with either version, this one is absolutely worth playing and will likely be more accessible to modern audiences without losing much of what made the original so great without replacing it with something equally so. VR support is solid, and makes this a must buy game for anyone looking for VR games to get lost in. This is a world I think everyone should explore at least once, even if you don't ever finish the game. If anything about this game intrigues you - a screenshot, the premise, a recommendation - don't hesitate and jump in.

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic remake of a classic. all the new puzzles were pretty tough but not too tough, i figured most everything out myself (aside from an embarrassing moment where i forgot i started a new save file and the notes i took for a code in my original save didnt apply anymore due to being randomized. oops)i love that two areas you were originally confined into a single room in were expanded. the expanded areas arent essential to puzzles or anything they just serve as wonderful setpieces to explore a bit more of the ages. highly recommend for both newcomers and returning players!as mentioned though i did have to start a new save due to a bug that softlocked me into an area connected via elevator without any switch to call back the elevator. the game just released and i did email cyan about this issue so im hoping its fixed so other players dont experience it. also worth mentioning i played this in standard flatscreen, i have no clue what the VR experience is like so your mileage may vary in that regard

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan has done something magical with Riven. Riven is an excellent sequel to 2020's remake of Myst and a perfectly fine starting point of its own. _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing retelling of the classic puzzle/narrative game. The Myst remake a couple years ago was beautiful and wonderful to re-experience, and the new randomized puzzle solutions feature was a welcome addition giving a bit more replay value than the original had. But what Riven 2024 does is far beyond that. Not only are there additions, but there are also changes to some of the puzzles, lore, narrative, and clues. Many elements are really fleshed out and it also allows you to explore further in some areas that longtime fans have always wanted to poke around in. Think of it like an Extended Director's Cut. It's almost like an alternate universe Riven where the story is more or less the same, but it's been somewhat remixed in that you cannot simply play through Riven 2024 with knowledge of how to beat Riven 1997 and expect to finish it easily. It's a retelling of the same game, but it's like a game you've never played before at the same time with new puzzles that you can solve all over again! And it does this rather well and with care for those who are very familiar with the original.You'll find new areas to explore, new puzzles to solve, new dialogue, and new music. It's often been said that Riven has all of two puzzles and the whole game is more about exploring and discovering the information and clues you need to tie it all together and unraveling the compelling plot at the same time. All you're missing is the information. The remake is no different, but there are new elements to discover as well. We also used to get the pen and paper out to make notes on our discoveries. You can still do this, but the game also graciously offers a Notebook feature that allows you to take screenshots and add notes to them allowing you to reference them at any time during the game. Sometimes drawing is easier (and more fun) to really work out the details, but you can absolutely get by with just the Notebook feature. A very welcome addition!And then there's the graphics. Ever since the first realMyst (3D remake of Myst) by Sunsoft in 2000, I've longed to play Riven in full 3D as well. But as time went on and graphics capabilities improved, I more and more wanted to see Riven given the quality it was due. The Starry Expanse fan project sought to remake Riven in full 3D and put a ton of work and effort into it over the course of the past two decades and even released a small demo of one section of the game. The feeling was amazing. But I really was hoping that the graphics quality would improve. Then Cyan created Obduction and we got to see what a full 3D adventure game by the creators of Myst could look like. It was very nice, but didn't quite reach my standards for what a Riven game should be. Then they remade Myst. Wow! In my opinion it was a few steps above in quality of what they did for Obduction. But now with Riven 2024.....well, it's everything I could have hoped for. The photorealism in full 3D I always dreamt of. The graphics are absolutely stellar. If you poke hard enough you'll find things that look a bit off, but I'd say 98% of everything is about as photo-realistic as you can get with an excellent graphics quality to performance ratio with a system with decent specs. I'm running on somewhat medium setting graphics with an RTX 2060 at 4k and I'm quite happy with the results. I don't always get a full 60 fps, but it is certainly satisfying enough.My next playthrough will be in VR and I can't wait to experience it. I HIGHLY recommend this game for old fans and newcomers alike! The puzzles themselves, as I said, deviate quite a bit from the original but they're also a lot more fair I feel. I love the original Riven experience and I wouldn't change a thing, but all those little sore spots that people have had with the original for all these years I can safely say have been very competently dealt with and made more fair with all the clues you'd need to notice things. No more "how could I have known that??" moments. But it really gives return players like me a new reason to enjoy the game. It's not something I can beat in 25 minutes, like the original, and I really appreciated it allowing me a real reason to spend more time in the game and discover all the new areas. Maybe some return players might not appreciate this, but I certainly did. The original is always there and this remake is not SO different that it disappointed me. It gave me a GAME to play and not just run through the motions with. I loved it and I expect/hope you will too.So support Cyan's amazing effort, buy Riven, and enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth buying and supporting the developers if your an old school fan or have never played it before. The game is the byproduct of developers who care. It holds up after all these years, so to speak. Thank you for your hard work and dedication in developing this perfect remake! And most importantly, making me feel like I actually am revisiting Riven.

_childDocuments_.review: As an adult I cried three times in my life. Once when I got married, once when my kids were born, and once when I stood on the cliff of Temple Island on Riven in VR. This game is an absolute masterpiece. The amount of love that was poured into it's creation in 1997 and again in 2024 is unmeasurable. The Myst franchise is much MUCH MUCH more than 6 video games. It is an experience. The beauty and depth of the series is unparalleled. The attention to detail is remarkable. The lore........... oh gosh the lore, is a masterful rabbit hole you will willingly hurl yourself into. Every game in the franchise brings its own depth to the story. But Riven....... Riven is the heart and soul of Myst. It's characters are timeless, it's vision is supurb, it's story is rock solid. The sound and visuals are carefully in harmony with each other. Riven was the first video game to rival a Holywood Blockbuster. (as far as I know) it was the first video game to have a tv commercial. Myst was the best selling PC CD-ROM game of the 20th century.1 game, 4 sequels, 1 spin-off, 3 novels, a comic book series, a GAP ad, a real linking book. No other game franchise has ever risen to the heights of Myst. Cyan does NOT make games, they engineer masterpieces, they create worlds.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely Fantastic! this game is so incredibly optimised and put together, that even though the minimum requirements state that you should have a Ryzen 7 2700x, it runs perfectly fine on a Ryzen 5 5600x, with no issues at all.MYST and RIVEN have been two titles from my childhood that I still regularly revisit for Nostalgia sake, and now that RIVEN has been re-imagined for the modern era, a new generation of folks can experience storytelling and amazing puzzles; sharing in the experiences we had decades before them.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven was one of those games that I loved and hated back in the day, because even though I was completely immersed in its world, the puzzles were too difficult for a kid like me (or maybe I was just too stupid, who knows). I gave up on finishing the game at the time, but the whole experience was memorable and even a little surreal due to the live-action clips and the real actors talking and looking at the camera. For those who are too young to know, Riven is the direct sequel to , two ‘90s games that are considered some of the most important puzzle games of all time. The latter has already had a successful remake in 2021, so now it’s time for its sequel to shine with a complete overhaul.Playing Myst is obviously recommended for many reasons, but you can prepare for Riven simply with a quick story recap. In short and without major spoilers, you play as a nameless stranger who is tasked by a man called Atrus to rescue his wife, Catherine, from his dangerous father, Gehn. Atrus is a descendant of the D’ni civilization, capable of writing worlds and traveling between them using some sort of magical books. Riven is one of these worlds (which are actually called “Ages”) and the place where Catherine and Gehn are imprisoned. Your objective is to free the woman and capture the evil father following Atrus’ plan, but nothing goes as planned in videogames and you will have to rely on your brain cells to make sense of everything. The story also includes multiple endings, so there is definitely some replayability if you feel like speed running through all the puzzles again.While there aren't any major changes from a story perspective compared to the original, there are certainly many visible differences in the gameplay and graphics. The game has been entirely rebuilt with the Unreal Engine 5 and looks simply fabulous. I had to watch a video comparison with the old one not only to see the insane graphical leap, but also the faithfulness of the developers in recreating the same feeling and atmosphere, which was perhaps the most difficult thing to achieve. Each location is gorgeous, and the level design is intricate and well-connected through puzzles. The old technical limitations have been removed (you had to move through different static images in the original game) and now you can move freely through the beautiful 3D environments. This really enhances exploration, offering a greater level of immersion and expanding the ways you can solve puzzles. The characters that were once played by real actors have now been replaced by 3D models that aren’t as expressive, but the voice acting and performance capture are still quite convincing.A few minutes into the game and I remembered why I didn’t finish Riven before. The game doesn’t hold your hand, it doesn’t tell you where to go or what to do. It’s your job to understand everything and you must figure out how to solve puzzles on your own. Instead of common puzzle mechanics (explore a location, solve the puzzle to remove the obstacle, proceed to the next location and repeat), Riven offers an open world structure where each puzzle is multi-layered and interconnected. Think of it as something more like  (which obviously took its inspiration from Cyan). Some puzzles will require you to learn different languages and number systems, while others will remain unsolvable until much later when you gain more knowledge or new items. I won’t give you any spoilers because this is the central part of the gameplay, but know that sometimes you will have to test your luck by randomly interacting with objects hoping to figure out how to progress. Between puzzles, you will explore, read, learn and be fascinated by the deep universe that Cyan Worlds has created. I’m not gonna lie, I smashed my head during the first hour trying to solve puzzles, but then something clicked in me as I was fully immersed in the world of Riven and I started to think with the game’s logic. Solving puzzles became more intuitive, still very challenging, but also rewarding because there is nothing better than feeling smart (or powerful). Some puzzles can be very difficult even for veterans of the genre and I won’t hide the fact that being unable to solve them and progress (without using external guides) will likely cause players to feel confused, frustrated or bored (perhaps all three at the same time). Riven is not a game for the average casual player who just wants to walk through beautiful, peaceful locations, but you know what? I love it! Even though it’s a remake, you finally get a real puzzle game that makes no compromises and doesn’t align with the general idea that all games should be easy and accessible to all players. I recently read a quote from the director of  saying “a game for everyone is a game for no one” and I was thinking “wow, this applies perfectly to Riven”.While the original Riven will always retain its charm, this is probably the best version to date and the one that most people should play, including those who own a VR headset. It is a spectacular remake, incredibly faithful but also enhanced in many aspects, starting with the transition from static backgrounds to 3D environments and free exploration. I think that even in modern days there still isn’t a puzzle game as difficult and complex as Riven, maybe because it wouldn’t be mainstream or maybe because players have been used to a certain level of ease and guidance in videogames that prevents them from enjoying games that test their intelligence rather than their manual skills.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece. What I love most about Riven is that it's not just some puzzles sitting disconnected and half-motivated in an environment, It's this whole world that is coherent and makes sense and motivates the things you can solve and interact with. Very little suspension of disbelief needed (with very few exceptions. looking at you, ). Never seen the world-building and the mechanics so close together in any game of this kind. _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the original Riven, so I can't compare this game with the old one, but my exposure to a similar game was the remake of Myst, which I enjoyed and which led me to buy Riven.I have mixed feelings about the game. Overall, I like how things are tied together and enjoyed the overall story and world. I cannot highlight specifics without spoiling the game. Sadly, there were a couple of things that I disliked and that made my experience worse.For my liking, there is too much traveling, considering how things are spread out. It's fine the first time, maybe the second time. But when you're stuck and looking for solutions, it becomes tedious. Taking almost 10 minutes to return to a specific place is just too much. My solution was to make saves for each place, so instead of traveling I just loaded a save. That feels like a bad design to me.I also checked how puzzles were done in the original Riven (1997) by watching some playthroughs, and I feel the Jungle Island puzzles were done better due to more obvious visual clues. The same goes for a few other places.One thing that initially surprised me was the option to take screenshots and save them in a notebook. Sadly, the execution is very poor, and it's better to take notes outside of the game. The biggest problem is the resolution: the in-game screenshots are not taken at the same resolution you see while playing. Additionally, the navigation is frustrating. When you view a screenshot and then return to your list, it throws you back to the beginning instead of where you left off.Having said that, I would still recommend the game, but there are better puzzle games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remake of a landmark title. Some differences are in place but the original 1997 release still exists and does run well on modern hardware for purists. Most impressive to me is how well the game communicates the feeling of the original prerendered 3D art. For those new to the game, in terms of modern titles Riven is closest to the Outer Wilds or Return of the Obra Dinn in its world and puzzle design. Gaining an understanding of the world is how one progresses, and there isn't anything quite like the way things 'click' in this game. One complaint I do have is that the achievements take some of the mystique out of the game, specifically by naming locations/providing more detail on art and objects you find in the world. Personally I prefer drawing my own conclusions on things in the world without the pop-ups butting in. The in-game notebook is also a bit underbaked, although a great idea. Taking notes on a pen and paper is still the ideal way (and you will need to take notes).I recommend disabling the steam overlay for your first time through.Bring a notebook, try not to look up any hints, and enjoy your first experience on Riven. You only get one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's undeniably wonderful to see one of the greatest puzzle games ever made get a modern update, but this version has a great many issues that would need to be resolved before I could recommend it without reservations. The first and most glaring issue is that almost nothing in the game is skippable, which is particularly bizarre when you consider that the original game, 27 years ago, allowed you to skip almost any animation, as the creators undoubtedly understood that even the most beautiful animation can be tedious after you've been forced to watch it 50 times. While there are specific settings that allow you to always skip ladder and vehicle animations, they don't cover the dozen other repetitive animations in the game, particularly anything involving the domes or the rotating room on Temple Island. This is even more annoying for the end credits, as if you get one of the "bad" endings and wish to restart, you're better off just hitting alt-F4, as pressing escape does nothing. Turning on ladder skips also always black-screens as it skips the animation, which I personally find kind of jarring.The game also just feels generally unfinished and lacking in polish, which is a bummer for such an incredibly gorgeous piece of art as Riven. A lot of the transition animations either prevent the camera from moving or move it in sudden and jarring ways, and the character animations feel particularly janky—doubly so for anything involving the characters' hands or facial animations, whether it's pages flapping around as Gehn flips through a book, or his glasses clipping through his hands as he sets them down on the table. The character models also feel weirdly low in detail compared to the rest of the world, especially for a modern game on a modern engine. The lack of polish in these areas really hurts the immersion, which I'd argue is an important element of the experience for a game like Riven. Despite running in a modern build of the Unreal Engine (which the game's marketing materials can't wait to remind you), you can't rebind the keys from the in-game menu, which as a left-handed person is just obnoxious. Engine performance is also inconsistent, often microstuttering at weird times. That would be a bigger issue if this were an action game, but it's still annoying.While I'm ultimately glad this remake got released, I really hope that it gets some patches to improve general polish and performance. It's a less consistent outing than I would expect from a legendary studio like Cyan.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Cyan or have never heard of Myst or any of the titles Cyan has created, the Riven remake is wonderful. There are things that have been expounded on that make the game that much sweeter from it's original in 97. I look to see Cyan address some of the graphic issues as they always have to polish Riven to a high gloss. Relax and play within worlds you can never quite forget. The sun always shines in Riven.

_childDocuments_.review: Man am I happy I played Myst first, this game is about 5 times as difficult and obscure.Good:- Graphically stunning.- Great VR mode, with a ton of comfort options.- Great performance, average ~100 fps in 1440p on an rtx 3060, on high settings (dlss quality)Kinda eh:- VR is difficult to run well, average ~40 fps on an rtx 3060 on low settings (dlss performance, playable but not great)- Puzzles are much harder than those in Myst, sometimes a bit unfair imo.- Oddly enough, no height adjustment in VR. This was present in Myst.There's a guide you can buy, but you can also use the internet to help you out, no shame in it lol.The guide gives you a guarantee that you can at least try it with a vague hint first, and not accidentally read the answers on a search engine result. But it's a bit steep, for something that you might only refer to twice.

You really feel like you have been transported into the game. I loved every minute of it.The puzzles are solvable without help, although I had to use some time of thinking in between and some solutions or progressions didn't come to my mind easily, but thats just how it should be!Also the 3D Models look much better than in the Myst Remake. What I didn't like so much are the Domes that take a long time to  each time. Other than that everything was bug free and a real Masterpiece once again. I made a terrible mistake at the last big puzzle that had me go a little crazy looking for hidden levers here and there, until I figured out that my notes haven't been correct at some point earlier, but as in every Cyan Game: Don't give up guys. The ending is worth it! I loved the Looking forward for the next VR Remake or maybe even a new Age..? ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing CYAN since Windows 3.1. MYST was one of the first games I ever played. I have played RIVEN way too many times, on PC, PlayStation, etc. I am old. To anyone, young and old, buy this game. If you liked the Original version, you will adore this new visit to RIVEN. If you have never played a CYAN Game, buy this game. Think about playing MYST first, but either way buy this game. If you know nothing about any of this, but are interested in being dropped off on a mysterious island and spending time wandering to figure out what in the world this place is, buy this game. If you like puzzles, buy this game. If you want tie-in books, buy this game.If you want a pretty place to sit in in VR and watch the butterflies, buy this game. I just want y'all to buy this game. It means so much to me, and I am so glad that after decades I can hang out on RIVEN in full movement and HD, just like I used to do while lying down in bed and pretending once my parents would kick me off the computer. In MYST History, there are three big moments for me: EXILE 360 look, realMYST full movement, and the new remakes of MYST and RIVEN. We are living in a MYST golden age, and this old dude could not be happier.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the perfect remake. Never have I play a game with such distinct mood and ambiance, I'ts as good as when I first played it back in '94.It's like discovering Riven again for the first time, go play the first Myst remake, and then dive into this amazing adventure!
