_childDocuments_.review: Thought the graphics looked no better than the mid-90s one I'd played before, but then discovered that Epic textures really are that good. Anything lower than that looks like garbage which is a shame.Walking through 3D space helps you get your head around the actual lay of the land much more intuitively than the earlier click-navigation, which makes the puzzles seem a little easier maybe? I never solved the old one but I'm further in this one than I was before.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the original Riven like I have, you're probably thinking that this is just a fresh coat of paint (a beautiful coat of paint, mind you). However, this version of Riven is simultaneously familiar and brand new at the same time. Although the ambiance remains largely the same, most of the puzzles have either been completely replaced with new ones or reworked in one form or another. Honestly, this makes it feel like I'm experiencing Riven for the first time when I was a child. There is a sense of awe and wonder that Riven manages to capture that other similarly styled games don't quite achieve.There are also some quality of life improvements such as an in-game notebook to write notes and take pictures all in-game.That having been said, there are a couple of minor gripes that I and some others have that mostly boil down to the controls. These are the issues that I know of that are in the game at the time of writing this review and may be/have been changed.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's fantastic. A wonderful remake in every way. It's beautiful, runs well (3080, 5800X3D, 4K), and remixes things in great ways to make it so you cannot simply rely on your memory from years ago. The music is a wonderful ambient backing track that is eery & incredibly memorable - it really plucks the nostalgia strings well.The major puzzles have their answers re-generated each run, so you need to learn the systems & actually have an answer. Only complaints is some things not well optimized for controller (like twisting wheels, which happens often).
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of the original Myst and Exile, but never played Riven. All new experience. First few hours were pretty wild, as the style of puzzles were very different from the other two imo. However, once I got into it, I realized very quickly it was huge, and the amount of puzzles I needed to remember were too. Needed a legit notepad for the first time. Very, very interesting puzzles. Once I got near end game, the dome puzzle was wild. Thankfully when I original found that info, it was such a clear wtf is this, it was pretty easy to put together and solve back. Love the dev, great 10 hours. Only thing I have a question for, there's two books in "233." One in the firepit, and one not active. What are these?PS to dev: I had a few bugs. 1. I hit ESC on the cart in the tunnels, and my character's hitbox went to zero and I dropped forever until I kept hitting keys and magically appeared in the rebel linking area. 2. I also seemed to have a performance issue when looking at the ocean and having the spinning dome in the same frame. 3. My interaction would freeze for a while after I openned the notebook.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely faithful remake of the original. Having played Riven since the mid 90's, I know many of these places from memory. Even though ive been to them before, the visuals leave me with a sense of awe and wonder seeing them in HD. The puzzles have been redone to be a little less tedious, but still leave plenty of challenge for you to consider bringing out the notebook to write stuff down. My only complaint is some of the animations can be a little jank and a few minor bugs, but these are not a huge hindrance and are being worked on.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: For a moment I was a bit set back when I went to find old places where I knew puzzle pieces for later were. Then I found out how they implemented the newer puzzle element and they are a BLAST even more so in VR.  Also its absolute surreal to stand in The Temple of Gehn and get a scale of how huge the ego of this guy is. There are a few things in there also from the Book of Atrus and I am super happy. Very well made so far, cant wait to beat it fully in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Guys. Guys! I got to play Riven, and it looked great and I could move around and look at everything and omg...Okay, ramble over. 3.5 hours in on Release Day, it's everything I could have hoped for as a fan since the original came out in 1997. (Remember having to change CDs every time you changed islands?) Puzzles are tweaked so you can't just copy-paste your old notes, which is a change I support.Visually? Overall, stunning. It almost feels as though the events of Myst and Riven took place a year or two later than originally depicted, and the world is truly ready to fall apart no matter what you do. I'll mention only one example to not spoil too much:  There were some tremors when I was on the first island, some steam vents opened up under the ocean, and I watched in real time as the water parted from the heat. I almost cried; it was a change that felt so true to the original that I almost -mourned- never having seen it until now. They've done everything I could have ever asked to elevate the environment with the flexibility of modern programs.My one criticism? Same as it's been for a little while: Characters are janky. It's a sincere attempt, and it's leagues better than Myst V, but takes you out of it a little bit. Beyond that, it has none of the problems the previous remakes of the original Myst had/have.If I was a new gamer looking for an exploration puzzle game? 8 out of 10. But for a long time Riven lover? 11 out of 10, no question. Seriously, put yourself in the shoes of The Stranger once more and jump into Riven.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A True Gem in the (re)MakingThis is one of those rare cases where the sequel surpasses the original in almost every category, and mind you, the original on its own is a legendary title. It's the same with this remastered/slightly remade version of the '97 classic. Myst was amazing, Riven twice that much. Bigger, better, baddasser.The story expands so much in Riven that it is a joy to unravel, the world-building and the amount of lore infused in it is brilliant, and you are constantly rewarded for your efforts, every step of the journey. Your keen eyes, ears and touch will be your guiding stars, and your brain will love you for it. Yes, it gets hard, but never to the point where nonsense, plot armor, or deus ex machina, for that matter, take hold. Instead, just like Myst before it, every piece folds PERFECTLY into the puzzle that is Riven, no pun intended. Oh, and by the way, the game looks absolutely stunning on every front, and the audio design is right there to follow. A sheer joy to play, especially in an age where we are left starving for the genre that has long been forgotten, but hopefully not lost. Minor drawbacks go to technicalities such as the mysterious absence of your notebook hotkey (I'm looking at you devs, and at your letter "P", Myst), some strange optimizations I've noticed beyond 60fps (e.g. 120 with VSync felt like limitless and uncapped, my rig started roaring), and a few glitches that occurred (not gamebreaking, just weird OOB/no clip moments at one specific ingame cutscene), and the lack of polish for the UI, with a particularly ugly and unimaginative main/options screen menu, just like in the Myst remaster.All in all, games don't get better than this, go get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Like a lot of people here, Riven is one of my very first memories. For years, I've been watching The Starry Expanse Project, just hoping that one day I could see Riven again with fresh eyes, where it looked as real as it felt all those years ago.I wasn't sold in the beginning. Right away I noticed some subtle changes that threw me off. I was expecting an exact remake, with no changes aside from what was absolutely necessary. Some puzzles were changed, or removed entirely, and I just about threw my hands up and gave it up. It wasn't my Riven.I'm glad I finished it. One thing I love about Cyan games is feeling like they know me, that their games are for people like me, who have been here for decades. And I had a moment with a puzzle where I knew the change was made for people like me, to make me slow down and enjoy the game instead of blitzing through with solutions I memorized 15 years ago. I already knew how solve the  puzzle, I've solved it a hundred times, and they know I know how to , so HA! Now the puzzle makes you ! This is a Cyan game, and you will not leave without . I felt like I was being punked. I couldn't believe it. I felt like Rand was sitting on the other side of my screen laughing, because there was no brute forcing my way through. I had to solve it myself.So what it really comes down to, is I didn't love all the changes in the beginning (but in hindsight most of them made sense, either from a story perspective or a flow/sequence perspective). Most of all though, I came to appreciate what a gift it was. Riven (1997) is as familiar to me as my own house. Cyan gave me the gift of seeing it again with for the first time. I got just a little bit of that excitement back that comes from discovering something new, and solving a puzzle for the first time, experiences I thought I would never have again in a game so important to me.If you want this to be a shot for shot remake with not a single pixel out of place, you will be disappointed. If you meet it where it is, you can play Riven for the very first time, again.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The terms "remake" or "reimagining" often provoke skepticism, frequently perceived as mere commercial ventures exploiting a fanbase's nostalgia. These projects might showcase enhanced aesthetics, higher resolutions, and better compatibility with modern hardware, yet they rarely offer substantial innovations to the original game. Therefore, when news of Riven's remake emerged, I was initially apprehensive.In 1997, Riven was celebrated as a masterpiece of environmental storytelling. Its visuals, narrative, and puzzles were pivotal in cementing the success of Myst. The question persisted: why revisit the islands of Riven after so many years? However, this new rendition of Riven is not merely a nostalgic journey but an entirely reimagined experience. The puzzles have been meticulously redesigned, the storyline has been expanded, and the previously subtle lore has been elaborated upon, rewarding those who delve deep into its intricacies.The visuals are nothing short of stunning, a testament to Cyan, the small yet talented development team based in Spokane. Their dedication and craftsmanship have once again brought this immersive world to life. This remake is not just a game to be played; it is an experience to be fully embraced and lived. Although it is indeed a remake, it has been reconstructed from the ground up, surpassing its distinguished predecessor in every conceivable way.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the original in 1998, this remake was 15 hours of intense dopamine rush - completing the multiple endings and hunting down all of the side achievements. It would have been an extra bonus if they could have somehow preserved the original video capture versions of the characters, since the 3D animated versions were a bit... awkward. But this is a very small gripe. This game is a real gem in a sea of crap.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited since Riven's original release for this retelling and it is worth it.I was an avid Myst fan when it first came to Windows in the 90's, but my computer couldn't run Riven then, so I missed it on release. I read the books, I saw the box, but I never took the leap. I played later installments, I early beta tested Uru! But I never went back for Riven.Playing this version of Riven took me back to a place I'd only ever been next to and it felt familiar and fresh. I've since played the original Riven and I appreciate the reworking of some puzzles, refinement really, and the little visual touches and changes that take advantage of a fully-3d engine. Playing this game has made me want to revisit the books, the later installments, and the community I'd spent so much time with. This is a worthy and level-setting recreation of a great game and I hope the team has it in them to continue to explore the many worlds of the D'Ni with fresh games and retelling of the originals.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven, like Myst, is a great "escape room" game that doesn't take by the hand at all.Remember to *look around* everywhere, and when to go in a room/zone where you haven't been yet, do not run: walk, look-around, be curious and take your time.The game would definitely benefit from some quality of life improvement like fast-travel between two locations that you already have been, but enjoing it like it is 1997 may be part of he "fun".
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, look, I'm gonna level with you - I realize you JUST finished wandering around a bunch of weird empty island worlds in Myst, and you have to go through this whole process of realizing that my two psycho sons are trapped in books, but...I'm gonna need you to wander around a bunch MORE weird empty islands. They used to be one big island, but now they're a bunch of little island, so we're calling it "Riven," get it?Also I'm going to need you to put my psycho father in a book, just like my psycho sons. It's important.Are you taking notes? You're probably going to want to keep notes. Like - a TON of notes.Oh random question: How are you with foreign number systems? There's one, maybe two that you're going to have to learn while you're here, actually. Hope you're good with that. Definitely something to keep notes about.So yeah, you know, basically the world is in your hands, aaaaaaand - I'm going to warp away now and leave you to it. Good luck!

I'm happy to say that I solved the two main puzzles without help, but I did need a couple hints for the following:I wish it was easier to backtrack, There are some fast travel methods to get between the islands, but you need to sit through a fairly long animation each time you use them (for example, the maglevs turning around and their doors closing, or the . I REALLY wish the bridge between the temple island and boiler island was still usable, because if you . That's a lot of animation to sit through!Also, I was getting some weird frame drop/stuttering. _childDocuments_.review: This was a surprise to see but I am up in bounds happy to see this game finally get a remake. It was far over due since Myst got ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 3. Although I never got around to playing the original; I always saw it here and there and loved what it did far more than Myst.Rather than just being a bare-bones power point of basic puzzles like Myst. Riven was all about the atmospheric world.This is a great remake, even if the puzzles have changed and the fmvs are changed for real-time ones. _childDocuments_.review: Riven the sequel of Myst was a graphical masterpiece for it's time and had a so much more consistent world and story than Myst. It is great that we can now revisit in 3D. I thoroughly enjoyed the revisit. While the environments are familiar major puzzles have changed so there is lots to discover, also some areas were added or changed completely. _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful remake of a classic. They tweaked almost all the puzzles, but not to make them easier or harder - just altered, so you get to experience the journey with a fresh take. Finally, I got to experience beating this through my skill alone. As a teenager it was mentally impossible, and playing off of memory would have been boring.The only downside is the character models aren't quite there, especially when FMV is the comparison. But it's serviceable, and what really matters - the environment - is jaw dropping. I am completely satisfied, and wish Cyan the best going forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This remake of Riven brings the 1997 classic into a real-time 3D environment. With enhanced visuals and an expanded story, it stays true to the original while offering new experiences. Experience Riven like never before and uncover its secrets.Riven 2024 Ultimate Walkthrough Guide: All Endings, Puzzles, and Cutscenes
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Felt really good to play this masterpiece once again after so many years! Aside from the 3D characters that felt odd in most cases (skin texture, lighting and some animations or scaling that don't look quite right), the visuals really match the original game. Not gonna lie tho, I found myself missing the old live action footage characters at times ...Lengthwise, I've beaten the game after about 16 hours leaving no stone unturned and no ending not seen however like I mentioned at the beginning, I played the game before so I knew exactly where I was going and why. I still stopped to enjoy some of the views otherwise it would have been done even faster. Don't get me wrong, I really enjoyed those hours! And the new puzzles and locations are a welcome change and make lots of sense with today's technology.If, like me, you've played Riven before then trust me: it's well worth revisiting. _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: After 27 Years, Riven returns. I went into this remembering almost nothing of it since original release. I often remembered this as being one of, if not the greatest puzzle game ever devised. However... As I replay this remake, it really shows me how much of a game it is... for its time. In 1997, they came hot off the success of MYST. Naturally, a more expansive, larger and more challenging game was set in their sights. This is a great concept... in 1997. The issue I was concerned with, even before playing the remakes, was the world design. The original Riven was a point and click adventure, where you have puzzles, and constant large new areas to explore. The great thing about a point and click is that you can move forward virtually as fast as you can click. One of the problems in an open world 3D WSAD game is the pace at which you travel. Granted you can run, but these large areas turn into a walking sim without the ability to travel quickly. This may not seem like a huge issue at first, but when you have to fetch between islands quickly for puzzles that have solutions on other islands, ♥♥♥♥ gets tedious fast. I ended up just making save points everywhere. Granted, Cyan did at least notice this to some level. They allow you the ability to skip ladder and vehicle transitions, however that's really not enough due to the distance between objectives. They also added in a world shortcut area which did not exist in the original, once again though, this doesn't save much time. Overall, the game is kind of 2 steps forward 1 step back, but you eventually reach the end. I beat this once before, but I am still working out some of the end puzzles I don't remember. There is some frustration there. The game in general feels like you are doing a lot of nothing a lot... except finding new pieces. The contrast with MYST here is that it ends up being a bunch of little things which are the key to a large puzzle that is the game. MYST is sort of contained, where the game has a bunch of small puzzles that lead to the end of the game. They are different approaches. Despite all my criticism, I have to give it a thumbs up. It is a classic inspirational game. So much so, that it served as the jumping off point for many other puzzle games. Although the world design and transport is a bit dated, it is worth exploring. The game just works better as a point and click. Riven and MYST are great. However, in the end, I will say as good as both games are; Quern: Undying Thoughts did a better MYST like game than CYAN ever accomplished.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing but improvements over the original; the only gripe I have is sometimes unreal will fail to load something like an onclick event (ladder near the town dock being the biggest problem) or inventory item (frequently prison book, infrequently moiety lens), and if you pass up the first "you first" prison book encounter and go back for the second, the window / click event is misaligned. Otherwise, fantastic job modernizing; I look forward to seeing what modders do to tighten up the character models a hair over the next couple years.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven ("The Sequel to Myst") was a true masterpiece, helping to define what a point-and-click puzzle adventure game could be and *should* be. This remake preserves the same degree of immersive environmental storytelling and gorgeously-rendered worlds, while also expanding and modifying the gameplay to keep veteran players on their toes. Truly a delightful experience. If you have never played a Myst game before, please try the original Myst game or the Myst remake (both on Steam). Myst 1 has some story and lore elements that could help your experience with Riven. Otherwise, watch some Myst 1 YouTube videos and just dive straight into Riven (which IMHO is a better game anyway).I did not get a chance to play this in VR, but I will at my first opportunity. It doesn't seem like the VR market is quite there for content vs affordability, but Cyan keeps releasing VR-compatible games which, collectively, give me some hope that VR technology could become more accessible.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent modern adaptation of the classic!  The world felt completely familiar, with many nods to the original (and at least one other work), yet different enough to be new and challenging once again, and with expanded areas of Riven not previously accessible to explore. _childDocuments_.review: What a treat to get to play Riven again! I think I bought my first computer to play that game in 1998! And, in 3D! I would rate Riven as one of the best video game stories ever written. And I've beat hundreds of games. Here's my list of best stories ever: Batman Arkam Knight, Outer Wilds, Riven, Planescape Torment,  Tides of Numenera, Myst 4, Mass Effect 2, LA Noire, Portal 2.  In this remake I really missed the live action though, but it'll keep me buying the next version in 2050 lol (fingers crossed). I liked the new puzzles a lot, and they sorted out some loose ends in the story that I had trouble with understanding. Hard to believe that the graphics in this new version are even better than the images in the original game. Time heals all video game limitations :) Thanks Rand, Robyn, and team!

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, good remake, they changed A LOT of things, new rooms, new puzzles (some good, some awful), new musics BUT you need a good gaming PC for the game.I can run the new 2021 MYST game perfectly on my couple of years old PC but not this one, it loads for around 1 min, sometimes I got to a area and watched many different “layers” load for 7+ seconds ruining the “feel” of the game, I had to refund, sorry I’ll play the 1997 version.Biggest gripe is some of the new puzzle, (the "space" linking dome) new puzzle breaks any "suspension of disbelief" of a possible real world from before strait into fantasy, and adding the new number "language puzzle" (yes a second one) is beyond ridiculous, and breaks the tone previously achieved.While other updated puzzle was nice, the throne room projector controls relocation, the fixed "under the door fiasco" and the contained new "space breach" where all very nice additions.It did not need to be so high in requirements for "top of the line graphics", leaving your older family PC out. _childDocuments_.review: I only just played a few hours, Did the old Riven somewhere in 1997, so much memories come up now, the sounds, the music, it was such a great game back then. _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A true masterpiece, as a remake and as an original game.As a huge fan of he series I loved it so much- Fans of the original will get their magnificent full 3D 4K remake, that is incredibly beautiful and smooth in regular 3D, and the VR is marvelous, and if you dreamed of being on Riven there you have it nowThe modification / additions are well balanced, with some new/modified parts and puzzle while keeping the original very well preserved. So it's enough to be surprised if you know it, and amazedRand of course, but also Robyn Miller for the music and especially Richard Vander Wende came back to capture the same magic that happened in 1997, but even better. The orignal voices are kept as well, which is great particularly for Gehn voiced by John Keston, and of course Rand as Atrus.- Newcomers will discover the best puzzle game of all time, with welcomed tweaks for the most difficult puzzles of the orginal, making them more accessible without changing their essence. To me, it's the smartest world building and puzzle game ever made, because it works as actually one meta-puzzle that you have to reconstruct piece by piece, gradually understanding the world as a whole.SLIGHT SPOILER : The only small regret I have are the 3D characters, I would have loved to have the original live actors like the most recent version of Myst but it's understandable that it just wasn't doable technically, as they move around and the footage from 1997 would probably wouldn't have worked out.TLDRIt's a wonder and a classic for any puzzle and worl building games fan, and a marvel in every aspect, new and preserved, for the fans of the original. Unmissable

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved Riven growing up, and returning to the islands felt magical. I especially loved the changes and added content that made it feel new and exciting—they simplified a few things, resolved some weird inconsistencies, and expanded on the lore. Loved it! An absolute must-buy for any fan of the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan turned my favorite of the Myst series into a breath-taking real-time adventure. Somehow, they managed to top themselves making the game I loved many years ago more beautiful than I remember. Again, the water is just stunningly spectacular. The new puzzles and changes were a lovely change. Now I have to go back and complete the series (again).
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven. The fifth age. The sequel to Myst. The original Riven is a game that I've carried with me for most of my life. I got a copy on DVD as part of the Myst Trilogy box set, and I was hooked. Everything about it was entrancing, and I kept coming back to it even after I finished it solely to admire the beautiful world. Riven, the remake, is like being able to come back to the world you remembered, but with things being ever so slightly different. Some of the puzzles in this version are slightly different, including the infamous Fire Marble puzzle. This gives the world both a sense of familiarity and a sense of newness as you learn the things that have changed, and get to appreciate the gorgeous visuals with a fully unlocked camera. And that right there is the main thing that this Riven remake does the best. If Riven 1997 let you see into a world, Riven 2024 lets you ENTER that world. When URU was once described as "D'ni In Real Time," THIS is what I had envisioned. It's Riven, rendered in real time, looking just like it did as a point-and-click game. There are a few weaknesses the game has. Namely, the people are a little...off. As a result of supporting VR and having a fully controllable camera, the live-action video has been replaced with 3D modeled people, and the result can be a little bit unsettling. Ultimately it's not a huge problem, because you can easily suspend disbelief for most of the game, but the people have a bit of an uncanny valley effect going on, and not just with their looks. The animations are just a little too jerky and robotic at times, but you ultimately can get used to it, especially since people are a relatively rare sight in this game. The only other potential weakness is the notebook system. The game has a notebook, allowing you to take screenshots and make notes about the screenshots from inside the game. This is a great feature! However, I wish there was a way to access the notebook without having to press the escape key a few times to get to the menu. It would be great if a key, say N, could take you directly to the notebook. In short, Riven is a fantastic experience that I strongly advise adventure game fans play. If you loved the original Riven, you'll still find lots to love here. If you've never played it before, then this is a fantastic way to do so.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Breathtaking. While I miss some of the minor visual odds and ends that were cut for simplification [] overall this remaster is sensational. Cyan back at their best in decades, and I'm hoping this leads to further success for them. Aside from how well it plays, how beautiful it looks, how faithfully they were able to recapture and improve on what made the original so iconic, what truly gripped me was the sensation of being so deeply immersed in that core memory from my childhood again. Being shown this by my dad when I was a child was such a formative event, it influenced what I've found interesting for my whole life following. And like the original, this was so captivating and convincing and rich and lived in and mysterious and ancient, it was like taking a bite of that Confit byaldi and being transported back to that experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Completely blown away by this version of the game.I just wanted to run the game for five minutes to see what the developers could do with one of my favorite video games before playing it in more depth.I was stuck for an hour and a half rediscovering a world I thought I knew.I'll update this review later, but I just wanted to give the game a thumbs-up to support it and say that this is perhaps the most beautifully crafted world you can explore in a video game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the original or any of the Myst games before. My puzzle game experience is purely rooted in the Talos Principle. However, this was one hell of an experience & one I much prefer. The open ended puzzle nature and total absence of direction makes for an authentic experience in much the same vain as a game like System Shock which I loved for the same reason. I did not find it too challenging to get 3 of the endings (locked out of 4th cause of the order I did some stuff). This game requires a lot of mental thought, some will naturally pick this up like I did, whilst others may not. Prepare for a lot of thinking instead of playing at certain points. Visually speaking, its beautiful & I love the world created here, it is what drew me to the game to begin with. This game worked its way into one of my favourite games of all time & I highly recommend it if you have the mental stamina for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remake! It changes way more than I expected, and all of it just adds to the experience and immersion. You can tell Rand kept a notebook of little things he always wished he could go back and improve. This is a must play, even better than the Myst remake, since it had so much more to update and yet kept the tone and style more intact.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a treat. The beautiful scenery, the atmosphere and the ambiance are so immersive and cozy.The story of Riven is exciting to uncover and the world is full of visual storytelling.Knowing that this game's puzzles are cryptic, I went in with the expectation that I'd eventually get stuck on a difficult puzzle, put the game down, and be done with it, yet somehow I pulled through and I'm so glad I did because I had a great time in Riven. It felt really rewarding to solve the puzzles on your own.It's cryptic nature is not for everyone but it worked well for me. I can highly recommend this game for the enchanting world alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is an example of what a modern remake should truly be. A modern update to the game that fixes what didn't work in the original and upgrades what did work. There are various remakes that are designed to show what the game would be if the tech we have now was what we had back then, and Riven is one of those. It takes the locations, and imagery of the original 1997 game and gives them a major glow up. It fixes some of the more tedious puzzles from the original (the fire marble puzzle from the end of the game for example). The music that is has really emphasizes the ambient atmosphere more that the original, thanks to its use of real instruments. Add VR compatibility to the mix, and you have a remake that is a brilliant love letter to the fans of the MYST franchise. This really makes me excited to see if Cyan Worlds Inc. are going to remake MYST III and IV.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: My feelings on this game are very mixed. I should probably start by saying I never played the original Riven, so I'm coming at it from a new player's perspective.On the one hand, it's a very immersive experience, with beautiful visuals, a genuinely interesting setting and a compelling story. All the puzzles feel naturally integrated into the world, and it has one of the coolest/most unique fast-travel features I've seen in a game. However, as many others have already pointed out, the way the game is structured means you will likely need backtrack a lot, which results in most of the game time being getting from point A to B. I didn't mind it too much just because the animations are engaging enough, but I can definitely see it being a turn-off for other people. My other main issue is just how short the game is. There are really only 2 main puzzles, with lots of little mini-puzzles in between, and I was really hoping for some more.If there was a bit more content this would be an easy recommendation, but as it is, it depends on how much you're willing to pay for a ~10-12 hour experience. A memorable and unique experience, no doubt, but a short one. Though I do think if you have VR it definitely adds more value to the offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I have to give Cyan Worlds the utmost praise for this remaster. I remember playing the original version that released in 97 and remember all the notes I took while playing it. Now its back fully remastered in UE5 and it looks absolutely gorgeous. I am just at a loss for words as to how almost photorealistic these environments look. Not to mention the time and care that went in to remastering the soundscapes as well. Looking back now this is how I remember imagining the original looking.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original has always been at the top of my favorites list.  This new version joins the original in that slot.  The 1st person navigation makes the game so much more immersive.  The revamped puzzles were an outstanding bonus - I thought I was just going to breeze through the paces of the old game, but it wasn't long before... wait, whats this???  LOL.  I give this game a high thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I never beat the original, and this has been updated to be a pleasure to play. I'm not sure that I could have gone back to play the original anymore, just the way that games have evolved in the last 24 years.  I'm so glad the remake is finally here after such a long journey. Big thanks to the Starry Expanse project team, to Cyan, and everyone else who made this happen. Definitely buy and play!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's amazing. But it also has many very annoying flaws that they should have improved prior to releasing it, and that I still hope they will improve.For the most part, the visuals feel both beautiful and realistic at the same time. However, I am very frustrated by the comparatively poor quality of the people. It's very sad that the very first thing you experience in this game is seeing a very cartoony looking Atrus. It feels like you are just watching some stupid kids cartoon. The movement of his mouth doesn't even match the words coming out! I don't get it, did they not play their own game before releasing it? If so, it should have been obvious that the character models are terrible and they needed to have an FMV video footage option, at least for non-VR users, as many people are not playing this game in VR. Or just make the 3D models more realistic somehow, but this is just terrible, and I doubt they could have ever gotten any 3D models to look nearly as good as FMV could have.The way you enable HDR is stupid and confusing. Figuring out how to enable HDR is not supposed to be one of the puzzles in Riven! They couldn't just include it with the other graphic settings? Anyway, once you do figure out how to turn it on, even if you have an HDR display with HDR enabled, it actually looks worse not better. What I mean is, the game looks the best if you have HDR disabled for both your monitor and in the game settings, enabling it in the game does make it look better than having HDR enabled on the monitor but not in the game settings. Anyway, with HDR fully enabled for both the monitor/system and in the game settings, when you are looking at something very bright and shiny, like the sun or the outside of the temple, yes it pops much more and looks way more amazing. But normal scenes look washed out, and the game is a lot less beautiful overall.I haven't finished the entire game yet, but so far the puzzles are nice and different enough from the original that I can enjoy playing the game. They fit well into the world, they make sense, and are fun to solve. I will update this section after completing the game.I don't really remember what was in the original game's journals, but this time around, reading them really helps you to understand what this world is about, and the characters and story around what is happening. It's not a ton of reading, and it doesn't have to read like a well written novel, you are just reading people's journals and it helps you to fill in what they are like, and what has been and is happening.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I got to play Riven for the first time -- again.This new Riven is completely faithful to the original in its world, the story it tells, and the attention to detail that made the original so memorable. And visually, it's stunning (except for the 3D character models -- those are kind of meh).Most of the changes are to the puzzles: Some were slightly tweaked while others have been completely replaced. Probably most notable is that they made the fire marble puzzle quite a bit simpler. That's fine, as far as I'm concerned, since getting every detail right in the original was more of an annoyance than a satisfying solving experience.Difficulty-wise, the end result is probably easier than the original, which should make it more approachable for new players. For me, someone who's seen everything the original has to offer several times over, getting a new set of puzzles to solve in the same awesome setting of Riven made the whole thing feel fresh, instead of just an indulgent nostalgia trip.Cyan's recent non-Myst titles have been somewhat underwhelming (particularly Firmament), but the new Riven shows they still know how to get it done.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is the greatest game I've ever played by far, and the Unreal engine takes it to a whole other level. It has everything I loved about Myst and more. The interplay between the islands is just fascinating; each one has its distinct sense of adventure but they complement each other so well. I played this game as a kid but gave up because I was too dumb and it was too hard, so coming back to it as an adult in this remastered version has been an absolute pleasure.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is a great game.This is not only from the game looking absolutely AMAZING but also how the world feels like it could be real. From the people (NOT the C.G.I ones) to the architecture and the world as a whole.Riven is also fun to just walk around and look at things, and maybe actually trying to Finnish the game every once in a while.Plus with the remaster some of the old puzzles were either moved, changed ,or in some cases I believe cut altogether. (But I could be wrong about that last bit.)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm...I would give a mixed review if I could. A lot of love went into this, and - for the most part - it brings back amazing childhood memories. However it also deviates from the original in some significant ways that are difficult to accept. I'm also very sad to see that the real life acting scenes have been replaced with subpar 3d ones. I think part of what made the original Riven so iconic and part of what really drew you into the story, was the delivery of the actors which just sadly doesn't come through with the 3d character models.Would I recommend it? Yea sure. It retains a lot of the atmosphere. But I don't think I would recommend it to someone over the original unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I had several crashes on my Valve Index, particularly around the domes, also shadows looked really strange, semi-transparent, and would appear and disappear as I moved my head. When I started playing on my desktop, for some reason the VR 'comfort' setting was still enabled, which removes transport sequences, once I found the setting I was able to view them again, but for a while thought they didn't exist in the game. _childDocuments_.review: Riven was my favorite of the Myst games when I was a child and it remains a game I place today with my iOS port. It was the first game that made me pull out a notebook and keep a physical log of notes an clues to solve the puzzles. The sound design and the rendered art was so captivating to me and it sparked my imagination like no other game before or since. This remake is perfect, a serious 9.9/10 and it recaptures everything I loved about the original. The art looks so fantastic and it looks as alive as my imagination made the original seem. In desktop and in VR this experience is like no other and the only thing that could make me happier is to somehow mod in the original live action FMV's.

_childDocuments_.review: it only took 27 years for graphics technology to be able to do Riven in real time. seriously, though, this is an excellent remake, a remake done right. every change feels like it fits, and makes the experience better. i can't wait to someday play this in VR, too, once i can afford the setup for that. if you like the original Riven, any version of Myst, Cyan's other games, or are just an adventure game fan in general, this is a must-get!

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is the sequel to Myst, picking up right where the previous game left off. If you've not played Myst yet, I recommend playing that game first. There are many different versions of Myst, and I have a review on the Steam page for the most recent version (simply titled Myst) that should help you decide which version is right for you.Unlike Myst, which has three different remakes, this is the first time that Riven has been remade. As such, playing this version - with updated graphics, free-roam movement, VR support, extra content - seems like a no-brainer. Unfortunately, the situation is far more complicated than that. Calling this a "remake" isn't the most accurate description. This game is a dramatically different take on the source material. Though the broad strokes of the original story of Riven are still there, the details have been changed, and the gameplay is almost unrecognizable.Reworking this game so thoroughly was a bold choice. I had always been a fan of the original Riven because it was one of the only puzzle games I've ever seen to create puzzles that integrated perfectly with the environment. Nothing in the world of Riven is an explicit puzzle, rather the puzzles are derived from your lack of knowledge about the cohesive, coherent world that you have invaded. There are no purpose-built test chambers or arbitrary locking systems, rather there are practical mechanisms that aren't documented because you were never supposed to be the one using them. There is a culture that you don't understand because you were never supposed to be visiting them. The game is coherent in a way that almost no other game I have ever played has been. To fundamentally rework Riven without upsetting that intricate weaving of narrative and world-building and gameplay would take some significant effort. I am a firm believer that with enough dedication to that goal someone could make another game like Riven, but it would be no easy task.What did Cyan do to maintain that cohesion in this game? Effectively, they didn't even try, and the result has left me with mixed feelings. The new Riven is far closer to Myst in structure, with a world that is physically believable, visually intriguing, but functionally ridiculous. In that regard, I suppose it resembles most puzzle games. While the puzzles may be somewhat more narratively justified here than they were in Myst, they are nowhere near as perfectly integrated as they were in the original Riven. There are puzzles for puzzles' sake. There are character behaviors that don't make logical sense. There are unconvincing environmental behaviors. All of these in the name of explicit puzzles.For me, this destroys a fundamental appeal of Riven, but what it *doesn't* do is make this game a bad experience. Riven had always been a unique case, and I have enjoyed plenty of puzzle games that had more direct approaches to their puzzles. When taken for what it is, this version of Riven is just that: a very good but fairly standard puzzle game. In my opinion, that's a step back from the incredible work of art that the original game was, but it's not a bad place to be in a vacuum. If you didn't know this was a remake, you'd probably have a good time here.That said, as someone who has played both versions of the game, I see this release somewhat differently.  I have watched many people play through the original game, and often those who stopped before reaching the end did so because they found it too difficult. This is a common sentiment. Riven is generally considered to be an incredibly difficult game. That difficulty largely arises from the indirect nature of its puzzles. Seasoned gamers will come into Riven looking for more traditional puzzles and won't find them. Piecing together the components of the world that will help you do what you're trying to do is exponentially more difficult if you're thinking of that original Riven as a game and not as a world.  game doesn't require that mental shift. This game presents the player with a far more guided path through far more explicit puzzles. As such, I see it as a welcome alternative for those who enjoyed Myst but couldn't make it through Riven on account of the difficulty. You'll get the broad story arc and be set up to play the later games, but the experience will be far more Myst-like.For returning players, the recommendation is more difficult. Part of me is disappointed in this game. It is a clear downgrade from the original product, and the fact it bears the Riven name and is sold as a remake will undoubtedly cause many people to play this version instead without knowing any better. Given the number of Myst remakes that have happened over the years, perhaps the work put into this product will result in a more faithful remake of Riven at some point in the future, though I wouldn't hold my breath for it. I would love to see such a product. It deserves to exist.Still, another part of me is happy that I have something to point to for those who struggled with that original game. If this is the gateway that gets more people to play Myst III, perhaps it was worth it after all. And of course, I did have a good time with it. If these puzzles comprised Myst VI, I wouldn't be feeling as confused as I do right now. I would be singing the praises of another solid puzzle game in the Myst universe that lives up to the original Myst's standards. The only reason this elicits negative feelings is the fact that it doesn't live up to Riven, the title it bears.If I could rate "mixed" here on Steam, I would. Since I can't, I think "not recommended" is the better option. If I'm recommending against this game for first-time players, I think that's the recommendation that ought to take precedent in my selection.

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop: Definitely the way to go. You can take notes (and you should). The landscape is gorgeous. It was wonderfully nostalgic, and it overall felt very faithful to the original. A few of the puzzles were simplified from the original, but I don't think the game is worse off for it. The character models look a little simple and out of place in contrast with the extra detailed environments... but you don't interact with people often, so I didn't mind that too much. Overall, wonderful experience.VR Experience: A beautiful game to explore, but the puzzles are not friendly with my Steam Index considering how many notes you need to take. I had some areas that crashed frequently (moving through the marbles occasionally made me crash, and the submarine always made me crash). There were some very difficult to activate levers throughout the game that were made worse by the VR experience. The screenshot "notes" are extremely cumbersome to reference, so it's probably best just to lift up the headset and take notes manually. Except if you walk through a wall, the game crashes. I really struggled to read the cursive through my headset.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is what my 12 year old brain thought Riven looked like when it released all those years ago. Camera controls are fantastic. Visuals and sound design are super immersive, as I hoped it would be!Running the game on a fairly powerful computer, I experienced no bugs other than a few difficulties using an XBOX controller for certain puzzles, in which case I just switched to a mouse for finer control. Framerate never dropped to where I noticed it, and while there were a few texture pop ins on the tram rides, they were so quick that I barely noticed.Absolutely loved the reimagining of certain crucial puzzles, and was very happy that someone who has replayed the original many times could still struggle a bit, be surprised, and have that same awesome feeling when a puzzle was solved.To the devs: Thank you for listing the Starry Expanse team in the credits, as well as the original team. And thanks for making this an amazing experience I'll definitely share with others.PS: Did you really have to

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a sold remake of the '97 RIVEN classic game. The additions and changes made sense, and the world is beautifully rendered. The ability to freely roam around the word took me back to my childhood days of staying up late and trying to solve the most difficulty of puzzles. Like last time, I did resort to a few hints and nudges, though I mostly managed to make it through on my own. The character animations while decent enough, are the one element that feels a bit less polished than the rest, but they don't detract from the experience (also, note: character animation is HARD).  There was also one 'age' I would like to have been able to roam around a little more and there's one memorable image from an old Cyan calendar that still didn't make the game, but those are minor gripes from an old fan. To the casual gamer, you won't notice these things.TLDR: If this is your first time journeying into Riven, pick this up and enjoy it. Your're in for a treat! Note, played in flatscreen but also tested in VR.  VR seemed solid with the only gripe being that shadows have to be set to the lowest setting. It's not my computer either, I have an RTX 3090. That said, the game plays well in either mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I've never been so happy to be totally stuck in a game I've "already finished".As excited as I was to revisit Riven, I was concerned I would just blaze through the remake.  Cyan have made some really interesting changes to make the experience fresh for those of us returning to Riven.  I am loving exploring the environment in beautiful 3D and the sound design and music is just the best.  No-one else builds worlds as immersive as Cyan games do.Riven is my favourite adventure game by a wide margin and I've long desired the feeling of playing it for the first time again.  This iteration of the game has done that for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely masterful and well overdue remake of one of the greatest adventure games from the 90's.  The visuals are beautiful, the puzzles, though redone, will still require a lot of thought and attention to detail, and they've managed to make a game that both feels nostalgic and fresh.  I'd even argue this turned out better than the Myst remakes.  I cannot recommend this more highly.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere is impeccable. The puzzles are (mostly) enjoyable. The music is beautiful.The travel cutscenes are lovely and the animations are fantastic. But after the 30th time travelling back and forth on a mine cart, or a jet-rail train, or waiting for spinning orbs to come to a stop, open, close, load and open... it grows tedious, time-consuming and eventually straight-up frustrating.Forgot one small clue on another island? There goes 10 minutes of nothing but travel and backtracking.I appreciate the artists desire to show off all their amazing animation work. But at some point you have to understand that we've seen it, and we'd like to skip it. Same with the credits.I can't in good conscience recommend this game when so much of it is padded with forced travel tedium.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Be aware, this is not a straight remake of the original. It's mostly the same, but if you played the original then early on you will notice some things have changed. Mostly for the better, there's some amazing additions. The 3d character models aren't as expressive as the FMV of the original and some of those moments are absent in this version, but that's just the nature of the new format. On the whole, I'd say it's worth experiencing at the asking price. I tried it out the VR mode on a Rift S, it was decent. It's clearly a non-VR game adapted to VR, so it's a little awkward, but not unplayable. I had a bit of texture twitching here and there, nothing too bad. I'd say if you can, it's worth trying just to stand in these incredible environments.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As a first time player of Riven, it was strangely also the only game in the Myst series I had not played yet. With this remake, it felt like the right time. I have not played it in VR, only on PC.In relation to the other Myst games, Riven is a treasure trove of good puzzles and a great story. The remake makes the world more easily accessible and feels immersive. There were a couple bugs, most graphical related, but after fixing those the game ran smoothly from beginning to end.If you like the Myst series, this is definitely a recommendation! If you are new to the Myst series, or have not played point-and-click puzzle games before, this is a very good one to start with.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's great that everyone else seems to be enjoying the game, but I was looking forward to replaying a game I had trouble with in my childhood so  I could solve it now that I am better at such things.Seeing all the radical changes they made for the sake of making the game easier really made me not want to play it. Familiar places are now entirely different. The creators really don't seem to understand their own source material and what made it great. Instead of updating a classic they made a new game. I don't understand why they did this, Myst was remade much better than this.Not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is a gorgeous remake of a beloved classic - and I say beloved, even though I had no concept that the game even existed before I played Myst (2021) last week, and grew immediately hungry for more. I can say definitively, without the rosy glasses of nostalgia, that this game was a fantastic experience and stands up to today's exploration-puzzler titans entirely on its own merits. Riven picks up right where Myst left off, though newcomers joining the series here would not feel like they had missed much by not playing the first entry. While Myst is a great game that I also recommend playing, Riven's greater focus on characters and story means that it's much easier to get invested in the stakes of the game right away.Riven is not a direct one-to-one remaster of the original title; instead, some mindful additions have been made, and the flow of the game has been altered slightly to enhance the experience and ensure that even veterans of the title have a few surprises waiting for them along their journey. Myst (2021) launched with a Photo Album, allowing you to take pictures of the game world for later reference, in case it was needed. Riven enhances this feature, calling it Notebook, by allowing you to type notes alongside any images you capture. In my playthrough, I used this feature not just for picture references, but as a journal to record my experience. Anything that interested me, I took pictures of and scribbled down a few lines. By the end of the game, I had a robust journal that documented my entire journey, and I took some great joy in reliving it, even just hours later, as new revelations recontextualized things I had seen earlier.I highly recommend Riven to anyone who likes exploration puzzlers, but especially to those who might be interested in the lore and history of the world it presents - a world where writers, using an ancient formula of written language, create books that transport the user to distant and fantastical Ages, and how the civilization that produced these writers spread their imperfections into the worlds that they would come to inhabit.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I lack the words to adequately express my abiding love for Cyan Games reviving this beloved entry in the MYST series. I recently left a crestfallen review of Firmament, expressing my disappointment that both as a narrative and a puzzle game, it fell short of even boring for me. I specifically completed every one of it's achievements to exhaust its potential, hoping I had simply missed something. I concluded after doing so that I had not. That Firmament was simply an unrefined vision whose realization failed to meet with its own self-imposed expectations. I expressed my heartbreak at how far the publisher had seemed to have fallen in making masterpieces and how desperately I hoped it wasn't true.Riven as a game did more than just restore my faith in Cyan to publish high quality games that reach into the beauty of aesthetic. It nailed the elements that made Riven special as a game in its time. The photo realistic design language presents a unique fusion of a quasi-historical-true-to-industrial-steam-and-aether-punk fantasy setting. Every element is like walking into a living history museum of a truly fantastic universe where the magic of leather-bound journals, stoppered vials, and alien astrolabes comes alive everywhere you look.And if all of that sounds too esoteric for you, I would humbly ask that you package that feeling and stow it somewhere to be forgotten. Because of all the things which Cyan does best, it is giving the player the opportunity to truly and personally learn to appreciate the world you find yourself dumped into with each successive game. Relish the beauty of the mystery, indulge in the wonder and prospect of unraveling the hidden things and appreciating the sublime connections between.Now before you buy this game, I would make a recommendation. Go out and buy yourself a beautifully embossed or decorated leather-bound journal to take notes in. And use that book to muddle through every puzzle you work through as you play this and every MYST series game you play. Participate in the game with your own journal entries as you untangle the myriad of puzzle elements. From counting systems to mechanical troubleshooting and rudimentary mapping, truly let yourself sink into the sloppy yet elegant messy work of taking your own notes, wrestling with ideas, and jotting your own theories and suppositions to amend with later entries. Do the things which characters throughout this game do and you will come to a deeper appreciation of the characters and your combined investment in their well-being. I whole-heatedly believe you will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Better than the original classic in nearly every way. The detailed visuals, the haunting sound track and the layered world-building all come together so well. If you've never played the original and you like puzzle or exploration games at all, you should really experience this masterpiece. If you have played the original, there are enough surprises to make it feel nearly like a new game. The only minor gripe is with the animated characters replacing the captured performances - but it is minor. This remains one of my top 10 games of all time and this remake only cements that standing.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I am mildly recommending this.I played the original version roughly 25 years ago. There's changes, and QOL improvements. I don't remember the puzzles being this frustrating. They've changed through.But the thing I was looking forward to the most was the VR experience, like with the Myst remake. Riven and VR seemed like a match made in heaven. Once again, the VR experience seems to be an afterthought.I play this with my Quest 2, over air link, through to Steam where I bought the game. It plays well enough, but it very consistently crashes every single time the little sub/tank thing in the village arrives at a destination. So I have to keep switching to "regular" mode just to navigate through there. I cannot count how many times I've seen the startup screen for this game.Like Myst VR, there is a "note taking" feature, which consists of simply taking screenshots which go into a gallery "notebook". At least it didn't take 1.5 years for them to implement it this time.... Not that it does a lot of good, because so much of the puzzles just can't be screenshot. Sure, it helps, but you will inevitably be resorting to pen and paper. An example - the little hangman game that give you a glyph count... can't capture that information. It'll just see what's presented on the gadget without the animation that you had to count in your head.You practically need a spreadsheet to help cross-reference the 800 million different kinds of symbols/glyphs/lettering/colors/quantum spins/etc. So if you're looking for a good VR experience... it's mostly fine, but just be ready for pain. I do not grasp why they thought the screenshot approach was going to suffice for people wearing headsets.Oh right - that "notebook" is excruciatingly slow and clunky to get into, navigate, enlarge, go back, resume game... every single time you need to look at something - one thing - at a time. On a few occasions, I accidentally quit the game instead of resuming, as I have to carefully aim my laser pointer hand at the "Resume" button in the menu.I'm sure in 15-37 months, this will be polished and worked out.I'm largely ranting out of frustration, as I really wanted to enjoy this, but find myself ripping off the headset in frustration more often than not.

I myself do not trust the words of most men, so I don't expect you to believe me. In the end, though, you may discover that  have more than  to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Returning to one of my favorite worlds in VG history in this stunning remake using Unreal Engine 5.Riven pushes you to open your mind and think creatively about your surroundings. It's not just about figuring out , but also  — like an explorer and engineer.The puzzles are organic in that way. They integrate seamlessly into the universe, which feels like a real, dynamic world with a deep backstory. It doesn't hold your hand or set you on a linear path so remember to use the in-game notebook/screencaps frequently because you have to deduce the story and solutions on your own. It's never tedious however as the resulting escapism is unparalleled, you genuinely feel like you've transported into a new world.27 years after its release, it's safe to say that no puzzle game has matched Riven's depth and quality. This remake is a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A really awesome remake of a beautiful classic game. While the 3d character replacements are no match for full motion video... its understandable why they had to do it, and not 'so terrible' it ruined the game. Loved the changes to some puzzles, and the re-imagining of some spaces.I am not disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Never played Riven until now. I was afraid it was going to be similar to the Witness or the original Myst, but found it much closer to Outer Wilds in a lot of ways. While not as good as that game, what Riven does do well - it does really well. Riven is a slow burn puzzler where the puzzles have meaning within the world and story. You will certainly get stuck as you explore this familiar, exotic place, but there's a value to that. Slowing down to take in the sights and sounds gives you time to chew on the puzzles as you figure out what this strange pocket dimension is all about. Having played through Myst first , what caught my attention with Riven was how much more reserved and focused it was than its predecessor. Reducing the scope to  just one "Age", rather than the original's 4-5, really gives the story the space it needs to thoroughly explore its setting and characters. As a remake, I also believe that this is the definitive way to play this game. While having only played the original briefly (I bought the original/remake bundle), it feels a lot like Riven(2024) is just a second draft of an already airtight script. There's one primary narrative/puzzle change that I was honestly shocked to discover wasn't even a part of the original game. I think so much of this works because so many of the original designers returned to head this project. That kind of authenticity can be felt, especially when paired with new talent. I'm looking at you person who came up with the idea for weird water-rift things.Really good time here.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It is actually insane how good this remake is. The new additions and lore expansion are not only welcome changes, but tied so well into the world itself that my jaw was on the floor multiple times through my playthrough. Amazing work Cyan and Starry Expanse teams, you've done something TRULY amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I tried the original a few years ago for maybe about 10 minutes, but couldn't really get used to the slideshow-style navigation, so I decided to hold out for the inevitable remake. I can finally see why the game is considered to be such a classic; it has the same mysterious feel and practical puzzle design sensibilities as Myst, but it took the integration with the environment and lore and pushed it to the next level. It's such an old game, but I haven't seen another that does cryptic environmental storytelling this well.There were a few puzzles that felt a bit cheap (find the inconspicuous collection of pixels to click on), but in the grand scheme of things those few moments felt pretty forgivable - or even refreshing, in a weird way. I've played a lot of games lately where I can feel the designer's hand guiding me almost every step of the way, where every little potential frustration or inconvenience has been sanded off. The result is often something hollow and inoffensive where I'm just guessing the designer's intentions, being right most of the time, and going through the motions instead of playing the game in an organic way. Riven was a breath of fresh air in that regard. I never once thought about what the game wanted in a meta sense, I was just immersed in an interesting world that had left me to my own devices.As I understand it, they've redesigned a lot of the original game's puzzles, so I'm curious what the differences are. I'd guess that some fans with heavy nostalgia for the original might be upset with some of the changes. They could be right, maybe the original game's puzzle design was more interesting; I wouldn't know. But as someone who came in with no prior opinion, I thought it was a fantastic game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is peak Cyan, always delivering impressive attention to detail, respecting the original Riven, but also improving where the gaming experience requieres so.The only thing I'd change is I would have tried to keep the original actors instead of the new 3D models. I feel like one of the most powerful elements of the MYST saga is that real characters make the Environment feel real. No matter how detailed, a real time 3D model won't make it.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan is a religion and Riven is our temple. I think everyone should play both versions. I loved them both and there will never be another Riven, I admit I expected it to be a visual upgrade only and that I may have tinkled a little with the changes. There's also a few things I missed from the original: the sentry and baby girl in the village, trolling for unnecessary toxic frogs, changing like 630 CD's, constructing an entire notebook of charts and grafts and drawing maps and grids and pictures of symbols that all ended up looking like a meatloaf... but I knew what they meant. It was my adventure and my collection of meatloaves, and I solved both versions without any other hints or outside help. I'm still proud of that. Atrus is still shockingly ungrateful and Catherine is still out there in some self-absorbed head space and in the new version they both look like hideously drawn cartoons living in a hyper realistic island paradise, but I don't give a damn. Riven is my home...and Dorothy, there's no place like home.

_childDocuments_.review: Without hesitation I'd say this is a great remaster. Better than the recent Myst remaster in terms of graphics, and the sense of atmosphere the game commands. Its huge, deep, and both nostalgic and fresh at the same time. Some elements have added or tweaked, but only with the result of making progress. The 3d characters are passable, not perfect, but good enough to keep the story working. They are the only thing that doesn't feel AAA about this game.Specs are modest and my 7 year old GTX 1080ti runs it perfectly.Myst series fan? Get this game!

_childDocuments_.review: ( Non-VR Review )tl;dr: If you've played Riven 1997 before, this one is different than what you remember, but it is my opinion that all the changes are enhancements, and you will enjoy your new trip through Riven with some new mysteries and questions to answer. If you haven't played the 1997 one before, then you should know that this is one of the finest worlds ever created, stuffed full of environmental storytelling, puzzles, art, mechanisms, and mechanics. If you're into that sort of thing, try it!---I'm a big, big, big fan of the Myst series. I played Myst pretty young, 6 or 7 or so, initially with my dad helping me click around, but he got frustrated with it and left it to me. It took me a really, really long time, but I figured it all out and beat the game... by trial and error if anything, honestly. My house didn't have Internet back then, so it's not like I could look up answers. I had my notebook and the game and time and that's about it.Not long after, Riven released in 1997 and I begged my parents for a copy and received about a year later. This game took me a really long time, too, but not as long as it should have if I hadn't improved from my time with Myst at all - eventually, I learned how the world of Myst connected and why, and the world-consistent puzzles helped a lot. I could never go back to other adventure games that have disjointed, out-of-place, or nonsensical puzzle elements - the puzzles in these games are much more connected to the world. There is some justification for their existence. Myst was a bit looser with this, but Riven is strict. This sense helped me with Riven (1997) a lot, but the original release was nonetheless quite difficult. My struggle understanding and exploring the world, I feel, set me up to be good at creative problem solving for the rest of my life - I don't think I'd have the things I have now or enjoy the things I now enjoy if not for the lessons and patience I learned from those 5 noisy CD-ROMs in a cardboard box.This 2024 remake of Riven made me nervous when I was going into it, before I had seen it. I knew that it was partially the fruits of the labor of the Starry Expanse project, which began remaking (and re-remaking, and re-re-remaking, as I recall) Riven in full 3D quite some time ago and formed the basis for this project which the original Riven (1997) developers Cyan then continued and completed. I was worried that I would find that the world didn't land the same way as it did before, or that the world would have been changed, or that somehow the nature of full 3D exploration would somehow diminish the value I used to receive from every still frame of image from the original. Not so.At first, I was just thoroughly pleased to walk around and see the game from new perspectives. It's quite pretty. I wasn't disappointed. Then, I realized a bit too late that it seemed like I was somewhere that I ought not to have been so early in the game, and I realized something has been changed... several things, in fact. When I discovered the nature of one of the larger changes concerning the multitude of domes scattered around the islands, I was uncertain how to really feel until I realized that I felt the same brand of wonder that I remember feeling from the 1997 release, way back when. And just like that, I was sold.Every change that's been made, I feel, has strictly been an enhancement. There's not a moment where I thought "Darn, I miss how it used to be." There were times I was surprised something wasn't where it was supposed to be, or surprised something didn't exist at all - but after a few moments of thought, I almost universally returned to "You know... that might be for the better." Some weird lore loose ends from the original now have justification. Some weird idiosyncratic elements of the original are now either replaced or contextualized enough that they blend in. I think it's all good. That's just personal opinion, though.I'm exceptionally pleased by this remake.A tiny spark of hope is now lit within me for a full 3D remake of this caliber of Myst III: Exile, someday. Am I being greedy?Performance/Stability: Good. Played on Linux via Proton, zero issues. My rig is quite capable and was able to play on high settings with no trouble, hitches, stutters, or slowdowns.Music and Audio: Excellent. Played with headphones. Robyn Miller's music is beautiful, haunting, and evocative. The sounds of the mechanisms and machines are all so satisfying.Visuals: Great! I was worried they would be inferior to the pre-rendered stills of the original, but technology has advanced so far...Story: Fantastic. I've played every Myst game and read every Myst book. I'm not objective.
