_childDocuments_.review: This is fantastic. Riven is one of my favorite games of all time, and this remake does not disappoint. The additional puzzles and changes to the original puzzles keep it fresh even if you already know the core goals or mechanics. I often find myself delighted by what *isn't* there from the original, because it means there's something new to solve. It's awesome actually feeling the islands and landscapes connect. That first maglev ride is ::chefs-kiss::.Pros: No switching CDs every time you change islandsCons: You still have to wait for maglev door to close every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the original game you may be thinking this is the same game just enhanced. You would be wrong. It is like the original and it is enhanced but a lot of puzzles have been changed up. To me it is an almost  completely new game with some difficult puzzles to solve. So far I have enjoyed it immensely. I am getting the same satisfaction as I did back in 1998 when it first came out. If your a fan of Myst, get it. You'll love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know more I can add to the conversation, other than I freaking love the Riven remake. The graphics, environments, sound, lighting, music.. All 10 out of 10. The original 1997 game is one of my favorite all time games ever since it first released. It's my favorite of the Myst series and my favorite out of all Cyan's games. One of the best surprises about this remake, for me, is how they reworked some of the puzzles. It made this game feel both old & familiar and new & refreshing. I've played a ton of remasters/remakes over the years but never anything quite like this. It feels and sounds exactly like I remember the original game. The new puzzles add a newness to the experience that made playing it more interesting that I anticipated.Riven is a game rich in ambiance and environmental story telling that draws you in. It's the kind of game I like to play with the lights down and a good headset or sound system. The puzzles never feel arbitrary. From start to finish it is a very rich and rewarding experience.If you're a fan of Myst you owe it to yourself to play this. If you love first-person adventure/puzzle games, I heartily recommend it. Riven was a masterpiece when it came out, and this remake is equally masterful. Thank you, Cyan! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's easy to see where all the love for this series comes from now.I played the original Riven and then this more or less back to back and can say this game is a treat for new and returning players. The game's structure is the same, but small changes in puzzles and the islands' layouts making navigation much better.The immersion and world building on display are really top notch and this remake has successfully smoothed over any rough edges the original had.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original Riven a few years ago for the first time and it quickly became my favorite puzzle game, and I can pretty confidently say that this is an incredibly faithful remake of it that not only does justice to the original, but goes as far as to add additional content that makes the game even better. They put a lot of time and effort into reworking a few of the puzzles (one of which is honestly mind-blowing when you figure it out), and also expanded some of the areas in the original you only get to briefly visit. They also added little bits of detail all over the game that accentuate the overarching narrative. Aesthetically, it's an absolutely gorgeous game, and they did an incredible job of bringing the world of Riven to 3D. I still don't love the way the people look (something about the old FMV stuff is just super charming to me), but they're definitely a big step up from the previous Myst remake.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Long time lover of Myst and Riven. This remake is amazing. I know the answer to every puzzle from the original, so the changes of this remake were enough to bring back the wonder and adventure again. Every time Cyan Worlds release a game, I feel something that I don't get with other games. The world building is fantastic.Don't worry about the 3D characters. Once you're in the game, they're actually absolutely fine.Lots of love to all at Cyan Worlds. I wish them continued success.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I've been wishing for a Riven remake for 15 years at least, and now its here. It is a faithful recreation of the classic I played so much as a child. They changed the puzzles around just enough so that an experienced player can't just smash through it right away. You need to think about things to progress. The environments are beautiful and immersive, the sound is incredible even though many of the dialogue recordings were made in the 90s, and the sense of familiarity with the world feels comforting. I'm glad to be back. I give the remake a 9.5/10, with 1/2 a point lost because they didn't re-create the moment on your first mag-lev journey where the car gets air and leaves the tracks for a moment. As a child, i could always feel that little jump in my stomach, and was a little bit disappointed that it wasn't reproduced.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the original game of Cyan. I could see that most of the other fans were quite excited by this remake and were saying very good things about it even before the release. Were they just hyped? I was quite worried and a little reluctant at the idea of Riven, a real gem, being remade in a 3d engine. As an example, I'm also a fan of Final Fantasy 7-9 on the PS1, and when I see the result of Final Fantasy VII Remake, even though it has many qualities, I started to think that it might not be such a good idea to remake those good old prerendered games from the 1990s. So I jumped into Riven Remake with apprehension. I have motion sickness, so I cannot play a lot without feeling nauseous, but it's ok in Riven. My computer is old (2013) so in addition I cannot set the graphic settings at a elevated level. In fact, I couldn't even launch the game initially, black screen, because my GPU wasn't happy with a DX12 feature. In the end I could start playing it with the -dx11 option and it plays nice. First steps in Riven... As I feared, I'm not very fond of the 3d characters, but I anticipated it, so that's fine. And they're not so bad, could have been worst. I prefer Atrus in the original intro, but he's quite convincing in 3d too. Then I'm teleported to Riven in the jail at the beginning, and after the short scene, I can make my first steps. Wow the graphics are somptuous! Even with low quality settings, it's amazing. The feeling of freedom in exploring the islands is just beathetaking when you knew the first game. There are small animations here and there, trees, sea waves, insects... The world is familiar yet different, I'm visiting it for real! I quickly get used to the changes and take my old habits, and I know what to do and where to go. Ah, I quickly notice that various things have changed. At first I'm not very happy with these changes. The armchair room is not where it used to be and so I can't climb in the maglev as quickly as I wanted to. Mmmh, a little disappointed. But then I start to play with the rotating room and I find what I know, more or less. Except that the full 3d makes it much easier to understand what we are doing, and this is a very good point! So I rotate the rooms, open several doors, go here and there and finall fnd the armchair that I was looking for, at last. Not bad. I open the door to the maglev and go back on my steps, taking notes and screen captures on my way. I take the maglev, there is still the "wow" effect inside. I visit the 2nd island, enjoy the sea creatures. I go look for one of the Riven balls that, I know, is located near them on a rock. But it's not there anymore, things have changed. That makes me a little grumpy because I liked to search for those wooden balls in the past, enjoying the sound effect associated with each of them. Maybe they're still somewhere else, but instead I have found a strange magnifying glass with invisible paiting. Reminds a bit of The Room. I don't like a lot the idea of having to wear that glass to not miss hidden clues, but well, why not. I continue, visit the forest, take more screen captures and notes on my paper. Then go back on my steps and climb in the small wagon. I reach the 3rd island and the ride was cool like before. I find my marks quickly on this island, it hasn't changed a very lot at the beginning. Quickly I reach Ghen's lab and there are many changes inside that I like and find logical. More and more, all of the changes make sense to me, and I start to really like it. I'm curious about the stone orbs.I continue, open the doors, take captures, etc. Finally I arrive on the 4th island and visit it. I love the environment of this island, it's so unique, almost like a fantasy world with all those rocks. I play with the device and quickly find the code to the hidden level with the lift. I reach the cave where we can see the Wharck, a very rivenesque sea creature, that I wouldn't like to meet for real. The place is beautiful with that gigantic blue circle. I take some more notes and leave, back to a previous island, and now I can use the submarine, which lead me to having fully access to the small village. I'm visiting, I'm now fully immersed in the game and I love it, I can't stop despite the motion sickness. I'm at 3 hours of games and I have made a lot of progress, but at the same time there is still so much to do! I left plenty of devices and clues on my way that I will have to check again, and understand how they work. Riven Remake worried me, now I am reassured and I can say that it is a masterpiece. I'm glad I jumped into the adventure despite my firt idea of a remake, despite having an old pc, and despite loving the old version. I'm not one of those fans who thought it would be great even before I started playing it. I had to really dive into it to enjoy this creation. And I can tell that it's incredible. Of course it might still be too difficult for many young players, particularly novices who never played an adventure game, or for less patient players. The game is sometimes slow and takes it time. Some will not like it, personally I find it relaxing. There are no enemies, you can't die, there's no TPS view, no battles. It's pure exploration, joy for the eyes and the ears, joy also when you solve a challenging thing and get that "ahah!" moment, and you can continue your exploration when you were stuck. It's a very very beautiful world, very similar to the original version but better with the UE engine, and yet different enough from the old game to justify buying it again. Am I in love with this remake? Maybe not totally yet, I still haven't finished it and I know that I still have a long way. But from what I saw it's a new masterpiece and I hope that the flame of Riven will continue to burn for many many years in the hearts of many people! At least, Cyan did something really cool here, that must be awesome to play it in VR. I recommend this game, definitely!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Great nostalgia for those of us who remember playing it in 1998.This is a fun puzzle game with world building. High quality in PC/Mac and a little lower quality in VR but fun. However, some of the puzzles can be quite hard and you're going to likely need playthrough help sometimes. What makes this a little difficult is that some of the puzzles are randomized per game so you'll need to do some of your own sleuthing to solve, even with a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The remake of this classic has taken my breath away. The detail of the original, six disc CD-ROM game from 1997, and all its nostalgia is here. But even more than that, now its in Ultra HD, where i can let my eyes take in every corner of the world, as if I were standing right in the middle of it.  The entire time of my play through felt as though I was walking through a dream of time long ago, when I was in high school trying to be the first one in my friends group to beat the game. However around every corner, everything in the world felt different, a good different, Game developers take note, This team knows how to do a proper remake. This is truly a masterpiece for the ages and Cyan has accomplished it twice in my lifetime!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with the original Myst, but never got around to playing any of its sequels. I'm constantly surprised at how good Cyan is at creating environments that feel truly alien. I JUST WISH THE GRAPHICS WEREN'T KNEECAPPED BY UNREAL ENGINE'S STUPID POST-PROCESSING BULLS#!T. Seriously, why the hell can't I turn off anti-aliasing? It looks horrible seeing ghosting EVERYWHERE and there's nothing I can do about it. It feels like my glasses are smudged. Anyway, I highly recommend keeping a journal of some kind while playing, the high I got when I figured out certain puzzle solutions is genuinely unmatched.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a few glitches that some optimizations could fix, small lag spikes when going from one preloaded area to the next sort of stuff (still way better than changing between 5 CDs lol). Overall, the game is fantastic. I grew up playing the Myst games. This was like a trip home in a way considering all the hours i spent in it as a kid. I will say that this version is easier than the 1997 one. I am not just saying that because I am not 8 anymore, but the I feel that some of the harder puzzles are dumbed down a bit. The spinning eye half globes for one are significantly easier, the large golden dome puzzle is significantly easier, They took out the sound puzzle all together which in a way is nice because that one really was a bear if I remember correctly.A couple of things that they missed out on is first your notebook. It would have been really cool if the pictures you took and the information you wrote down ended up in a book in your bag that you could draw out; instead of hitting the escape key and opening it like some kind of setting. I also miss the live acting. I understand that 27 years is a long time and no one looks the same anymore, but the live acting had a charm to it that the CGI people sorely lack. Ehhh, rose colored glasses I suppose.Thank you Cyan for this remaster!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves the Myst series, I loved this remake/remaster. It is so invigorating to be able to freely walk everywhere in these Myst games and even more so in Riven. The ability to walk and see everything instead of "still" images is so much more immersive even if just to look behind rocks. They changed a bit of things with still keeping the original feel of everything making the story and puzzles more in depth. It also makes revisiting Riven even more fun as its like playing for the first time in some cases. The only downside I've ever had with these remakes is the lack of FMVs but it comes with updating everything else so I'll take what we can get. Definitely pick it up if you were ever curious of playing the first two of the Myst series.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid, Riven was the most incredible looking thing I had ever seen. I was a child, and I was too dumb to figure out what to do. Now, as an adult, nothing has changed.Okay, maybe I can solve the puzzles now, but sincerely, this game is a masterpiece. You will be transported, literally and figuratively. If you're even remotely interested in this game, then it is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I finished it after 29 frustrating but satisfying hours I will say this game was absolutely great.  The VR (bigscreen beyond ) was superb but there were a few bugs to deal with for now.  The graphics are very nice (UE5 i believe). The game itself is very challenging but I'm happy I resisted any temptation to look up solutions.  My frustrations were well worth it upon completing the game. Highly recommend. Great VR experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original 1997 release of Riven was one of my favourite games of all time, so I was very excited to hear about and play this remake. Having finished the game just a few minutes ago, I have almost nothing but praise. It was like playing it for the first time all over again, because this isn't a 1:1 translation from the original. Most of the puzzles (and even a few minor elements of the lore) have been almost completely rebuilt and remastered, and the care and attention that has gone into this work is on full display. Even if you're someone like me who has played the original enough times to have it memorised start to finish, while you won't be knocked quite back to square one, you'll have hours of fun figuring out how everything works again. As I've said to a few friends when discussing the game, it's like learning new lyrics to a familiar tune, and I enjoyed every minute of it.To be balanced, the game does have a few flaws, as not everything perfectly translates from the original 2D point-and-click game to the modern 3D-rendered, VR-experience I played through. Some of the VR controls are a little clunky at times, and I think I still prefer the original live-action actors to their 3D counterparts. But on the whole, this new version of Riven retains the soul of the original, with outstanding puzzles and an immersive world. Whether you're an old veteran or a first time visitor, I couldn't recommend this game highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Nostalgia city! And what a beautiful remake. Love that the puzzles are a little updated but still keep the lore in tact. Too many moments have I yelled in excitement about the interesting new changes, and the places I wish I could have explored when I was young. Cyan Worlds, always incredible work :)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: My first comment was very negative. As others, I also had difficulty with input sensitivity and in some cases the game becoming stuck. I found that quitting and re-entering helped in later cases so not needing me to go back to a previous (too long ago) save. Frustrations aside, I've enjoyed the story. I'm now wondering at other possible ends.Quite a change from the Room Series I played before this. Those games are very linear. This is more a detective story - explore, pick up clues, piece it all together. I have to admit to having found guidance in a couple of places. Would I have worked it out without? I can see the mental path needed but it would have taken a lot of time (perhaps not helped by not knowing whether I'd failed to solve something or whether I was suffering an input problem in the game). There is a fair amount of walking around (running helps) if you do need to go back to collect any more information so it's good to note everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: +++ Gorgeous visuals.+++ Several redesigned puzzles, objects, and gameplay elements.+++ Built-in randomizers on some puzzles.--- Character models of abysmal, immersion-breaking quality.--- Some pixel-hunting at times.--- Technologically demanding.While the character models are awful by modern standards, they still show a marked improvement over the much worse Myst models. The Riven remaster contains a goodly handful of little twists that will make sure players of the original can't exactly rely on their rote memory to solve this game, helping to keep the experience fresh. At the same time, several redesigns help to make some of the most legendarily obscure and fiendish puzzle a little more palatable, especially to newcomers. It helps to drive in the impression of a new and improved experience rather than a simple rehash, and the bet proves to be successful with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible game, and it's such a good example of a well executed remake. I never finished the original but I loved the time I spent staring at its gorgeous late '90s CGI and its absolutely brutal puzzles. I didn't expect a remake to come out so soon and I'm happy to say it's a slam dunk; not only does it capture the magic of the original game but it makes its own changes while being respectful. I cannot get over just how good this game looks, seriously.As if that wasn't enough, being able to experience the entire game in VR is the cherry on top. I was only able to play it like this for an hour but if you are a fan of the original, I cannot recommend it enough, it's easily the nicest looking VR game I've ever played (on the PC version at least).Puzzles are still brutal here, though if you've beaten the original then you definitely have a great head start, but things have been changed around considerably, and it's probably a bit easier than the original. A notepad and a pen is still a must. The game does have a feature that lets you take screenshots of what you're looking at and refer to them from the pause menu, but you will still need to take some physical notes, and this does hurt the VR experience a little. I also hope a future update adds some slight puzzle randomisation like in the Myst remake to make repeat playthroughs more enticing, but the game might already randomise some elements for all I know. Still, those are minor nitpicks, if you love challenging puzzle games, or loved the original, you will have a delightful time here.EDIT: I've since played the game a second time, fully in VR with the support of the notes I wrote the first time. The VR version is wonderful, though not without a few nitpicks. There's some visual artifacts randomly from time to time, and one time the feature that lets you skip stairs when using teleportation broke, sending me out of bounds and falling out of the map, which would have been very nauseating had I not been sat down. Also I feel like there are a decent amount of objects that should be interactable but aren't. The game does randomise the major puzzle solutions which is nice. Aside from those nitpicks, it's so, so good in VR. It's very immersive and really looks as gorgeous as the flatscreen version, albeit a little blurry.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven absolutely holds up, but not in the way I anticipated it to.  To set the stage, my 1st experience playing the myst games was between the ages of 7 and 11, and consequently my approach to playing them was click around on things at random until I got bored and moved on.  I recognize that they were well made, and that these were difficult puzzles that could be solved, but I did not understand how to approach them.  Consequently, I have always held Riven as an example of one of the hardest puzzles games ever made because when I did finally read what some of the solutions were, I simply could not wrap my mind around the complexity involved.  It was not until the 3rd Myst game, Exile, that I finally developed an approach to the world and the puzzles contained therein.  But, since I never went back and playing the originals, I did not have an opportunity to utilize this approach with the older games, and so the Ruby glasses stayed on.After binging the absolute hell out of the game yesterday, I am probably about 90% complete.  After logging off, I 1st found myself a little disappointed.  I was absolutely tearing through the game without encountering much in the way of difficulty, as I had the previous day while playing Lorelei.  In changing the puzzles, had they nerfed the difficulty? Was I just a really dumb kid back then, and it was never that hard to begin with?Having had time to process it, I think the true answer lies more in how the puzzles are being presented and what purpose they serve.  In most puzzle games, the primary attraction are the puzzles themselves, usually in regards to their difficulty or inventiveness.  The narrative can either be secondary, or at least separate from the act of solving.  To use a very recent example, several of the locked doors in Lorelei & the Laser Eyes can be solved by rearranging numbers and dates from nearby posters.  While fun and engaging, the puzzle itself does not add anything to the narrative.  It merely stands as an obstacle to be bested.Riven takes a wholly different approach.  Almost every puzzle in some way serves to further the story or teach you something about the world it large or build upon a mechanic that will be encountered later.  Many of the puzzles you will encounter do not even seem like puzzles at all, because they are so carefully woven into the context of the world around them.  Encountering puzzles in Riven is like being tasked with starting a train engine.  There many dials and switches and levers with unusual descriptions, and you have no idea where to start other than pulling and pulling at things and seeing what happens.  By the time you have it all figured out, it does not seem like a puzzle anymore because the design of a train follows its function.  It would not make sense in the real world to have to re assemble a key every time he wanted to turn the thing on.I think the design of Riven was a progession of their design philosphy in Myst, in which there were many puzzles that were just kind of there for no reason other than to solve them. With Riven, the story guides everything, including the puzzles.So to sum up, the game absolutely holds up, and while it may not be as mind-meltingly difficult as some games out there today, it stands apart in the completeness of it's design and the context of how puzzles are used.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Everything is phenomenal about this EXCEPT the following in order of significance:- Getting places takes longer than the 1997 version. A lot of waiting for sounds/animations to finish- Character animations are of lower framerate, inconsistent quality, and not always in sync- Loading screens (though infrequent)- Mouse controls can be wonky at times - Screenshot system saves only low-res screenshots which lack sufficient detail at timesI don't give 9/10s often for games, but this remake has earned it despite the minor annoyances.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I only have one complaint, otherwise I absolutely love this remake! My one complaint is that I hope they can make a patch so that the "ride" sequences (the "mag-levs" and mine cart) can be made to work in ultrawide. Everything runs at 21:9 except these sequences, so that's a bit immersion breaking, especially since I loved these as a kid and wanted to immerse myself in these rides! Riven has a special place in my heart. I remember being in school as a teenager thinking about all the puzzles at school and going home to try my ideas out again. Something about the world is eerie but beautiful at the same time. This remake is gorgeous, runs well on a pretty powerful PC, and is also different than the original! I love that the puzzles aren't quite the same. It makes this more fun to play, and so far I really like how they've changed the puzzles. I'm not just blowing through the game again knowing how everything works. I also feel like these new puzzles are more intuitive and sensible than in the original, so an actual improvement. But they kept the same look and sound effects and the nostalgia is all there.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This has been an amazing remake, and one that definitely encapsulates what I imagined Riven to look like in the 90s. They didn't forget their original fans either, as puzzles solutions are randomized for each playthrough.The only downside is that, like the Myst remake, 3D characters aren't quite "there" yet. Compared to the real-life acting of the original FMVs, the 3D counterparts are stiff and jerky, like a first-pass motion capture, with very little facial expression. But don't let that subtract from the absolutely beautiful scenery, literal world-encompassing puzzles, and mountains of lore.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's Riven, but in 3d / VR. Except.. different?It's still Riven, so it'll automatically get a recommended from me, but I don't think its nearly as good as the original. If you're someone that can't play the original due to compatiblity issues, issues with slideshow graphics, or the (significantly) higher difficulty, then this is better, otherwise I would suggest you play/experience the original first, and only then revisit this if you want more.I played the original Riven as a child, and never managed to finish the puzzles, I just remember fondly wandering around the islands. I did watch videos of others completing the game back then, but this was well over 10 years ago (probably around 15 years ago). I haven't revisited the puzzles or solutions since, and only broadly remembered the story and elements that went into the various puzzles.That said, I finished this game in about 6 hours, playing at a leisurely pace, reading all the journals out loud. I was able to finish every puzzle first try, and never got stuck except for 1 time when I . Add an additional ~1h to complete the achievements and bad endings, and this is a very short game. That might be what you are looking for, but not at all what the original Riven did, where you would want to take a break and think about the stuff you found. Here it kept being quite clear what to do (or aim for at least) or what I still needed.In general I think none of the changes are 'bad' - they are integrated well narratively and fit gameplay wise - but I never had a question of what to do next, I always knew exactly what I needed to do or what piece I was missing, while that might sound like a good thing, that was part of the magic of the original.Disclaimer: I haven't tried the VR yet, and I will probably replay in VR over the next few days, though I expect it will be very immersive it cannot really address the other points.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As far as a remake goes, this was probably the best way they could have done it. It's a good blend of new puzzles with rewritten story elements that added really well to the experience and finally allowed us to have a good look at the inside of Tay and outside Gehn's second lab/house.All said and done, the environment that Riven '97 released in was a very different one from today and I think they adapted well. I hope Myst 3 and 4 get the same treatment.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is how to do a remake.   It takes the original game, and improves it massively.Myst plays so much better as a fps than it ever did back in it's original point and click format.Playing as a fps, it really lets us concentrate on the puzzles,  rather than trying to work out which part of the screen to click on.The graphics are stunning....  The gameplay is much improved.  AND I get the vr version too.Just wow.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A much-needed update to a classic, fantastic game. Of all the Myst series, this one has the most interesting story.  You find out about the characters' motivations and you are rewarded for your puzzle-solving with new areas & new revelations about the characters and what's going on. Even though I'd played the 1997 one a couple of times, I still struggled with some of the puzzles here, in a good way. I love a game that has me taking notes and struggling to see patterns or figure out codes. The Myst series really did pioneer logical puzzles that made sense--not only in terms of the puzzle itself, but also the story. If there's a puzzle, there's a reason why it's there--every machine has a thought-out purpose in the world you're exploring. I have to admit, though, I do miss the old FMV video--the characters aren't quite as lifelike or relatable when rendered with graphics, and while the facial mapping is getting much better, they still don't look like real people, the way video does.  I'm sure it was too complicated/impossible to update in that way, so not a criticism to the devs. Overall, I can tell this update was made with serious love & effort, and it shows major respect for the spirit of the original. And the new areas and fully-fleshed-out graphics were very cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Still as outstandingly great as it was in the 90s.All the conceptual changes made to the original actually serve to better present the Riven's backstory, or make the it clearer why a puzzle works the way it does.By that I mean the puzzles are a bit less "tacked on" than they were in the original. They are not puzzles for the sake of there being puzzles, like some in Myst and later titles in the series. For every clue you have to find, there is a very good in game reason, why that clue was left and why it was left in that particular way.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven (2024) is an absolutely incredible remake of the 1997 original. It perfectly captures the artstyle and tone, while managing to remove some of the original's annoyances.I would argue that the only downgrade is the character animations. The original's FMVs using actors still hold up great, whereas the remake's rendered characters and their somewhat choppy animations stick out among an otherwise unfathomably beautiful game.What is Riven? Simply put: A point and click adventure from a first-person view. You do not collect a lot of items, instead you are expected to pay attention to the environment and the lore scattered within. You are expected to keep your own notes and learn the systems of Riven's world.If you like adventure games and you are interested in Cyan's works, this version is a great introduction.Riven is not as cryptic as Myst and the fully 3d environments make navigating the world considerably easier than clicking through the static images of the original.As someone who originally played Riven in 1998, I cannot recommend this game highly enough. The original is still a beautiful game in its own right (and holds up surprisingly well), however the ammenities of the remake granted by 25 years of technological advances make it a much more accessable game for players today.This game is a true labour of love by Starry Expanse/Cyan.Again: Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.user: LAM from hit game Deus Ex (2000)
_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps the greatest microcosm of the loss of uniquely spiritual, eerie quality of Riven 1997 that I fell in love with in favor of dull light fantasy rationalism in Riven 2024 is how animal life and natural formations, previously intertwined with the fate of Moiety, now stay firmly outside the text. With changes to puzzles and visuals, the Sunner's belch, along with the rock they lounge on, cease to be means by which you immerse yourself in the world and culture of Riven, becoming simply window dressing, temporary distractions that ring hollow. None escape this fate. Look at le epic fish! Isn't it kewl :OKeeping them as aesthetic background of the age and pasting right over with a more grounded, technology-first solution (even if there's something intriguing about literally viewing the world through the lens of oppressed), resembles a palimpsest. In it, we see a fundamental shift that Cyan began with Myst remakes come to fruition. Through this choice, and indeed many similar smaller choices, Riven 2024 conveys a different message than the original 1997 version and ironically could be seen as Gehn's preferred take on Riven - logic and technology not only first, but uber alles. To me, as much as I enjoyed my time revisiting familiar places with improved graphics, this alone warrants a negative review. VR-first nature of remake's design doesn't do it any favors either. Between fervent adherence to sliding doors, numerous puzzle simplifications with strictly chest-high interactions, various cool levers homogenized into VR-friendly buttons, weird blink-alike blackening of the screen at key moments where your character has to be repositioned even with accessibility turned off... You have to wonder whether collapse of the bridge between boiler and temple was staged so as to prevent VR players from having a tedious long walk and further commit to a more instant, less delayed gratification philosophy of jingling keys in front of their faces. An irony second only to "Gehn's Riven" is how putting supposedly immersive technology forward actually reduces variety in interactions and progression.VR necessitating use of 3d models over live actors further undermines the magic - clearly the developers are more skilled at environment design than modelling humans. Poor likenesses, stilted animations, HORRENDOUS lip sync that made me double-triple check whether I'm hallucinating. This cheapens every moment of character interaction, but none as much as your first impression of Rivenese village, now seemingly bereft of life. Barely noticeable 3d models run out of the frame before you can spot them, as if ashamed of their ugliness being recorded next to numbers in my notebook.I suppose it's inevitable that as creators age, their perspective changes and so does their output. This is an eternal curse of the remake - you only have to peek at now seemingly so dated Star Wars discourse to see how much grief there's been over various modifications Lucas committed to over the years. Parting one world (of the original) from another (of the remake) is something I therefore encourage and hope that this remake will not come to be seen as the "definitive version" in the future.Here's to hoping Cyan turns the page on remakes and produces more new, original games to find themselves again - though if firmament is any indication, the studio seems to be running out of juice. Still, one must imagine the ending has not yet been written!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Whether you played the original in 1997 or not, this game is one of the most gorgeous exploration-puzzle games, really one of the best "experiences" I've ever had and the remake took something that was beloved and excellent and improved it in surprising and subtle ways. When was the last time you played a game that you just got completely lost in and couldn't put down that wasn't just loot/respawn/next match? Riven is truly an engrossing world that draws you in and makes you want to keep looking a little further, playing a few minutes more. If you've ever done an escape room, if you've ever read a fiction book that you couldn't put down, if you love exploring, if you gasped a little bit when you first played Breath of the Wild and saw how big and gorgeous that world was, you should absolutely play this game. I played the entire game through on Steam Deck and although I couldn't have the graphics cranked up to full, it played smoothly and still looked so excellent. Sometimes I played on the deck, sometimes docked to the TV or a computer monitor. Always played with lights down and headphones or good speakers on. It is so immersive. The only challenge playing on the Deck itself was that some of the writing/symbols you need to be able to see clearly require a little squinting, which could be hard for first-time players and I'd recommend running it on a monitor/TV if you are playing on Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven... I can't believe it. Myst, sure, remake that it's the most famous, but this one. Wow. I played Myst as a kid with my dad. It was an awesome adventure, even if I didn't understand it all. But Riven was what really shaped my kid mind, the first time I was really able to understand a complex story. Wow and what a story. 5 disks for 5 islands - explore thoroughly, because switching them is a pain! I never forgot it, never gave up hope that I would be able to really explore it, like I could Myst.It was an awesome game, and this is a great remake. Hear and seeing Atrus, Gehn, Catherine, even that guard at the beginning again after all these years... If you ever wanted to really explore the awesome environment and story that Cyan made in this game, this is how you do it! The only thing I miss is seeing the real people.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is magnificent. For those who played the previous game, it is a dream come true, that of being able to move within these mysterious islands. Everything is reproduced with coherence, but many "licenses" of structuring the environment have been corrected due to the fact that immersion in a 3D world (and no longer point and click) requires greater coherence and precision in the terraforming of spaces.Level design-wise, it is truly a gem. Playing in VR, the spaces are balanced to move with the right sense of freedom, while being guided to follow specific pre-established paths. It is clear that this choice is the best to return the same experiential response of the point and click game.The biomes, the non-dispersion of the spaces, the artistic choice of colors and lighting sources, the composition of each glimpse (always studied in detail to evoke the maximum WOW effect. It seems like you are there, and you would like to live there, it is so beautiful.Great Cyan, for me your most successful product ever
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Faithful recreation of the classic game, with many new very welcome additions and changes that further expand upon the games design, art and feel. The changes from the original seem to all be things that "just make sense," and create a more fleshed out and intentional atmosphere, which is hard to do considering the art and design of the original being as phenomenal and immersive as it is. The visual style and graphics are incredible, the colors and ambiance is pure fantasy. The sound design and music is very similar to the original with wonderful additions and re-imaginings. It feels like the game I remember through the ever present "nostalgia-glasses" that are hard to take off, plus the awe of discovering many new things and places to explore. I applaud the studio Cyan for this release, reigniting the magic I felt playing Riven all those years ago, truly re-imagining the experience for today's hardware and graphics.Overall, 9/10.An absolute must play for Riven fans and newcomers alike. Please play this game, there is so much to take in, you won't regret any of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome rebuild so I got the full nostalgia hit, but enjoyed a new immersive experience.  It felt like my computer was showing me all the things I used to imagine back in 1997 when Riven was originally released.Absolutely amazing that they managed to fully build out this world in 3D, and managed to make some puzzle/gameplay changes to maintain the old feeling, but that works when we're able to roam around freely instead of looking at static images.I couldn't stop playing once I started it up until I finished it
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Good graphics, VR worked well. This is my first time playing Riven and from my understanding they made some of the puzzles a bit easier. However they still kept me very busy!The only real issue I ran into was that you can't really take notes without taking off the VR headset, which is immersion-breaking. Yes, you can take screenshots, but the screenshots are a bit dim in the menus. It took putting multiple screenshots together and being able to write on something to figure out the number systems. Yes, they're simple enough once you have figured out they are base 5 and base 3, and after that point, I didn't have to take off the headset again,. I don't know if it would be realistic to actually allow us to take notes in VR mode by some means. Maybe we could have had our own "notebook" in the bag along with the rest, and have the screenshots go there, and a pencil to write with. Yeah, it'd be clumsy in VR, but it would be a start.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A masterclass in  retouching of a legendary adventure game! Vusials are razor sharp "just as I remember it 25 years ago!". but in freakin' VR. Puzzles are mostly the same but different in VERY welcoming ways, the narrative has been expanded and improved greatly, enveloping the story in much greater detail. A must play for every adventure player. Thank you, The Starry Expanse Project for keeping Riven 3D alive for so many years, thank you Cyan for putting high octane fuel into that slow burning passion project! What a time to be alive!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven has always been one of my favorite adventure/puzzke games. This remake is done so well and holds true of its origin, with the controls and first person gameplay as the original game should have been, but the graphics and technology was simply not there at the time.Only caveat is the 3D characthers, they stand i bit out of the scenery. In the original its real people.Indeed my recommendation whether or not you'ved played the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this expecting yet another ...After not personally connecting with Obduction or Firmament, if you'd pitched me on the idea of modern Cyan doing a full-on Riven  with changes to puzzles and additional content, given how much the game means to me, I'd have urged them to play it safer...Thankfully, I dove right in without reading anything about it, so the changes were a complete surprise!I'm delighted to have been preemptively proved WRONG, and have been enjoying the heck out of this version. Some of the puzzles have been tweaked to be a bit more intuitive, others have been replaced entirely with new puzzles and mechanics that are more accessible, (especially for the hearing impaired) and what I've seen of the new content has intriguing world-building implications that don't really feel like they retcon or go against the spirit of the original.That said, the old game is still well worth playing, because it feels darker, dirtier, and scarier; (I don't have a VR headset but assume that the increased visibility and cleaner textures here and there were necessary visual comfort changes)It's probable that making small tweaks to a masterpiece is much easier than creating from scratch, however... , but if design changes are on the table, and THIS is what Cyan is now capable of, part of me hopes they remake Myst 3, 4, and 5 at this quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended (with a few caveats)The flatscreen experience is fairly polished and the game itself is great with a super unique approach to puzzle design. However, there seem to be a lot of issues running the game in VR at the moment. I finished this game with a mix of both flatscreen and VR  modes and really enjoyed my time with it for the most part and it seemed to played well in both modes. However, I've had to start the game twice over due to save file corruption and redo several sections for the same reason. I think this might have been the result of jumping between VR and flatscreen modes. I also had several UE5 crashes while only using the flatscreen mode. Which may have been caused by continuing the game from a VR save. For VR players, it might be worth waiting until a few more patches have been released before purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: Inferior to the original but still good.  Dont like how Atrus just goes off and doesnt continue to stabilize riven when your in there.  Some of the newer puzzles i think were unnecessary or not as good as the original, graphics werent as good as the original either.   I think the worst part for me is the removal of the original full motion video of the characters, i think there should have been an option to include that somehow even if its forces you to not be able to look around for certain moments.I did enjoy being able to walk around and look more than in the original.  I do think this is a good game and I am glad others can play it easier now.  Hopefully an update includes the FMV and maybe we can get an exile remake, or even better just remake Myst 5 so it actually feels like a myst game and gives a fitting and fulfilling ending to the series hopefully with more FMV.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I'm impressed! I was expecting a basic remake exactly the same as the original, but Cyan really went out of their way to change things up and add new content. A lot more than I would've expected. There's still the familiar puzzles but the new ones are great too. It felt like playing Riven for the first time again. Not to mention the world looks STUNNING and so immersive.• New or revamped puzzles means some of the original ones have changed or parts are missing, this might disappoint a small subset of original fans and cause them confusion while playing but I think it's an improvement.• The video actors have been replaced by 3D characters. Although it was done better than the cartoony style in the recent Myst remake, it might still be a negative for some people since it's not as hyper-realistic.• New or revamped puzzles to keep the original fans busy, I was very excited by the changes.• Beautiful graphics,  a huge upgrade from the original 1997 Riven.• New elements in the environment that help backup the lore more.• As always, fantastic music and sound design, Cyan is known for this.• The game feels immersive, it's easy to forget how long you've been playing.• A lot of depth to the lore, much can be discerned within game but some of it might need to be discovered in the other games in the series and the trilogy of books.All-in-all, whether you're an old fan or new to Cyan games, I highly recommend this game. You can't miss this one if you enjoy puzzle, narrative, or detective games. Hope you enjoy your adventure as much as I did!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful and detailed remake of a wonderful old game. The new puzzles are enough that I needed a whole page of notes to solve them in addition to completing the ones I already knew from playing the original, and the recreation of the environments with modern materials and audio is so fantastic. I had a very nice time. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible re-imagining of a classic game. This game came out the year I was born, so it's safe to say that I knew exactly how long we've been waiting to see it come back again. Cyan, you've knocked it out of the park. Not only did you remake the game, you changed the way some things are done in order to subvert the expectations of those who are veterans to the experience. It didn't take me as long as I figured it'll take most, but I will say that is in large part to having recently played the original experience and carrying over knowledge. I had such a blast playing this, and my favorite part still remains the tram rides. Looking forward to whatever comes next from your team.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The changes made in this and the VR of it all is amazing. I didn't want it to end. A couple puzzles I had to look up, but it wasn't TOO bad. I really hope they do the VR treatment for the other games. The MYST series has come a long way from it's innovative beginnings. I look forward to more VR content from Cyan Worlds. They know how to do it right!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you so much for this amazing remake, Cyan! I hadn't thought a true 3D Riven would ever be realised, so the announcement came as a big surprise and now I can say you surpassed all my expectations!What I love is that it's really the Riven we know. It looks just like you would expect it to look like. Yet at the same time, there are changes and new areas... but it almost feels like they were always there! It has truly received the love and attention for detail that one would hope for. I don't think it could be any better... it feels like this is Riven as it should be!Thank you so much!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven from 1997 is one of my favorite games of all time, and it is extremely exciting to finally be able to play it again with modern fully 3d graphics, and in VR!I feel like this remake strikes the perfect balance that a modern remake should strive for: Keep the spirit of the original intact while changing enough to make it feel justified, rather than simply uncritically retreading old ground. Even if you played the original, you will get stuck again and have to re-evaluate what you know. This really is the closest thing you can get to the feeling of playing the game for the first time. However, it's not so different that it is unrecognizable as the same game. Again, I think they threaded this needle extremely well.The things that make this game great are the same that made the original great. Beautiful, scenic and artistically crafted graphics accompany a compelling backstory and narrative. You won't find a game that does environmental storytelling better: Literally everything has a justified purpose of some kind. This blends into the puzzles. At it's best, Riven's puzzles don't feel like puzzles, they feel more like a test of how well you understand this world and its culture. As with anything that changes a beloved classic, the original fans (like myself) will always have some nitpicks. However, for me personally, for every change that might not be to my taste, there is another change that I really like that actually fixes a pertinent issue from the original. And at the end of the day, I am just extremely grateful that this game finally has a lovingly crafted remake from the original developers. (After the 5th Myst remake, it was about time! :P )
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven lives up to the hype! I'm blown away by how good it is.The three pillars of Cyan's games, the environment, puzzles, and narrative, have all been improved while staying true to the essence of the original. The visuals are stunning and filled with detail. I like the zoom feature that lets you see details up close or observe far away objects more clearly. Logical inconsistencies from the original have also been corrected. Additionally, the remake gives us new lore to dive into, which is the first in a long time in the Myst/D'ni universe. The original directors all returned in some capacity for the remake, and it shows. The whole team clearly has a lot of talent and passion for Riven. Thank you for creating this masterpiece for us!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remake. I was concerned my nostalgia for my original playthrough in the 90s was rose-tinted, but no, this is the real deal. Buy if you enjoy adventure puzzles held up by lore and logic rather than the all-too-common strange combinations of meaningless objects.All that said, I still highly recommend the original as well. This game is a significant technical redesign, making both '97 and '24 versions worth trying for their own reasons. Lots of little callbacks to the original elements are a nice touch, but this is *not* the same game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, yes, yes! This was totally worth it. Walking around in a world I first experienced as a teenager. I love how they kept the original game alive, while actually changing most of its key elements. New puzzles, changed puzzles, but everything felt in place and in touch with the world that was created so many ears ago. Thanks Cyan team, for allowing us to experience this again.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing!! Seeing Riven come Alive after so many years is like a dream come true! Works like a charm on a RTX2080 Super! _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only part way in, but wow.  I feel like a kid again. _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this and I think I can still recommend it because it's a gorgeous setting and the puzzles seem well done and not too overwrought, but beware - playing this (standard version, not VR) gave me pretty bad motion sickness. So just a heads up, if you're like me: this game might make you motion sick. Decreasing FOV and fiddling with the control settings might mitigate this for some people, but it didn't for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Congratulations to the Cyan team for an amazing remake. The art and love put in this remake are remarkable and the new puzzles gave a smile on my face when I found the solutions.I played the original game when it was released and I cannot be excited enough when my 5 year old son saw the Riven poster on steam and ask me "what is that?". _childDocuments_.review: Ok, I usually don't  write reviews, but! Riven was my first love (and hyperfixation) on PC back in '97 as a teenager.This remake is GLORIOUS! The music, the ambience, the puzzles, it's all still there! The additions and slight changes to the game were done beautifully and I cannot thank Cyan and the team who worked on that enough! I streamed the whole game in one go, 12 hours and my chat was as invested as I was!Highly recommend to new and returning players! Now I've got to play Myst's remake as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Played original Riven many Ages ago... this new version is so incredibly immersive. _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent. A very faithful remaster and still an enjoyable experience after all these years. It's a little rough around the edges in some places but there are no obvious deal breakers that would stop me from recommending the game.The performance is a little iffy, mostly due to stuttering which happens whenever you enter a new area. A lot of the easter eggs from the original appear to be missing, and the overall vibe of the game is a little different. The puzzles are still quite difficult and I feel like a hint system would be been a great edition to the game, but old walkthroughs and hint guides are still valid here.All in all though, it's a fantastic remake of one of the greatest point and click adventure games of all time. If you're a fan of puzzle games it really doesn't get much better than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This world feels just as surreal, beautiful, haunting, creepy, and threatening as the original Riven did.  It's one of very, very few fictional places that I've been able to fully lose myself in.  While the geometry of the world is fairly simplistic, the texture work in this remake is absolutely gorgeous, and I'm so glad they included a zoom feature so I can marvel at the fine details.  Materials have multiple layers of ware and many tiny ornamental details.  As beautiful as the game is, it's the sound design (much of which seems to have been preserved from the original) that makes this place real.  Everything you interact with has weight to it, takes time, and sounds distinct from everything else.  The haunting music in this game makes me feel a very specific sort of fear and awe, which fits the game's plot perfectly.Some of the larger and more iconic puzzles have been simplified, but that didn't detract from the experience for me.  I love being able to write notes on screenshots.  I still had to use a little physical paper to solve a few puzzles.  If you enjoyed the original or have any interest in puzzle games this is a must play.  I would recommend playing Myst first if you haven't already, since it will make the story easier to interpret and will show the huge leap in progress Cyan made with world building between the two games.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is the sequel to Myst and the story picks up right where the original left off. Atrus needs your help to free Catherine from Gehn, Atrus' estranged father.  When you arrive on Riven you are instantly captured, but you are freed a very short time later by a mysterious benefactor. You come to realize that there are two factions fighting for control of Riven, those who are loyal to Gehn and those who want to be free from Gehn's tyranny. It's up to you to find Gehn and trap him in a one man prison that looks like a linking book. But making your way through this world is not as straight forward as you hoped. You must overcome numerous obstacle in order to proceed.Pros:Superb GraphicsSimple ControlsNon-linearOpen World MapMultiple EndingsMany puzzles to solveCons:Some of the mechanics are painfully slowOne puzzle was misleadingI absolutely loved the 1997 version of Riven and the remake is nothing short of a masterpiece. Some of the puzzles have changed from the original and each time you play the remake, the game is slightly different because the order for some of the puzzles are random. Best of all, for the first time, you can see Riven in 3-D and go where ever you wish.The only two things I didn't like about the remake. The way the machines work on Riven tend to work very slowly especially domes that lead to the Starry Expanse. They could have been sped up a bit. The other problem I had was with one of the puzzles. Unless I missed something, it was intentionally misleading making it illogical but it's the only one.At the time of this review, Riven 2024 was selling 34.99.  I love the Myst worlds and I this remake is well worth the price. Bring on Myst III: Exile.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This was definitely a day one purchase for me since the original Riven is one of my most memorable gaming experiences. Now I've bought both on release!With only an hour of playtime I have already had multiple jaw dropping experiences and while I was skeptical about changing up the game with new and altered content, I am now pretty much all steam ahead enjoying this experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible remake that balances the old with the new. It is very familiar for veterans of the original but with enough changes to make the experience fresh. If you are a fan of puzzle games, you owe it to yourself to pick up an excellent remake of one of the best puzzle games ever made.Only thing I can say as a small knock against this remake is that we don't have the charming live action people imposed into the game for cut-scenes. The models they use here are fine and look great but there's a charm to using live action people that is a little bit missed lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute masterpiece. Granted it was when it was originally made, but what stands out in this rendition, is what many remakes don't usually get right. This has really been re-thought for the modern age, some parts changed quite a bit, but each time those changes generally draw a gasp, or become a reminder of what made me love the original.Bravo Cyan, I know the work it must have taken to make such a beautiful remake, and knowing that they arent working with AAA budgets makes it even more commendable. So please give them some money and buckle up for a beautiful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent update of the classic into full realtime 3D. Cannot recommend highly enough! Finally fans of the original who always wanted to see what was just out of shot of the fixed renderings can turn their heads.For players of the original there are enough changes and new puzzles to make it worth a replay. No game before or since has done as well making the puzzles seem part of the world as Riven, and that continues in this version.The only ♥♥♥♥♥♥ is the replacement of FMV filmed characters with kinda-ok-but-not-great 3D models. I can see why they had to do this as it's now a real 3D environment, not a 2D rendering of one.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly as an old-time fan this feels like the definitive version. Gorgeous and the move to 3D really helps to feel the space out and see how everything connects in relation to each other in a way that the original's slideshow couldn't really do. Some changes and additions were made to puzzles but not in a way that detracts imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A missed opportunity for greatness. It nails the visual and auditory feel or the original. Phenomenal graphics. Being able to freely explore the world, and view spacial relations realistically is amazing. The subtle expansions to the areas you can explore are a nice touch.A few of the changes  are welcome. Most, unfortunately, are not. They follow a general pattern: They remove one aspect of what made Riven great and unique, which is the holistic design of the world and the main two puzzles. (The other aspect: The beautiful world and graphics, remains intact!) The new gameplay is comparatively linear and piecemeal, instead of integrated. This is in some cases acute , and in some cases subtle: The navigation , the replacement for the  etc.I feel like the redesigned puzzles are inferior to the original; my suspicion: it's to make game time more predictable, and to prevent players from getting stuck.An advantage of a gameplay redesign is fresh exploration for those who already know the original. For this selfish reason, I had a better time with it than I might have had with the original, since it introduced new elements. Because of the specifics of the redesign, I would recommend the original to someone who hasn't played Riven.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: NUMBER 5NUMBER 5NUMBER 5NUMBER 5...no wait, that's the wrong number. Sorry Yoko.Either way by the time you are done Riven the Fifth Age of the Mysthology will be embedded in your brain thoroughly.This is going to sound extremely hyperbolic, but I truly believe this is the greatest PC game ever created. Now, much is owed to the original of course - but this is not an exact replica of the original. Some things have been changed. Some have been improved. But despite this, Riven is NO LESS diabolical than it ever was. It's the greatest puzzle of all time in digital form, which is an impressive feat considering how FEW puzzles its world actually contains.Sure, there is learning the mechanical flow of how things operate. There is experimentation with switches and valves, staples of Myst echoing Channelwood mainly. There is the necessity to build a deep, comprehensive knowledge of the culture of the Moiety, the world itself, and it's various trappings, right down to the fauna that inhabit it. But the actual "sit there and hammer away to figure out a puzzle" parts of RIven are far less in their distribution than Myst, far more sensible, and FAR FAR more gratifying to the point where it is sometimes difficult to even see that these two games are from the same series since the philosophy behind them seems to vastly, vastly different. Riven is such an unmistakably large leap ahead of Myst in every possible way that its surprising to hear it only came out a mere few years after Myst. It feels like the natural progression of a series that was around for twenty years before it eventually was refined to where it was now. I am gushing, but this is the point - I've never played a game like Riven, and I know I never will again. Cyan has done interesting work over the years, but Riven is their absolute masterpiece, and this remake is such a massive leap forward in so many ways that it really is hard to believe. Visually its absolutely stunning. It captures the look and feel of the pre-rendered world of the original to the nines. It's easily the most glorious and breathtaking game world I have ever seen. The one negative here, the sole thing holding this back is that the character models in Cyan games are still incredibly weak in comparison to their contemporaries. Better than the Myst remake, yes. On par with more recent Cyan affairs, perhaps, but nothing beyond that. It's just very hard to reconcile a game world that is absolutely unmatched in its art direction and execution with the decidedly far, far lower fidelity of the character models. The game world itself looks like it would be a far better math with character models, say, on the level of a Larian Studios game such as Baldur's Gate 3. But games cost money. They take time. They take tools, they take, and take, and take, and at some point, SOMETHING has to give. I think the character models are a fair trade for a world that looks this beautiful, and the only reason its even worth nitpicking is because it is the ONE flaw in an otherwise completely immaculate visual experience.It's really hard to not gush on and on here because this is just such an incredible remake. I never thought I'd see Riven remade in such a triumphant and celebratory way while actually improving on the old game (in my opinion) but not replacing it. That is one of the things that was so smart here - to give even existing Riven fans a new experience by changing just enough that their memory wouldn't be able to fill in all the blanks. The inherent issue with Myst is that you fundamentally understand, as a Myst fan, what needs to be done immediately. You can just never go back to not knowing, to that original discovery. RIven fixes that in every regard. Riven for a time was the best PC game ever made. The remake extends and improves upon it, and is the new reigning king.The king is dead.Long live the king.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting this. Not just nostalgia, but like hearing a record remastered in Atmos. It's amazing on large screens, even running well on my M1 Air. Advice: its not the old Riven, so many modern ideas, especially one from the Witness was a surprise. It still requires patience, but the goal of the game is to engage with this strange place, and the devs made it well worth the trip!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I was surprised at how much the game had been developed.  Really enjoyed it.Not only was the sound and the graphics enhanced, but the whole game play too.  From the interactions to the puzzles being revamped to randomised outcomes and endings - which took a bit of time to sort out and understand.The price, though helps with the developer is considered OK, I didn't feel like my eight hours was justified,  That said, I'm happy to pay for it , to help them and maybe give them funding to develop other Myst games.Well done, I'd expect a lot of positive reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: VAGUE SPOILERSI was nervous that I would be disappointed by the changes made to the remake. After playing the demo and seeing big differences, I actually got excited to see what else was new. Aside from a couple bugs (fingers crossed they get patched out), this is the most fun VR game I've played since Half-Life: Alyx. It's also a visually beautiful game, in and out of VR. _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the story and the graphics of the game, they are both so intricate and consume you from the moment you begin playing. The puzzles were hard and I won't lie, I had to get some help online a few times toward the end but they were really enjoyable regardless. I think it's worth the time it took to play and its price. So if you're interested, I would tell you to just go for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what a remake should be. Able to capture the feeling of the original game but with enough thoughtful changes to make it feel like a new experience.  I played original Riven when it was released in 1997 and never thought I'd be playing it again feeling just as immersed as I did 28 years ago, truly a surreal experience. Thank you so much to the teams at Cyan behind this.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good faithful remake of the original. Some have claimed the puzzles are not as well integrated and lying everywhere. Not entirely true. The puzzles for the 'mild spoiler' rebels are actually more lore friendly than the original as they are supposed to be secretive and good and going undetected by the antagonists of the story. Making them more hidden and using more native symbology was a much needed improvement over the original. The thing I wish had been added into the puzzles a little and a way to learn it was the language. It is present, but there is not a way to learn it. Also there is not a way  to learn how combinations of higher numbers work without using an outside of the game source. It would have been nice to have been in game. A little bit more exploration for some of us that like more of a challenge than others. Also the final puzzle was harder in the original. This point I agree with many others. It is too simplified in the remake. If this had to be done for some players then a harder mode should have been made for others. Other than these points and the fact that the original video could not have been upscaled with AI and reused in the remake, the remake is pretty good. Worth it for new players. Old players will enjoy the new graphics, but miss certain things that the original had and maybe did better in some areas of the game. With this game I would suggest playing both versions. I guess the old version will run on windows 10 or 11 like  the new. If it doesn't it will with a program called SCUMVM. It is a VR machine that does a near perfect run of the old version of Riven. You only need Windows 10/11 to run the new version. I did notice it had a bug that made it crash once though partway through. This only happened once and didn't occur again. Also beware of 'spoiler' walking in a certain area with the walkways upside down as you can get stuck. This fix is exit the game and go back in on the autosave when reloading the game. Do not try to save first if you are stuck here. This bug can happen elsewhere, but mainly in the area I mentioned. For those of us that played the original, don't expect things to be in the same places or work in the same way. Some puzzles and locations have  changed or been expanded and work differently now. Better I think too. One bugged area that was in the original is now fixed in the remake. The biggest thing for players of the original; you will get to go in new areas that you could not go in before, and this alone makes the remake worth playing. For all players the story is the best in the series and very engaging. Without it all the rest would be pointless. For this alone I would strongly recommend this game to play and consider the graphics, new areas to explore, and puzzle revision to be the icing on the cake. If you like puzzles and a good story this is not one to miss out on.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: My name might give it away that I grew up to be a Myst fan. Riven was, in fact, my "first video game" that my dad played with me when I was 4. The entire series including original Riven has seen multiple replays and I was more than excited for a 3D remake.What surprised me immensely is that my expectations were exceeded by Cyan not just doing a raw remake but also having the courage to make changes that streamline the puzzles, storytelling, and progression of the game. Not only did that flow feel better - it also allowed me to feel almost like I'm playing this for the first time again. Some new puzzles and elements were added as well.Overall I had a very enjoyable time with the game and am very excited that this beauty has finally seen the light of day.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Having played and liked the 1996 version of Riven, this refurbished edition of the game is a welcome return to it. Cyan outdid themselves with the graphics, having beautiful visual effects on high settings, and (unlike some other nice-looking titles) has a high-performance profile for lower-end systems that doesn't eat up power more quickly than a pregnant lioness in a hamburger factory.Though this game has a Playable rating for the Steam Deck, I have played it exclusively on the deck at the time of writing, and in my opinion, it should have a Verified rating, because it's very well-behaved, power-friendly, and for me, worked out of the box. Worth the price.Nice job, Cyan. I approve.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Artwork is great, good flow of play.Many of the puzzles are reminiscent of the 1997 version, but the art and gameplay is better now (as it should be!), very fluid (with very few initial release bugs that I'm sure will be worked out with the fast response of the dev team).I played through this game straight through - only _having_ to stop because I needed to sleep (and give my brain time to work out some of the puzzles).The only 'caution' I would have is if you have any sort of trouble with 'flashy scenes/lights', you should be very careful of this game - I just looked away from the screen while 'traveling' (play the demo and you will get an idea...) - otherwise, I really enjoyed the game and recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this in VR if you have a strong PC. My 4090/7800X3D was still struggling a bit with this w/ Q3 over VD. It's perfectly playable, but there are some frame rate issues. This has the same weird shadow issue as Firmament. It looked blurry at first, but setting AA to low and DLSS off made it better.
