_childDocuments_.review: A Timeless MasterpieceFew games can claim the timeless brilliance of Riven, and even in 2024, it stands as one of the most breathtaking achievements in interactive storytelling and world-building. As the sequel to the legendary Myst, Riven took everything the original did well and elevated it to an entirely new level, creating a gaming experience that remains unparalleled decades later.Visuals That Transcend TimeEven by today's standards, Riven's pre-rendered environments are nothing short of stunning. The artistry and detail poured into every inch of this world make it feel alive, mysterious, and eerily real. The intricate design of the islands, the beautifully woven cultural elements, and the subtle animations breathe life into Gehn's fractured domain. Its ability to immerse players in an alien yet familiar world feels as fresh today as it did in 1997.A Puzzle Design MasterclassWhat makes Riven truly timeless is its brilliant puzzle design. The challenges are deeply integrated into the narrative and the environment, requiring players to truly understand the world rather than brute-forcing solutions. Every puzzle feels meaningful, serving as a piece of the grand narrative puzzle that slowly unravels as you explore. It’s the kind of game where solving a challenge delivers not just satisfaction but also a deeper appreciation for the care and thought that went into the design.Narrative Depth and ImmersionIn 2024, storytelling in games has evolved immensely, but Riven's narrative structure remains a benchmark for excellence. The game tells its story primarily through exploration, environmental clues, and cryptic details, allowing players to piece together the lore at their own pace. It’s an experience that rewards curiosity and critical thinking, making every revelation feel personal and earned.Why It Still MattersIn an age dominated by fast-paced games and instant gratification, Riven stands as a reminder of the power of patience, observation, and slow-burning mystery. Its influence can still be seen in modern narrative-driven titles, and its atmosphere, music, and puzzles continue to inspire awe in new generations of players.ConclusionWhether you’re revisiting Riven for nostalgia or experiencing it for the first time, the game remains a shining example of what the medium can achieve. In 2024, Riven is not just a classic—it’s an essential gaming experience that feels as magical and rewarding as it did when it first captured imaginations.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun puzzle game, I had to get a few hints because I was oblivious to certain things that are supposed to be easy to find and would have taken me hours otherwise. The puzzles are very in depth and often layer over each other. If I didn't get tiny hints every once in a while though there could have easily been 5-10 more hours added onto my playtime
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: From a purely graphical and immersive experience standpoint it's great. Between the free roam and updated graphics, it's fun to see.However, if you care about the puzzles more, this game is a massive downgrade from the original. They massively simplified most of the puzzles, they changed most areas of the game in more ways than just graphics and walking around, so purists that liked the original are going to be mad. They also gave Riven the "yellow paint" treatment in some regards where they removed a lot of "extra" stuff and highlighting important things or making things like buttons much more noticeable.Walking everywhere takes forever, There is no Zip Mode, Most animations can't be skipped and loading in new areas can take several seconds and isn't done in parallel with the animations.Also, it's 2024 and we are still releasing games with controls you can't configure? Isn't that functionality BUILT IN to Unreal? You just have to implement it?
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Instantly brought back nostalgia from my childhood playing the original with my dad. It was really amazing to see all the beauty from the original recreated in high definition with modern 3D graphics. There are a few janky character animations and the 3D modeled characters do lack some of the charm of the original live-action video from the original, but overall a really beautiful and faithful re-imagining of an all-time Classic. Highly recommended for fans of challenging puzzle games and Sci-fi
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe this is real. I'm so immersed I struggle to remember what was in the original game or not. I'm glad they changed some things because the most difficult puzzles are the one I remember, and the most evil doors. Nice to see the doors are intact lolIf you have a 13/14th gen intel cpu, you might run into crashes when trying to launch the game. Your mileage may vary, but whenever a game gives me this crash I just need to turn down the Performance core ration in Intel Xtreme tuning utility. _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time playing Riven to completion. Loved every second of it and was sad that it was over when I got to the end.The 3D characters are a little jarring if you're used to the greenscreened characters from years ago, but I understand why they had to do it.The graphics were amazing and detailed, and I didn't mind backtracking because I was able to marvel at them each time. Will def boot this game up every once and a while to just walk around and take it all in again.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I never really had the chance to do a true play through of the original Riven. I'd watched a let's play of it well before I ever had an opportunity to play, because I wanted to know the stories. This rebuilt Riven feels like it was purpose built just for me and that situation. I knew bits of pieces of what I was doing which helped steer me on a forward course but otherwise I had to take my own notes for the brand new puzzles, while exploring new areas. I loved every minute of it.The world felt rich and fleshed out, even more so than before, and getting to walk in these locations in VR was especially fun though I did switch to normal play near the end for convenience for note taking.My one complaint is the lack of transitions. If this is a graphical thing then I take it back since my computer isn't really up to snuff for this, but every transition movie was made into a black load screen. Every elevator, mine cart, maglev train, ladder, and even just turning the maglev around spawns a black screen and very brief load. This felt really disappointing as it removed some of the most breath taking moments from Riven, the mine cart ride in particular. I hold some hope that maybe a future patch or mod might put these sequences back in, but given the rest of the world's face lift, I was willing to forgive this draw back.At the end of the day I played this to get lost in a world and be part of a story that wasn't interested in holding my hand. I got both of these in spades and loved it dearly. But I swear to Yeesha if you remake Myst 3 and don't include the marble ride I'm burning Cyan to the ground.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A great puzzle game, technically a sequel but you can get away without playing the first game. The environment is beautiful, but character models are a little lackluster. Luckily, it's mostly a solitary game so you don't see them much.Riven is the sequel to Myst, but you can get away without playing it first. It'll just provide what's essentially an extra paragraph or two unless you really dig deep into some in-game and meta lore. I highly recommend Myst: Masterpiece Edition for the point-and-click fans and realMyst: M.E. for the free-roam fans. Myst (2020) is fine as well, I just prefer the older games' FMV cutscenes + graphics.I've played Riven (1997) previously. A good few times now, and about a year or two ago most recently. It took me around 12 hours to 100% this version, alongside finding most of the non-achievement alternate endings.If you're new to the series expect a base completion to take a fair bit longer (maybe 20-30 hours depending on your puzzle solving skills). I'm tempted to say the original game is harder, but this one had a new system that I'm not entirely sure I figured out. The new music tracks are great, and I'll always be a fan of the old ones. While environmental detail is utterly beautiful most of the time, it falls short very rarely (the LOD for the massive leaves on Jungle Island from Temple is not very good). Sadly, a lot of the character animations are a bit clunky: although 3d models for characters are improved compared to Myst (2020), they still run at a lower fps than the rest of the game and their animations aren't always aligned with in-game objects.I experienced one or two funky bugs with interactive objects, but it really wasn't a common occurrence. Riven (1997) is a decently different experience than this one, and I'd recommend having a look at it alongside Exile (the sequel) if you enjoyed this. You could likely play both Rivens in either order without losing out on much from either, but I couldn't say for sure.One desire I had that I saw someone else mention in the reviews:    I was a bit disappointed that the  didn't retain its complexity. I was very excited to go into it after having completely forgotten how it worked. It still isn't a bad puzzle  by any means, but it'd be amazing for some form of original puzzles to return.Also, the

_childDocuments_.review: The game does a great job making the puzzles feel like extensions of the world rather than arbitrary obstacles (with a couple of exceptions).  It constantly feels like you're learning about a new world, culture, and technologies.There were 2 main downsides.  The first was a couple of puzzles, my difficulty was with finding what I was meant to interact with, rather than what the solution was.The other is the slow animations of travel between islands.  It feels thematic, but also when you need to reread something on another island, the only 2 methods of travel are very very slow.  I'd estimate 40% or more of my playtime was backtracking.Overall, this might be my favorite puzzle game.  Highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is overall enjoyable, a lot of quality from it comes from the 1997 Riven (such as the story, puzzles etc) but this is well recreated.Some puzzles and layouts were changed, and I think it's fine overall, it's the kind of stuff that would fit in the universe and the original game.However there are some important flaws to note : The game clearly lacks optimization, there are some glitches, some crashes, overall it's a bit rough on the edges even though it doesn't ruins too much the experience, it would just be nice to have some more polishing.Also, I don't really see what's the point of VR, this is clearly not optimized enough for it and there's nothing really interesting that VR brings to the table.Also, I lost 5 years of my lifespan on that unskippable rotating room animation on the temple island, as well as the starry expanse domes transitions.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved the original.Completed it back then when it came out, even though it took me a few years to solve. Was just a child. ^^Riven 2024, looks goregous in the Unreal 5 engine.However, as for any engine that renders characters, they still look a bit plastic.At a late point in the game, the bad guy would open up a door and is directly grabbing through the doorhandle. ^^Well, I am spoilt by the live action FMVs from the original.So when coming from the original where real actors have been used, it feels a bit off.Well... but just slightly.Aside of that I also experienced some minor shadow glitches, but I cannot enjoy this gem on highest settings since my rig isn't that good for. :(Yet, it still looks awesome, despite these minor flaws. The performance also isn't all too bad when using DLSS Quality, as I do.I've missed a few things like the villagers or the outpost guy who rings the alarm.STILL, clear thumbs up.They stood quite nicely to the original, added some new stuff (including new riddles) and you'll experience even totally new rooms or let's call it "pictures" when speaking about the original. XDIt was one of the first games I played and I was astonished that zapping through pictures can be that entertaining.Here you can freely move around and enjoy all the Ages of Riven. Explore and find solutions for the riddles.If you liked the original and are not too mad about rendered characters compared to live action ones, this remake will absolutely entertain you.There might be some questionable things that have been altered or left out, but then again it's a remake.The overall lore fits and even got a bit expanded.So this sounds quite mixed, as I had some mixed feelings during my first playthrough.Now after finishing it once, I actually enjoy it and see it as a good reimagination of the original. <3Oh and these are also back:Even though they are not really part of a riddle anymore as in the first one.Well... Technically they are, but you do not need to know how they sound by sneaking up on them. :P

_childDocuments_.review: I played this entire game in VR and let me just get this out of the way: This game in VR, right now, is a hot mess. It is extremely resource intensive, very often struggling to maintain 90 fps on my setup (RTX4090 + 13900k) WITH DLSS quality on. It supports both Steam and openxr runtimes so you CAN use steam overlay, but for some reason, the game turns into a jumbling mess while the overlay is open, to the point where everything would shake uncontrollably while the achievement window popped up. And, by far the worst part: Out of the 3 or 4 fast travel methods the game has, it consistently crashed to desktop when using 2 of them. By consistently, I mean about 60% at first, and that rate just went up as my game progressed. One of the fast travel methods isn't even optional, but mandatory for completing the game, so whenever I had to use it and it crashed, I just opened the game in flat mode while in VR, fast travelled, saved, closed the game, and resumed it in VR. That experience is exactly as miserable as it sounds.And yet, I'm giving it a positive review. The reason for that is that this is an absolute gem of a game. Having never played Myst or Riven before, I went into these 2 games completely blind, and played both of them in VR. While Myst felt like a fun interesting little adventure, Riven was absolutely breath taking. The VR mode makes you work for it, but it's absolutely worth it. The feeling of being in a beautiful and unknown world full of secrets to be unlocked and a mission is only amplified by the VR experience. The writing pulls you into its world and characters, and somehow, the remake of a 1997 game feels more modern and sophisticated than most of the contemporary stuff I play. I finished this game over a week ago and I still think about it every day, whether it is a puzzle, a line of text, a specific place in its world, or just about the sense of wonder and discovery it made me feel as I slowly peeled each layer of mystery away from its onion.Bottomline is, the VR iteration of this game is frustrating, but be patient with it. It's well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't aware that puzzles and other content had been changed from the original when I started playing, so it threw me off at first as I thought I was loosing my mind trying to find an area I was sure was in a specific spot. But once I realized it wasn't exactly the same game but a re-imagining, things wen't much more smoothly (some puzzles are virtually identical, some are modified/improved, and others are new or completely different). I actually liked the changes as they add a bit more depth and nuance without taking away from the original.As always, Cyan delivered excellent graphics and sound that immerse you in their worlds. Character facial details and animations are better than the Myst remake, but aren't on par with their tech demo from a few years ago (which was amazing but I wonder if it was too demanding for most systems). I only encountered 2 bugs overall (one skipped animation if repeated, and a glitchy book page turning animation). Neither was that big of a deal. Otherwise the game ran rock-solid.As a long-time Cyan / Myst / Riven fan, I give it two thumbs up!Can't wait to hear what Cyan is working on next!

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original game I have to say, it's a great game and a great remake (coming with some slight changes)The graphics are beautiful, it recreates the locations of the original faithfully and  makes them come to life.I really love the worldbuilding and storybuilding, have been for the original and do for this remake.It's a testimony to the original pre-rendered graphics that we only now get an accurate representation of a real-time rendered riven but oh does it look beautiful.Yes it changes details and puzzles from the original but at least for me those changes all seemed to serve to make the game more cohesive.The few puzzles I felt were a bit too much of a stretch in the original became easier while still retaining their character. _childDocuments_.review: This is how a remake should be done. _childDocuments_.review: One of the great modern remakes of a PC classic that actually adds to and enhances the original in a lot of surprising, smart, and fun ways. Even better than the Myst remake, which I also really enjoyed. A gorgeous and ear-pleasing experience in VR or not, I loved the visuals and music and sounds throughout. This game not only holds up but still stands as a shining example of puzzle, narrative, and world design that doesn't get copied and referenced nearly enough. You can really tell that Cyan is taking notes from modern games with some of their changes to the mechanics and level design to make playing Riven for the first time a much less confusing and more accessible experience. Definitely recommend picking up the Companion guide as well if you're not super confident in your deductive reasoning skills (like me) but still want to experience all the joys and friction this game has to offer. There are certainly some areas that could use improvement, like how unnoticeable certain important objects and paths are as well as some minor optimization issues (and I really miss the FMVs), but the problems are minimal and don't detract much at all from the overall experience. Figuring out the overarching puzzles and plot threads of Riven will almost certainly make you feel like a genius and look at the world a little differently than you did before. If you're a fan of walking sims and puzzle games, you simply have to play this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler-free review.What an amazing experience. Riven is a glorious sequel to Myst, and both these games will make you feel smart like no other game can. In both games you arrive into a place full of mystery. You get bits and pieces of information, and at first everything will be very confusing, and you will have no idea where you are, where you must go and what you should do. But eventually you start piecing everything together, solving puzzles, and the world will unravel before you. Stumbling around for hours like a blind kitten until everything clicks together and you figure out a way to move forward is extremely gratifying. The in-game screenshot & notes feature is a brilliant quality of life addition, but expect to still be required to take notes and make some napkin drawings to keep track of tips you discover. The visuals are stunning, the world and locations are gorgeous, and a pleasure to marvel at. Sound design and music are also on point.That's the good parts so far. Unfortunately, there are some downsides. The game's stability, particularly in VR mode, leaves something to be desired. I bought Riven on release and tried using it in VR right away, and the game would crash the moment I'd try moving around. Perhaps the issue was patched out since then, I haven't checked.In normal mode tha game would sometimes crash as well, but the auto save does a good job, and I never lost any progress. Performance ins't amazing either, moving around some locations caused hitches and frame drops, despite me having a *very* powerful gaming PC. On several occasions, my progress was stumped purely because some tips / interactable objects were not highlighted clearly enough. You can blame this on haste and lack of attentiveness, but I still think it's a legitimate problem. Probably caused by transitioning from the original frame-by-frame design of the game into a realtime 3d space.Another annoyance is traversal. Vast majority of playtime in this game is spent on moving around and between locations, and often the path between where you are and where you must go is convoluted, and requires multiple loading screens and waiting for painfully slow animations of interactable objects. If you enjoy puzzle games at all, I cannot recommend Riven enough, despite the technical issues and small gameplay annoyances.And do yourself a favor, and avoid cheating by looking at walkthroughs. Even if you're stumped and roam aimlessly for hours. Trust me, all of the game's puzzles can be figured out if you pay attention and think, with no need to look into outside sources. I cheated only once, and I regret it endlessly, because the answer was right before me, but I was impatient.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy "Myst like" adventure games, then this is  game you should not miss.RIVEN is, quite simply put, the greatest game that has ever been made. Full stop.Now, thanks to Cyan and The Starry Expanse Project, I get to relive this game anew after over 20 years.I've only just begun this remake, and have been impressed with it even more than I thought I would be. That is quite a feat considering my bias in feeling that this is, once again, the greatest game of all time. I've played every Myst game and read all the novels (many times), and deeply adore this franchise.I was concerned about the switch to 3D rendered characters in place of the old FMV sequences, but the team's care and attention to detail has laid my concerns to rest. The level of expression and detail in the character models absolutely fits the game's style, and look great.I look forward to experiencing the changes, a couple of which I've already noticed just in the first half hour of game-play, and exploring this delightfully well crafted world in full 3D.Thank you to the teams at Cyan and The Starry Expanse. A special thank you to Rand and Robyn Miller.Edit: Completed my first playthrough in ~9 hours. I maintain my opinion that this is a very well-crafted remake that is not only respectful of it's source, it enhances it.If you aren't familiar with RIVEN then it could easily (and likely will) take you longer to complete. I would have easily completed it in far less time had I not been taking my time to look at all the beautiful scenery, as well as the changes/additions to the puzzles. I don't even know how long I walked through and watched the butterflies on Jungle Island.I knew I was going to love this remake, but I am so grateful that it is even better than I anticipated.Potential Spoiler (Story not Puzzle spoiler): RIVEN (1997) was my favorite game of all time. How fitting that it took RIVEN (2024) to overtake it. My new favorite game, is a remake of the original. I couldn't have wished for more.Thank you again to everyone at Cyan and Starry Expanse.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely stunning reimagining of a puzzle game classic, this remake should be played by both newcomers and experienced Riven players, as it has something to offer to both.Riven has always been a uniquely striking virtual place, with memorable environments and a lonely, moody atmosphere. This remake plays to the strength of its engine and said environment is now better looking than ever, with added detail and ambiance, and the addition of the freelook camera and movement to offer a much more personal exploration feel.When the project was announced, one of my concerns regarded said freelook camera, as most puzzles in the original were helped by the static viewpoints, allowing to focus on the various mechanical moving parts, and not figuring out where they were at all. I was worried more freedom would make elements easier to miss, but those concerns have been laid to rest: most of the puzzles have been redesigned to account for the new visual and control scheme, and barring one or two exceptions, are extremely well suited to such a freeform exploration method.The game, overall, is more streamlined and accessible than the original, leaving aside some of its more esoteric elements, but it manages to capture the same core spirit. The feeling of learning a new counting system or figuring out the different parts of the single central enigma remains as strong as ever. In addition, the game smartly introduces new elements using the strength of its new presentation: let's just say the Star Fissure now ranks high in the Myst series memorable places. There are enough surprises and winks to make the journey enjoyable for Riven veterans, while the core experience remains an unmatched example of the genre for newer players.Whereas Myst itself has been regularly revisited throughout gaming history and has lost some of its sheen through its various remakes (effectively reducing it to a somewhat effective proof of concept), Riven has remained a more elusive experience, much like the universe it depicts. For the first time since its original release, we get to properly set foot on these islands again, and revisit them along with our memories, or for the first time at all for a new generation of players. And for both, it remains a towering giant, a fantastic example of mood setting, world building, lore writing, and puzzle solving. In short: (re)play it. Riven itself might be collapsing, but the game is as engaging as it's ever been.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m a big fan of the original Riven so I jumped on this new edition the moment it came out. It’s a lovingly made new version this time in three dimensions. A lot of work has gone into streamlining the puzzles and while that make it more welcoming to new players I do think some important aspects have been lost.For example there is a new inventory item that is introduced early in the game that takes something away from the game only being about observation. Some hints have been made more explicit and no longer require some essential deductions. Finally the newly introduced number system wasn’t used to its full extend in my playthrough. I could get away with only understanding parts of how it worked and the game never pushed me to understand all of it.This version has some additional story bits and I think I really enjoyed the additional detail. The way Riven combines the lore and puzzles remains unparalleled and I really do hope Cyan decides to continue developing new material in the Myst universe again.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven was one of the games that brought me and my best friend together as kids, 2 decades ago. We would spend hours poring over every inch of the game, trying to squeeze as much info out of the journals, taking notes on printer paper, and really pushing the tiny gears in our heads to try to figure out the solutions to what are truthfully some of the most difficult puzzles in the series.Last night, my friend and I finished playing the Riven remake together :) I can truthfully say that it is perhaps one of my happiest moments in gaming, and that's in no small part due to the love and care that Cyan has put into this remake.I still love the original Riven, but I will be the first to admit that it has some very rough edges. At times, its puzzles and solutions seem overly obtuse and contrived. It's a highly ambitious game held back by the technical constraints and design limitations of the time.The remake addresses all of that. The original locations and puzzles are all here, but have been much more fully realized. In many cases, small alterations have been made for better pacing. In other cases, entirely new mechanics, items, and points-of-interest have been added to more logically lead you towards the solutions of the game's most notorious puzzles. Locations that were under-utilized in the original have newfound purpose. None of it compromises the integrity of the original's vision, and all of it is tied together by an absolutely gorgeous graphical upgrade.Every change combines to create the definitive version of Riven. It feels like the game that Cyan always intended for us to have. It's a love letter to everybody who played the original, and a gift to anybody who never had the chance. This is, officially, my favourite in the Myst series, and it makes me dream of what would be possible if Exile, Revelations, or End of Ages were to receive a similar treatment.If I had to nitpick, my friend and I were ever so slightly disappointed in the quality of the character models and animations. They just don't quite manage to match the charm of the original's FMV scenes. The remake also maintains some of the "hidden in plain sight" puzzle solutions from the original that largely just rely on you being very attentive and thinking a bit outside the box, which at least to me have always been more frustrating than satisfying to figure out. But I would be lying if I said that these minor gripes really had any measurable impact on our enjoyment of this incredible game. It was a pleasure from start to finish, and I'm so glad my friend and I got to experience it all these years later. Thank you from the bottom of my heart to everybody who made this possible <3
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent retelling of the classic point-and-click game. This game provides a deep and rich adventure that is profound and engaging. It explores deep themes of how a tyrant builds power and how his power is challenged by a rebellious faction. Layered over the deep story and world-building is a vibrant and enticing world to explore.Cyan is a scrappy studio that produces works with profound artistry around environmental design, storytelling, and puzzle construction. Unfortunately, the low budget nature of the game does show, particularly with the polish of the 3D characters. Other features such as ray-tracing or path-tracing would be a good addition and help polish the visuals.Overall, it is still a masterwork in gaming and more games should pursue the environmental exploration and puzzle solving style of gameplay design. Hopefully, this game can be a guiding light away from heavy reliance on resource harvesting and crafting that is more common in modern adventure games.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr It's a pretty great remake of, arguably, the best puzzle game ever made. So yeah, buy it.This review contains no spoilers.I'm gonna open this review by disclosing that Riven (1997) has remained my #1 game of all time for most of my time on this planet, so this review is probably a little biased both in my praise and my criticism. But that also means i know this game like the back of my hand and I noticed every single change and put a lot of thought into my conclusions here. With that said:Riven (1997) is the best game ever made, and Riven (2024) is also pretty damn good for a lot of the same reasons. They are, however, not the same game. Besides the obvious technical advantage of making a game for hardware 25 years newer, Riven (2024) has a good number of things that are outright alterations or additions to the old game. Unlike the many Myst remakes over the years, Riven (2024) does  attempt to just be Riven (1997) in 3D. Instead, there are new areas added, new lore, and virtually  of the puzzles have been replaced with new puzzles. But, also very importantly, Riven (1997)'s fantastic visuals and music still remain, even prettier (in most aspects) now that the technology is 25 years newer. The final result is an updated and slightly expanded version of an already amazing game, which gives you... an amazing game.But Riven (2024) is not flawless. Riven (1997) suffers some downsides both because the game's technology is old and the game's puzzle design philosophy is old. Riven (2024), meanwhile, suffers a little because the game's technology and design philosophies are too . Riven (1997) was also a highly funded and published game, while Riven (2024) was done by an 100% indie Cyan (woo!) and some amazing work by the volunteers in the  team, but the budget was almost certainly smaller.On the technical side: Riven (1997) was highly limited by what home computers were capable of doing in 1997. The actual core artwork of Riven is practically flawless: Riven (1997)'s renders were made by a large team of well-funded artists using extremely powerful hardware and software to make cutting edge computer graphics. And then those absolutely spectacular renders were compressed down into 608x392 dithered images and some little quicktime videos (running  in rectangles above the still images) with a bitrate that might  a meg a second. And those tiny little pictures still managed to fill 5 CD-ROMs to bursting. Riven (1997) is an absolutely gorgeous achievement in computer art, and you gotta watch it through a little grimy window.So, how did they get around that in Riven (2024)? Now we're in Unreal Engine 5, an engine I don't like very much, but benefits from 25 years of advancements in computing. Both Talos Principle 2 and Riven (2024) suffer from a lot of the same UE5 problems, including framerates lower than what they really should be, really aggressive asset streaming that often breaks the immersion, and movement physics that are really not great. (If you've played a UE5 game you probably know what I mean, but you've almost certainly played a UE4 game, and UE4 had a similar but milder stink of its own.) However, UE5  looks pretty damn good, and you can bulldoze over any unoptimized software by just dumping more watts through your big green space heater. The result is a game that  has more visual fidelity with the same brilliant art direction, plus more freedom of movement than Riven (1997) could ever hope to achieve at the time. Now, instead of clicking through little pictures, you're walking around a pretty gorgeous island that looks a whole lot like the one you remember. But there were still things that prerendered graphics could do that you can't do by strapping a facebook phone to your skull, so some things have been lost, too. Some other subtle but noticeable downgrades and/or alterations have been made for the sake of VR compatibility and motion sickness prevention. There have also been a couple of small areas that are completely new, but only one of them has any sort of gameplay in it whatsoever, while the rest are pure (and very pretty) eye candy that you simply walk through once and then you're done. The good news is that virtually all of the problems I just mentioned are now patchable and may simply disappear by the time you read this review (I'm on day 1 patch right now), and you still end up with something that's pretty damn good.On the design side: Riven (1997) was /hard/. The puzzles were fantastic, but they pulled no punches. Riven (2024) has replaced all but a few minor puzzles with new ones that slot pretty seamlessly into the world and incorporate new content that expands the lore and the game itself. But they're easier puzzles for sure. And I don't have a problem with that at all: the old puzzles are still there to go play on the old game, which runs just fine on the current steam/gog version or through scummvm. I do, however, think the new puzzles don't integrate into the world quite as seamlessly as the old ones did. The new music /mostly/ fits in pretty well and is all pretty great, but there's one new song that doesn't quite fit the rest of the soundtrack. The new 3d animated characters are, naturally, worse actors than the literal amazing actors that did the 1997 FMVs, though the new voices are superb and John Keston remains a perfectly voice Gehn. The writing that has been replaced, both in journals and in dialogue, seems a little bit worse as well, but I find that a little harder for me to be objective about, so that point might just be my grumpy old man bias talking. But, still, you end up with something that's pretty damn good.(If anyone wants to talk specifics about any of the above points, that would require spoilers, but get in touch and I'll talk about Myst stuff all day any day)In the end, we have two versions of Riven, neither of which are perfect, but both of which are very very very good. And, importantly, Riven (2024) is far more accessible, both in its technology and its difficulty. Both games are definitely worth playing, but if you're reading this review because you're thinking about buying Riven (2024), do it. Buy it for your best friend too. You probably ought to play  or  first, but it's not a strict requirement.Cyan's still here and still producing gold, and Riven is a masterpiece that everyone should experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. It's been about 25 years since I played it, and I really only remember fragments of the original, certainly none of the puzzles, so it's been as though I played a brand-new game! Graphics are wonderful, and the puzzles are fun. Hoping Exile will be available (for macOS) someday!If I had to pick one nit, it's that the animated characters were not as pleasant to watch as the original, live-action ones. I suppose that's just the way it goes, and they weren't bad, but I prefer more realistic characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I play Riven in VR, revisiting it after playing it first in 1998 when I bought my first PC. The Myst series absolutely lend themselves to VR where you really are exploring the world. Hopefully the rest of the series will appear in the future. I confess to having bought into the series many years ago, so there is a degree of preaching to the converted.This is not a game for those who require constant action: there is a lot of thought, backtracking and note taking involved. You need to take your time and properly explore. I admit to consulting a crib sheet occasionally! The reward is that the gorgeous graphics allow me to enter a world that, certainly in VR, is as immersive as any I have come across, as near to 'being there' as you can get. The rides on the Riven transportation systems are fantastic! One proviso is that you need a reasonably powerful PC and high resolution headset. (I use Ryzen 9 5900x and Nvidia 4080 super with Vive Pro 2). Being able to easily play seated is a bonus for me due to arthritis and general back trouble. I hope others will get as much enjoyment out of the game as I am doing so at the moment. I do not know if Cyan representatives read these reviews, but I will make a couple of what I hope are constructive criticisms for future games of this type.  These specifically apply to VR which, unfortunately, much as I would wish otherwise, a niche market. The photo note system is not as good as that in 'Obduction'. Some form of easily accessible virtual keyboard note system would be welcome, after all, it rather spoils things to have to take off your headset to check clues. This, of course does not apply to playing in flat screen. Also, perhaps some further thought into optimising frame rate with high quality graphics: this was well managed with 'Half Life: Alyx'. I leave this to the coders.As stated, these are meant as constructive criticisms. If you enjoy the adventure game genre, then you must try this.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Game looks fantastic with an art style that oozes charm and feels very polished. The world building, story and lore really do wonders investing you in the world of Riven and its many secrets.The puzzles are incredibly well built, offering a solid challenge while also feeling like they have purpose for existing instead of just being there for the sake of gameplay.Being able to take screenshots is a welcome bonus though I still had a pen and paper to hand for when I needed to cross-reference the pictures.Multiple endings are pretty fun also.Cons (Might not be a con for you) Puzzles, while well designed, sometimes wont give their payout straight away and will combine with others later on. Sure the payoff then is absolutely euphoric but you may leave many areas feeling like you've missed something when you haven't and that can sour the victory a little.Backtracking downright sucks. It'll take you an age waiting for the train system to arrive, turn around and take you to the next island (can be sped up by setting vehicle comfort to comfortable in the options) only to repeat the process again because you need to get on a different train from that island to reach your destination. There's a fast travel machine that'll take you directly to your island of choice but even that takes a while with its two load zones and two minor puzzles you need to complete each time you want to use it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven was the first game I'd ever bought and it fostered a life-long love of puzzle games. The audio track still fills me with nostalgia and the steampunk / mechanical puzzle aesthetic is right up my alley. The Good:- Amazing graphics- The same atmospheric soundtrack- A fascinating world filled with puzzles and exploration.The Bad:- Game breaking VR bugs, I quickly had to switch to pancake as the VR is unplayable.- Poor optimisation leading to numerous stutters and texture popping. - I was sad that the characters had been replaced with CGI, I understand why it was done but it robbed the game of some of it's original charm.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: "Riven" used to be my favourite game when I played it over 20 years ago and it has never given up that status. But also, since that very first day I wandered through the world (well "clicking through" really), I was hoping that one day I could explore the islands walking around. Over the last decade, I've been occasionally following the Starry Expanse project, who had the aim of creating a sort of "Real Riven", always hoping it would one day bring me that possibility. And so I was over the moon when the original developer, Cyan, joined to finish this project.To be honest, I would have been fine with a 1-to-1 remake of the original, but what Cyan have done here has exceeded my expectations. I have to admit that I haven't finished it yet, but every change I encountered so far has been interesting in a good way. And it is strangely satisfying to stand in front of a door I've easily opened about a hundred times before, only to find myself being stuck now due to a different puzzle setup.Most importantly, back before the year 2000 while playing the original game, I got this unbelievable feeling of immersion in a computer game world, something I have never experienced that much since then. "Myst III" and "Myst IV", as well as "Obduction" had some very good moments, "Schizm" as well despite some subpar live acting videos and animations, and I also enjoyed games like "The Witness" or "Quern" or the "Portal" or "Talos Principle" series, but nothing came even close to the atmosphere and world building of "Riven". Today, I finally got that feeling back and that was extremely cool!There is one negative point that I should mention and that is the character animations. I know they are pretty decent, but nothing replaces the real video footage of the orginal game for me. Especially the intro to the game is missing some "punch" or urgency that the original had. But that's really just a minor issue.All in all, thank you Cyan for giving me back this amazing feeling of being there. It was worth the wait and I'm excited to see what you do next!EDIT: I have now finished the game, so I thought I could update my review as well. I am still extremely happy with the new version of the game. The graphics, sounds and immersion have set a very high bar for other games. I want to slightly take back my criticism of the character animations. I got more into them as the game went on and they are pretty acceptable. Still not as good as live action footage, but ok. Unfortunately, they do lack a bit of punch and urgency not only at the beginning but also at the end and that's a shame. Maybe an update could fix that slightly. But as an unexpected further plus point, there are new areas that you weren't able to access in the old version of the game, and being allowed to experiencing them now was such a nice treat! Obviously, I wish the world was five times the size, I could wander around for many more hours just getting lost in the world.Without spoilering too much (so I'll stay vague), I briefly want to have a look at the two major puzzles in the game and assess their significantly reworked versions.1) "Animal" puzzle: I was a huge fan of the old version. I have to say, though, that the reworked version is the new standard for me here. The way it is presented makes so much more sense now with the backstory of the Moiety. It made me appreciate their entire lore so much more. And that's all done without sacrificing complexity while staying fair. Big thumbs up!2) "Marble" puzzle: There were aspects of the old version I liked, but some bits felt slightly obscure for the sake of making it harder. Like the other puzzle, the reworked version lets some aspects make more sense with the backstory. But the aspect of placing the marbles could have been kept closer to the previous version. I find this too easy and fast, leading to the slightly dissapointing fact that one spends relatively little time on one of the islands because there is no need to.But all negative sounding points I raised are so small in comparison to the positive outcomes out of this reworked version. All in all, in a game that values the story of the world probably higher than just presenting puzzles, the changes for me made me fall in love with the whole world even more. If I hadn't given a thumbs up to this during my first review after only an hour of play time, I would do so now!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I never expected to see a fully-3D Riven remake, not just because the game is massive compared to Myst, but because the original 1997 Riven is still possibly the best-looking pre-rendered adventure game of all time, outdoing even its own sequels for just how believable each of its scenes look. The first thing I did when I booted up this remake in VR was let my jaw hang in awe at just how perfectly the very first area matched the original Riven's opening image 1:1 while giving me the ability to fully explore it.I'm not exaggerating when I say Riven may be the most important VR game since HL: Alyx. You can play this flatly, but it feels like VR was made for Riven, and vice versa. Either way, the only thing you're missing out on by playing the remake over the original are the (IMO) stellar live-action performances by Rand Miller and the late John Keston. What you get instead is a chance to experience a dark, diabolical narrative set in an expertly-crafted world in a whole new light.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most formative games of my youth and one I return to quite regularly, even if it's just to listen to the still incredible soundtrack by Robyn Miller. Riven is an absolute standout in the annals of gaming history as the overachieving if somewhat overlooked younger brother to Myst. It is exactly what the Empire Strikes back is to Star Wars or the Godfather II to the original. The superior sequel. It also has that unique bittersweet quality that some of the best things in life have: You can truly only experience them once. In trying to remake a classic, I think Cyan has made something special here. The people who developed this remake knew exactly what they were doing and who was going to buy this game. This IS Riven but it's a more self aware Riven that knows that some changes had to be made but they serve a dual purpose 1. to be more inviting to new players but 2. to change it up and surprise and delight returning players. No easy feat. They also absolutely NAILED the look of the original game. There are parts that look to my eyes like a cleaned up SGI render as if they brought back all the original models or uprezed original renders. It's just that good. They also kept much if not all of the original sound work which is absolutely iconic. While the music is much ballyhooed the sound design for Riven was pivotal in it's presentation.Praise be said, I do have some negatives:I had my doubts after playing the 3d remakes of Myst. Maybe its that you take your time a bit more to scan the information presented in each frame. Maybe its that your mind fills in the blanks with the limited information you're given forcing a more grandiose sense of the world. Maybe the faster pace of full traversal makes the world you're in feel a bit smaller. Or maybe it's some combination of all of these but something is lost in the jump to 3d and that feeling is definitely present here in this remake. It's something that I can't place my finger on but it's a definitely a sense I have. There's less atmosphere. Less of a feeling of solitude, or that you're being watched. Something feels missing.  Something inside me thinks "That's it?"Another bit of charm lost in the transition to realtime 3d is the character models. Seemingly seemingly a necessary evil the replacements are stiff and stilted. Worse, they have none of the charm of a Cyan hallmark that was even brought back for Obduction. Worse yet, in some instances they actively change the tone and pacing. A perfect highlight is the introduction sequence with Atrus, one I consider one of the best introductions to any piece of media, ever. The new version lacks the pacing and gravitas of the original and even comes off as somewhat jovial which is just the wrong tone. Here's a video that illustrates what I'm talking about so you can see for yourself: Lastly, some of the changes. I understand why some of the changes are there and in some areas they absolutely add to and deepen the experience. But in others, they feel like additions for the sake of additions. Change for changes sake. A perfect example of this is the area with the frog trap with the vent passage above on Boiler Island. I don't want to spoil anything and I know exactly why they changed that section but the new bit doesn't really much at all. It's essentially just a longer hall way. Granted, it's a very pretty hallway with a couple distractions. But it still serves exactly the same function. There's a ton more I can rant on but and I don't want to elaborate too much on the negatives because so much here is positive. It's amazing that they could get so close, or even nail something I think many have wanted for decades. The artists and game designers should be commended on their work. I hope they decide to make a brand new entry in the Myst series. One that picks up where Riven leaves off. If they can keep up the quality like they do here, I think it would be something special too.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is a first person point and click adventure where we solve puzzles and decipher cryptic codes across volcanic islands, each strewn with steam powered machinery and ancient artefacts. Set against the backdrop of a collapsing world held in the grip of Gehn, the game unfolds through a series of quests to free our protagonist, Catherine, from captivity. The narrative deepens as we interact with characters like Atrus and the rebellious Moeity faction, ultimately influencing multiple endings based on our choices. The scenery throughout is just mesmerising - from the metallic, polished domes to the rusted machinery and lush, verdant landscapes - every environment in Riven is crafted to evoke a sense of surreal, otherworldly beauty. The sky's vivid azure hue contrasts with the subtly artificial glow of warm interior lighting, creating a visual atmosphere that feels both familiar and completely unreal. Riven invites us to solve its mysteries at our own pace, immersing us in a world where every click is a step towards understanding.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I was a kid when I first played Riven. I was hooked for a long time, and the music stayed with me since then. I am now a father of 4, and when I started Riven remaster, it was the most beautiful slap in the face. So many memories came back at once. I knew the original game by heart, but I was surprised by all the changes. I knew where I was, but didn't know the solutions. Cyan has taken the best route for a remaster. Old players are delighted, and new players are now discovering this gem.My kids saw me play this, and participated in finding solutions to the puzzles. They were hooked by the music, the graphics and how they needed to think and use their eyes. Cyan, you have made an old fan happy, and 4 new little fans. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven 2024 is somehow just as incredible and engaging as it was 27 years ago. The things that are new and different almost universally fit as if they had been there all these years, while making it a fresh experience for someone like me who already remembers the puzzle solutions from the original. It looks amazing, it  right, and it all comes together to make an incredibly exciting game to play. If you loved the original, this will be as close as you could ever get to getting to re-experience it for the first time.The only thing that doesn't quite compare to the original is the character art and animation, but you're kind of in an impossible situation there. The FMV from the original game can't just be brought over, but you also can't get the kind of fidelity you'd need to rival FMV from 3D characters without an obscene budget and an army of people.My one and only actual complaint, which is present in the original game as well, is story-related. I have loved Riven for most of my life. It made a huge impact on me growing up, and stands out to me as the best of the Myst series. Riven 2024 lives up to that, and in my view stands side by side with the original as two of the best adventure games ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game I've been waiting for ever since real Myst came out. (~23 years ago)  The changes to the game, one in particular, really came unexpectedly and had me in a state of giddy-shock.  The effects and soundtrack are great as always.  This game always had that one unique visual look that I loved.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I remember not playing Riven until after having finished Exile. I had played MYST endlessly through several platforms: PC, Sega Saturn, etc. And I knew there was a sequel, but for some reason, I assumed it was just a cash grabbing, bad sequel, since in my head, nothing could top the first one. So, I never gave it a chance. I remember almost buying it for the Playstation, but even then, I didn't. So, after having been floored by Exile, and buying a brand new PC to be able to run it, I decided to go out and get a copy of RIVEN, and so it began...how one game became my favorite of all time, in over 4 decades of playing video games. I've played it all. Throughout my time picking up every console, and trying out every kind of game, I always came back to the bright and sunny world of the Fifth age. And of course, having seen MYST get a "Masterpiece Edition", and a realMYST, and a realMYST Masterpiece edition...those of us who were fans of Cyan worlds waited patiently for a RIVEN remaster of some sort. But it never came. And then the people at the Starry Expanse gave a glimmer of hope, but without much official word that it might be completed, or that it might get "picked up" by Cyan. All hope was not lost, but it was also not confirmed. But it's finally here. So, as a long time MYST fan, what is my final word?: 1. It is NOT a 1:1 recreation of RIVEN, so don't expect that. It's not a "remaster", but it's also not a remake. Probably what you'll hear a lot is the comparison of Resident Evil and their remakes. It is essentially the same game, but almost as if it's an alternate version of it. This is a great thing, because it gives not only a fresh coat of high resolution paint to our beloved game, but it's also a horrible thing because it adds and subtracts things that we were expecting, that were familiar to us, that we wanted. It's almost exaclty equally a good and a bad thing.2. Puzzles are slightly reworked...for some reason. I guess to keep the theme of "not just a fresh coat of paint" going. At times though, I felt this was unnecessary. Sure, some changes are welcome, because of modern gaming standards, and because of the "friendliness" to VR that it has to have. But again, for those veterans like us, there's almost no way to see it as "contrived" at times. 3. Some puzzles are entirely different. Again, I appreciate the effort of introducing brand new things. But again, it made me have a feeling of unfamiliarity that was unwelcome. It felt like coming home, to what you thought was a remodeling of your home, but there's a couple of important things missing, and there's something things and objects that weren't yours and were just added to your house, and you have to keep them and live with it. It feels "intrusive". 4. I do appreciate them winking at us Veteran MYST players a lot, with some puzzles, with some trophies, with some "occurrences" in the game. There's some specific nods that only "we" will get. It's nice to know that this is not just a game for new people, but that those of us who have stuck around for 26 years waiting for a remaster/remake are being acknowledged.I have 2 "uglies": - The endless glitches. Sure, these will be patched, as so far at the time of this writing, I believe we're on patch #2. But man, at times it feels so rushed. Especially if you think about the timeline from when we heard from Starry Expanse that they might be headed in that direction, and now it's only been a couple of years. Makes you think that we'd rather have had more time polishing it, than rushing it out the door.- Going full cg rendering for the characters, instead of reworking, reutilizing the old live action. This is a straight up "no" for me. It did not land AT ALL for me. It gave me trauma from the MYST V days, and I was hoping never to feel that way again. It looks SO OUTDATED - I'm not exagerrating, it looks like from the mid 2000's kind of graphics - except with 2023 resolution. So, pretty much MYST V, played on a high end PC with max settings. Sure, I appreciate keeping a lot of the voice acting from the late John Keston and Sheila Gould. And while I do see it as a nice way to pay homage, I couldn't help but think that to some, the thought "they did them dirty" might come to mind. I didn't think it was disrespectful, but I thought they could have done something else. Maybe AI upscaled the old footage, I don't know - something. Something ELSE other than going full CG. But I'm not surprised that CYAN went in that direction. It's just disappointing. I thought there was a little hope, with OBDUCTION. but FIRMAMENT cemented that they'll probably never give us live action again. So, is this what we've all been waiting for? For the most part, "sure". I don't think anyone will come out actually disappointed in it. I know some of us were JUST expecting a remaster/rework of the old one since, especially going back to play it on a big, modern screen - we can definitely tell that the graphics, and the resolution does NOT hold up after all this time. So, while this is not our "chance" to play the old RIVEN but with a brand new 4K fresh coast of paint, it is a good re-imagining that preserves MOST of what we loved about it.I AM glad they didn't just "reboot" it, and completely changed everything about to make it unrecognizable. I have RIVEN on my computer, on my phone, on my tablet. And I play it every now and then and have been for 26 years. I show it to new people, and enjoy seeing them experience it for the first time. But it's such a deep foundation of my time spent with games, that it begs the question: Will this game replace my playing of the old game?Street Fighter II CE completely replaced playing World Warrior. UMK3 completely replaced playing MK3. Sonic 3&K completely replaced playing Sonic 3. While this game is beautiful for the most part, and gives us things we never saw before (like finally going inside of Tay, something we were never able to do, until that one guy made the interior of it on Dreams, in that video on youtube). For me, I will never get rid of RIVEN (97) and will go back and visit it at some point in the future.But there's no denying that this is great accomplishment in its own right.

_childDocuments_.review: This is how you make a remaster. Keep the same feel of the original, but with modern tech. Change up puzzles add new areas to keep the veteran fans immersed. I always wondered what it would be like to visit Riven and peak around the corners you could only see in the background. Now I can, and it's gorgeous!

_childDocuments_.review: I played myst and riven as a kid, and without internet it was one of the coolest games I've ever played.  I was probably 8 or 9.  I "beat them" using strategy guides back then.  Now I'm 37, and nostalgia is heavy for Riven, which was my favorite out of the two (it looked so real back then!). I remember bits and pieces, but I know they've added things that aren't in the original, and so far it feels seamless and intuitive.  I get excited getting to a new area, and learning and discovering as the game intended.  The only negative I have is that it's a little clunky to get to the Notebook quickly when you want to quickly jot something down, but that's a very minor nitpick.  It's a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Following Myst (2021) i now also played through Riven for the first time. Again great story and visuals. Even a bit better than Myst imho. The world is beautiful. _childDocuments_.review: Coherent story line which encourages one to move on and adventure - the story line occupies the mind and draws you into the story as you observe and solve puzzles.Good nonlinear game play.Similar to but different from the previous Riven - greatly enjoyed both.Not a great fan of using plural pronouns when the singular is meant.Waiting for the next in the series ........

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable remake with a lot of clever updates, fun for fans of the original while also more accessible for first time players. I'm still disappointed they traded FMV acting for 3D models but I also get why they must have felt they had to. Hopefully future Cyan games keep up the FMV though like they did in Obduction :)I enjoyed the easter eggs and alterations to puzzles and paths through Riven too. One issue I had however was the game kept crashing during a particular travel transition - turning off vehicle travel animations for that one transition got me through it but hopefully it gets patched.

_childDocuments_.review: A reasonably faithful remaster of the original world, with enough changes to make it a new puzzle experience. The 3D actor replacements are good enough for VR at least, though the animation is a bit rough. Having played the original, the new puzzles slowed me down enough to get around 8 hours of play time, and I only got stuck once.
