_childDocuments_.review: This is how games should be remade. Riven is far more than just a modern copy of the original, it is a reimagining that improves upon the source material at every turn. The new puzzles are more intuitive and satisfying, the world building is even better than the original, and everything just looks gorgeous.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: When I heard that there was going to be a 3D remaster of Riven I was incredibly excited. Riven is a game that brings me right back to my childhood, gazing at the mesmerizing stained glass style art on the cardboard box and sleeves that contained it's 5 disks. I remember spending weeks stumped and roaming around the amazing world that Cyan had created, the deep and immersive lore is some of the most formative mythology of my childhood. I expected to load up this new remastered version and gawk at the stunning graphics, reminisce with my favorite objects and environments, breeze through the main puzzles (as I have essentially committed them all to memory and that which is not memorizable I could find very quickly), get goosebumps as the final cutscene plays, and call it a night. Seriously, I thought I could cruise through in one night. Boy was I wrong, and in the most amazing way.I had read that there would be extra puzzles, and I thought, "great!" What I had imagined was an extra switch on boiler island, a new path to go down to find some familiar clue, and the like. Well, I got that, and so much more. It is a really daunting task to take a game that is so beloved by so many, and is so furiously nostalgic to it's player base, and just change a whole bunch of it. The fact that it was such a massive success and provided hours of enjoyable gameplay to even a seasoned veteran Myst player is a true testament to the passion and care that was taken by the development team. The people who worked on this game love Riven, and that love saturates every pixel you encounter. This was not a cash grab, this was not a vanity project. This is what a remake should be. The core puzzles of the game have been reimagined and reimplemented so that the game is fun for both new and returning players. They fit seamlessly into the world, to the point where if you were playing it for the first time, you probably couldn't tell what was old and what was new. The new puzzles utilize the environment and lore with such masterful grace that has become the hallmark of Cyan games. They don't feel like cheap rip-offs of the original puzzles, and hit the sweet spot of challenging but not impenetrable. Many of the areas of the game are expanded and fleshed out. Previously inaccessible areas are opened up to the player for exploration. I was almost giddy when I, just for laughs, clicked on a door I knew could not be opened and it swung open. "Wait, I can walk around out here?!" It was so cool and so well done, it truly is like a love letter to the fans. Both the visual and sound design is stunning, just like the original. Words can barely describe the pure dopamine given by being able to experience one of your most cherished childhood fantasy worlds in full HD 3D environments. Some voice parts are re-done and others are preserved from the original (RIP John Keston) and both are fantastic. The music hits at the pit of your being like no other soundtrack can, "atmospheric" doesn't even come close to describing the level to which the music elevates this game. Again, pure gold.All together the remastered content is a tribute to the blood sweat and tears that were obviously poured into this game and the original. Alas, nothing is perfect. The flaws in this game are far below the threshold of significantly taking away from the experience. The live action FMV videos of the old game are replaced with CGI models which works.... about as well as could be expected. They don't quite succeed in climbing out of the uncanny valley, but it's understandable, the team really didn't have any other options and did the best with what they had. You spend very little of the game interacting with other people so it's only a footnote. Something that could be addressed is the occasional de-sync between the voices and the actors which is just a tad more distracting than is necessary. I saw a handful of rocks and set pieces just pop into existence, particularly while using the public transit available on Riven, and also had one or two crashes to desktop. That being said, warts and all, this is one of the best remastered games I've ever played.95/100Would link again.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: breathtakingly beautiful, with many of the sharp edges sanded off or replaced.the new puzzles and updates to existing puzzles all play really nicely and still present an engaging and sprawling challenge- even for those of us that are returning for the second or third time. In many ways the new puzzles make more sense as part off the world. I understand that designing engaging puzzles is incredibly challenging, but this team has absolutely nailed it.Visually, this is the best the game has ever looked, the textures are fantastic and combined with the sound design create an incredibly believable world. so many moments in this game you are confronted by some strange unknown object that is simultaneously completely believable- you know exactly what it would sound and feel like to tap on that giant rusted steel plate, and you feel that you could. this has always been Riven's greatest strength. if you love the original- buy this and play it, the updates are well done and make the game feel fresh. If you have never played- buy this version and play it, it will surely be the definitive version of a  wonderful game
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An ABSOLUTE TRIUMPH!!! The level of care and attention to detail put into this game is incredible--I am so grateful and relieved the team approached the redesign with the respect and care this sacred experience deserves. The original is an incredible achievement in of itself, and has a serious tone, but this redesign makes the game more colorful and fun.  It clarified and developed the larger concepts, but also smoothes out smaller experiences that were confusing or ambiguous in the original.  I loved learning more about the Rivenese culture in particular and also captures the spirit and visuals of the original. The main puzzles are a good mental exercise, but they are fair and quite fun.  I bought copies for friends.  THANK YOU THANK YOU CYAN!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Not just a remake, but a re-imagining.As someone who read the prequel books before diving into the original Riven on release (back in my Uni days... damn I'm old), this 2024 version hits all the right notes. It's faithful to the original without slavishly holding on to its more frustrating qualities, and it even elevates the game in some aspects.My only complaint is that I miss the original FMV performances, but I can see how there'd have been no way to integrate them into the 3D format.Word of warning: Some of the puzzle solutions are randomised on a per-player basis, so you can't just look up the solutions in a newsgroup like some of us did in the 90s...
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan really managed to re-capture the look and atmosphere of the original game, the textures look great, most of the sounds and music are identical, but that is certainly not a bad thing. Cyan, however, has chosen to make many changes to the game, and they end up as a bit of a mixed bag. I really appreciated them changing up the puzzles, even if some were a bit streamlined, but the addition of yet another number system feels like old hat at this point, they did it in the original game as well as Obduction, so I suppose it has become their gimmick. I also enjoyed the extra lore additions, like harvesting a fire marble, showing how Gehn went about making them for his own uses, and some other stuff I won't spoil here.The FMVs have been replaced with 3D actors which is of course understandable, and they look much, much better than what they did for the Myst remake which ultimately added an option to restore the old FMVs for that. The issue with the 3D models is the animation quality is not terrible, but also just not great, but at the end of the day this is a minor nitpick in a game where you interact with other characters only a select few times. Sadly, Cyan has repeated another shortcoming and left the keybinds unable to be rebound, also there's no indication in the default keys that pressing R is a very handy shortcut to bring up the Moiety lens, a tool you will often use, I happened to read that elsewhere. I was happy to see that you can set the cursor to automatically disappear when you're exploring and only appear when you want it to for interacting with things. All in all, it's a solid remake, it looks  great, but you may or may not like the changes they made if you're a big fan of the original game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan and the Starry Expanse fan game team have done it! Riven is back, bigger, prettier, and crazier than ever!Don't make the mistake of expecting a carbon copy of the original game - new and expanded puzzles, a few familiar challenges, lore tweaks, and other things that Rand himself approved of await.No, I'm not gonna spoil anything for first timers.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was and is a huge fan of the original Myst games, I can safely say that this remake is both true to the original and confidently unique from it. The two central puzzles (finding the Moiety, reaching the 233rd Age) are brilliantly reimagined while retaining the soul of the original puzzles. The art direction is remarkably faithful to the original; I frequently found myself experiencing deja vu. Occasionally there would be some distracting pop-in and weird animation issues, especially clipping and jerkiness with the human characters. But in the face of everything this game does well, these are minor complaints.I can't help but think this remake is the true realization of the creators' original vision. The 1997 version is undoubtedly a triumph in its own right, but this version is proof that the substance of the game is timeless. And it really is timeless; with its rich lore, challenging puzzles, delightful visuals and stellar sound design, Riven reasserts itself as a paragon of the puzzle game genre.Wow this reads like a game journalist review lol i just really love this game
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It seems like it has potential and it revives the MYST feeling, but in some technical aspects it felt unfinished.after playing for ~1,5h i got pushed out of the walkable area and was stuck out of bounds. Falling out of the map didn't reset me and the last autosave was out of bounds with no way back in. Since the "reset to last checkpoint" option just did not work i gave up on the game for now because i dont want to start the game from scratch again. Maybe i'll come back to it after some patches.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Coming back to Riven on Steam Deck while traveling overseas, and then again in Steam VR after I got home, I can say that it has exceeded my expectations. The environments are immersive and captivating. The experience of exploring the ages again, this time with my young niece by my side was a wonderful time. The rides are so much fun. Getting to look around on the rides in VR is the best part. Definitely use a good chair for a proper experience. Loved all the small minutia and grand events and sights that make the world feel lived in and hint at its rich history. Riven is definitely worth exploring again.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm quite pleased and impressed by how well Cyan pulled this one off. Also as an old-school fan with high expectations I'm mostly pleased. The puzzles are still some of the best in this genre, and the game environments look  at their max settings and the atmosphere of this game is as magical as ever. I did not play this in VR, however this game made me consider buying a headset (!), it was that gorgeous to me at times.If you like puzzle, deduction and exploration games, or have enjoyed games similar to those of the Myst series before, then this will likely be a ! To me, Riven is the peak example of how you should go about incorporating world design with puzzle design in a game. The puzzles are moderate to quite challenging, but not such infamous brain teasers as they were in the original version.This game is more of a 're-imagining' than a strict 'remaster' of the original Riven. So be aware that this is not a 1-to-1 version of the original game's experience, more like a 'director's cut'. Besides the changes resulting from the impressive graphical uplift into true 3D, there are changes and additions to the world and its puzzles. Most of these feel welcome to me as attempts to either flesh out the world more, improve on the game's progression and puzzle designs or to make the game more approachable to a modern audience. In the end I think these were all mostly good and well thought-out changes, and to me they never undermine the original game.Lastly to give one criticism of the game, I have to mention the quality of the characters and their animations. The voiced dialog is still the same great dialog from the original game, but all of the original game's live action recordings have been repurposed into 3D animated characters. These characters unfortunately come of as simplistic, flat-looking and oddly cartoon'ish in their detail and design-style next to the hyper realistic 3D world of Riven. They feel out of place and poorly implemented. Thus I feel like this might have been some sort of technical trade-off or compromise by Cyan, and it is sad how poorly the original actors performances has been maintained. A lot of depth and emotion is no longer visible or properly conveyed on the characters faces during their monologues. Not to speak of the sometimes poorly synced or keyed animations to the dialog itself.There are also new performances that show character quality and animation that are leaps and bounds better, having clearly been motion-captured through some other workflow; and they look AMAZING. I just wish all characters had this level of detail during their monologues. So, it's painful to see that Cyan didn't manage to preserve the performance of the original actors to a similar level. I hope that this is something they can, and decide, to improve upon.Otherwise I had a great time with the game. It ran well for me, it looked amazing (for the most part) and threw in some unsuspected and delightful changes and additions to a real gem and masterpiece of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This remake perfectly captures the feeling of playing the original Riven back in the 90s - both the joys and the frustrations. Playing the original now is rough because games have developed so much over the years, and that old interface (and the graphics which were once astonishing for the time) just haven't aged well. The remake is beautiful, controls well for the most part, and provides the same joy of discovery without the need to swap CDs every five minutes.One important tip: DO NOT RELY ON THE IN-GAME SCREENSHOTS TO TAKE YOUR NOTES. The screenshots are not of good enough quality and sometimes the information you need is not visible in them! I learned this the hard way at one of the final puzzles in the game. I'd taken screenshots of several things I knew for sure would be important, only to discover that the symbols I needed to see where not visible at all. I then had to spend ten minutes traveling back to the location I'd screenshotted to check the clues again. If you think something is important, WRITE IT DOWN IN A NOTEBOOK. It was disappointing to realize this potentially helpful feature wasn't really functional.The puzzles are for the most part not too difficult if you pay close attention and note down details in the environment. I'm not sure if this one is easier than the original or if I've just gotten a bit cleverer as I've aged, but I didn't need to consult any walkthroughs to get the best ending (whereas I relied on walkthroughs for pretty much the whole original game back when I was a teenager).Be prepared to be patient, however. Where the transport between areas was once a point to swap discs, now they are long cutscenes which I presume are used as fancy loading screens for each area. Riven is made to feel like a world you're actually inhabiting, which means there is no fast travel. If you forgot to write something down on the other end of the map, you'll just have to travel back there (although there are some settings which can reduce some of the animations, at least). Players used to modern games streamlining the process of getting around might be frustrated by this, so go into the game prepared for it.The only other disappointment I felt was in the character animations. I understand that using FMV wouldn't be an option for a remake of this style, and so 3D models were probably their only feasible option, but the animations for the characters are just awful, and not nearly as realistic as the environment surrounding them. Still, these are a very small part of the game, and hardly a deal breaker.Congratulations to the team who remade this classic game. I was ready to be disappointed, but you really nailed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy remake of a wonderful game.For fans of the Myst series, there is nothing better than finally being able to explore more of the enigmatic worlds that made the series so successful. This is the game we imagined back in the day when it came on 5 cds.If you're unfamiliar with the series, you do not need to play Myst first, though doing so will enhance your experience. The puzzles are challenging, though slightly easier than the original. Because the game is now 3d, they can't reuse the old FMVs from the original, and they've been replaced with passable 3d models. The voice acting is still intact.Fans of Myst and Riven will be happy with this. First time players may experience a little bit of confusion, but that's almost the signature of narrative puzzle games. Especially Myst games...it's the experience falling into a starry expanse...
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I am absolutely blown away by the work this team has put in.  I remember playing the original Myst when it came out and from then on footage of the others games, learning the story of the D'ni race, Atrus, Catherine, and so much more.  The visuals are gorgeous and breathtaking, the puzzles hard enough to be challenging but not controller throwing difficult, and the music and sound design, velvet to the ears!   If you are a fan of the originals, love puzzle games, or just want something to enjoy while you can relax with beautiful scenery WHILE engaging your mind at the same time, check out Riven and you won't be disappointed.  After all there are many ages, yet infinite truths...
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original was one of the first video games I ever played. This remake brings back all the magic I experienced as a child. I thought the puzzles might be easier now playing as an adult... but I was wrong and I'm glad. Incredible world, an extremely immersive game, and an absolute masterpiece. Please make more games like Riven!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely beautiful game. It has such an atmosphere that's hard to describe but so wonderfully present everywhere in the game. I love that the game is very deliberately paced. And the architecture is so intriguing and upfront! 9/10.My only gripe is a functional one - you can't rebind keys, and I'm a WERD player instead of WASD. It's very easily fixed by using the Keyboard Manager in Microsoft's PowerToys, so you can hard-rebind keys while playing the game.Once again, a masterpiece. I'm thankful for Cyan's revival.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I remember as a kid seeing the Riven box on my dads work/computer desk. I knew he didn't play games so I installed it at night when he wasn't in the office and remember it feeling like I took a secret journey to another world. I later found out it was a gift for my birthday. Riven has always played a special part by introducing me to PC gaming, and also unlocking my imagination in ways I never knew. Thanks Cyan.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful in VR, if very demanding. Turn off DLSS (or it will be blurry) and check the comfort settings before you start.I've replayed MYST too often, but never Riven. I remember so little of it. It's wonderful to experience the world as a real space. Everything makes a lot more sense. Controls are a little fussy, like grabbing and turning things, turning book pages. Books: Hold it with one hand. With the other hand, point at the edge of the open book - right at the stacked pages - until that hand turns red, then grab and drag all the way to the other side of the book.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is mysterious, treacherous, yet beautiful. A world and civilization on the brink of collapse, torn apart by family conflict and a madman intent on making himself into a god.Picks up right where the first game in the series, Myst, left off, but if you'd like to start here, then the brief journal Atrus gives you at the beginning will explain everything you need to know. There is a prequel novel, Myst: The Book of Atrus, that I greatly enjoyed as a Myst fan but is optional for playing Riven, and arguably might be more enjoyable after playing both games.This is a remake of the 1997 game by the same designers, expanding on it in thoughtful ways but maintaining the strange yet familiar atmosphere that made the original so unforgettable. It is difficult but satisfying to puzzle your way through the islands of Riven, where an understanding of the world, factions, and characters is your greatest tool in making progress.A masterpiece, and the best game I've played all year.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan did it! They made a remake of the best puzzle game ever and one of my favourite games of all time, and made it even better. Riven remake is a perfect example of how to improve on an already great original, staying true to old fans while capturing new ones. Since I've played through the original several times I thought this was going to be a great nostalgic time experiencing the world in 3D, otherwise just running through the puzzles, but what a pleasant surprise I was in for. Do yourself a favour and get lost in one of the most captivating game worlds there ever was.Thank you Cyan!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful remaster! Original Riven players will find new twists to an otherwise familiar world. Much of it will be as you remember, but relying too much on past playthroughs will be its own trap.If you're new to Riven, grab a pen and notebook, and settle in for an evening of exploration that culminates into one grand puzzle.  My only Cons with the game is that I wish some parts moved a bit faster to cut down on 'waiting'.Pros: I loved being able to fully explore the world of Riven in full 3D, including some expansion on old material.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: From watching my brother play this weird game called Myst on his Playstation, to playing through Myst 3 on the Xbox, to the Ages Beyond Myst where you are you, to the revelations of Myst 4, to catching up on Gametap with RealMyst, Riven, and the return of Myst Online, to the End of Ages of Myst 5. Riven was never my favorite, but after playing the demo I had to buy it. Upon contemplation I realized a psychosomatic like thing where I realized that the name of the game is what averted me from picking it up, and if they had titled the game Myst 2 I would have been all over it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The team somehow managed to capture the feeling of playing it again for the first time. What an amazing job they did on this remake. The lore feels rich and immersive, and the puzzles are fresh and exciting. If you played the original, there are little easter eggs all over for you to appreciate, but the game stands well alone by itself as well so if you have never played a Myst game before, you can still jump in and enjoy all Riven has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a nostalgia trip. I remember hours of being about 7 and trying to help my mother solve the puzzles. Now being able to enjoy the same game in updated graphics is amazing. I have always loved this series and being able to enjoy it again and being able to experience it again like its the first time is again amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Lousy remakes that overpromise and underdeliver are a dime a dozen these days. Unlike those, *this* is how you remake your game. Bluntly speaking, other than one or two nitpicks about the intro, this is an upgrade to every part of the game in nearly every way. Moving through Riven had me asking myself if it was a fever dream, so many areas are the spitting image of the 2D slides of the original, and clearly much thought and effort went into translating everything into a real 3D space. Not to mention the sheer number of revisions for lore accuracy and realism/immersion, and the expansion of underdeveloped parts of the story.And it released stable and mostly bug free, not to mention decently well optimized. I've played nearly every game Cyan has put out and own multiple copies of several, including physicals from decades ago, and this one is a big winner. You guys improved the masterpiece, and it was probably the closest I'll ever get to playing Riven again for the first time. Thank you for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I have a ton of nostalgia for the original game, but seeing as I was only 10 years old, I probably didn't appreciate (or understand) the game that well in 1997.  Immersing myself in the writing and the lore of this remake was an absolute joy. I was similarly engrossed as when I was playing outer wilds. That is probably still accurate of the original game, but the remake goes so far above and beyond my expectations, I was thrilled.  Even as a fan that remembered so much of the original, the remake does a great job of subverting expectation around every corner.  I had so many "Oh WHAAAT?!" moments when I found something new or when I realized I could further explore a previously closed-off area.  Pros: The visuals are absolutely fantastic, great new puzzle designs, really cool additional new areas.  The sound design, music, and atmosphere are faithful to the original and top notchCons: I really felt the animated characters jarringly broke my immersion, the rest of the game honestly looks so real that the animated characters stand out in a really poor way.  The performance is overall pretty good, but I had a lot of stuttering of the frame rate, some pop-in here and there, and one hard crash.  Performance could use a few patches but It's perfectly playable as is.  Overall, very happy with the remake.  It's gorgeous, nostalgic, intuitive, immersive, and very faithful to the original while making excellent new changes.  Highly recommended from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played Myst or Riven. There is no way this slog is worth 30+ € without some hardcore nostalgia to keep you going.The main problem is that the game does not respect your time. Think you missed something in a place you visited previously? Good luck hiking for 10 minutes through various "quick travel" systems to get there. Wait 30 seconds for a cart to come to you after calling it with a button. Wait 10 seconds for a door to close while you can't even see it, because you're control-locked staring forward at something you can't interact with yet. Oh, there wasn't anything to that hunch of yours after all? Well, time to hold down shift (because of course there is no toggle for running) for another 10 min wading through the world and staring at the same unskippable animations! This is not immersion, it's boredom.The puzzles aren't that good in and of themselves anyway, but their cryptic and sometimes pixel-hunting nature combined with the absolute drudgery of getting around the world ruin what satisfaction solving them could have brought.Unless you are in it for the nostalgia, don't play this. There are better (equally obscure and cryptic) puzzle games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Faithful to the source while still feeling fresh. I was worried at first this would be a tedious retread of what I already knew, but things have changed in this Riven, and discovering its secrets was genuinely thrilling at every breakthrough. It's like revisiting a place in your dreams, knowing it's different to the last time. I thought Myst III was my favourite in the series, and Riven would remain that haunting, elusive, 5-CD labyrinth from my childhood. The deeper into this Riven I have gone though, the more I'm convinced it hasn't been topped, much as I still love Myst III. The aesthetics of the design, the music, and the gorgeous visuals are absolutely iconic, and unravelling mystery upon mystery is immensely satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible remake. Expands on the original in thoughtful and surprising ways while always respecting the tone and authenticity of the world. The puzzles are cleverly changed and all the additions and alterations work together to improve the game and flesh out the lore.The animated characters and some visual areas of the game are not executed as well as the original, but these are minor shortcomings in what is one of the best remakes I've ever played. If you love the original you'll love this, and if you're new, you're in for an amazing journey through one of the most compelling and well crafted game worlds ever created.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It is a master piece in environmental puzzle.  Played the original when I was younger a long time ago and it still hold up to the memory.  Puzzle have a different solution and some puzzle have been greatly improve.  The notebook is a great addition in those kind of game put accessing it via the pause menu takes time. I would suggest playing with a pen and paper along side. It is not mandatory to have played the original Myst but I would strongly suggest playing it before.   It gives explanation and is a good introduction to the kind of puzzle.  I would strongly recommend.  Be patient with it and don't fear to  look at hint or the original but try to avoid spoiling yourself the solution to puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I was curious to see how much better Riven could be with a powerful PC driving it (13900 and RTX4080).  Since it was already attached, I first tried Riven with my Oculus Rift S, and while it was certainly better than the Quest version it was still lacking that “knockout punch” to set itself apart from recent competition in the VR space.  Most of the technical issues were eliminated or reduced playing with the SteamVR version, but I had forgotten about the Rift’s screen door effect that was blatantly obvious given the generally flat shaded nature of Riven’s art in VR.  Switching back to my Quest 3 and using Steam Link to wirelessly connect to my PC offered me the best possible results of all my VR solutions, giving me stable technical performance and the best color and visual clarity.  I was shocked at just how different the same game looked and played on the same headset based on which version/store it was purchased.Unknowingly, throughout all my testing I had been slowly getting better and better quality, but when I stowed the goggles and sat back to enjoy the game on a 77” OLED in full 4K it was like stepping into a new world.  As transformative as experiencing Riven in VR can be, playing it on a high-end PC at full Epic settings in 4K is often beyond words and even screenshots.  What we all thought was photo-real back in 1997 was just a hint at the expansive 3D island chain Cyan Worlds has created today using Unreal 5; while not even tapping into the advanced feature set you would expect for an outdoorsy game such as this.  Seeing Riven running all-out can easily bring tears to your eyes – or maybe that’s me just not blinking – but rest assured this is not your dad’s (or granddad’s) Riven.Read full review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan worlds are the GOAT's of old school, intelligent puzzle games - creating some of the most awe inspiring environments to grace a screen across so many of their games (personal favs being Myst, Myst 5 & Obduction).  In remaking Riven, this has solidified this fantastic games' place in the 21st century and this is a brilliant example of how to bring a game nearly 30 years forward in time.  Amazing job guys, keep it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Just binged the whole game. Had a big, stupid grin on my face the whole time. Loved all the changes they made to the puzzles; it felt like playing a whole new game in a deeply familiar setting. The new narrative, content, and extra areas they added all made it feel fresh and exciting to explore as well. Can not recommend this game enough to both fans of the original and the uninitiated alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original Riven on launch in 1997. Like Myst, the world built by the team at Cyan has always stayed with me. A fantastical and tangible place that no game has really managed to create since. Both Myst and Riven truly are masterpieces, a word that is now sadly over used.At the time my friends and I dreamed of being able to actually walk around the world of Riven in real-time. Just imagine if this incredible world could be explored like other 3D games?Well here we are, 27 years later, and it has absolutely been worth every year I've had to wait.This Riven remaster has absolutely shattered, and I mean SHATTERED, my expectations. It's utterly captivating and mesmerising. The puzzles are more accessible and I just love being in the world.I hope the team at Cyan get the opportunity to release Myst again using all the UE5 technology on display in Riven. I also hope that Exile gets this treatment as well. I feel so fortunate to be able to explore this world with the graphics I always imagined would be impossible. It's truly wonderful to be alive and to be a gamer right now. THANK YOU Cyan.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 2:  The crash in the submarine when playing VR seems to be fixed!EDIT 1:  Looks like a lot of heart is going into the updates and there may be a fix in the latest patch for the VR crashes I was experiencing.  I haven't had a chance to review it yet, but will change this to positive with the hope that it is indeed fixed.===== ORIGINAL POST ====My time is precious.  In fact, everyone's is.  That's why when I sit down for an hour or two to play a game on the weekend, it needs to just work.THIS game crashes in VR a lot.  Especially when using the submarine, but it has happened to me in other places as well.  It's just super reproducible in the submarine.  What do you have to do a lot when a game is crashing?  Re-load the game.  That brings me to my second point... the load time is way too long.  Probably 50% of that is just sitting and waiting for the Cyan logo / animation to finish.  How is that not skippable?  Any time that is not spent loading should be skippable!Aside from crashes, the VR performance is a C+ at best.  Lots of stutter, pop-in, and weird shadow effects.  I'm on a 3080 with 64 gigs of ram, Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700K CPU @ 4.00GHz  ....  Should be fine.Other than that my other gripes are that this is mostly just a port.  There's none of the things you expect in VR like hand interactions (they just move through everything)... no full body support ... no physics interactions etc.Lastly, from a perspective there are a lot of rough edges.  Music transitions are abrupt.  Not enough music and ambient noise to build atmosphere.  On the plus side the graphics are good, the puzzles are fun, and of course the story is interesting.I should add that I fully understand that this is a small team and frankly, this would be a positive review if it weren't for the crashes.  It's just that even with a positive review, there would be some negatives that I listed above.  All in all, I appreciate that the game was made and will change this to a positive review if the VR crashes are fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an absolute masterpiece (pun intended) and I hope that everyone had as much fun as I did with this.I had played Riven The Sequel to Myst years ago on my PS3 using the PS1 disc back in 2012 since I had discovered Myst and was absolutely obsessed with it. I bought every game in the series on disc at the time.I even had them sent to my home under the name "The Stranger." XDI love the series and I hope we get a remake of III, IV, and V at some point, but I only want that to happen if they have the passion to do so. If they don't feel like it, that that makes sense.This game put into Real-Time graphics what I imagined it would look like with those pre-rendered pictures and FMV sequences. It is so detailed and runs very well on my computer.I think the eye/head tracking for the NPCs is especially astonishingly intimate and immersive. I personally don't mind the 3D NPCs because the look good to me.The ones in the newest iteration of Myst look very off, but these look totally fine to me.I love the environments and I believe the changes made here and there to the locales and puzzles alike are not just understandable, but welcome. It breathes fresh air into the remake while keeping enough of the old game to appease fans of the 1997 release.Please do yourself a favor and buy this game. I was lucky enough to get it for a discount upon a discount since I already owned the most recent Myst remake.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A simply amazing remake to one of my all time favorite games since I was a child. My only small complaint I have is the the change of the . Over all, it's obviously a must play for any Myst and Riven fan for those long time players or those just now starting to discover these games. And as always, the ending has truly yet to be written.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: 'Riven has seen Cyan Worlds use what is possible with current day tech to give their classic title from 1997 a new lease of life, and they have done this successfully again following the same treatment being given to Myst in 2021. Bringing it with it some of the most challenging puzzles I have ever faced, which are designed perfectly for both flastscreen and Virtual Reality. With the world of Riven looking truly stunning and a pleasure to explore as you work out the puzzles. Cyan Worlds are doing great with bringing the best and most taxing puzzle games to VR. Where the puzzles do get difficult, when you solve them you see how fantastically they are designed, for this reason any puzzle game fans should add Riven to their library as soon as possible.'Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed Riven 2024 yesterday, and it's worth checking out and revisiting again if your a fan of Cyan and puzzle games. I've done 2 play-throughs of Riven prior, once when it first came out and second right before Exile as a refresher pass. And let me tell you this version might be my favorite. I was hesitant because the unreal engine games usually gives me motion sickness, couldn't play Obduction because of it. With this version's options and acceptability settings, I can finally play Cyan games again. Lowering the frame rate, Field of view and allowing for ladder skips really helped with this. New puzzles and, for the sake of spoilers I'll just say "new additions" to the game kept me on my toes. It's Riven like you know it, but it's not your same carbon copy of the 1997 game. I did miss the real-time acting from the actor's emotions to sell some of the story plots. But I get it. The game needed 3D models for this version to work.  There were some bugs as to be expected, I clipped out of bounds in the Jungle and some popping in and out, having saving check points was necessary. Over all, I really liked this game and it makes me want to jump into Exile to do a another playthrough. Thank you Cyan for making games with this much attention to detail, and care for solution logic puzzle-solving fans like myself.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Dream come true, as someone who's been into the Myst series ever since I was a kid.The thing with this game is I would've been completely content with a 1:1 remake of Riven, if it meant I could play it in VR. Not only do I get to play Riven in VR, but they went above and beyond with the changes and new content they've added.Kudos to The Starry Expanse Project and Cyan themselves for a decade's worth of dedication and effort in making this possible. This is now my favorite VR title.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I've never actually played the original Riven or Myst, but I picked up both of their remakes in the Steam sale. Having now experienced both, while Myst is definitely one of those "play it for the historical significance" games, Riven's design philosophy really does hold up today. It's a game that does atmosphere and environmental story-telling incredibly well, and while its pacing and payoffs are a little too heavily skewed towards the tail-end of the game, I still really enjoyed finally getting to see why this title's considered such a classic. Myst is a game about solving puzzles, but Riven is a game about being trapped inside one.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original was one of my favourite games, and at first I must admit I wasn't too keen on there being changes between this and the original. It didn't take me long to overcome this feeling and fall in love with the world all over again. I think most of the differences either made the game tighter or else added interesting new areas to explore, and in at least one case both. The new puzzles were fun to solve - something I was unable to do the first time around without a walkthrough. Whether that means they are easier or I'm simply more accustomed to the world and the type of puzzles it can throw at you I'm not sure, though I suspect a bit of both. Either way it was a lovely experience which I definitely recommend to anyone who is a fan of deeply immersive worlds.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible remake for new and old fans alike. The refactored puzzles were an absolute thrill to work through, journal and pen in hands, just like the original. The best part is (minor) lore changes and additions which makes the islands feel more lived in and practical. And then there's the new fanservice for die-hard Myst fans. I wish series like Zelda could pay off like Myst has over the years.10/10 and I haven't even tried VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best adventure / puzzle games of all time. A lovingly crafted remaster and remake that fully recaptures the spirit of the 1997 classic while adding some great quality of life features. Play without a guide if possible for one of the most immersive and rewarding puzzle experiences in gaming.Pros:- A masterful puzzle game that is genuinely clever, intricately designed, immaculate- Score worth playing on repeat, sound work is phenomenal, the best creaky board sounds in the business- Gorgeous art direction- In-game notebook so you can take a million pictures and forget everything anyway- Some randomized puzzle elements make brute-forcing impossible (brainlets in SHAMBLES)- No guidance, forcing you to think and make connections between areas that can be stimulating and full of brain expansion momentsCons:- No guidance, forcing you to think and make connections to a point that can sometimes feel punishing to the point of brain implosion moments- Navigation is slow, sprint toggle please, making the mandatory backtracking such a chore I wish to throw myself into the Starry Expanse- Confusing ending structure, easy to get a doo doo ending and have to replay a lot, good option would be to have a "point of no return" notice- One cutscene feels longer than church, skip please- Crusty FMV characters removed in favor of, let's just say, very not great looking CG models.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic remake of the original game from 1997. This isn't a 1 to 1 remaster, but rather Cyan decided to go full 3D and include a decent VR mode as well. Additionally they decided to replace or reconfigure puzzles so even for old fans there will be surprises. Also randomization is built in so there is replay value.Difficult puzzle game especially if you haven't tried anything in the Myst series before. It is ok to look for hints, I know I did.Some tips: Use ingame screenshots for note taking (press X on keyboard), and if you're on keyboard pressing R will bring the most recent inventory item back to your hands. I wish I knew that during my first playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remake and not a remaster, but it's still Riven. The worst part of the game is not being able to click super fast to zoom around. PC mode is beautiful even if it turns my machine into a furnace. VR needs control improvements, it's not consistent in how you can interact with ladders, and some of the puzzles are restrictive in how you have to interact with them.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's Riven, it's beautiful, it's immersive. Makes me want to get a VR set to experience it. One minor letdown is the character models vs. the original full motion video. I get why they did it since you have full movement, but it was jarring since I vividly remember the original. Still, I can overlook that because the rest of it is so amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having an absolute blast, but I took a break to come and report that Riven is great in VR on the Valve Index. I have wanted to play a Cyan game in VR for a long time, but the last few VR games they released had critical, game breaking flaws on the Index. I haven't been able to find any here, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I deliberated a lot before choosing 'no'. In the end, I decided that what I have to say would be more useful to someone checking why they might NOT enjoy it.Riven, even in its 2024 incarnation, is like a really old, really good, really old movie. Something with Gene Hackman and lots of saxophone and brushed hi-hats. The kind of movie where maybe three things happen over the course of two and a half hours. It's been remastered in 4K Dolby Atmos, but at the end of the day it's still two and a half hours of Gene Hackman.Aesthetically, it's delicious. It has that balmy Mediterranean ambience that I loved in AC: Odyssey and ICO, and it's a really nice place to spend time. The writing and story is excellent, it's woven into the world and presented from different perspectives most effectively. If you're here for the story and want to pore over journals and really look at the world and think about what it's telling you about that story, you're going to love it. I should imagine it's also a wonderful VR experience if you are so equipped.On the other hand, if you're looking for another Talos Principle or The Witness - if you're looking for an actual puzzle game - maybe wait until there's a sale. There are relatively few true puzzles in Riven; often the 'puzzle' is realising that there's another way you can exit an area, or looking around for the one button/lever/wheel to progress. There are only two puzzles worthy of the name, and they're so much more spread out and difficult than the rest that it can feel like hitting a wall. Compared to the best examples of, say, web-based point-and-click adventures over the last decade, Riven felt a bit thin.Also - guys, we're nearly a quarter of the way through the century, and I'm not getting any less left-handed as time passes. Where the hell is my key rebinding screen?Minor gripes: while there's superb art direction and the expected Unreal Engine prettiness, and movement is probably as free as one could hope for a game gated behind interaction animations, the interface is distractingly janky. You'll often find yourself having to move in order to access your satchel inventory without it clipping into scenery, and your Notebook (where screenshots are kept) is inexplicably relegated to the system menu rather than being present in game.In conclusion: I did enjoy Riven, at full price - but as a very pretty narrative walking simulator with extra steps. If that sounds good to you, and you don't mind arthritis if you're left-handed, you'll love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Have been waiting for like 15 years for this since I first heard about Starry Expanse Project and it did not disappoint. Was surprised to see how some of the puzzles were reworked, some of which are totally different than the original but just as well done. I did feel there were a few parts that were a bit easier than the original, but some of the extra areas to explore and additional puzzles more than made up for it. Lastly, there is one totally new thing in the game that flipped me upside down and all around (you'll know what I mean when you see it lol) and was a bit of a jaw-dropping moment for a huge Myst nerd like myself....great work Cyan really well done
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Waited years for this and so exciting to see it real at last. Wonderful to see the attempt to change it up some for a new generation of players. For those of us who want the original experience we will always have it but this so clearly has been crafted with love. One of the best puzzle games out there, and this version no longer has to come with a strong esoteric based asterisk.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Let's be honest - this game needed more time in the oven. Why it didn't get it is beyond my understanding. Riven was fine. Some fans wanted to do their own remake. Then Cyan swooped in, announced an official remake, and it was out within a year. For VR, even!So positives first, the puzzle and level redesigns are mostly great. Some even lend more context to the story. I love that! And of course the environment is beautiful. I absolutely love the quality put into the journals, though a few of the rewrites and additions are a bit silly to me and use phrases I'm not sure these characters should be familiar with.There are a lot of little things that are distracting. Goofy animations in places, weird timing. Pop-in. Bad looking character shadows. Robotic faces at times, and glowing white eyes on the characters. The huts seem really tiny now.Which brings us to VR. It's clear that a few things have been redesigned to accomodate VR, which is fine, but they didn't even implement it well. None of the VR interactions give any sense of the friction or weight of the levers and buttons. Everything in VR feels really small too, like they need to scale it up and run a separate iteration of the game FOR VR instead of plopping a camera into the 2D one and giving you hands that are about as functional as a regular mouse cursor. It was immediately disappointing to me. That, and it performed so poorly on Quest 3 (where I originally purchased it) that I refunded the game and had to switch to the flat version on PC.All gripes aside, I'm glad they took another pass over Riven and found some new inspiration for it. I hope they make more games in this universe, honestly, and take more risks. But I want higher quality out the gate. Make us wait. Take your time. And consider re-approaching FMV again. Myst V and 7th Guest VR are good examples of what I'd prefer to see. Even Obduction was preferable to the jank on display here (honors to the work on Gehn, though. Well done there.)At the end of the day, I had to fill a full page of a physical notebook with diagrams and symbols and backtrack a bunch to beat a video game in 2024, and that's a damn good feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As an absolute die-hard Riven (1997) fan, I was equal parts thrilled and skeptical of a remake, but Cyan absolutely delivered. They managed to take a remarkably believable (albeit fantastical) puzzle world and make it somehow even more grounded in its own lore, adding attention to details and fixing inconsistencies that I hadn't even considered before. Fans of Riven absolutely owe it to themselves to check out this version. Even if you have the original entirely committed to memory, you will very quickly find that there is more to dig into here.For new players... I suspect it's probably a touch easier than the original? I think there are accidental shortcuts to solving a couple mysteries thanks to some interface changes, and some of the altered puzzles seem a bit more straightforward. But considering that the original was among the hardest games in its genre, that's perhaps for the best. The essence of Riven is still alive and well as ever--there are really only about two real puzzles in the game, but understanding what they are, where they are, and how to solve them requires piecing together information from across the entire game world. Not many games have even tried a design like that, let alone succeeded so well.Sorry about the bridge, I didn't know that would happen. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: "I wanted a life full of magic, full of books that bridged worlds, that lit up the darkness like stars." As someone who has a lot of very fond memories of playing the original Riven, I admit was a bit sceptical when I heard that a remake was in the works. This was completely unwarranted - I had a wonderful time playing this new version. <3It made me feel both nostalgic through the beautiful reimagining of the old and excited and happy about the discoveries of the new. The only thing I missed a little were the awesome FMV performances from the original, but I realize that they would not have been possible to integrate seamlessly into this version. To the team at Cyan - thank you so much for all the good times, then and now.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't finished the game yet, but this is the right way to do a remake. True to the feel of the original. Runs just fine on my potato. Looks great at 1440p running on lowest graphics settings (textures set to High, Super Sampling set to Quality)  my 4k 65" TV.One complaint/bug is the very first viewfinder that points at a spinning dome wasn't rendering any animation right away. Walked to another location related to the "puzzle" and when I came back, it worked fine. Not sure if it was my graphics settings or an actual bug in the game. If Cyan plans on remaking Myst 3: Exlie, I'm buying it on release date. 11 out of 10Edit : Finished the game. Some of the puzzles were frustrating, but it brings back memories of how frustrated the puzzles were in the original Riven. Still happy to play this game on release date and glad to support Cyan.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Faithful to the original while still feeling fresh at the same time. Beautiful game, stunning visuals and brilliant music and sound, it's a wonderful experience, in my opinion only improving on the original, not taking away from it in any way. I will always still love the original game but this is now the best way to experience Riven by far. Simply beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cons: 1. The 3D models are better than Myst (2021), but still take away from the experience.2. Concessions made for VR makes some areas feel flat/odd. (Tram rides)3. Optimization needed to smooth out some stuttering, but this will likely be fixed in updates4. Some achievements seem to be bugged. Again, will be fixed in an update.5. New music from Robyn Miller is good, but feels out of place. Pros:1. Faithful recreation of the original game’s art that is mind blowing.2. Music and voice direction still incredible.3. Any changes to the game are all well thought out and make for a surprising and engaging experience even for someone who has played the old game every year since 1997.Riven is my favorite game of all time. I played Myst at the age of 5 and followed it up with Riven when I was 8. No other piece of media has shaped who I am so completely than Riven. The prospects of a remake had been very interesting to me for over a decade but ultimately I viewed as an inevitable disappointment.I stand corrected. Riven (2024) is the modern (pre/post-Obduction) Cyan Worlds magnum opus. Not only is it a faithful recreation of the spirit of Riven, but also changes the game to always be surprising for the seasoned player and ever engaging for the transition to 3D.Is it perfect? No. But after the disappointment of Firmament (the gameplay, not the art or story) I was ready to also be dissatisfied in this. The first images of the new 3D models were disheartening, and in the final game they still aren’t great, but far better than the similar attempt for Myst (2021). Other downsides are some of the new compositions by the great Robyn Miller which is great music, but sounds more like cut tracks from Obduction rather than for Riven.Riven (2024) is a triumph. It might not hold a candle to original which is still so very special to me, it displays that Cyan has what it takes to navigate into the future. Possibly with new Myst games as teased years prior.Final Thoughts: would like to see the lighting “unlocked” or something to see some of these areas at night or at afternoon. The decision to bake in the lighting makes sense to keep the Riven vibe, but it would be cool have like a “sandbox” version of the Riven environment to play with lighting and potentially weather. I know it isn’t “realRiven” but could be fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is done!  It might have taken less time if not for my immersive journaling, but so worth it.  This is the game fans have been waiting for.  The environment is so gorgeous it takes my breath away, with some surprises along the way!  It's not as difficult as I remember, though that may be just me growing more puzzle savvy.  Even the marble puzzle made sense! :)  The cg characters were a tiny bit odd, given the realistic graphics, but still very well done.  Not one thing I can complain about with this game.  Am I going to start it over again right now?  ...I might do just that. ^-^

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. In terms of gameplay, it feels like the focus is on exploring the world, observing things, trying to learn and understand some of what you encounter, and problem solving based on that, which I found to be pretty engaging. It feels more organic and a bit less video-gamey compared to Myst and the puzzles in that. I also enjoyed the setting, story, and the visuals, which despite being updated and looking very nice and modern, also retain some of that surreal 90s pre-rendered vibe, which is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. I'm a huge fan of escape rooms in real life, and this game is essentially several immersive digital escape rooms tied together, with deep lore and much exploring/learning required!I haven't played Myst (yet), so I came in with zero context for the lore/game mechanics. It was NOT easy, which is honestly exactly what I was hoping for!  There's zero tutorial, zero explanation of how things work, and zero apologies for being so difficult. This makes solving puzzles that much more exciting and satisfying. It also makes getting stumped that much more frustrating... but worth it in the end! If you're like me, you want to do the entire thing with absolutely zero walkthrough support. I made it through 96% of the game without looking anything up, but there were 2 things that had me genuinely confused... which I won't spoil... but both were near the end, and I was glad to find out I was actually on the right track anyway! I finished in about 22 hours, and I honestly feel quite proud of myself!All that to say, this is definitely "Type 2 Fun." Not a casual game, and not stimulating in the typical flashing-lights-moving-pictures type of way, but deeply fascinating and intriguing for curious and determined minds. And loads of "fun" in that sense! Don't give up! And good luck :)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely wonderful. Changes plenty of puzzles yet still keeps the core intact, this reads as an alternate universe version of Riven, and it's most welcome. Before I get into anything, I highly recommend this game, I had a fantastic time unlocking this puzzle box and seeing where the unique concepts of Myst were expanded.There are some problems sadly. The game hitches in a handful of sections on my very high end rig, and it's always the same locations. Pop in on the trams is pretty rough. most times an animated character interacts with an object, it visually breaks in some pretty rough ways. Lip sync is non existent and the 3d characters look so utterly uncanny I deeply wish they kept cutscene control out of the player's hands just so we could have an option to reinsert the original live action performances cut out and put into the game, even at a low res. I had a couple moments where the main menu completely locked up because i used a controller at some points. I had an unfixable glitch where I paused and opened the satchel at the same time, causing the animation to freeze me in place permanently until a reload.I do also want to add that this along with Myst both desperately need a point and click mode. There is a lot of gorgeous visual direction lost, along with some puzzles becoming so wildly obscured by unlocking the player's vision that I wish there was an optional mode.These are issues that need fixed, adjusted, or tweaked for sure. however, none of them kept the core of this game from blasting through brighter than one would ever expect.The music, PEAK. The visual design, PEAK. The puzzles, PEAK. every other facet of this title is rendered with such masterful precision that I still hope the rest of the Myst series is remade, despite my sickness of remakes.If you want to take some time to exercise your brain with music that goes OFF paired with gorgeous and striking visuals, play this, no questions asked. After Myst of course.And if you want an EVEN BETTER time, play the original. This acts as a nice refresh of the classic.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not just a remake of Riven with a fresh coat of paint. I mean: it IS a photorealistic recreation of the 90s game in Unreal Engine, but it ALSO changes up SO MANY puzzle elements of the game that it feels more like a sequel to the classic. Those familiar with Riven's OG puzzles will immediately notice something is ... different as they begin their exploration. New challenges and game dynamics give this towering cultural icon of a game a whole new level of depth and interest.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a magnificent reimagining of Riven. If you've never played it, buy it now! If you played Riven back in the '90s, buy it now! :) What can I say without spoilers? It's stunningly beautiful, deeply thought out, and filled with more story, worldbuilding, and puzzles than before. As fantastical and strange as it may get, Riven always feels like a deeply real place, and the new version is quite likely the greatest game Cyan has ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the original Riven I can say that the remake is well worth picking up. It is incredibly well made and while there are some very minor visual shake ups, this feels like I'm walking through the prerendered pictures of the original. I was very surprised to see that many of the puzzles were remixed slightly, it still feels like Riven but changed enough to feel like a new experience. If you love Myst, buy it. If you're new to Myst, buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't think I've ever played a game like Riven.  I played and got stuck on the original way back in 1997, and even back then I felt like it was something wholly unique.  Its predecessor, Myst, while certainly somewhat dense in the way its puzzles were presented, played mostly like vignette of challenges that helped you progress through its various Ages, and that's essentially how most puzzle games I've played have felt.  Riven is... different.  It seems to have more in common with "walking simulators".  Rather than a series of mostly disparate puzzles, the player's focus is on immersing yourself in the art, culture, and science of an unfamiliar world and its inhabitants.  There are a few minor, quick puzzles throughout the story, but the game as a whole is about using the knowledge you gain to complete what amounts to a single, "final" puzzle that both literally and figuratively connects everything you've seen.  (Incidentally, that puzzle is what I got stuck on back in 1997.)  That Riven does this in a way that feels so natural and intuitive - while still taxing your brain - makes completing it feel rewarding in a way that I have never experienced in a puzzle game.  Add to that the fascinating premise of Ages and Linking Books that Cyan Worlds put so much thought and creativity into all those years ago, and I can't help but think that this remake has taken the spot as my favorite puzzle game of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven has always been one of those games I wish I could experience for the first time again, and Cyan have done exactly that!  It looks like how I imagined it looked as a kid, but actually hi-def this time.  The sounds and music (and even the color of the rocks and sky) immediately brought me back to playing the original Riven.This new Riven captures the feel and sense of the original Riven, but includes some updates to keep it fresh.  Some puzzles are tweaked, and others are completely new.  The original will always be there for those who want it, and I love this new version!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Playing the best puzzle game ever made in VR was a treat.  There are some changes from the original version, but for the most part I liked the changes.  You need a very good gaming pc to run Riven in VR with the highest quality graphic settings.  I have a 3080 TI and a 9700K cpu and I was just able to run it on the high settings with a 72 hz refresh rate.All though I do love playing this game in VR, I think Cyan is falling behind other companies who make VR games.  For example, in games like Half Life Alyx, you have realistic physics so you can pull or push open a standard door.  Cyan's solution to this is having these sliding doors and when they tried to have a swinging door, they were a bit clumsy.  I feel sliding doors is a lazy solution.  Also, instead of the simple solution of having a crouch button for puzzles that are low to the ground, Cyan chose to change those puzzles so they are at standing height.  If pressing a crouch button is too complicated for your player base, they are too dumb to be playing your puzzle game.  In the latest version of Myst, there is a glaring example of this in the channel wood age, where they had these insanely long levers (which looked ugly to me) to divert the water.  I would have rather just had the lever closer to the ground and I would press a crouch button to get low to the floor so I could manipulate the lever.  Or another solution could be the lever is close to the floor but I could manipulate it from a standing position by pointing at the handle and the lever is highlighted and then I can press the grab button and then when I move my arm it moves the lever.There are some things I did like which Cyan did in VR, like fast travel for ladders and having a seated mode.  I particularly like having a seated mode, because you can sit and be the height in the game that you would be if you were standing, this is important for puzzle games as sometimes you are standing in one place for awhile trying to solve a puzzle.  There is a strange group of people who think VR must always be a complete simulation and if you are pressing a button, you might as well play the game flat, but that is just silly.  These same people used to think if you're not physically walking in your play space, your immersion is ruined, but logic prevailed and people now use an analog stick to move around in VR.  Same thing goes with a crouch button, I don't want to bend down a million times in real life, but I also don't want everything to be be designed at waist height because of that.I hate to nitpick but I love Cyan games and I love playing VR.  This game is awesome and you should play it.  My nitpicks are just to highlight where I see room for improvement.  I give it a 9 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game that I would recommend to everyone, there really aren't many like it. Maybe there are none exactly like it. Walking around this mysterious world feels amazing, it feels like a visually stunning almost real place.There are "puzzles" to solve, but they're not really puzzly-puzzles. It's more like you're discovering a world that is the way it is for good reason, with a rich history and story, and you're a visitor trying to figure out how it all works. It's actually genius. The story isn't super in your face, it's told through careful observation of the environment, but when things click, it's the best feeling in the world.It's a little tough, but not SUPER hard, I managed to beat it with only 2 small nudges in the right direction.Begging the developer for more games, no one does it like them!

_childDocuments_.review: Yup, it's Riven and it's free roam! Love it from the start, the puzzles I ran through so far work really well in this format. Sort of disappointed with the Myst VR part, so it's probably the same with this: locomotion is a huge detraction for this style of game in VR -- plays much better flat gaming.

_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The remake of Riven masterfully captures the essence of the original game, transporting players back to the mystical and enigmatic world with remarkable fidelity. The developers have succeeded in recreating the same mood and atmosphere that made the original a classic, yet have introduced new and surprising puzzles that keep even veteran players on their toes.From the moment you start the game, the meticulously crafted environment draws you in. The lighting and sound effects are nothing short of perfect, creating an immersive experience that feels both familiar and refreshingly new. The ambient sounds and visual details work in harmony to enhance the sense of mystery and adventure, just as they did in the original.Despite initial expectations that the game might be a quick walkthrough, the complexity and ingenuity of the new riddles ensure a challenging experience. Each puzzle is thoughtfully designed, requiring players to engage deeply with the game world and think creatively to progress. The balance between maintaining the spirit of the original and introducing new elements is handled with finesse, making the remake a standout success.In summary, the Riven remake is a testament to the developers' dedication to honoring the original while providing a fresh and engaging experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original when I was a kid, with very fond memories of all of the iconic locations. I wasn't old enough to solve the puzzles then, but I was always mesmerized by this world of Riven. This remake is absolutely incredible. Jaw-dropping. An incredible interactive work of art. A world hand-crafted with loving detail, and something that I will never forget. I'm loving the puzzles so far, 4 hours in, and I can tell there's a lot more still to uncover and explore in this world. It's familiar, but SO much has changed that it feels completely new all over again.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remake. You could criticize the puzzles being redesigned but honestly the original 1997 game's puzzles were infamously difficult to solve.  I found it fairly quickly it occured to me that not all people might.As well, I used to follow Starry Expanse Project over the years and was aware of the fact that the original game did a lot of "magic" let's say, to make the layout appear to be what it was, rather than something that works in a real continuous 3D space. As such, I totally understand the layout changes on various islands, although it sometimes made me imagine that the protagonist showed up 20 years later and a lot of things just fell into disrepair.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely incredible remake. Exceeded my expectations many times over.If you're a fan of the original, you'll love it. The game is visually impressive. Exploring the world of Riven freely in 3d makes it feel more real than before. I would have been fine if that was the only change, but the puzzles have received an update, as well. I won't say too much in a review, but your first peak inside one of the spinning domes will leave you stunned.For those that are new to the series, I'd still recommend it. The Riven remake is not merely playing with nostalgia. But get it with the Myst remake if you haven't played the prequel already.My only real complaint is that some of the animations are clunky. I understand why why the developers can't use FMV in an environment the player can walk around in, but at the same time, the lack of quality in character movement leaves me feeling like something was lost in the upgrade.Suffice to say, the Riven remake that us fans have been wishing for all these years has finally arrived, and it is more satisfying than we could have anticipated.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I grew up with the original Myst and Riven and loved Riven so much I played it 4+ times in the row as a kid. The world was beautiful, and it felt lived in. However, the game, while difficult, was nowhere near as difficult and time-consuming as the remake. The remake is a whole other beast, and I must admit, I found it infuriatingly confusing at times, partially due to UI-related bugs which broke the game temporarily (until a reload/restart).Here's the breakdown:+ ~8 hours to complete one story from beginning to end with as little guidance as possible.+ ~14 hours to 100% all achievements without a guide, though I sought out hints from time to time and utilized my existing knowledge of Riven from over 2 decades ago.+ Beautiful environments to explore! Walk around in familiar but somewhat refreshed environments with WASD and FPS style camera movement. Beware: some puzzles are harder to figure out because of the new control scheme but not a ton.+ Some randomization occurs with the puzzles, making this somewhat replayable.+/- OG Riven's puzzles and world are way different, so your past knowledge may be more of a hindrance than a boon, making this a mostly new experience for all players but also making it much harder to figure out, with or without a guide.- FMV sequences were replaced by impressive but ultimately inferior 3D models.- Some levels and gameplay mechanics of the original Riven were completely removed or dumbed down in the remake.- Interactive elements are somewhat limited. I expected more physics objects in this remake, but for the most part, items were static and had scripted movements.- VR is supported but only barely. I recommend just playing this game in flat, non-VR mode. It's simply more enjoyable that way in my opinion. Your mileage may vary with different headset and controller combos. You may have some trouble with Index controllers when paired with certain headsets. I noticed problems with mine in a brief test but after a PC restart, they randomly worked.Overall, it's a great remake, but it messed with the formula that made the original Riven beloved too much. After playing this remake, I went back to the original and realized I would have enjoyed a remaster of the original more. Oh well. Still a great experience. Well worth the asking price if you're a long time fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The reworking of many of the puzzles was a smart choice. I narratively knew how to beat the game, but I still had to take notes to solve the new-ish puzzles. It really made the remake feel just fresh enough to warrant the cost of admission. Thanks Cyan for finally finishing this 3D remake over a decade in the making. Now please make Myst VI or something... or at least another novel. Finish the Book of Marrim pretty please!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven, the remaster of the 1997 best selling game, is a nostalgic walk down memory lane for those of us who played the original when it was released. The 1997 original featured some of the best looking scenery and incredible world building that has ever been made in video game history. While the original game was made from pre-rendered images and video in low resolutions by today's standards, this remaster brings the game into the Unreal engine, accomplishing in real-time what we could only ever dream of or hope for 27 years ago. Cyan's treatment of the setting has always been one of verisimilitude, forsaking the spectacular in order to try to maintain a grounded sense of reality, encouraging the player to inhabit the role of the "stranger".Not only has this remake captured the heart and soul of the original, in my opinion it elevates the experience. Some of the original puzzles were overly complex have now been simplified. Some have been removed and replaced. Old players will find the experience comfortably familiar, yet be sufficiently different to make the purchase worthwhile. New players can sink themselves into the world of Myst and discover a beautiful and compelling world and story.Advice for new players: you will be tempted to look up walk-throughs and guides. Don't. The biggest joy in these games is figuring out the puzzles for yourself. Take your time. Look everywhere. Read everything. Yes, read.I hope Cyan will consider making more games in the universe of Myst, if not the series. There is much still to explore about the D'ni and the ages they learned how to link to.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this back in '97 on five CD ROMs the old fashioned way... v2024 is amazing!  It's great in HDR on Mac.  It's UNREAL on my VR Headset. It's just unreal.  Haven't had this much fun since Alyx. Oh-It's great on my Steam Deck too!
