_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this.The original Riven was one of the very first games I played. I replayed it two years ago and I can confidently say that - besides the abysmally low resolution - it has held up well both graphically and in terms of gameplay, given its age. This remake is, unfortunately, a disappointment both in comparison to the original and as a stand-alone game in my opinion.Before I get into why that is, I want to applaud Cyan for this remake because it is clear that a lot of effort went into this game. The graphics are stunning and are a faithful and genuine improvement over the original graphics. The water and animal animations are great. Some aspects of the game were reworked due to the nature of the original being a point and click game and while I am not a huge fan of most of the solutions (see below), it is undeniable that a lot of creativity has been employed to come up with them.All that being said, here is why I think this game falls short:The linearity in this game is crushing. One of the key factors to Riven's success was how most of the game was accessible right from the start and the game put very little effort into putting you on the right track. The remake is the polar opposite: Most of the hints needed to solve a puzzle are collocated and fairly on the nose. I imagine some of this was done to save some backtracking, which takes a lot longer in this iteration (clicking through islands was extremely quick in the original). I can appreciate the idea here, but it takes away a lot of immersion and realism. To further illustrate this point, let's examine the game's two main puzzles and compare them to their original versions:Another aspect of the game I disliked was the constant locking of your character and camera. The immersion that a true 3d game brings is dependent on your character actually being able to use all degrees of freedom. A lot of clickable interfaces in this game violate this idea by zooming themselves into view and stopping you from moving your camera or character at all. In doing this, the remake degenerates to a point and click game with slightly better graphics. Some of these locked angles are supposed to help the player better understand cause and effect of the machinery they are manipulating. I found this to be further unnecessary hand holding for the most part. I would have much preferred if the puzzles, wherever possible, let you click buttons, push levers etc while still allowing you to move your character and camera. The rather slow animations when zooming in certainly didn't help here either.All in all, I would love a more faithful remake that keeps most of the puzzles as is or at least keeps them within the spirit of Riven and seamlessly integrates the puzzles into the world rather than making them stick out like a sore thumb.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven remains the single best adventure game ever made, and it's not close. 2024 is the year that real-time 3D graphics can finally live up to the promise of photorealistic pre-rendered scenes from 1997; the game is so gorgeous is hurts a bit. The puzzles and the way the game progresses have been made more accessible at the cost of a little bit of the brilliantly organic verisimilitude of the original game, but I can forgive the game for that. Riven deserved a full 3D remake, and this game absolutely does the original justice. I am blown away. It was like I was a kid again playing with my mom and my sister, except I'm older so I had more of an idea of what I was doing and was better equipped to fully appreciate and enjoy it. I really just can't speak highly enough of the remake, as someone for whom the original is one of THE three games that got me into game development.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven is probably my number one game of all time. It impacted me greatly as a teen back in the late 90s and is one of the biggest influences on my entering the game development field myself. To have Myst and now Riven, both so influential memories of my childhood, be remade so excellently has been a dream come true. I've had so much fun playing both Myst and now Riven with my children, going back through memory lane but also giddy in excitement at the changes that have been made and the new puzzles and clues to discover!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the original Myst, Riven, and Exile. They're three of the only games I care about, quite frankly, and Riven was my favorite of the three, for its spooky environment, and amazing plot. I also happened to enjoy the 2021 Myst remake, if you select "classic" video mode, and get rid of the CG characters. So what went wrong with the Riven remake?As you can probably already guess, I am not a fan of the CG characters. They're the number one thing that ruins the realism of the game. I tried out the game on two different computers, and there was a lot of fine-tuning required at the beginning to get Atrus and Cho looking halfway decent. Yet their hair had a fuzzy-yet-transculent quality that bothered me. Was there really no way to get video footage of human beings into the game? If the resolution of the original footage was too low to work in the new game, I'd much rather Cyan use footage with new actors.The game has substantial issues, however, which extend beyond the use of CG characters. It's been revamped to such an extent that it feels like a re-interpretation rather than a remake. Some of the changes make sense plot-wise (such as the Moiety using the Rivenese numbering system, rather than the D'Ni one), but most are completely arbitrary and needless. Plateau Island has been completely gutted and dumbed-down. I'll leave it at that. I'm also puzzled by Atrus linking to Myst during the opening cutscene, rather than continuing with his writing, so he can stabilize Riven. Has the purpose of this ever been addressed by the developers?Most surprisingly to me, the new game is a lot more linear than the old one. You have a few randomized puzzles, but other than that, there's a singular line you need to follow if you want to win. In the original, you had a lot of leeway in choosing which order to the solve the puzzles. Case in point, once you got to Jungle Island, you either had a choice of staying there and solving some puzzles, going to Crater Island, or going to Plateau Island (if you knew about the trick with the Wahrk Elevator). In the new game,  - at least as far as I can tell.While the visuals in the Riven Remake are cool at times, it is still a vastly inferior game to the original. While the original may have a low resolution, it looks amazingly organic and real, compared to Riven in the "Unreal" engine. The use of real human actors was the icing on the cake. What I could see happening is someone devising an AI-upscaled version of the original Riven which ends up being superior to the remake. I know there is already an AI-upscaled version of Exile that looks OK.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really comment for new players of Riven, as I know the original game inside and out so I already knew what to do and how to think in most cases. But as a long time Myst fan, this remake was incredibly fun to play. New puzzles, finding familiar spaces in new places, secrets, and some surprises along the way!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The return of the king of first person puzzle games; as beautiful, haunting, and puzzling as ever. Free movement in Riven is like a dream come true. The gorgeous fifth age has a few new tricks up its sleeve as well.My only complaint is the replacement of the FMV actors with in-game character models that honestly don't look that great. I wish I could have chosen my experience between the two.Still - it's an excellent version of an all time classic that really highlights the shortcomings of Cyan's last game, Firmament. Next time keep the AI away from the art.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing, beautiful, and immersive, just as the original was.  Would highly recommend to anyone who loves puzzle games and especially those who've played the original.  Cyan again brings puzzles that are wonderfully integrated into the world building and storytelling of the game!  I have been really enjoying so far and am excited to be solving brand new puzzles and hearing the new music added!Was a huge fan of the original and so I was incredibly excited for the new release.  It was a nice surprise to find new puzzles that I could solve from scratch instead of just slowly remembering how I solved the original.  Almost every change is justified, as the original game was largely unbeatable by the general public and most people who played the original would be lying if they said they didn't need to look up at least one of the puzzles solutions.  From rearranging locations, to streamlining your path through the world, the changes are designed to better guide you through the more difficult puzzles.There is of course a bit of sadness, when finding some of the locations changed more than expected, but overall I think the changes are good, making the game more appealing to new players.  It's important to remember the goal is to solve every puzzle in the game ,  looking at a guide or cheat-list.I'm so happy this game was made, and I'm always happy to support Cyan so they can continue to make great games with beautiful worlds and storytelling.  Can't wait to see what they'll put out next!

_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I wish Steam had a third option to the question "Do you recommend this game?" and that third option would be "Maybe". And this game is a big maybe to me.As the sequel to Myst, I was very excited to try the Riven remake out, as I had loved the Myst remake Cyan Worlds had previously made. I could never get into the original game, as it was far too outdated by the time I wanted to try it. Same went for Riven, where I tried to play the original, but I just couldn't get past the horrible controls and the graphics. I was happy to see a remake of Riven was in the works and wish listed it immediately. Now it's here and I can't exactly say I love this game, but I don't exactly hate it either.The game itself is gorgeous. The graphics and details are quite impressive for a world that is largely lifeless. You see some animals here and there, with some other humans sprinkled in at a handful for times throughout the game, but for the most part it's just you and the scenery. And the scenery is quite beautiful. I found Riven to be a very quiet game. It felt like there was a lack of ambient sound in many areas and some sound effects were either delayed or nonexistent. You will click buttons or pull levers only to hear silence. The cut scene audio sounds like it was ripped right out of the original game, which would explain its poor quality. There isn't very many cutscenes or spoken dialogue, so it wouldn't have hurt to have hired voice actors to redo the lines.The puzzles themselves are just like Myst, where they are solved by interacting with the environment and not having to carry items around or combine items. The puzzles are mainly based around interacting with the environment and numbers and symbols. As you progress through the world of Riven you'll have to call back upon many details you came across during your travels. And that is where this game drove me nuts. Having to recall minor details in an area you haven't visited in hours. There is a journal, where you can take a screenshot and make notes on it. I appreciate the notebook, but that isn't the problem here. You need to collect screenshots of EVERYTHING in order to understand the later puzzles, but you won't know this until it's too late because for most of the game you can easily progress without utilizing the journal for anything. Then all of a sudden the game turns around and drops multiple puzzles with code combinations that require you to decipher a made up language and number system that up until this point was hardly used. Now you have the fun task of traveling back to multiple areas of the game to collect clues, which require you to go through the longest traveling animations I have seen in a game in a long time. I hate having to consult online guides for hints or an outright answer, but I was forced to several times towards the end of the game where I was just so damn sick of numbers and symbols. I enjoy difficult puzzles, but I absolutely despise having to backtrack for them and this game makes you do a ton of it, even beyond just the puzzles. I hinted at it in the paragraph above, but traveling between islands and even in some parts of the islands themselves can be a massive pain. There are two main ways to travel between islands and they involve a trolley system and . Both of the these methods have long animations and aren't fast in any way imaginable. You'll have to utilize both of these methods frequently and by the end you'll be glad to never use them again. Oh and how can I forget the damn rotating room on the first island. There is this rotating room with five different doors, but you can only use two doors at once. As you rotate the room with a button from the outside you'll need to wait until the doors line up with where you are standing and then with another door. To get from one specific door to another, you need to go through the painfully long animation of the entire room rotating multiple times until you can walk through, but then it might require you to do this whole process over again at another door to get somewhere else. If you want to see first hand how stupid this puzzle is just go on YouTube and see for yourself. The game makes you go through this area many times later in the game, but requires you to do the rotating puzzle each time you pass through and need to access a slightly different door. In the end, I am going to recommend this game, but barely. I love puzzle games and I have to support them, especially with remakes like this one. However, they need to be better than this. That's not to say I didn't like the game. I did, but the negative aspects of it just drove me nuts. It's never a good sign when you're playing a game and are trying to finish it because you just want it to be over. That's what happened in the last three hours of Riven for me. I wanted to be done with this game and uninstall it, so I can move onto something better.

_childDocuments_.review: My dad first plopped me down in front of Riven when I was about 7. Since then I've played almost every re-release of it. This has been the best by far. I do think that this has to be the last time I buy the game...right?

_childDocuments_.review: Such a wonderful game, still as good as it was when it first came out 27 (!) years ago. Back then it was a behemoth of a game, way ahead of its time, and today… I've still never played a puzzle game that has managed to weave together its puzzles, story and environment as well as Riven. It feels like it hasn't aged.And for old farts like me, this remake has been smart enough to change things around so it feels fresh even after several playthoughs of the original. Books have been rewritten, puzzles have been modified or replaced, areas moved or added to force you to take different paths from before. It almost felt like playing for the first time again. I was giddy with excitement every time I started it up.This was finally the game that made me like VR, too. Bought a headset just for this, and I'm glad I did. Though, to be honest, when you need to write notes occasionally, VR is still kind of a pain. Oh well.

_childDocuments_.review: I played realMYST: Masterpiece Edition in 2015, and that was my introduction to the series. (Thank you, brutalmoose!)Not long after that, I played and loved the rest of the series after they came to steam (back in 2018-ish) using  of hints along the way - a habit from trying to solve the first Myst.Then, barely a year ago I marathoned through the entire pentalogy using no hints, just pen and paper as well as a familiarity with what I'm  to find and  to find it. And that was great! Definitively enjoyed them all more the second time around.So tl;dr, I consider myself a pretty big Myst fan!And as all Myst fans knew of course, there was a fan-effort to build a realtime 3D version of 'The Sequel to Myst'. Eventually, that fan-effort transformed into an official remake announcement, and I've been even more hyped for realRiven ever since 2022. With how good Myst (2021) turned out, I knew that Cyan could tweak and improve upon the foundations of the 1997 masterpiece, with modern graphical fidelity, lore updates and so on. But best of all; let Riven be played and solved in that oh-so liberating real-time 3D and free mouse look!So after playing it, I think this remake turned out amazing! I had a fantastic time playing through it all-- pen and paper in hand, as well as its new built-in screenshot/journal function --where every update and change was a welcome surprise and a remix of the original. Though it's not exactly "improving upon perfection", I'm glad Riven (2024) forged its own identity which now usurps the old Riven journey for me with the expanded areas added. Those remixed elements in this new version therefore cause this (more well-balanced difficulty-wise) replacement to the original to not be a replacement for it - which I'd say every remake and re-release of Myst has attempted to be.But yeah, this game hits it out of the park in the ways that matter; audio, graphics, , impact, immersion, discovery, and a Tolkien-level of worldbuidling.Even with the solutions to the original fresh in my mind, I managed to get lost at least once when looking for an important (but skippable) marker, and I'm split on whether I should be thrilled at the game letting me got lost before arriving at the solution myself, or disgruntled at how that particular part, , was intended to be solved.I can only hope that realEXILE is next - my favorite of the entire series.

_childDocuments_.review: - all about point and click adventuresIs this game a masterpiece? 27 years after the release of the best-selling game of 1997, a complete remaster has now been released. Is it a cheap re-release or a contemporary renovation?Riven (by brothers Robyn and Rand Miller) is the direct successor to Myst. Myst was released back in 1993 and took the world by storm at the time. It became the best-selling game ever and defended this position for several years until it was replaced by The Sims 10 years later. The reason for its resounding success at the time was probably its excellent graphics (as one of the first good PC games to use the CD-ROM as a medium - along with classics such as Rebel Assault or The 7th Guest). In addition, it was also a game that was extremely well received by female gamers. Myst has been re-released several times over the years in an improved version, and finally underwent an excellent complete remaster in 2021.But what about Riven? With Riven, the developers at Cyan have continued the success story of Myst, but this time they had a slightly bigger budget. When it was released in 1997, it was already common practice (and technically no longer completely new territory) to publish new PC games on CD-ROM. Riven took up five CDs back then. Although it no longer set any new sales records, it still sold extremely well. In contrast to Myst, however, there were no new versions of Riven in the following years (apart from a DVD-ROM version, console and cell phone ports). So if you wanted to play Riven until now, you could either try to somehow get your old original to run on new PC hardware (difficult), install it via ScummVM, play it on your cell phone or play a console version (PlayStation, Saturn). The edition available on Steam was also just the old original without any improvements and with ScummVM as an emulator. So it really was time for a new version - and it has finally been released!Riven throws us straight into the story. If you haven't played Myst before, you won't understand much of the story, at least at first. We continue to play a dimensional traveler who is transported to the world of Riven by Atrus in order to find and rescue his wife Catherine. Riven is ruled by his evil father Gehn and is slowly being destroyed. Arthur makes it clear that we can't leave Riven the same way we traveled there, but hopefully he'll bring us back once we find his wife and Gehn is neutralized. And what's more, he may have found a way to bring us back to the world we originally came from...Once we arrive in Riven, one of our books is stolen, but the thief can't enjoy his booty for very long. After this introduction, the game begins - and it is structured very similarly to its predecessor. We are in a world that is sparsely populated by other creatures, but is full of strange buildings and other constructs. We have no idea what the various devices are for or how they work. The gameplay consists of exploring the world and solving various puzzles, which are usually related to the machines in the environment. Press switches and buttons, flip levers, move things around, always with the aim of opening up new paths and making progress. There are a total of five large islands to explore. Some puzzles also use musical clues. We have to use our intellect and intuition to discover the truth about Riven and its inhabitants. Riven has several possible endings - from a positive ending to the absolute failure of the player.The new version of Riven, like the remaster of Myst before it, has been completely reprogrammed. In contrast to the original, we now move completely freely in a 3D environment developed with the Unreal Engine, and can no longer just travel from point to point. In addition, the story has been expanded at some points and new graphics have been added. Some puzzles have been adapted to our new movement options. However, if you already know the original, you will recognize most of the locations and puzzles without any problems. The graphics also look excellent in high resolutions, and the many small movie sequences in the game are now of a much higher quality than before.This is what a lavish new edition should look like. With the new version of Riven, the old classic from 1997 has been perfectly reworked and adapted for the current generation of players. Riven is of course of particular interest to players who have already played Myst and now want more of the same - without any major changes to the game mechanics. Many puzzles, the solution to which is only revealed by attentively observing the surroundings, lead through a leisurely developing adventure - without time pressure and skill interludes. You'll have to decide for yourself whether you still find this type of gameplay contemporary.Finally a lovingly revised new version of this all-time classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. I have the fondest memories of playing the original back in the late nineties with my dad and brother, and can happily say that they've recaptured the magic here perfectly. I haven't played it in VR yet but intend to once I get the opportunity. Honestly, nostalgia glasses aside, I really can't think of any serious criticisms of this game - most of the puzzles are, at their core, the same puzzles from the original, with some QoL changes here and there and some new puzzles thrown in. The atmosphere and immersion are just as good, if not better, as the original game, to the point that I was never unhappy having to backtrack or wander around or simply be patient while I worked out what to do next. I sincerely hope Cyan continues working on the Myst series and pray that this game does well enough to convince them to keep at it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I never played  as a kid.  I was aware of its existence for sure, but I didn't play the game proper until I was in my twenties.  So I didn't have much of an attachment to the game, at least not to the same level as I did with .  When I heard that Cyan Worlds was making a re-make of , my reaction was essentially a "huh that's neat" before moving on.  Fast forward to June 2024, and I notice there's demo for  as part of the Steam Next Fest.  So on a whim, I decided to install it and fire it up.My jaw dropped.The modern remake of  is utterly gorgeous.  To be able to experience it in 3D with high-quality, photorealistic graphics is something that could only have been dreamed of back in 1997.  I can't quite put my finger on what makes this one in particular stand out to me.   has gone through so many remakes and revisions, yet none of them wowed me the way  did.  Perhaps it's because  was left untouched for decades.  There was a team working on a fan-remake (they ended up being picked up by Cyan Worlds to help with the remake, which is really cool), but aside from that  never got the same love as its predecessor.  Maybe that made the jump from the original graphics to the new that much more stunning.Or maybe it's just me.  Maybe my lack of expectations made it much more spectacular for me.For the uninitiated,  is an adventure game.  You walk around the environments, picking up pieces of the story as you go, and solving puzzles.  Even back in the day,  was unique in that its puzzles would often require you to have an understanding of the world around you.  In particular, some of the late game puzzles will test you to make sure you've been paying attention and not just brute forcing your way through everything.Some of the puzzles in the remake have been drastically changed from the original game (the animal totems one comes to mind).  These puzzles, from what I can remember, are definitely an improvement from the original.  They're more clear about what you need to do while still retaining that key aspect of being integrated into the world's lore.  Some more avid  fans may have a different perspective on that, but for my part they were a good change.  There are other changes as well (including an entirely new area that wasn't in the original game).The story will be a bit confusing for those who maybe haven't played  before.  Some of that confusion is intentional, but considering  is a direct sequel some of the concepts will be difficult to untangle for those unfamiliar.  It's not impossible to come to grips with it, but you'll be playing a bit of catch-up if you jump in unaware.The one major issue I have with this remake is the cartoon-y character models.  The lip syncing on them is very off at times, and they don't always fit in quite right with the environment.  They're a massive improvement over the terrifying 3D abominations they had in the 2021 remake of , but they still feel out of place compared to the world around them.The only other complaint I can think of at the moment is one I had with the original: occasionally the story will just drop a twenty page journal in your lap and expect you to read it.  And you'll have to, because the journal could contain a necessary clue for progression.  It's nothing major, but it is a bit irritating to have your exploration interrupted because you suddenly need to read an entire short story.But aside from these complaints, the  is a fantastic achievement.  So whether you're an old fan looking to re-experience a classic, or someone who was just too young or never played the game growing up, this 2024 version of  is hands down the best way to experience it.  Just be prepared to challenge yourself, and plunge into a fantastical world of puzzles and secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that can appeal to both players who have never played riven and players who have played the original version. The game largely has its original puzzles but with some small changes and twists that makes it exiting for everyone. I highly recommend this game to anyone who loves puzzle games but are okay with being frustrated with hard puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful beyond belief. It's fascinating how they were able to translate the still visuals of the original game into a modern first-person perspective with free movement.Some of the puzzles and enigmas you have to solve require a lot of attention to the environment and quite a bit of back and forth, but the sheer beauty of the scenery made every moment a joy.Another thing that I loved was the way the game tells its story although this should be credited to the design of the original game. The story is not handed to you, it is given in small bits of dialogue, writings and environmental detail. As you progress you realize that small details in the environment that seemed purely cosmetic at first actually tell part of the story. It's up to you to connect the dots and many details are left for your interpretation.This game as become one of my favorite games of all time. Thank you, Cyan!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A mesmerizing and beautiful game. More of an adventure than a puzzle game but the way it culminates at the end is a fantastic puzzle. The way they translated the prerendered and 90's art aesthetic to Unreal 5 is fantastic. The art is quite timeless and imo much more interesting and unique than what we have seen recently from Cyan and other modern games.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I guess 2 out of 3 = a thumbs up.PROS: [1] Being able to freely walk through Riven; really take it all in and see it from every angle.[2] Just the right amount of changes were made from the original to make the play-through as fresh as possible without risky brain surgery.CONS:[1] What truly set Myst and Riven apart when they were released was that they were the pinnacle of photo-realistic 3D adventure gaming through their clever use of pre-rendered images. The things you saw and could interact with looked real. This remake, despite how infrequently it happens, RIPS you right out of that realistic immersion with arguably some of the least realistic 3D models from a modern game and that didn't stop with humans. Apparently not even the sacred whark deserved professional-level modeling and texturing.Imagine using Unreal Engine to create an immersive, lush, vibrant, mysterious, elegant 3D environment and THEN using cardboard, crayons and glue to make the characters to paste onto your screen during gameplay as needed. That's the equivalent of what they did and I can't imagine why. Was it rushed? I mean it's been 26 years...
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: great semi-remake, some puzzles have changed or are missing but there is a whole new set that have replaced them. this is nearly how i imagined the world of riven from the original 2d frame by frame moving game. world building is beautiful, runs pretty smoothly, not perfect (day 1 no updates yet) but very good. some small bugs. still have not completed the remake with about 5-6 hours so far, im expecting at least another 2-4 hours until finished, and was told some of the puzzles are randomized every play-through for repeatability. if you like puzzle games that can be a bit convoluted or sometimes just no sense of direction, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Liked it a lot. I did not play original and game structure reminded me of Outer Wilds. You explore and collect information, and when you have enough information you can finally solve large puzzles. Story and lore are quite interesting and world itself is pretty unique.It looks beautiful and is much more impressive than Myst remake. There are some occasional stutters, but overall it works fine.The only issue is that game ruined marble puzzle for me. Gehn's journal contains picture of directions and shapes which points to the dome and exactly matches dome structure. But if you try to match shapes using this information, you fail. It does not help that puzzle has no feedback loop: solution either works or not. I do not understand why that piece of incorrect information was added to the game, as puzzle can be solved without it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Although there are a lot of pros and cons for me, I recommend this remake - simply because it's stunningly beautiful. I loved every second of the visuals. I don't liked the heavy changes that were made to the puzzles - especially the biggest one. Instead of a more modern version that is a bit less unfair, it got replaced by an equally other weird puzzle. Also the use of the Rebel lense felt like something a classic Cyan game just shouldn't have. But otherwise, this was an amazing trip back to my childhood with lots of cool new stuff to discover.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just about to beat it, but I'll write my review now. After remaking Myst about a dozen times, the one I really wanted Cyan to do was Riven...and finally it's here. I've always preferred Riven to Myst because the world was just better realized and had more depth. Yeah, there were some really crazy puzzles in the original that frustrated many but there were just as many "aha!" puzzles that kept it going.Okay, so I really thought this would be a straight-up remake and then I  and thought...okay, this isn't the same at all. Think Riven Remixed and you'll have a good idea of what this remake is all about. Sure...the character models aren't great compared to the FMV cutscenes from the original, but that's such a minor part of the narrative/game that I don't even care. The new puzzles/mechanics are really awesome and that's really all that matters.If you liked OG Riven...you don't want to miss this.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The penultimate version of Riven. It takes all of the obtuse puzzles and open ended to the point of annoying mechanics and rewrites the game to be smart, breathtaking, and challenging.I was at first apprehensive of them changing some core elements of my beloved Riven. However after beating it and getting most if not all endings; I can say this is an amazing game! It literally felt like they took the still CG slides and made it all real time. Unreal 5 takes the cake as producing the closest thing to what you remember in the original CG slides with no sacrifices in beauty.The ONLY thing I will say I'm not a fan of is them removing FMV for the 3d Characters. Sometimes they are janky and I just felt connected to the performances of the originals. This is my ONLY gripe. The other changes that they made are really just amazing.All in all if you want a good 20 hour puzzle game and chill walking atmosphere game where you feel transported to a place with rich lore and cool ideas being presented, this is your game!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Im going to have to give this a guarded yes,  for a stand alone remake of the classic Riven game it is still very enjoyable and I am happy that so many new players get to experience a bit of the wonder the original game has.     Graphics are crisp, its a beautiful world to explore.  Lots of nostalgia as you wander around familiar yet changed worlds.   The soundtrack is the same, with most of the ambiance of the original.   Its a seamless play, no gltches.  Playing on epic settings and there is no lag, though start up loading screen and some transitions are long.    Its nice to plug and play, no fiddling with workarounds with the original to get around the old programming   I really enjoyed the new areas, puzzles and exploration, it felt like a new game at times.Now for the bad.  Its not Riven.  They took out alot of the exploration, all the tiny and huge flavor sounds, beeps, boops, doo daws, thingamijiggies and animations that made each world a wonder to explore, charming and at times horrifying with realization of what went on.   it was maddening in that you just knew the tiniest detail was vital for solving those infamous puzzles.  Notes were mandatory.   They took away the huge reward for solving those world puzzles, the linking books that took you to a whole new world with new sound tracks, exploration.   Each world was a stand alone environment, felt natural.    This Riven is a shell.   a beautiful one, still wondrous to explore, but empty.   The separate worlds are crammed into the main one and seem incongruous to the environment.the incredibly bad.  the in game characters.  their rendering is atrocious, they interrupt flow and pacing.  really ruined the lonely desolation of the worlds.  too busy and unnecessary.   old riven it was such a shock to see another soul, it was very eerie and alarming.  here they just plunk em down. its still a good adventure game.   I would highly recommend players also buy a copy of original Riven on GOG and give it a try.   you will need a walkthru but its worth it.  (the gog version works, im afraid the steam versions of myst and riven were not working last time i tried, they may have gotten them working by now as its been years, but i doubt it.)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely phenomenal remake. If you enjoy puzzle games on any level and a very rich universe and story then definitely pick this one up.The developers should be very proud of themselves, and my only hope is that Cyan are able to continue making these detailed and lived in worlds I love discovering.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome in VR, better than Myst VR and Firmament VR. 9/10.Works great with Index, but you need a fast gpu for optimal graphics. In this game, motion smoothing is your friend, not your enemy :-)Tested using RTX 3090, i9 10900K, 32GB 3200MHz and Win10 Pro. Using Index 80 Hz to push res to the max (I'm using res 400%, DLSS Performance, Epic graphics - with motion smoothing, the games looks amazing and feels like 80 fps).
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this puzzle adventure! I had no nostalgia for this game, so this was a new game for me and I thoroughly enjoyed it. The environments looked amazing and the environmental storytelling was good. Took me around 8 hours to beat and the puzzles were just the right difficulty for me, who doesn't play too many puzzle games. Would highly recommend!I only have 2 major complaints:1: I had my character freeze completely 3 times during my playtime, had to fully restart the game to fix it. Luckily there's good autosave so I lost no progress or had to redo any puzzles.2. No option for plain text. The game has all its notes and diaries in handwritten cursive, which at points is extremely hard to read to the point I had to start guessing words and sentences. By the midpoint i just gave up reading them since there was so much to read and it became tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing the OG Myst and Riven alongside my family, trying to work out the puzzles as a team. Especially Riven stood out as a very special game with its worldbuilding, and visually made a huge impression on me as a kid. The one caveat of the original was that it was borderline too difficult for us to complete even working through it together. With this new remake, to me it feels more intuitive, immersive, and just the right amount of challenge, and amazingly extremely accurate to the original (it looks absolutely stunning), the exception being the puzzles which have been changed up in some surprising ways (personally, in a good way).I followed this project over the years eagerly waiting any news and updates from the Starry Expanse team, and now seeing it finished feels totally unreal (no pun intended) and like a dream come true. From the music and visuals to the lore and story, it is everything I was imagining it would be. I did encounter a few bugs playing on Steam Deck, but nothing major that prevented progression.Thanks Cyan and the Starry Expanse team for reviving my childhood nostalgia and fulfilling their dream to become fully immersed in this beautiful world!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, but.........................  like for the previous gqme version how mqny time did i have to wait for an animation to finish... Even if I was understanding the over-thought "puzzles" (making correspondance/translations of numbers, places or many symbols) made me question more and more the logics behind (for example ), this was the reproach i had on previous Riven game, making them look very complex by spreading the pieces all over the islands do not make them complex but just feel boring (because of the long animations going back and forth). And I do not even mention the screenshots that become difficult to read when consulting them afterwards (whether for reading symbols or colors is really tricky, better writing things done). It is not that I am disappointed, my feelings are quite split when finishing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's Riven 2024, a very hard, (you've ben warned) puzzle game. It's different than the original in certain details and puzzles, and it looks a lot better. It has some pretty nice puzzles. The series has a story, some of which is rather original, but unfortunately the characters are not well written. Many character decisions and motivations (including the players) are a case of "What? Really? Why?". So I'd say it's neither good nor bad, but a tiny bit more on the bad side.Why?: 1. If you kind of know what you're doing, you can play through in less than 14 hours and I remembered no details from the old version and took my time (apart from looking up 2-3 details; you can easily miss certain objects as some areas are very dark or you're looking at things from the wrong angle).  You can definitely play this a lot faster. And the reason it takes so long is that you're travelling back and forth between places which takes a lot of time. So the "fun" is over rather soon. 2. SPOILER ALERT....Even the good ending sucks. The guy you did all of this hard work for including saving his wife, has nothing better to do than leaving you to die and does so for no apparent reason. He could have just offered the player to touch his book just as his wife did seconds earlier and everything would have been fine. Terrible terrible writing.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely insane remake. Loved every second of what I've seen so far. A few puzzles have changed, but given the fact that its changed to full 3d/VR from point and click, I think the changes are more than welcome. The detail, the design, and the thought that went into this is absolutely astounding, Highest of recommendations if you're a fan of the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan changed a few things around but the things they added or changed make sense lore-wise and add greater context to the world. It's all around very faithful to the original and only has a few minor bugs I am sure will get patched out. Be careful on the sub though, I got soft locked in a perma-loop once.I definitely recommend this game to seasoned fans or just fans of puzzle games in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews. I've been a gamer since I was 8 years old until 41. I was thinking to finally dismiss gaming 'cause the games that exist nowadays bore me. And by the way, at my age you don't have so much time to play, because of duties that a man has to care about. But I always checked the destiny of Cyan. I had so many good times with their adventures and puzzle. I never found again the atmosphere they created, worlds that you can understand with time and patience and the spellbound their environments and stories had on me. I've been pleased to hear the good news with Obduction: Cyan is on the road again! And since then, I think that Rand is taking the right way, confirmed by the game I'm playing right now. This remake is a work of art and love. The assemble of all sceneries of the old game I constructed in my mind are here in 3D, before my eyes. Everything I remembered is enhanced. Same chilling, same awe. I literally lost many minutes staying in a scene and simply look and stare, amazed. Are there better game with better graphics out there? Obviously. Are there more exciting and dynamic games out there? Absolutely. But if you lived in the golden age of good games and you're bored like me (and you have some years on your shoulders) this is a must to play and experience. This game is like a good book (maybe a linking book?) that you can open when you want to relax and stimulate your mind. And what is very important to me, you can close that book whenever you want, without the stress that games nowadays give as a standard rule. My hope is to see the entire myst series remake. I expect to se Exile next. Go on Rand, make the like of us happy while we "age" together! =)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven 2024 is vastly different than the game I am so used to. A lot of things have changed, including expected pathways are gone or blocked. It is a totally new and fresh experience. I'm running the game on PC, a lot of the scenes don't load right away, NPC's appear headless for a few moments, animated vehicles lag quite a bit the first time you ride them. It is something I hope will improve in time. The CGI characters, honestly, look like something from 12 years ago. I understand why they went with CGI, a lot of the actors are much older or dead. I remember getting to the sub was fairly easy, now it's hidden away and I cannot imagine how to get to it now. I'm 5 hours in, only 1 crash, and 1 place I got trapped by unrezzed statues lol So all in all not bad for a new game! I will write a more detailed review once I finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original Riven, but this is fantastic. It could do with an option to skip or speed up travel scenes, because these take pretty long, and are common, because it's not always clear where you're supposed to go. But my god, the puzzles in this game are simply spectacular. They are some of the most elegant and interesting puzzles I've ever come across in a game. The story is hard to follow at times, especially if you haven't played the first game. But it's kind of told in an "after the fact" manner - a bunch of things happen, and later you find a journal explaining what you saw. It's difficult to keep up with all the details sometimes, but it's a cool story. It's really beautiful as well, with gorgeous graphics and lifelike environments. Highly recommended overall!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of the original games (yes, even End of Ages) and the books. I'd been looking forward to playing this since I heard about the Starry Expanse Project years ago. I enjoyed the Myst remake a couple years ago and this hit about the same. It's somewhere between a remake and a re-imagining. The new things that were added didn't feel out of place. I think the weakest parts of the game were the character animations, as well as the tram and cart rides. They didn't quite feel as exhilarating as the original. Maybe it was the jittering, maybe it was the sound quality. It just wasn't as much fun to ride from island to island.If you were a fan of the original, I think you'd enjoy this as well, but go in with the understanding that it isn't the original Riven.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: a great remaster, but DON'T go into it expecting it to be an exact copy of the original game - they've changed almost all of the puzzles and made lots of tweaks to the environments, which isn't a bad thing, but it threw me for quite a loop since myst 2021 was a much more straightforward adaptation.the only issues i had with the remaster are:-the comparatively lackluster character models/animations. they were better than myst 2021 though-cutscenes cannot be skipped like they could in the original game, which makes commuting between islands take forever-like the original, i'm feeling iffy on how the rivenese are depicted... it felt to me like a mashup of stereotypes about [insert any non-white culture here], but some of the things we know about the rivenese actively contradict those stereotypes in a good way, so?????????? i do think overall the game was very critical of colonialism, especially with gehn's character, so that's a good thing.otherwise, this is a very solid remaster. 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is... honestly a bad game. Full of back-tracking, with most of the puzzles boiling down to finding that one hidden button that you missed.I also tried playing it in VR, but the experience was not very good. - Shadows only render if they are visible from the left eye, makes everything weird to look at- The screen goes black if you move close to a wall while in some cutscenes, like at the start, even with the camera being visibly away from the actual wall!- Some menus render in front of your hands and the aim lineIt's a product of its time, with a mediocre story, and mechanics that are a fun gimmick at first, but quickly become repetitive when you have to wait for the same animation to play for the 100th time as you back-track once again because you missed something.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: About as perfect of a remake as you can get. The puzzles and a few other things have been reworked, keeping the game fresh for both veterans like myself of the original 1997 game, and new players alike. I would highly recommend getting The Riven Companion Guide with the game if you're not used to these kinds of puzzle solving games, just in case you get stuck and need a small hint here or there. As a veteran myself, I needed to briefly use it for one small part.Cyan Worlds has truly knocked it out of the park with this remake. From both the quality of the worlds, to the quality of the new character models for everyone, faithful to the original games in both visuals and audio (they carried over the original game's music, along with new tracks), I really can't think of a single flaw without nitpicking.I'd give it a full 5/5. Would highly recommend picking this up!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven was so hugely influential to me in my earlier gaming years. I played the whole series and read the books, but Riven is still the best. The remake is a beautiful tribute to the original, while not letting us veteran players waltz through like we wrote the place. I appreciate the love and effort that went into this game, the higher-quality beauty of this world I love, and the changes made to still keep me on my toes. Thanks for this lovely gift.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games ever and the remake doesn't disappoint.  Really it's more of a reimagining in some ways and even experienced players will find new and unexpected things.  All of the changes felt like they were made for internal logic and consistency in the world and not arbitrarily.  The only thing that's a downgrade are the 3D character models replacing live actors but that's pretty much an unavoidable compromise to make this VR compatible and free-roam.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A rare experience that fully invites one into another world — an anthropologically rich fictive culture, a society torn apart on a crumbling reality in thrall to an ersatz God. There are additions here that expand and fortify the 1997 masterpiece including some breathtaking moments that produce both awe and sorrow. For someone whose childhood was indelibly stamped those decades ago, this was like tying a tourniquet around the arm and mainlining pure nostalgia. I can't quite imagine what this must be like for a complete newcomer but this represents a unique game whose holistic puzzle design will leave one seeing connections between seemingly discrete challenges and I would argue, is far more intuitive and surmountable than the abstractions of its predecessor, .A stunning achievement but one that requires patience and scrutiny.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This remake is simply wonderful. Riven looks like how I'd always imagined it to be back in the original game. Cyan have taken the opportunity to change some of the puzzles, doing things that simply weren't possible back in the original and making the 5th Age just a bit more magical. If you're a returning player like me, you'll actually have to use your brain and your notepad in order to complete the game. It doesn't feel like playing Riven for the first time again, it's more like hearing a new story from an old friend. I fully recommend picking it up if you're a Myst/Riven fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I was amazed to see this show up on my store page I have been a long time must and riven fan! Loved the original point and click Adventure puzzle but as a kid I always wondered what the world was like in person and the VR scratched that itch perfectly the world is absolutely stunning and even playing the game before still feels completely new and I Love it! 10/10 would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The remake is just brilliant. The puzzles are masterfully executed and perfectly integrated into the lore and environment, the feeling you get when you piece everything together is priceless. Visually this game is stunning, definitely one of the best looking game of the year. More than a few places have left me in awe, the level of details and environmental story telling is just insane. Some of the new places have gotten my heart race of excitement...Definitely one of the best game of the genre, in line wild Outer Wilds. I cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing remaster in terms of graphic upgrades and full 3D world. Unfortunately the puzzles have changed, and are somewhat easier, but still the essence of what they did was kept. Would love a version with the original content in tact, but I can't really complain since this comes with an amazing VR version too. Stuttering is present in both versions, but they are working on it and since its slow paced, it doesn't detract too much. Overall it was an amazing nostalgia trip that made me smile many times over, thanks for making it!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: 9.8/10I was giddy about the original game when I got it for Christmas as a kid. Let me simply say this - this is how you do a remake. A few clunky animations and glitches aside, which I am sure will get patched, this is a masterpiece that improves on a masterpiece. I truly appreciate the fidelity to the original while still updating and modernizing it, while also remixing most of the puzzles to be new and fresh while still feeling like they belong in the universe of the D'ni.They don't make games like this anymore, which is truly a shame. If you're on the fence, just buy it. Do it. It's worth the adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: This new remake + reimagining of RIVEN is hands-down my Game of the Year. I was completely blown away. Cyan Worlds somehow improved an experience I didn't think could be improved. It's like stepping inside the best speculative fiction you've ever read and becoming a protagonist.1997's Riven was already the most compelling fictional world I'd ever explored, but there are some changes and expansions that the marketing for the new version hasn't even hinted at. I gasped. I laughed. At one point I cried. At one point I almost jumped out of my chair. Five stars out of five.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.I was 3 years old when the first Riven released, I still remember watching my brother and dad figure out this puzzle of a game. Some of my earliest childhood memories are getting lost in this world. I personally had no idea what I was doing, it was just incredible being able to point and click and adventure.Revisiting it in 2024 is just pure nostalgic bliss. And it feels amazing being able to solve this on my own. It's incredible how well Riven stands up after all these years.The visual storytelling is second to none.Tips for newcomers to this age: bring a pen and pencil, avoid hitting the 'sprint' button, take your time.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a surreal experience seeing it all in moving 3D, even after playing through the Myst remake. Will be nice if one day video actors can be incorporated in 3D environments well. The game overall is beautiful and not having the images cut away makes it all make more sense spatially and I am understanding it all a lot more than I did as a child. It's nice to get lost in the world of it, I can't wait to get to the beehive, I could never get that far as a kid.

_childDocuments_.review: I realize this isn't going to be a very popular opinion, but unless you get this game in a great sale, I would take a pass.  By the way, this will be the first game I've ever reviewed that I didn't recommend.1. It's esoteric to the point of frustration.  I've watched multiple people play this and the reactions are all the same - basically what the heck is going on?  That should be the feeling during the first minutes of a new game, not the entire game.2. For those of us who loved Myst, this is NOT Myst.  Not that it needed to be, but you can play and enjoy Myst and still dislike Riven.  I loved Myst, including on VR.3. I enjoy exploring a virtual world - every nook and cranny.  But the game areas were difficult to move back and forth between, and the fast travel mechanism was incredibly annoying.4. VR - I bought this because it had VR support.  I played a majority of the game in VR, and found the control interaction to be hit and miss.  Maybe it was just that I was already frustrated, but when I finally ended up going back to the PC screen to play, I wasn't much happier.  I can usually tell ahead of time the games that I will return to in a couple years and replay - and there have been bunches.  Sadly, this isn't one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Some thirty years ago, my brother and I were two little kids that hopped on our family's humble Macintosh IIci and became enamored and awestruck by an immersive 3D-rendered world that was Myst and then later Riven. It was very different from any of the sprite-filled 16 or 32-bit games at the time and seemingly beyond the scope of what two tiny grade schoolers would comprehend.We'd confuse our teachers as to why we would go to school drawing black triangles on the corners of our composition notebooks, complemented by a rune on front and square drawing on the first page, and then treating them as mystical teleportation books (and yes, with the added sound effects). Or bewilder our family by walking around the house with our hands stretched outright, "clicking" our way across the house. There was also never a shortage of Myst or Riven island drawings, or increasingly ornate Linking Books, strewn about our family and friends homes and classrooms. My brother even created an Atrus outfit for Halloween once. Eventually, my interests turned elsewhere in games, but Riven always maintained an impact on my brother. He even promised me that he would one day work for Cyan. At the time, I kind of shrugged it off as a cute but unrealistic dream.Riven had inspired my brother so much that for Christmas one year he didn't ask for toys or video games like a typical kid would, but instead a complicated 3D modeling software called StrataVision 3D, the very same software used to render scenes in the original Myst. I had no idea what my Dad was thinking to get his grade-school child an expensive piece of software that he may have no idea how to use, let alone for however long, but he did. With only the paperback manual, my brother went on to teach himself how to craft an impressive 3D island-world directly inspired by Temple Island in Riven and navigate it using HyperCard. And throughout his school years he continued to model and draw art for many of his projects because of this. Eventually, as an adult, he finally broke into the gaming industry and I figured that was the end of it.Much more recently, I returned home after living ten years abroad as an expat. I came home to find his computer on and that some kind of game was running on it. I was shocked to find out that he created a welcome home game in Unreal Engine to greet me. And woe and behold, the first thing I'm greeted by is the very island-world that he created as a kid. It was instantly recognizable and only something that we would understand, as we shared it together so many years ago. Somehow he was able to painstakingly port it over from that old 3D software and turned it into a playable adventure world. It was a small game to play through, but it was chock-full of inside jokes and childhood references to Macintosh games or pop culture we once used to enjoy as kids.I was also surprised when he told me that he got into the Starry Expanse Project, who were working on the remake of his favorite childhood game, Riven. Little did I realize that some thirty years later my brother would come full circle from the dreams and imaginations of his childhood self to end up contributing to the development of the very game that inspired him to break into the gaming industry in the first place. The fact that he achieved his childhood dream and pursued his inspiration due to this game has left me incredibly astonished and proud. Truly, there is no one in life that you will know longer than your own sibling and I only have one. I love him very much and this accomplishment is a memory I will treasure.I am buying this game once more to show how grateful and supportive I am to Starry Expanse and Cyan in remaking such a fantastic world and story to get lost in once again. Thank you for the impact and inspiration you've had on our lives.Edit: Clarifying that he was involved with Starry Expanse not Cyan.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning, and runs like a dream on my mid-level gaming laptop. The game's auto detected graphics settings were medium - high and I bumped it up to epic mode and it still runs nearly seamlessly. _childDocuments_.review: It feels like Cyan did everything right, here.They made no compromise in remaking the original world from 97 into one that feels real and compelling to walk through in the 3rd dimension. The attention to detail, both in the recreation of the original environments and sets, as well as bringing those environments into a modern graphical context is clearly visible. There was a lot of care put into this project, and I am happy to see that.The puzzles differ slightly from the original, in some ways for the better (better integrating puzzles into the world, having them make more sense in context, etc.), but they are still pretty rewarding to solve. I think between Cyan's current track of modern remakes, Riven far outshines the 2020 Myst remake in just about every way. There is a lot more integrity preserved this time around, and while my current recommendation for playing Myst in the modern day still teeters between the 2020 remake and realMyst, I have basically 0 issue recommending the 2024 Riven remake to anyone interested in pursuing the Myst series.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Solid remake. Well worth it if you're a fan of the original and you can't go wrong if this is your first foray into Riven. If you've played the original you'll notice a few differences from the 1997 version, but they are changes for the better. Only thing I prefer from the original is the FMV actors, but I understand why they had to make the change to CGI characters. They look comparable to any other modern video game character so you won't even notice if you've only ever played the remake.Playing Myst is not necessary to enjoy the game, or appreciate the story, but if you can swing it get the Definitive Collection bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A stunning remake, the original stands as one of the most engaging worlds I have ever visited and this version of it is even more beautiful, dynamic and vibrant. If you have any interest in slow intricate puzzles this is one of the best of all times, and this version is by far the most accessible.While some puzzles are easy to miss, all are signposted in some way and once you understand that even the more convoluted ones start to open up. Everything was placed deliberately and taking notes is vital, you never what information will be needed later to solve a puzzle but this leads to my one gripe: Flicking to and from your journal is a little clunky particularly in VR. This is a major missed opportunity and I found myself using a physical pen and paper more than the in-game systems.There are some legitimate concerns I have seen raised around some of the new puzzles, and they do give a different vibe to the original. But they fit so seamlessly into the world that they feel like they could have been in the original game. They are not worse just different. While I have not played since I was a kid, I was surprised by how many puzzles I remembered how to solve, so everything new that I had not experienced was a refreshing surprise that I adored.TLDR: One of the best ways to enjoy one of the best puzzle games of all time. If you hate puzzle games give it a skip, but otherwise you owe it to yourself to experience the world of Riven.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I will never forget begging the game shop clerk to let me try out this mysterious game I had found while browsing the PlayStation section: It had what looked like an alien knob celery on the cover and appeared enticing. The clerk begrudgingly put  in the demo unit, which was meant for adult paying customers, not 11 year old kids with no money. Instantly I was taken to a world unlike anything else I had ever seen. I didn't know about , or -likes. After five minutes of walking around Temple Island my demo session was over and I had learned: Games could be more than virtual playgrounds for kids. Many years later I tried to get into  for real, bought the version on Steam, the one on iOS, but never got very far, to be honest. Now, in 2024, I'm playing this stunning Unreal Engine showcase and I'm in awe. Getting to walk ALL AROUND all this puzzle machinery in full 3D helps so much with actually understanding what is expected from me. Currently I'm switching between the 2D and VR versions, and both have their advantages: The 2D version runs like a dream, in luxurious high definition, not an ounce of jank to be found. VR is a different story. While there are plenty of comfort features – I can actually use smooth locomotion without getting sick thanks to the vignette feature – the shadows look all wrong and flickery, you easily clip into objects and the resolution obviously is limited to what your kit delivers (I'm using a Quest 2), taking away some of the visual sheen. I probably won't play the whole game in VR, but getting to see what different islands look like in stereoscopic 3D is such a privilege, I imagine telling that to 11 year old me, that one day in the future I would explore theses places with a computer strapped to my face, amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I like puzzle games & VR but I don't recommend Riven in its current implementation.Graphically its really well presented, the art style/originality and quality are very good my principal issue with Riven is pacing and gameplay. The main issue is that once you are well into the game there is no way you can progress unless you start making handwritten notes about things that you learn... how the hell do you do that in VR? You can't you are forced to remove the headset or go back into the game in monitor mode.The second issue is its very easy to miss something in VR that would otherwise be much clearer or obvious to monitor mode, which then makes the game difficult to work with... its not a puzzle at that point its just frustration having to retrace your steps looking for some detail you may or may not have missed or retry interaction objects that should just work.Finally I get the need to not spoon feed players, but in Riven knowledge is given to you in such a poorly thought out way its almost as if they assume you've played Riven before and come to the game with outside knowledge. For the most part things just don't make any kind of sense, you move through the islands completely unaware of what is going on around you with no real purpose other than to find things to do. When you are given some knowledge its dumped on you, who wants to read a huge hand written journal in VR or notes that you can't carry around with you or maybe you can but you can't get it to work...In summary its not been properly play tested in VR imho, you have to rely on external information to make sense of what is happening making the experience needlessly frustrating. Yes its hard but hard in the wrong way imho because things are too easily missed and not explained well if at all.

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 35 years of gaming, if one asks me what my favorite game of all time is I would answer without hesitation 1997’s Riven the Sequel to Myst. I was 15 when I played it for the first time, and it took me several months to finish it. No Internet back then :)If you like this type of games and have enjoyed Myst go for it! It is a well-made fun puzzle game that looks awesome with a great story for you to discover. More important, it is Riven on easy mode. Having said that, I urge you to play the original simply because it is a masterpiece and an experience like no other.I have mixed feelings for this remake. I totally enjoyed revisiting Riven islands and be able to walk freely but… that's it for me. Although it is visually stunning it felt soulless. I found the character animation and voice acting mediocre. However, my biggest problem with the remake is the puzzles. In the 1997’s Riven, you are placed in a world you understand nothing about it. The only way to solve the notoriously hard puzzles is to understand the environment, the people living in this world, their culture and their relationship with the main characters, Cathrin and Ghen. No Myst-like hints for puzzles, no nothing. This is not the case with the remake. The remake offers some hints for puzzle solving, that make no sense. For example, Would I prefere a remake exactly the same as the original? I really don't know. I probably tend to beleive that there was no need for a Riven remake and I only wanted one for the sake of nostalgia and my need to see more of this magnificent world Cyan has built back in 1997.I wish steam had an option other than "recommended" and "not recommended" since, for me, Riven Remake falls somewhere in the middle. By no means this is a bad game...but it is not even close to the masterpice 1997's Riven was.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the original, oh man, this is so good. SO good. The changes and additions to the game are absolutely an enhancement, and I'm so happy to be back. This is what happens when people who designed the original get to design the remake. I am not disappointed in the least!If you haven't played Riven before, it's one of the best exploration/ knowledge based puzzle games of all time. It's beautiful, engaging, and (let's be real) a masterpiece. Many of us have known this for decades, but it's really great to be able to share this with new players!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a fan of Cyan games for a long time. I personally enjoy playing Riven, and it is one of those memorable games from my childhood. I was super excited to hear and eventually buy the new game. This remake is truly what most remakes wish they could be, a faithful update and improvement to the game. Cyan went beyond simply remaking the game in a 3D environment. Puzzles that needed better explanations and more logical solutions were improved. All in all, Riven easily knocked it out of the park.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Cyan Games!  I played Uru almost exclusively for years when it first came out and then played Myst and Obduction in VR.  These games are absolutely phenomenal and all these games mentioned, along with Riven remake have one thing in common:  They contain stunning, explosive set pieces and stories that truly blow my mind for around ten hours each before they become redundant.  I never finished a single title.  I never wanted to and never really felt I needed to.  I get everything I want from these games within the first ten hours, and then I’m done.Riven is my favorite of all the games mentioned.  playing without a guide, figuring everything out as I go along, wide mouthed and amazed at the sheer imagination and imagery contained - truly a wonderful experience.  The same experience I had with all the games mentioned.  Even though I think I'm done with the game for now, the experience those ten hours gave me are probably the most intense and satisfactory of any game I played this year and I doubt I will experience the same level of intrigue and fascination with any game coming out this year.  Highly recommended - even if you enjoy for a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: NO SPOILERS REVIEWTL:DRFor me, a 10 out of 10 experience. Genuinely loved everything they did in the game, this maintains everything you loved about the original Riven while adding enough new areas and puzzles to make this adventure feel fresh and exciting. Plays brilliantly, runs smoothly, visually stunning, original OST is present and correct. Myst and Riven fans will love this masterpiece all over again.FULL REVIEW:This is a stunning remake of Riven. A game that looks almost exactly like the original game but adds enough new areas and new puzzles to make the experience feel fresh, new and just as interesting as if you had picked it up for the very first time all over again.Visually it's amazing, especially if you have a good 4K TV or monitor. Crank it up to 4K and prepare for your jaw to drop at each and every location. The soundtrack from the original is present and correct in each area, untouched, exactly as you remember it. A really nice touch. Gameplay wise, it plays like a modern adventure game. It's fully free roam, there's no point and click option in here. You can explore every inch of this amazing world in full free roaming and beautiful 3D. It supports VR too, though I do not have a headset so I cannot say anything as regards playing the game that way.I'm happy to say that the voice acting is as excellent as it always was. Atrus lines appear to have been re-recorded, as have Catherines but Gehns original voice acting (by the late, great John Keston) is present and correct, which is a really nice touch. His original performance was amazing in the original Riven so it's great to see that they haven't changed that.There are a few faults in here, though they're all minor nitpicks. There are some huge stutters as the game physically pauses (albeit very briefly) and loads in the section ahead of you, especially noticeable in the domes and on entering new areas. Also the 3D character models are a bit weak, albeit they are a lot stronger than the models used in the Myst remake. Atrus and Gehn do genuinely look quite good and move pretty well but the other character models in the game look a bit awkward at times. There is no option (at the time of writing this review) to revert to the FMV actors of old so just make note of that if that's an option that you would prefer.As I said, minor nitpicks overall.I very highly recommend this game to adventure game fans and especially to Myst series fans and fans of the original Riven alike. This is everything you will want it to be and more. A brilliant achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: New Riven is everything the original was, but immensely more enjoyable due to the improved navigation and modern technology. It is just fresh enough too that there is still a good deal of problem solving, exploration, and discovery to be made for veterans of the original.Riven is a a beautiful game even on lower end hardware, and audio is absolutely part of the experience. Remember, audio was one of the few things that helped you feel the world was alive in the original game and not just a series of still photos. Be sure to play this game with good headphones or speakers!The character animation is pretty dang good, but not flawless. There are some awkward movements and clipping issues, but we aren't talking about an expensive AAA game here and I think we can easily forgive the rough edges. It's certainly an improvement over the previous Myst title.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic remake of the 1997 classic with a couple changes here and there, though in my opinion they're certainly not bad ones. Except for the fact that all the standard doors now slide to accommodate VR folks, eugh.The only glaringly obvious issue I have with it otherwise are the character models. I recall seeing better back in Far Cry 3 and that was 12 years ago. But given you don't see them very often, this isn't the biggest issue, especially because the environment design and texturing is top-notch. The golden dome especially just looks real, I can't believe how good the texture work on that is specifically, and the whole of the game looks absolutely stunning besides which.If you're a fan of the original game or even if you've never played it, this is an easy recommendation. It's faithful enough that even a new player should have no problems jumping in and getting a similar experience.Edit: Looking at this again with a like-for-like comparison of the original, I'm surprised how much was changed and cut. There are many paths which no longer exist, and comparing screenshots to screenshots from the same locations, some areas feel very much smaller and likewise the distance between areas seems to have been shortened in some cases (albeit not too dramatically). If you're a fan of the genre you'll definitely need to play the original still for the authentic experience, but this remake is still fine all the same.
