_childDocuments_.review: Moon first released in 1997 for the original Playstation but unfortunately never made its way outside Japan and never got officially located until 2020 when a worldwide Switch re-release of this lovely game happened, it wouldn’t be until 2021 when this adventure would arrive to PC but here we are, let me go straight to the point, Moon was a very special, weird and lovely adventure and while I will recommend it for everyone, I know for sure not everyone will enjoy this game due to its weirdness and perhaps structure but if you are a bit interested, I invite you to keep reading this review and find out if it’s the game you want to play or, more importantly, the game you need to play right now.We are a kid who’s playing his RPG “Moon” on the Gamestation when all the sudden gets transported into the game’s world, Love-de-Gard, as a nameless entity referred as kid or your nickname, sooner rather than later you will realise that you are inside the game and you will follow the storyline but with a catch, instead of the merciless Hero you came here to spread love among all living things and change the destiny of the creatures of this world. Saving the strange animals of this world, helping their inhabitants and most importantly, changing the fate of this world by spreading love, not violence.As you can see, the story of this game seems to be very RPG standard, you know, be the hero, save the kidnapped princess, slay the dragon and while that’s true, that’s NOT our story, we follow the same path as the hero but our objective is completely different, our presence in this world brings joy and hope for those who get slayed and kicked by the hero, who is a dumbass and a merciless vile character, in this world our objective won’t be kill the monsters but help them, chat and learn about the people who live in this world, explore the different places of this lovely place and of course, end the story in a different way.You will find this place both interesting and eccentric at times, there are countless references to the real world of the late 90’s - very early 00’s (trends that peaked in this era that started in the 90’s) and even some philosophy and metacommentary about you and the meaning of what you are doing, the further you go into this adventure, the clearer the picture becomes, this was a very special journey in which you will be able to see through the eyes of different inhabitants and that’s really special, in general I thought this approach of getting love by doing good actions for others was probably what I needed the most at the moment of this review after all what’s happening and happened to the world in the last few years, who would have guessed an old classic could give me a positivity boost just by giving me the option of making love and not war.Let’s talk about this world, Love-de-Gard is similar to an island in which all biomes fuse to create a colourful and varied place to explore and live, world is size limited though but please remember this is a 1997 game so it’s completely normal and yet, it feels big, condensed and deep.Castle Town, Mushroom forest, Technopolis or the Tropical fields are just a few examples of places you will find and explore during the adventure and you will see how each place feels different from others, every place has a distinctive style, type of characters and most importantly, new ways of getting love and spreading your good actions.Even though the game’s world is not really big, there a one-direction fast travel to a few locations of the map that will make your walks shorter, however, you won’t be able to return via the same method, you will have to go back in a normal way but the way is integrated it makes complete sense why and it’s very…. “Moon-y” hehe.When it comes to visuals, you can expect a PSX game with sharper details given the different panels we have nowadays but overall the visual aspect hasn’t been changed and, to be honest, I don’t think it needs to change anything, it’s a product of its moment, game is 25 years old and as so it’s being shown, however, the art style and the imaginary put in this game is lovely and mind blowing.Animals, characters and locations do have a peculiar and distinctive aspect, I think they even used real clay models for the monsters back in the day and you can see how they look in here, a real world touch in a game that talks about the thin boundary of reality and fakeness? Amazing touch here.What you can see in the screenshots it’s what you will find in the game, I found it to be very pleasant and I enjoyed the visual style of the game.Sound and music is another aspect I liked, character voices are non-real language gibberish, quite common in RPGs as you know, and that was fun but the cool aspect of this segment is music, all music was composed back in the day by independent musicians and you can see the vast variety of styles and themes, I think they nailed it, if I had to name my favourite track right now, I think I would go with “Kera Ma-Go” which is very cheerful.Gameplay has a few things to keep in mind, first of all, even though it’s called Moon RPG it’s NOT a JRPG, it is an adventure that refers to itself as RPG as a metacommentary from what happens inside the game, so if you came here expecting levelling up by fighting and getting new gear, forget about it, you level up by completing tasks and saving animals.Saving animal souls is easy, read the description of each body you find (some are really hidden, in case you want to complete all of them) and learn what are the requirements to make the souls appear, once the animal soul is accessible, just hug it, easy, right? One button. Completing tasks is something a bit more tricky, it requires objects, reading the details of the conversations and thinking a bit about the clues, but they are quite simple mechanically speaking, it’s always hugging, getting an object, stocking an object or using music, simple as that.The clock, you must keep in consideration the red arrow as it marks the moment you won’t be able to continue if you don’t sleep to change the day,  as you will be really tired, or by eating to extend the limit a bit to reach your bed on time before you collapse and game over reaches you.As I mentioned before, there’s also a fast travel option that works in one direction, you see those spiral roots? Well, keep those in mind.Gameplay loop is simple but there are tons of hidden interactions that you will appreciate and of course I didn’t mention a few things.When it comes to performance I played this game on Steam Deck and it’s officially “unsupported” . How so? Well, let me tell you that, like Valve said, Unsupported doesn’t mean the game doesn’t run on Deck, it means it might have a problem or two and well, they are right, it took me 15 hours to reach the ending and I only got 1 problem, on a very specific cinematic event game crashed but once I re-entered the game this didn’t happen and I continued perfectly fine.Playing process was painless and the experience was console-like, I installed it, the controller profile got configured automatically and deck did some background translation for some Windows processes, once the first boot was done, everything ran perfectly fine with no errors at all aside from that specific one, which I think might have to do with some codec translation in the background but I can’t be sure, this problem is likely not present on the regular windows version so rest assured this game will run well on your machine, it doesn’t consume that many resources.And that’s about it, Moon was exactly the game I needed right now and it delivered a wholesome experience that I won’t forget, I can’t recommend it enough to all of you even though I know this game is not for some of you, the very least I can do is to encourage you to play it and see if you like it, a timeless classic.Great job, Onion Games, you made it.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: To even attempt to describe just how wonderful and culturally important this game is would be a waste of my time and a waste of the time you could be spent playing it. Instead, one should go in completely blind EXCEPT for the official translated guide that Team Onion so lovingly (heh) put together for players to use. It explains basic functions for the player that would be hard to understand in-game AND it feels so nice to read. Is it a perfect game? No, far from it. But it is a game made by a team that truly loves video games and loves the player to bits. So please, don't be a hero.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: This game can often be very confusing and frustrating, and even the most dedicated fans will agree it's a bit of an acquired taste. The main gameplay is solving puzzles, most of which are less about finding a clever solution and more about figuring out the meaning behind vague and often really obtuse hints. It's absolutely okay to not enjoy this game, however widely praised it is by everyone.But moon is worth experiencing just for its cultural significance alone. It's a game you have to try out regardless whether you think you'll like it or not. And it's interesting not just in the historical context, but also as a work of art of sorts. The game has an extremely strange and fascinating surreal style that you won't find in any other media, which for many will outweigh its weaknesses.Note that this is a game where you need to be VERY attentive to all the hints and dialogue, explore every corner of the game world, and take notes for pretty much everything you see on screen, otherwise you will likely not get full enjoyment out of it.If you play for a couple of hours and it doesn't connect, feel free to stop, it's a long game and you don't have to torture yourself. But do at least give it a try. I assure you that no matter how much time you spend on it you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by stating  is not a perfect game. Just like Chulip, translation inaccuracies often turn somewhat vague puzzles into challenges much harder than they should be and end up hurting the experience. Furthermore, as seen on the , the originally planned ending was quite different from what we got, which clarifies why some things are left partially unexplained.Still, from the way the plot is conducted to the gameplay mechanics themselves, there's so much inspiring stuff to see here that telling anyone not to give it a try would be a crime. Stuff that any RPG would do well to take inspiration from, yet only Undertale did (and honestly, not as well as it could). If you're a fan of adventure and RPGs in general, I'd already list this as a must-play.Also, I'm not sure how different this version is from the previously released Switch version (the one I've played before), but it's a good sign that they've made the most relevant parts of the game's manual available if you press Tab. Maybe we can expect new easter eggs and mistranslation corrections?One way or another, be sure to give Moon a chance if you're looking for something different and oozing creativity. And if you like it, do consider trying out Chulip next. The setting is just as great, and if you had enough patience to reach Moon's ending, you already have what it takes.: Since I've mentioned this version could have extra stuff, I think it might be a good idea to add this piece of info from :"

_childDocuments_.review: a timeless masterpiece about diegesis, games as art and lovethis game hates everything about standard violent games, compulsive gaming and especially on which values we're absorbing while interacting with videogamesthis game is about what lies beyond entertainment: meaningeven if undertale's emotional core is a lot stronger since the characters are more present, moon is a much more sucinct and thematically deep approach to metalinguistics. Please, don't expect this to be Undertale, they're both great but for different reasons, even if they share a similar intention.obligatory for anyone who wants to study videogames instead of just playing them, just beware the main mechanic is basically waiting and the game revolves around being contemplative, so it's definitely not for everyonei loved it, a lot

_childDocuments_.review: Moon is probably one of my favorite RPG's of all time. It's a very relaxing experience where you don't have to worry too much about anything. Exploring and experimentation is encouraged. This is an older game, so checking out the manual is a big help (which you can find here):  If you have a few hours and want a unique RPG experience that really shows how games can be art, I highly recommend checking out this underrated gem. _childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest up front: I didn't finish this game. I played for quite a bit, and then I got to a point where I figured out what the main objective of the game was, then realised in order to get to the end, I'd have to deal with RNG, time-of-day sensitive events, and most importantly, one of the worst fishing minigames I've ever seen.But still, it's overall pretty interesting. I especially like how everything is a neat puzzle, how you have to pay attention to context cues, your environment, put multiple things together. It made my brain feel big. I like the world, the characters, and how both unhinged and grounded everything is. It's weird, but in a way that makes sense.In short, I really like the premise, the themes, and the overall ideas on display here. It's just the actual execution I have problems with. But then again, this game is over 25 years old, so I won't hold it too much against it. Games were literally built different back then.It is a recommendation because what it does, it does very well, and as a historical artifact, it is very compelling. I would definitely play a modern reinterpretation of this formula, with better controls, quality of life improvements, an in-game calendar, and less punishing timings. Oh, and a better fishing minigame. Or no fishing at all, that'd be good too.Although at that point I could just be playing Undertale again.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny and strange and full of creativity.  It's clear how this inspired Undertale, Majora's Mask, Dropsy, Petscop, etc.  It's a commentary on RPGs, made by former SquareSoft employees.  Experience an RPG from an outside perspective.  Time passes and characters have daily schedules which makes things feel more alive.  It plays a bit like a point-and-click adventure, though it's suitably non-linear, and if you ever get stuck, there's a wiki you can consult that will give you gentle hints in the right direction.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe i haven't written a review for this game yet despite it now being one of my fav games of all time. wonderful little adventure across a silly world with silly characters, with a deeper message about love and storytelling if you look for it. by modern standards, the slow burn pacing is a bit of an acquired taste. it has a day/night cycle and a weekly calendar, with some events only happening on very specific times that you'll have to figure it out from obtuse hints. its best to keep a guide on hand for whenever you feel stuck. despite that, everything about moon's presentation is designed to be best played at your own leisurely pace, and i rarely ever felt bored even when i was just walking from place to place.i highly recommend everyone giving this game a try even if it doesnt seem like something you'd be into! don't be a hero, experience the love :)

_childDocuments_.review: moon: Remix RPG Adventure (also referred to as just moon) is my favorite game of all time, and I've only discovered this masterpiece back 2 years ago in early 2020 and played for the first time when it released back in August of 2020 on Nintendo Switch. I understand that this game is sadly not for everyone but I do honest to god recommend everyone to give this game a shot once. Even with some annoying bits from time to time, playing through moon again and 100% it AGAIN really makes me realize that this game has aged beautifully. Kinda like Mario 64 where the camera controls are always ♥♥♥♥, it doesnt matter because Mario moves so gracefully 20+ years later.The game has a great sense of progression from the get go. I've seen alot of people complain about how the time mechanic "ruins this game", which I COMPLETELY disagree with. In the game it specifically states that "hey you are very VERY weak still, but with time youll be able to explore moon world with ease." so you need to play patiently and your reward for playing well and doing a set amount of things in a specific day is the ability to explore more, catch more animals,  and experience more of this game. I understand that this aspect of this game maybe what brings people away from the game, but im telling you having a little patience and trying to plan out what you can do in a day really helps and is worth it to experience this game.almost every other aspect of the game is just near perfect to me. The music (more specifically the purchasable MDs that you can get after you get your own house) is this beautiful compilation of all these different genres. The characters all have their own motivation and goals outside from how they may look on the outside. The designs of the NPCs and animals are amazing making the digital world they inhabit even more interesting. The story is the cherry ontop of this masterpiece of a game, not too much to overwhelm the player but just enough to prod your mind and keep you engaged throughout the entire game. Also the detail and hints that they dropped throughout the game were so deep, that I only noticed everything on my 2nd playthrough. Its absolutely how much detail they crammed into this old PS1 game.Now this game is not perfect, my main issues with the game are the late game (for 100 percenting) and the fishing mechanic. Some of the late game catches are just wait around for the soul to spawn at day, or wait around for the soul to spawn at night. Heck even some of the character missions in the last area had me just waiting around for night and sleeping for it to be a specific day. which is not what I've grown to love about this game. and the fishing, good LORD THE FISHING. just actually the worst thing about this game. and you have to fish ALOT in this game, for normal completion and for 100%ing. its just not fun, and horribly implemented. But even with these two stains, this game is still really REALLY good.moon is a once in a lifetime game that, for the longest time, was trapped due to languages but im now glad that it is readily available. Please try this game, there really is nothing truly like it. Even when the creators try to recreate/recapture the spirit, something is missing from the GOAT moon (note all of the love-de-lic legacy games are also bangers but i like moon the most :) ).
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: There's no neutral recommendation so I'll put this here: ONLY PLAY THIS IF YOU'RE GENUINELY CURIOUS about the game. Otherwise, I'd recommend to just watch an LP for it. _childDocuments_.review: (I've already got every piece of Love in the Switch version so ignore the low play time)The actual gameplay part is an acquired taste and an exercise in patience but the characters and writing are easily some of if not THE best I had ever experienced in a game.This game is everything I could have wanted since I recently fell in love with games like OFF and Yume Nikki after a childhood of playing Chibi-Robo, the latter I believe was made by some of the devs who worked on this too. Has the same dog, Tao, too!And that's not even to mention the excellent presentation of this game, every piece of music distills such pure emotion and childlike wonder, all the visuals are such a unique mix of 3D renders, claymation and traditional sprite art, all of it looks great, no matter if you have pixel blurring turnt on or off, easily the best looking PS1 game I have ever seen, it really hasn't aged a day.The only knock I could possibly give this game would be the price point, as an outsider it just looks like a 26 year old game with a translation patch on it, but I truly don't know how much effort went into the localization but I would imagine it must be a lot since it feels entirely appropriate to the time period of this game's initial release and never once broke my suspension of disbelief.TL;DR and less pretentious formulation: Cute game and dialogue makes me haha

_childDocuments_.review: It takes a lot of patience to play moon. The game is from the early PlayStation era, and it's riddled with a  of obtuse, archaic, and outright ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ puzzles-- even for its time. On top of that, you have to complete a vast majority of them to reach the end. You move around at a snail's pace, have huge potential to lose a ton of progress in the early game, and will spend a vast majority of time just waiting or wandering without any sense of direction. From a design perspective, it's outright awful. Once you've completed the small amount of easy, coherent puzzles, and reach your inevitable point of cluelessness, the game becomes a game of guessing and dumb luck, and is nearly impossible to beat without clairvoyance. So why the hell am I recommending it?What moon lacks in engaging, or better-put,  game-play, it makes up for with so much more-- EVERYTHING else, really. The sum of it's parts, I would call it. It's just so intriguing, exploring this vivid and wild setting. Moon is very ambitious in just about every sense, and the game is brimming with soul. Just look at it. Every corner turned when I DID make progress in the game got a reaction, and somehow made the tedium worthwhile. The title just continued to surprise me, for better (the encounters and characters) or for worse (the cryptic ass puzzles). It's an experience I can't compare to anything else, and this is why I think anyone who plays video games should play moon.See, if you're willing to see the game through to the end, it all comes full circle. Despite the imperfections and obtuseness, by the time I reached the end of the game, everything came together. It all made sense, and it only clicked because I had experienced what I did. This game speaks something  to those who have played it-- something obtuse and profound about the nature of certain things, and the only way to really understand what it has to say is to give it your time, despite the glaring flaws. It's not for everyone, but if you have the interest, the time and the patience, (and the humility to look up help), you'll walk away with an undeniable impression, and a lot to think about.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: There's something so charming about how it completely disregards directed game design in favor of encouraging the player to slow down and take everything in. How could you not when everything is so cute? It's fitting for this game about having patience for people to build a community dedicated to learning every bit of it. Once you get into a rhythm, even the slow walk speed is fun. It gives you time to take in the environments, which are the best EVER. Every JRPG needs claymation. It's also just really weird and funny. Timeless game. (The fishing minigame is evil though I cannot lie)

_childDocuments_.review: What a special game. I didn't realize until I had started playing that this was created by the studio and director of Chulip, which is another great game. The gameplay is very addicting, due to the satisfying, yet sometimes complicated puzzles. The cast is quirky and fun, the message is nice, and the music is top notch. PC port:The devs quickly released a patch to make you able to use a controller. Honestly, it doesn't make much of a difference because there are very few portions that require much execution. _childDocuments_.review: A fantastic little adventure game set in a parody of a JRPG, where one of the primary goals is to find the ghosts of all the monsters the "hero" has killed and reunite them with their bodies.This is an earlier game from the same team that went on to make Chulip, and there are a lot of similarities, and a lot of things that Moon actually handles better!Most of the game's puzzles are fairly straightforward and can be figured out by the clues provided in-game, and I only needed to consult FAQs for some of the more obscure, optional things.Something to note that took me a while to figure out: when you run out of inventory space, any additional items you get are NOT thrown away, they go into your "stock", and you can move things in and out of your stock via the menu accessed with the Y button.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Basically imagine if Earthbound had puzzles instead of battles and it was a PS1 game developed in part by the Super Mario RPG people and you're halfway there. Really beautiful game even if I hate the fishing mechanics with a passion.Apart from the music and playful use of RPG tropes, one of the coolest things about it for me is the weird mix of aesthetics. A lot of more recent JRPG critique has mentioned the PS1's era's weird mix of 16bit and 3D aesthetics. Instead of trying to shy away from this in a cowardly fashion, Moon leans into this ♥♥♥♥ in a way that brings to mind Courage the Cowardly Dog but on a PS1 in the mid 90s. Stop motion, early 3D, refined 16bit - it's all here contrasting in a way that is thematically brilliant.The writing is among the best in videogames. The prelude of the game - where you play a kid playing as the "hero" - vs the actual game - where you play the kid sucked into the game trying to sort out all the ♥♥♥♥ the psychopathic "hero" did - is really funny anyway, but then you're in the mushroom forest with a guy called florence who can travel between universes because he ate a golden mushroom and he reminds you how ♥♥♥♥ our world is and uses the sound of traffic to examplify his point and you're like "yeah, fair enough".In spite of saying that, the game's best moments often come from either the semi-mundane - buying records and listening to them, helping people with their everyday  problems, waiting for animals to do stuff - and the game really is about seeing the beauty in everyday life.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game, moments were tranquil yet have suspense, there was a aura of bliss just walking through the world and seeing what you can do. Figuring out puzzles and details that people tell you. The feeling of figuring out gives that classic "Aha!" feeling. Learning the world and its wacky characters gives a warm and fuzzy feeling that everyone has there own little secrets, hobbies, and activities to discover.If you enjoy those types of gameplay and can learn to appreciate patience, it gives an experience like no other. A world were most of the adventure is walking around, yet are now blissful and with purpose.However the moment that stuck to me the most I cannot say and must be experienced for yourself, as there were times I questioned why they did certain things a certain way, only to realize later that it was planned, deliberate, on purpose, and executed EXACTLY the way they wanted.This game will be an experience I will keep thinking and remembering for years to come. It has done something to me that no game will ever do ever again, if it's executed in the right way for you, you might feel the same. Highly recommend, If you have the time to sit down and learn about love.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely and unique game, and what I feel is a product of the early experimental game development era of Japan. Of course, like many other Playstation / SNES games with experimental/non conforming game designs, Moon did not make it to western shores. I do not blame the developers for keeping this one local, as I just could not see it being popular with western audiences at the time, nor with the mainstream audiences of today. This is why steam makes for a perfect home for this forgotten gem, as it fits right in with the indie scene that flourishes here.I will say it out right, Moon isn't for everyone, in fact, I don't think it's for most people. The game is a very slow burn, and lacks any real action to it. There is no fighting, there is no platforming, and there isn't even a run button to my knowledge. It's a slow paced, open world, puzzle game at its heart, but Moon is also the perfect example of a piece of media that is much more than the sum of its parts. It has an odd charm to it, in that the game is mostly light hearted and brimming with humor, however, there are points in which the game flawlessly transitions to pulling on your heart strings. For those who have played games like earthbound, you will find a similar vibe, albeit the games are nothing alike. The best way I can describe a game like Moon is simply that it is full of heart, and while it may only appeal to a very niche market, those that do it enjoy it will enjoy it to its fullest.Do I recommend Moon? Maybe. There is nothing wrong with the game, but chances are you won't be entertained by it, and that's okay! This is a great game to exercise the 2 hour refund policy on. Give it a try, see what you think, and you never know, you might really dig it! If not, well, you can always get your money back and say that you tried.If you do decide to try it, I recommend not reading anything about it. The less you know the more interesting it will be. So don't read anymore reviews, just try it! Like right now O_O

_childDocuments_.review: probably the weirdest game i've ever played. felt like a fever dream but in the best way possible. unlike any game ive ever played and most likely ever will play. silly and fun characters with weird designs, good dialogue and clashing art styles that work so well together. gameplay is super unique and flips your normal rpg on its head (hence anti-rpg). story is deeper than i expected going into it. great music. one of the only times ive played a game and it has moved me personally with its message. all of the dialogue and storytelling culminate in an amazing ending, just make sure you say no when asked at the very end :). man what an amazing experience. if you like weird games or just rpgs in general, please play this game you won't regret it. Did i find Love? yes and it’s this game right here

_childDocuments_.review: "moon" can easily be seen as a cornerstone of meta-narratives in gaming, and is without a doubt one of the niche-masterpieces of the PS1-era. Glad, that this port exists (even if the price-tag can be offputting for an over two decades old game) for a physical copy is quite hard to come by."moon" is many things, sometimes pioneering in different design-aspects that are used and appraised in more recent indie titles with a "self-aware" narrative. At it's core it is a slow, laid-back adventure game and a persiflage of common jrpgs, satirising the murderous and self-entitled rampage of the so called "heroes" for the sole means of grinding XP. In contrast to that, here the main protagonist gains "Love" to extend the amount of time you have each day, adding more interaction.The character design is exceptional and quirky, the art and sound direction is bold and great and the overall tone is trippy and surreal, but it is not for the unpatient, for you backtrack and wait a lot sometimes (there is a day/night and week-day-cycle with a different scedule depending on the character). Alas, this is intentional. The game is meant to be played slowly. (Heck, you can collect singles and put on a custom playlist, so that the strolling is more chill).The ending, (while it may be a little bit preachy for some) is also really strong.A definite recommendation for everyone that is interested in out-of-the-box-experiences of video game history!
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: If you go in expecting moon to be something that it's not, you're going to have a bad time with it. If you go in with an open mind and no expectations, you'll probably still be confused and have difficulty at first, but you'll feel the game start to communicate with you in its own way about what it expects of you. And once you start to understand that, you'll find a fun, smart, funny, rewarding, well-written experience in moon.Unless you're trying to 100% it. There are two things in this game that are mean beyond reason, and even if you connect with this game on every other level, these two will be Hell. But they're entirely optional (if you're not a compulsive completionist like me... x_x).
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: what a beautiful game.it starts out slow -- the action limit seems like a bigger deal than it is, and once you start leveling up it quickly becomes a non-issue. what follows is that you start to unfold this huge, colorful world filled with characters of all shapes and sizes, and a story that lets you take it at your own pace.the time management aspect feels fairly natural and while there are times where you're stuck waiting (the end of the game i was skipping through weeks just to finish the last sidequest) it starts to feel less and less exhausting as you take in more of the world around you. part of me wishes some of the ui was better, particularly in shops: you can only buy one of an item at a time, meaning if you want a stack of them you have to mash the A button for a good while. but you start to realize it's not about hoarding, about grinding the fishing to get money (you can actually make it through the game without ever donating to hager, which i wish i had looked into sooner). i mean, sure, i could buy a hundred octolips and never have to walk anywhere again. but i'd miss the sounds of the birds, the ambient background tunes. the wind in the valley. flora's song in the town. the crickets.is it hard? yes. will you need a guide? most likely. will it make you feel like a genius for completing a puzzle by yourself? absolutely.so go and save those animals! talk to plants! build a rocket! survey robots! buy some records! (buy all the records. make a little playlist of your favorites and share it with me.) get wasted on an island full of musical monkeys! talk to little mushroom creatures in a foreign language! have a drink with wanda. catch some fish. smell the roses. collect all the love you can. wring out every little drop, every ounce of it. and when you do, when you've loved as hard as you can, shut the game off. but never stop loving.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I watched a playthrough of it not long ago, and I mostly bought it to support the devs (in hopes of a Chulip port). As others have said, it really isn't for everyone, but it's super charming and makes you feel good. The puzzles are pretty obscure and the translation words things a little vaguely at times, but it's a solid port. I've had no issues with it, and the ability to turn off the blur filter and the little TAB menu is super nice. Gramby makes me want to cry. Please support Onion Games so we can get more great ports!
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Moon with low expectations, mostly because I had a bad experience with another game by the same developer called Chulip.Chulip was confusing, overly mean & difficult, and just didn't make sense. When Moon was re-released, I was expecting the worst. To my surprise, I absolutely loved it! The art styles are super unique. You get a mix of pixel art, Claymation, 3D, 2D graphics, and even realistic photos. The environmental design is equally excellent; everything is cute and fun to look at. Walking around and talking to NPCs is a joy, as they all have unique and funny ways of speaking. The game’s day and night cycle, along with the weekly cycle, is mind blowing for a 1997 PS1 game. The quests in Moon are some of the bests I've seen in any game. They’re witty, heartwarming, and very rewarding. Completing them leaves you with a good feeling. The ending is meta, fitting perfectly with the game’s overall theme.Not everything is perfect. Some quests are random and depend on luck, like the fishing quest and the bird colour quest. There are also some moon logic quests, like having to fish a PS1 console out of a specific pond. How was I supposed to know there’s a console in there with no hints? Some puzzles are annoying to do.Despite these issues, Moon is a beautiful game. I never thought I’d enjoy it as much as I did, especially after my experience with Chulip. After playing Moon, I even wanted to give Chulip another try, maybe I’ll like it more this time around.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I played this on Switch last year, I just purchased it again because I love it so much and wanted to support Onion Games further.Very good game, a bit of a product of its time and this is a direct port with no QOL enhancements so expect some early PS1 era crust. Though that doesn't keep me from recommending it any less.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Moon has the fame of being a hard and cryptic game, but you can pretty much enjoy the world of Moon without a guide due to its OpenWorld-like structure, as a matter of fact, you can perfectly reach the love level that allows you to beat the game without using a guide. Beating it may be a different case, but there is plenty of fun to have. I played for 14 hours before deciding I wanted to beat it(I was way above the love level minimum requirement), and after meeting the requirements for the ending, I still played it for a while. This is not a game where you go with the mentality of “I need to beat it” as fast as possible.Despite having the whole anti-RPG thing as one of its main selling points, Moon is pretty light on meta jokes and content, you will even forget you are supposed to be in a game for the most part. Despite being one of Toby fox’s inspirations, don’t expect an Undertale Zero, Its setting is more mundane and its humor is less juvenile, and yet the game charmingly delivers that.Overall, it’s a game more focused on puzzles and exploration, the characters' roles in the moon world are pretty light and short, don’t expect character arcs, they exist to awaken curiosity in you.The title is pretty slow-paced, literally a lot of the puzzles require waiting and observation, you also have only one-direction fast travel, so that slows things down, but at least it helps you to get more involved in the world of moon and its puzzles.The game also has a stamina system, it's kinda annoying in early game, but then you just forget about it in mid and late game because you get plenty of energy. It’s mostly used as a  “skill check” for certain parts of the game. Unless you have caught a soul, quitting the game was the fastest method of transportation for me.Honestly, this is a pretty barebone port, they could have implemented some QoL improvements such as being able to choose what hour or day you wake up, it also has some really slow transitions, which makes the game feel even slower.Overall, it’s a slow game with a charming world. The story and concept won't blow your mind, but it's still an unique experience.The game doesn't notify you when a “puzzle” has been solved, this may be a problem in large areas, especially when you consider that you have limited time to catch a soul. You may end up thinking you didn't solve it.Don’t overthink the solutions, the game doesn’t require multiple steps to solve a problem like other puzzle games, one simple action is usually the solution and you usually don’t have to leave the room to solve the puzzle.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll write a more detailed review when I finish my journey through moon, though I'll say I'm enjoying it quite a lot so far!First of all, thank you so much for bringing this game to more platforms! The more people that can experience the love, the better.And here comes the main reason I wanted to write a review so soon: I really appreciate the option to turn off filtering (push "5" key on keyboard!) as I do prefer my pixel art games looking crisp and, well, pixelated. But there seems to be an issue on how the game is scaled, as there is quite a bit of shimmering when the camera moves.Also, there seems to be some serious screen-tearing going on in fullscreen mode. I haven't seen anyone mention this, so it could be a problem on my end? I'll settle for windowed mode for now, I suppose.Regardless, I've been enjoying my time with moon, and I can't wait to play more of it!

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I'm not entirely sure I DO recommend this game but I DID like it.It has a really cool and ahead-of-its-time concept, but unfortunately the gameplay is extremely tedious, and sometimes VERY cryptic! It might just be a problem with going back to old games after playing games with modern conveniences, but the lack of effective timeskips, the slowness of a lot of transition cutscenes, and the basically nonexistent fast travel features all make the game feel incredibly tedious sometimes. Also the long unskippable cutscenes in which you do nothing.BUT!! The ideas are SUPER cool and there are a lot of cool details! I think the game is worth playing, but you should probably be aware that the actual experience of playing the game can be REALLY cumbersome. I give this game a dragon rating of 10/10 because of a plot-critical and very awesome dragon.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: So, Moon is a pretty decent game. The general plotline is super fun, and the characters are all unique and interesting. The art style is a lot of fun, very whimsical, where no two characters look remotely the same. The minigames can be fun, with some exceptions. However, it does have some flaws. The sound design is just awful. Between music tracks playing over each other, loud repetitive shrill noises, and music tracks that are (I checked) two seconds long, it could certainly do a lot better. When I say that this game made me want to rip off my ears at times, I'm not exaggerating.And on top of that, the game is SLOW. A lot of the time you spend in this game will be spent waiting. I played this game for 18 hours, and I'd wager a solid 9 of those hours was spent sitting and doing nothing. You will see the idle animation a lot. But, despite those things I do recommend it. It's very unique, and if you have the patience to get past the negative aspects, it's the kind of game that can take over your life for about a week. Just make sure to temper your expectations, and have a LOT of patience.Decent game, 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Playing through Moon RPG is sorta like reading a classic like "Hamlet", but for a certain specific flavor of quirky game. There are parts of it that are dated and clunky, but for every bit of frustration there is also timeless enjoyment to be found. It really is one of those games that should be experienced if you have any interest in it. (Most likely with a guide if you want to keep your sanity in some areas) The art in this game really pops, its main art director worked on Mario RPG and it shows in the best way. The mix of 3D renders, pixel art, and claymation are unique and memorable. The one real downside is the few pretty unkind racial depictions in the game that really date it and stick out like a sore thumb against an otherwise perfect art style.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I honest to God haven't enjoyed a game this much since I was a kid. There's so much warmth and heart that was put into this game, I don't know where to begin. Moon is a very meta game, and it explores concepts way ahead of it's time. The overall message is pure, and the world would be a better place if everyone could ponder what it's trying to say. I don't want to spoil anything about this game, you'll just have to take my word for it and play it for yourself. It's certainly a strange game, mechanically, and it's not for everyone right off the bat, but stick with it for a few hours and once you get the hang of it, you'll never forget it. Thank you to the wonderful people who made this game, and to those who went out of their way to translate it all these years later and bring it out of the realm of Japanese obscurity.

_childDocuments_.review: I've already played this through to the end when it came out on Switch a while back, but believe me when I say that this game is so lovable that I had no reservations about buying it a second time. It is a slow burner for sure, but it is one of the most quirky and unique games you could possibly find.This is a re-release of a Japan exclusive PS1 game that was recently translated into English by the fabulous team at Onion Games! In terms of gameplay, it mostly leaves you to your own devices to wander around and figure out how to progress by talking to people and tracking down creatures that sometimes require tricks to figure out how to catch them. There are some sections of the game that feel a little too obtuse to figure out on your own, so I'd honestly recommend a walkthrough if you get stuck.For fans of classic RPGs, there is a lot to appreciate. It deconstructs what it is like to live inside the world of a JRPG like Final Fantasy or Dragon Quest, though not from the point of the protagonist. The charming character artwork, the way the sound design subtly decorates important areas, and the unique premise mix together to create a memorable experience that doesn't leave you easily.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: moon flips the JRPG genre on its head. Typically, you play the hero who fights monsters to level up and beat the final boss. In moon, the hero is not you and is actually seen as more of a murderous pest. Instead, you play as an invisible boy who wanders around gathering love and trying to rescue the monsters killed by the hero by reuniting their souls with their bodies.This will be a polarising JRPG for some, because the gameplay is mostly limited to walking and talking, rather than battling and grinding. The real meat of the game is figuring out how to capture the monster souls and what you need to do to get love from people. The game has its own day/night cycle and also a weekly cycle, so certain events only happen at certain times of day/night or on certain days of the week. The game offers you clues as to how to proceed if you get stuck, but these can be almost as cryptic as the puzzles themselves sometimes.There is a basic story there and you can dig a little deeper to uncover some additional details, but largely the story is as irreverent as its presentation. You're playing for the humour and the presentation more than the narrative. Each character in the world has a distinct identity and their own schedule. Discovering everyone, learning their schedules and uncovering their secrets is the key to this game and you'll probably love it or hate it based on this.This is one of those 'quirky' Japanese games like Earthbound with a niche but cult following. I'm a fan of those and I like this game too. If you are, there's a good chance you'll like this too, but otherwise it probably won't appeal to most.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: this game has been in my radar for a very long time, I ended up picking it up after asking for someone to sell me on it on the onion games discord. It is a very very very good game, surprisingly little direction was needed in my completing the game and I had a really fun time with it. My only complaint is that I was partially sold on the story of the game being emotional, which I really didnt get much out of. Don't get me wrong here, the story is great! It's engaging and the characters are amazing, but it's never make you cry sad or anything like that. Speaking of characters, this game has so much character! Even though this was released in 1997, to an american in 2022 it is amazingly refreshing to play a game that feels so alive and so interesting. I could go on for ever and ever about how great the soundtrack is, or the quests, or the interactions, or hell, even the claymation (spoiler alert I LOVE CLAYMATION). This game is great, I think you, (yes you reading this) should pick it up if you have a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Moon is a weird game. It's not exactly an RPG like it says it is. It's one of those games that is really just an experience honestly. It can get a bit tedious (especially getting the last of the love), but it's such a neat thing that it doesn't bug me a ton. I honestly think it's worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: So I decided to change my joke review to a real one. The Good: The fact that this game is even on steam is a minor miracle. It is rather unique and thoughtful in terms of presentation and plot.The Not-so-Good: Gameplay-wise, the entire thing is one big scavenger hunt. Collect ghosts and find items that will make people happy. Exploration is fun and all, but that's really all you do, and the pacing really starts to drag. Some of the mini games that are required to progress are incredibly obnoxious; I'm never going to play that memory game again as long as I live. Also, having to buy background music means that I'm going to be playing in silence most of the time, which is a shame.Another big problem in this version is screen tearing. In most games I hardly notice issues like these, but here it honestly kinda hurts my eyes. Messing around with v-sync does nothing.Overall, while Moon is a good RPG, but there were no shortage of better choices on the original playstation. It is probably best enjoyed in small doses over time. It is a good game to play while taking a break from work or other games.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: More cryptic than La-Mulana, which would actually give you instructions, Moon is a game about having a rough idea of what to do, waiting days in game to have the oppurtunity to act upon it, realizing you weren't supposed to do that yet, and then vaguely amble around in a stupor. Despite the main draw of the game being its flush world and colorful characters, I found myself constantly frustrated by my inability to talk to them about nearly every topic in the game, and could not get them to say anything about a myriad of items directly relevant to their interests. Getting additional interesting events to proc is frequently as or more difficult than advancing through the main story, so I don't understand how anyone is meant to play through this without liberal use of a guide, or a group of friends going through/having gone through this beside them. I can't exactly criticize the game for being "too hard" in its adventure-game puzzle design as that is, as the kids call it, a "skill issue", but the game offers nothing but these hard puzzles, and nothing to guide you on the right path. Even once you do complete a given event good work, now you may have to grind out fish for an hour looking for a particular item or end up with little to no reward. The atmosphere of the game is non-existent, and you're expected to program your own playlist of 7 or so tracks in the in game discman, which is frankly awful to navigate, and spend your ground out yenom to buy the tracks for it.Frankly if you want to play this game for its colorful characters and setting use a guide. It will save you the trouble of trying a myriad of wrong and unnecessary time wasting problem solving, but will totally ruin what little "gameplay" was left. It will also ensure you see all of the events that I was not privy to because I didn't try ramming the magnifying glass up every character's ass. I had a terrible time with this game and I found the ending insulting.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games you would give to someone serving a life sentence because it would take that long to solve it without hints.Very charming, but very very tedious. Did not finish and don't intend to. The amount of "puzzles" that rely on you just sitting there wasting time is too much. A reasonable person without a guide would just assume they were doing something wrong, but this game wasn't made for reasonable people.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I would of appreciated it when it first came out if it came to the west, but I love everything about this game now. I also have waited a very long time to finally play it. Shares very similar dna to mario rpg which is incredibly uplifting to see what I have been missing all these years. The game oozes charm at every corner. The people who made this game created something truly special, and I hope more people give it a try in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Moon seems to market itself as a calm experience compared to the counter part of playing an action-packed RPG, but it is anything but that. There is a time limit mechanic introduced early on in the game, which will give you a few minutes everyday to get as much love as possible. At first this sounds okay, until you realize on your first death that when you die, you ACTUALLY die. You go all the way back to your last save point which is very annoying since your character is very slow so if you stop to take a breather, you will die from the loss of energy by just existing. So you are always on the constant move and quickly looking for what you got to do next. When you are getting close to dying, you would think the game would give you a little boost to ease the stress, wrong. The game slows down your already snail-paced character, if you have no food at that stage just give up and git gud and start over I guess. However, if the time limit mechanic sounds good to you then go ahead and buy this game because everything else in this game is amazing. It really upsets me that I can't ever enjoy Moon properly because of always being rushed throughout the game, which even though the art, music, and story are all on point. I still can't ever recommend anyone to buy this game, the time limit mechanic is just too game killing.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I have very mixed feelings on this game. It's unique and charming, but it can be quite daunting to actually play. I haven't finished it yet and I am not sure if I am going to. Yet I still feel like I'd recommend this game because it's quirky and special. I really respect and appreciate developers who do something different, even if it doesn't always work. I've been thinking that a game can be confusing or overwhelming. It isn't a bad thing. Moon can certainly be enjoyed in more of a relaxing or chill manner than I am making it sound. You go around collecting "love" by doing things like helping the various NPCs you meet in game. It's simple enough, but each NPC has their own daily schedule which can change depending on the day of the week. Without a guide it can be difficult to know when certain events can be triggered but there is no need to complete everything. Some puzzles can also be challenging without a guide. The game links an instruction manual and it's kinda mandatory to read before playing or to keep it on hand. I definitely think Moon is worth trying for yourself. It's a game where you can really get swept up in its unique and charming atmosphere. It may not click for me exactly, but its a game that I think is worth experiencing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most unique games I have played, with its weird artstyle and portrayal. It absolutely feels like I'm going through some weird fever dream, and the message it gives is as straightforward as it gets. I enjoyed it well enough to go through the whole thing, but I am absolutely not working towards 100%-ing it because it isn't a very eventful game. Two times there were "travelling" sections and it took a very long time for them to finish, which I can understand as a PS1 thing that aged like milk but it still just extended the playtime ever so slightly. The characters all feel different and give fun dialogue that complements the theme of the game, many times a random character can have tons of dialogue given to them! However, despite all of this, it still felt like the game took ages. It is a slog and a half, and many parts felt ok-ish at best. While this game absolutely didn't age the best, I still ended up enjoying going through it. I still do not recommend this game to most people, since they are likely spoiled by modern pacing and the one this game gives will probably deter them away.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing moon. It is an important piece of gaming history that intersects heavily with my interests. Starting from Super Mario RPG and connecting down to moon, the lineage of folks who worked on this game branches out and touches other video games that also mean a lot to me, Contact being a huge example. Furthermore, you can see how the concepts in this game would come to be hugely influential in other works to come. I think most folks who play moon probably know about the connection to Toby Fox and Undertale.Despite being published in 1997, I found the gameplay experience to be refreshing and personally am unable to call it dated in any way. I appreciated the slow pacing, waiting around for things to happen while listening to my MD collection, and following folks around hoping to catch something suspicious afoot! There is an in-game hint system for love events involving people that is very helpful. I did find myself referencing a guide at times to work out the details, and I'd probably recommend that to most folks who have jobs and busy lives -- it will make it easier to fit this game into your schedule.I did everything I could while playing moon. The ending was bittersweet and beautiful. It feels like I've been given a gift, having been in the world of Moon with its creatures and people, and now I can carry them with me.After this experience, I plan to devote more time to older games than I have in past years. Thank you, moon. I feel the love!
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: The grandpappy of meta-narratives in RPGs. So glad this game got a proper English translation. The adorable set pieces, silly characters, and catchy tunes are what kept me pulled in. It saddens me to see so many great moments hidden behind such cryptic steps. As long as you can stomach using a guide at times, you can experience all this game has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I would use a guide for this sparingly, Because You'll need it if you get stuck. This game is pretty amazing and very unique for its time. I'm grateful that people were able to experience this in the west. This is NOT an RPG but more like a parody of RPGS of the time period(Dragon Quest). The use of cultural references are akin to earthbound. If you like really out there games, Check this out AND Love-Del-lics other games like UFO a Day in the life and LOL Lack of love
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this with a heavy asterisk.1. This is not an RPG. Don't expect an RPG. It's an adventure game that parodies RPGs (primarily Dragon Quest)2. The beginning of the game is pretty outrageously difficult because your life gauge is really small but it gets easier the more levels you gain.If you're in the market for a game with really fun and endearing characters that you have to help on a time limit with specific daytime and nighttime events that allow for you to help these characters, then get this game.All of the things outside of this game that people say about it, only really hurts expectations of it. Undertale might've been inspired by this game, but it isn't Undertale, don't make that mistake in assuming it is.If you stick with it you and see all the game has to offer, you might end up with a new all-time favorite game like me.moon is a game that is bursting at the seams with heart, charm and kindness. It's definitely one of the best adventure games I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game. As most reviews will say it's certainly not for everybody but if you want the best of it take in the atmosphere and chill. Sometimes you'll have no clue what to do but that's ok. I'd only really look at a guide if you think you have 0 idea how to move forward, but there's no shame in doing it (some of these puzzles are ROUGH). I will say this is only a retranslation of a fairly old game, so I accidentally locked myself out of 100% love by doing events in a different order. But that's not needed for the ending + as long as you figure out the "king's secret" before investing too much time around dr. hager you'll avoid the problems I did. This is a game that literally wants you to wait and take it all in, so pop on some of the in-game tunes and embrace it!

name: Crysis Remastered
detailed_description: The classic first person shooter from Crytek is back with the action-packed gameplay, sandbox world, and thrilling epic battles you loved the first time around – now with remastered graphics optimized for a new generation of hardware. What begins as a simple rescue mission becomes the battleground of a new war as alien invaders swarm over a Lingshan island chain. Armed with a powerful Nanosuit, players can become invisible to stalk enemy patrols, or boost strength to lay waste to vehicles. The Nanosuit’s speed, strength, armor, and cloaking allow creative solutions for every kind of fight, while a huge arsenal of modular weaponry provides unprecedented control over play style. In the ever-changing environment, adapt tactics and gear to dominate your enemies, in an enormous sandbox world. Suit up: Your Nanosuit’s speed, strength, armor, and cloaking allow creative solutions for every kind of fight. Adapt: In an ever-changing environment, adapt your tactics to dominate on battlefields ranging from frozen jungle to alien environments. Customize: A huge arsenal of modular weaponry provides unprecedented control over play style, with options ranging from the experimental to the alien. Conquer: Life-like enemy AI requires a strategic and flexible playstyle, as new challenges – including a zero-g battlefield– require players to take the offensive and be proactive. Explore: Choose your own path through the open world of Crysis, destroying obstacles, driving vehicles, and using the environment itself against your enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis remastered had a rough start at since there were lots of bugs and optimization is non existent. However, I can certainly say that they've patched almost all the annoying things that were either overlooked or not properly tested.Game mechanics are easy to learn and fun to mess with, however remastered edition certainly have broken some things such as dynamic buildings. It used to take quite an effort to demolish a building but now one power fist is all it takes. I can certainly say that the gun-play in this game is annoying since enemies are like bullet sponge (humans), and it takes the immersion and fun away for me. However once you get used to it you'll just go on.I was actually expecting some kind of Crysis Warhead remaster as well, since I believe that game really worth playing and had more things to offer than the first game.For this price point, I can certainly say that this game is worth it. The korean island setting is pretty cool with super open areas despite the game being linear -- you can tackle things in different ways. _childDocuments_.review: After playing through the whole game, I have noticed a number of bugs that I would hope the devs address in an update. Let me go over some of the good things then I can cover any other issues that I came across.-----Pros-----Game can be set back to classic mode:By default the game is set to run more like the sequels rather than the original. So we will need to go into settings to make some changes. First, we need to get the power wheel back so we need to go into Settings > Game Settings > Game Tab >  Check Classic Nanosuit Mode. Next, we will need to change some keybindings. By default, the Q/E are set to Armor/ Cloak mode and the Left/Right lean are set to T/H. These changes should be all you need to do to get the controls back to the original.Powers seem to be relatively untouched:From my tests the powers seemed to be the same. Another Review mentioned that the speed mode was heavily nerfed. However, this does not seem to be the case because after running from various points and comparing them to the Original the energy consumption was almost exactly the same. Testing of other modes such as Armor, Cloak, and Strength mode all seemed to be the same as well in terms of energy consumption.Combat:When fighting enemies, combat still seems to be the same for the most part. Shooting an enemy in the head kills them instantly no matter what difficulty you have the game set at, which is nice. I would rather not have enemies be bullet sponges.-----Cons-----No quick saves:Going through the game on Delta difficulty makes it very apparent that quick saves are missing. If you die you can only use the last autosave that was made which can set you back a good amount. You are at the game's mercy at when it decides to make a save point which seems to be at scripted areas or distances from an objective which seems to be the same as the original. I don't know why quick saves were removed but that seems like a really dumb decision.Graphical bugs:In the first level, I noticed that there were some assets that were floating above the ground. Some examples are rocks or grass that will be floating a couple of inches off the ground. The grass was less obvious until I was looking at it from a different angle.Audio bugs:There were a whole lot of audio bugs that I found in the game.- Cloaking and then using the binoculars makes audio stutter- Cloak distorts the audio of surrounding assets like the chicken. It deepens and slows the clucks down like it was being put through slowmo.- Stepping on wood sounds like you are breaking planks. I discovered this while traversing one of the hanging wooden bridges.- Artillery at the beginning of the "Assault" mission is basically non-existent unless you are standing right next to where the explosion is happening.AI pathing:AI pathing seems to be an issue in this version of the game. I have had many times where the AI would be trying to walk up the side of a mountain to get to me, trying to go through walls, and even just going a slightly different direction than where I was located."Fatal" error bugs:On the mission onslaught I ran into a pretty error that I have never seen before in the original. After you get the Gauss rifle from the VTOL drop off, you come across this "checkpoint" with like 10+ guards. When I died here, the game just stopped with a black screen and gave me two error windows and asked if I wanted to Abort, Retry, or Cancel. I selected Retry for both popups and the game seemed fine until I killed all the enemies at the checkpoint. Four soldiers in particular just existed...You couldn't kill them and they were just walking back and forth really fast.Is it worth $30? ehhh not really. I think if you own the original on Steam and with the Launch discount you can get it for $15 which seems like a more reasonable price.

_childDocuments_.review: Experience – First TimeWorld/Setting – 7/10Story – 6/10Music – 5.5/10Gameplay – 6/10Overall Review – 6/10One Line Review – Game of Two HalvesReviewWorld/SettingThe World of Crysis is gorgeous to look at. From the moment you parachute in to the world, you are amazed by it. The vegetation, environment, water etc. everything impresses you about the world, considering the game came out in 2007. But once you get used to it, it becomes boring pretty quickly. And the reason for that is simple: repetition. For the first half of the game, you are only exposed to the jungle. It is only in the second half that you experience the real reason for this game’s existence: aliens. After that, the second half of the game becomes much more interesting! The environment constantly changes. One level you are inside an alien ship and in the next level you are struck by blizzard. The variation in the levels makes the second half of the game ‘the better half’.StoryThe story of Crysis is good, but pretty predictable. The reason for that is: We have been exposed to these kinds of stories for a long time, from transformers to AvP etc. The difference comes because this is a game, which means interaction. You discover everything by your own. The first half of the story is, you fight North Koreans who have captured a research team along with the entire archipelago. The second half: you fight aliens! That is all I am going to say.MusicThe music was good. If you can call a single track playing again and again ‘good’.GameplayThe gameplay was pretty lackluster, apart from nano suit feature, which was great! The guns were good to handle, at least some of them were. The nano suit features were great! But were limited in its scope. It did not help that the ‘power bar’ drained so quickly that you could not really experiment with your nano suit features at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This short review is less about Crysis, the game itself, and more about the lack of effort put into this "remaster." The original game had its fair share of glitches and nothing was done here to fix them. AI pathing issues like enemies moving back and forth against walls/objects, animation issues like helicopters turning sideways without animation and zipping into a wall and exploding, etc. just stupid things you can laugh at, They aren't as bad during the majority of the game since the way the levels are structured are semi-open with your main objectives being having to interact with/destroy an object, or reach a marker, which means stupid AI behavior can be ignored. However, during the final quarter the game decides to become more cinematic and turns into a linear scripted shooter with aliens where you have to follow npcs, clear waves of enemies or wait for scripted sequences to play out. The game completely falls apart here. Enemies will fall over dead with their AI deactivated when their hp reaches zero, but their full death animations won't play out so they won't register as killed by the game, forcing a checkpoint restart if you're lucky, or having to fully quit and restart the game, or, in the worst case scenario, a full level restart. The final level is especially bad at this, with bugs where the sort-of final boss straight up won't spawn once you reach the end, requiring a full level restart and hoping it fixes itself, or, upon beating it and waiting for the real final boss to show up, hoping a scripted event that leads up to it actually playing correctly and not ending up with the npcs not responding, in which case no amount of checkpoint restarts will fix it, so the level has to be completely restarted and you'll have to hope it fixes itself. These issues were present in the original release and no attempt was made to fix them here (there's other minor but annoying issues still present too, e.g. vegetation counting as an object so the main character will place c4 on a bush in mid-air instead of throwing it and not being able to pick it back up). This extends to the rest of the remastered trilogy, but the first Crysis is easily the worst and most prone to game ending issues compared to the sequels. The game itself is decent, though even back in the day it went downhill once you stop fighting human enemies due to the change in game structure from semi-open levels to a linear cinematic shooter like I said before. And even then there's some parts during its better levels where it gets kind of annoying to play, such as some pointlessly big barren areas where most of your time is spent sprinting from one place to another. This is one of those things where the sequels are way better despite being more cramped due to their console-focused design. In short, get this discounted and, once you reach the final few levels, watch the cutscenes and ending on Youtube. Or don't, since the rest of the franchise never directly follows up on this games ending and it was solved in a tie in comic.

_childDocuments_.review: That famous catchphrase known in PC gaming! For this Remastered Edition though, your PC will undoubtedly run Crysis since it is a pretty average XBOX 360 PORT, sadly. There are some good parts from this PORT and naturally, bad parts too.So for this CRYSIS REMASTERED Edition, I'll be comparing the original Crysis played back then in 2007 at release and lately, versus the Remastered version that released back in 2021, played at the time of this review.So, at release back in 2007, I would say I was disappointed with Crysis Original Edition. Very unoptimized and released too soon for its time. About the same as Crytek's first game, Far Cry, that was pretty demanding back in 2004. Crysis OG struggled to run at medium settings. So technically speaking, the game had a harsh launch but wow oh wow, the game was the BEST LOOKING THING EVER... even when playing in a "slideshow mode". Aside from the specs, the gameplay was pretty great which was what made Crysis known with the freedom of approach to the missions. The controls in the original version are very akin to PC gaming. You have the peaking functions where the Remastered Edition removed them (apparently, they got brought back with a patch but I never bothered to use them in the RE). The crosshair in the original is again, very PC-like where the Remastered is the same reticule as the XBOX360. For the powers, you have a wheel and choose on the fly the power you want. On the Remastered, the controls are very like Crysis 2 and Crysis 3, where the controls are more fluid than using that powers wheel. Talking about your nanosuit powers, you do run longer with the speed power in the Remastered edition.Visually, it shows a lot about the low textures and graphical fidelity on the Remastered edition. The graphics are very downgraded compared to the original Crysis. You can compare them yourself by either playing the game on EA Desktop or GOG... or by watching this YouTube video that compares it all:

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis was a game I skipped over in my playthrough of the trilogy and to be honest I don’t know if that’s for better or worse.You can see my other reviews of the Crysis games if you want details but in short I found Crysis 2 to be bland and boring and Crysis 3 was better but still kind of mid (maybe a step above a Call of Duty campaign).  I didn’t really have a ton of fun. I mostly just finished because I had already started and it really bothers me when I move onto other games without finishing the one I’m on regardless if it’s good or not.I say this because Crysis: Remastered did something the others didn’t.  I started having fun.  I wasn’t on the edge of my seat or anything but shooting a rocket and having it completely eviscerate a house some poor chap was hiding in is just so satisfying.  The combat is still pretty generic but you have to remember this was 2007.  Call of Duty 4, the game that would be emulated by almost every other shooter after it, came out a day before this.  All things considered the gameplay has held up pretty well over the years.I’m a lot less lenient on games like Crysis 2 and 3 being younger and having more time to refine their gameplay while this one was a testing ground.  Not only that, there are vehicles here and open ended maps, both of which were taken out of the next two entries.  The destruction was a surprise which I thoroughly enjoyed.  The only thing that carried over to the next two Crysis games is the under utilization of player mechanics.  Like picking up enemies or throwing objects are super can be fun but shooting the bad guys is always just easier and more convenient .I’m not sure, maybe it’s more useful on harder difficulties.  The game gets more annoying when you get into the caves.  The final boss is also frustrating, slow, and not very fun but it’s not enough to sink the game.I really can't fathom why they made the next two games linear after this one.  It feels like such a natural fit to the gameplay.  It’s like Far Cry on steroids and I love Far Cry.  Maybe that’s why I’m so much more lenient towards this game, but a game can’t help being fun.The graphics are, well you know it’s Crysis what do I have to say.  The remaster does a pretty good job too.  I had a few glitches and some of the shadows were weird but for the most part the game played buttery smooth and looked really good.  Again it needs to be noted this game came out in 2007 so some of the jank still remains.  You can tell it’s from 2007 but it’s been fluffed up enough to both still look nice and retain it’s authentic feel.6/10 - I may be a bit more generous here then the game deserves but compared to its sequels it is the best out of the bunch.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an updated review from my initial one. I have now finished the game on the hardest difficulty and earned all achievements. The core game is perfectly fine. However, there is just so many things missing from a remaster. I never played the original, but there's a bunch of things missing that I learned was in the original. Quicksaves, which would have made my delta difficulty run much more bearable and less annoying. Not to mention things could have improved, such as the difficulty descriptions in menus. Delta difficulty was described as having less modifiers than there actually are. For example, enemies recieve aimbot and can notice you from across the map. The player has reduced health and the game is much more unforgiving. However, the game gives no indication of this, which led me to play quite a bit of the game under the impression this just is how the game was. The game just has so many inconsistences that may have been understandable for the first release, but not for a remaster. Just don't buy the remaster, buy the original.
