_childDocuments_.review: 30/100 Just an unbelievably bad game.  It hasn't aged well.I completed the original many years ago.  Playing it now was not fun.  It has awful checkpoints and no manual save, aliens that are in the sky but a game engine that does not allow you to look straight up with your rifle.  Boss fights that are just a mess, with continual freezing of your player and loss of agency/control.  An atrocious enormous alien cavern level with no visual clues which way to go.  The VTOL controls are rubbish, the sound volume is deafeningly loud in some places (especially the boss fights), you get stuck on the terrain, there is a TAC cannon gun that only works on certain aspects of the final boss but with no explanation of why, you have to manually pick up ammo for some reason, your suit and the VTOL regenerates but for some reason the tank doesn't, the binoculars don't mark enemies correctly.  Avoid even on 90% discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Its been about 5 years since I first played crysis so I cant really say theres a massive difference with the remastering. I was on a 1650 system on the original game and it struggled. Now im on a 3070 system playing 1440p at ultra settings with performance raytracing. What I do remember is several spots losing fps like crazy. Still the same no doubt the engine's fault. It was still a fun game to play. If youre to play these games it probably is best to buy this version if you ever upgrade to a better pc. I got it as a bundle for under $20. All the hours combined of the three games is about 27 hours. So in my eyes it was worth buying. I would attempt to play the crysis trilogy with a 4gb card. Having a smooth experience is out the question even 1080. The story is still great. Though I really wish they would have redone the in game cinematic cutscenes better. They still look like 2010 cutscences (Not gameplay ones). But the FREAKING TRANSPORT MISSION WITH THE TORNADOES. STILL ABSOLUTE CRAP. They couldnt have put a little effort in making the controls better. It is still one of the worst missions I have ever played in a game. Because its never your controllers fault. Through my playthrough my controller worked fine but the game bugged out to where it wouldn't register my thrust. Had to restart the game. There were a total of 4 moments where I had to either restart the game entirely multiple times, last checkpoint load, or restart entire mission multiple times. This game still is buggy like the original. Which is a shame because this is supposed to be the best version. Overall crysis is still a good game but what was the point of remastering when they still havent solved the original issues over a decade later. Wont matter which version you buy original or remastered, both have their issues. Though I less in this version. Gameplay is fun and enjoyable. Nomad is definitely my favorite character in the entire trilogy. Worth a play if your pc can run crysis.

The graphic is even better when you are underwater / diving.I recommend this version. Especially for those who wants to experience the real weather / climate in Philippine.(spoiled alert) About the sound effect. It was great. Way better and realistic than the original. _childDocuments_.review: I have kinda mixed feelings about this remaster.I like, that classic style of Crysis from 2007 has been kept, with some improvement to the graphics.. though, I remember how the game looked back in the day, when was playing it on Core 2 Duo with Geforce 8800GTS. It's an improvement only, not evolution - so it's kinda mixed bag, especially that Crysis was always the game with leading, astonishing graphics. Of course, as FPS when it comes about gameplay, it's done right - they didn't break it (*fanfare*). And as of today, haven't noticed any major bugs, maybe only sometimes destroyed objects can permeate through itself. Nothing terrible, but I think such things should be fixed, especially when we talk about remaster (because it's remaster, right?). Though haven't finished game yet, so maybe my opinion there will change...From definitive cons. Ray Tracing, are you there? If you see a view (at least in current version of game) with and without ray tracing, most of you probably wouldn't notice any difference. Oh sorry, you will - as you just cut your performance by half. I think those effects have been limited with latest updates to minimum (due to poor performance? that's not how you fix problems, seriously)Speaking of performance, I'm playing with Intel Xeon E5-2697 v3 @ 3.8GHz and Radeon RX 6700 XT 12GB. At this setup with "Can it run Crysis?" settings at 1920x1200, without RT, game keeps average at 100fps, 60-70 at open areas, and 130-140 at closed areas, and that is fine. Not fine is, that frames per seconds can randomly dip even below 20-30 frames for no reason, even when staying still. It irritates a lot and is not acceptable, generally for FPS genre. FPS lock at 75 (Vsync) kinda helps a bit though...Can I recommend the game? Eeeeeh, maybe. But on some discount, definitely not for full price. I still have fun while playing, but overally I'd say, that this remaster is below expectations, it doesn't make it a bad game though. If I could give points, it would be 5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game and it brought back many memories. There's one thing I didn't like that much - color palette. The original game looked more photorealistic and that was one of its selling points. This one feels too much like Far Cry 1 and has this almost "stylized graphics" feel going. It's just too colorful. On the other hand those visuals do shine later on in game when you switch environments. Maybe some people will like it and actually prefer it. Level of detail is much better. No more empty mountains when you're too far away like in the original game.There are some minor audio bugs here and there, but I didn't encounter anything major. I wish they didn't remove the ability to save your game manually, though.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis has a really good start, and the first half of the game is great. But the later parts are only mediocre. For example, the alien ship interior section is more annoying than fun (seems to be mostly padding for a fairly short game). The Remaster may look a little nicer but plays somewhat worse than the original. Additionally, the autosave system doesn’t improve some of the more frustrating parts of the game either. While I can’t recommend Crysis Remastered for the full price (especially if you own the original) if you can get it on sale for 75% off it is worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's Crysis, so it automatically gets a thumbs up, however I would like to say a few things:Is getting the remaster worth it? Nah. I only got it because it was at a deep loyalty discount for owning the original, but other than that it is really not worth getting. The original didn't even need a remaster in my opinion, even though it did release in 2007. But that's what made it so special, because it was so advanced for its time.The remaster is different, but not necessarily in a good way: Some graphics improvements are better, some are not. Some audio changes are good, some are not. The physics seem worse than the original and I also encountered a few game breaking bugs, like rushing a scripted scene and an enemy spawning inside a rock, so I had to restart the mission in both of those cases. So, objectively I would give this a thumbs down, but my heart won't let me... If you want the best Crysis experience, my advice would be to play the original instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Greatly Remastered.Overall graphics are adorable. Running on D3D11, which is confusing, but still uses Ray Tracing flawlessly. many textures have been remade, and some of them are just the upscaled old ones. The performance is still a bit weird but it can be solved by turning on DLSS. Particles and effects don't look perfect though, which is a weak point of the graphical part but I still don't blame them since it's just a Remaster (at least a better remaster than the other Cryses with lazy 480p cutscenes). And, insane reflections. On maximum graphics with RT Boost mode enabled, you can notice your own character's reflection on many surfaces, from a slight dark halo of your body shape on rough metal parts, to a full picture of yourself on every glassy surface (Well, to blame the other games on the industry, at least it doesn't use  & SSR while their games allegedly has RT support). I think the ugliest part of the game is the character design. Almost every character's eyelids got noticeable problems, they're not textured professionally, and all of them are textured with the upscaled old textures with visible upscaling artifacts. They need to be remade, for sure.The gameplay has slightly changed (as far as I know). It's still tough to figure out the mechanics and learn the behavior of the enemy and how to deal with it, But it's mostly enjoyable. Still got many parts that make you frustrated, but that's acceptable. It has some bugs, but not annoying at all. None of them will affect your gameplay.And to talk about the actual game, it has a well-made concept with a cool badass alien-invasion-kind-of story. It's really worth it, and it always goes on great discounts, so don't miss it if you have a good PC!

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal remaster, plays like a dream on the Steam Deck (just press OK on that weird alert at the beginning and you are good to go). _childDocuments_.review: This is, without a doubt, the most busted game I have played this year, and easily one of the most busted that I’ve ever played. Here’s just some of the issues that I experienced:- Some of the worst human enemy AI I have ever seen. Sometimes they spot you easily from a long distance, other times they fail to spot you when you’re cloaked right next to them. Sometimes they struggle to hit you up close, other times they hit you perfectly from 50 metres away. But most of the time, they’re just insanely dumb, failing to use any sort of realistic tactics or behaviour to take me down. They only posed somewhat of a challenge on the hardest difficulty because a few of them could kill me in less than a second.- Blatantly unfinished sound mixing. Sometimes the guns would fire very loudly, other times I could barely hear them. Music just didn’t play during certain scenes, and sometimes after alt-tabbing, it would return whilst blasting over the rest of the mix, making all the human voices nearly inaudible. - Frequent, immersion-breaking animation glitches and physics ragdolls. One enemy vaulted over a barrier that just wasn’t there, many NPCs walked into walls and objects when they should have gone around them, and multiple character ragdolls got stuck halfway through the floor. A few of these are fine, but I’ve seen more of them in this game than I’ve experienced in the 70 or so hours I’ve put into Starfield so far, and that’s a Bethesda game.- Inexplicable frame drops within areas where no frames should be dropping. Apparently, a gigantic battle can maintain 60fps perfectly fine, but quieter parts of the game where there is far less going on? Tanked straight down to 30fps. - Every boss fight was completely laughable. The first one, a human general, ended up crouch walking away from me the entire fight. I’d unload two mags into him, he’d disappear then reappear someone else, then he’d return to crouch walk away from me again. Did this three times and he was dead. Not a single shot was fired at me, ruining what was meant to be the most critical moment of the game up to that point. And in terms of the large alien robots, while they weren’t inherently broken, they were just lame. The massive spider-looking one had no weakpoints, so I just unloaded a thousand bullets and rockets into it until it died. The mothership only had weakpoints, and they were all available at the start so there were no attacks to dodge or tasks to complete before they became exposed. Both bosses can kill you near instantly, so instead of being able to use that really cool suit the game gave you, you’re stuck to popping in and out of cover until they blow up, nothing special about it at all.Maybe this is just a messed-up remaster, maybe this is how the game always was. All I know is that my first proper experience with this franchise was verging on complete disaster in terms of its technical competency. Yes, the shooting is fun, I enjoyed using the suit abilities, and the early level design is really great. But all of these elements were marred by consistent annoyances that either took me out of the experience or ruined parts of it entirely. You know those videos of games like Aliens Colonial Marines and Fallout 76 that showcase the funniest, most buggy parts of the experience to the world? What you see in those videos is close to what I experienced in Crysis Remastered. Why does it matter if I can run Crysis, if the game I’m trying to run just isn’t an enjoyable experience?This is made even worse by the fact that these developers had a year to fix the game up on the EGS before it was released on Steam, but it’s evidently been hardly patched since that original release. Furthermore, this is a pretty short game, taking no more than 6-8 hours to 100% the entire thing, so the fact that there are this many issues, in what should be a super streamlined experience, is pretty ridiculous. And let’s not forget that this remaster was based on the console versions instead of the iconic PC version for some reason, alongside the omission of the multiplayer mode and the Warhead expansion.Somehow, this game has a mostly positive reception on Steam, so maybe you will be luckier than I was. Unfortunately, I can only speak from my experience, and all I’ll say is that I’m happy this torture was over relatively quickly. Fingers crossed that the remasters of 2 and 3 aren’t as completely broken as this game was for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly unremarkable remaster of a technological vanguard.Crysis Remastered makes the game finally playable on modern CPUs without the framerate becoming a slideshow, and while the game may look much better than the original 2007 version technologically, certain changes to the overall art are questionable at best and downright garish at worst -- not too dissimilar to Halo: Combat Evolved Anniversary (also remastered by the same company, coincidentally).There are still some bugs present in this remaster (which I don't remember the original ever having), but given how much work Crytek has already put in into improving the game since launch, I'd expect those bugs to be fixed fairly soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:It runs, unlike the original which had to be tricked into thinking it's running on an FX processor to make it run on a Ryzen this one just works.It looks ok, comparable to the first imo. Didn't put them side by side but it gives the same look and feel imo (no RayTracing active so no idea there, not on an RTX GPU).The levels were not changed all that much, which is a good thing, plenty of other remasters/remakes tend to change level design for the worse (make levels more linear, remove stuff, etc).The aim mode and crouch/prone are both hold and toggle at the same time which is kinda neat: if you hold aim it will go out of ADS once you let go, but if you just tap it once it will toggle on/off.Cons:Sometimes sounds cut out or in sharply, and here I mean stuff like combat music and so on. The sound for single/auto fire for some weapons is completely different, as if they forgot to update it for both fire modes (one is new, the other is the old one). Tap firing a weapon very quickly while it's in full auto will make the sound of the gun cut out and go silent while you keep tap firing, this only happens in full auto mode, you can tap fire away in single.Quite buggy imo, things in the distance disappear quite quickly for me, helicopters are not visible more than 100m or so away, boats and even terrain objects like rocks behave the same. To be fair this may just be the LOD settings it applied automatically, speaking of which it put EVERYTHING on low on a gtx 1080 (the recommended is a 1660 Ti, so that's odd). At my settings (all on low, with textures on high), at 1440p it had anywhere between 90 and 120 FPS, usually stayed at 105-ish (on a Ryzen 7 2700x and gtx 1080 for reference).Continuing the bug trend and avoiding spoilers: a specific enemy that has to be killed as a mission objective glitched out and was stuck under the floor, rendering it unkillable, loading a checkpoint did not work as he was already spawned and in the floor, will soon see if restarting the level fixes it. Which brings us to the next point, an autosave system has replaced the combo manual saves+autosaves that existed previously. Flexibility has been traded for ease of implementation as I see no other reason for this choice. A manual save system would allow both for replaying certain points in a mission if that's what you wish and for bypassing some of these bugs without having to restart the mission (as mentioned, sometimes the checkpoint is too close and you have to reload farther back).So is it worth it? I think that if I knew all this I would've just reinstalled the old one and got a patch or something to get it working, and then wait for this to be fixed. When the bugs are gone maybe it'll be worth it, but until then, nah, even with a sale and as part of a bundle I felt like I should've bought a pizza with that money, would've had more fun playing the old one while eating it.

_childDocuments_.review: had the potential to be a glorious return to a genre-defining shooter, but it's ruined by a slew of technical issues. The game is riddled with bugs, from graphical glitches to constant crashes, making the experience frustrating and unstable. The frequent Blue Screens of Death (BSODs) due to memory leaks are particularly infuriating. While some might blame outdated hardware, the  runs far smoother on the same system, highlighting the developers' failure.My goal of conquering the game on Delta difficulty and collecting all achievements turned into a nightmare due to these crashes. Progress was often wiped away, making achievements nearly impossible to unlock without immense frustration. Each hard-earned victory felt pointless with the constant threat of crashes. is a missed opportunity. Despite the core gameplay still being fantastic, the technical issues make it a chore to play. Unless major patches are released, avoid this remaster and stick with the original .Consider if you're a die-hard  fan willing to endure technical issues or if you have a high-end PC (though there's no guarantee it will help).

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis was huge deal back when it was first released. With it's gameplay and amazing graphics it gathered every gamer's attention. Playing it years later made me realize why Crysis is a special game. Crysis has a unique story and it's not just a generic war game like Call Of Duty or Battlefield. Original Crysis' graphics are still looking good in my opinion and with this remastered they really turned the game into an eye pleasing experience. The new technologies they added, the particle effects, textures, everything looks fantastic. The gameplay feels a bit dated considering today's standards but playing Crysis is still lots of fun. I love the gunplay and the weapon modification aspect of the series. You can change the attachment of your weapons any time to suit your needs. I think every FPS game must include this feature. The nanosuit is a complete game changer. You are not a normal soldier in Crysis. Thanks to nanosuit you can become invisible, run fast and absorb bullets with the suit's armor. Most of the missions are open ended and lets you use both your weapons and nanosuit in any way you want. Unfortunately, the sandbox aspect of the game is removed in the later games but in Crysis 1 you are free to tackle challenges in any way you like. My roblem with the Crysis is that it's too short. You can finish the game under 6 hours. You get used to contols, the environment and all of a sudden you are in an alien ship and about to finish the game. I guess devs chose quality over quantity. At least, the game is awesome to play so you can start a second playthrough to increase the lenght. Overall Crysis is a masterpiece. If you haven't played it, you should definitely try it whether it's the remastered version or the original. It is one of the best FPS games on the market, and playing it's a fantastic experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy the remastered trilogy on a Steam sale and revisit a classic. Sometimes it's nice to go back to an old-fashioned simple, linear game; no progression, no upgrades, no microtransactions, no loot etc. Just enjoy the story, take in the sights, and shoot some damned aliens!The remaster looks and runs great albeit a couple things worth mentioning:1. On an ultrawide monitor, during loading screens, the sides of the screen flicker and glitch in such a way that I would caution people with sensitivity to flashing lights who are prone to seizures. It's pretty bad.2. The "Can It Run Crysis" graphics settings are a joke in the sense that I've toggled them on/off, ultra max to very high, and all it does is cause performance issues with little to no benefit to visual quality. _childDocuments_.review: Crysis was an incredible game that destroyed computers not only with its graphics, but also because of how badly optimized it actually was. And uhh, yep, Crysis Remastered follows literally the same formula. Not only was the game based on the newest version of CryEngine, making it look absolutely gorgeous, the game was also poorly optimized.Other than that I still recommend this game. I'd say you'd definitely enjoy it, if you have a good computer, this is probably the only reason why the reviews are so negative. I played this game on an RTX 3060 Ti, which is a fairly powerful graphics card, and yet I was still not able to turn Ray Tracing on without the game getting too laggy to actually enjoy.When it comes to the actual game and not its optimization, I'd say it's still good, definitely give it a try. _childDocuments_.review: Crysis Remastered brings back the iconic 2007 shooter that revolutionized gaming graphics and became a benchmark for hardware. The remaster promised to refresh the game and bring it closer to modern standards. So, how does it hold up?The main selling point. Even after all these years, Crysis still looks stunning, and the remaster adds ray tracing, improved textures, and updated effects. The tropical island feels alive, sunsets are gorgeous, and explosions remain as epic as ever.The iconic nanosuit gameplay lets you tackle situations your way: become a stealthy predator picking off enemies one by one, or a walking tank smashing through everything in sight.Collapsing buildings, trees falling apart, and realistic water effects still impress. Considering the game’s original foundation, this level of interaction feels ahead of its time even today.Surprisingly, the remaster runs better on modern hardware. Stable FPS on high settings is a huge improvement compared to the original’s infamous performance issues.While the nanosuit is still fun, certain aspects of the gameplay feel clunky by today’s standards. Enemy AI can be inconsistent, and some missions feel too straightforward.Although optimized for new hardware, the game still struggles on mid-range or older PCs, especially with ray tracing enabled.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Even though the abovementioned quote might be a bit cheesy, I could not help myself because of how ironic it is. As a fan of the original  from 2007, I was sceptical about this new version, especially after I heard numerous complaints when it was released a year ago on a different platform. I wanted to try it out nonetheless, though. Perhaps it got better after a few updates?Well, that certainly did not happen, hence the FUBAR quote. is not a step forward, nor it does not at the very least stagnates like other remasters. Instead, it manages to be worse than the original game, indolently ruining already existing aspects rather than making them better or bringing some modern quality of life improvements.Thus, it was a bit hard for me to write this critique of mine. While the core of this first-person shooter remains the same, the said aspects are subpar, making my experience tiresome. Due to that, I was forcing myself to finish it, as that was not  lovely  anymore but rather its butchered version. And that is not a moaning of a nostalgic guy with so-called pink glasses because I have replayed and even  the original a year ago, so it is still fresh in my mind.Let us get to the game itself, though. The premise of its narrative is not extraordinary nor a reason why you should play , but it is serviceable for what it is. You are supposed to rescue a bunch of scientists from North Korean claws on the Lingshan Islands. To achieve that, you have a powerful Nanosuit that enhances your combat possibilities by increasing your strength, speed or even making you invisible for a while. However, you will find out soon enough that there are some strange alien beings on this very island, and they are not exactly happy with your presence. Despite these aliens and futuristic equipment, I still find the fact that North Koreans successfully conquered a foreign piece of land as the most unrealistic one.Nevertheless,  excels with its simple yet engaging gameplay loop, which could be the remaster’s case, too, if it was not for several shortcomings. The freedom in how to approach each situation, whether by going all-in with a minigun and grenades, armoured vehicles or by silently killing enemies one by one, is still present. You can even customize the weapons by adding various attachments, such as scopes or different ammo types. However, artificial intelligence seems to be even dumber than before, as I witnessed it demonstrate brilliant tactics like observing the nearest wall or walking in circles. Moreover, it felt as if there were fewer foes, as several patrols I expected to encounter were missing during my playthrough; it seems as if they did not spawn at all. Lastly, there are some unnecessary changes, such as providing players with infinite ammunition when controlling a tank—this allows you to obliterate everything from a distance, destroying the original’s purpose of being careful and scavenging for supplies. Due to all of that, it felt significantly easier to play this remastered version even on the highest difficulty setting.What made my experience even worse were the weird controls, as the mouse movement is not as smooth as I am used to and meddling with its settings did not solve this issue; it felt as if it was constantly fighting with me, so I could not relax and enjoy my time with it. Another problem is that some actions, like reloading and changing fire mode, are set to a single key, due to which neither of them works, and you have to rebind them from scratch to be able to use actually use them. Additionally, changing the colour of the interface swaps it only in the main menu but not in the game itself. Ah, I almost forgot… both manual and quicksaves are not implemented to this very day either. I would guess that all of these oversights happened because of porting it from an old engine used for consoles rather than using the original one.Then, there is an aspect that is completely missing—the multiplayer part. I have adored playing it years ago, as it had a bit unique take on large-scale battles, with capturing crucial points and using vehicles as the  series presents nowadays. Its inclusion could make  worthy, as it would revive its community; alas, that did not happen.As for audiovisuals, there is a massive issue with the imbalance of audio, which is mainly noticeable when firing from weapons. For example, a regular handgun’s sound almost blew off my eardrums, while a fully automatic assault rifle is barely hearable. I could forgive such inconsistencies in a small indie title but in a remastered version of a triple-A game? That is both sad and laughable; mainly, when you consider the fact that this has not been fixed for over a year by now. I guess some of the updated visuals deserve a bit of praise, but the original already looked amazing; I mean, it is  after all, which started the infamous  meme.Honestly, I do not see a single reason for which I should recommend buying . The audacity to ask the owners of the original title to pay for this subpar, butchered version is beyond me. For a long-time fan of the series, it feels like a slap in the face. I would not suggest this even to newcomers, as  from 2007 is much cheaper. A counter-argument could be that some people have problems with launching the original, but that only underlines my point! If someone did not bother to fix these issues over the years, they should not tell their customers: . Disgusting. There are already many questionable remasters with performance problems, such as  or , but even those were at the very least provided for free—that does not mean we cannot criticize them, but at the very least they do not present themselves as the second coming of Jesus when their state is worse than his during the crucifixion.

_childDocuments_.review: Once hailed as a technical marvel, Crysis 1 really shows its age and no amount of so-called remastering - reskinning in essence - would bring it back to its 'glory' today. The enemy AI, the gun animations and gunplay, the level design and storytelling and performance are either showing their ages or simply bad. For instance, the game is remembered as an open-world shooter while its openness is limited to the first several sections and most of the time you proceed in a linear manner with NPC(mostly Prophet) warning you about the enemy activities up ahead. And players can't really tell whether they are using the gun or underbarrel attachment from the way the protagonist holds the gun, and switching between rifles and underbarrel attachments always show the animation of protagonist adjusting fire mode selector. It's not even fit for being a benchmarking tool either, since its graphics isn't good enough to justify its poor performance on the highest settings or higher settings.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was once the benchmark for rig capabilities, while I beat the original back in the day I did not remember much of it. So I’ll base this review off the remastered version. Pro’s: • Visually the game is still pretty decent, obviously it’s not anywhere near today’s AAA titles. Graphically it’s somewhere in between a PS4/PS5.• It plays well on deck but it does drain your battery. I get about 2 hours of gameplay on a full charge. • It’s a good before bed game, it doesn’t require much thought and you can unwind while playing it. Cons:• Cloaking doesn’t seem to be as effective as it once was, it seems to randomly not work. • Ammo for the SCAR is scarce so you spend the majority of the game using whatever crap you find on the ground. • Enemies seem to materialize out of no where, while this can make the game entertaining after awhile you end up running by them to avoid the repetitive BS. Conclusion: I see a lot of people complaining about hit markers and TTK on enemies. This is not COD and the game was from a different era. It’s somewhat of a cross between Soldier of Fortune and DOOM. It was experimental at the time with a lot going on (with the nano suit) compared to typical FPS at the time. It’s a good game if you remember what it is.. is it worth 30$??? Not really, then again if it keeps me entertained for more than 10 minutes it’s better than most 60$ games. TLDR: If you played the OG crysis give this a shot, if you just got your drivers license in the last 10 years don’t bother.

_childDocuments_.review: It is still staggering to believe that a game of this graphical calibre came out in 2007. From a visual perspective, Crysis at its best can still look better than many AA games coming out even today. For older gamers, it is worth getting just to actually be able to run it on max settings now (provided you have the hardware), for younger gamers, it is a look into the past and an opportunity to experience a technical feat firsthand.This is not to say that Crysis is perfect though, far from it. While the story premise is reasonably interesting, there is barely any depth to it. Certain sections like the flying part, while ambitious, will definitely feel lacking now that one has the experience of controls in modern games. Some of the UX design is a bit questionable as well and the power-jump is just downright wonky.That being said, it is still worth getting, at least when on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis with a new coat of paint, kind of. There are a number of features that are straight up missing that makes the first game more fun, biggest offenders being modding support and quicksaves. No leaning is not gone, it's just set to a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ bind by default. Outside that, the game's art style has also changed to something a lot more vibrant (). The game also seems to nerf strength mode and speed mode even in classic mode. Only real improvements made to the game are optimization (though it doesn't feel like it once you set everything to very high), and the removal of SecuRom. Honestly I'd prefer if Crytek changed the Steam client of Crysis to the one they sell on GOG instead of spending all this time on an inferior port. Overall, I'd only recommend this game if you're a die hard Crysis fan that wants to see some extra eye candy. $15 isn't too bad of a price for this game, but I personally would not pay a penny more than that. If you don't have the first game, I highly recommend it still, just get it from GOG instead and play with mods.Honestly I'm open to changing this review but only if strength and speed mode are reverted, gameplay changes like trees not breaking from punches are fixed, color settings and times of day are reverted to what they were in the first game, modding support is added, Warhead is included in the game, and further optimizations are made for multithreaded cpus. So yeah, just buy the GOG version and mod it.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing Crysis back in the day and being blown away. I've had an absolute blast coming back to it years later but ran into a game breaking bug near the end. There's an on-rails section where an NPC is driving while you shoot, but he crashes the car instantly killing me at exactly the same corner every time. I tried many things to get past the problem: restarting the level, changing arbitrary settings, verifying files and even moving the game's install directory but the bug persisted. As a last resort I decided to uninstall the game and re-download it. Turns out the game doesn't support could saves so I've lost all my progress. I probably should have checked but that's the last straw for me. I'm not playing all the way to the end again knowing that I might just get stuck  anyway. A real shame as I was really enjoying the remaster and it holds up remarkably well so many years after the original release. I don't think this bug is particularly common, as there's not many people talking about it online so your mileage may vary (FYI I was playing on Deck) but I can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis 1 has aged like milk. The first half is filled with boring, uninspired semi-sandbox levels you can just sprint through. The second half is linear shooting sections against the same 2 alien types over and over again. Exposition is dumped on you in the last level and then the game abruptly ends. Impressive for 2007, Crysis 1's visuals cannot carry it's lackluster shooting. Voice acting is laughably bad, especially from it's side characters. Weapons spurt out flat, tinny noises vaguely resembling a gunshot; throwing objects through certain walls results in a mess of visual bugs and broken physics. The suit noises are still delightful though. How I do enjoy hearing "maximum"...well anything really over and over again. As for the remaster fixing performance issues - the addition of DLSS has the game running way better than before. Which is a massive benefit due to how the original Crysis is held together with duck tape and glue. Optimizations have been made across the board, which don't so much fix the longstanding CPU issue, but rather circumvent it. With modern hardware you'll be seeing Crysis 1 for the first time at 144fps+ which is worth any sort of other visual downgrades to the color pallet. It does however, still run noticeably worse than Crysis 2 & 3; despite those games visuals still holding up to modern titles.

_childDocuments_.review: I was fooled by misleading reviews for Crysis Remastered and Crysis 2 Remastered. TL;DR: Crysis Remastered is the best Crysis game (even better than the original) and Crysis 2 Remastered is the worst of all three remasters.Disclaimer: I am a PC player and I never play action games on consoles. For me its blasphemous to even think of playing games like Crysis on a console.Important Note: I have seen some reviews mention that they have changed the gameplay aspect of using the nanosuite. While this is true, for those of us who liked the original behaviour, they have provided an option in the gameplay menu to switch back to  the classic mode.Suggestion to players: Play on Hard difficulty (even if you are playing it for the first time).Longer version: Crysis Remastered genuinely feels like a remaster unlike Crysis 2 which even after remaster looks like trash. The visual upgrades in Crysis Remastered are evident and they are not just some subtle changes over the original. The game looks like those upcoming photorealistic UE5 games that we see in YouTube videos. And I am saying this based on the gameplay without ray tracing turned on. This reminds me of just one con this game has- on some AMD GPUs you cannot turn on the ray tracing. I surfed internet for some workarounds but none of them actually worked. Other than that this game is a masterpiece. When I say this, just know that this is coming from a long time fan of Metro and S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series. One of the most difficult thing in video games is handling AI especially AI of human enemies/NPCs. Crysis put many modern games to shame in this department. BGM and SFX is spot on in this game. And the setting of tropical island perfectly handled. Plot is engaging and keeps you intrigued till the very end.Ratings:Graphics: 9/10Aesthetics: 10/10BGM: 10/10SFX/Sound effects: 7/10Story/Plot: 7/10Gameplay: 9/10Performance - No ray tracing (PC: i5 13600k + RX 6700xt): 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I played this for about 2 hours and couldn't understand why I wasn't having fun. Crysis 1 is a fantastic game, that is not in question. I was enchanted as a kid by the physics engine and the very small detailed interactions with things like palm trees, bushes, and foliage. But...- The suit is, by default, the Crysis 2/3 suit and for a game that's designed with the Crysis 1 suit in mind, this decision baffles me. There's a toggle to force it into the Crysis 1 suit but that should be the default IMHO as the game was designed for it.- The hotkeys for the suit do not work or at least don't change from the Crysis 2 hotkeys.- They removed manual saves and quick save/load. I lost about 5 minutes of gameplay because I had to get up and go to work. I was in a safe place with no enemies around (because I had dealt with them) and I didn't have enough time to push forward to the next checkpoint.- You can't skip splash animations. Yes it's a nitpick, but I don't need to be told who made the game every single time I boot it up. Yeah I get it, can I play now?- The game is three times the size of the original. And speaking as an inexperienced loser nerd, yeah the game's graphics are better so I understand high-resolution textures add on a gig or two. But the graphics aren't that much better to warrant the size of the remastered version.For all these problems, the fundamental game has been, to my knowledge, untouched. Go find the original. Buy it on GOG or something, find one of the fan patches that allows the game to run, and play the original.You'll save a couple bucks, the game will run better, it'll only take up a third of the drive space, and the game will be a better experience for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately this is sadly an inferior version of the original Crysis. This game also lacks Mod support so I doubt that any of the excellent modded maps or campaigns will be compatible.  Just a shame really.  It's still fun - and still beautiful, just you can tell that there's a lot missing.  Furthermore, neither this or the future remastered crysis games will feature multiplayer at the time of writing.  So..  even less value.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of this game since I tried it in 2010. It was she who made me leave PS2 for PC. So I played the 2007 original (luckily I have it) to be as objective as possible. I played both games on "SWAT" difficulty in hopes of fixing the problems that the original 2007 version had.    It's cool to go back in time. Such familiar cards, as if they had never left them and the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥ balance of opponents (the enemy in the cap can withstand 5 blows to the head or dies immediately) Eh... MEMORIES!!!   Controlling the suit from part 2 is very inconvenient (for the reason that the developers didn’t just cut out one mechanic and replace it with another, but put two on top of each other (they conflict with each other), so I returned the controls to the completely original ones (although I think the controls are the second part is the best). The problem of the original with the strange use of processor cores has been solved, but added “probably for balance” optimization problems have been . Played on graphics settings (CAN IT RUN CRYSIS?) with Ray tracing and immediately my video card (2060 super) transferred me from the native resolution (4K) to FullHD. On FullHD, stays around 57-53 FPS. In a battle and with high dynamics, it drops to 47-44 FPS. You can turn off “Rays”, then you will get +10 fps, but the shadows and lighting greatly lose their beauty, and sometimes even the shadows of the guys, which hurts the eyes. You can also turn on "DLSS", you will also get an increase of +30-40 FPS, but the picture loses a lot in detail and smoothing. I played with on "Rays" and "DLSS" are disabled. So the minimum optimization requirements are still lacking. The enemies hit much harder than in the original, it feels like I'm going against them with my bare ass, and not in an armored suit. Also, the suit’s energy is consumed faster, so you have to sit out more often to charge (a little annoying).   As expected, I beat a game from my childhood that isn't as amazing as it used to be. A very strangely made remaster. Updated textures and shadows were added only to certain elements (vegetation, ground, water, rocks, lighting and costume), and everything else was forgotten. And it looks strange when there is a cool detailed costume on which shadows and lighting play, and the face of the Prophet or Psycho is the same as in the original (was it really difficult to add details). For my personal taste, the picture is also very oversaturated and the atmosphere of some locations is lost. Everything else is the same as before.   A remaster of a game that many wanted but ended up underwhelming. I would advise you to play the 2007 version (if you can find it) and experience more sensations from childhood, and modern builds will already give more fps than before (I got 85 in 4K with a drop to 72 FPS). I expected more from this game, but unfortunately it disappointed me. So I cannot advise an ordinary person (not familiar with the series) to buy it, and to an ardent fan of the original I can only say that it is at your own peril and risk.If you got here, then know that you are the BEST!!!         P.S. More detailed information about my PC can be found in , and you can also ask a question)))

_childDocuments_.review: Started off loving it! It brought back great memories, it looked awesome and played much better than the original, but in the end I can't say that this version is worth it.Getting the positives out of the way; the game is loads of fun to play, looks way more detailed () than the original and you can play the game on maxed graphics without frame issues ().If you played the original from 2007, maybe you would be enticed to get a copy of this game. Fortunately for me, it was on a massive sale and I decided to give this a shot since I haven't played the game in years. I was impressed by the detail and how well things were running, up until they weren't.Although the graphics look awesome, the game is still poorly optimised and you'll notice it particularly in some areas where there's lots of water. Raytracing isn't really worth it as well, but you especially need to lower object detail to medium to get better frames. In fact, everything on medium looks pretty good, so just play on that for better frames.The worst part though is the amount of model glitches and poor controls. Mouse sensitivity was way too fast and I had to adjust my mouse DPI. Keybindings are just crap. I play ESDF style so naturally that'll include my tank and VTOL. It doesn't respond at all and I was forced to use WSDF on these missions, not a game breaker... at least not until the VTOL mission.. Mouse controls on this mission don't work at all! I've read forums or guides and nobody seems to have a solution that I saw. Your only option is to plug in a controller, which I had, but it was an awful experience. I got incredibly frustrated during this mission and it made me wonder what was the point of remastering a pretty damn good game and then you mess up so many things, especially the controls. It just appears to be grabbing a quick buck and ruining the memory of a great game, I don't understand this logic, but it's becoming far too common nowadays!You're better off playing the 2007 version. It works, it still looks great and it doesn't have half of the problems the remastered version has.If you're like me who got it on a very good deal, then sure, pick up a copy. I got all of the achievements in one single run, so that was pretty cool, but make sure to get a controller as well, since you won't be able to beat the VTOL mission without it.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? The original was a masterpiece when it was released in 2007 - it had jaw-dropping visuals and was a good shooter, too. This remastered version makes the game playable on Windows 10, with new resolutions (ultrawidescreen worked fine), and adds raytracing if you are one of the few owners of a supported GPU. It also removes the quicksave option of the original and does not include multiplayer or the Warhead expansion. I finished the campaign without problems, but it had a few visual glitches now and then. I would not really call it a masterpiece today anymore - but it was still great fun to fight as a US commando soldier with an overpowered suit and kill North Korean soldiers and then aliens. And yes, I did enjoy the fight against the aliens, too, even if this part of the game plays completely different from the first few hours. The tropical island still looks awesome, some of the levels are really big and you can explore them freely, using different vehicles. The story is absolutely stupid, but who cares - at least it has a story to follow. There may be better FPS out there today, but I still had my fun up to the last fight with the alien mothership. They don't make shooters like this today anymore!FPS for nostalgic fans who want to re-experience the classic, or gamers who want to know if their rig can run Crysis.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, first time Crysis player here. I really enjoyed this after I could get into the swing of things. Sure there's tonnes of criticism from purists - but if you haven't experienced it then I suggest you do.I really didn't like Far Cry 1 at launch or now, but this really takes the cake on everything that title should have been. There's rather unique concepts such as the nanosuit, a range of  limited but effective weapons. Overall it's a very polished experience such as reflects gaming around the time of release.I'm excited to head back to the franchise - as soon as the titles become available through Steam in a year's time. Big thumbs up from me - I could never play this one back in the day.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a boring game.You start out in a repetitive cycle of fighting enemies in the way to your object, fighting enemies at the objective, and disabling a few "signal jammers" (which feels like a massively cheap side quest). This wouldn't necessarily be a problem, hadn't the combat been so bland either. Shooting heads doesn't kill, same for close-range shotgun rounds. Long time to kill leads to slow pacing. Pair this with the use of your suit and the time you'll be waiting for it to recharge, and pacing goes down the drain.That's the first half. Midway through, you're dumped into this obnoxious alien ship, with unclear routes, unresponsive character movement and a couple of aliens which are again, not fun to fight.And then there's the mission where you pilot a ship - more unresponsive movement and boring combat. Not to mention that all throughout your allies keep rushing you to get to the objective, which honestly doesn't do anything for the game's atmosphere, it's just really annoying.Meh, not for me. It's an old game, I get it. Maybe it was fine back when it launched. I don't think it is by today's standards. I'd save the money and skip this one.

OH WOW MUCH ELITE, SUCH BADASS, VERY SOLDIER, KEKG*Go play Stalker Anomaly for an example of Intuitive AI (which, btw, is a 2004 game by a small company modded and updated even until 2021)- ZERO Multi-approach; "Oh, a different branching path? SIKE it's just a 10 metre-difference vantage point that gives you a slight advantage over YET ANOTHER of the HUNDREDS of 3-5 people brain-dead mobs*Go play the Dishonored series for a great example of multi-approach that ACTUALLY makes a difference in story progression, upgrade system, and ending- Weapon variability; with a remaster, at least you'd consider weapon degradation (just for hardest difficulty is fine, just AT LEAST make an effort to make things different), rewarding exploration with different mods for your weapons, or dropships for your suit upgrades (since, you know, your MOST ELITE JSOC soldiers are in trouble in a remote island). The weapon mods are just 3-5 things that you'll only change 1 every 30 min or so (I only swapped between reflex sight and assault scope for my single-shot silencer AK for 1/3 of the game, simply because switching other mods in other weapons does not bring any difference nor variability to the way i approach objectives anyways)- Gameplay Loop (or, in simpler terms, Addictiveness); Crysis is basically "Fight this 3-7 people brain-dead mobs with this slightly cool suit with ONLY 4 functions" repeated ad nauseum. No effort whatsoever in the remaster to add new gameplay elements whatsoever, improve existing AI or interaction, nope, nothing... even the options to interact with the suit functions feels counter-intuitive (why is there no options to quickly toggle between "normal" shield mode with "heavy shield" mode on PC? the elite of the elite suits for TACTICAL COMBAT and they can't make this distinction???)*The perfect example of excellent gameplay loop is Dredge; ironically i just played it before this, a LITERAL FISHING GAME less than 1 GB is so well-designed it's actually MORE FUN than a shooter with "one of the best graphics" in terms of gameplay loop- Scripted scenes; in one of the missions, I'm cloaked, sneaking around the forest, suddenly the detection bar jumps up to max, a group of soldiers insta-appears right in front of me, then stand there doing nothing and the previously max-out detection bar jumps to 3/4 and start lowering... This is just one of the examples of badly designed scripted scenes, and is a stellar example of lazy game design; mind you, I'm not trying to break the game nor glitch it, I'm simply using the stealth-mechanics AS INTENDED lore- and gameplay-wise*Plenty of games have cleverly designed scripted scenes that feels "natural"; Sekiro, Deus Ex, Fallout NV, that does not break immersion in such a jarring wayTLDR; One-dimensional shooter with the same "here's 3-7 brain-dead AI enemies that can't even comprehend where you are even when their friend was shot ONE METER IN FRONT of them" gameplay loop repeated ad nauseum, a seemingly cool tactical suit that's actually counter-intuitive (in PC at least) designed to impress 7-14 year-olds by visuals(ironically, the only reason i played is because i remembered back then the only good thing regarding this game is its graphics, and i wanted to reconfirm, in case I'm wrong LOL)

_childDocuments_.review: My opinion on Crysis remains the same ever since it launched back in 2007.The semi-open sandbox gameplay gives you freedom to choose whatever approach suits your play style (pun not intended).With objectives scattered throughout the island in combination with the nanosuit and a decent selection of arsenal to choose from, the first half of the game is one of the best tactical shooters ever made.The 2nd half of the game unfortunately is still as disappointing as ever and really kills the pacing of the game.The remaster is no doubt a technically better looking game than the original in many ways and runs better too. However, I can't help but feel something was lost along the way. The saturation and colors make the setting seem more fantastical in nature which is neither a good or bad thing. Just different.There are obvious visual downgrades in some areas thanks to the console port. Character skin straight up looks worse in the remaster perhaps due to the lighting from the new engine.Overall, I'd say the remastered visuals are too different and not a clear improvement over the original to replace it.With all that said, I would still recommend getting the game in this form. It's not a bad way to play Crysis by any means and can look stunning at times.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis remastered had a rough start at since there were lots of bugs and optimization is nonexistent. However, I can certainly say that they've patched almost all the annoying things that were either overlooked or not properly tested.Game mechanics are easy to learn and fun to mess with, however remastered edition certainly has broken some things such as dynamic buildings. It used to take quite an effort to demolish a building but now one power fist is all it takes. I can certainly say that the gun-play in this game is annoying since enemies are like bullet sponge (humans), and it takes the immersion and fun away for me. However, once you get used to it, you'll just go on.For this price point, I can certainly say that this game is worth it. If you've never played Crysis before or get used to triple A games in 2023, it will certainly feel clunky. Crysis was always a janky but beautiful tech demo. The remastered is the same mess but with one huge change of adapting the more intuitive suit controls from Crysis 2 and 3. Now the janky can be navigated with relative ease, making this a far better experience. Recommended only to buy within the 3-game bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I was a boy, pining for time to play on the diminutive Game-Cube with my friends in 2007, I knew of this game."The game of the future" as some said, "Unbelievable graphics!" and "A game so advanced, you need a computer from NASA to run it!"Now that I'm grown, have my own beefy computer, and the game has a modern remaster to pull it to relevance a decade and a half later - I thought I'd give this remnant from the past a shot and see what I was missing out on.Mind you, I have no rosy lens or nostalgia goggles when I see this game, and I wasn't expecting to be blown away or witness some legendary epiphany of gaming through this - I was expecting a fun, entertaining game.It is a shame that I found a great deal of disappointment and mediocrity where I was expecting thrill and fun.The presentation alone is a specific taste. The mid-2000's was known for this cringe-inducing irreverence and "too cool" pretense that saturated entertainment and made games like Halo a poetic masterpiece in relativity, and this game is no different as a product of that era. Characters talk as though they are in a Saturday morning cartoon, everything feels disjointed and dulled as though its intended market was around the age of 10.While the premise begins interesting, it doesn't take long for things to devolve.While the marketing material and all of the best gameplay points to an immersive shooter, the truth is that the creators modeled their work after Call Of Duty 2 and 3 - which achieved near parody of Modern Warfare which came out that very same year. Instead of focusing entirely on the solid core of shooter gameplay, the game constantly introduces setpieces and new mechanics that last for a level (Or sometimes only a part of a level) which throw the entire tone off from being an immersive piece into being a wacky, zany comic book from history's dust-bin.This remaster has done a lot to bring the game into the modern landscape, but there's only so much that a Remaster can do to turn a 15 year old game into a relevant technological marvel. Once I toned Raytracing down, my computer was running more than fine with only a few dropped frames at intense moments of the game - but in the end, there are a lot more visually impressive experiences around today, or even from many years ago. Textures are low resolution, god-rays look like a flat widget, dust effects are cheap. While the game was ahead of its time with things like Real-Time-Shadows and the sort, such comforts are not nearly as stone-cold impressive as they must have been back when Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare was released. Simply put: Its main selling point has failed to stand the test of time, what was once jaw-dropping and ground breaking has become a modern convenience.When you get into the game, the dissonance begins to creep in like an insidious illness. Within a few minutes, the most optimal strategy will become clear: Use your cloak to line up a headshot, uncloack and shoot, recloak instantly, move a little and repeat.The combat aspects were ahead of its time, indeed, as the game feels like an unholy mixture of Call Of Duty games blended with Far Cry. But, as one may remember, Call Of Duty and Far Cry games are all about aggression and speed - but Crysis, on the other hand, revolves around a more methodical approach. The two aspects of gameplay are laid out plain to see: on one hand you have an incredibly fast-paced power fantasy with superhuman powers that allow players to become a walking army... on the other there is an ultra-realistic hardcore simulator that wants to break your bones for broth. These two elements clash. Does the game want you to sit behind cover as you're pinned down by a turret, waiting for an opportunity to run to the next foxhole like Call Of Duty - does it want you frantically fleeing into the woods to lay an ambush like Far Cry - or does it want you to storm in like a super-soldier and trash the place? Answer: None of the above, but all at the same time. It's a mess. The most efficient way to play is the most boring.Something more at the game's core is the Energy System. Everything you do costs Energy: Running, Jumping, Throwing, Cloaking, Armor. And it takes ~10s to replentish. During this time, you will basically have to wait before you continue playing the game. As a loose calculation, I suspect that ~10s out of every 70 that I played this game, I was simply WAITING for my energy to return so I can get back to playing it. Which means that, in my 7 hours of playing the game, nearly 1 HOUR of it was me WAITING to jump, sprint, interact, cloak, or have armor.To make matters worse - AI is severely lacking. The basic grunts are generally brick-stupid and make for easy fodder, but more 'advanced' enemies later in the game follow a formulaic move-set that players will learn in a matter of seconds, and then have to endure for another couple of hours. It is not an engaging interaction between man and machine as much as a test of patience.Grunts were bad enough, but the game forces a couple of extremely contrives and laughably bad "boss fights" your way at a few points, which are so poor - it begs the question "Why even bother?"The most blatant misplay of all was the lack of collectables, secrets, or character growth. Abilities cannot be expanded upon or increased, weapons will always be disposable, no hidden collectable items, no secret power ups, no "true ending". It's just the same march from A to B every game with a static player and static gameplay. There are no dynamics in play outside of the visual presentation. With a few exceptions of strange puzzles that don't belong in this game at all.And in spite of levels appearing open-ended, they are all linear in every practical way.I used a term to describe the game experience to my wife: "The Thin Cloak Of Immersion"I love IM-Sims, where players get into the mind of the character and project an attitude as though the events of the game are real or serious by nature. Playing this way in Crysis, I had an enjoyable time sleuthing past enemies, knocking out foes, and killing rival soldiers when they saw me to best conceal the truth of my nature... but after a meaningless death for a silly reason or another (Falling, random land mine, pressed the wrong button, etc.) the Immersion was broken like tension on a water's surface. Fickle and fleeting as it was, I had fun trying to extract some semblance of immersion, but the truth is that the game is such a trial of endurance - the first sacrifice to play is Immersion itself.This was a big lesson that I learned from this game - Time is the enemy of immersion. And a game that demands players use TIME as a currency to play, will never draw players in.The other lesson that I learned from this game is that POLISH < SUBSTANCE. While a well polished product, Crysis simply lacks substance to elevate it over the other offerings in this day and age.What holds it back is not so much negativity, but mediocrity.The only thing worse than an unspeakably bad game is one so tortuously boring that it feels like a chore to play.It got to the point where I was tabbing out of the game to get some remote work done in my spare time.You heard that right.I literally was so bored with the game I chose to do WORK over playing it.~TL;DR5/10Crysis is an Average game. (Painfully so)it feels like a very ambitious tech demo, but what holds it back the most is that on one side it has a comic book power fantasy, and on the other it has an immersive, serious simulator presentation - and the two clash horrendously throughout the playthrough. In spite of its ambitions to spark a flame that will elevate it into stardom, this game has been left in the cold - buried deep down and forgotten under a mountainous island of superior alternatives.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Crysis now in 2021 is a surreal experience and also an extremely enjoyable one. I can only imagine how awesome this game was back in the day (if you had the hardware to run it). Sadly, I didn’t and I never played it back then, even though I would have loved to. Playing this game now for the first time puts the rest of the series into context for me. I understand the other games better and the series, as a whole, makes more sense. I like the visuals in this remaster and I love how surreal it feels to play an old game that's been cleaned up a bit. The game looks great to me and I think it’s a fantastic mix between old and new aesthetics. I tried to play OG Crysis here on Steam a while ago but I couldn’t enjoy it. I did manage to get it working to some degree on Windows 10 but there was no proper controller support. The performance of this remaster is totally fine and the proper controller support is really what made the game accessible for me... finally. I also got it for a great price because I already owned the original here on Steam, so what is there to complain about?Crysis is a lot of fun to play, it’s like a military sandbox simulator with crazy Koreans and science fiction elements. I always liked the idea in the Crysis sequels, of fighting the soldiers first and then changing things up, to fight the aliens for the second half of the game. Playing through the remaster let me experience that idea in it’s first iteration. Which in-turn made me appreciate the sequels even more and what they were trying to achieve. The hardest difficulty setting (Delta) is great because it makes the game more immersive, without becoming annoying (except for the final boss). It’s really cool to actually need to use the suit powers and environmental cover while taking head-shots and feeling like a bad-ass ninja. There are some cool details on the hardest difficulty too like having to listen for grenades without HUD markers. While the human enemies only speak Korean which makes it harder to determine what they are doing.Where as the rest of the game is totally fine, the final boss is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pain in the ass, on the hardest difficulty setting. Crysis is a lot of fun, just like the sequels and on the harder difficulty settings it’s even more fun, with the only exception to this being the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ final boss. Which required me to die a lot and come up with a crazy trial and error strategy. There is also a fairly crappy level where you have to fly an aircraft and the controls are pretty bad but it’s actually not too difficult, once you get used to it. Crysis Remastered is also a relatively easy and fun game to get 100% achievements on (again with the exception of the final boss). A couple of the more advanced achievements are fairly bugged though, such as the ones for completing the game on the harder difficulties. It’s do-able but they are a bit janky and you need to work around this. Anyway.. this remaster made this fantastic game accessible to me, playing with a controller on Windows 10, for a very low price. I really enjoyed it and I highly recommend that you play it too!

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis Remastered is exactly what it says on the tin. A new paint job of the classic 2007 sandbox shooter.And although it's a remaster of one of the most notorious computer-melting video games, it doesn't look as mind boggling as you'd think, and somehow manages to take some steps backwards.If you've played Crysis 1 before, you'll know exactly what to expect here. It's the same game. I'll go into the differences momentarily.If you haven't played this game before, then I can let you know that it's an incredibly fun sandbox experience that stands the test of time, for the most part. You're dropped into a jungle, in enemy territory, with a super suit. It comes with cool super power abilities like invisibility, super speed, high jump, super strength and an armor mode that minimizes damage. The physics and AI are incredibly fun to play around with. Throwing enemies into flimsy buildings is hilarious. Coming up with creative kills is gratifying, and both stealth and loud combat can be exciting. If enemies see you go invisible, they will wildly shoot around where they think you are. They push forward and try to flush you out.Enemies patrol throughout the island, in unexpected areas, and sometimes fully camouflaged. If you want to be stealthy, you actually need to constantly pay attention. Also, enemies don't all get marked so you can follow them through walls, like most modern stealth games. If anything, the AI can sometimes be a bit too observant.The game has beautiful destruction and vegetation. Crawling through lush bushes, and shooting tree trunks to watch them collapse is so cool.I found the story to be mildly interesting, and not the main attraction of the game.Ok, so what's different? The graphics got an overhaul.For the most part, textures, shadows and lighting look a lot better. I also personally like the more green, saturated look all vegetation has. The game looks gorgeous. Although, not as gorgeous as I'd expect from  the legendary Crysis. I think there are better looking games out there nowadays, but that's quite a minor complaint, as it still looks beautiful.Although, strangely enough, if you make some direct comparisons to the original, some of the graphics took steps back. Some geometry, and underwater effects looks worse. Strange, but not really an issue.Now, the biggest problem I had with the remaster, is the removal of manual saves. The game now forces you to a checkpoint system, which means if you die, you are at the mercy of auto saving, and have to hope you aren't sent too far back. Crysis 1 at its core is a sandbox game all about messing around and experimenting. I remember I used to quicksave in the original so I could try encounters out in different ways. That is now gone. Perhaps to prevent savescumming, but that should have been left to higher difficulties.Also, people saying there is no leaning anymore are most likely citing older reviews of the Epic version without doing their own research. You can lean, as it was patched into the game since.In the end, I think it's a good remaster. If you haven't played the first Crysis, I would recommend this version. On the other hand, if you HAVE already played the original, I'd say only grab this one if you love the game, and want another excuse to replay it.

_childDocuments_.review: I know the joke for years was "Can it run Crysis?" Well the best GPU at the time was a 480. The game was then ported to PS3/360. THAT port was them "remastered" on PC and this is what we get. I have a 4090 now, originally was recommend a 480. I ran down a street and I had a pretty steady 40fps for about 5 seconds straight. Whenever you can see into the distance, your frame rate absolutely tanks. The optimization is awful. Crysis is bringing PCs to its knees! The game looked amazing when it came out, and still looked amazing years later. The game is 17 years old now and on top of the line machines today, it still runs terribly. It's not because the game looks great, it's because the optimization is awful. For a 17 year old game that got "remastered," it still looks great, but there's absolutely no reason for this terrible optimization when they've had this long to work on it... Oh, and to top it all off, there are no manual saves.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Ultrawide supported just fineYoung people coming up can play and enjoy a legendary shooter that I loved so much back in college...that's about itCons:The manual save system is completely removed. It has checkpoint saves only and you can't choose to go back to specific checkpoints either...your only options are the most recent checkpoint or the beginning of the level and that's it.Every time I start the game back up, that dastardly motion blur setting is back on again no matter how many times I turn it off.While some of the sound effects have been improved (starting rifle and the pistol for example), some are just as bad as they were before (the fictional AK sounds unchanged) however some are significantly worse...the footsteps, even when walking on grass or sand sound like you have giant metal boots and are moving on a metal floor...even when sneaking softly.To use the suit quickwheel menu like the old game, you enable this in the gameplay settings. When you are crouching down and access this wheel, it causes you to stand up for no reason. So hiding behind something and accessing this wheel to cloak means standing up and being seen, defeating the purpose of cloaking because now you need armor mode and are in a fire fight. If you disable this classic wheel mode, you are either in armor or strength mode and just manually enable cloak when needed. However, when you run, it auto uses speed mode! What, why!? I don't want to use speed mode every single time. That should be its own separate setting in my opinion.I think the stealth is off...I used to be able to crouch and hide in bushes/shrubs or prone crawl in high grass until fairly close to an enemy, causing them to get surprised. Now I can sit perfectly still in some bushes and the enemies see me from a pretty good distance away. Crysis 2 and 3 had that issue where stealth was REALLY bad so I'm guessing they maybe used a newer Crytek engine from one of those games to make this one and weren't able to replicate the awesome quality stealth that the original had.The game is horribly optimized.Optimization deserves its own section:I'm no fool, I get that the highest settings are often designed for screenshots and to attract gamers. It gives us something to upgrade for, gives us something to compare to, gives us something to benchmark etc. So typically if I can't max a game I lower stuff one setting at a time as needed and eventually play it smoothly. My system currently is an i9-12900k, 3090ti and 32GBs of DDR5 running windows 10 on a gen 5 (EDIT: oops gen 4 not 5) PCIe NVMe. Theoretically it should be strong enough for everything I can throw at it since I am only running a 1440p ultrawide, not a 4K but still, the max settings were aimed at being future proof such as with the original game so I began tweaking the usual suspects like ray tracing and shadows etc without being annoyed. I got to the coastal house of level 1 (when the sun is up and the jet flies by) and disabled v-sync so I could begin troubleshooting. I ended up basically lowering EVERYTHING to low and it still didn't feel smooth and playable. There is one setting however (Objects Quality) that can't be changed in game so I went back to the main menu to change it. After it lagged on 'Can it Run Crysis' I tried 'Very High' and then 'High.' It started to feel better on 'Medium' but didn't feel smooth until 'Low.' You have got to be kidding me. It seriously either lagged hardcore or felt like my walk speed was varying in speed as I moved along with anything above 'Low.' Never seen a single setting so badly optimized. Isn't a dealbreaker by itself but really odd.Long story short - I think this was a huge disappointment and can't recommend it to anyone that played the original.If you did NOT play the original then this one is probably a better choice since the original is also horribly optimized but also struggles in other ways on modern systems.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a re-textured downgrade. The graphics are fine i guess but I cant shake the feeling that this could have just easily been a community mod instead of a separate game. I made a list of everything I encountered during my play through. If you dont wanna read it fine, here is a small summary.This game is a graphic overhaul. It adds nothing, and removes a lot of things unnecessarily. This is almost like the crysis version of the gta definitive edition. If you want this for benchmark purposes get it at $5.things I noticed and encountered vol. 1- The graphics look about the same as any dumbass "remaster" game released in todays gaming market.- The controls are weird. It's like Crysis 3 with a Crysis 1 story- No quick saving. As someone who loves to do stupid things in games this being removed really annoyed me- seat changing in vehicles (you can switch between driver and gunner but nothing else)- Sensitivity in the gunner seat of vehicles is ungodly low. Even at max (sensitivity in game) it is super slow. Increase your mouse to about 3000 dpi and you can destroy anything in your path. -grenade changing is weird. Nothing wrong with it just weird. - you can drive the tank all the way to the end of the onslaught level. (good thing)- that bug where you could put like 100000 bullets into a guy and they dont die until you get within arms length of them is fixed (good thing)- I'm surprised that they kept the "suit shortcuts" setting. (good thing)- sometimes the sound would cutout (like explosions would make no noise) or play continuously (like gunfire would play but no one would be shooting). - Cant pick up a few of the items. Example; in the original, you could pick up rocks, sticks, branches and crates. Everything was intractable. In this version you cant pick up any of those items, but they are still animated in the world. Not a big deal but weird that they'd remove being able to pick up these items but keep them looking like pickup-able items.- ai is retarded. Lots of enemies walk around with no weapon or spawn without one and pretend to shoot at you. Also had an occasions where the enemy would spawn outside their vehicle (like a tank in onslaught or AAA gun in assault) and just do nothing. - No grenade launcher indicator. y'know when you have the grenade launcher attachment and you hold mouse 1 it gives a reticle to aim at. Yeah that was removed. -occasionally my controls would mess up where I could not do most of the key functions. I could only shoot and use wasd. - that one flying frog glitch when you pick up a frog and throw it straight up and it would fly away. I know its considered a bug but I thought the devs would have kept it as a joke or something. - the pistol sounds different in single fire but if you switch it to double round burst it sounds like the original pistol. It's sort of the case with most guns and their firing mode. - on the relic level, when approaching the graveyard in a vehicle, you can't. in the original you could drive a vehicle into the graveyard and gun down the nanosuit enemies. But in this version, the tree that you could just drive under now completely stops you.- cant hold crouch and open your suit radial menu at the same time. BUT if you tap the crouch button THEN open the suit menu, you stay crouched. - no cold on guns in the paradise lost level. What I mean is; in the original when you get to that level the guns would be frozen over and the red dot is also clear as day where in the original it was frozen over and near useless. - There was no feeling of environment change. In the first level when you see the sunrise the world is completely bright. The point of that in the original (I assumed) was to show off the lighting affects the engine was capable of. This game felt like cl_fullbright was on at times it should have been.- in the last level there are a few npcs you can push around. If you move them into cut scenes they can make the cut scene 10x better- "funny how the older version of the cry engine almost seems better than the current." is a thought that crossed my mindI will never play this version of the game again
