_childDocuments_.review: Crysis was my favorite video game franchise as a teenager, yet I was lukewarm at Crysis 1 for a few things – balance, level design and AI, but this remastered version turns out to be more likeable thanks to rebalance.The original is not an easy game and the high-tech nanosuit always feels like it is no thicker than a piece of paper, especially for my younger self who was a much less experienced gamer. Some weapons are difficult to work with because of the range and recoil, and damage seems wildly inconsistent, like a helicopter could eat 3 shots of RPG like nothing.With the rebalance in remaster, nonsense like that no longer happens and all weapons are more manageable and fun to use with consistent damage. Difficulty and playtime drop as a result (15 vs 7 hours for the first playthrough), but it is a major step up for the experience. On the flip side, the necessity of stealth largely decreases, and I find myself always in favor of direct combat with the game becoming easier, so I say the remaster is less strategic and more simple shooting fun, though higher difficulty should revert that.Perhaps because of the rebalance and the lower difficulty, or the developer made some changes in levels (I am not sure if there are any), or just me became a better gamer, the remaster doesn’t have a lot of frustration the original has, which is why back then, I was not a fan of the more open level design of Crysis 1.With the frustration gone, I started to appreciate the more open level design allowing more freedom to decide how to approach objectives. I also become appreciative of the level variety that has car, ship, tank and aircraft levels arranged in an organized manner like Halo, which the second and third Crysis no longer have. That said, it is still confusing AF on how to kill the first boss in the final level as the game still doesn’t give clear instructions.It is disappointing that the remaster doesn’t fix the biggest issue - AI. They are still dumb AF and they still have hypersensitive detection as the original - the lush vegetation makes it difficult for players to spot enemies, but they have no trouble seeing through, reminding me why the OG is so frustrating.The OG has great graphics for its time but is not comparable to modern games. The remaster updated but didn’t overhaul graphics, and what really noticeable changes are clearer water, bluer sky, greener vegetation and more saturated color tones, which make it less photorealistic than the original. While doing so, the game introduces a contrast issue causing dark areas to be very hard to see, but without offering a proper tool to calibrate.In conclusion, the remaster indeed is a better version of the game, but I don’t think the improvements are substantial enough to warrant a re-release (an rebalance update to the OG is probably enough). It is more of an eye-grabber for Cry Engine and future sequel. But if you have the original, you can get the remaster dirt cheap now, so why not?

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be as honest as I can with this Crysis 1 "Remaster"I'm brand new to Crysis, never having had the ability to run these games when they were in their prime, back circa 2007 or whatever. I've since bought the original Crysis 1 after this remaster made me puke blood.So naturally, anyone new to the series who's buying this version of Crysis 1 for the first time would probably think: "Well, I've never played the original so I might like the remaster purely for what it is, despite it's many claimed differences".Wrong.You're going to shoot yourself in the foot if you approach this Remaster with that attitude, and you ain't going to have no nanosuit to protect those toes either. Allow me to begin:(1) The "volumetric clouds" look like silly bubbles.(2) The sky is so blue that it makes me feel like I'm in Bikini Bottom from Spongebob.(3) The grass is a saturated cartoon green that makes me feel as if someone tried to put me in a jar with a leaf so that they could attempt to mimic my human environment for me.(4) My "3080Ti Mobile" flings the fps counter from 90 down to 45 in two person gun fights, showing some very poor optimization that shouldn't be evident in a game this old. The pain doesn't stop there, I promise. This version is essentially the pc version, ported to console with downgrades, then ported back again from console back to PC with "enhancements". Lies, all lies.The old version of Crysis 1, which has since been removed from Steam, never really was the way to go either. Steam's original version was 32bit only, making it a avoidable version at best.Just avoid this, unless you like Fortnite or something.

Crysis works well for me because it's got a lovely outdoor setting, not claustrophobic at all so far. It's also got an easy mode for people who love to murder but aren't very good at it. I still die, but not that much... There are four difficulty settings, so for you people out there with skills, I'm sure you'd find the more difficult settings fun. This game is not overly complicated. I don't understand anything about guns, so it'll take me some time to figure out which ones work best for what situations, but it's not hard to switch between them and shoot. If you're looking for a super complex game, this probably isn't it. I just get my missions and keep moving through them with stealth or force or both. MAJOR CON:This game would not run for me at all initially. Steam said it was running, but no window opened anywhere with the game. I have Windows11 on a pretty decent gaming laptop. My brother-in-law ultimately had to make the game use windows 8 compatibility settings for it to run. It works fine now, but you need to know it might not run on a newer setup.

_childDocuments_.review: Buggier, looks worse, has features removed, gameplay tweaks make it worse, performance is worse. Everything about this game is worse; it's the opposite of a remaster. - Some bugs make the game outright unplayable, like losing the ability to perform any actions like switching weapons or picking up items midway through the game. The game also frequently hangs when a level has loaded 100%. Mouse movement also doesn't work for the VTOL mission, meaning you literally cannot play the game pass the VTOL mission if you don't have a controller, and even then, the controls on the gamepad are horrible, and even still bug out sometimes, where the left stick would stop working altogether. This is after the patch that was said to fix most of the issues. - It looks worse despite using the improved engine with a bunch of new graphical features, looking over-saturated and contrasty. - They removed the ability to save manually, so you'll have to rely on autosaves. - Ammo in your gun counts towards your total ammo, which didn't happen before. This doesn't make sense, the magazine in the gun isn't in my pocket, so why the change? In fact, if you empty your magazine by 1 round, you can pick up 1 additional round. This makes zero sense. - The new suit mode sucks, but at least they let you switch back to the old mode. - I can't figure out what is causing my performance to drop so badly despite the settings being similar to the old Crysis. If all this game did was add higher res textures, SMAA, TAA, DLSS, and Raytracing, that would have been at least a half-decent 'enhanced' edition, which when combined with the discount for existing Crysis owners would be fine. Then they could have thought of extras like recorded playback, crosshair customization, an FOV slider, and maybe even co-op campaign, and that would have been a good remaster. It's amazing how they instead managed to make the game worse. I literally have never had such a frustration experience trying to play a game in my life. This is such a disservice to the original Crysis which is a legendary game. Whoever is thinking of playing the game, just get the original, it's way better than this piece of crap and is even available DRM free on GOG.

_childDocuments_.review: Transport yourself back to the scorching summer of 2008, a time when gaming was forever altered by the arrival of Crysis. I vividly recall being a wide-eyed 9-year-old, eagerly exploring the realms of PC gaming for the first time. With my father's purchase of our inaugural computer and my uncle's installation of Crysis, I was thrust into a world of unparalleled excitement and challenge.In those early days, the term "but can it run Crysis?" hadn't yet become ubiquitous, but the impact of Crytek's masterpiece was palpable from the get-go. As I delved into the game, I was immediately captivated by its stunning graphics and immersive gameplay. Every pixel seemed to pulsate with life, drawing me deeper into the lush jungles and sprawling landscapes of the game's setting.But Crysis was more than just a visual spectacle; it was a true test of skill and perseverance. As a young player, navigating the game's challenges was no easy feat. From tactical encounters with enemy soldiers to heart-pounding battles against otherworldly foes, every moment was a thrilling adventure filled with triumphs and setbacks.Yet, despite the difficulty, I found myself utterly engrossed in Crysis, spending countless hours honing my skills and pushing the limits of what I thought was possible. The sense of accomplishment that came with overcoming each obstacle was unlike anything I had experienced before in a game.Looking back now, it's clear that Crysis set a revolutionary standard in gaming. Its groundbreaking graphics and innovative gameplay mechanics pushed the boundaries of what was possible in the medium, paving the way for future generations of titles to follow.As the years have passed, my admiration for Crysis has only grown stronger. And with the recent announcement of Crysis 4, I find myself eagerly anticipating the next chapter in this iconic franchise. If Crytek can capture even a fraction of the magic that made the original Crysis so special, then we're in for a truly unforgettable gaming experience.In conclusion, Crysis remains a timeless masterpiece that continues to captivate players young and old. Its stunning graphics, challenging gameplay, and enduring legacy make it a must-play for anyone with a love for gaming. So here's to Crysis, a game that will forever hold a special place in my heart and the hearts of gamers around the world.

_childDocuments_.review: They always ask "Can it run Crysis?", but no one ever asks "How is Crysis?"Germany is a funny country full of funny people with funny inventions. Like, beer, for example. ACTUAL beer. Or tilted windows. But the one german invention that truly propelled the human evolution forwards was nothing other than this little game right here.Welcome to Crysis, the best Battlefield game ever made. And sadly i´m not even kidding.Story:The year is... 2020? Damn, that triggered my Corona related PTSD...Anyway, you´re part of a taskforce of the US military about to infiltrate a North Korean island.Your primary mission is to rescue Seth Rogan who was abducted for filming "The Interview" and now is in need of rescue. Your secondary mission however is to file a ticket for some dumbass who parked his boat in the middle of the jungle.Oh and also there´s aliens because what kind of game do you think this is?That´s basically all the plot. The MC even talks so rarely that i thought this game had a mute protagonist.All the story you get is some context for why you´re going to a place with lots of Koreans in need of their lead medicine and that´s basically it. This is a compliment by the way. I like it more when games focus more on their gameplay.Speaking of which:Gameplay:As a supersoldier wearing what is basically the Mjolnir Armor from Halo just cooler, you´re always changing between different settings. You can change from neutral to invisible, or from neutral to armored, or your enemies kneecaps from healthy to nonexistant. It´s all possible thanks to your Nanosuit.Basically, if you use the simplified controls like me you´ll have the two afforementioned modes. Invisibility is pretty self explainatory. Enemies can´t see you anymore so you can sneak around them and surprise their children with a dead father this christmas. The armor mode however is a bit different, because in this game it´s practically useless. No joke. Enemies burn through your suits energy so quickly that you´re basically just tanking one more shot than usual which doesn´t really make that much of a difference...However, the speed and strength mode are a bit more interesting. Speed turns you into a drug addict, but you can also run so fast that pink hedgehogs with comically large hammers start simping for you. Strength lets you punch a mf into his next incarnation and punches through walls like an alpha-Kyle. It also reduces recoil in exchange for energy which is always welcome for more intimate long distance relationships.So you probably wonder what that Battlefield joke was all about?Well, this games singleplayer plays like a chaotic Battlefield match. You gun down enemies while F-35 jets are dogfighting above you and some poor dudes house got leveled by a car bomb. And none of that is scripted. This game managed to pull off what ever other BF game failed in: Having a good singleplayer that relied on the sandbox aspect of these games. It´s just funny that the best Battlefield campaign isn´t even in a Battlefield game.Anyway, enough dunking on BF fans. If you´ll excuse me now, i´ve got some chickens to throw.MAXIMUM VEHICULAR MANSLAUGHTER/10

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis Remastered brings the classic shooter into the modern era with significant graphical updates and support for the latest display technologies, including HDR. The game's innovative suit powers and diverse combat scenarios remain as engaging as ever, providing a gameplay experience that is both challenging and rewarding.The remaster enhances the iconic storyline and setting, allowing both new and returning players to experience the game's narrative in a visually stunning manner. The addition of modern resolutions support ensures that Crysis Remastered looks its best on contemporary hardware.However, the game's transition to the modern era is not without its flaws. Notably, the VTOL mission presents a significant challenge for PC players due to control issues when using a mouse, necessitating the use of a controller for an optimal experience. Additionally, the game suffers from a variety of bugs, including sound issues that detract from the immersive experience. Sound effects may get stuck or disappear entirely, and invisibility glitches can break the gameplay flow.Performance-wise, Crysis Remastered demands more from systems than expected, considering the technological advancements in gaming hardware. Players with high-end PCs may find the game running poorly, even when other graphically intense games perform flawlessly on the same setup.In conclusion, while Crysis Remastered successfully revives a beloved classic with stunning graphical enhancements and maintains the core gameplay elements that made the original game a landmark in the FPS genre, it is hampered by technical issues. These include control problems, bugs, and unexpected performance requirements. Despite these setbacks, for fans of the series and newcomers alike, the game offers a worthwhile experience, albeit with some caveats.

_childDocuments_.review: Its fun, yes. It was a milestone when it was initially released, and while its a super linear story shooter, it still manages to suck you in. A lot of the features of this engine was soon to be the standard in later released games.However, strictly talking about the first Crysis Remastered Game, I cannot advise you to buy it.What is the problem?The Crysis 1 Remaster is based on the Xbox 360 Release Code, and therefore is heavily downgraded in a lot of areas. (e.g. Vegetation doesnt even react to your explosions anymore.)It also just runs bad. Lets face it, its not a debate. The game has no noteworthy upgrades besides a very basic raytracing implementation and some lighting upgrades. Playing the original game heavily modded with similar upgrades, is still running - twice - as good as this remaster. How can such an old game only run on 70 fps on a modern mid-end machine? (RTX 3080, 5600x) I used to play the original game on a 7800 GT with an Athlon XP 3200+, just think about this for a moment. Im not even talking about the "Can it run Crysis?"-Meme Graphic-Mode, that has practically no noteworthy difference then just running the game in a slideshow.While not so important for me personally, as I dont think a lot of people would still play it today, its also missing the multiplayer part of the original game. Something that should be mentioned.It also doesnt come with the standalone addon Crysis Warhead, and there is also no Remaster-Version in general for Crysis Warhead. Something I think is needed, considering the price-tag for this remaster.So as long as you are not buying it for the integrated nanosuit-hotkey mode (Introduced in Crysis 2 and 3), or the achievements, you are better off with the original game. You can get the original game on origin for like 2 dollars, or on GOG for like 5 dollars. Also buy the original Crysis Warhead.Only ever buy this remaster when the whole Trilogy is heavily discounted and you already know you want to play the sequels.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game, horrible remaster.This is a game that I’ve played since 2007, I still have my physical copy of it on my shelf and I’ve played it many times with many hardware configurations, so without a shadow of a doubt, I kinda have a feeling when a scene is rendered correctly or not.I played this remaster from start to finish with Ray Tracing  and it sure does look absolutely beautiful, one of the best looking games of 2007 is still one of the best looking games in 2023, no question about it. But it only looks great in very specific circumstances, for example, in bright daylight the RT technology shines (no pun intended), but in the second half of the game which involves a lot of dark areas and a lot of snow, you’d be hard pressed to tell if RT is still being used if it wasn’t for the performance hit.The last level was particularly painful for how darn DARK it gets, there’s a certain lab scene that makes it unreasonably dark when there’s like 5 people in the same room, it sure as heck should be a lot brighter with that many people in it. Not only the dark scenes get comically dark, but I’ve also found plenty of gameplay bugs, especially in the second half, like rocks that sway back and forth like leaves, soldiers getting stuck in important doorways, dialogues that trigger a second time in a row after going back to where the trigger was, music cutting in and out… I understand this is an old game with very different tech than what is considered standard nowadays, but it sure as heck didn’t feel like it was falling apart like a house made out of sticks and glue with a shiny polish.And that’s without mentioning how bad they screwed with the controls, Saber Interactive, in their infinite wisdom, wanted the controls to feel closer to it’s sequels, but it only feels like a forced, dumbed down version of the original without the tight feel of the sequels, fortunately you can go back to the original controls, but ALSO they took away the quick save feature in place of a crappy checkpoint system without letting you pick from earlier saves if you somehow get screwed by said system.I’m in a sort of predicament with this review, I do not recommend this remaster because of how buggy it felt throughout my playthrough, but I also hesitate to recommend the original release instead because of how hard it is to make it run at reasonable framerates on modern computers. Don't buy the original on Steam, instead I’d recommend the GOG release of the original Crysis along with Warhead, you can get both for dirt cheap and they both already have most fixes applied, namely without DRM --which was a big issue with both games back in the day.Game is still worth playing, but stay away from this remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: Go as part of an elite squad to Lingshan Island to rescue a group of scientists from captivity.Take advantage of a special nanosuit that gives a person abilities that exceed those of an ordinary person! Jump several meters high, disappear - to get close to enemies from any direction, destroy buildings and objects around you, run like lightning! And all this in an updated graphics!With the release of Crysis in 2007, Crytek raised the bar on graphics to heights that many other titles could not. The game (for that time) could boast not only excellent graphics, but also destructible environments, good voice acting and immersiveness. The player immersed himself in the game and, together with the hero, thought out his way to the point of the task - through the Jungle filled with Koreans.In 2020, Crytek decided to play on the feelings of the players and just released the same game again. Only slightly improving the graphics in some places - adding a newfangled rtx. Which, instead of making an already great game even more colorful, did the opposite.With the advent of rtx in the world of Crysis, the surrounding space became bright, pale and lost most of the shadows. In addition, Crytek has significantly degraded most of the textures. Because of what it is already impossible to look at the faces of the heroes without a shudder.I sincerely believe that Crytek wanted to make the game better - but simply loading the game with new technologies is not the same as improving it. Due to the changes, the game has become hundreds of times easier, losing the former challenge that the original threw.I do not recommend this game. Especially if you have not played the original, then I advise you to buy it easier than this remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: This game may have been great for its time, but it doesn't seem to hold up too well in the modern day.Personally, I would recommend starting with Crysis 2 if you are interested in the series and if you want to know about the story, either look up a playthrough or spend an hour on the wiki reading up on the story.My reasons for this conclusion: -  (it took me a bit under 8 hours to beat) - . There were quite a few times where I was looking at a situation and asking myself, "Why, why would you do that?!" or "How did I get here again?" -  The game ends rather suddenly and at a weird time with no true resolution to the plot. To further add to the confusion, when moving onto the next game, it is as if the characters of this game (Nomad, The doctor, Psycho) never existed -  At the start of each boss fight, I found myself thinking, "Is this a boss fight? Why are we fighting? What just happened to 'x'?". And the fights themselves were of the type where you didn't know what was actually going on and after shooting at the boss a bunch you start wondering if there is a weak-spot or something that you need to hit to deal damage. A good example is the answer to the 2nd boss is to shoot it with ~4500 minigun rounds. (Because after shooting the boss with the first 1000 rounds and seeing nothing happen you are likely to consider shooting at it more with the same weapon). After every boss fight I just found myself thinking,  -  This game if full of elements that directly contradict each other's purpose. A good example of this would be the stealth feature in the game, you are incentivised to use stealth in the game, problem being that enemies can frequently spot you at points where you still can barely make out the enemy with a 4x scope. Enemies spotting you is also instant or close to it. Additionally, if you fire when cloaked, your energy is instantly set to 0 (even with a suppressor) meaning you can only fire out of cloak (this does get addressed in later games) this also applies to all weapons, so a shotgun is just as valid as a pistol in terms of energy conservation. Human enemies also only die in 1 hit to headshots and can take 3+ hits to die to body shots. So, if you shoot and miss the head, you have alerted the entire enemy force to your presence. You also have your energy instantly get set to 0 if you get shot so using cloak so using it in a dangerous situation is likely to just leave you without energy and still in danger. All these factors made it so that it was far easier, less time consuming and less risky to just sprint past all the enemies you see -  Despite wearing the most advanced suit of armor in the world, you still go down to a second of sustained fire from any weapon. Even if you use armor mode, it will only block maybe 4 bullets and leave you with no energy and no health -  There wasn't a second I fought the Ceph that I enjoyed. They are tanky, there is a lot of them, they are fast, and they can fly. I would find myself constantly looking into the sky wondering where I was being attacked from while being shot at from 3 different directions all while every enemy takes 2-3 shots from even the strongest weapons in the game. The only saving grace was that they dealt rather low damage. (again they are much more pleasant to fight in the later games)In all, this game's primary effect on me was making me appreciate the other games more for their improvements to the formula

_childDocuments_.review: Great example of an earlier FPS with open ended gameplay. The map design allows for you to truly tackle situations in a multitude of ways, including avoiding enemies entirely. While I appreciate how unrestricted this is, it's difficult for me not to take the stealth approach and avoid everyone, never firing for long sections. Constant stealth feels like the wrong way to play. The real enjoyment comes from playing with the AI and some of the physics. This is also a perfect setup for the story of Prophet and the rest of Raptor Team.While I would recommend this to any fans of shooters, I should warn that we employ a stableboy named Caleb who struggled with this game. We hired him because he's slow and can't really work anywhere else. He thinks our cows are called dogs and also thinks our goats are called dogs. Actually, he believes most things are dogs. I saw him looking at the table salt at lunch one day and he asked, "Can you pass the dog?" Anyway, I recommended this game to him and he couldn't work for a week because he was convinced there were aliens in his clothes.
_childDocuments_.name: Crysis Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: If you have Crysis already; don't bother buying this, it's just the same game with a new lick of paint; it's a good game, and achievements alone made the purchase worth it to me; but for most people I don't think that's a justifiable purchase whatsoever so I would recommend against it if you already own Crysis.Crysis 1 is a great Sandbox Shooter and it's just like Far Cry 1 but where you are a Superhuman vs an Army. I really love the Delta difficulty's balance; always kinda being difficult and never really trivializing the difficulty; that and it's such a nice, cool thing to hear the enemy speak in their native language rather than in English. Very jarring and Delta really is so cool for that.  Anything easier than Delta and the game becomes a bit of a cakewalk as you are very superhuman.I do think the game takes a HUGE nosedip in enjoyment once the Ceph show up cause it's just not fun to fight those aliens; I had a lot more fun fighting against the KPA, the AI there was brilliant and so enjoyable to play against, as they take cover and will stick together rather than just bumrush you and expect to win somehow. Great game, fairly fairly short, I never knew that about Crysis how short it was cause I only ever played the first level always. But for the 15 euro sale price that owners of the originals got, I can definitely say I'm happy with my purchase and I'm happy to have experienced the game in this manner compared to the original (even though the original still holds up perfectly; just crashes sometimes at boot which can be a pain)
_childDocuments_.name: Crysis Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis remastered is one of the best shooters out there. A badass game about a couple of veritable 100 % Giga-Chads: United States Army Delta Force Operators(Nomad, Prophet, Psycho) equipped with highly advanced cool nanosuits who are sent to uncover the mystery behind the discovery of an ancient built structure that has been found buried inside a mountain in the fictional Lingshan Islands, which turns to be of alien origin. You(Nomad) and your team end up fighting North Koreans and aliens: the Ceph in an attempt to try to stop an alien invasion.This game will increase your testosterone unlike the woke puke we are presently fed on a monthly basis. I never got sick of hearing"Cloaked engaged", "Maximum armor" "Maximum speed". Words said in the most manly way possible. The game offers some nice gameplay elements in an open-world map. You have the stealth approach where one can use the nanosuit powers(cloak) and silencers to silently infiltrate an enemy base/get past a jungle patrol and fulfill the objective. If you do not like the silent, more passive approach you can opt for the obvious head on approach where you attack directly an enemy base/jungle patrol killing anyone in sight-using your suit armor power for protection.There are some additional elements to the combat gameplay that makes things more fun if you find your self in a pickle-low on ammo. Firstly you can use environmental objects to throw at the enemies to incapacitate them/kill them. Secondly you can grab the enemies by neck and throw them like nothing using your powerful grip. The game has also some additional vehicular/aircraft gameplay which is a nice break from the normal shooting mechanics. Makes the experience more whole with this added variety. The weapons variety and customization is nice. It allow players to find their own style and quickly adapt to new challenges by being able to modify them in real time. Turn a weapon to a silent one by putting a silencer or reverse it back. Put a sight scope for close range fights or a sniper scope for a long distance target and vice versa changing it as your needs change. Put a flashlight or a laser sight or maybe a grenade launcher for increase damage. You have the SCAR the primary assault rifle, XM2014 the a military-grade combat shotgun, FY71 Assault Rifle capable of both fully-automatic and semi-automatic fire, the dual wielding Pistols, the powerful Hurricane Minigun, The Molecular Accelerator-Ceph weapon, The sniper-DSG-1, the LAW-disposable compact missile launcher and the TAC Gun which is a prototype hand-held nuclear weapon. You also have your fists, grenades, C4 and the weapons from the tanks, patrol boats, military jeeps.  The game physics is one of the best putting to shame most games from today. Most parts of the environment can be subject to manipulation. There is a nice destruction system where you can have fun with the environment: mow down trees with your Minigun, collapse a building on top of enemies, blow entire bases to smithereens. The game story is good enough for a shooter and the characters are memorable and likeable enough. Mostly Nomad, Prophet and Psycho. Prophet voice is one of the coolest voice I have heard in all my years of gaming. It is so memorable and will stick in your memory. The graphics is another aspect where the game excels. The remaster comes with real-time voxel traced global illumination, extremely high resolution textures. The lush jungle, the water, the bases and the weapons looked very good on my 50" TV on 4k Very High on my RTX 4080. Made some nice screenshots.  The combat and AI is pretty challenging and fun especially on higher difficulty but even on normal difficulty. The enemies are pretty relentless and will spot you from a distance, hear you if you run-make noise and get alerted, they will even call for reinforcements. You will need to use your suit powers, quick reflexes, a bit of strategic planning(use things from environment: destruction, distractions) to defeat them.Overall Crysis remastered is a very good game with open world design, good graphics, nice weapon variety and customization, memorable characters, one of the best game physics, good fighting mechanics. The games deserves every dollar it asks for.I would rate the game a 8.5 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't know how it compares to the original Crysis, but here's my thoughts.Positives:Looks absolutely astonishing, especially in the hyper-atmospheric and detailed alien structure levels.Fairly small download size for such a good-looking game, and system requirements aren't too bad either. Turns out it can run Crysis!Decision to stick to a relatively manageable and linear progression path in such a large play area, rather than go full-on open world, is to be applauded, so not much unnecessary busywork or meandering.Gameplay is mixed up with armour and cloak abilities engineered into your nano-suit, letting you go stealthier if you want to, or help you out in seemingly impossible situations.Negatives:It's short. The end credits (which are interminable) feel longer than the game. For completionists, there's no excuse for that. I wasn't able to use the mouse to steer the vehicles, like I could with the Halo games. You may have to make do with arrow keys or get a controller.Foliage, no matter how dense, does not seem to hide you from enemies well enough, and yet it's difficult to see them.Feels slightly bland and generic at first, like a typical AAA shooter (but persevere with it and you should have fun). The unimaginative story doesn't help.Overall, it's fine, not life-changing but entertaining enough while it lasts. I wonder how good the rest of the games in the series are.

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from the novelty of the ultra amazing graphics for its time, the game leaves a lot to be desired. The biggest flaw i see in this game is the open world level design. There's certain missions like one convoy escort mission where a dead alien enemy's body fell straight onto my tank, making it explode and insta kill me. _childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to say about CrysisAfter playing the game three times and starting a new one againI can defienetely tell, this game does love its open approach to mission accomplishmentsAnd while the gameplay sometimes feels weak (you cant climb or jump in long range for example also some missions can be unforgiving on hardest difficulty), the neat part about it tho - you can complete the game however you like, using any weapons or any approach you can musterPreviously, I hated this remaster for butchered visuals and broken performanceBut, they actually fixed the performance issuesAnd while I certainly miss some old schoold effects, you gotta give credit for new texturesThe plot is still hillarious and soldierly AFThe replay value certainly existsMusic is...epic but not a masterpieceAnd the level design - it may be not perfect but it still kinda works.So, forgive me for previous negative review, I take all my words back, Crysis is great and Remaster was pretty well doneIn the end at least.Warhead Remaster anyone?

_childDocuments_.review: It was fun to relive 2007 again and the remaster basically feels like the original game, but not running like ♥♥♥♥ this time around. Some nitpicks though:- If I alt-tabbed out of the game, I got a mouse cursor on screen outside of the menu that I couldn't get rid of without restarting the entire game (even alt-tabbing again, or switching from fullscreen > windowed > fullscreen doesn't fix it)- Despite there being simple and advanced mouse settings, you can't just have one mouse sens for every situation for some reason. When I set the default sens, looking around unarmed at the start of the game was different to holding a weapon, which was different to aiming down sights, which was different to being in a vehicle...... I ended up (partially successfully) having to use console commands to try and make them similar. Also I had to set my mouse DPI stupidly low to even make the game playable in the first place. There's no good reason for it to be this complicated!- No manual saves any more- The remaster is missed opportunity to make a little more of the environment destructible (almost everything is breakable apart from these little metal fences around the compounds you fight through, which is a bit jarring)These weren't too annoying once I got around them, and I got the game cheap though, so I would still recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: A classic reborn with some tweaksPeople often think of Crysis as a shallow tech demo game versus an actual fully formed open world romp. You are on an island, you get objectives, now go explore and find ways to complete those objectives. Its a semi-linear branching path where you can do all sorts of mayhem in the destructible game world. Its a simple plot, nothing too deep here, but enjoyable all the same.Its a short romp, only about 6-7 hours, probably about 15 if you wanna replay on the Delta difficulty and go for all the achievements. But it doesnt really overstay its welcome. The remaster of the game has some simplified control options (and the ability to go back to classic) but it can feel a bit clunky at times, especially picking up ammo and weapons can feel very..well.. frustrating at times, not helped by them sometimes clipping through terrain. The big highlight on the remaster is the RT reflections, which are really cool and add a lot to the game, in fact the RT and SVOGI implementation makes the game look absolutely stunning if you have the hardware to run it, but it is an older game and there are limits to it compared to more modern titlesWould I recommend it? Yes I think I would to anyone just getting into PC gaming, Its a classic and a game that crushed PC hardware 15 years ago and with RT, manages to strain it today. Just remember its a 15 year old game and it has its quirks.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game and the remaster is... fine. It's absolutely unnecessary if you already own it, but the controller support is nice. It runs worse and doesn't look that much better for it. There's also quite a few glitches, especially on the flying VTOL level that required multiple restarts just to scrape through the level without the ship spinning wildly through the scenery but not actually crashing on almost every attempt.The biggest problem isn't with the remaster but with the game itself. It's a lot of fun, right up until about the final third of the game. It's been said before, but it's absolutely true. Once the aliens arrive, the fun just drops out of the game. Fighting human enemies in the nanosuit is amazing, but these enemies from the zero gravity level onwards are tedious and annoying and that continues for the rest of the game. Just endless fire from above from floating enemies, but they also often hove directly above you and the game doesn't actually let you aim directly up for some stupid reason, so there are levels where they will occasionally shoot you from a position you cannot fire back from. It doesn't seem intentional, but it happened enough to make it annoying.So get the game, play it up until the aliens, and then honestly just quit right there. It's actively anti-fun from that point onwards and it doesn't get better.

_childDocuments_.review: "Yeah, but can it run Crysis?"Never thought I'd hear that once again in my life. Quite the trip down the memory lane, down to the stutters and laggy stuff right out of the gate. I seriously can't complain about the lack of optimization, because it's just part of the Crysis experience.Only buy if you have some spare money that you don't know what to spend on, else, you're better off with the original and some graphical mods, RT is pretty useless and unnoticeable in this game (although you'll feel your FPS tanking because of it), and I'd guess the only true advantage this has over the original, is it's capability of running on Windows 10/11 without any external executables and such, or if you care about achievements, since the remasters have those.Still, again, nice trip down the memory lane, even that sad feeling of thinking "hey, I can run this game pretty well!" while at that starting nightly beach, just to realize you are at 40 FPS once you get to the first open area.

It is a realistic military shooter that would be extremely difficult without the armour and invisibility powers. It uses the checkpoint system, and there are enough to make it playable, and not tedious if you bite the bullet.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.0/10All these years later I finally decided to bite on Crysis. I probably didn't have a PC worthy of playing it back in the day, but I sure do now! I was able to grab the remaster for $10 cdn and let me tell you I am glad that I did.I don't read other people's reviews and I don't buy into the hype of new movies and games (like last night I started watching the new "prey" movie and it was garbage...sorry fan boys I turned it off after 30 minutes. The original Predator was miles better...) And to that end, this game has that old school vibe to it - something you had to be around to savour in the old days of gaming (I'm 46 and have played thousands and thousands of hours of PC and console games - so I know!!)This game has a campaign story that I am enjoying, and some gimmicks that are fresh (to me) like the Nano suit. The enemies are fast and capable of honing into you so even on normal it's not a cake walk. Use your head though (like an old school gamer) and this a damn fun game!It's good enough, that I just instantly bought the remasters of part II and III which dropped on Steam today.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to be honest, my heart has always leaned more towards "Crysis 2." Maybe it's the nostalgia of that urban battleground or the more polished feel. But that doesn't mean the original "Crysis" doesn't pack a punch.Set in a lush, tropical paradise, the game is a beautiful mix of stealth and chaos. The suit's capabilities, switching between armor, speed, and stealth, are a game-changer (quite literally). Each encounter feels like a sandbox where strategies can be mixed and matched. And then there's that iconic tagline: "But can it run Crysis?" This game was, and still is, the benchmark for graphical prowess.The remastered version? It does justice to the original, amplifying what was already a graphical marvel. The sun filtering through the dense foliage, the ripples in the water, the detailed textures — it's all enhanced and feels more alive.For all its worth, while "Crysis 2" might have stolen my heart, the original "Crysis" laid the foundation. It set the stage for what was to come, introducing us to the Nanosuit, the alien threat, and a world where strategy and raw firepower go hand in hand.So, if you're curious about the Crysis universe and wondering where to start, "Crysis Remastered" is the gateway. It's the genesis of the series, and it provides context to the sequels. While it might not be my top pick of the franchise, it's undeniably essential. Strap on that Nanosuit and dive in; the jungle awaits.
_childDocuments_.name: Crysis Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: Even in Dec 2022 and almost 2033, this games have the potential to give you chills in several instances. Every bit of worth playing in 2023. The graphics are alright. _childDocuments_.name: Crysis Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Crysis 1 Remastered is a 8/10Game is great, Crysis has always had some of the most interactive game play out of anything I've ever played. Cloaking System is fun, Max Armor makes Survivability on many missions much easier.The game has some minor issues regarding graphics, only problem I ran into was the Laser pointer glitching and making a massive red glare on my screen pointing in different directions.I never had the pleasure of playing the original, but I'd have to say, the original will probably always hold up better than the remaster, nostalgia will always make it seem better than it actually was. One thing some people fail to realize is that most companies when they remaster games only "improve" upon the graphics, they don't offer any extra content for players to experience, only enhancing it by making it more immersive with a more realistic feel, they tried to keep the game in a retro style by adding RayTracking and "Can it Run Crysis" but keeping the old models with slightly better graphics, giving it a Halo Master Chief Collection feel (Halo CE updated graphics mode). Overall I'd have to say that if you want to experience this game, you should play the original, unfortunately they removed the ability to purchase the original from the steam store quite some time ago. Missions were fun and weren't too difficult playing on Normal Mode, I was able to beat it within 12 hours (3 of the 15.7 hours played was me falling asleep on the couch lol). Once you reach the core of the Mountain tho things start to fall apart, games becomes much more over tuned and the feel starts to diminish, game was much more fun when fighting the Koreans and not the Aliens. Beating the game doesn't feel very rewarding as the final mission is buggy and you tend to get frozen very often when fighting the final boss, the mechanics are over tuned as if its a newly released World of Warcraft raid that no one is able to get past 90% health. My Tip to beating the final boss with little to no frustration is by hiding next to the Forklift on the right side of the Carrier ship and cloaking right before the Mother Ship tries to 1 shot you, it prevents the cruisers from attacking you and allows you to pop out of cloak for a split second to nuke the wings and then the core, you have to sit IDLE for a good 3 mins before the fight will end, otherwise it'll freeze you over and over again killing you because you can't play. (Getting Frozen also prevents you from using Max Armor, meaning you just get chain frozen and die due to the beam and cruisers)Final Words would have to be: If you want to play it, do it, but i recommend buying it with the Trilogy so you can get access to the other 2 games, its not worth buying it on its own, especially with the sales (I purchases it during the 2022 Winter Sale)Good Luck, Have fun, and f*** the final mission.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played Crysis before, I think I would still recommend starting with the original version, but if you're a longtime fan this remaster offers an interesting new lens to play the game through and it never hurts to play Crysis again. I would probably give the game a sideways thumb if I could, since there are aspects both better and worse than the original, but considering owners of the original can get a pretty good discount it's worthwhile if you can get it cheap.There are definitely some visual aspects that look a bit nicer. It's not revelatory but the new reflection effects to make certain things pop a bit better and I've always been of the opinion some of the original game's textures looked a bit over-sharpened, which the new volumetric fog smooths over nicely. The raytracing is pretty tasteful and in-line with the original art direction without being overdone, and there's some cool uses of it, such as being able to see your own reflection when you pick up a CRT Television. Character models seem largely the same but again, the facial textures don't seem as overdone on the sharpness filter and faces are a bit nicer to look at in general. For some reason the original Crysis didn't have anti-aliasing which struck me as odd even at the time given the game's intent of having every graphical technology under the sun. The blues and greens of the island seem to pop more as well, which is very pretty to look at and the water in particular looks great.What is disappointing is that the Godrays seem toned down compared to the original. The scene in the first part where you finally step out onto the beach at sunrise was not only an iconic moment of the game, but a historic moment in game history itself that said "This is what games are gonna look like in 5 years" and the lighting just felt toned down here compared to the original which made that bit lose some of its edge. So while I do like a lot of what the remaster does, it's not a complete upgrade. Performance seems fine, but admittedly I'm running the game on the deliberately absurd "Can it Run Crysis?" mode, which on my 3090 tends to hover around 50fps which is pretty playable. I'm sure if I dialed it down to something more normal I would get a great framerate but my Tim Allen-like desire for MORE POWER UGH UGH UGH prevents me from setting my games to anything less than the maximum, and frankly if the newest edition of Crysis runs smoothly on Max it means that either it's time for a new Crysis or that society has come too far.The default control scheme in this remastered edition is also . Thankfully you can more or less set everything to how it was in the original but the default setting makes the game way more awkward to play. They tried to streamline the suit controls by basically having the powers activate when you do an action that can use that particular power. So for example, if you hold the jump or throw buttons you can do a "strength jump" or "strength throw". It works fine for the suit and cloaking (which is just the e key), but every time you sprint the suit goes into speedmode which wastes precious suit energy and it doesn't seem to let you just do a normal sprint. The streamlined controls worked in  and 3 because the whole game design was pared down for a more consolized experience, but trying to put a consolized control scheme in what is otherwise an unchanged full-fledged tactical PC shooter is just a mess of a default to ship the game with.The placement of the hotkeys also means that the lean keys are mapped to T and H by default which is wildly inconvenient and I personally feel that making the deliberate choice of suit mode before jumping into combat was a deliberate part of the tactical considerations the original game wanted you to make rather than being able to just have everything at the press of a button. Again, you can set things back to how they originally were, and I get the feeling the streamlined setup was meant for the console ports then somehow got backported onto PC, but the default binds make the game significantly more clunky for no reason and deeply uncomfortable to try and use in combat. There's a weird weapon select menu if you press the 6 key which is absolutely  but thankfully the original weapon switch keys are normal by default as well. That said though, the quick tips never change based on what your key setting are, so you might have the game telling you to press a button you mapped to something else, which feels unpolished.Once you get over the jank of trying to remap the controls though,  is still as fun as ever. The game was derided by some at the time as a mere tech demo, but I find myself coming back to it again and again over the years even after the visuals begin to look dated in spots (and the original still mostly looks amazing). It's a true tactical sandbox, and while the game isn't "open world", each level is wide enough that you can approach from any direction and really get creative with how you want to handle a scenario. See a vehicle you like? Jump in and rampage through town. While there have been other sandbox shooters since, like the various  sequels (and keep in mind  was the follow-up to  1, before Ubisoft took that series in a different direction),  and the  series are the only big ones that really do it this well. Your suit is powerful, but it won't compensate for bad decisions and the level design is just great. I do agree with the general consensus that the last quarter of the game isn't as good as the first due to a shift in the enemies you fight, but it's still fun. The gameplay feels pretty much the same, one or two weapons seem to have a punchier sound effect, but it's still the same old  and you don't have to twist my arm to much to get me on a new playthrough.While  isn't perfect, it certainly isn't a  either. The visual refreshes are interesting enough to be worth going through again and I wouldn't be surprised if someone either mods the remaster to have the better aspects of the original, or ports stuff from the remaster into the original. It is a pretty glaring omission that they left out the  expansion which is fantastic in its own right, but it's nice to see  being done with the series.  If you've never played the original, I'd again recommenced the original, but if you're already a fan and looking for something new, it's not a bad way to kill a few days.

_childDocuments_.review: + No Denuvo DRM. + Support for Achievements.+ DLSS Support for Nvidia RTX Cards.+ Still plays like Crysis (2007) overall, despite the negatives I’m about to list from what I’ve experienced and read from other people.- No Cloud Saving Support. - No Multiplayer and Crysis Warhead is still treated like the red-headed stepchild of the Crysis Family.- It’s based off the PS3/XBOX 360 version which means the benefits of being able to quicksave are completely gone and now, the nanosuit powers have been nerfed both in effectiveness and how they control/feel.- Apart from SVOGI and Ray Tracing, the “remastered” graphics artistically look much worse and uglier overall than the original PC version. Said Ray Tracing isn't worth the hit to performance since it only focuses on reflections.- Optimisation on PC is still busted thanks to Cryengine still only using single threaded performance from the CPU. This results in constant stuttering even at the lowest settings while using v-sync. - Lingering bugs that aren’t fixed in the Epic Games version still persist in the Steam version.- Now uses EOS (Epic Online Services) despite strictly being a single player experience.- Casts doubt that the remastering efforts for Crysis 2 and 3 won’t be a disaster, since both of them will be still Epic Games Store exclusives for a year.  - All of these negative aspects, combined with no actual improvements equate to making the 20% discount at launch and an extra 30% for those who own the original PC version, still a complete rip-off for what you’re paying for vs what you get.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, but only as part of the Crysis Remastered Trilogy bundle. Note that it doesn't feature multiplayer, and there are no cloud saves at time of writing.The Remaster:- This is an interesting remaster since it's not built on the original engine of the PC version of Crysis, resulting in some gameplay differences, notably AI not behaving quite the same. It's not a big deal if you've never played the game before since the general gameplay features are still there, but if you've played the original on PC the experience is a bit different. There is also a revised set of Nanosuit controls, which I think is designed to function more like Crysis 2 and 3, but I never actually tested them and instead used the classic Nanosuit controls that behave like the original Crysis.- Performance wise things aren't too bad if you change a few settings to avoid CPU problems: if you put objects to high, vegetation and shadows to medium / high, you get a level of detail and draw distance that's similar or better than the original game for increased performance, and most other settings (apart from ray tracing) can be turned up to maximum without much impact. Another advantage of the remaster is that it works out of the box on Windows 10, whereas the original game requires user fixes to launch at all.- In terms of graphics, it's a bit of a mixed bag. The updated assets generally look quite nice, but compared to the original the colour tone is a bit over-saturated during the day, yet the dawn and dusk sequences have less atmosphere. There are ray traced reflections too which are nice to have if you've got the hardware, though the number of reflective surfaces is a bit limited in many areas.- Unfortunately there are a few annoying problems with the remaster. I had to use console commands to set additional min and max sensitivity values, as the menu slider didn't give me a low enough value, but then the tank had a ridiculously low sensitivity so I had to change them during gameplay too. There are also some audio problems, such as shooting an enemy from long distance and his shouts from being hit are like he's right in front of your face, and there are other similar imbalances which don't help with positional audio and dialogue during gameplay either.Conclusion:- Overall it's not a terrible remaster, but I feel like the lack of polish and some of the visual changes hamper it a bit, and given how iconic the original was for PC gaming at the time, I recommend playing the original first if you can just for the classic experience. That said, the remaster is worth a play if you get it as part of the Crysis Remastered Trilogy bundle, and if you've never played the original the remaster will still give you the general gameplay feel so you're not missing out, without any fixes required to get it running either.The Game:- The first half of the game features sandbox levels where you fight the Korean army using your Nanosuit features for temporary increases in speed, strength, or a cloak for near invisibility. You can interact with just about anything; picking up objects and throwing them, shooting down small trees, destroying buildings, and driving around in vehicles. You can acquire shotguns, assault rifles, a sniper rifle and more, picking up attachments along the way such as lasers, scopes and grenade launchers. This gives a good variety of options for traversing the tropical island and completing objectives - you can go in guns blazing or sneak around with the cloak etc.- The second half of the game is where most people's complaints come from. It becomes increasingly linear, and you start fighting aliens instead with a reduced amount of combat options. I personally don't mind it that much, but the first half of the game is definitely where things shines and why (in combination with the visuals) it was so iconic back in the day.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I did my very first and only (as of this review) playthrough (~6-7 hours) on Delta difficulty, the hardest one to choose from.You're a soldier, part of a squad enhanced with nanosuits, set out to find what the Koreans are up to on this rather bleak island.This game is a lot of fun. It's a staple of its time: the era of single-player action-story games. It's linear in terms of objectives—as was the standard in its era—but it's for good reason. It features "secondary objectives," but really they feel more like additional objectives. They're along the way to the main objective and are really hard to miss.There's this one section that stands out to me, it's where you get to pilot and fight with a tank. The vista is amazing and grand. It captures the pure contrast between a paradise-like island and opposing forces fighting against each other.Stealth is also done in an engaging manner. Not only do you have to manage your suit energy and de-cloak a opportune times, but also doing any kind of offensive action (like shooting) while cloaked drains all your suit energy. This means to pull off stealth kills, you have to de-cloak -> shoot -> cloak in rapid succession.The hardest difficulty, delta, forces disabled crosshair, does something with binoculars (I do not know what exactly as I have not tested/looking into it), and makes enemies speak Korean instead of English. Why these options are limited to difficulty is an odd choice. I noticed that no crosshairs makes gameplay a lot more immersive. Would be interesting to see more games of the modern era come out with options to limit visibility of HUD elements (like Dark Souls/Elden Ring hiding the UI when out of combat) to improve the immersion.The difficulty scaling is a nice balance, at the highest difficulty it's hard enough that you cannot go-in guns blazing with no effort, but also not frustratingly unbalanced. It might be a little on the easier side, but I'd say it's practically balanced by having both you and the enemy be glass cannons, you both can deal a lot of damage, but also receive that same amount of damage. You can also pick up enemies (which, note, kills them instantly once you throw them), which is a load of fun and has a nice risk/reward to it when out of stealth engagements. There is a specific enemy in the later game that can be a little more tough, and being able to pick them up screams "nanosuit soldier" and it's really cool.AI can be a little dumb and unfair at times (note: AI have some very good eyes, i.e. being in their line of sight is enough to get instantly spotted, despite there being a reasonable amount of foliage in front of you), but they are rather unique. AI will attempt to shoot in the general location you were upon cloaking, which is a nice feature. Tanks can also instantly spot you if you get too close even while cloaked, which doesn't make much sense, but it doesn't matter much because it's practically a non-issue with how the game plays outSomething really nice about this game is dynamic crouch/sprint context. You can tap crouch/sprint to make it act like tap crouch/sprint; you can also hold crouch/sprint to make it act like hold crouch/sprint, where you will stop crouching/sprinting after releasing the key. This is a very nice feature that would be really cool to see in modern games.Although my system is rather weak (1650 mobile) and the game ran a "smooth" 20-30 FPS on all low settings like a Captain Underpants fight sequence, it still looked amazing. This game is  graphically intensive, making my GPU work absolute overtime and a half at a constant 100% usage. It does not, however, make much use of the CPU, as only about 20-40% was reported to be used by the entire system throughout while playing.Crysis is essentially an interactive action movie. You can tell the passion poured into the game, it's definitely worth the price. If you're looking for a fun experience, you'll get one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is really a toss-up between yes and no. Since there is no Neutral option, I am voting no.Crysis in general is a very good series. However, this game when compared to its original, is just a downgrade overall, and here's why: It feels a little lazy? The streamlined suit just doesn't work well, and while the classic suit option is still there, it feels weirdly clunky. Foliage animations are at 30fps, so if you're at 60+ then this will be very noticeable. Enemies also don't make foliage move, and in the early game that's actually quite invaluable since it's one of the few ways you can see them when they're using their environment. I did have one major issue with the LAST Crysis game. I couldn't beat it. Technical issues forced me to quit the game right at the end as the boss fight just wouldn't stop crashing, I tried everything I could to alleviate it with no issue. That being said, this one was actually beatable! So that's nice. All in all Crysis is a great game, and a very fun game. But I can't help to think that maybe the devs did a way too little with this, and it led to an overall weaker product overall. I enjoyed the achievements, I even got them all...well the rarest achievement (throw 10 items to kill enemies) was literally given to me during the final act due to just....holding a box while enemies died. But overall the Delta difficulty does offer some good challenge. Crysis is a part of gaming history, but since this remaster was released in modern day, it does not stand to any other AAA title released around when this was. While I would recommend it, I'm leaving the review as negative since the overall game feels broken. Pick this up on a steep sale, $5-$15 anything more is really pushing it. I picked it up during the Summer Sale in a bundle, and for that it was worth it. But on its own? eh. There are some amazing indie games out there that play better by today's standards.

_childDocuments_.review: I still remember the first time I played Crysis Remastered, and it was like stepping back into a game that defined a generation. The moment I entered the lush, tropical island filled with breathtaking visuals, I was immediately struck by how stunning the graphics were. Every detail—from the leaves swaying in the wind to the sunlight shimmering on the water—made the world feel incredibly immersive.The gameplay is just as exhilarating as I remember. The freedom to approach each mission in multiple ways is what makes Crysis stand out. Whether I wanted to go in guns blazing or take a stealthy approach, the nanosuit gave me a thrilling range of abilities. I felt like a super-soldier, seamlessly blending speed, strength, and cloaking to outsmart my enemies.The storyline, with its mix of sci-fi elements and military action, pulls you in and keeps you engaged. I loved the way the game escalates, introducing new challenges and enemies that kept me on my toes. Each encounter felt intense, especially when the AI would adapt to my tactics, forcing me to think on my feet.The remaster also did an excellent job of updating the graphics without losing the essence of the original. The enhanced textures and improved lighting really brought the game into the modern era, making it look and feel fresh. I found myself stopping just to admire the scenery—something I never thought I’d do in a first-person shooter!However, I did encounter a few bugs along the way, which is expected with remasters. Some glitches occasionally disrupted the flow of gameplay, but they didn’t take away from the overall experience.In summary, Crysis Remastered is a fantastic trip down memory lane that still delivers an exhilarating experience. The stunning visuals, versatile gameplay, and engaging story make it a must-play for both newcomers and fans of the original. It’s a reminder of how groundbreaking Crysis was, and it still holds up remarkably well in today’s gaming landscape.
_childDocuments_.name: Crysis Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis is a fun, pretty game that ultimately doesn't deliver on the initial promise of its first levels. It's still worth playing, even if it's just to experience the entertaining nanosuit abilities and marvel at what was, and is, a very good-looking game.The first few levels are these big open environments that give you freedom in how you approach their objectives. But this is only true in the most literal sense; you can approach the objectives from any direction, because you aren't boxed into a linear path. But that's where that freedom ends; there aren't any options in terms of how you actually complete the tasks set for you, or any "immersive sim" style gameplay choices.After these early levels, the game becomes much more of a linear shooter. It's still entertaining, but it's probably not what you came for, or expected.Playing on the hardest mode, the game is mostly weirdly easy, with very generous health and shield recovery and plenty of ammo available. The nanosuit's ability to make you super strong, invisible, or really fast mean you can easily out manoeuvre enemies and any challenge really just comes from making sure you get the first shot on any enemy you encounter.The biggest disappointment I have with Crysis is that most of the weapons are boring to shoot. There's this great system where you can modify weapon attachments on the fly, but you never really get a truly exciting weapon, with the possible exception of the missile launcher (when is a missile launcher ever not fun?)This remaster is mostly fine, though there are some pretty severe audio balancing issues, and moments where sound effects or music aren't audible when they should be. Vehicles that are hundreds of metres away sound like they're right on top of you, weird stuff like that. This version of the game also uses a checkpoint system with no manual saving, which is a really poor substitute.It's a recommend with several caveats, but I did have a good time for the most part. Something about the suit announcing "Cloak. Engaged." triggers a dopamine release for me, so that alone was worth the price of admission!

_childDocuments_.review: While crysis is a good game this just isn't worth it. Visuals:  It looks better than the original but the performance you get doesn't match the quality of the visuals.   It is also very inconsistent, some things look great while others look like they reused original textures.   It creates this unbalance that looks worse than either would on their own.   Like the way things are destroyed looks really really bad and cheesy.     On top of that even with a top of the line graphics card there is a good amount of studdering.  Gameplay:The gunplay itself is excellent and the guns are fun to use.    The enemies in general are fairly tough although that is one of my major complaints is when the enemies literally take more shots to kill than they can kill you in when your the one wearing the high tech nanosuit.  Balance is all over the place for the most part, some things were stupidly easy and others ended up overly difficult.    There isn't a good difficulty curve to the game it just randomly spikes and dips.  You get sections that are a joke followed by an overly difficult part and then another overly easy section.      Balance is utterly broken at times and some things are just flat out bugged.   For example, on the final fight it is possible to get chain frozen until you die which is just annoying and makes the fight a chore instead of being fun.       Enemies seem to sometimes just know your location and will just look straight at you if you get too close even with stealth and crouched and the lack of a takedown makes actual stealth gameplay suck since you can't really misdirect enemies or take down enemies without alerting everyone around.  The strength options are completely useless in the game and honestly even the defensive shield gets chewed through so quickly by the more dangerous enemies that it is borderline useless.   On the other hand you can completely cheese the stealth mechanic and enemy AI with a bit of range by shooting from stealth hiding behind a tree and stealthing again.     It made the gameplay balance just feel terrible and should have been something you would have expected to be fixed in the remaster.  Sound: the sound is pretty much the same as the original and not that good.  There is nothing to say here, it sounds like a 15 year old game.  It honestly didn't seem like they did anything with the remake in that department.    Pretty much if you never have played the original it is worth buying because the game is still fun and the price isn't bad for the 6-10 hours your going to get out of the game at 25 dollars.  Honestly though that is the most I would say it has in value.   It has very little replay value, no multiplayer and isn't very long.  Ideally I would recommend wait for a sale to be honest.   The game definately isn't worth the price if you already own the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying That Crysis is a very special game to me. No lie I've probably played this campaign about 25 times. Back in the day when I built my first computer with the phenom 9950 and a GTS 250 I was looking at benchmarks and I discovered this game. I got the demo and played it so many times. Then I got the game, and I loved every part of it: the human conflict, the aliens, the story, everything. Original Crysis wasn't the most optimized game out there and I saw a cry engine showcase with a part that looks just like the island from the first mission of the game then I heard a remaster was inbound, so I was expecting the quality from that showcase to be the entire game and boy was I wrong.I'll start at the beginning. Crytek sold their souls to the devil and released Crysis remastered on the piece of ♥♥♥♥ epic game store as an exclusive for an entire year. I know they are starving for money, but this still stings. Anyways about a year later I got the entire trilogy for 70% off and today, I finally got around to playing it.Some minor Spoilers I guess…..And man, this game has issues. From visual minor to severe visual glitches that never existed in the first game to mechanics changes such as in that boss fight against that one guy in the nanosuit when you hit him, he has an EMP blast that completely stuns you and you can't do anything when you're stunned, that was not in the original game nor a feature of the nanosuit. That part made me mad as hell lol. That was a big change instead of a 1 vs 1 duel to the death everything is slowed down massively because you can no longer attack him immediately you have to run around and hunt for a weapon and then attack him while the doctor keeps yelling stop him the whole time which she says a lot due to how drawn out this fight is now and he seems to be made of titanium because he's a super bullet sponge now even just in strength mode.Other changes include at the end when the big Ceph Walker thing grabs you can no longer face it to attack it to go free you're just kind of screwed if you get thrown too far and you die.Also, when you're on the vehicle turret even if you turn off hold mouse to aim down sights you still must hold mouse to aim down the side of the turret it's quite stupid.Regarding all these mechanical changes: a remaster is supposed to preserve everything, just improve visuals and optimizations and not reinvent the wheel by changing gameplay mechanics.One surprising thing is this game preserved the VTOL mission which honestly, I was not expecting because that was cut from the original game that this is based off which is the Crysis version released for the PS3 and Xbox 360 so in short, we're basically playing a port of a PS3 and Xbox 360 game with some extra additional things bolted on.This remaster was probably the most important remaster to me, and they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ it up which is well known at this point. The only thing honestly that was improved was the 8K textures they used for the game, but you can fix that by playing the original with just a HD texture pack and done. Also, I was able to play the game from start to finish without a single crash so that's also a positive because their original game if you play about three missions straight, you're going to crash it's weird. There are all kinds of other examples of visual downgrades but a few I can think of is 1) at the starting of the first mission prophets face in the first mission intro had a lot more detail in the original. in the “Remake/Remaster” all the detail his face is just flat and 2) per object motion blur being completely removed that's something else you can see at the intro to the first level. This reviews all over the place, but I had to write what I'm feeling right after I finished it. I'm going to uninstall this crap and stick with the original which is far better. They shoehorned in cry engine 3 or whatever version they're using into this game, and it shows. This port/half assed remaster is trash I'm very disappointed. This is also much harder to run, and I don't see much visually to warrant that. The difference between Ray tracing on and off is next to none.TLDR:  Sadly, I cannot recommend this at all. What I can recommend is that you go either on EA Origin or GOG and get the original Crysis and Crysis warhead they are both amazing open ended sandbox games.

_childDocuments_.review: I have sort of a longstanding relationship with Crysis, but this playthrough was my first seeing it through to the end, and I played on Hard. The first PC I ever built with my dad saw this game installed onto it in its first hours online. It rings true that this game is a benchmark title, but every attempt to make this benchmark test an actual video game fails so spectacularly that I find myself shocked we ever saw a sequel greenlit.2007 was an incredible year for video games and somehow this game sneaks into that pantheon for its memetic/cultural impact alone. "Can it run CRYSIS?" The thing is, you can go back to Halo 3, Bioshock, or COD4, and those experiences will still hold true to the standard of quality that they set. Playing Crysis in 2024 feels like a joke. It's tacky, clumsy, and probably the most damning of all, just not fun whatsoever.To speak on graphics, it's just okay today. The remastering effort is fairly uneven actually. Noticeably, the first half of the game saw the most attention, it's generally a lot prettier. What a strange position this game finds itself in, where so many people are buying it are doing so just to test out their systems. Less than 30% of steam users rolled credits. These buyers, who are just stopping by for the eyecandy, are probably having more fun doing that than I am seeing what the game actually has to offer. It's not much. Past the first hour or so, it becomes painfully clear that "fun" was more of a tertiary concern to Crytek.Every design decision this game makes feels geared towards making your time with it the least fun it can possibly be. Broken, hair-trigger AI kneecaps your potential to make interesting plays with cloak stealth, maximum speed takes you all of about 15 feet before knocking out your entire energy meter, maximum strength feels like it was put in the game to showcase EPIC PHYSICS KILLS!!! in the trailers, leaving maximum armor to be your slow, plodding, default ability. For an assortment of what are essentially superpowers, it's downright incredible how they all feel designed to make the game less enjoyable the more you interact with them.The story is nothing to write home about. There's one pretty blah boss battle and most of your squad dies so quickly as to rob them of any and all character development. That piece of garbage game Haze on PS3 had better characterization to its supersoldiers than Crysis does, but this is hardly Crysis' worst offense, as the narrative does well enough to stay out of the way. The game's main intention is to let you roam and chose your fights in a big dense jungle with very little to chew on past its map markers.Even the guns, while serviceable in feel, barely have their time in the sun. The weapon variety improves in the last 15% of the game, but so much of the experience leaves you hamstrung if you decide to run with any weapon you don't routinely find on the ground. If you choose to engage with the game's content, you'll find yourself without ammo incredibly quickly for any weapon but the pistol and AK. I will put this another way. I found so little to appreciate with this game. If Crysis 2 and 3 interest you as they do me, you are more than safe to skip it. I hope that the sequels prove me wrong, but this was a bad first taste of what this series has to offer. Don't waste your time.
