_childDocuments_.review: There's not much new that can be said about Crysis that hasn't already been said over the last 17 years since the original was released. The original blew my mind with its graphics and whilst this remaster cannot do the same thing, it definitely does refresh and update the visuals without changing the visual style of the original game too drastically. Performance wise this remaster is playable on a lot wider range of hardware than the original ever was and that's a good thing, as the game is still snappy and fun to play. Wide corridors give you quite a bit of flexibility in how you approach an objective, no excess secrets or hidden objectives to distract you and good voice acting mean that you are drawn into the game and can progress quite quickly through the game. This game is well worth owning if you love FPS games, even if gameplay standards have evolved in the time since. Also, if you push the graphics high enough, it's still great for making your PC sweat and for those reasons and more, it deserves a place in your library.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it, tried it and refunded it.It looks better  but plays worse. My recommendation is to simply play the originial instead. You get better gameplay for less money and on maxed settings it's still pretty solid visually.Starting with the positives: - The game now looks like how I remember it. Visually it's been brought to the 2020s and my nostalgia is happy about that.Sadly thats it. End of the positives. (comparing to the orignal of course, not making a review about Crysis as a game. Love this game)The negatives:- The mouse sensitivity is insane. Even on the absolute lowest setting its still twice as high as what I play normally, and I know a lot of FPS gamers who play significantly lower sense than me. I was struggling more with controling my character than I was with the actual enemies. - Which brings up the second point: the AI is terrible. Seemingly completely unchanged from the original, but in the mean time us gamers have all gotten used to for more responsive and interesting enemies.- Movement feels sluggish and unresponsive. Its like moving through syrup. I don't recall the original feeling like it was constanly holding me back. Even with speed mode enabled I don't feel like a fast and deadly super soldier, instead I feel I'm obese and cannot run properly.- Various performance issues. Poor optimisation on some features, frame drops and the likes. I didn't play long enough to really give detailed feedback here.- A big one. Audio. WHY, just why, do they put all this effort into visual improvements but apparently haven't put a single minute of effort into actual audio improvements. These are the same gunshot sounds, impact sounds and explosions from 15 years ago and many of them sounded unimersive and unrealistic even then. Even the most beautiful environment won't feel immersive if it sounds 20 years dated.- Not so important for me personally but still relevant: the multiplayer content was cut out entirely.

(check out current Intel CPU performance 'jumps' last years and don't even start on dimnishing returns, they can do better but why should they?)Fastforward to 2024 and Crysis Remastered is not that much better looking, AI is dumber than it was, game has more bugs and overall it is a worse product - like almost all games in the past 5 years, making good business hurts the industry.If you're in for a quick nostalgia trip and want to see how much power can your GPU draw under max load this game is for You, otherwise skip.PS This one can not run on 3x3.2Ghz CPU paired with 512 DDR3 RAM shared with GPU peaking at 0,24 TFLOP like Crysis 1,2 and 3 did back on Xbox 360, RTX 4090 is over 400x faster...

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis: Remastered is a sci-fi futuristic first-person shooter developed and published by Crytek and released on Steam in September 2021. I will note I finished Crysis: Remastered last weekend, before Patch 3 was released this week.If you find this review to be helpful, please leave a thumbs-up. I also have a review page here: I originally played and reviewed Crysis in 2016, on some PC that included a GTX 560 Ti. For those interested, the link to the original is here: For the time, I thought Crysis was an enjoyable experience but could not play it on Ultra without performance issues. Have a look at my (back in the day) rating system, below.These ratings were based on a couple of key things from my original play, including:The above is still fairly accurate, noting in the Remastered version that:That said, Crysis: Remastered is sold on updated visuals and technological features and is optimised to current hardware. Playing on a PC with a i5-6600k, GTX 1070, and 16GB ram, I found the Remastered was optimised extremely well and I did not experience any framerate or stability (e.g., crashes) issues. The overall graphical fidelity is a broad improvement on the original and the Lingshan Island is still a beautiful sight, credited to an updated lighting system. While the graphics are broadly improved, the Remastered did not update all assets and objects (i.e., bag in opening scene, some characters), and therefore, the textures on these are disappointingly low-resolution and blurry. I am also surprised to find a number of bugs throughout my experience, including, but not limited to, the aforementioned AI scripting, as well as constant sound drop-outs during missions and the AI boss fight not triggering in the final mission, requiring a level restart(!).I commend the legacy of Crysis I, and Crysis: Remastered is a nice trip down to memory lane, particularly in a nice campaign. But I am conflicted because the Remastered version was not overly a good experience. It adds a nice overall graphical upgrade and performance optimisation is fantastic (and I will note Patch 3 further optimises it), but it falls in several areas. First, it does not address issues from the original game such as AI scripting and if that is not fixable, I appreciate that. It is also unfortunate that the visual improvement does not impact all assets, resulting in a number of low-resolution characters and objects, and there are a high number of bugs and glitches throughout the game. On this basis, I do not recommend Crysis: Remastered.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis Remastered looks better and runs better than the original games in everyway, especially with the raytracing features turned on. However, due to being made from the PS3/Xbox360 console port instead of the original PC release, the Remastered version has a few shortcomings and missing features but it is not enough to hamper the gameplay experience. What does hamper the gameplay experience however was the plethora of new bugs and glitches found in this version that did not exist in the original 2007 release nor the console ports. Although these can be fixed the  mod by , it is disappointing that the game has stopped receiving official updates.What's more disappointing however is the lack of the multiplayer and full scale mod support that the original got, which offer players a tonnes of replayability and variety of user made content and modes both online and singleplayer. Resulting in an overall short experience that can be completed in under 10 hours without much replayability. I've 100% the game and got all achievements within 9 hours.Overall, Crysis Remastered looks impressive and play as well as the original, bar the new bugs and glitches. It's a game I can wholeheartedly recommend and well worth experiencing again even if you've played the original. But without the modding capability the original has, Crysis Remastered feels lacking when compared to the 2007 release.

_childDocuments_.review: BEST ON DECK: 6 - 7 hours battery, 60 FPS, No Setting Changes NeededA simple rescue mission goes haywire in the worst way possible in the remaster for the classic FPS game that defined the benchmark question: "Can it Run Crysis?". In Crysis Remastered, you are armed with your nanosuit and swap between super speed, strength, armor, and cloaking to tackle your enemies in a constantly changing environment. Using your suit and tools, you will need to tackle threats beyond this world and figure out just what the hell is going on.Crysis Remastered has gotten mixed ratings due to a couple reasons. These include bugs, some graphical downgrades from the original, and it being a port from the console releases. Unfortunately, this is the only way to play the original Crysis unless you owned the original before it was delisted from Steam. The good news is, it plays quite well!I started off at the medium settings and was pleasantly surprised how well it ran. For the most part, it could stick to 45 FPS without any caps, but the battery would drain a bit more than I would like during some high octane parts of gameplay like driving into an explosion, tons of enemies on screen shooting, and sprinting across the world. I decided for a recommended initial build to stick to 40 FPS with some settings lowered to "low" for stability purposes. I also lowered resolution to 1152x720 as this drastically helped during those intense moments.Crysis Remastered also supports simultaneous KB+M and Gamepad inputs at the same time, which means enabling gyro controls through Steam Input will work well! I have found setting the gyro behavior to mouse feels a bit better, but setting to joystick works too.For the full review, I will provide 2 other builds that will make improvements to battery and a higher framerate, but due to Crysis Remastered being a large game, I want to test more before making those recommendations. I didn't encounter any major bugs that were specifically due to the Steam Deck and overall I felt the game ran without a hitch. I did blow up many houses and tried to instigate a lot of physics movements, but it held strong. I have been pleasantly surprised so far how well it is running and feeling, especially coming from how hard it was to run the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I've said "Yes" to whether I would recommend it, this review should be taken as a criticism rather than praise towards the game. Let's start with some gameplay views: The nanosuit now functions a lot like the way it does in 2 and 3. Default is Strength mode and the suit regenerates energy only in this mode. Armor mode passively drains energy aside from taking hits. The good news is, this can all be reverted by heading to Options --> Game Settings --> check mark Classic Nanosuit. Suit shortcuts is also something you may want to look at, as enabling Classic Nanosuit mode makes you unable to use the toggle keys to quickly switch modes. A mixed bag, but my preference is using the Classic Nanosuit.As for the rest of the game. Quite a few graphics glitches are noticeable in many environments. A.I. behavior is not as refined as before and can end up behaving very strangely at times, or stuck in a spot especially if you reload a checkpoint near a patrol.One pain point for me is that the game does not play all the dialogues properly. Like the in the final part on the aircraft carrier and in the mines there are missing some dialogues. Technically they are there in the game but the game proceeds too quickly before they can play. Can be rectified somewhat with some xml edits but we shouldn't have had to.Biggest owie for me is during the final fight on the carrier deck against the mothership. Very often one of two things or both will occur: 1. Psycho and Helena don't disable the shields even if all hostiles have been cleared, and this can happen for either of the "arm" shields. 2. The boss will be stuck continuously using its freezing beam for several minutes non-stop leaving you on a constant loop of being frozen, unfrozen and refrozen even on the easiest difficulty. Eitherways you have no choice but to reload the checkpoint.So, if given a choice, I'd recommend you get the original Crysis from GOG which incorporates a fix for the executable.I will say this much for the game though: the looks have definitely been touched up and a lot of places and objects are certainly more detailed and more beautiful. VFX also improved. But yes, buggy.

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't hold a candle to the original on PC, most likely because the Remaster is actually a remaster of the X360 version, not the original PC code. Irrespective of that, it still performs poorly, even on an i9-9900k with a 3080ti. Story wise, it is still the same as before, so it hits quite a bit of the nostalgia, however gunplay and sound definitely do not "feel" like the original, and nor does the suit. It may just be my memory, but the first few chapters on the beach definitely also feel differently paced, which leads me to believe that there were some choices made to reduce some of the slow pacing of the original, but sadly not to any benefit (due to gunplay feeling different and the visuals not being as crisp as the original).All in all, it is a poor port. I will finish it, as I am already over my 2h and want to keep the trilogy, but definitely not enjoying this game. If you can get it cheap, bite the bullet, otherwise stay clear of it. It just isn't good, and it definitely is not a Remaster. It is a poor enhancement of an even poorer X360 port of the original PC version.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played Crysis Remastered via Crysis Maximum Edition that came out before most people started becoming more PC eccentric. With that in mind, I can honestly not really recommend Crysis Remastered unless you buy it super cheap, like 5$ cheap. It's a pretty poor remaster of a classic game that honestly wasn't good either, but it paved it's way to better games like Battlefield, Crysis 2, etc (many of which, took the trope of super power suits/ gunplay, etc). When you compare side by side, the remastered is still poor in many ways, from its weird lighting/ color engine, to its HDR implementation. HDR is insanely weird, where the color of the beach looks so off white it basically removes the texture at certain angle - think  ray tracing for the sands, but sands shouldn't have rt. Lighting is strange, because at certain angles, it looks phenomenal, specially if you are high above a cliff and looking at the beach, but other times, in the forest, you can't tell where you are because it focuses so much on making things look darker when it shouldn't be necessary do so. And why is it, everything on this island is so diluted in specific colors, that I understand looked good back in the day, but for now, it feels strange, like they didn't think maybe plants could be more than just a normal green color.I think the worst offender is the game design. Sadly, it's weird to me that Crysis 2/ 3 has utilized the nano suit so much better than Crysis 1 remaster (all things considering they could have balanced the game more since it is a remaster). You run out of energy exponentially quickly, or can't really play rambo-esque that the original trailers of Crysis encouraged. It's more of, you sneak in, shoot someone, and sneak out. Maybe getting another kill in between, but other than that, it doesn't really allow you to jump around throwing people or things that it kind of depicts (while Crysis 2 seemed to focus on that so much better). On top of that, the main issue is the open world, and it's so badly used. You really have no reason to explore, and even when you try to, the terrain/ box placement is so bad, it kind of feels like stumbling upont he geometry 24/7 to get to a destination. Guns also feel weak,or just downright inaccurate compared to modern shooters. I have so many complaints regarding the game design that I could write a thesis about it, and it still wouldn't be enough.All in all, I said originally that maybe it's worth 5$, I take that back, it's not. Time is a valuable thing, and wasting on this game (modeless mind you) is 100% not worth investing into.

_childDocuments_.review: All this game did was make me appreciate the original from 2007 more. For a remaster released in 2020+, this version is a little underwhelming. Textures, water effects, particle effects, depth of field -- sure, all of these things have improvements for the most part. But when you compare side by side, the improvements feel kind of minor, which only speaks to just how good the original already looked to begin with.To ensure I was getting the most out of this, I enabled the "Can It Run Crysis?" mode with the raytracing enabled, which cranks everything to the max. On my watercooled rig (5950x CPU + 3090 GPU + 64 GB RAM), in 1440p mode with VSync enabled, on a 144 Hz monitor -- framerates usually hovered in the 120 FPS range with some dips going under 100 during heavier scenes, and otherwise capping at 144 when not much was happening. It also pushed my coolant temps to 37C, which is the highest I've ever seen it go (for context, most games barely push it north of 30-31C. Harsher games might put it to 33C or even 35C).Still very playable, but it's strange to see a remastered version of Crysis that 1. still looks dated by today's standards with little improvement over the original, even with maxed settings, and 2. is way harder on my machine than several modern titles that look better and perform more efficiently.I enjoyed the game, but mainly the first half where stealth and infiltration were more viable strategies. Once things go all alien on you, I feel like the nanosuit starts to lose its edge and things devolve into braindead shooter territory. The whole game is over in 6-8 hours, even if you are going for all the achievements and playing on the hardest difficulty mode. Once it's over, there's not much in the way of replayability. There's no multiplayer mode in this version, so I'm not sure what more there is to do. I bought this game on sale for $4.49, mainly to get the achievements. Had I paid the full $29.99, I would have probably felt really dissatisfied with how little this remaster offers over the original.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the "Crysis-Remaster Edition" together with "Hunt Showdown" for roundabout 30€(~34,92USD). I played through the whole game on "Delta" (Highest Difficulty). I played it for ~10H in 3 sessions.By default, you get a suit more similar to "Crysis 2". An easier to control suit with less versatility. It is perfect for console players, but if you're using a mouse and Keyboard i highly recommend switching to the more versatile "Classic" Nanosuit.Options -> Game options Tick "Classic Nanosuit"(Don't forget to Click Apply, if you just press ESC afterwards your changes will not be applied)For newcomers having problems with the Classic suit just remember:M3+Mouse Forward = Speed (A movement as if you would engage)M3+Mouse Backward = Cloak (A movements as if you would retreat)M3+Mouse Right = Strength (Imagine a Knight, Sword in the Right hand)M3+Mouse Left = Armor (Imagine a Knight, Shield in the Left hand)The default controls of the remastered edition could be described as very "Creative".Like Putting lean left and right on T and H or changing fire mode on 5.I highly recommend changing the controls to something similar to the original.I use the Classic nanosuit with these control changes:Q/E - Lean left/rightH - Change GrenadeC - Fire Mode (I put it on C instead of X because i have big hands)X  - Customization MenuSTRG - CrouchT - Melee(Certain Objects like toilet brushes can be used as melee weapons.)If you change your Grenade through the Grenade-Selection-Window and left click, you will throw the selected grenade;  in my case a smoke. Afterwards the grenade display in the HUD changed from frags to smokes. Up to this point everything is working as intended.The smoke grenades were still displayed as the "active" grenade in my HUD. I was quite surprised when I intended to throw a smoke under myself to cover my retreat, but got blasted into space instead. It does not matter which grenade you have selected, if you press G and are in possession of a frag, a frag will be thrown.For some things you have to hold the key, just pressing it wont work. I repeatedly pressed F like a madman until I realized that I had to hold F to exchange my SCAR for a Shotgun.If you aim at a person who is on your side, you get a red X and your gun won't fire. This includes dead friendlies. The "Gunlock" hitbox is bigger than the actual hitbox of the entity. If you sit manually on a friendly tank you cannot openfire since you are sitting inside the gunlock-box. On the Aircraft Carrier I often could not shoot at the enemy, because my dead teammates were triggering the "Gunlock" making the end boss fight very frustrating.Ohh the Alien Trooper is right in front of you tearing through your HP? Sorry, I can't let you attack it because somewhere in that direction is a dead body that theoretically could get hit. Oops, you're dead. Thanks game!The AI in general seems to be more perceptive, you are no longer a ghost when activating "Cloak" mid combat. Also even when invisible the AI will notice you when you get too close; I noticed that the hard way when I tried to sneak past an ATV (Jeep) and the gunner unloaded his MG right into my face.The only annoying part is that they seem to "Lock On" and sometimes see through brush. Once they are (Red)alerted to your presence they do not care how many bushes, trees, fences, etc. are between you and them, they'll shoot at you with pinpoint accuracy. On the other hand, if they're still yellow, they are sometimes stupidly blind.If I recall correctly, the AI navigation inside the Cryengine is mostly done with "Forbidden Area" and "Navigation Area". The First one just prevents the AI from stepping inside the zone, the second is made for precise Navigation, where the AI can only move from and to placed navigation points and can only enter and leave the zone through placed entry markers. The Navigation Area appears to be not working. The AI is walking against walls, gets stuck in buildings.In the original Crysis game where invisible AI-behavior markers where the Enemy AI would perform certain actions like smoking or repairing something. Most of these Objects do not work. I noticed it when the guy who is usually relieving himself next to an explosive barrel was missing in the first level.The "spawning" of enemy AI is done through Flowgraph. Something happens like entering an area and then an AI Entity is switched from Disable to Enable and it pops into the world.This leads to some enemies standing around in a pose that looks like someone pulled the Plug. Like at the end of level 2 some of the patrolstaff stood on a rock, armes straight down, with their FY71 attached to their right hand, staring into the jungle. In the original the boats in the first level were spotting you quite fast. They may have been a bit annoying but they were definitely a threat. The Boats in the remake are no longer the Hawks of the original, instead they are completely blind. In the 1st Level, I killed the first boat's gunner from the Jammer position and destroyed the second boat with the MG of an ATV(Jeep) from a beach near the KVA Command Post. In both cases the Boats did NOT return fire.The battle tanks in the 5th map only fight back if you drive close to them, a few foot soldiers of that map just run past the player, not even attacking when you shoot at them.In the original I remember a surge of helicopters getting in my way. There were so many of them that they were absolutely annoying. But in the remaster, there were only a few of them, I'm not sure if they were removed or the AI just couldn't find their way anymore.The Alien Scouts(Flying Tentacle Monster) didn't use their Secondary attack even once(Charge Attack, firing an explosive projectile). The Alien Troopers(The little jumpy ones) had trouble moving in the Aircraft Carrier, sometimes being unable to attack.I might be wrong, but the damage dealt by throwing objects seems to have been nerfed. This is a good thing. One Shotting the NVA-General with a Box was kind of a balacebreaker.I don't remember if it was the same in the original but incoming fire comes with Camerashakes and other effects. It makes returning fire more difficult, I like that.In the Cryengine, The Roads are drawn with a Pathtool and then plastered onto the map like a decal. But it seems a few of them are floating.

_childDocuments_.review: Released in 2014, this review of Crysis Remastered takes into account the criteria and standards of that era.(̿▀̿ ̿Ĺ̯̿̿▀̿ ̿)̄ 👍TLDR: Crysis Remastered impresses with breathtaking visuals and retains the beloved game play mechanics of the original. However, the game is marred by occasional bugs and glitches, while the traversal system and final map could use further polishing. AI improvements are also desired. Despite its flaws, Crysis Remastered offers an immersive experience for fans seeking nostalgia.With all the said.. Still recommend.Pros:Breathtaking Visuals : Crysis Remastered stuns with its meticulously redesigned environments, impressive lighting effects, and attention to detail. The game takes full advantage of modern hardware capabilities, creating a visually immersive experience.Refined Game play Mechanics: The remastered edition retains the beloved core gameplay mechanics, such as the versatile Nanosuit and open-ended level design. Players have the freedom to approach combat in various ways, adding depth to the game play experience.Engaging Nostalgia: Crysis Remastered successfully captures the essence of the original game, offering a nostalgic journey that fans will appreciate. The updated visuals and refined controls breathe new life into the classic game play.Cons:Bugs/Glitches: Crysis Remastered is not without its share of bugs and glitches, as has been commented on by many players. While my play through was relatively smooth, I did encounter one level-breaking bug that forced me to restart the final level.Polishing Travel Mechanics: The traversal system in Crysis Remastered could benefit from further polishing. Walking across terrain feels less smooth than expected, with abrupt level changes that disrupt the fluidity of sprinting.Frustrating Final Map: The final map proves to be a source of frustration. Navigating through small hallways and doors is acceptable, but encountering issues with passing through NPCs or NPC bodies necessitates reloading checkpoints to progress.AI Improvements Needed: Although the AI has been enhanced, some players may find that it could have been further improved in terms of enemy behaviour and tactical decision-making.Conclusion:Despite its captivating visuals and enjoyable game play, Crysis Remastered falls short in a few areas. The presence of bugs and glitches, although not pervasive, can disrupt the overall experience. Additionally, improvements are needed in the game's travel mechanics to ensure smoother movement and eliminate abrupt level changes. Lastly, the frustrating aspects of the final map, particularly the issues with interacting with NPCs, can hamper immersion and progress.

_childDocuments_.review: You can still buy the original Crysis by searching for , then selecting . You can also buy it from , if Crytek decide to pull it from Steam completely. If you're keen on the remaster's visual improvements there's a  that improves the original's visual fidelity beyond those of the remaster, giving it 4K textures, global illumination, screen-space ambient occlusion, real-time reflections, tessellation, volumetric clouds, and so on.As many of you know, Crysis Remastered is a PC port of a console port of the original Crysis. Destructibility has been scaled down. Physics are worse. Performance is worse. Quick saves have been removed. Difficulty is lower; enemies do less damage and hit less frequently. The most damning thing about the remaster is that the gameplay has been changed significantly from the original game. Certain suit modes have become tied to actions, such as speed with sprint and jump with strength. Furthermore, you suit mode can't be changed while in vehicles (I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loved ghosting past enemies—they'd know I was there, but they wouldn't know  in the vehicle I was).The original Crysis was hard by design. By making  select suit modes on the fly, you had to think when planning out and enacting combat situations. The remaster takes away a lot of this and Crysis plays more like an action game rather than an immersive sim. I died a lot going through the same levels in the original Crysis, but those deaths made me consider the inadequacies of my play style. I breezed through the first thirty minutes of Crysis Remastered without a sweat. This is not necessarily a bad thing, because it  still enjoyable, and there's no fault in enjoying a breezy game. What's unforgivable, however, is that Crytek has tried to hide the original game as much as possible, rewriting the experience of Crysis to conform more with its successors, Crysis 2 and 3. As I said earlier, the first felt like an immersive sim, where you  had to discover new ways of playing the game through experimentation. Mapping suit functions to actions streamlines this process of experimentation, and I think it's an incredibly sad thing to do. The richness of the original game is lost.You can read more about my thoughts on the original Crysis , as well as ways to make it perform well on modern PCs.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this is a tough one. Did it give me a nostalgia? Yes.Do I like the game? Yes.Would I recommend it full price? Never. This is a half-assed remaster so you should pay a half assed price for it. Get it on at least a 50% sale (or in the remastered trilogy bundle when on sale)My main gripes with the game are: Who the f* playtests those games? I just can't believe how fast the mouse sensitivity is at the absolute minimum.(at 800dpi) I had to configure the slider myself via an autoexec file to make the mouse feel like it's not on crack.After fixing the FOV and the sensitivity for the main game - the vehicle aiming is just absolutely unusable. It's WAYYYY too slow. Like I'd use my whole mousepad area for the damn camera in-game to barely move 10 degrees, and playing on DELTA difficulty, it was IMPOSSIBLE to kill those enemies in the sky with the anti-aircraft vehicle or whatever that thing is. I had to get out of it and use other guns to do what I was supposed to do in a vehicle. Like genuinely this makes me question if the devs responsible for the mouse controls even playtested this. Like, did they just make it somewhat work and decided "eh, whatever that's good enough"???How does the game just go from sonic aiming to turtle mode in vehicles? Can't it just strike a balance somewhere in the middle? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Second: The performance is...good-ish? But I'd still expect better. On a 3080+Ryzen 9 5900x I was getting about 80-160 fps, perhaps with rare drops into the 70's, that's running max settings, apart from object detail, which was set to high. Running at 1440p with DLSS on quality. Graphics: Objectively it looks better in places, the draw distance is better, the lighting is better, the reflections are good. However the faces of characters look really bad here, I'm even going to say they were better in the original. The caves just look terrible here, the volumetric lights are gone. Gameplay: The game is easy once you understand what it wants from you, however it doesn't always make sense. It's not fair. Your AR bullets would rarely go where you aim because of bullet spread, so unless you have a gauss rifle or a precision rifle (aka sniper), then you're way better off sneaking up to enemies in cloak mode then killing them. Now this would be okay if only the enemies ALSO had this bullet spread, but no, they can mow me down like they're shooting a fully automatic sniper rifle with no recoil. Sometimes the game would glitch and your cloak wouldn't even work. Like I was cloaked behind cover far away from a tank, I walked all the way to the other side of a road and the second I see the tank I'm dead, WHILE CLOAKED. Other times I can't even see the enemies cause they're on the other side of the map, yet they can see me perfectly fine. This just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ruins the "predator" vibe you're supposed to have with that suit (at least on the delta difficulty), because the enemies just have the best eyesight in the world, you hide, cloak walk around them faaaaaar away, the second you uncloak (if you're not in the bushes) you're spotted. OH, and why the hell remove the ability to manually save? It's now a checkpoint based saving system. TL;DROkay-ish graphical improvements, performance is good but not amazing, gameplay is the same old crap with a few improvements but also a few drawbacks compared to the OG. AND WHAT THE F IS WRONG WITH THAT MOUSE SENSITIVITY??? If you wanna play it, go for it, buy it on sale, the game is GOOD, but don't expect a fully polished game.6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to break this game down into three parts. There will be spoilers ahead but this game has been out since the early 2000's so most people should know what the story is by this point. The Good:- This game functions as a perfectly fine FPS. It does exactly what it says on the tin. The integration of the nano suit makes combat with the game varied enough so that it doesn't feel like your typical Modern Warfare/Battlefield game play loop. - The environments and the design of the game from a visual stance is nice to see. The jungles feel very dense with different areas that can be used for tactical use such as hiding or cover when needed. The way that enemy strong points gave access to different approaches of combat was also refreshing. The visuals themselves, while I don't have a rig that can run the game at maximum settings, was very pretty and you could tell why this game pushed graphical boundaries to not only their limit but even made new ones. - The difficulties paired with enemy A.I. felt reasonable. I played the game at medium difficulty because if I wanted to play a difficult game, I would go play Dark Souls. This I wanted to be more of a fun and relaxing, unwinding experience. - Weapon variety is nice and there are certain combinations for almost every player type. If you want to go stealth or extremely aggressive or something in between there are plenty of options to choose from. The Bad:- The story and the characters are a mayonnaise sandwich. While the nano suit is a very nice addition to the game, the actual game play loop is uninspiring and lacks a lot of creative impact or direction. This game feels like it's selling points was the nano suit and how amazing the graphics could look if you had the insane hardware requirements needed in order to do so. - While the environment is nice to look at and game in, it does get repetitive after a while. I really wish there were more areas to use and plan your mode of attack through instead of just a enemy encampment or dense jungle. There are a few select areas that do change it up slightly, one being in the alien ship where you had to align yourself correctly while floating in zero gravity and enemies could come from any angle. but other than that, attention to include environmental combat and having a wider ecosystem to fight in would have been fantastic to see. - Maybe it was just my experience, but there were times I would pick up a weapon that had it's flashlight on or there was mention that I had the option to use different ammo types or an under-slung weapon system. It didn't matter what I pressed there was no way to use any of these options or turn the flashlight off. - The inclusion of the nano suit was nice, but a lot of the times I just opted to use one feature of the suit for a huge chunk of my play-through. The sprinting feature was the only other option I used. I think if the game had been designed around the suit and the features it included would have brought the game head and shoulders where it is now. The Ugly- This game is horrifically buggy. The A.I. would act up and not function properly. There were swathes of the game that I couldn't interact with anything or a prompt wouldn't appear and I would wonder around gormless until I had to look up what I was supposed to do next. Events that characters in the game would exclaim and point out never actually appeared on screen and I just had to use my imagination of what could or might have happened.  - There is no reason to use any of the features the nano suit provides instead of its invisibility feature. Pair that with any weapon with a sight and you can breeze through most if not all of the game in no time. Paired with the buggy A.I. and it makes the game play even less interesting. - I had to stop playing the game because the second part of the final boss fight I could not get through. Not because it was difficult, but because I was caught in an endless loop of the alien mother ship freezing me over and over, which you have to spend time breaking out of, while the smaller alien ships around it would endlessly hit me and I would just die with no way out of it. I tried every tactic I could think of and nothing worked. - There are plenty of times where whatever I was shooting at, the bullets would just phase through the target. This is especially frustrating during the final boss fight where you need to hit certain points on the mother ship and your bullets would just go right through it and cause absolutely no damage. - The story and the characters bore me to tears. You're not invested in anything that happens on the island because everything has the same impact and depth as rice paper. Enemy units start employing their own type of nano suits? No further investigation into that, it just gets brought up once and never mentioned again. You discover alien life and that the strange structures around the island belong to an advance alien race and the island is sheltering a huge alien ship? Your character barely comments on any of this. The game put all of it's eggs into the graphics and hoped you didn't pay attention to anything else. - I would not buy this game and because of the experience I had I will not be buying any of its future installments either.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis Remastered is a remaster of the iconic shooter by Crytek. In the latest version, only the quality of the graphics has changed, but as this is my first time with this series, I will review it from scratch.We play as Nomad, a super-soldier who, together with his unit, goes on a mission to the Lingshan Islands to investigate Korean activity, which ends up in a fight for survival against very aggressive aliens. In general, this game can be compared to typical American action/sci-fi movies from the early 2000s. It is a shooter where we do not need to use too much brain power, but the characters that accompany us, the main character and the opponents are interesting enough to generate specific feelings for them. and opinions. Overall, I found the game-pacing to be very good here, the alien discovery intrigue and the final alien encounters are well separated from each other, creating tension and making the encounters more meaningful. All in all, each character has something to add here, and they have their own experiences and motivations, most of them aren't useless so even though we're a powerfull super-soldier, we don't feel like we have to do everything completely on our own.The mechanics of being a super soldier are great. We can run very fast, modify our weapons, and our super-strength and durability allow us to break through buildings and massacre opponents in melee combat. Speaking of buildings, I like that the environment, i.e. structures and trees, are mostly destructible, so the environments are very interactive, which is a lot of fun to just smash and blow things up. The shooting itself is good, some enemies are damage sponges, but overall it's good. The island itself is surprisingly huge, and while it's mostly jungle, the massiveness of the map is admirable. Moving on to the aliens, I really liked them, although they follow the same logic as all the aliens from early 2000s and late 90s movies. Anyway, the game tries to make them original enough. The skirmishes with them are very dynamic, we often fight side by side with normal soldiers, and we fight for survival in very explosive skirmishes against an opponent that has much better technology, and some terraforming capabilities. Pure epicness and the last act of the island evacuation is brilliant. The only problem with all this is the part of the game where we enter the alien base, where gravity is turned off. The environment, although full of detail, is full of annoyingly fast enemies, it's hard to navigate, and the fact that we're constantly turning in place certainly didn't help my hungover stomach when going through this mission.Graphically it's very good, but in the tradition of Crysis, the optimization is poor. At least the game doesn't crash to desktop. As for the music, it's okay, typical sci-fi action game music. The voice actors did a good job, but the biggest plus of all this are great visual, and sound effects.A shooter classic, and a good game that is basically a game version of old American movies. A lot of good fun that doesn't require a lot of brain-usage from us. While it's nothing super special, I still think it's the best Crysis game out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis Remastered is a polished version of the popular 2007 sci fi first person shooter game 'Crysis' developed by Crytek in 2007. The original game takes place through the eyes of a elite soldier nicknamed 'Nomad', a member of a U.S. elite military group named 'Raptor Team' sent on a hostage extraction mission on Lingshan islands after the U.S. archaeologists have made a world-changing discovery that is undergoing siege by the Koreans. Nomad, alongside with his colleagues, is equipped with the state of the art 'nanosuit', a exo skeleton that is designed to give soldiers a upper hand in every situation with unique abilities that makes them superhuman. The mission goes awry at the very start after your colleague was kidnapped and later found slaughtered alongside Koreans by a mysterious entity that later on is identified as a otherworldly organism named 'Ceph' with the mission of conquering the planet. It us up to Nomad to rescue the archaeologists and fight his way through war with the Koreans and the Ceph.The original game was way ahead of its time with its beautiful graphics, outstanding lore and unique gameplay style that surpasses most games made today. It is a unique experience where you can do anything, the map is not designed linearly which allows the players to roam and do whatever they want. The soundtrack, the AI, the physics and much more are all beautifully made that gives lots of replayability as you can approach the game from any way, be it a silent sniper, onepunch man, rambo, there are always new ways to play the game. The characters are all unique with distinct personalities with lots of lore to each one, the nanosuit that makes us look cool and makes us feel powerful, the tank battles, the dogfights(aircraft fight) are all super fun and unique. The addition of mods just puts the cherry on top, with the large community designing new maps, new graphical mods and even a brand new game for the engine that the game is running on allows for many new opportunities which is why the original game is so beloved.That being said, after the massive success over the years, Crytek decided to remaster the game, improving the already beautiful graphics, unnecessarily bringing over the suit modes from Crysis 2 and 3 which personally I favor but there are lots of people disappointed, since you are always stuck in power mode contrary to the 2007 version where the default was armor mode. Apart from the graphics, there isn't really much more added in the remaster. There are no new weapons, no new attachments, no new hostiles, no new areas to explore, no new missions, it is simply a graphical overhaul mod made by the original developers. Performance wise, to get over 100 fps you would have to lower the settings to low or medium as the improved graphics also take a toll on the GPU, and that makes the game unpleasant to look at the mass amount of jagged edges. The highest difficulty setting isn't that much of a challenge, the secondary objectives have no impact on the game, the AI sometimes doesn't behave as expected, they all negatively impact the game and make you question the whole remaster deal. The only better thing is the graphics at high settings, they look amazing, however, you would need to invest in a decent GPU as even the better GPU's struggle to run at the max settings.I personally only enjoyed it as I am a huge Crysis fan, I am addicted to the amazing lore of the game and would like to take a different approach to the game after many years of not playing. Conclusion, I enjoyed Crysis as a way to experience the nostalgia and would recommend to play it, however, the remastered aspect is nonexistent, it is only made to test the developers graphical work. If you can get it for a lower price, the remastered is a good game but it is still disappointing, all the effort put into graphics are laid to waste as most people can't run the game with high settings with decent framerate. Crysis 2007 11/10Crysis Remastered 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the sloppiest 'remaster' design choices I've ever experienced; but still one of the best games ever made.Pros:- Plays almost identically to the original.  A successful port of the maps and combat.- New Ray-Tracing looks stunning and adds much more realism and depth to the environment.  - I didn't have a crash throughout my entire playthrough.  The original never ran stably for me; on 5 different systems....Cons:- Many cutscenes have been worsened by goofy lighting, animation glitches, and the occasional audio glitch (late music, missing lipsyncing for 1 line of dialogue etc)- QuickSaving requires a MOD.  I realize the other Crysis games were Auto-Save only, but the more linear gameplay allows for that.  Experimenting with the AI, physics, and combat mechanics were part of what made the original Crysis so replayable and it's an essential part of the experience!- The game has been 'reshaded' with too much saturation for my taste.  The game feels much more 'cheerful' than the original.  The aliens are less scary as a result, too.Recommend only on deep sale or if you've never experienced the original.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was highly sceptical because of bad reception from the community comparing it to the original game. But I changed my mind when I installed the original and directly compared them.👎 The bad:- worse faces somehow;- still optimized for 1 core of CPU;- many graphical options are 'overkill' on purpose, with highest named 'Can it run Crysis?' It's a joke.👍 The good:- in general, better graphics: originally, many features were locked behind maximum settings for marketing reasons (like normalmaps); but here many of them are overhauled. DLSS included. Even with the Original at maximum settings, the Remastered shows much more details. Also, you don't need raytracing;- suit got rebalanced with better control scheme. Also, originally, Maximum Speed mode was glitched with dramatically fluctuating speed and acceleration, god knows why it was doing that. In Remastered, the speed is more consistent and consumes less energy which gives you more options.- Remastered does what it should: has better compatibility and accessibility on modern systems.😃 I recommend it for you more than Crysis 2 & 3 if you want to feel more like a kid with a gun in a sandbox, playing Predator. It manages NOT to feel like a linear scripted shooter while being one. Pure magic.

_childDocuments_.review: For some reason, this doesn't feel remastered at all.Starting on positive note, the graphics is ok, and probably when this title came out, it must've been quite a mind breaker that certain objects on the map can get demolished.Now with all positives out of the way, my main gripe with this title is that the gameplay somehow doesn't sit right. Controls feels out of whack, I think there was a weapon wheel but the key to pull it out was so inconvenient that I was using scroll to swap weapons and I know that you can change key bindings, but I refused because this is how authors wanted it to be played. Flying VTOL? You better be joking. Thank god there was only one point that required flying, because generally speaking the controls are so botched, I might as well fly with display off using floor rag as input device and achieve the same result. Right from get-go the game misleads you to thinking that you can play each mission quietly by adding suppressors to almost any weapon and hinting that there is alert meter. Better ignore that crap because enemies spots you from kilometers sometimes even without even looking at your direction while crawling inside bushes. They'll raise the alarm and you're cooked. You can wait for it to go down a bit, but that unnecessary extends the time spend playing it plus on other difficulty levels than easy you die easier than in Souls franchise. I finished the game under 8h [and spent like 1h afk] including completing all extra tasks, but some sections you just gotta sprint and forget about enemies. About sprinting, idk who's idea that was to stick sprinting, jumping and melee under "power" meter, but it's more than annoying and again extends playtime without adding much in return. There was mentioned at the beginning, that the map can be destroyed, but it's super limited to certain tree types and constructions, most of objects still remain indestructible, which I don't see the main reason why remaster couldn't bring those too. My tip for you: find sniper rifle, use it whenever you can because it's honestly one of the better weapons due to low recoil and huge damage. Plus you can take out enemies from longer range from which they can't hit you.

_childDocuments_.review: I can remember checking Far Cry 5 like a month ago, and it was nothing. But this is such a blast, been awhile since I enjoyed just walking around and taking down npcs that much. Because map design is amazing and AI behaviour is kinda fun. And I completely forgot about vehicles and all that beautiful destruction you can cause to most things you see around. Unfortunately, it gets much more linear and boring in the final chapters. As for the remaster version, I think they tweeked some stuff because I remember this game originally being more clunky and difficult gameplay-wise. I guess that's the reason why they removed quicksaves, call it balance. The remaster looks great and I don't have any technical problems running it with most settings maxed out with my Radeon RX 580, Ryzen 5 2600 3.40 Ghz and 16 Gb RAM. Some people say they don't like the new terrain re-color or the new water looks, but I actually do.As for downsides, I've spotted some eye-catching ugly textures and models, 2007 style, which I think might have gotten into the remaster version straight from the original, with no work done over them whatsover. Overall, they aren't many and mostly start showing up in the second half of the game. But I feel like crytek gave up remastering the final levels, the latter the worse looking they are. As for the bugged AI that so many complain about, I've seen it a couple of times, can't say it was a game-breaking experience. In total, this is a nice version of Crysis to grab in 2021, regarding it's on steam and even cheaper than the original.

The new features, such as support for 4K, HDR, and ray tracing, make the visuals even more stunning.The gameplay in Crysis Remastered is still as fun as ever. _childDocuments_.review: Crysis was loved by PC fans and hated by those who only had one PC fan.Sometimes I still think "will it run Crysis?" when thinking about a pc, not realizing it was released over 15 years ago.Crysis 1 on Delta with Advanced A.I Mod and a graphic config used to be one of my favorite FPS experiences and I’ve played FPS games for 20 Years. And to this day it’s in my Top 5 FPS Games of all time. Its not perfect, like no game really is, but it did so much right and did not dumb down the whole game to be a multiplattform game, which sadly will never happen again.The first Crysis remaster is a bit spotty and deviates more towards “looking pretty” than it does “looking realistic” and removed things like manual saving. It's a mostly-better version of the original, but it's not a 1:1 comparison due to certain physics and shading features breaking in the Remaster, like vegetation reacting to explosives, or SVOGI drastically changing the Cutscenes in a decidedly worse way at times. Overall though? It's a smoother package, more widely accessible, and the RT is damn good.I would personally recommend this remaster. I think it's overall, especially with the fan patch, a solid experience that runs well, looks pretty nice, and has friendlier balancing and pacing, and who doesn’t love screwing with Koreans?The modern nanosuit controls are more intuitive to a lot of players, and the game's AI isn't as aim-bot-like anymore. And unless you're really familiar with Crysis, a number of the bugs won't be noticable.If you don't enjoy this Crysis 1 remaster though, don't let that dissuade you from trying Crysis 2. Crysis 1 is an interesting game, and well worth playing, but it's kind of a mess, and it's not uncommon for newcomers to be like, "It has interesting ideas, but I don't see what the fuss is about."7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the original Crysis every once in a while since it came out. This version is like one step forward, two steps back. There's been some gameplay tweaks, but also new bugs. For example, jeeps explode more quickly when shot in the gas tank and cloak is less of a power hog, but now crouching while prone makes you stand when you release crouch, and selecting the nanosuit mode with the mouse while crouching makes you stand. _childDocuments_.review: A different take for the original Nanosuit system. It's good fun. A little overpriced I feel, but I do recommend getting it on discount. Differences (aside from graphics, obv): 1. The biggest difference is there's no manual save, only checkpoints. I'm playing on delta and hardly noticed any difference, honestly, not a lot of difficulty increase. 2. Nanosuit. You CAN switch back to the original, but if you played the original, the new system offers some different experiences.     2.1: Your energy regens A LOT faster. This makes the "cloak - regen - cloak" loop a lot faster.     2.2: Sprinting in speed mode costs MUCH LESS energy.     2.3: Jumping in strength mode costs less energy.     2.4: Armor mode is completely useless. Not only does it bleeds energy, it costs pretty much the same amount of energy as the original when shot, which was the default mode in the original... So in total it tanks LESS shots cuz of the bleeding.     2.5: Your default mode is strength, meaning you don't get the passive protection like in the original, and might get one-shotted more often.     2.6: The new strength mode doesn't seem to suppress gun recoil. I really like that you activate modes with one button instead of the wheel. I just hope armor mode was still the default mode, unlike the garbage it is now. But oh well, it's still fun. Other than that, gameplay wise it's pretty much the same as the original, crouching around in cloak and shooting stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis is utterly beautiful; be it in its original form or this 2020 remaster. The game offers genuine technological prowess in its gorgeous outdoor jungles and industrial indoor bases. It has some truly jaw-dropping vistas, and it serves as a perfect benchmark for those who bought a new, more powerful graphics card and/or processor.Also, as a game, it slaps; It's a pretty solid shooter built around non-linearity in a linear framework, courtesy of the Nanosuit, the game's main gimmick. Cloak gives you the advantage to begin a quiet assault, Armour gives you protection if you want to go in guns-a-blazin', Speed gives you a powerful sprint for hit and run attacks, and Strength allows you to jump further and throw farther, whilst giving you a powerful punch. Coupled with some [mostly] solid AI, the end result is some truly fun gunfights and engagements.However, it's not for me. The gameplay, despite doubling as a power fantasy, has an odd quirk where enemies take less damage from bullets... but neither do you. You take as much as you deliver, and because of this the game is far more tactical than other futuristic power fantasy games about taking control of the battlefield and emerging victorious I.E. Halo, F.E.A.R., and Doom. Don't get me wrong, it still holds up, but for me it's not my cuppa tea.So yes. I'd happily recommend it but players more familiar with an arcade-style of shooter should be aware of what they're getting into: This is a thinking man's game, and if your reflexes aren't up to snuff, you will be punished. Otherwise, if you have new hardware in your computer (or a new computer period), Crysis Remastered is basically a must.

Notability Ascension mission missing the soundtrack entirely.-Integrated achievements to Steam-Some special effects from the original game are not present here. _childDocuments_.review: The good- Gorgeous graphics ahead of its time. In this remastered version it has become even better with high resolution textures and revised atmospheric lighting.- Great physics that were innovative for back then. You can interact, shoot, throw or shatter almost everything in a very convincing way. After a battle has finished, the landscape will be absolutely destroyed. A feature that even new games miss.- Well paced battles with many things happening simultaneously. Good immersion level at a war situation.- Gameplay allows you to choose between various approaches, either more tactical or entirely destructive. Cloak and shield powers of nanosuit are good additions that give the gameplay extra depth.- Awesome survival atmosphere. Some parts have a weird dark, terrifying feeling. After a certain point it gets surreal and artistic.- Fantastic sound design. Both environmental and battles' design feels natural and rich of sounds. Surround is well implemented and helps you understand enemies' direction.- Interesting music that fits perfectly in each situation and gives an extra boost to the atmosphere.- Nice animations especially at enemy creatures and at the protagonist's hands.- It is very cinematic for its age. Great direction and camera movement with some nice timed events and special effects. Cool cut scenes too.- You can drive a boat, a hummer, a tank and even fly an airplane.- The story has a cliché beginning but after the middle it offers some interesting twists. It is still simplistic but descent enough for this king of shooter.- It is well balanced. Normal difficulty will challenge you without being too hard.The bad- Navigation mechanics and interaction commands are not very responsive. Constant small glitches here and there (e.g. when crouching) will sometimes ruin the pace and the vibe you are into.- Big loading screens and bad optimization for a game that old. You have to enable vsynch, otherwise the game will roast your cpu.- Mediocre enemies' AI. Sometimes they react very slowly and others they run towards you instead of covering.- Small variety of weapons and even fewer weapons' upgrades.- You cannot save whenever you want. Sometimes there is a long distance to cover between two autosave points.- The map is bad and most things on it are indistinguishable.- The control mechanics of the airplane part are poorly implemented. Frustrating.- It has small duration and abrupt ending. In fact there is no ending. I didn't like this weird final boss battle too.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original Crysis so I picked this up. Here's what I can say. There's a story to be told but the game doesn't tell it. instead the game has you going from point A to point B without any proper explanation of whatever the ♥♥♥♥ is going on. Additionally, the open world setting does absolutely nothing except making the process of moving from one objective to another an absolute hassle. Finally, the biggest issue of this game is the absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AI that can spot you from miles away. The AI makes stealth in this game more of a chore, as more of then than not, no matter how careful you plan your approach, the chances of some AI detecting you from 100 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ feet away is always high. Even when you're hidden the enemies will sometimes just randomly detect you for no good reason leading to inevitable combat. Which brings me to the combat, which is ♥♥♥♥ smeared ass cheeks. Enemies are HP sponges and they're able to soak up your bullets without even flinching. Did I also mention that there's literally a mission where aiming with the mouse doesn't work (search for Crysis Remastered Ascension mouse not working.) I could go on and on but the verdict is this: the only thing that aged well in Crysis for both the original and Remastered version is the graphics. Sprinting is sometimes a death sentence because I'll be rushing at MACH 12 and I don't get enough time to react to getting shot to get armor turned on, and even when I do I barely have any energy left to protect myself. Too many times the janky physics got me killed.Everything about this game was either "meh" or "oh my god, why?" Even the character models suck at times, whether it's the San Andreas "remaster" style sleeves, or Prophet's jaw clipping through his suit. Or some muscle strands not being properly bound to the rest of the body, making it clip through a raised bicep.This game is honestly not worth it at this point. It had its run back then, but now it sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Yet another "remaster" that has enshittified a beloved classic and neutered it. If you REAAAALLY want this, try and wait for 90% off sale. Otherwise avoid it. If you want a truly remastered(ish) Crysis, I would suggest firing up original one with Tactical Expansion Mod, awailable here: For optimizing original to run on newer hardware, refer to PC Gaming Wiki here: Pros: Newer CryEngine (3, I think) gives you better graphics, and nominally better optimizations: but I haven't seen much difference between original's maxed out and Remaster's High setting graphics.Onslaught Level gives you as initial spawn tank with infinite main cannon ammo, unlike original where it was limited to 25-30 shells, if I remember correctly.Achivements, maybe, due to most of them being tied to story progression, with only about 5 or 6 referring to various gameplay and physics shenanigans. And most of those are achiveable on first playtrough. For Achievement hunters, do not expect to sweat too much if you want to get them all.Cons: EVERYTHING ELSE.  Mods? ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gone.Multiplayer? ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gone.Warhead expansion pack/sidestory? DOUBLE ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gone. Seriously, you only get first Crysis, and it is playable trough in 6-8 hours, I have about 8.5 hours of game time at writing this, and had made a playtrough on Medium while suffering from cold, so thus was not at 100%. Sound: some details are better, as well as audio cues about suit status being more prominent, but other are at same exact level as original.AI: braindead idiots, with occasional wallhacking spots of "briliance". (I also play Star Citizen, game based on heavily modified Cryengine off-fork and even with SC's servers running badly, AI there is still miles better and more lethal that here.)UI: worse. Older players may remember how you could choose between different colors for HUD and menus, and EVEYRTHING would be adjusted for color. Well, not in this remaster. Original's Olive Drab Green still remains strong in game and on menus.I also noticed stutterings, mostly on Assault and Onslaught levels, ones that are massively sprawling and stretch for kilometers. SO, my guess is, the game has not been nearly as well optimized and it should have been. Closing: I only bought this because it was on 90% sale, and I still feel ripped off. Remaster that is more of a sloppily done port to newer hardware and OS rather than proper remaster. Think long and hard if you really would like to buy one.

_childDocuments_.review: Can it run Crysis, the term has been renewed. That is the short version.Considering this is a remaster, not an entire remake. It will on that setting, demand an RTX 3080 or better to run, at least in 4k.The original was released in 2007, running the second iteration of CryEngine.A piece of gaming history.What has changed, considering it's a remaster it still uses the original game's assets. Like all remasters do.What has been added:*Higher Draw Distance LOD, would be the most noticeable.*Completely new lighting techniques, including Ray Tracing. Your GPU doesn't even need to support it, it's built into the engine itself. While the game offers some basic extension to it, turned on by a simple checkbox.*Tesselation on more objects such as rocks, mainly is where you will notice it.*Texture resolution on assets, some are even remodeled from scratch.*Sound samples, mainly on guns and they way they sound.* Ray Tracing light effects, you can run this effect in this game even without an RTX enabled GPU. It's embedded in the engine's software according to Linus Tech. Also here the minuses begin, it's demanding. A lot!* Quality of Life improvements to the controls. The control scheme is taken from Crysis 2 and 3, and gives you easier access to the nano suit. However if you preferred the original game's controls, you can still go back to that. Other QoL stuff is the intuitive toggle function on certain actions such as aim down sight and crouch. The original game locked ADS to toggle and crouch to hold and you could not change that. This point is probably the only reason I would recommend the remaster over the original. That and this remaster IS very good looking if you can afford to turn up the graphics settings.-Shaders, makes the game look like a cartoon. It's not celshading thankfully. Everything is just too green, too lush. Where the original showed moonlight on the palm leaves, here they simply look... unreal. You can easily mod this however.-HDR, but absolutely gives nothing for it. We're not talking anything remotely HDR10 here. It's like they forgot that HDR supports 10bit color depth but all the assets are still 8bit. Games that supports W11 HDR enhancement looks better using it than this game does with official HDR support.-Again Texture resolution, apparently or obviously resolution doesn't always mean sharper. Some look even worse than the original, like parts of trees, even the nano suits in some places like the helmet. Faces of the main characters? Generic NPC's look better now than the main cast of the game.-Shadows, they simply shimmer all over the place now a lot of the time. Most likely to the in game Ray Tracing lighting. When it works, it looks great, but it often does not.-Vegetation, as beautiful it looks on picture, once you're in the game you may notice how static they are. Trees and brushes no longer moves in the wind, no longer do you or NPC displace vegetation in the same realistic manner, nor does the brushwork hide you effectively as they did in the original game.Also the animations on them seem to be locked at a very low frame rate whenever displacement does occur.Game does support DLSS! For those with an nVidia card who wants to enjoy this title in 4k. You will need that turned on. Or simply install the original and run it in 4k with ease. It demands about 4GB V-RAM (Which is one of those reasons it never ran well at all on older machines when the original came out, most cards sported about 256-512MB at best back then, but then the target resolution was 1024x768, not even 1920x1080 widescreen, 4k was a dream far far away nobody had probably even thought of being a possibility in video gaming back then)The original Crysis runs very well on modern machines from the last 6 years or so. A GTX 1080 can run it in 4k. This remaster however, not so much.I was running this remaster with an RTX 3080, on an Intel machine 10th Gen i9 10900k, 32 GB of DDR4 RAM at 3000MHz XMP and from an M.2 Drive. Still PCI-X gen 3.0 but... on "Can it run Crysis" settings with DLSS on Quality I get about 40-50 frames per second, in 4k. A stable 60 if I run on Very High. With experimental RTX effects and HDR turned on. This for comparison is about the same I get from Cyberpunk 2077 with Ray tracing turned on and reflections on Psycho and with DLSS on Auto. (Not Quality setting for DLSS it becomes unplayable in 4k for some reason on nVidia cards now when everything else is maxed out, except maybe on a 4090 and is thus the pinnacle on hardware demanding PC games currently, despite even this remasters release trying to clearly be mainly intended to take that back) Either way I guess it's safe to say my machine can run Crysis =)This though is from a remaster of a game that have much smaller levels and was made in 2007.Does it look good? Yes, is it indeed does, but it still feels like an old game even visually. You can tell it is a remaster, not a remake.Don't buy this if you are just looking for a good game to enjoy, unless it's on sale, otherwise I would go for the original version. Because it was great as a game and still is!Especially on Delta difficulty where you really had to think and plan before you acted. Even on easy it was difficult to go full Leroy Jenkins, but on Delta it truly shines.Only buy this version if you want to push your new hardware to the max or are interested in getting the Steam Achievements. Though you can also buy this version of the game on Epic Store depending who has the better prices for the moment.The best part of this release however, it's an EA owned IP, but doesn't require neither Origin nor EA Play third party applications or accounts to run. It does blow a bit of fresh air into an old but fondly remembered title that is indeed a very important part of PC Gaming History.Crysis. A title that pushed boundaries of video game fidelity, in fact CryTek, just like Epic has always been about that and the simplicity to use their engines for video game creation. This particular title was definitely a big reason why other video games started looking much better than before. It was and still is a great showcase what games can look like, and I mean even games made today! 13 years later. This version, is sadly a bit generic. Adds things you will most likely not notice all that much, unless you run a comparison of them next to each other. If you want a showcase of RTX effects, even Minecraft and Quake II RTX does a much better job of doing that, or I recommend Cyberpunk 2077 or Watch Dogs Legion to best enjoy that as a tech demonstration.I would buy this remaster only for the Benchmark, "Can it run Crysis" hence the other title comparisons, and the Steam Achievements. Otherwise, the original release will do you just as well.You should also know there are MASSIVE differences in the game play when using the sequels mechanics. They were better the first time around I felt, even if they caused you to think before you acted more.Also the AI is MUCH better at spotting you in the remastered version, even on Delta, making the game immensely harder than the original release.And last but not least, the original did not use checkpoints or constrain you to to them, the original uses the old fashioned manual saving system and relied on that. The remaster does not offer this, it is a MUCH harder game than the original in comparison. Even on easier difficulties.Another last minute negative thing: The expansion for the original, Warhead, is NOT included in this release.Though Warhead was also standalone, you do not need the original game to play it.

Some of them you may know from the original game, most of them are new, at least for myself. Especially at the end of the game they where quite some of them around, but nothing game breaking. Sometimes the frames dropped for a few seconds for whatever reason, sometimes there's no muzzle flash, invisible walls or rubber banding. Also I had a weird facial animation bug one time. When having the "reduced movement" bug just change weapons and you're good. In its core its still Crysis of course, it will always be one of my fav games, but besides the updated graphics (raytracing looks great) I'd still prefer the original, maybe with some mods. Textures where updated and looked nice in 4K, but they forgot soem spot here and there.Achievment wise its very easy, got all of them in one run under 10 hours. Delta difficulty is pretty easy, thanks to your suit. I recommend to start "Marathon man" early on so you dont have to power-sprint around at the end of the game to pop the achievment. Also look out for the yellow markers for side objectives, but they are very easy to spot, plus the game tells you every time.Final verdict: If you loved the first one its cool to come back after all these years, if you got the hardware. _childDocuments_.review: You can still buy the original Crysis by searching for Crysis Warhead, then selecting Crysis Maximum Edition. You can also buy it from gog[], if Crytek decide to pull it from Steam completely. If you're keen on the remaster's visual improvements there's a mod that improves the original's visual fidelity beyond those of the remaster, giving it 4K textures, global illumination, screen-space ambient occlusion, real-time reflections, tessellation, volumetric clouds, and so on.As many of you know, Crysis Remastered is a PC port of a console port of the original Crysis. Destructibility has been scaled down. Physics are worse. Performance is worse. Quick saves have been removed. Difficulty is lower; enemies do less damage and hit less frequently. The most damning thing about the remaster is that the gameplay has been changed significantly from the original game. Certain suit modes have become tied to actions, such as speed with sprint and jump with strength. Furthermore, you suit mode can't be changed while in vehicles (I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loved ghosting past enemies—they'd know I was there, but they wouldn't know where in the vehicle I was).The original Crysis was hard by design. By making you select suit modes on the fly, you had to think when planning out and enacting combat situations. The remaster takes away a lot of this and Crysis plays more like an action game rather than an immersive sim. I died a lot going through the same levels in the original Crysis, but those deaths made me consider the inadequacies of my play style. I breezed through the first thirty minutes of Crysis Remastered without a sweat. This is not necessarily a bad thing, because it is still enjoyable, and there's no fault in enjoying a breezy game. What's unforgivable, however, is that Crytek has tried to hide the original game as much as possible, rewriting the experience of Crysis to conform more with its successors, Crysis 2 and 3. As I said earlier, the first felt like an immersive sim, where you necessarily had to discover new ways of playing the game through experimentation. Mapping suit functions to actions streamlines this process of experimentation, and I think it's an incredibly sad thing to do. The richness of the original game is lost.You can read more about my thoughts on the original Crysis here, as well as ways to make it perform well on modern PCs.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis Remastered is really not worth the money nor the hype it originally received. When I saw this game and hear the original reviews for it I was all well and good to ignore any negative criticism and just try the game out to see its 'quality' for myself, But personally I don't believe Crysis Remastered really adds a whole lot to improve to the original game and the graphical 'improvements' aside the only really noticeable additions this remaster really makes is with the enemy AI, but even that is a laughable claim. I also experienced painful issues with the view models and collision models of objects not lining up correctly, with the case often being that i'd shoot at an enemy that is in view but the shot will not connect because it hit the 'rock'. I have also encountered many other bugs such as: weird water effects appearing on boats that are completely out of water, odd water effects on boats sitting in water, enemies that are very large distances away sounding as if they are 5 metres from my face, odd bullet physics with bullets landing far above where they are shot, and other weird physics related bugs with cars and debris. So in conclusion if you are looking to play Crysis but the original and if the graphics really concern you that much slap on a few community made mods and you'll have a similar but more refined experience than what Crysis Remasterd can offer.Side Note: The water caustics do look quite nice though, so at least that's something nice

_childDocuments_.review: It's I, Starscream, once again, to share my recent experience with Crysis Remastered on my new OLED TV. Previously, I extolled its virtues, but alas, after this recent encounter, my opinion has shifted.The original game was akin to wearing a golden armor, reminiscent of my legendary exploits in the Transformers episode, The Golden Lagoon. However, what I've noticed in this remastered version are not upgrades but downgrades. The lack of plant physics is appalling. In the old game, you could interact with foliage, pushing plants aside as you moved through them. Now? You simply clip through them like a malfunctioning Decepticon.And the nighttime, supposed to be an immersive experience with ray tracing, falls utterly short. Instead of darkness, the night is as bright as an energon cube, ruining the tension the original game offered. The flashlight no longer serves its purpose, leaving me disappointed and vexed, much like Megatron after a failed conquest.In conclusion, Crysis Remastered on my new OLED TV is a letdown. It's like encountering a malfunctioning Seeker in the midst of battle. The downgrades from the original, particularly in plant physics and the lack of darkness in the night, have soured the experience. I'd have to give this version a Starscream-revoked rating of , purely due to these disappointing deviations from the original game's immersion and mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a great nostalgia trip that I really enjoyed. It clocked in at about 9 hours for me to do a complete play through of the storyline. Open world is fun to screw around in, but guided missions are much better for story telling.The story itself was a pretty decent sci-fi, there is no forced romance or crappy plot written in.
