_childDocuments_.review: Legendary game by a very well-known publisher that is unfortunately not known by many because it was overshadowed at the time by Pokemon, due to their similar nature - likely due to Pokemon's accessibility and ease of use by children, while Monster Rancher is a bit more complicated. Have played hundreds of hours before Steam release, somewhat detailed review inc.Monsters are much more personal in MR, as you only raise one at a time and it grows in size and power before your eyes over time through training (and resting) and battling/gaining tournament rank, until it's eventual death -- having differing potential for stat gains from training and success rates as they age, creating incentive not necessarily to minmax (though you definitely can get into the more hardcore side of MR if that's your preference) but to raise the monster correctly in a way that allows you to progress the furthest or do the most with that particular monster.Monsters come in Main and Sub breeds and can be combined (eg Dino/Dino and Tiger/Tiger makes D/T or T/D depending on first monster chosen) and have 6 different stats. They have Loyalty levels depending on how you treat them (praising or punishing them for things and giving them items/monthly food type) , different and unique moves per monster that each scale with one of two of the stats.. Plenty of room for different builds for different monsters, allowing for nearly infinite replayability.This has been all over the place, but the game is a very easy 10/10, couldn't believe my eyes when I saw that Koei-Tecmo was 'remastering' MR 1+2. If Pokemon or any kind of monster raising/battling/collecting type game holds your interest AT ALL, I can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: GRADE B+. Monster Rancher 1 feels clunky and outdated. But Monster Rancher 2 still holds up and is worth playing. However, like many of these CLASSIC game ports on steam, they just didn't do much to update the game other then some very minor QoL improvements. I would have loved to see A remastered score or updated graphics or maybe some Voice acting would have been amazing, Even something as basic as adding achievements would have given some motivation for me to spend more time revisiting the game.Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX on Steam is a faithful port of the DS versions, offering classic monster raising with no frills. Hatch pixelated pals from a search engine (which is better then switching out a ton of CD's) Train their quirks, and battle for glory in tournaments or take your monsters on adventures and explore the mysteries of the setting. It's a really nice hit of nostalgia for fans, but expect no modern bells like online play or remastered graphics or even something as basic as achievements. it's a little bit sad to see the wasted opportunity to throw a little polish on a classic gem. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Despite being two decades old, this game is just as good as I remembered it. If you like breeding games, you must give this a try.I remember playing this for the first time when I was little. My parents had just bought me and my brother a PS1, and a few games for christmas, this being one of them. Back then, my English was not very good, and my parents weren't exactly interested in our games, so it took me literal years to learn that you could actually use CDs to summon other monsters. Even so, I loved the game from the very beginning.When my brother told me he saw the game on Steam, I didn't hesitate and bought it immediately, and I'm glad to say it hasn't lost its magic. Aside from the title screen music, which I do find quite annoying, the remastered soundtrack was a great touch. I know many aren't that fond of it compared to the original one, but to me, those melodies bring such great memories, and the funeral dirge bgm is honestly amazing with that choir. This game was always fun to me as a kid, but as an adult, I'm simply amazed by how complex it actually can get. Managing stress and fatigue, combination seasonings, drugs, growth stages, all the new things I ignored at that time have pulled me even more than before. I'm quite glad it came back to life.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who lived on Monster Rancher as a kid, I fully admit that I am biased. I know I love this game, but the reasons I love the games are why I think others will love them as well. It's true that the graphics are largely the same as the originals - though it does seem like there's some smoothing, at least, and unlike every attempt at emulation I've made over the years, MR1 doesn't break random layers and the font is actually fully readable. This is what it is - a port of an old game with bugfixes and updates to make up for the lack of CD availability in modern day. It isn't, however, a lazy port; there are legitimate bugs that could stop you from getting unlocks or end up with items stuck in your inventory forever now fixed. There is also more variety added, with boss monsters previously inaccessible now being trainable as well as variations in generation that never existed before. I suppose not removing - or making removable - the phone buttons IS lazy, and they get points docked for that, but the underlying fixes and port in general are still good enough as to warrant a recommend.I truly hope this is KT dipping their toes into the franchise for bringing it back; I would love to see proper ports of 3 and 4, as neither works *quite* right on emulation. It's a rather unique series - most stat sims tend to be buried in dating sims, and having one where you raise and fight monsters is satisfying. It's a niche that needs more entries, and I hope that we get them. Until then though, despite the admittedly dated graphics (although I love the sprites in MR1 still, hah), it's still an extremely solid sim with a LOT of life.One thing I'll say is definitely go into it blind if you're new; looking up optimum training regimens and unlocks will seem extremely daunting at first until you learn how the game works, and it takes away the fun of exploration to have it all laid out in front of you. At least, uh, until you want to unlock beaclons. Screw doing that on your own. It's dumb.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: No resolution options but you have borderless full screen. Works great on Steam Deck, but you'll want to swap 'A' and 'B' buttons in the controller configuration menu for the game before you boot. Maybe wait for a sale. I saw a streamer play this game and wanted to play it for myself from how much fun I saw from the game. Before this remastered re-release happened, I was already looking at playing Monster Rancher 2 on original hardware, however from my experience collecting old video games, Playstation 1 games are one of the 3 main pillars of pain to collect for when you're on a budget as a vast amount of Playstation 1's library is incredibly expensive. Luckily this re-release package deal for not only Monster Rancher 2 exists, but it also includes the first Monster Rancher as well as their respective manuals, but on Koei Tecmo's website...For the most part I played Monster Rancher 2, so a lot of my review will be based around it. First off, if you want to change your resolution, you must go through the launcher which allows you to select which Monster Rancher game you want to play, however the resolution options are the worst I've ever seen. You have a full screen option and only a 854x480 resolution choice (for context, the menu shows a drop down menu for changing the resolution but can't be selected to be changed). That's already egregious, but what's worse is that the startup settings window is stylized as a Windows 2000 application (whether that is good or bad is up to you) and simply shows bare minimum effort was put into this small portion of the game, and although there are no other resolution options, at least when you select for the game to be played in full scree, it is borderless full screen so that's good. These are my gripes with this version of the game and they end here at simply "start up settings menu sucks and is bare bones."I went ahead and also played this version of Monster Rancher 2 on Steam Deck (while also comparing it to the PC version) and I believe MR 1&2 DX is completely Steam Deck compatible. No display issues, no sound quality issues, nothing of real note other than the control scheme for the buttons which they use on PC as well. I recommend swapping A and B around if you're using a Xbox controller or a Switch controller for this game because it seems those inputs are hard coded to be in those positions. Simply swapping them makes playing MR2 a lot more organic. Other than a minor control scheme change, everything plays great! MR 1&2 DX should get a Steam Deck Verified icon at some point in the future unless I've missed something catastrophic that prevents it from getting verified.I want to note one this before finishing this review, and it's the weird icons that are to the left and right sides of the screens while playing either one of the MR games, and doing some bare minimum research, I found that there were mobile ports of the first two Monster Rancher games. I have no idea if the Monster Rancher games used in this re-release are those same mobile ports as those mobile ports are, to my knowledge, Japan exclusives and I cannot find any footage, discussions, or even any screenshots that are floating around the net. I'm not saying that the games used were from mobile builds of the same games, but I want to bring attention that these icons are far too familiar (and also functional) to many other mobile ported games that have on screen press-able buttons. However if anyone has more information about this, please let me know as I'd like to know more whether or not if my assumption is correct or not.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever played a Monster Rancher game before, you know what to expect here. This is a perfectly serviceable port of Monster Rancher 1&2. No, the resolution isn't even 1080p, but I'm not playing Monster Rancher for the graphical fidelity. It runs well, it plays well, it works the way I would want it to. I'm very happy with it, and I hope my money helps convince them there's demand for a new Monster Rancher game in the future.If you haven't played a Monster Rancher before, the start's as good of a place to jump in as any! Far from being a Pokemon clone, the series focuses on raising a single monster at a time to be the best it can, retiring it, and fusing it with another monster you've raised to create a mega-powerful super monster. It's fun to see what you'll get from the various CDs you choose to use to create a monster from (now a database rather than actually using physical media, but honestly? I get the same kind of fun out of it). While the gameplay is definitely somewhat repetitive, it also has that just-one-more-month appeal as you schedule, raise and battle through your monster's lifespan.Give it a shot! If you like making numbers go up and battling weird-looking monsters, you'll have a good time.

This was a re-release and not a remaster, I know, but I feel like they definitely could have spruced things up a bit more in the graphics department. They also could have put more effort into making sure the dialogue made sense. My biggest gripe, however, is the fact that there isn't a slider to adjust the sound. I'm not sure what they were thinking just using a toggle switch and it's the main thing that I wish could get fixed. I do not need clown music blasting into my ears every time I go to town. Overall, I do really enjoy the games! I have a lot of fun and get really into raising every monster I take back to the ranch. _childDocuments_.review: So i would like to give people a honest review of this vs the ps1 versionLets get the negatives out the way first.First of all this is not a remaster its a port disguised as a remaster this has bothered me when they call this a remaster when in reality the models look as if they just had anti aliasing put up to the max to smooth pixels and made the music HD rather then redoing any of it to a remastered quality.The monster cards looks as if they just copied and pasted from the ps1 version i am assuming they ran out of time launching this and was on crunch time because taking new photos and sticking them on a card for the system to utilise as the new card surely should not that that much effort.The music has a bug where it wont loop properly or change and you will get dead silence in combat kind of destroying the immersion.No remote play that is odd because this game would look as if it would work very well with a remote play even if it was a special one that allowed both players to control their monsters as the online only allows AI control.Okay now onto corrections needed for steam.Steam why is there no multiplayer label this game does have multiplayer also why cant you add to allow it to have remote play literately playing this game is a must have with controllers. Now for the positives.If you love nostalgia your going to love this game as it brings back all those memory's from monster rancher 2 from the good old PS1 era if this game is ever on sale 100% buy it as this game works very nicely on the steam deck.If your craving a monster battler with more complexity compare to like Pokemon for example this game i would even call it the dark souls of monster battlers due to your monster can in fact die if you fail to train it correctly or allow it to be critically hit in battle its the first game where forfeiting is a core mechanic nothing worst then losing your handwork to a critical hit killing your monster out right.Also its the first game i think when it comes to monster training that address the concept of life spans and death that will make you sad when you find out your training routine was too harsh on your buddy and reduced its life span to a fraction of what they should have.Overall if you view this as a port and your more in for the challenge harsh punishments for messing up as well as the reward for succeeding to feel like you accomplished something great i would say give this game a go but if you was expecting a remaster and you don't like the idea you can be punished i would say give this game a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I imagine these were fun for other people back in the day, but now its extremely dated. I'm not talking about the graphics, but the game's nightmarish grinding system, combined with super obscure mechanics (that pretty much force you to look up a guide that spoils the entire game for you). The game is mainly watching unskippable cutscenes to watch your monster's stat numbers go up, fight in tournaments with absurd RNG difficulty, and eventually having to repeat (almost) everything over again once your monster either randomly dies from being knocked out, or hits its age time limit (which this remake makes even worse than the original US releases apparently). It's definitely kinda unique, but it's a slog to play through and apparently there's not really much different as you progress. The combat's weird and janky, and I feel the main draw of this game is just that it has a lot of 3D models for monster combinations.Also some of the monster designs are sorta... questionable I've gotta say.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by clarifying; this is not a bad game. The reason I don't recommend the purchase it's due mostly to it's age and overall gameplay quality and how a broad audience might receive it.This is a menu navigation game.Very little actual "playing" is involved here. Most of what you're doing is scheduling rest or exercise and watching numbers increase. Only a very small amount of this game is adventuring or fighting and even then the adventuring is kinda clunky and the fighting wasn't great even before this port made it worse.HOWEVER!There is a charm to be found here. Raising your monster can be enjoyable. And this isn't your typical RPG where you just get the numbers up high enough to ROFL-stomp the main villain and then it's over. It is exactly what it's advertised as, raise monsters and try to bring out their full potential. Endlessly. If that sounds like fun feel free to borrow a friend's copy of the game or get it cheap on sale to confirm you'll enjoy it, and don't feel bad if you don't. This hasn't aged well.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest games for the PS1 and now finally ported to the PC. I couldn't recommend this game more. Great gameplay, great graphics, great music, tons of complexity and variety that keeps you entertained forever. It's one of those games that have tons of things to unlock, before people had to pay to unlock content in games, we used to unlock things by playing, experimenting, and of course, reading guides online (and to fully experience this game you have to read guides online, trust me).Monster Rancher 2 is all about getting the bigger number, but the way to do it is very complex. You can spend ages playing and reading about this game and you still find out something new here and there. It's the perfect game for those who enjoy a subtle grind that doesn't even feel like grinding because of how fun it is. If I am going to praise this game for one thing in particular, its the quality of its animations, full of personality. Treating your monster badly legit makes you feel bad, and vice versa. I could not love this game more, definitely in my PS1's top 5 (maybe first place). The best part about this port is that it uses Steam Cloud, so all your unlocked stuff is safe when you feel like playing it years after you got bored with it (and I know I did many times).Give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original as a kid, but I always wanted to. I was excited when I heard that it was being brought to steam, but as mentioned by others it just feels like a mobile port. And a bit of a lazy one at that.The UI is clearly designed for mobile users. Bars and buttons on either side of the screen, and, for some baffling reason, only partial controller support. The buttons on either side of the screen aren't generally mapped to anything on the controller forcing you to use the mouse even when using a controller, which feels like the right way to play old console games, to me, at least.Graphics are what you would expect from a PSX game. Which is either good or bad, depending on your preference, but I would have enjoyed touch ups to the old graphics personally. (They are probably upscaled, maybe they did work on them, but it doesn't seem so to me.)Gameplay is actually pretty fun overall. If you're not into monster raising then obviously you're not going to enjoy this game. But if so, this will scratch an itch. It's grindy as it can be, and unfortunately the game doesn't really give you much info to go on. The internet has your back on that, but if you don't want to keep alt tabbing or reading a guide on a second monitor then you'll probably find it a bit annoying.Personally I don't recommend it, but I do enjoy seeing the classics brought to the modern day. Sadly, this port feels like someone found the source code on an old computer in storage, whipped up a mobile port and then released it on PC and Switch as well. It was close, but it missed the mark in my opinion.Happy Ranching!

_childDocuments_.review: I was transported to a farway planet to a place where monsters rule, I played the game like an Ace now we're in this place to save the monster from the evil Mu!Okay 90's nostalgia aside, this is a great game.. a Tamagotchi for adults. And it is for adults, sexual themes, death, realistic consequences, and a difficult curve that will infuriate you (The grind is real)I recommend this game, but I also recommend knowing what you're getting into.This game will seem familiar to many who remember the cartoon that ran alongside Pokemon on Kids WB.The show gave many false impressions of what the game is like. First of all, know that this is not Pokemon. While the show adopted many themes from Pokemon in order to cash in on its popularity, the game is not a Pokemon ripoff or knockoff in anyway. Outside of it being about monsters fighting, they're nothing alike. (To say Pokemon and Monster Rancher are the same thing because they're about Monster Fights would be like saying Hotel Transylvania and The Lost Boys are the same because they both have Vampires)Pokemon is a child-friendly experience about catching all the pokemon and forming permanent bonds with your favorites.Monster Rancher has you picking out one monster and trying to raise it to be as strong as you can in order to win prizes. Your bond will not be permanent as monsters have limited lifespans. The game will warn you to retire a monster (by freezing it), and major progress will be made by fusing retired monsters together to create stronger monsters.The pacing is rather slow, but the gameplay and grind can be quite addictive.This collection includes two games, the first has 20 monster types, and the second has 38 (17 of the monster types from the first game, and 21 new ones. The rejected monster types are replaced with stand-ins. Doodles are now part of Monolith, Magics are now Bajarals, and Discs are now Nitons, with the latter two having skins based on the monsters they replace)There's not much of a story, just raise the best monster and unlock all the breeds.I recommend this game for anyone who wants to piss away a lot of time while being immersed.It's definitely one of those games that looks boring, but is quite fun if you get sucked in, and hooboy, call this game Kirby cause it will suck you up.Tecmo, please port Monster Rancher 3, 4, and EVO, or better give us Monster Rancher 6!

_childDocuments_.review: . However If you are a fan and didn't want to get a PS1 and/or overpay for a used copy of these games then you'll probably have a great time.  For everyone else, it's too expensive for what feels like a straight port of the PS1 games. They can claim enhanced graphics or whatever but that's generous. It looks exactly like the old versions of FF7 you could buy on Steam. It might be somewhat better in the character models, but the backgrounds are all still awful PS1 textures. I thought I would really miss the CD swapping feature for the Monsters and...I do. But what they have in place works pretty well. I suppose it's about as good as you can get today and I'm ok with that. It does take away that moment of anticipation from the discs though, where you're waiting to see if the physical disk you had contained a "special" monster. I really love Monster Rancher and have fond memories of playing it on the PS1 in college and then playing 3&4 on the PS2. Back in the day when people would come over for parties they would go through my CDs and ask why I had sticky notes on every case with something like "Rabbit/Dino" or "Stupid Plant Caterpillar" written on them. For me it's barely worth the cost just for the nostalgia and I couldn't believe how I still remembered so many of the arena names and the music since it's easily been over 20 years since I fired up MR2.So, it's fun for me but I'm a big fan. My kids (teenagers) wanted to see this game in action as I had told them about it for years and years and they were highly unimpressed. I don't blame them. The graphics and animations make me feel old and poor when I see them. If someone showed this to me and talked about how awesome it is I would think they were out of their mind. I think that without some significant visual updates it will be hard to get anyone into this if they haven't played the series. Maybe they were banking on it mostly selling on the Switch since the highest resolution I can get is 1600x900. I suppose if you're playing it on that tiny screen it might look better? Even messing with the ini I can't get it higher than that.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: buy and play if you're a veteran of 1 and 2, or if you're determined to make it all the way through them, otherwise, there are other far more reasonable entries in monster training games to play. this title will remain on my steam list, in my library, because it's an important part of gaming history, but I don't see myself putting any more time into them.I came in to this series at the 4th game, on the PS2. I had not seen, nor played, the first 3 games until this steam port. to begin with, this appears to be a MOBILE port, which doesn't make sense to me, it's an old playstation game why would you port it to mobile and port *that* to PC when playstation 1 emulation is still strong and possible? but that's a comparatively petty issue I have.the larger issue is the lack of a CD reading system, and a lack of a reliable music library to search. I can only assume it wants you to search by *song* titles and band names rather than album like it says ON THE STEAM PAGE. further more, I tried famous albums, I tried famous songs, by well known artists over and over and came up with 0 results EVERY time, finally, I hit the random button and . . . . I'm not even sure most of these bands names are written in english at all, much less who the hell they are.so, using the random option, I finally get a monster for both games and start getting into the game itself, and realize that it's in no way as refined or friendly to new players as the 4th entry is even once you get past the problem of not being able to just rip from CDs you actually have (yes I know, most people no longer have a CD tray on their PC, but you have to accept the HUGE liability with completely removing that and using your OWN library for monster data), and once I have my monster, and  take it to my ranch, I find out about the RNG. both games have what seems, at least at this early stage, to be VERY unfair RNG. be it for the training, or the tournaments the RNG seems entirely stacked against you. And you only earn money from tournaments in 2, and from work and tournaments in 1, and the money that cmes in from work is a TINY sum compared to the ammount for winning a tournament, but good luck winning a tournament.both of which also have a month long hard core training regimen for your monster that has a HUGE pricetag that takes winning at least a D rank tourney to earn, yes, WINNING the tournament because if you win a D rank, you get 1,000 plus some bonus . . . . get second place and you earn about 350. _childDocuments_.review: Once more, I crawl out from under my comfortable rock to get a steam badge.At least this review will be an easy one for me, as this just seems to be a mostly accurate re-release of a game I spent literal days of my life not only directly playing, but digging through my father's CD collection in order to create monsters with.  If anything, some degree of my quite varied tastes in music might have stemmed from conversations he and I would have about the various artists whose work I was popping into my PSX.  Coupling that together with the genuine attachment I would feel for these creatures that I would raise from infancy, it actually can reach you on an even more emotional level than something like Pokemon, or even ARK despite the latter's growth mechanics.  These games would make me question how harshly or softly to raise a creature for more than the mere mechanics.  I would actually feel personally -guilty- if I felt I was too strict on a monster, or even wondering if being too lax was actual a detriment to their long term potential, as if they actually cared on some level about how successful they would be in combat.In shorter terms, I would put more thought and care into my relationship with these colorful pixels than I would with peers from school I interacted with every day.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Monster Rancher fan, my play time doesn't calculate all of the save files I've messed around with in the two games in both their original releases and the Japanese Switch port prior to DX's release. This release, in particular, is a very good one (bar one bugged tournament, the New Years Cup in MR2 when played on Fast Forward), featuring many quality of life changes. While lifespan for all of the monsters is still shorter by 100 weeks compared to the original English version, the rest of the changes more than make up for that. This features the Swim Bug fix, 20 freezer spots for monsters, unlimited shrine usage (was limited in base MF1&2 Switch), a fast forward/2x speed mode, the Pocketstation minigame, and works great with the fanmade Advanced Viewer. Now, for a review with previous fans less in mind. Monster Rancher 1 and 2 are raising simulators where each action takes time and has effects on a monster's overall lifespan and disposition. Your goal is to train monsters to fight, unlock other monsters, and, eventually, combine them to make stronger baby monsters to repeat the process. Fights are done in a tournament styled system, all Round Robin in MR1, with an additional Bracket Style introduced in MR2. The battle system typically has a fight running on a 60 second clock (3 minutes in errantry fights) with monsters moving on a 2D plane split into 4 distance types. Each distance has its own techs (moves) a monster can use with its own guts cost. Battles have increased dynamics due to the guts system acting as a cost for attacks, leading to things like guts correction, which make it safer to wait out attacks to make them stronger. The person with the higher percentage of life/HP at the end of the match wins!Over time, you will find out which monsters you prefer raising, what methods are worth using, and which techs are worth spending lifespan over. Monster Rancher 1 feels like Monster Rancher 2's prototype in many ways, but, even there, the cute sprite work makes it worth your while. Now go out there and raise some Worms!

_childDocuments_.review: I was in my early 20s when the first Monster Rancher came out. I spent hundred, if not thousands of hours playing it and its sequel. You can't skip the training animations, the skip feature was from the U.S. release and this is based off of the Japanese one. There seem to be some new monsters and I notice that the monsters you unlock from cd's differ from the old PSX versions, at least some of the unique ones that were attached to certain albums. Thats not really a complaint, just an observation. They did a good job with the upscaling and some modern conveniences. The mouse actually works great for most of the interface although I am still using the controller if I decide to manually fight.I rarely buy games directly from Steam but this really deserves some support. There is a lot of gameplay here. Not a whole lot of main story, work your way up to the top. Its the exploration missions, and little events that pop up and special matches you can aim for that add so much to it. This is a great game that deserves a modern sequel. Between the Monster Rancher series and the Deception series, Tecmo made some of the funnest games with the best replay value during that era. If you liked these in the past, this is probably the best way to play it now if you want to generate a variety of monsters.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a set of old games, from 1997 and 1999 respectively. I tried Monster Rancher 1 and couldn't stand how lacking it was compared to 2, so I can only speak about 2. The biggest difference between the original and this, if my friend that has emulated the game is to be believed, is the overall speed of the game. The cutscenes, the text boxes, and most significantly, the fights. All of these are at least twice as fast as the original. This is a good thing, since the game can get a bit repetitive as you're raising your monster.I highly recommend using a controller, not mouse and keyboard.Pros and cons of the game if you haven't played it before:PROS*It's an ambitious foray into the (then new) Pokemon genre, monster training. The gameplay is not at all close to Pokemon, but that's the closest equivalent I have. There's a great amount of detail, a lot to learn. Many monster types, many moves, many things to unlock.*Your assistant trainer, Colt, has an interesting and dynamic personality. It's going to quickly become clear that this is a Japanese game translated (occasionally awkwardly) into English. But in spite of that, the assistant trainer is memorable and a large part of what makes the game great.CONS*It's an old game and the graphics haven't really been revamped. That might be a shock to you if you haven't seen Playstation 1 era graphics before.*It can get repetitive and you might not know what you're doing at some point. Fortunately, there are plenty of detailed online resources to help.Two resources I can recommend, one new and one old:This is old GameFAQ, originally from 2006 but there have been updates to it since then, the latest of which was in 2019. A lot of detailed and very useful information. I didn't have a great combining result with my CrabSaurian, stats wise, but other than that I have nothing but good things to say about the guide.This is a modern resource of how to unlock each of the (many) locked monsters. That will take a good amount of time if you want to do all of them. The website also has a good many other resources on it, including an in-depth guide on combining monsters  Very, very useful!My guess is you're either going to like the game a lot or not at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely ENTHRALLED to see this port of a childhood favorite make its way overseas.For those finding their way here without former knowledge, Monster Rancher is a game in which you, surprise surprise, raise monsters. Your goal is to claw your way from the bottom to the top ranks, managing your monsters' health and stats as you enter them into tournaments to fight. It's much more about managing stats of one specific creature than other monster-oriented games that were released at the time, and there's a bit of a learning curve it you're jumping in blind. These elements really set it apart and make it feel much more personal than the rest, even without its once iconic method of obtaining your various beasts via real world CDs.The only real disappointment is just how low-effort this port is. It was designed for mobile first and foremost, with touch control buttons on either side of the window at all times, even if you're playing with keyboard/controller. There have been no optimizations to visuals, so you'll sometimes see holes in the models and the like. The games are LOUD, with no option to adjust the volume in-game. The names of the windows are even unchanged from their japanese counterparts. It is the absolute bare minimum, with the only change being to the monster generation system, which was more of a necessity for the games being ported to mobile than anything else. But I'll state again, I'm glad to have gotten a localization of this extremely niche franchise at all. Monster Rancher is a fantastic time, and offers an incredibly unique experience I've never encountered before or since, and I'd highly recommend giving these games a try if they pique your interest! I'd be overjoyed to see these games not only succeed, but also communicate to Koei Tecmo that maybe, just maybe, a new entry in this long dormant franchise would be a worthwhile endeavor.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with Monster Rancher 2 as a kid, kinda sucks that you were never able to generate and raise Enemy Monsters without a cheating device on the original version for the Playstation, but... NOW YOU CAN! At least in this port anyway, thanks to the online database. But the problem is, you can only generate them after encountering them in Errantries or in the case of White Mocchi and White Suezo, the Legend Cup, but that's after you've beaten the Major 4 with a single monster. Anyway, if you enjoyed the Monster Rancher anime and the 2 games for the Playstation, I recommend buying this wonderful masterpiece. You will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: My review is positive but let me explain some things first.Monster rancher 2 is easily emulated, and the competitive scene has been alive for awhile, and modding the game to 'hard mode' for better balancing. -DX does not offer mod support as it stands which is disappointing.-DX fixes some glitches then creates some more, like audio bugs and the game crashing sometimes when joining the New Year Cup.-DX rebalenced the AI so they no longer wait until 45 guts to attack. This changes the game a bit for good and bad.Why should you buy DX then?- Play with friends easily. You can't both control your monsters, but AI vs. AI has always been the bog standard. - Tecmo mentioned patching the game. Hopefully this game will be bug free.- If you have never played monster rancher it is such a great game. Basic in concept, a lot under the hood. This is a great introduction to the series, and if you are considering competitive, a lot more people are switching held tournaments to DX for the sake of it's popularity.It's a good game. I am no where near being done playing the game and the joy I get is always worth it. 8/10. Nice casual game to run while talking to friends or multitasking. With all your committed brainpower this old stone is a hidden gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Obvious mobile port but haven't noticed any major issues except for you being unable to skip training animations. You can toggle a fast forward function in the menu so effectively it's the same though.As for the games themselves, it's a monster training game with a little more simulator aspects like monster stamina and feeding requirements than your average monster game. It's hardly overbearing though. What really set Monster Rancher apart really was the fact you created monsters from CDs you had laying around the house. The ports effectively can't replicate that so instead you input a song/soundtrack and artist now and it generates a monster based on that. As just an example, I used Linkin Park's Hybird Theory to get a bunny girl. Then I created a demonic Wolf using Gorillaz's Demon Days. It's a fun little way to further personalize your favorite music. As far as I can tell there isn't much new to the ports except an autosave, so for me the purchase was a matter of convenience to access the games with little set up.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX

I love it they added the new job feature, which helps one get additional in-game incomes.The only things the game is lacking of and I would like they to add in future updates, is the compatibility with a PlayStation controller, as well as the "skip" feature for the errantry training stages the original game had.Keep up the good work and thanks again!!!

I hope that the game will meet it's market goals so that we can see further remasters and perhaps even future games! I hope that you enjoy these games as much as I do!

_childDocuments_.review: To the people that played this game in the past... It is just as you remember it. Some things a little different, like how you get monsters, but otherwise the same classic game is there. It is an absolute blast!To those who have never played it, capturing the magic that those of us who have played it in the past may be a bit difficult. Generating monsters, is still fun, but not nearly the same as rifling through all you're parents CDs trying to find something cool. Combat is basic and at times can be frustrating, there are a lot of mechanics that the game does not really explain. Raising monsters is fun, but once you figure out a solid method, it can become tedious. Is it worth 30 bucks? To fans of the series trying to have fun with the game again, absolutely. To new comers, it can be, but i would recommend watching a video or two just so you know what you are getting into.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game when I was a kid. Playing it again as an adult and you know what.. it still holds up. Super solid monster raising/battling game. You get a monster which you take to your ranch. You feed it, you train it, go on adventures with it, fight in tournaments with it, then it dies, then you cry. After all that then you will take a new monster and do it all again with that one! This game is both very simple and also very complex. There are a TON of under the hood mechanics that you may never even know about unless you really dive into it. But it can also be played casually and you can just look at it like a fun monster raising simulator. Even by modern standards this game is quite fun IMO. As for the quality of the port? It's just ok. It gets the job done and is playable. I would have liked better resolution options or just more options in general but that is probably my biggest issue with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX

_childDocuments_.review: A Great remaster of the original games. It plays well, and so far has had no crashes, or bugs. Its keybinds are fully customizable, and work on both controller and kb + m. There are also full mouse control should you want to be lazy with that, but those controls are sometimes awkward in a fight. Stick with a controller if possible (it is what the game was designed for). The side buttons shown are neat shortcuts to get to monster data quickly, which can be helpful. I will be playing this game for many hours, even if I am already S rank in 5 hours in Monster Rancher 1. I am hopeful this will bring a resurgence to the franchise, and we get the Monster Rancher 4 remaster that was teased at TGS this year.

_childDocuments_.name: Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game a ton as a kid, and while I'm really enjoying the game I wish there were a few things that were different.1.) The autosave feature is awesome and saves a ton of time, so other quality of life features like buying multiples of certain items at once would have been a very welcome addition.2.) Sadly as of right now there is no way to skip ahead during training sessions, I think this isn't intentional as you can still skip the cut scenes for errantries, but its something that needs to be looked at regardless.3.) Controller binding and the ability to disable that blinding light that appears whenever you click on something using the mouse would be nice as well.All in all I'm just happy to have this game available, it is nice that the game has been re balanced and some of the bugs have been fixed as well. I love that we have a VS mode online, and I like how they adjusted the Shrine so you can still have some semblance of mystery around getting random monsters. As of right now I'd recommend this to fans of the series, but for a newcomer some of these design choices might seem archaic and time consuming. Hopefully they continue to adjust and patch this.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is well worth the value, and a lot of fun. If you're new to the series and wondering what a "monster rancher" is, well it's really it's own unique game - so if you're imaging some pokemon 1v1 it's much more like 1 on 1 time with your favourite 'mon. I'm so glad it's back and hope this will inspire more games. I played this game extensively as a kid and was worried the remake might not be as great as I remembered, now that I'm coming back with an adult's eyes. Let me tell you - I played 11 hours straight today and it was a blast. The new shrine feature to replace CDs had me spending and hour just searching favourite songs, popular songs and meme songs alone. Its every bit the game I remember with some small QoL improvements. I played with a ps4 controller and apart from some small adjustments the new controls have it was like a time machine into one of the funnest ps1 games that will just eat your time without you noticing!

_childDocuments_.review: Ahh one of my personal favorite game! Was pleasantly surprised that it was ported to the PC out of the blue. Monster Rancher and Digimon are my 2 fav franchises for the PS1 days, I still have them on all my devices to play with emulators today.Concept of the game is pretty simple, take care, train and raise your monster, compete in tournaments for cash and glory, go on expeditions when it comes up, send your monster to errantry to gain bonus stats, learn new skills and even encounter wild monsters of varying strengths.What makes the game unique is the ability to summon new monsters using CDs if you are playing with the PS1 version, this port changes that mechanic to search for songs online instead and uses the songs to generate the monsters. You could also combine 2 monsters into a new monster or even use the disk items in combination to set them to become a specific monster.There are also a number of improvements made to the port like far shorter loading times, better music quality (i think?), part-time job and I think they improved some of the sprites.All in all, I just love MR1, 2 and the card battle game. Very happy to see it ported officially to PC, hoping to see more ports and hopefully more improvements and addons to them in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Rancher 2 is an absolute classic, one that I've been playing regularly for 20 years, and this new port to PC with Monster Rancher 1&2 DX is solid overall. The bug fixes and small mechanical improvements present are very much welcome, though some of the minor technical details of the PC port are questionable (like the buttons intended for the mobile version being visible when they are not needed for controller users). For full details check out my video review for Niche Gamer (pre-release copy was provided by Koei Tecmo.)

If you haven't I would suggest giving it a shot!

My only issue is that there's no way to control the volume inside the game itself, but that is such a minor nitpick because guys it's here and it's good and it's everything I've been hoping for these past ten years ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ <3

The beloved series makes its triumphant return with Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX, bringing together the wildly popular simulation games – Monster Rancher and Monster Rancher 2 – all in one amazing collection. name: Starfield
detailed_description: STARFIELD DIGITAL PREMIUM EDITION Premium Edition includes: Starfield Base Game Shattered Space Story Expansion (upon release) 1,000 Creation Credits Constellation Skin Pack: Equinox Laser Rifle, Spacesuit, Helmet and Boost Pack Access to Starfield Digital Artbook & Original Soundtrack Buzz About the Game Starfield is the first new universe in over 25 years from Bethesda Game Studios, the award-winning creators of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim and Fallout 4. In this next generation role-playing game set amongst the stars, create any character you want and explore with unparalleled freedom as you embark on an epic journey to answer humanity’s greatest mystery. In the year 2330, humanity has ventured beyond our solar system, settling new planets, and living as a spacefaring people. You will join Constellation – the last group of space explorers seeking rare artifacts throughout the galaxy – and navigate the vast expanse of space in Bethesda Game Studios’ biggest and most ambitious game. Tell Your story In Starfield the most important story is the one you tell with your character. Start your journey by customizing your appearance and deciding your Background and Traits. Will you be an experienced explorer, a charming diplomat, a stealthy cyber runner, or something else entirely? The choice is yours. Decide who you will be and what you will become. Explore Outer Space Venture through the stars and explore more than 1000 planets. Navigate bustling cities, explore dangerous bases, and traverse wild landscapes. Meet and recruit a memorable cast of characters, join in the adventures of various factions, and embark on quests across the Settled Systems. A new story or experience is always waiting to be discovered. Captain the Ship Of Your Dreams Pilot and command the ship of your dreams. Personalize the look of your ship, modify critical systems including weapons and shields, and assign crew members to provide unique bonuses. In deep space you will engage in high-stakes dogfights, encounter random missions, dock at star stations, and even board and commandeer enemy ships to add to your collection. Discover, Collect, Build Explore planets and discover the fauna, flora, and resources needed to craft everything from medicine and food to equipment and weapons. Build outposts and hire a crew to passively extract materials and establish cargo links to transfer resources between them. Invest these raw materials into research projects to unlock unique crafting recipes. Lock and Load Space can be a dangerous place. A refined combat system gives you the tools to deal with any situation. Whether you prefer long-range rifles, laser weapons, or demolitions, each weapon type can be modified to complement your playstyle. Zero G environments add a chaotic spectacle to combat, while boost packs give players freedom to maneuver like never before.

_childDocuments_.review: This would best be described as "Chinese Balder's Gate". It's a western style RPG created by Chinese Devs set in the warring states period. Despite having no childhood memories I'm having a blast, and it's killing me to give this a thumbs down.The problem is that to there are both graphical issues and performance issues that need to be solved. While you can find the solutions on the forums, it took me a full hour of tweaking to get it playable. Even now, there's alot of jank that is just frustrating enough to detract from the experience. Unless you are willing to put in the time to fix it and deal with minor continued tech problems...  it's not even worth a deep discount sale.Past that, the translation is pretty bad along with distractedly awful Voice Overs. That said, it's generally playable and you can generally tell where to go, what to do and what you need to know. There's just a few questions such as "Is Shoot Rate your accuracy for melee weapons?" or chuckles like "Are you sure you want to overlay your save file". From here, this it's all uphill. From here, I'd genuinely say that this is a fantastic game and if the first issues don't scare you away you have amazing game here.The plot is about a prince who was ordered to kill himself for crimes against his father. He decides to ignore the order until he has confronted his father only to find himself in the middle of a conspiracy to eliminate all the heirs to the throne. You travel the land trying to punish those responsible, evade the law and protect the innocent people caught in the middle.There are tons of quests to complete, many with multiple paths or at least results. You'll be able to recruit several heroes, collect unique equipment and treasures, and decide what kind of a ruler you want to become. This game also features a crafting system that would still be considered innovative today. The materials that you collect can have their level of quality and special bonuses that they offer. The items you craft are a direct result of the ingredients that you use. If you want to build a fire sword, collect ingredients that offer bonuses to FIRE and hopefully also are high enough quality for strong base stats. The crafting is more than a raw numbers game and leads to a really cool system that I haven't seen before.Combat falls somewhere directly between Diablo and Balder's Gate. It feels faster and less RNG than a traditional Tabletop RPG but still has just enough stats and skills to make you feel unique. Enemy actions tend to be more interesting than D&D also as wolves will howl to alert nearby allies or lunge at you to move out position and dodge your attacks. They revolve around a much more action game style than traditional RPG.This does lead to some frustrations as some enemies don't stay still long enough for your characters to hit them or enemies running away leading to long boring chases.  The ideas are fantastic and absolutely add to the game, but aren't perfect. Overall, I played this odd-looking game on a whim and I'm glad I did. Of all the western RPGs I'd played, I'd put this near the top in terms of raw enjoyment. But the hoops you have to jump through are enough trouble that 9/10 players won't enjoy the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to recommend this game generally, but it's a good nostalgia tour if you happened to get to play this game around the era it was released in. I want to say this game came with a random bundle pack my mom picked up somewhere not knowing what made for a good PC game, and as much as my modern tastes here have let me down, the game is better than you might guess. That said, modern tastes have spoiled me and the game mechanics are not great for the single player campaign at least. It's playable, and the historical fiction set in Fantasy china is cool, but like Kong Gang the muscleman, that concept does a disproportionate amount of the weight carrying. If I'm being honest, this game would probably play a lot better if it were a tactical turn based battle, like XCOM, since a lot of the clunkiness is just from clicking around and your party walking to an enemy then doing a few laps around them before doing anything useful. I find I often have to pause, select each character individually and queue up actions and then unpause and let things run for a few seconds. The astute among you will recognize this is turn based battle with extra steps - but your mileage my vary.The dialog options are full of cultural stuff that I think gets lost in translation, so you might struggle playing through the game without a walkthrough on a second screen to refer to when the morality checks don't make much sense to westerners, and to be honest I don't actually mind this. It would have been a disservice to localize it, and for better or worse, we're getting a better approximation of someone's interpretation of period specific Chinese culture.If you've played this game decades ago, grab it and play it until you can't be bothered to finish. If you're a big fan of ARPGs and don't mind fighting the UI and can get this on a decent sale, try it out. Otherwise, maybe if you're interested, watch a play through online somewhere and be like "oh wow, that was a neat little project that someone made over 20 years ago".

As from what I could read up there is China only version that has the widescreen support patch and couple other fixes (I think you can buy it on steam for like $1 by searching 秦殇 steam on google).  As for the game itself, it's Diablo 2 with a twist that you can have multiple characters that will vanish on their demise, so you will play it safer for a while and grind up some "lower level" mobs to just be that bit stronger. Story is a okay, there are some twists and turns, but for the time it's a good one. Controls tend to be a bit clunky, like main character moving somehow way faster than everyone else, mobs glitching in a weird way, or PC's moving around and taking a ton of damage to just try and hit that one enemy. Ye it takes a patience and a guide to get some things in Story Mode, but I would rather take a friend and play MP so you can create your own character and not be forced to play the main character. If you like older diablo clones, it's a fine one, and if you are looking for another "asian based arpg" blade and sword is one I played as a kid and is fine too.

name: ASTLIBRA Revision
detailed_description: If you haven't purchased ASTLIBRA Revision yet ASTLIBRA Revision is a quite an unique game. We recommend you play the public demo first (it is just above the Add to Cart button) before deciding whether to purchase it. The demo provides full Prologue and Chapter One content, as well as a demostration of late-game battle systems. It takes 1-2 hours to complete. Have fun! About the Game Join our Discord Server Travel Through Unfamiliar WorldsExplore a vast, dangerous, yet beautiful world. Broken up through multiple chapters, join the protagonist and Karon, his talking bird companion, as they confront time and fate. Back to The Golden Age Of JRPGs, with Side-scrolling Action Slashing, Smashing, thrusting countless enemies while building up stamina for powerful Possession Skills, which are enough to melt away anything that blocks your way, including huge bosses that could take half, or even more of the screen. Fight aggressively while thinking strategically, always pick up the most trust worthy equipment, and select the best suited skills to deal with ever changing circumstances. Fight God-Like Boss Battles Battle ferocious bosses throughout the story, each with their own set of attacks and challenges. Upgrading abilities and acquiring new skills are vital to finishing each battle and progressing through the protagonist’s story. Multiple Ways to Build Your Character A warrior mastered ranged combat with bows and throwing knives? A mage smashing enemies with staffs and cast magic at the same time? Play it in your way. Gathering experience to level up, collecting force to grow up, forging and mastering equipment to open up more tactical options. Combat and Story, Why Choose When You Can Enjoy Both 14 years in development and more than 1 year for revision, award-winning indie developer KEIZO gave his all into this work. The plot keeps twisting as characters growing in an ever expanding world; Classic themes like time travel and tons of spoilers are all custom-made with the developer's own style. In ASTLIBRA, Story elements are often made into game mechanics, for example, your soul-mate Karon is not just a sidekick to talk with. Fruitful Endgame with Even More Challenges With 6 difficulty options, all kinds of players can enjoy the combat system at their own pace, but no one can finish all those contents casually - even after you 'beat' the game, the Postscript after Final Chapter will provide extra story, new adventure and fresh system, tapping the potential of skills, equipment, as well as your imagination.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Astlibra Revision is an excellent 2D action RPG, with a meaty main storyline and a substantial amount of post-game content. Set aside 50+ hours for completion, though it's an easy game to get back into if you can only play it in short spurts. The main combat system is quite robust and fun, which makes the grindy parts enjoyable. The storyline is interesting, exploring a number of interesting themes around time travel and the existence of parallel universes. I found the high school humour detracted a bit from the emotional impact of the story, as did the rough translation, but not to the point where playing the game was not a joy.  The flaws are a consequence of the game being a one man passion project and it's incredible how polished the game actually is.  While the game is linear, some backtracking is required to obtain 100% and additional grinding may be required to overcome some of the more challenging bosses. The main gameplay loop is addictive - that's the key to a great game. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Just got all the achievements (minus DLC) and I can confidently say that this is one of the best games I've played in recent years. This is definitely one of those game that I wish I could forget just to experience it again.

_childDocuments_.review: ++: Gameplay is so much fun! It's addictive and rewarding. The game pushes you to experiment with fighting styles, and as you constantly change your habits, dispatching enemies keeps feeling great. Levelling up your attributes, choosing gear is a mini-game of its own. Playing with a controller with rumble support provides great haptic feedback, it just feels good! The plot is also cool, with unexpected twists and turns, but there's an issue with it, more on it below.--: A lot of cringe-y sexual innuendos, and I mean, A LOT. Imagine every sex-related trope of Japanese games (female underwear, enormous breasts, awkward compliments from total strangers, sharing the bed with a friend of an opposite gender HINT HINT), and it's there. Almost every dialogue revolves around this or that. Who said we need to save the world? Forget it, we are going to enjoy watching a cute girl undressing because she misunderstood what was asked of her! No, seriously, it often seems the game was written by a horny teenager. The plot suffers from that greatly, it kills mood and involvement. But if you're only there for the combat, it should be ok.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: MASTERPIECE!! This game keeps on giving. I would recommend that you play it on impossible difficulty if you like soulslike games, it works very well. (It can be grindy at the start on impossible difficulty but it gets hella good and it is a decent challenge.) The backgrounds are AWESOME. Music is good. There is a good of variety of ways to fight and there is no copypasta monsters. Every zone comes with brand new mobs. It plays a bit like a metroidvania/Megaman X. Literally one of the best games I've played in a while. Anyways, if you're thinking about it, go for it!!Edit: I forgot about the story, the story is well made and is about time travelling. Main characters are all interesting and have good personalities. TLDR: Press buttons, unreal fun happens. 11/10 GOTY not even kidding.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so after getting every achievment in this game, I think I am qualified to put in my input.For starters I just wanna say I love this game. I found the story very captivating, and wanted to see what was going to happen next. I found the combat to be fun and enjoyed grinding (which is rare) the puzzles for the most part were pretty fair with some challange, with the exception of a couple that I had to look up, and I probably wouldnt have figured out on my own.I think the most controversial thing in this game are the endings, and without spoiling I wanna say I actually really loved how they went about the endings. This game will take a good chunk of time to complete, if you are an achievment hunter, I would highly reccomend starting the game on Hard Mode to get the achievment otherwise you will have to do 2 full playthroughs like I did. The story can be beaten pretty quick if you know what to do, and skip all the cutscenes, but a first time run with no knowlage can take awhile. That being said I highly would reccomend, and am hoping to get another DLC or sequel in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra Revision is a masterful blend of innovation, narrative depth, and breathtaking visuals, but Astlibra Revision is more than just a pretty face; it's a game with substance. _childDocuments_.review: This game captivated be for the better part of a whole week. Playing it alternately on my PC and Steam Deck throughout the whole week on Hard difficulty it took about 60 hours to 100% the game, without really being stuck anywhere.It's not perfect, far from it. But it was so entertaining and fun to play, I just have to recommend it.Game ran absolutely flawlessly on Deck and hardly drained the Battery.Only flaw in that regard is, that as of now the Deck automatically sets the resolution to 1280x720 and saves the resolution for when it is next started on PC, and to change it on PC the game has to be opened, resolution changed and restarted again. Little tedious.The Story was the biggest surprise. No matter how you guess the Story continues, the game throws a curveball and something completely unexpected happens. And that exact scenario happened like 15 times; just when I thought I knew what would happen the game did a sharp turn and shattered my guesses.The Combat is simple, but very fun nonetheless. You mash a lot, try to jump and dash around to avoid being hit while occasionally using items. Simple stuff, but executed very well.There are a couple flaws I want to point out though.First of all, as many said before, translations are a little weird at times. It's not unintelligible, but it's just... off at times. You will notice the weirdness here and there in the translations, but that won't stop you from understanding the Story. If you don't understand the Story, that's just because the Story is absolutely convoluted and insane (but still great), not because of any errors in translation.Also, the game feels a little stretched with a lot enemies being recycled throughout the end (last chapter).But that's it already, there isn't much else for me to negatively point out.I had a ton of fun, more fun than I had with some Triple-A Games.It certainly could profit from some improvements to the UI and its navigation as well as improved translations, but it's perfectly fun as is. If you enjoy some mild grinding and 2D Rpgs, this is probably gonna bring you some fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not be fooled by people saying this game is a generic jrpg.  The game definitely starts with some common jrpg elements such as a childhood friend, amnesia, and an animal mascot guide.  However, at the very beginning, I have never seen a jrpg story hook that starts with "and then the main character and his animal companion wanders through a seemingly endless forest for eight years."I mostly watched my girlfriend play this game since she really wanted to play it after I beat the first boss of the game, but there were a lot of elements of this game I could appreciate even just watching.  The storyline has a lot of subtle references and foreshadowing that don't seem significant, and then later it blows you away by showcasing them as central focal points of the story.  Much like Dark Souls, even small tidbits of lore you find in pages on the ground such as gods, otherworldly beings, and concepts about the world become relevent to the story.  You read about a god of war?  You actually encounter said god in the story.The way they present dialogue is also quite good and shows a particular attention to detail.  The dialogue has natural slowdowns and pauses as if the characters are actually talking, and it feels incredibly natural to read.  This takes a lot of time to attention to detail to perform itself considering how much dialogue is in the story.It's sad to say, but it has been a long time since I've seen a story with main characters who genuinely try their best.   I didn't see too much woe is me type of characterization while watching this game all the way past post game.  The attitude of everyone is generally hopeful while still having moments of heart breaking despair throughout the storyline.  There isn't any character in this story I was actively annoyed with, which is a feat because I typically find animal mascot companion characters extremely annoying (looking at you Paimon), but Karon ended up being one of the most endearing characters I genuinely cared about.The gameplay is simple and easy to get into.  There are many ways to optimize your character and instill growth from leveling up, the grow tree, balancing libra scales, equipment, mastery of equipment, customizing Karon skills, enhancing scale pans, enhancing equipment, setting scale boards, mastering/using different possession skills, and gaining new techniques.  The game encourages you to use and collect every piece of equipment (except accessories) since mastering equipment grants you magic crystals to use more Karon skills or gives you a new Karon skill entirely.  You can distribute your level up stats however you want and redistribute them however you wish very easily.  Techniques you don't want to accidentally use can even be sealed temporarily.I watched this game being played on Hell difficulty, and the beginning of the game is quite difficult but becomes more manageable as you continue playing.  Enemies are not to be taken lightly on the hardest difficulty you can play when you start up the game, you can die typically within a few hits.  However, there are a lot of systems in place to mitigate damage, but none of them are able to be used infinitely.  The backdash has a cooldown, guard has a guard gauge you have to watch, some attacks can't be guarded, and possession skills have i-frames but aren't immune to status effects (unless you equip a very expensive Karon skill) and use ST.  This game is not impossible on the hardest difficulties, but it is not easy.  Only after gaining access to specific Karon skills that boost magic power was the game starting to reach the godlike game breaking power I'm used to from most jrpgs.In the past, the game supposedly had a poor translation, however I only esperienced the game post translation edit patch.  I must say, whatever bad translation was part of the game doesn't seem to be present.  Occasionally I'll see the random grammatical error, but nothing that breaks the immersion of the game.  If you are worried about this, don't be.Atlibra Revision is an epic adventure game about a hero's journey with many twists and turns, as well as endearing characters.  The gameplay is entertaining and easy to get into with many aspects of grinding to improve your power level.  The grind is more of an equipment and item grind like Monster Hunter, the best kind of grinding.  After fifty hours of gameplay, the game still isn't done yet.  Recommended unless you don't like anime for some reason.

_childDocuments_.review: A game comes to mind when I think of Astlibra. Infinite Space. A game that I'm sure only a very select few people would even know. It was a game that really brought home what it's like to go on an adventure, think to yourself "well what could possibly top what I just experienced?", and proceed to answer that question with something even crazier and more exciting, constantly, in that same game. Likewise in Astlibra, the game kept going, and I fell deeper and deeper into its story and world. There's very few games that do this. Other examples are games from the Ys series, Labyrinth of Refrain, Octopath Traveler. It's the escalation of problems that really drives it home for me, and I've always held Infinite Space as King when it comes to that. Astlibra however almost gives it a run for its money. The story gets crazier and stranger, but it stays true to its rules and you really just want to keep playing to see what on earth happens next.On top of all that, the gameplay loop and progression is pure crack. The various mechanics to strengthen your character is very well done, and with its real-time combat, really just makes you want to keep killing ♥♥♥♥.I really can't sing many more praises than this. Astlibra will have a permanent home in my heart as one of the greatest RPGs I've ever played of all time, and I think it's the games that take up real estate in your memories that are exceptional.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game that held my full attention nearly to the end.Core gameplay is SOTN-esque combat and power growth loop, though unlike a true Metroidvania, exploration really isn't part of the game. If anything it's probably closest to something like a cross between a Ys game and Faxanadu.Story-wise, it suffers from the circumstances of its creation: the game as you'll play it was put together piece by piece over a sixteen year period, and while many people contributed to the overall project, most of it was done by just one author. In this regard it's an interesting cross-section of the author's own coming of age and their own changing priorities, hopes, and fears.Chapters are episodic in the style of an anime, replete with the jarring addition of the credits rolling at the end of every chapter. They can be inconsistent in story quality and tone: the early chapters possess a dreamlike apocalyptic tone which I loved, including the open question as to whether any of what's happening is real at all, though the middle sadly gets bogged down in pretty much every anime trope you can think of. The end tries its best to reconcile these clashes in tone while also hastening to make its point (as well as figure out what it was in the first place), while the post-script "Revision" content focuses mostly on closing plot holes and tying off loose ends.Even if it gets to be a little "spot the trope" for awhile in there, the gameplay is always solid and the central mysteries of the game remain compelling enough for even the most jaded (that's me) to stick around. And honestly, the story throws so many twists and turns at you that if you're currently rolling your eyes at one segment, everything will likely be turned on its head in the next hour anyway.Oh, and the music is uniformly fantastic, excepting maybe one track I really had no taste for. Fortunately it's only used in one place.It's up there with Crystal Project as one of my personal best. Play it!

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra is something that hardly any other game is these days. It's a finished and incredibly polished. Astlibra can easily take its place among the JRPG behemoths of the 16 bit era, and it may well be one of the best -if not THE best- JRPG ever made. The fact that this was created by a single person is simply mind blowing.Although you can still clearly feel the indie jankiness in the game, it has been polished to the degree where it just becomes its art style. At times you feel like you're playing a mid-2000s flash game that has been iterated on a million times until it was effectively a AAA release. It borrows stylistic elements from at least a dozen other successful IPs yet manages to outshine most of them in execution.While I could go on endlessly about the things Astlibra does well, let me critique the few things that it didn't. - The music is sometimes a bit of off. While overall the soundtrack has been very good, it does have weak points.- The translation work is occasionally lacking. It's not nearly as bad as it could be, but you can tell it's a game made primarily for a Japanese audience.- There is a strong focus on grinding for power. This is perfectly fine and expected in the genre, but especially towards the level 40-50 areas you are no longer expected to grind where the story takes you. If you fail to figure that out, it can feel like you're running into a brick wall.- The hardest challenges in the game effectively turn into bullet hell gameplay. That's also fine, but at times the visual clarity is severely lacking which can make the challenge feel artificially difficult.- There are some random pop-ups of out of place sexually suggestive art that can at best be explained by "Japanese game". They are very few though.- The optional content (i.e. arena challenges) are not very optional at all and yield de-facto required items.To recapitulate: 10/10, amazing game, would recommend to anyone even remotely into JRPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game ? Yes. 100% yes.Now for the explanation. Gameplay spoilers ahead.This game is a bundle of good ideas. You've got so many ways to improve your character. The weapons, shields and armors you get have a dedicated EXP gauge, and when it's maxed out, you get either a new passive that you can toggle in a separate menu or a boost of its stats along with a crystal. Said crystal is used to equip passives BUT if you equip the piece of stuff that gave you a passive, then you can equip the passive for free. Long story short, think FF9 or Tactics.When you level up, you get 5 gems that you can allocate among HP, ATQ, DEF, MAG, SPD, LUC and ADA. The first 4 are obvious, SPD allows you to wield your weapons faster and to go further with your shield bash, LUC nets you more exp per enemy defeated as well as more loots of course. ADA, for adaptability, is a niche stat which allows you to make the breathing gauge last longer when your character is underwater. Basically, you never up it except when needed. In case you're worrying about a bad choice, don't fret, you can change the allocation at every level up as well as at a spot in the shops here and there.At some point, you get a set of scales, on which you can put items from your inventory, granting you several effects, which work at best when the scales are, as a certain Marvel villain would say, perfectly balanced. As you advance, you'll get more scales, to put more items and activate more effects.There's also a massive tree similar to FF10, in which you expend Force, a currency dropped by enemies, to earn more stats, as well as bonus crystals and pieces of stuff. The clever part is that it's blocked at several points, and you need to advance in the story to go further.The gameplay is terrifyingly efficient, and once you've got a nice stuff, you mow enemies like there's no tomorrow.The story is quite nice, with some plot twists. There are a few mistakes here and there, but nothing that would stop you from understanding the plot.A little negative aspect would be that there are some "false choices", leading you to the main screen and making you load your game. Fortunately, the game is generous in the number of save points, and when such a choice is ahead, there's often a save point right before.If you've read this all, congratulations, but... why are you still reading instead of playing this game ?

_childDocuments_.review: I came to Astlibra Revision like many folks, due to word-of-mouth from online communities and friends. It's not the kind of game I'd usually find myself digging into - I'm not big into Metroidvanias or more action-y RPGs. But I gave it a chance and found myself really, really enjoying it, I played on Easy mode (which I'm sure is anathema to many), but as a 40 year old with heavy work and family commitments, I just don't find the joy in "gitting gud" that many do. But even on Easy, I found it appropriately challenging for a relative newcomer to the genre. The way the game expands systems and options over time felt really thoughtful, and the story is weird but a lot of fun. Some of the quirky, very JRPG-ish sexuality is juvenile and embarrassing, but nothing worse than you'd find in games of the era it's celebrating. I finished the main game and did quite a bit of the new game plus and heartily recommend it. Considering the size of the development staff involved, this game is genuinely a wonder and provided me way more enjoyment than many, many games with hundreds of devs and unbelievable budgets. Highly recommended, and I expect if you're looking to for the mastery angle, cranking the difficulty will certainly deliver, but other reviewers' experience will be more relevant there. Thanks to everyone who recommended this game to me - I would never have found it or picked it up otherwise.
