_childDocuments_.review: AstLibra Revision is pretty incredible. I came into this game knowing basically nothing, it was just this interesting-looking side scroller that was highly rated that I bought on sale. And here I am almost 70 hours later, absolutely blown away at the end of it all. So, let me shill this game and talk a little more about it.Overall: 9/10- This game is not perfect, and has its flaws, but I believe it is very worth giving a shot if you enjoy action games, JRPGs, metroidvanias, etc. There is even a demo to play to give it a shot, although the demo throws so much at you at once, I honestly think it's better to just jump straight into the game itself. There is a lot of information and systems to understand, and its definitely digestible in context of the game and story, but not so much all-at-once. Also this is my score on my feeling for the overall game, I'm not averaging my scores based on some individual sections.Story: 9.5/10I was shocked at the story of this game. I really did not see a lot of what happened over the course of the game coming. There are times that get a little uncomfortable because of over-done fanservice and some of the character writing, but overall it's insignificant compared to the twists and turns and genuinely interesting paths the story takes (I really would go more into it, but I don't want to spoil). Seeing the story through to the post-game end was very satisfying, and I would definitely recommend even to those who may be hesitant based on how the game looks or even if they did not enjoy the combat as much. Visuals: 7.5/10AstLibra Revision is an odd-looking side scroller at first glance. The character models sort of float in front of the backgrounds as these very clear 2D images and the combat animations are also nothing to write home about. As you progress in the game as well you will notice that there are a significant amount of enemies with very horny designs as well, which also made me uncomfortable at times. Overall, however, the art design and direction for many of the bosses, weapons, armors, etc. impressed me and were very detailed. I think the visuals are the weakest part about this game, especially if you aren't into the fan service, but not a deal-breaker by any means.Music & Sound: 8/10There are genuinely some bangers in the ost 100%. However, songs will loop quite a bit in the sections of the game that they play in enough that you may get a little tired of them, so it's not perfect. Music most of the time was nice and added to the atmosphere to some story scenes significantly. Besides the music, most of the time you'll be hearing the combat sounds over everything else, and it can definitely get loud at times compared to the rest of the game. There are also quite a few re-used sound effects between bosses, magic, and many of the weapons sound the same as well. Can get a bit repetitive, but I still liked it even at the end of the game.Combat: 9/10I think this is the biggest love it or hate it part of the game. I think to enjoy the game overall, it's important to enjoy the combat as it is the biggest portion of it. Weird hitboxes on attacks and the absolute reliance on magic to help invulnerability yourself through some genuinely stupid attacks during fights are my only real complaints. The weight system is interesting because as you progress in the game, weapons get heavier and heavier, and you need to level agility to be able to move and wield them with any sufficiency at all. High-weight combat is worse than fat-rolling in souls-likes because you cant even swing your weapon, you're just locked into the animations as they slowly roll through. However, if you get your weight to 0 (which I HIGHLY recommend) you are machine-gunning attacks and building your magic gauge incredibly fast so you become a dps god and can focus more attention on the rest of the fight. Magic and abilities are also incredibly important, but many of these are earned through a progression grid or mastering weapons & equipment, so the game can feel a bit grindy sometimes. Combat itself is very simple, but there are several systems at play, so there is a satisfying amount of prep-work and builds you can put together for different fights. I had a ton of fun with the combat, and while it does take some getting used to, I think it would appeal to many action game fans.Performance: 8/10This game is not very intensive and usually runs pretty smooth, but there are times in combat that there is genuine game lag when there is a lot happening. The entire game just slows down briefly when it happens, but I never experienced any crashing or performance spikes on my computer. It's there and noticeable when it does happen, but it didn't really impact my experience with the game. There were also several times that enemies would fly halfway off the screen and drop chests that I couldn't grab because they ended up in the wall, which is kind of annoying. I think this is more a design decision than a bug however. I did not experience bugs that I can recall. Overall, I was satisfied with the games performance. With how much I enjoyed AstLibra Revision and for the amount of time I enjoyed it, I gladly would have paid full-price, even $80+ for this game. This game at $25 is still a steal, and it goes on sale quite a bit as well. Definitely check this gem of a game out.

_childDocuments_.review: ASTLIBRA ～生きた証～ Revision ReviewThe best and the weirdest thing about Astlibra is that it feels, looks, and sounds like an artifact from the past; like a forgotten PS1/PS2 game. And in some sense, it really is — being mostly made by a single person over 15 years. It is one of the comfiest games I've played, with difficulty tuned to be just right (I beat the game on Hard), the grind being just long enough not to become dull, the progression giving you new things to look up to and think about often enough to keep the combat from turning stale, and the story always throwing curveballs to keep you on your toes and prevent you from guessing what's going to happen next.In terms of gameplay, the closest comparisons I can draw are Dust: An Elysian Tail, and the Ys series. The former being a straightforward action platformer with a robust combat system. The linear structure and the fast-paced, action-oriented gameplay are rather refreshing in this age of endless roguelites and metroidvanias. The latter having a classic JRPG story about fighting against seemingly insurmountable odds to save your loved ones. After falling out of touch with modern JRPGs that either overload you with a dozen of proper nouns in the first hour and try to involve you in some political conflict; or simply being about a bunch of whiny school children (and often being very problematic about it) doing stupid things but still coming on top of incredibly incompetent adults this game's story is anime, but in a good way — in the same way as TTGL or DBZ is.Astlibra starts slow in every sense of the word. The game begins with a lengthy cutscene (the textbox even warns you that the intro is long and absent of action), slow and simple combat, and a bare minimum of RPG progression. But over the course of 60-80h, it really ramps up, only dropping the tempo a handful of times, but never entirely stopping until the very end of the 3rd ending. What initially began as a search for your childhood friend turns into a time-travel adventure involving gods of inner and outer realms, multiple intertwined storylines, and a sizeable cast of major and episodic characters. A relatively slow and simplistic attack-and-block combat turns into an air-juggling and spell-slinging visual feast.A basic STR/DEF/MAG RPG system expands multiple times, unlocking more and more ways to affect your character stats and abilities, including, but not limited to systems similar to NieR: Automata's Plug-in Chips, FF X Sphere Grid, and FF Tactics' Equipment abilities.PS: I almost forgot to mention an absolute banger of a soundtrack, consisting primarily of a Vocaloid-infused drum and bass EDM tracks straight from '00-'10, with an occasional brostep thrown into the mix. While it might not be everybody's cup of tea, it definitely works well for the action and the story that it frames and deserves to be called one of the most daring soundtrack choices in my recent memory.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this right after I beat the main storyThis game is absolutely insane. The art is good, the combat feels fluid,  the art is great, and the story is really something to behold. I want whatever the dev was smoking when they made this plotline because it's fantastic but makes no sense if you try to describe it to someone. Just when you think you're finally going to get to the conclusion, it goes insane-o mode and really sucks you in (spent like 3 straight nights playing it trying to finish only to find out there's still more story).I think the endgame is where this stuff really shines. You feel as powerful as the game says you are at that point, and the big completionist style rewards are surprisingly achievable. Sure there's some tough spots at the end, but beating a boss is less about "git gud" and more playing around their patterns and knowing your toolkit. If something feels too hard, chances are there's some skill/item you've overlooked or haven't unlocked that'll put the boss to bed.The progression system is also really nice. You've got your classic level up and allocate stat points, but there's an expansive stat tree maze, and all of the weapons and armor you come across can gain XP and level up to give skills or an item and enhanced stats. There are very few points where you've maxed out everything you can, and at that point it's best to chokeslam whatever big bad is causing trouble and move onto the fresh new stuff.Probably the first time in years a game has dragged me this deep into its mechanics/story, and I loved the ride. Not for everyone, but if this seems up your alley get the demo and then get the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid 4 in many ways. The gameplay is quite decent and the story even if it has big lows (Hotel room chapter... xD) ends in a high note in many ways. Some of the mechanics are unexpectedly deep, the soundtrack is quite varied (and has a couple of fully voiced JPOP songs in case that's your preference), the struggle throughout the story is consistent and even if there are difficulty spikes (Was playing on hard, all said), the game can get quite easy if treated as a classic JRPG.Some of the negative points are unclear or weirdly thought puzzles, some maps are unnecessary convoluted, some chapters are quite off-putting, has a lot of forced anime tropes (YMMV), the chest rarity is mostly worthless (Gold chests can have basic items in them), and keys are too expensive in general.This is a love project by someone that really enjoyed the game and were able to release their vision, and it shows in many areas (combat, major plot points, some branching of dialogues and actions are quite impressive, equipment and level system have several rare and even unique approaches). And to the creators I just want to say, thanks for making this game. It was enjoyable and fun.Post DLC: The DLC is fun, an other than a misseable achievement (easy to miss if you are not aware), it has nice content in a Rogue-lite environment going throught the maps of the original game and fighting monsters as the Baker's daughter you heard so much about on the original story.The DLC in general is enjoyable, even if the story is a bit lacking. Being able to use "classes for the character", dressing up the character is fun for a bit, and you can save the world looking like several characters in the story (girls/only... wouldn't have minded dressing up as some guys as well). Boss fights in the arena are challenging but usually you will be able to destroy the strat bosses (unless you avoid exploting magic-caster invulnerability).

_childDocuments_.review: I have little experience in the Metriodvania category, the 2.5D sidescroller action rpg niche thing. The only other game that I've play similar is Symphony of the Night, which I played until the disc cracked. And even still, I played this game for days straight, got 100%, and am already waiting on the sequel. It brought me back to the younger days, on summer break, pushing Alucard to beat "luck-mode" with my younger brother on the sofa beside.To start, the game is as hard or as easy as you want it to be, with 6 (I think) different difficulties. I played through on "hard" - once I got to about 75% completion though I wish I had selected one difficulty higher. The story was solid. It did get somewhat convoluted, but that happens with JRPGS, some of the translations could be better, but the majority of the dialogue was good. The combat is fast paced and fun. The skills and magic system are easy to use and critical in your success. Master weapons to learn new skills, unlock new magic through growth. There is a great selection of weapon types and styles, and in the back third or so of the game you can make even your starter gear as strong as the end game stuff. What I miss in the newer RPGs I play is farming - THE GRIND. Astlibra doesn't require you to dump HOURS into powering up your character, but if there's an empty bar that needs to be filled.... I'm gonna fill it. A huge plus for me was the multi-layered leveling system: You earn experience, you earn a spendable growth currency, and even weapon exp. In the back half of the game you can also find supplements to your gear that further enhance your stats and skills. I will eventually replay this. I will need to be in the mood to invest the time though, like SoTN it is an investment to clear completely.I thoroughly enjoyed the time I spent on Astlibra Revision. I would recommend this game to any who are a fan of the genre, and even to those that haven't dip their toes in the water since Konami was king. These are the games the AAA studios should be pushing.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. Good music, extremely engaging and fun game-play, and an interesting story. So much playtime and such a bargain, I'm so glad I found this.However, : There are many translations that are misleading or wrong for skills and stats. Look things up if they seem wrong, or look them up anyway. As an example, a core stat (Adaptability) apparently increases resistance to abnormal status ailments - this is not mentioned anywhere; going by the description it only improves your attacks while underwater. Another example, an ability is described as "+10 against all status ailments, 1.5x damage taken". It was previously translated even worse, to make players believe they would deal more damage under certain circumstances. But it is still wrong, and is actually +100 against all status ailments which is a huge difference. These issues are not nearly enough for me to recommend against the game, just enough for me to warn people to look things up if they sound weird.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be using a template and try to highlight separately from both the main game and the DLC.ASTLIBRA Revision is a side-scrolling game that revolves around a young man looking for his friend after his hometown was attacked by demons. The gameplay is simple yet complex, the RPG elements are very thought of, everything was superb.ASTLIBRA Revision (Gaiden: Cave of Phantom Mist) is a separate DLC with the same gameplay mechanics but with an added feature of roguelite elements, the story tells of a baker's daughter and takes place in parallel with the main game, so it's best to completely finish the main game first.Strongly Recommended - ✔✔☐ Very Difficult☐ Difficult☐ Moderate☐ Easy☑ Very EasyFor both the MG (Main game) and DLC, the controls are pretty much the same. I didn't do too many changes but the controls feels very fluid.☐ Poorly Balanced☐ Somewhat Balanced☐ Moderately Balanced☐ Well Balanced☑ Perfectly BalancedDifficulty in this game actually affects the mechanics of the game, where for the 2 hardest difficulties, the game won't pause when you are casting magic and using item from the quick slot. I'd say these changes are what makes the game veerryy smooth in terms of gameplay.I did a blind Hell (2nd hardest) difficulty playthrough for the MG, and Impossible (Hardest) for the DLC. The difficulty spikes are well balanced as long as you properly equip yourself. Increase in difficulty typically just raises the enemy's damage and health points, the AI itself doesn't seem to change. I rarely encounter a case of damage sponge bosses. The attack patterns of the enemies are beautifully telegraphed and designed, especially the bosses and they are enough to keep you on your toes but still mesmerized by the effects!☐ Not at all☐ Slightly☐ Moderately☐ Very☑ ExtremelyI got 100 hours in just a week with a 100% achievement. Need I say more?Jokes aside, I never feel bored even when grinding, everything feels very rewarding. The game also has SKIP feature so it doesn't make repeating story tedious after you die, or when you want to try another choice regarding the story.☐ Meaningless☐ Not Meaningful☐ Somewhat Meaningful☑ Quite Meaningful☐ Highly MeaningfulAfter a certain chapter, you will encounter some cases of Choices Matter that affects endings and how the rest of the chapter plays. So it's best to have multiple saves. Exploring the map, finding out hidden treasures and bosses, grinding for materials, all of them will reward you and it doesn't feel like looking for every detail is useless. Post-game also has mechanics where you will be able to crank up early game gears and make it viable for end-game dungeons and FASHION.☐ Not Interesting☐ Slightly Interesting☐ Moderately Interesting☐ Very Interesting☑ Extremely InterestingOh boy.Main game story, as I said, revolves around a boy looking for his friend after his hometown was attacked by demons. Story was really captivating and beautiful, no cliches no niches, LOTS of plot twists and things that will leave your mouth hanging and wanting for more. The story involves eradicating demons and time traveling, with every side characters perfectly impacting the story. Keizo did a very amazing job for this.DLC story takes place at least after the 2nd chapter of the main game (I think?), with more plot twists. It's shorter than the main game but it has the perfect length for the DLC, the narration itself is still beautiful.☐ Not Immersive☐ Slightly Immersive☐ Moderately Immersive☐ Very Immersive☑ Completely ImmersiveThe world building is beautiful, the backdrop for most areas gave me a wide-eye as I am awed by the design. It may not use unreal engine and all that stuff but, man, even my girlfriend was captivated when she watched me play this game.☐ Not Appealing☐ Slightly Appealing☐ Moderately Appealing☐ Very Appealing☑ Extremely AppealingSometimes you'll feel familiar with the visuals. Some will make you feel nostalgic, stunned, and wondering... "Have I seen something like this before?"Well it's none other than  from VanillaWare! The particle effects of magic, weapon swing animation, skills, they feel very impactful added with a really good SFX.☐ Very Unfriendly☐ Unfriendly☐ Neutral☑ Friendly☐ Very FriendlyPretty easy to navigate, inventory sorts by itself and cannot be sorted manually. _childDocuments_.review: Astlibra is a 2D side scrolling action RPG with lite platforming and puzzle elements. Visually, the graphics and animations of the game remind me of old flash games I used to play back in the day, which isn't a bad thing. It's a pretty big game with lots of content that rewards exploring. It's clear that the developers cared about the game they were making.The gameplay loop goes something like this: you enter a new area, go from one end of the screen to the other while defeating enemies, collect drops from enemies and gather resources from the environment to craft new weapons and gear, equip the new weapons and gear and master them to get new passive abilities, and defeat the boss in the area. Each area is self-contained and separated from the others, only abstractly connected to each other through a hub area. You can go back to areas you've previously gone to in case you missed something. There are several different game mechanics/leveling mechanics that you can play around with to min/max and optimize your play style. It's somewhat complex but easy to understand and the depth is appreciated.The story, in abstract, is like an iceberg. When you first encounter something, you are only seeing the surface. The reality is often much deeper and darker and each layer of the iceberg slowly gets revealed as you progress through the story. This type of story telling will keep you engaged and will make you want to keep playing to find out the truth behind the world. If you want to play the game blind then you should stop reading here.As a brief synopsis without spoiling anything, you play as a nameless, silent protagonist along with a mysterious talking crow as his companion searching for his sole childhood friend, a girl named Anulis, who he got separated from when their village was attacked by demons nearly a decade ago. The hero obtains a legendary artifact that allows him to travel through time but only under certain conditions. With this power, he is able to go back in time and change events or prevent things from happening thus creating a more ideal future. This often creates unintended consequences which the hero finds out the hard way. In fact, it is a recurring theme in the story "you can't have your cake and eat it, too." There are only trade-offs. As the story progresses, more and more truth behind the reality of his world is revealed. Despite suffering from setbacks and being placed in hopeless situations, the hero presses on, never straying from his goal of finding his childhood friend, even if it means taking on the entire world. Overall, it is an emotional roller coaster and i enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute masterpiece of an experience. One of the rare times where the phrase "greater than the sum of its parts" is not only applicable, but is a gross understatement. I completed all achievements in 65 hours and I was very surprised at how much content this unassuming indie title has for you. The basic premise is that it is a 2D JRPG "Metroidvania" with fast and smooth combat. When I say "Metroidvania", I don't mean Symphony of the Night, where it is one (two) giant map. This is more like Order of Ecclesia, where there are several smaller maps that aren't physically connected. The visuals are both great and also lacking. The sprites are all wonderful, though I wish the animations had more frames. In the middle of combat you don't notice the frames of animation that the sprites have in the slightest and everything moves fluidly as the actual FPS is stable. The biggest complaint I have visually are some of the background and foreground environment sprites have clear lines so you can tell exactly how it is all tiled together. Again, in the heat of combat you will not notice it at all. That being said, everything looks cohesive and nothing ever seems like it was designed and created for another project and just pasted into the game without care. The combat is awesome. It is fast and simple on the surface but also has depth to it. You will have a bad time if you are just mashing the attack button and not much else. You must utilize the offensive and defensive skills you learn along the way. Possession skills are great and eventually become very overpowered once you master how to fight. It becomes so fun once you get into the groove of it all that you will want to take the time to max out the exp on all of the weapons, shields, and armor... and it won't feel like a chore at all. The RPG mechanics for leveling stats, crafting, weapons, armor, shields, Karon magic, the Force board, Possession skills, Libra system, Item boards, and enhancing your equipment keeps you busy and you always feel like you're making progress and improving. Each aspect is straightforward on its own and in conjunction with the other systems forms a tight web of character progression not seen often enough. This game respects your time in ways most others in the JRPG/RPG realm fail to by having several ways to respec almost at any time. There are tons of free places to do it in town or at mokyun shops. From shops you can buy respec potions so you can do it anywhere. It is a nice touch. The story is very JRPG but man did I care about it. I didn't really expect that going into it based on the demo and screenshots of the game, as well as other reviews that suggested it was all over the place and what not. I didn't think so at all. I don't normally care about story too much as a lot of times it appears to be just a means to an end, kind of thought up on the spot to justify mechanics of the game, but that isn't the case here. I was very invested in the goings on of everyone. Almost brought to tears, empty pit in my chest levels of invested in the story. The music is done by a bunch of different artists and it is basically all wonderful. There was some random rap song in one optional room I didn't care for. On the other hand, the third area music was done by the legendary S.S.H. and it shreds. Other styles are present as well and it really fits so much better than you would think. I'm going to be listening to a few of these tracks for a very long time down the road. Some things that you need to do to progress the game aren't totally communicated well to you, though that is most likely due to the translation. If you pay attention and don't skip cutscenes or conversation, you'll probably be able to figure out what you need to do 90% of the time. There were a couple spots where what was needed seemed sort of obtuse and I didn't really seem to understand how I was supposed to glean what to do from the story or conversations with NPCs or environmental clues. Though when you bring up the menu it will give you direction on what you're supposed to be doing overall, but again, a couple times that wasn't any help at all. Trust me when i say this game is great. I don't ever write reviews. I am sacrificing sleep to write this because I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game. This is much better than so many AAA big budget RPGs and it was just a labor of love from one guy. That passion is palpable through out the entirety of this game. This is a steal at full price, if it ever goes on sale, do no hesitate to pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite an interesting game.  Don't expect cutting edge controls or platforming.  However, it has a great story (including a lot of post-game content which extends the original story significantly).  It has a ton of RPG like elements and in many ways a "classic" RPG feel.  It's not exactly a metroidvania, though you DO get new abilities and DO backtrack to certain areas, but not in the same way as you would with a metroidvania, so don't expect the same type of experience.The combat is pretty fun, but not overly complicated either.  There are a plethora of progression systems to upgrade your character.Ultimately, it comes down to the story though.  Any time I play a game or watch a movie, I'm trying to piece together what's going to happen in advance so I can predict all the twists.  I thought I had this game all figured out from the beginning.  Boy, was I wrong!  There are so many crazy twists and turns that keeps the game fresh, and in the end, the story actually made sense, despite being a such a twisting journey along the way.  It's funny, fresh, and has a ton of ups and downs.As long as you're not expecting cutting edge, AAA features or a typical metroidvania experience, and you like RPGs and an old-school feel, then this game is a good fit for you.  I'm definitely glad I played it.

_childDocuments_.review: Play on "Difficult"Aslibra's heavy usage of stock assets and sprite tweening make it one of the ugliest games I've set my eyes upon, and yet, Keizo's choice of music as well as great gameplay make it a must buy, the moment to moment action and customization makes it one of the most engaging games I've played in a while.Now, the game is difficult and expects you to learn all of it's mechanics (which are not made entirely clear thanks to the translation) as you advance, chapter after chapter you'll stumble upon a new wall that may make you rage quit, and the schizophrenic usage of save points will make you curse the developer's lineage each time you die after a bossfight. That being said, not once did I feel that my situation was hopeless, Astlibra lets you respec your character freely and experimenting with builds is heavily encouraged and necessary for unlocking new abilities, however, this makes the game a grind if you have no idea what to look for.It's kino, get it now

_childDocuments_.review: (+) Couldn't get myself to play anything else while addicted to this(+) Style blends Castlevania combat, FF weapon skills system, Chrono Trigger plot (but crazier and twistier)... and yeah it's as good as that sounds(+) Relatively casual difficulty level (in Normal difficulty) and lots of pauses between events, so it can be played by busy people despite being long(-) Not much negative to say, but some things could be more intuitive and some menus could be more efficient, that's where the solo dev thing shows. Nothing that really hinders enjoyment though.Worth mentioning it is an RPG that does not hold your hand tooooo much when it comes to telling you what to do, making collectibles obvious, etc. It's by design tho and there are skills that you can get that facilitate finding things. I like that.

_childDocuments_.review: Well this was something else.- The graphics look generally terrible, barring a few exceptions like the beautiful plains area.- The translation of some stuff is at once hilarious and hopelessly confusing. You'll have no choice but to test out or look up what some abilities or perks do to because many descriptions make no sense- It's got its good moments but overall the story is convoluted, anime trope-filled nonsense - complete with the weird pervy sexual innuendos and physics-defying bitties. I burst out laughing the first time i met a certain godess with her melons individually flopping around in every direction.So why the positive review? - The combat is oh so satisfying. Hits have a short pause to them so you have that comfortable microsecond to plan your next attack, most weapons feel nice, and there's many options for solid builds. - There is a TON of content. I put 70 hours into with a "try to be decently thorough" approach, without overdoing it. There's a ton of secrets to find, megabosses, that kind of thing.- The difficulty felt just right. I did a spot of light grinding here and there to top off some weapon masteries but that was it. I minimised fast travel so that the grinding felt organic.  - The progress feels great. Lots of secrets to find, weapons to unlock, and skills to master. There's many ways you can tweak your character and by the end I felt deliciously powerful without it being too easy. In the end if you want a fun side-scroller RPG with outstanding gameplay, this is it. Show this solo dev some support; I look forward to their next project

_childDocuments_.review: Only in the very early going but the title seems promising. Attractive art style that shines through in the sprite work. I read that one of the designers worked for Vanillaware which is impressive to learn but makes sense. Fun hack and slash combat that already shows some promise with a few different learned abilities accessible.Update: Just wanted to add to my impressions after playing a couple more hours. While I have only progressed a tiny bit further into the game, I've learned a bit more about the leveling and "grow" system. The game has regular exp. that you collect from defeating enemies, but also gives you different color gems. You can then turn these in for various stat buffs and even new abilities. It feels like a slightly more free form sphere grid from Final Fantasy X.I've also just unlocked the second "summon" ability. I am blanking on the proper name, but you gain "ST" via attacking enemies. This in turn fills up a gauge from which you draw upon to perform special attacks with the aid of your quasi "familiar" avian ally. This adds a nice wrinkle to the already enjoyable hack and slash combat.You also have character passive and active skills you must manually activate from it's own menu. You must have the required amount of magic crystals for the given skill you wish to require. These range from things such as displaying enemy health values, showing you how much damage you're dealing, as well as more active abilities such as being able to guard in mid air or dash/sprint with the press of a button (or double tap of a direction) .I already managed to write quite a bit, and from the slight bit I've read online (I'm trying to avoid spoiling too much as I get the feeling the game could get pretty wild) I'm barely scratching the surface of what the game has to offer both mechanically and from a narrative perspective. I look forward into delving further into the adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It's very apparent that the Dev was very passionate about this game.Story: 9/10I enjoyed the characters, can't say much about the plot without spoiling. It's not too long or too short. There's a couple of sidequests, but they don't really feel like sidequests, Idk if I should call them that. One of them is a guy giving you a reward for getting all the weapons,shields and armor in the game. 99% of the game is Linear main story stuff. There are no missables, the game has a system where you can go back to any location, sometimes the story will lock this functionality for a bit, but it unlocks right after that specific story segment anyway. You can go back to all previous areas in between main story chapters.Some part of the true/alternate ending is locked behind a little bit of grinding. This is the reason why it's not a 10/10 for me. It should be lower, but I enjoy the combat enough to not hate the grind enough to lower the score more.Gameplay: 9/10Combat feels nice and impactful, Items feel varied enough, weapons with the same type feel similar to play but they have different skills attached to them so I guess it's okay if you think of them as something to use until you master the skill. The spell variety is nice, and you can change their effects later in the game via item customization with boards. Overall it didn't get boring to play for the 60 hours I put into it.The scales mechanic is unique and interesting for me. You can use basically any non-equippable item to give you passive stat boost, the stat depends on the item, and it depends on how you balance the "weight" of the items on a scale.Soundtrack: 9/10Purely subjective, but I think some songs were pretty memorable enough. After A play session, I would randomly remember some of the songs in the game playing in my head.Some Negatives:It's a bit grindy, but not really required. I did end up unintentionally grinding for a while because I wanted to get some weapon skills so I can't really say how the game would be like if you did zero grinding. I can imagine the bosses might feel a bit bullet spongey if you have low stats or something. But Since I did grind some, I didn't personally experience this, on average I had high enough stats to not have any problems with bosses, I did use a lot of consumables though.I personally didn't mind the grind because I was having fun with the combat, but I can see people being put off by the grind.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on calling this game underrated because it really isn't for everybody. It's grindy, the combat doesn't evolve all that much especially with how much the game makes you do it, and a lot of the interactions can skeeve some people out. However, if this game strikes a chord with you, then it is legitimately one of the most amazing games ever made.The combat, while simple, has a lot of underlying interactions that makes deeper than what makes it initially seem. None of the weapons have any special unique animations, but weapons such as knives are faster and can charge your magic bar better, staves have a total of 1 attack power but have strong secondary effects such as shooting fireballs, and heavy swords have great range and power at the cost of speed and weight, which you will immediately and intuitively feel out as you play the game. Yes, the game has a lot of grinding, but it also keeps rewarding you for all the small actions you do. Of course you can level up like in all RPGs, but Monsters also drop "force" which you can use to permanently upgrade your stats or even unlock new spells and weapons/armor/accessories. Monsters also drop chests with a whole host of loot that will make grinding actually exciting to engage in, from new equipment recipes, to straight up new equipment, to resources you can use in your adventures such as healing items. All these are not carrots-at-the-end-of-the-stick that other grindy rpgs have to force you into grinding, but fun rewards the game constantly throws at you. Not to mention the sound design and all the little visual flourishes that attacks do make the simple act of actually just fighting monsters all that much more fun to do.The music, while not wholly original, fit the tone of each stage all the tracks are placed in, which really transcend the experience. Stand out tracks for me include the boss theme of Act 3 and the stage theme of act 7, which you wouldn't even know weren't actually originally made for this game unless you looked it up or someone told it to you with how well they were implemented into the game.The story is the biggest pain point for any players who enjoy games such as these. It attempts to explore a lot of weighty subjects such as fate, death, loss, all wrapped around a time travel mechanic, which has historically not worked out well for stories that use them, while also having very "anime" interactions, an example being, one of the female characters repeatedly misunderstanding that they are being sexually propositioned by a merchant when it was actually a wholesome interaction all along. There's also a secret boss in chapter 5 that will be very offputting for a lot of players that aren't used to, let's just say. very very "anime" media. Don't take this part as a condemnation from me though, as you can really feel the love from the dev weaved through every bit of every interaction you have with all the characters. Once you realize the stakes of the story, you really feel this sense of unease and dread at what might happen when you go along because you really grow attached to these characters. TLDR, it's not for everybody, but if you let your guard down or if you already enjoy games and stories like these, it is a magnificent experience that will stick with you for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a newly-huge fan of metroidvania games, and came here from recommendations based on Bloodstained: Symphony Of The Night and Timespinner. Was playing Afterimage, tried this one out on a whim, and stopped Afterimage completely to do this instead.It's a beautiful game, way too fun. Have close to 100%'d it at eighty-one hours, at least as close as I'm willing to get. The conclusion of the game and its final chapter were so satisfying that it'd feel weird to fire it back up just to check some boxes. Aside from some uncomfortably-outdated tongue-in-cheek perversion, I found the story and its characters genuinely charming and engaging. Twist after twist, especially late-game, with what felt to me like few plot holes. Fun game mechanics, responsive controls, satisfying empowerment and a decent amount of customization. Actually laughed out loud a few times, even with a culture barrier.If you like metroidvanias at all, I think you'll love this game, and the demo's a great way to find out. In the demo, there's a showcase version that lets you try out some of the early-game gameplay, and you can start a new game which transfers over seamlessly if (when) you purchase the full thing.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: This game. This game. This game. It's too good! The story just keeps on going and going and going. If you think you're at the end, you're not. And then once you finally do finish the main game, the DLC adds even more to the story with a new character with a couple of new ways to improve, more of a refinement than a reinvention. SAVE OFTEN. Don't rely on a single save. There are choices to be made in the game, although many of them tend to lead to instant endings.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that’s clear from the beginning that it’s going to be a cult hit and one of the all time greats. The gameplay is fantastic and the story actually interesting. My only gripe is that it used the old school save point system so if you die, you will lose all progress since the last save point
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even remember how I found this game, but I'm definitely gonna remember this journey, what an amazing experience.It may not be the prettiest one you can find, but it repays you with everything else. Story that is going from slapping random demonic jellies with a sticc to transcending beyond the meaning of time and slaying some omega-creator-god with your Cookieblaster +69. That pretty basic concept for jRPGs is full of really cool ideas, amazing twists that made whole story fresh and realize how much emotions simple textboxes can create. Entire cast of characters are great without exception. You will cheer for your companions and feel the ultimate power of friendship™ when they help you defeat well thought antagonists that are not evil for the sake of being evil.Depth of mechanics are exceeding the deepest point of Great Canyon. Shuffling your equipment, looking for best synergies with your powers, creating builds and minmaxing their efficiency are constantly evolving through entire game that keeps throwing new mechanics with very good pacing - you having a loot of time to enjoy what you have before discovering something new. With that combat is what surprises me the most with the bossfights as it's cherry on top. I can't really stretch out how unique and epic every single encounter was till the very end.It also will be a sin not to mention the music. You have variety of sad and emotional tracks, chill ones, 200bpm fantasy epic techno and crazy metal tracks that makes you wanna headbang.So experience this hidden gem yourself and tell your friends about Astlibra, it deserves more attention.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna preface this by saying its not a terrible game, its okay at best, but I think this is definitely a "pickup on sale for $10 or less" kinda deal. I don't think there is anything constructive I can add to all the negative reviews that hasn't already been said. I do agree though that this game is very much over-hyped by all the positive reviews and even find it kinda funny that it has 15k reviews with a "overwhelmingly positive" rating but achievements show only about ~30% of players have even reached close to the end game.I think all I have left to say is that in 15 years the developer never figured out how to make sloped terrain function in their game (all slopes are stepped platforms with a background/foreground effect to make it seem sloped) and my god does it get in the way at times during the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: I didn´t have big expactations for this title.Mainly because I aint very passionate for side-scrollers, metrovanias, Jump´n Runs and similar stuff.But this one is something else. Its the most captivitating game I played since FinalFantasy 7 in my childhood.I dont know how Keizo did it, but Astlibra made it to become in just a couple of hours my all time favourite. _childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like SotN?  Do you like side scrollers? This game is for you!  It has lots of ways to grind if you want.  It rewards using lots of different weapons. When maxing a weapons experience you unlock stat bonuses and most of the time persistent skills your able to equip.  It also has an almost sphere grid like system with slowly unlocking stat bonuses using "force" dropped by monsters. Unlike other games, it is constantly rewarding you for the time your putting in with new skills and better stats.  The story so far has been pretty good and has my interested to see where it goes from here.  Combat feels good!  There also seems to be quite a few different approaches to combat. ranged weapons, magic, shield, two handed.  Overall this is most likely going to end up my favorite side scroller since Symphony of the Night.  Who knows?  It might even take the crown by the end!  Will update this review if I manage to complete it, but some far I love it and would recommend it to anyone who likes this type of game. Don't hesitate to try the lengthy demo and see if this gem of a game is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: I can't praise this game enough. From having only one programmer/lead developer. To using royalty free music, yet somehow it all works.The game has so much depth, that me leaving a review wouldn't even do it justice, and this game was made by one person.This should tell you just how bad AAA games have gotten. I am still left speechless by his 10 years in the making masterpiece, thank you Keizo.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: I am the type of person that normally does not write a review of the game. But after 67 hours and reaching the true end, All I have to say is, wow, what a journey. Not once have I felt bored throughout the playtime of this game.In the interest of not spoiling the game, I will not be discussing any story elements. To put it in vague terms, the story is constantly able to keep me on the edge and give me surprises. There are a few other comments that mentions some occasional juvenile humor that really troubles them. However, it hardly bothers me and gave me a few good chuckles on occasion. But I will mention it just in case you are sensitive regarding this type of humor. The combat of this game is also great! I never knew that having multi hit per weapon attack will feel SO GOOD. This is something that more 2D side-scrolling action combat game needs to take note. The music is freeware music that is available on the internet. But not only does it not diminish the experience, it just highlights that the freeware Japanese music creation community are masters of their craft. Every important moment is accentuated so well by the music, and quite frankly, I prefer this style of music of the vast 99% of AAA game that I have played. Many of those musics are now on my regular playlist.Thank you Keizo, for spending 15 years giving us this amazing experience. And thank you to all the others who help make the Revision version possible. I will now pledge my thumbs up to the sea of positive reviews. Astlibra Revision is now one of my favorite games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game. The main story was pretty good and the time traveling was handled well. The "Mastery" system was quite refreshing way of obtaining custom/special passive skills and customizing your gameplay. "Grow" system (passive stat tree) can be somewhat frustrating to navigate especially when you backtrack to fill out previous nodes. The controls take some time to get used to but everything can be rebinded as you want. Overall i must say the game is surprisingly deep, engaging and very fun to play. Definetly up there with games like Xenoblade and other AAA JRPGs (in my opinion).
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: Despite surface level appearances, ASTLIBRA is one of the best 2D ARPGs on the market. Great combat, solid writing, tons of content, and packed full of soul; it's no wonder the one-man-army developer behind ASTLIBRA spent sixteen years perfecting it.It's proof that anyone can make a game, and one of the best I've played this year at that.Go in blind, play on Difficult (or higher if you're a hardass/completionist), and have fun with it. It's worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: Was initially a little skeptical- not going to lie. However, this game is OUTSTANDING.  I am having a blast, the friends I have recommended the game to are having a blast. Awesome. Not just a diamond in the rough- it is the entire diamond mine. A detailed list of how amazing this game is would basically be an encyclopedia of compliments.  Can't say enough good things. Maybe a bit heavy on some 'fan-servicey' character/enemy/summon designs and dialogue, but looking past that- the story and characters felt good to watch develop over the course of the game. _childDocuments_.review: "The fruit of 15 years of development and love."I'm not a big fan of 2D sidescrollers. While I appreciate the genre, for some reason, games like Hollow Knight or Dust tend to bore me after a few hours. The only other 2D game of this type that I enjoyed till the end was Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, a game that, till the end, I felt I really didn't want to end. Astlibra was the same for me.There is much I could say about the very interesting progression mechanics, the fun and challenging combat on higher difficulties, and the unique and interesting art style that fits the game perfectly. Above all, I'd like to compliment the story. While the twists and revelations of many stories across all media became predictable to me after many years, Astlebra kept me guessing until the end. I don't want to spoil anything, so I will keep it short and simple. The characters are great, the backstory is well developed and introduced at a great pace for the player, and the twists and turns are surprising but not in an unbearable way with the related elements of the story already introduced. There are also many side details that you can piece together from clues found around the world through exploration.It's not really a complaint; it doesn't bother me, but I know there are people who are bothered by some innuendos and sexualization. I wouldn't say there is a lot of it in the game, and for me, it was in no way a distraction from the story, but it is there. Some of it could be said to fit with the themes of the story, as gods and goddesses of old religions were heavily sexualized. (I think there could be a big debate about what sexual stuff is natural for us since we are beings born of desire, but well, I don't think review is the place for this.) Aside from that, I think it could do without, but it does help to develop the characters' relationship in some ways. Anyway, just be mindful of it if it's something that bothers you.Well? What are you waiting for? Go and experience this unique game!
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: After a hundred hours of playing, I have finally finished this game, beaten the final boss, and borne witness to a beautiful ending. I am actually baffled that an indie RPG of this depth and quality exists; no matter how much I played, it always had something else up its sleeve to surprise me with. This is nothing short of a passion project with emphasis on the passion; I am actually moved to tears by having played something that is like... this. I haven't felt this way since . I feel invigorated and purposeful for playing this game. I am actually angry at having played other indie games that aren't this deep, this full of content, this .I do have a couple of issues, though. I'm going to forgive the choppy translation and the hideous mishmash of textures and graphics; this is a passion project by someone in their basement, after all, and I expect it would be tremendously rough.What I do take issue with is our hero having no name and no voice. The silent protagonist is a trend that I really wish would die in video games already as technology's evolved past the need to keep text boxes sparse in order to preserve disk space. Same goes for not having a name. It just feels weird and strange for everyone to call you "dear hero" or "this guy", and it's  weird when it is outright stated that your name is written somewhere in game but no one ever refers to you by it.A character having no name and no voice is meant to allow the player to project onto them but that simply doesn't work here: our hero is indeed a character with driving motivations that characterise him, the search for Anulis. We should be drawn deeply into our hero's passionate and lifelong search for his beloved childhood friend but the lack of actual characterisation on display feels like a wall of jelly that I can't get through. What's more, the hero does talk to other people a lot and express himself but, without words, all you get are people constantly repeating everything you say like Solid Snake. "What's that, dear hero? You want to buck common sense and leap into danger to save them?"A lot of scenes in the story are diminished by the hero's inability to speak but none more so than one specific moment near the very end. The knees of that scene absolutely buckle as it tries to convey what  be a moment of such heartwarming sincerity and fulfillment but only has one half of it.I stress that our hero is very much a character and so the typical strengths of a silent protagonist, however meager, do not apply here. If the protagonist spoke, the game would be so much better for it.But this most certainly does not impede the quality of . Play it. Play it play it play it play it play it. Play the demo. Be made curious by the demo so that you buy and play the whole thing. If you're a fan of , this game will exceed every expectation you have and more. If you're a fan of any RPG ever, you need to play this because it nails the feeling that every RPG hopes to scratch. Just .

_childDocuments_.review: Definition of Indie masterpieceBest plot of the year for me. (You have to play NG+ too to get the full plot)So many twists and turn but it doesn't feel forced, everything is naturally connected.The story keeps you engaged through and through, and starts getting really good pass chapter 3.On top of masterfully crafted plot, the progression/ game-play is another highlight.So many weapons/ spells/ skills for you to build around. The exploration feels super rewarding and will drive you to complete everything the game has to offer, yet not being too tedious and grindly like many other JRPG games. A perfect balance.You can feel how much heart and effort went into this project as you play this game.The only downside of the game is first chapter is a bit of slowburn and the game combat is somewhat tedious/ boring at the beginning, especially if you play on higher difficulty. Also the graphic and cut scene are nothing to write home of either, but given it's from single developer you can tell he tried his best already.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really falling in love with this game, I played something like 10 hours of just the demo/trial earlier this week, so I'm already a ways into Act 3 continuing from that save. The combat's very satisfying and fun (and quite challenging on Hell difficulty) with a pretty neat and easy to use magic system, and all the art's just gorgeous imo. There's a good variety of different progression mechanics that have kept me hooked; maxing out the XP bar for each weapon, shield, and armor piece to either unlock new skills or more capacity to equip skills has been especially compelling. Currently trying to survive while using the tree branch from the beginning of the game because I'm finally getting enough XP from enemies to make good progress on its bar haha. The story hasn't done much to blow me away yet but its mysteries and few core characters have been interesting enough. There's time travel shenanigans involved so I expect things might get pretty wild eventually. Highly recommended checking the demo out at least, especially if you're a fan of games like Odin Sphere or SotN.EDIT: Oh yeah the music absolutely RIPS, definitely a big part of why I'm having so much fun just spending time farming monsters.

_childDocuments_.review: An utterly phenomenal game that just keeps going and going. _childDocuments_.review: Only nine hours in, and boy does this game scratch an itch. I like grinding, finding rare items, combat doesn't seem super complex and deep yet, but it is getting there. _childDocuments_.review: What an incredible game!  I haven't been able to stop playing it since I started and I can already tell this will be one of those games I'll be sorry to see come to an end. _childDocuments_.review: The game has a very addictive and compelling structure if you are the type of player who likes to explore thoroughly and grind a bit to stay ahead of the curve in your RPGs. Basically, most gear in the game is constructed from materials dropped by enemies, and repeatedly using said gear unlocks most of your important magical abilities. There are two separate systems for gaining better stats by killing enemies: from gaining experience and leveling up, and from collecting colored orbs and using them on a Final Fantasy X type grid, where the latter system also unlocks some magical abilities and some items/gear. Additionally, stats are also modified by placing items on the pans of a magical scale, where you have to balance item specific bonuses and getting the weight balance right. There is also a crafting system where you can create a variety of items from several magical recipe books. The 8 hour postgame/postscript adds additional systems that are beyond the scope of this review. The character progression systems are wonderfully complex and interlocking, but still easy to grasp early in the game. The game makes great use of an act system and restrictions on how far you can progress on the grid to restrict the current possibility space to make short term goals achievable and clear. When I got to a new act, I could not wait to grind the new enemy types for the materials/items, build all available gear, get the corresponding magical abilities and advancing on the grid system until the next hard lock.The game has a quite convoluted story focused on time travel. I personally liked most of it, but at times I mashed the progress button hoping to get along to the next farming spot ... The quality of the story varies a lot between different segments. Looking back at the game, the best and worst segments were sometimes contained in the same act.The graphics seemed off-putting at first, like a botched up-resing job of a game that may have looked better with a more pixelated look, but I got used to the visual style. The 2d traversal and combat feel great and contribute to how addictive it is to collect materials/items for the character progression systems.In conclusion, this is a well structured and frankly pretty addictive action RPG. The game is great for people who have a hard time getting into games and remaining interested in them, where the clarity of the game's structure and your short term goals are a big part of this.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game.The difficulty is pretty high if you don't grind your personal and weapons XP. _childDocuments_.review: First thing first, I should say two facts about the game before anything. Supposedly this game mostly made by one Japanese person and finished in a very long time - about 15 years afaik- . I guess the aim was making a grand jrpg. Did he managed to make a grand jrpg game by himself in 15 or so years. Yes. Did he also made a great jrpg. Hell yes! Truly an another showcase of so called 'human spirit'. You should not judge this game by its graphics. Its not about that. Its about obtuse jrpg mechanics that we love. Ofcourse there will be mind bending, twisty grippy storylines. Fighting with basic mobs or important bosses (apart from couple enemies) was delightful and satisfying, never a dull moment. It contains very iconic themes but lets not spoil them here, though you could guess them. I am amazed that the whole experience was so smooth, no bugs or anything. Lightning fast and reliable, from top to bottom. I have got even suprised by some very fitting kick ass tunes. Everything was better than I expected. There is a reason for some random ass indie jrpg to get very impressive reception. This is truly a great game, it showcases the meticilous, passionate and caring touch of its creator

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the mixed media art style and open license music fool you, this game is pure crack. _childDocuments_.review: I genuinely do not understand what people see in this game.What 11 hours I've wasted on it have been filled with banal, rote combat where nearly every weapon feels the same, and the only interesting form of progression that doesn't feel like a checklist (Scales) is dripfed at a snail's pace so its potential goes completely ignored as of yet. Combat devolves into "hammer X to shred every single enemy until you reach the room with ones that barely telegraph and then stunlock you to an instant death because what the ♥♥♥♥ are iframes?" and the game has the audacity to do the Resident Evil thing where you get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ off to your last checkpoint upon death, whereupon you repeat room after room after room of this banal ♥♥♥♥♥. In a game where one unlucky enemy combo can take you from full health to the morgue within a second that is not a fun thing to deal with, especially when it gets stingy with checkpoints."Oh but it gets better at 20/30/50/100 hours i-" ♥♥♥♥ OFF.This could be the second coming of Jesus come the 20 hour mark but I don't accept that cope for any other game so I'm not hearing it for this one. _childDocuments_.review: Rating: 9/10. I beat the game on Hard and got every achievement.An amazing RPG experience: great combat, awesome visuals, epic boss battles and a lovable cast of characters. The story isn't anything profound but it has lots of twists and does get pretty involved so if you like a good story, you'll love this game. The environments are beautiful with only a few out of place elements. It also rewards exploring and backtracking to find hidden loot.It does have some bad anime tropes in it but not enough to detract much from the overall experience. _childDocuments_.review: This game was almost exactly what I needed when I needed it--during a frustrating quarantine over the holidays. The gameplay scratches an itch like few games do, with a progression system that is multifaceted, meaningfully impacts your success, and feels nigh endless. Enemies hit hard, but you have good defensive options between your shield, Castlevania backstep, and i-frames on your summons. New abilities come from weapons and armor, which all require certain enemy drops. The game can absolutely be grindy, but I happen to be someone who enjoys a grind that feels rewarding! It also doesn't hurt that most of the area music is fantastic, and the soundtrack is varied in a way that not many games are willing to commit to.As for the story, there's a lot to praise! I think a lot of the appeal is in the storytelling, as the chapters like to play with your expectations. Most chapters are only at their halfway point when you'd traditionally expect them to end. It feels inspired by the tone of games like Nier, taking a mostly straightforward fantasy setting and storyline before throwing in a bunch of twists that cause you to reflect and recognize the horror of the situation. Things gradually unveil themselves as you go on, but not without a number of curveballs and emotional gut punches. While I think the structure and plotline are pretty strong, the characters leave a little more to be desired. In particular, Astlibra Revision has a serious issue with its treatment of female characters. Frankly, the oversexualization and abuse of women in this game would have been outdated 15 years ago when this game was first being written. There are plenty of mentions in the comments about chapter 4 (which is painful to play through at times), but parts like chapter 5's treatment of Shiro are just as bad. Its a distracting and obnoxious feature of a game that otherwise has a lot of merit. I think that Astlibra Revision is best enjoyed by those with nostalgia for action rpgs of the late 90s and early 2000s, who are willing to delve into a darker tone and look past some of the more dated parts of the game. I do like this game quite a bit, but my enjoyment is muddied by the fact that I can't wholeheartedly recommend it to friends who might otherwise be interested if not for the rampant misogyny.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: How did I not know about this at some point in the last 15 years? Well, I'm here for the finished product, and it's amazing. It brings back memories of wiling away lazy weekends with a random Sega Genesis game rented from Blockbuster, yet has all the modern improvements to the genre that have been made since then. Buy this RIGHT NOW if you fondly remember 2d-sidescroller RPGs of Y('s)'ore. Give the demo a try if you lack the nostalgia... there's still plenty to like without the rosy red specs.Challenging but not punishing, always rewarding new toys to play with, well-developed characters you will care for before the half-way point, and a story that never pulls its punches. I don't even know how this game could be improved. It's one of the most solid titles I've played in my 35 years of gaming on console and PC.

_childDocuments_.review: ✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨☑️Reasonable price tag.☑️Delivers a unique RPG experience.☑️Great story.☑️Great character personalities.☑️Great music / boss music.☑️Addicting as hell combat.☑️Menu sound effects are great.☑️Incentive to farm mats for new weapons.☑️A system to grow your character.☑️Build the way you want.☑️Weapons respond well to their WEIGHT.❌A few minor translation errors. ❌Boss HP scaling is absurd. Astlibra is a unique experience. I went in expecting the game to be mediocre due to the trailers showing overly complex designs for the characters and back grounds. But putting that aside, I decided to give it a honest try.It felt like I was a kid again as silly as that sounds, playing games like Maplestory, running around mindlessly mowing down hoards of monsters for the sake of wanting to level up and farm materials for quests / weapon crafting. The story is pretty predictable, as in if you know something the characters do not you have to force them to do what you know you shouldn't, if that makes sense. The story is good regardless, but the desire to want to actually go out and farm materials from monsters and minerals is just as good. I spent 2 hours in the demo area alone just unlocking everything and having fun and another 4+ hours in the lava cave, once again farming. The proficiency system as well gives you a lot of reason to want to keep mowing down enemy after enemy along with the very fair growth system which is kind of similar to Final Fantasy XII with it's "Zodiac" system. Granting you new skills and bonuses in your overall character stats at the cost of grains from your enemies. If you can't afford lets say 5 green, you can use 15 of another colour to grow without having to search for those specific types of monster drops. The issue with Boss HP scaling comes with the difficulty setting. Monsters will gain a lot more damage to you, while also having a lot more health. Easy mode has most bosses and the very first boss you encounter at level 7-9 (unless you power farm) with about 9k health which takes forever, but it's fine cause you take like no damage, however, the harder boss fights have over 20k while being able to one shot you if you haven't been power-leveling or doing proper hit and run tactics.I rarely get this attached to video games, the last time I was this invested in a story was when I was playing through Divinity Original Sin II. Lost in thought and the world I was exploring. Try the Demo. It's very short and doesn't offer to much, but it will at the very least help you understand what the game is all about. It can be a little bit confusing at first, but it's honestly really fun. The combat isn't perfect, but it's a Hack & Slash! Run in, mow down enemies and bosses, farm the materials and get some new gear, unlock new skills and weapons to take on bigger foes and challenges. The game was developed by a solo Japanese developer for over 14 years. KEIZO has a daily job and only worked on the game after he got back home. You know it's not easily to develop a video game on your own especially over 14 years of development. However, with the help of prolific artist Shigatake (Dragon’s Crown) and Haku Tatsufuchi (Magic: The Gathering), and Publisher WhisperGames, the game has got a "Revision" upgrade, which you see here today. Stay and pay attention to the story, it might have it's translation errors here and there, but outside of that, it's pretty solid. It definitely makes me want to play it, not for any other reason than it's good and nostalgic.EDIT:It keeps getting BETTER and BETTER the more I play this game. The time travel, the plot, the story, the characters. My god.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the best Action RPGs ever made. Beautiful 2D graphics, awesome soundtrack, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy anime story with tons of dialogue (easy to skip if you don’t care) and super responsive gameplay. The game is crammed to the ceiling with content. There are so many levels, monsters, bosses, more monsters, more bosses, items, gear, hidden treasures, puzzles, likable characters, vast amounts of difficulty options, arena challenges and more. And don’t get me started on all the RPG systems that are put into this game. It can sound overwhelming when reading about all the systems before starting the game, but Astlibra manages to introduce the systems step by step over dozens of hours of gameplay. The player character can level up, distribute attribute points, learn magic, add items to a magic Libra to improve all kind of stats, distribute points on a giant Sphere Grid, find and craft dozens and dozens of weapons, shields, armors and accessories and unlock boards for every single weapon, armor and accessories to improve them even more. Seriously, if you like to become the baddest of badass RPG characters with fun grinding, optimization and build options, this is your game. But it is also your game if you like crazy anime stories. Or just a laid back, relaxed Hack’n’Slay with nice graphics. You know what? If you like videogames even a bit, you have to get this game. Period. It’s a masterpiece. Some of the best 20€ you can spend on Steam. Get it and spread the gospel. Don’t believe me? Try the demo. And oh, this is the PERFECT Steam Deck game as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty amazing side-scrolling RPG (especially considering small dev team) with reasonably complex combat and thoroughly complex plot. The fighting is similar to Dust: An Elysian Tale, or a Tales series game so far as attacks hitting multiple enemies multiple times per swing, with a millisecond pause per hit and pretty open movement.I will note that the game is clearly anime-inspired: obfuscated plot, teenagers killing gods, and immature male fantasy depictions of women (afaik, the artwork was censored from the original version). Thankfully, it never goes full stereotypical anime with squeaky voices, exaggerated expressions, or vocalizations for every single action or special ability.+Some legitimately impressive artwork+Every NPC has unique portrait and sprite+Every item has detailed inventory art+Equipped gear shows on your character+Plenty of equipment and build options+Pretty fluid combat once you unlock some abilities+Bosses can require some strategy and even bullet hell management+Re-spec nearly anywhere+Infinite inventory (Hint: Don't sell anything! You'll regret it later.)+Varied music of decent quality+All  music tracks playable from main menu+Frequent save points and almost 200 save slots+Multiple difficulties, and can switch during play+An unending amount of things to level up+Nearly every item you master provides a worthwhile bonus+Optional/hidden areas+Game warns you before high-difficulty areas and final bosses+Game notifies you when conditions for true ending met+Arena usually requires clever use of equipment and skills+Fast travel, including to old areas+Can't miss any content (despite what it sometimes seems)+Items and skills to help find missing collectibles+Can skip dialog and cutscenes+Mild puzzle elements, requiring some thought+Enemy abilities telegraphed by sight, sound or nameplates+English translation cleaned up in May of 2023+Can download old translation if you prefer Engrish nostalgia+Can re-bind controls, decent number of options+Perfectly stable for me+A number of unique mechanics+Generally likable characters, with some humor+Time travel taken casually. No headache-inducing cause-and-effect.+Game just doesn't end. Post game and another post-post game and another.+The final post-game adds a bunch of new mechanics+Story, twists, & lore being revealed through credits fadeout+Between 40-100 hours of play, depending on thoroughness and difficulty (took me 74 casual hours for nearly 100% normal)~Story can be confusing at times. Reveals may take tens of hours.~A few plot holes and unresolved minor items~Seriously, how did she provide those panties?~Couple of typos/misspellings and very minor bugs~Combat is largely a button mashing scrum on lower difficulties~Combat effects can obscure detailed bosses or enemy attacks~Some doors have enemies behind them that instantly hit you~Can immediately re-try failed bosses at cost of items you used~Grindy, but rewarding. Not too hard to get OP.~A couple of brief difficulty spikes, even on lower difficulties~Final dungeon can be a bit RNG if you're going for true ending~Doing arenas early can lightly spoil some content~You're going to need a guide to understand a few mechanics~Animations can be hit or miss~Minor swearing, sexual themes and all-but-nudity~Portrayal of women's art and personalities is a little immature-Chests, coins, and force can occasionally get stuck in walls-Some non-critical enemies can get stuck off screen-Final weapon is given too late in the game to be usefulPlayed on:i7-12700, RTX3060, 16GB DDR4-3200 @ 1920x1080Using PowerA Enhanced Wired Controller for Xbox Series X|SNormal Difficulty

_childDocuments_.review: "Castlevania meets Chrono Trigger"That's an apt way of describing this game in a nutshell. Gameplay-wise, I feel it shares the most in common with Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow and Dawn of Sorrow. But even though I can compare it to those two, ASTLIBRA Revision manages to be it's own thing.That being said, go into this game anticipating a lengthy story -- it is an Action RPG, and it very much keeps true to the "RPG" aspect. Personally, I think the story is excellent even though I've yet to finish the game. It starts off a bit slow, but after a certain point everything just clicks, and before you know it you're flying through the game eager to see what happens next.But hey, you don't have to take my word for it: This game has a demo! You can experience the entire First Chapter for free, and your saved game(s) will be carried over into the full game. Try it out for yourself. It may only take 1~2 hours to get through if you're playing it casually, but if you decide to complete absolutely everything? Well, that took me ten hours.And all that effort gave me a running start into the rest of the game. It's worth the price tag, but you don't have to rely on my word on that. All in all, I absolutely recommend this game. It has been a 10/10 experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, Astlibra, is a true hidden gem. Never played any version other than this Revision, but if this is the best version there is, I'm thankful for all the bells and whistles.You play a young man whose childhood friend goes missing after a demon attack, accompanied only by a talking crow. Between your swordplay and the crow's magic, you fight through demons to find other human settlers and hopefully what happened to your old hometown.The graphics are very basic that feel like they were from an RPG maker built, and yet are used so vibrantly and creatively they appear almost high-end, much nicer than most AAA games. Which is good because with how you fight waves of waves of monsters and how one swing of a sword can hit multiple demons at once, there will be a lot of numbers flying around your screen. Battles are also a joy, as they are like a blend of metroidvanias (especially Castlevania Symphony of the Night) with their traversal maps and enemy fighting, with older Ys games and/or Trails games in both the rocking music for each area and how many ways you can get stronger. There are weapons and armor you can craft through enemy parts you get from drops. The weapons have experience bars where mastering them gives you either new skills or points to use said skills. There's a growth map that gives you bonus stats, and even some rare bonuses like equipment and new magic spells, based on mana points you also get from each kill. And of course the basic level up system where you can put points into stats on each level, and total freedom to rearrange them later.Best of all is the story, that hits closer to home than one might expect. Sure it's a tried-and-true metroidvania hack-and-slash singleplayer game where you guide your hero on a journey to slay demons. The dialogue is rather witty about the character's actions, and has some nice levity moments where the hero's androgenous looks gets him mistaken for girl more often than not, or how your crow companion, Kanon, brags they can protect themselves in a bubble when entering water but the hero sheepishly admits that he can't swim. But this is also a story where the core theme is about what it means to live, and how some people would sacrifice everything for others. The first two chapters hit me so emotionally because of how chilling and real it reminds you that it is a world where there are so few people left, making the ones that the hero and Kanon find after eight years of solitude all the more impactful. As well as all the more tragic when some of them are gone, even long before you realize. Special mention goes to Chapter 2, which stars an old couple living in a swamp with a guardian dog. The dog was not initially friendly and even bit the man's fingers off when trying to feed him. But the old man insisted to help the dog to eat and live, as dying is easy but living is worth something. It turns out the dog, Polin, is more than meets the eye since he has a nearby goblin tribe out to get him, but the ending is just beautifully tragic that it got me teary eyed just remembering it. Astlibra is an amazing game that has everything one could ask for: beautifully detailed world, intense and rewarding gameplay with even scaling difficulty levels from kid-friendly to hardcore, killer soundtrack that would make you think Falcom had a hand in it, and a story that just moves you. I regret not playing this sooner, and strongly urge others to give this a try.
