_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra is kinda like if you took Symphony of the Night and made it into a JRPG about time travel instead of a metroidvania.The plot is absolutely BONKERS in the standard JRPG ways, and the characters are fun and likable and interesting. It drags a little towards the end, where you are so powerful nothing challenges you anymore but you still have like 8 hours of game left. I played on Hard and I would say that is a good balance of not too hard but mostly not trivial. The combat is fun if kinda simple, but it's just deep enough to be enjoyable throughout most of the game.This game feels like they squeezed every last drop of potential from it. Every character, every location, every idea is explored to the fullest extent with the resources available, which is admittedly not a bunch, but oh man Keizo does not let that stop him from creating the 40 hour epic he dreamed of. This game is the maximal exploration of what is possible in this particular genre fusion, and I felt compelled to collect and do as much as possible, and that is usually pretty rare for me nowadays, and says a lot about my enjoyment of the game.All in all if you are someone who likes JRPG stories and SotN/Bloodstained gameplay and don't mind some questionable/actually wrong translations occasionally I would easily recommend Astlibra for the full $25, even moreso if it ever goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: An indie masterpiece that blew my mind and transported me to another world. Not since the likes of Cave Story and Soul Blazer has a game surprised me by its depth of story and mechanics. This is one of the only games I have ever 100%ed and it's due to the innate urge to see everything Astlibra Revision has to offer. The creator, KEIZO, has created a side scrolling action RPG that expands its mechanics throughout its episodic structure. Many reviews I read and watched before playing sounded opaque about details, but were lavish with general praise, and this review will be no different. Astlibra's story structure reminds me of Yoko Taro titles, where the overall objective and even plot of the game may shift several times during the story through a variety of viewpoints and "endings".  This game has a plot that kept me guessing and continually thrown off by where it goes. Astlibra, enters the same level of game plot pantheon as: Chrono Trigger, 13 Sentinels, and Nier Automata.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:-Really enjoyable, satisfying hack and slash combat with endless customization. Each weapon, shield, and piece of armor has it's own unique skill that you can learn eventually, allowing you to mix and match different skill sets to fit your playstyle.-Great boss battles (barring a couple, screw that volcano boss).-The actual designs of the bosses and some of the monsters are really cool.-An interesting story about time travel and it's consequences, not just in the story but also in the characters around you.-A BANGING soundtrack.-Plenty of puzzles that don't have logical, but not immediately obvious solutions.-Clever uses of in-game mechanics used in the world. One example I just went through on my playthrough is that in order to pass a blizzard that is constantly pushing you backwards, you have to use the Weight mechanic by putting on your heaviest equipment so that it can't push you back anymore.The Mixed:-The way you buy weapons and armor is strange. Regular items you can just buy with gold, but anything that has a skill attached to it requires specific monster materials along with the regular cost. This can cause a fair bit of grinding, which isn't too bad since the combat is fun, but it is grinding nonetheless.-The artstyle is very hit-or-miss. The game goes for a photorealistic style for the backgrounds, but the character and monster designs are either cartoony or just anime. In practice it looks weird but you get used to it after a while.The Bad-The first 2-3 chapters of the game are kinda boring plot-wise. I get they're still establishing how the world and the time-travel McGuffin works, but not a lot actually happens. Chapter 4 and onwards though are a rollercoaster though.-The translation...needs a few more passes. It's still perfectly readable, but typos and strange phrasings are abundant. I don't have any examples on hand, but in practice it can look something like "We must go to the mountain over there!Hurry follow me!... ..." or something like that. The translation issues can take you out of the game a bit which is a shame since the story is really quite good.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid recommend, an incredible game with an epic plot and meticulous game design and artwork courtesy of Vanillaware's Shigatake. _childDocuments_.review: It's a good action game, a little rough in spots, like areas where the BGM doesn't loop cleanly, but it's all minor nuisances really.It consists of a simple gameplay-loop, you go into a location, which will consist of some 5 to 10 screens, you fight your way through some 4 or 5 different enemies (unique to said area), you unlock all the items available in that area, there's a boss fight, the story progresses, and then you go into a new location.Combat is very fast and responsive,  not so intricate, you have a few different moves, but you couple regular melee attacks with powerful magical attacks/buffs  (that are activated by entering directional commands, kinda like a fighting game but not quite)Progression is multi-faceted:- you have your regular leveling system, just gaining exp from defeating  enemies, then distributing your points in different stats- there's what the game calls the "grow system" which is this huge tree of, mostly, minor stat bonuses, that you get by spending a type of energy you get from defeating enemies, there are 6 different types of said energy, and you'll need a balance of them all (different enemies give off different types) to complete the whole tree, you can also get new magic skills and improve said skills in this same tree- The game has MANY pieces of equipment, and each  has it's own progression of sorts, in which, while wearing/wielding an item, all experience you gain by killing enemies goes towards said item "mastery", when mastering an item you gain a new ability OR a crystal used to activate said abilities (it's a basic balancing system, for example, you have 8 crystals, and 10 abilities to chose from, some abilities need 3 crystals, some 4, some 1, and you have to decide which ones to enable)And it's all very satisfyingI also like how the game respects the player's time, for instance you can respec every time you level up, or at any time in specific locations, plus you don't have to worry about missing any content since, after a certain point in the story progression, you can revisit any previous area to get anything you might have missed.The story is your usual anime-grade nonsensical stuff, but it's alright

_childDocuments_.review: On a gameplay basis, I can recommend this game. On a story basis, I can mostly recommend this game.The gameplay is genuinely REALLY great,  and I thoroughly enjoy the progression and systems in the game. It is so meaty in that aspect, and I will continue to play it to the end. I will also continue to play to the end because the story is serviceable and good for the most part. I say for the most part because none of the characters are really all that deep, nor do they have a ton of character. When you boil down multiple female characters to fawning over the main character or being in awkward situations with him, or just straight up saying weird fetishy things ("Wake up now or I'll pull off your pants! Wake up now or I'll put my sweaty feet on your face!"), it really just feels out of place and weird. Also, playing off a lesbian relationship as goofy and non-serious in the face of demise left a bad taste in my mouth. What feels even more weird and out of place is a weirdly literally romanticized sibling relationship between two characters. It's seems like it's supposed to be serious, which really ruins the impact of any moments between those two characters. It just turns those moments into a weird semi-pedophilic creepy relationship. I can recommend this game for the gameplay and most of the story, but I feel that those uncomfortable beats in the story so far should be mentioned. It really caught me off guard and soured my view on the game somewhat.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pleasantly surprised when I played this game. It perfectly fulfilled my expectations for a game of this genre after playing "13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim." The story is just as captivating as other JRPG+sci-fi+cute girl games like "Nier" and "13 Sentinels."While these types of games may not be extremely popular worldwide, I personally really enjoy them. However, I have to point out one thing. The script relies heavily on character illustrations. Many times, the reason I kept playing this game was that my wives (referring to the characters) are incredibly beautiful. I would be devastated if they died. If it were a man or an ugly woman who died, I wouldn't bother risking my life to save them. Consequently, the plot wouldn't progress either. As for the protagonist, his only motivation might be to save himself and the world.Later in the text, it's mentioned that the gods specifically designed these scripts to train the male protagonist and challenge the rules established by the Creator. However, these scripts also seem too coincidental. It's stated that the male protagonist is the only one to reach the end among tens of thousands of parallel worlds. It's also said that the Divine Balance is actually a device to restart the entire floating island, not just time and space travel. Furthermore, it's mentioned that time and space travel did occur, and the gods bore the consequences. It's also said that the gods have abandoned humanity but want to train them to fulfill their purpose. Honestly, as I progressed, I found the setting of the script somewhat confusing. These settings are actually inconsistent. If the Divine Balance isn't a time and space travel device but just a repeated restart, then there's no need for the goddess to pay the price. The true time traveler is the artificial intelligence Anubis, who can send consciousness back in time. But that has nothing to do with the gods.Overall, I feel that the author intentionally tried to make the script more logical and scientifically convincing, but it ended up creating some contradictions.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it.  There was something about the basic game play that I found entertaining and satisfying.  There are a couple of issues.  There is the usual reserve difficulty curve, as the chapter 1 & 2 bosses are probably the hardest in the game.  Some difficulty spikes when a new chapter hits and the occasional infuriating RNG streaks.  You really want all the equipment in the game.  Despite all that it was worth playing.A few tips for a new player.  Once you get Aigis blocking becomes very safe.  Few attacks cannot be blocked, and while some will just guard crush you that is a stat/gear issue.   Energy Drain is incredibly powerful as it is fairly easy to bait attacks and use a summon/magic to heal.  Certain summons (Blade Waltz) are basically full heals during bosses with Energy Drain because of how long the invulnerability lasts and how much the character moves.  Ranged attacks are completely viable.  The bow kind of sucks, but knives & the crossbow are quite powerful.

The writers did not have the talent to tell a coherent time travel story.The characters are boring and one note. Every female character exists to be sexualized. It is not easy to develop a video game on your own. 14 years of development is just too long for anyone. However his love to video games and his will to continue made KEIZO come this far. Mr. KEIZO has given his all to this game.The game has a subtitle called "Proof of Life". As one player commented, it is indeed the proof of life of Mr. KEIZO himself!I respect Mr. KEIZO with my heart and would like to invite you all to join this unique journey of returning to the golden age of JRPGs!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly a masterpiece. KEIZO's 15 years of work really paid off, he made something truly special here. It's been awhile since I couldn't put down a singleplayer game, and since I played something where the pure passion of the developer was tangible while playing. Story is excellent (though I'm a sucker for time travel and the butterfly effect, and we ignore how cringe chapter 4 was) but more than that I just love the compelling sense of adventure it provides, and just how ridiculous the scale of it gets. Gameplay is fantastic and incredibly addictive, I never got tired of experimenting with new builds. There's tons of ways to consistently get a bit more powerful, and there's a lot of incentive to collect all of the weapons and gear and level them up - they're always useful since you unlock skills that can be used with any build. Also this game is BEEFY. Every time you think the story is coming to and end it just keeps going, and going...but at the same time it doesn't outstay its welcome. Just the main story took me almost 70 hours to complete (though I really took my time grinding and making sure I didn't miss any secrets because I was having a ton of fun). Postscript really took me by surprise, because I wasn't expecting it to introduce new mechanics. Also while the DLC doesn't add too much to the story - if you enjoyed the combat you'll have a lot of fun with it, and I wasn't ready for it to be over, so I was happy to have it. Very highly recommend playing it on at least hard mode, because while the game isn't afraid to kick you in the ♥♥♥♥ -  it's SO rewarding when things click for you and you finally beat that bastard boss that was giving you trouble. Absolute must play for any lovers of oldschool JRPGs and well worth 2x the price. While I certainly wasn't expecting it, it very quickly snuck into my top 10 favourite games of all time. Actual 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I didn't think I would summons and fights big tiddies anime girls. Literally one of my favorite games right after NieR:Automata including the musics which is a really high praise because I  NieR OST and I swear I heard vocaloid in at least one of the songs and damn it was good. You have to play this game to experience the story yourself, I think this game is best play on hard.When I first saw this game on release I thought it was weird base on the gameplay trailer, enemy movements kinda stiff like papercut animations, the game seem to have microstutters or pause for a bit when you hits your enemies, I thought it was a low quality product but trust me it's not, I was dead wrong, those things are crucial to the gameplay. This game may look like a metroidvania but it's not, it's more like a liner game where each chapter take place in an area that you can come back later, there's no one big map with many zonesI highly recommend trying the combat demo, if you like the basic combats you gonna loves this game. I played on Hell and only just finished like half postscript. This game is the definition of underrated, it has no reason to be this good for this price, normally I don't even like JRPG (mostly anime games not Janpanese games) or side scroller.The combat actually has a lot of depth in it, at first I thought it would just be stand in one place spamming attack button to build up ST to use possession skills but the more you play the better the combat gets. You can do melee attack, range magic attack, guard, perfect guard, back step, double jumps, air dash, upper cut, downward slash, guard counter, shield bash, shield charge, you can also change how some of your attack works later on.There are many weapon types and each has different basic attacks moveset, swords have medium range and speed, daggers are short but really fast, hammers are really good at breaking enemy poise/posture which will stun them for awhile, magic wands are crazy good at ST build up but need to be used at melee range, spear has long range and medium speed but need to be two handed, big swords/hammers are slow but have highest damage per hit. This is not a game where you pick a weapon you like and stick with it, expect to change weapons a lot depend on what you're fighting, there's a very early weapon you can get that will help you cheese most of the arena challengesThere are 6 elements in the game, each has 5 possession skills that you will slowly unlocks. They are really fun to use and you will be using them a lot as they are your best damage source, they also provide iframes, you can get healed if you're attacked during possesion skills later on so they are very important.Boss fights are awesome, it's like a dance where you have to learn the boss movesets, some boss are just bullets hell though. There's only one boss that I despite in this game even in postscript, it's literally just a bad boss design that is unfun and unfair to fight on high difficulty, even in the lowest difficulty this boss is still a menace. It's chapter 3 boss which is like a breaking point for this game, the story will only get better after chapter 3 but it is also the worst boss fight I've ever experienced in any video games, I swear killing Sword Saint Isshin in Sekiro is less frustrating than this stupid boss. The boss is At one point the game turned into a which is nicheI do have some minor nitpicking: There's absolutely no  what so ever, even after a long boss fight or a long cutscene, you literally have to manually save at a checkpoint.If you die in a boss fight you'll have the option to restart the fight but that doesn't mean the game will load previous save because there's no auto save in this game, any consumable items you used will be gone.Later on there will be moments where so many things are happening on the screen you can't see the enemy animations so you don't know when to guard or dodge so you just take damage for no reason.Relic soldier's attack hitbox is bigger than what the animation shows.Chapter 7 by far is the worst (it's only like 30m or the first half of the chapter but still), no karon, can't walk without dying in 3-4 hits at level 50, shield can only block so many hits before it break, long walks without save spot, not even after a CUTSCENE, you have to fight 2 BOSSES without karon, I know there's a rare item that you can use to destroy mobs and probably intended to be used for this chapter but I don't like using items, it isn't fun but neither do stripping the player's abilities.There should be a setting to adjust brightness and contrast, the map sometime too dark so you can't appreciate the detailsSome attacks will just blend in with bright background and you can't see anything.This is probably the longest review I've ever written and that's how much I like this game, one of the must play game just like Nier:Automata.Edit: Finished the postscript. Wow, what a journey, I've played nearly 100 games, 10 000 hours on steam and this has to be one the most amazing story in gaming I've ever experienced, my second favorite story ever after One Piece which I still love after probably over 10 years. Thank you for creating this masterpiece KEIZO-san.

_childDocuments_.review: A Diamond in the rough. It's all here, though. Better than decent story, fantastic music, great combat. Expect a lot of grinding if you're a completionist like me, but the rewards have so far been 100% worth the effort.If I have a single gripe, it's this: While the game keeps the fanservice and horniness to a pretty low level for the most part, when it does come up, it's the kind of writing that you'd expect from a 14 year old. I've seen worse in AAA titles, but I feel like it doesn't add anything to the story or characters when it happens, and takes away from the experience. Thankfully, they've been pretty short, so easy to get through and forget.Don't let my above statement prevent you from giving the game a shot. Edit, now that I've Finished the game. It's a solid 9.6/10. IT would have been my easiest recommendation for a game, and a nearly perfect score, but DEAR LORD, the unnecessary horny dialogue, boss models and cutscenes. _childDocuments_.review: This isn't a clear recommend. The game is very long (60+ hours), and while I had a good time with it, I'd give it an overall rating of 7/10. Was it worth the time commitment for the content? I lean towards yes, but am on the edge.Pros- Decent plot that has good pacing with gradually escalating stakes from start to finish. - Solid music, solid art direction- The game could have ended at several points and been good enough, but the developer has a clear obsession w/ this game and would not let it end until he was finished. - Fun allusions to other doujin games and somewhat obscure Japanese franchises. If you're this deep into doujin games, you probably were hyped to see Shade in the music credits. Keizo gets it.Cons:- There is nothing truly new here. The game is high quality from start to finish, but there wasn't anything mind blowing. This is why the game is hard to recommend, it's requires such a commitment, and while it has several high points, there was nothing euphoric in here for me.- There's varying opinions on the story. For me personally, it was whatever, although I think the way it was presented was fantastic. I will not remember most of the characters names in a week or two.- Combat gets stale around the midpoint, full completion is a boring grind. Part of this was brought upon myself by playing on a high difficulty (see footnote)- All females in the game are overly sexualized to a degree that it distracts from the plot. Boss characters have massive breasts with hand crafted jiggle animations. I couldn't take these characters seriously.One note, I played the game on hell mode, and I absolutely do not recommend it. Enemies kill you so quickly on hell mode, compelling you to grind right before major story beats until you find breaking combos towards the second half. End game bosses have so much health that you're compelled to go for a full completion playthrough. I don't know how difficult hard mode is compared to hell mode, but I imagine that lower difficulties would have given me more flexibility to rush through the early game.

_childDocuments_.review: ASTLIBRA is an absolute gem of a game. Its an action JRPG/platformer with all of its standard fare, but with the added bonus of everything being really well done, having good gameplay mechanics, an amazing soundtrack, and a fantastic story to keep you immersed in the game.The game is an action JRPG, so nothing turn-based about the gameplay. The action is smooth and really fine-tuned, at least in my opinion, and that becomes especially apparent as you grind and raise your stats. One part of the game has some elements in it that are added to the existing game later on and it opens up the possibilities for all manner of grinding and stat min-maxing. The weapons handle different and weight will determine how fast or slow you go with a weapon based on what type of weapon it is (some weapons are slower than others, and some are really fast). Weapon range and handling also play a factor in how well a fight goes. On top of this, there is a growth tree that can up you stats and give you summoning skills that are really helpful through out the game (and some are so helpful that they are on par with the most powerful summons you can obtain). On top of all of that, there is the Libra system where you can put items on a scale that gives you even more stats or resistances and even allow for more money/force (used in the growth tree)/experience gain. Balancing it perfectly allows you to get the stat boosts and such from both sides of the scale without them being diminished on one side versus the other. The weapons, armors, and shields are all items that you can play with and level which will net you either some new abilities that you can select later or magic crystals that will allow you to equip said abilities if you are not using the item in question. If you equip the item with an ability, you can choose to equip that ability with no extra cost to your magic crystal pool, which is a great way to maximize your usage of abilities to their fullest. Accessories do not come with any leveling mechanic so they are static (at least until the latter half of the game). There is also a new customization mechanic later in the game that will enhance weapons, armors, shields, and accessories that can not only up the stats of everything, but allow for changes to abilities or adding new stats, which was a interesting answer to the usual "I've grinded all the stuff, now what?" question and even attachments that can be added to them (although most of it comes with RNG, so there is a reason to continue grinding to get the best stuff). The story itself is absolutely wonderful, well written, and executed so well done that it ties up all manner of loop-holes very well, including ones that you didn't even know it had (or forgot about which is a phenomenal surprise when you realize some things later on or remember certain characters). It has its tense moments, which are assisted by the gameplay obviously, its funny moments, its sad moments, and some of the twists you don't completely see coming either. It does well in foreshadowing some events and even some inconsequential story pieces end up showing up when you least expect it, There are some things that are predictable and, again, this is a JRPG so it has many of the staples embedded in the story, but it works in its favor rather than to its determent, or at least I think so. Its been a while since I've played another game as enjoyable as this one. I absolutely recommend this game to anyone looking for a good JRPG to enjoy your time with that has the right amount of gameplay mechanics, story, and overall enjoyment that can be found in ASTLIBRA. I hope to see more games from this developer that are as fun and enjoyable as this game was.

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and well-designed action adventure game similar to the Ys games on the SNES or Zelda 2. The gameplay is action-based combat with RPG elements in a sidescrolling format. The gameplay is tight and reactive, it's very easy to fumble your movement options if you get sloppy, but the default difficulty is forgiving enough to generally let you recover from mistakes. The difficulty curve is gentle until about Chapter 6, where the game spikes hard and basically tells you to get ready to rumble for the rest of the game. The system mechanics are extremely robust, with tons of options to make your numbers go up and to get stronger. And you need all of them, because if you don't you're going to get chewed up and spat out. DO NOT ignore the Grow board, it is a bigger source of stats than actually levelling up and your actual main stat progression method. There are a couple puzzles that are a little frustrating in the way the game signposts the answers, but there are answers to them here and there if you want to look for them and can't get the answers on your own. The translation is a little stiff in the beginning, but don't let it put you off. The plot develops steadily and goes from a charming 80s style 7 to 11. I found the plot compelling and interesting, and they eventually wrap up all the core questions of the game. The game apparently had been in development a long, long, time, and the breadth of content is actually quite staggering once you've broken past the surface layers. The game is absolutely worth your time and money. If you like this kind of thing, get it!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall rating for me: 9.5/10This game looks great, the controls are tight, the music does a great job at being interesting and appropriate for the locations, environments are highly varied, enemy design is top-notch, combat is fast-paced and frenetic, and the story is absolutely incredible.  But none of these things compare to how interesting the progression systems in this game are.  You will be given a huge variety of methods to increase your character's abilities, with new systems appearing throughout your journey even into the endgame.  The epilogue alone introduces multiple new systems that completely redefine every aspect of the game if you delve into it.  In short: There's plenty here to keep min-maxers busy.  These systems are accompanied by some great QoL features (such as being able to freely reallocate skill points as needed) that make grinding optional but still quite rewarding.  Each piece of equipment feels unique when you get it, and EVERYTHING is useful in the endgame, so you have a ton of freedom to play how you like.  The only criticism I have of the game is that difficulty settings have no impact other than boosting/nerfing enemy stats, which means the highest difficulty is just smacking around slimes for 3 hours while trying not to get hit more than once or twice.  Higher difficulties slow the game down without making enemies more interesting to deal with, but given that this is the industry standard anyway it's more of a nitpick than a real complaint. For its price this game is an absolute must buy imo.  Don't sleep on this title!

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing old-school adventure game / RPG's when they were new. Your Final Fantasys, Secret of Mana, Castlevania, Act raiser, Valkyrie Profile etc. There's been a drought of JRPG's lately, and I sorted Steam by the JRPG tag to see what was up. Most of the games were fine, but nothing really piqued my interest or my eye. Then I saw a game with a funny name, terrible graphics and "overwhelmingly positive" for the reviews. I scanned the page, watched the trailer and checked out some images. The old-school progression and side-scrolling combat looked fun, but even an older dude like myself was completely turned off by the graphics.I am so glad that I gave it a chance despite my first impressions. This is one of the best games I have played in the past decade, perhaps even in my lifetime. I put this game up there with other genre-defining titles such as Final Fantasy VII/IX/X, Nier, Nier Automata, Legend of Dragoon and the likes of Squaresoft/Enix's blockbusters. If you are anything like myself and are interested in this game but turned off by the graphics, please give this game a chance. With this out of the way, I'll get into the review proper, taking the most time with the gameplay systems and tackling graphics last.: Gameplay is a 2D side scrolling action game like Castlevania is. The thing here is the game has MANY avenues for character progression, with some of the options being incredibly interesting and different from what the industry has done previously. These features heavily influence the aforementioned 2D side scrolling action combat. You have an equipment system where nearly every piece of equipment in the game has a skill which you need to earn enough EXP to unlock (Think Final Fantasy IX). These range from simple stat boosts to straight-up entirely new mechanics that you will weave into your gameplay loop.You have a "scale" system, where you have to put in items you collect on your adventure (Potions, food items, materials, monster drops, etc) to gain bonus stats. Each item has a weight value attached to it, and your goal is to balance these sets of scales according to the benefits the item in question brings and the weight it has attached to it. This causes a lot of thought based on what stats you value and how to make them work in the confines of the weight attached to them.And finally you have "possession" skills that rely on a meter you fill up with active combat attacks. These skills are varied, you can swap them out for other skills, and using them makes you invincible for a short period upon activation. These skills range from buffs, to attacks, to utility and more.What makes this game such a masterpiece is how all of these systems work together to form such a fluid combat system that has an immense amount of depth and fluidity. You learn the basics in the first 5-10 hours of gameplay, and you're constantly having new tools available to the player as you progress but nothing makes anything else obsolete. They just give you more options and more tools to mix up the flow of combat by weaving these options together. Most of these tools have either cool downs/resource bar requirements to work and how you play the game will drastically change depending on how aggressive you want to be in encounters. You COULD run it, hit the boss a few times and run out and block, or you could mix up Possession skills for invincibility to block a huge boss attack, be aggressive, block a few attacks with your shield - but now your block gauge is gone and you have no meter for Posession skills, so you backslide for the iframes THROUGH a boss attack to get enough meter and shield gauge to continue the flow of combat.I could honestly go on and on about simple things, such as how the hitstop slows combat down enough so that you can see the insane amount of action on the screen at once so you can make a decision that would not be afforded to you if you were playing passive and NOT slowing down the combat with the hitstop. It is so fluid and masterfully executed that I'm beyond impressed that a single guy managed to pull off what I consider to be one of the best combat systems I have ever played in a game. The combat is as intricate as you want it to be. The better you, as the player, will determine how aggressive and relentless you will be. - The story is excellent. I wasn't expecting much, but I was honestly really impressed with what I got. It started out as a simple story with some intrigue, light-hearted themes with some melancholy thrown in. As you continue to play the game the world, its characters and its plot opens up and becomes more and more intriguing with the stakes being raised through your action. I can't go too in depth without spoiling the game, but I will say that this game can blend future-dystopian themes with gods, folklore, demons and mechs. What's amazing here is how Mr Keizo has let these themes be disjointing when they need to be to suit the story, and seamless and fluid when that is important to the story. Nothing touched on in this story is pretentious, and the story itself is pretty simple as far as a story involving time travel can go. But it's humbling, it's comforting and while it doesn't reach the insane heights' something like NIER does, it's a competent and compelling story in its own right. You end up caring for the characters, the world and the story. The only issue is some rough translation work that can make some of the script come across as a little "stiff" at times, but it's not too intrusive to take away from the experience. - The music is fantastic. There's your standard fantasy violin tracks, piano pieces and it all is really competent and makes the world feel alive. When the story needs it, it even has modern tracks like some electronic with vocals that honestly sounds wonderful. I felt like each piece fit the location really well, with the exception to a couple tracks that honestly really did not fit their encounters. JRock when fighting a fiery demon god? I can dig it but it just didn't really fit and kind of took me out of that fight. - And here's what I saved for last, and with good reason. Out of all the cons I have for the game (Some area design from a gameplay standpoint, enemy placement, enemy design from a gameplay standpoint) graphics are objectively pretty poor. The developer, Mr Kezio, was virtually a one-man team and did what he could with what he had. The terrain is especially jarring, but when you take into account the fact it was one man working on this I feel like it's forgivable. I would argue that perhaps due to the limitations on the graphics that the other systems were allowed to be so fleshed-out and shine like they do. The graphics ended up appealing to me after a while, perhaps Stockholm syndrome. The quality improved a lot as the game went on, which I have to assume was due to the game being a 14-year passion project by a lone guy. If anybody is going to be turned off from the game, I have to imagine this is where it will be. I hope you will overlook them, as the game itself is a complete masterpiece, but I understand if you cannot. - This is perhaps one of the best, most fluid and cohesive games I have ever played in my life. The gameplay is unbelievably well executed and imagined, and the story and the supporting systems add a level of depth and versatility that is refreshing and honestly startling given how this was made by one guy. This game is a masterpiece and deserves your attention. I could go on, but character limits and all.

_childDocuments_.review: Having beaten both the main game and the postgame, I can safely say:  This is the best 2D RPG I've ever played in my life, no contest.  Minus a small stumble with an early boss and chapter 8 stumbling a bit heavily on mechanics and frustration factor, there's so much incredible good packed everywhere around it that it's beyond easy to just say "Yeah that's just That One Level and That One Boss." and leave it at that, and honestly, it comes right before the introduction of one of my favorite mechanics in the game.The game's a great riot, Hard is genuinely challenging, and there are difficulties beyond for those who truly like to push themselves.  Fun, steady gameplay progression, pretty fluid controls, a very fun fighting system, a unique and fun to play around with magic system, a whole grid of powering up to do, a skill system based on mastering weapons...there's genuinely not a single part of this game I don't like.If I had to pick one nitpick...some of the skills are bound to inconvenient buttons, IE float and block both being holding Down on input, and some attacks can get lost in the utter kerfuffle that is mid to late game magic spam with screen spanning attacks from you and the boss alike, making you suddenly die to something you never even saw.  Though, fairly, that's also your fault for filling the screen with clutter before you knew what was coming~.You're doing yourself a favor by picking it up and playing it.  I got it in a bundle with Chained Echoes, and I originally wanted Chained Echoes, knowing nothing about this game.I didn't stop playing it on my Deck until I'd beaten the whole thing.  Genuinely, I love this little game.  Thanks Keizo, looking forward to seeing what's next.

_childDocuments_.review: Whew, well.  Like I always tell people. I rarely write reviews, and when I do its either for a game that deserves it meaning mostly its positive, or a short one which I will remove later being negative, like I did for RCG2 due to its release state.  Considering I been playing video games longer than most steam users have been alive, I pretty much seen it all.  Well thats enough intro  lets get down to it. Astlibra, a hidden gem of a game, coming out of nowhere.  Quite honestly in my opinion, could be a Indie nominee for the VGAs *I feel sorry for the VGA host, he almost, almost got to have one go without incident, just right there at the end, poor guy* And I say this due to how well created the game is, harking back to the old era of video games.  I see alot of primary influences in it, particularly the old Y's games, and a little bit of Drakken 2 Dragon View.  What influences you may ask?  Oh I can name quite a few, even seen references to them.  Final Fantasy, Dragon Quest, Zelda, Chrono Trigger, heck even Metroid for a particular area.  The developers  who seemingly spent 15+ years creating this have obviously been playing video games for a long time, and are all what the Japanese term calls them "Your everyday Salaryman"  thus why it took them so long to create this.The basic plot of a very, very long story, which, heavily influenced by both Chrono Trigger, and a very, specific game for a twist over midway thru,  is that you are a Silent Protagonist orphan who as a boy was attacked by Demons invading your village and tried to run away with your childhood sweetheart.  You both got surrounded, and then you lost consciousness as you got attacked by a giant powerful demon, only to wake up in a cabin in the middle of absolute nowhere with a talking Raven.  You realize you are far, far from human civilization, so far that their are not even any demons around since they tend to stay near human settlements only for some reason.  You and the raven who seems to act as your surrogate father, tries to live life in this cabin, but your urge and desire to go back to your village and find the girl you have feelings for is too much, and you keep attempting to leave, only to realize the forest surrounding your cabin goes on seemingly forever. The raven then relents and decides to go with you and guide you.  The two spends eight, entire years, walking thru the frontier with no demons or humans in sight until finally you do come across civilization at last, and you are now a fully grown man.  Thus the adventure truly begins. The game uses some very beautiful background images, similar to how the SNES days have done it, with excellent character and monster animations with some enemies looking like they been hand drawn.  Its a action RPG combat system with near infinite stat growth, you can constantly keep getting stronger but to a certain extent.  You can gain levels, get these monster essences called Force, to boost your stats in a sort of stat board placement system similar to what FF 10 uses.  However to keep you from getting too overpowered, their is a maximum you can go on this Placement System which is defined by locks you cannot open until you reach the next chapter.  You also have a skill system that uses Magic Crystals that you collect via various means.  You gain these skills by mastering the massive assortments of weapons, shields and armor.  Most of these will have a skill attached that once mastered, you can either use the skill for free long as you use that piece of equipment, or assign Magic Crystals to that skill to have it on permanently for as long as you have crystals assigned.  This allows you to customize your character to your play style.  All this allows you to do basically three different types of builds I primarily see.  Want to be fast and defensive? Use a one hand weapon with shield,  with a shield you can block most attacks so long as they dont break your block gauge.   Spec to skills and stats that favors this.  Want to use a two handed weapon or thrusting weapon?  Spec for agility, use skills that boosts the range or speed of these weapons.  Want to use a magic staff and throw out fireballs and lightning like a wizard?  Spec for Magic over ATK and select skills that compliments Staff usage.  You also have a summon system called Possession, which uses button inputs to dictate what you summon.  You earn these summons via the Stat board and they are categorized in six different elements. Fire, Water, Earth, Wind, Dark and Light.  You can set these summons however your play style or need is and they use a gauge called ST or Stamina which you regain simply from attacking.  Standard play loop is, attack until bar fills up, then use possession, then repeat.   Possessions are a way to cause massive damage all over, or to get yourself out of a bad situation.  I personally like using possession skills where you become the Summon for a fixed period of time allowing me to consume healing items in safety if needed.  Due to near infinite stat growth, and of two, new mechanics that comes up post game, I wont spoil those, but I do wonder why the developer did not put those at the start.  I highly recommend to play the game on either Hell or Impossible difficulty, since the game seems balanced around those two difficulties.  You can change difficulties at will at any point until chapter 2.  Once you go past chapter 2, you can only go down in difficulty and cannot go up again.  Which is a weird design decision, I played the game on Hell and often wished I could put it up to Impossible since I am a completionist and I often will find ways to circumvent or cheese anything difficult.  I still had quite a challenge on Hell mode, but most bosses just seemed too easy due to the amount of grind I would put in and simply due to collecting all the weapons and armor to gain more skills or Magic Crystals.  In short, if you want to be lightly challenged, play it on Hell, otherwise, I recommend Impossible if you want to at least 90 percent the game.  Many enemies and bosses can become bullet hells where dodging or blocking is needed depending on your playstyle.  Difficulty will determine how much you need to grind or simply be patient and dodge and block as much as possible. Just keep in mind the game has Near, infinite, stat growth.  You CAN with enough grinding, be so overpowered that even the true final boss, or the optional final arena boss, will be as weak as kittens to you, even on impossible, but that would take a tremendous amount of grind, and you would have gone and collected and done everything long before then either way, unless you get unlucky collecting....Hearts, at the near end. Wont spoil that. Now, the soundtrack.  Honestly again, I see influences from past games on this, particularly Y's.  Now most JRPG fans would have played a Y's title or two, and would know the awesome high energy soundtracks that tends to come from that franchise.  They did pretty well with this in Astlibra,  using the same high energy seen in Y's.  The first area, Volcano area, and Demon Castle being very notable.  Sounds fantastic and makes you pumped to play which is what I believe the developers were intending.  Overall and I will say this, I have over 200+ games in my backlog.  Many on steam, many physical.  I have in my immediate concern to play and finish right now, Harvestella, Dragon Quest Treasures, Star Ocean Divine Force, Made in Abyss Binary star, Strangers of Paradise Final Fantasy Origins, and Sword and Fairy 7.  FF and DQ being in my top 5 franchises to complete start to finish. Yet, I chose to play this over them. Give it a shot. It well deserves your attention.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing RPG platformer that I can't recommend enough. It's a sidescrolling 2D RPG (Think Metroidvania with less focus on exploration) with a very cool skill and combat system. Using your partner to use "possession skills" you can summon or transform into various spirits of different elements using a very intuitive casting system (almost like fighting game inputs rather than menu navigation), in addition to your weapons, armors, and shields teaching you passive skills (similar to Final Fantasy IX) and a MASSIVE skill tree to increase your stats and learn new spells. It's also quite long, often with a "just when you think you're done, there's a new arc of the story" factor that feels great. Playing on Hard is a good balance of difficulty, and it's not particularly grindy. With optional bosses, lots of completionist achievements, and postgame methods of improving your character and gear, you'll be fully occupied all the way to the end.The story is actually pretty good too. A lot of twists, turns, drama, and comic relief, none of which overstays its welcome. There is some time travel in the plot so as you can expect things get pretty crazy, but it's never convoluted or hard to follow. The only cons I can really give are bugs so minor as to be negligible (a certain achievement not unlocking until a complete game restart for instance) some translational errors (to instead of too) and in my opinion some of the terrain construction looks a bit odd with how tiles match up. None of this is so obvious or egregious as to be distracting from the overall quality but I would be remiss in not mentioning it. Despite these cons, I can only recommend it. An absolutely masterful RPG and an independent one no less. Not perfect, but just about as close as you can get.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like simple side-scrolling action RPGs like the older Ys titles or Metroidvanias this will be worth playing.  But the more important dive begins with the following questions: Do you like systems in your game?  How about systems within your systems?  How about external systems that allocate into the previous systems, but then allow you to unlock additional systems?!  This game is like a Billy Mays ad where every time you think you figured it out, there's a NEW system that only ADDS to the old, without taking anything away.  This game can be as simple or complicated as you desire, but the complexity is a dream for players who enjoy that kinda' thing.  The story is great, and Nier fans will appreciate some of the seemingly convoluted aspects contained.  Are their flaws?  Plenty.  But when you scroll through the credits in under two minutes you know each of those people put a great deal of care into how the game was delivered.  At worst, you discount the game because "there's other games like it" out there, other 2D Metroidvania-esque whatevers and they might play better.  But at best, you will play the game and enjoy it for what it is.  It was a 110 hour journey for me on the "Hell" difficulty to 100% (I go slow).  I hope others can get a fraction of that time to just give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: A while back, I was fed up and tired of some of the more negative aspects of Astlibra, so I wrote a negative review for it and uninstalled it. But after a week or so, I realized I couldn't stop thinking about the game. So I gave it another shot... and I'm glad I did. I've changed my mind. This is a great game. But the game still isn't perfect, and I want to go over it's flaws first.The game is less of an action-RPG and more JRPG-action. That isn't an inherently bad thing if you like JRPGs, but for me, I've found as I've gotten older I have less patience for these types of games. However, if you hate JRPGs to the core, I think you can stop reading here; you won't like this game. There is an action element to this game, certainly, and being better at action games will give you an advantage, but as compared to skill, your stats are much more of a deciding factor.Speaking of stats, be prepared to grind. But not in the way you may think. There are a ton of things to collect in this game, but what I want to talk about is equipment. Armor, weapons, and shields all can be mastered by killing enough enemies with them equipped, which grants a permanent bonus or skill unlock; even when you don't have the weapon equipped. The thing is, you have to kill so many enemies that there's no way to progress through the game and master weapons naturally; you have to grind enemies over and over again if you want to master everything. Which believe me; you do. The bonuses are too good to pass up and mastering equipment is a big part of this game; that's just how it is.There's also a lot of backtracking. Go A, then B, back to A, then B so you can go to C, then back to B so you can go back to A... etc. It isn't horrible, but I almost rolled my eyes a few times when story events unfolded in such a way that I had to go back to ABC AGAIN.The grinding and backtracking gets in the way of progressing the story, which is cheesy and somewhat predictable... but at the same time, it's charming, and while there are a lot of things you'll see coming a mile away, there are also a few twists you'll never see coming. One of the best elements of the story is the characters, in my opinion. At the end of the game I realized that I was very fond of many of the... "main-side" characters in this game. Many of them had an external struggle or a personal weakness to overcome; a few had neither, some had both. When everything finished, it left me with an immensely satisfied feeling.The game's story drastically improves when the "main game" ends and something called the "post-script" begins. Even though it's called the "post-script", many of the most important events in the game take place and some things that didn't make sense before start to add up. There's even new mechanics added. The post script is about 1/3 of the actual game, I'd say. With more interesting mechanics added(on top of the ones that were already interesting), less grinding and less backtracking, it's easily the strongest part of the game. I hope i'm not giving off the impression that you have to get through 2/3 of the game to get to the "good part", because everything before the post script is still worth playing on it's own, but I do wish the first part of the game played more like the second part. There is still some potential grinding in the postscript if you want to unlock everything though, especially if you had the misfortune to not find certain optional items that you could only find before the postscript... in which case, buckle up, because those items are an extremely rare drop.A couple of other negatives I need to bring up; firstly, there's some odd progression issues in the story, as well as in equipment. You can acquire legendary swords early on that don't even remotely compare to normal equipment you'll find later, and your character will accomplish such unbelievable things that some of the conflicts later in the story seem silly after reflection. Secondly, this game has a few bugs. Reading a book for the very first time doesn't allow you to scroll down to read more text, and there's also a bug with a hidden ability that tells you how many unopened chests are still on-screen; if there are 4 of them you've found and 0 you haven't found, it will tell you 44. Nothing is game-breaking and I've never had the game crash once over 60+ hours so this is just a minor nitpick.From here on out I only have praises to sing. The game's combat system is excellent, it's so good that even someone like me, who normally doesn't like hack-n-slash games, loves it. I don't have anything more to say, it's that good.There's plenty of ways to make your character stronger. You can level up, which gives you crystals to allocate to stats. You can also acquire "force" by defeating enemies, which you can allocate to a growth tree to increase your stats that way. Furthermore, you can place items, which weigh different amounts, on a set of scales to get different kinds of bonuses; which vary by the item. The catch is that obviously, the scales need to be balanced. All this, PLUS all the mountains of equipment in the game, which can be upgraded and customized in the postscript. I wouldn't go as far as to say there's "builds" in this game but I'm willing to bet everybody's endgame character looks at least a little different from eachother's. There's plenty of hidden secrets to find by being attentive to your surroundings. They can be a big help, they're not just cosmetic or very small upgrades, so it pays to pay attention to your surroundings. Furthermore, while they aren't usually in plain sight, they're also not hidden in the kind of old-school, cryptic "how was I supposed to know that" way; if you search for long enough, you should be able to find pretty much everything on your own. Additionally, there's an optional area you can visit to complete challenges to earn even more upgrades.The music is fantastic. I believe most if not all of it is free useage/open source, but it all sounds great and fits what the mood should be. I believe a good soundtrack is one of the most important parts of a game, and this passes with flying colors.The art style is... interesting. I wouldn't say it's amazing, nor would I say it's bad, but I'm not sure I've seen anything that looks quite like this game, and it's grown on me to the point that I'd say I like it.When it's all said and done, I think that this is a special game. Certainly it isn't perfect, but I doubt I'll ever forget it. If you're still on the fence, try the demo.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great game hampered by some odd platforming and obscure puzzles. I know this was a huge labor of love for the developer and it's a very impressive piece of work. I think when I saw all the reviews were overwhelmingly positive I was expecting a masterpiece, however the game would be about a 7ish out of 10 for me personally. I'm sure it's a 10/10 for many people, which is great for them and I'm glad they enjoyed it. I just wanted to add another perspective that will help evaluate whether to spend the money on it or not.Personally I don't think this game is like Castlevania SotN or Bloodstained, more of a linear RPG with similar combat. ====Amazingly beautiful character and sprite artwork (REALLY really nice)Tons of content and optional bosses that can be tricky to beatKaron and Gau have amusing personalitiesIncredibly wide weapon, armor, and accessory options that all look fantasticLots of ability to modify your character build and min/max Earning special attributes from the weapons is a fantastic idea and was well implementedSpectacular looking and very useful spells that are easy to use on the flyThe story premise is interesting and more introspective than mostYou can easily dodge the enemies if you don't feel like fighting themSave points are well spaced and restore lifeDifferent difficulty options make the game accessible to all skill levelsFinding the hidden targets and arrows is entertainingController support is excellentFun achievements to unlock in Steam====The largest issue by far is that It can be very difficult to know what is foreground and background. This complicates progression as it can be difficult to know what to do next... platform assets are not obvious, hidden entrances can only be found by throwing yourself at walls, it would be nice if the background was blurred, had less contrast, was darker, etc.  Music during fighting is frenetic rapid tempo electronica or synth rap that is irritating. This is my second least favorite part of the game. More approachable music would have been preferable. Tons of travelling back and forth solely for the sake of increasing game timeCut scenes with the dialog feel long because of the constant ellipsis and pauses. While I normally love puzzles, many in this game seem obtuse and will require you to consult the web. Dialog has tropey anime stuff baked in  I personally don't like the silent protagonist, but I realize it's an artistic choice. The decision to replay the intro after every chapter is strange, but at least can be skippedSome artwork is taken from photos and is sometimes a 3D view which clashes with the 2D sprites, and the bridges that are a black silhouette are odd. Getting the ingredients you need for crafting can require plenty of mindless grinding until end game when your luck is much higher.Ultimately at the end of the day I feel like the amount of content and effort easily justify the price, I find myself getting a little bored with the slow pacing, running back and forth over the same areas, grinding for drops, not being able to figure out what to do next, and rapid pressing the button to get through slow dialog scenes. I wasn't sure if I would finish the game but it gets better after Chapter 5 and is more enjoyable. My ideal version of this game would make the platforming surfaces more contrasting and obvious and make the background look like the background, add a couple more clues on what the character needs to do next, eliminate the fetch quests back and forth, allow the user to skip the dialog bubbles and pauses with a button press, and include some music that's not high tempo. If you have the patience to deal with the issues listed above, there is much fun and tons of content to be had.

_childDocuments_.review: "Wanderers of Ys,Simon's Quest,and Cadash had a class reunion with their old chum Chrono-trigger!" ~Game-Sport"When you think it's over it's not. You'll get your money's worth!" ~Ferbes"If Square made a Final Fantasy into a side scrolling action rpg it would play out something like this!" ~Electronic Mayhem"Will take you Nier and far. Has fangs like Symphony Of The Night whilst being much broader in scope. Astlibra is not afraid to get deeper and darker yet also retains the nostalgia of being a fun high fantasy romp. Its' scales are perfectly balanced!"" ~ Independent Gamers Anonymous "Remember how Zelda II The Adventure Of Link was a good but very flawed game? Imagine a similar idea constructed with better parts and a more adept engineer. All whilst throwing in some existentialism and science fiction into the fantasy rpg cauldron!" ~RPG-ArgonautsAstlibra is simultaneously a game and an experience. Around 10 or so hours in isn't even the tip of the iceberg but consider the fact in those 10 hours I could hardly put it down and I stopped only to say that yes,while it is on sale you should consider picking it up! If you were on the fence before it's a good excuse to dive on in! There is no secondary launchers,no season passes,and no current year politics. Just a really good side scrolling action rpg involving time travel,past lives,altering fate,spooky eldritch mysteries,and becoming as gods. Somehow manages to line up in the vicinity of Final Fantasy,Ys,and Iga-era Castlevanias on the pie chart! English translation is superb and the story-telling is based. I haven't been on this many emotional roller-coasters for quite awhile if I'm to be bluntly candid.Ditto for the soundtrack,art assets,and overall presentation. All this put together by "one guy" whom got a bit more help by equally passionate animators,illustrators,and composers down the road. Astute creative pioneers whom obviously saw the true value in this project and the potential it held.You can only get something like this naturally. It requires raw no-holds-barred imagination. No trust and safety committees. No sensitivity squads. No share holders. No mega corps. Just individuals passionate about the craft that is game design. It's too bad the AAA industry has become out of touch with the wild-west that was once game development. When passionate programmers made masterpieces in their basements on their spare time on the weekends! It was a different time and I would argue a better time.Anyway,that's all I gotta say. If this was the last game I ever got to play I'd be content with that. I'd feel as if I was going out on a high note as they certainly do not make em like this anymore.Pros+Presentation is retro yet simultaneously jaw dropping!+ The soundtrack is on a whole other level. I don't have the words....+The game's systems are varied yet accessible.+The story-line really is like binge-ing thru a superbly written manga or a really good episodic anime!+Excellent crafting system!+Boss fights have just the right balance of spectacle and challenge.+Loot is everywhere and in everything! +Puzzles so far have been fun and fair! If you pay attention you will rarely get stuck.+Armor pieces and weapons look different from each other when you equip them on the protagonist. + Refreshing fan service and even some playful adult innuendos. I appreciate that because in current year including those things denotes conviction and courage!+The combo system that mixes in additional inputs to summon final-fantasy-like guardian spirits as you are simultaneously hacking and slashing away is poetry in motion!Neutral+/- Rpgs in the late 90's surprised gamers with what I call "climatic continuations". By that I mean you think the game is leading you to the last battle when in truth you are just at the midway mark. One door closes as another door opens. You get the gist! In FF6 this counted as the 'Land Of Ruin Arc" after Kefka messed with the magic statues and rained down his wrath upon the world. In Chrono Trigger there was a hidden quest to recruit Magus and the game even continued on after Crono died as all his friends had to once again travel through time to bring him back. You could even fight Lavos in the past,present,or future to trigger different outcomes. Astlibra does something similar and even introduces brand new systems to upgrade your gear. Excessive? Repetitive? Unnecessary? Certain people might think so but if you enjoy grinding for that true ending whilst attaching ridiculous deity-tier attributes and super charged abilities to your collective armory and arsenal then Astlibra's penultimate chapter will be a nostalgic time-warp back to those golden days of gaming! It feels akin to that fond memory of renting a hidden gem from block buster,convincing your parents to eventually buy it for you,and then having all summer to gleefully unravel its' mysteries! Cons-There is very little in the way of hand holding. You are given the basics in an isolated tutorial section then dropped into the world proper like a baby being delivered by the stork!-No voice acting. You are going to have to read a lot. I don't personally consider this a sore-spot but I know certain folks are used to even their computers and their i-phones talking back to them!-End game is "brutal". Even on a lower difficulty the fates will chew you up and spit you out! While it doesn't entirely undermine the whole experience it goes from "Challenging but reasonable" to "Welp,guess I'm gonna have to excessively grind and find those hidden god-artifacts!" in the blink of an eye once you cross a certain threshold.

_childDocuments_.review: When I beat this game, I had two reactions. My first reaction was WOW, this is seriously impressive and quite inspiring for a solo dev. One man over the course of 15 years slowly perfected the game. The combat is fun and satisfying, as well as quite simplistic (you just mash attack and sometimes cast spells by holding a button and inputting 1 or 2 directions). There is some depth to the combat, such as backsteps with I-frames and perfect blocks, but really nothing beats mashing square at a ridiculous attack per minute rate. Can induce carpal tunnel, but it's very fun. Over the course of 50 hours not once did I get bored or tired of the combat. I went out of my way to fight enemies to grind for resources, and I loved every minute of grinding in this game. I would compare the combat to something like Symphony of The Night or Aria of Sorrow, except with a few extra moves tacked on, and spells don't require as many inputs to cast and are actually pretty much all worth using. However, don't be fooled - this isn't a metroidvania, you don't backtrack to previous areas once you acquire some form of power up to progress through the game. This is just a 2D side-scroller jRPG, and it's linear.Progression is tied to resources and can be easily described as "number go up". When you kill an enemy, they drop money, "force" (a resource spent leveling up stats by small increments, acquiring new spells and some other goodies in a special menu board), experience points, chests and crafting materials. Chests can contain recipes for particularly powerful items for the chapter you're in, and crafting felt rewarding because equipment stats are palpable. Additionally, each piece of equipment, excluding accessories, has an XP bar you can fill up. Once you do, you either upgrade its stats or receive a skill which you can slot in using crystals you can acquire throughout the game. This system gives the player a wide array of customizable options to choose from, allowing the player to min-max their equipment (as is suitable for a jRPG game). The soundtrack is fantastic. The surprising part is, as far as I know, it's nearly entirely royalty free music. The tracks vary in genre, and you never really know what you're gonna hear this chapter. The music might be grating to some people, and I'd understand if that were the case, but I loved all of it.The writing is insane. The less you know about it, the better. It's unpredictable and unironically has a "twist-per-hour" rate that keeps the game going that kept me interested and invested. I've seen some people say the game doesn't know when to end, and to an extent that is true, but I never once felt like the game was padding itself. It doesn't need to. The writing isn't perfect, though, and specifically characters suffer from this. They can be somewhat inconsistent as well as very, very, VERY trope-y. Treat the characters as if they're from an anime from, like, 2009 or earlier. There were moments where I shook my head, mumbling "this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game" to myself, but I still loved every character in the game. Nobody really outstays their welcome, and the sheer magnitude of the plot absolutely eclipses any issues I had with any particular character's scene. Seriously, the plot is a wild ride. Then, once you beat the game, there is a new game plus - a "postscript" - and it's probably one of the coolest iterations of a new game plus I've ever seen in a game. The new game plus is also more plot and the fact that it's a new game plus is part of the plot. It also adds new mechanics, though mostly just for extra stats so you can power yourself up into outer space. That was my first reaction. My second reaction was what the ♥♥♥♥? Hey, KEIZO? WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥?I loved every hour of this game, money well spent, and I highly recommend it to anyone who wants a more classic jRPG approach to gameplay with the writing of early Final Fantasy entries and Chrono Trigger mushed together. There's genuinely few games with a story like this out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra was an absolutely amazing game, and I loved every second of time I played through. Initially I was a little hesitant to start the game, but I regret not starting sooner. The story was amazingly well written and thought out, and even though it can feel confusing due to the many twists in it. There were also a ton of moments that had me giggling like crazy as well.  I found that overall there were very few plot holes or things left out. The characters were all extremely well written and none of the dialogue felt forced or artificial. The artwork was gorgeous beyond belief in my eyes and I always made sure to stop and appreciate the scenery. Even though the game play loop was simple and basic spam attack I always had fun just plowing through mobs, especially in the end game where you can make yourself infinitely more powerful. The music was spot on and Astlibra had many straight bangers. My favorite part was definitely the weapons mastery system because It forces you to use and learn the different weapon types. Enemy designs were also stellar and I love the way they all look. Even though some achievements got extremely grindy it did not take too much time to achieve everything after I finished the end game. Astlibra immediately became one of my most favorite games of all time and I fully support buying this game at full price. Honestly I think this game even at full price is cheap for how amazing it is.

_childDocuments_.review: I am very picky about games under the "metroidvania" genre and the "JRPG" genre. Both, if done well, are some of my favorite types of games. When I saw this, I figured I had to give it a try. This has turned out to be the biggest hidden gem I have ever found, and may in fact be my favorite indie game that I have ever found on Steam. The battle mechanics, the story the style, the bosses, the spells, the skills...all of these were done so well and were so well-polished. There is no doubt that this was not a typical cookie-cutter indie game release. This was a passion project. 10/10. It has tons of gameplay, with a length that well exceeds 70 hours (if you want it to with post script) and will have you hooked. Get it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a pleasant surprise. I tried the demo on a whim, and enjoyed it so much I bought the full game as soon as it released. The game was much lengthier than I expected it to be, and I spent a lot of time playing it; I initially bought it to tide me over until Persona 5 Royal hit Steam, but I ended up wanting to completely finishing the game even after it released. I obtained all of the achievements in around 80 hours, playing in Hard (or Difficult) mode, and even want to go through the game again on Hell mode.There are some flaws, and the game could use a touch-up and polishing on the clarity of the translations, but the overall experience is great. The main story is interesting enough and will keep you wanting to progress more. The combat is addicting enough to just blast enemies to level up and/or farm materials and not feel like a chore most of the time. Boss fights can get pretty tense and even some normal enemies will keep you on your toes since there are a few jank hitboxes. There's a wide variety of equipment and skills to extract from said equipment to equip. The music is top-notch in most sections, even if a bit odd sometimes. There's even Vocaloid songs, surprisingly. I wish there was a way to get the OST or listen to it outside of the game somehow.Highly recommend this game if you are interested in 2D side-scrolling Action RPGs similar to Castlevania and others of the same vein. The current asking price of $25 feels like a great deal, although I got it for 10% off from the launch discount. Heck, just try the demo. You can play the entirety of the first chapter and a small sample of mid-game combat which will help you decide.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game that delivers old school vibes (snes) in modern clothing (qol). Played through the game on hard difficulty and it felt a bit rough early on, but just right at around act 3+ (hard lets you get all achieves in one playthrough).I enjoyed the story quite a bit, and it managed to tie all the knots at the end (at least for the perfect ending). The game would have been better if it had dropped the attempts at sexual humor, but I feel like thats an issue with many asian stories in general. If you enjoyed the story in snes games like Soul Blazer and Gaia, this one will most likely satisfy you, but dont expect it to rival a Brandon Sanderson novel.Exploration felt rewarding (even though the game is quite linear) and the combat kept me entertained. Some puzzles actually require thinking and/or exploration to solve.Grinding was never required for progress, but I enjoyed the hunt for gear and power. Endgame left me with around 5-10 hours of grind to max out everything (nowhere near stat-maxed, but got all achieves and the perfect ending).All in all, I enjoyed the game more than the quality of its parts. I look forward to the upcoming DLC.If you are on the fence I recommend downloading the demo (start a new game, dont bother with the "demo" imo) it contains about 3-4 hours of playtime and progress carries over to the full game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was quite the surprise for a metroidvania type.  Very well crafted and you can tell the developers put in a lot of time into this game.  The music is fantastic and really brings in the atmosphere.  The subtle sound effects are placed in both the background and in conversations which is a nice touch.  Graphics are collages and conglomerates of realistic photos.  Most of the time they work beautifully but there are times where the transitions are rough around the edges.  The combat is smooth and gives much freedom for personal player style.  The only down side really is the game starts a little slow in story but every chapter really draws in an immersive hook.  Overall, there are very few metroidvania's out there that can compete with this one.  Astlibra is definitively worth buying even without a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally beat the game at 63 hours.I'm really glad that the youtube algorithm gods bestowed is piece of gem to me.The story really phenomenal for a indie rpgthe scope is huge and it delivers, the only complain is that the dialog can be meh at times and the tropes being outdated (but tbf it was developed for around 14-16 years)I can see it being a 10/10 masterwork if these issues are fixed along with filler content between the main chapters to give us more time to develop feelings for characters.The combat is also pretty outstanding for a 2d sidescroller, the impact is great, there are many ways to do combos on enemies and freedom of movement is high.as you progress and explore, you keep discovering new abilities that can change how you approach combat, you also get new passives from maxing out exp with a weapon, encouraging players to try out every type of weapon and play style.Combine the combat and the story you'll have a game that glues you on the seat until you realize it's sun rise.Thank you, KEIZO, for this amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so I (largely) absolutely love this game. But, there are some parts that are so bad it could deter people from playing this game. But I think I've got a succinct reason, and that's because every single mobility or function (back dash, double jump, **invulnerability for a brief moment after taking damage**, etc) is locked/hidden. The most important one being the ever so brief period of invulnerability after taking a hit. Without that, you can and most likely will be killed by an attack you get caught in, forcing you to start back at the beginning of a gauntlet. My only other gripe about this game that some of you may not mind, is the random barely story related busty babes with jigglies in battle with me, all but hitting me with their cleavage as an attack. For me that was my initial experience. HOWEVER!! When you get those abilities, and youre more mobile, you truly start to love this game. Every weapon, every armor, every shield (and some accessories), all show up on your character. Each piece must be crafted, and actually used in battle to get its benefit and it makes you experience weapons you wouldnt normally use. The areas are fairly huge and have such incredible detail. Every creature is unique. There are so many ways to play the game and alter your character. But as a true metroidvania lover, you ask "What about the secrets?" This game has so many damn secrets and things that are hidden that when you discover them, it kind of gives you a sense of wonder. Highly recommend this game to anyone who loves metroidvania style games with exploration!
