_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game two weeks ago, finished it with the DLC in about 9 days on hard difficulty after 75 hours of hyperfixation. I recommend it. TL;DR at the end. While good, the gameplay is nothing new, so I'd recommend it more if you're in there for the full experience rather than just the 'pushing buttons' part of the game. Astlibra's a weird game to evaluate, it has things it does extremely well and its good at selling it to the player, and there's some other things that vary between mildly annoying to very bad.First off, the game feels extremely satisfying to play, you can feel the extreme attention to detail in just about everything. The action pacing is nothing short of exceptionnal, everything feels good. One thing I like is that there is a lot of freedom when customizing your build. However the game is very grindy, and you're going to have to suck it up if you're going for the higher difficulties (which you have to for one achievement if you're a completionnist). Fortunately one of the last stage is designed for grinding and it has super cool music to keep you entertained so it wasn't such a bad experience, but still it was a bit much. Speaking of which, the ost is also hard to evaluate. I might be wrong about that but there is no original song and even if there is, the vast majority of the soundtrack come from copyright free libraries. That being said, the ost is nothing short of absolute perfection.Every music that you are going to hear, and I mean EVERY. SINGLE. MUSIC. blend perfectly with whatever is happening. It's never boring, every track that is playing at some point fit like nothing else can. I still remember how great and hyped up I felt at the beginning of the game when you get your first weapon and the 1st zone track starts playing, there could have never been a better fit, and I have plenty of other such anecdote on how the music made me feel at different point of the game. Seriously, it's memorable.A review of Astlibra wouldn't be properly done if I didn't talk about the story, which is also hard to evaluate. I've been thinking about it a lot and my opinion might be unpopular but... I don't think it's as good as other who like the game will tell you.Don't get me wrong, I liked it. Like everything else in Astlibra there is a lot of stuff that was done right. I liked how dramatic it felt. I liked how everything is tied together. I liked the themes the dev was going for. I liked how much efforts were put into world building. I liked how every character's actions are driven by their own motivation instead of plot convenience, which is always appreciated in that kind of stories. And while this last point is a major strength of the story it's also one of its weakness. You see, other than exactly three characters (Gau, Karon and the great sage), everyone is one-dimensionnal, characters in this world don't have a lot of depth to them so I don't feel much attachment to them when something happen. Overall the story felt very predictable, I won't spoil it for you, but every plot twist can be smelled miles away. Some subtle story elements were pleasant surprises but those were minor things that are barely relevant (like why a certain someone stopped showing up at the inn). In addition to that, there's a metric ton of plot holes in there, they don't really get you out of the action but I strongly advise you not to stop in order to think about anything related to the power of the scales, just accept things as they are presented to you. Does all of that make the story bad ? No. It's good, it really is and it's definitely a unique experience. But don't buy Astlibra expecting perfection, time-travel stories are hard, alright ?TL;DR : Overall, Astlibra is a very unique blend. It's done well, has a lot of toughts put into it on nearly every part. It deserves every single bit of praise it received, and the story is good but flawed in a way that doesn't take from its uniqueness. Also, I'm definitely buying anything the dev make from now on.Free tip : The game gives you a lot of save slots to work with. This is done purposefully. Use them. Also expect 70h to 120h of gameplay if you're a completionnist.

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea how to describe this game. It is a 2D hack and slash jrpg. That's easy enough, but it is so much more. I found it to be a mix of Chrono Cross/Nier Automata/ the best of Vanillaware. It is sad and funny and weird all wrapped up into one. And there are like three ways to level up, two more ways to customize the way your character fights, and weapon upgrading. Astlibra Revision is more than the some of its parts, and I more than I would like to admit found myself smiling one minute completely amazed by how the game was progressing and where it was going next narratively then; ultimately, brought to tears by the next major development. I absolutely loved this game. It is my favorite game ever, and I urge everyone to give it a try. It even has a free demo.

_childDocuments_.review: A "thumbs-up/thumbs-down" system is very inadequate in helping me rate this game; it's somewhere in-between, but mostly towards the "thumbs-up" side, so that's where I'm landing. The Good:- As others have said, the music is fantastic and complements the game well.- The story can have its fits and starts, and each chapter feels a LITTLE disjointed, but overall is serviceable and does its job.- I really like the scale and magic crystal systems, combined with equipment mastery. It allows you to do different builds without having to change much up, and experience gain on equipment doesn't require much grinding.- It's fun finding legendary items out in the world, and I appreciate that you can mold keys right in inventory to access chests in the field; returning to a shop to buy them would have been an absolute pain. - The combat feels impactful and it's surprisingly fun. It's the big reason to play Astlibra.The "Meh":- The graphics are fine. Artwork can be a little inconsistent-feeling, but I definitely appreciate how sharp the graphics are. - Grindy. I don't see this as an upside or downside because I can handle it, but there's some DEFINITE grind that has to happen to get souls, and then BAM suddenly you're OP. I tried taking on the dragon boss at Level 8 and got my ass handed to me. Ground out a few levels, and it was trivial. I'm STILL riding that trivial wave into Chapter 3, but because I now know what to expect.  The "No Bueno":- There are some BIG tone issues when chatting with NPCs when combined with the story. Yes, I get that our protagonist is good-looking;  is just ODD. Then there's the NPC in town that talks about how the barmaid has an awesome rack. I mean, come on. It's just jarring to have such a serious tone and get smacked in the face with weird commentary like this. It doesn't serve the overall narrative, and they're just throwaway lines. - The game has an odd idea of convenience. For instance, I traversed through the swamp back and forth like 5 different times to get story breaks that told me to go the other direction to continue. It felt padded out. Then out of nowhere, I have a warp portal that eliminates the need to traverse? I appreciate the portal, but it just underscores how much the game expected me to accept back-tracking over and over. - The platforming can be infuriating. Sometimes the edges of platforms aren't exactly the edges of the platforms. Your double-jump is has a certain window that doesn't allow late second-jumps. I'm thankful that outside of a few arena missions that precision in platforming isn't required; otherwise I'd have quit the game long ago. Overall:This is CLEARLY a labor of love, and mad respect for putting together a competent RPG with so many little systems to tinker with. If it weren't for that fun combat loop and experimentation and sense of discovery, this game would just be another boring grind-fest. It keeps it fresh, and it keeps me coming back, and I suppose it deserves a thumbs-up for that. If you're in the mood for a serviceable story that'll keep you going for a few dozen hours, you could certainly do worse.

_childDocuments_.review: {Ignore short Steam playtime - Finished game with 'best' ending on Normal on my Switch, just under 89 hours)Astlibra Revision is an incredible game and I simply cannot recommend it highly enough.  It combines the best of older Japanese PC games and 8 and 16-bit adventures, then adds its own twists and mechanics for a genuinely unique action adventure experience.  If you enjoyed the likes of Faxanadu on NES and are a regular watcher of Basement Brothers on YT, this game is 110% up your alley.What initially seems like a basic action RPG slowly unfolds with a story on par with classic JRPGs, addictive combat, and a highly customizable equipment and magic system.  Without spoiling anything, the story grows in breadth and depth all the way through the end.  Each of the player's eventual companions has their own personality and unique stakes in the storyline.  By the end, your attachment to each one will be genuine.  The only knocks I can give to the story is the occasionally puerile humor and unpolished localization*.  The cringy moments hew closer to '80s anime than desperately salacious; the overall story beats, philosophical quandaries, and emotional chapters mostly make up for the 'bewb' jokes.  In fact, there is a particular chapter in the game where I was genuinely moved and deeply saddened.  At its best Astlibra Revision generally knows how to establish melancholy, regret, and redemption to often excellent payoffs.  *The game was updated with a new localization after launch.  That's the version I played and, in general, you can easily understand the plot and dialog.  If you played any number of 16-bit JRPG then the syntax will be quite familiar to you.  I do hope one more editing pass can be made in the future.  There are some really great moments in the game which would have benefited from localization polish.The action in the game is incredibly fun.  AR gives you the ability to cater combat to your style(s) using different weapon types, armor, shields, and accessories.  By the endgame, most any loadout is viable (at least on Normal).  It's possible for your early equipment to outclass the boss-level weapons if you so desire.  The summoning and ability mechanics are beyond the scope of this review address in depth, but I guarantee that you will have a blast customizing your build in any number of ways.  Want to leave a trail of mines as you do a shield charge, juggle enemies to the sky with your bubble staff and flying boulders, then crash down with ice spikes and launch a freakin' shark into the air to finish them off?  You can do that, and it's not even the best mix I eventually came up with!The game heartily pays off players willing to grind and look for the boundless secrets in each area.  Leveling up your core equipment unlocks abilities, and recipe books allow you to craft items for healing, some puzzles, and crafting.  Oh yes, you'll be forging ores and smelting materials for upgrading while also grinding ingredients to make matcha ice cream and hamburgers for stat upgrades.Don't let the graphics fool you.  I absolutely grew to love its doujin charm and atmosphere.  The majority of the bosses in the game (animated by Vanillaware artist Shigatake, also known for his eye-melting Devil Blade Reboot shmup) are HUGE, sometimes taking up more than one screen in reach.  Multiple moving parts, awesome attacks, and sweeping animations.  These boss fights are where the game does chug at times, but mostly during the death animation.  Nevertheless, it never impeded my gameplay as 99.9% of the game plays smoothly.Music is drawn from open-licensed tracks, but the developer chose appropriate music and interludes.  There are a couple of tracks with vocals that get repetitive, but on the whole every song truly feels like it belongs in this game.This game is worth the $25 for how many hours I and many others have lovingly played it.  Despite my comments above, it almost defies description unless one plays it for themselves. It's a rare, unique game, and I give it my highest recommendation.Final notes (some spoilers which I've hidden):- Postgame is fantastic ()- There are a few puzzles here and there that had me stumped.  Mainly had to do with the localization and interface.  There's a great mostly non-spoiler guide via Steam in case you need a tip.  I'll just say this: when asked SAY NO TO INVESTIGATING THE SCALES ;)  Thank me later :D- Okay, one more early tip: - There aren't any critical missables AFAIK.  The game goes out of its way to allow you to navigate and grind where and what you want and need.

_childDocuments_.review: After fully beating this game, I can certainly say Astlibra is a masterpiece of the action JRPG genre. The gameplay is extremely fun, with a good mixture of button mashing while still retaining a need for situational awareness or tactics. The weapon experience system unlocking new abilities was always a treat, even if the weapons more or less played the same and having a shield was almost always better. I really enjoyed the designs despite that and working on a build that felt good for me to play. The summoning skills really add more depth to the gameplay as well, and I always found it fun to mess around with them and figure out which ones I liked or didn't like using for different encounters or areas. Just moving around in the game feels great, and everything is very responsive. That said, puzzles can sometimes be obtuse or confusing, and the EN translation isn't always consistent, but I can give it a pass.The overall story was so much better than I expected, even if it does follow many JRPG tropes, which you may love or hate. It continued to surprise me up to the very end. Some things seemed like they were obvious only for the scene to be turned upside down onto its head as the story unfolded. My biggest complaints about the story were the silent and unnamed protagonist, even though multiple times he "talks" in a small wordless speech bubble and people say "this has your name on it" a few times, and the weirdly perverted moments that can be very typical of Japanese fiction. I was able to look past those moments for the rest of this beautiful gem, however, and I think if you can as well, you'll really like this game.I would suggest this game to anyone who enjoys side-scrolling Castlevania games, DMC, Chrono Trigger, or the Final Fantasy series. It's not the type of game for everyone, but if you enjoy action RPGs and the JRPG genre I think this is absolutely worth your time and money. It hit almost all of the right buttons for me at the right time, and I basically played this game nonstop from start to finish. Absolutely incredible.

_childDocuments_.review: If there’s anything at all that catches your attention in the first couple hours, then PLEASE see this game through. I know first-hand the game can be damn annoying, plain frustrating at points in the early chapters.However, the combat, the gameplay loop, the intrigue of the cast, the world-building, the dopamine rush of pressing attack to see numbers go up, the sense of wonder finding new legendary gear, the scale of boss fights… if you enjoy JRPGs I’m pretty confident there will be something to grab your attention here. After all, ASTLIBRA is a love letter from KEIZO to JRPGs and its fans.If you are curious then please try the demo. It is 1–2 hours long, and it will be representative of the combat system with some decent upgrades and gear available. It will definitely feel weird in terms of the pacing but that’s for the sake of putting the player in a position where they can experience a well-equipped Hero and some story beats in a condensed experience.I’m taking a break from the game before playing the roguelite DLC, but this game is still very much living rent free in my head. If you enjoy (J)RPGs then I sincerely hope you get to play this game and see it through yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra has it all. Flashy and fun combat with tons of new skills and abilities to unlock. A story about friendship, family, romance, the dark side of humanity, and fighting against corrupted deities. Graphics which likely utilized assets from every royalty free source imaginable along with monster and character designs from the guy that did a lot of the art for Dragon's Crown. Initially I was lukewarm towards the visuals but they started to grow on me and now I find them quite appealing. Then there's the soundtrack which just kind of pops off for most of the game injecting banger after banger into your eardrums. It's an all around fantastic time and a definite recommendation from me if side scrolling JRPGs, anime, and doujin games are your jam. This is honestly one of my personal favorite games I've played in years and I hope many more can discover it. This game deserves all the love it's been getting and so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a fun side scrolling action RPG.Pros:1) The skill learning system is ADDICTIVE. You learn skills from mastering swords, shields, and armor. Which leads in to...2) Crafting. The crafting system is great. Some people might hate it because it's a bit grindy, but for me I LOVED getting into a new area, fighting new monsters, and discovering what drops I could get to make new gear (and then discovering what new skills you get from that area)3) The combat is responsive and felt really good4) The diverse amount of spells you can learn is great. Also, the input system for casting spells is really cool and innovative. It uses a fighting game style input, each element has it's own combo for casting spells.5) The story ended up being really interesting (although a bit convoluted at times).Cons:1) The writing in some places isn't great. Leads to some confusing situations in solving puzzles in certain places2) (Subjective) Lots of fan service. It's not overly egregious, but some bosses/NPCs are very scantily clad, and some of the party members are overly sexualized by the other party members.

_childDocuments_.review: Action-focused sidescroller that features an engaging fantasy story featuring an MC searching for their lost friend with some interesting twists. It has an engaging story making you wonder more about why the events that happen occurred.  Soundtrack isn't bad either despite being a mixture of different sources that somehow work really well with the game's aesthetics and atmosphere.There are passive abilities that can be slotted in order to adjust combat abilities, make grinding easier, and add additional UI features which each take up a magic crystal capacity that can be expanded . Combat features button mashing which differ in moveset for sword/2h-sword/lance/wand/hammer/etc., directional attacks which tend to be the same for every weapon, and skills that vary from summons, support, and active attacks which each provide some level of invulnerability time. All of these are not gate-kept behind going to specific areas to swap out when you really need specific builds during boss fights. Want to focus on two handing and then swap to sword-shield in the middle of battle because bullet hell? Open the menu, navigate to the equipment/skills/abilities, swap out, done and no additional futzing. However, the game does force you to be on the lookout for hidden treasure in the clunky map designs since the way you unlock more moves is via treasure chests in the world. This involves searching for tiny directional arrows, mini-bullseye, and obscure hidden paths. Some of these can only be reached once the appropriate skills and combat maneuvers are acquired to combo together. Puzzles are relatively easy and obscure since sometimes the game provides prompts noting an interactable and other times they're just obstacles that you mash buttons and/or use random baubles you find to interact with it.The game is fast and doesn't futz around with handlholding so much meaning combat, puzzle solving, and story keep the momentum going. Absolutely recommend this game. Also, I will never forgive KEIZO for Chapter 5. Both for the questionable "correct" choice and the aftermath of the "wrong".

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's good and probably better in Japanese/Chinese - this is a public warning that you may not experience the 'overwhelmingly positive' vibes the other reviews give off. I'll chuck another 20 hours into it and we will see if the game re-defines my life, gives me a 6-pack and causes me to reach spiritual enlightenment like every other reviewer.Vibe check follows: The systems in this game are incredibly deep and provide an incredible amount of customisation and depth which is a real shame because the weapons all feel very same-y. Heavy weapons feel exactly like magic weapons which feel exactly like shortswords. Combat appears flashy but is pretty shallow when you get into it. It boils down to find the summon with iFrames and abuse it while you spam whatever attack most efficiently builds up the summon gauge. The game feels like it's running at a lower FPS than it is because of all the slowdown when you hit an enemy with a weapon. Combat is like a vintage car, very pretty but you wouldn't want to drive it to work. Art wise, in screenshots it looks incredible - but the animations don't feel fluid. Most enemies and characters feel like cardboard cutouts stuck on ice-cream sticks. Character animations look like they were created with motion tween, 10 000 layers in Photoshop and blutac. Personal taste though - your mileage may vary.People are really hype on the story - leading me to assume they played the game in Japanese or Chinese because some translations to English feel, for lack of a better term, constipated? (Like they're nearly right but still not quite there and it's really difficult to squeak it out and get a good flow going). The developers seem very active and responsive to issues with translation/community though so credit for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap, what a game. I guess I'll start by saying I love this game and I'll probably play everything this developer continues to make for the foreseeable future. That being said it also has a LOT of issues. The game straight up lies to you. There's multiple points in the game where it tells you "this is the final battle" and then the game continues to give you more missions after that final battle. And not like Super Ultra, secret post final boss missions. The game literally just casually continues like it didn't just tell you it was about to end. It's like that awkward friend that says goodbye, and then continues to hang out for hooours. Which wouldn't be as bad, if that friend didn't also continue saying goodbye throughout the night. The game lying to you is made even worse by the fact that there's a lot of mistranslations too, so not only is the game lying, but you're also being given just completely untrue information. And I understand this next point comes with the territory of making a game centralized around Time Travel as a theme, but Astlibra really takes it too far. Killing off and resurrecting characters multiple times really desensitizes you and trivializes any sense of tragedy. There was one character that died in a bad timeline because I made a bad choice. I struggled tooth and nail to save her, and was so relieved to have her back, only for her to die again in another timeline, and then revived again because I went even further back in time and did something that undid it all. Again. This doesn't happen once, twice, or even just three times. It happens a LOT to multiple characters. And it's a shame, because I actually cared a lot about every single character that was introduced, until they were killed and resurrected for the fifth time. The combat is fun, but only if you unlock everything. And I cannot fathom why the developer hid some of the combat mechanics as secrets. One of the early game skills you have to really go out of your way to unlock is a jump slash. And if you miss this secret skill, you essentially go through the whole game not knowing that air combos exist, because you have no way of launching enemies into the air. It really feels like a bad oversight to have splintered these essential skills off as secrets. And it wouldn't be so bad if the secrets were easy to find, but a lot of them are really obtuse. And the last thing I'll touch upon is that the game has too many twists. There were several versions of the story I liked, but each of those stories then got undermined by another new twist that revealed that was never the real story all along, all along. For example, there's a "main story ending" that is probably one of the more incoherent and straight up idiotic endings I've ever seen. But then there's a New Game+ that is supposedly just extra content, but at some point it continues to main story and fixes the ending by making it all actually just a dream. I accept this, because the main story ending was REALLY bad, but it really leaves you scratching your head if the NG+ content is canon then, because it specifically refers to itself as just extra content. This goes back to what I was saying about the game straight up lying versus misinformation. Overall, I enjoyed the game and recommend it, but expect to be left very conflicted. There's simultaneously so much good and so much bad, I'll be very surprised to find anyone that just straight likes or dislikes this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game and enjoyed it overall, but it's hard to recommend generally and I think a lot of issues are being overlooked in the positive reviews I've seen.Pros:* Gameplay is surprisingly fun and in-depth, lots of progression systems - by far the best part of the game* Best battery life I've ever gotten on my Steam Deck, even compared to other 2D games* Funky world setup with an interesting premise* Postgame (avoiding details for spoiler reasons)Cons:* Great concepts, but the writing is a bit of a mess and character writing in general is weak/inconsistent* Some really awful and horribly out-of-character anime cringe especially in Chapters 4-6 that nearly killed the game for me* The game is pretty grindy in the mid-section, and features some obtuse/confusing puzzle design especially in Chapter 6. Expect lots of backtracking and repeated environmentsThe gameplay is a lot of fun, and the game pulls a fakeout that I think is pretty novel. But the overall writing execution just isn't that good - characters constantly make baffling choices to advance the plot, details get overlooked everywhere for convenience, etc. Most of the characters are very inconsistently written (the worst being turning characters into sex offenders as a joke out of nowhere), which made it much harder to get invested in them.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique title with a unique look, Astlibra is a blend of JRPG mechanics with Metroidvania-style combat (though it is not a Metroidvania) that tells a story spanning across time. While naive at times, the writing is fun and tackles a number of unique, thought-provoking situations.Final Fantasy players from the Playstation era will notice heavy inspiration from FFIX's Ability system and FFX's Sphere Grid, and a "Possession" system that treats summon monsters as single-fire spells. Oldschool RPG players know the drill. At the same time, and much unlike an oldschool RPG, the combat system encourages quick reflexes through the use of Fighting-game combo inputs to pull off a variety of dazzling moves. Throw in the readily-available respec system, multiple RPG-style leveling paths, dozens of arena challenges, and a simple crafting system, and Astlibra becomes a surprisingly fun take on a variety of well-known mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: 17.3 hours - initial review:It looks weird, the grinding is heavy, The dialogue is difficult to read sometimes (Slight leniency for it needing to be translated) and the inventory/crafting is kinda rough.... but I can't stop playing this game.For some reason fighting is addicting. I can't explain why it is, it just is. The heavy grinding is slightly redeemed due to how addicting and satisfying it is to mash the attack button and whip out different spells.There is an absurd abundance to collect. You get skills, and you get weapons that you need to use to get more skills, and then you level up to get more skills, and you level up to get points, and you collect gems to get stats that also give you more skills and it just keeps going, and normally I hate it, but for some reason it's fun here, I really don't know why.I give it a recommend if you want a game with an absurd amount of content and some addicting hack and slash game play. I don't think I'm far enough into the story to know if I can recommend that yet, but I'm definitely wondering what's gonna happen next.Edit @ 30.9 hours in: The  dialogue is still really rough to get through some times. It's hard to write good RPG dialogue, but when it's read out one line at a time which is sometimes just 2 words and a bunch of ellipses, it really gets rough. However, the story has really taken shape pretty well in my opinion, and the gameplay loop is still fun.One thing I will say is that I widely underestimated the importance of Defense and HP. All the way through , I had no HP, and just max Speed and Attack.  hit me like a truck, and I basically just switched all my level up points into Defense and HP and my damage really didn't suffer that much, but my survivability went wayyy up. Still having a good time, looking forward to the rest of the story.Final Edit 37 hours: The story ended up being a lot more interesting than I thought it would be. , however, is BRUTAL. There's one enemy in particular that kind of ruined this section for me, and I knew I was close to the end, so was more just looking to get through the game which made it more annoying. I was wrong however that I was close to the end! Seriously the amount of content this game has is ridiculous, if you enjoy hacking and slashing and grinding, this game is pretty great.

_childDocuments_.review: This thing is bizarre, I haven't even finished it at ~65 hours and it's so much fun I haven't even registered the fact that I've already spent a AAA RPG amount of time with it, with the ending not even being in sightHow does this game have zero visibility while simultaneously having one of the best review ratings on Steam I've ever encountered, as well as (going by the % of people completing certain achievements) about a quarter of anyone who's purchased this has played the game to full completion (which again is a time investment of ~80 hours)?!If you like at least a few of the following:- Platformers- Action RPGs- JRPGs- Very blatantly Japanese game design- Mysterious juego aesthetics- Involved narrative- Consistent presentation- Item management- Obscure secrets and hidden content- Character builds- FFX Sphere grid / FF12 License boardyou're guaranteed to enjoy yourself with this.It's obvious that this was created by a person who had their taste shaped by predominately Japanese games, wouldn't be surprised if a whole slew Falcom games provided inspiration for this (old school PC-88 Xanadu comes to mind a lot), especially also when some of the background tracks are absolute bangers which sound like they were workshopped by Falcom Sound Team JDK and provided royalty free or something.The game just keeps throwing more content at you. I genuinely thought I'd reached the end about two times and still got blindsided when it occurred for a third time.The only thing I can knock on a bit is the sporadically horny writing which sometimes comes out of nowhere, but this game is otherwise such a beautiful work of passion I can forgive it a few negatives.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat's got that addictive mix of simple yet satisfying. I can put up with my fair share of anime cringe, Neon White was unironically GOTY, but there's a line man. Once you get to chapter... I believe it's 5, the game just starts getting overtly sexual in a way that's more than a bit uncomfortable. The big tiddy anime girl goddess(es) were one thing, the wink-wink-nudge-nudge 'one bed' bit was pushing it, the lesbians who are only lesbian to talk about ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ was a bit much for my taste, forcing the sorceress character to parade around in lingerie (something she explicitly doesn't want to do) is where it started to feel unforgivably gross, and following up by having her be told by the leads that she got blackout drunk and started stripping for the town is where I decided I wasn't recommending this game to human people. _childDocuments_.review: 60 hours of pure gameplay bliss and my personal favorite game of the year. I BEG the developer to implement some sort of NG+ system down the line. I just want a reason to keep playing the game over and over again.The combat system starts off very basic, and as you go along it starts to become insanely fast-paced by the end of the game when you’re practically lawn-mowering enemies (unless you’re playing at Hell or higher diff).The mechanics of strengthening your character are diverse, yet not confusing at all. You have a few routes to go about it: 1) Leveling up, 2) Karon skills (which are essentially combat mechanic modifiers), and 3) Ability tree (FFX/PoE style grid-like stat tree). Much later on in the game you will unlock additional systems that make progression a bit more refreshing.As for the story, I happened to enjoy most of it a lot, although it may be hit-or-miss for people. If you don’t like the stereotypical anime tropes of JRPGs, you won’t like the story or dialogue in this game, either. However, if that’s your thing as it is with me, you might really be intrigued with the story. I found the characters to be quite charming and lively, and the protagonist, although silent, manages to display a broad range of characteristics in spite of it. You really get the sense that the protagonist has his own clear-cut personality and identity despite being silent (though  at that point, why even make him a silent protagonist to begin with?)9.5/10 gameplay, 7/10 story, 6.5/10 visuals, 8/10 music, and overall a 9/10 experience. It really does give the impression that one person put their heart and soul into this project.I thoroughly enjoyed staying up all night playing this game during my work week.

Players can customize their character's abilities and equipment to suit their playstyle, adding layers of depth and complexity to each encounter.- Stunning Pixel Art: ASTLIBRA Revision's pixel art is a feast for the eyes, capturing the essence of classic RPGs while incorporating modern touches. The detailed environments, character designs, and animations create a visually enchanting experience.- Atmospheric Soundtrack: The game's soundtrack perfectly complements its nostalgic aesthetic, with a mix of melodic tunes and ambient sounds that enhance the overall atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: I wish there were a “Recommend with Reservations” option for reviews…This game is a lot of fun. The combat is fantastic and makes grinding not a chore. There’s a wide variety of weapons, armour, and skills to master. I like the pseudo-crafting system they use for buying new equipment too. And then there’s the story. It starts out interestingly enough. Kind of generic but with a couple of hints of twists to come. But around chapter four, it derails in a distractingly bad way. It pivots to being very juvenile. It is briefly horny - which is fine, I have no issue with sexual themes, but it comes out of nowhere - and then abruptly stops in favour of “twists” that feel like a little kid making up a story. The chapters stop leading into each other and become just a series of “and then this happens.” It was still fun, but I found myself getting bored and even frustrated watching cutscenes. I’ll recommend it, but with the caveat that you might want to play it while doing something else to keep your attention during the non-combat parts. Pros:- The gameplay is great. I loved the combat. - The skill system is fairly extensive and customizable.- It manages to make the occasional platforming puzzle kind of fun to try.Cons:- The story has a lot of missed potential. It promises a lot more at the start than it can actually accomplish.- Plot twists are either bad or bizarre.- Side characters are inconsistently written.- It drags in the middle.- The puzzles are either basic or obtuse with not much in between.I played this on the Steam Deck and it works perfectly right out of the box. _childDocuments_.review: There are a few things to note about Astlibra before I get into the positives about this game and why you should play it, as they could turn you off from playing it. However, I will say that if you don't mind anime, have enjoyed hacks and slashes, and don't mind a bit of a grind, you will really like this game. However, if these things turn you off, don't bother; otherwise, go and buy it. This game can be very easily ruined by spoilers, as the story is a big selling point.With that out of the way, the games are amazing, and if you have ever enjoyed games like Kingdom Hearts, youll also like this, though unlike KH, this game is entirely in 2D, which I think doesn't work too well with a hack and slash, but I think the game does well regardless. Only towards the end and EX maps do the bosses and enemies get too tanky, and you have to start grinding if you really want to start doing damage again.Now what I think is its best selling point is its story. I'll try to avoid spoiling anything, but let's just say that not only is it compelling, all of the twists and turns are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wild that the game at a few points of the story tries to lull you into a false sense of security only to pull the rug out of under you the whole time. Don't get me wrong, towards the end it starts to feel a little annoying, but most of the time at the end youll feel satisfied with where the story ended up.Now its not all sunshine and rainbows, however, as mentioned before, this game not only has a bit of a grind, but unless you follow a walkthrough, not only will you miss things that can be important to the story, you may also miss items that make the game 10 times easier (make sure to 100% the arena). Also, having to level up every piece of equipment is annoying, and I wish you had the option of just skipping leveling some items as all weapons and armor are worth leveling up either for the karon crytal or the special passive.All in all, it was a great experience that I won't forget anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: I am thoroughly enjoying this game so far. It's a really interesting and slightly complex story but I've been interested the entire time, even enough to read additional in game lore books and the like. For a JRPG the grind doesn't feel all too bad, but I also haven't done any end game stuff yet, so I could be very wrong about this soon, so far though resources/money/experience and equipment mastery have been easy to gain and have consistently grown in proportion to the difficulty. This game is an action JRPG, and a unique one at that. While the animations look a bit choppy, the game play is quite smooth, and it encourages the use of all skills at your disposal, the controls are very polished in this regard as well, the game feels fun and intuitive to play. This game is either a collectathon enjoyer's worst nightmare or dream game. There is a ton of things to collect whether it be magic abilities, weapons and materials, equipment skills, filling out the "growth" map., etc. A ton to do, however it's made more rewarding due to the fact that you can easily plan out very efficient farming routes for both enemies and resources all while swapping in and out weapons/shields and armor to max out equipment skills or get an item for 'mastering' the particular weapon or armor all at once. Also by equipment skills I mean abilities like passive upgrades to attack speed, or elemental damage, or even item magnet abilities. You can use them for free if you have the weapon or armor equipped, or you also have a growing ability to use unequipped but mastered skills which grows over time. The actual combat itself, while it feels nice does get a bit mundane as eventually when you get good at it, it's quite easy at normal difficulty. There is a variety of things you can do combat wise, and it grows over time as you collect combat abilities. Though these you usually get from chests it seems. Blocking is valuable as well, it's great for projectiles and protects against status ailments. You also can utilize the invincibility frames you get when you use the magic in this game, and you use both ranged and melee abilities along with magic as sort of a catch all Gary Stu type. On top of this you also have a variety of items you can use to fit any situation, from all enemies in a room being heavily damaged, to throwing an arrow by hand which is surprisingly powerful early on. The game also utilizes a delayed item use system. So you use a healing item, a progress bar appears, and then the item is used. If you are struck/leave that zone etc it will cancel it. It hasn't been difficult to break away from fights to heal/shoot a bow at a distance as well. No autosave system, save often, and when you interact with a save point all enemies not in that zone are resurrected. If you leave your zone and come back those enemies do respawn as well.There is a lot of depth to this game too. An arena with multiple and varied "cups" ranging from platforming  and combat challenges to speed challenges. You are able to backtrack after you've progressed to a certain point in the story, so don't overly stress on leaving things behind. Though the catch is you have to complete the chapter again. Makes the game ideal for speed runners I guess. You even get your own house and back yard. Unknown if any visual or functional customization is possible. There is a lot of freedom in character customization as well. You can allocate 5 points to attributes every level, but you can reallocate them as you see fit at specific points scattered throughout the game, and there is some strategy to this, even terrain dependent strategy. You're well served just bumping attack, defense, and health too, at least as far as I've gotten in the game.There are many puzzles, and a lot of context clues as you watch cutscenes. This game is cutscene heavy, so for those of you who may remember that boss fight with Riku during the old PS2 KH1 days you can rejoice, for this game features a skip button.It's a semi silent protagonist. I think it's deliberate, as the character will talk in game, but you can't see his words. There is always context that let's you know what he's talking about, but let's you sort of fill in the blanks of how he communicates it with your own imagination.This game plays excellently on Steam Deck. There's some choppy audio, but I've not been bothered enough to try and fix it, so there may be a workaround for it I just haven't utilized. It's also really good with the battery life. Like you're hitting the top end of the "possible hours" of a single charge. Though that may be obvious as its not that graphics intensive. Overall I definitely recommend this game, there's a lot to do and it's very approachable but if you want to can turn the difficulty up to 11. I haven't tried that yet so I don't know how the challenge is balanced, I would say it's likely a damage sponge method given the health pools of some bosses. This is speculation though, and it could be user error with regards to my damage output, so your milage may vary. Lastly, it's pretty clear a lot of love and care went into this game, and I think the developer nailed something really cool, unique and fun to play here. There's even a demo if you really need to see for yourself. I believe that this game is definitely worth picking up.*Edit: I am incorrect about having to complete whole chapters over if you go back to them.Game finished edit: I can honestly say this is a must buy for me. Probably if not definitely my GOTY. I literally played non-stop until I finished it, and I didn't feel like any part of it was a chore except one specific thing at the absolute very last part of the game, but even then the methodology is interesting and fun for the most part. You're doing yourself a disservice if you like anything that you see on this page and don't pick it up in my honest opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I've written a whole thesis on this game over the course of playing it, but at this moment, I have a short way to figure out if this game is for you.Do you like Grinding, Interesting Gameplay, Carrots On Sticks That Incentivize Collecting And Levelling Every Weapon, Shield, And Armor in the Game?If so, regardless of any negatives, you'll probably enjoy the game. The Core Gameplay was very fun for me, playing on Hell Difficulty, it was challenging, and figuring out strategies I enjoyed was fun. Certain areas were harder than others, but I was adamant on buying and levelling every new weapon, shield, and armor in each chapter, to stay on top of what new abilities I could use. Genuinely, the gameplay is the Shining Star that is this incredibly unique video game. Notice how I (and probably others) haven't once mentioned that this game looks like a Bitcoin Miner Fever Dream, with all of it's stock photos, fighting PNGs of Flowers and ♥♥♥♥. That's because by the 20th hour, you'll be used to it. It's incredible what the human mind can adapt to.The negatives for me are: The story is ALMOST good, it's interesting enough to keep me reading it, but good god this game was so clearly written by one person who shoves as much horny, fetishistic, 14 year old humor in it it's insufferable. The first few times I wasn't sure if he was just trying to write some fan fiction or not, by the end of the game, (with a very specific "If you don't wake up, I'm going to sit on your face and fart" moment) I knew he wasn't even writing the fan service for the fans, but for himself. Dialogue is basically Horrible to Insufferable whenever you hear that Goofy Music that is always playing right before one of the characters completely ruins the tone and mood that the overarching story has been setting up just to make a "WOAH SHE'S GOT FAT BOOZOONKOOS" joke. Now I obviously want to and AM faulting the game for these moments, but I have to give credit where it's due, you can simply press Start and Skip literally ANY dialogue in the game, even if it's one single message box. And it skips Very Fast. Big ups for that, but the story was just interesting enough to make me read it, and also hate the game for ruining what it was setting up.Another negative that really depends on your Taste and Preference, the music. Some of the music is good, some of it is laughably out of place. I couldn't help but burst out laughing every single time I heard a Monstercat-esque copyright free dubstep song just start blaring over what would otherwise be a somewhat interesting or important moment. It completely kills the vibe sometimes. You don't get used to it, at least I didn't. An important thing to note about all of these faults is that this was originally a browser game, when you learn that, and learn that it was put online in about 2011, a lot of these choices make much more sense. The dubstep, the horny fanservice, the Stock Photo Trees and Clouds, the RPGMaker lookin Characters, the general way the plot goes in general I've seen like 20 times at least in these types of browser / flash games tbh. Just thought I'd mention that as well.The game genuinely adds 3 or 4 new mechanics to the Post Game Chapter (After the Final Chapter), which is awesome, because they're good mechanics that spice up the Core Gameplay, and the Core Gameplay is the only thing that kept me playing, but I wish they had been added in far earlier than Post-Script. Mostly because, in general Post-Script feels like it overstays it's welcome. I got to Post-Script 60 hours in. I have 80 hours now completing the game, and I intentionally didn't do the "Good Ending" yet because that would be another 2 hours of grinding (not complaining about the grinding, I was just ready to be Finished with this game 10 hours ago).I hate giving number ratings because they're arbitrary as hell, I very much enjoyed my time actually playing the game, theorycrafting, doing fake math with the Libra Scale Balancing, optimizing my Berserk Usage, etc. Reading the story and dialogue, horrible, it might be for you, it certainly was NOT for me. Take that as you will, have a good one.

_childDocuments_.review: Walked in blind and was pleasantly surprised at how crisp the gameplay feels. You have quite a bit of reign on how you want to build your character, and you're not severely penalized for completely neglecting certain stats. I've dumped all of my points into attack power because I was enjoying the weapon gameplay and how each weapon feels unique from one another, but I still cast spells to take advantage of invincibility frames when I get in a tight spot. I can see myself trying a pure caster build in a future playthrough.I'm playing on hard and it's just about how I expected it to feel: a decent challenge where you get punished for mistakes, but not to the point where you're one-shot by a random slime. I do have some frustrating times where I get hit-stunned and die, but that's because I did something stupid. Thankfully, the skip event system is actually pretty good.This game should be able to run on practically anything out there...it has support for DX9, if that says anything.Story's decent so far ... just hit chapter 4. It's not going to blow your socks off, but it's pretty well-written and the characters actually have personalities you can pick out.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the entire game(+dlc) with achivements i think this game deserves a review.The gameplay is fun from fighting enemies melee or with magic  to getting stronger in many different ways likelvl up, the grow board, stat cards etc.The music fits pretty much every time so i didn´t even know that most of it is free music.The graphics are quite beautiful from the background to the enemy disigns. The enemies moving around somewhat reminded me of that one lovecraftian roguelike game where every part of the monsters kept moving on its own which i found funny.The story surprised me a lot. Sometimes i was already expecting something which was mostly correct and sometimes it took a turn i didn´t see comming. After talking about the good things of the game it´s now time to talk about the bad ones with some spoilers in it.Since i played on hell until act 5 and then replayed on impossible until the end i can say if you just want to enjoy the game play hard max and if you want a challenge hell. Impossible is for people that really know the skills necessary to survive or in my case find a way.The first boss that was just unfair was meldine in act4. She shoots earth spikes at you which can be blocked no problem BUT if the spikes hit the ground next to you( because that magic is sprayed around) it creates earth magic that cannot be blocked.Unless you invest some points in healt and def you will insta die. The same boss fight becomes easy in the postscript because you can stay in the air where it doesn´t matter if it hits the ground. The second boss that is the reason you could never no death speedrun this game is the fake demon lord(demon summoner or something). He summons two enemies after some time up to six i think which includes bosses. And they are not just as strong as they were in the act you played in nooooo they have hitpoints like act 5.Just evil and i didn´t know you can buy the mokyu dolls postscript so i wanted to save all of them. Luckily he teleported into the ground/stairs where he did nothing and i just crossbowed him to death.Overall if you can´t defeat a boss just put all points into magic and use double crossbow unless its a 3:1 bossfight which happens in act8 and post act 8 twice(and the greater demon when you don´t have karons skills). One thing that felt like a missed opportunity was the secret marionette boss and the postscript marionette fight where if you fought it before Karon and Gau could make remarks on Shiro getting almost naked again. Since Shiro is the only character that  in postscript never regains her past memories for some reason it would make sense that it surprises her again.Another problem that i had with the game is that once you got all the loot out of gold and silver chests they only drop keymould B. Why? I can get stat cards out of the cheapest chests but the rare chests only drop moulds? That took all the excitement out whenever i saw them. Now in postscript the crossbow exploit and magic overall becomes almost negligent since you can buff weapons and armor but weapons only give atk not mag dmg.So i have a 30+weapon with over 2000atk(4000+ with everything) but only 1500 magic. All the skills in the maingame look cool but are really weak unless its a situation where it really hits like a truck.(phoenix for dmg and sylph and berserk for melee buff)The enemies that get controled by geas get a slightly different attack pattern which i found cool. Sadly after act 4 post they don´t have any new attacks which i found dissapointing.Last the achivements:the only two achivements that are pure evil and kaizo should be ashamed of it is the hit 200000 times and walk 50000 steps. When i finished the game i was at around 31k steps and 141k hits. So i had to put a fork in my keyboard to walk against a wall for 45min and spend another hour on the training stones. That was zero fun in a game that entertained me the entire time. Just reduce it by 50000hits and if possible it should be distance instead of steps since most people would move with air dash.Now to Gaiden(dlc)Gameplay wise it does so much better than the main game. The magic is strong, you can get stat cards out of all chests, the growth at the end where you can spend infinitly gives five times more statpoints etc. One of the biggest problems why i didn´t play with the berserk skill was the fact that enemies can spawn right at the door instakilling you. Why not make every a spawnfree zone of 1 1/2 character sprites to the left and right of the entrance?Also even in the last stratum no new enemy got introduced (the final boss not included in this) which i think is a lost opportunity. Another point i just remember is how after every run the game reminds you how you can spend force to grow....i got the message the first time why does it appear over and over again? Same goes for the Arena after every stratum that gets finished. The story in Gaiden makes no real sence in the main timeline as far as i can see. Maybe the first gameplayloop where you´re a ghost could be when the demons attacked the city but the hero was never trapped in the cave of mist(which kai apparently did to stop him from using the scales but in the main story he helps the hero getting into the future at that time sooo not really?).Also when you kill the hero becoming the new master of the scales looking at the main story where kuro kept ownership of the shield of laia after time rewinding and so on  it makes no sense in the timeline. The timeline when the goddess Lieselotte appears can be considered after the main game since the entire idea is to help Al Khasim revive Astarea but again at this point the Hero and Karon should freak out that the scales are just gone.The ending itself gives me mixed feelings kind of negating the sacrifice that Astarea made and not really making sence why the God of Life and Death calls the Bakers daughter the secret weapon that the gods planned for all along but at the same time giving a happy ending( For the end scene kaizo could have made a sleeping astarea dragon animation but whatever).Overall it´s a must play for fans of this genre and i hope the sequel baiting at the end of Gaiden will result in another dlc at least and a new game with a more planned out story than gaiden at best.Edit:Just remembered a few things. Shiro staying alive after chapter 5 is optional so i guess it makes sense that she never remembered her past life.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra is a fantastic experience. It blends together exploration, RPG elements, and hack-and-slash gameplay in a way that will always leave you wondering if you've seen everything it has to offer. And, unlike many of its peers that dwindle towards their ends, Astlibra walks its walk: from start to finish, you'll get to enjoy the same sense of discovery you had during the first chapter. The story is fantastic. The narrative structure is unique and punchy. Akin to the gameplay, you'll think you know everything--but you don't. I often found myself very excited reach the next cutscene. Carried by pacing, characters and dialog, these snippets defy what I feel is a glaring weakness inherent to a lot of games within a similar, idk, "vibe." It's great. I never skipped a scene, and the big picture these scenes compose are wonderful. The game is worth its full asking price--prohably worth more. Get it running, start up on normal difficulty (or hard for an additional achievement), and enjoy the ride. ...Or, you can peel another layer off the onion and play Hell or Impossible mode. I played through on Hell mode. They say the opposite of love is indifference, not hate. Both love and hate are instances of passion, after all, similar to how hot and cold are both temperatures. I love Astlibra so much, and I know that because of how much I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HATE ASTLIBRAYou know the story about the ant and the grasshopper? The ant has the power of foresight and prepares for the Winter. Meanwhile, the grasshopper is a dumb weak little ♥♥♥♥♥ who thinks they can handle Hell mode because the "slimes weren't THAT dangerous." By the time the wintry blizzards blow in during the game's third (or so) chapter, it's too late for the grasshopper. All they'll know is the mounting cold. The hunger. The misery. And the season their hubris has exposed them to never seems to end. With each chapter, the game's enemies are slightly more engineered to hurt you. Not the character. YOU. It's like looking at your Webcam and finding the little red light's on; you start to realize exactly how cognizant the game is of how its players will behave. It knows your hopes, your dreams, your desires--mainly the desire to get to the other side of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ screen without dying. By chapter six, every area is a different torture device, like an art gallery of tucker telephones. By chapter seven? The fact a bug can send its spiny tongue in TWO directions is enough to make a grown person weep. If you've ever played Dark Souls, you are probably familiar with the dread of discovering the 'bonfire to boss' run is long. On Hell mode, you get to enjoy that dread over. And over. And over. Sometimes you'll finish a fight, go to the next screen, and see ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BASTARDS instead of a save crystal. The hopelessness that inflicts is mentally scarring. Hell's difficulty is a straight line upward, up and up until it has broken past the boundaries of the graph. You arrive at a fight, or a set of screens before the next checkpoint. You die, and you are CONVINCED this is impossible, it's too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ unfair to be possible. You just barely managed the last thing you thought was impossible. And then you win. And your reward? Something that makes you wish to go back to the last thing. Anyway, play on Hell difficulty. Feel the call of the void and dive into the deep end. It is, as tacky as it is to say, the full Astlibra experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra: Revision is one of my all-time favorite games. I was completely addicted for over 100 hours, until I finally finished the game and got the true ending. Astlibra is a 2D side-scrolling action RPG with amazingly deep mechanics with regard to both the action side and the role-playing side. On the action side, this game perfectly integrates the following mechanics: blocking, parrying, deflecting, jumping, double-jumping, triple-jumping, hovering, dashing, air-dashing, backflipping, combos, juggles, special moves, staggering, critical hits, sword-and-shield builds, two-handed weapon builds, magic-focused builds, ranged weapons such as bows and crossbows, and more! On the RPG side, the game provides countless ways to customize and uniquely level-up your character, including different weapons, shields, suits of armor, boots, clothing, talismans, magical enhancements, consumable items (that often need to be crafted or cooked first), weapon upgrades, magical items, and so on.The story is incredible too. It is imaginative, intricate, gripping, and moving. The game's world and its story showcase a unique blend of fantasy, medieval adventure, and science fiction. And the 2D visuals bring everything to life with a style that manages to be both adorable and spectacular.Finally, the music in this game is mind-blowingly good. I listen to the OST in my free time, because the music is that good. The mix of genres is sensational, including classical, folk, rock, metal, hip-hop, dubstep, drum & bass, techno, trance, and more. You might not think that such a mix of genres would work in a game like Astlibra, but each song is perfectly matched to the level it belongs to, as well as the events of the story surrounding it.If you like character action games with deep combat, and if you also like story-driven Japanese RPGs with complex character customization, then you will surely love Astlibra: Revision as I do. The gorgeous 2D graphics and world-class music simply seal the deal.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra is a fantastic Metroidvania with surprisingly good combat mechanics. This game is absolutely what you're looking for if you want to play something like Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. The story can get surprisingly dark and mysterious which makes it very compelling.The game also features a game mechanic where your companion learns passive skills from the equipment that you find from your journey (Weapons, Shields, and Armor). Enemies drop elemental "force" that you can use to give stat buffs to your character, unlock new offensive magical spells, and treasures to gain more power for your character (advancement of this mechanic is restricted at certain points until you further advance the story).There is also a passive system that uses the items that you find and craft on your adventure to empower your character and offer unique benefits to your character such as increased resistance to all manner of status effects, increased exp, increased coins from enemies, and even passive Health recovery.Many treasures are well hidden, and side content like the Arena offer fantastic rewards. The story is linear, but at certain points you are able to backtrack to seek missing treasure or additional force to power up your character. There is content in the game that you can miss depending on your decisions at certain points in the story.I spent quite a bit of time on this game and it was very enjoyable. I honestly did a bit more grinding than I needed to when I could have just used a different setup to defeat a certain boss. Mix up your tactics and try different weapons as wildly swinging your weapon may not be enough to overcome your enemies.The sound quality can be off at times as some enemies make strange sounds, but this game's soundtrack is quite fantastic. Visual quality is also very good overall. Be wary that some bosses fire many projectiles and you can lose track of what's going on if you have additional characters on screen when using your character's abilities. I would also strongly advise that you reduce the screen flashing in the options menu.Overall this game is easy to recommend for anyone wanting a Metroidvania with a lot of content. It will keep you busy for quite some time and challenge you as much as you wish.

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt an amazing JRPG. Taking nods from gaming classics such as Chrono Trigger and Castlevania, and combining them into a perfect blend of exactly everything I miss from the 90s/early 2000s of gaming. Mechanically the game constantly adds new features and abilities all the way up to its very finish. This keeps the gameplay fresh and does a very good job of gating power so you do not become too easily overpowered on higher difficulties. While a bit grindy at times to unlock new abilities on gear or get enemies to drop specific materials, most of this can be lightened with abilities or increasing luck. The story does a good job of keeping you wondering what is going to happen, and has a hell of a payoff at the end. It took me around 110 hours to fully 100 percent the game on the second highest difficulty. And that was with me being a bit slow because I loved playing so much. With all those glowing points, I cannot stress enough that this game may not be for everyone. There is VERY Japanesey writing and characters that unless you enjoy the tropes and the goofiness I can see why someone may be put off. On the other hand, if you enjoy these things pick it up immediately because the game is brilliant.For a one guy love project that took 15 years and is easily better than the AAAA standard nowadays, its an easy sell. I love this game, and I hope more people get a chance to experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: You start with a stick, beating slimes and soon are fighting dragons and other epic creatures, a slow and intense, not really boring grind to reach godhood levels, seeing big numbers popping over and over as you slash or explode your enemies.Developed by a single person in the span of about 15 years, Astlibra Revision is an enhanced version of Astlibra proof of life. It adds a new chapter - and has new art by Shigatake, making it closer to almost being a Vanillaware title.The plot is as heavy as any RPGs and visual novels, making it an interesting and important point. Hell, so many good time travel stories spawned since its initial development that I feel a little burnt out by them, but it's always cool and exciting to see.Finding hidden equipment, learning new mechanics and plot details, challenging bosses you missed before, having a huge variety of equipment and customization that make progression extremely fun.And the soundtrack is really cool as well, mixing many genres and a lot of good and memorable Vocaloid songs. They are memorable, and I still listen to them from time to time.Chapter four was the lowest point for me, mostly due to story-related reasons. Chapter 3 and everything else gets better as you go, plus the post-game teaches you new mechanics with a lot of content, making it worth your time with a rewarding and fulfilling new ending.This game is an inspiring indie achievement and I'm glad to have played it. Might play the DLC someday.Pumpkin Hill Part II -

_childDocuments_.review: What certain news outlets touted as the "lovechild of Final Fantasy and Castlevania" is a really fun game, though I would  call it either of those things. It'd be a disservice to what this game is.This game is its own thing. Sure, it shares some similar mechanics (weapon variety, "spells", license board-like power ups) but the meat of the game is in the fluid combat, how you go from melee to "magic" and back, the importance of using the right elements and the right abilities for each combat, and how each "build" is viable. It's a fun experience and a treat to both the eyes and the hands.The downside is there's not much  variety in the style of gameplay, if you want to blast enemies with magic, you have to use your weapons to charge up. If you don't care about magic and want to go full caveman, you're still gonna have a hard time passing up those i-frames and high-defense moments the spellcasting gives you. However, that's kind of a minor downside if you ask me.The GREAT thing is how much you can customize. Seriously, you prefer to have a skill that lets you shield bash more often AND one that lets you put your shield up more quickly over having double jump? Sure, you can do it. You want to get skills to suck up money but don't have enough currency for activating the skill? There's ways around it. And don't get me started on the puzzles. They're great. Cleverly hidden, you're gonna probably feel like Sherlock or Poirot when you find the solutions. From what little I've played, NOTHING is there by accident, and that's amazing.Now, the real downer is the translation: this game has got a terrible translation. I'm sorry, there's just no way around it, you're gonna be scratching your head half the time figuring out the mechanics of a skill or how to solve a puzzle solely on the fact that the translation is dead-wrong. Still, Google is a thing, most of the things have been asked already.Hopefully I haven't scared you out of getting this gem.Oh, did I mention it's criminally cheap? A true labor of love, this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The story provides and engaging and nuanced take on the old time travel formula with multiple endings possible. The characters are likable and almost all of them have depth and some form of a backstory. Game play is excellent if you like side scrolling hack and slash, metroidvania-esque item hunting, and loot farming type of games. The controls aren't extremely precise but the hit boxes feel fairly accessible so the game play isn't hindered. The challenge remained consistent on hard mode although by postscript endgame, I was severely overpowered. That's more a testament to how satisfying the grinding/loot farming was than a critique on the balance of the game.If I absolutely had to complain about something, it's that this game reeeealllly leans into tropes of traditional gender roles, damsels in distress, and casual misogyny for humor. Not really anything that we're not all used to and probably has a lot to do with the fact that this game has been 14 years in the making (!!!) but just seems like we can progress beyond that at this point.Overall, a fantastic game that you makes you feel like you're visiting old friends when you boot it up. I'll be praying to Goddess Astraea that Keizo releases a sequel before mankind goes extinct.

_childDocuments_.review: I was sceptic seeing people praise this game since the screenshots looked pretty average, but after having finished the game I was blown away. It's very satisfying overcoming them (definitely play on hard difficulty, I assume normal is too easy)+ very nice boss designs+ grand story: seriously it just keeps going + likeable charactersCons:- this is the biggest problem this game has and which was also a thorn in my side: I assume its the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ translation:The dialogue can sometimes sound very awkward (not how normal people would speak) and can get up to straight up incomprehensible. _childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10 for meThis game is generally filled with incredible highs and a few low points that are extremely annoying to slog through -Fantastic story involving time travel that delves into the consequences of altering the past, as well as having      an epic 'present day' narrative.  It has great foreshadowing for some of the big moments as well as a few      twists that caught me completely by surprise.-Amazing music-Fun action combat that can be played in multiple ways depending on your equipment and skill selection-Good balance between weapon types((weapon+shield,2-handed weapon,magic wand/staff,focusing on your     companion summons)-the game incentives you to experiment with all the equipment you find by unlocking skills for each piece of      gear you 'master'-multiple progression systems to increase your character power -some of the puzzles are quite obtuse, I got stuck and had to use a guide twice(chapter 6 was terrible for     this), although some of the puzzles are also very clever and felt satisfying to solve-I would describe some of the humor as being 'cringe' anime inspired sex jokes, chapter 4 was the worst for    this.  There were only a few scenes where it came up but if you don't like that style of humor this game    may not be for you-graphics are mid, although either the style grew on me as I played the game or the background designs     improved throughout the gameI actually played the game for like 58 hours, not 38, but I didn't have internet for a few days while playing so steams timer is wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's some information about the game for folks who don't know what to expect from such high user score:Side-scrolling action rpg with heavy influence from Japanese comics and animation;No voiced dialogues which is to be expected considering the game is done by two men and the fact that we play as silent protagonist;Cutscenes are skippable and text boxes can be sped up;Fanservice is ecchi level, but it does occur only few times. There's also fetish stuff in some dialogues;No new game+ (instead there's postgame), the story progress is linear for most of the time. The few choices that happen during it doesn't affect the ending - if anything, it affect the grinding for true ending;Expect backtracking and some platforming;True ending require collecting gear (weapons, armors and shields) and defeating optional bosses;In order to 100% the game You need to play at least on Hard. Once set, the difficulty cannot be changed during the game;The variety of mechanics and gear allow making different builds.Personal impressions:Fun, fluid combat;Good, clean visuals;Simple, but proper soundtrack with some variety;The writing could be better (plot itself is fine for the most time, but it feels being dragged toward the ending and two dimensional characters doesn't help either);Given that and mentioned earlier fanservice, I wouldn't recommend this title to everyone.Why not giving a proper review? Simple, go download the demo - it covers the entire first chapter of the game (of all ten). That's how I ended up purchasing the game and I'll most likely buy the next one from Keizo.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't leave many reviews, yadda yadda, but for people on the fence TL;DR, if you enjoy the demo at all, grab it. I'm cheap as hell, I was on the fence for a month. You'll get way more than your money's worth honestly and it only gets better as the game goes on.(potential spoilers below)This game did three things incredibly I just haven't seen out of many, if any, games in recent memory:1. Respecting player time and curiosity2. CONSTANT progression3. Build freedomNot to mention the most Billy Mays moment I've had in over a decade.There were a few moments in the game that soured the experience for me, just mechanically, but overall, a very solid game that's difficult to find major fault with. The fighting has enough depth and peculiarity to feel fun (although a bit too often you find yourself locked out of horizontal movement) The story has enough unique spikes, some mature tones and needs more recognition for not being afraid to just do crazy things. The OST is pretty much perfect for the game (Ys fans will feel right at home with the OST) And the menuing, oh I could go on about how solid the menus are for a JRPG. Still a bit too sticky here and there, but considering how much menu work needs doing on harder difficulties, they are damn responsive.Easily memorable characters, EARLY MOVEMENT ABILITIES, weird eccentric enemies, even moreso for the bosses.This game has a good amount of little faults and frustrations, but it feels like an old game where there's so much NEAT AND COOL AND GOOD that the little irritants are just that...just a "oh that sucks...welp, screw that and move on." Classic console jank in the best way.So again, highly recommend, probably the only reason you wouldn't enjoy it is if you don't like the base concept of growth based rpgs. Also, as an odd side note, if you play idle/incremental games, it scratches some of that itch too. Between the menuing and build layout, it feels incremental-like.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what I was looking for.  I started working a midnight shift at a hotel which allows several hours of gaming time.  I wanted something that a workplace computer was capable of playing but was more engaging than endless pac-man or finding ninja cats.  My thought process went from either a retro snes era rpg, an older mmorpg, a 2d side-scroller metroidvania style throwback like maybe Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night.  First I downloaded Ultima Online to give the OG a try but unfortunately it felt very dated.  Then I was considering MapleStory, because it brought my lots of joy and nostalgia probably about a decade ago.  Finally while browsing the store I came across ASTLIBRA and it is honestly a culmination everything I was looking for.  There are elements of nostalgia, old-school rpg, metroidvania, solo mapling with better combat.  It's really turned this overnight hotel gig into my favorite of my 3 jobs.  Loving the game.  Crow homie is cool.  Excellent stuff.Now that I'm 60 hours into it I have some slight criticisms, though I still thoroughly enjoy the game.  I feel like its an odd creative choice to play the same credits video half a dozen times, but that's whatever.  The seriousness of the story is slightly diminished by the sexual innuendo and gratuitous bussin' tiddy.  And while i'm not some prude who is above an innuendo and a tiddy, it sometimes feels out of place and inconsistent.  Still, even with these minor issues it's still a solid 8.8/10
