_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others Note: This title was reviewed with a review code for both Nintendo Switch and for Steam. Golf. Yes Golf, it was never a sport that fascinated me. But what if this concept was mixed with aspects of roguelike and in a way platforms? It sounds risky, but it is in fact something that Cursed to Golf manages to present in a very positive way. When you think of Golf, the first adjectives that usually come to mind are relaxing or even therapeutic… Something that doesn’t happen at all in this title. In fact, think of anything but relaxation. In the midst of labyrinths of platforms, fans, sand and even TNT’s, there is room for a whole range of unexpected dangers that make even the greatest professional in this sport lose a few hairs.This title puts the player in the position of a professional golf player, who is on the way to winning a tournament that is widely recognized worldwide. At the last shot, a huge storm overshadows the area and a lightning strikes our little champion, in a scene that seems to be taken from the old movie ” Caddyshack “. In this way, the little golfer’s soul is sent to a kind of purgatory. The objective is to come back to life again, but for that, you will have to complete 18 holes in a somewhat spooky environment.All the mechanics are presented by the friendly Scotsman, the ghost of a Scottish golfer who finds himself in the same situation as our character. Already resigned that he will never get out of this situation, he becomes a kind of Master Roshi from DragonBall, from purgatory, where his goal is to help those who literally fall there. There isn’t much more to explore regarding the story, as all the benefit you can get will be from your gameplay. The magic of Cursed to Golf comes from the small moments when you discover the perfect way to get to the hole in mechanically interesting ways.The gameplay is presented in a simple and intuitive way. It is necessary to choose the type of club, of the three clubs available, choose the angle and the force that you want to apply in the next shot. It may seem simple at first, but there is a somewhat steep learning curve, as the levels are not completely linear. There are occasions where it is necessary to use different mechanics to reach a point higher than the player, this is because the action does not only unfold in the side scroller sense, as it is also possible to move horizontally. It’s interesting to note that in a way, it also unfolds as a platformer, where instead of jumping with the character itself, you’ll have to hit the ball to make it reach the desired platform. The accuracy of the shot is very important.The very construction of the levels makes things more interesting, presenting different ways to cause problems for the player. Sand and water are present, but they are joined by elements such as graves with zombie hands, where if the ball lands there, the shot is lost and it returns to the same place before the shot, spikes, fans, and even boxes of TNT. Most of the time, TNT boxes hide behind them detours or shorter paths that help the player to get to the hole in fewer strokes. In most cases, success depends on choosing the correct route that you might think it’s possible to overcome. But the actual act of overcoming in a positive way is another story. That’s the premise of a Roguelike, right?It is important to pay special attention to the number of strokes you can make. The player is given a limited number of strokes, which can be increased by using cards. However, if you run out of strokes, the player will return to the starting point, not from the level he is on, but from the Run, right at the beginning of the first hole. Of course, you can try as many times as you want and possibly with new knowledge acquired from previous Runs, but you will never stop feeling that pressure of needing to reach the hole still with shots to be made.As for the cards, this is also where the Roguelike premise comes in. During the levels, it is possible, in the path choice menu, to pass through houses with gold boxes, or even through houses where Booster packs can be found. In this way, it is possible to buy cards, with the money previously saved, or to open these Booster packs. Cards function as perks, such as having +2 strokes, or as active skills, which help the player overcome dangers. Techniques such as making the ball heavy by pressing the button, separating the ball into three different balls with the possible choice of the one you want at the end, are just some of the examples. If by chance the player goes back to the beginning by missing the hole, the cards are removed from his inventory.Things get a little repetitive as there isn’t a huge variety of skills, or a natural progression or upgrades to them. Yes, there is, the demotivating feeling after a few hours of effort applied to try to reach a point so advanced and run out of shots… Yes, it hurts a lot. It kinda becomes a personal battle against the former self, in order to beat the level that previously couldn’t be achieved. It wasn’t addictive in my case, but it will certainly find that niche of people.Cursed to Golf is an interesting golf title. It creatively mixes elements from different genres, features eye-catching pixel art graphics, and has a synth-heavy soundtrack with a Halloween breeze that helps keep things lively. But watch your ears, the first sound when you press “Play” is huge. I wouldn’t say it’s just a title for fans of the sport, I’m not, and I managed to take advantage of the fun of venturing into this purgatory.Looking for a good challenge? Will you have what it takes to unleash the professional golf player in you?

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty neat game that does have some drawbacks that will probably not make it entirely replayable, like a game of Everybody's Golf. But a lot of the complaints in reviews are just outright stupid, largely put forth by simpletons. The camera? without its limitations the game would be ridiculously easy, more than it already is. Being able to see exactly where the ball is gonna land at mid range, but having to calculate it at long range was the only trade-off that makes sense for a 2D golf game.The complaints of difficulty and punishment? Honestly, the game is just pretty easy. If you can't beat the game within 10 rounds you aren't using the cards right and taking advantage of shortcuts put there for a reason.Literally my only complaint with the game is its length does tend to hinder the thought of replaying it. The game sorely needed a separate mode outside the Roguelike setting.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Rouge-likes and golf games (Mario Golf and Golf Story), this game was a let down. In a game where every shot counts, the lack of control you have in your aiming made the game too frustrating for me to want to continue. In the hour I played this game, too many of my runs felt like they came down to either slightly mistiming my shot and barely hitting the lip of a wall, putting me into a situation where I have no chance to recover, or botching the use of one the ace cards, again putting me into an over all worse position had I not tried anything fancy and went for the 'intended route' on the course. While these issues are mostly on me for the lack of trying and not wanting to put more time to 'git-gud'; the severe lack of meta progression in this game is the main reason I felt like I should leave a review. Apart from the ability to put spin on the ball after you fail your first run, the only other meta progression I noticed was 'banking' your ace cards for future runs. No talents, stats, or equipment of any kind to help give you an edge on the course. With basically all of the shortcuts to the hole gated by the usage of ace cards (U-Turn to gain height or Practice shot/Explosion to destroy TNT), I don't see what's fun about crippling my current run in the hopes I'll save the right cards for the right situation in a different run. Maybe if you could bank a card when you lose a run it could be even a little more interesting, but having it only be available at a shop makes for a poor experience when you still can't even reach the first boss and have no idea what to expect in future runs.TL;DR 5/10 - Interesting concept, but the controls were too frustrating for a 'precision-platform' golf game and a lack of meta progression had me losing interest very quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I cannot recommend this game. The only positives about it are the idea and the characters. Before buying I watched an ~1hour episode of this game on YouTube, unfortunately with this game - it gets worse the longer you play.1. Game is still bugged, sometimes the game does not show what it should (apparently game logic does not go in pair with what is displayed on the screen), second boss brought this bug once to another level, by completely locking a game, because something went wrong with his core mechanic and the game didn't know how to continue.2. Every next level is longer and more difficult, which is normal in most of the games, but here it's too much. While it is mostly managable during "normal" levels (using idols and some cards), the boss levels are a joke. Not only you still need to care about the "par" count (which you basically need to exclusively deal with using cards, as you don't have time to pursue idols), but you also face an opponent. AI never makes any mistakes, its shots are perfect or close to it every time. First boss only shoots with more power than a player, so with some shortcuts he can be beaten, but second one? Still shoots with more power, but also has a mechanic that makes a course twice as difficult for the player? When we add to it the length of a course, you easily need dozens of cards and perfect play to even have a minor chance of beating this level.3. The runs are too long for the use of roguelike mechanics, you can really feel like ♥♥♥♥ after losing a couple hours run due to a single mistake or two.4. Some of the cards (Iceball for example) lack description of what they actually do or help with.

_childDocuments_.review: Terrible game.  Decent concept but just garbage execution in so many ways.  Game doesn't even let you zoom out to see where your shot will go.  You are always so far zoomed in, you can't see where the ball will go which leads you to have very little understanding of what will actually happen when you shoot it.  Top that off with just absolute unforgiving gameplay where one bad shot means you effectively isnta-lose the entire hole (since getting stuck somewhere bad means two or three shots lost). This game looks and feels like someone played Golf Story and thought they could do a similar thing.  But clearly this person didn't understand game play design, controls, UX design, and story.  Music is okay but super repetitive.  The bones are here of something that could have been good, but the truly cursed things are the actual game and the fools who play it.  Not even worth it on discount, don't bother with it at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: I like the idea of it, but the execution has a lot of problems that just make the prospect of playing this game not fun.The biggest reason I won't play the game any more is that there are multiple tracks where you MUST have a dynamite card to progress or to get out of certain paths. As the cards are random and extremely limited, and you only start with one dynamite card, you are certain to get stuck through sheer RNG.Additionally, the cards are a poor system that just make the game feel worse. I feel it would have been better if instead of a limited one time resource, the cards were available to you at every course. They would need to be less plentiful and have you choose how you obtain them more, but it would be a far more satisfying and reliable system.You're also not able to stay zoomed out while shooting, which is another infuriating element that I just can't comprehend why they would choose it to be like that. For a game that is supposed to be strategic in play, this makes no sense.As it stands, I just can't bring myself to play this game.EDIT: Apparently just hitting the dynamite with the ball will detonate it. But the game introduced the mechanic with the card and it never said that. That was merely the straw that broke the camel's back. The rest of it has enough problems that I'm not willing to play this.

_childDocuments_.review: I love roguelikes and these style of golf games so I really wanted to like this game but in the end I just couldn't. It isn't difficult as much as it is clumsy. They improved some of the most glaring issues (slow down speeds, zoom out to see more of where you are aiming, although still not far enough with bounces) but ultimately the clunky controls do not mesh with the required precision. There are other things I don't love about the game (animations and transitions take FOREVER, courses can be too long, ace cards are difficult to navigate) but ultimately those are just minor annoyances. The controls make the game fundamentally unenjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a fantastic idea, but sometimes tries way too hard to force the story down your throat. This was totally fine up until the 18th hole. Originally I wasn't going to review this game either way, but enough has happened that I feel like despite the cute ascetic and fun concept, I can't in good faith recommend playing this game as a fan of rogue-likes.I feel like it is also important for me to add, unlike a lot of the other negative reviews, I don't actually think the difficulty is that bad, as long as you realize that the only things that really matter are pins. I beat the game my first time playing it, and ended with a deck of over 30 cards, 9 of them being +6 pars, so honestly I felt it was a bit easy just slow.TLDR: Far more focus on story than gameplay (granted the story is cute), it's not actually all that hard imo (assuming you heavily invest in good pins), and in my opinion it's good to play once ever as a singleplayer story, rather than a roguelike.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. The gameplay is petty straight forward and totally itches the scratch of "jump in and play a few holes".Unfortunately, I feel like this is mostly a missed opportunity. It's missing key roguelike elements like the ability to add skills to your bag or any type of skill tree or character points. The only way to win is to get good and, many times, lucky. Your deaths are meaningless because you're never building towards anything. Not a stronger shot, or spin, or different clubs, or the ability to see more map, etc. There are so many ways to enhance the gameplay and depth of the game that it feels a bit unfinished in its current state. It's really a shame. I love the art style and the controls/feel of the game. It's just a little too shallow for me, especially at this price point.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is average at best, they wanted a dark souls style of golf game but I never once felt like I truly deserved the round loss. It got to where I just force closed the game if I was going to lose the hole or fight. Each loss was always due to some cheese, prime example is the first boss teleported through a wall and beat me to the hole. speaking of the holes they are long and drawn out with confusing layouts, some having 2 finishing holes, some only have 1. The game does a horrible job at explaining mechanics like spin until after you have a round loss under your belt, or that you can blow up TNT with a standard ball hit instead of having to use the ace card. _childDocuments_.review: I was excited by the concept, unfortunately, after playing I have to conclude that the game is more suitable for portable consoles or phones than for desktop gaming. First of all, the game is too overplayed, from the boring tutorial to further narration. Secondly, there is the rigid and not very pleasant system of aiming while hitting. It's simplified to just choosing the direction, and doesn't give you any more freedom for precise strikes. You only choose the force of the hit and the game itself controls the flight vector, which is very rigid, like in the old games. Unfortunately, I like mobile golf and have seen many better solutions.  This makes the game slow and boring to play at the computer. It would work perfectly for playing one game portable, for a quick game because the rest of the aspects from the great pixel art, music to the out-of-the-box idea itself is awesome. ps. it would be useful to have an option to speed up time without having to hold the key, or just skip the animations

_childDocuments_.review: "Cursed to Golf" is a golf based roguelike where you try to escape hell by beating all 18 holes.This via various "illegal" moves.Horrible - Bad -  - Good - AmazingAlmost every achievement is story related - exceptions being a hole in 4 to a hole in 1.The latter ones aren't too difficult, just requiring some game knowledge and map rng.I enjoyed this game a good bit, but that's not to say it's perfect.The inherent gameplay loop is a bit repetitive as you need to go through 4 areas (some with very long holes) and fight the same 3 bosses over until you beat the game, after which they will not be there anymore.The card variety is good, but that tends to make it fairly rng dependent on whether or not a boss will be easy to beat. I also didn't see the phantom ball at any point, which is kind of disappointing.The legendary cards are inherently OP (as to be expected), which can make some holes trivial. The portal card for example lets you skip an entire section of the last hole, kind of defeating the point of a difficult path.Pins are a fun addition, but come with the same liability towards difficulty. (Mini rocket toggle let me skip 80% of the last course for some reason.) Considering how cheap those are, and how they're both infinite use, and up to 3 different kinds, that basically renders the game difficulty to be a joke if you get good store luck.Playing courses normally you'll constantly find yourself hitting the par count (failstate), which makes it fairly tedious as you'll have to constantly aim for idols, or spam par count cards. With a boss power up this count also becomes near irrelevant, kind of ruining the point of a difficult game... - To add to that, you can exit to menu to restart a hole at any time, which makes it feel even less like a roguelike and more like a puzzle game.My final real gripe is that this game is  I'm talking 5 or so freezes, a few loading errors, and multiple crashes. This can be especially frustrating when you're almost done with a hole and the game decides to crash on you (which resets you to the last hole). These feel like things that should've been fixed years ago but haven't yet...Bad stuff out of the way:This game booms with charm and swagger and has a pretty amusing story to carry its weight. Every enemy golfer felt distinctly different and had their own cool design. The boss fights were also one of the more interesting parts as their inherent mechanics added a lot of otherwise missed challenge.The road choice system is fun as you can usually choose between a cursed or normal hole (cursed ones giving better rewards), as well as cash or card rewards. The hole and sound design are also really good (give or take tnt destroying your eardrums once in a while...), and definitely add a lot of the visual charm that this game radiates. Not really a roguelike; charming even with its flaws. If you're looking for a sports roguelike? Absolutely not.If you're looking for a charming game, and you're fine with the downsides? Sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Golf? Love it. Roguelikes? Big fan. So, naturally, *Cursed to Golf* should’ve been a hole-in-one for me. But for some reason, I just can’t get into it. It works great on my Steam Deck, the story is cool, and the levels are visually interesting. But the gameplay mechanics? They’re more frustrating than fun.   *Cursed to Golf* has an interesting concept and a lot of potential, but it just didn’t click for me. While it runs well and looks cool, the mechanics are more frustrating than fun, making it hard to stick with even one round. If you’re a fan of the genre, it might be worth a try, but for me, it’s a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice game. The idea is great and I do enjoy the roguelike nature of the game. But a few things make it fall flat from getting a solid 10/10 - 1. Being unable to aim - the aiming trajectory isn't something you can set. You can't aim yourself. The trajectory keeps moving up and down and you have to press the hit button at the exact moment to get the ball going where you want to. This was an awful feature as many a times I've hit corners/overshot/undershot just because I was a millisecond too late in hitting the button. Not cool.2. The camera - There's a zoom in and zoom out button. But the zoom out button does not zoom out far enough for some cases. If your shot goes out of the camera zone, it doesn't zoom out to show you where it could end up (before making the shot). You just have to hope the ball ends up where you'd like it to end up.These are my two major gripes with the game which merits it a 7/10. Had these mechanics been different, it would've been so much more enjoyable. Devs, learn from Super Stickman Golf if you can!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game and the concept, and I didn't even mind the super long runs since I would just split up my play sessions. I did however feel that the game was too easy, and I beat it on my first run. I think the "too easy" aspect combined with the really long runs creates an experience that grates on people. It's a fun game, but I think it could have been better had the runs been broken up differently or a bit shorter. Maybe each world could have been a separate zone to run, where each time you beat one you unlock the next and start a new run. Cards are super broken, if you just save your gold and buy a crap ton of card packs you can cheese your way through most holes without much effort. I know that is the intent, but the rocket cards are a little too strong and trivialize parts of the game.Pins were a cool addition, but I also think they destroyed the balance of the game, as they aren't even that expensive and can give you a huge advantage at all times even though the game was likely originally balanced around the cards.Overall, I think this is a good game, but I would have felt a lot better if it was $15 instead of $20. _childDocuments_.review: What a delightful game! I regret to say that I let the Mostly Positive review rating on Steam put me off buying the game for some time but it really looked like a game I would enjoy. And so when it was on a deep discount for the summer sale I took the shot and wowowow what a great little arcadey golf game!Someone else said it best: This is a precision platformer under the guise of a golf game. You won't find your dad's golf game here. This is an arcadey 2D turn-based platformer with procedurally generated levels and permadeath (unless you bind a "Force Game Shutdown" button and quit before the game saves your progress after you lose).I'm happy to say that I didn't need the force quite option to win this game on my first attempt. The game was a bit challenging but it gives you so many fun little powerups to get you through the game. Perhaps I just had a really lucky first run but I never even came close to running out of my par meter. This surprised me the most because of all the negative reviews.It took me 4.5 hours to play through one round though. So I can see how someone going in blind to this game could be very frustrated losing a hole and losing literal hours of progress. But again, just bind the "force quit" action to something or press Alt+F4 if you don't want to play that way.But having already beaten the game once, I'm still hungry for more. The game felt like it was just getting started with all the different cool things you can do with the powerups you get from Ace Cards. Having beaten the game once, there feels way less stress on seeing all the content in the game and I can just enjoy messing around trying to get the coolest shortcuts.This game is an absolute blast and I'm honestly ashamed I waited so long to play it. The pixel art is top tier. The characters are very fun and there's so much heart that was poured into this game. Go into it knowing what it is and you'll have a great time!

_childDocuments_.review: While I think the core game itself is great, the rogue-like elements just doesn’t fit with the level designs. Maybe if the courses were shorter like putt putt this would’ve worked much better. But with how long each hole takes to complete, and the fact that there’s 18 holes for each run, it’s such a chore to slug through each time you have to start over! And it sucks because like I said, I really liked the core golf gameplay, the story was simple, the graphics were cute. This would’ve been a fine golfing game without the rogue-like design. If they removed the rogue like part, make each hole much more unique in their design, I would easily recommend this. But sadly I cannot. What a shame. ONE NOTE: There is a loophole to avoid the roguelike portion. If you exit before you lose the game, you reset to the last hole you were on. Just something to note just in case the rogue like was the only portion that was preventing you from buying this.

_childDocuments_.review: This arcade-style golf game provides some intriguing similarities to it's big brothers, EA Sports PGA Tour and PGA 2K, in showcasing the risk-reward of the actual game.  If you ever thought to yourself, "There's no way I'll hit that hazard!" you'll be proven wrong time and time again.  There's a level of sophistication here I simultaneously enjoyed and hated (see:  final three holes).  I don't believe the game is quite that difficult, it's just that I often went Tin Cup trying extremely risky shots over and over again or going ham off the tee at every opportunity.  In my experience, my mistakes were mostly my own.  Play it safe and you'll almost always succeed.  Some minor quibbles, I often forgot(?) to activate a card and I often forgot to press "B" to activate a power mid-flight.  Additionally, I'd like to see a demonstration of new powers when they are obtained.  Because of the lack of information, I often wasted a card and a shot figuring out how it works.  For instance, Drill Shot transforms the ball immediately and not upon bounce.  In short, lots of risk, plenty of rewards (and frustrations), and playing conservatively is often correct, but where's the fun in that?

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game and absolutely loved it - until i realised the developers COMPLETELY broke the game with the Golf Pin update. The game was orignally very balanced, with usable upgrades as cards. With the Pins however, the balance is completely broken. 2-3 holes in, i could buy PINS that completely triviliased the game. Permanent scattershots and permanent +5 shots on each holes. Just ridicilous. I get the impression the developers tried to respond to people who found the game difficult by adding pins - but... there was absolutely zero balancing done, just lazily implemented superpowers that made you invisible. For comparision, to show how broken it is. You can buy a scattershot card for make 450 gold, meaning you can split the balls into 3 balls for one shot. Once. Superuseful. But this pin, for maybe 900 gold - makes it so you can PERMANENTLY split balls, every shot - with no penalty. Worse yet, they didnt even... seem to add pure classic mode or whatever, they just broke their game. Too bad because the core game is wonderful. But i refunded it. Take notes devs, balance is King.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't get very far into the game, but unfortunately I found the golf mechanics a little frustrating for a roguelike.The game will communicate to you where your ball will go with the dotted lines, but these can sometimes go off the screen making the shot blind. I don't mind the dots moving so you have to time your shot as it adds a level of impreciseness which brings some needed risk into the roguelike element, but some more visual communication or control over the abilities would go a long way. For example one ability lets you stop the ball's momentum so it can fall vertically, but I didn't find the game responsive enough to successfully fall down gaps I was aiming for so I couldn't be accurate with the ability at all. Also one ability lets you split into three balls but there's no visual communication where those will go after a split, so again you're using an ability that feels more like random luck. This makes it feel like the game is at odds with itself, where it wants to give you accuracy and control but also make the game more random using those exact same mechanics.The initial tutorial is good and I didn't mind it being a bit longer to ensure you got mechanics, but I couldn't get to grips with ball spin which is introduced later - the tutorial description wasn't quite clear enough and I felt like I fluked the tests, which meant I wasn't going to risk using it in a level/run.These things may be fine for most, but are enough to put me off giving the game more time at the moment. The presentation and everything else was good.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very charming and fun game. I know a lot of people dislike it because of the difficulty curve but after understanding how the game works and understood that your literally in golf purgatory so the game isnt even suppose to be fair, it was easier to approach and think of solutions. There is 3 settings. One viewing distance perfect for short ranged wedge shots, and one viewing distance perfect for medium range Iron shots. Then there is the birdie view to move around and view the whole course as long as you held a button down There is no good viewing distance for Driver shots so a lot of the time your shooting into the dark which is really dumb. _childDocuments_.review: I like golf games - I don't know why. I like roguelikes - I do know why. Cursed to Golf scratched a very, very specific itch at the intersection of both of those for me, and I had a great time. However, in order to like this game you really need to be sold on the "golf" part of it.The golf mechanics are fun. The spin system is satisfying. The randomly generated holes are sufficiently wacky, presenting daring skill shot and shortcut opportunities for the brave. It's always tempting to try and thread the needle through a line of spikes rather than take the nice, easy, long way around. The power ups are interesting and let you get creative, (with the exception of the "+X Stroke" and "Practice Shot+" cards, see below)As a roguelike, the game stumbles - this game desperately wants you to beat it. You never have to re-fight a boss. You can store your power cards between runs. You eventually unlock double shots per level and the ability to set a restore point. There's no reason to use a "+2 Shot" card until you're on your last stroke, and you get a lot of them, so a lot of the strategy other roguelikes derive from deciding when to use and when to save power-ups is removed. With enough of the over-powered "Practice Shot +" cards stored up between your runs, it's possible to complete every hole in "1" stroke. It feels like the game started out as a much harder and more interesting challenge, and then that got pared back with feedback and testing until it was impossible not to win somewhere between runs 4 and 8.The game is fun and cute, and has a great soundtrack. It's worthy of a thumbs-up. But you need to genuinely enjoy golf games - the rogue-like elements can't carry it.

_childDocuments_.review: This has got to be one of the best games I've played in a long time! I've always loved golf in real life, and this game takes the aspect of golf and turns it into a strategy, puzzle adventure. It was certainly frustrating when I played a given hole/area for the first time, but when I played it a few times, I got used to it and the challenge became fun. Yes, it is annoying having to go back to the start if I run out of strokes, but after beating each boss and getting their reward, it makes getting back to where I lost easier and more rewarding. The story, world, and characters are fun and creative, taking aspects of actual golf and molding them into fantasy elements. Like the villain being called The Greenskeeper (not a spoiler as he is introduced right away) was clever as Greenskeepers in real golf are often overlooked and can be annoying when they change the pin's location on the green.Only minor, technical complaint is you use a driver on the fairway, which you should never use a driver except on the tee itself (yes, you can use it on fairways, but it is highly frowned upon as it could break the driver's head as it is the most fragile club). _childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever written a steam review before, but this game deserves it so much.This game is an absolute masterpiece. Mixing a rogue-like with 2D golf makes this completely unique.It starts off as a simple 2D golf game until later holes are reached where the focus shifts almost completely to foresight and strategy.Throughout the holes you gain cards in a variety of different ways, each with a unique helpful perk. Knowing which card to use when becomes almost inevitable and at the same time the more you play the more you start having preferences for certain cards which will ultimately define your style of play. And the game rewards this creativity.The story is pretty simple and straight forward yet engaging. The dialogues and little sounds really set the tone for the game's atmosphere and character development throughout, which to me is just the right amount for a game of the genre.It's easy-going compared to other rogue-likes, but on certain moments it becomes an absolute nail-biter and this balance to me was something really enjoyable. Considering a full campaign can take along the lines of 6 hours of play, the game isn't meant to be played in one sitting and that's also very appealing if you're looking for a casual game that you can play for however long or little you want on any given day.I wish I could nitpick something bad about the game, but I honestly can't. I read many steam reviews prior to buying it that said that the game was very hard for beginners. I managed to finish it on my second ever run so if anything I would argue the opposite. The game gets progressively harder for sure, but it levels out with the correct usage of the perks you're given throughout the campaign. I can't stress this enough - there is a HUGE emphasis on strategy at the later holes and you WILL feel this. It becomes SO much more interesting. You'll find yourself scanning the entire hole for almost longer times than you will be taking shots.If I had to mention ONE thing it would be the repeatability. Once you've finished the game there isn't much more to do besides repeating everything all over again with minor changes. I understand that's the whole idea behind rogue-likes and the game does randomise the holes, but adding additional characters, more paths, more hole environments, maybe a co-op even? Still for the price the game is currently priced at, even if you only finish it once and never again, it's more than worth it.Graphics are top notch. The game controls are fantastic. Shooting, perks, ball spin, I never had a moment where I felt like the game BSd me. If I f'd up, it was my fault. The different paths to take available on the levels also have a perfect balance between risk and reward.For me personally, as a lover of goofy golf games like Everybody's Golf, this was an absolute masterpiece. Bravo to everyone involved that made this.

_childDocuments_.review: Score w/o Context: 8.5/10 StrokesThe Context:I'm no good at golf. I'm not sure why golf games have such a hold over me then, when actually playing it makes me frustrated and tired. Is it wish fulfillment? An ability to excel at something I otherwise flail at like I have hot dogs for fingers? A fantasy of extending my mini-golf prowess to greater heights? I'm not sure myself....what was I saying? Oh, right. Cursed to Golf is another good golf game to add to the list.The stinger for Cursed is that it's not a 3D or top down golf sim, but a 2D side scroller roguelike. Gone are the days of 3,4 and 5 par, and all that's left is surviving 18 holes without running out of strokes and being sent back to the start of the course. Sure you might start with 5 strokes, but statues along each course allow for extras to be added. Or, you'll run into a zombie and lose 1. Along the way you are gifted 1-time use power cards usable at any time to help you navigate the sometimes labyrinthian greens, which you'll have to decide if and when they're necessary. These provide the core of the experience, from basic time slowdown to ice and rocket balls. There's always a use for them, thanks to the randomized courses.Each hole is created from a collection of segments smushed together, meaning each run will feel different, and optimization is impossible. Sure, there are a couple permanent powers you can receive that make the full 18 more doable, but for the vast majority you're left to your own devices. Essentially the value you can take out of this is however interested you are in solving these par puzzles. I didn't think the game itself overstayed its welcome, but it also didn't provide much in the way of replayability, which is a shame. When I was knee deep in the game, it provided a compelling tug of war between saving my powers and attempting a risky shot, or using my cards and facing the unknown future with less in my inventory. I just wish there was more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely worth it for the sound track alone in my opinion. I often hear incredible video game music and think, "this is so good, but man I could really evolve the percussion if I had a chance." The drumming in these songs is likely the best I've ever heard in video game music. Listen to, "A For-tuitous Meeting" with a good pair of headphones. Sure, the call and answer of the drums could be extended to focus on four to eight bars instead of two. The hi-hat, kick, and snare could be really mind blowing if they had additional left / right panning, but I've never heard any music that's done that so far... Except for my own ;) The melody takes it to the next level through stereo panning while the drums compliment every aspect of the timing. There is clearly a strong 'Rush' influence in this music, and it's pulled of incredibly well.The game is pretty great too. Most people will probably lose interest after a round or two. For those who stick with it, this game is rewarding. Improving your skill and ability to make difficult choices is the biggest permanent upgrade you'll get. The secret to making permanent progress is that you can actually save the best cards you obtain by accessing the 'Eterni-tee' shop. It would be nice if you could get a full overview / map of the course at the beginning of each area, and didn't have to fast forward through each highlight of the key points each time. Update: As I was writing this review, I had the opportunity to listen to the entire soundtrack of this game. While the rest of the soundtrack is pretty good, none of the other songs come close to the masterpiece known as, "A For-tuitous Meeting." So, unless this game appeals to you, I recommending skipping at, and just listening to that incredible song with quality headphones.

_childDocuments_.review: especially if you're a fan of similar, not-so-serious golf games such as , or much of the  series as I am. My 2nd, and winning, round, took place over nearly 5 short and sweet hours. This conflicts with my playtime due to me playing while offline on a laptop, I now notice, so it's a great, power efficient time killer if you have no internet.I played Cursed to Golf with an Xbox controller, and found it very comfortable. I look forward to replaying this game with the Steam Deck—it seems as though  very well.Pacing was fine for the most part, it appears as though I'm the only one who noticed and adequately used the Fast Forward button throughout the campaign as I read other reviews, but locking such a vital mechanic, the Spin mechanic, behind a lost run seemed disingenuous.This was compounded into an issue with the unforgiving level design at a macro standpoint. Each terrain block in the very first world(I think that's called The Swamp) is, well, . This means when you land too close to one, for the most part, you're just screwed. Take a Wedge shot backwards an inordinate distance, and you  be allowed to use your Driver next time. It's not as though the level designers shy away from rounding out corners in The Desert, where large sections of bunker hazards have diagonal slopes, so I think having sloped out, fairway corners in The Swamp could've reduced some initial frustration.There was also some  throughout the rest of the campaign, where you had about one or two frames to confirm your shot angle, or the entire shot was denied, often ending up in a penalty. I don't mind this being a challenge, but I would've much preferred an Ace Card that allowed you to guarantee these shots(by manually setting your power/angle through pixel-perfect steps, if you needed them) as opposed to , which I hardly ever found a use for.(Ironically, I did find it helpful to undo the insane setbacks in the very last biome, but the last biome doesn't really need more handicaps.) A card like this would likely be balanced by not allowing you to use other mid-shot Ace Cards during its effect.Above all else, though, I would've enjoyed planning shots more if I had any sort of description for what would happen with certain hazards and  description on Ace Cards.  the allure of an electrical status effect on my Golf ball meant absolutely nothing to me, and thus, I never used the Ace Card that electrified your Golf ball. Why would I? Nothing seemed to fit with that interaction.  freezing water, and  burning through vines was straightforward enough in comparison. Instead of throwing text at the issue, perhaps consider video examples of interactions, which replace the card's beautifully illustrated art after hovering over the card for a while.Of course, you could just unlock the Driving Range to all biomes instead of just the first one, which was a bit of a strange design choice to me. The Driving Range in general was a bit lacking in unique hazards though—I hardly ever felt the need to visit it while it was available. It would likely need to dynamically expand as you progress through the game if you are to consider this an alternative. The choice is nice, though.Birdie Eye view features a big crosshair, but it's useless beyond making sure you follow your  while in the mode, I guess. I believe it would make sense to describe hazards in this mode—nothing more than text descriptions. I understand that elemental interactions are dynamic, so instead of explaining the interaction on Ace Cards, you can explain the interaction  through Birdie Eye view. This sort of interaction would also allow you to see  and easily follow Drill bits without squinting for minutesThe rouge-like mechanics didn't really strike me, as I reasonably breezed through most of the game on what  my first real round. I did make extensive use of both available "second chance" abilities, and planned for future runs by banking Ace Cards, but by the end of the cavernous area, I just broke the bank with my newfound safety(The third ability was worded pretty weirdly, but I  I would've been safe?) and had a very powerful Ace Card deck.The economy in general wasn't very engaging, although I understand that it's a tradeoff between scoring terribly, and thus racking up mid-hole bonuses, to get that kind of profit, and scoring efficiently to end up tight on cash. When you're on the left side of this equation, there's little to zero reason to not sweep Eterni-Tee clean of all products—if you don't, the next time you're around, you'll just have a ton of cash and no stock to buy into. Would have been interesting to see your liquid assets mean something by the end of the game, but unfortunately, that doesn't seem to happen.Comparing myself against the leaderboards, though? I placed in the top 1000, and I would consider my round a very mediocre round. I would have loved to see some kind of replay of the current World Record run, which sits at a Hole-In-One in  extremely well beyond what #2 has! Other reviews mention plainly including some sort of Multiplayer mode, and I think an addition of that sort would be well received, but I don't think it should define the identity of this game.This review may seem critical, but at the end of the day, I definitely enjoyed my time golfing in the underworld. It's a fine addition into what I feel is an unsaturated genre, the arcade golf genre, and I can always enjoy a return to this style of gameplay. The story wasn't pedantic to me, although the ending was a bit mute to my actual experience, and the art is as gorgeous as it comes; particularly when combined with the amazing soundtrack  agrees on.This kind of game might simply not appeal to your choices, but it's far more exciting than real Golf. It's certainly less action packed than something like , though. Once again: if you're into the genre, Cursed to Golf is well worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to go with the neutral review, leaning on the side of positive. I actually didn't even realize that this was a roguelike until purchasing, otherwise I probably would have passed. But that's my fault, not the dev's. Despite the fact that rogulikes aren't my favorite genre, I feel like this game is fundamental proof that golf and roguelike don't mix well. The amount of skill you obtain while playing is minimal, and golfing itself is very slow, tedious, and precise. So re-playing the same holes and bosses isn't very fun because you don't really achieve any feeling of mastery on each additional pass. Some holes are incredibly long, and even though the game provides powerup cards, you'll still get stuck with an impossible-to-make shot somewhere. Missing a single shot that requires pixel-perfect precision, especially on a boss stage, can completely tank your run. And you can argue that's just how a roguelike works- but for me the process of replaying these stages has no appeal. I'd love to see the devs take these mechanics and presentation and apply them to a more standard, linear style of golf game.

_childDocuments_.review: (Full disclosure, some of the devs are friends of mine.)I've followed this game from way back when I would see little snippets and concepts being posted on Twitter and loved watching it grow into a full product available for the world to enjoy. The art is amazing, the music bouncy and fun, and the overall presentation is extremely charming (love the Scotsman's big booming laugh). I'm not really one for golf games so no point of reference there but it honestly reminded me a lot of the old Worms games. Precision firing is crucial and it takes a lot of time to really get a feel for just how much range and height different clubs can provide at different levels of power. Courses are rarely going to wind up in a straight line and you'll need to really puzzle out how to go up, down, left, and right in order to finally get that little guy into the whole. It can be quite a challenge and plotting out courses can be fun to work out while using the Birdie Cam to plot a course. Admittedly, sometimes a particular hole can feel impossible without the right Ace Cards (recalling one particular hole in which a wedge shot absolutely would not give me the height I needed and the only cards I had remaining were for adding strokes to my par meter), so forethought is definitely a necessity when playing. Or maybe some sort of Infinite Mulligan difficulty can be added in exchange for not being included on the leaderboard. I'm still in the early stages of play but definitely looking forward to getting into the back nine. The curse compels me!

All time sensitive inputs are done with the mouse so for most of the time I only need to be using one arm to play. The visuals are easy on the eyes with a lovely spread of colours and cute, smooth, impactful animation. The sound and music help create a great atmosphere as you progress on each hole.Each time I interact with the game there’s this level of polish and charm that can’t help but make my day just a little bit brighter.If you’re looking for a tough as nails roguelite to consume you I don’t think this game is for you.If you’re looking for a game oozing with charm, polish, and character, then this is the game for you. I don’t even like golf, but the way the whole package comes together makes me enjoy every thwack of the character’s club hitting the ball.

_childDocuments_.review: Cursed to Golf mixes Roguelike, Dungeon Crawler, and a Golf game. There is also a Deckbuilding aspect to this game too. The cards take some time to get used to. It feels, unlike any other golf game I have ever played, but in a great way. This game is not easy, and it takes time to learn what to do.  The game is easyish until you get into a curse dungeon that rotates curses, and then you need to do a set number of shots before the curse goes away. Curse dungeons are worth doing, though. The boss was also not easy. You can not make too many mistakes in the boss fight, or you will lose. It is vital to master the spin move. You can go to the firing range if you want to test ace cards or practice hitting the ball. You can get there by going to the right at Etern-Tee. The firing range can be used during a round if you go to the shop in the first area. I recommend buying everything you can from the shop when there too.When in a course, watch out for obstacles and hazards; some can be a pain in the rear. Also, keep an eye on your par count; if you get to 1, you must use an ace card or try to get a statue. It is not always worth going for the statue. Do not trust that you will hit a statue even if it is red; if it is too far up, it could say you will hit it, but you do not. I lose a round because of this. It is sometimes better to skip them. It is also important to pick the right club for what you want to do. I recommend planning out your shots at the start of the course. Zooming out on the map helps the most.Overall, this game is super enjoyable and challenging. It makes you think, and the puns are great.Find more reviews from me on my Steam curator page:Here is the YouTube video of my first impressions of the game:

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept. The premise of the game is trying to escape golfing hell. To do this you must complete 18 holes while getting a par in every hole. There are ways to help you achieve that such as giving you extra shots and cards that have varies effects such as stopping time or changing the direction of the ball in mid-air. I've only played a couple hours, and only made it to the second area, so I'm sure there is more to unlock, but that's the general idea. Win holes to get more cards at the shops that appear ever so often to help in your current round. There are tougher cursed holes and boss holes to provide extra challenge and usually come as a trade off for some extra cards or cash. Overall its pretty simple with not a lot (if any) meta progression which I would really like in these kinds of games because frankly I lack the skill to not have some sort of system making me better.I don't know how much of this game I'll play, but I say its worth giving it a shot and its a game I'm sure I'll come visit every now and then

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I've played many roguelikes, and many with crazy concepts, but this is probably the most unique one by far, and that's a super good thing.Everything in the game from the witty dialogue, to the stunning soundtrack, and especially the UI just oozes with passion and charm. With every second I play this game, I appreciate more and more the amount of love and care the creators put into making something they really loved. Things like the cute remixes of the main character's themes in the shop, and the diagonal slants on the camera angles after finishing a hole, and especially the character animations make everything so much fun, despite being in purgatory lol.The gameplay itself is surprisingly difficult at first, but it quickly grew on me, as I started making it further and further into each run. With the permanent upgrades you unlock after each boss, the game went from living off of Par Cards in order to have a chance at winning to being able to beat most holes while being able to rely only on shot idols.As for problems, I only really have one active issue with the game, and a few suggestions-As of right now, the game can be incredibly buggy at times, resulting in sometimes having to take shots underwater, spawning in walls, or having the game just softlock altogether during bossfights (along with minor visual glitches, like edges of text looping back around the the other edge of the image.. The first two can be negated using the Mulligan ace card, but the softlocks can be pretty annoying. To be fair though, as of writing, the game literally only came out 4 days ago, so I can't really complain that much, and I never really feel frustrated if I get a softlock or glitch, I can get by with just thinking "oop, that's not supposed to happen."-the map can sometimes feel a bit empty, I think the game could definetely use some more map events, such as a trading kind of thing, or maybe some temporary upgrades that only last for that run.-I think it'd be cool if upon landing the golf ball in the hole there was a bit more flair, since right now there's the polite applause and that's pretty much itOverall though, other than the bugs and small nitpicks, the game overall is an absolute BLAST to play. It's a really fun roguelike, a fun amount of difficulty, and has charm and passion at every corner. Amazing game!
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY wanted to like this game, and there really is a lot to like about it. My biggest gripe with Cursed to Golf is the pacing of the game. I found that there was a tremendous amount of downtime, waiting for animations, driving from hole to hole, etc. that made things far less fun for me. Because I felt like a lot of time was just spent "waiting", the game felt less responsive and more boring, so ultimately I'm recommending against it as this somewhat ruined the experience for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game! My main quibble is not being able to see where you're hitting the ball when you're lining up your shot. I'd like the ability to either zoom our or scroll a bit more to see where my drive or iron shot is going to land at least. My other issue is I feel like the game is a little content light at the moment. In roguelike games I like a reason to replay it, whether that's unlocking higher difficulty levels, unlocking new skins or anything like that. I feel like relatively small additions such as an ascension mode which adds extra modifiers, extra modifiers in general, daily challenges (beat X hole and you start with X cards), the ability to practice individual holes and go for a high score could go a long way toward enhancing the replay-ability which is so crucial to making the best roguelike games so great. As is, I beat the game on my second run and I probably won't play much more in the near future, but I look forward to potential updates down the line and definitely still recommend the game as is!
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: In the first time I was in a boss fight in this game, I'm pretty sure I felt EVERY POSSIBLE EMOTION as I tried to figure out every possibility and trick to get through and win. It was exhilarating, and I really had to think of every possibility in the chaos that was the boss fight. And in the end, by doing so, I ended up winning.That's a mark of a great game as far as I'm concerned.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: Quite honestly, lots of fun and a bizarre concept that works. The mechanics definitely take some getting used to, but once you've got the hang of it, you can pull off some hilarious trick shots. The graphics just click in the right way. Somehow the retro pixel style works with the concept that you're trapped in purgatory. And the music? The music absolutely SLAPS. In a golf game. Why is the music so damn good in a GOLF GAME?I've seen tons of reviews talking about how hard it is to get through certain holes, or that you absolutely need certain cards to clear them. Three pieces of helpful advice I'd like to offer prospective buyers and anyone playing the demo:1. Don't skip the tutorials. There's more to the game than you'd think. Especially not the one about Spin.2. You need to know how to Spin to Win.3. Quite a few Ace cards can be used to mess with the course in ways you wouldn't expect.Keep this stuff in mind and you'll likely have a good time if this is your thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first 18 hole run so I feel like I have enough experience to talk about this now. Cursed to Golf is incredibly unique, charming, challenging, and flawed all in one. While I think the difficulty might be a positive for some, it will alienate players that may otherwise enjoy the great roguelike. Pros:-Golf Roguelike (nuff said)-Awesome art and music-Fun level design that requires both imagination and skill to achieve the best outcome-Card powerups rule but could be more descriptive-Great replay value – In 10hrs I have yet to get the same hole twiceCons:-Too hard especially starting out-Runs take way too long to justify the difficulty-While imagination is key, perma-death makes you play it safe-Hit boxes are not precise enough (I’m looking at you spikes)-Checkpoint mechanic in the last few holes is beyond frustrating and not interesting or funFeedback:I think as it stands, the current game should be an entirely different mode (maybe call it the Golf Gauntlet). I would prefer saves after each world/boss to allow anyone to make it through the main story an experience the game while saving the super precise, flawless play to the people wanting an extra challenge. The game is far too difficult for 4hr+ runs to result in permadeath because the spike had a scuffed hitbox or you couldn’t make one hyper difficult shot after playing flawlessly. I would also love to see a more fleshed out practice mode that lets you freely attempt any hole you’ve already played so you can really practice mechanics or experiment with card interactions. Being confined to experimenting on the fly feels more punishing than rewarding. TLDR: Keep the core elements that make it fun but increase the accessibility/respect the average player’s time.Recommendation: This could easily be a universal recommendation with a couple of tweaks, but in its current state, I think the target audience is much more niche. If you plan to buy this game, expect long runs that might result in restarting hours in, expect the need to master mechanics and think outside the box (no easy mode), and keep trying.P.S. I also want to point out that there is the ability to save scum any hole by backing out to the title screen before you lose, so even you can be a Golf Legend!
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: Great twist on the rogue-like nature appearing in games this generation. Fun mechanics and special shots. Love the addition  of fast forward from the demo. One of my only complaints, though, is that the game doesn't save your settings between plays. I have to reduce the master volume and music *everytime* I start the game. I had hoped this was just an issue with the beta/demo, but nope. Here were are in 2022, and the game won't save my audio settings between boots.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: The game features a lot of depth using simple mechanics. That's the golden goal of game design, there's not much more I can say about it. If you think you may like the game, I am sure you will, it's great. The animations are detailed and cute and the sound design is great, the songs are a banger. The beginning was a tad too slow imho but the speed-up button helped.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: My grandpa took me golfing on a boiling hot summer day many years ago.It was a day like any other. I couldn't compete with him because of his decades of golf experience but I tried my best and he helped me improve my skills while we played.I still golf to this day and I cherish the memories of the time well spent with my grandpa.Thanks for giving me an opportunity to reflect on the recent passing of my grandpa.He continued golfing until he was no longer able to do so and I like to think that he's taking up the hobby again in Heaven. Not through some kind of otherworldly curse, but by choice, for the love of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Its one of those titles that no one asked for (a roguelike golf game lmao) but works super well. Gorgeous pixel art, killer soundtrack, and fun-to-play mechanics such as a trading card system that gives the player advantages, mulligans, turn your ball into a rocket etc. Lovable characters with spooky designs, and the need to GiT gUd, to conquer the courses. If you can snag it on sale, do so, but it is worth 20 bucks if youre super interested. The only thing its missing is PVP, it has potentially to be an absolutely lit party game with friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: In short, it's a fun arcade-golf game with a ton of charm and challenge. Music is an absolute vibe that matches games like Mario Tennis/Golf/Kart. The dialogue and aesthetic triggers nostalgia, but also feels fresh. The actual gameplay is deep, requiring a lot of complex decision making hole-by-hole as well as course-by-course.My only complaint is that this game lacks a lot of "guidance" that would help the player succeed without taking away the challenge. There's a bit of a somewhat lengthy tutorial at the beginning that gives you the basics, but I found myself often not knowing what key bindings were used for specific actions on the course and off it, causing me to make mistakes for simply not knowing the keybind and using the wrong keybind in the moment.If I could improve the game in any way, I would add more keybinding hints to the UI for things like card activation and choosing a path with the golf cart.Overall, highly recommended. If you're into indie games, I would call this a must-play for 2022, hands down. It'll just be a little frustrating to learn at the very beginning.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like real golf, infuriating and yet somehow consistently fun.This is a perfect game for a couple hour gaming session (less time if you're me, but you know, if you're good at the game the round will last longer). There's something about this game that brings me back to being a kid playing games on the old Sega Genesis. It might be the music, it might be the adorable animations and pixel art, or it might be the fact that it feels like a fun video game-y concept without being overly violent or serious. (Not that I'm against violent games, my avatar is from Killing Floor 2 for goodness sake.) It's a breath of fresh air to play a game this polished and intent on making sure the player is smiling and having fun even while hitting their golf ball into the water trap for 4th time in a friggin row. Conclusion? Buy it! Especially if you have a Steam Deck and want something relaxing to play when you have a spare moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Cursed to Golf is a game where you can absolutely feel the passion coming from the team with every choice they make. name: NeverAwake
detailed_description: A girl who never wakes up. She has been fighting monsters in her dreams... 'NeverAwake' is a nightmarish twin-stick shooter with a unique worldview and original game rules. The girl fights against vegetables, dogs, school friends, and other things she hates. What does the girl see at the end of the battle? And will she be able to wake up? About NeverAwake 'NeverAwake' has a unique worldview with its high quality hand-drawn graphics and beautiful animations. The enemies are not demons...but vegetables and dentists that the girl hates. Things and creatures that everyone has had a bad experience with at one time or another become monsters and attack the protagonist 'Rem'. With over 80 levels, dozens of bosses, and a unique gameplay system that allows players to retry many levels, NeverAwake is suitable for both beginner shooters and experts. Combine a multitude of weapons and accessories to fight off the monsters in your nightmares. The ending of this title will change depending on the player's dedication. Please play and see what the girl sees at the end of the battle. Features Kick the veggies, dentists, and other monsters out of the way and blow away the painful memories of your childhood! A unique world view set in the 'inside of a girl's nightmare' Beautiful hand-drawn graphics and animations Unique game rules and high retryability Fast-paced gameplay and powerful boss battles More than 80 levels and dozens of tricky bosses Numerous weapons and accessories, and builds that combine them Great storytelling and multiple endings

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely incredible. I've played almost all of the best games in the "shmup" genre and this one comes pretty close to the top of my list. This game has extremely unique theming and art and it has some of the best enemy pattern and boss design I've ever seen. It also has quite a lot more content than I was expecting.The soul gathering system may seem a little bizarre, especially for bosses. You can basically skip the second half of every boss if you collect all of the soul items they release. I'm still not entirely sure what the reasoning behind this mechanic is but it gives the player a lot of choice in how they play the game. For example, if a player finds a boss to be too easy, instead of trying to finish the boss as quickly as possible they can try to endure as many loops as they can (when you kill a boss without reaching the soul goal, instead of winning, you fight a harder version of the boss) and then cash out when they feel they can't survive any longer. I think this system gives the game a lot of replayability since you can always try to get further into a boss or stage.The equipment system also gives the player a lot of play style options. The game can be made much easier or harder depending on how you choose to use the equipment. Equipping an item that gives you more max health and an item that allows you to regenerate health under certain conditions can make the game feel much more forgiving. A more confident player might forgo extra health and take equipment that improves their dash, increases damage, etc. The equipment system along with the soul system make this game both accessible to beginners and exciting for veterans. I highly recommend it to anyone at all interested in this genre!Edit: The looping system is fun but it really feels like it's missing one important feature: the ability to start from any loop that has been reached. The looped versions of bosses can be very fun to fight but it is not so fun having to fight the early loops of a boss every time you want to attempt a later loop since that can take quite a long time. Giving the player the ability to start from any loop they have reached on each individual level would give the game nearly unlimited replayability since you could work you way up through the loops for each level. In my opinion this feature would perfect this masterpiece of a game. I don't know if the devs have a feature like this planned but I can only hope. I know they still have some features they plan on adding (like online leaderboards) so there's still a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Just popping in here to recommend the heck out of NeverAwake.This is Neotro's latest game. You might remember VRITRA, their previous effort, which was really quite good. This shmup is even better. Rather than go for the typical 5-8 stages of arcade action, NeverAwake has 70+ stages to shoot through. What's interesting is that all of these stages loop indefinitely, with each loop featuring more enemy bullets and higher scoring potential. Now bear in mind that unlike most "survival" games, your score is not recorded if you die. The only way to progress & achieve high scores is to collect 100% souls. Souls drop from most enemies, so depending on your skill-level & playstyle, you can either rush to collect souls, or push your limits to get a great score.In any case, you must be aware of the importance of special weapons. There are a multitude of them to purchase and equip, and they can function as a shotgun, rebounding bullets, or homing lasers. Experiment to find the right special weapon for each stage. Accessories are also important part of your kit, as they can increase your shields, give you more ammo, and add numerous other powers. There's a lot of customization to work with here, allowing players to find a build that works for them. Bear in mind however that aside from the special weapon, all you have to work with is your maneuverability and your main cannon. To put it another way, managing resources is just as important as dodging bullets. If you waste your ammo, it'll spell disaster for you down the line. Accessory slots are also limited. Consider this an opportunity to choose accessories that play to your strengths or cover for your weaknesses.One other very important ability is the dash. There will be multiple instances where an attack simply can't be weaved in-between. This is where the dash comes into play. The player-character is invincible while dashing, but there is some recovery time. It's a powerful move...when used properly. Otherwise, the key to surviving strenuous bullet-spreads is to "lead" them away from yourself. Never settle for merely reacting to what the enemy throws at you. If you don't take the initiative, you'll be overwhelmed and wiped out, especially on the higher loops.Throughout the game, there are several bosses to face. These dastardly and visually intriguing foes have a wide array of attacks. Much like any regular stage, you can focus on gathering souls to end the fight quickly or destroy the boss repeatedly to boost your score. Naturally, successive loops result in bosses that are more aggressive and toss bullets with greater frequency. It's on you the player to manage your special weapon and soul count to achieve a satisfactory score. The last thing you'll want is to destroy a boss multiple times a row, without ever bothering to pick up a single soul. The level of difficulty makes a very significant jump after eight loops, so you don't want to be caught without a means to finish the stage quickly.Like numerous other classic 2D shooters, NeverAwake rewards players who memorize enemy patterns and develop routes. The scoring system mostly relies on surviving multiple loops in a row, and there aren't any convoluted subsystems to account for. Despite the voluminous number of (looping!) stages, the game never feels repetitive or slow. On average, a single stage can take about a minute to complete, provided that you're rushing for 100% souls. In that minute, you'll face not only a solid variety of enemies, but you're also bound to fly into creative problems that require creative solutions. Some stages can involve block pushing or using objects as a shield from deadly lasers. This variety never comes off as gimmicky or takes away from the rest of the game. There's never a point where you'll think "Oh no! It's the block-pushing stage! I absolutely loathe it." Everything comes together wonderfully, adding to the game's identity and appeal.I'd also like to add that the visuals and atmosphere is flat-out superb. There are seven worlds and they're all quite distinct from one another. Each world has their own unique enemies, as well as the aforementioned "creative problems". You'll witness (and destroy) all sorts of nightmarish fiends. The bosses are especially creative and well-realized. There simply is not a weak fight in the game. Also, the boss-battles end quickly enough that fighting them over several loops in a row never becomes frustrating or tiresome. The pacing is absolutely a large part of what keeps this game so engaging. The average play-through can take upwards of four hours, and many more if you're shooting for high-scores and all of the optional content. For a shmup, this could be considered a fairly sizable amount of time. Nevertheless, you always have a goal to strive for, and you're always entertained. Altogether, NeverAwake is one of the strongest entries the shmup genre has seen in quite some time. Its structure and method of progression is unlike most anything else out there, and yet it all works wonderfully. Neotro knew exactly what they wanted to do here and delivered an astounding game. It's a twin-stick shooter that doesn't just require good reflexes, it teaches you the essentials of resource management and positioning. The level of depth on display here is really impressive. It's sure to keep novices and experts glued to their controllers.So yeah. I recommend the heck out of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting take on the loop mechanic commonly seen in arcade STG / SHMUP!The game is basically as hard as you want to make it. So it should prove appealing as much to hardcore players as to casual ones.That being said, base difficulty is surprisingly not that low : expect some serious struggle toward the end of the game.However to compensate, the game regularly unlock equipments based not just on progress but also total numbers of death. So you can still improve no matter how many times you fail (SO NEVAH GIVE UP!!).Special mention to the mesmerizing art direction, and the amazing soundtrack!
_childDocuments_.name: NeverAwake

_childDocuments_.review: NeverAwake is one of the most charming twin-stick shooters available on Steam.The game is an audiovisual tour de force, featuring a Gothic style that almost makes it seem like it was designed by Tim Burton, and an awesome soundtrack that wouldn't be out of place in Plaid's discography.It's a fun, accessible title, with 80+ stages, a steady stream of power-up unlocks (which should help anyone struggling with the difficulty of certain stages, but it also means there's quite a variety of different loadout combinations possible, so veterans will have plenty of ways to maximize their scores), and unusually for the genre, an engaging storyline, even featuring multiple endings.In short, NeverAwake is a worthy addition to the library of anyone who enjoys the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: NeverAwake

_childDocuments_.review: A good twin stick shooter at this price is pretty much an insta-buy from me, as it was here.  I'm getting older and my reflexes are very much dulling, but I'm sill reasonably handy at a SHMUP.  So your experience with the difficulty level may not be the same as mine.But for me this game has such a finely tuned, and enjoyable, difficulty level that seems way more interested in me having fun than beating me over the head until I give up.  Almost like the devs want me to see and experience the entire game. and have a great time along the way  Totally refreshing!I'm up to world 6 and have completed the challenges on the first 2 worlds so there is still quite a bit to do.  But I couldn't carry on without trying to spread the word about how good this game is in pretty much every way.The weapon and accessory swapping is just great at adding depth and making sure constant changes in strategy are rewarded.   The graphics are truly spot on with easy to read bullets and some great patterns.  The levels have great variety in obstacles.  The bosses are never a pain, inventive, plentiful, and gorgeous to look at.  The story is interesting enough but never gets in the way of the action and the music is funky and fits the game nicely.Honestly, if you have any interest in the genre, or curiosity about it, just buy it.  Well done devs this is great work!

_childDocuments_.review: Having a lot of fun with this. A shooter with a remarkable art style and the level/enemies/bosses design is unique. You play through a whole bunch of levels that you clear by gathering a certain amount 'souls' that drop from enemies. The levels are short and loop around, but each loop the levels get progressively harder (so you typically don't want to wait around). There's a lot of upgrades to unlock as you play through the game, and additional challenges to do.If you're on the fence, there's a demo available.
_childDocuments_.name: NeverAwake

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really fun indie shoot 'em up game! If you like classics like Contra and Gradius & Parodius, or even the more recent Cuphead, you'll like this game! You play through stages, fight bosses, and find out the truth about the protagonist, Rem. The story is mostly given through notes you read as you beat or lose in stages and it's genuinely a emotional plot which I won't spoil. You collect currency as you beat stages and as you either win or lose in stages you unlock new passive abilities to buy and use. My favorite part of the game is the bosses, they're very well done! For the most part most of the game is well-designed, a few sections are a tad hard but most of the game has a fair difficulty such that anyone can beat the game - even I'm not the best at shoot 'em ups but this game was fine for me to beat. The only stage I disliked was the one with drawers? that kept popping in and out, it was very troublesome.And the great thing is that this game will observe if you're losing a lot and will give you specific hints for the stages/boss you're on, and if you keep losing you'll unlock the ability to buy more power-ups to help you out, so someone who struggles more early can buy upgrades earlier, but if you didn't die as much you might unlock them later. The game purposely puts hard enemies and sometimes it's better not to disturb really aggressive enemies.The game has optional stages and you only have to beat one of two of certain stages to progress, so if one stage is too hard then you can skip it and still get to the credits. The final boss was hard but fair and I felt very accomplished after I finished the game and there's good payoff for finishing the game. After you beat the game there's optional challenges in the previous stages you can complete to unlock more content. Overall a very fun indie game, it has great artwork for both the protagonist and enemies, and the bosses are amazing. Definitely one of my favorite shoot 'em ups!
_childDocuments_.name: NeverAwake

Amazing audio, fun level design, and looping anything was incredibly satisfying. Only issue is that I feel it's not easy to tell where your character's hitbox is, but I also have this problem with most flying person shmups so it might just be me.
