_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this masterpiece! Never left a review for a game before, but this was just soo good. It is incredible, just about everything in the game is top tier imoThe story (without spoiling anything): The story seems simple the earth is destroyed and it needs to be fixed. Sure thats the main objective but there are so many nooks and cranies to find out more about the EC itself, the people that work there, and some EC pets. It adds depth to the world, as well as humor at some points. And the twist that this game provides is bone chilling and done 100% right!The visuals: The game looks amazing, it is absolutely mesmerizing but at the same time its also terrifying at points. (like the state of the planet slowly falling apart as the game goes on. And the ending is absolutely jaw dropping!Puzzles and Game Mechanics: The puzzles utilizes all the elements that are shown to its highest potential. I myself got stumped a few parts. _childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre is a time- and mind-bending love letter to the Portal franchise with a unique compelling story alongside great mechanics and puzzles to guide you through it. While exploring the centre, players gradually piece together the story by examining fragments from the past before culminating in a wonderful climax. The moods it sets along the way with the soundtrack and visuals are stunning and make for some great atmospheres (or lack thereof :>) to solve puzzles by. There's just something about being stumped at a puzzle while seeing the earth burst into a planetory inferno in the corner of your screen.The game isn’t perfect, some animations are a bit odd, there’s a few places you can softlock and there are enough undecorated places you're not supposed to be able to reach that you can find scattered across the game, but all of those imperfections are made up for by the overall polished experience.Ultimately, I would definitely recommend this game. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Portal started something special 15 years ago and The Entropy Centre continues its legacy in its own way. It is a good puzzle game that borrows a few ideas and executes them well. The core element of rewinding objects through time has a decent learning curve and suitably harder challenges near the end. Detours through backrooms, and the external lush biome, serve as energizing breaks between the puzzle chambers. And the lively AI companion, ASTRA, helps to make saving the world a bit less lonely. Although it could have used a trim and polish, there is still eight hours of solid entertainment here. It is definitely worth playing The Entropy Centre, if you get time.

_childDocuments_.review: A melancholic Portal with a dose of optimism. The Entropy Centre is a game very much in the vein of Portal. It's a first person puzzle solving game featuring a female protagonist who uses a fancy gun to solve puzzles. However, unlike Portal, The Entropy Centre messes with time instead of space, Further, your character"s interactions with the world are not done in silence. Aria (the protagonist) has a personality of her own and will offer commentary on what is going on. This is done in conjunction with an AI (Astra) that lives in the time gun. The interactions between Aria, Astra, and E (an lovable entropy bot) are more whimsical and optimistic than the witty cynicism of Portal. This optimism contrasts with the the dire situation that the game places you in. This juxtaposition ultimately enhances the bittersweet feeling achieved by the end of the game. Gameplay wise, this is all the standard Portal fare of using blocks and your time gun to solve puzzles and generate entropy energy that can be used to solve the problem Aria finds herself in. Many of these puzzles are fairly easy to figure out. However, puzzle elements (block types) increase over time and there were a few of the later puzzles that really forced me to think hard in four dimensions. Graphically, the game is beautiful. The sparse areas are covered in specularity and realtime reflections on top of the ray tracing. The game hitched and crashed on me only once, and there were a handful of times where I would find myself stuck between some crates, or accidentally near the edge of the world, but these were all rare moments that never hurt the experience.Game length is on par with Portal 2 if not a bit longer. There were moments towards the end where I thought I was about to finish the game only to suddenly find myself in a new set of circumstances that tacked on another hour or two of play time. The game doesn't overstay its welcome, but it does get close. Not that I'm going to knock the title for giving me extra play time. The autosave feature ensures that if you find yourself getting too overwhelmed or bored, you can stop wherever and return to nearly where you left off. Overall, if you enjoyed Valve's Portal series and would like to experience a time-shifting version of it, The Entropy Centre is well worth a buy even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Was really stoked for this game when I watched the trailers for it, and while it did deliver on visuals and had a neat story premise, the main aspect of the game (the time reversal mechanic) got old really fast. Let me spoil the solution of like 97% of the puzzles for you: You put the box in a position where it needs to be for the final step of the puzzle, reset the box's entropy to zero, bring the box over to do whatever you need to do to get to the aforementioned final step, then reverse the box to the point you reset it and finish the puzzle. Sure new box types and devices are introduced while playing and their are some neat solutions related to them, but overall they all fall into the same sort of end pattern. I don't even think this would bother me that much except for the fact that you have wait so long each time for the boxes to reverse their entropy. The first few times you do it, you're like "woah cool I can see the path I took with the box in reverse!" but when you already figured out how to solve the puzzle and it takes a whole damn minute to get the end because you have to watch the box go from point A to point B, you just want to be done and move on.As for story, it's a cool concept, but if you read a good chunk of the computer emails you already kind of figure out where it's going and the ending happens exactly the way you think it will. I found the ending to be kind of depressing too as it seems kind of hopeless, which on its own isn't a bad thing, but if you're looking to be treated to some kind of big victory or revelation for completing the game, you're going to be disappointed.Overall, shouldn't be your first pick if you're scrounging for more puzzle games to play.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:. The game takes very heavy inspiration from the Portal series and innovates on its concepts and mechanics, the story futures a similar idea. Gameplay follows a similar formula but throws some new staff into the mix to keep thinks fresh. Simply if you enjoyed Portal you will like this one.The game equips you whit a gun named “The Entropy device” witch allows moving objects back in time 30 seconds. The mechanic sounds a bit scary at first but the game starts up very simple and introduces the mechanic very slowly and gradually scales the difficulty very well, So Evan me a person witch is not good at puzzle games had very good time solving puzzles. The game also introduces new mechanics very regularly to keep the game fresh and uses them very creatively. In addition, you can also rewind some parts of the environment which is not only used for traversal but also to solve some puzzles. To differentiate itself from other games. The game introduces halfway through combat section versus “The Entropy bots” a quite simple enemy witch functions more like word building then a serious threat. They also future in some puzzles but they do not get in your way, you can kill them very easily and don’t respawn outside of combat stages. The dedicated combat rooms which have a bit more to be desired of and In my option where more annoying then fun, the combat isn’t that flashed for fighting more bots at the same time. the game also struggles a bit whit momentum and physics puzzles. they font feel consistent at best and doesn’t work at worst. Overall, the gameplay it’s fun whit couple of rough edges but uses its main mechanics to the full potential.The story is similar in concept to Portal but branches out in an interesting direction. You wake up in abandoned Entropy center you play as Aria Adams a puzzle operative whose job is to generate “Entropy Energy” by solving puzzles. the “Entropy Energy” is used to rewind the earth in case of a cataclysmic event on earth. She acquires the “The Entropy device” which has a AI assistant build in named Astra she cracks jokes and helps Aria navigate the abandoned Entropy center.The game nails the abandoned sterile aesthetic, The overgrown center looks remarkeble and becomes more destroyed as the game goes on. And the word files real like someone really worked there you get taken to the employ commendation rooms, stores, and recreational areas. The game really shines when you get outside. The music also ties the environment together most of the soundtrack are environmental sounds and make the word fell more alive than it already is.As mentioned in the paragraph above the graphics are beautiful that unfortunately take a big toll on your hardware. There are a ton of particles and Unreal engine 4 effect but if you have a 2–3-year-old PC you will be able to run the game on HD high swimmingly.All achievements the game has are quite simple no challenging staff most of them are resaved just by playing the story. At minimum for casual players are 2 playthrough required, but if you are willing to read the achievements before and search every corner of all rooms to get the only collectible and couple of collection achievements you can get them in one playthroughThanks for reading.gest2356

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre is a first-person puzzle game where you are tasked to  reverse! Solve complex puzzles with your trusty AI gun ASTRA and manipulate objects in this time-bending adventure to find the truth behind The Entropy Centre and save Earth...if you can. I couldn't help but compare this to Portal 2 a bit, but I wouldn't say it is a negative statement here. I felt a similar joy playing this and I enjoyed the visuals and witty dialog I encountered throughout my time. I can say, without a doubt, it was definitely worth the experience. But now we have to take a look on how it really runs on the Steam Deck!Since the demo, The Entropy Centre has come a long way and definitely gotten significantly better in terms of optimization, but it is not perfect. At max settings, depending on the area, you will get a range of 30-50 FPS with battery drain around 22W - 25W. This fluctuated even more when moving around, so max settings definitely isn't the way to go, at least not like this!Thankfully, with how much more optimized The Entropy Centre is now, I was able to easily get 3 different builds focusing on different aspects. This one was harder for me to choose which I preferred, but the battery focus will be my favorite as it still feels really smooth, looks great, and lasts a bit longer than the others. For the recommended build, I kept all settings on high except for Shadows and Effect quality, a 1152x720 resolution and FSR Sharpness 1, and resolution scale of 70%, I was able to keep battery drain under 14W most of the time, with the average being around 12.5W for 3+ hours of battery life.I then proceeded to create a build that would keep almost all settings on ultra with a 100% resolution scale. This was achievable with a 40 FPS cap, shadow quality on high, and TDP limit of 11. While the TDP could be pushed higher and could maybe increase framerate to 50, there were too many times the game dropped framerate noticeably and 40 just felt way more comfortable.From there, I decided to create a 60 FPS build as well, but it does require some compromises. With this build, you will get around the same battery drain as the quality, but everything will need to be lowered a bit. The compromises aren't so bad in the grand scheme, and it is harder to separate on the smaller screen, but it can be noticeable in certain places regarding high concentrations of shadows.Regardless of whichever build I chose, there were always certain sections that stuttered a little. This mainly occurred when entering new areas, though running around semi-outside areas that have collapsing architecture tended to slow things down a bit too. These only lasted 5 seconds at most and then went back to normal, but they did still happen and wouldn't completely go away. Otherwise, I didn't have much issue keeping stable framerates!The Entropy Centre was one of the demos I tried for NEXT last month and loved the premise and visual presentation, so it brings me great pleasure to say it has only gotten better! In the demo, hitting 40 felt like a stretch, but being able to hit 50 and 60 so easily and stable while staying under 20W drain is an accomplishment. Overall, the pros heavily outweigh the cons and I am happy to recommend adding this one to your libraries!

_childDocuments_.review: The style is very much like portal, but with a different approach.Difficulty is in the lower middle, almost every puzzles are solved by using reverse-thinking, slightly monotonous.Plot and graphics are enjoyable, cute character designs, but I personally don't like this kind of ending, of course unless there is a sequel of it, let's hope they can count to 2,3 and more unlike valve!Almost no translation error, that's definitely a plus.If you are a portal fan, this is a game that you cannot miss out, despite it's not as good as the portal series(which is really on top of the celling), hopefully it will still ease some of your emotions waiting for portal 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay-wise, this is of course inspired by Portal and has many extremely similar elements. There are enough new ideas to keep things fresh and interesting, but don't expect some revolutionary take on the Portal formula. If you loved Portal and want more of it, you'll likely enjoy this game. I found it extremely well-balanced difficulty-wise, and there are plenty of those wonderful "OH I GET IT NOW" moments. There's plenty of content to keep things interesting too, and I feel like the game didn't overstay its welcome and become a slog towards the end either.My issues with the game really come down to the story. Some of those issues I would argue are objective flaws, and those are covered without spoilers; my more opinionated take requires a discussion of particular plot points so that one is marked as spoilers below.Non-spoiler version: There is no subtlety or nuance to the game's message. That by itself isn't really an issue, but the story doesn't really have anything new or particularly interesting to add to the topic. Credit where it's due: the story is (imo) well-written in terms of pacing and delivery, and good at getting you emotionally invested, and the reveals aren't so obvious as to be boring. I just wish the writers had tried to say something more instead of just rehashing an old theme - however well that rehashing was done.My issues with the story aren't enough for me to recommend against the game, but imo this definitely isn't the kind of game you pick up for the narrative. It's merely serviceable as a setting for the gameplay, nothing more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, but has its flaws. It's too much, I wouldn't say even Portal 1, because even there half of the game was applying what we learned in puzzle rooms outside of them, and here, it's all puzzle rooms. Not counting small sections at the start/end of the chapters, it's all puzzle rooms. Instead of "learn, learn, learn, apply what you learned to traverse enviroment in an organic way", it's "puzzle x4, traverse one room/outside area, puzzle x4, traverse..." and so on for 15 chapters. Don't get me wrong, the game is fine, but around chapter 10 it becomes tedious, even though each chapter has new puzzle elements.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I thought this would be a Portal clone. It is true that there are lots of elements that are similar, and Portal fans will definitely enjoy this, However, this game has its own soul and quickly distinguished itself. This game has excellent storytelling as well as pacing. Puzzles are difficult, but the spacing of the most difficult puzzles is enough to give your brain time to rest. In addition, the story portions and set pieces are spectacular. I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Good, but missing a lot of the polish of something like Portal. (I know, smaller team, but still.) A lot of the puzzles rely on precise jumping, but the jumping pads are very inconsistent and you can't even quicksave. The worst puzzle took me less than a minute to solve and more than  to actually execute the  required to complete it...The puzzles are overall not too difficult, but they are interesting and there are a few really satisfying ones. _childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: A good game but not a great one.Main characters are likable but not particularly deep.The puzzles take a long time to get interesting but there are some pretty good ones. Nowhere near the difficulty or utilization of mechanics as something like Talos Principle or Portal, but not bad.The environment design is pretty enough and has a nice feel, but immersion suffers due to overuse of the same assets, and a context that makes suspension of disbelief a little flimsy.Collectible documents range from good world building to insultingly pointless. Some also try way too hard to be 'cute', and it kind of takes away from the weight of the story.The overarching story itself is incredibly predictable but not uninteresting.  Overall, I wish this game had introduced its mechanics faster, and not been afraid to mix them earlier on. Probably 60% of the puzzles consist of; see the steps required, perform them in reverse then play them back. Especially in the early acts, there are several back to back puzzles that are functionally identical.Still very impressive for a small team, and a worthwhile puzzle game. (Still so much better than Qube 2 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥)
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre is as close as we can expect to a portal 3 until Valve decides to give me what I want. This game HEAVILY draws from the portal games in mechanics but in direct cube for rather than a device you need to redirect due to the lack of a redirection device. These cubes include a basic cube, bridge cube, laser cube, and jump cube. The mechanics of a repulsion bean are also replicated using fans. The game does innovate through its inclusion of a large breakdown cube, transport belts, as well as cube alteration fields. For the most part this game plays very similarly to the Portal games which I would say is an incredible feat.Some could say this is purely derivative but I say that the additional human element by having our player character Aria be able to speak really does give the game additional character and heart. Rather than feeling for the other characters you really get to feel for who you play as. Aria and Astra's dynamic is also incredibly enjoyable and touching.This game was genuinely very enjoyable and I would say anyone who enjoyed the portal games and mods (Especially Portal: Revolution) should check this one out.Hope to see more from these developers soon :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy Portal, you'll enjoy The Entropy Centre. It's clear inspiration comes from Portal, but with different mechanics. Great story telling, lovable characters and pretty good visuals. Got 7 hours of playtime out of the main story, got this in a collection, so kinda for free. My only real critique is that the mechanics don't seem consistent all of the time. Sometimes you repair something and it stays there, other times it breaks after you have fixed it, seemed a bit random. Other than that, great game. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed this game, and it's more than just a spiritual successor to the Portal games. It has its own unique style, so instead of portals, you have the ability to rewind time with object placements. Until Gabe makes Portal 3, this is the closest as we're gonna get. _childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I've barely played this, but let me tell you how my initial experience went:1. I walk through an abandoned facility, very reminiscent of Portal but with terminal entries to find. All good so far.2. I find that some old-looking rubble is blocking my path. The corridor probably collapsed ages ago, but at the very least it must have been before I was within hearing range as I wandered through these easily-echoing halls. I would imagine it was around the same time that the ceiling began to crack and the plants began to grow.3. I enter a room with a sealed-off chamber, hit a button to unseal the chamber, and wait patiently for 10-20 seconds as a mounted gun does something sciencey4. I enter the unsealed chamber and press a button on the mount, whereby the gun lights up and talks for 20-30 seconds, introducing itself before explaining that it can rewind an object up to 38 seconds into its past.5. I then walk out of the chamber, walk out of the room and rewind the rubble that was blocking my path, until it reforms itself as a structurally sound section of corridor.Can you tell where something went wrong?I get that the "38 second limit" explanation was a lore-friendly way to excuse Unity engine's limitations when it comes to tracking past positions of objects I mess with, but the game has contradicted itself less than 15 minutes in. I'll probably take another crack at it later since I admire mindbending puzzle games like Portal/Antichamber/Superliminal, but it sure gave a weak first impression

_childDocuments_.review: Being a devoted enthusiast of entropy and puzzle games, delving into this one was a must for me.The puzzles themselves are decent. Each new area introduces a fresh set of mechanics, with the difficulty steadily escalating through the total five levels.The narrative revolves around the concept of loops, omnipresent and interwoven. _childDocuments_.review: kind of a "meh" recommendation.  the story is interesting enough and there is nothing wrong per se except for it evokes portal and it's nowhere near as fun or well-made.  lots of cube puzzles but no real head scratchers.  only difficulty comes from awkward placing and then having to start over mid-puzzle.  definitely worth picking up on sale but it won't blow your mind
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this?  Well yeeess... kinda.  I mean, it's a decent game.  VERY thinly veiled clone of the Portal games - enough so that one would think the lawyers must be getting excited and breathless, but the one unique aspect here is, sadly, also literally the only mechanic - you can (for a limited duration, and on a limited and not-very-logical selection of objects) rewind time.  That's pretty much it.  OK, there's a couple of other interactive items lifted straight from Portal, too, but a lot less variety than you'll find there.  Still, if you liked Portal, you'll probably like this.  Voice acting and story are a bit trite and silly, but that's 95% of games, so no news there, and that's not what you're playing this for anyway, right?  The puzzles are not bad; not too hard, mostly not too easy, though a few are of the annoying "easy to figure out, hard to implement" variety thanks to slightly jittery tracking of motion in the rewind, or the frustratingly fiddly placement of jumping plates.  But the very limited set of mechanics means that they also get repetitive pretty quickly.  So, decent game built around the time-rewind mechanic, but I found myself getting bored with it by the fourth level of puzzles, and nothing much changes after that either.  If you want a much more engaging set of puzzles, try The Talos Principle (which also has a time-rewind mechanic, but a LOT more besides) or The Witness - now there is another game with just the one simple mechanic, but which manages to remain challenging, interesting and compelling right the way through.  So I'd recommend this somewhat on its own merits, but I more strongly recommend you spend your coin on other two instead!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This entry has absolutely deserved a spot in the enjoyable Portal-formular game list.i love the  that is scattered throughout with bits of information, some of which are hidden away. it keeps you guessing how excatly this place works (or worked) and what the purpose of it all is. its clever, good written and served with a neat little twist at the end. are never to hard nor to easy imo. the mechanics work well together and are easy to grasp.also,  is one of the most important tools to consider in a game, and i think The Entropy Centre hits the spot between mystery and tension. 3/5 top
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason I recommend this is because there are so few of these games. This game has a lot of flaws. It has unique mechanics and a set of puzzles that I had to work through and I think everything else mostly harmed that focus. The visuals are good, until you recognize how "the bridge is broken, you cant go this way" the whole map is. Portal kept you in puzzle rooms and mostly obscure factory settings, which aided their vision. In Entropy Center human environments have catwalks to nowhere. Immersion is always broken as you are always in human environments. Entropy center has a very serious plot and the whiplash you experience with the environment is bad. This is a world where somehow we can reverse entropy, yet the entire facility was built by morons. It gets worse with the humor. Unfortunately this use of incompetence as humor just conflicts with the serious tone of the story even more. In portal the various AI are goofy and lack human understanding at times, but they were top of the line within their world. The employee emails you can find are ALL incompetence humor. Throughout the entire game there is essentially no standout example that anyone ever knew what they were doing. This is the "simple jack" of puzzle game stories. You can contrast genius with incompetence, but not the other way around. I am okay with the humor, but would prefer more wit. The last thing is the puzzles. The puzzles have some jank. The jump blocks move after you bounce sometimes. The jump pads sometime shoot you to your death. I am not confident I solved all the puzzles the way they were intended. A bit frustrating, but you ultimately learn the flaws and can play with them. I think the puzzle feel could have been ironed out with less focus on the story and unnecessary environment detail. The combat should not exist, it just feels bad to throw the explosives.I really liked the serious parts of this game. Towards the end I was really hoping for the remnant timelines to be more impactful on the story, but it didn't. I hope there are more puzzle games in the future. BUT, keep it simple and commit to a tone!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine the decrease in suicide rates if guns game standard with Emotional Support functions.Anyway this is visually impressive and very creative sleeper indie title that takes some ques from Portal but in the end manages to still feel like its own thing. The time manipulation puzzle system is very neat and with the level editor released it will be very interesting to see the limits of the concept tested by some of the more big brain members of this game's community.If you like unconventional puzzle solving or puzzle solving in general this game might be for you. I would suggest if you're on the fence and not already leaning towards getting it, to wait for sale even though I think the asking price is reasonable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre: Time-Bending Puzzles That’ll Twist Your Brain in the Best Way ⏳🧠If you've ever wanted to break the laws of physics and twist time to your will, The Entropy Centre is here to let you do exactly that... while giving your brain the workout of a lifetime! 💡💥This mind-bending first-person adventure isn’t just about solving puzzles—it’s about rewinding time like a puzzle-solving wizard. That’s right, instead of just pushing buttons or pulling levers, you’re rewinding objects through time to outsmart the impossible. It's like you’re the Doctor, but with way more boxes and slightly fewer Daleks. 🕰️🔧Each puzzle is a little slice of genius, and the game really keeps you on your toes. The feeling of solving a seemingly unsolvable puzzle? Absolutely chef’s kiss perfection. 🤌 But it doesn’t just stop at clever mechanics—The Entropy Centre has a stellar narrative that hooks you in just as much as the puzzles do. You’ll be solving time loops while unraveling a story that’s equally as intricate. 🎮📖The puzzles are delightfully tricky but never feel unfair. You’ll spend a few minutes scratching your head, then suddenly feel like a genius when that one object clicks into place. And trust me, when it does? Oh, it’s like a mental mic drop. 🎤🧠If you love puzzle games that challenge your mind, get ready to fall in love with The Entropy Centre. It’s a thought-provoking adventure with plenty of twists, turns, and timey-wimey fun to keep you hooked. Just be prepared to think in reverse... literally. ⏳🔄Created with <3

_childDocuments_.review: If i were to describe this in brief terms it'd be Asda value portals.Don't take that as a negative as this is still delicious...like all Asda value goods.This game is a puzzle platformer with a very interesting story and theme that i really did enjoy for the most part. The game play itself is rewarding and intuitive though I would say that the movement physics could use a bit more polish.If I were to pick holes I would say that the game outstays its welcome towards the end and kinda loses momentum and coherency going for a rather undefined bioshock infinite ending which would have been fine if it had been laid out a bit better.Overall i cannot fault this game aside from the fact that i would happily put this one back in the oven with a far bigger budget if given the option.7/10- Make a better tommorrow

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre is a Portal inspired puzzle adventure that wears its inspiration on its sleeve  - from the intro to the many different puzzle elements introduced throughout the game and even the tragicomic tone that permeates the story. And honestly, that's not a bad thing. I love Portal.Unfortunately, however, I can only just... like TEC. While the story is definitely where the game shines the most, it's time rewinding gimmick which is central to solving the game's puzzles. definitely starts to feel a bit annoying by mid-game, when you find out for the umpteenth time you missed something or mistimed a final jump or something else and realize you have to end up repeating everything again.Nonetheless, it's a decent game and one I can recommend if you're looking for a Portal-like experience without wanting to revisit GLaDOS again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: A crazy good portal-like puzzle game. The puzzles are varied and challenging, and the plot and characters are very entertaining. Game took me around 8 hours to complete. _childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Portal, you will definitely love this. Hmm, that was a bit cheesy and overused. *rewind review*It's a puzzle game with time rewinding powers. _childDocuments_.review: First part of the game is ok, you work your way through the puzzles at your own pace and stuff. _childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: edit after 2 more hours: it does not get better. I tried, dont bother. I feel bad for all of the environment/asset artists that make this game shine visually when the gameplay designers refused to make a decent game out of all that care and love. its such a shame really.This game is aggressively mediocre. the graphisk and lore is well presented but the voiced protagonist is stupid and poorly acted [always sounds childishly stupid and fails to put together things the audience has with the same amnt of information], as well as the puzzles being very poor. all of the puzzles are extremely simple but rely on the most painfully tedious method to 'solve' them. this is the kind of 'solve' where you know exactly what to do and the entire time you are just fighting the needlessly obtuse mechanics to complete them. the most challenging part of the game is figuring out where you need to hover a box for 10 seconds before you sit and watch it float around the room. the only margin for error is doing things in the wrong order, or worse rewinding 1 nanosecond too long so you have to do everything over again. its just so un fun and lame. theres never the wheres-waldo style pause other similar games give you. you never have to sit and analyze the room to figure out the solution. its just painting by numbers and the annoying mc and nonsensical environment design leave a lot to be desired. I cant even really recommend you get it on sale- play portal if you havent, if you have play cube. if you have played both then join me in suffering land as we accept that games like this will never be as good as the things that have come before them.ps: the physics in this game are ASS and SO MANY puzzles rely on them. the bounce pads have a 50/50 chance to flip themselves over or cancel all momentum when you use them. what the ♥♥♥♥ is the point? if you are going to rip off pretty much every tertiary mechanic from portal (cube/button based testing, hard light bridges, bounce pads, laser cubes, emancipation grids... seriously, all taken wholesale from portal) at least have the decency to do it well, for the love of god. anyone rating this game positively is so dazzled by the eyecandy that they fail to see how poorly this game measures up to its contemporaries- or they just never played them. portal came out in 2007 and this fails to come anywhere close to that in its puzzles. portal 2 came out in 2011 and similarly fails to match up to the environmental story telling and characters that game brought to the table. its just the worst game in its own genre and it deserves 100% of this criticism by ripping those games off so blatantly. do not buy for any amount of money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: While imperfect, this is the best first-person puzzle game I've played since The Talos Principle (I have not yet played TP2, I expect that to be better). It has some frustrations. I do not like combat in puzzle games, the precision platforming you have to do at times first-person games aren't really made for it, and most significantly the puzzles start very easy and keep on being very easy for a number of chapters, BUT they do eventually hit a nice level, I think. If this is fine with you, I recommend the game. Oh, and it has a pretty interesting story too (I don't really play puzzle games for story).
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Is the game heavily inspired by a certain popular puzzle game? YesIs this game designed and published by Valve? NoShould you be reading any reviews or watching any videos before beating this gem of a game? Absolutely notIt's obvious by playing through this game that it is lovingly made by a very passionate team. The concept of entropy is fascinating and the way this game displays it is remarkable. _childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game that has strong roots in the benchmarks for the genre. A gun with magical, sci-fi powers is par for the course, but this game is highly original and is very fun. The puzzles are unique, interesting, and combine challenge with player confidence. It is difficult to strike a balance of challenge and reward, but perhaps that means I have perfectly average problem solving ability. I found the puzzles to be quite balanced, not too challenging but just enough to keep me engaged. 0604 took me about 3 minutes, for reference. I also see some room for non-deterministic solutions, which is excellent.I am shocked by how smooth and well implemented all the features are. I am used to objects getting stuck on terrain or especially in doors when carried around, and I experienced very little of that. I am amazed that all of this dynamic collision works as well as it does. It is clear how hard the devs worked on this game.The game is filled with cute humor and lots of interesting secrets. Beans rooms, hats, etc. I saw many cats, likely owned by the devs, which is a nice self-aware touch. I also like cats.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Great little puzzle game. While I think the forced combat and chase sections were a bit unneeded. The visuals and characters won me back though. Astra is one of the most underrated companions of the past few years. Yes it's very portal-esque and while I can see the comments around the puzzle design being a little simple once you have trained your brain to work on entropy logic, I felt it introduced enough variables to keep it fresh.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good, but flawed. I recommend it to anyone who enjoys puzzles, but not if you are peeved by any of the following:-The game's puzzle mechanics are well utilized, but some puzzles can be quite tedious with the rewind mechanic. You do a lot of dragging things around, and standing around while you wait for them to rewind.-The game's story is fine, but has some nagging inconsistencies which I don't wanna delve into for spoiler reasons. In particular, the dialogue could have definitely been kept to a minimum. (This is less an issue with the game, and more with me preferring silent protagonists)-The game is severely unoptimized. I had very frequent frame drops, even at low settings down to 30fps when physics objects were moving, and environments were being destroyed. Maybe that's in part to my 6-7 year old computer with a 1660ti and i7-8700 in it, but a certain other game that has influenced this one managed to do physics in a similar manner without tanking my frame rate, so idk.-The game takes about 7-10 hours to finish, which I may have liked to be shorter, since I felt like it was kinda padding for time. I kinda wanted it to be wrapped up around the 6 hour mark. More than ever, I'm appreciating games that are short and sweet.All in all, I'd give it a 6/10. Wait for a sale if you're really intrigued.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I want to give this game a proper review to do it justice, but it's a bit tricky. Although there are a few similarities with Portal (which the other reviews will probably also tell you), I wouldn't call it a rip-off, clone, or competitor. The game stands on its own as a good and enjoyable experience, despite a few minor bugs. However, it's not as polished as Portal, as there are some glitches in the physics and hitboxes that can occasionally disrupt immersion and make levels easier than intended.Regarding the content, I think it's pretty solid. The characters are likable, and while the enemies are not particularly challenging, they add urgency and speed to the gameplay. (Where they are applicable) They're also cute, which makes it emotionally more difficult to fight them, but you can avoid killing them if you choose. (for the most part) It makes the game a bit more challenging. The story is decent, although it's a bit spoiled by the game's tendency to give away the outcome of the story. It doesn't exactly ruin the experience but it wouldn't exactly be my approach to game-story design. But hell what do I know? I'm not a writer nor a game dev so take that with a grain of salt. Is it worth the price? If you're a fan of puzzle games and don't mind a few flaws, it's definitely worth considering. Recently, the developers added a custom-level editor that adds more value to the game, making the price more reasonable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game in all honestly i wasn't super into the story until i figured out what truly was going on i got way more invested all the puzzles were well made and scratched that itch portal had left behind one flaw though is the battle portions where you would just rewind an orb to destroy the object which felt a bit bad? idk overalla must play for portal fans for sure
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle solving game. A deep story. All around an enjoyable experience.Best played blind. And really do try not to look up a walk-through.Puzzles by their very nature, are boring. You sit and look at the screen, thinking. That's something most people haven't done in decades, since they got a smart phone. But by making something unique, or just different in any capacity, puzzle games can be fun. Just look at Portal 1 and 2. Take away the portals, and it's just a run of the mill boring puzzle game. The same goes for this game. It just has a different unique element. (And a cool story like Portal has.)Similar to the Portal series, but no good puzzle game isn't.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun Portal-like. It's not quite as mindbending as a game like Antichamber, and it doesn't have the same level of comedy as Portal, but the comedic beats are there, and the companion is adorable. Think "Portals" with slightly easier puzzles and a bit more serious narrative. Definitely worth a play!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good story for a puzzle game. Around the second hour I wasn't really enjoying the puzzles, most of them had exactly the same solution, and I almost refunded the game, but I wanted to give it a chance just because the story. And I'm glad that I did because right after the puzzle quality went up and never down again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid puzzle game. Took me about 10 hours to clear. Very strong Portal vibes where you have a secretive benevolent(?) corporation, a mysterious need to solve puzzles, and an AI that you aren't sure you can trust. The main puzzle theme is a time rewinding gun, which I usually dislike time travel in puzzle games, but it's fun here. You can rewind items for up to 35 seconds of memory, but you can also suspend them in air, or drop them and watch them fall to the ground. These modifications to the time rewinding make it fun to try and get clever and break the game.Overall it felt like a quality game to me. Good visuals, good voicing, good atmosphere and lore. And it feels like a full story game. The last few levels get pretty unhinged and I think I solved most of the last 2 acts without even using half the puzzle elements. That was really fun trying to cheat the game, or maybe that was how it was supposed to be solved? Either way, it felt naughty and I liked it.They did add a custom level editor, but there isn't anything substantial there. Just not enough people making maps and not enough people playing/reviewing them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I am done, I can't take it anymore. The Entropy Centre is a never ending chore. Felt like I was a test subject.This game is a good example how you should NOT design your game. The developers haven't heard anything about such a thing as narrative pacing. They say at the beginning of the story you have to get to the reactor. GOOD LUCK, EVEN AFTER 10 HOURS YOU WON'T GET TO THE REACTOR. And when you finally reach that damn reactor there are more puzzles you need to solve, the end is not even near.You need to run to survive and everything around you is blowing up? Solve puzzles.You need to get rid of your enemies? Solve puzzles.You need to open a door to start a next puzzle? Solve puzzles.You need to learn more lore? Solve puzzles.You need to solve puzzles? Solve puzzles.Horrible pace, horrible.If only the puzzles were interesting. Almost all of them are solved by rewinding from the end to the beginning. And the damn jumping cubes. You miss by just an inch when jumping from a height, and you have to do the whole solution all over again.The amount of puzzles is absurd.Update: I finished the game anyway, I was a little emotional earlier. The game is generally fine, but I won’t change the negative rating. The game has a disgusting slow pace and the number of puzzles is absolutely absurd. By the way the achievement for completing the second act is broken.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay like Portal with the graphics aesthetic of Control. Game is fantastic but sometimes drags a bit. If you ever get stuck on a puzzle then you might be over thinking things. Some others experienced bugs but I didn't.Here's my review in an even smaller nutshell: If the end of the game had suddenly burst out that it was Portal 3 I wouldn't have been surprised.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game never fails to fill you with emotions. The main aspect of the game, puzzles, aren't extremely hard, but usually require you to think for some time. Some of them actually challenging enough to make you happy about finding the solution. From time to time they can even deceive you into thinking that you have found your own unique way to solve them. 8/10Regarding the story, it's breathtaking, and the storytelling is outstanding. Voice acting is great, environmental storytelling is awesome, READING NOTES IS ENTERTAINING!!! You really can tell how much love and dedication author put into that gem of puzzle videogames. 10/10Pleasant graphics and level design. Though, sometimes you can tell that this isn't an AAAA game. 8/10Overall, this game is a wonderful experience you shouldn't miss. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: A fun puzzle game! The comparisons to Portal cannot be avoided, but it tries to differentiate itself with its game mechanics and story.I recommend the game, but it did only take me 10 hours to beat. I'm not disappointed with my purchase (10% off at release), but if you are hesitant definitely wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This is an easy game to recommend. I like the FPS puzzle genre and played probably most of them that were worth something. As the genre goes, this one is pretty good.The game is about 6 hours long (though I got stuck on one puzzle for maybe 20 minutes). Overall the story is there - it's kind of the same story as always. Whatever. Music is competent, sounds are memorable.The structure is also the usual: do room puzzle, quips happen, you are in the next room, every now and then plot moves a bit, rinse and repeat. I don't mind the formula though, I am here for the puzzles.The little problem I have with this game is that even if you figure out the solution step by step it still takes time to actually execute it. Luckily some care was taken to make sure you don't miss your jumps and there is quite a lot of leeway. It would be perfect if I could rewind the game a bit as well so I would not have to replay levels when I accidentally fall somewhere I did not want to. Also, the combat seemed unnecessary.The puzzles themselves are a bit easy - and I say that after I have played a ton of similar games so I am probably pretty biased. For a newcomer to the genre I think the difficulty is pretty all right. It won't make you frustrated by being too hard. The game is very competently signposted so you don't get lost or lose track of what you were doing.Ultimately I feel like there is a lot more potential - there are plenty of mechanics in the game so I would love to see a DLC that would showcase some harder levels. Perhaps the level editor will fill the steam workshop with interesting content.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I think Portal was my first of these sort of puzzle games and I have played of number of them since (e.g. Q,U,B.E) and enjoyed all, but none seemed to come up to the quality and style of Portal and Portal 2. Entropy comes fairly close. The idea is good and the execution is great, in particular the interaction between Aria and Astra. The puzzles are interesting and the challenge level is probably about right for the story part of the game, considering that there are tougher ones available after completion. I was fortunate enough to get this game for free and otherwise I'd only have bought it in a sale (I only buy in a sale), but I see that it is £16.75 and I played for 17 hours (without the custom levels) so I'm going to suggest it is good value for money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Portal without being portal :DIt has wonderful level design, a good story and it's own "personality".I was kinda skeptical when I saw clichés like a puzzle gun or a companion that quips with the MC, but they made it work.It's one of those games that charm you and make you bummed out about finishing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I am astounded that this game was made by one developer.  I'm going to get my nitpicks out of the way so I can get to the positives.Can't crouch, can't stand on cubes, no manual saves, enemy homing projectiles sometimes go through terrain.Okay now onto the positives, this is probably the only game where I used motion blur and it works very well, challenging puzzles that stumped me, it makes puzzle solving part of the story,  I had fun, YEET. 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, I enjoyed it a lot, but there are parts that I really wish had been better crafted.First, the puzzle. Without giving away too much hints, I feel like the puzzles have about the same difficulty level for the entire game, save maybe for a few ones. I also found some levels to be cheesable, not sure if those were intended (like Portal's time trial solutions), but there are quite a number of instances where you can access out of bound areas, which led me to believe that those cheeses are design oversights.Second, the story. I really got intrigued by the plot, the build up towards the end was so good, however the climax was a bit underwhelming for me. I was hoping to see a grander ending, I really thought the idea has so much potential.None of that is a major concern though, would definitely rewind myself back in time and play it again if I could :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre is a clear love letter to Portal that unfortunately has too many annoyances to be enjoyable.I found the Portal-inspired storyline, humor, and level design to be great. However, I quickly became frustrated with the game as I got further and further into it.The lack of an in-game manual save is a major annoyance. The game only saves at arbitrary checkpoints you can't control. If, for example, you played through the beginning of an action scene but failed the final jump, chances are you'll have to replay the whole scene from the very beginning.The same goes for the puzzle solving. Due to the nature of the gameplay, you usually fully set up every test element with the solution in mind, and then execute the planned sequence of events. If you fail to execute correctly, you'll have to set up every element again, since you can't save after initial setup. And this means manually moving each element on the level in the same exact way as before, which is boring since you already figured out the solution in your head.And you will fail to execute, since some parts of the gameplay are extremely finicky. One of those is the conveyor belt, which sometimes makes physics go haywire and launches your boxes all across the map. Another is the jump pad, which you will often miss because there's no course-correction like in Portal, and other times it will just decide not to preserve your momentum. These faults are completely out of your control and you will most likely have to replay the puzzle from the beginning when they occur, which is extremely frustrating.The action/fighting scenes I also found to be quite boring. They help spice up the pacing a little, but they also suffer from gameplay issues. Enemy projectiles can sometimes travel through obstacles, and then you don't have enough time to react to them. On levels with rich foliage, you can sometimes just not notice the enemy until it's too late.Overall, I really feel like there is a solid foundation for a good puzzle game, but the gameplay issues and frustrations make me unable to recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Portal clone with some new twists good story/lore, totally worth it if you love the genre.The Entropy Centre is heavily inspired by Portal and it's very similar in a lot of aspects aspects, but it manages to bring something fresh through new puzzle mechanisms. I found the first series of puzzles to be quite simple and a bit repetitive, but there's a point where the difficulty ramps up a bit and it gets much more gratifying to solve one.The story is not mind-blowing, but it's still dramatic and interesting. It's well balanced by the humor of the AI living inside your time gun. Also, if you take to time to explore just a little bit, you'll stumble on computers with secondary lore that contributes to the atmosphere in a nice way.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Very similar to Portal except no portals! Instead you get a time gun that can turn back time for objects you aim it at. It's all a question of thinking backwards. Starts off very easy and ends up a little more taxing.  It's all pretty easy, and there are unintended solutions. There are one or two puzzles where you are chased, so you have limited time, and others where there are enemies in the same puzzle so it's difficult to concentrate! Mostly, though, there is no time limit to complete each puzzle. All together a well executed game but what really stands out is the story, not the puzzles. If you liked Portal and want more, then this is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: When i bought the game people described it as "Portal 3", and this was a major part of me buying it.It is GREAT! Like Portal, but no portal mechanics to speak of, obviously, just time manipulation.Challenging, great story, worth the $25. Obviously if you are hesitate to buy, wait for it to be on sale for $15-20 would be a steal. My *only* complaint would be that with time manipulation being only 1 direction (no fast forward with the gun), there are places you can get physically stuck at (and cant kill yourself) and you have to return to the main menu, then reload your save to restart a puzzle. I would like a menu option to restart a puzzle without doing that. That being my only complaint should say alot about the game itself.10/10 Enjoyed 100% would love an extended version or modded puzzles in the future :) Thanks for the great game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lot like portal, only the "gun" you wield, the core mechanic of the game, rather than portals, is time travel. You "shoot" objects to reverse them through time. So say you need to put a cube on button 1 to travel through door 1, then you need to put the same cube on button 2 to travel through door 2, you put it on button 2 first, then move it to button 1, then go through door 1, reverse the cube through time so it moves itself to button 2, and go through door 2. Totally not confusing, right?There are multiple types of cubes. Cubes that shoot lasers to activate stuff, sorta like portal has the laser redirect cubes. Cubes that make light bridges, like portal has the light bridges built into the stage. Cubes that make you go boing, and cubes that lift up and down. You basically have to mentally solve the entire level in advance, then do everything backwards with the cubes, starting from the end, and putting them in reverse through all the spots they need to be in, then finally place them in their starting position, then you use the cube to do A, shoot the cube for a bit, use the cube to do B, shoot the cube for a bit, use the cube to do C, and finish the level. Except, you know, with like three cubes at once all doing different things.Also they managed to make solving puzzles be about literally saving the entire planet, and have it make sense and be believable in a really neat way.TLDR: If you liked portal, and especially portal 2, you'll like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: You know, when you create a game based on puzzles, the hardest thing to do should not be dealing with the ♥♥♥♥ physics you're asking for after having already figured out the answer. The amount of times I had to redo some nonsense ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ setup because I barely missed some jump due to your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of the jump height or some ♥♥♥♥ like that is beyond stupid.This was my initial negative review and the point still stands. But if you can get past the frustrating physics bs, there is a good game with a neat atmosphere and good story with sadly pretty unfulfilling ending. given the lack of good puzzle games, this will get a recommend after all. I wanted to continue but sometimes the game just made it very hard to enjoy it (e.g. having the answer and physics shenanigans failing your execution).
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a pretty good puzzle game, on the shorter end of the spectrum. I beat the game in 3 days over 7 hours. The puzzles had good difficulty ramping and all provided a unique use case of the provided puzzle elements. The story is also decent and provides a good setting for the game. No user made levels at this time, but if they do add that, it would be a very welcome addition.------ Edit -----User levels have been added, great game
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I like a portal-like as much as the next guy. Entroy Centre, while not as good as portal, still manages to bring some charm into its unique puzzle concept. That said, there were definitely moments where the pacing felt sandbagged by the loop of puzzles required to complete in order to advance. I get it, it's hard to create a unique story that supports puzzle rooms, but I definitely felt less and less connected to the story as the gameplay dragged on. I will say the pace of puzzle element introduction was well done; each "act" features a different mechanic, and you will spend 5ish puzzles playing with that mechanic. So that at least helped with the monotony. I'd say get this on sale (I got it from a humble bundle, so I think it was worth the ~$3 that it ended up costing), but don't be afraid to put it down if you start to get bored.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Good Portal-like, it even does without the more annoying parts of puzzles where you have to find the right pixel to click: here you have all the elements from the beginning and it's really about figuring out what part goes where and when.The story moments that arrive late enough are worth the long puzzle solving marathon that is the first half of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw this game pop up on steam I was really excited, a portal-esque game using time travel? I'm all in. I eventually picked it up in a bundle for essentially £2.50 which is an absolute steal. It's almost like Portal but with more focus on the story, though I did enjoy the puzzles that are here. The game lasts 3-5 hours depending on your puzzle skill or more if you go for the achievements.The gameplay here is very similar to Portal, you wake up, make your way through puzzle rooms as you progress your way through the story. The game has a lot of puzzle objects similar too: Cubes, Lasers, Gates, Jump pads but because of the nature of the time-travel aspect of the game you have to think about puzzles backwards in a different way to what you typically do with other puzzle games.As for the puzzle design itself, it's good, but it's not flawless, I found myself stuck on multiple puzzles and finding silly ways to throw cubes that are definitely not the intended solution. I had an absolute blast with the jump pads which can be used mid-air, any puzzle involving jump pads has some way of skipping 1 or all of the steps which was honestly just really fun to do more than anything.The game also includes an In-game level editor and level browser to play user-created levels, this gives basically infinite replayability whether you enjoy creating or playing maps, the editor feels like a game engine with a complete free-build setup.I really like the world-building of this game and the story they told and I think the way puzzle-solving fits into the story makes sense, however, even though you know how the game is going to end way before it does, I wish you were able to prevent what happens.I think there's a lot to explore in this world and would love to see more to this story and would absolutely buy a sequel for that alone. If not, this games' ending works perfectly in isolation.Most of the achievements are straightforward for playing through the campaign but there are a few like the collectable messages that are significantly easier with a guide.The only comment I want to make on the music is that there were a lot of chase/intense areas where there was a threat like rising water or robots chasing you where the music was just not intense at all, other than that the sound design in the game is great.3 save slots. Chapter select, unlocked after beating main game. In-game level editor and level browser - Level editor is completely free-build. Rebindable keyboard controls, gamepad supported. 13 languages supported, only English supported for audio.Fun Portal-esque time-manipulation puzzle game. Solve puzzles in reverse. A lot of the puzzles are easy to cheese by skipping sections. Interesting world and story. Level editor/browser included. Achievements are easier with guide.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best puzzle games that I have ever played. It reminds me at games as Portal and Q.U.B.E. The special gun you use could bring objects back in time. For example you need to run away from something, but the building is collapsing. So you need to use the gun to repair the building on time while you are running away. The game also has a fighting system. Until now the fights are pretty easy, but maybe that could be more intense further in the game.So yes, I really could recommend this game. It is polished, the (many) puzzles are great and there is also some action included.Here is some gameplay from me:

_childDocuments_.review: Truly great puzzle design. The kind that have you walking away feeling just a smidge cocky and never calling BS.It's not Portal, but it's maybe the best attempt at being a replacement so far. _childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre is a charming and funny game. While it at times reminds me of Portal, it definitely brings its own style of humor to the table.The puzzles stay rather simple for a while, and at first that worried me, but now I realize that the purpose of those simple levels is to acclimatize the player to the rather counter-intuitive approach to puzzle solving that the Entropy Centre asks of you. Fear not, the Entropy Centre *does* get more difficult later on, but it never becomes unapproachable. Never did I encounter a puzzle that made me confused as to where to even start. Solving the more challenging puzzles is very satisfying, and several mechanics are introduced throughout to spice things up.In terms of story, without spoilers, the Entropy Centre is intriguing and mind-bending at the best of times, and a bit silly at the worst. It's lowest points are never very low, and it's highest points had me shouting to my friend (who I was in a discord call with at the time). Rest assured, the ending of the Entropy Centre is well worth the journey (and its fun and charming writing style will keep you entertained along the way).There's only two real characters in the Entropy Centre, but they're both handled quite well. While the character you play as is a little shallow and generic feeling at first, she does get fleshed out later on. Your companion, meanwhile, starts off a little quirky and cold feeling, but she will quickly draw you in and make you invested in her.If you do decide to play the game, I encourage you to search out the optional readables. Some of them are hidden behind optional challenges, which can be quite fun to solve on their own, but the readables really add to the mystery and buildup of the story, and can make some revelations even more impactful. You don't need to exhaustively find every single one, but even just a few could make the whole experience stronger.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: After 8.7 hours of gameplay, I've finally finished The Entropy Center. A spiritual successor to the Portal series, The Entropy Center aims to give us that Portal 3 experience we so deeply desire. Not only does The Entropy Center fill my "Companion cube shaped hole", it does so much more, truly making it a game of its own. I'm astounded that it was put together by such a small team, and I look forwards to future releases from Stubby Games.  This game is one of the best I have ever player, competing with the likes of Portal 2 on my list of favorites. The Entropy Center builds on the mind bending puzzles of Portal, creates a realistic and believable atmosphere, and has an intricate story that truly makes you feel like part of another world.I've mentioned Portal too many times already in this review, but this game is NOT Portal, its a game that does the same thing with a different core mechanic. The Entropy Center swaps your portal gun for an entropy gun, completely changing the concept. The game does however, use many of the same concepts elsewhere, like with the cube, laser (thermal discouragement beams), and bridge cubes. These cubes all employ mechanics seen in Portal, but rather than using portals to change their locations, you must put them in their locations first then rewind them back to where you need them. This concept allows for many new kinds of puzzles where you bring one cube and then the other, or where you use two cubes together to bring them both over a gap, the game may take from Portal, but it also builds on the mechanics. The Entropy Center doesn't just learn from Portal, it also adds its own content with things like the tall cube. This is an example of entirely new concept that melds with the time rewinding mechanic of your gun, the tall cube doesn't have its position rewound, rather its sate, going from large to small. The tall cube isn't the only new idea, there are fans, conveyor belts, and transformers that are all completely original and innovative ideas, bringing the game away from being 'Portal 3', and closer to being 'The Entropy Center'. Although there is a clear inspiration behind The Entropy Center, it truly is a game on its own, not just a Portal replica.The Entropy Center successfully creates an interesting an believable atmosphere. The game knows what it is and how it does it. There are only a few titles within the video game industry that excel at keeping the player's disbelief at bay, my favorites being Bioshock and Metro Exodus, like those, nothing feels out of place in The Entropy Center. The are explanations behind everything, the computers containing lore-emails are all in offices (or whats left of them), the break rooms between puzzles, even the puzzles themselves have a purpose (something I struggle to find in the Portal series, "testing" what kind of excuse is that). The game doesn't just focus on what the puzzles are for, but also life outside of the puzzles, with the lore emails, and relaxation areas. Showing life outside of puzzle solving fleshes out the game's atmosphere and makes the player feel like they are in a functioning environment. A functioning environment tells a story, and answers many of the players questions about the world, creating a more realistic feel. The Entropy Center gives every object a purpose and creates a believable environment that I enjoyed exploring.The narrative in this game is controversial, though it moves incredibly slowly, it manages to keep the player somewhat captivates throughout the entire game. I was always looking for that next computer, searching for the next bit of lore I could find to flesh out the story all while solving puzzles. This captivation shows how good this game is at keeping the player enthralled in its story. The game doesn't have all that many story beats, I found this to be the biggest downside. The player has to keep looking for that next bit of hidden story to keep them engaged. If you aren't one to look around and would rather focus on gameplay, The Entropy Center might become a bit repetitive for you. This game is lacking in narrative beats considering its duration, but it you're willing to look, the game will keep you engaged start to end.Overall I found The Entropy Center to be one of the most enjoyable video games I have ever played. It's definitely on my favorites list. A must play for any Portal fan, or any video game fan for that matter.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Portal with more action. There's light bridges, companion cubes and Lasers. Had fun trying to figure out puzzles in reverse. Dialogues are not Portal level funny tho. Story is gripping from the startJust finished it, the last few puzzles are extremely hard, loved the story. 9/10 because I got exhausted. and there are bugs, cubes disappear when pushed against a wall which was really frustating
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect game, worthy of being a Portal succesor. Main benefits:- Storytelling in different forms is constantly present so there are frequent breaks from puzzle solving- Puzzle elements have excellent introductions- There are environmental puzzles, and designed puzzle rooms and sometimes they are joined together- Voice acting, music, visuals- Almost no platforming/having to time things (and if we need some time or space precision there is usually a lot of room for error)- Puzzles are quite short and easy, and yet still very satisfyingMain downside: Jump pad is way too small. I have anxiety when I have to jump on it. I wasted way too much time than necessary having to start over only because I did not hit teeny-tiny jumppad collider.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie I'd say this is simple math: If you like Portal, buy it. If you don't like Portal don't buy it. In all seriousness I already heard and read in advance that The Entropy Center will remind you on Portal, but after playing it I would say  like Portal, just with another gun mechanic: Level like game construction like Portal, similiar block mechanics and a companion who talks funny all the time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Center is a puzzle platformer in first person perspective, staring Aria and her rewind device Astra, as they try to prevent a cataclysmic event happening on earth, through the use of Entropy Energy generated from solving puzzles.The game is a bit Portal x Braid, as it has a somewhat dystopian setting with quirky chippy dialog as backdrop for the puzzles, puzzles which utilize a rewind feature. That means you have to essentially solve the puzzles backwards and work your way back to the beginning, which probably is also the theme of the games plot. Although when time parallels and time rewind mechanics are involved, you never know.The puzzles themselves aren't overly involved, and the game would rather push new and different puzzle cubes at you, but ever so seldom make you utilize multiple of them in a given chapter, at least not until towards the end. At the same time the difficulty of the puzzles doesn't really evolve either, despite new puzzle cubes being introduced, ultimately in the end it's about rewinding the cubes back to their respective triggers to open a door.There's a couple of segments throughout the game that involves dexterity, especially involving the conveyor belts, that the game could have been without. Similarly there are a couple of segments with simple puzzles that also has repeatedly spawning enemies that are just a nuisance and in the way of the puzzle element of the game.Overall a solid production for an indie title, although the environments does get a bit bland and repetitive. The music is fitting and dramatic at times,Technically the game could have been better, developers should have learnt by now that, if they intent on forcing film grain, motion blur, mouse acceleration (what year is this even?) and all other nonsense elements, that they at least make it possible to turn those off in the games settings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the puzzles, the story and the humor and changes of gameplay. This game is really well done, i have no complaints as of now but i didn't complete the game yet so if i notice anything bad i will update the review. So, this game reminds me a lot of portal but it doesn't feel like a knock-off or anything like that. It has it's own puzzles, characters and form of gameplay and scenery which i all really like. The puzzles feel fresh and i really like how the story is told. Some people have complained about performance but my game runs at over 144 fps on ultra and i only have a 3050ti. If you like puzzle games like portal, you will like this
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend? "Yes, but...".The world design is gorgeous, the puzzles and the story are good in general, but there's a point where the puzzles - rather than introducing new obstacles/elements, or making you feel excited about having mastered the mechanics to proceed faster - just become "same old, same old" tedious.OK, at this point you're probably 3/4 through the game and you might just want to hang on, to see how it ends, but it's just a shame, the game lacks a little bit of "breath", to make the whole game as interesting as the first half.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and interesting, the lore is not too deep, no need to look too much into it, and the ending is a bit underwhelming, I mean of course it's all very exciting in the moment but it's bittersweet.All in all I would definitely recommend this, it's fun, not too hard, challenging, funny at times, spectacular, a bit moving and the whole mystery can be very entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty well polished, runs great, but the puzzles just aren't very interesting. The puzzles deal with setting up puzzle pieces and then you can rewind them along the path that they moved. Easily half of the puzzles have essentially the same solution where you move the single puzzle piece from position to position, in reverse order, and then rewind that puzzle piece step by step as you use it to get through the puzzle. I kept waiting for some ability or puzzle piece to be introduced that makes the game interesting, but it never happened.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥, buy it, no questions askedThe Entropy Centre is a puzzle game where your main interaction with the world is by reversing objects in time. You play as Aria, a woman who wakes up in a science organization with little recollection (sound familiar?) and you are accompanied by Astra, the assistant in your gun-like tool that reverses time. Although it has little direct offensive capabilities, there is actual combat in the game, and some options open up to you with how you can fight back - the mainstay being reversing the enemy's projectiles in time and guiding them right back to them.If you think this game sounds like Portal, then you're somewhat right. There are story beats that feel right at home, some of the puzzle elements, the dry, witty banter between Aria and Astra, the Entropy Centre collapsing in a dilapidated state - but it has more than enough to stand on its own. Particularly, the lore and worldbuilding and how it ties into the current story is extremely fascinating, and I adored the ending.This game was made mostly by a solo developer, and with that in mind, the production quality is insane. This game barely has any bugs or glaring issues. It's not perfect, mind you, I found a few tiny things here and there - but by and large the game does an extremely good job of making sure that everything is as it should be. I brought a jump cube from a previous puzzle into the next puzzle and it got fizzled before I could bring it in - it was made sure that I couldn't cheat in any obvious way.Overall: great story, fun characters, nice music, mind-bending puzzles. Absolutely worth it
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Takes a lot of pages out of Portal 2's book, but I ain't mad at that. I enjoyed the story, the puzzle mechanics that got increasingly more challenging, the dopamine hit I got when I'd solve a real head-scratcher. If, like me, you've given up on there ever being a Portal 3, this will scratch the itch!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-nice art direction-decent characters-passable story (although predictable)Cons:-rewinding doesn't add to the puzzles. it only makes things unnecessarily confusing and convoluted-later puzzles are overly complex-making minor mistakes forces you to set up the entire solution again, which can take a few minutes
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Fun-to-solve puzzles with an intriguing story, quirky humor, impressive visuals and effects, great sound design, great music, and attractive lore scattered throughout the campaign. The only negatives are the clunky movement of your character, and I also have mixed feelings about the ending. Overall, it is worth getting if you are a lover of puzzle games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre
