_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to play the second game for years, but discovered that PS2 emulation sucks. It sucks in general and for this game it literally didn't work for decades.And finally this year they've released both games on PC. This is a very good package. It features both games and adds an easy difficulty. It removes the lives system which was a terrible coin-munching idea to begin with. Also it increases the range of the attack from point blank to almost point blank. Doesn't improve attack angles, though.The first game uses sprites with few frames of animation. The second game uses cell-shading. This release unifies the art-style but it has a generic 3D render. Some of the personality is lost but that's a justified sacrifice to have both games natively run at modern resolutions and modern aspect ratios with proper graphics.Klonoa's ears are connected in an awkward way. His textures are tiled so he looks a bit weird. And some of the background textures are a bit weak. The second ark was of noticeably lower resolution.Loading times are weird. The games run fine but sometimes it takes a lot of time to load into one or the other game from the main menu.The cutscenes can be sped up or skipped, which is a very good addition especially for the sequel.A good platformer should be so tight that it feels more like a rhythm game. Being a 2.5D game but with 3D levels there are weird alignments, wonky hitboxes and no way to aim. In this game the tolerances are so loose that you constantly overshoot every target. (There are two places in the first game where the placement makes it a 95% chance of undershoot. But those are static and somewhat safe.) The game asks you to underperform instead of giving it your all. Which is not the most pleasant feeling.Playing both games in this package or the original was fine in the story mode. It's very simple and it rarely asks of you to perform a long chain of actions with accumulation of tolerances. But there are three bonus levels which do exactly that. And all three are required for the achievements.They are a damn nightmare and the first game's bonus is a ten times nestled nightmare. They require more than the absolute perfect timing and you have to work against the wonky acceleration arks. The level design amplifies every slight miscalculation. And in the first game the level still spend your lives. If i went for it on the original hardware even after accumulating the maximum allowed number of lives i would still run out. Two of the rooms are absolutely insane. I had to switch to keyboard controls fro the Chamber o'Horrors and because i smashed my thumb for it i had to learn how to play with a mouse to finish EXTRA VISION. To prolong the torture there is no instant respawn/reset and every failed attempt has a loading time to it.Well, at least all of the achievements are in working order. Nothing exciting — the typical story progress trackers and collectibles trackers. Good thing there are no achievements for the stupid gems.風のクロノア2 〜世界が望んだ忘れもの〜 [Kaze no Kuronoa 2 〜sekai ga nozonda wasuremono〜]So i thought that the first game is inferior because it lacks puzzles. But it turned out that in the sequel they are barely present. The first one appears past the middle of the game and in total there are probably less than ten of them. Even the double armour is used only in one level.I liked the first game but this doesn't do it for me. It still has Klonoa's own set of mechanics, the sound is great and the designs are cool. But the soundtrack has no memorable tunes outside of one track. The character was redesigned and instead of looking absolutely great now it looks like a sanik OC. Ghadius is a great character; the sequel instead has some weeaboo drama set in a jumbled world. The cutscenes are extremely long and slow and aren't entertaining much. The levels are very linear and the spring-jumping and the snowboarding ones are kinda bad. Several levels are outright recycled.This game turned out to be just a diet version of more of the same. It's enjoyable but not great.So Klonoa traveled to a new world. But it still has moos, and everyone knows about the ring and how to use it. The gems are the same too.Instead of a straight plot of the first game the sequel offers a convoluted nonsense. Sorrow is too hard to handle for them, but the eternal-civil-war-kingdom is just right? The game is referring to some things which are never explained or appear again. Who's Claire? Who's Lunatea? It's all stupid weeaboo drama about nothing.The game is very simple (and easier than the first one) but some levels are a nightmare. Without the infinite lives they would be very irritating. The level design is just not very good, especially when hunting for the bells. And if you even think about collecting all 150 gems that already is unsettling every time you see a gem. Without quicksaves or even an ability to restart at the checkpoint, even with infinite lives it would be a torture. The game is made of sawtooths and stupid sliding / riding levels. There are many timed sequences that are already tight, and each one of them have gems in difficult to access areas, while the walls of death never contemplate slowing down. Or even allowing to be outrun. They reset the distance when you get to far. It's not about just collecting them either, every x2 bonus have to be executed perfectly with sub-second tolerances while all the hitboxes and alignments are still whack. And in the second game it doesn't even re-colour the gems. The GUI doesn't even track the collected gems on the level, so you have to manually count them.The second game is quite good but i don't feel greatness from it. Without the collection of gems with quicksaves, it feels like i do not engage with content. It can't compete with the enjoyment of re-Spyro 2 and 3. But also being less tight than Crash 4 it doesn't feel as fulfilling. I waited for it for about 20 years and it is expensive so i expected more from it.風のクロノア door to phantomile [Kaze no Kuronoa]The re-made version loses in several areas — new Ghadius is weak and generic; the re-made music is not as impactful and sounds blurred; there's lens dirt retarded effect; the map screen is weaker. The original looks more cartoonier and uses a more aggressive and fun palette. But with the new engine they have close-ups on Klonoa during the cut-scenes, highlighting his top notch original design. Even if with the weird ears and tiling textures. But all cutscenes needed another QA pass on clipping solids — these are very noticeable and very distracting.The voices are kinda quiet too, even with everything else being 35% quieter the are still sometimes drown in music.The new version is undeniably a better game better technology, modern render better readability and light GUI. But there is less greatness and character in it.So replaying the first game that i considered to be really great after finishing the sequel, it's easier to see the difference. The variety of mobs is bigger. The gameplay is snappier and less slow. The complexity is much higher and the layouts are more enjoyable. At times this feels like a high-budget version of Nebulus. There are more voiced character and the voices are the best feature of this franchise.The first game is hard as all ass. I thought that having that much HP was excessive on easy difficulty in the sequel, but here it was just right. With loose mechanics and weird hitboxes this was the amount of HP needed for the boss-fights. And the Extra Vision. I died on every phase of the last boss and died on the boss on the swing even with the boosted HP.The core of the story is simple enough — go defeat the bad guy. But the ending is weird forced drama and it creates and envelope of weirdness and conspiracies that make you question what the hell was even happening in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic art, beautiful/catchy music, tight platforming and excellent level design - Klonoa has it all and I can highly recommend it! As a first time player, these 2 games have been a blast to play (fresh off playing Kirby and the Crystal Shards). I love 2d and 3d platformers and these games did not disappoint - Klonoa may be simple in its premise and controls, but the platforming is so natural and the difficulty/design curve from level-to-level is smooth and progressive, with each new stage introducing harder challenges for already-learned concepts. The art is gorgeous and I love the character designs and voices. The music is seriously good and I've heard several that are definitely up there with some of my favourite VG tracks during my playtime. A 2.5d platformer that genuinely uses 3d elements for both visual pleasure and gameplay novelties that really work well.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like underrated platformers with great gameplay, cute characters, and emotionally touching stories, these games will be right up your alley.These games are very nostalgic for me and it's nice to finally have them in an easily accessible form. _childDocuments_.review: A charming PS1-era platformer, Klonoa offers a nostalgia trip for fans of those late 90's era 2.5D side-scrolling action games. If you're a fan of other games in a similar genre such as Rayman, Super Mario, or Kirby, this is definitely a great game to pick up (especially on sale!).This collection includes two different games which ran me around 12.5 hours total to fully complete (100% all achievements). The second game definitely builds on the same mechanics which it utilizes from the first game in very creative ways. This will be a bit of a platforming challenge as the game tests your accuracy in it's mechanics!

_childDocuments_.review: Before I played this game, I knew next to nothing about this series. I bought this game on release out of curiosity, and promptly fell in love with the series. The price is admittedly a little unreasonable, but in exchange you'll fully understand why people want this series to come back- and add just a bit to the miniscule chance that Namco will one day decide to bring this series back.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review from someone who has played the originals, so I am definitely biased in the regard that I like these games. I'll also be writing this review mainly from the perspective of someone who has played one or both of the originals and is considering getting these remakes.Starting from the conclusion: yes, you should buy it. Even if you're not going to replay them, it will show Bandai Namco there is interest in the series. Now for the details:Klonoa: Door to PhantomileI personally love the treatment this game got. The environments look amazing, the sliding present in the Wii remake is completely gone, and the music sounds as wonderful as ever. Some people take issue with the fact that there was a lot of reuse of the Wii remake's textures, but I personally thought the Wii version looked fine so I'm perfectly happy with it. I'm also happy they decided to bring back the fantasy language instead of the English dub- it's always been something that added to the atmosphere of the series for me. Another thing that's been pointed out, however, is that they use the original audio from the PS1 version of the game for the dialogue, and it sounds very crunchy and compressed. It would have been nice to get a re-dub and potentially allow you to choose which version you wanted to listen to, but I understand they may not have been able to get ahold of important voice actors, especially considering how much time has passed. This may however be a turn-off for some people. Finally, one caveat- they really cranked the saturation up in both games, and while that works wonderfully for most areas, there are some that I would have liked to see have a bit more of a muted palette. Sometimes the overly bright colors detracted from the serious tone the game was trying to go for.Klonoa 2: Lunatea's VeilFor many people, I would say that this is the main reason to buy this collection. At the time of writing this, the original on PS2 goes for about $80-100 on eBay which makes it inaccessible to most people, and that's a shame because it's an amazing game. I personally know a lot of people that have played 1 but not 2 precisely because of that accessibility issue. The fact that it's now only technically $20 is big. That being said, however, from what I've played it feels like more effort went into Door to Phantomile than Lunatea's Veil. There are good looking areas in 2, yes, but there are also ones that I quite frankly dislike in comparison to the original. A lot of these areas are at the start of the game, too, which is a shame because I'm afraid it will turn off new players. In addition, some of the sound effects (most notably the wind bullet grab) have been altered. This sounds minor but they're important SFX you'll be listening to often so I do take some issue with it. Overall, though, this is likely the definitive way to play 2 for the majority of people and has made it much more accessible, and just for that I'm willing to give it a pass on some of its rougher edges. It's a really fun game, definitely play it.Other notes that apply to both games:- The tutorials are annoying but you can thankfully turn them off- The question of difficulty is hard to answer. I enjoy normal difficulty for the harsher health restrictions, but at the same time I feel like the wind bullet hitbox is too small. You can't even pick up enemies if they're going down a slope whereas in the originals you definitely could. This would be a trivial thing to fix so I hope a patch eventually comes that addresses this, but unless you're really good I'd recommend playing on easy mode for now. Normal can be frustrating and unfair sometimes.- Another minor QOL thing, but you can't see how many gems you've collected in a stage until the end. 2 had this feature and it meant you didn't have to second guess whether you'd found everything or not. I'm sad it's gone now and I hope they bring it back.- There are minor sound glitches, namely some sound effects don't play if you perform multiple actions too quickly. It fixes itself so it's not serious, but hopefully a future patch addresses this.- The DLC, as others have talked about, doesn't give you the music and art files, it simply allows you to view them in-game. I'd say only buy it if you really enjoy the series and want to show your monetary support.All in all there are some rough edges, but I really want to see this series come back and I trust in Bandai-Namco to make improvements if we get a sequel, so I want to ask everyone who is interested to buy the game.Do it for the fluffy boyo.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful. Is it the best remaster I've ever seen? No, but it's a remaster for two games I never thought I'd see. While I recognize there was a remake on the Wii, it seemed to lack a lot of the spirit and charm of the original on the PSX, but so far, this game seems to have found that charm and translate it much better this time around. Add the fact we finally get a Klonoa 2 remaster and this is something you better believe I'm going to 100% in a day or three. If you missed the chance on playing these 20 some years ago, now is the time to give Klonoa a try. The story, while simple, is engaging enough for anyone to follow along with and dare I say, maybe even get emotional over. The soundtrack is fantastic for both games. The art style itself is reminiscent of the vague Cirque du Soleil style that was prominent in NiGHTS Into Dreams... on the Saturn. 20 years later, does this still hold up as a solid platformer? Absolutely. Easy to learn, a challenge to truly master. This is worth a chance if you have the time and interest. Try something new, and bring back an old but charming character and concept from obscurity.

_childDocuments_.review: The first game, Door to Phantomile, maintains the quality and spirit of the original Playstation game... that is, it's good but sometimes it feels like it hasn't aged well. The second game, Lunatea's Veil, is the best part of this collection; it's like a fever dream, weird but pleasant; the level desings are really fun and the story goes darker than I expected. I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: ---This is a review only for the second game---Let's start with what I liked:The puzzle platforming is a solid upgrade over the first game. It's more challenging, more elaborate, with more tools and options at your disposal. The art style is distinctive, colorful and charming, and kingdoms all having unique music leitmotifs made them stand out in an overall pretty good OST. Now, unlike the game itself, it's sadly not all sunshine and rainbows. The controls can get really finicky and floaty at times, to a frustrating degree. I've died more than a few times through no fault of my own. That camera can also obfuscate certain details at times that are crucial to progressing on puzzle solving or platforming. The skateboarding gameplay segments were easily some of weaker, more annoying parts of the game. It had no reason to be part of a puzzle platformer game. Lastly, the story felt really rushed and lacked depth. I didn't get to connect with the world or these characters- heroes or villains-and it was overall an inferior story compared to the first game.If you enjoyed the Klonoa 1 gameplay, you'll find more of that here. And if you can look past its faults, you may enjoy it too.

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished Klonoa 1 so far and having played a bit of Klonoa 2 i can confirm that this is a worthy collection made by two amazing remasters.Klonoa 1 has some jank however, it really shows that they just grabbed the wii version, changed some things without proper adjustments and called it a day. Still the wii version is truly the game that needed a remake considering how dry and dark that one felt compared to the original.Phantasy Reverie gives the game the color it needed, changes klonoa's model to be more similar to the ps1 model and removes the weird dub they made for the wii (not gonna miss it tbh), although the voice lines are a mix of compressed and uncompressed files from the original, which is the weirdest choice i've ever witnessed. That aside the level design remains unchanged meaning that its still the amazing game i played as a child a long time ago.And from what little i've played of klonoa 2 i really like it, klonoa feels strangely slow and there are some visual glitches, but nothing terrible so far. Since i don't have much experience with klonoa 2 (because of its imprisonment on the ps2) i will be very happy to finally be able to play it properly without game breaking bugs or compatibility issues!.I wholeheartedly recommend this collection, please save my boy Klonoa!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This is a mostly informational review. Although I am not recommending this collection, the gameplay is fundamentally sound. The reason why I cannot give it a positive review is for reasons that will be explained below. For those who want a quick answer: play the originals, and do not support pointless remakes of games that are already good. This is basically a review of the the package itself, and considers the changes made to the original games. If I were to actually rate the original games, Door to Phantomile would be a 7.5, and Klonoa 2 would be something like an 8. They are great games, and that makes the lacking care and accuracy of this collection all the more disappointing.This is a collection of remakes of Klonoa: Door to Phantomile (1998) and Klonoa 2: Lunatea's Veil (2001) released for PlayStation and PlayStation 2 respectively. In my opinion, both are great "2.5D" puzzle platformers featuring interesting mechanics and good level design. There's some especially clever moments near the climaxes of both games when the difficulty ramps up. Generally though, they are quite easy, sometimes insultingly so. The real challenge in them comes from finding the collectables in each level. However, there are two sets of collectables: the main set of six (known as Phantomilians in the first game, and Momett Doll Bells in the second) is very easy to find, but the 150 "Dream Stones" are frustrating to collect for the wrong reasons. First of which being the fact that you must get them all in a single run, and then there's the instances of easily missable strings, forcing you to kill yourself just in order to try again. I recommend only finding the six main collectables and avoiding the urge to get all 150 of the Dream Stones if you value your sanity. Though, you are rewarded with really challenging extra levels for finding them all, which are among the best in both games because they push the mechanics to the absolute limits.Anyway, the main reason why I struggle to recommend these versions is simply because they're pointless remakes. It's initially less apparent in Klonoa 2's case, but everything has been touched up for the worse in both games. The first Klonoa originally had a very beautiful art style that was violated completely in the Wii remake from 2008, which this version uses as a base, but somehow modifies further anyway. Klonoa 2 was tampered with slightly less, but still looks significantly worse than the PS2 original. Problems affecting both games include: missing effects (such as the characters' facial expressions), much worse color usage, and this annoying bright bloom effect that is very overbearing. All-in-all, if the the games interest you, they should be played in their original formats. Are these remakes horribly ugly? Absolutely not, and they are nice in their own right (in a vacuum), but ultimately degraded versions of more appealing looking games. This is largely about integrity, and the importance of keeping older games in circulation. It's also downright insulting to the original developers when you disregard the details of their work. The collection should have been comprised of only the original games in the first place, but Bandai Namco could have included emulated versions of them in the package at the very minimum. In an ideal world, the collection would have simply been top notch emulations, with some optional bells and whistles (such as the regional versions) for those who want that kind of thing.Later edit: I ended up removing the score, because this review is mostly about the collection.

_childDocuments_.review: True to form, Klonoa continues to be an underrated series of platformers, now brought to modern consoles and PC in the Phantasy Reverie Series. The original games released in 1997 and 2001 respectively, failed to sell well outside of Japan for a number of reasons not limited to issues like poor marketing, making physical copies of the games extremely expensive and rare. Not only does this collection give players new and old the opportunity to legally play the games for cheap, but also with modernized graphics that look brighter and more detailed than ever, especially Door to Phantomile. The games themselves both hold up extremely well in both presentation and gameplay, and I really hope this game does well enough to warrant a true sequel in the future. This port both runs very well and has a good number of options for video, audio, and control. Bandai Namco made the smart decision to maintain the original voices, music, and sound effects of most everything while touching up many of the cutscenes, balancing the gameplay (including a two-player mode and difficulty options), and overall polishing that the original PS1/PS2 games in a way they couldn't originally due to hardware limitations. I highly recommend you pick this collection up if you enjoy great platformers with fun gimmicks and amazing story.

_childDocuments_.review: Klonoa 1 and 2 on their own are masterpieces, I love them. This remaster however is completely half assed low effort with issues that weren't in the originals such as lighting bugs, missing facial expressions, wind bullet length being messed up, low quality audio, and more. Biggest problem is how these issues could be fixed easily with a patch but there hasn't been any 2 months later and that is just a telltale sign this crap about how if Klonoa sells well enough they'll make more games was nothing more than a PR stunt to guilt trip the fans into buying it and pressuring others into doing so and the fact that so many of the reviews are just meme tier people begging others to buy it says it all and i regret my purchase very much.It's clear bandai has no interest nor reason to make any new games if they can't even bother to patch it and I implore you  to not spend $40 on inferior versions of two amazing games when you can easily go search for them and play them for freeI love Klonoa and wouldn't mind his series making a comeback but Klonoa deserves better and if this is all we're going to get then I think this series is better off dead instead of ruining it's legacy.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: Klonoa's deeply melancholic tale fits into the mascot platformer craze of the 90s the same way Doki Doki Literature Club fits into Steam's Romantic Visual Novel library. Combining puzzle solving elements with action platforming, Klonoa frankly has more in common with Celeste than anything of its time, and the fact that I just used two games from the past five years to describe these 20+ year old games should give you an idea of how ahead of their time these titles were.Are there nitpicks with this remaster? Sure, but nothing that dramatically inhibits the experience outside from a couple moments (which would be easy to patch if Namco gives this package the love it deserves). But at the end of the day, I'd still recommend this as the ideal way to play both these absolutely perfect games with impeccably lean level design, fantastic and distinct music, and some of the best writing that exists for a "children's game." 100% worth the price at $40, but if it's currently on sale, don't even think about it, just get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful remake, but for some reason the audio for Klonoa 1 is the compressed audio from the PS1 game and it's really weird because it's all muffled sounding compared to the rest of the game's audio, and then the final cutscene klonoa suddenly sounds crisp and clear and I was just like ???Also they thought it was a bright idea to add forced tutorial cards that interrupt gameplay and take you out of the experience all the while achieving the opposite of what they were meant to do by confusing the player in some instances like with the first locked door in the game, which is absurd considering the game naturally teaches players the mechanics anyways so it's all redundant information and takes away the player's ability to discover. This would be okay if you played on the game's "easy mode", but I was playing on normal, the hardest difficulty you start with.I won't go into more detail about how building critical thinking skills in players is important, but it's the biggest gripe I have with the game, which is saying how dang good this remake is.In the end, I guess we can say this: Wahoo!

_childDocuments_.review: The Klonoa series (if you can even call it one by now) continues to be genuinely one-of-a-kind, criminally overlooked by both general audiences and even it's own creators and sincerely deserves more. Bouncy, bubbly adventures that fulfill the bright, colorful platformer criteria in both presentation and gameplay with wholely unique 2.5D level design that's barely been replicated to this day.+ Outstanding use of 2.5D elements in levels that wrap around through the foreground/background+ Bright, bubbly, and colorful visuals accompanied by light, airy sound design- Some levels in both games outstay their welcome

_childDocuments_.review: A fun side-scroller with unexpectedly profound storytelling. I preferred the first game when I emulated the PS1 version, but Klonoa 2 is fantastic and definitely worth getting this remaster for. _childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: SIDENOTE - Most of my hours are spent on the Switch version of the remaster. I'll always love the Klonoa series. It's one of those games where you can play it and have a good time. However, the series has gone more rare in recent times and games go for insane prices online. This meant that the series was inaccessible for many people unless you knew emulation or got one of the GBA games on eShop before they shut for good. Then Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series came along and introduced a bunch of people to a series I hold dear to my heart. _childDocuments_.review: Good gameplay concept, I just wish that it wasn't so easy and that there were more knobs and dials to complement the core "yoshi jump" mechanic. The challenge levels are really fun to think about and complete. I would've wanted more of the game to be like those bonus levels (albeit not as difficult but still fun and challenging).Despite the game being really easy I think it is beautiful and relaxing. It puts a smile on my face and makes me appreciate the design work that went into everything. That's really the only reason I got this game.If you're looking for something relaxing that will cheer you up and make you smile, it is wonderful. If you're looking for consistently challenging and colorful gameplay, look somewhere else. Though, the price is steep for what the games provide. I would recommend waiting for a sale or buying a cheaper key.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: Despite Klonoa: Door to Phantomile having some minor issues that the PS1 (Better cutscenes and overall presentation) and even the Wii-make (New bonus stages and modes that don't return in Reverie) does better, this bundle is a perfectly serviceable and accessible way to play these two masterpieces, most especially Klonoa 2, which was rough to be able to find and play beforehand.Both games still hold the magical childhood wonder that I fell in love with ages ago, such simple yet engaging stories, simple yet challenging platforming, and boundless amounts of charm in the artistic and vocal talent used to create one of the most memorable platforming series of the fifth and sixth generation consoles.And as for the stories that these games tell. I cried the first time I played through the both of these games when I was a young teen. And I can't hide the fact that I couldn't help myself from crying again even after so long.

_childDocuments_.review: While the games look like they are for a younger demographic, they still hold meaningful plots with valuable lessons to learn, that and the game play slowly ramps up in difficulty on Klonoa 1, and holds it (even raising it a bit) for Klonoa 2. They are enjoyable and if you really want to, you could speedrun them in a day (although getting 100% is tricky, specially with the collectible gems, those are kind of a nightmare)Upsides:Klonoa 1 is based on the Wii version and fixes the color profile that the game used, making it look more vibrant and on par with Klonoa 2's visual design, this was the main point to having the Wii version instead of the PSX version.the music is sublime, it gives a very relaxed vibe, even in the more tense moments of gameplay.everythign about this game is just cute! Seriously i love the little wahoo critter.Downsides:the main con is that this collection lacks the volleyball game and the portable console games (Moonlight Museum, Empire of Dreams, Dream Champ Tournament and Legendary Star Medal) which is a bit sad as it effectively is more Klonoa content that is still forgotten by Bandai.Audio Quality is subpar, you can hear the crunchiness of some lines in both games.The controls are a bit... janky? not to the point of being unplayable, but the game feels very much unforgiving with the precision jumps you are asked to do to get 150 gems on each stage, or some of the collectibles. I am unsure if it was this way as I haven't played the original versions of the games, but other's claim the controls are worse (i will revise this point if i ever do play the games)All in All, If you ever wanted to play the games, this is the Official way to do it and not half-bad at that. this collection fixes the core issue of Klonoa being both A) Forgotten and B) hard to acquire. Although it feels like it was done in a "Bare Minimum" kind of way.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, Klonoa 1 and 2 are both amazing games that have held a special place in my heart since childhood.  If you want to know if those games are good, then I will tell you that they are amazing.  This review of Phantasy Reverie will be focused mainly on how well it remade the originals.GRAPHICSThe graphical fidelity is amazing.  All the models and textures look great.The lighting is good, more brighter and cartoony where it needs to be.  Old PS2 and Wii games had a weird tendency to be very desaturated.  In Phantasy Reverie, things look bright and colorful when they need to be, which makes the darker areas stand out even more.  One issue I have is there are a few areas where the lighting doesn’t have enough contrast, making it hard to tell which part of a cube is the side and which is the front, for example.  It was never a problem gameplay wise, just something that could have looked a little nicer.Furthermore, several graphical effects from the originals are missing e.g. Joka’s singed appearance after his boss fight.  Leorina and Tat being in shadow before their reveal.  Some of the animations in Klonoa 2 were seemingly imported incorrectly (?) so characters don’t always have the exact right mouth shapes in cutscenes, there’s currently a mod on github to fix this issue, so hopefully this can be patched in the future.GRAPHICS: BMUSIC AND SFXMusic and Sound Effects are virtually unchanged from the original.  This is fine by me, I’ve seen enough remakes that replace music with worse versions that remove all the emotion from the original, that I’m more than happy seeing the music in Phantasy Reverie remain untouched.  Because, honestly, the original tracks are very nearly perfection.  The sound mixing felt off in places.  In Klonoa 1 the voice samples sounded slightly too quiet and in Klonoa 2 the music sounded slightly too quiet.  Unfortunately the default volume of every channel is  the highest volume, so the only way to get around this was to lower the volume of the other channels and then turn up the computer volume.MUSIC AND SFX: A -GAMEPLAYGameplay is largely unchanged, though Klonoa 1 is closer to the Wii remake than the PS1 remake, which means that the level design is slightly easier.  I did notice that the physics of the Wind Bullet felt slightly off, either the bullet’s hitbox was too small or the hang time was too short, or some combination of the two.  It was the kind of thing that was easy to get used to and anyone playing for the first time might not even notice anything is wrong, but I feel like I had to say it.  Also, there are a bunch of tutorial pop ups (some even right before or after a cutscene tutorializing the exact same thing) but they could be turned off in the menus which is really nice.GAMEPLAY: A -MISCELLANYThere’s an inconsistency in how Doubled Gems are shown.  In the first game, they’re shown as orange, but in the second game they’re normally colored.  Would have been nice if they were orange in both games for consistency and ease of reading. There are two rats chilling in Joilant Park in the original that are missing in Phantasy Reverie.The health bar changes appearance based on the level you’re playing, which is a nice touch.FINAL THOUGHTSAn amazing remake of two amazing games.  If you haven’t played the originals then this a great way to play them without having to deal with the high prices on EBay or Amazon.  If you’ve already played the originals, then you might be impressed by the new graphics or challenged by the introduced Hard Mode.  It’s hard to improve or even match something that is so close to perfection, but this remake comes close.  If there’s ever a patch to fix some of the minor issues noted above, I’ll increase the score.FINAL SCORE: B+

_childDocuments_.review: If you love platformers, especially ones with cutesy mascots, then this may be for you. The remake of both games sets itself to be balanced and enjoyable that you can pick up a controller and know you'll pretty much need only two buttons, or a old school NES Controller. If you want to go easy, there's a easy mode that provides the player with infinite lives, and normal with a set number of lives, which can be said for hard mode. However, if you want to play on the hardest difficulty, on either game you pick, you'll need to beat either on easy or normal mode first. Each game allows the player to change costumes, but are limited without DLC, with only two. (Classic and Moo Impersonator). For Door to Phantomile's case, its a disappointing downgrade, as I would have loved it to run around with the Costumes presented in the Wiimake's version for both games. Maybe that's something that can be remedied in a future update or DLC in the future. The games will have you collecting gems, solving puzzles and saving multiple prisoners and dolls that are trapped and lost. Al while you go out to save a singing Diva from a Mystique Figure and his henchman and go out and travel various locations to collect Elements to save Lunatea, Collecting gems, prisoners and dolls will present the player with rewards if they collect a max limit, with prisoners being indicated by the HUD. The HUD, while it is workable and clean, could have been a little better for Gem counting. As if you miss some, the games may not directly let you know until you reach the end of the level. What is nice, you can revisit any levels as soon as you finish them without having to beat the games first, an issue first presented by Door to Phantomile's PlayStation 1 version. The games will have extra levels once you have met certain conditions such as collecting dolls and being the main stories of both games. The extra levels will test your skills on whether or not you can get to the end. Doing so will grant a music player in Door to Phantomile, and a blue check in Lunatea's Veil. Now, if you plan to get every achievement in this game, you won't have to worry too much, as the achievement list focuses more so on whether you can tackle bosses and collecting dolls and prisoners. No gem collecting achievements, as i'm sure that some would be fuming over. Also finishing the extra levels too, with Multiplayer granting you and a buddy to strategize unique jumps. Overall, a fun game to pick up and blast through with moderate ease.

_childDocuments_.review: KPRS is a beautiful remaster of two of my favorite platform games ever. They sport gameplay that rewards both tight reflexes and smart thinking, wonderful music, and surprisingly interesting storylines, now with a fresh coat of paint. All of the content in the original versions is here and accounted for, and they've been given new difficulty options for accessibility.*  is unfortunately marred with a quite a few presentational and sound problems, but the gameplay itself is still quite solid despite a few changes in the physics.* , a game stuck on the PS2 for over 20 years, is the crowning piece of the collection, playing every bit as well as the original, but retaining the same style of cutscenes and a myriad of small details that veterans will appreciate. I still have a few nitpicks, but I'd say KPRS is worth getting just for this one game.It is unfortunate that games like these were overlooked for so long, but they've been given a second chance to shine for a reason. If they seem interesting, please give them a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Klonoa is a series that has been very obscure for a long time, but there is not many other communities that are as passionate for the games as the fanbase of this one. Klonoa's last game was in 2008 with the release of a remake of Door to Phantomile on the Wii, which had limited success. This game exists solely because of the passion and heart of the developers and the community who have always kept Klonoa close to their hearts.This game isn't going to be perfect, and as of right now there is some issues with things like changing your screen resolution. Nothing I've encountered so far has been remotely gamebreaking though. Both games that are included are faithfully remastered and I can tell that they've considered input and criticisms from the fanbase. The first game uses the voice lines from the original game, which can be a little jarring when contrasted with the vibrant, HD textures and models that are used. However, I got used to them after the first few levels.I have noticed a lot of people complaining about the graphics and saying that the art direction is inferior to the original. Personally I haven't had any issue with any of the graphics, and there is also an option to disable bloom in the game settings if it's something you don't like. I highly recommend this game if you're a fan who's played all the original games, or even if you're someone who's never gotten into the series before. This is a perfect entry point for people who have an interested in the series or like puzzle-platformers in general. On one last note, I hope there's an option to disable tutorials in the future. The pop-up screens are really intrusive and disrupt the experience.TLDR; Phantasy Reverie Series is a faithful recreation of the original and anyone who buys this is directly contributing to the possibility seeing Klonoa in a brand new adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING port of an AMAZING game. Music is crisp and high quality, controls feel good, includes easy difficulty for new players (the game is surprisingly tough if you try to speedrun it, enemies can hit you twice a second if you're touching their hitbox) and it's THE best way to play the original PS1 Klonoa and PS2 Klonoa 2. The first game plays fine despite some weird music loops during emotional cutscenes messing with the tone, and the second game plays literally 1:1 as the old game did and is absolutely perfect.I only have three small complaints - the first Klonoa game in the Phantasy Reverie collection is based off of the Wii version that came out in the mid 2000's which had issues, namely the voiceover and graphics. The cinematography during cutscenes is a bit more dull and flat than the original PS1's very dynamic, sometimes dutch-angle cutscenes and crisp pixel art, instead going for a total 3D approach (you're given the option to play with a pixel filter, although I haven't tried it). New players won't notice this or care, but hardcore fans will likely realize it's a downgrade in that sense.My second complaint is the audio - the original PS1 voiceover sounds muffled and reverb-heavy like a lot of old PS1 games (Metal Gear Solid voices are a good example of how common heavy reverb was with voiceover back in the 90s), and while they re-recorded it for the Wii version it didn't quite have the same emotion as the original despite coming incredibly close. The Wii version started BY DEFAULT with a crappy English dub that sounded like something 4Kids dubbed (Sonic X quality, Klonoa's VA said he was given almost no direction or context when recording), and thankfully this game doesn't include that option AT ALL. But what's weird is that the game mixes the old muffled PS1 voice lines with the Wii's cleaner ones - gameplay has clean audio, cutscenes have PS1 audio. I don't care too much, but as an audio engineer I could hear that every *single* line ended with an abrupt cut for some reason (the reverb stops abruptly, it's noticeable). But again, nowhere near a deal breaker for how amazing this game/port is.My last nitpick is the "Skip / 5x Speed" button prompts that appear in the bottom-right corner and never fades away during cutscenes, so it's a mild eyesore.I anticipate all or most of these issues will be fixed by any dedicated modders, but as it stands it's simply a difference I wanted to point out and is by no means a reason not to buy the game. I'm just a giant fan of the original and these small changes are a very slight downgrade.Klonoa 2 got an HD upgrade but is otherwise entirely identical. This is the best way to play/record Klonoa 2 since the original PS2 version of the game had the odd quirk of changing resolution every time the game would dip into a loading screen, and then reverting it again when gameplay would resume. This would lead to capture cards having long pauses and not recording the first few seconds of cutscenes/gameplay, which was rough since this would happen every loading screen and sometimes you'd have to act quickly to collect items or defeat enemies in those first few seconds of entering the next area. Phantasy Reverie does NOT have this issue, thank Lephise!Please buy it ASAP instead of waiting for a sale. The developers said they'd consider making Klonoa 3 and other expansions/remasters if this game gets enough love. That's amazing considering it's been 3 console generations since Klonoa 2 came out (over a decade ago) and it would be amazing to see this IP get resurrected as a result of a huge outpouring of support.I hope this review has informed you enough to consider purchasing the game, and if you do, have fun! It's such a phenomenal series, and they simply don't make games like this anymore because most video game enjoyers prefer gun games instead of cutesy furry platformers.Enjoy!!!

_childDocuments_.review: (Don't mind the play-time, I've beaten both games on my Nintendo Switch)Two timeless games, one great collection. The Klonoa series is super underrated, and I hope lots of people buy this game so we could possibly get more Klonoa games. That would be awesome! Both of these games are fantastic and still hold up today, and while these remakes feel a bit low budget, the fun is completely intact, and you can feel the love and care put into this compilation. There are some things the originals do better (such as the cutscenes), and some things the remakes do better (such as the graphics), but you can't go wrong either way. The graphics are good, the music is great, the gameplay is simple bliss, the stories are immaculate, and the endings are emotional. I won't spoil anything, but you might want a box of tissues on hand. These games aren't that difficult, but in turn they are quite relaxing.Klonoa 1 is a remaster of the Wii remake, while Klonoa 2 is a brand new remake. New difficulty options have been added, graphics and character models have been updated, the English voice acting has been removed, and new side modes are included. The only omissions are the Reverse Mode, Character Viewer and alternate costumes from the Wii version. Please play these games, you won't regret it! And unless Namco remakes them as well, emulate the other Klonoa games. I'll give you a list of every other Klonoa game:- Klonoa: Empire of Dreams (GBA)- Klonoa Beach Volleyball (PS1/PSX)- Klonoa 2: Dream Champ Tournament (GBA)- Klonoa Heroes: Densetsu no Star Medal (GBA)- Kaze no Klonoa: Moonlight Museum (Wonderswan)Klonoa Heroes and Moonlight Museum are in Japanese only, but you can easily find fan-made English patches online. I would suggest that you only get the DLC if you're a big Klonoa fan though. I know I sure am, since I bought it. Klonoa is definitely one of my favourite series out there! Here's hoping for a Klonoa 3 in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR version: Klonoa just like you remember it, difficulty levels in case you need assistance, a optional 2P helper mode to give you a extra jump. Easy to start off before the final levels crank the difficulty up alot. Easy achievements to earn and perfect. Quality single-player platformer game with no added BS. As for price, think of it as £20 per game rather than a full £40.Personal note: We need more fun single-player games without live-services and micro-transactions, and these games are one of the few that i hope will prove just that, because no matter what corporate companies say, if a game is treated with love and care without greed in the forefront of their mind, if they stay true and pure to a games route, that's what makes a game feel like magic and a lot of fun. Bring on the rise to single-player games~Full version: I knew about Klonoa for a long time since the PS1 days, yet i never played the game fully, only the demo which i played multiple times, since then it had a second game on PS2 and even a remaster(?) on Wii/Wii U for the original. This game bundle comes with the first two games, the first one being a port of the Wii version i believe, and a upgraded graphic version of the second. Both games play near enouth the same, which is fine, you move, jump and briefly hover, and shoot a wind bullet, that's the entirety of your controls, simple and effective. The gimmick of the game is your wind bullet, shoot a Moo-Moo *I believe that's one of the basic enemy names* with a wind bullet, and you'll inflate it and carry it around with you, with it you can throw it as a projectile that does damage to enemies or used to break items around your throwing range, that's not just limited to left and right, you can even throw it towards and away from the screen as well, you can also use it as a double jump or to break/attack underneath you. Most stages will have gems to collect, which do carry other levels, with a max to earn being 150, 100 collected gems reward you with an extra life, aside from that there are 6 hidden *or clearly seeable but tricky to find* collectables, collect every single one and at the end you can unlock a hidden stage that'll put your abilities to the test. And honestly that's pretty much everything to the game.The ending for the first game, without going into detail, if you are weak of heart, just have some tissues on hand just in case, the second game isn't as emotional but it still has its moments.Overall i had a blast with the games, achievements were easy to earn, which i don't really care about, all i care about is a good game that is treated with respect, which thankfully is done with this, the game is just pure to its roots, a single player platformer game, nothing more, nothing less, no live-services or microtransactions *if you ignore the soundtrack, digital artbook and cosmetic hats since they give no effects whatsoever*, what most games needs to be nowadays in my opinion.I honestly say the price is just right for the games since i think of it as £20 each for both games, and its a happy nostalgia trip for me. I just hope and pray that wherever Klonoa ends up next, if ever, he'll be able to save the world from what its slowly becoming and make everyone happy. Wahoo~! *And if you want to go even further back, remember that Klonoa had a beach volleyball game on the PS1 after Klonoa 2, plus i think there was a gameboy game also but i cannot speak on that.*

_childDocuments_.review: Lighthearted and colourful, but not terribly thrilling. The pixel filter on Klonoa 2 is pretty and hides the edges of simple models, so imagination can do what the budget could not. That is one of few potential reasons to choose this iteration of the games over the originals.I appreciated the way that the platforming was grown around the grab-and-throw mechanic (throw enemies into others, at bosses, or downward for an extra jump), but I felt an additional element was needed for this basic formula to have a lasting appeal. Mario runs and jumps. Even in his first platformer, his ability to carry momentum into leaps made for an interesting expert experience and it remains appealing to this day. Klonoa is missing its "momentum" mechanic. It also lacks its Fire Flower. Level design gives the player puzzles to solve in a usually obvious but absolutely required way, which defeats the purpose of playing an acrobatic character in the first place. I feel like I am taking instructions from the environment rather than practising and innovating. Depth is missing.I like Klonoa's designs, and some of the areas are beautiful in motion. There was even one music track in the later part of the first game that I added to a playlist outside the game. But I did not ultimately find the gameplay engaging enough to play without having something to listen to in the background.

_childDocuments_.review: In this remaster, we follow the journey of Klonoa in his first game, Door to Phantomile, and his second game, Lunatea's Veil, in remastered HD. Both games do a fantastic job at providing fun and engaging puzzles, while also incorporating elements of action and adventure. The story of Door to Phantomile and Lunatea's Veil are what really put the icing on the cake for the two games. Door to Phantomile presents itself as a very happy-go-lucky platformer, where you must save the world from 'darkness'. We learn later that the game is much more than this. In Lunatea's Veil, Klonoa is more aware of himself and what he must do to help his friends. The second game hints at what our hero must do to rescue the world, and this task goes far beyond the, 'save the world by defeating the evil' trope.I highly recommend Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series, especially if you are someone that wants a fine introduction to the Klonoa games.

Klonoa 2 remaster is just a remaster of the OG PS2 version.Make sure to turn the tutorials OFF before playing each game, or you will get annoyed quickly. I'm also not a fan of that visual novel skip/fastforward button prompt that's permanently welded to the screen with each cutscene, how about GIVING THE OPTION TO TURN THAT OFF?!Klonoa veteran here... well, sort of. Then eventually played the fan translated Japanese exclusive games, also good.The remasters certainly look better than the originals... in certain areas. Then sometimes the characters are in cl_fullbright 1 mode and aren't lit correctly... like at all.Yo Namco, surely you'll port the rest of the games, yeah? _childDocuments_.review: These new versions are good for normies who don't know how to use emulators but for fans, just stick with the originals. Door To Phantomile is based on the godawful Wii remake, and while Lunatea's Veil is mostly faithful to the PS2 version despite the graphical overhaul, several facial animations are missing, and a few lines of dialogue are censored. This is still a great purchase for fans to see the unique differences, and LV is definitely a good alternative if you don't want to deal with the headache of making a PS2 function properly on a modern TV without having to deal with Composite AV, but the originals are still better, ESPECIALLY Door To Phantomile. It's downright criminal in the way the story was butchered on the Wii remake, and even though the dialogue and voice acting from the PS1 version were mostly restored, the cutscene animations are ported directly from the Wii and they still look terrible. They even swap to the Wii voices sometimes in certain cinematics and it just comes off as a heavily modded Wii version.I still recommend this collection for players new and old, because the games themselves are still excellent in their own right, with Lunatea's Veil specifically being one of the best sidescrollers ever made in my opinion. Not to mention we MUST convince Namco to make more Klonoa content. This franchise is really special to us fans for multiple reasons and it just gets treated so dirty by Namco. We were lucky to even get something like this at all, and more official content to expand on the lore set by the first two games would be a godsend. I still think you should play the originals first but Phantasy Reverie Series is definitely worth your time, if not for the interesting differences and a surprisingly good version of Lunatea's Veil.

_childDocuments_.review: I hope you don't mind me getting sentimental, but I've been a fan of Klonoa for nearly 7 years. I was around 12 at the time, and what started as me checking out this obscure 2000s series because i thought it looked cool, led to an unforgettable experience that has helped shaped me into who I am today and showed me just how effective video games can be as a storytelling medium. Ever since i got into this series, I've been hoping for this series to get a second chance, just one more shot in the spotlight.And here we are, with the release of Phantasy Reverie Series. Finally, an accessible way to officially purchase klonoa and support the franchise. it may not be the perfect way to experience these games, but it IS the perfect way for us to show bandai namco that we care about this series.Now if you don't know anything about Klonoa, all of this probably meant nothing to you, but I included it to show you just how much these games matter to me and everyone else who grew to love them. Klonoa isn't just a master class in platforming design, these two games are unforgettable experiences, with memorable characters, beautiful worlds, fantastic soundtracks and narratives that stick with you for the rest of your life. If you love platformers, cute games, games with good stories, or just games in general, i highly implore you to give klonoa a shot. You'd be surprised at what it can do to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for a Klonoa revival for a long time and its nice to see the franchise getting some love.I don't know how to describe it but, the little fella left a big impact on my teens although i've never finished the first game until yesterday.Beautiful and cute graphics with a powerful soundtrack. A delight to the eyes and ears.So far, the package its good, i'm going to start the second one.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: Great set of games!Unfortunately Klonoa 2 is worse than the first in literally every way but not to the point where it's bad, just lacking.The level design, story, gameplay elements, music all are either slight or significant downgrades.On top of that the zero post game content other than "hard mode" is just kinda disappointing even Klonoa 1 had at least an extra stage that was super challenging and fun.For that I'll say the first game is a solid 8.5/10 and the second is a 6/10Making the collection a rounded up 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: ...I hate having to write reviews like this...Minor spoilers I guess. This review is purely geared towards Klona: Door to Phantomile (1).---TLDR: If you want to support Klonoa and buy this game, great. But if you want to see why Klonoa is such a beloved and fun game, just play the original for PS1. I'm giving this a thumbs up just so people don't think this is a bad game. It's just a bad VERSION of the game. I used to play this, Tomba 2, and Jumping Flash 2 almost nonstop as a kid, so this review is probably biased af. But that's just how I see things. ---Graphically speaking I feel like a lot of the charm of the original game was stripped. I noticed certain boss animations were completely gutted for reasons I'm not sure, enemies just look different or were changed completely (the rat for example), level designs almost look flatter than they did on the PS1 which is odd so that whole 3D effect goes right out the window, and things like dust falling down from the platforms in 6-2 were missing as well. The missing loading animations between boss fights was also a sad loss.Sound wise, I hate it. I love that they used the original sound file for dialogue and such, it was perfect then and it's perfect now. But my god, for the stuff they decided to update they sure did butcher the ever living life out of it. It just doesn't have any life or character, stale static. Bosses seemed less interesting because the original sound effects apparently no longer met their standards. What happened to that nice crisp ring after you defeated one of the bosses? Nah, just silence now. A good example is the King Seadoph fight. It just sounds and feels so...empty. Speaking of which, why did they change the layout of the boss arena itself? Was that gap in the middle really considered too difficult? Just, what?I feel like this is more of a revision than it is a remake. This isn't the same game I played when I was a kid. Some levels are WAY different and have been dumbed down, the constant barrage of tutorial boxes is ridiculous, if you lose a boss fight ONCE they just flat out tell you what to do. Much like the new oddworld, crash, spyro, I quickly learned that "remake" just means "scambait". Klonoa had its time in the sun, and if this is what they consider a fleshed out Klonoa 2022 game should look like, I'd rather it live on in history via the PS1. Not even gonna touch on the "DLC"...just...RIP Klonoa, sorry they old yeller'd you.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good compilation overall. there's a few issues. Door to Phantomile kind of got the worst treatment, since it's based on the Wii Remake with some new visuals to be more like the ps1 original, and it doesn't really work sometimes, Klonoa's new model still uses the old Wii model animation rig so his arms constantly clip through his collor and it doesn't look great, the model is also a bit lifeless in some instances. The Bloom makes the game an eye Sore so i'd suggest turning it off. The colors are also kind of to saturated. There's also a lack of the mirror mode in Door to Phamtomile, but no one will really miss that. The audio is also a mixed bag for Door to Phantomile. The cutscene audio mostly uses the og ps1 recording which sound like crap and are not consistent with the fact that they use SOME Wii audio. the music is also compressed, i believe it's in Mono. Klonoa 2: Lunetea's Veil on the other hand was definitly given the better treatment. Only because it only needed higher quality models and cleaner texture work, the one downside is the lighting isn't as good as the ps2 original. But overall i must say... $40 is an absolute steal to get these hidden gems so that you don't have to pay $700 for the ps1 version of Door to Phantomile. or over $70 for the Wii remake or Klonoa 2 alone. IF this sells well enough, there is potential that Namco could see that there IS interest in this series. These games are very near and dear to many people's hearts, including mine. is I highly recommend it, despite it's flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend picking up this collection for some stellar platformers. BUT, if you want the best experience, I would recommend playing the PS1 version of the first Klonoa before playing this remake. The presentation, cutscene animation, and level design take considerable steps backwards compared to the original, which is a damn shame. There's still fun to be had here, and it can definitely be enjoyable, but the PS1 original is a near perfect game imo, so I would recommend firing up an emulator to play that version (which is incredibly easy to do). Klonoa 2 in this collection is great though, highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: While I was never able to pick up the originals and only played the Klonoa 2 demo 100 times over, I'm really happy that this HD remaster was released. It's a cute game with a lot of charm and a game you probably want to play as a die-hard platformer fan. I do have to say that I remember the game being more fun than it is. It's still fun, but it's definitely not the best out there. If the team decides to make a sequel, I really hope they make it to modern platformer standards and update/remove a lot of the outdated and not so fun mechanics.The characters are cute and the story is alright. I feel like the graphics are fine, but they're a bit over-saturated.Though I did hit recommend, I really with that Steam had a "maybe" button because I don't recommend against it, but I also wouldn't recommend it to my friends unless they could pick it up for 25 euros. I's a nostalgia cash grab. For a steep 50 euros you get 2 HD remasters, not remakes. This while beautifully remade games like Spyro & Crash were cheaper on release and have 3 games each. Added to that a "DLC" with costumes, an artbook and soundtrack (you don't even get the mp3/midi files) for 20 euros. What I also find incredibly annoying is the big "speed up" and "skip" buttons on the cutscenes. I'm happy you can skip them when you rerun a level but for Pete's sake at least hide these hideous buttons.If you're a die-hard fan of the series you've probably bought it, but if not I'd really wait for a sale. Also please don't buy the dlc, it's just a cash grab.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it on PS1, loved it on the Wiieeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee, and love it on PC now.This is by far the prettiest version, with an unlocked frame rate and high res support.Controls feel lag free to me (SN30 Pro 2), and my only minor complaint is that you can't manually set buttons, but there are two profiles which should suit either d pad/6 front button controllers like the M30, or diamond button layout controllers like Xbox. Both Analog stick and D pad work, thankfully. Because Klonoa's movement is not analog, having D pad support is a really good thing in my opinion.I have always loved the cheery overall soundtrack which has remained the same from the PS1 version - the game is just happy fun and leaves you in a good mood, smiling.For those who haven't played, it's an action platformer with mild easy puzzles and some exploration to find all the gems and artefacts per level (if you want to 100% it but it's not mandatory).I'm enjoying it immensely for the third time, and I have just tested the second game briefly to make sure it worked well also, but I never owned that one, so it will be all new to me. That was a PS2 exclusive game so it's great to see it re released for modern platforms! From what I can see it looks like more of the same, which is a good thing in Klonoa's case.No performance issues here with Razer laptop/3070M/11800H/G-SyncIf you look around there are a couple of legit stores doing an intro discount. I paid 33.99 USD which I think was very worth it.Note, these are not long games, 10 hours total playtime, or less, will get you through both of them, so it's up to you what kind of money you think that's worth.For me though, yes I recommend them, for sure. They are FUN! And fun is what gaming is about!
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: Buying this game is like a fundraiser for a new entry in a 30 year old series that has spent 14 years dormant because of the developers lack of care of the series (despite passionate outcry from fans for them to make a new entry for many years), except, as a thank you for donating to help the franchise continue existing and possibly get a new entry, they give you a well-made remaster of the main two games people fell in love with in the first place to go alongside it, for you to enjoy.Please buy this game to help the franchise continue existing in the future, Klonoa fans spent a long 14 years without any acknowledgement from Bandai Namco for this moment, if not buy it for that reason, buy it to experience what all these people are passionate in supporting, a great game franchise with a great story, world, characters, and gameplay. Please enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: These remakes are dissapointing. If you never played original you might like it and it's okay, but for those who did, this collection looks like a wasted potential. Games look both better and worse at the same time. I understand that high res textures and revisited models may look apealing but somehow the collection looks like it was made 10 years ago in a bad way.      If we talking purely technical aspect the game's graphics look bare bones, there are no modern lighting and shadows, anti-aliasing doesn't look good, models look weird and unpolished, and somehow game overall looks worse than PS1 prerenders. Game became easier and more forgiving even on normal difficulty which may be good for modern players but to me it seem unnecessary.      From artistic point games also took a weird aproach, adding more and showing less. Weather effects like brief rain in levels completely disappeared from the first game, and overall feel of levels are drastically different, where original looked best within limitations of original hardware and showed locations with various themes and and small deteails that doesen't steal your attention from what's going on on the screen, remake made locactions with almost the same lighting and brightness losing the concept of original feel of the levels and it's details sometimes are unnecessarily distracting like gems on the walls in the mines, not to mention oversaturated palette in every level even in dark and gloomy once. Characters look cheap and especially their textures, since most characters has blurry noses and other facial features that are shown up close. Camera shots also a lackluster. In original we see interior of Klonoa's house when he speak with his grandpa, and in remake they are on the porch for some reason. In level camera overviews are gone, and new cutscenes look really akward. I haven't played second game on PS2 so I don't have full picture, but from what I've seen my point still stands.      The game doesn't look bad but doesn't look graet eather. It's good that series are remembered but Namco really need to stop rushing their devs cause now they seem like a typical sweatshop that makes cashgrab games. I don't recommend buying this game for a fullprice, since devs themselves are not likely to get much money at all judging how Namco abusing it's staff last decade. Real shame, I used to wait for your releases, not anymore.       Also buying overpriced game just to show greedy publishers that you care, makes them feel justified in making cheap product for high price, since you'll buy it anyway.
