_childDocuments_.review: I originally decided to try out Klonoa to scratch my Kirby itch as I attempted to wean myself off of my Switch and transition to Steam Deck only. Unexpectedly, rather than being a replacement, Klonoa has carved his own special place in my heart. What seems like a simple story actually has an extremely emotional core. Both games included in Phantasy Reverie Series had me moved to tears by the end. Besides the story, the characters are lovable, the music is beautiful, and of course, the gameplay is very fun. In my opinion, Door to Phantomile starts out easy but gets more challenging towards the end, which prepared me for Lunatea's Veil and helped it to feel less difficult but still fun throughout. I really enjoyed the puzzles and platforming challenges in both games.All that to say, if you are considering getting this game, do it. I'll never forget my experience playing it for the first time. It's left me eager to try out other previously released Klonoa games and hoping that we will get a Klonoa 3 someday.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: Dead honest, I think the original 1997 PS1 Door to Phantomile is still the best version. Since this is a remaster of the Wii version, some of the charm is lost by not having those incredibly beautiful pre-rendered PS1 cutscenes, especially the one when Cress rises and the one at the end. I will also warn you that the hitboxes in Door to Phantomile can be a bit... imperfect, shall we say.HOWEVER, they made the chad choice to use the OG PS1 audio, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ does it sound great. And the music on my modern headphones is an absolute treat. The music in DtP was always bangin' from start to finish, but I love hearing it on a pair of quality headphones instead of from the TV. And while I think some of the charm is lost, I still adore this game.As for Lunatea's Veil, there's really nothing changed here save for the buttery frame rate and upscaled resolution. But it already had a pretty timeless look, and it's still just as fun to play here as it was on PS2. I was stoked when they announced this remaster, and I'm glad I was not disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: ~BENEFITS~~Klonoa: Door to Phantomile-Phantasy Reverie Series~Fun gameplay similar to the original Klonoa: Door to Phantomile.Epic level design that fits with your pace of playing.Good music you'll want to listen to all of the time.Characters are cute, memorable and endearing. (The villains are of impeccable design)New modes to play in and a two player feature that can be quite fun.Fun to play if you're casual or serious!~Klonoa 2 Lunatea's Veil-Phantasy Reverie Series~Very close to the original Lunatea's Veil.A fresh adventure that is as amazing as it's predecessor.Characters are likable and playful but somehow holds down a serious tone.It spices things up with snowboarding segments.Normal levels are vast and a joy to explore.~DOWNSIDES~~Klonoa: Door to Phantomile-Phantasy Reverie Series~Easier than the original. (even on normal mode)There are tips that pop up on the screen constantly. (However you can remove them via the options screen)The first boss Rongo Lango, has his textures mapped incorrectly.Some of the NPCs (Jugpot soldier,Pamela,Karal,Grandpa,Huepow) are from the Wii remake that doesn't match the original art style.The colors and bloom effects can sometimes obscure the characters facial expressions/mouths.Expressions of main characters are out of kilter and do not give the emotional story justice.Most if not all of the dialogue has been unnecessarily and bizarrely edited, they should have simply kept the original dialogue.(it now feels like I'm trying to read a run-on sentence poorly translated into English.)The dialogue auto scrolls, it pauses on short phrases and quickly skips long sentences.(Very irritating if you are trying to enjoy the story at a slower pace.)The music often loops incorrectly and plays at the wrong time during important sequences.The roof of Klonoa's house changed to blue instead of the original orange. (why? Now it blends in with the windmill.)~Klonoa 2 Lunatea's Veil-Phantasy Reverie Series~As with Phantasy Reverie's Door to Phantomile remake, this also suffers from over saturation and heavy bloom.Klonoa's mouth and eyelids do not emote in certain situations that are integral for us to understand Klonoa's personality.A small amount of textures are looped oddly, but nothing majorly jarring.Leorina's outfit was changed to purple instead of the original blue. (why?)~CONCLUSION~Klonoa was like a phantom until it was unveiled to many with Phantasy Reverie Series releasing.While it does have inherent flaws that are annoying to longtime fans of the original games (such as myself) it holds up as a remake of two amazing games that will hopefully never be forgotten again, and to be enjoyed by a new generation of Klonoa fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: This bundle from the early 2.5D platformer era is a really cute game, with the PS1 first game updated with the Wiimake's visuals but none of the other problems that plague that version. First game feels like Kirby x Mario 2's long lost lovechild and the second game adds a bit of Crash Bandicoot-esque early 2000s game energy.  Overall I liked the first game more than the second, but they're both solid and competent platformers worth your time for a quick romp. Quick being the operative word, because both games are quite short, but what's there is quite good so I don't mind (100% achieves in 12 hours short). Both games being bundled together is a great marketing decision that makes it still feel worth your money despite the lack of longevity in the individual games. Expect a good time, not a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: I almost decided not to recommend this one for reasons I'll get into in a moment... but I'm going to recommend it anyways because at the end of the day, if you've never played the Klonoa games this is likely the easiest way to get into the original two stories in the modern day and age, plus if there's enough interest it may inspire some more Klonoa releases sooner rather than later.HOWEVER, if you already own the originals and can still play them, this remake is going to infuriate you. It's not as bad as when they tried to remake the first game on the Wii, but they got too creative with camera angles in the cinematics, all of the subtleties are missing, the graphical effects are surprisingly bland compared to the original games, the controls are not perfect as there's weird delays which can cause your jumps not to fire as reliably as in the original, and ALL of the collision volumes have been made tighter, causing a massive spike in difficulty in some of the least expected spots.As a game, it's not bad, but as a remake it completely misses the mark in every way. :(
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: 2 Klonoa games made their way from the 2000s to 2023. That's enough to recommend this cult classic Bandai game.Klonoa still lives up to its glory as a 2.5d Platformer with a gimmick of grabbing enemies to throw their corpses and jump higher (don't think of the moral implications too much). The story hits just as strong as it did when I was a kid, and the bonus levels and no damage boss runs are still the hardest things in gaming for me. There's something in this game for everyone, from the aesthetic cute mascot characters, collect-a-thon nature of some levels, and casual nature of the game as a whole. Here are some issues in Phantom Reverie (I played this on the Wii, the version this is based on, and have played the original on the PS1)- Klonoa's jump height is fixed. I had to check with my old console version, but in classic and Wii to an extent, you could control jump to manuevre through obstacles easier, with level design clearly built around it. This makes the game frustratingly more difficult, especially with the on-rails surfing sections and last levels so timing must be precise. - Wind Bullet attack has a smaller hitbox. Should have been hotfixed. - A small of input delay. I see some reviews attributing this to the change from sprites to 3D models. This is not a big issue, but if you get to/know of the infamous levels.... every little delay matters. I could not notice issues with Lunateil's Veil other than what I think is input delay. Nothing big. That being said, the game carries over the annoying on rails skateboarding elements which are very difficult to control and infuriating for completionists. I wish this was amended to have a better brake button or better ways to control. The big issue is really just the floaty finnicky controls and a camera issue that is unforunately inherent to 2.5 platformers. If you're obsessed with completionist, fair warning it's not worth it. Also, don't bother with the DLC. The music box can only be played in game, is unlocked after bonus stage anyways, and the costumes are purely aesthetic. (Monkeycraft, pleas let us have mp3 and FLAC files!) Use the DLC money to buy for a friend when it''s on sale instead. For all the issues this game has, those are all that I have. I honestly hope this game's revival can hopefully gather fans new and old. Klonoa has such a simple but vivid story and unique twist on platformers that no other game I can think of has done that I can't not recommend it. If the advert/promo video intrigues you in the slightest, you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so this my introduction to Klonoa, so I'm gonna rate this without knowing how the original games are like, but this was an amazing experience. Everything was just so pleasant from the moment I started. Short but really sweet (and honestly we need more short games these days imo). The puzzles were really creative; challenging but not too difficult. The level design was also really well executed too, being a side-scrolling platformer that really took advantage of it being a 3D game. And the stories are really great too. Phantomile was especially emotional for how short it was, but Lunatea was still really delightful. I'd like to go back someday to 100% this game cuz of how fun it was. While the backtracking is done really well, I did sometimes get annoyingly lost. With this being a remake, they could've made a couple of small adjustments to prevent that from happening. But overall a really great couple of 2.5D platformer games. I think they should try making an open world Klonoa game honestly because it seems like they wanted to have that vibe but had to work with limitations.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play these games as a kid, and had minimal experiences with the games as an adult via emulation etc, tho I grew up with the PS1 and its one of my favorite consoles, the PS2 is up there too. I think these are pretty great remasters/remakes, a decent amount of options and such. It's hilarious theres a guy complaining below about tutorials and things being "bright" when you can turn them off, and change the bloom and some other options. Would have been nice with a few more PC centric options, but it does alright as far as that goes. Visuals look great to me, framerate is pretty stable, though I had some tearing without Vsync even though im on a VRR laptop and the AA apparently is broken, but both can be fixed, along with the  facial animations for Klonoa 2 apparently which if youre like me you wont care.As someone with some familiarity with the series, but no "nostalgia" or anything, its great. My only real issue was with the first game the controls are a little stiff and maybe had some lag, but that could be with my Vsync issues and I was lazy using a BT controller. In Klonoa 2 it felt a bit tighter which is good. But I finished the first game on normal so idk, wasnt that bad. Def worth it overall, fun 2.5D platformers, the second one (havent finished) already seens better in every way. I still can't get over that other review... it's hilarious listening to people complain about legally owning a game that obviously had a ton of effort put in at the least, does exactly what it says, and menu options solve 50-100% of the claimed issues... and now you can go play the dang emulated version if you have that much of a problem lol. Dont think Namdai Bando will care if you purchased this lol.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic remaster of the two main games in the Klonoa franchise. Both are extremely faithful to the originals, with the Door to Phantomile remaster actually being made to resemble the PS1 source material more than the Wii remake did. Highly recommended for anyone who wants to experience the games again, or those who want a great simple to learn, hard to master platformer game with cute characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: Really had a blast playing this. A great port of solid 2D platforming from a bygone era that really scratches the itch for that type of game, even when you don't know you have it. Completely sucked me into its gravity, I ended up 100%'ing the game. The extra stages as rewards for collecting all the citizens/dolls are absolute joys to play. At a sale price of 75% off, it's a no brainier. $40 is a little steep for a game this short.Klonoa 3 please. The streets need it. Shoutout to Running Shine for putting me on to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: First thing you see after company logos is a yes or "no" page asking if it's okay for them to collect data + your location. Off to a great start. First thing I do is head to the options to adjust it for my display, as it boots in windowed 720p by default. I'm rocking a 1050 Ti at the moment but it should be fine, a target platform is Switch and the PS1 original ran at an almost unbroken 60FPS throughout its entire playthrough. Ah, nope. There's the.. what? Why is it running at like 30FPS lol. Oh well, lowered resolution, now it's 40FPS. What? Put settings to minimum. Still 40. Uh... Okay. Restart game, now it's running 60FPS... except not really, it has awful microstuttering every second or so. Great. Oh well, let's look at the costumes. Oh, the costume I mean. The rest are all tucked away behind a $20 DLC bundle.Environments look flatter than the PS1 game, there's an obnoxious "X TO SKIP" prompt on every cutscene that's 100% opaque and distracting. Any nitpicks I had with Spyro Reignited or Crash NSane are utterly microscopic compared to this, and those all had 3 games for the same price and other cool new features. Please at least attempt to give a s#it Bamco.EDIT: The more I see the worse the PS2 remake looks compared to the original. I'm immensely disappointed and expected a lot better from something they're asking $40; would've preferred a straight port over this.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: Both Door to Phantomille and Lunatea's Veil provide excellent 2D Action/Platforming fun. Klonoa is a great 90's/2000's platforming protagonist and the levels have some fantastic design with fun segments and bright, colorful graphics. The music is great too and both stories get surprisingly deep for a game of this type. While Klonoa 1 has a bit of jank with a few of the final levels and the Wind Bullet should probably have a slightly bigger hitbox, but that is a minor blemish on an otherwise fantastic set of games. The achievements here are not super challenging but can still be a bit demanding for those who love challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: It may only take about 6 or 7 hours to get all the trophies between both games and the story might be a bit simple, but the puzzle platforming 2.5D gameplay makes this game one of the best games I've ever played, both as a remaster and for nostalgia. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Had never played the games before these remasters, ended up loving them to the point that i 100%ed them both.Never played these games as a kid, most i saw was a picture of the main character and the title in magazines but I'd always heard good things. Finally gave the series a try and man I'm so glad I did.First game was a fun time, some really cool level designs that must've been super ahead of their time when they came out. the hitboxes for grabbing enemies can sometimes be a little finicky but then again i chose to play on "normal" which doesn't extend the range of the air shot like the "easy" mode does. Game was pretty chill and easy until the last portions of the game when they threw in a bit of challenge which was a nice change of pace, and saving all the people gets you a neat challenging little time trial course. Second game was a fantastic time, it really took the mechanics of the first game and polished them to be much more precise and fast. Had some challenging bits (mostly towards the end) but it was a blast throughout. I like the music a lot in the first game but the music in this one is even better in my opinion. Pretty much everything is better in this version from the character design, to the story, to the platforming variety and thanks to the always enjoyable snowboarding sections that make quite a few appearances in the story. I would've loved both of these games as a kid if I'd given them a chance, I just honestly barely saw either of these games in stores or at friends' houses and they completely passed me by. If you like platformers like Kirby but with a little more emphasis on precision then you'll definitely have a good time with either of these games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is based off Klonoa 1 so farThe Good:- Environments look spectacular- A lot of the character models fixed from the ugly Wii designs-If you die after rescuing a villager, they'll still be rescued when you respawnThe Bad:- Wind Bullet has extremely short range from what I remember and sometimes simply doesn't hit/grab things even if you're right on top of them. Also if you're on a slope it hits the ground as opposed to the enemy literally 2 inches from you.- The double-jump is a little inconsistent sometimes- The knockback from enemies is way too much. In the original game you'd go back the length of made 1/2-2/3 of Klonoa's width at most. Here, you go ROCKETING back sometimes to like 2-3 TIMES his width leaving you to either miss a platform or fall into pits- Inconsistent dubbing: Most lines are clearly ripped straight from the PS1 game without so much as a decompression or touching up (I'm not an audio engineer so I'm not sure if there was much that could be done about it) whiile other lines are re-dubbed by the new voice actors.  Why not just redub the whole thing instead of this weird halfway point? I'd gladly take a full redubbing in Phantomilan to fit the more modern graphics than hearing crunchy PS1 voices coming out of HD character models.- Unlike the PS1 game where cutscenes were like a visual novel where you push a button to go to the next line of dialogue, here, they're on a sort of auto-pilot leaving a LOT of pausing in between nearly every single line of dialogue. This is where, again, a full redub would have beneffited them as recycling the old PS1 lines while using the Wiis timing for the cutscenes leaves empty space as one was recorded with the VN style word progression in mind while the other was animated with an entirely different dub in mind- Klonoa's facial animation in a certain scene is utterly dissonant from the mood. He's supposed to be super sad but when not talking he merely looks tired and when he is talking....HE SMILES!!! Sure an argument could be made that he's trying to force a smile but in the context of the scene, he's at his lowest point in the story so far. He shouldn't be smiling!Other minor nitpicks:-Sometime sounds like boss grunts and bubbles popping don't play-Joka and Ghadius don't taunt you when you get hurt in their fights which takes a bit of the charm awayOverall while it is dodgy in some ways, it's still one of of not my favorite platformers ever and I'm so excited to have it back again.

_childDocuments_.review: Klonoa: Door to Phantomile is my favorite console game ever. I've been obsessed with it for years and was really excited that it finally got enough recognition to warrant a remaster. Unfortunately, I don't recommend this to anyone who adored the original. So many minor changes and creatives liberties that make the game feel unrecognizable to me. There's WAY too many pop ups explaining every tiny little detail about how the game works which is entirely unnecessary. I played the original at age 6 without a tutorial and figured it out. Part of the fun of Klonoa is discovering how things worked by playing instead of reading a tooltip for literally anything that moves. They also appear to have made all the boss fights easier, which were not challenging to begin with. I played until the second boss where they removed a gap that you'd normally have to navigate over which would result in death if failed. By the 4th level I had noticed changes on every single level and requested a refund. I also had a lot of technical issues getting my controller to work properly which was unique to this game. Additionally, the screen resolution was not functioning properly and causing my 2nd monitor to bug out rendering it unusable while playing. This feels like a very lazy cash grab. There is no love for the original, it's "close enough". If you've never played Klonoa before you may enjoy it but if you're looking for the same experience the PS1 version offered you will be very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Klonoa is a remake/remaster of an old side-scrolling platformer from the 90s. Without much awareness of the game's history, I wouldn't be surprised if it pioneered a variety of gameplay options that made it a stand-out game at the time (hence it getting a remake). The controls are fairly simple, with a  short-range grab of an enemy being the primary non-movement ability. Once an enemy is grabbed, they can be used to double jump (it's a 90s game, so double jump wasn't ubiquitous) or thrown as a projectile, and occasionally other abilities.This seems like a solid revamp. The graphics are good, it seems to play pretty smoothly, and I can tell that the music has been redone so that it's not... whatever it would have been like originally. I think I'd be pretty happy to see other revamps handled similarly. Seems bug-free.There are some genuinely challenging platforming components, even by modern standards.Character design is coolLook, it's an 90s game. That's not to say that there isn't awesome stuff that has been made in this time period, it's just that the overall feel of the game is a little dated (The baseball cap and boarding segments especially). It'd probably be amazing if I had nostalgia to boost me along, but I never played the original so that's fairly lost on me.The second game is notably better than the first. If it'd continued making games, it's clear it learnt a lot over its time, so maybe a future one would be another full step forwards.There are collectables with no real reward for fully collecting them. However, they are often  hard to collect all of them due to arbitrary time restrictions, so if you're a perfectionist and like a challenge...Price. Frankly, this is the primary reason I give this a do not recommend. It's ludicrously expensive for a short playtime, and even with the 75% off sale it still feels more expensive than it should be. Sure, it's a nice remaster, but the story and gameplay itself is very blah.If you're aiming for a true perfect complete, good luck! You need to get  to succeed, and the timing on some of these requires absolute perfection with no lee-way whatsoever. Also it's totally irrelevant.The price of this is really the primary reason to knock this down. If the sale price was the actual price, I'd still wait for a sale. I can imagine it'd be awesome if you'd played the original for the nostalgia, but coming from a fresh perspective, the gameplay feels dated considering the other quality platformer titles around. It just feels like a not especially remarkable Kirby knock-off.

_childDocuments_.review: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series comprises of two games, KLONOA: Door to Phantomile and KLONOA 2: Lunatea’s Veil!  From the main menu screen, you can choose which of the two games to play, after which you will be able to choose the games difficulty. Both games have an Easy and Normal difficulty, an easy game allows you to start a game with maximum Hearts (Five) these are your health and you’ll lose some health through damage.  Damage is another thing which is determined by the game's difficulty, on Easy, damage is reduced by one third. Once all hearts have been reduced of their health you will then lose a life. Easy game allows you to have an infinite number of lives. A normal game gives you a starting number of three hearts, damage is reduced by half and you only have three lives to start with. Klonoa uses a magic ring to fire Wind Bullets which fly further in easy mode but in normal mode they fly the same as they did in the original game. Both games play basically the same, you make your way through a Vision (game level) collecting Dream Stones, freeing Dreamers you are trapped in their nightmares. Each of the visions will have varying obstacles and enemies in your way. Using the Wind Ring you’re able to grab hold on an enemy and use it in multiple ways depending on your current situation. Grabbed enemies can be used against other enemies and obstacles by throwing them. Some enemies are covered in armour so they’ll require two thrown enemies to vanquish them. Obstacles such has levers can be activated; boxes can be destroyed allowing you to pass by throwing an enemy in their direction. You can also use the enemy to perform various other actions than throwing them. You can grab them and then perform a double jump allowing you to reach higher ground. Different enemies can be used for different things, some will allow you to fly, others will fire you high above the world or hang you in the air. Springboards, cannons and other items can help you to navigate your way through each of the visions. The visions that you visit will have themes, forests, city rooftops, amusement world and others. While you make your way through these visions, you’ll meet some characters who may need your help and could help you on your travels. However, there are also some characters which will try and stop you from completing your missions. They will try anything to stop you and at times you will be confronted by a Boss. Defeating the boss will allow you to move onto the next Vision area. The boss fights usually have you running around a centralised baddy and you grabbing and throwing enemies at them while dodging the boss's attacks. There are scattered around some Ngapoko Eggs which can hide some item of value inside, at times you may even find a rare item once the egg is broken. Not all eggs are visible but you can spot where they are by the shadow they cast on the ground, so keep your mince pies open. Collecting one hundred Dreamstones will give you an extra life and if you find and free a Mirror Spirit it will double the number of dreamstones collected for a short period of time.  The game can be played with two players using Support Mode, this will then allow the second player to play as Klonoa’s sidekick. In the settings there’s options for Display - Window Type, Resolution, Antialiasing, V Sync, Textures, Shadows, Depth of Field and Bloom. Sound - Background Music, Sound Effects and Voice Volume Sliders. Controls - Control Pre-Sets and Custom Keyboard and Mouse as well as Game Pad Binds. I did have a couple problems with playing Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series, the first being unable to make some jumps, more so in the first game. It would seem I could jump high enough but I would not be able to grab the ledge in order to move on. So, I was stuck trying to move forward, I’d be flapping about at where I’m supposed to be but I would just not grab the ledge for some reason. Sometimes you could get passed like the time with a big Moo on a rope bridge, a nicely times jump over him and a flapping of my tabs and I could pass, however, that’s not always possible and can leave you stranded until you can get the jump right.  I found the second game a bit easier in its execution and the overall feel of the game was better than the first. The other problem I had was again in the first game and it was the Wind Bullets. I would have to get up real close to the enemy if I was to grab them when using the wind bullets. This would cause me to lose plenty of health and at times die, sending me back to the start of the vision where I might get stuck again trying to make a jump. Other than that, the games are nice, they aren’t really that hard to play. The graphics and stories are good and you can play with two people via split screen co-op. Positives  + Nice graphics + Two games in one + Enjoyable game + Has achievements + Has cards Negatives  - Some jumps frustrating to make - Wind bullets not travelling very far Help Klonoa and friends save the world in the 25th anniversary remastered games in Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I randomly came across this game for the very first time during the Bandai-Namco sale about two months ago and it was the best game discovery I’ve made since seeing my brother’s Half Life 2 case got me back into PC gaming 10 years ago. I’ve been completely obsessed with the series since then, and I’ve been playing both this package and also all the original versions and spin-offs I can find (Klonoa Beach Volleyball being a surprise favourite of mine; trust me, it’s much better than it sounds). I’ve listened to some of the soundtracks so much that I’m now bored of them.I’d recommend this package to essentially everyone, but there are one or two things to consider, especially if you’ve played the original versions:- The package is quite expensive (£40), but its sale price (£24) is perfectly reasonable. Bear in mind however that original copies of Klonoa 1 and 2 go for £130 and £40 respectively, and that’s assuming you still have a PS2 and preferably a CRT TV. For some reason, it’s currently (Christmas 2022) on sale on the Humble Bundle but not Steam, and if I have no idea if this is a mistake or not.- This package is almost hands-down the definitive way to play Klonoa 2 (but make sure you disable bloom in settings to tone down the over-brightness and white objects' glowing), but the remake of Klonoa 1 is much more controversial. The remake of Klonoa 1 here is the Wii remake made to look more faithful to the original, resulting in a mish-mash of the original and Wii remake which both keeps and removes good and bad things from both versions. Thus you could make a case for all three versions being the best. In fact, I’d recommend also trying to play the original version of Klonoa 1 in some way. Unfortunately, there is no way to do this in Europe which is both cheap and legal, but in America and Japan you can get it on the PS3 store, I think for $7.- The wind ring (the weapon Klonoa uses) works slightly differently and requires more precision in the remakes, and the jumping can be a bit awkward in Klonoa 1 (I’ve run off the edge of platforms earlier than expected multiple times).Of course, none of these things are too much of a concern if you’re new to the series. Play all the versions you feel like and come to your own conclusion. But please buy this remake; it’s the second time Bandai-Namco have tried to bring Klonoa back from the dead, and if this fails he will never be coming back.P.S. When playing Klonoa 1, I’d strongly consider pausing the game at the following points and watching the original CGI cutscenes on Youtube instead: the opening cutscene, after Vision 5-2, and the ending cutscene after Final Vision (NOT Vision 6-2). The original’s three CGI cutscenes are much better and more impactful than the remake's in-engine replacements.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. It has that undeniable charm of the original Playstation era in its soothing music, beautiful backgrounds and hearty story. But with that comes another thing, jankiness and unresponsiveness befitting of a game that, despite being based on a 2008 remake, is definitely still from 1997. Vision 6-1 and 6-2 turned a good game on its head I feel and didn't scale at all accordingly to prior levels. They are uncharacteristically difficult compared to the Visions prior which I thought were fantastic in their back and forth platforming and level verticality. I would normally appreciate the challenge, I mean ♥♥♥♥ it was only a few months ago I got all achievements for Helltaker which is unimaginably harder than this. But that spike in difficulty is not overcome by skill because its created by a game with unresponsive controls (jumps consistently not registering), enemy placements done for no reason other than to spite you and more importantly what seems to be a very inconsistent hitbox that restricts you from grabbing enemies on time (which is a MUST for these levels). I paid £15 for this collection and have been waiting to play since the demo last year so I obviously don't quit lightly here. But it annoyed me to high heavens man and I thought what with a "remaster" some of these things would've gotten a little gloss.

_childDocuments_.review: You give an honest review, talk about the state of the game, even the differences between the PS1/PS2/Wii versions, talk about the pricing, and somehow someway, someone will gift you clown awards as they feel like it's a personal attack on their game, don't like someone else's opinion, or they are too afraid they will never see another release.It's one of those ''If steam had a Mixed rating'' instead of negative/positive.Since it is on sale, i decided to buy it again and give it another chance after i refunded on day release. I still witness stutters within game, although less frequent  you still get them, but not enough to detract from the game play like on day 1. Aliasing is still rather bad, but if you go to the options and enable the pixel filter, it does help a lot to make the game look more natural and it even adds more detail to the game. The games don't pack the same punch or detail they once did on previous consoles, but if your new to the franchise you will likely enjoy it. The game feels like it could of been so much more, they could of added the original PS1 version of the game and the volley ball version as a bonus or even the GBA versions of the game, but sadly it is just Klonoa 1 and 2. At full price it is a hard pass for me, but i have the luxury of playing the originals and the Wii version. My friend who is also a retro game enthusiast loved the game, but he couldn't get his hands on the originals and so badly wanted to play them, so he bought the game for the switch and said how nice it is to own them both in one place to play on the go and they felt really good to him.  Previous review Never have i witnessed reviews begging people to buy a game because they don't want a franchise to die. So many of the reviews for this game can not be taken seriously.This review is based off Klonoa one only.I do not care for the second.Runs awful. Stutters a lot. The fps is up and down more then a yoyo. And if you can take the time to do a side by side of the wii version vs this you can see that this version is inferior. No aliasing, Shadows missing off objects, details missing,literally moss on rocks on the wii version is gone on this version, loads of tiny little things that bring the game to life are gone.The wii remake is a graphical upgrade from the original and is a graphical upgrade from this version as well!!!! that say's a lot. It is unity , so i should of expected a mess,i have refunded. I wouldn't even recommend on a sale unless it was under half the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe I am living in a mini-pocket universe or some sick developer tailor made a horrible version of the real game just for me.Everyone I know loves this series AND these remasters, and I would love to understand why. I played both games until full completion and I absolutely hated every single minute of it.The presentation, visuals, music, level design, everything is so mediocre it hurts.On top of that, the gameplay is straight up broken; Klonoa shoots his lightbeam about a toenail away from his body and it lingers less than a microsecond; and the levels DO NOT accomodate for this kind of limitation. There are SO many jumps I have missed over not having the most perfect microtiming possible and shooting a balloon bird in the air a frame earlier. The game had me constantly dying over things that absolutely felt unfair, I seriously struggle less on 2D platformers that are "advertised" as difficult compared to this.I would not recommend this game, ESPECIALLY for its high pricetag........... but it has its fans for a reason. I adore 2D mascot platformers, DKC being one of my favorite video game series of all time.... so it's not like I dont like the genre either.Total respect if you dig this game, but just because I respect it, does not mean I understand it in the slightest. _childDocuments_.review: Three words: obvious, criminal, and ironic.It is obvious that Bandai Namco doesn't care about this title. If they did, they wouldn't give it to a non-existing studio with, I strongly assume, zero budget to work with. They had PLENTY of time to give this game the proper attention it needs, but they didn't. While textures can be nice here and there, this game is otherwise so, SO unpolished and unoptimized, to the extent that at plenty of occasions, the originals (1998 and 2001 games) look better. So much so that it is criminal.It is criminal, to give this game so little care, in spite of it being already under the hood for so many years, and then on top of it, have the audacity to sell it for 50 euros. There's a small community that still held this title dearly in their hearts, waiting for all these years for something to come to light. Me, I don't want to know if Namco acknowledged this demographic in making this game. Maybe it's for the best.Alas, it is also ironic, that either in their incompetence or enigmatic self-awareness, they left the sound of these games largely untouched. For me, it is the only reason this game is playable. I believe Klonoa 2, in particular, is a wonder when it comes to sound. Everything from the incredible soundtrack to the little sound effects make this game pure magic.Maybe I didn't mention it, but since you've reached this far, I'll tell you this: it is painful. It is painful because I can vividly envision how this game COULD be, and the reality of how it ended up, the two crashing into one another like two planets. Because one can still see, like a mystical stream flowing through time, the passion and the talent of the people who worked on it, some of whom are sadly, not in this world anymore. It is painful, to know that their modern legacy comes in the form of an unfinished, halfhearted dream.TL;DR: for those who've played this game, DON'T buy it at full price.For those who've never played it... I can't say anything. I'd say play the original, but good luck with that.

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts out fine, nice relaxing colourful platformer until you get to the later levels where the game does everything in its power to be as annoying as possible.Klonoa is deceptive, it fools you into thinking it's going to be a fun chill platformer when in reality it's a frustrating ordeal.The platforming seems interesting at first but in later levels you begin to loathe how specific every maneuver is when they start requiring you to time everything perfectly to progress.Not only that but there's enemies that are constantly respawning and it's difficult to see where they will land... could be on top of you and you'd have no idea.On top of this there's so much vague ♥♥♥♥ in this game in terms of progression that it begs the question of whether it's worth finishing it. Like this game is supposedly short, had to use a guide because of how annoying vague the game can be at times but the last few levels make me want to rage quit. I cannot fathom what went through the developers minds when they made some of these levels, the whole game just becomes troll game design central when you reach the later levels and it's really annoying, it's like the developers recognized that the core mechanics weren't working so made everything cheap to annoy you.That's what they game feels like to play.Now sure the game can be beaten relatively easily if you just keep throwing yourself at it but is that fun? No it isn't. It's just annoying. Play Kirby 64 instead, it's a better version of what this game tries to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly have no idea why Klonoa is considered a classic. I played through the first game until the boss fight with Joka, and really, it's pretty awful. Enemy design is obnoxious, level design ranges from mediocre to infuriating, bosses are awful (with Joka being a particularly terrible fight). If you're a completionist, the game is even worse, as gathering all 150 gems in each stage is a tremendous pain in the ass, with every stage having sections where you have to activate a gem doubler a grab a bunch of nearby gems before it runs out. This wouldn't be awful, except the timing on these is far too tight (apparently much tighter than in the original game). Combine this with many areas where there are missable gems and no quick way to restart at a checkpoint if there's not a convenient instant kill pit available, it just makes getting 100% a terrible slog.I quit after the Joka boss fight, that was my limit, and honestly, I doubt I'll go back to try Klonoa 2. Screw this game, I'm glad the series is dead.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't even gotten to the second game in this collection and I'm floored. This is easily the cheapest, most low-quality piece of crap shovelware I've ever seen sold for $40, and it's a disgrace to the Klonoa series. This is coming from someone who's never even played the original games, I just know they have to be better than this garbage. Strip away the beloved IP, and all you're stuck with is a poorly made, overly demanding Unity game with the same level of love and care graciously put into Rise of Kong.First of all I want to say how incredibly poor the performance is. My first impression of the game was fantastic; inconsistent 40 FPS, visuals that look worse than the Nintendo Switch, and PC fans going off like crazy. Not even in game by the way, this is a cutscene. Or, it was before I had a system crash. Yup! Didn't even get in-game on my main PC before it killed itself. Rest of the game I've been forced to play on my Steam Deck, where it...runs! Poorly. It still heats the machine to high hell - I've never seen the poor thing so stressed in my life. So, fantastic, the game's performance is so poor that I can barely play it to begin with. Off to a great start!Getting in game, I can't help but notice the game's level design is...poor. So, very, extremely poor. I can only assume I'm near the end of the game, and there hasn't been one level that I've had fun on. Luckily, the game's story, as many have said, IS quite captivating, and the only thing that stopped me from refunding this trash. I'm hesitant to make this critique since I'm pretty sure the level designs are mostly taken directly from the original, but...GOD, they are SO unfun to play. Who thought any of this was fun? Who playtested this? And then we get to where I am. A big Joka boss fight. The fight was going kinda poorly and I was getting frustrated, when as if to add salt onto the wound...the game froze. The whole system! Great! Can't escape this happening anywhere, I guess! Jesus tapdancing Christ Bandai Namco, this is shameful. FORTY DOLLARS, the game runs like crap, looks like crap, sounds like crap (all of the audio is compressed beyond recognition lmao, didn't even bother remastering it), plays like crap...I have no words. It's such a colossal failure on so many levels. Story is legitimately the  thing it EVER got right.Now, I know why this game is so highly rated. Namco's actually paying attention to the series! We may get a new game! I can totally understand the hype around something like that! This is crap. This is a cheaply thrown together Unity hackjob that was made with a budget of two paperclips and a water bottle. I understand you want to see another game in the series, but I promise you if this is indicative of what Klonoa 3 will be, it is going to be a colossal disappointment. We can only hope and pray Namco doesn't take this game's success as a sign that they don't have to try anymore. Shame on you, Namco.

_childDocuments_.review: Overwhelmingly positive? For this? No, not by a long shot! The whole gimmick of using enemies to overcome obstacles is an intriguing idea, but eventually becomes annoying due to the repetitive nature of this game's design. Especially in later levels this becomes incredibly infuriating when you have to perform pixel-perfect actions to proceed. Having to not only abide by the game’s monotone playstyle but also the lack of variety, inevitably takes the joy out of it. And of course, every level has precisely one and only path for you to tread upon, making it even more boring. If you played one level, you played them all. Increasing the difficulty or even the length by an absurd degree doesn’t make it any more interesting, it further amplifies the annoyance factor. All of this paired with the fact that this entire experience would normally cost me 50€ is pure theft. Everyone who finished 6-2 knows the utter misery that comes out of this game. Having to force myself through a level because I don’t want to restart it from scratch really says it all. The only variety to the tedious gameplay were the few snowboarding levels in the second game. Although nothing special, it was a relief that I didn’t have to play another level clustered with annoying puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Foreword: I have never played the original versions of the Klonoa games, so this remake is my first approach to the series.That said, despite not being without flaws, I enjoyed my time with everyone's favourite cabbit, so much so that I got all the achievements (not a difficult task, but still...).So, what can I say about this Phantasy Reverie Series?PROS:+ GAMEPLAYAs many gamers know, the fundamental aspect of a platformer is the consistency and precision of its movements; from this point of view, the game does its job in a way that's not perfect, but still broadly decent: Klonoa moves fluidly and predictably, responding quickly to the player's controls (for the record: I played the whole game with a controller), even if a few rare times on platform edges I happened to fall down even when it was obvious I wasn't over the edge...+ CHARACTER DESIGNI've always had a soft spot for furry, brightly coloured characters; in this respect the game did not disappoint: I especially liked the round shapes and colour palettes of Klonoa, Huepow and Lolo, and also their personalities make them likeable, if a little clichéd.+ PLOTCONS:- OPTIMISATIONI won't sugarcoat it: this game is poorly optimised. The recommended specs include a GTX 660 graphics card to play at 1080p at 60 fps with settings at ‘high’; well, even though I played with a GTX 745, the game barely ran at 20 fps. To run it at 60, I had to reduce the screen resolution to 720p, in windowed mode and with the graphics settings at ‘low’. Not good.- ANIMATIONSNow, I wasn't expecting a Pixar-like level of animation, but I expected at least some fluidity in the movements; instead, I didn’t even get that: during cutscenes, the characters move in a wooden and lazy manner, like they were animated in 5 minutes at most.- PRICEI have to say, for what the game has to offer, the price tag is pretty hefty: at 40 US$ (and even worse in the EU: 50 €!) the quality/price ratio is not great. Fortunately you can buy the game at a 75% discount during sales, so at least you won’t spend too much (that’s how I got my hands on it).To summarise: if you enjoy retro mascot platformers, get this game when it's on sale. This way you can enjoy a good entry in the genre without overpaying for it.7/10 would wahoo again.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who never played the originals, this was a fun way to catch up on some platforming history. The mechanics are simple with the use of throwing enemies around for puzzles and combat, into the fore- or background, and as a double jump giving it a fairly novel feel and identity. Both games are fun with a reasonable difficulty curve and a fine sound track. I 100% both games and found it enjoyable. The only things that could get kind of frustrating were getting 150 gems in each level (which in DtP unlocks nothing and in LV only unlocks some art and so is very optional) and the bonus levels unlocked for getting all of the other collectibles which may for a tough but fun challenge separate from the main story. Boss are mostly serviceable to fun and make good use of the mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those days I wish Steam had a neutral review option.I'd want to give Klonoa a thumbs up because it's one of those retro games millennials grew up with. Characters are adorable, the story is good and bosses are fun. This was one of those games I wanted to play as a kid, but never managed to get my hands on it. Thus I bought its remake now, 20+ years later.Then again thumbs down tempts me, because it's very unlikely I'll ever be able to beat this game. Not the 1st one, at least. In the beginning it's very easy and chill. Reminds me a bit of Spyro. A little beyond halfway through the difficulty spikes to Oddworld. I had played way over 2 hours so unable to request a refund. Okay, no problem, I grew up in Oddworld. Challenge accepted.However, in vision 6-2, there's this certain jumping puzzle, which you must get 100% right. If you're late even for ½ second, you fail. It's very merciless and requires absolutely flawless accuracy and timing, and there's a time limit. My fingers are literally unable to move this fast. I spent about half an hour trying to build muscle memory, but no. Not in a single Soulsborne boss I've died as many times as I did in this puzzle. I even checked a walkthrough video to make sure I wasn't doing it wrong, and yep: I'm just not fast enough.If I had known Klonoa has locations like this, I would've passed this game entirely. A word of warning: If you even suspect you have similar issues as myself and you might not be able to do this kind of things, don't bother with this one.I'll give a thumbs up, because it was pretty fun up to the point I got stuck. Heh, I guess this was the last puzzle platformer for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this by saying I played only 16 hours, which isn't much, honestly; but that's because I played both games in their original forms. I had Klonoa 1 for PS1 (and then bought the PS1 version on PS3 years down the line), Klonoa 2 I could get from a cousin and I played a BUNCH of that, too (albeit not as much since, y'know, it wasn't mine and I couldn't hog it forever). So, I only played the remaster/remake a couple of times for each games, normally and then trying out hard mode- and since I know them like the back of my hand, I could complete them almost 100% quite fast, much faster than a new buyer who's never tried them.With that out of the way, I'll start by going about the remake/remaster. Klonoa 1 in here is inferior to the original PS1 version. The gameplay feels a bit more floaty than it originally did, it's not as tight. However, it's not to a level where it feels unplayable- and this is a ME problem, because I know the original so well that I've got muscle memory for how to play this. I'll use the wind bullet and jump in certain ways and with certain timing that emulates how it should be in the original, so even a tiny fraction of a difference causes me to take damage or fail something when it shouldn't. But, again, it's a ME problem, not something wrong with the game.Klonoa 2, however, plays pretty much exactly like the original to a tee. It feels just right and perfect. Graphics are great and look so good, just like they used to but upscaled perfectly, sound is great, gameplay hits as it should...Now, onto the games themselves, something that could work for new customers, too. First things first, don't let the cutesy art style fool you. These are not games just for children. Children can get a lot out of it, yes, but teens and even adults can find something to love in Klonoa 1 and 2 both. From the story, to the gameplay, to the music, to the sceneries... It's such a pity that this franchise was so slept on for so long... Klonoa 1 was a good selling game, but 2 wasn't advertised and it almost killed everything; the spin offs on other portable consoles couldn't really keep things alive on their own.The story can be emotional and hit deep at times, too, while still retaining a child-like innocence from start to end. It's so well written it's baffling. And I couldn't even tell you if 1 or 2 has the better story. I prefer 2 because it feels a little more mature and I've grown older, so that resonates more with me... But damn, 1's story is so impossibly good, too. Normally, one would need to say you don't exactly need to know 1 to play 2 because they are connected but not in the sense of a direct sequel, since there are some call backs (mostly musical call backs in some themes near the end of the game), but that's about it- but this package has both, so, y'know, play 1, then 2. And play both.They are HIGHLY recommended. I'm not a technical guy, I'm a feeling guy. These games make me feel emotions. Many emotions. Good ones, and bad ones; but the bad emotions aren't frustration from a bad game, rage from things not working- it's somber, melancholic feelings that are needed at times in life to reflect on things.And yes, that is how this game can make you think about it.If you have a bit of curiosity and you got the money, buy these games. You won't regret it. They're some of the best platformers of the time and they still hold up excellently today. If you're only partially sure, wait for any discounts, but make sure to grab it then.Trust me and play these games, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted to be a fuzzy creature with floppy ears, saving the world one dream at a time? Look no further than Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series! This game has more charm than a cat in a top hat – and yes, that happens here too.From the moment you start, you're whisked away into a whirlwind of whimsy. Whether you're bouncing on clouds or using enemies as impromptu projectiles, there's never a dull moment. Plus, who knew dreams could be so practical? Need to reach a high ledge? Dream it! Can't solve a puzzle? Dream it! Forget to set your alarm clock? Dream it! (Okay, maybe not that last one.)But it's not all sunshine and rainbows – unless you count the adorable rainbow-colored enemies you'll be taking down. Prepare for a rollercoaster of emotions as you navigate through levels filled with laughter, tears, and maybe a few facepalms when you miss that easy jump for the tenth time.In conclusion, Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series isn't just a game; it's a therapy session for your inner child. So grab your controller, suspend your disbelief, and get ready for a wild ride through a world where anything is possible – especially if you can dream it.

_childDocuments_.review: Klonoa is the epitome of an underrated video game franchise. Both games are complete packages, featuring creative game and art design, stellar music, moving stories, and a very likeable protagonist. This remake is the most convenient way to experience the two most prominent games in the franchise... but not the best way, in my opinion.Sadly, this collection continues the trend of Klonoa receiving unduly poor treatment from his publisher. These games are ports more than they are remakes. The Door to Phantomile "remake" is mostly a spit-shine of the Wii version with a few visual tweaks, and as a result has lost most of the charm that the PS1 original had. On the other hand, Lunatea's Veil is mostly kept intact from its PS2 release, but some strange changes made to the game's visual presentation leaves the emotional tone of the game feeling miscommunicated compared to the original. That is NOT to say these games are bad --far, far, far from it -- they're just not the IDEAL way that I hope one would experience them. If you want to experience the best versions of these platforming masterpieces (which is a label I don't assign lightly), I would recommend playing the originals on PS1 and PS2 first. If you don't own them, you'll either have to scour the internet for original copies or emulate them, but it's very much worth it. Otherwise, I beg you to buy this game at whatever price you honestly feel is worth it, even if just to support the franchise. Namco needs to see that Klonoa is a worthwhile investment before they consider making a third mainline game, even though the rest of us, few that there are, still see the potential the series has held all along. Frankly, the fact that this collection exists at all is a miracle, and I'm taking it as a good omen for the series going forward.Don't sleep on Klonoa. He deserves all the attention he can get.

_childDocuments_.review: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie is a remake of the original two games on PS1 and PS2. It's a very well done series and easy to recommend, with the warning that the first game gets genuinely hard. There are some fundamental changes from the originals, but nothing I'd say is either better or worse, just different.They are a series of 2.5D platformers focused on grabbing enemies. You can throw them, you can double jump off held enemies, and you can solve puzzles using them. Being 2.5D many of the puzzles involve throwing items towards or away from the camera or taking platorms/cannons to other layers of the level.The controls are functional enough, the hitboxes are generally good, and the level design is pretty solid, So tech-wise its everything you need.It's probably worth noting that about 70% of the game is platforming, and the other 30% is platforming PUZZLES. You need to learn how to use the existing enemies to hit all the switches quickly, or navigate switches/keys/maze etc.  You NEED to get really good at both because some of the late game require a specific order and near frame-perfect timing in order to get through a section. It's not a bad thing, but the flow of the game comes to a half when you hit a puzzle. You need to be willing to stop, look around, think and experiment before continuing the level. It's just a strange feeling for the pacing of a classic platformer.As for the changes from the original, the original game had a really unique art style and used alot of extreme camera changes. Visually, this remake is more consistent and far less of a spectacle. The colors are less eye-catching and the more standard 3D models feels less unique than the billboarded sprites. The bosses seem to have been made easier, though I don't know if it was necessary due to the next change.The most major change is that the remakes better handle curved maps by allowing a thrown object to follow around a corner.  This makes it far easier to fight bosses on circular platforms. But the new game has a smaller grab hitbox which makes is far harder to grab enemies on slopes or traversing grabbing sections. The ultimate feeling is that both versions are frustrating in their own way.The second game feels less changed just because they'd already made it more approachable. There's fewer slopes in the level design, the camera work was dynamic but not overbearing, and the puzzles don't require as high a skillset. Overall, this was my first real experience with Klonoa and I had a blast. But the negative reviews here convinced to me play the originals as well and I can see their view.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was already a revolutionary title when it first came out on the PS1, for it to come back to the west in a full remake along side the second game is amazing. However despite how great this game is, I have some notes.     The "Pixel" filter is cool for the first few levels, however, I had to turn it off at some point because it started to hurt my eyes, and I couldn't even see anything, movement for the most part is solid, but sometimes it becomes semi stiff when you try to perform certain actions, for both games, the audio for the most part is just an import and an import only, so for klonoa 1, some scenes still have that really crusty ps1 audio and it feels off, and finally, shadows aren't always casted, so this may just be me, but that def caused some depth precision issues.     Despite the minor flaws, I think this is a good game for anyone who likes kirby, yoshi's island, or just if you just like platformers in general. _childDocuments_.review: Two fantastic 2.5D platformers from the PSX and PS2! Gameplay - The game play consists of going through side scrolling levels with paths that branch and weave in an out of each other. Klonoa can shoot a short distance projectile from their ring, jump, and then hold jump to flutter in the air for a second. The main gimmick is you can use the ring to grab enemies and then throw them or use them to vault off of to get an extra jump! This turns enemies from just an obstacle to surpass to a necessity for traversing the levels and solving puzzles. This especially shines when used to chain from one enemy to the next to reach great heights or cross wide gaps! Presentation and Story - The stories presented are simple but cute and heart tugging at points, the characters are all charming with the voices being a fictional language that the series is known for. The voice overs are taken directly from the original games and while Klonoa 2 sounds fine, the first game's voice audio has that PSX crunch to it and while fine, it is sort of jarring next to the HD visuals.Minor Gripes - Both these games go for crazy prices if you want them in their original format and while Door To Phantomile has seen a few re-releases on the PS3 store and a Wii remake, this is the first time Klonoa 2 has ever been made available outside of the PS2! So if you just want a simple and easy way to play, this is it!However, I do feel some of the art direction is lost with Door to Phantomile not having the pre-rendered sprites and cut-scenes and Klonoa 2 not having the black outlines on the character models. I would like if there was an update to play the games with their original visuals. That being said, the new visuals are still a treat to look at and still do the games justice!There was also some extra content of the Wii version of Door to Phantomile (which this version is based on) that is sadly missing, like the mirror levels with hidden challenges in them.Overall - While they are by no means revolutionary, if you want games that set out to do something and do it well, I can't recommend these games more!I do hope if this collection does well, we can get a collection of the Wonder Swan and GBA games!
_childDocuments_.name: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not someone who has nostalgia for this series (I played klonoa on the ps1 last year) but it's easy to see why they're held up as some of the best platformers of all time.The klonoa games have only two buttons, grab and jump. Enemies can be grabbed and then used to extend jumps or throw at things left and right as well into and out of the screen. The mechanics feel so simple, but both games somehow manage to give you a constant stream of imaginative puzzles to solve with them. The restriction of a 2d plane also somehow seems to expand the room for creativity, making the other dimensions features in puzzles or hidden paths.All of this is then basted with a tasty 90s-japan glaze of dream-themed art and music, that I can only really liken to old sega games like Nights.It's a treat to have these games available and restored with clean modern graphics and features. I'd recommend these to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: These games are much better experienced than reading a review on them or watching them be played. If you like simple platformer games than this collection is a must-buy.There *are* a few minor issues with the collection, mainly dialog being stilted as it isn't as easily skipable as in the original games, but pacing issues aside, the stories that unravel themselves as you progress through the games are all too relatable, even if i'm not exactly the target audience for this type of game.These games are one of the only few platformer games that put effort into storytelling, and it pays off well. It doesn't needlessly overcomplicate things and the moments hit when they need to.There isn't much I can say about why this game is great without spoiling, but the writing of these games is what makes them stand out from others in their genre and the series has earned a cult-classic status for.I can't wait to see what is next for Klonoa, but since this is the latest Klonoa thing since the Nintendo Wii its kinda hard to get excited. I really, really hope there is more to this series than just these two games.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played Klonoa way back in the day and figured I should finally give it a shot since I know it had a bit of a cult following. It's a pretty good platformer with some great style to it. The game play is mostly 2D but the world is 3D. Platforms will twist and turn and the camera turns perfectly to go with you to give you the illusion of playing in 3D while playing in a 2D world. The only thing you really get that makes it feel 3D is when platforms move you to the foreground or background, or when you can throw enemies into the foreground or background.The jumping felt a bit off and got noticeable in the last world. If you hold jump or press jump again in the air, you'll do a small flying animation. You won't be able to fly for long but it helps you bridge some gaps or stay in the air longer to avoid hazards. The annoying thing with this is that you would run off the edge of platforms just a bit sooner than you'd expect which would make you use your fly earlier than expected and likely lead you to your death. Furthermore, grabbing enemies is a very short range. It can get pretty problematic on angled platforms as well as when you're trying to do it while jumping. Again, this becomes prominent in the last world. The last world was particularly frustrating which made it lose some points because the rest of the game was genuinely a lot of fun. This game handles pretty much exactly the same as Door to Phantomile. This one actually had some challenging skill based puzzles that was lacking in the first. It definitely feels like an improvement over the original except it still has the similar problems where platforming can feel a bit float-y at times and the last couple levels can feel very frustrating as a result.They did include a nice change with some snowboarding style levels. It was a nice change of pace and they were pretty fun to play through. That change of pace with some new game mechanics made the second a bit more enjoyable than the first. They're solid platformers. The enjoyment you'll get out of the sequel is pretty much the same as what you got out of the first. If you enjoyed the first, play the second, if you didn't like the first, don't even bother with the second. It's just a little bit better.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not much I can say that doesn't spoil the game, nor would I want to spoil it. But this pair of games right here is 100% worth the full price.Experiencing these games for the first time (since I didn't grow up with anything that wasn't really Nintendo or Sega) was an absolute blast. The story was enthralling and captured me from the start for both games, and the second one was only an improvement upon the first game. Both of the endings to each game actually brought me to tears because of how emotional and moving they were, and upon completing the second installment I was happy to have embarked on the journey that was Klonoa.If you're looking for a pair of relatively casual platformers with a bit of difficulty here and there, but not so much that you'll want to whip your controller at the wall, then buy this at full price. I promise you that you'll fall in love with this game and the wacky cast of characters as you take on the mantle of The Dream Traveler. My only wish with the games was that they were longer, averaging about 2 1/2 to 3 hours on your first play through of each, but at the same time, I never felt Klonoa had overstayed his welcome while also never seeming to leave in a hurry either, a perfect balance for an amazing pair of platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic remake/remaster of the two primary entries in the wonderful Klonoa series. Pitch perfect pacing and difficulty, with a unique way to interact with the back and foreground with your "wind" ability which can grab enemies and inflate them which immobilizes them above your head which then allows you to use the enemy for a number of tasks. The most obvious is simply throwing them at other enemies which will indeed kill them as you'd expect. You can also use them to gain an extra jump, or throw them into background or foreground to attack enemies, collect items, and solve puzzles among other things. There is also a charming cast of characters that help fuel a surprisingly robust plot that is only expanded and refined in the excellent sequel! Graphically I think the remakes are pretty great, I do miss the slightly more cel shaded look of Klonoa 2 on the PS2, but I will not argue that these don't still look great. It is very well done and stays true to the original release.All in all I can't recommend this enough. on sale or not!

_childDocuments_.review: Both Klonoa games included in this are nice platformers.Responsible, not too hard, more on the easy side of things, but not too easy either, nice platforming puzzles and so on.The graphics are.. Well, they're ok. Nothing to write home about. Looks like a mid 2010 game, despite coming out last year. It's a bit inconsistent at times, with some stuff being very low poly and something next to it not.The first cutscene of the first game, where his collar already clips through his body despite being the first thing the player sees, exemplifies the graphics. Not bad but kinda lazy.But the cutscenes. Holy hell. You either have the patience of a nice old grandma or you will miss the story. Those are some of the most awful cutscenes I ever witnessed. The cutscenes progress mostly on their own, only occasionally you have to press a button to continue, but you can't "skip this dialog window" either. They speak so slowly in their fantasy language that you could read it 3 times, and to add insult to injury there's a 3-second pause after every bit of dialogue, as if they wanted to add a laugh track but forgot it.So, what do you do? You skip. There are even two ways to skip, a 5x speed boost and a "skip all". The problem, every now and then the game actually has a few lines of dialogue that are not so painfully slow. So you 5x over that way too long one, and accidentlly over the next 5, just to then see them standing around saying nothing for seconds even at 5x speed before they continue.A simple "skip to next dialoge", quasi-standard in most games that even have dialog boxes, would have fixed that.Sorry for spending so much time on this but those damn cutscenes man.Now the pricing. This is a remake of two 1997 games. Putting this out at 60 bucks is just an insult. It should be half that, possibly less. Do not buy outside of a massive sale

_childDocuments_.review: Klonoa's original release was a classic, and still is; a game that spends that much time on so many "best-of" lists has something to it. As a platformer it's very much in the mold of a Mario or pitfall: you're introduced to the main abilities you'll have early on, and the game's challenges overall involve using your limited abilities in interesting ways.Unlike a lot of games of this genre, it uses the idea of 3D and 2D in interesting ways: movement is constrained to left or right, but things may be in the foreground or background, or may involve shooting something perpendicular to your movement. Enemies might come from the background to the foreground or vice-versa, and you might be swining on a bridge or some suchas. While it sounds confusing, the game does a good job of making things obvious and understandable, helped by the gorgeous and bright art style.Another thing to say is that while the game looks like mascot platformers of the past, brain dead and simple, the game hits hard with some of the hardest platforming and execution of it's era. IT comes from the era of "Short, but brutal" and lives up to it: with only ten levels in the first one, the game makes sure to pack as much as it can into that. Overall, this is definitely a game for both new and old gamers; both those who have nostalgia for the original release, and those who want a new and fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series is a two part collection of the original two Klonoa games.  The two are fun & well designed platformers, utilizing the mechanic of being able to grab all enemies above Klonoa's head, & either toss them or use them as a double jump, tossing them down.  Though the flutter jump Klonoa uses to temporarily float takes a bit to get used to it's odd arc, the ability to chain double jumps gives the platforming a unique puzzle feel, especially in Lunatea's Veil, which noticeably ramps up the difficulty.  Door to Phantomile is mostly based of the Wii remastering, while Lunatea's Veil is the first ported rerelease of the original PS2 title.  There are small differences, such as changing Klonoa's design in the original to more closely match the look of the original PS1 title.  The story is rather simple in both titles, keeping itself mostly light-hearted, minus a few moments in both games.  The visuals pop in a colorful & wonderful manner, & the soundtrack is catchy & quite enjoyable. Sadly, this collection does have a few problems.  Let's get the potentially patchable one out of the way first.  There's a bit of input lag when it comes to the attacking in the game.  This means in the latter stages when platforming over bottomless pits, it becomes even harder than the original release to cross.  It seems the attack, the wind bullet, doesn't move the same way it did in the original games.  This will only be noticeable to those who played the original releases, but it can get fairly annoying.  The real hiccup this title has is the audio of Door to Phantomile.  For some reason, they ignored the updated speaking audio from the Wii release.  This doesn't mean the translated track, this means they ignored the audio in the Phantomilian language.  In turn, it seems like they replaced it with the audio from the original PS1 release.  This means the audio sharply drops in quality, becoming harder to hear, & much more crunchy. Klonoa's list is nice & straightforward, requiring a completion of the games while collecting all residents of Phantomile or Momett Dolls.  The only ones of slight challenge require completion of the extra stages, though this merely requires heavy use of double jump chaining.  Thankfully, one doesn't need to collect all 150 dream stones in every stage, & that reward is so negligible it's barely worth it. Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series is a wonderful collection that comes so very close to being the absolute definitive way to play these titles.  For the first, I still believe the Wii version is better, if only slightly.  Regardless of that, this is still a must own two pack for lovers of platformers, & when it comes to the second, those who enjoy an increase of difficulty & length compared to the first.  To fans of Klonoa, this is a much welcomed addition to a long since dormant franchise.

If you have played Klonoa Lunatea's Veil on PlayStation 2, this is just a port for the Wii version. _childDocuments_.review: Klonoa finally makes its way to steam and modern hardware after many years of silence. There is a lot of items to collect within the game in order to 100% each of them and a lot of replay-ability as a result, the levels are fun that this is not a chore.Story: The story is pretty wholesome throughout with some harder subjects thrown in but nothing too obscene without going into spoilers, certainly better than most game's storylines in this rating.Difficulty: Played both games on Normal, not hard by any stretch, plenty of challenges and particular levels to keep you on your toes. Hard difficulty is able to be unlocked which I have not tried which may remedy the difficulty being too easy.Overall you're getting two games for the price of one, both excellent in quality and shine. I recommend this remaster of two of the main Klonoa games, very underrated franchise and I'd love to see Klonoa 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Two absolute gems of platforming that haven't aged a bit. In fact, they still feature amazing gameplay and some truly ingenious gimmicks - especially Klonoa 2, which exponentially improves its predecessors in just about everything. These remasters/portings of the original versions are quite good, especially the first Klonoa which has been rebuilt from the ground up and made more similar to Klonoa 2 both visually and gameplay-wise without adulterating its core mechanics and feel. Unfortunately, Klonoa 2 suffers from a few collision issues and some sporadic input eating, nothing gamebreaking but it can be quite annoying, and some of the characters' facial expressions during cutscenes seem to have been lost somehow. That is the main concern to me, there are mods that can fix this but I think it's really sad when a company releases an otherwise good product but doesn't bother to fix it after several months. These are some of my favourite games ever and it just feels bad to see some of the most emotional moments kinda ruined by a character's model just standing still with a blank face. If it wasn't for this, I'd have no reservations about recommending this collection to anyone.If you've never played these titles and you like platformers, then don't think twice and grab them, they are marvellous games that will fill your heart with joy - but they will also make you cry, like a lot. You have no idea just how sad the story of a cute jumping cat with long ears can be. But it's worth it, trust me. Otherwise, if you're already familiar with the series but you just want a big dive into nostalgia I say go for it, but be mindful of the issues I've mentioned and maybe follow the modding instruction you can find on the PC Gaming Wiki beforehand: Now let's just hope that Namco will finally give this series justice and make a proper new installment. I still want to share another dream with you, Dream Traveller...
