_childDocuments_.review: "We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie" stands as a monument to the gaming industry's unyielding commitment to repackaging the familiar in ever so slightly shinier foil, proving that innovation is merely an optional garnish in the feast of mediocrity. This title, if one could grace it with such a designation, endeavors to recapture the whimsical charm of its predecessors, yet manages only to ensnare itself in the sticky web of its own nostalgia, delivering a gaming experience as fresh as last week's sushi. The developers, in their infinite wisdom, decided that the zenith of creative achievement was to take a beloved classic and give it the digital equivalent of a fresh coat of paint, expecting applause for their courage in not altering a single pixel more than necessary.The gameplay, a term I use as loosely as the developers applied their effort, remains a Sisyphean exercise in futility, rolling up objects ad infinitum in a quest for size that mirrors the game’s own bloated sense of self-importance. The controls, as intuitive as a Rubik's Cube for the colorblind, only add to the existential ennui that permeates every moment spent in this kaleidoscopic hellscape. It’s a digital odyssey that promises the joy of creation but delivers only the monotony of accumulation, a metaphor for consumerist society wrapped in the guise of a 'fun' activity. One cannot help but ponder the philosophical implications of dedicating hours to rolling up virtual clutter, a sobering reminder of the hours of real life irretrievably lost to the void.Investing time in "We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie" is akin to pouring your life's sands through the hourglass of mediocrity, each grain a testament to the moments you'll never reclaim. The game, with its relentless repetition and superficial charm, serves as a stark warning against the dangers of nostalgia unchecked by innovation. It’s a vivid demonstration of how the gaming industry, in its relentless pursuit of profit, can take a concept sparkling with potential and reduce it to a tedious chore, leaving players to wonder why they bothered in the first place. In the end, this title will likely be remembered not as a crowning achievement but as a royal reverie best left forgotten, a dream from which we wake, regretting the waste of our precious, fleeting time.

The gameplay feels a lot more polished and the controls are more fleshed out. The QoL changes introduced in this game are a welcome change and really encourages you to try to complete it 100%. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a ball! There's nothing else quite like it.I saw someone playing a katamari game a long time ago in passing, and had no idea what it was. For years, it stuck in my mind and remained a mystery. Luckily, I rediscovered it. And even luckier, they've been ported to Steam.The game is presented in bite sized, themed levels that can range anywhere from roughly 5 to 30 minutes, broken up with  king's text dialogue between each stage. This is a chill game, but the time limits also give it a sense of excitement, without getting too frustrating. As the ball grows, so does your ability to pick up progressively larger objects. The sense of progression as your katamari is covered by the wide variety of things within each level, and visually seeing your katamari "become" whatever level you're rolling around in, is very satisfying. This game overflows with charm and uniqueness. I've put many hours into the first game, on switch and Steam, and right now, this will definitely be my go-to game for unwinding or killing time.Oh, and the soundtrack is also fabulous.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game all about picking up small items & adding them to a ball so that you can pick up bigger items.The sky is the limit in the later levels where you'll be picking up literal continents.Crazy controls make a comeback, but you can always turn on the simplified controls if you're having trouble.Def better than Katamari Damacy & I recommend getting this one if you're looking to get into the series.The only things I dont like about this game are1. If a stage has multiple player characters to be unlocked, you have to replay the stage as many times as the stage has characters. For example the last level being the longest you have to beat it 4 times to unlock all of the characters it has to offer.2. The stickers that appear all over the place are a collectable that you're most likely going to miss out on even if you manage to find a couple of them, as the only way for you to pick them up is to take a picture of them with a camera thats hidden in 1 of the earlier levels. _childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This is a review of the game as a Remake not a review of the game itselfBut as a game itself: We Love Katamari is an amazing game worth your time with creative uses of foundation set by the original Katamari Damacy with an even better soundtrack and fun dialogueIf you want a Solid Remake of an Amazing game then here it is! We Love Katamari Reroll + Royal Reverie is pretty competent as a remake. It does it's job being another way to play the best game in the series and then some. For the first time since Katamari forever this game boasts original and interesting content courteous of the titular Royal Reverie. It adds an extra half hour of content with Sonic Mania Encore mode levels of remixing to the base game levels. Although if you ask me, I still prefer the Original We Love Katamari. Unlike the remake of the first game Katamari Damacy Reroll which I can confidently say is a straight up replacement of the original, We Love Katamari in of itself was a vast improvement over the first game that only thing you could do for a remake besides enhanced graphics was to add more content and Fix the fact that you have to replay a stage up to 4 times just to get all the cousins in a stage since some cousins are locked behind future replays.  Reroll only does one of those two things and in fact has made some parts of the game (albeit a few) kinda bollux. the Cousins stage is a pain to get a good score at because the two cousins circling the tree are nigh impossible to roll up in a reasonable time for instance. The credits scene feels needlessly hard and I can't put my finger as to why. Heuey has Knees and should not have any if anything doesn't belong in the Katamari series Heuey's Knees is one of them. Also due to the redesigns that the remake of the first game introduces, the collection description of Ace is inacurate as he no longer has a spiky butt. These are nitpicks I know but the first two Katamari games is full of fun little details to the point that missing things like this is very weirdOutside of accessibility, If you Liked the first game's remake than you'll love We Love Katamari's remake, If you have the original like me then outside of the fact that it's on PC and has songs from the series later half, then you don't have much of a reason to get this remake outside of brand loyalty (I guess)

While it's not a bad addition to the game, I can really only describe it as.. More Katamari. No complaints here but I found myself avoiding it to play the original game.I have one complaint. _childDocuments_.review: A sizable improvement on the first game, if not one that adds too much to the formula.This game goes straight for fourth wall breaking to an intense degree, especially when compared to the first game. It works well, given the general sense of humor of the games. The fans are consistently fun, and the game's snarky attitude at anything less than perfect performance is refreshing given the current atmosphere of games coddling the player.The music in this game felt slightly less memorable than the previous game, though not by much. The main theme is fantastic, of course; some of the normal stage music less so, though. In general it felt a bit more formulaic, and less insanely eclectic like in the first game. There's no real low points, unlike some of the music in the original game. Of particular note is that the music for the collection screen is good and not awful, which improves things immensely.The gameplay receives a few subtle but important improvements from the first game. It's substantially harder to get stuck inside objects when the katamari is very large; this makes a huge difference on many stages. There's many, and more varied, stages, especially compared to the 3 stages total in the first game. There's a few extra rules introduced, but not many. By and large the goals are identical (and the bear/cow stages make a return). In this game the end goal is to roll up the sun; having this separate from the main stages worked very well in my opinion, and the ending was satisfying. During gameplay I thought the king was much more passive; in the first game he would often interject with absurdities, but here he rarely says anything at all. The various absurd scenarios on the stages themselves continue on from the first game.The end-game content in this game is very odd; the achievements end more or less where the normal game ends, with nothing for the post-game content. There's a bonus stage with an insane victory condition, plenty of rare objects to roll up, stickers hidden throughout the stages, and the various presents from fans which are not tracked as far as I can tell. There's not much in the way of rewards for finishing the stages from the King's memory either. As usual, the gameplay is its own reward with this kind of thing; I would have preferred a few more achievements, but it's no real issue.In a lot of ways, this feels like what Katamari Damacy was trying to be, and that the original game was more of a tech demo. That's pretty incredible, since the original game was fantastic on its own; this game then is even better. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: A loving remaster of a game that was out of place even when it first released, let alone now. There's a playfulness and a willingness to be weird in We Love Katamari that had been sorely missed almost two decades ago, and in the time since then can still mostly only be found in smaller passion projects. But it's on display here with the budget and scope of a small-ish dev team working at a big studio, and I like to treasure when corporations accidentally fund a thing like this.We Love Katamari is still the sequel the creator of the series never wanted to make, though. In a way, for this one sequel, that was actually kind of a blessing. Faced with the task of figuring out how to make a second one of these that actually feel original enough to be worth making, the team decided to explore what strange and niche tasks you could hand to someone stuck in the Katamari engine. The standard "roll 'em up and get big" levels are still here, but there's so many one-off level ideas. In one, you roll a sumo into food to make him bigger so he can win his upcoming match (it plays with the concept of what counts as food is, of course). In my personal favorite, you're tasked with rolling up the biggest cow or bear you can, with the stage ending the moment you roll a cow or bear up; the game is extremely impish about what it considers a cow or a bear, and even more mischievous about where they'll place those things. The variety on display means that We Love Katamari ends up feeling so much more playful than maybe any game I've ever played. It's here to make you laugh, and it's here to show you a fun time; the game doesn't have need of any other trappings. The colorful toy room-like graphics are still there, and the music is still an upbeat delight, but the core of what made this game stand firmly in the memory in a way further sequels didn't is that focus on its playful spirit.As for the remaster, it's good! No complaints whatsoever. The graphical update is pretty well done, but I do think there are some areas that needed work (water), and that the lighting effects have slightly less charm than the flatter colors of the original; fortunately, if you end up feeling the same, you can revert the game to its original lighting and shading effects in the in-game settings! The addition of Endless versions of some stages is a great update. The new photo mode is, honestly, kind of confusing and inconvenient, but it's a nice idea for an extra thing to do. New stages were added almost in the form of a small new Katamari game stapled on called Royal Reverie, and they've got some interesting ideas, though the levels are ultimately kind of forgettable. There's a "Series Music Bundle" that comes with the Special Edition; it almost feels like a must-have for how good some of the tracks on it are, and it's the kind of thing that would have just come with the game during the era this originally came out in, but that's just the era we live in now. So yes, I recommend this game. It's a little slice of joy, a game firmly interested in making you smile. I downloaded it, played a bunch of levels, and then started playing one level a day, like a desert I was keeping squirreled away in the fridge and picking away at here and there. You might enjoy that, too.

_childDocuments_.review: My first Katamari game is finally remade, with a fresh coat of paint and a new lease on life. Is it still great? Yes.Are some levels still infuriating? Yes, thank you very much CowBear level.For anyone unfamiliar, Katamari is a series where you roll a ball of stuff to roll up other stuff. You use two inputs (either two thumbsticks or WASD & IJKL keys) to roll it around. You typically have a limited amount of time to roll up bigger and bigger things in order to get a high score. It's very fun and surprisingly challenging.The soundtrack is both strange and beautiful, with most songs being about Katamari itself but done in surprisingly interesting styles.Overall, it's a very fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The Great Cosmos... A world of mystery both tantalizing and terrifying... Not a very well publicized world, you understand, but a glamorous and influential world nevertheless. Both yet sensitive, and rugged to boot. Tolerant and compassionate with a heart deeper than the oceans. Such is the Great Cosmos, and the King that rules over it is marvelous to behold. Except for the one time that he destroyed all the stars in the Universe. No big deal really. Having come to and realized the folly of his ways, the wisest of King sent to the planet Earth his beloved son, the Prince, and commanded him to make a katamari of ample proportions. Tossed unceremoniously to Earth, the valiant Prince rolled the katamari entrusted to him by the King, rolling up more things than you can count. Vaulting boxes, pencils, erasers, postcards, ramen, robots, cows, sheep, this girl, that boy, moms and dads, bicycles, motorbikes, homes, buildings, rainbows, clouds, islands, hopes and dreams. The Prince rolled them all up, rolled and rolled until the katamari was big enough to be lifted up to Space to replace the shiny stars that were so grievously lost. And that, dear friends, was the plot and purpose of the fabulous game called:KATAMARI DAMACY Its popularity recognized no boundaries or borders, and it rolled right out of the game to bundle away the many and sundry ills that blight the modern world. Overnight, the King found himself a superstar. The adulation of the crowd knew no limits."I want to meet the King!""I think it should be bigger!""The King is so cool!""I want to roll up more stuff!" Oh dear, such a chorus! Fans crying out from all over the world for the magnificent King to do his thing.Wooooowww!!! Woooowww-w-w-w-wooooo!!!Hmm... Still not enough stars here...
_childDocuments_.name: We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie

_childDocuments_.review: Another great entry in the Katamari series! this one really builds off of the original and improves it, and the bonus levels where you play as the king are just that, a nice little bonus. _childDocuments_.review: I'm so glad they final fixed this. It's a shame it released in the state that it did, but it's lovely now. Cheers.
_childDocuments_.name: We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie

_childDocuments_.review: I ADORE the Katamari games.A unique and strange style, sense of humor, soundtrack, and gameplay is already enough to get on my good side. Every time I see a ball pick something up in another piece of media I think of this series.I honestly just do not feel the need to convince anyone this series is wonderful. It's so imaginative it makes almost every other game look like they're barely trying.The physics of this PS2 Era game where everything can be picked up is sometimes a little janky or confusing, but that's the closest thing I can think of that's an objective flaw.Also, this game is silly. I'm hesitant to call it jokes, stacking 15 cows on top of each other doesn't feel like a joke, but it's certainly silly, and Katamari fully embraces being silly.Try one of these games if you haven't. There is nothing like them, other devs just straight up do not try to emulate what Katamari did. You don't know what it's like until you try it.

_childDocuments_.name: We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes the first one, Katamari Damacy, and expands on the premise greatly. Instead of each stage being simply "make the Katamari bigger than the last" (and there still are stages that are that), there are also fan requests where you have to get as big as a Katamari as you can make with only 50 objects, rolling the head of a snowman just right, collecting up to 1000 paper cranes, keeping a flame burning to light a huge bonfire, and so much more. It helps to keep the premise fresh and fun, while still being at its core the same Katamari we love.The Royal Reverie is short but fun. Staring the King of All Cosmos in his childhood, he has to go through his dad's tough training to be a good king. There are only five stages, remixes of existing stages, but they're overall tougher than the main game, requiring you to reach the goal quicker, avoid obstacles that can end the stage early, and finding hidden objects. It's a fun little mode that gives the King some backstory.If you love Katamari, or are looking for a place to start loving it, this is an excellent game to go with.
_childDocuments_.name: We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games on the PS2. One of the better games on PC. If you liked Katamari Damacy, if you were curious, grab this one. This game is better than what came before. Better maps, more interesting scenarios, equally solid music, and a better plot. Very weird, very japanese game. I adored it as a kid. I still love it now.
_childDocuments_.name: We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie

_childDocuments_.review: I have the original PS2 game and this port is fantastic.  The refreshed graphics are very bright and colorful and the controls are smooth, though this Katamari always had better controls than the first one.  One difference I noticed is that the voices of the characters you have to help are speaking in Japanese, while in the PS2 version they speak in English.  There are probably a few other minor differences as well but I haven't played the original in a long time and don't remember it well.  This version also has a little extra content such as more songs and some story content involving the King of All Cosmos when he was a boy, which is a nice treat for those who have the original game.  The Katamari Damacy series is one of my all-time favorites, so it's great to now have them on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie

_childDocuments_.review: I love Katmari. We Love Katamari. This game will certainly make YOU Love Katamari!Honestly my only complaint is that the ending and transition to post game feels really abrupt. I didn't feel as satisfied when I reached the credits compared to the first game. And if you disliked the gimmicky levels in Damacy this game is your worst nightmare. A lot of people also complain about the soundtrack being weaker than the first game and unfortunately I have to agree on that.Basically, this game really is just a giant filler game for fans who wanted more Katamari. And, well, I am one of those fans who wanted more Katamari, so this game is perfect for me.
_childDocuments_.name: We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie

_childDocuments_.review: How do you make a sequel to a game like Katamari Damacy? Well, exactly like this.I have to say, for a PS2 game with a deliberately low-poly style, this game looks fantastic. It's really aged well and has a bright, pleasant pastel vibe going on. Really easy on the eyes.The game controls better. You can be a little strawberry prince, or a little cow prince, or a little fat prince. The music is, again, amazing. It has more innovative levels. It tries to push the longevity of the concept through various challenges. It's a proper sequel and definitely worth playing if you're a fan of the original game.The cutscenes deserve an academy award.It's such an upbeat, joyous game that it might cure your clinical depression.Still opens in window mode but you're able to change it faster than the original.
_childDocuments_.name: We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie

_childDocuments_.review: Explaining a Katamari game to someone who has never played it is a bit like explaining portrait to a blind person.  Let's try this.  Imagine a joyful imaginary game a kid with Synesthesia (google it, it's wild) comes up with about gobbling up the world with his little toy ball.  Now give that kid acid and set him loose in the park.  The first one was easier to fall in love with, but the core of these games is just weird, senseless fun.  Unapologetic in it's campy weirdness.  10/10 would sing along to the theme song again.  I've bought these games on every system I've seen them release on because I'm just addicted to madness.  TLDR; buy the ticket, take the ride.  Get theme song trapped in your mind permanently. na-nanananananana katamari damacy
_childDocuments_.name: We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie

_childDocuments_.review: Lighthearted, comical game with intentionally difficult controls. Just as great as it was on PS2. You can't adjust draw distance which is a bit disappointing. _childDocuments_.review: This is a remaster of the Second Katamari Damacy Game  That came out on The PS2 in 2005  I found the Shorter Time Limits quite challenging at times but the Series Addicting Game play remains largely unchanged.  Except that there are More Objective Based Levels now in addition to Levels with Size Targets like the first Game.This Game shows us what it was like for the King of the Cosmos Growing up.  I didn't even play Royal Reverie which I think has even shorter Time Limits to Beat the Levels.I enjoyed my Time with this Game and I will probably play it More in the future. also it Has Keyboard Controls but Id recommend using a Controller.I should also Mention that there's some Good Music in this Game.
_childDocuments_.name: We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie

_childDocuments_.review: It's good but not as good as the the original katamari. It's basically a lot more of the same thing with the occasional gimmick thrown in there.I liked:- More of the same! Katamari is always pretty fun- Some of the new gimmicks are pretty interesting. The get big then roll something up was cool- Cool collectible cousins- Cool collectible giftsA few issues I have:- Score boundaries are much harsher. Expect to finish levels way over target and be ridiculed for how bad you were- Score boundaries are not displayed anywhere. If you finish under the top score, you'll just be told "Do better" with no idea how much you need to do.- You have to play time trial versions of the stages before you can replay the original stage. It's not communicated well that this is the case and gets irritating when you finish a level and do badly and want to go back.- "Royal Reverie" is actually just a couple of stages made a bit harder. _childDocuments_.review: When Katamari Damacy REROLL suddenly rolled into existence less than 5 years ago, I absolutely loved it. And my biggest complaint was the lack of We ♥ Katamari content, as it felt to me that a new title mixing both the original and the sequel would’ve been a far better choice. Well We Love Katamari REROLL is here now, with lots of improvements, a little added bonus in the form of Royal Reverie and, sadly, with a few unfortunate issues.Just like the original Katamari Damacy or it’s enhanced remaster, the gameplay of the title is very unorthodox, but also fun, simple and exciting. As the Prince of All Cosmos, you are sent on tasks by your father King of All Cosmos, all of which involve you rolling a ball (though there are exceptions) that can be rolled over other objects to get them stick to it. Which objects can or cannot stick to the ball fully depends on the size of the ball itself and usually at least one of the objectives for the game is to simply get a bigger Katamari ball before the time limit runs out.Unlike the first game, however, We Love Katamari has lots more levels where simply getting the Katamari as big as possible isn’t the main task and instead you have other goals. And many levels in the game also have several stages of completion, from one that lets you consider the level complete and move on, to the one that fulfils the ultimate goal that is often very hard to achieve. Doing so, unlocks more fun stuff and specifically in the remaster, more levels in this new Royal Reverie mode, where you play as the young King of All Cosmos and try to complete the tasks his Papa set for him, all of which are usually harder than the main game and all of which are somewhat based on the little scenes you see when you’re playing through the story.The only huge complaint with the game is that it has several odd technical issues that are either entirely new and were not in the 2005 PS2 original, or are remnants of the old design that was kept and sometimes feels at odds with the game. The new issues include the horribly small draw distance for a lot of objects, that actually makes the game harder in stages where you need to collect specific things, as you don’t see them from just a dozen meter away and can lose precious time when going for best scores. Another issue is the fact that the game can occasionally freeze for several seconds for no apparent reason, before continuing as if nothing happened. And finally, as a remnant from PS2, every time you get bigger than a specific size, some levels have a bit of a loading before you can continue, which seems odd for a game like this in 2023, but at least keeps the cute dialogue boxes from the King.Other than that, a lot of little improvements were introduced and the game is more fun to play. I’m also glad that unlike Katamari Damacy REROLL, that for some reason lacked autosave (at least when I’ve played it), We Love Katamari REROLL does have it. The visuals are more beautiful than they were in the first remaster. The music is as amazing as it has ever been, remaining catchy and fun and you will be singing along before you realize it. The controls are as finicky as they used to be, which is a shame, but also a part of how these games work.I loved We Love Katamari REROLL+ Royal Reverie and while it’s hard to choose between the two, I tend to prefer the sequel. If you were to choose which of the two games to start with, I’d suggest this one. But really, you owe it to yourself to play both now that they’re available on modern systems. They’re absolutely lovely.

_childDocuments_.review: I sunk countless hours of time in younger days into Katamari Damacy. During the pandemic, I fired up my old Playstation 2 and played through We Love Katamari with my roommate, finding every cousin and present along the way. Having recently played the PS2 game to its completion, I can confidently say this.This game is what your rose colored glasses remember We Love Katamari to be. The sound and visuals, though improved, remain true to their source material. (Yes, the motorcycle guy still makes his ridiculous v-v-v-vrroom vroom when you snag him.) The textures are all enhanced in such a way as to make things clearer while still maintaining the cartoonish charm. The controls are responsive to boot.I would recommend using the normal graphics if you're on an older or lower end computer rather than the enhanced ones. Though the game ran on my computer at max settings remarkably crisply, it did have framerate issues when I booted it up on an older machine that I would have said were on par with the original PS2 game when several items were on screen and a lot of chaos was going on.I do wish the Royal Reverie added more levels rather than just applying some rules to levels and giving me a short time frame to get some King time in, but they're fun enough little sidequests that can eat up an hour or two of your time.Final Verdict: If you love Katamari, buy We Love Katamari Reroll+ Royal Reverie and teleport yourself back to 2005 for at least 10 hours of play. If you don't already love it, snag this or its predecessor on a sale and discover that love without the pressure of its full price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: We Love Katamari REROLL is the well anticipated sequel to Katamari Damacy REROLL, being just like the original releases, a second shot to hone the craft of the games, done well with, in my opinion, great additions to quality of life and graphical capability. This review will just detail We Love Katamari and this rerelease, if you want my opinion on the series as a whole, my original Damacy review is lengthy enough to get an idea of that, so I'll spare some words on this one.Katamari Damacy is now a hard sell to people new to the series, simply because We Love Katamari evolved on the original recipe and, in my opinion, completely compromises the existence of Damacy. WLKR brings with it not just more of the incredibly unique and beloved Katamari gameplay from the PS2 exclusive to updated consoles and PC, but even more updated QOL features and graphical features into the new games that both streamlines the game much more than it already was on release and brings the vision more in line with Keita Takahashi's most recent renditions of the game and cast's style- subtle, but it is there.Functionally speaking, it runs great at 1080p and can easily take advantage of high refresh rate monitors which is by far the best advancement any old game can get. The controller inputs from what I can tell are just about as responsive, if not better (please use a controller, not keyboard). The only issue the game has is a down-pitch that is applied to a lot of sound effects, mostly on random people voices, but this should hopefully get a patch soon if it hasn't already. The included Random and Favorites list with shuffle for BGM is by far the best feature in any Katamari game, especially for those longer Eternal runs.The additional parts for Royal Reverie are in a weird spot where they are fun little additions, but also very trivial both in challenge and in why it needs to be there in the first place, which in itself is a double-edged blade. I have not noticed any say of the aforementioned Takahashi's involvement in the reproduction of the Katamari series, so without his input, I would be skeptical about how faithful new storied parts or new stages would come together. So, I'll call it the cherry on top that isn't necessary, but it's generally an appreciated gesture as a nod to the series. But, maybe fingers crossed that a new entry is coming down the horizon in a few years.$30 in my opinion is a well worth price for WLKR, especially if it funds more Katamari projects, but I could see arguments made to go down towards $20-$25, maybe $15 if you want to stretch it, and fair play to those people. The Soundtrack DLC however is really only for fanboys like myself, as it doesn't even give Steam Soundtrack access or MP3s or anything, it's purely in-game, quite an awful value proposition even for the bundle discounted price of $10. It's a good set of songs, but horrendous price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great remaster of a great videogame. The soundtrack is one of the greats, the music DLC is good (but clunky in how you select the tracks to play in a level), and the Royal Reverie levels are nice (but small) additions to the overall package.At the time of this writing there's a pop-in issue that badly hurts a few of the levels, but I think that is one of the things that will get patched. _childDocuments_.review: A few years ago Katamari Damacy ReRoll hit steam, a remastered version of the game that started the series. I'd never had the chance to play it, it not releasing in my region, but I tried it and was amazed. Ever since then I've tried to find a few of the other games, but We Love Katamari remained out of reach. Colour me gleeful when the ReRoll version was announced. Bought it on the launch day and have been rolling, rolling, rolling happily since. So what's the deal with this ReRoll of what many call the best game in the series? Updated graphics, cloud saving, modern hardware optimisation and a crossplatform release? That, but they've added more things to this version in the form of the Royal Reverie and the expanded ingame OST that includes the Yuri mixx of Sayonara Rolling Star. So you not just have the base game levels, their speed-run alternate versions and the original ost... but 5 new levels with their counterparts, playing as the King of all Cosmos (prince form) and you can set ANY track as the music.Like in KDRR you can roll up practically any object in the game world if your Katamari is large enough. From a thumbtack to a house, from a child to the entire school, from simple bushes to all the continents. If you can make it big enough within the time limits. Some levels have alternative rules, extra effects or goals and there's a ton of creativity in finding objects combined to depict something else... Even then, the game has tons more basic objects than its predecessor, nevermind the amount of cousins and presents you can also acquire by rolling them into the Katamari and finishing the level. You can then talk to a cousin to switch with them to replay a level as a cousin.We Love Katamari is a fun action puzzle game with so many things to discover that its a solid recommend even if you played the original gray. Get it, get it full price or at a discount, but don't miss out on this amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely AMAZING game compared to the original Katamari Damacy REROLL. Unlike KDR, the game has been completely remade with actual graphic settings (finally), new levels, a whole new area to play in and TONS of new content. First of all, every Katamari game in the past has been capped at either 30 or 60fps (with most of the games never even getting close to 60fps). We Love Katamari REROLL is the first Katamari game to have fully unlocked fps and it is BEAUTIFUL. I have a 280hz monitor and seeing the game this smooth is seriously something else. The game performs perfectly, with so far only one bug and zero frame drops.Second, this game has SO much new content. I'm only 3 hours into the game and I've already noticed so many new things. There's new levels, new characters, an entirely new stickers section? I don't wanna spoil everything but the amount of just new stuff in this game is awesome.Lastly, whether you've played the rest of the Katamari series or not, this is such an amazing game in general and I highly recommend buying it. Hours of fun, amazing music and such an adorable game.

_childDocuments_.review:
The King of the Cosmos once accidentally destroyed all the stars in the universe. He sent his son, the Prince, to Earth and ordered him to create a large katamari.
The Prince rolled the katamari and made the katamari bigger and bigger, rolling up all the things on the earth. The katamari that he created floated in space, sparkling, and brought back the lost starry sky.
As the starry sky was restored, the King's fans gradually grew in number all over the world. The King wanted to respond to the wishes of his fans for his success, and the Prince kept rolling the katamari to make everyone's dreams come true.

•We Love Katamari Damacy has been powered up!
We Love Katamari Damacy, the second title in the Katamari series released in 2005, has been remastered.
The graphics have been completely redesigned, and the in-game UI has been revamped to make it even easier to play.

•New additional features such as Royal Reverie are also available!
In his youth, the King received a strict education from his father, the Great King. New challenges have been added where you can roll around as the King in his boyhood!
The days of hard study and intense training can all be rolled through in 5 all-new challenges.
Will the young King be able to clear the tough challenges?
In addition, a selfie mode has been added, allowing the Prince and his cousins to take quick photos while rolling through the stages!

name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars
detailed_description: Game Editions Get the main game, future DLC, and digital products in one great value package. Asterigos: Curse of the Stars - Ultimate Edition includes: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars original game Asterigos: Call of the Paragons DLC Asterigos: Curse of the Stars Complete Soundtrack Asterigos: Digital Art Book Asterigos: Curse of the Stars - Deluxe Edition includes: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars original game Asterigos: Call of the Paragons DLC Join our Discord About the Game Discover the long-forgotten secrets and hidden paths in this high fantasy world, featuring exhilarating battle encounters, interconnected maps full of places to explore, and an immersive story where every choice matters. Play as Hilda – a brave young warrior from the Northwind Legion who embarks on a journey to the cursed city in order to save her lost father. The gameplay elements inspired by soulslike games alongside a lighter, dynamic combat system, create a fresh take on the modern action RPG genre, providing you with a harmonious difficulty and exploration balance. Explore the magnificent city of Aphes inspired by classical Greek designs and unveil the truth behind the city’s curse. Combine and change your weapons on the go. Equip two different types of weapon at once and become unpredictable in combat. Battle more than 60 different enemies and encounter 22 bosses in the main story and side quests. Decide the fate of Aphes. Every decision you make in Asterigos matters and will affect the story. Find over 100 collectibles, complete numerous side quests, and forge your destiny in the NewGame+ mode. Test your combat skill in the brand new boss rush mode: Gauntlet of the Stars. Welcome to Aphes – a city-state full of magic and wonder inspired by ancient Rome and classical Greek designs. From the mist-covered bazaar streets to gloomy sewers, the enigmatic forests at the city’s outskirts to deep chasms full of glittering crystals, the landscapes of Aphes are full of beauty and dangers. Choose from a variety of ranged and melee weapons on the go and combine them as you wish! The talent system allows you to pick and expand your combat style by choosing two out of six completely different weapons: sword and shield, dual blades, spear, hammer, staff or even magic bracelets . Equip a magical staff to obliterate your foes from the distance or switch to a gigantic battle hammer to squish them in a close combat. Whilst Aphes might distract you with its breathtaking views, this city is not for the faint of heart. Fight your way through 60 different monsters and encounter 22 unique bosses – each with its own unique battle mechanics. Every choice and every decision you make matters. Your journey in Aphes will lead you to discover the truth behind the city’s curse, letting you piece together its history through conversations, discovered documents and cinematics, as well as Hilda’s own diary, which she’ll update with sketches and observations. The world of Asterigos is full of secrets and untold stories. Complete numerous side quests , find collectibles and win rewards from Gift of the Nexus , test your combat skills in the brand new boss rush mode: Gauntlet of the Stars and build on your legacy in the New Game+ mode !

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid indie souls-like that I enjoyed and I feel like we need more games like this in the genre. The only negatives I can think of are that the quests are too convoluted and that there is too much dialogue in the game. The way quests are designed in this game is confusing and lead me to look up some of them online. It is easy to get lost on what to do/where to go next. There's also a LOT of dialogue in the game - not a negative per se, but it was for me. There was too much reading in the game for my liking, but some gamers do enjoy extensive dialogue and lore. The last thing I'd mention is that the game feels "slower" in terms of its pacing, story and overall gameplay. Fast travel is not unlocked until a bit later and at the beginning you only have warp crystals, which are somewhat uncommon. That didn't bother me but I can see it annoying some people.Overall I'd definitely recommend the game for fans of the genre. If you're hesitant then pick it up when it goes on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: I thought the premise was great. Another fantasy historical implementation of the current trend. I wanted to like this, but the stuttering and general sluggishness of the controls made this one a big question mark for me. But not only that-Where the hell do I go? There is no map. Nothing. zilch. No book to employ where you are at in a given quest. You're aimlessly running around trying to find something-anything other than running around. You basically have to kill all the enemies to give you an impression of where you'd been. No enemies? You've been here already. Its not a bad game. Just wish it'd had more time in the oven.I'm really disgusted with the perk system. Usually when you aquire a perk, its a win win, right? Not here. You have to take a negative with the boon. For example dodge an attack earlier than normal but at a increased Sp cost or gain more HP healing, but carry less HP potions.  I've noticed that most of the skills are the same way, Gain some new ability from a weapon, but subtract from it's strength or stamina to use it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is competent, I had no technical issues and for us perverts there is a nude mod for the player character.The story is everpresent. The NPCs have lots to say, though not all dialogue is voiced (but hey, if Nier Automata can do it, so can Asterigos). Plenty of stuff to read, if you want. Most of this is optional and can be ignored if you want. The combat is ok, but the enemies are not very difficult to beat. The bosses are fine but very few of them, you'll spend hours without fighting anything challenging. The loot system is horrible. All you get is upgrade materials. Do you remember those purple shiny loots in Elden Ring? The anticipation of something great, only for it to be a freaking arteria leaf. Yeah, this is that. Sure it's useful, but when you get just that it sucks.There is other stuff that could have been better, but no game is perfect.Also is has a furry waifu who calls you cute and sweet all the time, so that's great.EDIT: Alright, I've beaten it. It's a very ok game. Story: Passable, not nothing mind blowing.Combat: I've only used 2 out of 6 weapons, but I can still say that dodge and hit ♥♥♥♥ till it dies is basically the gist of the combat.Bosses: Too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ few, man. Sprinkle in some tougher bastards, devs. Hours can pass by without a boss fight.Loot: Still garbage, it's just upgrade mats and healing flasks. Add in more amulets with special effects devs. And more costumes!PS: I've looked under everyone's skirt and yeah, fine asses are there.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game, the mechanic, world-building, story and characters are great!However, the side-quest is a bit hard because there was no tracker what-so-ever, so most of my time spent going around wondering where to go, or trying to figure out what's next on the side-quest. So many back-tracking.The combat overall is enjoyable, or at least for me when I'm using spear or dagger. Spear counter-attack is very satisfying while dagger's skill is mostly to cheese your enemy if you plan to win the game under level (level 20 or below achievement). Sword and Gauntlet is okay..? then the rest I just dont find the charm in their 'special ability'. But all and all, really enjoy the game. And the lovely art ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I really like the game. Combat had some promise in the beginning but at some point I just went the lazy route of mining everything instead of spamming attack. _childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars is a game with an interesting atmosphere and plot, as well as well-written characters. In my opinion, the game is distinguished by a very good combat system, we have a lot of weapons, you can play as a mage, assassin, warrior and so on, we just choose the weapon we want and choose spells for it and that's it. I think that the game offers a lot of different cool options and thanks to this we can play however we want and there are no limits to us, we can even combine these weapons and spells into sets and make, for example, half a mage and half a warrior, and such a solution changes the way we fight.The game does not have any specific errors that I could criticize here, and the game time itself is also satisfactory because the game is not too short or too long. First of all, I recommend it to people who like challenges and, most importantly, the action genre. The game is not overly difficult, but it is not easy either. As for the negative comments about the game, I don't agree with them because the game is really good. I am aware that it may not be the highest level but the game is still not that bad, it has limitations resulting from the game's budget and you can feel it, but apart from that the game is very well made.My rating is:9 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite good, I recommend getting it on sale but maybe not the DLC. The story is decent and there is a lot of collectable items that expand on the lore of the game. The combat is not very complex but is still fun, there are 6 weapons to chose from each with a unique combat style. There is also a lot of side quests and optional boss fights.The side quests in this game can be a pain and you will almost certainly get stuck and need to use a guide. The "good" ending is also tied behind completing certain quests in specific ways and you can get locked out of the "good" ending just from choosing the wrong dialogue option.This game is a mixed bag of pros and cons but I still enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: RecommendedLove this game. Really solid and fun experience. Pleasing artstyle. Good combat mechanics. The difficulty is just right, easy even if you actually invest in the skill tree system. The area is varied enough to not make it feel repetitive. The story is compelling. The music is enjoyable to listen to. The only downside is if you want to collect all the chest/documents/achievement, you must seek out a guide/walkthrough or you will waste so much time walking around. All in all, I actually hope this game has a sequel or something, because the lore is intriguing enough. Maybe the next game can take place in Anbari instead?

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars is a good game combines the style of traditional RPGs with a soulslike template, resulting in a challenging but more accessible game that’s able to forge its own identity without hiding its influences.  Despite these shortcomings, the gameplay is still enjoyable and the emphasis on storytelling and world building helps make up for it. The biggest divisive factor with Asterigos is that it tries to appeal to both fans of more traditional RPGs and Souls games by combining elements of both, and as a result doesn’t excel at either. But if Asterigos is approached without a purist mentality it can still be a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Great souls-like combat with a decent story. There's no map, but the levels are mostly linear the first time through, then lots of shortcuts open up as you explore.The game has 6 weapon options, but once you get comfortable with two of them (you can carry two weapons at a time), then proceed to level them up, there's no good reason to switch to the other weapons, especially as upgrade materials can be rare.Dying results in losing some money without any means to recover it (no corpse run). You can work around this by either spending your money first, or save/reload for each try.A way to track side quests would have been nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly the product of a number of highly skilled games industry folk but features a number of deep flaws that feel due to problems at the producer level within the studio.Asterigos is clearly inspired by Dark Souls but seems to just miss the underlying fundamentals of why Dark Souls works as a game.Show Don't Tell: The story is interesting (despite Hilda not being the strongest character), but there's just way too much of it. I quickly hit sections of the game with exceedingly long sections of dialogue in the span of what felt like 5 to 10 minutes of just characters talking. Now, I like story, I am ok with long periods of dialogue, but these plotbumps are just everywhere. You can't go more than 50 feet before finding another note with anywhere between 5 to 30(!) paragraphs of text or another echo that amounts to a cutscene that would be an audiolog in another game. I eventually found myself just skipping any and every amount of dialogue, only putting the briefest amount of effort in to skim the context. Just too much text.Mostly Empty Space: Many sections of the game are wonderfully crafted and just gorgeous to look at, but for every section of village there exists an equal amount of invertly drab and exhausting space to travel through. Fast travel comes midway through the game, (and thankfully you can use items to warp to and from the hub before then), but with or without it, getting from A to B within a zone sometimes feels like a chore and an exercise in thumb cramps as you'll click the left stick in over and over to burn through countless stamina gauges worth of terrain in sometimes weirdly immense spaces. The Barracks area of the game is an especially strong example of long periods of travel, especially if you're trying to clear out the zone of collectibles. And, if you do go hunting for collectibles and side stuff, (which, to steal from Robert Palmer, you might as well face it you're addicted to loot), you're going to do a LOT of pushing run and/or dash. I all but know for a fact that their QA recommended a better way to mitigate the long stretched of running which was surely veto'd by Production.So Many Skills, Little To Do: I only used a handful of skills the whole game and was never even curious about all the ones I had access to. That said, I used the Staff all game and even was spec'd hard towards skills but found that I built up AP so slowly that using skills on the regular was just wildly inefficient to just maxing attack and HP. Maybe I would have been more interested in skills if I hadn't just stuck to blasting stuff with charged shots (a manually aimed long range attack you can almost always dodge out of). I even stopped using the ultimate stance for the staff, which wholly uses your main attack, largely because the final staff attack rarely hits anything and has long uncancelable animations. Whereas, Magic Breath (a charged attack that does lock you into an animation) did so much damage in a window that I would largely just hop around and wait for a window to start standing and deliver. All this is a real shame as the skills are all just amazing to look at and the few I did use felt very crunchy, I just never had any AP to use them.Let Me Innnnnnn!~: There's just a lot of story gates in the game. In Dark Souls you have locked gates, but often you have some clear path forward towards some new boss or zone. In Asterigos, you have several major story gates you just Can Not Pass until X moment and plenty of minor gates within zones themselves. Did you find an area you're meant to be in later too early? Welp, go back and progress the plot because this door don't open until you've finished your meat. At least three times I also found myself just unable to figure out where I was meant to go next, but this is probably because I was skipping dialogue. On the other hand, I wouldn't need plot text to make forward progress.Conclusion:So to be honest, I'm still playing Asterigos and expect to finish, mostly because roaming around and blasting enemies with the staff and daggers became reasonably satisfying after getting pasted in combat trying to block or parry things. (This is on me for forgetting Soulslike Rule 1: Never Fight Fair, Hidetaka Miyazaki said it's cool dudes, cheese is legit, but you play the way you want to play, you are valid.)And a number of the boss fights are pretty good even if the melee combat feels a little clunky. And the game is quite pretty. But, I'm invested at this point. If I could go back, I'd tell past-me not to buy the game. So, here's me warning you as a proxy for past-me: There's better stuff out there to spend your time on.It's just a shame that Asterigos didn't have stronger Producers.(oh and Devs, please don't take this too harshly. You did a lot of good work here, I wouldn't have taken the time to write all this up if I didn't think there wasn't something here. Respectfully, Monster)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a long game. There is a teleport system like other soulslikes, but you'll be what feels like a long ways in before you unlock it. Don't worry about level grinding too much, you'll get a lot later in the game. I personally recommend the spear/javelin (whatever they call it) and magic staff for main weapons, but completely up to you. I also ran with all my points into ATK only, no HP or SP buffs, which is why I ran the spear for the parry ability. Overall I'm really en joying this game and would be satisfied with a AAA price tag, so even at retail price this is a steal. I'm not a huge Dark Souls fan simply because of the difficulty, but soulslikes with a solid story are always good imo. I give it a solid 4.8/5. Would be 5/5 but takes way too long to unlock teleport imo. I may update this later as I believe I'm not even halfway done based off the amount of achievements I have left for killing certain bosses, and i have not started the DLC yet.Edit: I was probably 3/5 of the way through at review time, but the teleportation made it way faster to get things done. Since I do so much damage the boss killing was relatively quick and easy. If you go for achievements, get to level 20 then lock your level with the trinkets it gives you. You can 100% the game with only one playthrough. Best advice I have is thoroughly explore, but don't waste time killing every single enemy, they aren't worth your time if you're going for quick playthroughs.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this extremely negative review by saying this game is beautiful to look at, i really wanted to like it.  The environments were nice to look at and the art team did a great job. I even bought the deluxe edition and i will endure the game to the end regardless. That said - dark souls wannabe with 10x worse combat. There is 0 feedback when you get hit. Your character just blinks. There's no Estus, its a random healing item you pick up that cant be upgraded, slowly heals like 1/4 of your health over time and isn't renewed at the games bonfires.I'm fighting a boss where if you parry him, a secondary fire attack hits you that goes through the parry. They have designed the game to literally be at odds with how they designed it. Why make a weapons mechanic be to parry and then have the weapon mechanic be punished? 100000000000000000IQ guys well done. This game has 6 WEAPONS FOR THE ENTIRE GAME. You get all of them at the start and just upgrade them. While it seems like you can get other "outfits" it's not armour you can collect and upgrade or anything. I'm 13 hours in, not got a single new outfit yet,Now there's a boss you need to destroy crystals on 2 obelisks with waves of enemies for both, if you dont get back to the middle of the room insanely fast the boss insta kills you. This game is actually retarded. Bed of Chaos on steroidsSpeaking of upgrades, many of the upgrades are actually hidden behind character side quests. Think Dark Souls embers but much more obscure and you will likely never find them accidentally. Great, you hid a large part of the upgrade system, genius.I have memed every single boss and enemy but this one (warden), they were too easy. This boss just breaks the spear. So on my second attempt i just spammed with spells. Stop making games if you A. Have such tragic attempts at design as thisB. Have to add a difficulty mode. It's not a souls like if you do this. I have only died to 1 boss but it seems like you don't lose "souls".C. Have voice acting for 50% of the dialogue. Its jarring as hell when people suddenly turn muteD. THERE ARE 2 BUTTONS TO RUN BUT ONLY ONE OF THEM LETS YOU JUMP...WHYThe in game player character model looks crisp at 4k/max settings/sharpness filter. You look at your character in the inventory and it turns into a 480p style low quality/resolution image. You can turn your character when are in the inventory to look at them, but their movement is like 15 or 30 fps. Why would you just randomly do this? This game just reeks of babies first dark souls but somehow worse with terrible design choices. I couldnt wait for it to be over.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is an ARPG with lockout combat animations, invulnerability frames, and generic 'action' button (F) to prompt your toon to execute some random task like opening doors, climbing walls, pick up an object, vaulting, etc..    This game VERY story driven.  I mean, you will get frustrated with how in-your-face the story is.  You can click though dialogue to skip it at least.  Some parts of the game basically require you to click-through all the 'talk' options with NPCs in order to open certain parts of the game, or to advance sequences.Asterigos is NOT sandbox, open-world, or free choice.  It has a linear story, following a predetermined sequence of events.  Levels/zones are like streets with platforming. Platforming in this game sucks, due to the 'jump' key being "G" for no good reason, and TONS of invisible object collision.  If it looks like a clear path, you will probably hit an invisible wall.  Vaulting can only vault things that are knee high, and only if you get the prompt that you can click on it to vault.  Clicking on the prompt means you need to get the prompt to vault to properly show up on your HUD.  (Proper facing, distance). Thanks to trashy unreal physics, your character doesn't turn, as much as they drift around an arc to get a proper facing.  This makes aligning the UI a PITA sometimes, when trying to interact with some object.  Gotta run a ways back, get lined up, and calculate your deceleration trajectory to land in the hit box for the prompt in the correct facing.  Attack sequences are basically, 'hold down button' to see your character execute a series of animations in an action-packed wow swinging around and flailing in random directions while you are getting mobbed!  So cool! At least they allow you to interrupt attack frames with a dodge or power.  Alternatively, if you want to avoid the chain-combo attack, you can mash the attack button to repeat basic attacks.  You CAN lock onto your target, but your attack combos often send you past your foe, and continue executing attacks away from your enemy's backside.  Like, you for real get stuck into a wild weapon-swinging-fest like your dude can't stop randomly failing at thin air.  It would be great if the enemy was moved along with your toon, but nope.  You just attack right past the target and keep going!  It is also possible to attack right off a cliff.  Watch those ledges.Suffice to say, combat leaves a LOT to be desired, due to ARPG lockout garbage, and action-spectacular attack animations.In conclusion, wait for a sale.  To me, this game is worth maybe $10-$15, it is graphically appealing, but otherwise a clunky click-through action story.  I dislike click-through action games, like assassin's creed, dragon age, witcher, and similar.  If you like those games, you will probably enjoy this one too.  If you don't like click-prompt ARPG with lockout animations?  Then check other titles.  This game is at least pretty, even for being so basic.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly a gem. It's a big fan of Dark Souls, and I've tried several Soulslikes and Soulslites, and this is definitely a great example of a good Soulslite. That is, it's similar to Dark Souls in having engaging, difficult combat, but it's a little easier because it doesn't punish you as severely for dying. Better yet, it has more of a story than the typical Souls game, plus an attractive and lovable main character named Hilda. Hilda's beauty, style, and spunk add a lot to the experience.While Asterigos isn't perfect, it's really a worthwhile and fun game. I do think it would've been better if it had a greater variety of weapons and if you collected weapons like in Dark Souls. Instead, you start out with all of the weapons. This does give you a lot of flexibility in playstyle, and you do unlock new skills for the weapons as you level up.For anyone who likes a good Souls-style experience but is not expecting an exact clone of the Souls formula, this is game is a good choice. Alternatively, I think it could also be a good way for younger players to try out the Souls experience without it being prohibitively difficult for them. My kids enjoy watching my play Dark Souls and similar games. I think my pre-teens could get into playing the game soon.In short, I highly recommend Asterigos. I'd really glad that I bought it, and I bet you won't regret it either.

_childDocuments_.review: Another reviewer described this best, as a "Souls-Lite" rather than a "Souls-Like." A lot of the familiar elements are there, and there can be a more challenging experience if you want one, but the game is vastly more accessible with both a "normal" mode (which I found to be slightly challenging at times) and an easy mode, which I can only imagine must be pretty darn easy.If the mere existence of an "easy mode" turns you off then, well, there you go, but you'll be missing out on an absolutely fantastic game.It's much more mobile than a true souls-like, where you can not only dart around faster and utilize a greater degree of weapon movement, but can even gain a trait to make your dodge much more responsive (at the cost of shorter I-frame duration). With all of the different weapon/build combos there's plenty of replayability for gameplay alone, and this is one of the few games where I enjoyed combat as much on the last boss as I did at any other point in the game.Speaking of bosses, there are no more than you'd expect (one for each zone, give or take a mini-boss or a boss for the zone's expansion). However, the variety of them and their mechanics makes this another rare game where I looked forward to the next boss fight, rather than dreading it. A couple of them even made me grin like an idiot as they were introduced.It's also visually and auditorially quite pleasing, not just in terms of the models and sound but the use of color and space. Weapons feel impactful (you definitely want to use a controller for this one), animations look fluid (mostly), and there were only a couple of zones where I wasn't at any time distracted by the environments or some of the characters.There are a lot of characters of course, and many of them have a lot to say. Not all of their dialogue is voiced, but when it is, it's great. When it's not, there's a lot of reading. There are also a lot of hidden things to find for more reading. If you don't mind reading a lot in a game (and I don't), and you find the story interesting enough to look for more details (and I did), you will get a lot more out of it than someone who ignores exploration or skips through text.However, on my second playthrough, skipping all text was pretty much a given, except after exploring different choices and options. It's a one-and-done sort of story, despite the allusions to alternate paths (they're not too meaningful) which brings us to the game's weaknesses.First of all, all of these elements, from style of gameplay, to aesthetics, to characters and story, are subjective, and you may take or leave them, hating everything I loved. But there are a few glaring issues which are more or less objective. They were not too big of an issue for me, but they may be for you.First is the A.I. I couldn't ever quite tell if enemies just had really low poise or were just freezing up. Using the staff is easy mode on all levels, as you can range and kite just about anything to death, sometimes before it even reacts. Enemy mechanics are quite fun, but they're not always consistent. Some will stop mid-fight as though having forgotten they were trying to kill you. This considerably increased the game's easiness.Second is the backtracking. Almost every large level has a means of creating a shortcut to its beginning, but these are not always obvious, or they may be delayed to very late in exploration. The Academy (which I otherwise loved) was probably the worst offender here, and where a lot of running back and forth over long distances became the most annoying. You gain  at around the 60% mark, which helps a lot, but is an ability that would have been welcome much earlier.Finally, the jumping mechanics are terrible, which can make one particular jump  absolutely maddening, especially as it's necessary to progress. Seriously, I wish I could skip that jump on every successive playthrough, it is so wonky. Add to that the weird combination of inputs to jump in the first place (one prone to sending you rolling off, rather than jumping, or jumping, rather than dodging), and you have a big thorn in the game's side.But to be honest, although memorable enough, I was still really reaching for those flaws. Not since Skyrim have I wished I was playing a game whenever I wasn't.Great game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have since revised my review after getting much deeper into the game.Initially I thought it was great. However, at some point, I started one shotting enemies with magic, so I bumped up the difficulty.  It didn't really change anything except for the fact I was taking more damage.Here is why I cannot recommend this game, even though I want to support an indie dev and welcome new IP's:STORY- it's confusing, and the voice acting is awfulCOMBAT- clunky, and the AI can be very exploited and will glitch outEXPLORATION-confusing. No map, no markers, vague hints. And the main quest has you backtracking constantly.  Questlines even stop mid exploration forcing you away from an area, only to have to return later in the story.CONCLUSION-In the era of backlog overload, I'd pass on this unless you have a lot of free time and patience.  I'd say it's worth $8.99

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but the similarities to the recently released Soulstice are striking - again we play a young girl who kills monsters in melee combat while exploring a city abandoned by god and the world. The city of Aphes was once the seat of an advanced civilization that researched and successfully used magic. Unfortunately, something went wrong in the process over time. Time to clear up the matter and rid the city of its problems. It's not exactly the first hack and slay action game on the market, but unlike very many competitors, it not only has the quality of graphics and animations right, but the playability fits as well. It's simply fun to move from battle to battle through the city, always getting new information about the background story. The battles aren't just against the same enemies over and over again, but against a variety of different enemies that always require new tactics to defeat.A city that has been suffering from a terrible curse for 1,000 years, full of horrible monsters and countless dangers... and a young girl is sent to sort out the situation. Typical computer game storyline, Shakespeare would turn in his grave at such a ridiculous premise, but we gamers can be glad to at least get some story. Actually, it's like that in most games anyway - we play a lonely hero who slashes his way through endless hordes of monsters in the fight against evil. And the story is actually not that bad, it is told in detail in many cutscenes, (magical) flashbacks and with the help of many written documents and contains quite a few more details than "evil wizard creates monster army and wants to conquer the world". Our decisions have an impact on the further course of the story.We play Hilda, a young warrior who is sent to investigate what happened to an expedition led by our father. Our father set out with some warriors to explore the city of Aphes - and has been missing ever since. So we'll explore Aphes, the fallen city of stars, and over the course of the game we'll try to solve its problems and restore the city to its former glory. To do this, we'll just have to destroy a few monsters. We can choose between several weapons, besides our short swords we also have a hammer, a spear and a wand (for ranged attacks) to choose from. With our shield we can block attacks. As a trained warrior, we can handle all of these things, though of course we'll get better and better as we progress through the game, focusing on specific weapons.We get to know Minerva, who has retreated with her faithful to an underground part of the city. This serves as our headquarters, where we can use the services of the blacksmith between missions or just relax. This is also where we receive new missions from Minerva. The city is influenced by Greek architecture and actually looks quite impressive... however, it is relatively empty. The interaction possibilities are limited. There are monsters hanging around every few meters, but little else is going on. A huge scenery with little content. Unfortunately, there is no overview map, and the individual sections are not that small.Using attribute points obtained in battle, certain characteristics of our heroine can be improved. Health points are increased, more damage is inflicted during attacks, and so on. Besides, there are also talent points to learn special abilities. For example, you can massively increase your efficiency with certain weapons - though of course you'll have to decide which weapon(s) you want Hilda to specialize in. Hilda can equip 2 weapons at the same time. Trinkets also improve hero attributes, while potions, salves or shards can be used for one-time bonus effects. Consumable items can of course be placed in fast access slots. Equipping two weapons at the same time and being able to quickly switch between them in combat, combined with the skills, talents and magic elements, leads - after a little practice - to incredibly fast-paced combat.A good-looking, challenging, yet accessible action-adventure game with many conversations, fast-paced combat but a relatively empty and repetitive game world.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice RPG set in a somewhat northern/viking/greek/roman-inspired world. First playthrough took me about 50 hours, but that's for a rather completionist approach. Pros: World design (looks beautiful with lots of details and hidden stuff), spells & skills (choose 2 of 6 different weapons to be used for fights, each with specialized techniques), fighting system (has a really intuitive and fluent feeling to me), story (is quite elaborated and well thought through).Downsides: Quest log (there is none, you only have a diary which contains some basic information), map (there is none, but a map would make this game about 50% easier); protagonist skins (since we're talking about a very young woman / girl here, some skins are just a bit too much skin and insufficient clothing); naming of NPCs (for lack of creativity, villagers or brawlers are simply named "Villager A", "Villager B" and so forth), enemy balancing (enemies seem to be set to a certain level which doesn't change when you level up -> first bosses are really hard to fight whereas in the second playthrough you just kill them in the blink of an eye).Overall a good game, although you have to keep lots of stuff in mind (when to do what & where) since some basic tools like a quest handling system are missing, which makes it easy to miss some quests and therefor parts of the story. 7/10Note: If you like dogs, be rather careful if you want to play this one, since the developers are clearly NOT dog-persons.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT : After playing through the DLC i can no longer recommend this game. The DLC is EA level cash grab, maybe even worse. Stay away from this janky Dark Souls copycat You'll get your money's worth of entertainment, but at the same time this game definitely isn't a must-play. I'd say the 8/10 is a bit too high, but 6.5-7/10 would be fair.I'll split this review into two parts, there will be some spoilers about gameplay itself but not much about story, since i really didn't pay any attention to it after like first 6hours of gameplayPersonally i really like this cartoony graphics style and the game is, at times, really nice to look at.I also like the progression system of this game. Right at the begining, in like first 10minutes, the game gives you all the weapons and you are free to experiment with them all and choose the ones that suit you the best(you always have 2 weapons equipped and can use them at the same time, combine attack of both mid-combo etc..). The weapons are upgradable, but all the upgrades do is increase the dmg you deal with that particular weapon. Upgrades do cost some rescources, which are quiet easy to come by, but if you are completionst, and would aim to upgrade all of them, then some grind would be inevitable. I personally was using daggers/staff and managed to get them both within 1 playthrough to +10/+9(+10 is highest) without any grind, but with quiet throrough exploration of the maps themselves.Besides weapons and upgrades, you also gain talents and atribute points for our protagonist Hilda. Those are quiet straight forward, you get some passive buffs, you get some active abilities etc... and what is nice is that if you make mistake/want to respec for different weapon(the talent points unlock more skills for particular weapon) the you can easily do so with potion from Quintus, or later on from the Iraneous guy so thumbs up for not punishing people for bad choices and allowing players to experiment with builds.Map design, in terms of the layout, is quiet well done and if you've played the mighty Dark Souls, especially DS1, then you will immediately see a lot of similarities to that game. There is ton of shorcuts to open, maps are nicely interconnected and exploration feels rewarding in terms of loot.Game is also pretty solid on technical level. During my ~30h of gameplay i encoutered only few bugs and had to forcequit the game only once because Hilda got stuck on some box. Also ran the game on GTX970(6-7year old card) on 2nd highest settings 1920x1080 at around 60ish FPS so if your PC isn't an absolute potato you should be able to run it without much issues. Even though i've gotten my money's worth of entertainment out of this game, there definitely was quiet a few instances where i was considering to just quit and don't look back.Even though i like the graphics style, i have to leave thumbs down for the devs because of the locations they chose to put in the game. First map you start in is nice lushish forest and is really gorgeous, but then you go to village that is ran down and looks as if it was in the middle of the desert. Then you go to ugly mines, then you go even deeper into the mine,then later in game you go to Alcatraz-like looking prison, then there is the mandatory sewer level that at very first glance you are like "huh, this looks like New Londo, but worse",the shelter itself is like firelink shrine from Dark Souls 3, which i really didn't like, then you have a city that could look real nice, but doesn't because of the fog and color pallete of blue/white/grey. There is few maps i enjoyed being in, but those are definitely in minority. In future DLCs, if there will be any, i would appreciate if the devs chose more interesting, colorful maps to really make that graphics style shine, because in the base game the mark is, for the most part, missed.I praised the progression system in "The good" part of this review, but the combat itself was intetionally not mentioned there, because it doesn't deserve to be there. The combat is serviceable, but feels super clunky at times. Game does not allow for animation cancelling, which is really annoying. For example:Staff has this "fire breath" looking attack, that you have to charge(the charging part is possible to cancel) but once you release the attack, which lasts for around 3-5 seconds, you are locked in position and you  move. This is real pain and can easily cost you your life if you haven't noticed an enemy behind you. In short, please add the posibility for animation cancelling.Bosses. Some of the bosses are quiet well designed(the crocodile that you fight at the very start of the game, Twin colossi or the big bird), but some of them are downright frustrating and they feel as if they were designed for a different game. BOSS SPOILERS AHEAD.Magic enchantments-you have at your disposal 4 elements(astral, fire, ice and lightning), but they are nothing more than switches of "how much DPS am i gonna do to this enemy". One would expect that fire would, i don't know, set enemis on fire, but no. If you have fire resistant enemy, you will just do less damage, if the enemy is weak to fire you are gonna do more and same goes for all of the other elements. There are some instances where you have to use specific element , but other than that, it's just DPS switch. Story. I really wasn't paying much attention to it, which speaks for itself. One thing i will say is, that the ending cutscene feels as if it was written before the rest of the story was. I Would like to say more about this game, but sadly character limit exists so yeah, this would be it. Thanks for reading.
