_childDocuments_.review: (Spoiler free)I finished the game after 50 hours and I have to say it ist pretty damn good, especially for an Indie-Debut-Game. Technical:The game is extremely well polished, I had no major bugs throughout (except a few spelling errors) and the sound- and art-design was absolutely phenomenal.Gameplay:I really enjoyed exploring this game and finding all the hidden materials in the world. The combat is very simple and straight forward but in a good way and I always had to think on my feet to survive (I played on medium difficulty). Trying out the different weapon-combinations was a lot of fun and the fights are pretty well balanced to make each weapon viable, though I am pretty sure you will have quite a difficult time without the staff.Story:The history and lore of Aphes and how the curse came to be is very interesting, the characters involved are quite well written and interesting and the way their relationship develops is believable. Hilda struggling with her lack of experience as a character-arc is an interesting idea, though I feel the payoff of her learning that there are consequences for her actions could have been given more weight by actually showing those consequences directly (perhaps in the ending slideshow).Bossfights:None of the bosses drop the ball as far as I can tell. They all have varied movesets that develop throughout the fight with the second boss being a particular standout. Unfortunately the last boss (no spoilers) did not really deliver anything memorable. It was well balanced and by no means bad but I feel like it should have been something more unique and interesting, to make the ending of the game feel more climactic.Conclusion:A great choice for fans of the souls-like genre with only a few rough edges that do not detract from the rock-solid experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I  wanted to like this game. It seemed like a scaled-down Dark Souls for those who don't have that kind of patience, or a more fleshed out Kena Bridge of Spirits. _childDocuments_.review: I was really torn on posting a review this early into the game, but it's got to be said that the narrative here is objectively bad. The gameplay is good, but not revolutionary. The story is interesting, even if it tries a little too hard to pull off the Dark Souls breadcrumb-style approach to lore. But if "Choices Matter" is a tag you care about, prepare to be disappointed. Instead of just letting itself be a linear Souls-like, Asterigos instead made the bizarre decision to give you no real choices, and then actively gaslight you into thinking there was a choice and that your decision was not just morally gray, but was actually the "evil" choice. And it's not just once, it's constantly, and the NPCs are all-in on shaming you for it. It's the weirdest narrative choice I've seen in a long time, and it makes an otherwise decent play experience feel really cumbersome.There is also a ton of time-inflation based on the lack fast travel between bonfires, you end up wasting a ton of hours traversing through completed areas trying to find the next one. I'm still going to try to finish it, but the second or third time the game artificially pulled the chair out from under me and tried to make it seem like I made a choice, I stopped pretending that this was a game you play for the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars is a third person action game set in a fantasy themed world of magic and monsters. Player character Hilda has travelled to the city of Aphes in search of her father, the commander of a legion of soldiers who are on their own quest to find a cure for their cursed king.•	There are 6 weapons to choose from and you can have 2 equipped, which allows you to quickly swap between them during combat. I mostly used the staff to attack from long range, and the daggers so that I could quickly dodge enemy attacks. You could also use sword and shield, spear, hammer, and bracers.•	Weapons can be upgraded to perform special attacks, and you can also use fire, frost and lightning magic.•	Enemy variety is good. In addition to warriors equipped with sword and shield, spear, bow, or magic staff, you’ll have to fight against minotaurs, harpies, lions, bulls, giant insects, and rock monsters.•	There are also several massive bosses who are quite challenging. While their health bars are a mile long, you can quickly lose half of your own health in a single hit from their powerful attacks. These fights were the most enjoyable part of the game.•	I played on “adventure” (medium) difficulty, which is mostly well balanced. I died a few times, especially during boss fights, but still made consistent progress.•	Non-boss enemy AI can be easily exploited at times. It seems like they’ve been programmed to defend specific areas, so if you back off far enough they’ll just disengage and walk away, allowing you to get in several free hits. Its also possible to use ranged attacks to aggro individual enemies to take out groups one enemy at a time while the others stand around and watch.•	Completing side quests is more annoying than it should be because Asterigos lacks two features that most modern games provide. Firstly, the journal doesn’t list active quests so its hard to remember what you’ve been asked to do by some random NPC a few hours ago.•	There’s also no map, which sometimes leads to confusion when simply trying to figure out exactly where you need to go. While progress through the main story is mostly linear, each area contains several branching paths that loop back around and can occasionally feel like trying to navigate a maze. •	Overall story quality is average. Hilda’s relationship with her dad was the most interesting part, but unfortunately the story was more focused on the local politics of the city which I didn’t really care about.•	Voice acting is good. The dialogue/writing lacks quality, but I think the actors did the best they could with what they had to work with.•	Key story conversations are voiced, but any “ask for more details” dialogue options are text only.•	Conversations feel low budget because they aren’t shown through typical cutscenes, just the normal gameplay camera angles. Also characters’ mouths don’t move when they speak, and their body language animations look stiff.•	It took me 26 hours to finish the main story.•	I didn’t have any problems with bugs, crashes, or framerate.•	Controls are fully rebindable and work well with mouse and keyboard.•	I like the colourful art style.I would have given Asterigos: Curse of the Stars a neutral rating if Steam allowed it. While the boss fights are the highlight, everything else is pretty average. I’d suggest waiting for a deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing rpg's for over twenty years. Some of my favorites are Kingdom of Amalur, Dragons Dogma, God of War. And, now this one, Asterigos. I really like the fights and weapons. I was going to main with  Hammer and sword and shield.  In nearly every single rpg or mmo I have ever played, the Caster/mage is weak and just a boor to play. ( Dragons Dogma has a awesome magic wielder, just so you know). But, Asterigos has created a magic class that just kicks  the bad guys off the planet. So, I went with the Staff and dual daggers. The Staff is amazing. Lots of spells to choose from. Love the story, so far only 24 hours in. Highly recommend this game.SO, after 54 hours total playing the game { round one  } I had a great time.  My criteria for whether I like a game is simple: Am I having fun. And I did. My compliments to the entire staff of Amerigos for making a awesome-to-play game.

_childDocuments_.review: This could have been a good game. It had potential. The combat is.... clunky. Every move Hilda makes is so slow compared to the enemies.Bosses are spongey and hyper fast movements compared to Hilda.--The devs idea of difficulty is slowing the player moves down and speeding up the enemies movements.There is SO MUCH exposition (AND LONG WINDED) in this its maddening. _childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: The best part about this game is that it lets you skip dialogues and (most) cutscenes. The story is entirely uninteresting, NPCs are forgettable, and the few side quests you can find might as well not exist.This is not an open world RPG, I wouldn't call it a souls like either. The closest it gets to Dark Souls is pointless "platforming" that's only there to justify having a jump button. There is no map of any kind, no fast travel between areas either, so running back to open up a side area once you unlocked a new ability is a very painful experience.None of the enemies are fun, interesting or challenging to fight, same goes for bosses. You can mostly run away from everything or attack them from range and you won't ever be in any danger.To top it all, the game is very badly translated, many of the menu text and dialogue options do not even make any sense.Basically, someone played a God Of War or Darksiders game, tried to replicate it and failed miserably in every single aspect. Do not buy this game if it's above $5-$10, you WILL regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some good stuff, some okay stuff, and some bad stuff.Good- the combat is solid. Not Nioh, mind you, but funnish. Doesn't take loads of skill IMO, but enough to keep you going, and the skill system is cool. I found the Hard level difficulty to be about right, but it ain't no Demon's SoulsThe 'Okay-' they obviously put a lot of effort into the story, but this ain't The Last Of Us. The story may be really good, but I'm just not here for a deep plot. It seems passable. However, there is a lot of story chatter sometimes, so you can't just ignore it. But X'ing through ten lines of dialogue breaks immersion. This isn't THAT bad- characters are alright, and it isn't forced ten minute cutscenes all over, but it's a little more story than I'm looking for. You may enjoy it! Really, the story isn't awful by any stretch.Bad- Enemy AI pathfinding- dumb as rocks.There is no map. Now, I like the idea of no map in the sense that it forces you to learn the layout of the game. It can add something; a certain intimacy with the levels. HOWEVER, many of the areas are homogenous. Which means- sometimes, there isn't a whole lot that makes the one look obviously different from the other. So it's hard to tell which of these similar looking rooms, with similar clutter in different arrangements, you may be in. It's not as easy to make a mental map when there is a lot of asset re-use. So that's a quibble, but here's the bad part:The missions give you NO help in figuring out where to start them. The first mission from the shelter, which is not tiny- I ran around for 15 minutes trying to find my way out. The thing about no map and no directions is- UNLIKE real life, you can't go to someone and say 'hey, I know you told me to go to Black Streets, but which direction is that out of here?' And that information is not offered.Likewise with the following mission- I beat the first boss, returned to my team, told them- and got some new missions. BUT- the missions are from a new area, in a totally different direction out of the main base. Which it doesn't mention. So I'm back in Boss one's area looking around the new paths that have opened up, and running into blockages everywhere.Might be that they did explain this to me, but I doubt it- I was skimming the text quickly, but I was reading it. At best, it was mentioned, but from a design point of view- HEY THE BAZAR IS NOT THROUGH BLACK STREETS would have been welcome information.So- the bad can be summed up with this- there is no map, which encourages you to get intimate with the environments, but there's also no good explanations, which will lead you to making the wrong choices with your well-honed gamer sense.Still a thumbs up. I've been griping a lot, but I am enjoying it. The lack of direction is tough though. Google it if you're running in circles.

_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Really had fun with this one! It's more of a beginner souls like, so if you're not that much into the pain of regular souls-likes it's still pretty fun. It obviously reminds a litte of fenyx rising, which I loved too, so it really appealed to me. I personally love the kind of a new twist on the regular souls like, that are just dark and grim. Not that it's always extremely colorful, but it shows more colors than other souls like games.A bit of a bummer is being unable to set a custom key binding, but they are working on it to fix it, so this will be solved in the future.The combat system is really fun and feels ok in my opinion. Yes, it could be improved and I think they are working on that as well, if i'm not wrong, but it wouldn't really bother me if they didn't change too much about it.Another more negative one is the auto focus. Sometimes it's pretty helpful, but when you fight in a smaller area, especially on like a bridge or similar places (where you can fall of) it's just annoying and I died several times because of it, so I started to play without the auto focus, but you can easily play without using it, so it's not really affecting your gameplay or experience that much.One last thing is that I would have prefered it, if some achievements would have been hidden, because there was one spoiler, that I'm not going to point out here.All in all I really enjoyed the game and can recommend playing it. Probably would give it a solid 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic in every way. It's like if Darksouls and God of War had a cuter, baby. The combat feels good, especially as you unlock further attacks through the skill tree, the enemies and bosses are dangerous and can easily take out an unprepared Hilda, and the story is a lot of fun to explore. honestly solid 8.5 or 9 out of 10only real thing I missed was the fashion-souls. Would love to have been able to have armor as a further piece of gearing up.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS NOT TRYING TO BE DARK SOULS - Other action games exist (as far back as Ninja Gaiden and older) that use checkpoints and bossfights. A whimsical, hack and slash adventure game with loosely interconnected levels, a cute protagonist, and combat focused around weapon arts. The relatively low difficulty made it something to enjoy on weeknights as a casual, enjoyable action game. It's rough around the edges and cheesy with a bit much dialogue and backtracking but this charming first title from a new studio is a diamond in the rough that deserved more attention and nowhere near this much negativity.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely underrated. I felt this was absolutely fantastic and will likely do additional playthroughs. My only negative is that the DLC is significantly overpriced. _childDocuments_.review: After having suffered from gaming depression for some time and finding out it was due to forcing myself to always finish what start, regardless whether I enjoy it or not, I stop playing games that are just not fun after giving them enough time to show their cards, but not enough to burn me out again.What I disliked about the game:The story so far was really boring, all over the place and excessively pushed down the player's throat. Characters often have dialogue trees straight out of full-on RPGs and you have to read most of that because only conversations directly related to story progression are voiced. And there are just so many characters in this game you can talk to and so many letters and scrolls you find that I stopped bothering after reading a bunch in the beginning and not finding a single bit of lore that interested me. Because of that most characters you meet are bland and forgettable. The fighting mechanics are lacking in depth as well and battles in general feel more like a round-based RPG, but you press buttons instead of choosing an action from a list. It's definitely not a souls-like imho, it doesn't fit any definition I know of. Music and Sound design? Unremarkable as well.In summary: quantity over quality? Oh well, I could write more about the level design and total lack of player guidance, but I'm off to find a different game I will enjoy now. Take care, bye.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with a good protagonist, plot, and gameplay. The major weaknesses of the game are in some bad character writing for some of the NPCs and some bad voice acting. Wish there was deeper progression on the weapons as they did feel like they plateaued too early, and the other techniques you get you just don't have the time to use in a combat situation.All that said, its a solid and fun game with in a well designed setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Nowadays, for whatever reason, I almost never end up staying invested in a game and sticking with it to the end. With Asterigos, I never felt like I had that problem. For perspective, I completed the game, did pretty much all the side quests, all the secret bosses, and (almost) got the secret ending in around 30 hours. I do think the story was genuinely interesting, and the game play was enjoyable as well. Yes, you have a limited set of weapons, but I used the daggers with the staff as a secondary, and the combat never got too dull. The art style is really charming and almost all of the characters have great voice actors and interesting stories. Yes, this is very much a AA game, you can tell they were working on a smaller scale, and if you go in expecting Elden Ring you'll be disappointed. But if you go in just wanting to run around a beautiful city, fight some dudes, do some side quests and look past some flaws, you'll come out the other end happy. I really hope this game does well enough to allow the developers to expand and make a sequel, I'd love to see what they could do with more time, more funding, and more people!

_childDocuments_.review: It is a competently made souls-like clone that lacks some things to make it great. I had fun playing it but it could have been so much better. The exploration gameplay is great - the whole map is interconnected and is really interesting to explore and see different types of zones. No demerits here.The combat is a mixed bag. Out of the 6 available weapons, I used the Spear and the Staff, and they made combat a complete joke even on max difficulty. The only stuff I slightly struggled with were the optional 'endgame' bosses that spawn right before the end of the game. The staff lets you just artillery strike enemies from half a map away and they can barely do anything about it. It doesn't work well on bosses as they tend to have quick gap-closer abilities, but for bosses you have a spear, which has a parry ability, that lets you nullify any damage from an attack, gives you a very strong counter-attack and has a chance to stagger your target. And you're heavily incentivized to pick two weapons and stick with them to the end of the game, since you'll be putting your trait points into weapon abilties, and putting your crafting materials in improving those specific weapons. Sure there are options to re-spec and to farm more reagents, but they are time-consuming and annoying.That said, the combat is still pretty enjoyable. I would have preferred it leaned in more on using more than the two weapons you pick for variety's sake, but even just using the two, I was satisfied with it throughout.The story is ... eh. It is waaay, waaaay, waaaaay too wordy. There are dialogue trees inside dialogue trees inside dialogue trees for pretty much any major NPC about the most minute uninteresting unimportant crap. I wasn't intrigued, I wasn't hooked, I didn't care. There are a few interesting character designs, but they end up standing still and doing nothing the whole game.Overall, it's still more positives than negatives and the negatives are tolerable and didn't stop me enjoying my time with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: i was realy wrong about this gameinitialy i thought "just another souls-clone, mixed with greek mythology"both takes couldn't be more wrongAsterigos is probably one of the best (if not the best) 3rd person action-rpg i ever played.why?a nigh perfect core-gameplay, aka the combat, exploration and progressionan incredible deep, highly detailed and well thoughtout world and stunning audio-visual design (neither video nor screenshots do the actual game justice)the most important part about any and all action games is the combat. Asterigos nails this part like no other.you basicaly get all possible weapons (the new dlc apperently added more options) pretty much from the get go. you can equip 2 weapons at the same, but mix and match at all times via the ingame profile (inventory). each active weapon has one normal attack and one respective special.these attacks vary incredible. from heavy hitting aoe hammer bashes, to sword'n board stabs, pike pokes to magical balls of fire. the sword'n shield might allow you to block, while the staff offers as it's special a snipe shot. doesn't sound that great? how about mix and machtching attack chains between each equipped weapon?you combo staff ranged attacks with the possibility to weave in a sword'n shield block'n parry at any point of the staff chain. or you combo with sword'n shield but suddenly you need to get out of the way? weave in a staff attack and your character jumps back while leaving an elemental aoe attack behind. this goes for all weapons and all combinations. now mix in unlockable (talent-tree) ressource costing skills (like creating magical shields, aoe-buffs, damaging companions, large scale attacks), and the ability to switch your attack element via simpel button press (often enough changing each weapons effect significantly) and you get so many tools and options. it's snappy, meaty, responsive, and one of the best combat-systems i ever played in one of these games. then there's the progression.you earn exp by killing stuff, each level up offering you one attribute point (or two every two levels) and one talent point (large, hughe, talent tree) to shape your character. the talent tree is also very well done. it doesn't just offer both new active and passive abilites, or changes existing abilities completly (these changes can be turned on and off in the perk-menu), but furthermore it weaves in the usual % increases to stats with actual abilities...you get 2 for one. to use skills unlocked in the talent tree you also don't need to have the respective weapon equipped which offers just so much variety. similiar to soulslikes you also find materials (enemy drops, enviroment) to upgrade pretty much everything: weapons, elemental damage, etc. . and while there might not be a real armor-system (you unlock and get different cosmetic outfits), basicaly you get 4 permanent gear slots, to equip different "trinkets", offering everything from mitigation boni to changes to your loadoutsize. unlocking hidden chests doesn't just reward it's contents, but you also fill a sorta battlepass bar, which unlocks new stuff after certain keystones are met (like permanent increases to your "mana" or stamina, new outfits, etc.). the world might look like an oldschool disney movie ala Hercules come to live, and it's very pretty to look at, especialy in motion, but it's certainly not ment for children. the game gets dark very fast. adiction, heck even canibalism, sorrow and pain litter these streets. main and side quests are all part of a greater narrative so is the incredible amount of lore-material filling this world. names and some design aspects might look like greek mythology, but it's not. it's a sci-fi / fantasy world, build around seemingly mythological aesthetics. your character is part of a nordic-special task force, many of your allies could very well exist in the greek patheon. the voice over, writing and music are stellar. especialy the music is just incredible well done, often mixing arabic, greek, even modern influences while beeing very well produced and always fitting the enviroment you are currently traversing. what the game is not is a souls like. you can save at all time (hard save), which will save the general world state (dead enemies, looted stuff), but not your position, you will resapwn at the last checkpoint (well) upon loading. you also do not lose your exp-ressource upon death, just a little bit (standart 10%) of your currency (trading, upgrading) which is permanently lost, but easy to grind back. also there are difficulties.yes, checkpoints (well) do respawn enemies upon resting and thus restoring your health, etc. . yes, bosses can deal insane amounts of damage.but calling this a soulslike is a stretch. it's a masterfully crafted 3rd person action rpg. think Zelda, meets Metroid-vania, meets Fromgames. most of critic i saw on steam was down to a lack of handholding or direction. there's no questmarkers, no map. but the game is designed for exploration. each area is distinct, hidden loot or lore around every corner. exploration (and also backtracking) is part of the core game design and it's absolutly wonderfull.you should believe all these youtube videos claiming Asterigos is an overlook gem. it's hard to describe how well made this game is. i realy do hope a sequel is already in planning. great IP, wonderfull game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:The main character (Hilda) is forgettable and whiny as hellThe story is forgettableSome of the maps are dull and needlessly confusingThere is little to no assistance on what to do, you are told once and then left to figure it outOnly some NPCs have voice lines, the rest are just word wallsThe voice acting is shoddy at best*Nitpick* A LOT of the NPCS don't have names, they're just "ruffian A, ruffian B, ruffian C, Hunter A, Hunter B, and the commoners are just named "Poor" Throughout the game that bothered me more than it should because it felt really, really lazy.Pros:The combat was funThe weapons were diverseThe skill tree was AWESOME, gives much room to experiment withYou can use two different weapons that will not breakYou can choose different elements to permanently enchant your weapons and change on the fly after acquiring them.The music is 10/10 especially for the bossesThe boss fights were great and the most funThe artwork is beautifully doneYou can change keybinds if you wantedYou can choose the difficultyStat point attributes are simple and easyPersonally, I didn't care for the game about half way through, but I finished it because of the same reason that I am recommending it and that is because I already paid for it. _childDocuments_.review: I really kind of hate this game..This is a mostly fine action adventure RPG. I hesitate to say it's Souls-like because it does a few things to set itself apart from Souls games that I find put it more in line with a more traditional action RPG, like across between a Souls game and something like Devil May Cry, or Castlevania Lords of Shadow.The things I like, in the interest of fairness, are the character designs, the world building, and *sometimes* the combat, although I'll get to that. It's.... it's not technically competent, there are absolutely a ton of bugs and design flaws, but it is a STABLE game. I don't get unexpected crashes and the performance has been admirable. I'm able to mostly maintain a high framerate at ultra settings, so credit where credit is due.I like that the game gives you a variety of different weapons from the get go to experiment with as opposed to something like the classic God of War that just hands you 1 weapon and has you continually unlock moves and combos with it-- although you can also unlock different perks and moves for each weapon with a talent point system.The things that are frustrating in it are unfortunately things that I see many Souls-like games try to do to great detriment to the quality of the game; try to pack it with a ton of extra mechanics and systems that add nothing and overcomplicate the game to "differentiate" it. For example, the game not only gives you a compliment of different weapons to try with their own playstyles, but it  forces you to use 2 at once. This is a horrible mistake. While the idea of choosing two weapons to use that compliment each other-- maybe 1 slow, heavy weapon, and one quick weapon-- sounds cool, the controls are poorly optimized for this, and the game is bloated with so many other systems during combat that I mostly find myself cursing whoever made this decision. The game, aside from the weapons, also has an element system that you can change on the fly, a Dark Souls-style item quadrant for quickly using consumable, a special technique system that has special, mana-fueled attacks for each of the weapons, and 'special' attacks for each of the equipped weapons. This is too much. The best demonstration of this I can give is the game's comical control rebinding screen that has so many things that are required to sit in specific places in the controller I don't know why they bothered to allow rebinding. Any attempt I've made to rebind these has failed because it left a required control, wired to one of the games many systems,  absent. And I think this is the deepest wound that shows how overly bloated with unnecessary things this game is, if you can't already tell from the combat.And in the midst of having these convoluted systems, you get oddities like a required, dedicated jump button that is used extremely rarely, to the point that I'm baffled why it's there. Dark Souls resolves this issue, maybe not elegantly, but it at least understands that the other controls are more important. Asterigos wastes your controller space with this thing you almost never use expect to access some secret collectibles or resources.The combat. Ugh. It really is a spectrum between classically satisfying action game combat and a cheap system that uses tricks and artificial difficulty to imply a level of challenge it never earns. The game is lousy with projectiles. More than one of your weapons allows you to make ranged attacks, and they do not consume mana, they consume your stamina, so essentially you have unlimited ranged attacks. If you think this breaks the game to a degree, you'd be right. It compensates by making enemies have tons of projectiles they can throw, or summon, or conjure, and these are usually awful. Your projectiles stop at the first enemy they encounter. You'd expect enemy projectiles to behave identically, and you would be wrong. Enemy projectiles can pass through whatever enemies are in front of them to get to you and this is not OK. Certain enemies can conjure a ranged attack to trigger under you, and they don't require line of sight which is also not OK.But there are plenty of other problems. Your character's attacks can't handle different terrain elevations, so you'll be trying to attack an enemy on stairs slightly lower than you and miss every attack. Bosses are cheap and poorly designed, often not telegraphing major attacks, or having horrible hit detection that sometimes winds up causing damage for attacks you successfully dodged. They all also essentially follow the same formula of having 1 attack that can be comboed over and over just "until you take damage." AOEs are too broad and deal damage to you (LOTS of damage) when you're not near them.The game also has bugs. In the briefing after the black streets, the overlay with documents wouldn't go away so I couldn't see what I was doing. When I tried to keep pressing cancel to clear it, my character closed the dialog entirely and was chided by the NPC. In the same dialog, the left and right arrows indicating more pages were set on the document instead of to either side, and for some reason the designs thought that these arrows should be the SAME COLOR as the parchment.There's a light you eventually get to help you in dark areas, and the light also has some helpful exploration functions, but it's relegated to an inventory item that you need to use in order to turn on and off. This should just be a thing that's allocated to your character and stays on, since I don't see any reason why you'd ever take it off. It's a weird design decision.As I sit here and type this, the thing that pissed me off enough to finally stop giving this games chances was a boss that appears in the area as part of a scripted sequence. The sequence ended, but doesn't do anything to communicate to the player that it's over, so I took a ton of damage from an incoming attack. I left and did the whole bonfire thing to start over, since I consider this pretty cheap. The next time I hid behind a wall, and wouldn't you know it, the ranged attacks go through walls. So now here I am just trying to make it to a place where I can even start observing and seeing what kinds of things this enemy can do other than cheat, and I've already wasted 2 rests on it. These are the kinds of things that betray that the game doesn't respect you and doesn't respect your time.I cannot recommend this game. I have hopes that they'll eventually fix the weird walking animation for Hilda, curb projectiles, stop making me go back and 'select' that I accept a mission after my character has already agreed to accept it in dialog, and that some of the bloated mechanics will be trimmed down to be accessible and useful in combat instead of a steamer trunk full of bad ideas. But I'm not holding my breath.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen the term 'souls-lite' to describe this game, and with my limited experience in the genre(Elden Ring and Code Vein, neither finished yet), I'd say that fits. The HUD, overall feel of combat and weapon progression are familiar, with the big difference that character leveling in separate, with a more traditional exp system. This exp is not lost in any manner on death, so it feels less punishing to die. And in addition, you only lose some 'Stardust' (the money side) on death, although it is instantly gone, and not dropped.The game as a whole feels more forgiving than the other games I mentioned, which, combined with the exp, make this feel like a good option for someone whose intimidated by the genre, and can scratch the itch of veterans that want a slightly 'tamer' experience.A few negatives though.Lack of a map, no mini-map, nothing, can make it frustrating to get from point A to B.Side quest tracking, made more obvious by the prior issue, it can be a chore to remember what side quests you have active, and where/what you need to do.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:- The customization of you skills/talents is very interesting and fun. It makes leveling enjoyable as you unlock new talents. - The other good thing is the different weapon customization and elements. I would play around with different builds for fun. Sometimes it felt like I didn't need anything other than daggers though, since they are so mobile. The gameplay is enjoyable but not spectacular. Overall the game seems pretty easy, unless you want to lock your XP but then you don't get the fun talents. Overall the talents and different weapons is what makes this game fun and unique to other games.- I like the design of the maps. I'm a bit of an explorer in games and it was enough to make me feel like I could explore but also not like that's all I was doing. The assets aren't as bad as others have said but they are pretty simple.- Game runs smoothly, no issues. It's mean for controller though so I'd recommend sticking with that.The Bad:- Sound design is just terrible. I don't know if it's because my headphones offer surround sound, but enemies often sounded like they were coming from behind when they were in front of me. - Story isn't engaging and is executed poorly. Often times you are just given too much information/text and I found myself wanting to speed through it so I could get to fighting.- The Voice acting isn't great and the dialogue isn't any better.- The enemies attack patterns can be a little basic and exploitable. Overall: It's an okay game. I enjoyed the combat versatility but there's not much that stood out besides this. It might be worth getting at a discounted price or if you don't have any other games in this genre to play and you're getting a craving.

_childDocuments_.review: is done and dusted. This is a pretty honest Soulsborne experience, albeit a lot more colorful, with a lot more dialogue and a full story, and generally easier gameplay overall. In other words, Souls vets will enjoy it, but people new to the genre will also find it to be very approachable.Combat is quite fluid, with a fair amount of special moves and such. The areas can definitely be confusing and there is are no maps to consult, so you’ll be going off of memory, which is fine once you unlock fast travel. Until then, you’ll probably feel lost and wander for a bit. If there is a sequel, a map is thing I'd definitely include. The game does reward exploration. There is a bonfire system in the form of teleporters, and there is a central hub where you can upgrade gear, buy stuff, advance quests, get new missions, and so on. Actual leveling can be done anywhere, and includes an ability node system centered around your weapons.Speaking of weapons, you basically summon them from a magic bracer you wear, and although you can upgrade them in various ways, you get all the weapons in the tutorial section. What you can find or craft/buy are trinkets (buffs), materials and consumables. You also don’t leave “souls” on the ground when you die, although you do pay a souls penalty when you are resurrected.Anyway, I didn’t do all the side quests and it took me about 24 hours to do what side quests I did finish plus the main story. There are a lot of optional bosses as well. All in all, there is quite a bit of game here, and I expect you could easily add another 10-20 hours if you’re planning to do all the content. You will also have to play twice to get all the cheevos, and my recommendation would be to use a guide for your second run as the eight (out of ten possible) conditions you need to meet to get one of the endings are very specific and easy to mess up.Btw, I played this exclusively on the Steam Deck. It was a fantastic game for the system. Which reminds me: the graphics were stellar and the voice acting, of which there is a lot, was also very well done. The protagonist, although not voiced by Ashly Burch, sounds a lot like her, and if you’ve played either Horizon game, you could be forgiven for thinking of Aloy as you listen to the dialogue lol.*I did receive a review key from tinyBuild pre release. Highly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: I highly enjoyed this game! I'd describe it as something of a souls-lite, in that it definitely has carry over's and design stylings of souls games, but, also a lot of just typical action-adventure RPG stylings. For those who are on the fence with soulslikes due to their generally very high difficulty, I found the medium setting to be a really fun experience, it had a few difficult moments, but, very casual compared to a souls game, more in line with what you'd probably expect from your typical RPG.The game is very story-centric and I'd say overall it's pretty solid on that front, there is a lot of dialogue and writing in the game so that might be hit-or-miss for people, but, I thought the dialogue was fairly well done with great voice acting particularly for the protagonist, and the lore dump writing while fairly dense at times was quite interesting and gave a lot of insight into the events and structure of the world and the people within it.The game definitely isn't perfect by any means, it sorely needs an update to its journal and general quest handling, as well as either needing more guiding indicators in-world for getting around when exploring or backtracking or a basic map, I mean look, your character is frequently writing down information and observations in their journal, it would only make sense for them to be keeping some sort of roughly drawn map for getting around, or even if the map is a no go, at least keeping track of quests and objectives better, I know the point is to focus more on the organic exploration and discovery, but, even from a lore and in-world perspective, it doesn't make sense to have so little info given the nature of the protagonist and the mission they are on.There's a lot I could say about the game because I truly did love my experience with it, but, I know it's also highly tailored to me in style and setting and thus I'm definitely more able to overlook faults that would otherwise be pretty frustrating. I certainly recommend the game, but, of course, I'd suggest reading a couple of reviews both good and bad, and watching some gameplay to get a better idea if it is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Pre-release review (Spoiler free)While it is tagged/advertised as a souls-like - this game really feels nothing like it. The combat is fun and diverse, the game gives you many different weapons to choose from right from the start so you can mix and match a build that you enjoy playing with. Whether that is a spear throwing mage, or a hammer wielder that switches to daggers to quickly finish off their enemies. The world is colorful and rich with details, and every location feels different from the other. Following the main objectives, there are also many side missions that can be done in all the different regions. At the end of each main mission, you will be facing a boss and I must say I actually really liked the boss designs in this game. Especially monsters from the animal kingdom.  The bosses in this game aren't ridiculously hard and the animations are good, and that is what really spiked my interest in playing this game. As this is a pre-release review I sadly can't share too much of the story and don't want to spoil anything but overall you are playing as Hilda, a warrior set out to save the world from the Asterigos curse that was brought upon the people by the evil aphenian Eumenidies. The story isn't dragged out and all cutscenes/dialogue has voice acting, which I really like, and there are lots of written lore that can be picked up and read from your journal. Overall, I really enjoyed my time with this game and I would definitely recommend this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Really loved this game. Bought it initially as a test for myself in the souls-like genre, but this game is so accessible for all styles of gameplay. I guess this is what happens when a company focuses on delivering an enjoyable product to players to gain profit, rather than a lackluster product peppered with micro-transactions and gutted content as dlc. This game gives you the whole package for the price you pay and its totally worth it.Points that i loved:Voice actingMusic [lovely]Level design, textures, detailsPerformance [no issues, smooth experience]Game play [loved parrying haha]Story line, writing, dialogueAccessibility Art [loved the journal art in particular]Points that i didn't like:Honestly i can't think of any, but many people didn't like that it doesn't have a map. _childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is a lot of fun, and I do recommend it if you are into third-person action RPGs.  I'm hesitant to call it a souls-like though, as the combat feels a lot more reminiscent of Kingdoms of Amalur.  The combat is fun, with 6 fairly distinct weapons to choose from with their own skill trees and play styles.  Despite not really agreeing with the souls-like tag, Asterigos clearly shares plenty of aspects with souls-likes - bonfire-esque resting points (conduits), enemies respawn after you die/rest at one of the conduits, dodge rolling with iframes, a stamina bar, etc.  There's a few things that differentiate it pretty strongly though, and make it less of a souls-like.  The first being that even though there is a stamina bar and dodge rolling, your attacks don't consume any stamina.  Second, and more important, is the story/world - it's not ambiguous and open to interpretation like in Dark Souls. Rather, it's a linear story which is central to the progression in the game.  Also, there are three difficulty options, meaning that the game won't necessarily be that difficult for you.  I've been playing on the medium difficulty, and outside of some environmental hazards I haven't really died at all, so if you are looking for that Dark Souls difficulty, I'd advise you to play on the hardest difficulty.Regarding performance, the only issue I've had is frames dropping for a few seconds when entering a new area for the first time.  I haven't encountered any bugs.Despite having only played Asterigos for 6 hours, I think I have a good grasp on the game, and I do recommend it.  Just keep in mind that if you are looking for another Dark Souls-like experience, you probably won't get a great one here - you'll instead get a fun action game centred around its linear story.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly good, story-rich action rpg, that no one noticed. The combat reminds me of Dark Souls, but feels better, especially good with keyboad and mouse, something that From can never achieve. It is done right. Not difficult, but can be challenging on hard. But there is a bigger focus on the story part of the game. Dialogues and notes, and more dialogues and notes, and more... Sadly, less important dialogues aren't voiced and it's the biggest downside of the game for me, really breaks the immersion. Lots of side quests are well hidden in those dialogues, sometimes too hidded, you need to speak with every NPC until you're sure they won't say anything new, then speak again just to be sure. The locations are well made, encouraging exploration and rewarding it. Many secrets are hidden here and there, they're also done right. Not always obvious, but nothing crazy. I had fun looking around for them. The performance is great, always stable fps on 1060 without a single frame drop or stutter. No crashes. No bugs that I could notice. it really is a big surprise during the times, when every game comes out as a broken buggy mess, that barely works. Good job devs. For me it's a solid game. I didn't expect it to be that good.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars is at times great, mostly good but on occasion bad, however, on the whole it has an impressive amount of quality content. It is good enough for me to keep an eye on the developers’ future projects. this review might be updated after the release of the DLC.The game takes place within the Cursed City of Aphes where you travel to re-establish contact with your father, the commander of an operation to cure your king from a curse. However, you quickly get involved in the matters of the city and the plots of the factions. The story feels well-paced without superfluous tangents and is broadly well told. However, there is some exceptions to this, particularly the overwhelming amount of dialogue when you first reach the . It slows the game down to a crawl and unfortunately the information you receive is not too interesting. Unless you enjoy reading about worldbuilding. These conversations are typically handled without any further player input which gives you some insight into the player character Hilda, but in certain cases you are given dialogue options. Since there are only a few of them they can have relatively large consequences such as affecting quest rewards or your progress towards a specific ending. Furthermore, this game has something called  that are recorded conversations from various points in the timeline, unfortunately they are visually completely static. Personally, these are some of the most intriguing conversations, as I love the way it lets me slowly uncover the history of Aphes and its inhabitants. There are also a number of side quests, and for the most part they could have been handled better. It is mostly fetching items or running between two characters so it can get pretty vague especially since no one repeats themselves. Yet there is a journal, surely it is of some help, right? No, the journal is mostly Hilda’s thought and reactions to the quests, which I do like, however, most people would have written down what they are supposed to be doing. As I have made clear there is a lot of reading, but there is also voice acting in this game, typically reserved for quests and . It is understandable why they limited the amount of voice acting, but what is here is not flawless either. For the most part its fine, and sometimes it gets really good, but when it is bad it is really bad and sometimes you cannot even hear them over the cacophony or music. Asterigos is obviously not a realistic game, which is good, it leans into its more fantastical aspects and gives you a lot of artistically different environments and enemies while they are still clearly of the same world. It also has a nice contrast between more vibrancy and colour versus foggy greys each making the other sections stand out more. The enemy designs are also quite cool especially some of the later enemies, such as the guards of Styx. It is quite clear what they drew influence from, and it works rather well. There is also the aforementioned journal, there are a number of things relating to it that I like. Firstly, they added the neat detail that Hilda actually writes in it when it gets updated. Secondly, and more importantly every page of it gets covered in her drawings that relate to the quests you are doing. I thought it was kind of cute. The fact that they also look good is just a bonus.Regarding the soundtrack, its great it has unique songs for bosses, areas and as rewards for completing certain quests. It knows when to be bombastic, but it also knows when more melancholic or sombre tracks suit something. It is probably the most consistently high-quality aspect of the game.   This is an Action-RPG therefore you get attribute points and talents both of which are rather self-explanatory. Naturally the talents are more interesting, you get various types that can be divided into augments which are passive, skills which you activate and perks that typically carry trade-offs, like changing a movesets. The inclusion of all of this is good particularly if you do a low-level playthrough and so can only select a limited number of talents. In such cases perks can change the way you approach an encounter while on a high-level playthrough you might mix and match perks to a greater degree.    Concerning the active skills, they are rather powerful and come in many different forms each requiring your AP resource. The quickest way to recover your AP is by drinking a potion but it also replenishes while you are fighting. I especially like the skills that includes dashes as they can be used to kite enemies while damaging them. It also synergises well since the game favours an offensive playstyle as it recovers AP more rapidly. However, the game is not difficult, enemies telegraph their attacks very clearly which makes for an easy dodge or an easier parry with the spear, as a result encounters are hardly ever a challenge, but they are fun due to the fast-paced combat and the way different weapons work together and mix their combos. One particular issue is the damage feedback when you are hit with projectiles. Sometimes Hilda does not react at all, and you might not even notice that you were hit, while in other cases you will get a devastating stun that seems to last an eternity. It is even more dangerous if you get stunned while near any lingering area of effect damage as those are atypically deadly. These things can make a few bosses a bit annoying, but it is easily surmountable as no boss is particularly complex, though a few of them are still spectacles, especially the last boss. The rest are a bit varied in quality, the worst of which being an early boss that forces you to wait for an extended amount of time, and one hours later that seemed to feature respawning enemies. As for the best it would probably be the aforementioned final boss, an optional boss that while featuring respawning enemies is an actual fight, and the three duel fights. On another note, it was rather disappointing to see that all but one of the optional bosses were locked behind an end-game event. Most of them are not even unique, as they are boss variants of enemies you have already fought against but with a few more attacks. It is fine to do it this way, but I find it a bit tragic too.   One of my favourite things about this game is the interconnectedness of the areas especially in the early game. There are shortcuts looping around within a region but there are also several unlockable paths that connect them to each other and back to the , however after unlocking teleportation the areas become more self-contained.Unfortunately, actually exploring the areas is less interesting, in general the only thing worth considering are the collectibles and the quest items, as the rest of it feels very unrewarding. Yes, there are items and chest to pick up but the only thing you receive are consumables or crafting material and in low numbers at that.What they could have done is reward you with e.g., trinkets, reusable consumables or parts of an unlockable outfit. Something like this would make certain chests stand out and the chance that you could get something special would elevate the rest of the experience Speaking of there are some chests that do stick out, because they are mimics. Outwardly I could never figure out if they have any special tells which is a problem since their grab can be lethal, but you can in fact tell them apart by striking them or by aiming at them. I dislike that that seems to be the only way as you feel foolish for attacking every chest, but the mimics are placed rather effectively, and I often found one just after letting my guard drop.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is incredibly fun and really sucks you in. It is a Souls-Like for sure with the stamina meter, roll/dodge, dying and reviving at a "bonfire" while losing some currency. BUT it is way more forgiving, the level progression is not linked to the currency you collect and with the game providing all the weapons at the start for you to choose two to play with at anytime you don't need to worry about gearing out after halfway through the game for your play style. The Combat is really fun, as you level through different weapon trees it will unlock different attacks/patterns and abilities that change the flow of you attacks. Also, the different enemies and types of attack patterns between all the regions didn't leave me wanting anymore, I had fun fighting everything. The only draw back to the combat I have is there is not way to check the weaknesses (elemental) for each enemy, causing me to do a lot of attacking, run away, swap element, attacking and again and comparing the numbers. Other than that I had fun with the combat and enjoyed every special animation done. The story was really great as well, I enjoyed that certain outcomes and decisions made throughout the story that you may seem insignificant at the time really does change the outcome of certain situations. The main story will have you going through each of the area thoroughly as you progress, and there are several side mission you stumble upon across that way. My main gripe with the side mission is there is no way to track them so if you don't pay attention and do it right away you'll probably forget. Some of the side missions are story-line based as well to where instead of going and doing the boss of that region you have to back track to the beginning of the region to drop something off then go back through the whole region to fight the boss. Overall I give the game a 8/10, Solid combat, great story, forgiving enough to not make your blood boil, but hard enough to make you have to take a few of the bosses a couple tries. The main downside I had with this game is that you don't unlock the teleport feature between the "bonfires" early enough in my eyes. Forcing to run through so many different zones again and again to get back to where I left off for first 10 hours of the game was monotonous.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big souls-like fan, but I did not enjoy this game. To initiate one, you have to stumble upon some random door where you get some voiceless text from someone you can't see needing you to go fetch some random thing or deliver something to someone. Many of these quests require you to run back and forth between doors and sometimes NPCs to complete the quest. The supposed decisions you make in the game don't really seem to matter. _childDocuments_.review: This was a really unexpected gem. I played this on next fest and expected a basic little soulslike romp but ended up getting sucked into this world for 50 hours.I can tell a lot of heart went into this, its such a charming game world with a whole host of interesting characters. Some rambling thoughts on it all:The combat is fun and gives you some options right off the bat for weapon types, you can carry 2 at a time and each weapon has its own skill tree with some of the later skills feeling very powerful and fun to use. The only downside to this is the upgrade materials are expensive and fairly hard to come by so despite filling the skill trees out for my first weapon set around halfway through the game I didnt really have enough to switch over to a new set for variety sake. But theres ng+ for that. I enjoyed almost all of the bosses and enemies, I played on the hard setting and it was an enjoyable difficulty with no major wall points just a handfull of tries for each difficult part that never dipped into true frustration. The story is what surprised me the most. This game is absolutely loaded with lore, and to get the most out of the story (or really to get anything out of it at all) you do have to be willing to coax it out of optional dialogue options, side quests, and notes found in the world. Basically you are piecing together what happened a thousand years ago and the relationships between characters and how that all comes together to affect the present time. It was refreshing to play something without much handholding, theres a main quest tracker which i suggest disabling in the menus but aside from that theres no map or waymarkers, sidequests are kept in a journal with illustrations and notes instead of a "quest tracker" and there is a ton of missable content in the way of items and lore to pick up that then lead to further interactions and quests. I really do recommend playing this at a slow pace and soaking up the world.The game world is quite large with levels that are fairly porous and have shortcut connections within themselves and connections to neighboring areas, teleporting will have to be unlocked later in the game so its up to you to navigate and understand shortcuts for awhile. Some downsides:the 2 worst issues that affect the whole game are, it does that thing that ive seen some other games do where distant enemies will have reduced animation framerate, and then some sort of interpolate blur thing on top of that so they look really wacky from afar. But im not even talking cross map it can happen even within aggro tether range. Another issue is direction sound is really bad, enemies will often sound like they are behind you and you can clearly hear things even if they are behind multiple walls. Keybinds are not currently supported as of writing this but are planned to be added later. But as long as you are on a qwerty keyboard the default bindings are fine and I still prefer it over a controller. Those issues aside, a really nice game and I definitely got my money's worth. Its clear a lot of care went into the game and it has a sort of oldschool charm to it. I hope the devs continue to make more. There is a dlc coming out next year which I will check out for sure. These sort of AA indie titles are always such a good experience for me, I come in with no real expectations and less money on the line and walk away feeling really good about the experience. Hopefully you enjoy it too if you give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear developers, please repeat after me: if we're going to rip off the souls-like formula, let's actually make a good game.  This review pains me because this game has highly unique blend of mechanics: Rome/beautiful location + souls-like.  But what a slog it was!This game is arguably bigger in size than any typical soulslike game and that's because the areas are ridiculously drawn out.  Checkpoints are very, very far apart in some cases, which makes unexpected death significantly more frustrating than a typical souls game. And die unexpectedly you will!  This game is clunky as all hell!  As many other reviewers mention, the game doesn't always register key presses as succinctly as a dark souls game.  This results in sometimes the game not picking up a pause or you needing to spam the health button to get one to fire off while breaking mid combo.  The game also lacks a lot of quality-of-life mechanics and does absolutely nothing to point you in the right direction when you end up wandering the map for minutes on end.  There was one mission where you have to get 4 keys to open a door.  I spent hours searching the swamps for 4 keys but alas you only get the 3rd key when you do a side mission that requires knocking on random doors.  Then the 4th key just appears at the door. Again, no visual queues or anything to guide the player.  There's also just plain poor computer programming in this game like the fact that you can buy infinite potions and it doesn't prevent you from buying more than the max you can hold on hand... so the extras just get purchased and vaporized?  Oy.And this game is just so, so unnecessarily long.  There is lore freaking everywhere and probably 20 straight hours of dialogue if you really read through it all.  I just don't understand what the hell the devs were thinking.  Like, they could've just put a Rome skin on a dark souls game but they had to add so much lore at the expense of tweaking the gameplay.  The result is a mess that 50% of the time does not respect the player's time.Developers - you can still save this game.  Just rip out half of it and we'll be good, mmmkay?

_childDocuments_.review: So, Asterigos is not a great game, sadly.  I had seen some trailers and liked the idea of souls-esque combat in an ancient roman setting.  Stylistically, that's very much my jam. Unfortunately, while the combat has some neat ideas with the dual weapons that you can combo between on the fly, hot-swappable elements to exploit enemy weaknesses, and of course big special moves to help you take down bigger baddies, it all just falls apart in the execution.The combat feels decent enough when you focus on your own moves, but enemies are kind of erratically aggressive. Hits deal a lot of damage when they connect, but so far into the game there's very little reason to be afraid. The game gives you more healing than you will ever need, and enemies often let you just stand and wail on them in-between their own attacks which come out haphazardly, and far too seldom.The first story-boss, Baraad, is no exception. While he does have a bevvy of moves to make the fight varied, and brings them out gradually to ramp up the challenge as the fight goes on, the whole thing just moves too slowly to be any fun. It's like a poorly rehearsed stage fight, where the actors have to constantly, and politely wait and check that their partner is ready for the next phrase of combat. Plus he's got stupid amounts of health that drag the fight out for far too long given how humdrum it feels.And as if that's not bad enough, the writing and acting are just a complete miss for me. The story is both simplistic nonsense and too convoluted for anyone's good, throwing new proper nouns at you without any context every few story beats, and the dialogue and voice acting are at best Saturday morning cartoon levels. Sometimes not even that.Sadly, this is not a game I recommend at all. It would need quite a lot of polish to be enjoyable in the long run

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game made with love. I'm so chuffed I took a chance on it after coming across the title. It is a beautifully balanced action adventure with Dark Souls styling - a growing favourite genre of mine, the Souls-lite ;P Many aspects of it reminded me of 'Ashen', but the endearing character of Hilda as lead heroine (what a stellar protagonist) easily launched the story and the gameplay into it's own uniqueness. The combat is engaging and punchy; shield combat is particularly satisfying - I would recommend playing the game on Hard/Challenge difficulty to truly make it shine (I do hope in a sequel that the extra risk might yield greater rewards as well, instead of mere stat alterations).The world, which encourages environmental exploration and is a pleasure to discover, the lore, the narrative, the art, the design, ambience, these were all unexpected masterpieces presented in this game and of a calibre unexpected when first considering the title. The only little flaws for me were some odd bits of dialogue and a few exchanges that seemed out of place, or more precisely, out of character, and some pieces of lore (that went on for pages) broke the pace of exploration a bit too much. Otherwise, this game is a triumph of its genre and expresses an incredible talent of a passionate indie? development team. I hope Asterigos sells well. I hope the studio makes a sequel. I cannot wait to play their sequel! This has become one of my all-time favourite titles. Remarkable. Thank you for your art.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars is a fairly unusual duck in the pond of games, it's a Greek-inspired soulslike and -lite that does a lot of things right, even if its not a perfect game by any means. I definitely am curious to see what the dlc will be like and what more the team that made it can do in the future.The game takes place chiefly in the curséd city of Aphes and its surroundings where protagonist Hilda, a teen battlemaiden with magic weaponry has come to seek out the lost expedition led by her father. Aphens was once an advanced civilisation reliant heavily on magic and a rigid caste system where one man unleashed a catastrophe that turned all of the people living there into purple skinned near immortals who rely on stardust for their survival. Attempts to lift the curse have not been effective so far, in part due to there not being enough information, but also due to the martial law laid down and the inability of the noble caste to cast off their hubris.Hilda comes into contact with the Adherants, a rebel group led by Minerva who is trying to lift the curse despite being seen as criminals by the remaining archon Marble and his army and as heretics of the old faith by the Ethrus cult running amok. NVM as plain enemies by the actual criminal gangs and such. So prepare to die as you're tackling this game, though unlike in Dark Souls Hilda is merely whisked to safety on losing all hp.Something you do need to keep in mind while playing this game is that the inhabitants of Aphes have been bitterly enraged throughout the thousand years this curse has gone on. So don't expect them to be overly inclined to be reasonable or open to new ideas unless you insert them with a crowbar. You can only access portions of the city, many buildings and areas being inaccessible and a lot of in-area npc's being door-npc's (aka you talk through the door of their home). Somewhat of a pity, but understandable. There's not a ton of enemy variety but they make the most of what is there.From plumetailed critters with sickles to werewolves, minotaurs and harpies. From bandits, soldiers, elite soldiers to lions, bulls and colossi. Possessed miners to crystallised humanoids, geode monsters to hangers (snake-scorpion-bugs). There's a good selection of storyline bosses and a good few optional ones. The issue is though that the game's not very challenging on the first run, mostly relying on some cheap mobbing in places to up the difficulty as enemy AI is a bit simple.There's a lot of humor in the game as well, even if it does sometimes try a rug-pull on you. For example, when you make it to the shelter, one of the first things you'll notice is the red wolf lady working as a smith. It isn't until sometime later that you learn why a furry-like is in a game or why the explanation is in-game plausible. At least you do get a slightly oversized murderfloof to join you mid to late game who'll open up a trade shop... Khajit has wares if you have junk, neh?I have to say the big draw of the game, aside from its inspired setting, is its boss roster. The storyline ones get an introductory cutscene and do require you to think ahead. There's a few with a fair nod to Dark Souls and such, prime example being the academy boss fight. Starts off against Asterigos is a fun game, but you do need to slog through a cool to lukewarm start. Grinding for stardust is tedious, nvm fetchquests needing item x. You can mitigate it somewhat by ensuring you collect all of Quintus' lost stock so you're not entirely reliant on enemy drops. It's certainly not a perfect game, but in the end it is definitely one I'd recommend. Just be aware that there's a fair bit of uncanny valley and overly long death/revive animations.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very satisfying souls-like, probably one of the better ones made. Combat is very smooth and fluid. It does not suffer from the typical "eurojank" complaints (and yes, it is not european). There is a very heavy emphasis on story, so this is not one where you have to fill in the blanks. In addition all the NPCs are very well fleshed out with full story arcs. Great voice acting all around. Combat gives a fast dodge cancel, so that makes combat feel great. You get all weapons near the start, and playing through the game, seems you can max (+10) one weapon (possibly more?) and almost max others if you want to grind. Weapons have an attack and an alternate mode. Daggers give "dodge through" spears do parry, staff gives ranged attack. Probably staff should be mandatory as second weapon since the ranged attack is so good. You also have 4 elemental stones, which add bonus damage to attacks and can solve some environmental blockers. Each stone can be upgraded to +3, for more it is RNG with a trade partner to get materials.Crafting is used to upgrade weapons and elements and to make accessories, There are 4 accessories "slots" which can be mixed and matched at will. They may absorb certain damage types and also give some minor buffs. For players that want an absolutely brutal hardcore experience there are two early accessories to absorb all XP (no leveling) and to set all resistance types to -30. After the game is completed a NG+ mode is available.Probably my biggest complaint about the game has to do with the side quest mission structure. There are a lot of things to find and many of them relate to side quests. There are so many side quests and so many items it is hard to remember who needs what and where to find it and so on. You do have a journal and while that helps somewhat it is still difficult to figure out who needs what from where. Resolving side missions often means searching down character dialogue trees for "gold" dialogue options. That could be done better. Not getting all the items will mean some story arcs may not be completed. Which might be a minor thing unless you are a completionist.Anyway if you don't like hand holding, then this will be a game for you. Game length, probably 30-60 hours if you take your time and attempt to do all the side quests. The game is a soulslike but the difficulty is overall much easier than dark souls. Soulslike in this case means you lose some money on death, and regular monsters respawn, but not much else.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars is a really charming game. The art direction for this game is really outstanding, and there's a level of attention to detail that you don't see too often in other games. All this while the game is very appealing to look at.The combat is fine, it's not anything groundbreaking but they let you pick two weapons that you can use at the same time out of a total of six. There's a skill tree where you can unlock skills for your weapons, and perks that give you bonuses whilst at the same time giving you a negative effect. There's also different elements for your weapons and they're supposedly more effective towards certains enemies, although the game never makes it clear which enemies are weak to what, and you have to guide yourself a bit through gut feelings. There's a fair amount of bosses, but they vary in difficulty and should be looked at as a way to finish you journey through an area. They're cool at least.The story is a highlight, but it can also be a turnoff. It's one of those stories where you're dropped in the middle of everything and only get fed droplets of information as you progress, and understand more as you get further into the game. It's a good story, but the problem is that it can be very confusing to follow because the details of the story are told through items that let you listen to conversations from the past, but they're just figures talking to each other, there's no cutscenes or anything to follow and the events you're seeing can be from 15 minutes or a 1000 years ago. This is all made worse by the fact that the game a lot times doesn't take into consideration what you know/ have seen and what you don't know. You can be saying you have no idea what something is in one dialogue, and explaining it thoroughly in the next. Sometimes characters will talk about something that you should've seen already but you're just left confused as to whether you've forgotten something or it really is just the game not knowing what you've seen (mostly the latter). This game is rather cutscene shy, they would've made this game a lot better, but I'm guessing that the lack of cutscenes were just a limitation. At least your character keeps track of what happens through her diary with cute drawings and short explanations. The lore of this game is quite rich, perhaps a bit too much, but you can tell that the developers wanted to create an expansive world, and in that they succeeded. There's tons of diaries/books/notes to read that all delve deeper into the details of the city you're in, and what motivated each character.The music also deserves some credit. It's really well done and the tracks are of good quality, they set the mood and are played at the right times so as to set the tone for some encounters.There's a lot of side missions in this game, and of good quality. The problem though is that keeping track of them isn't easy. The little journal you have keeps track of which side missions you have, but aside from some cryptic things your character may write, you better never stop playing this game or you'll forget what characters told you to do, because after they tell you once, they'll never say it again aside from a few instances. You also never get notified properly when you're finished with the side mission aside from getting an achievement for some missions, and when there's no more space to draw in your diary Despite being labelled a Soulslike, this game plays more like a Hack and Slash with Soulslike elements than a proper Souslike game. You still have stamina management, there's the equivalent of bonfires, you lose resources when you die, etc. One thing that is oddly Soulslike about this game that I noticed midway through and haven't really seen anyone comment about it, is that the game's structure is pratically identical to that of Dark Souls 1. Allow me to explain:This doesn't detract from the game in any way, but it's something that I couldn't help but notice.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an indie Souls-like/action RPG. Graphics are pretty basic but there are some great looking environments. There is some kind of story here but the dialog goes on for way too long and it's not particularly interesting.What it is good at is being a good entry point to the Souls-like genre. It has a difficulty setting. Attacks cost no stamina. You can hold up to 20 healing potions at a time and nearly every enemy drops one. You keep your stardust (souls) when you die and you don't have to worry about returning to your corpse. Enemies only respawn when you rest at a waypoint but to be honest there is no need to rest as it only fills your health bar. You could play the entire game without resting and respawning enemies. There are a lot of collectables and secrets here. A bunch of optional bosses with their own achievements. Overall, a lot of content if your looking to 100% a game. With that in mind, full price isn't too bad. It's well worth it on sale for a nice breezy run through for Souls veterans
