_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant souls-like that's not very challenging (even on Challenge difficulty) compared to more usual games in the genre.Main things that make the game easier1. The healing potions are just an item you can get as a drop or buy, all without the need to rest at the checkpoint.2. When you die, you only lose a portion of your money, the experience for leveling is a separate bar and is not reduced upon death.3. The dodge is very generous with invinsibility period, and you can do it a lot of times in succession before running out of stamina.4. Weapon attacks do not consume stamina (DLC can change that). So you don't need to manage stamina when it comes to combat, you can just dodge behind an enemy, land some attacks, dodge again, rinse and repeat.Good1. You can switch between different weapons, each of which has unique skill. This allows you to pick your preferred playstyle and experiment with different combinations. Later you also receive gems which apply elemental damage to weapons and allow for even more variety. You only have those 6 weapons that you start with which might seem restrictive but in practice I think it's just enough.2. The atmosphere is a mix of bright, colorful visuals and dark themes like slavery, human torture and experimentation, exploitation of desperate people, etc.3. The level design is alright. Maps are interconnected, so you have an incentive to look around and explore. You'll find shortcuts, treasure chests and other useful loot.What could be improved1. The game relies heavily on side quests, but there is no proper journal to keep track of their progress. You have notes with some scribbles which are not particularly helpful. Even if the game wants to be a proper souls-like, the quest log would be beneficial for experience. No need to follow Dark Souls' formula too closely.2. You get the ability to teleport around halfway through the game. It could be introduced a bit earlier to cut down on running around when exploring and completing quests. You do have consumables that teleport you to the shelter or to the last used checkpoint but they only work if you need to go to shelter and back, but if you want to go to other areas you still have to run on foot.3. The game has a lot of dialogues and reading. The lore is presented through notes. Some might find it irritating and not very "soulsy". I didn't mind it that much personally.DLCDLC adds new, more challenging, boss fights. You get rewarded with materials to modify your weapons (separate from weapon upgrades of base game). Considering that combat alone is not the strongest side of the game, it's weird that the developers decided to focus on that. The balance is all over the place, some fights are manageable, others can be quite brutal.I'd suggest getting the game if you want more relaxed souls-like. Even if you don't like souls-likes, you can still give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the stars at first glance appears to be a game that would struggle to make its mark in the plethora of titles in the action RPG genre. However there are modest improvements over its peers that I think should be lauded in its genre and other story-linear games. Choices or lack thereof, matter. I am sure everyone has seen that near every story focused game has this claim, however Asterigos early on examines your willingness to follow the easy and direct solution without question as is usual in combat focused titles. Characters will criticise your willingness to blindly follow the most obvious path ahead. It's not entirely groundbreaking stuff, but it is presented in a way that you may scrutinise how you may or may not be accustomed to the typical questing system of go to area A, kill all enemies and return to quest giver B without regarding any consequence or purpose except to simply proceed. Again nothing crazy, it's a hack and slash game but it shows that the developers attempted for it to be more than just what its genre defines. The game's combat system is modestly expansive and designed so the player can choose early what weapons and set ups they prefer with a mix of skills that combine harmoniously. For example skills can combo with your basic move-set, weapon ability, a quick swap between two allocated weapons and everything in between. Ultimately you could spam the same same actions and make your way through the game, but ultimately the fun comes pulling off attack with varied move-sets, kinda like a fighting game. Again nothing super ground breaking but it (a smaller and focused title) does go beyond what most AAA games in the genre attempt. The game is stylised to where it can be compared to Fenyx Rising but that's not necessarily a bad thing, it's a very pretty game. The voice acting is not always present but it is excusable for a AA title, and what's there, is of a high standard. It won't win GOTY or compete with the big guns and could use some polish, but with what it attempts to accomplish, it (in my opinion) shows that it was made with more introspection than many other games with larger budgets and dev teams behind them.

_childDocuments_.review: I played on the highest difficulty and found it an okay challenge compared to other games of the genre. While it's certainly clunky at times, it mostly plays well enough. This is apparently the first game of the studio and it's a pretty good debut.The negatives? Combat gets repetitive because you have 6 weapons and that's it, little variation. Some skills are much better than others so you stick to that skill and that's it (whatever the dagger thingy is where you slice around like crazy). Sometimes the damage feels weird - like you get borderline oneshot at higher levels which is weird. Some enemies are also health sponges which is annoying. I think styx was the worst offender in that regard. Navigation was also hard at times because some of the scenery just looked the same and you can get turned around quickly that way.The positives? Really cool aesthetics, a neat story, variations in scenery throughout the levels and enemy variety - like every level offers up new enemy types and not mere reskins.Ultimately, this was solid fun for some 33 hours until the 2nd / true end given a rather low price at that. I enjoyed it. I probably won't replay it like I do some other games of the genre because the combat was rather one dimensional but as a one time adventure, it was certainly worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: 92 hours at review - beat the game 1x and am only missing 2 achievements: getting the Determination ending and beating the game at the Level 20 cap.Asterigos is certainly inspired by the Souls series, but has a great deal more emphasis on character relationships, upfront lore and traditional questing. For players that enjoy slowly exploring through the world, reading lore notes and digging through the details of a quest, you will have a lot of fun on the first playthrough.Despite the depth of the skill tree and the variety of 6 different weapon styles, I found that the game does not have too much replayability. You can respec often and a lot of the content hits its mark only the first time around. The DLC is also not made as carefully as the base game, with some imbalanced, tedious bullet-hell fights, and very little storyline to enjoy.Nevertheless, a satisfying Soulsian indie game for those that ever wished the Souls games had a more classic quest structure, some towns to visit and NPCs to talk to.

_childDocuments_.review: Ape-like men and delicate women populate this Roman and Greek mythology inspired... wait that can't be right. Roman and Greek? That's what the tagline says... Maybe in the loosest of senses. It is more accurate to say that its a city of people cosplaying Roman elements who didn't look up what an archon is and then imported templars from the medieval period and... Look, if you're going to to publicly peg your setting to a particular inspiration, get it right. Otherwise, just let your setting be. The audience is smart enough to figure it out if or when it matters.Anyhow, your clearly Celtic inspired Murder Waif will somehow tote around six sets of weapons as she is rightfully called a child by everyone even as they rely on her martial prowess... even though most are immortals who apparently never bothered learning to use a sword in the last thousand years... *sigh* Embrace being an elite child soldier who was left behind by her father and whom complete strangers will use to further their agendas by sending you into danger!On this journey, you'll be aided by a fox smith with noodle arms named Vulcan, whose connection to Roman mythology is that vulpine and Vulcan have the same prefix. See? Totally related. What's that? The actual Latin roots are vulpes and vulcanus, two completely unrelated words? Don't tell the writers that! Also don't mention that this game includes Odysseus (Grecian hero) and Minerva (Roman name for Odysseus's patron), as that may cause them to actually give their source material more than a cursory look.As implied, the writing leaves much to be desired. It comes across as U.S. high school level at best, which is to say that it is loud and obvious. The biggest failing though is how characterizations can be inconsistent. In one area Murder Waif can scream about how she's fighting to help the people oppressed by a local gang. Then in another area she screams at smiths for not respecting a guard that was bullying them when it is clear they are prisoners forced to work. I get that she's a traumatized child soldier who has been resurrected a few times and is only valued in this game for her murdering, appearance, and gullibility, which is itself enough to cause a psychotic break, but I don't believe the writers considered that when then wrote this.The game is not without bugs: My UI vanished (it came back after save and reload), and I got stuck on a wall (also fixed by save and reload). Some of the controls are needlessly strange as well: you use one key to confirm attribute choices and another to confirm talent choices, and one's a tap, while the other's a hold for... reasons? Some animations also look a tad strange, like the copious shoulder movement when running, but they are mostly solid.If you read this far you're probably wondering how I could have possibly given it a thumbs up. Well, I must admit that no matter how dumb a game might be (or at least I haven't hit my limit), I do enjoy playing a Murder Waif. On top of that, the graphics are solid, especially the environment, and the gameplay is excellent. Where It is certainly not the advertised souls-like, but it is fun and engaging. It is clear that the designers are top notch - the web of quests, particularly how they interact with each other, is great, and the level design as fabulous, particularly Styx. There are definitely features I'd like to see, like putting voice to the rest of the dialog or more unlockable outfits (folks should know by now that end game = fashion) or having sword and shield about more than the shield or an automap, but what's there is still fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know much about this game upon purchasing, didn't even know it was souls-like. I just had it on my wishlist for a long time, looking at potential purchases I looked into the game more and most comments just said combat was good which is what matters most to me. To preface this, I don't actually enjoy souls-like games, too shallow combat wise and what I normally associate with souls games is a vague story you learn about through objects. Well this game definitely fir's the bill with the die and lose some resources on death, but this game has a full story the whole way through with the collectibles giving you MASSIVE lore dumps about the world.The story was entertaining beginning to end and if you like a ton of background lore in the world there is massive amounts and found myself reading everything everything I came across,  which is most everything in the game. My biggest complaint about this is while it is nice getting this info, getting notes titled NICELY HANDWRITTEN NOTE, OR NOTE WITH TERRIBLE HANDWRITING. But the font is the same no matter what, if it's neatly written SHOW IT don't explain that, you can have an option where you press a button and you can easily read it. But instead they definitely went with the "tell don't show" option here.Combat which is something I care about the most is actually quite enjoyable. you have 6 weapons to choose from pretty much right at the start and can upgrade any as long as you ave the materials to do so. (MAX 3 WEAPONS PER RUN CAN REACH HIGHEST LEVEL IF YOU FIND THE MATS) Each weapon feels different and great in their own way I experimented a lot in the beginning until I fell into my favorite two weapons to use for the remainder of my first run. You have several skills for each weapon and perks that change how certain moves work that you can toggle on and off. It isn't the deepest combat system but it is enjoyable with a good variety of enemies to fight. The game had a good amount of difficulty throughout and never felt like it got easier as you go on. You also get to choose difficulty at the beginning I do recommend doing Challenge at the start if you are looking for a bit more difficulty. Although, if you are looking for a brutally hard game this also is not that.Speaking of difficulty there is a point in the game where it turns to night and a bunch of hard bosses spawn around the world, these bosses are definitely the hardest part of the game and the fights are VERY fun.The story itself was good, but the greatest story ever told. It dragged me in enough to reed the lore, listen to what the characters in the shelter had to say about the current and past state of Aphes. The devs really put as lot of care and attention to the world taking a ton of inspiration from Greece and Roman mythologies. The only complaint I have about the story is that to get the "best ending" is super extremely vague that absolutely requires a guide to get. You have to meet certain requirements and a certain amount of them to get this ending. A lot of it is hidden and a nice chime happens when you meet a requirement and you can check how many you have on the corner of Minerva's desk at the shelter.Now arguable the biggest problem with the game is the "quest log" or lack thereof. Therte is no map so exploration is up to you entirely, which bothered me at first but not in the grand scheme of things as this game is a lot more linear than it appears to be, there is always only one path forward. The problem is the main quest it does tell you what you need to do it's up to you to find what to do which really isn't an isn't an issue. The real issue is the side quests, you better have a damn good memory or a guide because once you are told something that is the last you will hear or read of it. Hilda writes a vague entry in her journal that explains nothing. Most things you can do on the spot but some you can't do anything about until later in the game and you get a quest item and you just think "I dunno wtf to do with this" because you spoke to some one at the earlier parts of the game that wanted it. Well you better start going to any NPC you can talk to you if you don't have a guide, or write down what/where people are.I am dedicating this  sentence at the end just to say I LOVE the soundtrack it's REALLY good.Overall it was a very enjoyable game and I loved just about everything in the game, it is rough around the egdes in a lot of ways but the pros outweigh the cons in the end. I enjoyed it enough the get all the achievements and plan on returning to this game again sometime in the future. I recommend people to try this game if you like a linear-ish souls-like with a story inspired by Greek and Roman mythologies and a good but not particularly deep, but satisfying combat system.

_childDocuments_.review: I've beaten this game twice. i don't usually go for a second run so soon but I really enjoyed my time here.It is important to note this game is not AAA. It's a very well made game but it is clearly AA and there are minor ways this makes itself known. A lot of issues I had were fixed though and these were mostly quality of life in nature. The gameplay itself is very enjoyable. It is a tad souls like, but in a much more casual friendly way. Your weapons have many more options and there is some fun in tinkering with various builds. Gameplay is smooth and reactive. Enemy variety is decent enough. The game's length is great as it doesn't wear out its welcome. It has different endings depending on some rather obscure choices which could be better, but it's not the most impactful change so you will not miss much. Bosses are decent but could use a little more kick in some cases.What I really liked was the overall aesthetic and story of the game. It has likable characters and some actual character progression for many. The MC makes mistakes but grows and learns. Initially it can feel like some of the characters giving you jobs are too harsh on you, but it all makes sense as you progress. The world has established beliefs and a culture too. It doesn't shy away from certain themes and I like how it felt well thought out.I hope for more like this and would love to see more of Hilda

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to review. The game does things badly , does some things great and mostly is middling.There is no doubt in my mind that the developers of Asterigos have huge amounts of passion and talent. This looks to be the first game they have developed or at least the first to hit the western market and i have to say if this is true then im impressed. It's not often that eastern developed games outside of japan can hit the western market and appeal to many western gamers , however i think that this does a good enough job to warrant a purchase (on sale). With this being said however the game does fall flat in a few areas which bring it down into mediocrity. or Slightly above average.The good:I love the music , animation/art and world building. The game makes me want to explore it , the music is varied and fires on all cylinders , the animation is simply one of the best ive seen. The world building is almost in my top 5 of games.The average:The combat is pretty average , its more i-frame based than reaction , and if you get hit you stumble leaving a feeling of clunkiness which is often what reviewers dont quite understand in the feedback loop of gameplay , so instantly get turned off and refund. Other then that it plays more like kingdoms of amalur (combat wise) then say dark souls, although gameplay generally has a souls LITE feel to it.Difficulty could be ramped up a bit , so talents ,attributes and weapon choices feel more impactful , To increase difficulty i would make the ai more adaptable and harder to stun lock , also almost getting rid of the small aggro range and reset the mobs seem to have. The perfect difficulty to start would be that of the 10 secret bosses during the last part of the game , at the moment these are optional but i would say that they were probably of normal difficulty which would have been a good type for the start of the game.I actually like the talent tree , almost all of the skills in it changes your abilities and attacks in various ways and are not just stat boosts , i love this , but would like to see a larger tree with more neutral skills that are not just tied to certain weapons.I would also like to see more and different weapon types , and different looks to each weapon , i.e there could be multiple swords with different stats and bonuses (But i get this is usually the way eastern rpgs are made , in its current form) I would also like to see actual armour that can also be upgraded , not just trinkets. This would lead to bosses being more exciting , if for example they all dropped unique items , not just upgrade materials so you can upgrade your generic weapon to +2.I think if they worked on the ai , balancing , and game play progression systems , The next time around i can really see a good game forming. But as the product stands now i would give it an average 5/10 ,

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with Asterigos. Gameplay overall was solid with multiple viable options when it comes to combat. Since upgrading every weapon can definitely get grindy I would recommend testing all available weapons in the early game and focus your upgrades on 2-3 weapons to get the most out of them. I played on "challenging" so if you choose an easier difficulty you maybe able to use more weapons throughout your playthrough. The general progression felt good, level ups and trinket upgrades combined into a nice power curve over the whole experience. Graphics are good, the artstyle may not be everybody's cup of tea but I liked it. One gripe I have is that animations on enemies more than half their framerate when the player puts some distance between themselves and the enemy. Most of the time sightlines are not that far out though so its not a big issue. Sound design and music are great overall, lots of themes that I enjoyed a lot and I am very happy that the soundtrack is available for purchase. The story was good, I enjoyed all the characters although it took some time to get going and to hook me. I would say if you do not like reading in games this game has quiet a lot of it and I would argue it is almost necessary to read a lot of the documents one can find to get the bigger picture about this games story and world. Not an issue for me though, I like reading a lot in games :3So overall definitely an easy recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good. It's a souls-like but with it's own refreshing take and a much more obvious story. Bosses are fun - for the most part, some are hot garbage that aim to overwhelm you with either add control, extreme RNG (much more so that the souls games) or both. *Disclaimer* This statement is directed at the non-main story bosses, which should be challenging, but not all of these ones are designed very well.The quest system needs a rework. Like most souls-like games, there is no easy way to track what you are doing (which is fine), but they attempt to provide you journal here. The journal is confusing at best and would have been better if they left it out. If they reworked it to properly track quests - because lets be honest, this is souls-like but much more forgiving, then it would probably add a nice touch to the game.Difficulty is fairly easy. Challenging (the highest you are allowed to choose on your first play through) is still much easier than a normal souls-like play through, enemies just hit much harder and have a bit more HP. Overall its worth it, I look forward to what the DLC and further game updates fix/add to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a review, these are my first impressions of the first 7 or so hours of the game plus additional time spent replaying older parts. I have a video talking about the game here for those who prefer the format: The game is estimated to be 30-40 hours in length. This is also based on a pre-release version of the game.You're probably looking at this game and thinking "oh Jesus, ANOTHER souls-like RPG with a unique setting?" but this one is good, quite good. In fact, there's a lot more to it than just that. While the pacing, enemy and level design, boss design, and world-building are very similar to a souls game, the game's combat attempts to be a much more fast-paced character-action affair.  Think Devil May Cry or Bayonetta but without the insane combos. Your attacks are fluid and fast so there's more focus on dodging and dancing around your target while constantly keeping up attacks. You have all kinds of special moves to use in combat that are flashy and fun to make up for the lack of a deeper combo system ala Dynasty Warriors or Senran Kagura. The one thing the developers really nailed here is execution. The controls are smooth, and the animations and transitions between attacks are slick. It genuinely feels like the developers had someone on their team who was some kind of character-action guru telling them what to do. It's as if Hideki Kamiya was staring right into the programmers' eyes, judgingly, making sure that everything was where it should be. I've seen AAA games screw this element up horrifically and yet this newer studio with a AA publisher does it perfectly.The question is does it hold up for the 30-40 hours you'll be playing? I have over 6 hours into a save (the rest was spent replaying older areas) and I will say that while I enjoy the combat, I am cautious about recommending it. The big fundamental problem with adding a fast-paced traditional character action game to a slower, more methodical souls-like RPG is that they kind of clash as you'd expect. You can't be styling on enemies and throwing them in the air to do a thousand combos on them in a game that is paced like souls. So instead, you have to remove those combos to make the game flow a bit better in terms of pacing since this is a non-linear game. The problem is that Asterigos can get weighed down by the need to grind as you'll only be given a small choice of weapons from the start of the game and you'll be carrying them (for me, 7 hours) for a while, possibly the entire game. This means you'll be using similar move sets most of the game and in the case of this game: you have to grind to keep more than two of them viable to use at once. There are affinities that give you magic damage but they don't change how the weapons work. For example, the fire weapon affinity doesn't let you drop flames as you roll-attack around with the spear. Once again, I need to draw your attention back to the controls. If this game didn't have excellent technical systems regarding the controls and general fluidity, I would not be talking this game up so well in that first paragraph.As for the other parts... The story is alright, the setting has Greek-Roman-inspired elements but it doesn't feel like that all the time, feels like a mix of other stuff. Would've liked them to stick to the Greek theme more. Some of the vistas and backgrounds look genuinely amazing. Performance is mixed. This game ran really well for me on an older 1070ti but after switching to a 6800xt I'm having some performance problems on the exact same settings, mainly due to a hitching related to when the game loads stuff in the background. The music is really pleasant to listen to at times, sometimes excellent. Sound mixing is good too on headphones. The story and voice acting are just sorta there. It's a bit of an info dump near the start of the game and the motivations are sound for the characters and there is a bit of a mystery to unravel I really like the narrative setup for each district you'll be killing stuff in. But overall, it's not why you play it and you'll only get invested because of your playtime, not the characters themselves. You play it for the level design and to fight enemies and thankfully, at least for the first 7 hours, that has been really fun. But if you're a souls veteran I do recommend you put the game at the highest difficulty. Medium/adventure difficulty I found to be almost boring. After 2 hours of play, I restarted the game and found even more secrets in the first area. You can change the difficulty at any time in the options menu within a loaded save though, which is nice. I wouldn't call it a "more accessible" souls game due to it being very different in many respects (mainly the combat) but if you don't like some of the more punishing parts of souls, such as the actual currency/experience system, you'll be happy to know that you don't lose potential experience points when you die, so your progress never feels wasted. You do lose 10 percent of your cash and you can't get that back after each death though.I do think this is a game to throw on your wish list at the very least or buy on sale or even buy right now if you're really aching for another souls game to play before we get more stuff from Elden Ring if the first 7 hours are anything to go by. This is one of those games where I feel the execution of the game is better than its own concept. Please read other write-ups on the game and reviews, don't just use mine though. Thanks for reading, if you wanna see more stuff like this we have our own curator page you can follow here:

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos curse of the stars is a 3rd person adventure RPG about a young woman named Hilda, who has found herself in a predicament with an unlikely ally.The story of this game is extremely long and filled with lots of lore. If you are not a fan of very long dialog you will not like this game. While the main story is fully voice acted, any of the optional dialog is text only. The combat consists of the use of multiple weapons the player can choose at will from swords, spears, daggers, magic, and melee.Combat itself can sometimes feel a little clunky and I wish it flowed faster. The magic however was really fun to use and a good way to keep back some of the mobs.I see a lot of reviews comparing this to dark souls. This is no where near a dark souls experience.  Sure it has some mechanics used by dark souls such as dodge rolling and respawning of all enemies should you heal at a save fountain. But that’s it. Nothing else in this game nor the difficulty is anything near as frustrating as dark souls.I thought this game was great and was filled with tons of things to go and places to explore. There is also no map in the game. I wish there was for easier navigation but I eventually learned the different location layouts as you visit them a few times.Overall this was an outstanding game 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: updating after 100%, upticking to 7.5/10 (after reading all the lore this time, lots of interesting stuff in there, good world building bumps this up.  Also played with more classes this time through, spear stole my heart).This game's solid.  7/10. I recommend it, but it has its problems I'll vent about here,MINOR SPOILERS FOR WEAPON PROGRESSION, NOTHING ON STORY THOUGHIts a pseudo souls-like that works well enough.  The dialogue feels really poorly translated at first, but it improves somewhat as time goes on.  If you like reading texts, you'll get a lot out of this game - the quests are voiced, but every other dialogue is just text and there's 300 or so documents to read (which I liked but it can be a lot).  Also a whole lot of in-game cutscene style lore in the form of big blue glowy balls, which are fine, but its a lot.  There's a whole lot of lore that's a bit overwhelming and I found myself skipping through a lot.  I want to do a run where I watch it all, its just a bit too much all at once, and often I think that's because its incredibly vague and a bit all over the place as you piece things together; some of that is intentionally keeping your character in the dark, some of it is the mystery your character is actively trying to uncover, and the rest is a pretty confusing backstory... its a lot of intrigue and fogginess that comes from too many angles to hold my interest all at once.If you like achievements, you can one shot this game with a second save at a critical juncture.  But then you can't level past 20 and that's a bit of a bummer.  I did it in two, the level 20 first and then a difficulty uptick for the real thing.The maps are fun once you know them but so horribly confusing at first.  Only world map is in the hub, but its decently detailed.  It feels a bit like the surge in terms of mapping confusion if that helps at all, but the world map is much more usable, at least for the city area.Quest log is absolute dogwater.  Its the worst part of the game.  It tells you what happened and nothing about where to go for sidequests.  If you go back to the last character in the chain you get nothing. So you better remember everything. I get being a souls like you want to be minimalist in some ways, but if you have this many plotthreads, at least make it a bit more navigable. Gameplay stuff:I've had no responsive or visual issues playing this game thus far.  some ranged attacks hit walls I don't agree with but nothing more severe than that.  Hitboxes seem pretty on point (though splash damage goes a bit further than animated sometimes, so dodge a bit harder than you think), iframes work as expected. I've seen other reviews complain about this stuff and I don't really get it. Classes.  There are 6, each is good in its own right, but some have things that set me off.  Here's a pointless personal ranking (to clarify it, I used Sword&Sheild primary and Magic Gauntlets as my secondary on the lv20 run and on hard I ran Spear w/ Daggers alternating with Spear (though i dropped the daggers for the hammer at the halfway mark)1. Spear (parry), throwing a spear is great, which you could do a weaker one off mana though.  Dodge attack is an aoe (one of the only two and the more effective of them). Ult is a moonlight greatsword, gotta love it. 2. Sword & Shield (Block / Shield Bash), just solid standard stuff that works well.  Ult is a boomerang shield, you have abilities where you can toss your shield and keep swinging and recall it at will.  One really nice leg-cut dash that works well to set up anime finishes to a lot of boss fights3. Staff (ADS for beam attack).  Hear me out. This one is boring af at first with just a spam thing.  This scores up high entirely on the back of unique weapon animations per enhancement, particularly in the combo finishers (which you unlock in the tier - each weapon has one to unlock that way).  The ult lets you spam that (though for some reason doesn't let you swap enhancements during the ult, which is a shame and a half and drops this one down to 3)4. Magic Gauntlets (mines).  If it wasn't for the mines this weapon would be top tier for me, they're just uninteresting and take up so much of the tree its annoying.  You get some cool magic weapons on charge atks, which I wish were a bigger part of the kit over the mines.  The skills here are great, astral knockback and the ice wall thing in particular are great add ins for most builds I used which brings this one higher). Ult is just a range extender on the combo, animations for the weapon (and the magic melee charge things) are based on the enhancement, which makes the weapon feel more versatile than it is.  Makes for a good secondary weapon for the charge swings though and the roll is the second aoe and the combo has splash at parts. 5. Daggers (dash).  I love the daggers, lots of fun. Abilities are a bit all over the place and I only stud with the tele dash (the whirlwind sounds better on paper than it performs).  Ult is good though.  Biggest gripe is the dash being a second ability instead of a roll replacement, I get the stam cost weight, but its awkward if you like to swap weapons around.  Since I had to bench them over this (basically trying to dodge a lot when not having them equipped when I wanted to alter, it was ultimately best to retire them.  Damage isn't as aggressive as you'd like and not quite as fast to make up for that during strike moments in boss fights).6. Hammer (heavy swing). Don't at me.  its a fine weapon. The grav throw thing is great. The ult is just a boring slow earthshatter thing and i just got bored of it.  Its as traditionally played as the sword and shield, but with less innovation to make it stand out, basically.  But its good for what it is and I'd imagine its many people's favorite.Respeccing is available, first by a merchant with increasing prices for each go, then by another guy later that is more specific (talents or abilities) which is nice for weapon variability as I like to switch things up. Chests overall are poorly implemented.  Way too many mimics honestly. (EDIT: originally complained about needing to double roll, spear or staff solve that, but you can just throw a dagger, I didn't really touch throwables enough playthough 1).  Chests loot is really lackluster as you have to open several to get anything and they're just passive stat bonuses.  EDIT: you do in truth get upgrade mats as well, but they are largely the same stuff that's farmable, so its pretty meh to always be that.  I know it can't have weapons, which is usually the fun stuff, but even some fancy rare trinkets or weapon skins or something would've gone a long way to making them rewardable - or just make less if you have nothing too creative to put in em).  They also follow a clear path.  Would be more fun for replay if each chest did something specific so you could focus on a build. Enemy variability is decent for a souls-like.  Compared to the likes of surge, code vein, and steel rising, you'll have much more variability here.  Each zone is pretty unique.  Some reskins but the interactions are different enough that you don't notice it much. They do have elite variants of enemies too which I always like.  Boss variability stands out well until you get to the bonus bosses and they're just reskins thrown in for fun, which is fine, but a bit of a chore for achievement hunters.TLDR: biggest problems for me are the side quest log, way too many mysterious plot lines to follow at first, no bow class, basic magic options and you usually just have fire on, chests are not rewarding enough and almost feel like they shouldn't even be there.Biggest pros are replayability, weapon variations (though not as many as I'd like, each one is really thorough), clean solid play, fair hitboxes.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little souls-like with a great main/player character, considered world-building, interesting characters with pretty good voice work on average, decent music, and competent combat though it could use a little tightening up (and probably another usable ranged weapon other than having the staff beam as the only option). Story is pretty good if a little verbose, and feels like it has a better balance of having sad outcomes for a lot of characters/questlines while not being as outright depressing as your usual soulslikes. Size, interconnectedness, and visual variety of the areas is pretty good, and exploration freedom is decent. Definitely worth the asking price, especially with the free content like outfits and such that they gave out after release. Really hoping this gets a sequel as this has a fantastic main character/side characters (timeskip older Hilda perhaps?) and world/setting that I would love to jump back into.

_childDocuments_.review: I Wanna See More of This PleaseIt’s been quite some time since I’ve been doodling around the Souls series. I’ve played a variety of games you could call the infamous “soulslike,” or games that have mechanics and elements inspired by the Souls series, though none from From Software actually. One such game is Asterigos: Curse of Stars.To me, Asterigos came at a time when Greek mythology was flourishing in pop culture, as it does every now and then. It released just a few years after Ubisoft made a fortune with Assassin’s Creed Odyssey and Immortals Fenyx Rising, the great yet often overlooked gem. I think this game rode that same wave of popularity. Without that push, maybe Asterigos wouldn’t even exist. But the thing is, I like Greek mythology. I’m interested in it. I played and enjoyed both of those earlier titles, so when I saw this, my interest lit up immediately.Asterigos has a lot of content to offer. Its story goes deep into its own web, and there’s plenty to uncover. Exploring the world and its secrets feels rewarding, and that’s one of the game’s strengths. Even though it’s set against the backdrop of Greek mythology, it’s surprisingly original—it avoids the usual tropes like gods constantly meddling in human affairs or overusing famous mythological creatures. Instead, it carves its own path, with an original story that stands apart from typical mythological renditions.There’s a certain charm to being a kind of hidden indie gem. Sure, it’s a bit underdeveloped in places—most of the text isn’t voice-acted, the cutscenes are few and far between, and lip-syncing is practically nonexistent. But all these things are forgivable here. That high-budget polish isn’t the point. Think of it as Assassin’s Creed Odyssey mixed with Dark Souls, with a dash of Breath of the Wild thrown in for good measure, all for a fraction of the cost.That said, there’s room for improvement. Hilda, the protagonist, is a bit of a disappointment. She’s the lead, but she feels more like a plot device than a fully realized character. Her actions, her attitude, and the way she views the world all serve to push the story forward, but she doesn’t feel like she’s growing or evolving in a meaningful way. Every other character in the game has a complex backstory or some depth to them, but hers? It’s the oldest cliché in the book: the perfect daughter seeking her father’s approval. She has no real flaws. I mean, is being too altruistic supposed to count as a flaw? It feels like the writing here, much like other parts of the game, is a bit underdeveloped.The visuals in Asterigos are very Disney-like—bright, colorful, and almost whimsical—which isn’t exactly my cup of tea, but I’ll admit it works here. There’s something welcoming about it. Despite the game being centered around fighting against authoritarianism, with gameplay focusing on tough, hard-hitting combat, the visuals are lighthearted and comforting. It kept me wanting to play more. If the game had gone for a darker fantasy atmosphere, maybe I would’ve had to step away from it more often. That’s just a guess, though.Now, let’s talk about combat. It’s fun, well-designed, and full of interesting mechanics, but here’s the thing: it lacks that “ahh” moment—that flash of brilliance that makes it truly stand out. It’s solid, but it’s missing that extra spark that would make it rise above the crowd of other soulslikes. It’s good, but not groundbreaking.As for my final thoughts: I like the game. I had fun, and I’d recommend it to anyone who’s looking for a solid action RPG with a unique take on Greek mythology. It may not be perfect, but it’s a charming, enjoyable experience. Asterigos: Curse of Stars gets a 7 out of 10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially the “Souls-like” tag had put me off. I have absolutely no desire whatsoever to put myself through anything Souls-like. However, it came out that there is a difficulty setting and further reading online alleviated my fears and I went for it. And good news, I played on Story/Easy and it was a relaxing romp. I died twice (so far) in combat but that was due to my own sluggishness.PROThe difficulty setting. Main sell point for me.Combat feels quick and fluid. It doesn’t feel as slow and unresponsive as some of the Souls-like games do.You can switch and change your weapons quickly (primary and secondary weapons, and enchantments), but other load outs (trinkets and other weapons) you can also change but via the character menu.There is a LOT of lore, so the story is deep.CONTHERE’S NO MAP. This made exploring, especially in the beginning, really frustrating. I got lost so many times. So many times I did not know where to go or where to hand in a quest.THERE’S NO QUEST LIST. Only the "Main" quest shows, and that is on screen. You have a Journal that keeps track, like a diary, of people whom you’ve met or things that have happened, but like a diary, it does not tell you what you must do. “So this thing happened, this was interesting.” Yes, and? What must I do? Before the final showdown I tried to clean up side quests that I missed. I had to exclusively rely on online guides and it is then that you realise that there may have been a few quests that you may have broken by killing the wrong person or giving the wrong answer, because you had completely lost track of what was going on. The tidal wave of lore documents also does not help, because you miss so much.Anything else that could be wrong with this game does not even matter, it is so minor. But these two, the lack of a map and quest list, will be the major obstacles in preventing me from playing this game again (which I would like to do very much).

_childDocuments_.review: is a story driven and dynamic combat based action Game in a Universe that leans a lot onto Greek mythology. As a very impatient young Hero, the Protagonist starts to follow the steps of the Northwind-Legion with the goal to not just follow a cursed Kings commands, but also to gain more Prestige in the Ranks of said Army and in the Protagonists Fathers Eyes.Various different Weapons are put into the Players hand to pick from and to allow different Playstiles to fight off the Enemies that populate the mystical Lands of Aphes. And not just Enemies are along the way. Also some NPCs in need for Help and for the Player to make decisions that can sometimes have a significant effect on further in the Story appearing Elements.The Games strength is definitely its Explorable Gameworld that leaves it mostly up to the Player in which direction to go next. Also the Combat is not to complicated and after a few attempts goes very smoothly, as special after unlocking new Skills in a large Tree of different abilities.The Story offers a lot to enjoy too and gives the different NPCs a lot of Character to be uncovered by Reading through Manuscripts written by those NPCs, by using new dialogue Options that pop up and by then accepting and finishing their personal Questlines.But also the weak Points need to be mentioned. And in Asterigo’s Case it is coming from the weird difference about the Voice-Over. While some Dialoques have a voice over, other have not. That may seem minor, but it destroys the Immersion everytime it shifts from voice over to not voice over.Also the Camera needs some updates, as specially on some big Bosses who are then almost off of the screen and, when locked on force the player to not been able to see the rest of the combat zone, or when not locked on are like invisible and hard to dodge when they do some major Attacks.Another thing that needs mentioning is also the missing Questlog. Its hard to tell which Quests are still followed, halfway finished or completely finished and so it would be nice to have a little overview on that.I recommend this Game to People who like dynamic action-based Combat Games, as specially those who like the Fantasy-Genre to fight various Bosses in a nice to explore designed world. ---------------------------------6,5 / 10 Grafics (They have their own Style on this one, but the Characters could still use a little bit more Details and Polys)7 / 10 Gameplay (Easy to manage the Weapon- and Skill-Menus and the Combat-Mechanics are not to complex to handle)6,2 / 10 Soundtrack (Interesting Soundtracks that support the Atmosphere in Locations and during Bossfights)8,2 / 10 Main-Story (The Main-Story is well implemented and leads the Player through the Game-World. Some Plots are sadly predictable tho.)6,4 / 10 Side-Story (Interesting Side-Stories from various NPCs, but sadly almost no Voice-Over like they did with the Main-Story.)7 / 10 Characters (Interesting set of Characters you can meet up with and uncovering their Background with lots of Dialoque Options)6,3 / 10 Enemies (Lots of Enemies, tho they start to feel repetitive after a while and only differ in which Element they are weak to rather then forcing Players to come up with new strategies)8,7 / 10 Boss-Fights (I totally like difficult Bossfights. Very challenging on the highest Difficulty-Setting where each could lead to Players having to make a new setup of Equipment and Skills to beat them. – Depending on the Players own Gaming-Skills :P)

_childDocuments_.review: I expected to have fun with Asterigos' decently executed combat and idly pay attention to the plot just to make it through the game; I was certainly not expecting my favorite part of the game to be the incredibly detailed and fleshed out world of Aphes, full of complex characters and motivations, intricate storylines and genuinely nuanced and deft writing. My progress through the game soon became one of searching out documents to learn more about the people and history and pushing storylines through to reveal dramatic plot points or further political intrigue.Hilda is a member of the Northwind Legion, this world's viking/Celt analogue who journeys to the mythical city of Asterigos to discover what happened to her father's company of soldiers. Their king has been cursed with an artifact from Aphes and sent the Legion to search for a cure, though Hilda was not yet experienced enough to join them. When she arrives, she finds a city in stasis for 1000 years due to the curse and becomes involved in all the problems that have arisen during that time.I honestly cannot heap enough praise on the writing. While it can sometimes be delivered clumsily or awkwardly, and the voice acting can be uneven, the writing is strong enough to shine through any flaws in delivery. Early on when Hilda goes off plan and does something most games would applaud you for, everyone in game reacts in a way that surprised me. Very few, if any of the characters are simply good or bad. It's hard to explain without spoilers, but every boss I took down had more to them than being an obstacle, every ally I made had mistakes and ugly parts of their past, all of them were linked with each other and the city. These were complicated people with millennia of history. Very rarely was anything I accomplished not tempered with some sort of consequence. And it's strengthened all the more because the city and world it takes place in is so strong and full, the developers really put in an impressive amount of effort to make a place that had such an enormous history. Documents abound everywhere, you'll read one that is simply poems that a famous playwright did, then one on laws regarding rationing and naming someone that appears in a later note about being jailed for breaking martial law curfew, or notes on experiments to solve the curse referencing a note you read hours ago that a scientist wrote about sabotaging something. The only glaring flaw that stuck out to me was honestly Hilda and her story mostly because in a game where it puts so much emphasis on how going off and doing what you want has consequences...she is still the primary mover of every event. Legendary monster? This teenager can kill it. Stalemate as a result of too many lightning dogs? Tiny girl will kill em all. It just felt really incongruous, but I also realize you can't have a game where the protagonist watches other more capable people solve everything. It just can sometimes feel weird to have Hilda be the one to solve an issue by throwing her face into it.The graphics aren't a AAA title, but the style and aesthetic are great. Honestly, picking ancient Greece/Rome as the inspiration for Aphes was great because it's a very underutilized style. And they did a lot of great work in giving the city it's own identity and keep it consistent with the setting. There are a very healthy amount of environments and the game does a very good job at weaving them through each other so you'll sometimes get that "Ah, this path leads back here!" that can be fun when exploring.I was expecting the game to have a smaller scope, but after 31 hours and hitting the credits this is actually a hefty game. There is quite a lot to do, many sidequests and optional activities/fights with even just the main storyline being a good time investment. I will give a small aside that despite doing all the sidequests, I apparently solved some of them 'wrong' and thus was locked out of one of the endings which only irked me because for most of them I wasn't sure exactly what I could have done differently or how I would know to do a certain step unless I looked it up. Small complaint though.The combat is good. It's...fine. I may be the wrong person to go in depth for this as I'm not exactly a wizard with action games. Though it says Soulslike on the tin, I'd liken this more to a character action game or simply action RPG. Rather than finding weapons and armor everywhere, you get all your weapons from the start and can equip two of them to use. I went with the hammer and daggers and even those were enough to make me feel overwhelmed with options. Someone better than me at these games would probably find a cornucopia of options to play with as you level up and get more options and special abilities. Meanwhile, I kinda soldiered through while upgrading only two weapons and rarely using more than 3 abilities or switching elemental weaknesses. As a result I found the difficulty decent, sometimes a bit...not jank but I'd wonder about a hitbox here or there or why I didn't hit with an attack. The aformentioned more talented gamer will probably find the game a tad easy, so a higher difficulty might be worthwhile for them.Even if sometimes the combat wasn't my favorite part of the game, I loved my time with it. There was just so much to like about it, so much more of the world I wanted to see and characters I wanted to learn about. Well worth the price, even when it was full price. There's a large amount of content, replayability to try different loadouts and get a different ending and a truly fantastic set of characters to follow to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: A game of constant highs and lows. At least it's not boring, but it definitely tests my patience at times. The art style and visuals are wonderfully varied and colorful with lots of dynamic, impactful animations. But the graphics can get buggy and choppy (i think it's the game reducing framerate of distant objects to save memory but doing it five feet from my face).The sound is distinct, crisp and unique with such detail and quality work that I can tell exactly what enemies are doing just from the audio. But the mixing is bugged and it always sounds like distant enemies are right next to me and the music will drown out conversations.The combat is varied, snappy, and challenging with lots of enemies that feel satisfying to fight without being too unfair. But the moveset and attacks have frustrating quirks that mean I die when it's not my fault (like the dagger dodge sometimes changing to an attack instead, thus killing you when you don't move like you expect to).There's lot's of lore, exposition and details to make for a very lived-in world that feels alive. But the character dialogue is stiff and a lot of "tell, don't show" meaning I didn't care about anyone except the blacksmith.For every point of praise, there's something that really bothers me. It's an interesting game and at least as fun as it looks. Pick it up and play, but be warned.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is a very fun action game that suffers from an excessively bloated story and trying just a little too hard to be like Dark Souls. For me, this is a solid buy-on-sale chill weekend game.At it's core, the game features most of the standard souls elements, high damage enemies, a focus on i-frame dodging, losing currency on death, respawning at infrequent checkpoints, resting to restore potions and respawn enemies, hidden chests, mimic chests, interconnected levels full of unlockable shortcuts, no (useful) map, rare items found by hunting small enemies that run away, an animal that trades items for other random items, a story about the slow decay of a kingdom to a mysterious curse, obtuse questlines that require specific actions or dialogue choices to get right or fail, etc., etc. Sometimes you'll feel like they ripped a chunk of an area straight out of Yharnam or the ramparts of Boletaria, or the Tower of Latria, or the Crystal Cave. However, I found moment to moment gameplay to be much less like souls and more like classic action games. The difficulty is significantly lower than the standard soulslike, but if you're new to the format, the challenge is a decent balance. Most of the time you can just hack through enemies, occasionally dodging away during the infrequent "red glow" unstaggerable attacks. The weapon system involves equipping two weapons at a time out of six options with possible chain attacks. There is an upgrade tree for weapon skills but I rarely found it worth engaging with since the standard combos made short work of enemies anyway. There is no armor system and the item inventory is scarcely used except for healing items and the odd quest item. This means your starting sword and board basic combos will last you for the entirety of the game, and tbh, that's just fine. The game is also very colorful and vibrant, which is a nice change from the usual souls gloom. There are moments where it seems to get uncharacteristically dark though which stand out as strange, particularly the Tower of Latria equivalent which is caked in blood from torture victims. Though those moments might have been more impactful if I wasn't mashing through the endless dialogue to get to the next gameplay segment. The story is told in a method so overflowing with detail it puts the Silmarillion to shame. NPCs, the very frequent diary entries, the ghost flashbacks, the grave headstone inscriptions, the man behind the door with a candle near it, none of these people will EVER stop talking. As Willaim Shakesman once said, "brevity is the soul of wit." No wit was found this day. You might think I'm exaggerating. I enjoy fantasy stories with in-depth lore, and yes I HAVE read the Silmarillion. I found myself mashing through the endless dialogue before the end of the third area. There are 20-50 notes, headstone inscriptions, graffiti markings, loose pages, etc. to find in each area, often with full page or multi-page lore dumps. All of it is the bog standard "we tried to deal with the curse, we failed." I scraped areas as clean as I could and I was still missing many notes. There is a lot of voice acting in the game and it is used very poorly. The actors do a fine job with the material, but conversations just do not flow together. Sometimes a character will obviously have the wrong voice, like the seedy merchant/info broker (Greirat wannabe) who has the voice of a whimsical old man. Important npcs have voiced dialogue for story and quest lines, but not for incidental dialogue, which is fine. However, a lot of quests are secretly hidden behind npcs you can't see because you have to knock on a random door, to be greeted with pages upon pages of unvoiced dialogue that ends with a journal update signalling that you somehow started a quest. However, the journal will not summarize the important information for you and is thus useless. Additionally, while wandering areas you will occasionally encounter enemies which you can eavesdrop upon while they talk about the local situation. However, there is no voice acting for these goons and listening will not stop them from attacking you, so it is usually better to just kill them before they can finish talking. And perhaps worst of all, story progression is gated behind periodically returning to the hub area (on foot for the most part) and listening to yet another half-hour lecture from your boss before she opens a door at the end of the area you literally just cleared.I like this game a lot. I had a lot of fun with the relatively simple hack-and-slash combat. The story delivery is just so abysmal and the Dark Souls elements are just so forced. I'd love to see a sequel where this character/game come into their own and shed the shackles of mediocre imitation.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is a very interesting and competent indie ""Souls-Like"" (as in "Combat is lethal, you respawn at bonfire equivalents and so do the enemies") with a very compelling setting and excellent replayability, thanks to its varied weapons and movesets : I completed the game with the Swords & Shield and the Spear (which allows Sekiro-esque parries), but you can mix & match just about any of the 6 weapons and end-up with something as outlandish as a spellcaster/bomberman hybrid with the Staff & Bracelets (but completely foregoing the blocking mechanics)Despite taking place in a single city, the locations are relatively varied with a decent level-design, even though they lack originality and can feel derivative at times : you have interesting and gorgeous locales such as an Acropolis or overgrown Greek ruins, alongside places you'd swear you've already played through, such as basically Demon's Souls' Asylum with Diablo's artstyle.The story is pretty classic, with serviceable characters ... but the setting, along with the artstyle, are pretty captivating : I loved the mix of Roman/Hellenic influences for the City and its inhabitants and Norse (for the main character) viewed through the lens of Taiwanese developers. It's full of neat and quirky ideas and reimagination of myths and concepts that I never thought I'd see, and left me longing for more of these kind of original settings for Action RPGs.I've rambled enough. Asterigos is a decent game well worth its price, especially for the first game of the studio ! I'm pretty interested in what Acme will be proposing next ! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Thought it was a hidden gem.I nearly dropped it a few hours in, as I didn't get the combat at first. Turned out, I approached it as a typical hack-and-slash action, while it isn't - it's on the slower side and takes some time to understand how it works. It has its "rhythm", and it won't work if you simply mash it and hope for the best. Although the prologue can give you that impression ! Soon though, you will learn that knockdowns and parries and invulnerability animations are vital.Very solid and interesting story, although some characters feel kind of out of place the way they're written (Is Harold a Marine ?). There are choices in the story you have to make, but none are "good" or "bad" and the game will not flash a red warning sign telling you that you might regret it later. I liked the part that it's not advertised though.One of the best parts - lore, story and quests exposition is done masterfully and in a very immersive way. The journal looks like it's being written by Hilda for herself, not "the player". Same for the quest item descriptions - you have to pick up what they're for from subtle hints in the game-world. Can't think of a good term for this in videogames - but perhaps something akin to the fourth wall in theatre ?For that reason it can be sometimes difficult to say which stage of a given quest you're on - you sort of observe  as it unfolds while gathering more details - there's no checkmark to tell you "this is the last bit". There's no TL;DR - you really have to understand what's going on to proceed and I thought that was beautiful and enjoyed it thoroughly.It's open world. But an open world - without any fluff. There are chests scattered around but for every few you get a meaningful stat upgrade and valuable items. The world is up there with the ones I consider the best open world designs like Sekiro. Each zone flows seamlessly into another, sometimes intersecting - exploring it is pure fun.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I haven't actually played this game since early this year when a free update was released at around the same time as their unfortunately disappointing (according to the reviews) DLC. Some of the things I mention may have been altered or improved since then. The TL;DR is it's an 8/10 souls-like with an easy difficulty setting that most players should be able to finish without much trouble. I'm not very good at games and the only other souls-like I've played so far is Code Vein, which I probably only got through due to the constant AI companion and grinding out some levels at a few points. Yet despite my shortcomings I was able to beat this game's easy difficulty with only 9 deaths, all of which felt like they were caused by some unavoidable B.S. and never my skill issues. I was also able to get the platinum without too much trouble, though some of the boss fights really felt like a proper souls-like when doing the under level 20 run.Starting with the negatives, most of the game's issues come from the fact that it's a AA title made by a fairly small team. There's a healthy amount of indie jank, a few spelling errors, much of the dialogue is unvoiced (to be fair, decent voice actors can be expensive and there's a ton of talking), some odd looking animations, and a general unpolished feel that does not impact one's enjoyment of the game. Besides this, you'd have to be a psychic to figure out how to do some of the side quests and there are some pretty basic things the game doesn't really tell you that you might not figure out on your own. Thankfully there's a great youtube channel called Akifini's Gaming that pumps out easy to follow videos with no commentary or unnecessary junk, and they've seemingly covered almost every aspect of this game. I wish I found them earlier in my first playthrough as I actually ended up resorting to watching videos on bilibili for the help I needed, which was a little difficult to navigate as someone who only understands English. Some things I'm more neutral on are the fact that you're treated like a child at times (though it makes perfect sense as the playable character Hilda is maybe 15 at most), are sometimes railroaded into doing stupid things (because again, you're playing as a teenager who doesn't always get the big picture or know when she's being manipulated), and there's such a massive amount of lore I actually got tired of reading it all at roughly the halfway point. Really, there's something like 200+ documents to find in a game you could probably hammer through in under 15 hours if you know what you're doing or just don't care about all the optional content. I love learning about game worlds and this one is really interesting, but there was just too much. Going back to being treated like a child for a moment, I will say I was very impressed at how real a lot of the interactions felt. Now, on to the things they did right, which is pretty much everything else. The music is spectacular, the world they've created is amazing (the greco-roman world with a touch of Norse inspiration was a fantastic choice), the combat is very fun and extremely satisfying, and there are options to suit most play styles and skill levels, the voice acting is mostly great (I'd like to particularly praise the actors who portrayed Hilda, Otto, Seryne, Minerva, Vulcane, Shaye and Eumenides) however there are a few issues with other cast members. Nothing too bad though, you've definitely heard worse. The boss fights were pretty good, and a couple of them were great, with the final optional challenge boss during Trinity Night near the end of the game being a real standout. Moves are well telegraphed and you should be able to find or create openings with relative ease. They also managed to make the obligatory gank fight fair, which is something I haven't really seen before. The game's story content is a little more mature than I was expecting from the T rating, it's far from The Witcher but there's still some pretty dark stuff happening at times and a bit of adult humour (which innocent Hilda doesn't get) occasionally. Most things are implied or something you come across after the terrible thing has happened, which I'm a big fan of. I love it when media trusts us to understand what's really going on without being needlessly edgy about it or trying to exploit the subject matter for shock value. Speaking of the story, I really loved it however I can see where some might not like as much. There's quite a bit of depth to it, lots of additional information earned through completing side content that enhances the overall experience, a fair bit of it adding some surprisingly hefty emotional weight. Many characters aren't as one dimensional as they first appear to be, and a subtle little twist right at the end that players who hadn't completed certain side quests won't even get blew my mind, putting so many things into perspective. I'm pretty critical when it comes to most stories, and these devs really got it right.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Twilight Princess and Dark Souls adopt Fenyx' little sister. Although the game shamelessly "borrows" many design choices and mechanics from games you know and love, the sum of its parts is definitely its own thing. Challenging but forgiving combat, with different weapon types that each comes with a skill tree. There's lots to explore in various biomes that all feel different. No quest markers, no (mini)maps, unlocking short cuts as you traverse. There's a fist full of bosses thrown at you during your adventure, with a whole set of extra optional bosses to boot. However, the storytelling is absolutely horrendous; the bare bones story is fleshed out out by a mountain of needless exposition and false drama.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish steam had some mid ground for reviews.But I'm going to tilt to no for this one. The character controls are a weird mix of fluid and clunky which overall makes the game feel even more clunky. You have these smooth moments that are just completely interrupted by nonsense like not being able to dodge out of a sprint sometimes so you have to stop sprinting in order to dodge. Only being able to jump while sprinting like this is some Dark Souls 1 wannabe or something. No input buffering so you cant press your heal button mid roll to have your character drink a potion right after ending a dodge. For an action combat game the enemies have strange attacks and hitboxes that dont do a good job of communicating to the player whats happening. The character has no minor stagger animation but getting hit makes you lose control of her.... but she just stands still doing nothing for half a second. The alternative is getting knocked down just has her take a knee for about 2 seconds. I don't mind instances of losing character control as punishment for not avoiding certain attacks but something about this game just does an awful job of delivering it. I overall had fun with this game but think it still needs work and polish to not feel so claustrophobic to play.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly well crafted casual souls-like, if those words could ever appear together. The game is a lot more forgiving than Fromsoft's entries, with only 10% of your currency lost on death, and an arcadey, comically long distance roll. The combat appears very well polished and engaging, with a good variety of play style choices and abilities. I don't have any complaints in regards to combat but I have so many complaints in regards to player experience. This game is designed to inconvenience and annoy you. You have no fast travel until 20+ hours in, no map, no quest marker or even quest logs. Finding anything is up to pure luck. If you want to do a quest, you better memorize every line of dialogue from the quest NPC because he won't repeat it, and you won't have access to that information ever again.Final verdict: it's a fun game if you're willing to put up with the developers' ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: The full price of $34.99 is fair for what the game is -- it's clear that hard work was put into this -- and the full price is what I paid, but getting it on sale might make the the mediocrity hurt less. If I could give this a more middling review I would. It took me a very long time to finish the game because I lost interest and stopped playing for some months before returning, then took another break, before finally pushing myself to finish. I'm glad I did manage to see it through the end as the premise of the game was what drew me into it initially.The combat was pretty simple, but enjoyable with some fights being easy to cheese if you're having trouble. The music was fitting although forgettable and the characters were generally likable but only Hilda, Minerva, and Eumenides were memorable. The rest were okay, although I admittedly forgot how Shay and Hilda are connected other than Hilda was after him in the past for some shenanigans he got up to?, but I was quick to forget them. Roxane started interesting, but she was kicked to the wayside so early on that you forget she exists until the very end when there's a little blurb in the end cutscene about her.I wasn't a fan of the choice in art style, which reminded me of Pixar films, and while you heard the characters speaking their mouths didn't move unless it was part of a short animation that looped to convey an emotion. It made the characters feel rigid while the voiced lines were playing and detached from their own voices.My biggest gripe with the game was the lack of a minimap or even a larger area map that you could view from a menu. I'm the type of person that gets easily lost so I got lost often in the twisting and connecting pathways. This made navigating areas more frustrating than anything else.The story was solid -- nothing groundbreaking -- but still pretty good and the only reason I decided to finish the game. There were some sidequests but I didn't go out of my way to complete any as I didn't feel compelled to do so if they weren't a requirement. Any I did finish was by chance.The bosses never seem to get more difficult in terms of, well, difficulty so the final fight didn't exactly feel as rewarding as it was probably meant to. Perhaps this was because I used the daggers. Daggers are the dual-blade weapon option and it was easily the best weapon choice for me. Spamming blade dancer made every fight a breeze including the last two big boss fights. The speed of attacks made chipping away at health when I ran out of SP quickly depleted any enemy's HP to the point where it almost felt unfair to use them. Supposedly Round 2 (Asterigos's version of NG+) makes the enemies tougher, but I didn't bother with a replay.All in all the story was solid but nothing fascinating and the rest of the game was rather bland. The limited color palettes for most of the environments didn't help this either. While there were a few characters I enjoyed, most I could've done without or at least with less dialogue as there's a lot, but only the main dialogue paths are voiced the rest is text-only. The story was what carried the game and the combat was simple but fun albeit mindless. Without those two things I would've abandoned this game a long time ago and wouldn't have considered coming back. It was worth a playthrough, I didn't feel any of my money was wasted, but I don't have an interest to play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a 10/10 for me.Combat is awesome. You get six weapons each with their own talent tree and a special skill. You always have two of these six equipped. Daggers have a dash, snb have a block, spear parries, bracers throw mines, staff fires a laser beam, hammer has well a hammer attack. I preferred daggers and staff (staves are long range). You can learn skills for each weapon (uses mana) and perks which can change how your weapons attacks and specials might operate. All weapons can be upgraded at a smith.You get four elements to imbue your weapons with on the fly and each of those can be upgraded. There are attribute points but only three stats so it's hard to screw up your build. Also respeccing is cheap.Combat is very fun. Fast paced. exploring is fun, ton of branching paths that can open up shortcuts. You do unlock fast travel eventually. There's a lotta like notes and letters and books you find that'll expand on the lore. Game is very dialogue heavy too, mostly in between boss fights though. Story is fine I guess. I'm playing on normal but considering a replay on hard. There is a story mode as well. A couple bosses are piss easy but a few of them took me more than one try (especially when rolling off a cliff is possible). You lose some currency on death but not xp. _childDocuments_.review: A well optimized game, with a decent story, and actually good action combat. Large zones with no loading screens, sporting what I can only describe as Vindictus combat. Honestly their old trailers don't even do it justice, the hits definitely have some meaty impacts. I nearly 100%'d the game without realizing it, which is extremely rare for me. I might actually do it, and I hate collectathons.  Despite having a souls-like tag, it's not a souls-like at all. It has physical checkpoints and enemies reset on death/rest and that's it. It is some classic ps2-era action combat and it's actually refreshing to see some decent combat in an action game. None of that "oh their doing a special uninterruptable attack that you must parry" Simon Says ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. If you want to dodge all attacks you can, if you want to block all attacks you can(kinda), if you want to parry all attacks you can, if you just want to "face-tank-trade and see if you knock them down before they knock you down" you can. No electric slides, except for the enemy that actually has an electric slide. Clean hitboxes with the exception of enemies with mining picks that can wipe out entire continents with their downward swing. Even Cleaner numbers, this isn't maplestory where at endgame you deal billions of damage. At level 50 for example you might have 5-6x the hp of a level 1. Same goes for the raw damage. This allows for a decent player to take on mid-end-game enemies at level whatever, and that's pretty nice. At the time of playing and completing the game in 30ish hours on patch 1.04, I can say this was a surprisingly well made game. If I had to be nitpicky, could've used a personal map, especially in the city. The game has rather rewarding questlines that can open up sometimes downright absurd npc interactions, or apparently change the outcome of the game. However quests can sometimes be finicky on whether or not the game thinks you completed or failed a quest. For instance you can get the reward for a quest, and still get reprimanded for failing the quest because you didn't confirm the quest completion back at town. Audio can be a bit strange as the audio is centered on the character's position and facing, which can cause a little confusion. Also the enemy AI is very non-aggressive out of combat, removing a lot of the danger if you choose to use any sort of tactical approach, you can very easily separate large platoons with a few throwing knives. Wish the music that you can earn and have play in the hub would stay until changed. If I were forced to be objective, it's an easy 8/10 probably an 8.5/10. An action game that stands on it's own without the need of gimmicks, but more importantly it just works. Now if I didn't have to be objective 10/10 I'm actually already pre-ordering their next however many games.
