_childDocuments_.review: ====1/1/23 Update====A very promising combat system, for the most part, from a future AAA developer. Heck, you could say the game is already a AAA title, in some respects. The combat is great and reminds me of Fable meets Dark Souls, minus the cool assassination (back stab) moves of Dark Souls, or the ability to stab them when they're on the ground, though, I wish it had a clean parry/ counter-attack system. Hilda, with her sword and shield, has a neat shield bash counter-attack that is completely Spartan and I love it: She draws her shield back and drives/ slams the rim of her shield into the opponent. The only frustrating element there is that the enemy has time to hit her in the middle of countering, which is pointless as counter attacks go. If all counter-attack does is make you vulnerable? Why do it? Especially if they can also hit you before you've recovered from doing it! A counter-attack should work in a way that sets you up for a clean opportunity to stun/ jar them, while dealing notable bonus/ crit damage, and even possibly serving as a finisher. As is? It's just not feasible to use.The story is well done, but the voice acting suffers and so too does the in-game dialogue/ writing. Some of the responses are riddled with throwaway lines that the NPC doesn't even need to say, or responses that don't line up and because of that I just skip past most conversation. It makes me wonder if it's just poor translating to English. On the topic of writing? I think the person who wrote the story did not write the in-game dialogue because the bits of story that are narrated by Minerva sound well done. Graphics are well balanced an clean and the art style is gorgeous and reminds me a bit of something between Fenix Rising, Fable and World of Warcraft, but no ray tracing, no native HDR... It basically has the aesthetics of what a remastered Fable might look like i.e. it's definitely not pushing any present day FX... Not even real-time lighting. Should you remove the excessive fogging effect, using r.fog=0, within engine.ini, the lighting is jacked because it relies on the fog to mask the problem of lighting and shadows. With fog removed, it's just like someone painted black in the corners where shadows would be. You seen this technique, a lot, in games like 1995's Tomb Raider and Quake. Performance on a 6900 XT is actually kind of bad. I should be getting an easy 4K 120FPS, even on consoles, with what we're seeing onscreen. It shouldn't be that much more demanding than, say, Trine 4, to be honest and therefore should even be an 8K game, yet? I can't manage over 70FPS and can't figure out what's using that much GPU. I also receive slight stutters...even with VSYNC. This is while using the latest drivers. On my laptop, which uses a 3060TI, I run the game at 1080P and it has no issues meeting my monitor's 144Hz limit, ultra settings. Performance-wise I can run Assassin's Creed - Valhalla with 30% more frames at similar resolution, but AC Valhalla is doing ALOT more and in a much larger world with high res texture.  It's just a shame the game doesn't seem have true 4K or 8K texture assets, if DVD format were still a thing? This would be a DVD-9 install game, as weighs in at about 10GB. a small 4K game, these days? Should at least be over 20-30GB.Animations are a little stuttery, like when watching distant NPC/ enemy walk, it's like 15FPS. The animations are all together floaty, especially for Hilda. I'm an immersion player and prize being able to just walk in an analogue fashion, sometimes I walk slow and sometimes moderately fast, and I use gamepad for these sort of games for that reason, but sometimes PC games will let you control your walk speed, via, mouse wheel for this reason as well. Walking really slow (just a hair of thumbstick pressure) seems okay, in terms of animation, but it's so unnaturally slow that I don't think people walk like that, unless they're afraid of what's ahead or have a medical condition. Any additional pressure to move forward results in slow motion jogging, where HIlda's steps are too tall to be considered walking. It's like they took the running animation and just slowed it down and called it walking. Basically? The faster you walk, the more hideous it looks. In fact? Even running without sprint looks odd as well, but running with sprint looks more natural, but still floaty. When you walk down stairs Hilda is about 1 foot off of the ground and when she's standing out on the grass/ dirt her feet are under the soil a lot of the times.The game tends to get congested and uses the old school "follow the path" model, where you find yourself doubling back through the same areas, crossing over/ under previous areas and paralleling the same areas. It's fine because I grew up playing games like this, but nowadays? It's also nice to at least instill a sense of open-world, with some good open-world like areas. A game like this in a scaled down version of the Elden Ring map would be perfect, as it would combine a good balance between open-world and re-visiting old areas, in order to deeper explore places you didn't have access to prior. I did love, however, the labyrinth systems, like in the aqueduct and Stella Mines/ Glittering Mines, I felt like I was playing something between Ocarina of Time and a dungeon crawler at once. Audio is definitely not a problem. There are some sweet sound FX in this game, unlike others I have heard. Ambiance and mood is definitely not the game's problem. The music is very well composed.Side quests are lacking and lack direction. Half of them are obtained by knocking on doors of people you'll never see. I have some very cryptic quests in my journal that just say something like "Treachery! Enlisting the help of gangsters (or something to that effect)!" and I have no idea what it's alluding to, where I even got, nor where I am to go. Some of them just seem like vague statements or opinions than they do something more direct, like "Otto wants me to check the lab on the second floor of Styx" or "The stranger at Black Street asked me to collect 10 starite fragments..." Something we could all understand.The biggest crux?The game lacks CUSTOMIZATION!!! You can't have an RPG without this! I was excited to see there was a trinket system...none of the trinkets show up on Hilda! They're just passive stat increases. A major trick was lost. A deeper customization system is NEEDED! If you were not fortunate enough to catch the pre-order of this game because, like many, you had't heard about it until now, you've literally lost out on 1/3 of the customization options: there are only 3 possible outfits, including her starting gear. What's more? The devs don't seem keen to throw us any free content and add to the quality of life of the base game, instead? We have to wait to pay for DLC.Further more, on the topic of appearance, I feel like her sheath (more like luggage case) is way too big and distracting for her petite build and wish they'd have just gone with a minimalist approach and just show the two primary weapons you have selected...easy peasy. Her shield can go over her sword on her back, her staff/ spear/ hammer can co-exist with her hip/ lower back placed daggers, and her sword/ staff/ spear/ hammer can all be slung on her back, either in an X figure, or in parallel (Witcher style)...literally anything is better than a Death Stranding backpack. Add to this, no hair colors, no hair styles, no dyes for clothing...literally nothing to grind for but rocks and potions.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a licensed PS2 game.Like a publisher saw God of War 2 and thought "wow we can make money with that" and used an available IP to make their own game. That's not what happened here obviously, but it gives me the same janky feel. Like Nightmare Before Christmas on PS2. A DMC-like that was juuuuuust a little step or two away from being amazing.It's not bad, but everything feels just slightly off.Attack animations from enemies are ambiguous, they don't have the kind of tells other games of this kind do with audio cues or visual cues, and often have lots of small follow-ups. it's really easy to get stun-locked by very quick attacks like this. The parry is completely unreliable for most attacks because of this animation issue, you can learn the moves but they don't have anything actionable you can associate with them like a Dark Souls or DMC enemy would, and on top of that, hitboxes seem to be all over the place especially with humanoids.The first real boss, a big crocodile, has a giant AoE beam that sweeps extremely fast and it's not really easily reactable, you gotta predict it and the stance he takes he also uses for a much weaker attack that you can punish for good damage. The following boss, which is a scripted fight granted, has lightning spells that will stunlock you very easily too, which he'll use to cover his other attacks, and that's fine, but it  off. It's hard to put into words what's wrong because it's just janky.I like it so far, I can deal with the jank and will likely get used to it, but it needs a lot of polish which the devs seem to be totally onboard for. I look forward to that, for now I'll just keep playing. It's a good game for what it is and if I'm totally honest I do dig the jank a bit, it's kinda nostalgic that way.

_childDocuments_.review: in summary: I like this game. somehow, through all of it's flaws, it captured me. try it if you want to play an easy souls-like game in an interesting greco-roman fantasy setting.asterigos has good combat, a large variety of skills, weapon combinations, and spells at the player's disposal. it really feels like the combat is one of the most polished aspects of the experience. there is a lot of freedom afforded the player when it comes to choosing your fighting style. there's a large variety of enemies and bosses for you to combat, and the fighting never really gets stale.the cons...the game is extremely lore-heavy. characters you've never met before will tell you paragraphs of information about people and places and events you've never heard of. the world is clearly very complex, and the writers must have put in hundreds of hours constructing the history of the universe...but some things are better left a mystery. the pacing of the game often suffers from too much information being dumped on the player.aside from the hyper-verbosity of the storytelling, there are other issues with the writing. the story being told doesn't make particularly compelling reading. I mean, you don't have to sit down and write the next lord of the rings, but it certainly wouldn't hurt if the writing style was a bit more creative. the prose is dry: there is little humor, very little information is left to the imagination, and almost no plot detail isn't spelled out to the letter. I WISH the story was cut down to just the most interesting events, and the documents were fewer and a bit snappier. if you really like getting into the story of any game you play and you want to become an aphesian history professor, you're in luck!a nitpick about these documents: there are quite a few documents called things like "faded old document" or "document with lively handwriting" or "document with odd signature". they all use the same set of paper colors, and they ALL use the same exact font. video games are a visual medium, people. you can SHOW me handwriting on an old sheet of paper if a document is meant to be handwritten. you can SHOW me the odd signature on the dossier or what have you. show, don't tell applies to many arts, but the visual arts have the unique freedom to show almost anything you can imagine. just show it!hilda, our protagonist, is positioned awkwardly within the narrative as both the savior of aphes and also as a child who no-one respects...and at the same time, it's shown that hilda doesn't really respect herself, either. even by the end of the game, after becoming ostensibly the most powerful warrior of all time, her aspirations are modest and her plans for her future are dull and boring, if not bleak. the entire game, she seems to see herself as just a rank-and-file soldier, subservient to everyone and everything. it would have been a MUCH more interesting game if there was some form of character development beyond her stat numbers increasing.the "quest log", also known as the journal, is almost completely useless. unfortunately, when hilda is given a quest, she seems to not care about writing down what to actually *do* -- she seems to prefer writing down her miscellaneous, sometimes unrelated thoughts. this is just unmarked side quests with more steps. if you're going to have a character who actively journals during the game -- hell, you can SEE her literally pull out her little book and write stuff down -- let her write down a quest log! the things she writes down don't make sense. why wouldn't she, presumably a highly trained and disciplined soldier, make a log of her activities? skyrim did a similar thing, albeit with a much less diegetic "journal". to the game developers: you're not making dark souls. you don't have to copy *everything* they did.on top of that, all the text -- dialogue, item descriptions, scattered documents and the like -- is riddled with egregious typos and grammatical errors. without even that baseline level of writing polish, it's hard to care about what the game is trying to get you to read -- and again, there's a LOT of reading.the level design is fairly good...but it's intensely, noticeably barebones most of the time. the shelter is one of the areas that feels most "alive", due to items being scattered around, people lounging about, and npcs that you can talk to. hell, one of these npcs actually MOVES (vulcane the smith, who walks back and forth between her desk and anvil). imagine that. the rest of the world is mostly barren of all life save enemies to kill. if only there were a bit more decoration here and there, some lighting variation like the sun or moon's rays piercing through clouds, a person who doesn't just stand in one spot like a statue, a bit more color contrast in environments.... many of these levels feel dead and odd, like those false cities designed for military training.the mechanical issues are less noticeable during a regular playthrough, but they still exist. for context, I played my very first run on "challenge" difficulty. I figured there was *no way* this game is as hard as an actual souls game, so I played on the highest difficulty. one of the biggest effects of this mode is that your resistance to damage starts in the negatives; minus seventy per resistance type, to be exact. at the very late stages of the game, through careful gear selection, was actually able to get my resistance to either fire, magic, or ice all the way up to...zero. which is where it *starts* on the "adventure" difficulty.however, even on "challenge" difficulty -- in which you take almost double damage from nearly everything -- it's mostly an easy experience, especially if you've played the soulsborne games. but when it gets hard, it really gets pretty damned hard. however, I'm only referring to the optional paragon bosses that are accessed via the shrines throughout the game.some of these bosses, like , really feel like you'd need a doctorate in stamina management to effectively dodge every attack. some of them felt very unintuitive, with awkward movement required to beat them. some of them, like alkinoos (who's thankfully not very difficult), require performing some mind-numbingly repetitive event before getting to the actual boss fight.the difficulty of each boss is wildly inconsistent, both with the other paragon bosses and the rest of the game. I'd say both the  were MUCH more difficult than even the final boss of the game --  if you have multi-phase bosses and bosses that interact with the player before arriving at the "arena" proper, why in the name of heaven would you NOT use those mechanics for the ultimate enemy of the game?there seem to be a lot of audio bugs. even if you turn the volume down to the lowest setting on all the sliders, some sounds, such as lightning strikes from certain bosses, will still come through at full volume. it's odd how something like sound effects not responding to the volume slider didn't make it through testing.I really liked playing through this game. I'm currently trying to get all the achievements I accidentally locked myself out of via missing unmarked side quests, so I'm playing it again. I just wish it had a little more polish put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a hidden gem indeed. it has many elements that makes it a good souls-like, but it also has flaws that might be the reason why this game is not popular. Let's get into it:Game Design 8/10The character design is similar to overwatch, like crossover between Disney and Japanese 3D anime. The characters are finely detailed, especially the weapons. There is this one character with over-engineered weapon that is similar to Cloud's weapon from final fantasy 7 that can morph into another forms, the problem is that this character has very short screen time lol. When you see it in action you'd wished the main character has it too. It incorporated greek-roman theme which brings you unique souls experience.Map Design 9/10Many people complain about how they can get lost easily in this game and there are no map feature to locate and mark something for you to revisit later. As souls veteran, I'm used to this and it's perfectly fine, in fact, I personally prefer it like this. There are lot of hidden places, shortcuts you can unlock later, and overall very good map design. They are detailed, make sense, and most importantly, interesting enough for you to explore. Though at the endgame section, the map design is too bland, spacious and tedious, the only place that I give thumbs down. Story and Lore 8.5/10The characters in this game are memorable because they have good writing on their dialogues and the overall plot is interesting to follow. The politics are complex, makes you have to think in different perspective to fully understand the motives of each characters. Even though the main quest is too cliche, the writing will keep you entertained. Characters also has more dialogues the more progress you made or if you have anything relevant to them.Music 7/10Music is decent. The music you can play via a certain character in the game later, are quite nice to hear. Some characters have the best VA I ever heard. Combat 6/10Enemies: Too predictable and cheese-able. Each area doesn't have a lot of enemy variations, but each enemy have several good movesets especially the bosses. The problem is, they are very predictable and combat AI is too simple to execute each moveset. For example, get closer and they do moveset A, get far away they do moveset B, drops below certain HP and they do moveset C. In dark souls, you get more variations and enemies do take side walk, keeping its distance, do simple attack before doing specific moveset, which harder to predict. Weapons: Janky, sometimes unresponsive and unbalanced.There are 6 weapons you can choose and their respective skill tree. Each weapon has unique play style and customizeable moveset depending which skill you activate. For example a twin dagger can unleash flurry of attacks and you can pick what kind of followup attack; Be it jumping slash or charged flurry, you can customize it. Some skills and weapons are just too OP that you don't need specific weapon to defeat specific enemies. You can just use that one OP weapon and skill to the endgame. You cannot change your weapon easily. You have to go to menu, select primary and secondary weapon, then go back to fight. In summary, this game has a lot combat potential but the execution is not good enough. For indie dev, it's quite decent. Gameplay 7/10You got no markers, no quest trackers, no map. It's all in the narrative and how well you remember what to do. You do have journal where the main character keep track about things she found along the road including side quests. Personally I love it, but I understand that some people will prefer the convenience of maps and trackers. The fast travel feature will be unlocked later in the game, until you have it, you got to navigate manually. Obstacles on the road prevents you from getting further but you will eventually find shortcuts, keys, or other items later to get over it. To be fair, most souls game also has no map and quest trackerWeapon upgrade, augments and "trinkets" are not that interesting. There are no poison, bleed, etc. Only poise and elements. Replayability 2/10Unfortunately, this game has bad replayability due to the broken combat and the RPG dialogues. There are lot of dialogues and cutscenes, even though you can skip most of them, they're really taking your time. Don't get me wrong, a good writing is enjoyable at the first time you see it, but become tedious on NG+. The combat is harder in NG+ but that just makes the enemy more spongy and will easily oneshot you. You can get all the achievements on single playthrough, if you're following the guide and very skilled in combat or use easiest difficulty (one of the achievement needs you to cap your level to 20).

_childDocuments_.review: This one really hurts, because the Demo was so promising. A fresh wind in an otherwise cluttered "tRiPlE a" gaming season. Well, I think not. I gave it a fair chance, but after 75 minutes I am getting closer ot my 2 hour refund limit, which I certainly dont want to hit yet. Well, welcome to the burial of what I hoped would be my valentine.First off, I dont appreciate having control being taken away while dialogue is happening. "Our writer was so bad we need to disable all other buttons, so the player pays some attention to it" is all this is making me think of it. Then, I dont appreciate having the AI tracking be so bad, that I can literally always stay on someones butt and not ever get hit by anything. I dont appreciate that my smith is furry, although thats a personal thing but cmon man. And then the quest system. Why do I have to accept a main quest on this awkward quest board, when theres only one way to go anyways? Next, I absolutely dont appreciate a game that runs worse and even LOOKS WORSE than the demo did. The performance is all over the place. In some areas I cant even hit 10 fps on Balanced Preset, and then the next area gives me 40 fps on the Ultra Preset. WHAT is going on with this game? Then to top it all of, the developers business practices are really shady man. First PC players had to pay the same as console players for pre-order, but they did get a 72 hour early access and we didnt. People say "lol at least PC got the demo which console didnt" but the demo was free for christs sake and has nothing to do with the product I recieve upon purchase. The fact of the matter is, PC players got treated worse. But the worst is yet to come, because the discount only is available to people who own the game, yet everyone else had to pay full price for it. So I payed full price, the exact amount as console players, but didnt get all console players got, and then was PUNISHED for trusting the devs when preordering, because everyone who waited had to pay less. This hurts. I am sad. I really have to refund this, and I dont wanted to. I really had such high hopes after that perfect demo. Sad day for me. It is going to take alot of time to get me to trust Acme with their next game, I sure am never prepurchasing their games ever again, i learned that lesson.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review.In this episode I check a new Fantasy RPG called Asterigos: Curse Of The Stars. This game is the breakout title by small development team Acme Gamestudio and is published by Indie Powerhouse and friend of the channel Tinybuild.Asterigos follows the Adventures of Hilda, a young warrior from the Northwind Legion, a peacekeeping force which has been dispatched to the city of Aphes, which has come under seige from a a deadly curse that has decimated the population along with an army of Corrupted monsters. After her fathers squad goes missing shortly after arriving in Aphes, its up to Hilda to unravel the cities mysteries, and join forces with the survivors of Aphes to retake the city from the monsters.This game is an incredibly challenging experience that pays homage to classic action RPGs like Kingdoms of Amalur along with taking a little inspiration from the Dark Souls Series. The player is given freedom to build their character from a number of weapons and skills including close range combat, ranged weapons and magic. This is a solid Indie RPG that i highly recommend to fans of Tinybuilds previous work, or are just looking for an RPG to enjoy.Please note: All opinions in this video are my own. _childDocuments_.review: My friend and I just had a new profound love for souls-like games and it is when she bought it for me. Thank you Maruh! <3Let me start off by saying that you need no soulslike experience to play this gem. You might get fooled by videos, thinking the movement and controls are stiff, but in fact when you actually play it yourself everything is so smooth and the combat is very abstract once you unlock some skills. You have a good choice of weapons to use and elements to it (like fire, magic, thunder and ice).My friend would ask me to stream my gameplay for her and we would sometimes laugh our asses off as I was playing on hard mode and struggling to kill mobs mostly and falling down the map :D It has a good amount of interesting side-quests and side-bosses that you can enjoy, in case you are an explorer. All the bosses have a unique design and set of attacks, so they are enjoyable both on easy and hard difficulty mode. The maps are prettily design and the mobs are so good to the point that they annoy the ♥♥♥♥ out of you :D but you end up making fun of them At the first stages, the game has no map so it was a struggle for me but then I found if you talk to NPCs, they will give you some directions - don't worry, at a later stage you can teleport at any check points and you get so hooked into exploring and getting all items/chests, that you don't even need a map.The game has two endings and if you are an achievement hunter, you might enjoy the 'better' ending as it requires you to complete a certain set of side-quests in order to get to that ending. There are some guides online if you struggle.All in all, this game is definitely worth the money as it is a good amount of hours playtime (mind you I spent 37 and I still did not complete all quests) and the graphics are just beautiful. :coolchick:

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game has been fun, the combat is interesting and allows for several different styles. Personally I play aggressive and risky with daggers and bracelets for fast and slow attacks. There's 6 weapons in total: sword and shield, spear, staff, bracelets, daggers, and hammer. You can get damage upgrades to assign to your favorite weapons, blah blah, typical souls-like stuff here. however dying offers almost no punishment other than enemies respawning, it'd be nice if they had a soul system to buy levels and items but sadly exp is free. Personally I'm not that good at souls-like titles but I find this game to sort of be a breeze, I've counted every death in my play time and it totals to 6, 4 if you don't count falling into the endless void. So far I've beaten 3-4 bosses and haven't died to any of them. For people familiar with souls like games that want to give this a try, there's a pair of rings in the hub area that reduce all your stats by 30 and stop you from gaining exp, I recommend putting those on and playing on hard mode. YES, it has an easy mode. This would probably make for a good low-risk introduction to the genre for people that want to get an idea of what it's like. My biggest personal gripe with this game is getting from one zone to another. It's annoying and has probably taken me 45 total minutes to figure out how to get from one zone to the next so far. In the games defense, my navigation skills rival those of Roronoa Zoro.TLDR: fun but easy adventure that offers methods of boosting the challenge for veterans, somewhat unique combat system that *kinda* evolves as you get further in. The toughest challenge yet: finding the next area lol.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat loops are very good, but the boss fights are too easy if you spend time grinding by trying to navigate the mapless maze-like levels.The lack of map or guidance is the reason this game took 50 hours instead of 15. I spent *significantly* more time trying to find the next correct tunnel in the wild twist locations than actually progressing the story.Some major missed opportunities with great environmental interactions and changes to the map. Except for knocking a tree over a canyon (3 times) every one of them is used fewer times.Enemy's perception zones are just laughably small and the AI is very slow in their attacks.The story is utterly garbage. Disjointed, fleshed out by exposition 'echos'. No ones mouths move. You're introduced to teleportation in the first ~5 minutes of gameplay, but well into the main story your character is in awe of the concept being real. ...You've used it several times by then. The protagonist is amazed by what 'stardust' can do, but is a master of 6 *shape shifting* weapons powered by OP battle magic.Every NPC is demeaning to the protagonist. The subplots don't fit together. In combat she's far more powerful than her father, physically 5 times her size while the dude is insulting and dismissive. The side characters all share one of 4 enemy models making them instantly forgettable. The magic system is just anything and everything. Necklaces are the only consistent thematic piece. There's no guidance on which of the 3 quest threads to do in what order, even though you need elemental power-ups from one to complete the next, leaving you wandering for hours more. There's no map, there's no markers.

_childDocuments_.review: My initial impressions were that it is a "poor man's Darksouls game". Similar exploration and hack-n-slash combat themes. Animation-lock will be your biggest annoyance during combat.Although I was a little unsure of how I'd like the game, it quickly grew on me. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid MEH. I don't think it deserves an outright negative review, but it needs a light discount at least to be worth it. However, there are many glaring problems.Pros:1) A charming art style and good character design.2) Decent controls and move-set. Being able to seamlessly switch between your two carried weapons is cool and the particle effects from the moves look pretty too.3) An okay story. Nothing phenomenal, a bit convoluted, but decent enough to keep your interest along your journey.Cons:1) Bosses simply do not feel rewarding in this game because you are rewarded with nothing other than trinkets and crafting materials upon defeating them. Getting great loot after a hard fought battle is one of the best parts of a souls-like and it is simply missing here.2) You are stuck with the weapons you get at the beginning of the game and simply upgrade them throughout. This would be perfectly fine if it was a linear game, but a game like this should have things for you to discover, cool outfits and hairstyles to unlock and so on in my opinion.3) The lack of a proper map to use for navigation is huge oversight. It is a tremendous quality of life upgrade as games such as Elden Ring have demonstrated. I hope the devs add this as a patch. On the topic of navigation, teleportation between conduits takes a little too long to unlock (about a third into the game) and should have been allowed much earlier.----P.S. : I genuinely hope that the game does well enough for the developers to be able to justify making an Asterigos 2. For a small studio, they have achieved quite a lot; if they take feedback and learn from their mistakes from the first title, I truly believe they could make a proper gem of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game! Story, lore, characters, environment and graphics are all beautifully done. There are incentives to play this game several times. Combat is so fun and well design! People like to compare everything to Souls games these days so I will do the same - I would describe this as much easier Dark souls. Different weapons with their respective skills and perks offer so many possibilities. For example, I always like to play a mage character in these games, but there are no explicit spells here. However, one of the weapons is staff and using it feels like casting spells. Dodging feels incredibly satisfying and is spot on. Different elements further enhance combat. There are manu upgrades, collectibles, and side quests that are also similar to Souls system, i.e. there is no quest log and often you have to deduce yourself what needs to be done. Perhaps a little more mercifully, you at least have a journal here to help you with that. The only little criticism I would have is inability to create our own character, which I like more than playing with a set character. Hilda is OK, but during my playthrough I kept imagining how it would look like with a custom character and I did not see any moment it would not work. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: A respectable action-adventure game.  While it shares some similarities to the "Souls-like" genre, I don't feel it quite earns that distinction.  There are plenty of opportunities to cheese fights with range/techniques and stamina rarely runs out when you need it most.  The dungeon designs were sprawling and memorable, but sometimes overstayed their welcome (looking at you, Styx).  Quests are "logged" in your journal but otherwise tracking them is a chore - there are several I left open, because I didn't feel the need to see them through to the end and backtrack through an area for the 20th time to get lackluster crafting loot as a reward.  Combat is enjoyable and responsive, with dodging being able to interrupt your attack combos quite quickly allowing for more risky and aggressive play style.  Each weapon set felt good to use, though I ended up settling for the Spear and Staff for the majority of my playthrough.  Each weapon has a "talent tree" that you will easily be able to spec into two of (accounting for the ability to quickly swap between two equipped weapons in combat with fluid transitions), which link to special skills(spells) for each weapon type.  Many of the actual skills seem gimmicky and not altogether useful considering how precious mana becomes in prolonged engagements, but there are several exceptions that upgrade the weapon's damage output or utility considerably.  The story I felt was the weakest link, and the ending itself seems to come abruptly and with little consequence to your actions as a player.  You can skip most dialogue, which I found myself doing on a few occasions when conversations were clearly trying to build the world's lore, but had constant interruptions with poorly timed "reactionary" comments from the main character.  All in all, this is worth a shot if you're looking for a 25-30 hour single player adventure with fun combat and a large world to explore.  Worth it at asking price and a steal on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is likely one of my favorite games of this year. I've played Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous, Elden Ring and the Horizon series for most of the year and this game has scratched the adventure RPG itch for me quite well.The latest update improved a lot of the main gripes I had (especially the stamina drain while dashing in the main hub).I've not completed the game, yet, but so far the story (especially all of the lore you find around the game) has really kept me interested in finishing it. The skill trees are all very interesting and lend themselves to multiple playthroughs to see how you enjoy different playstyles. There are hybrid weapon combos that are hidden and only discoverable through experimentation.At the end of the day, though, the game is very easy to grasp though difficult to master. It would be nice to have a harder difficulty to play through in the New Game+ because the enemies in my current playthrough are pretty easy to beat once you get their attack patterns down.Overall, I'm a major fan of this game. I'll be following this studio for future releases for sure, and I'm excited for the DLC. I will update this review once I beat the game and add some more detail.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a very nice AA soulslike game with a bright colour palette with some dark areas and story beats. If you're looking to get into the story, side quests, characters and lore, there is a lot to chew on here and I'd highly recommend giving it a try. If you just want the combat and exploration, the game is nice but there are better alternatives out there.As someone who has never played (but knows some stuff about) Dark Souls, I feel like this game is baby's first soulslike. The combat and the level design/exploration seems very inspired by the former, although more forgiving in all fronts. The game has 2 possible endings, and most of the dialogue choices don't matter. The ones that do matter in regards to the Glory Ending (the alternate ending) can only be found out by paying a lot of attention to the lore and/or by playing more than once and paying attention to the special sound queue that plays after relevant choices are locked in. None of the choices truly alter the story in any big way, even if the narrative leads you to believe so in your first playthrough. Consider this a linear game with a normal and an alternate ending, not a choice-based game (regardless of the marketing might lead you to believe).

All the general criticisms about lack of map, delayed fast travel, endless irrelevant lore & tedious text conversations, and some bland detailing are true, but cope with those and you can enjoy slick controls, fast-paced combat, decent weapon / skill choices, varied and clearly themed locations, a consistent style and some cool designs. _childDocuments_.review: This isn't a "souls-like", it's a "dark souls clone", it's so utterly faithful to the original Dark Souls formula in every way. I could write a page straight just listing every single aspect of it that is lifted directly from the Fromsoft games. This includes combat, level structure, loot design, and so much more. They've laid over top a fairly boring plot and quest structure - but it is just about entirely skippable and optional: you can just kill your way to the next boss, skip some talking, and repeat until the game ends. This - like any souls clone - is about the moment to moment combat - and the combat is very good. It's not *quite* as tight as Fromsoft's own combat, but it's well beyond serviceable. Parrying and countering with the spear is an absolute delight. The rolls feel great, the bosses are fun and fair with plenty of character to each of them, the trash mobs are great fun to knock over with well-timed parries... if you're into the slow blow-trading combat of Dark Souls, you'll probably love this.Strict Fromsoft purists will surely find many slight nitpicks to complain about if they try, as they cannot help but do - but if you just want to do some Dark Souls style combat in a pretty game with a new, brighter setting, and some bosses you haven't fought before, hoo boy does this deliver. A lovely, lovely time. Polished, pretty, satisfying - it's Dark Souls with a Sekiro parry option and fresh aesthetics. What more can one ask for?

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is fun, similar to Dark Soul but easier. The i-frames on dodging seems to be much longer and outside of some bosses there are very few enemies that can one shot you or nearly one shot you. I use a 3-1-2 distribution for attack-health-ability levels.Performance/graphics is good for me at all max settings, but I'm also using a 3090 so your mileage may vary. Key binds cannot be changed, which is massive glaring issue. The developers have said that they are fixing this. The story is interesting enough, but there is way too much text. I mostly just skim through it.Ultrawide works but you need to edit an ini file otherwise it just shrinks your vertical fov to "zoom in". Character customization is very limited. No visual changes, you just pick 2 of 6 weapon types and use those for the entire game since the perk system is fully tied to each weapon. There is no map and I only unlocked fast travel 10 hours into the game. If you're not someone who can remember routes then you might have a frustrating experience of running in circles. The side quest system is absolutely abysmal. You've got a journal but it doesn't tell you what to do or where to go. It only lists what you've already done. So again you better have a good memory and be able to figure out where to go and what to do based on context clues.Overall the game is worth the $35 price point, but barely. It's good points are really good and it's bad points are really bad, so value will differ depending on the person. Check some gameplay videos out before you buy.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, mostly. The combat's not incredibly nuanced, but you can dodge-cancel out of many attacks, which helps, because everything hits like a truck.Outside of the weapon mod system (unlocked in the expansion), your basic attacks don't consume stamina, just dodges, sprinting, and whatever alt-fire mode your weapons have. But stamina regens extremely fast, so it's not really worth worrying about except for some edge cases. One of the Expansion's challenges is one such case.There's a lotta dialog, there's a lot of documents... none of them matter all that much. And very little of it is going to stick with me, I'm afraid. The story is... there. The characters are what really shine. They do have nuances. Although I was getting *extremely* sick of the game insisting on moral relativism and you have to figure out your own answers about good and evil, but everyone clearly *has* thoughts about what's acceptable, and it comes across as extremely hollow.There's 2 endings, and the process for getting the better ending... there's some guide-dang-it bits, because it's about certain sidequests being resolved correctly, and I wouldn't have guessed the right responses, or even if a given quest could result in a point towards the good. BUT the war table does sprout a wee badge each time you get one right, so there's *some* way to track it.It's alright. I was rather surprised to find out that the recently added bonus stats from finding chests wants you to find more than all of the chests in the game. (NG+) And I was really irritated by a couple of the optional final-chapter bosses, and a couple of the expansion's arenas felt unfair. (A couple were really cool to solve though.)I waited for the DLC to drop, which turned out to be smart with how post-release patches added whole systems as well as polish. And as per usual, there was a sale to coincide with that.It kept me interested and entertained. And even the most frustrating bits only needed a handful of retries. (Though one, I only won due to a glitch in my favor.) So, it's a recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay Video:  ✔️ ; your name is Hilda and you visit the city of Aphes to find and save your father, and figure out what the heck is going on in this city. You will find at least 250 documents and hidden notes in the world that either adds more to the lore, or some pointless and boring statements/stories that have nothing to do with it. There are tons of side quests that you can find and a lot of interesting characters to talk to❌ ; there are two endings (and side characters endings shown as a slideshow, similar to Fallout), but story is pretty linear; there are no branching paths or butterfly effect, you will fight the same bosses and take the same missions. That being said, for some reason the game shames you for killing a certain boss/doing a certain action, and I thought to myself that there had to be another way, so I loaded an old save and kept exploring the same areas multiple times, tried to find different paths and even avoided fights, but there wasn’t, and I wasted more than 3 hours of my time. However, picking certain choices and finishing specific side quests can unlock more dialogue and affect which ending you’ll get.❌ ; at a certain point, the game will give you three separate missions with their own substories to finish, and you can choose which one you want to begin with. However, each one stops halfway through (when the story starts to get good, the game gives you a poor excuse like “the door is closed, i’ll think of a way to open it later”), and in order to continue you must complete the other two (halfway though as well), then complete an entirely new quest, and then you will come back to them. Not to mention that the quests are heavily scripted and have to be done by the book or else you won't be able to progress. , there was one sidequest later in the game, I found most of the notes, I knew what was going on and where to go, I found the locked door that led to the next objective, and I had the key to open it, yet I couldn’t do so, why? Turns out I had to find one more hidden document first, and then I can open itThis is just me being nitpicky, but what makes a souls-like game awesome is the emphasis on environmental storytelling and lets the player connect the dots, and not constantly spoon-feeding it to us, which the game does constantly.✔️ ; staff, daggers, sword and shield, hammer, bracelets and spear, and you can only equip two weapons and four different abilities. You can upgrade weapons and unlock powerful abilities using stardust (aka points that you get from killing enemies) and materials that you find in the world. They are fun to use against enemies. If only they added more ranged weapons other than the staff (such as a crossbow).✔️ ; “story” aka easy mode, “adventure” which is the normal difficulty, and “challenge” which is the dark souls level of difficulty (and sometimes even harder). You won’t gain extra experience/stardust if you choose a higher difficulty, but enemies will do more damage to you. In addition, if you play on “adventure/challenge” diff. you will lose 20% of your stardust when you die, if you choose “story” difficulty then you'll lose only 10%.✔️ ; there are over 22 bosses (main, optional and endgame), and most of them have their own unique design, combat style and music theme. The endgame bosses are difficult so prepare yourself before facing them. I played it on the hardest difficulty and they were pretty challenging to the point that they can oneshot you if you aren’t careful.❌ ; for example:✔️ ; the game has a similar art style to Immortals Fenyx Rising. There are a lot of interesting locations to explore, tons of hidden passages and different regions to visit.❌ ; some doors look openable but they aren't, some platforms look reachable but actually aren't, and some buildings look accessible but they are actually out of bounds.✔️ ; butter-smooth 60 FPS.❌ ; unexpected camera movement, large enemies fit into tiny doors, game freezes when saving, character disappears when teleporting, odd hitboxes, getting stuck between objects and weird surround sound(?) (fighting an enemy in front of you but the sound comes from behind). All in all, the game took me about 25 hours to complete, and it’ll probably take 10 more hours if I want to find the rest of the endgame bosses and complete all the achievements. So many cons but I still recommend it; it is a decent game with fun combat, good story, great soundtrack and challenging bosses. As for the issues: yes, I know this is an indie game from a new indie studio, but coming from ex-"Blizzard, X-Legend, XPEC, and Runewaker '' developers, it is still a good game but it could’ve been better.

_childDocuments_.review: Devs, sorry for a bad review. I see that you put a lot of work in this title, but if you don't know how to do a soulsborne mechanics right - just don't do it.Combat is a main break point - and this is a focus mechanic of the whole game. Unpleasantly slow, unresponsive, and sluggish. We are not wearing Havel's Set here, and look at Bloodborne or Nioh - she don't need to be so slow.A small tip for you:Reduce inactivity frames, speed up her attacks for 20% and general speed for at least 30%, make her rolls longer and faster - if it plays more fun this way - implement it.Enemies have a very badly telegraphed attacks. _childDocuments_.review: makes a strong first impression but after half a dozen hours or so you'll quickly come to realize most of its mechanics and features are merely superfluous, hiding how shallow it all actually is. You gain access to all 6 weapons from the start but once you start leveling two of them there's no incentive to ever swap out the selection. Combat itself isn't bad per se but does feel like they've tried to disguise a hack-and-slash game as a Soulslike. Which, for obvious reasons, doesn't really work. Stamina isn't tied to combat and so you can basically just swing away endlessly without any major penalties. The difficulty while playing on Challenging is borderline unplayable at times as it suffers from huge spikes in difficulty and I quickly found myself sticking it on "Story" instead. Life's simply too short and this game, despite its best efforts, doesn't deserve my time what with all of the poorly designed boss fights and enemy attacks that can outright ignore geometry or reach you despite not being anywhere near the attack.The environments look nice and offer a nice change of pace from all of the dark and oppressive levels we've seen from other titles in the genre but unfortunately provide very shoddy signposting and can often become maze-like. When you are not trying to find your way around the place you'll often be stopped in your tracks by endless (and I mean ) amounts of dialogue, lore texts and other uninspired exposition dumps (have fun knocking on an inordinate amount of doors and read how "Character B" talks to "Character D" without any voice acting or flavour). For people who obsess over lore this game has you covered as there's entire novels around almost every corner and desk but for people who prefer to play a game instead of reading one at least know that you can thankfully skip most of it with the press of a button. I'm not sure what they were thinking including this many narrative elements though. I can enjoy a good story in a game as much as the next guy but the way its told in  borders on being obstructive. It's simply too much. Obviously it's a budget title and as such as can excuse some of the jankiness but even when looking past some of those issues  remains a mediocre Soulsite (I use that term loosely here) albeit with an inviting art style. It throws everything at the wall in hopes of something sticking and unfortunately most of it doesn't. It's an "okay" game at best but an incredibly frustrating one at worst. So I can only recommend this if you're somewhat new to the genre and when it's on sale at that. Otherwise you're better off playing something like  instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasantly surprised by this game. I'm into souls-likes and this game is on the easier side. I like the story, characters, atmosphere, exploration and level design. I think they pretty much nailed it with the labyrinthine levels and multitudes of unlockable shortcuts. The game's story/lore is sometimes darker than you might expect. There are sad and tragic moments and also outright disturbing ones. But it's all kept together by the cheerful personality of the protagonist. I didn't really find any flaws. This is one of the games that I have to force myself to quit after several hours because the flow is so great. I always want to explore just a bit further. People complain about the lack of key/button remapping but I'm fine with the controller controls. There are four presets that you can choose from (as a western souls-like player I chose "type c") but they also promised that they are going to provide remapping capabilities in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I had Asterigos on my wishlist for months before finally giving it a try (haven't played the DLC). I'm the kind of player who would become incredibly frustrated with Dark Souls and Bloodborne (I played some of the latter and quit early because of said frustration), but Asterigos offers me a similar kind, but easier, challenge, even on normal. This game feels ACCESSIBLE. I cannot overstate how overjoyed I am about this, too. I play on normal, so I can imagine easy will be even better for those who need more breathing room than I do when playing a game. That's not to say that it's dirt easy, though, I was left a little frustrated with some encounters, but not to the extent that made me quit Bloodborne before I'd even progressed past the first area.The story is amazing. If you're used to loads of hints on where to go next, it might be a bit challenging, but if you've the heart of an explorer like me, this won't be much of a problem - the game pretty much goes out of its way to reward exploration! If you like to delve into lore, there's a bunch of documents and dialogue (even if not fully voice-acted) that will paint a clear picture of Aphes and its history.If you're aesthetically inclined, Asterigos is also a clear winner. The character and environment design is just stunning. I'm a great fan of the effects, too.I know some feel that combat can become a bit repetitive, but I'm not sure I agree - the enemies are quite varied, and you need to learn how their attacks work to time your parries (I really love the spear) and dodges, as well as to effectively counter.TL;DR: This is a story-rich, accessible, semi-soulslike and beautiful game that I wholly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played just under 8 hours of the game but there are a few things that stand out quite sharply to me. The story is quite interesting, finding out parts of the history of Aphes through fragments as you explore the world is very interesting and leaves an air of mystery.The questing isn't completely linear. Instead of fetch and complete types of quests it allows you the ability to do quests in the order you prefer, it also has fun little side quests along the way that add to the history of the game. However, that leads me to my only complaint (so far).There is no map. And I mean NO MAP. No waypoints, no markers, nothing. A lot of the game comes down to aimless wandering because of this and the NPC's are not good at giving directions. A lot of the time I'm having to trace and retrace my steps to figure out where I am and where I'm going or I find myself running through the same area 2/3/4 times before I figure out how to progress. It can be quite jarring overall.Overall, I would suggest this game, the lack of a map does give a major drawback but the combat and story leave you wanting more.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I'd like to say that I like the ideas and what developers at Acme wanted to do with Asterigos. Despite its very obvious and stylelized look, not very huge budged and feel to it, the game is very ambitious when it comes to lore and world building, which is a blessing and a curse at the same time, depending on peoples tastes, what they're looking for in games and what they like in this genre - which is character/story-driven dialogue heavy single player Action RPG.There's so much lore, so much dialogues, many characters to talk to for at least 10-15 min (if not more), so many various texts you can read etc., that it is owhervelming. And on top of that you can go to doors, overhear conversations and even partake in them if you want, which is a very strange design decision cuz you're basically talking with doors and not actuall characters you can see.I get that this is a way to make the game's world feel alive, but unfortunately it just doesn't work for me, it's not very interesting, ingaging or memorable, the ambition is there, but not the actual interesting part of it for you to see and experience, or at least I don't think that it was fully realized. Take A Plague Tale: Requiem for example, you can't talk for 99% of NPC's in cities and towns, but it wasn't NPC's purpouse, their purpouse was to make the world feel alive without ovhervelming you with not very needed or not interesting conversations and there was actual NPC's there, not locked doors with voices... oh, wait, I mean't texts.You see, only very few dialogues (and scattered throughout the world memories of the past) are voiced, everything else is text only. Now this is for sure related to the games budget and totally understandable. Cuz let's face it, if there's something else in the game that can be made better be it gameplay, combat, visuals and what have you... then to cut VA's budget is for sure the right thing to do in my eyes, especially since there's so much text and digalogues. Plus, the very best games of old didn't even had VA to begin with, relying on a huge amount of text instead (partly due to very small CD space budget of just 700MBs back when there was only CDs available), so... that's not a huge problem. As for the lore, billions of scrolls, text notes etc., well I'm sorry, but there's just way too much of them and I've stopped reading very lenghty ones with multiple pages. I mean, c'mon, I admire the world and lore building and it is very well written, but at one point in development you really need to make hard decisions and axe some stuff / scale it down and only leave the most important stuff for players to read. I can't say I know how it feels to not put something you worked hard on into the game you've been worked for years, but at some point you just have to make difficult decision and make your game better for it and not bloat it while chasing for ambitions.Now, let's talk about gameplay. I'm just gonna say it... I don't like combat in Astergos. It works for sure, there's multiple weapons you can use with their own playstyles so if you like it, you will have options. But in a world where Kena exists, which is a much less ambitious game overall and there's not that many weapons you can use in it, despite all that lack of variety in weapons and playstyles, it just feels better to play, more fluid visually, more polished and responsive. I can't say that combat in Asterigos is bad, far from it, I've played far, FAR worse games over the last 30 years than Asterigos, it's just to me the fact that it's just works is not enough to like it. I hoped that after the patch (which fixed and improved many things in the game) it'll be made more enjoyable, but it didn't happen.The actual design of the world is not very good also. I mean, visually it looks good and I like the art and modeling, but it's way too large, there's not such thing as easy navigation, no such thing as a map to let you explore the world and see where you've been or not yet etc. There's no way to track quests or any sort of clear, working and understandable system for this, there's a journal, but it's a mess. There's also very strange way for you to fast travel - you use scrolls to teleport to the game's main hub, but you can't teleport to places you've been already to finish side quests (which are not very good in terms of what you actually doing). You can only travel to the very last point on the map you have saved at and you can't travel freely between these points which is absolutely buffeling to me. The levels are HUGE in this game so you'll be walking and running A LOT, but to make it less boring and tedious... there's only half a solution in the game right now, while very obvious one is right there for everyone to see, which could've been less of a pain than what's in the game now. To be clear, I'm not talking about markers showing you were you need to go etc., no, the actuall world navigation and exploration of it needs to be enjoyable, but it isn't, not yet anyway.I guess to summ it all up... it's Acme's first game as a team, so I'm willing to close my eyes on a lot of things cuz let's face it, what developers strided to achieve is very, Very admiring. You can just see that there's a ton of work people put into this game, but sometimes it's not the ambitions you need to stride for, but to make the best possible game in every aspect which you can actually fully realize with what's possible looking at your budget. And with that, despite all of this criticizm, various flaws and very strange design decisions, I still think that it's a good game overall and I think there's an audience for it for sure, so it get's a Recommended rating from me.If developers are reading this - guys, I'm sure that after reading a ton of feedback you will make your next game better, it's just innevitable. So, i'm wishing you the best of luck with what you'll come up with next time.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this was a very solid arpg. I recommend this and I look forward to the already planned DLC. My thoughts below.Story- Not bad, Greek mythology inspired but it's own thing. Dialogue can be pretty cheesy but I really warmed up to it after initially brushing it off. Only important bits are voice acted. There is a ton of written lore to find if you are into that.Combat- Decently fun. I didn't get bored with it despite using the same 2 weapons for my entire playthrough. You area offered 6 weapons within the first few minutes of the game and can use any 2 at once. Each weapon has up to a 4 hit combo and a special ability. You can finish a combo from one weapon with the final blow from the other. There is a skill tree that allows you to unlock passives and 5 (I think) unique skills and a stance for each weapon to further customize your playstyle.Quests- Only main quests are tracked. The only slightly negative that I have with this game is side quests aren't tracked and aren't always straight forward. I either forgot or didn't understand what I needed to do because I missed the dialogue due to real world distractions. I ended up not finishing several side quests due to this which also means I missed unlocking some secrets that were tied to those quests. There is a journal, but I didn't feel like it really helped with the way it was structured. Turning in quests isn't always straight forward as I always found myself just going through every dialogue option with all the NPC's until I found the correct option to turn the quest in.

_childDocuments_.review: Right, so let's talk about this game shall we? Coming from a background of a lot story driven games as my favorite choices, I can confidently say that on story telling this game delivers big time. The only issue I find in it, is the pacing, there are times where you feel like you need have rewind button to get all the indepth details. Especially when some of the side quests come into play. But overall, the story is a gripping adventure that keeps you engaged from start to end.Gameplay can feel a bit wonky, it is a learning curve with weapon and skill combo's you can have, and in that lies the real challenge, as upgrading your weapons, talent points etc. is something you don't -just- reset without paying a price. Mobs and Quest have a decent difficulty and some depending on the how you've upgraded yourself, can at times feel like fighting a Dark-souls-esc battle.Is there anything I would have liked to be different? Well, a longer story for one, perhaps a bit more varied end content that lets it feel like you've now truly become a master of your weapon and skill. A plot-twist somewhere there as well and of course, a sort of multiple endings deal... Why the multiple endings? Well, there were some encounters that gave the heavy vibe that different outcomes could be reached depending on dialog, but that wasn't the case, and felt really unfulfilling.I recommend giving this game a go if your looking a fabulous story with fun fantasy hack'n'slash.7/10 - would play again.

_childDocuments_.review: Good first entry for a new studio.Cool bosses, fluid combat, good level design, replayability in terms of quest lines, an interesting world with memorable characters. Stuff like the drawings as your quest log shows the devs really put a lot of effort into making this.The art direction is also really nice, it gives you that feeling of seeing some stuff way off in the distance and you go "yup, ill go there in the future". Definitely worth playing if you're into this sort of stuff.Now i'll rant about a few things that bugged me while playing:Slow. Elevators. Remember that elevator in Drangleic Castle? Well, all the elevators basically move at that speed.You know how straightforward Dark Souls quests are, right? Well now imagine the options to advance are 2 layers deep in a dialogue tree. Although you generally know where characters will be if you pay attention.Combo system is good, but a bit basic. (sequel pls)Early game spoiler: Too much dialogue, stuff gets repeated often, for instance a character gets mentioned. Later on you meet him, he introduces himself and Hilda (MC) is like "Who dis?"I played on Challenge difficulty, however i think, while in normal NG it was balanced how i like it, in NG+ the poor design difference for these modes starts to rear its head. This is because there are three difficulties, Casual, Adventure and Challenge. Casual gives you a ♥♥♥♥ ton of extra health, Adventure is just "normal" and Challenge gives you a -70 penalty in defense. So, you just take 70% extra damage, right? Seems ok for a hard mode? The thing is defense gear is borderline useless because of this. (Armor effectiveness is reduced by more than half, and that gap only grows as you get more armor)♥♥♥♥ Blood Vials.Anyways, a very solid start and i'm looking forward for the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely impressiv, detailed and most importantly fun adventure.Beautiful fantasy edition of Disneys Brave vs Romans. The settings are at the same time consistent and varied enough. Huge world that you can walk from end to end (except the tutorial area) without interuption. You get different types of fast travel pretty quickly (Town portal first, free teleport later). Since there is no map and a lot of quests are only described to you, it helps if you aren't dependant on minimaps or mindless 'follow the glow' markers. If navigating Netflix is the limit for you, head elsewhere.Storytelling is largely well done. There are some cultural implications of this being a (chinese?) asian production which the very good localization can't hide. Some character are on the weird side and the narrative can be a bit jarring (you meet a person for the first time and there is a huge amount of backstory that only ever gets alluded to, but only spelled out in tiny bits). The characters being on the weird side isn't exactly bad. You aren't running around as a random hollow slaying mute at least.Pretty satisfying experience all told.

_childDocuments_.review: Wasn't particularly 'souls-like' in my opinion but proved to be a solid RPG.Pro's:- gameplay/combat was fine, with some dodge/weaving expected- Art style was nice with plenty of variety between different areas- Story was... ok, alot of it told through letters/collectibles- Lots of chests/collectibles, reasons to explore the map and take some risksCon's:- music was... ok? Nothing egregious but never got that sense of hype on boss battles, for example- Story was a bit hard to follow if I wasn't collecting and reading everything to fill in the gaps- Didn't like the 'souls' attempt at losing Starite on death. Was a bit odd to lose a chunk but have no way to get it back like in most souls-like games. If I had low Starite at any time, I was often compelled to just run through areas and look for chests rather than fight my way through it, as I had little to lose and gear doesn't get damaged upon dying- Alot of enemies were very easy to kill, so combat didn't always feel as calculated and risky as I expect from a 'souls'. Recommend putting onto the hardest difficulty if you want that punishing factor added back inGot this on discount and easily got my money's worth. Missed quite alot in my first playthrough so might do the NG+ version in the near future. If I knew the game would be as enjoyable as it was for me I probably would've bought sooner at full price- but I just took a gamble and it paid off nicely.8/10 as an all-round RPG for the collection6/10 if being strict on what I expect from a souls-like

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is playing on Challenging difficulty, I can assure you that Asterigos is Soulslike and very difficult.Normal enemies would hit you like 35% - 50% of your HP per hit, while you need to hit back 4-5 times (at least with spell) to kill each of them. Boss enemies have unique mechanics where all of them can one-shot you to death. You have to get familiar with their animations / movesets before you can actually defeat it - expect to get killed 4-5 times before winning the fight. Things might get more convenient once your character is at higher levels, but still not to the point that you can unga-bunga everything.Overall, it's a great Adventure RPG - refined graphic, great soundtrack, difficult yet satisfying combat mechanics, huge map zones to explore, and deep storyline (you can choose to read or skip most of it). :)

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly enjoyable experience. I tried all the weapons at the start and settled on daggers because of how quickly you can dodge, but they all have really useful upgrades, skills, and abilities that seem to make them all feel really strong.exploration is pretty satisfying with not a lot of dead ends, and the way the main quest line continues is pretty straight forward too. There's also an insane amount of readables/lore dumps that at first I just decided to skip through, but started reading through them and found myself really enjoying the reads. The bosses were pretty easy for the most part compared to the rest, but they looked cool at least, and felt decent. Good spread of checkpoints and shortcuts too in the level design.I've just been prompted for the point of no return, and I've really enjoyed my time. _childDocuments_.review: Super cool, especially for the price.Comparing it to Souls games isn't right, it's more like Nioh with a vastly simpler equipment system, though it does have some of those Soulslike influences.I think my favorite part of the game is the two weapon system, letting you kinda make up combos on the fly, and it's surprising that all six weapon types have their own switch attack that happens if you change weapons mid-combo.The characters are interesting (if really longwinded exposition-y), the setting is cool, and the combat is great.Anyway, complaints, since I don't like reviews that just list off the good stuff:1. The skill tree is kinda weak since there's six paths, one for each weapon, and that's it, unless the game unlocks something fancier later on, but I don't think it does. This means you're very unlikely to do anything more than just two paths and maybe some of the starter passives.2. You have three (3) stats to put points into. That's it.3. (Haven't gotten far enough in the game to really see it much, but) apparently the game's marketing has always been about it being some game with a bazillion choices that matter, but people have been saying there's really only like two or three situations where that's true. Also, the game tried giving me a serious choice to make, but then I looked it up later and found all three options result in the same thing, no changes.4. As much as I love it, the bracelet weapon is an abhorrent mishmash of random stuff all jammed together in one weapon, like they just couldn't decide.5. There's a whole "switch elements on the fly" system, but no way to tell what any enemy is weak to, so you're stuck randomly guessing and hopefully remembering what you find out, AND hoping you fight groups that are weak to the same things.6. Equipment is basically just "two weapons, plus four accessories" and I'm really hoping the accessories become more complex than just defensive stats later. Really hoped for something more complex than this.7. There's one of those battle pass things just randomly stapled onto the game. It's nothing bad and it's free, you just earn a point when you open a chest during your adventures and slowly unlock things as you go, but why is it even in the game?8. Jump and climb mechanics are weak. it's got that generic "climb what the devs manually marked as climbable" thing, where you'll never be sure if you're allowed to climb something or not, and you can't jump to grab onto the ledge unless they manually marked it as such too, which comes with silly moments like a rock that's a pixel higher than your jump preventing you from going up there, making you backtrack for the "proper" way.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm updating this review after playing the game more extensively. I was excited to see this game release, as it was very similar to a game that I had in mind and wanted to make. There is a lot of potential here, but I don't think that it was particularly well executed.After more play, and the initial hype has died down, I have a few criticisms to make:The story makes little sense. It doesn't feel like the characters or the city have as long of a history as is explicitly stated. There are times when the protagonist knows things that they shouldn't, or their scope of knowledge leaves the player in the dark. While the amount of lore is impressive, with an incoherent story, I find that my motivation to play is significantly reduced.There was a lot of potential in the combat, and still is, but it's too clunky for my liking. Very few of the attacks actually feel good or rhythmic. It's like I press a button, wait for an age, and then my character will do damage. The overall system of chaining light and heavy attacks and using special mana-consuming abilities, however is solid I think.Still standing from my previous review, the downsides that it's not visually remarkable by modern standards still stands. The light and shadows could use an overhaul. There are also a few bugs that need addressing. I encountered one where I was attacked and killed during dialogue with an NPC, which caused my UI to disappear upon respawn until I restarted the game. I've also found holes in the map where meshes don't hide the murky space that is the skysphere and fog.Overall score is going down to 2.5/5 from 4/5. Huge potential, delivery is shaky. I'll update again if I manage to finish the game's story and am impressed.

_childDocuments_.review: Great souls-ish type game, on the easier side for that kind of game which is a positive to me. Has a fairly interesting story with lots of good lore and worldbuilding, told in a much more direct way compared to the usual in its genre. My main annoyance with the game is a trend taking hold of gaming in general lately, boring rewards for exploration (it's pretty much always just upgrade materials since they give you all the weapons at the very beginning of the game and have a leveling system to acquire skills from) so I don't really hold it against the game too much. It's also a lot longer than I was expecting, and I didn't really find that to be in its favor, the second half of the game doesn't add much to mix things up gameplay-wise  and will probably be purely running on how much you enjoy the story at that point. Overall though, I enjoyed my time with the game and am excited for the expansion and whatever else comes out of this studio in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game game!!! It's the perfect gateway to the soulslike genre being far more approachable in terms of difficulty, but keeping some of the core mechanics. The combat system is fluid and engaging with multiple weapons to choose from to adapt to any style even though the common enemies are rather easy and predictable, the main characters are well written in the majority of cases and keep you engaged until the end. the lore is excellent: choerent, plentifull and well written all around. you really feel you get to know the world of asterigos reading the various document you will find in your adventure and the story is not shakespeare but it's far from the worst I've seen in a videogame. Good things on the technical side too: the graphic are semi-cartoonish so no photorealism here but still very well realized. in 50ish hours of game i only had one crash and the few lag i saw were during the loading so no complaints there. the audio compartment is solid but nothing that you will remember for years and i liked the voice acting. All in all it's absolutely worth buying it at full price but if you got it on sale, which happens pretty frequently, is a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is like many say a not really a soulslike, I want to start with that. The game is good the story is quite more direct and the gameplay has many similarities with the genre but the game is far easier. Yes you can still die but the times I did was because I got thrown off a cliff in an already tight space.Performance is good, I played at 3440x1440 (21:9) all the way and while I had to make a quick fix for the fov, I played at 120 fps all the time. Yes I had some stutters when loading the game but it would recover a few seconds later and stay strong the rest of my play sessions.Now, gameplay. Yes it has soulslike elements but the game can be abused with the save system so the penalties are avoided but the penalties are usually so small that is not really an issue. I finished the game on easy and I still had a bit of challenge as I decided to finish the game not going above level 20 (you have to find an item hidden in a chest in the shelter for this to be an option). Most bosses are fairly easy at least the main ones, I only went for 1 optional and I didn't do it on purpose.The game has a pretty impressive skill tree that you can reset to work better with the weapons you like the most. I only used the shield sword as main and daggers as secondary. Both main and secondary can be used at the same time for combos and use special skills to unlock in the trees making your fighting style feel good although combos are pretty simple.Do I recommend it? yes. The story and the aesthetics made me stay, the dialogue is sometimes week but in general is a pretty good experience for the value. It has plenty of content and the difficulty can be increased for those more skilled in the genre. But please don't expect a full soulslike experience as is more of a hack n' slash game with soulslike elements.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is an ARPG that borrows some elements from Souls-like games, but is not itself a Souls-like. For one thing, the difficulty is nowhere near similar to the Soulsborne series. I'm playing this game on Challenging, the highest difficulty, and it's easier compared to a Soulsborne.However, that doesn't mean the combat is bad. It's actually really good for an ARPG, with just the right amount of customization that let's you build your own character. The story has a good premise and good lore behind it, but the writing for the dialogue and some collectible documents is super cringe that it makes me flinch reading or hearing it. Your mileage may vary though.All in all, it's a good game for it's price tag, and I'm having fun with it.
