_childDocuments_.review: If you can see through the fact that your caracter looks like a Bratz doll from 20 years ago, this is actually a really good game, carried by the really, really good exploration. ( like REALLY good.) it will take alot of time to find all items, dokuments, chests etc.. Lots of doors that opens from the other side, ladders to kick down, mimics in chests, respawning enemies, ng+ and other soulslike elements. That being said, it has been critisized alot for having an "easy mode", but any dark-souler knows that just because theres candy infront of you, doesnt mean youll have to pick it up. So dont go easy mode, because even on hard mode its not really that hard if you are experienced in the world of souls-like games. You can however very early on put on an item (like agape ring in ds2) so you wont gain experience, meaning you can go through the game on lvl 7 or something, and also theres another item that will take 30 % of all your stats if you wear it. do that and your playthrough will be more challenging and alot more fun. As for the visual part i liked the atmosphere of the areas, but would have loved to be able to change the appearence of the "cartoonish" caracter, which just doesnt fit into the universe or the surrounding visuals Imo :) As for Controls and move-sets its pretty decent, and switching between your two carried weapons feels nice and fluid, like the game itself. Theres not any ground-breaking new mechanics you havent seen before, but If you like the exploration part of souls games, you will like this. If you however only are into the "Fighting challenge" part of soulslike games, you might get a bit dissapointed even on hard mode. For me the exploration kept me interested (still need a few chests) and ill def do annother run sometime soon, just for that "holy" achievement :)  7,5 /10

_childDocuments_.review: LET ME SAY FIRST THAT YES, I WOULD BE UP FOR ASTERIGOS 2, BUT....It's a game of half and half, and I really wanted to wait to review this near the very end of the game. It's not a definite yes or no, but it's in the "maybe" pile. The concept is a very nice design. I want to be brutally harsh on this game on as much as possible, but before I plunge the knife, Acme did a good job. It's a learning curve to a good recipe. The edges on this first attempt are just..quite burnt. POSITIVES- Hilda. Great design, hope to see again and see more development as a person- Weapon choice. Got a little bit of freedom.- Voice acting from all is pretty good. Two thumbs up.-Elemental mechanics. Nice variation, stuff like ice putting out fire, lightning breaking goo, which also teaches you to stun mimics.-very good environmentally in terms of area design. -Butcher boss-Jumping is fluid and works quite wellNEGATIVES- Harold comes off as a..REALLY dislikable character. I feel like the game is too mean to Hilda too quickly, and a lot of characters you just won't like, and won't really grow to change that opinion. Harold's setup is worthy of a punch however. Definitely not a fault in the model design or the VA, but more a script issue? There's a lot of made-up terminology they have to make up and that'd take a lot of work, but just..yeah, the script doesn't flow for me. Could do with some polish.- Costumes are set as post-game rewards, and the preorder costume does NOT work. I don't really plan on doing multiple rounds, so this just feels like a slap in the face to miss this. It's not a core part of the game, but like, why make 3 costumes when 2 are locked, and the 3rd doesn't work? There's a lot of people complaining about this in general.- The shield mechanic within the sword+shield weapon is just not viable.- Grab attacks from mimics and centipedes deal overwhelmingly high damage, and feel a little visually uncomfortable. Would be nice to see it toned down, block some damage with a qte, or just like, something more vanilla? Have a guard throw binding bolas's or a grappler that throws you across the room or such.- The "Area-wide" blast from a certain gigantic boss is kinda poorly set, Needs a bit more, direction to guide the player close first BEFORE the callout. Chances are, if you're on the second floor still, you won't make it.-Certain quests are bugged or have poor timeframes for completion- Sword+Shield ankle slide. Great attack, but bugged if you slide into certain objects and get permanently stuck WITHIN the object.-Feather shots can pierce through certain coverIt's flawed, but good. Even with my criticism, i'd honestly say, people should buy it just to encourage Asterigos 2.

_childDocuments_.review: So I don't usually leave reviews but I've put in enough hours to give my honest opinion. I've played all of the souls games other than demon souls since day 1 release of Ds1. I love the souls series and I'm always super hesitant on "soulslike" games. This one however has honestly been a really fun one. The combat is crisp and the way its implemented is unique. Leveling up is straightforward and it has a skill tree kind of thing, but it's not crazy massive and overwhelming. Upgrading your weapon is similar to the souls games except there's another component that works in tandem with your weapon that also needs upgrading. Usually that can become tedious, but so far is not the case for me.  It's easy to understand and it's not like the BEST story in the world, but it has been interesting enough for me to actually read a lot of the dialogue. In my honest opinion, I'm a fan and am pretty hooked at the moment. I hope these developers keep making games because they've got some talent.

It's sort of like the magic system was added at the last minute and there was no attempt to balance around it.The levels are well designed and circle back on themselves at surprising times, but the areas are all so samey-looking you won't know if you're backtracking for quite a while.C+  buy it for your 10 year old

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 50 hours in game, completing most of the side quests and the first round of the game. I must say that this game gets a recommendation from me.  This is my first soulsbourne like game, I am a complete newbie to this genre. But I enjoyed it immensely for being my first foray into the game. The combat was slick with style, while not holding your hand you learn to use magic and all your weapons through the game. Learning not only monsters, but environment reactions to your weapons and element was a major factor for my enjoyment. The art style was enjoyable through out, the in game character models are distinct and memorable, while Hilda's journal held enough art to it that it felt like an entirely different game. I am looking forward to accomplishing more rounds to this game and exploring all of what I missed or could not cover in my first play through. I would recommend this whole heartily to those whom are fence on this game, it is well worth the price and I look forward to the DLC and future sequels to explore this world.

_childDocuments_.review: This game in its demo seemed very promising, but the story is so absolutely boring I found myself skipping through dialogue to just get to the next gameplay point. And that's where I find an issue. The gameplay is fun, and fast, but the number of times enemies just sit there in between animations  at you while you prep a charge attack is just very obvious. There's also moments where I've gotten hit at the end of an enemy combo, only for the character to just stand still "stunlocked" with no clear visual of why, and the enemy standing still as well. Combat itself at the core is just too easy, just spam your abilities, back off, and dodge constantly. This game is just too forgiving with its I-frames allowing for dodge roll spam, and unnecessarily punishing with AOE attacks (love a big dude falling on me 3 feet away somehow crushing me). That there is no true fast travel system except to "last point you traveled" and "hub that is way too empty early on with nothing to do", just makes this game feel hollow. I really tried to give this game a shot, but it does not scratch the itch I thought it would when I had played a demo.The walking speed in this is so slow. It feels like it was lowered so that it would take players longer to traverse maps that are fairly empty in some locations to draw out play time. I wish I had gone with my gut at just before the 2 hour mark because this is definitely a purchase I regret.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure I'd recommend it for its price, I got about 32 hours out of it and didn't do everything. It's a good game, but it's far, far from a great game. It's like baby's first souls-like adjacent game. It's got bonfires, and very light souls currency mechanic. That's about it. The pros:- Great visuals- Great music- Expansive world, like in true Dark Souls fashion, you can run from one point in the world to the other technically with never hitting a loading screen. It just makes uses of long ladders and elevators instead.The cons:- Way, way, way, way, way too much dialogue and reading!!! This game is overly story told, they just keep cramming dialogue and reading in where they can it certainly seems. It's so overdone that I actually lost interest in reading anymore, and just button mashed through dialogue not even halfway through the game. It's..ridiculous honestly. It's further insulting since there's copious amounts of flyers, posters, pages, and books to read all around the adventure that do a great job of world building on its own. You can infer just as much about the story and setting just by reading the materials instead of having a stupid amount of NPCs with overwhelming, mind-numbing dialogue. - Some hit boxes on somethings throughout the game are questionable.- Some typos here and there in dialogue, load screens, etc.- The Bracelets weapon was a disappointment. I was hyped going in expecting to have a souls-like brawler, but nope they just lock you into a slow, sluggish, very short ranged magic ball attack thing. It was very confusing, because there are brawler/monk enemies in the game who have unarmed fighting animations...is it that hard to give the main character the same thing?I may recommend it, but I'll be haunted for some time at how great this game could have been if it had just hard-line emulated Dark Souls 1 (To the creators' original artistic direction's dismay). If you played DS1 and play this, then you'll probably be disappointed and may understand where I'm coming from with this thought. It just would've been so much better with minimal dialogue & NPCs and no story direction other than what you can infer exploring and reading materials/flavor text.

_childDocuments_.review: Played it from start to end with all the little and big things I could do along the way. Was extremely happy with the: graphics, the gameplay, the storylines - Main and Sides, and the characters - Heroes and Villains. It finds itself moving along like Zelda from 64 days in the storylines and the depth of the characters is even more than you could hope for in most characters! FYI - NOT SOULS LIKE!!! Only people who think that are people who didn't play Souls or cheats at games>>>>However, there are some parts that really need some work like: the map system - specifically being able to see where you need to go more precisely even if its not a teleport, the quest list - being able to read it and follow through to next objective or at LEAST know when its been completed, there are some bugs - like in Laurel house when I was going back through the building to the top of the stairs during one mission segment there was a bug that kept making my character fall through the ground instead of completing stairs to door to outside motion(expected its new)(not a big deal).Loved the game and can't wait to see what these developers can do in the future!!! It was worth every penny and even got me through a dark time of losing my best friend of around 3 1/2 years. Was sad of course then at the Faithful Lion Pet part of the game : ( : (. _childDocuments_.review: First of all - this game does everything correctly. It kept me hooked until I have beaten the third boss, then I suddenly lost interest. It simply felt like I had seen all aspects of the game already.Recommendation-wise: Asterigos has nice story and characters in the vein of JRPGs with its emotional and relational twists. Gameplay is mostly souls-like from the checkpoints that heal/save/respawn enemies, to the souls gathering (but used only as currency). Crafting/trading system is clearly taken from Dark Souls III, and movements/skills system from Nioh as well as potion mechanics. Sounds are great, and music is beautiful sometimes creating really nice atmosphere, and all that complemented with more than decent voice acting.All in all - I'm glad I've received a good 1 hour per euro paid here, might even finish the game in the future.7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending only to the people who are desperately eager to play a game which includes:1. 3D close combat2. Nice looking female protagonist3. Attribute/Ability customization4. without any other additional requestsIn addition, recommending only to the people who are OK with:To be honest, the battle itself is challenging and acceptable. The attribute and ability systems are customizable and interesting. It's possible that you get killed by a mob while you are distracted. So, if you could continuously discover the joy of struggling, you could be happy/satisfied. The motivation is the problem though.As an ex-Sqaure Enix fan (I was born in 80s in Japan.) I thought for over 10 years: "Square Enix is still a good storyteller. Yet, their games often lack an integrity between story and gameplay. I'm not gonna watch movies."But ironically, Asterigos made me think the contrary. Yes, we need the both to play - A good story motivates you to move your character. A good gameplay motivates you to discover further episodes of the story. The each of them needs to be linked together well like a perpetual motion machine.Playing Asterigos gives you such a feeling like you are playing, just in 3D, a 1980s'/90s' game which no one of your school mates knew though it was allegedly not selling so bad.Personally, I am satisfied with the game because I wished the above mentioned 4 conditions anyway before the purchase and could buy it earlier for a huge discount price. However, if I had bought it for the full price, I definitely had blamed the game and myself for days.As a result, If the game costs less than 20 Euros/USD, 2000 JPY AND you are 100% sure about your wishes, then I can recommend you it. But if you pay more/have more expectations - No. I can't.Having all said, I actually have a positive feeling towards the development team since they are releasing bug fixes and improvements one after another. I don't hate the game, I think it's a pity that its story, text lines, heroine's voice and personality are so powerless in comparison to its combat system.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Damn. I was very pleasantly surprised by "Asterigos". I went in not expecting much really, but instead got delivered a high quality, challenging and detailed RPG with beautiful character models, exceptional boss fights, with very fluid and customizable combat system, and an engaging progression system that makes you want to explore and fight enemies. Also the game runs very smoothly and you can get super high frame rates even on maxed out settings. Cons:For all its pros listed above, there are cons, and one very major one. The worst offender is the sheer, staggering amount of expository dialogue in this game. Oh boy, it never ends. There is so much in fact, that about 60% of the total dialogue is not actually voice acted, which is extra jarring- people are talking to each other one second, and the next, complete silence for all the other dialogue choices. And when you add the document system into this, (story notes), at _MULTIPLE_ times the game slows down to an absolute CRAWL, where you are going nowhere for the next 50 minutes if you want to learn more about the cursed city of Aphes. Better click all those dialogue boxes and read all the notes. Yeah no, I gave up after like 10 hours in. Too much is too much. You will understand once you play it yourself.  The other significant one that will affect, and has affected many peoples playthroughs, is basically the complete lack of a mapping system of any kind. No large "M" button area map, or a minimap with markers. Nope. You get a dimly glowing throwable marker that will disappear into the background faster than you can take a sip of sparkling water and look back at the screen. Mostly, completely useless.  Those 2 cons are what I'd keep in mind when making the purchase- other than that, I give "Asterigos" a warm recommendation on behalf of the things the game does exceedingly well.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but nothing about it is worth recommending. I can think of many cons, but no legit pros. Here goes.CONS:- fortnite/valorant graphics, yet the game still doesnt run well compared to other games that look far better- gameplay is hella janky. Movement, hitboxes, abilities, none of it feels right- story is delivered through excessive amounts of dialogue. And I really mean excessive. These characters just wont shut up. Its like the polar opposite of Dark Souls storytelling...- audio is weird, especially water sounds. Fountains and checkpoints sound like flushing toilets- game is too easy even on the hardest difficulty, except you'll occasionally get 2-shot by bosses- you get all 6 of the weapons in the game right away. Theres no gear progression and nothing to find except passive buffs. This makes exploration boring- there are way too many of the same enemies in some areasIt's really not a good Soulslike. The devs really tried, but it just didnt work for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.Captures the worldspace inter-connectivity and pacing of DS1, with a smoother less jank combat system. It has deliberate pacing in combat (slow estus heals, attack commits, long skill casts, knockdowns, etc,) that mirrors true souls-likes yet has snappy moves, combos and general speed of something closer to elden ring or code vein. Very clean and rewarding combat; no input queuing issues or iframe jank at all.Generally great boss fights (especially towards the end of the game and in the DLC) with few long boss runs and quality design- they test the players spatial awareness and pattern recognition rather than quick twitch reactions, like a true souls-like should. Enemy movesets become increasingly diverse but always remain exceptionally readable and telegraphed, so they always seem fair (even one shots). I played primarily as a staff mage build and the enemy boss kiting felt fair; frenetic at times, most bosses had interesting gap closers and directional combos to keep a ranged combat difficult and satisfying (I played on challenge mode for reference).Story showed that you can weave a moderately complex narrative into a souls-like and enrich the game; the cutscenes and verbose dialog and notes engendered me to the story, rather than taking me out of it. Character customization felt meaningful and solid, playstyles felt diverse and unique depending on build.Can't say enough glowing remarks about this game. They took the souls-like formula and knocked it out the park. I especially like that they were able to develop a quality souls-like without any of the unfathomable genre-defining 'waste the players time as a meaningful failure consequence' design garbage that even Miyazaki has now abandoned.Don't let the unique aesthetic fool you; this is an exceptional game for souls fans, and considering its an indie title it deserves far for recognition.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a VERY GOOD "double A" game.  Dark Souls 1 inspired.  Little sprinkle of Zelda?  Stamina management.  Connected level design.  Hidden sub bosses.  Nice mix of Roman and Greek mythology.  Fine art direction and world building.  Hilda is charming BUT a little chatty.  I really hope DEVS do a sequel.  IMHO, would be cool to get more mature or seasoned Hilda.  Maybe... in her late 20s or early 30s.  More experienced.  Stalwart.  Not as talkative.  That is my only negative.  Man, too much chit chat.  Small talk and dialogue... slightly messed with flow and pacing for me.  Game runs good.  FSR works fine.  On my rig, very good resolution and FPS.  No crashes or major issues.  All in all, nice ARPG.  Enjoyed my time with it.  8/10

_childDocuments_.review: It is a rather decent indie souls-like type of game with nice art direction and mostly responsive combat. Story is and characters aren't particularly memorable but they are good enough to create a believable setting. Gameplay-wise, Asterigos falls on the easier side of the genre (it is also closer to something like Kingdoms of Amalur than Dark Souls) as even on highest difficulty the timing windows for blocking and dodging are generous and enemies aren't particularly aggressive. The combat does become slightly repetitive after ~20 hours as there are only 6 weapons with limited move-sets. The game doesn't have a map which is normal for the genre yet here I wished it wasn't the case as some of the areas you're running through in early-mid section of the game are particularly similar looking (city corridors) and it might be confusing at first on where to go next and which alleyways are dead-ends you've been to before an hour ago.Overall the game is a 7/10 to me, I enjoyed it for most of the time but it would have been better if it had more variety in terms of weapons and character customisation, or if it ended few hours earlier.

_childDocuments_.review: If I was going to give it any accolade it would be: The game with the most savage chest mimics award :')A very good game with a fully realised world, which includes heaps of flavour text embedded in notes etc throughout each of the areas. Was expecting a short and sweet 10 hours romp, but have been pleasantly surprised by the amount of content included without there being an excessive amount of backtracking, which becomes a non-issue about a quarter of the way in.  Doesn't break new ground as far as combat goes, does what it does competently and has a decent variety of weapons with their own skill trees. Had me at breaking point with one of the bosses and another that took a few attempts. Recommend playing on the hardest setting for the best experience as its quite well balanced and feel like how it is intended to be. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to anyone who likes Action RPGs, but Nier fans in particular will appreciate its sense of world-building and lore. The graphics, music, and overall presentation are above average for a game like this. The greco-roman world sparkles (sometimes literally) with detail. The voice acting comes across believably and convincingly, especially emotional and important scenes. The main character Hilda is curious, driven, and capable, traits which I found endearing.Difficulty is fairly customize-able. There's an easy, normal, and hard mode. You take a lot of damage but trinkets and awareness help you reduce it. You can easily grind your level too high if you feel like it, but there are also trinkets you can equip which make you take more damage and earn no XP. Get ready to read and also get ready to lose your bearings. If these two things don't automatically disqualify the game for you, you'll find an enjoyable and replay-able experience here.

_childDocuments_.review: It's at least a polished and optimized game. But it completely fails to keep me interested.The art style isn't my cup of tea, with those self illuminated weapons and gadgets, as if everything is glass or plastic with built-in LED lights. The voice acting (especially one of the voices) is sometimes terrible, and sounds like your nerd friend trying to sound powerful during a live RPG.I've tried to force myself through this game. But dodging and killing monsters all the time is not what I consider fun - so I cheated with WeMod so I could focus on other things. It got a small tad funnier that way, since I could spend more time with exploration and story. But... Somewhere mid game you get some objectives in places NOT marked on your map. So you have no idea where to go. I suppose you are encouraged to explore. But that is only fun to the point where you believe you've covered every inch already, and can't figure out what spot you have missed. The levels are a maze after all, where every room looks the same as the other, and there's no map (not a useful one at least). So it gets difficult.At that point, I feel like I have milked every drop of fun there is out of this game. It wasn't much, so... Not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Changing my review sadly to a negative. There is some positives but the negatives are starting to outweigh the good the further into the game I progress. To the point it is getting more frustrating than fun. Sadly the AI is unpredictable. Sometimes they notice me and other times I walk right up to them.  A lot of times when I try to interact with items such as picking up notes or potions it does not register or when it does it takes multiple tries. This in combination with the more annoying, rather than game breaking elements such as not being able to re-bind your keys, not being able to turn off sub-titles, and not being able to track one mission at a time (coupled with no mini map or compass) is just grating.  The core concept is there, the combat on the players end does feel good and the weapons fun to use. However in its current state I would wait for a steep sale or until a few patches have come out. _childDocuments_.review: Sure it looks like a game DISNEY could have made. It promises a lot of content and that it delivers. Does it contain chests to find? Yes it does! When you discover a new area, do you see it big on screen? Yes it does! This game scores on all fronts, yet the execution of it is in my opinion and experience: bad.As if everything is made of out of wood and the grease is wearing out.Has a lot of lore and content. Eat your heart out with the many written dialogues, fixed angle echos, fixed dialogue encounters, manuscripts, tiles, posters, letters, cutscenes, voice acting...It's okay, she is a protagonist, she will talk in that way a lot "oh is that a stairway? Should I go up that stairway? I think I am going up that stairway to see what is up there" But also a lot of encounters with other character with their own unique tone and personality. Well that is fully up to the developer, but I paid 35 for it and to me it feels like overpriced. Like I had way more fun playing "Venetica" then with this game. I would have recommended it for 14.99 (euros).Some are quite nicely designed, there is variation. But with the controls and game mechanics, not THAT enjoyable as it should.Some effort was done to create these towns, cities, surroundings, nothing to complain, other than that they work like a maze. Nothing wrong with that, it offers short cuts in the long run, so that is how its build on that. It definitely sets the mood.There is quite some journey to travel upon. Fast travel back to the shelter is by using scrolls, which you can purchase but also just find throughout the world.There is quite some variation in entities, but some just don't make sense WHY they are there in the first place and the assets are well used. Some a bit too much, but that is okay, better something than only bald spots everywhere where only a ladder offers the "variation" right?Sounds are on point.There is a skill tree to master specific weapons you want to focus on and to get more perks to help you on your way. More health, more strength... It's started sluggish, but I read everything, the story is compelling. But eventually I stopped, because there was too much useless information, same with the encounters. Eventually doing a speedrun as it feels, but I do enjoy the story and only that. For the rest, I don't care anymore. It's imho horrible... Yet, I say YES to recommendation, because it delivers what it promises, only the execution of it all is done very poorly. To me, it's annoying, to you it might be very enjoyable, who knows... I played it with keyboard & mouse, maybe it plays better with a controller... But if you are a gamer like myself, I would NOT recommend it. My biggest annoyance is her recovery time when being punched to the ground. Takes forever to stand up. When you died, you spawn back at those checkpoint saving points, the overexessive animations are not needed. Some you can skip but a lot you can't.  But I never got stuck, no gamebreakers, it plays and you discover a lot in a long lasting journey. I would wait for the price getting lower, but other then that: Go for it! There is a DLC coming, I won't buy it, will be happy when I finish it purely for the story and that is that. Maybe the DLC is better made, like with that DLC from the game "Ashen" :D :D :D
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: The game is MEH. If you can't sleep, you should start playing this, in 20 minutes you will start submitting to combo of artistic calmness and music. Not every conversation is voiced, that was a big disappointment for me.I can't say, that I do not recommend the game, cause it's fine, but at same time, it was not worth it for me. The setup had noting to do with Rome/Greek except the artistic design and likeness to Olympus. There was no religion aligned to this phenomenon. It felt alien, felt like a child, being schooled on all the steps.[SPOILERS AHEAD] Made second guessing my own decisions at times, not really like a hero to save the day. even as you finish game, you get back home to be trained by father. WTF did I need that for, how did my character grow trough this, where is the reflection of this? Do not confuse it with the very weak recognition told as a legend to kids. [END OF SPOILERS]Game needs also a map. Visuals are great, I like the flow of fighting, different weapon stiles and combos. Effects are neat too. The connection build up to other characters felt weak. The most connected I did feel was to a lion that was not even my companion, and the smith that was so enthusiastic that it felt hard to not feel a kindred spirit.The tracking of quest trough Journal is a mess. Can make great scratches, unable to draw a map of the place. Unacceptable. Following up on the side quest is a hustle. Decision trough dialog are minor and when they happen, they felt like they sneak up on you. You better make a save prior next dialog, you might want to take another path. If you forgot that, the auto-safe will make sure to solidify your choice if you are unwilling to repeat last 1h of playtime or more.My recommendation, skip this. Wait for Gothic 1 Remake and be blown away.I did finish the game, so thanks to developers to make a quality product that did entertain trough most of my time spend of the game, despite the shortcomings I listed.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly good game. Genuinely the most fun I've had with a Souls-like outside of Nioh 2. In short, it looks good given its very particular art direction, animations are smooth and solid, and combat ,while looking a bit clunky, is responsive and smooth. All the issues I have with most other souls-like games tend to be around terrible i-frame registration, stiff combat, no animation/dodge-canceling and cheap enemy tactics. In truth, there isn't a single Souls-like game I even enjoy outside of Nioh 2 which, to be fair, deserves to be in its own category and not viewed as a Souls-like. All that said, this game has none of those aforementioned issues. For being an indie-game (and it does feel like an indie game), it is very well done and polished. An easy 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, very fun and well made. It feels more like a Darksiders-like than a Souls-like which is in the tags. Everything from the artstyle and gameplay, to the progression of the story and quests feels like it did in Darksiders 2. Which is a good thing. The animations are well done and combat flows really well, doesn't feel clunky at all. The world is interesting, based on Greek mythology. It's also very interconnected, you sometimes end up in a past area that you didn't think you were near. You find lots of shortcuts etc, Generally just good level design. The only thing that bugs me is that it feels like the game was made with gear and equipment drops in mind, but it was cut out last second or something. The systems are there but they aren't really used. You have slots for some trinkets, but thats it. You can make these at a smith but they don't appear on your character.And there are countless hidden areas and secrets with big shining treasure chests to loot, and in every one of them all you find is 1 or 2 upgrade materials. Which just feels kind of dissapointing after a while.It does make me think that the devs had intended to implement gear and drops but just couldn't finish that aspect up in time, or didn't have the budget.Either way very good for a new studio. Can recommend it for anyone, especially if you like Darksiders or action RPG's generally. Hoping this does well and they can make an even better sequel sometime.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wonderful in my opinion. It's single player, open world, with main quests and side quests. _childDocuments_.review: Greece-themed manapunk. I love itDifficulty: Mediocre. I guess it can be a good introduction to souls-like genre. 1Gameplay: Dynamic and flashy. Six different types of weapons at your disposal with different utilization. But stances are just broken. 1Story: If Siddhartha Gautama was nurtured to help the poor, instead of becoming Buddha, he will become Uchiha Madara. There are also some speculations regading social class system, but i find them underdeveloped. 0World: Forget about the vagueness of souls-like, because you will be buried under the freakin library of internal documents what shed light on in-game events. 1Main bosses: They're distinctive and enjoyable. I would say they're all almost at they same level of difficulty. Except for Eulalia. You suck, Eulalia. 1Optional bosses: Cool creeps and they're more challenging than the main ones. But there is one but. In order to find them, you have to go to the same locations, and there is zero motivation to do so. 1Things that annoyed: - Hilda keeps her journal and, if you expect to find relevant information about quests, you're dead wrong. She almost NEVER writes down what exactly needs to be done and where to go. She just contemplates on a situation. If you postponed a quest, your only option is Google. -1- The customization of the main character is almost absent. You cannot change an apperance of your weapons. You have only one additional outfit for your first playthrough. That's it. -1- I wouldn't say that this one  annoyed me, I'm just dissapointed. Final boss is epic however extremely weak. I expected a proper challenge. -1 So, I give this game 2 bad endings out of 0. Nice game. Play it. But don't expect much. Just enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best souls-like games I've ever played, despite its cartoonish style and and relatively simplistic story.Pros:* no local map (only quite uselesss global Sekiro-like one);* no quest markers;* net-like locations will require you to memorise where you've been and where you haven't; intertwined by openable shortcuts;* different types of weapons with different animations and different skills;* good visual style, architecture, characters' and weapons' models;* good calming music (though, maybe, not a lot of it);* good optimization;* good price (12 USD is the full price in my country);Cons:* if the location is designed to be like I've described above ("will require you to memorise all the paths") it should be less monotonous, it should contain more noticeable and memorable objects, to spark the idea of the location-learning in the player (and simplify it, the learning);* if you don't have what interesting to show on the part of the location -- don't stretch it and inhabit by identical/similar enemies; better make it at least just a bit more compact, but instead more interesting, memorable, concentrated;* I may be blind. But if I'm not, and the game indeed somewhere in the first half of it(self) allows you to craft 4 mediocre trinkets and nothing new is being added till the end of the game (no new trinkets to craft and no upgrades to existing ones) -- I'm not sure why you've spend your time on that feature at all. This feels half baked;* I don't see a reason why healing potions aren't automatically replenished as soon as I return to the hub. Other consumables as well.* not required, but it would probably be nice if in the description of the quest at least a respawn point would be mentioned, like "blah-blah-blah, where you can get if you start from the A point and turn to the left". Then the player opens the "special" map finds a point A by its name, "goes" there and knows where to go next. But that's minor, I had problems with not knowing where to go, but rarely;* please don't disable "skip cutscene" button, ever, if possible;* a ton of collectible texts, which I have nothing against of, but since I'm not a big reader, I find them more redundant then useful (or at least interesting);* BUG: if you change the outfit of your character to the alternative one, come close to the ladder from the top (at least the stone wall, maybe other kinds of ladders too) and press "go down", the character will either try to do that but stay on the top, or try to do that and fall down; I don't remember when I've seen something like this the last time 😮Conclusion: recommended, even strongly, for its price. Waiting for the next part.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my wishlist for a while. And as as soulslike fan I really tried to enjoy it. But after only 3 hours playing on "epic" difficulty I find this game incredibly underwhelming.First thing you will notice when starting the game is the clunky controls. Man, this really feels like controlling a character from the N64 era. The default walking animation is so abysmally synced. While doing one step the character travels the distance of 3 steps for example making it just look really weird all the time.Followed by terrible hitboxes. Right in the tutorial area for example there is a small canyon with a tiny enemy blocking the way. Your character should be able to pass it on both sides easily, yet it blockes the whole passage.The most important thing in a soulslike is the enemy / camera lock mechanic - which basically does not work in this game. To make it work you have to perfectly aim on the enemy with your character, otherwise it won't lock on the enemy. In most souls like games when an enemy comes from behind, you just press the camera lock, to turn around and fight it. Here you click it 20 times while rotating the camera without being able to lock onto it. SO basically in 95% of all encounters you just attack enemies randomly without the camera lock. You can't even lock an enemy right in front of you just because it walks up the stairs. Terrible.Next terrible flaw is having to press the heal button for something like 0,5 - 1,5sec before triggering the heal. I don't know who thought of that but healing in a soulslike should be an easy task. Here you have to remove your finger from the trigger, and risk being hit by not being able to control your character, only to realize that the 3 or 4 attempts of hitting the heal button didn't work and you have to try again and again. Why?Not being able to hit multiple enemies which huge swings while they stand next to each other randomly, also confuses me.dashed into the quintus area with the 3 robbers... got killed by them during dialoque animation not being able to move... I found the storytelling so boring and forced that I started skipping dialogues right after the tutorial area.So yeah - finished 2 1/2 areas after 3 hours - which I did not enjoy exploring - like at all.By the way. In the windows task bar the game is misspelled "Asteriogos" while running.

_childDocuments_.review: Game had tonnes of screen tearing and stuttering for me, which doesn't happen in much more demanding titles, so something's up with this game in particular.Gameplay felt stiff and just didn't engage me at all. Looking at the trailers and such I expected something more fluid and akin to Horizon Zero Dawn, which I loved, but this is so so far from that experience. I regret the time I put into this. A wholly lackluster experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Frankly, it started off well. Combat was slow and clunky, but the few abilities and the weapon variety seemed interesting. Unfortunately, problems just kept cropping up.Want to know where you are? Nope. Want to know how to get ANYWHERE? Nope. Want good level design that naturally leads you to objectives? Occasionally, but mostly you're just left there with literally no idea where to go and no map at all. Want an easy way to backtrack and check places? Nope, we'll only give you a 'teleport back to last bonfire-esque thing you used' and 'teleport back to hub, an area that seems to be designed to aggravate anyone that likes efficient and logical layouts. Want to upgrade your weapons? Yeah... If you randomly stumble on the furry blacksmith hidden in a corner, who easily blends in with the random background clutter in the mess of a hub. Want to not waste your time wandering down a massive pathway that makes you do a slow wading animation only to end in a gate without any prompt or hint as to how it should be opened? HAHA Nope, good one, right? Sure got me there, game! Nice one! Now I'd better teleport back to the hub and try again from the start, right? Cool!You could say 'git gud' to the above, and I did push through several zones despite the above. The issue I ran into is that I always felt like I was going the wrong way or doing the wrong thing, rather than naturally exploring. Rather than an interlocked design making the best of linear mixed with some exploration pathways, it just felt like they'd somehow done both of them, badly.I loved Elden Ring, and I enjoyed most of the Dark Souls-type games. This one is trying to borrow the general design, add in an anime-tier storyline about a girl searching for her 'papa', but it lacks most of the creative flair and intelligent design to not leave players frustrated. Unfortunate, as it started off well enough as a 'budget-ish' title. My suggestions to ease the above: Add in an optional waypoint / directional hint system (easier than redesigning the levels I imagine), add in a teleport to specific shines (or whatever they were called) with options for each one in an area, and at least TRY to hint that the random NPC in a corner behind the ten other NPCs is useful to you. Souls games are difficult and somewhat opaque, but they usually make sense once you break the surface, and usually offer you the tools to not waste hours of your time backtracking from the literal hub whenever you want to make any progress. This... Not so much.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite enjoyable for a dark souls lite. I do believe if the combat was a bit faster it would definitely help with the weapon combo system. Story is pretty good but I think it would've helped the writers build the story more if progression was straight forward instead of choosing where to go out of 3 or 4 areas. A pretty interesting world lore if you spend the time searching for documents and doing side quest. By the way, some side quest and story lore are dark which I was surprised since the game looks friendlier. Some of the skills/passive are a bit useless and more customization would help with making builds. Overall, I liked it enough to want to see another game from this world they built.7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the stars is an action-adventure soulslike with great resemblances to God of War, Hellblade & ofc Dark Souls. For an indie game it surely exceeds expectations with its beautiful graphics & animations, bonna fine cinematics, gorgeous combat & pacing,its mesmerizing neo-classical OST & generally great attention to small details.With all that being said, it still has a few issues, bugs & peculiar direction choices but nothing game breaking.It can feel both quite challenging & an easy going breeze & I shall explain further below why.Story follows Hilda, a ginger female warrior who's after finding her dad who went missing on one of his expeditions. Things get twisted when she reaches the city of Aspes, in which she learns about strange political schemes and that her dad has a part in all that.While generic it has a fine pace but it's definitely not its strongest points. The world is semi-open with few linear areas, but everything being quite explorable & interesting with a dozen of secrets areas. You collect a plethora of notes & lots of echoes, which are magical holograms of the past, to learn parts of it. There is voice acting which is mediocre imo & occasionally the dialogues are overwhelmingly long with not so much concept.Combat wise, it plays like a mixed soulslike hack'n'slasher. You start almost immediately with 6 different weapons, each having its own combo & one special ability & further down you choose between the 4 elements to magically boost your weapons. This is where the cheese strats start, and with few trial & error, you can find ways to progress the game while challenging yourself or easily destroy anything that stands your way. For example, while you have a dodge button, it's much better using the dagger weaponswhich have an invisible dash that covers triple the dodge distance and have better I-frames. One weird thing though that should be mentioned, is that running, dodging & using special abilities use your stamina bar, but attacking doesn't (!?) Which means you can spam endlessly while using the stamina required abilities quite often since it also regenerates while attacking. Trash mobs are easy to deal with & half of them being battle sponges. Bosses on the other hand are quite excellent, with great attack patterns & phases.There is also a noteworthy talent tree, which you can try various builds as you can re-spec with the use of a consumable item at any time.Now, regarding the cons, bugs & peculiar direction choices that I mentioned above. While a soulsike with the classic "bonfire" system, unlike in other similar games,on Asterigos you immediately lose a percentage of your collected "souls" each time you die. But... it has an manual save/load system,which you can cheese to not lose used items or souls on death, further talent point testing etc. Locking on enemies while outnumbered doesnt always feel good, since you get dead angles much more than you'd expect, getting in corner when fightingn gets you stucked & bodyblocked. Game has a jump button but it's the same key as the dodge one, with the difference beingthat you can jump while sprinting and dodge while not, making it hard to use if needed while in combat. Some platforms and areas that seem reachable ain't,you can jump and grab ledges but not ladders and you can get blocked by tiny object that you'd normally step over. Pressing escape to change options doesn't pause the gamebut it does when hitting tab to change your weapons, level up or read your Journal.Also collecting stuff while enemies are nearby, locks you into dialogue or whatever the collectible has to offer but the enemies are free to hit & kill youduring that time. In few occasions I also couldn't collect stuff for unknown reasons until I made a circle around doing nothing & returning to it.All in all, Asterigos might not be perfect but it's surely above decent, exploration is neat & rewarding, combat is fantastic, the overallfeel is cozy & it keeps you in its own way in wanting to play & progress further. For me it's a solid 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually a fan of the souls-like genre, but I found this game very enjoyable. I liked the Greek fantasy meets Norse fantasy aesthetic a lot, and the characters were very well managed. Many of the characters were very honor and duty driven, whether they were soldiers or aristocrats, while others were much more selfish and unscrupulous. These characteristics were present among both the 'good guys' as well as the 'bad guys'. The characters were the strong point for me, which enhanced the plot as well. The villain had a noble goal (equality) that was taken to a dangerous logical extreme (equity), which made him more interesting than a basic ♥♥♥♥♥ power monger.The voice acting was good, but there was a lot of dialogue. Too much at times, but my main issue was when new dialogue options would open up with characters you'd have to root through the dialogue trees to find them. Some games would put little icons next to dialogue options to entail that there were new options for the player to pursue, I wish Asterigos did something like that. Would've helped a lot, I was often paranoid I'd miss something so I'd just scour dialogue options just to be sure. Sometimes I ended up getting very valuable input as a result of this.Weapon balance could use some work. Daggers are probably the best, and paired with the staff you have great ranged options. Idk how you'd fix it though, as speed helps deal with many enemy attacks, but the spear had a counter attack that was a lot of fun. It's just not as reliable as dashing around with daggers, I personally would've liked a chime sound effect of some kind to accompany the spear to rely on audio cues to prompt counter opportunities rather than just try to memorize every mob's attack pattern and grunts. In the end, it was just too easy to rely on daggers to avoid damage altogether.I'd give the game a 7/10 but if I liked souls-like games more, I'd push it up. But, I enjoyed it more than I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars is an indie action RPG that draws clear inspiration from the Dark Souls series but differentiates itself with a vibrant, cartoony art style and a unique setting inspired by ancient Rome and Greece. From the get-go, the game offers a diverse and flexible combat system. Main character has an immediate access to an array of weapons—swords, spears, magic staves—each fostering unique fighting styles and allowing for experimental tactical approaches. Unlike in FromSoftware games, the combat here is far less punishing.However, its level design can be confusing, It is easy to get lost or overlook critical paths. The game's universe is detailed and expansive, evidenced by numerous cutscenes, a wealth of documents to read, and many dialogues with various NPCs, which, unfortunately, tend to drag on.Despite its charm and the obvious dedication poured into its creation, Asterigos suffers from annoying technical issues. Even after several patches, the game experiences glitches, occasional frame rate drops, animation bugs, and problematic camera angles, particularly in dense or chaotic scenes.Recommended, but when it's at least 50% off.

_childDocuments_.review: Still got a ways to go but I wanted to rate this while it was still on sale, I think it went a bit under the radar on release and seems to have gotten a few updates to address initial complaints.Asterigos is an action adventure game with an emphasis on combat and exploration. I think it's level design takes a few things from dark souls but if I'm being honest it doesn't actually mechanically resemble it too much. My expectation for that might come from reviews rather than the game itself, or maybe the UI. Even on hard the difficulty is much easier, it doesn't punish you past a small amount of money loss on death and you don't get a magic infinitely replenishing potion item (the one you have is something you find in the world and functions more like a slow heal over time.) On hard combat is intense enough where you need to pay attention, but moment to moment the character kind of plays like a... pretty good ps2 game. Outside of skills most weapons have 3-4 attacks and a single, permanent gimmick (bracelets make mines, spear has a parry) While a lot of the enemies are easily exploitable with -certain- attacks, I'm trying to stick with obvious intended attack use, and I think it all plays quite well. Also the hard mode, which is characteristically unbalanced in a good amount of games like this, feels pretty good. Enemies feel like they have the right amount of health so far, and my character seems to scale reliably to them.Visually the game looks great, it runs pretty good (loading map chug is apparent, might be an engine thing, idk I don't have that particular issue with most open world games) In lieu of grimdark they adopted a very cartoonish artstyle, and I think the characters are very cute. In addition to adding more variable scale to humans, I think it also makes some attack animations a little easier to read. I think the cartoony aesthetic at some points undermine story segments, where something serious will be happening or there's extremely morose or depressing dialogue, and Hilda does very exaggerated emoji expressions in response. On the note of dialogue, I don't think the "voice" is quite right. Characters like priests talk like teenagers, dialogue sometimes feels completely unnecessary and a good amount of the incidental questioning dialogue doesn't actually build up the bigger picture. It could be the prior expectation of a soulslike that's poisoning my perception of this, but I would have just liked more succinct world building dialogue.The story itself is fine. I like that it's not just a retelling of Greek myth but a genuine unique story world grounded in that mythology. There are surprisingly heavy implications for how your actions influence the world, sometimes a little forced, sometimes a little preachy, but definitely a lot more than I would have expected from a game like this. I think this game has a better establishment of moral grey area with minor couple-sentence npcs than most fantasy games do for their main stories. Technically, the game hasn't crashed for me or anything. There are a few weird collision things where I can sometimes climb up to something I'm not supposed to, but I think that's kind of fun. I like the fortnite season-esque sequential unlock of goodies from finding chests, I think that's a cute mechanic to add to a single player game, and a good motivator to search for something even if I'm certain it's another astral shard I don't need. I assume that was something added in post, since I think there were only a couple outfits on launch.Anyways, definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, it is at its core , a 3rd person action RPG. Some compare it to Fenyx Immortal Rising, which i have also played. In terms of look and theme, yes,  but Fenyx got a ton more stuff (typical of ubisoft open worlds).Eg:  There's no flying , no mounts, no real jumping and no puzzles.  Asterigos is a bit more focused, i did not find the world super open or super big, the story leads you down a fairly concentrated path with regions only opening up as you progress. Once you finish a region, you would find little reason to return other than some side-exploration. The game took way too long to open up teleporting/fast-travel, which also made the "back tracking" tedious, so i didn't do much of it until the end of the game , and by then i felt it was not particularly necessary.There's also a souls-like tag on this game, i got no idea why, this is not a souls-like. I did not find it punishingly difficult (and i do not like souls-likes for that reason ). The only souls-like thing here is how you die / resurrect at the last visited fountain (aka "save point") and enemies respawning upon death.  However, since there's a casual difficulty , i'd say the game is easy enough that this is not a major problem. These fountains are fairly well spread out and i did not feel like i ever had to backtrack too much . You can of course save anytime, but reloading will also place you at the fountain, but not always with the enemy respawned.The combat is fun, i felt there's a decent amount of styles to play. While you get all the weapons from the start, you can only use 2 weapons at a given time [no quick swapping] . The skill trees go down each weapon and can change their styles a bit. I used alot of re-spec potions [and later you can just pay a guy] to try the different styles. I did however feel the staff being the only ranged weapon made it overpowered and a requirement to be in my rotation , i would have liked more options or limits here, i felt at a disadvantage using 2 melee weapons.In terms movement/exploration the jumping and climbing in this game seems "scripted" and limited to very specific situations. Your character do not have a true jump button for example, the character will do a run-jump across gaps and can jump when there's an object it can jump over, otherwise it won't do anything. I found the story a little long winded, i did not really get into the story, i guess the presentation style did not work for me. The dialogs are often in-game and i felt would drag on too long. The end-of-chapter cinematics are just drawings on a book page and i felt like it was trying to be too poetic and not necessarily clearly telling me "this is where we are now with the story" . My biggest pet peeve is the journal / questing page . I could for the life of me, never figure out what is going on with the side quests . The whole journal page is by default written in greek

_childDocuments_.review: Well done!It's a good game with competent action combat and well-told story.Souls-like? Not really. A better description would be souls-lite. It's more dynamic and action-driven rather than methodical. Most of your actions can be cancelled at any time and dodge has wide iframes with full invulnerability. Attacking doesn't cost stamina and there is no attribute to scale it. Combat is fun and engaging.You also get all weapons from the very start and you can use two of them at the same time. There is no swap mechanics, so you can combine fast attacking daggers with shield blocking. This also adds to the fast paced, action oriented combat. I was really amazed by the animations, everything feels smooth.There are no drops and it was a good decision. You get all weapons from the very start, so you can try what combination you like. And when you start upgrading them you already know what you want to use, so there is no fomo.Armor is replaced by trinkets and they are all craftable. However, you need to find the blueprints first. It's not a very fleshed out system, but it's ok. There are also few consumables, besides HP/MP potions, but they're used for exploration purpose (or pure utility), not really as a fightning tool.The progression in every zone is linear, but the whole map is designed like Dark Souls 1 (the first half). You also don't get teleportation in the first half of the game. Generally it's very well done, but you need to pay attention and to remember where you are and where you should be going. There is no map to help you.Due to the level design, there is a lot of secrets, interconnections and hidden doors, so the exploration is a reward on its own. However, the only physical reward you get is a chest with a progression system, so every 5 or so chests you get some small reward like boots to your defenses etc.The story is surprisingly mature, despite all the cartoonish visuals and child looking main character and it's well told, for most parts. Moreover, all quests are handled in-game. There is no quest log, no arrow above your head pointing out the direction, no hand holding. Hints are given through dialogue or item description. This is how it should be done. However, it's not without a big flaw.And the big flaw is that there is too much dialogue. It's ok for character development or for the purpose of story telling, but there is also a lot of lore exposition handled through the dialog system. I believe this could have been handled better.The game is great, but it's not AAA production. Dialog outside the main story is not voiced, the cartoonish style is sometimes "too much" and it has the "off putting" feeling in it. Generally, I feel like the visuals don't match the game design.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I kinda want to like this game. I am a sucker for lore, and the lore here is interesting enough. But the gameplay feels jus so mediocre. Most normal enemies aren't really an issue, the bosses are the hardest part, but they aren't really that hard to begin with. The atacks are extremely well telegraphed. Just that you need to know what is telegraphed how. And to learn hat you often are forced to take damage. Especially considering that they kinda like to make bosses a bit unfair to learn.And because this tries to be a souls-like, especially on hard, you probably die seeing the attacks. And then you have to run back again. And running you will do, because the checkpoints are really ridiculous. Instead of having one right before a boss, like most modern games do, the checkpoint is often very far away. I don't like bosses to just fall over and die. But at least don't make it a pain to get back to the fight. When I have to run back a long way, and then take an elevator ride again to reach the boss, it's more a lesson on tedium. You take longer to get back to the fight, than you do actually fighting. And god forbid you stumbled upon the boss without first opening the shortcut.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, especially for the price. I would define this as a souls-lite game, where there is obvious odes to souls games (some punishment for death, large areas with shortcuts/secrets, similar upgrade systems) but more streamlined with less to really customize. While there is skill customizations for each weapon type, this largely just replaces the fact there is six weapons and not dozens. The combat is very smooth and the dual-weapon equips really makes combat much more engaging and lets you cater the play-styles. The downside is the enemy AI is..... unbelievably basic?Lots of story, nice voice acting, way to much (but you can ignore it) exposition that is dumped. But the characters / voicing really carries it. The only two qualms I would add:1. is the world design, while nice aesthetically, is sort of poorly done in terms of exploration / pathing. Many shortcuts are borderline useless due to how frequent they are. They tend to cut very short amounts of time off running around, and they feel less like a reward for progressing than a normal souls-like game would.2. is the difficulty. currently on the hardest difficulty, the game has been incredibly easy with the sheer amount of healing mixed with a rather subpar AI. They can be slow, have super long attack tells and, with daggers or dodge rolling, super easy to avoid with i-frames.If you're looking for a hardcore experience and difficult game, this isn't it. But if you're fine relaxing to a souls-LITE game that has some excellent quality in almost every aspect, and is a super fun casual game to play, it's definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's not good at Souls-like games, I can say that having difficulty options makes this game pretty much the perfect game for newcomers in terms of difficulty. Normal feels just as difficult as it should be for someone who doesn't care about dodging every attack at just the right time or parrying in a 0.1 seconds time. The game also does away with the "3 health potion charges" mechanic, opting for a whooping TWENTY potions (again, or normal difficulty). Meaning, you can take a whole bunch more damage and be just fine. With that out of the way, the world itself is nice, not the most varied one, but with a game that takes place mostly in a city, you can't really expect anything too crazy. The characters are pretty lame, with boring backstories and stories that might start interesting but ended up causing me to roll my eyes so far back that I could almost see the insides of my brain rotting....and the dialogue is really cringy at times...The combat isn't that great, it works really well against some smaller, humanoid enemies, but it becomes frustrating against other kinds that aren't so easy to read. Fortunately, you also have some magic at your side and the ability to fight from distance. There are only 4 item slots to mess with (not counting the weapons), and some of them are interesting, but they're given to you way too late into the game to make much of a difference.Some of the talents are nice, but some are just bad or boring,or just don't fit many playstyles. Like, if you go for a more damage focused character, you won't have as much "mana" and "mana generation", so having access to 10-20 spells doesn't help, since you're so limited in what you can do, and there are some that are clearly better than others in all but some very specific situations. Overall, a decent game to buy on a sale, and good for someone who wants to try a souls-like game that's on the "manageable" side, but a bad story and many lame characters make it impossible to recommend buying at a full price.

_childDocuments_.review: The decision of whether or not to recommend this game was a tough one. Obviously you already know where this review ends up because it's like at the top even before my text is. But while writing this I do not know. So that's kind of exciting right? Well I can say that is certainly more exciting than this game. :/This game has a lot going for it, and a lot going against it. And I want to address two things about this game before we start that you probably have seen in other reviews.1. This game is not a souls-like. I do not know why people are saying this. It does not look like Dark Souls, it does not feel like Dark Souls, it does not play like Dark Souls. It's more like those 3rd person action RPGs from the mid to late 00's like Darksiders or that Dante's Inferno game. If you are going into this wanting to play a Souls game you are going to be sorely disappointed. The game play is much more rigid and does not feel as crisp and smooth like Dark Souls does, but still just as clunky. This leads the combat to be a lot more sluggish and less responsive. Thankfully this game is also ridiculously easy on the standard difficulty 1st play through. Can't comment about any other difficulties or NG+.2. The lack of a map in an exploration focused game is not an issue in and of itself. The reviews that are bemoaning the lack of a map while trying to acquire the various collectibles comes more from the art design of the game. This game looks really nice, a lot of the asses are really crisp, well designed, aesthetically pleasing to look at, and do not look like some Unity Asset dropped from the void into place. The issue though is that a lot of assets are recycled. A lot. Really often. Like near constantly. This gives every area a sameness quality that makes it difficult to navigate because every room looks like the last and the one that came before it. I completed most of the zones (with the exception of the final zone which I will touch on later) on my own, but did have to use a guide to locate a few items because I would just endlessly run in circles never knowing if I had stumbled onto a new area or not because this area looked so similar to the last. This seems to be where a lot of the complaints on this stem from.Alright that out of the way, overall this game is totally fine, but it is far from great.The story is bland and uninteresting, and the characters follow the same suit. I never cared about anyone or what they were doing or why they were doing anything and quite frankly the writing didn't seem to either. Furthermore a MASSIVE amount of the exposition is delivered through ponderous meandering statements that are entirely nonvoice-acted. So if you've been reading this review and thinking, wow, this guy sure talks around his point a lot more than he talks about his point, I am purposefully doing this as a stylistic choice to emulate to you, the reader, how exactly much of the world, character, and narrative information is delivered by the game to the player.The combat is also fairly dull, which is the main reason it did not feel like a Souls-like to me. You acquire through leveling special moves that use what is essentially a mana bar that completely trivialize the already easy encounters in the game. In addition to giving an absurd amount of I frames (the shield final special in specific hooboy) they also deal #tonsofdamage leading most bosses to be defeated in a single cycle of mana.The exploration mostly sucks due to the aforementioned issues above and the games TRULY DREADFUL PLATFORMING controls. The greatest negative this game has is its insistence on you doing platforming that is very precise but it just feels so clunky and unresponsive and is just not satisfying or fun at all.So overall, yeah this game kinda blows, but it was at least engaging enough for me to beat it and at least interesting enough to spend the better part of 20 minutes writing this review so I would recommend it if ONLY because this is Acme Gamestudio's first game so as far as a 30 second google search relayed. But this is like a 51% recommend 49% do not recommend. It's really just on that razor's edge for me.Oh, and don't buy the dlc. It's way overpriced for the costume and boss fights. Again, they look good, but just as with the main game, aside from the art design. It's all just meh.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, you guys made a wonderful game here. It's beautiful and fun and I'm excited to see all it has to offer. You have made some bizarre and annoying interface decisions that you really need to fix.>Why is there a half-second delay with the jump? Annoying. Make the response instant as expected in literally every game ever made.  >ELIMINATE THE PRESS AND HOLD SELECTION. Bad news: Nobody in the human race wants that or likes that. It's annoying. Get rid of it. >Forcing the user to press yet another button to transform the journal text from gibberish to readable is ridiculous. I get it, immersion. But in this case: NO. Make it a readable human language from the start. Very stupid.>The save screen should close immediately after a save. You are not a Japanese company. Be more modern. >And finally, a personal pet peeve: "Ask about herself." THIS IS INCORRECT ENGLISH. It's "Ask about her." You get it? Adding "-self" to a word does not make it a more formal version. There is a specific grammatical instance for "herself" "himself" and THIS IS NOT IT. These should all be easy fixes that will elevate this otherwise wonderful classic-feeling game out of the amateur space and into the pro space. USABILITY.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my favorite soulslike - even better than Elden Ring (don't hate me for opions). The game is sort of a cross between Dark Souls and Kingdoms of Amalur (with a little Immortals: Fenyx Rising and Dragons Dogma flavor). As you would expect, there's shield-blocking, dodging, and parrying, but for some reason there's no backstabbing. I'm not sure if this was for game balance or if the devs just didn't have time to implement it. Also, parry doesn't stagger enemies so if they're in a middle of a combo, you still get hit even if you're successful and there isn't a clear sound like Dark Souls so you mainly just can tell by looking at your hp barThe combat feels less impactful than Dark Souls and maybe also Fenyx Rising - like the weapons don't feel like they have weight. It's feels more similar to Kingdoms of Amalur, but you have lock-on so that at least is better than KoA.The basic attributes don't seem to affect which weapons you can use so (love it or hate it), it's different than Dark Souls in that regard. The are special attacks to unlock so maybe stats affect which ones you can unlock idk.Also, it has an amazing OST and looks very good visually - I'm using a reshade setting that enhances it as well. The level design is hit and miss. They have the shortcuts that we all know and love from souls games, but they don't always seem necessary. They're also too big and it's easy to get lost. The enemy diversity is pretty good. They rarely ever have the same enemies from other areas.The first boss was relatively challenging on the hardest difficulty (harder than Asylum Demon, but around the first DS3 boss in difficulty). However, the 2nd boss was a lot harder. And the 3rd boss even harder. Definitely as hard as several bosses in Dark Souls. Several people in a forum thread are saying the hardest difficulty is significantly easier than Dark Souls and soulslikes, but I'm finding it almost as hard. Maybe a little easier, but not as much as some people claim.Edit: The bosses in the first half are relatively challenging and somewhat comparable to Dark Souls, but the areas are less punishing than Dark Souls. However, the normal enemies get a lot harder in the 2nd half of the game. SCREW ALL YOU SOULS HEADS FOR ACTING LIKE EVERYTHING IS EASY. YOU'RE THE REASON WHY ELDEN RING IS TRASH.I'm currently burnt out on Soulslike games and bought this because it sounded less punishing. I haven't played enough to give a final verdict (I'll change my review to negative if I change my mind later).Edit 2: I'm changing my review to negative (maybe it would be neutral if Steam had the option). This game is harder than the first 2 Dark Souls and maybe as hard as Dark Souls 3. I've beaten the game on the hardest difficulty, but some of the bosses are absolutely miserable to fight. They'll one-shot you if you don't put a bunch of points into health and they're HP sponges on top of that. It's like fighting Dark Soul bosses on New Game Plus. The last boss is the absolute worst. Full of projectile and AoE spam so you don't have a chance to get that many hits in or heal. The majority of the time you're just running around. He's what made me change my review to negative. And yes, I have beaten him on the hardest difficulty.There are a lot of little annoyances on top of that like how save games and potions work. Other things that I can't remember off the top of my head. I still stand by what I said about this being my favorite soulslike, but the problems just make me more angry every time I try to play.Below is my original positive review. Like I said at the end, I would revise my opinion once I had a better idea about the difficulty. Despite all my complaints, they at least have easier difficulty options. I just feel like I'm cheating if I lower the difficulty since I am able to beat it on Hard. I just don't feel like bashing my head against the wall for 30-60 minutes to beat a boss.Edit 3:I'm changing my review back to positive. I was salty over some of the more difficult bosses (and I still think some are poorly designed and/or too hard). Also, I found out you can change difficulty settings in the middle of the playthrough. I generally don't like doing that in games, but I can't really complain (as much) about the difficulty if I can just make it easier with in-game settings.

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite Souls-like, although some would say that's not a proper comparison. I say it's similar enough that people who are into Souls-likes would like this game and thus calling this game that would only benefit more people. The changes this game makes from the typical Souls formula is only for the better in my opinion.+Melee combat with a bit of ranged and various skills.+You respawn at conduits "bonfires" where instead of losing all currency you only permanently lose like 10%.+Currency doesn't directly improve your stats but is instead used, in conjunction with rare items, to increase the stats of your weapons, elements, and to buy defensive trinkets.+The game is difficult but not unfairly so. Pay attention and use your skills and you will be good.+Selectable difficulties! And you can change them at any time. So if this style of game sounds fun you can enjoy it still on easy, unlike other Souls-likes. There's also a hard mode if you want it more difficult.+It does make a massive and positive change with the story presentation, where there is a lot of it and optional lore, making a stark contrast to Souls-likes whose stories are barebones and difficult and annoying to follow. On the one hand, you're back into the action in Souls-likes faster, but on the other if you care about such things you can learn a lot more about the world and characters here if you wish.+The side quests aren't mere fetch quests and are usually much more involved and interesting.+Side quests sometimes give you choices and these choices do have an impact on the conclusion of those characters later. The main quest will also give you choices too.+6 weapons, each completely viable to beat the game with. You can only have 2 equipped at a time, but if you desire you can swap them out with any of the other weapons at any time. Each weapon offers a completely different way to fight.+Skills add more depth to the game, where each weapon has its own skill tree and where perks will drastically change how you use that weapon, but can be disabled if you don't like the change it makes.+A lot of great and memorable characters.+The blacksmith is the cutest most kindest furry girl.+Some people say the combat doesn't feel right, I don't know what they're talking about. It feels great to me, very fluid and always does what I want it to do.+If you take your time and read every lore and exhaust all conversation options you can expect a ~40 hour game on your first playthrough. But even if you ignore that and just want to fight, it will still take you quite a bit of time. And then there's new game plus and beating the game with different weapons!+-A lot of side quests but some of them can be difficult to find. They usually aren't too hard to complete, but I had to look up a few.+-No real map. The game is huge and often interconnected and can get confusing, although that's a welcome staple of Souls-likes (learning and memorizing the layout is fun). However later in the game you do unlock the ability to fast travel between every conduit (bonfire) you've used.-Can't do the sublimation ritual and become a furry.Seriously I can't think of anything truly negative about this game. Worth the price even not on sale if you're into this type of game.
