_childDocuments_.review: I'd rather leave this one a neutral review, but since cons slightly outweigh the pros for me, negative then it shall be.So, everyone here is praising the game's story, combat, progression, etc, etc. And at the beginning, I thought the same - wow, this one's fresh, cool. What I didn't know when I started playing it was how damn boring it would become by mid-game and what a tedious chore it would end up by the grand finale. In a nutshell. + Fun and fluid combat system (that really has nothing to do with souls-like games)+ Nice story - pretty solid, albeit extremely simple+ Good progression until about mid-game+ Pleasant visuals+ Sometimes fun side quests+ Pretty interesting boss battles and boss lore (especially the endgame ones)+ Curious language/alphabet system - reading the journal, you can switch between the original text and its English translation, which, if you're inquisitive enough, can help you read all those writings on the walls in Aphes. This isn't in any way required gameplay-wise, but it sure adds to the atmosphere.+ A secret ending that you can only get if you fulfil a number of conditions (and the game won't tell you what they are, so figure it out on your own)- WAY TOO MUCH LORE. This game explains every single damn thing in its world in so much (unnecessary) detail that at some point you start thinking the writing part was given to some graphomaniac. As a person who read all the notes and item descriptions in Control and loved it, I can say Asterigos doesn't do even a lukewarm good job of its writing. It's teeming with dates, names, and events that you start forgetting as soon as you've stopped reading yet another proliferative note or plaque.- On the same note, a veritable TON of dialogues. You can chat with every meaningful character in the Shelter, and oh how much chatting it is. As soon as I saw the sheer number of dialogue options with Minerva, I realized I would never know what she has to say about many matters. And somehow I feel like I didn't lose much.- With the previous point in mind - side quest dialogue lines are hidden deep within those innumerable dialogue options, and a lot of the time the questions you need to ask to get there make no sense whatsoever. I was lucky to find that out at the beginning of the game, while I was still interested in reading and hearing every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ line of its lore. So I just skipped through entire portions of dialogue later to see if there was something related to the side quest I was trying to complete.- While NPCs are happy to chatter on for hours about trivialities and the history of Aphes, and while you're able to ask them to repeat this useless stuff any number of times, quest NPCs will  repeat what you need to do to complete their errands. So if you accidentally skipped that single line where they said what they wanted from you, or you missed the point because you were hypnotized by their ceaseless blabbering, you won't be able to ask them to repeat that one meaningful part. You're on your own now, cowboy.- Speaking of, side quest rewards are... nonexistent? Wherever I finished a side quest, the only thing I was rewarded with was a characteristic jingle. Or I might've missed something, can't say for sure. In any case, that felt pretty anti-cathartic.- Crazy amounts of backtracking. It gets much easier after a certain event mid-game, but until then you have to run back and forth with just a precious few shortcuts to help you out. Not fun.- Absolutely useless journal (apart from the language deciphering part I mentioned in the pros). Your character jots down stuff that doesn't say anything that you can use to navigate through quests, and sometimes it even leads you astray instead of giving you hints at what you should really do. - Some enemies and bosses are simple reskins of other enemies and bosses. Given that this game has a rather simplistic design to begin with, it feels like cheating on the part of devs.- You're given a choice of weapons to use, and you can switch them up all you want, as well as their respective skills, providing you with a rich variety of distinct fighting styles, but by mid-game it becomes old. Strange as it is, I was bored by all the options given me after about 25 hours in the game, and I only completed it because I thought it a waste not to after all these hours.- I'll put this one under a spoiler because it might contain some. All in all, it's not really a bad game, but it does get old after a dozen hours, and my advice would be to skip as much writing and dialogue as you can to keep your interest sparked all the way until the end titles. Otherwise, you just might drown in the swamp of empty chit-chat and feel frustrated.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game on the whole. Few flaws  Maybe 8/10. It really is trying to copy the Dark Souls game style, though it is far more upbeat.   In fact, almost everything wrong with the game is due to trying too hard to be like Dark Souls. The game on the whole is great, which I don't say often.But let's break it down a little: { PROS }+ : Nice art style.  Stylised but not too stylised.  The slightly cartoony look helps to empathise with the characters. + : Beautiful level design, at least in places. The Greek aesthetic works well.+ : Well-written story.  Lore seems decent.  And for all that it tries to be like Dark Souls, there is a lot more focus on plot.  I like that. + : Relatable characters.  Again, it deviates from Dark Souls here in the sense that the game mostly doesn't feel too lonely.  It is nice to actually chat with characters knowing that you aren't just leading them to their doom.  And they're well-written with believable personalities and motivations.  The characters are probably my favourite part of the game.+ : Weapon movesets are rather cool...  though there is an addendum I'll get to now...  { CONS }- : Lack of Customisation or Replay Value.  You play as Hilda.  No choice in that.  The alternate costumes are all garbage, so there is no point changing outfits.  The trinkets don't meaningfully change any aspects of gameplay, so there is no point changing them up.  There are two endings (one "Normal" and one "Good"), but you can get them both in one playthrough if you know what you're doing.  The only thing that changes is weapon build, but some are vastly more viable than others... so why bother changing?   The game simply has no replay value.  UNFORTUNATELY I went full hog with 100% completing the game to the point where I locked myself out of the Normal Ending... yeah....  Perfect or nothing. So I've got to replay just to get an ordinary ending. - : The game pushes the "Souls-Like" angle a bit too hard.  While it avoided the grimdark tone of FromSoft games, the whole immortality plot, campfire substitutes, respawning enemies, random platforming deaths, NG+ difficulty, and bugger knows what else just screams "Dark Souls ripoff".  I feel like the game was too constrained by rigid adherence to this formula, and could have done better by doing just about any of these things differently.  - : Labyrinthine 3D stage lay-out.  No compass.  No maps.  And in some stages, very poorly lit.  I prefer open-world games, but I don't mind linear games.  What I don't like is trying to navigate a maze where I can't work out which way I'm going except by trial and error.- : Really poor side-quest handling.  The "journal" is purely decorative.  While the only things that are truly missable are mostly inconsequential "e.g. trinkets", not even knowing whether or not you've completed a side-quest can be kinda damning sometimes. - : Collection Achievements.  It is a fact of life that in any game where there are achievements for  or whatever, 95% of my focus and energy is going to be sunk into the pointless scavenger hunt and not on the plot of the game.   At least these ones aren't missable. - : Weird lighting issues.  There is a range of artificial darkness around Hilda which is obvious by the way the distance looks brightly lit until you get close and it plunges into darkness. Much more apparent if you're using the little glowing light source, which doesn't really help with visibility most of the time but is necessary for finding chests.  - : The American dub is jarring.  The voice actors all have really strong Murican accents that sound completely out of place with the game setting. Sometimes it is hard to take the game seriously because I'm laughing at all the awful drawling.   Okay, to be fair, the voice-acting isn't "bad". It is actually pretty good, but it is also very very american. - : Not really a game fault, but since this game was never particularly popular, information on where to find things / how to complete quests / etc is kinda sparse in the community.  It HAS all been found, I believe, but I had to tap a lot of different discussions here, on Reddit and Youtube to get to the bottom of everything.Anyway...  it has been a fun time... which I expect will be considerably less so on the second playthrough I need for that last ending and the 2 achievements remaining...

_childDocuments_.review: My reaction to Asterigos was very high...and then kinda low...and then high again by the end. Allow me to explain.My first experience with the game was a bunch of youtube ads that made it seem like a AAA game and then the demo in Next Fest that sold me on the high production quality. Graphics are good, systems looked promising, world design was fantastic. I didn't have much time to play with the combat, given that you have six weapons to choose from and can use any two of them, but all things considered I figured this was a game to wishlist and wait for the price to come down since it was sure to be priced out of my cheap-ass range.And then someone bought it as a gift. So I started playing. First half hour matched the demo, and then I got to learn more about the actual story and start exploring new areas...and...I got lost. A lot. I'm fantastic at navigating 2-D spaces, but 3-D games can be tough sometimes, and Asterigos was especially tough for me. There's no map in this game, no fast travel (initially), and a decently large enough area to roam and explore and fight your way through that I enjoyed it but I knew I was fumbling my way through. And gradually I leveled up, unlocked abilities, etc. But the main NPC in the game gives you three quests out of the gate and I was stumped trying to complete them at several turns mostly just because I missed which way to turn. Plus a few other issues which were probably my own fault. But more than anything, in this phase of the game, everything felt much slower than it should have. I needed 13 hours to finish these first three quests -- I know because I made a post on the forums at the time -- and I was seriously considering bailing.Then I finished the third of those quests, unlocked an *actual* fast travel system, and the game opened way up. Following those three are four more quests in new sections of the map, and they all felt fresh and interesting and fluid. The game just absolutely took off for me at that point, and I think a big part of it was simply that I actually had some sense of geography. I also had maxed out everything I could train in my first weapon chosen and started working on a second, and being able to use the staff effectively as my second weapon choice really altered my gameplay as well. So basically I want to acknowledge that, at least for me, the game dipped initially despite many really great things going for it, but it also pulled back up and became very good by the end.So let me talk a little more specifically:Asterigos is the story of Hilda, a legionnaire from a town whose main detachment of special forces went into the legendary city of Aphes. Aphes has been essentially quarantined from the rest of the world due to a sort of curse of immortality called Asterigos. Nobody wants to go there and nobody from inside can really leave, until a mission prompts Hilda's Northwind Legion to stage operations there...without her. Three months later, she's sent to reinforce them or at least scout for their progress. She's also the legion commander's daughter, which had something to do with her being left behind, but now she's making some real waves in Aphes.Hilda fights with six different weapons -- sword, spear, 2H hammer, daggers, magic staff, and magic bracelets. You can equip any two of them and use them somewhat interchangeably. Each has a basic attack style, a special ability (like blocking, parrying, a charge attack, an aimed shot mode, a quick dash in) and each has an entire section of Hilda's talent tree dedicated to it, where you can learn several activated abilities and really specialize in that weapon. Combat will inevitably be compared to Dark Souls, which is slightly warranted, but not enough to call this a "souls-like."The art in Asterigos was one of the first draws. It's very vivid, stylized and fluid. At no point does the game ever really disappoint visually. The world and level design is fantastic (when I'm not getting lost in it) and there's great variety and a ton of work put into making Aphes feel alive. Many of the scenes in the game have full VA, with quality acting, but then the game supplements that with infodumps that are purely text. The characters in the game are generally charming and the game did have me guessing at a couple points who precisely would be the final villain. It's probably no surprise that you get to fight all the candidates for the title by the end. Hilda is very much the "hero" trope and the game even leans into this and calls her out on it at a couple points.There are a few negatives I should address. Beyond what I've already mentioned, fighting in enclosed spaces is sometimes difficult to manage in a game where you're sometimes expected to dodge-roll and counterattack because the enemy is now behind you and you can't see what they're doing. Or they're flying about you, out of reach. There is an auto-targeting mechanic, but there are times when it's better not to use it. The game is also *just* Dark Souls enough to sometimes lock you into attack animations when you aren't expecting it.However, I think the biggest thing that frustrated me with this game is falling. Asterigos has **ZERO** failsafes against falling off an edge. Most games have at least a little bit of guardrailing, but in Asterigos, you go from on the platform to off the platform and falling one pixel apart. Given that many of the battles take place around edges or while charging up ramps and stairs to hunt down archers, and it's not hard to see how you might roll defensively and find yourself flying over the edge. Or getting knocked back by an enemy and sent over the precipice. Or simply forgetting which button is your daggers' special move and suddenly lunging ahead off an elevator. That last part happened 4 or 5 times to me. (Oops.) But because of the lack of fast travel during the first half of the game, when I did this while trying to run out of an area that took a very long time to reach the end of, and then I got warped back to the bottom and had to run back out again, I got very irate at the game for wasting my time.So while this is a very quality game and you will come to appreciate it by the end, it does take a little bit of time to click -- time I almost didn't give it. You'll probably notice these things after the two-hour mark. Until then, it feels very immersive. And after the halfway point, it was very immersive. The 10-50% mark should have been, too. The bones were there. Just a few design choices and a lack of developing experience with the controls and navigating the map held it back in that interval. So not 10/10, but still very much deserves a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: The Short: A fun Soulslike for beginners and fans of the genrePros- Colorful art style- Easy to learn mechanics- Open world exploration without bloat- Quality Score- Focus on a small pool of weapons Cons- Much of the dialog lacks voice acting- Feels a bit too much like a budget title- Weak story (so far)   I've hear Astergos described like some kind of Dark Souls lite by way of Disney.  I think an argument could be made to refute that, but I'm not going to.  Mostly I think it's a positive.  Hilda does look the part of a princess with a pinch of Link thrown in and as these games go it's quite easy, but how is that a bad thing?    If you want to get your kids or a non-gamer into Action/Adventure games this is a pretty great starting point.  It's also an easy recommend if you know anyone who found Elden Ring or Niohs difficulty too oppressive.  Final if, like me, you can't get enough good Soulslikes here's another one.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw footage of the demo of this game on Youtube, I was sold. The artstyle immediately caught my attention. It looked colorful, even charming to me. The sound design was great, the animations seemed well done.So, when it got released I bought it straight away and I do not regret doing so. The areas past the demo look just as stunning. When I'm exploring, even when backtracking, I keep finding stuff that I've missed. I didn't expect this game to be so large in scale. Everything is connected aswell. There is a fast travel option to the various resting places, but you unlock it quite  late into the gams. I was worried that option would never be there.The combat is a lot slower than the FromSoftware games, so if you play those games regularly you won't have a lot of trouble here. There is a lot of variety to the combat with the various weapons and skill perks that you can play around with. When you unlock new perks, you can enable/disable them to try out different playstyles.The enemy/boss design is nothing super special, but it's well done and looks great. It adds to the overal artstyle. There isn't a whole lot of enemy variety, and their moveset is also pretty limited. The AI isn't the best, with enemies getting stuck sometimes, or returning to their position when you're running away after agroing them like nothing happend. They are not on high alert, or change their paterns at all. Also, a lot of the time they do not seem to notice when something near them is getting attacked.I feel like the enemys and AI is the weakest point of the game. It's not bad, by any means. It might feel boring after awhile. Story is told, aside from talking to npcs, through pieces of paper or highlighted objects within the world. There is a lot of it so I tend to pick it up and not read it. Important to note that only options highlighted in yellow when talking to npcs has dialogue. Others is just text. I don't really feel attached to the story, unlike Bloodborne, for example.Overall, for its price point, I think it's a very well made game. Lots of weapon and perk variety, great artstyle and a lot of exploration and secrets to find. If the enemy moveset could've had more variety, and the AI was improved it would've been even better. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I was thoroughly impressed with how much I came to enjoy this game.Footnote: I hate Souls games and the overwhelming majority of all Souls-likes. I hate the feeling of playing a game that hates you just for buying it; it's one thing to have a gradual difficulty curb, it's another to punish unfairly. But, despite the obvious characters that make this game a Souls-like, Asterigos feels pretty damn rewarding and doesn't punish for no reason. Having played a normal run-through and am now currently working on a "Challenge" playthrough, I'm pleasantly surprised and impressed with how balanced the game feels overall.If you're curious about Souls-like games but want less of a hassle, Asterigos is a game for you. Might not get the most play-time out of it as you would other games, but it will be an enjoyable experience at a fantastic price.

_childDocuments_.review: Review so far, what makes me interested in this game is because it takes the concept of souls-like games. tps, exploration, hub, checkpoint such as bonfire/grace, enemies can spawn again if rest at the checkpoint, the use of stamina in combat and resources lost when die. because it's similar to souls-likes in general, so I like almost everything in this game. but no one is perfect. there are some things I like, and some things I don't like(+) difficulty option, when you die the resources not completely lost, great for people who want to try souls-like games (+) colorful visuals, beautiful (subjective)(+) combat system, I really like this one, 6 weapons and unique skill variations, the effect of the skill is very beautiful, parry is not so difficult, unlike Kena which is not clear timing parry(+) variety of enemies and boss(+) poor a, poor b, poor c. best NPC name ever!(-) cringe dialog, especially when in the mine when talking to one of the characters (don't remember what his name) (-) you can't feel character being hit by an attack, there is no effect, especially for long-range attacks, when you look at the health bar, you are already dying, unlike elden ring, sekiro, or dark souls which have details if we are hit by an opponent's attack(-) why is there no restock automated system? it's annoying to have to go back to the hub just to restock items, especially potions(-) exploration, it seems that there is no souls-like game whose exploration is as fun and satisfying, like sekiro and elden ring(-) no customization(-) elemental damage that doesn't really work significantly in combat and enemy, no effect on enemy, and no effect visually on enemy when player attackalthough there are some negative points, I still like this game. _childDocuments_.review: If you're fence sitting right now on buying it I would suggest go for it. It's a really good game, is it perfect no, but for an indie-studio with veterans it's solid. They put out a game that doesn't need patches out the @$$ right outta the gate, gotta get credit for that at least. You'll see some people griping about lack of this or that, they must not work in any industry where a project goes out as an MVP (ie missing some features that need to be released further down the timeline), and the dev team has already stated they're looking to add some of those features ASAP.Combat, story etc. I won't comment on in detail as that's really all down to personal taste. What I will say is that it's not ground breaking but it's not bad either. Really the only gripes I have with the game are things like the UI (areas of it could just be done better), lack of a proper journal, more costumes, and fast travel being unlocked later than I would have liked.Overall this is a very solid outting for a new studio and their debut release. _childDocuments_.review: The combat is fun and satisfying, with just one or two nitpicks, like whether I stagger an enemy with my spear or not seeming to be entirely random, and which attacks I can parry and which leave me staggered also being unclear.The exploration is a bit... janky. It's got the proper "Oh god where am I going? Oh thank ♥♥♥♥ a dead end, now I know there's nothing here" kinda feel, but since it gives you all six weapon types right at the start all exploration can reward you with is upgrade materials, and that's just not terribly exciting. Useful! But not exciting.The upgrade system is also perfectly fine, I have one petty nitpick in that you can only upgrade at the home base, and depending on where you are, it can be one HELL of a walk back. This was especially annoying on the second real boss, who is miles harder than any other boss I've fought so far. Walking ALL the way back to the sanctuary just to get one more upgrade for my two main weapons was a major annoyance. _childDocuments_.review: A great little indie soulslike that has great style, an interesting story and a lot of love.This game is a great indie game that hits all the soulslike notes when it comes to gameplay with some unique twists of its own. For starters all the weapons you will ever need you get from the beginning of the game and you can pick any two to use at a given time with the rest easily swapped to in the pause menu. The upside to this is theres no need to run around the map collecting potentially useless weapons on the downside some of the weapons feel a lot less useful when compared to others. The other addition this game has done differently to other similar games is that this game features usable abilities that range from damaging to defensive you can have four of these active at a time and each one is not limited to using a specific weapon, although each one is linked to a specific weapon. These abilities are unlocked via skill trees, there is one skill tree per weapon. While an interesting idea some of these abilities allow you to cheese the game very easily removing a lot of the point to changing up play styles (i stuck with the same two weapons throughout the game).The games story starts off pretty similar to the souls games with the plague of undying that cant be cured type deal but the use of npcs to flesh out the relationships they have to one another, how they feel and how the class structure of the city works it does start to feel different from those games in areas. You play as a soldier called hilda whose father led the army to find the source of a curse that threatens their king, and you are trying to find them and check on their progress in the search.Visually the game is very pleasing the setting is styled after a mostly greek/ roman gods type setting with some norse thrown in with the main character. The theme mostly fits and despite a few uncanny valley feels from the protagonist it seemed to all mesh together very well.Theres some pretty good music for some of the bosses aswell as a lyre player that will play some nice instrumental tracks for you in the main hub but nothing stuck out a lot it was just pleasant and a welcome addition to the game.Overall a great game with some noticeable downsides, mainly the lack of tracking or even coherent notes for side quests and the combat could be cheesed very easily with certain abilities. Despite that I had a lot of fun with it so it deserves a 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that this game does not have a map is a major issue for me.It's ok if I do not have a minimap or quest markers with the exact GPS coordinates of the quest targets, but not having a map at all can make this game a chore at times.I've literally been running in circles for hours on because I didn't know where I had to go.Unfortunately many parts of the map look rather similar and do not have special points that can easily be memorized for orientation.The quest log is also not very good.I have tons of quest items in my inventory where I don't know what to do with them.Otherwise the gameplay is fun, although some of the bosses are really hard.I had to fight Eulalia well over 20 times and still couldn't beat her on normal difficulty, so I had to switch to easy difficulty in the end.What made this experience even more annoying is the fact that certain cutscenes (e. g. the  cutscene where you enter the arena with Eulalia) cannot be skipped...Ok, so after spending a couple of more hours in the game I'm going to swtich my recommendation to "Yes".What I did probably not poperly consider is that this seems to be the first game from this developer and considering that, it's amazing what they managed to create.Besides, I did not have a single crash in more than 40 hours, which is more than I can say of some other games by some bigger and (as of yet) more renown developers.Yes, the missing map hurts and a quicksave function would also be nice, but it's still a fun game to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a game made for those who want to explore and revisit areas, looking for documents and reading some lore. I enjoy those things so maybe that's why I really liked this game.After paying attention to the documents in the game and the dialogues, you can see the work that was put into making the city of Aphes was immense. It has a very intricate and solid lore. It took many aspects of the roman and greek civilizations to make a very unique magical setting. Definitely a nice work of art for me, even if the soul-like combat style isn't my preference.I got this game on sale (without DLCs) and enjoyed it a lot. Definitely recommended.WARNING: Devs state that this game pays importance to your decisions. That is true, but probably not how you would expect it to be. Decisions in this game are actually either of the following:1) Vaguely descriptive speech bubble choices during key dialogues.2) Whether or not you did a side quest. That's it. If you do a side quest it sometimes counts as a "decision". Also, to officially finish some quests, you might need to talk to an NPC even after you did everything that was relevant. Keep in mind that to get some quests/events, you might need to explore dialogue options on friendly NPCs.Another weak point on decisions is that it's not clear what you are exactly choosing most of the time. Whether doing a quest or choosing a dialogue option is going to have a positive or negative impact in the game is mostly unclear.Overall (my ranking is: 1 Awful - 2 Really bad - 3 Bad - 4 Kinda bad - 5 Mid - 6 Okay - 7 Good - 8 Pretty Good - 9 Great - 10 Amazing):Combat - Good: I'm not a fan of soul-like combat gameplay, but I still enjoyed it.Character progression - Mid: There are only 3 stats you can level up, which makes it very simple, not necessariliy a bad thing. The skill tree is nice, but equipable items are very plain and more flavor could have been easily added here.Exploration - Pretty good: Zones feel very big as you discover them, yet small once you revisit them. I think that's a really good point it its favor.Main story - Pretty good: The strongest points might be how emotions and motivations of the characters are very well portrayed in their dialogues and you can see how they struggle with their past and ideals.Side quests stories - Great: The narrative aspect can get really dark, even though the visuals are cute.Characters - Amazing: Characters have good reasons for the way they behave and the decisions they take. ThBackground lore - Amazing: Aphes is very well built, not just visually. The historical and social aspects of this city are greatly detailed.Visuals - Pretty good: Its notably weakest point is that the main character's animations are a bit bland. If it wasn't for that, the game would have great visuals.Sound - Great: The soundtracks are really good for the most part and there are some few ones that i really liked.Decisions - Bad: The decision system is just not well done. If you really care about this, please consider that it will very likely not be a satisfying point of the game.Rankings will obviously be different from person to person, so keep that in mind. I don't think this game is perfect, but also has very few remarkably weak points, and has some clear strong points. I'd recommend it if you like finding out about what's really going on in a story, beyond what is told in the main line's dialogues or if you like immersing yourself in the game's world with a beautifully detailed environment and fitting music.

_childDocuments_.review: Pro: - Combat feels great - the world is beautiful and interesting with a surprisingly complex and compelling story - Traversing the world gave me the Souls feel of "oh! I'm here!" after exploring for a while - The map and eventual fast-travel mechanic work nicely togetherCons (ish): - Some dialogue implies there are multiple approaches to some boss fights, but there isn't,  which can be frustrating, but those fights are also fun, so I didn't fight that to be a big deal.  - The side quests can be a bit of a slog, but if you're coming from Souls then this won't be all that different - Weirdly distributed non-pre-order outfits. Only two in the base game (from what I can tell), and the rest are in NG+. Doesn't effect gameplay, it just seems weird. None of the cons were bad or annoying enough for me to stop playing, and the pros were enough that I wanted to do an NG+ run, especially since some things actually do change a bit in NG+. Very well done game for what seems like an indie developer.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll update this review once I get further along, but after a few hours and taking down two bosses, I have some preliminary thoughts:1. Combat is fairly fun, although I'm not swapping around weapons as much as I thought I would be since you end up having to commit to specializing in one or two weapons. Don't get me wrong, I don't consider that to be a negative, but I was kind of expecting to be swapping weapons around to counter various enemy types based on the gameplay videos I had seen.  In the end, I decided on dagger/staff for fast attacks and ranged, and it's amazingly easy to cheese most fights with the staff since it has a sniper rifle mode. I actually stopped using that mode because it felt too powerful. Most smaller enemies fights pretty much involve rush up -> mash light attack -> enemy is stunned -> enemy dies. Larger enemies may require a bit more rolling during engagement, but so far the combat feels less risky than I was hoping on challenge difficulty.2. This is not a particularly Souls-like game. Yeah, it has a comparable bonfire mechanic and a dodge roll, but everything else plays more like an action RPG. Actually, it reminds me more of Kingdoms of Amalur that I played back in the day, with fairly smooth controls and motions. Some people have complained about control stiffness, but I haven't had any issues with a PS5 controller. Don't expect weapons and fighting to have the same weight as Dark Souls, you're going to be playing this more like Zelda (I haven't played an action RPG in awhile, so my references are a bit dated).3. I've seen a lot of complaints about the storyline and dialogue. Having gone in with zero expectations, I think it's fine. I'm not sure why people were either expecting the usual dark environmental Souls-like storytelling or a Mass Effect-level story, because you're probably not going to find too many indie games like that. It's fine for what it is, and it's been keeping me entertained.4. The sound effects are actually fairly solid, the voice acting has been tolerable, and the music is either pleasant to the ear or blends into the background. As long as the sounds/voice/music doesn't stick out badly, I'm fine with it, and that's what we have here.5. The greatest weakness of the game so far are the enemies, because there are several problems. The enemies don't engage very quickly, so it's easy to rush up and destroy them with daggers before they ever land a hit. They also have difficulty navigating around obstacles sometimes. Sometimes they don't really react much during combat, I'm not sure if they're being stunned by my flurry of attacks, or if something else is happening. Bumping up the enemy reaction speed and allowing them to block/parry/dodge me would help make combat feel a bit more engaging.6. The levels do have some Souls-like inspiration with a central hub and branching levels, but it doesn't have the same level of complexity with secret areas so far. You won't be crawling over every surface trying to find hidden areas, but there is some exploration to do. Items that you pick up won't be terribly varied, but they do serve useful purpose in upgrading weapons or creating trinkets.7. I've only run across two side quests. One had me run back and forth between two NPCs a few times, and the other was a typical fetch quest. Probably one of the weaker points of the game so far, but again, I've only played 3 hours and have only seen two quests. I'm probably not going to be expecting Witcher 3 or Greedfall level sidequests for this game, though, which wasn't really my initial expectation going in anyway.8. The only glitch I've seen so far is that sometimes the enemy model refresh rate is oddly low when sniping them from a distance. It's pretty jarring to see an enemy running at me with really low frame rate movement.In conclusion, I'd recommend this game as long as you have the right expectations going in. The thing that I think would benefit the game the most at this stage is either adding a higher difficulty level or tweaking the enemy AI to be more aggressive at the current highest difficulty level. If you're the type looking for high risk, high reward Souls-like combat, I'd go play something else. If you're fine with an action RPG that has embedded some Souls-like elements, you'll probably be happy here, especially if you're someone who usually plays on easy/normal difficulty modes.

_childDocuments_.review: For $35 game, this is a reasonable to good investment of time/money. Comparisons to AAA titles are unfair. The fact that they're being made at all is a testament to how good this game looks despite its modest polygon count. Combat feels a little clunky at first and there are certain awkward aspects that never go away. For example, you need to be standing completely still to use a potion. You can't queue a drink action during a role like you can in Dark Souls. However, once you lower your AAA expectations a little and earn enough perk points to get a build going, combat starts to feel fun and strategic. I believe there are certain exploits that might make the game too easy, but as a sword/shield and staff build, I didn't notice anything too cheesy.The lore is surprisingly good. There's a fun Greco-Roman motif with a mix of Sanderson-esque fantasy. As a connoisseur of classic literature and Brandon Sanderson, this was very satisfying. The story itself suffers a little from exposition dumps and a tell-don't-show philosophy, but most of it is skippable and the game's atmosphere is potent enough to make up for any missed exposition.I wish there was an easier way to keep track of side quest. Main quests are easy to keep track of, but for all the work that went into making the journal menu aesthetically pleasing, I wish a little more thought was given to it's functionality.Slight spoiler alert, but you eventually get the ability to teleport between waypoints. This should have been a thing from the very beginning because the world is surprisingly large and maze-like for a 10 GB game. While this fits perfectly with the whole Greek motif, it can make navigating a chore.There are occasionally odd difficulty spikes between areas, but nothing that can't be coped with a la older rpgs.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars - A Souls-lite with plenty Rough Edges that has its shining momentsIn Asterigos, the combat shines with a diverse range of skills and engaging fights against various enemies and bosses. The game's Greco-Roman fantasy setting adds a unique flavor to the experience.Pros:    Polished combat system with freedom in fighting styles.    Engaging variety of enemies and bosses.    Beautiful SoundtrackCons:    Excessive Lore: The lore-heavy approach can overwhelm, affecting pacing.    Character Development: The protagonist's growth feels lacking.    Quest Log Issues: The journal lacks practicality, focusing more on miscellaneous thoughts.    Typos and Grammar: Numerous errors in dialogue and text.    Level Design: While good, environments lack vitality.    Technical Issues: Audio bugs disrupt immersion.    Inconsistent Difficulty: Boss fights vary widely in difficulty and not in the fun way and some enemy as well ( not sure how is on other difficulty finished the game on the hardest and felt very unbalanced)Conclusion:Asterigos offers an somehow enjoyable souls-like experience in a unique fantasy world. Despite flaws in writing, character development, and technical aspects, the combat and intriguing setting can make it worth exploring for fans of the genre yet at the end of the day it didn't satisfy me and left me with a mediocre taste, there are better AA Souls like games out there for sure, this is in the end not a great not a terrible game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wholeheartedly recommend this game. The game borrows some names and the aesthetics of Greek mythology, but the story or the characters are far from just copies. The story and worldbuilding are really good. So do not worry that you will know what is going to happen if you played God of War or watched Hercules. I would say the gameplay and the story are the best parts. The quests can be confusing sometimes. There is a journal, but it does not help if you get lost, because it mainly contains the thoughts of the protagonist and not really any hints for the many quests. There is no map.Another aspect that can lead you astray, are the choices you make during the early quests. The first main quest you receive can not be done, like you are asked to. You have to keep a low profile, but you can not and even get told off by the quest giver because you had to do something you could not control. The first sidequest in the game gives you two times two different options how to proceed, but they do not change anything regarding the reward or the outcome of the quest. So naturally you would think the quest or your choices do not really matter, but a little spoiler here, the choices you make in the rest of the game matter a lot. So be careful. Maybe the point of designing the early quests this way, was to make you think about what you do onwards, but it can feel awkward in the late game, when you notice that your choices have an effect, after the game taught you they do not in the early stages. But the game was still so much fun, that I had to get all the achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an overall polished game with good combat and decent character and world design. It does not break any new ground as far as action RPGs go, but the parts involved are all serviceable at the very least. You can tell there was a loving craft and passion behind the project even when the game stumbles.Combat/Progression:You are given all weapons pretty much right at the start and will unlock skills that widen their movesets over time. You are encouraged to experiment a little bit towards the beginning but will most likely eventually end up with two main weapons since you can only equip two at a time. The game further ushers you in this direction through the skill tree, as you will only get enough skill points to solidly invest in two weapons. There is also an ability to change your element type on the fly, but this does not change the movesets much (staff excluded). As a result, element swap mostly amounts to just being a simple test of game knowledge.Stat investment is the other area you can customize your character, but it is extremely simple. You can only invest in damage, health, and ability point regen/damage. I found nearly no use in investing in anything but more damage and health. You can also gain trinkets that bolster your resistances, albeit only slightly. A few of them have other extra benefits, but they are all minor effects.Combat flows similarly to the newer Assassin's Creed games. You have a dodge roll, basic combos, charged attacks, blocks/parries, and magic/ranged options. You also have activated skills that are very powerful and even game breaking at times. The animations are very smooth and the controls feel very responsive leading to combat feeling satisfying and fluid. At its worst, it will seem too easy even on the harder difficulty setting. Enemy design and variety will keep things interesting enough until the end of the game, though the AI can feel janky at times.Level Design:Not too much to say here. It is fairly decent and features simpler levels that have a few branching paths and shortcuts that you can unlock creating loops. Secrets are hidden in the world here and there, but the rewards are never particularly interesting. I did find exploration fun enough on its own though to do so anyways. Story/Character/World Design:One of the weaker aspects of the game. There is some good here but the problem lies in the presentation and the volume. There are simply too many text and dialogue boxes in the game, and I say that as someone who grew up on JRPGs. It would be fine to have that much text if the writing were just of a higher quality and did more to keep you interested. This is sadly not the case but it's not all bad. I do like the characters overall and I think the voice actors are carrying a lot here too. You can tell they are really trying to do their best with the script they got. As a result, the most bearable parts of the story/dialogue are the parts that are voiced. I think the game would have actually functioned just fine if all text minus the voiced lines were cut. The voiced sections also just seem better written as well.Final Thoughts:I can definitely recommend this game to anyone who enjoys action RPGs where combat is the main draw. Expect the combat to carry the game, with serviceable parts all around otherwise. Don't expect a whole lot of innovation in its design and you will likely enjoy your time with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a proper action RPG with some familiar Soulsian tropes, like strategic bosses, emphasis on a stamina system, and the kinda-sorta bonfires that serve as save/respawn points for both yourself and enemies.Other than that, it plays more akin to classic Action RPG hack'n'slashers, like Fable or perhaps even Kingdoms of Amalur. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~I finally finished! At over 70hrs, and I'm sure I missed a few things since I didn't get the vaunted "Glory" ending, this was not a short game by any stretch of the imagination, but it was a bloody marvellous one! I had so much fun with this, the art style is lovely though the technical "quality" definitely feels date with low quality models, textures, and whatnot, but it still held together and looked quite delightful due to the colourful and slightly-less-realistic aesthetic. Music was melancholic and atmospheric, voice acting was above par, and the gameplay loop was genuinely enjoyable.Yeah, I enjoyed this immensely, and it ran *flawlessly* too, no performance issues at maximum settings and 1440p.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never been one for Soulslike games, but this one is a lot of fun. I was initially drawn to the game by Malukah's cover of "Nostalgia," and the music in game did not disappoint.The story is fantastic, and malleable, story mode is wonderful for a casual or a newbie to Soulslike games, and the optional challenges are amazing. Collection logs, optional bosses, secret locations, there is so much to do and find.I very much enjoy the side stories you can choose to participate in, and how the smallest details can change the outcome of any event. Crafting & upgrades are simple, and the wide variety of traits allows for varied builds of all sorts.Some of the writing choices make me very angry, however. The player is considered a child, and no one lets that fact go. From everyone doubting the abilities of the individual who single handedly toppled three criminal organizations that the Legion couldn't handle, as well as assaulted the Legion fortress itself and came out on top, simply because you're a child, to being belittled by important allied individuals, many characters make my blood boil.Worse still is that not only does the main character accept this treatment, she eventually apologizes to the individuals belittling her and says they were right. When events actually proved the player right, somehow she sees it as her being wrong.Do I recommend the DLC? I purchased Paragon & the Northwind outfit on sale.The outfit was wonderful for just a few dollars, a small buff that's useful even into late game, and what I personally think is the best outfit in the game. Very fitting for the character. Most of the negative reviews on the outfit are from people angry that the preorder reward is available as a cheap DLC, and they're right to be angry about that. But that aside, it was worth getting (on sale).The Paragons DLC was also worth it, to me, on sale. The outfit that comes with it wasn't to my tastes, and I definitely don't see it as a plus. The weapon mods are interesting and useful, allowing for fun experimentation. The boss fights are more involved than the main game fights, and really turn up the challenge, even in story mode one mistake can be fatal in some of them. Buying it when I got the game was a good choice, as there is not a ton of content there. Buying it after having played would have felt less satisfying.Summary: A wonderful game, loads of fun, be prepared to be treated like you're simultaneously a heroic great warrior and a five year old throwing a tantrum because others don't think your accomplishments deserve any respect, the DLCs are worth buying, but only when on sale, and best bought when you start playing rather than later on.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is a great game.It excels in story, gameplay, and atmosphere, having a well-put together soundtrack, well-developed bosses, and enemies and skill trees that are constantly providing new mechanics to the game. Legitimately, almost every single skill point you use WILL meaningfully alter combat, providing new combos, charge attacks, and minor mechanics at every opportunity. The weapons are also varied, each with their own distinctive special abilities, and every enemy has different attacks and ways of dealing with them.I truly loved this game. The experience was slightly hampered by a few minor bugs, but I trust the devs will address them in the future. The game, coming from a Chinese studio, is also very well-translated. There are minor grammatical errors here and there, but the vast majority of the game's dialogue (which is well-voiced) and lore findings are well-written and completely understandable.It's very clear that the developers put a lot of passion into their game, ensuring the entirety of it was well-fleshed out. The design and stories of all the areas and characters are also well-developed, and they dont skimp out on giving backstory to even the bosses. In some spots the smaller AA budget is noticeable, such as some awkward animations for idle characters when they're talking and a lot of non-important dialogue being unvoiced, but the animations for all of the enemies and for combat sequences hold up, as well as the existing voice acting.Whatever the devs make next, I very much look forward to playing, and I'm glad we can still get nice, well-made AA games like this with plenty of heart put into them. The game pulled at my heartstrings, tested my skill, and wowed me with gameplay variety.

_childDocuments_.review: Disney meets Dark Souls. No. Seriously, it feels like sometimes.You play as a stronger than hundred men teenager girl who is half the size of any adult and is constantly trying to prove herself.There is a lot of lore laying around the game like documents and images for you to waste time reading and collecting to probably forget a few minutes after. Believe me I've read everything I found in game and frankly there is sometimes too much, but you can just skip to the action anyway, every dialogue option and cutscene is skipable except end credits.The story itself is okay, you try to help some people to lift a curse that's so bad it makes everyone immortal to the point everyone just wishes to die.There are a lot of self righteous and whiny npcs that makes it feels like the world is so unfair and that anything you do trying to help them just makes them angrier and whinier and blame you for their lack of strength to make the world their utopic vision.The game itself is quite fun, I enjoyed the combat and it has some mechanics like dodge, limited potions each checkpoint, dodge, respawning enemies if you die or rest in checkpoints, newgame+, block with shield, parry with spear, weirdly spinning with a hammer and also a staff that can be used as if it was a longbow, you can aím it!What you see is what you get. The weapons you get in the early game are the same you gonna see the entire game, there are no finding cool weapons or shining armors around, but with a 6 weapon type variety in combat and they can combo together, they're also upgradeable and each weapon has its own talent tree with abilities and perks which makes things interesting. Perhaps adding new weapons and outfits would make things better.Difficult itself isn't that much even if you play in challenge mode, the bosses could be something more, they tend to be pretty friendly and allow you to heal up and giving you enough openings to destroy them with ease despite their fancy moveset but the game has its challenging moments.Graphics wise it's a really good looking game and has stuff like scaling fsr and the performance is good. I only encountered a bug that happens sometimes where the talent page font gets black making it hard to read them, but if you restart the game it fixes. Probably they gonna fix it soon in future updates.It's a good and entertaining with the combat and talents, there's a nice story and annoying npcs and dialogues. I can easily recommend though, but I think the upcoming dlc should be part of the base game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this critique in the hopes that Acme Gamestudio (hereinafter referred to as "AGS") will read my feedback and take my suggestions for improvements into account. So far, as of my writing of this review (with the game being at patch 1.04), I would recommend Asterigos. However, I do so with caveats in my recommendation, as the moments of enjoyment I experienced while playing were interrupted by periods of  frustration that I feel didn't have to exist in this game and only were in the game because the developers mistakenly think certain frustrating elements make the game better or more satisfying to overcome. I wouldn't even be publishing this critique right now if the people working at AGS haven't clearly demonstrated their willingness to keep an open mind to constructive criticism, as is evidenced by the numerous quality-of-life improvements they introduced in patch 1.04, such as the ability to rebind controls and the removal of stamina depletion when running around without any enemies alerted to make exploration and backtracking enjoyable. With the "Asterigos: Call of the Paragons" expansion DLC scheduled to come out on February 24 next year, AGS has plenty of time to implement the suggestions I am about to offer. Most of my suggestions call for very simple changes that can probably be easily patched in a future version of the game. I hope they take my proposals to heart, because I really do think that this game needs them, especially since a lot of what I'm suggesting are things that a lot of other Asterigos players in forums have also suggested in the past.In short, the problems I have with this game can be divided into three main categories::: I thank any of the developers at AGS for taking the time to read this critique. My words may seem overly negative, but if I didn't actually enjoy the game and saw very easy and clear room for improvement, I wouldn't be writing any of this. I look forward to seeing future patches improve the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game definitely has potential. And for that, I am going to recommend playing it. There are a few things I've noticed so far. To start, the performance on my system is great I'm getting well over 100fps with my setup:AMD Ryzen 9 5950x w/30805120x1440 resolutionPerformance on the steam deck (high settings) is acceptable, around 40-70fps. The first thing I noticed is the cut-off text in the menu due to my widescreen resolution. The dialog boxes in-game are off-center which I assume is also due to my resolution. Cut screens and the menus do not support the resolution, this is not a game breaker.You cannot change the binding. This blew my mind because, in the year 2022, this is a really basic feature that should've been available from the start. However, the developers are currently working on adding this.Something strange I noticed is the way the character walks. Who walks like that? In the couple of cutscenes I've seen so far, the characters just kinda stand there with no lip-syncing to the voice acting. They move their head back and forth as they talk. It's really boring and doesn't pull you in.Apparently, due to my widescreen, my view was very zoomed in. I fixed this with a tweak from a guide posted on Steam (have not tested it yet). During a boss fight, I got pushed into a corner and couldn't really get out of it because the boss was just clipped through me. This actually happened two times and since there is no camera control, I could not correct myself and I ended up dying both times.The water seems to be pretty ugly, but the rest of the game looks nice. Overall, I think this game has a lot of potentials. The negative reviews related to being unable to rebind your keys are because people simply didn't read the developer's notes. I'll probably play it on and off until a few patches come out for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried so hard to like Asterigos.The first five or so hours were very intriguing. I found myself going out of the way to look for and rifle through every piece of lore. I wanted to know more about this city, what happened to it, why so many character were at odds... Then at about the seven, or eight hour mark, I stopped caring. About the lore, characters, zones, etc. And after fifteen hours, I ran from objective to objective, not stopping to fight unless I absolutely had to, simply to be done with it all.The boring world and its bland characters would have been less of an issue had the gameplay been ever-changing. But it wasn't. It became stale fast. There is very little variety. Every weapon in-game is given to you from the jump and from there, you simply upgrade them to make them stronger while also distributing attribute and talent points in certain trees to cater to your "playstyle" (which is a term I use very loosely as, again, the lack of variety is mind-numbing). However, I will be honest: all of these upgrades did not matter. Once I learned the dagger spin-to-win move, I blasted through every enemy and boss with very little issue. And so that's what the game became: running through every area, using the same skill over and over and over again until the credits rolled.I have been told the End Game is pretty redeeming? But it took me 20 hours to finish the base game and I have zero interest in going back. I can appreciate what they were trying to do here, but almost everything fell flat. That said, I must give props to the composer. The music is gorgeous and was by far the best part of this otherwise very dull experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being in souls-like genre, this game has a difficulty slider. An appreciated feature for those who are new to the genre and want to try it first without experiencing the trauma from difficulty (Thank you, Dark Souls!).Visuals is fantastic. Love the match-up of Pixar-looking graphics and the greek-mythology artstyle. Movements are flashy when they need to be and the game did not abuse particle effects, unlike other Triple-A games. I did not experience any visual issues the entire game.Soundtrack is also really good. It's so good that in some boss fight, I had to turn down the background music because it was hyping me too much.Storytelling is good and the game is rich in lore. They made an effort to really dig into the details of the main NPCs in the game in a way that their own side-quests reveal details about them.World-building is great. Lots of areas to explore and things to uncover. Each biome is unique on its own and at the same time coherent with one another (meaning you can go from one area to another without needing to fast travel) and it almost feels like open-world. Enemies did not feel repetitive at all. And there's very minimal boss-now-normal-mobs-later issue.After-input delays - my biggest gripe in this game. The developers implemented so much delay in between every action that combat can oftentimes feel clunky and slow. You're using potions and you want to dodge an incoming attack? Delay. You want to double-dodge? Delay. You dodged and now you want to aim your ranged weapon? Guess what, delay!TL:DRSupport good small indie devs! It's one of those underrated indie games. Games like these are like gems of our lifetime - very hard to find.

_childDocuments_.review: By the time i write this review, i'm currently into the third main area of the game.How is it possible that no one has ever talked or published this game before!? I actually found out about Asterigos thanks to the Souls like tag on Steam, else i would have skipped this masterpiece.This is really a AAA production masked as indie project with low budget, because the devs did wonders.Map design is great, it really feels like a true souls style quality shape. There are multiple hidden paths and treasures, verticality is very well rendered in creating the multi-path and shortcuts are tricky and smart, just like Bloodborne.The combat system is the true gem of the game. Asterigos provides a dual-weapon switch combat style, where the common "light" and "heavy" attacks are replaced by the "weapon 1" and "weapon 2" attack. Attack patterns, effects and animations depend on the combo, so mixing them is fundamental to pull out your true strength. Each weapon also has a special attack or move, which also replaces some canon souls mechanics. For example, the "parry" mechanic is bound to the Spear's special move, so if you're a veteran of the genre and you like parrying, this is the weapon for you.There are also many more combat features, such as sliding, charging and changing freely the elemental nature for your weapons, but i won't dig into them not to spoil everything!Lore wise the game is story-driven. There are many cutscenes and NPCs are not cryptic. Still, if you really want to know everything for real, you must read all the documents you find scattered in the world. There's also an Echo feature which reminds a lot of Code Vein, which recreates an event long-gone past since like a memory stored in magic.Characters are far away from being as complex as Dark Souls' ones, but they provide their fair share of progression. Politics reigns supreme in Asterigos, as it is the true engine that moves everything in the game. There are a few characters that, once met the first time, make you feel uncomfortable (they seem not convincing), but your POV will change as you progress with the lore and find out how they are like that (one example for this point is the blacksmith).Graphics are 3d styled-cartoonish, something calling out many references to the great Roman and Greek productions such as Hercules, the great Caesar and so on. And it's fine, since the game draws from that pool.The game is very well polished and optimised: in 13 hours I've never experienced a single drop of frames, stuttering or whatsoever - and i play on max settings with FSR2 on quality mode in 1440p resolution! (RTX 2070 Super)Longevity wise, the game feels way from being over on my playthrough. I'm definitely taking my time exploring every corner, every wall, every path, looking for breakable walls, mimics (♥♥♥♥ them!) and farming stardust (the "souls" currency) in order to upgrade my weapons, my elemental powers - but i'm already aware that after this area there shall be at least one more since i already have the main quest to go. Also, i already know there will be at least one more main quest later, since an entire region of the city is still locked from me.Where's the catch? Well, AI behaviour is not as smart as it should be on a souls game, they are pretty straight forward and bosses only are very fun to fight against. Also, i play on the highest difficulty and the game doesn't sound so much punishing. I've died some times, and i only lost some stardust from my count, instead of dropping them all and move back to retreive them (so you permanently lose some currency on each death, but you never drop it).I could talk a lot more about all the other mechanics, but i won't spoil anymore.This game is a masterpiece and the music is so great.Don't make my mistake, get this game now and but the Ultimate Edition. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Just finished my first playthrough on Challenge Difficulty, and it was GREAT! Gotta give the Devs props for a great action RPG game, it was a blast and I'm already starting my NG+ which offers more items and better upgraded items so there's incentive to. Keep up the good work guys!If you like Action RPG's, then this one is a great one to go with and the price is very fair for what you are getting, definitely recommend as long as you can put up with a little "Indie" feel to some of the games elements and a tad buggy at times(enemies and yourself can get knocked up into the air on an invisible platform from time to time but you can get down so not a big deal)Not finished yet but close. Great little Indie ARPG, NOT a Souls-like as this game is much easier than what Dark Souls would be, that being said if you are familiar with Souls-like games then this one will come pretty naturally to you. The beginning first few zones can feel a bit tedious while you work towards unlocking fast travel, but due to the lack there-of early in the game it incentivizes you to explore, and you WILL miss stuff your first time through. 45 hours into my playthrough and I'm STILL finding stuff I missed even very early on that I totally could have gone to if I had kept lookin for it.The combat is very fluid, the bosses and their mechanics are fun, and the world looks great, very aesthetically pleasing from the bright forest areas to the dark dingy dungeons.I'm playing on "Challenge" which is he games Hard Mode and it has been a very fair challenge I feel, again if you are familiar with Souls games then this will feel just about right to you. One Note is that on Challenge all of your resistances (both physical and elemental) are heavily reduced, this is where Challenge mode enemies get their damage from, and even a trinket that reducces damage from a source from -65 to -45 will actually make enough of a difference in your survivability.LOTS or Lore to find/read if you are interested, I've read most I've come across but some stuff is just really extra to be extra and I still don't feel like I'm missing out on the main story/plot by skipping some of it.The Quest design is made to make you think and explore, as the joural really doesn't help, it basically tells you what's happened during a Main or Side quest but never tells you if it is complete or not, nor how many steps there are to completing it, and some have different outcomes based on your actions/choices, so good luck and I hope your memory is good!

_childDocuments_.review: 7 Hour Review: "If you're looking for more of a 'casual' "Souls-Like" game to play. This is it." So far I'm enjoying the story, character (great voice acting), skills/combat, and overall environment of the game. I haven't come across any glitching or poor performance issues. The only 'Con' I have is that the game does not have a map so sometimes you can spend 15-30 minutes (or more) trying to find your way to the new area you've unlocked. On this note, I did figure out that you should look for 'Blue Fish' markers, as they kind of point the way to your main quest line areas and then small subtle things like birds, rats, bugs, etc... will make a noise when near a side area. You can also keep out this 'light' which will change its appearance when you're near a secret. (Which is nice!) Review Update: I've finished the game! It was a really fun experience. I went with Daggers + Staff and it felt just right for me. There are a lot of side quests you can spend time on in this game, and there is a 'best ending' thing if you do enough of them. This really is a hidden gem that you can spend at least 30+ hours playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Aphes – a city-state full of magic and wonder inspired by ancient Rome and classical Greek designs. From the mist-covered bazaar streets to gloomy sewers, the enigmatic forests at the city’s outskirts to deep chasms full of glittering crystals, the landscapes of Aphes are full of beauty and dangers. Choose from a variety of ranged and melee weapons on the go and combine them as you wish! The talent system allows you to pick and expand your combat style by choosing two out of six completely different weapons: sword and shield, dual blades, spear, hammer, staff or even magic bracelets. Equip a magical staff to obliterate your foes from the distance or switch to a gigantic battle hammer to squish them in a close combat. Whilst Aphes might distract you with its breathtaking views, this city is not for the faint of heart. Fight your way through 60 different monsters and encounter 22 unique bosses – each with its own unique battle mechanics. Every choice and every decision you make matters. Your journey in Aphes will lead you to discover the truth behind the city’s curse, letting you piece together its history through conversations, discovered documents and cinematics, as well as Hilda’s own diary, which she’ll update with sketches and observations. The world of Asterigos is full of secrets and untold stories. Find over 100 collectibles, complete numerous side quests and build on your legacy in the New Game+ mode!

name: Phantom Fury
detailed_description: Shelly “Bombshell” Harrison is back in this highly interactive mix of first person action and road movie adventure. Embark on an adrenaline-fueled journey around the USA. Use an enormous arsenal of weapons and skills to battle treacherous soldiers and vile mutants, all while trying to save mankind. Taking place many years after her fight against Jadus Heskel, Shelly “Bombshell” Harrison awakes in a new world, pulled out of a coma at the behest of an old colleague, with a new bionic arm. Tasked with securing a highly dangerous artifact, the legendary Demon Core, Shelly embarks on an intense journey around the US, as she tries to overcome her own past to save mankind’s future. Key Features An intense mixture of bombastic action and road movie - Fight through seedy hotels in Albuquerque, explore abandoned facilities in Los Alamos, secure the streets of Chicago, and so much more! An insanely interactive world - An incredible amount of interactivity brings the environments to life. Fully usable computers, helicopter flights, playable arcade machines are only a few examples of what you can expect. A vast array of weapons - Over 20 unique weapons are at your disposal! Fan favorites like the Bowling Bombs are joined by brand-new equipment such as armor-piercing shotguns and electrified foam shooting devices. Unlockable weapon upgrades and mods with completely new fire functions will give you the necessary control needed to overcome any fight the way you want! A wide range of unlockable skills and upgrades - Weapons aren’t the only way to overcome the many challenges waiting along the way. Upgrade your bionic arm and suit with powerful new abilities, such as a punch attack or an electric shield. A terrifying number of enemies - Encounter vicious cyborgs, menacing soldiers and disgusting mutations, each with their own special skills. Push your skills to the limit in exhilarating boss battles.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a different format for reviewing games.  Titles like this straddle the line between "recommend" and "not recommend".  Phantom Fury is not done.  It has bugs, some levels (especially the open format ones) feel unfinished, the game is clearly lacking ambient sound, the AI is pretty bad, etc.However, I've had fun with it.  I'm on the 12th of 15 chapters, and not once have I thought the core gameplay is bad.  The weapons hit hard, the level design is good, and the enemies, while not varied, are fun to fight.  The game has had 2 patches since launch, and they have improved the game quite a bit in regards to the bugs and sometimes spotty performance.  I think this title is something that anyone who likes the type of FPS titles that were released in the late 90s to mid 2000s would enjoy.  It's no Half-Life 2 or Far Cry, but it's worth 10 bucks or so.  Wait for it to go on sale and scoop it then. It's not nearly as bad as forums and youtubers would have you believe.

_childDocuments_.review: Also fire your audio director.With the discussions around the game being generally negative (and rightly so after that demo), I wanted to take a look at the gameplay to see if the negativity really is warranted. What follows below is  that caught my attention during the first level of the game.It starts with me realizing that 3DR really did pull down the demo after everyone rightly ♥♥♥♥ on it. They never put it back up, or updated it with the "fixes" that were "almost there but not ready for the demo's release". So thank god Steam support is very generous with refunds. That's definitely not the best start after all the demo drama.The first thing that catches my attention is the graphics, or just how mismatched it feels to be exact. The Colonel stares down at me with oddly smooth and , yet the rest of his textures are pixelated to fit the Ion Fury style. In fact, a lot of models are weirdly high-poly yet have texturing that would match a more low-poly model. This isn't as bad as it sounds, but it's just noticeable enough for you to pick up on it.The Colonel phases out of the room as you conveniently glance away, as you never hear the door open or close. I then go to punch my way out of the room and break the dash ability on the punch by using it on the slope . Another fun fact, if the game loads directly here skipping the cutscene, the door model doesn't even load at all but the collision remains.Some tutorial box with a missing keybind. Weird! This happens quite a lot, even with things I didn't rebind.Around this point I start throwing objects around, and it feels like . I don't want to say  did it better, but the standard for throwing stuff was set in 2004. When you throw things in this game, they just glide through the air as if moved by an invisible force. , which is something objects would actually do if someone ever threw them. It looks  bad and like it was quickly slapped in to the game. Also, objects that impact surfaces make almost no noise. Glass beakers and vials make the tiniest tinkle as they shatter, and even some larger objects just make a quiet "bump".After making my way through and finding the baton, I watch rubble from a falling ceiling rise up out of the floor before the debris from the ceiling even has time to hit the floor. Weird! There's a keypad here with a code you can physically input, which would be neat if the pad highlight followed your mouse input properly. Pressing a number causes it to delay with the tracking and freak out.Also vents display their broken graphic if hit by an explosion, but their collision isn't removed.Then I get the pistol. You use the pistol to shoot down a ladder, which you completely just noclip onto. Like, you don't holster your weapons, there's no camera bobble or anything, there's not even . You just float upwards and get spit out next to it. It feels extremely lazy.After a couple of melee swings to hit the electricity box in the same area, I noticed that Shelly wasn't making any sound at all. Like, not a peep out of her as she whips around slaming people with her arm (and baton). Not a grunt, yell, or even just a sharp exhale. This sounds trivial, but it's the little details like these that help to sell things like weight and impact. This even applies to things like climbing and sliding. The only noises Shelly makes are pain grunts. I am being dead serious, she has 20 lines for pain grunts, 1 line for eating, and a pant VO. I don't even know if this panting VO is used since I never heard it (like at low hp or sprinting).And I should probably mention Shelly's voice.  I can't tell if they recorded her lines in a cardboard box, or if this was a... "stylistic" choice. She is the  character to have a filter like this, excluding radio calls. Everyone else sounds perfectly fine. Why? Was the audio director trying to emulate the sound of retro voices? Why not for the rest of the characters then? Why not change any of the other sounds? WHAT IS GOING ON???Here's a direct comparison for your listening pleasure:While we're on the subject of audio, I'd like to mention the lackluster ambiance in this level. You hear:Where's the computer hums? Where's the hum and clicks of a server rack? The hum of the lights, hissing vents, or refrigeration units? Some of these things  have sounds, but are  you have to be on top of the object to hear anything. This level feels lifeless and dead because it's so damn QUIET. Drones you fight have this same issue. They explode after being killed, but the charge-up sound is so quiet that you can't even hear it unless you pick one up.I then get stuck trying to find a way to open a door. Turns out I need to interact with this PC to open the door. You wouldn't think to use the PC given that there's . The only difference is that this one has a faint green light on the front, which is very easy to miss in an already cluttered room. When the important objects get mixed in with the set dressing, better care needs to be taken to  important areas or objects.Shelly is fireproof.Generic statement about the bad AI.Nearing the end of the level, I find what could be some of the worst design choices I've seen in this level. After clearing a lab of two enemies, I see a big sign and arrow pointing up towards a waste disposal area. Ok, that's the way I guess I need to go. Following this path leads you to a dead end with a pickup box. To my left is a slightly open door with a visible weapon at the bottom. It's brightly lit and there are explosive barrels I can shoot. Ok, logic would dictate that there's some way to get down there. You wouldn't just highlight something so well to not make it obtainable, right?To your right is a vent trailing off, which looks like the same ones you crawl down. There's a red light and a "No Entry" label slapped above it. Try as you might, this vent will never open. It's at this point it hits me why that sign is there. The devs saw beta testers get stuck here trying to reach the weapon below, despite the weapon not being obtainable. They then slapped the no entry text above the vent and called it a day, instead of just designing the area better. Why not remove the weapon? Why not remove the interactable barrels? Why not just make it darker so you don't think to look down there? Why not change the vent so you don't think you can enter it? Instead, they took the laziest approach possible and threw some "nothing to see here" text up.And yes, that area is indeed inaccessible.This was . If that's the first level, the  your game gives to the player, then I don't want to stick around to see the rest.
