_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: While I didn't feel the same elation playing this game that I did with Ion Fury, this is still a good retro-esqe game and I did enjoy playing it. The jump from Duke3D graphics to this newer style is nice, the combat is varied and the enemies are decent. The levels are decently made, and the keycard-hunting style of progression wasn't as tedious as some games in the genre. Now the gripes. The story was very predictable, I would say it's basically every cliche in the genre all wrapped up together. It was a real cheese-fest. I was also bothered by the checkpoint system with no manual save ability. Finally the performance. Even though it looks like an older game, it's way more demanding than I thought it really should be. Playing on a 7800X3D and 7900XTX, I should have had a locked 144FPS @4k, but even after lowering the settings from the Ultra to High preset, I would often see dips as low as the mid the 60s and major stuttering in large areas. No doubt this game could use with some optimizations. I did finish the game in a weekend, and while overall I would say that it was worth playing, I don't see myself doing any replay as I did with Ion Fury and I would really recommend to wait for a bit of a sale. $25 isn't bad for this game but under $20 would be easier to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I'm heavily mixed on this one. What I'll say in short is that - it's not a bad game but it's not a great game.At times it's very solid and has good interactivity with nice animation, but at other times it feels extremely unbalanced. Now when I say unbalanced there are just some strange choices in gameplay that don't work great together.1 - Enemies move way too damn fast. Like, mid combat with a group of enemies all running around me while I can only focus on one which in most games wouldn't be the biggest problem, in this one they just move so fast I end up spending more time aiming than being able to dodge the rest or keep moving. And this is not isolated, you have enemies that run between cover spots, enemies that charge you, suiciders that charge you and explode, tiny floor enemies that charge you but are hard to see. Either make the protagonist run a lot faster, or slow these enemies down a lot because I run as slow as tar compared to how fast these enemies are running laps around the map.2 - Enemies do more damage than they take. The worst offender of this is the big guys that charge at you and dive at you causing a large area damage. These guys are ridiculous. They move way faster than you can outrun them, and the distance that the leap at you is way too large to be able to back pedal or to do a run\dodge\shoot. And to make things worse that leap attack does a LARGE amount of damage. They can easily kill you in 3 leap attacks, and because of their speed they can do those 3 extremely quick. And because of how quick you can't get to a reasonable distance to counter attack, the only real attacks that kill them quick are explosives so you just end killing yourself in the process. Any other gun treats them as bullet sponges and you just won't kill them quick enough. Basically if you have more than 1 of these guys attacking you at once - your just screwed.3 - Guns just feel weak and sluggish. The roster of guns on paper are a solid loadout. But in gameplay, they just don't work well. For one, switching between weapons in combat is a nightmare - there really should have been a weapon wheel or something cuz to go from a pistol to a rocket launcher is going to get you killed at least a handful of times with how long it takes. And for the weakness of these guns, for instance the shotgun, there is really no reason why a point black blast from the shotgun only insta kills weaker enemies once and while, or why even headshots from the pistol or crossbow only sometimes are instant kills. There are a sort of zombie enemy you run into a lot, 8 times out of 10 a point black shotgun blast only smacks them back, from a distance that should pretty much paint the wall with them. OCCASIONALLY, they die in one shot but don't get your hopes up, it's less than random. You many times end up a warzone of many enemies at once but the guns are so weak that you spend more time trying to run for cover just so you can reload or equip something better. 4 - Ammo and reloads.. Look, in a game like this reloads can either make or break the entire flow of the game and here.. It's a break. This ties into my first point about enemy speeds, if you are going to have excessive speeded enemies - then either my reloads need to be lightning fast or the guns have to have no reloads at all. It's unbalanced. I'm stuck in a 4-5 second reload while desperately backpedaling from enemies or trying to find cover and it just ruins everything. I've died plenty of times mid reload cuz it's just too slow and your character moves too slow to buy you any time to complete it. Ammo amounts are pretty BS too, there aren't many ammo pickups while at other times there are too many which wouldn't be a problem BUUUUT you can barely carry any of it so you end up never having any ammo when you need it, which puts you in the spot of being too afraid to use your better guns because you have no idea if your going to get any ammo for it any time soon. Hell even your main pistol which a six shooter - you only can carry 36 rounds for, that's six reloads before your empty and YOU WILL go empty quick. No upgrades for this in gameplay either5 - Health pickups. Yeah there really aren't many. For the amount of damage you take, there really should have been either health a plenty or the individual pickups need to give an actual substantial amount. SO many times I had to go into combat with 1, 10, 14 etc. amounts of health because there was not a single pickup for whole stretches of a map section. Even with full health and armor, enemies drain your bars so fast in such a short amount of attacks that you have zero confidence to go into the next area because your damage resistance is just tissue paper even against the weakest enemy variants.Those are my main complaints right now. This game has much potential to a be a great and fun single player shooter, but some of this stuff really needs to be addressed and rebalanced. It's worth playing, but if your looking to experience that Duke Nukem Forever '01 magic we we're robbed of, this just isn't really there yet. I think that's the real problem here, this game should've been way more Duke Nukem and way less Half Life 2, especially when Ion Fury was already a perfect mid-fast paced game in the same way Duke 3D was.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: I give up. This game is a massive disappointment.I loved the previous game, Ion Fury. I came into this expecting it to be that, with a "modern" touch to it (modern as in an early 2000s game). But somewhere, something was seriously lost.The humour in the game is gone. You have the main protagonist from Ion Fury, Shelly "Bombshell" Harrison, acted wonderfully, but with nothing to do. The funny or pop-culture referencing one liners are all but gone. I tried to find more references in the early levels, but gave up because there's no secrets to find. Just little loot caverns. The story is mediocre at best. You wake up and have a robot arm. Escape this facility. Do this. Do that. No explanation why you were in a facility, why you now have a robot arm. Suddenly Shelly's great grand dad is involved? Why, so you could make it personal for Shelly? Ion Fury had her snap when Heskel took over the city, because he spilled her drink. She doesn't need a personal reason to take him down. Plus, you're fighting GDF soldiers everywhere. Why? Shelly doesn't seem concerned by this, and neither does your support people. It's never clearly told to you why this is happening.The shooting doesn't feel impactful. The weapons are clunky and not very accurate. Switching on auto-aim makes things a bit better, but not by much. The upgrade system is toothless. Oh, I can stun a guard for three seconds now. Boring. Shelly's arm upgrades are also boring, and i think don't work properly. The foam gun is hot garbage, it blocks your vision and seems to do no damage, and the upgrade that is supposed to narrow the stream does bugger all.The levels are okay. The pacing is all over the place and there are tons of moments where they'll just randomly drop enemies on you with no warning. Those drones that fly around are the worst, you shoot them and they fall, no problem, right? No, you need to shoot them again while they're on the ground, otherwise they'll explode and do a ton of damage to you, only you can't do that, because they always spawn en mass and bum rush you.I may end up going back to finish this, but my god its a slog. Good thing i got it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: Old guy with loads of shooter experience here. Phantom Fury: What a great melange! Duke Nukem 3D & Forever meet Half-Life 1 & 2, plus a ton of own or remixed ideas. Definitely give this game a shot if you like "modern retro shooters", it's far better that current reviews suggest. It's completely different from Ion Fury and other mid-90's inspired shooters - in the best way possible. BUT: The decision to not release the game on GOG is a huge mistake, I still hope they reconsider.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot on good conscious recommend this game in its current state. The game has potential, but it feels more like a late-stage Early Access title than a polished game. If you are like me, and interact with the environment and objects around you, then you cannot even leave the  without running into an interaction bug. This sets the stage for the rest of the game and what you'll experience.Other reviewers typically mention that the game "becomes good" once you hid the midpoint or thereabout, however in my opinion this isn't the case. What you end up getting is a bunch of weapons and abilities that allows you to end the awful combat even faster; typically by running, shooting, and punching your way through hordes and hordes of enemies. But the gameplay and combat loop never becomes engaging or fun. It's just a chore to play through.The final levels are the worst ones, as you just move between combat areas and mow down the same enemies over and over again with the same weapons, with barely any variation or challenge. It's just boring and awful slog to play through as it never really ends. I was so bored that I had to stop playing the game a couple of times just to get some much needed variation.In the middle of playing through Phantom Fury I made a detour and played through Half-Life 2 and its two episodes and... oh boy... It's clear that Phantom Fury tried to take  of inspiration from Half-Life 2 and Valve, but sadly it never understands what made those games great. Half-Life 2 easily holds your attention and doesn't waste your time. Phantom Fury is the complete opposite.Do not buy this game! It would be a waste of your time  money. Go play something better in the genre instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Phantom Fury is like a fan attempt at doing a Duke Nukem Forever 2001 game but it ends up being like DNF 2011 where some will have fun with it and others will bounce off of it. I think the game is really fun, but it took me until the train level for the combat to click. First impressions weren't great, I didn't like the weapons, the enemies or the set pieces for the first couple hours of the game. I started liking it a lot more once I unlocked weapon mods like the shotgun flashlight.It's nice to play a new retro-inspired FPS where is inspirations are games from 1998-2002 rather than 1994-1997. The predecessor to this game, Ion Fury, is good enough to enter the Build engine canon alongside Duke Nukem 3D, Shadow Warrior and Blood. However, I don't think Phantom Fury is nearly as good as Half-Life, SIN, Halo, etc. It's more like Unreal 2, Blood 2, World War Zero, the B-grade FPS games that released around that time period. I don't have any issues with this because I love those 4-6/10 games. But I can see why some people are disappointed.I hope more games like this come out. I'm looking forward to whatever Slipgate Ironworks makes next (and hopefully they will stay alive and well after Embracer did their thing)

It could have been an amazing experience if it wasn't for some pesky issues, primarily of a technical nature.Read more on:

_childDocuments_.review: Take the soulful perfection of Ion Fury, with its incredible map design, well hidden secrets, flowing combat...and remove all of that - this leaves you with Phantom Fury. Phantom Fury is what you get when you lobotomize a better game.The level design is tedious and uninspired, encounters are formulaic, no secrets to find, and the sound design is abysmal. Regarding the sound design, weapons lack any punch and corners have been cut, for example there being no audio for footsteps in water - it's as if the water doesn't exist. There are plenty of map issues too, the game encourages you to explore but doing so will frequently leave you in locations you cannot escape and so forces you to reload to a previous checkpoint. Expect bugs too, significant ones, such as having a weapon mod randomly stop working and buying the alternative one for the weapon won't even enable switching between them - the mod shows as purchased but will no longer equip, so I guess I won't get to use that for the rest of my play-through.I'm so disappointed as I loved Ion Fury so much, but sadly it has to be said: don't waste your money on this uninspired, low-effort, slop.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: Worth a play. Not nearly as bad as people made it out to be but definitely some very questionable design decisions.The Good:- Decent length- Some cool physics, destructibility, enemies pick up things and throw them at you with funny results some times- Guns are generally good, theres a few that i tried once and never used again. audio is fine in this department mostly. some guns have very cool alt fires- Environment/architecture/asset design is excellent and there's a lot of neat details, everything is well done section to sectionThe Bad (it's a lot):- No quicksave, this is a pretty big sin but the checkpoints are decent- Level design, there's a lot of very bad sins here. Figuring out where to go was never this bad except in the worst games. A lot of times I had to use a video guide just to figure out where something was and progression is often via a completely unassuming room you'd write off as a side exploration area.- Vehicles, in 1999 this would've been impressive for sure but the main thing letting it down here is that you're usually on rails for these except for the Halo jeep scenes. The weapon on the jeep leaves a lot to be desired, the lack of stagger is very odd here considering it's a mounted mg- Enemy variety, I think you should've done a 3rd race for a game this length- Upgrades, you very rarely feel they come into play. I never used the shield once and the fist I rarely used because the range is so limited. The weapon upgrades should improve the weapon not just offer a different firing style. Many upgrades are just badly thought out, the aoe reload is something that never helped once.- Lack of any real attempt at NPCs, there's some cops that fight with you which would've been an opportunity for some nice one liners or comedy but they just stand there. There's one guy that shows up to give you a magnum and then you never see him again. Seemed utterly pointless- Puzzles, I think modern devs struggle to understand what makes a good puzzle and that's reflected a lot here. A lot of puzzles are just finding a hidden item you have to just look for. You have an engine where you can pickup almost anything in the game and I don't think that's used once. Physics aren't leveraged really.- Gunplay/Gameplay, a lot to say here. the stagger system is very confusing. in some cases a smg will stagger an enemy but a high caliber or explosive weapon won't. the whole thing feels very inconsistent and you can end up on the backfoot so often because you feel your weapons have no weight to them or ability to crowd control. it seems like knockback was implemented for the shotgun with gsf grunts and then they washed their hands of it completely- Unfinished ideas, the bladesaw is an example of this where they put in a whole weapon that basically only opens doors. this could've been expanded on so much in puzzles. eg cutting power wires or cutting holes in walls. You randomly get a magnum pistol towards the end of the game that seems very thrown in at the last moment.- Movement, the jump slide chaining is there but it's not particularly do-able. Getting at items is often awkward and movement in general just feels slightly anemic. I think they backed off letting you go nuts on the jump slides once the physics issues kept cropping up which is a shame.I think the problem here is they should've got the basic fundamental gameplay down first but I think this probably suffered from too many chefs in the kitchen. A lot of ideas for vehicle sections, weapons, power-ups etc but no one was paying attention to the actual gameplay feel. You have so many tools and they all feel like a half-measureI think a sequel that addresses a lot of the gameplay issues would be great, but please get the gameplay down first then start with the ideas.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: The good: game looks gorgeous, a modern take on early 2000s FPS with nice graphics and a distinct art style. The shooting has been improved a lot from the demo and the rest of the arsenal is satisfying to use, enemies react a lot better to your movement and getting shotThe bad: past the halfway point the levels are not great, the last ones are straight up unfinished with tons of empty spaces, or they have an embarrassing amount of backtracking and terrible signposting. Most of the upgrades don't feel great (faster reload only when you have armor? what??). Some TERRIBLE vehicle sections that go for longer than needed. It also takes quite a bit from Half-Life to be just "a funny reference/callout".What will be improved: tons of gamebreaking bugs (by the time I'm writing this they solved a couple of them so the team is working on it, which says a lot more than other 3DR releases).Long story short, this game needed more time in the oven, but even then it'll end up being decent, not as good as it's predecessor in the Build Engine.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having fun, only one minor bug so far (clipping from an elevator). I'm not getting the same experience as the most prominent YT reviewers so far, AI seems to act fine (i like that they have friendly fire) level design is aight, i haven't got lost or anything, feedback is good, but nothing is exceptional (aside from the visuals), is  just good enough, for the price is worth it.Fun to play overall, but Ion is still the better game. Is weird that they tried to push fury as a franchise, but every game is for a different audience. The genre shift is the thing that is hurting this game the most in my opinion. Because I wish firefights were longer and more frenetic, alongside a banger of a track, but I guess I'm wishing for this game to be more of a boomshot than a SIN/HL like, which I think is a fair expectation to have since most people are here because of Ion.Anyways, the game itself don't deserve the hate and the studio behind this one actually delivered this time, which was the biggest surprise to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to give this game a fair chance after finishing IF: Aftershock.im not bothered that it took a slower approach to single player FPS combat, similar to half life 2, i actually enjoy those just as much as old boomer shooters.the game has good ideas, but executes them poorly, one of the biggest being the illusion of having multiple ways to approach a set-piece, alot of the map is plagued with invisible walls and areas that look like shortcuts being complete dead-ends, gameplay and design-wise everything just has a very undercooked feel to it, this game needed more time.i dont hate it, but i wish it wasn't so rushed, but i cant recommend it yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed it. The weapons are fun to use, the gunplay and destruction from the first game is there, and the attitude remains. It's not as good as the first game, with the focus less on pure, destructive gameplay. This works against the game, as it now shifts some focus to puzzles that are partly frustrating, partly dull. There's also some game design choices that are lacking. Environments aren't as fun to traverse. The game is attempting to bridge Half Life and Duke Nukem instead of being a pure Duke Nukem homage, going against the old adage of "if it isn't broken, don't fix it". While complaints against it and people's dislike is valid, I had fun. For those looking for an enjoyable shooter that is mostly focused on the action, you'll find plenty of that here.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun.Worth the price from what i have enjoyed so far. I'm about three hours in as of writing this and feel i've played enough now to form an initial impression. The good stuff. The art direction is great. I love the look of the game from the lighting to the textures and environments. It's got this nice retro pixelated aesthetic but in a modern crisp engine with nice lighting tech and great physics. Things explode - the explosions knock other things around. Corpses pile up. Limbs go flying. Its great and satisfying.Combat is also fun. The weapon roster is really good. Not a single weapon feels like a waste of space. I enjoy using them all and they are all powerful and useful in any fight. You can upgrade them in various ways to make them even better. I actually had a hard time choosing an upgrade because the base weapon was already so damned fun to use. Combat is also nicely interactive. Heads fly off with a satisfying mushy pop and a spray of blood. Limbs can be shot off. Some enemies turn into grenades that you can throw back at the enemies. The AI really isn't as bad as some reviews had made out. Only had a couple of moments when AI was doing something stupid. The zombies... they ARE stupid but that is by design. Surely reviewers aren't picking on that? Level design is really nice. It taps into that old school layout where you have some nice backtracking where the level leads you back to the start where your exit is located. Key hunting isn't difficult at all. All the level design makes sense and is clearly signposted within the art direction its self. Only a few times i had to scratch my head a little - but in a good way. I don't want to just sprint through.The pace is good as well. It's not a fast paced shooter. You take your time. It plays very similar to the pace of Half Life. Tonally it feels very much like the original half life as well. No it's not on par but there are definite notes and cues taken as inspiration for this game.Lead character is nice. Her voice work is really good. The support characters voices are also really good and fit well within the tone of the project. Flaws? I mean its not a perfect game. There are some things that at time feel they lack just a little polish. The second area - big open area - that felt a bit lacking in some places -  but its really not the train wreck i think some people are claiming. Maybe my standards are lower. I went in without expectations. Maybe later on it craps the bed. I'll find out when i get further but  going in blind without having watched reviews or previews and without being told by others what to think and what to enjoy - i can honestly say i'm enjoying this and will play it to completion (which i don't do with many games)EDIT: I'm now well over half way through the game and still enjoying myself. While there are some moments that are weaker (mainly the vehicle sections) the rest is just fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, leading up to today’s launch, I was a bit apprehensive about this game (because of the negative reviews of the game on youtube), but after playing 2 hours I am enjoying it and wouldn’t say that it’s mediocre or a bugfest or any of the ways I saw it described in those videos. I was still excited to jump into this game because I love Ion Fury and Shelly and Retro shooters (from the 90s-inspired games all the way through to early 2000s). I’m starting to get old now, so I remember playing Doom and Duke Nukem 3d Shareware versions when I was 7-8 and just getting into gaming. In the last few years, I have really enjoyed this revival of indie FPS games that are attempting to recreate games from that era. This game is more in-line with Half-Life 2 than Duke Nukem 3D, which was clearly the inspiration for Ion Fury. Phantom Fury wasn’t developed by VoidPoint, so don’t expect a game that plays exactly like Ion Fury, because you could be disappointed. Instead, I would say- be open to an evolution of Ion Fury's formula and gameplay loop. I believe this is using Unreal Engine 4, so the game has much higher fidelity as a result of that. It still goes for a retro look, but with much better lighting and higher quality assets and materials.So far, I’m having fun with this and am happy with what I received for $22.50. The art direction is very impressive, so is the interactivity in this game. It’s not on the level of an immersive sim or anything, but it’s very similar to Ion Fury in this one specific way, you can open up lockers and smash crates and use soda machines- each can restores 1 health point. The guns and combat are enjoyable, most of the weapons are here, like the Loverboy revolver and the bowling bombs and they function just like in Ion Fury. The shotgun is the only weapon that needs some help, mostly just that its shots are wide enough. It's barely any different than targeting with a pistol, and should be quite a bit easier to hit moving targets with it but it's not.I will probably update this review because I usually don’t like to review games this early in, just think of this as a first impression. I definitely think it deserves to have a higher rating than “mixed” and that’s why I’m writing this. I understand that Slipgate/3DR has made a lot of mistakes and missteps over the years, but I’ve been happy with this one and Wrath: Aeon of Fury. 3DR is unique because they are really the closest thing we have to a “AAA Boomer Shooter” developer, alongside New Blood. There are countless retro shooters being released nowadays, but the vast majority are not of the same production quality as what you will get from Slipgate/3DR. Hopefully after a few patches, this game will be recommendable to all, because what we have already is still very enjoyable from my point of view. It's a fun, somewhat disposable story with Shelly and lots of shooting, it doesn't get a whole lot deeper than that, but I'm completely fine with what it is and think it accomplishes what it sets out to be.Also- I recommend playing on hard, rather than normal. It seems to improve the enemy behavior, just based on some of the complaints I saw from the video reviews. They have been pretty aggressive and providing a decent challenge without the issue where they stop attacking if you’re far away from them.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game certianly has its highlights (The loverboy being a huge highlight), there are alot of parts to this game that feel really... REALLY unfinished. I'm playing through the game on its hardest difficulty for my first playthrough, and i wasn't really blown away by its delivery, but just kinda... meh I felt meh about it. I tried playing it like it wants me to, exploring, interacting with stuff, and visually, the game looks solid, not bad for working in unreal 1 if I do say so, although the game does lack in the exploration department. the levels I have played through have felt very linear, very A to B, and for a game thats I think trying to be an Imsim, you really gotta have the levels opened up... and invisible barriers... OOOHHHH I would rather not get into that. One of my biggest grievances started to show when I died for the first time to this... large tanky zombie? I dunno, my first encounter went something along the lines of me trying to gun it down with my shotgun, and it just spamming this jump attack in a horribly narrow coridor and killing me in two seconds from when I saw it to death. That made me realize two things, one: I was going to be dealing with some stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (including getting soft locked, and clipping through an elevator somehow?) and two: that there is a checkpoint system, that feels like it puts you waaaay to far back. and on top of that, there is no quick saving. why? I dare ask, why no quick saves? If i'm going to be dying to stupid crap, and the game is going to punish me by putting me way back, the least you could do is allow me the luxury of diligantly quick saving.As of right now, i've played about 6 hours of the game. It has some good highlights, i'll give it that, i'm finding some things that feel okay. This game however does feel unfinished in ALOT of areas, and with that, I cant really recommend people this game in its current form. like a 6/10 right now.Edit 1: the game is now a 4/10. I have progressed a little further and have hit the wall I guess I could sum up as a zombie boss thing, and literally the only thing keeping me from beating it is getting soft locked, or getting insta killed by the those attrociously balanced tanky zombies. seriously, who okayed these things? I knew they were awful when one killed me near instantly when I first encountered them. but the boss summons like 6, maybe more, i dunno. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful.Edit 2: I have finished the game, and the ending was the most cliche underwhelming slop to ever be. The whole 'Unfinished' feel comes really, REALLY hard once you get to the city area. I was able to get out of the map, alot near the end of the game, and its nice, having alot of area to explore in a map sometimes, its just that when you walk all the way to a place, and discover there is literally nothing there... its an awful feeling. Also, the fact that your sprint is like only 2% faster than your run, its just... uuuuuugh. I did however, discover some movement tech you can do. If you do a slide, then jump as you are sliding, you preserve that momentum. So I'm not saying I dolphin dived through most of my playthrough, but I like going fast, and it made me go fast. The final fight was, not suprising me at all at this point, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. you fight in a small room, only for the boss to blind you, only for like 40 enemies to ambush you, for you to find the boss, and fight him, in another small room. Least, I thought that was the final fight, nope, got one more. it was a little better than the other fight in my opinion. but the lead up to it was... awful. especially when shelly is casually murdering like thousands of EDF solders, zombies, and killer robots, its weird shes like... hyperventilating over a bomb of all things.Anyway, this is a 5/10 from me. yeah, there was some fun to be had... but oh my god... there were some issues. Highlights: 1) gunplay for the most part was okay2) the enviroment design is great3) The loverboy is my favorite gun in the gameAwful ♥♥♥♥:1) no quicksaves, checkpoints feel way too punishing2) levels feel very linear at the start, when it does open up though...3) THERE IS ALMOST NOTHING TO FIND.4) the game feels unfinished, and that feeling grows ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ huge as you approach the end of the game5) the story is very bland, and the pacing is way, way off.6) The tanky zombies are the worst enemy in this game by a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mile. 7) there is a chance you will get yourself soft locked. (I stood on a box, and it shot me up out of the map. I was switching weapons on an elevator, I clipped through the elevator... what?)8) There are way too many places where it looks like you can go, only for there to be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ invisible wall put in the way. this happens way too much.9) The game decided to reset all my armor upgrades near the end of the game... for whatever reason. thats cool.10) as far as I know, there is nothing to do post game, other than play through again.11) Some of bombshells lines felt a little... off character it seemed. I dunno, it was like comparing Duke 3D Duke to Duke Forever 2011 Duke... I dunno, she seemed more spiteful I guess...This was a game, for the most part, I was looking forward too. I really enjoyed Ion Maiden (*fury) and was hoping this would live up to that games quality, it doesn't. Till this game get some work done, I cannot recommend this at all. Till then, to the development team... blink twice if you were being forced to rush this out...

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended only because I loved the first game and played this through because of that.I won't sugarcoat it, the game needs a lot of polish and to be honest if you want to experience a proper old school feeling shooter play Ion Fury, the first game instead.This game... I want to say that I enjoyed it at parts. Some fights were extremely fun, but many times I couldn't help but giggle at how the AI got stuck to the simplest of things and actually sometimes wouldn't even notice fighting alongside their other AI companions only being alerted towards me when I shot at them.The graphical presentation is beautiful, but I don't know if it was sound glitches or what sometimes sounds would cut off and Shelly wouldn't react to being shot. No pain grunts or scream. I felt like when I died it was mostly of something unfair than in Ion Fury I felt like if I died it was my mistake for not learning what the AI does and how it responds to my moves. There were lots of other glitches too especially when I was trying to find my way in the world and ended up breaking the game just by trying to explore more.Some assets were up in the air. Like a lamp post or some rubble, but I know those can be fixed and polished later on. I see the vision of the developers, but I do feel like this falls short from an experience standpoint. I had moments where I was lost in the levels wandering and trying to find where to go and when I did find where to go I usually would be caught off guard by suddenly spawned enemies that just immediately yell out your name, run at you mindlessly and shoot while doing it. Only thing that kept me going was the story. It is enjoyable and I love seeing more of Shelly's character. I wish there were more lines she'd say, but that is just a minor complaint on my part.Graphics and story are fun.AI path finding and overall experience with the game need polish.Still enjoyed the game, but play Ion Fury if you want to have a better experience and a more of an old school shooter experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Phantom Fury is a half-baked  that gets a half-hearted thumbs-up from me, mostly because , finding door codes, solving simple environmental puzzles and so on. Yes, I’m aware that this game didn’t have half the budget that  had, but even compared to other low-budget projects, . How much the game is carried by its  is nowhere more apparent than in its last couple of levels. In  in particular, Phantom Fury just ditches all of its good bits in favour of forcing you through a gruelling series of samey arena fights against hordes of enemies instead. And it’s here that we get a glimpse of how bad Phantom Fury truly could have been if not for some inspired ideas that manage to make the previous 15 levels of the campaign genuinely entertaining.Overall, I don’t think Phantom Fury is half as bad as its reputation, as  before those final levels. But if a couple of good ideas isn’t enough for you to overlook the core flaws of the game, then I don’t think you’ll enjoy Phantom Fury very much.One of these core flaws (which was almost enough for me to give the game a thumbs-down instead) is its story. Yes, I know, “who cares about the story in a retro shooter?” Well, I do – and evidently, so did the person at Slipgate Ironworks who decided that Phantom Fury should be a much more story-driven experience, with in-game cutscenes and an entire flashback dream sequence in the middle. Unfortunately, that person didn’t tell the writer, so . There is almost no worldbuilding here and the motivations of what few characters the game introduces remain nebulous throughout. At multiple points did I feel like the devs just strung together whatever levels they had and then added some radio chatter in an attempt to give us the vaguest of ideas of how we went from one to the next.As it is, I don’t regret playing Phantom Fury, though, and I’ll probably even play it again at some point in the future. , which is something I personally really enjoy in a shooter. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: I removed the date of May 30th from this review as I had hoped the game would receive constant updates but with the cancellation of this year's Realms Deep, it may be a while before a patch comes out.)Despite not being the perfect Half-like that I imagined ( Some areas could be highlighted better,a couple enemies could be nerfed, the A.I at times could be a little smarter, the  last act of the game could've received some polish before release, & the vehicle sections are a little weird.)but I've enjoyed my time with Phantom Fury, as it's lush environments & artstyle keep me replaying it no matter what. The gameplay, though janky, has many fun moments, & you're always able to adjust to a certain playstyle.However, if the devs ever consider making future patches, I would recommend improving the basic combat between GDF Soldiers & yourself. While the tension is there, they lack much death animations, which could be changed as they could react similarily to enemies in Soldier of Fortune, resulting in them reacting to limb removal or groaning in pain, making killing them much more satisfying, & more environmental hazards around them would help alot, as for a game that talks about interactivity, I've never found myself using it too much to my advantage. I would still recommend this game to someone wanting to see where Shelly's adventure leads or even just enjoy a game that tries it's best to bring a spiritual continuation to Ion Fury, I'd still say give it a chance, even if it feels a little rough compared to other releases. I still hope the team is proud of what they did, & hopefully Slipgate can try & rebuild what was lost with this year's layoffs.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest here, I'm going to focus on the negatives first & formost before saying anything positive.Let's go!-. The enemy AI is dumb. Enemies are varied & do have different abilities, but they all default to the same tactic of bum rushing the player. This is something that needs to be patched as quickly as possible.. A game with this kind of graphical style shouldn't be chugging at certain times. Especially with my desktop's hardware. We're talking RTX3060, Intel i5-13400 & 24gb of RAM.. Sound effects on some of the guns just lack impact.. Everything this game does has already been done before & done better.. In the bar in the desert, WHY THE HELL CAN'T I PLAY POOL WHEN I PICK UP A QUE & BRING IT TO THE TABLES!? I can play darts, FRIGGIN DARTS, pinball, an arcade game & drink other peoples drinks but not pool!?+. The Duke Nukem 3D interactivity has translated over really well to the new fully 3D space & the inclusion of Half-Life style realism has allowed for either the same level of dynamic interaction, if not more, than what Ion Fury had.. The weapon arsenal is varied & gives the player plenty of options. Special attacks & abilities are a welcome addition & can really help you in a pinch or reserve ammo.. The levels & set pieces are just as varied as the weapons & enemies, so the game never starts to feel samey.7/10Phantom Fury is far from a bad game, but it is a flawed one. I don't like the mantra of, oh they'll fix it with patches it later, since that's why get stuff like Medal of Honour: Warfighter, but this is a case of that.There is fun to be had with this game in it's current state, but if Slipgate & 3D Realms manage to address the issues with patches soon, then it could transform in to a genuinely great game. An 8/10.Hell maybe even a modern classic.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it but it's not amazing. There's some interesting stuff here. The weapons are good. The levels can be interesting. The enemies aren't all just your bog standard enemies and they can require you to think on your feet to deal with them. For instance, there's drones that explode a few seconds after you kill them which you can use to your advantage (or can hurt you if you're not careful). I thought the game was decent in length. It ran well on my machine (steady 120 FPS with 2 minor stutters over the whole game). I encountered very few glitches.The bad though. The enemy AI is a little on the stupider side. They still are compentent enough in most the game but I would have liked better. There's 2 or 3 really rough parts of the game that feel unfinished or rushed. Most the game is good but it's hard to ignore this. There is definitely some jank here too. Little things work but might be a little off from how you'd expect, like the weapon switching. A few of the upgrades feel necessary and unfortunately the game doesn't tell you which ones (fortunately it's pretty easy to figure out). I didn't pay attention to the story but it seemed fairly generic.It's definitely no Ion Fury but it's definitely got enough in it to enjoy. Just expect some rough spots and some jank. It's definitely closer to Half Life than other boomer shooters. I'd definitely play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to write a review about this game. I enjoyed it, even though that it was different than I expected.First of all, you can't compare Phantom Fury with Ion Fury. If you do so, you are gonna get disappointed in almost every single aspect. If you want to compare it with other titles, I think Half-Life 1 fits the most.The first half of the game was clearly the better one. There were some parts in later missions that felt really streatched where I had to run through a big map to kill more and more pointless amounts of enemies.Missions take 5 minutes up to 1 hour.Some of the guns simply feel bad and weak while enemies took multiple shots before they finally died, even on the lowest difficulty. This is bad balanced.I also encoutered the well known bug that made me lose all my abilities - for the rest of the whole game. I don't know how something like this can happen at all.The puzzles were sometimes challenging. It's not that they were difficult, but due to some bad level design decisions they felt harder than they actually were. Not a negative point for this, but it needs to get mentioned.Overall, I had a good time playing Phantom Fury. It's far from perfect, but it is indeed a pretty solid shooter. Even though I mentioned mostly the bad aspects of the game, there is a reason why I recommend it, and this reason is that I had much "fun".

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for this game and, eventually, I got a lot of fun during its first half. The level design had nothing to do with pesky old school level designs where you need to run in circles finding keys and whatnot. No, in Phantom Fury's first half it was as great as it was in Cultic: elegant, streamlined, yet intriguing levels that award you for exploration. Alas, once I got to the lab complex, the late 90's wired level design manifested and... I dropped the game, eventually. I still recommend this title, but only on discount. No patches can solve the level design issues, so don't wait patches, wait for discounts instead to truly enjoy awesome, fierce, diverse 1st half of the game. The first half is a love letter to Half-Life and F.E.A.R., but with its own face, which is quite an achievement.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, here we go again, for what it HOPEFULLY the last time.So, you all know me by now -- the tastemaker, the expert, the one who called EVERYTHING out along the way.  I knew this was how it would all end, and its funny to see it all come to a head after being told off by so many sheep. Its okay, I forgive you for being wrong, because there is no way you couldve known. I did though.Anyways, enough celebration, lets get into the review. This game is dogwater. Every aspect of it is wrong, clearly displaying the skillful mismanagement of 3DRealms and one Fred S. -- The poison in the water, the snake in the grass. If it wasn't obvious before now, it should be readily apparent that THIS is the true problem with 3DRealms (We will not acknowledge Slipgate in this review, they don't exist as a separate entity, and they never did. They are the same company, that exists in the same physical space, with the same personnel). All of the art assets, models, sounds, animations etc. in this game are all fantastic on their own. That isn't the issue at hand, you can FEEL the talent of the hardworking developers that went into this game. But it is so PAINFULLY clear that the management of these individuals was among the worst ever. A sad attempt to mimic the past and misunderstand every decision the forebears made. There is no balance, the combat is dreadful, the AI does nothing but run at you or stand in place (this is distinct from the very very common bug where the AI just completely deactivates). There are also too many weapons in order to appease the ADHD of the producer. However only maybe 3 of them are useful with little compelling reason to switch off of those weapons.The level design is at best bland and at worst among the most painfully confused experiences you can find in an FPS (Chapter 11 should be an actual war crime). They levels are comprised of recycled ideas from DNF2001 because Fred made this game as a way to brag about being the only person able to access the build -- but that all was for naught because one of his employees clearly leaked it to steal his thunder. What ISNT lifted directly from dnf2001 (most of the game was) is just from half life pretty much. Real grim mate.Beyond this is *terrible* writing (hey queener its me again), a nonsensical plot, emotionless voice acting, forced IP crossover?? the almost total lack of music, and bugs *EVERYWHERE*... you could go on and on, and many will, but you dont need me to list the litany of issues. The whole package is truly slapdash. You can FEEL the cutbacks, the forced scheduling, the laid off employees.One can only hope that this is the REAL end of the road for 3DRealms in its current iteration. Their last four releases have been among the worst games I have ever played, and their management should be ashamed for abusing the talents of their developers. Please make your exit from this field, nobody wants you here, and youve done nothing but damage the careers of promising people, break hearts,  and waste time.P.S. To the texture/3d artists who worked on this game - your work is great, but please try to match texel density in your future endeavors! This has been an issue in wrath, graven, and this game. I understand this likely isn't on purpose, but it is distracting!

_childDocuments_.review: **edit after completing the gameIn the current state I cannot recommend the game.  It is built on a good base but it needs a hell of alot more polishing to get it where it needs to be.  The AI is lackluster, you get stuck on random objects in the world, etc.  I have found a few game breaking bugs in the game.  In the Chicago level if you try to use the upgrade station you will lose all of your upgrades.  If you lose your upgrades and do not have enough upgrade points by the final boss fight it will cause a soft lock and you will not be able to progress to the final boss. The game does have many good points but it just lacks the polish.  This is not to say that I did not enjoy some of the game but I cannot recommend it in it's current condition.  I would hope that 3DR would have learned some things after the previous games it has released (KPR, Wrath, Graven)  But it appears that they have repeated many of the same mistakes.This game stands on its own but it is going to take some work to get it to walk on its own.  I hope that it does not meet the fate of previous releases by 3DR.  One final thing the estimate that the devs gave of 14-15hrs for a single play through is false,  I was able to complete the game on the medium difficulty clocking in 9hrs and 10mins of gameplay. **Edit #2Completed the game on the 3rd run on the hard difficulty taking only 6.5 hrs to complete.  Once you figure out the game mechanics the length of the game decreases greatly. The PR/advertising dept. at 3DR needs to work on marketing to more accurately represent their products.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok well I played phantom fury from begining to end and I have to say it's not bad but not good either. First with what's bad..It's bad in the sense that a lot of the animations and sounds for weapon reloading and character related stuff feels like it's been copied and pasted from half life series and the duke nukem 3d game and another game I can't remember the name of and it's full of so many glitches it's not funny.One glitch for example was when you get to the sewer entrance after escaping the sub base, I got out of the mini sub I was in and all my nanaites and upgrades were gone and I had to start the chapter form the start to get them back. Another glitch that happens frequently is if I accidentally nudge a box on the floor I don't see I go flying backwards across the room taking damage for the landing. There's so many other glitches that I could go on for hours listing and explaining but I wont so i'll leave it at that.I also didn't like there were open areas like the city or the forest that the story led to and left you with no clear path for where to go leaving you searching the map for hours for where to go.Lastly I felt that the difficulty levels being easy, normal and hard have been mixed up because i set it to normal and when I went into the game everything acted as though it was on hard mode because for example I was bearly able to land hits as they moved so much and I also found myself wasting a full clip of ammo sometimes 2 on an enemy that should only need half a clip to kill and also all the new weapons just felt like the same weapons just done up differently making nothing exciting or enjoyable about them so all the extras weren't necessary as it was like I said pretty much the same weapon different look and different ammo.Upgrades for the weapons didn't really change the weapons effectiveness or your suits or arms effectiveness either and most of them remained locked until close to the end so the upgrade system was pointless to have.With the autosave feature I both like it and hate it though i hate it more as there were so many times I was in a good place before a boss fight or tense situation or coming up to an ambush and I couldn't save it and when I died I could load up the checkpoint to be miles from where I was at and have to struggle to get back there.Also a lot of the boss fight arenas were poorly stocked for useful pickups and made the fights close to impossible.Now for what is good...The story was good though a little predictable to me at least, it was nice seeing some old weapons return especially the loverboy revolver which is my favourite. Graphics weren't too bad as it wasn't the cardboard cutout looking graphics of the first one although I like the 3d realms cardboard graphics as i'm a fan of old games and the old style graphics. All in all for a cut paste copy of half life and duke 3D it's a decent game with a good story and decent graphics but it could have been so much better if Slipgate came up with there own graphics and mechanics for it instead of just taking 2 other great games and slapping ion fury on top of it.I still recommend it to play as it's a good story.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game since its announcement, like many others. For me, I got what I wanted. The game was enjoyable and I had a good time with it. I played through it on Hard.The music, when it plays is pretty good. I enjoyed the artstyle and graphics of the game. The environments were fun to explore in. The amount of interactivity, while a nice little distraction at times, and aside from interacting with vending machines and the like in order to eat/drink in order to get some health back, and reading files on computers, everything else provides nothing other then distraction for the curious.The guns were all good. They were all great to use and all of them are essentially overpowered, which I have no issues with. Its up to you whether you want to favor certain weapons or try to use all of them. I generally used mostly all of them in order to get a good value of it all. They also sound great as well. Some people think the guns don't sound "boomy" enough, which I disagree entirely. They don't sound too weak and they don't sound too loud. I don't require guns to blow out my ear drums in order to think they are good. That point of criticism that others have, is stupid, in my opinion, which I have more. The upgrades you can get for some of the guns, while some are good, some are useless have no point in getting. The Assault Rifle's grenade launcher attachment, for example, does EXTREMELY low damage. It explodes into an AOE effect and it can take AGES for things to die.The main point of contention is the AI. I don't understand why some people are pointing out how "bad" the AI is in this game. The AI in majority of boomer shooters is not good, at all, period. They either do 1 of 3 things. Standing in place shoot you, or they strafe and shoot, or they charge you. So, why is it okay for those games to have terrible AI and be praised, but its somehow a crime for this game? The AI in this game is basic. Its nothing special but it gets the job done and they do more then the average boomer shooter. They will either stay far back and shoot you, some in cover and others not. They will try to flank you. Some will charge you. They will also try to get you out of cover by throwing grenades at times. They can do a combination of all those things. They all do different things at different times, and its fine, its just fine. There are some bugs where some will stand still and do nothing and also sometimes the spawning in of enemies bugs out where multiples of enemies spawn on top of eachother, not allowing them to move. I only encountered these types of issues a handful of times and wasn't a problem for me because it did not hinder my progression. If people are expecting FEAR quality AI then what are you even doing playing these types of games?The story is basic and nothing to be amazed at. There are plot holes. There will be times when things make no sense. Things do just happen out of nowhere for very little to no explanation. I found it entertaining but I can see why people have an issue with this games "story".I enjoy this version of Shelly. Shes more dark because of what shes gone through, and lost, and some of the things she says during combat got a chuckle or a smile out of me. She has a bit of a darker sense of humor in her comments, which I do enjoy. I also love Ion Fury's version of Shelly. I love both versions.It took 12 hours for me to finish on Hard. I died a few times here and there on some levels. It did provide a decent challenge. I do recommend this difficulty for anyone wanting to play this game because you get more out of the game and from the AI. All in all, I recommend the game. It has its flaws but its an enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 50/50 on whether or not to recommend this game. I'd maybe recommend picking it up on sale. Is it amazing? No. Is it the worst game ever? Absolutely not. With a few patches I'd say it's a solid 7/10.The developers also faced some pretty big issues with their previous publisher, and I suspect a lot of the problems with Phantom Fury stem from that. That said, it's still a hard game to recommend, but I think after a few patches it will definitely be worth playing at least, especially if you like the late 90s / early 2000s shooters like Halo CE, Unreal 2, C&C Renegade, Red Faction, and the Half-Life expansions.In a nutshell: there are a few very good levels (a missile base, an underground lab, and the final tower level), some boring / bland levels (all of the vehicle levels, the train level), and some downright bad levels (the second last level in the Chicago streets). The guns range from great (the revolver, the shotguns), to average (assault rifle, SMG, rocket launcher) to way over-powered (the bee launcher), to "I never used this after I got it" (the plasma launcher, the "can opener," and a few others I don't want to spoil).A lot of what people are saying about this game is true. It's buggy, at times it feels unfinished, and it's definitely not as good as Ion Fury, but it's far from being the worst game ever. The first few levels are good, but the design starts to take a massive dive towards the end, then an uptick again in the very last level. The story feels wedged in and to be honest I wasn't even sure what the story was until maybe a quarter of the way through. I still don't know why Shelly woke up in a lab.But, what can you expect from a game inspired by the 2001 trailer for DNF. There are moments of genius, like the level that riffs on Resident Evil, and the final tower level is pretty good too.  The Resident Evil level could honestly be expanded into an entire game on its own I think, with a few more enemy types and an inventory system. There's one level with a 'Blood Gulch' kind of aesthetic which felt decent.I think it does a good job of being what Duke Nukem Forever 2001 would have been. It certainly has most of the moments from the trailer. It has a lot of variety, too, and a good amount of interaction.There are some levels that could be half the length (like the Chicago streets level, or the dirt road level), or cut entirely (the underwater level, the helicopter level). There are some later areas that feel outright unfinished, with lamp-posts floating in the air, haphazardly placed enemies that don't react to you consistently, and major glitches that can remove your upgrades and powers. The developers are fixing some of this, but I think some issues will likely never be fixed because the sheer number of issues is overwhelming, and some levels are so large it will be difficult to find and fix the issues without fully rebuilding them. Some of the design choices are also baffling, and I found myself wandering around a lot wondering what the developers wanted me to do, only to find a switch or valve or ladder tucked away out of sight. At other times, it's extremely hand-holdy, and the objective text was almost patronizing.This is a hard game to recommend conclusively, but I think once some of the major issues are fixed, it will be quite a bit better. There are some great, memorable moments, and some truly bad moments that need to be fixed or cut. I'd buy Ion Fury and Aftershock first, then revisit this later when the issues are ironed out, or a director's cut version is released.So, do I recommend this game? Yes, but wait a bit first.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a complicated one. For me I unironically really like Phantom Fury. I went into it expecting a janky “Half-Like,” as they described it and that’s exactly what I got. The level design and art design are top notch. The combat’s serviceable but you can feel that It’s lacking something which keeps it from being something great.The story so far is well…it’s there. Another issue is the more serious tonal shift in Phantom Fury is a bit jarring at first. The game has some truly weird oddities. The music is so low in the mix that you have to turn the master volume up and then lower everything. Shelly’s quips occur sometime at the most random times. It feels like if enemies have alerted to you sometimes she’ll just randomly rattle off a one-liner. Another weird oddity is that the quips don’t seem weapon/enemy sensitive so you’ll kill a droid and she’ll say something the pertains mostly to killing a human. There’s also some weird omissions like no sound for when you climb a ladder or on the upgrade menu no sound plays when you upgrade something. The game launched with some weird key binding bugs too but I haven’t experienced those despite rebinding almost every key. Overall I know it’s really popular to ♥♥♥♥ on Slipgate Ironworks at the moment (rightfully so,) but this title is actually pretty good if your expectations are right. Shelly “Bombshell,” Harrison is a great protagonist and I really hope we continue to see more of her.

_childDocuments_.review: If you look past the bugs and the unfinished parts there is still a prevailing feeling that this game suffers from a identity crisis. On one hand it wants to be Half-Life and on the other it wants to be a boomer shooter. This is very apparent when you look at the beginning of the game where it is very close to Half-Life with slower paced gameplay and the ending where you are jumping around blasting enemies with heavy weaponry.  The problem with that is that the combat for most of the game is dreadful and you lack weapons to take out bigger enemies in a fun way, then when you get proper tools to play it like a boomer shooter it looses the Half-Life identity that it built up in the beginning but at least the combat becomes fun in the last part.Overall the game is pretty mediocre, it has some fun moments but it also has moments where you just want it to end. It's such a shame given how great Ion Fury and Aftershock is. Well, at least it is very pretty to look at for the 11~ hours it will take to finish. (accidentally left it running in the background, hence the inflated playtime)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nowhere close to as good as Ion Fury. Pretty much every aspect of it is a downgrade from Ion Fury. The dialogue, from Shelly and the other characters doesn't have the same impact as Ion Fury. I'm pretty sure that Shelly's voice actor is the same in this game, but she sounds off. There isn't as much emotion. The guns don't feel good and aren't very accurate. They don't sound unique anymore either. There are several gimmick sections that go on too long. There is somehow no map in a boomer shooter type game. So you'll sometimes be walking around aimlessly looking for the next objective. No manual saves so you have to pray to fps Jesus that you don't get stuck on a godawful checkpoint. The worse levels are the ones that have infinitely spawning guys. The worst was the underwater base level where suicide enemies would infinitely re spawn. Now the bugs. Sometimes when you click on an object you get launched into the air. When you reload a checkpoint every item box in the level is re spawned. Once after using the upgrade terminal my view was locked forward and I had no weapon I had to reload. After an underwater section the audio stayed muffled after I left the water. In a section where I needed 2 batteries to open a door, I got the batteries but one mysteriously disappeared until I spammed e on the battery slot and it spawned 3 more in my inventory. The turrets are supposed to be removable, but only 2 worked for me and one of those I couldn't after I had reloaded the checkpoint. This game is not worth your time.

The guns are fun and powerful with each type being useful at various times.  Enemy AI is what you would expect from a late 90s FPS like Duke, Blood, Shadow Warrior, Doom, ECT.  All fine in my book.Some other positives:Enemy variety (ie. vulnerabilities)Sound production is greatLevel design in most areas are fun to explore.  Came across one soft-lock area in a sewer part.Computer terminals are fun to interact withZombie enemies pickup any items within their reach to throw at you!Vehicles drive smoothly.Fun boss fightsCharacter designVoice actingThis isn't a perfect game but for $25 this is an impressive release.  If you can pick this up less than this, it's a steal if you're still reading this.The only thing plaguing this game are the bugs.  One major bug I encountered was after getting off the underwater ski-jet in "Underwater Passage", it left me with no guns and all my equipment upgrades were removed.  My guns were back after going back and getting on the jet-ski, then off again.  Still my perks were gone and auto-saves weren't saving properly as I progressed thru the level.  I ended up going back to the main menu and selecting the "Underwater Passage" level in level select. _childDocuments_.review: I have no idea why this game is on Mixed rating and flew completely under the radar. I was pretty discouraged to play this seeing all the negativity, but it turned out to be great fun.Unlike most retro shooters Phantom Fury does not imitate Doom or Quake, but is inspired by Half-Life games instead. Which is actually pretty original thing to do as I can't think of any game imitating Half-Life so closely. Sure, it cannot compare to all time classic like Half-Life, but I'd say it captured many aspects of its gameplay pretty well. I found shooting to be especially similiar to that of Half-Life 2, it has similiar 'weight' to it. They also included several vehicle and crane sections, to break up the shooty bits. Level of environmental interaction and physicality of the world also bring HL2 to mind. Phantom Fury is a rather linear shooter with many action packed set pieces and less of a focus on secret hunting. Its actually pretty refreshing considering most retro shooters bombard you with dozens of secrets per level and finding them is not my strongest suit. Other than one slower horror-ish section (not a good one) its a 9 hour adrenaline rush and I did it basically in one sitting, I was having so much fun with it.Its a looker too, despite the pixelated assets and textures there is a lot of detail and a strong artstyle throughout. Animations are buttery smooth and many objects can be destroyed or thrown. On the other hand audio part of the game is a bit middling and none of the tunes really caught my attention.There are some problems though. AI is very basic and gets stuck on environment sometimes. I encountered some buggy graphical effects and some maps had a bit 'unfinished' corners. Also its easy to get lost sometimes not knowing what to do to progress, it doesn't do a good job of subtly leading the player despite its linearity. I never got stuck for long though. Enemy variety could be better, they are a bit samey and the zombie enemies are annoying as sh!t, especially in levels that keep on spawning them. Fortunately none of these problems were able to ruin my fun with Phantom Fury.Overall Phantom Fury is an easy recommendation for any fan of single player shooters and especially Half-Life games. Sure there is not a single original idea in this whole game, but so what. I don't need my shooters to be original, just fun action romps to unwind. I feel sorry for the devs, they receive so much hate even before this game released, even though they did a great job with Phantom Fury and deserve much more recognition for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy - what a masterpiece. The negative reviews are a bit confusing tho - my guess is that they mostly come from a younger audience that has a certain idea of what a game from the early 2000's must be like, but has not experienced that era first hand. I really can't find a different explanation - the game is very close to perfection. Perfection in this context meaning that it does what it suppose to do in the best way possible. If that game would have come out in 2001 it would have been on the cover of every major gaming magazine.  Phantom Fury is not only a worthy sequel to Ion Fury - it's an absolute blast and one of the better FPS of the past 20 years. It is obvious that the people who made this game really understood what shooters in that era where really about. Especially the later part of the game in Chicago is so perfectly designed, where the world itself tells you a story. I really hope there will be a DLC like Aftershock for this game - I haven't had such a good time in..well a long time.  On the negative side, the design of some areas is confusing. It's not always clear where the path to follow is - especially in the subnautic level. This could have been done better. But if you love honest, down to earth FPS without unecassary RPG elements - knock yourself out. You'll love this one. It's a reminder of how good games used to be. I just hope this won't be the last we've seen of Shelly Harrison.

But here's the kicker: I play it on my Steam Deck. Game works just fine. But the default config is basically unplayable. There is so little health spread around the levels that I am constantly at 15 health trying to stay alive. Enemies swarm you and instakill you, even on easy. When I finally have my aim on them I am dead. Sodas give 1. ONE! health. It's so dumb! Other items give equally little, so you'll end up just dying again and again and again. And there's nothing you can do about it.Enable autoaim? Broken, doesn't work on Steam Deck. Does absolutely nothing. Enable gyro precision aiming through the Steam menus? This works well, but only makes it slighly easier. I still die all the time. Using the gyros should be part of the default config. Why isn't it?Weapons reloads are excrutiatingly slow for a game this fastpaced.I want to love this game. It looks fantastic and it could be a fun game on the Deck. But currently it's basically impossible to play. Not recommended on Deck.Things that need fixing:- Make gyro aiming part of the default config (Deck specific)- Make aim assist actually work for those who want it (Controller and Deck specific)- Make health less grindy (General problem)- Make enemies less precise when aiming at you (Might be less of a problem on PC with precision mouse aiming)

I'd already asked other's opinions and despite the warnings, I still went ahead and bought it because I loved Ion Fury so much.Like others in this comment section, I was somewhat shocked and disappointed with the amount of bugs, the jankiness of simple things like picking up items being awkward, getting stuck a lot in places, being flung across the map by a random item... I even found an area towards the end city level with what looked like unfinished texture. However, I was exploring on purpose for secrets. So I did it to myself.Despite all of this, I love the story, I felt the need to finish the game and I was hooked!Is it perfect? Nope. Are other games in this genre, though?I can see where the passion was in this game development. All the little details, all the secrets, the beautiful art direction... As long as it continues to get patched and the creases get ironed out, I think the scores for this game will improve. Can I recommend this game? Yes. But with all the warnings from all the other comments. Take it for what it is and roll with it. Just enjoy the game and if you get stuck, try jumping and crouching to get out. That's how I made my way out of many places. Good luck, Shelly fans. And have fun!Side note; last night I started my second playthrough. So I can't be that bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I didn't grow up with the original "boomer shooters." I got my first PC running Windows 95 in 1996 with which I played SimCity 3000 and X-Wing Alliance. Due to life circumstances, I stopped playing games on PC before games like Half-Life and Deus Ex came out, both of which would have run much better on a more powerful computer than the one that I had when Half-Life and Deus Ex were released. /End of disclaimerI'm really enjoying Phantom Fury. I'm nearly up to the Grand Canyon stage. I'm enjoying Phantom Fury a lot more than I enjoyed Ion Fury. I agree that it can be difficult to know where to go and what to do in-game. I don't mind, though. I don't know if the flares in the missile testing range stage were added in post-release patches or not, but they helped.Another concern that people have is the AI. Yeah, the enemies aren't especially good at hunting you down. I don't see the AI as much different than the AI is in Ion Fury, and I don't know if people expect that.I don't even know what "gunplay" is, so I'll skip that. As for the story, though, I don't play these kinds of games for the stories. However, I haven't seen a mention that Shelly was in a coma or stasis within the game when that was all over the marketing material. Additionally, the Colonel tells you to find the Demon Core in the driving stage that follows the train stage. This is done before you learn anything about the Demon Core.Despite these flaws, I'm greatly enjoying my time playing this game. I have difficulty with most "modern" 3D games where the characters interact with each other in cutscenes. I experienced these difficulties playing Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered and Hi-Fi Rush. I've been facing no such difficulties with Phantom Fury. I've been enthralled and I'm eager to see what's next in-game!Edit: I wanted to address the crazy ragdoll physics that often take place in-game. I just assume that the crazy ragdoll physics are a part of the meta-commentary.Edit 2: Regarding the game's lack of a manual save feature and reliance on checkpoints instead, I don't mind. It true that it makes things a little bit more annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: It was pretty decent, although obviously not as good as Ion Fury.I think we were all expecting this to be an attempt to try to release Duke Nukem Forever the 2001 version (without the Duke Nukem IP obviously) and although it takes a lot of elements from that, it also takes elements from other games of the era, such as half life.So while Ion Fury is mostly fast paced, with the cyberpunk and build engine aesthetics, Phantom Fury on the other hand is a lot more slow paced, and has a very dark and half life type of aesthetic.Some of the cons of the game are:- Some of the aspects of the game feel a little janky (such as the punch attack for instance) although I think a lot of people really exaggerate the jankyness of the game as if it's completely unplayable.- It's not always clear where you have to go (especially for new players who don't want to read the entire story) and they could have done a better job highlighting the consoles as distinct from ordinary computers, or highlight the area where a key is located, for a key is a very small item that is not always sticking out, especially in a dark room (which is like 75% of the game). This in turn makes people waste more time than is necessary to advance in the game.- For some reason drones on this game feel a lot more annoying than they do on Ion Fury, they just have very weird patterns where sometimes they just go away and come back some time later, or they come straight towards you. While on Ion Fury I enjoy facing the drones a lot more.- I think overall the aesthetics are less appealing than both Ion Fury and Duke Nukem Forever 2001, even though the latter also has a lot of dark aesthetics, it manages to combine them with the goofyness of the casino.Some of the pros of the game are:- Some weapons (such as the loverboy) just feel a lot more powerful (even though you have much less ammo and significantly reduced clip size)- You have a lot more weapons than Ion Fury and a whole bunch of upgradesAll in all it's pretty decent, even though I didn't expect it to be able to compete with Ion Fury (as I am just a huge fan of the build engine aesthetic as well as cyberpunk aesthetics) I think the game would have been better had it tried to stick closely to Duke Nukem Forever 2001 and tried less to combine it with stuff from other games, also made it easier to spot their objectives and stuff for new players and fixed some of the jankyness.So I would recommend it, I just wouldn't go in expecting it to either be like Ion Fury, or like Duke Nukem Forever 2001, and if you are impatient and don't like to read through the story you will feel fustrated at times not knowing where to go since it's not always clear.

_childDocuments_.review: (Mixed Review)I really enjoyed playing through Phantom Fury. Despite its flaws and lack of polish and refinement in some areas. I can say it is a decent playthrough. I had not experienced too many bugs, only really a tank in frame rate every now and again. Shooting feels good and all the weapons are fun to use. I really enjoyed the visual style and games music. The story was a decent scenario for the game, nothing groundbreaking but was a good excuse for the gameplay. Valerie Arem again does an amazing job as Shelly "Bombshell" Harrison and displays a great range of emotion for the character.  The game took me about 15-16 hours to play through first time through so its a decent length.  My GripesI found the balancing in some areas to be a bit unbalanced and cheap at times. Some levels are really cryptic on where to go and require tons of walking around just trying to figure out where to head to next. I found the enemy variety leaving a bit more to be desired as by the end there really isn't that much variety in combat encounters.Overall I feel that this is definitely the best game Slipgate Ironworks has made by themselves (Way way better then Graven!). I do not agree with 3D Realms philosophy of screwing over their developers and sending out half baked products to the public using nostalgia as bait. I also do not agree with 3D Realms bashing reviewers for giving there honest take on these products. 3D Realms really needs to sort themselves quick in my book, otherwise they can say goodbye to everyone and fade back out of existence.
