_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun adventure. It reminds me of a lot of PS2 era games: Timesplitter, Killzone, project snowblind, the James Bond games, half life 2. You get in many situations: run and gun, puzzles, driving sections...At launch, the game is a bit buggy. Hopefully this will be fixed.It's an OK game, it's not the next Half-Life, nothing will ever be. But the price is correct, I enjoyed my time with it. I'm looking forward to replay it after a few patches.Maps: Most maps are good, they look nice and have a variety of vistas. In a game like that the maps are the most important part. Some maps have unique gimmicks and puzzles, it gives them personality. There are however one or two maps that are a bit less well developped and confusing (the chicago streets were weird, I wasn't sure what I was doing).Guns: they feel great, with the gibbing and their reactions of the enemies you really get a good feedback. There's a large amount of weapons in the game.Enemies: the AI could be better. it works well in arenas were the enemies can easily reach covers. In tighter sections however, the enemies tend to run around, I feel they try to take cover from you. The issue is that they may run next to you to get somewhere. I think the AI should not zip around the map so quickly (most enemies are too fast) and if they are caught in the open they should opt more often for shooting at you, kneeling or stuff like that (like they do in Goldeneye 007).Story: the story is a bit weird, it's the convoluted nonsense you can find in a bonker 80 b movie. There is a part of the story that delve a bit on Shelly's past, I really like that, most modern games lack earnestness and sincerity, I like that she's not just are psycho killing machine. I wish the story in general was way simpler and more personal for Shelly. [STOP READING IF YOU WANT TO AVOID SPOILER] I think the antagonist should have been the bad guy from the start, no twist: Shelly has to retrieve the demon core from the claws of mister bad guy. The demon core is her grand-father sin and it's her duty to atone for his sins by saving the world. Most of the story beats could have stayed the same. The stakes would have been clear from the start, and Shelly's involvement would have been less random.I hope we get some more games with Shelly in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Only a few levels in, but really enjoying the game so far. Well worth it at the budget-level asking price. At times, it's really reminiscent of mid-to-late 90's, 3dfx-era shooters like Unreal, Half-Life, Shogo, SiN, Daikatana, etc. This is my jam. I spent my senior year of high school playing the Heretic shareware episode over and over because I couldn't afford the full game. Quake II is still one of my fav shooters of all time. I have a modest collection of old PC hardware (described in my profile) that I still use to play games, and this feels like it would fit right in.All that said, Phantom Fury also brings its own vibe. It's not those other games, and it doesn't need to be. I dig the mix of modern visual effects (e.g., lighting, post-processing) and retro-inspired textures and models. The characters and their voices are fun. The devs managed a sufficient compromise between modern polish and old-school jank in the feel of movement, level traversal, and combat. I get what they were going for, and I think they pulled it off pretty well.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a bit of fun with the game, it wasn't all bad. I can understand why some people liked it, but I understand the people who hated it so much more. There is a sense of bugginess and junkiness throughout the whole game, I cannot possibly recommend it to anyone. It's about 12 hours long and unless you've played most other similar shooters, you can do better.Took me 0 seconds to get stuck, and after dealing with that bug, it took me 5 more to be stopped by another bug. Those numbers are exact btw. Then I proceeded to clip to my death through an elevator more than 10 times in a row, until I finally didn't. After that I did get stuck in the geometry, clipped through textures, weapons upgrades stopped working, a traffic cone launched me umpteen meters in the air and out of bounds, but nothing too crazy a reload or something couldn't fix. I've seen plenty of save-ruining bugs, but most you can circumvent by restarting the last level from the main menu. This is not as bad as Graven, you will not get hardlocked cause you sneezed during a loading screen. Still, you better hold it.Enemies are split in two types, zombies and non-zombies. They are not zombies, but whatever. Most enemies and their AI sucks, though it doesn't make them easy to deal with. Non-zombies are running in a straight line or zig-zagging towards you, or running around like headless chickens all while they are accurately shooting at you, it's a pain. It's also very silly and rather annoying. I don't think they are hitscanners, but if you are standing still they never seem to miss either, at least on hard. It's like they are hitscanning you, but their recticle is slower than your speed, so if you are side stepping they can't hit you, assuming there is some distance between you. You are circling around, they are training for the 100 meter dash, good luck going for them headshots. Zombies are better, cause this AI makes more sense and more weapons are useful against them. The soldiers are way more.Even a lot of the game's strongest critics seem to praises the weapons. Overall, I did not like them. Maybe they are good in theory, or in a vacuum, but with this combat I found 2/3 to be useless, redundant, or very situational. Same thing with the upgrades. You have Loverboy, an 18 barrel magnum, firing 3 bullets with each shot. Its alt-fire marks up to 3 targets and shoots them up to 2 times on the head. By far the most useful weapon in the game, never runs out of bullets and elevates the combat from horrible to almost decent. I regularly used 3 more weapons, 4 if I am being generous, and that is not counting upgrades, some of which change the weapon completely. For the top of my mind, there are like 17 weapons in this game. I am not saying all the others are useless, but why use them when you get much better results and take way less damage using, for example, Loverboy. You may be thinking it's not a big deal, 5 useful weapons is good enough and you can ignore the rest. Introducing weapon categories. That would be the college most guns went and graduated from "useless" to "in the way".Can't stress enough how much I hate weapon categories. It's exactly as it sounds, weapons are grouped together under the same keybind. You can't bind guns separately, you have to deal with this. You can't even cycle through weapons in the same category, nooo, that would be too convenient. Each weapon is bound to a certain number of presses. Doesn't matter weather you are holding the 3rd weapon of a category and you want to switch to the 4th. A tanky enemy is charging at you and you want to switch to your railgun, better press the key 4 times. Oh, you pressed it 3 times by mistake. Is the weapon's list still visible on your HUD, cause then there is still time for a 4th press. If not, then you need 4 more, so you better pay attention. It is a very realistic representation of trying to draw a certain weapon, while holding 17.Finally, the level design and signposting. It's a very linear game, so we are not getting permanently stuck, we are talking about constantly losing a couple of minutes trying to find the way forward. At times it almost feels like the devs are trolling you. It goes beyond poor signposting, it's often counter-intuitive. I'll talk about some of the easiest to describe cases:1) You interact with a computer and learn the Storage code. You then reach a corridor. On the right there is a broken door saying "Storage" and on the left an explosion sends a body through the glass and leaves a hole right above some barrels. Well, the room on the left is useless. It has another computer with the code inside, but that is pointless since you already got that. What you need to do is enter the code and the broken door opens. Bruh, what's up with the double misdirection? Just remove the first computer and fix the door. That's the tutorial btw.2) On your right, a narrow street guarded by a sniper, something the game has told you to avoid a gazillion times. On your left, a trapdoor you open with a valve, a valve you pick up and install. There is absolutely nothing to do down there, it's pointless. Just yolo the road.3) You've punched a cart and used it open the way. You've punched a whole wagon, twice, to get it out of the way. Now you are stopped by two wooden planks at the end of broken rails. There is a wagon 5 feet away, this time lit green. Why are you trying to punch it you moron, jump in, fly in the air and comically crash-land face first. They know and you know they know, cause at some point the objective stealthily changed from "Reach somewhere" to "Climb in the wagon". Was it not for that, I may still be there, not climbing on the wagon on the rails which end in 5 feet.4) You want to open a bunker door. You enter a building and turn on the power, the lights turn on, but that's it. The door is still closed, no levers to pull, no buttons to press. It's important to note here that every computer you interact with is the same computer, same colour and turned on. Introducing the only turned off, differently shaped computer, which only light up when you use it. Not even on a central location, simply on a table in some corner. Keep in mind someone went out of their way to do that.5) You fight a helicopter on some interconnected platforms at the side of a building, or dam. After killing it, I check all the doors on the right, nowhere to go. I check the ones on the left, nada. As I make my way back to where I started from, a different helicopter spawns and drops enemies. After killing those, nothing else happens and I've been everywhere. Haven't been everywhere twice though. One of the doors I had already checked had opened for no discernible reason. The area is pretty large, copy pasted and with huge pillars between the platforms. It's not at all clear from afar and a previously closed door has opened.There were so many such cases. Constantly wasting a couple of minute for no reason kills the game's pacing.Special mentions to: Not making any sound when jumping into water. Swimming as slowly as the engine allows, avoid at all costs. A driving section, where it's often better to leave the car and shoot the enemies yourself. A flying section, where you have no control over the helicopter and your "homing" missiles are drunk. An underwater section, where your submarine is drunk. Your explosives having very small blast radius, which doesn't match with the visuals. A maze level where the forcefields blocking your way change 3 times, while enemies are endlessly spawning knowing your exact location and being able to walk through said forcefields. Your homing grenades doing whatever 1/3 of the times. Oh, and a special mention to the writing, hahaha... the writing.And then we have the glass tankers full of water. When you shoot them they start leaking and the water level slowly drops, but only until it reaches the bullet hole. How did that one random object go so much more attention that the rest?

name: Yurukill: The Calumniation Games
detailed_description: Pardon or kill. Let the madness begin! At the edge of despair, lurks the unsettling past, and an unspeakable truth. What lies hidden in the twisted attractions of the secluded amusement park, Yurukill Land? Who will emerge victorious from its cruel, fiendish games? Clear Your Name: Take on the nerfarious attractions of Yurukill Land for a chance to prove your innocence. Partner up with your Executioner and set your sights on emerging victorius from the Yurukill Games. For the victors, absolution awaits. Risk Your Life: Solve puzzles and uncover hints about the crimes you stand accused of, and put it all on the line in Maji-Kill Time—tense life or death cross-examinations. One wrong answer, and all is lost. As you progress, the grim truths of each incident will come to light. Take to the (Virtual) Skies: Pilot your Yurukill Fighter through a series of virtual reality challenges. Put your understanding of each case to the test in High-Speed Quizzes: choose the correct lane, and you'll be rewarded with extra lives. In the Prejudice Synapse, present evidence from your investigations, and destroy your Executioner's prejudices. Each top-down shoot ‘em up section (courtesy of veteran developer G.rev!) ends with a nail-biting Prisoner vs Executioner showdown. Whether you're a shoot 'em up expert or newcomer to the genre, find the perfect challenge to suit your level with a choice of Easy, Normal, and Hell difficulties. Run the Gauntlet: Choose your craft, set the difficulty, buckle up, and blast through shoot 'em up sections from the main game in Score Attack mode. Features global online rankings. Original Story / Scenario: Homura Kawamoto / Hikaru Muno Director / Producer: Shinsuke Umeda Character Design: Hiro Kiyohara Soundtrack: Yuko Komiyama Shoot ‘em up development: G.rev *For players wishing to use a Nintendo Switch Pro Controller: Access the Steam Controller Settings menu and enable 'Switch Pro Configuration Support,' then disable 'Use Nintendo Button Layout.' If a Nintendo Switch Pro Controller is connected via cable while 'Disable Steam Input' is active in the game's controller settings, the controller will not function properly. *Internet connection required for online ranking. ・Nintendo Switch is a trademark of Nintendo.

_childDocuments_.review: A mash up of a detective, danganronpa like visual novel with a shoot em up section. It's a mix of eccentric humour and a death game like setting. I think that if you liked danganronpa you would like this as well. This game also reminded me of a lesser known game that didn't sell that well called Gachitora. In that game you are a teacher who solves students' problem by going in their mind and "beating" them. This has a similar section.Has an interesting mix of eccentric characters with famous voice actors playing them. Some notable actors that I recognized are Sugita Tomokazu (gintama) and Kobayashi Yuu (Sachan in gintama and Sasha in Attack on Titan). They play their characters really well.Characters are paired up and come to term with various crimes they were involved with. In short, you learn about both characters as you go through the story. The shoot em up part of the game is kind of like the trial in danganronpa as it serves as a way for you to find a solution to the dilemma the characters find themselves in. The demo takes you through one such story and should give you an idea about the gameplay loop. Think of the shoot em up part of the game as the repeatable part once you know the story. It can be played independently for extra challenges as you unlock characters and stages through story mode. Each character has a different aircraft that has its own quirks. _childDocuments_.review: This game is mid. Overall, the individual aspects are pretty much watered down versions of other games within the genre. It features a budget Zero Escape style death game and escape rooms but without all the interesting thought experiments and actual puzzles. Many of the mystery and minigame elements are like Danganronpa but without all the fun and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Hell, Binko is basically funny female Monokuma. If there is one thing they really focused on, that would be the voice acting; every single line in this game, even the inconsequential flavor text happens to have voice lines. I must concede that the voice acting was executed to great effect.As a shmup nerd, the fact that a new shmup made by G.REV was included as a main element of the game was a main selling point. On the whole, the shmup sections were quite well designed, with a lot of emphasis on making a unique hybrid of horizontal and vertical, with many bosses having relatively innovative attack patterns that require the player to do a lot of problem solving, routing, and overall not sitting at the bottom of the screen. (I cleared the game on HELL, requiring at least 15 retries, all told). The scoring system leaves much to be desired, but it's clear that G.REV at least knew what they were doing.However, I feel that this game was also quite rushed. There are clear instances where I could tell the devs wanted to do something like insert a CG to illustrate an event, but simply showed a white flash since there was no art to show. There were some extremely scuffed animations and some of the renderings looked generally low-effort, but I think this was just due to a lack of time or budget - you gotta take your time with this stuff! But I still don't think it would totally solve the ultimately predictable plot line.Adding to the rushed point, the one big blemish of the shmup sections is Stage 6. Why in the hell does stage 6 exist????? It has the most ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and unplayable patterns in the game, to the point where the final attack is simply unroutable, completely murdering my chances of going for a proper HELL 1cc. (Stage 7 is completely balanced.) The background is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ static image - seriously? It's a complete embarrassment compared to the well-made visuals of LITERALLY every other stage. It doesn't add anything, since it's a boss rush which reappropriates old patterns. The game doesn't need it to fill the time, a full run is already an hour long without it. Hell, even the accompanying story is pretty unnecessary - you could remove it and the plot would be still coherent. What the hell were they thinking with that one...Anyways yeah. TL;DR: Rushed game, shmup good, remove stage 6 you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bastards

_childDocuments_.review: After thoroughly playing the game, from start to finishthe story mode on hell difficulty (1st playthrough), i can only recommend thisgame to everyone who likes visual novels, shoot em ups and puzzlesbecause this game has it all, and the way the developers merged all these genres togetherinto how many lives you can have at the start of the shoot em up stages is done masterfully.The game truly shines when you are playing this on hell difficulty because all of your decisions be it success or failures will put you on the edge ofyour seat knowing you need all the help you can get, to get through hell difficulty, in the story mode you get 10 lives per stage to clear it, each lower difficulty adds 10 more lives.That being said for the hardcore shmup fans...You unlock score attack mode after finishing 6 chapters of story mode.Score attack has additional phases that need to be cleared vs story mode making itmore punishing, also score attack doesn't have any of the dialogues story mode has its pure stg, for good reasons of course (also hell gives you 5 lives, with each stage having1ups hidden for you to collect while attempting 1cc's and or high score runs).It's classic g rev with score multipliers when using your outburst shot,it has bullet cancelling, it has a ranking system meaning the game can dynamically increase the difficulty slightly morebased on how well you perform.Also pretty challenging and a healthy variety of bullet patterns, sometimes evenmultiple to keep track off at the same time, both in size and speed mixed with different trajectories makes for some frantic maneuvering. You can select which ship you want to use, each with different strengths and weaknesses.I've enjoyed all of the boss designs and mechanics the same goes for the stages,but the true last boss does have a few minor complaints i won't spoil much about itbut it does has some very hard to see patterns that hide behind other largerbullet patterns that can cause unintentional deaths, would've preferred them to bemore visible.Overall the cast is likeable except for wu wu wu wu wu wu,Before this game came out Elden Ring (300 hr, 7 fresh playthroughs) was my GOTY so far in 2022.. but after experiencing Yurukill this has become my GOTY, and i doubt anyother game releasing this year will be able to trump it both in terms of enjoymentand the hefty challenge it presented, it stands above anything else i've seen so far this year.I have yet to scratch the surface of score attack mode as i plan to atleast 1cc it on hell, so there is still so much time to invest into the game for me personally.Very underrated and misunderstood game. I highly recommended Yurukill: the calumniation games 9/10 excellent game!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I enjoyed it despite the flaws I named but I can't recommend it at full price. Too much VN in my Shmup :)Just finished it annnnnnd....If you want a mediocre/terrible story and questionable puzzles wrapped up in some genuinely nice presentation despite the obviously mid-ish budget... that gets in the way of what appears to be a decent if not earth shatteringly innovative shmup by G-Rev....Then Yurukill: The Hallouminati is the game for you!I was gifted this by a friend but if I had to pay £35 for this I would have been dissapointed. I would have rather paid £6-10 for the Shmup Section by itself (See Sol Cresta... though I don't like that game I applaud the idea of removing the story and making it optional DLC)The Score Attack Mode will definitely give Shmup Enthusiasts a new challenge for themselves, but having to sit through 8-10 hours of VN to get it might not be their thing. Maybe there is a code to unlock the shmup section from the beginning?I'm also more in the shmup side of things so I'd would have rather just seen all the effort being put into that portion. On the plus side....I am super glad that they managed to pull this off as it is definitely unique. Risks being taken in game design is a plus!Some very memorable and entertaining Voice Acting for Binko!Nice Soundtrack!Matrix Style visuals for pick ups in the shmup mode is a great touch!I will disclose that I am in my mid-thirties and this kind of fiction isn't my thing, but arcade action and gameplay is. I finished the game within 8-9 hours and I was skipping a lot of the dialogue as a lot of it isn't interesting, or was redundant.  Also, I have played the Zero Escape trilogy and they do the VN thing way better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: Renowned author Homura Kawamoto delivers a twisted, multifaceted story in Yurukill. Accused of arson and the murders of 21 people, protagonist Sengoku Shunju is forced to fight for his freedom and prove his innocence. As one of six Prisoners, he must pair up with one of five victims, referred to as Executioners, within the confines of the strange and secluded amusement park known as Yurukill Land. Together each of the five teams—Mass Murderers, Death Dealing Duo, Crafty Killers, Sly Stalkers, and Peeping Toms—must face and overcome the entertainment venue's so-called "attractions" in order to attain what they desire. Should the Prisoners succeed, their crimes shall be pardoned. But if the Executioners win, they will be granted revenge for their loved ones. The in-depth story offers unique gameplay experiences including collating evidence, gathering testimonies, and solving puzzles.Yurukill’s shoot-‘em-up gameplay developed by veteran developer G.rev features action packed and fast-paced combat. In addition, online leaderboards give players the opportunity to see how they stack up against the competition.

name: Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX 2
detailed_description: Break into the new apeX of 2D action! Luminous Avenger iX 2 takes the series' original speedy and stylish 2D action gameplay to the next level as Copen rips through enemies with his new 'Break-Shift' form. His new destructive capabilities makes the high-speed action more satisfying than ever! INTI CREATES is proud to present new apeX of cutting-edge 2D action with Luminous Avenger iX 2! ●2D action that breaks new ground! With his new spinning blade weapon, the Razor Wheel, Copen rips through any enemy standing in his way as he traverses an enormous tower. A wide variety of stages with powerful boss characters lurking in them await him. Copen earns a new EX Weapon for his arsenal whenever he defeats a boss. He uses these weapons to target enemies' weak points to bring them down faster; a key strategy to clearing stages and ascending the tower quickly. Copen's Bullit Dash that allows him to fly freely through the air has also been powered up! Super-stylish maneuvers reward those who master the Bullit Dash's high-speed capabilities! ●Tear through your enemies at break-neck speed! Copen takes on all challenges by changing seamlessly between his two forms: the power-focused 'Break-Shift' and the speed-enhanced 'Bullit-Shift.' Crush your enemies in Break-Shift to bank points and activate Overdrive! In Overdrive, Copen can stay in Bullit-Shift mode longer, allowing him to zip through the air at high speed. ●The 'Muse of Hope' Lola is lovelier than ever! Her songs really light up the stage! When Copen's HP hits 0, Lola can transform and activate her Anthem skill to bring Copen back to life using the power of song. She brings that recovery power to the frontlines in Luminous Avenger iX 2 with her newest and cutest form yet: Healing Mode! This powerful new ability heals Copen to full HP at any time, anywhere, and as often as he likes...with no cost! Build up over 1000 Kudos points and Lola will really heat up the battle with her song! ●An intense standalone story! Luminous Avenger iX 2 is set in a parallel world where a dystopic story unfolds in a ruined desert wasteland where only robots exist. Characters both familiar and new come together for this exciting story, featuring English voiceover for the very first time in the entire Gunvolt series! English Voiceover Cast Copen: Alejandro Saab Lola: Cassandra Lee Morris Kohaku: Kira Buckland Null: Natalie Rose Hoover Dacite: Connor Colquhoun Vespa: Brittany Cox Autochrome: Daman Mills Brigade: Steve 'Warky' Nunez Hail: Jennifer Losi Ace: Arin Hanson Narrator: Matt Papa Japanese Voiceover Cast Copen: Yuma Uchida Lola: Mayu Mineda Kohaku: Yumiri Hanamori Null: Sumire Morohoshi Dacite: Shunsuke Todo Vespa: Akane Fujita Autochrome: Takuya Sato Brigade: Yoshitaka Yamaya Hail: Akira Sekine Ace: Makoto Furukawa Narrator: Takahiro Kageyama

_childDocuments_.review: Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX2 is quite a controversial title, and that's putting it very mildly. Plenty of people are severely disappointed, others think the game is great, so I figured I'd leave my thoughts here, with the least bias possible.Alright, story. iX1 was already not as strong as the mainline games, but overall, the plot worked (plus the iX games are more of action games, so the story took a backseat). iX2, however, is such a mess I'm appalled that the writer for the beautifully made GV1 and GV2 and even iX1 created this "fanfic", honestly. Copen finds a Blaster Rifle by chance, gets sucked into an alternate world with his crew and has to fight his way upwards in the Grave Pillar. The plot takes a huge dive in the endgame and it's arguably the worst of all 4 games by a long shot.Gameplay doesn't fare super well, either. People who're expecting to play the same Copen as iX1 and GV2 are mostly in for a disappointment, because you can't whoosh your way through the stages anymore. Gotta earn 1000 Kudos and enter Overdrive with just one non-reloadable dash, and even then, you have a Bullit gauge that, while it gives you infinite dashes instead of just 3, the meter depletes fast and can be only refilled by bouncing off enemies or terrain. To reach OD, you have a new melee weapon that honestly is one of the worst gimmicks I've had the chance to play around with. Not a single enemy can be killed with a slash, three-hit combo only deals 12 HP, and the hold wheel after that stops you in your tracks, but continuously does mediocre damage. The weapon is practically useless on bosses, with two of them being exceptions.Taking a break from negativity for a bit, I really admire the sound and graphics team's work. Stages look nothing short of gorgeous, making this game have the best presentation so far. Soundtrack is pretty diverse, as usual, and I think even picky choosers will find a favorite of theirs or two. Though I must say, Lola's songs aren't quite as likable as in iX1, and this doesn't seem to be the sentiment only I express, as I've heard similar opinions (I imagine it has to do with the songs not having their usual 150 BPM, like all the other games). Result screens for missions look even flashier than before, so it feels really good to boast of your X Ranks to people (yes, X Ranks, not S+...).…And we're back to drawbacks. When I say this game is a buggy mess, I truly mean it. I avoided the nastiest ones during my blind run, but managed to get a few stinkers (invisible walls in the middle of a stage, enemies not getting stunned from the Razor Wheel, bosses messing with the arena geometry, etc.). It speaks volumes of how the game was very rushed, and I truly think that could've been better with maybe a year more of dev time.Hard Mode came back from its long hiatus and players got to experience it in iX2. I like the concept and most of the mode, but I *detest* how players are forced to do Hard Mode to see the continuation of the story and the true ending, especially because the changed aspects, namely ridiculous nerfs and super buffed bosses, will make for a rough time. But you know what's the worst offender? Lives. Lives in a freaking Gunvolt game. That single-handedly ruined the experience of this mode when I did it the first time. It doesn't help that the continuation of the story barely does anything substantial and doesn't really wrap up the many mysteries players would be curious to see unveiled. So much for making your games accessible, right, Inti…?And the last topic: price. Dear god, where do I even begin… The price increase from $15 to $25 is for the wrong reasons. We have 3D Lola music videos (which are good, don’t get me wrong), we have an English Dub that doesn’t suck as much as the other Inti game that had it, but again, I would’ve rather seen more content in the actual game to justify the price hike. For $25, you get roughly *8 stages*, while the other games offered 14 (albeit some of them were “remixes”). As someone who’s a diehard GV fan and a Score Runner, I got my fill around 80% with 90 hours spent in the game, but casuals will clear the game in 3-4 hours and probably won’t go for replayability, which is the defining point of the games. One more thing to mention is DLC: this game has 4 VS Missions against crossover characters currently, but guess how much they cost? Three of them are a whopping $8 (fourth one is $4, but for the wrong reasons). Jesus, that’s a third of the game’s price, and you’re telling me a 2 minute fight + mediocre reward are worth it? Buzz off, Inti, this is a huge freaking scam, especially when you’ve done much better DLC for past games, some of them underpriced, I dare say (like BMZ extra characters, which are only $2 each).To conclude, this game is a dark curtain on Inti’s otherwise pristine reputation. iX2 took one step forward, but *three* steps back. Marketing is such a joke I legit want to punch through a wall in anger. With all due respect, I suggest you avoid picking up this title unless you’re super eager to play as Copen, even despite the changes I’ve talked about. I think the game is more or less worth it if you can get it at half the price (which is probably what Inti will do when GV3 release week is near, just like how iX2 did it). Overall, in terms of rating, it’s a B Rank from me, or 6/10.Thanks for taking your time reading through this. I really appreciate it.

Before this, each title in the series have some same problems also, like short react time and attacks' visibility due to same saturation and brightness of the dot sprites; but this time things get even worse when Copen's lock attack spawns too many effects which covers everything(including enemies' bullets) and force you into a hardcore mode with feature-removed controls.Too many design are just not catch-up the current era.  Some may say "practice yourself before criticize about the difficulty", but sorry you should have a fair design (or even say "fun enough gameplay") first, then your game is worth to practice.In Inti's RMZ series (at GBA) I've practice and got All S and actually had fun; in GV series it's still good enough, but it's just not as so in this(iX2). I'd rather trying no damage in something like Sekiro or souls or got high rank in bayonetta, not trying figure out which sprite is enemies' attack in tons of player's attack effect and Rola's 8 pieces flying around, lost my character in sight after every damage or even after dash, while air dash uses different mechanism form ground with no leeway design so due to a near frame a jump input can lead to many results (ok ok player skill, still a very miss-able design compare to other games like Celeste), AND with all of above, running in a HARD mode, each 3 retry wastes a whole level's play time.So I can't recommend it.Btw developers can you guys add an option just VANISH THE VISUAL of Copen's lockon attacks? _childDocuments_.review: They took something that worked and made it worse.If you're coming into this from Gunvolt 2 or Luminous Avenger iX, you will immediately attempt to multi-dash, only to wonder why it doesn't work. Eventually you may note there's no Bullits in this game, despite dashing still being called Bullit Dashing. What this means is that you can no longer multi-dash at all outside of Overdrive mode, removing a core feature of Copen's gameplay: speed and bouncing around from enemy to enemy. "Oh but it's easy to get into Overdrive," no, for casual players it won't be, especially since checkpoints reset your kudos.They also gave Copen a 3-part melee combo meant to evoke Zero from Mega Man X/Zero. However, the combo can only be used when standing still, you cannot walk/run and combo, making it a strictly worse and functionally unusable way to kill enemies. It looks cool, but you'll never be using it practically over any other option you have.Though everything else about this game so far is amazing, I cannot recommend this game over Gunvolt 2 or Luminous Avenger iX due to the unnecessary change to dashing/Bullits, and the unusable melee combo.

_childDocuments_.review: Among reading the other reviews it's pretty easy to grasp why some people don't really like this game and it all stems from how the main protagonist Copen (or Acura if you prefer the JP name) plays. This game doesn't carry over the exact playstyle he had in Gunvolt 2 and iX 1 and instead goes for something that starts off a little slower; you only have one midair bullit dash and he has more of a melee emphasis akin to something like Zero from the Mega Man X and Mega Man Zero.I'd also argue that the story comes off initially weak with it effectively just being the premise of an isekai. For the most part I'd say this holds true for most of the main campaign until near the very end where things basically start ramping up to 11. Which ramping things up to 11 is a standard for this series so do know if there ain't anything catching you immediately, just hold out for an hour it's a shocker.But with those out of the way... HOLY HELL this game really caught me off guard with how the game flows. Granted not everyone is going to like how Copen plays but once you get a good handle of him, you definitely find yourself cleaving and dashing through everything in your way. I think I actually like this approach to gameplay more since I feel more attentive to the level design instead of dashing by everything with barely a moment to breathe and even then once Overdrive is active you can go back to doing that anyway.Music as usual is pretty great and I'd argue this game also has some of the best general level and boss music out of the series thus far. Some of it feeling like it's calling back to other Inti Creates or even other Mega Man games like the forest level giving heavy X4 influences.Briefly talking about the graphics there definitely seemed to be a lot of attention to detail with things interacting with surfaces. Copen's razor blade and other enemy interactions leave marks on the terrain and whilst it's mostly similar tile markings it does go a long way in making the environments feel inhabited. Aside from that the game doesn't look too different from other Inti outings, the graphics are clean and expressive where it counts. I know some people want higher definition sprites but to be honest I have no qualms with these ones. They're smooth, clean and convey what they need to petty well. And also the other renders and CGs are well drawn too, albeit you'd probably have to stomach the anime style if you're not into that.This game. Has. Secrets. Okay granted EVERY Gunvolt game has some secrets but this game in particular has so much optional content that ties back to the main story, it's absolutely nuts. There's a secret mode and at the time of writing this, I haven't even beaten it yet and I'd take it that some more advanced people are REALLY gonna gravitate to this mode, especially since in some respects it justifies the gameplay shift better than the main campaign. This is also among smaller stuff that's generally nice with one pretty funny yet dark secret among them also.Overall I think my expectations have been exceeded from what I was generally expecting. It makes me curious how Inti is going to construct Gunvolt 3, because if the way this game structures it's content is any indication then I'm VERY eager for what's coming soon.EDIT: Oh yeah, kind of forgot to talk about the English dub.They're not bad voices but there didn't seem to be any direction as to how they present the lines. Comparing with the Japanese dub there's also some lines that should have a certain reaction with them come off dull. All I got to say is if Inti wants to have an English dub for their game, they REALLY got to get a proper voice director.ONE MORE THING: So at the time of writing this last edit one of the DLCs have finally dropped and all I gotta say is... It's pretty disappointing that the DLC is as expensive as it is, especially since all it gives are an extra boss and unlockable ability.You'd think for how small this DLC is, at minimum it probably should have been 1/6th or 1/12th of the games price at a minimum. At the very least with the current pricing I won't say it's predatory but it's still kind of scummy. Wait for a sale on those if they ever get one.Still leaving it positive cause I do still like the game... This is just kind of a distracting stain though.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR Not worth the asking price. Gameplay and story are massively downgraded for the sake of "newness". Also ♥♥♥♥ DLC practices.Longtime major Inti fan here. I literally have thousands of hours across their games. I can tell this game didn't get a fraction of the love or care the rest of their games get.Story is a bogus wet fart. Jump in a wormhole, beat up robots, leave. Nothing happens, no real revelations to give a damn about, nothing. Might as well been a dream. Also the true end is locked behind Hard Mode, which gives you no upgrades, buffs bosses, and gives you limited lives. Not that the true end amounts to anything either.Gameplay is a gigantic downgrade. Normal Copen is locked behind holding 1000 Kudos, to force the weak sauce pizza cutter on you. It's weak, clunky, inexplicably does nothing if you hold the first hit, and doesn't even give you a good or interesting way to score. You just walk up and press YYY on every enemy until 1000, because they couldn't figure out a way to make it actually useful. Also it's only 6.5% stronger than locking on and holding shoot. Considering Gunvolt bosses are Gunvolt bosses you get maybe one opportunity to saw a boss mid fight... Assuming you're not locked on. Yeah. Shooting and melee are the same button for some God unknown reason. They literally mapped nothing to the A button too lol. Also they buffed locked shots making the saw totally useless if you can mash. There's ways to mitigate the awfulness of the Razor Wheel but at the same time why is it just this bad to begin with? Why is canceling it with an EX Weapon downright necessary? Why must you use the time slow to effectively do damage to bosses with it? Couldn't it of just been useful to begin with?When you can actually play Copen in Copen game again it's still not great. The locked hoops take a while to reach their target, and none of the EX Weapons are quite as snappy as Hailstorm Blade. On top of the physics being off too, it just feels bad all around. The EX Weapon selection is "better" than iX1 in the sense it doesn't feel like a slog to attempt to play the game with them, but there's even less reason to use a variety of weapons now with further inflated ammo values.Stages are messy. Don't really feel right with or without OD. With one dash you can still fly over everything easily, and is encouraged on Hard Mode. Going for Quick Razor bonuses can be hard, Air Combos are as effortless as ever. Also one stage is just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ maze. Barf.Bosses are totally ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Since you don't always have OD they're designed around you not having it. They're challenging without OD but with you can wall camp and generally stay out of reach with no risk. If you spot a challenge you can just push the time slow button, it works on almost all of them. And it does so little damage to most bosses it actually comes out to where it's optimal to use it from saving time. Then you have mashing. In previous games Copen could't shoot faster than the autofire rate. Now you can shoot as fast as you can push the button. With a good mashing technique you can reach ludicrous rates like 30 mashes a second and gun down bosses in seconds. Afraid of taking damage while focusing on mashing? Time slow. Lol. You can't even just not mash because his basic gameplay loop is to tag and precisely count out shots before finishing with an EX Weapon as fast as possible. At least iX1 had fun bosses, this game has nothing.X Ranks (the new S+) aren't terribly fun either. On Normal you're locked to Gutless and can tank hits with no real penalty to score. On Hard you're locked into Fearless and the free panels are removed so you spend twice as much time using the stupid saw.Also it's a buggy mess. Much has been patched but there's freaking phantom walls to bonk on while flying. The score multiplier doesn't display the right values in certain situations. The sound engine is royally ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and can sound blast you at random. Boss SP moves can be skipped.Last but not least, the price. DLCs are single boss fights and gamebreaking upgrades... For 8 dollars. Something you'll at most get an X Rank on in 20 minutes and never touch again. Absolutely putrid. The base game meanwhile is a huge price hike and yet you get no story, less dialog, and less content. They we're high when they priced this garbage and fortunately nobody is buying it. Do me a favor and don't pay full price if you decide to purchase it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This series has always had some weird decision making, but I think this entry has some of the most baffling of all. They've limited Copen's default air dashing to a single air dash, removing the core of his previous gameplay being chaining air dashes on enemies to reset your bullit counter and stay off the ground. You can actually get air dash chaining back in this game, but only after you've accumulated 1000 kudos in a level. This has some problems: 1.) Gameplay before you reach 1000 kudos is boring compared to LAIX 1. 2.) Post-1000 Kudos gameplay is fun, but encourages you to play cowardly because the game being fun is now a privilege locked behind artificially induced challenge runs with no checkpoints or healing (outside of RNG drops). 3.) The Gunvolt Chronicles series continues its weird tradition of baking accessibility options into its standard difficulty and punishing the player for using them instead of either designing the standard difficulty with these tools in mind or just making an alternative easy mode that unlocks them. Possibly the craziest of these accessibility options yet appears in Luminous Avenger IX2: access to a practically unlimited supply of full heals that eat your score and your kudos while consuming minimal resources otherwise. Its literally a "get out of jail free card": a tiny devil sitting on your shoulder that's constantly staring you in the face and asking why you aren't using it. But you know that if you use it, its going to steal your fun gameplay away. Its seems really poorly balanced and thought out, and should be something you have to opt into instead of being in your skillset by default. All of these issues add together to make an experience that almost seems designed to make the game miserable to play on your first playthrough. You're constantly having to choose between "fun gameplay" vs "checkpoints" or "fun gameplay" vs "that cool animated screen clearing move" or even "fun gameplay" vs "moving fast" which defeats the point of the fun gameplay even existing in the first place, when you're too afraid of using your air dashes to their full potential out of fear of losing them. And its frustrating because they made fun gameplay. They really did. Copen's air dash chaining is really fun. But locking it behind an arbitrary point system and making the player, on a per level basis, re-earn it guarantees that at least half of the level will be un-fun while you build up to it.Fun gameplay shouldn't have to be earned. It should be the default. That's why we're playing the game. That's not to say you can't reward the player for doing a good job. But locking the core gameplay of the series behind an arbitrary score system that then proceeds to locks you out of other features and encourages you to play cowardly is not the way to do it. Come up with a cool new feature for players to earn at 1000 Kudos. Something that feels good to add onto Copen's existing skillset. Don't just take away core skills that he's had for multiple games to repackage them as a "reward".

_childDocuments_.review: Just want to say that, no the game isn't bad or devoid of fun. It runs great, and the controls are still fluid and precise. I just think this entry isn't particularly great in any aspect. The story is the worst of the series. With a smaller cast of characters compared to IX1, somehow they're still incredibly one note and forgettable. Copen has it the worst, somehow he talks and sounds like a walking corpse in this entry. And when the game's story finally ended, I shrugged. I didn't feel anything once I got to the ending. Somehow with a setting like being transported into another world, we got a generic videogame storyline of collecting macguffins and rescuing Kohaku. And as it turns out, that was the "normal" ending. They're gatekeeping the "True" ending where things are actually interesting behind HARD MODE. So they created a bland normal ending, and kept the good stuff behind the hardest challenge imaginable. People who play just for the story usually don't bother with this kind of thing, so I'm wondering why they even did this.Gameplay, they advertised Copen having 2 modes. That's not really how it is, it's one mode and an overdrive state. The breakshift mode, where Copen is stuck having only 1 dash is the default mode, while overdrive gives him a few dashes to work with once you get 1000 kudos. That's as far as differences go. They both use the new melee saw and both are able to make use of the dash stun and the many upgrades found in the store.The saw is just a melee version of his peashooter from previous entries, really. It gives the illusion that it's powerful when the game throws a ton of big beefy trash mobs at Copen for him to saw apart while standing still. The moment he starts to walk, the saw becomes a butter knife on par with his pistol. The saw is entirely pointless in boss fights. It doesn't deal as much damage as simply locking on with the homing shots, and most bosses are moving constantly so you don't have much opportunity to keep slashing.The recoil dash works on less than half the bosses and enemies in the game, I seriously wonder why they even bothered with this "Breakshift Mode". It's supposed to stun enemies once you slam into them, but for most of the enemies, they'll just shrug it off and you wasted a chance to perform a lock on. However, it does push most smaller enemies and some stationary ones gets flipped over to show their weakpoint. So there's some use for it, but it's still very underwhelming.Copen also lost the ability to ground slam, sure he doesn't have bullits to reload anymore, but losing the ability to quickly land after dashing is super awkward and takes a lot of time to get used to. All of that combined and you wonder what the hell Copen is thinking with his new armour and moveset. In Hardmode he also loses Kudos immediately after 1 hit, so he's perpetually stuck having 1 dash if you're not a god at the game.Does all of that make it a bad experience or a bad game? No, it's still fun at times. The EX weapons are really good this time around, and they make up for the underperforming saw. And I did enjoy the conversations between Kohaku and Null in the menu. It's just, there's nothing outstanding or great to be found in this entry in my opinion. The changes made in this game are questionable and don't really add to the experience. Like I said, his new saw is on par with his old pistol. There's really no reason to have it.

_childDocuments_.review: I heard about Luminous Avenger iX 2 and was curious to know what they could possibly do with it. Although  I liked some aspects of the game, I'm still disappointed.Compared to the gunvolt titles and Luminous Avenger, this game has no real content it is very short and not hard at all. - The levels are good.- The soundtrack is fine.- Copen is nerfed in this game, do not expect to relive the same experience you will be   disappointed.- Bosses are really easy.- The game tells you to use ex weapons but they are not really useful and I didn't really cared  about purchasing upgrades.- The story is predictable and not important it's just a pretext for a new very short adventure.- I liked being able to hear the characters talking during levels and boss fights in past titles but   it seems that in this game this is not the case which makes the experience more boring. _childDocuments_.review: Short Review (Already finished the game) :Thank you INTI CREATES for creating this game even though playing for the first part was bad memories but the more I spend time on it the better it feels since most useful passives seems to be lock in credits upgrades.About the game, the game story is really another what if setting for Copen seeing the prologue isekai stuff until the latter half, the characters are lovable, the new character Null is lovely and even the bosses too. Music in the game is great as always even the instrumental, the gameplay introduces new fun elements but at the same time takes some of the fun aspects.Things to look out for :- The game starts weak since your stuck with a nerf Copen but once you unlock most passive seems like he can become quite fun to play with unlimited bullit dash and ex weapons in overdrive.- You can only bullit dash once when not in overdrive so the gameplay you had with Copen in GV2 and LAiX is not the same since there is no bullits and no recharging them, you have to get use to the razor wheel and pushing enemies.- You can heal with no cost meaning you can heal repeatedly 3x since the heal has no cooldown though it acts like a skill now since it banks your current kudos.- Hyperguard is broken your opponent will always deal 1 damage.- If your wondering about costumes(Kohaku) then yes they have it unlockable after beating VS missions. - The game is short last 2-4 hours at most if you only play normal mode.- True ending is lock in hard mode, hard mode also has a difficulty spike.- The game features dual audio.- Last Note : INTI CREATES has fixed the regional pricing on some countries, still its a drop compare to the 1st LAiX but hopefully it gets a sequel since this Copen has a better personality.

_childDocuments_.review: Luminous Avenger iX2 is an awful game and one of Inti's worst, taking a character known for his high speed flying through the air and turning him into a character that feels so bad to play now. Copen in the previous games is basically entirely gone now, with his gun being swapped out for the new Razor Wheel. The Razor Wheel gives Copen a new 3 hit combo, emphasising a new stop and go playstyle that feels incredibly unsatisfying. But sure Copen's untagged gun was kind of awful before, so this must be an upgrade right? No not really they removed all of the other fun stuff from Copen. Bullits completely gone now. "But wait, you needed those to air dash, so how is it handled now?" They didn't, you get one air dash for the whole game now. That's not like how air dashing with 1 bullit worked in the previous games either, hit a wall or enemy mid air dash and you'd get a bullit back, no you get just 1 air dash before being hit eith an empty indicator on screen and having to touch the ground again. But hey! The old Copen isn't entirely gone, now you just have to hit 1000 kudos to get your old playstyle back! But why change that? Why fix what ain't broke? It's not even the same as old Copen, now you have a timer on your dash limiting how long you can be airborne for, because why not i guess. The new bullit-less system also means that now you can't reload them anymore, obviously, but that also means no more slam move, making getting back to the ground from those rare moments you're in the air also incredibly awkward.But hey, no worries, that's where the DLC comes to the rescue! For £6.29/£3.14 per boss, you can unlock upgrades that bring Copen back to his old gameplay style! They knew, so they locked it behind DLC! This might not seem too bad, Gunvolt games have always had DLC before, except those were way cheaper than these. DLC Blade in iX1 was £1.79. Except Blade didn't lock Copen's old playstyle behind an overpriced boss fight. All the dlc bosses in total will run you £25.15, which by the way, is £5 over the base game price, and even worse is £15 more than this game is on sale. Buying the full package of LAiX2 is £45, just under what a full price game is here. All that for a barely hour long game that i hated most of my time playing. Speaking of price, let's compare to other games with a playable Copen, all of which are much better than iX2.Azure Striker Gunvolt 2 - £19.99 (7.99 on sale)Luminous Avenger iX1 - £13.49 (6.74 on sale)Mighty Gunvolt Burst - £8.99 (£3.59 on sale) + £3.99 for the Rivals DLC pack (comes with 3 playable characters by the way)Blaster Master Zero 2 - £8.99 (£4.99 on sale) + £1.79 for the Copen DLCAll of these games are cheaper than iX2, give a more fufulling experience. iX2 is by far one of Inti's worst offerings, and you're much better buying any of their other games, which are mostly much cheaper than LAiX2 and also happen to be some of my favourite games ever. There's more i could rant about but i don't care enough this game to do so, and you can easily find someone else who will.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX2 is one of if not the worst games in gunvolt history if not in the history of 2D platformers. where should I start? how about the main game play loop, the game play loop is rather boring and unchallenging at all in normal mode. the main issues being the infinite healing and lack luster stage design. the stages are boring and half of them can be directly linked to other games mainly megaman games, as for the bosses and enemy's you can out right ignore the enemy's and attack patterns due to the infinite healing you are provided, anthem has roughly a 35% to 40% chance of triggering even if you do die which is most likely from not paying attention to your heal bar, not to mention the bosses are heavily inspired if not based on other bosses form other games (a example being that The final boss copies from sonic and kirby bosses). As for gameplay itself the movement is like trying to use a tank in a racing game, it doesnt feel good to say the least, not to mention the outright downgrade from Luminous avenger iX 1 where you start with 3 dashes and can buy more, in this game you cant buy more dashes at all and are stuck with one dash (without spending 8 dollars for infinite dashes). Not to mention the rest of the downgrades of this game, When falling down you cant fast fall down like you could in iX1, when wall jumping you feel like gravity is constantly pulling you down unlike iX 1, you also cannot dash into enemies on the ground to lock onto them like in iX1. As for story I can forgive bad stories however because the game play is so abysmal I was hoping the story would be better, but no its full of character assassination left and right, Lola is reduced to a glorified EZ bake oven, Copen is not very involved in his own story (unless you count creator), Kohaku gets downgraded from a character who can at least fight back to a damsel in distress, null gets far to much screen time just to be killed off, and don't get me started on mothers bad divorce. as for upgrades they'll practically useless because EZ Bake oven Lola can heal you to max making any all upgrades worthless even if you can scrounge the currency up. now in previous gunvolt games there was challenge to get Max rank on the stage like for example being fast or not getting hit, this game? you just need to not die, you can have 99:99:99 on the clock and still get that max rank if you don't die. Now for the main weapon you'll have this pizza cutter, it looks cool but its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrible, the weapon has a 3 hit combo that you would expect to one shot a basic grunt, it doesn't, not to mention that starting with anchor nexus makes this worse, ever game that Copen has been in has had at the start a long range special off the start, this game with only one dash neuters anchor nexus and why it was so good in iX 1. this game is about 2~3 hours of playtime if you're not brain dead, hard mode is maybe 6 to 8 hours due to the infinite healing being gone and if your brain dead. if you want a fun 2D platformer for the same price as base price of iX 2 please spend your money else where, for example you can buy a game like AfterImage same price as iX 2 and is at least 5 times longer, and 20 times better, a game you can get for cheaper is Icey a fun little game that is a hidden gem, the megaman collections are cheaper and  honestly play a whole lot better then this game. the fact that this game is being held as the standard for the future gunvolt games and that gunvolt 3 which has a bad story yes but infinity better game play does not spell well for the series a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Right, where do I begin?Let me preface this by saying that I am a huge fan of Gunvolt and Mega Man. Easily my two favorite side-scrolling franchises. I have bought every Gunvolt game thus far on both Switch and PC, so I can play it on-the-go and with my preferred input method. I am a raving lunatic for Gunvolt. However, this is not Gunvolt.Luminous Avenger iX 2 is a game that sees Copen transported to another world, a world that completely overhauls fundamental aspects of the series. The hyper guard, hard mode, and razor wheel are poorly implemented at best. Hyper guard, when used by anyone with a cerebral cortex, effectively renders the entire game null and void. Hard mode has the polar opposite problem. I may just suck at the game, but as someone who has S+ ranks on every stage in iX1: Why is this so unnecessarily difficult? Most of it is fine, outside of the strange inclusion of the lives system from classic Mega Man games (why? I thought we moved past that?), however, the final boss is just... ridiculous without assist mode. If it weren't for this fight, hard mode may have been the saving grace of iX2 for me.If you want a reasonable platforming and combat challenge in a 2D package, this is not the game you're looking for. Go buy iX1 or GV2.

_childDocuments_.review: The Bosses - They were pretty fun and fair to fight on my first run. Albeit some of them get absolutely washed down by their weaknesses. Favorites are Ypsilon(), Autochrome, Ace and   The fights with Ypsilon are incredible as they can set the bars for testing your skill. And his boss theme is great to listen to.The EX Weapons - Each of them are useful in their own right. My favorites would have to be Optic Barrier, Gatling Blitz and Rolling Ripper. The OST - But that's pretty much a staple on the series now isn't itStages - Each of the main stages have unique atmospheres and their own obstacles that gives them their own identities. Copen's Comboing - It feels pretty smooth to do and it makes the bisections feel satisfying.The Return of VS MissionsThe Dub - I'm 50/50 on this since there's top-notch voices like Connor as Dacite. But Brittany as Vespa or Cassandra as Lola are way too high-pitched or "out-of-tone" for me. Also, Arin Hanson as Ace is a memable but welcomed decision for me.The Endgame - I wished there were more special and creative things for this such as duo-fights like  with things like Hail + Ace and Dacite + Brigade whom could've had their own stages for the passages to the top floor  you fight Ypsilon.  Copen's Bullit Limiting - Feels annoying to constantly have to fall on ground to do another dash and the fact that full bullits are locked behind a 1000+ high-score is a bit much. It's kinda worse how even then your air-time when dashing during Overdrive is limited too.Least Favorite Bosses - Final Boss(I'll get to that) and The Difficulty - The game is incredibly easy and I never died to the bosses on my first run for normal mode. In fact I only died 3 times, and those were slip-ups I had on the stages themselves. Hard Mode - On the OTHER side, this difficulty locks your abilities, healing mode, keeps you on level 1 and gives you lives. Not only that, the bosses' difficulty are CRANKED to 100% and they get new attacks that nobody wanted. These attacks just come out of nowhere and these EX Bosses took me at least multiple attempts. (Spoiler)  If you somehow beat these EX Bosses on your first try, I title you as the Kratos of this game.The Story (Potential Spoilers: Read at Your Own Risk)            6.5/10I don't see this game as the "DRV3" or "MMX6" of Gunvolt, rather far from it. There's things that may make this game step down from iX1 while it also has step-ups. But I'm unbothered when I say that I had tons of fun with the combo gameplay while traversing the stages and bisecting enemies. Conclusively, I have a love-hate relationship with this game and it's playstyle which is saddening in concept.

_childDocuments_.review: : Well boss, Luminous Avenger iX was a success! People really seem to enjoy Copen's unique combat style! How should we handle the sequel?: L E T ' S M A K E M E G A M A N Z E R OAnd thus, Luminous Avenger iX 2 was born. It looked towards its brothers, Gunvolt 2 and Luminous Avenger iX, with a beaming smile full of excitement and sparkling eyes filled with hope, exclaiming "Look, brothers! I have a playable Copen just like you!" Gunvolt 2 and Luminous Avenger iX simply nodded and smiled softly, hands behind their backs firmly clutching their high-speed air-based combat out of view from their youngest sibling, whose version of Copen is weighed down by significant amounts of papier mache.Those expecting to see Copen in his usual game of The Floor is Lava might be understandably disappointed to see that in this game he plays more like...well, a traditional Mega Man X/Zero game; he's limited to a single Bullit Dash that can only be used in the air and automatically reloads on landing, his default weapon is now a close-range buzzsaw while his gun only activates when an enemy is tagged, and he no longer has Flashshield. In the intro cutscene he mentions that this is his new gear, so apparently his idea of innovation is nerfing himself.That said, if you can look past that, then LAiX 2 is a solid and fun game. The difference between this entry and the previous one lies in more than just Copen's mobility, with both ups and downs depending on your preference; Kudos are no longer lost on damage, but the lack of Bullit Dashes means comboing is impossible outside of Overdrive, which gives you infinite Bullit Dashes as long as you keep bouncing off of enemies, but it only activates when your Kudos is over 1000; your main method of actually reaching Overdrive is probably finding secret emblems, as there are four in each stage and a single one gives you 500 Kudos. Unfortunately, touching checkpoints and using Lola's new healing form banks your Kudos, immediately ending Overdrive, so I suppose it's not really the intended playstyle until you become really good at the game.That Mega Man Zero comparison was mostly a joke, but this game does remind me a lot of the ZX series; for one, unlike in previous games where the environments are mostly urban settings, LAiX 2's Tower of Isekai contains a lot of different biomes in it, so that's cool; for two, boss weapons now serve more purpose than just damaging enemies, as they can be used in exploration and traversal--for example, the Whirling Chopper is needed to boost you upwards through a small spike-lined passage to get one of the secret emblems in the fourth stage.Additionally, despite only having one Bullit Dash, you  still rely on homing attacks to take out enemies, it's just much slower compared to previous installments.So, all in all, LAiX 2 is a good game whose main problem is not fully adopting LAiX's identity, which can drive some fans away.P.S. I'm finding it significantly more difficult to get S ranks in this game; I wonder if that has anything to do with its lack of speed.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like this game is dead set on sabotaging itself - every design choice in this seems to run counter to every other aspect of the gameplay.The game wants you to play fast, yet it limits your mobility heavily; it wants you to get high combo scores, yet takes away Copen's primary combo utility until you're already almost done with whatever stage you're playing; it wants you to play aggressively, yet your optimal weapon for scoring is temporarily overwritten whenever you use your primary movement option aggressively and and and... I just... what were they thinking? I'm sure there's some sort of logic here, but all I see is a game that has no idea what it's actually trying to be and which makes for a vastly inferior experience compared to its predecessors.I'd recommend you play just about any other game in this entire franchise instead of this one. And that's before getting into the abhorrent DLC practices inti experimented with here. Gotta love that wonderful strategy of creating a problem where there was none and then selling you the solution at a ludicrous price. Lovely stuff.(Oh and as for the story... there's practically none here, it's an isekai story about nothing and nobody which is also completely irrelevant to the overarching plot of the series.)Update after finishing the game, like a dingus: Yup, doesn't get any better. Hell, the True Ending Hard mode arguably makes it even worse. I love me a good, challenging difficulty mode, but this definitely ain't it, chief. Yikes.

_childDocuments_.review: Luminous Avenger iX2 may not be the "ApeX of Cutting-Edge 2D Action", but damn it sure comes close.Right out of the gate, you'll find the same wonderfully tight controls, rockingly catchy music and incredibly detailed art, but you'll want to keep in mind this is definitely a side game through & through in terms of story. I'll touch on this more later.Gameplay wise, Copen has been "nerfed" from iX1 in that he no longer has the insane air mobility of the Bullit Dash. He's limited to 1 dash in air unless you bounce off walls & ceilings like iX1 or obtain Overdrive. His fighting style- thanks to the Razor Wheel- is more "stop-n-go" akin to Gunvolt himself as you'll often be stopping to rip the blade into tough enemies and have to time a ground dash to safely get out. This can either be really fun & intense, or really frustrating- but for me I enjoyed it! He also keeps his aerial attacking from past games, so don't worry there. Upgrades are also far easier to obtain than in iX1 too, and many really help. Sadly, they don't carry into the unlockable Hard Mode which, while a great challenge- is made irritating thanks to them bringing back lives from before Gunvolt. Important story content is also locked behind Hard Mode...Leading into the story, it's extremely simple in comparison to even iX1, and this can be a double edged sword. This is great if you want to quickly show the game off to friends without spoiling the core series' plot (even easier now that there's english voices too!). There's references here and there to past events, but the story is less about this huge new world and past plotlines and more of a character study of Copen & Lola, considering the story of the main antagonists. You need to look into it heavily to see it however and that can be a plus or minus.iX2 is a great experience, but can really leave you with a feeling of wanting , especially story wise- and for many, limiting his air mobility can feel really restrictive. But the game is still an amazing action platformer regardless, and seeing another melee character coming to Gunvolt 3, I can only hope their combat is a big improvement to what we see here in iX2!! As a fan this was a must buy and I got it as soon as I could, but I know many will be mixed on it. Just keep an open mind and I'm sure you'll have one hell of a time!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best Megaman game released ever since Megaman Zero 3. If you're a fan of Megaman X/Zero/ZX you owe it to yourself to play this game, even if you disliked the first two Gunvolts and the first Luminous Avenger like I did, as it plays very differently from those games, for the better.I highly recommend disabling Anthem in the pause menu and not using the healing skill altogether. Doing that will make for a very satisfying experience with a good level of difficulty on Normal mode.I've got nothing to say about the story as I skipped all of it, I'm only interested in the gameplay in these types of games.Basically, if you're an older fan of MMX/MMZ and came into the Gunvolt series looking for a spiritual successor to those games only to be disappointed by how fundamentally different they were, then this is the game you've been looking for. This game is for you, not for people who actually like what the previous Gunvolt games were doing.I'd also recommend looking into Gunvolt 3 if you enjoy this game. It's not quite as good as this one, but it's still a great Megaman-like that is very much worth playing, and waaaaaaaaaaay better than the first two Gunvolts.This game feels like a gift, made specifically for me and everyone who loved Megaman Zero and ZX/ZXA. Thank you Inti Creates, from the bottom of my heart.Update:I've just finished the hard mode. It sucks. Stick to normal mode and just look up the extra cutscenes if you care about the story.

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty easily the worst gunvolt game. They absolutely cripple Copen's previously super fun gameplay, the story is meaningless nonsense, and the true ending is locked behind a tedious and uninteresting hard mode. I appreciate this game for introducing the HD sprites to the series, and the soundtrack is quite good, but I'd honestly recommend just skipping this, even if you're a big fan of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Good:+ Control feels very tight. Copen in this game is a tank, so lil sluggish control is kinda expected.+ Graphics is a massive step-up. Not a straight up 3DS port or anything, which is ... thank god.+ The soundtrack is also banger, too! Although I don't get why the boss theme sound like I'm fighting against Mr. Grinch at Akiba on Christmas.+ If you look at the presentation, this game looks amazing, butBad:- For whatever reason, the game (kinda) took away Copen's basic mechanics, and replaced it with new weapon type: Razor Wheel. Its chip dmg is so weak that I don't even bother unless certain parts required it to bypass. It's a pain in the ass to get used to that pizza cutter since I'm so used to his super-fast-af-boi air dash, and I don't like him in Gunvolt 2. You better get used to Razor Wheel, or the game is really hard to play, wait, this game has difficulty? I'll get into it. Yes, Bullit Dash is still a thing, but only once instead of 3 (more than that in iX 1 if you upgraded Copen). If you wanna play like normal Copen, you're required to get 1000 kudos, which grants him an almost infinite Bullit Dash. I'm sorry, but replace Copen's core feature that personalized him as Adept Slayer with a tanky pizza cutting boy is never a good idea.- The difficulty on Normal mode is non-existent. It's Gutless only. You have UNLIMITED HEAL (ARE YOU KIDDING ME, INTI CREATES?), so have fun damage boosting everything if Kudos means nothing to you. I'm fine with hard mode that limit your heal, but asking me to master Razor Wheel? No thanks.- The game is horribly unbalanced, too! You can just turn on Cryo-Flash and then use Gatling Blitz on the tagged target, and they'll be down in a sec, especially bosses. Since Cryo-Flash (slow-down time) worked on EVERY SINGLE BOSSES, they have no chance to fight back. If you find this too much difficult to do, then try getting 1000 kudoes for that almost unlimited Bullit Dash because all bosses are designed with tank Copen in mind, so if you can utilize the OD mode, they should consider opening a circus. Oh, did I mention the unlimited heal makes the Normal mode become a Journalist mode?- I need to unlock tagged ground dash instead of having it at the beginning? And why is EC rank reward locked behind the shop, anyway? and why does it give so little? Did anyone at Inti Creates playtest the whole upgrade shop at all?- The story is literally an anime filler, so don't complain why I don't put it in spoiler. You're being isekai'ed with Kohaku, so it's up to you two to find a way out inside a big-ass tower. There was no connection to the main story. No build-up. Not even a single personality to anyone, including the Worker bosses. Unlike bosses in GV1,2, and IX 1 where they gave us some context of their background, These IX 2 bosses can be summarized as "We found an intruder. Let's kill him!" If you want the story to be more coherent, you must beat the game in hard mode, which again, required mastering the pizza cutter that's as strong as a used toothpick. C'mon, Inti Creates, this is Luminous freakin' Avenger iX 2, not Ghouls'n Ghosts.- The DLC practice is glorified sh!t. They're all paid advertisement, and last for like 20 minutes in total cuz all are just boss fight that gave you even more game-breaking weapons, and don't forget Cryo-Flashy day of Gatling Blitz can obliterate them with no problem.- Heck, $25 is asking far too much for a game that's heavily relied on replay value to make the price tag worth, and the entire Gunvolt series has even less playtime than a single Blaster Master Zero game.I may be too harsh about this game, but if you still wanna buy this game, wait till it's less than $10. However, before that, you should buy iX 1 first. It's far better than this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels more like the X and Zero games, than the previous entries - which is both a blessing and a curse. You'll get more of the classic run-and-gun action with platforming that fans of the classics will enjoy, but it's less of the hyper-paced, high-flying experience of Luminous Avenger 1, or even Gunvolt 2. You tend to rely more on your power ups to defeat enemy types, since Bullet Dash isn't the one-size-fits-all it was in previous games. Though, when you get Overdrive, it feels fun to let loose and feel overpowered again.I personally enjoyed this more focused experience, primarily because I've been itching for something similar to the Mega Man Zero series since completing Cyber Shadow last year. It's tricky and testing, but still a fair and fun game like all the others in the Gunvolt series. The story is probably the weakest point, only in that it makes a lot of leaps and leaves the player to assume a lot of missing context. However, from an overall presentation standpoint, it's the most polished game in the series yet. Runs at a smooth 120fps, has exciting character animations for Super moves, and a fully voice acted cast of characters. This makes anticipation for the next mainline Gunvolt game even more eager. Avenger iX2 is a solid game, with great fun to be in its classic-style gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: iX 2 is what happens when people say "I wish Gunvolt were more like Megaman" and Inti actually listens. Many people compared Copen's gameplay to Megaman X and Megaman Zero in GV 2 and iX because of how agile he was, but this is something of a falsehood. Copen is more agile than any Megaman ever was, and his free dashes allowed you to get away with circumventing an absurd amount of the game's challenges, and outright avoid them if you aren't going for score.In iX 2 Copen now actually plays like his predecessors in the 2D sidescroller world, limited to a single air dash and with level design that forces him to face most of it's obstacles head on, and it's a hard pill to swallow. If you came in expecting more lightning fast blitzing off walls and destroying things that dare to blink at you in an instant, you'll be disheartened to find that the game only allows that during Overdrive mode, making the gameplay you're used to a reward for playing well, rather than the default state.This comes with up-sides, like special weapons being more useful than they've ever been, but becomes a problem when a lot of the game's core design philosophy is still based around nigh-infinite dashes. The game also unfortunately retains the franchise's masochistic tendencies in punishing your score for using the options it gives you. The writing is also the weakest it's ever been in the Gunvolt Franchise, and I didn't find myself very attached to the world by the end. It's not terrible, but forgettable.iX 2 is by no means a bad game, but it's not iX, and whether or not that'll make it or break it for you depends on how much you liked iX. If the game allowed you to upgrade your way back to iX levels, I probably wouldn't have any issues with it, but even I find myself missing the old gameplay, even if I do like a lot of what iX 2 does.
