_childDocuments_.review: I saw the trailers for this game, and I was 110% in when I heard the tongue-and-cheek humor. The gameplay as well looked really smooth, so I knew I was going to enjoy the game. I had no idea that I'd be playing a game that was on the level of Dead Cells, arguably better!Have a Nice Death is very similar to Dead Cells in that it's a 2D Action Roguelike. You have your standard melee attack  in the form of a scythe. In contrast to Dead Cells, your standard melee attack has a lot of moves. You can attack up and down, there's a charged attack, there's a charged dash attack, etc… There's even a rage attack that you can use every so often as your rage bar fills up. All of these different moves honestly makes the game feel like Devil May Cry to some degree. There's even aerial combat, which is another thing that this game has over Dead Cells.In addition to your standard melee attack, you can also gain 2 more attacks. These 2 additional attacks can range from separate melee attacks such as spears, daggers, hammers, etc… to magic spells such as fireballs, lightning storms, explosions, etc… A melee build will play very differently from a ranged build, so that's nice and adds replayability. You can upgrade both your standard melee attack as well as these 2 additional attacks in a special "control room" up to 3 times at the cost of currency. These upgrades can drastically increase the usefulness of these additional attacks such that you may find yourself only using your main attack in the beginning to only using your 2 other attacks near the end.While you have a decent amount of offensive options available to you, it wouldn't mean much if the enemies didn't put up a decent challenge. Thankfully, they do. To be clear, if you were fighting pretty much any enemy 1 on 1, you would absolutely destroy them without ever getting hit. However, most of the combat in this game happens in arenas where waves of multiple enemies constantly spawn. The combination of multiple enemies is really what makes the combat challenging. You have to constantly be on the offensive in order to take out enemies quickly so that you don't get swarmed. Enemies can also get stunned if you attack them enough (with different attacks having different degrees of stun buildup), which further incentivizes you to play aggressively. As the game progresses, the enemies become more and more challenging with them shooting multiple projectiles, having huge range to their attacks, shooting homing projectiles, exploding on death, teleporting behind you, etc… The developers honestly did a great job in making a large variety of enemies so that you'll constantly be challenged.The bosses are another highlight of this game. They all have multiple attacks, fight very differently from each other, and their attacks are difficult to dodge. I've beaten the game twice, and I still have difficulty not getting hit by the 2nd boss onwards. Part of the difficulty stems from the fact that, similar to Dead Cells and Hollow Knight, you can't just dodge in order to avoid attacks. You also need to jump and simply move very carefully. On top of that, you need to time your dodges and jumps well. Therefore, there's a lot to master in regards to the defensive aspect of this game. I'd also like to say that the bosses in this game are some of my favorite to fight of any game I've played. That's not because they're the most difficult or complex bosses I've ever faced. It's because all the bosses have personality in regards to the opening scenes introducing them and in regards to how they attack (I particularly like Candice). Also, when you beat them, they become a crying mess, which is always fun to see >:D. It should also be noted that if you take damage, it's not very easy to heal up again. This is because not only are potions (called anima) fairly rare in this game, but taking damage causes some of your health to be permanently lost (or at least, can't be gotten back except for very costly/even more rare items). This increases the difficulty even further and forces you to really master the game in order to beat it.There's two progression systems in this game. I mentioned that you can upgrade your weapons up to 3 times which can drastically increase their effectiveness. You can also get "curses" which are basically passive effects. These passive effects are separated into 3 categories: Melee, defense, and spells. When you are first offered a choice of curses, there are only 3 options available. However, as you specialize more and more into 1 category of curse, that category will start having more options going from 1 option to 2 to 3 (while still showing 1 option for the other categories). So it makes sense to specialize in order to optimize your build. These curses can offer some really epic benefits such as providing all your attacks with lifesteal, bleed, burn, mana gain on hit, etc… So there's usually something to look forward to when you're offered a curse selection. This system is a lot better than Dead Cells' scroll system where you simply pick the scroll that suits the weapons you have on hand, increases a % increase to damage and health.The permanent progression on the other hand is fairly lackluster in that you can only unlock new additional attacks to find in a run. Apart from that, there's absolutely nothing to improve your character for future runs. Hopefully this gets improved upon over time, as the game is still in early access.While this game is really good, it still has flaws. Apart from various minor bugs that hopefully get ironed out throughout early access, there are 3 core issues:	• Game can start getting repetitive: While this may just be because the game is in early access and so the diversity of items is limited, I found that once I decided on a build to play, my run would be very similar to any other run where I chose the same build. The thing is, there are really just 2 different builds in this game: Melee and Ranged (magic). Having just 2 different ways to play the game isn't a whole lot of diversity. I constantly found the same attacks over and over again throughout my time playing this game. Hell, there were 2 runs where I found the exact same 2 attacks (that formed my build). Hopefully this gets better as new items are released.	• Ranged is far superior to melee: As with most games, when you give players melee options and ranged options, the ranged options are usually superior. This game is no different. In fact, it's one of the worst offenders. Not only do ranged attacks allow you to sit back in relative safety, but they can also do a lot of damage, cover a huge AOE, and can be spammable. It should also be noted that most bosses are meant to be attacked during their "down time" when they're not attacking, or else you risk getting hit. However, with ranged attacks, you can pretty much constantly attack. So the ranged attacks are not just better for groups of enemies, but also against bosses! Hopefully the developers balance the builds better throughout early access.	• Moving around isn't very dynamic: Because of the level design of this game, it feels like I am constantly just moving left to right in every stage. This is in stark contrast to Dead Cells where there was a lot of verticality to levels and I was constantly moving around all over the place, and also doing some light platforming, in order to progress. While the combat in Have a Nice Death might be arguably better than Dead Cells, I think general movement/platforming is hands down better in Dead Cells.Overall, this is a really fantastic rogue-like. This game is fast paced like Hades and yet has the difficulty of Dead Cells. It also a great sense of humour, and overall I just love the idea of Death being an overworked boss who has had enough and is trying to get his minions under control. I really enjoyed my time playing this game, and I look forward to this game in its final form :)

_childDocuments_.review: I like Rogue likes in general. This one has a very nice story line to it: funny twist on the corporate life. I feel that the permenent effect shop is a bit lacking. There are no permenant hp/mp and attack buffs. This hinders the sense of progression of the game. Thus there's too much of a get GUD attitude to a game that hasn't really made it's name yet. It would be engaging in this regard if the attack animations had more mobility, but because you have allot of static attack animations; this is not very conclusive to quick multiple run training grounds.Another pitfall of the game is the faulty retaliation mechanics for the curses. Every single on hit mechanic (you get buffed for receiving damage) is invalidated by the fact that there is vertually no viable and reliable healing system in the game. Heals are few few and far between to validate getting hit much at all. The grey health max heal the system is interesting, but once again, to few heals are available in the game for the system to be worth mentioning. it is so much to the point this way that Vit-amin levels are only valuable for the additional mp they provide. The additional max HP is essentially useless because it's up to RNG for ti to be worth anything.One more thing, enable the dash to animation cancel the basic attack combo. It's really annoying not being able to dodge out of your animationsAll in all, cool game look and attack animation design, but the whole upgrade stat and heal system need a rework, Absolutely NOT recommended for casual new players; wait till these guys fix their game. Even for core rogue like players, I'd still say wait. the game is too RNG and not rewarding enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review a couple of days after the early access release.I'll start out this review by iterating this game is beautiful and funny as ****. All of the art is hand-drawn, and wonderfully crafted. Rogue-likes that are this smooth on release deserve all the merit they can get. They do have their own handful of flaws on this game, however, and it is a long way from being finished. (I assume that's why they put that good ol' "early release" title like all indie devs do).Pros:- The game is smooth and seamless with its animation, and it gives you a feeling that a high profile team that has been making games with way more experience than the team that made this actually has. Each level is a cog in "Death Inc's" machine, and you can see the gears turning and come to life!- This game has a perfect blend of poppy colors that contrast with the dark and drab backgrounds it displays, constantly impresses me with its awe-inspiring art with every attack and boss battle presented.- The soundtrack is so fitting for the colorful and playful tones this game sets while being centered completely around such a dark theme of death. I love it in every way possible, there is no song I would not play over again.- The characters you are introduced to are dead, but they could not be more alive. Each employee under death has their own beaming, sometimes cheeky sometimes cute personality, and the way they interact with each other and death is hilarious and never gets old. All the NPC's that are important have their own way of talking, and I believe it was voice acted perfectly (in the same regards as Undertale's characters but with human sounding noises). Their interactions are really extensive and fresh, and in the 5.5 hours I've played this game I'm still seeing new dialogue.- The game's combat feels fair, and you're rarely left with moments of feeling cheated out of a cool combo once you get the hang of how it all works. (I'll explain later why I said rarely). It mirrors the timeless "git gud or die" template, and it feels awesome when you clear a room without taking a single tick of damage.  Collecting weapons and spells that better your survivability is RNG based like The Binding of Isaac, and you soon outgrow simply using the scythe main weapon you start out with.- Another character point I found awesome is that the joke of "haha death in a corporation" isn't shoved down your throat, and allows some breathing room for you to just enjoy the game, while not taking itself too seriously.- It's ****ing CHEAP for how much gameplay you'd get out of it. The $15.00 pricepoint gives you endless replayability and there are challenges everywhere.Cons:- When items or shops are described in this game, the descriptions are brief and make you feel like you should already know what it is or does. For instance, the game never explains what your "cloak" does, yet it is referenced many times during lots of upgrade processes. Eventually I figured out that the cloak is referencing any secondary or tertiary weapons that are physical and not spells, but this was still never explained anywhere. Another example is how the shops are described once in brief, easily skippable detail, and you are left to read over the "tutorial guide" later if you're confused that gives little to no detail on what the shop is for; i.e There are no descriptors in Joe's shop, and nothing indicates what each item does when you buy it with gold, it just...exists and gives dialogue from the character once purchased.- While the combat feels fair most of the time, the team definitely has some bumps to buff out. The odd dash will not give as much time as normal for invuln, and can lead to some pretty frustrating deaths.- Speaking of deaths, dying in this game sends you ALL THE WAY BACK TO THE START, in Binding of Isaac fashion of course. You never get a "game over", but there are absolutely no checkpoints in the game at all so far. It very quickly makes you feel under-powered in combat once you reach a point you've never gotten to. This is technically a pro as well, as I know this is a stylistic choice like in "Getting over it", but god is it frustrating.- My final gripe is with the health and pickup system. Health definitely needs to be more common than it is and do more healing than it does right now. Entire runs of nothing but Soularies when I needed health bad have made it feel like an unfair death at times, and doesn't make for a fun playthrough if there could have been no way to survive a few attacks. (inb4 git gud spammers)Overall, this game is already a comedic, lively (heh, death) masterpiece, and although I abhor the "early release" title that all devs put on their games nowadays, I can see the cons I talked about easily being implemented into the game in its current state if the devs listen to reason. Now if you'll excuse me, I have some expense reports to give the old fashioned CEO "okay" on.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm only 4 hours in, but those 4 hours have been great. Its kinda like Dead Cells, but kinda not. There aren't really any paths to take, thought it looks like they will be adding something like that. You are stuck with a scythe (though rarely in a run you can power it up to a slightly different version) and two abilities, either magic or cloak abilities. Magic uses mana (which recharges very fast, like a few seconds after spending it all) and cloak does not use mana. You also need to conserve your life beacause you CANNOT HEAL MISSING HEALTH only the most recent "injuries" which is a greyish part of the healthbar about equal to the last hit you took. So in order to regain HP once you lose it, you need to find an item that turns your entire bar into injury mode and then pop whatever heals you have available. This makes the game more difficult as you really need to focus on not getting hit and basically use your heals when you get hit by a big boss attack or something of the sort to get the most out of your heals.You will lose a lot and replay the exact same fights a lot, so its good that they have an absurd amount of dialog for the fights. Like some bosses I've done 10 times now and I haven't seen a repeat of dialog yet. Honestly, this game is fun right now and it has a ton of potential for the future. If you like action roguelikes then this is a game you will enjoy. If you are unsure then put it on your wishlist and wait 6 months to a year and check back. I'm sure its going to be considered one of the best games in the genre in a year or 2.Oh also, there is no upgrading outside of a run. You can unlock weapons which gives you the chance to find new things during future runs, but that's it. No stat upgrades or anything.

_childDocuments_.review: I love everything about this game's writing, art, animation, music, and how it all comes together for the general presentation. The core gameplay is a bit harder to praise. This particular action roguelike leans towards the higher end of the difficulty scale. It's not so much that enemies are difficult to deal with as it is that mistakes are sometimes extremely punishing. It's not uncommon to go from full health to nearly dead after just a few hits later in a run, even if you stack your max health into the triple digits. The flow of combat is swift and the mechanics are simple, but these enemies don't wait long to swing after winding up to hit you and multiple enemies WILL attack at the same time if they're in the position to do so. If you don't stack defense buffs (either from items or mid-run skill trees), you're gonna lose some pretty big chunks of your health bar when you get hit. I've had quite a few amazing runs go down the drain in seconds just because I panicked while trying to dodge a sudden flurry of attacks, dodged into the wrong corner, and received a swift beatdown from some common enemies. It stings every time.I think the game is a fun challenge, but I can't recommend that you jump right in if you're interested. Instead, you should probably watch some (hopefully spoiler-free) gameplay of a run or two first to see if it's a challenge that you personally want to tackle. If you do try it, remember the premise of the game:Death just wants to take a break. You should try to take one too if you start feeling tilted.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with great potential. Pro:- great gameplay- nice flow- nice music- good variance in items and weapons (still hope there will be more)- good boss design- sweet animations- funny its in own wayCon:- kinda easy- not a fan of the healing system- very few explanations (like dmg ticks on burning/poisen or extra dmg on lightning and bleeding)- the indicator that shows enemies attacks (so u can dodge them) is not that accurate- the life and mana bar does not expand when u get more life/mana (personal preference. i like it when it grows)I played this game for ~14h and unlocked most items so far and can beat the game quite consistently. And even tho i love rouge likes/lites i'm not a god (still struggle with dead cells), but still, this game is kinda easy. the bosses are very simple and u can read the attacks real good. Like i mentioned in the cons, i dont like the healing system. healing is rare in this game with makes the loss of max life kinda annoying imo, and the amount of healing u get by using anima is not that much either. someone might say its punishing, but i just dont like it in general. life and mana bar does not expand, as i stated. i would love it when the bar grows so i can see, without looking at the numbers, how much life i would gain if i use an healing item. its just a quality of life thing.but the biggest issue i have is the attack indicator on enemies. i cant even count how often i got hit cause the enemy got the indicator, i dodge behind him and he turns around an hits me anyway. But all in all i had a great time with this game. it has great potential and if the devs keep going, this could be a good counterpart for dead cells. just a bit more content, little fixes here and there, quality of life changes and there this game would be awesome. even tho its early access, this game is worth its money

Too many of them and too short.-Each enemy needs to be hit like at least 5 times to die, which starts feeling too slow after the first run.-Also you are kinda locked in the scythe and it is really rng if you can update it, cuz it requires a lot of resources and to have the needed luck to encounter the "control room" stage.-Curses, took inspiration from Hades and that is okay and nice, but receiving them feels kinda inconsistent, badly balanced and slow. This will also fix the nonexistent exploration(depends on how you handle level generation).-Implement more scythe variations to start with.-Re-balance the curses system, buff the useless curses, make the npc spawn more frequently.-Weapon upgrades- add it to the game, cuz currently i see only "switching" the scythe variant as an upgrade, everything else is worthless because you have to pile up kills which is boring and kinda pointless.-Healing-remove/rework-Stop using the excuse "game is balanced and focused around combat", combat is not fun.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is good. Very very good. The art style, the combat, the movement; all some of the best I've ever had. However...the main reason I can't suggest this game AS IS, is due to one single factor: There's no real permanent progression. What I mean by that is this: Think of Dead Cells, or Rogue Legacy. You can upgrade your gear to get better drop percentages, or upgrade your castle to make your player stronger over time. This allows you a better chance to make it to the end boss and actually finish the game. This game does not have that. The game does give you the option to upgrade your weaponry, in one specific room, using an extremely rare token that's dropped on your run (MAYBE), but when you die, you restart all progress and have to hope once again that you come across the room, AND you have the tokens available to upgrade. The drop rate is too low, harkening back to "I wish I had something more permanent to make me feel better"Also in these two games I mentioned (Dead Cells, and Rogue) your options to heal are, depending on a few factors, vast and varied and MUCH more lenient than this one. In this game it's almost impossible to get back to full health once you drop down past a certain point unless you just HAPPEN to get one of the two drops that may make it possible. And of course these two things are also extremely rare. The games drop rates need to be fixed at the LEAST. I can't tell you how often I get ♥♥♥♥ abilities that aren't useful to me, and never see the good ones I unlocked. Oh throwing knives? Oh throwing knives AGAIN?! AND AGAIN!? wow. Can't wait to not pick them up for a 4th time!Anyways. I really really want to enjoy the game, and recommend it...but I can't to either at this current time

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually do reviews but this game is a fantastic rougelike. As the CEO of Death INC. you are overworked and would like a nice vacation, too bad your department heads (and pesky guard) are WAY too efficient, money hungry, or lazy(looking at you GUARD). Head through the various departments and show them who's boss, be warned though, it won't be easy. Everything from the art to the characters is dripping with charm and personality. The combat feels fun and varied with different weapons, spells and upgrades that all feel good to use. Big enemy in the way, why not try THE GIANT FIST(s) or Unga Bunga them with a hammer? Flying enemies that are pelting you at a range? Don't mind If i cast some homing/Aoe spells! You may always start with your trusty scythe but it can be upgraded and transformed to change up how the weapon combos with different curses. SPEAKING OF...Curses are your randomly obtained perks you can grab throughout the run. These curses can range anywhere from giving you a small boost in health to your scythe and all its' transformations doing BUTTLOADS more damage, heck they can even infuse all your attacks with poison or lightning strikes. All in all I enjoy this game and I am very excited to see what else it has to offer on its final release and any future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of good qualities, to name a few:- Characters are funny/quirky (the cast is unique and I've started to adore them and their interaction)- Story is in an interesting setting (I know that the death god theme has already been used in the roguelike game Hades but I still think this game has lots of potential using the Grimm Reaper take on this theme)- It looks cute in a creepy way (the art looks like a combination of the metroidvania Hollow Knight and the roguelike Dead Cells and it really attracted me to buying this game)However there are a few things that prevent this game from really shining, the biggest ones being:- Player character sometimes glitches and gets stuck in passable platforms when jumping through (this is also occasionally accompanied with the soundtrack temporarily breaking)- The spawn rate for healing items is very low (I have gone thru runs where none spawned in the first world, leaving me with barely any HP to fight the boss)- The rare/special currency and the upgrades you could buy with it are lost upon a run ending (you'll get extra points for having it but it still feels kind of useless to get/use sins it will ultimately make no difference to gameplay, admittedly I only managed to get past the first world boss)- The hit boxes are way to big (I can hit enemies that are about 2 player characters away from me and enemies can hit me even when I dodge)- The game doesn't feel rewarding on the long run (besides the glowing bubbles at the spawn room, the codex entries, and the dialogue from the NPC's there just aren't any other changes to the world which just doesn't make me feel like I'm progressing gameplay wise)In the end I really like this game, it's brimming with potential and I hope the developers can work out the few programming kinks and gameplay imbalances.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best rougelikes i've ever played, it is a mix of different rougelikes, or that is how it feels, personally it feels like a main mix of Hollow Knight and dead cells, which are both two brilliant games. The art style is absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Amazing and then there's the sounds, the sound is brilliant and just overall all sounds are different for levels (If you beat a boss you go to a new level). This game feels alot like a dungeon crawler also, the reason for this is because at the end of every level you always go down an elevator and can choose where you would like to go, such as the shop or control room, both extremely useful within the game. This game is still in early access so i will definitely say not to get angry at any bugs, just make sure to let the dev's and people know. Next thing the bosses are quite hard, because this game depends alot on skill, because sometimes you might not be able to get what you want, because it is a rougelike everything is random in getting items and getting curses (Curses are a type of upgrade  for your character, such as you can get a infusion of bleed).Up to now there has not been any bugs that i know of, or that have happened to me, i also personally think that this game could've even been released without early access, but there are no achievements yet (i have no idea if there will be). CONS:Healing, Healing can be extremely hard to get, or well it feels that way, because you have to kill enemies to get healing (Mainly) but it does feel like it takes a long time to get healing also known as anima's (i think) but it is a rougelike so it should be hard to gain things, but yet again i personally feel like healing should be easier to get.Achievements, i would love to see some achievements in this game, then it will be brilliant, because then you can finish the game and have something to push forFinal con the bosses are quite easy, after being beat a couple times. And i also feel like there should be more bosses added, because it is quite quick to get past the game, and beat it. As long as you play for a couple hours that is. Overall this game i brilliant and i couldn't recommend it moreGame 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I had such high hopes for this game. I saw the ads, and I loved it immediatly. I was eager to try what looked like a fun, casual roguelike with a charming atmosphere and quick, responsive gameplay. And at first, that's what I got. The sound was great, the fighting felt punchy and fluid, and the animations were stunning. But as the hours set in and I started to realize just how aggravating this game is, my enjoyment was sapped away.  Besides the vary short tutorial, practically nothing was explained. The first boss was like a brick wall; no matter how many times I threw myself at him, I never felt as though I was making meaningful and satisfying progress. I found myself desperately hoping for useful spells and for enemies to drop heals. And all the while, the gameplay and music just got more and more monotonous. I shouldn't have to rely on RNG to even have a chance to beat a boss. I shouldn't have to grind for an hour to upgrade my scythe, and only find out after dying that it doesn't carry through runs. I shouldn't have to preform perfectly executed moves just to avoid taking damage on the third mini-boss arena in a row. I shouldn't have to wait a full year for the inclusion of difficulty settings. And most of all, I shouldn't have to write a three-paragraph rant about a game that had so much promise.

_childDocuments_.review: Fell in love with this game the second I saw it during the Game Awards, and I'm happy to say that it's already off to a great start. Combat is fast and satisfying to pull off, the items you can collect are fun to use, and artstyle is excellent. I look forward to playing this more and seeing the game develop.Just a few things I'd like to see added for future updates. Nothing major, or even necessary, just some small QoL additions:1. A visual cue for the dash -  This critique was addressed in the latest Infrastructure update. You now see a puff of smoke when the dash cooldown is finished.2. A quick-start option - starting a new run following a death doesn't take too long, and it is nice going back to the main office to see what new items you've discovered or what you can purchase in the shop with your gold. That said, having an option either in the pause menu or on the Death/Results screen to immediately start a new run and skip the office would be a nice option. Update 5/11: While the Infrastructure update didn't add a quick-start option, it did add a new Contract system, where you can receive an extra item or buff at the start of your run in exchange for completing a certain criteria or sacrificing health or mana. A good way to spice up new runs, and an incentive to return to the Office to select one prior to a run.3. A recycling ability - a common issue with games of this kind is that you'll inevitably run into items you want to skip out on because they either don't work with the loadout you current have, or you simply don't want them. Recent roguelikes such as Dead Cells or Curse of the Dead God have addressed this issue by allowing you to destroy that item and get a small bonus in exchange. Would be nice to have that ability here too - exchanging unwanted weapons/spells for extra money or a small amount of health, depending on the quality/strength of the item you're getting rid of. It's not much, but it does help with making the process of reaching those items worthwhile even if they end up not being useful to you directly. Update 5/11: The newest update doesn't add a recycle ability, but does add new methods of gaining additional health throughout your run without relying on enemy drops. A much appreciated change.Update 7/8: The Fast Food Update adds an additional inventory slot that you can use to store items to later sell for additional money.4. Extra visual variety - I love the game's artstyle. It gives off a modern cartoon vibe, especially with the opening cinematic. It's very striking and makes it standout from other games of its genre. It would be nice if the environments had some more recognizable flair to them though. Not to say the environments aren't already great, but the muted palette and lack of colors other than green can make certain areas blend together visually. That said, the animated backgrounds do a good job of distinguishing the game's major locations, so the color palette is more of a nitpick than it is a glaring flaw. Everything else about the game's visuals are brilliant. Update 5/11: The Infrastructure update has added new environmental variations to certain departments. For example, the first area now has a garden environment that you'll periodically encounter. It isn't much atm, but it is a step in the right direction in addressing the visual variety.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the early build of this game long ago and been holding off on playing the game since then, till its official release drop but now the time is now ripe it would seem. Never seen a game look so stylish and visually stunning yet look so bleak at the same time, in a good way. The environment does an exceptional job at capsulizing how dreary and gloomy the cubical workspace is. Except now, you can finally say "we are living in hell"... literally. Charming narrative, lots of dark humor, smooth combat with a somewhat decent variety of builds to choose from. The game has a small arsenal of weapons but they offer a nice rage of move-sets in a form of ground/aerial directional input. Which is a big plus for a game (rouge-like) of this nature. When put into motion, everything feels very snappy and responsive (with really flashy animations to boot). Weapons and skills also have their own “EX” specials that can only be executed through the special gauge. Although, some skills/weapons are outright superior. Most of the time you probably don't even need to dodge, hell even early game you can pick up skills that can let you outright clear rooms while standing still. Some people will say the bosses can be unforgiving, but I dare say, due to how forgiving i-frame dash can be and how busted the RNG can work in your favor. The game can offer a decent challenge at times. _childDocuments_.review: I didn't recommend this in its first released state, but as of the first update I'm actually quite pleased with Have a Nice Death. Enemies now drop items frequently enough to actually justify fighting them instead of avoiding them through each level. Contracts give you a leg up in the beginning so the first world feels different each time instead of the same bland routine. Your health upgrades at the end of each world, and there are more and greater variety of helpful items available to offset the permanence of failure and make each run, even ones where you don't make it to the end, feel meaningful and enjoyable.The art was always beautiful, the controls responsive and the combat fluid. Enemies usually telegraph their attacks so once you get used to them you can almost always get into a rhythm that prevents you from taking any damage at all. Bosses are much harder to dodge perfectly but it can be done.I'm not even a big fan of roguelite games generally; I'll take them for a spin but get bored quickly with the lack of progression and leave them forever. This one has kept its hooks in me far longer than most, so I can't help but recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried to give this game a chance for 15 hours, but sadly, I can't recommend it. The art style, VFX and music are amazing, and the movement and fighting are very smooth, but the gameplay loop gets boring quite quickly, and it doesn't feel like a game has (or will have) much to offer in general, despite plenty of weapons and spells. I played it since it launched in Early Access in March 2022, and despite game receiving few content updates since then, it doesn't feel like anything was improved in terms of core gameplay and depth, and I doubt it will be improved at all.Some levels are too big without a reason - plenty of empty spaces, but not enough enemies, meaning you'll spend your time running, dashing and jumping to get to the section with enemies. The levels look really good, at least.There are 2 healing systems, which seem completely unnecessary and only create confusion.On a plus side, the game has a good sense of humour, with plenty of puns and jokes, so it will keep you entertained for a while. The music is pleasant to the ear and fits the atmosphere very well, and the elevator tune during a loading screen is a nice touch. The art style reminds of Rayman Legends, and is very strong aspect of the game, but is not enough to keep a player entertained.Would give it 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: first of all the game is game is great! the animations, the style, the characters, the story, the music, the sounds, everything is there. there are however a few things to that needs to be resolved on the gameplay side because it honestly is too frustrating at the moment.First of all, fighting enemies outside of arenas where you get rewards is pretty much pointless. Enemies have a chance to drop items but it is way too small to be worth fighting them. The only thing you're risking is loosing HP which bring me to my second point.Second of all, like many other people have said, you have absolutely no sustain whatsoever. enemies can drop healing orbs which heal a tiny bit of hp but as i said before, it is very rare (i've had multiple runs where not a single enemy has dropped one). I was expecting to find a healing spot after the defeating the boss of every level but again no. most of the time the resting spot gives you a buff you don't need when you're 25% HP. These 2 problems the best strategy is to rush past every enemy outside of arenas because you don't get anything other than loosing health which is way too hard to recover. A third and final problem and this is maybe on a personal side, the camera isn't very good. when i move foward, the camera is following my character but too far back which means i can't really see what's ahead of me.I also found the levels weirdly short. if you expect the levels to be as long as they are in hades for example, you'll be in for a shock because they are really small and it doesn't help that you have to rush past all the enemies because fighting them isn't worth it.I can't recommend this game right now because it simply is too hard and not rewarding enough. The game is still in early access however and these are problems that can easily be fixed. Fixing these issues would make the game so much enjoyable and really unlock it's whole potential because it really has a lot of potential. Hopefully, an update in the future will resolve these problemsEdit after the infrastructure update : The situation about the lack of healing is a lot better. enemies have a bigger chance to drop healing orbs, there's a thing in the break room where you can buy healing orbs at increasing prices, getting a blue orb while you're already holding 3 blue ones will upgrade one to a yellow orb and there's a new room that literally just heals you. All these changes have honestly made a big difference in terms of gameplay and it's a lot more enjoyable. The developpers seem to really be listening to the community and have added a lot of content with the latest update. i would say that the game is now worth buying

_childDocuments_.review: As this game is in early access, I am aware there are still is some things for this game to iron out. For Bugs, only once in my 8 hours have I encountered one, I somehow got stuck into the platform/ground forcing me to restart my run. But other than that, so far bug free. I don't know the genre name off the top of my head, but like the binding of isaac, or enter the gungeon, H.A.N.D is a dungeon crawler where you see how many floors you can get through while fighting a variety of enemies and bosses. If you die, you have to start from the beginning again. I find myself enjoying playing in 30-60 minute chunks of time.The first hour was quite frustrating as I kept dying to the first boss (aka Brad). Loathing going through the first floor of enemies just to be cross with myself at my lack of skills when I would meet Brad again. But after a bit I got the hang of it and found I was able to go further. I had a run where I beat the 5th boss, granted I had some pretty overpowered abilities that run. But at this point I most often die to the 4th boss.Now like other games in this genre. Items, abilities, and weapons are all random. I wish I could get the occasional extra healing item at this point in the games development, but I guess it's all part of the challenge. For how random things are, I would say it's close to being well balanced. Sometimes it can feel unfair, but if you keep at it you will have a good run.Now the final thing I will say is this game has SO MUCH CHARM. I am not a fan of dark themes or the Grim Reaper, but the cartoon artwork and animations are so well done and captivating. And the Platforming itself is smooth and quite enjoyable.So if you have the patience to go through dying a lot and starting over, you will enjoy the thrill of seeing just how far you can go. Super fun to play!

_childDocuments_.review: The game appears to be made with a lot of love, and I really want to like it, but can not...The graphics, animations, and the overall atmosphere are just lovely, however:For an early access title, starting this game feels more like logging in to World of Warcraft after a 10 year break - you are bombarded with new systems, characters, dialogue, unlocks without any meaningful way to learn them or any motivation to care. There is a tediously long tutorial that overexplains the rudimentary basics, but fails to cover any of the important game systems. It would be great to have a better learning curve, where the game elements are introduced and explained as you progress and discover them. Some basic systems in the game are unnecessarily convoluted, and could benefit from being simplified. For example unlocks, curses or healing. After about 8 hours of playing, I still don't understand how the bizarre 2 tier health system works or what is the point of it. Standard things have unintuitive names, which creates a need for a lot of tooltips and makes already convoluted systems even harder to understand. Weapons are called cloaks? Health has wounds, vitam, anima, max HP?Curses and weapons appear to have some kind of rarity system to them. However, it is difficult to see or feel any power difference between an orange curse and a grey curse. Curses seem to somehow form a progressive tree, but the number of curses in the game seems to be much higher than what can be seen in the tree? Unlocking things between the runs doesn't feel meaningful. There is a bunch of new spells & weapons that can be unlocked for a chance to appear in the run, similar to Dead Cells. However, there are so few opportunities to find new spells and weapons during the run, it feels like investing in needles in a stack of hay. Combat is beautifully animated, however, the scythe combos can not be cancelled, which is very frustrating. Your character will be hitting the air for several seconds trying to complete the combo while the nearby minions are chomping at your health. There are not enough opportunities to heal, while some bosses and minions can kill you in few hits. I will keep an eye on this game and follow it's development, but playing it is just not enjoyable at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright I've had it up to here with this player-base's lack of common sense, Just go to recent reviews and you'll immediately see my point. You'll notice most talk about things that can be solved with simple common sense, but instead choose to make mute points to make a marvelous game look like the hottest piece of trash on the market. So let me spin my review on why this game is amazing for first month release.  For the shortest answer If you're too busy with your day, its a 8/10 maybe 7 ATM. For the more dedicated or simply curious individuals, here's the more in depth review. :  Have a Nice Death is a 2D-platforming Rougelite in which you take control over Death himself in managing his own company in the afterlife, known as Death inc. The game-play loop revolves around you navigating these 2D environments via exploration, combat, and the occasional Mini-Boss/Thanagers and Area Bosses/Sorrows. To aid you in all of this your good friend T. O'Shah (not even Death himself can escape mandatory OSHA inspections), who provides you with curses which are buffs that assist you throughout your journey to beat your employees back into submission. There are several different departments you'll navigate as you venture out through the company, ranging from the damp and odorous Pollution Department, To greasy and savory Toxic Food-Processing Department; HAND is sure to deliver some creative and diverse set-pieces for your eyes to enjoy.     While most who have 'played the game' in the negative section would call it slow and clunky, this cannot be further from the truth. The game allows for diverse methods of movement, be it with your invincible Dash or even through more creative means with your Up-Slash with your Scythe allowing almost instantaneous upward momentum. The game revolves around you not taking damage and actively aids in helping you do this easier through the curses, though a good portion don't seem to understand this and chalk it up to either bad design or "difficulty". Besides your Scythe which comes equipped with several different variations you may have the chance of encountering at the very beginning of each run, Death inc. supplies you with other tools such as Cloak weapons and Spells. The key difference between the 2 being that Cloak weapons are bound by a cool-down, while Spells are dependent on Mana conservation. They are also buffed more by the red 'Attack' portion of the tree while spells have their own green 'Spell' tree, with Blue being largely for healing and defense. While minor ATM due to the games fresh release, there are some creative ways the moveset interacts with your environment, such as using your form of healing (Anima) to unlock secret rooms which house special goodies ranging from MORE healing, to temporary buffs, to even legendary spells and weapons! All of your arsenal would be arbitrary if you didn't have some good enemy archetypes to knock some sense back into, luckily you don't get skimped out there either. The game provides a wide cast of not so employee of the month co-workers for you to smack around, all fitting their environment beautifully. Reaching the end of each part of a department allows you to take an elevator through to different parts of said department, each room having its own rewards, such as Cloak Stores having one Cloak weapon by the end of that segment, Anima deposit having Anima, and so on and so forth. The ending floor for each department contains the boss or Foreman for their respective part of the company, which provide a nice challenge and are plenty fun to duke it out with. The runs end when you either reach the final boss or you perish due to being overwhelmed by the power of even later common threats.   This section will be kept very brief seeing as how it's not a MASSIVE part of the game. Now I will fully go on record and say in bias that..I love almost every character in the game. They're all so unique and identifiable with all their own quirks and kinks. I will fully admit however that some of the humor can be a little dry or can fall flat, but that rarely happens. The side quests are all cute and creative if you choose to read the dialogue which unfortunately I don't even see most content creators for the game do.   Unfortunately, I can't just be bias and say the game is perfect as it is admittedly riddled with problems. To start, lets start with the more tame issues, some achievements and Side-stories are bugged in which they will be soft-locked and inaccessible for the save file as of the most current patch. The more major changes that should definitely be looked at is how the game is balanced. The skill tree feels like there isn't too much variety in how it powers you up, though they do make you notice the difference they add to your build via the power higher tier curses gives your current run. The base game feels a tad too easy, keep in mind I am currently on breakdown 9; however I am aware that after 10 it becomes exceedingly unfair when it comes to the difficulty spike, but not impossible if you don't have an OP build. All these things I expect to be fixed though seeing as the game has only been out for little over one singular month, yet people expect the world from a new developing team not used to creating games. : Single-handedly the biggest issue is ironically enough the Devs. I don't want to give them too much hate nor unneeded critique when as a whole they did great for a first release; however their willingness to change their games vision just to appease angry "fans" needs to be looked at and addressed. I am more then glad that they are so responsive and willing to make needed changes, but when you start say lowering the skill ceiling as well as the skill floor, you start to get a game that ends up being way too easy. For a Rougelite/Rougelike, that's a pretty blatant flaw that could cause even players who sink several hours into the game, could cause them to grow disinterested.     :   There's so much more I could've gone on and on about, and arguably it could be for the better. But I simply wish to give you insight from someone who's played the game a good amount, and is looking from a perspective of a game in a very early stage of its life that can still change drastically if needed to. If I ever feel like making a follow up review or state of the game discussion, you will most likely find me in the game's Community Center. For potential buyers of the game, I must recommend it, it's cheap, fun, and a great game you can fit into your schedule with the shortest runs only lasting about half an hour. Finally to the people who have complaints like   I hope you enjoyed this albeit not very in depth review of the game, but hopefully it should suffice and lead to more conversation and thinking about what's actually good for the game vs people who deter new players when they cant even beat Brad. -Icedragon64302

_childDocuments_.review: The problem with Have a Nice Death is that is gets very boring very quickly. The actual idea is fun and so are the boss fights but all the other levels are either mindlessly hitting enemies or (rarely) doing one of the timed levels. The movement feels good but also the way that any noticeable changes in your playstyle happen late into the run makes every attempt feel monotonous. They could make boss levels closer together or introduce new ideas but for now it feels slow. With other roguelikes such as Dead Cells or Hades, there are clear ways that make each run different andake you want to play again. In Dead Cells, the sheer number of weapons and upgrades allow you to make unique builds, while slowly uncovering the plot. In Hades, the way that you interact with other characters and progress your relationships with them makes you want to play more and uncover the NPCs' stories. In Have a Nice Death, there isn't anything like that. You just go in and hit some enemies until you get to a boss. If you want to play a platformer roguelike based around interesting combat, just play Dead Cells. And Dead Cells has DLC

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: The game is too unfair to you. When you die, you don't power up, you just rinse and repeat with a wider RNG pool of weapons. Whenever you lose health, it's nearly impossible to get back to MAX HP, literaly.I can't recomend the game on it's current form. I consider myself above the average gamer with quick reflexes, and for me it's basically a repetitive frustration, where getting to the end is mostly impossible. Let me elaborate... Whenever you die, you expect to come back stronger, but not here. You only unlock a currency to unlock more weapons that deal the same damage every round, opening even more the pool of weapons RNG that you can get. All runs are pure RNG.You have 3 types of health: 1- Your current Health; 2- The health you heal through blue orbs (they are rare); 3- The health you can heal until MAX Health.I'll explain... If you take damage, you lose current health and you lose a "pseudo" max health. If you pick blue orbs, you can't get over that threshold, only gold orbs will do it. So near the end, what has happened to me, is I have 140 Max HP, but can only heal 50 and I'm going against a boss with a current health of 20. It's impossible.Then you die, you come to the begining and you don't have anything to make you more powerful, you just have the chance to unlock more weapons to the RNG pool and there you go.You are heavily penalized each time you take any damage and the mobs after the first stage are brutal... They spit stuff from where your screen don't even show, below you or even above... So you are bound to take damage and never get it back.

_childDocuments_.review: This game seriously needs some love, which it's getting, thankfully. Right now there are, as I see it, three huge issues: Healing, Upgrades and Abilities. There is not enough healing for the course of your run, however that could be ignored if the point is to not need to heal at all. But the dash, as it appears, is meant for quick movement and not actually dodging. The I-frames, or period of invincibility during/after the dodge, are abysmal. Okay, so you need to stay moving, got it. But almost all of the enemies are ranged, save for a couple. So you are mostly going to be flying around, never getting a chance to attack, and if you do, it does entirely too little. So you'll need to upgrade that, and you can. Once per run, if at all, and it isn't permanent. And it costs what you may not have. So, what abilities do you get. A lot actually! There are ranged, melee, utility, and none of them are entirely useless. You can unlock more between runs, using gold. So, I want to say one more time, nothing carries over. Every single bit of currency that you didn't spend, as well as some other stats, get turned into proportionate gold. This gold is used to unlock items that you can find during your run.That's it.That's all gold does.Which is cool, but some permanent upgrades could really help with making the game more bearableHowever, before I end, I do want to say that the devs are awesome, and have openly stated that all player concerns will be addressed when updating the game. So, All of these problems that I (And a few others) have, will likely be fixed in the future.So, yeah, TLDR: The game needs a couple huge fixes, but the devs are ready and willing. _childDocuments_.review: Have a Nice Death is a 2d action roguelite in which you play as an overworked Death suffering from burnout. Relatable, right? It has a company called Death Inc., which, you know, handles killing people and harvesting their souls on behalf of Death. Except since Death is suffering from burnout, things have gone a bit crazy in the company. After getting fed up with the dismal state of the place, it is decided: death will put the company in order again. You have basically three main attacks, which are your ever-present scythe and two special attacks using special weapons and spells you can collect. The controls are simple, with your movement, your i-frame dash, and your attacks, but that doesn’t mean you can’t do much with them. Depending on when and how you attack, you can perform all sorts of nice combos using your three weapons. You can even use a unique devastating attack with your special meter that charges as you hit enemies. I mean it,   though you won’t have access to all of them at the beginning of the game. Instead, you have to permanently unlock them between runs using ingots - a type of currency you can find - in your office. The buying system is actually pretty cool: everything has a set price but it gets progressively cheaper as you accomplish missions throughout your runs, like killing X boss 3 times or something. So if you really want something, you can unlock it as soon as you get enough ingots, but if you’re patient, you can eventually get it for a lot cheaper. You can also even change your own scythe’s attack patterns at the beginning of each run, allowing some customization for your otherwise static weapon. And if that’s all not enough, within each run you can also upgrade your weapons for the run using the temporary currency you can find, which are akin to souls.But your weapons are not the only things that offer lots of variety in the runs - far from it. If you meet up with your HR employee during your runs, you’ll  By themselves, the buffs you get are not too great, but the idea is to combine many of them to truly buff your character. You get stuff ranging from a flat defense increase all the way to infusing your attacks with different elements, adding crit chance, and others. There seem to be 3 types of curses, represented by the red, blue and green colours. While it may not look like it, and while this system might not offer as much variety as some other games in the genre, you can get some pretty crazy builds here. My first successful run had me stack up the blue defensive curses that made it so I basically took very little damage from trash mobs, and had a 30% chance to drop anima, which are healing items, upon getting hit. So what would often happen is I’d find an arena, get hit a ton because I suck, and still walk out with more health than I entered the arena with. It was absolutely insane.  I’ve seen, when doing research, plenty of reports of people getting stuck in floor 3 or such for quite some time, and I can absolutely see that happening. I managed to beat a run on my 7th or so attempt without any difficulty, but I’m pretty sure that’s just because of my busted defensive build that I was really lucky to stumble upon. This is not the norm. And if it is the norm for you, rejoice!  That’s right, everytime you get to the end, you can increase the difficulty by one level, which eventually changes attack patterns on trash mobs, thanagers and bosses.What? You have no idea what thanagers are? Well, each department has a number of floors you have to get through. At the end of all those floors, you find the department boss, which works as the main story boss for the zone you’re at, per say. However, as you clear each floor, you can choose amongst a few randomized options where you want to head to next. The name is usually a good hint of what awaits you: you have the HR floor which will certainly give you a new curse, anima floor which will definitely have an anima waiting for you at the end, etc. One of these floors, if you feel particularly daring, is the thanager floor, which has basically a miniboss waiting for you at the end, a thanager. Well, I say miniboss, but really, they even have a boss health bar. They’re just not story bosses. As I said though, the game is hard, and chances are said bosses will kill you many times.  Aside from the weapons I talked about, you can use ingots to buy decorations for several rooms in the company, and you can also level up using exp you gain at the end of each run. The levels take longer to gain, but they’re the ones that give you the best upgrades, like starting a run with one anima, out of three max, or even unlocking shortcuts that bypass entire departments and skip straight to their boss.But if you think leveling up and buying new stuff is all you’ll do between runs, you’re very mistaken.  Often, when you die, you can find new dialogue from several NPCs, usually progressing some sort of self contained story. I was privy to a strike, and I got to hold on to the edge of my seat as I saw an employee try to locate his missing shoe, just to mention a few. There’s always something going on. The dialogue is pretty funny at times, and always charming!If all you care about is the story, though, be warned that it won’t be over by the time you finish your first run. There will still be plenty for you to find before you truly get to the end, and you may, perhaps, even find a secret boss… You may also already have seen, but the game is super charming not only in its dialogue, but also in its visuals!  I mean, just look at death! Death is adorable!  I really enjoy this in a roguelite.Anyway, there’s more I can say about the game, but I’ll let you find the rest out by yourself. The basics have been covered, and that should be enough for you to decide if it is something you want to experience. As per usual, it’s not an experience for everyone, and some will not like the sometimes lackluster curses, or how hard the game can be. I’ve even seen complaints about the combos: they’re there, but if you hit enemies enough, you stun them, which makes it so you effectively don’t have to really take advantage of all your moves… at least in easier difficulties, since you can rush enemies and basic attack them a few times, stun and kill them. None of that bothered me, but it’s still worth a mention as I did see complaints. If you do pick up the game, I hope you enjoy it!

_childDocuments_.review: This should be one of the action roguelike genre's staple. This game is quite charming. On par with the fan favourite ''Hades'' on my opinion. Animations are so slick, textures are so crispy. I really enjoyed how everything look, sound and move. As a genre hallmark, movement is very nice and comfortable. Unless I get frustrated or panicked somewhat, I get to move how I wanted %100 of the time. Lots of weapons have a good range to it, so I get to feel powerful usually. As a story and messages in dialogues, characters and enviroments there are a lot of things to unpack I think. But tbh I did not fully engage with it. Since it is a fast paced game, I didn't fully read everything. There were parodies and messages about workplace, life and the world in total all over the game. Without sounding dumber than I really am, I say they were very - in tune? -. So as a game, this is a total package. If it only crashed 1 or 2 times, I couldn't find a real con in the game. So in a perfect world, where this game does not crash; Have a Nice Death should be very much popular. The game does everything right.  Recommended to actiony platformy roguelikey game players.

The music is great, the characters are fun, and the overall theme is on point.However, I struggle find myself drawn in. There is very little choice give to you and no meta progression allowing you to better your situation. No currency to accumulate between runs, no different play styles to unlock. _childDocuments_.review: Hmmm I have mixed feelings on this. It gets a narrow recommendation from me. The primary value of this game is that it is a roguelike with the polish of an AAA game, an exceedingly rare occurrence in this genre that I've really only seen so far in Deadlink and Void Bastards. However, this is supposed to be a roguelite, not a roguelike and it utterly fails at being a roguelite. There is no meaningful meta progression at all. So like in all roguelites you're going to find yourself getting killed on the first floor and then the second floor as you learn the game but unlike other roguelites you never get stronger so you just stay at that level. Oh but wait, there is an easy mode that will allow you to progress! Yeah, that's not how this is supposed to work. You're supposed to get stronger through a meta progression system and then be able to win on the initial difficulty once you're strong enough. That's also why roguelites later challenge you to harder difficulties so that you can continue to have a challenge and play the game again on a harder difficulty once you've gotten too strong for the normal difficulty. This game offers such challenges as well, funnily enough. This lack of a meaningful meta progression is a major design fault and I can't recommend this for fans of roguelites, only for fans of roguelikes. With fair regional pricing, fair overall pricing, and an astounding level of polish, this will provide enough value for the money paid.Edit: After having played this more I can see it isn't as extreme as I initially thought. I have to admire the game doing everything in its power to keep you interested and distract you from the lack of a traditional meta progression. It is good, you should buy it, Just keep your expectations in check. View the game as a binding of isaac clone instead of a rogue legacy clone.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the same game as the one from Early Access...This obviously goes without saying, but I feel like the game has changed drastically from what it used to be during it's development. The overload of content and update after update turned what was once a simple, quirky, yet appealing time killer into a generic try-hard. For a rogue-like, there is little freedom of choice in how to go about your next playthrough. Of the overwhelming amount of weapons and curses this game has, there are few that actually help you get through the game. Most of them will only help you through a little of the beginning while some are just useless, and the ones that are good are rare to come across. In other words, the game is luck-based. In all the hours I have put into this game, the only times I can remember beating the game were when I got lucky enough. On top of that, the game is horribly unbalanced. There are features not present before that make things too easy or too hard. You would think these two would balance each other out, but that could not be further from the truth. The "Contracts" for example. While they are a great idea on paper, and definitely fitting for this type of game, they are poorly done here. Once you progress to a certain point, you get to choose three contracts before starting a playthrough, and given the choice of four(?) random contracts to select for each of the three slots. A majority of them are terribly unbalanced to the player's favor, especially the "Take It or Leave It" contract, which basically just gives you a free item. You may also choose to change your selection of contracts at the cost of 50 gold, meaning you can basically just cycle through them and pick out the good ones to give yourself an advantage at the beginning of the game. And there is more stuff like this as you progress. Level up high enough and you can start the game with free curse re-rolls, animas, and soulary. On the first level you can choose one of three random scythes the use throughout the game, and gain elevator access to all the main bosses, allowing you to just skip through certain parts of the game entirely. Maybe these criticisms are invalid and I just don't understand rogue-likes (I don't...not entirely anyway), but I feel like being able to start the game with all this stuff right off the bat takes from the excitement of starting a game empty handed wondering what weapons and items you will collect for this playthrough. It also makes each playthrough a little less unique, I feel. Maybe I am just old fashioned, but I feel like this game was much better before all this new content. Sure it still had some problems with balance, as well as other problems of its own, but at least back then it had an excuse as, again, it was still in development. Also why did you change the soundtrack for the Physical Illness dept., Mental Illness dept., Maxxx, and Krank? The old soundtracks were much better, and I wish new players of the game could have heard it.Despite all this, and many more problems I have with the game, I still love the theme, visuals, and atmosphere of the game. The concept is neat and original, and playing as Death is a lot of fun. It is just a shame that it has all been kind of wasted by the overload of new content and the developer's "quantity over quality" mindset. The only way the game could be fixed now is with some sort of cut-back...if only the developers could go back the games roots during it's Early Access phase, and focus more on balancing it out and introducing more ways to beat the game, rather than dumping out more and more content for the game. And please bring back the old soundtrack...at least as an option. TL;DR: The game has changed. The difficulty, weapons, and curses are terribly balanced. It is mostly luck-based, with there being just about only one way to beat the game. Please bring back the old soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to use one word to describe this game, it would be "Inconsistent"This is what can define most of the game really, it's an okay experience, and the gameplay feels fun to try out, but there are huge issues with this game just about anywhere you lookIt's hard to describe this game entirely, nothing here is properly badly designed, but, it feels like the devs weren't too sure what they wanted this game to be, it seems like they mostly took ideas from similar titles that worked well, and put them together without any understanding of what makes those ideas good.From room selection to enemy type including (but not limited to) level design, progression, controls, traversal, the game feels very rough.At base value the game looks really nice but, mastering a game that is this inconsistent on so many levels is extremely frustrating, 90% of the time it feels like you've died from a lot of small reasons that really you had no way of controlling, a lot of the time you do things without even wanting to do them, your character gets stuck in a certain animation, or the screen freeze when you get hit causes your inputs to get deleted, messing up what you were doing, in most games it'd be okay to lose a few runs like this, but this game has NO META PROGRESSION, unless you can actually progress in the game you'll likely unlock nothing at all, and even then, what you unlock aren't upgrades, they're weapon unlocks, and like in most games with unlocks, a lot of them are terrible, and unlocking them makes the run harder.One other big problem I have so far with the game is the lack of explanation, the game uses a lot of terms unique to it with close to no explanation on what things do, buffs you collect don't even have the slightest text attached to them, upgrades for weapons often don't have a description, and a lot of things in general are unclear, it's a major issue when the game never explains to you some of the core mechanics.Speaking of explanation, the tutorial of this game is... Very annoying, it doesn't last super long, but it's a "tell don't show" kind of tutorial, you get walls of text flavored with useless dialogues that just drag on, to tell you base stuff like how to jump or move, but no matter where you look it's impossible to know anything about how healing exactly works in this game!I could go on and on about enemy variety being very limited and poorly exploited, bosses being absurdly RNG dependent, useless map and poor level design... But I'm not going toSo here's what I'm going to say about this game : It has amazing potential, it can be amongst one of the greatest roguelikes out there being a game as pretty and intriguing as hades, and with gameplay as varied and deep as dead cell, but for now, it ain't any of that, but given time, perhaps, and if that's the case, I'll be sure to update my review.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll confess that I'm not really a big fan of rogue-likes. There is a lot of personality crammed into every inch of this game, with the characters, setting and dialogue oozing with dark, meta humor. The characters will even reference previous runs you've done with Death himself seeming to remember exactly what killed him.I also like how the moveset customization is handled, with there not only being different types of scythes you can unlock and equip, which completely change up your basic attack combo, but there is also a large variety of extra weapons and spells you can use to augment your play-style.My only real complaint here is that due to its rogue-like nature, there are different currencies or mechanics that don't come up in runs nearly as often as others, making it difficult to fully explore every aspect of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has it's work cut out for it since it sits smack-dab in the middle of Dead Cells and Hades. Dead Cells being the gameplay it's trying to emulate, clearly, but over that it plastered a unique style that looks really nice and catches the eye. All of the animations look amazing and smooth so the game feels incredible even in fast-paced fights. The sound design is really well done as well. I don't know how the story will play out but for the time being, it's interesting enough, however it is light-years behind what Hades did in terms of progression and plot.The problem is just about everything else. I realize it's an early access game, however there are gameplay elements that are not explained to you in the slightest, like how the hp system works, and what are the hits that cause wounds compared to the ones that drain hp entirely. Hp regen after killing an 'area' boss should be a given, instead it's decided by rng once you open a fridge, sometimes you might not even get hp regen. You are not given any details in regards to what room does what and to how you are expected to use currency/upgrade gear.The weapons. Your main is the schythe which feels nice to use and scales decently if you are lucky enough stumble across a prism to use to upgrade and also a Cauldron room in which you can upgrade it. It feels really conditioned, not something you can do on the fly. The other weapons/spells just stumble across them in the level after you've unlocked them. I would've liked at least a system like in Dead Cells where you can choose one weapon from a randomized set before you begin the run.Apart from all the improvements needed or features lacking, the game really did manage to keep me invested and also to keep me coming back for more. It is not a bad game, just an early access one which is why i'm willing to give it a thumbs up and hope that it be properly supported further.

_childDocuments_.review: It looks great, and the writing is humorous enough, but the game is just boring and has some truly puzzling design decisions.So, combat starts with your basic attack. Mash attack 3 times, and you have a combo. The enemies get dizzy if you do enough damage to them, which prevents them from hitting back. Usually simple to do on smaller enemies, and for larger enemies you have an i-frame capable dash. Fine. No problems.The stages however, are devoid of ANYTHING. Most of the first stage has you walking right. You can go up and down (think Dead Cells).... but there's nothing there. Sometimes a small enemy.... sometimes. I don't expect to find the best item in the game every time I venture out of a straight path but... something? No? Okay.Your meta progression is fine. You collect gold and unlock "weapons", which are not actually weapons, they are abilities that are good for that one run you are on. These range from overpowered to completely worthless, and RNG determines what you get. This is my first problem. Roguelite/roguelike games are all about making a run work even in the most awful imaginable situation. Well, aside from a very few things, almost every case is awful, and none of it works. You do so little damage and the mobs just keep eating away at....your health. So here, we have a bar of health. It goes down when we get hit. Cool. Wait. There is also a grey bar. What? So here's how it works. When your main health bar goes down, you have a grey health bar. If you happen to find a (almost never dropped) healing item, you only recover some of the grey bar. So essentially, you LOSE max HP... by getting hit. Look folks, I beat Contra back in the day, but Contra was designed around that. Here, I'm traveling right across (5?) boring stages, please don't ask me to be perfect, just make them more interesting. Once you get over THAT hurdle you discover that the once nice looking graphics are just... green. And then you see that after beating a level boss (if you get overpowered in a few hits, or if you are underpowered in about 10 minutes of dodging around), you come to a fridge that gives you +defense for 10 minutes. A side scroller, a linear one at that, offering an MMO style booster of 10 minutes of +attack or defense. You can even unlock more of these with meta progression currency! They doubled down on this idea. Oy! And shortly after, you come to the review section and make this game sound like it made you eventually feel; bored, annoyed, and wishing you never bought it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game at first, but the more I played the more apparent all of its flaws were. It's a neat style with a great moveset and amazing animations, but combat itself quickly becomes incredibly repetitive. The terminology for lots of things isn't great. Some mechanics feel completely useless. There were lots of small things, like lots of pickups having no icon or sprites, or characters suddenly not appearing during dialogue.My biggest issue is the balancing with pretty much everything. Weapons, curses, penalties, enemies, bosses.. I'm no stranger to roguelikes, I know well that the outcome of your runs often depends on RNG. But I've never seen any game where that was as true as it is here. Rarities and ranks practically seem useless, common rarity equipment can be magnitudes stronger than the rarest stuff and vice versa. The rarity also leads to your pool of options being narrowed, since common equipment seems to appear way more than other rarities no matter what so you miss out on everything else. Some penalties are ridiculously harsh compared to others, like making a single enemy type that you can choose to avoid entirely do slightly more damage vs making everything do twice as much damage.It doesn't feel like I'm playing along with what I get like in other roguelikes, it's more like I'm rolling dice and if I don't get perfect numbers then the rest of my run will be completely unfun to play. tl;dr Lots of small issues and absolutely horrid balancing. Wait for the problems to be fixed before you buy it, or at least wait for a big sale.
