_childDocuments_.review: So...I love rogue-lights (and roguelikes, but I like a Hades way more than a spelunky), they make up 90% of my steam playtime and I've logged 100s of hours into enter the gungeon, hades, Nuclear throne, isaac, and most relevant for this game: Dead Cells. Although the game is still in early access, after the latest big patch, I think Have a Nice Death has the bones (no pun intended) to become the next big contender to the rogue-light crown. A 2d fast paced action game hasn't felt this tight since Dead Cells, and you can tell that some (or all? not up on my game org charts) of that game's staff helped make this; and if you're a dead cell's fan; let's be honest, you've already bought this. that said, if you're at all a fan of the genre, It's still a hard recommend. Beyond how the game feels, The game is GORGEOUS like...cuphead gorgeous, with beautiful hand drawn art and some pretty crazy effects. That doesn't mean the game is perfect; it's unforgivingly difficult (as opposed to forgivingly difficult, like a dead cells, or a dark souls), and currently, a major aspect of in-run progression (the ability to level up your weapons) is entirely based on RNG, and could either never come, or come too early or too late to actually come in handy; and it's darn near required to advance past the 2nd biome. There's also next to no metaprogression; meaning there's nothing that you can do to improve your character run-to-run. The only thing you can unlock are more items...which never seem to spawn when you need them! However, the devs have heard these issues, and seem to be correcting them, but don't buy a game with the promise of future updates.Also, even now, the game is so hard, completing a 4 biome run might take you a REALLY long time, but the combat here is so fun, you won't mind!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a roguelike. Roguelikes are fundamentally flawed for what I like in games, the level design is either incredibly boring out of necessity, and they're inconsistent, also out of necessity. You can't really master them because they're always changing. This one feels pretty good to play, but it's also really annoying to get a really good item one run, destroy everything, then get nothing the next and get destroyed. This one also doesn't explain it's mechanics super well, such as what the symbols on the select screen mean. Other games have that, sure, but that doesn't mean it's not bad. You're just at a deficit for the first few runs, when you're already at a deficit because you haven't played the game yet. The movement feels pretty good, and the attacks are quick, but taking more than one attack to stun an enemy like the Pyromancers, or whatever they're called, doesn't seem like a great choice, given that you can't see what they're doing when you're attacking them. If the scythe's trails didn't last so long or didn't cover the enemy completely, that issue simply wouldn't exist. Enemies immediately turning around during wind-ups in a game where every single hit matters is also really bad, especially considering it's 2d, and being close enough to get behind them during the wind up time is already a challenge. It feels really good to play and it has nice charm, but there are plenty of mechanics that I don't like so far, mostly due to it being a roguelike. It's not a bad game, but it's not great, either. I guess this would be a recommend if you like the things that I dislike about roguelikes.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of great things about it; the art is phenomenal and the animation is smooth, the aesthetic and charm are abundantly clear, great sound design, serviceable story that only adds to the charm, funny little characters and last but not least good combat. Yes, there's a lot of good in this games if you enjoy games like deadcells or hollow knight I would definitely give it a try. It's also at a fair price point I'd say, the average roguelite enjoyer could easily spend a lot of hours in this game trying different weapons or aracana, for sure with the plan to add more content as the EA goes on.Having said all of that, it is still in EA and it is noticeable. For starters here's a couple of bugs that I have personally ran into and that are a tad annoying; 1) You can get stuck on little ledges where you have to jump to get out of being stuck, it's happened to me once during combat, I don't think I have to explain why this hampers the flow of combat/movement and is not desirable. 2) When you only have 1 cloak weapon/aracana and you switch it to the second position (I personally prefer having my arcana on B for Xbox controller), it automatically swaps back to the first position at the start of a new level. Of course this isn't a major issue but it is annoying to go to the menu and swap them around again. 3) Not really a bug, but sometimes when dashing it feels like you run into a forcefield and slowly get pushed back (happens most often with big enemies and sometimes walls) this has seriously messed with me on one of the bosses  causing me to get hit when i was trying to dash behind him to avoid his punch. 4) I think this is a bug but it could be an intentional feature, when I took the elevator to a prisium deposit I didn't find any prisium only a curse. In the same run when I went to HR to get a curse I only found a permanent health upgrade. I don't think I have to explain why this messes with trying to get the run you desire and can really hamper the experience. It could be a fun thing as a challenge mode, but in a normal run it's rather bothersome.Other than that there's some balancing issues I'd say with certain arcana/weapon cloaks dealing a lot of damage for a fraction of mana/time of other spells/weapons (looking at you boulder rain). I wouldn't suggest nerfing these as they're honestly a blast to play around with but maybe upping damage values or lowering mana values for other spells to balance it out a little. Lastly some personal nitpicks; 1) One of the curses in the red tree that you can get is more of a penalty than a bonus (talking about +15% damage cloak weapon/scythe damage for -25% damage in the one you didn't pick), this honestly is a curse that I refuse to pick up because there's almost no benefit to nerfing myself while all other curses I've found so far only gave a straight buff.2) The amount of times I find prisium deposits when leaving the control room is hurting me, I don't know if there's a way to make some sort of algorithm that checks if there will be a control room and prisium room and tries to make sure you get prisium first. This is incredibly minor but it does bother me sometimes.I know this review points out a lot of the things that are less than stellar at the moment but please don't let that dissuade you, there's a great game here that is honestly so fun to play for sure when you're in the flow of the combat, I just wish this game to get even better and for that purpose I want to highlight any and all bugs I have found and all things that personally kind of bother me. If you think this game looks fun give it a try, I don't think you'll regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I do hope this game gets better, but in it's current state I barely do not recommend this.Art and music are alright, but the graphics seem to be made for 1080p, as they feel very scuffed on a 2k display. FPS also seems to be locked at 60, though I'm not too sure that's much of a problem. Enemy projectiles have an issue of blending in with the backgrounds, which makes avoiding them a little annoying sometimes.The gameplay loop and style is very reminiscent of both Dead Cells and Hollow Knight, but falls short of what makes both masters in their category. You can get locked into attacks, unlike in other similar games where you can cancel an attack midway if you need to dodge, which feels extremely bad due to enemies being a majority ranged. It's like a bullet hell where you have to stand still to attack enemies and just watch as you tank a shot or two.Loadouts and build choices feel very... weak. Weapons/Spells other than your scythe almost always have a cooldown, mana cost, or ammo tied to them, sometimes multiple of those. This makes them feel like tools rather than alternate playstyles, and it really hinders the rougelike feel they are going for. You CAN upgrade your scythe into alternate versions, but the option to do so is entirely up to RNG via the handful of rooms you get to choose at the end of each level, and only occasionally comes up within the first set of levels. In Dead Cells, weapons feel like just that, WEAPONS. Each with their own attack pattern, strengths and weaknesses that you had to learn and master. Here they just feel like one-use damage bombs and that's it.The Curse system, their passive buff/debuff building system, really feels negligible. They have very weak effects and don't feel very useful. A lot of them seem to be "Retaliate" based, which means they activate when you get hit. That's the one thing you DON'T want to do.Healing is almost non-existent, and what is there feels really bad. The game utilizes a grey health system, where you can only restore a portion of your missing health rather than all of it. This can lead to situations where you have 3 charges of the built-in heal, but only a "max" recoverable health of say 25% your original max. The only way to regain health past this cap is to find RNG drops from enemies, shops and other sources which give "Pure Healing", and most of these options give you less than 25% health. This system feels like complete and utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It would serve the game better if the game were more fleshed out like Dead Cells, where you have a choice limited amount of health potions but have other means of gaining health through the build and weapons of your choice alongside the rng drops.Replayability, as far as I have discovered, is limited to just unlocking new weapons for new runs. No permanent buffs, no new inherent abilities, no feeling of getting stronger. You can use Souls gained throughout a run to upgrade your Scythe and additional weapons, but as soon as that run is over you lose all of those upgrades. It's hard to want to play a rougelike when they don't give the feeling of improvement with every run.

_childDocuments_.review: After repeatedly slamming my head against the wall with this game, I don't feel inspired to get up and try again, I just want to forget I ever bought it and leave it buried in my backlog. Unlike many Roguelites that I have had the pleasure of playing, I frequently felt like I didn't understand what killed me and I found myself frustrated with the game, rather than eager to improve myself. With most Roguelites, I can beat the game within ~10 runs of playing the game. I have accomplished this with Dead Cells, Soulstone Survivors, Death Must Die, Vampire Survivors, Risk of Rain 2, Deflector, and Hades. I have yet to beat the final boss in Have a Nice Death after more than 20 attempts. I do not feel inspired to try again.Damage phases on bosses and minibosses can suddenly and without warning give way to invulnerability phases. It is often unclear when it is safe or unsafe to attack. The game is not stingy with its healing items, but the healing is so paltry that taking a single hit from a Thanager or a Sorrow can overwhelm your capacity to heal yourself. Boss attack patterns and hitboxes are hard to read, and this problem is hugely exacerbated in boss fights in the later stages. Attacks come out so quickly and with so little warning that it becomes genuinely frustrating to play the game, and I feel like I don't improve in my mechanics or the improvement is so meaningless in the face of a lost run that my mechanical progress doesn't matter. This is assuming, of course, that the build that I've assembled by the time I've reached the later stage Sorrows isn't totally unworkable. Half of the unlockable weapons in this game are genuinely not fun to use and vastly inferior in comparison to your alternatives.The dialogue boxes with your employees are annoying, overly verbose, and irritating more often than they are charming, endearing, or funny. The art style is very aesthetically pleasing, the sound design is sharp, and the feeling when you are doing well at the game is definitely rewarding. But the highest highs of this game do not justify the crushing and repetitive lows that it presents to you in its current state. It is not worth my time to 'git gud' at the game because I'm not invested enough in the gameplay, characters, or challenge to want to see the culmination of any of these aspects. I cannot recommend buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to talk about something that is really pissing me off and, in my opinion, that is a fatal flaw in the game design. First off, I like the game. i have a good time even though it is repetitive, even though the gameplay isn't that new between two run, but the atmosphere, the fluidity, I have a good time. Why am I giving this a negative review then? SPOILER ALLERT/!\ _ /!\/!\ _ /!\/!\ _ /!\Now, what in my opinion makes a rogue-lite a good type of game ?1 - The feeling that the more you progress the more strong you become2 - The diversity of gameplay, forcing you to optimise your build based on what your run has to offer3 -  The replayability. Since each run is different, each obstacle, enemy will feel different as well because you will have different tools to face them.Even though the game is not perfect on all of these items, it checks some marks.Let's talk about the final boss. The REAL final boss. they though it is a good idea to make the final boss strip you of all your items, spells and, i am not sure, curses (upgrades).In a rogue-lite. You heard me right. BUT WHAT IS THE POINT OF THAT???It completely destroy the feeling of power. It will force you to have the same gameplay whatever you do during your run (auto attack that is). It destroys your items and spells; but guess what, what happens if you happen to base your run on spells and secondary weapons? Well, you are screwed my dear. What are you supposed to do then? Well, upgrade your auto attack (your scythe) and be a master at using it. But guess what, if you do that, all of your run start to feel the same, because you will have to use the same upgrades, take the same routes, and to the same thing all over again. This design alone kills the game, and this design alone is keeping me from continuing the game. Because you can increase difficulty and replay... But why would you do that if every run looks the same? I Hate this. I truly do. So yeah, there you have it. A decent game destroyed by a fatal flow (still according to my opinion). Have a nice death.

_childDocuments_.review: This game just isn't that fun.It's got potential but as of the 'new employee orientation' update it's potential, and it's actually frustrating.First this game is Very Hard. It's punishing. missing a dash is easy to do because dashes don't cancel attacks your in the middle of. If you miss a dash and get hit your HP goes down a lot and your total HP also decreases. You can heal your missing hp and also your total HP which is kinda confusing because one color heal orb heals your HP and total HP but the other will only heal missing HP. The result is the game is silly punishing. Mid-bosses are best avoided because you likely won't be able to heal away any damage you take.The killer is that there's a real lack of progress. You unlock more spells and moves but they are hard to find in the game, and only a handful of them are actually good.They don't really combo in meaningful ways. A lot of people are comparing this game to hades and I don't see it, This is more like dead cells. That said dead cells is Very Hard, but it's fun because you progress. There isn't any sense of progress besides unlocking things, and the unlockables aren't good enough to make later runs substantially different from your early runs.The levels are also lacking. They take a long time to load between levels which makes the game flow poorly and they all look the same. They are randomly genereated, but the ways they can differ don't really matter. There aren't secrets to learn to exploit. The good: This game has a good style and writing. If they manage to balance it and improve the problems I mentioned this could be a decent game. As it stands the game misses on too many fundamentals to make it actually worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine being Death, the grim reaper, and getting fed up with the monotony of a desk job. That's the amusing premise of "Have A Nice Death," a rogue-lite action platformer. As Death, you embark on a mission to clean up souls and ensure your staff is doing their jobs.The game features cute and well-written characters, offering a refreshing change from the typical dark theme associated with the grim reaper. "Have A Nice Death" allows you to customize your office hub between runs, affecting more than just the aesthetics. For example, changing to the Halloween theme not only decorates your office with pumpkins but also influences character dialogues and interactions.While the extra levels are somewhat linear, they offer different options. As you finish one floor, you can choose from various options for the next one, like visiting the armory for better weapons, fighting minibosses, or raising your max mana.In each run, you select a scythe, which can be standard or various other forms. Sub weapons like throwing stars, hammers, and magic can be found or acquired on each floor. The combat allows for dodging through enemy attacks, but be cautious with weapons that feel like dodges but don't grant invulnerability.One issue is the noticeable frame rate drop when traveling between floors, which can disrupt the flow of the game."Have A Nice Death" boasts a fantastic soundtrack that matches the game's style and aesthetic. The cute, well-detailed graphics create a lighthearted atmosphere, helping players overlook the game's darker themes about accidents and death.The game's humor shines through Death's exasperation with his office job, offering a relatable theme. Mini-bosses have satirical names, adding to the game's humor.Overall, "Have A Nice Death" offers an enjoyable gaming experience with cute graphics, engaging gameplay, and a great sense of humor. While it has some minor issues, it's a fun roguelike that could become a beloved indie title with continued developer support."Have A Nice Death" is a game that will delight fans of roguelike action platformers with its cute characters, engaging gameplay, and a great sense of humor.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot write a real review with only nine hours of playtime. So far, I love the combat, I love how fast it can be, HOWEVER, the game crashes constantly on me. It runs perfectly well, without skipping frames or slowing down, until it suddenly dies. I would love to play for a good two hours per session, but it is quite frustrating.I like it so far, I enjoy mostly everything about it, although I cannot properly judge until I have at least beaten it once (and this is a game you want to beat many times).One other thing besides it crashing that I can mention, however, is that inputs on keyboard are not as responsive as they could be. For example, pressing "UP" then "ATTACK" launches you upwards, and pressing "DOWN" then "ATTACK" will do a down smash. However, the game doesn't register the last input you pressed, if you haven't let go of the first one. If you pressed "UP" then "ATTACK" and didn't let go of the "UP" button, then press "DOWN" then "ATTACK" the game will not input "DOWN," making you slash in the air and not come back down. That's an issue because this game is very fast paced. It's a minor issue which could be solved on the player's end, but it'd be a nice change if they tweaked that a bit. Sometimes you're just not fast enough to let go of the button, because of the game's nature. The same thing happens if, mid-air, you are pressing "LEFT" or "RIGHT," and try to smash down. If you haven't let go of "LEFT" or "RIGHT" before pressing "DOWN" then "ATTACK," you will slash mid-air.Great game so far, I hope to play more in the upcoming weeks.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, combat feels sharp and quick, and though oftentimes there are moments of unfair projectiles it's really not enough to bother me.I like a lot of stuff about this game, don't get me wrong, but there are a lot of flaws as well.oh boyI just want to note that I can understand difficulty. I get losing over and over again can often be beneficial, and I get rogue-like games are literally built around the concept of dying over and over.But there's a difference between fun difficulty, and frustrating difficulty.The movement in the game is super imprecise, which isn't really that bad usually, but the straight, slow dash can often end up just moving you into a different attack, since it can't be cancelled early, and it doesn't have enough invincibility frames to compensate. Some enemies (I don't really wanna spoil much so I won't note them) have attacks that are ridiculously difficult to dodge, or projectiles that home in on your position far too well to be fair. In terms of area's, there's only two I have a problem with.(SPOILERS FOR THOSE AREA'S BTW)The addiction department is just absurd.Every time I attempt to get past it, I'm hit with the stupidly unfair range of the jack-in-the-box style enemies (haven't looked in to them so I'm not sure what they're called) every hit is negated by the enemies that make other enemies invincible, and it's basically a nightmare.And then of course it puts you up against maxx, a boss that's so much more difficult than Hector Krab it's actually a bit goofy.The second area I have a problem with is the inevitable time department.Most of the enemies are actually pretty fair, and are fun to fight against!Except for those big guys with the hammers.Even with insane defense buffs, they still dealt FORTY damage with one hit, which, if you don't know, is usually around a fourth of your health. If I could, I killed them with attacks that didn't require me to be anywhere near them to do damage, or just ignored them, because otherwise they could potentially end the run that had already gotten pretty far.And the boss of the area is pretty ok actually, he's kind of fair and you can start to learn his patterns pretty-Sorry what was that?Oh yeah right, the boss of the area actually ISN'T the boss of that area.Yeah so he's basically a guardian to the actual boss, but he's so difficult, and placed in the exact position the boss normally would, that it makes him seem like the actual boss.So you're tricked into thinking he's the boss, and when you beat him and find out he's not, it ruins that moment of fulfillment where you're like, "this was a really cool super tough challenge and I beat it that's so cool!"Nah there's just another, harder boss waiting in that exact same room.In terms of characters, they're decent designs, fun and interesting and their dialogue can be pretty funny, but after a few runs I found myself skipping through pretty much everything they had to say that didn't give me key story points. They just became... not interesting, so quickly, which is a shame, because I do WANT to care about them. I think they're fun and cool and have a ton of potential! But... Idk why, but I just started to care more about finishing/playing the game than interacting with them.And I want to end out saying that again, I do understand difficulty, and I'm willing to roll with it and lose a ton of times, but it's just so much more frustrating and annoying to die than fun to go for another run after completing the first.It just stops being rewarding, and there's not much you can look forward to or work on, mostly just passive stuff that you get for playing the game that you just stop by to collect from time to time.And of course, it was a fun game to play, but I just... I can't muster the same excitement about it as I can other games, like Hollow Knight or Hades.Anyway, you didn't read all that, so byeEDIT:I'm now just realizing that I didn't even talk about how annoying the anima system is.Oh well I'll summarize my beef with it really quick1. Some runs you'll get basically no anima2. The wound/injury system is horrifically explained 3. After gaining three golden anima, all other anima earned are completely useless4. Making the only healing item in the game also basically being the only way to unlock some area's that often don't even lead to anything useful is kinda jankAnd also, I just wanna let the devs know (though they absolutely will NOT see this) that this is still a game with a ton of potential, and I can see how awesome it can still beKeep doing what you're doing, and you can make something even more awesome

_childDocuments_.review: Have A Nice Death (HAND) is a beautifully hand-drawn Roguelite action platformer teeming with humour, character, charm but most importantly: fluidity. I could ramble over how besotted I am with the animation and environment quality of the game for several paragraphs alone. More importantly, here are my impressions and compliments from playing the game. Death's moveset is silky-smooth and every move can be chained into another: You can string together a scythe combo, dash, spell, alternate attack, upward and downward movement all in the span of 2 seconds. When you start mastering your movement and start recognizing enemy movements, the sky is the limit for how brazenly you can play; chaining together every attack and dodge/dash in a beautiful balette of Death (himself). Oh, did I mention that your primary weapon has multiple forms with different movesets? Yeah, well, your secondary/alternate weapons most often have several moves too by holding up/down and/or by being in mid-air. To top it all off, EVERY primary, alternate weapon and spell have their own unique Super attack triggered by filling a meter which you charge up faster by mixing up your attacks with different moves and/or weapons. It's crazy. Combat is fast-paced and hectic, especially when encountering arenas ("minion hordes") and bosses. If you're unfamiliar with action platformers it's easy to get overwhelmed at first: You will most likely die a fair couple times until you start seeing progress. However, every enemy attack has a visual tell, and said attacks (wherever applicable) vary depending on distance to the player. Practice and knowledge allows you to outmaneuver even the hardest of boss patterns. Combine this with the fact that your primary attacks stun most smaller enemies in a couple hits, and you have a fantastic combat flow potentional where hyper-aggressiveness is heavily rewarded when executed properly. Additionally, charged attacks and heavier alternate weapons (aquired randomly and by choice every run) have the capacity to even easily build up to stunning bosses if you pile enough attacks on them. That being said, the game is not easy by any means. Each enemy has their own, unique attack(s). Hordes and bosses will always keep you on your toes unless you have aquired a particularly broken build, and even then you can easily die if you aren't careful. Speaking of which... Let me start this off by stating the following: The game is perfectly fair in all the challenges it presents, but balance-wise it is not perfect in its current state. It is definitely is a work in progress and the developers are perfectly aware of these problems. Some weapons/builds underperform without certain upgrades, others overperform with certain upgrades to the point of nullifying a lot of the challenges the game has to offer. This problem is further exacerbated by weapons+upgrades being somewhat RNG and the fact that basic enemies gain a flat damage reduction at higher difficulty settnings once every world, resulting in chip-damage weapons doing zero damage on later worlds/departments in a run without the proper upgrades. You need to complete the game multiple times for you to reach this level of difficulty settning, however.Additionally, to the player's advantage you have plenty of influence over the RNG in question: You can choose the primary reward for every level/floor you play, in every world. Be it extra currency, guaranteed drops for a weapon and/or spell, guaranteed stat upgrades, ability upgrades/additions, shops (which may include healing, stats upgrades, abilities and weapons), forges(where you upgrade your equipment) as well as mixes with random but often multiple rewards or levels with more enemies that have increased chances of dropping pickups.About upgrading abilities, or "curses". This is where you choose how to build your character every run, the curse system has three different ability upgrade trees where each upgrade type on every step of said upgrade tree is random but predictable and influenceable with clear power progression. The more curses you pick for a single upgrade tree, the more powerful the curses for that tree offered to you become. The trees are primarily focused on weapon damage, utility/economy/defense and spell useage+damage respectively, but may grant abilities that heavily benefit the player by mixing things up. A full run usually lasts 1-2 hours in the games current state. Which, for being a roguelite is perfectly fine in my opinion. It really feels like the game respects your time. Speaking of respecting your time, every run is a fresh start with new possibilties. As previously mentioned, there are no permanent upgrades which carry over runs. But there are unlocks. New weapons, spells, food items (boosts offered to you after every boss fight), risk vs. reward challenges/"contracts" and stacking difficulty settnings hades-style. The one area where game noticeably lacks in content is that the amount of different room layouts available is rather limited. The excellent moveset and varying playstyles provided by the arsenal of alternate attacks available makes up for this however. It took me 35 hours to reach and beat the highest difficulty of the game with the current content available as of writing this review. And I had a blast all the way through. I still have a select few unlocks to go, and will keep on playing experimenting with builds and challenging myself to different playstyles. The promise of future worlds, items and content throughout early access and hopefully further on will only add to this playtime further still.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand this game is in early access right now so any criticism should be taken with a grain of salt. I enjoy playing this game for it's humor, combat, and art style. It's fun to play like a hack and slash before your health is whittled down to nothing. One issue with this game is it is VERY punishing. Taking any form of damage will most likely result in a shorter run. The health recovery in this game is abysmal. It seems that when you kill enemies or break urns there is a chance they may drop anima (a healing orb). You may store up to three healing orbs and use them manually to recover health. Cool right? There are two problems with this. The drop rate for the anima is extremely low. Chances are you go through every floor up to a boss and never see any. If you do happen to receive anima they don't heal very much of your health bar. Combine that with the fact that you take a percent of damage as semi-permanent damage and your gameplay becomes a war of attrition.Another relevant, but smaller issue is room generation. When you go to the next floor you are given one to three choices of the next room type you go to. This will determine what rewards you will receive throughout that floor. The main problem is the amount of rooms before you reach the boss. Shops and The Forge become useless if you don't have enough currency. You will sometimes find yourself unable to purchase anything from the shop (heals included) simply because you didn't get enough soulary in previous rooms. Weapons and spells in the shop are expensive and are rarely worth it if you have your weapon slots already filled. Prismium floors may not show up in the random floor pool and only give one prismium. So being able to evolve your scythe is a coin flip. As bad as it seems, I think there need to be more floors before the boss. This would give the player more risk/reward. However, this would only be reasonable if the health issue was resolved.Don't think these things completely ruin the experience though. Have a nice death is a fun (and challenging) game. The weapons are cool, and the fury mechanic is amazing. The characters are charismatic and funny, and the art is top notch. I'm excited to see the future of this game.

Gorgeous and the theming of it all is a delight.The setting? It's unique and I like and the world around me in the game well.... It's sneaky, quippy way as I got pummeled a few times by Brad and the world responded to it by having new dialogue after defeat or even npcs talking about it.The gameplay? It's not reinventing anything within the genre but it has the fundamentals and that's the beauty of it, it's a system we know. We don't need to learn 17 billion new button combos or learn a whole array of stats. Nope just some terms that make the game unique and not have the same terminology as your cookie cutter rogue-like.All in all I can see myself easily sink hours into this game even when it's early access. And honestly the early access excites me to see where the game goes when it fully releases.

_childDocuments_.review: Have a Nice Death is a great roguelite that has some clear inspirations from Hollow Knight and HadesHere are some positive points about the game:- Great moment to moment gameplay, the way Death moves around really make the game fun to play- Graphics and animations look really good and have a nice style- I really like the satire and humor of the whole game- The weapons and spells are really different from each other, so every run feels a bit different- The game runs really well, in 30+ hours I only found a single minor bugHere are some parts that I didnt like:- Too much RNG, I know that this is common for roguelites, but this game goes a bit too far IMO (when you star a run you pick random contracts, get random weapons, random rewards, etc...)- Finding secret rooms is a pain in the ass, you have to walk near the walls to find the secret room icon AND waste a healing item to open It, but sometimes the reward is not worth the wasted healing- The difficult curve is a bit weird, some of the later bosses hit a bit too hard, so you can lose your run because of a couple small mistakes- Sometimes buying upgrades feels like a downgrade (when you buy a new weapon/food It enters the random pool, but If you dont like what you bought It will just decrease your chance of getting the good stuff)tl;dr: Get this game if you like a challenging roguelite with a great 2D combat system and a lot of RNG

_childDocuments_.review: For simplicity sake i'll be abbreviating this game to "HAND". HAND is a rogue-lite action game where you play as death, a charming overworked boss who is supported by the lovable pumpkin boy intern, as well as a larger crew of employees who are happy to see death out of the office again. Your task being to take down the "sorrows". Gameplay feels VERY hollow-knight, abit with less head bouncing. The dash basically being a shadow dash on its own. And that being a good thing, after a few hits an enemy will be stunned, allowing you time to hit them with a big spell or continue comboing. Health however is hard to come by, and you are advised against taking hits as each hit decreases your max hp for that run, causing you to rely on random drops to increase the max hp back up.In HAND, Each run is separated into a branching path of levels that you can choose, do you go to the storage unit and look for gear, or do you go to a floor with more healing? Each level in the run takes about 2 minutes to clear, maybe more, maybe less, it entirely depends on the procedural generation. Meaning you can usually reach the boss of the floor by 10-15mins, which ends up making the runtime fairly short compared to something like dead cells, risk of rain, or gunfire reborn.Visually the game could stand to have a little more than grayish tones for the background, but the animation quality, cut-scenes and character expression are just gorgeous, easily in my top 10 for indie games in that department.So far I'd give the game a solid 9/10, and now i'm going to continue playing for the rest of the day.

_childDocuments_.review: Another game that is a Rogue-like.And one of the most-challenging I've seen.  About the only flaw I could cite with this game, compared to other Rogue-like games, is that the difficulty is more fixed and can't really be customized, compared to the likes of Hades or Rogue Legacy.  There is the occasional bug, but the devs have the few I've seen, addressed so they do not severely interrupt gameplay.That said, the game is engaging, funny, and very enjoyable all around.  And the fact it addresses the real-life issues of workplace stress, abuse, and burnout makes it a game that subtly makes it clear these are issues anyone can potentially experience.Admittedly, one small cosmetic detail I think I'd enjoy is if I could reset the soul-counter at the front desk of Death Inc.  Watching the numbers roll and increase is rather fun and kinda amusing to observe.  One it hits the cap, you get the achievement for it... and there's nothing more to that counter.

_childDocuments_.review: Hop around as the scythe-wielding master of death and beat up workers that seem to have forgotten about their CEO amidst all the overwork at some point. So far, so good.This is one of the titles where I'd like a middle ground between the positive/negative review options. The setting definitely has potential and the game manages to portray it in a fun and humorous (if macabre) way in the beginning; but beyond that the game just feels... hollow? Soulless?I'm fine with the rogue-like nature of few improvements between runs, but the runs themselves severely lack in variation. Fighting through an area boils down to wailing your scythe (or whatever additional weapons you've got with you) at the same 3-4 enemy types in similar sub-areas, interrupted by a few items and possibly a miniboss, until you reach the area boss and proceed to the next area; aaand repeat. As a result, each run feels like a lengthy marathon rather than an entertaining experience.The few character interactions at the beginning and between areas don't really do much to keep the motivation going, either; especially with the humorous tone the game seems to want to strike in the first place.That being said: the game is still in its Early Access phase (about halfway through, judging by release date and EA FAQ) - if the devs manage to expand the areas to offer players a bit more variation, I can definitely see myself coming back to play it more.I do look forward to future updates and won't refund the title, but in its current state I just can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Aslında oyunu kazanmadan/bitirmeden inceleme yazmayacaktım ama 9 saat harcadım ve bitiremedim. Oyun zor bitirmem uzun sürecekmiş gibi hissediyorum o yüzden yazıyorum. Oyun aşırı eğlenceli bir rogue-like. Rogue-lite'lık tek kısmı öldüğünüzde oyun içi düşebilecek eşya açıyorsunuz başka yükseltme yok tamamen yeteneğinize bağlı bir oyun. Oyun dead cells ve hades karışımı özellikle bazı bosslar kesinlikle dead cells bosslarından esinlenilmiş. Oyun ilk çıktığında 150 liraydı. O zaman arkadaşımla yapımcının facebook, instagram, twitter hesaplarına bölgesel fiyatlandırma getirilsin diye yazdık ve ayrıca mail attık. Bizim etkimiz var mı bilmiyorum ama oyun 50 liraya düştü ve düştüğü gibi satın aldım. Parayı hak ettiğini kesinlikle düşünüyorum. Oyuna günde 4 saat gömecek kadar eğlenemedim çünkü kaybetmenin acısı gerçekten büyük oyunda ama yarın olduğunda direkt tekrar giresim geliyor oyuna.Oyunun eksileri diyebileceğim şeyler.Bazen dash atmıyor ya da dash buga giriyor erken erişimde oyun düzeltileceğine eminim basit bir hata çünkü.Bir de başta bug sandığım ama aslında mekanik tercihi olan bir şey var. Yanınızda bir kitap var ve o kitap sayesinde yetenek atabiliyorsunuz. Eğer sola döndüğünüzde kitap sağa dönük ise yeteneği attığınızda yeteneği sola değil sağa atacaktır. Açıkçası akıcılığı bozduğunu düşünüyorum ama alışınca ona göre oynamaya başlıyorsunuz. Diğer akıcılığı bozduğunu düşündüğüm şey ise eğer fury atmak istiyorsanız 1 saniyelik basılı tutuşun ardından fury atabiliyorsunuz bu da mekaniksel bir tercih ama direkt atılsa daha iyi olurdu diye düşünüyorum.Eklenmesi gereken şeyler:BaşarımlarTürkçe dil desteğiSilahları deneyebileceğimiz bir odave yeni içeriklerNOT: Erken erişim olduğu için içerik eksikliği hissedebilirsiniz ama size şunu söyleyeyim. Buna rağmen 9 saat oynattı 10-20 saat daha oynarım diye düşünüyorum. Dead cells ve hades erken erişimden çıktığında çok farklı oyun olmuşlardı bununda böyle olacağını düşünüyorum.EN: (Google translate)Actually I wasn't going to write a review until I won/finished the game but I spent 9 hours and couldn't finish it. I feel like it will take a long time to finish the game, so I'm writing. The game is an extremely fun rogue-like. The only part of the rogue-lite is when you die, you open in-game items that can drop, no other upgrades, it's a game entirely dependent on your skill. The game is a mixture of dead cells and hades, especially some bosses are definitely inspired by dead cells bosses.When the game first came out, it was 150 lira. At that time, my friend and I wrote to the producer's facebook, instagram, twitter accounts to bring regional pricing, and we also sent an e-mail. I don't know if we have influence, but the game dropped to 50 liras and I bought it as it fell. I definitely think it deserves the money. I couldn't have fun enough to bury the game for 4 hours a day because the pain of losing is really big in the game, but when tomorrow comes, I have to re-enter the game.What I can call the cons of the game.Sometimes the dash doesn't throw or the dash gets into a bug because I'm sure the game will be fixed in early access because it's a simple bug.There is also something that I thought was a bug at first, but actually has a mechanical preference. You have a book with you, and thanks to that book, you can throw talents. If the book is facing right when you turn left, when you throw the skill, it will throw the skill to the right, not to the left. Frankly, I think it breaks the fluency, but once you get used to it, you start playing accordingly. The other thing that I think disrupts the fluency is that if you want to throw fury, you can fury after holding down for 1 second, which is a mechanical choice, but I think it would be better if it was thrown directly.Things to add:achievementsTurkish language supportA room where we can test weaponsand new contentNOTE: You may feel a lack of content as it is early access, but let me tell you this. Despite this, it played 9 hours, I think I can play for 10-20 more hours. Dead cells and hades were very different games when they came out of early access, I think this will be the case.

_childDocuments_.review: Began playing last week, and upon reading the reviews, it really seems like the Dev team took onboard the tips and ironed out a lot of bugs. These include having more bosses, level variety, an area to view all your past attempts, more curses/abilities, and enough choices when moving between levels to make them fun. Although the map layouts are repetitive, the weapon randomisation keeps things interesting. There's amusing employee characters; past reviews from others breathed life into the game. MY favourite part is the Hack n slash.My only gripe is not having many more opportunities to heal, meaning mistakes are costly as you ascend, (or rather descend) each level. But I don't care, I like respawning and having a choir sing: 'Welcome to the After Life~~~'. It never gets old. Unpopular opinion, I would place this game above Dead cells. Dead cells was very imbalanced with the sentry gun being the only overpowered tool out there to beat the game. I got bored with it very quickly, and the pixels obscures the game...making it messy. Have a Nice Death has very clean swipes and spell effects that doesn't overcrowd and leaves you in awe.GET . THE . GAME. . .

_childDocuments_.review: After one successful run on the base normal difficulty I have to say this game is solid. The combat is fluid and fast paced, the game provides constant progression so that it does not feel stagnant even after failing again and again, and that isn't even mentioning the best part of the game, which is the animation and design department. My only complaint is that character dialogue for side quests can be a bit too wordy for such a fast paced game, but that is more than made up for by the boss dialogue, which has not had a repeated line in my 9 hours so far and seems to use your current run for a basis for what they say (for example: when I ran a build based around poison, Brad the first boss commented on how the toxic gas cloud I used was stinking up the place). Overall this game is just incredibly charming and fun and I would highly recommend it to anyone who has a liking for Rogue-Likes in general.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the hardest games ever for me to decide whether I'd recommend it to someone or not. The sense of style that this game oozes, the exceptional options menu, the charming and immersive music and character that this game has is some of the best in a 2d game. It just radiates character. The moveset that Death uses is also absolutely amazing. It feels like playing mini simplified Devil May Cry because of quick combos that you can pull off and how many moves each weapon has. If this is enough to get you excited to play this game, it is probably gonna be a game that you'd enjoy at least to some extent. But the issue comes from the fact that the strategies to deal with 90% of 'minion' enemies is to dash into their face while evading 1 attack and then hitting them. Once you hit them they are stunned and you just need to spam click or use a spell that is off cooldown and you are done. So all the amazing moves that you have at your disposal just come down to passing a dps check on a static enemy, and it completely shut down my will to play the game after I've realized that. That being said, the game is reviewed overwhelmingly positive and even I love so many things about this game that I am so torn whether or not to recommend it. If you resonate with what I've written here and you're someone who is a rogue like or character action enjoyer, I've made a more in-depth video because nobody (including me) will read a wall of text.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of roguelikes of various kinds, here are some thoughts I have after playing similar games like Dead Cells and Skul extensively:Pros:The artstyle and music are both pretty goodDecent variety of weapons to choose fromThere are a reasonable amount of moments you are left with a decision between two or more things that actually make you weigh your options (which is a great thing to strive for in roguelikes vs the alternative of one option always being best and making the randomness obsolete)I've beaten up to Breakdown IV so far, but it seems it goes quite a bit past that, so it's nice that there's depth to the difficulty (I can't say at this time whether the upper levels are "fair" however)Cons:Balancing could use some work. Some abilities together can make a run effortless sometimes ("Gain 1 max hp every time you get hit (not take damage, but receive an attack)", along with something that gives you enough defense to take no damage, suddenly getting tons max hp for absolutely free for just standing still in front of an enemy for a while). On the note of balancing, the rarity of curse rewards don't quite line up. Sometimes a common reward is way more useful than some of the epic or even legendary rewards. I think it's weird that you can be offered some that are contextually useful or useless (EG: Legendary curse that doubles defense...which is useless if you have no defense curses or weapons that give defense like Parasol).There's also a noticeable gap between enemy difficulty and boss difficulty. Enemies are pretty easy as you can just mash the scythe and stunlock them as you go through the rooms, while bosses typically require constant dodging. The flow of combat between these two are a bit dissonant from each other.Some spells' usefulness doesn't seem to quite match their rarity, or perhaps I haven't found the application that makes them worthy of the rarity given.Reaching Breakdown IV there only seems to be a handful of things left to unlock with Ingots, so perhaps more things to unlock to encourage longer playing is an idea I'd suggest to the developers as well.Neutral things:Like most/all roguelikes, the game often is very difficult as you learn how the game works and learn patterns. The game is pretty difficult on the whole, but I'd ignore reviews calling the game unfair. It may take 5-10 hours to really get the hang of things, but a lot of the difficulty can be overcome by not trying to mash your way through everything (which unfortunately the normal enemies encourage because it's so effective), and actually stop your combo to give time to dodge attacks.In terms of the speed/flow of combat compared to other action roguelikes, I'd say it's slightly slower than average, but not by much. I wouldn't mind if the game was slightly sped up on the whole, but it's nice that most enemies project their attacks ahead of time.This game has limited healing items to find, and finding them is random, so it's similar to Dead Cells in that optimal play encourages getting hit as little as possible as your focus.Overall Score: 7.5/10It's not bad, it's not great. I am having fun right now, but I'm not sure if this game will be able to capture me to complete its hardest difficulty challenges like other roguelikes have. There isn't enough depth to make this a game that you'd replay for hundreds of hours, so much as unlock the things/beat the challenges and be done with it in my opinion.Feedback for developers:Fine tune balancing on the whole, maybe consider making healing a little more accesable to acquire (Relaxation room is incredibly rare to find in runs, and anima being mostly luck based is annoying sometimes), clarify some descriptions (specifically with "X do more damage in this department", making it disappear or cross out when you're done with that department and doesn't appear as ongoing despite the description). A way to see more status buffs you have would be nice too (food effects on pause screen, or hover with mouse at least on the UI, a timer with how much of the effect is left would be great too). Soulary Department could afford to offer more soulary for choosing it, it feels like a weak room choice unless that extra 10 soulary would really make the difference down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a cute and fun game but after a few hours two problems become clear. The first is how tedious the areas between the bosses are, it always feels the same and gets tiring quick . At a certain point you come to realise that you can simply run past everything and so you do to get to the bosses, not only to waste tedium away, but because you don't gain much from killing minions and you have more (hp) to lose fighting them. That's my biggest gripe. A far more minor gripe would be that the controls feel a bit awkward and clunky, and your character can easily get lost in a busy room (You're usually black and grey on a dreary background. Your enemies actually have colors on them, such as a bright red or pink so they're more eye catching then you,) but that will fade as you get used to it. I'd rate the game as it is now somewhere a 5/10 or 6/10? Wait for sale or until it comes out of early access. After more polish I'm sure the game will reach something of a 8/10 or higher.

_childDocuments_.review: Competent. It's damning with faint praise, but that's the only real word that can be used to describe Have A Nice Death. In mechanics, tone, aesthetic, structure, and story nothing in this game hasn't been done elsewhere and done better, but what's here is rarely outright bad. It's just even more rarely outright good. This sort of psuedo-metroidvania combat is always tricky to get right and with its bloated HP totals and ferocious enemy damage this game misses the mark. What's worse is that while powerful defensive and healing abilities exist they often incentivize waiting around for slow cooldowns to tick over. The writing is decent enough if you enjoy this sort of Dilbert-tier lampooning of office culture, but it has no insights or clever characterizations and what few characters are interesting are archetypes portrayed with more love and more finesse in Hades. The muted color palette makes it difficult to distinguish enemy attacks during larger fights, and the movement is too floaty for some of the precision platforming they occasionally demand. It's a death of a thousand cuts where if any facet of this game was phenomenal I could see myself sticking around despite the rest, but there's just nothing to look forward to once you've run through the basics. If you just want to hit buttons for a dozen or so hours until you get sick of it, this will certainly do the job and there's worse options out there, but there's nothing here you haven't already seen.

_childDocuments_.review: I am seriously pissed that this somehow slipped through the cracks and I didn't play it when it fully released last year. I'd had my eye on it for a while.This game is epic. It is everything a Roguelike should be; it gives you the tools to create insane game-breaking builds, it's fast-paced and fun, the enemy variety is enough that it doesn't feel repetitive but not so overwhelming that you can't remember what each enemy does, and it has a wacky set of memorable characters and a hilarious sense of humor. Please add DLC where I can play as Pump Quinn. I will give you all my money and worldly possessions.Unfortunately, this game commits a roguelike cardinal sin by just being too darned short. It's clearly trying to do a Hades-style thing where every run you go through unlocks new dialogue and there's little narrative quests you can do by talking to people in order, but the dialogue gets exhausted pretty fast and some of the quests are bugged and straight up never initiate (I think). The thing that makes Hades so unique is that you can play it for dozens upon dozens of hours and still feel like you haven't found every conversation, which this game ends up failing to do even if the conversations it has are really funny and charming.It also expects you to play it a LOT. There are fifteen difficulty levels that can only be unlocked in ascending order by beating the game on the previous one, which is clearly meant to be the endgame "god gamer" achievement challenge that all roguelikes should have. Ok, nothing wrong with that. But there's definitely not enough content in the game to sustain playing for that long without it getting at least a little stale, even if the moment-to-moment stuff is still really fun.Overall, this is a perfect 30-hour-or-so Roguelike, a great 60-hour Roguelike and an ok 150-hour Roguelike. I still loved playing it and definitely expect to have fun doing the endgame stuff (unless it's bugged, in which case I'm outta here), but it's not going to give you Binding of Isaac levels of replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this game is a 5/10. Now please remember what that means, average. This is an average game. It isn't terrible by any means, nor is it particularly astounding, it just an okay game. The game isn't a broken buggy mess, nor does it employ anything particularly new or profound.In terms of style I commend the art team for making something as grim as death and its topics look so absolutely cute. Character designs are unique and play along with the character's punny names or defining features.For story, it isn't really anything grandiose, just a bunch of co-workers with their boss stuck in an eternal job together just doing their own things with those who mess around or slack off being put in their place. For those who work a regular 9-5 office job, the story will resound particularly well.In terms of combat, it is swift and flashy but also is very "swingy", as in your own experience with how easy or tedious combat will be is entirely dependent on what curses or drops you are able to find throughout your run(If you can find any). Any one particular run can feel either like an episode of one-punch man or death by a thousand cuts, emphasis on the thousand. Given that all drops are random and you can't force the game to have you start with a specific weapon you've unlocked (other than another RNG starting armory), you can't really make a character "build" per say when you start a run either. Unfortunately this makes it very hard to take any sort of accomplishment as a player to have any sort of meaning when a fight can take anywhere from 10 seconds to 4 minutes simply on RNG gear alone.In terms of resources throughout a run, unfortunately that too is very "swingy". Even with all items unlocked, you could kill an entire genocides worth of enemies and feel either like an unkillable millionaire with way too many resources or a pauper constantly on the verge of death with how frequent or infrequent soulary, anima, or general consumables drop. Even if you do get a decent amount of resources, shop or upgrade prices make you feel like your 30 minutes of killing mobs and mini-bosses is tantamount to only 1 shop purchase or upgrade. This is a shame for each weapon and ability can be upgrade up to three times but you will be hard pressed to even get even one to level 2 let alone level 3 with the price spikes. Now lets talk about Prismium. Prismium, this all powerful resource that allows you to upgrade your base scythe or upgrade the shop's inventory is more scarce than a drop of water in a desert. Not only that, but when you finally do find this mythical resource and spend it, lo and behold after you die you find out that the upgrade to either the shop or the scythe isn't even a permanent thing. So I ask you, what is even the point of this resource if it can take you literal hundreds of runs to encounter it once, only for it to mean literally nothing?This brings me to the feeling or sense of progression, there isn't any really. Other than story progression and slowly unlocking the chance to encounter weapons, abilities, or consumables, there aren't permanent character upgrades. Yes there is a level up system, but its passive bonuses are only there to alleviate problems that the game creates itself. You will always start out with 65 health, you will always deal 10 damage, and bosses (and some general mob enemies) will still kill you in just a few hits. In addition, weapon and ability upgrades you get in a run don't carry over to the next so even if you do somehow get enough resources to get even one weapon to level 3, know it will revert to level 0 in your next run.All in all when I first played my first couple of hours, I did genuinely have fun and that's what counts, and at the same time I slowly became dissatisfied with its experience as I played more to the point where I don't even want to achieve my first full run clear. The game has a periodic tendency to remind the player about "burn out" and while I took this as a funny 4th wall break joke at the beginning, its message soon started to resonate with me as I played more and more until I reached the point where the second half of the devloper's message set it. If you feel burned out, please do not hesitate to stop playing this game. To me the short experience was worth the 25 dollars and now its time to put it into my library where it will stay until I ever feel like playing it again.

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is honestly absolutely gorgeous, easily one of the most stunning I have ever seen. This needs to be stressed because I am in love.The characters, the world, and the story (all the little arcs, too) are so lovely. It has a unique charm that I simply can't get enough of.The combat is, mostly, fluid, fun and pretty fantastic - the controls take a bit to get the hang of, but not because it's clunky: it's just so dynamic, anything you do seamlessly blends into the next move. It feels so full and intense, and yet also really simple. It's also REALLY fast - not a bad thing, just takes a bit to get used to.The gameplay and difficulty... this is tricky. I put these two together because the difficulty forms a crucial part of the gameplay - of course, this is true for all roguelikes, but this one, even more so, and not in a good way, imo. I think that it's got some serious downsides. Part of the charm of many roguelikes is that when you die, it's not just a bad thing - you are stronger / better. Hades is an obvious example, from the mirror to the weapons to even just the talismons, and ofc the "god mode". This game has that god mode, sort of, but it caps pretty early and is really weak. You can unlock new weapons (endless weapons, so many weapons, how are there so many weapons), which does help keep runs fresh, but you can't CHOOSE your weapon. You just gotta hope you get a good one, and then during the run, pick between rolling the dice again to try get a different weapon or getting things like health or mana bar upgrades. Which, again, isn't something you can upgrade in between runs, it just stays pathetic, so upgrading it feels crucial during the run. Overall, when you die, it often just feels like a waste. I gained nothing. I gained practise, sure, and can get better in that way, of course, but it doesn't always feel great, just demoralising. It can also feel really hard, unfairly hard, unless you cheese it a bit. The bosses mostly need you to just wait out their attacks, dodging. The minions come down to about two strategies - they mostly need to be stun locked, which happens after 1 hit, and then working from there. Mostly, it seems like keeping enemies a w a y from you is what's best. Picking a ranged weapon seems to be the smart thing to do, for both minions and bosses, as it will get you the best results... which sucks, because all that fluid lovely combat and game play doesn't translate to simply standing as far away as possible and just taking pot shots, or other, very similar, cheeses. You don't HAVE to do that, of course, but it is way easier, and the game is pretty hard with absolutely no way of improving your character. So having all those weapons doesn't feel like a good thing, it's just another obstacle. Dying changes nothing. The enemies somehow manage to be both a lil too hard, a lil too repetitive, and not rewarding - and honestly, that sums up how the gameplay ends up feeling: a lil too hard, a lil too repetitive, a bit too unrewarding.I think this ended up as a fun beginning, and then just... I don't know. Mixed feelings. Love-hate. I still enjoyed it. It still has loads of good. I plan to keep playing it, at some point. But there's pretty important parts that just feel... unfriendly. I'm still going to recommend it, because I think it's genuinely stunning, has loads of charm, and feels unique and fun. It has huge potential, I adore it. But the downsides are definitely there.

_childDocuments_.review: After 5 hours of gameplay, I can officially say that I do like this game. However, there are a few things that frustrate me while its in the Early Access, and I hope they get fixed:1. The clearly inconsistent Anima drops. Sometimes i'll get dozens in a run, even when on full health. Then next run I will need them, and I will get absolutely none until after first Biome boss. Definitely needs to be adjusted. 2. The fact that there is no real 'reward' for repeat runs. Having played many rogue-lites over the years, my favourite thing about them is that you do actually feel some kind of progression, even when dying and having to start over. This doesn't have that, you have the same exact run every time, with the difference being potentially you may find new spells/weapons. You always deal the same damage, always have the same start of currencies, etc. Its my biggest gripe - I wish they rewarded you for continuous play. That's the one thing that's going to stop me from playing this over and over sadly - unless they introduce something like this to keep you playing. Overall - 7/10 so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I have very mixed feelings about this game. The soundtrack and the art style is great and the animation is beautifully smooth. I'm a sucker for this kind of animation. The characters are cute and fun, especially Pump Quinn, he's adorable. The gameplay is nice but after a while it gets extremely repetitive. It took me 82 deaths until I was able to beat Time.I am competitive and a completionist and seeing that the game has 17 difficulties (easy, normal, breakdowns 1-15) and that you have to beat the game on the highest difficulty to get an achievement but in order to reach breakdown 15 you have to play 14 different times, rising in difficulty just to reach it, is extremely obnoxious and I am not a fan. I've been stuck on breakdown 3 for too long and have started to rage when I'm unable to progress.Overall this game is beautifully made but the game itself is too repetitive. I recommend this game to those who love challenges and repetition.

_childDocuments_.review: Out the gate, no denying, this game is pretty AF, lovingly animated, and wonderfully written.  And i hate playing it...Look, im here figuring stuff out and dying to the first boss again and again.  I put it down, pick it up again, give it a couple more fruitless goes while i figure out more game stuff, and by the...fifth time i die to the boss, a screen pops up saying "Feel Like Youre Not Getting Anywhere?" here's Easy Mode, yada yada.  It kicks on and its the most EMBARASSINGLY OP nerfening, and look...I like a hard game, but this game doesnt have a difficulty curve, it has a rapidly ascending wall.  The floors leading up to the boss are sprinkled with the same 5 or so enemies that, after a run or two, offer no real challenge.  The levels are pretty much run to the exit, unless you wanna go on mild diversions for any loot, with an occassional cage match with the afformentioned five monsters, and once youve done that long enough, there's a boss with multiple attack patterns, who can potentially 1 hit you.  Hell, the minibosses can 1 hit you.The Easy mode feels like a headwind rule to make up for really unevenly distributed challenge.  Id say give it a mo, as its EA...but this thing is launching on Switch in less than 2 months, and that's just port work.Couldnt advise, maybe watch someone else playing.

_childDocuments_.review: By this point I have beaten the final boss 3 times.I love this game its, its face paced and keeps originality throughout the roguelike genre, feeling more like metroidvainia at times. I was having trouble making it to the end until I realized investing only in scythe upgrades guarantees that you make to to the end as it is way more powerful compared to any other abilities you can pick up and thats not just cause your scythe is better, it's because there are not enough curses that buff things like magic or cloak. So you waste a bunch of time to get to a boss, just to be wiped out in literal seconds.I'm also not a fan of having to deal with random rolls each run. Just let me select from the items I've purchased from the store already so I can use my favourite build.I can't recommend this to anybody except the hardcore rougelite fans who want to devote that level of time into it, or your godly skilled at these type of games already. _childDocuments_.review: I like this game, but I struggle to weigh the positives against the negatives. It's something I might come back to in a year to see how the balancing is. There is a lot to like here and not just the art style. The combat is fun and snappy, and the power-ups are interesting as well. Although, honestly, there were only a couple I really liked.This game is difficult, and I would even say more difficult than other similar games I've played. I am playing through Dead Cells atm too and had an easier time with BC4 last week than I have advancing in this one. Most of that is simply due to the RNG not really offering much. I would have entire runs with very little healing. I would sometimes make it to a boss without finding a weapon. Then I would have a run where there was a plethora of goods to be had. I usually expect some runs to be better than others, but here it just seemed to be skewed heavily in one direction or the other. An aspect it borrows from Dead Cells is that if you unlock too many weapons you will clutter the supply with a bunch of useless ones. I sort of hate this mechanic as it punishes progression. If I were to start another save I would choose more wisely. But, here I found that there was one weapon I really liked and I only found it twice in 50+ runs. But I ran into some common junk ones a lot. I could see me loving this game in the future. It really has some good bones and a solid foundation. I just don't think I want to play anymore until there have been some more updates. Do I recommend this game? Yes, sort of. You might very well love it. Especially if you enjoy unforgiving souls kind of games.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: In its early access state the game feels very polished but very punishing. Healing feels very unintuitive and having two "systems" to deal with makes the already low healing availability feel even worse. Killing enemies feels unrewarding in most cases due to how little currency you gain and floors feel very repetitive due to low enemy variety. Weapon "subclasses" could help alleviate some of the staleness if you could choose them from the start. At the moment the game is very much a "get good" simulator. Not unfair, just unfun at times, especially if you have just a couple of really rough battles. The curse/perk system feels good. The animations, music and combat fluidity feels amazing. The characters are lovable and memorable. With a few balance changes and (coming) updates, this game will be an absolute GEM. A hesitant recommend in its current state, but definitely deserves a place on your wishlist (or as an early buy-in in case the price increases later).

_childDocuments_.review: This review is an EXTREMELY CONFLICTED "thumbs down" that I've considered multiple times over the course of writing this as giving it an EXTREMELY CONFLICTED "thumbs up." Bear with me here.Really stunning visuals for a game that's pretty average in execution. The concept is interesting, but for a game that seems obviously geared to be plot-heavy, it's quite weak in that area. It's loaded with interesting characters, but there's never enough of a presence for any of them to be memorable. Progressing through each area gets old very fast, while also being pretty vague when introducing any new variations, like "consequences" for certain perks.When it comes down to it, Have a Nice Death ends up being like a lamer version of Hades by most measures of gameplay. You start each run through with a choice of base weapons, pick up perks and upgrades along the way, while helping side characters progress their own narratives as you get further through the game. But all of it is so watered down that it almost feels like the developers decided they wanted to make a game that looked Hollow Knight and played like Hades, and cobbled together a game around that....That's way too mean, though. I don't think Have a Nice Death is a hollow shill knock-off of better games. It's not a soulless cash-grab. I bought this game in Early Access because it looked right up my alley, and honestly I think there was a lot of love that went into this game. But the couple times I played it before its official release, the game was honestly a mess. It was confusing, frustratingly difficult in unintentional ways, and much more boring that it is now. I think Have a Nice Death was a well-intentioned labor of love that the devs couldn't quite make work the way they imagined, and defaulted on a similar structure as Hades because it was the closest to the game mechanics they wanted.I don't want to be mean. Plot-wise, it's nothing like Hades, and aesthetically, it's not that similar to Hollow Knight despite the graphics. And I've played many, many Metroidvanias that suck, and this isn't one of them. The best praise I can give it, and maybe its biggest selling point, is that it's a much cozier version of those other two games. There's no deep lore that takes extensive gameplay to unfold, there's no convoluted plot that requires a lot of thinking to keep straight, and there's not that much strategy to consider. It bills itself as being Soulslike, but it's too easy for that, and it's probably a better game for it. You can just jump right in, play for a bit, and leave it alone for however long before jumping right back in. Plus, it's actually pretty good at humor? It's not laugh-out-loud funny, nor is it really clever, but it's goofy and doesn't take itself too seriously.This isn't the game I wanted it to be, and it's not the game it's trying to bill itself as. But it IS a good game, I guess, for some people. I might've enjoyed it more if I had a better idea of what it was going into it. I don't regret buying it, and though it's not something I plan to play more of any time soon, I could definitely see a day when it's exactly the kind of game I need, and I'll already have it ready to go.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great entry into the rogue-like genre.  I love the art and the quirky characters.  The controls are very tight, it's like if Dead Cells and Hollow Knight had a baby and Tim Burton was the god father.  The weapons are creative but need a bit more balancing and I'm hoping the variety will continue to expand with further updates.  The story-line is simple and cute. I actually preferred the game prior to the major update. My biggest criticism right now is that I now have to choose between the Environmental Disasters and War worlds instead of getting to do both worlds at once.  This has had a huge impact on the design of the game.  It feels a bit too short now and I actually miss the power spike that I'd get from additional resources (esp curses, and shop visits) that come from having to do an extra world.  Getting to fight an extra boss is just more fun. The character just feels...less well rounded when going into the final stages of the game and then the enemies are suddenly way too strong in the final zone. Overall: 8/10 would recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Now that the game has been out for a while, I can definitely say the characters and the story has only grew immensely, and thanks to the large amount of storylines you go through when playing that aren't necessarily related to the main storyline, the game feels so alive, as if you really are in Death Inc. Major props to the developers for writing such good characters and have them interact in a really fun and interesting way. The characters, story and visuals are definitely my favorite part of this game.I say that also because in my opinion the gameplay is not the most innovative, it feels like your standard platformer, however a lot of weapons and your scythe have additional attacks depending if you're airborne, aiming up or down, and I really appreciate it, it makes the gameplay, while not the most unique, still feel good to play with. Movement is fairly simple, but mastering dodges with dashes and aerials is something that might take a few runs to really start utilizing well.Progression feels decent, doesn't lock you into a specific playstyle or achieve specific achievements to unlock items.Runs can get long which is somewhat tiring at times, but you're able to leave the game and return to right where you stopped(at the start of the floor you chose) so you can take a break and come back later, which is really nice.Overall, very solid game, with a lot of soul put into it. I still feel like it would've been better if it was story driven game rather than a roguelike, I feel like the characters could shine really well in that environment, but the game is still fun.

Cribbing another Hades feature, being able to select weapons from the start and modify their abilities with powerups would be a great feature too.  Otherwise amazing game, i'm looking forward to it's further development.
